The younger brother of the military minister Chanyu, King Zuoguli Yizhixie, established himself as a Chanyu and defeated the military minister Shanyu's prince Yu Shan.
Yu Dan fled and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty named Yu Shan the Marquis of She'an. He died a few months later.
In the summer after Yi Zhixie Chanyu succeeded to the throne, tens of thousands of Xiongnu cavalry invaded Dai County, killed the prefect Gongyou and looted more than a thousand people.
In the autumn of that year, the Xiongnu invaded Yanmen again, killing and taking away more than a thousand people.
The next year, the Huns sent 30,000 cavalry to attack Daijun, Dingxiang, and Shangjun respectively, killing and taking away thousands of people.
King Youxian of the Xiongnu resented the Han Dynasty for taking away the land on the south bank of the Yellow River Hetao and building Shuofang City, so he repeatedly invaded and looted at the border. He also invaded the south bank of the Hetao, harassed Shuofang City, and killed and robbed many officials and civilians.
In the spring of the next year, the Han Dynasty appointed Wei Qing as the general, commanded six generals and more than 100,000 troops, and went out of Shuofang and Gaoque to attack the Xiongnu.
King Youxian thought that the Han soldiers could not come, so he got drunk. The Han soldiers went six to seven hundred miles outside the wall and surrounded King Youxian at night.
King Youxian was shocked and ran away, followed by many elite cavalry.
The Han Dynasty captured 15,000 men and women under King Youxian and more than ten people of King Xiao.
In the autumn of this year, 10,000 Xiongnu cavalry invaded Daijun, killed Zhu Ying, the commander of Daijun, and looted more than a thousand people.
In the spring of the next year, the Han Dynasty sent General Wei Qing to lead six generals and more than 100,000 cavalry. They once again traveled hundreds of miles from Dingxiang to attack the Huns. They killed and captured more than 19,000 people. The Han Dynasty also lost two generals and more than 3,000 cavalry under their command.
The right general Su Jian was able to escape alone, but the former general Xihou Zhao Xin was in trouble and surrendered to the Huns.
Zhao Xin was originally a small king of the Xiongnu. He surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and the Han Dynasty made him a Marquis of Xi. Because the former general and the right general merged their armies, and marched separately from the large army, he met Shan Yu's army alone, so the whole army was destroyed.
Now that Shanyu had obtained the Marquis of Xi, he made him the second king, married his sister to him, and discussed with him how to deal with the Han Dynasty.
Zhao Xinjiao Chanyu moved further north, crossing the desert, in order to lure the Han army and make them tired, and then attack them when they are extremely tired, and do not go to the Han Dynasty's frontier fortress.
Shanyu listened to his plan.
The next year, 10,000 Xiongnu cavalry invaded Shanggu County and killed hundreds of Han people.
In the spring of the next year, the Han Dynasty sent Hussar General Huo Qubing and led 10,000 cavalry out of Longxi, crossed Yanzhi Mountain for more than a thousand miles, attacked the Xiongnu, killed and captured more than 18,000 Xiongnu, defeated King Xiutu, and obtained the Golden Man to worship the sky.
In the summer of this year, General Hussar and Marquis Heqi led tens of thousands of cavalry out of Longxi and the north for more than 2,000 miles to attack the Xiongnu.
After passing Juyan, they attacked the Qilian Mountains and killed and captured more than 30,000 Xiongnu people, including more than 70 people below King Bi Xiaowang.
At this time, the Xiongnu also invaded Daijun and Yanmenjun, killing and robbing hundreds of people.
The Han Dynasty sent Bowang Hou Zhang Qian and General Li Guang out of Youbeiping to attack the Xiongnu Zuoxian King.
King Zuo Xian besieged General Li. General Li's soldiers, about 4,000 strong, were about to be wiped out, but the number of Huns killed by General Li's army exceeded the losses of his own army.
Just as reinforcements from Bowang Hou arrived, General Li was able to escape.
The Han Dynasty suffered thousands of casualties. Heqihou delayed the date set by General Hussar, so he and Bowanghou Zhang Qian were both sentenced to death, paid a ransom, and became civilians.
In the autumn of this year, Chanyu was angry about the fact that King Hunxie and King Xiutu lived in the west and were killed and captured tens of thousands by the Han Dynasty. He wanted to summon them and kill them.
King Hunxie and King Xiutu were frightened and plotted to surrender to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty sent hussar generals to meet them.
King Hunxie killed King Xiutu, merged his army, and led the army to surrender to the Han Dynasty.
There are more than 40,000 people in total, known as one hundred thousand.
Therefore, since the Han Dynasty accepted King Hunxie's surrender, Longxi, Beidi, and Hexi were less and less intruded by the Xiongnu. They began to move the poor people in Guandong to the south bank of the Hetao and the new Qinzhong area that were recaptured from the Xiongnu, enriching the population here, and reducing the garrison west of the Northland by half.
The next year, the Xiongnu sent tens of thousands of cavalry to Beiping and Dingxiang to invade, killing and plundering more than a thousand people.
In the spring of the next year, the Han Dynasty monarchs and ministers planned to deal with the Xiongnu. They said: "Zhao Xin, the Marquis of Xi, proposed a plan to Shanyu to live north of the desert, thinking that the Han Dynasty army could not reach it."
They fed the horses with corn, sent out 100,000 cavalry, and added 140,000 people who volunteered to bear food and horses to go with the army. The food and baggage were not within this number. They ordered the general Wei Qing and the hussar general Huo Qubing to divide the army equally. The general led his troops out of Dingxiang, and the hussar general led his troops out of Daijun. They both agreed to cross the desert to attack the Xiongnu.
When Shanyu heard the news, he sent the baggage far away and led his elite troops to guard Mobei.
The Xiongnu fought with the army of General Wei Qing for a day. At sunset, a strong wind blew, and the Han army quickly besieged Shanyu from the left and right flanks.
Shanyu himself was sure that he would not be able to defeat the Han army, so he alone and hundreds of strong cavalry broke through the Han army's encirclement and fled northwest.
The Han army chased him at night but failed to catch him.
However, during the march, 19,000 Huns were killed or captured alive. When they reached Zhao Xincheng in Tianyan Mountain in the north, they retreated.
When Shanyu fled, his army often fought with the Han army and tried to follow Shanyu.
The Chanyu had not seen his large army for a long time. His right king, Gu Li, thought that the Chanyu was dead and established himself as the Chanyu.
The real Chanyu found his army again, so King Youguli automatically removed his title of King Chanyu and assumed the title of King Youguli again.
Huo Qubing, the hussar general of the Han Dynasty, traveled more than 2,000 miles from Dai County and fought with King Zuoxian. The Han army killed and captured more than 70,000 Huns in total. King Zuoxian and his generals all fled.
General Hussar worshiped heaven at Langjuxu Mountain, worshiped land at Guyan Mountain, and held the ceremony of enshrining Zen. He did not return to his army until Hanhai.
After that, the Xiongnu fled far away, and there was no royal court of the Xiongnu south of the desert.
The Han Dynasty army crossed the Yellow River and headed west from Shuo to Lingju. They often built ditches and cultivated fields there. There were 50,000 to 60,000 officials and soldiers. They gradually encroached on the land in the north, and the territory was close to the north of the Xiongnu's old land.
At the beginning, the two generals of the Han Dynasty sent out large-scale troops to besiege Shanyu, killing and capturing eighty or ninety thousand people. Tens of thousands of Han soldiers also died, and more than one hundred thousand horses of the Han Dynasty died.
Although the Xiongnu were exhausted and fled away, the Han Dynasty could no longer pursue them because of the lack of horses.
The Xiongnu adopted Zhao Xin's strategy and sent envoys to the Han Dynasty to put in good words and ask for peace.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty handed over this issue to his ministers for discussion. Some people said that they would make peace with each other, while others said that they would take the opportunity to make the Xiongnu surrender to the Han Dynasty.
Prime Minister Ren Chang said: The Xiongnu have just suffered a defeat and are in a difficult situation. They should be allowed to serve as foreign ministers and come to the border to worship the emperor every spring and autumn.
The Han Dynasty sent Ren Chang as an envoy to the Xiongnu to meet the Chanyu.
Chanyu was furious after hearing Ren Chang's plan, and detained him in the Huns, preventing him from returning to the Han Dynasty.
Prior to this, the Han Dynasty had also surrendered the Huns' envoys, and the Chanyu also detained the Han Dynasty's envoys to compensate.
The Han Dynasty was re-gathering soldiers and horses, and it happened that Hussar General Huo Qubing died of illness, so the Han Dynasty did not go north to attack the Xiongnu for a long time.
A few years later, Yi Zhixie passed away in the 13th year after taking the throne, and his son Uwe succeeded as the Chanyu.
This year was the third year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Uwe Chanyu succeeded to the throne, and the Emperor of the Han Dynasty began to go out of the capital to inspect counties.
After that, the Han Dynasty was killing Nanyue and Dongyue in the south, but did not attack the Huns, and the Huns did not invade the Han border.
Three years after Uwe Shanyu succeeded to the throne, the Han Dynasty had already destroyed South Vietnam, so he sent Sun He, the former imperial servant, to lead 15,000 cavalry out of Jiuyuan for more than 2,000 miles, and only retreated when they reached Futou Well. No Huns were seen.
The Han Dynasty then sent its original subordinate Zhao Ponu to lead more than 10,000 cavalry out of the land of Lingju, which was thousands of miles away. They only withdrew when they reached the water of the Xiong River, but did not see a single Huns.
At this time, the emperor inspected the border and arrived at Shuofang County. He commanded 180,000 cavalry to show his military might. He also sent Guo Ji to inform Shanyu tactfully.
When Guo Ji arrived at the Huns, the host and guest of the Huns asked him about his mission. Guo Ji bowed humbly and said some kind words, saying: I will speak to Shanyu personally when I see him.
Chanyu met with Guo Ji, who said: The head of the King of Nanyue has been hung on the North Tower of the capital of the Han Dynasty.
Now if the Chanyu can go to fight the Han army, the emperor will personally lead the troops and wait for you at the border; if the Chanyu cannot go, he should face the south and declare himself a vassal of the Han Dynasty.
Why run away in vain, hiding in a cold, difficult place with no water and grass to the north of the desert, and doing nothing?
After he finished speaking, Shanyu became furious and immediately killed the host and guest who allowed Guo Ji to come in. He also detained Guo Ji and refused to allow him to return to the Han Dynasty. He moved him to Beihai.
The Chanyu also refused to go to the Han Dynasty border to invade and plunder. He only rested his soldiers and horses, practiced archery and hunting skills, and sent envoys to the Han Dynasty many times to put in good words and ask for peace.
The Han Dynasty sent Wang Wu and others to spy on the Xiongnu.
The laws of the Xiongnu stipulated that Han Dynasty envoys could not enter the felt tent unless they gave up the knot and tattooed their faces with ink.
Wang Wu was from the north and was familiar with the customs of the Huns, so he gave up the festival and tattooed his face with ink, so he entered the felt tent.
Shanyu liked him, pretended to make a promise with good words, and sent the prince to the Han Dynasty as a hostage, in order to ask for peace with the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent Yang Xin to the Xiongnu.
At this time, the Han Dynasty captured Gura and Korea in the east and established counties, while Jiuquan County was set up in the west to isolate the Xiongnu and Qiang people.
The Han Dynasty also went west to communicate with the Yueshi and Daxia, and married the princess to King Wusun as his wife, in order to alienate the relationship between the Xiongnu and the Western aiding countries.
The Han Dynasty expanded its fields to the north and reached Pinglei, which served as a frontier fortress. The Huns never dared to express dissatisfaction with this.
In this year, Xihou Zhao Xin died. Officials of the Han Dynasty thought that the Xiongnu were weakened and could be turned into vassals.
Yang Xin was an upright and stubborn man. He had never been a noble minister in the Han Dynasty, and the Chanyu did not get close to him.
The Chanyu wanted to summon him to the felt tent, but he refused to give up the knot, so the Chanyu sat outside the felt tent to receive Yang Xin.
After Yang Xin saw Shan Yu, he said: If he wants to make peace, he will send Prince Shan Yu to the Han Dynasty as a hostage.
Shanyu said: This is not the previous covenant.
The old treaty stipulated that the Han Dynasty often sent princesses to the Xiongnu, and also sent different quantities of silk cloth, silk cotton and food to make peace with the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu did not harass the Han Dynasty's borders.
Now I have violated the ancient covenant and asked my prince to be a hostage. If I do this, there is no hope of getting married.
According to the custom of the Xiongnu, when the Han Dynasty envoy is not a favored eunuch in the palace, but a Confucian scholar, he will think that he is here to lobby, so he will try to refute his rhetoric; if he is a young man, he will think that he is here to accuse the Xiongnu, and he will try to thwart his momentum.
Every time an envoy from the Han Dynasty came to the Xiongnu, the Xiongnu always wanted to reward him.
If the Han Dynasty detains the Xiongnu envoys, and the Huns also detain the Han Dynasty envoys, the number of people detained by both sides must be equal before they stop.
After Yang Xin returned to the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty sent Wang Wu as an envoy to the Xiongnu, and the Chanyu flattered him with good words. He wanted to get more property from the Han Dynasty, so he deceived Wang Wu and said: I want to visit the emperor in the Han Dynasty, make a treaty with each other, and become brothers.
Wang Wu returned and reported to the Han Dynasty, and the Han Dynasty built an official residence for Chanyu in Chang'an.
The Xiongnu said: If I don't see the distinguished person of the Han Dynasty acting as an envoy, I won't tell him the truth.
The Xiongnu sent one of his nobles as envoys to the Han Dynasty and fell ill. The Han Dynasty gave him medicine in an attempt to cure his illness, but unfortunately he died.
Lu Chongguo, the envoy of the Han Dynasty, wore a seal of two thousand stones and went to the Xiongnu as an envoy. He also escorted his funeral procession. The funeral expenses were generous and worth thousands of gold. He said: This is a nobleman of the Han Dynasty.
The Chanyu believed that the Han Dynasty had killed my distinguished envoy, so he detained Lu Chongguo and refused to allow him to return to the Han Dynasty.
What Shan Yu said was just to deceive Wang Wu in vain. He had no intention of going to the Han Dynasty to pay homage to the emperor, and he had no intention of sending the prince to the Han Dynasty as a hostage.
So the Xiongnu repeatedly sent commandos to invade the Han Dynasty's borders.
The Han Dynasty appointed Guo Chang as the general to suppress the Hu, and he and the Marquis of Zunye were stationed east of Shuofang to defend against the Xiongnu.
When Lu Chongguo was detained by the Xiongnu for three years, the Shanyu died.
Uwe Chanyu died ten years after he succeeded to the throne, and his son Wu Shilu succeeded him as Chanyu.
Because Wushilu was young, he was called Er Chanyu.
This year is the sixth year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
From then on, the Chanyu moved more and more northwest, with the army on the left reaching Yunzhong County, and the army on the right reaching Jiuquan and Dunhuang County.
After Er Chanyu succeeded to the throne, the Han Dynasty sent two envoys, one to express condolences to Chanyu and the other to express condolences to King Youxian, hoping to sow a wedge between their monarch and his ministers and cause chaos in the country.
The envoys entered the Huns, and the Huns sent them all to the Chanyu.
Chanyu became angry and detained all the Han envoys.
There were more than ten batches of Han Dynasty envoys detained before and after the Huns. When the Huns envoys came to the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty also detained an equal number of Huns envoys.
In this year, the Han Dynasty sent General Li Guangli of the Second Division to the west to attack Dawan, and ordered General Yinjue Gongsun Ao to build a surrender city.
This winter, it snowed heavily in the Xiongnu, and most of the livestock died of hunger and cold.
Er Chan is young and likes killing people and fighting, which makes most people in the country uneasy.
Captain Zuo wanted to kill Shanyu, so he sent someone to report to the Han Dynasty privately: I want to kill Shanyu and surrender to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty is far away. If the Han Dynasty sends troops to meet me, I will kill the Shanyu immediately.
At first, the Han Dynasty heard this and built the city of surrender. The emperor thought that the city was far away from the Xiongnu.
In the spring of the next year, the Han sent Zhao Ponu, the Marquis of Zhaoye, and led more than 20,000 cavalry out of the northwest of Shuofang County, more than 2,000 miles away, and agreed to reach Junji Mountain before returning.
Hou Yehou arrived at the appointed place on time and then came back. Lieutenant Zuo wanted to kill Chanyu but was discovered. Shanyu killed him and sent troops from the left to attack Houye Yehou.
Hou Yehou hunted and killed thousands of Xiongnu people as he walked.
When the Marquis of Zunye returned to a place four hundred miles away from Shouxiang City, 80,000 Xiongnu cavalry besieged him.
Zhao Yehou went out to find water alone at night. The Huns secretly searched for him, captured Zhao Yehou alive, and took the opportunity to attack his army.
Guo Zong in the Han army served as the guard, and King Wei served as the leader of the Xiongnu troops. The two discussed: Don't persuade each other to return to the Han Dynasty while the captains are afraid that they will be killed by the Hanjun if they lose their generals.
The Han army was trapped by the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu Chanyu was overjoyed and sent a commando to attack the surrendered city.
The city was not captured, so they invaded the border fortress and left.
The next year, Chanyu wanted to attack Shujiang City himself, but he died of illness before he could reach Shujiang City.
His son Shanyu died three years after he succeeded to the throne.
When his son was young, the Huns appointed King Youxian, the younger brother of his uncle Uwe Chanyu, as Chanyu.
This year is the third year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
After the Chanyu of Yali Lake succeeded to the throne, the Han Dynasty sent Guanglu Xu Ziwei to go hundreds of miles away from Wuyuan Fortress and more than a thousand miles away to build small castles and outposts as far as Luqu. It also sent guerrilla general Han Shuo and Changping Houwei and his wife to garrison here, and sent strong crossbow captain Lu Bode to build a castle in Juyanze.
In the autumn of this year, the Xiongnu invaded Dingxiang and Yunzhong on a large scale, killing and plundering thousands of people, and defeated several high-ranking officials with a salary of two thousand dan before leaving. During the march, the castle built by Guanglu Xu Ziwei was destroyed.
He also sent King Youxian to invade Jiuquan and Zhangye and plunder thousands of people.
When the Han Dynasty general Ren Wen intercepted and rescued them, the Xiongnu lost all the Han people they had captured and left.
This year, General Li Guangli of the Second Division conquered Dayuan and killed the King of Dayuan before returning.
The Xiongnu wanted to intercept Li Guangli, but failed to arrive.
In the winter of this year, the Xiongnu wanted to attack Shouxiang City, but Shanyu died of illness.
The Chanyu of Yali Lake died a year after he succeeded to the throne, so the Huns made his younger brother Zuo Dadu Wei and Tutanhou the Chanyu.
After the Han Dynasty killed the King of Dayuan, it shocked foreign countries.
The emperor wanted to seize the opportunity to besiege the Xiongnu, so he issued an edict saying: Emperor Gao left me with worries about Pingcheng. When Empress Gao was in power, what Chanyu said in his letter was extremely unreasonable and rebellious.
Once upon a time, Duke Xiang of Qi reported his grudges from nine generations ago, and the "Spring and Autumn Annals" praised him greatly.
This year is the fourth year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
After Shan Yu, the Marquis of Qi, succeeded to the throne, he sent back the envoys who had been detained by the Han Dynasty and refused to surrender. Lu Chongguo and others returned to the Han Dynasty.
The Chanyu had just succeeded to the throne and was afraid that the Han Dynasty would attack him, so he said to himself: I am a son, how can I dare to compare with the emperor of the Han Dynasty!
The Emperor of Han is my elder.
The Han Dynasty sent Zhonglang Su Wu to send generous gifts to Shanyu.
The Chan Yu became more and more proud and his etiquette was very disrespectful. The Han Dynasty was greatly disappointed.
The next year, Zhao Ponu, the Marquis of Zhaoye, fled from the Xiongnu and returned to the Han Dynasty.
The next year, the Han Dynasty sent General Li Guang of the Second Division to lead 30,000 cavalry out of Jiuquan and attacked King Youxian in the Tianshan Mountains. He killed and captured more than 10,000 Huns. When he came back, the Huns surrounded the General of the Second Division and barely escaped. Sixty-seven out of ten of the Han army died.
The Han Dynasty also sent General Yinjuo Gongsun Ao out of the Xihe area to meet Captain Qiannu at Zhuotu Mountain, but nothing was obtained.
He also sent the cavalry captain Li Ling with 5,000 infantrymen to go more than a thousand miles north of Juyan and met Chanyu. The two sides fought. Li Ling's army killed and wounded more than 10,000 Xiongnu people. Finally, they ran out of weapons and food. Li Ling wanted to get out of the predicament and return, but the Huns surrounded Li Ling. Li Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu, and his army was destroyed. Only 400 people could return to the Han Dynasty.
The Chanyu then favored Li Ling and married his daughter to Li Ling.
In the second year after this, the Han Dynasty sent General Ershi with 60,000 cavalry and 100,000 infantry out of Shuofang County.
Lu Bode, the strong crossbow captain, led more than 10,000 people to join the general of the second division.
Guerrilla general Han Yue led 30,000 infantry and cavalry people out of Wuyuan.
General Gongsun Ao led 10,000 cavalry and 30,000 infantry out of Yanmen.
When the Xiongnu heard the news, they transferred many of their valuables to the far north of the Yuwushui River. The Shanyu led a hundred thousand cavalry to wait for the Han army south of the Yuwushui River and fight with the general of the Second Division.
The general of the second division left his place, led his troops back, and fought with Shan Yu for more than ten days.
General Ershi heard that his family had been exterminated for the crime of witchcraft, so he surrendered to the Huns together with his army. Only one or two of his troops could return to the Han Dynasty out of a thousand.
Guerrilla general Han Shuo gained nothing.
Because General Gongsun Ao was at war with King Zuoxian, the situation was unfavorable, so he led his troops back to the Han Dynasty.
This year, the Han Dynasty troops who went out of the frontier to fight against the Xiongnu could not say how much they deserved, because their achievements could not compensate for their losses.
The emperor ordered the arrest of the imperial physician Ling Suidan, because it was he who revealed the news that the general's family was exterminated, which led Li Guangli to surrender to the Huns.
Tai Shigong said: Confucius wrote the "Spring and Autumn Annals" in a clear and clear way about the events during the reigns of Lu Yingong and Lu Huan Gong. However, during the Lu Dinggong and Lu Shengong periods, the descriptions were obscure and implicit, because this is a text that is close to contemporary politics but has nothing to praise, and is a taboo word.
The mistake of those secular people who talk about the Xiongnu issue is that they want to gain temporary power by chance, so they devote themselves to making flattery and favoring their one-sided views, without considering the actual situation of the Xiongnu and the Han Dynasty. The generals only relied on the vastness of China's land and strong morale to deal with the Xiongnu. The emperor formulated countermeasures based on these, so the achievements he made were not profound and extensive.
Although Yao was wise, he was unable to complete his great cause on his own. Only after he obtained Dayu did the whole of China enjoy peace.
If you want to carry forward the tradition of the Great Holy King, you just have to choose and appoint generals!
It just depends on choosing and appointing generals and ministers!
summary:
The Xiongnu, whose ancestor was Chunwei, a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern wilds. They moved with their livestock—horses, cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys—in search of water and pasture, without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements. From childhood, they learned archery and riding, and all men were armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized warfare and plunder, favoring attack when advantageous and retreating without shame. They respected the strong and disdained the weak, practiced levirate marriage, and had no taboo against using personal names. Their leaders were called Chanyu, and they held seasonal gatherings for sacrifices and censuses. Laws were harsh, with punishments for murder and theft, and burial practices included human sacrifice for the Chanyu.

Historically, the Xiongnu and their predecessors, such as the Shanrong and Xunzhu, interacted with Chinese dynasties. During the Zhou dynasty, King Mu of Zhou campaigned against the Dog Rong, and later, King You of Zhou was killed by the Quanrong, leading to the Zhou capital's eastward move. The Qin dynasty, under Qin Shihuang, sent Meng Tian to drive the Xiongnu from the Ordos region and built the Great Wall. After Qin's fall, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman, who was killed by his son Modun. Modun, after training his troops with a signaling arrow, usurped power and expanded Xiongnu territory, defeating the Donghu, Yuezhi, and other tribes, and amassing over 300,000 cavalry. He established a hierarchical structure with left and right kings, generals, and officials, and his rule marked the Xiongnu's peak, making them a major threat to the Han dynasty.

The Han dynasty, after its founding, faced constant Xiongnu raids. Emperor Gaozu was besieged at Pingcheng by Modun but escaped through bribery and a peace treaty involving marriage and tribute. Subsequent rulers, including Empress Dowager Lu and Emperor Wen, maintained this policy despite Xiongnu provocations. The Xiongnu, under Chanyu Laoshang and later Junchen, continued to raid border regions, while Han envoys like Zhonghang Yue, who defected to the Xiongnu, advised them to resist Han cultural influence. The Han dynasty alternated between appeasement and military campaigns, with Emperor Wu launching large-scale offensives led by generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, who defeated the Xiongnu in the Ordos and Gobi, capturing key territories and forcing them northward.

Despite these victories, the Xiongnu remained resilient. After Huo Qubing's death, the Han halted major campaigns, and the Xiongnu, under Chanyu Uwei and his successors, continued to raid and negotiate. The Han attempted to sow discord among Xiongnu leaders and used diplomacy with western states like Wusun to isolate them. However, internal strife and harsh winters weakened the Xiongnu. Later Chanyu, such as Er Chanyu and Huyan, faced rebellions and military defeats, including the capture of Han general Li Ling and the defection of Li Guangli. The Han built fortifications and expanded into the Hexi Corridor, but the Xiongnu persisted in their raids, leading to a prolonged stalemate.

The historian Sima Qian notes that the Xiongnu's nomadic lifestyle and martial culture made them formidable adversaries. He criticizes Han officials for short-sighted policies and emphasizes the importance of selecting capable generals, as even wise rulers like Yao needed talented ministers to achieve success. The Xiongnu's lineage, from Chunwei to Modun, spanned over a thousand years, with their power fluctuating until Modun unified them. Their social structure, with hereditary titles and a focus on warfare, allowed them to dominate the northern steppes and challenge Chinese authority for centuries.

translation:
The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was from Zhending and his surname was Zhao.
The Qin State annexed the six countries, captured and pacified Yang Yue, established Guilin, Nanhai and Xiangjun, and resettled the people who had committed crimes and migrated to these places, and lived together with the Yue people for thirteen years.
Wei Tuo was appointed as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai County during the Qin Dynasty.
During the second year of Qin Dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the commander of Longchuan, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others had launched a rebellion, and that the Qin Dynasty was pursuing cruel and unjust policies, and the people of the world were resentful of this. Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, etc. all gathered people in their respective states and counties at the same time, formed armies, and fought for the world like tigers. The Central Plains region was in turmoil, and it was unknown when peace would be restored. Heroes betrayed the Qin Dynasty and opposed each other.
Nanhai County is remote and remote, and I am afraid that the bandit army will invade the land. When I attack here, I want to mobilize the army to cut off the newly built road to the Central Plains. I have taken precautions in advance and wait for the changes in the princes. It happens that I am seriously ill.
Let’s talk about Panyu. There are dangerous mountains behind us to rely on, and there is the sea as a barrier to the south. It is thousands of miles away from east to west. We have some Central Plains people to assist us. We can also be the lord of a state and establish a country.
There is no one among the governors of Nanhai County who is worthy of me to study these things with him, so I have summoned you to tell you these things.
Ren Xiao immediately issued an appointment document to Zhao Tuo, asking him to act on behalf of Nanhai County.
After Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo sent a message to Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxiguan, saying: The bandit army is coming, so we must quickly cut off the road, gather the army, and defend ourselves.
Zhao Tuo took this opportunity to gradually use the law to kill the officials installed by the Qin Dynasty, and use his cronies as acting governors.
After the Qin Dynasty was destroyed, Zhao Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiangjun, and established himself as King Wu of South Vietnam.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already pacified the world. Because the people in the Central Plains were tired and miserable, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty spared Zhao Tuo and did not kill him.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, he sent Lu Jia to South Vietnam and ordered Zhao Tuo to inherit his title of King of South Vietnam, make an agreement with him, exchange envoys, and let him coordinate Baiyue so that they can live in harmony and not become a scourge to the south of the Han Dynasty. South Vietnam borders Changsha to the north.
During the post-Gao period, officials from relevant departments requested that South Vietnam be prohibited from purchasing ironware in border markets.
Zhao Tuo said: Emperor Gao made me the king of South Vietnam, and the two sides exchanged envoys and supplies. Now Gao Hou listens to the opinions of the slanderers, treats the barbarians as aliens, and cuts off the source of the artifacts we need. This must be the idea of ​​King Changsha. He wants to follow the Han Dynasty in the Central Plains, eliminate South Vietnam, double as the king of South Vietnam, and establish his own merits.
So Zhao Tuo took advantage of the title and called himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue. He sent troops to attack the border cities of Changsha and defeated several counties before leaving.
Empress Gao sent General Longlu Hou Zhou Zao to attack Zhao Tuo.
In the hot and humid climate, most of the soldiers became seriously ill, making it impossible for the army to cross Yangshan Mountains.
More than a year later, Queen Gao died, and the Han army stopped attacking.
Therefore, Zhao Tuo relied on his army to show off his power on the border, and bribed Minyue, Xiou and Luoyue with property to make them all belong to South Vietnam, making his territory more than 10,000 miles long from east to west.
Zhao Tuo actually rode in Huangwu Zuohu's chariot and issued orders as the emperor, which was equal to the status of the Han Dynasty.
In the first year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, when the emperor had just ruled the world, he sent envoys to the princes and the rulers of the barbarians from all over the world to inform them of his intention to come to Beijing from Dai to ascend the throne, and to let them know the emperor's saintly virtues.
So for the tomb of Zhao Tuo's parents in Zhending, a tomb guard was set up, and sacrifices were held on time every year. His cousins ​​were also summoned, and they were given honorable official positions and generous rewards to show their favor.
The emperor ordered Prime Minister Chen Ping to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to South Vietnam. Chen Ping said that Lu Jia, a native of Haochou, had served as envoys to South Vietnam many times during the late emperor's reign.
The emperor summoned Lu Jia, appointed him Taizhong doctor, and went to South Vietnam as an envoy. He took the opportunity to blame Zhao Tuo for proclaiming himself emperor and not sending an envoy to report to the emperor.
When Lu Jia arrived in South Vietnam, the South Vietnamese king Zhao was particularly frightened and wrote an apology to the emperor, saying: The barbarian chief husband Chen Tuo used to isolate and discriminate against South Vietnam. I secretly suspected that the king of Changsha was a slanderous minister. I also heard in this distant place that the high queen killed Zhao Tuo's clan and dug and burned the graves of his ancestors. Therefore, he abandoned himself and invaded the border area of ​​​​Changsha.
Moreover, in the low and humid land in the south, among the barbarians, Minyue in the east only had thousands of people, but they called their ruler king; in the west, naked countries like Xiou and Luoyue also had to call themselves kings.
So I arrogantly stole the emperor's title to comfort myself. How dare I report this to the emperor!
Zhao Tuo kowtowed deeply and apologized, saying that he would remain a vassal minister of the Han Dynasty for a long time and abide by his duty to pay tribute to the emperor.
So Zhao Tuo issued an order to the whole country, saying: I heard that two heroes cannot coexist, and two sages cannot live together in the same world.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty was a wise emperor. From now on, I will get rid of the imperial system and will no longer ride in Huangwu Zuohu's car.
Lu Jia returned to Beijing to report the matter, and Emperor Wen of Han was very happy.
Continuing to the era of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Tuo professed his vassalage to the Han Dynasty and sent people to Chang'an to meet the emperor in the spring and autumn.
However, in South Vietnam, Zhao Tuo always stole the title of emperor. He only became king when he sent envoys to meet the emperor, and accepted the emperor's orders just like the princes.
In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Zhao Tuo died.
Zhao Tuo's grandson Zhao Hu became the king of South Vietnam.
At this time, King Ying of Minyue launched a war to attack the border towns of South Vietnam. Zhao Hu sent people to write to the Emperor of Han, saying: South Vietnam and Minyue are both vassals of the Han Dynasty and cannot send troops to attack each other without permission.
Now that Fujian and Yue have invaded me, I dare not send troops to fight. I hope that the emperor will issue an edict to deal with this matter.
So the emperor praised the South Vietnamese for their loyal behavior and abiding by their duties and covenants, sent troops for them, and sent two generals to attack Minyue.
Before the Han army crossed the Yangshan Mountains, Yu Shan, the younger brother of the King of Minyue, killed Ying and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, thus stopping the crusade.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty sent Zhuang Zhu to explain the court's intentions to the King of Nanyue. Zhao Hu kowtowed deeply and said: The emperor sent troops to attack Fujian and Yue for me. Even if I die, I can't repay the emperor's kindness!
Zhao Hu sent Prince Yingqi to the court to serve as a bodyguard.
He then said to Zhuang Zhu: The country has just been invaded by the enemy. Please leave first.
Zhao Hu was preparing his bags day and night to go to the capital to meet the emperor.
After Zhuang Zhu left, his ministers admonished Zhao Hujin and said: The Han Dynasty sent troops to kill Ying, and they also used this action to warn South Vietnam.
Moreover, the late king once said in the past that when serving the emperor, one only hopes not to be rude. The most important thing is not to go to the emperor just because you like to listen to the good words of the messenger.
If you go to court to see the emperor, you will not be able to come back. This is a situation of national subjugation.
So Zhao Hu used illness as an excuse and did not go to see the Emperor of Han in the end.
More than ten years later, Zhao Huzhen became seriously ill, and Prince Yingqi asked to return to the country.
When Zhao Hu died, he was given the posthumous title of King Wen.
After Ying Qi Dai was established as the King of Nanyue, he hid the seal of Emperor Wu of his ancestor.
When Yingqi went to Chang'an to serve as a guard, he took a daughter from Handan's family as his wife and gave birth to a son named Zhao Xing.
When he ascended the throne and became king, he wrote to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, requesting that his wife Xi be made the queen and Zhao Xing be the prince.
The Han Dynasty repeatedly sent envoys to tactfully advise Ying Qi to go to the emperor. Ying Qi liked to kill people arbitrarily and was afraid that if he went to the capital to worship the emperor, he would be forced to follow the laws of the mainland and implement the laws of the Han Dynasty. Therefore, he used illness as an excuse to not go to the emperor and only sent his son Cigong to the capital to serve as a guard.
When Yingqi died, he was given the posthumous title of King Ming.
Prince Zhao Xingdai was established as the King of Nanyue, and his mother became the Queen Mother.
When the Queen Mother was not married to Yingqi as her concubine, she had committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, a native of Baling.
After Yingqi's death, in the fourth year of Yuanding, the Han Dynasty sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade the King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother to go to Beijing to worship the emperor like the princes in the interior. He ordered the debaters to admonish the official Zhongjun and others to publicize this idea, and asked the warrior Wei Chen and others to assist him where they were insufficient. Guard Lu Bode led his troops to garrison in Guiyang, waiting for the envoy.
The King of Nanyue is young, and the Queen Mother is from the Central Plains. She once committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji. This time Anguo Shaoji came to serve as an envoy and committed adultery with her again.
Most people in South Vietnam knew about this, and most of them did not rely on the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother was afraid of unrest and wanted to rely on the power of the Han Dynasty. She repeatedly persuaded the King of Nanyue and his ministers to request to belong to the Han Dynasty.
So he sent a letter to the emperor through an envoy, requesting that the princes in the interior should meet with the emperor once every three years and remove the border barriers.
So the emperor agreed to their request and gave the silver seal to Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, and also gave the official seals such as internal history, lieutenant, and master, and the rest of the official positions were placed by South Vietnam himself.
They abolished their previous punishments of tattoos and torture, and used the laws of the Han Dynasty to compare with the princes in the interior.
The envoys stayed to pacify South Vietnam.
The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother packed their belongings and valuables in preparation for going to Beijing to meet the Emperor.
Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, was very old and had assisted three kings. There were more than 70 officials and officials in his clan. The men all married the princess's wives, and the women married the princes and their brothers' clan members. They were related by marriage to the King of Qin in Cangwu County.
His position in South Vietnam is very prominent, and the South Vietnamese people trust him. Many people have become his cronies, surpassing the King of South Vietnam in terms of popular support.
The King of Nanyue wanted to write to the emperor. He repeatedly suggested that the king give up this move, but the King of Nanyue did not listen.
He had the idea of ​​​​treason against the King of Nanyue, and repeatedly excused himself from meeting the Han Dynasty envoys due to illness.
The envoys paid great attention to Lu Jia's words and deeds, but due to the situation, they did not execute Lu Jia.
The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were also afraid that Lu Jia would be the first to attack, so they arranged a banquet and planned to use the power of the Han Dynasty envoys to kill Lu Jia and others.
At the banquet, the envoys all faced east, the Queen Mother faced south, the king faced north, and Prime Minister Lu Jia and the ministers all faced west, sitting and drinking with them.
Lu Jia's younger brother was a general and led his troops to wait outside the palace.
While drinking, the Queen Mother said to Lu Jia: It is in the interests of the country that South Vietnam belongs to the Han Dynasty, but Prime Minister, you complain that this is not good. Why?
The Queen Mother wanted to anger the Han Dynasty envoy.
The envoy hesitated and did not dare to kill Lu Jia.
Lu Jia saw that the people around him were not his cronies, so he stood up and walked out.
The queen mother got angry and wanted to hit Lu Jia with a spear, but the king stopped her.
Lu Jia went out, divided some of his brother's soldiers, and arranged them around his residence. He refused to meet the king and the envoy because of his illness.
Lu Jia secretly prepared to launch a rebellion with his ministers.
The King of Nanyue had no intention of killing Lu Jia. Lu Jia knew this, so he did not launch a rebellion for several months.
The Queen Mother had engaged in promiscuous behavior and no one in the South Vietnam country would join her. She wanted to kill Lu Jia alone, but she was unable to do it.
The Emperor heard that Lu Jia disobeyed the King of Nanyue. The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were weak and could not control Lu Jia, and the envoys were timid and incapable of decision-making.
He also believed that the king and the queen mother had surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and Lu Jia was the only one causing trouble, so it was not worth sending troops. He wanted to send Zhuang Shen and 2,000 people as an envoy to South Vietnam.
Zhuang Shen said: If we go for friendly negotiations, a few people will be enough; if we go for violence, two thousand people can't do much.
Zhuang Shen refused to go, so the emperor dismissed Zhuang Shen from his position.
Han Qianqiu, a strong man from Jiadi and the prime minister of the former King of Jibei, said: "For such a small South Vietnam, the King of South Vietnam and the Queen Mother are acting as internal agents, and only Prime Minister Lu Jia can destroy it. I am willing to get 200 warriors to go to South Vietnam. I will definitely kill Lu Jia and report to the emperor when I come back."
So the emperor sent Han Qianqiu and the Queen Mother's younger brother Zhen Le to lead 2,000 troops to South Vietnam.
They entered South Vietnam, and the people of Lu Jia finally rebelled and issued an order to the people of South Vietnam: The king is young, the queen mother is Chinese, and she had an affair with the envoys of the Han Dynasty. She wanted to belong to the Han Dynasty. She took all the treasures and valuables of the late king and presented them to the Han emperor to flatter the Han emperor. He took many of his followers with him, went to Chang'an, and sold them to the Han people as servants.
She only wanted to gain the temporary benefits of her escape, and did not take into account the Zhao family's national power, nor did she intend to plan for the permanent plan for future generations.
So Lu Jia and his brother led troops to attack and kill the King of Nanyue, the Queen Mother and the Han Dynasty envoy.
He also sent people to inform King Cangwu of Qin and officials in various counties and counties that Shuyanghou Zhao Jiande, the son of King Ming's eldest son and his wife of South Vietnamese nationality, would be the King of South Vietnam.
At this time, Han Qianqiu's army entered South Vietnam and captured several small towns.
After that, the South Vietnamese simply moved out of the way and provided food and drink, allowing Han Qianqiu's army to advance smoothly. When they reached a place forty miles away from Panyu, the South Vietnamese attacked Han Qianqiu and others with troops, and wiped them all out.
Lu Jia had the Han Dynasty envoy's talisman packed in a wooden box, sealed it, placed it on the border fortress, said some nice and deceptive words to apologize to the Han Dynasty, and at the same time sent troops to guard key places.
So the emperor said: Although Han Qianqiu did not succeed, he was still worthy of being a pioneer among soldiers.
The emperor granted Han Qianqiu's son Han Yannian the title of Marquis of Cheng'an.
Zun Le, his sister was the Queen Mother, she was first willing to belong to the Han Dynasty, so Zun Le's son Guangde was granted the title of Longkanghou.
The emperor issued an edict of pardon and said: "The emperor is declining and the princes are trying their best to conquer the traitors. People will ridicule the ministers for not knowing how to punish the traitors."
Now Lu Jia, Zhao Jiande and others have rebelled, and they can safely proclaim themselves kings. I ordered the criminals and the sailors south of the Yangtze River and Huaihe River, a total of 100,000 people, to attack them.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuan Ding, Weiwei Lu Bode became General Fubo and led his troops out of Guiyang and went straight down to the Huishui River; Lieutenant Yang Pu, the Lord Commander, became the general of the building and ship, left Yuzhang and went straight down to Hengpu; two people who had returned to the Han Dynasty and were made marquises A South Vietnamese man became General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li and led his troops out of Lingling. Then one army went straight to Lishui and the other to Cangwu. He asked Chiyihou to use the sinners of Bashu to mobilize Yelang's soldiers and go straight to the Zoke River. In the end, they all met up in Panyu.
In the winter of the sixth year of Yuanding, General Lou Chuan led his elite troops to first capture Xunshan, then broke through Shimen, paid the warships and grain of South Vietnam, took the opportunity to advance forward, defeated the vanguard of South Vietnam, and led tens of thousands of troops to wait for General Fubo.
General Fubo led the pardoned sinners. The road was far away, and the date of rendezvous happened to be missed. Therefore, only more than a thousand people joined General Louchuan, so they moved forward together.
General Lou Chuan was in front and fought straight to Panyu.
Zhao Jiande and Lu Jia were both defending in the city.
General Louchuan chose a favorable place to garrison in the southeast of Panyu; General Fubo garrisoned in the northwest of Panyu.
Just when it was dark, General Lou Chuan attacked and defeated the South Vietnamese and set fire to Panyu City.
The South Vietnamese have heard the name of General Fubo in normal times, but now that it's dark, they don't know how many troops he has.
General Fubo set up camp, sent envoys to summon those who surrendered, gave them official seals, and then sent them back to recruit others.
General Lou Chuan fought hard and burned the enemy, but drove the rebels into General Fubo's camp to surrender.
At dawn, all the enemy soldiers in the city surrendered to General Fubo.
Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande had fled into the sea with hundreds of their subordinates at night and took a boat to the west.
General Fubo took the opportunity to ask the South Vietnamese nobles who had surrendered, and then he knew Lu Jia's whereabouts and sent people to hunt him down.
Su Hong, a former school captain who is now an officer of General Fubo, captured Zhao Jiande and was named Chang Haihou; Nanyue native Lang Guan Duji captured Lu Jia and was named Lincai Marquis.
Zhao Guang, King of Cangwu, had the same surname as the King of Nanyue. Hearing that the Han Dynasty troops had arrived, the Jieyang County magistrate named Ding of Nanyue decided to join the Han Dynasty. Weng, the governor of Guilin County in Nanyue, informed Ou Luo to surrender to the Han Dynasty. They were all sealed.
Before the troops of General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li, as well as the Yelang army so called mobilized by Marquis Chiyi, had arrived, South Vietnam had been pacified.
So the Han Dynasty established nine counties here.
General Fubo increased the number of fiefs, and General Louchuan's army broke through the enemy's strong defense, so he was granted the title of General Lianghou.
After Zhao Tuo first became king, the Kingdom of Nanyue was destroyed for five generations, a total of ninety-three years.
Tai Shigong said: Wei Tuo became the king of Nanyue because of Ren Xiao's promotion and persuasion.
Just as the Han Dynasty was initially stabilized, he was made a prince.
Longluhou led his troops to attack South Vietnam. They encountered a hot and humid climate. Many of the soldiers were infected with diseases and were unable to march, which made Zhao Tuo even more proud.
Due to mutual attacks with Ou Luo, South Vietnam's national power was shaken.
The Han Dynasty's army pressed on the territory, and the South Vietnamese prince Yingqi had to go to Chang'an to serve as a guard.
Later, South Vietnam fell, and the sign was that Yingqi married a daughter of the Hu family. Lu Jia's small loyalty caused Zhao Tuo to cut off the heir to the throne.
The general of the building and ship indulged his desires and became lazy, arrogant, dissolute and chaotic. General Fubo's ambitions were not in his favor, and he became more and more resourceful and thoughtful, which was a blessing in disguise.
It can be seen that the transition between success and failure is as unpredictable as Jiu Mo.
summary:
The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo (Zhao Tuo), was from Zhending. During the Qin dynasty, after conquering the six states, the Qin annexed Yang Yue, establishing Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiangjun, and resettled criminals there to live with the Yue people for thirteen years. Zhao Tuo served as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai. In the second year of the Qin dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai, fell ill. He summoned Zhao Tuo and explained that with Chen Sheng’s rebellion and the Qin’s cruel policies, the Central Plains were in chaos. He noted that Nanhai was remote and could be defended by mountains and sea, and suggested Zhao Tuo could establish a state. Ren Xiao appointed Zhao Tuo as acting captain. After Ren Xiao’s death, Zhao Tuo cut off roads, gathered troops, killed Qin-appointed officials, and replaced them with his cronies. Following the Qin’s fall, he annexed Guilin and Xiangjun and declared himself King Wu of Nanyue.

Emperor Gaozu of Han, due to the people’s exhaustion, spared Zhao Tuo. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, he sent Lu Jia to confirm Zhao Tuo as King of Nanyue, with an agreement for envoys and harmony with Baiyue. During Empress Lü’s reign, officials banned ironware trade with Nanyue. Zhao Tuo suspected King Changsha’s influence, declared himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue, and attacked Changsha’s border cities. Empress Lü sent General Zhou Zao to attack, but heat and illness halted the army. After her death, the Han stopped. Zhao Tuo expanded his territory to over 10,000 miles, bribing Minyue, Xiou, and Luoyue, and acted as an emperor.

In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, the emperor honored Zhao Tuo’s parents’ tomb and his cousins. He sent Lu Jia to rebuke Zhao Tuo for claiming the emperor title. Zhao Tuo apologized, citing fear of King Changsha and the queen’s actions, and claimed he used the title for self-comfort among barbarians. He pledged vassalage to Han, removed imperial trappings, and continued as a vassal. During Emperor Jing’s era, Zhao Tuo outwardly submitted but secretly kept the emperor title. He died in the fourth year of Jianyuan, succeeded by his grandson Zhao Hu.

Zhao Hu faced an attack from Minyue’s King Ying. He requested Han intervention, and Emperor Wu sent troops, leading to Ying’s death. Zhao Hu thanked the emperor but, advised by ministers, avoided visiting the capital, fearing captivity. He died as King Wen. His son Yingqi, who had married a woman from Handan and fathered Zhao Xing, became king. Yingqi hid his grandfather’s emperor seal, refused to visit the capital due to fear of Han laws, and died as King Ming. Zhao Xing succeeded, with his mother as queen mother.

The queen mother, who had previously committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, sought to submit to Han. Emperor Wu sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade them. The young king and queen mother agreed to become vassals, but Prime Minister Lu Jia, who had served three kings and held great influence, opposed. He feared losing power and plotted rebellion. At a banquet, the queen mother tried to provoke the Han envoy to kill Lu Jia, but the envoy hesitated. Lu Jia left, gathered troops, and refused to meet the king. The queen mother’s efforts failed.

The emperor sent Han Qianqiu with 2,000 troops to South Vietnam. Lu Jia rebelled, killed the king, queen mother, and Han envoys, and installed Zhao Jiande as king. Han Qianqiu’s army was ambushed and destroyed. The emperor then launched a large-scale attack in the fifth year of Yuanding, with generals Lu Bode, Yang Pu, and others leading forces from multiple directions. In the sixth year, Yang Pu’s troops captured Panyu, and Lu Bode’s forces accepted surrenders. Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande fled by sea but were captured. South Vietnam was pacified, and the Han established nine counties. The kingdom lasted five generations for ninety-three years. The historian notes that Zhao Tuo’s rise was due to Ren Xiao, and the kingdom’s fall stemmed from internal conflicts and Lu Jia’s actions.

translation:
General Wei Qing was a native of Pingyang County. His father Zheng Ji served as a minor official in the county and served in the family of Pingyang Marquis Cao Shou. He had an affair with Pingyang Marquis's concubine Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing.
Wei Qing's half-brother is called Wei Changzi, and his half-sister is called Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty in Princess Pingyang's family, so he pretended to be surnamed Wei. Wei Qing, whose given name is Zhongqing.
The eldest son of Wei changed his surname to Changjun.
Changjun's mother is Wei Yu.
Wei's eldest daughter is called Wei Ru, her second daughter is Wei Shaoji, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu.
Later, Wei Zifu's younger brothers Bu and Guang both pretended to be surnamed Wei.
Wei Qing was a servant of the Hou family in Pingyang. When he was a child, he returned to his father Zheng Ji's house, and his father asked him to shepherd sheep.
Zheng Ji's sons from his first marriage all treated him as a slave, not as a brother.
Wei Qing once followed someone to the living room of Ganquan Palace. A prisoner with an iron shackle around his neck came to Wei Qing and said, "You are a noble man. You will be a high official and a marquis in the future!"
Wei Qing smiled and said, "I was born of a slave. I would be satisfied if I didn't get beaten or scolded by others. How could I think of becoming a marquis?"
When Wei Qing grew up, he became a cavalryman of the Pingyang Hou family and often followed Princess Pingyang.
In the spring of the second year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by Emperor Wu.
Queen Chen Ajiao is the daughter of Liu Piao, the eldest princess of Tangyi. She has no sons and is jealous.
The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing.
At that time, Wei Qing was serving in Jianzhang Palace and was not yet famous.
The eldest princess arrested and imprisoned Wei Qing and wanted to kill him.
Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and some strong men snatched him out. For this reason, Wei Qing did not die.
When Emperor Wu heard the news, he summoned Wei Qing and appointed him as the supervisor of Jian Zhang, with the title of Shizhong. Together with his half-brothers, they all received high status, and the emperor's rewards for them accumulated as much as a thousand pieces of gold in a few days.
Wei Ru became the wife of Grand Servant Sun He.
It turned out that Wei Shaoer had an affair with Chen Zhang, so Emperor Wu summoned Chen Zhang and made him a noble person.
As a result, Gongsun Ao became more and more prominent.
Wei Zifu became Emperor Wu's wife.
Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor.
In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Wei Qing served as the general of cavalry and attacked the Xiongnu, marching out of the fortress from Shanggu; Sun He, the imperial servant, served as the general of light chariots and marched out of the fortress from Yunzhong; Gongsun Ao, the Dazhong doctor, served as the general of cavalry and marched out from Daijun; Wei Wei Li Guang served as the general of heroic cavalry and marched out of the fortress from Yanmen; each army had ten thousand cavalry.
Wei Qing led his troops to Fucheng and killed hundreds of enemies.
The cavalry general Gongsun Ao lost 7,000 cavalry, and the guard Li Guang was captured by the enemy and escaped. Both Gongsun Ao and Li Guang were sentenced to death, but they both paid ransom and were exempted from death penalty and became civilians.
Gongsun He also had no credit.
In the spring of the first year of Yuanshuo, Wei Zifu gave birth to a boy and was made queen.
In the autumn of this year, Wei Qing became a general of chariots and cavalry. He went out from Yanmen and led 30,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu, killing thousands of the enemy.
The next year, the Xiongnu invaded the border, killed the governor of Liaoxi County, captured more than 2,000 people in Yuyang County, and defeated the army of General Han Anguo.
The Han Dynasty ordered General Li Xi to attack the Xiongnu and send troops from Daijun; it also ordered the cavalry general Wei Qing to set out from Yunzhong and go west to attack the Xiongnu as far as Gaoque.
So he captured the Henan area and reached Longxi, captured thousands of enemies, seized 100,000 livestock, and drove away King Aries and King Loufan.
The Han Dynasty changed the Henan area to Shuofang County, and designated 3,800 households to enfeoff Wei Qing as Changping Marquis.
Wei Qing's lieutenant Su Jian had military merits. The imperial court also designated 1,100 households to enfeoff Su Jian as Pingling Marquis and sent Su Jian to build Shuofang City.
Wei Qing's captain Zhang Cigong had military merit and was named An Touhou.
The Emperor said: The Xiongnu rebelled against the laws of nature, violated human relations, violated the elders, abused the elderly, specialized in stealing, defrauded various barbarian countries, planned conspiracies, and relied on their force to repeatedly invade the borders of the Han Dynasty. Therefore, the imperial court mobilized troops and sent generals to combat their crimes.
Doesn't it say in the "Jing": The expedition against Xi'an went as far as Taiyuan, and the chariots and horses galloping out to build the Shuofang City.
Now the chariot general Wei Qing crossed the Xihe area to Gaoque, killed 2,300 enemy troops, captured all their chariots, baggage, and livestock, and was made a prince. He then went west to pacify the Henan area, patrolled the ancient fortresses of Yuxi, crossed Ziling, built a bridge across the Beihe, and launched a crusade. Puni, defeated Fuli, beheaded the enemy's agile and elite soldiers, captured 3,071 enemy scouts, caught the enemy's plot, cut off the enemy's left ear for credit, drove back the enemy's more than one million horses, cattle and sheep, preserved the army, returned to the division in victory, and granted 3,000 additional Wei Qing households.
The next year, the Huns invaded the border, killed Gongyou, the prefect of Daijun, invaded Yanmen, and plundered more than a thousand people.
The next year, the Huns invaded Daijun, Dingxiang, and Shangjun on a large scale, killing and plundering thousands of Han people.
The following year, in the spring of the fifth year of Yuanshuo, the imperial court ordered the cavalry general Wei Qing to lead 30,000 cavalry troops from Gaoque; Wei Wei Su Jian was ordered to serve as a guerrilla general, Li Ju, the internal historian on the left, was a strong crossbow general, Sun He, the imperial servant, was a cavalry general, and Li Cai, the prime minister, was a light chariot general.
They all went to attack the Huns. King Youxian of the Xiongnu was facing the soldiers of Wei Qing and others. He thought that the Han army could not reach here, so he started drinking.

As a school captain, he followed General Wei Qing to fight against the Huns.
In the fourth year of Yuanfeng's reign, he became General Bahu as a Taizhong doctor and garrisoned Shuofang.
After returning, he led troops to attack Kunming, but he had no merit and was stripped of his official seal.
General Xun Shen was from Guangwu, Taiyuan County.
He applied for an audience with the emperor because of his ability in driving, and was appointed as a servant and a school captain. He accompanied the general Wei Qing to attack the Huns many times.

Because Yang Pu, the captain of the ship arresting building, committed a crime, he was executed.

Tai Shigong said: Su Jian once said to me: I once blamed the general Wei Qing for being extremely noble, but the wise men and officials in the country did not praise him. I hope the general can follow the example of those famous generals in ancient times who recruited wise men, and work hard.
The general refused and said: Ever since Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi, and Tian Fan, the Marquis of Wu'an, treated their guests favorably, the emperor often gnashed his teeth and hated them.
It is the king's authority to get close to and appease the scholar-bureaucrats, to recruit talented people, and to abolish the unworthy ones.

summary:
Wei Qing, a native of Pingyang County, was the illegitimate son of Zheng Ji and a concubine of the Pingyang Marquis household. His half-sister Wei Zifu gained favor with Emperor Wu of Han, leading Wei Qing to adopt the surname Wei. As a youth, he served as a servant and shepherd, enduring mistreatment from his half-brothers. A prisoner once prophesied his future nobility, but Wei Qing dismissed it. He later became a cavalryman for the Pingyang Marquis.

When Wei Zifu entered the palace and became pregnant, Empress Chen, jealous, attempted to kill Wei Qing. His friend Gongsun Ao rescued him, and Emperor Wu subsequently appointed Wei Qing as a palace supervisor, elevating his status. Wei Zifu later became empress, and Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor.

In 129 BCE, Wei Qing led a cavalry attack on the Xiongnu, achieving modest success. Subsequent campaigns saw him capture the Henan region, driving out Xiongnu kings and establishing Shuofang Commandery. For these victories, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping. Further campaigns against the Xiongnu resulted in significant victories, including the capture of King Youxian's forces and vast numbers of livestock. Emperor Wu granted Wei Qing additional households and enfeoffed his sons as marquises, though Wei Qing humbly declined, crediting the emperor and his officers.

Wei Qing's nephew, Huo Qubing, emerged as a brilliant commander, earning the title of Champion Marquis for his daring raids. Huo Qubing's campaigns were marked by deep penetrations into Xiongnu territory, capturing kings and vast numbers of enemies. He became increasingly favored by the emperor, eventually matching Wei Qing in rank and power. Huo Qubing famously declined a mansion, stating, "The Xiongnu have not yet been eliminated, so I have no intention of considering private matters." However, he was known for his lack of concern for his soldiers' welfare, often discarding food while they starved.

After Huo Qubing's death, Wei Qing's influence waned. Wei Qing died four years later, and his descendants lost their titles due to legal infractions. The text concludes with a list of Wei Qing's and Huo Qubing's subordinates, many of whom became generals or marquises. The historian Sima Qian notes that Wei Qing, despite his nobility, refrained from recruiting scholars, fearing the emperor's displeasure, a principle Huo Qubing also followed.

Sima Xiangru was born in Chengdu, Shu County, and his courtesy name was Changqing.
When he was a boy, he liked to read and learn swordsmanship, so his parents named him Quanzi.
After Sima Xiangru completed his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name to Xiangru.
Initially, due to his family's wealth, he was awarded the position of Langguan, guarded Emperor Xiao Jing, and became a regular servant of martial arts, but this was not his hobby.
It happened that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty did not like Ci Fu. At this time, King Liang Xiao came to the capital to see Emperor Jing. He was accompanied by people who were good at lobbying, including Zou Yang from Qijun, Meicheng from Huaiyin, and Mr. Zhuang Ji from Wuxian. Xiangru fell in love with these people when he saw them, so he resigned from his official position on the pretext of illness and lived in Liang State.
King Liang Xiao asked Xiangru and other scholars to live together. Xiangru had the opportunity to get along with scholars and lobbyists for several years, so he wrote "Zixu Fu".
Just when King Liang Xiao died, Xiangru had to return to Chengdu. However, his family was poor and he had no occupation that could support his life.
Xiangru always got along well with Wang Ji, the magistrate of Linqiong County. Wang Ji said: Chang Qing, you have been away from home for a long time and are seeking an official position. It is not satisfactory. You can come to see me.
So Xiangru went to Linqiong and lived in the capital pavilion in the city.
The Linqiong County Magistrate pretended to be respectful and visited Xiangru every day.
At first, Xiangru still met each other with courtesy. Later, he lied about being ill and asked his entourage to refuse Wang Ji's visit. However, Wang Ji was more cautious and respectful.
There are many rich people in Linqiong County. For example, the Sun family of King Zhuo has 800 slaves, and the Cheng Zheng family has hundreds of people. The two discussed with each other and said: The county magistrate has a distinguished guest, and we are going to prepare a banquet for him.
The county magistrate was also invited.
When the county magistrate arrived at the Zhuo family, there were already hundreds of guests in the Zhuo family.
At noon, I went to invite Sima Changqing, but he refused to come, saying that he was ill. Linqiong ordered to see Xiangru not come and did not dare to eat. He went to greet Xiangru himself.
Xiangru had no choice but to come to Zhuo's house. All the guests were amazed and envious of his charisma.
When the wine was in full swing, the Linqiong County Magistrate stepped forward, placed the harp in front of Xiangru, and said, "I heard that Chang Qing likes to play the harp very much, and I hope to listen to a piece of music to cheer you up."
After thanking Xiangru, he played one or two pieces of music.
At this time, Zhuo Wangsun had a daughter named Wenjun, who was newly widowed and loved music. So Xiangru pretended to respect each other with the county magistrate, and secretly aroused her love with the sound of the piano.
When Xiangru came to Qiong, he was followed by carriages and horses. He was dignified in appearance, quiet and elegant, and very generous. When Zhuo Wang and Sun's family were drinking and playing piano music, Zhuo Wenjun secretly looked at him through the crack in the door. He was very happy and liked him very much, but he was afraid that he would not understand his feelings.
After the banquet, Xiangru asked someone to reward Wenjun's waiter with a large sum of money to convey his admiration to her.
So Zhuo Wenjun ran away from home at night and eloped with Xiangru. Xiangru and Wenjun hurried back to Chengdu.
When I entered the house, I saw nothing but four walls.
When Zhuo Wangsun learned about his daughter's elopement, he was furious and said: "My daughter is extremely unqualified. I can't bear to hurt her, but I won't give her a cent either."
Some people tried to persuade Zhuo Wangsun, but he still refused to listen.
After a long time, Wenjun felt unhappy and said: "Chang Qing, as long as you go to Linqiong with me, you can make a living by borrowing money from your brothers. Why have you made yourself so miserable?"
Xiangru came to Linqiong with Wenjun, sold all his carriages and horses, and bought a hotel to sell wine.
He also asked Wenjun to personally take charge of the wine shop business in Longqian, while he put on his calf-nosed trousers and worked with the employees, washing wine vessels in the busy city.
When Zhuo Wangsun heard about this, he felt so ashamed that he stayed behind closed doors.
Some brothers and elders talked to Zhuo Wangsun and said, "You have a son and two daughters. What the family lacks is not money."
Now, Wenjun has become the wife of Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of running away from home. Although he was poor, he was indeed a talent and could be completely relied on. Besides, he is a distinguished guest of the county magistrate, why do you despise him like this!
Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun 100 slaves, 1 million in money, clothes, bedding and various belongings when she got married.
Wenjun returned to Chengdu with Xiangru, bought land and houses, and became a wealthy family.
After a long period of time, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu County, served as a dog supervisor to serve the emperor.
One day, Emperor Wu read "Zixu Fu" and thought it was well written. He said: "I cannot be at the same time as this author."
Yang Deyi said: My fellow countryman Sima Xiangru claimed that he wrote this poem.
Emperor Wu was very surprised and summoned Xiangru to ask.
Xiangru said: There is such a thing.

Please ask me to write a poem about the emperor's hunting trip. After the poem is completed, I will present it to the emperor.
Emperor Wu agreed and ordered the minister to give him a pen and wooden slips.
Xiangru used the fictitious words "Zixu" to state the beauty of the Chu State; "Mr. Wu You" means that there is no such thing, and uses it to refute the Chu State for the Qi State; "Wu Shi Gong" means that there is no such person to clarify the principle of being the emperor.
