Therefore, Duke Zhou's achievements flourished during the reign of King Cheng, and his merits surpassed those of King Wen and King Wu.
Judging from its beginning and its end, there are no particularly outstanding achievements that can be compared with the current Han Dynasty.
However, Zhou people still went up to Liangfu Mountain and Mount Tai, established noble titles and gained a respected reputation.
The benevolence of the great Han Dynasty surged out like a fountain, spreading grandly and spreading in all directions. It spreads like clouds and mist, reaching up to the nine heavens and down to extremely distant places in all directions.
All living beings receive kindness, the harmonious spirit spreads widely, and the mighty spirit drifts away. Those who are near are like swimming in the source of grace, and those who are far away are like swimming in the last stream of grace.
The leaders of evil will be obliterated, and those in darkness will gain light. Even all kinds of animals were happy and turned around to face the Chinese court. Then, precious beasts such as Zouyu gathered in the garden, monsters such as Bailin entered the fence, selected a six-tasseled Jiahe in the kitchen for sacrifice, sacrificed a white lin with a branched horn, obtained the treasure tripod left by the Zhou Dynasty and the raised sacred turtles in Qishan, and summoned the divine horse from the swamp to ride the yellow. Ghosts and gods greet the gods and spirits and treat them as guests in the pavilion. Rare things, strange and extraordinary, infinitely varied. It's so admirable that all the auspicious signs are appearing here, but he still thinks that his merits are meager and he dare not praise the matter of being enshrined in Zen.
Once upon a time, when King Wu of Zhou Dynasty was crossing a river, a white fish jumped into the boat. King Wu thought it was a good sign of auspiciousness, so he burned the white fish as a sacrifice to heaven. In fact, this kind of talisman is very small, but because of it, I climbed Mount Tai. Isn’t it too shameful?
The Zhou Dynasty should not have enshrined Zen, but the Han Dynasty should have enshrined Zen, but did not. How far apart are the principles of advancement and concession?
So Grand Sima Jin admonished: Your Majesty nurtures the people of the world with benevolence, and conquers those who refuse to obey with morality. The princes of China are willing to pay tribute, and the barbarians all hold gifts to worship the emperor. The virtues are equal to those of the previous sage kings, and the achievements are the same. The good merits and achievements are generally harmonious. The signs of Fu Rui change in many ways. The periods of fulfillment will come one after another, not just for the first time.
I think the purpose of setting up altars in Mount Tai and Mount Liangfu is to hope that the emperor will come and confer honorary titles to compare with the glory of the previous saints. God's grace and blessings are intended to recommend to heaven with success. Your Majesty's humility and not conferring Zen are cutting off the favor of God, Mount Tai, and Mount Liangfu, making the royal etiquette incomplete, and the officials feel ashamed.
Some people say that the way of heaven is simple and obscure, so rare signs cannot be rejected. If you push it away like this, there will be no opportunity for Taishan to make a mark, and there will be no hope for sacrifices at Liangfu Mountain.
If the ancient emperors were glorified for a moment and then perished, then what else can the narrator say to future generations? And can there be a saying that the seventy-two emperors were granted Zen status?
If you cultivate your moral principles, God will grant you auspiciousness. If you follow the auspiciousness and perform the act of enshrining Zen, it cannot be regarded as exceeding the rites.
Therefore, the sage kings do not abolish the ceremony of Zen, but practice etiquette, respect the earth gods, sincerely appeal to the gods, carve stones on Songshan Mountain to record their merits, in order to commend the most noble status, promote the virtues of the Ming Dynasty, display their titles and honors, and bestow great blessings so that the people can be honored.
The act of enshrining Zen is majestic and grand. It is the grandeur of the world. The great cause of being a king cannot be underestimated.
I hope Your Majesty will preserve it.
Then, the Taoist skills of the recommended gentlemen were combined, so that they could be illuminated by the distant light of the sun and moon, so that they could display their talents as officials and concentrate on running political affairs. It is also necessary to correct the time of the day, narrate human affairs, expound the great righteousness, revise and polish the text, and make it into a classic book like the Spring and Autumn Annals. The old six classics will be followed and added to the seven classics, and spread endlessly, so that it can still inspire loyal and righteous people after thousands of generations, raise microwaves, fly the voice of wisdom, and deliver lush fruits.
The reason why the sages of the previous generation could always maintain a great reputation and were often praised was that when performing the ceremony of enshrining Zen, one should order the aide to report all the great meanings of the enshrinement to His Majesty for viewing.
So the emperor changed his expression as if he had some realization and said, "Okay, I'll give it a try!"
The emperor thought about it, summarized the discussions of the ministers, asked about the specific situation of Feng Chan, recorded the greatness of the favor, and deduced the richness of Fu Rui.
So he wrote a hymn saying:
The sky covering me is filled with clouds.
With universal dew and timely rain, the land can be traveled.
The water that nourishes all things penetrates into the soil, and all living things are nourished. A stalk of good grain bears six ears, so why not accumulate the grain I harvest? Not only does it rain, but it also moistens the earth; it not only moistens me, but also spreads widely.
Everything is bustling and happy, nostalgic and longing for everything.
Famous mountains should have a prominent position and look forward to the arrival of the Holy King.
King, King! Why not perform the ceremony of Zen?
Zou Yu, who is rich in literary splendor, likes my garden; its white texture, black pattern, and its appearance are lovable. Be harmonious and respectful, just like a gentleman. I only heard about its reputation in the past, but now I’m witnessing its arrival. There were no footprints left on the road, which was a sign of auspiciousness from heaven.
This beast also appeared during the time of Yu and Shun, and Yu and Shun prospered because of it.
The fat Bailin once played in the five fields.
It was the tenth month of Mengdong, and the emperor went to the suburbs to offer sacrifices.
Bailin galloped to the king's chariot, and the king used it to burn it to the sky, bringing happiness to heaven.
Before the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, there probably was no such strange thing.
The flexing and stretching yellow dragon ascends to heaven because of encountering holy virtues. The colors sparkle and shine.
The appearance of the dragon body will surely awaken the people.
It is recorded in the "Book of Changes·Tuan Zhuan" that this is the so-called chariot that the emperor was appointed to ride on.
Tian Fu Rui has made it clear that there is no need to warn him again.
It should be entrusted accordingly and tell the king to hold a Zen ceremony. Looking through the classics, we can see that there is a relationship between nature and human society, and the two inspire each other and are harmonious.
The virtue of a wise king is to act conscientiously and cautiously.
Therefore, we must consider decline when we are prosperous, and be aware of danger when we are peaceful and happy.
Therefore, although King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou were in the highest position, they still maintained the virtue of seriousness and respect. During the ceremony, Yu Shun still observed and reflected on his shortcomings and mistakes.
That's the truth. Sima Xiangru had been dead for five years before the emperor began to worship the earth god.
Eight years after his death, the emperor finally offered sacrifices to Zhongyue Mountain first, then to Mount Tai, and then to Liangfu Mountain and Zen Suran Mountain.
Xiangru's other works, such as "The Book of the Marquis of Pingling", "The Dilemma with the Five Young Masters", and "The Book of Caomu" are not included, but his works that are particularly famous among public ministers are included.
Tai Shigong said: "Spring and Autumn" can delve into the most subtle aspects of things, "Book of Changes" is originally subtle but can be explained in a simple way, "Daya" talks about the virtues of princes and the common people, "Xiaoya" ridicules the gains and losses of humble authors, but its rumors can affect court politics.
Therefore, although the external manifestations of words are different, their gentle and enlightening effect is the same.
Although the similar articles contain many false words and exaggerated statements, their main theme is frugality. How is this different from the satirical remonstrance in the Book of Songs?
Yang Xiong believes that among Xiangru's gorgeous poems, there is a one hundred to one relationship between words that encourage luxury and words that advocate frugality. This is like playing the sounds of Zheng and Wei to your heart's content, but playing a little elegant music at the end of the piece.
Doesn’t this detract from the value of Xiangru’s words? I have collected some of his explanatory words and written them in this article.
summary:
Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. As a youth, he studied literature and swordsmanship, and later admired Lin Xiangru, changing his name accordingly. He initially served as a Langguan under Emperor Jing of Han due to family wealth, but disliked his post. When Emperor Jing showed little interest in rhapsodies (Ci Fu), Xiangru befriended scholars like Zou Yang and Mei Cheng during a visit from King Xiao of Liang. He resigned on pretence of illness and lived in Liang, where he wrote "Zixu Fu." After King Xiao's death, Xiangru returned to Chengdu impoverished.

Xiangru's friend Wang Ji, magistrate of Linqiong, invited him to stay. Wang Ji feigned deference, but Xiangru eventually refused visits, feigning illness. Wealthy locals, including Zhuo Wangsun and Cheng Zheng, hosted a banquet for the magistrate. Xiangru initially declined but attended after the magistrate personally invited him. During the feast, Xiangru played the zither, captivating Zhuo Wangsun's newly widowed daughter, Wenjun, who secretly admired him. After the banquet, Xiangru bribed her attendants to convey his feelings, and Wenjun eloped with him to Chengdu, where they lived in poverty with only four walls.

Zhuo Wangsun was furious and refused to support them. Wenjun suggested they return to Linqiong, where they sold their possessions and opened a tavern. Wenjun managed the shop while Xiangru worked publicly in menial tasks. Ashamed, Zhuo Wangsun, persuaded by relatives, eventually gave them 100 slaves, money, and belongings, enabling them to become wealthy.

Later, Emperor Wu of Han read "Zixu Fu" and admired it. Yang Deyi informed him that Xiangru was the author. Summoned, Xiangru offered to write a grander rhapsody about the emperor's hunting grounds. He composed "Shanglin Fu," using fictitious characters—Zixu (Chu), Mr. Wuyou (Qi), and Wu Shigong (the emperor's perspective)—to contrast princely extravagance with imperial virtue. The rhapsody described vast landscapes, hunting scenes, and concluded with a call for frugality and benevolence. The emperor was delighted and appointed Xiangru as Langguan.

Xiangru served as an envoy to blame Tang Meng for harsh policies in Ba and Shu, issuing an imperial proclamation reassuring the people. He later advocated for reopening southwestern territories, becoming Zhonglang General to pacify the region. Despite opposition, he succeeded, and the emperor was pleased. However, accusations of bribery led to his dismissal, though he was later reinstated as Langguan.

Xiangru suffered from diabetes and avoided court debates. He advised the emperor against dangerous hunting, writing a remonstrance. He also composed "Ode to the Immortals" and "Adult Fu," depicting celestial journeys. His final work, a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices, urged the emperor to perform these rites. The emperor later conducted them after Xiangru's death.

Sima Qian noted that Xiangru's works, though ornate, promoted frugality, akin to the "Book of Songs." Yang Xiong criticized their imbalance between luxury and admonition, but Sima Qian defended their value.

translation:
Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan.
During the period of Qi Jinggong, the Jin State sent troops to attack Qi State's Dong'a and Zhencheng, and the Yan State invaded Qi State's territory on the south bank of the Yellow River.
Qi's army was defeated.
Qi Jinggong was very worried about this. So Yan Ying recommended Tian Rangju to Qi Jinggong, saying: Although Rangju is the bastard of the Tian family, his literary talent can make everyone join him; his military strategy can make the enemy fear him. I hope the king can give him a try.
So Qi Jinggong summoned Rangju and discussed military and state affairs with him. After discussing with him, Qi Jinggong was very happy and immediately appointed him as a general and ordered him to lead troops to resist the armies of Yan and Jin.
Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials. The soldiers will not obey and the people will not trust me. If a person has little qualifications, authority cannot be established. I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army. That will be enough."
So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
After Rang Ju bid farewell to Jinggong, she made an agreement with Zhuang Jia: "We will meet at the camp gate at noon tomorrow."
The next day, Rang Ju rushed to the military gate first and set up a wooden watch and a clepsydra to wait for Zhuang Jia.
However, Zhuang Jia has always been arrogant and dignified. He thinks that he is leading his own army and he is the supervisor of the army, so he is not particularly anxious. His relatives and friends bid farewell to him and invited him to drink wine.
It was already noon, but Zhuang Jia had not yet arrived.
Rangju knocked down the wooden watch, broke the clepsydra, entered the military camp, inspected the camp, organized the army, and issued various rules and orders.
By the time he finished his deployment, it was already dusk when Zhuang Jia arrived.
Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time?
Zhuang Jia apologized and explained: My friends and relatives sent me off, so I was delayed.
Rangju said: As a general, you should forget about your family from the moment you receive an order. When you come to the army and issue the prescribed orders, you should forget about personal friendships. When you beat the drum and march, you should forget about your own life when the battle is urgent.
Now that the enemy's invasion has penetrated deep into the country, there is unrest in the country, the soldiers have been exposed on the frontline battlefield, and there is no place to hide, the monarch has trouble sleeping and eating sweetly, and the lives of the people in the country are hanging on you, so why talk about farewell!
So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded.
Zhuang Jia was very frightened and sent Pegasus to report to Qi Jinggong and ask him to rescue him.
Not long after the messenger left, but before he could return, Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies. The entire army was shocked and frightened.
After a long time, the envoy sent by Qi Jinggong came to pardon Zhuang Jia with the festival talisman. The carriages and horses galloped straight into the military camp.
Rangju said: "Generals are in the army, and they do not have to accept some of the king's orders."
He also asked the military judge: "What is the military law stipulating that driving a chariot and horse galloping in the military camp?" The military judge said: He should be beheaded.
The messenger was extremely frightened.
Rangju said: The king's envoy cannot be beheaded.
So he beheaded the servants of the messenger, cut off the wooden carriage on the left side, killed the horses driving the carriage on the left side, and paraded in front of the three armies.
He asked the envoy to go back and report to Qi Jinggong, and then set off.
The native soldiers set up camp, dug wells and set up stoves, drank water and ate food, inquired about diseases, and arranged medicine. Tian Rangju personally checked and cared for them.
He also used all the supplies and food he had as a general to entertain the soldiers. He and the soldiers shared the food equally.
Count up the weak and sick. Three days later, the army was reorganized and prepared for battle.
The sick and weak soldiers also asked to go to the battlefield together and competed to fight for him bravely.
When the Jin army learned of this situation, they withdrew their troops.
The Yan army knew about this situation and was dispersed as it retreated northward across the Yellow River. The Qi army took advantage of the situation to pursue them, regained all the fallen territory, and then led its troops in triumph.
Before reaching the capital, war preparations were lifted and wartime regulations and orders were cancelled. After swearing an alliance, they entered the capital.
Duke Jinggong of Qi led all the civil and military officials to greet him outside the city. After comforting the soldiers according to etiquette, he returned to the palace.
Duke Jinggong of Qi met Tian Ranju and appointed him as Grand Sima with great respect and admiration.
From then on, Tian's status in Qi State became more and more prominent day by day.
Later, the officials Bao, Gao and Guo were jealous of him and slandered and framed him in front of Qi Jinggong.
Qi Jinggong dismissed him from his official position, and Rangju died of illness soon after.
Tian Qi, Tian Bao and others therefore resented the people of the Gao and Guo families.
After that, when Tian Chang killed Duke Jian of Qi, he killed all the Gao and Guo families.
When Tian Chang's great-grandson Tian He arrived, he established himself as king and was named King Qi Wei. When he led his troops in battles and exercised his authority, he widely imitated Rang Ju's methods, and princes from all over the world came to Qi to pay homage.
King Wei of Qi sent officials to study and discuss the ancient "Sima's Art of War", and also included the great Sima Tian Ranju's art of war in it, so it was named "Sima Ranju's Art of War".
Tai Shigong said: When I read "The Art of War of Sima", I felt that it was grand, broad and far-reaching. Even the wars of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties failed to fully develop its connotations. It would be too much to recommend it if the text of "Sima Ranju's Art of War" is attached to it now.
As for Tian Ranju, he was just leading troops to fight for a small vassal state. How could it be compared with "Sima's Art of War"?
Since there are many "The Art of War of Sima" left in the world, I will not comment on them anymore and only write this "Biography of Sima Ranju".
summary:
Sima Ranju, a descendant of Tian Wan, was recommended by Yan Ying to Qi Jinggong during a crisis when Jin and Yan attacked Qi. Despite his humble status, Ranju’s literary and military talents impressed the king, who appointed him general. Ranju requested a trusted minister, Zhuang Jia, to supervise the army. They agreed to meet at the camp gate at noon. Ranju arrived early and set up timing devices, but Zhuang Jia, delayed by farewell feasts, arrived at dusk. Ranju condemned his lateness, citing that a general must forsake family, friendships, and personal safety in war. He executed Zhuang Jia under military law, shocking the army.

When Qi Jinggong’s envoy arrived with a pardon, racing into camp, Ranju declared that generals in the field need not accept all royal orders. He executed the envoy’s servants and horses, parading them before the troops. Ranju then personally cared for soldiers, sharing provisions and tending to the sick. After three days, the army was revitalized. The Jin and Yan forces withdrew upon learning of this discipline, and Qi reclaimed lost territory.

Returning in triumph, Ranju was appointed Grand Sima by Qi Jinggong, elevating the Tian family’s status. However, officials Bao, Gao, and Guo slandered him, leading to his dismissal and death from illness. The Tian family later retaliated, killing the Gao and Guo clans. Tian He, a descendant, became King Qi Wei, who imitated Ranju’s methods and incorporated his strategies into the “Sima’s Art of War.” Sima Qian notes that while Ranju’s achievements were for a small state, the “Sima’s Art of War” is profound, and he refrains from further commentary, presenting only this biography.

translation:
Lu Buwei was a big businessman in Yangzhai. He traveled around, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, so he accumulated a fortune worth thousands of gold.
In the fortieth year of King Zhao of Qin, the prince passed away.
In the 42nd year of King Zhao, King Zhao established his second son An Guojun as the prince.
Lord An Guo had more than twenty sons.
Lord An Guo had a concubine whom he loved very much. He made her his wife and called her Mrs. Huayang.
Mrs. Huayang has no son.
An Guojun had a middle-ranking son named Zichu. Zichu's mother was named Xia Ji, who was not favored.
Zi Chu was sent to Zhao as a hostage as the son of Qin.
Qin State attacked Zhao State many times, and Zhao State did not treat Zi Chu politely.
Zichu was the grandson of the concubine of the King of Qin and was a hostage in the State of Zhao. He was not rich in carriages, horses and daily necessities, and his life was difficult and very unhappy.
Lu Buwei went to Handan to do business. After seeing Zi Chu, he felt very fond of him and said: Zi Chu is like a rare commodity that can be hoarded.
So he went to visit Zi Chu and persuaded him: I can expand your family.
Zi Chu smiled and said: "For now, let's expand your own family first, and then come and expand mine!"
Lu Buwei said: "You don't understand. My family has to wait for your family to grow before it can grow."
Zi Chu knew what Lu Buwei meant, so he sat him down together and had an in-depth conversation.
Lu Buwei said: The King of Qin is old, and Lord An Guo was made the crown prince.
I heard privately that Lord An Guo dotes on Mrs. Huayang very much. Mrs. Huayang has no son, so only Mrs. Huayang can choose the prince.
Now you have more than twenty brothers, and you are ranked in the middle. You are not favored by the King of Qin and have been left as a hostage in the vassal states for a long time. Even if the King of Qin dies and An Guojun succeeds to the throne, you should not expect to compete with your eldest brother and other brothers who are by the King of Qin's side sooner or later.
Zichu said: That's true, but what should we do?
Lu Buwei said: "You are very poor and embarrassed, and you are living here as a guest. You can't give anything to your relatives and make friends with the guests."
Although I, Lu Buwei, am not rich, I am willing to spend thousands of dollars to lobby for you to the west, serve Lord An Guo and Mrs. Huayang, and ask them to make you the crown prince.
Zichu then kowtowed and thanked him and said: If your plan comes true, I am willing to entrust the land of Qin to share it with you.
Lu Buwei then gave 500 gold to Zichu for daily life and making friends with guests. He also took 500 gold to buy rare things. He took these things with him and went west to the Qin State to lobby. He first paid a visit to Mrs. Huayang's sister and dedicated all the things he brought to Mrs. Huayang.
By the way, I mentioned that Zi Chu was smart and virtuous, and he made friends with princes and guests all over the world. He often said, "I, Zi Chu, regard my wife as the same as the sky. I cry day and night and miss the prince and his wife."
Madame was very happy.
Lu Buwei took the opportunity and asked Mrs. Huayang's sister to persuade Mrs. Huayang: "I heard that if you use your beauty to serve others, once your beauty fades, your favor will also decrease."
Now, madam, you are serving the prince, and you are very favored, but you have no son. If you don't take advantage of this opportunity to make a capable and filial person among the prince's sons, make him his heir and treat him like your own son, then your husband will be respected when he is alive, and after his death, your son will succeed to the throne and he will not lose power in the end. This is what people say, and it will be beneficial for all generations.
Instead of laying the foundation when the appearance is beautiful, if you wait until the appearance fades and the favor is lost, even if you want to have a word with the prince, is it still possible?
Now that Zi Chu is capable, and he knows that he is in the middle, he cannot be appointed as heir according to the order, and his biological mother is not favored, so he will take the initiative to attach himself to Madam. If Madam can really promote him as heir at this time, Madam, you will be respected and favored in Qin all your life.
After hearing this, Mrs. Huayang thought it was so. While flattering the prince, she tactfully said that Zichu, who was a hostage in Zhao State, was very talented and everyone who came and went praised him.
Then he cried and said: I am lucky enough to be in the harem, but it is a pity that I have no son. I hope to make Zichu my heir so that I can have someone to rely on in the future.
An Guojun agreed, and he and his wife carved jade talismans and decided to make Zi Chu his heir. Both An Guojun and Mrs. Huayang gave many things to Zi Chu, and asked Lu Buwei to be his teacher. Therefore, Zi Chu's reputation among the princes grew.
Lu Buwei married the most beautiful woman from Handan who was good at singing and dancing. He lived with her and found out that she was pregnant.
Zi Chu once drank with Lu Buwei. After seeing the girl, he liked the girl very much, so he stood up and toasted to Lu Buwei, asking for the girl to be given to him.
Lu Buwei was very angry, but then he thought about it and realized that he had spent a lot of money on Zi Chu in order to catch rare goods, so he sacrificed this woman.
Zhao Ji concealed her pregnancy and gave birth to her son Mingzheng twelve months later.
Zi Chu made this concubine his wife.
In the fiftieth year of King Zhao of Qin, he sent Wang Jue to besiege Handan. The situation was very urgent and Zhao wanted to kill Zi Chu.
Zi Chu conspired with Lu Buwei and gave six hundred kilograms of gold to the officials guarding the city. They were able to escape and fled to the Qin army's camp before successfully returning to Qin.
The State of Zhao also wanted to kill Zi Chu's wife and son. Because Chu's wife was the daughter of a wealthy family in the State of Zhao, he was able to hide it, so the mother and son survived.
King Zhao of Qin passed away in the fifty-sixth year. Prince An Guojun succeeded to the throne as king, Mrs. Huayang became queen, and Zi Chu became prince.
The State of Zhao also escorted Zi Chu's wife and son Ying Zheng back to the State of Qin.
King Qin died a year after he succeeded to the throne, and his posthumous title was King Xiaowen.
Prince Chu succeeded to the throne, and he became King Zhuang Xiang.
King Zhuang Xiang honored his mother, Queen Huayang, as the Queen Mother of Huayang, and his biological mother Xia Ji was honored as the Queen Mother of Xia.
In the first year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, Lu Buwei was appointed prime minister, granted the title of Marquis Wenxin, and made 100,000 households in Luoyang, Henan, his food town.
King Zhuang Xiang died three years after he ascended the throne. Prince Ying Zheng succeeded him as king, respected Lu Buwei as the prime minister, and called him "Zhongfu".
The King of Qin was still young, so the Queen Mother often had an affair with Lu Buwei. Lu Buwei's family has ten thousand servants.
At that time, there was Lord Xinling in Wei, Lord Chunshen in Chu, Lord Pingyuan in Zhao, and Lord Mengchang in Qi. They all treated virtuous officials and made friends with guests.
And we have to compete in this regard. Lu Buwei thought that the Qin State was so powerful that it was a shame to be inferior to them, so he also recruited literati and bachelors and gave them generous treatment. There were as many as 3,000 diners under his disciples.
At that time, there were many talented debaters in various princely states, like Xunqing, who wrote books and established theories that were popular in the world.
Lu Buwei ordered his diners to write down what they saw and heard, and combined them into eight readings, six treatises, and twelve disciplines, totaling more than 200,000 words.
I think it includes the history of heaven and earth and all things from ancient times to the present, so it is called "Lu's Spring and Autumn Annals".
He published it at the city gate of Xianyang, with a reward of one thousand gold hanging on it, and invited tourists and guests from all over the world. If anyone could add or delete a word, he would be rewarded with one thousand gold.
Qin Shihuang gradually grew up, but the Queen Mother continued to be promiscuous.
Lu Buwei was afraid that the matter would be exposed and disaster would befall him, so he secretly sought out a man with a large penis, Lao Ai, as a guest. He often indulged in sexual pleasures and asked Lao Ai to run his penis through a small wheel made of Paulownia wood to walk. He also tried to let the Queen Mother know about this and use it to seduce her.
After the Queen Mother heard about it, she really wanted to possess him secretly.
Lu Buwei offered him Lao Ai, pretending to have someone accuse him of committing a crime worthy of castration.
Lu Buwei secretly said to the Queen Mother: You can let Lao Ai pretend to be castrated, and you can get him among the people working in the palace.
The Queen Mother secretly gave many things to the officials who presided over the palace punishment, and pretended to punish Lao Ai. She plucked out his beard and pretended to be a eunuch, so that he could serve the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother secretly committed adultery with him and was especially fond of him.
Later, the Queen Mother was pregnant. She was worried that others would know about it and pretended to have bad fortune. She needed a change of environment to avoid it, so she moved to the palace in Yongdi.
Lao Ai always followed him around, and received very generous rewards. Lao Ai decided everything.
Lao Ai's family has thousands of servants. There were more than a thousand people who came to Lao Ai's family in order to obtain official positions.
In the seventh year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, King Zhuang Xiang's biological mother, the Queen Mother Xia, passed away.
Queen Xiaowen was called Queen Mother Huayang and was buried in Shouling together with King Xiaowen.
The Empress Dowager Xia's son, King Zhuang Xiang, was buried in Zhiyang, so the Empress Dowager Xia was buried separately to the east of Duyuan. She once said during her lifetime: You can see my son to the east, and my husband to the west.
In a hundred years, there will definitely be a city with ten thousand households nearby.
In the ninth year of Emperor Qin Shihuang's reign, someone reported that Lao Ai was not actually a eunuch. He often had fornications with the Queen Mother and gave birth to two sons. They hid them. He also conspired with the Queen Mother that if the King of Qin died, we would support our son to succeed him.
So Qin Shihuang ordered relevant officials to investigate the matter strictly and find out all the truth. The matter implicated Prime Minister Lu Buwei.
In September of that year, he killed all the three tribes of the Lao Ai family, killed the two sons born to the Queen Mother, and moved the Queen Mother to live in Yongdi.
The diners of Lao Ai's family had their property confiscated and moved to Shu.
The King of Qin wanted to kill the Prime Minister Lu Buwei, but because of his great service to the late king and the many guests and debaters who interceded and put in good words for him, the King of Qin could not bear to bring him to justice.
In October of the 10th year of Qin Shihuang's reign, Lu Buwei was dismissed from the post of prime minister.
When Mao Jiao, a native of Qi, persuaded the King of Qin, the King of Qin went to Yongdi to welcome the Queen Mother and made her return to Xianyang, but sent Lu Buwei out of the capital to the fiefdom in Henan.
More than a year later, guests and envoys from various vassal states came in an endless stream to visit Lu Buwei.
The King of Qin was afraid that he would launch a rebellion, so he wrote to Lu Buwei: "What contribution have you made to Qin?"
The State of Qin granted you a grant in Henan, with a settlement of 100,000 households.
What is your relationship with King Qin?
He is actually called Zhongfu.
You and your family will all move to Shu!
When Lu Buwei thought that he was gradually being persecuted and feared that he would be killed in the future, he drank poisonous wine and committed suicide.
Lu Buwei and Lao Ai, whom the King of Qin hated, were both dead, so he ordered all Lao Ai's followers who had migrated to Shu to move back to Kyoto.
In the 19th year of Qin Shihuang's reign, the Queen Mother passed away and was given the posthumous title of Emperor Queen Mother. He was buried in Zhiyang together with King Zhuang Xiang.
Tai Shigong said: Lu Buwei brought along with Lao Ai Guixian, and Lu Buwei was given the title of Marquis Wenxin.
Someone reported on Lao Ai, and Lao Ai heard about it.
Qin Shihuang inquired about it, but the matter was not revealed yet.
When the King of Qin went to Yongdi to offer sacrifices to heaven, Lao Ai was afraid of the imminent disaster, so she conspired with her close associates to steal the Queen Mother's seal and mobilize soldiers to rebel in Qinian Palace.
The King of Qin mobilized officers and soldiers to attack Lao Ai, but Lao Ai failed and escaped. He chased him to Hao'an and beheaded him, and then beheaded his entire family.
And Lu Buwei was reprimanded as a result.
The "hearing" that Confucius mentioned refers to people like Lu Buwei!
summary:
Lu Buwei, a wealthy merchant from Yangzhai, amassed a fortune through low-cost buying and high-price selling. During the reign of King Zhao of Qin, the crown prince died, and An Guojun was appointed as the new prince. An Guojun had many sons, including Zichu, a middle-ranking son sent as a hostage to Zhao. Zichu, neglected and impoverished, caught Lu Buwei's attention. Lu Buwei saw him as a rare commodity to be hoarded and offered to help him gain power.

Lu Buwei traveled to Qin to lobby An Guojun and his favored concubine, Mrs. Huayang, who had no son. He persuaded Mrs. Huayang to adopt Zichu as her heir, ensuring her future influence. An Guojun agreed, and Zichu became the designated heir. Lu Buwei gave Zichu funds and married him to a beautiful dancer, Zhao Ji, who bore a son, Ying Zheng.

During a siege of Handan, Zichu escaped to Qin with Lu Buwei's help. After King Zhao's death, An Guojun became king, and Zichu became prince. An Guojun died shortly after, and Zichu ascended as King Zhuang Xiang, appointing Lu Buwei as prime minister. King Zhuang Xiang died three years later, and Ying Zheng became king, with Lu Buwei as regent.

Lu Buwei, competing with other lords, hosted 3,000 scholars and compiled the *Lüshi Chunqiu*, a comprehensive text. He later introduced Lao Ai, a man with a large penis, to the Queen Mother, who had an affair with him. Lao Ai gained power and fathered two sons with her. When discovered, Lao Ai rebelled but was executed. Lu Buwei was implicated, dismissed, and exiled. Fearing further persecution, he committed suicide by drinking poison.

translation:
King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, the brother of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Seven years after Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, he named Liu Zhong the acting king.
Later, when the Xiongnu attacked Dai, Liu Zhong could not hold on, so he abandoned the country and fled. He took a small road to Luoyang and surrendered to the emperor.
Because the emperor was a brother of flesh and blood, he could not bear to be punished according to law, so he only deposed the king and demoted him to be the Marquis of Heyang.
In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Zhunnan rebelled, annexed the Jing territory to the east, hijacked the troops of the local princes, crossed the Huai River to the west, and attacked Chu State. Emperor Gaozu personally led the army to punish him.
Liu Zhong's son, Peihou Liu Bi, was twenty years old and strong. As a cavalry commander, he followed Gaozu and defeated Yingbu's army at Huizhen in the west of Qixian County. Yingbu fled.
King Liu Jia of Jing was killed by Yingbu and had no heirs.
The emperor was worried that the people in Wu and Kuaiji were frivolous and aggressive, and there was no brave king to restrain them. His sons were young, so he made Liu Bi the king of Wu in Pei, with jurisdiction over three counties and fifty-three counties.
After he had received his official seal, Emperor Gaozu asked Liu Bi to come and see him. After seeing him, he said: "You have a rebellious appearance."
At the same time, he felt regret in his heart, but he had already appointed him, so he patted him on the back and warned him: "There will be a rebellion in the southeast in the fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty. Is it you?"
However, everyone with the same surname is one family, so you must not rebel!
Liu Bi kowtowed and said, "I don't dare."
By the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, the world had just stabilized, and the princes of some counties were working hard to appease their own people.
Wu State owned the copper mines in Yuzhang County, so Liu Bi recruited desperadoes from all over the world to mint money privately and boil seawater to make salt. Because of this, the state did not levy taxes and the state expenses were very abundant.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Crown Prince of Wu came to Beijing for an audience and was able to accompany the Crown Prince to drink and play chess.
Prince Wu's teachers were both from Chu. They were frivolous, strong, and arrogant. When they were playing chess with the crown prince, they had an argument over the chess game and their attitude was disrespectful. The crown prince picked up the chessboard and threw the chessboard at Prince Wu, killing him. Afterwards, his body was sent back to Wu for burial.
When they arrived at the state of Wu, King Wu said angrily: If a family with the same surname in the world died in Chang'an, they should be buried in Chang'an. Why should they be sent to the state of Wu for burial?
The body was then sent to Chang'an for burial.
From then on, the King of Wu gradually disobeyed the etiquette that his vassals should abide by, claiming to be ill and refusing to enter the court.
The people in the capital knew that he claimed to be ill and refused to enter the court because his son had died. After questioning, he was indeed not ill. After that, when the envoys of the King of Wu came, they detained him, questioned him, and punished him.
The King of Wu was frightened and even more actively planned rebellion.
Later, the King of Wu sent someone to Beijing for the autumn invitation, and the emperor questioned the envoy again. The envoy told the emperor: The King of Wu is indeed not sick. The imperial court detained and punished several envoys, so he claimed that he was ill and could not come back.
And there is such a thing: it is unlucky to see fish in a deep pool.
Now the King of Wu began to pretend to be sick. When the court noticed and was severely questioned, he became more and more eager to conceal his behavior for fear that the emperor would kill him. The plan of claiming to be sick was out of helplessness.
It is hoped that the emperor will put aside his past grudges and give King Wu a chance to start over.
So the emperor pardoned Wu's envoys and allowed them to go back. He also gave King Wu a few swords and a staff, thinking that he was old and could not go to the capital to see him.
The king of Wu was able to absolve him of his sins, and the rebellion was relaxed.
However, the feudal state where he was located had no income from copper salt, so the people did not pay taxes.
Soldiers are paid in lieu of service and the price is fair.
At a certain time every year, they visit talented people and give rewards to common people.
The king of Wu took in fugitives who were wanted by law officials from other counties and did not hand them over.
After doing this for more than forty years, the king of Wu was able to control and utilize his people.
Chao Cuo served as the prince's family order and gained the prince's favor. He encouraged the prince many times to say that the king of Wu was guilty and his fiefdom should be reduced.
He also wrote many times to persuade Emperor Wen. Emperor Wen was generous and could not bear to punish him, so King Wu became even more arrogant.
When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo became the imperial censor, and advised the emperor: In the past, when Emperor Gaozu had just settled the world, he had few brothers and young sons, so he widely enfeoffed people with the same surname. Therefore, his concubine, King Tuohui, was granted the title of King of Qi and ruled over more than 70 counties.
Now, because of the suspicion that his son had been beaten to death in the past, King Wu pretended to be ill and refused to go to the capital to see him. According to ancient laws, he deserved to be killed. Emperor Wen couldn't bear it, so he rewarded him with a seat and a cane.
He was very kind to him and should have reformed.
But he became even more arrogant and excessive, casting coins from copper mines, boiling sea water to make salt, seducing desperadoes from all over the world, and plotting rebellion.
Cutting him off now is also a rebellion, and not cutting him down is also a rebellion.
If you reduce it, it will be done quickly and the disaster will be small; if you don't reduce it, it will be done late and the disaster will be great.
In the winter of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, the King of Chu came to court. Chao Cuo took this opportunity to say that when King Liu Wu of Chu was in mourning for Empress Dowager Bo last year, he had secretly committed adultery in the house where he lived in mourning, and requested that he be killed.
Emperor Jing issued an edict to pardon his death penalty, but only reduced Donghai County as punishment.
Subsequently, Wu's Yuzhang County and Kuaiji County were reduced.
Two years ago, King Zhao reduced his Hejian County because of his guilt.
Liu Xuan, the king of Jiaoxi, reduced his six counties due to fraud in the sale of titles.
The ministers of the Han Dynasty were discussing reducing King Wu's land.
Wu King Liu Bi was worried that there would be no end to the land expropriation, so he wanted to take the opportunity to reveal his plot and raise an army to attack.
He also thought that there was no one among the princes who could make plans together, and knew that the King of Jiaoxi was brave and eager to fight for victory. Several princes and kings in the same area were afraid of him, so he sent Ying Gao, the middle official, to seduce the King of Jiaoxi.
There is no letter, but a verbal notification: The King of Wu is not talented and has worries that will come soon. He does not dare to treat himself as an outsider, so that you can understand his good intentions.
King Jiaoxi said: Any advice?
Ying Gao said: Now the emperor appoints ministers, is deceived by evil ministers, likes the immediate interests, listens to slander, changes laws without authorization, seizes the fiefdoms of princes, demands more and more fiefdoms, and kills and punishes good people. These situations are becoming more and more serious.
As the saying goes: After eating rice bran, you will eat rice.
The King of Wu and the King of Jiaoxi are famous princes. Once they are noticed, they may not be able to live in peace and freedom.
The King of Wu suffered from internal illness and had been unable to see the emperor for more than twenty years. He was once worried about being suspected and had no way to explain it. Now he hunched his shoulders and walked in small steps, still afraid of not being understood.
I heard that the king was punished for selling his title. I heard that the feudal lords had their fiefdoms reduced. The crime should not be punished in this way. I am afraid that this kind of punishment can only end with the loss of land.
King Jiaoxi said: Yes, there is such a thing.
What do you think we should do?
Ying Gao said: Those who hate each other help each other, those who have the same hobbies stay with each other, those with the same emotions help each other, those who have the same desires pursue the same, and those with the same interests die together.
Now the King of Wu thinks that he has the same worries as the King. He is willing to take the opportunity to comply with the situation and sacrifice his body to eliminate harm to the world. Can you think about it?
King Jiaoxi said in surprise: How dare I do this?
Although the emperor is now threatening and urgent, I am already guilty of capital punishment. How can I not support him?
Ying Gao said: Chao Cuo, the imperial censor, deceived the emperor, invaded the princes, and blocked the loyal and virtuous people. All the ministers in the court felt hatred and resentment, and the princes all had the intention of betrayal. He has done his best to serve the people.
Now comets appear and locust plagues continue to occur. This is the only opportunity that comes once in a lifetime, and the time of sorrow and labor is the era when saints are born.
Therefore, the king of Wu wanted to use the crusade against Chao Cuo as an excuse at home, and follow the king's chariot outside, galloping around the world, making the places he faced surrender, and conquering the places pointed by his fingers. No one in the world dared to disobey.
If your Majesty can promise me a word, then the King of Wu will lead the King of Chu to capture Hangu Pass, guard the grain of Aocang in Xingyang, and resist the Han soldiers.
Build a house for the army to be stationed and wait for the arrival of the king.
If the king really comes, then the world can be annexed. Isn't it also possible for two monarchs to divide and rule the world?
King Jiaoxi said: OK.
Ying Gao went back to report to the King of Wu. The King of Wu was still worried that the King of Jiaoxi would not participate in the rebellion, so he personally acted as an envoy to Jiaoxi and made an alliance with the King of Jiaoxi in person.
Some of the officials in Jiaoxi learned about King Jiaoxi's rebellion plan and advised him: "Serving an emperor is the happiest thing."
Now the king and the king of Wu are marching westward. If things succeed, the two masters will definitely have differences and disputes, and disaster will start from here.
The land of the princes is less than two-tenths of the imperial counties, and betraying the imperial court will also worry the Queen Mother. This is not a long-term solution.
King Jiaoxi refused to listen.
So he sent envoys to join forces with the King of Qi, the King of Sichuan, the King of Jiaodong, the King of Jinan, and the King of Jibei. They all agreed and said: For the sake of justice, King Chengyang Jing will attack those surnamed Lu. Don't let him participate in the army. After the incident is completed, just give him some land.
The princes were shocked and frightened by the recent punishment of reducing their land, and most of them resented Chao Cuo.
When the documents to reduce the Wu Guoji and Yuzhang counties were sent to the state of Wu, the king of Wu first launched an army to rebel. On Bingwu of the first month, the king of Jiaoxi killed the officials sent by the court with less than 2,000 shi, as did the kings of Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao, so they marched westward.
King Qi later regretted it and committed suicide by taking poison, violating the covenant.
The King of Jibei's city wall was damaged and had not been repaired, so his lieutenant ordered him to be kidnapped and guarded so that he could not send troops.
The King of Jiaoxi was the leader, and together with the King of Jiaodong, the King of Sichuan and the King of Jinan, they led troops to besiege Linyi.
King Liu Sui of Zhao also rebelled and secretly sent envoys to the Xiongnu to discuss joint operations.
When the Seven Kingdoms launched a rebellion, the King of Wu conscripted all his soldiers and ordered the whole country: I am sixty-two years old and personally command the army.
The youngest son is fourteen years old and also leads the way.
Therefore, people who are the same age as me, and the same age as my youngest son at the lowest level, all have to go to war.
More than 200,000 people were conscripted.
He sent envoys to Minyue and Dongyue to the south, and Dongyue also sent troops to follow the king of Wu.
In the first month of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, King Wu first set out from Guangling.
He crossed the Huaihe River to the west and joined the Chu army.
The letter sent by an envoy to the princes said: King Wu Liu Bi respectfully greets the king of Jiaoxi, King of Jiaodong, King of Suichuan, King of Jinan, King of Zhao, King of Chu, King of Huainan, King of Hengshan, King of Lujiang, and the son of the late King of Changsha: I hope to get your advice!
Because there are treacherous ministers in the court who have done nothing for the world, but they invade the land of the princes, send officials to impeach, arrest, interrogate and punish the princes, and only insult the princes. They do not treat the Liu family's relatives with the etiquette of princes and kings. They ignore the meritorious officials of the late emperor, promote and appoint bad people, confuse the world, and want to harm the country.
Your Majesty is frail, sick and mentally disturbed, and cannot clearly understand the political situation.
I want to raise an army to punish them, and I respectfully follow your advice.
Although our country is small, the land is only three thousand miles in radius; although the population is small, we can prepare 500,000 elite soldiers.
I have been serving South Vietnam for more than thirty years, and their monarchs have not refused to recruit and assign soldiers to follow me into the army, and I can get more than three hundred thousand people.
Although I am not talented, I am willing to follow all the princes personally.
Yue is bordering Changsha. They can follow the son of the King of Changsha to pacify the north of Changsha, and then attack Shu and Hanzhong westward.
I sent people to tell the King of Dongyue, the King of Chu, and the King of Huainan to attack westward with me. After the kings of Qi and King Zhao pacified Hejian and Hanoi, some of them entered Linjin Pass and some joined me in Luoyang. King Yan and King Zhao originally had an alliance with the Xiongnu.
I hope everyone will work hard.
The sons of King Yuan of Chu, King Huainan, King Hengshan, and King Lujiang of Huainan have been focusing on their own affairs for more than ten years. Their resentment has been deeply rooted in their bones and they have wanted to take action for a long time. However, I do not know the kings' intentions and dare not obey orders.
Now if the princes can preserve and perpetuate the country that is about to be extinct, support the weak and hoe the strong, and stabilize the Liu family, this is what the Ancestral Temple Sheji hopes.
Although our country is poor, I have saved the cost of food and clothing, saved money, repaired weapons and armor, and accumulated food, working day and night for more than thirty years, all for today. I hope all the kings will work hard to take advantage of these conditions.
Anyone who captures and kills a general will be rewarded with five thousand catties of gold and ten thousand households; whoever captures and kills a general will be rewarded with three thousand catties of gold and five thousand households; whoever captures and kills a deputy general will be rewarded with two thousand catties of gold and two thousand households. If an official with a salary of two thousand dan is arrested and killed, he will be rewarded with a thousand catties of gold and a thousand households with food. If an official with a salary of one thousand dan is arrested, he will be rewarded with 500 catties of gold and 500 households with a fief. Those who have meritorious service above can be made marquises.
Those who surrendered with an army or a city with ten thousand soldiers and ten thousand households in the city were treated like generals; soldiers with five thousand households in the city were treated like generals; soldiers with three thousand households in the city were treated like lieutenants; soldiers with one thousand households in the city were treated like officials with two thousand stones; those small officials who surrendered also received titles and rewards according to their positions.
Other rewards were doubled as stipulated by the Han Dynasty.
The number of people in the original enfeoffed cities will only increase and will not remain the same.
I hope that the kings will clearly declare to the scholar-bureaucrats that I dare not deceive them.
My money is available everywhere in the world, and I don't necessarily have to come to Wu to get it. The kings can use it day and night and they can't use it up.
Someone who deserves a reward tells me that I will go and give it to him.
Respectfully inform the kings.
After the emperor was notified of the rebellion of the seven kingdoms, the emperor sent Taiwei Tiaohou Zhou Yafu to lead thirty-six generals to attack Wu and Chu; he sent Qu Zhouhou Liji to attack Zhao; general Luan Bu attacked Qi; General Dou Ying was stationed in Xingyang to monitor the armies of Qi and Zhao.
When Wu Chu and other rebellious letters were heard, the Han Dynasty's army had not yet set off, and Dou Ying had not yet set out to praise Yuan An, the prime minister of the former King of Wu, to the emperor.
Yuan Ang was relaxing at home at the time, and the emperor summoned him to see him.
The emperor was planning the army and rations with Chao Cuo. The emperor asked Yuan Ang: "You once served as the prime minister of the King of Wu. Do you know the character of Wu's minister Tian Lubo?"
Now that Wu Chu is rebelling, what do you think?
Yuan Ang replied: It's not worth worrying about, we can defeat them immediately.
The emperor said: The king of Wu relied on copper mines to mint coins, boil seawater to make salt, seduce the world's heroes, and raised his troops to rebel when his hair was gray. How could he launch a rebellion without a comprehensive plan?
Why do you say he can't make a difference?
Yuan Ang replied: It is true that the copper mines in Wu State are beneficial to boiling salt. Where can I get heroes and seduce them?
If King Wu can really get heroes, he should help King Wu do what is reasonable, and he will not rebel.
Those whom the King of Wu seduced were all scoundrels, treacherous men who fled to make money, so they seduced each other and rebelled.
Chao Cuo said: Yuan An’s analysis is correct.
The emperor asked: How can we come up with good countermeasures?
Yuan An said: I hope to reject the people on the left and right.
The emperor asked everyone around him to retreat, but Chao Cuo remained.
Yuan An said: Even a minister cannot know what I say.
So he dismissed Chao Cuo again.
Chao Cuo hurried to the east chamber to escape, and was very angry about this.
The emperor finally asked Yuan An again, and Yuan An replied: The letters exchanged between Wu and Chu said that the emperor Gaozu appointed the Liu family's children as kings and had their own enfeoffed lands. Now the traitor Chao Cuo has demoted and punished the princes without authorization, and deprived the princes of their land.
In the name of rebellion, they jointly attacked to the west and jointly punished Chao Cuo. They would stop fighting when the original fiefdom was restored.
The current strategy is to kill Chao Cuo, send envoys to pardon the sins of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, and restore the original reduced fiefdoms. Then the war can be over without blood staining the weapons.
So the emperor was silent for a long time and said: What is the real situation? I will not reject the world just because I love someone.
Yuan An said: There is no stupid plan of mine beyond this. I hope the emperor will seriously consider it.
So Yuan Ang was appointed Taichang, and Dehou, the son of King Wu's younger brother, was appointed Zongzheng.
Yuan Ang prepares his luggage secretly.
More than ten days later, the emperor sent a lieutenant to summon Chao Cuo and tricked Chao Cuo into taking a car to patrol the Dongshi. Chao Cuo was killed in Dongshi wearing the clothes of the previous emperor.
Then Yuan An was sent as Taichang to serve the ancestral temple, and Dehou as Zongzheng to assist relatives, to inform the King of Wu according to Yuan An's plan.
When they arrived in the state of Wu, Wu Chu's army had already attacked the Liang state camp.
Because Zong Zheng was a relative, he went to see the King of Wu first and told the King to kneel down and accept the edict.
When King Wu heard that Yuan An was coming, he also knew that he wanted to convince him, so he smiled and replied: I have become the Eastern Emperor, who else should I kneel down to?
He refused to see Yuan An and detained him in the army, hoping to force Yuan An to become a general.
Yuan An refused, so he sent people to surround and guard him, and were about to kill him. Yuan An was able to escape under the cover of night, left on foot, ran to King Liang's military camp, and then returned to the court to report.
Tiaohou took a six-horse carriage and met at Xingyang.
When he arrived in Luoyang, he saw Ju Meng and said happily: "The Seven Kingdoms rebelled. I arrived here in a carriage. I didn't expect to arrive safely."
I thought that the princes had already obtained Ju Meng, but Ju Meng had no intention of raising an army now.
I have taken Xingyang again, and there is nothing to worry about east of Xingyang.
When he arrived in Huaiyang, he asked his father, Jianghou's former retainer Deng Duwei, "How can I come up with a good strategy?"
The retainer said: Wu Bing is very energetic and it is difficult to win against him. Chu soldiers are impetuous and cannot maintain their vigor for long.
Now I propose a strategy for the general. It is better to lead the army to build a fortress in Changyi in the northeast and give up the Liang State to the Wu Army. The Wu Army will definitely attack Liang with all its elite troops.
The general dug deep trenches and built high fortifications to hold on, and sent lightly-armed troops to cut off the confluence of the Huai River and the Surabaya River and block the Wu army's food route.
Due to the stalemate between Wu and Liang, they were exhausted and their food supplies were exhausted. Then the troops that maintained their strength and vigor were used to subdue those extremely exhausted armies, and it was inevitable to defeat Wu. Tiao Hou said: OK.
According to his plan, he stayed in the south of Changyi, and then sent lightly-armed troops to cut off Wu's army's food routes.
When King Wu first sent troops, Wu Chen Tian Lubo was the general.
Tian Lubo said: If the army gathers together to march westward, it will be difficult to succeed if there is no other way to produce surprise troops.
I would like to lead 50,000 people, and go up along the Yangtze River and Huaihe River, gather the troops from Huainan and Changsha, attack Wuguan, and join forces with the king. This is also a strange plan.
Prince Wu advised: "My father takes rebellion as his banner. It is difficult to entrust such an army to others. What should I do if I entrust others to rebel too?"
Moreover, having an army to act alone has many other advantages and disadvantages that cannot be known in advance, and it will only harm yourself in vain.
King Wu did not agree to Tian Lubo's suggestion.
A young general Huan from the state of Wu said to the king of Wu: The state of Wu mostly has infantry, and infantry is suitable for fighting in difficult terrain; the Han army has many chariots and cavalry, and the chariots and cavalry are suitable for fighting on flat ground.
I hope that if the cities that the king passes through cannot be captured, he will simply give up and leave, quickly march westward to occupy the Luoyang armory, eat Aocang's grain, and rely on the dangers of the mountains and rivers to command the princes. Even if he cannot enter the pass, the overall situation of the world has actually been settled.
If the king is slow to advance and stays to attack the city, and the Han army's chariots and cavalry arrive and rush into the countryside of Liang and Chu, the matter will fail.
The King of Wu consulted the old generals for their opinions. They said: This young man's strategy for charging is okay. How can he know the far-reaching strategy?
So the King of Wu did not adopt General Huan's plan.
King Wu arbitrarily concentrated his troops and led the troops in person. Before crossing the Huaihe River, many guests were awarded the positions of general, lieutenant, marquis, and Sima. Only Zhou Qiu was not appointed.
Zhou Qiu was from Xiapi and fled to Wu. He liked drinking and had bad conduct. King Liu Bi of Wu despised him and did not appoint him.
Zhou Qiu paid homage to King Wu and said to him: Because I have no talent, I cannot serve in the army.
I dare not ask to lead the army. I hope that if you get a Han Dynasty talisman from your Majesty, I will be able to repay you.
The king of Wu gave him the talisman.
Zhou Qiu got the talisman and drove into Xiapi overnight.
When Xiapi heard that King Wu had rebelled, they all defended the city.
Zhou Qiu arrived at the guest house and summoned the magistrate of Xiapi County.
The county magistrate walked in and asked his entourage to kill him on the pretext of the crime.
Then he summoned the wealthy officials who were friends with his brothers and told them: King Wu's rebel army is coming. After arriving, the people in Shajinpi City will only have time to eat.
If you surrender now, your family will be saved, and talented people will be granted the title of marquis.
After these people went out, they told each other that all the people in Xiapi surrendered.
Zhou Qiu got 30,000 men in one night, sent someone to report to the king of Wu, and led his army to the north to capture the city.
By the time they reached Chengyang, the army had grown to more than 100,000 people and they defeated Lieutenant Chengyang's army.
Later, when he heard that King Wu was defeated and fled, he thought that no one would be able to achieve success with him, so he led the army back to Xiapi.
Before arriving, he died of a sore attack on his back.
In mid-February, King Wu's army was defeated and fled, so the emperor issued an order to the generals: I heard that those who do good will be rewarded with blessings by God; those who do evil will be rewarded with disaster.
Emperor Gaozu personally commended his merits and granted titles to princes. The titles of King You and King Mouhui were cut off. Emperor Xiaowen took pity on them and gave them special favors. He named Sui, the son of King You, and Yan, the son of King Mouhui, as kings. They allowed them to worship their ancestors in their ancestral temples and became vassal states of the Han Dynasty. Their kindness matched that of heaven and earth, and their light was as bright as the sun and moon.
King Wu Liu Bi violated kindness and morality, seduced the world's fugitive sinners, disturbed the world's coins, and refused to attend court in Beijing for more than 20 years, claiming to be ill. The ministers in charge petitioned many times to punish Liu Bi for his crimes. Emperor Xiaowen forgave him and hoped that he could change his ways and become a good person.
Now he actually made a covenant with King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Zhao, King Liu Xian of Jiaoxi, King Liu Piguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Sichuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong, and committed rebellious and immoral acts. He sent troops to endanger the ancestral temple, massacred ministers and envoys of the Han Dynasty, coerced tens of millions of people, killed innocent people indiscriminately, burned down civilian houses, dug graves, and was extremely cruel.
Now Liu Xun, the king of Jiaoxi, and others are even more rebellious and unruly, burning down the ancestral temple and plundering the royal utensils in the ancestral temple. I hate them very much.
I wore white clothes and avoided the main hall. The generals wanted to encourage the scholar-bureaucrats to attack the rebels.
When attacking a rebel enemy, it is meritorious to go deep into the enemy's army and kill as many enemies as possible. The captured officials must be killed if their salary is more than 300 dan and do not release them.
Anyone who dares to discuss the imperial edict or do not act in accordance with the edict will be punished by being cut in half.
At the beginning, the King of Wu crossed the Huaihe River and marched westward with the King of Chu. They defeated the Han army at Jibi and moved forward with great vigor.
King Xiao of Liang was afraid and sent six generals to attack King Wu. Two of King Liang's generals were defeated again, and the soldiers fled back to Liang.
The King of Liang repeatedly sent envoys to report the situation to Tiaohou and ask for help, but Tiaohou refused.
He also sent envoys to speak ill of Tiaohou in front of the emperor. The emperor sent people to ask Tiaohou to rescue Liang State, but Tiaohou still insisted on a strategy that was beneficial to him and refused to send troops.
The King of Liang sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, the younger brother of the Prime Minister of Chu who was killed for state affairs, as generals, and was able to slightly defeat the Wu army.
The army of the state of Wu wanted to march westward, but the state of Liang held on to the city. The army of Wu did not dare to advance westward, so they ran to the place where Tiaohou was garrisoned and met Tiaohou's army in Xiayi.
The Wu army wanted to fight Tiaohou, but Tiaohou stood firm and refused to fight. Wu's army was short of food and its soldiers were hungry. They challenged Tiaohou several times to no avail, so they attacked Tiaohou's camp at night and harassed the southeastern corner of the formation.
Tiaohou sent people to guard the northwest, and the enemy invaded from the northwest.
The Wu army was defeated. Most of the soldiers starved to death, and some defected and dispersed.
So King Wu and his men, thousands of strong men, fled overnight, crossed the Yangtze River and fled to Danyang, where they were protected by Dongyue.
There were about 10,000 troops in East Vietnam, and they also sent people to take in the deserters gathered in Wu.
The Han Dynasty sent people to lure Dongyue with huge profits. Dongyue deceived the King of Wu and asked the King of Wu to go out to comfort the army. He sent people to assassinate the King of Wu with a spear and halberd, put his head on his head, and sent an express train to quickly report to the emperor.
The sons of King Wu, Zihua and Ziju, fled to Minyue.
When the King of Wu abandoned his army and fled, his army collapsed, and most of them surrendered to the armies of Taiwei and King Liang one after another.
King Liu Wu of Chu was defeated and committed suicide.
The kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong and Sichuan of Qi besieged Linyi of Qi and could not capture it for three months.
When the Han army arrived, King Jiaoxi, King Jiaodong, and King Sichuan each led their armies back.
The King of Jiaoxi then sat on a straw mat, shirtless and barefoot, drinking water and apologizing to his mother, the Queen Mother.
Crown Prince Liu De said: The Han army has come from afar. I think they are already very tired. I can attack them. I hope to collect the remaining troops of the king to attack the Han army. If the attack fails, it is not too late to flee to the sea.
The King of Jiaoxi said: My soldiers have been dispersed and can no longer be mobilized.
Didn't listen to the prince's words.
Gong Gaohou, the general of the time, sent a letter to the King of Jiaoxi: "If you come to punish the unjust people under the imperial edict, those who surrender will have their sins forgiven and their original titles and lands restored; those who do not surrender will be killed."
What will your Majesty do? I am waiting for a reply to take appropriate action.
The King of Jiaoxi went to the Han army's camp and knelt bare-chested and begged: "I, Liu Xun, violated the king's law and disturbed the people, so the general came all the way to this poor country and asked to be punished for my crime of being cut into pieces."
Marquis Gonggao came to see him holding a golden drum and said: The king is suffering from the war. I want to know the reason why the king sent troops.
The King of Jiaoxi knelt down and replied: At that time, Chao Cuo was the emperor's minister. He changed the laws of Emperor Gaozu and usurped the land of the princes.
We thought this was unjust and worried that he would bring chaos to the world, so the seven kingdoms sent troops to kill Chao Cuo.
Now that we heard that Chao Cuo had been killed, we withdrew our troops and returned.
The general said: If your Majesty thinks Chao Cuo is not good, why don't you report it to the emperor?
Without getting the emperor's edict, he sent troops to attack the righteous princes who abided by the king's law.
From this point of view, your original intention is not to kill Chao Cuo.
He took out the edict and read it to him.
After reading it, he said: Your Majesty, please think about what you should do!
King Jiaoxi said: People like me deserve to die.
Just committed suicide.
The Queen Mother and the Prince also died.
King Jiaodong, King Sichuan, and King Jinan also died successively, and the feudal state was abolished and returned to the Han Dynasty.
General Li besieged the capital of Zhao for ten months before conquering it, and King Zhao committed suicide.
Because the King of Jibei was kidnapped, he was not executed and was moved to the title of King of Sichuan.
At the beginning, Wu King Liu Bi took the lead in the rebellion and led the Chu and Wu armies together, uniting the armies of Qi and Zhao.
In the first month of the year, the army started a rebellion, and in March the whole army was defeated. Only Zhao State was finally conquered.
Emperor Jing also named Pingluhou Liu Li, the youngest son of King Chu Yuan, as King of Chu, as the successor of King Chu Yuan.
Liu Fei, the king of Runan who moved to Wu, took over the original fiefdom of Wu and became the king of Jiangdu.
Tai Shigong said: King Wu Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu because his father was demoted.
The King of Wu was able to exempt taxes and support the people because he had the convenience of copper mines and sea salt.
The idea of ​​​​rebellion came from the death of his son.
He got into trouble because of a chess dispute, and eventually his country was destroyed and he died; he got close to the foreign Yue people and murdered his fellow clan, and finally he died.
Chao Cuo made great plans for the country, but disaster befell him instead.
Yuan An was good at contingency lobbying. He was favored at first, but suffered humiliation in the end.
Therefore, in ancient times, the land of the princes did not exceed a hundred miles, and the mountains and seas were not divided among the princes. If you don't get close to the Yi and Di, you will alienate your clan members. This was probably what you said to the King of Wu, right? Those who don't make plans will be punished. Isn't that what Yuan Ang and Chao Cuo said?
summary:
King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, brother of Emperor Gaozu of Han. After Gaozu pacified the realm, he named Liu Zhong acting king, but Liu Zhong abandoned his post during a Xiongnu attack and was demoted to marquis. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, Yingbu rebelled, and Liu Bi, then twenty, served as a cavalry commander, helping defeat Yingbu. Gaozu, concerned about the unruly people of Wu and Kuaiji and lacking mature sons, appointed Liu Bi King of Wu over three counties. However, Gaozu noted Liu Bi's rebellious appearance and warned him against rebellion, which Liu Bi denied.

During Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao's reigns, Wu prospered by minting coins from copper mines and making salt from seawater, avoiding taxes and attracting desperadoes. Under Emperor Xiaowen, a chess dispute led to the Crown Prince of Wu's death at the hands of the Han crown prince. The King of Wu, angered, buried his son in Chang'an and began feigning illness to avoid court, gradually disobeying etiquette. The court detained Wu envoys, prompting the King of Wu to plan rebellion. Emperor Xiaowen later pardoned Wu's envoys and granted the king leniency, easing tensions. However, Wu continued to harbor fugitives and control its people for over forty years.

Chao Cuo, favored by Emperor Jing, repeatedly urged reducing Wu's territory, arguing that rebellion was inevitable. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Chao Cuo reduced the lands of Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, and Wu. King Wu Liu Bi, fearing further losses, plotted rebellion. He sent Ying Gao to recruit King Jiaoxi, citing Chao Cuo's tyranny and promising joint action. King Jiaoxi agreed, and alliances formed with Qi, Sichuan, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Jibei. The Seven Kingdoms rebelled, with Wu conscripting over 200,000 men and gaining support from Dongyue. King Wu issued a letter to the princes, denouncing Chao Cuo and calling for a punitive campaign, offering rewards for capturing Han officials.

Emperor Jing responded by sending Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and other generals against Qi and Zhao. Yuan An advised killing Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, and Chao Cuo was executed. Yuan An then attempted to negotiate with Wu, but King Wu refused, declaring himself the Eastern Emperor. Zhou Yafu, following a strategy to avoid direct confrontation, cut off Wu's food supplies. Wu's army, led by King Wu, failed to adopt effective strategies, such as a surprise attack on Wuguan or a swift march to Luoyang. After a prolonged siege of Liang, Wu's forces starved and scattered. King Wu fled to Dongyue but was assassinated by Dongyue forces bribed by Han. Other rebel kings, including those of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, and Zhao, were defeated or committed suicide, and their states were abolished.

The rebellion lasted from January to March, with Zhao falling later. Emperor Jing reinstated some royal lines and granted Wu's territory to others. The historian concludes that Liu Bi's rebellion stemmed from his son's death and greed, while Chao Cuo's plans led to his own death, and Yuan Ang's strategies brought initial favor but eventual disgrace.
