translation:
Lord Shang was the son of the concubine Ji of the Kingdom of Wei. His name is Yang Yang and his surname is Gongsun. His ancestor’s original surname was Ji.
When he was young, Gongsun Yang was interested in the study of criminal names and magic. He served his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei State, and served as the middle concubine.
The uncle knew that he was a virtuous man, but he had not yet had time to recommend him to the king of Wei.
Just when the uncle was sick, King Wei Hui went to visit him personally and said, "What will happen to the country if something unexpected happens to your illness?"
The uncle replied: My bastard son Gongsun Yang is young, but he is talented. I hope that the king can hand over all the affairs of the country to him and let him govern.
King Wei Hui was silent after hearing this.
When King Hui of Wei was about to leave, the uncle withdrew his entourage and said: If the king does not use Gongsun Yang, he must be killed and not allowed to leave the country.
King Wei agreed to his request and left.
The uncle summoned Gongsun Yang and apologized: Just now, the king asked about people who could serve as prime minister, and I recommended you. Judging from the look on his face, the king will not agree with my suggestion.
I must first be loyal to the king and then consider the position of the minister, so I advise the king that if Gongsun Martingale is not appointed, he should be killed.
The king agreed to my request.
You should leave quickly, otherwise you will be captured soon.
Gongsun Yang said: Since the king cannot listen to you and appoint me, how can he listen to you and kill me?
In the end, he did not leave Wei State.
After King Hui left, he said to his attendants: "The uncle's illness is very serious, which is really sad. He wants me to hand over all the affairs of the country to Gongsun Yang, and after that, he persuades me to kill him. Isn't this very confusing?"
Shortly after Gongshu Zuo's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin ordered to search for talented people throughout the country in order to restore the hegemony of Duke Mu of Qin and regain the lost territory in the east. He went west to enter the Qin State and relied on Duke Xiao's favored minister Jing Jian to seek an audience with Duke Xiao.
Duke Xiao summoned Wei Yang and asked him to talk about state affairs for a long time. Duke Xiao fell asleep while listening and couldn't listen at all.
Afterwards, Duke Xiao was angry with Jingjian and said: "Your guest is a bully. How can you appoint such a person?"
Jing Jian again used Xiao Gong's words to blame Wei Yang.
Wei Yang said: I used the methods of Yao and Shun to persuade the king, but his mind could not understand.
A few days later, Jing Jian asked Duke Xiao to summon Wei Yang.
When Wei Yang met with Duke Xiao, he explained the way of governing the country incisively and vividly, but it was not in line with Duke Xiao's wishes.
Afterwards, Duke Xiao blamed Jing Jian again, and Jing Jian also blamed Wei Yang.
Wei Yang said: I used the methods of Yu, Tang, Wen and Wu to persuade the king, but he would not listen.
Ask him to summon me again.
Wei Yang met Duke Xiao again. Duke Xiao was very friendly to him, but he did not use him.
After exiting the meeting, Xiaogong said to Jingjian: Your guest is good. I can talk to him.
Jing Jian told Wei Yang, and Wei Yang said: I used the Five Hegemons' methods of governing the country to convince the king, and I saw that he was ready to adopt it.
If you summon me again, I'll know what to say.
So Wei Yang met Duke Xiao again, and Duke Xiao had a very good conversation with him. He unknowingly moved his knees forward on the mat, and they talked for several days without feeling tired.
Jing Jian said: How can you win over the king? Our king is very happy.
Wei Yang replied: I advised the king to adopt the imperial method of governing the country and establish a prosperous age like Xia, Shang and Zhou. However, the king said: The time is too long, I can't wait, let alone a wise king. Who doesn't want to be famous when he is in power? How can I be asked to wait in obscurity for decades or hundreds of years to achieve the great cause of becoming an emperor?
Therefore, I used the method of enriching the country and strengthening the army to persuade him, and he was very happy.
However, this cannot be compared with the virtues of Yin and Zhou.
Shortly after Qin Xiaogong appointed Wei Yang, he planned to change the laws, but he was also worried that people in the world would talk about him.
Wei Yang said: If you hesitate in action, you will not become famous; if you hesitate in doing things, you will not succeed.
Moreover, behavior that goes beyond ordinary people is often criticized by the world; people with unique opinions will definitely be laughed at by ordinary people.
Foolish people cannot figure it out after it happens, but smart people can foresee what is going to happen in advance.
You cannot plan the creation of new things with the people but you can share the joy of success with them.
Those who pursue the highest morality do not collude with the world, and those who achieve great achievements do not collude with ordinary people.
Therefore, as long as the saint can make the country strong and prosperous, there is no need to follow the old rituals; as long as it can benefit the people, there is no need to follow the old rituals. Duke Xiao said: Well said.
Qianlong said: That's not the case.
The sage imparts education without changing the folk customs; the wise man governs the country without changing the established laws.
If you follow the customs of the people and impart education, you will be successful without any effort; if you follow the established laws and govern the country, the officials will be accustomed to it and the people will be stable.
Wei Yang said: What Qianlong said is a secular saying.
Most people are content with old customs, while scholars stick to what they see in books.
It's okay for these two types of people to abide by the law, but you can't talk to them about reforms other than the established law.
The three dynasties had different ritual systems but they were able to unify the world; the five uncles had different legal systems but they were able to dominate each other.
Wise people make laws, and stupid people are restricted by them; wise people change rituals, and ordinary people are restricted by rituals.
Du Zhi said: Without a hundred times the benefit, the law cannot be changed; without ten times the effect, the old instrument cannot be replaced.
There is no fault in imitating the established laws, and there is no deviation in following the old rites.
Wei Yang said: There is no fixed way to govern a country, and it is beneficial to the country not to follow the old laws.
Therefore, Tang and Wu were able to rule the world without following the old laws, and Xia and Yin perished without replacing the old rituals.
Those who oppose the old laws cannot be criticized, but those who follow the old rituals are not worthy of praise. Duke Xiao said: Well said.
So Wei Yang was appointed as the chief of Zuo Shu, and finally the order to change the law was made.
Wei Yang ordered the people to be organized into ten families into one clan, and five families into one team, to supervise and report each other. If one family breaks the law, the ten families will be jointly punished.
Those who do not report evil will be punished by being cut off from the waist; those who report evil will be rewarded the same as beheading the enemy; those who hide evil will be punished the same as those who surrender to the enemy.
If there are more than two adult men in a family, the tax will be doubled if there are no separate households.
Those with military merit will be promoted and rewarded according to the standards; those who fight over private matters will be sentenced to different punishments according to the severity of the case.
Those who are committed to agricultural production and have a good harvest of grain and increased production of cloth are exempted from labor or taxes.
Those who were poor due to being engaged in industry, commerce or laziness had them and their wives confiscated as official slaves.
Those in the royal family who have no military merit cannot be included in the family roster.
The hierarchy of titles and titles was clarified, and each family occupied land and real estate according to their grade. The clothes and clothing of retainers and servants were determined according to the title and grade of each family.
Those who have military merit are distinguished and glorious, but those who do not have military merit cannot show glory even if they are very rich.
The new law was ready but had not yet been announced. Worried that the people would not believe it, Wei Yang erected a three-foot-long log at the south gate of the market behind the capital, and recruited people who could move the log to the north gate and rewarded them with ten gold coins.
The people thought this was strange and no one dared to touch it.
He also announced that anyone who could move the wood to the north gate would be rewarded fifty gold.
A man moved it away and immediately gave him fifty gold to show that he would do what he ordered and would never cheat.
New laws were enacted afterwards.
The new law was implemented among the people for a whole year. Thousands of people from Qin State came to the country and said that the new law was not suitable.
At this time, the prince violated the new law.
Wei Yang said: The new law cannot be implemented smoothly because the people at the top violate it.
The prince will be punished according to the new law.
The prince was the heir to the monarch and could not impose punishment, so he punished Gongzi Qian, the teacher who supervised his behavior, and Gongsun Jia, the teacher who imparted knowledge to him, with ink punishment.
The next day, all the people of Qin implemented the new law.
Ten years after the new law was implemented, the people of Qin were very happy. No one picked up other people's lost things on the road, there were no thieves in the mountains and forests, and every family was rich and sufficient.
The people have the courage to fight for the country and dare not fight for personal gain. There is order in the villages and towns.
The people of Qin who initially said that the new law was not suitable also said that the law was suitable. Wei Yang said: "These are the people who disturb the enlightenment, so he moved them all to the border areas."
After that, no one among the people dared to discuss the new law.
So Wei Yang was appointed as Daliang Zao.
He led the army to besiege Anyi of Wei State and forced them to surrender.
Three years later, the Qin State built a palace city in Xianyang and moved the capital from Yongdi to Xianyang.
It was ordered that fathers, sons, and brothers of the common people were not allowed to live in the same room.
Sporadic towns and villages were merged into counties, and county magistrates and county magistrates were set up. A total of thirty-one counties were merged and divided.
Abolish well fields and redraw the boundaries of farmland, encourage the reclamation of wasteland, and balance taxes.
Unify the national weights and measures system.
After four years of implementation, Gongzi Qian violated the new law again and was sentenced to death.
Five years later, when the Qin state became prosperous and powerful, the Emperor of Zhou gave the sacrificial meat to Duke Xiao of Qin, and princes from all over the world came to congratulate him.
The next year, Qi's army defeated Wei's army in Maling, captured Wei's crown prince Shen, and killed general Pang Juan.
Another year later, Wei Yang persuaded Qin Xiaogong: The relationship between Qin and Wei is like a person suffering from a heart disease. Either Wei annexes Qin, or Qin annexes Wei.
Why do you say that?
The Wei State was located to the west of the high mountains, with its capital in Anyi. The Yellow River was the boundary with the Qin State and it monopolized the geographical advantage east of Mount Wei.
When the situation is favorable, they will invade the Qin State to the west, and when the situation is unfavorable, they will expand their territory eastward.
Now, with the help of the king's virtuous and sage wisdom, Qin is prosperous.
The Wei State was severely defeated by Qi last year, and the princes betrayed it one after another. They can take this opportunity to attack Wei State.
Wei cannot resist Qin and will definitely retreat eastward.
Once it retreats to the east, Qin will occupy the dangerous terrain of the Yellow River and Huashan Mountain, and can control the princes and countries to the east. This is the great cause of the emperor to unify the world.
Qin Xiaogong thought it was right and sent Wei Yang to lead an army to attack Wei.
The state of Wei sent its son Yan to lead troops to attack the Qin army.
When the two armies met and confronted each other, Wei Yang sent someone to send a letter to the general of the Wei army, Gongzi Yan, writing: I had a good relationship with the young master at the beginning, but now you and I are generals of two hostile countries and cannot bear to attack each other. Can we meet the young master in person, conclude an alliance, have a few drinks, and then withdraw our troops, so that both Qin and Wei will be in peace.
Wei Gongzi Yan thought that Wei Yang was right.
The two made an alliance, and then held a banquet and drank wine. However, the armored warriors who had been ambushed by Wei Yang suddenly attacked and captured Wei Gongzi Yan. They took the opportunity to attack his army, completely defeated the Wei army, and escorted Gongzi Yan back to the country.
King Wei Hui's army was defeated by Qi and Qin many times, leaving the country empty. Wei was getting weaker day by day. King Wei Hui was very panicked, so he sent envoys to cede the Hexi region to Qin in order to seek reconciliation.
Wei then evacuated Anyi and moved its capital to Daliang.
King Wei Hui said: I really regret not taking the advice of Gongshu Zuo.
After Wei Yang returned from defeating the Wei army, Qin Xiaogong granted him fifteen cities in the Yu and Shang areas, with the title Lord Shang.
Lord Shang served as Prime Minister of Qin for ten years, and many princes and nobles resented him.
Zhao Liang went to see Shang Jun.
Shang Jun said: I can see you because of Meng Langao's introduction. Now I ask to make friends with you, is that okay?
Zhao Liang replied: I don't dare to hope.
Confucius said: Recommend the virtuous and those who are supported by the people will come; gather the unworthy, and even those who can become kings will retreat.
I am not talented, so I dare not obey my orders.
I have heard this saying: Holding a position you shouldn't have is called position greed, and enjoying a reputation you shouldn't have is called fame greed.
If I accept your friendship, I am afraid that I am greedy for both position and fame.
So I dare not obey my orders.
Shang Yang said: Are you unhappy with how I govern Qin?
Zhao Liang said: Being able to listen to other people's opinions is called cleverness, being able to self-examine is called Ming, and being able to restrain oneself is called strong.
Yu Shun once said: People who are humble are respected by others.
You might as well follow Yu Shun's advice without asking me.
Shang Yang said: At the beginning, the customs of Qin were the same as those of Rong and Di. Father and son were not separated, and men, women, old and young lived in the same room.
Now I have changed the culture of Qin, made them separate men and women, and made them live separately. I built a large palace and city, and made Qin look like Lu and Wei.
Do you think I am more capable in governing the state of Qin than Dr. Wuxi?
Zhao Liang said: A thousand sheepskins are not as valuable as a fox armpit, and a thousand people who follow the advice are not as valuable as one person who speaks out.
King Wu allowed his ministers to express their opinions frankly, and the country prospered. King Zhou did not like his ministers to give advice, so he perished.
If you don't object to King Wu of Zhou's actions, then please allow me to speak frankly in my poem without being blamed, okay?
Shang Jun said: As the saying goes, words that appear pleasant are like flowers, words that are true and sincere are like fruits, words that are bitter and unpleasant to the ear are good medicine for curing diseases, and words that are flattering are diseases.
If you are really willing to speak out and justly all day long, that will be the best medicine for my illness.
I will worship you as my teacher, why do you refuse to make friends with me?
Zhao Liang said: That Doctor Wuxi is a remote countryman from Chu State.
I heard that Duke Mu of Qin was a virtuous man, so he wanted to see him in person. But he didn't have the money to go, so he sold himself to the people of Qin, wearing a coarse short coat and feeding their cattle.
A full year later, Duke Mu of Qin found out about this and promoted him from the cow's mouth to the top of ten thousand people. No one in Qin was dissatisfied.
He served as the Prime Minister of Qin for sixty-seven years. He went east to conquer Zheng, supported the king of Jin three times, and sent troops to rescue Chu once.
Implement morality within the country. The country of Pakistan came to pay tribute; it governed the princes virtuously, and ethnic minorities from all over the world came to pay homage.
When Yu Yu heard about this situation, he came to knock on the door and seek refuge.
When Doctor Wuxi was appointed as the Prime Minister of Qin, he did not ride in a car when tired, did not hold an umbrella in the scorching heat, and traveled all over the country without accompanying vehicles or armed defense. His merits were recorded in the annals of history and hidden in the treasury, and his virtues were taught to future generations.
When Wu Xianfu died, both men and women in Qin State cried bitterly. Even the children did not sing ballads, and the people who were pounding rice did not make corresponding calls out of sorrow.
This is the virtue of Doctor Wuxi.
Now that you are able to meet the King of Qin, you rely on the recommendation of the King of Qin's favorite minister Jing Jian. This is not a reputation at all.
As the Prime Minister of the Qin State, if you build palaces on a large scale without benefiting the people, this cannot be said to be a contribution to the country.
Punishing the prince's master and using cruel methods to harm the people is accumulating resentment and accumulating disaster.
Educating the people is more deeply rooted in the hearts of the people than ordering them, and it is faster for the people to imitate the behavior of the superiors than to order them.
Now you are unreasonably establishing authoritative change procedures. This is not to educate the people.
You proclaimed yourself king in the south of Shangyu fiefdom, and used new laws to persecute the nobles of Qin every day.
The Sutra says: Rats still know how to be polite, but people have no manners. Since people have lost their etiquette, why don't they die quickly?
According to this poem, it really cannot be flattering to you.
Gongzi Qian has been in seclusion for eight years. You killed Zhu Huan and punished Gongsun Jia with ink.
"The Book of Songs" says: Those who gain the revitalization of the human heart will perish if they lose the human heart.
None of these things are popular.
As soon as you go out, dozens of vehicles are following behind you. The vehicles are all armored guards. Strong men serve as personal guards. People with spears and halberds run close to your vehicle.
If you lack any of these defenses, you will definitely not dare to go out.
"Shangshu" says: Prosperity depends on virtue, and destruction depends on force.
Your situation is as dangerous as the morning dew that will soon disappear. Do you still plan to prolong your life?
Then why not return Shang's fiefdom of fifteen cities to the State of Qin, go to remote and desolate places to water gardens and cultivate their own land, and persuade the King of Qin to reuse those talents who live in seclusion in the mountains and forests to support the elderly and raise orphans, so that father and brother can respect each other, rank according to merit, and respect virtuous people. Only in this way can peace be guaranteed.
You also want to covet Shang Yu's wealth, take monopolizing the political and religious affairs of Qin as an honor and favor, and arouse the resentment of the people. Once the king of Qin abandons his guests and cannot be in power, how many people will Qin want to arrest you?
The day of your death will come as quickly as you lift your feet.
But Shang Jun did not follow Zhao Liang's advice.
Five months later, Qin Xiaogong died and the prince ascended the throne.
Gongzi Qian and his gang reported that Shang Jun wanted to rebel, and the monarch sent people to arrest Shang Jun.
Shang Jun fled to the border crossing and wanted to stay in a hotel.
The owner of the inn did not know that he was Lord Shang, and said: Lord Shang has an order, and the owner of the hotel will jointly and severally sentence the people staying in the hotel without documents.
Shang Jun sighed longly and said: Alas! The legacy of enacting new laws has reached such an extent!
He left Qin and fled to Wei.
The people of Wei resented him for deceiving the young master Yan and defeating the Wei army, and refused to take him in.
Shang Jun plans to go to other countries.
The people of Wei said: Lord Shang is a fugitive from Qin. Qin is powerful, but its fugitive comes to Wei. It is impossible not to return him.
So he sent Lord Shang back to Qin.
After Lord Shang returned to Qin, he fled to his fiefdom of Shang. He and his subordinates mobilized the soldiers in the city to attack Zheng in the north to seek a way out. Qin sent troops to attack Lord Shang and killed him in Lingchi of Zheng.
King Hui of Qin divided Shang Jun into five pieces and showed it to the public, saying: Don't rebel like Shang Yang!
So he killed the whole clan of Lord Shang.
Tai Shigong said: Mr. Shang is a cruel and merciless person by nature. It should be considered that when he used the way of an emperor to persuade Duke Xiao, he relied on pretentious talk and it was not his own qualifications.
Besides, relying on the recommendation of the king's favorite minister Jing Jian, when he was appointed, he punished the prince Qian, deceived the Wei general, the prince Xian, and refused to listen to Zhao Liang's advice, which is enough to prove that Lord Shang was cruel and ungrateful.
I once read a book about Shang Jun's Kasai farming campaign, and the content is similar to his own actions.
But in the end, he got a bad reputation in Qin State for treason. There is a reason for this!
summary:
Lord Shang, originally named Gongsun Yang, was the son of a concubine of the Kingdom of Wei. As a youth, he studied criminal law and magic, serving under his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei. When his uncle fell ill, King Wei Hui visited and asked about a successor. The uncle recommended Gongsun Yang, but the king remained silent. The uncle then privately advised the king to kill Gongsun Yang if he was not appointed, to prevent him from leaving the country. However, Gongsun Yang refused to flee, reasoning that the king would not heed advice to kill him if he ignored advice to appoint him. After his uncle's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin sought talented individuals to restore Qin's former glory. He entered Qin through the recommendation of Duke Xiao's favored minister, Jing Jian.

Initially, Duke Xiao was unimpressed, falling asleep during discussions of ancient imperial methods. After several attempts, Gongsun Yang shifted to strategies for enriching the state and strengthening the army, which pleased Duke Xiao. Despite concerns about public opinion, Gongsun Yang convinced Duke Xiao to enact legal reforms, arguing that extraordinary actions often face criticism but are necessary for success. He was appointed as Zuo Shu Chang and implemented a new legal code, organizing households into mutual surveillance groups, rewarding military merit, punishing private disputes, and promoting agriculture. To build trust, he erected a log at the market and rewarded a man who moved it, demonstrating his commitment to the law.

The new law faced opposition, including from the crown prince. Gongsun Yang punished the prince's tutors, Qian and Gongsun Jia, with facial tattooing, after which the law was widely accepted. Over ten years, Qin prospered: lost items were not stolen, families became wealthy, and the people were courageous in public duty but avoided private conflicts. Gongsun Yang was promoted to Da Liang Zao and led campaigns against Wei, capturing Anyi. He later oversaw the construction of Xianyang, reorganized territories into counties, abolished well-fields, and standardized weights and measures.

After further victories, Gongsun Yang persuaded Duke Xiao to attack Wei, exploiting Wei's recent defeat by Qi. He tricked Wei's general, Gongzi Yan, into a meeting, captured him, and defeated the Wei army. King Wei Hui ceded land and regretted not heeding the uncle's advice. Gongsun Yang was granted fifteen cities and titled Lord Shang. As prime minister for ten years, he faced resentment from nobles. Zhao Liang warned him of his dangerous position, criticizing his reliance on harsh methods and lack of virtue, but Lord Shang ignored the advice.

Five months after Duke Xiao's death, the new prince ascended. Gongzi Qian accused Lord Shang of rebellion. Lord Shang fled but was turned away by innkeepers due to his own laws requiring identification. He escaped to Wei, but the Wei people, angry over his deception, returned him to Qin. He attempted to raise troops in his fiefdom but was captured and executed by dismemberment. His entire clan was killed. Sima Qian concluded that Lord Shang's cruel and ungrateful nature, reliance on deceit, and refusal to heed wise counsel led to his downfall.

translation:
Dawan was discovered by Zhang Qian.
Zhang Qian was from Hanzhong and served as a Langguan during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the emperor asked the surrendered Huns. They all said that the Huns attacked and defeated King Yuezhi and used his skull as a drinking vessel. The Yuezhi fled and often resented the Huns, but they had no friends to fight with them.
At this time, the Han Dynasty was about to attack the Xiongnu. After hearing these statements, it wanted to send an envoy to Yuezhi to contact them.
But to go to Yuezhi, you have to pass through the Xiongnu, so you recruited people who could be sent as envoys.
Zhang Qian responded to the call as a Langguan and was sent as an envoy to the Yuezhi. He left Longxi with a former Huns slave named Ganfu from Tangyi. When passing by the Huns, he was captured by the Huns and handed over to the Chanyu.
The Chanyu retained Zhang Qian and said, "The Yueshi are to the north of us. How can the Han Dynasty send envoys there?"
If we want to send an envoy to South Vietnam, will the Han Dynasty allow us?
He detained Zhang Qian for more than ten years, married him, and gave birth to children. However, Zhang Qian kept the talisman of the Han Dynasty envoy and did not lose it.
Zhang Qian stayed with the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu's care for him gradually relaxed. As a result, Zhang Qian and his followers fled to the Yueshi, and ran westward for dozens of days until they arrived in Dawan.
Dawan heard that the Han Dynasty was rich in money and wanted to communicate with the Han Dynasty, but failed. Now that I saw Zhang Qian, I felt happy and asked Zhang Qian: "Where do you want to go?"
Zhang Qian said: I sent an envoy to the Yuezhi for the Han Dynasty, but the Huns blocked my way.
Now that we have escaped from the Huns, I hope the king will send someone to guide and escort us to Yuezhi.
If we can really reach Yuezhi, we can return to the Han Dynasty. The wealth that the Han Dynasty presented to the king cannot be described in words.
Dawan believed that Zhang Qian's words were true, so he asked Zhang Qian to set off and sent him a guide and translator to reach Kangju. Kangju transferred him to Dayuezhi again.
At this time, the king of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his prince was appointed king.
This king had conquered Bactria and settled here. The land here is fertile and fertile, and there are few enemies to invade it, so the mood is comfortable and happy. I also thought that I was far away from the Han Dynasty and had no intention of revenge against the Huns.
Zhang Qian arrived in Daxia from the Yueshi, but after all he did not get the clear attitude of the Yueshi towards uniting the Han to attack the Huns.
Zhang Qian lived in Yueshi for more than a year and returned home. He traveled along the Nanshan Mountains and wanted to return to Chang'an from where the Qiang people lived, but he was captured by the Huns again.
He lived with the Xiongnu for more than a year. When the Chanyu died, King Zuoguli of the Xiongnu attacked the prince and proclaimed himself the Chanyu. The country was in chaos. Zhang Qian took the opportunity to escape back to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Tangyi father.
In the Han Dynasty, Zhang Qian was granted the title of Taizhong Dafu, and Tang Yifu was granted the title of Envoy Lord.
Zhang Qian was strong, powerful, broad-minded, honest and trustworthy, and all the barbarians liked him.
Tangyi's father was a Huns and was good at archery. Whenever he was in poverty and danger, he would shoot birds and animals for food.
Initially, Zhang Qian had more than a hundred followers when he was sent as an envoy. Thirteen years after leaving the Han Dynasty, only he and Gan Fu returned to the Han Dynasty.
Zhang Qian visited Dayuan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju. Legend has it that there were five or six big countries next to these countries. He stated the situation to the Emperor of Han one by one, saying: Dayuan is southwest of the Xiongnu, due west of the Han Dynasty, about 10,000 miles away from the Han Dynasty.
The local custom is to settle in one place, cultivate the fields, and grow rice and wheat.
Produces wine.
There are many good horses. The horses are sweating and bloody. Their ancestors are the sons of Tianma.
There are city walls and houses there, and there are more than 70 large and small towns under its jurisdiction, with about hundreds of thousands of people.
The weapons of Dawan are bows and spears, and people ride horses and shoot arrows.
It is bordered by Kangju in the north, Dayuezhi in the west, Daxia in the southwest, Wusun in the northeast, and Chugui and Yuzhi in the east.
To the west of Zhi, the rivers flow westward and flow into the West Sea. The rivers east of Yuzhi all flow eastward and flow into the salt lake.
The water in the salt lake flows secretly underground. To its south is the source of the Yellow River, from which the Yellow River water flows out.
Jade is abundant there, and water from the Yellow River flows into China.
The towns of Loulan and Gushi both have city walls, close to Yanze.
Yanze is about five thousand miles away from Chang'an.
The right side of the Xiongnu was east of Yanze, up to the Longxi Great Wall, and connected to the Qiang residential area in the south, blocking the road to the Han Dynasty.
Wusun is about 2,000 miles northeast of Dawan. It is a country where people do not settle in one place. People move around according to the needs of grazing, which is the same as the custom of the Xiongnu.
There are tens of thousands of soldiers who draw bows and fight, and they are brave and good at fighting.
They were originally subordinate to the Xiongnu, but when they became powerful, they took back the hostages who were bound to the Xiongnu and refused to worship the Xiongnu.
Kangju is about 2,000 miles northwest of Dawan. It is a country where people do not live in one place. The customs are mostly the same as those of the Yueshi.
There are 80,000 to 90,000 warriors who draw bows and fight, and they are neighboring countries with Dawan.
The country was small, so the south was forced to serve the Yuezhi, and the east was forced to serve the Xiongnu.
Amcai is about 2,000 miles northwest of Kangju. It is a country where people do not live in one place, and its customs are mostly the same as those of Kangju.
There are more than 100,000 warriors who draw bows and fight.
It is near a large swamp with no shore, probably the North Sea.
The Dayue clan is about two to three thousand miles west of Dayuan and north of the Guishui River.
It is bounded by Daxia in the south, Anxi in the west, and Kangju in the north.
It is a country where the people do not settle in one place. People move around according to the needs of grazing, which is the same as the custom of the Xiongnu.
There are one to two hundred thousand warriors who draw bows and fight.
When they were strong in the past, they despised the Xiongnu. When Maodun became the Chanyu, he defeated the Yuezhi. When the Xiongnu became the Chanyu, he killed the Yuezhi king and used the Yuezhi king's skull as a drinking vessel.
At first, the Yuezhi lived between Dunhuang and Qilian. When they were defeated by the Xiongnu, most of them left far away, passing through Dawan, and went west to attack Daxia, defeated it, and made them submit to the Yuezhi. Then they established their capital north of the Guishui River as the royal court.
The remaining small group of Yuezhi people who could not leave preserved Nanshan and the place where the Qiang people lived, and they were called Xiao Yuezhi people.
Rest in peace about a few thousand miles west of Dayuezhi.
Their custom is to settle in one place, cultivate the fields, grow rice and wheat, and produce wine.
Its towns are like Dawan.
It has hundreds of towns and cities under its jurisdiction and a land area of ​​thousands of miles. It is the largest country.
There is a market near Guishui, and people use cars and ships to transport goods for business, sometimes to nearby countries or places thousands of miles away.
They used silver to make coins, and the coins were minted to resemble the king's appearance. When the king died, they changed the coins because they wanted to imitate the king's appearance.
They drew horizontal lines on the leather as text.
To the west is Tiaozhi, to the north are Yancai and Lixuan.
The branches are thousands of miles west of Parthia, near the Western Sea.
The weather there is hot and humid.
People tilled the fields and grew rice.
There arose a great bird whose eggs were as big as an urn.
With a large population, some places often had small princes, and Parthian servants governed them.
Think of it as a peripheral country.
The people of Tiaozhi are good at magic. The old people in Anxi said that there was Weushui and Queen Mother of the West in Tiaozhi State, but they had never seen them.
Daxia is located south of the Guishui River, more than 2,000 miles southwest of Dawan.
The local custom is that people settle in one place, with towns and houses. The custom is the same as that of Dawan.
There is no grand governor, instead each town has a small governor.
The country's military is weak and afraid of war.
People are good at doing business.
When the Da Yuezhi moved westward, they defeated Da Xia and ruled the entire Da Xia.
There are many people in Daxia, about one million.
Its capital is called Lanshi City. There is a trade market here. Sells various items.
There is a poisonous country in the southeast of Daxia.
Zhang Qian said: When I was in Daxia, I saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, so I asked them: Where did they get these things?
People from the Daxia Kingdom said: Our merchants bought it from the Shendu Kingdom.
Shendu Country is about several thousand miles southeast of Daxia.
The custom there is for people to settle in one place, which is roughly the same as in Daxia, but the terrain is low and humid and the weather is hot.
Its people fought on elephants.
It is near a flood.
I estimate that Daxia is twelve thousand miles away from the Han Dynasty and is in the southwest of the Han Dynasty.
Shendu Country is located thousands of miles southeast of Daxia and has products from Shu County, which means that it is not far from Shu County.
Nowadays, if an envoy is sent to Daxia, if he passes through the Qiang residential area, the terrain is dangerous and the Qiang people hate it; if he goes slightly north, he will be captured by the Huns. The road from Shu should be straight and free from intruders.
The emperor has heard that Dawan, Daxia, Anxi, etc. are all big countries that produce many strange things. The people live in one place and their lives are quite similar to those of the Han Dynasty. However, their armies are weak and they value the property of the Han Dynasty. There are countries such as Dayuezhi and Kangju in the north. Their armies are powerful, but you can use gifts and benefits to induce them to come to pay homage to the Emperor of Han.
And if we can really get them and make them our own with morality, then we can expand the territory of thousands of miles, and through many translations, attract people with different customs, so that the prestige and kindness of the emperor of the Han Dynasty can be spread all over the world.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was happy and thought Zhang Qian's words were right, so he ordered Zhang Qian to send secret envoys from Shu County and Jianwei County to set off in four groups at the same time: one from Zhan, one from Ran, one from Qi, and one from Qionbo, each traveling one or two thousand miles.
As a result, the northern route was blocked by Di and Zuo, and the southern route was blocked by Xi and Kunming.
Countries like Kunming had no rulers and were good at robbing and stealing. They often killed and robbed the Han Dynasty envoys, but the Han Dynasty envoys failed to pass.
However, I heard that more than a thousand miles west of Kunming, there was a country called Dianyue where the people rode elephants. Some of the merchants from Shu County who smuggled goods out of the country had been there, so the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom because they wanted to find a way to Daxia.
At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to open up the southwestern barbarians, but it wasted a lot of money and the road was not opened, so they gave up.
When Zhang Qian said that it was possible to connect to Daxia from the southwestern barbarians, the Han Dynasty resumed the work of opening up the southwestern barbarians.
Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu as a captain. Because he knew where there were water and grass, the army could not be exhausted. The emperor named Zhang Qian the Marquis of Bowang.
This happened in the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
The next year, Zhang Qian became a guard and set out from Youbeiping with General Li Guang to attack the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu soldiers surrounded General Li. His army suffered many casualties. However, Zhang Qian was sentenced to death because he missed the agreed time. He spent money to atone for his sin and became a civilian.
In this year, the Han Dynasty sent Hussar General Huo Qubing to defeat tens of thousands of Huns in the west and came to the foot of the Qilian Mountains.
The next year, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his people to surrender to the Han Dynasty. From then on, there were no more Huns in the area from Jincheng, west of Hexi and Nanshan to Yanze.
The Huns sometimes sent scouts here, but this rarely happened.
For two full years after this, the Han Dynasty drove the Xiongnu Chanyu to the north of the desert.
After that, the emperor repeatedly asked Zhang Qian about the affairs of Daxia and other countries.
At this time, Zhang Qian had lost his marquis, so he said: When I was in the Xiongnu, I heard that King Wusun was called Kunmo. Kunmo's father was the king of a small country to the west of the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu attacked and killed Kunmo's father, and Kunmo was abandoned in the wilderness after he was born.
Birds flew to him with meat in their mouths and fed him; wolves came and fed him.
The Chanyu felt strange and thought he was a god, so he took him in and let him grow up.
When he came of age, he was asked to lead troops in battles. After many meritorious service, the Shanyu gave him his father's people and ordered him to stay in the Western Regions for a long time.
Kunmo adopted his people and attacked nearby small towns. Gradually, he had tens of thousands of soldiers who could draw bows and fight, and they were familiar with the skills of offensive warfare.
After Shanyu's death, Kunmo led his people to move far away, maintaining their independence and refusing to worship the Huns.
The Xiongnu sent a commando to attack Kunmo, but failed to win. They believed that Kunmo was a god and stayed away from him. They restrained and controlled him instead of launching a major attack on him.
Now Shan Yugang was very tired after being beaten by the Han Dynasty, and the place controlled by King Hunxie was unguarded.
The custom of the barbarians is to covet the property of the Han Dynasty. If Wusun can be gifted with rich property at this time to attract him to move eastward, live in the place formerly controlled by King Hunxie, and become brothers with the Han Dynasty, Kunmo should be able to accept it according to the situation. If he accepts this arrangement, then it will be like cutting off the right arm of the Huns.
After uniting Wusun, Daxia and other countries to its west can be recruited as foreign vassals.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty believed that Zhang Qian was right and appointed him as Zhonglang General. He led 300 people, each with two horses, tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, and carried money, cloth and silk worth tens of millions. He also appointed many deputy envoys holding talismans. If the road could be opened, he would send them to neighboring countries.
Zhang Qian had arrived at Wusun, and King Kunmo of Wusun received the envoys of the Han Dynasty with the same etiquette as he treated the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian felt ashamed in his heart. He knew that the barbarians were greedy, so he said: The emperor gives gifts, and if the king does not thank him, the gifts will be returned.
Kunmo stood up, thanked him, accepted the gift, and continued to do other things as usual.
Zhang Qian explained the purpose of his mission to Kunmo and said: If Wusun can move eastward to King Hunxie's old land, then the Han Dynasty will send a daughter of a prince to marry Kunmo as his wife.
At this time, the Wusun Kingdom had been divided. The king was old and far away from the Han Dynasty. He did not know its size. It had been owned by the Xiongnu for a long time, and it was also close to the Xiongnu. The ministers were afraid of the Xiongnu and did not want to move. The king could not make the decision alone.
Therefore, Zhang Qian failed to get a clear attitude from King Wusun.
Kunmo had more than ten sons, one of whom was named Dalu. He was strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived in another place.
Dalu's brother is the prince. The prince has a son named Cen Marry. The prince has died long ago.
When he was dying, he said to his father Kunmo: He must marry Cen as the prince and don't let anyone else take his place.
Kunmo sadly agreed to him, and finally let Cen marry and become the prince.
Da Lu was angry that he had failed to replace the prince, so he recruited his brothers and led his army to rebel, planning to attack Cen Maru and Kunmo.
Kunmo was old and often feared that Da Lu would kill Cen Marry, so he gave Cen Marry more than 10,000 cavalry and lived in another place.
And Kunmo himself has more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense. In this way, the Wusun Kingdom was divided into three parts, but still generally belonged to Kunmo. Therefore, Kunmo did not dare to discuss this matter with Zhang Qian alone. Zhang Qian then assigned deputy envoys to Dayuan, Kangju, Dayuezhi, Daxia, Anxi, Shendu, Yutian, Chuyi and several nearby countries.
Wusun State sent a guide and translator to send Zhang Qian back to his country. Zhang Qian and the Wusun Kingdom sent dozens of envoys, bringing dozens of horses to return and thank the Emperor of Han. By the way, they allowed them to have a peek at the situation of the Han Dynasty and understand the vastness of the Han Dynasty.
Zhang Qian returned to the Han Dynasty and was appointed Daxing, ranking among the nine ministers.
More than a year later, he died.
Wusun's envoy had seen that the Han Dynasty had many people and rich property, so he went back and reported to the king. Wusun Kingdom paid more and more attention to the Han Dynasty.
More than a year later, most of the envoys sent by Zhang Qian to communicate with Daxia and other countries returned to the Han Dynasty together with the people from the countries they went to. As a result, the northwest countries began to have contacts with the Han Dynasty from this time on.
However, this kind of exchange was initiated by Zhang Qian, so in the future, envoys to various countries in the Western Regions were called Bowang Hou, in order to win the trust of foreign countries, and foreign countries also trusted Han Dynasty envoys.
After the death of Bowang Hou Zhang Qian, the Xiongnu heard that the Han Dynasty had contacts with Wusun, and they were very angry and wanted to attack Wusun.
When the Han Dynasty sent envoys to Wusun, and from the south to Dayuan and Dayuezhi, the envoys continued one after another. Wusun became frightened and sent envoys to offer horses to the Han Dynasty, hoping to marry the daughters of the Han Dynasty princes and become brothers with the Han Dynasty.
The emperor asked the officials for their opinions, and they all said: They must send betrothal gifts first, and then they can marry the daughters of the princes.
Finally, the emperor opened the "Book of Changes" for divination, and the book said: The divine horse will come from the northwest.
After getting Wusun's good horse, the emperor named the horse Tianma.
When the horses from Dawan became stronger and stronger, they renamed the Wusun horses to "Xiji" and the Dawan horses to "Tianma".
At this time, the Han Dynasty began to build the Great Wall pavilion west of Lingju, and initially established Jiuquan County to communicate with the northwest countries.
So additional envoys were sent to Anxi, Yancai, Lixuan, Tiaozhi, and Shendu countries.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty liked Dawan's horses, so there was an endless stream of envoys to Dawan.
The number of envoys sent to foreign countries ranged from several hundred to more than a hundred, and the things each person carried were roughly the same as those carried by Bowang Hou.
From then on, missions became commonplace. The number of people assigned decreased.
The Han Dynasty sent out envoys in roughly a year, sometimes more than ten batches, sometimes five or six batches. In places far away, it would take eight or nine years for the envoys to return; in places close, it would take a few years.
At this time, the Han Dynasty had already destroyed South Vietnam, and the Shu region and the southwestern Yi states were all frightened, and asked the Han Dynasty to appoint officials for them and to visit the emperor of Han Dynasty.
Therefore, the Han Dynasty set up counties such as Yizhou, Yueqi, Zangke, Shenli, and Wenshan, hoping to connect the land together and then lead to Daxia.
So within one year, the Han Dynasty sent more than ten groups of envoys, including Bai Shichang and Lu Yue, from these newly established counties to Daxia. However, they were blocked by Kunming. The envoys were killed, their money and materials were robbed, and they ultimately failed to reach Daxia.
So the Han Dynasty dispatched the sinners of the Sanfu, plus tens of thousands of warriors from Ba and Shu, and sent two generals, Guo Chang and Wei Guang, to attack those who blocked the Han Dynasty's envoys in Kunming. They killed and captured tens of thousands of people and then left.
After that, the Han Dynasty sent envoys, and Kunming carried out another robbery. In the end, they still failed to communicate with Daxia.
On the way to Daxia from the north through Jiuquan, there were already many envoys. Foreigners were more and more satisfied with the Han Dynasty's cloth and property, and no longer felt valuable about these things.
Since Bowang Hou gained honor and wealth for opening up the road to foreign countries, the officials and soldiers who followed the envoys all rushed to write letters stating the rare things, strange things and interests of foreign countries, and asked to serve as envoys.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty believed that foreign countries were very far away and not everyone was willing to go there, so he accepted their requests, granted talismans, recruited officials and people regardless of their origins, equipped them with personnel, and sent them on missions to expand the roads to communicate with foreign countries.
Those who returned from missions had to embezzle cloth and property, and deviate from the emperor's wishes. The emperor believed that they were familiar with the Western Regions and the work of the envoys, and often investigated their crimes deeply to anger them, and asked them to pay for their sins and ask to be envoys again.
Since then, there have been endless incidents of envoys, and they have easily broken the law.
The officials and soldiers often repeatedly praised foreign things. Those who spoke nonsense were awarded the title of official envoy, and those who were boastful and petty were appointed deputy envoys. Therefore, those who talked nonsense and had no virtue rushed to imitate them.
Those who sent envoys were the sons of poor people. They took the gifts given by the government to various countries in the Western Regions as their own, hoping to sell them at low prices and gain private profits in foreign countries.
Foreign countries also hated the Han Dynasty envoys because everything they said was untrue. They estimated that the Han Dynasty army was far away and could not reach them, so they cut off their food and made the Han Dynasty envoys suffer hardship.
The envoys of the Han Dynasty lived in poverty and were cut off from supplies. As a result, they developed grudges against the countries in the Western Regions and even attacked each other.
Loulan and Gushi were small countries located on strategic transportation routes, so they attacked the Han Dynasty envoy Wang Hui and others with great force.
The Huns' assault troops also frequently blocked and attacked Han Dynasty envoys who were envoys to the countries in the Western Regions.
The envoys rushed to talk at length about the dangers of foreign countries. Although there were towns in various countries, their armies were weak and easy to attack.
Therefore, the emperor sent his subordinate Zhao Ponu to lead tens of thousands of cavalry and soldiers from various counties to the Xiong River to attack the Huns, but the Huns all left.
The next year, when they attacked Gushi, Zhao Ponu and more than 700 light cavalry arrived first, captured King Loulan, and captured Gushi.
Taking advantage of the victory's military power, he besieged Wusun, Dayuan and other countries.
After returning to the Han Dynasty, Zhao Ponu was granted the title of Hou Yehou.
Wang Hui went on many missions and was made very miserable by Loulan. He told the emperor about this, and the emperor sent troops and ordered Wang Hui to assist Zhao Ponu to defeat the enemy, so he made Wang Hui a noble prince.
Therefore, the Han Dynasty built pavilions from Jiuquan to Yumen Pass.
King Wusun used a thousand horses to marry a girl from the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty sent the daughter of the royal family Liu Jian, King of Jiangdu, to marry King Wusun. King Kunmo of Wusun took her as his right wife.
The Huns also sent a princess to marry Kunmo, who regarded her as his left wife.
Kunmo said: I am old. He ordered his grandson Cen to marry the princess.
Wusun is rich in horses, and the rich families have as many as four or five thousand horses.
Finally, when the Han Dynasty envoy arrived in Parthia, King Parthia ordered the relevant people to lead 20,000 cavalry to greet them on the eastern border.
The eastern border is thousands of miles away from the royal capital.
When you get to the king, you have to pass through dozens of towns, where the people are connected and the population is large.
When the envoys of the Han Dynasty returned, Parthia sent envoys to follow the Han envoys to observe the vastness of the Han Dynasty, and dedicated the big bird eggs and Li Xuan's magicians to the Han Dynasty.
As for the small countries of Huanqian and Dayi to the west of Dayuan, and the countries of Gushi, Chuyi, Su Xie and other countries to the east of Dayuan, they all came with the Han Dynasty envoys to pay tribute and pay homage to the emperor.
The emperor was very happy.
The envoys of the Han Dynasty tried their best to explore the source of the Yellow River. The source came from the country of Yu. The mountains there were rich in jade. The envoys collected it. The emperor studied it based on ancient books and named the mountain where the Yellow River originates as Kunlun Mountain.
At this time, the emperor was inspecting the seaside areas many times, and every time he asked foreign guests to follow him, and he had to pass through most crowded towns. He also distributed money to reward them and prepared generous gifts for them to show the wealth of the Han Dynasty.
So large-scale hornet's events were held, strange plays were performed, and many monsters were exhibited, attracting many people to watch. The emperor then gave rewards, gathered wine into a pool, hung meat into a forest, and allowed foreign guests to view the materials stored in warehouses everywhere to show the vastness of the Han Dynasty, making them overwhelmed with horror.
After the magic skills were added, the horns and spectacles changed into new tricks every year, and the prosperity of these skills began from this time.
Foreign envoys from the Western Regions kept coming and going.
However, the envoys from the countries west of Dawan felt that they were far away from the Han Dynasty. They were still proud, indulgent and comfortable. The Han Dynasty could not restrain them with courtesy and make them obediently obey the prince's orders.
From the west of Wusun to the Parthian countries, because they were close to the Xiongnu, the Yuezhi were in trouble. Therefore, when the Xiongnu envoys took a letter from Shan Yu, these countries took turns supplying them with food and did not dare to stop them and cause them suffering. As for the arrival of the Han Dynasty envoys, they would not be provided with food and drink if they did not bring out cloth and property, and they would not be able to get mounts if they did not buy livestock.
So this situation occurred because the Han Dynasty was far away. The Han Dynasty had money and things, so they had to buy to get what they wanted, but this was also because they feared the Huns' envoys more than the Han Dynasty's envoys.
Countries around Dawan all use Pu Tao to make wine. Rich people have more than 10,000 shi of wine in their collections, and it will last for decades without deterioration.
Local custom is to drink alcohol, and horses like to eat alfalfa.
The Han Dynasty envoys retrieved the seeds of Pu Tao and alfalfa, so the emperor began to plant Pu Tao and alfalfa on the fertile land.
With more Tianma and more foreign envoys coming, the Han Dynasty's palaces and gardens were planted with Pu Tao and alfalfa as far as the eye could see.
From the west of Dawan to Anxi, although the languages ​​​​of the countries are different, their customs are roughly the same, and they can understand each other.
The people there have sunken eyes, heavy beards, are good at business, and will argue over every penny.
The local custom respects women. When a woman speaks, her husband will resolutely comply and dare not violate it.
There is no silk or lacquer everywhere, and they don't know how to make money or utensils.
When the fugitive soldiers of the Han Dynasty envoys surrendered to them, they were taught to forge weapons and utensils.
When they got gold and silver from the Han Dynasty, they used it to make vessels, not coins.
More and more envoys from the Han Dynasty went to the Western Regions. Most of those who had been envoys since their youth reported to the emperor the situation they were familiar with, saying: "There is a good horse in Dayuan. In Ershi City, they hid it and refused to give it to the envoys of the Han Dynasty."
The emperor already liked Dawan's horses. When he heard the news, he felt very happy and sent his warriors Cha Ling and others with a thousand pieces of gold and golden horses to ask the king of Dawan to exchange for the fine horses from Ershi City.
Dawan already had many things from the Han Dynasty. King Wan and his ministers discussed with each other and said: The Han Dynasty is far away from us, and there are frequent deaths in our country through the salt lake. If you come from the north, there will be Xiongnu intrusion, and if you come from the south, there will be a lack of water and grass.
There are often no towns and food is scarce.
Envoys from the Han Dynasty came in groups of several hundred people each time, but often more than half of them died due to lack of food. How could they send a large army in such a situation?
There is nothing they can do to us, and besides, the second master’s horse is a BMW from Dawan.
He refused to give it to the envoys of the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty envoy was angry and casually threatened to smash the golden horse and leave.
The noble officials of Dawan were angry and said: The envoys of the Han Dynasty underestimate us!
He sent the Han envoys away and ordered Yu Chengguo in the east to intercept and kill the Han envoys and seize their belongings.
So the emperor was furious. People who had sent envoys to Dayuan, such as Yao Dinghan and others, said that Dayuan's army was weak. If he could really lead less than three thousand Han Dynasty troops and shoot them with strong bows and crossbows, he could capture all their troops and defeat Dayuan.
Because the emperor once sent the Marquis of Zhaoye to attack Loulan, he led 700 cavalry to attack Loulan first and captured the king of Loulan. Therefore, the emperor believed that Yao Dinghan was right and wanted to make his favorite concubine Mrs. Li's family a marquis. Therefore, the emperor appointed Mrs. Li's brother Li Guangli as the general of the second division. He mobilized 6,000 cavalry from the vassal country and tens of thousands of irregular youths from various counties to attack Dawan.
The purpose was to go to Ershi City to retrieve good horses, so he was called "General Ershi".
Zhao Shicheng served as military commander, the former Haohou Wang Hui served as the army's guide, and Li Duo served as the captain, in charge of military matters.
This year is the first year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, a serious locust plague occurred in Kanto, and the locusts flew to Dunhuang in the west.
General Ershi's army has already passed through the salt swamp in the west. The small countries they passed were afraid and each held their own castles and refused to provide food to the Han army.
The Han army attacked the city and was unable to capture it.
You have to capture the city to get food and drink. If you can't capture it, you have to leave within a few days.
When the Han army arrived at Yucheng, only a few thousand soldiers followed, and they were all hungry and tired.
They attacked Yu Cheng, and Yu Cheng defeated them. Many Han soldiers were killed and wounded.
General Ershi discussed with Li Duo, Zhao Shicheng and others and said: If we can't capture Yucheng, let alone the king's capital?
So he led his troops back and went back and forth for two years.
When they retreated to Dunhuang, only one-tenth of the remaining soldiers were left.
They sent envoys to report to the emperor: The road is far away and there is often a lack of food. Moreover, the soldiers are not afraid of fighting, but only worried about starvation.
There are few people, not enough to capture Dawan.
I hope to temporarily withdraw our troops. In the future, more troops will be sent to attack.
After hearing this, the emperor was furious and sent an envoy to stop them at Yumen Pass, saying that anyone in the army who dared to enter Yumen Pass would be beheaded.
General Ershi was afraid, so he stayed in Dunhuang.
In the summer of the second year of Taichu, the Han Dynasty lost more than 20,000 troops of the Hou Yehou to the Xiongnu.
The ministers and deliberation officials all hoped to stop the military campaign against Dawan and concentrate their efforts on attacking the Xiongnu.
The emperor has attacked Dayuan, but Wan is a small country but failed to capture it. Then Daxia and other countries will despise the Han Dynasty, and Dayuan's good horses will never be obtained. Wusun and Luntai will easily cause trouble to the Han Dynasty envoys and be laughed at by foreigners.
So they punished Deng Guang and others who said that the crusade against Dawan was particularly unfavorable, pardoned prisoners and brave soldiers who had committed crimes, and sent more young men with bad conduct and border cavalry. In more than a year, 60,000 soldiers set out from Dunhuang, not including those who brought their own food and clothing to join the war.
These soldiers carried 100,000 cattle, more than 30,000 horses, and countless donkeys, camels and other items.
They also brought a lot of food and all kinds of weapons. At that time, the whole country was in turmoil. According to legend, there were more than fifty captains who were ordered to conquer Dawan.
There were no wells in King Wan's city, so they had to draw water from outside the city into the city. The Han Dynasty army sent hydraulic workers to change the water channels in the city so that there was no water available in the city.
The Han Dynasty also sent an additional 180,000 armored soldiers to garrison north of Jiuquan and Zhangye, and set up two counties, Juyan and Xiutu, to protect Jiuquan. The Han Dynasty also dispatched seven types of criminals across the country to carry dry food to supply the generals of the second division.
There was an endless stream of people transporting supplies, all the way to Dunhuang.
He also appointed two people who were familiar with horses as driving captains, preparing to select the best horses from Dawan after conquering it.
So the General of the Second Division went on another expedition, leading a large number of soldiers. Every small country he went to welcomed him, and they all provided food to the Han army.
They arrived at Lundou Kingdom, which refused to surrender. They attacked for several days and bloodbathed the country.
We went west from Luntou and arrived at the royal city safely. The Han army arrived with 30,000 people.
The Wan army attacked the Han army, and the Han army defeated the Wan army with arrows. The Wan army retreated into the city and guarded it against the city wall.
General Ershi's soldiers were about to attack Yucheng, but fearing that they would be delayed and make Dawan do more deceitful things, they attacked Dawan City first, cut off its water source, and changed its water channels. Then Dawan was already deeply worried and in danger.
The Han army surrounded Dawan City and attacked it for more than forty days. The outer city was destroyed and the brave general Jian Mi among the Dawan nobles was captured.
The people of Dawan were very frightened and ran into the city.
The senior officials of Dayuan discussed with each other and said: The reason why the Han Dynasty attacked Dayuan was because King Wuwu of Dayuan hid good horses and killed the Han Dynasty envoy.
Now, if King Wuwu of Wan is killed and a good horse is sacrificed, the Han army will probably break the siege and leave. If not, it will not be too late to fight hard and die.
The high-ranking officials of Dayuan all believed that this was correct, so they jointly killed King Wan Wuwu and sent nobles to take Wuwi's head to see the general of the second division. They made an appointment with him and said: The Han army should not attack us. We will hand over all the good horses for you to choose and provide food and drink for the Han army.
If you do not accept our request, we will kill all the good horses, and reinforcements from Kangju will also arrive.
If their army arrives, our army will be in the city and Kang Ju's army will be outside the city, fighting with the Han soldiers.
I hope the Han army will carefully consider where to go?
At this time, Kang Ju's scouts were peeking at the situation of the Han army. Because the Han army was still strong, they did not dare to attack.
General Li Guangli of the Second Division discussed with Zhao Shicheng, Li Duo and others: I heard that a Han man has recently been found in Dawan City. This man is familiar with well-drilling technology, and there is quite a lot of food in the city.
The purpose of our coming here is to kill Wuwu, the culprit.
Wuwu's troops have been obtained, but they do not agree to their request to relieve the siege and withdraw their troops, then they will resolutely hold on, and Kangju's army will come to rescue Dawan when they see that the Han army is tired, and they will definitely defeat the Han army.
The officers all thought it was right and agreed to Dawan's request.
Dayuan Cai donated their good horses to let the Han army choose, and also provided a lot of grain to the Han army.
The Han army selected dozens of their good horses, as well as more than 3,000 stallions and mares of average and below average, and appointed Mocai, one of the Dawan nobles who had treated the Han envoys well in the past, as the king of Dawan. They made an alliance with them and withdrew their troops.
The Han army never entered Dayuan City, so they withdrew and returned to the Han Dynasty.
Initially, the general of the Second Division set out from the west of Dunhuang. He thought that because of the large number of people, the countries he passed through were unable to provide food, so he divided the army into several groups and advanced from the south and north.
School captain Wang Shensheng, Yuan Honglu Hu Chongguo and others led more than a thousand people to reach Yucheng from another road.
Yu Chengcheng insisted on defending the city and refused to supply food to the Han army.
Wang Shensheng left the army two hundred miles away. He thought he had something to rely on and despised Yu Cheng. He asked for food from Yu Cheng, but Yu Cheng refused to give it. He peeped at the Han army and knew that Wang Shensheng's army was decreasing day by day. One morning, he attacked Wang Shensheng's army with 3,000 people and killed Wang Shensheng and others. The army was destroyed. Only a few people escaped and ran back to the general of the Second Division.
The general of the Second Division ordered Shangguan Jie, the captain of Sosu, to attack Yu Cheng.
King Yucheng fled to Kangju, and Shangguan Jie pursued him there.
When Kang Ju heard that the Han army had captured Dayuan, he dedicated King Yu Cheng to Shangguan Jie. Shangguan Jie ordered four cavalry to tie up King Yu Cheng and escort him to the general of the Second Division.
The four cavalrymen discussed with each other and said: King Yu Cheng is a person hated by the Han Dynasty. If he is sent alive now, a sudden accident will be a big deal.
They wanted to kill him, but no one dared to do it first.
Zhao Di, the youngest knight from Shanggui, pulled out his sword and chopped it off, killed King Yu Cheng and took his head with him.
Zhao Di, Shangguan Jie and others caught up with Li Guangli, the general of the Second Division.
At first, the general of the Second Division sent troops for the last time, and the emperor sent an envoy to tell Wusun, asking them to send more troops to jointly attack Dawan with the Han army.
Wusun dispatched 2,000 cavalry to Dawan, but they adopted a fence-sitting attitude and waited and watched.
The general of the Second Division returned eastward victoriously. When the small countries he passed heard that Dawan had been defeated, they all sent their sons to accompany the Han army to pay tribute to the Han Dynasty, pay homage to the emperor, and stay in the Han Dynasty as hostages.
The general of the Second Division attacked Dayuan, and Zhao Shicheng, who was in charge of the army, fought hard and made the greatest contribution; Shangguan Jie bravely led his troops deep into the army, and Li Duo was able to make suggestions, and the army returned to Yumen Pass with more than 10,000 people and more than 1,000 horses.
The last time the general of the Second Division sent out troops, the army was not short of food, and the casualties were not too many. However, his generals were corrupt, most of them did not love the soldiers, and robbed them of food and wages, so many people died.
Because they traveled thousands of miles to conquer Dawan and did not remember their mistakes, the emperor made Li Guangli the Marquis of Haixi.
He also named Zhao Di, the knight who personally killed King Yu Cheng, as the new Marquis of Qi, Zhao Shi, the military commander, became the Guanglu doctor, Shangguan Jie as the Shaofu, and Li Duo as the Shangdang prefect.
Among the officers, three were promoted to the rank of Jiuqing, more than 100 were promoted to ministers, governors, and officials at the level of 2,000 stone, and more than 1,000 were promoted to officials below the level of 1,000 stone.
Those who volunteered to join the army received military positions beyond their expectations, and those who joined the army due to punishment were exempted from crime and did not take credit.
The rewards given to soldiers were worth forty thousand gold.
Two campaigns against Dawan took a total of four years to end the military campaign.
After the Han Dynasty conquered Dayuan, he established Mo Cai as King of Dayuan and withdrew. After more than a year, the senior officials of Dayuan believed that Mecai was good at flattery, which led to the killing of Dayuan, so they conspired with each other to kill Mecai, made Wuwi's brother named Chanfeng the king of Dayuan, and sent his son to the Han Dynasty as a hostage.
The Han Dynasty also sent envoys to give gifts to Dawan to appease it.
Later, the Han Dynasty sent more than ten groups of envoys to some countries to the west of Dayuan to search for strange things, and also to inform and inspect the power and merits of the expedition against Dayuan.
Dunhuang and Jiuquan have since set up captains, and all the way to Yanshui in the west, there are often pavilions on the road.
There were hundreds of soldiers stationed in Lundou, so the Han Dynasty set up envoys there to protect the fields and accumulate grain to supply envoys on their missions to foreign countries.
Tai Shigong said: "The Benji of Yu" says: The Yellow River originates from Kunlun.
Kunlun is more than 2,500 miles high. It is the place where the sun and the moon hide from each other and emit their own light.
Above Kunlun there are Liquan and Yaochi.
Now that Zhang Qian was sent to Daxia as an envoy, he finally found the source of the Yellow River. Where can we see the Kunlun Mountains mentioned in "The Book of Yu"?
So when talking about the mountains and rivers of Kyushu, what "Shang Shu" says is closest to the actual situation.
As for the monsters recorded in "Yu Benji" and "Shan Hai Jing", I dare not say.
summary:
Zhang Qian, a Langguan from Hanzhong during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, discovered Dawan. The emperor, learning from surrendered Xiongnu that the Yuezhi had been defeated by the Xiongnu and sought allies, recruited envoys to contact the Yuezhi. Zhang Qian responded, leaving Longxi with Ganfu, a former Xiongnu slave. Captured by the Xiongnu, he was detained for over ten years, married, and had children, but kept his envoy's talisman. Eventually, he escaped westward to Dawan.

Dawan, eager to connect with the wealthy Han Dynasty, welcomed Zhang Qian and provided guides to Kangju, then to Dayuezhi. The Yuezhi king, having conquered Bactria, was content and unwilling to attack the Xiongnu. After over a year, Zhang Qian returned via the Nanshan Mountains but was recaptured by the Xiongnu. He escaped during internal Xiongnu chaos, returning to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Ganfu. He was granted the title Taizhong Dafu.

Zhang Qian reported on Dawan and neighboring states: Dawan, southwest of the Xiongnu, had settled agriculture, wine, and fine horses. It had over 70 towns and hundreds of thousands of people. Kangju, a nomadic state with 80,000-90,000 warriors, served the Yuezhi and Xiongnu. Dayuezhi, west of Dawan, was nomadic with 100,000-200,000 warriors, having defeated Daxia. Anxi, a large settled state with towns and trade, used silver coins. Tiaozhi, near the Western Sea, was hot and humid. Daxia, south of the Guishui River, had weak military but strong commerce, ruled by the Yuezhi.

Zhang Qian noted that in Daxia, he saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, bought from Shendu (India), suggesting a route from Shu. The emperor, intrigued by these wealthy states, sent envoys from Shu, but they were blocked by tribes like Kunming. Zhang Qian later joined General Wei Qing against the Xiongnu, earning the title Marquis of Bowang. After a failed campaign with Li Guang, he was reduced to commoner status.

The emperor, seeking to ally with Wusun, sent Zhang Qian as Zhonglang General with 300 men, gifts, and deputy envoys. Wusun's king, Kunmo, was hesitant due to Xiongnu influence and internal divisions. Zhang Qian dispatched deputies to various states. Wusun sent envoys to the Han Dynasty, impressed by its wealth. Zhang Qian died as Daxing, a high official.

Subsequently, the Han Dynasty established ties with Western Regions states, though envoys faced challenges from Xiongnu and local resistance. The emperor launched campaigns against Dawan for its horses, leading to two expeditions under Li Guangli. The first failed due to lack of supplies, but the second succeeded with a large army, capturing Dawan and securing horses. The Han Dynasty expanded its influence, setting up commanderies and protecting trade routes.

translation:
In the past, when Zhuanxu ruled the world, he appointed Nan Zhengzhong to be in charge of astronomy and Bei Zhengli to be in charge of geography.
During the Tang and Yu dynasties, the descendants of Chong and Li continued to be in charge of astronomy and geography until the Xia and Shang dynasties. Therefore, the Chongli family was in charge of astronomy and geography for generations.
During the Zhou Dynasty, Cheng Boxiu Fu was their descendant.
During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the Chongli family became the Sima family because they lost their official position.
The Sima family has been in charge of Zhou history for generations.
During the reigns of King Zhou Hui and King Zhou Xiang, the Sima family left the capital of Zhou and went to the Kingdom of Jin.
Later, the marshal of the Jin army fled to Qin, and the Sima family also moved to Shaoliang.
Since the Sima clan left Zhou and came to Jin, the clan members were scattered in various places, some in Wei State, some in Zhao State, and some in Qin State.
In the Wei State, he became the Prime Minister of the Zhongshan State.
In the State of Zhao, they were famous for teaching the theory of swordsmanship, and Kuai Kuai was their descendant.
A man named Sima Cuo who lived in Qin State once had a dispute with Zhang Yi, so King Qin Hui sent Sima Cuo to lead an army to attack Shu State. After the capture, he made him the governor of Shu.
Sima Jin, the grandson of Sima Cuo, served Wu Xinjun Bai Qi.
Shaoliang has been renamed Xia Yang.
Sima Jin and Wu Xinjun killed the Changping Army of Zhao State. After returning, they were killed in Duyou together with Wu Xinjun and buried in Huachi.
Sima Chang, the grandson of Sima Jin, was an official in charge of iron smelting in the State of Qin. He lived in the era of Qin Shihuang.
Sima Xian, the great-great-grandson of Kuai Chi, was a general under Wu Xinjun and led troops to capture Chaoge.
When the princes were vying to be king, Sima An became king in Yin.
When Liu Bang, the king of Han, attacked Xiang Yu, the overlord of Chu, Sima An surrendered to the king of Han, and the Han Dynasty made the Yin region Hanoi County.
Sima Chang gave birth to Sima Wuze, who served as the mayor of the Han Dynasty.
Wuze gave birth to Sima happy. Sima happy was awarded the title of five great officials. After his death, they were all buried in Gaomen.
Sima Xi gave birth to Sima Tan, who became Grand Historian.
Tai Shigong studied astronomy from Tang Du, the Book of Changes from Yang He, and Taoist theory from Huang Zi.
Tai Shigong was an official from Jianyuan to Yuanfeng. He was worried that scholars could not understand the essence of each school and what they learned was contradictory, so he discussed the essence of the six schools of Yin and Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Ming, Dharma and Taoism:
"Zhouyi·Xici Zhuan" says: People all over the world pursue the same thing, but their specific plans are diverse; they achieve the same goal, but the methods they take are different.

In ancient times, when Zhuanxu ruled the world, he appointed Nan Zhengzhong to oversee astronomy and Bei Zhengli to oversee geography.
