translation:
Ji Bu was from the Chu region. He was ambitious and chivalrous, and was very famous in the Chu region.
Xiang Yu sent him to lead the army, which embarrassed Liu Bang, the king of Han, many times.
After Xiang Yu's death, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty offered a thousand gold reward for Ji Bu's capture, and ordered anyone who dared to harbor Ji Bu to be punished for his crime.
Ji Bu hid in the home of a family named Zhou in Puyang.
The Zhou family said: It is very urgent that the Han Dynasty offers a reward for your capture. The tracking and search will come to my house. General, if you can obey my words, I will dare to give you a plan; if not, I would rather commit suicide first.
Ji Bu agreed to him.
The Zhou family then shaved off Ji Bu's hair, tied his neck with an iron hoop, put him in coarse cloth, put him in a cart, and sold him to the Zhu family of Lu, along with dozens of Zhou family's slaves.
The Zhu family knew in their hearts that it was Jibu, so they bought it and put it in the fields for farming. They also warned his son: "Everything about farming in the fields must be obeyed by this slave, and he must eat the same food as him."
The Zhu family took a light carriage to Luoyang and paid a visit to Ruyin Marquis Teng Gong.
Duke Teng left the Zhu family to drink for several days.
The Zhu family took the opportunity to ask Duke Teng: What serious crime did Ji Bu commit that made the emperor so eager to pursue him?
Teng Gong said: Ji Bu embarrassed the emperor many times on behalf of Xiang Yu. The emperor resented him, so he had to catch him before he could rest.
Zhu Jia said: What kind of person do you think Ji Bu is?
Teng Gong said: He is a talented person.
The Zhu family said: Each minister is sent by his master, and Ji Bu is sent by Xiang Yu. This is entirely within the scope of his official duties.
Can Xiang Yu's ministers be killed all?
Now that the emperor has just conquered the world, why should he show his narrowness to the world when he pursues a person based solely on his personal resentment?
Moreover, because of Ji Bu's talents, the Han Dynasty pursued him so urgently that he would either flee north to the Huns or south to Yue.
This behavior of hating the warriors and going to support the enemy country was the reason why Wu Zixu wanted to whip the body of King Ping of Chu.
Why don't you look for an opportunity to explain it to the emperor?
Teng Gong, the Marquis of Ruyin, knew that the Zhu family was a great knight, and guessed that Ji Bu must be hiding in his place, so he agreed and said, "Okay."
Teng Gong waited for the opportunity and reported to the emperor exactly what the Zhu family wanted.
The emperor then pardoned Ji Bu.
At this time, many famous people praised Ji Bu for his ability to turn toughness into suppleness, and the Zhu family became famous at that time.
Later, Ji Bu was summoned by the emperor to plead guilty, and the emperor appointed him as a doctor.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Ji Bu served as Zhonglang General.
Chanyu, the king of the Huns, once wrote a letter to insult Empress Lu and made rude remarks. Empress Lu was very angry and summoned all the generals to discuss the matter.
General Fan Kuai said: I am willing to lead 100,000 troops to sweep away the Xiongnu.
All the generals catered to Empress Lu's wishes and said in unison: "Okay."
Ji Bu said: Fan Kuai really deserves to be beheaded!
Back then, Emperor Gao led an army of 400,000 people and was besieged in Pingcheng. How could Fan Kuai sweep the Xiongnu with 100,000 troops now? This is lying to your face!
Besides, it was precisely because the Qin Dynasty used troops against the Huns that Chen Sheng and others rebelled.
Until now, the wound has not been cured, and Fan Kuai flatters him in person, hoping to make the world uneasy.
At this time, the generals in the palace were frightened, so Queen Lu retreated from the court and finally stopped talking about attacking the Xiongnu.
Ji Bu became the governor of Hedong County. During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, some people said that he was very talented, so the Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty summoned him and planned to appoint him as the imperial censor.
Others said he was brave, but drunken, willful and unapproachable.
Ji Bu came to the capital Chang'an and stayed in a guest house for a month. After the emperor summoned him, he was sent back to his original county.
Ji Bu therefore said to the emperor: I have no merit, but I have been favored by you and served in Hedong County.
Now that your majesty has summoned me for no reason, this must be because someone praised me and used me to deceive your majesty; now that I have come to the capital and was sent back to my original county without accepting anything, this must be because someone is slandering me in front of you.
Your Majesty summoned me because of a person's praise, and asked me to go back because of a person's slander. I'm afraid that after hearing this, the knowledgeable people in the world will get a glimpse of the depth of your conduct.
The emperor remained silent, feeling embarrassed, and after a long time he said: Hedong is the most important county to me, like my thighs and arms, so I specially summoned you!
So Ji Bu said goodbye to the emperor and returned to his original post as governor of Hedong County. There was a gentleman named Cao Qiu in the Chu region. He was good at rhetoric and eloquent. He used his power to obtain money many times.
He once served nobles like Zhao Tong and had friendship with Dou Changjun.
When Ji Bu heard about this, he sent a letter to advise Dou Changjun: "I heard that Mr. Cao Qiu is not a highly respected person. You should not associate with him."
When Mr. Cao Qiu returned to his hometown, he asked Dou Changjun to write a letter to introduce him to Ji Bu. Dou Changjun said: "General Ji doesn't like you, so don't go."
Cao Qiu insisted on asking Dou Changjun to write a letter of introduction. After finally getting it, he set off.
Cao Qiu first sent a letter of introduction from Dou Changjun to Ji Bu. Ji Bu was furious after receiving the letter and waited for Cao Qiu's arrival.
When Cao Qiu arrived, he bowed to Ji Bu and said, "There is a proverb among the Chu people: getting a hundred catties of gold is not as good as getting a promise from Ji Bu." How could you gain such a reputation in the Liang and Chu areas?
Besides, I am from Chudi, and you are also from Chudi.
I spread your reputation all over the world, am I not important to you?
Why do you reject me so firmly!
Ji Bu was very happy. He invited Cao Qiu to come in and stayed with him for several months. He treated him as the most distinguished guest and gave him generous gifts.
The reason why Ji Bu's reputation is famous far and wide is because Cao Qiu promoted it for him!
Ji Bu's younger brother was named Ji Xin, and his courage surpassed all the people in Guanzhong. He was respectful and prudent in his treatment of others, and was willing to do justice and chivalry. Scholars from thousands of miles around were vying to serve him.
Ji Xin once killed someone and fled to Wu Di, hiding in Yuan Si's home.
Ji Xin served Yuan Si with the same courtesy as her elder brother, and treated Guan Fu and Ji Fu like her younger brothers.
He once served as a Sima under the Lieutenant, and Lieutenant Zhidu did not dare to treat him disrespectfully.
Many young people often secretly pretend to be his name and go out to do things.
At that time, Ji Xin was famous for his bravery, and Ji Bu was famous for his promise. Both were famous in Guanzhong.
Ji Bu's uncle Ding Gong served as the general of the Chu army.
Ding Gong once chased Han Gaozu for Xiang Yu to the west of Pengcheng, which put Gaozu in an embarrassing situation. When the soldiers were fighting hand to hand, Gaozu felt the crisis and turned to Duke Ding and said: Are we two heroes going to make things difficult for each other?
So Ding Gong led his troops back, and the King of Han escaped to relieve the siege.
After Xiang Yu's death, Ding Gong paid homage to Gaozu.
Emperor Gaozu captured Ding Gong and put him in the military camp for public display, saying: Ding Gong was unable to be loyal as King Xiang's subordinate, and it was Ding Gong who made King Xiang lose the world!
So he beheaded Ding Gong and said: "Let future generations serve as ministers not to imitate Ding Gong!"
Luan Bu was from Liang.
When Liang Wang Pengyue was a commoner, he dated Luan Bu.
Luan Bu's family was poor, so he was hired as a servant in Qidi for a liquor seller.
A few years later, Peng Yue came to Juye to work as a bandit, but Luan Bu was forcibly kidnapped and sold into the Yan Kingdom as a slave.
Because Luan Bu avenged his master's family, Yan general Zang Tu recommended him to be the captain.
Later Zang Tu became King of Yan and appointed Luan Bu as general.
When Zang Tu rebelled and the Han Dynasty attacked Yan, they captured Luan Bu.
When Liang Wang Pengyue heard about this, he proposed to the emperor and asked to redeem Luan Bu and make him the official of the Liang Kingdom.
Later, Luan Bu went to Qi as an envoy, but before he returned, the Han Dynasty summoned Peng Yue, punished him for treason, and killed Peng Yue's three tribes.
Afterwards, Peng Yue's head was hung under the gate of Luoyang City for public display, and an order was issued: If anyone dares to come to collect or visit the body, he will be arrested immediately.
At this time, Luan Bu returned from Qi and reported the situation of his mission under Peng Yue's head, while offering sacrifices and crying.
The officials arrested him and reported the matter to the emperor.
The emperor summoned Luan Bu and scolded him: "Are you going to rebel with Peng Yue?"
I ordered no one to collect the body, but you insist on sacrificing him and crying for him, then it is clear that you are rebelling with Peng Yue. Cook him quickly!
When the people around the emperor were lifting Luan Bu towards the soup pot, Luan Bu turned around and said, "I hope you can let me say a word before I die." The emperor said: What did you say?
Luan Bu said: When Your Majesty was trapped in Pengcheng and defeated at Xingyang and Chenggao, the reason why King Xiang could not advance westward smoothly was because King Peng held Liang and joined forces with the Han army to create difficulties for Chu.
At that time, as long as King Peng turns around and joins forces with Chu, Han will fail; if he joins forces with Han, Chu will fail.
Let’s talk about the Battle of Gaixia. Without King Peng, Xiang Yu would not have perished.
Now that the world has stabilized, King Peng accepted the Fujie and was granted the title, and he also wanted to pass on the title from generation to generation.
Now His Majesty only went to Liang to recruit troops. King Peng could not come due to illness, so His Majesty became suspicious and thought that he was planning to rebel. However, the signs of rebellion were not revealed, but his family was destroyed because of his strict demands on details. I am worried that everyone with meritorious deeds will feel that they are in danger.
Now that King Peng is dead, I would rather die than live, so please cook me.
So the emperor pardoned Luan Bu's sins and appointed him as captain.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Luan Bu served as the Prime Minister of the State of Yan, rising to the rank of general.
Luan Bu once said: When he is poor, he who cannot withstand physical and mental humiliation is not a good man; when he is rich and noble, he who cannot satisfy his gratification is not a virtuous man.
Therefore, Luan Bu would repay those who had been kind to him generously; and he would definitely use the law to get rid of those who had a grudge.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Luan Bu was granted the title of Marquis of Yu for his meritorious service in the war, and became the prime minister of Yan.
In places like Yan and Qi, temples were built for Luan Bu, called Luan Commune.
Luan Bu passed away in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty.
His son Luan Ben inherited the title and served as Taichang. Because the animals used for sacrifice were illegal, the feudal state was abolished.
Tai Shigong said: With Xiang Yu's arrogance, Ji Bu became famous in the Chu region for his bravery. He personally destroyed the enemy troops and took out the enemy's flag many times. He can be regarded as a hero.
However, he was punished and refused to die as a slave. How despicable he looked!
He must be conceited and talented, so he suffered humiliation without feeling ashamed, hoping to develop his unused talents, so he finally became a famous general in the Han Dynasty.
A virtuous person can really value his death. As for slaves, concubines and other lowly people who commit suicide out of anger, it is not considered brave. It is because they think there is no other way.
Luan Bu cried bitterly to Peng Yue. He regarded going to the soup pot to die as if he were going home. He truly knew that he should die well and not begrudge his life.
Even those who valued righteousness over life in ancient times could surpass him!

The Zhu family, recognizing Ji Bu, treated him well and arranged for him to work in the fields. translation:
Qu Yuan, named Ping, has the same surname as the Chu king's family.
Served as the left disciple of King Huai of Chu.
Qu Yuan was well-informed, had a strong memory, understood the principles of national stability and turmoil, and was good at rhetoric.
When Qu Yuan was at court, he discussed state affairs with King Huai of Chu in order to issue orders; when outside the court, he received guests and dealt with the affairs of the marquis.
King Huai of Chu trusted him very much.
The official Shangguan had the same position as Qu Yuan. In order to gain the favor of King Huai, he was very jealous of Qu Yuan's talents.
Once, King Huai ordered Qu Yuan to formulate a national law. Qu Yuan had just finished writing the draft but had not yet completed the final revision.
When Shangguan saw it, he wanted to take it for himself, but Qu Yuan refused to give it to him. He spoke ill of Qu Yuan to King Huai of Chu: Your Majesty, you asked Qu Yuan to make a decree. No one at the top or bottom did not know about it. Every time a decree was issued, Qu Yuan boasted of his achievements, saying that no one could make it except me.
King Huai was very angry after hearing this, so he alienated Qu Yuan.
Qu Yuan felt extremely sad that King Huai was unable to distinguish right from wrong, that his vision was blinded by flatterers and unable to distinguish truth from falsehood, that evil harmed justice, and that upright people were not tolerated by the court. Therefore, he wrote "Li Sao" with deep sorrow and deep thought.
The so-called "Li Sao" means encountering sorrow.
God is the origin of man; parents are the foundation of man.
When people are in a difficult situation, they have to remember their roots. Therefore, when the fatigue and hardship are extreme, there is no one who does not call God; when the pain is unbearable, there is no one who does not call for the parents.
Qu Yuan insisted on notarization, acted upright, was loyal to the king, and used his talents to the best of his ability. However, he was provoked by villains, and his situation could be said to be extremely embarrassing.
How can one not feel grief and indignation when one is doubted by the king because one is sincere for the country, and one is slandered by villains because one is loyal to the master?
Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao" precisely to express this feeling of grief and indignation.
Although "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" contains many works describing the love between men and women, it is not chaotic; although "The Book of Songs: Xiaoya" reveals the people's slander and resentment against the government, it does not advocate open rebellion. Qu Yuan's "Li Sao" can be said to have the advantages of both.
In "Li Sao", Qu Yuan traced the deeds of Emperor Ku upwards, praised Qi Huan's great achievements in modern times, and described the virtues of Shang Tang and Zhou Wu in the middle to criticize current affairs.
It explains the breadth and depth of moral content and the inevitable cause and effect of the rise and fall of ordering chaos. These are all explained in great detail.
Its language is simple and concise, but its content has profound meanings, its emotions are noble, and its conduct is honest. Although its sentences are about small things, its meaning is extremely grand and profound. Although the examples it cites are common examples, the meaning they entrust is extremely far-reaching.
His emotions are noble, so he likes to use vanilla as a metaphor.
His character was upright, so he would not relax his demands on himself even until his death.
Being able to be washed clean in the muddy water is like a cicada being able to be freed from the turbidity and filth. It floats outside the dust and is not stained by the turbidity of the world. It is pure and noble, emerging from the mud without being stained.
Inferring his noble emotions, it is appropriate to compete with the sun and the moon.
Qu Yuan had been demoted. After that, Qin planned to attack Qi, and Qi and Chu joined forces to have a blind date. King Qin Hui was worried about this, so he sent Zhang Yi to pretend to leave Qin and bring rich gifts to serve Chu. He said: Qin hates Qi very much.
King Huai of Chu greedily listened to Zhang Yi's words, broke off diplomatic relations with Qi, and sent envoys to Qin to accept the land.
Zhang Yi deceived the envoy of the Chu State and said: I, Zhang Yi, agreed with King Huai of Chu to be six miles, but I have never heard of six hundred miles.
The Chu envoy left Qin angrily and returned to report to King Huai of Chu.
King Huai of Chu was angry and raised troops to attack Qin.
The Qin State sent troops to attack the Chu army, and defeated the Chu army in the Danshui and Xishui areas. It killed 80,000 Chu soldiers, captured the Chu general Qu, and took advantage of the situation to seize the Hanzhong area of ​​the Chu state.
King Huai of Chu dispatched all the troops from across the country to attack Qin and fought in Lantian.
When Wei heard the news, he sent troops to attack Chu and penetrated as far as Deng Yi.
The Chu army was frightened, so they withdrew from Qin and returned home.
However, the state of Qi finally refused to rescue the state of Chu because of anger, and the state of Chu was in great distress.
The next year, Qin proposed to cede the land in Hanzhong to make peace with Chu, but King Huai of Chu said: I don't want to get the land, I just want Zhang Yi and I will be content.
When Zhang Yi heard this, he said: "I, Zhang Yi, can come to Hanzhong and ask the king to allow me to go to Chu."
After Zhang Yi arrived in Chu State, he gave generous gifts to Jin Shang, the powerful minister of Chu State, and used sweet words to deceive King Huai's concubine Zheng Xiu. King Huai actually listened to Zheng Xiu's words and let Zhang Yi run away again.
At this time, Qu Yuan had been alienated and no longer held important official positions. He had just been sent as an envoy to Qi State. After returning, he admonished King Huai and said: Your Majesty, why don't you kill Zhang Yi?
King Huai felt very regretful and sent people to chase him, but it was too late.
After that, all the vassal states jointly attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army, and killed the Chu general Tang Wei.
At that time, King Zhao of Qin was married to Chu and wanted to meet King Huai of Chu. King Huai of Chu wanted to go. Qu Yuan advised him: Qin is a greedy and violent country like tigers and wolves. It cannot be trusted, so it is better not to go.
But King Huai's youngest son Zilan persuaded King Huai to go, saying: "Why do you want to cut off King Qin's good intentions?"
King Huai finally went.
But as soon as he entered Wuguan, the Qin Dynasty's ambush cut off his return and detained King Huai in order to make him agree to cede the land.
King Huai was furious and refused to agree.
He fled to the State of Zhao, but the State of Zhao refused to accept him.
Then he came to the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin. His body was transported back to the State of Chu for burial.
King Huai's eldest son, King Qingxiang, succeeded to the throne and appointed his younger brother Zilan as Ling Yin.
Zilan persuaded King Huai to enter Qin and eventually died in Qin. People in Chu blamed Zilan for this.
Qu Yuan also hated Zilan very much for what he did. Although he was exiled, he was still attached to the Kingdom of Chu, missed King Huai, and always thought about returning to the court. He always hoped that the king would suddenly wake up and change his bad customs.
He always remembered the king, revived the country, and reversed the situation, so he expressed this feeling many times in a work.
However, there was nothing he could do, so it was impossible to return to the court. This also shows that King Huai did not wake up in the end.
As a king, no matter he is smart or stupid, talented or not, he hopes to find loyal ministers and wise men to assist him in governing the country. However, the destruction of the country and the destruction of the family continue to happen, but the sage king and the peaceful country have not been seen for many generations. The fundamental reason is that the so-called loyal ministers are not loyal, and the so-called wise men are not wise.
Because King Huai did not know the duties of a loyal minister, he was deceived by Zheng Xiu internally and deceived by Zhang Yi externally. He alienated Qu Yuan and trusted Shangguan officials and Ling Yin Zilan.
As a result, the army was defeated miserably, the country was invaded, and the territory of six counties was lost. He also lived in a foreign country, died in Qin, and was ridiculed by the people of the world.
This is a disaster caused by ignorant people.
"Book of Changes" says: It is sad that the well has been dredged but no one comes to drink water.
If the king is wise, everyone can be happy.
And King Huai is so ignorant, how can he deserve happiness?
Ling Yin Zilan was furious when he heard the above situation, and finally asked Shangguan officials to speak ill of Qu Yuan to King Qingxiang. King Qingxiang banished Qu Yuan when he was angry.
Qu Yuan came to the riverside, his hair disheveled and walking on the grass in the wilderness, groaning in sorrow and indignation.
His face was haggard and his body was thin.
When a fisherman saw him, he asked: "Aren't you Dr. Sanlu?"
Why come here?
Qu Yuan said: The whole society is dirty but I am the only one who is clean. Everyone is drunk but I am the only one who is sober, so I was exiled.
The fisherman said: For a person who has reached the highest level of moral cultivation, his views on things are not static, but can change with the secular trend. People in the whole society are dirty, why don't you just follow the trend?
Everyone is drunk, why don't you eat some leftovers among them?
Why do you want to maintain your beautiful character and end up being exiled?
Qu Yuan replied: I have heard that people who have just washed their heads must flick off the dust on their hats, and people who have just washed their bodies must shake off the dust on their clothes. Who among the people is willing to let his innocent body be tainted by the dirt of the outside world?
I would rather jump into the long river and be buried in the belly of the fish than let my innocent character be polluted by the world!
Therefore, Qu Yuan wrote the work "Huaisha", in which he wrote:
In the early summer when the sun is strong, the grass and trees are growing lushly.
Sadness always fills my chest, and I hurried to the south.
There was a vast expanse in front of me, so silent that there was no sound.
My mood is gloomy and sad. This sad day is too long. He can reflect with his heart without making any mistakes, and he can restrain himself without fear when he is wronged.
I want to cut square wood into round wood, but the normal method cannot be changed. Forsaking the right path and taking a crooked path will be despised by a gentleman.
Clarify the norms, keep the laws in mind, and never go back on the original intention of the past. He has a loyal character and an upright heart, and is praised by gentlemen.
If a skilled craftsman does not wield an ax to chop, who can tell whether it is up to standard?
If the black pattern is placed in a dark place, a blind person will say that the pattern is not bright; Li Lou can see it very clearly with a glance, but the blind person will say that he is blind.
Things are so confusing, up and down.
The phoenix was put in a cage, but the chickens and pheasants were flying around there.
Beautiful jade and rough stone are mixed together, and some people actually think that the two are not much different.
Those gangsters are despicable and jealous, and have no understanding of my noble sentiments.
There is a long way to go, the load is too much, and we are stuck and unable to move forward. You are blessed with beautiful jade and are of high moral character. Who can you offer it to when you are in a difficult situation?
The dogs in the city were barking randomly, thinking they were seeing something strange and barking. Slandering a handsome man and doubting a hero is the ugly behavior of a villain.
I am rough on the outside but simple on the inside, but no one knows my brilliance. The uncarved material was thrown away, and no one knew the wisdom and virtue I possessed.
I pay attention to the cultivation of benevolence and righteousness, and strengthen it with respect and loyalty. Yu Shun will never be seen again, and who knows that I can calmly persist in my ambition.
It is rare for ancient sages to be born in the same world. Who can understand the reason?
Shang Tang and Xia Yu are so far away from us now. It is so vast and boundless that it is difficult to catch up.
Suppress your grief and anger, suppress your heart and make yourself stronger. I will not change my original intention despite suffering. I just hope that my ambition will become an example for future generations to follow.
I followed the road north again, facing the fading sunlight. Containing melancholy and forcing a happy face, death is not far ahead.
Epilogue: The mighty Yuanjiang and Xiangjiang rivers are constantly flowing and surging with waves.
The road is long and dark, and the future is so unclear.
I keep singing with long-lasting sadness, sighing with emotion to end this life.
No one in the world understands me. Who can listen to my heart?
The sentiment is noble, the quality is beautiful, and the fragrance is pure and unparalleled in the world.
Bole has died a long time ago. Who can identify the Chollima horse as Junliang?
Life is a destiny, and everyone has different arrangements.
With a firm heart and a broad mind, there is nothing else to be afraid of!
Heavy sadness and long sigh, sighing and mourning forever.
The world is turbid and there are few close friends. People's hearts are unpredictable and difficult to guess.
You must die in this world, so don't cherish your own life too much. Tell this clearly to the world, gentlemen, that I will always be a role model for others.
So Qu Yuan threw himself into the Miluo River with stones in his arms and committed suicide.
After Qu Yuan's death, there were Song Yu, Tang Le, Jing Cha and others in the Chu State. They all loved literature and were famous for their good poetry and poetry. But they all only learned the euphemistic and implicit side of Qu Yuan's speech, and in the end no one dared to express his advice as bluntly as Qu Yuan did.
After that, the Chu State became weaker and weaker day by day, and was finally eliminated by the Qin State decades later.
More than a hundred years after Qu Yuan sank into the river and died, there was a man named Jia Sheng in the Han Dynasty who passed by the Xiang River when he was serving as the Prince of Changsha. He wrote a poem and threw it into the river to pay homage to Qu Yuan.
Jia Sheng's name is Jia Yi, and he is from Luoyang.
At the age of eighteen, he became famous locally for reciting poetry and writing articles.
When Wu Tingwei was serving as the governor of Henan County, he heard that Jia Yicai had excellent academic performance, so he summoned him to serve in the Yamen and regarded him very highly.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he heard that Wu Gong, the governor of Henan Province, had outstanding political achievements and was ranked first in the country. He was from the same hometown as Li Si and had learned from Li Si, so he recruited him as a court captain.
Wu Tingwei recommended that Jia Yi was young and talented, and could be proficient in the knowledge of hundreds of schools of thought.
In this way, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty recruited Jia Yi to serve as a doctor.
At that time, Jia Yi was more than 20 years old and the youngest among the Ph.D.
Every time Emperor Wen ordered the doctors to discuss some issues, the older gentlemen had nothing to say, but Jia Yi could answer them one by one, and everyone felt that they had said what they wanted to say.
Doctors all believed that Jia Sheng's talent was outstanding and unparalleled.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty also liked him very much and promoted him to Taizhong doctor within a year.
Jia Yi believed that it had been more than twenty years since the founding of the Western Han Dynasty and Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had reached peace in the world. It was the time to correct the calendar, change the colors of clothes, establish systems, determine official names, and revitalize rituals and music. So he drafted various rituals, advocating yellow, following the theory of the five elements, and creating official names, which completely changed the old laws of the Qin Dynasty.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had just ascended the throne and was too modest to make concessions in time.
However, subsequent changes in various laws and regulations, as well as the fact that princes must go to the fiefdom to take office, were all Jia Yi's ideas.
So Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty discussed with his ministers and wanted to promote Jia Yi to the position of public minister.
However, Jianghou Zhou Bo, Guan Ying, Dongyang Hou, Feng Jing and others were jealous of him, so they slandered Jia Yi and said: This Luoyang man is young and has little knowledge. He only wants to monopolize power and make political affairs a mess.
After that, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty alienated Jia Yi, no longer adopted his opinions, and appointed him as the Grand Tutor of Changsha.
After Jia Yi said goodbye to Emperor Wen, he went to Changsha to take up his post. He heard that Changsha has a low-lying terrain and humid climate. He thought that his life would not be very long, and because he was demoted to this place, he felt very unhappy.
When he was crossing the Xiang River, he wrote a poem to commemorate Qu Yuan. The poem said: I respectfully obeyed the emperor's edict and came to Changsha to take up a post despite being guilty.
I have heard that Qu Yuan died after sinking into the Miluo River.
Today I came to the bank of the Xiangjiang River and asked the water to pay homage to Mr.
Encountering a chaotic society forces you to commit suicide and lose your life. Oh, how sad!
Just in time for those unfortunate times.
Luan and phoenix lurk and hide, but owl and owl fly freely.
Untalented people are noble and distinguished, while flatterers are ambitious and ambitious; sages and sages cannot follow suit, and upright people are relegated to inferior positions.
The world actually calls Boyi greedy, but the thieves are honest; Moye's sword is too blunt, but the lead knife is sharp.
Alas! Sir, you are so unfortunate that you have suffered this misfortune for no reason!
He abandoned the priceless tripod passed down from the Zhou Dynasty and regarded the broken gourd as a rare item. They drove tired old oxen and lame donkeys, but let the horses pull the salt carts with their ears drooped.
How can we live like this for a long time with a good hat used as an insole? Oops, it’s such a shame, Mr. Qu, that you are the only one to suffer this unexpected disaster! Epilogue: Forget it!
Since the Chinese people don’t understand me, who can I talk to about my depression and unhappiness?
The phoenix flies away and flies away, as it should have retired.
Follow the example of the divine dragon and hide in the depths of the abyss, hiding deep to avoid disaster and cherish yourself.
How can we be neighbors with ants, leeches, and earthworms when we are hiding in a hidden place?
The moral character of a saint is the most valuable. He stays away from the troubled world and hides himself.
If a good horse can be tied, how can it be different from dogs and sheep?
The world is in chaos and this disaster has happened, and the gentleman himself is also to blame.
You can choose your prince when you travel across the nine states, why should you be reluctant to leave your hometown?
The phoenix flies thousands of feet and only comes down to rest when it sees a virtuous king. Once you see signs of danger, fly high and fly away.
How can a small, dirty puddle accommodate a large fish that swallows a boat?
The big fish that dominates the world will eventually be controlled by ants.
In Jia Yi's third year as the Prince of Changsha, an owl flew into his residence and landed next to his seat.
The people of Chu called the owl Fu.
Jia Yi originally came to Changsha because he was demoted, and Changsha has a low-lying terrain and a humid climate, so he thought that his life would not be long, and he was sad and sad, so he wrote a poem to comfort himself.
The poem reads:
In the early summer of April of the Dingmao year, when the sun was setting on Gengzi Day, an owl flew into my house. It stopped next to the seat, looking so relaxed and at ease.
A strange bird came into my house, and I secretly wondered why. Open the hexagram book for divination, and it contains the following words: If a wild bird flies into the house, the owner will leave the house.
Please tell me, bird, where will I go when I leave here?
If it is good luck, please tell me; if it is bad luck, please tell me what kind of disaster it is.
Life and death are determined by delay and speed. Please tell me the time limit carefully.
The bird sighed after hearing this, raised its head and flapped its wings in understanding. If you can't speak with your mouth, please use your thoughts to guide yourself.
All things in heaven and earth are constantly changing, and there is no end to them.
Such as vortex rotation, repeated circulation.
The transformation of the appearance and inner energy continues, evolving like a cicada's transformation.
The truth is so profound that words cannot explain it comprehensively.
Blessings are hidden in disasters, and disasters are also hidden in blessings. Worry and joy come together, good fortune and misfortune are in the same realm.
The state of Wu was so powerful back then, but King Wu Fuchai was defeated because of it. The Yue Kingdom was defeated in Kuaiji, and Gou Jian used this to dominate the world.
Li Si traveled to Qin successfully, but finally suffered five punishments. Fu Yue was originally a prisoner, but later became the Prime Minister of Wu Ding.
What is the difference between misfortunes and blessings and the entanglement of ropes?
Destiny cannot be explained in detail. Who can predict its outcome?
The water turns into a torrent with great force, and the arrow can be shot far if it encounters strong force.
All things are cyclical and turbulent, changing each other in motion.
The clouds rise and the rain falls repeatedly, and the changes are complicated and complicated.
The movement of heaven and earth creates all things, so boundless and vast.
The way of heaven is profound and unpredictable, and it is difficult for mortals to think and plan.
Sooner or later, life and death are determined by fate. Who can know when it will come?
What's more, the heaven and the earth are a giant furnace, and nature is the stoker. The movement of yin and yang is the charcoal of a furnace, and everything in the world is made of copper.
Where can there be traces of routines in gathering and dispersing or birth and death? Intricate and varied, with no end in sight.
Adulthood is also an accident, not enough to cherish and cherish eternal life. Even if you die and turn into a foreign body, why worry and fear!
People with little wisdom take care of themselves, despise external things and value their own bodies. How magnanimous it is to understand people's enlightenment, and there will be no misfortunes or blessings in life or death.
A greedy husband sacrifices his life for money, a martyr forgets his life and death for his name. Those who like false fame die for power, while ordinary people are afraid of death and greedy for life.
And those who are tempted by fame and fortune, forced by poverty and low status, travel west and east in order to make a living. People with extremely high moral cultivation will not succumb to material desires and treat millions of things equally.
A foolish man is fettered by worldly burdens and is restrained like a prisoner. A person with supreme virtue can abandon the world and exist only with the Great Way.
Everyone in the world is confused and filled with feelings of love and hatred. People with true virtue are indifferent and live alone and in harmony with the great road.
Abandoning wisdom and forgetting oneself, becoming transcendent and unaware of oneself. In that empty and trance state, soar together with the avenue.
Riding on the flowing water, one can travel freely and stop when one encounters a small island. Entrust your body to fate and do not regard it as a private body.
Living is like living in the world, and dying is like a long rest. Inner peace is like a waveless abyss, and floating is like a boat without a mooring line.
Do not focus on your own life because of living, and cultivate your ethereal nature without being rigid. The most virtuous person has no worldly burdens, and he is happy and knows his fate, so there is no need to worry!
Trivial matters are nothing worth worrying about!
More than a year later, Jia Yi was recalled to the capital to meet the emperor.
At that time, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was sitting in the propaganda room, receiving blessings from God.
Because Emperor Wen was interested in ghosts and gods, he asked Jia Yi about the origin of ghosts and gods.
Jia Yi took the opportunity to explain in detail the various situations that led to the occurrence of ghosts and gods.
By midnight, Emperor Wen was so absorbed in listening that he unconsciously moved towards Jia Yi in his seat. After listening, Emperor Wen sighed: I haven't seen Jia Yi for a long time. I thought I could surpass him, but now it seems I'm still not as good as him.
Soon after, Emperor Wen appointed Jia Yi as the Taifu of King Lianghuai.
King Lianghuai was the youngest son of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty. He was favored by Emperor Wen and liked to read, so he asked Jia Yi to be his teacher.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty also granted the title of Liehou to the four sons of King Li of Huainan.
Jia Yi advised him, believing that the rise of national disasters would start from here.
Jia Yi appealed to the emperor many times, saying that some princes had too many fiefdoms, even covering several counties, which was inconsistent with the ancient system, and their power should be gradually weakened, but Emperor Wen of Han refused to listen.
A few years later, King Liang Huai fell off his horse and died due to careless riding, leaving no descendants.
Jia Yi believed that he had failed to fulfill his responsibilities as a tutor. He was very sad and cried for more than a year before he died.
He was only thirty-three years old when he died.
Later, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ascended the throne and promoted Jia Yi's two grandsons to serve as county guards. Among them, Jia Jia was the most eager to learn. He inherited Jia Yi's family business and had exchanges of letters with me.
By the time of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, he held the post of Jiuqing.
Tai Shigong said: After reading "Li Sao", "Heavenly Questions", "Calling the Soul" and "Ai Ying", I felt very sorry for Qu Yuan's ambition.
When I came to Changsha and visited the place where Qu Yuan drowned himself in the river, I couldn't help but shed tears and miss him as a person.
After reading Jia Sheng's poem in memory of Qu Yuan, I privately blamed Qu Yuan for his talent. If he went to lobby the princes, which country would not tolerate him? And actually put himself in such a situation!
After reading "Ode to the Birds", I realized that life and death were treated equally, and the ups and downs of one's life experience were not taken seriously. I couldn't help but feel at a loss.
summary:
Qu Yuan, named Ping, shared the same surname as the Chu royal family and served as a left disciple under King Huai of Chu. He was knowledgeable, had a strong memory, understood statecraft, and was skilled in rhetoric. King Huai trusted him deeply, but the official Shangguan, jealous of Qu Yuan's talents, slandered him by claiming Qu Yuan boasted about his own decrees. King Huai believed this and alienated Qu Yuan. Grief-stricken by the king's inability to discern truth from falsehood, Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao," a work expressing his sorrow and indignation. The text praises "Li Sao" for combining the virtues of "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" and "Xiaoya," using metaphors like vanilla to symbolize noble character, and comparing Qu Yuan's purity to the sun and moon.

After Qu Yuan's demotion, Qin, fearing the Qi-Chu alliance, sent Zhang Yi to deceive Chu. King Huai, swayed by greed, broke ties with Qi and was tricked into believing Qin would cede six hundred miles of land, only to receive six. Enraged, King Huai attacked Qin but suffered a devastating defeat, losing 80,000 soldiers and the Hanzhong region. Wei also attacked Chu, and Qi refused aid. Later, Qin proposed peace, but King Huai demanded Zhang Yi. Zhang Yi bribed Chu officials and King Huai's concubine, Zheng Xiu, to secure his release. Qu Yuan, then an envoy to Qi, urged King Huai to kill Zhang Yi, but it was too late. Subsequently, vassal states defeated Chu, killing General Tang Wei. King Zhao of Qin invited King Huai for a meeting; Qu Yuan warned against it, but King Huai's son Zilan persuaded him to go. King Huai was captured, refused to cede land, fled to Zhao (which rejected him), and died in Qin. His body was returned to Chu.

King Qingxiang succeeded King Huai and appointed Zilan as Ling Yin. Qu Yuan, exiled but still loyal, blamed Zilan for King Huai's death and hoped for reform. However, Zilan and Shangguan slandered Qu Yuan to King Qingxiang, leading to his banishment. Qu Yuan wandered by the river, disheveled and gaunt. A fisherman asked why he was exiled; Qu Yuan replied that he alone was pure in a corrupt world. The fisherman advised adapting to the times, but Qu Yuan refused to taint his integrity, preferring to die in the river. He wrote "Huaisha," expressing his resolve to maintain his principles despite injustice. He then drowned himself in the Miluo River.

After Qu Yuan's death, Chu scholars like Song Yu imitated his style but lacked his boldness. Chu weakened and was conquered by Qin decades later. Over a century later, Jia Yi of the Han Dynasty, while serving as Grand Tutor of Changsha, wrote a poem to honor Qu Yuan. Jia Yi, a talented young scholar from Luoyang, was favored by Emperor Wen of Han but slandered by officials like Zhou Bo, leading to his demotion. He wrote "Ode to the Birds" to console himself, reflecting on the cyclical nature of fortune and the futility of worldly concerns. Later, he served as tutor to King Liang Huai, who died in a riding accident. Jia Yi, blaming himself, died of grief at age 33. The historian Sima Qian, after reading Qu Yuan's works and Jia Yi's poems, initially criticized Qu Yuan for not seeking refuge elsewhere but later, after reading "Ode to the Birds," understood his equanimity toward life and death.

Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a young master of the State of Zhao.
Among the many princes, Zhao Sheng was the most virtuous and talented. He was hospitable and cultivated scholars. There were about thousands of guests who came to his sect.
Lord Pingyuan served as the prime minister of King Zhao Huiwen and King Xiaocheng. He left the position of prime minister three times and was reinstated three times. His fiefdom was in Dongwu City.
Mr. Pingyuan's house has a tall building facing the houses below.
There was a lame man in the house who always limped out to fetch water.
A beautiful concubine of Mr. Pingyuan lived upstairs. One day she looked down and saw the lame man fetching water, and she burst out laughing.
The next day, the cripple came to Lord Pingyuan's house and asked: "I heard that you love scholars. The reason why scholars are not afraid of traveling thousands of miles to join your family is because you value scholars and despise concubines."
I was unfortunately ill and disabled, but your concubine was laughing at me from a high building. I wanted to get the head of the person who laughed at me. Mr. Pingyuan smiled and replied: "Okay."
After the lame man left, Lord Pingyuan smiled again and said: Look at this boy, he wants to kill my concubine just because of a smile. Isn't it too much?
I didn't kill that person after all.
More than a year later, more than half of the guests and diners on errands left one after another.
Mr. Pingyuan felt very strange about this situation and said: I, Zhao Sheng, never dare to be rude in all aspects of my treatment of gentlemen, but why are so many people leaving me?
A retainer stepped forward and replied: Because you did not kill the concubine who laughed at the cripple, everyone thought that you liked beauty and despised the scholars, so the scholars left one after another.
So Lord Pingyuan cut off the head of the concubine who laughed at the cripple. He personally visited the lame man's house and offered it to him, and took the opportunity to apologize to him.
From then on, the original guests came back one after another.
At that time, Qi State had Lord Mengchang, Wei State had Lord Xinling, and Chu State had Lord Chunshen. They were all hospitable to scholars, so they competed to be more courteous to scholars than others in order to attract more talents to themselves.
When the Qin State besieged Handan, King Zhao sent Lord Pingyuan to ask for help. At that time, he planned to recommend Chu as the leader of the alliance and make a joint alliance to fight against Qin. Lord Pingyuan agreed to go to Chu State with twenty of his followers who were brave, resourceful, and capable of both civil and military affairs.
Mr. Pingyuan said: It would be best if we can succeed through polite negotiations.
If the negotiation fails to succeed, then the king of Chu will be coerced to confirm the alliance in public, and he must confirm the alliance before returning home.
The civil and military people who are going with me don’t have to look outside. It’s enough to choose from the diners under my sect.
In the end, nineteen people were selected, and there was nothing left to choose from. There was no way to gather twenty people.
At this time, a man named Mao Sui among the diners walked up to the front and recommended himself to Lord Pingyuan: I heard that you are going to Chu State, and let Chu State be the leader of the alliance to make an alliance. You also agreed to go with twenty diners, and no one will go outside to search.
There is still one person missing now, I hope you can use me to recharge and go together.
Mr. Pingyuan asked: How many years has it been since Mr. Wang stayed with me?
Mao Sui replied: It has been three years now.
Mr. Pingyuan said: A talented wise man living in the world is like an awl placed in a pocket, its sharp edge will be revealed immediately.
It has been three years since your husband has been under my care for three years now. None of my close ministers have ever praised or recommended you, and I have never heard of you. This is because your husband has no expertise.
Sir, you can't go. Sir, please stay.
Mao Sui said: I just want to put it in my pocket today.
If I had been placed in the pocket, the entire cone would have been exposed, not just the tip.
Lord Pingyuan finally agreed to let Mao Sui go with him.
The nineteen people winked at each other and laughed at Mao Sui secretly, but did not make a sound.
When Mao Sui arrived in Chu, he discussed and argued with the nineteen people about the situation in the world. All nineteen people admired him.
The Lord of Pingyuan negotiated with the King of Chu to establish a joint alliance. They repeatedly stated their interests. They negotiated from morning until noon until no decision was made. The nineteen people encouraged Mao Sui and said: "Sir, please come to the court."
So Mao Sui gripped the hilt of his sword tightly, trotted all the way up the steps to the palace, and said to Lord Pingyuan: Talking about cooperation is either beneficial or harmful, just two sentences.
Now we have been talking about the marriage since the morning, but by noon we still can’t decide. What’s the reason?
When the King of Chu saw Mao Sui coming to the court, he said to Lord Pingyuan: "What does this man do?"
Lord Pingyuan replied: "This is my retainer."
The King of Chu shouted sternly: "Why don't you let me go down?"
I'm negotiating with your master, what are you doing here?
Mao Sui clenched the hilt of his sword and stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty, you dare to scold me, but you are relying on the large number of people in Chu."
Now I am only ten steps away from you. Within ten steps, the king cannot rely on the large number of people in Chu. The king's life is in my hands.
My master is right in front of me. Why are you scolding me like this in front of him?
Moreover, I heard that Shang Tang once ruled the world with a land of seventy miles, and King Wen of Zhou made the world surrender with a land of a hundred miles. Is it because they had many soldiers? In fact, it was because they were good at grasping the situation and exerting their power.
Nowadays, the Chu State has a territory of 5,000 miles and millions of soldiers. This is the capital it relies on to strive for kingship and hegemony.
With the Chu State being so powerful, no one in the world could stop its power.
Bai Qi of the Qin State was just a child. With tens of thousands of troops, he sent troops to fight against the Chu State. In the first battle, he captured Yancheng and Yingdu, in the second battle, he burned Yiling, and in the third battle, the king's ancestors were greatly humiliated.
This is a hatred that has lasted for centuries in the Chu Kingdom. Even King Zhao felt ashamed, but the king did not feel ashamed.
The alliance alliance is for the Chu State, not for the Zhao State.
My master is right in front of me, why are you scolding me like this?
After hearing Mao Sui's words, the King of Chu immediately changed his attitude and said: Yes, yes, it is indeed as the gentleman said. I will do my best to fulfill the alliance covenant.
Mao Sui pressed further and asked: Is the alliance agreement confirmed?
King Chu replied: "It's confirmed."
So Mao Sui said to the king of Chu's ministers in a commanding tone: "Bring the blood of chickens, dogs, and horses."
Mao Sui knelt down with the copper plate in his hands, presented it to the King of Chu and said: Your Majesty, you should suck the blood first to show your sincerity in confirming the alliance. The next one is my master, and the next one is me.
In this way, the alliance alliance was confirmed in the palace of Chu State.
At this time, Mao Sui held up a plate of blood with his left hand and called to the nineteen people with his right hand: "Everyone in the audience will also suck the blood from the plate. Although you are mediocre, you have completed your task. This is what is called relying on the strength of others to complete your task."
Lord Pingyuan confirmed the alliance and returned to Zhao State. After returning to Zhao State, he said: I don't dare to observe and identify talents anymore.
When I observe and identify talents, I say thousands at most and hundreds at least. I thought I would not miss out on all the talented people in the world, but now I have missed Mr. Mao.
Mr. Mao's first visit to the Chu State made the status of the Zhao State more noble than the national treasure of Jiuding Dalu.
Mr. Mao, with his eloquent mouth, was actually more powerful than an army of millions.
I no longer dare to observe and identify talents.
So he treated Mao Sui as a distinguished guest.
After Lord Pingyuan returned to the State of Zhao, the State of Chu sent Lord Chunshen to lead troops to rescue Zhao State. Lord Xinling of Wei State also pretended to ask for his orders and seized the military power of Jin Bi to lead troops to rescue State of Zhao, but none of them arrived yet.
At this time, Qin State quickly besieged Handan. Handan was in a hurry and was about to surrender. Lord Pingyuan was extremely anxious.
Li Tong, the son of an official at the Handan Hotel, persuaded Lord Pingyuan: "Aren't you worried about the demise of Zhao?"
Lord Pingyuan said: If Zhao is destroyed, then I will be a prisoner. Why not worry?
Li Tong said: "The people of Handan are using human bones as firewood and exchanging children for food. It can be said that they are in extreme danger. However, you have hundreds of concubines and maids in your harem. The maids wear silk embroidered clothes and cannot eat the fine food. However, the people are unable to cover themselves with coarse shorts and cannot eat enough wine dregs and grain husks."
The people are tired and their weapons are exhausted. Some people sharpen wood to use as spears and arrows, but your precious playthings, copper bells and jade, are still intact.
If the Qin army breaks Zhao, how can you have these things?
If the State of Zhao can be preserved, why would you worry about not having these things?
Now you can really order all the members below the wife to be organized into the soldiers, and they will be responsible for the labor of guarding the city, and distribute all the things in the house for the soldiers to enjoy. When the soldiers are in crisis and hardship, it is easy to be grateful.
So Pingyuan Jun adopted Li Tong's advice and got 3,000 soldiers who dared to risk their lives.
Li Tong joined a team of 3,000 people and rushed to the Qin army for a decisive battle. As a result, the Qin army was pushed back thirty miles.
At this time, it happened that reinforcements from Chu and Wei arrived, and the Qin army withdrew, and Handan was preserved.
Li Tong was killed in battle with the Qin army, and his father was granted the title of Marquis Li.
Yu Qing wanted to request additional fiefdoms for Lord Pingyuan on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan.
When Gongsun Long heard the news, he drove overnight to see Lord Pingyuan and said: I heard that Yu Qing wanted to ask for additional fiefs on your behalf on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan. Is this true?
Mr. Pingyuan replied: Yes.
Gongsun Long said: This is very inappropriate.
It is said that the monarch appointed you as the prime minister of Zhao State, not because your intelligence and talent are unique to Zhao State and no one else has them.
The title of Dongwu City is granted to you not because of your meritorious deeds, but because you are a close relative of the monarch.
You didn't refuse to accept the seal because you were incompetent, and you didn't refuse to accept the title because you had no merit. It was also because you considered yourself a close relative of the monarch.
Now Lord Xinling has sent troops to save Handan and you ask for an increase in the number of fiefs. This is because you accepted the fiefs as close relatives when you had no merit, but when you did meritorious service, you asked for rewards based on ordinary people's merits.
This is obviously very inappropriate.
Moreover, Yu Qing holds the initiative on both sides of success and failure. If the thing succeeds, he will ask for compensation like a deed to collect debt; if the thing does not succeed, he will use the false name of claiming credit for you to make you grateful to him.
You must not listen to his advice.
Lord Pingyuan then rejected Yu Qing's suggestion.
Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Zhao Xiaocheng's reign.
Lord Pingyuan's descendants inherited his title from generation to generation, and his descendants were finally cut off when the Zhao Kingdom was destroyed.
Lord Pingyuan treated Gongsun Long very kindly.
Gongsun Long was good at debating the "Li Jian Bai" proposition. When Zou Yan visited Zhao State, he discussed the most upright principles and refuted Gongsun Long's famous debate proposition. After that, Lord Pingyuan dismissed Gongsun Long.
Yu Qing was a talented person who was good at lobbying. He wore straw sandals and an umbrella on his shoulders and came all the way to lobby King Zhao Xiaocheng.
When he visited King Zhao for the first time, King Zhao gave him a hundred yi of gold and a pair of white jade. When he visited King Zhao for the second time, he became the minister of Zhao, so he was called Yu Qing.
Qin and Zhao fought in Changping. Zhao was unfavorable in the first battle and lost one captain.
King Zhao summoned Lou Chang and Yu Qing to discuss the situation and said: "Our army did not go well in the first battle and the captain died in battle. I will roll up my armor and go to the enemy to fight the Qin army. What do you think?"
Lou Chang said: If there is no benefit, it is better to send important envoys to seek peace.
Yu Qing said: The reason why Lou Chang advocated for peace was that he believed that if he did not seek peace, our army would be defeated.
But the initiative to control the peace talks lies with Qin.
Moreover, Your Majesty, please estimate Qin's war intention. Is it to defeat Zhao's army, or not?
King Zhao replied: Qin has tried its best without reservation and will definitely defeat Zhao Jun.
Yu Qing went on to say: Your Majesty listened to my words and sent envoys to bring valuable treasures to unite Chu and Wei. If Chu and Wei want to get your Majesty's valuable treasures, they will definitely accept our envoys.
When envoys from the State of Zhao enter Chu and Wei, the State of Qin will definitely suspect that all the princes in the world are united to fight against Qin, and will definitely panic.
In this way, peace talks can proceed.
King Zhao did not listen to Yu Qing's advice and negotiated peace with Pingyang Lord Zhao Bao, so he sent Zheng Zhuxian to Qin to contact Qin.
Qin accepted Zheng Zhu.
King Zhao summoned Yu Qing again and said: I sent Lord Pingyang to Qin to seek peace. Qin has accepted Zheng and Zhu. What do you think?
Yu Qing replied: If the king's peace talks cannot succeed, Zhao Jun will definitely be defeated.
The envoys from all the princes in the world to congratulate Qin on its victory are all in Qin.
Zheng Zhu is a noble person. When he enters Qin, the king of Qin and the princes of Ying will definitely publicize Zheng Zhu's arrival in Qin and show it to all the princes in the world.
Chu and Wei believed that if Zhao went to Qin to seek peace, they would definitely not rescue the king.
The State of Qin knows that if the princes of the world do not rescue the king, then the peace talks will not be successful.
As expected, Marquis Ying publicized the fact that Zheng Zhu came to Qin and showed it to the envoys from all over the world who congratulated Qin for his victory, but he refused to negotiate peace after all.
The Zhao army was defeated in Changping, so Handan was besieged and was ridiculed by the world.
After the Qin State lifted the siege of Handan, King Zhao was planning to visit the King of Qin, so he sent Zhao Hao to the State of Qin to make a treaty and make peace with six counties.
Yu Qing said to King Zhao: "Look, Your Majesty, did Qin attack your Majesty and then withdraw because it was exhausted?"
Or is it able to attack, but stops attacking out of pity for the king?
King Zhao replied: Qin attacked me without any reservation and tried his best. He must have withdrawn because he was tired from the attack.
Yu Qing said: Qin used all its strength to attack the land it could not seize, but returned exhausted. However, the king gave Qin the land it could not seize for free. This was tantamount to helping Qin attack itself.
If Qin attacks the king again next year, the king will be unable to save himself.
King Zhao told Zhao Hao what Yu Qing said.
Zhao Hao said: Can Yu Qing really know the details of Qin's military strength?
If you really know that Qin's troops cannot attack this year, if you don't give it such a small piece of land, and let Qin attack the king again next year, won't the king want to cede the hinterland to it to sue for peace?
King Zhao said: I followed your advice and ceded six counties. Can you ensure that Qin will not attack me next year?
Zhao Hao replied: This is not something I dare to take on.
In the past, Han, Zhao and Wei had contacts with Qin and were friendly to each other.
Now that Qin is friendly to Han and Wei and attacks the king, it seems that the king's intention to serve Qin must be less than that of Han and Wei.
Now I will relieve you of the attack caused by betraying the good relationship with Qin, open the checkpoints, exchange trade, and have the same level of friendship with Qin as Korea and Wei. If next year the king alone invites Qin's attack, it must be that the king's intention to serve Qin has fallen behind Korea and Wei.
So, this is not something I dare to take on.
King Zhao told Yu Qing what Zhao Hao said.
Yu Qing replied: Zhao Hao said that if Qin doesn't make peace, next year Qin will attack the king again. Wouldn't the king want to cede his hinterland to it to seek peace?
Now that they are making peace, Zhao Hao believes that there is no guarantee that Qin will not attack again.
So what is the benefit of ceding six cities now?
Attack again next year, and cede to it the land that its troops cannot seize to sue for peace. This is a recipe for self-destruction, so it is better not to make peace.
Even if Qin is good at attacking, it cannot easily capture six counties; even if Zhao cannot defend, it will not lose six cities in the end.
If Qin is tired and withdraws its troops, the army will inevitably be weak.
I used six cities to gather the princes of the world to attack the weak Qin army. This is why I lost six cities to the princes of the world and gained compensation from Qin.
Our country can still benefit, which is better than ceding land for nothing, weakening itself and making Qin strong?
Now Zhao Hao said that the reason why Qin was on friendly terms with Han and Wei and attacked Zhao was that the king was not as willing to serve Qin as Han and Wei. This was to ask the king to devote six cities to serve Qin every year, which meant giving away all the cities in vain.
Next year Qin will ask for land again, will your Majesty give it to it?
If you don't give it, you will abandon the gains obtained by ceding the land and provoke Qin's attack; if you give it, there will be no land to give.
As the saying goes: The strong are good at attacking, the weak cannot defend.
Now they are simply at the mercy of Qin, and Qin's army can gain more land without any effort. This will make Qin stronger and Zhao weaker.
Let the increasingly powerful Qin State seize the increasingly weak Zhao State, and Qin's plan to seize Zhao's land every year will not stop.
Moreover, the king's land is limited but Qin's demands are unlimited. If the limited land of Zhao is used to meet the unlimited demands of Qin, then there will inevitably be no more Zhao.
Before King Zhao's idea was settled, Lou Huan returned to Zhao from Qin. King Zhao discussed this issue with Lou Huan and said: Which approach is better, giving land to Qin or not?
Lou slowly declined and said: This is not something I can know.
King Zhao said: Even so, you might as well try to express your personal opinions.
Lou Huan then replied: "Has your Majesty also heard about Gongfu Wenbo's mother?"
Gongfu Wenbo, who was an official in the state of Lu, died of illness. Two of his wives and concubines committed suicide in their bedroom for him.
His mother didn't even cry when she heard this.
The nanny of Gongfu Wenbo's family said: Where is the mother who doesn't cry when her son dies?
His mother said: Confucius was a great sage who was expelled by the State of Lu, but he no longer followed Confucius.
Now that he is dead, two of his wives and concubines have committed suicide for him. In such a situation, it must be that he has a weak affection for his elders but a deep affection for his wives and concubines.
So if a mother says something like this, she is a virtuous mother; if a wife says something like this, she must be a jealous wife.
Therefore, although the words are the same, the meaning of the words changes due to the different standpoints of the speakers.
Now I have just come from Qin. If I say not to give it, it is not the best policy. If I say to give it, I am afraid that the king will think that I am helping Qin. So I dare not answer.
If I can think about it for your Majesty, I might as well give it to you.
After hearing this, King Zhao said: Yes.
When Yu Qing heard about this, he went to the palace to see King Zhao and said, "This is a hypocritical argument. Your Majesty must not give Qin six counties!"
Lou Huan heard about it and went to see King Zhao.
King Zhao told Lou Huan what Yu Qing said.
Lou Huan said: No, Yu Qing knows one thing but not the other.
The enmity between Qin and Zhao caused war disasters, but all the princes in the world were very happy. Why is this? Said that we will use the strong country to bully the weak country. Now that Zhao's army is besieged by Qin, all the princes in the world congratulating them on their victory must be in Qin.
Therefore, it is better to cede the land quickly and make peace, so as to make the princes of the world doubt that Qin and Zhao are already on good terms and to appease Qin.
Otherwise, the princes of the world will take advantage of Qin's anger and Zhao's fatigue to carve up Zhao.
The State of Zhao is about to perish, so what plans does it have for the State of Qin?
Therefore, Yu Qing knows one thing but not the other.
I hope your Majesty will consider these aspects and decide to give it to you, and stop thinking about it.
After Yu Qing heard this discussion, he went to see King Zhao and said: "We are in danger. Lou Huan is here to help Qin. This only makes the princes of the world more suspicious of us. How can we appease Qin?"
Why didn't he say that doing so would show the princes of the world that Zhao was weak and could be bullied?
Besides, what I advocate about not giving land to Qin does not mean that we should just refuse to give it to Qin.
Qin asked the king for six cities, and the king gave these six cities to Qi.
The State of Qi is the mortal enemy of the State of Qin. If we get the king's six cities, we can join forces with us to attack the State of Qin. The King of Qi listens to the king's plan and agrees without waiting for the words to be finished.
This means that although the king lost six cities in Qi, he was compensated by Qin.
By doing this, the deep hatred between Qi and Zhao can be avenged, and it can also show to the princes in the world that King Zhao is capable.
Your Majesty, spread the word about the alliance between Qi and Zhao. Our troops will not have to go to the border to conduct reconnaissance. I will see Qin's valuable gifts sent to Zhao and in turn sue for peace from your Majesty.
Once peace is made with the King of Qin, when Han and Wei hear the news, they will try their best to respect the King. Since they want to respect the King, they must take out precious treasures and rush to pay tribute to the King.
In this way, the king's move can establish friendship with the three countries of Han, Wei, and Qi, and thus change the status of dealing with Qin. After hearing this, King Zhao said: Great.
So he sent Yu Qing east to visit the King of Qi and discuss with him the issue of attacking Qin.
Before Yu Qing returned to Qi, Qin's envoys were already in Zhao.
When Lou Huan learned the news, he immediately ran away.
King Zhao then granted a city to Yu Qing. Soon after, Wei State requested a treaty with Zhao State.
King Zhao Xiaocheng summoned Yu Qing to discuss the matter.
Yu Qing first went to visit Lord Pingyuan. Lord Pingyuan said: I hope to hear you discuss the way of combining vertical and horizontal lines.
Yu Qing entered the palace to meet King Zhao.
King Zhao said: The state of Wei requested an alliance.
Yu Qing said: Wei Guo was wrong.
King Zhao said: I didn't agree to it at first.
Yu Qing said: Your Majesty is wrong.
King Zhao said: Wei Guo asked for alliance, but you said Wei Guo was wrong; I did not agree to it, and you said I was wrong again. In this case, is it impossible to form a vertical alliance after all?
Yu Qing replied: I heard that small countries work together with big countries. If there are benefits, the big countries will enjoy the fruits, and if there are disadvantages, the small countries will bear the disasters.
The current situation is that Wei is willing to bear the disaster as a small country, but you refuse to enjoy the fruits as a big country. So I say that the king is wrong, and the state of Wei is also wrong.
I personally think that a vertical alliance is beneficial. King Zhao said: OK.
So he made an alliance with Wei State.
Because of Wei Qi, the Prime Minister of Wei State, Yu Qing preferred to abandon the title of Marquis of Wanhu and the Prime Minister's seal, and fled from a small road with Wei Qi. Finally, he left Zhao State and was trapped in Daliang of Wei State.
After Wei Qi's death, Yu Qing became even more dissatisfied. He wrote a book, collected historical facts from "Spring and Autumn", observed the modern world situation, and wrote a total of eight articles: "Jieyi", "Title", "Speculation" and "Political Strategy".
It is used to criticize the success and failure of national politics. It has been circulated in the world and is called "Yu's Spring and Autumn Annals".
Tai Shigong said: Mr. Pingyuan is a handsome and talented son in troubled times, but he cannot understand the overall situation.
As the saying goes: greed for personal gain will lead to loss of reason. Lord Pingyuan believed in Feng Ting's heresy and coveted the Shangdang he gave, which led to the Zhao State's defeat in Changping, more than 400,000 Zhao soldiers were killed, and the Zhao State was almost destroyed.
Yu Qing analyzed the affairs, speculated on the situation, and made suggestions for the State of Zhao. How thoughtful and ingenious he was!
In the end, I couldn't bear to watch Wei Qi being hunted down, and finally found himself in trouble in Daliang. Ordinary people knew they couldn't do this, let alone talented people.
But if Yu Qing had not been poor and sad, he would not have been able to write books and make his reputation known to the world and pass on to future generations.
summary:
Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a virtuous and talented young master of the State of Zhao, known for hosting thousands of scholars. He served as prime minister under Kings Huiwen and Xiaocheng, leaving and returning to the position three times, with his fief in Dongwu City. A crippled man fetching water near his home was laughed at by one of Lord Pingyuan’s concubines. The cripple demanded her head, but Lord Pingyuan initially refused, causing many scholars to leave. He later killed the concubine and apologized to the cripple, regaining his guests.

When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan sought help from Chu to form an alliance. He needed twenty followers but could only find nineteen. Mao Sui, a retainer for three years, volunteered. Lord Pingyuan doubted his abilities, but Mao Sui argued that if placed in a pocket, the entire awl would show, not just its tip. Mao Sui joined and impressed the others. In Chu, negotiations stalled until Mao Sui confronted the King of Chu, threatening him and highlighting Chu’s past defeats by Qin. The king agreed to the alliance, and Mao Sui sealed it with a blood oath. Lord Pingyuan later praised Mao Sui as more powerful than an army.

After returning, Chu and Wei sent reinforcements, but Handan remained in danger. Li Tong advised Lord Pingyuan to mobilize his household and distribute resources to the people, gaining 3,000 volunteers. Li Tong died in battle, pushing Qin back thirty miles, and Handan was saved when reinforcements arrived. Yu Qing sought additional fiefs for Lord Pingyuan, but Gongsun Long argued against it, noting Lord Pingyuan’s position and fief were due to kinship, not merit, and that Yu Qing’s proposal was self-serving. Lord Pingyuan rejected the request.

Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Xiaocheng’s reign, and his descendants held the title until Zhao’s fall. He treated Gongsun Long well but dismissed him after Zou Yan refuted his debates. Yu Qing, a skilled lobbyist, advised King Zhao against ceding land to Qin after the Changping defeat, proposing instead to ally with Qi. King Zhao initially agreed but later followed Lou Huan’s advice to cede land, leading to further conflict. Yu Qing eventually fled to Daliang, where he wrote “Yu’s Spring and Autumn Annals,” criticizing political failures.

Tai Shigong noted that Lord Pingyuan, though talented, failed to grasp the bigger picture, leading to Zhao’s defeat at Changping and the loss of 400,000 soldiers. Yu Qing’s plans were thoughtful, but his inability to avoid trouble in Daliang highlighted his flaws, though his writings ensured his legacy.
