translation:
Bian Que was from Miao, Bohai County. His surname was Qin and his name was Yue.
When he was young, he was the manager of a guesthouse.
A guest named Chang Sang came to the guest house. Only Bian Que thought he was a strange person and always treated him respectfully.
Chang Sangjun also knew that Bian Que was not an ordinary person. He had been coming and going for more than ten years. One day, he asked Bian Que to sit with him and quietly said to Bian Que: I have a secret medical prescription. I am old and I want to pass it on to you. Please don't leak it.
Bian Que said: "I respectfully obey my orders."
Then he took out the medicine in his arms and gave it to Bian Que, and said: Take this medicine with the dew on the grass and trees, and you will know many things in thirty days.
Then he took out all his secret recipes and gave them to Bian Que.
Suddenly the person disappeared, maybe he was not a mortal.
Bian Que took the medicine as he said for thirty days, and he could see the people on the other side of the wall.
Therefore, when diagnosing other people's diseases, you can see all the symptoms in the five internal organs, but on the surface, you are still taking the patient's pulse.
Sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Qi, and sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Zhao.
When he was in Zhao State, his name was Bian Que.
During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, the power of many officials was strong but the power of the monarch was weak. Zhao Jianzi was a doctor, but he was in charge of state affairs alone.
Zhao Jianzi fell ill and was unconscious for five days. The doctors were very worried and summoned Bian Que.
Bian Que came into the room to examine the patient and walked out. Doctor Dong Anyu asked Bian Que about his condition. Bian Que said: "His blood is normal, why should you be surprised!"
Once upon a time, Duke Mu of Qin was in this situation and fell into a coma for seven days before he woke up.
The day he woke up, he told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: I am very happy when I arrive at the Emperor of Heaven.
The reason why I stayed there for such a long time was that the Emperor of Heaven wanted to teach me.
The Emperor of Heaven told me that the Jin Kingdom was about to be in chaos and that the Five Dynasties would not be able to live in peace.
Then someone will become the overlord, and he will die soon after becoming the overlord.
The sons of overlords will make their country's men and women promiscuous. Gongsun Zhi wrote down these words and kept them. Later, the history books of Qin recorded this matter.
You have heard of the promiscuity of Duke Xian of Jin, the dominance of Duke Wen of Jin, and the indulgence of Duke Xiang of Jin after defeating the Qin army in Miao Mountain. You have heard of these.
Now your lord's illness is the same as his, and he will be cured in less than three days. He will definitely say something after he recovers.
After two and a half days, Zhao Jianzi woke up and told the doctors: I was very happy when I went to the Emperor of Heaven. I played with the gods in the center of the sky, where various musical instruments played many music and dances were performed. It was not like the music and dance of the three ancient times. The music was heart-stirring.
There was a bear trying to catch me, and the Emperor of Heaven ordered me to shoot it. I shot the bear, and it died.
A crab came over, I shot it again, and hit it again, and the crab died.
The Emperor was very happy and gave me two bamboo baskets with jewelry inside.
I saw my son beside the Emperor of Heaven. The Emperor of Heaven entrusted me with a Zhai dog and said: Give it to your son when he grows up.
The Emperor of Heaven told me: The Jin Kingdom will decline from generation to generation, and will perish after seven generations.
The Qin people will defeat the Zhou people to the west of Fan Kui, but they will not be able to possess his power. After hearing these words, Dong Anyu recorded and collected them.
People told Zhao Jianzi what Bian Que had said, and Zhao Jianzi gave Bian Que 40,000 acres of land.
Later, Bian Que passed through Guo State.
When the prince of the Guo Kingdom died of illness, Bian Que came to the gate of the palace of the King of Guo and asked a concubine who was fond of medicine: What disease did the prince have? Why did the capital hold rituals to ward off evil spirits and diseases more than many other things?
The concubine said: The prince's disease is caused by the irregular circulation of blood and qi, the intertwining of yin and yang and the inability to drain it. It violently breaks out on the surface of the body, but in fact the internal organs are damaged.
The human body's righteous energy cannot stop the evil energy, and the evil energy accumulates and cannot be released. Therefore, the yang energy weakens and the yin evil becomes strong, so the person suddenly faints and dies.
Bian Que asked: When did he die?
The concubine replied: From the time the rooster crows to now.
Asked again: Has it been buried?
He replied: Not yet, he died less than half a day ago.
Please inform Mr. Guo that I am a Qinyue native of Bohai County, and my home is in Midi. I was unable to look up to the king's majesty and pay homage to him.
I heard that the prince passed away unfortunately and I can revive him.
The concubine said: Sir, are you not talking nonsense?
Why do you say the prince can be resurrected!
I heard that in ancient times, there was a doctor named Yu Fu. He did not use decoctions, medicinal wine, trowels, needles, needles, guides, massages, medicinal irons, etc. He could identify the location of the disease as soon as he undressed and examined the acupoints of the five internal organs, then cut the skin and muscles, dredged the meridians, and tied them Tendons, massage the brain, touch the bones, straighten the diaphragm, cleanse the stomach, cleanse the five internal organs, cultivate the essence, and change the expression and complexion. If the gentleman's medical skills can be like this, then the prince can be reborn; if he can't do this, but you want to resurrect him, you can't deceive the baby who just learned to laugh.
After a long time, Bian Que looked up at the sky and sighed and said: The treatment methods you mentioned are like looking at the sky through a bamboo tube or looking at patterns through the gaps.
The treatment method I use can tell the cause of the disease without taking the patient's pulse, looking at the face, listening to the voice, or observing the patient's posture and expression.
If you know the external manifestations of a disease, you can infer the internal causes; if you know the internal causes of the disease, you can infer the external manifestations.
Diseases in the human body will be reflected from the body surface, and based on this, patients thousands of miles away can be diagnosed. I have many ways to make decisions, and I cannot just look at the problem from one angle.
If you think what I said is untrue, try going in and examining the prince. You should hear his ears ringing, see his nose flaring, and feel his legs and genitals, which should still be warm.
After hearing Bian Que's words, the concubine's eyes were dull and he could not blink, his tongue was stuck out and he could not speak. Later, he went in and told Guo Jun what Bian Que had said.
Guo Jun was very surprised after hearing this. He went out of the inner court to meet Bian Que at the middle gate of the palace and said, "I have heard about your noble moral character for a long time, but I have never had the opportunity to meet you."
This time, sir, you are passing through our small country. I hope you can help us. I, the king of this remote country, am so lucky.
As long as the husband is here, my son can be saved. Without the husband, he will throw his body into the wild and fill the ravines, and he will never come back.
Before he finished speaking, he started sobbing with sadness, his mind was in a daze, and he shed tears for a long time. The teardrops rolled down and stuck to his eyelashes. He couldn't restrain his sorrow, and his appearance and expression changed.
Bian Que said: Your prince's disease is what people call corpse disease.
That's because the Yang Qi sinks into the Yin vessels, and the pulse Qi entangles and impinges on the stomach. The meridians are damaged and the meridians are blocked. They flow into the lower burner and the bladder respectively. Therefore, the Yang vessels sink and the Yin Qi rises. The Yin and Yang Qi converge, block each other, and cannot be unblocked. The yin energy reverses upward movement, and the yang energy has to move inward. The yang energy is in vain stirring in the lower part but cannot rise. The upper part is blocked and cannot be driven by the yin energy. There are veins above that isolate the yang energy, and there are muscles and joints below that destroy the yin energy. In this way, the yin energy is destroyed and the yang energy is isolated, making the person's complexion decayed and the blood vessels confused, so the person's body becomes as quiet as if he was dead.
The prince actually did not die.
Because if yang attacks yin and blocks the internal qi, it can be cured; if yin attacks yang and blocks the internal qi, it will die.
These conditions will suddenly occur when the five internal organs are reversed.
A good doctor can cure the disease, a bad doctor can endanger the patient through confusion.
Bian Que then asked his disciple Ziyang to sharpen the needle stone and use Sanyang and Wuhui to inject needles.
After a while, the prince woke up.
He also asked his disciple Zi Bao to prepare a medicinal iron that could penetrate into the body for five minutes, and then mix and boil the medicine with eight prescriptions, and then apply it alternately under the two flanks.
The prince was able to sit up.
After further harmonizing the yin and yang, my body returned to the same as before after just taking the decoction for twenty days.
Therefore, people all over the world believe that Bian Que can resurrect the dead.
Bian Que said, "I can't resurrect the dead. He should live. All I can do is help him recover."
When Bian Que arrived in Qi, Marquis Huan of Qi treated him as a guest.
He went to the court to pay homage to Marquis Huan and said, "You have a small illness between your skin and muscles. If it is not treated, it will go deep into your body."
Marquis Huan said: I am not sick.
After Bian Que walked out of the palace, Huan Hou said to the people around him: Doctors love utilitarianism and want to attribute the cure of people to their own merits.
Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in your blood. If you don't treat it, it may go deep into your body."
Marquis Huan said: I am not sick.
After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy.
Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in the intestines and stomach. If it is not treated, it will invade deeper into the body."
Marquis Huan refused to answer.
After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy.
Five days later, Bian Que went there again. When he saw Huan Hou, he backed away and ran away.
Marquis Huan sent someone to ask him why he ran away.
Bian Que said: If the disease is between the skin and flesh, decoctions and medicinal irons can cure it; if the disease is in the blood, acupuncture and stone can cure it; if the disease is in the intestines and stomach, medicinal wine can cure it; if the disease enters the bone marrow, even the God in charge of life can do nothing.
Now that the disease has entered the bone marrow, I dare not ask for treatment.
Five days later, Marquis Huan fell seriously ill and sent for Bian Que. Bian Que had already fled Qi.
Marquis Huan fell ill and died.
If Marquis Huan could know in advance the hidden symptoms and let good doctors diagnose and treat them as early as possible, then the disease could be cured and his life could be saved.
People worry that there are too many diseases, and doctors worry that there are too few treatments.
Therefore, there are six types of illness that cannot be cured: those who are arrogant, indulgent and unreasonable are the first incurable; those who despise the body and value money are the two incurable; those who dress inappropriately and eat improperly are the three incurable; those who have Yin and Yang disorder and the five internal organs are not functioning properly are the four incurable; those who are very weak and unable to take medicine are the five incurable; those who are superstitious in witchcraft and do not believe in medical skills are the six incurable.
It is very difficult to cure a situation like this.
Bian Que's reputation spread throughout the world.
When he arrived in Handan, he heard that the local people respected women, so he became a doctor to treat women's diseases; when he arrived in Luo, he heard that Zhou people respected the elderly, so he became a doctor specializing in treating deafness, blindness, limbs, and pain; when he arrived in Xianyang, he heard that Qin people loved children, so he became a doctor to treat children's diseases; he changed the scope of his treatment according to the customs of various places.
Li Xi, the imperial physician of Qin, knew that his medical skills were not as good as Bian Que's, so he sent someone to assassinate Bian Que.
Up to now, people all over the world who talk about pulse diagnosis methods follow Bian Que's theory and practice.
This man in Taicang was the chief officer in charge of the granary in the capital of Qi State. He was from Lingan, his surname was Chunyu, and his given name was Yi.
Young but fond of medical skills.
Eight years after Han Gao's death, he once again studied medicine with Gongcheng Yangqing from Yuanli in the same county.
At this time, Yang Qing was over seventy years old and had no descendants who could inherit the medical skills, so he asked Chunyu Yi to put aside all the medical prescriptions he had learned before, and then gave him all the secret recipes he had mastered. He also taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, and the method of diagnosing diseases by observing different colors on the face, so that he could know the patient's life and death in advance, determine difficult diseases, judge whether they could be cured, and the theory of pharmaceuticals.
After studying for three years, he cured people's illnesses, predicted death and life, and accomplished many things.
However, he traveled among the vassal states to practice medicine and study, and did not take care of his family. Sometimes he refused to treat others, so many patients resented him.
In the fourth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone wrote to the court to accuse him. According to the criminal law, he had to be escorted to Chang'an in a carriage.
Chunyu Yi had five daughters who followed him and cried.
He got angry and cursed: If you don't give birth to a boy, there will be no one available at the critical moment!
So the youngest daughter Tiying was very sad after hearing her father's words, so she followed her father westward to Chang'an.
She wrote to the court and said: My father is an official of the court. The people of Qi State praise him for his integrity and justice. Now he has violated the law and been sentenced.
I am very sad that people who are executed cannot regenerate, and those who are disabled by torture cannot recover. Even if they want to change their ways, there is no way to do it, and in the end they cannot do so.
I would rather join the government and become a slave to atone for my father's sins and give him a chance to reform.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty read Tiying's petition, felt compassion for her, and pardoned Chunyu Yi, and abolished corporal punishment that year.
Chunyu Yi lived at home, and the emperor issued an edict asking him how many people had cured people and made decisions about life and death, and what their names were.
The question asked by Chunyu Yi of Taicang before the imperial edict was: What are the specialties of medical skills and what diseases can they cure?
Are there any medical books?
Who did you learn medicine from?
How many years have you studied? Who have you cured?
Where are they from? What disease do you have?
How is your condition after treatment? All answered in detail.
Chunyu Yi replied:
When I was young, I was fond of medical prescriptions, and most of the time I tried to treat people with the medical prescriptions I learned had no effect.
In the eighth year of high school, I was able to meet my teacher, Gongcheng Yangqing in Linshan Fanli.
Yang Qing was now over seventy years old, and I was able to pay him a visit and serve him.
He said to me: Put aside all the medical books you have studied, these are incorrect.
I have the pulse diagnosis books of Huang Di and Bian Que taught by ancient ancient doctors, as well as the method of diagnosing diseases by observing the different colors of the face, so that you can predict the patient's life and death, determine difficult diseases, and determine whether they can be cured. There are also books on pharmaceutical theory, which are all very insightful.
My family is rich, and just because I like you in my heart, I want to teach you all the secret recipes and books I have collected.
I said: I'm so lucky, these are not things I dare to hope for.
After saying that, I left the seat and thanked the teacher again. I studied the "Pulse Book", "Shang Jing" and "Xia Jing" taught by him, as well as facial diagnosis, auscultation, external observation of yin and yang, pharmacology, meteorite magic, Fang Zhongshu and other secret books and medical skills. I paid attention to analysis and experience while studying, which took about a year.
The next year, I tried to treat people, but although it was effective, it was not perfect.
I have studied with him for about three years in total. The patients I have treated and the people who have diagnosed their conditions and made decisions about life and death have all been effective and have reached a sophisticated level.
Yang Qing has been dead for more than ten years now. I have studied with him for three years. I am now thirty-nine years old.
A censor named Cheng from the State of Qi reported that he had a headache. After checking his pulse, I told him: Your condition is serious and cannot be explained clearly at once.
After coming out, he only told his brother Chang: This is gangrene, which occurs between the intestines and stomach. It will swell in five days, and in eight days, you will vomit pus and blood and die.
Cheng's illness was caused by having sex after drinking too much.
As a result, he died as expected.
The reason why I was able to diagnose his illness was because when I took the pulse, I could detect the pulse qi of the liver disease.
If the pulse is heavy and turbid but calm, this is a serious disease on the inside but not obvious on the outside.
Pulse theory says: The pulse is long and straight like a bowstring, and cannot change with the changes of the seasons. The disease is mainly in the liver.
Although the pulse is long, straight and hard but uniform and harmonious, it means that the meridians of the liver are diseased. If the pulses are sometimes sparse and sometimes dense, restless and powerful, it means that the meridians of the liver are diseased.
If the meridians of the liver are diseased but the meridians are even, the disease is caused by the tendons and marrow.
His pulse was sparse, dense, stopped, and weak. His illness was caused by drinking heavily and having sex.
The reason I knew he would swell up after five days and die after eight days of vomiting pus and blood was that when I cut his pulse, I found that the Shaoyang meridian had a pulse pattern similar to that of the pulse pulse.
Daimai is a disease of the meridians. If the disease develops throughout the body, the person will die.
Symptoms of the collaterals occur. At this time, the Dai pulse appears in the first branch of Guan on the left hand. This is the heat accumulated in the body but the pus and blood have not come out. When it reaches the fifth branch of Guan, it reaches the boundary of Shaoyang meridian. Eight days later, it will vomit pus and blood and die. Therefore, when it reaches the second branch of Guan, pus and blood will appear. When it reaches the boundary of Shaoyang meridian, it will swell. Afterwards, the sore will burst and pus will leak out and die.
Once the internal heat scorches the Yangming meridians and burns the branches of the collaterals, collateral disease will lead to stagnation and swelling of the meridians. The stagnation and swelling of the meridians will then cause erosion and dissociation. Therefore, the collaterals are blocked alternately.
This causes the heat evil to invade the head, causing the head to be disturbed and causing a headache.
The boy, the second son of the King of Qi, was ill, so he called me to take his pulse and diagnose him. I told him: This is a gas diaphragm disease. This disease makes people feel depressed, unable to eat, and often vomit gastric juice.
This disease is caused by depression and frequent anorexia.
I immediately prepared some qi decoction for him to drink. The diaphragmatic qi subsided in just one day, and he was able to eat after another two days. After three days, he was completely cured.
The reason why I knew his condition was because when I took his pulse, I found that he had a heart disease. The pulse was turbid, heavy, and irritable. This was Yang collateral disease.
Pulse theory says: If the pulse is strong and rapid when it reaches the finger, but is difficult and inconsistent when it leaves the finger, the disease is in the heart.
The whole body feels warm and the pulse is strong, which is called Double Ninth Festival.
Excessive yang energy will disturb the mind, so the heart will be depressed and unable to eat, and the collaterals will be diseased. If the collaterals are diseased, blood will come out from the top, and if the blood comes out from the top, the person will die.
This is a disease of inner sorrow, a disease of melancholy.
A doctor named Xun of Qi State was ill. Many doctors believed that the adverse qi started from the lower body and traveled upwards into the abdomen and chest, so they used acupuncture to treat him.
After examination, I said: This is a hernia. This disease makes people unable to urinate and defecate.
Xun replied: "I haven't been able to urinate or defecate for three days."
I gave him fire medicine decoction. After taking one dose, he could urinate and defecate. After taking the second dose, his urination and defecation were very smooth. After taking the third dose, he was cured.
His illness was caused by sexual intercourse.
The reason why I knew the disease he was suffering from was because when I took the pulse, the pulse in the cunkou of his right hand was urgent. The pulse did not reflect any disease in the five internal organs. The pulse in the cunkou of his right hand was strong and fast.
A fast pulse means heat evil is surging in the middle and lower burners. A fast pulse in his left hand means heat evil is flowing downwards. A fast pulse in his right hand means heat evil is surging up. There is no reaction of disease qi from the five internal organs, so it is said to be "gushing hernia".
The middle burner accumulates heat, so the urine is red.
A man named Xin from the Imperial Palace of Qi State was ill. I went to his house for diagnosis and treatment. After taking his pulse, I told him: It is the pulse Qi of a fever. However, due to summer heat, excessive sweating and weak pulse, it will not lead to death.
He also said: I got this disease when I bathed in running water when the weather was very cold, and my body became hot after bathing. He said: Well, that's it!
Last winter, when I was on an envoy to the State of Chu for the King of Qi, I walked to the Yangzhou River in Ju County. I saw that the Ju Bridge was badly damaged.
I immediately prepared a liquid decoction and fire medicine for him to drive away the heat evil. After taking one dose of the medicine, he no longer sweated. After taking two doses of the medicine, the fever subsided. After taking three doses, the disease stopped.
After letting him take the medicine for another twenty days, he felt like a healthy person.
The reason why I knew about his illness was because when I checked his pulse, I found that his pulse belonged to the "Bingyin pulse" where heat evil merges into the body.
Pulse theory says: Death caused by internal heat and external heat being confused and intertwined.
When I took his pulse, I found no internal heat and external heat mixed together, but they were both Yin pulses.
Those with Yin pulse and smooth pulse can be cured by Qing method. Although the heat evil is not completely eliminated, it can still be cured and life saved.
I diagnosed that his kidney qi was sometimes heavy and turbid. I could vaguely detect this situation at Taiyin Cunkou, which was water qi.
The kidneys are responsible for the movement of fluids, so we know his condition from this.
If it is not treated for a while, it will become a disease with alternating colds and hotness.
The Queen Mother of the King of Qi was ill and summoned me to check her pulse. I said: It is a disease caused by wind-heat attacking the bladder, making it difficult to defecate and defecate, and the urine is red in color.
I gave her the gunpowder decoction. After one dose, she was able to defecate. After two doses, she was cured and her urine was the same color as before.
This is a disease caused by urinating while sweating. The disease is caused by taking off clothes and letting the sweat dry.
The reason why I knew about the illness of the Queen Mother of Qi was because when I took her pulse, I found that the opening of the Taiyin was moist, which was due to wind-induced pulse energy.
Pulse theory says: The pulse is large, solid and strong when the pulse is cut forcefully, and is large, tense and strong when the pulse is cut gently, which indicates kidney disease.
But when I took the pulse at the kidney area, the situation was opposite. The pulse was thick and restless.
A thick pulse indicates a disease in the bladder; a restless pulse indicates heat in the middle burner, and the urine is red in color.
Cao Shantao in Zhangburi, Qi State, fell ill. After checking his pulse, I said: This is Fei Xiaobing disease, combined with cold and heat syndrome.
I told his family: This disease is fatal and cannot be cured.
You just satisfy the sick person's request and provide for him, and there is no need to treat him any more.
Medical theory says: This disease will cause you to go crazy and run around in three days, and you will die in five days.
Then he died as expected.
Shanta's illness was caused by having sex after being angry.
The reason I knew about Shantao's illness was because I took his pulse and found out from the pulse that he had lung-qi heat.
Pulse theory says: If the pulse is not steady or pulsating, the body is weak.
This is the result of repeated illnesses of the lungs and liver. So when I took the pulse, the pulse shape was unstable and there was a phenomenon of substituted pulse.
An unstable pulse means that the blood energy cannot be stored in the liver; the pulse is sometimes chaotic, sometimes impetuous, and sometimes grand.
This is because the collaterals of the lungs and liver are severed, so it is said to be fatal but cannot be cured.
The reason why I say add cold and heat is because his spirit is weak and his body is like a corpse.
A person whose spirit is scattered and whose body is like a corpse will definitely become weak. For a weak person, acupuncture cannot be used, nor can strong medicines be taken.
Before I diagnosed and treated him, the imperial doctor of Qi State had already diagnosed and treated his disease. He applied moxibustion on his foot Shaoyang pulse and asked him to take Banxia Pills. The patient immediately had diarrhea and became weak in the abdomen. He also applied moxibustion on his Shaoyin pulse, which severely damaged his liver and tendon Yang Qi. This repeatedly damages the patient's vitality, so it is said to be an injury caused by cold and heat.
Therefore, it is said that people will go crazy after three days. This is because the collaterals of the liver cross the breast and are connected to the Yangming meridian. Therefore, the crossing of the collaterals causes the heat evil to invade the Yangming meridian. If the Yangming meridian is injured, the person will run crazy.
Death after five days is because the liver and heart meridians are five minutes apart, and the vitality of the liver is exhausted in five days. When the vitality is exhausted, the person dies.
Pan Manru, the lieutenant of Qi State, suffered from lower abdominal pain. After I checked his pulse, I said: This is the gas left in the abdomen, which has accumulated to form a "mast disease".
I said to Qi's imperial servant named Rao and his internal history officer named You: If the lieutenant cannot prohibit sexual intercourse himself, he will die within thirty days.

His illness was caused by drinking and having sex.
The reason why I knew his illness was because I took his pulse and it was deep and weak. The combination of these three conditions indicates a diseased pulse in the spleen.
Moreover, the pulse at the cunkou of the right hand was tight and small, showing the pulse condition of a lump.
The two qi restrict and influence each other, so you will die within thirty days.
If the three Yin meridians of Taiyin, Shaoyin and Jueyin appear together, it is consistent with the rule of death within thirty days; if the three Yin meridians do not appear at the same time, the time to decide life and death will be shorter; if the intersecting Yin meridians and Dai meridians appear alternately, the time to death is still short.

Bian Que, a physician from Bohai County, was originally named Qin Yue. As a young innkeeper, he met a mysterious guest named Chang Sang, who recognized his potential and gave him a secret medical prescription. After taking the medicine for thirty days, Bian Que gained the ability to see through walls and diagnose illnesses internally. He practiced medicine in Qi and Zhao, where he became known as Bian Que.

During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, Zhao Jianzi fell unconscious for five days. Bian Que diagnosed him, noting his blood was normal, and predicted he would recover in three days, similar to a past episode involving Duke Mu of Qin. Zhao Jianzi indeed woke up after two and a half days, recounting a vision of the Emperor of Heaven. He rewarded Bian Que with 40,000 acres of land.

In Guo State, Bian Que encountered a prince who had seemingly died. He explained the prince suffered from "corpse disease," caused by an imbalance of yin and yang, and was not truly dead. Using acupuncture and medicinal applications, Bian Que revived the prince, though he insisted he could not resurrect the dead, only help those who could recover.

When visiting Qi, Bian Que warned Marquis Huan of a minor illness between his skin and muscles. The marquis ignored him, and over successive visits, the disease progressed to his blood, then intestines and stomach, and finally to his bone marrow, where it became incurable. Marquis Huan died five days after Bian Que fled, illustrating the importance of early treatment.

Bian Que's fame spread, and he adapted his practice to local customs—treating women in Handan, the elderly in Luo, and children in Xianyang. However, Li Xi, the Qin imperial physician, jealous of his skills, had him assassinated. Despite this, Bian Que's methods in pulse diagnosis endured.

Yangqing taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, along with diagnostic methods. After three years, Chunyu Yi became skilled but faced legal trouble in the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign. His daughter Tiying petitioned the emperor, offering to become a slave to atone for his crimes. Moved by her plea, the emperor pardoned Chunyu Yi and abolished corporal punishment.

A doctor had dental caries from poor hygiene, treated with moxibustion and rinses. A pregnant woman with dystocia was given hyoscyamus powder to deliver. A servant with spleen damage died in spring, as foreseen. King Shichuan had a fever from washing hair, cured with cold water and acupuncture. Song Jian had kidney paralysis from lifting heavy objects, treated with a soft decoction. A maid named Han had internal cold from unfulfilled desire, cured with medicine and moxibustion. A woman with pinworm disease was treated with a purgative. Sima Chunyu had Dongfeng disease from overeating and running, cured with fire agent soup. A man named Po Shi died from lung damage after a fall, as predicted. A doctor named Sui developed gangrene from improper use of Five Stone Powder, dying as warned. The King of Qi, as Marquis of Yangxu, had paralysis from sexual intercourse, cured with gunpowder porridge. Cheng Kaifang developed tracheitis from drinking and wind, becoming paralyzed and mute. Xiang Chu died from male hernia after strenuous activity, as predicted.

Chunyu Yi explained that disease names often overlap, requiring careful pulse diagnosis to distinguish them. He noted that patients' deaths sometimes deviate from predictions due to diet or improper treatment. He avoided serving as a court physician, traveling to learn from multiple teachers. His teacher Yangqing, from a wealthy family, taught him secretly. Chunyu Yi also taught several students, including Songyi, Gao Ming, Wang Yu, Feng Xin, Du Xin, and Tang An, though not all mastered his skills. He admitted that errors in pulse diagnosis could lead to mistakes in predicting outcomes.

The historian concluded that Bian Que suffered due to his medical skills, while Chunyu Yi faced punishment but was saved by his daughter Tiying's petition, reflecting Laozi's saying that beautiful things are unlucky.

translation:
Since ancient times, only those who have received destiny can become kings, and the rise of kings does not depend on destiny through divination!
This situation was particularly prevalent in the Zhou Dynasty and can still be seen in the Qin Dynasty.
When the kings of the Han Dynasty came to Beijing to inherit the throne, they were also left to the fortune tellers.
As for the emergence of diviners, they began to appear since the rise of the Han Dynasty.
Lord Sima Ji is from Chu State.
He was doing divination in the east city of Chang'an.
At this time, Song Zhong was appointed as a doctor, and Jia Yi was appointed as a doctor. One day, the two of them went out to the court to take a bath and take a break. While walking, they discussed and learned the governance methods of the previous kings and saints, and extensively explored the world and human affairs. The two looked at each other and sighed.
Jia Yi said: I heard that ancient saints, if they were not officials in the court, must be among the ranks of diviners and doctors.
Now, I have seen the three princes, nine ministers and the sergeants and officials of the court, and I can know their talents, learning and character.
Let’s try to observe the soothsayer’s style.
The two of them went to the city in the same car and visited the divining restaurant.
It had just rained, and there were very few people on the road. Lord Sima Ji was sitting leisurely in the pavilion, with three or four disciples accompanying him, explaining the principles of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun and the moon, and the origin of good and bad luck in yin and yang.
The two doctors bowed twice to Lord Sima Ji.
Master Sima Ji looked at their appearance and saw that they seemed to be knowledgeable people, so he returned the courtesy and asked his disciples to lead them to sit down.
After sitting down, Sima Jizhu re-explained what he had said before, analyzed the origin and end of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun, moon and stars, distinguished the differences between benevolence and righteousness, listed the signs of good and bad luck, and talked about thousands of words, all of which were logical.
Song Zhong and Jia Yi were surprised and understood. They adjusted their crowns and belts, straightened their clothes, sat respectfully, and said, "I see your appearance and listen to your conversation. I have never seen anything like this in the world of today."
But why is your current status so low and why is your career so dirty?
Sima Jizhu laughed loudly and said: "It seems that the two doctors are people with Taoism. How could they say such superficial words and use such crude words now?"
What kind of person do you think a sage is?
Who do you think is a noble person?
Why do you regard me, an elder, as humble and dirty?
Song Zhong and Jia Yi said: Noble official positions and generous salaries are valued by the world, and worthy people enjoy them.
The position your husband is in now is not that kind of status, so he is considered to be in a lowly position.
What is said is not true, what is done is not effective, and what is taken is inappropriate, so it is dirty.
Diviners are despised by the world.
People all over the world say: fortune tellers often use exaggerated and grotesque words to cater to people's wishes; they falsely raise people's fortunes to please people's hearts; they fabricate disasters to make people sad; they use ghosts and gods to defraud money; they are greedy for rewards to benefit themselves.
These are behaviors that we consider shameful, so we say they are lowly and dirty. Lord Sima Ji said: "You two sit quietly for now."
Have you seen those wholesale boys?
If the sun and moon shine, they will walk; if the sun and moon do not shine, they will not walk. Ask them about the eclipses of the sun and moon and the good and bad fortunes of people, and they can't explain it.
From this point of view, there are too few people who can distinguish the virtuous and the unworthy.
All sages who serve as officials follow the path of integrity, advise the king with correct words, and abdicate if their advice is not accepted. They praise others without expecting anything in return, hate others without caring about others' resentment, and always take the convenience of the country and the people as their own duty.
Therefore, if you are not qualified, you will not do it even if you are given an official position; if it is not his fault, you will not accept money.
Now the sages you call are people who are worthy of being ashamed of themselves.
They worship in a low voice and speak servilely; they seduce each other with power and induce each other with interests; they form cliques for selfish interests and exclude righteous men in order to gain respect and reputation and enjoy public salaries; they seek personal interests, distort the monarch's decrees and plunder the property of farmers; they rely on their official positions to show off their power, use decrees as their own tools, pursue private interests, and are retrograde and violent: they seem to be no different from those who threaten others with a sharp knife.
When he first became an official, he tried his best to use cunning tricks, cover up false merits, and use flashy documents to deceive the king in order to climb to a high position; after being appointed to an official position, he refused to let wise men state his merits, but boasted about his own merits, made false claims true, turned nothing into something, and changed less into more, in order to gain something. They are powerful and high-ranking; they eat and drink a lot, have fun everywhere, have everything they want, ignore their parents and relatives, only engage in illegal activities and harm the people, squander freely, and waste their public wealth: This is actually a group of people who are robbers without using bows and spears, attack others without using swords and arrows, abuse their parents without being convicted, and kill the king without being punished.
Why do you think they are wise and wise people?
Robbery occurs but cannot be stopped; barbarians cannot be subdued without restraint; evil cannot be curbed if evil arises; public affairs are depleted but cannot be rectified; the four seasons are not in harmony but cannot be adjusted; the year is bad but cannot be adjusted.
If you have talent and study but do not do it, this is disloyalty; if you do not have talent and study, you will live in an official position, enjoy the emperor's salary, and hinder the status of the worthy, this is stealing the official position. Those who have connections will be promoted to official positions, and those who have money will be treated with courtesy and respect. This is called hypocrisy.
Haven't you ever seen an owl flying with a phoenix?
The orchid zhixiong was not abandoned in the wilderness, but the wormwood grew densely into a forest, causing the gentleman to retreat and not be famous. This was caused by the princes in power.
Telling without doing anything is the true intention of a gentleman.
Nowadays, fortune tellers must imitate the heaven and earth, take the changes of the four seasons, comply with the principles of benevolence and righteousness, distinguish strategies, judge hexagrams, rotate the zodiac disk, divination and hexagrams, and then explain the power of heaven and earth, the good and bad success or failure of human affairs.
In the past, when the kings stabilized the country, they would first use turtles to divine the sun and the moon, and then dare to govern the people on behalf of heaven; they would choose the right day before entering the capital; when a child was born in the family, he would first divine the good or bad fortune, and then he would dare to raise it.
From Fuxi's creation of the Eight Diagrams, King Wen of Zhou evolved it into 384 lines and then the world was brought to great rule.
King Gou Jian of Yue imitated King Wen's Bagua and defeated the enemy's country and dominated the world.
From this point of view, what is there to worry about in divination?
As for the divination practitioner, it is a sign of etiquette to clean up and then set up a seat, straighten the crown and belt, and then talk about good and bad things.
Their words allow ghosts and gods to enjoy the sacrifices, loyal ministers to serve their king, filial sons to support their parents, and loving fathers to raise their children. This is a sign of morality.
And if the inquirer spends dozens or hundreds of money out of moral reasons, the sick may be cured, the dying may be alive, the disaster may be avoided, things may be successful, and the daughter-in-law may be able to live a healthy life: Is this kind of merit only worth tens or hundreds of money!
This is what Lao Tzu said: A person with great virtue does not think he is virtuous, so he is virtuous.
Today's fortune tellers do a lot of good things to others but receive little gratitude from others. Is what Lao Tzu said different from what the fortune tellers do?
Zhuangzi said: A gentleman has no worries about hunger and cold inside, and no worries about being robbed outside. He is prudent and rigorous when he is in a superior position, and he is not jealous of others when he is in a lower position. This is the way of a gentleman.
Nowadays, fortune tellers are engaged in a profession that does not require piles of savings, no treasury for storage, and no carriages for migration. The equipment is simple and light, can be used when staying, and will not be used up.
Even Zhuangzi's behavior cannot be better than that of wandering in the endless world with endless things. Why do you say that divination is not allowed?
When the sky is not enough to the northwest, the stars move to the northwest; when the earth is not enough to the southeast, the sea is used as a pool; the sun must move westward at noon, and the moon must be waning when it is full; the holy way of the former kings suddenly exists and then disappears.
And the two doctors require that the fortune teller must be truthful in his words. Isn't this enough to make people confused?
Have you ever seen a lobbyist or an advocate?
Thinking about problems, making decisions and planning, you must rely on this kind of people. However, they cannot please their master with just a few words, so they must refer to the previous kings in their speeches and quote ancient times in their discussions; they may consider problems, make decisions and plans, or praise the success of the previous king's career, or describe their failures and corruption, so as to make the master's mind either happy or fearful, so as to realize their desires.
There is nothing more powerful than false boasting.
But if you want to make the country rich and powerful, have a successful career, and be loyal to the king, it won't work if you don't do this.
Today's diviners answer people's questions and educate people's ignorance.
How can those who are ignorant and confused become wise with just one sentence!
Therefore, never tire of talking.
Therefore, the Qiji cannot ride in the same carriage as the tired donkey, the phoenix does not flock with the swallows and the sparrows, and the sage does not ride with the unworthy.
Therefore, a gentleman always stays in a humble and inconspicuous position to avoid the public, hides himself to avoid the shackles of human relations, secretly observes the moral conformity of the world, eliminates all kinds of harm, shows the nature of God, helps God to nurture living beings, and hopes for more benefits without seeking any status or honor.
You two are just casual commentators, how can you know the truth of the elders!
Song Zhong and Jia Yi were in a daze and seemed to be lost after hearing this. They were at a loss, looked melancholy, and could not speak.
So he got up and dressed, bowed twice and said goodbye to Lord Sima Ji.
The two of them walked without knowing the difference between east, west, north and south. When they went out, they had to get into the car by themselves, lying on the railing, not daring to raise their heads, and could never catch their breath.
Three days later, Song Zhong saw Jia Yi outside the palace gate, and took him away from everyone to talk about it. He said with emotion: The higher the morality, the safer it is, and the higher the power, the more dangerous it is.
In a prominent position, death is imminent.
Even if the divination does not work, it will not be deprived of the refined rice that it deserves; if the advice for the king is not thorough, there will be no place for him to stand.
The two are too different, just like the sky and the earth are completely different.
This is just as Lao Tzu said: Namelessness is the origin of all things in the world. Ha!
The sky and the earth are vast and boundless, and all things are prosperous and happy. Some are safe and some are dangerous. No one knows where he should live.
How qualified are you and I to comment on them?
The longer they live, the happier they will be. Even Zhuangzi's ideas are not different from this.
After a long time, Song Zhong went on a mission to the Xiongnu but returned before he arrived, and was therefore convicted of a crime.
Jia Yi was the tutor of King Huai of Liang. King Huai of Liang accidentally fell off his horse and died. Jia Yi took the blame and went on a hunger strike and died with hatred.
These are all examples of pursuing glitz and risking one’s life.
Tai Shigong said: The reason why diviners in ancient times are not recorded is because most of their deeds are not found in documents.
When Sima Ji is the master, I will write down his words and deeds in a chapter.
Mr. Chu said: When I was a Langguan, I once visited the city of Chang'an and saw wise officials engaged in the profession of divination. I observed their daily life, walking and sitting up naturally and decently. They often dressed up their clothes and hats to receive the people in the countryside, and they had the wind of a gentleman.
When I met women who liked to solve doubts and enjoyed divination, I treated them seriously and never smiled.
Since ancient times, sages have escaped from secular society. Some live in desolate depressions, some live among the people and keep silent about worldly affairs, and some live in seclusion among diviners to protect themselves.
Sima Jizhu was a wise official of the Chu State. He studied in Chang'an and was proficient in the "Book of Changes". He was able to state the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi. He had extensive knowledge and far-sightedness.
Judging from his responses to the two noble men and his quotations from ancient Ming kings and sages, he was not a person with shallow knowledge and low abilities.
As for those who are famous for their divination as a profession, they can often be found everywhere.
The biography says: Wealth is the first, followed by nobles; now that they are noble, each of them still needs to learn a skill to stand in the society.
Huang Zhi is a doctor and Chen Junfu is a woman. They are famous for their good horse fortune.
Zhang Zhong and Qu Chenghou of Qi State were famous all over the world for being good at stabbing with swords.
Liu Changru is famous for being good at looking after pigs.
The Chu family of Xingyang became famous because he was good at fortune-telling.
There are many people who are famous for their skills. They all have a demeanor that is higher than the world and surpasses ordinary people. How can we say it all?
So it is said: If it is not the right place, nothing will grow if it is planted; if it is not in line with his intention, nothing will be accomplished if he is taught.
When elders educate their children, they should look at what they like. If their preferences are inclusive of the way of life, they should follow their preferences and take advantage of the situation to cultivate them.
Therefore, it is said: What kind of house to build and what name to give to the son are enough to show the ambition of the scholar-bureaucrat; when the son has a job to settle down in the world, the father can be called a wise man.
When I was a Lang Guan, I worked in the same yamen as my colleagues who were waiting for the imperial edict to be Lang Guan. They said: During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, he summoned various experts in divination to ask whether it would be possible to marry a daughter-in-law on a certain day.
The Five Elements family says it's okay, the Kanyu family says it's not possible, the Jianchu family says it's unlucky, the Congchen family says it's a big misfortune, the Li family says it's a minor misfortune, the Tianren family says it's a small auspiciousness, and the Tai family says it's a big auspiciousness.
Each family debated the disputes and could not make a decision. They could only report the relevant situation to the emperor.
The emperor ordered: To avoid the taboo of death, the opinions of the Five Elements experts should be used as the basis.
This is why people adopt the advice of the Five Elements Master.
summary: The role of divination in ancient China, particularly during the Zhou and Han dynasties. Kings historically received destiny without relying on divination, but by the Han dynasty, diviners had emerged. Lord Sima Ji, a diviner from Chu, practiced in Chang'an's east city. Two officials, Song Zhong and Jia Yi, visited him after discussing governance and saints. They questioned why Sima Ji, despite his wisdom, held a lowly position. Sima Ji defended divination, contrasting it with corrupt officials who exploit power for personal gain. He argued that diviners follow moral principles, aiding people through predictions and advice, unlike officials who engage in deceit and greed. He cited historical figures like Fuxi and King Wen of Zhou to highlight divination's value in governance. Sima Ji criticized the hypocrisy of those who judge diviners while ignoring their own ethical failings. He emphasized that diviners serve society by promoting virtue and preventing harm, often without recognition. The officials were humbled by his words. Later, Song Zhong and Jia Yi faced personal misfortunes—Song was convicted for a failed mission, and Jia Yi died after a student's accident. The text concludes with reflections on diviners' wisdom and their role in society, noting that many skilled individuals, like Sima Ji, remain unrecognized. It advises that elders should nurture children's talents and that diverse skills, including divination, are valuable. The narrative underscores the tension between worldly status and moral integrity, advocating for humility and the pursuit of virtuous living.

translation:
Chun Shenjun is a native of Chu State, his name is Xie and his surname is Huang.
He once traveled around to learn from his teachers, gained profound knowledge, and served King Qingxiang of Chu.
King Qingxiang thought Huang Xie was eloquent and asked him to go on a mission to Qin.
At that time, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Hanhe, defeated Han and Wei in Huayang, and captured Wei general Mang Mao. Han and Wei surrendered to Qin and served Qin.
King Zhao of Qin had ordered Bai Qi to attack Chu with South Korea and Wei, but the Qin army had not yet set off. At this time, King Chu sent Huang Xie to Qin by chance and heard about Qin's plan.
At this time, the State of Qin had occupied a large area of ​​Chu State, because before this King Qin had sent Bai Qi to attack the State of Chu, captured Wu County, Qianzhong County, captured the capital of Yancheng and Ying, and marched eastward to Jingling. King Qingxiang of Chu had to move the capital eastward to Chen County.
Huang Xie saw that King Huai of Chu was lured by Qin and went to Qin's court for negotiation. As a result, he was deceived, detained and died in Qin.
King Qingxiang was the son of King Huai of Chu, and the state of Qin did not pay attention to him at all. Huang Xie was worried that the state of Chu would perish if a war started.
So he wrote a letter to persuade King Qin:
Among the princes in the world, no one is more powerful than Qin and Chu.
Now I heard that your Majesty is going to conquer Chu State, which is like two tigers fighting each other.
When two tigers fight each other and the inferior dog takes advantage of it, it is better to be friendly with Chu.
Please allow me to state my opinion: I have heard that when things develop to their peak, they will inevitably go to the opposite direction, as is the case with the changes between winter and summer; when things accumulate to extremely high levels, they will be dangerous, as is the case with stacked chess pieces.
Now the land of Qin occupies the western and northern borders of the world. This has never been the case since the beginning of mankind, not even the territory of the emperor.
However, for three generations, the first emperors, King Wen, King Zhuang, and the king himself, never forgot to connect the land of Qin with Qi, so as to cut off the key parts of the alliance between the countries.
Now the king sent Shengqiao to serve as a garrison in South Korea. Shengqiao annexed the land of South Korea to the Qin State. This was a good way to obtain hundreds of miles of land without using any soldiers or force.
The king can be said to be talented.
The king sent troops to attack the Wei State again, blocking the access roads to and from the Wei capital Daliang, captured Hanoi, captured Yan, Suanzao, Xu, Tao and other places, and then invaded Xing. The Wei troops fled in all directions like white clouds blown by the wind and did not dare to save each other.
The king has accomplished enough.
The king stopped the campaign to rest and reorganize his troops, and sent troops again two years later; he also captured Pu, Yan, Shou, Yuan and other places, and then marched to Ren and Pingqiu, while Huang and Jiyang retreated and defended themselves. As a result, Wei surrendered to Qin;
It can be said that the power of the king has been exerted to the extreme.
If your Majesty maintains your merits, masters your power, gets rid of the desire to conquer, and spreads benevolence and righteousness, so that there will be no future disasters, your career will be equal to that of the three kings, and your power will be equal to that of the five hegemons.
If your Majesty, relying on the large number of strong men, relying on the strength of the military, and taking advantage of the power of destroying the Wei State, wants to use force to make the princes of the world submit, I am afraid you will be in trouble in the future.
The Book of Songs says: No one wants to have a good beginning, but few people can have a good ending.
"Book of Changes" says: When the little fox was about to cross the water, his tail got wet.
What these words say is that it is easy to start but hard to end.
How do you know this is the case?
In the past, Zhibo only saw the benefits of attacking Zhao Xiangzi, but he did not expect that he would be killed in Yuci. King Wu Fu Chai only saw the benefits of attacking Qi but did not expect to be defeated by Yue King Gou Jian in the dry tunnel.
It is not that these two countries have not made great achievements, but because they were greedy for immediate benefits, they ended up getting disaster later.
Because King Wu Fu Chai believed Yue's compliment, he went to attack Qi. After defeating the Qi people in Ailing, he was captured by Yue King Gou Jian at the Sanjiang River when he returned.
Zhibo believed in the Han and Wei families, so he attacked the Zhao family and Jinyang City. Victory was just around the corner. However, the Han and Wei families betrayed him and killed Zhi Boyao on the platform.
Now the king is jealous that the Chu State will not be destroyed, but he has forgotten that destroying the Chu State will make Han and Wei stronger. I think for the king and think that this cannot be done.
There is a poem that says: The army never travels long distances away from its homestead.
From this point of view, Chu is a helper and neighboring countries are enemies.
"The Book of Songs" says: The cunning rabbit jumps and jumps, but cannot run away when encountering hounds; I can figure out other people's thoughts.
Now the king believes that South Korea and Wei are on good terms with you, just as Wu Guo believes in Yue.
I heard the saying that the enemy cannot be tolerated and the opportunity cannot be missed.
I'm afraid that South Korea and Wei are actually deceiving Qin by asking Qin to eliminate the trouble.
How can you see it?
The king has no kindness for South Korea and Wei for many generations, but he has resentment for several generations.
The fathers, sons and brothers of the kings of Han and Wei have been killed by Qin's sword for nearly ten generations.
Their territory was incomplete, their country was ruined, and their ancestral temples were burned down.
From the generals down to the soldiers, they were disemboweled, beheaded and disfigured, their heads separated, their bones exposed in the wilderness and swamps, their heads stiffened, and corpses strewn everywhere in the country. The father, son, old and weak were tied up by the necks and hands, and became prisoners who were allowed to be humiliated. They walked on the road in groups.
The people were unable to live, their relatives fled, their flesh and blood were scattered, and they were exiled and reduced to male servants and female slaves, all over the country.
Therefore, if Han and Wei are not destroyed, this is Qin's biggest worry. Now, the king is using them to attack Chu together. Isn't it inappropriate?
Besides, how will the king send troops to attack Chu?
Will the king borrow a road from his enemies South Korea and Wei?
If so, then the day of sending troops is when the king is worried that they will not be able to return. This means that the king is lending his troops to his enemies, South Korea and Wei.
If the king does not borrow the road from his enemies Korea and Wei, he will definitely attack the area on the right side of Suishui.
The area to the right of Suishui is full of large rivers, mountains, dense forests, deep streams and valleys. Even if the king occupied these grain-free areas, he would not get the land.
This is because the king has a bad reputation for destroying the Chu State without getting the benefits of occupying the land.
Besides, from the day your king attacks Chu, the four countries of Korea, Zhao, Wei, and Qi will all send troops to deal with your king.
Once Qin and Chu go to war, they will continue to fight and cause trouble. Wei will send troops to attack cities and places such as Liu, Fangyu, Zhi, Huling, Dang, Xiao, and Ping. All the land originally occupied by the Song Kingdom will be lost.
The people of Qi attack Chu in the south, and the Surabaya area will definitely be conquered.
These places were flat, open and fertile lands extending in all directions, but they were allowed to occupy them alone.
The king defeated Chu, which made Han and Wei stronger in the Central Plains, and made Qi even stronger.
As Korea and Wei became stronger, they were able to compete with Qin.
Qi State has Surabaya as its border to the south, the sea to the east, and the Yellow River to the north, so there will be no future troubles. No country in the world is more powerful than Qi and Wei.
With the vastness of the king's land, the large population, and the powerful military equipment, once he sends troops to enmity with the Chu State, Han and Wei will become emperors. This is a mistake in the king's plan!
I think for your Majesty, there is no better way than to be friendly with Chu State.
Qin and Chu united as a whole to attack South Korea, and South Korea must restrain itself and dare not act rashly.
If the king manages to set up the dangerous terrain of Dongshan and takes advantage of the favorable conditions surrounded by the Yellow River, Korea will definitely become a vassal of Qin.
If this situation is created, the king will garrison Zheng with 100,000 troops, and Wei will be frightened, and Xu and Yan will retreat and stand firm without attacking, then the connection between Shangcai and Tailing and Wei will be severed, and Wei will become a vassal of Qin.
Once the king has good relations with the Chu State, the two countries of ten thousand chariots within Hangu Pass, Han and Wei, will cede land to the Qi State, and the vast area of ​​​​Jizhou on the right side of the Qi State can be easily obtained.
The king's land spans the east and west seas and binds the princes of the world. In this way, Yan and Zhao do not have Qi and Chu to rely on, and Qi and Chu do not have Yan and Zhao to rely on.
Then the king used danger to frighten the two countries Yan and Zhao, and directly shake the two countries Qi and Chu. Then these four countries would surrender to Qin without a sudden attack.
After reading Chun Shenjun's letter, King Zhao said: "It's really good."
So he stopped Bai Qi from going on an expedition and resigned from Han and Wei.
At the same time, he sent envoys to send generous gifts to Chu, and Qin and Chu formed an alliance to become friendly countries.
Huang Xie accepted the alliance and returned to Chu State. The King of Chu sent Huang Xie and Prince Wan to Qin State as hostages. Qin State detained them for several years.
Later, King Qingxiang of Chu fell ill, but Prince Wan was unable to return to Chu.
However, the prince had a very good personal relationship with the Qin Prime Minister Ying Hou, so Huang Xie persuaded Ying Hou: Prime Minister, are you really very good to the prince of Chu?
Ying Hou said: Yes.
Huang Xie said: Now the King of Chu may be ill, so it would be better for Qin to let the prince go back.
If the prince can be established as king, he will definitely serve the Qin State deeply and be grateful to the Prime Minister for his kindness that will never be exhausted. This is not only an expression of goodwill and friendship between the countries, but also retains an ally of a great country for the future.
If he is not allowed to go back, then he will be just a commoner in Xianyang City at best; Chu State will establish a new crown prince, and he will definitely not serve Qin State by then.
That would lose the trust of friendly countries and cut off the allies of a powerful country. This is not the best policy.
I hope you, Xiangguo, will consider this matter carefully.
Ying Hou Fan Ju reported what Huang Xie said to the King of Qin.
The King of Qin said: Let the teacher of the Prince of Chu go back to inquire about King Chu's condition first, and then make a plan after he comes back.
Huang Xie made plans for the prince of Chu and said: The purpose of Qin detaining the prince is to obtain benefits.
Now the prince is powerless to benefit Qin. I am very worried about you.
Moreover, Yang Wenjun's two sons are both in the Chu Kingdom. If the king unfortunately dies and the prince is not in the Chu Kingdom, Yang Wenjun's son will definitely be his successor, and the prince will not be able to enjoy the country.
It is better to flee Qin and go out with the envoy; please let me stay and bear the consequences of this with my life.
The Prince of Chu changed his clothes and pretended to be the driver of an envoy from the Chu State to get out of the customs. Huang Xie stayed in the guest house, always refusing to receive guests on the pretext that the Prince was ill.
It was estimated that the prince had gone far and Qin could not catch up, so Huang Xie took the initiative to report to King Zhao of Qin: The prince of Chu has gone back and is far away.
I deserve death, please grant me death.
King Zhao was very angry and wanted to allow Huang Xie to commit suicide.
Ying Hou said: "As a minister, Huang Xie sacrificed his life for his master. If the prince is established as the king of Chu, he will definitely use Huang Xie in an important position. Therefore, it is better to spare him the death penalty and let him return to his country to show his goodwill towards the Chu country."
The King of Qin listened to the advice of Marquis Ying and sent Huang Xie back to his country.
Three months after Huang Xie returned to Chu, King Qingxiang of Chu passed away, and Prince Wan was appointed King of Chu. This was King Kaolie.
In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, Huang Xie was appointed prime minister, granted the title Lord Chunshen, and was rewarded with twelve counties in Huaibei.
Fifteen years later, Huang Xie proposed to the King of Chu: The area north of the Huaihe River is close to the State of Qi. The situation there is urgent. Please classify this area as a county to make governance more convenient.
At the same time, he offered twelve counties in Huaibei and asked for the seal to be transferred to Jiangdong.
King Kaolie agreed to his request.
Chun Shenjun built cities in the old capital of Wu and made them his own capital.
Chun Shenjun has already served as the prime minister of the Chu State. At this time, Qi State has Mengchang Lord, Zhao State has Pingyuan Lord, and Wei State has Xinling Lord. They are all vying to treat virtuous corporals, attract guests, compete with each other for wise men, and assist the king in controlling the state affairs.
In the fourth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu, Qin defeated and killed more than 400,000 Zhao Changping garrison.
In the fifth year, Handan, the capital of Zhao State, was surrounded.
Handan asked for help from the Chu State. Chu State sent Chun Shenjun to lead troops to rescue Handan. After the Qin army retreated, Chun Shenjun led his troops back to Chu State.
In the eighth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu State, he marched northward for Chu State, destroyed Lu State, and appointed Xunqing as the magistrate of Lanling County.
At this time, the Chu State became prosperous and powerful again.
Once, Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao sent envoys to visit Lord Chunshen, and Lord Chunshen arranged for them to stay in a first-class guesthouse.
The envoy of the State of Zhao wanted to show off the wealth of the State of Zhao to the State of Chu, so he specially put a tortoise shell hairpin in his crown, showed off his sword scabbard decorated with pearls and jade, and asked to invite the guests of Lord Chun Shen to meet him. The distinguished guests of Lord Chun Shen all came to see the envoy of the State of Zhao wearing shoes made of pearls, which made the envoy of the State of Zhao feel ashamed.
In the fourteenth year of Chun Shenjun's tenure as prime minister, King Zhuang Xiang of Qin came to the throne, appointed Lu Buwei as Prime Minister of Qin, and granted him the title of Marquis Wenxin.
Captured the Eastern Zhou Dynasty.
In the 22nd year of Chun Shenjun's appointment as prime minister, the princes of various countries were worried that Qin's conquests would be endless and unstoppable, so they made an alliance with each other to crusade against Qin in the west. The king of Chu served as the leader of the six-nation alliance, leaving Chun Shenjun in charge.
After the Allied Forces of the Six Nations arrived at Hangu Pass, the Qin army came out to fight. The Allied Forces of the Six Nations were defeated and fled.
King Chu Kaolie blamed Chun Shenjun for the defeat in the battle, and Chun Shenjun was gradually alienated.
At this time, one of the guests, Zhu Ying, who was watching Jin, said to Chun Shenjun: People think that Chu is a strong country and you have made it weak. I think this view is wrong.
The former king had good relations with Qin for twenty years but Qin did not attack Chu. Why?
It would be very inconvenient for Qin to cross the fortress of Ji Pass to attack Chu; it would also be impossible for Qin to attack Chu by borrowing roads from the Western and Eastern Zhou Dynasties and turning its back on Han and Wei.
The current situation is no longer like this. Wei is in danger and cannot begrudge Xu and Yanling, and agrees to cede these two cities to Qin.
In this way, the Qin army is only 160 miles away from the capital of Chu, Chen. What I will see is that Qin and Chu are at war with each other day by day.
At that time, the Chu State moved its capital from Chen to Shouchun; while the Qin State moved its vassal Wei Yuanjun from Puyang to Yewang and established Dongjun.
From then on, Chun Shenjun came to the fiefdom of Wu and performed the duties of prime minister at the same time.
King Chu Kaolie had no sons. Chun Shenjun was worried about this matter, so he looked for women suitable to give birth to sons and donated them to the king of Chu. Although he donated a lot, he never gave birth to a son.
Li Yuan of the State of Zhao came with his sister, intending to present his sister to the King of Chu. He also heard that the King of Chu was not suitable for giving birth to a son, and he was afraid that he would not be favored for a long time.
Li Yuan looked for an opportunity to become Chun Shenjun's attendant. Soon he asked for leave and went home, but deliberately delayed his return.
After he came back, he went to see Lord Chunshen. Lord Chunshen asked him why he was late. He replied: The King of Qi sent an envoy to ask for my sister to marry him. Because I drank with the envoy, my return was delayed.
Chun Shenjun asked: Has the engagement gift been delivered?
Li Yuan replied: No.
Chun Shenjun asked again: "Can you let me see it?"
Li Yuan said: Yes.
So Li Yuan dedicated his sister to Chun Shen Jun, and she immediately gained Chun Shen Jun's favor.
Later, Li Yuan learned that his sister was pregnant, and discussed further plans with his sister.
Li Yuan's sister found an opportunity to persuade Chun Shenjun: "The King of Chu respects and favors you even more than his brother."
Now you have been the prime minister of Chu for more than twenty years, but the king has no sons. If the king of Chu will have brothers after his death, then after the king of Chu is established, each of them will make the people he trusted more prominent. How can you be favored for a long time?
Not only that, you have been in charge of political affairs for many years, and it is inevitable that you have been rude to the brothers of the King of Chu. If the brothers of the King of Chu are really established as kings, disaster will befall you. How can you keep the prime minister's seal and the Jiangdong fiefdom?
Now I know I'm pregnant, but no one else knows.
I have only been favored by you for a short time. If you offer me to the King of Chu based on your noble status, the King of Chu will definitely favor me. I rely on God's blessing to give birth to a son. This will mean that your son will become the King of Chu, and the whole country of Chu will be yours. How is this compared with the unexpected disaster you suffer?
Chun Shenjun thought that what he said was very right, so he sent Li Yuan's sister away from home, arranged her in a strict residence, and then told the King of Chu that he wanted to donate Li Yuan's sister.
The King of Chu summoned Li Yuan's sister into the palace and favored her very much. He gave birth to a son, made him a prince, and made Li Yuan's sister a queen.
The King of Chu valued Li Yuan, so Li Yuan participated in the government affairs.
Li Yuan sent his sister to the palace, made her a queen, and made her son a prince. Worried that Lord Chun Shen would reveal his secret and become more arrogant, he secretly raised an assassin. He planned to kill Lord Chun Shen to silence him, and some people in the capital knew about it.
In the twenty-fifth year of Chunshenjun's tenure as prime minister, King Kaolie of Chu fell seriously ill.
Zhu Ying said to Chun Shenjun: There are unexpected blessings and unexpected disasters in the world.
Now that you are in a world where life and death are uncertain, and you serve a moody monarch, how can you not have people come unexpectedly?
Chun Shenjun asked: What is unexpected blessing?
Zhu Ying replied: You have been the prime minister of Chu for more than 20 years. Although you are the prime minister in name, you are actually the king of Chu.
Now the king of Chu is seriously ill and is about to die. You assist the young king and control the state affairs on his behalf, just like Yi Yin and Zhou Gong. When the king grows up and then hand over the power to him, doesn't it mean that you go south to claim the king and occupy the Chu country?
This is what is called unexpected blessings.
Chun Shenjun asked again: What is an unexpected disaster?
Zhu Ying replied: Li Yuan is your enemy if he is not in charge of national affairs. He has been raising assassins for a long time without caring about the military. As soon as the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will definitely enter the palace first to seize power and kill you to silence you.
This is what is called an unexpected disaster.
Chun Shenjun then asked: What do you mean by someone who comes unexpectedly?
Zhu Ying replied: If you arrange for me to be the doctor, when the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will be the first to enter the palace. I will kill Li Yuan for you.
This is what is called an unexpected person.
After hearing this, Chun Shenjun said: "You have to give up this plan." Li Yuan is a weak person, and I am very friendly to him. Besides, how could he get to this point!
Zhu Ying knew that his suggestions were not adopted, and he was afraid that disaster would affect him, so he ran away.
Seventeen days later, King Chu Kaolie passed away. As expected, Li Yuan entered the palace first and ambushed the assassin at Thorny Gate.
When Chun Shenjun entered the Thorny Gate, the assassins raised by Li Yuan caught him from both sides and killed him. He cut off his head and threw it outside the Thorny Gate.
At the same time, he sent officials to kill everyone in Chunshenjun's family.
Li Yuan's sister was favored by Lord Chun Shen and became pregnant. Then she entered the palace and was favored by Queen Chu Kaolie. The son born to her was established as King of Chu. This was King Chu You.
This year, Qin Shihuang has been on the throne for nine years.
Lao Ai also had an affair with the Queen Mother of Qin. After being discovered, the three tribes were destroyed by the barbarians, and Lu Buwei was deposed because of his involvement.
Taigong Shi said: I went to the Chu region and visited Chun Shenjun's old city. The palace buildings were very magnificent!
At that time, Chun Shenjun persuaded King Qin Zhao and risked his life to send people to send the Prince of Chu back to Chu State. What a smart and brilliant move it was!
But later he was controlled by Li Yuan and became confused.
As the saying goes: If you fail to make a decision when you should make a decision, you will suffer disaster in turn.
It means Chun Shenjun lost Zhu Ying's opportunity to kill Li Yuan, right?
summary:
Chun Shenjun, a native of Chu named Huang Xie, served King Qingxiang of Chu. He was sent to Qin after King Qingxiang recognized his eloquence. At that time, Qin, under King Zhao, had been attacking Chu's allies, and Huang Xie learned of Qin's plan to invade Chu. Worried for Chu's survival, he wrote to King Zhao, arguing that Qin and Chu, as the two strongest states, should not fight each other, as this would benefit weaker states like Han and Wei. He warned that Qin's past victories had made it powerful, but attacking Chu would strengthen its enemies and lead to future trouble. Citing historical examples, he advised Qin to ally with Chu instead.

King Zhao agreed, halted the attack, and formed an alliance with Chu. Huang Xie returned with Prince Wan of Chu as a hostage in Qin. When King Qingxiang fell ill, Huang Xie persuaded the Qin prime minister to let Prince Wan return, arguing it would secure Chu's loyalty. When Qin hesitated, Huang Xie helped Prince Wan escape disguised as a charioteer, staying behind to face punishment. King Zhao initially wanted to execute him but, on advice, spared him and sent him back. Three months later, King Qingxiang died, and Prince Wan became King Kaolie of Chu, appointing Huang Xie as prime minister and granting him the title Lord Chunshen with twelve counties.

As prime minister, Chun Shenjun governed effectively, moving his fief to Jiangdong and building a capital in the old Wu city. He competed with other lords in attracting talented guests. In his fifth year, he led Chu forces to relieve the siege of Handan, Zhao's capital. In his eighth year, he conquered Lu for Chu, restoring Chu's strength. However, in his twenty-second year, a six-state alliance against Qin, led by Chu, was defeated at Hangu Pass, leading to his alienation by King Kaolie.

Chun Shenjun later became involved with Li Yuan, who presented his pregnant sister to him. She convinced Chun Shenjun to offer her to the childless King Kaolie, ensuring his son would become king. The king favored her, and she bore a son, who became prince. Li Yuan, fearing Chun Shenjun would reveal the secret, secretly raised assassins. When King Kaolie fell ill, a guest named Zhu Ying warned Chun Shenjun of Li Yuan's plot, but he dismissed it. Seventeen days after the king's death, Li Yuan ambushed and killed Chun Shenjun at the palace gate, then massacred his family. Li Yuan's sister's son became King You of Chu.

The historian comments that Chun Shenjun's early wisdom in persuading Qin and risking his life for the prince was admirable, but he later fell victim to Li Yuan's schemes, failing to act on Zhu Ying's advice, which led to his downfall.
