translation:
King Weiman of North Korea was originally from the state of Yan.
Initially, when the Yan Kingdom was in its heyday, it conquered Zhenfan and North Korea, made them belong to the Yan Kingdom, appointed officials for them, and built defensive castles at the border fortresses.
Later, the Qin State destroyed the Yan State, and North Korea became a border country outside Liaodong County.
After the founding of the Han Dynasty, because North Korea was far away and difficult to defend, the previous passes in Liaodong County were renovated until they were bounded by the Xishui River, which was under the jurisdiction of the State of Yan.
Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and went to the Huns. Weiman also went into exile, gathered more than a thousand of his companions, wore cone-shaped buns and barbarian clothes, walked out of the Great Wall in the east, crossed the Xu River, and lived in the original empty land of Qin called Shangxiazhang.
During the time of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of the Han Dynasty, when the world had just stabilized, the governor of Liaodong County agreed that Wei Man would be the foreign minister of the Han Dynasty to protect the barbarians outside the border fortresses and not allow them to come to the border to harass and plunder. The barbarian leaders wanted to see the emperor from the Han Dynasty and did not prohibit it.
The governor of Liaodong reported this situation to the emperor, who agreed to the condition. Therefore, Weiman was able to use his military power and wealth to invade and surrender the small countries around him. Zhenfan and Lintun both surrendered and belonged to Weiman. The area under his control was thousands of miles in radius.
Weiman passed the rule to his son, and then to his grandson Youqu. During this period, more and more refugees from the Han Dynasty were lured to North Korea, and Youqu never went to see the emperor of the Han Dynasty. Many small countries around Zhenfan wanted to submit letters requesting an audience with the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, but were blocked from letting the Emperor know about their request.
In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent He He to blame and inform Youqu, but Youqu refused to accept the Han Dynasty's edict.
Shehe left North Korea and came to the border. Facing the Xu River, he sent a driver to assassinate the North Korean Pi Xiaowang who was escorting Shehe. Then he immediately crossed the river, galloped back, and entered the Han Dynasty border fortress. So he returned to the capital and reported to the emperor: I killed a North Korean general.
The emperor believed that he had a good reputation for killing Korean generals, so he no longer pursued his fault, but awarded him the official position of captain of eastern Liaodong.
North Korea resented Shehe and dispatched troops to make a surprise attack and killed Shehe.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty ordered the recruitment of prisoners whose crimes had been pardoned to attack North Korea.
In the autumn of the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent general Yang Pu of Louzhou to cross the Bohai Sea by boat with an army of 50,000 people. General Xunshe of the left led his troops out of Liaodong County to attack Youqu.
Youqu mobilized troops to defend strategic locations to resist the Han army.
General Zuo's pawn named Duo was the first to lead the Liaodong troops to attack the enemy. As a result, the team failed and became separated. Most of them ran back and were executed for violating military law.
General Lou Chuan led 7,000 soldiers from Qi to arrive at Wangxian City first.
Youqu was guarding the city and heard the news that General Lou Chuan's army was small, so he went out to attack General Lou Chuan. General Lou Chuan's army failed and fled in all directions.
General Yang Pu lost his army and fled to the mountains to hide for more than ten days. He gradually recovered his scattered soldiers and reunited them.
General Xun Shen of the left attacked the Korean army stationed west of the Xu River, but failed to break through the enemy from the front.
Because the two generals failed to achieve military victory, the emperor sent Weishan to use his military prowess to tell Youqu clearly.
Youqu met with the Han Dynasty envoy and kowtowed to apologize: I am willing to surrender, but I am afraid that Generals Yang and Xun will kill me through deception. Now that I see the symbol of integrity, please allow us to surrender.
Youqu then sent the prince to the Han Dynasty to apologize, offering five thousand horses, and also presented military rations to the Han army in Korea.
There were more than 10,000 Korean people with weapons in their hands, and they were about to cross the Xu River. The envoy and General Zuo suspected that the Koreans had rebelled, and said that the prince had surrendered and submitted, and they should order the people not to carry weapons.
The prince also suspected that the Han envoys and General Zuo wanted to deceive and kill him, so he stopped crossing the river and led the Korean people back.
Weishan returned to the capital and reported to the emperor, who killed Weishan.
General Zuo defeated the North Korean army on the Haishui River and then advanced until he reached the foot of Wangxian City and surrounded the northwest of the city.
General Lou Chuan also went to join forces and garrisoned in the south of the city.
Youqu then held on to Wangxian City. Several months passed, but the Han army failed to capture Wangxian City.
General Zuo has always served the emperor in the palace and is favored. He led soldiers from Yan and Dai who were very fierce and took advantage of the opportunity to win the battle. Most of the soldiers in the army were very proud.
General Lou Chuan led his troops to cross the sea to fight, and there were many casualties in the battle. When they fought against Youqu, they suffered difficulties and humiliation, and suffered many casualties. The soldiers were frightened, and the generals felt ashamed in their hearts. When they surrounded You Can, General Lou Chuan often held peace talismans.
General Zuo tried his best to attack the enemy city, and the North Korean ministers secretly sought an opportunity to contact General Lou Chuan to discuss North Korea's surrender. The two sides exchanged talks, but no decision had been made.
General Zuo repeatedly agreed with General Lou Chuan on the date of simultaneous attacks. General Lou Chuan wanted to reach a reduction in the treaty with North Korea as soon as possible, so he did not send troops to join General Zuo. General Zuo also sent people to look for opportunities for North Korea to surrender. North Korea refused to surrender to General Zuo, but wanted to surrender to General Louchuan. Therefore, the two generals cannot coordinate with each other to fight the enemy together.
General Zuo thought about General Lou Chuan's fault for losing the battle in the past. Now he was secretly friendly with the North Korean minister, but North Korea refused to surrender, so he suspected that General Lou Chuan had a rebellion conspiracy, but he did not dare to take action.
The emperor said that the general was incompetent. Not long ago, I sent Weishan to tell Youqu to surrender. Youqu sent the prince to apologize, but Weishan, the messenger, could not handle the matter decisively and made mistakes in his plans with General Zuo, which finally broke the agreement of North Korea's surrender.
Now the two generals are besieging Wangxian City, but they are contradicting each other and cannot act in unison, so the problem cannot be solved for a long time.
Gongsun Sui, the governor of Jinan, was sent to correct their mistakes. If there is a convenient and favorable opportunity, he can handle the affairs on his own at any time.
After Gongsun Sui arrived in North Korea, General Zuo said: North Korea could have been captured long ago. There is a reason why it has not been captured yet.
He also told Gongsun Sui that he had agreed with General Lou Chuan on the date of march, but General Lou Chuan did not come to join forces. He also told Gongsun Sui that he had always suspected General Lou Chuan of treason, and said, "If we don't arrest him now, I'm afraid it will be a big harm. Not only will General Lou Chuan rebel, but he will also unite with North Korea to destroy our army."
Gongsun Sui also thought that this was the case, so he used the talisman to summon General Lou Chuan to General Zuo's camp to discuss the matter. He ordered General Zuo's men to capture General Lou Chuan on the spot, merge his troops under General Zuo, and then reported the incident to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty.
The emperor killed Gongsun Sui.
General Zuo merged the two armies and tried his best to attack North Korea.
Korean Prime Minister Lu Ren, Prime Minister Han Yin, Prime Minister Nixi, and General Wang Xi discussed with each other: At first, General Lou Chuan was wanted to surrender, but now General Lou Chuan has been arrested, and only General Zuo leads the combined army. The war is becoming more and more urgent. We may not be able to persist, and the king refuses to surrender.
Han Yin, Wang Yi, and passers-by all fled to the Han army and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Passers-by died on the road.
In the summer of the third year of Yuanfeng, Nixi Xiangcan sent people to kill the Korean king Youqu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Before Wang Xiancheng was captured, Cheng Si, the former minister of Youqu, rebelled again and attacked the Korean officials who did not rebel with him.
General Zuo sent Youqu's son Changjian and Xiangluren's son Lu Zui to tell the Korean people clearly that they would kill him. Therefore, the Han Dynasty finally pacified Korea and established four counties.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty granted Shen the title of Marquis of Qingqing, Han Yin as the Marquis of Diju, Wang Xi as the Marquis of Pingzhou, and Chang demoted them to Jihou.
Lu Zui was named Marquis of Wenyang because of his meritorious service after his father died.
General Zuo was recalled to the capital. He committed the crime of competing for merit, becoming jealous of each other, and violating the battle plan, and was publicly executed.
General Lou Chuan was also sentenced to death because he committed the crime of attacking the enemy first without authorization when his troops arrived at Lukou. He should have waited for General Zuo, resulting in many casualties. He atone for his crime with money, was exempted from the death penalty, and became a civilian.
Tai Shigong said: King Youqu of Korea relied on the rugged terrain and the country was wiped out.
She He's deception to gain credit became the beginning of sending troops to attack North Korea.
General Lou Chuan acts with a narrow mind and suffers disaster when in danger.
I regretted that I had failed in the capture of Panyu, but was suspected of rebelling.
Xun Zhen and Gong Sun Sui were both beheaded as they fought for merit.
The two armies of Yang Pu and Xun Shen who conquered Korea suffered humiliation, and the generals were not granted the title of marquis.

King Weiman of North Korea, originally from the state of Yan, settled in the empty region of Shangxiazhang after Yan's fall and Lu Wan's rebellion. During the reigns of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of Han, the Liaodong governor appointed Weiman as a foreign minister to protect border barbarians, allowing him to use military power to subdue nearby states like Zhenfan and Lintun, expanding his territory. Weiman's rule passed to his son and grandson Youqu, who lured Han refugees and blocked smaller states from contacting the Han emperor.

In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han sent Shehe to reprimand Youqu, but Youqu rejected the edict. Shehe assassinated a Korean general on his return, earning a promotion but provoking a Korean attack that killed him. The Han emperor then recruited pardoned prisoners to attack Korea. In autumn, General Yang Pu led 50,000 troops by sea, while General Xun She led forces from Liaodong. Youqu defended strategic points. Yang Pu's initial assault on Wangxian City failed, and his army scattered. Xun She also failed to break through Korean defenses.

The emperor sent Weishan to negotiate, and Youqu agreed to surrender, sending his prince with tribute. However, suspicions arose between the Han envoys and the Korean prince, leading to a breakdown. Weishan was executed for mishandling the situation. Xun She then defeated the Korean army at Haishui River and besieged Wangxian City, joined by Yang Pu. The two generals disagreed on strategy: Xun She favored aggressive attack, while Yang Pu sought peaceful surrender. This discord prolonged the siege.

The emperor sent Gongsun Sui to mediate, but Xun She convinced him to arrest Yang Pu on suspicion of treason. Gongsun Sui complied, but the emperor later executed him. Xun She merged the armies and intensified the attack. Korean officials, fearing defeat, killed King Youqu and surrendered. The Han established four counties, granting titles to defectors. Xun She was executed for rivalry and violating battle plans, while Yang Pu was reduced to civilian status after paying a fine. The historian notes that Korea's reliance on terrain led to its fall, and the generals' conflicts caused their downfall.

translation:
General Li Guang was a native of Chengji County, Longxi County.
His ancestor was Li Xin, a general of the Qin State who captured Prince Dan of Yan.
His home was originally in Huaili County, but later moved to Chengji.
The art of archery has been passed down from generation to generation in Li Guang's family.
In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan with great force. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at riding and archery, and killed many enemy heads, he was appointed Zhonglang.
Li Guang's cousin Li Cai was also appointed as Zhonglang. Both of them were appointed as regular servants of the martial arts, with an annual salary of 800 shi of food.
Li Guang once traveled with the emperor, often charging into battle, resisting enemies, and killing ferocious beasts. Emperor Wen said: What a pity! You haven't encountered a good opportunity. If you catch up with the Emperor Gaozu's era and be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households, what's the point?
After Emperor Jing came to the throne, Li Guang was appointed as the Captain of Longxi, and then as the Cavalry General.
During the rebellion of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, Li Guang served as the captain of Xiaoqi and followed the Taiwei Zhou Yafu to fight back against the Wu and Chu rebels. He captured the enemy's flag at the foot of Changyi City and became famous.
However, because King Xiao of Liang privately awarded Li Guang the General's Seal, the court did not reward him after he returned to the court.
He was appointed as the governor of Shanggu, and the Huns came to fight every day.
Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, cried to the emperor and said: Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world. He relies on his talent to fight the enemy head-on many times. I'm afraid he will lose this good general.
So he was appointed as the prefect of Shangjun.
Later, Li Guang was transferred to the prefecture of the border counties, and then to the prefecture of Shangjun.
He served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Daijun, and Yunzhong, and was famous for his vigorous fighting.
The Huns invaded Shangjun in a large scale, and the emperor sent a eunuch to study military affairs with Li Guang and fight against the Huns.
The eunuch led dozens of cavalry on horseback. When they encountered three Huns, they fought with them. The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the eunuch and almost killing all his cavalry.
The eunuch fled back to Li Guang. Li Guang said: "This must be a Xiongnu expert in shooting vultures."
Li Guang then took a hundred cavalry to chase the three Huns.
The three men had no horses and traveled on foot.
After walking for dozens of miles, Li Guang ordered his cavalry to spread out to the left and right and outflank them in two directions. He personally shot the three men, shot two to death and captured one alive. As expected, it was the Huns' eagle shooter.
After tying him onto his horse, he saw thousands of Huns cavalry in the distance. When they saw Li Guang, they thought he was a cavalryman luring the enemy. They were surprised and ran up the mountain to set up their formation.
Li Guang's hundreds of cavalry were also frightened and wanted to run back.
Li Guang said: We are dozens of miles away from the main army. According to the current situation, as soon as our hundred cavalry run away, the Huns will chase and shoot us, and they will be killed immediately.
If we stay, the Xiongnu will definitely think that we are a large army coming to lure the enemy, and they will not dare to attack us.
Li Guang ordered the cavalry: Advance!
The cavalry moved forward, and when they reached a place about two miles away from the slave position, they stopped and ordered: Everyone, dismount and unsaddle!
The cavalry said: There are so many enemies and they are so close. What should we do if there is an emergency?
Li Guang said: Those enemies thought that we would run away, but now we have taken off our saddles to show that we will not run away. This will make them more convinced that we are soldiers who lure the enemy.
So the Huns cavalry finally did not dare to attack.
A Hun general riding a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang immediately mounted his horse and galloped with more than a dozen cavalry. He shot the Hun general riding a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry team, took off the saddle, and asked the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down casually.
It was dusk at this time, and the Xiongnu army always felt strange and did not dare to attack.
In the middle of the night, the Xiongnu soldiers thought that the Han Dynasty had an ambush nearby and wanted to sneak up on them at night, so the Xiongnu troops retreated.
The next morning, Li Guang returned to his army camp. The army did not know where Li Guang was going, so they were unable to respond later.
Several years later, Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu ascended the throne. All the ministers on the left and right thought that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred from the prefect of Shangjun to the chief of the imperial guard of Weiyang Palace, and Cheng Bushi also came to be the chief of the imperial guard of Changle Palace.
Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both served as governors of border counties and were also in charge of military garrison.
When it came time to attack the Xiongnu, Li Guang marched without strict formations and formations. He stationed troops near places with abundant water and lush grass, and set up camps and lodgings, which was convenient for everyone. He did not call for self-defense at night. The shogunate simplified various documents and books, but he placed sentries far away, so he did not encounter danger.
Cheng Bushi had strict requirements on the organization of the troops, marching columns, and garrison formations. He kept watch at night, and the military clerks had to wait until dawn to process performance appraisals and other official documents and books. The troops had no rest, but they never encountered danger.
Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's army is simple and easy, but if the enemy suddenly attacks him, he will be unable to stop him; but his soldiers are comfortable and happy, and they are willing to die for him.
Although my army is busy with military affairs, the enemy does not dare to invade me.
At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi at the border of the Han Dynasty were both famous generals, but the Huns were afraid of Li Guang's strategy, and most of the soldiers were willing to follow Li Guang and suffered the hardship of following Cheng Bushi.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Cheng Bushi was awarded the title of Taizhong Dafu because he repeatedly spoke out and remonstrated. He was an honest man and strictly abided by the court documents and laws.
Later, the Han Dynasty used the city of Mayi to lure Chanyu and sent a large army to ambush in the valley near Mayi. Li Guang was appointed as the general of Xiaoqi and was controlled by the guard general Han Anguo.
At that time, Shanyu discovered the Han army's plan and ran away.
None of the Han troops had any military exploits. Four years later, Li Guang was appointed as a general from the guard and went out to Yanmen Pass to attack the Huns.
The Huns had more troops and defeated Li Guang's army and captured Li Guang alive.
Shan Yu usually heard that Li Guang was very talented, so he ordered: If Li Guang is captured, he must be brought alive.
The Huns cavalry captured Li Guang. At that time, Li Guang was injured and injured, so they placed Li Guang between two horses and placed him in a rope net bag to lie down.
After walking for more than ten miles, Li Guang pretended to be dead and squinted when he saw a Hun boy riding a good horse next to him. Li Guang suddenly jumped on the Hun boy's horse, took advantage of the situation to push the boy off, took his bow, and galloped southward for dozens of miles. He met the remaining troops of his again, and led them into the pass.
The Huns dispatched hundreds of cavalry to chase him. As Li Guang fled, he picked up the bow of the Hun boy and shot the chasing cavalry, so he was able to escape.
So he returned to the capital of the Han Dynasty, and the court handed Li Guang over to the law enforcement officials.
The law enforcement officer ruled that Li Guang had suffered too many casualties, and he himself was captured alive by the enemy and should be beheaded. Li Guang used money and materials to atone for his death penalty and reduced his position to serve the people.
In the blink of an eye, Li Guang has been living at home for several years. Li Guang's family and Guan Qiang, the grandson of the late Yingyin Hou Guanying, live in seclusion in Lantian and often go hunting in Nanshan.
One night he went out with an entourage on horseback and drank with others in the fields.
When he came back, he walked to Ba Ling Pavilion. Ba Lingwei was drunk and shouted loudly, prohibiting Li Guang from passing.
Li Guang's entourage said: This is the former General Li.
Tingwei said: The current general is not allowed to pass, let alone his predecessor!
So he detained Li Guang and asked him to stay under Ba Ling Pavilion.
Not long after, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the prefect of Liaoxi and defeated General Han. General Han moved to Youbeiping.
So the emperor summoned Li Guang and appointed him as the right governor of Beiping.
Li Guang immediately asked to send Lieutenant Ba Ling to join him, and he was killed when he arrived in the army.
Li Guang was stationed in Youbeiping. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they called him the "Flying General of the Han Dynasty" and avoided him for several years, not daring to invade Youbeiping.
Li Guang went out hunting and saw a stone in the grass. He thought it was a tiger and shot at it.
Then he ejaculated again, but after all, he couldn't ejaculate anymore.
Li Guang had been stationed in various counties. When he heard about tigers, he often went to shoot them himself.
When he was stationed in Youbeiping, he went to shoot the tiger again. The tiger jumped up and injured Li Guang. Li Guang also shot the tiger to death in the end.
Li Guang was an upright official, and he distributed rewards to his subordinates. He always shared food and drink with the soldiers.
From his life to his death, Li Guang served as an official with a salary of two thousand stone for more than forty years. He had no extra property in his family and never talked about family property.
Li Guang was tall and had ape-like arms. He was good at archery and was gifted. Even if his descendants or outsiders learned from him, no one could compare with him.
Li Guang's speech was slow and he didn't talk much. When he was with others, he would draw military formations on the ground, and then shoot arrows. Whoever hit the denser rows or the wider rows would be punished with drinking.
He specialized in archery as a pastime until his death.
When Li Guang led his troops, he encountered a place where food and water were short of food. He found water, but the soldiers had not drank all of it, so he did not go near the water. The soldiers had not yet fully eaten, and Li Guang did not taste a morsel of food.
Li Guang was kind, gentle and not harsh to the soldiers, so the soldiers loved him and were willing to use him.
Li Guang's method of archery is to not shoot if he sees the enemy approaching and if he is not within a few dozen steps, he will probably miss the target. As soon as it is fired, the enemy will immediately fall to the ground with the sound of the bowstring.
Therefore, he led his troops to be trapped and humiliated several times, and he was also injured by wild beasts when shooting at them.
Not long after, Shi Jian passed away, so the emperor summoned Li Guang and asked him to succeed Shi Jian as Lang Zhongling.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang was appointed as the rear general. He followed General Che Weiqing's army out of Dingxiang to conquer the Xiongnu.
Many generals were made marquises for their military merits because they killed the enemy's heads in compliance with the prescribed amount, but Li Guang's army had no military merits.
Two years later, Li Guang, who held the title of Langzhongling, led 4,000 cavalry from Youbeiping. Bowang Marquis Zhang Qian led 10,000 cavalry to join Li Guang in two separate routes.
After marching for several hundred miles, King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led 40,000 cavalry and surrounded Li Guang. Li Guang's soldiers were very frightened, so Li Guang sent his son Li Gan to ride towards the Xiongnu army.
Li Gan galloped alone with dozens of cavalry, passed through the Xiongnu cavalry formation, and protruded from its left and right wings. He came back and reported to Li Guang: "The enemy Huns are very easy to deal with!"
The soldiers felt relieved.
Li Guang formed a circular formation, facing outward. The Huns attacked fiercely, and arrows rained down.
More than half of the Han soldiers were dead, and their arrows were all used up.
Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the Huns' lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns army gradually dispersed.
It was getting late at this time, and the officers and soldiers were all expressionless, but Li Guang looked calm and paid more attention to rectifying the army.
From then on, everyone in the army admired his bravery.
The next day, they went to fight hard again. Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns retreated.
The Han army was very tired and could not pursue him.
At that time, Li Guang's army was almost completely wiped out, so he had to withdraw his troops and return to the court.
According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, if Bowang Hou marched slowly and delayed the deadline, he should be sentenced to death, use money to atone for his crime, and be reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang's merits and demerits were equal to each other, so he was not rewarded.
At first, Li Guang's cousin Li Cai and Li Guang served Emperor Wen together.
By the time of Emperor Jing, Li Cai had accumulated merit and obtained an official position with an annual salary of two thousand dan.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, he served as the prime minister of the country.
Five years before Yuan Shuo, Li Cai was appointed as General of Qingchao. He followed General Wei Qing to attack King Youxian of the Xiongnu. He met the requirement of beheading the enemy and was named Marquis of Le'an.
Two years ago in Yuanshou, he was appointed prime minister on behalf of Gongsun Hong.
Li Cai's talents were among the lower class, and his reputation was far from that of Li Guang. However, Li Guang was not granted a title or land, and his official position was not higher than Jiuqing, but Li Cai was made a lord, and his official position reached Sangong.
Some of Li Guang's officers and soldiers also received the title of marquis.
Li Guang once chatted privately with the astrologer Wang Shuo and said: Since the Han Dynasty attacked the Xiongnu, I have never failed to participate. However, the talents of the officers below the rank of captain in each army were not as good as those of average people. However, there were dozens of people who were made marquises for their military merits in attacking the Huns. I, Li Guang, am not worse than others, but I don’t have any merit to obtain the fief. Why is this?
Shouldn't I be granted the title of Marquis because of my fortune?
Or is this the way it was meant to be?
Wang Shuo said: General, think about it yourself, has there ever been anything worth regretting?
Li Guang said: I was once the governor of Longxi. The Qiang people rebelled once. I tricked them into surrendering. More than 800 people surrendered. I used deception to kill them all on the same day.
To this day, my biggest regret is this incident.
Wang Shuo said: There is no greater disaster than killing those who have surrendered. This is why generals cannot be made marquises.
Two years later, General Wei Qing and General Huo Qubing led a large-scale expedition against the Xiongnu. Li Guang personally requested several times to accompany them.
The emperor thought that he was old and did not agree. It took a long time before he allowed him to go and made him a former general.
This year is the fourth year of Yuanshou.
Li Guang soon followed the general Wei Qing on an expedition against the Huns. After leaving the border fortress, Wei Qing captured the enemy soldiers and knew where the Shan Yu lived. He led his elite troops to chase the Shan Yu and ordered Li Guang to merge with the troops of General You and attack from the east.
The east road is somewhat circuitous, and the army is walking in a place where there is a lack of water and grass, so it is inevitable that they will not be able to march together.
Li Guang personally requested: "My position is a former general, but now the general ordered me to send troops from the east route. Besides, I have been fighting against the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and I have only got a chance to confront the Shanyu today. I am willing to be a vanguard and fight to the death with the Shanyu first."
General Wei Qing was secretly warned by the emperor, thinking that Li Guang was old and had a bad fate, so he should not let him confront the Chanyu, as he might not be able to realize his wish to capture the Chanyu.
At that time, Gongsun Ao had just lost his title of Marquis and was appointed lieutenant general, accompanying the general on the expedition. The general also wanted Gongsun Ao to fight against Shanyu with him, so he deliberately transferred former general Li Guang away.
Li Guang also knew the inside story at the time, so he insisted on asking the general to withdraw the transfer order.
The general did not agree to his request, and ordered the chief historian to write a document and send it to Li Guang's shogunate, and said to him: Hurry up to the right general's chariot troops and follow the document.
Li Guang set off without saying goodbye to the general. He was very angry and went to the military headquarters. He led his troops and joined forces with Zhao Shiqi, the right general of the chariot army, and set off from the east road.
The army has no guide and sometimes loses its way and ends up falling behind the general.
The general fought with Shanyu, but Shanyu fled, and Wei Qing had no choice but to return his troops.
The general traveled south across the desert and met the former general and the right general.
After Li Guang paid an audience with the general, he returned to his army.
The general sent Chang Shi to bring dry food and wine to Li Guang. The envoy asked Li Guang and Zhao Shiqi about the situation of losing their way. Wei Qing wanted to write a letter to the emperor reporting detailed military information.
Li Guang didn't answer. The general sent Chang Shi to urgently order the personnel of Li Guang shogunate to go for trial and confrontation.
Li Guang said: The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will personally go to the shogunate to be tried and confronted.
When he arrived at the shogunate of the general, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have fought more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and now I have the honor to follow the general on an expedition to fight the Shanyu army. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and long road, and they lost their way. Isn't it God's will?
Besides, I am already over sixty years old. After all, I can no longer bear the insults of those swordsmen and pen officials.
So he drew his sword and killed himself.
All the soldiers in Li Guang's army cried bitterly.
When the people heard the news, whether they knew him or not, whether they were old or young, they all shed tears for Li Guang.
The right general Zhao Shiqi was handed over to the law enforcement officials alone, and he should be sentenced to death. He should use property to atone for his crime and be reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang had three sons named Danghu, Jiao and Gan, all of whom were appointed Langguan.
Once the emperor was playing with the jester Han Yan, and Han Yan acted a little wanton. Li Danghu went to beat Han Yan, but Han Yan ran away, so the emperor thought Danghu was brave.
Li Danghu died early, and Li Jiao was named the prefect of Daijun. Both of them died before Li Guang.
Li Danghu had a posthumous son named Li Ling.
When Li Guang died in the army, Li Gan was following the hussar general Huo Qubing.
In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai used his position as prime minister to occupy the open space on both sides of the road in front of Emperor Jing's mausoleum. He was convicted and should be sent to law officials for investigation. However, Li Cai did not want to be tried and confronted and committed suicide. His feudal state was abolished.
Li Gan served as a school lieutenant and accompanied General Hussar to attack King Zuoxian of the Huns. He fought hard, captured King Zuoxian's war drums and flags, and beheaded many enemies. As a result, he was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei and granted 200 households in the city. He succeeded Li Guang as Langzhongling.
Soon, Li Gan resented the general Wei Qing for causing his father to die of hatred, so he wounded the general. The general concealed the incident and did not make it public.
Not long after that, Li Gan followed the emperor to Yong County and went hunting in Ganquan Palace.
General Huo Qubing was related to Wei Qing, so he shot Li Gan to death.
Huo Qubing was a noble and favored man at the time, so the emperor concealed the truth and said that Li Gan was killed by a deer.
More than a year later, Huo Qubing passed away.
Li Gan had a daughter who was the prince's concubine and was very favored. Li Gan's son Li Yu was also favored by the prince. However, he was greedy for money and profit, and the Li family gradually declined.
When Li Ling reached his prime, he was appointed as the supervisor of Jianzhang Camp, supervising all the cavalry.
He was good at archery and loved to nurse soldiers. The emperor believed that the Li family would be generals for generations, so he asked Li Ling to lead 800 cavalry.
Li Ling once penetrated more than two thousand miles into the Xiongnu territory, crossed the Juyan Sea, observed the terrain, and came back without encountering any enemies.
He was later named Cavalry Captain and commanded 5,000 Chu soldiers in Danyang. He taught archery in Jiuquan and Zhangye and stationed them there to guard against the Huns.
A few years later, in the autumn of the second year of Tianhan, Li Guangli, the general of the Second Division, led 30,000 cavalry to attack King Youxian of the Xiongnu in the Qilian Mountains. Emperor Wu sent Li Ling to lead 5,000 infantry archers and sent troops to a place about a thousand miles north of Juyanhai. He wanted to use this method to disperse the enemy's forces and prevent them from dealing with the General of the Second Division.
Li Ling had to return his troops by the scheduled time, but Chanyu surrounded and intercepted Li Ling's army with 80,000 troops.
Li Ling's army only had 5,000 men. They had shot all their arrows and most of the soldiers were dead, but they also killed more than 10,000 Huns.
Li Ling's army fought while retreating. They fought continuously for eight days and returned to a place more than a hundred miles away from Juyanhai. The Huns soldiers blocked the narrow valley and cut off their return. Li Ling's army lacked food and reinforcements were not available. The enemy stepped up their attack and persuaded Li Ling to surrender.
Li Ling said: I have no face to repay the emperor!
So he surrendered to the Huns.
His army was completely wiped out, and only more than 400 people were able to escape and return to the Han Dynasty.
After Chanyu got Li Ling, he had heard about the reputation of Li Ling's family and was very brave in war, so he married his daughter to Li Ling to make him noble.
When the Han Dynasty found out, they killed Li Ling's mother, wife, children and his entire family.
From then on, the reputation of the Li family fell into decline, and people in Longxi who had been guests of the Li family were all ashamed of it.
Tai Shigong said: "The Analects of Confucius" says that if a person in a superior position behaves correctly, things can be carried out without giving orders; if he behaves improperly, no one will obey even if he gives orders.
This is General Li!
The General Li I saw was honest and kind, like a country boy, and was not good at talking. But on the day of his death, people all over the world, whether they knew him or not, mourned him heartily.
His loyal character has indeed gained the trust of the soldiers!
The proverb says: Peach and plum trees cannot speak, but a path is naturally trampled under the tree.
Although this is a trivial matter, it can be used to describe a big principle.
summary:
General Li Guang, a native of Chengji County, Longxi, descended from Li Xin, a Qin general. Skilled in archery from a young age, he joined the army during Emperor Wen's reign, distinguishing himself against the Xiongnu and becoming a Zhonglang. Emperor Wen lamented his unlucky timing, suggesting he would have been a marquis in Emperor Gaozu's era. Under Emperor Jing, Li Guang served as a cavalry general, capturing enemy flags during the Rebellion of the Seven States but receiving no reward due to a private seal from the King of Liang. He later governed several border commanderies, earning fame for his fierce fighting.

During a Xiongnu invasion of Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu. He cleverly dismounted and unsaddled his men, feigning a lure, which deterred the enemy from attacking. At night, the Xiongnu retreated, suspecting an ambush. Under Emperor Wu, Li Guang became a palace guard chief alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng's army was strict and disciplined, Li Guang's was simple and flexible, earning soldiers' loyalty. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategy, though his lax approach sometimes led to danger.

Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting pursuers. He was sentenced to death for losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner. Later, as Right Beiping governor, he killed a disrespectful Ba Ling guard and was called the "Flying General of Han," causing the Xiongnu to avoid him for years. He once mistook a stone for a tiger and shot it, but could not repeat the feat. Li Guang was generous, sharing rewards and food with soldiers, and lived simply despite decades of high office.

In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang joined General Wei Qing's campaign but had no military merits. Two years later, he was surrounded by 40,000 Xiongnu with 4,000 cavalry. His son Li Gan's bravery calmed the troops, and Li Guang's personal archery killed several enemy officers, forcing a retreat. Despite heavy losses, Li Guang's calmness earned admiration. His cousin Li Cai, though less talented, became a marquis and prime minister, while Li Guang remained unenfeoffed. Astrologer Wang Shuo attributed this to Li Guang's past massacre of 800 surrendered Qiang rebels.

In the fourth year of Yuanshou, Li Guang, now a former general, joined Wei Qing's campaign against the Xiongnu. Wei Qing, warned by the emperor about Li Guang's age and bad luck, ordered him to take a circuitous eastern route. Li Guang protested but was overruled, leading to his army losing its way. After the campaign, Wei Qing demanded an inquiry. Li Guang, refusing to face humiliation, declared, "I have fought over seventy battles. Now, at over sixty, I cannot bear the insults of clerks," and committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning.

Li Guang's sons—Danghu, Jiao, and Gan—served as officials. Danghu died young, and Jiao became a prefect. Li Gan, a marquis, wounded Wei Qing in revenge but was later killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer accident. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling, a skilled archer, led 5,000 infantry against 80,000 Xiongnu, killing over 10,000 before surrendering due to lack of supplies. The Han executed his family, ending the Li family's reputation. The historian concluded that Li Guang's honest character, like peach and plum trees, naturally drew people to him, despite his lack of eloquence.

translation:
Li Si was a native of Shangcai, State of Chu.
When he was young, he worked as a minor official in the county. He saw rats eating dirty things in the toilet near his office. Whenever someone or a dog came near, he would be frightened and run away.
Later, Li Si walked into the granary and saw the rats in the granary eating the stored grain and living under the big house without having to worry about being disturbed by people or dogs.
So Li Si sighed with emotion: A person's talent or incompetence is determined by his environment, just like a mouse.
So Li Si learned from Xunzi how emperors governed the world.
After completing his studies, Li Si estimated that the King of Chu was not worthy of serving, and that the six kingdoms were already weak and there was no hope of making contributions to them, so he wanted to go west to Qin.
Before leaving, he said goodbye to Xunzi: I heard that if a person encounters an opportunity, he should not slack off. Nowadays, all the vassal states are striving for opportunities so that lobbyists can make meritorious deeds and gain real power.
Now that the King of Qin wants to annex other countries and proclaim himself emperor to govern the world, this is a good time for political activists and lobbyists from civilian backgrounds to travel around and express their ambitions.
Being in a humble position and not thinking about seeking fame and wealth is like an animal. It only wants to eat meat when it sees it. It only has a human face but can barely walk.
Therefore, the greatest shame is humble status, and the greatest sorrow is poverty.
Being in a humble position and difficult situation for a long time, yet still criticizing society, hating fame and wealth, and slandering oneself as uncontested is not the original wish of a scholar.
So I am going west to lobby the King of Qin.
After Li Si arrived in Qin, just as King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, Li Si asked to be a retainer of Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin. Lu Buwei appreciated him very much and appointed him Lang Guan.
As a result, Li Si got the opportunity to lobby. He said to the King of Qin: Mediocre people often lose opportunities, but those who can achieve great achievements are those who can take advantage of opportunities and be ruthless.
In the past, although Duke Mu of Qin dominated the world, he did not move eastward and annex the six kingdoms of Shandong. What was the reason?
The reason was that the number of princes was still large and the prestige of the Zhou Dynasty had not completely declined. Therefore, the five hegemons emerged alternately and successively promoted the Eastern Zhou royal family.
Since Qin Xiaogong, the royal family of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty has been weak and weak, and the princes have merged with each other. The area east of Hangu Pass has been transformed into six kingdoms. Qin State took advantage of the victory to gradually conquer the six kingdoms. It has been about six generations now.
Nowadays, the princes obey Qin just like the counties obey the imperial court.
With the power of Qin and the wisdom of the king, just like sweeping away the dust on the stove, it is enough to wipe out the princes, achieve the emperor's cause, and realize the unification of the world. This is the only opportunity that comes once in a lifetime.
If we are slack now and do not take action on this matter, when the princes become stronger again and enter into alliance alliances, even if they are as capable as Huang Di, they will not be able to annex them.
Qin Shihuang appointed Li Si as the chief historian, followed his plan, and secretly sent counselors to various countries with gold and jade treasures to lobby.
If famous figures from various countries can be bribed, they will be bribed with gifts; if they cannot be bribed, they will be killed with sharp swords.
These are all strategies to alienate the relationship between the princes and their ministers. Then, the King of Qin sent good generals to attack later.
The King of Qin appointed Li Si as his guest minister.
At this time, the Korean Zheng Guo came to Qin as a spy in the name of building channels, and was soon discovered.
The royal family and ministers of the State of Qin all said to the King of Qin: Most of the people who come from various vassal states to serve the King of Qin are lobbying for their king, just to alienate the State of Qin. They ask the King to expel all the guests.
Li Si was also among the guests planned to be expelled.
So Li Si wrote a letter saying:
I heard that officials were talking about expelling guest guests. I privately thought that this was wrong.
In the past, Duke Mu of Qin recruited talented people, and he obtained Yu Yu from Xirong, Baili Xi from the garden of Chu in the east, Uncle Jian from Song, and Pi Bao and Gongsun Zhi from Jin.
None of these five people were born in Qin, but Duke Mu of Qin used them to annex more than 20 countries, and then dominated Xirong.
Qin Xiaogong adopted Shang Yang's new method and changed customs. As a result, the people prospered and the country became rich and powerful. The people were willing to serve the country and the princes sincerely submitted. He defeated the armies of Chu and Wei and captured thousands of miles of land. To this day, the country is politically stable and strong.
King Qin Hui adopted Zhang Yi's strategy and captured the Sanchuan area, annexed Ba and Shu to the west, occupied Shangjun to the north, captured Hanzhong to the south, captured Jiuyi, controlled Yan and Ying, and occupied the dangerous Chenggao in the east, seizing fertile land, and further disintegrated the alliance of the six countries, making them face the west and serve the Qin State. Their achievements continue to this day.
King Zhao of Qin won Fan Sui, deposed Ranghou, expelled King Huayang, strengthened the public house, and eliminated the power of private dignitaries. Like silkworms eating mulberry leaves, he gradually annexed the lands of the princes, and finally laid the foundation for Qin to unify the world.
These four monarchs all relied on the power of guest ministers from other countries.
From this point of view, in what way does Ke Qing feel sorry for Qin?
If these four monarchs refuse guests rather than accept them, and alienate scholars without using them in important positions, this will make Qin neither rich nor powerful.
Now, Your Majesty, you have obtained the beautiful jade from Kunshan, the pearl of Suihou, the jade of the He family. You hang the bright moon pearl, wear the Tai'a sword, ride a Xianli horse, erect the green phoenix flag, and place the Lingnu drum.
None of the above treasures were produced in Qin, but Your Majesty loves them very much. Why is this?
If it must be produced by Qin and then used, then the luminous jade cannot be used to decorate the court, rhino horn and ivory products cannot be admired by you, the beauties of Zheng and Wei cannot be listed in your harem, and good horses cannot fill your stable. Gold and tin from Jiangnan should not be used, and paintings from Xishu should not be used as paint.
If the things you use to decorate your harem, serve as your concubine, and please your eyes and ears, must come from the Qin State, then the hairpins decorated with Wandi pearls, the earrings inlaid with jade beads, the clothes sewn from Dong'a white silk, and the gorgeous embroidered ornaments cannot be presented to you, and the fashionable and elegant, beautiful and quiet Zhao women cannot stand by your side.
And those who bang the earthen altars and pots, play the zither, slap their thighs, and scream to satisfy the appreciation requirements, this is the authentic music of the Qin Dynasty. Musical pieces such as "Zheng", "Wei", "Sangjian", "Zhao", "Yu", "Wu" and "Xiang" are music from other countries.
Now you abandon the set of Qin music of banging earthen altars and pots and listen to the sounds of "Zheng" and "Wei"; you don't listen to playing the zither but enjoy the music of "Zhao" and "Yu". What's the reason for this?
To put it bluntly, it is just for the pleasure of the eyes to satisfy the viewing needs of the ears and eyes.
But this is not the case when you employ people now. You don't ask whether the person can be used or not, and you don't ask about the merits of the person. As long as he is not a native of Qin, he will be dismissed, and as long as he is a guest, he will be expelled.
It seems that what your Majesty values ​​​​is beauty, music, pearls, and gems, and what he despises is talent.
This is not a way to unify the world and subdue the princes.
I have heard that the vastness of the land means abundant food, the vastness of the country means the large population, and the strongness of the army means the bravery of the soldiers.
That's why Mount Tai can be so tall without rejecting soil; rivers and seas can become so deep and wide without being picky about small streams; and only those who achieve kingly status can show their great virtue by not abandoning the masses.
Therefore, regardless of whether the land is southeast or northwest, the people do not distinguish one country from another. The grains are abundant all year round, and ghosts and gods grant blessings. This is why the Five Emperors and Three Kings are invincible in the world.
And now, Your Majesty, you have abandoned the people to help the enemy, rejected the guests and made them contribute to other vassal states, made the talented people in the world retreat and dare not go west, stop and dare not enter Qin. This is exactly what people say: lending weapons to the enemy and sending food to thieves!
There are many items not produced in Qin that are worth cherishing; there are also many scholars who were not born in Qin who are willing to be loyal.
Now you are expelling guests to support the enemy, harming the people to help the enemy, weakening yourself internally, and creating resentment with the princes externally. If you continue like this, it is impossible to keep the country from danger.
Therefore, the King of Qin abolished the order of expelling guests, restored Li Si's official position, finally adopted his strategy, and his official position was also promoted to that of Tingwei.
After more than twenty years, he finally unified the world and honored the king as "Emperor". The emperor also appointed Li Si as prime minister.
They also demolished the city walls of counties and counties in various countries, destroyed weapons in various places, and stated that they would no longer be used.
The Qin State did not have an inch of enfeoffed land, nor did it make the emperor's sons or brothers kings, nor did it confer meritorious officials as princes, so that the country would never have the scourge of war from now on.
In the thirty-fourth year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, he held a banquet in Xianyang Palace to entertain officials. Dr. Zhou Qingchen and others praised Qin Shi Huang's military might and virtue.
Chun Yuyue, a native of Qi State, advised: I heard that the Yin, Shang and Zhou dynasties ruled for more than a thousand years, and they enfeoffed clan members and heroes as their own auxiliary forces.

Li Si could not come to see him, so he wrote a letter to expose Zhao Gao's shortcomings and said: I heard that no minister can be as good as the monarch without harming the country; no concubine can be as good as her husband without harming the family.
Some ministers now have the power of rewards and punishments without authorization, and they are no different from you. This is very inappropriate.
In the past, Sicheng Zihan was the prime minister of the Song Dynasty. He had the power of punishment and acted with authority. One year later, he hijacked the king of the Song Dynasty and usurped the throne.
Tian Chang served as a minister of Duke Jian of Qi. His title was so high that no one in the country could rival him. His own wealth was as much as that of the public family. He performed favors and benevolence, winning the love of the people and the support of the ministers. He secretly stole the power of Qi State, killed Zaiyu in the hall, and killed Duke Jian of Qi in the court. In this way, he completely controlled Qi State.
Everyone in the world knows this.
Now Zhao Gao has an excessive ambition to ward off evil and behaves treacherously and rebelliously, just like Zihan did when he was the prime minister of Song Dynasty; his private wealth is as much as Tian Chang's in Qi Dynasty.
He also used the rebellious methods of Tian Chang and Zihan to steal your majesty's prestige. His ambition was just like that of Han Qi when he was the prime minister of Han An.
Your Majesty, if you don't plan ahead, I'm worried that he will launch a rebellion sooner or later.
The second said: What are these words?
Zhao Gao was originally an eunuch, but he did not do whatever he wanted just because he was in a comfortable situation, nor did he change his loyalty because he was in a dangerous situation. He was honest and devoted to good deeds. He got where he is today through his own efforts. He was promoted because of his loyalty and kept his position because of his faith. I do think he is a talented person, but you doubt him. What is the reason?
In addition, I lost my father at a young age and have little knowledge and do not know how to manage people. And you are old, so I am worried that you will be isolated from the people of the world.
If I don't entrust the state affairs to Zhao Gao, who else should I use?
Besides, Mr. Zhao is a shrewd and honest man, he does his best, understands the people's conditions below, and adapts to my wishes above, please don't doubt it.
Li Si said: Not so.
Zhao Gao used to be a humble man who didn't understand the truth, was greedy and constantly seeking profit. His status and power were second only to His Majesty, but his desire for status and power was endless, so I say it was very dangerous.
The second son had believed Zhao Gao in the morning and was worried that Li Si would kill him, so he secretly told Zhao Gao these words.
Zhao Gao said: The prime minister is only worried about me, Zhao Gao. After my death, the prime minister can do what Tian Chang did.
So the Second Emperor said: Let Li Si be handed over to you, the doctor, to investigate and deal with it!
Zhao Gao investigates Li Si.
After Li Si was arrested, he was put on a torture device and imprisoned in prison. He looked up to the sky and sighed: Oh! How sad!
How can the ignorant and foolish king advise him!
In the past Xia Jie killed Guan Longfeng, Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan, and Wu Wang Fucha killed Wu Zixu.
Are these three ministers disloyal? However, death was inevitable. Although they died loyally, it was a pity that they were not loyal to the people they were.
Now my wisdom cannot keep up with these three people, and the cruelty and cruelty of the second generation exceeds that of Jie, Zhou, and Fu Cha. It is right for me to die because of my loyalty.
Besides, isn’t it nonsense to govern the country in the second generation?
Not long ago, he killed his brother and established himself as the emperor. He also killed loyal people, reused lowly people, built the Epang Palace, and levied tyrannical taxes on the people of the world.
It's not that I don't give advice, it's that he doesn't listen to me.
All ancient sages and emperors had a certain degree of restraint in their diet, a certain number of vehicles, horses, and utensils, and a certain limit in their palaces. They issued orders and did things, and prohibited anything that increased expenses and was not conducive to the people, so that long-term peace and stability could be achieved.
Now the second generation is using unnatural and cruel methods on his brothers, without considering what disasters will happen. He persecutes and kills loyal ministers without considering what disasters will happen. He vigorously builds palaces, increases taxes on the people of the world, and does not hesitate to spend money. After these three measures were implemented, the people of the world did not obey.
Now the rebels have accounted for half of the people in the world, but the second generation has not yet awakened in his heart, and actually appointed Zhao Gao as his assistant. I will definitely see the thieves invade Xianyang and turn the court into a place where elk roam.
So the Second Emperor sent Zhao Gao to examine the prime minister's case, punish him, inquire about Li Si and his son Li You's rebellion, and arrest all his guests and family members.
Zhao Gao punished Li Si and tortured him more than a thousand times. Li Si could not bear the painful torture and unjustly confessed.
The reason why Li Si did not commit suicide was that he was arrogant and eloquent, and he had made great contributions to the Qin State. He really had no intention of rebellion. He hoped to write a letter to defend himself, and hoped that the Second Emperor would wake up and pardon him.
Li Si then wrote a letter in prison saying: I have been serving as prime minister to govern the people for more than thirty years.
When I came to Qin, the territory was still very small.
During the time of the late king, the land of Qin was no more than a thousand miles long, and its soldiers were no more than a few hundred thousand.
I used up my meager talents, carefully implemented the decree, secretly dispatched advisers, funded them with gold, silver and jewels, let them lobby in various countries, secretly prepared armies, rectified politics and education, appointed brave and capable officials as officials, and promoted The social status of the heroes gave them high titles and salaries, so they finally threatened South Korea, weakened Wei, defeated Yan and Zhao, flattened Qi and Chu, and finally annexed the six countries, captured their kings, and made King Qin the emperor.
This is my first crime.
The territory of Qin State is not vast. It has to expel the barbarians and raccoon dogs in the north and pacify Baiyue in the south to show the power of Qin State.
This is my second crime.
Respect ministers and improve their titles to consolidate their close relationship with the King of Qin.
This is my third crime.
Establish the state and build ancestral temples to show the lord's wisdom.
This is my fourth crime.
Change the symbols engraved on the scales, unify weights, measures and words, and promulgate them to the world to establish the prestige of the Qin Dynasty.
This is my fifth crime.
Build roads and places for sightseeing to show that the Lord is satisfied with his will.
This is my sixth crime.
Lighten penalties and reduce taxes to satisfy the Lord's desire to win over the people, so that all people will support the Emperor and never forget the Emperor's kindness until death.
This is my seventh crime.
It has been a long time since a minister like me, Li Si, committed a crime worthy of death. The emperor hopes that I will do my best to survive to this day. I hope your majesty will understand.
After the memorial was submitted, Zhao Gao asked the jailer to throw it aside instead of reporting it, saying: "How can a prisoner submit a petition!"
Zhao Gao sent more than ten of his disciples to pretend to be censors, visitors, and servants, and took turns interrogating Li Si.
When Li Si responded truthfully, Zhao Gao had people torture him again.
Later, the Second Emperor sent someone to verify Li Si's confession. Li Si thought it was the same as before, so he finally dared not change his confession and admitted his guilt in the confession.
Zhao Gao presented the verdict to the emperor, and the second emperor said happily: Without Zhao Jun, I was almost betrayed by the prime minister.
By the time the envoy from the Second Sect arrived in Sanchuan to investigate Li You, Xiang Liang had already killed him.
When the envoy returned, just as Li Si had been handed over to the custody of the jailers, Zhao Gao fabricated a whole set of charges against Li You for treason.
In July of the second year of the Second Emperor's reign, Li Si was sentenced to five punishments and sentenced to be cut in half in the Xianyang market.
When Li Si was released from prison, he was escorted together with his second son. He turned around and said to his second son: I want to go out to Cai Dongmen with you and lead the yellow dog to hunt and chase cunning rabbits, but how can we do it?
So the father and son cried bitterly to each other, and all the people of the three tribes were executed.
After Li Si's death, the second emperor appointed Zhao Gao as the prime minister. Zhao Gao made all the decisions, no matter how big or small.
Zhao Gao knew that he had too much power, so he offered a deer and called it a horse.
The Second Emperor asked his attendants: Is this a deer?
Everyone said: It's a horse.
The second generation panicked, thinking that he was confused, so he summoned the fortune teller and asked him to calculate a divination. Taibu said: Your Majesty goes to the countryside to offer sacrifices in the spring and autumn, and worships the ghosts and gods of the ancestral temple. He is not pious when fasting, and that is why he is like this.
You can fast again sincerely according to the appearance of a sage monarch.
So the second generation went to Shanglin Garden to fast.
He spent the whole day playing hunting in Shanglin Garden. Once a pedestrian walked into Shanglin Garden, and he shot him to death with his own hands.
Zhao Gao asked his son-in-law Yan Le of Xianyang to come forward to impeach, saying that someone unknown killed the person and moved the body into Shanglin Garden.
Zhao Gao advised the Second Emperor to say: The emperor kills innocent people for no reason. This is not allowed by God, and ghosts and gods will not accept your sacrifice. God will bring disasters, and you should stay away from the palace to pray for relief.
The second generation left the palace and went to live in Wangyi Palace.
The Second Emperor stayed in Wangyi Palace for three days. Zhao Gao pretended to be the Second Emperor's order and asked the guards to wear white clothes and face the palace with weapons in hand. He entered the palace and told the Second Emperor: Bandits from all walks of life in Shandong are coming in large numbers!
The Second Emperor went to the balcony to watch and saw the guards heading into the palace with weapons. He was very frightened. Zhao Gao immediately forced the Second Emperor to commit suicide.
Then he took the jade seal and carried it with him. None of the civil and military officials around him followed him. When he ascended the hall, it seemed to collapse several times.
Zhao Gao knew that God would not grant him the position of emperor, and the officials would not agree, so he called the younger brother of Qin Shihuang's younger brother and handed the jade seal to him.
After Ziying came to the throne, he was worried that Zhao Gao would cause trouble again, so he pretended to be ill and did not go to court to handle government affairs. He discussed with the eunuch Han Tan and his son how to kill Zhao Gao.
Zhao Gao came to see him and asked about his condition. Ziying summoned him to the palace and ordered Han Tan to assassinate him and annihilate his three clans.
Three months after Ziying came to the throne, Liu Bang's army invaded from Wuguan and arrived in Xianyang. All civil and military officials revolted against Qin and did not resist Pei Gong.
Ziying, his wife and children all tied ribbons around their necks and went to Zhidao Pavilion to surrender.
Liu Bang handed them over to the custody of his subordinate officials.
Xiang Yu killed them after arriving in Xianyang, and Qin lost the world.
Tai Shigong said: As a commoner in an alley, Li Si traveled to the princes, entered the customs to serve the Qin State, seized the opportunity, assisted Qin Shihuang, and finally completed the great cause of unification. Li Si occupies the position of the Three Officials and can be said to be very important.
Li Si knew the gist of the Confucian "Six Classics", but he did not devote himself to political clarity to make up for the emperor's faults. Instead, relying on his noble status, he flattered and followed at will, implemented harsh methods of torture, listened to Zhao Gao's heresy, abolished his legitimate son Fusu and established his concubine Hu Hai.
When rebellions broke out in various places, Li Si wanted to directly advise him. Isn't this too stupid?
People think that Li Si was so loyal that he died of five punishments. However, when I carefully examined the truth of the matter, I found it was different from the popular view.
Otherwise, Li Si's achievements would really be comparable to Duke Zhou and Duke Zhao.
summary:
Li Si was a native of Shangcai in the State of Chu. As a young county official, he observed rats in the toilet fleeing from people and dogs, contrasting them with granary rats that ate stored grain undisturbed. This led him to conclude that a person's competence depends on their environment. He studied under Xunzi to learn the art of governing an empire. Afterward, deeming the King of Chu unworthy and the six kingdoms too weak for him to achieve merit, he decided to go west to Qin. He told Xunzi that opportunity must be seized, and that the King of Qin's ambition to unify the world was a perfect chance for a commoner to gain fame and wealth. He considered humble status the greatest shame and poverty the greatest sorrow, rejecting the notion of a scholar who claims to be above worldly pursuits.

Upon arriving in Qin, Li Si became a retainer of Prime Minister Lü Buwei, who appointed him as a Lang official. He then advised the King of Qin that while Duke Mu of Qin had dominated the world, he could not annex the six kingdoms because the Zhou dynasty's prestige had not yet declined. Since Duke Xiao of Qin, the Zhou had weakened, and the six kingdoms had formed. Now, with Qin's power and the king's wisdom, the time was ripe to unify the world. He warned that hesitation would allow the princes to strengthen and form alliances, making conquest impossible. The King of Qin appointed Li Si as Chief Historian, following his plan to bribe or assassinate key figures in other states to alienate them from their rulers, followed by military attacks. Li Si was later made a Guest Minister.

When the Korean spy Zheng Guo was discovered, Qin's nobles urged the king to expel all foreign guests, including Li Si. Li Si wrote a letter arguing against this. He cited Duke Mu of Qin, who used five non-Qin officials to dominate Xirong; Duke Xiao, who used Shang Yang to make Qin rich and powerful; King Hui, who used Zhang Yi to expand territory and break up alliances; and King Zhao, who used Fan Sui to strengthen the royal house. He argued that these four rulers relied on guest ministers. He then compared the king's love for foreign treasures, music, and women to his rejection of foreign talent, stating this was not the way to unify the world. He concluded that expelling guests would weaken Qin and aid its enemies. The king abolished the expulsion order, restored Li Si's position, and later promoted him to Tingwei. Over twenty years, Qin unified the world, and Li Si became Prime Minister.

In the 34th year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, Dr. Zhou Qingchen praised the emperor, but Chun Yuyue advised enfeoffing clan members, warning that without strong assistants, the dynasty could not last. The First Emperor asked Li Si, who dismissed the argument. Li Si wrote that in ancient times, scholars used the past to criticize the present, undermining the emperor's authority. He requested that all "Poems," "Books," and works of the hundred schools be banned, with punishment for those who disobeyed, except for books on medicine, divination, and planting. The emperor approved, confiscating these texts to make the people ignorant. Li Si also contributed to unifying the writing system and building imperial villas. His sons married Qin princesses, and his daughters married Qin royalty. At a banquet, Li Si lamented that his wealth and status had reached their peak, and he feared the decline that must follow.

In the 37th year, the First Emperor died at Shaqiu. Li Si, Zhao Gao, and Hu Hai kept his death secret. Zhao Gao withheld the emperor's edict to Fusu and persuaded Hu Hai to usurp the throne, arguing that power was in their hands and that great deeds required decisive action. Hu Hai agreed, and Zhao Gao convinced Li Si by warning that Fusu would replace him with Meng Tian, leading to his death. Li Si wept but complied. They forged an edict making Hu Hai crown prince and another ordering Fusu and Meng Tian to commit suicide. Fusu obeyed, but Meng Tian was imprisoned. Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, and Zhao Gao gained great power.

The Second Emperor wanted to indulge his desires, but Zhao Gao warned that the princes and former ministers were suspicious and might rebel. He advised implementing harsh laws, killing all opponents, and replacing them with loyalists. The Second Emperor agreed, revising the law. Many princes and ministers were executed, including ten princes beheaded in Xianyang and twelve princesses dismembered. Prince Gao requested to die with the First Emperor, which the Second Emperor approved. Laws grew crueler, taxes heavier, and corvée endless, leading to rebellions like that of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang. Li Si tried to remonstrate but was blamed by the Second Emperor, who argued that a ruler should use the world to satisfy his own desires, not labor like Yao or Yu.

Li Si, fearing for his position, wrote a letter flattering the Second Emperor, advocating strict supervision and severe punishments to ensure the ruler's absolute power and pleasure. He cited Shen Buhai, Han Fei, and Shang Yang, arguing that harsh penalties for minor crimes prevent greater offenses. The Second Emperor was pleased and intensified supervision and taxation, leading to half the population being prisoners and corpses piled in the markets. Zhao Gao, fearing exposure, persuaded the Second Emperor to stay in the palace and not meet ministers, allowing Zhao Gao to control all affairs. Zhao Gao then tricked Li Si into seeking an audience during the emperor's leisure, angering the Second Emperor. Zhao Gao accused Li Si of involvement in the Shaqiu conspiracy and of colluding with rebels through his son Li You. The Second Emperor ordered an investigation.

Li Si wrote to expose Zhao Gao's ambition, comparing him to usurpers like Tian Chang. The Second Emperor defended Zhao Gao, but Li Si warned of his greed. The Second Emperor told Zhao Gao, who accused Li Si of plotting rebellion. Li Si was arrested and tortured into confessing. In prison, he lamented that the Second Emperor was worse than Jie and Zhou, killing brothers and loyal ministers, building the Epang Palace, and overtaxing the people. He wrote a letter listing his seven crimes, which were actually achievements, but Zhao Gao suppressed it. When the Second Emperor sent investigators, Li Si, fearing torture, did not change his confession. He was sentenced to five punishments and executed in the Xianyang market, along with his entire clan.

After Li Si's death, Zhao Gao became Prime Minister. He tested his power by presenting a deer and calling it a horse, which all officials affirmed. The Second Emperor, confused, went to fast in Shanglin Garden, where he killed a pedestrian. Zhao Gao advised him to leave the palace to pray, then forced him to commit suicide. Zhao Gao tried to take the throne but failed, so he installed Ziying, a younger brother of the First Emperor. Ziying, fearing Zhao Gao, feigned illness and had him assassinated, annihilating his clan. Three months later, Liu Bang's army entered Xianyang, and Ziying surrendered. Xiang Yu later killed them, and Qin fell. The Grand Historian commented that Li Si, though a commoner, achieved great success but failed to correct the emperor's faults, instead flattering him and implementing harsh laws. He listened to Zhao Gao, deposed the rightful heir, and when rebellions arose, his belated advice was foolish. His loyalty was questionable, and his achievements, while great, were not comparable to those of the Duke of Zhou.
