translation:
Wuyang Hou Fan Kuai was a native of Peixian County. He made a living by killing dogs and selling their meat. He once hid in the countryside with Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
At first, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and raised troops in Fengyi and captured Peixian County.
When Emperor Gaozu was the Duke of Pei, he used Fan Kuai as his servant.
He followed Pei Gong to attack Huling and Fangyu, then returned to guard Fengyi. He attacked the army of the Sishui County Supervisor in Fengyi and defeated them.
Then he went east to pacify Peixian County, and defeated the army of Sishui County Governor to the west of Xue County.
Fighting with Sima in the east of Dang County, he defeated the enemy and beheaded fifteen people. Pei Gong granted him the title of a senior official in other countries.
Pei Gong attacked Zhang Han's army in Puyang. When he attacked the city, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city and beheaded twenty-three Qin soldiers. Pei Gong also gave him the title of Duke Dafu.
After that, he often followed Pei Gong. When he attacked Chengyang, he took the lead in ascending the city and captured Hufu. He defeated Li You's army, beheaded sixteen people, and was awarded the title of Shangjian.
When the follower Pei Gong besieged the governor of Dongjun in Chengwu, he repulsed the enemy, beheaded fourteen people, captured eleven people, and granted the title of five great officials.
Following Pei Gong, he attacked the Qin army and passed south of Boyi.
The troops of the governor of Hejian were in the camp, and Fan Kuai defeated them.
They also defeated Zhao Bi's army in the north of Kaifeng. Fan Kuai defeated the enemy and took the lead in ascending the city. He beheaded one of the military commanders, beheaded 68 people and captured 27 people. Pei Gong gave him the title of Qing.
Following Pei Gong, he defeated Yang Xiong's army in Quyu.
When attacking Wanling, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city, beheaded eight people and captured 44 people. Peigong gave him the title of Xian Chengjun.
He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe and Sheyuan, blockaded the Yellow River ferry, went east to attack the Qin army in Shixiang, and went south to attack the Qin army in Taoyi.
Defeat Lu , the governor of Nanyang County, in Yangcheng. When attacking Wancheng to the east, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city.
Arriving at Li County in the west, Fan Kuai repelled the enemy, beheaded 24 of them and captured 40, and was rewarded by Pei Gong with an increase in rank and salary.
Attacked Wuguan, and when they reached Bashang, they killed one captain, beheaded ten people, captured 146 people, and surrendered 2,900 enemy soldiers.
Xiang Yu garrisoned under the stage and prepared to attack Peigong.
Pei Gong sent more than a hundred cavalry with him to meet Xiang Yu through Xiang Bo, and stated that he had not blocked the pass.
Xiang Yu held a banquet in honor of the army lieutenants. While they were drinking heavily, Yafu wanted to murder Pei Gong. He sent Xiang Zhuang to draw his sword and perform a dance in front of the banquet, hoping to take the opportunity to assassinate Pei Gong. However, Xiang Bo repeatedly protected Pei Gong.
At that time, only Pei Gong and Zhang Liang could enter the camp and sit down. Fan Kuai stayed outside the camp. Hearing that Pei Gong's situation was urgent, he entered the camp with an iron shield.
The guards of the military camp stopped Fan Kuai, but Fan Kuai ran straight in and stood under the tent.
Xiang Yu looked at him with his eyes and asked him who he was.
Zhang Liang said: "It's Fan Kuai who is accompanying Duke Pei."
Xiang Yu said: Strong man!
He gave him a cup of wine and a pig's leg.
After Fan Kuai drank the wine, he drew his sword, cut the meat, and ate it all.
Xiang Yu asked: Can I drink again?
Fan Kuai said: If I die, I will not refuse, let alone just drink a glass of wine!
Besides, Pei Gong first entered the Pass to pacify Xianyang and camped in Bashang to wait for the king.
As soon as the king arrived today, he listened to the villain's slander and had a problem with Pei Gong. I am worried that the world will be divided and the people will doubt the king.
Xiang Yu remained silent.
Pei Gong went to the toilet and called Fan Kuai out.
After coming out, Pei Gong left behind his carriage and rode only one horse. He followed Fan Kuai and four other men on foot and took a small path down the mountain to escape back to Bashang's military camp, leaving Zhang Liang to say goodbye to Xiang Yu.
Xiang Yu also had his way, so he had no intention of killing Pei Gong.
On this day, if Fan Kuai hadn't broken into the camp and condemned Xiang Yu, Pei Gong's situation would have been in danger.
The next day, Xiang Yu entered the city and bloodbathed Xianyang, and made Peigong the king of Han. The king of Han also made Fan Kuai a prince, called Linwuhou.
Later he was promoted to doctor and followed the King of Han into Hanzhong.
When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, Fan Kuai led another army to attack the army of the county magistrate of Xi County to the north of Baishui, and to the south of Yong County to attack King Yong's light cavalry troops and defeated them.
Following the king of Han, he attacked the two cities of Yong and Zhe, and was the first to ascend the city. When attacking Zhang Ping's army in Hao'an, he took the lead in ascending the city and rushed into the enemy's formation. He killed one county magistrate and one county magistrate each, beheaded 11 people and captured 20 people. He was promoted to the rank of Cavalry Commander.
Following the King of Han, he attacked the Qin army's chariots and cavalry in the east of Rang Township and repulsed the enemy. He was promoted to general.
He made the greatest contribution in attacking Zhao Bi and occupying Yixian, Huaili, Liuzhong, Xianyang and other places. He also made the greatest contribution by diverting water to irrigate waste hills.
When they arrived at Yueyang, the king of Han granted Fan Xiang, who was enfeoffed to Du Ling, as Fan Kuai's food town.
He followed the king of Han to attack Xiang Ji, washed the dates with blood and boiled them.
Defeated the armies of Wang Wu and Cheng Chu in Waihuang.
Capture Zouxian, Luxian, Xiaqiu and Xuexian.
Xiang Yu defeated the King of Han in Pengcheng and regained all the lands of Lu and Liang.
When Fan Kuai returned to Xingyang, the king of Han added 2,000 households in Pingyin as his settlement, and asked him to guard Guangwu as a general.
A year later, Xiang Yu led his troops eastward, and Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to attack Xiang Ji, occupy Yangxia, and captured 4,000 soldiers of General Zhou of Chu. They surrounded Xiang Ji in Chen County and defeated him.
Bloodbath in Hu Ling.
After Xiang Yu's death, the King of Han became the emperor. Because of Fan Kuai's meritorious service in holding on to the city and attacking in battles, he granted 800 households a new enfeoffment.
Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to attack the rebellious King of Yan Zang Tu, captured Zang Tu, and pacified the Yan territory.
King Han Xin of Chu launched a rebellion. Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Chen County, arrested Han Xin, and pacified Chu.
Emperor Gaozu changed Fan Kuai's title to that of a noble prince and established a trustworthy relationship with the princes, so that they could be passed down from generation to generation. Emperor Gaozu removed Fan Kuai's former food town and gave him food in Wuyang, naming him Marquis of Wuyang.
Later, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Daidi as a general to attack the rebellious King Xin of Han.
From the Huo people to Yunzhong, Fan Kuai, Jianghou Zhoubo and others jointly pacified it, so an additional 1,500 households were added.
Later, Fan Kuai led his troops to attack the armies of the rebels Chen Xi and Manqiuchen, and fought in Xiangguo. When he captured Bairen County, he took the lead in ascending the city. He also surrendered and pacified twenty-seven counties in Qinghe and Changshan counties, and destroyed Dongyuan County. He was promoted to Prime Minister Zuo for his merits.
In Wujing and Guangchang, he defeated the armies of Qi Wuyan and Yin Pan and captured them alive.
In the south of Daidi, the army led by the Hu general Wang Huang under Chen Xi was defeated. Then, he marched to join forces and attacked Han Wangxin's army. Fan Kuai's men killed Han Wangxin.
In Henggu, Chen Xi's Hu cavalry troops were defeated, general Zhao Ji was killed, and ten people including the Prime Minister Han Liang, the governor Sun Fen, the general Wang Huang, Tai Pu Xie and the general were captured.
Together with the generals, he pacified seventy-three villages and towns in Dai.
After that, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled. Fan Kuai led the army to attack Lu Wan as prime minister, defeated the army led by Prime Minister Lu Wan in the south of Jixian County, and pacified a total of 18 counties and 51 townships in Yan.
So Emperor Gaozu gave Fan Kuai an additional 1,300 households, confirming that he would be the Marquis of Wuyang with a total of 5,400 households.
When Fan Kuai followed Gaozu in the battle, he beheaded 176 enemies and captured 188 enemy soldiers.
He led the troops to fight alone, defeated seven enemy armies, captured five cities, pacified six counties and fifty-two counties, and captured one enemy prime minister, 12 generals, and 11 officials ranging from 2,000 to 300 shi.
Because Fan Kuai married Empress Lu's sister Lu Xu and gave birth to a son, Mr. and Mrs. Fan, Gaozu was closer to Fan Kuai than other generals.
During the Yingbu rebellion, Gaozu was very ill and hated seeing people. He lay in the palace confinement and ordered the gatekeepers not to let the officials in to see him.
Among the officials, such as Jianghou Zhou Bo, Guan Ying and others did not dare to enter the palace.
After more than ten days of this, Fan Kuai once pushed open the palace door and rushed in, followed closely by the officials.
I saw Gaozu lying alone with a eunuch on his pillow.
After Fan Kuai and others saw the emperor, they cried bitterly and said: I think your majesty joined us in raising troops from Fengpei to pacify the world. What a feat it was!
And now that the world has settled down, how exhausted you are!
Besides, you are seriously ill, the ministers are panicking, and you are unwilling to meet us to discuss state affairs. Do you just want to decide with a eunuch?
Besides, haven't you seen anything about Zhao Gao?
After hearing this, Emperor Gaozu smiled and got up from the bed.
Later, Lu Wan rebelled, and Gaozu ordered Fan Kuai to attack Yan as prime minister.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu was very ill again. Some people slandered Fan Kuai and the Lu family for forming a party. If the emperor died one day, Fan Kuai would lead his troops to kill Madam Qi and King Zhao Ruyi.
When Emperor Gaozu heard about it, he became furious and immediately ordered Chen Ping to drive Jianghou Zhou Bo in a chariot to replace Fan Kuai, and immediately beheaded Fan Kuai in the army.
Because Chen Ping was afraid of Empress Lu, he did not carry out Gaozu's order, but sent Fan Kuai to Chang'an.
When they arrived in Chang'an, Gaozu had passed away, so Empress Lu released Fan Kuai and restored his title and fiefdom.
In the sixth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Fan Kuai passed away, and his posthumous title was Marquis Wu.
His son Mr. and Mrs. Fan replaced him as marquis.
Fan's mother, Lu Xu, was also named Linguang Hou. When Gao Hou was in power, Lu Xu was also in charge of political affairs and was very arbitrary. All ministers were afraid of her.
In the ninth year when Fan and his wife were the Marquis of Wuyang, Empress Gao passed away.
The ministers killed the Lu family and Lu Xu's relatives, and then killed Fan and his wife.
The title of Marquis of Wuyang was suspended for several months.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, Fan Shi, the son of Fan Kuai's concubine, was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang, and his original title and fiefdom were restored.
Fan Shi died after reigning for twenty-nine years, and his posthumous title was Huanghou.
His son Fan Taguang succeeded to the throne.
Six years later, some members of Wuyanghou's family offended Fan Taguang and resented him very much. So he wrote a letter saying: A man in Huanghou City lost his fertility because of illness, so he let his wife have fornication with his brother and gave birth to him. In fact, he is not the son of Huang Hou, so he should not inherit the throne.
The emperor ordered the matter to be handed over to officials for trial.
In the sixth year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Fan Taguang's title was abolished, he was demoted to a commoner, and the feudal state and food towns were also removed.
Li Shang, the Marquis of Quzhou, was from Gaoyang.
When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, he gathered a group of young people and recruited thousands of people.
Peigong attacked the city and captured the territory and came to Chenliu. More than six months later, Li Shang led more than 4,000 soldiers to Qitou and returned to Peigong.
He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe and took the lead in ascending the city. Pei Gong conferred a title on him and named him Xinchengjun.
Following Pei Gong, he attacked the Feng family, blocked the Yellow River ferry, and defeated the Qin army east of Luoyang.
Following Pei Gong, he captured Wan and Rang, and also pacified seventeen counties.
He led an army to attack Xunwu alone and pacified Hanzhong.
After Xiang Yu destroyed Qin, he established Peigong as King of Han.
The King of Han bestowed upon Li Shangxin the title of Lord and made him the Captain of Longxi with the rank of general.
Li Shang led his army alone to pacify Beidi and Shangjun.
They defeated the army led by King Yong Zhanghan at Yanshi, defeated the army led by Zhou Lei at Yiyi, and defeated the army led by Su Zao at Niyang.
So the king of Han gave Li Shang 6,000 households in Wucheng County as his food town.
As the captain of Longxi, he followed the Duke of Pei to attack Xiang Yu's army for five months. He sent troops to Juye and fought with Zhong Limei. For his meritorious service in the fierce battle, the Duke of Pei granted him the seal of Liang Guoxiang and granted him 4,000 additional households.
During the battle of Longtuo, Li Shang charged into the battle, took the lead in ascending the city, and defeated Zang Tu's army in Yixia.
Because of his meritorious service in killing the enemy, he was promoted to the right prime minister, and was given the title of a lord. Like other princes, he cut the talisman as a letter, and it will never be extinguished from generation to generation. He took the five thousand households in Zhuoyi as his food town and was titled Zhuohou. As prime minister on the right, he led troops to pacify Shanggu alone, and then attacked Dai. Gaozu granted him the seal of the prime minister of Zhao.
As the Prime Minister of the Right and the Prime Minister of the State of Zhao, he led his troops, together with Jianghou Zhou Bo and others, to pacify Dai Heyanmen, and captured alive the Prime Minister of Dai Cheng Zong, the Prime Minister Guo Tong, and a total of 19 officials ranging from generals to 600 shi.
After the victory, he served as the bodyguard of the Supreme Emperor as a general for one year and seven months.
Then he used his position as Prime Minister You to attack Chen Xi and destroy the Dongyuan city wall.
As Prime Minister of the Right, he followed Emperor Gao to attack the rebellious Yingbu. Li Shang led his troops to storm the enemy's forward positions and captured two positions, allowing the Han army to defeat Yingbu's army. Emperor Gao changed his fiefdom to Quzhou, increasing it to 5,100 households, and took back the food fiefdoms he had previously granted. In total, Li Shang defeated three enemy armies, surrendered and pacified six counties and seventy-three counties, and captured the prime minister, the prime minister, one general each, two junior generals, and nineteen officials ranging from 2,000 shi to 600 shi.
Li Shang was serving Xiaohui. When he was a queen, he was unable to take care of political affairs due to poor health.
His son Li Ji was very close to Lu Lu.
In this year, Li Shang passed away, and his posthumous title was Jinghou.
His son Li Ji succeeded to the throne, and everyone in the world said that he had betrayed his friends.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, the vassal states of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao jointly rebelled. The emperor appointed Li Ji as general and besieged Zhao City, but it was not conquered for ten months.
After Yu Hou Luanbu pacified the Qi State and came to help in the war, he took the city of Zhao and wiped out the Zhao State. King Liu Sui of Zhao committed suicide and the feudal state was abolished.
In the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, Li Ji planned to marry Pingyuan Jun, the mother of Emperor Jing and his wife. Emperor Jing was furious and handed Li Ji over to judicial officials for trial. He was found guilty and deprived of his title of marquis.
Emperor Jing named Li Shang's other son Li Jian the Marquis of Mu to continue the Li family's descendants.
After the death of Miao Jinghou Li Jian, his son Kanghou Li Suicheng succeeded to the throne.
After Li Suicheng died, his son Huaihou Li Shizong succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Li Shizong, his son Li Zhonggen inherited the throne and served as Taichang. Later, the feudal state was revoked because of breaking the law.
Xia Houying, Marquis of Ruyin, was from Peixian County.
He began to take charge of horse breeding and driving in the stable of Peixian County.
Whenever he drove back after seeing off envoys or guests, he would go to Sishang Pavilion in Peixian County to chat with Gaozu, and they would chat for most of the day.
Later, Xia Houying served as a probationary county official and became closer to Gao Zu.
Once, Gaozu accidentally injured Xia Houying because of a joke, and was reported to the government.
At that time, Gaozu was the chief of the pavilion, and he had to be severely punished if he hurt someone. Therefore, Gaozu complained that he had not harmed Xia Houying, and Xia Houying also proved that he had not been harmed.
Later, the case was reversed. Xia Houying was imprisoned for more than a year because of Gao Zu's involvement, and received hundreds of slaps. However, Gao Zu was eventually exempted from punishment.
When Gaozu led his disciples to attack Pei County, Xia Houying contacted Gaozu as a subordinate official of the county magistrate.
On the day Gaozu surrendered to Peixian County, Gaozu made him Duke of Pei, gave Xia Houying the title of Seventh Doctor, and appointed him as his imperial servant.
When following Gaozu to attack Hu Ling, Xia Houying and Xiao He surrendered to Sishui County Supervisor Ping. Ping handed over Hu Ling and surrendered. Gaozu gave Xia Houying the title of fifth doctor.
He followed Gaozu to attack the Qin army east of Dang County, attacked Jiyang, captured Hufu, and defeated Li You's army in the Yongqiu area. During the battle, he drove a chariot to attack quickly and fought bravely. Gaozu gave him the title of silk guard.
Xia Houying also used his position as a servant to command chariots and follow Gaozu to attack Zhang Han in Dong'a and Puyang. During the battle, he drove chariots to attack Zhang Han quickly. He fought bravely and defeated the Qin army. Gaozu gave him the title of Zhigui.
He also commanded military chariots to follow Emperor Gaozu in attacking Zhao Ben's army in Kaifeng, and in Quyu he attacked Yang Xiong's army.
During the battle, Xia Houying captured 68 people, surrendered 850 soldiers, and seized a box of gold seals.
Then he commanded military chariots to follow Gaozu to attack the Qin army east of Luoyang. He drove into the battle and fought hard, and Gao Zu granted him the title of Duke Teng.
Then he commanded the chariots to follow Gaozu to attack Nanyang. In the battles at Lantian and Zhiyang, he drove the chariots to fight bravely and fought bravely until he reached Bashang.
After Xiang Yu entered the Pass, he destroyed the Qin Dynasty and made Peigong King of Han.
The King of Han bestowed upon Xiahou Ying the title of Marquis of Zhaoping. He also took the position of Taiwen and followed the King of Han into the Shu and Han regions.
Later, the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and Xia Houying followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu's army.
Marching into Pengcheng, the Han army was severely defeated by Xiang Yu.
The king of Han was defeated and fled quickly on his chariot and horse.
Xia Houying drove the car, walking slowly at first, and then drove quickly after the two frightened children hugged his neck tightly. The King of Han was very angry about this and wanted to kill Xia Houying more than ten times, but he finally escaped from danger and sent Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan to Fengyi safe and sound.
After the King of Han arrived at Xingyang, he collected the defeated army and regained its military power. The King of Han gave Qiyang to Xiahou Ying as a food town.
After that, Xia Houying commanded the chariots to follow the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu, pursuing them all the way to Chen County, and finally pacified Chu. When he reached the land of Lu, the king of Han added another county of Zishi to him as a food town.
In the autumn of the year when the king of Han became emperor, Zang Tu, the king of Yan, rebelled. Xia Houying followed Emperor Gao as a servant to attack Zang Tu.
The next year, he followed Emperor Gao to Chen County and arrested King Han Xin of Chu.
Emperor Gao changed the title of Xia Houying's food to Ruyin and cut the talisman into a letter so that the title could be passed down from generation to generation.
He also used his position as a servant to follow Emperor Gao to attack Daidi, and fought as far as Wuquan and Yunzhong. Emperor Gao gave him an additional 1,000 households.
Then he followed the King of Han to the vicinity of Jinyang and defeated the Huns cavalry belonging to Han Xin.
When chasing the defeated troops to Pingcheng, they were surrounded by Huns cavalry and were trapped for seven days without being able to escape.
Later, Emperor Gao sent people to give many gifts to the Queen of the Xiongnu King Maodun, and then the Xiongnu King Modu opened a corner of the encirclement.
As soon as Gaodi escaped from the siege and came out of Pingcheng, he wanted to drive away quickly. Xia Houying resolutely stopped the carriage and horses and walked slowly, ordering the archers to draw their bows fully and draw outwards. Finally, they were out of danger.
With this merit, Emperor Gao granted Xiahou Ying a title to a thousand households in Xiyang as a food town.
He also followed Emperor Gao as a servant to attack the Huns cavalry in the area north of Gouzhu Mountain and won a great victory.
As a servant, he attacked the Huns cavalry in the south of Pingcheng and broke through the enemy's formation many times. He made the most contributions. Emperor Gao gave him 500 households in the captured city as food.
He also used his position as a servant to attack the rebel armies of Chen Xun and Yingbu. He charged into battle and repelled the enemy troops. He also granted a settlement to a thousand households. Finally, the emperor designated Xia Houying's food town in Ruyin, with a total of 6,900 households, and revoked other food towns that had been sealed before.
Xia Houying followed Emperor Gao to raise troops in Peixian County and served as a servant for a long time until Emperor Gao's death.
Later, he served Emperor Xiaohui as a royal servant.
Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu were very grateful to Xia Houying for rescuing Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan on the road to Xiayi, so they gave him a first-class mansion close to the north of the palace, named "near me", which meant that he could be closest to me, and expressed their special respect for Xia Houying.
After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, he served the Empress Gao as a servant.
When Empress Gao passed away and King Dai came to the capital, Xia Houying went to the palace as a servant to clean up the palace together with Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju, deposed the young emperor, and used the emperor's method to drive to the palace of King Dai to welcome King Dai. Together with the ministers, he established King Dai as Emperor Xiaowen.
He died eight years later and was given the posthumous title Wenhou.
His son Yihou Xiahou Zao succeeded to the throne and died seven years later.
His son, Gonghou Xiahouci, inherited the title and died thirty-one years later.
His son Xia Houpo married Princess Pingyang. In the 19th year after he inherited the throne, that is, the second year of Yuanding, he committed adultery with his father's maid and committed suicide in fear of crime. The feudal state was also revoked.
Yingyinhou Guanying was originally a small businessman selling silk silk in Suiyang.
When Emperor Gaozu had just raised an army to rebel against Qin and established himself as Pei Gong, he conquered the city and came to Yongqiu City. Zhang Han defeated Xiang Liang and killed him. The Duke of Pei also retreated to the Dang County area. Guan Ying followed the Duke of Pei as the official in charge of the chamberlain. He defeated the army of the Dongjun prefect in Chengwu and the Qin army stationed in Gangli. Because of his bravery in killing the enemy, he was awarded the title of Seventh Doctor.
Later, he followed Pei Gong to fight the Qin army in the south of Bo County, Kaifeng and Quyu. Because of his hard fighting, he was given the title of Zhibo and was named Xuanling Lord.
He then followed Pei Gong to fight the Qin army from the west of Yangwu to Luoyang, defeated the Qin army in the area north of Xixiang, and then cut off the Yellow River ferry to the north. Then he led his troops southward and defeated the army of Nanyang County Governor Lu  east of Nanyang County, thus pacifying Nanyang County.
Going further west, he entered Wuguan and fought with the Qin army in Lantian. Because of his bravery and fighting, he fought all the way to Ba Shang, and was given the title of Zhigui and was named Changwenjun.
After Pei Gong was named King of Han, the King of Han worshiped Guan Ying as a doctor. He followed the King of Han to march into Hanzhong, and in October, he was appointed as the Visitor of the Middle Kingdom.
Following the King of Han, he returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, captured Yueyang, and surrendered to the King of Sai, Sima Xin.
The returning army surrounded Zhang Han again at Feiqiu, but failed to capture it.
Later, he followed the King of Han eastward to Linjin Pass, surrendered to King Dong Yi of Yin, and pacified the area under his jurisdiction.
In the area south of Dingtao, he fought with Xiang Yu's subordinate Long Qie and Wei Prime Minister Xiang Ta's army. After a fierce struggle, he finally defeated the enemy.
Due to his meritorious service, he was given the title of Marquis of the Marquis and was named Marquis of Changwen. Pingxiang in Du County was granted the title of his food town.
Later, as a visitor, he followed the King of Han to capture Dang County and marched into Pengcheng.
Xiang Yu led the army to attack and defeated the king of Han.
The King of Han fled westward, and Guan Ying retreated with the King of Han and stationed himself at Yongqiu.
Wang Wu and Wei Gong Shen Tu rebelled, and Guan Ying followed the King of Han to attack and defeated them.
After conquering Waihuang, he recruited soldiers to the west and stationed himself in Xingyang.
Xiang Yu's army came to attack again, and there were many cavalry among them. The king of Han selected people in the army who could serve as cavalry generals. Everyone recommended Li Bi and Luo Jia from Chongquan, the former knights of the Qin Dynasty.
The King of Han was about to appoint them, but the two of them said: We are originally Qin people, and I am afraid that the army sergeants think we are unreliable, so please appoint someone who is always by your side and is good at riding and shooting as our leader.
Although Guan Ying was young at that time, he fought bravely in many battles, so he was appointed as the middle doctor, and Li Bi and Luo Jia were appointed as the left and right captains. He led the Langzhong cavalry to fight the Chu cavalry east of Xingyang, and defeated the Chu army.
On the order of the King of Han, he led an army alone to attack the rear of the Chu army, cutting off the Chu army's food supply line from Yangwu to Xiangyi.
In the area of ​​​​the Lu State, they defeated the army of General Xiang Guan of Xiang Yu. His soldiers killed the Chu Army's You Sima and one of his cavalry officers.
After defeating Duke Zhe and Wang Wu, the army was stationed in the western area of ​​​​Yan State. The soldiers under his command killed five generals from Lou Fan and one from Lian Yin.
Near Baima, Wang Wu's general Huan Ying was defeated, and the soldiers under his command killed one of the captains.
He also led the cavalry to cross the Yellow River south and escorted the King of Han to Luoyang. Then the King of Han sent Guan Ying to Handan to meet the troops of the Prime Minister Han Xin.
When he returned to Aocang, he was promoted to the imperial censor.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, Guan Ying obtained the Shiyi Ping Township of Du County with the title of Liehou.
Later, as a royal censor, he led the Langzhong cavalry, subordinate to the prime minister Han Xin, and defeated the Qi army in Lixia. The soldiers he led captured the chariot general Hua Wu and injured 46 generals.
He forced the enemy soldiers to surrender, captured Linyi, and captured Qi's defense minister Tian Guang alive.
He also pursued the Qi State Prime Minister Guotian Heng to Ying and Bo, defeated the Qi State cavalry, and the soldiers he led beheaded one Qi State cavalry general and captured four of the Qi State cavalry generals alive.
He conquered Ying and Bo, and defeated Qi general Tian Sui in Qiancheng. His soldiers beheaded Tian Sui.
Then he followed Han Xin and led his troops eastward, attacking Long Qie and Liu Gongxuan's troops in Gaomi. The soldiers they led beheaded Long Qie, captured You Sima alive, one person each from Lian Yin, and ten generals from Lou Fan. He himself captured Zhou Lan alive.
After Qi was pacified, Han Xin proclaimed himself King of Qi and sent Guan Ying to lead an army alone to the north of Lu to attack Chu General Gong Gao's army and achieved a complete victory.
Guan Ying sent his troops south, defeated the army led by the Xue County Sheriff, and personally captured one of the cavalrymen.
Then they attacked Fu Yang, marched to Tongcheng southeast of Xiangxiang, and took the area around Li and Xucheng.
After crossing the Huaihe River, they conquered all the cities in Huainan and then arrived at Guangling.
Later, Xiang Yu sent Xiang Sheng, Duke Xue and Duke Tan to regain Huaibei.
So Guan Ying crossed the Huaihe River and went north, defeated Xiang Sheng and Tan Gong in Xiapi, beheaded Xue Gong, and captured Xiapi. Defeated the Chu cavalry at Pingyang, then surrendered Pengcheng, captured Xiang Tuo, the pillar state of Chu, and surrendered the counties of Liu, Xue, Pei, Feng, Xiao, and Peng.
Attacked Kuxian and Qiaoxian, and captured the general Zhou Lan again.
Then he met the King of Han in Yixiang.
Following the King of Han, he defeated Xiang Yu's army in Chen County. The soldiers he led killed two generals and captured eight generals.
The king of Han gave 2,500 additional households to the infants.
Xiang Yu was defeated at Gaixia, and then broke out and escaped. At this time, Guan Ying, as a censor, was ordered by the King of Han to lead the cavalry troops to pursue Xiang Yu and completely defeated him in the east city.
The five soldiers he led jointly killed Xiang Yu, and they were all named princes.
He also surrendered one man each from the left and right sima, and 12,000 soldiers, and captured all the generals and officials in Xiang Yu's army.
Then, they captured Dongcheng and Liyang, crossed the Yangtze River, defeated the army led by the Wu County Sheriff in the Wu County area, and captured the Wu County Sheriff. In this way, the three counties of Wu, Yuzhang and Kuaiji were pacified.
Then he returned to the army and pacified the Huaibei area, a total of fifty-two counties.
After the King of Han established him as emperor, he granted Guan Ying three thousand households a new settlement.
In the autumn of this year, he followed Emperor Gao as a chariot general and defeated the army of King Zang Tu of Yan.
The next year, he followed Emperor Gao to Chen County and arrested King Han Xin of Chu.
After returning to the dynasty, Emperor Gao cut the talisman into a letter and made it immortal from generation to generation. He granted the 2,500 households in Yingyin to Guanying as a food town and named him the Marquis of Yingyin.
After that, Guan Ying followed Emperor Gao to Dai as a cavalry general to attack the rebel King Xin of Han. When he arrived in Mayi, he was ordered by the emperor to lead his army to surrender the six counties north of Loufan, beheaded the Prime Minister Zuo of Dai, and defeated the Huns cavalry north of Wuquan.
He also followed Emperor Gao to attack the Xiongnu cavalry belonging to King Xin of Han in the Jinyang area. The soldiers he commanded killed one of the Xiongnu general Bai Ti.
Emperor Qin ordered the cavalry troops from Yan, Zhao, Qi, Liang, Chu and other countries to be led together, and defeated the Xiongnu cavalry at Qianshi.
When they arrived at Pingcheng, they were surrounded by a large army of Huns. They followed Emperor Gao back to Dongyuan.
When following Emperor Gao to attack Chen Xi, Guan Ying received the emperor's order to attack Chen Xi's Prime Minister Hou Chang's army alone in the Quni area, and defeated the enemy. The soldiers he led killed Hou Chang and five special generals.
Qu Ni, Lu Nu, Shang Quyang were surrendered, Anguo and Anping were conquered, and Dongyuan was conquered.
When Yingbu rebelled, Guan Ying led his army as a general of chariots and cavalry. In Xiangxian County, he defeated the army of general Yingbu and killed three generals, Yajiang and Loufan.
Then he marched to attack the army of Zhuguo in Yingbu and the army of Da Sima.
He then marched and defeated the army of Ying Bubie general Feizhu. Guan Ying personally captured Zuo Sima alive, and led his soldiers to kill ten of his junior generals. He pursued the enemy's defeated general's remnants all the way to the banks of the Huaihe River.
Therefore, the emperor gave him another 2,500 households.
After the Taing Bu was pacified, Emperor Gaozu returned to the court and determined that Guanying's food towns in Yingyin totaled 5,000 households, and revoked the food towns previously sealed.
In all the previous battles, Guan Ying accompanied Gaodi to capture two officials worth two thousand stone. In addition, he led his troops to defeat sixteen enemy armies, surrendered forty-six cities, pacified one vassal state, two commanderies, and fifty-two counties. He captured two generals, one each from the Zhu State and the Prime Minister, and ten officials worth two thousand stone.
When Guan Ying defeated Ying Bu and returned to the capital, Emperor Gao died. Guan Ying served Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu as a marquis.
After the death of the Queen Mother, Lu Lu and others appointed themselves generals as King Zhao and garrisoned Chang'an in an attempt to launch a rebellion.
After Liu Xiang, King Ai of Qi, learned of this, he sent troops westward to the capital, saying that he would kill those who should not be kings.
After General Lu Lu and others heard about it, they sent Guan Ying as a general to lead the army to stop the attack.
When Guan Ying came to Xingyang, he discussed with Jianghou Zhou Bo and others and decided to temporarily station the army in Xingyang. He secretly signaled to King Ai of Qi that he was ready to kill Lu, so the Qi soldiers stopped advancing.
After Jianghou Zhou Bo and others killed Zhu Lu, the King of Qi withdrew his troops and returned to his fiefdom. Guan Ying also withdrew his troops from Xingyang and returned to the capital. Together with Zhou Bo and Chen Ping, he established Dai Wang as Emperor Xiaowen.
Emperor Xiaowen then granted Guan Ying a land of 3,000 households, gave him a thousand catties of gold, and appointed him as Taiwei.
Three years later, Jianghou Zhou Bo was relieved of his position as prime minister and returned to his own fiefdom. Guan Ying became prime minister and revoked the position of Taiwei.
This year, the Huns invaded Beidi and Shangjun in a large scale. The emperor ordered Prime Minister Guan Ying to lead 85,000 cavalry to attack the Huns.
After the Xiongnu fled, King Liu Xingju of Jibei rebelled, and the emperor ordered Guan Ying to withdraw his troops and return to Beijing.
More than a year later, Guan Ying died while serving as prime minister, and his posthumous title was Yihou.
His son Pinghou Guuan'a inherited the title.
He died twenty-eight years later, and his son Guan Qiang succeeded to the throne.
Thirteen years later, because of the crime of rape, the title was suspended for two years.
In the third year of Yuanguang, the emperor made Guan Ying's grandson Guan Xian the Marquis of Linru and made him the successor of Guan Ying. Eight years later, Guan Xian was found guilty of bribery and his feudal status was revoked.
Tai Shigong said: I once visited Fengfei, visited the local elders, looked at the place where Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fan Kuai and Teng Gong originally lived, and asked about their relevant stories back then. What I heard was really amazing!
When they kill dogs or sell silk silk, do they know that they will be able to attach themselves to Jiwei, be named in the Han Dynasty, and pass on their virtues to their descendants?
I have had a relationship with Fan Kuai's grandson Fan Taguang. The stories he told me about the great ancestors' deeds when they started their business are exactly what I have described above.
summary:
Fan Kuai, a native of Peixian County, initially made a living by killing dogs and selling meat. He joined Liu Bang (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) in raising troops, capturing Peixian, and serving as a servant. Throughout numerous battles, Fan Kuai consistently demonstrated valor, often leading assaults on cities and beheading enemy soldiers. His military exploits included defeating Qin forces at Puyang, Chengyang, and Kaifeng, among others, earning him successive titles and promotions from Pei Gong (Liu Bang). A pivotal moment occurred at the Hongmen Banquet, where Xiang Yu plotted to kill Pei Gong. Fan Kuai, stationed outside, burst into the camp with an iron shield, confronted Xiang Yu, and condemned his actions, ultimately saving Pei Gong's life. Following Xiang Yu's defeat, Fan Kuai continued to serve Gaozu, suppressing rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Lu Wan, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang with 5,400 households. He married Empress Lü's sister, Lü Xu, and remained close to Gaozu. During Gaozu's illness, Fan Kuai boldly entered the palace to urge him to attend to state affairs. Later, slandered for conspiring with the Lü clan, Gaozu ordered his execution, but Chen Ping delayed, and after Gaozu's death, Empress Lü released him. Fan Kuai died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, posthumously titled Marquis Wu. His descendants held the title until it was revoked in Emperor Jing's time due to legal transgressions.

Li Shang, from Gaoyang, initially gathered followers during Chen Sheng's rebellion and later joined Pei Gong with over 4,000 soldiers. He distinguished himself in battles, capturing cities like Changshe and Wan, and was appointed Lord of Xincheng and later Captain of Longxi. Li Shang fought against Xiang Yu, defeated forces of Yong King Zhanghan, and pacified regions including Beidi and Shangjun. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuoxian with 5,000 households, later serving as Right Prime Minister and leading campaigns against Chen Xi and Yingbu. His fief was changed to Quzhou with 5,100 households. Li Shang served under Emperor Xiaohui but was unable to govern due to illness. His son Li Ji succeeded but was executed for treason during the Rebellion of the Seven States. Another son, Li Jian, continued the lineage until it was eventually revoked for legal violations.

Xiahou Ying, from Peixian, began as a stable hand and befriended Gaozu, even taking a false imprisonment for him. He joined Gaozu's uprising, serving as a chariot commander and fighting in key battles such as Dong'a and Kaifeng. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Xiahou Ying rescued Gaozu's children during a retreat and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ruyin with 6,900 households. He served as a servant under Gaozu, Xiaohui, and Empress Lü, and played a role in welcoming Emperor Wen to the throne. He died posthumously titled Wenhou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for adultery.

Guan Ying, a silk merchant from Suiyang, joined Pei Gong and fought in numerous campaigns, including against Qin forces and Xiang Yu. He distinguished himself as a cavalry commander, defeating Chu forces and capturing key figures like Zhou Lan. After Xiang Yu's death, Guan Ying pursued and killed him, leading to his enfeoffment as Marquis of Yingyin with 5,000 households. He later suppressed rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Yingbu. During the Lü clan crisis, he feigned support but secretly allied with Zhou Bo to establish Emperor Wen, becoming Taiwei and later Prime Minister. He died in office, posthumously titled Yihou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for bribery.

Sima Qian notes that these figures, originally humble commoners, rose to prominence and established lasting legacies through their service to the Han dynasty.

Chuilizi, named Ji, was the younger brother of King Hui of Qin. He and King Hui were not born to the same mother.
His mother is a Korean woman.
Chuilizi was eloquent and resourceful in dealing with people, so the people of Qin called him "the wise man".
In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, Chuilizi was granted the title of Yougeng. The King of Qin sent him to lead an army to attack Quwo in the State of Wei. He drove away all the people there and occupied the city. The land around Quwo was annexed to the State of Qin.
In the twenty-fifth year of King Hui of Qin, the King of Qin appointed Chuilizi as a general to attack the State of Zhao. He captured General Zhuang Bao of the State of Zhao and captured Linyi.
The next year, he assisted Wei Zhang in attacking Chu, defeated Chu general Qu Gai, and captured the Hanzhong area.
The King of Qin granted him the title Chuilizi, with the title Yan Jun.
After the death of King Hui of Qin, Prince Wu came to the throne, expelled Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, and appointed Chuilizi and Gan Mao as the left and right prime ministers.
The King of Qin sent Gan Mao to attack South Korea and captured Yiyang in one fell swoop. At the same time, he sent Chuilizi to lead a hundred chariots to the Zhou Dynasty capital.
The king of Zhou sent soldiers to line up to greet him with a very respectful attitude.
When the King of Chu learned about it, he was furious and scolded the King of Zhou because the King of Zhou should not be so respectful to Qin's uninvited guests.
In this regard, You Teng persuaded the King of Chu on behalf of the King of Zhou: When Zhibo attacked Qiu You before, he used the method of giving away carts to take the opportunity to let the army follow behind, but Qiu You was destroyed.
Why?
It’s just because I’m unprepared.
When Duke Huan of Qi attacked Cai, he claimed that he was punishing Chu, but in fact he was attacking Cai secretly.
Now the Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger and a wolf. He sent Chuilizi into the Zhou capital with hundreds of chariots, with ulterior motives. The King of Zhou viewed this matter based on the lessons of Qiu You and Cai Guo, so he sent soldiers with halberds in front and sergeants with strong bows in the back. On the surface, they were guarding Chuilizi, but in fact they were keeping him under guard to prevent any unexpected events.
Besides, how could the King of Zhou not worry about the Zhou Dynasty?
I'm afraid that once subjugated, it will bring trouble to you, Your Majesty.
King Chu became happy after hearing this.
After King Wu of Qin died and King Zhao came to the throne, Chuilizi was even more respected.
In the first year of King Zhao, Chuilizi led his troops to attack Pucheng in Weiguo.
The chief of Pucheng was very frightened and asked Hu Yan for advice.
Hu Yan stepped forward and said to Chuilizi on behalf of the chief of Pucheng: Are you attacking Pucheng for the sake of Qin or Wei?
If it is for Wei, then of course it is good; if it is for Qin, it is not advantageous.
The reason why Weiguo became Weiguo was because of the existence of Pucheng.
Now if you attack it and force it to be included in the territory of Wei State, the entire Wei State will surrender and attach itself to Wei State.
Wei lost the cities outside Xihe but was unable to regain them because its military strength was too weak.
Now the attack on Pucheng will merge the Wei State into the Wei State, and the Wei State will definitely become stronger.
When Wei is strong, the cities occupied by your country are in danger.
Moreover, the King of Qin wants to observe your actions. If it harms the State of Qin and benefits the State of Wei, the King of Qin will definitely punish you.
After hearing these words, Qilizi said thoughtfully: What should we do?
Hu Yan took advantage of the situation and said: "You give up Pucheng and don't attack. I will try to go to Pucheng for you to tell you this, so that the king of Wei will not forget the kindness you have given him." Qilizi said: Okay.
After Hu Yan entered Pucheng, he said to the officer: Chuilizi has grasped Pucheng's difficult situation, and he promised to capture Pucheng.
However, I, Hu Yan, can make him abandon Pucheng and stop attacking.
Chief Pucheng was very frightened. After hearing Hu Yan's words, he felt as if he had seen a savior. He worshiped again and again and said, "Please help me."
So he offered three hundred catties of gold and said: The Qin army has really retreated. Please allow me to report your achievements to the king of Wei, so that you can enjoy the same treatment as a king.
Therefore, Hu Yan received a large sum of money from Pucheng and became a prominent figure in Weiguo.
At this time, Chuilizi had relieved the siege and evacuated Pucheng, and returned to attack Pishi, the city of Wei State. Pishi did not surrender, so he withdrew again.
In the seventh year of King Zhao, Chuilizi died and was buried east of Zhangtai, south of the Wei River.
Before his death, he prophesied: A hundred years from now, there will be the emperor's palace sandwiching my tomb here.
Chuilizi Yingji's home is in Chuili, Yinxiang, south of the Wei River, west of Zhaowang Temple, so people commonly call him Chuilizi.
With the rise of the Han Dynasty, the Changle Palace was built to the east of his tomb, while the Weiyang Palace was to the west of his tomb, and the arsenal was directly opposite his tomb, just as it was said.
There is a proverb from the Qin people: If you are strong, you should be considered Renbi, and if you are resourceful, you should be considered Qili.
Gan Mao was from Xiacai.
Mr. Shi Ju, who once served Xia Cai, learned from him the theories of various schools of thought.
Later, he got the opportunity to meet King Qin Hui through the introduction of Zhang Yi and Chuilizi.
After King Hui met him, he liked him very much and sent him to lead troops to help Wei Zhang seize the Hanzhong area.
After King Hui died, King Wu came to the throne.
At that time, Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang had left the State of Qin and ran to the State of Wei in the east.
Soon, Qin Gongzi Shuhou Hui and his assistant Chen Zhuang rebelled, and King Wu assigned Gan Mao to pacify Shu.
After returning to Qin, King Wu appointed Gan Mao as the prime minister of the left and Chulizi as the prime minister of the right.
In the third year of King Wu of Qin, King Wu said to Gan Mao: I have a wish to ride in a carriage with hanging curtains, pass through the land of Sanchuan, and see the capital of the Zhou Dynasty. Even if I die, I will be considered satisfied.
Gan Mao understood this and said, "Please allow me to go as envoy to the Wei State and make an appointment with the Wei State to attack South Korea. Please allow Xiang Shou to assist me in going together."
King Wu agreed to Gan Mao's request. After Gan Mao arrived in Wei, he said to Xiang Shou: Go back and report the situation to King Wu. Wei has listened to my advice, but I hope the king will not attack South Korea first.
Once the work is done, it will be all your credit.
Xiang Shou returned to Qin and reported Gan Mao's words to King Wu. King Wu went to Xirang to greet Gan Mao.
Gan Mao arrived at Xirang, and King Wu asked him why he didn't attack South Korea first.
Gan Mao replied: Yiyang is a large county. Shangdang and Nanyang have accumulated wealth for a long time.
The name is county, but it is actually a county.
Now the king has left several dangerous passes where he has strongholds and traveled thousands of miles to attack them. It is very difficult to win.
Once upon a time, Zeng Shen lived in Feiyi. In the state of Lu, a man with the same surname as Zeng Shen killed someone. Someone told Zeng Shen's mother that Zeng Shen had killed someone. His mother was weaving cloth with a calm expression.
After a while, a man came again and told his mother that Zeng Shen had killed someone. His mother was still weaving and her expression remained unchanged.
After a while, another person told his mother that Zeng Shen had killed someone. His mother dropped the shuttle, got off the loom, climbed over the wall and ran away.
Based on Zeng Shen's virtue and his mother's deep faith in him, three people doubted him, and his mother was really afraid that he would kill someone.
Now I am not as talented as Zeng Shen, and your Majesty does not trust me as much as Zeng Shen's mother trusted Zeng Shen. However, it is not just three people who doubt me. I am afraid that your Majesty will also doubt me like Zeng Shen's mother did.
At the beginning, Zhang Yi annexed the land of Bashu in the west, expanded the territory beyond the Xihe River in the north, and captured Shangyong in the south. People in the world did not praise Zhang Yi for this, but thought that the king was worthy.
Marquis Wen of Wei asked Le Yang to lead troops to attack Zhongshan Kingdom. It took three years of fighting to capture Zhongshan.
Le Yang returned to Wei State to discuss his merits and ask for rewards, but Wei Wenhou showed him a box of denunciation letters.
Leyang was so frightened that he knelt down and worshiped twice and said: This is not my fault, it all depends on the power of the Lord.
Now I am a minister who lives here.
Chuilizi and Gongsun Dashu will argue with me about the pros and cons of attacking Korea on the grounds that Korea is strong. The king will definitely listen to their opinions. This will result in the king deceiving the king of Wei and I will be resented by Han Xianggong Zhongchi.
King Wu said: I will not listen to them. Please let me swear an oath to you.
Finally, Prime Minister Gan Mao was allowed to lead troops to attack Yiyang.
After fighting for five months, Yiyang still could not be captured. As expected, Chuilizi and Gongsun Shi raised objections.
King Wu summoned Gan Mao back to his country, intending to withdraw his troops and stop attacking.
Gan Mao said: The soil is there, don't forget it. King Wu said: We made an oath.
So he mobilized all his troops and asked Gan Mao to attack Yiyang, killing 60,000 enemies, and finally captured Yiyang.
King Xiang of Han sent Gong Zhongchi to Qin to apologize and make peace with Qin.
King Wu finally passed through the land of Sanchuan and reached the capital of Zhou, where he died.
King Wu's younger brother came to the throne and became King Zhao.
King Zhao's mother, Queen Mother Xuan, was a woman from Chu.
King Huai of Chu resented that when Qin defeated Chu in Danyang, South Korea sat idly by and did nothing to save him, so he led troops to besiege the Yong family of South Korea.
The king of Han sent Gong Zhongchi to Qin to ask for help.
King Zhao of Qin had just ascended the throne, and the Queen Mother was from Chu, so she refused to send troops to rescue.
Gong Zhongchi went to entrust Gan Mao, and Gan Mao advised King Zhao of Qin on behalf of South Korea: Gong Zhongchi dared to resist Chu because he was eager to be rescued by Qin.
Now that the Yong family is under siege, and the Qin army refuses to go out to Mt. Miao to rescue them, Gong Zhongchi will look down upon Qin and not come to court.
Uncle Han will also ask South Korea to move south to unite with Chu. Once Chu and South Korea unite, Wei will not dare to disobey it. In this way, the situation of attacking Qin will be formed.
What do you think is more advantageous than waiting for others to attack versus taking the initiative to attack others? King Zhao of Qin said: OK.
So the army was sent down Miao Mountain to rescue South Korea.
The Chu army immediately withdrew.
The King of Qin asked Xiang Shou to pacify Yiyang, and at the same time sent Chuilizi and Ganmao to attack the Pi family of Wei.
Xiang Shou was a relative of Empress Dowager Xuan. She had been close to King Zhao since they were young, so she was appointed by King Zhao.
Xiang Shou arrived in Chu State first. The King of Chu heard that King Qin respected Xiang Shou very much, so he treated Xiang Shou generously.
Xiang Shou garrisoned Yiyang for Qin, preparing to attack South Korea accordingly.
Han Xianggong Zhongchi sent Su Dai to say to Xiang Shou: A wild beast can knock over a hunter's car if it is in a hurry.
Although you conquered South Korea and humiliated Gong Zhongchi, Gong Zhongchi could still clean up the situation in South Korea and then serve Qin. He would think that he would definitely get a grant from Qin.
Now you give Jie Kou to the State of Chu, and give Du Yang to Xia Xiaoling Yin, so that Qin and Chu can have good relations.
The alliance between Qin and Chu is nothing more than attacking South Korea again, and South Korea will definitely perish.
If South Korea is to perish, Gong Zhongchi will personally lead his private disciples to resist Qin tenaciously.
I hope you've given this a lot of thought.
Xiang Shou said: I unite Qin and Chu not to deal with South Korea. Please explain this to Gong Zhongchi for me, saying that the relationship between Qin and South Korea can be cooperative.
Su Dai replied: I would like to tell you something further.
People say that only by respecting what others respect can you win the respect of others.
The King of Qin is not as close to you as he is to Gongsun Xi; the King of Qin does not appreciate your wisdom and talent as much as he appreciates Gan Mao.
But now these two people cannot directly participate in the major affairs of the Qin State, but you can only make decisions on the major affairs of the Qin State with the King of Qin. What is the reason for this?
They each have their own places where they lose trust.
Gongsun Shi favored South Korea, while Gan Mao favored Wei, so the King of Qin did not trust them.
Now the state of Qin is competing with the state of Chu, but you favor the state of Chu. This is the same path as Gongsun Shi and Gan Mao.
How do you differentiate yourself from them? People say that the Chu State is a country that is good at adapting to changes. You will definitely have trouble making friends with the Chu State, and you will be asking for trouble.
You might as well plan a contingency strategy with the King of Qin to deal with Chu's changes, be friendly with South Korea and guard against Chu, so that there will be no worries.
If South Korea forms a good relationship with Qin, it must first hand over state affairs to Gongsun Shi and obey his opinions, and then entrust the country to Gan Mao.
South Korea is your enemy.
Now you propose to be friendly with South Korea and guard against Chu. This is a diplomatic alliance without avoiding enemies.
Xiang Shou said: That's right, I really want to cooperate with South Korea.
Su Dai replied: Gan Mao once promised Gong Zhongchi to return Wu Sui to South Korea and let the people of Yiyang return to Yiyang. Now you are only thinking about taking back Wu Sui, which is difficult to do.
Xiang Shou said: In this case, what should we do?
Will Wu Sui not be able to get it after all?
Su Dai replied: Why don't you take advantage of the prestige of Qin and ask Chu for Yingchuan for South Korea?
Yingchuan is the place of sustenance of South Korea. If you ask for it and get it, it will mean that your decree is implemented in Chu State and you will take Chu State's territory to make South Korea grateful to you.
If you ask for it but don't get it, then the hatred between South Korea and Chu cannot be resolved and they will end up fawning over Qin.
Qin and Chu are competing for power, and you blame the Chu State little by little to make Han gradually move closer to you, which greatly benefits the Qin State.
After Xiang Shou heard this, he weighed the pros and cons and couldn't make up his mind for a moment, so he said casually: What should we do?
Su Dai immediately replied: This is a good thing.
Gan Mao wanted to use the power of Wei to attack Qi, and Gongsun Xi planned to use South Korea's power to attack Qi.
Now that you have captured Yiyang as a credit, you have gained the trust of Chu and South Korea and stabilized them, and then punished Qi and Wei for their crimes. Because of this, the plans of Gongsun Xi and Gan Mao will be in vain, and their power in Qin will be further weakened.
Gan Mao finally proposed to King Qin Zhao to return Wu Sui to South Korea.
Xiang Shou and Gongsun Shi tried their best to oppose this, but failed.
Xiang Shou and Gongsun Xi were resentful because of this and often spoke ill of Gan Mao in front of King Zhao.
Gan Mao was frightened and feared that something might happen, so he stopped attacking Puban of Wei State and took the opportunity to escape.
Chuilizi reconciled with Wei and withdrew his troops.
Gan Mao escaped from Qin and ran to Qi. He happened to meet Su Dai on the way.
At that time, Su Dai was on an envoy to Qin on behalf of Qi.
Gan Mao said: I was convicted in the Qin State and fled out of fear of disaster. Now I have no place to stay.
I heard that a girl from a poor family and a girl from a rich family were twisting twine together. The poor girl said: I don't have money to buy candles, but fortunately you have a surplus of candlelight. Please give me some of the remaining light. This will not damage your lighting, but it will enable me to enjoy the convenience of candlelight as you do.
Now I am in a difficult situation, and you are on a mission to the state of Qin, with great power in your hands.
My wife and children are still in Qin. I hope you can use your spare time to help them.
Su Dai agreed and sent an envoy to Qin.
After completing the task, Su Dai took the opportunity to persuade King Qin: "Gan Mao is an extraordinary scholar."
He has lived in the Qin State for many years and has been used in important positions for three consecutive generations. He knows all the terrain from Zhuoxi to Guigu, whether it is dangerous or flat.
If he relied on Qi to form an alliance with South Korea and Wei, and in turn plotted against Qin, it would not be beneficial to Qin.
King Qin said: If this is the case, what should we do?
Su Dai said: Your Majesty, why not give him a more valuable gift, give him a more generous salary, and welcome him back. If he comes back, he will be placed in the Ghost Valley and will not be allowed to come out for life. King Qin said: OK.
Immediately, Gan Mao was given the official position of Shangqing, and someone was sent to Qi State with Xiangyin to greet him.
Gan Mao insisted not to return to Qin.
Su Dai said to King Qi Min: That Gan Mao is a wise man.
Now the State of Qin has given Shangqing the official position and brought him the seal to welcome him.
Because Gan Mao was grateful for the king's gift and liked to be his minister, he declined the invitation and refused to go to Qin.
Now, my lord, what can you do to honor him? King Qi said: OK.
He was immediately appointed to the position of minister and left in Qi.
Qin also quickly exempted Gan Mao's family from taxes and corvee and competed with Qi to buy Gan Mao.
The State of Qi sent Gan Mao as an envoy to the State of Chu. King Huai of Chu had just intermarryed with the State of Qin and was very affectionate towards the State of Qin.
When the King of Qin heard that Gan Mao was in the State of Chu, he sent someone to say to the King of Chu: I hope to send Gan Mao to the State of Qin.
The King of Chu asked Fan Shu: I want to appoint a prime minister in Qin State. Who do you think is suitable?
Fan Shu replied: I am not capable enough and I cannot tell who is suitable.
The King of Chu said: I plan to let Gan Mao serve as prime minister. Is it appropriate?
Fan Shu replied: Inappropriate.
That Shi Ju was the gatekeeper of Xia Cai. He could not serve the king in big matters, nor could he manage the family well in small matters. He was famous for his survival, low personality, and lack of moral integrity, but Gan Mao was very respectful when he served him.
Therefore, considering King Hui's wisdom, King Wu's acumen, and Zhang Yi's eloquence, Gan Mao was able to serve them one by one and obtain ten official positions without committing any crime, which is difficult for ordinary scholars to achieve.
Gan Mao was indeed a talented man, but he could not serve as prime minister of Qin.
It is not a good thing for the state of Chu that the state of Qin has a capable prime minister. Moreover, the king had previously recommended Zhao Hua to serve in the Yue State. He secretly encouraged Zhang Yi to attack and caused chaos in the Yue State. Therefore, the Chu State was able to expand its territory, using Limen as a frontier and Jiangdong as a county.
I think the reason why the king's achievements have reached such a glorious level is that the country of Yue was in chaos and the country of Chu was in great rule.
Now the king only knows how to apply this strategy to Yue but forgets to apply it to Qin. I think it is a serious mistake for you to send Gan Mao to Qin to serve as prime minister.
Then again, if you plan to install a prime minister in Qin, it would be more suitable to install someone like Xiang Shou.
Xiang Shou was a relative to the King of Qin. When he was young, he wore the same clothes as the King of Qin, and when he grew up, he rode in the same car, so he could directly participate in state affairs.
Your Majesty must arrange for Xiang Shou to be appointed prime minister in Qin State, and that will be a good thing for Chu State.
So the King of Chu sent envoys to ask the King of Qin to let Xiang Shou serve as prime minister of Qin.
Qin finally made Xiang Shou the prime minister.
Gan Mao eventually failed to return to Qin, and later died in Wei.
Gan Mao had a grandson named Gan Luo.
Gan Luo is the grandson of Gan Mao.
When Gan Mao died, Gan Luo was only twelve years old and served Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin, Wen Xinhou.
The first emperor of Qin sent Cai Ze, the newly established king, to the state of Yan. Three years later, the king of Yan sent Prince Dan to Qin as a hostage.
The State of Qin was preparing to send Zhang Tang to the State of Yan to serve as prime minister, and planned to attack the State of Zhao with the State of Yan to expand the territory in the Hejian area.
Zhang Tang said to Marquis Wenxin: I once attacked the State of Zhao for King Zhao, so the State of Zhao resented me. He once said: "Whoever can capture Zhang Tang will be rewarded with a hundred miles of land."
Now to go to Yan State, you must pass through Zhao State, and I can't go there.
Marquis Wenxin was unhappy after hearing this, but there was nothing he could do to force him to go.
Gan Luo said: Junhou, why are you so depressed?
Marquis Wenxin said: I asked Cai Ze, Lord Gangcheng, to serve the State of Yan for three years. Prince Dan of Yan has come to Qin as a hostage. I personally invited Zhang Qing to serve as Prime Minister of the State of Yan, but he was unwilling to go.
Gan Luo said: Please allow me to persuade him to go to Yan State.
Marquis Wenxin scolded and said: "Go away!"
I personally asked him to go, but he was unwilling. How could you let him go?
Gan Luo said: Xiang Luo became Confucius's teacher at the age of seven.
Now that I am twelve years old, you still let me give it a try. Why are you so anxious to scold me?
So Wenxinhou agreed. Gan Luo went to see Zhang Qing and said: "Compared with your contribution and that of Lord Wu'an Bai Qi, who has greater contribution?"
Zhang Qing said: Lord Wu An defeated the powerful Chu State in the south, used his power to intimidate Yan and Zhao in the north, was able to win in battle, conquered in attack, and captured countless cities and towns. My achievements cannot compare with him.
Gan Luo said again: When Yinghou Fan Sui was the prime minister of Qin, who had greater power compared with the current Marquis Wenxin?
Zhang Qing said: Marquis Ying is not as powerful as Marquis Wenxin.
Gan Luo then said: Do you really understand that Marquis Ying is not as powerful as Marquis Wenxin?
Zhang Qing said: I really understand this.
Gan Luo went on to say: Marquis Ying planned to attack the State of Zhao, but Lord Wu An deliberately made things difficult for him. As a result, Lord Wu An died in Duyou as soon as he left Qili of Xianyang.
Now that Marquis Wenxin has personally invited you to serve as Prime Minister of the State of Yan but you insist on refusing, I don't know where you are going to die.
Zhang Tang said: Then follow your boy's advice and go to Yan State.
So people packed their bags and prepared to go on the road.
The departure date had been set, and Gan Luo said to Marquis Wenxin: Lend me five carriages, and please allow me to say hello to Zhao when Zhang Tang goes to Yan.
Marquis Wenxin went into the palace and reported Gan Luo's request to Qin Shihuang, saying: In the past, Gan Mao had a grandson named Gan Luo. He was very young, but he was a descendant of a famous family, so the princes all heard about it.
Recently, Zhang Tang wanted to excuse himself from going to Yan State because he was ill, but Gan Luo persuaded him and made him go resolutely.
Now Gan Luo is willing to go to Zhao State first to inform Zhang Tang about Zhang Tang, and please agree to send him there.
Qin Shihuang summoned Gan Luo and sent him to Zhao.
King Zhao Xiang went to the outskirts to welcome Gan Luo.
Gan Luo persuaded King Zhao and asked, "Has your Majesty heard that Prince Dan of Yan went to Qin as a hostage?"
King Zhao replied: I heard about it.
Gan Luo asked again: Have you heard that Zhang Tang is going to Yan State to serve as prime minister?
King Zhao replied: I heard about it.
Gan Luo then said: Prince Dan of Yan came to Qin, which shows that Yan will not deceive Qin.
Zhang Tang went to Yan State to serve as prime minister, which showed that Qin State would not deceive Yan State.
Yan and Qin do not bully each other. They obviously want to attack Zhao together, and Zhao will be in danger.
Yan and Qin did not bully each other for no other reason than to attack Zhao to expand their territory in the Hejian area.
Your Majesty, why don't you give me five cities first to expand Qin's territory in Hejian? I ask the King of Qin to send back the Prince of Yan, and then help the powerful Zhao State attack the weak Yan State.
King Zhao immediately set aside five cities to expand Qin's territory in the river.
Qin State sent back Prince Yan, and Zhao State had no fear and attacked Yan State. As a result, Zhao State obtained thirty cities in the upper valley, allowing Qin State to occupy eleven of them.
After Gan Luo came back, he reported the situation to the King of Qin. The King of Qin then rewarded Gan Luo and made him a minister. He also gave Gan Luo the land and house that belonged to Gan Mao.
Tai Shigong said: It is common sense that Chuilizi was favored because he was a brother of the King of Qin. However, the people of Qin praised his intelligence and recorded more of his deeds.
Gan Mao was born among the common people in Xiacai, and his reputation was well-known among the princes, and he was highly respected by the powerful Qi and Chu states.
Gan Luo was very young, but he came up with an ingenious plan and his reputation will be remembered by future generations.
Although he is not a loyal gentleman, he is also a veritable counselor during the Warring States Period.
It should be noted that when the Qin State became strong and prosperous, the world became more and more inclined to pursue the art of contingency and deception!
summary:
Chuilizi, named Ji, was the younger brother of King Hui of Qin, born to a Korean mother. Known for his eloquence and resourcefulness, he was called "the wise man" by the people of Qin. In the eighth year of King Hui's reign, he was granted the title of Yougeng and led an army to attack Quwo in Wei, driving out the inhabitants and annexing the land. In the twenty-fifth year, he captured General Zhuang Bao of Zhao and seized Linyi. The following year, he assisted Wei Zhang in defeating Chu, capturing the Hanzhong area. King Hui granted him the title Chuilizi, with the title Yan Jun.

After King Hui's death, King Wu expelled Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, appointing Chuilizi and Gan Mao as left and right prime ministers. King Wu sent Gan Mao to attack South Korea, capturing Yiyang, while Chuilizi led a hundred chariots to the Zhou capital. The King of Zhou greeted him respectfully, angering the King of Chu. You Teng persuaded the King of Chu that the Zhou king's actions were precautionary, not disrespectful, and the King of Chu became appeased.

Under King Zhao, Chuilizi was even more respected. In the first year of King Zhao's reign, he attacked Pucheng in Weiguo. Hu Yan, on behalf of Pucheng's chief, argued that attacking Pucheng would strengthen Wei and endanger Qin, leading Chuilizi to abandon the siege. Chuilizi later attacked Pishi but withdrew when it did not surrender. He died in the seventh year of King Zhao and was buried east of Zhangtai, south of the Wei River. Before his death, he prophesied that an emperor's palace would flank his tomb, which came true with the construction of Changle and Weiyang Palaces during the Han Dynasty.

Gan Mao, from Xiacai, studied under Mr. Shi Ju and met King Hui through Zhang Yi and Chuilizi. He helped capture Hanzhong and later pacified Shu under King Wu, who appointed him left prime minister. King Wu wished to pass through Sanchuan to see the Zhou capital, so Gan Mao proposed attacking Yiyang. Despite doubts from Chuilizi and Gongsun Shi, Gan Mao captured Yiyang after five months, killing 60,000 enemies. King Wu died after reaching the Zhou capital.

Under King Zhao, Queen Mother Xuan, a Chu native, initially refused to aid South Korea against Chu. Gan Mao advised sending troops, and the Chu army withdrew. Xiang Shou, a relative of the Queen Mother, was sent to pacify Yiyang. Su Dai advised Xiang Shou to ally with South Korea against Chu, but Xiang Shou hesitated. Gan Mao eventually fled to Qi after conflicts with Xiang Shou and Gongsun Shi. Su Dai persuaded King Zhao to welcome Gan Mao back, but Gan Mao refused and served Qi instead. He later died in Wei.

Gan Mao's grandson, Gan Luo, served Lu Buwei at age twelve. He persuaded Zhang Tang to go to Yan as prime minister and then convinced King Zhao of Zhao to cede five cities to Qin, leading to Zhao's attack on Yan and Qin's gain of eleven cities. Gan Luo was rewarded with a ministerial position and Gan Mao's former lands.

Tai Shigong noted that Chuilizi's favor came from his royal lineage, while Gan Mao rose from commoner status to fame. Gan Luo's youthful ingenuity earned him lasting renown, though neither was a loyal gentleman, both were true counselors of the Warring States period, reflecting the era's trend toward cunning strategies.
