Ji An, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Puyang County.
His ancestors were favored by the king of the ancient Wei Kingdom.
By the time he was the seventh generation, he had been serving as ministers and officials in the court for generations.
Ji An relied on his father's recommendation. During the reign of Emperor Xiao Jing, Ji An became the prince Xima. He was respected by others because he was a serious man.
When Emperor Jing died, the prince succeeded to the throne and appointed him as the official of the audience.
There was an attack between the Minyue and Ouyue people in East Vietnam, and the emperor sent Ji An to inspect.
Before he reached Dongyue, he turned back when he reached Wuxian and reported: The Dongyue people are attacking each other because the local folk customs are so aggressive that it is not worth bothering the emperor's envoys to inquire.
A fire broke out in Hanoi County, burning more than a thousand households. The emperor sent Ji An to inspect.
He came back and reported: Ordinary people there accidentally catch fire. Because the houses are densely packed, the fire spreads, so there is no need to worry.
When I passed through Henan County, I saw that the local poor were suffering from floods and droughts. There were more than ten thousand families affected by the disaster, and some even went as far as father and son eating each other. So I took advantage of the talisman I held and ordered the distribution of grain stored in the official warehouse of Henan County to provide relief to the local victims.
Now I request that the talisman be returned and bear the responsibility of falsely preaching the imperial edict.
The emperor believed that Ji An was a virtuous person, so he was exempted from guilt and was transferred to Xingyang County Magistrate.
Ji An thought it was a shame to be a county magistrate, so he resigned and returned home claiming illness.
When the emperor heard the news, he summoned Ji An to serve as a senior official in the imperial court.
Because he repeatedly expressed his opinions to the emperor, he was still not allowed to stay in the court for a long time and was released as the prefect of Donghai County.
Ji An admired Taoism, managed the government and handled civil affairs. He liked to be clean and tidy, and entrusted all matters to the capable county magistrates and book historians he selected.
When he manages county affairs, he just supervises his subordinates to act in accordance with general principles and does not pay attention to details.
He was frail and sickly and often lay indoors without going out.
In more than a year, Donghai County became very peaceful and peaceful, and people praised him very much.
After the emperor learned about it, he summoned Ji'an back to the capital to serve as the Lord Commander, and he was treated similarly to Jiu Qing's treatment.
He strives to govern by doing nothing, and promotes the big ideas without adhering to the legal provisions.
Ji An is very arrogant when dealing with others, does not pay attention to etiquette, contradicts people in person, and cannot tolerate other people's mistakes.
He would be close to and friendly to those who were congenial to him; he would be impatient to meet those who were incompatible with him, and therefore the scholars would not want to rely on him.
But Ji An was eager to learn and good at doing chivalry, and he paid great attention to his ambition and integrity. He usually lives at home and has good and pure conduct; when he enters the court, he likes to speak out and give advice, repeatedly offending the emperor's face, and often admires the conduct of Fu Bai and Yuan An.
He had good relations with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi and Zong Zheng and Liu Qi.
They were also unable to stay in their official positions for a long time because of their repeated remonstrances.
Just when Ji An was appointed Lord Commander and Lieutenant-in-Chief, the Queen Mother's younger brother Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister. When high-ranking officials with an annual salary of two thousand dan came to visit him, they all knelt down and bowed down, but Tian Fu actually refused to return the courtesy.
But when Ji An asked to see Tian Fu, he never bowed down and often bowed to him.
At this time, the emperor was recruiting literary scholars and Confucian scholars, saying what I wanted, Ji An replied: "Your Majesty has many desires in his heart and only practices benevolence and righteousness on the surface. How can he truly imitate the political achievements of Tang Yao and Yu Shun!"
The emperor was silent, angry in his heart, and then stopped courting with a sudden change of expression. The ministers were all frightened and worried about Ji An.
After the emperor retired from the court, he said to the ministers around him: This is too much, Ji An is too stupid and straightforward!
Someone among the ministers blamed Ji An, and Ji An said: Is it true that the emperor appointed ministers such as public ministers and hundreds of officials to be submissive and flattery, and put the monarch in a dilemma that goes against the right path?
What's more, I am already in the position of Jiuqing. Even though I cherish my life, what if I harm the important affairs of the court?
Ji An was sick and had been ill for three months. The emperor had repeatedly granted him leave to recuperate, but his illness never recovered.
The last time he was very ill, Zhuang Zhu asked for leave on his behalf. The emperor asked: How is Ji An?
Zhuang Zhu said: There is nothing extraordinary about letting Ji An become an official and deacon.
However, he can assist the young monarch, stick to the established cause, use inducements to prevent him from coming, use threats to prevent him from leaving. Even if someone claims to be as brave as Meng Ben and Xia Yu, he cannot regret his integrity. The emperor said: Yes.
In ancient times, there were so-called loyal ministers who ensured peace and security, and Ji An was very similar to them.
General Wei Qing entered the palace, and the emperor sat beside the bed to see him.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong usually asked to see him for something, but the emperor sometimes didn't even wear his hat.
As for Ji An's visit, the emperor would not receive him without wearing a good hat.
The emperor was once sitting in a majestic military tent. When Ji An came to report on official business, the emperor was not wearing a hat. When he saw him, he hurriedly hid in the tent and sent a close servant to approve his memorial.
Ji An was respected and respected by the emperor to this extent.
As soon as Zhang Tang became a court official by changing the criminal law, Ji An repeatedly questioned and accused Zhang Tang in front of the emperor, saying: As a minister, you are unable to carry forward the achievements of the late emperor, and you are unable to curb the evil desires of the people in the world. Safeguarding the country and enriching the people, and keeping the prisons empty of criminals are neither of these two things.
On the contrary, you try your best to do the wrong thing and make others guilty in order to achieve your own career. How dare you change the rules and regulations set by Emperor Gaozu?
If you do this, you will lose your descendants.
Ji An often argued with Zhang Tang. When Zhang Tang argued, he always deliberately delved into the provisions and demanded details. Ji An, on the other hand, was upright and serious in his speech, high-spirited and unwilling to give in. He scolded Zhang Tang angrily and said: "Everyone in the world said that an official with swords and pens should never be allowed to hold the position of public minister. It is true."
If we act according to what Zhang Tang said, people in the world will be so frightened that they will stand with their feet together and not dare to take a step, and they will not dare to look directly at him!
At this time, the Han Dynasty was conquering the Xiongnu and recruiting ethnic minorities in various places.
Ji An tried to keep the country in peace, and often took the opportunity to advise the emperor to propose peace with the Huns instead of raising troops to fight.
The emperor was devoted to Confucianism and respected Gongsun Hong, but he didn't care about it.
When domestic troubles arose, and low-level officials and lawless people tried their best to evade justice, the emperor decided to separate the laws and enforce strict laws. Zhang Tang and others continued to report important cases to win the emperor's favor.
And Ji An often slandered Confucianism and criticized Gongsun Hong and others face to face for being treacherous at heart but clever outside, in order to please the emperor to win favor; the swordsman and penman were dedicated to studying the legal provisions and slandering them with clever words to frame others as guilty. , preventing the truth from being revealed, and using victory in prison as capital to claim credit, so the emperor relied more and more on Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang. Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang hated Ji An deeply, and even the emperor disliked him and wanted to kill him for an excuse.
Gongsun Hong became the prime minister and suggested to the emperor: There are many dignitaries and royal family members living in the right inner history area, which is difficult to manage. It is not that a minister with a good reputation cannot take on this important task. Please appoint Ji An as the right inner history.
Ji An served as the internal history of You for several years. During his tenure, his political affairs were in order and never neglected.
The general Wei Qing has become more and more noble. His sister Wei Zifu became the queen, but Ji An still treated him as an equal.
Someone advised Ji An: "The emperor wanted all the officials to be subordinate to the general. Now that the general is respected and valued by the emperor, his status is even more noble. You must kneel down and worship him."
Ji An replied: "Because the general has guests who bow his hands and salute, does that make him disrespected?"
When the general heard what he said, he thought Ji An was even more virtuous. He asked him many times for advice on difficult matters in the country and the court, and regarded him better than people he had always known.
Liu An, the king of Huainan, conspired to rebel and was afraid of Ji An. He said: "Ji An loves to speak out and give advice. He sticks to his integrity and is willing to die for justice. It is difficult to tempt him with unfair things."
As for persuading Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, it was as easy as removing a covering or shaking off the falling leaves.
When today the emperor has conquered the Xiongnu many times and achieved great success, and Ji An advocated making peace with the foreigners without raising troops to conquer, he would not listen even more.
When Ji An was enjoying the treatment of Jiuqing, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang were just ordinary petty officials.
When Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang became more prominent and equaled Ji An in official positions, Ji An again accused and slandered them.
Soon, Gongsun Hong was promoted to prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Pingjin; Zhang Tangguan was promoted to Yushi Dafu; the former county magistrates and book historians under Ji An were also at the same level as Ji An, and some were re-employed and even surpassed him in status.
Ji An was narrow-minded and impetuous, and it was impossible not to complain at all. When he met with the emperor, he stepped forward and said: Your Majesty appoints ministers like a pile of firewood, and the later ones are piled on top.
The emperor remained silent.
After a while Ji An retreated, and the emperor said: A person cannot be without knowledge. After listening to Ji An's words, his stupidity became more and more serious.
Not long after, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his troops to surrender to the Han Dynasty, and the court conscripted 20,000 vehicles to pick them up.
The government had no money, so they borrowed horses from the people.
Some people hide their horses so that they cannot gather them together.
The emperor was furious and wanted to kill the magistrate of Chang'an.
Ji An said: The magistrate of Chang'an County is not guilty. As long as he kills me, the people will be willing to sacrifice their horses.
Moreover, if the Xiongnu generals betrayed their monarch and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, the court could slowly ask the counties along the way to prepare chariots and horses to pick them up in order. Why would it disturb the whole country and make our people exhausted to serve the surrendered soldiers of the Xiongnu generals?
The emperor was silent.
When King Hunxie arrived with his troops, more than 500 merchants were sentenced to death for doing business with the Huns.
Ji An asked for the opportunity to be interviewed, and met the emperor in the Gaomen Hall of Weiyang Palace. He said: The Huns attacked our fortresses on the main roads and severed the friendly relations between the relatives. Our country sent troops to conquer them. Countless people died and were injured in the battle, and tens of billions of money were spent.
I foolishly thought that when your Majesty captured the Huns, he would reward them as slaves to the families of those who died in the army, and would also give them the captured property, in order to thank the people of the world for their hard work and satisfy the people's wishes.
Even if this is not possible now, and King Hunxie leads tens of thousands of people to surrender, he should not spend all the property in the official treasury to reward them, recruit honest and dutiful people to serve them, and treat them like darlings.
How could the ignorant people know that if they allowed the Huns to buy goods in Chang'an City, they would be regarded as illegally smuggling property out of the customs by law enforcement officers who are obsessed with legal provisions and be sentenced?
Even though Your Majesty cannot seize the Huns' supplies to comfort the people of the world, you still have to use harsh laws to kill more than 500 ignorant people. This is the so-called practice of "protecting the leaves and damaging the branches." I privately think that Your Majesty's move is undesirable.
The emperor was silent and disagreed, and then said: I haven't heard Ji An's words for a long time. Today he talked nonsense again.
A few months later, Ji An was convicted of violating a minor law. When the emperor granted him amnesty, he was only dismissed from office.
So Ji An retired to the countryside.
A few years later, when the country changed the minting of five-baht coins, many people minted coins privately, especially in the Chu region.
The emperor believed that Huaiyang County was an important transportation route to Chu, so he conscripted Ji An and appointed him as the prefect of Huaiyang County.
Ji An prostrated himself on the ground and declined the imperial edict, refusing to accept the seal. The emperor issued edicts many times to force him to accept the order.
The emperor issued an edict to summon Ji An. Ji An cried and said to the emperor: I thought that my bones would be abandoned in the ditch after my death and I would never see your majesty again. I never expected that your majesty would accept me and appoint me.
I am often sick, and my physical strength is not up to the demands of the post of governor. I hope that the middle-aged man will go in and out of the forbidden gates of the palace to correct your mistakes and make up for your shortcomings. This is my wish.
The emperor said: "Don't you look down on the position of the governor of Huaiyang County?"
I now summon and appoint you.
Due to the tense relationship between the local government and the people in Huaiyang, I have no choice but to use your authority and ask you to stay at home and manage it.
After Ji An said goodbye to the emperor, he went to visit Li Xi, the great minister. He said: I was abandoned in a foreign county and can no longer participate in the affairs of the imperial court.
However, Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, was clever enough to block other people's criticism, and cunning enough to cover up his own mistakes. He used clever flattery words and strong arguments to find faults. He refused to speak uprightly for the people of the world, and devoted himself to catering to the emperor's thoughts.
If the emperor didn't want it, he would slander it; if the emperor wanted it, he would take the opportunity to praise it.
He likes to cause trouble and fiddle with laws and regulations. In court, he is deeply treacherous to cater to the Lord's will, and outside the court, he blackmails officials who harm society to strengthen his power.
You are the ninth minister. If you don't advise the emperor as soon as possible, both you and him will be killed.
Li Xi was afraid of Zhang Tang and never dared to remonstrate with the emperor.
Ji An managed the county affairs as he had in the past, and the politics of Huaiyang County became clear.
Later, Zhang Tang was indeed ruined. After the emperor learned what Ji An had said to Li Xi, he found Li Xi guilty and ordered Ji An to enjoy the salary treatment of the princes and ministers and still be in charge of Huaiyang County.
Ji An died seven years later.
After Ji An's death, because of Ji An's relationship, the emperor appointed his younger brother Ji Ren to be promoted to the rank of Jiu Qing, and his son Ji Yan to be promoted to the minister of the princes and states.
Ji An's aunt's son Sima An was also the prince Xima when he was young. He was good at juggling legal provisions and was skillful in serving as an official. His official position reached Jiuqing four times, and he died while serving as the governor of Henan County.
Because of him, ten of his brothers were promoted to the rank of two thousand shi at the same time.
Duan Hong from Puyang initially served Gaihou Wang Xin. Wang Xin recommended Duan Hong, and Duan Hong was promoted to Jiuqing twice.
But the officials in Puyang's hometown all respected Ji An and were content to live under him.
Zheng was born in Chen County with a courtesy name of Zhuang.
His ancestor Zheng Jun once served as a general under Xiang Ji. Soon after Xiang Ji died, he belonged to the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Gaozu ordered all Xiang Ji's former subordinates to call him by his first name when referring to Xiang Ji. Zheng Jun alone refused to accept the edict.
Emperor Gaozu decreed that those who were willing to address Xiang Ji by his first name would be worshiped as senior officials, and Lord Zheng was driven away.
Zheng Jun died during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen.
Zheng Zhuang took pleasure in being a chivalrous man and rescuing Zhang Yu from danger, and his reputation spread throughout Liang and Chu.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he served as Prince Sheren.
During every five-day holiday, he often bought horses in the suburbs of Chang'an, rode on horseback to visit old friends, invited and thanked guests and friends, and stayed up all night long, always worrying about omissions.
Zheng Zhuang loves Taoism and admires elderly and virtuous people. His affection is as intense as if he is afraid that he will never see them again.
He is young and has a humble official position, but his close friends are all from his grandfather's generation and are famous people in the world.
After Emperor Wu came to the throne, Zhengzhuang was promoted step by step from the lieutenant of Lu State, the prefect of Jinan Qun, and the prime minister of Jiangdu to the right internal history of Jiuqing.
Due to his improper opinions on the dispute between Wu'an Hou Tianfan and Wei Qihou Dou Ying, he was demoted to Zhan Shi and was later transferred to Da Nong Ling.
When Zheng Zhuang was doing the internal history of You, he warned his subordinate officials: If there are visitors, no matter they are noble or lowly, they are not allowed to wait at the door.
He respects the host's hospitality and subordinates himself to the guests with his noble status.
Zheng Zhuang was an upright person and did not purchase any private property. He only relied on his official salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends. The gifts he gave to others were only a few meals in bamboo utensils.
Whenever he goes to court and has the opportunity to give advice to the emperor, he will be praised by the most respected people in the world.
He recommended scholars and his subordinates, prime ministers and officials, and talked about them with great interest. He often praised them as more capable than himself.
He never addressed the officials by their first names, and when talking to his subordinates, he was so humble as if he was afraid of hurting them.
When I heard that others had good ideas, I recommended them to the emperor for fear of delaying the matter.
Therefore, scholars and well-known elders in the vast area east of Miao Mountain all praised his virtues.
Zheng Zhuang was sent to inspect the breach of the Yellow River, and he asked for five days to prepare his luggage.
The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Why did he ask for time to prepare his luggage?
Although Zheng Zhuang was popular with outsiders, he often agreed to obey his master's wishes in court and did not dare to express his views on right and wrong too clearly.
In his later years, the Han Dynasty conquered the Xiongnu and recruited ethnic minorities in various places. The world spent a lot of money and the country's financial and material resources were even more scarce.
The people recommended by Zheng Zhuang and their guests were responsible for transportation for the great peasant order, and they owed a lot of money.
Sima An was appointed as the prefect of Huaiyang County and reported the matter. Zheng Zhuang was held responsible for this. After atonement, he was demoted to a civilian.
Soon, he entered the Prime Minister's Mansion and held the temporary post of chief historian.
The emperor thought that he was old and asked him to be the governor of Runan County.
A few years later, he died in office.
Zheng Zhuang and Ji An were originally ranked among the nine ministers. They were honest in government and had pure conduct at home.
Both of them were dismissed from office during the process, their families were poor, and their guests gradually declined.
When he became a county magistrate, there was no property left in his family after his death.
Because of him, as many as six or seven of Zheng Zhuang's brothers and descendants have reached the rank of two thousand shi.
Tai Shigong said: Because Ji An and Zheng were so virtuous at that time, when they were powerful, the number of guests would be ten times greater, but when they were powerless, the situation was completely the opposite. If they were like this, let alone ordinary people!
Zhai Gong of Xiajun County once said that when he first served as a court official, his house was full of guests; but when he lost his official position, the outside became so deserted that people could gather to catch birds.
After he was reinstated, the guests wanted to see him again, so Zhai Gong wrote on the gate: "One death and one life are all friendships."
One is poor and the other is rich, which is a state of acquaintance.
One is noble and the other is humble, friendship is about seeing each other.
Ji An and Zhengzhuang also had this misfortune, how sad!

translation:
Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty. His mother was the concubine of Zhang Ao, the former king of Zhao.
In the eighth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Emperor Gao passed by Zhao from Dongyuan County, and King Zhao dedicated King Li's mother to him.
She was favored by the emperor and became pregnant.
From then on, King Zhao Zhang Ao did not dare to let her live in the palace, so he built another palace for her to live in.
The following year, the imperial court discovered that Zhao Xiangguan and others were plotting to kill Emperor Gaozu in Bairen County. King Zhao was also arrested and charged. His mother, brothers and concubines were all arrested and imprisoned in the Hanoi County government.
King Li's mother said to the jailer in prison: I am favored by the emperor and am pregnant.
The jailer reported truthfully that the emperor was angry because of King Zhao's incident and ignored the complaint of King Li's mother.
Zhao Jian, the younger brother of King Li's mother, asked Piyang Hou Shenshi to inform Empress Lu. Queen Lu was jealous and refused to plead with the emperor, so Piyang Hou stopped trying to persuade him.
King Li's mother was resentful after giving birth to Queen Li, so she committed suicide.
The jailer carried King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it and ordered Queen Lu to raise him and bury King Li's mother in Zhending County.
Zhending is the hometown of King Li's mother, and her ancestors lived there.
In July of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled, so the emperor appointed his son Liu Chang as King of Huainan, putting him in charge of the four counties and fiefdoms that were formerly under Yingbu's territory.
The emperor personally led an army to go out and annihilated Yingbu, so King Li took the throne of Huainan.
King Li lost his mother when he was young and grew up dependent on Empress Lu. Therefore, he was able to avoid political disasters during the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu. However, he always resented Marquis Piyang in his heart and did not dare to take action.
When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, King Huainan considered himself the closest to the emperor. He was arrogant and arrogant, and repeatedly violated laws and disciplines.
The emperor thought of his brother-sister relationship and often tolerated and pardoned his faults.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Huainan professed his own country and entered the dynasty. His attitude was very arrogant.
He followed the emperor to the imperial garden for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother".
King Li was talented and brave, and could lift a heavy cauldron with all his strength, so he went to the mansion of Piyang Hou to seek an audience.
When Marquis Piyang came out to see him, he took out an iron mallet from his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his attendant Wei Jing to cut off Marquis Piyang's head.
Afterwards, King Li galloped to the palace and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have been convicted of Zhao's rebellion. At that time, if Marquis Piyang had tried his best to save her, he would have been able to get help from Empress Lu, but he did not try hard. This was the first crime." King Zhao Ruyi and his son were not guilty. Empress Lu deliberately killed them, but Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade them. This was the second crime. Empress Lu made a relative of the Lu family king, intending to threaten the Liu family, and Marquis Piyang did not stand up to fight. This is the third crime.
I killed the treacherous minister Piyanghou for the people of the world, and avenged my mother. I came to the court to kneel down and plead guilty.
The emperor's desire to pity King Li, and out of brotherly love, did not punish him and pardoned him.
During this period, the Empress Dowager Bo, the Crown Prince, and all the ministers were all afraid of King Li. Therefore, King Li became more arrogant and unruly after returning to the country. He did not act in accordance with the court decrees. He issued orders to warn Qingdao when entering and leaving the palace. He also called the orders he issued "zhi" and made laws by himself, imitating the emperor.
In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Li asked seventy men without official titles to discuss with Chai Qi, the son of Chai Wu, Marquis of Jipu, and planned to use forty large trucks to rebel in Gukou County, and sent envoys to Minyue and Xiongnu to contact various places.
The imperial court found out about this, punished the rebels, and sent envoys to summon King Huainan to the capital. King Huainan came to Chang'an.
Prime Minister Zhang Bao, Dian Kechen Feng Jing, Imperial Censor Shizong Zhengchenyi, Tingwei Chenhe, and the thief Lieutenant Chenfu risked death. They reported: Huainan King Liu Chang abandoned the grammar of the late emperor, disobeyed the emperor's edict, and engaged in non-compliance with the law in daily life. He made his own chariot with a yellow satin umbrella that the emperor rode.
He appointed officials without authorization, appointed his doctor Zhongchun as the prime minister of the country, collected people from various counties and vassal states, as well as fugitives who had committed crimes, hid them in places to live, settled their families, and granted them money, materials, titles, salaries, and houses. The King of Huainan said: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, who had no place to stand, gathered a thousand people and started a uprising in Daze Township. They shouted for rebellion, and the whole country responded. When they went west to play in the water, there were 1.2 million people with them.
Although our country is small today, there are more than 100,000 strong men who are qualified to fight. They are by no means a mob forced to guard the border, and they do not hold wooden crossbows and halberd handles. Why do you say there is disaster but no luck?
Wu Bei said: In the past, the Qin Dynasty was tyrannical and cruel, and harmed the people of the world.
The imperial court requisitioned tens of thousands of private vehicles, built the Epang Palace, collected most of the people's income as taxes, and sent the poor people from the family to remote frontiers. As a result, the father could not protect his son's safety, and the elder brother could not let his younger brother live a comfortable life. The government's decrees were harsh and the punishments were harsh, and the people of the world endured all kinds of torture and were almost exhausted. The people craned their necks in hope, listened attentively, raised their heads to the sky and cried out in sorrow, beating their chests and resenting the emperor. Therefore, Chen Sheng shouted for rebellion, and everyone in the world responded immediately.
Now the emperor is ruling the world from his dynasty, unifying all parts of the country, loving the people of the world, and extending virtues and benefits.
Even if he does not speak, his voice spreads as fast as thunder; even if the edict is not promulgated, the rapid promotion of education seems to have magical power; if he has a thought in his heart, it will move thousands of miles, and the people will respond to the Lord, just like the shadow follows the shape and the echo responds to the voice.
Moreover, the talents of General Wei Qing are not comparable to those of Qin generals Zhang Han and Yang Xiong.
Therefore, I think it is inappropriate for your Majesty to describe yourself as Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rebelling against Qin.
The King of Huainan said: If it is really like what you said, can't it be a lucky success?
Wu Bei said: I have a stupid plan.
King Huainan said: What should we do?
Wu Bei replied: Today, the princes have no doubts about the imperial court, and the people have no resentment towards the imperial court.
However, Shuofang County has vast fields and rich water and grass, and the people who have migrated are not enough to fully develop the area.
The minister's stupid plan was to forge memorials written by the prime minister and censor to the emperor, requesting the relocation of powerful men, righteous men, and prisoners sentenced to more than 100 edicts from various counties to fill the borders.
Then he forged the case-handling documents issued by the emperor personally issued by the officials of Du Sikong, Shanglinyuan and the capital of Zongzheng Mansion to arrest the princes and favored ministers of the princes.
If this happens, the people will be resentful and the princes will be afraid. Then let the voluptuous lobbyists persuade them to rebel. Maybe they can get a tenth chance of success!
The King of Huainan said: This plan is feasible.
Although your worries are reasonable, I don't think it is that difficult to achieve this.
So the King of Huainan ordered his slaves to enter the palace and forged the emperor's seal, the prime minister, the imperial censor, the general, the military historian, Zhong Erqian Shi, the official seals of the various officials in the capital and county magistrates, the official seals of the prefects and captains of neighboring counties, and the official hats worn by the court envoys and judges, all planning to act according to Wu Qui's plan.
The King of Huainan also sent people to pretend to be convicted and escape from the Huainan Kingdom and go west to Chang'an to serve the general and the prime minister. He intended to have them assassinate the general Wei Qing immediately if an army broke out, and then persuade the prime minister to surrender. It would be as easy as removing a covering cloth.
The King of Huainan wanted to mobilize the army in the country, but he was worried that his prime minister and ministers would not obey his orders.
He and Wu Bei conspired to kill the Prime Minister and the Minister of Two Thousand Stones first. To this end, they pretended that there was a fire in the palace. The Prime Minister and the Minister of Two Thousand Stones would come to put out the fire, and they would be killed as soon as they arrived.
Before the plan was decided, they planned to send people wearing the clothes of soldiers who captured thieves, holding feathers, and galloping from the south, shouting "South Vietnamese soldiers have entered the border", so as to take the opportunity to send troops to march.
So they sent people to Lujiang County and Kuaiji County to implement the strategy of pretending to hunt down the thieves, but did not send troops immediately.
The king of Huainan asked Wu Bei: I am leading my troops to advance westward, and the princes must have people to respond. What if no one responds?
Wu was replied: You can seize the Hengshan Kingdom to the south and attack Lujiang County, seize Xunyang's warships, guard the city of Xiaji, strangle the mouth of Jiujiang River, block the passage of the Yuzhang River from the north to the Yangtze River at the mouth of Pengli Lake, and attack with strong bows and crossbows. Fortify the Yangtze River to prevent the Nanjun army from moving down the river; then attack the Jiangdu Kingdom and Kuaiji County in the east, and make friends with the powerful Yue Kingdom in the south. In this way, they can bend and stretch freely between the Yangtze and Huaihe Rivers and delay for some time.
King Huainan said: Very good, there is no better strategy.
If the situation is critical, go to Yue.
So Tingwei reported to the emperor that the confession of Huainan Prince Liu Jian implicated Huainan Prince Liu Qian.
The emperor sent Wei Lin to seize the opportunity to visit the lieutenant of Huainan Kingdom and arrest the prince.
When Ting Wei came to the Huainan Kingdom, the King of Huainan learned about it and planned with the prince to summon the Prime Minister and the Minister of Two Thousand Stones to come and kill them before sending troops.
The minister of state was summoned to the palace, and the minister of state came; the internal history was able to escape because he was out.
The lieutenant said: I am welcoming the envoys sent by the emperor and cannot come to see the king.
The King of Huainan thought that it would be of no use to kill only the Prime Minister, but the internal history and the lieutenant refused to come, so he gave up and let the Prime Minister go.
He hesitated again and again, unable to decide on a plan of action.
The prince thought that what he had committed was a conspiracy to assassinate a lieutenant of the imperial court, and that the people involved in the conspiracy were dead, so he thought that all the survivors would be cut off, so he said to his father: "All the ministers who can be relied on have been arrested before, but now there is no one who can be relied upon to carry out the task."
If you send troops when the time is not ripe, I am afraid you will not succeed. I am willing to go to the court to be arrested.
King Huainan also secretly wanted to give up, so he agreed to the prince's request.
So the prince cut his neck and committed suicide, but he did not die.
Wu Ban went to the law enforcement officials alone and reported his participation in the Huainan King's rebellion, and gave all the details of the rebellion.
The legal officials therefore arrested the prince and the queen, surrounded the palace, searched and arrested all the guests of King Huainan who participated in the rebellion, and also found the utensils of the rebellion, and then reported the matter to the emperor.
The emperor handed the case to the ministers for trial. The case implicated several thousand princes, two thousand stones, and local tycoons who had conspired with the Huainan King. They were all sentenced to death according to the severity of the crime.
Liu Ci, the king of Hengshan, was the younger brother of the king of Huainan. He was found guilty of the same crime and should be arrested. The official responsible for handling the case requested the arrest of the king of Hengshan.
The Emperor said: Each prince and king regards his own feudal state as the foundation of his life and should not involve each other.
You, together with the princes and princes, go to meet with the prime minister to discuss.
After discussion, forty-three people including King Pengzu of Zhao and Cao Xiang, the princes of Lieutenant, all said: King Liu An of Huainan is extremely treasonous and immoral. His crime of rebellion is clear and he should be punished without mercy.
Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, expressed his opinion: Liu An, the king of Huainan, ignored the king's law and did evil things. He was deceitful, disrupted the world, confused the people, betrayed his ancestors, and spread heresy.
"Spring and Autumn" once said that ministers should not lead the people to cause chaos, and they should be killed if they lead the people to cause chaos.
Liu An's crime was more serious than the rebellion, and his rebellion was a foregone conclusion.
I have seen clear evidence of his forged documents, talismans, seals, maps and other treasonous and immoral facts. His crime is extremely treasonous and immoral, and he should be executed according to law.
As for the officials in the Huainan Kingdom with an official rank of more than 200 shi and less than 200 shi, as well as the favored ministers of the clan who have not violated the law, if they cannot fulfill their duties to correct the Huainan King and prevent the rebellion of the King of Huainan, they should be removed from their posts, have their titles reduced, and be demoted to soldiers, and they will not be allowed to serve as officials again in the future.
Those other criminals who are not officials can use two pounds and eighty taels of gold to pay for the death penalty.
The imperial court should publicly expose Liu An's crimes so that everyone in the world will clearly understand the way of being a minister and will not dare to have evil ambitions to betray the emperor.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Tingwei Zhang Tang and others reported everyone's opinions, and the emperor sent Zongzheng holding a talisman to judge the Huainan King.
Before Zongzheng arrived in Huainan, King Liu An of Huainan had committed suicide in advance.
Queen Tu, Prince Liu Qian and all those who collaborated in the rebellion were all killed.
When the emperor of Huainan, Liu An, was dissuaded from rebelling because of Wu, his words were elegant and upright. He said a lot of good things about the government and wanted not to kill him.
Ting Wei Zhang Tang said: Wu Ban was the first to plot a rebellion for the King of Huainan, and his crime cannot be forgiven.
So Wu Bei was killed.
Huainan Kingdom was abolished as Jiujiang County.
The king of Hengshan was named Liu Ci, and Queen Chengshu gave birth to three children. The eldest son Liu Shuang was established as the prince, the second son Liu Xiao, and the third daughter Liu Wucai.
Concubine Xu Lai also gave birth to four children, and concubine Jue Ji gave birth to two children.
The two brothers, the King of Hengshan and the King of Huainan, blamed each other and complained about etiquette. Their relationship was estranged and they were not harmonious.
When the King of Hengshan heard that the King of Huainan was making utensils for rebellion, he also made friends with guests to guard against him, fearing that he would annex him.
In the sixth year of Yuanguang, King Hengshan came to Beijing to pay homage. His visitor, Wei Qing, knew alchemy and wanted to write a letter asking him to serve the emperor. The King of Hengshan was very angry and deliberately accused Wei Qing of committing a capital crime and tortured him to force him to admit it.
The domestic history of Hengshan thought it was wrong and refused to hear the case.
The King of Hengshan ordered people to write a letter to accuse the internal history. The internal history was forced to handle the case, but he bluntly said that the King of Hengshan was wrong.
The King of Hengshan repeatedly usurped other people's fields and destroyed other people's tombs to create fields.
The head of the relevant department requested that King Hengshan be arrested and held accountable for his crimes, but the emperor did not agree. He only took back his original power to appoint officials with an official rank of more than 200 shi in his country and replaced them with appointments by the emperor.
The King of Hengshan was filled with resentment and conspired with Xi Ci and Zhang Guangchang. They visited people who were familiar with the art of war and could observe the stars to predict good and bad luck. They encouraged the King of Hengshan day and night to plot a rebellion.
Queen Chengshu died, and the King of Hengshan made Xu Lai his queen.
Jue Ji also received favor at the same time.
The two were jealous of each other, and Jue Ji spoke ill of Queen Xu Lai to the prince. She said: Xu Lai ordered his maid to kill the prince's mother with false accusations and sorcery.
From then on, the prince resented Xu Lai.
Xu Lai's brother came to Hengshan Kingdom. The prince drank with him and stabbed the queen's brother with a knife during the dinner.
The queen was resentful and angry, and repeatedly slandered the prince to King Hengshan.
The prince's sister Liu Wucai was divorced and returned to her natal family after her marriage. She committed adultery with a slave and a guest.
The prince blamed Liu Wocai many times, and Wucai was very angry and stopped interacting with the prince.
When the queen learned of this, she showed great solicitude.
Wucai and his second brother Liu Xiao lost their mother when they were young, so they could not help but rely on Queen Xu Lai. She cleverly used tricks to protect them and let them slander the prince together. Therefore, the King of Hengshan beat the prince severely many times.
In the fourth year of Yuan Shuo, someone killed or injured the queen's stepmother. King Hengshan suspected that the prince had instigated the crime, so he beat the prince severely with a bamboo board.
Later, King Hengshan became ill, and the prince often claimed that he was ill and refused to serve.
Liu Xiao, the queen, and Liu Wucai all said bad things about him: The prince was actually not sick, but he claimed to be sick, with a happy face.
The King of Hengshan was furious and wanted to abolish his title of crown prince and replace him with his younger brother Liu Xiao.
The queen knew that King Hengshan had decided to depose the crown prince, so she wanted to depose Liu Xiao as well.
The queen had a maid who was good at dancing, and King Hengshan dotes on her. The queen planned to have the maid have an affair with Liu Xiao to taint him, so that she could depose the prince brothers and make her son Liu Guang the prince.
The prince Liu Shuang knew the queen's plot and thought that the queen had repeatedly slandered him and refused to give up, so he planned to have an affair with her to silence her.
One time when the queen was drinking, the prince came up to toast her birthday. Taking advantage of the situation, he sat on the queen's lap and asked to sleep with her.
The queen was very angry and told the king of Hengshan.
So the King of Hengshan summoned the prince and planned to tie him up and beat him severely.
The prince knew that his father often wanted to depose him and establish his younger brother Liu Xiao, so he said to him: Liu Xiao has committed adultery with his father's favored maid, and Wucai has committed adultery with his slaves. Father, please try your best to have more food. I request to write a letter to the court.
After that, he turned his back to King Hengshan and left.
The King of Hengshan sent people to stop him, but it failed, so he drove himself to hunt down the prince.
The prince talked nonsense, and the King of Hengshan imprisoned him in the palace with shackles.
Liu Xiao became increasingly close and favored by the King of Hengshan.
The King of Hengshan was amazed at Liu Xiao's talents, so he gave him the royal seal, called him a general, let him live in a mansion outside the palace, and gave him a lot of money to attract guests.
The guests who came to seek refuge secretly knew that both the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan had plans to betray the imperial court, so they welcomed and encouraged the King of Hengshan day and night.
So the King of Hengshan ordered Liu Xiao's guests Jiangdu people to rescue He and Chen happy to make chariots and arrows, and to engrave the emperor's seal and the official seals of the generals and military officials.
The King of Hengshan visited day and night for heroes like Zhou Qiu. He repeatedly praised and gave examples of Wu Chu's strategies during the rebellion, and used them to standardize his own rebellion plans.
The King of Hengshan did not dare to imitate the King of Huainan and hope to usurp the throne of emperor. He was afraid that the King of Huainan would rise up and annex his country. He thought that after the King of Huainan moved westward, he could take advantage of the situation and send troops to pacify and occupy the territory between the Yangtze River and the Huai River. He hoped that he would be able to do so.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuan Shuo, King Hengshan was about to go to Beijing to see the emperor. When passing through the Huainan Kingdom, the King of Huainan actually said some words of brotherhood, which eliminated the previous resentment and agreed to jointly create tools for rebellion.
The King of Hengshan wrote a letter saying that he was ill, and the emperor gave him a letter allowing him not to enter the court.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, King Hengshan sent people to write to the emperor requesting that the crown prince Liu Shuang be deposed and Liu Xiao be established as the crown prince.
After Liu Shuang heard the news, he sent Bai Ying, who was close to him, to Chang'an to write a letter accusing Liu Xiao of secretly making chariot arrows and committing adultery with the Huainan King's maid, intending to thwart Liu Xiao.
When Bai Ying came to Chang'an, before he could submit a letter, the officials arrested him and imprisoned him because he was involved in the rebellion of the King of Huainan.
When the King of Hengshan heard that Liu Shuang sent Bai Ying to write a letter, he was afraid that he would reveal the secrets of the country, so he wrote a letter accusing the prince Liu Shuang of committing treason and committing treason and should be punished with death. The court handed the matter over to Pei County for trial.
In the winter of the first year of Yuanshou, the minister responsible for handling the case went to Pei County to search for the criminals who had conspired with the King of Huainan. He was not arrested, but Chen happy was captured at the home of Liu Xiao, the son of the King of Hengshan.
Officials accused Liu Xiao of taking the lead in hiding Chen happy.
Liu Xiao thought that Chen Xiping had repeatedly plotted rebellion with the King of Hengshan, and was very afraid that he would confess the matter. He heard that the law stipulated that those who surrendered in advance would be exempted from guilt, and he suspected that the prince had instructed Bai Ying to report the rebellion, so he surrendered first and accused Jiu He, Chen happy and others of participating in the rebellion.
The interrogation by Tingwei confirmed that it was true, and the minister requested the arrest and interrogation of King Hengshan. The emperor said: Do not arrest.
He sent Lieutenant Sima An and General Li Xi to Hengshan Kingdom to interrogate King Hengshan on the spot, and King Hengshan answered truthfully one by one.
The officials surrounded the palace and guarded it closely.
The lieutenant and Daxing returned to the court and reported the situation. The minister requested that Zongzheng, Daxing and Peijun be sent to jointly try the King of Hengshan.
When the King of Hengshan heard the news, he cut his neck and committed suicide.
Liu Xiao was acquitted because he voluntarily surrendered and rebelled; but he was still sentenced to death for committing adultery with the maid of the Prince of Hengshan.
Queen Xu Lai was also guilty of murdering the former Queen Chengshu by falsely accusing her of poison, and Prince Liu Shuang was accused of unfilial piety by the King of Hengshan, so they were all executed and abandoned in the market.
All the criminals who participated in the rebellion of King Hengshan were killed.
Hengshan State was abolished and became Hengshan County.
Tai Shigong said: "The Book of Songs" says: "Fight the Rong and Di, punish the Chu people. This is true!"
Although the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan were close relatives, owned thousands of miles of territory, and were granted the title of vassal, they did not devote themselves to abide by the duties of vassals to assist the emperor. Instead, they blindly harbored evil plans and plotted rebellion. As a result, father and son were subjugated for the second time in succession. No one was able to enjoy the full life of his life, and was ridiculed by the world.
This is not only their fault, but also the result of the weak local customs and the bad influence of subordinate ministers.
The people of Chu are agile, brave, fierce, and fond of causing chaos. This has been recorded in books since ancient times.
summary:
Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of Han. His mother, a concubine of the former King of Zhao, was favored by Emperor Gaozu and became pregnant. After the King of Zhao was implicated in a plot against the emperor, she was imprisoned and, despite being pregnant, her pleas for help were ignored due to the emperor's anger and Empress Lü's jealousy. After giving birth to Liu Chang, she committed suicide. The emperor regretted this and had Empress Lü raise the child. Liu Chang was later made King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion.

Growing up under Empress Lü's protection, Liu Chang escaped political disasters but harbored resentment against Marquis Piyang for not helping his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, Liu Chang became arrogant, calling the emperor "big brother" and violating laws. He eventually killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes against him. The emperor pardoned him out of brotherly love, but Liu Chang grew more unruly, imitating imperial decrees and plotting rebellion.

In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Chang conspired with seventy men to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and he was summoned to Chang'an. Officials reported his numerous crimes, including forging imperial chariots, appointing unauthorized officials, harboring fugitives, and killing innocents. The emperor, unable to bear punishing him, deposed him and exiled him to Shu County. Liu Chang went on a hunger strike and died en route. The emperor later posthumously honored him as King Li and enfeoffed his sons.

Liu Chang's son, Liu An, became King of Huainan. He was cultured and sought to win over the people, but he resented his father's death and plotted rebellion. He befriended guests, accumulated weapons, and bribed officials. His daughter, Liu Ling, spied in Chang'an. The king's advisor, Wu Bei, warned against rebellion, citing the failures of Wu and Chu and the stability of the Han dynasty. Despite this, Liu An continued preparations, forging seals and planning to assassinate officials.

The plot was exposed when Liu An's grandson, Liu Jian, informed on the prince. The court investigated, and Liu An, fearing exposure, hesitated to act. His advisor Wu Bei again urged caution, but Liu An persisted. Eventually, the court arrested the conspirators, and Liu An committed suicide before his arrest. His queen and prince were executed, and Huainan was reduced to a commandery.

Liu An's brother, Liu Ci, King of Hengshan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his brother and prepared for war, forging documents and building weapons. His internal conflicts, including disputes over succession and adultery, led to his downfall. After his son Liu Xiao surrendered and revealed the plot, Liu Ci committed suicide. His kingdom was also abolished.

Sima Qian comments that despite their noble status, the kings of Huainan and Hengshan failed in their duties and plotted rebellion, leading to their ruin. Their faults were compounded by the influence of unruly subordinates and local customs.

Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was from Huaiyin.
When he was a commoner, he was poor, had no good character, could not be elected to be an official, and could not make a living by doing business. He often lived in other people's homes and had nothing to do, so most people hated him.
I went to the countryside many times to have a casual meal at the pavilion in Nanchang. For several months, the pavilion chief's wife was worried about Han Xin, so she made breakfast in advance and took it to the bed in the inner room to eat.
When it was time to eat, Han Xin went, but no food was prepared for him.
Han Xin also understood their intentions. In a rage, he actually left and never came back.
Han Xin was fishing under the city, and there were several old ladies rinsing the silk cotton. One of them saw that Han Xin was hungry, so she gave Han Xin food to eat. This continues for dozens of days until rinsing is complete.
Han Xin was very happy and said to the aunt: I will repay you heavily in the future.
The aunt said angrily: "A man can't support himself. I give you food out of pity for you, the young master. Do I hope you will repay me?"
A young man among the Huaiyin butchers insulted Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to carry a sword, you are actually a coward.
He insulted him in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, crawl under my crotch.
So Han Xin looked at him carefully, lowered himself to the ground, and crawled under his crotch.
People all over the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was timid.
When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huaihe River, Han Xin followed him with a sword, but he had no reputation among Xiang Liang's men.
Xiang Liang was defeated, and Han Xin was subordinated to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor.
He repeatedly offered suggestions to Xiang Yu in order to be reused, but Xiang Yu did not adopt them.
Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Shu, and Han Xin left the Chu army and submitted to the king of Han. Because he had no reputation, he only served as a minor official receiving guests.
Later, he was sentenced to beheading for breaking the law, and all thirteen people who were accomplices in the crime were killed. When it was Han Xin's turn, he looked up and happened to see Teng Gong and said: Doesn't the King of Han want to achieve the feat of unifying the world?
Why do you want to kill the strong man?
Teng Gong felt that his words were extraordinary and saw that he was handsome, so he let him go.
Talked with Han Xin, admired him very much, and reported the matter to the King of Han, who appointed Han Xin as the Commander-in-Chief of Su Su. But the king of Han did not see that he had any special talents.
Han Xin talked to Xiao He many times, and Xiao He thought he was a genius.
When they arrived at Nanzheng, dozens of generals from all walks of life fled on the way.
Han Xin speculated that Xiao He and others had recommended him to the King of Han many times, but the King of Han did not use him and ran away.
Xiao He heard that Han Xin had escaped and had no time to report to the King of Han, so he chased him personally.
Someone reported to the King of Han that: Prime Minister Xiao He has escaped.
The king of Han was furious because losing Xiao He was like losing his right and left hands.
A day or two later, Xiao He came to see the King of Han. The King of Han was both angry and happy. He scolded Xiao He and said: Why did you run away?
Xiao He said: I don't dare to run away, I will chase the escaping person.
The king of Han said: Who are you chasing?
He replied: It’s Han Xin.
The King of Han cursed again: Dozens of generals from all walks of life have fled, but you did not chase anyone; but you chased Han Xin, which is a lie.
Xiao He said: Those generals are easy to get.
As for outstanding figures like Han Xin, there is no second person in the world.
If the king wants to be the king of Hanzhong for a long time, he will naturally not need Han Xin. If he wants to fight for the world, there will be no one except Han Xin who can discuss important matters with you.
But it depends on what the king decides.
The King of Han said: I also want to develop eastward, how can I stay here for a long time with my heart depressed?
Xiao He said: The king is determined to develop eastward. If Han Xin can be reused, Han Xin will stay. If he cannot be reused, Han Xin will eventually run away.
The King of Han said: For your sake, let him be a general.
Xiao He said: Even if he becomes a general, Han Xin will definitely not stay.
The king of Han said: Appoint him as a general.
Xiao He said: Great.
So the King of Han summoned Han Xin to appoint him.
Xiao He said: The king has always been arrogant and disrespectful to others. Now appointing a general is like calling a child. This is the reason why Han Xin is leaving.
The king is determined to appoint him. He must choose a good and auspicious day, fast in person, set up an altar and square, and complete the etiquette.
The king of Han agreed to Xiao He's request.
All the generals were very happy when they heard that they were going to become generals. Everyone thought they were going to be generals.
When the general was appointed, it was Han Xin who was appointed, and the whole army was surprised.
After the ceremony of appointing Han Xin, the King of Han took his seat.
The king of Han said: The prime minister has praised the general many times. What strategies does the general use to teach me?
Han Xinqian gave in and took advantage of the situation to ask the King of Han: "Now that we are fighting for the world in the east, isn't the enemy King Xiang?" The king of Han said: Yes.
Han Xin said: The king himself estimates that compared with King Xiang in terms of bravery, strength, kindness, and military strength, who is better?
The king of Han was silent for a long time and said: "I am not as good as King Xiang."
Han Xin bowed twice and said in agreement: "I also think your Majesty is not as good as him."
However, I have served him before. Please let me tell you about King Xiang's character.
When King Xiang roared in anger, thousands of people were so frightened that they did not dare to move, but he could not let go and use talented generals. This was just the bravery of an ordinary man.
King Xiang was respectful and kind to others, and his words were gentle. When someone was sick, he would feel distressed and shed tears, and would share his food and drink with him. When someone had made military exploits and was about to be ennobled, he would put the engraved seal in his hand and play with it until it lost its edge and was reluctant to give it to him. This is what is called the kindness of a woman.
Even though King Xiang dominated the world and made the princes surrender, he gave up the favorable terrain in Guanzhong and built his capital in Pengcheng.
He also violated the agreement of the Righteous Emperor and made his close followers kings. The princes were indignant.
When the princes saw that King Xiang had moved Emperor Yi to a remote place in the south of the Yangtze River, they all went back and expelled their own kings, occupied good places and made themselves kings.
Every place King Xiang's army passed through was devastated and destroyed. Most of the people in the world were resentful. The common people were unwilling to surrender, but they were forced to obey by force.
Although he was the hegemon in name, he actually lost the support of the people in the world.
Therefore, his advantages can easily be turned into disadvantages.

When Han Xin arrived at Xiapi, he summoned the floating mother who had given him food and gave her a thousand catties of gold.

He summoned the young man who had insulted him by letting him crawl under his crotch, appointed him as a lieutenant, and told the generals and ministers: This is a strong man.
When he insulted me, couldn't I have killed him?
It was just that there was no point in killing him, so I endured the momentary insult and achieved what I have achieved today.
King Xiang's fleeing general Zhong Limei lived in Yilu and had always been friendly with Han Xin.
After King Xiang died, he escaped and joined Han Xin.
The King of Han resented Zhong Limei. Hearing that he was in Chu, he ordered Chu to arrest Zhong Limei.
When Han Xin first arrived in Chu State, he patrolled the counties and cities he belonged to, bringing armed guards with him when he came in and out.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, someone wrote a letter accusing Han Xin of treason.
Emperor Gao adopted Chen Ping's plan and asked the emperor to go out on an inspection tour to meet with the princes. There was Yunmengze in the south. He sent envoys to inform the princes to gather in Chen County and said: "I want to inspect Yunmengze."
In fact, he wanted to attack Han Xin, but Han Xin didn't know it.
When Emperor Gaozu was about to arrive in Chu, Han Xin wanted to send troops to rebel, but he thought he was not guilty. He wanted to see Emperor Gaozu, but he was afraid of being captured.
Someone said to Han Xin: If you kill Zhong Limei and go to see the emperor, the emperor will be happy and there will be no trouble.
Han Xin went to see Zhong Limei for discussion.
Zhong Limei said: The reason why the King of Han did not attack Chu was because I am here with you and you want to arrest me to please the King of Han. If I die today, you will die soon after.
So he scolded Han Xin and said: You are not a loyal person!
Finally he cut his neck and died.
Han Xin took his head and went to Chen County to pay homage to Emperor Gao.
The emperor ordered the warriors to tie up Han Xin and put him in the accompanying car.
Han Xin said: It is true as people say: when the cunning rabbit dies, the excellent hunting dogs are cooked and killed; when the high-flying birds are gone, the fine bows and arrows are collected; when the enemy's country is destroyed, the adviser dies.
Now that the world is at peace, I should have been cooked and killed!
The emperor said: Someone has accused you of treason.
So Han Xin was given torture instruments.
When he arrived in Luoyang, he pardoned Han Xin's sins and changed his title to Marquis of Huaiyin.
Han Xin knew that the king of Han was afraid of his own abilities and often excused himself from attending court meetings and attending court meetings due to illness.
From then on, Han Xin was resentful day and night, unhappy at home, and felt ashamed of being in the same position as Jianghou and Guan Ying.
Han Xin once visited General Fan Kuai. Fan Kuai knelt down to greet him and called himself a minister. Said: How come the king is willing to come?
Han Xin went out and said with a smile: I have been with people like Fan Kuai in my life.
The emperor often discussed the quality of the generals with Han Xin in his spare time, and believed that each had its own strengths and weaknesses.
The emperor asked Han Xin: How many troops can I command with my talents?
Han Xin said: Your Majesty can only command a hundred thousand people.
The emperor said: How are you?
Answer: I am the more the merrier.
The emperor smiled and said: The more you have, the better. Why are you still captured by me?
Han Xin said: Your Majesty cannot lead troops, but he is good at controlling generals. This is why I was captured by Your Majesty.
Besides, Your Majesty was given by God and cannot be achieved by human power.
Chen Xi was appointed as the governor of Julu County and bid farewell to the Marquis of Huaiyin.
Marquis Huaiyin held his hand and walked in the courtyard avoiding the attendants. He looked up at the sky and sighed: "Can you listen to my intimate words?"
I have something on my mind that I want to talk to you about. Chen Xi said: Everything is at the command of the general!
The Marquis of Huaiyin said: The area under your jurisdiction is where the best soldiers from all over the world gather; and you are His Majesty's trusted and favored minister.
If someone reports that you are rebelling, Your Majesty will not believe it; if someone reports you again, Your Majesty will become suspicious; if someone reports you three times, Your Majesty will be furious and personally lead his troops to encircle and suppress you.
If I work as an internal agent in the capital for you, the world can get it.
Chen Xi has always known Han Xin's talents and strategies. I am convinced and say: I will definitely follow your advice!
In the tenth year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled.
The emperor personally led his troops there, but Han Tuo was ill and had no followers.
Secretly sent someone to Chen Xi and said: Just raise troops, I am here to assist you.
Han Xin discussed with his retainers and falsely issued an edict at night to pardon the criminals and slaves serving in various government offices, intending to mobilize them to attack Empress Lu and the prince.
The deployment is completed and we are waiting for news from Chen Xi.
One of his retainers offended Han Xin, who imprisoned him and planned to kill him.
His younger brother wrote a letter of rebellion and reported to Empress Lu that Han Xin was preparing to rebel.
Empress Lu planned to summon Han Xin, but was afraid that he would not submit, so she conspired with Xiao Xiangguo to pretend that Chen Xi was coming from the emperor, saying that Chen Xi had been captured and executed, and all the princes and ministers came to congratulate him.
Xiao Xiangguo deceived Han Xin and said: Even if he is ill, he must work hard to go to the palace to congratulate him.
When Han Xin entered the palace, Empress Lu ordered the warriors to tie Han Xin up and kill him in the bell chamber of Changle Palace.
When Han Xin was about to be executed, he said: I regret that I did not adopt Kuai Tong's plan and was deceived by women and boys. Isn't it God's will?
So he killed the three Han and Xin tribes.
Emperor Gaozu returned to the capital from the army that suppressed Chen Xi's rebellion. When he saw that Han Xin was dead, he was happy and pitied him, and asked: What did Han Xin say before he died?
Queen Lu said: Han Xin said he regretted not adopting Kuai Tong's plan.
Emperor Gaozu said: That man is a lobbyist of Qi State.
He ordered Qi to capture Kuai Tong.
Kuai Tong was brought, and the emperor said: "Did you instigate the Marquis of Huaiyin to rebel?"
Answer: Yes. I did teach him that the boy would perish by not following my plan.
If that kid adopts my plan, how can Your Majesty destroy him?
The emperor said angrily: "Cook him."
Kuai Tong said: Oh, boil me to death, it is unfair!
The emperor said: You instigated Han Xin to rebel. What injustice is there?
Kuai Tong said: When the laws of the Qin Dynasty were corrupted and the political power collapsed, the six kingdoms of Shandong were in chaos. The princes from all walks of life revolted one after another. For a time, the heroes of the world gathered like crows.
The Qin Dynasty lost its throne, and all the heroes in the world came to snatch it, so those with high intelligence and quick actions were the first to get it.
Zhi's dog barked at Yao. Yao was not unkind, just because he was not the owner of the dog.
At this time, I only knew that there was Han Xin, but not His Majesty.
Moreover, there are too many people in the world who are sharpening their weapons and holding sharp knives in their hands who want to do what Your Majesty is doing, but they are just not up to the task.
How can you cook them all to death? Emperor Gaozu said: Let him go.
Kuai Tong's sins were forgiven.
Tai Shigong said: When I went to Huaiyin, the Huaiyin people told me that even when Han Xin was a commoner, his ambition was different.
His mother passed away and the family was too poor to bury her, but he still looked for a high and spacious cemetery where thousands of families could be placed next to the tomb.
I looked at his mother's grave and it was true.
If Han Xin could humbly give in and not boast about his achievements or rely on his own talents, that would be enough. His achievements in the Han Dynasty can be compared with those of Zhou Gong, Zhao Gong, and Taigong in the Zhou Dynasty, and future generations can enjoy endless sacrifices.
However, he failed to commit himself to doing this, and the world was already stable. Instead, he plotted rebellion and killed the clan. Isn't it right?
The integration of monarch and minister has been difficult since ancient times.
Han Xin was valued by Prime Minister Xiao He and highly recommended to Liu Bang. Because of his strategies, he was worshiped as a general.
In the battle of Weishui, they attacked halfway across the river, and in the battle of backwater, they uprooted the Zhao flag and changed it to the Han flag.
Belonging to the side of the Han Dynasty will increase the Han State's certainty of victory, and belonging to the Chu State will stabilize the Chu State.
In the end, he did not consider the three parts of the world, and ended up with Gaozu pretending to be Yunmeng and being demoted, which is really sighing.
summary:
Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was a native of Huaiyin. In his youth, he was poor, lacked good character, and could not secure an official position or make a living through business. He often relied on others for meals, which made him disliked. He frequently ate at a pavilion in Nanchang, but the pavilion chief's wife, annoyed by his presence, began eating breakfast early in the inner room. When Han Xin arrived, no food was prepared for him. Angered, he left and never returned. While fishing under the city, an old woman rinsing silk cotton pitied his hunger and fed him for dozens of days. Han Xin promised to repay her heavily, but she rebuked him, saying she did not expect repayment. A young butcher insulted Han Xin, calling him a coward and challenging him to either stab him or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin chose to crawl, and the crowd mocked him for his timidity.

When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River, Han Xin followed but gained no reputation. After Xiang Liang's defeat, he served under Xiang Yu as a doctor, offering suggestions that were ignored. He then joined Liu Bang, the King of Han, but was only made a minor official. Sentenced to death for breaking the law, he caught the attention of Teng Gong, who spared him after a bold speech. Teng Gong recommended him to Liu Bang, who appointed him as a commander, though without recognizing his talents. Han Xin frequently conversed with Xiao He, who considered him a genius. When Han Xin fled due to lack of recognition, Xiao He chased him personally. Liu Bang initially suspected Xiao He of desertion but learned he was pursuing Han Xin. Xiao He argued that Han Xin was unparalleled and essential for Liu Bang's ambitions to conquer the world. Liu Bang agreed to make Han Xin a general, and after a formal ceremony, Han Xin was appointed.

Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses, such as his inability to delegate, his reluctance to reward subordinates, and his harsh rule, which alienated the people. He advised Liu Bang to adopt the opposite approach, emphasizing the loyalty of the Qin people due to Liu Bang's merciful policies. Liu Bang followed Han Xin's plan, and in August, they advanced eastward through Chencang, pacifying the Three Qin regions. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, they subdued the kings of Wei and Henan. However, in April, the Han army was defeated at Pengcheng. Han Xin regrouped and met Liu Bang at Xingyang, defeating the Chu army. Later, King Bao of Wei rebelled, and Han Xin captured him, pacifying Wei. He then attacked Zhao with Zhang Er, defeating a 200,000-strong Zhao army at Jingxing by using a river-backed formation and a surprise cavalry attack. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised him to subdue Yan and Qi through diplomacy rather than force. Han Xin followed this advice, and Yan surrendered.

Han Xin requested that Zhang Er be made King of Zhao, which Liu Bang approved. The Chu army besieged Liu Bang at Xingyang, but he escaped and seized Han Xin's troops. Han Xin was ordered to attack Qi, and despite Liu Bang's envoy Li Shiqi persuading Qi to surrender, Han Xin, urged by Kuai Tong, attacked and conquered Qi. Chu sent Long Qie to aid Qi, but Han Xin defeated him by damming the Wei River and then releasing the water, killing Long Qie. Han Xin then requested to be made acting King of Qi. Liu Bang, initially furious, was persuaded by Zhang Liang and Chen Ping to grant the title to secure Han Xin's loyalty. Kuai Tong later advised Han Xin to rebel and divide the world into three parts, but Han Xin refused, citing Liu Bang's generosity. Despite Kuai Tong's warnings about the dangers of his position, Han Xin hesitated and ultimately remained loyal.

After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang demoted Han Xin to King of Chu and later, fearing his influence, arrested him during a visit to Yunmeng. Han Xin was pardoned but reduced to Marquis of Huaiyin. He grew resentful and avoided court. When Chen Xi rebelled, Han Xin conspired with him but was betrayed by a retainer. Empress Lu and Xiao He tricked Han Xin into the palace, where he was executed. Before his death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice. Kuai Tong was captured but spared after arguing that he only served his master. The historian comments that Han Xin's early ambition was evident, but his failure to remain humble and his eventual rebellion led to his downfall.
