translation:
Han Feizi said: Confucian scholars quoted ancient texts to disturb the rule of law, while chivalrous men violated laws by using force.
Han Fei ridiculed both types of people, but Confucian scholars were mostly praised by the world.
As for using power to obtain the position of prime minister, minister, and official, assisting the contemporary emperor, and his achievements are recorded in history books, there is nothing to say about this.
As for Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, they were ordinary people who studied hard, cherished the unique virtues of gentlemen, adhered to morality, and did not go along with the contemporary secular world. Contemporary people also laughed at them.
Therefore, Ji Ci and Yuan Xian lived in empty thatched houses all their lives, wearing coarse clothes and not even having enough to eat.
They have been dead for more than four hundred years, but their disciples from generation to generation miss them tirelessly.
Although the current rangers' actions do not conform to the standards of morality and law, they must keep their word and be resolute in their actions. They must fulfill what they have promised to show their honesty and are willing to sacrifice their lives to save others in danger. He has gone through the test of life and death, but he does not boast of his abilities and is ashamed to show off his merits. This is probably something worthy of praise!
Besides, critical things happen to people from time to time.
Tai Shigong said: In the past, Yu Shun encountered dangers when digging wells and building houses, Yi Yin once carried Ding Chu as a cook, Fu Yue once hid in Fu Yan and did hard labor, Lu Shang once suffered hardship in Jijin, Guan Zhong once wore shackles and handcuffs, Baili Xi once fed cattle as a slave, Confucius once was besieged in Kuangdi, and suffered starvation in Chen and Kui.
These people are all virtuous and benevolent people praised by Confucian scholars, but they have encountered such disasters, let alone ordinary people with moderate talents who have encountered troubled times?
How can we finish talking about the disasters they encountered?
Secular people have this saying: Why bother distinguishing between benevolence and righteousness? Those who have benefited are virtuous.
Therefore, Boyi thought it was shameful to eat Zhou millet and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain; but King Wen and King Wu did not harm the reputation of the kings. Pirates Zhi and Zhuang Qi were cruel and brutal, but their followers praised them for their boundless morality.
It can be seen from this that those who steal clothes and belt hooks will be beheaded, while those who steal state power are made marquises. People who are made marquises have benevolence and righteousness. These words are not false or untrue.
Nowadays, those who stick to one-sided views, some clinging to narrow principles, and have been isolated from the world for a long time, how can they compare with those who adapt to the world with low views and follow the ups and downs of the world to gain glory and fame?
As for ordinary people, they value the virtue of taking and giving in accordance with morality and fulfilling their promises. They follow morality thousands of miles away and die for morality regardless of worldly criticism. This is also their strength and cannot be done casually.
Therefore, when scholars are in poverty and embarrassment, they can devote themselves to learning and face their fate. Isn't this what people call the wise and heroic people?
If we compare the power, talent, and contribution of folk knight-errants to Ji Ji and Yuan Xian, they cannot be the same.
In short, from the perspective of the appearance of things and the fact that one must keep one's word, how can the knight's just behavior be missing?
I have never heard of civilian chivalrous people in ancient times.
In modern times, people such as Yanling Jizi, Mengchang Lord, Chunshen Lord, Pingyuan Lord, and Xinling Lord were all relatives of the kings. They relied on the wealth of their feudal states and ministers to recruit talents from all over the world, and they became famous among the vassal states. It cannot be said that they were not talents.
This is like shouting against the wind. The sound is not louder, but the listener feels clearly that this is due to the strong wind.
As for the commoner knight in Luxiang, he has cultivated his moral character and honed his reputation, and his reputation has spread all over the world. No one will not praise his virtue, which is difficult to do.
However, both Confucianism and Mohism rejected them and did not record them in their documents.
Since the Qin Dynasty, the deeds of civilian knights have been buried and cannot be seen. I am very sorry.
According to what I heard, since the founding of the Han Dynasty, there have been people such as Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Wang Gong, Ju Meng, and Guo Xie. Although they often violated the laws and prohibitions of the dynasty, their personal behavior was moral, honest and modest, and they were commendable.
Their reputation was not falsely established, and scholars did not echo them without basis.
As for those powerful people who form gangs, collude with each other, rely on their wealth to enslave the poor, use their power and violence to bully the lonely and weak, indulge their desires and satisfy themselves for their own pleasure, this is also considered shameful by the knight-errants.
I feel sad that secular people cannot understand the true meaning of this, but mistakenly regard the Zhu family, Guo Xie and others as the same kind as the violent and powerful people and ridicule them together.
The Zhu family of Lu State and Gaozu were of the same era.
The people of Lu were educated with Confucianism, but the Zhu family was famous for being a knight.
He has hid and rescued hundreds of heroes, and countless ordinary people he has saved.
But he never boasted of his talents or was complacent about his kindness. Those to whom he had given favors were afraid of seeing them again.
He helped others in need, starting with the poor and lowly.
There was no money left in his family, his clothes were torn and incomplete, he didn't have more than two kinds of meat dishes for each meal, and his ride was just an ox-drawn cart.
He was more interested in rescuing others in distress than doing anything private for himself.
He once secretly saved General Ji Bu from the misfortune of being killed. However, after General Ji Bu became honored, he refused to see him again for the rest of his life.
From Hangu Pass to the east, people craned their necks hoping to make friends with him.
Tian Zhong of Chu was famous for being a knight. He liked swordsmanship and served the Zhu family like his father. He thought that his conduct could not keep up with the Zhu family.
After Tian Zhong's death, a drama Meng appeared in Luoyang.
The people of Luoyang made a living by doing business, and Ju Meng became famous among the princes because of his chivalry.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Zhou Yafu, the marquis of Tiao, was a Taiwei. He rushed to Luoyang in a post car, found Ju Meng, and said happily: The seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu launched a rebellion without asking Ju Meng for help. I know they have done nothing.
The world is in turmoil, and the Taiwei getting him is like getting an equal country.
Ju Meng's behavior is roughly similar to that of the Zhu family, but he likes to play chess. Most of what he does is a teenager's game.
But when Ju Meng's mother passed away, there were probably thousands of cars coming from far away to mourn her.
When Ju Meng died, his family didn't even have ten gold coins.
At this time, Wang Meng from Fuli was also famous among the Yangtze River and Huaihe River for his chivalry.
At this time, Zhou Yong of Chendi, a family named Gui in Jinan, was also famous as a hero. After Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty heard about it, he sent envoys to kill all such people.
After that, people named Bai from Daijun, Han Wupi from Liangdi, Brother Xue from Yangdi, and Han Ru from Shaanxi appeared one after another.
Guo Xie was a native of Zhi County, and his courtesy name was Weng Bo. He is the grandson of Xu Ning, who is good at meeting people.
Guo Xie's father was killed during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty because he was a knight.
Guo Xie was a short man, smart and strong, and he did not drink.
When he was a child, he was cruel and cruel, and when he was angry and unhappy, he killed many people with his own hands.
He did not hesitate to sacrifice his life to avenge his friends, hid desperadoes to commit illegal robberies, minted coins privately when he stopped, and dug graves. His illegal activities were countless.
But they can be blessed by God, often escape from distress and crisis, or encounter amnesty.
When Guo Xie got older, he changed his behavior, took care of himself, repaid those who hated him with kindness, gave more to others, and rarely resented others.
But his own preference for Xingxia became stronger and stronger.
He has saved other people's lives, but does not boast of his merits, but his heart is still cruel and vicious, and his sudden anger and violence over trivial matters are still the same as before.
The young man at that time admired his behavior and often avenged him, but did not let him know.
The son of Guo Xie's sister relied on Guo Xie's power to drink with others and asked them to toast.
If the person's alcohol capacity is small and he can't drink anymore, he will force-fed the person.
The man got angry, drew his sword, stabbed Guo Xie's sister's son to death, and then ran away.
Guo Xie's sister got angry and said: With my brother Weng Bo's loyalty, they killed my son but could not catch the murderer.
So she dumped her son's body on the road without burying it, hoping to humiliate Guo Xie.
Guo Xie sent people to secretly find out where the murderer was.
The murderer was embarrassed and came back on his own initiative to tell Guo Xie the real situation.
Guo Xie said: You should have killed him, my child is not justified.
So he let the murderer go, put the blame on his sister's son, collected his body and buried him.
When people heard the news, they all praised Guo Xie's moral behavior and became more attached to him.
Every time Guo Xie went out or came back, people avoided him. Only one man sat on the ground and looked at him arrogantly. Guo Xie sent someone to ask his name.
Someone among Guo Xie's retainers wanted to kill the man. Guo Xie said: "I live in the countryside and are not respected by others. This is because I have not cultivated my own morals enough. What crime does he have?"
So he secretly asked Wei Shi: This person is the one I care about most. When it is his turn to serve, please exempt him.
From then on, when he was serving in the army, there were many times when the county officials did not find this person who was rude to Guo Xie.
The man felt strange and asked the reason. It turned out that Guo Xie had exempted him from the service.
So, he exposed his body and went to Guo Xie to apologize.
When the young people heard this news, they admired Guo Xie's behavior even more.
There were people in Luoyang who were enemies of each other, and there were dozens of wise men and heroes in the city to mediate between them, but the two sides never listened to persuasion.
The retainers came to see Guo Xie and explain the situation.
Guo Xie went to meet with his enemies at night. Out of respect for Guo Xie, the enemies reluctantly listened to his advice and prepared to reconcile.
Guo Xie said to his enemies: I heard that the princes of Luoyang were trying to mediate for you, but most of you refused to listen.
Now that you have listened to my advice, how can I come from other counties to usurp the rights of the virtuous officials in this city?
So Guo Xie left that night without letting anyone know, saying: "Don't listen to my mediation for the time being. After I leave, let the heroes of Luoyang mediate, and you just listen to them."
Guo Xie maintained a respectful attitude towards others and did not dare to enter the county government office by car.
He went to nearby counties to do things for others. If the things could be done, he would definitely get them done. If the things couldn't be done, he would have to satisfy all parties involved before he dared to go and have dinner with others.
Therefore, everyone respects him very much and competes to serve him.
Young men in the city and wise men and heroes from nearby counties often came to visit Guo Xie in more than ten cars in the middle of the night, asking to take the guests of Guo Xie's family back to their homes for support.
In the second year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the imperial court wanted to move wealthy families from various counties to live in Maoling. Guo Xie's family was poor and did not meet the transfer standard of three million yuan. However, Guo Xie's name was on the relocation list, so the officials were afraid and did not dare to let Guo Xie move.
At that time, General Wei Qing told the emperor on behalf of Guo Xie: Guo Xie's family is poor and does not meet the criteria for relocation.
But the emperor said: The power of a common man can make the general speak for him, which shows that his family is not poor.
Guo Xie's family was then moved to Maoling.
People paid a total of more than 10 million to see Guo Xie off.
The son of Yang Jizhu, a native of Zhi County, was a rafter in the county, and he nominated Guo Xie to be moved there.
The son of Guo Xie's brother beheaded Yangxian Rong.
From then on, the Yang family and the Guo family became enemies.
Guo Xie moved to Guanzhong. The wise men and heroes in Guanzhong, no matter whether they knew Guo Xie before or not, now that they heard about his reputation, they all rushed to make friends with Guo Xie.
Guo Xie is short, does not drink alcohol, and does not ride a horse when going out.
Later, he killed Master Yang Jizhu.
Yang Jizhu's family wrote a letter to complain, and someone killed the complainer under the palace gate.
When the emperor heard the news, he ordered the officials to capture Guo Xie.
Guo Xie fled, placed his mother in Xia Yang, and fled to Linjin himself.
The young master from Linjin was not acquainted with Guo Xie, so Guo Xie took the liberty of meeting him and asked him to help him get out of confinement.
After Ji Shaogong sent Guo Xie out of the customs, Guo Xie traveled to Taiyuan. Wherever he went, he often told the people who kept him room and board about his situation.
The officials pursued Guo Xie and tracked him to the home of the young master.
Ji Shaogong committed suicide and his confession was cut off.
It took a long time for the government to arrest Guo Xie and thoroughly investigate his crimes. They found that all the people killed by Guo Xie had happened before the amnesty order was announced.
Once, a Confucian scholar from Zhi County was sitting around with the envoys who came to investigate Guo Xie's case. Guo Xie's disciples praised Guo Xie. The Confucian scholar said: Guo Xie only loves to do evil and illegal things. How can we say that he is a wise man?
When Guo Xie's disciples heard this, they killed the Confucian scholar and cut out his tongue.
The officials questioned Guo Xie and asked him to hand over the murderer, but Guo Xie did not know who the murderer was.
The murderer has never been found, and we don’t know who he is.
The officials reported to the emperor that Guo Xie was not guilty.
Gongsun Hong, the imperial censor, commented: Guo Xie acted as a commoner, played tricks, violated the law, and killed people for trivial matters. Although Guo Xie did not know it, this crime was more serious than his own murder.
Guo Xie was sentenced to the crime of treason and immorality.
So he killed Guo Jie's entire family.
From then on, there were many people who practiced chivalry, but they were all arrogant and unworthy of praise.
But Fan Zhongzi from Chang'an in Guanzhong, Wangsun Zhao from Huaili, Gao Gongzi from Changling, Guo Gongzhong from Xihe, Lu Gongru from Taiyuan, Changqing from Linhuai, Tian Junru from Dongyang, although they are chivalrous, they are respectful, cautious and modest.
As for the Yao family in the North Road, some people with the surname Du in the West Road, Qiu Jing in the South Road, Zhao Ta, Yu Gongzi in the East Road, and Zhao Tiao in Nanyang, these are just thieves among the people, and they are not worth mentioning!
This was something people like the Zhu family were ashamed of in the past.
Tai Shigong said: I think Guo Xie's appearance is not as good as that of a middle-aged man, and his language is not worth mentioning.
But people in the world, whether they are virtuous or unworthy, whether they know him or not, all admire his reputation, and those who talk about knight-errants all praise Guo Xie to improve their own reputation.
The proverb says: If a person can use a glorious reputation as an appearance, will there be an end to it? Alas, what a pity!
summary:
Han Feizi's critique of Confucian scholars and chivalrous men for undermining law and order, contrasting them with figures like Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, who lived in poverty but were remembered for their virtues. It praises rangers for their integrity, willingness to sacrifice for others, and modesty, despite their actions not always aligning with moral and legal standards. The text cites historical figures like Yu Shun, Yi Yin, and Confucius who faced hardships, emphasizing that even virtuous individuals encounter disasters. It critiques societal hypocrisy, where minor thieves are punished while those who seize power are honored, and notes that true chivalry involves keeping promises and aiding others without boasting.

The narrative then focuses on civilian knights from the Han Dynasty, such as Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Ju Meng, and Guo Xie. Zhu Jia, a knight from Lu, hid and rescued hundreds without boasting, living frugally. Tian Zhong served Zhu Jia like a father. Ju Meng, from Luoyang, was sought after by Zhou Yafu during the Wu-Chu rebellion, and his mother's funeral drew thousands. Guo Xie, initially cruel, later reformed, repaying hatred with kindness and saving lives without boasting. He mediated disputes, avoided taking credit, and maintained humility, earning widespread respect. However, his past crimes and a murder by his disciples led to his execution under Emperor Wu, with Gongsun Hong arguing his influence made him more dangerous than if he had committed the murders himself. The text concludes by noting that later knights were often arrogant, except for a few like Fan Zhongzi, and laments that Guo Xie's reputation outshone his unremarkable appearance and speech.

translation:
Confucius said: The Six Classics have the same role in governing the country.
"Li" is used to regulate people's words and deeds, "Music" is used to promote people's harmony, "Book" is used to record past deeds and regulations, "Poetry" is used to express emotions, "Yi" is used to spy on the magical changes of heaven and earth, and "Spring and Autumn" is used to understand the meaning of subtle words and weigh the right and wrong.
Tai Shigong said: The truth in the world is vast and boundless, isn't it great!
If the words can be slightly to the point, it can also resolve a lot of troubles.
Chunyu Kun was a son-in-law of Qi State.
Less than seven feet tall, he is funny and eloquent. He has been on many missions to the princes and has never been humiliated.
When King Wei of Qi was in power, he liked to talk in argot, feast all night long, indulge in excessive drinking, ignored state affairs, and entrusted political affairs to the officials.
The civil and military officials are dissolute and indulgent, and the princes and countries invade and invade. The country is in danger and is in danger in a matter of seconds. None of the ministers around King Qi dared to give advice.
Chunyu Kun used argot to admonish and admonish King Wei of Qi, saying: There is a big bird in the capital that landed in the king's courtyard. It has not flown or screamed for three years. Does the king know what happened to this bird?
King Wei of Qi said: If this bird does not fly, it will go straight to the sky; if it does not scream, it will amaze people.
So he ordered all the chiefs of the seventy-two counties in the country to come to the court to report. They rewarded one person and killed another. They also sent troops to defend against the enemy. The princes and states were shocked and returned the occupied land to Qi.
Qi's prestige lasted for thirty-six years.
All these things are recorded in "Tian Wan Family".
In the eighth year of King Wei of Qi's reign, the State of Chu sent a large army to invade its borders.
The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun as an envoy to the State of Zhao to request reinforcements, and asked him to carry a gift of a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse carriages.
Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed so hard that the string holding his hat broke.
King Wei said: Sir, do you think the gift is too little?
Chunyu Kun said: How dare you think too little!
King Wei said: Then you laugh, do you have any excuse?
Chunyu Kun said: Today I came from the east and saw a man worshiping the God of the Fields by the roadside. He held a pig's trotter and a glass of wine and prayed: "The grain harvested in the highlands fills the bonnet, and the crops harvested in the low fields fill the vehicles; the grains are lush and ripe, and the rice grains are piled up in the warehouse."
I saw that he brought few sacrifices and prayed for many things, so I laughed at him.
So King Wei of Qi increased the gifts to a thousand pieces of gold, ten pairs of white jade stones, and a hundred four-horse carriages.
Chunyu Kun said goodbye and set off for the Kingdom of Zhao.
King Zhao allocated him 100,000 elite soldiers and 1,000 leather-wrapped chariots.
When the Chu State heard the news, they withdrew their troops overnight.
King Qi Wei was very happy. He set up wine and food in the harem, summoned Chunyu Kun and gave him wine to drink.
Ask him: How much wine can you drink before you get drunk?
Chunyu Kun replied: I can get drunk even if I drink a dou of wine, and I can get drunk even if I drink a stone of wine.
King Wei said: "Sir, you will get drunk after drinking one measure. How can you drink one stone?"
Can you tell me this truth?
Chunyu Kun said: The king gave me wine in front of me, with the law enforcement officer standing beside me and the censor standing behind me. I was frightened, bowed my head and drank on the ground. I was drunk after not even one bucket.
If my parents have distinguished guests, I roll up my sleeves, sit down on my knees, and serve wine to the guests. The guests reward me with residual wine from time to time, and I raise my glass to toast many times to socialize, and I get drunk after less than two cups.
If friends are traveling together, they have not seen each other for a long time, and suddenly they meet again. They happily reminisce about the past and talk about their hearts. They will become drunk after drinking about five or six buckets.
As for gatherings in the countryside, men and women sit together, toast each other, and there is no time limit. They also play games such as Liubo and Hu Tou. They call friends and invite pairs. Shaking hands and talking happily are not punished, and flirting is not prohibited. There are fallen earrings in front of me and lost hairpins behind my back. At this time, I am happiest. I can drink eight measures of wine, and I am only two or three points drunk.
It was getting dark and the wine was almost finished. We put the remaining wine together and everyone sat down together, men and women sharing the same table. Shoes and clogs were mixed together. Cups and plates were in a mess. The candles in the main room had been extinguished.
Therefore, if you drink too much, you will easily get into trouble, and if you are extremely happy, something sad will happen. This is true of all things. This statement means that no matter what happens, it should not be taken to extremes. If it reaches extremes, it will decline.
Chunyu Kun used this to tactfully persuade King Qi Wei.
King Wei said: OK.
So King Wei stopped drinking and drinking every night, and appointed Chunyu Kun as the guest official to receive guests from the princes.
The royal family of the King of Qi held banquets, and Chunyu Kun often accompanied them.
More than a hundred years after Chunyu Kun, Yu Meng came out of the Chu State.
You Meng was originally a singing and dancing artist from Chu State.
He was eight feet tall and very eloquent. He often used jokes to persuade the king of Chu.
During the reign of King Zhuang of Chu, he had a favorite horse. He dressed it in brocade clothes, kept it in a magnificent house, slept on a bed without a curtain, and fed it candied dried dates.
The horse became ill and died because of obesity. King Zhuang of Chu sent his ministers to hold a funeral for the horse. They wanted to bury it in a coffin and bury it according to the etiquette of a doctor.
King Zhuang's ministers on the left and right quarreled with each other to advise him on this matter, thinking that it should not be done.
King Zhuang issued an order: Anyone who dares to remonstrate with the matter of burying a horse will be sentenced to death.
When Youmeng heard this, he walked into the palace gate and cried to the sky.
King Zhuang was surprised and asked him why he was crying.
Youmeng said: "The horse is the king's favorite thing. With a country as powerful as Chu, there is nothing that can't be done, but burying it with the etiquette of a doctor is too rude. Please bury it with the etiquette of a king."
King Zhuang asked: What should we do?
You Meng replied: I requested that the coffin be made of beautiful jade with carved patterns, the cover of fine catalpa wood, and the coffin blocks made of valuable woods such as urin, maple, hemp, and camphor. I sent soldiers to dig a grave for it, and asked the elderly and children to carry earth to build the tomb.
When the princes heard this, they all knew that the king despised people and valued horses.
King Zhuang said: "Has my fault reached this level?"
What to do about it?
Umeng said: Please allow me to bury it in the same way as an animal: pile an earth stove on the ground as a set, use a large copper pot as a coffin, use ginger and dates to season, use spices to relieve the smell, use rice as a sacrifice, use fire as clothes, and bury it in the human belly.
So King Zhuang sent someone to give the horse to the eunuch in charge of the palace's meals, so that the people in the world would not spread the matter for a long time.
Sun Shuao, the prime minister of Chu, knew that Youmeng was a wise man and treated him well.
When Sun Shuao was seriously ill and about to die, he told his son: After I die, you will definitely be poor.
At that time, you go to see Youmeng and say that I am Sun Shuao's son.
A few years later, Sun Shuao's son was indeed so poor that he had to rely on firewood to survive. Once I met Youmeng on the road, he said to Youmeng: I am Sun Shuao's son.
Before my father died, he asked me to go see Youmeng when I was in poverty.
Youmeng said: Don't go far away.
So, he immediately sewed clothes and hats similar to Sun Shuao's and wore them, imitating Sun Shuao's speech, behavior, voice and smile.
After more than a year, he imitated Sun Shuao so much that even the officials around King Zhuang of Chu could not tell him apart.
King Zhuang of Chu held a banquet, and Youmeng came forward to toast and bless King Zhuang. King Zhuang was shocked, thinking that Sun Shuao had come back to life again, and wanted to make him Prime Minister of Chu.
Youmeng said: "Please allow me to go back and discuss this matter with my wife, and come back in three days to take up the post of Prime Minister of Chu."
King Zhuang agreed to him.
Three days later, Youmeng came to see King Zhuang again.
King Zhuang asked: What did your wife say?
Youmeng said: My wife told me not to do it. It is not worthy to be the prime minister of Chu State.
Like Sun Shuao, who was the prime minister of the Chu State and governed the Chu State with loyalty and integrity, the king of Chu was able to dominate.
Now that he is dead, his son has no place to stand and is so poor that he has to carry firewood to make a living every day.
If you want to be the prime minister of Chu like Sun Shuao, you might as well commit suicide.
Umeng then sang: Living in the mountains and fields, it is difficult to live in the fields and suffer hardships.
Those who go out to serve as officials, are themselves corrupt and despicable, accumulate excess wealth, and have no regard for their integrity.
After his death, although his family was wealthy, he was afraid of corruption, bending the law, doing illegal things, and committing serious crimes. He was killed and his family was also destroyed.
What can a corrupt official do?
I want to be an upright official, abide by the law, be loyal to my duties, and never dare to do anything illegal until my death.
Alas, what can an upright official do?
For example, Sun Shuao, Prime Minister of Chu, insisted on integrity throughout his life, but now his wife, children and children are so poor that they have to collect firewood for a living.
It’s really not worth being an upright official! So King Zhuang expressed his apology to You Meng, and immediately summoned Sun Shuao's son and granted him the city of Qiuqiu with 400 households for the purpose of worshiping Sun Shuao.
Since then, there has been no interruption for ten generations.
It can be said that Youmeng's intelligence was just right and he seized the opportunity to display it.
More than two hundred years after You Meng, Qin State gave birth to You Zhan.
Youzhan is a singing and dancing artist from the Qin State. He is very short.
He is good at telling jokes, but they all make sense. During the reign of Qin Shihuang, a banquet was held in the palace. It was raining, and the guards standing guard under the palace steps were all wet with rain and cold.
When Youzhan saw them, he felt very sorry for them and said to them: "Do you want to rest?"
The guards all said: Very much so.
Youzhan said: If I call you, you must answer me quickly.
After a while, people in the palace toasted Qin Shihuang and shouted long live the emperor.
Youzhan approached the railing and shouted loudly: Guard!
The guard replied: Yes.
Youzhan said: Although you are tall, what good is it?
I was lucky enough to stand in the open air and get soaked in the rain. Although I am short, I am lucky enough to rest here.
Therefore, Qin Shihuang allowed the guards to reduce their duty by half and take over in turns.
Qin Shihuang once planned to expand the hunting area to Hangu Pass in the east and Yong County and Chencang in the west.
Youzhan said: OK.
Keep more animals inside. If the enemy invades from the east, it will be enough to let the elk use their horns to resist them.
After hearing this, Qin Shihuang stopped his plan to expand the hunting grounds.
Emperor Qin II came to the throne and wanted to paint the city walls with paint.
Youzhan said: OK.
Even if your Majesty did not say it, I would have asked you to do so.
Although the lacquered city wall brings sorrow and expense to the people, it is beautiful!
The walls were painted so slippery that enemies could not climb up even if they came.
To accomplish this, it is easy to paint, but what is difficult is to find a big house, put the painted city wall in it, and let it dry in the shade.
The second emperor laughed and canceled the plan.
Soon, the second emperor was killed, Youzhan surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and died a few years later.
Tai Shigong said: Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed, and King Wei of Qi followed his example throughout the world.
You Meng shook his head and sang, and those who carried firewood for a living were rewarded.
Youzhan leaned on the railing and shouted, so the guards holding shields under the palace steps were able to reduce their duty by half and take turns to rest.
Aren’t these all great and praiseworthy!
Mr. Chu Shaosun said: I am fortunate to be a doctor because I am proficient in Confucian classics. I also like to read historical biographies other than the Six Classics.
I couldn't be humble and conceding, so I wrote six more chapters of funny stories and compiled them at the back of Tai Shigong's original work.
It can be read and expanded, so that it can be passed on to future generations who are not afraid of troubles to read, so as to relax their minds and alert them to listen. It is specially attached to the back of the three funny stories of Tai Shigong above.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, there was a favored artist named Guo. Although his speeches were not reasonable, he could make the emperor feel happy after listening to them.
When Emperor Wu was young, the mother of Marquis Dongwu nursed him. When Emperor Wu grew up, he called her the "Big Wet Nurse".
I visit the DPRK about twice a month.
Every time the notification of entering the court was sent in, the imperial edict would send the favored minister Ma Youqing to reward the wet nurse with fifty pieces of silk and prepare food to support her.
The wet nurse wrote: There is a piece of public land somewhere, and I hope to lend it to me.
Emperor Wu said: "Does the wet nurse want it?"
So he gave her the public land.
The wet nurse did not listen to anything she said.
It was also decreed that the carriages used by wet nurses could travel on the imperial road.
At this time, all the ministers respected the wet nurse.
The slaves and descendants of the wet nurse's family ran rampant in Chang'an City, intercepting people's carriages and horses, and snatching other people's clothes.
When the news reached the court, Emperor Wu could not bear to use the law to punish the wet nurse.
The official in charge asked the wet nurse and her family to move to the border.
Emperor Wu approved it.
The wet nurse should enter the palace and say goodbye in front of Emperor Wu.
The wet nurse first met Guo Sheren and shed tears for this.
Guo Sheren said: Go in immediately to see and say goodbye, exit quickly, and turn around to see the emperor several times.
The wet nurse did as he asked. When she saw Emperor Wu to say goodbye, she quickly left and turned around to look at Emperor Wu.
Guo Sheren scolded the wet nurse loudly and said: Sigh!
Old lady, why don’t you leave quickly!
The emperor has grown up, does he have to wait for you to breastfeed him to survive? What are you looking at?
So Emperor Wu felt sorry for her and couldn't help but feel sad. He ordered to stop the move and not allow the wet nurse's family to be moved. He also punished those who spoke ill of the wet nurse.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, there was a man named Dongfang Shuo in Qi. Because he liked books handed down from ancient times and Confucian classics, he read extensively the books of hundreds of schools of thought.
When Dongfang Shuo first arrived in Chang'an, he went to Gongche Mansion to submit a letter to the emperor, using a total of three thousand wooden slips.
The bus office sent two people to carry his memorial together, and they were just able to lift it.
Emperor Wu was reading Dongfang Shuo's memorial in the palace. When he needed to stop reading, he made a mark there and read it for two months before finishing it.
Emperor Wu ordered Dongfang Shuo to be appointed Langguan, and he often served the emperor.
Emperor Wu was never unhappy when he was called to talk to him many times.
Emperor Wu often issued edicts to give him meals in front of the emperor.
After the meal, he put all the remaining meat in his arms and took it away, staining his clothes.
The emperor gave him silk and silk many times, but he always took it away, carrying it on his shoulder.
He used the money and silk given to him to marry a beautiful young woman from Chang'an city.
Most of them get married within a year and then abandon them to marry another one.
The money rewarded by the emperor was entirely spent on women.
Half of the emperor's courtiers called him "madman."
Emperor Wu heard this and said: If Dongfang Shuo didn't do these ridiculous things when he was an official, how could you compare to him?
Dongfang Shuo recommended his son to be a Langguan, and he was promoted to an emissary among the servants. He was often ordered to serve on envoys and go on official business.
One day Dongfang Shuo passed by the palace, and the officials said to him: "People think that Mr. Shuo is a madman."
Dongfang Shuo said: People like me are the so-called people who live in seclusion in the court.
People in ancient times lived in seclusion in the mountains.
He often sat at banquets, and when he drank to his heart's content, he would crawl on the ground and sing: Live in seclusion in the world, and hide from the world at the Golden Horse Gate.
Why live in seclusion in the mountains or in a hut when you can live in seclusion in the palace and protect yourself.
The so-called Golden Horse Gate is the gate of the eunuch's office. There is a bronze horse next to the gate, so it is called the Golden Horse Gate.
At that time, the imperial court convened the doctors and gentlemen in the academy to participate in the discussion. They all criticized Dongfang Shuo and said: Su Qin and Zhang Yi accidentally met the monarch of a big country, and they could occupy the position of prime minister, and their kindness would be passed down to future generations.
Now you, the old man, have studied the methods of the former kings in governing the country, admired the principles of the saints, and are familiar with the "Poems" and "Books" and the opinions of hundreds of schools of thought. I cannot give examples one by one.
There are also articles and writings, and they think that they are unparalleled in the world, so they can be said to be well-informed, intelligent and able to argue.
However, you have served the sage emperor with all your strength and loyalty for a long time and accumulated for decades. Your official title is only that of a minister and your position is that of a guard. It seems that you have not behaved well enough?
What is the reason for this?
Dongfang Shuo said: This is not something you can fully understand.
That was one era and now is another era. How can they be compared?
In the era of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, the Zhou Dynasty was in great decline. The princes did not go to court to see the emperor of Zhou. They used force to conquer power and invaded each other with military means. The world was merged into twelve vassal states, with equal power. Those who gained scholars became powerful, and those who lost scholars perished. Therefore, they listened to the advice of scholars, placed them in high positions, passed down their kindness to future generations, and their descendants enjoyed long-lasting glory.
Not so today.
The sage emperor is in charge of the government, his favor spreads all over the world, the princes submit and obey, and his power intimidates all directions. He connects the territories beyond the four seas into a paradise like a seat, which is more stable than an inverted bowl. The world is unified and integrated, and all actions are as easy as turning in the palm of the hand.
How to distinguish between virtuous and unvirtuous people?
Nowadays, because the world is vast and there are many scholars and people, they are trying their best to lobby, just like the spokes are gathered to the hub of a car, there are countless people who are competing to gather in the capital to offer suggestions to the court.
Although they try their best to uphold morality and justice, they are still trapped by food and clothing, and some even cannot find a way out.
If Zhang Yi, Su Qin and I were born in the same era, how could they dare to expect to be a regular minister if they couldn't even get a small official in charge of the old system and old rules?
Ancient books say: If there is no disaster in the world, even if there is a saint, there will be no place to display his talents; if the monarch and his ministers are in harmony, even if there is a wise man, there will be no place to build his achievements.
So, as times change, things will change accordingly.
Despite this, how can we not work hard to cultivate ourselves?
"Poetry" says: If you ring a bell in the palace, the sound can be heard outside.
Cranes chirp far away in the depths of the swamp, and the sound can be heard in the sky.
If you can cultivate yourself, why worry about not getting glory!
Taigong of Qi personally practiced benevolence and righteousness for seventy-two years. Only when he met King Wen of Zhou did he implement his ideas and enfeoffed him in the state of Qi. The influence of his thoughts has been passed down for seven hundred years without being extinguished.
This is the reason why scholars work tirelessly day and night to study knowledge and implement their own ideas without daring to stop.
The hermits in the world today, although they are not employed for a while, can be detached and self-reliant, living alone, looking at Xu You from a distance, and Jie Yu at close range. They are as resourceful as Fan Li, and their loyalty is comparable to Wu Zixu.
Why do you have doubts about me?
So the gentlemen were silent and had no words to answer.
An animal ran out from the double railings of the back pavilion of Jianzhang Palace. It was shaped like an elk.
The news reached the palace, and Emperor Wu personally went there to watch.
When I asked the officials around me who were familiar with things and well versed in classics, no one could tell what kind of animal it was.
An edict was issued to ask Dongfang Shuo to come and see it.
Dongfang Shuo said: I know this thing, please give me good wine and food so that I can have a full meal, then I will say it. Emperor Wu said: Yes.
After dinner, Dongfang Shuo said again: There are several hectares of public land, fish ponds and reed ponds somewhere. Your Majesty rewarded me, so I will tell you.
Emperor Wu said: Yes.
Then Dongfang Shuo was willing to say: This is an animal called Zou Ya.
There should be people coming to surrender from far away, so Zou Ya appears first.
Its teeth are the same from front to back and are equal in size without big teeth, so it is called Zou fang.
About a year later, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu came and surrendered to the Han Dynasty with 100,000 people.
Emperor Wu then rewarded Dongfang Shuo with a lot of money. In old age.
When Dongfang Shuo was dying, he advised Emperor Wu: "The Book of Songs" says that flies flying around will fall on the fence.
Kind and kind gentleman, don't listen to slander.
There is no end to the slander, and there is no peace for neighboring countries on all sides.
I hope that your Majesty will stay away from those who flatter people with clever words and rebuke their slander.
Emperor Wu said: Why do Dongfang Shuo mostly make good remarks today?
Be amazed by this.
Soon after, Dongfang Shuo died of illness.
Ancient books say: When a bird is dying, its cry is particularly sad; when a person is dying, its words are very kind.
That's what I mean.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, General Wei Qing was the elder brother of Queen Wei and was granted the title of Marquis of Changping.
He led the army to attack the Xiongnu and chased them to the Yuwu River before returning. He killed a large number of enemy soldiers and captured many prisoners. He made great achievements in battle and returned victorious. Emperor Wu ordered a reward of a thousand catties of gold.
When the general came out of the palace gate, Mr. Dong Guo, a native of Qi, was waiting at the carriage house as an alchemist. He stopped General Wei's carriage and horse on the road, paid homage and said: "I have something to report to the general."
General Wei stopped in front of the car, and Mr. Dong Guo said beside the car: Mrs. Wang has recently been favored by the emperor, and her family is poor.
Now that the general has received a thousand catties of gold, if he uses half of it to give to Mrs. Wang's parents, the emperor will be very happy to know it.
This is what is called a clever and convenient strategy.
General Wei thanked him and said: Fortunately, sir, you told me this convenient strategy. I will definitely follow the advice.
So General Wei used five hundred kilograms of gold as a gift to Mrs. Wang's parents.
Mrs. Wang told Emperor Wu about this.
Emperor Wu said: The general does not know how to do this.
When Wei Qing was asked where he got the strategy, he replied: "I got it from Mr. Dongguo who was on duty."
So he ordered Mr. Dongguo to be summoned and appointed him as the county captain.
Mr. Dongguo has been waiting for work at the bus station for a long time. He is poor, hungry and cold. His clothes are shabby and his shoes are not intact.
When walking in the snow, the shoes have sides but no soles, and the feet are all on the ground.
The passers-by laughed at him, and Mr. Dongguo answered them: Who can wear shoes and walk in the snow, and let people see that the top of the shoe is a shoe, and the bottom of the shoe looks like a human foot?
When he was appointed as an official with a salary of two thousand dan, wore a green ribbon, walked out of the palace gate to say goodbye to his master, all those who had been waiting with him in the past came to bid farewell to him in batches on the outskirts of the capital.
Glorious and glorious all the way, famous in the contemporary era.
This is what is called a man wearing coarse clothes but carrying a treasure in his arms.
When he was poor, everyone ignored him; when he became famous, everyone rushed to depend on him.
As the saying goes: A fortune teller misses a good horse because of his skinny appearance, and a fortune teller misses a talented person because of his poor appearance.
Is this the scenario you are talking about?
Mrs. Wang was seriously ill, and the emperor visited her in person and asked her: Your son should be crowned king. Where do you want to crown him?
He replied: I hope to be sealed in Luoyang.
The emperor said: No.
Luoyang has arsenals, large granaries, and is located at a transportation junction. It is the choke point of the world.
Since the late emperor, it is said that no king has been granted the title of king in Luoyang.
However, none of the feudal states in the Guandong area is larger than Qi, so he can be crowned King of Qi.
Mrs. Wang patted her head with her hands and exclaimed: So lucky.
After the death of Mrs. Wang, it was called the death of the Queen Mother of Qi.
Once upon a time, the King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun to the State of Chu to offer yellow swans.
After leaving the capital gate, the yellow swan flew away on the way. He had no choice but to hold the empty cage, fabricate a lie, and go to see the king of Chu, saying: The king of Qi sent me to offer the yellow swan. When he passed by the water, he couldn't bear the yellow swan to dry up, so he let it drink water. Unexpectedly, it left me and flew away.
I want to stab the abdomen or strangle the neck to death, but I am also worried that others will criticize the king for causing the scholars to commit suicide because of birds and beasts.
Yellow swans are feathered things that are very similar. I want to buy a similar one to replace it. This is dishonest and deceives the king.
He wanted to flee to other countries, but he was also sad that the communication between the monarchs of Qi and Chu was cut off.
So I came to plead guilty, kowtow to the king, and ask for punishment.
The king of Chu said: "It's great that the king of Qi has such a loyal person."
He rewarded Chunyu Kun with generous gifts, and his wealth was twice as much as that offered to Huang Hu.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the prefect of Beihai County was summoned to the emperor's palace.
Mr. Wang, a government official in charge of documents, took the initiative to ask to go with the prefect, saying: I will be good to you.
The prefect agreed to him. Many officials and meritorious officials in the prefecture reported: Mr. Wang likes to drink, talks a lot, and is less practical. I'm afraid he is not suitable for traveling together.
The prefect said: Mr. Wang wants to go, so it is not good to go against his wishes.
So he went with him.
Come to the palace gate and wait for orders at the palace gate.
Mr. Wang only took money to buy wine and drank with the captain of the guard. He was drunk all day long and did not visit the prefect.
The prefect entered the palace to pay homage to the emperor.
Mr. Wang said to the gatekeeper: Please call our prefect to come to the palace gate for me and speak to him from a distance.
The gatekeeper went to call the prefect on his behalf.
The prefect came out and saw Mr. Wang.
Mr. Wang said: If the emperor asked you how to govern Beihai County so that there are no thieves there, what would you answer?
The prefect replied: Choose talented people and appoint them according to their abilities. Reward those with outstanding talents and punish those who are not motivated.
Mr. Wang said: This kind of response is to praise yourself and show off your achievements, which is not acceptable.
I hope you will answer: It is not the power of the minister, but the effect of the majesty of the gods. The prefect said: OK.
The prefect was summoned into the palace and walked up to His Highness. He received an edict and asked him: "How do you govern Beihai County so that thieves do not dare to appear?"
The prefect kowtowed and replied: This is not the power of the minister, but entirely the result of the majesty of your majesty.
Emperor Wu laughed and said: Ah!
Where can I learn the words of the elders and praise them?
Where did you hear it?
The prefect replied: "It was taught by Literary Master Shi."
Emperor Wu said: Where is he now?
The prefect replied: Outside the palace gate.
Emperor Wu issued an edict to summon Mr. Wang and appointed him as Shuiheng Cheng, and Beihai Prefect as Shuiheng Duwei.
An ancient book says: Beautiful words can betray you, and noble conduct can make you superhuman.
Gentlemen give gifts with kind words, while villains give gifts with money.
During the reign of Wei Wenhou, Ximen Bao served as the magistrate of Ye County.
Ximen Bao arrived in Ye County and summoned senior and famous people to ask about the painful things among the people.
Those people replied: It is hard to find a wife for the river god, and for this reason he is poor.
Ximen Bao asked the reason and replied: The three elders and court officials in Yedi collected taxes from the people all the year round, and collected millions of their money. They used two to three hundred thousand to find a wife for the river god, and then divided the remaining money with the temple blessings and witches and took them home.
During that period, the witch patrolled around and when she saw a beautiful daughter from a poor family, she said that she should be the daughter-in-law of the river god, and immediately gave a betrothal gift to marry her off.
He bathed her, sewed new silk clothes for her, lived alone, cultivated her character, and built a house for her by the river, hung up a thick red silk tent, and let the girl live in it.
He also slaughtered cows to make wine and prepared meals for her, which lasted for more than ten days.
When the time comes, everyone will decorate the floating equipment together, like a bed tent and pillow mat for a married daughter, let the girl sit on it, and let it float in the river.
It floated on the water at first, then sank after drifting for dozens of miles.
Families with beautiful women were afraid that the big witch would marry their daughters for the river god, so most of them took their daughters and fled far away.
So the city is becoming more and more empty, with fewer and fewer people and more poverty. This has been the case for a long time.
As the folk saying goes: If you don't marry the river god, the river will flood your fields and drown the people.
Ximen Bao said: When it is time to marry the River God, please invite the three elders, witches and elders to go to the river to see off the bride. You also want to come and tell me that I am going to see off the bride too.
Everyone said: Yes.
On that day, Ximen Bao went to the river to meet everyone.
The three elders, officials, gentry and fathers from the countryside all arrived, together with the people watching, a total of two to three thousand people.
The big witch was an old woman, seventy years old.
There were more than a dozen female disciples accompanying her, all wearing silk single clothes, standing behind the big witch.
Ximen Bao said: Call the wife of the river god to come over and see if she is beautiful.
The witches helped the bride out of the tent and came to Simon Leopard.
Ximen Leopard looked at it, then turned around and said to the three elders, the temple priest, the witch and the elders: This girl is not beautiful. I asked the big witch to go to the river and tell the river god that a beautiful girl needs to be replaced. She will be sent the day after tomorrow.
Let the soldiers pick up the big witch and throw her into the river.
After a while, Ximen Bao said: "Why has the big witch not come back after being gone for so long?"
The apprentice went to urge her.
Another disciple was thrown into the river.
After a while, he said again: "Why did my apprentice not come back for so long?"
Send another person to urge them!
Another disciple was thrown into the river.
A total of three apprentices were thrown into the river.
Ximen Leopard said: The witch and the apprentice are women and cannot report the matter. Please help me go in and report the matter to the river god.
Then he threw the three elders into the river.
Ximen Leopard stood with a pen on his head, bent over, facing the river and waited for a long time.
Elders, officials and onlookers were all very frightened.
Ximen Bao turned around and said, "What should I do if the witch and the three elders don't come back?"
I want to send Ting Yu and a wealthy gentleman in to urge them.
Ting Yu and the noble gentry all knelt on the ground and kowtowed, their heads were smashed, blood was flowing on the ground, and their faces were ashen.
Ximen Bao said: Well, wait for a while.
After staying for a while, Ximen Bao said: "Let's get up."
It depends on the situation. The river god has been a guest for too long. You all should leave here and go home.
The officials and people in Ye County were very afraid. From now on, they did not dare to marry the river god again.
Ximen Bao enlisted the people to dig twelve channels to divert water from the Zhang River to irrigate the farmland, and all the farmland was irrigated.
When digging canals, it is somewhat laborious for the common people to dig canals, and they are not very willing to do it.
Ximen Bao said: The people can enjoy their success with them, but they cannot plan to start a career with them.
Although my fathers and sons now think that I have brought hardship to them, a hundred years from now, I hope that my fathers and sons will think about what I said again.
Until now, the people there have benefited from the river water, and the people have become rich.
Twelve canals cross the imperial road. When the Han Dynasty was established, local officials believed that the bridges on the twelve canals cut off the imperial road and were very close to each other.
I want to merge the canals and merge the three canals into one section that flows through the Royal Road, and only build one bridge.
The people in Ye refused to listen to the opinions of local officials, believing that those channels were planned and dug by Mr. Ximen, and the laws and regulations of the virtuous chief could not be changed.
The local governor finally listened to everyone's opinions and gave up the plan to merge the canals.
Therefore, as Ximen Bao is the magistrate of Ye County, he is famous all over the world, and his kindness is passed down to future generations. Can we say that he is not a virtuous doctor?
Ancient books say: When Zi Chan governs the state of Zheng, the people cannot deceive him; when the son governs Shan father, the people cannot bear to deceive him; when Ximen Bao governs Ye County, the people dare not deceive him.
Who among the three of them has the best talents?
Those who study governance will be able to tell the difference.
summary:
Confucius stated that the Six Classics serve the same purpose in governing a country: "Li" regulates conduct, "Music" promotes harmony, "Book" records past deeds, "Poetry" expresses emotions, "Yi" explores cosmic changes, and "Spring and Autumn" discerns subtle meanings and right from wrong. Tai Shigong remarked on the vastness of truth, noting that concise words can resolve many troubles.

Chunyu Kun, a short, witty son-in-law of Qi, often served as an envoy without disgrace. During King Wei of Qi's reign, the king neglected state affairs, indulging in feasting and drinking, leading to invasions and national peril. No minister dared to advise. Chunyu Kun used an allegory of a great bird that neither flew nor cried for three years. King Wei understood, summoned all county chiefs, rewarded one, executed another, and repelled invaders, restoring Qi's prestige for 36 years. Later, when Chu invaded, Chunyu Kun was sent to Zhao for reinforcements with modest gifts. He laughed at a farmer praying for abundant harvests with meager offerings, prompting King Wei to increase the gifts. Zhao then sent 100,000 elite troops, causing Chu to withdraw. King Wei asked Chunyu Kun about his drinking capacity. Chunyu Kun explained that his drunkenness varied by context: fear made him drunk after one measure, while joy allowed him to drink eight measures. He warned against excess, as it leads to decline. King Wei ceased nightly drinking and appointed Chunyu Kun as a guest official.

Over a century later, You Meng, a tall Chu performer, used humor to advise King Zhuang. When the king wanted to bury his beloved horse with grand rites, You Meng suggested an even grander burial to expose the king's folly. King Zhuang relented and had the horse cooked. Later, You Meng impersonated the deceased prime minister Sun Shuao to advise King Zhuang. He highlighted Sun Shuao's poverty despite his integrity, leading the king to grant Sun's son land and households for ancestral worship.

Two centuries later, You Zhan, a short Qin performer, used wit to aid others. During a rainstorm, he joked about guards being wet while he was dry, leading Qin Shihuang to halve their duty. He also dissuaded the emperor from expanding hunting grounds and Qin Ershi from painting city walls, using humor to highlight impracticality.

Tai Shigong praised these three for their clever advice. Mr. Chu Shaosun added six more tales, including that of Guo Sheren, who helped a wet nurse avoid exile by prompting her to show reluctance, moving Emperor Wu to pity. Dongfang Shuo, a learned scholar, used humor to gain favor with Emperor Wu, often receiving rewards but spending them on marriages. He defended his behavior as "court reclusion" and advised against slander on his deathbed. Mr. Dong Guo advised General Wei Qing to gift gold to Empress Wang's parents, earning himself an official post. Other tales include a clever envoy who lost a swan but gained rewards, a prefect coached by a drunkard to credit the emperor for peace, and Ximen Bao, who stopped the practice of sacrificing girls to the River God by throwing the corrupt priests into the river, then dug irrigation canals that benefited the people for generations.

translation:
Tian Dan was a native of Di County and a sibling of the Tian family, King of Qi during the Warring States Period.
Tian Dan's cousin and Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng was a powerful figure in the local area, and his clan was strong and very popular.
When Chen She began to raise troops and claim to be the King of Chu, he sent Zhou Shi to capture and pacify the Wei region, and then marched north to Di County, which was defended.
Tian Dan pretended to tie up his own slave and led his young men to the county government, claiming to kill the guilty slave after meeting with the county magistrate.
When they saw the magistrate of Di County, they took the opportunity to kill him, and then summoned powerful officials and young people to say: "The princes from all over the country have rebelled against Qin and established themselves. Qi is a country established in ancient times, and I, Tian Dan, am a member of Qi Wang Tian's clan and should be the king."
So Tian Dan proclaimed himself King of Qi and raised troops to attack Zhou City.
After Zhou Shi's army withdrew, Tian Dan took the opportunity to lead his troops eastward, seize and pacify the land of Qi.
Qin general Zhang Han led his troops to besiege King Jiu of Wei in Linji. The situation was urgent, and King Wei sent people to Qi to ask for rescue. King Tian Dan of Qi led the army to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han let his soldiers and horses hold the coins in their mouths at night, and took advantage of the cover of night to launch a sneak attack. He defeated the Qi and Wei coalition forces and killed Tian Dan at the foot of Linji City.
Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong gathered the remaining troops of Tian Dan and fled eastward to Dong'a.
After the people of Qi heard the news that Tian Dan had died in battle, they supported Tian Jia, the younger brother of the former King of Qi Tian Jian, as King of Qi, Tian Jiao as prime minister, and Tian Jian as general, in order to resist the princes.
When Tian Rong fled to Dong'a, Zhang Han pursued and intercepted him.
Xiang Liang heard that Tian Rong was in critical condition, so he led his troops to Dong'a City and defeated Zhang Han in one fell swoop.
Zhang Han fled to the west, while Xiang Liang took advantage of the victory to pursue him.
However, Tian Rong was very angry about the fact that the Qi people made Tianjie the king of Qi, so he led his troops back and attacked and chased Qi King Tianjie. Tianjie fled to Chu State, and Prime Minister Tian Jiao fled to Zhao State. Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian had gone to Zhao State for help before, so he stayed in Zhao State and did not dare to go back.
Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi the king of Qi and appointed himself prime minister. Tian Heng was made a general and the land of Qi was pacified.
After Xiang Liang pursued Zhang Han, Zhang Han's army became increasingly powerful, so Xiang Liang sent envoys to inform Qi and Zhao, asking the two countries to jointly send troops to attack Zhang Han.
Tian Rong said: If Chu kills Tianjia and Zhao kills Tianjiao and Tianjian, we will send troops.
King Huai of Chu said: Tianjia is the king of our ally. He came to us when we were desperate. It is unethical to kill him.
Zhao State was also unwilling to trade with Qi State by killing Tian Jiao and Tian Jian Lai.
The people of Qi said: If the hand is bitten by a viper, the hand must be cut off; if the foot is bitten by the viper, the foot must be cut off.
Why?
Because if not, it will harm the whole body.
But now Tianjia, Tianjiao, and Tianjian are not flesh and blood relatives to Chu and Zhao. Why not kill them?
Moreover, if the Qin Dynasty succeeds in conquering the world, not only will we be humiliated, but even our ancestors' graves may have to be dug up.
Neither Chu nor Zhao were willing to obey Qi, and Qi was very angry and eventually refused to send troops to rescue.
Zhang Han indeed defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Liang. The Chu army fled eastward, and Zhang Han took the opportunity to cross the Yellow River and besiege Zhao's Julu.
Xiang Yu went to rescue Zhao State, and therefore resented Tian Rong very much.
Xiang Yu had already protected Zhao State and surrendered Zhang Han and other generals of the Qin Dynasty, so he went west to Xianyang to kill, destroyed the Qin Dynasty, and then divided the princes and kings among themselves. So he changed the title of King Qi Tianshi to King Jiaodong and ruled in Jimo.
Qi general Tian Du followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao and then marched into Guanzhong. Therefore, Xiang Yu made Tian Du the king of Qi and ruled in Linzi.
Tian An, the grandson of Tian Jian, the former Qi king, captured many cities in Jibei one after another when Xiang Yu was crossing the river to rescue Zhao, and then led his troops to surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu therefore made Tian An the king of Jibei, and his seat was Boyang.
Because Tian Rong disobeyed Xiang Yu and refused to send troops to assist Chu and Zhao in attacking the Qin Dynasty, he could not be crowned king; Zhao general Chen Yu was also not crowned king because of his dereliction of duty. Both of them resented Xiang Yu.
After Xiang Yu returned to Chu, the feudal princes also returned to their own fiefdoms. Tian Rong sent troops to help Chen Yu and asked him to rebel against Xiang Yu in Zhao. Tian Rong himself also sent troops to fight against Tian Du, who fled to Chu.
Tian Rong detained Qi Wang Tianshi and refused to allow him to go to the administrative office of Jiaodong.
Tian Shi's men said: Xiang Yu is powerful and ferocious, and as the king of Qi, you should go to your own kingdom of Jiaodong. If you don't go, there will be danger.
Tian Shi was very frightened, so he ran away to Jiaodong.
When Tian Rong learned about it, he was furious and led his men to chase King Qi Tianshi and killed him in Jimo. When he came back, he attacked Tian'an, the king of Jibei, and killed him.
Therefore, Tian Rong proclaimed himself the king of Qi and occupied all the lands of Sanqi.
After Xiang Yu heard the news, he was very angry, so he launched an army to attack Qi in the north.
King Tian Rong of Qi was severely defeated and fled to Pingyuan. The people of Pingyuan killed Tian Rong.
Afterwards, Xiang Yu burned and leveled the walls of Qi's capital, and massacred everyone he passed. The people of Qi couldn't bear it, so they all gathered to rebel against him.
Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered Qi's scattered soldiers and obtained tens of thousands of troops to counterattack Xiang Yu in Chengyang.
At this time, Liu Bang, king of Han, led the army of the princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng.
After Xiang Yu heard the news, he let go of the Qi army and went back, launching an attack on the Han soldiers in Pengcheng. Then there were many battles with the Han army, and they were locked in a stalemate in Xingyang.
Therefore, Tian Heng was able to regain the large and small cities of Qi again, and established Tian Guang, Tian Rong's son, as the king of Qi. Tian Heng assisted him as prime minister and arbitrarily ruled the country. All political affairs, no matter how big or small, were decided by Tian Heng.
Three years after Tian Heng pacified Qi, King Liu Bang of Han sent Li Shiqi to Qi to lobby Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng to submit to the Han Dynasty.
Tian Heng believed that this was feasible, so he lifted Qi's defense against the Han army in Lixia.
Han Xin, the general of the Han Dynasty, was going to attack Qi State eastward.
At first, Qi State sent troops led by Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to station in Lixia to resist the Han army. When the Han envoys arrived, they abandoned their war preparations to defend the city, allowed the soldiers to drink, and sent envoys to make peace with the Han Dynasty.
However, after the Han general Han Xin pacified Zhao and Yan, he used Kuai Tong's strategy to cross the plains and make a sudden attack, defeating the Qi garrison stationed in Lixia, and then invaded Linzi.
When Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng saw the sudden appearance of the Han army, they were very angry. They thought they had been betrayed by Li Sheng and immediately cooked and killed Li Sheng.
King Tian Guang of Qi fled east to Gaomi, Prime Minister Tian Heng fled to Boyang, Prime Minister Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji led the army to garrison in Jiaodong.
At this time, Chu State sent Long Qie to lead the army to rescue Qi State. Qi Wang Tian Guang and Long Qie met in Gaomi.
Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated the Qi-Chu coalition forces in Gaomi, killed Chu general Long Qie, and captured Qi King Tian Guang.
Han general Guan Ying continued the pursuit and captured Tian Guang, the prime minister of Qi.
Guan Ying continued to march and arrived at Boyang. When Tian Heng heard that King Qi Tian Guang was dead, he proclaimed himself King of Qi and turned to fight Guan Ying. Under Yingxia, Tian Heng's army was severely defeated by Guan Ying. Tian Heng fled to Liangdi and surrendered to Pengyue.
At this time, Peng Yue supported the army and remained neutral between Chu and Han, as if for the king of Han and for the king of Chu.
After Han Xin killed Chu General Long Qie, he ordered Cao Shen to continue marching to Jiaodong, where he defeated Tian Ji and killed him in battle. Han Xin also ordered Guan Ying to pursue Qi General Tian Sui, defeat him in Qiancheng and kill him.
In this way, Han Xin pacified Qi and wrote to Liu Bang, asking him to make himself the false king of Qi. Liu Bang also took advantage of the situation and made Han Xin the king of Qi.
More than a year later, Liu Bang, king of Han, destroyed Xiang Yu, proclaimed himself emperor, and made Pengyue King of Liang.
Tian Heng was afraid of being killed, so he led more than 500 of his men to flee into the sea and live on a small island.
After Liu Bang, the emperor of the Han Dynasty, heard the news, he thought that Brother Tian Heng had already pacified Qi State, and most of the wise men of Qi State were attached to him. If he was left to wander in the sea without being taken in, he might be in trouble in the future.
Therefore, he sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summoned him to the court. However, Tian Heng declined and said: I once cooked and killed your majesty's envoy Li Sheng. Now I heard that Li Sheng's younger brother Li Shang was a very talented Han Dynasty general. So I was very afraid and did not dare to go to Beijing to follow the imperial edict. I asked you to allow me to be a commoner and stay on this island.
When the envoy came back to report, Emperor Gaozu immediately issued an edict to Weiwei Li Shang: King Tian Heng of Qi is about to arrive in Beijing. Anyone who dares to touch his entourage will be executed immediately!
Then he sent an envoy with a talisman to inform Tian Heng of the imperial edict issued by the emperor to tell Li Shang's situation exactly as it was. He also said: "If Tian Heng comes to Beijing, the largest one can be made a king and the smallest one can be made a marquis; if he does not come, an army will be sent to kill him."
Tian Heng and his two retainers took the stage carriage to Luoyang.
Thirty miles away from Luoyang, there is a place called Corpse Township. On this day, Tian Heng and others came to this inn. Tian Heng said to the Han envoy: As a human minister, you should take a refreshing bath before paying homage to the emperor.
So he stayed.
Tian Heng said to his disciples: At first, I, Tian Heng, and the King of Han were both lonely kings in the south. But now that the King of Han has become the emperor, I, Tian Heng, have become a slave of the subjugated country. It would be a great shame to have to serve him in the north.
What's more, I killed someone's elder brother and then served the same master side by side with his younger brother. Even though he was afraid of the emperor's order and did not dare to touch me, wouldn't I feel ashamed in my heart?
Besides, the reason why His Majesty the Emperor summoned me to Beijing is just to see my face.
Now that the emperor is in Luoyang, if I cut off my head and gallop thirty miles, my appearance will not change, and I can still see what I look like.
After saying this, he committed suicide, ordered two retainers to hold his head in their hands, follow the envoys and fly into the court to report to Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty said: Hey! It’s really amazing to be able to say and do this!
Starting from ordinary people, three brothers became kings one after another. Aren't they worthy people?
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty couldn't help but shed tears for him. Then Emperor Gaozu appointed two of Tian Heng's retainers as captains, and sent two thousand soldiers to bury Tian Heng with the funeral rites of a prince.
After burying Tian Heng, two retainers dug a hole next to Tian Heng's tomb, then committed suicide, fell in the hole, and followed Tian Heng to death.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty heard about this, he was greatly surprised and thought that Tian Heng's disciples were all talented people.
Emperor Gaozu heard that Tian Heng's men still had 500 people on the island, and sent an envoy to summon them to Beijing.
After entering Beijing, these five hundred disciples heard that Tian Heng was dead, and they all committed suicide.
From this, we can understand that Brother Tian Heng is indeed a person who can be supported by the wise men.
Tai Shigong said: Kuai Tong's strategy was too powerful. It disturbed the state of Qi and made the Marquis of Huaiyin arrogant. As a result, these two people were killed.
Kuai Tong was good at talking about the long and short, and discussed the expediency of the Warring States Period. He wrote 81 articles.
Kuai Tong was friendly with An Qisheng, a native of Qi. An Qisheng once asked Xiang Yu for help, but Xiang Yu did not adopt his strategy.
Later, Xiang Yu wanted to reward these two people, but they refused to accept it and fled.
Tian Heng's high demeanor and integrity made the guests admire Gao Yi and follow Tian Heng to death. Isn't he an extremely virtuous person?
Therefore I enumerate his deeds.
It is true that there are people who are good at painting in the world, but no one painted the death of Tian Heng and his disciple Mu Yi. What is the reason?
summary:
Tian Dan, a member of the Qi royal family, proclaimed himself King of Qi during the Warring States period after killing the Di County magistrate. He raised troops but was later killed by Qin general Zhang Han at Linji. His cousin Tian Rong gathered the remnants and fled east. After Tian Dan's death, the Qi people installed Tian Jia as king, but Tian Rong, angered by this, attacked and drove Tian Jia and his ministers into exile. Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi king and appointed himself prime minister, with Tian Heng as general.

When Xiang Liang requested Qi's aid against Zhang Han, Tian Rong demanded the execution of the exiled Qi leaders as a condition, which Chu and Zhao refused. Qi withheld support, and Zhang Han subsequently defeated and killed Xiang Liang. Later, Xiang Yu, after defeating Qin, divided the territories, demoting Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong and installing Tian Du as King of Qi. Tian Rong, resentful at being excluded, attacked and killed Tian Du and Tian An, proclaiming himself King of Qi. Xiang Yu retaliated, defeating and killing Tian Rong. Tian Heng then gathered forces, regained Qi territory, and installed Tian Rong's son Tian Guang as king, with himself as de facto ruler.

Years later, Han king Liu Bang sent Li Shiqi to negotiate Qi's submission. Tian Heng agreed and lifted defenses, but Han general Han Xin launched a surprise attack, capturing Linzi. Believing Li Shiqi had betrayed them, Tian Guang and Tian Heng executed him. Han forces defeated Qi and Chu allies, killing General Long Qie and capturing Tian Guang. Tian Heng then proclaimed himself king but was defeated by Han forces and fled to Liang. After Liu Bang became emperor, Tian Heng, fearing execution, fled to an island with 500 followers. Summoned by the emperor, Tian Heng committed suicide near Luoyang, ashamed to serve under Liu Bang after having killed Li Shiqi. His two retainers and later the 500 followers also died, demonstrating his ability to inspire loyalty. The historian Sima Qian praised Tian Heng's virtue, noting that despite his death, no painter has depicted his story.
