Fan Ju recommended Zheng Anping to King Zhao of Qin who had protected him, and King Zhao appointed Zheng Anping as a general.
Fan Ju then distributed his family's belongings to repay all those who had helped him and were in dire straits.
He will definitely repay any small favor that is given to him by giving him a meal, and he will definitely retaliate against any small grudge that is given to him by glaring at him.
In the second year after Fan Ju was appointed Prime Minister of Qin, which was the 42nd year of King Zhao of Qin, Qin attacked Shaoqu and Gaoping in South Korea eastward and captured these two cities.
When King Zhao of Qin heard that Wei Qi was hiding in Lord Pingyuan's house, he thought that he must avenge Fan Ju, so he pretended to be friends and wrote a letter to Lord Pingyuan, saying: I have heard for a long time that you have noble moral character, and I hope to make a close friend with you who is as free as a common person. If you are willing to come and stay with me for a few days, I am willing to have fun and drink with you for ten days.
Lord Pingyuan was originally afraid of Qin, but after reading the letter, he thought that King Qin Zhao really wanted to make friends with him, so he went to Qin to meet King Qin Zhao.
After King Zhao had a banquet with Lord Pingyuan for a few days, he said to Lord Pingyuan: In the past, King Wen of Zhou was honored by Lu Shang as Taigong, and Duke Huan of Qi was honored as Zhongfu by Guan Yi. Now Mr. Fan can also be said to be my uncle.
Mr. Fan's enemy lives in your house, and I hope you will send someone to fetch his head; otherwise, I will not let you leave Hangu Pass.
Mr. Pingyuan said: When you are rich, you still have to make lowly friends, so as not to forget the friendship you had when you were lowly; when you are rich, you still make poor friends, so you don't forget the friendship you had when you were poor.
Wei Qi is my friend. Even if he is really in my house, I will never hand him over, let alone he is not in my house at all now.
King Zhao wrote another letter to the king of Zhao, saying: The king's younger brother is here in our country of Qin, and Mr. Fan's enemy Wei Qi is at the house of Lord Pingyuan.
The king will send someone to get his head quickly; otherwise, I will launch an army to attack the State of Zhao and not release the king's brother from Hangu Pass.
King Zhao Xiaocheng read the letter and sent soldiers to surround Pingyuanjun's house. In the crisis, Wei Qi escaped from Pingyuanjun's house overnight and met Yu Qing, the prime minister of Zhao.
Yu Qing estimated that King Zhao would not be able to persuade him, so he took off his seal and escaped from Zhao with Wei Qi. The two took a small road to escape. After much deliberation, they found no one in the vassal states who could take refuge in the situation, so they rushed back to Daliang, planning to defect to Chu through Lord Xinling.
When Lord Xinling heard the news, he hesitated and refused to receive them because he was afraid that Qin would come to his door. So he asked the people around him, "How is Yu Qing?"
Hou Ying was also there at that time, so he replied: Although it is difficult for others to understand people, it is not easy to understand others.
That Yu Qing wore straw sandals on his feet and an umbrella on his shoulder, and traveled far to the Kingdom of Zhao. When he met King Zhao for the first time, King Zhao gave him a pair of white jade stones and a hundred taels of gold.
At present, people all over the world are vying to understand Yu Qing's character.
When Wei Qi was desperate, he defected to Yu Qing. Yu Qing didn't take his high official's salary seriously at all, so he took off his seal, abandoned his title of Marquis of Wanhu, and ran away with Wei Qi.
How about someone who can take other people's difficulties as his own and come to you? How about this person?
Although it is difficult for people to be understood by others, it is also not easy to understand others!
After hearing these words, Lord Xinling felt deeply ashamed and hurriedly drove to the countryside to meet them.
But what Wei Qi heard was that Lord Xinling was not willing to receive him at first, so he cut his neck and committed suicide in anger.
King Zhao learned that Wei Qi had committed suicide, so he finally took his head and sent it to Qin.
King Zhao of Qin then released Lord Pingyuan back to Zhao.
In the forty-third year of King Zhao, the Qin State attacked Fenxing in South Korea, captured it, and built a city on Guangwu Mountain next to the Yellow River.
Five years later, King Zhao adopted Fan Ju's strategy and implemented a counterintuitive plan to deceive the State of Zhao. For this reason, the State of Zhao let Zhao Kuo, the son of Ma Fujun Zhao She, lead the army instead of Lian Po.
As a result, the Qin army defeated the Zhao army in Changping and then besieged Handan.
Soon afterwards, Fan Ju formed a grudge with Bai Qi, Lord of Wu'an, and slandered King Qin Zhao and killed Bai Qi.
So King Zhao of Qin appointed Zheng Anping and sent him to lead troops to attack Zhao.
Zheng Anping was surrounded by the Zhao army on the battlefield and was in critical condition. He led 20,000 Qin soldiers to surrender to Zhao.
Fan Ju knew that he could not escape the blame, so he knelt on the straw mat and begged for punishment.
According to the laws of the State of Qin, if an official is recommended and the recommended official commits a crime, then the recommender will also be punished according to the crime of the recommended official.
In this way, Fan Ju should be sentenced to the crime of arresting his father, mother, and wife.
However, King Qin Zhao was worried about hurting Fan Ju's feelings, so he ordered that anyone in the capital who dared to discuss Zheng Anping's affairs would be punished according to Zheng Anping's crimes.
At the same time, Fan Ju, the prime minister, was rewarded with richer food to make Fan Ju feel at ease.
In the next two years, Wang Ji served as the governor of Hedong County. He had colluded with the princes and was executed for breaking the law.
For this reason, Fan Ju became more and more depressed day by day.
Later, one day, King Zhao of Qin kept sighing when he went to court. Fan Ju stepped forward and said: I heard that it is a shame for the ministers to worry about the monarch, and it is a capital crime for the ministers to be humiliated.
Today, the king is so worried about government affairs. I beg to be punished for my crime.
King Zhao said: I heard that Chu’s iron swords are sharp but their singing and dancing skills are poor.
If the country's iron sword is sharp, its soldiers will be brave; if its singing and dancing skills are poor, its monarch's plans will be far-reaching.
Commanding brave soldiers with far-reaching strategies in mind, I am worried that Chu is planning how to attack Qin.
If you don't prepare in advance, you won't be able to cope with sudden changes. Now that Lord Wu An is dead, and Zheng Anping and others have rebelled, there are no generals who are good at fighting at home and there are many hostile countries abroad, so I am worried.
King Zhao of Qin said this to inspire and encourage Fan Ju.
But Fan Ju felt frightened after hearing this and couldn't think of anything to do.
Cai Ze learned about this situation and came to Qin from Yan State.
Cai Ze is from Yan State.
He traveled around the country to learn from his teachers and sought official positions from many princes, big and small, but received no credit.
Once he asked Tang Ju to meet him and said: I heard that Mr. Li Dui met him and said that he would take over the power of a country within a hundred days. Is this true?
Tang Ju replied: "This is the case."
Cai Ze said: What do you think of people like me?
Tang Ju looked at it carefully and then said with a smile: "Sir, he has an upturned nose, straight shoulders, protruding forehead, flat nose bridge, and bow-legged legs."
I heard that saints are not judged by their appearance, so I am probably talking about Mr.
Cai Ze knew that Tang Ju was joking with him, so he said, "I already have wealth. What I don't know is the length of life. I want to hear your opinion."
Tang Ju said: Sir, your life span will be forty-three years from now on.
Cai Ze smiled and expressed his gratitude and walked away. Then he said to his coachman: I am carrying rice and eating fat meat, driving the carriage at a gallop, holding a gold seal in my hand, and wearing a purple ribbon around my waist. I am highly respected in front of my master and enjoy glory and wealth. I should be satisfied for forty-three years.
He left Yan State and went to Zhao State, but was driven out by Zhao State.
Then he went to South Korea and Wei State. On the way, he encountered robbers who robbed him of his cooking utensils such as pots and tripods.
He heard that both Zheng Anping and Wang Ji recommended by Fan Ju had committed serious crimes in the Qin State. Fan Ju felt ashamed and could not lift his head, so Cai Ze went west to the Qin State.
He was going to visit King Zhao of Qin. He first sent someone to make a speech in front of Fan Ju to provoke Fan Ju, saying: Cai Ze, a guest from the state of Yan, is a wise and eloquent man with extraordinary knowledge and eloquence in the world.
As soon as he sees the King of Qin, the King of Qin will definitely put you in trouble and deprive you of your power.
Fan Ju heard these words and said: I am familiar with the affairs of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties and the theories of various schools of thought. I can convince many people with their eloquent words. How can this person embarrass me and take away my power?
So he sent someone to summon Cai Ze.
Cai Ze came in and bowed to Fan Ju.
Fan Ju was unhappy at first. When he met Cai Ze and saw how arrogant he was, Fan Ju reprimanded him and said, "You once threatened to replace me as Qin's prime minister. Has this ever happened to you?" Cai Ze replied: Yes.
Fan Ju said: Let me hear what you have to say. Cai Ze said: Yo!
Why are you so slow to understand the problem? The four seasons of spring, summer, autumn and winter change in a year, and each one completes its mission and then recedes automatically.
All parts of a person's body are strong, his hands and feet are nimble, his ears can hear clearly, his eyes can see clearly, and his mind is intelligent. Isn't this the scholar's wish? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze said: He is based on benevolence, upholds justice, promotes the right path, spreads kindness, and is willing to realize his ambitions in the world. People in the world support, love, respect and admire him, and all hope to make him a monarch. Isn't this what a wise and eloquent person expects? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze also said: He who is in a position of wealth and glory, governs everything so that everything can be in its proper place; lives a long life, spends his life safely without dying; the world inherits his tradition, sticks to his career, and passes it on forever; his reputation is in perfect harmony with reality, his kindness is extended thousands of miles away, and he is praised from generation to generation as never ending and as long as heaven and earth: Isn't this the effect of promoting the right way and spreading kindness and the auspicious and good deeds mentioned by the saints? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze said: As for Shang Yang of Qin, Wu Qi of Chu, and Wen Zhong, the great official of Yue, are their tragic endings enviable?
Fan Ju knew that Cai Ze wanted to use these words to block his mouth and convince himself, so he deliberately quibbled and said: Why not?
That Gongsun Yang served Qin Xiaogong without any second thoughts throughout his life. He devoted himself to the public affairs and did not care about himself. He set up tortures with knives and saws to suppress treachery and evil, and implemented rewards and punishments to achieve peace in the country. He showed his loyalty and true feelings, suffered resentment and accusations, deceived old friends, captured Wei Gongzi Yan, stabilized the country of Qin, and benefited the people. Finally, he captured enemy generals for Qin, defeated the enemy troops, and opened up the territory thousands of miles away.
Wu Qi served the king of Chu, so that his private affairs could not harm the public, his loyal ministers could not be blocked by treacherous and slanderous words, he did not agree with everyone's opinions, he was scrupulous in his work and protected himself, he did not change his actions because of danger, he insisted on righteousness and did not avoid disasters. In this way, in order for the monarch to achieve hegemony and make the country strong, he will never avoid disasters and dangers.
The official Wen Zhong serves the King of Yue. Even if the monarch encounters difficulties and humiliation, he still remains loyal and unyielding.
These three gentlemen are originally standards of morality and examples of loyalty and integrity.
Therefore, a gentleman who suffers death for the sake of righteousness regards death as home; being humiliated while alive is not as glorious as death.
Scholars should have the ambition to sacrifice their lives to achieve fame. As long as it is for the sake of righteousness, there will be no regrets even if they die.
Why not?
Cai Ze said: A wise monarch and virtuous ministers are a great blessing to the world; a wise monarch and upright ministers are a blessing to a country; a loving father, a filial son, an honest husband and a loyal wife are a blessing to a family.
Therefore, Bi Gan was loyal but could not save the Yin Dynasty; Zixu was resourceful but could not save the Wu Kingdom; Shen Sheng was filial but the Jin Kingdom was in chaos.
These are all examples of loyal ministers and filial sons, but the country was destroyed and in chaos. Why is this?
It is because there are no wise kings or virtuous fathers to listen to their voices, so everyone in the world thinks that such kings and fathers are shameful, and pities their ministers and sons who sympathize with them.
Now it seems that Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Dafu Wenzhong were right as ministers; their kings were wrong.
So the world says that these three gentlemen achieved great achievements but received no good rewards. Is it because they envy them for not being noticed by the king and dying innocently?
If only death can establish a reputation for loyalty, then Wei Zi cannot be called a benevolent person, Confucius cannot be called a saint, and Guan Zhong cannot be called a great man.
If people want to make great achievements, don’t they expect their achievements to be there?
It is the best to be able to preserve one's own life, achievements and reputation.
If one's fame can be followed by future generations but one's own life cannot be saved, this is second-rate.
It is inferior to someone whose reputation is insulted but whose life is saved.
At this point, Fan Ju praised the words well.
Cai Ze seized some opportunities and took the opportunity to say: Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Wen Zhong, as ministers of others, are loyal to the monarch and have achieved great achievements. This is worthy of people's envy. But when Hong Yao served King Zhou Wen and Zhou Gongdan assisted King Zhou Cheng, weren't they loyal and full of wisdom?
From the perspective of the relationship between the monarch and his ministers, who is more enviable compared to Shang Yang, Wu Qi, Wen Zhong, Hong Yao, and Zhou Gongdan? Fan Ju said: Shang Yang and Wu Qi were not as good at writing as Hong Yao and Zhou Gongdan.
Cai Ze said: In this case, the monarch you serve is kind and benevolent, appoints loyal ministers, treats former friends with kindness and honesty, his virtuous and intelligent people can be as close as glue and lacquer to those talented people, he has deep feelings for people, and will not abandon the ministers who have done meritorious service for him. Who is better than King Zhao of Qin, Duke Xiao of Qin, King Mou of Chu, and King of Yue?
Fan Ju said: There is no way to know what it will be like.
Cai Ze said: Now your monarch is close to loyal ministers, but not more than Qin Xiaogong, Chu Yu Wang, and Yue Wang. You use your wisdom to help the monarch solve crises, rectify the country, quell rebellions, strengthen the military, eliminate troubles, eliminate disasters, expand the territory, increase grain, make the country rich and powerful, the people are rich, strengthen the power of the ruler, and improve the country. The status of the family shows the nobility of the royal family. No prince in the world dares to deceive or invade your king. The power of the monarch can intimidate any prince in the four seas. His achievements are demonstrated thousands of miles away. His reputation is like an eternal glory that will be passed down through the ages. In these aspects, how do you compare with Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Dafu Wenzhong? Fan Ju said: I can't compare.
Cai Ze said: Today, the king is not as good as Duke Xiao of Qin, King Mou of Chu, and King Goujian of Yue in terms of being close to his loyal ministers and not forgetting his original friends. And the credit you have created and the favor, trust, and intimacy you have received from the monarch are not as much as those of Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Wen Zhong, but what you have gained You have a lot of salary and a very noble position. Your personal wealth exceeds that of Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Wen Zhong. If you don't know how to abdicate voluntarily, I am afraid that the disaster you will cause in the future will be more serious than those three people. I secretly feel that you are already very dangerous.
As the saying goes, the sun will gradually tilt when it reaches the central position, and the moon will begin to wane after it becomes full.
Everything will begin to decline after reaching its peak. This is a universal law that exists between heaven and earth.
Advancing, retreating, expanding and contracting, changing with the changing times, this is the common sense adhered to by the saints in ancient times.
Therefore, when the country is politically clear, he will become an official, and when the country is politically dark, he will live in seclusion.
The sage said that flying like a dragon into the sky is more conducive to meeting virtuous people. Wealth and noble status acquired through unethical means seem to me like clouds floating in the sky.
Now that your revenge has been avenged, the kindness you have received has been repaid, and all your wishes have been realized, but you have no strategy to deal with the changes. Privately, I feel that you are very unwise.
Moreover, for animals like jadeite, swans, rhinoceros, and elephants, their location can be said to be far away from accidental death. The reason for their death is due to being confused by the bait.
The wisdom of people like Su Qin and Zhibo was enough to prevent them from being insulted and away from death. However, the reason why they were still insulted and died was because they were tempted by interests.
It is precisely because of this that the ancient saints created etiquette to control their desires, ask for limited amounts from the people, let the people serve according to the seasons, and have a certain degree of restraint in collecting property, so that their will will not be complacent, their behavior will not be proud, and they will always comply with morality without losing morality, so the world can be passed down from generation to generation.
In the past, Duke Huan of Qi made nine alliances with the princes, which immediately brought the world back to orthodoxy. However, when he met at Kuiqiu to make an alliance, he had a sense of pride and complacency in his heart, and nine princes opposed him.
The soldiers under King Wu Fu Chai could not find any rival among the princes in the world. He relied on his own bravery and strength to look down on the princes and bullied the two countries of Qi and Jin. Therefore, he was killed and Wu was destroyed.
Xia Yu and Taishi Po were both men who could shock and frighten the entire army with just one roar, but in the end they both died at the hands of ordinary people.
This is all because after they are in an extremely powerful position, they no longer care about conventional morality and affairs, they no longer maintain a modest and prudent attitude, and they cannot be frugal and restrain themselves from the disasters they cause.
Shang Yang helped Qin Xiaogong promulgate a clear decree, which banned the source of evil and evil. Honorable titles must be used for rewards, and those who commit crimes must be punished. He unified the standard units of weight, length, and capacity, adjusted the relationship between the weight and weight of goods circulation, and leveled the crisscrossing ridges in the fields, so that the people of Qin could be more secure. Production is carried out in a fixed area, which unifies the living customs of the people and encourages the people to actively engage in agricultural production. If a family has more than two adult men, they must live separately. People work hard to cultivate the fields, store food, and practice military battle formations in peacetime. Therefore, when the army is deployed, it can expand its territory, and when the army rests, it can make the country rich. Therefore, Qin has no rivals among the princes in the world, and has established a high prestige among the princes, which has laid the foundation for Qin's great achievements.
After the great deeds were completed, Shang Yang was eventually punished by having his car broken.
The land of Chu was thousands of miles wide, and there were more than a million soldiers holding halberds. However, Bai Qi led tens of thousands of Qin troops to fight against Chu. In the first battle, he occupied Yan and Ying of Chu, burned Yiling, and after another battle, he went south and annexed Shu and Hanzhong.
Later, he crossed the two countries of Korea and Wei to attack the powerful Zhao State, killed Ma Fujun's son in the north, and massacred more than 400,000 soldiers in Changping. The blood of the Zhao army flowed into a river, and the sound of the flowing blood was like roaring thunder. Then he entered the Zhao State and besieged Handan, laying the foundation for Qin to become an emperor.
Chu and Zhao are the two most powerful states among the princes in the world, and they are also the enemies of Qin. Since the end of the war, the reason why Chu and Zhao were afraid of surrender and did not dare to attack Qin was because of Bai Qi's power.
Bai Qi personally led his troops to conquer more than seventy cities. After establishing his achievements, he was eventually given a sword to commit suicide and died in Duyou.
Wu Qi helped King Chu Mourning to establish laws, weaken the excessive power in the hands of ministers, reduce the ministers' overly exalted status, remove incompetent officials, abolish officials of no use, eliminate secret officials, eliminate private requests, unify the life and customs of Chu State, prohibit people from wandering around without engaging in production, reward farming efforts, and With brave people and soldiers, they subdued Yang Yue to the south and annexed Chen and Cai to the north. They exposed the futility of the vertical and horizontal policies, so that those who lobbied the Chu State had no chance to speak. They prohibited the ministers from forming cliques and encouraged the people to engage in production. They stabilized the Chu State's politics, shocked the world with its military strength, and made all the vassal states surrender.
After the work was completed, Wu Qi was dismembered and died.
Wen Zhong planned far-reaching strategies for the king of Yue, avoiding the imminent crisis of being trapped in Kuaiji and making the situation of danger continue to exist. He used the humiliation suffered by the king and ministers to seek the glory of revenge, reclaimed the wasteland full of weeds, recruited people into the city, and opened up farmland. Come to grow food, bring people from all directions under the command of the King of Yue, unite the power from top to bottom, assist a virtuous monarch like Gou Jian, and finally avenge the hatred of Wu King Fu Chai for destroying Yue, finally eliminate the powerful Wu State, and make the Yue State the overlord of the generation.
Wen Zhong's contribution has been so obvious and confirmed, but Gou Jian finally betrayed morality and killed him.
The four worthy people I mentioned did not leave after the establishment of their merits, and they suffered such disasters.
This is what is called being able to stretch but not bend, being able to advance but not retreat.
Fan Li understood this truth, so he avoided the secular world with detachment and stayed in front of his Tao Zhugong for a long time.
Haven't you seen those people gambling?
Sometimes you have to make a single bet to make a profit, and sometimes you have to divide your bets into several times to make a profit. These are all things you know very well.
Now that you are the Prime Minister of Qin, you don’t have to leave your seat to make plans, and you don’t have to leave the court to formulate strategies. You can control and command the princes while sitting in your seat, and exert your interests on the Sanchuan area, thereby increasing the strength of Yiyang, cutting off the dangerous road to Yangchang Ban, blocking the main transportation road to Taihang Mountain, and cutting off the Fan family and the Bank of China. These passages to the territories of South Korea and Wei made it impossible for those six countries to implement the policy of joint control. The plank roads built were a thousand miles long, leading directly to Shu and Hanzhong areas, making all the princes in the world fear Qin from the bottom of their hearts.
If you don't know how to retire under such circumstances, you will be like Shang Yang, Bai Qi, and Wen Zhong.
I have heard this saying, if you look at the surface of the water as a mirror, you can see your own face; if you look at others as a mirror, you can know whether your future will be good or bad.
"The Book" says that when the work has been completed, it cannot stay for a long time.
The disaster of the four people mentioned above is already a good mirror. Why should you bear it?
Why don't you take this opportunity to hand over your seal and give up your throne to a capable person to be the prime minister of Qin? After you retire, you can live on the green mountains and enjoy the flowing water leisurely. You will definitely get a reputation as honest and honest like Boyi, and you will be your own Fan Ju for a long time.
So which situation do you think is better?
If you are unwilling to leave on your own initiative and are unable to make a decision on your own because of hesitation, then you will inevitably invite disasters like the four people mentioned above.
"Yi" says that when a dragon reaches its peak, it must guard against arrogance and impetuosity, otherwise it will regret it. This refers to the situation of being able to go up but not down, being able to stretch but not bend, and being able to advance but not retreat.
So I hope you will seriously consider this issue!
Fan Ju said: Well said.
I heard someone say that if a person's desires are never satisfied, he will eventually lose what he wants to achieve; if a person already has a lot but doesn't know how to stop, he will lose what he already has.
I am fortunate to have received your advice from my husband, and I respectfully accept your opinion.
So Cai Ze was invited to sit at the banquet and treated as a distinguished guest.
A few days later, Fan Ju went to court and spoke to King Zhao of Qin: There is a guest named Cai Ze who has just come from the east of Xiaoshan. This man is a very eloquent man. He knows the affairs of the three kings, the achievements of the five hegemons and the changes in the world. He can be entrusted with the great affairs of Qin.
I have seen many wise men, but no one can catch up with him, and neither am I.
I take the liberty of reporting this to you.
King Zhao of Qin summoned Cai Ze. After talking to him, he liked him very much and granted him the position of guest minister.
Fan Ju took the opportunity to plead for illness and requested that Xiangyin be sent back.
King Qin Zhao still tried his best to make him a deacon, so Fan Ju said that he was seriously ill.
Fan Ju was dismissed from his position as prime minister. When King Zhao first summoned Cai Ze, he appreciated his plan and appointed Cai Ze as the prime minister of Qin. Xiangdong destroyed the Zhou Dynasty.
Cai Ze had been the prime minister of Qin for a few months, but someone slandered him. He was afraid of being killed, so he pretended to be sick and sent him back to Xiangyin. He was given the title Gangchengjun.
Cai Ze lived in Qin for more than ten years and served King Zhao, King Xiaowen and King Zhuang Xiang.
Finally, he served Qin Shihuang and served as an envoy to Yan. Three years later, Prince Dan of Yan went to Qin as a hostage.
Tai Shigong said: Han Feizi said: People with long sleeves are good at dancing, and people with more money are good at doing business.
This is very true! Fan Ju and Cai Ze are what people call a generation of debaters. However, those who lobbied the princes until they were gray-haired and did not find a confidant did not have poor strategies, but that the conditions for the lobbying to be effective were insufficient.
When the two of them settled in the Qin State, they were able to achieve the status of prime minister one after another, and their fame spread throughout the world. The reason was that the country's strength was different.
But there are also occasional opportunities for debaters. Many talented people like Fan Ju and Cai Ze do not give full play to their talents because they have no opportunities. How can these people say everything?
However, if the two of them do not encounter difficult situations, how can they work hard and make a difference?
summary:
Fan Ju, a man of eloquence, initially sought to serve the King of Wei but was too poor to fund his journey. He first served under Xu Jia, a senior official in Wei. When Xu Jia was sent as an envoy to Qi, Fan Ju accompanied him. King Qi Xiang, impressed by Fan Ju's eloquence, sent him gifts of gold, beef, and wine, which Fan Ju refused. Xu Jia suspected Fan Ju had betrayed Wei secrets to Qi and reported this to the Wei prime minister, Wei Qi. Wei Qi had Fan Ju beaten severely, breaking his ribs and teeth, then wrapped him in a mat and threw him in a toilet, where drunken guests urinated on him. Fan Ju convinced a guard to let him escape, and later hid with the help of Zheng Anping, changing his name to Zhang Lu.

When King Zhao of Qin sent envoy Wang Ji to Wei, Zheng Anping arranged a secret meeting between Fan Ju and Wang Ji. Recognizing Fan Ju's talent, Wang Ji took him to Qin. On the way, they encountered Marquis Rang, the powerful Qin prime minister, but Fan Ju hid to avoid detection. Once in Qin, Wang Ji recommended Fan Ju to King Zhao, but the king was skeptical and housed Fan Ju poorly for over a year. During this time, Qin had expanded its territory significantly, but the king distrusted lobbyists. Marquis Rang and other relatives of the queen mother held immense power, with private wealth exceeding the state's.

Fan Ju wrote to King Zhao, arguing that a wise ruler rewards merit and talent, and that he was willing to die if his advice proved useless. Impressed, King Zhao summoned Fan Ju. At the palace, Fan Ju deliberately provoked the king by claiming Qin only had a queen mother and Marquis Rang, not a king. King Zhao apologized for the delay and sought Fan Ju's counsel. After three rounds of questioning, Fan Ju finally spoke, citing historical examples to emphasize the importance of trust and the dangers of powerful relatives. He outlined a strategy of befriending distant states and attacking nearby ones, starting with Han and Wei, to consolidate Qin's power.

King Zhao appointed Fan Ju as a guest minister and followed his advice, capturing cities from Wei and Han. Over time, Fan Ju gained the king's trust and exposed the overreach of the queen mother and Marquis Rang, leading to their expulsion. Fan Ju became prime minister, and the king granted him the title of Marquis Ying. When Xu Jia later visited Qin as an envoy, Fan Ju humiliated him for past wrongs but spared his life due to a gift of a robe. Fan Ju also recommended Zheng Anping as a general and repaid all who had helped him.

However, Fan Ju's later years were troubled. Zheng Anping surrendered to Zhao, and Wang Ji was executed for colluding with other states. King Zhao expressed concern about Qin's lack of capable generals, unsettling Fan Ju. Cai Ze, a strategist from Yan, then arrived and warned Fan Ju of the dangers of holding power too long, citing historical figures like Shang Yang and Wu Qi who died after their achievements. Fan Ju heeded the advice and recommended Cai Ze to King Zhao, eventually resigning as prime minister. Cai Ze served briefly but also resigned due to slander, living on in Qin for many years.

The historian comments that Fan Ju and Cai泽 succeeded in Qin due to the state's strength and their own perseverance through hardship, noting that many talented individuals fail without such opportunities.

translation:
Meng Tian, ​​his ancestor was from Qi State.
Meng Tian's grandfather, Meng Ao, came to Qin from Qi to serve King Qin Zhao, and became a high official.
In the first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, Meng Ao served as the general of the Qin State, attacked South Korea, occupied Chenggao and Xingyang, and established Sanchuan County.
In the second year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, Meng Ao attacked Zhao and captured thirty-seven cities.
In the third year of Qin Shihuang's reign, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities.
In the fifth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao attacked Wei, captured twenty cities, and established Dongjun.
In the seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao passed away.
Meng Ao's son was named Meng Wu, and Meng Wu's son was named Meng Tian.
Meng Tian once worked in prison litigation records and was responsible for managing relevant documents and prison litigation files.
In the 23rd year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Wu served as a general of the Qin State. He and Wang Jian attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Yan.
In the twenty-fourth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Wu attacked Chu State again and captured the King of Chu.
Meng Tian's younger brother is called Meng Yi.
In the twenty-sixth year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Tian became a general of the Qin State because of his background. He led his troops to attack the Qi State and defeated the Qi army. He was given the official position of internal history.
After the Qin State annexed the world, it sent Meng Tian to lead a huge army of 300,000 people to drive away the Rong and Di to the north and recover the land south of the Yellow River.
The Great Wall was built, taking advantage of the geographical situation, and setting up fortresses, stretching from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east, stretching for more than 10,000 miles.
So he crossed the Yellow River, occupied Yangshan Mountain, and extended zigzag to the north.
In the scorching sun, frost, wind and rain, I have been stationed in Shangjun for more than ten years.
At this time, Meng Tian's reputation shocked the Xiongnu.
Qin Shihuang particularly respected and admired the Meng family, trusting and appreciating their talents.
Therefore, he became close to Meng Yi and became the highest official. When he went out, he would ride in the same carriage with the First Emperor, and when he returned to the court, he would serve the king.
Meng Tian was responsible for military responsibilities outside the country, while Meng Yi often made suggestions in the court and was known as a loyal minister. Therefore, even other generals did not dare to compete with them for favor.
Zhao Gao is an estranged relative of King Zhao's family.
The Zhao Gao brothers were all castrated at birth and became eunuchs. His mother was also punished for breaking the law, so her status was low for generations.
When the King of Qin heard that Zhao Gao was very capable and proficient in criminal and prison laws, he promoted him to the post of Zhongche Mansion Order.
Zhao Gao then served his son Hu Hai privately and taught him how to decide lawsuits.
Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, and King Qin asked Meng Yi to punish him in accordance with the law.
Meng Yi did not dare to bend the law. According to the law, he should be sentenced to death and deprived of his official status.
The First Emperor pardoned Zhao Gao because of his diligence and hard work. His original official position was restored.
The First Emperor planned to tour the world, passing through Jiuyuan County and going directly to Ganquan Palace. He sent Meng Tian to open a road for him, from Jiuyuan to Ganquan, opening up the mountains and filling in the deep valleys, a total length of 1,800 miles.
However, the passage was not completed.
In the winter of the thirty-seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, the royal chariot went out on a tour of Kuaiji, leaning on the sea, heading north to Langye.
He got seriously ill halfway through, so Meng Yi turned back to pray to the gods of mountains and rivers.
Before Meng Yi could return, the First Emperor walked to the sand dunes and died. The news of the death of the First Emperor was blocked, and none of the civil and military officials knew about it.
At this time, Prime Minister Li Si, Prince Hu Hai, and Zhao Gao, the magistrate of CRRC, often served Qin Shihuang.
Zhao Gao usually received Hu Hai's favor and planned to appoint Hu Hai to inherit the throne. However, he resented Meng Yi for punishing him according to the law instead of protecting him, so he wanted to kill him.
He secretly planned with Prime Minister Li Si and Prince Hu Hai to make Hu Hai the crown prince.
After the crown prince was established, he sent envoys to fabricate charges and prepare the death penalty for Prince Fusu and Meng Tian.
After Fusu committed suicide, Mengtian became suspicious and asked for an appeal.
The envoy handed Meng Tian over to the officials in charge, and sent someone else to take over his duties.
Hu Hai used Li Si's retainers as military guards.
When the envoy came back to report, Hu Hai had heard the news of Fusu's death and immediately planned to release Meng Tian.
Zhao Gao was afraid that the Meng family would become powerful again and resented them.
Meng Yi returned after praying to the gods of the mountains and rivers. Zhao Gao took the opportunity to express his loyalty to Hu Hai and wanted to eradicate the Meng brothers, so he said to Hu Hai: I heard that the late emperor selected talents and made you the crown prince a long time ago, but Meng Yi tried to dissuade him and said: No.
If he knows that you are wise and capable and delays your registration for a long time, then he is being unfaithful and deceiving the late Emperor.
In my ignorant opinion, it is better to kill him. Hu Hai obeyed Zhao Gao's words and imprisoned Meng Yi in Daijun.
Before that, Meng Tian had been imprisoned in Yang Zhou.
After Qin Shihuang's hearse returned to Xianyang and was buried, the prince ascended the throne and became the second emperor. Zhao Gao gained the most favor and slandered the Meng family day and night, collecting their crimes, reporting and impeaching them.
Ziying advised: I heard that in the past, King Zhao Qian killed his wise minister Li Mu and appointed Yan Ju, King Yan secretly adopted Jing Ke's strategy and betrayed Qin's alliance, and King Jian of Qi killed his loyal ministers from the previous generation and adopted the strategy of later victory.
These three kings each lost their country and brought great disaster to themselves because of changing the old rules.
Now the Meng brothers are ministers and counselors of the Qin State, and the monarch intends to abandon them all at once. I think it is not allowed. I have heard that people who think about problems hastily cannot govern the country, and people who are arbitrary and self-righteous cannot protect the monarch.
Killing loyal ministers and appointing those without moral integrity will make the ministers unable to trust each other internally and weaken the fighting spirit of the soldiers externally. I think it is not allowed.
Hu Hai couldn't listen to Ziying's advice.
However, he sent Yushi Qugong to take a post to Dai County and ordered Meng Yi to say: "First of all, you wanted to appoint a prince, but you blocked it. Now the prime minister thinks that you are disloyal and your crime has implicated your family. I can't bear it, so I will grant you suicide. You are very lucky."
Think about it again and again!
Meng Yi replied: If you think that I cannot win the favor of the late Lord, then by serving as an official and a eunuch when I was young, I was able to gain favor until the late Lord passed away. It can be said that I was able to comply with the will of the late Lord.
If you think that I don't understand the prince's talents, then only the prince can accompany the late lord and travel around the world. Compared with other princes, there is a huge difference. I have no doubts.
The First Master's appointment of the prince was a result of many years of careful consideration. What else can I dare to say and what strategies can I dare to devise?
This is not an excuse for me to avoid the death penalty. I am just afraid that I will be implicated and dishonor the reputation of my late lord. I hope the doctor will seriously consider this and let me die as a result of the crime I deserve.
Moreover, the fulfillment of laws and regulations is what morality advocates; severe punishment and killing are not tolerated by morality.
In the past, Duke Mu of Qin killed Sanliang of the Che family and buried him, and sentenced Baili Xi to an undeserved crime. Therefore, he was given the title of "Miao" after his death.
King Zhaoxiang killed Bai Qi, Lord Wu'an, and King Ping of Chu killed Wu She.
King Wu Fu Chai killed Wu Zixu.
These four kings all made serious mistakes and were criticized by people all over the world, thinking that their kings were unwise. Therefore, he had a bad reputation among the princely states.
Therefore, it is said: Those who govern the country with morality will not kill innocent subjects, and punishment will not be imposed on innocent people.
I hope the doctor will seriously consider it!
The envoy knew Hu Hai's intention and refused to listen to Meng Yi's complaint, so he killed him.
The second emperor sent an envoy to Yang Zhou again and ordered Meng Tian to say: "You have committed too many sins, and your brother Meng Yi has committed a serious crime and will implicate you according to the law."
Meng Tian said: From my ancestors to their descendants, it has been three generations since I accumulated great achievements and established prestige for the Qin State.
Now I lead more than 300,000 troops. Even though I am imprisoned, I am powerful enough to rebel. However, I knew that I would definitely die, but I persisted in my integrity. I did not dare to insult the teachings of my ancestors, and I did not dare to forget the grace of my late lord.
Once upon a time, King Cheng of Zhou had just ascended the throne and could not completely break away from the child's sling and cloth bag. Duke Ji Dan of Zhou carried King Cheng on his back to accept the audience of the ministers, and finally brought peace to the world.
When King Cheng's condition became serious and dangerous, Gongdan cut off his own nails and sank them into the Yellow River, praying and saying: "The king is young and ignorant. This is because I am in power. If there is any fault or disaster, I should bear the punishment."
Just write down these prayers and store them in the archives. This can be said to be very honest.
When King Cheng was able to govern the country in person, some treacherous ministers spread rumors: Duke Zhou had been planning to cause rebellion for a long time. If the king was not on guard, something big would happen.
When King Cheng heard this, he became furious and Duke Zhou fled to Chu.
King Cheng went to the archives to review the files and found Zhou Gongdan's prayer book. He shed tears and said: Who said Zhou Gongdan wanted to cause chaos!
Kill the minister who spread the rumors and caused trouble, and invite Duke Zhou to return.
Therefore, the "Book of Zhou" says: We must inquire from multiple parties and review repeatedly.
Now our Meng clan has had no two minds from generation to generation, but things ended up like this. This must be because the ministers who planned the rebellion rebelled and deceived the emperor.
King Zhou Cheng made mistakes but was able to correct his mistakes and finally made the Zhou Dynasty prosperous; Xia Jie killed Guan Longfeng, and Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan without regrets, and finally died.
Therefore, I say that if you make mistakes, you can correct them and cheer up. If you listen to others' advice, you can be aware of them and be vigilant. These are the principles for a sage king to govern his country.
In general, the words I say are not to evade responsibility, but to die with loyal advice. I hope that Your Majesty will thoughtfully find the correct path to follow for the people of Li.
The envoy said: I accepted the order to impose punishment on the general, but I dare not report the general's words to the emperor.
Meng Tian sighed heavily and said: What crime have I committed against God that I should be executed for no fault of my own?
After a long time, he slowly said: My sin should have been punished by death.
Starting from Lintao and continuing to Liaodong, the Great Wall was built and trenches were dug for more than 10,000 miles. Is there no place where the earth's veins are cut off in the middle?
This is my sin.
So he swallowed poison and committed suicide.
Tai Shigong said: I went to the northern border and returned from the straight road. Along the way, I observed the Great Wall and frontier fortresses built by Meng Tian for the country. He excavated mountains, filled deep valleys, and connected the straight road. I originally did not pay attention to the people's manpower and material resources.
When the Qin State had just wiped out the other princes, the people of the world had not yet settled down, and the wounds had not yet healed. As a famous general, Meng Tian did not try his best to admonish and relieve the people's emergencies, provide care for the elderly, raise orphans, and devote himself to the work of making the people live a stable life. Instead, he catered to the wishes of the First Emperor and built the Great Wall on a large scale. Isn't it natural that their brothers were killed?
Where is the sin of digging up the earth's veins?
summary:
Meng Tian, a Qin general, hailed from Qi through his grandfather Meng Ao, who served Qin under King Zhao and later as a general under King Zhuangxiang and the First Emperor, conquering territories in Han, Zhao, and Wei before his death in 7 BCE. Meng Tian’s father, Meng Wu, also a general, defeated Chu alongside Wang Jian. Meng Tian began as a legal clerk, became a general in 26 BCE, and led 300,000 troops to expel northern nomads, reclaim land south of the Yellow River, and construct the Great Wall from Lintao to Liaodong. He garrisoned Shangjun for over a decade, intimidating the Xiongnu. His brother Meng Yi served as a trusted advisor to the First Emperor.

Zhao Gao, a eunuch of Zhao royal descent, rose to favor due to legal expertise, teaching Prince Hu Hai. When Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, Meng Yi sentenced him to death, but the First Emperor pardoned him. During the First Emperor’s fatal illness in 37 BCE, Meng Yi was sent to pray; after the emperor’s death, Zhao Gao conspired with Li Si and Hu Hai to install Hu Hai as crown prince, fabricating charges against Fusu and Meng Tian. Fusu committed suicide; Meng Tian was imprisoned. Zhao Gao, fearing the Meng family’s resurgence, falsely accused Meng Yi of opposing Hu Hai’s appointment, leading to his imprisonment in Dai. After Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, Zhao Gao slandered the Mengs daily. Ziying advised against killing them, warning of past disasters from killing loyal ministers, but Hu Hai ignored him.

Meng Yi was ordered to commit suicide; he defended his loyalty and criticized unjust executions, citing historical examples, but was killed. Meng Tian, ordered to die, declared his innocence and loyalty, recounting the Duke of Zhou’s story to urge the emperor to reconsider. The envoy refused to relay his words. Meng Tian lamented his sin of cutting earth’s veins while building the Great Wall and poisoned himself. Sima Qian criticized Meng Tian for failing to counsel the First Emperor to aid the people after conquests, instead building the Great Wall, which led to his and his brother’s deaths.

translation:
Yuan Ang is from Chu, and his courtesy name is Si.
His father once worked with bandits and later moved to Anling.
During the period of Empress Lu, Yuan An once served as Lu Lu's retainer.
When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, Yuan An's brother Yuan Kuai recommended him to be the lieutenant.
Jianghou Zhou Bo became the prime minister. After the pilgrimage, he hurried out of the court, very satisfied with his ambitions.
The emperor was very respectful to him and often sent him off in person.
Yuan Ang remonstrated and said: What kind of person do you think Prime Minister Jianghou is?
The emperor said: He is an important minister of the country.
Yuan An said: Jianghou is what is usually called a hero, not an important minister of the country. The important ministers of the country can live and die with the emperor.
When Empress Lu was in power, the Lu family was in power and granted the title of king without authorization. As a result, the Liu family's world was barely held together like a thin ribbon and was almost severed.
During this period, Jianghou Zhou Bo was the Taiwei and held military power, but could not correct the collapse of the Han Dynasty.
After Empress Lu died, the ministers jointly opposed the Lu family. The Taiwei took control of the military and happened to have the opportunity to succeed, so he was what is usually called a hero, not an important official of the country.
If the Prime Minister shows a proud look towards the Emperor, but His Majesty humbly gives in, both the minister and the Lord are violating etiquette. I privately think that Your Majesty should not adopt this attitude.
Later in the court meeting, the emperor gradually became more majestic, and the prime minister gradually became more awe-inspiring.
Soon after, the prime minister resented Yuan Ang and said: I have a relationship with your brother Yuan Kuai, but now you are slandering me in the court!
Yuan An also did not apologize to him.
When Jianghou was dismissed from his position as prime minister and returned to his feudal state, someone in the feudal state wrote a letter accusing him of treason, so Jianghou was summoned to Beijing and imprisoned in prison. Some princes in the royal family did not dare to speak for him. Only Yuan Ang declared that Jianghou was not guilty.
Jianghou was released, and Yuan An made a lot of efforts.
Jianghou then made a heart-to-heart friendship with Yuan An.
When Liu Chang, the king of Huainan, came to Beijing to see him, he killed Piyanghou. He was also quite arrogant in his dealings with others.
Yuan Ang advised the emperor: If the princes are too arrogant, disaster will inevitably occur. Their fiefdoms can be appropriately reduced.
The emperor did not adopt his opinion, and King Huainan became even more arrogant.
When it was discovered that the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, was preparing to rebel, he was investigated and punished. This incident implicated King Huainan, who was recruited, and the emperor demoted him to Shu and transported him in a prison car.
Yuan An was serving as Zhonglang General at that time, so he advised him: Your Majesty has always been arrogant and indulgent to the King of Huainan without any restrictions, which has led him to the current situation, and now he has suddenly defeated him.
The King of Huainan is an upright man. If he encounters a cold wind and dies on the way, his Majesty will be thought that the world is too big to tolerate him, and he will be infamous for killing his younger brother. What will he do then?
The emperor refused to listen and finally did so.
King Huainan died of illness when he arrived at Yongdi. When the news came, the emperor neither ate nor drank, and cried very sadly.
Yuan An entered and kowtowed to apologize.
The emperor said: Because your opinions were not adopted, this result was reached.
Yuan An said: Your Majesty, please relax yourself. This is already in the past. Can you still regret it?
Besides, Your Majesty has three behaviors that are above the world. This incident is not enough to ruin your reputation.
The emperor said: What are the three behaviors that make me higher than others?
Yuan An said: When Your Majesty was living in Dai, the Queen Mother was ill. For three years, Your Majesty never closed his eyes or took off his clothes to sleep. Any decoction that His Majesty had not personally tasted was not allowed to be given to the Queen Mother.
It was difficult for Zeng Shen to do this as a poor man, but now His Majesty has practiced it as a king, which is much better than Zeng Shen's filial piety.
When Zhu Lu was in power, ministers acted arbitrarily, but Your Majesty rode six inferior horse-drawn carriages from Dai to the capital where disaster and fortune were unpredictable. Even brave men like Meng Ben and Xia Yu could not compare with Your Majesty.
His Majesty arrived at Dai Guo's guest house in the capital. He resigned to the throne of emperor twice while facing west, and resigned to the throne of emperor three times while sitting facing south.
Xu You resigned to the world only once, but His Majesty resigned to the world five times, which was more than Xu You's four times.
Besides, Your Majesty demoted the King of Huainan to make him suffer some hardship and make him correct his mistakes. However, because the officials were not cautious in protecting him, he died of illness.
Then the emperor felt relieved and said: What should we do in the future?
Yuan Ang said, "The King of Huainan has three sons. It's just up to your Majesty's arrangement."
So Emperor Wen made all three sons of King Huainan kings.
As a result, Yuan Ang became famous in the court.
Yuan An often praised righteousness and spoke impassionedly.
Because the eunuch Zhao Tong was favored by the emperor more than once, he often secretly hurt Yuan Ang, which made Yuan Ang worried.
Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong persuaded Yuan Ang: "Fight with him and insult him in the court, so that his slanderous words will have no effect."
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went on a tour, and Zhao Tong accompanied him in the car. Yuan Ang lay in front of the car and said: I heard that the people who accompany the emperor on the tall chariot are all heroes in the world.
Although the Han Dynasty lacks talents today, why does Your Majesty only want to ride in the same carriage with people who have been cut by swords and saws?
So the emperor smiled and asked Zhao Tong to get off, and Zhao Tong got out of the car with tears in his eyes.
Emperor Wen went up the mountain from Baling and planned to run down the steep slope in the west.
Yuan An was riding a horse, leaning against the car and holding the horse's reins.
The emperor said: Is the general afraid?
Yuan An said: I have heard that people with rich families do not sit close to the eaves when they sit, and people with rich families do not lean on the railings of the balcony when standing. A wise monarch does not take chances when facing danger.
Now Your Majesty lets the six horses of the driver gallop down the high slope. If the horses are frightened and the vehicle is damaged, even if Your Majesty looks down on yourself, how can you be worthy of the Emperor and the Queen Mother?
The emperor finally stopped.
The emperor arrived at Shanglin Garden, followed by Queen Dou and Mrs. Shen.
When they were in the palace, Mrs. Shen often sat at the same table.
This time, when it was time to sit down, Director Lang arranged the seats, and Yuan Ang pulled Mrs. Shen's seat back a little.
Mrs. Shen was angry and refused to sit down.
The emperor was also angry, stood up, and returned to the palace.
Yuan An stepped forward to persuade him and said: "I heard that there is a difference between high and low, so that there can be harmony between the superior and the inferior."
Now that Your Majesty has confirmed the Queen, Mrs. Shen is just a concubine. How can the concubine and the Lord sit at the same table?
In this way, the distinction between dignity and inferiority is lost.
Besides, Your Majesty loves her so much, so reward her heavily.
The method His Majesty used to pamper Mrs. Shen actually became the root cause of her harm.
Hasn't your majesty seen human pigs before?
The emperor was happy, summoned Mrs. Shen, and told her what Yuan Ang said.
Mrs. Shen gave Yuan Ang fifty catties of gold.
However, Yuan An could not stay in the court for a long time because of his many outspoken admonitions, so he was transferred to the post of Captain of Longxi.
He was kind and caring to the soldiers, and they all rushed to serve him.
After that, Yuan Ang was promoted to prime minister of Qi.
He was also appointed as the prime minister of the state of Wu. When saying goodbye and setting off, Yuan Zhong said to Yuan An: King Wu has been arrogant for a long time, and there are many treacherous people in the country.
Now if you want to expose and punish their crimes, they will either write a letter to accuse you or stab you to death with a sharp sword.
The terrain in the south is low-lying and humid, so you'd better drink wine every day, don't care about anything, and just persuade King Wu from time to time not to rebel.
This way you might just get away with it.
Yuan An adopted Yuan Zhong's strategy, and the King of Wu treated Yuan An favorably.
When Yuan An asked for leave to go home, he met the Prime Minister Shen Tujia on the road and got out of the car to worship him. The Prime Minister only expressed his gratitude from the car. When Yuan An returned home, he felt ashamed in front of his subordinate officials, so he went to the Prime Minister's house and asked to see the Prime Minister.
It took a long time for the prime minister to come out to see him, so Yuan Ang knelt down and said, "I hope others will avoid him and meet him alone."
The prime minister said: If what you are talking about is a public matter, please go to the official office to discuss it with the chief minister, and I will report your opinion; if it is a private matter, I will not accept private conversations.
Yuan Ang knelt down and persuaded him: "As prime minister, please weigh yourself. How do you compare with Chen Ping and Jianghou?"
The prime minister said: I am not as good as them.
Yuan Ang said: Well, you even said you are not as good as them.
Chen Ping and Jianghou assisted in protecting Gaozu, pacifying the world, becoming generals, killing Zhu Lu, and preserving the Liu family. You only used the bow and crossbow to become a low-level warrior, and then promoted to captain. You accumulated merit and became the governor of Huaiyang. You did not come up with any strange tricks, and made military exploits in attacking cities and seizing land, and fighting in the wild.
Besides, His Majesty came from Dai. Every time he went to court and Lang Guan submitted a memorial, he never stopped to listen to their opinions. If the opinions could not be adopted, he would put them aside. If the opinions were acceptable, he would adopt them. No one would not praise and praise them.
What is this for?
He wanted to use this method to attract the wise scholar-bureaucrats in the world.
Every day the emperor hears things he has never heard before, understands truths he has never understood before, and becomes wiser and wiser day by day; now that you have closed the mouths of the people in the world, you are becoming more stupid day by day.
If you use a wise monarch to supervise a foolish prime minister, the day when you will suffer disaster is not far away!
The prime minister then bowed twice and said: I am a vulgar and vulgar person, but I am not smart. Fortunately, I have been taught by the general.
Shen Tujia invited Yuan An into the inner room to sit with him and treated him as an honored guest.
Yuan An had always disliked Chao Cuo. As long as Chao Cuo was around, Yuan An would leave. As long as Yuan An was around, Chao Cuo would also leave. The two never talked together.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, Chao Cuo became the imperial censor. He sent officials to investigate Yuan An's acceptance of Wu Wang Liu Bi's property and punish him according to the seriousness of the crime.
The emperor issued an edict to demote Yuan An to a commoner. News of Wu Chu's rebellion reached the capital, and Chao Cuo told the Prime Minister: Yuan An received a lot of money from the King of Wu and specifically covered it for him, saying that he would not rebel.
Now that the rebellion has become a fact, I plan to request Yuan Ang be punished. He must have known the plot of rebellion.
The Prime Minister said: Punishing him before the matter is exposed may interrupt the rebellion conspiracy.
Now that the rebels are marching westward, what is the benefit of punishing Yuan Ang! Besides, Yuan Ang shouldn't have any conspiracy.
Chao Cuo hesitated.
Someone told Yuan Ang about this. Yuan Ang was afraid and went to see Dou Ying overnight to explain to him the reasons for King Wu's rebellion, hoping to confront him personally in front of the emperor.
Dou Ying went to the palace to report to the emperor, and the emperor summoned Yuan Ang to the palace to meet him.
Chao Cuo was right in front of him. When Yuan An asked the emperor to meet him alone without others, Chao Cuo retreated, feeling very resentful.
Yuan Ang explained in detail that the King of Wu rebelled because of Chao Cuo. Only by killing Chao Cuo immediately to apologize to the King of Wu could the Wu army stop.
These words of his are all recorded in "The Biography of Wu Wangbi".
The emperor appointed Yuan An as Taichang and Dou Ying as general.
The two men have always been friends.
When the King of Wu rebelled, the prestigious people living in the mausoleums and the wise officials in Chang'an City were vying to attach themselves to the two of them, and hundreds of cars followed behind them every day.
After Chao Cuo was executed, Yuan Ang went to Wu as an envoy as Taichang.
The King of Wu wanted him to serve as a general, but Yuan Ang refused.
The king of Wu killed him and sent a captain to lead 500 men to surround Yuan Ang in the army.
When Yuan An was the Prime Minister of the State of Wu, a Cong Shi secretly had an affair with Yuan An's maid. Yuan An knew about it but did not reveal it, and treated Cong Shi as before.
Someone told Cong Shi that Yuan Ang knew about his affair with his maidservant, and Congshi fled home. Yuan Ang chased Congshi in his car, and gave him his maidservant, still calling him Congshi.
When Yuan An was sent as an envoy to Wu and was besieged, Sima happened to be the captain who besieged Yuan An. Sima sold all the belongings he carried and used the money to buy two loads of strong-flavored wine. It happened to be cold and the besieging soldiers were hungry and thirsty. They drank too much wine and the soldiers guarding the southwest corner of the city were drunk. Sima Cheng led Yuan An up at night and said: You can go, the King of Wu expects to kill you tomorrow.
Yuan Ang didn't believe it and said, "What do you do?"
Sima said: I am the one who originally had an affair with your maid in the history.
Yuan Ang then thanked him in surprise and said: "You are lucky to have your parents here, I can't let you get in trouble because of this."
Sima said: Just leave. I will run away and hide my parents. Why should you worry?
So he cut the tent of the military camp open with a knife and led Yuan Ang out of the road blocked by the drunken soldiers.
Sima and Yuan Ang parted ways and went in opposite directions. Yuan Ang took off his knot and carried it in his arms. He leaned on his staff and walked for seven or eight miles. At dawn, he encountered Liang's cavalry and fled on horseback. Finally, he returned to the court to report.
The Wu-Chu rebels had been defeated, and the emperor changed the title of Pingluhou Liu Li, the son of King Chu Yuan, to the king of Chu, and Yuan An became the prime minister of Chu.
Yuan Ang once wrote a letter to make suggestions, but they were not accepted.
Yuan Ang was exempted from official duties due to illness and lived at home, hanging out with the villagers and playing cockfighting and dog racing games with them.
Ju Meng, a native of Luoyang, once visited Yuan An, who received him warmly.
A rich man from Anling said to Yuan An: I heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you want to associate with him?
Yuan An said: Although Ju Meng was a gambler, when his mother passed away, there were more than a thousand guest cars at the funeral. This was also because of his extraordinary qualities.
Besides, everyone is in danger.
When you are in danger or something urgent knocks on the door, you don't use the excuse of having your parents around to shirk it, and you don't have to refuse by not being at home because of something. The only people the world looks up to are Ji Xin and Ju Meng.
Nowadays, you are often followed by several cavalrymen. If there is an emergency, can these people be relied upon?
Yuan An scolded the rich man and stopped communicating with him.
After everyone heard this, they all praised Yuan An.
Although Yuan Ang stayed at home, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty often sent people to ask him about strategies.
The King of Liang wanted to become the heir to Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and Yuan An persuaded him. After that, the discussion stopped. The King of Liang resented Yuan An and once sent someone to assassinate Yuan An.
The assassin came to Guanzhong and asked what kind of person Yuan An was. Everyone was full of praise.
The assassin then went to see Yuan An and said: I accepted the money from King Liang to assassinate you. You are a generous man and I cannot bear to assassinate you.
But there will be more than ten groups of people coming to assassinate you in the future. I hope you will be more prepared!
Yuan Ang felt very unhappy, and many strange things happened one after another at home, so he went to Mr. Piao to ask for fortune telling.
When returning home, the assassins from Liang Kingdom who were sent later stopped Yuan An outside the outer city gate of Anling and assassinated him.
Chao Cuo was from Yingchuan.
I once studied the punishment naming theories of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang from Mr. Zhang Hui of Zhi County, and I was classmates with Song Meng and Liu Li from Luoyang.
With his proficiency in classics, he served as Taichang's anecdote.
Chao Cuo was an upright and severe man.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, there was no one in the world who studied "Shangshu". I only heard that Mr. Fu from Jinan was a doctor from the original Qin Dynasty and had studied "Shangshu". He was too old to answer the call, so Emperor Wen ordered Taichang to send people to study with him.
Taichang sent Chao Cuo to Mr. Fu to study Shangshu.
After he came back from his studies, he took the opportunity to report to the emperor things that benefited the country and the people, and quoted and explained "Shang Shu".
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty issued an edict and appointed Chao Cuo as the prince's family minister, family official, and prince's family magistrate.
Chao Cuo won the favor of the prince with his eloquence, and the prince's family called him "the wise man".
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Chao Cuo wrote many times about reducing the power of the princes and amending the laws.
After dozens of petitions, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty did not accept them, but he believed that he had unique talents and was promoted to a middle doctor.
At that time, the prince praised Chao Cuo's strategy, but Yuan Ang and most of the other great heroes did not like Chao Cuo.
After Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, he appointed Chao Cuo as his internal historian.
Chao Cuo repeatedly requested the emperor to discuss political affairs with him alone. Emperor Jing always obeyed and favored him more than Jiu Qing. Chao Cuo revised many laws.
Prime Minister Shen Tujia was dissatisfied, but did not have enough power to harm him.
I plan to write a memorial about Chao Cuo's fault this time and request that Chao Cuo be executed. Chao Cuo heard the news and asked to go to the emperor alone that night and explained the matter to the emperor in detail. Prime Minister Shen Tujia went to court and took the opportunity to report Chao Cuo for cutting open the wall of Taishang Temple to make a door without permission, and asked the emperor to hand him over to the Tingwei for execution. The emperor said: The wall that Chao Cuo built was not the wall of Taishang Temple, but the wall on the open space outside the temple, so that it would not violate the law.
The Prime Minister apologized.
After leaving the court, he angrily said to Chang Shi: I should have killed him first and then reported it to the emperor, but instead I reported him first and was betrayed by this guy. It was a big mistake.
The prime minister finally fell ill and died, making Chao Cuo even more prominent.
Chao Cuo was promoted to the imperial censor, and requested that the feudal lords' fiefdoms be reduced accordingly for their crimes, and the counties and cities on the borders of each vassal state be recovered.
After the memorial was submitted, the emperor ordered the ministers, princes and royal family to discuss it together. No one dared to criticize Chao Cuo's suggestion. Only Dou Ying argued with him, so there was a gap between him and Chao Cuo.
The decree revised by Chao Cuo had thirty chapters, and the princes all shouted against it and hated Chao Cuo.
When Chao Cuo's father heard the news, he came from Yingchuan and said to Chao Cuo: The emperor has just succeeded to the throne, and you have taken power, infringing and weakening the power of the princes, alienating other people's flesh and blood, and people are talking and resenting you. Why do you do this?
Chao Cuo said: Things should be like this. Otherwise, the emperor will not be respected and the country will not be peaceful.
Chao Cuo's father then said: If this continues, the Liu family will be at peace, but our Chao family will be in danger. I will leave you and go back.
He took poison and died. Before he died, he said: I can't bear to see disaster involving myself.
Ten days after Chao Cuo's father died, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, in the name of killing Chao Cuo.
When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang came forward, the emperor ordered Chao Cuo to wear court clothes and execute him in Dongshi.
After the death of Chao Cuo, Duke Deng of Yezhe Pushe served as a school captain. When he attacked Wu Chu's army, he served as a general.
After returning to the capital, he wrote a letter reporting the military situation and went to see the emperor.
The emperor asked: "You came from the army and heard that Chao Cuo was dead. Did Wu Chu's army retreat?"
Deng Gong said: The King of Wu has been deliberately rebellious for decades. He was angry because you reduced his fiefdom, so in the name of killing Chao Cuo, his original intention was not Chao Cuo.
Besides, I'm worried that all the scholars in the world will shut up and never dare to speak out again.
The emperor said: Why?
Deng Gong said: Chao Cuo was worried that the princes would become too powerful and could not be subdued, so he asked to reduce the fiefdoms of the princes in order to favor the court. This is the benefit of all generations.
The plan had just started to be implemented, but he was actually killed, which blocked the mouths of loyal ministers internally, and avenged the princes externally. I privately think that it is not advisable for your Majesty to do this.
At this time Emperor Jing was silent for a long time and said: "What you said is right. I also regret this."
So Deng Gong was appointed as the lieutenant of Chengyang.
Deng Gong was from Chenggu and had many unexpected ideas.
During the Jianyuan period, the emperor recruited virtuous people, and the ministers all recommended Deng Gong. At that time, Deng Gong was dismissed from office, and he became the ninth minister from his leisure time at home.
A year later, he resigned and returned home, claiming to be ill. His son Deng Zhang was very famous among the court ministers for studying the theories of Huangdi and Laozi.
Tai Shigong said: Although Yuan Ang is not easy to learn, he is good at understanding and understanding. He takes benevolence as his essence and often praises righteousness and is impassioned.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had just ascended the throne, his talents happened to be at the right time, so they could be put to use.
The current situation was constantly changing. When Wu Chu rebelled, he proposed to kill Chao Cuo.
Although his suggestions were adopted and implemented, he was no longer used by the court.
People who love fame and show off their talents end up getting into trouble because of their pursuit of fame. When Chao Cuo was making the prince's family orders, he made many suggestions but they were not adopted. Later, he took power and revised many laws of the country.
The princes launched a rebellion, but Chao Cuo was not eager to correct the crisis, but wanted to avenge himself, which resulted in his death.
As the saying goes: If you change the ancient laws and mess up the routine, you will either die or escape. Are you talking about people like Chao Cuo?
summary:
Yuan Ang, courtesy name Si, was from Chu and later moved to Anling. He served as a retainer under Lü Lu during Empress Lü’s reign and was recommended as a lieutenant by his brother after Emperor Wen ascended. Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Wen about his excessive respect for Prime Minister Zhou Bo, arguing that Zhou Bo was a “hero” rather than a true “important minister” for failing to prevent the Lü clan’s usurpation. The emperor heeded his advice, and Zhou Bo later resented Yuan Ang but reconciled after Yuan Ang defended him when Zhou Bo was imprisoned for treason.

Yuan Ang advised against indulging Liu Chang, the King of Huainan, whose arrogance led to rebellion and exile. When the king died en route, Yuan Ang consoled the grieving emperor by citing his three virtuous acts: filial piety to his mother, bravery during the Lü crisis, and humility in refusing the throne. The emperor later made the king’s three sons rulers. Yuan Ang’s outspokenness caused friction with eunuch Zhao Tong, whom he publicly humiliated to prevent him from riding in the emperor’s carriage. He also dissuaded the emperor from reckless chariot racing and corrected seating arrangements that favored a concubine over the queen.

Transferred to Longxi, Yuan Ang won soldiers’ loyalty through kindness. As prime minister of Wu, he followed his nephew’s advice to avoid conflict by drinking daily and persuading the king not to rebel. He later confronted Prime Minister Shen Tujia for arrogance, warning that closing off advice would lead to disaster. Shen Tujia apologized and treated him as an honored guest.

Yuan Ang clashed with Chao Cuo, who investigated him for accepting bribes from the King of Wu, leading to his demotion. When Wu rebelled, Yuan Ang blamed Chao Cuo and urged his execution to appease the rebels. After Chao Cuo’s death, Yuan Ang was sent as an envoy to Wu but was besieged. A former subordinate, whom Yuan Ang had forgiven for an affair with his maid, helped him escape. Yuan Ang later served as prime minister of Chu but retired due to illness, living humbly and befriending gambler Ju Meng despite criticism. He opposed making the King of Liang the emperor’s heir, prompting assassination attempts. Warned by an assassin who spared him, Yuan Ang was eventually killed by Liang’s agents outside Anling.

Chao Cuo, from Yingchuan, studied Legalist doctrines and Shangshu under Master Fu. He gained favor as a prince’s tutor during Emperor Wen’s reign, advocating for reducing princely power. Emperor Jing promoted him, and he revised laws, angering nobles. His father warned him of danger but Chao Cuo insisted on centralizing authority. The Wu-Chu rebellion used his execution as a pretext. After his death, Deng Gong argued that Chao Cuo’s policies were for the empire’s benefit, and Emperor Jing regretted the execution. Deng Gong later became a high official but retired.

Tai Shigong commented that Yuan Ang, though unlearned, was benevolent and outspoken, but his fame-seeking led to downfall. Chao Cuo, despite his talents, failed to adapt and died due to his rigidity, as the saying goes: altering ancient laws brings ruin.
