translation:
King Han Xin of Han was the concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han. He was eight feet five inches tall.
When Xiang Liang supported King Chu Huai, the descendant of King Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had already established their own kings. Only South Korea had no successor, so Hancheng, Lord Hengyang among the Korean princes, was made King of Han, hoping to appease the land of the original South Korea.
Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao, and Han Cheng defected to King Huai of Chu.
When Pei Gong led the army to attack Yangcheng, he ordered Zhang Liang to surrender the original territory of South Korea as the Korean Situ. He obtained Han Xin and appointed him as the general of South Korea. He led his army to follow Pei Gong into Wuguan.
Pei Gong was appointed as the king of Han. Han Xin followed Pei Gong into Hanzhong and persuaded the king of Han: "Xiang Yu has sealed all his subordinates in the areas near the Central Plains, but you, the king, are in this far away place. This is tantamount to demotion!"
The soldiers under your command are all from the east of Mount Laoshan. They stand on tiptoe, eager to return to their hometown, so that while they are strong and strong, they can march eastward and compete for the world.
When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, he agreed to make Han Xin the King of Han. He first appointed him as Taiwei Han to lead troops to capture the old land of Korea.
The princes and kings granted by Xiang Yu all went to their respective fiefdoms. King Han Cheng of Han did not follow Xiang Yu in the battle and had no military exploits, so he was not sent to the fiefdom and instead made him a prince.
When he heard that the king of Han sent Han Xin to attack Han, he ordered Zheng Chang, the magistrate of Wu County when he was traveling in Wu, to be the king of Han to resist the Han army.
In the second year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin pacified more than a dozen cities in Korea.
When the King of Han arrived in Henan, Han Xin violently attacked King Zheng Chang of Han in Yangcheng.
When Zheng Chang surrendered, the King of Han made Han Xin the King of Han, and he often led the Korean army to follow the King of Han.
In the third year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han withdrew from Xingyang, and King Han Xin, Zhou Ke and others guarded Xingyang.
When the Chu army conquered Xingyang, Han Xin surrendered to the Chu army, escaped soon, and surrendered to the King of Han. The King of Han again made him King of Han, and finally followed the King of Han to defeat Xiang Yu and pacify the world.
In the spring of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty cut the talisman with Han Xin as a letter and officially named him King of Han, with the fiefdom in Yingchuan.
In the spring of the next year, Emperor Gaozu thought that Han Xin was strong and brave, and his fief Yingchuan was close to Gongxian and Luoyang in the north, Wanxian and Yexian in the south, and the important town of Huaiyang in the east. These were all strategic places in the world, so he issued an edict and ordered Han Xin, the king of Han, to move to the north of Taiyuan to prepare for resistance to the Xiongnu and establish Jinyang as his capital.
Han Xin wrote: "My kingdom is close to the border. The Huns have invaded many times. Jinyang is far from the border. Please allow me to establish Mayi as the capital."
The emperor agreed, and Han Xin moved the capital to Mayi.
In the autumn of this year, the Xiongnu Maodun Shanyu surrounded Han Xin heavily. Han Xin sent envoys to the Xiongnu many times to sue for peace.
The Han Dynasty sent people to lead troops to rescue, but they suspected that Han Xin had sent envoys privately many times and had the intention of betraying the Han Dynasty, so he sent people to blame Han Xin.
Han Xin was afraid of being killed, so he made an agreement with the Xiongnu to jointly attack the Han Dynasty, raised an army to rebel, surrendered the capital of Mayi to the Xiongnu, and led his army to attack Taiyuan.
In the winter of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the emperor personally led an army to attack Han Xin, defeated Han Xin's army in Tongdan, and beheaded his general Wang Xi.
Han Xin fled and defected to the Huns. His generals Manqichuchen, Wang Huang and others from the Bai Tu people supported Zhao Li, a descendant of King Zhao, as king. They also gathered Han Xin's defeated and fled army, and negotiated with Han Xin and the Xiongnu Maodun Shanyu to attack the Han Dynasty.
The Xiongnu sent the right and left wise kings to lead more than 10,000 cavalry and Wang Huang and others to station in the area south of Guangwu. When they arrived in Jinyang, they fought with the Han army. The Han army defeated them. They took advantage of the victory and pursued them to Lishi, where they were defeated again.
The Xiongnu again gathered troops in the Xijiang area of ​​Loufan, and Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty ordered chariot troops and cavalry to defeat them.
The Xiongnu were always defeated and fled, and the Han army took advantage of the victory to pursue the defeated troops. I heard that Maodun Shanyu was stationed in Daigu. Han Emperor Gaozu was in Jinyang at the time and sent people to scout Maodun. The scouts came back and reported that they could attack.
The emperor also arrived at Pingcheng.
When the emperor left the city and climbed Baishan Mountain, he was surrounded by the Huns' cavalry. The emperor sent people to give many gifts to the Queen of the Huns.
The Yan family then advised Maodun Shanyu, saying: Now that the land of the Han Dynasty has been captured, it is still impossible to live there; let alone the monarchs of the two countries do not besiege each other.
After seven days, the Huns cavalry gradually dispersed.
At that time, heavy fog fell from the sky, and the Han Dynasty sent people to travel between Baishan Mountain and Heping City. The Xiongnu did not notice at all.
Chen Ping, the lieutenant of the guard, said to the emperor: The Huns all use long spears and bows. Please order the soldiers to shoot two sharp arrows outwards with each strong crossbow, and slowly withdraw from the encirclement.
After retreating into Pingcheng, reinforcements from the Han Dynasty also arrived, and the Huns' cavalry finally relieved the siege and left.
The Han Dynasty also withdrew its troops and returned.
Han Xin led troops for the Huns to attack the Han army along the border.
In the tenth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin ordered Wang Huang and others to persuade Chen Xi, causing him to misbelieve and rebel.
In the spring of the eleventh year, Han Xin, the former king of Han, invaded Shenhe together with the Huns cavalry to fight against the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent General Chai to lead troops to attack. General Chai first wrote to Han Xin: Your Majesty the Emperor is generous and kind. Although some princes rebelled and fled, when they returned to submission again, they always restored their original titles and titles and did not execute them.
These are all things you know, Your Majesty.
Now you fled to the Huns because of their defeat. There is no serious crime. You should come and submit as soon as possible!
King Han Xin of Han wrote back: The emperor promoted me from a commoner in the lanes and made me king in the south. This is a great honor for me.
In the battle to defend Xingyang, I could not die to be loyal to him, so I was imprisoned by Xiang Yu. This is my first crime.
When the Xiongnu invaded Mayi, I could not hold on to the city and surrendered. This is my second crime.
Now instead, he leads troops for the enemy, fights with the general, and fights for life in the blink of an eye.
This is my third crime. Wen Zhong and Fan Li did not have a single crime, but after they succeeded, one was killed and the other fled; now I have committed three crimes against the emperor, and I still want to survive in the world. This is the reason why Wu Zixu was killed in Wu State.
Now I am running for my life and hiding in the valley, living by begging from the barbarians every day. My desire to return is just like a paralyzed person who never forgets to walk upright, or a blind person who never forgets to open his eyes to see, but the situation does not allow it.
So the two armies fought, and General Chai Tu Ping joined the city and killed King Han Xin of Han.
When Han Xin took refuge with the Xiongnu, he went with his prince. When they arrived at the city of Dandang, they gave birth to another son, named him Dandang.
Prince Han also gave birth to a son, named Ying.
In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Han Daidang and Han Ying led their men to surrender to the Han Dynasty.
In the Han Dynasty, Han Daidang was granted the title of Marquis of Gonggao, and Han Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangcheng.
When quelling the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu, Gong Gaohou's military merit exceeded that of other generals.
The title was passed from son to grandson, and his grandson had no sons, so the marquis was cancelled.
Han Ying's grandson was dismissed as a marquis for being guilty of disrespect.
Han Yan, the grandson of Han Dai who was born as a concubine, had a distinguished status and was very favored by the emperor. His fame and wealth were both prominent in the world.
His younger brother Han Yue was once again granted the title of Marquis, and was appointed as a general several times, and was finally granted the title of Case Daohou.
The son inherited the title of marquis and was executed for breaking the law more than a year later.
More than a year later, Han Shuo's grandson Han Zeng was named Long'ehou and inherited Han Shuo's title.
Lu Wan was from Fengyi, the same hometown as Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Lu Wan's father and Gaozu's father were very close, and when it came time to give birth to a son, Han Gaozu and Lu Wan were born on the same day. The villagers brought sheep wine to the two families to congratulate them. When Gaozu and Lu Wan grew up, they studied together and became very close.
The villagers saw that the fathers of the two families were very close friends. Their sons were born on the same day and became very close when they grew up. They once again came to congratulate them with sheep wine.
When Emperor Gaozu was a commoner, he was chased by officials and needed to hide. Lu Wan always accompanied him, running around. When Emperor Gaozu raised troops from Pei County, Lu Wan accompanied him as a guest. After arriving in Hanzhong, he served as a general and was always by his side.
When he followed Gaozu to attack Xiang Yu in the east, he had the status of Taiwei and could go in and out of Gaozu's bedroom. He was given generous rewards in terms of clothing, clothing and food. No other minister could match him. Even Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were only treated politely because of their merits. As for being favored by people, no one could match Lu Wan.
Lu Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an.
Chang'an is the original Xianyang.
In the winter of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu had been defeated, so he sent Lu Wan to lead another army to attack Linjiang King Gongwei together with Liu Jia, and defeated him.
In July, he returned triumphantly and followed the emperor to attack Yan King Zang Tu, who surrendered.
After Emperor Gaozu brought peace to the world, there were seven princes who were not named Liu but were granted the title of king.
Emperor Gaozu originally wanted to make Lu Wan king, but he was afraid that the officials would be resentful and dissatisfied.
After capturing Zang Tu, he issued an edict to confer the title of marquis on the generals and ministers, and selected meritorious officials among the ministers to confer the title of King of Yan.
All the civil and military officials knew that the emperor wanted to make Lu Wan king, so they all said in unison: Lu Wan, the Taiwei Marquis of Chang'an, often followed the emperor to bring peace to the world, and he made the most contributions, so he can be named King of Yan.
The emperor issued an edict and approved it.
In August of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Lu Wan was appointed King of Yan. No one among the princes and kings was as favored as King Yan.
In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled in Dai. Emperor Gaozu went to Handan to attack Chen Xi's army. King Lu Wan of Yan also led an army to attack Chen Xi's northeast.
At this time, Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to ask for help from the Xiongnu.
King Lu Wan of Yan also sent his subordinate Zhang Sheng to envoy the Xiongnu, claiming that the troops of Chen Xi and others had been defeated.
After Zhang Sheng arrived in the Xiongnu, Zang Yan, the son of Zang Tu, the former king of Yan, fled to the Xiongnu. When he saw Zhang Sheng, he said: "The reason why you are in important positions in Yan is because you are familiar with Xiongnu affairs."
The reason why the Yan State was able to exist for a long time was because the princes rebelled many times and wars continued year after year.
Now you want to eliminate Chen Xi and others as soon as possible for the Yan State, but after Chen Xi and others are eliminated, it will be the turn of the Yan State, and your group will also become prisoners.
Why don't you let Yan postpone the attack on Chen Xi and make peace with the Xiongnu?
The postponement of the war allowed Lu Wan to remain King of Yan for a long time. If there was an emergency in the Han Dynasty, it could also be used to stabilize the country.
Zhang Sheng believed that what he said was right, so he secretly asked the Xiongnu to help Chen Xi attack Yan.
King Lu Wan of Yan suspected that Zhang Sheng was colluding with the Xiongnu to rebel, so he wrote to the emperor requesting that Zhang Sheng's entire family be executed.
Zhang Sheng returned and told Lu Wan all the reasons for doing this.
When Lu Wan came to his senses, he found some substitutes and executed them, freed Zhang Sheng's family members and made Zhang Sheng a spy for the Huns. He also secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's place, hoping to make him defect away for a long time, so that the war would continue year after year.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, during the Eastern Campaign against Yingbu, Chen Kuai often led his troops to station in Dai. The Han Dynasty sent Fan Kuai to attack Chen Kuai and kill him.
One of his lieutenants surrendered and said that King Lu Wan of Yan sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi to exchange information and discuss plans.
Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to summon Lu Wan to Beijing, but Lu Wan refused to go because he was ill.
The emperor also sent the Marquis of Piyang to review the food, and Zhao Yao, the imperial censor, went to greet King Yan, and also questioned King Yan's ministers.
Lu Wan was even more frightened and couldn't hide behind closed doors. He said to his favorite ministers: The only ones who were named kings without the surname Liu are me, Lu Wan, and Wu Rui, the king of Changsha.
Last spring, the Han Dynasty executed the entire family of Huaiyin Marquis Han Xin, and in the summer, they killed Peng Yue. This was Empress Lu's plan.
Now the emperor was seriously ill and handed over all state affairs to Queen Lu.
And Queen Lu was a woman who always wanted to find an excuse to kill princes, kings with different surnames and ministers with high achievements.
So Lu Wan still refused to go to Beijing, claiming to be ill.
Lu Wan's subordinates and ministers all fled and hid.
But some of Lu Wan's words leaked out. Marquis Piyang heard about it and reported all this to the emperor, who became even more angry.
Later, the Han Dynasty got some surrendered Huns and said that Zhang Sheng had fled to the Huns and was the envoy of King Yan.
So the emperor said: Lu Wan has really rebelled!
He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.
King Lu Wan of Yan settled all his family members and thousands of cavalry under the Great Wall, waiting for an opportunity, hoping that after the emperor recovered from his illness, he would come to Beijing to apologize in person.
In April, Emperor Gaozu passed away, and Lu Wan led his men to flee to the Huns, who named him King of Donghulu.
Lu Wan was invaded and plundered by the Huns, and always wanted to return to the Han Dynasty.
More than a year later, Lu Wan died in Xiongnu.
When he was the Queen of Gao, Lu Wan's wife and children escaped from the Xiongnu and returned to the Han Dynasty. Just as the Queen of Gao was seriously ill and could not see each other, they lived in King Yan's palace in Beijing and planned to hold a banquet to see each other after they recovered from the illness.
But Empress Gao passed away unexpectedly and could not meet.
Lu Wan's wife also died of illness.
In the sixth year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Lu Tazhi, the grandson of Lu Wan, surrendered to the Han Dynasty as King of Donghu and was named Marquis of Yagu.
Chen Xi was from Wanqu, and he didn't know why he followed Gaozu in the first place.
In the winter of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Han Xin of Han rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu. The emperor returned to Pingcheng and made Chen Xi a marquis. As the prime minister of Zhao State, he led the border defense troops of Zhao State and Dai State. The troops guarding the border in this area were under his jurisdiction.
Chen Xi once asked for leave to return home. When passing through the State of Zhao, Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao State, saw that Chen Xi's accompanying guests had more than a thousand cars and filled all the official residences in Handan.
Chen Xi treated his guests with the same etiquette among common people, and he was always humble and respectful, and he treated others with humility.
When Chen Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang asked to come to Beijing to see him.
After meeting the emperor, he told the whole story that Chen Xi had many guests and had been in sole control of the military for several years. He was afraid that something might happen.
The emperor ordered people to investigate Chen Xi's guests for their violations of laws and regulations regarding property and property, many of which implicated Chen Xi.
Chen Xi was very frightened and secretly sent guests to Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen to inform them.
In July of the tenth year of Emperor Gaozu, the Supreme Emperor passed away. The emperor sent someone to summon Chen Wei to Beijing, but Chen Wei said that his condition was serious.
In September, he rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself the king of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai two places.
After the emperor heard about it, he pardoned all Zhao and Dai officials who were implicated by Chen Xi and committed plunder. The emperor went there in person and said happily after arriving at Handan: "Chen Xi will not occupy Zhangshui in the south and guard Handan in the north. From this we know that he will not do anything."
Zhao Xiangguo submitted a memorial requesting that the governors and lieutenants of Changshan be beheaded, saying: Changshan had a total of twenty-five cities, but Chen Xi rebelled and lost twenty of them.
The emperor asked: Have the county guards and county lieutenants rebelled?
Zhao Xiangguo replied: No rebellion.
The emperor said: This is because of insufficient troops.
They were pardoned and their duties as captains were restored.
The emperor asked Zhou Chang: Does Zhao still have generals who can lead troops to fight?
Zhou Chang replied: There are four people.
Then these four people were asked to meet the emperor. When the emperor saw it, he cursed: Can you boys lead troops to fight?
The four people lay on the ground in shame.
However, the emperor still granted each of them a thousand households and appointed them as generals.
The ministers admonished and advised: "Many people followed you into Shu County and Hanzhong, and then conquered Western Chu. They had meritorious service but were not generally rewarded. What merits do these people have now and why should they be rewarded?"
The emperor said: This is beyond what you can understand!
Chen Xi rebelled and occupied everything north of Handan. I sent an emergency proclamation to recruit troops from various places, but no one has arrived yet. The only troops available now are from Handan.
Why should I begrudge the four thousand households granted to four people and not use it to appease the young people of Zhao! All the ministers on the left and right said, "Okay."
So the emperor asked again: Who are Chen Xi's generals?
The left and right people replied: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were both merchants in the past. The emperor said: I understand.
So each offered a thousand gold rewards to buy the heads of Wang Huang, Manchuchen and others.
In the winter of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the Han army attacked and killed Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang at Quni City. They also defeated Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun in Liaocheng, killing more than 10,000 people.
Taiwei Zhou Bo marched and pacified Taiyuan and Daijun.
In December, the emperor personally led an army to attack Dongyuan, but failed to capture it. The rebel soldiers insulted the emperor. Soon Dongyuan surrendered. All soldiers who insulted the emperor were beheaded, and other soldiers who did not insult were sentenced to tattoos and tattoos on their foreheads.
Change Dongyuan's name to Zhending.
All Wang Huang and Manqiuchen's men who were offered rewards were captured alive, so Chen Xi's army was completely defeated.
The emperor returned to Luoyang.
The emperor said: Daijun is located to the north of Changshan Mountain, but Zhao Guo controls it from the south of the mountain. It is too far away.
So he named his son Liu Yuan the king of Dai, made Zhongdu the capital, and Daijun and Yanmen were all subordinate to Daiguo.
In the winter of the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Fan Kuai's soldiers chased Chen Kuai to Lingqiu and beheaded him.
Tai Shigong said: Han Xin and Lu Wan were not a family that had always accumulated good deeds. Instead, they were lucky enough to improvise and succeeded through deception and violence. Just as the Han Dynasty was just established, they were able to divide the territory and make the south the king.
Internally, it was suspected because of its strong power, and externally, it relied on foreigners for assistance. Therefore, he was increasingly alienated by the emperor, found himself in danger, had no choice but to surrender to the Huns. Isn't it sad?
Chen Xi was a native of Liang. When he was young, he always praised and admired Wei Gongzi Xinlingjun. Later, he led the army to guard the border, gathered guests, and treated virtuous corporals, and his reputation exceeded his actual status.
Zhou Chang doubted him, and many mistakes occurred from here. Fearing that disaster would come, the treacherous villain took the opportunity to speak again, and finally fell into a treasonous situation.
Oh, how sad!
It can be seen from this that the maturity and success or failure of the plan have a profound impact on a person!
summary:
King Han Xin of Han, a concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han, was a tall man. Initially, after Xiang Liang's defeat, Han Cheng was made King of Han to appease the region. Han Xin later served under Pei Gong (future Emperor Gaozu), persuading him to march eastward. He was eventually made King of Han after capturing Korean cities and defeating rival King Zheng Chang. However, fearing execution due to suspicions of betrayal, Han Xin allied with the Xiongnu, rebelled, and attacked Taiyuan. Emperor Gaozu personally defeated him, and Han Xin fled to the Xiongnu. He continued to lead Xiongnu forces against Han until General Chai killed him in battle. His descendants later surrendered to Han and were granted marquisates, though some titles were eventually revoked.

Lu Wan, a close childhood friend and neighbor of Emperor Gaozu, was exceptionally favored, serving as a general and Taiwei. After the empire was pacified, he was made King of Yan, the most favored among non-Liu princes. During Chen Xi's rebellion, Lu Wan sent Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu, who secretly aided Chen Xi. Lu Wan later realized this and continued to prolong the war. When Emperor Gaozu discovered Lu Wan's collusion with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan. Lu Wan fled to the Xiongnu, becoming King of Donghulu, but always wished to return. After Gaozu's death, Lu Wan died among the Xiongnu. His family later returned to Han, but his wife died before meeting Empress Gao. His grandson eventually surrendered and was made a marquis.

Chen Xi, a marquis and prime minister of Zhao, commanded border troops. Suspected by Zhou Chang, he feared investigation and rebelled with Wang Huang, proclaiming himself King of Dai. Emperor Gaozu personally campaigned, pardoning many officials and rewarding Zhao generals. The Han army defeated Chen Xi's forces, killing his generals and eventually Chen Xi himself in Lingqiu.

The Grand Historian comments that Han Xin and Lu Wan, lacking accumulated virtue, succeeded through deception and violence during the Han's founding. Suspected internally and relying on foreigners, they were alienated and forced to surrender to the Xiongnu—a tragic fate. Chen Xi, admiring Lord Xinling, gathered guests and exceeded his reputation. Zhou Chang's suspicions, fear of disaster, and treacherous whispers led to his rebellion. Thus, the success or failure of plans profoundly impacts a person's destiny.

translation:
Han Anguo, the imperial censor, was a native of Cheng'an County, Liang State, and later settled in Suiyang.
I once studied "Han Feizi" and the doctrines of Zajia from Mr. Tian in Zouxian County. He served King Xiao of Liang and served as a middle official.
When the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao of Liang sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals to resist the Wu army on the eastern front.
Because Zhang Yu fought hard and Han Anguo defended firmly, the Wu army could not cross Liang's defense line.
The Wu Chu rebellion was put down, and the reputations of Han Anguo and Zhang Yu became prominent.
King Xiao of Liang was the half-brother of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty. Empress Dowager Dou liked him very much and allowed him to have the power to nominate the Prime Minister of Liang and two thousand stone-level officials.
The scene of his coming in and out and playing games was more like that of an emperor than that of a minister.
When Emperor Jing heard about it, he was very unhappy. Empress Dowager Dou knew that Emperor Jing was dissatisfied, so she became angry with the envoys sent by Liang Guo and refused to receive them. Instead, she asked them about what King Liang had done.
At that time, Han Anguo was the envoy of the Liang Kingdom, so he went to see the eldest princess and cried: Why can't the Queen Mother clearly understand the filial piety of the Liang King as a son and the loyalty as a minister?
In the past, when the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled, the princes from the east of Hanguguan all united and marched westward. Only Liang was the most loyal to the court and became an obstacle to the rebels' attack.
King Liang thought that the Queen Mother and the Emperor were in Guanzhong, and the princes were in trouble. When he talked about it, tears streamed down his face. He knelt down and saw me and six other people off, leading the troops to repel the Wu Chu rebels. For this reason, the Wu Chu rebels did not dare to march westward, and finally failed and perished. This was all the power of King Liang.
Now the Queen Mother is blaming and complaining about Liang Wang for some strict etiquette.
King Liang's father and brother were both emperors, and the scenes he saw were great, so they cleared the way when traveling and prohibited people from passing through. When he returned to the palace, he emphasized vigilance. King Liang's car and flags were all gifts from the emperor. He just wanted to use these to show off in remote counties, let cars and horses gallop back and forth in the country, and let everyone in the world know that the queen mother and the emperor loved him.
Now when Liang envoy arrives, he will inquire and blame him.
King Liang was frightened and cried and missed him day and night, not knowing what to do.
Why was the King of Liang filial as a son and loyal as a minister, but the Queen Mother showed no mercy?
The eldest princess told Queen Mother Dou these words in detail, and Queen Mother Dou happily said: I will tell the emperor these words for him.
After telling the story, the knot in Emperor Jing's heart was relieved. He took off his hat and confessed his mistake to the Queen Mother, saying: We brothers cannot advise each other, which actually adds sorrow to the Queen Mother.
So he received all the envoys sent by King Liang and rewarded them heavily.
From then on, King Liang became even more favored.
Empress Dowager Dou and Princess Dachang rewarded Han Anguo with property worth about a thousand gold.
As a result, his reputation became prominent and he became connected with the imperial court.
Later, Han Anguo was convicted of breaking the law, and Meng County jailer Tian Jia insulted Han Anguo.
Han Anguo said: Will the ashes of death not resurface?
Tian Jia said: If it burns again, just urinate to put it out.
Soon after, the position of domestic history of Liang was vacant. The Han court sent envoys to appoint Han Anguo as domestic history of Liang. He started as a prisoner and served as an official with a rank of 2,000 stone.
Tian Jia abandoned his official position and ran away.
Han Anguo said: If Tian Jia doesn't come back and take office, I will destroy your clan.
Tian Jia took off his clothes and exposed his chest to apologize.
Han Anguo smiled and said: You can pee now!
Do people like you deserve my punishment?
Finally treat him nicely.
When the internal history of Liang was vacant, King Xiao of Liang had just recruited Gongsun Gui from Qi. He liked him very much and planned to request his appointment as internal history.
Queen Mother Dou heard this and ordered King Xiao of Liang to appoint Han Anguo as internal history.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng lobbied King Xiao of Liang and asked him to ask Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty to be the heir to the throne and increase the fiefdom. They were afraid that the court ministers would not agree and secretly sent people to assassinate the advisors in power.
Even after Yuan Ang, the former Prime Minister of Wu State, was killed, Emperor Jing heard about the plans of Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng and others, so he sent envoys to capture Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
More than a dozen groups of Han sent envoys to the Liang State, and a nationwide search was conducted from Liang State Prime Minister down, but still no one was caught for more than a month.
Han Anguo, the internal historian, heard that Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hiding in the palace of Liang Xiaowang. Han Anguo entered the palace and met with Liang Xiaowang, crying and saying: My lord has been humiliated and I deserve to die for my crime.
The king has no good ministers, so things are in such chaos.
Now that I can't catch Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, please let me say goodbye to you and give me permission to commit suicide.
King Xiao of Liang said: Why are you doing this?
Han Anguo burst into tears and said: Your Majesty, think about it for yourself, which one is closer between you and the Emperor, the Supreme Emperor and Emperor Gao, or the Emperor and King Linjiang?
King Xiao of Liang said: "It's not as close as them."
King Liang Xiao said: The relationship between the Supreme Emperor, King Linjiang, Emperor Gao and the Emperor is between father and son. However, Emperor Gao said: I am the one who takes over the world with a three-foot sword, so the Supreme Emperor could not interfere in political affairs in the end and lived in Yueyang Palace.
King Linjiang was the eldest prince, but he was deposed and demoted to King Linjiang just because of his mother's mistake. He also committed suicide in the Lieutenant's Mansion because he occupied the open space within the wall of the ancestral temple when building a palace.
Why is this so?
Because in governing the world, public affairs cannot be compromised by private affairs.
If you want to say: Even if you are your biological father, how do you know that he will not turn into a tiger?
How do even brothers know he won't turn into a wolf?
Now, Your Majesty, you are among the princes, but you listened to the false words of an evil minister, violated the emperor's prohibition, and obstructed the sage's law.
Because of the Queen Mother, the Emperor cannot bear to use laws against you.
The Queen Mother cried day and night, hoping that the king would change his mind, but the king never realized it.
If the Queen Mother dies suddenly, who can you rely on, Your Majesty?
Before he finished speaking, King Xiao of Liang burst into tears and thanked Han Anguo and said: I will hand over Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng now.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide.
The envoy from the Han court went back to report the situation, and Liang Guo's affairs were resolved. This was the power of Han Anguo.
Therefore, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty and Empress Dowager Dou valued Han Anguo even more.
King Xiao of Liang passed away and King Gong came to the throne. Han Anguo lost his official position for breaking the law and lived at home.
During the Jianyuan period, Tian Fan, the Marquis of Wu'an, served as the Taiwei of the Han Dynasty. He was favored and gained great power. Han Anguo gave Tian Fan something worth five hundred gold.
Tian Fu told the Queen Mother about Han Anguo, and the emperor often spoke of Han Anguo's talents, so he summoned him to serve as the captain of the North, and later he was promoted to the rank of chief minister.
Minyue and Dongyue attacked each other, and Han Anguo and Daxing Wang Hui led their troops there.
Before reaching Yue, the Yue people killed their king and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and the Han army withdrew its troops.
In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Hou Tianfan of Wu'an became the prime minister, and Han Anguo became the imperial censor.
The Xiongnu sent people to request peace, and the emperor handed it over to the courtiers for discussion.
Daxingling Wang Hui was a native of Yan. He had served as an official in border counties many times and was familiar with the situation of the Xiongnu.
He commented: The Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu usually made peace within a few years before the Xiongnu broke the treaty again.
It is better not to agree and send out troops to attack it.
Han Anguo said: Sending troops to fight thousands of miles away will not lead to victory.
Now the Xiongnu rely on the abundant army and horses, have the heart of animals, and migrate like flocks of birds in flight. It is difficult to control them.
The land we get cannot be considered as opening up new territory, nor can the people who own it be considered powerful. They have not belonged to our people since ancient times.
If the Han army goes thousands of miles away to compete for interests, the troops and horses will be exhausted, and the enemy will rely on its comprehensive superiority to attack our weaknesses.
Moreover, at the end of the day, even the thinnest white silk produced by the Lu land cannot be penetrated; the strong wind blowing from bottom to top, in the end, even has no power to flutter the goose feathers. It is not that the power was not strong at the beginning, but that the power failed in the end.
Therefore, it is really disadvantageous to send troops to attack the Xiongnu. It is better to make peace with them.
Most of the opinions of the officials agreed with Han Anguo, so the emperor agreed to make peace with the Xiongnu.
In the second year of the marriage, which was the first year of Yuanguang, Nie Wengyi, a wealthy gentry in Mayi City, Yanmen County, told the emperor through Daxing Wang Hui: The Xiongnu had just made peace with the Han, and they were close and trusted the people in the border areas, so they could lure them with financial benefits.
So he secretly sent Nie Wengyi as a spy, fled to the Xiongnu, and said to Shanyu: I can kill the magistrate, county magistrate and other officials of Mayi City, surrender Mayi City to you, and get all the property.
Shanyu trusted him very much and thought what he said was reasonable, so he agreed to Nie Wengyi.
Nie Wengyi came back, beheaded the condemned prisoner, and hung his head on Mayi City, pretending to be the head of an official in Mayi City, in order to win the trust of the envoy sent by Shanyu.
Said: The chief of Mayi City is dead. You can come quickly.
So Shan Yu led more than 100,000 cavalry through the border fortress and entered Wuzhou Fortress.
At this time, the Han Dynasty ambushed more than 300,000 chariots, cavalry, and infantry, hiding in the valley next to Mayi City.
Wei Lieutenant Li Guang served as the general of the cavalry, Grand Servant Sun He served as the general of the light chariot, Wang Hui of Daxing served as the general of generals and generals, and Taizhong doctor Li Xi served as the general of caiguan.
Han Anguo, the imperial censor, served as the general guarding the army, and all generals were subordinate to the general guarding the army.
It was mutually agreed that when Shanyu entered Mayi City, the ambush troops of the Han army would rush out and attack.
Wang Hui, Li Xi, and Li Guang also attacked the Huns' military supplies from Dai County.
At that time, Chanyu entered the Wuzhou Fortress of the Han Dynasty Great Wall.
There were still more than a hundred miles away from the city of Mayi, and they were about to plunder and plunder, but they only saw livestock grazing in the wilderness, but not a single person.
Chanyu thought it was strange, so he attacked the beacon tower and captured Wuzhou's Wei Shi.
I want to ask Wei Shi about the situation.
Wei Shi said: Hundreds of thousands of Han troops were ambushing the city of Mayi.
Shanyu turned around and said to the people on his left and right: "I was almost deceived by the Han!"
Then he led the troops back.
After leaving the frontier fortress, he said: It is God's will that we capture Wuzhou Weishi!
Call Wei Shi the King of Heaven.
It is said under the seal that Shanyu has retreated.
The Han army pursued them to the frontier fortress, but they probably couldn't catch up, so they retreated back.
Wang Hui and others had an army of 30,000 people. They heard that the Chanyu did not fight the Han army, and estimated that the military supplies used to attack the Xiongnu would definitely fight against the Chanyu's elite troops. The situation of the Han army must have failed, so they weighed the interests and decided to withdraw their troops, so the Han army returned without success.
The emperor was angry that Wang Hui did not attack the Xiongnu's logistics troops and led his troops to withdraw without permission.
Wang Hui said: It was originally agreed that as soon as the Xiongnu entered Mayi City, the Han army would fight the Shanyu, and then my troops would capture the Xiongnu's military supplies. This would be profitable.
Now Shanyu heard the news and returned before reaching Mayi City. My 30,000 troops could not defeat him and would only bring shame.
I knew I would be beheaded when I came back, but this way I could save your Majesty's 30,000 soldiers.
The emperor then handed Wang Hui over to Tingwei for punishment.
The Tingwei judged him that he should be beheaded as he walked to avoid the enemy and waited.
Wang Hui secretly gave Tian Fu a thousand gold coins.
Tian Fu did not dare to plead with the emperor, but said to the Queen Mother: Wang Hui first proposed the plan of Mayi to lure the enemy, but now it failed and he killed Wang Hui. This was to avenge the Huns.
When the emperor met with the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother told the emperor what the prime minister had said.
The emperor said: The person who first proposed the Mayi plan was Wang Hui, so he mobilized hundreds of thousands of soldiers from all over the world to follow his words and attack the Huns.
Besides, even if the Chanyu cannot be captured this time, if Wang Hui's troops attack the Huns' military supplies, they may still gain something, which can comfort the hearts of the soldiers.
Now I cannot apologize to the people of the world without killing Wang Hui.
When Wang Hui heard this, he committed suicide.
Han Anguo was a man of great strategy, and his intelligence was enough to cater to the world, but he did so out of a loyal heart.
He is greedy for money.
Those he recommended were all honest scholars who were more worthy than himself.
In the Liang Kingdom, Hu Sui, Zang Gu, and Zhi Ta were recommended, and they were all famous scholars in the world. The scholars also praised and admired him very much, and even the emperor thought that he was a talented person in governing the country.
Han Anguo served as the imperial censor for more than four years. When the Prime Minister Tian Fu passed away, Han Anguo acted as the prime minister. He fell off the car while guiding the emperor's car and became lame.
The emperor discussed appointing the prime minister and planned to appoint Han Anguo. He sent someone to visit him and found that he was severely lame, so he appointed Pingji Hou Xue Ze as the prime minister.
Han Anguo was dismissed from his post due to illness for several months. His foot injury recovered, and the emperor appointed Han Anguo as lieutenant.
More than a year later, he was transferred to the rank of guard.
The chariot general Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu, marched from Shanggu County, and defeated the Xiongnu in Longcheng.
General Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu and escaped; Gongsun Ao's soldiers suffered heavy casualties; they all deserved beheading, but later paid for their sins and became commoners.
The next year, the Xiongnu invaded the border and killed the governor of western Liaoning. When they invaded Yanmen, they killed and took thousands of people captive. The chariot and cavalry general Wei Qing sent troops to pursue them and marched out of Yanmen County.
Weiwei Han Anguo served as general Caiguan and was stationed in Yuyang.
Han Anguo captured prisoners, who confessed that the Huns had gone far away.
Han Anguo immediately wrote to the emperor saying that it was the farming season and requested that the army be temporarily suspended.
After stopping their military garrison for more than a month, the Xiongnu invaded Shanggu and Yuyang on a large scale.
There were only more than 700 people in the military camp of Han Anguo. They went out to meet the Xiongnu and fought with them. However, they failed to win and returned to the military camp.
The Huns captured more than a thousand people, livestock and property and left.
After the emperor heard the news, he was very angry and sent an envoy to blame Han Anguo.
Tiaohan Anguo moved further east and stationed in Youbeiping.
Because at that time the prisoners of the Huns confessed that they wanted to invade the east.
Han Anguo initially served as a royal censor and a general protecting the army, but was gradually ostracized and alienated, demoted and demoted; while the newly favored young generals Wei Qing and others had military merits and were even more favored by the emperor.
After being alienated, Han Anguo felt very frustrated; he led troops to garrison and was bullied by the Xiongnu. He suffered many losses and casualties, and felt very guilty.
He hoped to return to the court, but he was even transferred to the east to garrison, and he felt depressed.
A few months later, he fell ill and vomited blood and died.
Han Anguo died in the second year of Yuanshuo.
Tai Shigong said: Hu Sui and I reviewed the calendar and observed Han Changru's behavior. Judging from Hu Sui's deep and reserved kindness, the world said that Liang Guo has many loyal and loyal elders. This is indeed true!
Hu Sui did his best as an official, and the emperor was about to rely on him to become the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, but Hu Sui died again.
Otherwise, with Husui's honest character and upright behavior, he is really a humble and prudent gentleman.
summary:
Han Anguo, a native of Liang State and a student of Han Feizi and Zajia, served as a middle official under King Xiao of Liang. During the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, he and Zhang Yu defended Liang’s eastern front, preventing the Wu army from crossing. After the rebellion, their reputations grew. King Xiao of Liang, favored by Empress Dowager Dou, acted with imperial-like grandeur, angering Emperor Jing. As Liang’s envoy, Han Anguo pleaded with the eldest princess, explaining King Liang’s filial piety and loyalty during the rebellion, and his use of imperial gifts to display the emperor’s favor. The empress dowager relented, and Emperor Jing reconciled, rewarding Han Anguo generously.

Later, Han Anguo was imprisoned for a crime but became Liang’s domestic history after a jailer’s insult. He forgave the jailer. When Liang’s internal history post opened, the empress dowager ordered King Liang to appoint Han Anguo. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng plotted to make King Liang heir, assassinating Yuan Ang. Emperor Jing sent envoys to capture them, but they hid in King Liang’s palace. Han Anguo warned King Liang of the dangers, citing historical precedents, and the king surrendered the conspirators, who committed suicide. This resolved the crisis, and Han Anguo gained favor.

After King Xiao’s death, Han Anguo lost his post but later became a chief minister. During the Xiongnu peace debate, he argued against war, favoring peace. The emperor agreed. In the Mayi incident, Nie Wengyi lured the Xiongnu, but the plan failed when the Chanyu retreated. Wang Hui, who proposed the plan, was executed despite pleas. Han Anguo, known for strategy and loyalty but greedy, recommended many scholars. He served as imperial censor for four years, then as lieutenant and guard. After Wei Qing’s campaigns, Han Anguo was stationed in Yuyang but was deceived by prisoners, leading to Xiongnu raids. Demoted and alienated, he died of illness in 123 BCE. Sima Qian praised his loyalty and the integrity of Liang’s elders.

translation:
Mr. Wei's name is Wuji, he is the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and the half-brother of King Wei Anli.
After the death of King Zhao, King Anli came to the throne and named the son Lord Xinling.
At that time, Fan Sui fled from Wei to Qin and served as Qin Prime Minister. Because he was resentful that Wei Qi Qu beat him almost to death, he sent Qin troops to besiege Daliang and defeated the Wei troops stationed in Huayang, causing Wei general Mang Mao to flee in defeat.
The king of Wei and his son were very anxious about this matter.
The prince was kind, generous, courteous and virtuous. Regardless of whether the scholars had talent or talent, he interacted with them courteously. He never dared to look down on the scholars because of his wealth.
Therefore, scholars from thousands of miles around rushed to join him, and he attracted 3,000 diners.
At that time, the princes and states did not dare to invade Wei for more than ten years because of the virtuous son and the large number of guests.
One time, the young master and the King of Wei were playing chess, and an alarm came from the northern border, saying that Zhao State was sending troops to invade and would enter the border.
The king of Wei immediately put down his chess pieces and summoned the ministers to discuss countermeasures.
The prince dissuaded the king of Wei and said: "The king of Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border."
Then he continued to play chess with King Wei as if nothing had happened.
But the king of Wei was frightened and did not focus on playing chess at all.
After a while, news came from the north saying: King Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border.
King Wei was greatly surprised when he heard this and asked: How did the young master know this?
The young master replied: One of my diners can go deep into the secrets of King Zhao. If King Zhao takes any action, he will report it to me immediately, so I know about it.
From then on, the king of Wei was afraid of the young master's talents and did not dare to use him to handle national affairs.
There was a hermit named Hou Ying in the state of Wei. He was seventy years old and came from a poor family. He was the gatekeeper of the east gate of Daliang City.
When the prince heard about this man, he sent someone to see him and wanted to give him a generous gift.
But Hou Ying refused to accept it, saying: I have cultivated my moral character and insisted on integrity for decades, but after all, I cannot accept the prince's financial gift because I am a poor janitor.
The young master then held a banquet and entertained the guests.
After everyone came and sat down, the young master took the carriage, horses and entourage, vacated the left seat in the carriage, and went to the east gate in person to greet Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou tidied up his shabby clothes and hats, then got into the car and sat in the distinguished seat vacated by the young master. He had no intention of being humble at all, and wanted to observe the young master's attitude.
But the young master held the horse's reins more respectfully.
Mr. Hou said to the young master again: I have a friend who is in the slaughterhouse in the market. I would like to give him a ride and take me to visit him.
The young master immediately drove to the market. Mr. Hou got out of the car and went to meet his friend Zhu Hai. He squinted at the young master and deliberately stood there for a long time, chatting with his friend and secretly observing the young master.
The young master's face became more cheerful.
At this time, the generals, prime ministers, clan ministers and distinguished guests from Wei State were all sitting in the hall, waiting for the young master to raise their glasses to start the banquet.
Everyone in the market saw the young master holding the reins and driving the car for Mr. Hou.
The young master's entourage secretly scolded Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou saw that the young master's expression remained unchanged, so he said goodbye to his friend and got into the car.
After arriving home, the young master led Mr. Hou to sit on the upper seat and introduced Mr. Hou to all the guests with praise. All the guests in the hall were surprised.
When everyone was drunk, the young master stood up and walked to Mr. Hou to toast his birthday.
Mr. Hou took the opportunity and said to the young master: Today I, Hou Ying, have made things difficult for the young master.
I am just a man who holds the gate and locks it at the east gate of the city, but the young master has resigned himself to carriages and horses and personally welcomes me in the public. I should not visit my friend again, but today the young master condescends to accompany me to visit him.
But I also wanted to make the young master famous, so I deliberately stopped the young master's carriage and horse in the market for a long time, and used the opportunity to visit friends to observe the young master. As a result, the young master became more humble.
People in the market thought that I was a villain, but they thought that the young master was a noble person who could treat the corporal with courtesy.
After the banquet ended, Mr. Hou became the prince's distinguished guest.
Mr. Hou said to the young master: The butcher Zhu Hai I visited is a virtuous man, but people don't understand him, so he is hidden among the butchers.
The young master went to visit Zhu Hai many times, but Zhu Hai deliberately refused to pay his respects and thank him. The young master thought this person was strange.
In the 20th year of King Anli of Wei, King Zhao of Qin had defeated the Zhao army in Changping, and then marched to besiege Handan.
The young master's sister is the wife of King Zhao Huiwen's brother Pingyuan Jun. She has sent letters to the King of Wei and the young master many times, asking for reinforcements from Wei.
The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead an army of 100,000 people to rescue Zhao.
After King Zhao of Qin learned the news, he sent an envoy to warn King Wei: I am about to capture Zhao. It is only a matter of time. Who among the princes dares to save Zhao will definitely mobilize troops to attack it first after capturing Zhao.
The King of Wei was very frightened, so he sent people to stop Jin Bi from advancing further. He left the army to camp in Yecheng, nominally to save Zhao, but in fact he adopted a two-sided strategy to wait and see how the situation would develop.
The envoys of Lord Pingyuan came to Wei one after another, and they were often in urgent need. They blamed Mr. Wei and said: "The reason why I, Zhao Sheng, voluntarily rely on Wei to marry with Wei is because you have noble moral principles and can enthusiastically help others out of danger."
Now Handan is in danger, and sooner or later it will surrender to Qin, but Wei's reinforcements have not come yet. How can the young master help others get out of danger?
Besides, even if you don't take Zhao Sheng seriously, and abandon me to surrender to Qin, wouldn't you pity your sister?
The young master was extremely worried about this matter and repeatedly asked the King of Wei to send troops as soon as possible. He also asked the guests and debaters to try their best to persuade the King of Wei.
Because the King of Wei was afraid of Qin, he always refused to listen to the prince's opinion.
The prince estimated that he would not be able to obtain the consent of the King of Wei to send troops after all, so he decided that he could not let Zhao fall while alive, so he invited guests, gathered more than a hundred chariots, and planned to rush to the battlefield with the guests to fight to the death with the Qin army and die together with the Zhao people.
When the young master led the convoy through the east gate, he went to see Mr. Hou and told Mr. Hou everything about his plan to fight the Qin army to the death.
Then he said goodbye to Mr. Hou and prepared to go on the road. Before leaving, Mr. Hou said: "Young master, please work hard, I can't accompany you, old minister."
The young master walked for several miles, feeling unhappy, and said to himself: I have treated Mr. Hou well enough, and everyone in the world knows it. Now I am about to die, but Mr. Hou didn't say a word to see me off. Did I treat him wrongly?
So I drove back and wanted to ask Mr. Hou.
When Mr. Hou saw the young master, he smiled and said, "I knew the young master would come back."
He went on to say: The young master is famous all over the world for being hospitable and loving people.
Now that there is a crisis, the army that wants to go to Qin is like throwing meat to a hungry tiger. What is the use?
If this is the case, why are we guests used?
The young master treated me with great affection, but I did not see him off when he left, so I knew that he would be angry and I would come back.
The young master bowed to Mr. Hou twice in a row and then asked for countermeasures.
Mr. Hou asked the others to leave and talked secretly with the young master, saying: I heard that Jin Bi's military talismans are often placed in the King of Wei's bedroom. Among the wives and concubines, Ru Ji is the most favored.
I also heard that Ru Ji's father was killed. Ru Ji's desire for revenge had been building up for three years. All the ministers from the King of Wei on down wanted to avenge Ru Ji, but they failed.
For this reason, Ruji once cried to the prince, and the prince sent a retainer to cut off the enemy's head and present it to Ruji respectfully.
If Ru Ji wanted to die for the young master, she had no choice but to do so, but she just had no chance to act.
If the young master really asks Ru Ji for help, Ru Ji will definitely agree, and then he will be able to obtain the tiger talisman and seize the military power of Jin Bi. The north can save the Zhao State, and the west can resist the Qin State. This is the achievement of the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn Period.
The young master followed Hou Ying's plan and asked Ruji for help.
Sure enough, Ruji stole Jin Bi's military talisman and gave it to the young master.
The young master got the military talisman and was about to go on the road. Mr. Hou said: When a general is fighting abroad, he has the power to make decisions. He may not accept some of the king's orders in order to benefit the country.
When the young master arrives there, even if the two numbers match and are verified to be correct, Jin Bi still refuses to hand over the military power to the young master and instead asks the King of Wei for instructions. Then things will be in danger.
My friend the butcher Zhu Hai can go with you. This man is a strong man.
If Jin Bi obeys, that would be the best; if he doesn't obey, Zhu Hai can kill him.
After hearing these words, the young master cried.
Upon seeing this, Mr. Hou asked: "Master, are you afraid of death?"
Why are you crying?
The young master replied: Jin Bi is a brave, powerful and experienced veteran of Wei State. When I went to him, I was afraid that he would not obey orders and would definitely kill him. Therefore, I cried sadly. Why am I afraid of death?
So the young master went to ask Zhu Hai to go with him.
Zhu Hai smiled and said: I am just a butcher who kills animals in the market, but the young master came to greet me many times. The reason why I did not return my greetings and thank you is because I think small etiquette is of no use.
Now that the young master is in danger, it is time for me to sacrifice my life for him.
So he set out on the road with the young master.
The young master went to say goodbye to Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou said: I should have gone with you, but I am too old to make the trip.
Please allow me to calculate the date of your journey. On the day you arrived at the Jinbi Military Headquarters, I faced the north and cut my neck to death to express my loyalty to see the young master off.
The young master then set out on the road. When he arrived at Yecheng, the young master took out his military talisman and pretended to send an order from King Wei to replace Jin Bi as the general.
Jin Bi combined the military talisman and verified that it was correct, but he still doubted the matter. He raised his hand and stared at the young master and said: Now I command an army of one hundred thousand troops stationed on the border. This is an important task related to the fate of the country. Today you come to replace me alone. What's going on?
About to refuse to accept the order.
At this time, Zhu Hai took out the forty kilograms of iron vertebrae hidden in his sleeves and killed Jin Bi with one vertebrae. The young master then took command of Jin Bi's army.
Then he organized the troops and issued an order to the army: If father and son are in the army, the father should go home; if brothers are in the army, the eldest brother should go home; and if the only son has no brothers, he should go home to support his parents.
After reorganization and selection, 80,000 elite soldiers were obtained. Kaiba attacked the Qin army on the front line.
The Qin army broke up the siege and retreated, so Handan was saved and Zhao was saved.
King Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came to the suburbs to greet the young master. Mr. Pingyuan led the way, carrying a pouch full of arrows for the young master.
King Zhao thanked him twice and said: "None of the wise men from ancient times can catch up with the young master."
At this time, Mr. Pingyuan no longer dared to compare himself with others.
After the young master said goodbye to Mr. Hou, on the day he arrived at the Yecheng military camp, Mr. Hou actually faced north and cut his throat to death.
The King of Wei was angry that the young master had stolen his military talisman, and falsely conveyed the king's order to kill Jin Bi. The young master knew this.
Therefore, after repelling the Qin army and saving the Zhao State, he asked his generals to return to the Wei State with their troops, while the young master himself and his retainers stayed in the Zhao State.
King Zhao Xiaocheng was grateful to the young master for his righteous deed of seizing the military power of Jin Bi under the pretext of entrusting the king's orders to protect the Zhao state, so he discussed with Lord Pingyuan and awarded five cities to the young master.
After hearing the news, the young master felt arrogant and complacent.
One of the disciples persuaded the young master: There are things that cannot be forgotten, and there are things that cannot be forgotten.
If others are kind to you, you should not forget it; if you are kind to others, please forget it.
Moreover, under the pretense of King Wei's order, he seized the military power of Jin Bi to rescue Zhao State. This was considered a meritorious service to Zhao State, but it was not considered a loyal minister to Wei State.
However, the young master felt that he had achieved merit and felt that it was great. I privately thought that the young master really shouldn't do it.
After hearing this, the young master immediately blamed himself, as if he was ashamed.
The State of Zhao held a grand welcome banquet. The King of Zhao cleaned the steps of the palace, went to the door to greet the distinguished guests in person, performed the host's etiquette, and led the young master into the west steps of the palace.
The young master walked sideways, repeatedly refusing to give in, and took the initiative to ascend the hall from the east steps.
At the banquet, the young master said that he was guilty, sorry for the Wei State, and had no merit in the Zhao State.
King Zhao drank with the young master until evening. He was still embarrassed to talk about the conferment of five cities because the young master always blamed himself for giving in.
The young master finally stayed in Zhao State.
King Zhao rewarded the prince with the city of Haoyi. At this time, the king of Wei also returned the city of Xinling to the prince.
The young master is still in the state of Zhao.
The young master heard that there were two talented and virtuous people in Zhao who were not engaged in politics. One was Mao Gong who was hiding among the gamblers, and the other was Xue Gong who was hiding in the hotel. The young master wanted to see these two people, but the two men hid and refused to see the young master.
When the young master found out where they were hiding, he walked quietly to interact with these two people. They both enjoyed their acquaintance and were very happy.
Lord Pingyuan learned about this situation and said to his wife: At first I heard that my wife's brother Wei Gongzi was an unparalleled sage, but now I heard that he was doing random things and associating with the gang of gamblers and hotel clerks. The young master is just an ignorant and reckless person.
Lord Pingyuan's wife told the young master these words.
After hearing this, the young master said goodbye to his wife and prepared to leave, saying: "I heard that Lord Pingyuan was virtuous, so I betrayed King Pingyuan and rescued Zhao State, which satisfied Lord Pingyuan's request."
Now I know that Mr. Pingyuan's interactions with others are just a bold act to show his wealth. He is not looking for wise men and talents.
Since I was in Daliang, I have often heard that these two people are talented. When I arrived in Zhao State, I was afraid that I would not be able to see them.
I am still afraid that they will not want me when I am dating them. Now Mr. Pingyuan actually regards dating them as a humiliation. Mr. Pingyuan is not worth getting to know.
So I packed my bags and prepared to leave.
The lady told Lord Pingyuan everything the young master said. After hearing this, Lord Pingyuan felt ashamed and took off his hat to the young master to apologize, resolutely retaining the young master.
When the guests of Lord Pingyuan heard about this, half of them left Lord Pingyuan and joined the young master. All the scholars in the world also went to the young master and joined his family.
Mr. Pingyuan's guests were so admired by his conduct that they all came to his door.
The young master stayed in the State of Zhao for ten years and did not return to the State of Wei. When Qin heard that the young master was staying in Zhao, he sent troops eastward to attack Wei day and night.
The king of Wei was extremely anxious about this matter, so he sent envoys to invite the young master to return to his country.
The young master was still worried that the King of Wei would be angry with him, so he warned his guests: "Anyone who dares to deliver the message for the envoys of the King of Wei will be put to death."
Since all the guests had deserted Wei and came to Zhao, no one dared to persuade the young master to return to Wei.
At this time, Duke Mao and Duke Xue went to see the young master and said: The reason why the young master is respected in Zhao and famous among the princes is just because of the existence of Wei.
Now the Qin State is attacking the Wei State. The Wei State is in danger, but the young master does not care. If the Qin State breaks through the beams and razes the ancestral temple of your ancestors, how can the young master still have the face to live in the world?
Before he finished speaking, the young master's expression immediately changed and he told the driver to quickly hitch up the carriage and go back to rescue Wei Guo.
When the King of Wei saw the young master, the two of them couldn't help but shed tears. The King of Wei gave the young master the seal of general, and the young master officially assumed the highest position of commanding the army, the general.
In the thirtieth year of King Anli of Wei, the prince sent envoys to inform various princely states of his appointment as general.
When the princes learned that the young master had become the general, they all dispatched their own troops and generals to rescue Wei.
The young master led the armies of the five vassal states and defeated the Qin army south of the Yellow River, causing the Qin general Meng Ao to flee.
Then they took advantage of the victory and pursued it as far as Hangu Pass, trapping the Qin army in Hangu Pass, so that they did not dare to leave the pass again.
At that time, the reputation of the young master shocked the world, and guests from various princely states presented their art of war. The young master put them together and signed his name, so it is commonly known as "Wei Gongzi's Art of War" in the world.
The King of Qin was worried that the young master would further threaten the state of Qin, so he used thousands of kilograms of gold to go to Wei for bribes, find Jin Bi's former retainers, and asked them to slander him in front of the King of Wei: The young master has been in exile for ten years and is now a general of Wei.
The young master will also take this opportunity to decide to become king. The princes are afraid of the young master's power and prestige, and are planning to come together to support him as king.
The Qin State carried out rebellion many times, using the spies of the Wei State in the Qin State, pretending not to know anything and asking them to congratulate the young master and ask if he had been established as the king of Wei.
The king of Wei heard these slanderous words about the young master every day and could not help but believe them. Later, he actually sent someone to replace the young master as general.
The prince himself knew that he was being deposed for slander again, so he excused himself from going to court because he was ill. He feasted with the guests at home all night long, drank hard liquor, and often hung out with women. He spent four years having fun day and night, and finally died of illness due to excessive drinking. In this year, King Wei Anli also passed away.
When the King of Qin received the news that the young master was dead, he sent Meng Ao to attack Wei, captured twenty cities, and began to establish Dongjun.
From then on, Qin gradually invaded Wei's territory like eating mulberry leaves. After eighteen years, it captured Wei Wangjia, massacred the soldiers and civilians of Daliang, and destroyed the capital.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was in a low status, he heard many times that Mr. Wei was virtuous and talented.
After he ascended the throne and became emperor, he often went to worship the prince every time he passed by Daliang.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, he returned from the front line where he defeated the rebel general Yingbu. When he passed through Daliang, he settled five families for the young master to guard his tomb and let them worship the young master according to the four seasons every year from generation to generation.
Tai Shigong said: When I passed by the ruins of Daliang, I looked for the so-called Yimen.
It turns out that Yimen is the east gate of Daliang City.
There are indeed many gentlemen in the world who are hospitable and like people, but only Lord Xinling can make friends with those people who are hidden in every corner of society. It makes sense that he does not feel ashamed to make friends with the lower class.
His reputation far exceeds that of the princes, and it is indeed true.
Therefore, every time Gaozu passed through Daliang, he ordered the people to offer sacrifices to him without interruption.
summary:
Lord Xinling, named Wei Wuji, was the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and half-brother of King Wei Anli. After King Zhao's death, King Anli enfeoffed him as Lord Xinling. Fan Sui, who fled to Qin and became prime minister, resented Wei's mistreatment and led Qin forces to besiege Daliang, defeating Wei troops at Huayang. The king and lord were deeply troubled.

The lord was generous, humble, and virtuous, attracting three thousand retainers from across the realm. For over a decade, no feudal lords dared invade Wei due to his reputation. Once, while playing chess with the king, a false alarm about a Zhao invasion arose. The lord correctly identified it as a hunting expedition, revealing he had a spy in Zhao's court. This frightened the king, who thereafter feared the lord's abilities and refused him state affairs.

The lord befriended Hou Ying, a seventy-year-old gatekeeper, by personally driving his carriage to fetch him for a banquet. Hou Ying tested the lord's humility by sitting in the honored seat and visiting a friend, Zhu Hai, in the market. The lord remained respectful, winning Hou Ying's loyalty. Hou Ying later recommended Zhu Hai as a capable man.

In the twentieth year of King Anli's reign, Qin besieged Handan, Zhao's capital. The lord's sister, married to Zhao's Lord Pingyuan, begged Wei for aid. King Wei sent General Jin Bi with 100,000 troops but halted at Ye, fearing Qin's threats. Despite the lord's pleas, the king refused to advance. Determined to die with Zhao, the lord gathered retainers and chariots to attack Qin.

Passing through the east gate, the lord informed Hou Ying, who offered no farewell. Suspicious, the lord returned. Hou Ying explained the futility of a direct assault and proposed stealing Jin Bi's military tally from the king's favored concubine, Ruji, whom the lord had previously helped. The lord obtained the tally through Ruji. Hou Ying also advised taking Zhu Hai to kill Jin Bi if he resisted. The lord wept, foreseeing Jin Bi's death.

At Ye, Jin Bi verified the tally but refused to surrender command. Zhu Hai killed him with a hidden iron mallet. The lord reorganized the army, sending home fathers, elder brothers, and only sons, then led 80,000 elite troops to break the Qin siege, saving Handan. Hou Ying fulfilled his promise by cutting his own throat.

Fearing the king's wrath, the lord remained in Zhao. King Zhao offered five cities, but the lord, humbled by a retainer's rebuke, refused credit. He later befriended recluses Mao Gong and Xue Gong, angering Lord Pingyuan, who deemed them unworthy. The lord defended his actions, causing many of Pingyuan's retainers to defect to him.

After ten years, Qin attacked Wei. The king begged the lord's return. Mao and Xue convinced him to go back. The lord became general, rallied five allied states, and defeated Qin at the Yellow River, pursuing them to Hangu Pass. His fame spread, and he compiled "Wei Gongzi's Art of War."

Qin bribed slanderers to claim the lord aimed for kingship. The king believed them and replaced him. The lord feigned illness, indulged in wine and women, and died four years later. King Anli died the same year. Qin then conquered twenty Wei cities and eventually destroyed Wei.

Emperor Gaozu of Han, who admired the lord, ordered five families to guard his tomb and offer seasonal sacrifices. Sima Qian noted the lord's unique ability to befriend humble folk, ensuring his lasting renown.
