translation:
Wei Qihou Dou Ying was the son of the cousin of Empress Dou, Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty.
His father's generation and above have been Guanjin people for generations.
He loves guests.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Dou Ying served as the Prime Minister of Wu State, but was dismissed due to illness.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he took charge of Zhan.
King Xiao of Liang was the younger brother of Emperor Jing of Han Dynasty, and his mother, Queen Mother Dou, loved him very much.
One time when King Xiao of Liang entered the court, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty had a banquet with him as a brother. At this time, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty had not yet established a prince.
When the wine was in full swing, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said casually: After my death, I will pass the throne to King Liang.
Queen Mother Dou was very happy to hear this.
At this time, Dou Ying offered a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world was created by Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is the system established by the Han Dynasty. Why should the emperor pass it on to King Liang without authorization?
Queen Mother Dou hated Dou Ying for this reason.
Dou Ying also felt that Zhan Shi's official position was too small, so he resigned on the pretext of illness.
Empress Dowager Dou then expelled Dou Ying from entering and exiting the palace, and did not allow him to enter the palace to see him during festivals.
In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, seven kingdoms including Wu and Chu rebelled. The emperor found that no one in the royal family or anyone with the surname Dou was as capable as Dou Ying, so he summoned Dou Ying.
Dou Ying went to the palace to see him, but refused firmly, saying that he was ill and incompetent.
Empress Dowager Dou also felt ashamed.
So the emperor said: The world is in crisis, how can you refuse?
So he appointed Dou Ying as the general and rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold.
At this time, Yuan Ang, Luan Bu and other famous generals and wise men retired from their posts and stayed at home, so Dou Ying recommended them to the emperor.
The gold rewarded by the emperor was all displayed in the corridor. When the subordinate officers passed by, they were allowed to use it as they saw fit. None of the gold rewarded by the emperor was taken home.
When Dou Ying was stationed in Xingyang, he supervised the troops of Qi and Zhao. After all the rebellions in the seven countries were put down, the emperor granted Dou Ying the title of Marquis of Wei.
At this time, all the tourists and guests rushed to join Wei Qihou.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, every time the court discussed major military and political affairs, all the princes did not dare to sit on an equal footing with Zhou Yafu, the Marquis of Tiao, and Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi.
In the fourth year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, he established Prince Li and appointed Wei Qihou as his tutor.
In the seventh year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Prince Li was deposed. Wei Qihou argued for Prince Li many times, but to no avail.
Wei Qihou pretended to be ill and lived in seclusion at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian County for several months. Many guests and debaters came to persuade him, but no one could persuade him to return to the capital.
Gao Sui, a native of Liang, came to persuade Wei Qihou and said: The one who can make you rich is the emperor, and the one who can make you a confidant of the court is the queen mother.
Now you are the master of the prince. The prince was deposed and could not fight for it. His efforts could not succeed, and he could not die in the line of duty.
He retired due to illness, embraced the beautiful singer, and retired to live in seclusion instead of attending court meetings.
Comparing these situations with each other, this is your own statement that you want to publicize the emperor's fault.
If both the Emperor and the Queen Mother harm you, then your wife and children will all be killed.
Wei Qihou thought he was right, so he went back to the court and met the emperor as before.
When Taohou Liu She was dismissed from the post of prime minister, Empress Dowager Dou recommended Wei Qihou to be prime minister many times.
Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said: Does the Queen Mother think that I am stingy in not letting Wei Qihou become prime minister?
Wei Qihou is a proud and complacent person, prone to self-admiration, careless and frivolous in doing things, making it difficult for him to serve as prime minister and assume important responsibilities.
Finally, he was not appointed, and Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was appointed as prime minister.
Tianfen, Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing and Queen of the Han Dynasty. He was born in Changling.
After Wei Qihou became a general, when he was at the height of his prominence, Tian Fu was still an official, not a distinguished person. He went to and from Wei Qihou's home, attended banquets, knelt down and stood up like Wei Qihou's descendants.
In the later years of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Tian Fu also became prominent, favored and became a Taizhong doctor.
Tian Fu was eloquent and eloquent. He had studied books such as "Pan Yu" and the Queen Mother thought he had talent.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty passed away, the prince ascended the throne and the Queen Mother became regent. Her suppression and appeasement actions throughout the country mostly adopted the strategy of Tian Fu's guests. Tian Fu and his younger brother Tian Sheng were both named Marquis of Wu'an and Marquis of Zhou Yang respectively in the same year that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty died because they were the younger brothers of the Queen Mother.
Marquis Wu'an had just come to power and wanted to be prime minister, so he was very humble to his guests. He recommended famous people who were idle at home to become officials and make them prominent, hoping to overwhelm the power of generals such as Dou Ying.
In the first year of Jianyuan, Prime Minister Wei Wan was dismissed due to illness, and the emperor was planning to arrange for the prime minister and Taiwei.
Ji Fu persuaded Marquis Wu'an: "Wei Qihou has been a prominent figure for a long time, and the talented people in the world have always attached themselves to him."
Now that you have just made a fortune, you cannot compare with Wei Qihou. Even if the emperor appoints you as prime minister, you must give it to Wei Qihou.
If Wei Qihou becomes prime minister, you will definitely become Taiwei.
The noble status of the Taiwei and the Prime Minister are equal, and you have a good reputation of giving your position to the wise.
Marquis Wu'an then tactfully told the Queen Mother to hint to the emperor, so he appointed Marquis Wei Qi as prime minister and Marquis Wu'an as Taiwei.
Ji Fu went to congratulate Wei Qihou and reminded him: Your nature is to like good people and hate bad people. Today, good people praise you, so you become prime minister. However, you also hate bad people. There are many bad people, and they will slander you.
If you can tolerate both good and bad people, then your position as prime minister can be maintained for a long time; if you cannot, you will be slandered and resigned immediately.
Wei Qihou did not listen to him.
Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi, and Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, both loved Confucianism. They recommended Zhao Wan to be the imperial censor, and Wang Zang to be the doctor's order.
Welcoming Shen Pei, a native of Lu, to the capital, he prepared to set up a Mingtang, ordered the princes to return to their own fiefdoms, abolished confinement, and stipulated good and bad clothing and systems according to etiquette and law, so as to show the atmosphere of peace.
At the same time, people with bad moral character among the Dou family and royal family members were reported and condemned, and they were expelled from the clan.
At this time, most of the princes among the relatives married princesses and did not want to return to their respective fiefdoms. For this reason, words slandering Wei Qihou and others reached the ears of Queen Mother Dou every day.
Empress Dowager Dou liked Huang Lao's theory, but Wei Qihou, Wu'anhou, Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others tried hard to promote Confucianism and belittle Taoist theory. Therefore, Empress Dowager Dou disliked Wei Qihou and others even more.
In the second year of Jianyuan, the imperial censor Zhao Wan asked the emperor not to report political affairs to the queen mother.
Empress Dowager Dou was furious, so she dismissed and expelled Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others. She also dismissed the prime minister and Taiwei from their posts, appointed Bai Zhihou Xuchang as prime minister, and Wuqianghou Zhuang Qingzhai as the imperial censor.
From then on, Wei Qihou and Wu'anhou stayed at home as marquises.
Although Wu'anhou did not hold an official position, he was still favored by the emperor because of the Queen Mother. He discussed political affairs many times, and most of his suggestions were effective. The officials and scholars in the world who were in favor of others all left Wei Qihou and joined Wuanhou. Marquis Wu'an became more arrogant day by day.
In the sixth year of Jianyuan's reign, Empress Dowager Dou passed away. Prime Minister Xuchang and Yushi doctor Zhuang Qingzhai were dismissed from office because of poor funeral arrangements.
So Wu'an Hou Tianfan was appointed as the prime minister, and Han Anguo, the chief minister, was appointed as the censor.
The scholars in the world, including governors and princes, were even more dependent on Wu'anhou.
Marquis Wu'an was short in stature and unattractive in appearance, but he was very noble right from birth.
He also thought that the princes and kings at that time were all old, and the emperor had just ascended the throne and was very young. He served as the emperor's closest relative and confidant as the prime minister of the court. If he didn't rectify them severely and use etiquette to make them submit, the people of the world would not be obedient.
At that time, when the prime minister came to the court to perform affairs, he would often sit there for most of the day. The emperor would listen to what he said. Some of the people he recommended were promoted from idle residence to two thousand stone levels at once, transferring the emperor's power to his own hands.
The emperor then said: Have you finished appointing the officials you want to appoint?
I also want to appoint a few officials.
He once requested that the land of the Examination and Labor Examination Office be allocated to him to expand his residence. The emperor said angrily: Why don't you take away the weapons depot too!
Since then, I have calmed down a bit.
Once, he invited guests to a banquet and asked his elder brother Gaihou to sit facing south, but he sat facing east. He believed that the prime minister of the Han Dynasty was noble and he should not tolerate himself in private just because he was his elder brother.
From then on, Marquis Wu'an became even more arrogant. He built residences whose scale and luxury surpassed all the noble houses.
The fields and manors were extremely fertile, and there was an endless stream of people he sent to various counties to buy utensils on the road.
There are bells and drums placed in the front hall and long cranked flags erected. There are hundreds of beauties in the back room.
The princes presented him with countless treasures, gold, jade, dogs, horses, and playthings.
Since Wei Qihou lost Empress Dowager Dou, he was further alienated by the emperor and was not reused. He had no power. All the guests gradually left of their own accord, and even became lazy and arrogant towards him. Only General Guan did not change his original attitude.
Wei Qihou was unhappy every day, but he treated General Guan particularly well.
General Guan is from Yingyin.
Guan Fu's father was Zhang Meng, who once served as a retainer of Yingyin Marquis Guan Ying. Because of Guan Ying's favor, he recommended him to an official of two thousand stone level, so he pretended to be named Guan Meng after Guan's family name.
During the rebellion of Wu and Chu, Yingyin Marquis Guan He served as a general and was a subordinate of Taiwei Zhou Yafu. He recommended Guan Meng to the Taiwei as a school captain.
Guan Fu led a thousand men to join the army with his father.
Guan Meng was already old, and Marquis Yingyin reluctantly recommended him. Therefore, Guan Meng was depressed and frustrated. During battles, he often attacked the enemy's strong positions and died in the Wu army.
According to the provisions of the military law at that time, father and son joined the army together and participated in the war. If one died fighting for the country, the surviving son could escort the coffin back.
But Guanfu refused to go back with his father's coffin. He expressed impassionedly that he hoped to behead the King of Wu or the general of Wu to avenge his father.
So Guan Fu put on his armor and held a halberd in his hand, and summoned dozens of warriors in the army who had always been friendly with him and were willing to go with him.
After walking out of the military gate, no one dared to move forward.
Only the two of them and Guan Fu's slaves, a total of more than ten cavalry, rushed into the Wu army until they reached the Wu army's general flag, killing and wounding dozens of enemy soldiers.
Unable to move forward any further, he flew back to the Han camp. All the slaves he brought with him were killed, and he was the only one who returned.
Guan Fu suffered more than ten serious injuries on his body, but he happened to have precious medicine, so he survived.
Guan Fu's wounds improved a little, and he asked the general again: "I now know more about the twists and turns in the Wu army camp. Please let me go back again."
The general thought that Guan Fu was brave and loyal, and he was afraid that Guan Fu would die in the battle, so he reported it to the Taiwei Zhou Yafu, who resolutely stopped him.
When the Wu army was defeated, Guan Fu became famous all over the world.
Marquis Yingyin reported Guan Fu's situation to the emperor, and the emperor appointed Guan Fu as Zhonglang General.
A few months later, he lost his official position because of a violation of the law.
Later he settled in Chang'an, and many dignitaries in Chang'an praised him.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Guan Fuguan became the Prime Minister of the country.
Emperor Jing passed away and Emperor Wu, the current emperor, had just ascended the throne. He believed that Huaiyang was the transportation hub of the world and must be defended by strong troops, so he appointed Guan Fu as the governor of Huaiyang.
In the first year of Jianyuan's reign, he transferred Guan Fu Nei to the rank of imperial servant.
In the second year, Guan Fu was drinking with Changle guard Dou Fu. Guan Fu got drunk and beat Dou Fu.
Dou Fu is the brother of Queen Mother Dou.
The emperor was afraid that Empress Dowager Dou would kill Guan Fu, so he appointed him as the prime minister of Yan State.
A few years later, he was disgraced for breaking the law and lived idle at home in Chang'an.
Guan Fu is a strong and straightforward person, he is prone to drunkenness and does not like to flatter people in person.
For the emperor's relatives and powerful people, who were above him, he not only did not want to show respect to them, but also tried to find ways to insult them; for many scholars who were below him, the poorer he was, the more respectful he was and treated them as equals.
In public, it is recommended to praise those who are lower than yourself.
Scholars also respected him for this.
Guan Fu doesn't like articles and classics, and he likes to fight against injustice. He has already promised others things and will definitely fulfill them.
All the people he interacted with were either outstanding people or cunning people.
The assets accumulated in his family are tens of millions, and the number of diners every day ranges from dozens to nearly a hundred.
In order to build embankments and ponds in the countryside and irrigate farmland, his clan and guests expanded their power, monopolized interests, and became tyrannical in the Yingchuan area.
The children of Yingchuan then sang: If the Yingshui is clear, the Guan family will be at peace; if the Yingshui is turbid, the Guan family will be exterminated.
Although Guan Fu lived at home and was wealthy, he lost his power, and the number of dignitaries and ordinary guests gradually decreased.
When Wei Qihou lost power, he also wanted to follow Guan Fu to take revenge on those who usually admired him but abandoned him after losing power.
Guan Fu also wanted to follow Wei Qihou to make friends with other princes and the royal family to improve his reputation.
The two quoted each other and their relationship was as close as that between father and son.
They are in love with each other and have no objections. They just regret that it was too late for them to know each other.
Guanfu went to visit the Prime Minister during the period of mourning. The Prime Minister said casually: "I want to go with you to visit Wei Qihou. It just happens that you are in mourning and it is inconvenient to go."
Guanfu said: "You are actually willing to come to Wei Qihou. How dare I, Guanfu, refuse because of mourning?"
Please allow me to tell Wei Qihou to set up the curtains and prepare a banquet. You can come early tomorrow.
Marquis Wu'an agreed.
Guan Fu told Wei Qihou in detail, just like he told Wu'an Hou.
Wei Qihou and his wife specially bought more meat and wine, cleaned the house all night, arranged the curtains, and prepared the banquet. They were busy until dawn.
As soon as it dawned, the people in charge of the mansion were asked to wait in front of the house.
By noon, the prime minister had not arrived.
Wei Qihou said to Guan Fu: Has the Prime Minister forgotten this?
Guanfu was very unhappy and said, "I, Guanfu, don't mind being in mourning, so I agreed to his appointment and he should come."
So he drove and went to meet the prime minister in person.
The Prime Minister only agreed to Guan Fu as a joke the day before, and really had no intention of coming to the banquet.
When Guan Fu came to the door, the prime minister was still sleeping.
So Guan Fu went in to see him and said, "General, I was fortunate enough to pay a visit to Wei Qihou yesterday. Wei Qihou and his wife prepared wine and food, but they have not dared to eat anything from morning until now."
Marquis Wu'an pretended to be surprised and apologized, saying: I was drunk yesterday and forgot what I said to you.
So he drove there, but he went very slowly, which made Guan Fu even more angry.
When he got drunk, Guanfu danced a bit. After the dance, he invited the prime minister, but the prime minister didn't get up. Guanfu made fun of him during the banquet.
Wei Qihou helped Guan Fu leave and expressed his apology to the prime minister.
The prime minister drank until dark and had a great time before leaving.
The prime minister once sent Ji Fu to claim Wei Qihou's fields in the south of the city.
Wei Qihou said with great resentment: Although I have been abandoned and the general is noble, how can he take my land by force?
No.
When Guanfu heard about it, he was also angry and cursed Jifu.
Ji Fu didn't want there to be any estrangement between the two, so he made up some good words to apologize to the prime minister and said: "Wei Qihou is old and is about to die. Can't you bear it anymore? Just wait for now!"
Soon, Wu'anhou heard that Wei Qihou and Guanfu were actually angry and refused to give up the land. He also said angrily: Wei Qihou's son once killed someone, and I saved his life.
When I serve Wei Qihou, I always obey him. Why is he reluctant to part with these few hectares of fields?
Besides, why did Guan Fu intervene?
I don't dare to ask for this field anymore!
From then on, Marquis Wu'an resented Guan Fu and Wei Qihou.
In the spring of the fourth year of Yuanguang, the Prime Minister told the emperor that Guan Fu's family lived in Yingchuan and were very rampant, and the people suffered from it.
Ask the emperor to investigate.
The emperor said: This is the prime minister's duty, why bother asking for instructions.
Guan Fu also caught the Prime Minister's secrets, used illegal means to seek benefits, accepted money from King Huainan and said some things that he shouldn't have said.
The guests mediate. Only then did the two sides stop attacking each other and reconcile with each other.
That summer, the prime minister married the daughter of King Yan as his wife. The queen mother issued an edict, calling all the princes and royal family to congratulate her.
Wei Qihou visited Guan Fu and planned to go with him.
Guan Fu declined and said, "I have offended the Prime Minister many times because of my drunkenness and impoliteness. Recently, the Prime Minister has had a problem with me."
Wei Qihou said: The matter has been reconciled.
Drag him along.
When the wine was almost drunk, Marquis Wu An stood up to toast his birthday. All the guests left their seats and fell on the ground, expressing their disapproval.
After a while, Wei Qihou stood up and toasted everyone's birthday. Only those Wei Qihou's old friends left their seats, and the other half of the people sat there as usual, only slightly bowed.
Guanfu was not happy.
He stood up and toasted in turn. When the toast came to Wu'an Hou, Wu'an Hou sat there as usual, only bowed his upper body a little and said: "You can't drink a full cup."
Guan Fu got angry, so he smiled bitterly and said: "You are a noble man, I will entrust this cup to you!"
At that time, Marquis Wu'an refused to agree.
The toast came to Linruhou, who was whispering to Cheng Bushi without leaving his seat.
Guanfu had no place to vent his anger, so he scolded Marquis Linru and said: "Normally slandering Cheng Bushi is worthless. Today, the elders are toasting you for your birthday, but you are just like a girl, talking to Cheng Bushi."
Marquis Wu'an said to Guan Fu: General Cheng and General Li are both guards of the East and West. Now that General Cheng is being insulted in public, doesn't Zhong Ru leave some room for General Li, whom you respect?
Guan Fu said, "I don't care if I kill my head or pierce my chest today. Why do I care about General Cheng and General Li!"
The guests got up to go to the toilet and gradually left.
Wei Qihou also left, waving his hand for Guan Fu to go out.
Marquis Wu'an then got angry and said: "This is my fault for pampering Guan Fu."
He ordered the knight to detain Guan Fu.
Guanfu wanted to go out but couldn't.
Ji Fu stood up and apologized for Guan Fu, and pressed Guan Fu's neck to ask him to apologize.
Guan Fu became even more angry and refused to apologize.
Marquis Wu'an then ordered the knights to tie up Guan Fu and put him in the guest room. He called Chang Shi and said, "Today we invite guests from the clan to the banquet. This is because of the Queen Mother's order."
Guan Fu was impeached, saying that he insulted the guests at the banquet, insulted the edict, and committed the crime of "disrespect". He was imprisoned in a special prison.
So he traced his past affairs and dispatched officers to hunt down all the relatives of the Guan family. They were all sentenced to beheading in public.
Wei Qihou felt very ashamed. Even paying guests to plead with Tian Fu could not free Guan Fu.
All the officials of Marquis Wu'an were his eyes and ears, and all the people of the Guan family fled and hid. Guanfu was imprisoned, so he could not tell the secrets of Marquis Wu'an.
Wei Qihou stepped forward to rescue Guan Fu.
His wife advised him: General Guan has offended the Prime Minister and opposed the Queen Mother's family. How can he be rescued?
Wei Qihou said: I earned the title of Marquis, and now I throw it away. There is nothing to regret.
Besides, I can't let Guan Zhongru die on his own while I live alone.
So he went out privately to write to the emperor without telling his family.
The emperor immediately called him into the palace, and Wei Qihou explained in detail the situation in which Guan Fu had lost his speech because he was drunk, and considered it not enough to sentence him to death.
The emperor thought he was right and rewarded Wei Qihou for dining with him, saying: "Go to the East Palace to openly debate this matter."
Wei Qihou went to the East Palace and praised Guan Fu's merits, saying that he was guilty of drunkenness, but the prime minister used other crimes to frame Guan Fu.
Marquis Wu'an then tried his best to slander Guan Fu's arrogance and indulgence, and committed the crime of treason.
Wei Qihou thought that there was no other way to deal with it, so he attacked the prime minister's shortcomings.
Marquis Wu'an said: Fortunately, the world is peaceful and peaceful, so I can be the emperor's confidant. I like music, dogs, horses, and fields.
What I like are just people like karaoke artists and skilled craftsmen. They are not like Wei Qihou and Guan Fu, who gathered the heroes of the world to discuss and discuss day and night. They secretly slandered and harbored deep dissatisfaction with the imperial court. They spoke without scruples and were arrogant. They peered between the east and west palaces, hoping for changes in the world so that they could achieve success.
I don't understand what Wei Qihou and the others are going to do?
So the emperor asked the ministers at court: Which of the two of them is right?
Han Anguo, the imperial censor, said: Wei Qihou said that Guan Fu's father died for the country. Guan Fu rushed into the powerful Wu army with a sword and halberd. He suffered dozens of wounds and had the highest reputation in the army. He was a warrior in the world. If there was no particularly serious crime, it was just a quarrel because of drinking. It is not worthy of citing other crimes to sentence him to death.
What Wei Qihou said is right.
The Prime Minister also said that Guan Fu made friends with powerful cunning people, oppressed the common people, accumulated tens of millions of wealth, ran rampant in Yingchuan, insulted and invaded the royal family. This is what is called "the branches are bigger than the trunk, and the calves are thicker than the thighs". The consequences will either be broken or split. What the Prime Minister said is not bad either.
Let the wise Lord decide this matter himself.
The Lord Commander Ji An thought that Wei Qihou was right.
Internal historian Zheng also believed that Wei Qihou was right at the time, but later he did not dare to insist on his opinion and answer the emperor.
The rest of them didn't dare to answer.
The emperor angrily rebuked the internal historian and said: "You have talked about the strengths and weaknesses of Wei Qihou and Wu'an Marquis many times on weekdays. Today in the court debate, you are as timid as a colt under the shaft of a chariot. I will kill you all together."
He immediately got up and left the court, and entered the palace to serve the Queen Mother for dinner.
The Queen Mother has also sent people to the court to inquire about the news. They reported the situation of the court debate to the Queen Mother in detail.
The Queen Mother got angry and stopped eating, saying: Now that I am still alive, others dare to molest my brother. If I die, they will slaughter him like a fish.
Besides, how can the emperor be like a stone man and not make his own opinions!
Fortunately, the emperor is still here, and these ministers are following suit. If the emperor dies, can these people still be trusted?
The emperor apologized and said: They are all aunts of the royal family, so they are debating their affairs in the court.
Otherwise, only one jailer can solve it.
At this time, the doctor ordered Shi Jian to report to the emperor the affairs of Wei Qihou and Wu'anhou respectively.
Marquis Wu'an had already retired from the court, walked out of the parking lot, and called out to Dr. Han Yushi to ride in the same car. He said angrily: You and I are dealing with an old bald man together, why are you still ambiguous and hesitant?
After a while, Dr. Han Yushi said to the prime minister: "Why don't you love and respect yourself?"
If Marquis Wei Qi slanders you, you should take off your official hat, take off your seal and ribbon, return it to the emperor, and say: As the emperor's confidant, I was lucky enough to get this position. I was originally incompetent. What Wei Qihou said is correct.
Like this, the emperor will definitely praise you for your virtue of humility and will not dismiss you.
Wei Qihou must have felt ashamed and committed suicide behind closed doors.
Now when others are slandering you, you are also slandering others. You are scolding each other like a businessman and a woman quarreling. How ignorant you are!
Marquis Wu An admitted his mistake and said: I was too impatient during the argument and did not think that I should do this.
So the emperor sent his censor to investigate Guan Fu's crimes according to the records. There were many inconsistencies with what Wei Qihou said, and he committed the crime of deceiving the emperor.
He was impeached and imprisoned in a special prison called Dusikong.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qihou received his edict before his death, which read: If something inconvenient happens to you, you can adapt to the situation and report your opinions to the emperor.
When he was imprisoned and Guan Fu was convicted of genocide, the situation became more and more urgent day by day. No one among the ministers dared to explain the matter to the emperor.
Wei Qihou asked his nephew to write a letter to the emperor to report the acceptance of the imperial edict, hoping to be summoned by the emperor again.
The memorial was submitted to the emperor, but after checking the files kept by the minister, there was no final edict from Emperor Jing.
This edict was only sealed and hidden in Wei Qihou's home, and was sealed by Wei Qihou's retainers.
Therefore, Wei Qihou was impeached for forging the imperial edict of the late emperor and should be sentenced to beheading in public.
In October of the fifth year of Yuanguang, Guan Fu and his family were all executed.
It took a long time for Wei Qihou to hear the news. After hearing this, he was extremely angry and suffered from a stroke. He stopped eating and planned to die.
Someone heard that the emperor had no intention of killing Wei Qihou. Wei Qihou began to eat again, began to treat diseases, and discussed and decided not to impose the death penalty.
There were rumors and many slanderous words about Wei Qihou were heard by the emperor, so on the last day of December of that year, Wei Qihou was beheaded on the streets of Weicheng.
In the spring of this year, Marquis Wu'an fell ill and kept shouting, saying things like apology.
He asked a wizard who could see ghosts to diagnose his illness. The wizard saw the ghosts of Wei Qihou and Guan Fu guarding Wu'anhou and wanted to kill him.
Finally died.
His son Tian Tian inherited the title.
In the third year of Yuan Shuo, Hou Tiantian of Wu'an committed the crime of "disrespect" because he entered the palace wearing short clothes, and his title was revoked.
The rebellion of Huainan King Liu An was discovered, and the emperor ordered the matter to be investigated.
The last time King Huainan came to court, Marquis Wu'an was appointed as Taiwei. At that time, he came to Ba Shang to greet King Huainan and said: The emperor has no prince, and the king is the wisest and the grandson of the great ancestor. Once the emperor dies, who else should inherit the throne instead of the king?
The King of Huainan was very happy and gave Marquis Wu'an many gold and silver items.
Ever since the incident involving Marquis Wei Qi happened, the Emperor did not think that Marquis Wu An was right, and it was just because of the Queen Mother's hindrance.
When he heard that King Huainan sent gold and silver to Marquis Wu'an, the emperor said: If Marquis Wu'an is still alive, it's time to exterminate the clan.
Tai Shigong said: Wei Qihou and Wu'anhou were both in prominent positions due to their relatives. Guan Fu became famous at that time because he made up his mind to take risks and perform meritorious deeds.
Wei Qihou was re-employed because he put down the rebellions of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu; Wu'an Hou was promoted because he took advantage of the opportunity that the emperor had just ascended the throne and the Queen Mother came to power.
However, Wei Qihou really didn't understand the changes in the situation, and Guan Fu was neither knowledgeable nor humble. The two protected each other, which caused this disaster.
Marquis Wu'an relied on his noble status and liked to play with power; because of his resentment over a glass of wine, he framed two wise men.
How sad!
Tian Fu transferred his anger towards Guan Fu to Dou Ying, and his own life was short-lived.
Guan Fu was not supported by the people and eventually lost a bad reputation. How sad!
From this we can see the source of Guanfu’s disaster!
summary:
Dou Ying, the Marquis of Weiqi, was a relative of Empress Dowager Dou during the Han Dynasty. He served as the Prime Minister of Wu but was dismissed due to illness. During Emperor Jing's reign, he opposed the emperor's suggestion to pass the throne to his brother, King Xiao of Liang, angering Empress Dowager Dou. When the seven kingdoms rebelled, Emperor Jing appointed Dou Ying as a general. He recommended talented men, distributed his gold reward to subordinates, and successfully suppressed the rebellion, earning the title of Marquis of Weiqi. He later served as the tutor of Prince Li but was deposed after arguing for the prince. He retired but was persuaded to return to court. Despite Empress Dowager Dou's recommendation, Emperor Jing refused to make him prime minister, citing his arrogance.

Tian Fen, the Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing's queen. Initially humble, he rose to prominence after Emperor Jing's death, becoming a favored official. He became prime minister and Taiwei, promoting Confucianism and clashing with Empress Dowager Dou's preference for Taoism. After her death, Tian Fen became prime minister, growing arrogant and powerful. He built lavish residences and accumulated wealth, while Dou Ying lost influence and was alienated.

Guan Fu, a brave general, gained fame during the seven kingdoms' rebellion by charging into enemy lines. He later became a governor but was dismissed for legal violations. He was known for his straightforwardness, generosity to the poor, and disdain for the powerful. He accumulated wealth and became tyrannical in Yingchuan. After losing power, he befriended Dou Ying, and they supported each other.

Tian Fen once promised to visit Dou Ying but failed to show, causing Guan Fu to confront him. Tian Fen later sought to seize Dou Ying's land, leading to a feud. Tian Fen accused Guan Fu of tyranny, and Guan Fu retaliated by exposing Tian Fen's corruption. At a banquet, Guan Fu insulted Tian Fen, who had him arrested and charged with disrespect. Dou Ying tried to save Guan Fu but failed. Tian Fen slandered Dou Ying, leading to his imprisonment. Dou Ying claimed to have an imperial edict from Emperor Jing, but it was not found in records, resulting in his execution for forgery. Guan Fu and his family were also executed. Tian Fen later fell ill, haunted by the ghosts of Dou Ying and Guan Fu, and died. His son's title was revoked after a crime.

The historian comments that Dou Ying and Tian Fen rose through family connections, while Guan Fu gained fame through bravery. Dou Ying failed to adapt to changing circumstances, and Guan Fu lacked humility, leading to their downfall. Tian Fen abused his power and framed innocent men, resulting in his own demise.

translation:
Wei Bao was originally the son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period.
His elder brother is Wei Jiu, who was named Lord Ningling when he was in Wei State.
After the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, he was exiled to other places and became a commoner.
Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, and Wei Jiu followed him.
King Chen sent Zhou Shi, a native of Wei, to lead troops to seize the land of Wei. After Wei was captured, everyone discussed with each other and wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei. Zhou Shi said: Only when the world is in chaos can loyal ministers be revealed.
Now that the whole world is rebelling against Qin, morally speaking, we must support the descendants of King Wei.
Qi and Zhao each sent fifty chariots, hoping to establish Zhoushi as the king of Wei.
Zhou Shi refused to accept the offer and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu.
After five trips in total, King Chen agreed to send Wei Jiu back and establish him as King of Wei.
Not long after Zhang Han defeated King Chen, he marched to Linji to attack King Wei. King Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements.
Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army to follow Zhou City to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han actually defeated the reinforcements, killed Zhou Shi, and surrounded Linji.
Wei Jiu proposed conditions for surrender for the sake of the soldiers and people in the city.
After the negotiation was successful, Wei Jiu set himself on fire and died.
Wei Bao fled to Chu. King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao thousands of troops and went back to capture Wei.
By this time Xiang Yu had defeated the Qin army and surrendered to Zhang Han.
Wei Bao captured more than 20 cities one after another. Xiang Yu made Wei Bao King of Wei.
Wei Bao led his elite troops and followed Xiang Yu into the pass.
In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu divided the princes among the feudal lords. He planned to occupy the Liang land, so he moved King Bao of Wei to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty.
The King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties and led his troops across the Yellow River from Linjin. Wei Bao surrendered the entire country to the King of Han and followed the King of Han to Pengcheng to attack the Chu army.
The king of Han was defeated and returned to Xingyang. Wei Bao asked for leave and went home to visit his mother's condition. After returning home, he immediately cut off the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han.
Although the King of Han heard the news of Wei Bao's rebellion, he was worried about the Chu State in the east. He had no time to attack him, so he said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao for me. If you can persuade him, I will make you the Marquis of Wanhu.
Li Sheng went to lobby Wei Bao.
Wei Bao politely refused and said: Life is as short as the shadow of the sun passing through the crack in the wall.
Now the King of Han is arrogant and insults others at will. He scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no etiquette at all. I can't bear to see him.
So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured Wei Bao in Hedong, and escorted him to Xingyang in a post car, and changed Wei Bao's original territory into three counties.
The King of Han ordered Wei Bao to garrison Xingyang.
When the Chu army tightened its siege, Zhou Ke killed Wei Bao.
Peng Yue was from Changyi, with the courtesy name Zhong.
He often fishes in Juye Lake and joins a group of people to commit robberies.
Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose up, and a young man said to Peng Yue: Many heroes are rushing to raise banners to resist the violent Qin Dynasty. You can stand up, and we will follow their example.
Peng Yue said: Now is the time for the two dragons to fight, so let's wait.
More than a year later, more than a hundred young people from Zezhong gathered to follow Peng Yue and said, "Please be our leader."
Peng Yue refused and said: I don't want to work with you.
The young people persisted in their request, and he agreed.
Make an appointment with them to gather when the sun rises the next day, and those who are late will be beheaded.
When the sun came up the next day, more than ten people were late, and the last one didn't come until noon.
At that time, Peng Yue said apologetically: I am old and you insist on making me the leader.
Now, if there are many people late at the appointed time, we cannot behead all of them, but only the last person to come.
Order the captain to kill him.
Everyone laughed and said: "Why bother? I just don't dare to be late again from now on."
So Peng Yue took the last person who arrived and killed him. Set up an earthen altar, use human heads to offer sacrifices, and give orders to everyone who belongs to them.
Everyone was shocked and afraid of Peng Yue. No one dared to look up at him.
So he led everyone to seize the land and collected more than a thousand soldiers who had fled from the princes.
Peigong went north from Dang to attack Changyi, and Peng Yue assisted him.
Changyi was not captured, so Pei Gong led the army to march west.
Peng Yue also led his troops to garrison in Juye Ze to collect the fleeing soldiers of Wei.
Xiang Ji entered Guanzhong and divided the feudal lords, and then returned. Peng Yue's army had grown to more than 10,000 people, but he had no one to belong to.
In the autumn of the first year of Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed King Xiang, so he sent someone to give General Peng Yue a seal and asked him to march to Jiyin to attack the Chu army.
The Chu army ordered Xiao Gongjiao to lead his troops to attack Peng Yue, but was severely defeated by Peng Yue.
In the spring of the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han, King Bao of Wei and various princes went east to attack Chu. Peng Yue led more than 30,000 troops to join the King of Han in Waihuang.
The King of Han said: General Peng has recovered more than a dozen cities in Wei and is eager to support the descendants of King Wei.
Today, King Bao of Wei is the cousin of King Jiu of Wei and a descendant of the real King of Wei.
He appointed Peng Yue as the Prime Minister of Wei State, monopolizing military power and pacifying the Liang Dynasty.
After the King of Han was defeated in Pengcheng, he retreated westward. At this time, Peng Yue abandoned all the cities he had captured and led his army alone to the north to station along the Yellow River.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue often traveled and sent troops on behalf of the Han Dynasty, attacked the Chu army, and cut off their supply of food and grass in Liang.
In the winter of the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang and King Han were at a stalemate in Xingyang, and Peng Yue captured seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang.
When King Xiang heard the news, he sent Cao Jiu to garrison Chenggao, and he led his army eastward to recover the cities that Pengyue had conquered, returning them to Chu.
Peng Yue led his team north to Gucheng.
In the autumn of the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang's army retreated south to Xia Yang. Peng Yue captured more than 20 cities near Changyi and seized more than 100,000 bushels of grain, which was used as ration for the King of Han.
The king of Han was defeated and sent an envoy to ask Peng Yue to join forces to attack the Chu army.
Peng Yue said: Wei has just been pacified, but it is still afraid of the Chu army and cannot go there.
The king of Han raised his troops to pursue the Chu army, but was defeated by Xiang Ji in Guling.
He then said to Zhang Liang, who was waiting for him, "What should we do if the troops of the princes do not come to join the battle?"
Zhang Liang said: It is not your intention for King Han Xin of Qi to stand on his own feet, and Han Xin himself has no determination.
Peng Yue originally pacified the Liang region and made many military exploits. At first, because of Wei Bao, you only appointed Peng Yue as the prime minister of Wei.
Now, Wei Bao is dead and has no descendants, and Peng Yue also plans to become king, but you did not make a decision early.
You have made a private agreement with the two countries: if the Chu State is defeated, the land north of Suiyang to each city will be enfeoffed to Peng Xiangguo as king; the coastal area east of Chen will be enfeoffed to Qi King Han Xin.
The hometown of Qi King Han Xin was in Chu State, and his original intention was to regain his hometown.
If you can take out these lands and agree to divide them between the two of them, they can be recruited soon. Even if they cannot come, the development of the matter will not be completely despairing.
So the king of Han sent an envoy to Peng Yue to follow the plan of staying and waiting.
As soon as the envoy arrived, Peng Yue led all his troops to join the Han army at Gaixia and defeated the Chu army.
Xiang Ji is dead.
In the spring of that year, Pengyue was granted the title of King of Liang and his capital was established in Dingtao.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue went to Chendi to meet with Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Nine or ten years later, they all came to Chang'an to see him.
In the autumn of the tenth year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled in Dai. Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally led his troops to crusade. When he arrived at Handan, he asked the King of Liang to recruit troops and horses.
The king of Liang said that he was ill and sent his generals and troops to Handan.
Emperor Gao was very angry and sent someone to blame King Liang.
King Liang was very frightened and planned to go to apologize in person.
His general Hu Zhe said: The king did not go in the first place, but he went after being scolded by him. If he did, he would be captured.
It would be better to send troops to rebel.
The king of Liang did not listen to his advice and still said that he was ill.
King Liang was very angry with his servant and planned to kill him.
The servant hurriedly fled to Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty and accused King Liang and Hu Zou of conspiring to rebel.
So the emperor sent envoys to attack King Liang unexpectedly. King Liang was unaware of this, so he arrested King Liang and imprisoned him in Luoyang.
After trial by the officials in charge, they believed that he had sufficient evidence for treason and requested the emperor to sentence him according to law.
The emperor pardoned him, deposed him as a commoner, and exiled him to Qingyi County, Shu.
When Peng Yue was escorted west to Zheng County, Empress Lu happened to be coming from Chang'an and was going to Luoyang. On the way, she met King Peng. King Peng cried to Empress Lu and personally told her that she was not guilty and hoped to return to her hometown Changyi.
Empress Lu agreed and went east to Luoyang with him.
Queen Lu stated to the emperor: King Peng is a heroic and brave man. Now that he is exiled to Shu, he will bring trouble to himself. It is better to kill him.
So, I brought him back with me.
Therefore, Empress Lu asked Peng Yue's retainers to accuse him of plotting to rebel again.
Tingwei Wang Tiankai submitted a petition to kill Peng Yue's family, and the emperor approved it, so Peng Yue was killed, his family was killed, and his feudal state was abolished.
Tai Shigong said: Although Wei Bao and Peng Yue were born in poverty, they occupied thousands of miles of vast land like rolled mats and became kings in the south. They followed the enemy's bloodstains to pursue victory, and their fame grew day by day.
With a rebellious intention, when he failed, he failed to kill himself to become famous, but he was willing to be a prisoner, and even himself was killed. Why?
People with average intelligence and above are ashamed of their behavior, let alone those who are kings!
The reason why they endured the humiliation was for no other reason than because their wisdom and strategy were superior to others, and they were only worried about not being able to save their own lives.
As long as they can hold a little bit of power, they can perform their actions as the political situation changes, so they are imprisoned without escaping.

Wei Bao, son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period, had his elder brother Wei Jiu named Lord Ningling. After Qin destroyed Wei, Wei Bao became a commoner. Peng Yue, from Changyi, fished and robbed in Juye Lake. After Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose, youths urged him to lead, but he delayed. Over a year later, over a hundred youths insisted, and he agreed, executing a latecomer to enforce discipline. He gathered followers and assisted Peigong (Liu Bang) in attacking Changyi. In the tenth year, Chen Xi rebelled; Peng Yue feigned illness, angering Emperor Gao. Accused of conspiracy, he was arrested, pardoned to commoner status, and exiled. Empress Lu, fearing his influence, had him executed and his family exterminated.

Tai Shigong comments: Though Wei Bao and Peng Yue rose from poverty to become kings, their failure to die for honor and willingness to be prisoners led to their deaths. Their endurance of humiliation stemmed from superior strategy and fear for their lives, hoping to seize power as circumstances changed.
