translation:
Lu Zhonglian was a native of Qi.
He is good at analyzing unique, grand and extraordinary strategies, but he is unwilling to serve as an official and is willing to maintain high integrity.
He once visited Zhao State.
When Zhao Xiaocheng was king, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to lead an army to defeat Zhao Changping's army, killing more than 400,000 people in total. As a result, Qin's army advanced eastward and besieged Handan, the capital of Zhao.
King Zhao was very afraid, and no one from the reinforcements from the vassal states dared to attack the Qin army.
King Anli of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead troops to rescue Zhao. However, he was afraid of the Qin army and stationed in Tangyin and did not dare to advance.
The king of Wei sent his guest general Xinyuan Yan into Handan through a hidden path, and met with the king of Zhao through Pingyuan Jun. He said: The reason why the Qin army is eager to besiege Zhao is because it used to compete with King Qi Min to become emperor, and soon King Qi Min revoked the title of emperor.
If Zhao can send envoys to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor, King Qin will be very happy and will withdraw his troops.
Mr. Pingyuan was hesitant and unable to make a decision.
At this time, Lu Zhonglian traveled to the State of Zhao and caught up with the Qin army to besiege Handan. He heard that the State of Wei wanted Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao and proclaim himself emperor, so he went to Jin to see Lord Pingyuan and said: "What are we going to do about this?"
Mr. Pingyuan said: How dare we talk about such a big event in our country!
Not long ago, 400,000 troops were lost abroad, and now they are surrounded by the Qin army in Handan, and they cannot make them retreat.
The King of Wei sent the guest general Xinyuan Yan to ask the State of Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor. This man is still here.
How dare I talk about such a big thing!
Lu Zhonglian said: I used to think that you were the most virtuous son in the world, but today I know that you are not the most virtuous son in the world.
Where is Wei Guo's guest Xinyuan Yan?
I will blame him for you and send him back.
Mr. Pingyuan said: I would like to introduce you to Mr. Pingyuan.
So Mr. Pingyuan met Xinyuan Yan and said: "There is a Mr. Lu Zhonglian in Qi State. He is here now. Please let me introduce him to you so that he can get to know the general and make friends."
Xinyuan Yan said: I heard that Mr. Lu Zhonglian is a noble person in Qi State.
I am a minister of the King of Wei, and I have been ordered to be an envoy and bear my responsibilities. I do not want to see Mr. Lu Zhonglian.
Mr. Pingyuan said: I have revealed the news that you are here.
Niiguan Yan had no choice but to agree.
Lu Zhonglian saw Xinyuan Yan but said nothing.
Xinyuan Yan said: I think those who stay in this besieged city are all people who seek help from Lord Pingyuan. But now, I don’t think Mr.’s appearance looks like someone who wants help from Lord Pingyuan. Why do you stay in this besieged city for a long time and not leave?
Lu Zhonglian said: The world thinks that Bao Jiao committed suicide because of his narrow-mindedness. This view is completely wrong.
Most people don't understand his shame in living in a troubled world, and think he just has personal agenda.
The Qin State was a country that abandoned etiquette and only valued military merit. It treated its soldiers with power and deceit and enslaved its people like slaves.
If it were allowed to proclaim itself emperor without restraint and rule the world, I would rather jump into the East China Sea and die than be its obedient citizen. The reason why I came to see the general was to help Zhao.
Niiguan Yan said: How do you plan to help Zhao Guo, sir?
Lu Zhonglian said: I will ask Wei and Yan to help it. Qi and Chu have already helped Zhao.
Xinyuan Yan said: Yan State, I believe I will listen to you; as for Wei State, I am from Wei State. How can I ask Wei State to help Zhao State?
Lu Zhonglian said: Wei did not see clearly the dangers of Qin's proclaiming emperor. If Wei could see the dangers of Qin's proclaiming emperor, he would definitely help Zhao.
Xinyuan Yan said: What disaster will happen if Qin becomes emperor?
Lu Zhonglian said: In the past, King Wei of Qi once pursued benevolence and righteousness and led the princes of the world to pay homage to the Emperor of Zhou.
At that time, the Emperor Zhou was poor and weak, and no princes were willing to go to worship him. Only the state of Qi went to worship him.
More than a year later, King Zhou Lie died, and King Qi was late for the funeral. The newly succeeded King Zhou Xian was very angry and sent people to Qi State to report the funeral and said: The death of the emperor is as big as the earth falling apart. The newly succeeded emperor also has to leave the palace to mourn and sleep on a straw mat. Tian Yingqi, a minister of the eastern vassal country, dares to be late and should be executed.
After hearing this, King Qi Wei became furious and cursed: Bah! Your mother is nothing but a maid!
King Qi Wei was finally ridiculed by everyone in the world.
The reason why King Qi Wei went to see Emperor Zhou when he was alive and cursed him loudly when he was dead was because he couldn't stand Emperor Zhou's harsh demands.
Those who are emperors are like this, so there is nothing to be surprised about.
Niiguan Yan said: Sir, haven't you seen the slave?
If ten slaves serve one master, are they unable to match their master's strength or intelligence?
It's because I'm afraid of him. Lu Zhonglian said: Alas!
Comparing the King of Wei and the King of Qin, are they like servants and masters? Niiguan Yan said: Yes.
Lu Zhonglian said: Then, I will let the King of Qin cook the King of Wei and chop him into meat sauce?
Araguan Yan was very unhappy and said unconvinced: Oops! What you said, sir, is too much!
How could you let the King of Qin cook the King of Wei and chop him into meat sauce?
Lu Zhonglian said: Of course, I can tell you.
In the past, Jiuhou, Ehou, and Wenwang were the three princes of Yin Zhou.
Jiuhou had a beautiful daughter, so he dedicated her to Yin Zhou. However, King Zhou thought she was not beautiful, so he chopped her into pieces.
The Marquis of E was forthright in his remonstrances, argued fiercely, and killed the Marquis of E to make dried meat.
When King Wen heard this, he just sighed deeply, so King Zhou imprisoned him in Youli Prison for a hundred days, hoping to kill him.
Why do you become king like others, only to end up being chopped into meat paste and made into jerky?
When King Min of Qi went to the State of Lu, Yiweizi drove his chariot and served as his entourage. He said to the officials of Lu State: How are you going to receive our king?
The officials of the State of Lu said: We intend to receive your king with the etiquette of ten Tailao.
Yiweizi said: Where do you follow the etiquette to receive our king? My king is the emperor.
When the emperor goes to inspect various countries, the princes should move out of the main palace and move to other places. They should hand over the keys, lift up their clothes, arrange a few tables, and stand in the hall to serve the emperor's meal. After the emperor has finished eating, he can return to the court to listen to the governor.
After hearing this, the officials of the State of Lu closed the gate and locked it up, preventing King Qi Min from entering.
King Min of Qi could not enter the state of Lu, so he planned to go to Xuedi via the state of Zou.
At this time, the king of Zou State passed away, and the king wanted to go into the mirror to mourn. Yiweizi said to the heir of Zou State: When the emperor is mourning, the mourner must change the direction of the coffin and place the coffin facing north in the south. Then the emperor faces south to mourn.
The ministers of Zou State said: This must be the case, we would rather commit suicide with swords.
Therefore the king did not dare to enter the kingdom of Zou.
The ministers of Zou and Lu were unable to serve the king well during his lifetime, and they could not assist in the funeral ceremony after the death of the king. However, they wanted to perform the rites of the emperor in Zou and Lu, and the ministers of Zou and Lu finally refused to allow King Qi Min to enter the mirror.
Today, Qin is a country with ten thousand chariots, and Wei is also a country with ten thousand chariots.
They are all big countries with ten thousand chariots, and each has his own title of king. If it only wins a battle, he will obediently support it and call it emperor. This makes the ministers of the Three Jin Dynasties inferior to the servants and concubines of Zou and Lu.
If the Qin State is greedy enough and finally proclaims itself emperor, then the ministers of the princes will be replaced.
He will depose those he deems unworthy and replace them with those he deems worthy; he will depose those he deems unworthy and replace them with those he loves.
How could the King of Wei live a peaceful life when his children and troublemaking concubines were also allowed to be married to princes as concubines and live in the palace of Wei?
And how can you, general, gain your original favor?
At this time, Xinyuan Yan stood up, bowed to Lu Zhong twice and apologized, saying: "At first I thought you were an ordinary person, but today I know that you are a wise man in the world."
I will leave Zhao State and no longer dare to talk about King Qin proclaiming himself emperor.
When the Qin army general heard the news, he withdrew his army fifty miles.
It happened that Wei Gongzi Wuji seized the military power of Jin Bi and led the army to rescue Zhao and attack the Qin army, so the Qin army withdrew from Handan and returned.
Lord Pingyuan wanted to reward Lu Zhonglian, but Lu Zhonglian repeatedly refused and refused to accept.
Lord Pingyuan held a banquet in honor of him. When his ears were full of wine, Lord Pingyuan stood up and offered a thousand pieces of gold as a reward to Lu Zhonglian.
Lu Zhonglian said with a smile: The reason why outstanding people are respected by people in the world is because they can eliminate troubles, eliminate disasters, and resolve disputes without asking for compensation.
If you ask for remuneration, it will become a businessman's behavior. I, Lu Zhonglian, cannot bear to do that.
So I bid farewell to Lord Pingyuan and left, never to see each other again for the rest of our lives.
More than twenty years after this incident, a Yan general captured Qi State's Liaocheng. Someone in Liaocheng spoke ill of General Yan in front of King Yan. General Yan was afraid of being executed, so he stayed in Liaocheng and did not dare to go back.
Qi Guotian attacked Liaocheng alone for more than a year. Many soldiers died, but he could not capture Liaocheng.
Lu Zhonglian wrote a letter, tied it to an arrow and shot it into the city to General Yan.
The letter read:
I heard that a wise person will not go against the current situation and give up a favorable opportunity, a brave person will not avoid death and ruin his reputation, and a loyal minister will not take care of himself first and then the king.
Now you are venting your temporary anger and not taking into account that the King of Yan cannot control his ministers, which is disloyal; you die in battle, lose Liaocheng, and your reputation cannot be extended in Qi, which is not brave; your achievements fail, your reputation is ruined, and future generations will have nothing to say, it is unwise.
These three types of people will not be used as ministers by the current monarchs, and will not be recorded by lobbyists. Therefore, smart people will not be hesitant, and warriors will not be greedy for life and afraid of death.
Now is the key to life and death, honor and disgrace, dignity and inferiority. You cannot make a decision at this time, and the opportunity will never come again. I hope you will make detailed plans and not be like ordinary people.
Moreover, Chu State attacked Qi State's Nanyang, and Wei State attacked Qi State's Pinglu. However, Qi State had no intention of counterattacking south. It believed that the loss of losing Nanyang was small and outweighed the benefits of capturing Jibei, so it made such a decision to implement it.
Now that the Qin State has sent troops, the Wei State does not dare to march eastward; the situation of the Qin State's continuous alliance has formed, and the Chu State's situation is dangerous; Qi State abandons Nanyang, cedes the territory on the right without saving it, and pacifies Jibei, which is a decision made after weighing the pros and cons.
Besides, Qi State is determined to recapture Liaocheng, so you should not hesitate any longer. Now the armies of Chu and Wei have withdrawn from Qi State and Yan State’s reinforcements have not arrived.
All the troops of Qi State have no other aspirations for the world and are attacking Liaocheng with all their strength. If you still want to defend Liaocheng, which has been besieged for more than a year, I don't think you can do it.
Moreover, the Yan State was in turmoil, and the emperor and his ministers were helpless and confused. Li Fu led an army of 100,000 to fight five consecutive defeats abroad. However, the great country with 10,000 chariots was surrounded by the State of Zhao. The land was reduced, the king was trapped, and he was ridiculed by the people of the world.
The country is in decline, disasters abound, and the people's hearts are in disarray.
Now, you use the exhausted soldiers and civilians of Liaocheng to resist the attack of the entire Qi army, which is like Mo Zhai defending Songcheng.
When food and grass were exhausted, they ate human flesh to satisfy their hunger. They had no firewood and burned human bones, but the soldiers did not have the heart to rebel. This is like Sun Bin who is good at leading troops.
Your ability has been revealed to the world.
Even so, for your sake, it is better to preserve our troops and use them to thank the State of Yan.
The king of Yan will be happy if his troops return to the country of Yan in good condition; if his body returns to his country, the people will feel like they are seeing their parents again, friends will praise and praise him excitedly when they get together, and his achievements will be displayed.
On the one hand, it assists the monarch in commanding the ministers; on the other hand, it not only supports the people but also provides lobbyists, corrects state affairs, changes customs, and builds career and reputation.
If you do not have the intention to return to the Yan State, abandon the Yan State, abandon worldly opinions, and go east to the Qi State. The Qi State will divide the land and enfeoff it, so that you can be as rich and powerful as Wei Ran and Shang Yang.
These two options are good ideas to show off your reputation and are rich and affordable. I hope you will choose one of them carefully after careful consideration.
I heard that those who seek small details cannot achieve a glorious reputation, and those who are ashamed of small things cannot achieve great achievements.
In the past, Guan Zhong shot Duke Huan's belt hook, which was a crime. Giving up Prince Jiu instead of letting him die was cowardly. Being imprisoned with instruments of torture was a shame.
For a person with these three conditions, the king will not use him as a minister and the villagers will not associate with him.
If Guanzi had been imprisoned for a long time and died in prison without being able to return to Qi, he would have had a shameful and despicable reputation.
Even Nu Bei is ashamed to have the same name as him, let alone the public opinion in society!
Therefore, Guan Zhong did not feel ashamed because he was in prison, but he felt ashamed that the world could not be at peace. He did not feel ashamed that he could not die with his son Jiu, but he felt ashamed that he could not show his prestige among the princes. Therefore, although he had the triple fault of committing crimes, fearing death, and being humiliated, he assisted Duke Huan of Qi to become the leader of the five hegemons. His reputation was higher than anyone else in the world, and his glory shone on neighboring countries.
After Cao Mo became a general of Lu, he failed in many battles and lost 500 miles of land.
If Cao Mo had cut his throat and committed suicide without careful consideration and hastily made a plan, he would have been infamous as a defeated general.
Cao Mo ignored the humiliation of being defeated many times and came back to discuss matters with Lord Lu.
Taking advantage of Duke Huan's opportunity to convene the princes of the world, Cao Mo used a dagger to get close to Duke Huan's heart on the altar. His face remained unchanged and his speech was calm. He defeated the lost land many times and regained it in a short time. The world was shaken, the princes were horrified, and the reputation of Lu was higher than that of Wu and Yue.
Like these two patriots, it is not that they disregard the honor and integrity of the whole family and think that if they die, their reputation will be destroyed and their achievements will not be established. This is not a wise approach.
Therefore, give up temporary anger and establish a lifelong reputation; give up temporary anger and establish achievements for generations to come.
Therefore, these deeds and the achievements of the three kings compete to spread, and their reputation coexists with heaven and earth.
I hope you will choose one of these options and take action!
General Yan read Lu Zhonglian's letter and cried for several days, but still hesitated to make a decision.
He wanted to return to the Yan State, but there was already a rift, and he was afraid of being killed; he wanted to surrender to the Qi State, but too many Qi people had been killed and captured, and he was afraid that he would be humiliated after surrendering.
He sighed deeply and said: It is better to commit suicide than to let others kill me.
Just committed suicide.
Liaocheng was in chaos, so Tian Dan marched into Liaocheng and bloodbathed Liaocheng.
When he returned, he reported Lu Zhonglian's affairs to the King of Qi. The King of Qi wanted to knight him.
After hearing this, Lu Zhonglian fled to the seaside and lived in seclusion. He said: Instead of being rich and serving others, it is better for me to be poor and despise the world and let my own ambitions go.
Zou Yang is from Qi State.
When he traveled to Liang State, he interacted with Zhuang Ji, a native of Wu State, and Mei Cheng, a native of Huaiyin.
He wrote a letter of self-recommendation and was a disciple of King Liang Xiao among Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
Yang Sheng and others were jealous of Zou Yang and spoke ill of him in front of King Xiao of Liang.
King Xiao of Liang was very angry. He handed Zou Yang over to his subordinate officials and wanted to kill him.
Zou Yang traveled in the Liang Kingdom and was arrested for being slandered. Worried about being accused of unwarranted charges after his death, he wrote a letter to King Xiao of Liang from prison. He wrote: I heard that loyal people will be rewarded and honest people will not be suspected. I always thought it was right in the past, but today it seems to be just an empty talk.
In the past, Gao Yi, whom Jing Ke admired from Prince Dan of Yan, went to assassinate the King of Qin. Although there was a sign of a white rainbow penetrating the sun in the sky, Prince Dan of Yan was still worried that Jing Ke would regret it and did not dare to go; Mr. Wei planned the Changping event for the King of Qin, and there was also a sign that Venus would cover the Pleiades, but King Zhao of Qin was still full of doubts.
Their sincerity moved the world and showed signs, but they were not understood by the two masters Yan Dan and Zhao Wang. Isn't this sad!
Now I am trying my best to be loyal and give my best advice, hoping that your Majesty will adopt it. The people around you did not understand the situation and finally handed me over to the officials for interrogation. I was misunderstood by the world. Even if Jing Ke and Wei were resurrected, King Yan Dan and Qin Zhao would not wake up.
I hope your Majesty will examine this situation carefully.
In the past, Bian He offered jade, and the king of Chu chopped off his feet; Li Si tried his best to be loyal, but Hu Hai had him executed.
So Jizi pretended to be crazy and took his father into seclusion to hide from the world. They were all afraid of suffering such a disaster.
I hope your Majesty will carefully examine the sincerity of Bian He and Li Si, and don't believe in slander like King Chu and Hu Hai, and don't let me be ridiculed by Ji Zi and Jie Yu.
I heard that Bigan was disemboweled and Wu Zixu's body was put into a leather bag and thrown into the river. I didn't believe it at first, but now I know that such a thing happened.
I hope your Majesty will examine it carefully and show me a little mercy!
As the saying goes: Some people are strangers even after getting along with them for a long time, while some people feel like old friends as soon as they stop and talk.
What is this wish for?
It lies in knowing one's heart and not knowing one's heart.
Therefore, in the past, Fan Yuqi fled from Qin to Yan, and lent his head to Jing Ke to carry out Yan Dan's mission of assassinating the King of Qin; Wang She left Qi for Wei, and committed suicide on the city wall to retreat the Qi army and protect Wei.
Wang She and Fan Yuqi were not new friends with Qi and Qin, but old acquaintances with Yan and Wei. The reason why they left Qi and Qin to die for the two kings of Yan and Wei was because their actions and aspirations were consistent and they had infinite admiration for justice!
Therefore, Su Qin was not trusted by the people of the world, but he was as trustworthy to the Yan State as his first son; Bai Gui was defeated and lost the cities of the Six Kingdoms, but he captured Zhongshan for the Wei State.
Why is this?
It's really because of mutual acquaintance.
Su Qin was appointed as the Prime Minister of the Yan State. Someone from the State of Yan slandered him in front of the king. The King of Yan was angry with his sword and slaughtered his beloved horse and gave him the meat to eat.
Why is this?
The two masters and two ministers were so heart-to-heart and believed so deeply, how could they be swayed by rumors?
Therefore, regardless of whether a woman is beautiful or ugly, she will be jealous when she enters the court; whether a scholar is virtuous or unworthy, he will be jealous when he enters the court and becomes an official.
In the past, Sima happy was punished by having his kneecaps cut off in the Song Dynasty and finally became the prime minister of the Zhongshan Kingdom. Fan Sui had his ribs broken and teeth knocked out in the Wei Kingdom, and was finally made a Marquis of Ying by the Qin Kingdom.
Both of these people abide by certain rules and abstain from forming parties for personal gain. They are in a lonely position, so they are not immune to the persecution of jealous villains.
The reason why Shentu Di threw himself into the river and Xu Yan threw himself into the sea with stones in his arms was because they were not tolerated by the world, adhered to justice and were unscrupulous, and did not form cliques in the court for selfish purposes to shake the monarch's will.
So Baili Xi was begging on the road, and Duke Mu of Qin entrusted him with the affairs of state; Ning Qi was feeding cattle under the cart, and Duke Huan of Qi entrusted him with the administration of state affairs.
Could it be that these two people relied on the recommendation of officials and the praise of their cronies in the court to win the trust of Duke Mu and Duke Huan?
Inspiration is in the heart, unity is in action, intimacy is like glue, and inseparable like brothers. How can we still be deceived by so many slanders?
Therefore, only listening to one side of the story will lead to evil, and only using a few people will lead to disaster.
In the past, Lord Lu only believed in Ji Sun's words and drove away Confucius; Lord Song only believed in Zihan's strategy and imprisoned Mo Zhai.
The eloquence of Confucius and Mozi was not immune to the harm of slander, so the two countries of Lu and Song were in crisis.
Why is this?
If everyone agrees, even gold and stone will melt; if there is too much slander, even the relationship between flesh and blood will be destroyed.
Therefore, Duke Mu of Qin appointed Yu Yu, a Rong man, to dominate China; Qi State appointed Yue Meng, and made the two generations of King Wei and King Xuan strong.
Are the two countries of Qin and Qi stuck to popular customs, implicated in the world's customs, and bound by flattery and paranoid slander?
They listen to opinions fairly, observe things comprehensively, and maintain a good reputation in the world.
Therefore, if one's mind is in harmony, even if a foreigner is from Yue, one can be as close as a brother, as is the case with Yu Yu and Yue Meng; if one's mind is not in harmony, even the flesh and blood of the closest relatives will be driven away without leaving behind, as is the case with Zhu, Xiang, Guan, and Cai.
Today, if the monarch can adopt the methods of Qi and Qin and abandon the mistakes of Song and Lu, then the achievements of the five hegemons are not worthy of praise, and the achievements of the three kings are easy to achieve.
Therefore, if a wise monarch has a clear mind, abandons the hypocritical heart of Zi Zhi, and does not appreciate Tian Chang's false wisdom; if he imitates the descendants of King Wu of Zhou and appoints the loyal minister Bigan, and renovates the tombs of innocent pregnant women, then he will surely succeed in governing the world.
Why is this?
There is no satisfaction in following the good.
If Duke Wen of Jin gets close to his enemies, he can dominate the feudal lords; if Duke Huan of Qi appoints his former enemies, he can bring the world into order.
Why is this? Being kind-hearted, sincere to others, and influencing people's hearts with sincerity cannot be replaced by vain words.
When the Qin State appointed Shang Yang to carry out reforms, he weakened Han and Wei in the east, and his army became powerful in the world, but he was finally killed by his chariot. The Yue State adopted the strategy of Dafu Zhong, attacked and destroyed the powerful Wu State, and dominated China, but was finally killed.
Therefore, Sun Shuao left the position three times without regret; Yu Lingzhong resigned from the position of Sangong to water gardens for others.
Now if the king can really get rid of his arrogance, have the intention of letting others serve, reveal his confidants, show his true feelings, show courage and kindness, always share the joys and sorrows with others, and love the nobles, then even the arrogant dog can let him bite Yao, and Zhi's retainer can let him assassinate Xu You; not to mention you rely on the power of a great country and the talents of a holy king?
If this is the case, then Jing Ke is willing to risk the catastrophe of annihilating the seven clans and burning his wife and children to death. Is there anything worthy of praise?
I heard that although luminous pearls and luminous jade are treasures, if you throw them at pedestrians on the road in the dark, people will squint with their swords in surprise.
Why?
It's because the treasure was thrown in front of you for no reason.
The twisted tree roots are unique, but they can become objects of appreciation by the king.
And why?
It's because the people around the king have carved and beautified it in advance!
Therefore, treasures are thrown in front of you for no reason, even if they are a waiting pearl or a luminous jade, you still have to make a grudge and not please.
Therefore, if someone recommends it in advance, even a dead tree will make a contribution and will not be forgotten.
Nowadays, the common people and the scholars living in the back alleys are in a poor and humble environment. Even if they have the way of governing the country like Yao and Shun, have the eloquence of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, and have the ambition of Long Feng and Bigan, they intend to be loyal to the king of the day, but there is usually no one. With good words of recommendation, even if you try your best to dedicate your loyalty to assist the monarch in governing the country, then the monarch will definitely look at you sideways like a person throwing treasures. This is why the wise men in common cannot obtain the value of a dead tree!
Therefore, a sage monarch governs the country like a potter's fortune, with his own laws and regulations to educate the world, and will not be swayed by despicable opinions or changed by everyone's tongue.
Therefore, Qin Shihuang listened to the words of his concubine Meng Jia and believed Jing Ke's lies. Jing Ke was able to take out the dagger secretly and assassinate people unprepared. King Wen of Zhou was hunting in the Jing and Wei areas and carried him back to Lu Shang in a chariot, so that he could become the king of the world.
Therefore, King Qin listened to his ministers and was almost killed; King Wen of Zhou unexpectedly became king of the world.
Why is this?
Because King Wen of Zhou could transcend the restraints of the left and right, get rid of the restrained discussions of the world, and independently see the broad and bright road.
Nowadays, the king is indulged in flattery and flattery, surrounded by concubines and attendants, causing outstanding scholars to be mixed up with horses and old oxen. This is the reason why Bao Jiao is resentful of the world and has no nostalgia for wealth.
I heard that those who go to court solemnly and strictly will not be greedy for profit and moral integrity; those who pursue fame will not indulge their selfish desires and corrupt their character. Therefore, the county is called Shengmu, but Zengzi will not enter; the city is called Chaoge, and Mozi returns to his carriage and leaves.
Nowadays, if people with lofty ideals are frightened by the mighty power, suppressed by the high position, and deliberately use evil faces and dirty conduct to serve the flattering villains in order to get close to the king, then the ambitious people will die in the caves of old age. How can they be willing to follow the king with all their loyalty and faith?
This letter was presented to King Xiao of Liang, who sent someone to release Zou Yang from prison, and finally became King Xiao of Liang's honored guest.
Tai Shigong said: Even if the main purpose of Lu Zhonglian's discussion is not righteous, I applaud him for being a common man, free and easy, not yielding to the princes, commenting on the current world, but he has convinced the powerful ministers and prime ministers.
Even though Zou Yang's words are not modest enough, his comparisons between similar things are indeed touching. He can also be said to be frank, honest and unyielding, so I attach him to this biography.
summary:
Lu Zhonglian, a native of Qi, was skilled in grand strategies but refused to serve as an official, valuing integrity. During the siege of Handan by Qin, Zhao sought aid. Wei sent General Jin Bi, who hesitated, and envoy Xinyuan Yan proposed Zhao honor King Zhao of Qin as emperor to secure peace. Pingyuan Jun hesitated. Lu Zhonglian confronted Xinyuan Yan, arguing that submitting to Qin would bring disaster. He cited historical examples, such as King Wei of Qi’s humiliation by Zhou and the fates of Jiuhou and Ehou under Yin Zhou, to illustrate the dangers of imperial ambition. Lu declared he would rather die than serve Qin. Xinyuan Yan was convinced and withdrew his proposal. The Qin army retreated after Wei’s Prince Wuji rescued Zhao. Pingyuan Jun offered Lu a reward, but he refused, stating that a worthy person resolves conflicts without seeking payment, and left forever.

Over twenty years later, a Yan general held Qi’s Liaocheng. Lu Zhonglian wrote him a letter, urging him to choose wisely: return to Yan or surrender to Qi. He argued that clinging to a besieged city was unwise, citing Guan Zhong and Cao Mo as examples of those who overcame disgrace to achieve greatness. The general, torn between fear of execution and shame, committed suicide, leading to Qi’s capture of Liaocheng. Qi’s king offered Lu a title, but he fled to the seaside, preferring poverty to serving others.

Zou Yang, also from Qi, served King Xiao of Liang but was slandered by rivals and imprisoned. From prison, he wrote a letter defending his loyalty, citing historical figures like Bian He, Li Si, and Bigan, who suffered unjustly. He argued that true understanding between ruler and subject transcends slander, as seen with Su Qin and Yan, or Baili Xi and Duke Mu of Qin. He warned that listening to flattery leads to ruin, as with Lu and Song. King Xiao released him, and Zou became his honored guest.

Sima Qian comments that while Lu Zhonglian’s arguments may not be entirely righteous, his independence and ability to sway powerful figures are admirable. Zou Yang’s words, though immodest, are sincere and compelling, earning him a place in this biography.

Qingbu is from Liuxian County and his surname is Ying. During the Qin Dynasty, he was a common man.
When he was a child, a guest showed him a fortune and said: After being tortured, I will be king.
When he reached his prime, he broke the law and was sentenced to tattoo.
Tingbu smiled happily and said: Someone showed me a picture and said that I should be king after being tortured. Now, this is probably the situation, right?
Everyone who heard him say this laughed at him.
Not long after his conviction, Yingbu was sent to Lishan for hard labor. There were hundreds of thousands of prisoners in Lishan.
When Chen Sheng rebelled, Ying Bu went to see Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, and rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with his men, gathering a team of several thousand people.
Magistrate Fan even married his daughter to him.
After Zhang Han eliminated Chen Sheng and defeated Lu Chen's army, Yingbu led his troops north to attack Qin's left and right schools, defeated them at Qingbo, and then led his troops to advance eastward.
Yingbu heard that Xiang Liang had pacified Kuaiji in the east of the Yangtze River and crossed the Yangtze River to march west. Chen Ying led his army to Xiang Liang because Xiang had been the general of the Chu State for generations, and crossed the Huai River southward. Generals Yingbu and Pu also led their troops to join Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang led his troops across the Huaihe River and marched westward. In the battles against Jingju, Qin Jia and others, Qingbu was brave and good at fighting and was always ranked first among the troops.
Xiang Liang arrived in Xuedi and heard that King Chen was indeed dead, so he supported King Huai of Chu.
Xiang Liang was called Wu Xinjun, and Yingbu was called Dangyang Lord.
Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao. King Huai of Chu moved his capital to Pengcheng, and the generals and Yingbu also gathered in Pengcheng to guard it.
At this time, the Qin army stepped up its siege on Zhao State, and Zhao State repeatedly sent people to ask for help.
King Huai of Chu sent Song Yi as the top general, Fan Zeng as the last general, Xiang Ji as the second general, Yingbu and Pu as generals, all under Song Yi's command, to rescue Zhao State in the north.
When Xiang Ji killed Song Yi on the bank of the Yellow River, King Huai took advantage of the situation and appointed Xiang Ji as general, and all generals were under Xiang Ji's control.
Xiang Ji sent Yingbu to take the lead in crossing the Yellow River to attack the Qin army. Yingbu had the advantage due to his repeated military exploits. Xiang Ji led all his troops across the Yellow River and fought in coordination with Yingbu. They defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han and others to surrender.
The Chu army won many battles and conquered all the princes.
The reason why the armies of various princes can gradually surrender to Chu is because Yingbu can command the army to defeat many with less, which is impressive!
Xiang Ji led his troops westward to Xin'an, and sent Yingbu and others to attack at night and bury more than 200,000 Zhang Han's subordinates alive.
When they arrived outside Hangu Pass and could not enter, they sent Yingbu and others to take a small path to attack the defenders under the pass before entering the pass and reaching Xianyang City.
Yingbu often served as a pioneer.
King Xiang granted titles to the generals, named Yingbu the King of Jiujiang, and made six counties his capital.
In April of the first year of Han Dynasty, all the princes left the theater and returned to their respective feudal states.
King Xiang supported King Huai as the righteous emperor and moved the capital to Changsha, but secretly ordered Wang Yingbu of Jiujiang and others to sneak attack him on the way.
In August of that year, Yingbo sent generals to attack Emperor Yi and chased him to Chen County and killed him.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed the State of Chu. King Xiang went to attack Qi and mobilized troops to Jiujiang. The King of Jiujiang excused himself because he was seriously ill and could not go, so he only sent generals with several thousand people to enlist.
The king of Han defeated the Chu army in Pengcheng, and Yingbu excused himself from assisting Chu due to illness.
King Xiang resented Yingbu and repeatedly sent envoys to blame Yingbu and summon him to go. Yingbo became more and more frightened and did not dare to go.
King Xiang was worried about Qi and Zhao in the north, and worried about the Han Dynasty in the west. The only one he knew well was the King of Jiujiang. The King of Han particularly valued Yingbu's talents and planned to get close to him and appoint him, so he did not attack him.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han attacked Chu and launched a large-scale war in Pengcheng. After the defeat, he retreated from Liang and came to Yu County. He said to those close to him: People like you are not worthy of planning world affairs together.
Sui He, who was responsible for conveying the report, came forward and said, "I don't understand what your Majesty means."
The king of Han said: Who can send an envoy to Huainan for me, let them mobilize the army, betray Chu, and restrain King Xiang in Qi for a few months? Then I will be sure to seize the world.
Sui He said: I request to be sent as an envoy to Huainan.
The king of Han gave him twenty men to go on an envoy to Huainan.
After arriving, because Dazai was in charge, he waited for three days but could not see the King of Huainan.
Sui He took the opportunity to lobby Dazai and said: If the king doesn't summon me, he must think that Chu is strong and Han is weak. This is the reason why I am sent as an envoy.
I was summoned. If what I said was right, it was exactly what the king wanted to hear. But if what I said was wrong, let twenty of us lie on the chopping block and chop to death with an ax in Huainan Square. To show the king's intention to betray Han and get closer to Chu.
Dazai then conveyed the message to King Huainan, who received him.
Sui He said: The King of Han sent me to respectfully write a letter to the King. I secretly felt strange as to why the King was so close to the State of Chu.
King Huainan said: I face the north and serve him as a minister.
Sui He said: The king and King Xiang were both classified as princes, and they went north to serve him as ministers. They must have thought that the state of Chu was powerful and could entrust the country to him.
When King Xiang attacked Qi, he personally carried the tools to build the wall and took the lead. The king should dispatch all the troops in Huainan and lead them personally as the vanguard of the Chu army. Now he only sends four thousand people to help Chu.
Is this what the ministers who serve others are like when they face the north?
The King of Han is fighting in Pengcheng. Before King Xiang has sent troops to Qi, the king should mobilize all the troops in Huainan to cross the Huaihe River and help King Xiang and King of Han fight day and night under Pengcheng. The king has tens of thousands of people, but no one has crossed the Huaihe River. He is watching who wins and who loses with his clothes hanging down.
Is this what a person who entrusts his country to others is originally like?
The king pretends to be returning to Chu State, but he wants to rely on himself. I privately think that it is not advisable for the king to do this.
However, the king did not abandon Chu because he believed that Han was weak.
Even though Chu's army was strong, it still had a reputation of being unjust in the world because he broke the covenant and killed the Righteous Emperor.
However, the King of Chu thought he was powerful by virtue of his victory in the war. After the King of Han gathered the princes, he returned to garrison Chenggao and Xingyang. He transported grains from Shu and Han, dug deep trenches, built high barriers, and divided his troops to guard the border fortresses. If the Chu State wanted to withdraw its troops, there was Liang State in the middle, and the deep After entering the enemy's territory for eight or nine hundred miles, if you want to fight, you can't win, you can't attack the city, and the old and weak soldiers are transported thousands of miles away. When the Chu army reaches Xingyang and Chenggao, the Han army is standing still. It can't be broken when it attacks, and it can't escape the pursuit of the Han army when it retreats.
Therefore, Chu's army is not enough to rely on.
If the Chu army defeats the Han army, then the princes will be in danger and must rescue each other.
Once the state of Chu becomes powerful, it will be attacked by armies from all over the world.
Therefore, the situation of Chu State being inferior to Han State is obvious.
Now that the king is not friendly with the infallible Han State, but entrusts himself to the endangered Chu State, I privately feel puzzled for the king.
I don't think Huainan's army is enough to destroy Chu.
As long as the king sends troops to betray the Chu State, King Xiang will definitely be restrained. As long as he is restrained for a few months, the King of Han will be able to seize the world without fail.
I request you to carry a sword and surrender to the Han Kingdom. The King of Han will definitely divide the land and grant it to the king. Not to mention Huainan. Huainan will definitely belong to the king.
Therefore, the king of Han seriously sent envoys to propose immature strategies, hoping that the king would seriously consider them.
King Huainan said: I will follow your advice.
He secretly agreed to betray Chu and return to Han, but did not dare to reveal this secret.
At this time, the Chu State's envoy was still in Huainan, urging Yingbu to send troops and stayed in a guest house.
Sui He rushed in, sat on the table of Chu's envoys, and said, "The king of Jiujiang has surrendered to the king of Han. Why should Chu let him send troops?"
Yingbu looked surprised.
The envoy from Chu State stood up to leave.
Sui He took the opportunity to persuade Yingbu: "The important thing has been accomplished. We can kill the Chu envoy immediately. We cannot let him go back. Let's move closer to the Han Dynasty and fight together."
Yingbu said: Just follow your instructions and send troops to attack Chu.
So he killed the envoy and sent troops to attack Chu.
Chu State then sent Xiang Sheng and Long Qie to attack Huainan, while King Xiang stayed to attack Xiayi.
The war lasted for several months, and Long Qie defeated Yingbu's army in the battle of Huainan.
Yingbu wanted to lead his troops to retreat to Han, but he was afraid that Chu's army would intercept and kill him, so he and Suihe fled back to Han through a hidden trail.
When King Huainan arrived, the King of Han was sitting on the bed washing his feet, so he asked Yingbu to see him. When Yingbu saw this, he was so angry that he regretted coming and wanted to commit suicide.
When he exited and came to the hotel prepared for him, Yingbu was overjoyed again when he saw that the curtains, utensils, food, and attendant officials were as luxurious as those of the King of Han.
So he sent people to Jiujiang.
At this time, the King of Chu had sent Xiang Bo to recruit Jiujiang's troops and killed Yingbu's wife and children.
The people sent by Yingbu found Yingbu's friends and close subordinates, and took thousands of people to defect to the king of Han.
The king of Han gave Yingbu more troops and went north with him to recruit troops at Chenggao.
In July of the fourth year of Han Dynasty, the king of Han granted Yingbu the title of King of Huainan, and together with him he attacked Xiang Ji.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu sent people into Jiujiang and captured several counties.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu and Liu Jia entered Jiujiang and lured the great Sima Zhou Yin to surrender. After Zhou Yin rebelled against the Chu State, he mobilized the Jiujiang army and the Han army to jointly attack the Chu State and defeated the Chu army in Gaixia.
After Xiang Ji's death, the world was at peace. The emperor held a banquet, but belittled Sui He's achievements, saying that Sui He was a pedantic, conservative, and out-of-date scholar. How could such a person be used to govern the world.
Sui He knelt before the emperor and said: When your Majesty led troops to attack Pengcheng, the King of Chu had not yet left Qi. Your Majesty mobilized 50,000 infantry and 5,000 cavalry. Can you capture Huainan with this small force?
The emperor said: No.
Sui He said: Your Majesty sent me and 20 people as an envoy to Huainan. As soon as we arrived, Your Majesty got what he wanted. My contribution is greater than the 50,000 infantry and 5,000 cavalry.
But Your Majesty said that I am a pedantic, conservative and outdated scholar. Why is this? The emperor said: I am considering your contribution.
So he appointed Sui He as the guard lieutenant.
Yingbu cut off his talisman and became the king of Huainan. He established six counties as his capital. Jiujiang, Lujiang, Hengshan and Yuzhang counties all belonged to Yingbu.
In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu went to Chen County to meet the emperor.
In the eighth year of the Han Dynasty, he went to Luoyang to meet with him.
In the ninth year of Han Dynasty, he went to Chang'an to meet with him.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, Empress Gao executed Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, and Yingbu was frightened.
In the summer of this year, the king of Han killed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, and chopped him into meat paste. He packed the meat paste and gave it to the princes.
When he was sent to Huainan, the king of Huainan was hunting. He was particularly frightened when he saw the meat paste. He secretly made arrangements to gather troops to wait and detect the unexpected emergency in neighboring counties.
Yingbu's favored concubine fell ill and was sent to the doctor. The doctor's house lived across the street from the doctor's house. The concubine went to the doctor's house many times for treatment. Ben He thought that he was a servant, so he sent generous gifts and drank with his concubine at the doctor's house.
When my concubine was serving the King of Huainan, she praised Ben He as a loyal and honest person.
King Huainan said angrily: "How do you know?"
The concubine told him everything about their relationship.
The King of Huainan suspected that she had an adulterous relationship with Ben He.
Ben He was frightened and excused himself from going to work because he was sick.
The king of Huainan became even more angry and wanted to arrest Ben He.
Benhe wanted to report Yingbu's rebellion, so he took a post car to Chang'an.
Yingbu sent people to chase him but failed to catch up.
Ben He arrived in Chang'an and wrote a letter to declare rebellion, saying that Ying showed signs of rebellion and could be killed before the rebellion.
The emperor read his report and discussed it with Xiao Xiangguo. Xiangguo said: Yingbu should not have such a thing, I am afraid that he is framed because of a grudge.
Please imprison Ben He and send people to spy on King Huainan secretly.
When the King of Huainan saw that Ben He was absconding in fear of crime, he wrote a letter to change his words. He had already suspected that Ben He would reveal his secret arrangements, so the King of Han sent envoys again. After considerable verification, he killed Ben He's entire family and launched an army to rebel.
When news of the rebellion reached Chang'an, the emperor released Ben He and made him a general.
The emperor summoned the generals and asked: Yingbu rebels, what should be done to him?
The generals all said: Send troops to beat him and bury this kid alive, what else can we do!
Teng Gong, the Marquis of Ruyin, summoned Yin, the former magistrate of Chu State, to ask about this matter. Ling Yin said: He was supposed to be a rebel.
Teng Gong said: The emperor divided the land and made him the king, gave him titles to make him noble, faced the south to listen to the government and made him the lord of ten thousand chariots. Why did he rebel?
Ling Yin said: "Peng Yue was killed last year, and Han Xin was killed the year before. These three people have the same merits and are the same type of people. Naturally, they suspected that the disaster was affecting them, so they rebelled."
Teng Gong told the emperor these words and said: My retainer is the former Chu State Commander Yin Xue Gong. This man is very wise. You can ask him.
The emperor summoned Duke Xue.
Duke Xue replied: It is not surprising that Yingbu rebelled.
If Yingbu comes up with a good plan, the Shandong region will no longer belong to the Han Dynasty; if he comes up with a middle plan, it's hard to say who will win; if he comes up with a bad plan, your majesty can rest easy.
The emperor said: What is the best policy?
Ling Yin replied: If we seize Wu State to the east, Chu State to the west, annex Qi State, occupy Lu State, and send a message to Yan and Zhao to stick to their homeland, Shandong area will no longer belong to the King of Han.
The emperor asked again: What is Zhongce?
Ling Yin replied: Go east to capture Wu, go west to capture Chu, annex South Korea and capture Wei, seize Aoyu's grain, blockade Chenggao's main roads, it is difficult to predict who will win and who will lose.
The emperor asked again: What is the next step?
Ling Yin replied: If you seize Wu State to the east, Xia Cai to the west, move the baggage and treasures to Yue State, and run to Changsha yourself, your Majesty will be able to sleep at ease. The Han Dynasty was fine.
The emperor said: Which strategy will Yingbu choose?
Ling Yin replied: Choose the next best thing.
The emperor said: Why did he give up the best policy or the middle policy and choose the worst policy?
Ling Yin said: Yingbu was originally a prisoner of Lishan, and he worked hard to become the master of ten thousand chariots. This was all for his own wealth, without caring about the current people or future generations, so he chose the wrong strategy. The emperor said: Well said.
Grant Xue Gong the title of Marquis of Thousand Households.
The prince Liu Chang was canonized as King of Huainan.
The emperor mobilized the army and personally led the eastward attack on Yingbu.
At the beginning of the rebellion, Yingbu said to his generals: The emperor is old and hates fighting. He must not be able to lead troops in person and send generals. The generals are only afraid of Huaiyin and Peng Yue. Now that they are dead, the other generals have nothing to fear.
So rebelled.
As Duke Xue expected, he went east to attack Jing State. King Liu Jia of Jing fled and died in Fuling.
Yingbu hijacked all his troops and crossed the Huaihe River to attack Chu.
The state of Chu mobilized its troops to fight Yingbu between Xu and Tong. The state of Chu divided its troops into three groups and tried to adopt a strange strategy of mutual rescue.
Someone advised the Chu general: Yingbu is good at using troops to fight, and the people have always been afraid of him.
Moreover, the Art of War says: When princes fight the enemy in their own territory, once the soldiers are in danger, they will flee.
Now the troops are divided into three groups. As long as they defeat one of our troops, the rest will run away. How can they rescue each other?
The Chu general did not listen to the advice.
Sure enough, Yingbo defeated one of the armies, and the other two armies fled in all directions.
Yingbu's army advanced westward and met the emperor's army at Huizhen, west of Qixian County.
Yingbu's army was very elite, so the emperor hid in the fortress of Yongcheng and could not get out. When he saw that Yingbu's formation was just like Xiang Ji's army, the emperor was very disgusted with him.
Seeing Yingbu from a distance, he said to Yingbu from a distance: Why bother to rebel?
Yingbu said: I want to be the emperor!
The emperor was furious and scolded him, and then the two armies fought.
Yingbu's army was defeated and fled, crossing the Huaihe River. They stopped and fought several times, but all failed, so they had to flee to the south of the Yangtze River with more than a hundred people.
Yingbu was originally married to the magistrate of Fan County. Therefore, King Ai of Changsha sent someone to trick Yingbu into fleeing to South Vietnam. Yingbu believed him and followed him to Fanyang. The Fanyang people killed Yingbu in the houses of the people in Zixiang and finally destroyed Yingbu.
The emperor appointed Prince Liu Chang as the King of Huainan, and granted Benhe the title of Marquis of Si. Most of the generals were rewarded for their military exploits.
Tai Shigong said: Yingbu, are his ancestors the descendants of the British and Six Kingdoms Gaotao who were destroyed by the Chu Kingdom as recorded in the "Spring and Autumn"?
He himself was tattooed, so why could he rise to prominence so quickly?
Xiang killed thousands of people and buried them alive, and Yingbu was often the culprit.
His merits were ranked highest among the princes, so he was able to become king, but he could not avoid suffering the greatest humiliation in the world.
The root of the disaster is caused by concubine love. Jealousy leads to disaster, which actually leads to the destruction of the country.
summary:
Yingbu, a commoner from Liuxian County with the surname Ying, was predicted in his youth to become a king after being tortured. After being sentenced to tattooing for breaking the law, he laughed at the prophecy's fulfillment. Sent to hard labor at Lishan, he later rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, gathering thousands of troops. Yingbu joined Xiang Liang, proving himself brave in battle, and was titled Dangyang Lord. After Xiang Liang's death, he served under Xiang Ji (Xiang Yu), leading attacks that defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han's surrender. Yingbu buried over 200,000 Qin soldiers alive and helped Xiang Yu enter Xianyang. He was named King of Jiujiang and later killed the Righteous Emperor on Xiang Yu's orders.

During the Chu-Han conflict, Yingbu feigned illness to avoid aiding Xiang Yu, who grew resentful. The Han king, valuing Yingbu's talents, sent Sui He to persuade him to defect. Sui He argued that Chu was weak and unjust, while Han was strong, promising Yingbu land and titles. Yingbu agreed, killed the Chu envoy, and attacked Chu. After being defeated by Long Qie, he fled to Han with Sui He. Initially angered by the Han king's casual reception, he was pleased by the luxurious treatment. The Han king granted him the title King of Huainan, and Yingbu helped defeat Xiang Yu at Gaixia.

After peace, Yingbu grew fearful upon seeing the execution of Han Xin and Peng Yue. His favored concubine's praise of a doctor's neighbor, Ben He, led to suspicion of adultery. Ben He fled to Chang'an and reported Yingbu's rebellion. Despite initial disbelief, Yingbu killed Ben He's family and rebelled. The emperor consulted Xue Gong, who predicted Yingbu would choose a poor strategy—attacking Wu and Chu but fleeing to Changsha. Yingbu indeed attacked Jing and Chu, defeating them, but was routed by the emperor's army at Huizhen. He fled south with a hundred men, was tricked by King Ai of Changsha, and killed by Fanyang people. The emperor made Prince Liu Chang King of Huainan. The historian notes Yingbu's rise from tattooing to kingship, his role in massacres, and his downfall due to jealousy over a concubine.

Tai Shigong said: Since ancient times, the sage kings are about to establish a country, accept the destiny of heaven, and establish a cause. How can they not respect the use of divination to help achieve good deeds?
It is impossible to record what happened before Tang Yao and Yu Shun.
Judging from the rise of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, they were all based on auspicious omens from divination.
Dayu's marriage to the daughter of the Tushan clan was auspicious, so Xia Qi established the Xia Dynasty, which has been passed down from generation to generation; Jian Di swallowed the eggs of flying swallows, and the auspicious predictions were favorable, so the Yin Dynasty rose; Houji, who was good at sowing hundreds of grains, got auspiciousness, so the king of Zhou finally became the king of the world.
When the king decided on difficult matters, he would refer to the results of divination made with the turtle to make the final decision. This was an unchanging traditional procedure.
Although the Barbarians, Barbarians, Di and Qiang did not have the Chinese-style hierarchy of monarchs and ministers, they also had the custom of divination for making decisions and doubts.
Some use gold and stone, some use plants and trees, and divination customs vary from country to country.
But they can all be used to guide war operations, research, and achieve victory in wars. Each worships the gods of divination to predict future events.
I have heard a little bit: During the Xia and Yin Dynasties, yarrow turtles were found when it was time to perform divination, and they were discarded after the divination, because they believed that turtle shell yarrow would not be effective if stored.
In the Zhou Dynasty, diviners always collected yarrow and tortoise shells for later use. In addition, who is more intelligent and who is less intelligent? When using Turtleweed, which one comes first and which one comes last?
Every dynasty has different values. But in summary, the purpose of using turtle divination methods to help people predict the future is the same. Some people believe that there was never a time when the Holy King was undecided when encountering something; there was never a time when the Holy King lacked insights when solving problems. The reason why they set up the method of praying to gods and asking for divination is because they are worried that future generations will decline and decline. Foolish people will not learn from smart people. Everyone will be satisfied with their own knowledge. Differences in education will arise. The big principles will be broken into pieces and cannot be grasped. Therefore, they push the physical and emotional affairs to the most subtle realm, that is, the gods, and seek purity in the spirit.
Some people also think that what the tortoise is good at, the saint cannot catch up with.
It judges good and bad, distinguishes right from wrong, and is often more accurate than human predictions.
After Emperor Gaozu succeeded to the throne, he followed the system of the Qin Dynasty and established diviners.
At that time, the country had just been unified and the war had not stopped.
As for Emperor Xiaohui, his reign was short, Empress Lu was the heroine, and Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xiaojing just followed the old system and did not have time to study the divination in depth. Therefore, although fortune-telling has been passed down from father to son and passed down from generation to generation, many of its subtle and profound principles and methods have been lost.
Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he has opened up the path for talented people to advance, and has recruited various scholars. Anyone who is proficient in a certain skill will have the opportunity to contribute, and those with outstanding skills will receive preferential treatment. He is pragmatic and has no partiality. In the past few years, the Taibu official office has gathered many talents.
At this time, the emperor was about to attack the Xiongnu in the north, Dawan in the west, and Baiyue in the south. Divination could predict changes in events and suggest ways to gain advantages and avoid disadvantages.
Later, fierce generals were ordered to lead troops to charge and win on the battlefield, which also included the contribution of divination's pre-planning in the temple.
As a result, the emperor paid more attention to the fortune-telling officials, and the rewards sometimes amounted to tens of millions of dollars.
For example, Qiu Ziming and others' wealth increased dramatically, and they were greatly favored, overwhelming the ministers of the court.
Even divination is used to guess the behavior of witches and Gu, and the behavior of witches and Gu can sometimes be guessed accurately.
For those who had offended them even slightly, they would seek opportunities to avenge themselves and persecute them wantonly. As a result, the number of people who had their families destroyed was incalculable.
All civil and military officials were in panic, and they all flattered him that the theory of turtles and yarrow was effective.
Later, the true nature of the false accusation by the fortune teller was exposed, and the three clans were also wiped out.
Since yarrow is used to predict good and bad luck, and tortoise shells are burned to observe the omens, the changes are endless. Therefore, wise men are selected as divination officials. This can be said to be the importance that the saints attach to the important matter of divination!
Duke Zhou used tortoise shells for divination three times, so King Wu of Zhou could recover from his illness.
King Zhou was tyrannical, so even using a big turtle would not bring good luck.
Duke Wen of Jin was about to restore King Zhou Xiang to the throne. During the divination, he got a good omen that "The Yellow Emperor fought at Banquan". He finally succeeded and received the Tong Bow from King Zhou Xiang with the order of conquest, and became Hou Bo.
Duke Xian of Jin was covetous of Li Ji's beauty and wanted to attack Li Rong. He predicted that victory would be an unlucky omen. The disaster of attacking Li Rong actually extended to the fifth king of Jin.
King Ling of Chu was about to betray the Zhou royal family, and the divination was unlucky, which finally led to Qianxi's defeat.
The tortoise omen indicates the inner trend. At that time, people can see the external manifestation. Can we not say that this is consistent with the two?
A gentleman believes that those who despise divination and do not believe in gods are ignorant; those who abandon human plans and only believe in auspicious omens will not be treated fairly by ghosts and gods.
Therefore, there is a section on "Judgment" in "Shangshu·Hongfan", which proposes five objects that can be discussed with when solving difficult problems, and divination and divination account for two of them. When five people perform divination, one should rely on the judgment of the majority of them. This shows that although there are diviners, they are not arbitrary.
When I visited the south of the Yangtze River for investigation, I learned about the turtle yarrow and interviewed the elderly local people. They said that the turtle lived to be a thousand years old and could walk on the lotus leaves. The yarrow has hundreds of branches and stems, but it still has one root.
He also said that where turtles grow, there are no ferocious beasts such as tigers and wolves, and no poisonous weeds.
Riverside residents often raise turtles, drink their blood, and eat their meat. They believe that turtles can help people unblock their tendons, bring about vitality, and help people resist aging and provide for their old age. Aren’t these words true?
Mr. Chu said: I am proficient in Confucian classics. I am a doctor's disciple and study "Spring and Autumn". Due to my excellent performance, I was appointed as a Langguan. I was fortunate to serve as a guard in the palace and have been in and out of the palace for more than ten years.
I personally like "Tai Shi Gong Zhuan".
Tai Shigong's "Biography" said that the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties had different methods of tortoise divination, and the four ethnic groups also had different divination methods, but they were all used to judge good and bad luck. I reviewed their key points and wrote the "Biography of Guice".
I searched repeatedly in Chang'an City but could not find the "Biography of Guice", so I visited the Taidivination Official and asked the literary elders who were familiar with Guice's affairs for anecdotes. I wrote down the divination of Guice and compiled it below.
It is said that in ancient times, when the five emperors and three kings planned to launch major events, they would make decisions through divination in advance.
Ancient divination books say: There is Fuling below, and rabbit threads above; there are bunches of yarrow above, and the tortoise below.
The so-called Fuling grows under rabbit silk and looks like a bird.
After the first spring rain, if the weather is calm and windless, you can cut off the rabbit silk at night and use a lantern to illuminate it. If the lantern burns out as soon as it is illuminated, remember this place and surround it with four feet of new cloth. When dawn comes, dig down until you reach between four feet and seven feet. Nothing over seven feet.
Fuling is the root of a thousand-year-old pine tree. People who eat it can live forever.
It is said that if the yarrow has a hundred branches and stems, there will be a divine turtle guarding it below, and it will always be shrouded by blue clouds.
Ancient books say: When the world is peaceful and the king's law is implemented, yarrow can grow a stem one foot long, and a clump can be filled with a hundred stems and branches.
Today's search for yarrow cannot meet the requirements in ancient books, and we cannot find one with hundreds of stems and one foot long. It is very difficult to find one with more than eighty stems and eight feet long.

summary:
Tai Shigong observed that since ancient times, sage kings establishing states and accepting heaven's mandate have always respected divination to aid good deeds. Evidence from Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties shows their rises were based on auspicious divination omens: Dayu's marriage to the Tushan daughter was auspicious, leading to Xia Qi's dynasty; Jian Di swallowing a swallow's egg brought favorable predictions for Yin's rise; Houji's agricultural skill brought auspiciousness for Zhou kingship. Kings consulted turtle divination for difficult decisions as an unchanging tradition. Even barbarian tribes without Chinese hierarchy had divination customs using various materials like gold, stone, plants, and wood, all guiding warfare and predicting events.

During Xia and Yin, yarrow and turtle shells were discarded after divination, but Zhou collectors preserved them. Different dynasties valued divination differently, but all used it to predict the future. Some believed holy kings never lacked insights but established divination to guide future generations who might decline in wisdom. Others thought turtles' judgment surpassed human predictions. After Emperor Gaozu succeeded, he followed Qin's system to establish diviners, but the country's unification and ongoing wars prevented deep study. Emperors Xiaohui, Empress Lu, Xiaowen, and Xiaojing merely followed old systems, causing subtle divination methods to be lost.

When the current emperor ascended, he opened paths for talented people, recruiting scholars proficient in various skills. The Taibu office gathered many talents. The emperor planned attacks on Xiongnu, Dawan, and Baiyue, using divination to predict changes and suggest advantages. Generals' battlefield successes included divination's contributions. The emperor rewarded divination officials heavily, with some like Qiu Ziming gaining enormous wealth and favor, overwhelming court ministers. Divination even predicted witch and Gu behaviors accurately. Those who offended diviners faced revenge and family destruction, causing officials to flatter turtle and yarrow theories. Eventually, false accusations were exposed, and the diviners' three clans were wiped out.

Duke Zhou divined three times for King Wu's recovery. King Zhou's tyranny brought no good omens even from large turtles. Duke Wen of Jin's divination for restoring King Zhou Xiang showed a good omen about the Yellow Emperor at Banquan, leading to success. Duke Xian of Jin's divination for attacking Li Rong was unlucky, causing disaster extending to five Jin kings. King Ling of Chu's divination for betraying Zhou was unlucky, leading to defeat. Turtle omens indicate inner trends visible externally. Gentlemen believe despising divination shows ignorance, while abandoning human plans for auspicious omens displeases ghosts and gods. The "Shangshu·Hongfan" proposes five objects for solving difficulties, with divination accounting for two.

Investigating south of the Yangtze River, the author learned turtles live a thousand years, walking on lotus leaves, while yarrow has hundreds of branches with one root. Where turtles grow, no tigers, wolves, or poisonous weeds exist. Riverside residents raise turtles, drinking blood and eating meat to unblock tendons and resist aging. Mr. Chu, proficient in Confucian classics and a Langguan, studied "Spring and Autumn" and served in the palace for over ten years. He liked "Tai Shi Gong Zhuan," which said Xia, Shang, and Zhou had different divination methods, and four ethnic groups had varying customs, all judging good and bad luck. Searching Chang'an City for "Biography of Guice" failed, so he visited Taidivination officials and elderly experts to compile divination records.

Ancient divination books describe Fuling growing under rabbit threads, with yarrow above and turtles below. Fuling, resembling a bird, grows under rabbit silk. After spring rain in calm weather, one can cut rabbit silk at night, use a lantern to illuminate, and mark the spot where the lantern extinguishes. Digging four to seven feet deep reveals Fuling, the root of thousand-year-old pine trees, granting immortality when eaten. Yarrow with a hundred branches has a divine turtle guarding below, shrouded by blue clouds. In peaceful times, yarrow grows one foot long with a hundred stems per clump. Today, finding such yarrow is difficult; those with over eighty stems and eight feet long are rare. People can use yarrow with over sixty stems and six feet long.

Famous turtles include eight types: Big Dipper, Nanchen, Five Star, Eight Winds, Twenty-Eight Stars, Sun and Moon, Kyushu, and Jade turtles. Ancient books have words on turtle undersides indicating their type. Finding such turtles doesn't require one foot two inches; folks treasure seven or eight inch turtles. Jewels and jade shine out their gods, similar to famous turtles bringing wealth. Jade in mountains moistens trees; pearls in deep pools prevent shore vegetation from withering. Bright moon pearls from rivers and seas, hidden in clams with dragons, can protect the world when obtained by kings. Those obtaining a hundred-stem yarrow with a divine turtle underneath can ask a hundred questions and determine good or bad luck.

Divine turtles come from the Yangtze River. Lujiang County delivers twenty live turtles one foot two inches long to Taifu officials annually, who pick off turtle underbellies on auspicious days. Turtles reach one foot two inches after a thousand years. Kings drilling tortoise shells on temples determine good or bad luck when dispatching troops. Gaozu Temple has a turtle room collecting tortoise shells as sacred treasures. Ancient books say wearing a turtle's forefoot arm bone and hanging a turtle in the northwest corner prevents losing one's way in deep mountains. The "Wan Bi Shi Zhu Fang" mentions a magical turtle in Jia Lin south of the Yangtze River, where no tigers, wolves, owls, poisonous weeds, or insects exist, and wild fire cannot burn it.

Turtles in Jia Lin build nests on fragrant lotus. Text under the turtle's left side says obtaining it can make one a ruler or emperor. Those seeking turtles in white snake forests fast respectfully, offer wine to gods, let hair hang down, and beg for three days and nights. An old man in the south used a turtle to prop his bed for over twenty years; after his death, the turtle was still alive when someone moved the bed. Turtles can move qi. When diviners get live turtles, they kill them to pick off plastrons. Someone along the Yangtze River raised a famous turtle, making his family rich. Discussing releasing it, someone advised killing it instead. The turtle begged in a dream not to be killed, but the family killed it, causing the owner's death and family misfortune.

Commoners and monarchs have different principles; commoners obtaining famous turtles shouldn't kill them. Ancient Ming Kings and Holy Lords always killed turtles for use. King Song and Yuan obtained a turtle, killed it, and used it. In the second year of King Song and Yuan's reign, the Yangtze River God sent a divine turtle to the Yellow River. At Quanyang, a fisherman named Yuqie caught it in a net and imprisoned it. At midnight, the turtle entrusted a dream to King Yuan, saying it was on a mission for the River God but was blocked by a fishnet. King Yuan woke in surprise and summoned Dr. Wei Ping, who used divination tools to determine the turtle's identity. Wei Ping calculated the positions of sun, moon, and stars, determining the turtle was imprisoned. King Yuan sent someone to Quanyang, found Yuqie, and obtained the turtle.

The turtle was brought to King Yuan, stretching its neck and crawling forward before retreating. Wei Ping explained the turtle expressed gratitude and wished to leave quickly. King Yuan marveled at the turtle's spirit and wanted to release it, but Wei Ping argued against it, saying the turtle was the world's most precious thing, capable of making its owner emperor and winning ten battles. Wei Ping described the turtle's divine nature: born in the abyss, knowing heaven's way, understanding ancient affairs, living three thousand years without leaving its area, changing color with seasons, and clearly distinguishing yin and yang. King Yuan hesitated, fearing cruelty and tyranny, comparing himself to Xia Jie and Shang Zhou. Wei Ping countered, citing examples of hard work and treasure acquisition, urging the king to keep the turtle.

King Yuan eventually accepted the turtle, choosing auspicious days to fast and sacrifice. He killed a white pheasant and black sheep, filled the turtle with blood, and dissected it without damaging the shell. After burning thorn branches for omens, the omen pattern appeared clearly. The fortune teller's predictions were appropriate, and the country gained valuable treasure. King Yuan made Wei Ping prime minister, and Song became the world's most powerful state due to the turtle's magical power. Confucius later commented that divine turtles know good and bad but have hollow skeletons, comparing them to the sun bullied by a three-legged crow and the moon bitten by a toad. He noted everything has imperfections, and heaven itself is not perfect.

Mr. Chu concluded that the fisherman caught the turtle, which entrusted a dream to King Yuan. Wei Ping used formulas to calculate and urged keeping the turtle as a national treasure. This was good, as ancient divination always praised turtles for their efficacy. The text then lists taboos and methods for divination, including specific days for killing turtles, washing procedures, and prayers for various inquiries like illness, imprisonment, property, travel, warfare, and weather. Different omens like Hengji'an, signs, head raised and feet raised, and others indicate specific outcomes for each type of question, with detailed interpretations for conditions, prisoners, travel, and other matters.
