summary:
After the death of the great minister Huo Qubing, he submitted a memorial to Emperor Shu, expressing gratitude for the emperor's favor that allowed him to serve in the army. He stated that he should focus on border defense but dared to discuss other matters because he saw the emperor worrying about the world and the people, reducing his own food, music, and servants. Huo Qubing noted that the princes had grown up and could perform rites, yet they lacked official titles. He urged the emperor to appoint the prince as soon as possible on an auspicious midsummer day.

Following Huo Qubing's death, the emperor issued an edict to the censor. On the day of Yihai in the third month, Huo Guang, the censor and minister, sent a report to Weiyang Palace. The emperor ordered it handed to the censor. On Wushenshuo in the third month of the sixth year of Yuanshou, the censor Huo Guang, along with other officials, received the document. The prime minister Zhuang Qingzhai, censor Zhang Tang, and others submitted a memorial echoing Huo Qubing's request to title the princes, specifically Liu Hong, Liu Dan, and Liu Xu, as kings.

The emperor responded by citing the Zhou dynasty's enfeoffment of eight hundred princes, all with the surname Ji, and the "Book of Rites" stating that branch children cannot sacrifice in the ancestral temple. He questioned the proposal to merge vassal states, claiming he had never heard of it. The emperor argued that his virtue was shallow and he could not harmonize the country, let alone make an unlearned prince a king. He ordered a re-discussion.

On Bingzi day of March, another report was sent to Weiyang Palace. Prime Minister Chen Qingzhai and Censor Zhang Tang risked their lives to advise, discussing with princes and officials. They referenced the Zhou dynasty's enfeoffment and the examples of Uncle Kang and Bo Qin, who were granted titles due to their ancestors' virtues. They argued that the emperor's actions in honoring the virtuous and supporting the rise of declining states were commendable. However, they insisted that making the prince a king would disrupt the order of superiority and inferiority, and they requested that Liu Hong, Liu Dan, and Liu Xu be made princes and kings.

The emperor again cited Uncle Kang and the Duke of Zhou, emphasizing the difference between the wise and unworthy. He stated that this was enough to suppress unvirtuous princes and make them kings. On Wuyin day in April, another report was submitted, reiterating the request. The emperor repeated his previous reasoning.

On Guiwei day in April, the memorial was left in the palace without instructions. Prime Minister Qingzhai, Grand Servant Gongsun He, and others made another speech, referencing Huo Qubing's earlier memorial. They argued that Emperor Gao founded the world and named his descendants kings, and the laws of the late emperor should not be changed. They requested the emperor to order the historian to choose an auspicious day and prepare rituals.

The emperor issued an edict saying "Okay." On Bingshen day in April, a report was made, and the emperor decreed that Liu Hong be made King of Qi, Liu Dan King of Yan, and Liu Xu King of Guangling. On Dingyou day in April, the orders were entered into Weiyang Palace. On Yisi day in April, the emperor sent Zhang Tang to inform the temple and establish the princes as kings, issuing specific policies for each.

Tai Shigong commented that the king divided land to build countries and enfeoffed children to praise relatives, ensuring the royal family's stability. Chu Shaosun added that he obtained the seal policy books from elders and compiled them to pass down the wise master's will. He noted that Emperor Wu consecrated three sons as kings on the same day, writing policies to warn them. He also recounted the story of Mrs. Wang, who wished for her son Liu Hong to be king in Luoyang, but Emperor Wu chose Qi instead. Liu Hong died young, and the country was abolished. Chu Shaosun explained the ritual of receiving soil and the warnings given to each king, emphasizing the importance of following the emperor's instructions. He concluded by detailing the fates of the kings: Liu Xu plotted rebellion and committed suicide, and Liu Dan also conspired and died, leading to the abolition of their states.

He confessed to all his crimes and committed suicide out of fear of guilt.
So the feudal state was abolished and the feudal land was merged into the imperial court and became Guangling County.
Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, was named the king of Jiaoxi as a prince after the Wu and Chu kingdoms rebelled and were defeated in the third year BC by Emperor Xiaojing.
Liu Duan was cruel and cruel, and suffered from impotence. Whenever he came into contact with a woman, he would be ill for several months.
He had a beloved young man whom he appointed as Lang Guan.
The young official soon had an affair with the harem, and Liu Duan executed him, as well as his son and mother.
Liu Duan repeatedly violated the emperor's laws, and the ministers of the Han Dynasty repeatedly requested that he be killed. The emperor could not bear to do so because he was his ultimate brother, so Liu Duan's behavior became even more excessive.
Relevant officials twice requested to deprive him of his territory, so most of his fiefdom was deprived.
Liu Duan had a grudge in his heart, so he no longer managed the money in the country.
All the treasuries collapsed and leaked, and the corrupted property was counted in the billions, but in the end there was no cleaning up.
He also ordered officials not to collect rent or taxes.
Liu Duan also removed all the guards and sealed the palace gates, leaving only one door, from which he wandered out of the palace.
He changed his name many times, pretended to be a commoner, and went to other counties.
If any officials who went to Jiaoxi to serve as prime ministers or two thousand stone officials followed the laws of the Han Dynasty in governing political affairs, Liu Duan would always find out their crimes and report them to the court; if they could not find their crimes, he would devise a scheme to poison them.
His methods of devising tricks are extremely varied, he is strong enough to refuse the advice of others, and clever enough to cover up his own mistakes.
If the prime ministers and officials of the two thousand-stone level followed the king's laws in governing political affairs, they would be framed and punished by the court.
Therefore, although Jiaoxi is a small country, there are many officials with the rank of 2,000 stone killed and injured.
Liu Duan died after reigning for forty-seven years. In the end, because he had no son to inherit the throne, the feudal state was abolished and the feudal land was merged into the imperial court and became Jiaoxi County.
The first kings of the above-mentioned three kingdoms were all sons of Cheng Ji.
King Liu Pengzu of Zhao was named King of Guangchuan as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
After King Zhao rebelled and was defeated, Peng Zu was named King of Guangchuan.
In the fourth year of his reign, he was renamed King Zhao.
In the fifteenth year of his reign, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.
Peng Zu was a deceitful and sycophantic man, humble and flattering. On the surface, he was humble and respectful, but he was mean and vicious in his heart.
He likes to play with the law and slander others with sophistry.
Peng Zu had many beloved concubines and descendants.
If the prime minister and officials of the 2,000-stone level want to govern political affairs according to the laws of the Han Dynasty, they will harm the interests of King Zhao.
For this reason, whenever the Prime Minister or a 2,000-stone-level official arrived, Liu Pengzu would dress in black cloth and pretend to be a slave, go out to greet him personally, clean the residence where the 2,000-stone-level official stayed, and create more confusion to attract the other party. Once the 2,000-stone-level official made inappropriate remarks and violated the court's taboos, he would write it down.
If an official with a rank of 2,000 stone wanted to follow the law, he would threaten him; if the other party did not comply, he would file a report and frame the other party for committing adultery and breaking the law for personal gain.
During the more than 50 years of Liu Pengzu's reign, none of the prime ministers or officials of the 2,000-stone level could serve for two years. They were often dismissed from office for crimes. Those who committed major crimes were executed and those who committed minor crimes were punished. Therefore, no official of the 2,000-stone level dared to govern according to the law.
Therefore, the King of Zhao was very powerful and sent envoys to the counties to conduct patent sales. The income even exceeded the normal tax income of the State of Zhao.
Therefore, King Zhao's family had a lot of money, but all the money was given to concubines and concubines and was used up.
Liu Pengzu married the beloved concubine of the late Jiangdu King Liu Fei, who was later captured by Liu Jian and had an affair with, and he doted on her very much.
Liu Pengzu did not like to build palaces, nor was he superstitious about ghosts and gods, but he liked to do what officials did.
Write a letter to the emperor, volunteering to supervise the thieves in the kingdom.
He often led his troops to patrol Handan City at night.
The envoys and travelers did not dare to stay in Handan because Liu Pengzu was treacherous and evil.
Liu Dan, the crown prince of King Pengzu of Zhao, committed adultery with his daughter and his compatriot sister. Liu Dan had a grudge against his retainers, Jiang Chong reported on Liu Dan, and Liu Dan was deposed.
The state of Zhao changed its name to a crown prince.
Liu Sheng, King Jing of Zhongshan, was named King of Zhongshan as a prince in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
In the fourteenth year of his reign, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.
Liu Sheng was fond of drinking and seducing women. He had more than 120 descendants.
He and his brother King Zhao often criticized each other, saying: As a king of vassals, my brother specializes in managing political affairs on behalf of lower-level officials.
A person who is a king should listen to music and enjoy dancing and singing every day.
King Zhao also accused him and said: King Zhongshan only enjoys pleasure every day and does not help the emperor to comfort the people. How can he be called a vassal?
Liu Sheng died in the 42nd year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Liu Chang, King Ai.
Liu Chang died after one year on the throne, and his son Liu Kunchi succeeded him as King of Zhongshan.
The first kings of the two countries mentioned above were all sons of Mrs. Jia.
Liu Fa, the king of Changsha, and his mother Tang Ji, turned out to be Cheng Ji's maid.
Emperor Jing summoned Cheng Ji. It happened that Cheng Ji was menstruating and did not want to serve, so he dressed up his maid Tang'er and asked her to serve the emperor at night.
The emperor was drunk and didn't know what was going on. He thought it was Cheng Ji, so he slept with her, and she became pregnant.
Only later did the emperor realize that it was not Cheng Ji.
When he gave birth to a son, he named him Liu Fa.
Liu Fa was named the King of Changsha as a prince in the second year BC of Emperor Xiaojing.
Because his mother's status was low, she was not favored by the emperor, so she was made king of a small and low-income country.
Liu Fa died on the twenty-seventh day of his reign, and his son Liu Yong, King of Kang, succeeded him.
Liu Yong died in his 28th year on the throne, and his son Liu Yuan succeeded to the throne as King of Changsha.
The first king of the above-mentioned country was the son of Tang Ji.
Liu Yue, King Hui of Guangchuan, was named King of Guangchuan as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
Liu Yue died in the 12th year of his reign, and his son Liu Qi succeeded him as king.
Liu Qi had a favored minister Sang Ju.
Later, Sang Ju committed a crime, and Liu Qi wanted to kill Sang Ju, but Sang Ju escaped, and Liu Qi captured and exterminated his clan.
Sang Ju resented Liu Qi because of this, so he wrote a letter to accuse Liu Qi of committing adultery with his compatriot sisters.
From then on, in order to protect himself, Liu Qi repeatedly wrote letters to accuse the Han Dynasty officials and favored ministers such as Suo Zhong and others for their crimes.
Liu Ji, King Kang of Jiaodong, was named King of Jiaodong as a prince in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
He died after reigning for twenty-eight years.
When the King of Huainan was planning a rebellion, Liu Ji secretly heard about it, so he secretly made bows and arrows, prepared for war and defense, and waited for the King of Huainan to rebel.
Later, when the officials interrogated the King of Huainan for his rebellion, this incident was exposed in his confession.
Liu Ji had the closest relationship with the emperor. He felt guilty and grieved for participating in the rebellion. He died of an illness and did not dare to pass it on to his successor. Later, the emperor learned about this situation.
Liu Ji's eldest son was named Xian, but his mother was not favored; his younger son was named Qing, and his mother was favored. Liu Ji once wanted to appoint Liu Qing as his successor, but because it was not in line with the inheritance order and because of his own sins, he finally dared not say anything.
The emperor took pity on him and made Liu Xian King of Jiaodong and the successor of King Kang. Liu Qing was granted the title of King of Liu'an in the former fiefdom of King Hengshan.
King Liu Xian of Jiaodong died in the fourteenth year of his reign and was given the posthumous title of King Ai.
His son Liu Qing succeeded to the throne as king.
In the second year of Yuanshou, Liu Qing, the king of Liu'an, was named the king of Liu'an as the son of King Kang of Jiaodong.
Liu Cheng, the Ai King of Qinghe, was granted the title of King Qinghe as a prince in the third year of Zhongyuan Period by Emperor Xiaojing.
He died after reigning for 12 years. Because he had no sons, the feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Qinghe County.
Liu Shun, the Xianwang of Changshan, was named the King of Changshan as a prince in the fifth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
Liu Shun was the favorite youngest son of Emperor Jing. He was arrogant and lazy, engaged in many promiscuous affairs, and repeatedly violated laws and regulations. The emperor often pardoned him.
Liu Shun died in the thirty-second year of his reign, and his prince Liu Bo succeeded him as king.
It turned out that King Xian Liu Shun had a concubine who was not favored by him and gave birth to his eldest son Liu Xi.
Liu Chai was not favored by King Xian because his biological mother was not favored.
The queen concubines the prince Liu Bo.
There were many concubines in King Xian's palace, and his favored concubines gave birth to his sons Liu Ping and Liu Shang. The queen was rarely lucky.
When King Xian was seriously ill, the favored concubines often went to attend to him. The queen, out of jealousy, did not often go to see the sick and always stayed in her own room.
The doctor presented the medicine, but Prince Liu Bo did not taste the medicine himself, nor did he stay with the royal family to attend to the illness.
It was not until King Xian passed away that the queen and the prince arrived.
King Xian never regarded Liu Xi as his son. After King Xian died, he did not give him any property.
Some of the officials advised the prince and queen to share the property with the eldest son Liu Chai, but the prince and queen refused.
After the prince succeeded to the throne, he refused to accept and care for Liu Kai.
Liu Chao resented the queen and the prince.
When the envoys of the Han Dynasty came to see the funeral of King Xian, Liu Kai personally reported that when King Xian was ill, the queen and the prince did not wait at his bedside. When King Xian passed away, they only stayed for six days before leaving the mourning room, and that the prince Liu Bo secretly committed adultery, drank for fun, gambled and built for fun, rode with women in cars, traveled across the city, and entered prisons to visit prisoners.
The emperor sent an order to Zhang Qian to verify what the queen had done and to interrogate Liu Bo. He asked for the arrest of those who had committed adultery with Liu Bo as evidence, and Liu Bo managed to hide them.
Officials conducted a large-scale search and arrest, and Liu Bo was very anxious. He sent people to torture the investigators and released without authorization people who were imprisoned by the court as suspicious.
Officials requested that King Xian, Queen Xiu and Liu Bo be killed.
The emperor believed that Xiu had always had bad conduct, which led Liu Kai to report her as guilty, and Liu Bo committed the crime because he did not have the help of a good master and could not bear to kill her.
The officials also requested that Queen Xiu be deposed, Liu Bo be exiled, and his family members be moved to Fangling with him. The emperor agreed to this request.
Liu Bo was king for only a few months. He was demoted to Fangling and his country was exterminated.
More than a month later, the emperor noticed that King Xian was his favorite youngest son, so he issued an edict to the officials: King Xian of Changshan died early, the queen and her concubines were at odds with each other, and the concubines fabricated charges against each other and fought with each other. As a result, they fell into injustice and the country was destroyed. I pity him very much.
Liu Ping, the son of King Xian, has 30,000 households and is the true king; Liu Shang, the son of King Xian, has 30,000 households and is the king of Sishui.
In the fourth year of Yuanding, Liu Ping, the king of Zhending, was named the king of Zhending as the son of Prince Xian of Changshan.
Liu Shang, the Si Wang of Surabaya, was named the King of Surabaya as the son of Prince Changshan Xian in the fourth year of Yuanding.
He died after reigning for eleven years and was succeeded by his son Liu Anshi, King Ai.
King Ai died after eleven years of reigning without any sons.
The emperor took pity on the Queen of Surabaya and appointed Liu Anshi's younger brother Liu He as the King of Surabaya.
The first kings of the four kingdoms mentioned above were all the sons of Mrs. Wang Erjiao.
Later, the Han Dynasty added the title of King of Liu'an and King of Sishui to his descendants.
In total, there are six kings of Erjiao's descendants.
Tai Shigong said: When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was on the throne, all the taxes of the princes belonged to the princes and kings, and they could appoint officials below the level of internal history. The court only sent prime ministers to them and awarded them gold seals.
The vassal kings appointed censors, court officials, and doctors on their own, similar to the emperor.
Since the rebellion of Wu, Chu and other countries, during the era when the Five Sects were kings, the imperial court sent 2,000 stone-level officials to them, removed the "prime minister" and replaced them with "prime minister". The princes and kings could only enjoy the taxes within the fiefdom, and their power was deprived of their power by the court.
After that, the poor among the princes and kings could only ride on bullock carts.
summary:
Emperor Xiaojing had thirteen sons by five mothers, all named kings. Li Ji bore Liu Rong, Liu De, and Liu Yanyu; Cheng Ji bore Liu Yu, Liu Fei, and Liu Duan; Jia Fu bore Liu Pengzu and Liu Sheng; Tang Ji bore Liu Fa; and Mrs. Wang bore Liu Yue, Liu Ji, Liu Cheng, and Liu Shun.

Liu De, King of Hejian, was a Confucian scholar who attracted many followers. He reigned 26 years, succeeded by his son and grandson. Liu Rong, once crown prince, was deposed and later died by suicide after being convicted of expanding his palace onto temple grounds. His kingdom was abolished. Liu Yu, King of Lu, built palaces and loved music but stuttered. Liu Fei, King of Jiangdu, was a brave military leader who defeated Wu in the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms. His son Liu Jian committed suicide after plotting rebellion, adultery, and witchcraft. Liu Duan, King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and impotent, often killing officials who followed Han laws. He died without heirs, and his kingdom was abolished.

Liu Pengzu, King of Zhao, was deceitful and manipulative, causing many officials to be dismissed or executed. He amassed wealth through monopolies but spent it on concubines. Liu Sheng, King of Zhongshan, indulged in wine and women, fathering over 120 children. Liu Fa, King of Changsha, was born to a maid and ruled a small, poor kingdom. Liu Yue, King of Guangchuan, died after 12 years. Liu Ji, King of Jiaodong, prepared for a rebellion but died of illness. His son Liu Xian succeeded him. Liu Cheng, King of Qinghe, died heirless, and his kingdom was abolished. Liu Shun, King of Changshan, was favored but arrogant. His son Liu Bo was deposed after misconduct, and the kingdom was divided.

Sima Qian noted that after the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, the power of princes was reduced; they only collected taxes, and the court appointed officials. Some princes became so poor they rode oxcarts.

translation:
Uncle Kang of Wei State was named Feng, and he was the half-brother of King Wu of Zhou Dynasty. They also had a younger brother named Ran Ji, who was the youngest.
After King Wu of Zhou defeated Yin Zhou, he granted the remnants of Yin Zhou to King Zhou's son Wu Geng Lufu, making him the same as the princes, so that they could worship their ancestors and pass them on from generation to generation.
Because Wu Geng had not fully obeyed, King Wu was worried that Wu Geng had rebellious intentions, so he sent his younger brothers Guan Shu and Cai Shu to monitor and assist Wu Geng's father to appease the people.
After King Wu died, King Cheng was young and still in his infancy.
Zhou Gongdan took charge of state affairs instead of King Cheng.
Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected Zhou Gongdan, so they launched a rebellion with Wu Genglu's father to attack Chengzhou.
Zhou Gongdan asked King Cheng to organize an army to attack the state of Yin, killed Wu Genglu's father and Guan Shu, exiled Cai Shu, and granted Wu Geng Yin's remnants to Kang Shu, making him the king of Wei. He lived between the Yellow River and Qishui River, which was the ancient capital of the Shang Dynasty, Yinxu.
Zhou Gongdan was worried that Uncle Kang was young and would have difficulty maintaining his rule, so he repeatedly warned Uncle Kang: You must find talented, prestigious, and experienced people in the Yin Dynasty, and learn from them the history of the rise and fall of the Yin Dynasty, and you must care for and care for your own people.
He also warned Kang Shu that the reason for Zhou's demise was that he drank excessively, indulged in pleasure, and indulged in female sex. Therefore, the chaos in the reign of King Zhou began from here.
Zhou Gongdan also wrote "Zi Cai" in accordance with the principle that craftsmen must use rules when making woodenware, as a guideline for rulers to follow.
Therefore, it was called "Kang Gao", "Jiu Gao" and "Zicai", and was used to teach Uncle Kang.
Uncle Kang used these principles to govern the feudal country, stabilize and harmonize his people, and the people were very happy.
After King Cheng came of age, he personally took charge of the political power, appointed Uncle Kang as the Sikou of the Zhou Dynasty, and gave him many treasures and sacrificial vessels to commend Uncle Kang's virtues.
After Uncle Kang's death, his son Kang Bo became the king.
After Kang Bo's death, his son Kao Bo became the king.
After Kaobo's death, his son Sibo became the king.
After the death of Sibo, his son Boli became the king.
After Bo's death, his son Jing Bo became the king.
After the death of Jingbo, his son Zhenbo became the king.
After the death of Zhenbo, his son Qinghou was established as the king.
Because the Marquis of Qing bribed the King of Zhou Yi with generous gifts, the King of Yi ordered the King of Wei to be named Marquis.
Qinghou died in the twelfth year after he became the king, and his son Lihou became the king.
In the thirteenth year of Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled to the land of Hu, and Duke Zhao and Duke of Zhou took charge of the political power together, which was named "Republican Administration".
In the twenty-eighth year of Lihou, King Xuan of Zhou was established as the emperor.
In the forty-second year, Marquis Li died, and Prince Gong Boyu became the king.
Gongbo's younger brother He Zeng was favored by Marquis Li. Marquis Li gave He a lot of property. He then used these properties to bribe warriors and attacked Gongbo Yu in Lihou's cemetery. Gongbo was forced to flee to the tomb of Lihou and commit suicide.
The people of Wei buried Gongbo next to Lihou's tomb and called him Gongbo. They established He as the king of Wei, and he was named Wu Gong.
After Duke Wu came to the throne, he reorganized Uncle Kang's government affairs, and the people lived in peace and harmony.
In the 42nd year, Quan Rong killed King You of Zhou. Duke Wu personally commanded the generals to assist the Emperor of Zhou in quelling the invasion of Quan Rong and established military exploits. King Ping of Zhou ordered Duke Wu to declare himself duke.
In the fifty-fifth year, Duke Wu passed away, and his son Zhuang Gongyang became the king.
In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang's accession to the throne, he married a daughter of the State of Qi as his wife. The daughter of Qi was beautiful but childless.
Duke Zhuang then married Chen Guonv, who gave birth to a son who died in infancy.
Chen Nu's sister was also favored by Duke Zhuang and gave birth to a son named Wan.
After Wan's mother passed away, Duke Zhuang asked his wife Qi to raise Wan and made Wan the prince.
Duke Zhuang also had a beloved concubine who gave birth to a son named Zhouxu.
In the eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang, Zhouxu grew up and liked military affairs, so Duke Zhuang appointed him as a general in the army.
Shi Jue, the high minister of the Wei State, kindly came to admonish Duke Zhuang and said, "My son is fond of military affairs. Please make him a general. From now on, troubles will arise."
Duke Zhuang refused to listen. In the twenty-third year, Duke Zhuang passed away and the crown prince was established as the king. This is Duke Huan.
In the second year of Duke Huan, his younger brother Zhou Xu was arrogant and extravagant. Duke Huan deposed him and Zhou Xu fled abroad.
In the thirteenth year, Duan, Zheng Bo's younger brother, attacked his elder brother but failed to win and fled. Zhouxu asked for friendship with him.
In the 16th year, Zhouxu gathered the fugitives of Weiguo to attack and kill Duke Huan. Zhouxu himself established himself as the king of Weiguo.
Because Zheng Bo's brother Duan wanted to attack the state of Zheng, Zhouxu asked Song, Chen, and Cai to jointly support Duan, and the three countries all agreed to this request.
Zhouxu had just ascended the throne. Because he was fond of military affairs and killed Duke Huan, all the people in the Wei Dynasty hated him.
Because Duke Huan's mother lived in Chen State, Shi Que pretended to be friendly with Zhouxu. The Wei army marched to the outskirts of the capital of Zheng State. Shi Que and Chen Hou conspired and sent their right minister Chou to offer food to Zhouxu. They took the opportunity to kill Zhouxu in Pu, and brought Duke Huan's younger brother Jin back to Wei State from Xingdi and established him as king. This is Duke Xuan.
In the seventh year of Xuangong's reign, the people of Lu killed their king Yin Gong.
In the ninth year, the governor of the Song Dynasty killed his own monarch Shang Gong and his doctor Kong Fu.
In the tenth year, Zhuangbo Quwo of Jin State also killed his own king Aihou.
In the eighteenth year, Yi Jiang, the beloved wife of Duke Xuan, gave birth to a son named Ji, who was made the crown prince. Xuan Gong sent You Gongzi to teach him.
The right prince married a beautiful girl from Qi for the prince. The beauty was not married to Ji Baitang, but she was seen by Duke Xuan. Seeing the beauty of the girl from Qi, Duke Xuan liked her very much, so he married her himself and married another girl for the prince.
After Duke Xuan got the daughter of Qi, the daughter of Qi gave birth to sons Zishou and Zishuo. Duke Xuan sent Mr. Zuo to teach them.
After the death of Prince Ji's mother, Mrs. Xuan Gong and Zi Shuo jointly slandered and framed Prince Ji in front of Duke Xuan.
Duke Xuan originally hated the prince because he had snatched his wife, and he had long wanted to destroy him.
When he heard the bad things about the prince, he was so angry that he sent the prince Ji as an envoy to Qi and secretly ordered the thieves to intercept and kill Ji on the border.
Duke Xuan sent an envoy to Prince Bai Ya and warned the thieves on the border to kill the person holding Bai Ya's envoy as soon as they saw him.
Prince Ji was about to leave for the Kingdom of Qi. Zi Shuo's brother Zi Shou, the prince's half-brother, knew that Zi Shuo hated the prince and the king wanted to get rid of the prince, so he said to the prince: The thieves on the border will kill you as soon as they see you holding the Baiji envoy, prince. Prince, please don't go!
The prince said: It is absolutely not okay to go against the orders of your fathers to protect yourself.
So he went to Qi without hesitation.
Seeing that the prince did not listen to the advice, Zi Shou had no choice but to steal his Bai Ya envoy and drive to the border before the prince.
Seeing that the previous agreement had come true, the thief killed him.
After Zishou was killed, Prince Ji arrived again and said to the thief, "I am the one who should be killed!"
The thief then killed Prince Ji and repaid Duke Xuan.
Duke Xuan made Zi Shuo the crown prince.
In the 19th year, Duke Xuan died, and Prince Shuo became the king. This was Duke Hui.
The two young masters on the left and right were indignant at Zi Shuo being established as king. In the fourth year of Duke Hui, the left and right sons resented Duke Hui for slandering and murdering Prince Ji and establishing himself on his own. They launched a riot, attacked Duke Hui, and appointed Prince Ji's younger brother Qian Mou as king. Duke Hui fled to Qi.
In the eighth year of the reign of King Qianmou of Wei, Duke Xiang of Qi was ordered by the Emperor of Zhou to lead all the vassal states to jointly attack the Kingdom of Wei. He sent Duke Hui of Wei back to his country and killed the left and right young masters.
Wei Jun Qian Mou fled to Zhou Dynasty, and Duke Hui ascended the throne again.
Duke Hui fled three years after he was first established as king, and returned to defend his country eight years later, for a total of thirteen years.
In the twenty-fifth year, Duke Hui was dissatisfied with Zhou's acceptance and resettlement of Qian Mou, and he joined forces with Yan to attack Zhou.
King Hui of Zhou fled to Wen, and Wei and Yan jointly established King Hui's younger brother as king.
In the twenty-ninth year, Zheng Guo escorted King Hui back to Zhou Dynasty.
In the thirty-first year, Duke Hui of Wei passed away, and his son Yigong Chi became the king.
After Duke Yi ascended the throne, he liked to raise cranes and spend money on sexual pleasures.
In the ninth year, Zhai attacked Wei Guo. Wei Yigong led his army to resist, but some soldiers betrayed him.
The ministers said: If the king likes cranes, then send cranes to fight against the Zhai people!
So the Zhai people invaded the Wei State and killed Duke Yigong.
Yigong was the king, and the people and ministers were all dissatisfied.
From the time when Hui Gong Shuo, the father of Duke Hui, attacked and murdered the prince Ji and established himself as the king until Duke Yi, the people and ministers often wanted to overthrow them. Finally, they finally destroyed the descendants of Duke Hui and made Shen, the son of Qian Mou's younger brother Zhao Bowan, the king. He was Duke Dai of Wei.
Dai Gongshen died in the first year of his reign.
Duke Huan of Qi led the princes to attack Zhai because of the many turmoils in the Wei State. He built a castle in Chuqiu for the Wei State.
Duke Wen fled to Qi due to the turmoil in the Wei Dynasty, and the people of Qi sent him back home.
At first, when the people of Zhai killed Duke Yi, the people of Wei took pity on him and wanted to raise another descendant of the prince Ji who was murdered by Duke Xuan. However, Ji's son had died, and Zishou, who died in Ji's place, had no children.
Prince Ji had two brothers of the same mother: one was named Qian Mou. Qian Mou had been the king of Wei for eight years in place of Duke Hui, and was later driven out of Wei by Duke Hui. The other was named Zhao Bo.
Both Zhaobo and Qian Mou had died long ago, so the Wei people made Zhaobo's son Shen the Duke of Dai. After the death of Duke Dai, the Wei people made his younger brother Rui the Duke Wen.
When Duke Wen came to the throne, he reduced the people's taxes, clearly judged the crimes of prisoners, worked hard, and shared the joys and sorrows with the people, thus winning the hearts of the people.
In the sixteenth year, Jin Gongzi Chong'er passed by Weiguo. Duke Wen did not treat Chong'er politely.
In the seventeenth year, Duke Huan of Qi passed away.
In the twenty-fifth year, Duke Wen died, and his son Cheng Gong Zheng became the king.
In the third year of Chenggong's reign, Jin wanted to borrow a road from Wei in order to save Song Dynasty, but Chenggong refused.
Jin then changed its route and crossed the Nanhe River to rescue Song.
The Jin State conscripted troops from Wei. Doctor Wei wanted to agree, but Duke Cheng refused.
The official Yuan Yao attacked Duke Cheng, who fled to the state of Chu.
In order to avenge Duke Wen's rudeness when he passed by Wei State and Wei's failure to rescue Song State, Jin Wengong Chong'er attacked Wei State and gave part of Wei State's land to Song State. Duke Cheng of Wei had to flee to Chen.
Two years later, Duke Cheng went to Emperor Zhou to ask for help in returning to his country and met Duke Wen of Jin.
Jin sent people to kill Chenggong with poisoned wine. Chenggong bribed the person in charge of the poisoning in the Zhou royal family to let him use less poison, so that he could avoid death.
Soon, the King of Zhou petitioned Duke Wen of Jin on behalf of Duke Cheng. Duke Cheng was finally sent back to Wei, where he killed Yuan Yao and Wei Jun fled.
In the seventh year, Duke Wen of Jin passed away.
In the twelfth year, Duke Cheng went to see Duke Xiang of Jin.
In the fourteenth year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
In the twenty-sixth year, Qi Bingzha killed his king Yigong.
In the thirty-fifth year, Duke Cheng passed away, and his son Mu Gongtian became the king.
In the second year of Duke Mu's reign, King Zhuang of Chu attacked Chen and killed Xia Zhengshu.
Three years later, King Zhuang of Chu besieged the state of Zheng, and the Marquis of Zheng surrendered.
King Zhuang of Chu released him again. In the eleventh year, Sun Liangfu crusaded against Qi to rescue Lu and regained the invaded territory.
After the death of Duke Mu, his son Ding Gong Zang was established as the king.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Duke Dinggong, he passed away, and his son Xian Gong became the king.
In the thirteenth year, Duke Xian asked the musician Cao Cao to teach his concubine to play the piano. The concubine played poorly, so Cao Fei beat her as punishment.
Because the concubine Xian Gong favored him, she spoke ill of Cao in front of him and deliberately slandered Cao. Gong Xian also whipped Cao three hundred times.
In the eighteenth year, an announcement was made to invite Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi to a banquet, and they went as scheduled to wait.
It was getting late, and before Xian Gong went to summon them, he went to the garden to shoot wild geese.
The two of them had no choice but to follow Duke Xian to the garden. Duke Xian talked to them before he took off his clothes. They were very angry at his rude behavior and went to Suyi.
Sun Wenzi's son accompanied Duke Xian to drink many times, and Duke Xian asked the musician Cao to sing the last chapter of "Qiaoyan" in "·Xiaoya".
The musician Cao originally hated Duke Xiang for beating him three hundred times before, so he sang this poem, hoping to anger Sun Wenzi and take revenge on Duke Xiang of Wei.
Wenzi told Dr. Wei Zang Boyu about this, and Zang Boyu said: "I don't know."
So Sun Wenzi drove away Duke Xian.
Duke Xian fled to the state of Qi, and the state of Qi settled him in Juyi.
Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi jointly appointed their younger brother Qiu as the king of Wei. This was Duke Shang.
After Shang Gongqiu came to the throne, he granted Sufeng to Sun Wenzi Lin's father.
In the 12th year, Ning happy and Sun Lin's father came to attack each other due to competition for favor. Duke Shang asked Ning happy to attack Sun Lin's father.
Lin's father fled to the state of Jin and asked the state of Jin to escort Duke Xian back to his country.
At that time, Duke Xian was in the state of Qi. When Duke Jin of Qi heard the news, he and Duke Xiang of Wei went to Jin to ask for help in returning to Wei.
Jin then went to attack Wei and induced Wei to form an alliance with Jin.
Duke Shang of Wei went to meet Duke Ping of Jin. Duke Ping arrested Duke Shang and Ning happy, and then sent Duke Xian of Wei back to his country.
Duke Xian fled for twelve years and returned to his homeland.
In the first year of the reign of Emperor Xiangong, Ning happy was executed.
In the third year, Ji Zi of Yanling of the State of Wu was on an envoy and passed by the State of Wei. When he saw Zang Boyu and Shi Xi, he said: There are many gentlemen in the State of Wei, so this country will not be in trouble.
He passed by his place of residence again, and Sun Lin's father played the chime for him and said: "I am not happy, the music is very sad, this is where the Weiguo is in turmoil!"
In the same year, Duke Xiang passed away, and his son Xiang Gong was appointed king.
In the sixth year of Duke Xiang, King Ling of Chu met with various princes. Duke Xiang excused himself from going to the meeting because he was ill.
In the ninth year, Duke Xiang passed away.
At the beginning, Duke Xiang had a concubine who was very favored. After she became pregnant, she dreamed that someone said to her: I am Uncle Kang. I will let your son enjoy the title of Weiguo. Your son should be named Yuan.
When I woke up, I was very surprised and asked Kong Chengzi.
Chengzi said: Uncle Kang is the founder of Weiguo.
When my concubine gave birth to a child, and it turned out to be a boy, she told Duke Xiang about the dream.
Duke Xiang said: This is arranged by God!
So they named the boy Yuan. It happened that Mrs. Xiang Gong had not given birth to a son, so she named Yuan his legitimate son. This was Duke Lin.
In the fifth year, Duke Linggong met with Duke Zhao of Jin.
In the sixth year, Chu Gongzi abandoned his illness and killed King Ling and established himself as king of the country, calling him King Ping.
In the eleventh year, a fire broke out in Wei.
In the thirty-eighth year, Confucius came to the state of Wei, and the state of Wei gave him the same salary as when he was in the state of Lu.
Later, Confucius had a conflict with the king of Wei and left.
Soon, he traveled to Weiguo again.
In the thirty-ninth year, Prince Kuai Chi had a grudge against Nan Zi, the wife of Duke Lin, and wanted to kill Nan Zi.
Kuai Chi discussed with his retainer Xi Yangtian and asked Xi Yangtian to kill his wife during the court meeting.
When things came to a close, Xiyang regretted not taking action.
Kuai Kui winked at him several times, but when his wife noticed it, she was very frightened and shouted: "The prince wants to kill me!"
Duke Linggong was furious, and the prince Kuai Chi fled to the Song Dynasty, and soon fled to the Zhao family of the Jin Dynasty.
In the spring of the forty-second year, Linggong went on an outing and asked Ziying to drive.
Ying is the youngest son of Linggong, whose courtesy name is Zinan.
Duke Ling resented the prince for fleeing, so he said to Ying: "I will make you the prince."
Ying replied: Ying is not qualified enough to humiliate the country. You can think of other ways!
In the summer, Duke Linggong passed away. His wife made Zi Ying the crown prince and said, "This is Duke Linggong's order!"
Ying replied: "The son of the fugitive prince Kuai Chi is here, so I dare not take on this important task."
So the people of Wei established themselves as kings, which was called becoming a duke.
On the day of Yiyou in June, Zhao Jianzi wanted to send Kuai Kai back to his country, so he asked Yang Hu to send more than ten people to dress up as people from the Wei State and wear mourning clothes, pretending to come from the Wei State to the Jin State to greet the prince. Jianzi saw Kuai Kai off.
When the guards heard the news, they organized an army to attack Kuai Kui.
Kuai Chi could not return to the defense, so he had to run to his base to defend himself, and the defenders also stopped attacking.
Four years after leaving public life, Qi Tianqi killed his own king, the son.
In the eighth year, Qi Baozi killed his own monarch, Duke Ai.
Confucius came from the state of Chen to the state of Wei.
In the ninth year, Kong Wenzi asked Kong Zhongni for military advice, but Zhongni refused to answer.
Afterwards, the Marquis of Lu sent people to welcome Zhongni, and Zhongni returned to the state of Lu.
At the beginning of the twelfth year, Kong Yu Wenzi married the sister of the crown prince Kuai Chi and gave birth to her.
Kong Wenzi's servant Hun Liangfu was handsome and handsome. After Kong Wenzi's death, Hun Liangfu had an affair with Kui's mother.
When the prince was staying, his mother asked Hun Liangfu to go to the prince's place.
The prince said to the good husband: If you can help me return to my country, I will repay you by giving you a carriage for the doctor to ride in, and I will also forgive you three capital crimes.
Wearing purple clothes, bare fur clothes, and carrying a sword are not among the capital crimes.
The two made a covenant, and the prince also allowed his mother to be the wife of a good husband. In the leap twelfth month, Liangfu and the prince returned to the capital and temporarily stayed in Kong's outer garden.
In the evening, two people dressed in women's clothes and with scarves on their heads came in a car, driven by the eunuch Luo.
Luan Ning, the retainer of the Kong family, interrogated them about their names. They claimed to be concubines from their in-laws' family, so they successfully entered the Kong family's house and went straight to Boji's residence.
After dinner, Kui's mother went to Kong Kui's residence first, holding a gun. The prince and five others, wearing armor and carrying a boar, followed behind.
Bo Ji forced Kui into a corner, forced him to form an alliance, and hijacked Kui onto the stage, forcing him to summon his ministers.
Luan Ning was about to drink, but before the barbecue was cooked, she heard a messy noise and sent someone to tell Zhong Yu.
The escort drove him in a car, drank wine and ate barbecue, and escorted him when he was on duty and fled to the state of Lu.
Zhong You arrived after hearing the news and was about to enter Kong's house, where he met Zi Gao who had just escaped from Kong's house. Zigao said: The door is closed.
Zilu said: I will go and have a look for now.
Zigao said: It's too late, don't follow Kui and suffer.
Zilu said: If you enjoy your meager salary, you cannot watch him suffer without saving him.
So Zigao ran away.
Zilu was about to go in, and when he came to the door, Gongsun dared to close the door tightly and said, "Don't go in again!"
Zilu said: You must be Gongsun!
Taking other people's profits and avoiding other people's dangers.
I can't do this. Enjoying other people's salaries will definitely save them from danger.
At this time, a messenger came out, and Zilu took the opportunity to go in.
Zilu said: How can the prince need Kong Kui as his helper?
Even if he is killed, someone must take his place and attack the prince.
He also said: The prince lacks courage. If he sets fire to the stage, he will definitely release Uncle Kong.
When the prince heard this, he was very frightened and asked Shi Qi and Yu Xiao to step down and block Zi Lu. They struck Zi Lu with their swords and cut off Zi Lu's hat tassel.
Zilu said: When a gentleman dies, his hat cannot fall to the ground.
With that said, he fastened his hat and tassel and died.
After hearing the news of the turmoil in Weiguo, Confucius said: Alas!
Chai will come back, right?
But you, died.
Kong Kui finally made Prince Kuai Chi the king of the country. This was Duke Zhuang.
Duke Zhuang's father, Kuai Chi, was in exile. When he was on the run, he resented the officials for not welcoming him as king.
After he came to the throne in the first year, Duke Zhuang wanted to kill all his ministers, saying: "I have been away for a long time, have you heard about it?"
The ministers wanted to cause trouble, so Duke Zhuang had to give up.
In the second year, Confucius of Lu State passed away.
In the third year, Duke Zhuang climbed up the city wall and saw Rongzhou. Said: Why did the soldiers build cities?
The people of Rongzhou were very worried about his words.
In October, the people of Rongzhou told Zhao Jianzi that Jianzi was besieging Weiguo.
In the eleventh month, Duke Zhuang fled, and the guards made Prince Banshi their king.
The state of Qi attacked the state of Wei, captured Master Ban, and made the young master the king.
In the first year of Wei Junqi's reign, Wei Shimangui drove Qi away and fled to Qi State.
When Wei was on duty, he returned from Qi to Wei and became the king.
At first, he fled after being away for twelve years and had to return after being away for four years.
In the first year of his reign, he rewarded those who fled with him.
After he had been in power for twenty-one years and died, Chugong's uncle Qian drove out Chugong's son and established himself as the king of the country. This is Duke Mourning.
In the fifth year of mourning for the Duke, he passed away, and his son Jing Gongfu became the king.
In the 19th year, Duke Jing passed away, and his son Zhao Gongjiu became the king.
At this time, the Three Jin Dynasties became stronger and stronger, and Weijun was like a small prince, attached to the State of Zhao.
In the sixth year of Zhaogong's reign, Prince Qi killed Duke Zhao and established himself as king. This was Duke Huai.
In the eleventh year of Duke Huai's reign, the prince killed Duke Huai and established himself as king. This was Duke Shen.
Duke Shen's father was Gongzi Shi. The suitable father is Mr. Jing.
In the forty-second year, Duke Shen passed away, and his son declared himself the king of the country.
In the eleventh year, Duke Sheng died, and his son Chenghou Tianli became the king.
In the eleventh year of Chenghou's reign, Gongsun Yang entered Qin.
In the sixteenth year, Wei was demoted to Hou.
In the twenty-ninth year, Chenghou passed away, and his son Pinghou became the king.
Pinghou died in the eighth year, and his son Heijun became the king.
In the fifth year of his reign, the successor was demoted to the title of "Jun", and he only had the title of "Puyang".
In the forty-second year, the heir passed away, and his son Huaijun became the king.
In the thirty-first year, Huaijun paid homage to Wei, and Wei imprisoned and killed Huaijun.
Wei changed and established a successor, Jun's younger brother, who was Yuan Jun.
Yuan Jun was the son-in-law of Wei State, so Wei State established him.
In the fourteenth year of Yuanjun, Qin captured the eastern territory of Wei, and Qin began to set up Dongjun in this area. He also moved Weijun to Yewang County and merged Puyang into Dongjun.
In the twenty-fifth year, Yuanjun passed away, and his son Junjiao became the king.
In the ninth year of Junjiao, Qin annexed the world and Ying Zheng was established as the first emperor.
In the twenty-first year of the Qin Dynasty, the second emperor of Qin deposed Weijun, Junjiao became an ordinary commoner, and the Weiguo lineage was completely cut off.
Tai Shigong said: I read the records of the family and read that the crown prince of Duke Xuan of Wei was killed because of his wife. His younger brother Zishou and the crown prince gave in to each other and fought to die. This is the same as the prince Shen Sheng of Jin who did not dare to declare Li Ji's fault because he was afraid of hurting his father's feelings.
However, it is so sad to finally die!
Some fathers and sons kill each other, and some brothers destroy each other. Why is this?
summary:
Uncle Kang of Wei, named Feng, was the half-brother of King Wu of Zhou. After King Wu defeated the Shang dynasty, he granted the remnants of Yin to Wu Geng, King Zhou's son, but worried about rebellion. He sent Guan Shu and Cai Shu to monitor Wu Geng. After King Wu's death, King Cheng was young, and Zhou Gongdan ruled as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu, suspecting Zhou Gongdan, rebelled with Wu Geng. Zhou Gongdan suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, exiled Cai Shu, and granted the Yin remnants to Kang Shu, making him ruler of Wei. Zhou Gongdan warned Kang Shu to learn from Yin's history, avoid excessive drinking and pleasure, and wrote "Kang Gao," "Jiu Gao," and "Zi Cai" as guidelines. Kang Shu governed well, and the people were content. After King Cheng came of age, he appointed Kang Shu as Sikou and honored him.

After Kang Shu's death, his descendants ruled Wei for generations. Qinghou bribed King Yi of Zhou to have the ruler of Wei titled Marquis. During Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled, and the "Republican Administration" began. Later, Gongbo Yu was forced to commit suicide by his brother He, who became Duke Wu. Duke Wu reformed governance, and the people prospered. He assisted King Ping of Zhou against Quan Rong and was declared duke. After his death, Duke Zhuang succeeded him. Duke Zhuang married a Qi woman who was childless, then married a Chen woman who bore a son who died. Another Chen woman bore Wan, who was made prince. Duke Zhuang also had a son, Zhouxu, who loved military affairs. Minister Shi Que warned Duke Zhuang, but he ignored him. After Duke Zhuang's death, Prince Wan became Duke Huan. Zhouxu, arrogant and extravagant, was deposed and fled. Later, Zhouxu gathered fugitives, killed Duke Huan, and declared himself ruler. He sought to support Zheng Bo's brother Duan, but the people hated him for killing Duke Huan. Shi Que conspired with Chen Hou to kill Zhouxu and established Duke Huan's brother Jin as Duke Xuan.

Duke Xuan's beloved wife Yi Jiang bore a son, Ji, who was made prince. Duke Xuan married a beautiful Qi woman for the prince but took her for himself. She bore Zishou and Zishuo. After Prince Ji's mother died, Zishuo slandered Ji. Duke Xuan, resenting Ji, sent him as envoy to Qi and ordered thieves to kill him. Zishou warned Ji, but Ji refused to disobey his father. Zishou stole Ji's envoy token and was killed first. Ji then arrived and was also killed. Duke Xuan made Zishuo crown prince. After Duke Xuan's death, Zishuo became Duke Hui. The left and right sons resented him, attacked, and made Qian Mou, Ji's brother, ruler. Duke Hui fled to Qi. Later, Duke Xiang of Qi, under Zhou orders, attacked Wei, restored Duke Hui, and killed the left and right sons. Qian Mou fled to Zhou. Duke Hui later attacked Zhou with Yan, forcing King Hui of Zhou to flee. Zheng later restored King Hui. After Duke Hui's death, his son Duke Yi succeeded. Duke Yi loved cranes and indulged in pleasure. When Zhai attacked, soldiers rebelled, and Zhai killed Duke Yi. The people, long dissatisfied with Duke Hui's line, made Zhao Bowan's son Shen, Duke Dai. After his death, his brother Rui became Duke Wen. Duke Wen reduced taxes, judged crimes fairly, and won the people's hearts. He later treated Jin's Chong'er rudely. After Duke Wen's death, his son Duke Cheng succeeded. Duke Cheng refused Jin passage to rescue Song, leading to conflict. Jin attacked Wei, and Duke Cheng fled. He later bribed Zhou officials to avoid poisoning and was restored after Zhou interceded. After Duke Cheng's death, his son Duke Mu succeeded. Duke Mu's reign saw Chu attacks on Chen and Zheng. After his death, his son Duke Ding succeeded, then Duke Xian. Duke Xian whipped musician Cao, who later slandered him. Duke Xian's rude behavior angered Sun Wenzi, who drove him out. Duke Xian fled to Qi. Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi made Qiu, Duke Xian's brother, Duke Shang. Later, Ning and Sun fought, and Sun fled to Jin, asking Jin to restore Duke Xian. Jin attacked Wei, arrested Duke Shang, and restored Duke Xian. Duke Xian executed Ning happy. After his death, his son Duke Xiang succeeded. Duke Xiang's concubine dreamed of Uncle Kang, who said her son would rule Wei. She bore a son named Yuan, who became Duke Ling. Duke Ling's reign saw Confucius visit Wei. Prince Kuai Chi, resenting Duke Ling's wife Nan Zi, tried to kill her but failed and fled. After Duke Ling's death, his wife made Zi Ying ruler, but he declined, and the people made Zhe, Kuai Chi's son, Duke Chu. Zhao Jianzi tried to restore Kuai Chi, but Wei forces repelled him. Later, Kuai Chi, with help from Kong Kui's mother, returned, hijacked Kong Kui, and became Duke Zhuang. He wanted to kill ministers but relented. After his death, his son succeeded, but Wei faced turmoil. Eventually, Wei was demoted to a small state under Zhao. In the Qin dynasty, Weijun was deposed, ending the Wei lineage.

Tai Shigong remarked on the tragic deaths of Prince Ji and Zishou, noting the sorrow of fathers and sons killing each other and brothers destroying one another.
