translation:
Taibo Wu and his younger brother Zhong Yong were both sons of Gu Gong Danfu, King Tai of Zhou, and brothers of Ji Li, King of Zhou.
Ji Li was very virtuous and had a virtuous son Chang. The Taiwang wanted to establish Ji Li in order to pass the throne to Chang, so Tai Bo and Zhong Yong went to the land of Jingman. Like the local barbarians, they covered their bodies with tattoos and cut their hair to show that they could no longer inherit the throne, so as to avoid Ji Li.
Ji Li succeeded to the throne as Wang Ji, and Chang later became King Wen.
After Taibo fled to Jingman, he called himself Wu Ju.
The Jingman people believed that he was very righteous, and more than a thousand households followed him and respected him as Taibo Wu.
Taibo died without a son, and his younger brother Zhongyong succeeded him; he was Wu Zhongyong.
Zhongyong died and his son Ji Jian succeeded to the throne.
Ji Jian died and his son Shuda succeeded him.
Shuda died and his son Zhou Zhang succeeded to the throne.
At that time, King Wu defeated Yin Zhou and was looking for the descendants of Tai Bo and Zhong Yong, and found Zhou Zhang.
Zhou Zhang was already the monarch of Wu, so King Wu officially granted him the land of Wu.
He also enfeoffed Zhou Zhang's younger brother Yu Zhong to the former site of the Xia capital in the north of Zhou Dynasty. He was named Yu Zhong and ranked among the princes.
Zhou Zhang died and his son Xiong Sui succeeded to the throne.
Xiong Sui died, and his son Ke succeeded him.
Ke Xiang died and his son Qiang Jiuyi succeeded to the throne.
Qiang Jiuyi died, and his son Yu Qiaoxinwu succeeded to the throne.
Yu Qiao Xinwu died, and his son Ke Lu succeeded to the throne.
Ke Lu died and his son Zhou Yao succeeded him.
Zhou Yao died and his son Qu Yu succeeded him.
Qu Yu died and his son Yi Wu succeeded him.
Yiwu died and his son Qinchu succeeded him.
Qin Chu died and his son succeeded him.
After his death, his son Po Gao succeeded him.
Po Gao died and his son Goubei succeeded him.
At this time, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Yu who was north of the Zhou Dynasty, because Duke Yu lent a road to the Jin State, allowing the Jin army to destroy the Guo State.
Goubei died, and his son went to Qi to succeed him.
Qu Qi died, and his son Shou Meng succeeded to the throne.
After Shou Meng succeeded to the throne, the Kingdom of Wu began to become stronger, and Shou Meng called himself the king.
Counting from Taibo's founding of the Kingdom of Wu to the fifth generation, King Wu defeated the Yin Dynasty and named his descendants two kingdoms: one was the Kingdom of Yu, in the Central Plains, and the other was the Kingdom of Wu, in the barbarian zone.
By the twelfth generation, the Jin State destroyed the Yu State in the Central Plains.
Two more generations later, the state of Wu in the barbarian region became prosperous.
In total, it has been passed down to nineteen generations from Taibo to Shoumeng.
In the second year of King Shoumeng of Wu, the exiled official Shen Gong Wuchen of the Chu State defected to the Jin State because he was resentful of the generals of the Chu State.
Later, Wu State began to send troops to conquer Chu State.
In the 16th year, the king of the Communist Party of Chu conquered the state of Wu and reached Mount Heng.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Wu Shoumeng passed away.
Shoumeng had four sons: the eldest son was named Zhufan, the second son was named Yuji, the third son was named Yumei, and the fourth son was named Jizha.
Ji Zha was a virtuous man, and Shou Meng wanted him to succeed him during his lifetime, but Ji Zha evaded and refused to agree, so he let his eldest son Zhufan succeed him, prime minister of various affairs, and take charge of state affairs on his behalf.
In the first year of King Zhufan of Wu, Zhufan removed his mourning clothes after the period of mourning and wanted to give up the throne to Jizha.
Ji Zha declined and said: When Cao Xuangong passed away, the princes of various countries and the people of Cao State thought that the newly established Lord Cao was unjust, and wanted to make Zang Zang the Lord of Cao. Zizang left the State of Cao so that Lord Cao could continue to reign. The gentleman commented on Zizang that he was able to observe integrity.
As the eldest son, you are the legitimate successor. Who dares to offend you?
Being a king is not what I should be doing.
Although I have no talent, I am still willing to imitate Zizang’s righteous deeds.
The people of Wu insisted on establishing Jizha, but instead he abandoned his family and property to become a farmer. The people of Wu had to give up their plan to support him. In autumn, Wu attacked Chu again, and Chu defeated Wu's army.
In the fourth year, Duke Ping of Jin succeeded to the throne.
In the thirteenth year, King Zhufan of Wu died.
The purpose of leaving a will to pass the throne to his younger brother Yuji was to pass it on from brother to brother in order, and the throne must be passed on to Ji Zha to fulfill the last wish of the late king Shoumeng. And because the brothers all admired Jizha's noble character in relinquishing the country, everyone wanted to give up the position of king to others, so that it could gradually be passed on to Jizha.
Jizha was sealed in Yanling, so he was named Yanling Jizi.
In the third year of Wang Yuji's reign, Xiang Qing of Qi was convicted of a crime in Qi, and he fled from Qi to Wu.
The King of Wu rewarded him with Zhufang County as a city, and married the princess to Qingfeng. As a result, Qingfeng became richer than before in Qi.
In the fourth year, King Wu sent Jizha to visit the state of Lu. Jizha asked to see the Zhou Dynasty rituals and music preserved in the state of Lu.
Musicians from the state of Lu sang "Zhou Nan" and "Zhao Nan" for Jizha.
Jizha said: The song is so beautiful. It lays a solid foundation at the beginning, but it still does not reach the level of perfection. However, it sings the feelings of the people who are diligent in the king's affairs without complaining.
The musicians sang "Bei Feng", "阘风" and "Wei Feng" again.
Jizha said: The song is so beautiful, with a deep melody and a sense of urgency without confusing people.
I heard that the virtues of Uncle Wei Kang and Duke Wu were like this. Is this probably "Wei Feng"?
The musicians sang "Wang Feng" again.
Jizha said: The song is so beautiful, it is thoughtful but not fearful. This is probably the music after the Zhou royal family moved eastward, right?
The musicians sang "Zheng Feng" again.
Jizha said: The mood of this piece of music is too weak, reflecting that the people cannot bear the cumbersome government orders. This is probably a harbinger of the demise of the Zheng Kingdom, right? The musicians sang "Qi Feng".
Jizha said: The music is so beautiful, it is magnificent and has the demeanor of a great country.
Like the vast East China Sea, this is probably the legacy of Jiang Taigong, right?
The future of this country is limitless.
The musicians sang "Bin Feng".
Jizha said: The song is so beautiful, the momentum is broad and majestic, cheerful but not excessive. This is probably the music that reflects Zhou Gong's eastern expedition, right?
The musicians sang "Qin Feng".
Jizha said: This is the so-called voice of China.
Being able to admire China will lead to greatness, which is the ultimate in greatness. This is probably the music of the old land of the Zhou royal family, right? The musicians sang "Wei Feng".
Ji Zha said: The music is so beautiful. The music is melodious and melodious. The momentum is grand and broad. It is economical and easy to perform. With the help of moral education, you can be the leader of the alliance.
The musicians sang "Tang Feng".
Jizha said: "You are thoughtful. Isn't this the legacy of Tao Tang's family?"
Otherwise, why is the sense of worry so heavy?
Who could be like this if not the empress of the late king who possesses great virtue!
The musician sang "Chen Feng" again.
Jizha said: How can a country last long without a wise monarch?
The next thing the musicians sang was "Haifeng". From this point on, Ji Zha gave no more comments. The musicians sang "Xiaoya".
Jizha said: The music is so beautiful. There is a sense of worry but no second thoughts, and there is resentment but no words are expressed. This may be a sign of Zhou De's decline, right?
But there are still some customs left by the people of the previous kings.
The musicians sang "Daya" again.
Jizha said: This piece of music is really broad and majestic, harmonious and joyful, gentle and gentle yet upright and strong. This may reflect the great virtue of King Wen of Zhou, right? The musicians sang "Ode" again.
Jizha said: It is extremely beautiful. The melody is strong but not arrogant, gentle but not abject, close but not urgent, slow but not lax, the rhythm is changeable but not chaotic, the melody is repetitive but not boring, sad but not sad, joyful but not absurd, uses wisdom widely but not lacking, broad-minded but not ostentatious, benevolent but not wasteful, seeking but not greedy, the music stops but the lingering sound is still echoing, the music changes but does not follow the trend.
The five tones are in harmony, the eight tones are harmonious, the rhythm follows the law, and the melody conforms to the rules, just like a virtuous person.
Jizha watched the dances "Xiang Feng" and "Nan Xun" again, and then said: "The dance is so beautiful, but there are still some regrets."
Ji Zha watched the "Da Wu" dance again and said: "The dance is so beautiful. Isn't this the virtue of the Zhou Dynasty?"
He watched the "Shaohu" dance again and said: "The saint is so great, but he still feels ashamed of his own virtue. It shows that it is really difficult to become a saint!"
Ji Zha watched the "Da Xia" dance again and said: "The dance is so beautiful. You are diligent in civil affairs and don't take credit for it!"
Who else but Dayu could do it?
He watched the "Zhao Feng" dance again and said: The practice of virtue can be said to be at its peak. It is so great. Just like heaven, there is no place that cannot be covered. Just like the earth, there is nothing that cannot be carried. The virtue has reached its peak and cannot be added to it.
I am satisfied with watching the ritual music. Even if there are other rituals and music, I don’t dare to ask to watch it anymore.
Jizha left the state of Lu and went as an envoy to the state of Qi.
He persuaded Yan Pingzhong and said: Please hand over your fief and official position as soon as possible.
Without these two things, you will be safe from disaster.
齐国的政权快要易手了，在不能确定归入谁手之前，国家祸乱四不会平息的。 

Therefore, Yanzi handed over his fiefdom and official position through Chen Huanzi, so he survived the disaster of the Luan and Gao clans attacking each other.
Jizha left Qi and went as an envoy to Zheng. When he saw Zichan, it was like seeing an old friend.
He said to Zichan: The people who hold power in the state of Zheng are licentious and extravagant. A disaster is coming, and the power will fall on you.
When you are in power, you must be careful to govern the country with etiquette, otherwise the country of Zheng will decline!
After leaving the state of Zheng, Jizha went to the state of Wei.
He admired Qu Yuan, Shi Gou, Shi Loach, Gongzi Jing, Gongshu Fa, and Gongzi Chao very much, and said: There are many gentlemen in the defense of the country, so the country is safe.
When Jizha arrived in Jin from the state of Wei, he was about to stay in Suyi. When he heard the sound of drums and bells making music, he said: "Strange!"
I heard that if you have talent but no virtue, you will definitely be killed.
Sun Wenzi has offended the king and still lives here. He may not be careful enough. Can he still have fun?
Sun Wenzi's place here is as dangerous as a swallow's nest above the curtain.
Moreover, the king is still in the coffin and has not yet been buried. Is it difficult for him to have fun?
So he left.
Sun Wenzi heard Jizha's words and stopped listening to music for the rest of his life.
Jizha went to Jin, admired Zhao Wenzi, Han Xuanzi, and Wei Xianzi, and said: The power of Jin will fall into the hands of you three families.
Before he left Jin, he said to Shuxiang: You must do your best!
The king of Jin is extravagant and indulgent, but he has many good ministers and rich officials. The political power will fall to the three families of Han, Zhao and Wei.
You are an upright person and must think carefully about how to avoid disaster.
When Ji Zhagang was on his mission, he visited the king of Xu State on his way north.
Xu Jun liked Ji Zha's sword, but he didn't dare to say it. Ji Zha also understood Xu Jun's intention in his heart, but because he had to go to various countries in the Central Plains as an envoy, he did not present the sword to Xu Jun.
After returning from his mission, he passed through the state of Xu. Xu Jun had passed away. Jizha took off his sword and hung it on the tree in Xu Jun's tomb before leaving.
The entourage said: Mr. Xu has passed away, who should give the sword back to him!
Ji Zi said: No, I had promised him in my heart at the beginning. How could I go against my own wish just because of Xu Jun's death?
In the seventh year, the prince of Chu killed Chu King Jia Ao and proclaimed himself king, namely King Ling of Chu.
In the tenth year, King Ling of Chu formed an alliance with the princes to conquer Zhufang County of Wu State, in order to punish the original prime minister of Qi State, Guo Qingfeng.
The state of Wu also attacked the state of Chu, occupied three cities of the state of Chu, and then left.
In the eleventh year, the Chu State sent troops to attack the Wu State and fought all the way to Yu Lou.
In the twelfth year, Chu State again attacked Wu State and stationed troops in Ganxi for several days, but was finally defeated.
In the seventeenth year, Wang Yuji died and his younger brother Yu Mei succeeded to the throne.
The year before last, Chu Gongzi abandoned his illness and killed King Ling of Chu, and made himself king on his behalf.
In the fourth year, Wang Yumei died and wanted to pass it on to his younger brother Jizha.
Jizha avoided the situation and fled away.
So the people of Wu said: According to the decree of the late king, if a brother dies and a brother succeeds to the throne, the kingdom must be passed on to Ji Zi.
Ji Zi now escaped from the throne, and Wang Yumei became the last of his brothers to become king.
Now that he is dead, his son should be king in his stead.
So he established Yu Mei's son Liao as King of Wu.
In the second year of King Liao's reign, Prince Guang led an army to conquer Chu, but was defeated and lost the ship of King Wu.
Prince Guang was afraid of being punished for this, so he attacked the Chu army secretly and recaptured Wang Zhou before returning to the army.
In the fifth year, Wu Zixu, an exiled minister of Chu State, fled to Wu State. The young master treated him as a guest.
Prince Guang was the son of King Zhufan of Wu.
He has always believed that my father and four brothers should be passed on to the Jizi.
Now Ji Zi is no longer the king, but my father is the first to be the king.
Since the kingdom is not passed on to Ji Zi, I should succeed my father as the king.
So he secretly recruited the Magi, hoping to use them to attack King Liao.
In the eighth year, the King of Wu sent his son Guang to conquer the Chu State, defeated the Chu army, and brought the mother of the former Chu Crown Prince Jian back to the State of Wu from Juchao.
Taking advantage of the Northern Expedition, he defeated Chen and Cai's armies.
The year before last, Prince Guang conquered Chu State again and captured the two cities of Juchao and Zhongli.
At the beginning, a girl from the Beiliang clan in the border town of Chu State competed with a woman from Wu border town to pick mulberry leaves. The families of the two women were angry and attacked each other. When the officials of the two border towns heard about it, they attacked each other in anger, and the border town of Wu State was destroyed.
The State of Wu was furious upon hearing this, so it attacked the State of Chu, captured the two cities of Juchao and Zhongli, and returned.
When Wu Zixu fled to Wu, he told King Liao of Wu about the benefits of attacking Chu.
Prince Guang said: Zixu's father and brother were killed by the King of Chu. He advised you to attack Chu to avenge your own personal revenge. Attacking Chu will not be beneficial to Wu.
Wu Zixu then understood that Gongzi Guang had an ulterior motive. Zixu found a warrior named Zhuan Zhu and introduced him to Gongzi Guang.
Prince Guang was very happy and treated Wu Zixu with courtesy.
Zixu retreated to the countryside to earn a living, waiting for Zhuanzhu to take action.
In the winter of the twelfth year, King Ping of Chu passed away.
In the spring of the year before last, the King of Wu wanted to take advantage of the state mourning in Chu to attack Chu. He sent his sons Gaiyu and Zhuyong to lead troops to surround Chu's Liu and Hao towns, and sent Ji Zha as an envoy to Jin to observe the movements of the princes.
Unexpectedly, the Chu State sent a surprise army to cut off its retreat, and the Wu soldiers were prevented from returning home.
At this time, Prince Guang of Wu State said: This opportunity cannot be lost.
Tell Zhuan Zhu: If you don't take action, you won't get anything.
I am the true heir to the throne and should be made king. This is what I want to pursue.
Even if Ji Zi comes back, he will not oppose me.
Zhuan Zhu said: The conditions for killing Wang Liao have been met. There are only his mother and young son in the country, but his two younger brothers led troops to attack Chu and were blocked from returning.
Now King Wu is besieged by the State of Chu outside the country, and there are no upright and loyal ministers in the country. No one can stop us.
Gongzi Guang said: My body is your body, sharing weal and woe.
On the day Bingzi of the fourth month, Prince Guang ambushed the soldiers in the basement, and then invited King Liao to a banquet.
King Liao sent troops to line up along the road. From the palace to Prince Guang's house, to the gate, steps, door and seats of Guang's house, they were all covered with King Liao's personal soldiers, each holding a sharp sword.
After King Liao arrived, Prince Guang pretended to have a pain in his feet and hid in the basement. He sent Zhuanzhu to hide the dagger in the belly of the whole roasted fish and pretend to serve it.
When Zhuan Zhu brought the fish to King Liao, he took out a dagger from the fish's belly and stabbed Wang Liao. The guards on the left and right hurriedly stabbed Zhuan Zhu's chest with their swords, but Wang Liao was already killed.
Prince Guang was indeed appointed King of Wu on his behalf, and he became the King of Wu's house.
Helu appointed Zhuanzhu's son as minister.
Jizha returned to the state of Wu and said: As long as the sacrifices to the ancestors are not abolished, the people will not be without a king, and the god of the country is enshrined, then he will be my king.
Who can I blame?
I can only mourn the dead and serve the living to deal with the destiny arrangements.
If you do not create trouble yourself, you should obey the newly established king. This is the principle of our ancestors.
So Jizha went to King Liao's tomb, reported how he completed his diplomatic mission, cried bitterly to King Liao, and then returned to his place in the court to wait for the new king's orders. Prince Gaiyu and Zhu Yong of the State of Wu were besieged by the Chu army with their troops. When they heard that Prince Guang had killed King Liao and proclaimed himself king, they led their troops to surrender to the State of Chu. The King of Chu sealed them in Shu.
In the first year of the reign of King Wu of Helu, Wu Zixu was appointed as an official of Xingren and participated in state affairs.
The King of Chu killed Bo Zhouli, and his grandson Bo Pei fled to the State of Wu. The King of Wu appointed him as a doctor.
In the third year, King Helu of Wu, Wu Zixu, and Bo Pei led an army to conquer Chu, captured Shuyi, and killed Gaiyu and Zhuyong, the young masters of Wu who had fled.
Helu planned to attack Ying, the capital of Chu State. General Sun Wu said: The army and the people are very tired from fighting. We cannot attack the capital of Ying now. We must wait for the time to mature.
In the fourth year, Wu attacked Chu again and captured Liuyi and Yayi.
In five years, the state of Wu attacked the state of Yue and defeated the Yue army.
In the sixth year, the state of Chu sent his son Chang Nangwa to conquer the state of Wu. Wu Jun sent troops to fight and defeated the Chu army in Yuzhang. He captured Juchao of Chu state and returned to Wu with his troops.
In the ninth year, King Wu Helu asked Wu Zixu and Sun Wu: At first you said you could not attack Yingdu, what is the situation now?
The two men replied: The general of Chu State is often greedy, and both Tang and Cai States hate him.
If your Majesty is determined to attack Chu on a large scale, you must unite Tang and Cai to succeed.
Helu obeyed them, dispatched all the troops, and marched westward with Cai State of Tang Dynasty to attack Chu, and came to the edge of Han River.
Chu State also sent troops to resist, and the two sides formed formations across the water.
King Wu's younger brother Fugai wanted to fight, but Helu wouldn't allow it.
Fugai said: Your Majesty has entrusted me with the army. The best way to fight is to seize the favorable opportunity. What are you waiting for!
So he led his five thousand men to attack the Chu army. The Chu army was defeated and fled.
King Wu sent troops to pursue him.
When they arrived at Yingdu, they fought five times in total, and the Chu soldiers were defeated five times.
King Zhao of Chu escaped from Yingdu and ran to Yun County.
Duke Yun's brother wanted to kill King Zhao, but King Zhao fled to Sui with Duke Yun.
Wu soldiers entered the capital of Ying.
Wu Zixu and Bo Pei dug up the body of King Chu Ping from the tomb and whipped it to avenge their father's murder.
In the spring of ten years, the king of Yue heard that the king of Wu was stationed in Yingdu and that the country was empty, so he raised his troops to attack Wu.
Wu State sent another army to fight against the Vietnamese soldiers.
The State of Chu appealed to the State of Qin, and the State of Qin sent troops to rescue Chu and attack Wu. The Wu army was defeated.
Helu's younger brother Fugai saw that the Qin soldiers and the Yue soldiers defeated the Wu soldiers at the same time, and the king of Wu stayed in the Chu state and did not return. Fugai ran back to the state of Wu and proclaimed himself the king of Wu.
After Helu heard about it, he led his troops back to Wu and attacked Fugai.
Fugai was defeated and fled to Chu.
King Zhao of Chu was able to return to Yingdu in September, and sealed Fugai in Tangxi, where he became the Tangxi clan.
The year before last, King Wu ordered Prince Fucha to attack Chu and capture Panyi.
The king of Chu was afraid and moved the capital from Ying to Bo.
In the fifteenth year, Confucius photographed the affairs of the State of Lu.
In the summer of the 19th year, the state of Wu sent troops to attack the state of Yue, and King Goujian of Yue led his troops to fight against Li.
The Vietnamese soldiers sent death squads to challenge the Wu army. They lined up in three lines and rushed towards the Wu army, chanting slogans and committing suicide in front of the formation.
The Wu soldiers just watched this strange situation and relaxed their guard. The Yue soldiers took advantage of the situation to attack and defeated the Wu soldiers in Gusu. King Wu's toe was wounded by the Vietnamese army, and the army retreated seven miles.
Later, King Wu died of trauma in Helu. Before his death, King Wu ordered the crown prince Fu Chai to be king, and said to Fu Chai, "Can you forget that Gou Jian killed your father?"
Fu Chai replied: "I dare not forget!"
After three years, Wu finally took revenge on Yue.
The year before last, the doctor Bo Pei was appointed as Dazai.
King Wu insisted on training his army and always aimed to take revenge on Yue.
The year before last, King Wu Fu Chai dispatched all his elite troops to attack Vietnam and defeated the Vietnamese army in Fujiao, finally avenging the defeat of Gusu.
King Gou Jian of Yue had no choice but to hide in Kuaiji Mountain with 5,000 armored soldiers, and sent the official Wen Zhong to seek peace through Bo Pe, the Grand Prime Minister of Wu State, and was willing to use Yue State as a slave state of Wu State.
The King of Wu wanted to allow it, but Wu Zixu advised him: "In the past, the Guo family killed the Zhen Guan family and then conquered the Zhen Xun family, killing the empress of Xia.
Hou Min, the wife of the emperor's prime minister, was pregnant and fled to Youzhang to give birth to Shaokang.
Shaokang became the official of Mu Zheng in You still country.
The Youguo family wanted to kill Shaokang again, so Shaokang fled to the Youyu state. The Youyu family missed Xia Zhi's kindness, so they married their two daughters to Shaokang and granted him Lunyi. At that time, Shaokang only had a land of ten miles and only 500 subordinates.
But later Shaokang gathered the remnants of Xia and rectified the official system.
They sent people to penetrate into the Youguo clan, finally eliminated the Youguo clan, restored Xia Yu's achievements, and worshiped the Xia ancestor as the emperor of heaven. All the relics of the Xia Dynasty were restored as before.
Now the state of Wu is not as powerful as it used to be with the Guo clan, and Gou Jian's strength is greater than that of Shaokang.
Instead of taking this opportunity to completely eliminate the Yue forces now, we must forgive them. This is setting up trouble for the future!
Moreover, Gou Jian was a man who was tenacious and endured hardships. If he is not eliminated now, he will regret it in the future.
The King of Wu did not listen to Zixu's plan, but listened to Dazai Pei's words, and finally ceased war with the State of Yue. After the two countries signed a peace treaty, the State of Wu withdrew its troops and returned home.
The year before last, King Fu Chai of Wu heard that ministers were vying for power after the death of Qi Jinggong, and that the new king was young and powerless, so he launched an army to attack Qi State in the north.
Wu Zixu advised him: King Gou Jian of Yue did not eat more than two kinds of dishes, and did not wear more than two colors. He mourned the dead and comforted the sick. This was because he wanted to use the people to take revenge on Wu.
If Gou Jian does not die, he will definitely be a great trouble to the state of Wu.
Now the country of Yue is a serious problem for our country, but you don't pay attention to it and instead use your strength to the country of Qi. Isn't it a big mistake?
The King of Wu refused to listen and went north to attack Qi and defeated the Qi army in Ailing.
When the troops arrived at Zhuanyi, they summoned Duke Ai of Lu and asked for a hundred prisons.
Ji Kangzi sent Zigong to list the Zhou rites to persuade Dazai Pei, and King Wu stopped.
So King Wu stayed to seize the southern territories of Qi and Lu.
In the ninth year, he crusaded against Lu for Zuo and arrived in Lu. He made an alliance with Lu and left.
The year before last, he took advantage of the situation to attack Qi and return.
The year before last, there was another northern expedition to Qi.
King Gou Jian of Yue led his ministers to pay homage to the King of Wu and presented him with generous tributes. The King of Wu was overjoyed.
Only Wu Zixu was afraid and said: The Kingdom of Wu is going to be abandoned.
So he admonished the King of Wu and said: The Yue Kingdom is close to its heart. Although our country can defeat Qi now, it is like a field of stones, which is of no use.
Moreover, "Pangeng's Edict" said that the Shang Dynasty can only prosper if the chaotic and arrogant people are eliminated.
The King of Wu refused to listen and sent Wu Zixu as an envoy to Qi. Zixu entrusted his son to the Bao family of Qi to repay the King of Wu.
When the king of Wu heard about it, he was furious and gave Zixu a sword to commit suicide.
When Zixu was about to die, he said: If you plant catalpa trees on my grave and let them grow enough to make utensils, the Kingdom of Wu will be destroyed.
Plug out my eyes and place them on the east gate of the capital of Wu, so that I can see how the Yue Kingdom destroyed the Wu Kingdom.
Later, the official of Qi State, Bao Shi, killed Qi Daugong.
When King Wu found out, he cried bitterly outside the military gate for three days and then led his army to attack Qi from the sea.
The Qi army defeated the Wu army, and the king of Wu had no choice but to lead the defeated troops back home.
The year before last, King Wu convened the kings of Lu and Wei for an alliance meeting in Lugao.
In the spring of the year before last, King Wu went north to meet with the princes in Huangchi, hoping to dominate the Central Plains and protect the Zhou Dynasty.
In the sixth month of the sixth month, King Gou Jian of Yue attacked Wu.
On Yiyou day, five thousand Yue soldiers fought against Wu soldiers.
Bingxu, captured the prince friend of Wu.
In Dinghai, the Vietnamese army entered the state of Wu.
The Wu people reported the news of their failure to Fu Chai. The King of Wu was afraid that someone would leak the news and let the alliance princes hear the news, so he furiously killed seven people in front of the tent.
In the seventh month of Xinchou, the King of Wu and Duke Ding of Jin competed for the position of leader of the alliance.
King Wu said: My ancestor is the largest among the Zhou clan.
Jin Dinggong said: Among the countries named Ji, only our country of Jin has ever been the overlord.
Zhao Yang, the official of the Jin Dynasty, was angry and wanted to attack the king of Wu, so he made Jin Dinggong the leader of the alliance.
The King of Wu's alliance had concluded, and he separated from Jin Dinggong and wanted to attack the Song Dynasty.
Dazai Pei said: You can defeat the Song Kingdom, but you cannot stay and occupy it.
So he led his troops back home.
Wu State had no crown prince and the country was empty. The King of Wu had been away for a long time and his soldiers were tired, so he sent envoys with generous gifts to negotiate peace with Yue State.
The year before last, Qi doctor Tian Chang killed Qi Jiangong.
The year before last, the country of Yue had become stronger.
King Gou Jian of Yue led his troops to attack Wu and defeated the Wu soldiers in Lize.
Chu State destroyed Chen State.
The year before last, King Gou Jian of Yue attacked Wu again.
The year before last, Vietnamese soldiers besieged the state of Wu.
On Dingmao in November of the previous year, the Yue State defeated the Wu State.
King Gou Jian of Yue wanted to exile King Wu Fu Chai to Yongdong and give him a hundred households to live there.
The King of Wu said: I am old and can no longer serve the King of Yue.
I regret not listening to Zixu's words and letting myself fall into this situation.
So he committed suicide and died.
The King of Yue destroyed the Kingdom of Wu and killed Dazai Pi because he was not loyal to his lord, and then led his troops back to the country.
Tai Shigong said: Confucius said that Taibo can be said to be the pinnacle of morality. He gave up the world to others three times, and the people could not find words to praise him.
I read the ancient text "Spring and Autumn" and realized that Yu in the Central Plains and Juwu in Jingman were brothers.
The benevolent heart of Yanling Jizi persisted in admiring morality and righteousness throughout his life, and he was able to distinguish the pure from the turbid by seeing the subtle things.
Ah, what a well-informed and knowledgeable gentleman!
summary:
Taibo Wu and his younger brother Zhong Yong were sons of Gu Gong Danfu, King Tai of Zhou. Because their father wished to pass the throne to their younger brother Ji Li, and eventually to Ji Li's virtuous son Chang, Taibo and Zhong Yong fled to the land of Jingman. There, they adopted local customs by tattooing their bodies and cutting their hair to show they could not inherit the throne. The Jingman people, finding Taibo righteous, followed him and respected him as Taibo Wu. Taibo died without a son, and Zhong Yong succeeded him. The lineage continued until Zhou Zhang, who was officially granted the land of Wu by King Wu of Zhou after he defeated the Yin dynasty. The kingdom of Wu was passed down through generations, eventually becoming prosperous under King Shoumeng, who was the nineteenth generation from Taibo.

Shoumeng had four sons: Zhufan, Yuji, Yumei, and the virtuous Jizha. Shoumeng wanted Jizha to succeed him, but Jizha refused. The throne was then passed from brother to brother with the intention that it would eventually reach Jizha. After Yumei died, Jizha again fled, so the people established Yumei's son Liao as king. Prince Guang, the son of Zhufan, believed he should be king and secretly recruited a warrior named Zhuan Zhu. During a banquet, Zhuan Zhu assassinated King Liao, and Prince Guang became King Helu. Jizha, upon returning, accepted the new king, stating that as long as the ancestral sacrifices continued, the new king was his sovereign.

Under King Helu, Wu Zixu and Bo Pei were appointed to official positions. Helu, with the help of Wu Zixu, Sun Wu, and the states of Tang and Cai, launched a major attack on Chu, defeating the Chu army five times and capturing the capital, Ying. Wu Zixu and Bo Pei dug up the body of King Ping of Chu to avenge their fathers. Later, Helu's brother Fugai attempted to usurp the throne but was defeated and fled to Chu. In the nineteenth year, King Helu attacked Yue but was wounded and died. Before his death, he told his son Fuchai to remember that Gou Jian of Yue killed his father.

King Fuchai avenged his father by defeating Yue at Fujiao. King Gou Jian of Yue was forced to hide in Kuaiji Mountain and sought peace through the Grand Prime Minister Bo Pei. Wu Zixu advised against this, comparing Gou Jian to Shaokang, who restored the Xia dynasty from a small territory. He warned that Gou Jian was a threat, but the King of Wu listened to Bo Pei and made peace with Yue. Fuchai then focused on northern campaigns against Qi, ignoring Zixu's warnings about the greater threat from Yue. Zixu was eventually forced to commit suicide, asking for his eyes to be placed on the east gate of Wu's capital to see Yue's invasion. While Fuchai was at the Huangchi meeting vying for supremacy with Jin, Yue attacked Wu, capturing the crown prince. After the meeting, Fuchai sought peace with Yue. Eventually, Yue grew stronger, defeated Wu in battle, and besieged its capital. King Fuchai, regretting not listening to Zixu, committed suicide. The King of Yue destroyed Wu and killed Dazai Bo Pei for his disloyalty.

translation:
Since ancient times, the founding emperors who were appointed by heaven and the monarchs who inherited the orthodox and abided by the laws of the late emperors were not only intrinsically noble in character, but also mostly had the help of their relatives.
The rise of the Xia Dynasty was due to the daughter of the Tushan family, and Xia Jie's exile was also related to Moxi.
The rise of the Yin Dynasty also relied on the Nu family, and the murder of King Zhou of Shang was also related to his favoring Daji.
The rise of the Zhou Dynasty also relied on Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, and the capture of King You was also related to his fornication with Bao Si.
Therefore, the "Book of Changes" is based on the two hexagrams "Qian" and "Kun", the "Book of Songs" begins with "Guan Ju", the "Shang Shu" praises Yao for marrying his daughter to Shun, and the "Spring and Autumn" ridicules those who marry their wives without going to meet them in person.
The relationship between husband and wife is the most important ethical relationship in human nature.
In the application of etiquette, only marriage is the most cautious.
When music harmonizes the four seasons, it becomes harmonious. The changes of yin and yang are the rulers of the growth and change of all things. How can we not be cautious?
People can promote human relations, but they can do nothing about destiny.
Indeed, a king cannot get the love of his spouse from his ministers, nor can a father get it from his son, let alone those of low status!
After couples get together, some are unable to produce children and grandchildren; after they are able to produce children, some cannot find a good home.
Isn't this destiny?
Confucius rarely talked about the destiny of heaven, probably because it was difficult to explain clearly.
If we cannot understand the changes of yin and yang, how can we understand the principles of human nature and destiny?
Tai Shigong said: The situation before Qin was too ancient, and the details could not be recorded.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Lu Ehuang became the empress of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and her son was the prince.
In her later years, her appearance deteriorated and she fell out of favor. As Mrs. Qi gained favor, her son Ruyi almost replaced the prince several times.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed King Zhao Ruyi. However, the concubines in Emperor Gaozu's harem could only be safe if they were not favored and alienated.
Empress Lu's eldest daughter was the wife of Zhang Ao, the Marquis of Xuanping, and Zhang Ao's daughter was the queen of Emperor Hui.
Because of their close relationship, Empress Dowager Lu tried every means to try to get her to have a child, but she never had a child. She had to bring someone else's son from the harem and falsely claimed it was her son.
After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, the world had just stabilized and the person who would succeed the throne was not yet clear.
So he raised the status of his relatives, made the Lu brothers kings as assistants, and made Lu Lu's daughter the queen of the young emperor, hoping to make the foundation stronger, but it was of no use.
Empress Lu died and was buried in Changling with Gaozu.
Lu Lu, Lu Chan and others were afraid of being killed, so they plotted to cause trouble.
The ministers conquered them, and heaven guided the Han family's imperial line, and finally eliminated the Lu family.
Only Queen Xiaohui was placed in the North Palace.
The minister ushered the king into the throne, who was Emperor Xiaowen, and he enshrined the ancestral temple of the Han family.
Isn't this destiny?
If it were not destiny, who could take on this important task?
Empress Dowager Bo, whose father was a Wu man and whose surname was Bo, had an affair with Wei Wei, a woman from the original Wei king's clan during the Qin Dynasty, and gave birth to Bo Ji. Bo Ji's father died in Shanin and was buried there.
When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself King of Wei, and Wei sent her daughter to the palace of the King of Wei.
Wei Lao went to Xu Fu's place to see her fortune teller and asked him to see Bo Ji. Xu Fu said that she would definitely be able to give birth to the emperor.
At that time, Xiang Yu and Liu Bang, the king of Han, were fighting over the world in Xingyang, and it was not yet certain who would own the world.
Wei Bao initially joined the King of Han in attacking the King of Chu, but when he heard Xu Negi's words, he felt happy alone, so he betrayed the King of Han, first remaining neutral, and then allied with the King of Chu.
The king of Han sent Cao Shen and others to attack and imprison King Bao of Wei, changed the Gui land he occupied into a county, and sent Bo Ji to Zhizao mansion where criminals were housed.
After the death of King Bao of Wei, the King of Han once entered the Zhizao Mansion and saw Bo Ji's beautiful appearance. He issued an edict to take her into the harem, but she was not favored for more than a year.
When Bo Ji was young, she was very close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier. The three of them made a vow: Whoever gets rich first will not forget the others.
Later, Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier were both favored by the King of Han.
One time when the King of Han was sitting on the Chenggao Platform in the Henan Palace, the two beauties laughed at each other as they talked about their vows with Bo Ji.
When the King of Han heard about it, he asked them why, and they both told the King of Han the truth.
The king of Han felt a little sad and felt sorry for Bo Ji, so he summoned her and stayed with her that day.
Bo Ji said: Last night I dreamed of a blue dragon occupying my belly.
Emperor Gaozu said: This is a sign of a noble person. Let me fulfill it for you.
Fortunately, a boy was born, and he became the king.
After that, Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Dowager Lu was very resentful of the concubines such as Mrs. Qi and others who were favored to serve as Emperor Gaozu's bedtime, so she imprisoned them all and were not allowed to leave the palace.
Because Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu, she was able to leave the palace and follow her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming the Queen Mother of Dai.
The Queen Mother's younger brother Bo Zhao also followed him to Dai.
During the seventeenth year of King Dai's reign, Empress Lu passed away.
The ministers discussed the establishment of a new king. They all hated the powerful power of their relative, the Lu family, and praised Bo's benevolence and kindness. Therefore, they welcomed back the king and established him as Emperor Xiaowen. Empress Dowager Bo changed her title to Empress Dowager, and her younger brother Bo Zhao was named Marquis of Zhi.
Empress Dowager Bo's mother had died before that and was buried in the north of Yueyang.
At this time, Empress Dowager Bo's father was honored as Lingwen Marquis, and a garden of 300 households was set up in Kuaiji County. People below Changcheng were sent to serve and guard the tomb. The sacrifices and ceremonies in the ancestral temple were carried out in accordance with the prescribed etiquette.
There is also a cemetery for Mrs. Lingwenhou in the north of Yueyang. All the etiquette is the same as that at the Lingwenhou Cemetery.
Empress Dowager Bo believed that her mother's family was the descendant of King Wei. Her parents died young, and there were people in the Wei family who served Empress Dowager Bo diligently, so she ordered that the status of the Wei family be restored, and rewards were received according to the degree of closeness.
Only one person in the Bo family was granted the title of Marquis.
Empress Dowager Bo died two years later than Emperor Wen, in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, and was buried in Nanling.
Since Empress Lu was buried with Emperor Gaozu in Changling, she specially built a separate mausoleum for herself, close to Emperor Xiaowen's Ba Mausoleum.
Empress Dowager Dou was a native of Guanjin County, Qinghe County, Zhao State.
During the reign of Queen Mother Lu, Concubine Dou was selected from a good family to serve the Queen Mother in the palace.
Later, the Queen Mother sent the maids out of the palace and gave them to the princes and kings, five for each king. Dou Ji was among these maids.
Dou Ji's family was in Qinghe. Thinking that Zhao State was close to her home, she asked the eunuch in charge of the deportation: "My name must be put on the list of people going to Zhao State."
The eunuch forgot about this and mistakenly put her on the list of people going to Dai.
The roster was read, the edict said it was okay, and it was time to set off.
Dou Ji burst into tears and complained that the eunuch didn't want to go, so he forced her to leave before she was willing to leave.
When he arrived in the Kingdom of Dai, the King of Dai only favored Concubine Dou, and gave birth to a daughter called Prostitute, and later gave birth to two boys.
The queen gave birth to four boys.
The queen died before the king entered the court and became the emperor. When the king became the emperor, the four boys born to the queen also died of illness one after another.
A few months after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, the ministers requested the establishment of a prince. Dou Ji's eldest son was the oldest and was established as the prince.
Dou Ji was also made the queen, and her daughter Liu Piao was the eldest princess.
The next year, he established his youngest son Liu Wu as the acting king, and soon moved to Liang State. This was King Xiao of Liang.
Queen Dou's parents had died long ago and were buried in Guanjin.
At this time, Empress Dowager Bo issued an edict to relevant officials to honor Empress Dou's father as Marquis Ancheng and his mother as Mrs. Ancheng.
He ordered a garden town of 200 households to be set up in Qinghe, which was served and guarded by the local chief minister. Everything was done in accordance with the practices of Lingwen Garden.
Queen Dou's elder brother is Dou Changjun, and his younger brother is Dou Guangguo, also known as Shaojun.
When Shaojun was four or five years old, his family was poor and he was robbed and sold. His family did not know where he was sold.
He resold a dozen more houses and sold them to Yiyang. He went into the mountain to burn charcoal for his master. At night, more than a hundred people were sleeping under the cliff. The cliff collapsed and crushed all the people sleeping below to death. Only Shaojun escaped and was not crushed to death.
He made his own calculations and concluded that he would be made a marquis within a few days, so he went to Chang'an from his master's house.
I heard that Queen Dou was newly ennobled. Her hometown is Guanjin and her surname is Dou.
Although Guangguo was young when he left home, he still knew the name of the county and his family's surname. He also picked mulberries with his sister and fell from a tree. He used these things as evidence and wrote a letter to state his experience.
Queen Dou told Emperor Wen about this, and Guang Guo was summoned and asked him. He explained the situation in detail, and it was indeed good.
Asked what else he could use to prove it, he replied: When my sister left me to go west, she said goodbye to me in the post dormitory. My sister asked for rice soup to wash my hair and food for me to eat, and then she left.
So Queen Dou held her brother and cried bitterly, with tears streaming down her cheeks.
The attendants on the left and right also fell on the ground and cried, helping the queen to mourn together.
So he was rewarded with a lot of land, houses and money, and the Dou brothers, who had the same ancestor as the queen, were enfeoffed and allowed to move to Chang'an.
Jianghou Zhou Bo, General Guan Ying and others said: We people are not going to die, but our lives hang in the hands of the Dou brothers.
These two people were of humble origins, so they had to choose masters and guests, otherwise they would follow Lu's example and conspire to rebel again.
So he chose an older, virtuous and upright scholar to be with them.
From then on, Dou Changjun and Shaojun became humble and courteous gentlemen, and did not dare to rely on their dignity to be arrogant and arrogant towards others.
Queen Dou fell ill and became blind.
Emperor Wen favored Mrs. Shen and Yin Ji of Handan, but neither of them gave birth to children.
After Emperor Xiaowen died, Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne and granted Guangguo the title of Marquis Zhangwu.
Chang Jun died first, so he named his son Peng Zu the Marquis of Nanpi.
When Wu, Chu and other seven kingdoms rebelled, Dou Ying, the son of Queen Mother Dou's party brothers, liked to act chivalrously and led the army to put down the rebellion. He was named Wei Qihou for his military exploits.
A total of three members of the Dou family were granted the title of marquis.
Empress Dowager Dou loved the teachings of Huang Emperor and Lao Tzu. The emperor, the prince and all the children of the Dou family had to read "Huang Emperor" and "Lao Tzu" and respect Huang Lao's scholarship.
Empress Dowager Dou died six years later than Emperor Jing, and she was buried with Emperor Wen in Ba Ling.
He left an edict and gave all the money and property in the East Palace to the eldest princess Liu Piao.
The Queen Mother is from Huaili, and her mother's name is Zang'er.
Zang'er is the granddaughter of Zang Tu, the original king of Yan.
Zang'er first married Wang Zhong of Huaili and gave birth to a son named Xin and two daughters.
Later, Wang Zhong died, and Zang'er remarried to the Tian family in Changling and gave birth to sons Tian Fu and Tian Sheng.
Zang'er's eldest daughter married Jin Wangsun and gave birth to a daughter. Zang'er considered her children a title, and it turned out that her two daughters were both noble people.
So she wanted to rely on her two daughters, so she forcibly took her daughter back from the Jin family's home.
Jin was very angry and refused to break up with his wife, so Zang'er sent his daughter to the prince's womb.
The prince loved her very much and gave birth to three daughters and one son.
When the boy was still pregnant, Beauty Wang dreamed that the sun fell into her arms.
She told the prince about this dream, and the prince said: This is a sign of great wealth.
Emperor Xiaowen died before he was born. After Emperor Xiaojing came to the throne, Mrs. Wang gave birth to the boy.
Previously, Zang'er sent her youngest daughter Erjiao to the palace, and Erjiao gave birth to four boys.
When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo chose a woman from the Bo family to be his concubine.
When Emperor Jing came to the throne, this concubine was made Queen Bo.
The queen had no children and was not favored.
As soon as Queen Mother Bo died, Queen Bo was deposed.
Liu Rong, the eldest son of Emperor Jing, and his mother was Li Ji.
Li Ji is from Qi.
Liu Rong was established as the prince.
The eldest princess Liu Piao has a daughter who plans to be the prince's concubine.
Li Ji was jealous, and it was only through the eldest princess that the beauties of Emperor Jing met Emperor Jing. They received more honor and favor than Li Ji. Li Ji was resentful every day, so she declined the eldest princess's request and refused to marry.
The eldest princess wanted to betroth her daughter to Mrs. Wang's son, and Mrs. Wang agreed.
The eldest princess was angry about this incident, so she often spoke ill of Li Ji in front of Emperor Jing: When Li Ji gathered with ladies and concubines, her attendants would often spit and curse behind them, and use evil and deceptive techniques.
Emperor Jing was angry with Li Ji because of this.
Emperor Jing was once in poor health and unhappy, so he entrusted his sons who were crowned kings to Li Ji and said to her: After I die, you must take good care of them.
Li Ji was angry, refused to agree, and spoke rudely.
Emperor Jing was very angry, but his grudge did not break out.
The eldest princess praised the merits of Mrs. Wang's son every day. Emperor Jing also thought that he had both political integrity and talent, and he had the auspicious sign that his mother had fallen in love with him in the dream. However, he still could not decide on the idea of ​​making the prince a prince.
Mrs. Wang knew that Emperor Jing resented Li Ji, so while his anger was still lingering, she secretly sent someone to urge the ministers to petition Li Ji to be the queen.
After a court meeting, the chief executive said: "A son is more valuable than his mother, and a mother is more valuable than his son. Now that the prince's mother has not been given a title, she should be made queen."
Emperor Jing was angry and said: Is this what you should say?
As a result, the official was executed for the crime, the prince was deposed, and he was named King of Linjiang.
Li Ji was even more resentful and could not see Emperor Jing, so she died in depression.
Mrs. Wang was finally made queen, her son was made prince, and the queen's brother Wang Xin was made Gaihou.
Emperor Jing died and the prince succeeded him as emperor.
Zang'er, the empress dowager's mother, was honored as Lord Pingyuan.
Tian Fu was granted the title of Marquis of Wu'an, and Tian Sheng was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Yang.
Emperor Jing had thirteen sons, one son became emperor, and all twelve sons were crowned kings.
Er Ji died young, and her four sons were all crowned kings.
The Queen Mother's eldest daughter was titled Princess Pingyang, her second daughter was Princess Nangong, and her third daughter was Princess Linli.
Gaihou Wangxin likes drinking.
Tian Fu and Tian Sheng are greedy people and good at using words and arguments.
Wang Zhong died early and was buried in Huaili. He was honored as Gonghou and established a garden of 200 households.
When Lord Pingyuan died, he was buried in Changling together with the Tian family. The cemetery set up had the same specifications as the Gonghou Cemetery.
The Queen Mother died sixteen years later than Emperor Xiao Jing, in the fourth year of Yuanshuo, and was buried with Emperor Jing in Yangling.
A total of three people in the Queen Mother's family were granted the title of marquis.
Queen Wei, also known as Zifu, came from a humble background.
Probably her family was called the Wei family and was within the Pingyang Marquis fiefdom.
Zifu is the singer of Princess Pingyang.
Emperor Wu newly came to the throne and had no sons for several years.
Princess Pingyang selected a dozen girls from good families, dressed them up and stayed at home.
Emperor Wu came back from participating in the ceremony to eliminate disasters and pray for good fortune in Bashang, and stopped by Princess Pingyang's house.
The princess asked all the beauties serving her to come out to see Emperor Wu, but Emperor Wu didn't like it.
After drinking, the singer came in. When Emperor Wu saw her, he only liked Wei Zifu.
On this day, Emperor Wu got up to change his clothes. Zifu served in the emperor's clothes carriage and was honored by his relatives.
Emperor Wu returned to his seat, very happy, and gave Princess Pingyang a thousand catties of gold.
The princess took the opportunity to ask Wei Zifu to be sent to the palace.
After Zifu got in the car, Princess Pingyang stroked her back and said: Let's go, eat well and work hard!
If you are noble, don't forget me.
Zihu had been in the palace for more than a year, but he never received Emperor Wu's favor again.
Emperor Wu singled out the useless palace servants and asked them to leave the palace and go home.
Wei Zifu was then able to see Emperor Wu, and she cried and asked to leave the palace.
The emperor loved her and favored her again, so she became pregnant and became more respected and favored day by day.
Emperor Wu summoned her elder brother Wei Changjun and younger brother Wei Qing to serve as ministers.
Later, Zifu became very favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to three daughters and one son. The son's name was Zhu.
When Emperor Wu was still the crown prince, he married the eldest princess's daughter as his concubine. When he ascended the throne as emperor, the concubine was made empress, with the surname Chen, and she had no children.
The emperor can inherit the throne, and the eldest princess has contributed a lot, so Queen Chen is arrogant and arrogant.
Hearing that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu, he was very angry and sought death many times.
The emperor also became even more angry.
Empress Chen used women's witchcraft to deceive people. Emperor Wu was quite aware of this, so he deposed Empress Chen and made Wei Zifu the empress.
Empress Chen's mother, Princess Dachang, was the sister of Emperor Jing. She repeatedly reproached Emperor Wu's sister, Princess Pingyang, saying: The emperor could not ascend the throne without me. After he ascended the throne, he actually abandoned my daughter. Why don't you feel lucky and forget your duty?
Princess Pingyang said: It was because he had no sons that he was abandoned.
Empress Chen was eager to have a child and spent as much as 90 million on medical expenses, but she was unable to have a child.
When Wei Zifu was made queen, Wei Changjun was already dead, so Emperor Wu appointed Wei Qing as general. Wei Qing made Wei Qing the Marquis of Changping because of his military exploits against the Hu people.
His three sons were still in their infancy, and they were all named princes.
Empress Wei had an older sister, Wei Shaoer, and her son Huo Qubing was named a champion marquis because of his military exploits, and was known as the Cavalry General.
Wei Qing is known as the general.
Empress Wei's son Liu Zheng was made the crown prince.
The Wei family's relatives started their careers with military exploits, and five of them were granted the title of marquis.
When Queen Wei's beauty grew old, Mrs. Wang of Zhao was favored, had a son, and was named King of Qi.
Mrs. Wang died young.
Mrs. Li of Zhongshan was favored and gave birth to a son, who was named King of Changyi.
Mrs. Li died young, and her brother Li Yannian was favored because of his proficiency in music and was named a co-regulator.
The so-called Xielu refers to the former singing and dancing artists.
Their brothers were all exterminated for committing adultery in the harem.
At that time, her eldest brother Li Guangli was the general of the Second Division and was conquering Dayuan. He was not killed. When he returned to Chang'an, the emperor had already killed the Li family. Later, he showed mercy to his family and named him Marquis of Haixi.
The other imperial concubines also have two sons, King Yan and King Guangling.
Their mother was unloved and died of sorrow.
After Mrs. Li's death, Yin Jie and others were alternately favored. However, they all met Emperor Wu as singing girls. They were not women from princely families with fiefdoms and should not be matched with the emperor.
Mr. Chu said: When I was appointed Langguan, I asked Zhong Lisheng, who was familiar with the old affairs of the Han family.
According to him, the Queen Mother gave birth to a daughter when she was among the people, and her father was the grandson of King Jin.
Wang Sun was dead. After Emperor Jing's death, Emperor Wu came to the throne. Only the Queen Mother was still there.
Han Wang's grandson named Yan was usually favored by Emperor Wu. He took the opportunity to talk about the Queen Mother having a daughter in Changling.
Emperor Wu said: Why didn't you tell me earlier?
So I sent someone to take a look first, and she was indeed at home.
Emperor Wu went to meet her in person.
The road was cleared and no movement allowed, the cavalry that led the guard came out of the Hengcheng Gate, and Emperor Wu's chariot sped to Changling.
Entering the inner alley on the west side of the small market, the inner door was closed. Open the door forcefully. Emperor Wu's car entered the inner alley and stopped outside the Jin family's gate. He immediately sent armed cavalry to surround the house to prevent her from escaping and not being able to pick her up even if she came in person.
Then he sent his ministers on the left and right to search for him.
Everyone in the Jin family was frightened, and Jin girl hid under the bed in the inner room.
After finding her, the entourage helped her out and asked her to meet the emperor.
Emperor Wu got out of the car and cried: Ouch!
My eldest sister, why are you hiding so deeply?
He ordered the passenger car to pick her up, turned around and drove back to the city, straight into Changle Palace.
On the way, Emperor Wu ordered the people guarding the palace gate to inform the Queen Mother of his name, and he would go to see the Queen Mother as soon as the car arrived.
The Queen Mother said: Your Majesty is tired, where did you come from?
Emperor Wu said: Today I found my sister in Changling and came with her.
He turned back to his sister and said: Meet the Queen Mother!
The Queen Mother said: Is this my daughter?
Answered: Yes.
The Queen Mother burst into tears, and her daughter also fell to the ground and cried.
Emperor Wu came to congratulate the Queen Mother and his sister with wine in his hands. He gave 10 million yuan, 300 slaves, 100 hectares of land, and a high-class mansion to his sister.
The Queen Mother thanked her and said, "It's a waste of time for the Emperor."
So Princess Pingyang, Princess Nangong and Princess Linli were summoned to pay homage to her sister, and she was given the title Xiuchengjun.
She has a son and a daughter.
The son's name was Xiucheng Zizhong, and his daughter became the queen of the princes and kings.
These two children were not from the Liu family, so the Queen Mother loved them.
Xiuchengzi Zhong was arrogant and indulgent, and often bullied and oppressed officials and people. People were worried about this.
After Wei Zifu was established as queen, her younger brother Wei Qing, named Zhongqing, was granted the title of Marquis of Changping with the position of general.
He has four sons. The eldest son, Mr. Wei, is the prince who is preparing to inherit the title. He once served as the emperor's attendant, and his status is noble and very popular.
The three younger brothers of Mr. and Mrs. Wei were all granted the title of marquis, and each was given a land of 1,300 households. One was named the Marquis of Yin'an, the other was the Marquis of Fagan, and the other was the Marquis of Yichun. Their wealth shocked the world.
There is such a ballad circulating in the world: Don't be too happy when giving birth to a child, don't show your anger when giving birth to a girl, haven't you seen Wei Zifu dominate the world!
At that time, Princess Pingyang was a widow and she should choose a prince to be her husband.
The princess and her attendants discussed who among the princes in Chang'an City could be her husband, and they all said that General Wei Qing could be her husband.
The princess smiled and said: "He is a man who leaves my house. I often let him follow me on horseback. How can I let him be my husband?"
The attendants said: Now the general's sister is the queen, her three sons have all been ennobled, and her wealth has shocked the world. Why does the princess underestimate her?
So the princess agreed.
He told the queen about this, and the queen reported it to Emperor Wu, who ordered General Wei to be the husband of Princess Pingyang.
Mr. Chu said: A husband can change endlessly like a dragon.
The biography says: If a snake becomes a dragon, it will not change its pattern; if a home becomes a country, it will not change its surname.
When a husband is rich, all his stains can be covered up and eliminated, leaving only the glory and glory. How can the things that happened when he was poor and lowly affect him?
During the reign of Emperor Wu, he doted on his wife Yin Jieyu.
Mrs. Xing's official name is Ao'e, and people call her Aohe.
Aohe's rank is equivalent to an official with a salary of two thousand dan, Ronghua's rank is equivalent to that of a prince, and Jieyu's status is equivalent to that of a prince.
Someone was once promoted from Jieyu to queen.
Mrs. Yin and Mrs. Xing were favored at the same time, but Emperor Wu ordered them not to meet each other.
Once Mrs. Yin personally requested Emperor Wu to see Mrs. Xing, and Emperor Wu agreed.
He asked another lady to dress up, followed by dozens of attendants, pretending to be Mrs. Xing and came in front of her.
Mrs. Yin walked up to her and said, "This is not Mrs. Xing."
Emperor Wu said: Why do you say this?
Mrs. Yin replied: Judging from her figure, appearance and posture, she is not good enough to match the emperor.
So Emperor Wu ordered Mrs. Xing to put on old clothes and come alone.
Mrs. Yin saw her from a distance and said: This is true.
So she lowered her head and cried, feeling sad that she was not as good as Mrs. Xing.
The proverb says: Once a beautiful woman enters the house, she becomes the enemy of the ugly woman.
Mr. Chu said: Bathing does not have to go to the rivers and seas, the main thing is to remove dirt; riding a horse does not have to be a famous horse, the main thing is to be good at running; scholars do not have to be better than ordinary people in the world, the main thing is to understand the truth; women do not have to be of noble birth, the main thing is to be chaste and beautiful.
The biography says: No matter how beautiful or ugly a woman is, she will be jealous as soon as she enters the family; whether a scholar is virtuous or not, he will be jealous as soon as he enters the court.
Beautiful women are the enemies of ugly women, isn’t it right?
Mrs. Gou Yi, surnamed Zhao, was from Hejian.
He was favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to a son, Emperor Zhao.
Emperor Zhao was born when Emperor Wu was seventy years old.
Emperor Zhao was just five years old when he came to the throne.
After Prince Wei was deposed, there was no new crown prince.
And King Liu Dan of Yan wrote a letter, willing to return to the capital and join the palace as a guard.
Emperor Wu was very angry and immediately beheaded the envoy of King Yan in Beique.
The emperor lived in Ganquan Palace and called a painter to draw a picture of Zhou Gong carrying the king on his back.
So the officials knew that Emperor Wu wanted to make his youngest son the prince.
A few days later, Emperor Wu condemned Mrs. Gou Yi.
The lady took off her hairpin and earrings and kowtowed to apologize.
Emperor Wu said: Take her away and send her to Yeting Prison!
The lady looked back and saw Emperor Wu saying: "Go quickly, you can't live!"
The lady died in Yunyang Palace.
When he died, a storm blew up the dust, and the people were very sad.
The messenger took the coffin to the burial site at night and marked the burial place.
Afterwards, Emperor Wu asked around him in his spare time: "What do people say about this matter?"
The left and right replied: People say that since her son is to be established, why do they need to get rid of his mother? Emperor Wu said: Yes.
This is beyond the understanding of children and fools.
In the past, the reason why the country was in trouble was because the monarch was young and his mother was in her prime.
When a woman lives alone, she will become arrogant, arrogant and indulgent, and no one can stop her.
Haven't you heard about Queen Lu?
Therefore, all the mothers who gave birth to children for Emperor Wu, whether male or female, were not condemned and executed. Can we say that they are not sages?
Such a clear vision and careful consideration for future generations are not within the reach of those ignorant and ignorant Confucians.
The posthumous title is Wu. Is it a false name?
summary:
The crucial role of marriage and imperial consorts in the rise and fall of dynasties. Founding emperors and orthodox monarchs often relied on their relatives for support. The Xia Dynasty rose through the Tushan family's daughter and fell with Moxi; the Yin Dynasty rose through the Nu family and fell due to Daji; the Zhou Dynasty rose through Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, while King You's downfall involved Bao Si. The text emphasizes that husband-wife relationships are the most important ethical bond, and marriage is the most cautious ritual application.

The narrative then details several Han Dynasty empresses and their families. Empress Lu, wife of Emperor Gaozu, lost favor in her later years as Lady Qi gained prominence. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed Prince Ruyi. She tried to secure succession through her daughter's child but failed, eventually elevating her Lu relatives. After her death, the Lu clan plotted rebellion but were eliminated by ministers, who installed Emperor Xiaowen.

Empress Dowager Bo's story follows. Her mother had an affair with a Wei clan member during Qin times, producing Bo Ji. A fortune-teller predicted she would bear an emperor. Wei Bao, hearing this, betrayed the King of Han but was defeated. Bo Ji entered the harem but remained unfavored for over a year. Through friends' intervention, she gained the king's favor, dreamed of a blue dragon in her belly, and bore a son. After Gaozu's death, because she was rarely favored, she escaped Empress Lu's persecution and followed her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming Queen Mother of Dai. After Empress Lu's death, ministers chose her son as Emperor Xiaowen.

Empress Dowager Dou was selected for palace service during Empress Lu's reign. When palace maids were distributed to princes, she wanted to go to Zhao but was mistakenly sent to Dai. There, the King of Dai favored her, and she bore two sons. After the queen and her sons died, Dou Ji's eldest son became crown prince, and she became empress. Her brother Dou Guangguo, sold as a child, later identified himself through shared memories and was reunited with her. The Dou family received honors, and Empress Dowager Dou promoted Huang-Lao teachings.

The text also covers Empress Wang, whose mother Zang'er forcibly took her daughter from her husband Jin Wangsun and sent her to the prince's womb. She dreamed of the sun falling into her arms and bore a son who became Emperor Wu. Lady Li Ji, mother of the eldest son, refused the eldest princess's marriage proposal for her daughter, leading to conflict. Through manipulation, Mrs. Wang's son became crown prince instead.

Wei Zifu, a singer from Princess Pingyang's household, caught Emperor Wu's attention. After initial neglect, she became pregnant and gained favor, eventually becoming empress after Empress Chen was deposed for witchcraft. Her brother Wei Qing became a general, and her family produced five marquises.

The text concludes with Emperor Wu's later consorts and his controversial execution of Lady Gou Yi, mother of his youngest son. He explained that young monarchs with living mothers caused chaos, citing Empress Lu as an example. All mothers of Emperor Wu's children were executed to prevent such problems.

translation:
Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State.
His ancestor was from the Song Dynasty, named Uncle Kong Fang.
Uncle Fang gave birth to Bo Xia, and Bo Xia gave birth to Shu Liang He.
Shu Lianghe and Yehe, a woman named Yan, gave birth to Confucius. They got Confucius after they went to Niqiu Mountain to pray to the gods.
Confucius was born in the 22nd year of Duke Xiang of Lu.
The top of his head was concave when he was born, so he was named Qiu. The courtesy name is Zhongni and the surname is Kong.
Shortly after Confucius was born, his uncle Liang He died and was buried in Fangshan.
Fangshan was in the east of Lu State, so Confucius could not know for sure where his father's tomb was. His mother did not tell him where his father was buried.
When Confucius was a child, he played games, often setting up various sacrificial vessels and learning the ritual movements of sacrificial offerings.
After Confucius's mother died, she temporarily placed her coffin in the Five Fathers' Road without burying her. This was out of prudent consideration.
The mother of Wan's father, who was from Zouyi, told him the burial place of Confucius's father, and then Confucius moved his mother to Fangshan to be buried with his father.
When Confucius was mourning with a filial piety belt tied around his waist, Ji Sun held a banquet to entertain celebrities, and Confucius went to attend.
Ji Sun's retainer Yang Hu stopped him and said: "Ji's family is entertaining celebrities, but you are not invited."
Confucius withdrew because of this.
When Confucius was seventeen years old, Lizi, a senior official in the state of Lu, was critically ill. Before his death, he warned his son Yizi: Confucius is a descendant of a saint, and his ancestors perished in the Song Dynasty.
His ancestor Fufu He was supposed to succeed as the king of Song Dynasty, but he gave way to his younger brother Li Gong.
When another of his ancestors, Zheng Kao's father, assisted Song Dai Gong, Song Wu Gong, and Song Xuangong in three dynasties, he was more respectful every time he was given orders. Therefore, the inscription on Zheng Kao's father's tripod says: The first appointment was received with a bow, the second appointment was received with a bow, and the third appointment was bowed and received.
When I walked, I avoided the middle of the road and walked against the wall, and no one dared to bully me. I just made batter and porridge in this cauldron to survive.
His frugality has reached this point.
I heard that although the descendants of saints may not necessarily become kings and govern, there will definitely be people with outstanding talents and virtues.
Now Confucius is young and courteous. Isn't he a man of outstanding talents and virtue?
If I die, you must take him as your teacher.
After Meng Lizi died, Meng Yizi and Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, went to Confucius to learn etiquette.
This year, Ji Wuzi died, and Pingzi succeeded to the throne.
Confucius' family was poor and of low status.
When he came of age, he worked as a clerk in charge of the Ji family's warehouse, and he was a cashier who could calculate money and grain fairly and accurately. He also worked as a clerk in charge of pastures, and he was able to breed livestock well.
Therefore, he was promoted to Sikong in charge of construction projects.
Not long after, he left the state of Lu, was ostracized in the state of Qi, was expelled in the states of Song and Wei, was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai, and finally returned to the state of Lu.
Confucius was nine feet six inches tall. People called him "The Long Man" because they thought he was different from ordinary people.
The State of Lu was still very kind to him, so he returned to the State of Lu.
Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, said to Duke Zhao of Lu: Please allow me to go on a mission to Zhou with Confucius.
Duke Zhao of Lu gave him a carriage, two horses, and a boy servant, and set off with him to the Kingdom of Zhou to learn etiquette and pay a visit to Lao Tzu.
When they were saying goodbye, Lao Tzu came out to see them off and said: I heard that wealthy people give gifts with property, and people with noble moral character give gifts with words.
I am not a wealthy person, so I can only steal the name of a noble person and send you off with words. These sentences are: A wise and thoughtful person is often threatened with death because he likes to talk about others; a knowledgeable, eloquent and insightful person is often in trouble and endangers himself, because he likes to expose the sins of others.
Children should not have selfish motives, and ministers should not think only of themselves but the monarch. After Confucius returned to the state of Lu from Zhou Dynasty, more and more disciples followed him.
At this time, Jin Pinggong was promiscuous and immoral, and the six ministers of the Han, Zhao, Wei, Zhonghang, Fan, and Zhi families controlled the state affairs and constantly sent troops to attack the feudal states in the east. King Ling of Chu had a strong army and often invaded other countries in the Central Plains; Qi was a big country and close to Lu.
The state of Lu was small and weak. If it surrendered to the state of Chu, it would anger the state of Jin. If it surrendered to the state of Jin, it would cause the state of Chu to attack. If it did not serve Qi well, Qi's army would invade the state of Lu.
Lu Zhaogong was twenty years old and Confucius was thirty years old.
Duke Jinggong of Qi and Yan Ying came to the state of Lu. Duke Jinggong asked Confucius: "In the past, Duke Qin's country was small and remote. Why was he able to dominate?"
Confucius replied: Although the Qin State is small, its ambitions are great; although its location is remote, its governance is very appropriate.
Duke Mu of Qin personally pulled Baili Xi, who had been redeemed with five black ram skins, and awarded him the title of a great official. As soon as he was released from detention, Qin Jun discussed with him for three days, and then let him take charge of the state affairs.
Using this spirit to govern the country can even rule the entire world. Being an overlord is not a big deal.
Jinggong was very happy after hearing this.
When Confucius was thirty-five years old, Ji Pingzi offended Lu Zhaogong for having a cockfight with Li Zhaobo. Zhaogong led his army to attack Pingzi. If the king does not look like a king, the ministers do not look like ministers, the father does not look like a father, and the son does not look like a son, even if there is a lot of food, how can I eat it?
Another day, Jinggong asked Confucius for advice on the principles of government. Confucius said: The most important thing in managing a country is to save money.

If you want to use this set of rules to change the customs of Qi, I'm afraid this is not a good way to guide the people.
After that, although Qi Jinggong received Confucius politely, he no longer asked questions about etiquette.

Some of the officials of Qi wanted to harm Confucius, and Confucius heard about it.

Confucius then left Qi and returned to Lu.

The State of Wu attacked the State of Yue and destroyed the capital of the State of Yue, Kuaiji, and obtained a large bone that could fill a cart.

The envoy from Wu State asked again: "Who is the god?"

Wu envoy asked again: What is the Fangfeng family responsible for offering sacrifices to?
Confucius said: The county chief of the Wanggong family, who supervises the sacrifices in Fengshan and Yushan areas, has the surname Li.
In Yu, Xia, and Shang Dynasties, he was called Wang Yi, in Zhou Dynasty, he was called Chang Zhai, and now he is called adults.
Wu Shi asked: How tall can a person be?

After hearing this, the envoy from the State of Wu said: What a great saint!
Ji Huanzi had a favorite named Zhongliang Huai, who had a grudge against Yang Hu.
Yang Hu wanted to expel Zhong Liang Huai, but Ji's retainer Gong Shan Buxu stopped him.
In the autumn of this year, Zhongliang Huai became even more arrogant, and Yang Hu captured Zhong Liang Huai.

In the eighth year of Lu Dinggong's reign, Gongshan Buxuan failed under Ji Huanzi, so he took advantage of Yanghu's rebellion and planned to abolish the legitimate heirs of Jisun, Mengsun, and Shusun families, and establish a bastard son who Yanghu had always loved, so he arrested Ji Huanzi.
Huanzi designed to deceive him and was able to escape.
In the ninth year of Duke Dinggong of Lu, Yang Hu failed in his rebellion and fled to Qi.
At this time, Confucius was fifty years old.
Gongshan Buxuan used Philadelphia to rebel against the Ji family, and he sent people to summon Confucius to help.
Confucius has been exploring the way to govern the country for a long time, but he was depressed and had nowhere to apply it. Although Philadelphia is small now, it should be about the same!
Confucius wanted to go, but Zilu was unhappy and stopped Confucius.
Confucius said: If they invite me to go, will my trip be in vain?

Confucius was promoted from the chief of Zhongdu to Sikong, and from Sikong to the great Sikou.

Please arrange for Sima Zuo and You to go together.
Duke Ding said: OK.
So I took Zuo and You Sima with me.

Qi Jinggong felt very ashamed and directed the orchestra to retreat.

So some acrobats and short dwarfs came to perform.

Please order the officials in charge to execute it!
So the officials in charge cut them in half according to law and ordered them to live apart.
Qi Jinggong was greatly frightened and deeply touched. He knew that it was difficult to rival Lu in terms of morality.
