What should I do?
The official in charge stepped forward and replied: When a gentleman makes a mistake, he uses practical actions to apologize to others and admits his mistake; when a villain makes a mistake, he uses sweet words to cover it up.
If you feel sad, take concrete actions to express your apology.
So Qi Jinggong returned the land of Yun, Wenyang, and Guiyin of Lu State that he had invaded in the past, in order to apologize and repent to Lu State.
In the summer of the thirteenth year of Duke Dinggong of Lu, Confucius said to Duke Dinggong: Weapons cannot be stored in the homes of ministers, and city walls one foot high and three hundred feet long cannot be built in the fiefdom of officials.

In December, Lu Dinggong led his troops to surround Chengcheng but could not capture it.
In the fourteenth year of Lu Dinggong, Confucius was fifty-six years old. He acted as the chief minister in the affairs of the prime minister, with a look of joy on his face.
His disciples said: I heard that a gentleman will not be afraid when a great disaster comes, nor will he be overjoyed when a great blessing comes.
Confucius said: There is this saying, but isn't there another saying: "Being in a high position and treating the virtuous but a lowly person is content with yourself?"
So Confucius killed the official Shaozhengmao who was disturbing the state affairs.

Why not give them some land first?
Li Kuan said: Let's try to stop them first. If that doesn't work, then give them the land. Is it too late?

Ji Huanzi finally accepted the women's band sent by Qi State and did not attend to government affairs for three days. After the suburban sacrifice, he violated common etiquette and did not give the sacrificial meat and the ritual utensils used in the suburban sacrifice to the doctor.
So Confucius left the state of Lu and stayed in the camp overnight that day.
A musician named Shi Ji from the state of Lu came to see him off and said, "Sir, you are not at fault." Confucius said: Can I sing a song?
So he sang: Those women's mouths can drive away ministers and cronies; approaching those women can cause people to ruin their affairs.
Being leisurely and comfortable is the only way I can spend my time!
After Master Ji returned, Huanzi asked him: What did Confucius say?
Master, tell me the truth.
Huanzi sighed and said, "Sir, you blame us for accepting that group of female musicians from Qi State!"
Confucius then went to Weiguo and stayed at the home of Yan Zhuozou, the brother of Zilu's wife.
Duke Linggong of Wei asked Confucius: How much salary did you receive in Lu?
Confucius replied: Sixty thousand dou of salary.
Weiguo also gave him a salary of 60,000 dou.
Not long after, someone slandered Confucius in front of Duke Linggong of Wei. Duke Linggong of Wei sent Gongsun Yu to use troops to monitor Confucius' coming and going.
Confucius was afraid of being punished here, so he stayed in Weiguo for ten months and then left Weiguo.
Confucius was about to go to the state of Chen and passed a place called Kuang. His disciple Yan Ke drove his chariot for him. Yan Ke pointed his horse whip at Kuang and said, "I have entered this city through that gap before."

Yan Yuan said: Teacher, how dare I die while you are still alive!
The Kuang people besieged Confucius more and more urgently, and the disciples were very frightened.
Confucius said: King Wen of Zhou has passed away. Isn’t the ritual and music system of the Zhou Dynasty still with us?
If God wanted to destroy these rituals and music systems, it would not allow those of us who will die after death to assume the responsibility of maintaining them.
God did not intend to eliminate these rituals and music of the Zhou Dynasty, so what can the Kuang people do to me!
Confucius sent a disciple to the capital of Wei to serve as Ning Wuzi's retainer, and then he was able to leave Kuangdi.
After Confucius left Kuangdi, he went to a place called Pu. After more than a month, he returned to Weiguo and stayed at Zang Boyu's house.
Duke Linggong of Wei had a wife named Nanzi who sent someone to say to Confucius: Gentlemen from all countries who think highly of our monarch and are willing to establish a brotherly relationship with our monarch will definitely come to see our monarch's wife. Our monarch's wife hopes to meet you.
Confucius refused at first, but finally went to see her as a last resort.
The lady sat in the curtain made by Gebu and waited.
After Confucius entered the door, he kowtowed to the north.
The lady bowed twice in the curtain, and the jade jewelry she wore made a clear clanking sound.
Afterwards, Confucius said: I didn't want to see her before, but now that I have no choice but to see her, I should thank her politely.
Zilu was not happy.
Confucius swore: If what I say is not true, God will hate me!
Let God abandon me!
After living in Weiguo for more than a month, Duke Linggong and his wife Nan rode in a carriage together. The eunuch Yongqu accompanied him on the right side of the carriage. After leaving the palace, he asked Confucius to sit in the second carriage and follow him, walking through the market in a swaggering manner.
Confucius said: I have not seen him as fond of virtue as he is fond of beauty.
So he was disgusted with what Wei Linggong did, so he left Wei State and went to Cao State.
This year, Lu Dinggong passed away.
Confucius left the State of Cao and arrived in the State of Song, where he practiced etiquette with his disciples under a big tree.
Sima Huan of the Song Dynasty wanted to kill Confucius, so he cut down the tree.
Confucius had no choice but to leave this place.
The disciples urged: We can leave quickly.
Confucius said: Since God has given me the mission of preaching morality, what can Huan Miao do to me?
When Confucius arrived in the state of Zheng, he became separated from his disciples. Confucius stood alone at the east gate of the outer city.
When the people of Zheng saw it, they said to Zigong: There is a man at the east gate. His forehead is like Yao, his neck is like Gaotao, and his shoulders are like Zheng Zichan. But from the waist down, he is three inches shorter than Yu. He looks embarrassed and listless, really like a lost dog.
When Zigong met, he told Confucius the truth.
Confucius said happily: He may not be right when he describes my appearance, but he is absolutely right when he says that I look like a lost dog! Absolutely right.
Confucius then arrived in the state of Chen and stayed at the home of Sadako in Sicheng.
More than a year later, King Wu Fucha came to attack Chen State and captured three cities before retreating.
Zhao Yang attacked Chaoge.
Chu State surrounded Cai State, and Cai State moved to Wu.
The state of Wu defeated King Gou Jian of Yue in Kuaiji.

In the past, King Wu of the Zhou Dynasty conquered the Zhou Dynasty and destroyed the Shang Dynasty, which established ties with the various ethnic groups and allowed all ethnic groups of the Nine Barbarians and Barbarians to contribute their own local specialties, so that they could not forget their responsibilities and obligations.
So the Sushen tribe presented arrows made of mulberry wood and arrowheads made of stone, one foot and eight inches long.
In order to show his virtue, King Wu of Zhou gave the arrows of the Sushen tribe to his eldest daughter Taiji. Later, Taiji married Duke Yuhu, and Duke Yuhu granted him a title in the state of Chen.
At the beginning, the royal family distributed treasures and jades to the princes with the same surname to show that they valued their relatives; the tributes from distant places were given to princes with the same surname to show that they valued their relatives; the tributes from distant places were given to princes with the same surname to remind them not to forget to obey the Zhou Dynasty.
Therefore, the arrows from the Sushen tribe were distributed to Chen Guo.
After hearing this, Chen Minggong asked people to search in the warehouse where tributes from all parties were stored, and sure enough, they found this kind of arrow.
Confucius lived in the State of Chen for three years, which coincided with the struggle for hegemony between the State of Jin and the State of Chu. The two countries took turns attacking the State of Chen. Until the State of Wu attacked the State of Chen, the State of Chen was often invaded.
Confucius said: Go back, go back!
The disciples in my hometown all have high aspirations, they are all enterprising, and they have not forgotten their original intentions.
So Confucius left the state of Chen.
Confucius passed by a place called Pu, and happened to meet the Gongshu family who occupied Pu and rebelled against the country. The people of Pu detained Confucius.
One of Confucius's disciples named Gong Liangru brought five cars to follow Confucius around the world.
He was a tall man, talented, virtuous, and brave. He said to Confucius: I used to travel around Kuang with my teacher and encountered dangers. Now I encounter dangers here again. This is destined to happen.
My teacher and I once again encountered disaster and died fighting.
Gong Liangru fought fiercely with the Pu people. The Pu people were frightened and said to Confucius: If you don't go to Weiguo, I will let you go.
Confucius made a covenant with them, and then he let Confucius and the others go out through the east gate.
Confucius then went to Weiguo.
Zigong said: Can a covenant be broken?
Confucius said: God will not pay attention to a covenant made under threat.
Duke Linggong of Wei was very happy when he heard that Confucius had arrived and rushed to the outskirts to greet him personally.
Duke Linggong asked Confucius: "Can this place be conquered?"
Confucius replied: Yes.
Duke Linggong said: "My doctor thinks that it is not possible to attack, because the current Pudi is a barrier against Jin and Chu. I am afraid it is not allowed to attack with our defending army, right?"
Confucius said: The men in Pudi are determined to defend the country to the death, and the women have the desire to guard Xihe.
What I said I wanted to attack were only the four or five people who led the rebellion. Wei Linggong said: Very good.
But no troops were sent to attack Pudi.
Duke Linggong of Wei was old and was very lazy about state affairs, and he did not use Confucius.
Confucius sighed and said: If someone hires me, one year will be enough, and three years will be enough to achieve great results.
Confucius had no choice but to leave Weiguo.
Foji xī served as the chief of Zhongmu.
Zhao Jianzi of the Jin State attacked the Fan family and the Zhongxing family and crusaded against Zhongmou.
Foji then occupied Zhongmou, rebelled against Zhao Jianzi, and sent people to invite Confucius. Confucius planned to go.
Zilu said: I heard a teacher say: A gentleman will not go to someone who does bad things personally.
Now the Buddha's Pillow has occupied Zhongmou and is rebelling. You want to go there. Why?
Confucius said: I have said this.
But didn’t I also say that hard things can’t be polished off? Didn’t I also say that white things can’t be dyed black.
Am I just looking at the melons but not eating them? How can I hang them there without being eaten?
Once when Confucius was knocking on the chime, a man carrying a straw basket passed by the door and said: If you are interested, just knock on the stone chime!
The chime is beating loudly and urgently, which means that no one understands you and you are planning to give up!
Confucius learned to play the piano from his teacher Xiangzi. He studied for ten days in a row and did not learn any new music. Shi Xiangzi said: It’s time to learn some new songs.
Confucius said: I am already familiar with music, but I have not yet mastered the technique of playing the piano.
After some time, Shi Xiangzi said again: "You are already familiar with the technique of playing the piano. You can learn some new songs."
Confucius said: I have not yet understood the emotional meaning expressed in the music.
After some time, Shi Xiangzi said: I have understood the ideas expressed in the music and can learn more.
Confucius said: I have not yet realized what kind of person the composer is.
After some time, Confucius was solemn and quiet, thinking deeply about something, and then he felt relaxed and happy, showing his ambition.
Said: I can understand what kind of person the composer is. His skin is dark, tall, and his eyes are bright and deep. He is like a king who rules the four directions. Who else can be like this except King Wen of Zhou!
Shi Xiangzi respectfully left his seat, bowed twice to Confucius, and said: My teacher originally said that this is the "Wen Wang Cao".
Since Confucius could not be reused by Wei Guo, he planned to go west to meet Zhao Jianzi.
When they arrived at the Yellow River, they heard the news that Dou Mingdu and Shun Hua had been killed by Zhao Jianzi. Facing the Yellow River, he sighed with emotion and said: The Yellow River is magnificent, so majestic and grand. I didn't cross the Yellow River, it must be an arrangement of fate!
Zigong rushed forward and asked: "I would like to ask the teacher, what do you mean by this?"
Confucius said: Dou Mingdu and Shunhua were both talented and virtuous officials in Jin.
When Zhao Jianzi had not succeeded, he relied on these two talents to enter politics; when he succeeded, he killed them to take power.
I have heard that if a place kills its cubs by caesarean section, the unicorns will not come to its countryside, and the ponds will be drained to catch fish, so the dragons will not coordinate the yin and yang to create rain, and the bird nests will be overturned and the eggs will be destroyed, so the phoenix will not come here to fly.
Why is this?
A gentleman should not harm his own kind.
Those birds and beasts know how to avoid unjust behavior, let alone me, Confucius!
So he returned to his hometown, Zouxiang, and composed the music "Zou Cao" to mourn the two sages Dou Mingdu and Shunhua.
Then he returned to Weiguo and stayed at Zang Boyu's house.
One day, Duke Linggong of Wei asked Confucius about the formation of troops for battle.
Confucius replied: I have heard about sacrifices, but I have never learned about arranging troops.
The next day, when Wei Linggong was talking to Confucius, he saw wild geese flying in the sky. He just raised his head and looked up, but his expression was not on Confucius.
Confucius then left the state of Wei and went to the state of Chen.
In the summer of this year, Wei Linggong died, and his grandson was appointed as the king. This was Wei Chugong.

After the funeral was over, I thought I would return to Confucius.
Dafu Gongzhiyu said: In the past, our country Lu Dinggong once appointed him, but he failed to follow through and was ridiculed by the princes.

Ji Kangzi said: Who should I call?
Gong Zhiyu said: We must summon Ranqiu.

On this day, Confucius said: Go back, go back!
Those disciples in my hometown have lofty ambitions but broad-minded actions, and are rich in literary talents. I really don’t know where to start to educate them.
Zigong knew that Confucius missed his hometown and wanted to go back. When sending Ranqiu off, he told him that if he was re-employed, he should think about inviting the teacher back.
After Ran Qiu left, Confucius moved from the state of Chen to the state of Cai the next year.
Cai Zhaogong was preparing to go to the State of Wu, and it was the king of the State of Wu who summoned him.
Previously, Duke Zhao deceived his ministers and moved the capital to Zhoulai. This time he was going to the Kingdom of Wu again. The officials were worried that he would move the capital again. Gongsun Pian shot Duke Zhao with an arrow on the way.
Then, the Chu army came to invade Cai.
In the autumn of the same year, Qi Jinggong passed away.
In the second year, Confucius went from Cai State to Ye Yi.
Ye Gong asked Confucius how to govern. Confucius said: The key to governing is to recruit wise men from far away and make people nearby join.
One day, Lord Ye asked Zilu what Confucius was like, but Zilu didn't answer.
Confucius heard about this and said: Zhong Yu, why don't you answer him? He is a man who never gets tired when he studies principles, never gets tired of teaching others, forgets to eat when he is studying hard, forgets sorrow when he is happy, doesn't know that aging is coming, etc.
Confucius left Ye Di of Chu State and returned to Cai State.
On the road, he met Chang Ju and Jie Zhong, who were plowing the fields side by side. Confucius thought they were hermits, so he sent Zi Lu to find out where the ferry was.
Chang Ju said: Who is the man holding the reins of the horse?
Zilu replied: It is Confucius.
Chang Ju asked again: "Is he Confucius from Lu?"
Zilu said: Yes.
Chang Ju said: Then he should know where the ferry is. Jie Dong asked Zi Lu again: "Who are you?" Zilu said: I am Zhong Yu.
Jie Dun said: Are you a disciple of Confucius?
Zilu said: Yes.
Jie Dun said: The world is in turmoil everywhere, and who can change this situation?
Besides, instead of running around with those who are fleeing from the rioters, why not follow those of us who are fleeing from the troubled times?
After saying that, he continued to plow the fields non-stop.
Zilu told Confucius this, and Confucius said disappointedly: We can't live in the mountains and forests with the birds and beasts. If the world were peaceful, I wouldn't have to run around trying to change this situation.
One day, when Zi Lu was walking alone, he met an old man carrying a weeding tool on his shoulder. Zilu asked him: Have you seen my teacher?
The old man said: You people are not diligent in your limbs and cannot distinguish the grains. How can I know who your teacher is?
After saying that, he went to pull weeds on crutches.
Later, Zilu told Confucius what happened. Confucius said: This is a hermit.
I asked Zilu to look there again, but the old man was gone.
Three years after Confucius moved to the state of Cai, the state of Wu attacked the state of Chen.
The State of Chu rescued the State of Chen, and the army was stationed in Chengfu.
Hearing that Confucius lived on the border of Chen and Cai, Chu sent people to hire Confucius.
Confucius was about to go to see and accept the betrothal gift. The officials of Chen and Cai discussed and said: Confucius is a talented and virtuous man, and what he criticizes and satirizes are all about the shortcomings of the princes.
Now we have been stuck between Chen and Cai for a long time. The administration and actions of the officials are not in line with Zhongni's wishes.
Today's Chu State is a big country, but it came to hire Confucius.
If Confucius is reused in Chu State, then our officials in power in Chen and Cai will be in danger.
So both sides sent some laborers to besiege Confucius in the wild.
Confucius and his disciples were unable to move and their food supply was cut off.
The disciples who followed him were sick from hunger and could not stand up.
But Confucius continued to give lectures, recite poems, sing, and play the piano to everyone.
Zilu came to see Confucius angrily: Is there a time when a gentleman is in trouble?
Confucius said: A gentleman can maintain his integrity and remain unwavering in the face of adversity, while a young man will not exercise restraint when faced with adversity and will do anything that goes too far.
At this time, Zigong's expression also changed.
Confucius said: Ci, do you think I am a man of erudition and memorization?
Zigong replied: Yes.
Isn't it right?
Confucius said: No.
I grasp the basic principles of things and integrate them.
Confucius knew that his disciples were unhappy. Then he called Lai Zilu and asked: "The Book of Songs" says that it is neither a rhinoceros nor a tiger, but it is wandering in the wilderness. Isn't it because of the moral principles we uphold?
Why have we ended up in this situation?
Zilu said: Perhaps our kindness is not enough?
So people don’t trust us; it must be because we are not resourceful enough, right?
So they wouldn't let us pass.
Confucius said: Is there such a saying?
Zhong Yuan, if a virtuous person can be trusted by others, how could Boyi and Shuqi starve to death in Shouyang Mountain?
If a wise man can go ahead without any hindrance, how can a prince dare to have his heart betrayed?
Zilu withdrew, and Zigong came in to see Confucius.
Confucius said to Zigong: Granted, the Book of Songs says it is neither a rhinoceros nor a tiger, yet it wanders in the wilderness.
Is there something wrong with our doctrine?
Why have we ended up in this situation? Zigong said: The teacher's teachings are so profound that no country in the world can accommodate him.
Teacher, why don't you lower your requirements a little bit?
Confucius said: Grant, although a good farmer is good at farming, he may not necessarily have a good harvest; although a good craftsman may not have exquisite craftsmanship, his work may not satisfy everyone.
Cultivated people can study their own theories, just like a net, first constructing the basic Datong system, and then relying on it, but it may not be accepted by the world.
Now, instead of studying your own doctrine, you want to lower yourself to respect others.
Shi, your ambition is too modest.
After Zigong went out, Yan Hui came in to see Confucius.
Confucius said: Hui, the Book of Songs says it is neither a rhinoceros nor a tiger, yet it wanders in the wilderness.
Is there something wrong with our preaching?
Why have we ended up in this situation?
Yan Hui said: The teacher's teachings are so profound that no country in the world can accommodate him.
Even so, teachers still have to promote their own theories. What does it matter if they are not accepted by the world? Don't be accepted, so that you can show your true character as a gentleman!
If a person does not study his own doctrine, it is his own shame.
As for the doctrines that have been studied with great efforts and are not used by others, it is a shame for those in power.
What does it matter if you are not accepted by the world? Don't be accepted, so that you can show your true character as a gentleman!
Confucius smiled happily and said, "That's it, young man named Yan!"
If you have a lot of money, I would like to be your steward.
So he sent Zigong to the state of Chu.
King Zhao of Chu mobilized his army to meet Confucius, and this disaster was avoided.
King Zhao of Chu wanted to grant Confucius a 700-mile land with household registration.
Zixi, the envoy of Chu State, stopped him and said: "Among the envoys sent by your Majesty to the various vassal states, are there people like Zigong?"
King Zhao said: No.
Zixi asked again: "Are there any of the king's assistant ministers like Yan Hui?" King Zhao said: No.
Zixi asked again: "Does your Majesty have any generals like Zilu?"
King Zhao replied: No.
Zixi also asked: Are there any officials in charge of the king's ministries like Zaiyu?
King Zhao replied: No.
Zixi continued: Moreover, when our ancestors of the Chu State were granted the title of Viscount by the Emperor of Zhou, the land was equal to that of Baron, with a radius of fifty miles.
Now Confucius talks about the regulations and laws of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and affirms that Zhou Gongdan and Zhaogongsi assist the cause of the Emperor of Zhou. If the king appoints him, will the Chu State still be able to retain thousands of miles of land from generation to generation?
I remember when King Wen was in Fengyi and King Wu was in Haojing. As the lord of a land of only a hundred miles, he finally became the king of the world.
Now if Confucius was allowed to own the land of 700 cities, coupled with the assistance of those talented disciples, this would not be the blessing of Chu State.
After hearing this, King Zhao gave up his original idea.
In the autumn of this year, King Chu Zhao died in Chengfu.
The madman Jie Yu from Chu State one day walked past Confucius's carriage singing a song and said: Phoenix, Phoenix, how come your virtue has deteriorated?
Things in the past cannot be undone, but things in the future can be caught up again. Forget it, forget it!
The people in power now are hopeless!
Confucius got out of the car and wanted to talk to him, but he walked away quickly and failed to talk to him.
So Confucius returned from Chu to Wei. This year, Confucius was sixty-three years old, which was the sixth year of Duke Ai of Lu.
The next year, Wu and Lu met at a place called Zhen to form an alliance. Wu asked Lu to provide Bailao as a sacrifice.
The Grand Prime Minister of the State of Wu summoned Ji Kangzi.
Ji Kangzi sent Zigong to negotiate, and then the matter was dropped.
Confucius said: The political situations of Lu and Wei are as similar as brothers.
At this time, Wei Chu's father, Kuai Chi, did not succeed to the throne and was in exile. The princes repeatedly criticized this matter.
Many of Confucius's disciples served as officials in Wei State, and Wei wanted to invite Confucius to govern whenever he went out for public service.
Zilu asked Confucius: The State of Wei wants to invite you to govern. What are you going to do first?
Confucius replied: Then I must rectify my name first!
Zilu said: Is there such a thing? Teacher, you are too ignorant!
Why do we need to correct our names first?
Confucius said: How reckless, Zhongtian!
You must know that if the status is not correct, the words spoken will not be appropriate; if the words are not spoken appropriately, then things will not be done; if things are not done, then ritual and music education will not flourish; if music and education will not flourish, then the punishment will not be accurate and appropriate, then the people will be at a loss and not know what to do.
Therefore, a gentleman must do things in accordance with his status, and what he says must be practical and feasible.
A gentleman should be strict and casual about what he says.
The next year, Ran Youwei led the army for the Ji family and fought against Qi in Langdi and defeated Qi's army.
Ji Kangzi said to Ran Qiu: Did you learn your military talents?
Or is it natural?
Ran You replied: I learned it from Confucius.
Ji Kangzi asked again: What kind of person was Confucius?
Ran You replied: "His appointment must be consistent with his title. Whether his teachings are spread among the people or confronted with ghosts and gods, there will be no regrets."
Although I had meritorious service in the military and was granted a total of 2,500 families, Confucius would not be tempted. Kangzi said: I want to summon him back, is that okay?
Ran You said: If you want to invite him back, as long as you don't let villains hinder him, that's all.
At that time, Kong Wenzi, the official of the Wei State, was preparing to attack Taishu and asked Confucius for advice.
Confucius refused and said he didn't know. When he returned to his residence, he immediately ordered his carriage to leave Weiguo, saying: Birds can choose trees to live in, but how can trees choose birds?
Kong Wenzi firmly detained him.
It happened that Ji Kangzi sent Gonghua, Gongbin, and Gonglin to greet Confucius with gifts, and Confucius returned to the state of Lu.
Confucius left the State of Lu for fourteen years and returned to the State of Lu.
Duke Ai of Lu asked Confucius about the principles of government. Confucius replied: The most important thing in government is to choose ministers.
Ji Kangzi also asked Confucius about the principles of government. Confucius said: Use upright people and discard people with evil intentions, so that people with evil intentions can become upright.
Ji Kangzi was worried about stealing. Confucius said: If you have no desire, people will not steal even if you give them rewards.
However, the State of Lu failed to appoint Confucius in the end, and Confucius did not ask to be an official.
In the time of Confucius, the king of Zhou was in decline, rituals and music were in ruins, and the "Poems" and "Books" were also in short supply.
Confucius studied the etiquette system of the Xia, Shang, and Western Zhou dynasties, and compiled the chapters of Shuzhuan, starting from the time of Yao and Shun of Tang Dynasty, to Duke Mu of Qin Dynasty, and arranged them according to the order of events.
Confucius said: I can still describe the etiquette system of the Xia Dynasty, but the Qi State, a descendant of the Xia Dynasty, did not leave enough documents to prove it.
I can also tell you about the etiquette system of the Yin and Shang Dynasties, but the post-Song Dynasty of the Yin and Shang Dynasties did not leave enough documents to prove these systems.
If there are enough documents from Qi and Song, I can prove these systems.
After examining the additions and deletions made by the Yin Dynasty to the Xia Dynasty in the etiquette system, Confucius said: Even after a hundred years in the future, the increases and decreases can be predicted, because one kind of emphasis is on literary talent, and the other is on simplicity.
The etiquette system of the Zhou Dynasty was formulated based on the Xia Dynasty and the Yin Dynasty. It is so rich and colorful. I advocate using the etiquette of the Zhou Dynasty. Therefore, "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites" were both compiled by Confucius.
Confucius once said to the music official Taishi of Lu: Music can be understood.
At the beginning of the performance, they should cooperate with each other, and continue to have a harmonious rhythm, clear and continuous sound, until the whole piece of music is completed.
Confucius also said: After I returned to Lu from Wei, I began to correct the poetry and music, restoring the original tunes of "Ya" and "Song".
There are more than 3,000 poems handed down from ancient times. At the time of Confucius, he deleted the repetitive ones and selected those that were consistent with the meaning for etiquette education. The earliest ones traced the ancestors of Yin, Qi, and the ancestors of Zhou, Houji. The second ones described the prosperity of the Yin and Zhou dynasties, until the political absence of King Zhou You and King Li of Zhou. The beginning was a poem describing the relationship and feelings between men and women, so it is said: The movement "Guan Sui" is the first chapter of "Guofeng", "Lu Ming" is the first chapter of "Xiao Ya", "King Wen" is the first chapter of "Daya", and "Qing Temple" is the first chapter of "Ode".
Confucius was able to play and sing the three hundred and five poems in order to match the tunes of the music "Shao", "Wu", "Ya" and "Song".
From then on, the music system of the former kings was restored to the old view and could be described. The king's way was complete, and Confucius also completed the compilation of "Poetry", "Book", "Yue", "Yi" and "Spring and Autumn" which are known as the "Six Arts". In his later years, Confucius liked to study "The Book of Changes". He explained in detail the "Yun Ci", "Xici", "Gua", "Classic Chinese", etc.
Confucius read the "Book of Changes" so diligently that he broke the cowhide rope that woven the slips through many times. He also said: If I live a few more years, I will be able to fully understand the diction and meaning of "The Book of Changes".
Confucius used "Poems", "Books", "Li" and "Music" as teaching materials to educate his disciples. There were about 3,000 disciples studying there, and 72 of them were proficient in the six skills of etiquette, music, archery, charioteering, arithmetic, and shu.
As for people like Yan Zhuozou, there are even more disciples who were taught by Confucius in many aspects but were not formally naturalized. Confucius educated his disciples in four aspects: knowledge, words and deeds, loyalty and forgiveness, and faith.
Set four prohibitions for disciples: don’t speculate, don’t be arbitrary, don’t be stubborn, and don’t be self-righteous.
Things that he believed should be handled with special caution were: fasting, war, and disease.
Confucius rarely talked about profit. If he did, it was associated with fate and benevolence.
When he educates his disciples, he does not enlighten or enlighten them until they encounter real difficulties, become bored or anxious. He came up with a truth, and his disciples could not deduce similar truth by analogy, so he would not repeat it again. In his hometown, Confucius was as humble as a man who was not good at talking.
On occasions such as offering sacrifices in the ancestral temple and discussing affairs in the court, he was eloquent, clear and accessible, yet very respectful and careful.
When you go to court, when you talk to the senior officials, your attitude is pleasant and upright; when you talk to the lower officials, you appear to be peaceful and peaceful.
When Confucius entered the king's palace, he bowed his head and bowed with respect and caution. After entering, he walked forward quickly and was respectful and courteous.
The king ordered him to greet the guests with a solemn and serious look.
The king summoned him and set off without waiting for the chariot to be ready.
Confucius would not eat the fish if it was not fresh, if the meat was off-flavored, or if it was not cut according to the rules.
If the seats were not straight, Confucius would not sit down.
I never feel full when I eat next to someone in mourning.
If you cry in a day, you will never sing again.
When seeing a person wearing mourning clothes or a blind person, even a child will change his face to show sympathy.
Confucius said: Among three people walking together, there must be someone who can be my teacher.
He also said: Not cultivating morality, not pursuing academic studies, not going to study after hearing upright principles, not being able to correct shortcomings and mistakes, these are the problems that worry me.
Confucius asked someone to sing. If the song was good, he would ask the person to sing it again, and then he would join in the singing.
Confucius did not talk about weird, violent, ghost-related things.
Zigong said: The literary knowledge of literature imparted to us by our teachers can be learned through listening.
The remarks that teachers teach us about the way of heaven and nature cannot be heard or understood.
Yan Yuan praised and said: The more you look up at the teacher's teachings, the more noble you feel; the more you study them, the more solid and profound they are.
Seeing it right in front, I suddenly ran to the back.
Teachers are good at inducing people in an organized and planned way, using literature and classics to enrich our knowledge, and using etiquette and norms to restrain our words and deeds. Even if we want to stop learning, we can't do it.
I have exhausted all my talents and seem to be able to be independent in society, but if I want to take another step forward, I don’t know how to start.
The people in Daxiang said: How great!
Confucius was learned but not famous for any particular expertise. Confucius heard this and said: What is my expertise?
Driving?
Archery?
I'm still good at driving.
Lao said: The teacher once said that I learned so many skills because I failed to get an appointment.
In the spring of the fourteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu, he went hunting in Daye.
The merchants who drove the Shusun family hunted a monster, which they thought was an ominous omen.
Confucius looked at it and said: This is Qilin.
So it was taken away.
Confucius said: If the divine dragon Negative Picture no longer appears on the Yellow River, and the divine turtle Negative Luoshu no longer appears on the Luo River, I will be almost finished!
When Yuan died, Confucius said: God wants me to die!
When he went west to hunt in the wilds and saw Qilin, he said: My idea has come to an end!
Said with emotion: No one can understand me!
Zigong said: Why do you say no one understands you?
Confucius replied: I don't complain about heaven, nor do I blame people. I study human affairs at a lower level and understand the laws of heaven at a higher level. The only one who can understand me is heaven!
Confucius said: If you don't lower your ambitions and don't let your personality be insulted, only Boyi and Shuqi Bing can do it!
He also said: Liu Xiahui and Shaolian lowered their ambitions and insulted their personalities.
It is also said that Yu Zhong and Yi Yi lived in seclusion, did not talk about worldly affairs, behaved in a noble and pure manner, and abandoned themselves in a contingency manner.
He also said: I am different from them. I neither lower my ambitions or humiliate myself in order to make progress, nor do I live in seclusion and escape from the world. There is no absolute can and no absolute can't. Confucius said: No, no!
The most worrying thing for a gentleman is that he will not leave a good reputation after his death. If my ideas cannot be implemented, what should I leave to future generations?
So he made the Spring and Autumn Annals based on the history books of the Lu State, starting from the first year of Lu Yin to the fourteenth year of Lu Aigong, and included a total of twelve monarchs of the Lu State.
The narrative is centered on the state of Lu, respects the royal family of Zhou as the orthodoxy, uses the ancient traditions of the Yin and Shang Dynasties as a reference, and extends the legal tradition of Xia, Shang and Zhou Dynasties. The writing is simple and the purpose is broad.
Therefore, the people of Wu and Chu who claimed to be kings were still derogated as viscounts in the Spring and Autumn Annals; Duke Wen of Jin actually summoned King Xiang of Zhou to join the alliance in Jiantu, but the Spring and Autumn Annals avoid saying that the Emperor of Zhou came to Heyang on a hunting tour.
By analogy, "Spring and Autumn" used this principle to praise and criticize various events at that time. Later, some kings praised and promoted it, so that the justice and law of "Spring and Autumn" prevailed in the world, and the rebellious officials and traitors in the world became afraid.
When Confucius was an official in reviewing cases, he would never act alone if he needed to consult with others on wording.
When he compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded what he thought should be recorded, and what he thought should be deleted was deleted. Even a disciple like Zixia who was good at writing could not change a single word.
When the disciples listened to Confucius teach "Spring and Autumn", Confucius said: If future generations want to understand me, Confucius, they need to rely on "Spring and Autumn", and if they want to blame me, Confucius, they must also rely on "Spring and Autumn".
In the second year, Zilu died in Weiguo.
Confucius was ill, and Zigong asked to see him.
Confucius was taking a leisurely walk with a cane in his mouth and said: Ci, why did you come so late?
Confucius sighed, and then sang: Mount Tai is about to fall!
The beams are about to break and the philosopher is about to die!
He shed tears as he sang.
He said to Zigong: The world has lost its normal way for a long time, and no one advocates my doctrine.
When a person from Xia died, his coffin was placed on the steps of the east chamber, when a person from Zhou died, his coffin was placed on the steps of the west chamber, and when a person from Yin died, his coffin was placed between the two pillars of the hall.
Last night I dreamed that I was sitting between two pillars and being worshiped. My ancestor was the Yin Shang Dynasty.
After that, Confucius died.
Confucius was seventy-three years old and died on Ji Chou day in April of the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu.
Duke Ai of Lu wrote a eulogy for him and said: God is not kind and refuses to keep this old man. He leaves me alone and I am lonely and hurt. ah!
How painful! Nifu, there is no one who can serve as a role model for me to learn from!
Zigong said, "Master of Lu, can't he stay in Lu forever?"
The teacher said: Loss of Dharma will lead to confusion, and loss of status will lead to faults.
If you lose your will, you will become confused; if you lose your ability, you will make mistakes.
You cannot use the teacher while he is alive, but it is not appropriate to mourn him after he is dead.
It is inappropriate to call him "Yu Yiren" as a prince.
After his death, Confucius was buried on the shore of Surabaya, north of Lucheng. His disciples mourned him in their hearts for three years.
After three years of mourning, when everyone said goodbye and left, they all cried to each other and mourned each other; some even stayed.
Only Zigong lived in a small room next to the tomb and guarded the tomb for a total of six years before leaving.
His disciples and others from the state of Lu led more than a hundred people who lived near the tomb. So this place was named Kongli.
It has been passed down from generation to generation in the State of Lu that they regularly visit Confucius's tomb every year to worship. Confucian scholars also come here at this time to learn etiquette, go to the countryside for academic examinations, have drinking ceremonies, and perform archery competitions and other ceremonies. Confucius's tomb is an area of ​​one hectare.
The main hall of Confucius's former residence and the inner rooms where his disciples lived were later converted into temples to store the clothes, hats, musical instruments, cars, books, etc. that Confucius wore during his lifetime. Until the Han Dynasty, it was not abandoned for more than 200 years.
Emperor Liu Bang of Gao Dynasty passed through the land of Lu and sacrificed Confucius with Tailao, which was equipped with cattle, sheep and pigs.
When princes, ministers, officials, and prime ministers arrive at their posts, they often visit the tomb of Confucius before taking office and handling government affairs.
Confucius gave birth to a carp, named Boyu.
Boyu died at the age of fifty, before Confucius.
Boyu gave birth to Ji, whose name was Zisi. Guo was sixty-two years old.
Once trapped in the Song Dynasty.
Zisi wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean".
Zisi gave birth to Bai, named Zishang, at the age of forty-seven.
Zishang gave birth to Qiu, named Zijia, at the age of forty-five.
Ji was born in Zi's family, named Zijing, and he died at the age of forty-six.
Zijing gave birth to Chuan Chuan, named Zi Gao, at the age of fifty-one.
Zigao gave birth to Shen, who died at the age of fifty-seven. He once served as the prime minister of Wei.
Zishen gave birth to Yu, and died at the age of fifty-seven. He was a doctor of King Sheng of Chen, and died in Chen.
Yu's younger brother is named Zixiang, who died at the age of fifty-seven.
He once served as a doctor for Emperor Xiaohui of the Han Dynasty and was later promoted to the prefect of Changsha County.
Height nine feet six inches.
Zixiang gave birth to Zhong, who died at the age of fifty-seven.
Zhong gave birth to Wu, and Wu gave birth to Yannian and Anguo.
Anguo became the doctor of the current Emperor Xiaowu and became the prefect of Linhuai County. He died young and short.
Anguo gave birth to Yan, and Yan gave birth to Huan.
Tai Shigong said: There is this saying in "Poetry": The lofty mountains attract people to look up to, and the broad roads attract people to follow.
Although I have not been able to catch up with Confucius's era, I yearn for him in my heart.
When I read Confucius's works, I can imagine what he was like as a person.
When I arrived in Lu, I visited Confucius's temples, vehicles, clothes, and ritual vessels, and witnessed the students going to Confucius' old residence on time to practice etiquette. I lingered with reverence and didn't want to leave.
Since ancient times, there have been many kings and wise men in the world. They were all noble and glorious when they were alive, but nothing was lost when they died.
Confucius was a commoner. His reputation and teachings had been passed down for more than ten years, and people who read still respected him as their master.
From the emperor and princes to people all over the country who talk about the six arts, Confucius's teachings are regarded as the highest criterion for judgment. It can be said that Confucius is the supreme sage.
summary:
Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State, to Shu Lianghe and a woman named Yan after they prayed at Niqiu Mountain. His head was concave at birth, so he was named Qiu, with the courtesy name Zhongni and surname Kong. His father died shortly after his birth and was buried in Fangshan, but his mother did not reveal the location. As a child, Confucius played at setting up sacrificial vessels and learning ritual movements. After his mother died, he temporarily placed her coffin at the Five Fathers' Road until a neighbor told him his father's burial place, allowing him to bury them together. At seventeen, Meng Lizi, a senior official, warned his son Yizi that Confucius, a descendant of saints, should be taken as a teacher. After Lizi's death, Yizi and Nangong Jingshu learned etiquette from Confucius.

Confucius' family was poor and of low status. He worked as a clerk managing the Ji family's warehouse and pastures, where he was fair and efficient, leading to his promotion to Sikong. He later left Lu, was ostracized in Qi, expelled in Song and Wei, besieged between Chen and Cai, and finally returned to Lu. At nine feet six inches tall, he was called "The Long Man." Nangong Jingshu requested Duke Zhao of Lu to allow Confucius to travel to Zhou to learn etiquette from Lao Tzu, who advised him to avoid speaking of others' faults and to act without selfish motives. After returning, Confucius gained many disciples.

At thirty, Confucius advised Duke Jing of Qi that Qin's success came from its ambitious governance and use of talents like Baili Xi. At thirty-five, after political turmoil in Lu, Confucius went to Qi, where he studied music and advised Duke Jing on governance, emphasizing proper roles and frugality. However, Yan Ying dissuaded the duke from employing Confucius, criticizing Confucian rituals as impractical. Confucius left Qi and returned to Lu.

At fifty, Confucius was appointed governor of Zhongdu, then promoted to Sikong and later to Grand Sikou. In the tenth year of Duke Ding of Lu, he organized a meeting at Jiagu between Lu and Qi, where he confronted Qi's disruptive performances and had performers executed. Qi returned invaded lands to Lu. In the thirteenth year, Confucius ordered the demolition of the city walls of Ji, Meng, and Shu families to curb their power, but the Meng family resisted, and the city of Cheng could not be captured.

At fifty-six, Confucius acted as chief minister, killing the official Shaozhengmao. Within three months, Lu's markets became honest, men and women walked separately, and lost items were not taken. Qi, fearing Lu's rise, sent eighty beautiful women and 120 horses to Lu. Ji Huanzi accepted them, neglecting state affairs. Confucius left Lu after the suburban sacrifice was mishandled, traveling to Wei, where he received a salary of 60,000 dou but left after slander. He was besieged in Kuang, mistaken for Yang Hu, but escaped. He returned to Wei, met Nanzi, and left after Duke Linggong's behavior disgusted him.

Confucius traveled to Song, where Sima Huan tried to kill him, then to Zheng, where he was described as a lost dog. In Chen, he identified arrows from the Sushen tribe. After three years, he left due to invasions. At Pu, he was detained but escaped after a covenant. He returned to Wei, but Duke Linggong did not use him. He considered going to Jin but turned back after learning of the deaths of two virtuous officials. He returned to Wei, then left for Chen after Duke Linggong ignored him.

At sixty, Confucius was in Chen. After Ji Huanzi's death, Ji Kangzi recalled Ran Qiu, and Confucius hoped to return. He moved to Cai, then to Ye, where he advised on governance. He met hermits Chang Ju and Jie Ni, who criticized his efforts. He was besieged between Chen and Cai, running out of food, but continued teaching. His disciples questioned their plight, but Confucius maintained his principles. King Zhao of Chu planned to grant him land, but Zixi dissuaded him, and the king died soon after. Confucius returned to Wei, then to Lu after fourteen years.

In Lu, Confucius was not appointed to office. He compiled the "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites," corrected poetry and music, and studied the "Book of Changes," wearing out the binding cords. He taught about 3,000 disciples, with 72 mastering the six arts. He educated in knowledge, conduct, loyalty, and faith, avoiding profit unless linked to fate and benevolence. He was humble in his hometown but eloquent in court. He avoided spoiled food and improper seating, and showed sympathy to mourners and the blind.

In his later years, Confucius compiled the "Spring and Autumn Annals" based on Lu's history, covering twelve rulers. He used subtle writing to praise and criticize, making rebellious officials fearful. He died at seventy-three in the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu. Duke Ai mourned him, but Zigong criticized the eulogy. Confucius was buried north of Lucheng. Disciples mourned for three years, with Zigong staying six years. His tomb became a site of annual worship, and his former residence was turned into a temple, preserved for over 200 years. Emperor Liu Bang of Han sacrificed to him. Confucius' descendants continued his lineage, including his son Boyu, who died before him, and grandson Zisi, who wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean." The historian concluded that Confucius, though a commoner, became the supreme sage, with his teachings enduring for generations.
