Shi Miming killed the dog with his bare hands for Zhao Dun.
Zhao Dun said: Abandoning people and using dogs, although they are ferocious, what's the use!
However, Zhao Dun didn't know that Shi Miming was secretly protecting him.
After a while, Duke Linggong commanded the ambushed soldiers to chase Zhao Dun, and signaled Miming to fight back against Duke Linggong's soldiers. The soldiers could not move forward, and Zhao Dun finally escaped.
Zhao Dun asked Shi Miming why he saved him, and Shi Miming said: I am the hungry man under the mulberry tree.
Zhao Dun asked for his name, but he did not tell him.
Shi Miming therefore hid away.
Zhao Dun escaped, but not beyond the borders of Jin.
On Yichou Day, Zhao Dun's younger brother, General Zhao Chuan, killed Duke Ling in Taoyuan and welcomed Zhao Dun back.
Zhao Dun has always been respected by others and is very popular among the people. Duke Ling was young and extravagant, and the people did not follow him, so he was easily killed.
Zhao Dun regained his previous status.
Dong Hu, the Taishi of Jin State, wrote: Zhao Dun killed his own king.

Xuanzi is an excellent doctor, and he is willing to bear a bad reputation in order to abide by the law. Unfortunately, if Zhao Dun escapes from the country, he will be exempted from the crime.

On the day of Renshen, Duke Cheng went to Wugong to pay homage to his ancestors.
In the first year of his reign, the Zhao family was granted the title of official of the public clan.

The state of Jin sent Zhongxing Huan to attack the state of Chen, so he rescued the state of Zheng, fought with the state of Chu, and defeated the Chu army.

In the spring of the first year of Jingdong, Xia Zhengshu, a senior official of the Chen State, killed his monarch Linggong.
In the second year, King Zhuang of Chu attacked the state of Chen and killed Zhengshu.
In the third year, King Zhuang of Chu besieged the state of Zheng, and the state of Zheng asked for help from the state of Jin.

The Chu State captured the Jin general Zhi Xiang.
After the Jin army returned to the state of Jin, Lin's father said: I am a general. If the Jin army failed, I should be killed. I asked for the death penalty.
Jin Jinggong wanted to agree to him.
He then said: In the past, Duke Wen fought with the state of Chu in Chengpu. When King Chu Cheng returned to the state of Chu, he killed the general Ziyu, which made Duke Wen happy.
Today, Chu State has defeated our army, and we have killed our own generals. This is helping Chu State to kill Chu State’s enemies.
Jin Jinggong gave up after hearing these words.
In the fourth year, Xiangu caused the Jin army to suffer a defeat on the bank of the Yellow River because of his first suggestion. He was afraid of being killed, so he fled to Zhai and discussed with Zhai State to attack the Jin State.

At that time, King Zhuang of Chu was very powerful, so he defeated the Jin army by the Yellow River.

Xie Yang pretended to promise and finally told Song Guo what Jin Jun said.
The state of Chu wanted to kill him, but someone watched and remonstrated, so the state of Chu released Xie Yang.
In the seventh year, the Jin sect Suihui destroyed Chidi.
In the eighth year, the state of Jin sent Choke as envoy to the state of Qi.

After Jin Jinggong asked about the reason for the attack, he said: If you have grievances, how can you disturb the country?

Wei Wenzi asked to resign due to old age and recommended Choke, who took charge of the country.

The Jin State attacked Qi State, and Qi State sent the prince to Jin State to be a hostage, so the Jin army stopped attacking.

Qinggong offered his treasures to seek peace, but Jin did not agree.
Choke said: We must get Xiao Tong's nephew as a hostage.

You are so unfaithful that you request another war.
As a result, Jin Cai agreed to make peace with Qi and left.
Duke Shen of Chu secretly married Xia Ji and fled to the state of Jin. The king of Jin worshiped the witch as the doctor of Xingyi.

The Jin State attacked the Zheng State and captured Si.
In the fourteenth year, a landslide occurred in Liangshan.
The king of Jin asked Bo Zong, who thought it was not worth making a fuss about.
In the sixteenth year, the general of Chu State resented Wu Chen and killed Wu Chen's entire family.
The wizard was very angry and wrote a letter to his son saying: You will definitely be exhausted all your life!
So Wu Chen asked to be sent as an envoy to the State of Wu, so that his son could be a traveler of the State of Wu and teach the soldiers of the State of Wu how to ride in a car and use the army.
Wu and Jin began to have contacts and agreed to attack Chu together.
In the seventeenth year, Jin Jinggong killed Zhao Tong and Zhao Kuo and destroyed their families.
Han Jue said: How can we forget the contributions of Zhao Shui and Zhao Dun?
How can we cut off their incense?
Therefore, Jin Jinggong made Zhao Wu, the concubine of the Zhao family, a descendant of the Zhao family and gave him the city.
In the summer of the 19th year, Jinggong was seriously ill and made Prince Shouman the king. This was Duke Li.
A month later, Jinggong passed away.
In the first year of Li Gong, because he had just ascended the throne, Li Gong wanted to make an alliance with the princes, so he made an alliance with Qin Huan Gong across the Yellow River.
After returning home, Qin broke the alliance and discussed with Zhai to attack Jin.
In the third year, the State of Jin sent Prime Minister Lu to condemn the State of Qin, and took the opportunity to attack the State of Qin with the princes.
The troops arrived at Jingshui, defeated the Qin army at Ma Tun, and captured the Qin general Cheng Cha.
In the fifth year, Que Qi, Que Ji, and Que Zhi slandered Bo Zong, and the king of Jin killed him.
Bo Zong caused this disaster because he liked to speak out and give advice, so the people no longer trusted Duke Li.
In the spring of the sixth year, the state of Zheng betrayed the state of Jin and formed an alliance with the state of Chu. Duke Li of Jin was furious.
Luan Shu said: We cannot lose the princes in our generation.
So Jin sent troops to attack Zheng.
Duke Li personally commanded the army and crossed the Yellow River in May.
When he heard that Chu troops were coming to rescue him, Fan Wenzi asked Duke Li to withdraw his troops.
Quezhi said: If you send an army to attack the rebels and avoid strong enemies, you will no longer be able to give orders to the princes.
As a result, the state of Jin went to war with the state of Chu.
On the day of Guisi, the Jin army shot the King of Chu in the eye, and the Chu army was defeated at Yanling.
Zifan gathered the remaining soldiers to appease the Chu army, and wanted to fight Jin again. Jin was very worried about this.
The King of Gong summoned Zifan, and Zifan's waiter Shu Yanggu proposed a toast to him. Zifan was drunk and could not go to see the King of Gong.
The king of the Communist Party was very angry and blamed Zifan, who was shot dead.
The king of the Communist Party then led his troops back to Chu.
As a result, the state of Jin became powerful and powerful among the princes. Duke Li of Jin wanted to take this opportunity to command the world and seek hegemony.
Duke Li had many concubines. After returning home, he wanted to remove all ministers from their posts and appoint the brothers of his concubines.
There was an elder brother named Xu Tong who was fond of a concubine, and he had a conflict with Que Zhi. In addition, Luan Shu resented Que Zhi for defeating the Chu army without using his own tactics, so he sent someone to secretly apologize to the Chu state.
The Chu State sent people to deceive Duke Li, saying: In fact, the Chu State was summoned to participate in the battle at Yanling, but they wanted to cause chaos and welcome Prince Zhou to the Jin State to ascend the throne.
It just so happened that the allies were not ready, so it didn't work out.
Duke Li told Luan Shu the quotation, and Luan Shu said: "This may be the case. Your Majesty, you might as well try sending him to the capital of Zhou and investigate secretly."
As expected, Duke Li sent Qi to Zhou Jing.
Luan Shu asked Prince Zhou to meet Quezhi again, but Quezhi didn't know that he had been betrayed.
Duke Li verified the matter and believed that Quezhi really wanted to rebel, so he hated Quezhi and wanted to kill him.
In the eighth year, Duke Li went hunting and drank with his concubine. However, he killed a pig and offered it to Duke Li. The eunuch took it away, but he shot the eunuch to death.
Duke Li was very angry and said: "Ji Zi has bullied me!"
He planned to kill San Que, but he didn't do it yet.
Que Qi wanted to strike first and attack Duke Li, saying: "Although I may die, the king will also suffer."
Quezhi said: If you are loyal, you cannot betray the monarch; if you pursue fame, you cannot harm the people; if you are brave, you cannot stir up trouble.
Who will help me if I lose these three virtues?
I'd better die.
On Renwu in the twelfth month, Duke Li asked Xu Tong to lead 800 soldiers to attack and kill Sanque.
Xu Tong took the opportunity to kidnap Luan Shu and Zhongxing Yan at the court, saying, "If you don't kill these two people, disaster will definitely fall on you, the king."
Duke Li said: "I killed three ministers in one morning. I can't bear to kill any more."
Xu Tong replied: But others will have the heart to kill you.
Duke Li refused to listen and apologized to Luan Shu, explaining that he was just punishing Que for his crimes: the officials were all reinstated.
The two kowtowed and said, "I'm so lucky, so lucky!"
Duke Li appointed Xu Tong as his minister.
On Yimao Day of the leap month, Duke Li went to Jiangli's house for a visit. Luan Shu and Zhongxing Yan sent their party members to attack and arrest Duke Li, imprison him, and kill Xu Tong. They also sent people to welcome Prince Zhou back from the capital of Zhou and made him king. This is Duke Ao of Jin.
In the first year of the mourning period, on Gengshen day of the first month, Luan Shu and Zhongxing Yan killed Duke Li and buried him with only a cart.
Duke Li died after being imprisoned for six days. Ten days after his death, on the Gengwu day, Zhixian welcomed the master Zhou to Jin. When he arrived at Jiang, Shaji and the officials formed an alliance to support the master Zhou. This was Duke Mourning.
On Xinsi day, I went to Wugong to worship.
On Yiyou day in the second month, Prince Zhou ascended the throne.
Mourning Duke Zhou's grandfather Jie was the son of Duke Xianggang of Jin. He failed to succeed to the throne and was known as Uncle Huan. Uncle Huan was the most beloved by Duke Xianggang.
Huan Shu gave birth to Hui Bo Tan, and Tan gave birth to mourning Gong Zhou.
Duke Zhou was only fourteen years old when he came to the throne.
Duke Mourning said: Both my grandfather and father failed to succeed to the throne and took refuge in Zhou Dynasty, where they died.
I thought I was alienated and never aspired to be the King of Jin.
Today, the officials have not forgotten the wishes of Wen Gong and Xianggong and supported me, a descendant of Uncle Huan. I rely entirely on the power of my ancestors and the ancestors to inherit the sacrifices of the Jin Dynasty. How dare I not work conscientiously!
I hope the doctors will help me well!
So he expelled the seven ministers who were disloyal to the king, repaired the old achievements, extended favors to the people, and supported the descendants of the heroes when Duke Wen returned to Jin.
In autumn, Jin attacked Zheng.
The Zheng army was defeated, and the Jin army invaded Chen again.
Three years later, Jin State met with the princes.
Duke Mou asked the ministers who could be appointed, and Qi Xi recommended Jie Hu.
Jie Hu is Qi Xi’s enemy.
The duke then asked who else there was, and Qi Xi recommended his son Qi Wu.
The gentleman said: Qi Xi can be regarded as impartial.
Don’t avoid your enemies when recommending people outside, and don’t avoid your sons when recommending people inside.
While meeting with the princes, the Duke's brother Yang Gan disrupted the military formation, and Wei Jiang killed his driver.
The duke was very angry, and some people advised him to remonstrate with him. The duke finally realized that Jiang was very virtuous, appointed him to take charge of government affairs, and sent him to make peace with Rong. Rong finally became very close to the state of Jin.
In the eleventh year, Duke Mourning said: Since I appointed Wei Jiang, I have met with the princes nine times and reconciled with Rong Zhai. This is all due to Wei Zi.
The emperor gave him a band, but he declined three times before accepting it.
In winter, Qin State captured the oak trees of Jin State.
In the fourteenth year, the Jin State sent Liu Qing to lead the princes to attack the Qin State, crossed the Jing River, and defeated the Qin army until they left at Chulin.
In the fifteenth year, Duke Mou asked Shi Kuang about the principles of governing the country.
Shi Kuang said: Only benevolence and righteousness are fundamental.
In the winter, Duke Du passed away and his son Ping Gongbiao came to the throne.
In the first year of Ping Dynasty, Jin State attacked Qi State, and Qi Linggong fought with Jin State in Mixia. The Qi army was defeated and fled.
Yan Ying said: Since the king has no courage to continue fighting, why not stop fighting?
Qi Jun then left.
The Jin State pursued Linyi in hot pursuit, surrounded Linyi, burned all the houses in the outer city, and killed all the people in the outer city.
The Jin army reached Jiaoshui in the east and Yishui in the south. The Qi army held on to the city, and the Jin army retreated.
In the sixth year, Duke Xiang of Lu went to pay homage to the king of Jin.
Luan of Jin committed a crime and fled to Qi.
In the eighth year, Duke Zhuang of Qi secretly sent Luan Zhao to Quwo and sent troops to follow him.
When the Qi army went to the Taihang Mountains, Luan Zhao rebelled from Quwo Nei and attacked Jiang.
Jiang was unsuspecting and Ping Gong wanted to commit suicide. Fan Xianzi stopped Ping Gong and sent his own soldiers to attack Luan Cheng. Luan Cheng was defeated and fled to Quwo.
The Quwo people attacked Luan Zhao, and Luan Zhao was killed. The Quwo people also eliminated Luan Zhao's clan party.
Luan Zheng's grandson Luan Shu.
When he entered Jiang, he discussed it with Wei.
When Duke Zhuang of Qi heard that Luan Zhao had failed, he returned, captured Chaoge of Jin, and left in order to avenge the battle of Linyi.
In the tenth year, Cui Shu of Qi State killed his king Zhuang Gong.
The Jin State took advantage of the turmoil in the Qi State, and Gaotang defeated the Qi army and left in order to avenge the Taihang Battle.
In the fourteenth year, Yanling Jizi of Wu State came to Jin State as an envoy. He talked with Zhao Wenzi, Han Xuanzi, and Wei Xianzi. Afterwards, he said: The political power of Jin State will finally fall into the hands of these three families.
In the 19th year, Qi State sent Yan Ying as envoy to Jin State, and Yan Ying talked with Shu Xiang.
Shuxiang said: Jin is now in the last days.
Ping Gong levied heavy taxes on the people and built ponds and pavilions but did not engage in political affairs. The power of the country has fallen into the hands of private individuals. Can the Jin Kingdom last long like this?
Yanzi agreed.
In the twenty-second year, the Jin State attacked the Yan State.
In the twenty-sixth year, Duke Ping died and his son Zhao Gongyi came to the throne.
Duke Zhao died in the sixth year.
The six ministers of Jin were strong, but the official family was weak.
His son Qing Gong died and came to the throne.
In the sixth year of Qinggong, King Zhou Jing passed away, and the princes competed for the throne.
The six ministers of Jin quelled the chaos in the Zhou royal family and supported King Jing.
In the ninth year, Lu Ji's family expelled their king Zhaogong, and Zhaogong was forced to live in Qianhou.
In the eleventh year, the states of Wei and Song sent envoys to request the state of Jin to send Lord Lu back home.
Ji Pingzi bribed Fan Xianzi privately. After Xianzi accepted the bribe, he said to Jin Jun: Ji is not guilty.
In the end, Jin did not send Lu Zhaogong back to his country.
In the twelfth year, the grandsons of Qi Xi, the Duke of Jin, and the sons of Shu Xiang, slandered each other in front of the king of Jin.
The Six Ministers wanted to weaken the monarch's power, so they killed everyone in the two families in accordance with the criminal law, divided their fiefdoms into ten counties, and each appointed his own son to be a doctor.
The power of the Duke of Jin became weaker, and the six ministers became stronger.
In the fourteenth year, Qinggong passed away and his son Dinggongwu came to the throne.
In the eleventh year of Dinggong's reign, Yang Hu of Lu State fled to Jin State, and Zhao Yang and Jianzi stayed with him.
In the twelfth year, Confucius became the prime minister of Lu.
In the fifteenth year, Zhao Yang made an agreement with Wu, the Handan doctor, to move Weigong's Wumian family to Jinyang. Handan's father and brother refused. Zhao Yang thought he was unfaithful and wanted to kill Wu. Wu, Zhongxingyin and Fan Jishe attacked Zhao Yang together, and Zhao Yang fled to Jinyang to defend.
Jin Dinggong surrounded Jinyang.
Xun Yue, Han Buxin, and Wei Chi had enemies with Fan Qushe and Zhongxing Yin, so they mobilized their troops to attack Fan Qushe and Zhongxing Yin.
Fan Qushe and Zhongxing Yin rebelled. The Jin army attacked them and defeated Fan Qushe and Zhongxing Yin.
Fan Qushe and Zhongxing Yin fled to Chaoge and defended the city.
Han Buxin and Wei Chi apologized to the king of Jin on Zhao Yang's behalf, so the king of Jin pardoned Zhao Yang and restored his position.
In the 22nd year, Jin defeated Fan Jishe and Zhonghangshi, and these two people fled to Qi.
Thirty years ago, Duke Dinggong and Fu Chai, the king of Wu, met in Huangchi and competed to be the leader. Zhao Yang was a trader at the time and finally made the king of Wu the leader.
In the thirty-first year, Tian Chang of the state of Qi killed his own king, Duke Jian, and appointed Duke Jian's younger brother Ao as Duke Ping.
In the thirty-third year of Jin Dinggong's reign, Confucius passed away.
In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Ding died, and his son Chu Gongzhi came to the throne.
In the seventeenth year of his absence, Zhibo, Zhao Yang, Han Buxin, and Wei Chi jointly incorporated the territories of Fan Jishe and Zhongxingyin into their own fiefs.
Chugong of Jin was furious and appealed to Qi and Lu, hoping to take the opportunity to attack the four ministers. The four ministers panicked and counterattacked Chugong.
He was forced to flee to Qi State and died on the way.
So Uncle Zhi made Duke Zhao's great-grandson Jiao the king of Jin, and this was Duke Ai.
Duke Ai's grandfather Yong was the youngest son of Duke Zhao of Jin, and his nickname was Dai Zi.
Dai Zi gave birth to Ji.
Ji had a close relationship with Zhibo, but he died early. Therefore, Zhibo wanted to annex the Jin Kingdom, but he did not dare to do so, so he made Ji's son Jiao the king of Jin.
At that time, all government affairs of the Jin State were decided by Zhibo, and Duke Ai of Jin could not control the government affairs.
Therefore, Zhibo took possession of Fan Jishe and Zhongxingyin's territory, becoming the most powerful among the six ministers.
In the fourth year of Duke Ai, Zhao Xiangzi, Han Kangzi, and Wei Huanzi jointly killed Zhibo and annexed all his lands.
In the eighteenth year, Duke Ai passed away and his son You Gong Liu came to the throne.
When Duke You was in power, the kings of Jin were afraid of the officials due to their weakness, and instead worshiped the kings of Han, Zhao and Wei.
The king of Jin only occupied Jiang and Quwo, and the rest were merged into the three Jins.
In the fifteenth year, Wei Wenhou ascended the throne.
In the eighteenth year, Duke You raped a woman and went out of the city at night, where he was killed by bandits.
Marquis Wen of Wei sent troops to quell the civil strife in Jin, and appointed Duke You's son Zhi, who was Duke Lie.
In the nineteenth year of Duke Lie, King Weilie of Zhou granted the states of Zhao, Han, and Wei the title of prince, and made them all princes.
In the twenty-seventh year, Lie Gong passed away, and his son Xiao Gongqi came to the throne.
In the ninth year of Duke Xiao's reign, Marquis Wu of Wei had just ascended the throne and attacked Handan. He failed to win and left.
In the seventeenth year, Duke Xiao passed away and his son, Duke Jing, came to the throne.
This year is the first year of King Qi Wei.
In the second year of Jinggong, Marquis Wu of Wei, Marquis Han Ai, and Marquis Zhao Jing destroyed the Jin Kingdom and divided the Jin land into three parts.
Jinggong became a commoner, and the state of Jin stopped offering sacrifices.
Tai Shigong said: Jin Wengong was a wise monarch in ancient times. He lived in exile for nineteen years and lived in extreme poverty. When he came to the throne, he gave rewards and forgot about Jie Zitui. What about those arrogant and extravagant monarchs?
After Duke Linggong was killed, Duke Cheng and Duke Jin were extremely strict, and Duke Li was even more harsh. The officials were afraid of execution, so troubles occurred frequently.
After the mourning of Duke Jin, the state of Jin became weaker and weaker day by day, and the six ministers took over the power exclusively.
Therefore, it is not easy for a king to control his subjects!
summary:
Tang Shuyu of Jin was the son of King Wu of Zhou and younger brother of King Cheng. His mother dreamed that God would give her a son named Yu who would receive the land of Tang. When born, the character "Yu" was found on his palm, so he was named Yu. After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded and destroyed the rebellious Tang state. While playing, King Cheng cut a tung tree leaf into a jade shape and gave it to Shuyu, saying he would enfeoff him. When asked to formalize this, King Cheng claimed he was joking, but Shi Yi insisted the emperor has no jokes. Thus, Tang was granted to Shuyu, who became known as Tang Shuyu.

The succession continued through generations: Xie became Marquis of Jin, followed by Marquis Wu, Marquis Cheng, Marquis Li, and Marquis Jing. From Tang Shuyu to Jinghou across five generations, reign lengths were unrecorded. In Jinghou's 17th year, King Li of Zhou fled due to popular unrest, and ministers governed during the "Republic" period. After Jinghou died, his son Lihou succeeded. The line continued through Xianhou, Muhou, and others. During Muhou's reign, his wife gave birth to a prince named Qiu (meaning hatred) and a younger son named Chengshi (meaning success). A Jin teacher warned these names would bring chaos.

After Muhou died, his brother Uncle Shang seized power, forcing Prince Qiu to flee. In the fourth year of Uncle Shang's reign, Prince Qiu attacked and established himself as Wenhou. In Wenhou's 10th year, King You of Zhou was killed, and the Zhou royal family moved eastward. Wenhou's son Zhaohou granted Quwo to his younger brother, who became Uncle Huan of Quwo. Quwo grew larger than the capital, and a gentleman predicted turmoil would originate there. In Zhaohou's seventh year, Pan's father killed Zhaohou and tried to install Uncle Huan, but Jin forces defeated him and established Zhaohou's son as Xiaohou.

The conflict between Quwo and Jin continued for generations. Quwo Zhuangbo killed Xiaohou, and later Quwo Wugong killed Aihou and Xiaozi. Finally, in the 28th year of Hou Min, Duke Wu of Quwo destroyed Jin, presented its treasures to King Li of Zhou, and was appointed ruler of Jin. Duke Wu had reigned 37 years in Quwo before becoming Duke Wu of Jin. He died two years after replacing the Jin ruler, and his son Xian Gong succeeded.

Duke Xian attacked Li Rong, obtained Li Ji and her sister, and favored them greatly. Li Ji gave birth to Xi Qi. Duke Xian planned to depose Crown Prince Shen Sheng, sending him to garrison Quwo while sending Chong'er and Yiwu elsewhere. Li Ji falsely accused Shen Sheng of poisoning food meant for Duke Xian. Unable to prove his innocence, Shen Sheng committed suicide. Chong'er and Yiwu fled in fear. Duke Xian sent troops against them, and Chong'er escaped to Di while Yiwu fled to Liang.

After Duke Xian died, Li Ke killed Xi Qi and his brother, then invited Chong'er to return, but he refused. Yiwu was brought back with Qin's help and became Duke Hui. He broke promises to grant land to Qin and reward Li Ke, instead forcing Li Ke to commit suicide. When Qin suffered famine, Jin refused aid and attacked Qin instead. Duke Hui was captured at the Battle of Han Yuan but later released. After Duke Hui died, his son Duke Huai succeeded but was killed by Qin forces escorting Chong'er back.

Chong'er, Duke Wen, had fled for 19 years, traveling through Di, Qi, Cao, Song, Zheng, Chu, and finally Qin. He returned at age 62 and was welcomed by most Jin people. After securing his position, he rewarded followers but initially forgot Jie Zitui, who hid in Mianshang Mountain and died there. Duke Wen later granted the mountain to Jie Zitui's memory. Duke Wen became hegemon after assisting King Xiang of Zhou and defeating Chu at Chengpu. After his death, his son Duke Xiang succeeded.

The text continues through many generations of Jin rulers, including Duke Ling (who was killed for his tyranny), Duke Cheng, Duke Jing, Duke Li, and Duke Mourning. The power of the six ministerial families grew while the ducal house weakened. Eventually, Zhao, Han, and Wei divided Jin among themselves. In the second year of Duke Jing, these three families destroyed Jin, reduced the duke to commoner status, and ended the state's sacrifices.

Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County.
During the Qin Dynasty, Cao Shen served as the warden of Peixian County, and Xiao He was the chief official. They were already well-known officials in the county.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was the Duke of Pei, Cao Shen followed him as Zhongjuan.
Cao Shen led his army to attack Huling and Fangyu, and attacked the Qin Dynasty's county supervisors' army, greatly defeating the enemy.
He took Xuexian County to the east and attacked the army of the Sishui County Governor to the west of the outer city of Xuexian County.
Then he attacked Huling and successfully captured it.
Cao Shen led his army to move to guard Fang Yu.
Fang Yu had rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, so Cao Shen attacked Fang Yu.
Fengyi also rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, and Cao Shen went to attack Fengyi again.
Duke Pei bestowed upon Cao Shen the title of Seventh Doctor.
Cao Shen attacked Qin Dynasty Sima Yí's army east of Dang County, defeated him, and captured Shanzhiyi in Dang County, Hufu County, and Qi County.
Cao Shen then attacked the area west of Xiayi, as far as Yu County, and attacked Zhang Han's army.
When attacking Yuan Qi and Kang Fu, Cao Shen was the first to climb the tower.
Cao Shen was promoted to the fifth official position.
He went north to rescue Dong'a, attacked Zhang Han's army, captured Chen County, and pursued to Puyang.
He attacked Dingtao and captured Linji.
He went south to rescue Yongqiu, attacked Li You's army, defeated it, killed Li You, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's military commanders.
At this time, Qin general Zhang Han defeated Xiang Liang's army and killed Xiang Liang. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu led their troops back east.
King Chu Huai appointed Pei Gong as the governor of Dang County and commanded the army of Dang County.
Peigong granted Cao Shen the title of Silk Holder and was known as Jiancheng Lord.
Later, Cao Shen was promoted to the magistrate of Yuanqi County and was subordinate to Dang County.
From there, Cao Shen followed Pei Gong to attack the army of the prefect of Dongjun and defeated the enemy south of Chengwu.
They attacked Wang Li's army in the south of Chengyang and fought Wang Li's army in Gangli, defeating them severely.
Chasing the fleeing enemy troops, he went west to Kaifeng, attacked Zhao Bi's army, defeated it, and surrounded Zhao Bi in the city of Kaifeng.
Going west, he encountered the Qin Dynasty general Yang Xiong's army in Qu, defeated it, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's Sima and Yushi.
Cao Shen was promoted to Zhigui and followed Pei Gong to attack Yangwu, captured the Yuan and Feng clans, blocked the Yellow River ferry, returned to attack Zhao Ben's army, and defeated it to the north of Xixiang.
Following Pei Gong, he went south to attack Jiyi, and fought with Lu Xun, the governor of Nanyang County, east of the outer city of Yangcheng. He broke through Lu Xun's army, captured Wan County, captured Lu Xun, and completely pacified Nanyang County.
Following Pei Gong, he went west to attack Wuguan and Yaoguan, and captured these two passes.
He first attacked the Qin army in the south of Lantian, and then attacked the north of Lantian at night, defeating the Qin army. Then he reached Xianyang and destroyed the Qin Dynasty.
After Xiang Yu came to Guanzhong, he named Liu Bang King of Han.
The king of Han granted Cao Shen the title of Marquis of Jiancheng.
Cao Shen followed the King of Han to Guanzhong and was promoted to general.
He then followed the King of Han and returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties. He initially attacked Xiabian, Gudao, Yongxian and Xixian.
They attacked Zhang Ping's army from the south of Haotian, defeated Zhang Ping, surrounded Haodian, and captured Rangxiang.
The troops of Sanqin attacked in the east of Rangxiang and Gaoqiu and defeated them all.
They surrounded Zhang Ping again, and Zhang Ping broke out and escaped from the enemy's camp.
So he attacked the troops of Zhao Bi and Nei Shibao and defeated them.
He captured Xianyang from the east and renamed Xianyang Xincheng.
Cao Shen led his troops to guard Jingling for twenty days. Sanqin sent Zhang Ping and others to attack Cao Shen. Cao Shen sent troops to meet him and defeated the enemy.
The king of Han gave Ning Qin to Cao Shen as a food town.
As a general, Cao Shen led the troops to surround Zhang Han in Feiqiu, and as a lieutenant, he followed the King of Han to Jin Pass.
When they arrived in Hanoi, they captured Xiuwu, crossed the Yellow River from Weijin, and marched eastward to attack Long Qie and Xiang's army at Dingtao and defeated them.
Heading east, they captured Dangxian, Xiaoxian and Pengcheng.
Attacking Xiang Ji's army, the Han army was defeated and fled.
Cao Shen surrounded and captured Yongqiu as a lieutenant.
Han general Wang Wu rebelled in Waihuang and Cheng Chu rebelled in Yan County. Cao Shen led his army to attack and defeated them both.

Attacked Yuying in Kunyang and pursued to Yeyi.
回军攻打武强，随即又打到荥阳。

Cao Shen served as a general and lieutenant from Hanzhong, following the king of Han to sweep away the princes, until Xiang Yu was defeated and returned to Xingyang, a total of two years.
In the second year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Cao Shen was appointed to act as Prime Minister Zuo and led troops to garrison in Guanzhong.
More than a month later, King Bao of Wei rebelled. Cao Shen, acting as the acting prime minister of Zuo, and Han Xin led their troops eastward to attack Wei General Sun Jun's army in Dongzhang, and defeated Sun Jun's army.
Cao Shen took advantage of the situation to attack Anyi and captured Wei general Wang Xiang alive.
Attacked the King of Wei in Quyang, chased him to Wuyuan, and captured King Bao of Wei alive.
They captured Pingyang, captured the king's mother, wife, and children alive, and captured the entire land of Wei, gaining a total of fifty-two cities.
The king of Han gave Pingyang to Cao Shen as a food town.
Cao Shen later followed Han Xin to attack the army of Zhao Guoxiang Guo Xia Shuo in the east of Wu County, defeated Xia Shuo's army and beheaded Xia Shuo.
Han Xin and Zhang Er, the former king of Changshan, led their troops to Jingxing and attacked Chen Yu, the king of Anjun. At the same time, they ordered Cao Shen to return to the army and besiege Zhao's general Qi in Wu County.
General Qi broke through and fled, but Cao Shen pursued and killed him.
So Cao Shen led his troops to the camp of King Han in Aocang.
By this time, Han Xin had defeated the State of Zhao, became prime minister, and attacked Qi State in the east.
Cao Shen, serving as Prime Minister Zuo, subordinated to Han Xin, defeated Qi Lixia's army and captured Linyi.
The returning army pacified Jibei County and attacked the counties, Luoyin, Pingyuan, Li County and Lu County.
Soon after, Han Xin followed Han Xin to attack Long Qie's army, defeated the enemy, killed Long Qie, and captured his general Zhou Lan.
The state of Qi was pacified and more than seventy counties were obtained in total.
They captured the Prime Minister Tian Guang of the former Qi King Tian Guang, Xu Zhang who stayed behind in place of the Prime Minister, and the former Qi State Jiaodong General Tian Ji.
Han Xin became the king of Qi, led his troops to Chen County, joined the king of Han, and defeated Xiang Yu together, while Cao Shen stayed to pacify the unconquered areas of Qi.
Xiang Yu was dead, the world was at peace, the King of Han became emperor, Han Xin was renamed King of Chu, and the state of Qi was divided into counties.
Cao Shen returned the seal of the Han Prime Minister.
Emperor Gao made his eldest son Liu Fei the King of Qi and appointed Cao Shen as the Prime Minister of Qi.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the titles of the princes were enfeoffed. The imperial court and the princes cut the talismans as proof, so that the titles of the enfeoffed persons could be passed down from generation to generation without being extinguished.
Emperor Gaozu granted Cao Shen 10,630 households in Pingyang as a fiefdom, with the title Marquis of Pingyang, and took back the fiefdoms previously entrusted to Cao Shen.
As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen led troops to attack Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun's army and defeated the enemy.
Yingbu rebelled. As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen followed Qi Hui King Liu Fei and led 120,000 troops. Together with Gaozu, he attacked Yingbu's army and defeated the enemy.
They marched southward to Qi County, then returned to the army and pacified Zhuyi, Xiangxian, Xiaoxian and Liuxian.
Cao Shen's achievements: he conquered two vassal states and 122 counties in total; captured two vassal kings, three prime ministers of the vassal states, six generals, and one each of the county guard, Sima, military marquis, and censor.
In the first year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, he abolished the decree of establishing a prime minister's state in the vassal states and appointed Cao Shen as the prime minister of Qi.
When Cao Shen was the prime minister of Qi, there were seventy cities in Qi.
At that time, the world had just been peaceful, and King Huihui was very young. Cao Shen summoned the elderly and scholars to ask for ways to appease the people. But there were hundreds of scholars in Qi State, and they had different opinions. Cao Shen didn't know how to make a decision.
He heard that there was a Duke Gai in Jiaoxi who studied Huang Lao's theory intensively, so he sent someone to invite him with generous gifts.
After meeting Gai Gong, Gai Gong told Cao Shen that the most important way to govern the country is to be pure and inactive, allowing the people to settle down on their own. He recommended similar things in this regard and stated them all to Cao Shen.
Cao Shen then gave up his main hall and let Gai Gong live in it.
From then on, Cao Shen's method of governing the country was to adopt Huang Lao's teachings, so he served as the prime minister of Qi for nine years. The country of Qi was stable, and people greatly praised him as a wise prime minister.
In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Xiao He passed away.
When Cao Shen heard the news, he told his disciples to pack their bags quickly and said: I am going to the court to become the prime minister.
Soon after, people sent by the imperial court came to summon Cao Shen.
When Cao Shen left, he told the subsequent prime minister of Qi: The prison lawsuits and markets of Qi should be regarded as the sustenance of certain people's actions. These actions should be treated with caution and not interfere easily.
The later prime minister said: Is there nothing more important than governing the country? Cao Shen said: That's not the case.
Prison litigation and the market are both good and evil. If you interfere strictly, where will the bad people stay?
That's why I'm telling you this.
When Cao Shen was humble at first, he had a good relationship with Xiao He; but when they became generals and prime ministers, there was a gap.
When Xiao He was dying, the only good minister Xiao He recommended to Emperor Xiaohui Liu Ying was Cao Shen.
Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as the prime minister of the Han Dynasty. He did not change anything and followed the laws established by Xiao He.
Cao Shen selected elders from various counties and vassal states who were not good at speaking and acted steadily. After finding them, he immediately summoned subordinate officials who were appointed as prime ministers.
Those among the officials who are demanding about the details of their speech and writing and who want to blindly pursue reputation will be repelled and driven away.
Cao Shen himself drank wine all day long.
The officials and guests below the rank of Qing and Dafu saw that Cao Shen was not paying attention to political affairs, and everyone who came to the door wanted to give him some advice.
But as soon as these people arrived, Cao Shen immediately gave them wine to drink. After a while, some people wanted to say something, and Cao Shen let them drink again. Until they got drunk and left, they were never able to speak out to persuade them. This was customary.
The back garden of the Prime Minister's residence is close to the officials' houses. In the officials' houses, people drink, sing, and shout all day long.
Cao Shen's officials were disgusted by this incident, but they had nothing to do about it, so they invited Cao Shen to play in the back garden. Together they heard the drunken officials singing and shouting wildly. The officials hoped that the Prime Minister would summon them to stop them.
Instead, Cao Shen asked people to get wine, set up a table, and drank heavily. He also sang and shouted in harmony with the officials.
When Cao Cao saw other people's minor faults, he always concealed them, so everything was safe in the prime minister's house.
Cao Shen's son Cao Chang became a doctor.
Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty complained that Cao Xiangguo ignored political affairs, and felt that the prime minister looked down on him, so he said to Cao Cheng: After you go home, try to ask your father privately: Emperor Gao has just passed away, and the emperor is very young. As the prime minister, you drink and have fun all day long, and do not ask the emperor for instructions when something happens. How do you manage the affairs of the country?
But don’t say I told you these words.
Cao Cheng went home during the holidays and stayed with his father in his spare time, translating Emperor Hui's wishes into his own words to persuade Cao Shen.
After hearing this, Cao Shen was furious and slapped Cao Chang two hundred times and said, "Hurry up and enter the palace to serve the emperor. It is not your place to talk about important national affairs."
When he went to court, Emperor Hui scolded Cao Shen and said: Why punish Cao Cheng?
I asked him to advise you last time.
Cao Shen took off his hat and apologized and said: Your Majesty, please think carefully for yourself, who is more saintly and heroic compared with you or Emperor Gao?
Emperor Hui said: How dare I compare with the late Emperor!
Cao Shen said: Your Majesty, do you think my talents are better than those of Xiao He? Emperor Hui said: You are probably not as good as Xiao He.
Cao Shen said: What your Majesty said is correct.
Emperor Gao and Xiao He have brought peace to the world, and the laws have been made clear. Now His Majesty has lowered his clothes and handed over his hands. Isn't it enough for us to abide by our respective responsibilities, follow the original laws and not change them at will? Emperor Hui said: OK.
Take a rest!
Cao Shen served as the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty for three years.
After his death, he was posthumously named Yihou.
Cao Shen's son, Cao Cheng, succeeded his father as the marquis.
The common people praised Cao Shen's deeds and said: Xiao He formulated laws that were clear and consistent; Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as prime minister and abided by Xiao He's laws without changing them.
Cao Shen implemented his pure and inactive approach, and the people were peaceful and undisturbed.
Cao Cheng, Marquis of Pingyang, was the imperial censor at that time.
Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne and was dismissed as a marquis.
Cao Cheng died after 29 years as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Jinghou.
Cao Cheng's son Cao Qi took over the throne and died after seven years of service. His posthumous title was Marquis Jian.
Cao Qi's son Cao Shi succeeded him.
Cao Shi married Princess Pingyang and gave birth to a son, Cao Xiang.
Cao Shi got sick and returned to the feudal country.
Cao Shi died in his 23rd year as a Marquis, and his posthumous title was Yihou.
Cao Shi's son Cao Xiang succeeded him.
Cao Xiang married Princess Wei Chang and had a son, Cao Zong.
Cao Xiang died in his sixteenth year as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Gonghou.
Cao Xiang's son Cao Zong succeeded him.
In the second year of Zhenghe, Cao Zong was implicated in the mutiny launched by Emperor Wu's crown prince. He was convicted and executed, and the feudal state was abolished.
Tai Shigong said: The reason why Cao Shen, the Prime Minister of Cao, has so many military exploits is because he worked with Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin.
When Han Xin was eliminated, only Cao Shen was credited with the military exploits accomplished by other princes.
As the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, Cao Shen strongly advocated purity and inaction, which was completely in line with Taoist doctrine.
After the people suffered from the cruel rule of the Qin Dynasty, Cao Shen gave them a chance to recuperate, so everyone in the world praised his virtue.
summary:
Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County and served as a warden there during the Qin Dynasty. He followed Emperor Gaozu of Han (then Duke of Pei) as a Zhongjuan, leading military campaigns against Qin forces, including attacks on Huling, Fangyu, Xuexian, and Dang County. He defeated generals such as Zhang Han, Li You, and Wang Li, capturing cities and officials. After Xiang Yu named Liu Bang King of Han, Cao Shen was granted the title Marquis of Jiancheng and later promoted to general. He helped pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, capturing territories like Xiabian and Yongxian, and besieged Zhang Han in Feiqiu.

Cao Shen served as acting Prime Minister Zuo, suppressing rebellions by King Bao of Wei and others, capturing Wei and Zhao territories. He followed Han Xin to defeat Qi, pacifying over seventy counties. After Xiang Yu's death, Cao Shen became Prime Minister of Qi under King Liu Fei, governing with Huang Lao principles of purity and inaction for nine years, stabilizing the state. When Xiao He died, Cao Shen succeeded him as Han Prime Minister, adhering strictly to Xiao He's laws without changes. He selected steady officials, dismissed those seeking reputation, and spent his time drinking, avoiding interference in minor affairs. When Emperor Hui questioned his governance, Cao Shen argued that following the established laws of Emperor Gaozu and Xiao He was sufficient.

Cao Shen served as Prime Minister for three years, dying with the posthumous title Yihou. His descendants inherited the title until Cao Zong was executed for involvement in a mutiny, ending the feudal state. The people praised Cao Shen for maintaining Xiao He's clear laws and allowing peace through non-interference.

translation:
Liang Xiaowang Liu Wu was the son of Emperor Xiaowen and his half-brother to Emperor Xiaojing.
His mother is Queen Mother Dou.
Emperor Xiaowen had four sons: the eldest son was the prince, who was Emperor Xiaojing; the second son was named Wu; the third son was named Ginseng; and the fourth son was named Mingsheng.
In the second year after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he named Liu Wu the acting king, Liu Shen the king of Taiyuan, and Liu Sheng the king of Liang.
Two years later, Emperor Wen changed the title of King Dai to King of Huaiyang.
All the fiefdoms of Dai State were assigned to King Taiyuan, and he was named King of Dai.
Liu Shen reigned for seventeen years and died in the second year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign. His posthumous title was King Xiao.
Liu Deng, the son of King Xiao, succeeded to the throne and became King Dai Gong.
King Dai Gong reigned for twenty-nine years and died in the second year of Emperor Wu Yuanguang's reign.
Liu Yi, the son of King Gong, succeeded to the throne and is the current acting king.
Nineteen years later, the Han Dynasty expanded the pass, with Changshan as the boundary, and moved King Dai to King Qinghe.
The relocation took place in the third year of Emperor Wu Yuanding's reign.
Initially, in the tenth year when Liu Wu was granted the title of King of Huaiyang, King Liu Sheng of Liang passed away, and his posthumous title was King Huai of Liang.
King Huai was the youngest son of Emperor Xiaowen and was favored more than the other sons.
The next year, Emperor Wen changed the title of King Liu Wu of Huaiyang to King of Liang.
Liu Wu was first granted the title of Prince of Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign.
It took eleven years from the time when King Liang was first named King of Dai to when he was changed to King of Liang.
In the fourteenth year of King Liang's reign, he entered the dynasty.
In the seventeenth and eighteenth years, he entered the court for two consecutive years and stayed in the capital. He did not return to his feudal country until the second year.
In the twenty-first year, he entered the court again.
In the twenty-second year, Emperor Xiaowen died.
He entered the DPRK in the twenty-fourth year and entered the DPRK again in the twenty-fifth year.
At that time, Emperor Jing had not yet established a prince.
When the Emperor was having a banquet with the King of Liang, he once said in a casual conversation: After thousands of years, I will pass on you, the King of Liang.
After hearing this, King Liang quickly declined.
Although he knew that what Emperor Jing said was not true, he was secretly happy.
The Queen Mother was equally happy.
That spring, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled.
Wu and Chu first attacked Liang's Jibi and killed tens of thousands of people.
King Xiao of Liang guarded Suiyang City and appointed Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as generals to resist the troops of Wu and Chu.
Wu and Chu were blocked by Liang and did not dare to cross the Liang Kingdom to march westward. They had a stalemate with Taiwei Yafu and others for three months.
Wu and Chu were destroyed, and the number of Wu and Chu troops killed and captured by Liang was roughly as many as the imperial court. The following year, the imperial court established a prince.
Later, because the King of Liang was the emperor's brother and had made great achievements, he was granted the title of a great country and occupied the fertile land in the world.
Its fiefdom is bounded by Mount Tai in the north and reaches Gaoyang in the west. There are more than 40 cities in total, most of which are large counties.
King Xiao of Liang was the youngest son of Empress Dowager Dou. He was very favored and received countless rewards.
Therefore, King Xiao of Liang built Dongyuan with a radius of more than 300 miles and expanded Suiyang City to 70 miles.
A great deal of construction work was carried out, palaces were built, and overhead passages were built, which were more than thirty miles long from the palace to the platform.
There are banners awarded by the emperor, and thousands of people are accompanying them when they go out.
Horses are galloping and hunting everywhere, and the splendor of the scene is like that of an emperor.
When entering and exiting the palace, pedestrians are prohibited from clearing the road, and people are warned and warned.
The heroes from all over the country and the lobbyists from the east of Mount Laoshan, such as Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and others from Qi, all returned to Liang.
Gongsun Guiduo had many strange and bizarre plans. When he first visited the King of Liang, the King of Liang gave him a thousand pieces of gold and an official position of lieutenant. The Liang State called him General Gongsun. The Liang Kingdom forged many weapons, including hundreds of thousands of bows, arrows, and spears. The treasury had nearly one trillion yuan in money, and there were even more pearls, jade, and treasures in the capital.
In October of the 29th year, King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing to meet Emperor Jing.
Emperor Jing sent an envoy to hold the talisman and drive the emperor's horse-drawn carriage to the pass to greet King Liang.
After meeting Emperor Jing, he submitted a memorial requesting to stay in the capital, and was allowed to do so because the Queen Mother loved Prince Xiao very much.
When King Xiao entered the palace, he accompanied Emperor Jing on a chariot. When he left the palace, he went hunting with the chariot and went to Shanglin Garden to shoot birds and beasts.
Liang Guo's ministers, Langguan, and visitors only need to register their names in the name book so that they can enter and leave the emperor's palace, no different from the officials of the imperial court.
In November, the emperor deposed Prince Li, and Empress Dowager Dou wanted to make Prince Xiao his successor.
The ministers, Yuan An and others dissuaded Emperor Jing, and Empress Dowager Dou's motion was blocked. From then on, she no longer mentioned the matter of making Prince Liang his successor.
Because this matter is very secret, no one in the world knows about it.
The King of Liang then bid farewell to the court and returned to the feudal state.
In April of this summer, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince.
The King of Liang resented Yuan An and the ministers who participated in the heir discussion, so he planned with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others to secretly assassinate Yuan An and more than ten other ministers who participated in the heir discussion.
The court searched for the murderer, but failed to find it.
So the emperor suspected King Liang and captured the murderer, who was indeed the mastermind.
So Emperor Jing sent envoys constantly on the road to Liang State, where they repeatedly conducted inspections and arrested Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hiding in the harem of King Liang.
The envoy was urgent to question the officials of Erqianshi. Liang Xiangxuan Qiu Bao and Nei Shi Han Anguo came to admonish the king of Liang. The king of Liang ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to commit suicide, and then handed them over.
The emperor resented King Liang for this.
The King of Liang was frightened, so he sent Han Anguo to confess to the Queen Mother through the eldest princess and ask for forgiveness, and then he was forgiven.
The emperor's anger gradually dissipated, and King Liang wrote a letter requesting an audience.
After arriving at Hangu Pass, Mao Lan persuaded King Liang to take a cloth chariot and bring only two cavalry to the capital, hiding in the eldest princess's garden.
The imperial court sent envoys to welcome King Liang, but King Liang had already entered the pass. All his entourage, chariots and horses were outside the pass, and he did not know where he was.
The Queen Mother cried: Your Majesty killed my son!
Emperor Jing was worried about this.
So the King of Liang, carrying the instrument of torture on his back, prostrated himself before the palace gate, confessed his crime and asked for punishment. The Queen Mother and Emperor Jing were very happy, and wept relative to each other. The brotherhood was as good as before.
Then the officials accompanying King Liang were summoned into the pass.
However, Emperor Jing gradually alienated King Liang and no longer rode with him in chariots.
In the winter of the thirty-fifth year, King Liang went to Beijing again to see the emperor.
He submitted a memorial requesting to retain the capital, but the emperor did not agree.
After King Liang returned to his feudal state, he felt confused and depressed.
When he went hunting in the Liangshan Mountains in the north, someone offered him a cow. The cow's feet were long on his back. King Xiao was disgusted by it.
In mid-June, King Liang fell ill with fever and died six days later. His posthumous title is King Xiao.
King Xiao of Liang was very filial. Every time he heard that the Queen Mother was ill and couldn't eat or sleep well, he often wanted to stay in Chang'an to serve the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother also loved him.
When she learned that King Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou cried very sadly and refused to eat or drink, saying: Your Majesty really killed my son!
Emperor Jing was sad and worried about it, and didn't know what to do.
Emperor Jing discussed with the eldest princess and divided the Liang Kingdom into five kingdoms. All five sons of King Xiao were granted the title of king, and all five daughters were also granted the title of Tang Muyi to them.
After reporting these measures to the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother became happy and added an extra meal because of Emperor Jing's treatment.
The eldest son of King Liang Xiao, Liu Mai, inherited the throne and was named the King of Gong; the second son, Liu Ming, was named the King of Jichuan; the third son, Liu Pengli, was named the King of Jidong; the fourth son, Liu Ding, was named the King of Shanyang; and the youngest son, Liu Bushi, was named the King of Jiyin.
Before the death of King Xiao of Liang, his property amounted to hundreds of millions and was incalculable.
After his death, there were still more than 400,000 kilograms of gold left in his treasury, and other properties were also equivalent to this.
In the third year of Liang Gong's reign, Emperor Jing died.
King Gong died after reigning for seven years and was succeeded by his son Liu Xiang, who became King Ping.
In the fourteenth year of Liang Ping King Liu Xiang's reign, Liang Ping King's mother was the Queen Mother Chen.
The mother of King Gong is Queen Mother Li.
Queen Mother Li is the biological grandmother of Prince Ping.
King Ping's queen's surname was Ren, and she was called Queen Ren.
Queen Ren was very favored by King Ping Liu Xiang.
At first, when King Xiao was still alive, he had a bottle worth thousands of gold.
King Xiao warned his descendants to take good care of the bottle and not give it to others.
After Queen Ren heard about it, she wanted to get the bottle.
The Queen Mother Li, the grandmother of King Ping, said: The late king had a will not to give away the bottles to others.
Even if other things are worth hundreds of millions, you can take them for yourself.
Queen Ren insisted on getting this bottle.
King Ping Liu Xiang directly asked people to open the treasury to get the bottles and gave them to Queen Ren.
Empress Dowager Li was furious. The imperial envoy came to the Liang Kingdom. Empress Dowager Li wanted to tell the envoy personally about the matter. King Ping Liu Xiang and Queen Ren stopped her and closed the door. Empress Dowager Li struggled to open the door, and her fingers were caught in the crack of the door. Finally, she could not see the envoy from the imperial court.
Empress Dowager Li secretly committed adultery with the Chief Food Officer and the doctor Yin Ba, so King Ping and Queen Ren sent people to dissuade Empress Dowager Li with this hint. Empress Dowager Li gave up because of her lewd behavior.
Later, Queen Mother Li died of illness.
When she was ill, Queen Ren did not ask for her health; after her death, she did not pay homage to her.
During the Yuanshuo period, there was a Suiyang man named Lei Anfan. Someone insulted his father. This man went out in the same car with the retainer of the Huaiyang prefect. The prefect's retainer got out of the car and left. Lei Anfan killed his enemy in the car and ran away.
The governor of Huaiyang was furious and blamed Liang Guo's two thousand stone officials.
Officials with less than 2,000 dan were very urgent to arrest the rebels, so they arrested the relatives of the rebels.
Lei Lian knew the secrets in Liang's palace, so he reported to the court in detail the events surrounding the dispute between King Ping and his grandmother over the Lei Zun.
At that time, officials below the prime minister knew about this incident and wanted to use it to attack the senior officials of Liang State, so they submitted a petition to the emperor.
The emperor handed the matter over to the officials for investigation and interrogation, and it was indeed true.
The minister asked the emperor to depose King Ping Liu Xiang and make him a commoner.
The Emperor said: Empress Dowager Li committed adultery, and Liang Wang Liu Xiang did not have a good master, so she fell into such an unjust situation.
So the fiefdoms of eight cities in Liang were reduced, and Queen Ren was beheaded in the city.
There are still ten cities left in the Liang Kingdom.
Liu Xiang died in the 39th year of his reign and was posthumously named King Ping.
His son Liu Wushang was established as King of Liang.
King Liu Ming of Jichuan was the second son of King Xiao of Liang. In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jichuan by the Marquis of Huanyi.
Seven years later, due to the crime of shooting the lieutenant, the relevant officials in the court petitioned to kill King Jichuan. The emperor could not bear to kill him, so he deposed Liu Ming as a civilian and demoted him to Fangling. The fiefdom belonged to the court and became a county.
King Liu Pengli of Jidong was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jidong in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
Twenty-nine years later, Liu Pengli was arrogant and fierce, without the demeanor of a human king. He secretly went out at night with dozens of his slaves and desperate youths to rob, kill, and plunder other people's property for fun.
More than a hundred people were found to have been killed by him. The whole country knew about it and no one dared to go out at night.
The son of the man he killed wrote a letter to report.
Relevant officials in the imperial court petitioned to have him executed. The emperor couldn't bear it and deposed him as a commoner and demoted him to Shangyong. The fiefdom belonged to the imperial court and became Dahe County.
Liu Ding, the Ai King of Shanyang, was the son of Liang Xiaozi. He was named King of Shanyang in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
After reigning for nine years, he died without a son. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Shanyang County.
Liu Bushi, the Ai King of Jiyin, was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jiyin in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
He died after one year in office without any sons. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Jiyin County.
Tai Shigong said: Although King Xiao of Liang was granted the title of king in a fertile land because he was the brother of the emperor and the beloved son of the queen mother, he also coincided with the prosperity of the country and the prosperity of the people, so he was able to accumulate wealth, expand the palace, and his carriages, horses and clothing were similar to those of the emperor.
However, doing so would also constitute an act of transgression.
Mr. Chu Shaosun said: When I was a Langguan, I heard about the deeds of King Liang Xiao from the old Langguan who liked to gossip in the palace.
I privately believe that the trouble that made King Xiao of Liang resentful and dissatisfied, and wanted to be emperor was caused by the imperial court.
The Queen Mother at that time was the heroine of the country. Because she loved her youngest son, she wanted Prince Liang to be the crown prince.
The ministers of the DPRK do not promptly tell the reason why they cannot do this, but instead just flatter the Queen Mother, talk about trivial things, and privately please the Queen Mother in order to get rewards. This is not a loyal minister!
If ministers could speak openly and honestly like Wei Qihou and Dou Ying, how could there be any subsequent disasters?
Emperor Jing was having a banquet with Prince Xiao of Liang and was serving the Queen Mother to drink. Emperor Jing said: After I live forever, I will pass on the throne to you, Prince Liang.
The Queen Mother was very happy about this.
Before the banquet, Dou Ying fell to the ground and remonstrated: The legal system of the Han Dynasty stipulates that the throne is passed on to the eldest son and grandson. How can the emperor pass it to his younger brother now, violating the regulations of Emperor Gao without authorization?
Emperor Jing was silent at that time.
The Queen Mother was also very unhappy.
Once upon a time, King Zhou Cheng and his young brother were standing under a tree. He picked up a tung leaf and said to his brother: I will seal you with this.
Duke Zhou heard this and went forward to pay homage and said: "It's very good that the emperor entrusts his younger brother."
King Cheng said: I was just joking with him.
Duke Zhou said: As a monarch, you should not do inappropriate things or make jokes. What you say must be done.
So King Cheng granted Yingxian County to his younger brother.
From then on, King Cheng did not dare to make jokes throughout his life, and he would always do what he said.
"The Classic of Filial Piety" says: Don't say things that are illegal and don't do things that are unreasonable.
This is the clear teaching of the sage.
At that time, the emperor should not have used such nice words to make a wish to King Liang.
King Liang had the Queen Mother to rely on, and he had been arrogant for a long time. He had heard Emperor Jing's wish many times that he would pass the throne to King Liang after a long life, but in fact he did not do so.
In addition, according to the system of the Han Dynasty, the princes and dynasties should only meet the emperor four times in total.
When he first arrived in the capital, he went to the palace to have an audience, which was called "a small meeting"; in the early morning of the first day of the first lunar month, he held a leather cushion and placed jade to congratulate the emperor on the first month, which was called a "dharma meeting"; three days later, the emperor hosted a banquet for the princes and kings and gave them money and property; two days later, the princes and kings went to the palace to have a small audience again, and then said goodbye and returned to the country.
The total stay in Chang'an was only twenty days.
The so-called "Xiao Jian" means meeting each other in the palace without formal ceremony and having banquets in the forbidden areas of the palace, which are not accessible to ordinary scholars.
Now the king of Liang went west to Chang'an to see the emperor and stayed in the palace for nearly half a year.
He entered the palace and sat in the same carriage as the emperor, and when he left the palace he rode in the same carriage as the emperor.
The emperor used exaggerated words to sarcastically say that he would be emperor in the future, but in fact he could not fulfill it, which made the king of Liang complain and plot rebellion. Then the emperor started to worry about him. Isn't this too far away from the truth?
Except for the great virtuous and virtuous people, no one knows how to be humble and give in.
According to the etiquette system of the Han Dynasty, when an audience with the emperor was held to celebrate the first lunar month, it was usually a king and four princes who met together. Such an opportunity only occurred once in more than ten years.
But now the King of Liang often goes to Beijing to meet with him year after year and stays in Beijing for a long time.
As the saying goes: Arrogant children do not know how to be filial.
This is a good thing to say. Therefore, we should set up good masters and tutors for the princes and kings, and let loyal and upright people to speak out to assist them, just like Ji An, Han Changru and others. If they dare to speak out and give advice, how can disaster happen?
I heard that Prince Liang went to the capital to pay homage to the Empress Dowager Dou, and his family members met each other. He and Emperor Jing sat together in front of the Empress Dowager, and their mother, son, and brothers happily exchanged intimate words.
The Queen Mother said to Emperor Jing: I heard that the system of the Yin and Shang Dynasties respected their brothers, and the system of the Zhou Dynasty respected their ancestors. This principle is the same.
A hundred years later, I entrust King Liang Xiao to you.
Emperor Jing knelt on the seat, raised his body and said, "Yes."
After leaving the palace after the banquet, Emperor Jing summoned Yuan An and other ministers who were proficient in Confucian classics and said: "What does the Queen Mother mean when she says such a thing?"
Yuan Ang and others all replied: The Queen Mother wants to make Prince Liang the emperor's crown prince.
Emperor Jing asked about the reason, and Yuan Ang and others said: According to the tradition of the Yin and Shang Dynasties, one's brothers are close to each other, so the inheritance is passed down to his younger brothers.
The tradition of the Zhou Dynasty respected its ancestors, so it was passed down to their sons.
The tradition of the Yin and Shang Dynasties advocates simplicity. Simplicity means imitating heaven and being close to relatives, so it is passed down to the younger brother.
The tradition of the Zhou Dynasty advocates beauty, and beauty imitates the earth. Zun means respect, respecting its origin, so it is passed down to the eldest son.
According to the system of the Zhou Dynasty, when the prince dies, a legitimate grandson is established.
According to the system of the Yin Dynasty, when the prince dies, his younger brother is appointed.
Emperor Jing said: What do you think?
Everyone answered together: The current system of the Han Dynasty is modeled after the Zhou Dynasty. The system of the Zhou Dynasty cannot establish brothers, but should establish sons.
Because of this, "Spring and Autumn" accused Song Xuangong of this.
After Song Xuangong died, he passed the throne to his younger brother instead of having a son.
After his brother succeeded to the throne and died, the throne was given to his elder brother's son.
His younger brother's son fought for the throne and thought he should succeed his father, so he killed Xuangong's son.
So the country was in chaos. Disasters continue.
Therefore, "Spring and Autumn" says: A gentleman respects and follows the right path, and the chaos in the Song Dynasty was caused by Duke Xuan.
The ministers and others asked to see the Queen Mother to explain this truth.
Yuan An and others went to the palace to see the Queen Mother and said: The Queen Mother said that she would establish King Liang. So, who will be established after King Liang dies?
The Queen Mother said: I will raise the emperor's son again.
Yuan An and others stated the following historical facts to the Queen Mother: Duke Xuangong of the Song Dynasty did not establish a legitimate son who should succeed to the throne, which led to troubles. The troubles lasted for five generations without ending, and failure to restrain petty selfishness would harm the great righteousness.
After hearing this, the Queen Mother understood the truth and was happy. She immediately asked King Liang to return to the feudal country.
When the King of Liang heard that this opinion came from Yuan An and other ministers, he became resentful of them and sent people to kill Yuan An.
Yuan An turned around and saw the assassin and said: I am the General Yuan you mentioned. You can't get the wrong person, can you?
Assassin said: It's you!
The assassin killed Yuan An, discarded his sword, and stuck the sword in Yuan An's body.
Check the sword, it has just been sharpened.
Asking the craftsmen who made or sharpened swords in Chang'an City, the craftsmen said: Someone from Liang Guolang came to sharpen this sword.
After getting clues and discovering the conspiracy, he sent envoys to hunt down the murderer.
There were more than ten ministers whom the King of Liang wanted to kill. The law-enforcement officials traced the root cause, and the clues of the King of Liang's rebellion were clearly revealed.
The Queen Mother couldn't eat it and cried day and night.
Emperor Jing was very worried about this and asked the ministers for advice. The ministers believed that only by sending officials who were proficient in classics to deal with the matter could the Queen Mother's worries be relieved.
So Tian Shu and Lu Jizhu were sent to handle the case.
Both of them are proficient in classics and know great rituals.
After returning from the case, he went to the Ba Chang stable, took a fire and burned all the testimony of King Liang's rebellion, and played back and forth to Emperor Jing with his bare hands.
Emperor Jing asked: How did the case go?
The echo said: The king of Liang did not know.
The only people involved in this incident were his favorite ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others.
The ministers and others executed them according to the law, and King Liang was safe and sound.
Emperor Jing was very happy and said, "Hurry up and see the Queen Mother."
When the Queen Mother learned of this, she immediately got up and sat down to eat, her mood restored to calm.
Therefore, people who are not proficient in classics and do not understand the ancient and modern rituals cannot be appointed as three princes and close ministers.
A person who is ignorant is like peering into the sky through a tube.
summary:
Liu Wu, King Xiao of Liang, was the son of Emperor Xiaowen and half-brother to Emperor Xiaojing, with Queen Mother Dou as his mother. Emperor Xiaowen had four sons: the eldest became Emperor Xiaojing; Liu Wu was the second, followed by Liu Shen and Liu Mingsheng. Liu Wu was initially made acting king, later King of Huaiyang, and eventually King of Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign. He ruled for eleven years from his first title as King of Dai to becoming King of Liang. During his reign, he frequently entered the court, staying in the capital for extended periods. Emperor Jing once casually promised to pass the throne to him, which secretly pleased Liu Wu and the Queen Mother.

In the spring of the rebellion of the seven kingdoms, Wu and Chu attacked Liang, killing tens of thousands. King Xiao defended Suiyang with generals like Han Anguo, blocking Wu and Chu from advancing westward. After three months of stalemate with Taiwei Yafu, Wu and Chu were destroyed, with Liang's casualties and captures roughly equal to the imperial court's. The following year, a prince was established. Due to his merits and relation to the emperor, King Xiao was granted a large, fertile fiefdom with over forty cities. He was deeply favored by Empress Dowager Dou, receiving countless rewards. He built Dongyuan over 300 li in radius, expanded Suiyang City to 70 li, and constructed palaces and elevated passages over 30 li long. His splendor rivaled an emperor's, with banners, thousands of attendants, and hunting expeditions. Heroes and lobbyists from across the country, including Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui, flocked to Liang. Gongsun Gui, given a thousand pieces of gold and a lieutenant position, was called General Gongsun. Liang forged many weapons and amassed nearly a trillion in money, plus countless jewels.

In October of the 29th year, King Xiao visited Emperor Jing, who sent an imperial carriage to greet him. He requested to stay in the capital, which was granted due to the Queen Mother's love. He accompanied the emperor in chariots and hunted at Shanglin Garden. Liang's ministers could enter the palace freely. In November, after the prince was deposed, the Queen Mother wanted King Xiao as successor, but ministers like Yuan An dissuaded Emperor Jing, blocking the motion. The matter remained secret. King Xiao then returned to his state. In April, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince. Resentful, King Xiao plotted with Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to assassinate Yuan An and over ten other ministers. The court failed to find the murderer initially but eventually suspected King Xiao. After capturing the assassins, the emperor sent envoys to Liang, arresting Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, who hid in the harem. Liang's officials urged the king to have them commit suicide, which he did. The emperor remained resentful, but after Han Anguo pleaded for forgiveness through the eldest princess, King Xiao was forgiven. He later entered the capital in disguise, hiding in the eldest princess's garden, causing the Queen Mother to weep, thinking the emperor had killed him. King Xiao then confessed, and brotherly relations were restored, though the emperor gradually alienated him.

In the winter of the 35th year, King Xiao visited again but was denied permission to stay. After returning, he became depressed. While hunting, a cow with feet on its back disgusted him. He fell ill with fever in mid-June and died six days later, posthumously titled King Xiao. He was filial, often wanting to serve the Queen Mother when she was ill. Her grief was immense, but Emperor Jing divided Liang into five kingdoms, granting all five sons and five daughters titles, which pleased her. King Xiao's eldest son, Liu Mai, inherited as King Gong; others became kings of Jichuan, Jidong, Shanyang, and Jiyin. His wealth was immense, with over 400,000 kilograms of gold left after death.

King Gong died after seven years, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang as King Ping. A dispute over a valuable bottle led to conflict between King Ping, his grandmother Queen Mother Li, and Queen Ren. Queen Ren took the bottle despite Queen Mother Li's objections. Queen Mother Li later died, with Queen Ren neglecting her in illness and death. A man named Lei Anfan, seeking revenge, revealed palace secrets to the court. Investigations confirmed Queen Mother Li's adultery and King Ping's mismanagement. The emperor reduced Liang's fiefdom by eight cities and executed Queen Ren. Liu Xiang died after 39 years, succeeded by his son Liu Wushang. Other sons of King Xiao faced fates: Liu Ming was deposed for shooting a lieutenant; Liu Pengli was deposed for robbery and murder; Liu Ding died without an heir; Liu Bushi died after one year without an heir. Their fiefdoms became counties.

Tai Shigong noted that King Xiao's wealth and splendor, though due to his position and the prosperous times, constituted transgression. Chu Shaosun added that the trouble stemmed from the court's failure to properly address succession issues, with ministers like Yuan Ang and Dou Ying providing wise counsel. He emphasized the importance of adhering to ritual and law, as exemplified by the Han system of limited court visits. The Queen Mother's desire to make King Xiao heir was ultimately thwarted by ministers citing historical precedents, such as the chaos in Song caused by Duke Xuan. After the assassination of Yuan An, the case was handled by officials who burned evidence, preserving King Xiao's reputation and calming the Queen Mother.
