Zhao Gongxi has the same surname as the Zhou royal family, Ji.
After King Wu of Zhou destroyed King Zhou of Shang, he granted Duke Zhao a title in Northern Yan.
When King Cheng of Zhou was on the throne, Duke Zhao was in charge of the three Dukes: from the west of Shaanxi, Duke Zhao was in charge; from the east of Shaanxi, Duke Zhou was in charge.
At that time, King Cheng was still young, and Duke Zhou presided over the affairs of state on his behalf and held the power of the country, just like the emperor. Duke Zhao was suspicious of Duke Zhou's actions, so Duke Zhou wrote an article "Jun Shi" to express his confession.
Duke Zhao was still very dissatisfied with Duke Zhou.
Duke Zhou then praised the relevant historical facts of the Yin and Shang Dynasties and said: During the reign of Shang Tang, there was Yi Yin, whose merits reached heaven; during Taiwu's reign, there were people like Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, whose merits reached heaven, and Wu Xian managed the government; during Zu Yi's reign, there were people like Wu Xian; during Wu Ding's era, there were people like Gan Ban: these ministers all had the merit of assisting the king and presiding over governance, and the Yin Dynasty was governed and stabilized.
After hearing these words, Duke Zhao became happy.
Duke Zhao governed the western region and was deeply loved by the people.
When Zhao Gong went to inspect villages and towns, he saw a Tangli tree, and he judged lawsuits and handled political affairs under the tree. From marquises, counts to civilians, everyone has been properly accommodated, and there has been no neglect of duty.
After the death of Duke Zhao, the people missed his political achievements and the time when Duke Zhao handled political affairs under the Tangli tree. They were reluctant to cut down the trees and praised Duke Zhao, writing a poem called "Gantang".
After Zhao Gong, it was passed down to Huihou through nine generations.
The reign of Yan Huihou coincided with the time when King Zhou Li fled to Pig, and when Zhou Dinggong and Zhaomu Gong were in power together.
Huihou died and his son Lihou came to the throne.
This year, King Zhou Xuan had just ascended the throne.
In the 21st year of Lihou, Duke Huan of Zheng was granted the title of Zheng.
In the thirty-sixth year, Lihou died and his son Qinghou came to the throne.
In the 20th year of Qinghou's reign, King You of Zhou committed adultery and was killed by Quan Rong.
Qin State began to be classified as vassals at this time.
Qinghou died in the twenty-fourth year of his reign, and his son Aihou came to the throne.
Marquis Ai died after reigning for two years, and his son Marquis Zheng came to the throne.
Zheng Hou died in the thirty-sixth year of his reign, and his son Miao Hou came to the throne.
The seventh year of Yan Muhou's reign was the first year of Lu Yin's reign.
Marquis Mu of Yan died in the eighteenth year of his reign, and his son Marquis Xuan came to the throne.
Xuanhou died in the thirteenth year of his reign, and his son Huanhou came to the throne.
Huan Hou died after reigning for seven years, and his son Zhuang Gong came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Duke Zhuang, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate.
In the 16th year, Yan State, Song State, and Wei State jointly attacked King Hui of Zhou. King Hui fled to Wendi. The three kingdoms supported King Hui's younger brother Decai as King of Zhou.
In the seventeenth year, Zheng Guo arrested Yan Zhongfu and escorted King Hui of Zhou back to Zhou Guo.
In the twenty-seventh year, the Shan Rong invaded the Yan State. Duke Huan of Qi went to rescue the Yan State, so he led his troops north to attack the Shan Rong and then returned home.
Duke Zhuang of Yan sent Duke Huan of Qi out of the country, and Duke Huan of Qi ceded the place where Duke Zhuang of Yan went to the state of Yan. He asked Duke Zhuang of Yan and the princes to pay tribute to the emperor of Zhou, just like Duke Zhao of Yan during the reign of King Cheng of Zhou.
In the thirty-third year, Duke Zhuang died, and his son Duke Xiang came to the throne.
In the twenty-sixth year of Duke Xiang, Duke Wen of Jin convened the princes to meet in Jiantu to form an alliance and to dominate the princes.
In the thirty-first year, the Qin army was defeated by the Jin army in Miaoshan.
In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
Forty years later, Duke Xiang of Yan died and Duke Huan ascended the throne.
Duke Huan died in the sixteenth year of his reign, and Duke Xuan ascended the throne.
Duke Xuan died in his fifteenth year and Duke Zhao ascended the throne.
Duke Zhao died in the thirteenth year of his reign, and Duke Wu ascended the throne.
This year, the Jin State executed Dr. Sanque.
Duke Wu died in the 19th year of his reign, and Duke Wen ascended the throne.
Duke Wen passed away in the sixth year of his reign, and Duke Yi ascended the throne.
In the first year of Yi AD, Cui Zhu of Qi killed his king Zhuang Gong.
Duke Yi died in the fourth year of his reign, and his son Duke Hui came to the throne.
In the first year of Huigong, Gaozhi of Qi State fled and came to Yan State.
In the past six years, Duke Hui had many concubines whom he favored. He planned to get rid of the officials and install a concubine named Song. The officials killed the concubine named Song together. Duke Hui was afraid and fled to Qi.
In the fourth year after he arrived in Qi State, Qi State sent Gao Yan to Jin State to request a joint attack on Yan State and send Duke Hui of Yan back to his country to become king.
Duke Ping of Jin agreed and joined Qi in attacking Yan and sent Duke Hui of Yan back to Yan.
Duke Hui died just after arriving in Yan State.
The people of Yan State supported Duke Mourning.
After reigning for seven years, Duke Du passed away and Duke Gong ascended the throne.
Duke Gong passed away after five years of reign, and Duke Ping ascended the throne.
At this time, the monarchy of Jin State was weakened, and the power of the six families including Fan, Zhongxing, Zhi, Zhao, Han and Wei began to grow.
In the eighteenth year of Ping Gong, King Helu of Wu conquered Chu and entered the capital of Ying.
Duke Ping died in the 19th year of his reign, and Duke Jian came to the throne.
Duke Jian died in the 12th year of his reign, and Duke Xian ascended the throne.
Zhao Yang of Jin State besieged Fan and Zhonghang families in Chaoge.
In the twelfth year of Xiangong's reign, Tian Chang of Qi State killed his king Jian Gong.
In the fourteenth year, Duke Xian died and Duke Xiao came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Duke Xiao's reign, the three families of Han, Wei, and Zhao destroyed Zhibo and divided up his fiefdom. These three families gradually became stronger.
In the fifteenth year, Duke Xiao died and Duke Cheng ascended the throne.
Duke Cheng died in the sixteenth year of his reign, and Duke Min ascended the throne.
Duke Min died in the thirty-first year of his reign, and Duke Li ascended the throne.
In this year, Han, Zhao and Wei were classified as princes.
In the 30th year of Li Gong, Yan State conquered and defeated Qi State in Linying. Duke Li died and Duke Huan ascended the throne.
Duke Huan died in the eleventh year of his reign, and Duke Wen ascended the throne.
This year, Duke Xiang of Qin passed away, and the state of Qin became stronger.
In the nineteenth year of Duke Wen, King Wei of Qi passed away.
In the twenty-eighth year, Su Qin came to Yan State for the first time to pay homage to Duke Wen and talk about Duke Wen.
Duke Wen gave him vehicles, horses, gold and silk and asked him to go to Zhao. Marquis Su of Zhao reused him.
So Su Qin implemented a joint vertical policy with the six countries, and he became the vertical commander.
At this time, King Qin Hui married his daughter to the prince of Yan as his wife.
In the twenty-ninth year, Duke Wen died and the prince came to the throne. This was King Yi.
As soon as King Yi came to the throne, King Xuan of Qi took advantage of the opportunity to hold a funeral for Duke Wen to attack Yan and capture ten cities. Su Qin went to Qi to lobby and persuaded King Qi to return ten cities to Yan.
Ten years later, the king of Yan State officially became king.
Su Qin committed adultery with the wife of Duke Wen of Yan and was afraid of being killed, so he lobbied King Yi to send him as an envoy to Qi to stir up rebellion and disrupt Qi.
King Yi died in the 12th year, and his son King Kuai of Yan came to the throne.
After King Kuai of Yan came to the throne, the people of Qi killed Su Qin.
When Su Qin was in the State of Yan, he married his son-in-law, the Prime Minister of the state, Zi Zhi. Su Qin's younger brother Su Dai also had a close relationship with Zi Zhi.
After Su Qin's death, King Qi Xuan appointed Su Dai again.
In the third year of King Kuai of Yan, Yan united with Chu, Han, Zhao, and Wei to attack Qin, but failed to win and returned home.
At that time, Zizhi was the prime minister of the Yan State. He held a high position and was in charge of major national affairs.
When Su Dai went to Yan as an envoy from Qi, the king of Yan asked him: How is the king of Qi?
Su Dai replied: He certainly cannot seek hegemony.
King Yan asked: Why?
He replied: He did not trust his ministers.
Su Dai wanted to use these words to stimulate King Yan and make him respect his son.
So King Yan trusted Zizhi very much.
Therefore, Zizhi gave Su Dai a hundred yi of gold and allowed him to use it as he pleased.
Lu Maoshou said to King Yan: You might as well give up the country to the Prime Minister.
The reason why people call Yao the king, virtuous and sage is because he gave up the world to Xu You, but Xu You did not accept it. Therefore, Yao had the reputation of giving up the world but actually did not lose the world.
If you give the country to your son now, he will definitely not dare to accept it. This shows that you and Yao have the same noble character.
King Yan then entrusted the country to Zi Zhi, and Zi Zhi's status became even more noble.
Someone said to King Yan: Yu recommended Boyi, but appointed Qi's ministers as officials.
When Yu was old, he thought that Qi was not enough to take on the important task of governing the world, so he passed the throne to Boyi.
Soon, Qijiu and his accomplices attacked Boyi and took away the throne.
Everyone in the world said that Dayu nominally passed the world to Boyi, but in fact he let Qi take it back.
Now the king says that he has entrusted the country to his son, but none of the officials is a minister who is not the prince. This is why he has entrusted the country to his son in name, but in fact the prince is still in charge.
King Yan then collected the seals of officials with a salary of more than 300 shi and gave them to Zizhi.
Zi Zhi sat on the throne facing south and exercised the power of the king. King Kuai of Yan no longer dealt with government affairs in his old age, but became a minister. All government affairs of the country were adjudicated by Zi Zhi.
Three years later, the Yan Kingdom was in chaos, and everyone was afraid.
Jiangjun City was plotted by Prince Ping and prepared to attack Zizhi.
The generals of the State of Qi said to King Qi Min: We take this opportunity to send troops to the State of Yan, and we will definitely defeat the State of Yan.
The King of Qi then sent someone to tell Prince Ping of Yan: I heard that the Prince upholds justice and will abolish private and public affairs, rectify the ethics of monarchs and ministers, and clarify the status of father and son.
My country is too small to follow you.
Even so, we are willing to obey the prince's orders.
Prince Ping then invited his companions to gather his disciples, and Jiangjun City was surrounded by the palace. They attacked Zi Zhi, but failed to capture it.
Jiangjun City was captured and Baiguan attacked Tai Ziping in turn. As a result, Jiangjunshi was killed in battle and his body was displayed to the public.
This caused chaos in the country for several months. Tens of thousands of people died, the people were very frightened, and the officials were disloyal.
Meng Ke said to King Qi: Now go to attack Yan State. This is a good opportunity for King Wen and King Wu of Zhou to attack Zhou. You must not miss it.
The King of Qi then ordered Zhang Zi to lead the troops from the five capitals and join the soldiers on the northern border to attack the State of Yan.
The soldiers of Yan State did not fight, and the city gates were not closed. The king of Yan died, and the Qi army was victorious.
In the second year after Yan Zi's death, the people of Yan State jointly supported Tai Ziping, who was King Zhao of Yan.
King Zhao of Yan came to the throne after the Yan Kingdom was conquered. He used his humility and generous gifts to recruit talented people.
He said to Guo Wei: The State of Qi took advantage of our domestic chaos and was unprepared to attack the State of Yan. I know that the State of Yan is small and weak, and does not have enough ability to take revenge.
But if I can get wise men to rule the country together and wash away the shame of the late king, this is my wish.
When my husband sees such a suitable talent, I will definitely serve him personally.
Guo Wei said: If the king must recruit wise men, then he should start with me, Guo Wei.
As for those who are more worthy than me, will they still think that they are thousands of miles away and refuse to come?
So King Zhao rebuilt Guo Wei into a gorgeous residence and treated him with the highest level of etiquette as he would a teacher.
At this time, Le Yi came from Wei, Zou Yan came from Qi, Ju Xin came from Zhao, and the wise men rushed to Yan.
King Yan paid homage to the deceased, expressed condolences to the orphans, and shared the joys and sorrows with his ministers.
In the twenty-eighth year, the state of Yan became rich and prosperous, and its soldiers were willing to attack and were not afraid of war. King Yan then appointed Le Yi as general, and planned together with Qin, Chu, Zhao, Wei, Han and other countries to send troops to conquer Qi.
The Qi army was defeated and King Qi Min fled to other places.
The Yan army pursued the fleeing Qi army alone, invaded Linzi, the capital of Qi, seized all the treasures of Qi, and burned the ancestral temples and palaces of Qi.
The only cities in Qi State that were not captured were Liao, Ju and Jimo. The rest were subordinate to Yan State for six years.
King Zhao died in the thirty-third year of his reign, and his son King Hui came to the throne.
When King Hui was the crown prince, he had a quarrel with Le Yi; after he came to the throne, he did not trust Le Yi and asked Qi Jie to replace Le Yi as general.
Le Yi fled to Zhao State. With the strength of one city in Jimo, Qi State Tian Dan defeated the Yan State army and died in the battle. The Yan army retreated to its own country, and Qi State regained all its original cities.
King Min of Qi died in Jucheng, so the people of Qi supported his son as King Xiang.
King Hui passed away in the seventh year of his reign, and the three kingdoms of Han, Wei, and Chu jointly attacked Yan.
King Yan Wucheng ascended the throne.
In the seventh year of King Wucheng, Qi State Tian Dan conquered Yan State and captured Zhongyang.
In the thirteenth year, Qin defeated Zhao's army of more than 400,000 in Changping.
In the fourteenth year, King Wu Cheng died and his son King Xiao came to the throne.
In the first year of King Kao, the Qin army that besieged Handan lifted the siege and left Zhao.
King Xiao died after reigning for three years, and his son King Yan came to the throne.
In the fourth year of King Yan's reign, King Zhao of Qin passed away.
The King of Yan sent his Prime Minister Li Fu to establish a friendly alliance with the State of Zhao, and presented 500 yi of gold to the King of Zhao to buy wine and celebrate his birthday.
Li Fu returned to his country and reported to King Yan: "All the young and strong people in Zhao Kingdom died in Changping, and their children have not grown up yet. We can take the opportunity to attack Zhao Kingdom."
King Yan called King Lejian of Chang State to inquire about this matter.
Lejian replied: Zhao is a country that is surrounded by enemies and often fights wars. Its people are familiar with military affairs and cannot attack.
King Yan said: We are attacking one of them with five people.
Le Jian still replied: No.
King Yan was very angry. At this time, all the ministers thought it was okay to attack.
The State of Yan finally sent out two armies with 2,000 chariots. Li Fu led the army to attack Hao, and Qing Qin led the army to attack Daidi.
Only the doctor told the king of Yan: "We communicated with others, made an alliance, took out five hundred yi of gold to toast their king, and then turned around and attacked them as soon as the envoy came back to report. This is unlucky, and the battle will not succeed."
King Yan couldn't listen, so he personally led the flanking troops and set off with the army.
He grabbed the seal belt around King Yan's waist to stop him and said: Your Majesty, you must not go there in person, otherwise you will not succeed!
King Yan kicked him away with his feet.
Jiang Qu cried and said: I am not doing it for myself, but for the king!
When the Yan army arrived at Songzi, Zhao sent Lian Po to lead his troops and defeated Li Fu at Cha.
Le Cheng also defeated Qing Qin in Dai Di. Lejian fled to Zhao State.
Lian Po pursued Yan for more than five hundred miles and surrounded the capital of Yan.
The people of Yan requested peace talks, but the people of Zhao refused, so they had to ask General Qu to come forward to preside over the peace talks.
The State of Yan appointed General Qu as prime minister and went to preside over the peace talks.
The State of Zhao listened to General Qu's request and lifted the siege of the State of Yan.
In the sixth year of King Yan's reign, the Qin State destroyed the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and established Sanchuan County.
In seven years, Qin State captured 37 cities including Yulin of Zhao State and established Taiyuan County.
In the ninth year, King Qin Yingzheng had just ascended the throne.
In the tenth year, the State of Zhao sent Lian Po to lead an army to attack Fanyang of the State of Wei and occupied it.
At this time, King Zhao Xiaocheng passed away and King Mouxiang came to the throne.
King Mouxiang sent Lecheng to take over Lianpo's command, but Lianpo refused to obey orders and attacked Lecheng. Lecheng escaped, and Lianpo also fled to Daliang, the capital of Wei.
In the twelfth year, Zhao State sent Li Mu to attack Yan State and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng.
When Ju Xin lived in the State of Zhao, he was very close to Pang Nuan, but later fled to the State of Yan.
King Yan saw that Zhao was besieged by Qin soldiers many times and Lian Po left Zhao. At this time, Pang Nuan was leading the army to fight, so he wanted to take advantage of Zhao's fatigue to attack it.
King Yan asked Ju Xin at this time, and Ju Xin said: Pang Nuan is easy to deal with.
The King of Yan sent Ju Xin to lead an army to attack the State of Zhao. The State of Zhao sent Pang Nuan to fight, captured 20,000 Yan troops, and killed Ju Xin.
At this time, Qin State captured twenty cities of Wei State and established Dongjun.
In the 19th year, Qin State captured nine cities including Ye of Zhao State.
King Zhao Daoxiang passed away.
In the twenty-third year, Prince Dan of Yan was sent to Qin as a hostage, but he escaped back to Yan.
In the twenty-fifth year, Qin captured Han Wangan, destroyed Han, and established Yingchuan County.
In the twenty-seventh year, Qin captured Zhao Wangqian and destroyed Zhao.
Prince Jia of the State of Zhao established himself as acting king.
The monarchs and ministers of the Yan State saw that the Qin State was about to destroy the six countries. The Qin army had already reached Yishui, and disaster was about to befall the Yan State.
Prince Dan of Yan secretly supported twenty warriors. At this time, he sent Jing Ke to present the map of Dukang to the King of Qin and took the opportunity to assassinate the King of Qin.
The King of Qin found out, killed Jing Ke, and sent General Wang Jian to attack Yan.
In the 29th year, the Qin army captured Ji, the capital of Yan State. King Yan fled and later moved to Liaodong. He killed Prince Dan and presented his head to Qin State.
Thirty years later, Qin destroyed Wei.
In the thirty-third year, the Qin army captured Liaodong, captured King Xi of Yan, and finally destroyed the Yan state.
This year, Qin general Wang Ben also captured Dai Wangjia.
Tai Shigong said: Zhao Gongxi can be called a virtuous person!
That Tangli tree is still missed by the people, let alone Zhao Gong himself?
Yan State was forced by barbarians externally and attacked by Qi and Jin internally. It struggled to survive among the powerful countries. It was the weakest and was almost destroyed many times.
However, the country lasted for eight or nine hundred years and finally perished among the princes surnamed Ji. Isn't this the merit of Duke Zhao?
summary:
The history of the Yan state, beginning with its founder, Zhao Gongxi, a member of the Zhou royal family granted the title in Northern Yan by King Wu. During King Cheng's reign, Zhao Gong governed west of Shaanxi, while the Duke of Zhou governed the east. Suspicious of the Duke of Zhou's regency, Zhao Gong was appeased by the Duke's historical references to virtuous Yin ministers. Zhao Gong governed the western region with great popularity, famously adjudicating under a Tangli tree, which the people later honored in the poem "Gantang" after his death.

The succession of Yan rulers is then detailed, from Huihou through numerous generations, with key events interspersed: the flight of King Zhou Li, the rise of Qin as vassals, and the reign of King Xuan. The narrative covers Yan's interactions with other states, including attacks on King Hui of Zhou, invasions by Shan Rong (aided by Duke Huan of Qi), and participation in alliances against Qin. Internal strife emerges under King Kuai, who ceded power to his minister Zizhi, leading to chaos, Qi's invasion, and the death of King Kuai. King Zhao of Yan restored stability by recruiting talents like Le Yi, Zou Yan, and Ju Xin, leading to a prosperous period and a successful campaign against Qi, capturing its capital Linzi.

After King Zhao's death, King Hui's distrust of Le Yi led to Qi's recovery under Tian Dan. Subsequent rulers faced defeats by Zhao, including a failed attack advised by Ju Xin, resulting in heavy losses. The state weakened as Qin expanded, destroying Han and Zhao. Prince Dan of Yan's failed assassination attempt on Qin's king via Jing Ke prompted Qin's invasion, capturing Ji and forcing King Yan to flee to Liaodong. Eventually, Qin captured Liaodong, ending the Yan state. The historian concludes that Yan's survival for eight or nine hundred years, despite external pressures and near destruction, was due to Zhao Gong's virtuous legacy.

translation:
Chen Wan is Chen Ligong's son.
When Wan was born, Taishi of Zhou happened to pass by the state of Chen. Chen Ligong asked him to divine divination for Chen Wan. The hexagram obtained was "Guan Gua" changed to "No Gua". Taishi said: The meaning of the hexagram is: observing the customs and sentiments of the country is helpful for being the king's guest.
Does this mean that he will obtain the throne of Chen and own the country?
Maybe it's not in Chen country but in another country?
Or it may not be fulfilled on others, but be fulfilled on his descendants.
If it is in another country, it must be the country with the surname Jiang.
The surname Jiang is a descendant of the Four Mountains during the reign of Emperor Yao.
It is impossible for two things to be powerful at the same time. After the decline of Chen State, his branch will prosper!
Li Gong is the youngest son of Chen Wengong, and his mother is a woman from Cai State.
After Duke Wen died, Duke Li's brother Chen Bao came to the throne, and this was Duke Huan.
Duke Huan and his younger brother Chen were not born from the same mother.
When Duke Huan was ill, the people of Cai killed Duke Huan Chen Bao and Prince Chen Min on behalf of Chen Ta, and made Chen Ta the king. This is Duke Li.
After Li Gong came to the throne, he married a woman from Cai State.
This Cai woman committed adultery with a Cai man and returned to Cai many times. Duke Li also frequently went to Cai.
Chen Lin, the youngest son of Duke Huan, resented Duke Li for killing his father and brother, so he asked the people of Cai to trick Duke Li and kill him.
Chen Lin established himself as king, this is Duke Zhuang.
Therefore, Chen Wan could not be established as the king, but only as the official of the state of Chen.
Duke Li was killed because he went abroad for promiscuity, so the Spring and Autumn Annals said that "Cai people killed Chen Ta", which was an accusation against him.
After Zhuang Gong died, his younger brother Chujiu came to the throne. This was Chen Xuangong.
In the 21st year of Xuangong's reign, Chujiu killed the prince Yu Kou.
Yu Kou and Chen Wan were close, and he was afraid that the disaster would involve him, so Chen Wan fled to Qi State.
Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as minister, but he declined and said: "As a humble minister living abroad, I am fortunate enough to be exempted from all kinds of burdens. It is already a favor given to me by you. I dare not hold such a high position again."
Duke Huan of Qi appointed him as Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of workers.
Qi Yizhong wanted to marry his daughter to Chen Wan, so he conducted a divination for this matter. The result of the divination said: This is called the flying phoenix, with a harmonious sound.
The descendants of the Gui family will grow up under the Jiang family.
After the Five Dynasties, he will be prosperous and have the same status as Zhengqing.
After eight generations, no one can be higher than him.
He finally married his daughter to Chen Wan.
When Chen Wan fled to Qi, Duke Huan of Qi had been in power for fourteen years.
After Chen Wan's death, his posthumous title was Jingzhong.
Jingzhong gave birth to Yu Mengyi.
After Jingzhong arrived in Qi State, he changed the Chen family name to the Tian family name.
Tian Zhen Meng Yi gave birth to Min Meng Zhuang, and Tian Min Meng Zhuang gave birth to Wen Zi Xu Wu.
Tian Wenzi served Duke Zhuang of Qi.
Luan Cheng, a senior official of the Jin State, caused trouble in the Jin State and fled to the Qi State. Duke Zhuang of Qi gave him generous treatment.
Yan Ying and Tian Wenzi advised him, but Duke Zhuang did not listen.
Tian Wenzi died, and his son was Huanzi Wuyu.
Tian Huanzi Wuyu was strong and served Duke Zhuang of Qi, and was very favored.
Wuyu died and his sons were Wu Zikai and Liziqi.
Lizitianqi served Qi Jinggong as a doctor. When he collected taxes from the people, he collected them with a small bucket, and when he gave grain to the people, he used a big bucket. He secretly showed kindness to the people, but Qi Jinggong did not prohibit it.
Therefore, the Tian family gained the hearts and minds of the people of Qi. Their family became stronger and stronger, and the people's hearts turned to the Tian family.
Yanzi repeatedly advised Jinggong, but Jinggong refused to listen.
Soon Yanzi went to Jin as an envoy. He and his uncle said privately: The political power of Qi will eventually return to the Tian family.
After Yan Ying's death, the Fan family and the Zhongxing family rebelled in Jin.
The Jin State stepped up its pursuit of them. The Fan family and the Zhonghang family asked Qi to borrow grain. Tian Qi wanted to cause trouble and form a clique among the princes, so Qi Jinggong said: "The Fan family and the Zhonghang family have been kind to Qi many times, and Qi has to save them."
Qi State sent Tian Qi to rescue them and sent them food.
The prince of Qi Jinggong passed away. Jinggong had a favorite concubine named Rui Zi, and the son Rui Zi gave birth to was named Tu.
When Jinggong was ill, he asked his prime ministers Guo Huizi and Gao Zhaozi to make their son Tu the crown prince.
After Jinggong's death, the two prime ministers of Gao and Guo made Tu the king of the country. This was Yan Ruzi.
But Tian Qi was very unhappy and wanted to establish Jinggong's other son Yangsheng.
Yang Sheng usually has a good relationship with Tian Qi.
After Yan Ruzi ascended the throne, Yang Sheng fled to the state of Lu.
Tian Qi pretended to serve Gao Zhaozi and Guohui, and would accompany them in the car every time they went to court. He also said: At first, none of the officials wanted to have a child.
After Ruzi came to the throne, you two were appointed prime ministers, and the officials were all in danger and plotting to cause chaos.
Tian Qi lied to the doctors and said: Gao Zhaozi is very scary, let's kill him before he does it!
The doctors all obeyed him.
Tian Qi, Bao Mu and other officials led troops into the palace to attack Gao Zhaozi.
After Zhaozi heard about it, he and Guohuizi went to rescue the king.
The king's army failed.
Tian Qi's men went after Guo Huizi, but Huizi fled to Ju, and then returned to kill Gao Zhaozi.
Yan Ying's son Yan Yu fled to Lu.
Tian Qi sent people to the state of Lu to welcome Yang Sheng back.
Yang Sheng returned to Qi State and hid in Tian Beggar's home.
Tian Qi invited the officials and said: "Tian Chang's mother has prepared some coarse food and wine. Please come and enjoy the feast."
All the officials came to Tian's house to drink.
Tian Qi put Yang Sheng in his pocket and placed him on the central seat. During the banquet, Tian Qi opened his pocket and released Yang Sheng. He said, "This is the king of Qi."
The doctors all bowed to pay homage.
About to make an alliance to support Yang Sheng, Tian Qi lied and said: I conspired with Bao Mu to support Yang Sheng.
Bao Mu said angrily: "Have the officials forgotten Jinggong's death?"
The officials wanted to regret it, but Yang Sheng kowtowed and said: If you think I can do it, make me king, if you can't do it, depose me.
Bao Mu was afraid that disaster would happen to him, so he said again: "They are all the sons of Jinggong, why not?"
Finally, Yang Sheng was established as the king in Tianqi's house. This was Duke Mourning.
So he sent people to move Yan Ruzi to Ni and killed Ruzi Tu.
After Duke Mourning ascended the throne, Tian Qi was appointed prime minister and took over the political power of Qi.
Four years later, Tian Qi died and his son Tian Chang took over the position. This is Tian Chengzi.
Bao Mu had a disagreement with Duke Dao of Qi and killed Duke Dao of Qi.
The people of Qi jointly supported Ren, the son of Duke Ai, who was Duke Jian of Qi.
Tian Changchengzi and Jianzhi served as prime ministers and assisted Duke Jian.
Tian Chang was jealous of Jian Zhi, because Jian Zhi was very favored by Duke Jian of Qi and his power could not be removed.
So Tian Chang reused his father Lizi's method, using big buckets to lend grain to the people and small buckets to take it back.
The people of Qi State sang in praise of him and said: The old lady picked raspberries and gave them to Tian Chengzi!
When the officials of Qi State went to court, Yu Martingale admonished Duke Jian and said: Tian Chang and Jian Zhi cannot be appointed at the same time. Let the monarch choose!
Duke Jian didn't listen.
Ziwo is of the same clan as Jian Zhi, and is usually at odds with the Tian family.
Tian Bao, a distant relative of the Tian family, served Ziwo and was favored.
Ziwo said: I want to kill all the direct descendants of the Tian family and let you continue the Tian family line.
Tian Bao said: I am just Tian’s distant relative.
I won't listen.
Soon Tian Bao said to Tian, ​​"I am going to kill Tian. If Tian doesn't take action first, disaster will come."
I live in Duke Jian's palace, and the four Tian Chang brothers also rode to the palace and wanted to kill me.
I shut the door.
Justice Jian and his beloved concubine were drinking and having fun in Tantai, so they wanted to attack Tian Chang.
Taishi Ziyu said: Tian Chang did not dare to cause trouble, he wanted to eliminate harm for the country.
Only then did Mr. Jian stop.
After Tian Chang came out of the palace, he heard that Duke Jian had sent Nu, and he was afraid that he would be killed, so he wanted to flee.
Tian Zixing said: Hesitation is the enemy of career.
Tian Chang then attacked me.
Ziwo led his men to attack the Tian family, but could not win and had to flee.
Tian's men chased and killed Ziwo and Jianzhi.
Duke Jian fled, and Tian's men chased him to Xuzhou and captured him.
Duke Jian said: If I had listened to Yu Yang earlier, I would not have suffered such a disaster.
Tian's subordinates were worried that Duke Jian would kill them after he was restored to the throne, so they killed Duke Jian.
Duke Jian was killed four years after he ascended the throne.
So Tian Chang supported Ao, the younger brother of Duke Jian, to the throne. This was Duke Qi Ping.
After Ping Gong ascended the throne, he appointed Tian Chang as prime minister.
After Tian Chang killed Duke Jian, he was afraid that the princes from all over the world would unite to kill him, so he returned all the lands that he had occupied in Lu and Wei. The west made treaties with Jin, Han, Wei, and Zhao, and the south exchanged envoys with Wu and Yue to cultivate meritorious deeds, give rewards, and get close to the people. As a result, Qi regained stability.
Tian Chang said to Qi Pinggong: "To perform kindness is what people want, you should implement it yourself; if punishment is what people hate, please let me carry it out."
After five years of doing this, the political power of Qi State was controlled by Tian Chang.
So Tian Chang killed all the more powerful of the Bao, Yan, Jianzhi, and Gong clans, and divided the land of Qi from the east of Anping to Langye as his own fiefdom.
His fiefdom was larger than the land enjoyed by Qi Pinggong.
Tian Chang selected Qi women with a height of more than seven feet to be his concubines in the harem. There were more than 100 concubines, and he allowed guests and attendants to enter and leave the harem at will without any restrictions.
By the time Tian Chang died, Concubine Ji had given birth to more than seventy sons.
After Tian Chang died, his son Xiangzi Tianpan took over his position and served as prime minister of Qi.
Tian Chang's posthumous name is Chengzi.
After Tian Xiangzi became prime minister of Duke Xuan of Qi, the Han, Zhao and Wei families of Jin killed Zhibo and divided his territory.
Xiangzi also asked his brothers and his own people to serve as officials in Qi's large and small cities, and to communicate with the three Jin Dynasties as envoys. He almost owned Qi.
After Xiangzi died, his son Zhuangzi Tianbai succeeded his father.
Tian Zhuangzi served as the prime minister of Duke Xuan of Qi.
In the forty-third year of Xuangong's reign, Qi attacked Jin, destroyed Huangcheng, and besieged Yanghu.
In the second year, he attacked Lucheng, Geyi and Anling.
In another year, he captured a city in the state of Lu.
After Tian Zhuangzi died, his son Taigong Tianhe succeeded his father.
Grand Duke Tian assisted Duke Xuan of Qi.
In the forty-eighth year of Xuangong's reign, Qi captured the city of Lu.
In the second year, Qi Xuangong and Zheng Guoren met in Xicheng.
Qi State attacked Wei State and captured Qiu.
In the fifty-first year of Xuangong's reign, Qi Xuangong died, and Tian Hui rebelled in Linqiu.
After Qi Xuangong died, his son Kang Gongdai came to the throne.
For fourteen years after he took the throne, he indulged in wine and sex and ignored political affairs.
Taigong Tianhe moved him to the seaside and only built a city as a food town in order to provide sacrifices to his ancestors.
The next year, the Lu army defeated the Qi army in Pinglu.
Three years later, Qi Taigong Tianhe and Wei Wenhou met in Zhuoze and asked to become princes.
Marquis Wen of Wei sent envoys to report to the Emperor of Zhou and the princes of various countries, requesting that Qi Xiang Tianhe be made a prince. The Emperor of Zhou granted this request.
In the 19th year of Duke Kanggong of Qi, Tian He officially became the Marquis of Qi, and was listed in the royal family of the Zhou Dynasty, and the first year of chronology began.
Qi Hou Taigong Tian He died in the second year of his reign, and his son Huan Gong Tian Wu came to the throne.
In the fifth year of Duke Huan's reign, Qin and Wei attacked South Korea, and South Korea asked Qi for help.
Duke Huan of Qi Tian Wu summoned the ministers to discuss: Is it better to go to the rescue earlier or later?
Zuo Ji said: It is better not to save him.
Duan Qianpeng said: If we don't save it, Korea will be merged into Wei if it fails. It's better to save it.
Tian Chensi said: Your plan is wrong!
When Qin and Wei attack South Korea, Chu and Zhao must rescue it. This is God’s gift of Yan to Qi.
Duke Huan said: Excellent!
So he secretly told the Korean envoy to rescue him and send him away.
South Korea thought it had received reinforcements from Qi, so it went to war with Qin and Wei.
After Chu and Zhao found out, they sent troops to rescue.
Qi State took the opportunity to send troops to attack Yan State and occupied Sangqiu.
In the sixth year of Duke Huan, he sent troops to rescue the country.
Duke Huan died, and his son King Wei Yinqi came to the throne.
In this year, the original Duke Kang of Qi passed away, cutting off his descendants, and all the fiefdoms belonged to the Tian family.
In the first year of King Wei of Qi, the three Jin Dynasties took advantage of the funeral in Qi to attack Lingqiu.
In three years, Han, Zhao, and Wei destroyed the Jin Dynasty and divided its land.
In the sixth year, Lu attacked Qi and captured Yangguan.
Jin State attacked Qi State and reached Boling.
In the seventh year, Weiguo attacked Qi and captured Xue Ling.
In the ninth year, Zhao State attacked Qi State and occupied Zhencheng.
When King Wei first came to the throne, he ignored state affairs and left the political affairs to the officials. Within nine years, princes from all over the world came to attack him, and the people of Qi were not at peace.
So King Wei summoned the Jimo doctor and said to him: Ever since you took charge of Jimo, there have been slanderous remarks about you every day.
But I sent people to Jimo to inspect, and the fields were developed, the people lived a prosperous life, the government did not have a backlog of official affairs, and the east of Qi State was at peace.
This is because you will not flatter me in order to gain praise!
So, he was granted ten thousand households and a city of food, and he summoned the doctor Acheng and said to him: Since you have governed Acheng, I can hear words of praise for you every day.
But I sent people to inspect Acheng. The fields were deserted and the people were poor.
Once upon a time, the Zhao army attacked Zhencheng, but you were unable to rescue it.
Weiguo captured Xue Ling, and you didn’t know.
This is how you use your property to bribe my right and left to seek praise!
Doctor Acheng was cooked to death on the same day, and all the people who had praised him were also cooked and killed.
So he sent troops to the west to attack Zhao and Wei, defeated the Wei army in Zhuoze and besieged King Wei Hui.
King Hui of Wei asked for the city to be used to make peace. The people of Zhao returned the Great Wall of Qi.
As a result, the whole country of Qi was shocked. Everyone did not dare to cover up their mistakes and tried hard to show their loyalty.
The state of Qi was well governed.
After hearing this, the princes did not dare to send troops to Qi for more than twenty years.
Zuo Jizi went to see King Wei of Qi because he was good at playing the harp. King Wei liked him very much and let him live in the right room of the palace.
Not long after, King Wei was playing the harp, and Zuo Jizi opened the door and came in and said: "You play the harp very well!"
King Wei was suddenly unhappy. He left the piano player and pressed his sword and said, "Sir, you only see my appearance and haven't observed me carefully. How can you know that I am playing well?"
Zou Jizi said: The big string is slow and gentle, which symbolizes the king; the small string is high-pitched, bright and clear, symbolizing the prime minister; the fingers are pulling the string hard and letting it go slowly, symbolizing the government order; the sound of the piano is harmonious, the large and small are coordinated beautifully, and the twists and turns do not interfere with each other, symbolizing the four seasons: I can know how well you play from this.
King Wei said: You are very good at talking about music.
Zuo Jizi said: It is not just about music, it is also about governing the country and appeasing the people!
King Wei suddenly became unhappy and said: If we talk about the conditioning of the five tones, I believe there is no one who can compare with you.
If it is to govern the country and appease the people, how can it be among the strings?
Zou Jizi said: The big string is slow and gentle, symbolizing the king; the small string, high-pitched, bright and clear, symbolizes the prime minister; the string is played hard but released slowly, symbolizing the government order; the sound of the piano is harmonious, the large and small are coordinated beautifully, and the twists and turns do not interfere with each other, symbolizing the four seasons.
It goes back and forth without chaos because of political prosperity; it is coherent and brisk because it protects the dying country: so it is said that the harmonious tune of the piano can protect the peace of the world.
There is nothing more similar to governing a country and appeasing the people than the five tones. King Wei said: Excellent.
It took only three months for Zuo Jizi to see King Wei and he accepted the seal.
Chunyu Kun met him and said: "You are really good at talking!"
I have some superficial opinions that I would like to state in front of you.
Zuo Jizi said: Accept instruction respectfully.
Chunyu Kun said: If you serve the king with care and error, your reputation will be prosperous; if you are not careful or make mistakes, your reputation will be destroyed.
Zuo Ji said: "I accept your advice respectfully. I will keep your words in mind."
Chunyu Kun said: The purpose of smearing the axle with lard is to lubricate it. However, if the axle hole is square, it cannot rotate.
Zuo Shuzi said: I would like to receive your advice, and I must serve the king carefully.
Chunyu Kun said: The purpose of gluing bows that have been used for a long time is to stick them together, but the glue cannot completely close the gaps.
Zuo Jizi said: I would like to receive your advice and make myself dependent on all peoples.
Chunyu Kun said: Even if the fox skin coat is torn, it cannot be repaired with yellow dog skin.
Zuo Jizi said: I would like to receive your advice. I must carefully select gentlemen and not let villains mix among them.
Chunyu Kun said: If the cart is not straightened, it will not be able to carry the load properly; if the strings of the harp and harp are not tuned well, the five notes will not be harmonious.
Zuo Jizi said: I would like to receive your advice. I will conscientiously formulate laws and supervise cunning officials.
After Chunyu Kun finished speaking, he walked out quickly and said to his servant outside the door: "This man, I said five secret words to him, and he answered me like an echo. This man will definitely be sealed soon!"
A year later, King Wei granted Xiapi to Zuo Jizi, and the title was Chenghou.
In the twenty-third year of King Wei, King Qi and King Zhao met in Pinglu.
In the twenty-fourth year, the king of Qi and the king of Wei were hunting together in the countryside.
King Wei asked: "Does your Majesty also have treasures?"
King Wei said: No.
The King of Wei said: "As small as I am, and with ten luminous pearls one inch in diameter that can illuminate twelve chariots at the front and rear, how can a country as vast as Qi not have treasures?"
King Wei said: What I regard as treasure is different from that of the great king.
I have a minister named Tanzi, and I sent him to control Nancheng. The people of Chu did not dare to invade and plunder to the east, and the twelve princes on the shores of Surabaya came to worship.
I have a minister named Panzi, who is assigned to guard Gaotang. The people of Zhao do not dare to fish in the Yellow River to the east.
I have an official named Qian Fu, who is assigned to guard Xuzhou. People from Yan State come to the north gate to offer sacrifices, and people from Zhao State come to the west gate to offer sacrifices in order to pray for the gods to protect them from attack. More than 7,000 people moved to follow him.
I have a minister named Zhongshou who sent him to be on the lookout for thieves, but he ended up not picking up any items along the way.
These will illuminate thousands of miles, where are just twelve cars!
King Hui of Wei felt ashamed and left in despair.
In the twenty-sixth year of King Wei's reign, King Hui of Wei besieged Handan, and Zhao asked Qi for rescue.
King Wei of Qi convened the ministers to discuss: Is it better to save Zhao or not to save Zhao?
Zuo Jizi said: It is better not to save him.
Duan Qianpeng said: Not saving him would be unjust and would be detrimental to us.
King Wei said: Why?
Duan Qianpeng replied: If Wei annexes Handan, what good will it do to Qi?
If Zhao is saved and the army is stationed on the outskirts of Zhao, Zhao will not be attacked and the Wei army will be intact.
Therefore, it is better to attack Xiangling of Wei State in the south and tire the Wei army. Even if Handan is captured, we can use Wei State's fatigue to frustrate it.
King Wei listened to his plan.
Later, the relationship between Chenghou Zouji and Tian Ji was not good. Gongsun Yue said to Chenghou Zouji: Why don't you consider attacking Wei? In that case, Tian Ji will definitely lead the army.
If the victory is meritorious, it means your strategy is correct; if the defeat is unsuccessful, Tian Ji will either fight to the death forward or be defeated backward, and his life is in your hands.
So Chenghou suggested to King Wei that he send Tian Ji south to attack Xiangling.
In October, Handan was captured. Qi took the opportunity to attack the Wei army and defeated the Wei army in Guiling.
So the state of Qi became the strongest among the princes, and called himself king to command the world.
In the thirty-third year of King Wei, King Wei killed his doctor Mou Xin.
In the thirty-fifth year of King Wei's reign, Gongsun Yue said to Chenghou Zuoji again: "Why don't you ask someone to take ten pounds of gold to the street to divine fortune and say that I am Tian Ji's man?"
We won three out of three battles and our reputation spread all over the world.
Is it auspicious or unlucky to want to do big things?
After the person who asked the divination left, he sent someone to arrest the gentleman who divined for him, and verified the divination with King Wei. After Tian Ji heard about it, he led his men to attack Linzi, captured Chenghou, and ran away without winning.
In the thirty-sixth year of King Wei, King Wei of Qi passed away, and his son King Xuan Piqiang came to the throne.
In the first year of King Xuan, the State of Qin appointed Shang Yang, and the Emperor of Zhou awarded the title of overlord to Duke Xiao of Qin.
In the second year of King Xuan's reign, Wei State attacked Zhao State.
The State of Zhao was friendly with South Korea and attacked the State of Wei together. However, the situation of the State of Zhao was unfavorable and they were defeated in Nanliang.
King Xuan recalled Tian Ji to his original position.
South Korea asked Qi for rescue.
King Xuan summoned his ministers to discuss: Is it better to go to the rescue early or late?
Zuo Jizi said: It is better not to save him.
Tian Ji said: If we don't save it, Korea will fail and merge with Wei. It's better to rescue it as soon as possible.
Sun Bin said: If the armies of Han and Wei go to rescue before they are exhausted, then we will be attacked by the Wei army on behalf of South Korea, and then we will follow South Korea's command.
Moreover, the Wei State has plans to attack South Korea. If South Korea is about to perish, it must go east to ask Qi for reinforcements.
We take the opportunity to form a close relationship with South Korea, and we can take advantage of the Wei army's fatigue later, so that we can have greater benefits and gain a respected reputation. King Xuan said: Very good.
So he secretly told the Korean envoy and sent him away.
Because South Korea relied on Qi for rescue, it failed in all five battles, so it had no choice but to entrust the country to Qi eastward.
Qi State took advantage of the situation and sent troops, sending Tian Ji and Tian Ying as commanders and Sun Bin as military advisor. They attacked Wei State to rescue Han and Zhao. They defeated the Wei army in Maling, killed Wei general Pang Juan, and captured Wei Crown Prince Shen.
After that, the monarchs of the three Jin Dynasties were introduced by Tian Ying, paid homage to the King of Qi in Bowang, and left after swearing an oath.
In the seventh year of King Xuan, King Qi and King Wei met south of Ping'a.
The next year, we met again in Zhencheng.
King Wei Hui passed away.
In another year, King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei met in Xuzhou, and the princes called each other king.
In the tenth year of King Xuan's reign, the Chu army surrounded Xuzhou of Qi State.
In the eleventh year, Qi and Wei attacked Zhao, and Zhao's army was flooded by the Yellow River, so Qi and Wei withdrew their troops.
In the eighteenth year, King Qin Hui became king.
King Xuan loved scholars who were erudite and eloquent. Seventy-six of them, such as Zuo Yan, Chunyu Kun, Tian Pian, Jieyu, Shen Dao, and Huanyuan, were all given to the mansion and made them serve as senior officials. They did not deal with political affairs but exclusively discussed academic affairs.
Therefore, the number of Jixia scholars in Qi State increased again, reaching hundreds or even thousands.
In the nineteenth year of King Xuan, King Xuan of Qi passed away, and his son King Min Tiandi came to the throne.
In the first year of King Min's reign, the state of Qin sent Zhang Yi to meet with the ministers in charge of the affairs of various countries in Zhisang.
In the third year, King Min sealed Tian Ying in Xue.
Four years later, King Min married his wife from Qin.
In the seventh year, Qi and Song attacked Wei and defeated the Wei army in Guanze.
In the twelfth year of King Min, Qi attacked Wei.
Chu State besieged the Yong family in South Korea, and Qin State defeated Chu general Qu Gai.
Su Dai said to Tian Zhen, the minister of Chu State: I have something to do and would like to see you. This matter is very successful and will make Chu State beneficial to you. It will be a blessing if it succeeds, and it will be a blessing if it fails.
Today I was standing at the door, and someone said that King Wei once said to Han Feng and Zhang Yi: Zhuzao is about to fall, and the Qi army is coming to attack again. If you two come to save me, we will be undefeated; if you don't come to save me, we will be powerless.
This is just a euphemism.
If the armies of Qin and Han do not go east to rescue Wei, Wei will change its strategy in more than ten days. South Korea will follow Qin, and Qin will expel Zhang Yi and serve Qi and Chu. In this way, your mission will be successful.
Tian Zhen said: How can we prevent the Qin and Han armies from advancing eastward?
Su Dai replied: Han Feng's words to save Wei will definitely not tell the King of Han that I am doing it for Wei. They will definitely say that I will use the troops of Qin and Han to push back Qi and Song to the east. I will take advantage of the opportunity to gather the armies of the three countries and use the fatigue after Qu Gai's defeat to go south to ask Chu to cede territory. Korea will definitely regain all the old lands it lost.
Zhang Yi's words to save Wei will definitely not tell the King of Qin that I am doing it for Wei. He will definitely say that I will use the forces of Qin and Han to resist Qi and Song in the east. I will gather the armies of the three kingdoms and take advantage of Qu Gai's exhaustion after the defeat to go south to ask Chu to cede territory. In name, it is to save the dying country, but in fact it is to attack the three rivers and return. This is the cause of the king.
You asked the King of Chu to give land to South Korea, and let Qin control the peace negotiations between the two countries. You told the King of Qin, please let Chu give land to South Korea, and the king could show off his power in the Sanchuan area. South Korea got the land from Chu without using its army.
What would Han Feng's words about sending troops to the east say to Qin?
He said that Qin captured Sanchuan without troops, attacked Chu and South Korea, and embarrassed Wei, so Wei did not dare to join Qi to the east, thus isolating Qi.
What would Zhang Yi say when he sent troops to the east?
He said that Qin and South Korea wanted to gain land but did not move. Their prestige shocked Wei, and Wei had something to rely on if it did not want to lose its relationship with Qi and Chu.
Wei changed its attitude towards Qin and South Korea and competed to serve Qi and Chu. Chu wanted to be served by Wei but did not want to give South Korea land. You allowed Qin and South Korea to get the land without troops. This is a great kindness to the two countries.
The kings of Qin and Han were threatened by Han Feng and Zhang Yi and sent troops eastward to make Wei submit. You can always accuse Qin and Han with the ticket of victory. This will cost too much to make Qin and Han like you and dislike Zhang Yi.
In the thirteenth year of King Min, King Qin Hui passed away.
In the twenty-third year, the Qi and Qin armies defeated the Chu army at Chongqiu.
In the twenty-fourth year, Qin State sent Lord Jingyang to Qi State as a hostage.
In the twenty-fifth year, Lord Jingyang was sent back to Qin.
Xue Wen, Lord Mengchang, arrived in Qin and immediately became prime minister of Qin, but soon fled Qin.
In the twenty-sixth year, Qi, South Korea, and Wei attacked Qin and stationed troops at Hanguguan.
In the twenty-eighth year, Qin gave the land beyond the river to South Korea in order to make peace, and the armies of the three countries withdrew.
In the twenty-ninth year, the people of Zhao killed their master.
The State of Qi helped the State of Zhao to destroy the State of Zhongshan.
In the thirty-sixth year of King Min's reign, King Min of Qi called himself the Eastern Emperor, and King Zhao of Qin called himself the Western Emperor.
Su Dai came to Qi from Yan State and paid homage to the King of Qi at the east gate of Zhanghua.
King Qi said: Hey, very good, sir, you are here!
Qin State sent Wei Ran to send the emperor's title. What do you think?
Su Dai replied: The king's questions to his ministers are too hasty, and the production of disasters is often not obvious.
I hope your Majesty will accept the title of Emperor, but don't prepare to proclaim yourself Emperor right away.
After the Qin State proclaims itself emperor, if the world is stable, it will not be too late for the king to proclaim himself emperor again.
Besides, it doesn't matter if you show humility when competing for the title of emperor.
If Qin becomes emperor and everyone in the world hates him, the king will not proclaim himself emperor in order to win over the people of the world. This is a great asset.
Moreover, there are two emperors in the world. Does the king think that the world respects Qi or Qin?
King Min said: Respect Qin.
Su Dai said: If we give up the title of emperor, will the world respect Qi or Qin?
King Min said: I respect and love Qi but hate Qin.
Su Dai said: Is it more beneficial for the two emperors of the East and West to form an alliance to attack Zhao, or is it more beneficial to attack the tyrant of Song?
King Min said: It would be beneficial to attack the tyrant of the Song Dynasty.
Su Dai said: The alliance is equal, but if you become emperor together with Qin, the world will only respect Qin and despise Qi. If you give up the imperial title, the world will respect Qi and hate Qin. Attacking Zhao is not as beneficial as attacking the tyrant of Song. Therefore, I hope that the king will clearly give up the imperial title to win over the people of the world, abandon the alliance, abandon Qin, and not compete with Qin. The king will use this opportunity to capture Song.
During the Warring States and Song Dynasty, Wei's Yangdi was in danger; if it occupied the west of Jishui, the area east of Zhao's Adi would be in danger; if it occupied the north of Huaihe River, the eastern part of Chu would be in danger; if it occupied Tao and Pinglu, the gates of Wei's capital Liang would be blocked.
Giving up the title of emperor and replacing it with the crusade against the tyrant of the Song Dynasty. In this way, the status of the country will be improved and its reputation will be respected by others. The countries of Yan and Chu will be forced to submit due to the situation, and all the countries in the world will not dare to disobey Qi. This is a righteous act like King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou.
Nominally respecting Qin's proclaimed emperor, and then making everyone in the world hate it, this is the so-called way to change from humbleness to nobility.
I hope your Majesty will consider it seriously.
So the state of Qi gave up the title of emperor and became king again, and the state of Qin also gave up the throne.
In the thirty-eighth year of King Min, the State of Qi attacked the State of Song.
King Zhao of Qin got angry and said: I love Song State just as much as I love Xincheng and Yangjin.
Han Nie of Qi State is my friend, but he attacks the place I love. Why?
Su Dai said to the King of Qin on behalf of Qi: Han Nie attacked Song just for the sake of the king.
The Qi State is strong, and with the help of the Song State, the Chu State will definitely panic, and the panic will lead to the west to serve the Qin State. In this way, the king will not need a single soldier, will not hurt a single soldier, and will make the Wei State cede Anyi without any trouble. This is what Han Nie asked the king.
The King of Qin said: I am worried that it is difficult to see through the Qi State. Sometimes it is united vertically, and sometimes it is connected horizontally. How to explain this?
Su Dai replied: Can the situation of all countries in the world be known to Qi?
When Qi attacked Song, it knew that to serve Qin, it should have the power of a country of ten thousand chariots to assist it. If it did not serve Qin in the west, Song would not be stable.
The white-haired lobbyists in the Central Plains are racking their brains to alienate the alliance between Qi and Qin. Among those driving westward, no one is talking about making friends with Qi; among those driving eastward, no one is talking about making friends with Qin.
Why?
Because they don't want Qi and Qin to unite.
Why are the Three Jin and Chu so smart but Qi and Qin so stupid?
The three Jin and Chu alliances must discuss attacking Qi and Qin, and the Qi and Qin alliance must plan to attack the three Jins and Chu. Please, Your Majesty, decide what to do based on this situation! King Qin said: OK!
So the state of Qi went to attack the state of Song. The king of Song fled and died in Wencheng.
The Qi State occupied Chu State's land north of the Huai River in the south, invaded the Three Jin Dynasties in the west, and planned to annex the Zhou Dynasty and establish itself as emperor.
The princes in the Surabaya area, such as the kings of Zou, Lu and other countries, all surrendered to Qi, and the princes of all countries were very afraid.
In the thirty-ninth year of King Min, the State of Qin came to attack the State of Qi and captured nine cities.
In the 40th year of King Min's reign, Yan, Qin, Chu and the three Jins conspired to attack Qi with their elite troops, and defeated the Qi army west of Jishui.
King Qi's army broke up and retreated.
General Leyi of Yan then invaded Linzi, the capital of Qi, and plundered all the treasures and ritual vessels collected by the state of Qi.
King Min fled to the state of Wei, and the king of the state of Wei opened the palace for him to live in, paid homage to him and provided him with utensils.
King Min was very arrogant, so the people of Wei came to harass him.
King Min had to leave Wei and ran to Zou and Lu. He showed an arrogant air. The kings of Zou and Lu did not accept him, so he ran to Ju again.
At this time, the state of Chu sent Nao Chi to lead troops to rescue the state of Qi, so he assisted King Min of Qi. As a result, Nao Chi actually killed Min, and together with the state of Yan, he divided the land that had been occupied by the state of Qi and the treasures plundered.
After King Min was killed, his son Fazhang changed his name and went to work as a servant in the home of Ju Taishi Jiao.
Taishi Jiao's daughter felt that Fa Zhang's appearance was extraordinary and thought that he was not an ordinary person. She loved him and often happily gave him food and clothing and had an affair with him.
After Naochi left Jucheng, the people in Jucheng and the fleeing ministers of Qi gathered together to look for King Min's son and wanted to make him king of Qi.
Fazhang was first afraid that they were going to kill him. It took a long time before he dared to say that I was the son of King Min.
So the people of Ju jointly appointed Fa Zhang to the throne, and he became King Xiang.
Because he owned the city of Ju, he announced to all parts of Qi that the new king had ascended the throne in Ju.
After King Xiang ascended the throne, he made Taishi's daughter the queen, and she was called the queen. She gave birth to a son named Jian.
Taishi Jiao said: If my daughter marries without a matchmaker, she cannot be counted as my descendant. She has tarnished our family tradition.
He never met the queen for the rest of his life.
The queen is virtuous and does not lose the etiquette of being a daughter just because her father does not see her.
King Xiang lived in Ju for five years. Tian Dan relied on Jimo's army and people to defeat the Yan army, went to Ju to welcome King Xiang, and returned to Linzi.
All the original land of Qi State was returned to Qi State.
The King of Qi granted Tian Dan the title of Lord Anping.
In the fourteenth year of King Xiang, the Qin army attacked Gangshou of Qi State.
In the nineteenth year, King Xiang died and his son Tian Jian came to the throne.
Six years after King Jian of Qi came to the throne, Qin attacked Zhao, and Qi and Chu went to rescue it.
The state of Qin planned to say: Qi and Chu come to the rescue of Zhao. If they are close to each other, we will retreat; if they are not close, we will attack them.
Zhao State had no food and asked Qi State for grain support, but Qi State refused.
Zhouzi said: It is better to agree to it so that the Qin soldiers will retreat. If you don't agree to it, the Qin soldiers will not retreat. In this way, Qin's strategy will succeed, but Qi and Chu's strategies will fail.
Moreover, the State of Zhao is a barrier to Qi and Chu, just like there are lips outside the teeth. Without the lips, the teeth will get cold.
Today the State of Zhao is destroyed, and tomorrow the disaster will come to the States of Qi and Chu.
Moreover, rescuing Zhao should be like holding a leaky urn to pour out a burnt pot.
Saving Zhao is a noble act of justice; causing Qin soldiers to retreat will show their prestige.
It is a mistake to act righteously to save a dying country and to use force to defeat the powerful Qin army. Those who do not try their best to do this but focus on sparing food and making suggestions for the country are wrong.
The king of Qi did not listen to the advice.
The Qin army defeated more than forty troops of Zhao State in Changping, and then surrounded Handan.
In the 16th year of the founding of King Qi, the Qin State destroyed the Zhou Dynasty.
The king and queen of Qi died.
In the twenty-third year of the Qin Dynasty, the State of Qin established Dongjun.
In the twenty-eighth year, the King of Qi went to Qin to pay homage, and the King of Qin hosted a banquet in Xianyang.
In thirty-five years, Qin destroyed South Korea.
In the thirty-seventh year, Qin State destroyed Zhao State.
In the thirty-eighth year, the State of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. The King of Qin found out and killed Jing Ke.
The next year, the Qin army captured the capital of Yan, and the king of Yan fled to Liaodong.
In another year, the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, and the Qin army was stationed in Lixia.
In the forty-two years, Qin State destroyed Chu State.
In the second year, he captured Dai Wangjia, killed Yan Wangxi, and destroyed the Yan Kingdom.
In the forty-fourth year of King Qi's founding, Qin attacked Qi.
The king of Qi followed the prime minister's plan to win later and led his army to surrender to Qin without fighting.
Qin captured King Jian of Qi and moved him to Gongcheng.
Finally, the state of Qi was destroyed and turned into a county.
The world was unified by Qin, and the Qin king established the title of emperor.
At first, the king and queen were virtuous, cautious in serving Qin, and had good relations with the princes. Qi was located on the eastern seaboard, and Qin attacked Jin, Yan, and Chu day and night. Facing Qin's attacks, the five countries had to seek self-rescue. Therefore, King Jian of Qi did not suffer from war for more than 40 years in his reign.
After the queen died, Hou Sheng became the prime minister of Qi. He accepted a lot of money from Qin spies and sent many guests to Qin. Qin gave them a lot of money. The guests all came back to carry out counterinsurgency activities and persuaded the king of Qi to give up the alliance and return to Qin. Qin was able to destroy the five kingdoms.
After the five kingdoms were destroyed, the Qin army finally invaded Linzi, and no one dared to resist.
King Jian of Qi surrendered and was moved to Gongcheng.
Therefore, the people of Qi complained that Wang Jian did not join forces with the princes to attack Qin early, and listened to the words of treacherous ministers and guests, which led to the destruction of the country. They made up a song and said: Where is the pine tree or the cypress tree?
Wasn't it the guest who asked Wang Jian to live in Gongcheng?
It means that he hates Wang Jian for using guests without paying attention to inspection.
Tai Shigong said: Probably Confucius liked to read the "Book of Changes" in his later years.
As a piece of knowledge, the Book of Changes predicts the future from tangible and intangible objects. The principles are very profound. Who can focus on it if he is not a wise and reasonable person who is knowledgeable about the past and the present!
Therefore, when Taishi of Zhou Dynasty made divination for Tian Jingzhong, he could make divination for ten generations later. When Tian Wan fled to Qi, Yizhong also made divination for him.
The reason why Tian Qi and Tian Chang killed the two monarchs one after another and took over the power of Qi State is not necessarily because the situation has gradually developed to this point. It may be that they are following or complying with the divination omens!
summary:
Chen Wan, son of Chen Ligong, was born with a prophecy from a Zhou diviner: his descendants would prosper in a state ruled by the Jiang clan, likely after Chen’s decline. Chen Wan’s father, Ligong, became ruler after a series of violent successions involving the murder of Duke Huan and his son by Cai conspirators. Ligong was later killed for his promiscuity, and Chen Wan, unable to claim the throne, served as an official. Fearing for his life after a prince’s murder, he fled to Qi, where Duke Huan appointed him as a minister overseeing craftsmen. A divination for his marriage foretold that his Gui descendants would thrive under the Jiang clan, rising to prominence over generations. Chen Wan changed his surname to Tian, and his lineage grew influential in Qi.

Tian Wenzi served Duke Zhuang of Qi, but his son Tian Huanzi gained favor. Tian Lizi, a doctor under Duke Jing, won popular support by using unequal measures to lend and collect grain, amassing power. After Duke Jing’s death, Tian Qi opposed the appointed heir Yan Ruzi, instead installing Yangsheng as Duke Mourning. Tian Qi became prime minister, and his son Tian Chang continued consolidating power. Tian Chang killed rivals like Jian Zhi and Duke Jian, then installed Duke Ping, returning lands to appease other states. He controlled Qi’s government, executed powerful clans, and expanded his fiefdom. His harem of over a hundred concubines bore him seventy sons. Tian Chang’s son Tian Pan succeeded him, and the Tian family dominated Qi, with descendants like Tian He eventually becoming marquises, recognized by the Zhou emperor.

Tian He’s line continued through Huan Gong and King Wei of Qi. King Wei initially neglected governance, facing invasions, but reformed after executing corrupt officials and rewarding the virtuous. He defeated Wei and Zhao, stabilizing Qi. His minister Zou Ji advised him on governance through music metaphors, and later became a marquis. King Wei’s successors, including King Xuan and King Min, expanded Qi’s influence, with King Min briefly claiming the title of Eastern Emperor. However, King Min’s arrogance led to a coalition attack by Yan, Qin, and others, resulting in his death. His son King Xiang, hidden as a servant, was restored with help from Tian Dan, who defeated Yan. King Xiang’s reign saw Qi’s recovery, but his son King Jian eventually surrendered to Qin without resistance, ending Qi’s independence. The people blamed King Jian’s reliance on corrupt advisors and Qin spies for the fall.

The historian concludes that the Tian family’s rise, from Chen Wan’s flight to Qi to their seizure of power, may have been guided by the divinations of the Zhou priest and Yizhong, fulfilling prophecies over generations.
