Jianghou Zhou Bo was a native of Peixian County.
His ancestors were from Juan County and later moved to Peixian County.
Zhou Bo made a living by weaving silkworm foil, and often played the flute and played dirges at other people's funerals. Later, he became a warrior who could draw a strong bow.
When Gaozu was first called Pei Gong and he just raised his army, Zhou Bo followed Gaozu as an attendant to attack Huling and attack Fangyu.
Fang Yu rebelled, and Zhou Bo fought with them and repelled the enemy.
Afterwards, they attacked Fengyi and attacked the Qin army east of Dang County. The army returned to Liu County and Xiao County.
Attacked Dangjun again, finally broke through and captured Xiayi. Zhou Bo was the first to scale the city wall.
Emperor Gaozu gave him the title of Fifth Doctor.
Later, they attacked the two cities of Meng and Yu and captured them all.
When attacking Zhang Han's chariot and cavalry troops, Zhou Bo made a low-level contribution.
After the Wei Dynasty was pacified, they attacked Yuanqi and Dongmin, all the way to Li County, and captured all these places.
When attacking Zhisang, Zhou Bo was the first to ascend the city.
Attacked the Qin army under Dong'a City and defeated them.
He pursued to Puyang and captured Zhencheng.
He attacked Duguan and Dingtao, attacked and captured Wanqu, and captured Shan's father's county magistrate.
They captured Linji with a night attack, attacked Shouzhang, and then moved forward to Juan County and captured it.
Attacked Qin general Li You's army at Yongqiu City.
When attacking Kaifeng, Zhou Bo arrived at the city first and made military exploits.
Later Zhang Han defeated Xiang Liang's army and killed Xiang Liang. Peigong Liu Bang and Xiang Yu led their troops eastward back to Dang County.
From the time he started raising troops in Pei County to the time he returned to Dang County, it took a total of one year and two months.
King Huai of Chu gave Duke Pei the title of Marquis of Anwu and made him the governor of Dang County.
Peigong appointed Zhou Bo to follow Peiping in the position of Huben Ling to determine the territory of Wei.
In Chengwu, he attacked the army of Dongjun Commandery and defeated them.
Attacked Qin General Wang Li's army and defeated them.
Attacking Changshe, Zhou Bo was the first to ascend the city.
Attacked Yingyang and Fengshi and cut off the crossing of the Yellow River.
Attack Zhao Ben's army north of Xixiang.
Then he went south to attack Nanyang County and defeated Wuguan and Yaoguan.
Defeated the Qin army in Lantian, marched to Xianyang, and destroyed the Qin Dynasty.
After Xiang Yu arrived in Xianyang, he named Peigong King of Han.
The title given to Zhou Bo by the King of Han was Marquis of Weiwu.
Zhou Bo followed the King of Han into Hanzhong and was appointed general.
The Han army returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties. After arriving in Qin, the King of Han gave Huaide to Zhou Bo as a food town.
He attacked Huaili and Haoji and achieved great success.
In Xianyang, he attacked Zhao Bi and Nei Shibao and made great achievements.
Attack Qixian County to the north.
Attack the armies of Zhang Ping and Yao Xian.
Go west to pacify Qian County.
He returned to the army and captured Mei County and Pinyang.
Zhang Han's army was surrounded in Feiqiu.
Defeated the army of the Xixian County Magistrate.
The army that attacked Tieba defeated him.
Attack Shanggui.
In the east. Guard the Pass in the east.
Then he turned to attack Xiang Yu.
Attack Quni and achieve superior merit.
Return to guard Aocang and pursue Xiang Yu.
After Xiang Yu's death, he took the opportunity to move east to pacify Chu Sishui and Donghai counties, occupying a total of 22 counties.
He then returned to guard Luoyang and Yueyang. The king of Han gave Zhongli to Zhou Bo and Guan Ying as a common food town for them.
Zhou Bo followed Gaozu as a general to conquer Zang Tu, King of Yan, who rebelled against the Han Dynasty, and defeated them at the gate of Yi County.
The soldiers led by Zhou Bo resisted the enemy on the carriage road and made many military exploits.
Zhou Bo was granted the title of Marquis, and Emperor Gaozu split the talisman to ensure that Zhou Bo's title would be passed down from generation to generation and would never be extinguished.
8,180 households in Jiang County were given as food towns, known as Jianghou.
Zhou Bo followed Gaozu as a general to conquer Han Wangxin who rebelled against the Han Dynasty in Dai, and surrendered Huoren County.
Then move forward to Wuquan, attack the Hu cavalry, and defeat them north of Wuquan.
Then he moved to Tongtian to attack Han Wangxin's army and defeated them.
He returned to the army and surrendered six cities in Taiyuan County.
At the foot of Jinyang City, the Hu cavalry attacked King Xin of Han, defeated them, and captured Jinyang.
Then he attacked King Xin of Han's army at Rangshi, defeated them, and chased the defeated soldiers for eighty miles.
Returning to attack the three cities in Loufan, they took advantage of the situation to attack the Hu cavalry under Pingcheng. The soldiers led by Zhou Bo resisted the enemy troops on the carriage road and gained the most military exploits.
Zhou Bo was promoted to Taiwei.
Zhou Bo attacked the rebel general Chen Xi and massacred the city in Mayi County.
The soldiers he led beheaded Chen Xi's general on horseback.
Attacked Han Wangxin, Chen Xi, and Zhao Li's troops in Loufan, defeated them, and captured Chen Xi's general Song Zui and Yanmen County Guards.
Taking advantage of the situation, he turned to attack Yunzhong County and captured the county governor, Prime Minister Ji Si and General Xun.
The seventeen counties of Yanmen County and the twelve counties of Yunzhong County were pacified.
Taking advantage of the situation, he attacked Chen Xi in Lingqiu, defeated his army, beheaded Chen Xi, and captured Chen Xi's prime minister Cheng Zong, general Chen Wu, and captain Gao Si.
Pingding Daijun nine counties.
King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled, and Zhou Bo led the troops on Fan Kuai's behalf as Prime Minister, captured Jixian, captured Lu Wan's general Da, Prime Minister Yan, County Shou Xing, Tai Wei Ruo, and Yushi doctor Shi, etc., and massacred Hundu City.
Defeated Lu Wan's rebels in Shanglan, and defeated Lu Wan's rebels in Juyang.
They pursued to the Great Wall and pacified twelve counties in Shanggu County, sixteen counties in Youbeiping County, twenty-nine counties in western and eastern Liaoning, and twenty-two counties in Yuyang County.
He followed Gaozu on the expedition and captured one prime minister and two prime ministers, three officials each with an annual salary of two thousand dan. He also defeated two armies, captured three cities, pacified five counties and seventy-nine counties, and captured one prime minister and one general.
Zhou Bo was a simple, strong, honest and loyal man. Emperor Gaozu believed that he could entrust him with important matters.
Zhou Bo didn't like literature and learning. Whenever he summoned Confucian scholars and lobbyists, he would sit facing east and ask them: Tell me quickly!
His simple young literary talent is like this.
After Zhou Bo pacified Yan, he returned to the dynasty. Gaozu had passed away, and he served Emperor Hui as a prince.
In the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, the official position of Taiwei was established and Zhou Bo was appointed as Taiwei.
Ten years later, Empress Lu died.
Lu Lu served as the general of the Han Dynasty as King Zhao, and Lu Chan served as the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty as King Lu. They controlled the political power of the Han Dynasty and wanted to overthrow the Liu family.
Zhou Bo, as a lieutenant, could not enter the military camp; Chen Ping, as a prime minister, could not handle government affairs.
So Zhou Bo and Chen Ping planned to finally annihilate the Lu family and establish Emperor Xiaowen.
The intercession on this matter is recorded in "The Chronicles of Empress Dowager Lu" and "The Chronicles of Xiaowen".
After Emperor Wen came to the throne, he appointed Zhou Bo as the right prime minister, and gave him five thousand catties of gold and ten thousand households with food. More than a month later, someone persuaded Zhou Bo: You have killed the Lu family and established King Dai as the emperor, which is powerful in the world.
You receive generous rewards and are in a distinguished position. If you are favored like this, disaster will befall you over time. Zhou Bo was afraid and felt that he was in danger, so he resigned and asked for the return of the seal.
The emperor agreed to his request.
More than a year later, Prime Minister Chen Ping passed away. The emperor appointed Zhou Bo as prime minister.
After more than ten months, the emperor said: A few days ago, I ordered all the princes to go to their fiefdoms. Some of them have not left yet. Prime Minister, you are a person I value very much. I hope you will take the lead and go first!
So he was relieved of his position as prime minister and returned to his fiefdom.
After returning to the fiefdom for more than a year, whenever the governor and lieutenants of Hedong visited Dajiang County in various counties, Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Jiang, was afraid of being killed. He often wore armor and ordered his family members to hold weapons to meet the governor and lieutenants.
Later, someone wrote a letter to accuse Zhou Bo of rebelling. The emperor handed over the matter to Tingwei, the chief officer in charge of the prison. Tingwei in turn handed the matter over to Chang'an. The prison officer in Chang'an arrested Zhou Bo for interrogation.
Zhou Bo was scared and didn't know how to answer.
The jailers gradually bullied and humiliated him.
Zhou Bo gave a thousand pieces of gold to the jailer, and the jailer wrote on the back of the wooden slip to remind him: Let the princess bear witness for you.
The princess was the daughter of Emperor Wen, and Zhou Bo's eldest son Shengzhi married her, so the jailer taught Zhou Bo to let her come out to testify.
Zhou Bo gave all the rewards he received to Empress Dowager Bo's brother Bo Zhao.
When the case came to a critical juncture, Bo Zhao interceded with Empress Dowager Bo on behalf of Zhou Bo, and the Empress Dowager also believed that there would be no rebellion.
Emperor Wen met with the Empress Dowager. The Empress Dowager grabbed the scarf and threw it at Emperor Wen, saying: It turns out that Jianghou was carrying the emperor's seal and was leading the troops in the Northern Army. He didn't rebel at that time. Now he lives in a small county. Will he rebel instead?
Emperor Wen had already seen Jianghou's confession, so he apologized to the Queen Mother and said: The jailer just found out clearly and wanted to let him out.
So he sent an envoy with a talisman to pardon Jianghou and restore his title and food.
After Jianghou was released from prison, he said: I am leading an army of millions, but how do I know the dignity of the jailer?
Jianghou returned to his fiefdom.
He died in the eleventh year of Emperor Wen's reign, and his posthumous title was Marquis Wu.
His son Katsuyuki inherited the title.
Six years later, the princess he married was at odds with him, and because he committed murder, the fiefdom was abolished.
The title was suspended for a year before Emperor Wen selected Zhou Yafu, the virtuous governor of Hanoi County, from the sons of Jianghou Zhou Bo, and named him Tiaohou to succeed Jianghou's title.
When Zhou Yafu, the Marquis of Tiao, was still serving as the governor of Hanoi County without the title of Marquis, Xu Negation looked at his prime minister and said: You will be granted the title of Marquis in three years. After eight years of being granted the title of Marquis, you will be appointed as general and prime minister. You will be in charge of the power of the country.
In nine years after this, you will starve to death.
Zhou Yafu said with a smile: My brother has inherited the title of marquis from his father. If he dies, his son should succeed him. How can I, Zhou Yafu, be granted the title of marquis?
Since I am as rich as you said, how can I say that I will starve to death?
Please give me your advice.
Xu Negation pointed at Zhou Yafu's mouth and said: "You have vertical lines on your face. This is the face of starving to death."
Three years later, his brother Jianghou Zhou Shengzhi was convicted. Emperor Wen selected a capable person from Zhou Bo's sons. Everyone recommended Yafu, so he named Yafu Tiaohou and succeeded Jianghou's title.
In the sixth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Xiongnu invaded the border.
Emperor Wen then appointed Zongzheng Liu Li as a general to garrison Ba Shang; Zhu Zihou Li as a general to garrison at Jimen; and appointed Zhou Yafu, governor of Hanoi County, as a general to garrison at Xiliu in order to guard against the Xiongnu.
The emperor personally went to Wei Lao's army.
When they arrived at the barracks of Bashang and Thorny Gate, they entered at a gallop, and everyone from the general to the subordinate officers and soldiers rode to greet them.
After arriving at the Xiliu Military Camp, the officers and soldiers were all wearing armor, swords out of armor, bows with bows drawn, and bowstrings fully drawn.
The emperor's leader came to the military camp and could not enter.
The foreword says: The Emperor is coming!
The captain of the military gate said: Our general ordered that in the army we can only obey the general's orders and not the emperor's edicts.
Soon after, the emperor arrived, but he could not enter.
So the emperor sent an envoy holding a talisman to issue an edict to the general: I want to go in to comfort the army.
Yafu then sent word to open the gate of the military camp.
The non-commissioned officer guarding the camp gate said to the emperor's chariot and horse entourage: The general has regulations that horses are not allowed to gallop in the military camp.
So the emperor tightened the reins and marched slowly.
When he arrived at the camp, General Zhou Yafu saluted with his weapon in hand and said: "Soldiers wearing armor cannot kneel and worship. Please allow me to see the emperor as a military salute."
The emperor was moved by him, and immediately became solemn, leaning on the crossbar of the cart to greet the officers and soldiers.
He sent someone to express his gratitude to Zhou Yafu and said: "The emperor is here to express his condolences to the general."
After completing the military etiquette, he left.
As soon as they came out of the camp, all the officials looked surprised.
Emperor Wen said: Ah, this is the real general!
What I saw in the Bashang and Thorny Gate military camps was like child's play. Their generals might have been attacked and captured.
As for Yafu, how could he possibly violate him?
Praise him for a long time.
After more than a month, all three armies were withdrawn.
Emperor Wen granted Zhou Yafu the official position of lieutenant.
When Emperor Wen was about to die, he warned the prince: If a critical situation occurs, Zhou Yafu will really take on the important responsibility of leading the army.
After Emperor Wen died, Emperor Jing appointed Zhou Yafu as the Chariot and Cavalry General.
In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Wu, Chu and other places rebelled.
Zhou Yafu was promoted from lieutenant to Taiwei and led troops to attack the Wu and Chu rebels.
So Zhou Yafu personally asked the emperor for instructions and said: The Chu soldiers are brave and agile, and it will be difficult for us to win against them.
I hope to give up Liang Guo first and let them attack. We will cut off their food routes so that we can subdue them.
Emperor Jing agreed with this opinion.
After Taiwei Zhou Yafu gathered all the armies to Xingyang, the rebels of Wu State were attacking Liang State. Liang State was in a critical situation and asked for help.
But the Taiwei led his troops to the northeast and ran to Changyi. They could not defend themselves in deep ditches and high fortresses.
Liang Guo sent envoys to ask for help from the Taiwei every day, but the Taiwei believed that it would be beneficial to hold on and refused to rescue him.
Liang Guo sent a letter to report to Emperor Jing, who immediately sent an envoy to order the Taiwei to rescue Liang.
The Taiwei did not obey the emperor's order and held the fort without sending troops. Instead, he sent light cavalry led by Gong Gaohou and others to cut off the food routes to the rear of the Wu and Chu rebels.
The Wu army lacked food and the soldiers were hungry. They challenged them many times, but the Han army never came out.
At night, the Han army was frightened in the camp. The soldiers attacked and disturbed each other, and even caused trouble in the Taiwei's tent.
But the Taiwei never lay still.
Soon, stability was restored.
Later, the Wu army rushed towards the southeast corner of the Han army camp. The Taiwei asked people to pay attention to the northwest.
Then the elite soldiers of Wu State indeed rushed to the northwest, but they could not invade.
Wu soldiers were already hungry, so they retreated.
The Taiwei sent elite soldiers to pursue and defeated the Wu army.
Wu Wangbi abandoned his army and fled with thousands of strong soldiers to Dantu in the south of the Yangtze River to protect himself.
The Han soldiers took advantage of the victory and pursued them, completely captured the rebels, made them surrender, and offered a reward of a thousand gold for the king of Wu's head.
After more than a month, some people from Yue beheaded King Wu and reported it.
The two sides only had three months to attack and defend, and the Wu and Chu rebellions were defeated and put down.
Then the generals realized that the Taiwei's strategy was correct.
But because of this counterinsurgency. However, King Xiao of Liang had a grudge against the Taiwei.
After Zhou Yafu returned to the court, the imperial court re-established Taiwei officials, Zhou Yafu was promoted to prime minister, and Emperor Jing valued him very much.
Later, Emperor Jing deposed Prince Li. Prime Minister Zhou Yafu tried his best to argue but failed to dissuade him.
Emperor Jing distanced himself from him.
Every time King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing for an audience, he often told the Queen Mother about Zhou Yafu's shortcomings.
One day, Queen Mother Dou said: The queen's brother Wang Xin can be made a marquis.
Emperor Jing declined and said: At first, the late Emperor Nanpihou and Zhangwuhou did not make them marquises. They waited until I came to the throne to make them marquises.
It is not the time to make Wang Xin a marquis.
Empress Dowager Dou said: The monarchs all act according to the situation at that time.
When my brother Dou Changjun was alive, he could not be granted the title of marquis. After his death, his son Peng Zu was granted the title of marquis instead. I regret this very much. Your Majesty, please make Wang Xin a marquis as soon as possible!
Emperor Jing said: This matter needs to be discussed with the Prime Minister.
Emperor Jing discussed with the prime minister, and Zhou Yafu said: Emperor Gao had stipulated that people who were not from the Liu family could not be crowned kings, and people who had not made meritorious deeds could not be crowned marquis. Anyone who did not abide by this rule could be attacked by everyone in the world.
Although Wang Xin is the elder brother of the queen, he has no meritorious service. Making him a marquis is against the Emperor Gaozu's protocol.
Emperor Jing was speechless after hearing this and had to give up.
Later, the Xiongnu king Wei Xulu and five others surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Jing wanted to make them marquis to encourage those who came after them.
Prime Minister Zhou Yafu said: A few of them betrayed their monarch and surrendered to Your Majesty. If Your Majesty makes them marquis, how can you blame the unruly ministers?
Emperor Jing said: The Prime Minister's opinion cannot be adopted.
So Wei Xulu and others were all made marquises.
Zhou Yafu therefore claimed to be ill and retired to his home.
In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Zhou Yafu was dismissed as prime minister due to illness.
Soon, Emperor Jing summoned Tiaohou in the palace and rewarded him with food and wine.
There was only a large piece of meat on the table, no chopped meat, and no chopsticks.
Tiao Hou was dissatisfied, turned around and asked the official in charge of the banquet to bring chopsticks.
Emperor Jing smiled when he saw it and said, "Can't these meet your needs?"
Tiaohou took off his hat to apologize.
The emperor stood up, and Tiao Hou took the opportunity to retreat quickly.
Emperor Jing watched him go out. Said: People like this who show dissatisfaction when encountering things cannot be the servants of the young master!
Soon after, Tiaohou's son bought five hundred pieces of armor and shields for his father from a worker who specialized in making household supplies.
The moving workers were very tired, but they were not paid.
When the employees found out that he secretly bought the utensils for the emperor, they became angry and sued Zhou Yafu's son to rebel. Naturally, the matter involved Marquis Tiao.
The employee's petition was submitted to Emperor Jing, who handed it over to the officials for investigation.
The officials questioned Tiaohou one by one according to the contents of the document, but Tiaohou refused to answer.
Emperor Jing scolded him and said, "I won't use you anymore."
And ordered Zhou Yafu to be handed over to Tingwei.
Tingwei asked: "Do you want to rebel?"
Zhou Yafu said: The utensils I bought are all for burial. How can I say that I want to rebel?
The jailer said: Even if you don't rebel above ground, you should go underground to rebel!
The jailer's persecution became more and more intense.
At first, when the jailer arrested Tiao Hou, Tiao Hou wanted to commit suicide, but his wife stopped him. Therefore, he did not die and went to Tingwei's prison.
Zhou Yafu didn't eat for five days, vomited blood and died.
His fiefdom was removed.
Zhou Yafu's title was suspended for a year, so Emperor Jing changed the title of Zhou Jian, another son of Jianghou Zhou Bo, to Pingquhou, and succeeded Jianghou's title.
Zhou Jian died after reigning for 19 years, and his posthumous title was Gonghou.
His son Jiande succeeded him as marquis. Thirteen years later, Zhou Jiande was appointed as the prince's tutor.
Due to the poor quality of the gold offered as an acolyte, he was found guilty in the fifth year of Yuanding and his fiefdom was abolished.
Tiao Hou Zhou Yafu really starved to death.
After his death, Emperor Jing granted Wang Xin the title of Gaihou.
Tai Shigong said: When Jiang Hou Zhou Bo was a commoner, he was a rough and simple man, and his talents were no more than mediocre.
When he followed Gao Zu to bring peace to the world, he took up the position of general. The Lu family wanted to rebel and cause rebellion. Zhou Bo saved the country from crisis and restored the court to normal.
How can even wise men like Yi Yin and Duke Zhou surpass him?
Zhou Yafu always maintained dignity and perseverance in his military use. How could a famous general like Sima Ranju surpass him?
It's a pity that he was complacent but not open-minded to learn. He was able to observe moral integrity but did not know how to be respectful. In the end, he ended up in embarrassment. How sad!
summary:
Zhou Bo, a native of Peixian County, began his career as a weaver and funeral musician before becoming a warrior. He followed Liu Bang (later Emperor Gaozu) from the early days of his uprising, participating in numerous battles against the Qin dynasty and other forces. Zhou Bo distinguished himself in combat, often being the first to scale city walls, and was granted titles and rewards, including the Marquis of Weiwu and later the Marquis of Jiang, with a fief of 8,180 households. He continued to serve as a general under Gaozu, suppressing rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Lu Wan, pacifying many counties and capturing numerous enemy officials. Zhou Bo was known for his simplicity, strength, and loyalty, though he had little regard for scholarly learning.

After Gaozu's death, Zhou Bo served Emperor Hui as a prince and later as Taiwei. Following Empress Lu's death, the Lu family attempted to seize power. Zhou Bo, alongside Chen Ping, plotted to annihilate the Lu clan and established Emperor Wen. For this, he was appointed Right Prime Minister and given generous rewards. However, fearing his own power, he resigned and returned to his fief. Later, he was falsely accused of rebellion, imprisoned, and humiliated by jailers. He was eventually released after his daughter (the emperor's daughter-in-law) and Empress Dowager Bo interceded. He died in the eleventh year of Emperor Wen's reign, posthumously titled Marquis Wu.

Zhou Bo's son Zhou Shengzhi inherited the title but lost it due to murder. Emperor Wen then selected Zhou Yafu, another son, as Marquis of Tiao. Xu Negation predicted Zhou Yafu would be a marquis, general, and prime minister but would starve to death. Zhou Yafu became a general, famously commanding the Xiliu camp with strict discipline, impressing Emperor Wen. During the Rebellion of the Seven States, he served as Taiwei, successfully defeating Wu and Chu by cutting off their food supplies, though this earned him the enmity of King Xiao of Liang. He later became prime minister but fell out of favor with Emperor Jing over disputes regarding the appointment of marquises, including opposing the enfeoffment of the queen's brother Wang Xin and Xiongnu defectors.

Zhou Yafu was eventually dismissed as prime minister. After a banquet where he showed dissatisfaction with the lack of chopsticks, Emperor Jing viewed him as unfit for service. His son's purchase of burial armor led to accusations of rebellion. Zhou Yafu was imprisoned, refused to eat for five days, and died of vomiting blood. His fief was abolished. Sima Qian commented that while Zhou Bo saved the state from crisis, Zhou Yafu, despite his military dignity, lacked humility and met a tragic end.

translation:
King Jing Liu Jia is from the Liu clan, but it is not known which branch of the Liu clan he belongs to. When the trouble first broke out, it was the first year of the Han Dynasty.
The King of Han returned from Hanzhong to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, appointed Liu Jia as general, and asked him to pacify the Sedi, and then followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu from the east.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han was defeated at Chenggao. He crossed the Yellow River north and got the troops of Zhang Er and Han Xin. They stationed themselves in Xiuwu. They dug deep trenches and built high forts. He sent Liu Jia to lead two armies and hundreds of cavalry to cross Baima Jin and enter the Chu land. They burned the grain and grass stored there and destroyed the industry there so that they could not supply King Xiang with military grain.
Soon the Chu army attacked Liu Jia. Liu Jia always held fast to the camp and maintained a mutual dependence with Peng Yue.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty pursued Xiang Yu to Guling and sent Liu Jianan to cross the Huai River to surround Shouchun.
Liu Jia arrived soon and sent people to look for opportunities to recruit Zhou Yin, the great Sima of Chu.
Zhou Yin betrayed King Xiang and helped Liu Jia capture Jiujiang. The army of King Wu Yingbu met at Gaixia and jointly attacked Xiang Yu.
The king of Han then Liu Jia led the Jiujiang army and together with Taiwei Lu Wan, attacked Linjiang Wang Gongwei to the southwest.
After Wei Gong died, Linjiang was renamed Nanjun.
In the spring of the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, the Han King Liu Bang met with the princes in Chen County, deposed the Chu King Han Xin, and imprisoned him. His territory was divided into two countries.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu's son was young, had few brothers, and had no talents. He wanted to make a member of the same family the king to control the world, so he issued an edict saying: General Liu Jia has military exploits, and he should select the disciples of the Liu family who have military exploits to be crowned king.
All the ministers said: Liu Jia should be made King of Jing, commanding fifty-two cities in the east of Huaihe; Liu Jiao, Gaozu's younger brother, should be made King of Chu, commanding thirty-six cities in the west.
Liu Bang then appointed his son Liu Fei as King of Qi.
Only then did the Liu brothers begin to be crowned kings.
In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and went east to attack Jingdi.
Liu Jia, king of Jing, fought with him but failed to win. He fled to Fuling and was killed by Yingbu's army.
Gaozu personally defeated Yingbu.
In the twelfth year, Peihou Liu Bi was named King of Wu and ruled over the former homeland of King Jing.
King Liu Ze of Yan was a distant relative of the Liu family.
In the third year of Emperor Gaodi's reign, Liu Ze was appointed as a doctor.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaodi's reign, Liu Ze used his position as a general to attack Chen Xi, captured the enemy general Wang Huang, and was granted the title of Marquis of Yingling.
During the reign of Emperor Gao, Tian Sheng, a native of Qi, was traveling abroad and lacked travel funds, so he asked Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, for help by offering suggestions.
Liu Ze was very happy and used 200 kilograms of gold to celebrate Tian Sheng's birthday.
After Tian Sheng got the money, he immediately returned to Qi.
The next year, Liu Ze sent someone to tell Tian Sheng: "Don't you want to interact with me anymore?"
When Tian Sheng came to Chang'an, he did not go to see Liu Ze. Instead, he borrowed a large mansion and asked his son to see and serve Zhang Ziqing, the great emissary who was favored by Empress Lu.
A few months later, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to his home as a guest. Zhang Qing personally prepared a banquet.
Zhang Qing agreed to go.
Tian Sheng hung up luxurious curtains and arranged exquisite utensils, just like a prince.
Zhang Qing was surprised when he saw it.
While the wine was in full swing, Tian Sheng asked the left and right to step back and persuaded Zhang Qing: "I have seen more than a hundred residences of princes and kings, all of whom were meritorious officials during the reign of Emperor Gaozu."
Now the Lu family has always helped Gaozu complete the great cause of unifying the world. His contribution is very great, and he is honored by his relative the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother was old and the Lu clan was weak. The Queen Mother wanted to make Lu Chan the king and the king of the vassals on behalf of the land.
The Queen Mother wants to speak out about this matter seriously, but she is afraid that the ministers will not agree.
Now that you are most favored by the Queen Mother and respected by the ministers, why not politely persuade the ministers to report this matter to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother will definitely be happy.
After Zhu Lu is crowned king, all the princes will also be yours.
The Queen Mother wants to do this in her heart, but you are a minister. If you don't propose it quickly, I'm afraid disaster will befall you.
Zhang Qing agreed very much with this, so he politely persuaded the minister to report the matter to the Queen Mother.
When the Queen Mother went to court, she asked the ministers about this matter.
The ministers petitioned to establish Lu Chan as King Lu.
The Queen Mother gave Zhang Qing a thousand catties of gold, and Zhang Qing gave half of it to Tian Sheng.
Tian Sheng did not accept the gift, and took the opportunity to persuade Zhang Qing: "Lü Chan was crowned king, but the ministers were not completely convinced."
Now the Marquis of Yingling, Liu Ze, is a member of the Liu clan and serves as a general. He is the only one who is still dissatisfied.
Now you report to the Queen Mother and designate more than a dozen counties to make him king. He will get the throne and leave happily. The throne of the Lu family will be more consolidated.
Zhang Qing went to the palace to report the matter, and the Queen Mother thought it was right.
So Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was granted the title of King Langxie.
King Langxie and Tian Sheng went to the fiefdom.
Tian Sheng advised Liu Ze to leave quickly and not to stay.
As soon as they left Hangu Pass, the Queen Mother indeed sent people to chase and stop them, but Liu Ze had already left the pass, so the pursuers had to go back.
After the death of the Queen Mother, Langxie King Liu Ze said: The emperor is young, Zhu Lu controls the government, and the Liu family is lonely and weak.
So he led the army and planned with Qi King Liu Xiang to march westward, intending to kill the Lu family.
When he arrived in Liangdi, he heard that the imperial court had sent General Guan Ying to garrison troops in Xingyang, so Liu Ze returned to strengthen the defense of his western border, and then quickly rushed to Chang'an.
King Dai also happened to arrive from Dai.
The generals, ministers and King Langxie jointly supported King Dai as the emperor.
The emperor then moved Liu Ze to the title of King of Yan, returned Langxie to King Qi, and restored King Qi's original territory.
Liu Ze died in his second year as King of Yan, and his posthumous title was King Jing.
The throne was passed to his son Liu Jia, who became King Kang.
When the throne passed to Liu Ze's grandson Liu Dingguo, he committed adultery with his father, King Kang's concubine, and gave birth to a boy.
He also took his younger brother's wife as his concubine.
He also committed adultery with his three daughters.
Liu Dingguo planned to kill the Ying people, the magistrate of Feiru County. The Ying people and others reported Liu Dingguo's crimes. Liu Dingguo sent envoys to report, arrest and kill the Ying people under the pretext of other laws to silence him.
In the second year of Yuanshuo, the brothers of the Ying people once again wrote to report Liu Dingguo's ulterior scandal, and Dingguo's crimes were exposed.
The emperor ordered the ministers to discuss the case, and the ministers all commented: "Liu Dingguo acted like a beast, corrupted human relations, violated the laws of nature, and should be executed for his crime."
The emperor granted permission.
Liu Dingguo committed suicide, the feudal state was abolished and changed to a county.
Tai Shigong said: King Jing was granted the title of king because the Han Dynasty had just been established and the world had not yet been completely unified. Therefore, although Liu Jia was a distant relative of the Liu family, he was granted the title of king for his military exploits and held a powerful position between the Jiang and Huaihe Rivers.
Liu Ze was named king because he used power and intrigue to arouse the Lu family, so that Liu Ze could be king in the south for three generations.
Isn't it wonderful and great that things have been interfering with each other from the beginning!
summary:
King Jing Liu Jia was a member of the Liu clan, though his specific branch is unknown. During the early Han Dynasty, he served as a general under the King of Han, pacifying territories and joining campaigns against Xiang Yu. In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, after the King of Han’s defeat at Chenggao, Liu Jia crossed the Yellow River into Chu territory, burning grain supplies and disrupting enemy logistics. He held his position against Chu attacks, coordinating with Peng Yue. By the fifth year, Liu Jia crossed the Huai River, recruited Chu’s Grand Sima Zhou Yin, who betrayed Xiang Yu, and captured Jiujiang. He then joined King Yingbu at Gaixia to attack Xiang Yu. Later, Liu Jia led the Jiujiang army with Taiwei Lu Wan against Linjiang King Gongwei, who died, leading to the renaming of Linjiang to Nanjun.

In the sixth year, Emperor Gaozu deposed the Chu King Han Xin and divided his territory. Seeking to install family members as kings, Gaozu appointed Liu Jia as King of Jing, commanding fifty-two cities east of the Huai, while his brother Liu Jiao became King of Chu. Liu Jia was killed in battle against the rebellious King Yingbu in the eleventh year. His territory later passed to Liu Bi, King of Wu.

King Liu Ze of Yan, a distant Liu relative, began as a doctor and later became Marquis of Yingling for capturing an enemy general. During Empress Lu’s reign, Tian Sheng, a Qi native, advised Liu Ze to gain favor by supporting the Lu clan’s rise. Through Zhang Qing, a favored emissary, Tian Sheng persuaded the court to make Lu Chan king, then proposed making Liu Ze a king to secure Lu power. Liu Ze was thus made King of Langxie. After Empress Lu’s death, Liu Ze allied with Qi King Liu Xiang to oppose the Lu clan, eventually supporting King Dai as emperor. He was then made King of Yan, dying in his second year. His descendants included his son Liu Jia and grandson Liu Dingguo, who committed heinous crimes—adultery with relatives and murder—leading to his suicide and the abolition of his state.

Tai Shigong noted that Liu Jia was made king for his military exploits during the Han’s early instability, while Liu Ze gained his title through political maneuvering, enabling his line to rule for three generations.

translation:
Xiao Xiangguo Xiao He was born in Fengyi, Peixian County.
His knowledge of the law was unparalleled, and he was an official under the magistrate of Peixian County.
When the great ancestor Liu Bang was still a commoner, Xiao He relied on his authority as an official to protect him many times.
Liu Bang became the chief of the pavilion, and Xiao He often helped him.
Liu Bang went to Xianyang to serve as an official. All the officials gave him three hundred coins, but Xiao He gave him five hundred coins.
When the censor of the Qin Dynasty went to Sishui County to supervise the work of the county, Xiao He followed his subordinate officials and always handled things in an orderly and clear manner.
Xiao He then took on the job of being the historian of Sishui County, and ranked first in the official assessment.
The censor of the Qin Dynasty planned to enter the court to make suggestions to recruit Xiao He, but Xiao He repeatedly declined and refused to be transferred.
When the great ancestor Liu Bang rose up and became Pei Gong, Xiao He often served as his assistant to supervise the affairs.
When Pei Gong entered Xianyang, the generals rushed to the Qin Dynasty's treasury to collect gold and silk property. Only Xiao He entered the palace first to collect legal documents, geographical atlases, household registration files and other documents and materials in charge of the Qin Dynasty's prime ministers and censors, and treasured them.
Pei Gong became the queen of Han Dynasty and appointed Xiao He as prime minister.
Xiang Yu and the princes' troops entered Xianyang, slaughtered and burned them, and then left.
The reason why the King of Han was able to have a detailed understanding of the world's dangerous fortresses, the number of families and populations, the strength and weakness of various places, the sufferings of the people, etc. was all because Xiao He had completely obtained the maps, books and other materials of the Qin Dynasty.
Xiao He recommended Han Xin to the King of Han, and the King of Han appointed Han Xin as general.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".
The King of Han led his troops eastward and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. Xiao He stayed behind as prime minister to govern Bashu, pacify the people, issue decrees, and provide food and fodder for the army.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han and other princes attacked the Chu army. Xiao He guarded Guanzhong, served the prince, and governed Yueyang.
When formulating laws and regulations, establishing ancestral temples, communities, palaces, and counties, Xiao He would report everything he did to the King of Han in advance and only implement it with the King of Han's approval. If it was too late to report to the King of Han, he would handle certain matters as appropriate and report to him again when the King of Han came back.
Xiao He managed the registered population in Guanzhong and collected grain and grass to transport to the army at the front. Large numbers of soldiers fled from the Han army many times, so Xiao He often recruited soldiers from Guanzhong to make up for the shortfalls in the army.
Therefore, the King of Han specially appointed Xiao He to handle the political affairs in Guanzhong.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, the army of the King of Han and Xiang Yu's army faced off between Jingxian and Suocheng. The King of Han sent envoys many times to express condolences to Prime Minister Xiao He.
A man named Bao Sheng said to Xiao He: The King of Han is living in the open air on the front line, but he has sent envoys to comfort you many times. This is because he doubts your intentions.
For your sake, it is better to send all your descendants and brothers who are capable of fighting to serve in the military camp. The King of Han will definitely trust you more.
So Xiao He followed his plan, and the king of Han was indeed very happy.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu was eliminated and the world was pacified, so he was rewarded based on his merits.
Due to the competition among officials for more than a year, the credit cannot be determined.
Emperor Gaozu believed that Xiao He's contribution was the most outstanding, so he made him Marquis of Fou and gave him the most food.
The heroes all said: We wore armor, held weapons in hand, and participated in the battle in person. Some of us had experienced hundreds of battles, and some of us had fought for ten rounds. We captured cities and seized territory, and we all made military exploits of varying sizes.
Now Xiao He has no such great achievements. He just writes and talks, does not participate in battles, and the rewards are higher than those of us. Why is this?
Emperor Gao said: Do you know how to hunt?
The ministers replied: I know how to hunt. Emperor Gao asked again: Do you know about hunting dogs?
The ministers said: I know.
Emperor Gaodi said: When hunting, it is the hunting dogs who chase the wild animals, but it is the hunters who find the traces of wild beasts and point out where the wild beasts are.
Nowadays, everyone can only catch wild animals. This kind of credit is like the credit of hounds in the hunting process.
As for Xiao He, he was the one who discovered the traces of wild beasts and pointed out the hunting target. His contribution was just like the contribution of the hunter in the hunting process.
Besides, you are only following me individually, not more than two or three people from a family.
Xiao He, on the other hand, asked dozens of people from his own clan to join me in conquering the world. The credit cannot be forgotten.
None of the ministers dared to raise any objections.
All the princes had been rewarded, and when it came time to comment on their rankings to Emperor Gaozu, all the officials said: Pingyang Marquis Cao Shen suffered seventy wounds, attacked the city and captured the land, and made the most contributions, so he should be ranked first.
Emperor Gaozu had already wronged the heroes and rewarded Xiao He more. When it came to ranking, he did not refute everyone, but he still wanted to rank Xiao He first.
E Qianqiu, the Marquis of Guannei, said: The opinions of the ministers are wrong.
Although Cao Shen had the merit of fighting in various places and seizing territory, this was only a temporary matter.
The king had been in a stalemate with the Chu army for five years. He often lost his troops, his soldiers fled, and he escaped alone several times.
However, Xiao He often sent troops from Guanzhong to replenish the front line. These were not ordered by the emperor. When tens of thousands of soldiers went to the front line, it was the king's most critical moment. This has happened many times.
The Han army and the Chu army had been fighting against each other in Xingyang for several years. There was no existing rations in the army. Xiao He transported food by carriage and ship from Guanzhong, so the army's food supply was never lacking.
Although Your Majesty has lost the area east of Mount Laoshan many times, Xiao He has always preserved Guanzhong and waited for His Majesty. This is an immortal feat.
Even if there were not hundreds of people like Cao Shen now, what would be the loss to the Han Dynasty?
Even if the Han Dynasty obtained these people, they would not necessarily be able to survive.
How can one's temporary achievements be overridden by eternal merits?
Xiao He should be ranked first, followed by Cao Shen. Gaozu said: OK.
So Xiao He was determined to be the first, and he was specially allowed to bring a sword and wear shoes to the palace, and he could walk quickly without following etiquette when going to court.
Emperor Gaozu said: I heard that recommending talented people will receive high rewards.
Although Xiao He's contribution was very high, it became even more prominent after being commended by E Jun.
So based on the original title of Marquis of Guannei, E Jun was granted the title of Marquis of Anping.
On that day, more than ten people including Xiao He, his father, his son and his brothers were granted food fiefs.
Later, Xiao He was granted the title of two thousand households. This was because when Gaozu went to serve in Xianyang, Xiao He gave him an extra two hundred coins.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled, and Gaozu personally led his army to Handan.
Before the suppression of the rebellion was over, Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, rebelled again in Guanzhong. Empress Lu adopted Xiao He's strategy and killed the Marquis of Huaiyin. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".
Emperor Gaozu had already heard that the Marquis of Huaiyin had been killed, so he sent an envoy to worship Prime Minister Xiao He as the Prime Minister, granted five thousand households, and ordered 500 soldiers and a captain to serve as the Prime Minister's bodyguard.
Many people came to congratulate him, but Zhao Ping expressed his condolences.
Zhao Pingyuan was the Marquis of Dongling in the Qin Dynasty.
After the fall of the Qin Dynasty, he became a commoner, his family was poor, and he grew melons in the east of Chang'an City. The melons he planted tasted sweet, so people in society called them "Aventurine melons", which was named after Zhao Ping's title.
Zhao Ping said to the Prime Minister Xiao He: The disaster began from now on.
Your Majesty is out in the cold weather, and your troops are outside, but you stay in the middle of the court and are not in danger of war. Instead, you increase your fiefdom and set up guards. This is because the Marquis of Huaiyin has just rebelled in the capital and has doubts about your heart.
The purpose of setting up a guard to protect you is not to favor you. I hope that you will refuse the reward and donate all your property and assets to the army. Then the emperor will be happy.
Xiao Xiangguo followed his plan. Emperor Gao was indeed very happy.
In the autumn of the twelfth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu rebelled. Gaozu personally led an army to conquer him and sent people many times to ask what Xiao Xiangguo was doing.
Because the emperor was in the army, Xiao Xiangguo comforted and encouraged the people in the rear and donated all his wealth to the army, just like when he attacked Chen Xi.
A retainer advised Xiao Xiangguo: The day when your clan will be exterminated is not far away.
You are in the prime minister's position and have the highest number of merits. Can you add more merits?
You won the hearts of the people when you first entered Guanzhong. It has been more than ten years since the people have attached themselves to you. You are still so diligent in your work, have a harmonious relationship with the people, and are loved.
The reason why the emperor has repeatedly asked about your situation is that he is afraid that you will shock Guanzhong.
Now why don't you buy more land, use low prices, borrow money, etc. to ruin your reputation?
In this way, the emperor's heart will be at peace.
So Xiao Xiangguo followed his plan, and Gaozu was very happy.
When Emperor Gaozu returned from conquering the Taibu army, the people blocked the road and wrote a letter saying that the prime minister had forcibly bought a large number of people's fields and houses at low prices.
Emperor Gaozu returned to the capital and met with the Prime Minister.
Emperor Gaozu smiled and said: You, the prime minister, are so beneficial to the people!
Emperor Gaozu handed all the people's petitions to the Prime Minister and said: "You can apologize to the people yourself."
The Prime Minister took this opportunity to ask for orders and said: The land in Chang'an is narrow, and there are many open spaces in Shanglin Garden, which have been abandoned and deserted. I hope that the people can go in to cultivate and harvest grain, leaving the straw as feed for animals.
Emperor Gaozu was furious and said: Prime Minister, you accepted a large amount of property from merchants, and then requested for them to occupy my Shanglin Garden!
So he handed Xiang Guo over to Tingwei and imprisoned him in shackles.
A few days later, when a guard surnamed Wang was serving Emperor Gaozu, he came forward and asked: What heinous crime did the Prime Minister commit, and your Majesty detained him so harshly?
Emperor Gaozu said: I heard that when Li Si assisted Qin Shihuang, any achievements he made were attributed to the Lord, and any mistakes he made were his own responsibility.
Now the Prime Minister accepts a large amount of money from profiteers and asks them to occupy my garden and forest in order to please the people, so he is handcuffed and punished.
Wang Weiwei said: Within the scope of his duties, if it is beneficial to the people and he pleads for them, this is indeed the prime minister's duty. How can your majesty suspect that the prime minister accepts money from businessmen!
Moreover, Your Majesty resisted the Chu army for several years. When Chen Xun and Yingbu rebelled, Your Majesty personally led troops to quell the rebellion. At that time, the Prime Minister stayed in Guanzhong, and he only moved a foot, so the territory west of Hangu Pass would no longer belong to Your Majesty.
Didn’t the Prime Minister take advantage of this opportunity to benefit himself, but now he is coveting the money of businessmen?
Besides, Qin Shihuang lost the world because he couldn't hear his own faults. How could Li Si share his faults and be worthy of imitation?
Why does Your Majesty doubt the Prime Minister to such a shallow level!
Gaozu was not very happy after hearing this.
On the same day, Gaozu sent someone to pardon and release the prime minister.
The Prime Minister was old and always humble and cautious. When he came to see Gao Zu, he walked barefoot to apologize.
Emperor Gaozu said: Forget it, Prime Minister!
The prime minister asked for a garden for the people, but I refused. I am just a monarch like Jie and Zhou, and you are a wise prime minister.
The reason why I put you in chains is to let the people know my fault.
Xiao He and Cao Shen had never been on good terms with each other. When Xiao He was seriously ill, Emperor Xiaohui personally went to check on Xiang Guo's condition and asked by the way: "If you pass away, who can replace you?"
Xiao He replied: There is no one who understands his subordinates better than the monarch.
Emperor Xiaohui said: How about Cao Shen?
Xiao He kowtowed and said: Your Majesty has found a suitable candidate!
Even if I die, I will have no regrets!
Xiao He's purchase of land and housing must be in a poor and remote area, and he did not build a house with low walls when building his home.
He said: If my descendants are worthy, they can learn from my frugality; if their descendants are not worthy, they can avoid being taken away by powerful people.
In the second year of Xiaohui's reign, Prime Minister Xiao He passed away, and his posthumous title was Wen Zhonghou.
There were four generations of Xiao He's descendants who lost the title of marquis due to crimes. Every time the title was cut off, the emperor always sought Xiao He's descendants again and renewed their titles as Marquis of Fou. No one among the heroes could compare with him.
Tai Shigong said: Prime Minister Xiao He was just a small civilian official in the Qin Dynasty. He was ordinary and had no amazing achievements.
When the Han Dynasty prospered, relying on the emperor's remaining glory, Xiao He strictly adhered to his duties. Based on the fact that the people hated the harsh laws of the Qin Dynasty, he followed the trend of history and updated them.
Han Xin, Ying Bu, etc. have all been killed, but Xiao He's achievements are even more brilliant.
His status was the highest among the officials, and his reputation extended to later generations. He could compete with Hong Yao, San Yisheng and others.
summary:
Xiao He, born in Fengyi, Peixian County, was a legal expert and official under the county magistrate. He protected Liu Bang when Liu Bang was a commoner and later as a pavilion chief. When Liu Bang served in Xianyang, Xiao He gave him five hundred coins, more than others. Xiao He became historian of Sishui County, ranking first in assessments, but declined a transfer recommended by a Qin censor.

When Liu Bang became Pei Gong, Xiao He assisted him. After entering Xianyang, while others seized treasure, Xiao He collected Qin legal documents, maps, and household records. This allowed Liu Bang to understand the realm's geography and population. Xiao He recommended Han Xin as general. As prime minister, he governed Bashu and Guanzhong, managing laws, temples, and supplies. He reported to Liu Bang or acted as needed, recruiting soldiers to replenish the army.

In the third year of Han, Liu Bang sent envoys to Xiao He, suspecting him. Bao Sheng advised Xiao He to send his family to the army, which Liu Bang approved. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang ranked Xiao He first among heroes, comparing him to a hunter versus hounds, and citing Xiao He's clan contributions. E Qianqiu supported this, noting Xiao He's consistent support during crises. Xiao He was ranked first, allowed special court privileges, and granted fiefs.

During Chen Xi's rebellion, Xiao He helped Empress Lu kill Han Xin. Liu Bang rewarded him with guards, but Zhao Ping warned this indicated suspicion. Xiao He refused the reward and donated to the army, pleasing Liu Bang. During Yingbu's rebellion, a retainer advised Xiao He to ruin his reputation by buying land cheaply to ease Liu Bang's fears. Xiao He complied, and Liu Bang was happy. Later, Liu Bang imprisoned Xiao He for requesting Shanglin Garden for the people, but a guard argued Xiao He's duty, and Liu Bang released him.

Xiao He and Cao Shen were not on good terms, but on his deathbed, Xiao He recommended Cao Shen as his successor. Xiao He bought land in poor areas and built simple homes to teach frugality. He died in the second year of Xiaohui's reign, posthumously named Wenzhong Hou. His descendants lost the title four times but were reinstated, unmatched among heroes. Sima Qian noted Xiao He's rise from a minor official to a prominent figure, adapting laws to people's needs and achieving lasting fame.

translation:
The ancestors of the Zhao family and the Qin people have the same ancestor.
When it was passed to Zhongyan, he became the person who drove horses and chariots for Emperor Taiwu of the Shang Dynasty.
His descendant Feilian had two sons. One son was named Eilai and served King Zhou. He was later killed by the Zhou people. His descendants were the Ying Qin family.
Erlai's younger brother was named Ji Sheng, and his descendants were the Zhao people.
Ji Sheng gave birth to Meng Zeng.
Meng Zeng was favored by King Zhou Cheng, and this was Zhai Gaolang.
Gaolang begat Hengfu, and Hengfu begat Zaofu.
Zaofu was favored by King Mu of Zhou.
Cepheus selected eight horses and presented them to King Mu along with the famous horses such as Robber, Hualiu, and Luer obtained in Taolin.
King Mu asked Zaofu to drive his chariot to the west for inspection. He met the Queen Mother of the West and was so happy that he forgot to go back.
Soon, King Xu Yan launched a rebellion. King Mu rode a carriage and traveled thousands of miles a day to attack King Xu Yan and completely defeat him.
So he gave the city of Zhao to Zaofu, and he became the Zhao family from then on.
From Zaofu down through six generations, it was passed down to Yanfu, whose courtesy name was Gongzhong. When King Xuan of Zhou attacked the Rong people, he drove his chariot for King Xuan.
In the Battle of Thousand Acres, Yanfu saved King Xuan from danger.
Am's father gave birth to his uncle.
During the reign of his uncle, King You of Zhou was debauched and immoral, so he left the Zhou Dynasty and went to Jin, where he served Marquis Wen of Jin and began to establish the Zhao family in Jin.
From the uncle down, the Zhao family became more and more prosperous, and after five generations it was passed down to Zhao Su.
Zhao Su, in the 16th year of Duke Xian of Jin, conquered the three kingdoms of Huo, Wei, and Geng. He led the army to conquer the Huo Kingdom.
Huo Gongqiu fled to Qi State.
This year there was a severe drought in the Jin State, and the divination result said: The gods of Mount Huo Tai are causing trouble.
So Zhao Su was sent to Qi State to welcome back the king of Huo State, restored his status, and asked him to preside over the sacrifices at Mount Huo Tai. Only then did Jin State have a good harvest again.
Duke Xian of Jin gave the land of Geng to Zhao Su.
The year when Zhao Su came down to share the throne with Meng was the first year of Lu Min.
Mencius was born in the same family as Zhao Shui, whose courtesy name was Ziyu.
Zhao Shui used divination to decide whether to serve Duke Xian of Jin or other princes, but the result was unlucky. When the divination revealed that he was serving Prince Chong'er, the result was auspicious, so he went to serve Chong'er.
Chong'er fled to Zhai State due to the Liji Rebellion, and Zhao Shui followed him.
The Zhai people attacked Yao Jiuru and got two women. Zhai Jun gave the young girl to Chong'er as his wife, and the older girl to Zhao Shui as his wife, and they gave birth to Zhao Dun.
When Chong'er was in Jin, Zhao Shuai's first wife had already given birth to Zhao Tong, Zhao Kuo and Zhao Yingqi.
Zhao Shui fled with Chong'er for a total of nineteen years before he was able to return to Jin.
Chong'er became Duke Wen of Jin, and Zhao Shui became the official of Yuan. He lived in Yuan City and presided over state affairs.
The reason why Duke Wen of Jin was able to return and become the overlord was mostly due to Zhao Shuai's strategy. These things are all recorded in "Jin Family".
After Zhao Shui returned to Jin, his first wife in Jin insisted on welcoming back the wife he married in Zhai, and made Zhai's wife's son Zhao Dun the official heir, while his three sons served him in lower positions.
In the sixth year of Duke Xianggong of Jin Dynasty, Zhao Shui passed away, and his posthumous title was Cheng Ji.
Two years after Zhao Dun succeeded Cheng Ji in presiding over the state affairs, Duke Xianggang of Jin passed away and Prince Yigao was young.
Because the country was in trouble, Zhao Dun wanted to make Yong, the younger brother of Duke Xiang, the king of the country.
Yong was in Qin at that time, so he sent envoys to meet him.
The prince's mother cried day and night, kowtowed to Zhao Dun and said: "What sin did the late king have? Why did he abandon his legitimate son and establish another king?"
Zhao Dun was worried about this and was afraid that her clan members and officials would attack and kill her, so he appointed the crown prince, Duke Linggong of Jin, and sent troops to intercept the group of people who came to Qin to meet Duke Xianggong's younger brother.
After Duke Linggong ascended the throne, Zhao Dun took more control of the political affairs of Jin.
Fourteen years after Ling Gong succeeded to the throne, Zhao Lai became more and more arrogant.
Zhao Dun remonstrated many times, but Duke Linggong did not listen.
Once he ate bear paws, but because they were not cooked properly, he killed the catering officer and had his body carried out, where Zhao Dun happened to see him.
Duke Ling was frightened and wanted to kill Zhao Dun.
Zhao Dun was always kind and kind to others. He once gave food to a man who was hungry and fell under a mulberry tree. The man stepped forward to rescue Zhao Dun, and Zhao Dun was able to escape.
Before he could escape from the country, Zhao Chuan killed Duke Ling and made Heihui, the younger brother of Duke Xiang, the king. This was Duke Cheng of Jin.
Zhao Dun returned to preside over state affairs.
The gentleman ridiculed Zhao Dun: As a minister, he fled without leaving the country, and did not punish the rebels when he returned. Therefore, the historian recorded that Zhao Dun killed his king.
Zhao Dun died during the reign of Duke Jinggong of Jin Dynasty. His posthumous title was Xuan Meng, and his son Zhao Shuo inherited the title.
In the third year of Duke Jinggong of Jin Dynasty, Zhao Shuo led the Jin army to rescue Zheng State and fought with King Zhuang of Chu on the Yellow River.
Zhao Shuo married Jin Chenggong's sister as his wife.
In the third year of Duke Jinggong's reign in Jin Dynasty, the official Tu Anjia wanted to kill the entire Zhao family.
When Zhao Dun was still alive, he once dreamed that his uncle was hugging his waist and crying bitterly. He was very sad; then he laughed and clapped his hands and sang.
Zhao Dun performed a divination for this purpose, and the cracks burned on the tortoise shell were interrupted and then intact.
A historian named Yuan of Zhao State judged: This dream is unlucky. It did not come true on you, but on your son, but it was also because of your fault.
By your grandson's generation, the Zhao family will be even more in decline.
Tu Anjia was favored by Duke Lin at first. When he arrived at Jinggong, he became a scourge. When he was about to cause trouble, he first punished the rebels who killed Duke Lin in order to implicate Zhao Dun. At the same time, he informed all the generals that although Zhao Dun did not know about it, he was still the chief culprit.
A minister killed the king, but his descendants are still serving as officials in the court. How can we punish the criminals?
Please kill them.
Han Jue said: When Duke Linggong was killed, Zhao Dun was out of town. Our late king believed that he was not guilty, so he did not kill him.
Now you are going to kill his descendants. This is not the will of the late king but killing at will. Killing at will is causing chaos.
As a minister, if you have important matters but don't let the king know about it, this is to have no king.
Tu'anjia didn't listen.
Han Jue told Zhao Shuo to run away quickly.
Zhao Shuo refused to run away. He said: "You must not cut off the incense of the Zhao family. If I die, I will have no regrets."
Han Jue agreed to his request, and he lied that he was sick and would not go out.
Without asking the monarch for instructions, Tu'anjia and his generals attacked the Zhao family in the lower palace, killed Zhao Shuo, Zhao Tong, Zhao Kuo, and Zhao Yingqi, and exterminated their families.
Zhao Shuo's wife was Cheng Gong's sister. She was pregnant by Zhao Shuo, so she fled to Jin Jinggong's palace to hide.
One of Zhao Shuo's retainers was named Gongsun Chujiu. Chujiu said to Zhao Shuo's friend Cheng Ying: Why don't you die?
Cheng Ying said: Zhao Shuo's wife is pregnant. If she is a boy, I will support her; if she is a girl, it will not be too late for me to die.
Soon after, Zhao Shuo's wife gave birth to a boy.
After Tu'anjia heard about it, he went to the palace to search.
Zhao Shuo's wife put the baby in her pants and prayed: If the Zhao clan should be exterminated, cry loudly; if it is not going to be exterminated, don't make a sound.
When the search arrived, the baby had no sound.
After escaping from danger, Cheng Ying said to Gongsun Peijiu: "We didn't find anything in the search today. We must search again in the future. What should we do?"
Gongsun Chujiu said: Which is more difficult, raising an orphan or dying?
Cheng Ying said: It is easy to die, but it is difficult to raise an orphan.
Gongsun Chujiu said: The ancestors of the Zhao family treated you well, so you can do the difficult things reluctantly; I will do the easy things, and let me die first!
So the two of them managed to get someone else's baby to carry on their backs, wrapped him in embroidered swaddling clothes, and hid him in the mountains.
Cheng Ying came out of the mountain and pretended to tell the generals: "I, Cheng Ying, have no future and cannot raise the orphans of the Zhao family. If anyone can give me a thousand pieces of gold, I will tell them where the orphans of the Zhao family are hidden."
The generals were very happy, agreed to his offer, and sent troops to follow Cheng Ying to attack Gongsun Chujiu.
Chujiu pretended to say: Cheng Ying, you are such a villain!
You couldn't die when you were in trouble in the palace, and you plotted with me to hide the Zhao orphans, but now you betrayed me.
Even if you can't support him with me, how can you bear to betray him!
He held the baby and shouted: Oh my God! Oh my gosh!
What crime did the Zhao orphans have?
Please let him live and just kill me, Chujiu.
The generals did not agree and immediately killed Chujiu and the orphan.
The generals thought that the orphan Zhao was indeed dead and were very happy.
However, the real Zhao orphan was still alive, and Cheng Ying ended up hiding in the mountains with him.
Fifteen years later, Jin Jinggong fell ill and performed a divination. The divination revealed that Daye's descendants were causing trouble due to the cessation of sacrifices.
Jinggong asked Han Jue. Han Jue knew that the orphan of the Zhao family was still alive, so he said: Among the descendants of Daye who have now cut off their incest in Jin, isn't it the Zhao family?
The descendants descended from it all bear the surname Ying.
Zhongyan, a man with a human face and a bird's beak, came to the world to assist Emperor Taiwu of Yin, and the several emperors of Zhou assisted by his descendants all had good virtues.
Further down to King Li and King You, who were ignorant and ignorant, Shudai left the Zhou Dynasty and came to the Jin Dynasty to serve the ancestor Wenhou. Until they became dukes, they established achievements for generations and never stopped their incense.
Now only you, the monarch, have destroyed the Zhao clan, and the people of Jin are mourning for them, so it was revealed in the divination.
I hope you will consider this!
Jinggong asked: "Does the Zhao family have any descendants?"
Han Jue told Jinggong completely the truth.
So Jinggong discussed with Han Jue to create an orphan of the Zhao family, and first found him and hid him in the palace.
The generals entered the palace to inquire about Jinggong's condition. Jinggong relied on Han Jue's many followers to force the generals to meet the Zhao orphans.
The orphan of the Zhao family is named Zhao Wu.
The generals had no choice but to say: The incident in the palace was instigated by Tu'anjia. He falsely conveyed the emperor's orders and issued orders to the ministers. If not, who would dare to initiate a rebellion!
Even if the monarch is not sick, we ministers must support the descendants of the Zhao family.
Now that you have given the order, this is also our wish!
So Zhao Wu and Cheng Ying were asked to thank the generals one by one. The generals in turn joined Cheng Ying and Zhao Wu to attack Tu'anjia and annihilate his family.
Jinggong gave Zhao Wu the fiefdom that originally belonged to the Zhao family.
When Zhao Wu had the crowning ceremony and he was already an adult, Cheng Ying said goodbye to all the officials, and then said to Zhao Wu: "Everyone can die for the Lord because of what happened in the palace."
It's not that I can't die, I just want to support the descendants of the Zhao family.
Now that Zhao Wu has inherited his ancestral legacy, grown up, and restored his original title, I will go underground to report to Zhao Xuan and Gongsun Chujiu.
Zhao Wu cried and kowtowed, and insisted on requesting: "I would rather suffer my own bones and muscles to repay you until my death. Do you have the heart to leave me and die?"
Cheng Ying said: No.
Gongsun Chujiu thought that I could accomplish great things, so he died before me; if I don't come back to life now, he will think that I haven't accomplished this yet.
So he committed suicide.
Zhao Wu kept mourning for Cheng Ying for three years and arranged land for him to use for sacrifices. Spring and Autumn sacrifices have been passed down from generation to generation.
Eleven years after Zhao's title was restored, Duke Li of Jin killed three senior officials of the Que family.
Luan Shu was afraid that he would be implicated, so he killed Duke Li, the king of Jin, and replaced him with Duke Xiang's great-grandson Zhou, who was Duke Ao of Jin.
From then on, the power of the officials in the Jin Dynasty gradually became stronger.
Twenty-seven years after Zhao Wu succeeded the Zhao clan, Duke Ping of Jin came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Ping Gong's reign, Zhao Wu became Zhengqing.
In the thirteenth year, Yanling Jizi of Wu State came to Jin State. He said: The power of Jin State will eventually fall into the hands of the descendants of Zhao Wuzi, Han Xuanzi and Wei Xianzi.
After Zhao Wu's death, his posthumous title was Wenzi.
Wenzi gave birth to Uncle Jing.
During the reign of Uncle Jing, Qi Jinggong sent Yan Ying as an envoy to the State of Jin. Yan Ying talked with Uncle Xiang of the State of Jin.
Yan Ying said: The political power of Qi will eventually fall into the hands of the Tian family.
Shuxiang also said: The political power of Jin will fall into the hands of the six ministers.
The Six Ministers are very presumptuous, but our monarch does not know how to worry.
Uncle Zhao Jing died, and he gave birth to a son, Zhao Yang, who became Zhao Jianzi.
During the reign of Zhao Jianzi, in the ninth year of Jin Qinggong, Jianzi joined the princes to garrison in Zhou territory.
The next year, he escorted King Zhou Jing back to the Zhou Dynasty because he was in exile to avoid his younger brother Zichao.
In the twelfth year of Qinggong's reign in the Jin Dynasty, the six ministers executed the Qi and Yangyu clans of the monarch according to the law, and divided their territory into ten counties. The six ministers asked their own clansmen to be officials.
The Jin government was further weakened from then on.
Thirteen years later, Yang Hu, a rebellious minister of Lu State, fled to Jin State. Zhao Jianzi accepted the bribe and treated him favorably.
Zhao Jianzi fell ill and was unconscious for five days. The doctors were all frightened.
Doctor Bian Que came out after seeing it. Dong Anyu asked about his condition. Bian Que said: "My blood is peaceful, why should you be surprised!"
Duke Mu of Qin also had this situation before, and it took him seven days to wake up.
The day I woke up, I told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: I am very happy when I arrive at the place where the Emperor of Heaven lives.
The reason I stayed so long was because I happened to be teaching.
The Emperor of Heaven told me: The Kingdom of Jin will be in chaos, and there will be no peace for the fifth generation; their descendants will dominate and die before they grow old, and the sons of those who dominate will let men and women mix in your Kingdom of Jin.
Gongsun Zhi wrote it down and hid it, and the prophecy of Qin came out.
You know the chaos during the reign of Duke Xian, the hegemony under Duke Wen, the great defeat of the Qin army at Mt.
Now your monarch's illness is the same as Duke Mu of Qin. He will definitely recover within three days. After he gets better, he will definitely have something to say.
After two and a half days, Jianzi woke up.
He said to the doctors: I was very happy when I arrived at the Emperor of Heaven. I traveled with hundreds of gods in Juntian. I heard magnificent music played many times and saw thousands of dances. It was not like the music of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties. The music was very moving.
A bear came to catch me, and the Emperor of Heaven asked me to shoot it. The bear was shot and died.
Another turtle came over, and I shot it again. The turtle was shot and died.
The Emperor was very happy and gave me two bamboo boxes, both equipped with small boxes.
I saw a child next to the Emperor of Heaven. The Emperor of Heaven entrusted me with a Zhai dog and said to me: When your son grows up, give him this dog.
The Emperor of Heaven also told me: The Jin Kingdom will gradually decline and will perish after seven generations. The people surnamed Ying will defeat the Zhou people to the west of Fan Kui, but you cannot occupy it.
Now I recall the merits of Yu and Shun, and when the time comes I will marry Meng Yao, the daughter of Shun's descendants, to your seventh-generation grandson.
After hearing this, Dong Anyu wrote it down and kept it safely.
He reported what Bian Que said to Jianzi, and Jianzi gave Bianque four acres of land.
One day, when Jianzi was out, someone blocked his way and refused to leave even if he was driven away. His followers were very angry and wanted to kill him.
The roadblocker said: I have something to see the Lord.
The attendant reported his words to Jianzi. Jianzi summoned him and said upon meeting him: Hee! I have seen you clearly.
The man blocking the road said: "Please ask the attendants on the left and right to step aside. I have something to report."
Jianzi asked people to retreat.
The roadblock said: When you were sick, I was with the Emperor of Heaven.
Jianzi said: Yes, this is indeed the case.
What was I doing when you saw me?
The man who blocked the road said: The Emperor of Heaven asked you to shoot bears and pigs, but you shot them both to death.
Jianzi said: Yes, what will happen?
The person blocking the road said: Jin will be in great trouble, and you will be the first to bear the brunt.
The Emperor of Heaven has asked you to kill two ministers. Xiong and Zhu are their ancestors.
Jianzi said: The Emperor of Heaven gave me two bamboo boxes, each with matching small boxes. What does this mean?
The blocker said: Your son will defeat two countries in Zhai, and they both have the surname Zi.
Jianzi said: I saw a child next to the Emperor of Heaven. The Emperor of Heaven gave me a Zhai dog and said: When your son grows up, give him this dog.
What does it mean to give a Zhai dog to a child?
The blocker said: The child is your son, and Zhai Quan is the ancestor of Daiguo.
Your son will definitely occupy Daiguo in the future.
In your descendants, there will be changes in government decrees, and they will wear the clothes of the barbarians and annex two countries in Zhai.
Jianzi asked him his last name and wanted to appoint him as an official.
The man who blocked the road said: I am a countryman, and I just came to convey the will of the Emperor of Heaven.
After saying that, he disappeared.
Jianzi recorded these words and kept them in his secret palace.
Another day, Gubuziqing paid a visit to Jianzi. Jianzi called his sons to have his fortune read.
Ziqing said: There is no one who can be a general.
Jianzi said: Is the Zhao family finished?
Ziqing said: I once saw a child on the road, probably your son!
Jianzi called his son Wuxie again.
As soon as Wuji arrived, Ziqing stood up and said, "This is the real general!"
Jianzi said: This child's mother is a humble servant girl from Zhai. How can you say he is noble?
Ziqing said: Those given by God, even if they are humble, they will surely become noble.
From then on, Jianzi often called his sons to talk, and Wuxie behaved the best.
Jianzi once told his sons: I have hidden the treasure talisman on Mount Chang, and whoever finds it first will be rewarded.
The sons hurried to Changshan to look for it, but found nothing.
Wu Shi came back and said: The treasure talisman has been found.
Jianzi said: Just tell me.
Wuxie said: If you can see the state of Dai from Changshan Mountain, you can capture the state of Dai.
Only then did Jianzi realize that Wuxie was indeed a talented person. So he deposed Prince Bolu and made Wushe the crown prince.
Two years later, in the fourteenth year of Jin Dinggong's reign, the Fan family and the Zhongxing family rebelled.
In the spring of the next year, Jianzi said to Zhao Wu, the doctor of Handan, "Give me back the five hundred households of Weiguo's people, and I will resettle them to Jinyang."
Zhao Wu agreed, but when he returned, his father and brother disagreed, so he broke his promise.
Zhao Yang arrested Zhao Wu and imprisoned him in Jinyang.
He also told the people of Handan: I will kill Zhao Wu privately. Who do you want to take over?
So Zhao Wu was killed.
Zhao Wu's son Zhao Ji and his retainer Shebin rebelled with Handan.
The king of Jin sent troops led by Qin to besiege Handan.
Xun Yin, Fan Jishe and Zhao Wu had a good relationship, but they refused to help Qin and instead planned a rebellion. Dong Anyu knew about this.
In October, the Fan family and the Zhonghang family attacked Zhao Yang. Zhao Yang fled to Jinyang, and the Jin people surrounded Jinyang.
Fan Jishe, Xun Yin's enemy Wei Xiang, and others plotted to expel Xun Yin and replace him with Liang Yingfu; to expel Fan Jishe and replace him with Fan Gaoyi.
Xun Yue said to the king of Jin: The king ordered his ministers to kill those who lead the rebellion.
Now the three ministers are leading the rebellion, but expelling Zhao Yang alone is an unfair punishment. Please expel them all.
In November, Xun Yue, Han Buyi and Wei Duo followed the king's order to attack the Fan and Zhongxing clans, but failed to win.
The Fan family and Zhonghang family in turn attacked Dinggong, and Dinggong fought back. Fan family and Zhonghang family failed and fled.
On the day of Ding Wei, two people fled to Chaoge.
