summary:
The Zhao family shares a common ancestor with the Qin people. Their lineage traces back to Zhongyan, who served as a charioteer for Emperor Taiwu of the Shang Dynasty. His descendant Feilian had two sons: Eilai, who served King Zhou and was killed by the Zhou people, becoming the ancestor of the Ying Qin family; and Ji Sheng, whose descendants became the Zhao family. Ji Sheng's line included Meng Zeng, favored by King Cheng of Zhou, and eventually Zaofu, who served King Mu of Zhou. Zaofu presented eight fine horses to King Mu and drove his chariot westward, where the king met the Queen Mother of the West. When King Xu Yan rebelled, Zaofu drove King Mu thousands of miles in a day to crush the rebellion, and was rewarded with the city of Zhao, establishing the Zhao family name.

Six generations later, Yanfu served King Xuan of Zhou as a charioteer and saved him at the Battle of Thousand Acres. His son Shudai left the debauched court of King You of Zhou to serve Marquis Wen of Jin, beginning the Zhao family's rise in Jin. Five generations later, Zhao Su conquered the states of Huo, Wei, and Geng for Duke Xian of Jin. When a drought struck Jin, divination revealed the god of Mount Huo Tai was angry, so Zhao Su restored the king of Huo to appease the god, and the drought ended. Zhao Shui, a descendant, used divination to decide to serve Prince Chong'er, following him into exile for nineteen years. After Chong'er became Duke Wen of Jin, Zhao Shui became a high official and helped him become hegemon.

After Zhao Shui's death, his son Zhao Dun succeeded him. When Duke Xiang of Jin died, Zhao Dun initially planned to install a younger brother as ruler due to the young age of the crown prince, but the prince's mother's pleas led him to install the crown prince as Duke Ling of Jin. Duke Ling grew tyrannical, and when he tried to kill Zhao Dun, Zhao Dun fled. Before he could escape the country, Zhao Chuan killed Duke Ling. Zhao Dun returned to preside over state affairs, but historians recorded that he killed the king because he did not punish the rebels. Zhao Dun's son Zhao Shuo married Duke Cheng of Jin's sister. During Duke Jing's reign, the official Tu Anjia, seeking to destroy the Zhao family, falsely accused Zhao Dun of regicide and attacked the Zhao residence, killing Zhao Shuo and his brothers, though Zhao Shuo's pregnant wife escaped to the palace.

Zhao Shuo's wife gave birth to a son, Zhao Wu. Tu Anjia searched for the baby, but it was hidden. Zhao Shuo's retainers, Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu, devised a plan: Chujiu hid with a substitute baby, and Cheng Ying "betrayed" him to the generals. The generals killed Chujiu and the substitute, believing the Zhao line extinct. Cheng Ying then hid the real Zhao Wu in the mountains for fifteen years. When Duke Jing fell ill, divination revealed the Zhao family's sacrifices were causing trouble. Han Jue, knowing the truth, told the duke, who then restored Zhao Wu and destroyed Tu Anjia's family. After Zhao Wu came of age, Cheng Ying committed suicide to report to his fallen comrades.

Zhao Wu's descendants grew powerful. His son Zhao Yang, Zhao Jianzi, became a dominant minister. He defeated the Fan and Zhonghang clans, expanded Zhao territory, and was named Shangqing, effectively monopolizing Jin's government. His son Zhao Wuxie, Zhao Xiangzi, succeeded him. Xiangzi killed the king of Dai and annexed his land. When Zhibo demanded territory, Xiangzi refused, leading to a siege of Jinyang. With divine guidance from the gods of Mount Huotai, Xiangzi allied with Han and Wei to destroy Zhibo and divide his lands. Zhao became stronger than Han and Wei.

Xiangzi refused to make his own son heir, instead passing rule to his grandson Zhao Huan, who became Marquis Xian. After a brief usurpation by Xiangzi's brother, Xianhou's line continued. Subsequent rulers included Liehou, Jinghou, Chenghou, and Suhou. During Suhou's reign, Shang Yang of Qin attacked Wei. Suhou's son, King Wuling, ascended the throne. King Wuling, seeking to strengthen Zhao against enemies like Zhongshan and the Hu tribes, famously adopted Hu clothing and cavalry archery, overcoming opposition from nobles. He conquered Zhongshan and expanded Zhao's territory significantly. He later abdicated in favor of his son, King Huiwen, but a succession struggle led to his death by starvation after his son Zhao Zhang rebelled.

Under King Huiwen and his successor King Xiaocheng, Zhao faced the rising power of Qin. King Xiaocheng accepted the surrender of Shangdang from Korea, provoking Qin. This led to the disastrous Battle of Changping, where Zhao Kuo replaced Lian Po and was defeated by Bai Qi, with over 400,000 Zhao soldiers killed. Qin besieged Handan, but Zhao was saved by reinforcements from Chu and Wei. Later, King Xiaocheng's son, King Daoxiang, and his grandson, King Youmiao, ruled as Qin's power grew. Li Mu, a capable general, won victories against Qin, but was killed due to slander. Finally, in 228 BCE, Qin captured Handan, ending the Zhao state. Zhao Jia, a brother of the last king, briefly ruled in Dai before being defeated, and Zhao was made into a Qin commandery.

When the eldest son left, he also took several hundred yi of gold with him privately.
The eldest son arrived in Chu State and saw Zhuang Sheng's house close to the outer city of Chu Capital. He had to push back the weeds to reach Zhuang Sheng's house. Zhuang Sheng's living conditions were very poor.
But the eldest son still opened the letter and donated a thousand pieces of gold to Zhuang Sheng, exactly as his father asked.
Zhuang Sheng said: You can leave as soon as possible, but don't stay here!
When your brother is released, don’t ask why.
The eldest son left Zhuang Sheng's house and no longer visited Zhuang Sheng. However, he stayed in Chu State privately and gave the gold he carried to the dignitaries in charge of Chu State.
Although Zhuang Sheng lived in a poor alley, he was well-known in Chu State for his integrity and integrity, and everyone from the King of Chu on down respected him as their teacher.
Zhu Gong offered the gold, but he did not accept it intentionally. He just wanted to return it to Zhu Gong after the work was completed to show his trustworthiness.
So after the gold was delivered, he said to his wife: This is Zhu Gong's money. I will return it to Zhu Gong in full in the future, but I don't know when I will return it. This is just like I can't tell others in advance when I get sick. Don't use it. But Zhu Gong's eldest son didn't know what Zhuang Sheng meant, and thought that giving the property to Zhuang Sheng would not have any effect.
Zhuang Sheng took the opportunity to go to the palace to meet the King of Chu and said: "A certain star has moved to a certain place, which will be harmful to the Chu State."
The King of Chu usually trusted Zhuang Sheng very much, so he asked: What should we do now?
Zhuang Sheng said: Only by practicing benevolence and righteousness can disaster be avoided.
The King of Chu said: "You don't need to say more, I will do it."
The king of Chu sent an envoy to seal the warehouse where three coins were stored.
The dignitaries of Chu State were surprised and told Duke Zhu's eldest son: The King of Chu will implement a general amnesty.
The eldest son asked: How can you see it?
The noble man said: Whenever the King of Chu grants amnesty, he often seals up the warehouse where three coins are stored.
The King of Chu sent an envoy to seal it last night.
The eldest son of Zhu Gong thought that since the amnesty was granted, his younger brother could naturally be released. One thousand yi gold was equivalent to wasting Zhuang Sheng and had no effect, so he went to see Zhuang Sheng again.
Zhuang Sheng asked in surprise: "Didn't you leave?"
The eldest son said: He never left.
I came here because of my younger brother. Today, the State of Chu is discussing amnesty, and my younger brother will naturally be released, so I came here specifically to say goodbye to you.
Zhuang Sheng knew that he wanted to get the gold back, so he said, "Go to the room and get the gold yourself."
The eldest son broke into the house, took away the gold and left Zhuang Sheng, secretly rejoicing that the gold was recovered.
Zhuang Sheng felt deeply ashamed that he had been betrayed by his younger generation, so he went to the palace again to meet with the King of Chu and said: "What I told you about a certain star last time, you said you wanted to repay it by doing good deeds."
Now, I heard from passers-by outside that the son of the rich Taoist Zhu Gong was imprisoned by Chu after killing someone. His family sent people to bribe the people around the king of Chu with a lot of money. Therefore, the king did not implement the amnesty out of sympathy for the people of Chu, but he gave the amnesty because of Zhu Gong's son.
The King of Chu was furious and said: Although I am not virtuous, how could I give favors to Duke Zhu's son?
He ordered Zhu Gong's son to be killed first, and then issued an edict of pardon the next day.
The eldest son of Lord Zhu had no choice but to carry his younger brother's body home.
After returning home, my mother and neighbors were all very sad. Only Mr. Zhu laughed and said: I knew that the eldest son would not be able to save his younger brother!
It's not that he doesn't love his brother, he just has something he can't bear to give up.
He has lived with me since he was young, has experienced all kinds of hardships, and knows how difficult it is to make a living, so he values ​​money very seriously and does not dare to spend money easily.
As for my little brother, he has only seen me being extremely wealthy since he was born. He rides in fine cars, drives thousands of miles of horses, and goes hunting in the countryside. He doesn’t know where the money comes from, so he takes money very lightly and throws it away without mercy.
It turned out that I planned to let the younger son go because he was willing to give up money, but the eldest son couldn't give up money, and ended up killing his younger brother. This is reasonable and not worthy of grief.
What I was looking forward to day and night was for my second son’s body to be returned.
Fan Li moved three times and became famous all over the world. He didn't just leave somewhere randomly. He became famous wherever he lived.
In the end, he died of old age in Taodi, so people in the world called him Tao Zhugong.
Tai Shigong said: Xia Yu's contribution was great. He channeled the nine great rivers and stabilized the land of Kyushu. To this day, the whole of Kyushu is safe and sound.
When his descendant Gou Jian arrived, he worked hard and thought far, and finally destroyed the powerful Wu State, marched north to the Central Plains, worshiped the Zhou Dynasty, and became the overlord.
Can you say that you are not virtuous?
This is probably the legacy of Xia Yu.
Fan Li moved three times and left a glorious reputation that will last forever.
Is it possible for a minister and a monarch to do this without becoming famous?
summary:
King Gou Jian of Yue was a descendant of Xia Yu, son of a concubine of Emperor Shaokang of Xia. Emperor Shaokang's son was enfeoffed at Kuaiji, where he maintained Xia Yu's sacrifices. His descendants tattooed their bodies, cut their hair short, developed wasteland, and built cities. After more than twenty generations, rule passed to Yunchang, who had conflicts with King Helu of Wu. After Yunchang's death, his son Gou Jian became king.

In Gou Jian's first year, King Helu of Wu attacked Yue. Gou Jian sent death-defying warriors who lined up in three rows and rushed into Wu's position, shouting they would kill themselves. The stunned Wu soldiers were attacked by Yue forces, defeated at Jianli, and Helu was wounded. Dying, Helu warned his son Fucha never to forget Yue.

Three years later, Gou Jian learned Fucha was training soldiers to avenge Wu. Despite Fan Li's warning that weapons were dangerous and attacking immoral, Gou Jian attacked Wu. Fucha mobilized elite troops, defeated Yue at Fujiao, and surrounded Kuaiji with only 5,000 Yue soldiers remaining. Gou Jian regretted ignoring Fan Li's advice. Fan Li advised humility and generous gifts to Wu. Gou Jian sent official Zhong to beg for peace, offering himself as a slave and his wife as a concubine. Wu's Zixu advised against accepting, but Dazai Pi, bribed with treasures, persuaded King Wu to pardon Yue. Zixu warned that Gou Jian was a wise monarch with capable ministers who would cause chaos if allowed to return, but King Wu ignored him.

After returning home, Gou Jian worked tirelessly, hanging gall where he could taste it, asking himself if he had forgotten Kuaiji's humiliation. He farmed personally, his wife wove cloth, ate no meat, wore no fine clothes, treated worthy men with courtesy, helped the poor, and shared hardships with the people. He entrusted government to Zhong while Fan Li served as hostage in Wu for two years.

Seven years after returning, Gou Jian wanted revenge. A counselor advised patience, noting Wu was attacking Qi and Jin while lacking morality. Yue should befriend Qi, Chu, and Jin while treating Wu favorably. Two years later, when Wu prepared to attack Qi, Zixu warned that Gou Jian shared hardships with his people and would become Wu's worry, urging attack on Yue first. King Wu refused, defeated Qi, and scolded Zixu. Yue's Zhong tested Wu by requesting grain; King Wu lent it despite Zixu's objections. Dazai Pi slandered Zixu, and when Zixu entrusted his son to the Bao family while on a mission to Qi, King Wu sent him a sword to commit suicide. Zixu laughed, saying he should have his eyes hung on Wu's east gate to see Yue's army enter.

Three years later, Gou Jian asked Fan Li about attacking Wu. Fan Li said no. The next spring, while Wu's elite troops were at Huangchi with King Wu, Yue attacked, killed Wu's prince, and defeated Wu's forces. King Wu hid the news and sought peace. Yue agreed, unable to destroy Wu. Four years later, Yue attacked again, besieged Wu's capital for three years, and trapped King Wu on Gusu Mountain. King Wu sought peace, reminding Gou Jian of Kuaiji. Gou Jian wavered, but Fan Li insisted Wu must be destroyed, recalling God had given Yue to Wu before. Fan Li drove away Wu's envoy. King Wu committed suicide, covering his face, ashamed to see Zixu. Yue's king buried Wu's king and killed Dazai Pi.

After pacifying Wu, Gou Jian marched north, met with Qi and Jin princes at Xuzhou, and paid tribute to Zhou. King Yuan of Zhou rewarded him. Gou Jian donated land to Chu, Song, and Lu. The Yue army marched unimpeded, and Gou Jian became overlord. Fan Li then left, sending a letter to Zhong from Qi, saying: "When birds are gone, the good bow is hidden; when cunning rabbit dies, running dogs are cooked. You can only share adversity with the king, not happiness." Zhong claimed illness but was slandered as rebellious. The king sent him a sword, saying he had used three of Zhong's seven strategies against Wu and should try the remaining four with the late king. Zhong committed suicide.

Gou Jian died, and his descendants ruled for generations until King Wuqiang. During King Wei of Chu's reign, Yue attacked Qi. Qi's envoy persuaded Yue to attack Chu instead, arguing that Chu's forces were dispersed. Yue abandoned Qi and attacked Chu. King Wei of Chu defeated Yue, killed King Wuqiang, and seized all land from Wu to Zhejiang. Yue disintegrated, with various descendants competing for power, some claiming kingship, living south of the Yangtze and paying tribute to Chu. Seven generations later, Fujian Junyao helped princes overthrow Qin. Emperor Gao of Han restored Yue's kingship. Dongyue and Minjun were both Yue descendants.

Fan Li served Gou Jian for over twenty years, destroying Wu and making Gou Jian hegemon. Recognizing that great fame was difficult to sustain and Gou Jian could not share happiness, Fan Li left by boat with valuables, never returning. He changed his name, farmed in Qi, accumulated wealth, became prime minister, then resigned, distributed his property, and moved to Taodi, calling himself Tao Zhugong. He farmed and traded, accumulating millions. His second son killed someone in Chu. He sent his youngest son with gold to bribe his old friend Zhuang Sheng, but his eldest son insisted on going. The eldest son delivered the gold but later retrieved it when he thought amnesty would free his brother. Zhuang Sheng, ashamed, told the Chu king that the amnesty was due to bribery. The king killed Zhu Gong's son first, then issued amnesty. Zhu Gong had expected this, knowing his eldest son valued money while his youngest would spend freely. Fan Li died of old age in Taodi.

Tai Shigong commented: Xia Yu's contributions were great, channeling rivers and stabilizing Kyushu. His descendant Gou Jian worked hard, destroyed Wu, and became overlord—truly virtuous, likely Xia Yu's legacy. Fan Li moved three times, leaving a glorious reputation.
