translation:
Duke Hu of Chen was a descendant of Emperor Shun of Yu.
When Shun was still a commoner, Yao married his two daughters to him and lived in Guirui. His descendants took the name of this place as their surname and named them Gui.
After Shun's death, the empire was passed to Yu, and Shun's son Shangjun was made a prince.
In the late Xia Dynasty, the titles of Shun's descendants were intermittent.
After King Wu of Zhou defeated King Zhou of Yin, he once again searched for Shun's descendants. He found Guiman and sealed him in Chendi to worship Emperor Shun during his lifetime. This was Duke Hu.
Hu Gong died, and his son Shen Gong Xihou succeeded to the throne.
When Duke Shen died, his younger brother Xianggong Gaoyang succeeded him.
After the death of Xianggong, he appointed Duke Shen's son Tu as king, who was called Duke Xiao.
When Duke Xiao died, his son Shen Gong Yurong succeeded to the throne.
Duke Shen was in the reign of King Li of Zhou Dynasty.
Duke Shen died, and his son You Gong Ning succeeded to the throne.
In the 20th year of Duke You, King Li of Zhou fled to the Pigland.
In the twenty-third year, Duke You passed away, and his son Li Gongxiao succeeded him.
In the sixth year of Ligong, King Xuan of Zhou came to the throne.
In the thirty-sixth year, Li Gong died and his son Wu Gongling succeeded to the throne.
Duke Wu died in his fifteenth year and was succeeded by his son Yi Gong.
This year, King You of Zhou came to the throne.
Duke Yi died after reigning for three years, and his younger brother Ping Gongxie succeeded him.
In the seventh year of Ping Gong, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong, and the capital of Zhou Dynasty moved eastward to Luoyi.
The state of Qin began to become a vassal state.
In the twenty-third year, Duke Ping died and his son Wen Gongyu succeeded to the throne.
In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, he married a daughter of Cai Guo and gave birth to his son Tuo.
Ten years later, Duke Wen died and his eldest son, Duke Huan Bao, succeeded him.
In the twenty-third year of Duke Huan, Duke Yin of Lu came to the throne.
In the twenty-sixth year, the Wei people killed Wei Jun Zhouxu.
In the thirty-third year, the people of Lu killed Duke Yin of Lu.
In the thirty-eighth year of the first lunar month, on Jiaxu day or Jichou day, Duke Huan Bao passed away.
Since the mother of his younger brother Tuo was from Cai, the people of Cai killed their fifth father and Duke Huan's prince Fu for Tuo, and supported Tuo as his successor, Duke Li.
When Duke Huan was seriously ill, civil strife broke out and the people were dispersed, so another obituary was sent.
In the second year of Duke Li's reign, his son Jing Zhongwan was born.
When Taishi of the Zhou Dynasty was passing through the state of Chen, Chen Ligong asked him to use the "Book of Changes" to predict his son's fortune. The hexagram he got was "Guan Gua" changed to "No Gua". Zhou Taishi said: This is called being able to see the glory of the country, which is conducive to being a guest of the emperor.
He will probably replace Chen Guo and take possession of the country for himself, right?
Not in Chen country, probably in another country?
This wouldn't happen in his own lifetime, but probably in the lifetime of his descendants, right?
If it happened in another country, it must be in the country with the surname Jiang.
Because the surname Jiang is a descendant of Taiyue.
Things cannot develop fully in both aspects. It will probably take until the fall of Chen State that his descendants will prosper, right?
Duke Li of Chen married a woman from the State of Cai, who committed adultery with a man from the State of Cai. Duke Chen Li also went to the State of Cai many times to have sex with other women.
In the seventh year, the three younger brothers of Prince Huan, who was killed by Duke Li, were named Yue, Lin, and Chujiu. They asked the Cai people to seduce Duke Li with beautiful women. Then the three of them killed Duke Li together with the Cai people, and Li Yue became the king, which is Duke Li.
Duke Li was the son of Duke Huan.
Duke Li died five months after he ascended the throne, and his second brother Lin succeeded him as Duke Zhuang.
Duke Zhuang died after reigning for seven years, and his youngest brother Chujiu succeeded him as Duke Xuan.
In the third year of Xuangong's reign, King Wu of Chu passed away, and the state of Chu began to become stronger.
In the seventeenth year, King Zhou Hui married Chen Jun's daughter as his queen.
In the twenty-first year, Duke Xuan later gave birth to a son named Ji, whom he favored. Duke Xuan wanted to make him the prince, so he killed the original prince Yu Kou.
The imperial bandit had always liked Li Gong's son Wan, but Wan was afraid that he would be harmed, so he fled to Qi.
Duke Huan of Qi wanted Chen Wan to be his minister. Chen Wan said: As a minister living abroad, I am lucky enough not to do hard work. It is the favor you have given me. I dare not hold a high official position.
Duke Huan asked him to be an official of work and integrity.
Qi Yizhong wanted to marry his daughter to Chen Wan, so he first performed a divination. The divination said: Husband and wife are like male and female phoenixes flying together, with loud and clear chirps.
The descendants of the surname Gui will thrive in the country of the surname Jiang.
After the Five Dynasties, he will be prosperous and his status will be on par with the chief ministers.
Eight generations later, no one can compare with it.
In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Huan of Qi attacked the State of Cai, and the State of Cai was defeated. The Qi soldiers took advantage of the situation and invaded the territory of the State of Chu, heading south to Zhaoling. The army passed by the State of Chen when returning to Qi.
Chen Guo's official Yuan Taotu suspected that the Qi army was harassing them across the border, so he deceived Duke Huan of Qi and said that it would be better to return to Qi via the east road along the coast.
The road to the east was very dangerous. When Duke Huan of Qi learned the truth, he was furious and had Yuan Taotu arrested.
This year, Duke Xian of Jin forced his own prince Shen Sheng to death.
Forty-five years later, Duke Xuan died, and his son Qian succeeded him as Duke Mu.
In the fifth year of Duke Mu, Duke Huan of Qi passed away.
In the 16th year, Duke Wen of Jin defeated the Chu army in Chengpu.
In this year, Chen Mugong died, and his son Gong Gongshuo succeeded to the throne.
In the sixth year of Duke Gong of Chen, Shang Chen, the crown prince of Chu, killed his father, King Cheng of Chu, and established himself as king, King Mu of Chu.
In the eleventh year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
In the eighteenth year, Gonggong Chen passed away and his son Lingping Guo succeeded to the throne.
In the first year of Chen Ling, King Zhuang of Chu came to the throne.
In the sixth year, Chu State conquered Chen State.
In ten years, the state of Chen made peace with the state of Chu.
In the fourteenth year, Chen Linggong, Kong Ning and Yi Xingfu, Chen Guo's officials, all committed adultery with Xia Ji, and even wore Xia Ji's clothes to make fun of in court.
The doctor Xieye advised: "The king and ministers are so promiscuous, how can the people follow their example?"
Chen Linggong told Kong Ning and Yi Xingfu this. They asked to kill Xie Zhi, but Chen Linggong did not stop them, so they killed Xie Zhi.
In the fifteenth year, Chen Linggong, Kong Ning and Yi Xingfu drank and had fun at Xia Ji's house. Chen Linggong joked to the two of them: Xia Zhengshu looks like you.
The two retorted, "He looks like you too."
Xia Zhengshu was very angry after hearing this.
After Linggong came out after drinking, Xia Zhengshu hid at the door of the stable and shot Linggong with an arrow.
Kong Ning and Yi Xingfu were so frightened that they fled to Chu State, and Ling Gong Prince Wu also fled to Jin State.
Xia Zhengshu established himself as Marquis of Chen.
Xia Zhengshu used to be a doctor of Chen State.
Xia Ji is the wife of Uncle Yu and the mother of Xia Zhengshu.
In the winter of the first year of Chen Chenggong, King Zhuang of Chu led the troops of the princes to attack Chen on the grounds that Xia Zhengshu had killed Chen Linggong.
And he said to Chen Guoren: Don't be afraid, I just want to kill Xia Zhengshu.
However, after killing Xia Zhengshu, he took advantage of the situation to annex Chen State and occupied it as a county of Chu State. All the officials of Chu State congratulated King Zhuang of Chu for this.
At this time, Uncle Shen came back from Qi as an envoy and did not express his congratulations.
King Zhuang of Chu asked him why he was like this, and Uncle Shen replied: As the saying goes, someone takes a cow to take a shortcut and tramples on other people's crops. The owner of the field chases him and snatches the cow back to him.
It is indeed sinful to take a shortcut and trample on someone's field, but isn't it too much to take his cattle away because of this?
Now the king regards Xia Zhengshu's killing of the king as unjust, so he conscripted the troops of the princes to attack Xia Zhengshu to uphold justice. However, after the incident, he occupied Chen State and coveted other people's land. How can he command the world in the future?
So I don't congratulate you.
After hearing this, King Zhuang of Chu said: Well said!
So the crown prince Guiwu who brought back Chen Linggong from Jin State was made Lord of Chen, and he governed Chen State as in the past. He was Chen Chenggong.
When Confucius was reading history, he saw a passage in which Chu State restored sovereignty to Chen State, and he said: King Zhuang of Chu is truly a virtuous man.
He despises the kingdom of a thousand chariots but values ​​a helpful word.
In the eighth year, King Zhuang of Chu passed away.
In the twenty-ninth year, Chen State betrayed its alliance with Chu State.
In the 30th year, the king of the Communist Party of Chu conquered the state of Chen.
In this year, Chen Chenggong died, and his son Ai Gong weakly succeeded to the throne.
The king of Chu dismissed his troops and returned home because of the funeral of Chen Guo.
In the third year of Ai Gong's reign, Chu soldiers surrounded Chen State and later spared Chen State.
In the twenty-eighth year, the princes of Chu surrounded and killed King Jia Ao of Chu and established himself as King of Chu, namely King Ling of Chu.
In the thirty-fourth year, at first, Duke Ai of Chen married a wife from the state of Zheng. The eldest concubine gave birth to Crown Prince Shi, and the shao concubine gave birth to her son Yan.
Duke Ai also had two favored concubines. The eldest concubine gave birth to a son named Liu, and the younger concubine gave birth to a son named Sheng.
Duke Ai loved Liu the most and entrusted him to his younger brother Situ Zhao to take care of him.
After Duke Ai fell ill, in March, Zhao killed Prince Mourning and made Liu Liu the crown prince.
Duke Ai was very angry and wanted to kill Zhao, so he sent troops to surround Duke Ai. Duke Ai hanged himself to death.
The final move was to make Liuli the king.
In April, Chen State sent envoys to Chu State to report his death.
When King Ling of Chu heard that Chen was in civil strife, he killed Chen's envoys and sent his son Qiji to raise troops to conquer Chen. Chen Junliu fled to Zheng.
In the ninth month, Chu soldiers surrounded Chen.
In November, Chen Guo was destroyed.
The prince of Chu was ordered to give up his illness and become the Duke of Chen.
When the prince was killed, his son, named Wu, fled and went to Jin.
Duke Ping of Jin asked Taishi Zhao: Is Chen really going to perish?
Taishi Zhao replied: Chen Guo is a descendant of Zhuan Xu.
The Chen family will eventually perish when they gain political power in Qi.
The ancestors of Chen State from Mu to Gushang did not disobey the destiny.
Shun paid great attention to promoting virtue.
When Sui arrived, he abided by his way from generation to generation.
During the reign of Duke Hu, the Emperor of Zhou gave him a surname and ordered him to worship Emperor Shun of Yu.
Moreover, the descendants of Shengde's emperors will surely be passed down to a hundred generations.
The lineage of Yu and Shun has not yet reached a hundred generations, maybe it will continue to develop in Qi State?
In the fifth year after King Ling of Chu destroyed Chen, Prince Qiji of Chu State killed King Ling and established himself as King of Chu, that is, King Ping.
King Ping had just ascended the throne, and wanted to be friendly and gain the support of the princes, so he found Wu, the son of the former crown prince of Chen Guo, and made him the Marquis of Chen, which is Chen Huigong.
After Hui Gong ascended the throne, he dated back to the year of Ai Gong's death and took over the Chen Guoji as the first year. At this time, Hui Gong's reign was actually five years in vain.
In the tenth year of Duke Hui's reign, a fire broke out in the state of Chen.
In the fifteenth year, King Liao of Wu ordered Prince Guang to attack the state of Chen, capture Hu and Shen, and then return.
In the twenty-eighth year, King Wu Helu and Wu Zixu defeated Chu and invaded the capital of Ying.
In this year, Chen Huigong died, and his son Huai Gong Liu succeeded him.
In the first year of Huai Gong, after King Wu conquered Chu, he stationed himself in Yingdu and summoned Chen Huai Gong.
Duke Huai wanted to go, but Chen Guo's doctor said: The king of Wu has been very satisfied recently, but although the king of Chu escaped, he was an old friend of Chen and could not betray the friendship between Chen and Chu.
Duke Huai declined the meeting on the pretext of being ill.
In the fourth year, King Wu summoned Duke Huai again. Duke Huai was afraid and had to go to Wu.
The king of Wu was angry that Chen Huaigong did not come last time, so he detained him and finally died in the state of Wu.
Chen Guo then appointed Yue, the son of Duke Huai, as king, who was named Duke Min.
In the sixth year of Min Gong's reign, Confucius arrived in the state of Chen.
King Wu Fu Chai attacked Chen State and returned after capturing three cities.
In the thirteenth year, the State of Wu came to attack Chen State again. The State of Chen asked the State of Chu for help. King Zhao of Chu led troops to rescue him. He garrisoned Chengfu, and the Wu army withdrew.
In this year, King Zhao of Chu died in Chengfu.
At that time Confucius was still in the state of Chen.
In the fifteenth year, Song State destroyed Cao State.
In the 16th year, King Wu Fuchai launched a northern expedition to Qi State and defeated the Qi army in Ailing. He also sent someone to summon Chen Hou.
Chen Minggong was afraid and went to the state of Wu.
Therefore, Chu State conquered Chen State.
In the twenty-first year, Tian Chang, the official of Qi State, killed Duke Jian of Qi State.
In the twenty-third year, Bai Gongsheng of Chu State killed his commanders Zixi and Ziqi, and attacked King Hui of Chu.
Ye Gong of Chu State defeated Bai Gong, and Bai Gong committed suicide.
In the twenty-fourth year, King Hui of Chu regained his kingdom, raised his troops in the Northern Expedition, killed Duke Min of Chen, and then destroyed the state of Chen and made it the capital of Chu.
This year, Confucius died.
Duke Donglou of Qi State was a descendant of Dayu of Xia Dynasty.
During the Shang Dynasty, its feudal status was intermittent.
After King Wu of Zhou defeated Yin Zhou, he searched for Yu's descendants. He found Donglou Gong and sealed him in Qi to offer sacrifices to the Xiahou clan.
Gong Donglou gave birth to a son, Gong Xilou, Gong Xilou gave birth to a son named Gong Ti, and Gong Ti gave birth to a son who planned to marry Gong Gong.
It was during the era of King Li of Zhou that the Duke of Suyuan was in power.
She plans to marry Gong Gong and give birth to his son Wu Gong.
Duke Wu died in his forty-seventh year and was succeeded by his son Duke Jing.
In the twenty-third year of Duke Jing's reign, his son Gong Gong succeeded him.
Duke Gong died after eight years in office and was succeeded by his son De Gong.
Duke De died in the eighteenth year of his reign, and his younger brother Huan Gonggu Rong succeeded him.
Duke Huan died in the seventeenth year of his reign and was succeeded by his younger brother Xiao Gong.
Xiaogong died in the seventeenth year of his reign, and his younger brother Wen Gongyigu succeeded him.
Duke Wen died in the fourteenth year of his reign, and his younger brother Ping Gongyu succeeded him.
Ping Gong died in the eighteenth year of his reign, and his son Yu Gongcheng succeeded him.
Duke Yao passed away in the 12th year of his reign, and his son Yin Gong begged to succeed him.
In the seventh month, Yin Gong's younger brother killed Yin Gong and established himself as king, namely Li Gong Gong.
Li Gong died in the 19th year of his reign, and his son Li Gongwei succeeded him.
In the fifteenth year of Duke Min's reign, King Hui of Chu destroyed the state of Chen.
In the sixteenth year, Min Gong's younger brother Quelu killed Min Gong and established himself as king, namely Ai Gong.
Duke Ai died after reigning for ten years, and Duke Min's son succeeded him by imperial decree.
Chugong died after reigning for 12 years, and his son Jian Gongchun succeeded him.
One year after Duke Jian came to the throne, which was the forty-fourth year of King Hui of Chu, Chu destroyed Qi State.
Qi State fell thirty-four years later than Chen State.
The descendants of Shun were granted the title of Chen by King Wu of Zhou, but were exterminated by King Hui of Chu. This is recorded in "Aristocratic Family". After Yu's descendants, King Wu of Zhou granted him the title of Qi, and King Hui of Chu destroyed it, which is recorded in "Aristocratic Family".
The descendants of Qi are the Yin and Shang royal family, which are recorded in "Benji".
After the fall of the Yin Dynasty, the Zhou Dynasty granted its descendants to the Song Dynasty, and King Min of Qi destroyed the Song Dynasty, which is recorded in "Shijia".
The descendants of Hou Ji are the royal family of the Zhou Dynasty. King Qin Zhao destroyed the Zhou Dynasty, which is recorded in "Benji".
Some of Gaotao's descendants were sealed in the lands of Ying and Liu. King Chu Mu destroyed them, and there is no genealogical record. The descendants of Boyi were granted the title of Taigongwang in Qi during the reign of King Wu of Zhou Dynasty. The Chen family destroyed it, which is recorded in "Shijia".
Chui, Yi, Kui and Long, their descendants do not know where they were sealed, and no one has heard of them. The above eleven people were all famous ministers of merit and virtue during the reign of Yao and Shun; the descendants of five of them have been emperors, and the rest are famous princes.
Teng, Xue, and Zou were feudal states during the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties. They were small and not worth mentioning, so they were not included in the list.
During the reign of King Wu of Zhou, there were more than a thousand people who were granted the title of marquis or uncle.
After King You of Zhou became King Li of Zhou, the princes used their strength to attack each other and annexed each other.
There are countless small countries such as Jiang, Huang, Hu, and Shen, so they are not recorded in historical biographies.
Tai Shigong said: Shun's morality has reached its extreme!
He abdicated the throne to Xia Yu, and his descendants could still enjoy sacrifices through the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties.
After the State of Chu destroyed the State of Chen, Tian Chang took over the power of the State of Qi. Finally, it was still a feudal state, which lasted for hundreds of generations, with prosperous descendants and many people who were granted land.
As for Yu, his descendants were the kings of Qi during the Zhou Dynasty. They were very weak and not worth mentioning.
After King Hui of Chu destroyed Qi, King Goujian of Yue, a descendant of Yu, revived.
summary: The lineage and history of the State of Chen, founded by Duke Hu, a descendant of Emperor Shun. After Shun’s death, his descendants held intermittent titles until King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Guiman (Duke Hu) in Chen to continue Shun’s sacrifices. The succession of Chen rulers is detailed, including Dukes Shen, Xiang, Xiao, You, Li, Wu, Yi, Ping, Wen, Huan, Li, Zhuang, Xuan, Mu, Gong, Ling, Cheng, Ai, Hui, Huai, and Min. Key events include Duke Li’s son Wan fleeing to Qi after fearing persecution, where his descendants later rose to power. During Duke Xuan’s reign, internal strife led to the killing of Crown Prince Yu Kou. Duke Ling’s adultery with Xia Ji and subsequent murder by her son Xia Zhengshu prompted King Zhuang of Chu to invade Chen, initially annexing it but later restoring it after advice from Minister Shen. Chen later broke its alliance with Chu, leading to repeated Chu invasions. Duke Ai’s death involved a succession crisis where his brother Zhao killed the crown prince, leading to Chu’s destruction of Chen under King Ling. King Ping of Chu later restored Chen by enfeoffing Wu (Duke Hui). The state was finally destroyed by King Hui of Chu during Duke Min’s reign. The text also briefly covers the Qi state (descendants of Yu), noting its fall 34 years after Chen. It concludes with a reflection on the enduring legacy of Shun’s descendants, contrasting their prosperity with the decline of Yu’s line, and mentions other ancient states like Teng, Xue, and Zou as minor and unrecorded.

translation:
Chen Sheng, a native of Yangcheng, was named She.
Wu Guang, a native of Yangxia, was given the courtesy name Uncle.
When Chen She was young, he was hired to plow the fields with others. Once when he stopped plowing and went to rest on the ridge of the field, he lamented and resented for a long time and said, "If anyone becomes rich in the future, let's not forget each other."
The companions who were employed with him smiled and replied: You are hired to plow the fields, how can you be rich? Chen She sighed and said: Alas!
How can small birds such as swallows and sparrows understand the lofty aspirations of geese and swans!
In July of the first year of Qin II, the poor living on the left side of the lane were recruited to defend Yuyang. A total of 900 people were stationed in Daze Township.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang both joined the ranks of this expedition and became village commanders.
It happened to be raining heavily and the roads were blocked. They probably missed the deadline to reach Yuyang.
After the prescribed time limit, everyone should be beheaded according to the law.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang discussed it and said: Now it is death to escape, and it is death to rise up and do a great cause. It is also death. Is it good to die for national affairs?
Chen Sheng said: The world has been suffering from the rule of the Qin Dynasty for a long time.
I heard that the second emperor was the youngest son of the first emperor. He should not succeed to the throne. The one who should succeed was the young master Fusu.
Because Fusu repeatedly advised the emperor, the emperor sent him to lead troops to station in other places.
Now some people heard that he was not guilty of any crime, but was killed by the second emperor.
The common people heard that he was very virtuous, but they didn't know that he was dead.
Xiang Yan was originally a general of the Chu State. He had made many meritorious deeds and loved his soldiers. The people of Chu State loved him.
Some people thought he was dead, others thought he was on the run and hiding.
Now, if we use the names of Princes Fusu and Xiang Yan to call for uprising to the people of the world, many people will respond.
Wu Guang thinks it is right.
So he went to divine good and bad luck. The fortune teller knew their intentions and said: "You can succeed in everything and make achievements."
But have you ever asked ghosts and gods about good or bad luck?
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were very happy. They tried to figure out what the fortune teller meant by asking ghosts and gods about good or bad luck, and said, "This is to teach us to establish prestige among others first."
So he wrote the words "King Chen Sheng" on a piece of white silk with cinnabar, and stuffed it into the belly of the fish caught by others in a net.
The garrison soldier bought the fish and cooked it. He found the silk book in the fish belly and naturally felt very strange about it. Chen Sheng also secretly sent Wu Guang to an ancient temple overgrown with vegetation near the station, lit a bonfire at night, and imitated the voice of a fox and shouted: "Great Chu Xing, King Chen Sheng." The garrison soldiers were frightened when they heard this cry in the middle of the night.
The next morning, there was a lot of discussion among the garrison troops, and everyone was pointing and looking at Chen Sheng.
Wu Guang has always cared about others, and many people were willing to serve him.
Once, the county captain escorting the team was drunk. Wu Guang deliberately threatened to escape many times to anger the county captain, provoke him to humiliate him in public, and anger everyone.
As expected, the county lieutenant whipped Wu Guang, and the county lieutenant drew his sword again. Wu Guang rose up, grabbed the sword, and killed the county lieutenant.
Chen Sheng assisted Wu Guang and killed two county captains together.
Then he summoned his subordinates and said: "Everyone has encountered heavy rain here. Everyone has missed the deadline to go to Yuyang. If you miss the deadline, you will be beheaded according to regulations."
Even if they are not beheaded, six out of ten people will definitely die while guarding the border in the future.
Besides, as long as a man dies, he must be famous for future generations. Are princes, generals and ministers all born noble?
After hearing this, all the subordinates said in unison: We are willing to obey the orders.
So Chen Sheng and others staged an uprising in the name of Prince Fusu and Chu general Xiang Yan to comply with the people's wishes.
Everyone showed their right arms as a sign, under the banner of "Great Chu".
They also built a high platform to take the oath and used the general's head as a sacrifice.
Chen Sheng appointed himself as general and Wu Guang as captain.
First they attacked Daze Township, and after that they attacked Qixian County.
After Qixian was captured, he sent Ge Ying from Fuli to lead his troops to capture the area east of Qixian.
They attacked Qi, Feng, Kuzhe and Qiao in succession and captured them all.
As they marched, they continued to replenish their troops and expand their ranks. By the time they reached Chen County, they had six to seven hundred chariots, more than a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry.
When Chen County was attacked, the county guards and magistrates there were not in the city. Only the county magistrate who stayed behind led the troops and fought with the rebels under the city gate.
As a result, the county magistrate was defeated and died, so the rebel army entered the city and occupied Chen County.
A few days later, Chen Sheng ordered the three elders in charge of education and local heroes to be summoned for a meeting.
Everyone present said: General, you are wearing armor and holding sharp weapons. You have attacked the unprincipled king, destroyed the tyrannical Qin Dynasty, and re-established the Chu State. In terms of merit, you should be called the king. Chen She then proclaimed himself king and named his country Zhang Chu.
At this time, the people in various counties and counties who suffered due to the governance of the officials of the Qin Dynasty responded to Chen She by hijacking the officials to judge their crimes and killing them.
So Wu Guang was appointed as the acting king and led the generals to attack Xingyang westward.
He ordered Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu from Chen County to capture the original jurisdiction of Zhao, and ordered Deng Zong from Ruyin to capture Jiujiang County.
At this time, thousands of rebels from the Chu region gathered together, too many to count.
Ge Ying arrived at Dongcheng and established Xiang Qiang as King of Chu.
Ge Ying later heard that Chen Sheng had proclaimed himself king, so he killed Xiang Qiang and reported back to Chen Sheng.
As soon as he arrived in Chen County, Chen Sheng killed Ge Ying.
Chen Sheng ordered Wei people Zhou Shi to go north to capture the places that originally belonged to the Wei state.
Wu Guang surrounded Xingyang.
Li You was appointed as the governor of Sanchuan County to defend Xingyang, but Wu Guang could not attack it for a long time.
Chen Sheng summoned the heroes of the country to discuss countermeasures and appointed Cai Ci, the Lord of Shangcai Renfang, as the Shangzhu Kingdom.
Zhou Wen was a well-known sage in Chen County. He was once an official in Xiang Yan's army who divined good and bad times, and also served under Huang Xie, Prime Minister of Chu Chunshen. He claimed to be familiar with military affairs, so King Chen awarded him the seal of general and ordered him to lead troops west to attack the Qin army.
He gathered troops and horses as he walked along the way. When he arrived at Hangu Pass, there were thousands of chariots and hundreds of thousands of soldiers. When they arrived at the theater, they stationed themselves.
The Qin Dynasty sent Shaofu Zhang Han to pardon those who had committed crimes and served in Lishan Mountain, as well as the sons of domestic slaves, and recruited them all to attack Zhang Chu's army and defeated all the Chu army. After Zhou Wen failed, he escaped from Hangu Pass and stayed in Caoyang for two or three months.
Zhang Han chased him again and defeated him. Zhou Wen fled to Mianchi and stayed there for more than ten days.
Zhang Han came to pursue him again and defeated him miserably.
Zhou Wen committed suicide, and his army could no longer fight.
When the military minister arrived at Handan, he proclaimed himself King of Zhao, Chen Yu became the general, and Zhang Er and Zhao Sao became the prime ministers of the left and right.
King Chen was very angry when he found out, so he arrested and imprisoned the family members of Wu Chen and others, intending to kill them.
Cai Ci of the Shangzhu State said: Killing the family members of King Zhao, generals and ministers before the Qin Dynasty was destroyed, this is tantamount to giving birth to another Qin State that is our enemy.
It is better to take this opportunity to make him the king of Zhao.
King Chen then sent envoys to the State of Zhao to congratulate him. At the same time, he moved the family members of the military officials and others to the palace and placed them under house arrest. He also made Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao the king of Chengdu, and urged the Zhao army to march to Hangu Pass as soon as possible.
The generals and ministers of King Zhao's military officials discussed and said: Your Majesty, it is not Chu's original intention to proclaim yourself king in the land of Zhao.
After Chu defeats Qin, he will definitely attack Zhao.
The best way is not to send troops to march westward, but to send people northward to capture the original jurisdiction of Yan State to expand our own territory.
Zhao State is surrounded by the natural dangers of the Yellow River to the south, and the vast lands of Yan and Dai are to the north. Even if Chu State defeated Qin State, it would not dare to suppress Zhao State.
If Chu could not defeat Qin, it would definitely rely on Zhao.
At that time, Zhao State will be able to realize its ambition to rule the world by taking advantage of Qin State's weakness.
King Zhao thought it was reasonable, so he did not send troops westward. Instead, he sent Han Guang, a former soldier of Shanggu County, to lead troops north to capture Yan.
The former aristocratic heroes of Yan State advised Han Guang: Chu State has established a king, and Zhao State has also established a king.
Although the Yan State is small, it used to be a country with tens of thousands of military chariots. I hope that you, general, will become the king of Yan on your own.
Han Guang replied: My mother is still in Zhao State and cannot do this.
The people of Yan said: Zhao is worried about Qin to the west and Chu to the south. Its power cannot restrain us.
Moreover, the state of Chu was so powerful that it did not dare to kill the family members of the king of Zhao, generals and ministers. How could the state of Zhao dare to kill the family members of your general? Han Guang thought what they said was reasonable, so he became King of Yan on his own.
After a few months, the State of Zhao sent people to escort the mother of King Yan and her family to the State of Yan.
At this time, countless generals went to various places to attack cities and occupy territory.
Zhou Shi went north to capture the city and reached Di County. Tian Dan, a native of Di County, killed the magistrate of Di County and proclaimed himself the king of Qi. He relied on the power of Qi to counterattack Zhou Shi.
Zhou Shi's army was defeated and retreated to Wei, intending to make Ningling Junjiu, a descendant of King Wei, king of Wei.
At that time, Jiu was with King Chen and could not return to Wei.
After Wei was pacified, everyone wanted to support Zhou Shi as King of Wei, but Zhou Shi refused to accept it.
The envoys went back and forth between King Chen and Zhou City five times. King Chen agreed to make Ningling Jun Jiu the king of Wei and sent him back to Wei.
Zhou Shi finally became the prime minister of Wei.
General Tian Zang and others jointly planned and said: Zhou Zhang's army has been defeated, and the Qin Dynasty's army will arrive sooner or later. Our army surrounds Xingyang City and cannot conquer it. If the Qin army comes, it will be defeated.
It is better to leave less troops, enough to surround Xingyang, and lead all the elite troops to meet the Qin army.
Now the false king Wu Guang is arrogant and rude, and does not know the tactics of using troops to fight. We cannot discuss with him. If we don't kill him, the matter may fail.
Therefore, they falsely reported that King Chen had ordered Uncle Wu to be killed and his head was dedicated to King Chen.
King Chen sent an envoy to give Tian Zang the official seal of Ling Yin of Chu State and appointed him as the general.
Tian Zang sent his general Li Gui and others to surround Xingyang City, and he led his elite troops westward to Aocang to meet the Qin army.
Fighting with the Qin army, Tian Zang died in the battle and the army was defeated.
Zhang Han marched to Xingyang City to attack Li Gui and others, defeated them, and Li Gui and others died in the battle.
Deng Yue, a native of Yangcheng, led his troops to station in Jiacheng, but was defeated by a force led by Zhang Han's general. Deng Yue led his army to flee to Chen County.
Wu Xu, a Zhi man, led his troops to station in Xu County, but Zhang Han's army defeated him. Wu Xu's army broke up and fled to Chen County.
King Chen killed Deng and said.
When Chen Sheng first became king, Qin Jia from Ling County, Dong Jie from Zhi County, Zhu Jishi from Fuli, Zheng Bu from Qilu, and Ding Ji from Xu County all formed an army to rebel against Qin. They led their troops and besieged the governor of Donghai County named Qing in Tancheng.
After King Chen heard about it, he sent Wu Pingjun as a general to supervise and lead all the armies under Tan City.
Qin Jia refused to accept this order and established himself as Grand Sima, not wanting to be subordinate to Lord Wuping.
Then he told his military officials: Mr. Wu Ping is young and does not understand military affairs. Don't listen to him!
Then he killed Wu Pingpan under the pretense of King Chen's order.
After Zhang Han defeated Wu Xu, he then attacked Chen County. Cai Ci, the king of Chen's state, was killed in the battle.
Zhang Han then led troops to attack Zhang He's troops stationed in the west of Chen County.
King Chen personally came out to supervise the battle, but the Chu army was still defeated and Zhang He was killed.
In December, King Chen retreated to Ruyin. When he returned to Xiachengfu, his coachman Zhuang Jia killed him and surrendered to the Qin army.
After Chen Sheng's death, he was buried in Dang County, and his posthumous title was King Yin.
General Lu Chen, a former minister of King Chen, organized a "Cangtou Army" with their heads wrapped in green scarves. They attacked Chen County from Xinyang. After conquering, they killed Zhuang Jia and made Chen County the capital of Chu.
At first, when King Chen first arrived in Chen County, he ordered Song Liu, a native of Zhi County, to lead troops to pacify Nanyang and then march to Wuguan.
After Song Liu captured Nanyang, news came that King Chen had been killed, so Nanyang was taken back by the Qin army.
Song Liu could not enter Wuguan, so he went east to Xincai. Unexpectedly, he encountered the Qin army again. Song Liu led his troops and surrendered to the Qin army.
The Qin army escorted Song Liu to Xianyang and dismantled his car to show the public.
When Qin Jia and others heard that King Chen's army had been defeated and fled, they made Jing Ju king of Chu and led their troops to Fangyu, preparing to attack the Qin army near Dingtao.
So he sent Gongsun Qing as an envoy to Qi State to meet with Qi King Tian Dan, hoping to unite with him to march together.
King Qi said: I heard that King Chen was defeated and his life and death are still unknown. How could the State of Chu declare itself king without coming to me for instructions?
Gongsun Qing said: Qi established a king without asking Chu for instructions. Why did Chu ask Qi for instructions before establishing a king?
What's more, Chu was the first to revolt against Qin, so he should give orders to the world.
Tian Dan killed Gongsun Qing.
The left and right captains of the Qin army led their troops to attack Chen County again and occupied it.
After General Lu Chen failed to escape, he regrouped his troops.
He joined forces with the army led by Yingbu, who had been a thief in Poyang and was named Dangyang Lord, and attacked the army of Qin's left and right captains again, defeated them at Qingbo, and once again made Chen County the capital of Chu.
Just when Xiang Liang supported King Huai of Chu, his grandson Xin became King of Chu.
Chen Sheng was king for a total of six months.
After becoming king, Chen County was made the capital.
Once upon a time, a fellow who had been hired to plow fields with him heard that he had become king. He came to Chen County, knocked on the palace door and said, "I want to see Chen She."
The officer guarding the palace gate wanted to tie him up.
After he repeatedly explained, he was released, but still refused to inform him.
When King Chen went out, he blocked the road and called Chen She's name.
After hearing this, King Chen summoned him and took a carriage back to the palace with him.
After walking into the palace and seeing the halls, houses and curtains, the guest said: Hello!
King Chen She's palace is so tall and profound!
The people of Chu called Duo Huo She the king, so the saying that Huo She was the king started from Chen She.
This guest came and went in and out of the palace more and more freely, and often told people about Chen She's past events.
Someone said to King Chen: Your guest is ignorant and talks nonsense, which is detrimental to your majesty.
King Chen killed the visitor.
From then on, all the old and close friends of King Chen left voluntarily, and no one was close to King Chen anymore.
King Chen appointed Zhu Fang to be the Zhongzheng and Hu Wu to be the Supervisor of Supervision to supervise the faults of the ministers.
The generals captured the place and returned to Chen County. If they disobeyed the orders, they would arrest and punish them, and they would harshly seek the faults of the officials as a sign of loyalty to King Chen.
Anyone they don't like, once they make a mistake, they will punish them without giving it to the officials in charge of justice. King Chen trusted them very much.
Because of these reasons, the generals no longer stayed close to him. This is the reason why King Chen failed.
Although Chen Sheng was dead, the princes and generals he appointed and sent finally destroyed the Qin Dynasty. This was due to Chen She's first uprising against Qin.
During the reign of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, thirty families were placed in Dang County to guard Chen She's tomb, and they still kill animals on time to offer sacrifices to him.
Mr. Chu said: The terrain is dangerous and difficult to traverse in order to consolidate defense; the military reform of weapons and criminal law system is in order to rule the country.
These are still insufficient to rely on.
The former kings regarded benevolence and righteousness as the foundation for governing the country, but regarded strong fortresses and legal provisions as trivial matters. Isn't it right?
I heard Jia Sheng once said:
Qin Xiaogong occupies the dangerous terrain of Xiaoshan and Hangu, and owns the entire Yongzhou area. The monarchs and ministers are firmly guarding it, and they can always spy on the Zhou Dynasty's regime.
At that time, Shang Yang assisted Qin Xiaogong, established a legal system internally, devoted himself to farming and weaving, improved offensive and defensive weapons, and used the strategy of liaison and hegemony externally to make the princes fight against each other.
So Qin State easily and effortlessly acquired a large area of ​​land west of the Yellow River, just like two hands joined together.
After the death of Duke Xiao of Qin, King Huiwen, King Wu, and King Zhaoxiang of Qin took over the governance of Qin Xiaogong. Following the strategies left by their ancestors, they captured Hanzhong to the south, Bashu to the southwest, fertile land to the east, and strategic and dangerous counties to the north.
The princes were frightened and panicked because of this, and they met to form an alliance to discuss countermeasures to weaken Qin.
They spare no effort in precious treasures and fertile land to recruit talents from all over the world.
Adopt a cooperative strategy to form an alliance, support each other, and become one body.
At this time, the state of Qi has Lord Mengchang, the state of Zhao has Lord Pingyuan, the state of Chu has Lord Chunshen, and the state of Wei has Lord Xinling: these four princes are all wise, loyal and trustworthy, generous and kind-hearted and cherish talents, respect the wise and value scholars.
They agreed with each other to implement a joint vertical alliance to resist Qin and destroy Qin's alliance and horizontal strategy, and to unite relevant people from Han, Wei, Yan, Chu, Qi, Zhao, Song, Wei, Zhongshan and other countries.
So the talents of the Six Kingdoms included Ning Yue, Xu Shang, Su Qin, and Du He to plan for them; Qi Ming, Zhou Zui, Chen Zhen, Shao Hua, Lou Su, Zhai Jing, Su Li, and Leyi communicated their opinions; Wu Qi, Sun Bin, Dai Tuo, Ni Liang, Wang Liao, Tian Ji, Lian Po, and Zhao She commanded their armies.
The princes used ten times the land of Qin and an army of millions to attack Hangu Pass and attack Qin.
Qin opened the door to meet the enemy, but the armies of the nine kingdoms fled and did not dare to advance.
Qin did not waste a single arrow, but the princes in the world were exhausted.
So the alliance was dissolved, the alliance was broken, and each of them competed to cede territory to bribe Qin.
The Qin State had enough power to take advantage of the weaknesses of the princes, chase the fleeing enemies, and kill millions of their corpses, and the blood would float the big shields. The Qin State took advantage of the favorable situation and the convenient opportunity to divide the land, mountains and rivers, so the strong countries asked for submission, and the weak countries came to worship and profess their surrender.
It lasted until King Xiaowen and King Zhuang Xiang of Qin. Their reign was short and no major events happened in the country.
As far as Qin Shihuang, he carried forward the achievements passed down from six generations, whipped the princes like a chariot, annexed the two small kingdoms of Eastern Zhou and Western Zhou, annihilated the princes of the six countries, ascended the throne of emperor and controlled the world, whipped the people of the world with a cane, and frightened the world with his majesty.
They seized the land of Baiyue in the south and made it Guilin County and Xiang County. The princes of Baiyue lowered their heads, tied their necks with ropes to surrender, and put their lives in the hands of the lower-level officials of the Qin Dynasty.
So he sent Meng Tian to the north to build the Great Wall as a barrier to defend the border, and drove the Huns more than 700 miles north. The Huns did not dare to go south to herd horses, and the soldiers did not dare to set up their bows and arrows to take revenge.
So he abolished the way of governing the country and burned the works of various scholars in order to make the people ignorant. He also destroyed famous cities in various places, killed heroes, collected all the weapons in the world and concentrated them in Xianyang, melted swords and arrows, and cast them into twelve metal statues to weaken the resistance of the people of the world.
Then rely on Huashan Mountain as a city wall, rely on the Yellow River as a moat, rely on Huashan Mountain hundreds of millions of feet high, and guard the unpredictable Yellow River as a dangerous place to guard.
Good generals hold strong bows to defend important places; reliable ministers lead capable soldiers, arrayed with sharp weapons, and strictly check who is passing by.
The world was at peace, and Qin Shihuang thought that the Guanzhong was strong, like a thousand-mile golden city, which could serve as the foundation for his descendants to be emperors for eternity.
After Qin Shihuang died, his remaining power still shocked people from afar.
However, Chen She was a son of a poor family who used broken urns as windows and tied the door shafts with straw ropes. He was a farmer, a servant, and a conscripted guard on the border.
His talents are not comparable to those of ordinary people. He is not as wise as Confucius and Mozi, nor as rich as Tao Zhu and Yidun. He is among the ranks of the garrison, rising up in the countryside, leading the tired and scattered garrison soldiers. He commanded hundreds of people and turned around to attack Qin, cutting down wooden sticks as weapons and holding high bamboo poles as flags. The people of the world gathered together quickly like wind and clouds, rose up like echoes, carried grains, and followed him like a shadow. The heroes from the east of Hangu Pass in Xiaoshan rose up together and overthrew the Qin Dynasty.
Besides, the Qin Dynasty's world has not been reduced or weakened; the land of Yongzhou and the danger of Hangu Pass in Xiaoshan are still as strong as before.
Chen She's status was no more noble than that of the kings of Qi, Chu, Yan, Zhao, Han, Song, Wei, and Zhongshan; the handles of his hoes and halberds were no sharper than those of hooked halberds and spears; the people who were recruited to guard the borders were no more powerful than the armies of the Nine Kingdoms; and his foresight, marching, and combat command skills were not as good as those of the talented men of the previous six kingdoms.
But success and failure are completely different; merit is completely opposite. What is the reason?
If the princes from various countries east of Mount Wei and Hangu Pass were compared with Chen She to measure their length, compare their size, compare their authority, and measure their strength, they would simply not be of the same age or be compared to each other.
However, Qin State relied on a small area to develop into a powerful state with tens of thousands of chariots, and then controlled the other eight states, causing other vassal states with the same status to come to pay homage to Qin State. This has a history of more than a hundred years.
Then regard the four directions of heaven and earth as your home, and regard Mount Wei and Hanguguan as the palace walls.
But Chen She initiated the uprising alone, and the seventh generation ancestral temple of the Qin Dynasty was destroyed. Even the prince of Qin died in the hands of others and was ridiculed by everyone in the world. What is the reason?
This is because the situation of conquering the world without practicing benevolent government is different from that of defending the world later.
summary:
Chen Sheng, a native of Yangcheng, and Wu Guang, from Yangxia, were conscripted in July of the first year of Qin II to defend Yuyang, along with 900 others stationed in Daze Township. Heavy rain blocked the roads, causing them to miss the deadline, which meant execution by law. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang discussed that fleeing or rising up both led to death, but dying for a national cause was preferable. Chen Sheng noted the world’s suffering under Qin rule, suggesting using the names of Prince Fusu and Chu general Xiang Yan to rally support, as both were respected. Wu Guang agreed. They consulted a fortune teller, who hinted at establishing prestige through supernatural means. Chen Sheng wrote “King Chen Sheng” on silk, hid it in a fish, and had Wu Guang mimic a fox’s cry at night, shouting “Great Chu will rise, King Chen Sheng.” The garrison soldiers were startled and discussed it the next day.

Wu Guang, known for his care, provoked a drunken county captain, who whipped him and drew his sword. Wu Guang killed the captain, and Chen Sheng helped kill two others. Chen Sheng addressed the troops, stating that missing the deadline meant beheading, and even if spared, many would die guarding borders. He declared that princes and generals were not born noble. The troops pledged obedience. They rebelled in the names of Fusu and Xiang Yan, baring their right arms under the banner “Great Chu.” They built an altar, sacrificed the captain’s head, and Chen Sheng declared himself general, Wu Guang as captain. They attacked Daze Township and Qi County, then sent Ge Ying to capture eastern areas, taking Qi, Feng, Kuzhe, and Qiao. As they marched, their forces grew to six to seven hundred chariots, over a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry by the time they reached Chen County. The county magistrate was killed, and they occupied the city.

Chen Sheng summoned local elders and heroes, who praised him for attacking the tyrannical Qin and re-establishing Chu, urging him to become king. He proclaimed himself king of Zhang Chu. People in various counties responded by killing Qin officials. Wu Guang was appointed acting king to attack Xingyang westward. Chen Sheng ordered Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to capture Zhao, and Deng Zong to take Jiujiang. Ge Ying killed Xiang Qiang, whom he had made king of Chu, after hearing of Chen Sheng’s kingship, but Chen Sheng executed Ge Ying. Zhou Shi was sent north to capture Wei lands. Wu Guang besieged Xingyang but failed to take it. Chen Sheng appointed Cai Ci as Shangzhu Kingdom and Zhou Wen as general to lead troops west. Zhou Wen gathered forces, reaching Hangu Pass with thousands of chariots and hundreds of thousands of soldiers, but was defeated by Qin’s Zhang Han, who recruited criminals and slaves. Zhou Wen fled and committed suicide after repeated defeats.

Wu Chen proclaimed himself King of Zhao in Handan. Chen Sheng, angered, imprisoned Wu Chen’s family but released them on Cai Ci’s advice, sending congratulations to Zhao. Zhao’s generals advised against marching west, instead expanding north into Yan. Han Guang became King of Yan. Zhou Shi was defeated by Tian Dan, who declared himself King of Qi. Zhou Shi made Ningling Jun Jiu King of Wei. Tian Zang killed Wu Guang, claiming Chen Sheng’s order, and led elite troops west but died in battle. Zhang Han defeated other Chu forces. Chen Sheng killed Deng Yue and Wu Xu after their defeats. Qin Jia killed Wu Pingpan and made Jing Ju king of Chu. Zhang Han attacked Chen County, killing Cai Ci. Chen Sheng was defeated and killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia in December. He was buried in Dang County with the posthumous title King Yin. Lu Chen killed Zhuang Jia and made Chen County Chu’s capital. Song Liu surrendered to Qin and was executed. Chen Sheng reigned for six months. His former friend visited but was killed for speaking of past events, causing others to leave. Chen Sheng appointed Zhu Fang and Hu Wu, who harshly punished officials, leading to his failure. Despite his death, his uprising led to Qin’s downfall. Emperor Gaozu of Han later honored his tomb.

The ancestor of Korea has the same surname as Emperor Zhou, Ji.
His descendants were entrusted to the Jin State and were sealed in Han Yuan, known as Han Wuzi.
After Han Wuzi, Han Jue was born in three generations, and the name of his fiefdom was Han Weishi.

Zhao Dun was already dead, so he wanted to kill his son Zhao Shuo.
Han Jue tried to stop Tu'anjia, but Tu'anjia refused to listen.
Han Jue went to tell Zhao Shuo and let him escape.
Zhao Shuo said: "You must not cut off the descendants of the Zhao family, and there will be no regrets after my death."
Han Jue agreed to him.
When Tu'anjia killed the Zhao family, Han Jue claimed that he was ill and could not leave home.
Cheng Ying and Gongsun Jiu hid Zhao Wu, the orphan of the Zhao family, and Han Jue knew about it.
In the eleventh year of Jin Jinggong's reign, Han Jue and Chuke led a force of 800 chariots to conquer Qi. They defeated Qi Qinggong in An and captured Feng Chou's father.
From this time on, the Jin State established six ministers, and Han Jue ranked first, named Xianzi.
In the seventeenth year of Jin Jinggong's reign, Jinggong fell ill, and the divination results said that there were unfavorable people among Daye's descendants who were causing trouble.
Han Jue praised Zhao Shui's achievements and said that he had no one to continue the incense, so as to impress Jinggong.
Jinggong asked: "Does he have any descendants?"
Han Jue talked about Zhao Wu at that time, and Jinggong gave him the original Tianyi of Zhao family again, so that he could continue Zhao family's incense.
In the seventh year of Jin's reign, Han Xianzi grew old.
After Xianzi's death, his son Xuanzi inherited the title.
Xuanzi moved to Zhouyi.
In the fourteenth year of Jin Ping Gong's reign, Jizha of Wu State went to Jin State as an envoy. He said: The political power of Jin State will eventually belong to the three families of Han, Wei and Zhao.
In the twelfth year of Jin Qinggong's reign, Han Xuanzi, Zhao and Wei families divided themselves into ten counties of Qi and Yangyu.
In the fifteenth year of Duke Dinggong of Jin Dynasty, Han Xuanzi and Zhao Jianzi attacked Fan and Zhonghang families.
Xuanzi died, and his son Sadako inherited the title.
Sadako moved to Pingyang.
Han Zhenzi died and his son Jianzi succeeded to the throne.
Han Jianzi died and his son Zhuangzi succeeded to the throne.
Han Zhuangzi died and his son Kangzi succeeded him.

After Han Kangzi died, his son Wuzi succeeded to the throne.

In the sixteenth year, Han Wuzi died, and his son Jinghou came to the throne.

In the sixth year of Jinghou, Han, Zhao and Wei were recognized as vassal states.
In the ninth year of Jinghou, Zheng Guo surrounded Yangzhai in South Korea.

In the ninth year, Qin attacked Yiyang in South Korea and occupied Liuyi.
In the thirteenth year, Liehou died and his son Wenhou came to the throne.

He attacked the Song Dynasty, reached Pengcheng, and captured the king of Song Dynasty.
In the seventh year, he attacked Qi and reached Sanqiu.
The state of Zheng rebelled against the state of Jin.
In the ninth year, South Korea attacked Qi and reached Lingqiu.

In the first year of Han Aihou, Han, the three families of Zhao and Wei divided the Kingdom of Jin.
In the second year, South Korea destroyed the Zheng State and moved the capital to Xinzheng.
In the sixth year of Aihou, Han Yan killed his king Aihou, and Aihou's son Yihou came to the throne.

In the fifth year, the Marquis of Han and King Hui of Wei met in Zhaiyang.

In the second year, the Song Dynasty captured Huangchi in South Korea.
Wei State captured Zhuyi.
In the sixth year, the Han army conquered the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and captured Lingguan and Xingqiu.
In the eighth year of Zhaohou, Shen Buhe was appointed as the prime minister of South Korea. He used the monarch's power to control the ministers and implemented the Legalist way of governing the country. The country was stabilized and the princes did not dare to invade.
In the tenth year of Zhaohou, Han Ji killed his monarch, Duke Ai.
In the eleventh year, Zhaohou went to Qin.
In the twenty-second year, Shen Buhai passed away.
In the twenty-fourth year, the Qin army captured Yiyang in South Korea.

Qu Yijiu said: Zhaohou cannot get out of this gate.
Why?
Because it is inappropriate.

Zhaohou once had success, but he did not build Gaomen.

His son King Xuanhui ascended the throne.

In eight years, the Wei army defeated the Korean general Han Ju.
In the eleventh year, South Korea changed the title of King to King.
The king of Han and the king of Zhao met in District Rat.

So they strengthened their vigilance across the country, sent troops to rescue South Korea, and filled the roads with chariots. Then they sent envoys, equipped with many vehicles, and asked him to bring generous gifts to South Korea.

Besides, your Majesty has already sent people to inform the Qin State of our plans, and now he has decided not to go. This is deceiving the Qin State.
If you easily deceive the powerful Qin and listen to Chu's advisors, I'm afraid the king will definitely regret it.
The king of Han did not listen to the advice and finally broke off diplomatic relations with Qin.

In the 19th year, the Qin army defeated the Korean army at Anmen.
South Korea had no choice but to send Taizicang as a hostage to sue Qin for peace.

In five years, Qin captured Yiyang and killed 60,000 Korean troops.

In the ninth year, Qin once again captured Wu Sui in South Korea.

In the eleventh year, the Qin army attacked Han and occupied Rangyi.
South Korea and Qin attacked Chu and defeated Chu general Tang Mei.

Su said to Han Jiu: "He is in Chu State, and the King of Chu wants to send him back to his country."

Sima Geng, a native of Qin, traveled to and from the capital of Ying three times. Qin Prime Minister Gan Mao and Chu Prime Minister Zhao Yu met in Shangyu. summary: The ancestor of Korea shared the surname Ji with Emperor Zhou. His descendants were enfeoffed in Jin State at Han Yuan, becoming known as Han Wuzi. After three generations, Han Jue emerged, and his fief was called Han Weishi. During Duke Jinggong’s third year in Jin, Tu'anjia sought to kill Zhao Shuo, son of the deceased Zhao Dun. Han Jue tried to stop him but failed, then warned Zhao Shuo, who begged him not to let the Zhao line end. Han Jue agreed. When Tu'anjia massacred the Zhao family, Han Jue feigned illness. Cheng Ying and Gongsun Jiu hid the orphan Zhao Wu, which Han Jue knew. In the eleventh year, Han Jue and Chuke led 800 chariots to defeat Qi, capturing Feng Chou’s father. Jin then established six ministers, with Han Jue first, titled Xianzi. In the seventeenth year, Jinggong fell ill; divination blamed Daye’s descendants. Han Jue praised Zhao Shui’s deeds, prompting Jinggong to restore Zhao Wu to the Zhao line. Han Xianzi grew old and died, succeeded by his son Xuanzi, who moved to Zhouyi. In the fourteenth year of Jin Ping Gong, Jizha of Wu predicted Jin’s power would go to Han, Wei, and Zhao. Later, Han Xuanzi, Zhao, and Wei divided Qi and Yangyu counties, then attacked Fan and Zhonghang families. Xuanzi died, succeeded by Sadako, who moved to Pingyang. Subsequent rulers included Jianzi, Zhuangzi, Kangzi, and Wuzi. In Wuzi’s second year, Korea attacked Zheng, killing King Zheng Youhui. After Wuzi died, Jinghou reigned, attacking Zheng and occupying Yongqiu. In the sixth year of Jinghou, Han, Zhao, and Wei were recognized as vassal states. Later rulers included Liehou, Wenhou, Aihou, Yihou, Zhaohou, King Xuanhui, King Xiang, King Li, King Huanhui, and finally King Han, who was captured by Qin in the ninth year of his reign, ending Korea. Sima Qian noted that Han Jue’s act of restoring Zhao Wu was a rare virtue, and the Han family’s rise to princely status over ten generations was deserved.
