In the eleventh year, the Qin army captured Wei Qiu.
King Zhao of Qin said to his ministers: In which stage are Han and Wei stronger now than when they first started?
He replied: It is not as strong as when you first started.
The King of Qin said: "Compared with Ru'er and Wei Qi now, and Mengchang Lord and Mangmao in the past, who is more worthy?"
He replied: Ru'er and Wei Qi are not as good as Mengchangjun and Mangmao.
The King of Qin said: With the talents of Lord Mengchang and Mangmao, they led the strong troops of Han and Wei to attack Qin, but they still failed to do anything to me.
Now that the weak Han and Wei armies are led by the incompetent Ru'er and Wei Qi to attack Qin, it is obvious that they cannot do anything to me.
The courtiers on the left and right said: That's so right.
Zhongqi leaned on his qin and replied: Your Majesty's estimate of the world's situation was wrong.
When the Six Ministers of the Jin Dynasty were in power, the Zhi family was the strongest. They destroyed the Fan family and the Zhonghang family. They also led the troops of Han and Wei to besiege Zhao Xiangzi in Jinyang. They opened up the Jin River and flooded the Jinyang city, leaving only three levels high.
Zhibo inspected the water situation, Wei Huanzi drove the car, and Han Kangzi accompanied him on the right side of the car.
Zhibo said: At first I didn't know that water can destroy other people's countries, but now I know.
Since the Jin River can flood Jinyang, the Fen River can naturally flood Anyi, the capital of Wei, and the Jiang River can also flood Pingyang, the capital of Han.
So Wei Huanzi touched Han Kangzi with his elbow, and Han Kangzi also touched Wei Huanzi with his foot. The two made secret gestures with their elbows and feet in the car. As a result, Zhishi's territory was divided, Zhibo died and his country was destroyed, and he was laughed at by the people of the world.
Although the Qin soldiers are stronger now, they will not surpass Zhishi; although Han and Wei are weaker, they are still better than when they were under Jinyang City.
Now is the time for them to secretly unite with each other with their elbows and feet. I hope the king will not take the situation too simply!
So King Qin was a little frightened.
Qi and Chu united to attack Wei. Wei sent people to Qin to ask for help. There was an endless stream of envoys, but Qin's reinforcements did not come.
There was a man named Tang Sui in the State of Wei who was over ninety years old. He said to the King of Wei: The old minister requested to go to the west to lobby the King of Qin, and I must let the Qin army set off before I leave Qin.
When the king of Wei paid his respects again, he prepared his chariot and sent him there.
Tang Sui went to the Qin State and went to the palace to pay homage to the King of Qin.
The King of Qin said: It is so hard for the old man to come all the way to Qin State, exhausted!
Wei Guo has come to ask for help many times, and I know Wei Guo's crisis.
Tang Sui replied: Since the king already knew the crisis of Wei State but did not send reinforcements, I privately thought that the minister who made the plans was incompetent.
Wei was a big country with tens of thousands of chariots. The reason why Wei served Qin to the west, was called the Eastern vassal, accepted the clothes and crowns given by Qin, and sent sacrifices to Qin in spring and autumn, was because Qin was strong enough to become an ally.
Now the armies of Qi and Chu have gathered on the outskirts of Wei's capital, but Qin has not yet sent reinforcements, which means it is not too critical to rely on Wei.
If it comes to a particularly critical moment and it wants to cede territory to join the Hezong Group, what else are you going to save, Your Majesty?
You must wait until it is in danger before you save it. This means losing a Wei vassal in the east and strengthening the two enemy countries of Qi and Chu. So what benefits do you have, my king?
So King Zhao of Qin immediately sent troops to rescue Wei State, and Wei State restored stability.
The State of Zhao sent people to say to King Wei: "Kill Fan Cuo for me, and we are willing to give up seventy miles of land."
King Wei said: OK.
So he sent officials to arrest Fan Cuo and surrounded his home but did not kill him.
Fan Cuo then went up to the roof and rode on the ridge, and said to the envoy: It is better to trade with Fan Cuo alive than to trade with dead Fan Cuo.
If I, Fan Cuo, are killed but the State of Zhao does not give the king any land, what will the king do?
So it is better to demarcate the ceded land with Zhao Guo first, and then kill me. King Wei said: Very good.
Fan Cuo then wrote to Lord Xinling, saying: Fan Cuo was the prime minister who was dismissed from the Wei State in the past. The State of Zhao demanded that I be killed in exchange for ceding territory, but the King of Wei actually obeyed. If Qiang Qin follows the same method as the State of Zhao to treat you, what will you do?
Fan Cuo was released after Lord Xinling remonstrated with King Zhao.
Because Qin had rescued King Wei, he wanted to get close to Qin and attack South Korea in order to regain his original land.
Lord Xinling Wuji said to King Wei:
The people of Qin and Di Rong have the same customs. They are like tigers and wolves, greedy and vicious, greedy for profit but not trustworthy, and do not understand etiquette, justice and virtue.
If it is beneficial, they will not even care about their relatives and brothers, just like animals. Everyone in the world knows this, and they have never shown kindness or accumulated great virtues.
Therefore, the Queen Mother was originally the mother of the King of Qin, but she died of sorrow; Ranghou was the uncle of the King of Qin and had no greater merit than him, but she expelled him; the two younger brothers of the King of Qin were not guilty, but they were deprived of their fiefdoms again and again.
If this is true for relatives, how much more for the country of enemies?
Now that the king and Qin jointly attack South Korea, they will be closer to Qin's disaster. I am particularly confused.
Your Majesty, if you don't understand this principle, you are ignorant. If your monarch and ministers do not come to report this principle to you, they are disloyal.
Nowadays, Korea relies on a woman to assist a young and weak monarch. There is great chaos in the country, and there is a battle with the strong troops of Qin and Wei outside. Does the king think it will survive?
After the fall of Korea, the State of Qin will occupy the land of the original State of Zheng, adjacent to Daliang. Does the king think there will be peace?
If the king wants to get the original land, he must rely on his closeness to the powerful Qin. Does the king think this will be beneficial?
The Qin State is not a peaceful country. After the fall of South Korea, there will be another trouble. If another trouble occurs, it must find an easy and beneficial target. If you look for an easy and beneficial target, you must not go to Chu and Zhao.
Why is this?
If you cross the Yellow River across the mountains and pass through Shangdang in South Korea to attack the powerful Zhao State, it will be a repeat of the defeat of Yan Yu. Qin will definitely not do this.
If we go through Hanoi, turn our backs to Yecheng and Chaoge, cross the Zhang River and Fu River, and fight the Zhao army on the outskirts of Handan, we will encounter the same disaster as Zhibo, and Qin dare not do this.
To attack the Chu State, one has to go through Shibuya and march three thousand miles to attack the Ming'e Pass. The road is too far and the place to attack is too difficult, and Qin State will not do this.
If we take the route outside the river, with our back to Daliang, and Shangcai and Zhaoling on our right, we will have a decisive battle with the Chu army on the outskirts of Chencheng, but Qin will not dare.
Therefore, Qin will definitely not attack Chu and Zhao, let alone Wei and Qi.
After the fall of Korea, when Qin sent troops, there was no one to attack except Wei.
The Qin State already occupied Huaiyi, Maoyi, and Xingqiu. If it built a city at Qinjin and approached Hanoi, Gongcheng and Jiyi in Hanoi would be in danger; the Qin State occupied Zheng's homeland, gained Yuanyong City, and cut off Yingze. Flooding Daliang would definitely cause it to fall.
It was a mistake for the king's envoy to go to Qin, and he slandered the Anling family in Qin. Qin had long wanted to kill it.
Yeyang and Kunyang of the Qin State are adjacent to Wuyang of the Wei State. If the envoys are allowed to slander the Anling family and the Anling family is destroyed, the Qin army will bypass the north of Wuyang and approach Xu's homeland from the east. In this way, the south will be in danger. Is this harmful to the Wei state?
It is okay to hate Korea and dislike the Anling family, but it would be wrong not to worry that Qin does not love the south.
In the past, the State of Qin was in the hometown of the State of Jin in Hexi, thousands of miles away from Daliang. It was blocked by the Yellow River and high mountains, and separated by Zhou and Han.
Since the battle of Linxiang to the present, Qin has attacked Wei seven times and invaded Qinzhong five times. All the border cities have been captured, Wentai has been destroyed, Chuidu has been burned, the trees have been cut down, the elk have been hunted down, and the capital has been besieged.
The Qin army then drove to the north of Daliang, hitting the outskirts of Tao and Wei cities in the east, and hitting Pingjian in the north.
What was lost to the Qin State were the mountains south and north, the rivers outside and inside the rivers, dozens of large counties, and hundreds of famous capitals.
When the State of Qin was still in the hometown of the State of Jin in Hexi, a thousand miles away from Daliang, the disaster was already like this. What's more, let Qin destroy South Korea and occupy the homeland of Zheng. There is no Yellow River mountain to block it, no Zhou and Han to separate it, and it is only a hundred miles away from Daliang. The disaster is bound to start here.
In the past, the success of uniting Han Dynasty was because Chu and Wei were suspicious of each other, and it was impossible for South Korea to join the alliance.
Now South Korea has been suffering from war for three years. The state of Qin made it submit and make peace with it. South Korea knew that it was going to perish but refused to obey. Instead, it sent hostages to the state of Zhao, expressing its willingness to be the vanguard of the princes of the world and fight to the death with Qin. Chu and Zhao must gather their troops. They all know that Qin's greed is endless and will never give up unless all the princes and states in the world are completely destroyed and all the people in the sea submit to Qin.
Opening a road from Gongcheng and Ningyi to South Korea's Shangdang, and letting this road pass through Ancheng, and merchants entering and leaving must pay taxes, which is equivalent to Wei Guo using South Korea's Shangdang as a mortgage.
If there are these taxes, it will be enough to make the country rich. South Korea must be grateful to Wei, love Wei, respect Wei, honor Wei, and fear Wei. South Korea must not dare to rebel against Wei. In this way, South Korea will become a county of Wei.
If the Wei State gets South Korea as a county, Wei, Daliang, and Hewai will definitely be able to stabilize.
If Korea is not preserved, the East and West Zhou and Anling will be in danger. After the defeat of Chu and Zhao, Wei and Qi are very afraid. The days when all the princes in the world rush west to Qin to pay homage to Qin are not long.
In the 20th year of King Anli's reign, the Qin army besieged Handan. Wuji, the king of Xinling, falsely conveyed the king's order to seize the army of General Jin Bi to rescue the Zhao State. The Zhao State was preserved, and Wuji therefore stayed in the Zhao State.
In the twenty-sixth year, King Zhao of Qin passed away.
In the 30th year of King Anli, Wuji returned to Wei and led the armies of the five countries to attack Qin. He defeated the Qin army outside the river and drove away Qin general Meng Ao.
At that time, Prince Zeng of Wei State was a hostage in Qin State. The King of Qin was angry and wanted to imprison Prince Zeng of Wei State.
Someone said to the King of Qin on behalf of Prince Zeng: Gongsun Xi originally said to the Prime Minister of Wei: Please use the Wei army to attack Qin quickly. When the King of Qin is angry, he will definitely imprison Prince Zeng.
This will make King Wei angry and attack Qin again. Qin will definitely hurt Prince Zeng.
Now the king wants to imprison Prince Zeng. This is Gongsun happy's plan.
Therefore, it is better to treat Prince Zeng favorably and have good relations with Wei, and let Qi and South Korea doubt Wei.
Only then did King Qin cancel his plan to imprison Prince Zeng.
In the thirty-first year of King Anli's reign, King Qin began to ascend the throne.
In the thirty-fourth year of King Anli, King Anli died, and Prince Zeng ascended the throne. This was King Jingmin.
Xinlingjun Wuji passed away.
In the first year of King Jingmin, the Qin army captured 20 cities in the Wei State and established them as the East Commandery of the Qin State.
In the second year, the Qin army captured Chaoge of Wei State.
Weiguo moved to Yewang.
In three years, the Qin army captured Jiyi in the state of Wei.
In five years, the Qin army captured Wei's Yuandi, Puyang, and Yanyi.
In the fifteenth year, King Jingmin died, and his son King Wei assumed the throne.
In the first year of King Wei's holiday, Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate King Qin, but King Qin discovered it.
Three years after King Jie of Wei, the Qin army flooded Daliang and captured King Jie of Wei. Finally, the state of Wei was destroyed and established as prefectures and counties.
Tai Shigong said: I have been to the old city site of Daliang. The people there said: The Qin army conquered Daliang by diverting water from the chasm to flood Daliang. After three months, the city was destroyed, and the King of Wei asked for surrender, thus destroying the Wei state.
Those who discussed it all said that because King Wei did not reuse Lord Xinling, the country was weakened and even destroyed. I don't think so.
God's will is for the Qin State to pacify the sea, but its achievements have not yet been completed. Even if the Wei State is assisted by wise ministers like A Heng, what is the use?
summary:
The Wei family traces its ancestry to Bi Gonggao, a descendant of the Zhou royal family. After King Wu of Zhou defeated the Shang, Gao was granted the territory of Bi and adopted Bi as his surname. His descendants eventually became commoners, with some living in the Central Plains and others among the Yi and Di peoples. One descendant, Bi Wan, served Duke Xian of Jin and was granted the territory of Wei after military victories. A diviner predicted that Bi Wan's descendants would prosper greatly, and indeed the Wei family grew increasingly powerful within the state of Jin.

Wei Wuzi followed Chong'er into exile and later served him as Duke Wen of Jin. The family continued through generations: Wei Daozi, Wei Jiang, Wei Ying, and Wei Xianzi. During Wei Jiang's service to Duke Mourning of Jin, he killed a servant of the duke's brother who had caused disorder, initially angering the duke but eventually earning his trust. Duke Mourning credited Wei Jiang with eight years of successful alliances and peace with the Rong and Di tribes. As the Jin state declined, the six ministers grew stronger. Wei Xianzi served as a minister of Jin alongside Zhao Jianzi, Zhongxing Wenzi, and Fan Xianzi. Later generations including Wei Chi, Wei Huanzi, and eventually Wei Wenhou continued the family's rise.

Wei Wenhou's reign marked the formal establishment of Wei as a state. He studied under Zixia, treated Duan Qianmu as a guest, and gained praise from the princes for his respect toward worthy men. When selecting a prime minister, he consulted Li Ke, who advised examining five aspects of candidates: whom they associate with, whom they recommend when powerful, what they avoid when frustrated, and what they reject when poor. Li Ke determined that Wei Chengzi was the better choice over Zhai Huang, noting that Wei Chengzi spent nine-tenths of his income on employing worthy men like Bu Zixia, Tian Zifang, and Duan Qianmu.

After Wei Wenhou's death, his son Wei Wuhou succeeded him. The state faced various military campaigns against Qi, Zhao, Qin, and Chu. Following Wuhou's death, a succession dispute arose between Ziyi and Gongzhong Xu. The states of Han and Zhao disagreed on how to handle the situation, which ultimately saved Wei from partition. King Hui of Wei suffered repeated military defeats and sought to recruit worthy men, attracting Zou Yan, Chunyu Kun, and Meng Ke. Meng Ke advised the king that a ruler should focus on benevolence and righteousness rather than profit.

The later reigns of King Xiang, King Ai, King Zhao, King Anli, King Jingmin, and King Wei saw Wei's gradual decline. The Qin state repeatedly attacked Wei, capturing cities and territories. Despite efforts by figures like Lord Xinling Wuji, who successfully led a coalition of five states against Qin, Wei continued to lose ground. In the third year of King Wei's reign, the Qin army diverted water from the chasm to flood Daliang, capturing King Wei and destroying the Wei state, which was then established as prefectures and counties.

The Grand Historian concluded that while some blamed King Wei's failure to employ Lord Xinling for Wei's destruction, he believed the Qin state was destined by Heaven to unify the realm, and even wise ministers could not have prevented Wei's fall.

translation:
Duke Dan of Zhou was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou.
When King Wen was still alive, Dan, as his son, was very filial, loyal and kind, better than his other brothers.
When King Wu came to the throne, Dan often assisted King Bi Wu and handled many government affairs.
In the ninth year of King Wu's reign, he personally marched eastward to Mengjin, and Duke Zhou accompanied the army to assist him.
In the eleventh year, King Wu crusaded against Yin Zhou and the army reached Muye. Duke Zhou assisted King Wu and issued the "Oath of Mu" to mobilize the battle.
The Zhou army broke through the capital of Yin and entered the palace of Yin.
After killing Yin Zhou, Duke Zhou held a big axe, and Duke Zhao held a small axe. They flanked King Wu on their left and right, held the ceremony of provoking the community, and announced King Zhou's guilt to heaven and the people of Yin Dynasty.
Release the imprisoned Jizi.
Wu Genglu, the son of King Zhou, was granted the title of Father, and ordered Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai to assist him in order to continue the sacrifices of Yin.
After that, he was awarded the title of meritorious officials and relatives of the Zhou royal family.
The Duke of Zhou was granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, Shaohao's former ruins.
However, Duke Zhou was not allowed to go to his own kingdom, but stayed in Chaoyan to assist King Wu.
In the second year after King Wu defeated Yin Zhou, the unification of the world had not yet succeeded. King Wu fell ill and was unwell, and the ministers were frightened. Taigong and Zhaogong wanted to perform divination piously to know good and bad luck.
Duke Zhou said: "You cannot make our late king worry and grieve."
Duke Zhou then used himself as a pledge and set up three altars. Standing facing the north, holding a jade and a gui, he prayed to the spirits of King Tai, Wang Ji and King Wen.
The historian was ordered to write a congratulatory message saying: Your eldest grandson, King Zhou, will be sent to you. Hard work leads to illness.
If the three former kings owe God a son, please send Dan instead of Zhou Wangfa.
Dan is smart, capable, versatile, and able to serve ghosts and gods.
King Fa of Zhou was not as versatile as Dan and could not serve ghosts and gods.
But King Fa of Zhou was ordered by Heaven to help the whole world, and to enable your descendants to live peacefully in the world. People everywhere will respect him.
He can ensure that the heaven-given treasures are preserved for a long time, and our late king can be enshrined forever.
Now I obey the orders of the late king through the divination turtle. If you can agree to my request, I will offer the jade and obey your orders.
If you don't agree, I will hide the jade.
After Zhou Gong ordered the historian to write a book to congratulate King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen that he would replace King Wu with his own body, he went to the altar of the three kings to divine fortune.
People in fortune-telling said it was auspicious. When I opened the omen book, I found that it was indeed auspicious.
Duke Zhou was very happy, so he opened the lock and looked at the divination book hidden in the cabinet, which was also an auspicious sign.
The Duke of Zhou immediately entered the palace to congratulate King Wu and said: "You are not in trouble. I have just accepted the orders of the three ancestors, so that you only need to consider the long-term plan of the Zhou Dynasty and the world, and have nothing else to worry about."
This is what is called God’s thoughtful consideration for the Emperor. Duke Zhou put the scroll into a gold-wired cabinet and sealed it, warning the keepers not to leak it.
The next day, King Wu suddenly recovered.
Later, King Wu died and King Cheng was still in his infancy.
Duke Zhou was worried that people in the world would betray the court when they heard about King Wu's death, so he ascended the throne to handle government affairs on behalf of King Cheng and preside over the power of the country.
Guan Shu and his brothers spread rumors in the country: Duke Zhou will be detrimental to the king.
The Duke of Zhou then told Taigong Wang and Zhao Gongsi: The reason why I do not avoid suspicion and act in the affairs of the country is because I am afraid that the people in the world will betray the Zhou family and cannot explain to our ancestors Taiwang Taiwang, Wang Ji and King Wen.
The three ancestors have worked hard for the cause of the world for a long time, and they have just succeeded.
King Wu died young and King Cheng was young. I only did this to complete the great cause of stabilizing the Zhou Dynasty.
So he eventually assisted in becoming king, and ordered his son Boqin to go to the State of Lu to be granted a title on his behalf.
Zhou Gong warned Bo Qin: I am the son of King Wen, the younger brother of King Wu, and the uncle of King Cheng. My status among the people in the world is not low.
But I had to pull up my hair three times once I washed my hair, spit out the food I was chewing three times after eating a meal, and got up to receive the wise men. Even so, I was afraid of missing out on the wise men in the world.
After you arrive in Lu, don't be arrogant because you have a land.
Sure enough, Guan Shu, Cai Shu, Wu Geng and others led Huaiyi to launch a rebellion.
The Duke of Zhou followed the orders of King Cheng, raised his troops to march eastward, and wrote the "Great Edict".
So Guan Shu was executed, Wu Geng was killed, and Cai Shu was exiled.
Collect the remnants of Yin, grant Kang Shu to Wei, and Wei Zi to Song, and let him perform Yin's sacrifices.
It took another two years to pacify Huaiyi and other areas in the east.
The princes all followed the Zhou Dynasty.
God sent blessings, and Uncle Tang received two stalks of millet and one ear, which he dedicated to King Cheng. King Cheng ordered Uncle Tang to go to the eastern part of the garrison where Duke Zhou's army was stationed and present it to Duke Zhou, and wrote "Feeding Grain".
After Zhou Gong accepted it, he expressed gratitude and praised the emperor's order and wrote "Jiahe".
After the East became stable, Duke Zhou reported back to King Cheng and wrote a poem as a gift to King Cheng. His poem was called "Owl".
King Cheng did not dare to blame Duke Zhou.
On the last day of February in the seventh year of King Cheng, King Cheng went to Haojing to pay homage to Wuwang Temple, and then walked to Fengjing to pay homage to Wenwang Temple. He ordered Taibao Zhaogong to go to Luoyi first to survey the terrain.
In March, Duke Zhou went to Luoyi to build the capital city of Zhou and conducted divination. The results showed good luck, so he made Luoyi the capital.
King Cheng grew up and was able to handle state affairs.
So Zhou Gong returned the political power to King Cheng, who came to the court to listen to the government.
In the past, when the Duke of Zhou replaced King Cheng in governing the world, he faced the south and his back to the wall to accept the worship of the princes.
Seven years later, when King Cheng returned the throne, Duke Zhou faced north and stood in the position of a minister, still cautious and respectful as if he were walking on thin ice.
When King Cheng was young, he fell ill once. Duke Zhou cut off his fingernails and sank them into the river. He prayed to the gods and said: "The king has no opinions when he is young, and he offends the gods."
He also hid the blessing notice in the secret palace, and the illness of King Cheng was indeed cured.
After King Cheng came to the throne, some people said bad things about Duke Zhou, so Duke Zhou fled to the state of Chu.
King Cheng opened the secret palace and found the prayer book written by Duke Zhou. He was moved to tears and immediately invited Duke Zhou back.
After Zhou Gong returned to the country, he was afraid that the young king would indulge in debauchery while governing the country, so he wrote "Toast" and "Wuyi".
"Wu Yi" says: As parents, it is extremely difficult to start a business for a long time. Their descendants are arrogant and extravagant and forget the hardships of their ancestors, ruining the family business. Sons of man must be cautious!
Therefore, in the past, King Zhongzong of Yin solemnly and respectfully feared the mandate of heaven, was strict with himself when governing the people, competed in the industry and did not dare to neglect his career for his own pleasure, so Zhongzong owned the country for seventy-five years.
Emperor Gaozong of Yin worked hard among the people for a long time and lived with the common people. After he came to the throne, he went into mourning and remained silent for three years. Once he spoke, he won the support of his subjects and did not dare to indulge in debauchery. This made the country of Yin stable and the ministers of the common people had no complaints. Therefore, Emperor Gaozong reigned for fifty-five years.
King Zujia of Yin felt that he was not the eldest son and it was not morally right to be a king, so he escaped from the people for a long time. He was well aware of the people's needs. He stabilized the country and benefited the people. He did not regret being arrogant to a widowed and lonely man. Therefore, Zujia owned the country for thirty-three years.
"Toushi" said: From Tang Dynasty to Emperor Yi, all the kings of the Yin Dynasty followed the etiquette system to perform sacrifices, worked hard to be virtuous, and were able to live up to the destiny.
Later, when he came to Yin and Zhou Dynasty, he was very dissolute and indulgent, regardless of the will of God and the people. All the people thought that he should be killed.
King Wen of Zhou had no time to eat when the sun turned west every day, and he owned the country for fifty years.
Duke Zhou wrote these to warn King Cheng.
King Cheng lived in Fengjing. Although the world was stable at that time, the official system of the Zhou Dynasty had not yet been properly arranged, so Zhou Gong wrote "Zhou Officials" to delineate the responsibilities of hundreds of officials. He wrote "Establishing Government" to benefit the people and make them happy.
Duke Zhou fell ill in Fengjing and said before his death: I must be buried in Chengzhou to show that I dare not leave King Cheng.
After the death of Duke Zhou, King Cheng also showed humility, and finally buried Duke Zhou in Biyi, accompanying King Wen, to show that King Cheng did not dare to treat Duke Zhou as his minister.
After the death of Duke Zhou, just before the harvest in the autumn, suddenly there was a strong wind, thunder and lightning, all the crops fell down, and the big trees were uprooted.
The whole state of Zhou was greatly frightened.
At this time, King Cheng and the officials put on their formal attires, opened the Book of Golden Ribbons, and saw the brief letter stating that Duke Zhou was willing to take himself as a hostage and die for King Wu.
Taigong, Zhaogong and Chengwang asked the historian and other officials for confirmation. They replied: "This is indeed the case. At that time, Duke Zhou ordered us not to tell it."
King Cheng held the slip and cried: "I'm afraid there will never be such pious divination from now on."
In the past, Duke Zhou worked hard for the royal family, but a young person like me didn't know it yet.
Now that God is showing his majesty to commend Zhou Gong for his virtue, I will personally go to greet the God. According to the etiquette of our country, I should do the same.
So King Cheng went out of the city to hold a ceremony to worship the sky on the outskirts of the city. It started to rain immediately, the wind direction reversed, and the fallen crops stood upright again.
Taigong and Zhaogong asked people to pick up all the big trees that had been blown down, and use soil to build up the roots of the trees and tamp them firmly.
This year the whole country received a bumper harvest.
So King Cheng ordered the king of Lu to hold suburban sacrifices and worship King Wen.
The state of Lu had the emperor's rituals and music, which were used to praise Zhou Gong's virtues.
When Zhou Gong passed away, his son Boqin had already accepted the title of feudal state and was Lu Gong.
Uncle Qin, Duke of Lu, was originally granted the title of Lu, and it was only three years later that he reported the administrative situation to Duke Zhou.
Duke Zhou said: Why is it so late?
Bo Qin said: To change the customs and etiquette, the effect will only be seen after three years of mourning and mourning, so it is too late.
Taigong was granted the title of Qi State, and five months later he reported to Zhou Gong on the administrative situation.
Duke Zhou said: Why so quickly?
Taigong said: I simplify the etiquette between his monarch and his ministers, and do everything according to their customs.
Later, when the Grand Duke heard that Bo Qin was late in reporting the political situation, he sighed and said: Alas! The descendants of the State of Lu will be ministers of the State of Qi. If the government is not simple and easy to implement, the people will not be close to it; if the government is easy to approach, the people will definitely obey.
After Boqin came to the throne, Guan, Cai and others rebelled, and Huaiyi and Xu Rong also raised troops to rebel.
So Bo Qin led his army to Zhi Yi to attack him, and wrote "Zhen Oath", saying: Prepare your armor and helmets, they must be of good quality.
Do not destroy cattle pens and horse pens.
If horses and cattle are lost and slaves run away, sergeants are not allowed to leave their posts without authorization to pursue them. If other people's horses and cattle slaves run away to their own place, they must return them.
Robbery and intrusion are not allowed, and housebreaking and theft are not allowed.
The people in the outlying suburbs in the west, south and north of Lu State should prepare grain and grass trunks so that there is no shortage.
On Jiaxu Day, our army was building fortifications to conquer Xu Rong. We were not allowed to fail to arrive on time, otherwise we would be punished with death.
After issuing the "Oath of Death", he defeated Xu Rong and stabilized the state of Lu.
After Lu Gong Boqin died, his son Kao Gong Emirate succeeded to the throne.
Kaogong died four years later, and his younger brother Xi succeeded him as Duke Yang.
Duke Yang built the Maoque Gate.

In the summer, Duke Ai of Lu believed that Sanhuan was a worry to the state of Lu, and wanted to use the power of the princes to deprive Sanhuan of his rights. Sanhuan was also worried that Duke Ai would cause trouble, so there were many barriers between the monarch and his ministers.
Duke Ai went on a trip to Lingban and met Uncle Meng Wu on the street. Duke Ai said, "Am I about to die?"
Meng Wubo replied: I don't know.
Duke Ai wanted to use the power of the Yue people to attack Sanhuan.
In the eighth month, Duke Ai came to Xingshi.
Sanhuan attacked Duke Ai, who fled to Wei State, then to Zou State, and then to Yue State.
The people of Lu welcomed Duke Ai back to Lu, and Duke Ai finally died in the home of the Youshan family.
His son Ning ascended the throne and was Duke Mourning.
During the reign of Duke Ai, Sanhuan was strong and powerful, and the king of Lu was like a small prince, even more humble than the Sanhuan family.
In the thirteenth year, Han, Zhao, Wei and the Jin Dynasty destroyed Zhibo and divided the land among the three families.
In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Yu died, and his son Jia succeeded him as Duke Yuan.
Yuan Gong died in the 21st year, and his son succeeded him, namely Mu Gong.
Duke Mu died in the 33rd year, and his son succeeded him as Gong Gong.
When Gong Gong died in the 22nd year, his son Tun succeeded to the throne and became Kang Gong.
Kang Gong died in the ninth year, and his son Jinggong succeeded to the throne.
Jinggong died in the 29th year, and his son succeeded him, namely Pinggong.
At this time, all the six countries claimed to be kings.
In the 12th year of Ping Gong, King Hui of Qin passed away.
Twenty years later, Duke Ping died, and his son Jia succeeded him as Duke Wen.
In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, King Huai of Chu died in Qin.
In the twenty-third year, Duke Wen passed away, and his son, Qing Gong, succeeded him.
In the second year of Qinggong, Qin conquered the capital of Chu State, Ying, and King Qing of Chu moved his capital eastward to Chen.
In the 19th year, Chu defeated Lu, and the war zone was Xuzhou.
In the twenty-fourth year, King Kaolie of Chu conquered Lu.
Qinggong fled, moved to a small town outside the capital, and became a commoner. The sacrifices of the state of Lu were extinct.
Qinggong died in Keyi.
The state of Lu had thirty-four generations in total, from Duke Zhou to Duke Qing.
Tai Shigong said: I heard that Confucius once said that the morality of the state of Lu was really in decline!
People in Zhushui and Surabaya argued and argued endlessly.
Look at how chaotic the state of Lu was when Qingfu, Shuya and Min Gong came to the throne!
The succession of Duke Huan and Duke Yin occurred; Xiang Zhong killed his legitimate concubine; Meng Sun, Shu Sun, and Ji Sun were ministers, but they personally attacked Zhao Gong, causing Zhao Gong to flee.
Although they have always followed the etiquette of courtesy, their actual behavior is so contrary to this!
summary:
Duke Dan of Zhou, younger brother of King Wu of Zhou, was known for his filial piety and virtue. He assisted King Wu in military campaigns, including the conquest of Yin Zhou at Muye. After Yin Zhou's death, Duke Zhou participated in ceremonies announcing King Zhou's guilt, released the imprisoned Jizi, and helped grant territories to various nobles. Though granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, he remained in the capital to assist King Wu.

When King Wu fell ill, Duke Zhou offered himself as a sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, praying to die in King Wu's place. He performed divination, received auspicious signs, and King Wu recovered. After King Wu's death, with King Cheng still an infant, Duke Zhou assumed regency to prevent rebellion. His brothers Guan Shu and Cai Shu spread rumors that he would harm the young king. Duke Zhou explained his actions were to preserve the Zhou legacy, and eventually suppressed a rebellion led by Guan Shu, Cai Shu, and Wu Geng, executing Guan Shu and exiling Cai Shu.

Duke Zhou governed for seven years, then returned power to King Cheng when the king came of age. He wrote admonitions including "Wu Yi" and "Toushi" to warn King Cheng against indulgence, citing examples of Yin Dynasty rulers who prospered through diligence or fell through decadence. After Duke Zhou's death, King Cheng buried him beside King Wen. When a storm destroyed crops, King Cheng opened the golden-bound cabinet containing Duke Zhou's prayer to die for King Wu, realized his virtue, and performed ceremonies that restored the harvest.

The state of Lu continued through successive dukes. Duke Boqin, Duke Zhou's son, governed Lu and suppressed rebellions. The state experienced periods of stability and turmoil, with conflicts over succession and the growing power of the Three Huan families (Mengsun, Shusun, Jisun). Duke Zhao was forced into exile after attacking the Ji family, dying in Qianhou. The state declined as the Three Huan families grew increasingly powerful, reducing subsequent rulers to figureheads.

The state of Lu lasted for thirty-four generations from Duke Zhou to Duke Qing, when King Kaolie of Chu conquered Lu. The historian Sima Qian noted that despite Lu's reputation for ritual propriety, its actual history was marked by chaos, including the murder of legitimate heirs and ministers attacking their rulers, revealing a contradiction between their ceremonial observance and political reality.
