translation:
Empress Dowager Lu was Gaozu's humble wife and gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and his daughter, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan.
When Emperor Gaozu became the king of Han, he found Qi Ji in Dingtao. He loved her very much and gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao Yin.
Emperor Xiaohui was kind and weak, but Gaozu thought he was not like him, so he often wanted to depose the prince and make Qi Ji's son Ruyi, thinking that Ruyi was similar to himself.
Qi Ji was favored and often followed Emperor Gaozu to Guandong. She cried day and night and wanted to make her son the crown prince to replace the original crown prince.
Empress Lu was getting older and often stayed behind. She rarely saw Gaozu, and their relationship became increasingly estranged.
Ruyi was granted the title of Queen Zhao, and almost replaced the prince many times. Fortunately, the ministers' remonstrances and Liu Hou's strategy prevented the prince from being abolished.
Empress Lu was a strong and resolute person. She assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the world and killing ministers, mostly thanks to Empress Lu.
Empress Lu had two older brothers, both of whom were generals.
The eldest brother Zhou Luhou died in the line of duty, and his sons Lu Tai were granted the title of Lihou, Lu Chan was granted the title of Jiaohou; the second brother Lu Shizhi was granted the title of Jiancheng Marquis.
On April 25, the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he died in Changle Palace. The prince inherited the title of Emperor Gaozu and succeeded him as emperor.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu had eight sons: the eldest son Liu Fei, who was the brother of Emperor Xiaohui and had a different mother than Emperor Xiaohui, was named King of Qi; the rest were younger brothers of Emperor Xiaohui. Liu Ruyi, the son of Qi Ji, was named King of Zhao, Mrs. Bo's son Liu Heng was named King of Dai, the other sons of Ji's concubines were Liu Huifeng, King of Liang, Liu Youfeng, King of Huaiyang, Liu Changfeng, King of Huainan, and Liu Jianfeng, King of Yan.
Gaozu's younger brother Liu Jiao was granted the title of King of Chu, and his elder brother's son Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu.
Wu Chen, the son of Fan Jun Wu Rui, a hero who was not a descendant of the Liu family, was granted the title of King of Changsha.
Empress Lu resented Madam Qi and her son King Zhao the most, so she ordered Madam Qi to be imprisoned in Yongxiang, and summoned King Zhao to the capital.
The envoy went back and forth several times. Zhao Xiang Jianpinghou Zhou Chang said to the envoy: Emperor Gao entrusted King Zhao to me. King Zhao is still young.
I heard that the Queen Mother resented Mrs. Qi and wanted to summon King Zhao to kill him together. I dare not send King Zhao away.
Moreover, King Zhao was also ill and could not go there according to the imperial edict.
Empress Lu was furious and sent someone to summon Prime Minister Zhao to the capital.
When Prime Minister Zhao was summoned to Chang'an, he sent someone to summon King Zhao again.
King Zhao came and had not yet reached the capital.
Emperor Xiaohui was kind and knew that the Queen Mother was angry, so he went to Ba Shang to greet King Zhao in person, and returned to the palace with King Zhao, where he ate and lived with King Zhao.
The Queen Mother wanted to kill King Zhao, but could not find a chance.
In December of the first year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, Emperor Xiaohui went out to hunt in the morning.
King Zhao is young and cannot get up early.
The queen mother heard that King Zhao was alone at home, so she sent someone to give him poisoned wine to drink.
When Emperor Xiaohui returned at dawn, King Zhao was already dead.
So Liu You, the king of Huaiyang, was moved to the throne of Zhao.
In the summer, an edict was issued to pursue Yi Lihou's father as Lingwuhou.
The Queen Mother cut off Mrs. Qi's hands and feet, gouged out her eyes, burned her ears with fire, gave her dumb potion, made her live in the toilet, and named her "Ren Pig".
After a few days, Emperor Xiaohui was asked to watch the pigs.
When Emperor Xiaohui saw it, he inquired and found out it was Mrs. Qi, so he burst into tears and became ill and couldn't get up for more than a year.
He sent someone to see the Queen Mother and said: This is not what people do.
As the son of the Queen Mother, I have no face to govern the world.
From then on, Emperor Xiaohui drank and enjoyed himself every day and did not listen to the affairs of the court, so he became ill.
In the second year, King Yuan of Chu and King Hui of Qi both came to see him.
In October, Emperor Xiaohui and King Qi held a banquet and drank wine in front of the Queen Mother. Emperor Xiaohui believed that King Qi was his elder brother, so he placed him in the top position, just like the etiquette of ordinary people.
The Queen Mother was very angry, so she had two glasses of poisoned wine poured in front of her, and asked King Qi to get up and drink to celebrate his birthday.
King Qi stood up, and Emperor Xiaohui also stood up. He took the wine glass and wanted to celebrate the Queen Mother's birthday together.
The Queen Mother was so alarmed that she got up and poured out the wine in Emperor Xiaohui's cup.
King Qi felt strange and did not dare to drink the glass of wine. He pretended to be drunk and walked away.
When I asked later, I found out that it was poisoned wine. King Qi was very frightened, thinking that he could not escape from Chang'an, and was very worried.
The internal historian of Qi advised the King of Qi: The Queen Mother only gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
Now you own more than seventy cities, while the princess only has a few restaurants.
If you dedicate a county to the Queen Mother, as the princess Tang Muyi, the Queen Mother will definitely be happy, and you will definitely have nothing to worry about.
So the King of Qi presented Chengyang County and respected the princess as the Queen Mother.
Queen Lu was very happy and agreed to King Qi's request. She held a banquet at King Qi's official residence and drank happily. After the banquet, she asked King Qi to return to the feudal country.
In three years, the construction of Chang'an City began. In four years, half of it was completed. In five years and six years, it was all completed.
The princes came to the capital to gather.
In October, the princes congratulated the emperor.
On August 12, in the autumn of the seventh year, Emperor Xiaohui passed away.
During the mourning ceremony, the Queen Mother cried but did not shed any tears.
Zhang Pijiang, the son of Liuhou, who was fifteen years old at the time, was serving as a servant. He said to the prime minister: The Queen Mother only has one son, Emperor Xiaohui. Now that she has passed away, she does not cry sadly. Do you know the reason?
The prime minister said: What is the reason?
Zhang Bijiang said: The emperor has no adult son, and the queen mother is afraid of you ministers.
Now you request to appoint Lu Tai, Lu Chan, and Lu Lu as generals to command the Northern and Southern armies. Only when all the Lu family members enter the court and gain real power in the court can you ministers escape from disaster.
The prime minister followed Zhang Piqiang's plan.
The queen mother was so happy that her cries began to mourn.
Lu's power began to rise from then on.
Implement amnesty for the world. On September 5th, Emperor Xiaohui was buried.
The prince ascended the throne and became emperor, and visited the mausoleum of the great ancestor.
In the first year, all orders from the imperial court came from the Queen Mother.
The mother-in-law is exercising the authority of the emperor and intends to make the Lu family's children kings. She first inquires about the royal mausoleum of the right prime minister.
Wang Ling said: Emperor Gao killed the white horse and swore an oath with the ministers: If he is not a descendant of the Liu family and becomes king, everyone in the world will destroy him.
It is against the oath to make a descendant of the Lu family king now.
The Queen Mother was very unhappy.
Ask Zuo Prime Minister Chen Ping and Jianghou Zhou Bo.
Zhou Bo and others replied: Emperor Gao brought peace to the world and made his children kings. Now that the Queen Mother is in charge of the court, she can make her brothers and the children of the Lu family kings. There is nothing wrong with that.
The Queen Mother became happy and returned to the palace.
Wang Ling scolded Chen Ping and Jianghou, saying: Were you not present when we made a blood oath with Emperor Gao?
Now that Emperor Gao is dead, the Queen Mother comes to court as a heroine and intends to make the children of the Lu family kings. Even if you want to flatter and break your oath, how can you have the face to go to Jiuquan to see Emperor Gao after your death?
Chen Ping and Jianghou said: "Today we openly oppose in front of the Queen Mother and fight hard in the court, we are not as good as you; when it comes to protecting the country and stabilizing the kingship of Liu's descendants, you are not as good as us."
Wang Ling was speechless.
In November, the Queen Mother wanted to depose Wang Ling, so she made him the emperor's tutor and deprived him of his powers as prime minister.
Therefore, Wang Ling claimed that he was ill and was dismissed from office and returned home.
Then Chen Ping, the prime minister of the left, was made the prime minister of the right, and Marquis Piyang Shenshi was made the prime minister of the left.
Prime Minister Zuo did not manage government affairs and asked him to supervise the affairs of the palace, just like a doctor.
Therefore, Shen Shiqi was favored by the Queen Mother and often made decisions on government affairs. The ministers relied on him to decide important matters.
Then he pursued Li Hou's father as the King of Wuwu, intending to use this as the beginning of making the Lu family's children kings.
In April, the Queen Mother planned to make the children of the Lu family a marquis, so she first made Feng Wuze, a great minister of the Great Ancestor, the Marquis of Bocheng.
Princess Lu Yuan died and was given the posthumous title of Queen Mother Lu Yuan.
Her son was named King of Lu.
The father of King Lu was Zhang Ao, Marquis of Xuanping.
Liu Zhang, the son of King Hui of Qi, was granted the title of Zhu Xuhou, and Lu Lu's daughter was married to him.
Prime Minister Qi Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Pingding.
Yang Chengyan of Shaofu was granted the title of Wuhou.
Then they named Lu Zhong as Peihou, Lu Ping as Fuliuhou, and Zhang Mai as Nangonghou.
The Queen Mother wanted to make Lu's children kings, so she first made Liu Qiang, the son of Emperor Xiaohui's harem, the King of Huaiyang, Liu Buyi the King of Changshan, Liu Shan the Marquis of Xiangcheng, Liu Chao the Marquis of Zhi, and Liu Wu the Marquis of Huguan.
The Empress Dowager signaled to the ministers in a low voice, and the ministers requested that Li Hou Lutai be granted the title of King Lu, and the Empress Dowager agreed.
After the death of Lu Shizhi, Marquis of Kang in Jiancheng, his son who had inherited the title was found guilty and was deposed. His younger brother Lu Lu was granted the title of Marquis of Huling and succeeded Kang Marquis.
In the second year, King Changshan died, and his younger brother Liu Shan, Marquis of Xiangcheng, was appointed King of Changshan and his name was changed to Yi.
In November, King Lu Tai died. He was posthumously named King Su, and Prince Lu Jia was made king on his behalf.
For three years, nothing significant happened.
In the fourth year, Lu Yu was granted the title of Marquis of Linguang, Lu Ta was granted the title of Marquis of Yu, Lu Gengshi was granted the title of Marquis of Zheng Qi, and Lu An was granted the title of Marquis of Lu Cheng. In addition, five princes, prime ministers and ministers were granted the title of marquis.
When Xuanpinghou's daughter was Empress Xiaohui, she had no son, so she pretended to be pregnant, brought a beautiful son and called her son, then killed the child's mother and made the child the prince.
Emperor Xiaohui died and the prince ascended the throne as emperor.
When the emperor grew up, he heard that his biological mother had died and that he was not born to the queen, so he said: How can the queen kill my biological mother and call me her son?
I haven't grown up yet. When I grow up, I will rebel against her.
When the Queen Mother heard this, she was deeply worried. She was afraid that he would rebel, so she imprisoned him in Yongxiang. She said that the emperor was very ill and the courtiers around him could not see the emperor.
The Queen Mother said: Anyone who can rule all the people in the world should cover everything like the sky and accommodate all things like the earth. The emperor will comfort the people with joy and love, the people will serve the emperor happily, and the emotions from above to below will be harmonious, and the world will be governed.
Now that the emperor has been ill for a long time and is confused and confused, he cannot be the emperor's successor and worship the ancestral temple. It is not acceptable to entrust the world to him. Someone should be found to replace him.
The ministers all kowtowed and said: The Empress Dowager has really thought deeply about stabilizing the ancestral temple and the country for the benefit of the people of the world. We all kowtow and follow your edict.
The emperor was deposed and the queen mother secretly murdered him.
On May 11th, Liu Yi, king of Changshan, was made emperor and his name was changed to Hong.
The reason why the year is not changed and is called the first year is because the Queen Mother is autocratic in world affairs.
Liu Chao, the Marquis of Zhi, was the king of Changshan.
The official position of Taiwei was set up, and Jianghou Zhou Bo was appointed as Taiwei.
In August of the fifth year, King Huaiyang died, and his younger brother Liu Wu, Marquis of Huguan, was granted the title of King of Huaiyang.
In October of the sixth year, the Queen Mother said that King Lu Jia was usually arrogant and indulgent, so she deposed him and made Lu Chan, the younger brother of King Su Lu Tai, the king of Lu.
Summer, amnesty for the world.
Liu Xingju, the son of King Hui of Qi, was granted the title of Marquis of Dongmou.
In the first month of the seventh year, the Queen Mother summoned King Zhao Liuyou to the capital.
Liu You married Lu's daughter as his queen. He did not like her but liked other concubines. This Lu family's daughter was jealous and left angrily. She went to the Queen Mother to speak ill of him, falsely accused him of committing a crime, and said that King Zhao had said: "How can Lu family be crowned king?"
After the Queen Mother reaches 100 years old, I will definitely destroy them.
The Queen Mother was furious and summoned King Zhao to the capital.
King Zhao came to the capital and placed him in his official residence. He did not receive him and ordered his guards to surround him and deny him anything to eat.
Some of his subordinates secretly brought him food, and they were arrested and tried for crimes. King Zhao was hungry, so he sang: "Zhu Lu has the power, the Liu family is in danger; you are coercing the princes, forcing me to marry the Lu family's daughter as my concubine."
My concubine is jealous and slanders me for committing a crime; she slanders my daughter and brings chaos to the country, but the emperor doesn't understand.
I have no loyal ministers, otherwise why would I lose my feudal kingdom?
In the wilderness of suicide, Heaven must uphold justice in its affairs!
Alas, I have no regrets. I would rather kill myself as soon as possible.
I starve to death for the sake of the king, who has mercy on me?
Lu is unreasonable and has no choice but to ask God to avenge me.
On the 18th, King Zhao was imprisoned and died, and he was buried next to the graves of the people of Chang'an using the etiquette of ordinary people.
On the 30th, there was a solar eclipse and the day was dark.
The Queen Mother was disgusted and unhappy, so she said to the attendants: "It must be because of me."
In February, Liu Hui, the king of Liang, became the king of Zhao.
King Lu Lu Chan moved to the throne and became King Liang. King Liang did not go to the feudal state to take office, but stayed in the capital as the emperor's tutor.
The emperor's son Liu Tai, Marquis of Changping, was made King Lu.
Liang was renamed Lu, and Lu was renamed Jichuan.
The Queen Mother's sister Lu Yu had a daughter who was the wife of Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, who was a general.
The Empress Dowager conferred the title of king on a descendant of the Lu family. She was afraid that General Liu would cause chaos after her death, so she named Liu Ze King Langxie to comfort him.
Liu Hui, the king of Liang, was moved to the state of Zhao and became king. He was very unhappy.
The Queen Mother took Lu Chan's daughter as King Zhao's queen.
The queen's attendant officials are all members of the Lu family. They use their power exclusively to spy on King Zhao, but King Zhao cannot do whatever he wants.
King Zhao had a beloved concubine, and the queen sent someone to kill her with poisoned wine.
So King Zhao composed four chapters of poetry and asked the musicians to sing.
King Zhao was deeply saddened and committed suicide in June.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she thought that King Zhao had abandoned the ancestral ethics for women and would no longer allow his descendants to inherit the throne.
Zhang Ao, Marquis of Xuanping, died. Because his son Zhang Yan was the King of Lu, Zhang Ao was given the posthumous title of King Lu Yuan.
In autumn, the Queen Mother sent an envoy to tell King Dai that she wanted to move him to Zhao to become king.
King Dai declined, hoping to guard the borders of Dai's country.
Grand Tutor Lu Chan and Prime Minister Chen Ping all said that Marquis Lu Lu of Wu Xin was in the highest position and ranked first in the order. Please make him the King of Zhao.
The Queen Mother agreed and honored Lu Lu's father, Kanghou, as King Zhao Zhao.
In September, King Liu Jian of Yan Ling died. He had a son born from beauty. The Queen Mother sent people to kill the son. King Yan Ling had no heirs and the kingdom was abolished.
In October of the eighth year, King Lu Su's son Lu Tong, the Marquis of Dongping, was made King of Yan, and Lu Tong's younger brother Lu Zhuang was granted the title of Marquis of Dongping.
In March, Empress Lu held an exorcism ceremony. When she came back and passed by Zhi Road, she saw something like a black dog entrenched under Empress Gao's arm. Suddenly she couldn't see it again.
After divination, it was said that King Zhao was causing trouble as he wished.
So I got a problem with my high back armpits.
Because her grandson Zhang Yan, King of Lu Yuan, was young and lost his parents prematurely, he was alone and weak in power, so he made Zhang Ao's two sons from his former concubines marquis, Zhang Xi was named Xindu Marquis, and Zhang Shoufeng was named Lechang Hou, in order to assist Zhang Yan, King of Lu Yuan.
Zhang Shi, the great emissary of the Central Government, was also granted the title of Marquis of Jianling, and Lu Rong was granted the title of Marquis of Zhuzi.
Those Ling and Cheng who were served by eunuchs in the palace were all granted the title of Marquis of Guannei, and each of them had a settlement of 500 households.
In July, Queen Gao's condition worsened, so he ordered King Lu Lu of Zhao to be the general to command the Northern Army; King Lu Chan of Lu commanded the Southern Army.
Empress Dowager Lu warned Lu Chan and Lu Lu: After Emperor Gao brought peace to the world, he made an agreement with his ministers that if he claimed the title of king because he was not a descendant of the Liu family, the people of the world would destroy him together.
Now that Lu is the king, the ministers are indignant.
I am about to die, the emperor is still young, and I am afraid that the ministers will launch a rebellion.
You must control the army and protect the palace. You must not mourn me or be controlled by others.
On August 1, Empress Gao died, leaving an edict to reward each of the princes and kings with one thousand catties of gold. The generals, prime ministers, princes, and officials were all rewarded with gold according to their rank.
Amnesty to the world.
The king of Lu, Lu Chan, was the prime minister, and Lu Lu's daughter was the queen.
After Gao Hou was buried, Prime Minister Zuo judged him as the emperor's Taifu.
Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang were very powerful, and Dongmuhou Liu Xingju was his younger brother. They were both younger brothers of King Qi Ai and lived in Chang'an.
At that time, a group of people from the Lu family were monopolizing power and wanted to cause chaos, but they were afraid of Jianghou, Guan Ying and other ministers of the former Gaodi and did not dare to initiate it.
Zhu Xuhou's wife was the son and daughter of Lu Lu and knew their plot secretly.
He was afraid of being killed, so he privately sent someone to tell his brother, King Qi, that he wanted him to send troops to the west, kill the descendants of the Lu family and establish himself as emperor.
Zhu Xuhou planned to join the ministers to respond to the King of Qi.
The King of Qi wanted to send troops, but his prime minister refused to comply.
On August 26, the King of Qi was about to send someone to kill the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister Zhao Ping rebelled and planned to attack the King of Qi. The King of Qi took the opportunity to kill his Prime Minister, so he sent troops eastward and used deception to capture King Langxie's army. He led both armies to march westward.
This incident is recorded in "Qi Mourning the Family of King Hui".
The King of Qi wrote to the princes and kings: Emperor Gao pacified the world and made his children kings. King Hui Hui made him the king of Qi.
When King Hui Hui passed away, Emperor Xiaohui sent Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, to make me the King of Qi.
Emperor Xiaohui passed away and Empress Gao came to power. She was old and listened to the opinions of Lu's group and deposed the emperor without authorization. She also killed three Zhao kings one after another, abolished Liang, Zhao and Yan, and used the title of Lu's children as kings. Qi was also divided into four parts.
The loyal ministers gave advice, but the empress was confused and refused to accept it.
Now that Empress Gao has passed away, the emperor is still young and cannot govern the world, so he can only rely on ministers and princes. However, the Lu family prides itself on its position, gathers troops, uses its majesty to intimidate the loyal ministers of the princes, and orders the world under the pretext of imperial edicts. Therefore, the Liu family's ancestral temple is in danger.
I led the army to the court to eliminate those who should not be king.
When the Han court heard the news, Prime Minister Lu Chan and others sent Yingyin Marquis Guanying to lead an army to attack the King of Qi.
When Guan Ying arrived in Xingyang, he discussed with others that the Lu family had taken control of the army in Guanzhong and wanted to eliminate the Liu family and establish themselves as emperor.
If I defeat Qi's army now and go back to resume my life, this will further strengthen the Lu family's power.
So Guan Ying stationed troops in Xingyang and sent envoys to inform the king of Qi and the princes of other countries. We must unite with them, wait for Lu's rebellion, and get rid of Lu together.
After the King of Qi heard the news, he withdrew his army to the western border of Qi State, waited for the news, and acted as agreed.
Lu Lu and Lu Chan wanted to launch a rebellion in Guanzhong, but they were afraid of Suihou, Zhu Xuhou and others internally, and externally they were afraid of the armies of Qi and Chu. They were also worried about Guan Ying's rebellion, so they planned to wait until Guan Ying's army fought with Qi's army before launching a rebellion.
At this time, King Liu Tai of Jichuan, King Liu Wu of Huaiyang, King Liu Chao of Changshan, and King Lu Yuan, grandson of Empress Lu, who were nominally younger brothers of the Young Emperor, all did not return to the country due to their young age and lived in Chang'an.
Zhao Wang Changlu and Liang Wang Lu Chan each commanded troops and lived in the Northern and Southern Army. They were both from the Lu family.
No one among the princes and ministers felt that they would be able to save their lives.
Taiwei Jianghou Zhou Bo could not enter the military camp to take control of the army.
The Marquis of Qu Zhou, Li Shang, was old and sick, and his son Li Ji was friendly with Lu Lu.
Jianghou discussed the strategy with Chen Ping, the prime minister, and sent people to kidnap Li Shang, and asked Li Ji to deceive Lu Lu and say: Emperor Gao and Queen Lu jointly pacified the world. The Liu family was granted nine kings, and the Lu family was granted three kings. They were all agreed upon by the ministers. This matter has been notified to the princes, and they all think it is appropriate.
Now that the Queen Mother is dead and the Emperor is young, and you wear the seal of King Zhao, you do not return home quickly to defend the country, but as a general, you lead the army to stay here, and you are suspected by the ministers and princes.
Why don't you return the general's seal and hand over the army to the Taiwei?
And ask the King of Liang to return the seal and ribbon of the Prime Minister, make an alliance with the ministers, and go to his own kingdom. In this way, the King of Qi will definitely stop his troops, the ministers can be stable, and you can sit back and relax, and be king for thousands of miles, which will be beneficial to future generations.
Lu Lu believed in Li Ji's suggestion and planned to return the general's seal and return the army to the Taiwei.
They sent people to tell Lu Chan and the elders in the Lu clan. Some of them thought it was appropriate, while others said it was inappropriate. They hesitated and had not made up their minds.
Lu Lu trusted Li Ji very much and often went hunting with him.
Once when he passed by his aunt Lu Yu's house, Lu Yu was furious and said: If you give up the army as a general, the Lu family will have no place to settle down.
So he took out all the jewels and valuables and threw them away in the hall, saying: "Don't guard these things for others."
Prime Minister Zuo reviewed the food and was dismissed.
On the morning of August 10, Pingyang Marquis Cao Cheng, who acted as the imperial censor, met with Prime Minister Lu Chan to discuss matters.
The doctor ordered Jia Shou to go to Qi State as an envoy and came back. He accused Lu Chan and said: "You didn't go to your own country earlier. Even if you want to leave now, can you still do it?"
He told Lu Chan all about Guan Ying's alliance with Qi and Chu and planned to exterminate the Lu family, and urged Lu Chan to enter the palace quickly.
When Pingyang Hou heard these words, he rode on horseback and reported to the prime minister and Taiwei.
The Taiwei wanted to enter the Northern Army, but he couldn't.
Xiangping Hou Jitong was in charge of Fujie, so the Taiwei asked him to pass the imperial edict on the occasion of the festival, so that the Taiwei would join the Northern Army.
The Taiwei then asked Li Ji and Liu Jie, the Dianke, to advise Lu Lu: "The emperor sent the Taiwei to lead the Northern Army and wants you to go to your own country. Return the general's seal as soon as possible and leave here. Otherwise, a big disaster will happen to you."
Lu Lu believed that Li Ji would not deceive him, so he took off the general's seal and gave it to Dianke, and gave the military power to the Taiwei.
After the Taiwei took control of the army, he entered the army gate and ordered the army to say: Those who support the Lu family should bare their right arms, and those who support the Liu family should bare their left arms.
All the sergeants and soldiers in the army showed their left arms and supported the Liu family.
When the Taiwei came to the Northern Army, General Lu Lu had already taken off his general seal and left, so the Taiwei commanded the Northern Army.
However, there were still Confederate forces that were not under control.
Marquis Pingyang heard what Jia Shou said to Lu Chan and told Prime Minister Chen Ping about Lu Chan's plot. Prime Minister Chen Ping asked Zhu Xuhou to assist the Taiwei.
The Taiwei asked Zhu Xuhou to guard the camp gate.
The Marquis of Pingyang was sent to tell the Weiwei: Don't let Prime Minister Lu Chan enter the palace gate.
Lu Chan didn't know that Lu Lu had left the Northern Army, so he entered Weiyang Palace and wanted to cause trouble, but he couldn't enter the palace gate and wandered back and forth there.
Pingyang Hou was worried that he would not be able to win, so he ran off on horseback and told the Taiwei about the situation.
The Taiwei was still afraid that he would not be able to defeat Lu's group, so he did not dare to publicly declare to kill Lu, so he dispatched Zhu Xuhou and said to him: Enter the palace quickly to protect the emperor.
Zhu Xuhou wanted some troops, and the Taiwei assigned him more than a thousand soldiers.
Zhu Xuhou entered the gate of Weiyang Palace and saw Lu Chan in the palace.
At dusk, they attacked Lu Chan, but Lu Chan escaped.
A strong wind blew in the sky, so Lu Chan's officials were in confusion and did not dare to resist.
Zhu Xuhou chased Lu Chan and killed him in the toilet of the doctor's palace.
Zhu Xuhou had already killed Lu Chan, and the emperor sent an audience to express condolences to Zhu Xuhou. Zhu Xuhou wanted to seize the letter of loyalty, but the visitor refused, so Zhu Xuhou rode with him in a car, used the letter of justice to drive away, and killed Lu Gengshi, the guard of Changle Palace.
When he came back, he drove into the Northern Army and reported to the Taiwei.
The Taiwei stood up to congratulate Zhu Xuhou and said: "We are only worried about Lu Chan. Now that he has been killed, the overall situation of the world has been decided."
Immediately, people were sent to arrest the men and women of the Lu family respectively, and all of them, old and young, were executed.
On September 11, Lu Lu was captured and beheaded, and Lu Yu was beaten to death with whips and sticks.
He sent people to kill King Lu Tong of Yan and deposed King Zhang Yan of Lu.
On September 12, the emperor's tutor was appointed as the prime minister of the left.
On September 18th, the king of Jichuan was moved to Liang, and Liu Sui, the son of King You of Zhao, was made king of Zhao.
He sent Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang to tell the King of Qi about the execution of the Lu family and asked him to withdraw his army.
Guan Ying's army also withdrew from Xingyang and went to the capital.
The ministers discussed with each other privately: The young emperor, the king of Liang, the king of Huaiyang, and the king of Changshan are not really the sons of Emperor Xiaohui.
Empress Lu used deception to call other people's sons the sons of Emperor Xiaohui, killed the child's mother, raised him in the harem, and made Emperor Xiaohui his son, the heir to the emperor and the king, in order to strengthen the power of the Lu family.
Now that the Lu clan has all been wiped out, if the person they appointed becomes emperor, when he grows up and takes power, all of us will be killed.
It is better to choose the wisest among the kings and make him emperor.
Some people say that King Qi Yaohui is the eldest son of Emperor Gao, and now his legitimate son is the King of Qi. Looking at the origin from the perspective of close relatives and concubines, King Qi is the eldest grandson of Emperor Gao and can be established as emperor.
The ministers all said: The Lu family committed evil acts as a relative, almost endangering the Liu family's ancestral temple and destroying the heroes. Now the Sijun of Queen Qi's mother's family is a bad person. If King Qi is made emperor, another Lu family will appear.
He wanted to make him the king of Huainan, but he thought he was young and his mother's family was also very vicious.
Everyone said: King Dai is one of the sons of Emperor Gao who is still alive. He has the longest career and is a kind, filial and generous man.
Queen Mother Bo's family is cautious and kind-hearted.
Moreover, the one with the longest standing was already justified. In addition, the king's benevolence and filial piety were known all over the world, so it was completely appropriate to establish him as emperor.
So they secretly summoned the king to the capital together.
The king sent someone to say goodbye.
The envoy went to greet him for the second time, and then King Dai rode a carriage pulled by six horses. On Jiyou day at the end of September, he arrived in Chang'an and stayed at King Dai's official residence.
The ministers all went to pay homage, presented the emperor's seal to the king, and unanimously honored the king as the emperor.
Dai Wang repeatedly declined, but the ministers insisted on their request, and Dai Wang finally agreed.
Liu Xingju, the Marquis of Dongmou, said: I have no merit in getting rid of the Lu family. Please let me clean up the palace.
He and his servant Ruyinhou Tenggong entered the palace, stepped forward and said to the young emperor: "You are not from the Liu family, so you should not be made emperor."
So he turned around and ordered the guards holding halberds on the left and right of the young emperor to put down their weapons and leave.
Several people refused to lay down their weapons. Zhang Ze, the leader of the eunuchs, went to speak and they also laid down their weapons.
Duke Teng called for a chariot to drive the young emperor out of the palace.
The young emperor said: Where do you want to drag me?
Duke Xi said: Go out and live.
The young emperor was placed in Shaofu accommodation.
Then he used the Emperor's Dharma to go to Daiwang Guanxie to greet the Daiwang.
Report to the king: The palace has been cleaned up.
King Dai entered Weiyang Palace that night.
There were ten visitors holding halberds guarding the main entrance and saying, "The emperor is here, what are you doing in there?"
Dai Wang told the Taiwei about the situation.
The Taiwei went to explain, and all ten of the visitors put down their weapons and walked away.
The king then entered the palace to listen to political affairs.
At night, the officials separately killed King Liang, King Huaiyang, King Changshan and the young emperor in the official residence.
On behalf of the king, he was established as the emperor.
He died in the 23rd year of his reign and was posthumously named Emperor Xiaowen.
Tai Shigong said: During the period of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, the people were freed from the suffering of the Warring States Period. The emperor and ministers all wanted to recuperate and rule by doing nothing. Therefore, Emperor Xiaohui dropped his clothes and handed over his clothes. Empress Gao used the heroine to act as the emperor. Political affairs did not go out of the door, and the world was peaceful.
Punishment was rarely used and the number of sinners was few.
The people are diligent in farming and have more food and clothing.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty first started to rebel, Lu Pheasant became his wife.
After the world was pacified, Empress Lu began to dominate and prosper secretly.
Empress Lu was a stoic person with a cruel and suspicious personality. She poisoned King Liu Fei of Qi with poisoned wine, and cruelly cut off Concubine Qi's hands and feet and called her a human pig. When Emperor Hui died, Empress Lu pretended to cry and was not sad.
He appointed his relatives with the same surname to rule the world privately.
Kill the ministers, cut off the Liu family's queens and their heirs, harm the people, and make them miserable.
summary:
Empress Dowager Lu was the humble wife of Emperor Gaozu and mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. Gaozu favored Concubine Qi, who bore King Ruyi of Zhao, and often considered deposing the kind and weak Crown Prince Xiaohui in favor of Ruyi. Empress Lu, growing estranged from Gaozu, was resolute and assisted in pacifying the realm and killing ministers. After Gaozu's death in 195 BCE, Xiaohui succeeded him.

Empress Lu resented Concubine Qi and King Ruyi. She imprisoned Concubine Qi and summoned Ruyi to the capital. Emperor Xiaohui protected Ruyi, but during a hunt, the Queen Mother poisoned Ruyi. She then mutilated Concubine Qi, calling her a "human pig." Xiaohui, horrified, fell ill and abandoned court affairs, dying in 188 BCE. During his funeral, the Queen Mother cried without tears until ministers, following advice, appointed Lu family members as generals, securing her power.

The Queen Mother then ruled as regent, intending to make Lu family members kings. She consulted ministers; Wang Ling opposed, citing Gaozu's oath, while Chen Ping and Zhou Bo supported her. She deposed Wang Ling and promoted Chen Ping. She made Lu Tai King of Lu, and after his death, Lu Jia succeeded. She also made several of Xiaohui's sons kings, though they were not his biological children. The Queen Mother deposed and killed a young emperor who threatened rebellion, replacing him with Liu Yi, renamed Hong.

The Queen Mother continued to consolidate Lu power, killing or deposing several Zhao kings, including Liu You, who starved to death after opposing the Lu family. She made Lu Lu King of Zhao and Lu Chan King of Liang. In 180 BCE, she fell ill and warned Lu Chan and Lu Lu to control the army, fearing rebellion. She died, leaving edicts for rewards and amnesty.

After her death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. King Qi of Liu led forces against them, and ministers like Zhou Bo and Chen Ping conspired to remove the Lu. Zhou Bo, using deception, gained command of the Northern Army, and the soldiers supported the Liu family. Lu Lu surrendered his command, and Lu Chan was killed. The Lu family was exterminated, including Lu Lu and Lu Yu.

The ministers, fearing the young emperor was not truly Xiaohui's son, chose Liu Heng, King of Dai, as emperor due to his maturity and virtue. He became Emperor Xiaowen, reigning for 23 years. The historian notes that during Empress Lu's rule, the people recovered from war, punishments were rare, and agriculture flourished, despite her cruelty and nepotism.

translation:
Hou Ji, the ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi.
His mother was a woman of Tai family named Jiang Yuan.
Jiang Yuan was the emperor's concubine.
Jiang Yuan went out to the countryside and saw a giant footprint. He was so happy that he wanted to step on it. When he stepped on it, he felt his body vibrating as if he was pregnant.
When they were ten months old, they gave birth to a son. Jiang Yuan thought that the child was unlucky, so he threw him into a narrow alley, but horses and cows passed by him and avoided stepping on him, so he threw him in the woods. There were many people in the woods, so he moved to another place.
Jiang Yuan thought this was so magical, so he took him back and raised him as a human being.
Since I wanted to throw him away at first, I named him Abandoned.
When Qi was a child, he had the lofty ambitions of a great man.
When he was playing games, he liked to plant hemp and beans, and the hemp and beans he planted grew very luxuriantly.
When he grew up, he liked farming. He could observe the characteristics of the land and choose suitable grains to plant. The people followed his example.
When Emperor Yao heard about these things, he appointed Qi as a farmer to teach people how to grow crops. People all over the world benefited from this, and he made great contributions.
Emperor Shun said: "Sir, the people were suffering from hunger, thanks to you being the Houji to sow all kinds of grains."
Therefore, the enfeoffment was abandoned in Tai, known as Houji, and Ji was the surname.
Hou Ji is famous because during the Tao, Tang, Yu, and Xia generations, this family was very virtuous.
After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded to the throne.
In Buchu's later years, the Xia Hou family's state affairs declined, and they gave up the official post of Houji and no longer paid attention to agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi area because he lost his official position.
After Bucheng died, his son Ju succeeded to the throne.
After Ju's death, his son Gong Liu succeeded to the throne.
Although Gong Liu was in the Rong and Di, he resumed the business of repairing Houji's foundation, engaged in farming, and planted crops according to the cultivation characteristics of the land. He crossed the Wei River from Qishui and Ju Rivers, felled and obtained timber for use, so that those who went out had travel expenses, those at home had savings, and the people's lives improved thanks to him.
The people were grateful and loved him, and many moved to join him.
The great prosperity of Zhou Dynasty's statecraft started from here, so poets composed poems and music to praise and commemorate his kindness.
After Gong Liu died, his son Qingjie succeeded to the throne and established the capital in Bin.
After Qingjie's death, his son Huangpu succeeded to the throne.
After the death of the imperial servant, his son Chafu succeeded to the throne.
After Chafu's death, his son Ruihe succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Ruihe, his son Gongfei succeeded to the throne.
After Gong Fei's death, his son Gao Yu succeeded to the throne.
After Gao Yu's death, his son Ya Yu succeeded to the throne.
After Yayu's death, his son Gongshu Zulei succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Gongshu Zulei, his son Gu Gongdanfu succeeded to the throne.
Gu Gongdanfu re-established the foundations of Houji and Gongliu, accumulated virtues, and spread benevolence and righteousness. The people in the capital all supported him.
Xunyu and other Rongdi tribes came to attack them and wanted to plunder their property, so Gu Gong and Danfu gave it to them.
Soon after, the Rongdi tribe came to attack again, wanting to get the land and people.
The people were very angry and wanted to go out and fight.
Gu Gong said: The people support the monarch because they want him to seek benefits for everyone.
Now Rong and Di are coming to invade, with the purpose of wanting my land and people.
What difference does it make if the people follow me or follow them?
The people went to war because of me and relied on fathers, sons and brothers who sacrificed the people to be the monarch. I really couldn't bear to do this.
So Gu Gongdanfu and his relatives left Bin, crossed Qishui and Jushui, crossed Liangshan, and settled at the foot of Qishan.
And all the people in Bindi brought their old and young to the foot of Qishan Mountain, and all returned to Gu Gong's side.
Nearby countries heard that the ancient Duke was benevolent, and many people came to follow him.
So Gu Gong abandoned the customs of Rong and Di, built cities and houses, and set up towns for the people to settle down.
Five official offices were established: Situ, Sima, Sikong, Sushi, and Sikou. The people composed poems and music to praise him and praise his kindness.
The eldest son of Duke Gu was called Taibo, and the second son was called Yu Zhong.
Taijiang gave birth to a younger son, Ji Li, who married Tairen. Both Taijiang and Tairen were virtuous wives. Tairen gave birth to a prosperous son, which was a sign of sagehood.
Gu Gong said: My descendants will achieve great things, probably Chang, right?
The eldest son Taibo and Yu Zhong knew that Gu Gong wanted to establish Ji Li so that he could pass on to Chang in the future, so they fled to Jingman, got tattoos on their bodies, cut their hair short, and gave way to Ji Li.
After the death of Gu Gong, Ji Li succeeded to the throne and became Gong Ji.
Gong Ji practiced the way of governing the country left by the ancient Duke and resolutely implemented benevolence and righteousness, and the princes all obeyed him.
After Gong Ji died, his son Chang succeeded to the throne and became Xibo.
Xibo was called King Wen. He inherited the cause of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, followed the laws of Gu Gong and Gong Ji, practiced benevolence and righteousness, respected the elderly, and was kind to the young.
He treated the wise men with courtesy. In order to receive the wise men, he sometimes did not bother to eat at noon, so the scholars all attached themselves to him.
Boyi and Shuqi were in Guzhu country. They heard that Xibo was very respectful and took care of the elderly, so they went together to join Xibo.
Tai Dian, Hong Yao, San Yisheng, Huan Zi, Xin Jia and other officials also went to submit to him.
Chonghou Hu spoke ill of Xibo in front of King Zhou of Yin: Xibo has accumulated virtues and done good deeds, and all the princes have submitted to him, which will be detrimental to you.
So Yin Zhou imprisoned Xibo in Youli.
Hong Yao and others were very worried about Xi Bo, and tried their best to find beauties from the Xin family, colorful horses from the Lirong region, nine carriages from the Xiong Kingdom, and various other rare treasures, and presented them to King Zhou through Fei Zhongjin, a favored minister of the Yin Shang Dynasty.
King Zhou was very happy and said: "Anything in this is enough for me to free Xibo, not to mention there are so many other good things!"
So he pardoned Count Xi and gave him bows, arrows, axes and axes, giving him the right to conquer the neighboring princes.
King Zhou told Xibo: The person who framed Xibo was Chonghou Hu.
After Xibo returned home, he offered the land west of Luoshui and asked Zhou to abolish the criminal law of Paoluo.
Zhou agreed to him.
Xibo secretly did good deeds, and the princes came to ask him to judge right and wrong.
At that time, people from Yu and Rui had lawsuits that could not be adjudicated, so they went to Zhou.
They entered the realm of Zhou and saw that those who farmed fields gave way to each other, and the people regarded humility as a virtue.
Before the people of Yu and Rui saw Xibo, they felt ashamed and said to each other: "What we are fighting for is what the people of Zhou are ashamed of. Why are we going to do it? We are just bringing shame on ourselves."
So they returned and left with humility to each other.
When the princes heard about it, they all said: Xibo must be a monarch who has received orders from heaven.
In the second year, Xibo conquered Quanrong.
The next year, Mi Xu was conquered.
The next year, he defeated Qi.
When Zuyi of the Yin Dynasty heard about it, he was very frightened and reported the situation to King Zhou.
King Zhou said: Isn't it destiny to help me?
What can he do!
The next year, Xibo conquered Xin.
The next year, he conquered Chonghou Hu.
Fengyi was built and the capital was moved from Qixia to Feng.
The next year, Uncle Xi died, and Prince Fa ascended the throne, becoming King Wu.
Siebo reigned for about fifty years.
When he was imprisoned in Youli, he probably increased the eight hexagrams in "Yi" to sixty-four.
Judging from the praise of Count Xi by the author of "Poetry", it was probably in that year that Count Xi was appointed king and adjudicated the lawsuits between Yu and Rui.
He died ten years later, and his posthumous title was King Wen.
He once changed the legal system of Yin and formulated the calendar.
Zeng Zhui respected Gu Gong as the Taiwang, and Gongji as the Wangji: It probably means that the auspicious sign of the emperor began from the time of the Taiwang.
When King Wu came to the throne, Taigong Wang was appointed as Grand Master, Duke Zhou became assistant prime minister, and Duke Zhao and Duke Bi assisted King Wu and followed King Wen's legacy.
In the ninth year of King Wu's appointment, King Wu first offered sacrifices to King Wen in Bi, and then went to the east to hold a military parade and arrived at Mengjin.
Let King Wen's wooden master be carried on a cart and placed in the central army's tent.

Emperor Xia didn't know whether to kill them, drive them away, or keep them, so he performed divination, but the results were all unlucky.
The fortune teller asked if he could collect the dragon's saliva to get a good omen.
So he arranged coins and silk sacrifices, wrote simple policies, and prayed to the two dragons. The two dragons disappeared, leaving their saliva behind.
After the fall of Xia Dynasty, this weapon was passed down to Shang Dynasty.
After the death of Shang Dynasty, this weapon was passed down to Zhou Dynasty.
For three consecutive dynasties, no one dared to open it. It was only in the last years of King Li's reign that he opened it for viewing.
The saliva flows in the courtyard and cannot be removed.
King Li made the women naked and scream loudly.
The saliva turned into a black lizard and crawled into the king's harem.
There was a virgin girl in the harem who had just turned seven years old. She encountered him. When she was fifteen years old, she got pregnant after giving birth to a child without a husband. She was afraid and threw the child away.
During the reign of King Xuan, a girl sang a ballad and said: "Seeing a bow made of mulberry and a quiver made of dustpan wood, the Kingdom of Zhou will be destroyed."
When King Xuan heard this song, a couple happened to be selling mulberry bows and quivers made of wood. King Xuan ordered people to arrest them and wanted to kill them.
The couple fled to the road and found the baby that had been abandoned by the palace maid. They heard her crying in the middle of the night and took pity on her, so they took her in. The couple continued to flee and fled to Baoguo.
Later, the people of Baoguo offended the Zhou Dynasty, so they wanted to offer the girl abandoned by the little palace maid to King Li in order to atone for their sins. Because the girl who was thrown away was donated by Baoguo, they called her Baosi.
In the third year of King You of the Zhou Dynasty, King You went to the harem. He fell in love with the woman very much when he saw her, and gave birth to a son, Bo Fu. In the end, he deposed Empress Shen and the prince, and made Bao Si the queen and Bo Fu the prince.
Taishi Boyang said: The disaster has already occurred, and there is no way out!
Bao Si doesn't like to laugh. King You used many methods, but she didn't even laugh.
King Zhou You set up beacon fires, smoke and drums, and lit the beacon fire when enemies came to invade.
In order to make Bao Si laugh, King You of Zhou lit the beacon fire. When the princes saw the beacon fire, they all rushed over. When they arrived, there were no enemies. Bao Si laughed out loud as expected.
King You liked this method and raised beacons for Bao Si many times.
Later, losing trust, the princes gradually stopped coming.
King You appointed Guo Shifu as a minister to preside over the affairs of the country. People in the capital were very angry.
Guo Shi's father was a eloquent man who liked flattery and was greedy for wealth, but King You put him in high regard.
In addition, he deposed Empress Shen and removed the prince.
Marquis Shen was very angry and joined forces with Zhen and Quan Rong, who belonged to Xiyi, to attack King You.
King You raised beacon fire to recruit the armies of the princes, but none of them came.
Marquis Shen killed King You at the foot of Mount Li, captured Bao Si, and took away all Zhou's treasures before leaving.
At that time, all the princes came to Shenhou to jointly establish Yijiu, the prince of the former Youwang, as Pingwang, in order to maintain the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial tradition.
King Ping ascended the throne and moved the capital east to Luoyi to avoid the invaders.
During the reign of King Ping, the Zhou royal family declined, and powerful states annexed weak ones. Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin began to become powerful, and political orders often came from the hegemonic monarch.
In the forty-ninth year, Duke Yin of Lu came to the throne.
In the fifty-first year, King Ping passed away, and the prince's father died early, so he made his son Lin the king, who was King Huan.
King Huan is the grandson of King Ping.
In the third year of King Huan's reign, Duke Zhuang of Zheng came to court, but King Huan did not give him any courtesy.
In the fifth year, Zheng sent Wan to exchange Xu Tian with Lu.
Xutian is the land used by the emperor to worship Mount Tai.
In the eighth year, the state of Lu killed Duke Yin and established Duke Huan.
In the thirteenth year, when Zheng was attacked, Zheng shot and wounded King Huan, and King Huan fled back.
In the twenty-third year, King Huan died and his son, King Zhuang Tuo, ascended the throne.
In the fourth year of King Zhuang's reign, Duke Zhou Heijian wanted to kill King Zhuang and support Prince Ke.
Xin Bo reported the news to King Zhuang, who killed Duke Zhou, and Prince Ke fled to Yan.
In the fifteenth year, King Zhuang died, and his son King Li, Hu Qi, came to the throne.
In the third year of King Li's reign, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate.
In the fifth year, King Li died and his son, King Hui Lang, came to the throne.
In the second year of King Hui's reign, King Zhuang's favorite concubine, Yao Shi, gave birth to a son named Dai, who was favored by him.
When King Hui came to the throne, King Hui seized the gardens of his ministers and used them as his own hunting grounds. Therefore, Bian Bo, the official, and five other people made a rebellion and planned to summon the troops of Yan and Wei to attack King Hui.
King Hui fled to Wen, and soon lived in Yue, Zheng State.
They made King Li's younger brother Dai king.
A full set of dance music was played. The kings of Zheng and Guo were very angry.
Four years later, the kings of Zheng and Guo came to attack, killed Wang Dai, and re-elected King Hui.
In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he granted Duke Huan of Qi the title of uncle.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Hui passed away, and his son King Xiang Zheng ascended the throne.
King Xiang's mother has passed away long ago. The stepmother is Empress Hui.
Empress Hui gave birth to her uncle, who was favored by King Hui, but King Xiang did not trust him.
In the third year, Shudai negotiated with Rong and Zhai to attack King Xiang. King Xiang wanted to kill Shudai, so Shudai fled to Qi.
Duke Huan of Qi sent Guan Zhong to persuade Rong to make peace with Zhou, and Xi Peng to persuade Rong to make peace with Jin.
King Xiang received Guan Zhong with the courtesy of a superior minister.
Guan Zhong thanked him and said: "As a minister, I am just a lowly official. There are also two ministers in the state of Qi, Guo Shi and Gao Shi, who were personally appointed by the emperor. If they come to see the emperor in spring or autumn, how will you receive them?"
As a dual minister of the Emperor and Duke Huan of Qi, I took the liberty to decline. King Xiang said: You are an envoy from my uncle's family. I appreciate your achievements. Please don't refuse my kindness.
Guan Zhong finally accepted Xia Qing's courtesy and returned to his country.
In the ninth year, Duke Huan of Qi passed away.
In the twelfth year, Shudai returned to the Zhou Dynasty.
In the thirteenth year, the State of Zheng attacked the State of Hua. King Zhou Xiang sent You Sun and Bo Fu to intercede for Hua, and the State of Zheng imprisoned these two people.
Duke Wen of Zheng resented that after King Hui was escorted back to the court, he gave the wine utensils and jade to Duke Guo but not to Duke Zheng Li. He also resented King Xiang for helping Wei and Hua, so he imprisoned Bo Fu.
King Xiang was very angry and planned to use the Zhai people to attack Zheng.
Fu Chen advised King Xiang: When Zhou moved eastward, he relied on the strength of Jin and Zheng.
Zidai's rebellion was put down by Zheng Guo. Can he abandon it now because of a little resentment?
King Xiang did not listen to the dissuasion.
In the fifteenth year, King Xiang sent troops from Zhai to attack Zheng.
King Xiang was grateful to the people of Zhai and planned to make King Zhai's daughter his queen.
Fuchen also advised: King Ping, King Huan, King Zhuang, and King Hui have all benefited from Zheng. It is really not advisable for you, the king, to abandon Zheng, a relative of the same surname, and get close to Zhai.
King Xiang still didn't listen.
In the 16th year, King Xiang deposed Empress Zhai, and the people of Zhai came to punish her and killed Dr. Tan Bo of Zhou.
Fu Chen said: I have repeatedly advised the king, but the king has not listened. Now that we are in this situation, if I don't go out to fight, the king may think that I resent him!
So he led his followers to fight against Di Zi and died in the battle.
At first, Empress Hui planned to make Prince Shu Dai the crown prince, so she sent her followers to act as internal agents for the Zhai people, who then invaded Zhou Dynasty.
King Xiang fled to Zheng, and Zheng settled the king in Si.
Zidai ascended the throne as king and took Empress Zhai, whom King Xiang had deposed, to live with him in Wen.
In the seventeenth year, King Xiang complained to Jin. Duke Wen of Jin sent the king back to his country and killed his uncle.
Therefore, King Xiang gave Duke Wen of Jin Gui Zan, a hairpin, a bow and arrows, named him uncle, and gave the land in Hanoi to Jin.
In the 20th year, Duke Wen of Jin summoned King Xiang, and King Xiang met with him in Heyang and Jiantu. All the princes came to see him, and the history books covered it up, saying that the king of Zhou came to Heyang on a hunting tour.
Twenty-four years ago, Duke Wen of Jin passed away.
In the thirty-first year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
In the thirty-second year, King Xiang died, and his son, King Qing Renchen, came to the throne.
In the sixth year of King Qing's reign, he died, and his son Kuang Wangban came to the throne.
In the sixth year of King Kuang's death, his younger brother Yu came to the throne and became King Ding.
In the first year of King Ding, King Zhuang of Chu conquered the Rong tribe in Luhun. The army was stationed in Luoyi. The King of Chu sent people to inquire about the size of Jiuding.
King Ding ordered Wang Sunman to deal with him with clever words, and then the Chu soldiers left.
Ten years later, King Zhuang of Chu besieged the State of Zheng. Bo Zheng surrendered and soon restored the State of Zheng.
In the sixteenth year, King Zhuang of Chu passed away.
In the twenty-first year, King Ding died, and his son King Jian came to the throne.
In the thirteenth year of King Jian's reign, Jin killed their king Li Gong, took Zi Zhou back from Zhou, and made him the duke of mourning.
In the fourteenth year, King Jian passed away, and his son King Ling came to the throne.
In the twenty-fourth year of King Ling's reign, Cui Zhu of Qi killed their king Zhuang Gong.
In the twenty-seventh year, King Ling passed away, and his son King Jinggui came to the throne.
In the eighteenth year of King Jing's reign, the Queen and Prince Shengming died early.
Twenty years later, King Jing favored Zi Chao and planned to make him the crown prince. However, King Jing died at this time. Zi Beggar and a group of people fought against Zi Chao. People in the capital made Meng, their eldest son, king. Zi Chao attacked and killed Meng.
Meng Ji mourns the king.
When the Jin people attacked the Zi Dynasty and made a beggar king, they respected the king.
In the first year of King Jing's reign, the people of Jin escorted King Jing back to the court. Because the imperial court had established itself as king, King Jing could not enter the capital, so he lived in Zeyi.
In the fourth year, Jin led the princes to escort King Jing back to Zhou. Zi Chao became a minister, and the princes built a capital for Zhou.
In the sixteenth year, a group of people from the Zi Dynasty rebelled again, and King Jing fled to Jin.
In the seventeenth year, Jin Dinggong finally sent the King of Zhou back to the Zhou capital.
In the thirty-ninth year, Qi Guo Tian Chang killed their king Jian Gong.
In the forty-one year, Chu destroyed Chen.
Confucius died in this year.
In the forty-second year, King Zhou Jing passed away, and his son Yuan Wangren ascended the throne.
In the eighth year of King Yuan's reign, he passed away and his son Ding Wangjie ascended the throne.
In the sixteenth year of King Ding's reign, the three kingdoms of Zhao, Wei, and Han destroyed Zhibo and divided his land.
In the twenty-eighth year, King Ding passed away and his eldest son Quji ascended the throne. This was King Ai.
Three months after King Ai ascended the throne, his younger brother and uncle attacked and killed King Ai, and ascended the throne himself. This was King Si.
Five months after King Si ascended the throne, his youngest brother Wei attacked and killed King Si and proclaimed himself king, namely King Kao.
These three kings are all the sons of King Ding.
In the fifteenth year of King Kao's reign, he passed away, and his son Wei Lie Wang Wu came to the throne.
King Kao sealed his younger brother, Duke Huan of the Western Zhou Dynasty, in Henan, and asked him to inherit the official position of Duke of Zhou.
After the death of Duke Huan, his son Wei Gong succeeded him.
After Wei Gong's death, his son Hui Gong succeeded him and granted his youngest son the title of Duke Hui of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty.
In the twenty-third year of King Wei Lie, the royal city where Jiuding was placed was earthquake.
In this year, King Zhou appointed Han, Wei, and Zhao as princes.
In the twenty-fourth year, King Wei Lie died, and his son An Wangjiao came to the throne.
This year, thieves killed King Sheng of Chu.
King An died after reigning for twenty-six years, and his son King Lie came to the throne.
In the second year of King Lie, Zhou Taishi met Qin Xiangong and said: Zhou and Qin were together at first, but later they separated. After five hundred years of separation, they got together again. After seventeen years of being together, there will be a person who will dominate and unify the world.
Ten years later, congratulations to Duke Xian of Qin for his dominance. In the ninth year, King Xian gave the pork belly sacrificed to King Wen and King Wu to Qin Xiaogong.
In the twenty-fifth year, Qin made an alliance with the princes in Zhou.
In the twenty-sixth year, the king of Zhou gave the title of Fang Bo, the overlord of the princes, to Duke Xiao of Qin.
In the thirty-third year, congratulations to King Qin Hui.
In the thirty-fifth year, the meat sacrificed to King Wen and King Wu was given to King Hui of Qin.
In the forty-fourth year, King Hui of Qin became king.
From then on, the princes all became kings.
In the forty-eighth year, King Xian died, and his son King Shenliang came to the throne.
King Shenliang reigned for six years. After his death, his son Wang Yan came to the throne.
During Wang Nan's time, the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and the Western Zhou Dynasty were in charge of their own affairs.
Wang Nan moved the capital to the Western Zhou Dynasty.
The co-prince of Duke Wu of the Western Zhou Dynasty passed away, and he had five other sons, all of whom were concubines. There was no legitimate son who could be established as the crown prince.
Sima Jian said to the King of Chu: It is better to use land to support Prince Jiu and ask for the crown prince position for him.
Zuo Cheng said: No.
If Zhou doesn't listen to us, then you will be in an embarrassing and difficult situation, and your friendship with Zhou will be alienated.
It is better to ask Zhou Jun who he wants to make the crown prince, and then tell Jian privately, and Jian will ask Chu State to fund him with land.
As expected, the Western Zhou Dynasty established Prince Jiu as the crown prince.
In the eighth year, Qin attacked Yiyang, and Chu sent troops to rescue him.
Chu State thought that Zhou was helping Qin State, so it wanted to attack Zhou State.
Su lobbied the King of Chu on behalf of Zhou and said: How do you know that Zhou's help to Qin is a disaster?
Those who say that Zhou helped Qin more than Chu, want Zhou to join the Qin camp, so people put Zhou and Qin together and say Zhou Qin.
Zhou knew that he had no way to escape, so he would definitely join Qin's camp. This was a clever plan to help Qin capture Zhou.
If you really care about the king, then Zhou should be treated kindly if he works for Qin; he should be treated kindly if he does not work for Qin. Only in this way can Zhou and Qin be alienated.
After Zhou and Qin broke off relations, they would definitely surrender to the capital of Ying, the state of Chu.
The Qin State borrowed a road between the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and the Western Zhou Dynasty and prepared to attack South Korea. Zhou was worried that if he borrowed the road to Qin, he would offend South Korea. If he did not borrow the road, he would be afraid of offending the Qin State.
Shi Yan said to Zhou Jun: "Why don't you send someone to see Mr. Han?" He said to Uncle Han: The reason why Qin dared to pass through Zhou to attack Korea was because it trusted Eastern Zhou.
Why don't you give Zhou some land and send hostages to Chu?
Qin will definitely doubt Chu and not trust Zhou, so it will not attack South Korea.
Then he told Qin: Han Fei had to give land to Zhou in order to make Qin doubt Zhou in this way, so Zhou did not dare not accept it.
Qin must not have asked Zhou not to accept the land, so that he could obtain Han's land and obey Qin's orders.
Qin summoned the king of Western Zhou, but the king was unwilling to go, so he sent someone to say to the king of Han: Qin summoned the king of Western Zhou, and he wanted to send him to attack the king's Nanyang. Why didn't the king send troops to garrison Nanyang?
At that time, Zhou Jun will use this as an excuse to refuse to go to Qin.
If Zhou Jun does not go to Qin, Qin will not dare to cross the Yellow River to attack Nanyang.
The Eastern Zhou Dynasty was at war with the Western Zhou Dynasty, and Han sent troops to rescue the Western Zhou Dynasty.
Someone persuaded the King of Han on behalf of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty: The Western Zhou Dynasty was originally the capital of the emperor. There are many rare artifacts and valuable treasures. If the king does not move, the Eastern Zhou Dynasty will be grateful for your kindness, and all the treasures of the Western Zhou Dynasty can be obtained.
King Nan of Zhou was called Chengjun.
The State of Chu besieged the Yong clan of South Korea, and South Korea collected weapons and grain from the Eastern Zhou Dynasty. The Lord of Eastern Zhou Dynasty was very frightened and summoned Su Dai to tell him the matter.
Su Dai said: Why should you worry about this matter.
My ministers can prevent South Korea from requisitioning weapons and food from the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, and can also obtain Gaodu for you.
Lord Dongzhou said: If you really have such ability, I will make the whole country obey you.
Su Dai went to see South Korea's Prime Minister Zhongchi and said: The Chu State besieged the Yong family, and they promised to attack it in March. Now it has been five months and it still cannot be conquered. This shows that the Chu State is very tired.
Now, as the Prime Minister, you are asking Zhou for weapons and food, which is equivalent to announcing to Chu that you have suffered serious losses. South Korea's Prime Minister said: That's right.
But the messenger has already set off.
Su Dai said: Why didn't the state give Gaodu to Zhou?
The Korean Prime Minister was furious and said: If I don't requisition weapons and food from Zhou, it is already a big concession. Why should I give Gaodu to Eastern Zhou?
Su Dai said: If Gaodu is given to Zhou, then Zhou will turn to South Korea. When the Qin State hears about it, it will be very angry and resentful towards Zhou, and will cut off all contacts with Zhou's envoys. This is equivalent to exchanging the ruined Gaodu for a complete Zhou Dynasty. Why not give it? The Prime Minister said: What you got is right.
Sure enough, Gaodu was given to Zhou.
In the thirty-fourth year, Su Li said to Zhou Jun: Qin conquered South Korea and Wei, and defeated Wei's general Shi Wu. In the north, he captured Lin, Lishi and other places in Zhao State. This was all done by Bai Qi.
Bai Qi is good at using soldiers, and he is protected by destiny.
Now he led his army out of Yique fortress to attack Liang. If Liang was defeated, Zhou would be in danger.
Why don't you send someone to persuade Bai Qi?
He said: There was a man named Yang Youji in the state of Chu who was good at archery.
He could shoot an arrow a hundred steps away from the willow leaves and hit the target with perfect accuracy.
There were thousands of people watching on the left and right, and everyone praised him for his good shooting.
Only one man stood beside him and said, "Yes, you can leave it to him to shoot the arrows."
Yang Youji was furious, put down his bow, held his sword, and said: "My guest, what ability do you have to teach me archery?"
The guest said: I can't teach you the technique of holding the bow with your left hand and stringing with the right hand.
Shoot an arrow a hundred steps away from the willow leaves like just now, and you will always hit the target. If you don't know to stop when the shot is best, you will soon be exhausted.
Now you have already accomplished a lot by conquering South Korea and Wei, killing Shi Wu, and capturing Lin and Lishi of Zhao in the north.
Now you lead the army out of the fortress, passing through the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and the Western Zhou Dynasty, with South Korea as your back, and besieging the Liang Kingdom. As long as you fail to win a battle, all your previous efforts will be in vain.
You might as well claim to be ill and not fight.
In the forty-second year, Qin conquered Wei's dangerous territory of Huayang.
Zhou's minister Ma Fu said to Zhou Jun: Please allow me to lobby Liang Guo to build a city for Zhou.
So he went to the king of Liang and said: If the king of Zhou dies because he is worried about Qin's attack on Zhou, then I will definitely die too.
I request to take the initiative to offer Jiuding to the king. When the king gets the Jiuding, he will consider what I said for me. King Liang said: OK.
So he sent troops to him, claiming to be to guard Zhou City.
The horse prisoner took the opportunity to go to the King of Qin and said: Liang sent troops not to defend the city of Zhou, but to attack Zhou.
Your Majesty, you can try sending troops to the border to observe the situation.
As expected, Qin State sent troops.
The prisoner Ma took the opportunity and said to King Liang again: King Zhou's illness has been cured. The donation of Jiuding that I requested will be discussed later when the time comes.
Now that the king is sending troops to Zhou, the princes will be suspicious, and they will not believe you if you take any action in the future.
It is better to let soldiers help build the city of Zhou to cover up the princes' suspicion that you want to attack Zhou. King Liang said: OK.
So he sent troops to build the city wall of Zhou's capital.
In the forty-fifth year, Zhou Jun's guest from Qin said to Zhou Jin: Why don't you praise King Qin's filial piety and take the opportunity to dedicate the land to Qin as a place for the Queen Mother to support. King Qin will be very happy, and you will have friendship with Qin.
If the friendship is good, Zhou Jun will definitely think it is your credit; if the friendship is not good, those who persuade Zhou Jun to join Qin will definitely be punished.
When Qin went to attack Zhou, Zhou Jin said to the king of Qin: If it is for your sake, the king, don’t attack Zhou.
Attacking Zhou won't bring much benefit, but it will make your reputation feared by everyone in the world.
People all over the world are afraid because of Qin's reputation for attacking Zhou, and they will definitely go east to unite with Qi.
The army was exhausted from attacking Zhou, and everyone in the world joined Qi. In this way, Qin could not unify the world and become king.
The world is hoping to deplete Qin's strength, so it persuades you to attack Zhou.
If Qin and the princes are exhausted, your orders will not be carried out.
In the fifty-eighth year, Han, Zhao, and Wei jointly resisted Qin.
Zhou sent his prime minister to Qin, but because he was afraid that Qin would despise him, he returned halfway.
A visitor said to the Prime Minister: It is not yet known whether Qin despised or valued Zhou.
Qin wanted to understand the situation of the Three Kingdoms.
Why don't you go to the King of Qin quickly and say, "Please let me inquire about the situation in the eastern countries for the King. The King of Qin will definitely pay attention to you."
If Qi values ​​you, Qin will value Zhou, and Zhou will gain Qin's trust; Qi will value Zhou, and Zhou will already be in contact with Qi. In this way, Zhou will not lose its friendship with powerful countries.
Qin trusted Zhou and sent troops to attack Han, Zhao and Wei.
In the fifty-ninth year, Qin captured Yangcheng and Fushu in South Korea. The Western Zhou Dynasty panicked and betrayed Qin. He joined forces with other princes and led the world's elite soldiers out of Yique fortress to attack Qin, preventing Qin soldiers from reaching Yangcheng.
King Zhao of Qin was furious and sent generals to attack the Western Zhou Dynasty.
The king of Western Zhou fled to Qin, kowtowed and confessed his crime, and offered all his thirty-six cities with a population of thirty thousand.
Qin accepted the offer from the king of Western Zhou and asked him to return to Zhou.
After Zhou Jun and Wang Nan died, the people of Zhou fled to the east.
Qin obtained Jiuding and other valuable artifacts, and moved the king of Western Zhou to Hu.
Seven years later, King Zhuangxiang of Qin destroyed the Eastern Zhou Dynasty.
The Eastern and Western Zhou Dynasties all belonged to Qin. From then on, no one could preside over the sacrifices of the Zhou Dynasty.
Tai Shigong said: Scholars all say that Zhou conquered Shang Zhou and established its capital in Luoyi. However, comprehensive inspection of its actual situation is not the case.
Although King Wu once surveyed and built Luoyi, and King Cheng also sent Duke Zhao to divination to choose the location and place the Jiuding there, Zhou still made Feng and Hao its capitals.
It wasn't until Quan Rong defeated King You that Zhou moved eastward to Luoyi.
The so-called Duke of Zhou was buried in Bi, and Bi was in Duzhong, southeast of Hao.
It was Qin who destroyed Zhou.
More than ninety years after the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the emperor wanted to perform a ceremony of enshrining Zen in Mount Tai, go east to hunt and reach Henan County, visit the descendants of Zhou, and grant thirty miles of land to the descendants of Zhou.
summary:
Hou Ji, ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi. His mother Jiang Yuan, a concubine of the emperor, became pregnant after stepping on a giant footprint. She bore a son but tried to abandon him multiple times. Miraculously, animals protected him, so she raised him and named him "Abandoned." As a child, Qi showed great ambition, excelling at planting crops. When he grew up, he became skilled at farming, observing land characteristics to choose suitable grains. Emperor Yao appointed him as a farmer to teach agriculture, and Emperor Shun enfeoffed him in Tai, calling him Hou Ji, with Ji as his surname.

After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded. During Buchu's later years, the Xia dynasty declined and abandoned agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi region. His descendant Gong Liu revived Hou Ji's agricultural practices, crossing rivers to obtain timber, improving people's lives. Many people moved to join him, marking the beginning of Zhou's prosperity. Gong Liu's descendant Gu Gongdanfu further accumulated virtues and benevolence. When Rongdi tribes attacked, seeking land and people, Gu Gong refused to fight, saying he could not bear sacrificing people for his own sake. He moved with his relatives to the foot of Qishan Mountain, where many people followed him. He built cities, established towns, and created five official positions.

Gu Gong's eldest son Taibo and second son Yu Zhong fled to Jingman, giving way to their younger brother Ji Li, whose son Chang (King Wen) would achieve greatness. King Wen inherited the legacy of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, practicing benevolence, respecting elders, and treating wise men with courtesy. Many scholars and officials submitted to him. Chonghou Hu slandered him to King Zhou of Yin, who imprisoned him in Youli. Officials presented rare treasures to King Zhou, who freed King Wen and gave him the right to conquer neighboring princes. King Wen secretly did good deeds, and when people from Yu and Rui came to him with disputes, they saw the humility of Zhou's people and felt ashamed, resolving their conflicts peacefully.

King Wen conquered several states and moved the capital to Feng. After his death, his son King Wu ascended. In the ninth year of his reign, King Wu marched eastward to Mengjin, where eight hundred princes formed an alliance. Two years later, hearing of Yin Zhou's increasing tyranny, King Wu led 300 chariots, 3,000 warriors, and 45,000 armored soldiers eastward. At Muye, he swore an oath condemning King Zhou for listening to women, abandoning ancestors, and oppressing the people. Although King Zhou's army numbered 700,000, they had no will to fight and turned their weapons against him. King Zhou fled to the Deer Platform and burned himself to death. King Wu shot arrows at his corpse and beheaded him.

After conquering Yin, King Wu released prisoners, distributed wealth to the poor, repaired Bigan's tomb, and divided feudal territories. He honored descendants of ancient sage kings and granted lands to his brothers and officials. King Wu could not sleep at night, worrying about stabilizing the kingdom. He planned to build Zhou city in Luoyi. Two years after defeating Yin, King Wu fell ill and died. His young son King Cheng ascended, with Duke Zhou acting as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu rebelled with Wu Geng, but Duke Zhou suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and exiled Cai Shu.

King Cheng and King Kang's reigns saw peace for over forty years without using punishments. The Zhou royal family declined during King Zhao's reign. King Mu, who ascended at age fifty, restored order but foolishly attacked the Quanrong, causing distant states to stop paying tribute. King Li was greedy and tyrannical, suppressing criticism by killing those who spoke out. Duke Zhao warned him that blocking people's mouths was more dangerous than blocking water, but King Li refused to listen. After three years, the people rebelled and King Li fled. The country was governed by two dukes during the Republic period.

King Xuan restored Zhou's prestige, but King You foolishly lit beacon fires to amuse his concubine Bao Si, causing the princes to lose trust. He deposed his queen and prince, provoking Marquis Shen to join with Quanrong to attack and kill King You. King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi. The Zhou royal family declined as powerful states like Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin grew strong. Over subsequent generations, Zhou kings lost authority, with political orders coming from hegemonic monarchs. Eventually, Qin conquered the Western Zhou, obtaining the sacred nine tripods. Seven years later, Qin destroyed the Eastern Zhou, ending the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial traditions.
