Yu distributed rice seeds, provided relief to the needy, and facilitated food transfers between regions. His flood control journey began in Jizhou, where he managed rivers and lakes, classified soil types, and established tax and tribute systems based on land fertility.

Yu's efforts spanned nine provinces, each with distinct characteristics. In Jizhou, white soft soil was taxed at upper-first class with middle-fifth class fields. Yanzhou featured black fertile soil with sixth-class fields and ninth-class taxes. Xuzhou had red sticky fertile soil with second-class fields and fifth-class taxes. Yangzhou's moist soil ranked ninth-class fields with seventh-class taxes. Jingzhou's moist soil had lower-middle eighth-class fields and upper-lower third-class taxes. Yuzhou's soft fertile soil featured upper-middle fourth-class fields and upper-middle second-class taxes. Liangzhou's blue-black soil had lower-upper seventh-class fields and lower-middle eighth-class taxes. Yongzhou's yellow soft fertile soil had upper-first class fields and middle-lower sixth-class taxes. Each province contributed specific tributes, including metals, fabrics, stones, and exotic goods, transported via designated waterways.

Yu opened nine mountain roads and channeled nine major rivers, including the Yellow River, Yangtze River, Huai River, and Wei River, directing waters to the sea. This unified the nine provinces, enabling peaceful habitation, road construction, and tributary systems. Emperor Shun recognized Yu's achievements by granting him a black jade symbol. Yu, Boyi, and Gaotao discussed governance before Shun, with Gaotao emphasizing moral cultivation, understanding people, and appeasing the populace through nine virtues. Yu recounted his diligent efforts in flood control, food distribution, and land management. Shun stressed the importance of capable ministers and moral leadership, warning against decadence like Danzhu's. Yu noted his own sacrifices, including marrying Tushan's daughter and leaving his son Qi unraised, to complete water control.

After Shun's death, Yu initially yielded to Shun's son Shangjun but ascended the throne when all princes paid homage to him, establishing the Xia dynasty with the surname Si. Yu appointed Gaotao as successor, but Gaotao died before inheriting. Yu later granted state affairs to Yi. Ten years into his reign, Yu died during an eastern inspection at Kuaiji. Yi yielded to Yu's son Qi, who became Emperor Qi of Xia after gaining universal support. Qi suppressed the Youhu clan's rebellion, issuing the "Gan's Oath" to enforce discipline. Subsequent Xia rulers included Taikang, who lost his country due to neglect; Zhongkang; and others down to Jie, the final emperor. Jie's tyranny led to his defeat by Tang, who replaced the Xia dynasty. Tang enfeoffed Xia descendants, who later received Qi in the Zhou dynasty. Sima Qian noted Yu's surname Si, with descendants adopting various clan names, and Confucius' correction of the Xia calendar. Yu's burial site at Kuaiji Mountain, meaning "accounting," commemorates his assessment of princes' merits.

translation:
Emperor Xiaowen was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu.
In the spring of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Chen Xi's army was defeated and Dai was pacified. Emperor Xiaowen was made King of Dai and his capital was Zhongdu.
He is the son of Queen Mother Bo.
In the seventeenth year of his reign as King of Dai, it was the eighth year of the reign of Emperor Gao. In July of this year, Queen Gao passed away.
In September, Lu Chan and others from Empress Lu's family wanted to rebel and overthrow the Liu family's regime. The ministers annihilated the Lu family together and discussed summoning the king to come to the capital and establish him as emperor. This incident is recorded in "The Chronicles of Empress Dowager Lu".
Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Zhou Bo and others sent people to greet the king.
The king asked his ministers, Lang Zhongling, Zhang Wu and others for their opinions.
Zhang Wu and others suggested: The ministers in the Han Dynasty were all generals from the time of Emperor Gao. They were familiar with military affairs and were scheming and deceitful. Their real intention was not just that, they were just afraid of the power of Emperor Gao and Empress Dowager Lu.
Now that the Lu family has been annihilated and the capital has been bloodbathed, they are here to greet the king in name, but in fact they cannot be trusted.
I hope that the king will pretend to be ill, not go to the capital, and sit back and watch the situation change.
Lieutenant Song Chang said: The opinions of the ministers are all wrong.
When the corruption of the Qin Dynasty collapsed, the princes and heroes rose up at the same time, thinking that they could conquer the world. There were tens of thousands of people. However, it was the Liu family who finally ascended to the position of emperor. Those who competed in the world cut off the hope of becoming emperor. This is the first point.
Emperor Gao made his children kings, and the territories of the kingdoms were intertwined. This is what people call a clan that is as solid as a rock. Everyone in the world succumbed to the strength of the Liu family. This is the second point.
The rise of the Han Dynasty abolished the harsh decrees of the Qin Dynasty, simplified the laws, and benefited the people. Everyone lived peacefully and unshakably. This is the third point.
With the majesty of the Empress Dowager Lu, she established three of Lu's children as kings, who excelled in power and autocratic power. However, the Taiwei entered the Northern Army with integrity. When he called out, the soldiers all bared their left arms to support the Liu family and betrayed the Lu family. As a result, the Lu family was wiped out.
This is a gift from God and cannot be achieved by human beings.
Now even if the ministers want to rebel, the people are unwilling to be driven by them. Can their party members unite together wholeheartedly?
Today, there are relatives like Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou in the capital, and outside the capital there are people who are afraid of the power of the King of Wu, the King of Chu, the King of Huainan, the King of Langxie, the King of Qi, and the King of Dai.
At present, the only sons of Emperor Gao are the King of Huainan and the Great King. The Great King is older, famous for his virtuousness, saintliness, benevolence, and filial piety. Therefore, the ministers comply with the wishes of the people in the world and want to welcome the Great King as the emperor. The Great King has no doubts.
The king reported to the queen mother and held consultations, but he hesitated and did not make up his mind.
Use tortoise shells for divination, and the omens of the hexagrams will be great.
The omen said: Daheng heralds a change. I will become the king of heaven and carry forward the cause of the late emperor like Xia Qi.
Dai Wang said: I am already the king of vassals, what else do I want to be?
The fortune teller said: The king in question is the Son of Heaven.
So King Dai sent Bo Zhao, the younger brother of the Queen Mother, to the capital to meet with Jianghou. Jianghou and others told Bo Zhao all about their intention to welcome King Dai.
Bo Zhao came back and reported: The situation is real and there is nothing to doubt.
King Dai then smiled and said to Song Chang, "It's exactly what you said."
Song Chang was asked to ride on the right side of the car, and Zhang Wu and six other people took the transfer car to Chang'an.
After arriving at Gaoling, they stopped and sent Song Chang to drive to Chang'an to observe the changes in the situation.
When Song Chang arrived at Weiqiao, officials at all levels below the prime minister came to greet him.
Song Chang came back and reported to King Dai.
King Dai drove to Weiqiao, where all the ministers came to pay homage and called themselves ministers.
On behalf of the king, he got out of the car and paid his respects.
Taiwei Zhou Bo came to see him and said: I hope to talk to you alone.
Song Chang said: If what you say is official business, say it publicly.
What is said is a private matter, and the king does not accept private affairs.
The Taiwei knelt down and presented the emperor's seal and talisman.
King Dai said goodbye and said: "Go to Daiguo's official residence to discuss."
So he drove into Daiguo's official residence.
The ministers also followed them to Daiguo's official residence.
Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Zhou Bo, General Chen Wu, Yushi Zhang Cang, Zongzheng Liu Ying, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju, and Dianke Liu Jie all paid homage to Hou Jin and said: Prince Liu Hong and others are not the sons of Emperor Xiaohui and should not be emperors and be enshrined in the ancestral temple.
We discussed with the Marquis of Yin'an, Queen Qing, as well as King Langxie, the clan, ministers, princes, and officials of more than two thousand stones, and said: The king is now the eldest son of Emperor Gao, and is suitable to be the successor of Emperor Gao.
I hope your Majesty will ascend the throne and become the Emperor.
Dai Wang said: It is a very important thing to enshrine Emperor Gaodi in the ancestral temple.
I am not talented enough to serve in the ancestral temple.
I hope to ask the King of Chu to consider a suitable person. I dare not take on this important task.
The ministers all prostrated themselves on the ground and made a firm request.
The king of Dai surrendered three times while facing the west and twice more while facing the south.
Prime Minister Chen Ping and others said: "We have discussed below that it is most appropriate for the king to worship Gaodi in the ancestral temple. Even the princes and people of the world think it is appropriate."
We consider the ancestral temple and the country and dare not neglect our work.
I hope your Majesty will listen to our advice.
We solemnly and respectfully present the emperor's seal and talismans.
Dai Wang said: The clan, generals, kings, and princes all think that there is no more suitable candidate than me, so I dare not refuse any more.
So he ascended the throne as emperor.
The ministers served according to the etiquette and rank.
He sent his servants Xia Houying and Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju to clear the palace and use the Emperor's Dharma to greet the emperor at his residence.
The emperor entered Weiyang Palace that night.
At night, Song Chang was appointed as General of the Guard to subdue and organize the Northern and Southern armies.
Zhang Wu was appointed as the commander-in-chief and patrolled the palace.
The emperor returned to the front hall to sit in court.
So that night an edict was issued saying: Recently, the descendants of the Lu family have been monopolizing power, plotting rebellion, and trying to endanger the Liu family's ancestral temple. Fortunately, the generals, princes, clans, and ministers have eliminated them, and they have all received the punishment they deserve.
I had just ascended the throne and granted a general amnesty to the people. I granted the male heads of households among the common people a rank of nobility, and the female heads of households were given cattle and wine for every 100 households, and were allowed to gather and feast for five days.
On October 1, the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Ze, the original king of Langxie, was granted the title of King of Yan.
On the second day, the emperor ascended the throne and paid homage to the Gaomiao.
The right prime minister Chen Ping moved to the left as the prime minister, the Taiwei Zhou Bo became the right prime minister, and the general Guan Ying became the Taiwei.
The old lands of Qi and Chu that Lu had captured were all returned to Qi and Chu.
On the third day, the cavalry general Bo Zhao was sent to Dai State to greet the Empress Dowager.
The emperor said: Lu Chan appointed himself Prime Minister, and Lu Lu appointed himself General. They sent General Guan Ying to lead the army to attack Qi State without authorization, in order to replace Liu. Guan Ying stayed in Xingyang, held his troops inactive, and conspired with the princes to kill the Lu family.
Lu Chan attempted to launch a rebellion, and Prime Minister Chen Ping and Taiwei Zhou Bo used tactics to seize the military power of Lu Chan and others.
Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang first captured Lu Chan and others.
The Taiwei personally led Xiangping Hou Jitong to join the Northern Army in accordance with the imperial edict.
Dianke Liu Jie personally took the seal of King Zhao Lu Lu.
Taiwei Zhou Bo was granted the title of 10,000 households and received five thousand catties of gold.
The prime minister Chen Ping and the general Guan Ying were granted the title of three thousand households each, and were given two thousand catties of gold.
The titles of Zhuxuhou Liu Zhang, Xiangpinghou Jitong, and Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju were granted to each of them with 2,000 households and a limit of 1,000 kilograms of gold.
The Dianke Liu Jie was granted the title of Marquis of Yangxin and his son was given a thousand catties of gold.
In December, the emperor said: The law is the criterion for governing the country. It is used to prohibit cruelty and guide people to be good.
Now, after a person has been convicted of a crime, the innocent parents, wives, and brothers are brought together to confiscate their wives and children as slaves of the government. I strongly disagree with this approach.
Let’s discuss it.
Officials all said: The people cannot govern themselves, so they make laws to restrain them.
They sat next to each other and took their wives and children as slaves of the government, in order to restrain the people's psychology so that they would not dare to break the law easily. This practice has been around for a long time, and it is appropriate to continue the same practice as before.
The emperor said: I heard that if the law is fair, the people will be loyal, and if the crime is judged and the punishment is appropriate, the people will be obedient.
Moreover, it is the officials who manage the people and guide them to be good.
Officials are unable to guide them and use unjust laws to judge crimes. This actually harms the people and makes them commit violence and chaos. How can the law prohibit it?
I see nothing convenient about such a law. Think it over again.
The officials all said: The emperor's kindness to the people is so great and his virtue is so profound that it cannot be matched by our ministers.
Let us sincerely follow the edict and abolish the laws that prohibit one person from committing a crime, confiscate his wife as a servant of the government, and some other laws that are linked to each other.
In the first month of the year, officials came forward and said: The purpose of confirming the prince earlier is to respect the ancestral temple.
Please install a prince now.
The emperor said: I am already a man of poor virtue. The gods do not enjoy my sacrifices, and the people of the world are not satisfied.
Now that I cannot widely seek for the wise, sage and virtuous people in the world and surrender to the world, I say that I want to establish the prince in advance. This makes me even more virtuous. How should I explain it to the people of the world?
Let’s talk about it slowly later.
Officials said: To establish the prince in advance is to put the ancestral temple and the country first and not forget the world.
The emperor said: The King of Chu is my uncle. He is old and experienced. He understands many principles of the world and the general outline of the country.
King Wu is my elder brother. He is a benevolent man and likes to treat others with kindness.
King Huainan is my younger brother, and he comes to assist me with virtue. Doesn't this pre-solve the emperor's heir?
The princes, kings, clans, brothers, and meritorious ministers are all wise and virtuous people. If you recommend people with moral integrity to help and succeed me, who cannot die, this will be a blessing for the gods of the country and the people of the world.
If I don't mention it now, but I think it must be passed on to my son, people will think that I have forgotten the wise and virtuous people, and am focusing on my own son instead of thinking about the world.
I strongly disapprove of this approach.
The officials all requested resolutely: In ancient times, the Yin and Zhou dynasties established the country and brought peace and order to the world for more than a thousand years. In ancient times, no one who owned the world had a longer-term rule than Yin and Zhou. This is because Yin and Zhou adopted the method of passing on the throne to the son.
He must make his son his heir, as he did so a long time ago.
Emperor Gao personally led the soldiers and generals to pacify the world, feudal princes, and became the ancestor of all emperors.
The princes, kings and princes who initially accepted the feudal kingdom also became the ancestors of their own feudal kingdom.
The succession of descendants to the throne continues from generation to generation, which is the great justice of the world. Therefore, Emperor Gao established the system of succession to the throne to stabilize the country.
It is not Gao Di's idea to give up the candidates who should be appointed as successors and choose others from the princes and clans.
It is not appropriate to change someone else's practice.
Zi is the eldest son, he is kind and kind, please make him the prince.
The emperor agreed.
Therefore, the eldest son of the people in the world who should inherit his father's inheritance was given a rank of nobility. General Bo Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Zhi.
In March, officials requested the title of queen.
Empress Dowager Bo said: "The princes and kings all have the same surname, so let's make the prince's mother the queen."
The queen's surname is Dou.
Because of the establishment of a queen, the emperor gave a certain amount of cloth, silk, rice, and meat to the widowed, lonely and poor people in the world, as well as the elderly over eighty years old and orphans under nine years old.
The emperor came to the capital from the state of Dai. Not long after he took the throne, he extended kindness to the people of the world and appeased the princes and ethnic minorities from all directions. They were all happy and harmonious, so they rewarded the meritorious officials who came to the capital from the state of Dai in turn.
The emperor said: When the ministers killed the descendants of the Lu family to welcome me, I was hesitant and everyone blocked me. Only Lieutenant Song Chang persuaded me so that I could serve the ancestral temple.
He already respected Song Chang as General Wei, and then named Song Chang as Zhuang Wuhou.
The six people who followed me to the capital were all promoted to the rank of Jiuqing.
The emperor said: Among the sixty-eight princes who followed Emperor Gao to Shu and Hanzhong, each of them was granted a city of 300 households. In the past, the officials who followed Emperor Gao for more than 2,000 shi, including the governor of Yingchuan County, were granted 600 households each. Ten people including Shen Tujia, the governor of Huaiyang County, were granted 500 households each. Ten people such as Wei Wei Ding were granted 400 households each.
Zhao Jian, the uncle of the King of Huainan, was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Yang, and Si Jun, the uncle of the King of Qi, was granted the title of Marquis of Guo of the Qing Dynasty.
In autumn, Cai Jian, the prime minister of the original Changshan Kingdom, was granted the title of Marquis of Fan.
Someone advised the right prime minister: You originally killed the descendants of the Lu family and welcomed the king as the emperor. Now you rely on these merits to accept the greatest rewards and are in a distinguished position. Disaster will soon come.
Zhou Bo, the right prime minister, dismissed the right prime minister on the pretext of illness, leaving Chen Ping, the left prime minister, to serve as prime minister.
In October of the second year, the prime minister Chen Ping died, and Jianghou Zhou Bo was appointed as the prime minister.
The emperor said: I heard that in ancient times, there were more than a thousand princes who established kingdoms. Each of them guarded his own territory and paid tribute to the emperor according to the prescribed time. The people did not work hard, they were happy and rejoiced, and there was no loss of morality.
Nowadays, most of the princes go to Chang'an, which is far away from the feudal towns. The officials and soldiers there provide and transport the necessary materials, which is laborious and laborious, and the princes have no way to educate and train their people.
The princes were ordered to return to the feudal state, and those who held official positions in the court and had edicts to stay were sent to send the princes to the feudal state.
On the last day of November, a solar eclipse occurs.
On December 15th, another solar eclipse occurred.
The emperor said: I heard that God gave birth to all nations and set up kings for them to raise and govern them.
If the monarch is unkind and his governance is unfair, God will show him disasters and strange phenomena to warn him that the world is not governed well.
At the end of November, there was a solar eclipse, and God showed me its condemnation. No disaster could be more serious than this.
I am able to protect the ancestral temple and stand above hundreds of millions of people and princes and kings as a small individual. I am able to control chaos in the world. I only have two or three ministers in power who can act as my right-hand man.
I am unable to govern and nurture the main spirit of all things below, and I am damaging the glory of the sun, moon, and stars above. My unkindness is really too serious.
After the edict is issued, I must think about my mistakes and the things that I know, see, and think cannot be achieved, and I ask you to tell me.
And I also recommend virtuous and upright people who can speak out and give advice to correct my mistakes.
Take this opportunity to organize your own responsibilities and strive to reduce labor and expenses to facilitate the people.
Since I couldn't carry out the mission far away, I felt very uneasy and worried that people in remote areas might do evil things. For this reason, I did not lift the military alert.
Now even though we cannot get rid of the garrison at the frontier, we have ordered the soldiers to defend us strictly and withdrawn the troops led by General Wei.
The servant's existing horses were only enough, and the rest were given to the inn.
In the first month of the first lunar month, the emperor said: Agriculture is the foundation of the country. I will reclaim the land and personally lead the cultivation to provide grain for sacrifices to the ancestral temple.
In March, officials requested that the prince be made king of the vassals.
The emperor said: King You of Zhao died in confinement. I pity him very much and have appointed his eldest son Liu Sui as King of Zhao.
Liu Sui's younger brother Liu Pijiang, as well as the sons of King Hui of Qi, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, and Dongmu Hou Liu Xingju had meritorious services and could be crowned kings.
So Liu Bijiang, the youngest son of King Zhao You, was made King of Hejian, Zhu Xuhou, an important county in Qi State, was made King of Chengyang, Hou Hou of Dongmou was made King of Jibei, Prince Liu Wu was made the acting king, Prince Liu Shen was made King of Taiyuan, and Prince Liu Yi was made King of Liang.
The emperor said: In ancient times, when the world was governed, the imperial court had flags for offering good words and wooden pillars for writing critical remarks. In order to keep the way of governing the country smooth, people who can speak out and give correct advice can come to express their opinions.
Nowadays, there is a crime of defamation and evil words in law, which prevents ministers from speaking freely, and the emperor cannot hear his own faults. How can virtuous people from far away come to the court?
This law should be repealed.
If someone among the common people curses the emperor and agrees to hide it from each other, but later deceives and exposes each other, the officials will regard it as treason. If there are other remarks, the officials will regard it as slander.
These are the ignorance of ordinary people, and I strongly disagree with the death penalty based on this.
From now on, those who commit such crimes will not be tried or punished.
In September, the bronze tiger talisman used for dispatching troops and generals and the bamboo talisman used for envoys to go out and send out conquests were given to the county guards and the prime ministers.
On October 30, three years ago, a solar eclipse occurred.
In November, the emperor said: Some time ago, an edict was issued to allow the princes to go to their own feudal states, but some made excuses not to leave.
The prime minister is someone I value highly, and he should lead the princes to the feudal country.
Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Sui, was dismissed from the post of prime minister and returned to his feudal state, with Captain Yingyin Marquis Guan Ying as the prime minister.
The official position of Taiwei was abolished and its authority was vested in the Prime Minister.
In April, Liu Zhang, king of Chengyang, passed away.
Huainan King Liu Chang and his entourage Wei Jing killed Piyanghou and tried to eat him.
In May, the Xiongnu entered Beidi County and occupied the south of the Yellow River. They plundered and caused harm.
The emperor visited Ganquan Palace for the first time.
In June, the emperor said: The Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu are brothers and will not allow them to invade the border. For this reason, the gifts sent to the Xiongnu are very generous.
Now King Youxian left his country and led his troops to station in the areas south of the Yellow River that had surrendered to the Han Dynasty. He changed the original situation and went in and out of the border areas, killing officials and soldiers, expelling the barbarians in the castles and fortresses, not allowing them to live in the same place, bullying the border officials, and entering the interior to rob. He was very arrogant and unethical and violated the past agreement.
He dispatched 85,000 officials and cavalry from border areas to Gaonu, and dispatched Prime Minister Yingyinhou Guanying to attack the Xiongnu.
The Huns evacuated the frontier fortress. The lieutenant officer was dispatched to General Wei and stationed in Chang'an.
On the 27th, the emperor went from Ganquan Palace to Gaonu. He stopped by Taiyuan on the way and met with all the ministers of the former country and rewarded them all.
He also selected meritorious ministers and rewarded them separately, and the people in those villages gave them cattle and wine.
The people of Jinyang and Zhongdu were exempted from corvee service and taxes for three years.
We stayed in Taiyuan for more than ten days.
When Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, heard that the emperor was going to Dai and preparing to attack the Xiongnu, he took the opportunity to rebel and dispatched troops to attack Xingyang.
So the emperor issued an edict to the prime minister to stop attacking the Xiongnu, and sent Chen Wu, Marquis of Jipu, as a general to lead an army of 100,000 to attack the King of Jibei.
Qihou Zanhe was made a general and stationed in Xingyang.
On July 18, when the emperor returned to Chang'an from Taiyuan, he issued an edict to the officials: The King of Jibei violated morality and rebelled against the emperor, causing trouble for the officials and the people. It was a treasonous act.
If the army has not arrived, and the officials and people of Jibei settle down first, as well as those who surrendered with the army and local cities, they will be pardoned and their original official positions and titles will be restored.
Those who rebelled and returned with Liu Xingju, King of Jibei, were also pardoned.
In August, the army of Jibei feudal state was defeated and the king of Jibei was captured.
Pardon the officials and people of the feudal state of Jibei who followed the king of Jibei and rebelled.
In the sixth year, officials reported that Huainan King Liu Chang had abandoned the decrees of the late emperor and did not obey the emperor's edicts. The palace he lived in was not in compliance with the law.
The ministers discussed it and all said that Chang Liu should be executed on the street and his body exposed to the public. The emperor could not bear to deal with King Huainan according to the law, so he pardoned his sins and deposed him from the throne.
The ministers requested that King Huainan be exiled to the Qiongdu area of ​​Yandao, Shu County, and the emperor agreed.
Liu Chang died of illness on the road before he reached the place where he was exiled. The emperor took pity on him.
Later, in the sixteenth year, he honored Liu Chang, King of Huainan, with the posthumous title of King Li, and named his three sons King of Huainan, King of Hengshan, and King of Lujiang.
In the summer of the thirteenth year, the emperor said: I heard that disasters arise from resentment, and happiness arises from virtue. This is the law of God.
I should be personally responsible for the mistakes of all officials.
Now the officials praying secretly blame the ministers below, which makes my immorality even more obvious. I strongly disapprove of this approach.
It should be abolished.
In May, Taicang of Qi State ordered Chunyu Gong to commit a crime and should be punished. He was arrested and detained in Chang'an.
The Duke of Taicang had no boys, but five daughters.
When the Duke of Taicang was arrested and leaving, he scolded his daughter and said: "Whoever gives birth to a child but does not give birth to a boy has an urgent matter and it is of no use at all!"
His youngest daughter Tiying cried sadly alone and followed her father to Chang'an. She wrote a letter saying: My father is an official, and people in Qi state praise him for being honest and fair. Now he should be punished for breaking the law.
I am saddened that the dead cannot be resurrected, and those who are under punishment cannot join their limbs together again. Although I want to change my ways, there is no way out.
I am willing to be taken into the government as a slave to atone for my father's punishment so that he can change his ways.
Tiying's petition was sent to the emperor. The emperor felt pity for her and issued an edict: I heard that during the Yu family, criminals were painted on their clothes and hats to make them different from ordinary people, in order to humiliate the criminals and the people did not violate the law.
What is the reason for this?
It's because the politics are extremely clear.
Now the law stipulates three types of corporal punishment, but evil and illegal things cannot be prohibited. Where is the fault?
Isn't it because my virtue is poor and my education is not obvious?
I am deeply ashamed of myself.
Therefore, if the method of preaching is wrong, the people will fall into ignorance. "Poetry" says that a gentleman who is approachable is the parents of the people.
Nowadays, when people make mistakes, they are punished without education. Some people want to change their ways and become good, but there is no way to do it. I pity these people very much. The punishment is so severe that it can break limbs, scratch the skin, and never recover for life. This is so painful and immoral. How does it meet the meaning of being a parent of the people!
Corporal punishment should be abolished.
The emperor said: Agriculture is the foundation of the world, and nothing is more important than this.
Nowadays, people who work hard in agricultural production have to pay taxes. This is because there is no distinction between people who work for the basics and those who pursue the future, and the method of persuading people to work in agriculture is incomplete.
Farmland should be exempted from rent and taxes.
In the winter of the 14th year, the Huns conspired to invade the border and invade the border fortress, and killed Sun Yin, the captain of Beidi County.
The emperor then sent three generals to station in Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun. Lieutenant Zhou She was the general of the guard, and Lang Zhongling Zhang Wu was the general of the cavalry. They were stationed north of the Weishui River, commanding one thousand chariots and one hundred thousand cavalry.
The emperor personally comforted the soldiers, trained the troops, affirmed the teachings, and rewarded the officers and soldiers.
The emperor was preparing to personally lead troops to attack the Xiongnu. The ministers came out to dissuade him, but he refused to accept them.
The empress dowager firmly stopped the emperor, and the emperor canceled the original plan.
So with Dongyang Hou Zhang Xiangru as the general, Cheng Hou Dong Chi as the internal history, and Luan Bu as the general, they sent troops to attack the Xiongnu.
The Huns fled.
In the spring, the emperor said: It has been fourteen years since I was able to offer sacrifices to heaven and the ancestral temple with jade and silk. After a long period of time, I feel deeply ashamed that a person like me, who is neither smart nor wise, has been in charge of the world for a long time.
The sites for various kinds of sacrifices should be expanded and the amount of jade and silk used for sacrifices should be increased.
In the past, the kings of the past showed kindness without asking for repayment, held sacrifices without praying for blessings for themselves, respected the virtuous and talented, but did not value relatives, put the people before themselves, and were sage to the extreme.
Now I heard that when the officials in charge of sacrifices prayed for blessings from the gods, they only prayed for me and not for the people. I feel very ashamed.
For an immoral person like me, I enjoy the blessings of gods alone and the common people cannot share them, which aggravates my immorality.

summary:
Emperor Xiaowen, the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu, was made King of Dai after Chen Xi's defeat in the spring of Gaozu's eleventh year, with his capital at Zhongdu. In the eighth year of Emperor Gao's reign, Empress Gao died, and the Lu family plotted rebellion. The ministers annihilated them and summoned the king to become emperor. The king consulted his ministers; Zhang Wu advised caution, suspecting the ministers' intentions, while Song Chang argued that the Liu family's rule was divinely ordained, the people were loyal, and the king, as the eldest surviving son of Emperor Gaozu, was the rightful choice. After divination showed a favorable omen, the king sent his uncle Bo Zhao to verify the ministers' sincerity. Confirmed, he traveled to Chang'an, where he was greeted by officials. He initially refused the throne three times but eventually accepted, becoming Emperor Xiaowen.

Upon ascending the throne, the emperor granted amnesty, rewarded officials, and restored lands to Qi and Chu. He abolished the law of punishing innocent family members, stating it harmed the people and contradicted good governance. He initially hesitated to appoint a crown prince, suggesting his uncles or brothers instead, but officials insisted on his son, citing tradition. He agreed, and his eldest son became prince. He also established a queen and rewarded the poor and elderly. He honored meritorious officials from Dai, including Song Chang, and granted lands to followers of Emperor Gaozu.

The emperor faced natural disasters, interpreting solar eclipses as divine warnings. He urged officials to correct his faults, reduced expenses, and promoted agriculture. He abolished laws against defamation to encourage free speech. He dealt with rebellions, such as that of the King of Jibei, and conflicts with the Xiongnu, often opting for defense over aggression. He showed leniency to the King of Huainan, exiling him instead of executing him, and later honored his sons. He abolished corporal punishment after Tiying's plea for her father, emphasizing education over harsh penalties.

The emperor's reign was marked by frugality; he avoided building a terrace costing 100 pounds of gold, wore simple clothes, and forbade extravagance. He maintained peace with Nanyue and the Xiongnu through diplomacy, and tolerated critical ministers. His policies fostered moral education and stability. He died in Weiyang Palace in the seventh year of his reign, leaving a will urging simple mourning, minimal burial, and the release of harem women. He was honored as Emperor Xiaowen, and his temple was designated Taizong, with the "Zhaode Dance" created to commemorate his virtues. Historians praised his benevolence, humility, and effective governance, noting that his reign brought prosperity and moral clarity to the Han dynasty.

summary:
Emperor Xiaowu, the middle son of Emperor Xiaojing, ascended the throne after his father's sixteen-year reign. Upon becoming emperor, he showed particular devotion to worshipping ghosts and gods. During the early years of his reign, the Han Dynasty had enjoyed over sixty years of peace, and officials hoped the emperor would perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices to heaven and earth. The emperor, favoring Confucian scholarship, recruited talented individuals like Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, who proposed building a Mingtang for political and religious clarification. However, Empress Dowager Dou, who favored Huang-Lao teachings, opposed Confucianism, leading to Zhao Wan and Wang Zang's suicides and the abandonment of their plans. After the empress dowager's death six years later, the emperor recruited Gongsun Hong and others, and began performing suburban sacrifices every three years.

The emperor invited a divine spirit, originally a woman from Changling who died grieving for her son, to be worshipped in the Shanglin Garden. He also honored Li Shaojun, an alchemist who claimed to be seventy years old and capable of driving ghosts and making people immortal. Li Shaojun demonstrated his powers by identifying an ancient bronze vessel and advised the emperor to worship the stove, turn cinnabar into gold, and seek immortals on Penglai Mountain to achieve immortality. The emperor followed his advice, worshipping the stove and sending alchemists to the sea. After Li Shaojun's death, the emperor believed he had ascended to immortality and continued seeking alchemists.

Various alchemists presented methods for worshipping gods, including Bo Youji's teachings on Taiyi, the most noble god. The emperor built altars and performed sacrifices accordingly. Later, a young man named General Wencheng claimed to summon spirits and was rewarded, but his methods eventually failed, and he was executed after being caught deceiving the emperor. The emperor fell ill but recovered after consulting a wizard in Ganquan Palace, where he built the Longevity Palace and continued worshipping gods.

The emperor adopted year names based on auspicious signs, such as Yuanguang and Yuanshou. He performed the Hou Tu sacrifice at Fenyin and inspected various counties. Luan Da, recommended by Marquis Lecheng, claimed to have met immortals and was granted high honors, including marriage to a princess. However, his methods also failed, leading to his execution. The emperor continued seeking immortals, building temples and altars, and eventually performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai in the first year of Yuanfeng.

The emperor established a system of suburban sacrifices every three years and Feng and Shan ceremonies every five years. Despite numerous efforts by alchemists to find immortals, none succeeded. The emperor grew tired of their claims but continued hoping to meet real immortals. Taishi Gong, who accompanied the emperor on his tours, recorded these events to reveal the true nature of the worship practices, noting that specific details of rituals were handled by the responsible officials.

In the next three years, Yi Yin handled government affairs on behalf of the emperor, presided over state affairs, and accepted visits from princes.
Taijia lived in Tonggong for three years, reflected on and repented of his mistakes, and tried to be good again. So Yiyin welcomed Emperor Taijia back to the court and handed over the power to him.
Emperor Taijia practiced virtuous government, and the princes came to submit to the Yin and Shang Dynasties, and the people were peaceful.
Yi Yin admired Emperor Taijia very much, so he wrote three chapters of "Taijia Xun" to praise Emperor Taijia and called him Taizong.
After Taizong's death, his son Woding succeeded to the throne.
During the reign of Woding, Yi Yin passed away.
Yi Yin was buried in Bodi, so Jiu Shan wanted to use Yi Yin's deeds to instruct future generations, so he wrote "Woding".
When Woding died, his younger brother Tai Geng succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Tai Geng.
After Taigeng died, his son Xiaojia came to the throne; after Emperor Xiaojia passed away, his younger brother Yongji succeeded to the throne, and this was Emperor Yongji.
At this time, the power of the Yin Dynasty had declined, and some princes stopped coming to court.
After Yong's death, his younger brother Taiwu came to the throne. This is Emperor Taiwu.
Taiwu appointed Yi Zhi as his prime minister.
At that time, there was a strange phenomenon of mulberry and mulberry trees growing together in the court hall in the capital, and they grew as thick as two hands together overnight.
Emperor Taiwu felt very scared and went to ask Yi Zhi.
Yi Zhi said: I once heard that monsters cannot defeat virtuous people. Could it be that there are some flaws in your governance?
I hope you will still improve your moral character.
Taiwu followed Yi Zhi's advice, and the strange mulberry tree withered and disappeared.
Yi Zhi praised Wu Xian and told him about it.
Wu Xian was effective in managing the royal family's affairs. He wrote "Xianai" and "Taiwu", which recorded his achievements in governing the government and praised Emperor Taiwu's obedience and virtue.
Emperor Taiwu praised Yi Zhi in the Ancestral Temple and said that he could not be treated like other ministers. Yi Zhiqian refused and wrote "Original Fate" to reinterpret Taiwu's fate.
In this way, Yin became prosperous again, and the princes came to submit. Therefore, Emperor Taiwu was called Zhongzong.
After Zhongzong's death, his son Zhongding succeeded to the throne.
Emperor Zhongding moved the capital to Xian.
He Danjia later made his capital in Xiang, and Zu Yi moved his capital to Xing.
After the death of Emperor Zhongding, his younger brother Wairen came to the throne. This was Emperor Wairen.
"Zhongding" once recorded these things, but the book has been lost.
After the death of Emperor Wai Ren, his younger brother He Danjia succeeded him. This was Emperor Hedanjia.
When He Danjia was in power, the power of the Yin Dynasty weakened again.
After the death of He Danjia, his son Zuyi succeeded to the throne.
After Emperor Zuyi came to the throne, Yin prospered again.
Minister Wu Xian was appointed to an important position.
After the death of Zu Yi, his son Emperor Zu Xin came to the throne.
After the death of Emperor Zuxin, his younger brother Wojia came to the throne. This was Emperor Wojia.
After Wo Jia's death, Zu Ding, the son of Wo Jia's brother Zu Xin, came to the throne. This was Emperor Zu Ding.
After the death of Zuding, his younger brother Wojia's son Nangeng ascended the throne. This was Emperor Nangeng.
After the death of Emperor Nangeng, Emperor Zuding's son Yangjia came to the throne. This was Emperor Yangjia.
When Emperor Yangjia was on the throne, Yin's country was weak.
Since the time of Emperor Zhongding, the legitimate sons have been deposed and replaced by brothers and brothers' sons. Their brothers and their sons sometimes fight with each other to obtain the throne. There has been chaos for nine consecutive generations, so the princes have not come to court again.
After the death of Emperor Yangjia, his younger brother Pan Geng succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Pan Geng.
When Pan Geng was in power, the Yin Dynasty had established its capital in Amadi, north of the Yellow River. Pan Geng crossed the Yellow River and settled in Bo, Chengtang's former residence, south of the Yellow River.
So far, this is the fifth time the capital has been moved, and there has never been a fixed capital.
Everyone in the Yin Dynasty sighed and complained, unwilling to move again. Pan Geng then told the princes and ministers: "The great former king Chengtang and your ancestors worked together to bring peace to the world, and their laws and regulations should be abided by."
If we give up and do not work hard to pursue it, how can we achieve virtue?
So he crossed the Yellow River to the south bank, managed and repaired it, and obeyed and implemented Chengtang's decree. After that, the people were able to stabilize and the Yin Dynasty prospered again.
The princes also came to see him one after another. This was because Pan Geng followed Cheng Tang's moral policy.
After the death of Emperor Pan Geng, his younger brother Xiao Xin came to the throne. This is Emperor Xiao Xin.
When Xiao Xin was in power, Yin became weak again.
The people missed Pan Geng, so they wrote three chapters of "Pangeng".
After Emperor Xiao Xin passed away, his younger brother Xiao Yi came to the throne. This was Emperor Xiao Yi.
After the death of Emperor Xiao Yi, his son Wu Ding came to the throne.
After Emperor Wu Ding came to the throne, he wanted to revive the Yin Dynasty, but there was no suitable minister to assist him.
Wu Ding did not publish any political opinions for three years. Political matters were decided by Tsukasa, and he carefully observed the country's atmosphere.
Wu Ding dreamed of a saint named Shuo at night.
He observed the ministers and officials according to the appearance of the saint he saw in his dream, but none of them looked like the man in the dream.
So he sent hundreds of officials to search among the people, and finally found him in Fu Xian.
At that time, it was said that he was a slave working in Fuxian building roads.
The official brought the story to Wu Ding, and Wu Ding said it was this person.
After finding out the story, Wu Ding talked with him and found that he was really a sage, so he appointed him as the prime minister of the country, and the Yin country prospered in peace.
Therefore, the place name Fu Xian was used as the surname of Fu Shuo, and it became Fu Shuo.
Wu Ding offered sacrifices to the soup. The next day, a pheasant flew up and crowed on the ears of the tripod. Wu Ding was very frightened.
Zu Ji said: Your Majesty, don’t worry, let’s handle the political affairs first.
Zu Ji also taught Wu Ding: God examines the people of the world mainly to see whether they abide by morality. The life span given to humans by God may be long or short. It is not that God allows some people to die short-lived, but that they themselves end their lives midway.
Some people do not follow morals and do not obey judgments and punishments. God has decreed to correct their morals. Only then did he think of it and said: What should I do?
Alas, Your Majesty, you inherit the throne and treat the people respectfully. None of them are descendants of God. You must always offer sacrifices and do not worship those things that betray morality!
Wu Ding practiced virtuous government, and the people of the country were happy, and the Yin Dynasty prospered again.
Emperor Wu Ding passed away and his son Emperor Zu Geng came to the throne.
Zu Ji admired Wu Ding's virtuous administration because of the strange phenomenon of pheasants, built a temple for him, and called him Gaozong, so he wrote "Gaozong Xiri" and "Gaozong's Instructions".
Emperor Zu Geng passed away, and his younger brother Zu Jia came to the throne. This was Emperor Jia.
Emperor Jia became promiscuous and the Yin Dynasty declined again.
After the death of Emperor Jia, his son Lin Xin came to the throne.
Lin Xin died, and his younger brother Geng Ding came to the throne. This was Emperor Geng Ding.
After Geng Ding's death, his son Wu Yi came to the throne.
The capital of Yin State left Bo and moved to the north of the Yellow River.
Emperor Wu Yi was tyrannical and cruel. He made a puppet and called it a god.
He played chess with the puppet and let others make the moves for it.
If the god doesn't win, insult it.
He also made a leather pouch, filled it with blood, raised his head to the sky and shot arrows at it, calling it "shooting the sky".
Wu Yi went hunting between the Yellow River and the Wei River. There was a sudden thunder in the sky, and Wu Yi was killed.
His son Emperor Taiding ascended the throne.
After the death of Emperor Taiding, his son Yi came to the throne. When Emperor Yi came to the throne, the Yin Dynasty declined even more.
The eldest son of Emperor Yi was called Wei Ziqi. Qi's mother was of low status, so Qi was not qualified to inherit the throne.
Emperor Yi's youngest son was named Xin. Xin's mother was the queen, so Xin was appointed as his heir.
After the death of Emperor Yi, Xin succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Xin, and the world called him Zhou.
Zhou was talented, eloquent, quick in action, sharp in hearing and eyesight. He was also extremely strong and could fight wild beasts with his bare hands. His wisdom is enough to refuse the advice of his subordinates, and his language is enough to cover up his mistakes.
He used his talents to show off in front of his ministers, and relied on his prestige to promote himself everywhere, thinking that everyone in the world was inferior to him. He was fond of drinking, arrogant and licentious, and doted on women. He dotes on Daji especially and obeys everything Daji says.
So he asked the musicians to compose new debauched music, Beili dance music, and lascivious songs.
He increased taxes to fill Lutai's treasury and Juqiao's granary.
He collected dogs, horses and novelty toys to fill the palace. He also expanded the garden terrace of the sand dune, captured a large number of wild animals and birds, and placed them inside.
He was indifferent and rude to ghosts and gods, and invited a large number of performers to gather in the sand dunes. He used wine to make pool water, hung meat as a forest, made men and women naked, chased and played there, and drank and had fun all night long.
The people resented him, and some princes betrayed him. So he increased the punishment and invented a kind of torture called Pao Ge.
Zhou appointed Xibochang, Jiuhou and Ehou as the three Dukes.
Jiu Hou had a beautiful daughter who was dedicated to Zhou. She did not like to have sex and have fun. Zhou was furious and killed her. At the same time, Jiu Hou was also tortured and chopped into meat paste.
The Marquis of E resolutely tried to dissuade him, and the argument was fierce. As a result, the Marquis of E was also beheaded and made into dried meat.
When Xibochang heard about these things, he sighed secretly.
After Chonghou Hu knew about it, he reported it to King Zhou, who imprisoned Xibo in Youli.
Xibo's ministers, Hong Yao and others, brought beauties, treasures and fine horses to Zhou, and King Zhou pardoned Xibo.
After Xibo was released from prison, he offered the land west of Luoshui to Zhou Jin and asked him to abolish the torture of cannons.
Zhou agreed to him and gave him a bow, arrow and axe, so that he could conquer other princes. In this way, he became the leader of the princes in the western region, and he was known as Xibohou.
Zhou appointed Fei Zhong to manage state affairs.
Fei Zhong was good at flattery and greedy for wealth, so the people of Yin State were not close to King Zhou.
Zhou also allowed evil to come.
When evil comes, good will lead to slander and slander, so the princes became more and more alienated from King Zhou.
When Xibo returned to the capital, he secretly practiced virtuous governance and performed good deeds. Many people among the princes betrayed Zhou and came to join Xibo.
Xibo's power became stronger and stronger, and King Zhou gradually lost his power.
Prince Bigan came forward to persuade Zhou, but Zhou refused to listen.
Shang Rong was a talented and virtuous man, and the people respected and loved him very much, but Zhou deposed him.
When Xibo attacked the hungry country and destroyed it, Zuyi, the minister of Zhou, heard about it and resented Zhou. He was very frightened and went to Zhou to report: God has cut off the longevity of our Yin country. People who know good and bad luck use big tortoises for divination, but there are no good omens. It’s not that the late king didn’t protect our descendants, but that you, the great king, were licentious and tyrannical and cut yourself off from heaven. Therefore, God abandoned us, so that we can’t live in peace of mind. If we don’t understand God’s will, we can’t follow the ordinary laws. As a result, the people of our country all hope that the Yin Kingdom will perish. They say: Why doesn’t God show its majesty? Why haven’t God’s orders come yet?
Your Majesty, what do you want to do now?
Zhou said: Wasn't it that I was blessed by heaven when I was born?
After Zuyi returned home, he said: Zhou can no longer be persuaded!
After the death of Xibochang, King Wu of Zhou led his army to the east. When they arrived at Mengjin, the princes betrayed Yin and Zhou and came to join King Wu from eight hundred countries.
The princes all said: It's time to attack Zhou!
King Wu of Zhou said: You don’t know the destiny of heaven.
So the class teacher returned to China.
Zhou became even more promiscuous and had no end.
Wei Zi repeatedly advised Zhou, but Zhou refused to listen. Wei Zi discussed with the Grand Master and the Young Master and left Yin.
Bigan said: As a minister, I have to risk my life to advise.
So he tried his best to persuade Zhou.
Zhou was furious and said: I heard that the saint's heart has seven holes.
So he cut open Bigan's chest and took out his heart to see.
Jizi was frightened when he saw it, so he pretended to be crazy and became a slave. Zhou imprisoned Jizi again.
The grand masters and young masters of Yin State took the sacrificial vessels and musical instruments and fled to Zhou State in a hurry.
King Wu of Zhou led the princes to attack Yin Zhou.
Zhou also sent troops to resist the Zhou army in Muye.
On the day of Jiazi, Zhou's army was defeated. Zhou fled into the city, climbed to the deer platform, put on his precious jade clothes, ran to the fire and burned himself to death.
King Wu of Zhou cut off Zhou's head and hung it on a white flagpole.
King Zhou Wu executed Daji again, released the imprisoned Jizi, repaired Bigan's tomb, and commended Shang Rong's alleys.
He also enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng and his father, allowing him to continue to worship Yin's ancestors and order him to implement Pan Geng's virtuous government. The people of Yin were very happy.
So King Wu of Zhou became the emperor.
Because descendants of the Yin and Shang dynasties devalued the title of emperor, he was called king.
King Wu of Zhou made the descendants of Yin princes and subordinated them to Zhou.
After the death of King Wu of Zhou, Wu Geng, Uncle Guan, and Uncle Cai launched a rebellion. King Cheng of Zhou ordered Zhou Gongdan to kill them, and made Wei Zi the king of the Song Dynasty to continue the incense of the Yin Dynasty.
Tai Shigong said: I compiled the deeds of the Deed based on "Song of Shang". Since the Tang Dynasty, many historical facts have been collected from "Shang Shu" and "The Book of Songs".
Qi was the surname of Zi, and his descendants were enfeoffed and took the name of the country as their surnames, including the Yin family, the Lai family, the Song family, the Kongtong family, the Zhi family, the Bei Yin family, and the Mu Yi family.
Confucius once said that the people of the Yin Dynasty had the best cars, and white was valued in that era.
summary:
Yin Qi's mother, Jian Di, was the daughter of the You'u family and the second concubine of Emperor Ku. While bathing in a river with three others, she swallowed an egg dropped by a black bird, became pregnant, and gave birth to Qi. Qi grew up to assist Yu in flood control. Emperor Shun appointed him as Situ to promote the education of the five ethics, sealed him in Shang Land, and gave him the surname Zi. Qi's achievements during the eras of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Xia Yu brought stability to the people. After his death, his descendants succeeded him in a long lineage, culminating in Chengtang (Tang), who moved the capital eight times.

Chengtang, a Fangbo under the Xia Dynasty, first conquered Ge Bo for failing to offer sacrifices. He wrote "Tang Zheng" to record this. Yi Yin (Aheng) served Chengtang, either as a married servant or after being hired following five invitations. Yi Yin advised Chengtang on governance, left for the Xia capital, and returned to Bo, writing "Nv Jiu" and "Nv Fang." Chengtang's kindness was shown when he ordered a net set on all sides to be reduced to three, allowing animals to escape, which impressed the princes. Xia Jie's tyranny led Chengtang to raise troops, with Yi Yin following. Chengtang issued the "Tang Oath," defeated Xia Jie at Mingtiao, and conquered Sanke. He replaced the Xia social god but wrote "Xia She" to explain why it was not replaced. After the princes submitted, Chengtang ascended the throne, wrote "Tang Gao" to warn the princes, and revised the calendar to favor white.

After Chengtang's death, his son Taiding died before ascending, so Waibing and then Zhongren ruled briefly. Yi Yin then supported Taijia, Chengtang's grandson. Taijia's tyranny led Yi Yin to exile him to Tong Palace for three years, during which Yi Yin governed. Taijia repented, returned to power, and practiced virtuous government, earning the title Taizong. After Taizong's death, Woding succeeded, and Yi Yin died. Subsequent rulers like Tai Geng, Yong Ji, and Tai Wu saw decline, but Tai Wu's appointment of Yi Zhi and response to a strange mulberry tree event revived Yin, earning him the title Zhongzong. Later rulers like Zhong Ding, Wai Ren, He Dan Jia, and Zu Yi saw further decline and revival, with Wu Xian playing a key role.

From Zhong Ding onward, succession disputes among brothers and sons caused nine generations of chaos, weakening Yin. Pan Geng moved the capital to Bo, Chengtang's former residence, and revived Yin by following Chengtang's decrees. After Pan Geng's death, Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi ruled weakly. Wu Ding, seeking to revive Yin, dreamed of a sage named Shuo, found him as a slave in Fu Xian, and appointed him prime minister, bringing prosperity. A pheasant crowing on a tripod during a sacrifice led Zu Ji to advise Wu Ding on morality, further strengthening Yin. Wu Ding was later called Gaozong.

After Wu Ding's death, Zu Geng and Zu Jia ruled, with Zu Jia's promiscuity causing decline. Subsequent rulers like Lin Xin, Geng Ding, and Wu Yi saw further decline. Wu Yi's cruelty, including making a puppet and shooting a blood-filled pouch, led to his death by lightning. His son Tai Ding and then Yi ruled, with Yi's son Xin (Zhou) succeeding. Zhou was talented but tyrannical, indulging in debauchery with Daji, increasing taxes, and inventing the Pao Ge torture. He killed Jiu Hou and E Hou, imprisoned Xibo (later King Wen), who was released after bribes. Xibo practiced virtuous governance, attracting princes. Zhou's minister Bigan was killed for advising, and Jizi was imprisoned. King Wu of Zhou led a revolt, defeated Zhou at Muye, and Zhou burned himself to death. King Wu executed Daji, released Jizi, and enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng. Later, Wu Geng rebelled, and King Cheng made Wei Zi the king of Song to continue Yin's lineage.

translation:
The First Emperor of Qin was the son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin.
When King Zhuang Xiang was a hostage of Qin in Zhao, he saw Lu Buwei's concubine and liked her very much, so he married her and gave birth to the first emperor.
The First Emperor was born in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin.
When he was born, he was named Zheng and his surname was Zhao.
At the age of thirteen, King Zhuang Xiang died, and Zheng succeeded him as King of Qin.
At that time, the Qin State had annexed Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong, crossed Wan, occupied Ying, and established Nanjun; went north to the east of Shangjun, and occupied Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang counties; east to Rongyang, eliminated the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou Dynasties, and established Sanchuan County.
Lu Buwei became prime minister, granted a fief of 100,000 households, and was named Marquis Wenxin.
Recruiting guests and tourists, intending to annex the world.
Li Si was Shiren, and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, Hegong and others were generals.
The King of Qin was young and in the early days of his accession to the throne, state affairs were left to the ministers.
Jinyang rebelled, and in the first year of Qin Wangzheng's reign, General Meng Ao put down the rebellion.
In the second year, Duke He led his army to attack Juanyi and killed 30,000 people.
In three years, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities.
Wang Ye is dead.
In the tenth month, General Meng Ao attacked Wei's Yi and Yougui.
This year the food harvest failed.
In four years, he conquered Yi and Yougui.
In March, the troops were withdrawn.
The hostages of Qin returned from Zhao, and the prince of Zhao left Qin and returned to Zhao.
In October Gengyin, locusts flew from the east and covered the sky.
Plague in the world.
The common people paid a thousand stones of corn to pay one level of nobility.
In the fifth year, General Meng Ao attacked the Wei State and pacified the cities of Suanzao, Yanyi, Xuyi, Changping, Yongqiu, and Shanyang. They all conquered them by force, and captured twenty cities in total.
Start setting up East County.
Thunder in winter.
In six years, South Korea, Wei, Zhao, Wei, and Chu attacked Qin together and captured Shouling.
Qin sent troops, and the armies of the five countries withdrew.
The Qin State conquered the Wei State and invaded Dongjun. Wei Junjiao led his relatives to move to Yewang, relying on the mountain dangers to defend the Hanoi area within the Wei State.
In seven years, the comet first appeared in the east. Appeared again in the north. Appears in the West in May.
General Meng Ao died.
It was because he attacked Longyi, Guyi and Qingdu, and then returned to attack Jiyi.
The comet appeared in the west for another sixteen days.
Queen Mother Xia is dead.
In the eighth year, Zhao Chengyu, the younger brother of King Zhao Zheng of Qin, led an army to attack Zhao. Tunliu rebelled. As a result, all his officers were killed and the people there were moved to Lintao.
The general who came to attack Cheng Xi died, and the soldier Pu Hao who stayed in the camp rebelled again and died in battle. After his death, he was tortured by whipping his body.
Fish from the Yellow River rushed to the shore in large numbers, and people drove carriages to the east to find food.
Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin.
Give him the Shanyang region to live in.
There are no restrictions on Lao Ai in terms of palaces, carriages and horses, clothing, gardens, and hunting.
All matters, big or small, are decided by Lao Ai.
Hexi and Taiyuan counties were also changed into feudal states of Lao Ai.
In the ninth year, a comet appeared, sometimes shining brightly into the sky.
Attack Yuanyi and Puyang of Wei State.
In April, King Qin stayed in Yongdi.
In Jiyou, the King of Qin held a crown ceremony and wore a sword.
The conspiracy of Changxin Hou Lao Ai to cause rebellion was discovered, so she fraudulently used the seals of the King of Qin and the Queen Mother to mobilize the army and guards of the county, national cavalry, Rong Zhai leaders, and She people, planning to attack Qinian Palace and launch a rebellion.
When the King of Qin learned of the news, he sent his prime ministers Changping Jun and Changwen Jun to mobilize soldiers to attack Lao'ai.
In the battle at Xianyang, hundreds of people were killed and all received titles. Eunuchs who participated in the battle also received first-class titles.
Lao Ai and others were defeated and fled.
The King of Qin then issued an order throughout the country: Anyone who captured Lao Ai alive would be rewarded one million; anyone who killed Lao Ai would be rewarded five hundred thousand.
Lao Ai and others were all captured.
Twenty people, including Wei Wei Jie, Nei Shisi, Zuo Yi Jie, and Zhongda Fu Ling Qi, were all beheaded and hung.
They also cut their bodies into pieces and paraded them around, wiping out their clans.
Lao Ai's family members were punished for minor crimes by serving as ghost slaves.
More than 4,000 people who had their titles removed and moved to Shu lived in Fangling.
It's so cold this month that some people freeze to death.
Yang Duanhe attacked Yanshi.
The comet appeared in the west and then in the north, following the Beidou as it moved southward for eighty days.
Ten years later, the Prime Minister Lu Buwei was convicted of Lao Ai's involvement and was removed from the post of Prime Minister.
Huan  was made general.
The envoys from Qi and Zhao came to prepare a banquet with wine.
Mao Jiao, a native of Qi State, advised the King of Qin: The State of Qin is taking running the world as its own responsibility, and the King has the reputation of banishing his mother and the Queen Mother. I am afraid that the princes of various countries will hear about this and rebel against the State of Qin.
The King of Qin went to Yongdi to welcome the Queen Mother, returned to Xianyang, and asked her to live in Ganquan Palace again.
The King of Qin carried out large-scale raids and expelled guests from the vassal states. Li Si wrote a letter to dissuade him, and the King of Qin revoked the order to expel the guests.
He took the opportunity to advise King Qin. He first conquered Korea and made other vassal states fearful. So King Qin sent Li Si to attack South Korea.
The King of Han was very worried and discussed with Han Fei to weaken Qin's power.
Wei Liao, a native of Daliang, came to Qin and advised the king of Qin: With the great power of Qin, the princes are like the monarchs of a county. But I am worried that the princes will unite and attack Qin by surprise. This is why Zhibo, Fucha and King Min perished.
I hope that the king will not be stingy with money, bribe their powerful ministers, and destroy their plans. The loss will only be 300,000 catties of gold, and all the princes will be wiped out.
The King of Qin followed his advice and treated Wei Liao with equal etiquette every time he met with him. His clothes and food were also the same as Wei Liao's.
Wei Liao said: King Qin has a high nose, slender eyes, a chest like a bird of prey, and a voice like a jackal. He is mean and ungrateful, and his heart is like a tiger or a wolf. He is prone to humility when he is in poverty, and he is easy to devour others when he is successful.
I am a commoner, but when they receive me, they are often willing to be inferior to me.
If King Qin succeeds in conquering the world, everyone in the world will become his captives.
I can't get along with him for a long time.
Wei Liao ran away.
The King of Qin found out and firmly retained him, making him a captain of the Qin State, and finally adopted his strategy.
At this time, Li Si was in charge of the government.
In the eleventh year, Wang Jian, Huan , and Yang Duanhe attacked Ye Yi and captured nine cities.
Wang Jian attacked Dinglanyu and Puyang, and combined all the soldiers into one army.
Wang Jian took command of the entire army. After eighteen days, he deported the useless personnel in the army who were below the level of fighting, and elected two out of ten people to join the army. Huan  led the troops to capture Yeyi and Puyang.
In the twelfth year, Wenxinhou Lu Buwei died and was buried privately.
If Lu Buwei's family members come to mourn, if they are Jin people, they will be expelled; if they are Qin people, those with a salary of more than 600 shi will have their title removed and moved away from their old residence. If no one comes to mourn him with a salary of less than 500 shi, they will also move away from their old residence without losing their title.
From then on, those who govern the country's political affairs, like Lao Ai and Lu Buwei, are rebellious and unruly, and their whole family will be confiscated, and they will be dealt with in this way.
In autumn, Lao'ai's family members who were supposed to move to Shu were pardoned.
At that time, there was a severe drought for six months, and it didn't rain until August.
In the thirteenth year, Huan  attacked Pingyang of the State of Zhao, killed the general of the State of Zhao, Hu Zou, and beheaded 100,000 people.
King Zhao fled to Henan.
In the first month of the year, comets appear in the east.
In October, Huan  attacked Zhao.
In the fourteenth year, he attacked the Zhao army in Pingyang, captured Yi'an, defeated the Zhao army and killed its general.
Huan  pacified Pingyang and Wucheng.
Han Fei went to Qin as an envoy, and Qin adopted Li Si's plan and detained Han Fei in Qin. Han Fei died in Yunyang.
The King of Han requested to be a vassal of Qin.
In the fifteenth year, the State of Qin sent out a large number of troops. One army arrived in Yeyi and another army arrived in Taiyuan and captured Langmeng.
An earthquake occurs.
In September of the 16th year, troops were sent to take over the Nanyang area of ​​South Korea, and Teng temporarily acted as the county governor.
Men were ordered to register their age.
Wei State donated land to Qin State.
Qin established Liyi.
In the seventeenth year, Neishiteng attacked South Korea, captured Han Wangan, annexed all South Korean territory, and set up a county in its territory, named Yingchuan.
An earthquake occurs.
Queen Mother Huayang died.
The people suffered from severe famine.
In the eighteenth year, a large number of troops were sent to attack the State of Zhao. Wang Jian led the soldiers from Shangdi to capture Jingxing. Yang Duanhe led the Hanoi soldiers, Qiang Yu also led his army to attack Zhao, and Yang Duanhe besieged Handan City.
In the 19th year, Wang Jian and Qiang You all captured and pacified the Dongyang area of ​​​​Zhao and captured the king of Zhao.
He led his troops to prepare to attack Yan State and stationed his troops in Zhongshan.
When the King of Qin came to Handan, he killed all those who had a grudge against his mother's family when he was born in the State of Zhao.

summary:
The First Emperor of Qin, son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, was born Zheng in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin. At thirteen, he succeeded as King of Qin after his father's death. The Qin state had already expanded significantly, annexing territories like Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and establishing commanderies. Lu Buwei served as prime minister, with Li Si as a retainer and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, and others as generals. Due to the king's youth, state affairs were managed by ministers.

In the early years of his reign, Qin faced rebellions and military campaigns. Meng Ao suppressed a revolt in Jinyang and later attacked Wei, capturing twenty cities. The king faced challenges including a locust plague, famine, and a coalition attack from five states. In the eighth year, Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin and given extensive authority. The following year, his conspiracy to rebel was discovered, leading to a battle in Xianyang. Lao Ai was captured, and his followers were executed or exiled. Lu Buwei was removed as prime minister due to his involvement.

The king implemented policies to strengthen Qin, including expelling guest officials, though Li Si's counsel led to the revocation of this order. Wei Liao advised bribing enemy officials, a strategy the king adopted. Military campaigns continued, with Wang Jian and others attacking Zhao and capturing cities. In the seventeenth year, Qin conquered Han, establishing Yingchuan Commandery. The conquest of Zhao followed, with the king personally executing those who had wronged his mother's family in Handan.

The assassination attempt by Jing Ke of Yan failed, leading to Qin's attack on Yan. Wang Jian and others captured Yan's capital and obtained Prince Dan's head. Wei was conquered by diverting rivers to flood Daliang. Jing (Chu) was attacked, with Wang Jian capturing King Jing. Xiang Yan's rebellion was suppressed, and by the twenty-fifth year, Yan, Dai, and Qi were all conquered, unifying China.

The king declared himself the First Emperor, abolishing posthumous titles and establishing a system of succession for ten thousand generations. He adopted water virtue, with black as the color, six as the standard, and harsh laws. The empire was divided into thirty-six commanderies, with unified laws, weights, measures, and writing. Wealthy families were moved to Xianyang, and palaces were built imitating those of conquered states.

The First Emperor toured extensively, erecting stone tablets praising his achievements. He sought immortality, sending Xu Shi with boys and girls to find the elixir. He burned books and buried Confucian scholars alive, enforcing strict laws. The construction of the Epang Palace and the Lishan tomb involved hundreds of thousands of workers. The emperor's death was concealed, and a forged edict made Hu Hai the Second Emperor, forcing Fusu to commit suicide.

The Second Emperor's reign was marked by cruelty and rebellion. Chen She's uprising spread, and Zhang Han suppressed it with convicts. Zhao Gao gained power, killing officials and princes. The Second Emperor was eventually forced to commit suicide by Zhao Gao's agents. Ziying, made king, killed Zhao Gao but soon surrendered to Liu Bang. Xiang Yu killed Ziying and the Qin clan, burning Xianyang. The Qin dynasty ended after 610 years from Duke Xiang to the Second Emperor.
