The King of Han said: I heard that the title of emperor belongs to virtuous people. It is just a name but no reality, and it is not enough to hold the throne. I dare not accept the position of emperor.
All the ministers said: The king was born in poverty, punished the rebels, and brought peace to the world. Those who had meritorious service would cede lands and make them princes.
The king does not respect titles, so everyone has doubts about their titles and dare not take them seriously.
The ministers and others insisted to the death that the king should be called emperor.
The King of Han repeatedly gave in and had no choice but to say: "Everyone must think that this will benefit the country."
In order to benefit the country, the emperor took the throne north of Sishui during the Jiawu Period. The emperor said that Emperor Yi had no descendants.
King Han Xin of Qi was familiar with the customs of Chu, so he moved to be the king of Chu and established Xiapi as his capital. The feudal lord Pengyue was granted the title of King of Liang, and his capital was established in Dingtao. The original King Xin of Han was still the King of Han and established his capital in Yangdi.
Wu Rui, the king of Hengshan, moved to Changsha and established his capital in Linxiang.
Fanjun's general Mei Kuang had made military exploits and followed him into Wuguan. The emperor thanked Fanjun for his kindness.
King Yingbu of Huainan, King Zang Tu of Yan, and King Zhang Ao of Zhao all maintained their previous titles.
The world is basically at peace.
Gaozu established his capital at Luoyang, and all the princes became Gaozu's vassals.
The original Linjiang King Gonghuan rebelled against Xiang Yu and ordered Lu Wan and Liu Jia to besiege Gonghuan but failed to conquer.
Gonghuan surrendered a few months later and killed him in Luoyang.
In May, all the soldiers were disarmed and returned home.
The soldiers of the vassal states who stayed in Guanzhong were exempted from corvee for twelve years, and those who returned to their hometown were exempted from corvee for six years and were provided with food for one year.
Emperor Gaozu held a banquet in Luoyang Nangong.
Emperor Gaozu said: All princes and generals, please do not hide anything from me and speak your mind.
What is the reason why I can win the world?
Why did the Xiang family lose the world?
Gao Qi and Wang Ling replied: Your Majesty is arrogant and insulting, while Xiang Yu is kind and protective.
However, His Majesty sent people to attack the city and capture the territory, and the places he surrendered and captured were granted to him, sharing the interests of the people of the world.
Xiang Yu was jealous of the virtuous, framed those who had merit, and doubted the virtuous. He won battles without giving any reward for his merits, and gained land without sharing the profits. This was the reason why he lost the world.
Emperor Gaozu said: You know the first, but you don’t know the second.
When it comes to planning and planning in the tent, which is worse than a thousand miles away, I am not as good as the ovary.
In guarding the country, pacifying the people, supplying military supplies, and smoothing food routes, I am not as good as Xiao He.
With millions of soldiers in a company, we will win every battle and conquer every attack. I am not as good as Han Xin.
These three people are all outstanding people. I can use them. This is the reason why I have won the world.
Xiang Yu had Fan Zeng but could not use him. This was the reason why he was captured and killed by me.
Emperor Gaozu wanted to establish his capital in Luoyang for a long time, but Liu Jing, a native of Qi, dissuaded him. Zhang Liang, the remaining marquis, also persuaded Emperor Gaozu to enter Guanzhong as the capital. On the same day, Emperor Gaozu ordered him to get up and enter Guanzhong to establish his capital.
In June, there is a general amnesty.
In October, King Zang Tu of Yan rebelled and captured Dai.
Emperor Gaozu personally led the army to attack him, captured Zang Tu, King of Yan, and immediately appointed Taiwei Lu Wan as King of Yan.
He sent Prime Minister Fan Kuai to lead troops to attack Dai.
In the autumn of this year, Li Ji rebelled. Gaozu personally led troops to attack him, but Li Ji fled.
Li Ji was a general of the Xiang family.
When the Xiang family was defeated, Li Ji was the magistrate of Chen County and did not follow Xiang Yu. He fled and surrendered to Gaozu, who made him a marquis in Yingchuan.
When Emperor Gaozu arrived in Luoyang, he summoned all the Tonghous based on their names, and Li Ji was also summoned.
Liji was very frightened, so he rebelled. In six years, Emperor Gaozu met with the Grand Duke once every five days, just like the common people's father-son etiquette.
The Taigong's family order admonished the Taigong: There are no two days in the sky, and there are no two masters in the earth.
Now, although Gaozu is your son, he is the monarch of all peoples; although Taigong is Gaozu's father, he is a subordinate.
How can the monarch be allowed to pay homage to his ministers!
In this way, the monarch loses his majesty and dignity.
Later, Emperor Gaozu paid homage to the Grand Duke. The Grand Duke greeted him at the door with a broom in his arms and walked backwards.
Emperor Gaozu was shocked and got out of the car to help the grandpa.
Taigong said: The emperor is the monarch of all people, how can he destroy the laws of the world because of me!
Therefore, Emperor Gaozu respected the Grand Duke as the Supreme Emperor.
Emperor Gaozu praised his family order in his heart and rewarded him with five hundred catties of gold.
In December, someone wrote a letter to accuse Chu King Han Xin of treason. Emperor Gaozu asked the ministers on his left and right, and the ministers rushed to attack Han Xin.
Emperor Gaozu adopted Chen Ping's strategy and pretended to tour Yunmengze and met with the princes in Chen County. King Han Xin of Chu went to greet him and took the opportunity to arrest him.
On this day, the world is amnesty.
Tian Ken came to congratulate him and advised Gaozu: Your Majesty has captured Han Xin and established his capital in Qinzhong.
Qin is a place with a superior geographical situation. There are dangers of blocking mountains and rivers, and it is thousands of miles away from the princes. It has a million warriors with halberds. Qin is a hundred times better than other places.
The terrain is convenient, and sending troops to the princes from here is like a high-rise building.
As for Qi, there are the riches of Langye and Jimo in the east, the dangers of Mount Tai in the south, the natural boundary of Zhuohe River in the west, and the benefits of fish and salt in the Bohai Sea in the north. The area is two thousand miles away, and there are one million warriors with halberds. It is thousands of miles away from the vassal states. Qi is ten times better than other places.
So these two places are Eastern Qin and Western Qin.
If he is not your Majesty's biological son, don't send him to be the king of Qi. Gaozu said: OK.
Reward five hundred catties of gold.
More than ten days later, Han Xin was granted the title of Marquis of Huaiyin and his fiefdom was divided into two countries.
Emperor Gaozu said that General Liu Jia had made many military exploits and was named King of Jing, and he was called the Gong Huaidong.
His younger brother Liu Jiao became the king of Chu and became the king of Huaixi.
His son Liu Fei became the king of Qi and was granted more than seventy cities. All the people who could speak the language of Qi belonged to the state of Qi.
Emperor Gaozu judged the merits and deeds, cut talismans with the princes as letters, and granted the princes food and towns.
Move Han Wangxin to Taiyuan.
In the seventh year, the Xiongnu attacked Han Wangxin in Mayi, and Han Wangxin rebelled with the Xiongnu in Taiyuan.
Baitu Manqiuchen and Wang Huang established Zhao Li, the original Zhao general, as king and rebelled against the Han Dynasty. Gaozu went to crusade in person.
The weather was so cold that two or three of the ten soldiers lost their fingers from the cold, and finally arrived at Pingcheng.
The Xiongnu besieged Gaozu in Pingcheng, and they withdrew their troops after seven days.
Fan Kuai was ordered to stay and pacify Daidi.
He made his elder brother Liu Zhong the acting king.
In February, Emperor Gaozu passed through Zhaodi and Luoyang from Pingcheng to Chang'an.
Changle Palace has been built, and officials below the prime minister have moved to Chang'an to work.
In August, Emperor Gaozu led his army eastward to attack the remaining rebels of King Xin of Han in Dongyuan.
Prime Minister Xiao built Weiyang Palace and built the East Palace, North Palace, Front Hall, Arsenal, and Taicang.
When Emperor Gaozu came back and saw that the palace was extremely magnificent, he was very angry and said to Xiao He: The world is in turmoil and has been fighting hard for several years. The success or failure is not yet known. Why should we build excessively luxurious palaces now?
Xiao He said: It is precisely because the world is not stable that we take this opportunity to build the palace.
Moreover, the emperor's home is all over the world. If the palace is not spectacular and gorgeous, it will not be enough to show the emperor's nobility and majesty, and it is also to prevent future generations of palaces from surpassing them.
Only then did Gaozu feel happy.
Gaozu went to Dongyuan and passed by Bairen. Zhao Xiangguan and his superiors murdered Gaozu. Gaozu had an abnormal heartbeat and therefore did not stop at Bairen.
Liu Zhong, the acting king, abandoned his country and fled. He returned to Luoyang and was deposed as Marquis of Heyang.
In the ninth year, Zhao Xiangguan's plan to murder Gaozu was discovered, and all three of their clans were executed.
Zhang Ao, king of Zhao, was deposed as Marquis of Xuanping.
In this year, the nobles of the Chu State Zhao, Qu, Jing, Huai, and the Qi nobles Tian were moved to Guanzhong.
Weiyang Palace was built.
Emperor Gaozu gathered the princes and ministers and held a banquet in the front hall of Weiyang Palace.
Holding a jade wine cup in his hand, Emperor Gaozu stood up and congratulated the Emperor on his birthday, saying: "In the past, adults often thought that I was a scoundrel who could not make a living. I could not manage the industry and was not as diligent as Zhong Qing."
Now, compared with Zhong, who has accomplished more in my career?
All the officials in the palace shouted long live and laughed happily.
In October of the tenth year, King Yingbu of Huainan, King Pengyue of Liang, King Lu Wan of Yan, King Liu Jia of Jing, King Liu Jiao of Chu, King Liu Fei of Qi, and King Wu Rui of Changsha all came to Changle Palace to pay homage.
Nothing happens in spring and summer.
In July, the Supreme Emperor died in Yueyang Palace, and the kings of Chu and Liang came to mourn him.
Pardon the prisoners in Yueyang.
Li Yi was renamed Xinfeng.
In August, Zhao Xiangguo and Chen Xi rebelled in Dai.
Emperor Gaozu said: Chen Xi once worked for me and kept his word.
Daidi is a place that I value, so I made Chen Xi a prince and guarded Daidi in the name of the Prime Minister. Now he and Wang Huang and others plundered Daidi.
The officials and people of Dai are not guilty, so forgive the officials and people of Dai.
In September, Emperor Gaozu himself went east to attack Chen Xi.
Arriving at Handan, Emperor Gaozu said happily: "If Chen Xi doesn't go south to defend Handan, and relies on the Zhang River as a formation, I know he has no ability."
Hearing that Chen Xi's generals were all former merchants, Emperor Gaozu said: I know how to deal with them.
So he used gold to lure Chen Xi's generals, and many of Chen Xi's generals surrendered.
In the eleventh year, Emperor Gaozu's crusade against Chen Kuang and others in Handan was not over yet. Chen Kuang's general Hou Chang led more than 10,000 people to fight on the move. Wang Huang garrisoned in reverse, and Zhang Chun crossed the Yellow River to attack Liaocheng.
Han sent General Guo Meng and the generals of Qi to attack and defeated them.
Taiwei Zhou Bo marched from Taiyuan and pacified Daidi.
When they arrived at Mayi, they failed to capture it for a while, but later they attacked it and destroyed the city.
Chen Xi's general Zhao Li defended Dongyuan, but Gaozu attacked Dongyuan but failed to capture it.
More than a month later, Zhao Li's soldiers insulted Gaozu, and Gaozu was very angry.
Dongyuan surrendered and ordered those who insulted Gaozu to be beheaded and executed. Those who did not insult Gaozu were spared.
So he set aside the area north of Changshan in Zhao State, named his son Liu Heng the acting king, and established Jinyang as the capital.
In the spring, Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, rebelled against Guanzhong and executed three of Han Xin's clans.
In the summer, Liang Wang Peng Yue rebelled, abolished his title, and moved to Shu.
He wanted to rebel again, so he executed three of his clansmen. His son Liu Hui was named King of Liang, and his son Liu You was named King of Huaiyang.
In autumn and July, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and annexed the land of Liu Jia, King of Jing, to the east, and crossed the Huai River to the north. Liu Jiao, King of Chu, fled to Xue County.
Emperor Gaozu personally went to attack him and named his son Liu Chang the King of Huainan.
In October of the twelfth year, Emperor Gaozu defeated Yingbu's army in Huizhen, and Yingbu fled. Gaozu ordered other generals to pursue him.
Emperor Gaozu led his army back, passed by Peixian County, and stopped.
A banquet was held in Peigong, and all the friends, fathers and children from the past were called together to have a feast. Selecting Peizhong children, one hundred and twenty were obtained and taught them to sing.
After drinking to his heart's content, Emperor Gaozu was building a building, composed a poem by himself, and sang: The strong wind is blowing, the clouds are flying, the sea is full of power, we are returning to our hometown, and the warriors are safe and guarding the four directions!
Let the children learn to sing along.
Emperor Gaozu danced again, feeling sad and tearful, and said to his father and brothers in Peixian County: People who travel far away miss their hometown.
Although I have established my capital in Guanzhong, my soul will still miss Sipei County for thousands of years to come.
I started as Pei Gong, punished violence and rebelled, and finally conquered the world. I regard Peixian County as my Tangmuyi, exempting the people of Peixian County from corvee service, and they will not have to do corvee service for generations to come.
The fathers, brothers, elders, women, and old friends in Peixian County drank and drank happily every day, talking about old ways and making fun of themselves.
After more than ten days, Gaozu wanted to leave, but the elders and brothers in Peixian County insisted on keeping Gaozu.
Emperor Gaozu said: I have so many followers that my father and brothers cannot afford to support them.
So Gaozu set out.
The people of Peixian County came out in large numbers and went to the west of the city to contribute cattle and wine.
Emperor Gaozu stayed again, pitched a tent, and feasted for three days.
The fathers and brothers of Pei County all kowtowed and asked, "Pei County is fortunate enough to be exempted from the corvee, but Fengyi has not yet been exempted from the corvee. Please show mercy to Fengyi."
Emperor Gaozu said: Fengyi is the place where I grew up, and I will never forget it. I only went to help the Wei state because Fengyi rebelled against me because of Yong Chi. The fathers and brothers of Peixian County insisted on their request, and then they exempted Fengyi from the corvee. Like Peixian County, they made Peihou Liu Bi the king of Wu.
The generals of the Han army pursued Yingbu's army on both the north and south sides of the Taoshui River. They defeated Yingbu's army and captured and killed Yingbu in Poyang.
Fan Kuai led another army to pacify Daidi and killed Chen Xi in the city.
In November, Emperor Gaozu returned to Chang'an from the army that conquered Yingbu.
In December, Emperor Gaozu said: The First Emperor of Qin, King Chen She of Chu Yin, King Anli of Wei, King Qi Min, and King Zhao Daoxiang all died without heirs, and were given to ten families to guard their tombs, twenty families of Qin Shihuang, and five families of Wei Gongzi Wuji.
All local officials and people who were coerced by Chen Xi and Zhao Li were pardoned.
When Chen Xi's surrendered generals said that Chen Xi was rebelling, King Lu Wan of Yan sent people to Chen Xi to participate in the conspiracy.
Emperor Gaozu sent Marquis Piyang to pick up Lu Wan, but Lu Wan refused to come because he was ill.
Marquis Piyang came back and explained in detail that there were signs of Lu Wan's rebellion.
In February, Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo were sent to lead an army to attack Lu Wan, King of Yan. Pardon the officials and people of Yan who participated in the rebellion.
The prince Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan.
When Emperor Gaozu attacked Yingbu, he was shot by a stray arrow and fell ill during the march.
The condition was serious, so Empress Lu invited a good doctor. The doctor went in to see Gaozu. Gaozu asked the doctor. The doctor said: The disease can be cured.
So Emperor Gaozu scolded the doctor and said: I conquered the world as a commoner with a three-foot sword. Isn't this destiny?
Destiny is in the sky, even if there is a Bian Que, what's the use!
Emperor Gaozu refused to let the doctor cure the disease, rewarded him with fifty pounds of gold, and told him to leave.
Soon Empress Lu asked Gaozu: If your Majesty, Xiao Xiangguo, dies in a hundred years, who will succeed him?
Emperor Gaozu said: Cao Shen can do it.
When asked about the next step, Emperor Gaozu said: "The royal tomb is fine."
However, Wang Ling is a bit naive and Chen Ping can help him.
Chen Ping is very wise, but it is difficult for him to act alone.
Zhou Bo is steady and kind, but lacks literary talents, but the one who can stabilize the Liu family must be Zhou Bo, and he can be made a Taiwei.
Empress Lu asked the next question, and Gaozu said: This is not something I will be able to know in the future.
Lu Huo and thousands of cavalry stayed at the frontier and waited, hoping that Gaozu would recover from his illness and go to apologize to Gaozu himself.
On the first day of the fourth month, Emperor Gaozu died in Changle Palace.
After four days there was no mourning.
Empress Lu discussed with Shen Shiqi and said: The generals and the emperor are both common people with registered households. Now they are vassals in the north. They are often unhappy because of this. Now they serve the young emperor. If these people are not wiped out by the entire clan, the world will not be stable.
Someone heard the news and told General Li.
General Li went to see Shen Shiqi and said, "I heard that the emperor has passed away and there has been no mourning for four days. I want to kill the generals."
If this is the case, the world will be in danger.
Chen Ping and Guan Ying commanded 100,000 soldiers to garrison Xingyang, and Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo commanded 200,000 soldiers to pacify Yan and Dai. When they heard that the emperor had died and all the generals had been killed, they must have returned with their troops to attack Guanzhong.
The ministers are rebelling within, and the princes are rebelling outside, and the world is ready to be destroyed.
Shen Shiqi went to the palace and told Empress Lu these words, and then in Ding Wei a funeral was held and a general amnesty was granted to the world.
When Lu Wan heard that Emperor Gaozu had passed away, he fled to the Huns.
Bingyin buried Gaozu.
I have already established the prince as emperor and came to the Taishang Temple.
All the ministers said: Gaozu started from a humble common people, brought order to the chaos, and brought peace to the world. He was the founder of the Han Dynasty and had the highest merit.
His title is Emperor Gao.
The prince assumed the title of emperor, and this was Emperor Xiaohui.
Order all counties and princes of various countries to build Gaozu temples and offer sacrifices according to the seasons of the year.
In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, Emperor Xiaohui thought that Emperor Gaozu missed Peixian County, so he made Peigong the original temple of Emperor Gaozu.
The one hundred and twenty singing children taught by Emperor Gaozu were all appointed as music performers in Emperor Gaozu's original temple. If there were any vacancies in the future, they would be filled immediately.
Emperor Gao had eight sons: the eldest son was King Fei of Qi Yaohui who was a concubine; the second was Emperor Xiaohui, born to Empress Lu; the third was King Ruyi of Zhao Yin who was born to Mrs. Qi; the third was Wang Heng of Dai, who was established as Emperor Xiaowen and was born to Empress Dowager Bo; the third was Wanghui of Liang, who was renamed King Zhao Bing when Empress Dowager Lu was the one; the third was Wang You of Huaiyang, who was renamed King Zhao You when Empress Lu was the Empress; the third was Prince Li of Huainan; the third was King Jian of Yan.
Tai Shigong said: The politics of the Xia Dynasty were simple and kind. The disadvantage of simplicity and kindness was that it made the people rough and less polite, so the people of the Yin Dynasty succeeded it with respect and dignity.
The disadvantage of being respectful and paying attention to dignity is that it makes the common people believe in ghosts and gods, so the people of the Zhou Dynasty replaced it with paying attention to hierarchy.
The disadvantage of paying attention to hierarchy is that it prevents the common people from treating each other with sincerity, and there is no better way to remedy the inability to treat each other with sincerity than to govern with simplicity and kindness.
The rules of governance of the kings of Xia, Shang and Zhou Dynasties seemed to go back and forth in cycles, ending over and over again.
It can be said that between the Zhou Dynasty and the Qin Dynasty, the shortcomings of paying attention to hierarchy were exposed.
Isn't it absurd that Qin Shihuang Ying Zheng did not change the situation, but instead made the punishment cruel?
Therefore, the rise of the Han Dynasty, facing the ills of the past, changed the rules of governance so that the people would not be tired and get the laws of heaven.
The carriage uniforms were customized. The emperor's carriage was covered with yellow silk lining, and a feather-made pillar was erected on the left side of the carriage scale.
Emperor Gaozu was buried in Changling.
summary:
Emperor Gaozu, born Liu Ji in Peixian County, was the son of Taigong and Liu Yu. His mother became pregnant after dreaming of meeting a god while resting by a lake, during which a dragon appeared on her body. Gaozu possessed distinctive physical features including a high nose, dragon-like forehead, beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left leg. He was generous, charitable, and broad-minded, with lofty ambitions that set him apart from ordinary people.

As an adult, Gaozu served as the chief of Sishui Pavilion, where he became familiar with local officials and enjoyed drinking and women. He frequently borrowed wine from local establishments, where shopkeepers observed a dragon above him when he was drunk. During a corvée trip to Xianyang, he saw Qin Shihuang and expressed his desire to achieve similar greatness. Lu Gong, impressed by Gaozu's appearance at a gathering, married his daughter to him despite his wife's objections. This daughter became Empress Lu, mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

While serving as pavilion chief, Gaozu encountered an old man who predicted that Empress Lu and their children would become noble, and that Gaozu's own appearance was beyond description. When escorting servants to Mount Li, many fled, so Gaozu released the remaining servants and became a fugitive. Drunk one night, he killed a large snake blocking his path. An old woman later claimed the snake was the son of the White Emperor, killed by the son of the Red Emperor, which made Gaozu secretly proud and increased his followers' awe of him.

During the Qin II period, Chen Sheng's rebellion inspired the magistrate of Peixian County to consider revolt. Following advice from Xiao He and Cao Shen, Fan Kuai was sent to summon Liu Ji. After the magistrate reneged, the elders killed him and welcomed Liu Ji, who became Duke of Pei after initially declining. They raised two to three thousand soldiers, attacked nearby areas, and returned to defend Fengyi. When Yong Chi betrayed Pei Gong by surrendering to Wei, Pei Gong failed to recapture Fengyi and sought help from Xiang Liang, who provided additional troops.

Pei Gong joined forces with Xiang Yu, and together they achieved military successes while suffering setbacks. After Xiang Liang's death, King Huai of Chu appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang County and ordered him to march west into Guanzhong, promising kingship to whoever entered first. Despite Xiang Yu's desire to join, King Huai's advisors favored Pei Gong's reputation as a tolerant elder. Pei Gong collected scattered troops, defeated Qin forces, and through strategic decisions including sparing the governor of Nanyang County, gained widespread surrenders.

Pei Gong's army arrived at Bashang in October of the first Han year, where the King of Qin surrendered. After initially wanting to rest in the palace, Pei Gong heeded advice to seal the treasures and return to camp. He established the three-chapter law code, abolished harsh Qin laws, and won the people's support by refusing their offerings. When Xiang Yu's forces approached, Pei Gong's subordinate Cao Wushang informed Xiang Yu of his intentions, but Xiang Bo's intervention and Pei Gong's apology at Hongmen prevented conflict.

Xiang Yu later broke the agreement, making Pei Gong King of Han in Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong. The King of Han used Han Xin's strategy to march eastward, attacking and defeating King Yong Zhanghan. Over subsequent years, the Han and Chu forces engaged in prolonged warfare with shifting fortunes. The King of Han survived assassination attempts, built alliances, and eventually defeated Xiang Yu at Gaixia, where Xiang Yu's forces heard Chu songs and were routed.

After establishing the Han Dynasty, Gaozu faced rebellions from various kings including Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Yingbu. He personally led campaigns against them, executing or defeating the rebels. During a visit to his hometown Peixian County, Gaozu composed the famous Song of the Great Wind and exempted the county from corvée service. He died from an arrow wound sustained during the campaign against Yingbu, refusing medical treatment by declaring his fate determined by heaven. Before death, he designated successors for key positions, including Cao Shen, Wang Ling, Chen Ping, and Zhou Bo. Gaozu was buried in Changling with the posthumous title Emperor Gao, having established the Han Dynasty from humble beginnings.

translation:
"Kingdom" says: The east is called barbarians.
Yi means root, which means that God is benevolent and cherishes all living beings, and all things grow out of the ground against the soil.
Therefore, people in the East are docile by nature and can be easily controlled by morality, so that a country of gentlemen and a country of immortality appeared.
The Yi are divided into nine branches, they are the Yi, Yu, Fang, Huang, Bai, Chi, Xuan, Feng and Yang.
So Confucius wanted to live in the Jiuyi area.
In the past, Yao ordered Xizhong to live in Woyi. There was a place called Yanggu, where the sun rose.
Emperor Taikang of the Xia Dynasty lost his virtue and the Yi people began to rebel.
Since Shaokang, the Yi people have admired the teachings of the imperial court for generations, so they submitted themselves to the emperor and presented their music and dance.
Jie's rule was brutal, and barbarians from various tribes invaded the interior. Chengtang of the Yin Dynasty changed the destiny, attacked and pacified Xia.
By the time of Zhongding, Lan Yi invaded the interior.
In the more than three hundred years since then, the Yi people sometimes surrendered and sometimes rebelled.
When Wu Yi declined, Dongyi gradually became stronger and stronger, so they moved to the Huaihe River and Mount Tai areas respectively, and gradually lived in the Central Plains.
When King Wu of Zhou destroyed Zhou, Sushen came to contribute arrowheads made of stone and arrows made of wood.
Guan Shu and Cai Shu betrayed the Zhou court, so they recruited and seduced the Yi Di. Zhou Gong conquered Guan Shu and Cai Shu and finally pacified Shu Yi.
During the reign of King Kang of Zhou, Sushen came again.
Later, Xu Yi usurped the title of emperor and led the nine barbarians to attack Zongzhou and attack westward to the bank of the Yellow River.
King Mu of Zhou was afraid that Xu Yi would be strong, so he separated the princes in the east and asked King Xu Yan to rule them.
King Xu Yan lived in Shumian, Huangchi. The land was five hundred miles in circumference. King Yan promoted benevolence and righteousness, and thirty-six countries came to worship him from all over the land.
King Zhou Mu later got the horses Chiji and Quer, so he sent Zaofu to ride the horses to inform the Chu State and order the Chu State to attack the Xu State. They arrived in one day.
So King Wen of Chu raised a large number of troops to attack Xu State and destroyed Xu State.
King Xu Yan was kind but ignorant of political skills and could not bear to let his countrymen fight, so he failed.
King Xu Yan was finally defeated at the foot of Shushan Mountain in Wuyuan County, Pengcheng City. Tens of thousands of people followed him, so Shushan Mountain was called Xushan Mountain.
King Zhou Li was cruel and unruly, and Huaiyi invaded. The emperor sent Guo Zhong to attack Huaiyi, but failed to win. King Xuan of Zhou ordered Duke Zhao to go and conquer Huaiyi, and pacified Huaiyi.
When King You of Zhou became debauched and violent, the barbarians from all sides invaded alternately. It was not until Duke Huan of Qi established his hegemony that he repelled the barbarians.
When King Chu Ling was applying for an alliance, Huaiyi also came to participate in the alliance.
Later, the Yue Kingdom moved to Langye and fought with the Huaiyi. From then on, they invaded and harmed all the countries in the Central Plains and invaded and destroyed small countries.
Qin State annexed the six countries, and Huaiyi and Siyi were scattered into ordinary people's houses.
Chen She raised an army and the world collapsed. Weiman, a native of Yan State, took refuge in North Korea and thus ruled North Korea.
More than a hundred years later, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty destroyed North Korea, and since then the Yicai have been banned from visiting Kyoto.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, the Qi people invaded the border. In the early years of Jianwu, the Qi people came to pay tribute again.
At that time, the Liaodong governor's sacrifice to Xu was very powerful in the north, and his reputation was very high overseas. So Jia, Qi, Wa, and Han came to the court from thousands of miles away to contribute. Therefore, after Emperor Zhang and Emperor He, envoys communicated with each other.

summary:
The historical and cultural evolution of the Eastern Yi peoples, beginning with their origins and characteristics. The Yi, meaning "root," were considered docile and easily governed by morality, leading to the emergence of a "country of gentlemen" and a "country of immortality." They were divided into nine branches, and Confucius once expressed a desire to live among them. Early interactions with Chinese dynasties included Yao sending Xizhong to Woyi and the Yi submitting to Xia rulers, though rebellions occurred under tyrants like Jie. Over centuries, the Yi fluctuated between submission and revolt, with notable events such as Xu Yi usurping the title of emperor and attacking Zongzhou, only to be defeated by King Wen of Chu. Later, during the Zhou and Han dynasties, the Yi peoples, including Huaiyi and Siyi, were scattered, conquered, or assimilated, with periods of tribute and conflict under rulers like Wang Mang and Emperor Wu of Han.

The text then details specific Yi groups, starting with Fuyu, located north of Xuantu. Fuyu was a flat, fertile land producing horses, jade, and mink. Its people were strong, brave, and kind, using bows and swords, and practicing rituals like the "Yinggu" festival. They had severe punishments, including execution for adultery and theft, and practiced levirate marriage. Burial customs involved jade boxes for kings, provided by the Han court. Fuyu engaged in tribute and conflict with Han, including invasions under King An and later defeats by Gongsunyu.

Yilou, northeast of Fuyu, was a mountainous, cold region where people lived in caves and wore pigskin. They were brave archers using poisoned arrows and were known for plundering. Gaoguli, south of Fuyu, had five tribes and a history of conflict with Han, including invasions and tribute missions. Their customs included sacrifices to heaven, singing and dancing, and severe punishments. Woju, near Gaoguli, was fertile and known for farming and foot combat. Their burial practices involved large wooden coffins and bone collection.

Korea, originally granted to Jizi by King Wu of Zhou, had a culture of etiquette and prohibitions. Over time, it was influenced by Chinese refugees and eventually conquered by Emperor Wu of Han, who established four commanderies. The text describes the three Han states: Mahan, Chenhan, and Benchen, each with distinct customs, including farming, iron trade, and rituals. Japan, southeast of Korea, comprised over a hundred island states, with Yamatai as the leading kingdom. Japanese customs included tattooing, polygamy, and divination. The text concludes with a reflection on Jizi's influence on Korean customs and the gradual decline of these traditions due to Chinese contact.

Wuhuan was originally from the Donghu tribe.
In the early Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu Maodun eliminated Donghu, and the remaining people guarded Wuhuan Mountain, so they took Wuhuan as their tribal title.
The custom of Wuhuan is to be good at horseback riding and archery. Wuhuan people are mainly engaged in hunting birds and animals.
The Wuhuan people graze on water and grass and have no fixed residence.
They used felt tents as houses, with doors opening eastward toward the sun.
They ate meat, drank cheese, and made clothes from the hairs of birds and animals.
They attach great importance to young people and despise the elderly. They have a strong temperament and are not open-minded.
When he gets angry, he kills his father and brothers, but never kills his mother, because her mother has her own tribe and her father and brothers have no one to take revenge.
Anyone who is brave and strong and can handle decisive battles and lawsuits is elected as the leader of the tribe. The leader is not inherited from generation to generation.
Each town has its own small leader, and hundreds or thousands of towns form a tribe.
When the tribal leader called for something, he would carve wood as a talisman. Although there was no writing, the tribesmen did not dare to violate it.
The Wuhuan people do not have a fixed surname, and the surname is the name of the strong leader.
From the leader down, people herd livestock and run their own industries, and they did not rely on each other.
In terms of marriage, they first rob the woman and live together, sometimes for half a year or hundreds of days, and then give the woman cattle, horses, sheep and other livestock as betrothal gifts.
When a son-in-law follows his wife back to his parents' home, he pays homage to the people in his wife's family every day, regardless of his superiority or inferiority, but does not pay homage to his wife's parents.
After working as a servant in his wife's house for a year or two, his wife's house gave them many things to send their daughter away, and all daily necessities and belongings were prepared for them.
The custom of the Wuhuan people is to marry their stepmother and have an affair with their widowed sister-in-law. However, after their death, the stepmother and sister-in-law are buried together with their original husbands.
In terms of strategy, they listen to women's opinions, and only make their own decisions when fighting.
Father and son, men and women sit face to face.
They think it is easy to shave off their hair.
Women only grow their hair when they get married, and it is separated and coiled on both sides of the head. The headdress is made of Jujue, which is decorated with gold and jade, just like the Gebuyao in the Central Plains.
Women could embroider leather and weave woolen fabrics.
Men can make bows and arrows, saddles and harnesses, and smelt copper and iron to make weapons.
The boring land is suitable for planting Biaozi and Aunt.
The bunches are like fluffy grass, and the fruits are like rice. They will mature in ten months.
When the Wuhuan people saw the flying black beasts being pregnant and giving birth, they used this to distinguish the four seasons.
Wuhuan's custom is to respect death in battle. They use coffins to collect corpses and have mourning and crying rituals, but when they are buried, they send them off with singing and dancing.
They kept a fat dog and led it with a colorful rope. They also took the horse and clothes and belongings of the deceased and burned them with fire to send the deceased away. This meant that they entrusted the dog to escort the soul of the deceased back to Chishan.
Chishan is thousands of miles away in the northwest direction of Liaodong, just like the souls of people in the Central Plains return to Mount Tai after death.
They respected the gods and ghosts and offered sacrifices to the heaven and earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains and rivers, and those who had a strong reputation among their ancestors.
They sacrificed cattle and sheep, and burned them all to death after the sacrifice.
The Wuhuan people stipulate that those who disobey the tribal leader shall be punished with death; if those who invade and kill each other, let the tribes themselves avenge each other. If the revenge is endless, report to the tribal leader and let the enemy bring horses, cattle, and sheep to redeem his life;
There are many vipers in Wuhuan, located southwest of Dingling and northeast of Wusun.
Since Wuhuan was defeated by Maodun, his tribe has been lonely and weak. They often surrender to the Xiongnu. They send cattle, horses, and sheep skins every year. If they are not ready after the deadline, their wives and children are often captured.
When Emperor Wu sent Hussar General Huo Qubing to attack the left area of ​​the Xiongnu, he moved the Wuhuan people outside the fortress in the five counties of Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi and Liaodong to spy on the Xiongnu's movements for the Han Dynasty.
The leaders of the Wuhuan tribe paid homage to the emperor once a year. At this time, they began to set up Wuhuan captains with a salary of two thousand dan. They held the emperor's talisman to supervise Wuhuan and prevent Wuhuan from interacting with the Xiongnu.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, Wuhuan gradually became stronger and stronger, so he dug up the tomb of the Xiongnu Chanyu in order to avenge his hatred of Maodun.
The Huns were furious and went east to defeat Wuhuan.
After General Huo Guang learned about it, he sent General Fan Mingyou of Liao to lead 20,000 cavalry from Liaodong to intercept the Huns, but the enemy captives had already retreated.
Taking advantage of the fact that Wuhuan had just been defeated, Fan Mingyou attacked Wuhuan, killed more than 6,000 Wuhuan people, and returned with the heads of three princes in Dandan.
From then on, Gu Huan attacked Sister Hu again, but was always defeated by Ming You.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, the Wuhuan people gradually surrendered and guarded the border.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Wang Mang wanted to attack the Xiongnu and mobilized twelve troops. He sent Shuyu general Yan You to command Wuhuan and Ding Ling's troops to garrison Daijun, leaving all their wives and children as hostages in the county.
The Wuhuan people were dissatisfied with the local conditions and feared that the long-term garrison would be endless, so they repeatedly asked to be allowed to leave.
Wang Mang refused to let them go, so the Wuhuan people fled and rebelled, and in turn looted their property. Each county killed all Wuhuan's hostages, and Wuhuan and Wang Mang forged a hatred.
The Xiongnu took the opportunity to lure Wuhuan chieftains to serve as officials and win over others to join them.
In the early days of Guangwu, Wuhuan and the Xiongnu jointly sent troops to invade the border, and the areas bounded by Daijun suffered particularly serious damage.
The Wuhuan people live close to the border. They set out from their felt tents in the morning and arrived at the city at dusk. Every household in the five counties was harmed. Counties were destroyed and people were displaced.
Wuhuan in Baishan, outside the Shanggu border fortress, was the most powerful and wealthy.
In the 21st year of Jianwu's reign, the imperial court sent Fubo General Ma Yuan to lead 3,000 cavalry from Wuruan Pass to attack Wuhuan.
Wuhuan learned the news in advance and all fled one after another. Ma Yuan chased them and killed more than a hundred Wuhuan people and returned to the army.
The Wuhuan people followed Ma Yuan to attack again, but Ma Yuan fled back day and night. By the time he entered the border fortress, more than a thousand horses were dead.
In the 22nd year, the Xiongnu were in civil unrest. Wuhuan took advantage of the Xiongnu's weakness and defeated the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu moved thousands of miles north, and the area south of the desert was completely empty. The emperor bribed Wuhuan with money and cloth.
In the twenty-fifth year, Hao Dan, the leader of Wuhuan in western Liaoning, and other 922 people led his tribe to Fumo and went to the court to pay tribute, offering slaves, cattle and horses, bows and arrows, and the skins of tigers, leopards, and minks.
When he was sent, ethnic minorities from all over came to worship and celebrate in an endless stream. The emperor ordered a grand banquet to be held to express condolences to them and reward them with treasures.
Some Wuhuan people were willing to stay as guards, so the emperor named eighty-one Wuhuan leaders as princes and commanders, letting them live in the fortress and distribute them in the border counties. He asked them to recruit people from their own tribes and provide them with clothing and food. The Wuhuan people then scouted for enemy movements for the Han and helped Mo attack the Xiongnu and Xianbei.
At that time, Situ Peng Ban Biao reported: The Wuhuan people are naturally frivolous and cunning, and like to be bandits. If they are indulged for a long time without anyone to supervise them to surrender and gather, they will definitely invade and plunder the people living there. I am afraid that I will not be able to control them if they are only given to the subordinates who accept the surrender.
I foolishly thought that it would be best to re-establish the Wuhuan captain, which would indeed be beneficial to the Wuhuan people's surrender and gathering, and reduce the country's worries about the border.
The emperor accepted this suggestion. So in Micheng in Shanggu, Wuhuan captains were established again, a military general's office was opened, and Xianbei was also commanded. He also rewarded the sons of the Wuhuan people who were held hostage, and traded with them all year round.
By the time of Emperor Ming, Emperor Zhang, and Emperor He, the Wuhuan people were guarding the frontier and nothing happened.
In the summer of the third year of Emperor An's reign, more than a thousand Wuhuan people from Yuyang and Hu people from Youbeiping invaded Daijun and Shanggu.
In the autumn of this year, Wuhuan of Yanmen led the king Wuhe, together with the Xianbei leader Qiulun and others, and the Guduhou of the Southern Xiongnu, with more than 7,000 cavalry, they invaded Wuyuan and fought with the Wuyuan prefect at Gaoqu Valley in Jiuyuan. The Han army was defeated and the county officials were killed.
The imperial court then sent the cavalry general He Xi, the Liao general Liang Dong and others to attack Wuhe, and they were defeated.
There was no need to beg for surrender, and the Xianbei people fled back beyond the frontier fortress.
From then on, the Wuhuan people gradually became closer to the Han, and the imperial court granted the Wuhuan tribal leader Rong Zhumo the title of pro-Han captaincy.
In the winter of the fourth year of Emperor Shun's reign in Yangjia, Wuhuan invaded Yunzhong and intercepted more than a thousand ox-carts of merchants on the road. Geng Ye, the general of Liao Dynasty, led more than 2,000 people to pursue the Wuhuan people. The battle was unfavorable, and they fought again in Shanan, killing 500 people.
The Wuhuan people then surrounded Geng Ye in Lanchi City. The imperial court then mobilized 2,000 trace-seeking soldiers and 1,000 soldiers from the Duliao camp to cooperate with the garrison in Shangjun to conquer Wuhuan, and the Wuhuan people retreated.
In the fifth year of Yonghe, Wuhuan's tribal leaders Ajian, Qiangqu and others and Julongwusi from the left of the southern Xiongnu rebelled. Zhang Dan, the central general, defeated and killed them, and the rest all surrendered.
During the Yongshou period of Emperor Huan, the Wuhuan people in Shuofang rebelled with Xiuzhu Tuge. Zhonglang attacked Zhang Huan and pacified the enemy.
In the summer of the ninth year of Yanxi, Wuhuan, together with Xianbei and the Southern Xiongnu, invaded nine counties along the border. They rebelled at the same time. Zhang Huan conquered the enemy, and they all left the border fortress.
In the early years of Emperor Ling, there was a tribal leader named Nanlou in Shanggu, who had more than 9,000 tribes of tribes, and there was a leader named Qiu Liju in western Liaoning, with more than 5,000 tribes of tribes, and they all called themselves kings. In addition, Su Puyan in Liaodong had more than a thousand tribes and called himself King Qiao; Wuyan in Youbeiping had more than 800 tribes and called himself King Hanlu: they were both brave and strong and had many strategies.
In the fourth year of Chongchuo, the governor of Protozoa Mountain rebelled. He joined Qiu Liju's tribe and proclaimed himself King Mitian Anding. He then became the marshal of the Wuhuan people in each county and invaded and plundered the four prefectures of Qingzhou, Xuzhou, Youzhou and Jizhou.
In the fifth year, the imperial court appointed Liu Yu as the shepherd of Youzhou. Liu Yu offered a reward for recruiting people to cut off Zhang Chun's head, and the northern states were pacified.
During the Chuping reign of Emperor Xian, Qiu Liju died. His son Lou Ban was young, and his nephew Tadun, who knew how to use troops and had strategies, succeeded Lou Ban and took charge of the Wuhuan people in three counties. All the people obeyed his orders.
In the early years of Jian'an, Yuan Shao, the shepherd of Jizhou, was at loggerheads with former general Gongsun Zan. Tadun sent an envoy to Yuan Shao to request peace, and then sent troops to help Yuan Shao attack Gongsun Zan and defeated Gongsun Zan.
In the name of the imperial court, Yuan Shao granted Tadun, Nanlou, Su Puyan, Wuyan and others the Chanyu seal and ribbon.
Later, Nanlou and Su Puyan led their troops to support Louban as Chanyu and Tadun as king, but Tadun was still responsible for making suggestions.
Yan Rou from Guangyang was trapped in Wuhuan and Xianbei since childhood, and was attached and trusted by the Wuhuan and Xianbei people. Yan Rou then used the Xianbei tribe to kill Wuhuan captain Xing Ju and replace him.
Yuan Shao favored Yan Rou and comforted her, so as to stabilize the northern border.
When Yuan Shao's son Yuan Shang failed, he defected to Tadun.

Catching up with Cao Cao to pacify the north of the Yellow River, Yan Rou led the Xianbei and Wuhuan people to surrender, and Cao Cao immediately appointed Yan Rou as the school captain.

Yuan Shangyu, Lou Ban, Wu Yan and others all fled to Liaodong. Gongsun Kang, the governor of Liaodong, killed them all and gave their heads to Cao Cao.
The remaining more than 10,000 cities and towns were all moved to the Central Plains.
Xianbei is also a branch of Donghu. The Xianbei people also rely on Xianbei Mountain, so they use this as their clan name.
The language and customs of the Xianbei people are the same as those of Wuhuan.
Only when they get married, they shave their heads first and meet in large numbers by the Raole River in the last month of spring. After eating and drinking, they have sex.
The birds and animals there are different from those in the Central Plains. There are wild horses, salamanders, and horned oxen. Bows can be made from the horns of these cows, which are called horn-end bows among the people.

In the early Han Dynasty, Xianbei was also defeated by Maodun and fled far away to the frontier fortress in Liaodong, adjacent to Wuhuan, but had no contact with the Han.
In the early years of Chesi, Yu maggot was so powerful that he led Panbei and Guhuan to invade and plunder the northern border, killing and plundering officials and people. There is no peace for a year.

Why did he send troops to attack the enemy in the north year after year? When he returned, he always took the enemy's head and went to Liaodong to receive rewards.
Thirty years ago, Xianbei tribe leaders Yu Qiuzui, Mantou and others led their tribes to the capital to worship and celebrate. They admired the virtues of the Han Dynasty and submitted to the imperial court.
The emperor made Qiuben king and Mantou a marquis.

During the Ming and Zhang dynasties, the Xianbei people guarded the border and nothing happened.
During the reign of Emperor Yongyuan, the general Dou Xian sent the right commander Geng Kui to defeat the Huns, and the Northern Chanyu fled. The Xianbei people therefore moved and occupied the territory where the Huns lived.

In the ninth year, the Xianbei people from Liaodong attacked Feiru County. The prefect Ji Shen was defeated and convicted, and died in prison.
In the thirteenth year, the Xianbei people from Liaodong invaded Youbeiping, and then entered Yuyang, but were defeated by the Yuyang prefect.

Yan Shuo, a trooper and horseman, dissuaded him and said: "The road ahead is difficult and blocked, and the enemy's strength is difficult to estimate. Zhang Xian's spirit was very strong. He was very angry and wanted to kill Yan Shou.

Empress Dowager Deng issued a policy letter praising Zhang Xian and others, and rewarded Zhang Xian's family with 600,000 yuan, and appointed two members of his family as Langs; Yan Shuo, Wei Fu, and Xu Xian were each rewarded with 100,000 Yuan, and each family appointed a son as Lang.
During the Yongchu period of Emperor An, Yan Liyang, the leader of the Xianbei tribe, went to the court to pay homage and celebrate. One hundred and twenty tribes in Xianbei each sent people to serve as hostages.

In winter, Xianbei entered Shanggu and attacked Juyongguan. The imperial court once again mobilized troops from border counties, soldiers from Liyang Camp, soldiers who hunted for traces, infantry and cavalry, a total of 20,000 people, to guard various key places.
In the autumn of the sixth year, the Xianbei troops entered the Macheng border fortress and killed county officials. He and Zhonglang General Ma Xu led the army of Nan Shanyu to join forces with troops from western Liaoning and Youbeiping. They went out of the border fortress to pursue the Xianbei people. They defeated Xianbei and gained a lot of people, cattle, sheep, and property.
The imperial court also recruited 3,000 soldiers who were searching for traces and 3,000 horses, and sent them to the military camp of General Du Liao to garrison.
In the first year of Yongning, the leaders of the Xianbei tribe in western Liaoning, Wu Lun and Qizhi Tar, led their tribes to surrender to Deng Zun and offer tribute.
The emperor issued a letter from Shao and granted Ulun the title of king and the princes of Tartar. They were rewarded with different amounts of colorful silks.

The Xianbei troops therefore surrounded Xu Chang, the Wuhuan captain in Macheng.
Geng Kui, the general of the Liao Dynasty, and Pang Shen, the governor of Youzhou, mobilized soldiers from Guangyang, Yuyang, and Zhuojun to rescue in two ways. Since Yuli killed the governor many times, his courage and determination became stronger, and he had tens of thousands of cavalry capable of fighting.
In the winter of the first year of Yanguang, Xianbei invaded Yanmen and Dingxiang, and then attacked Taiyuan, looting and killing people.
In the winter of the second year, he went to Tartar and personally led more than 10,000 cavalry into the border post of the Eastern Territory. The troops were divided into several groups and attacked the Southern Xiongnu in Manbai. During the battle, the king died in the battle, and more than 1,000 people were killed.
In the autumn of the third year, he went to Tartar and invaded Gaoliu, defeated the Southern Xiongnu and killed King Jianjiang.
In the autumn of the first year of Yongjian reign of Emperor Shun, Xianbei Qizhi Tartar invaded Dai County, and the prefect Li Chao died in the battle.
In the spring of the next year, Zhonglang sent Zhang Guo to lead Nan Shanyu's more than 10,000 infantry and cavalry out of the frontier, defeated them to the Tartars, and obtained more than 2,000 kinds of baggage from them.

Wuhuan captain Geng Ye mobilized troops from the border counties and Wuhuan led the kings out of the border fortress to attack Xianbei, killing hundreds of people and obtaining a large number of people, cattle, horses and various utensils. In the third and fourth years of Yongjian, the Xianbei people invaded Yuyang and Shuofang many times.
In the autumn of the sixth year, Geng Ye sent Sima to lead thousands of Hu soldiers to the frontier fortress and defeated the Xianbei people.
In winter, the governor of Yuyang sent Wuhuan troops to attack Xianbei, killing 800 people and gaining cattle, horses and people.
Wuhuan's hero Fu Shuguan was brave and strong. Every time he fought against Xianbei, he always went deep into the enemy's formation. The emperor issued an edict and gave him the title of "leading all the kings".
In the winter of the first year of Yangjia, Geng Ye sent Wuhuan's close desert captain Rong Zhumo and Duogui and other princes to go out to the frontier to outflank and attack Xianbei. He killed many enemies and got a lot of things back. Xianbei later invaded the vassal state of Liaodong, so Geng Ye moved the garrison to Wulu City in Liaodong to resist Xianbei.
In the spring of the second year, the Xiongnu Zhonglang general Zhao Chou led Fu Shen, the Marquis of the Bone Capital of the Southern Huns, and others to go out to the frontier to attack Xianbei. They defeated the Xianbei people and killed many Xianbei people. They obtained a lot of things. The emperor issued an edict and gave Fu Shen a golden seal, purple ribbon and various amounts of silk fabrics.
In autumn, the Xianbei people crossed the border fortress and entered Macheng. The Daijun governor attacked the Xianbei people, but failed to win.
Later, he died, and the Xianbei people's raids and invasions gradually decreased.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, there was a man named Tan Shihuai in Xianbei. His father was Touluhou. He served in the Xiongnu army for three years, and his wife gave birth to a child at home.
After returning from Tou Luhou, he felt strange and wanted to kill the child.
The wife said that she once walked in broad daylight and heard thunder. She looked up to the sky. A hailstone happened to fall into her mouth. She swallowed it and became pregnant. Ten months later, she gave birth to a child. This child must have something extraordinary, so it was best to raise him up temporarily.
Hou Lu refused to listen and threw the child away.
The wife privately told her parents' family that she wanted them to adopt her and name her Tanshihuai.
When Tan Shihuai was fourteen or fifteen years old, he was brave, strong and resourceful.
The leader of another tribe robbed his grandfather's cattle and sheep. Tan Shihuai chased them on horseback and fought them. He was invincible and chased back all the robbed cattle and horses.
From then on the people in the tribe were afraid of obeying him. So Tan Shihuai issued legal prohibitions and judged right and wrong. No one dared to violate it, and he was finally promoted as the leader of the tribe.
Tan Shihuai then established his royal court by the Geqiu River in Danhan Mountain, more than three hundred miles north of Gaoliu. Tanshihuai's men and horses are very powerful, and the tribal leaders in the east and west all submit to Tanshihuai.
Tanshihuai took this opportunity to plunder the Han border areas to the south, defended against Ding Ling in the north, repulsed Fuyu in the north, attacked Wusun in the west, and occupied all the Xiongnu's original territory. It was more than 14,000 miles long from east to west and more than 7,000 miles wide from north to south. Mountains, rivers, swamps and salt ponds were all under its jurisdiction.
In the autumn of the second year of Yongshou, Tan Shihuai led three or four thousand cavalry to invade Yunzhong.
In the first year of Yanxi, Xianbei invaded the northern border.
In winter, the imperial court sent the Xiongnu Zhonglang general Zhang Huan to lead Nandanyu out of the border to attack Xianbei and killed 200 people.
In the second year, the Xianbei people broke into Yanmen again, killed hundreds of people, and looted wantonly.
In the summer of the sixth year, more than a thousand Xianbei cavalry invaded the Liaodong vassal state.
In the summer of the ninth year, Xianbei actually dispatched tens of thousands of cavalry into the nine counties along the border, killing and plundering officials and people. So the imperial court sent Zhang Huan to attack the Xianbei invaders, and the enemies left the border fortress.
The imperial court had been worried about Xianbei for a long time, but could not stop it, so it sent an envoy with a seal and ribbon to make Tanshihuai king, hoping to make peace with him.
Tanshihuai refused to accept it, and the invasion and plunder became more and more serious.
Then Tanshihuai himself divided the territory into three parts, from Youbeiping Yishu to Liaodong, more than 20 cities connected with Fuyu and Jiaqi were the Shu part, more than 10 cities from the west of Youbeiping to Shanggu were the middle part, and more than 20 cities from the west of Shanggu to Dunhuang and Wusun were the west part, each with a leader under their jurisdiction, and they all belonged to Tanshihuai.
After Emperor Ling came to the throne, the counties along the three prefectures of Youzhou, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou were not invaded and looted by Xianbei for a year, and countless people were killed and plundered.
In the winter of the third year of Xiping's reign, when Xianbei entered Lisi, the prefect Xia Zhi led Xiuchu Tuge to pursue and defeat the Diesheng Emperor's army.
The imperial court transferred Li Yu to the post of Colonel Hu Wuhuan.
In the fifth year, Xianbei invaded Youzhou.
In the summer of the sixth year, Xianbei invaded the borders of the three states.
In autumn, Xia Yu wrote a letter saying: Xianbei has invaded the border. There have been more than thirty cases since spring. Please fine-tune the troops from various counties in Youzhou to attack Xianbei from the border. In one winter and two springs, the enemy will be able to be wiped out.
The court did not agree.
Before this, Tian Yan, the captain of the Qiang Guards, was convicted but was pardoned. He wanted to establish his effectiveness, so he asked Wang Fu, the permanent attendant, to help him become a general. Wang Fu therefore discussed sending troops to join forces with Xia Yu to conquer the enemy. The emperor then appointed Tian Yan as the general of Zhonglang who defeated Xianbei.
Many among the ministers disagreed. The emperor then summoned the ministers to discuss the matter in the court.
Yilang Cai Yong expressed his opinion: "Shangshu" warns against barbarians disturbing China, and "Book of Changes" records that Gaozong conquered the ghosts. The Zhou Dynasty sent troops to attack Jianxi and Manjing, and the Han Dynasty sent troops to Tianyan Mountain and Hanhai.
Conquering other races has a long history.
However, times have similarities and differences, situations have conditions that can and cannot be done, so plans have gains and losses, things have successes and failures, and they cannot be treated the same.
Emperor Wu had a far-reaching strategy and was determined to open up the four borders. He conquered Baiyue in the south, conquered the powerful Hu people in the north, attacked Dawan in the west, and annexed North Korea in the east.
Emperor Wu relied on the savings of Emperors Wen and Jing and the prosperity of the country. Within a few decades, the government and the people were all in poverty.
Therefore, the state implemented the exclusive interests of selling salt, cast iron and liquor, and promulgated laws to reward those who reported rich households concealing their property and to increase taxes. The common people could not bear it, so they rebelled and became thieves. The Kanto region was in turmoil and the roads were interrupted.
Zhizhi envoys wearing embroidered clothes left the capital at the same time holding the E.
Soon after the emperor came to his senses, he stopped the war, dismissed the servitude, and made the prime minister a Marquis of the Rich People.
Therefore, Zhufu Yan said: No one who thinks only about winning the war and is busy with the war will not regret it.
With King Sejong's prowess, his generals virtuous and brave, his wealth and tribute, and the vast and far-reaching lands he developed, he still felt regretful.
What's more, now that both human and financial resources are insufficient, things are far worse than before.
Since the Xiongnu escaped, Xianbei has become strong and prosperous. It has occupied the original place of the Xiongnu. It claims to have an army of 100,000, has strong financial resources, and has become more and more scheming.
In addition, border security was lax and there were many omissions in the laws and prohibitions. All the fine copper and iron were owned by the enemies; the Han people who escaped capture were their main planners. Xianbei's weapons were sharp and his horses were fast, both of which were superior to the Xiongnu.
Duan Ying used to be an excellent general. He was familiar with military affairs and good at fighting. He had fought against the Western Qiang people for more than ten years.
Now Xia Yu and Tian Yan's talents and strategies may not exceed Duan Frequency, and the Xianbei tribe is no weaker than before.
And they planned to spend two years out of thin air, thinking that they could succeed. If the armies of the two sides fought and caused disaster, how could it be stopped?
Many people must be recruited to transport things endlessly. This will exhaust the power of the Central Plains and increase the strength of the barbarians.
Disasters on the frontier are like scabies on the hands and feet; poverty in the middle plains is like sores on the chest and back.
At present, the thieves in the county cannot be stopped, let alone such enemies can be subdued?
In the past, Emperor Gaozu endured the humiliation he suffered in Pingcheng, and Empress Lu put aside the humiliation caused by the Xiongnu's contemptuous letters. Compared with now, which one is more serious?
The mountains and rivers created by heaven, the Great Wall built by the Qin Dynasty, and the border walls built by the Han Dynasty were all used to separate domestic and foreign countries and distinguish different customs.
As long as there is no disaster that would embarrass or humiliate the country, is it necessary to argue with ants and cunning enemies?
Although Xianbei is sometimes defeated, can they all be wiped out?
And now the emperor is so busy that he doesn’t even have time to eat? He who wants to win may not win, and he who is skeptical may not lose.
Everyone thinks it is dangerous, and wise people will not adopt it; where the opinions of the court are doubtful, wise monarchs will not implement them.
In the past, when Liu An, the king of Huainan, dissuaded the conquest of Yue, he said: The emperor's army only conquers but does not fight, which means that no one dares to resist.
If the people of Yue risk their lives to fight against the emperor, and those soldiers of humble origins are unprepared and return in defeat, even if they get the head of the king of Yue, I will still feel ashamed of the big man.
And if you plan to sacrifice the people in exchange for numerous enemies, and use the emperor's prestige to suffer the humiliation of foreign barbarians, even if it is as they say, it is already dangerous, not to mention that the success or failure cannot be estimated?
In the past, Zhuya County rebelled, and Xiaoyuan Huanghu adopted Zitu's opinion and issued an edict saying: Dieya rebelled. Now everyone's opinions include that some can be attacked, and some think that they should be given up.
I thought about it day and night. I felt ashamed that my authority could not be implemented, so I wanted to conquer Zhuya. I made adjustments according to the changes of the times, and I was worried about thousands of people.
Which one is more important than the hunger of the people in the world or not conquering the distant barbarians?
The sacrifices in the ancestral temple cannot be fully prepared in years of famine, let alone avoiding insults that are not hatred?
Now Guandong is very poor and cannot provide relief for them, and they are preparing to start a war. It is not just the working people.
Therefore, Zhuya County was abolished.
This is the voice of benevolence issued by Emperor Yuan.
Sympathy for the people and the urgent need for relief, even complete counties and many counties have given up, not to mention that the outside of the border has never been a place where the people live!
Li Mu was good at strategies for guarding the border; Yan You gave the key to his views on guarding the border.
The achievements they left behind are still there, and the articles are still there. According to the strategies they mentioned and the plans of the previous emperors, I think it is okay.
The emperor refused to accept it, so he sent Xia Yu to set off from Gaoliu, Tian Yan to set off from Yunzhong, and Xiongnu Zhonglang General Zang Man to lead Nandanyu to set off from Yanmen. Each of them led 10,000 cavalry and divided into three groups to go out of the frontier for more than 2,000 miles.
Tan Shihuai ordered the leaders of the three tribes to lead their troops to fight. Xia Yu and others were defeated and lost their talismans and baggage. Each of them fled back with dozens of cavalry. Seventy-eight out of ten people died.
Three generals were conscripted into prison by the imperial court in prison cars, and they used money to redeem themselves as ordinary people.
In winter, Xianbei invaded Suxi.
In the winter of the first year of Guanghe, Xianbei invaded Jiuquan again, and everyone along the border was poisoned.
The population of Xianbei was increasing day by day, and agriculture, animal husbandry, and hunting could no longer satisfy the needs of the people. Tan Shihuai inspected the area in person. He saw that the Wuhousai River was hundreds of miles wide and stagnant. There were fish in the water, but there was no way to get them.
Tan Shihuai heard that the Japanese were good at fishing with gangs, so he attacked the Japanese eastward and obtained more than a thousand Japanese. He moved them to live by the Qin River and asked them to fish to make up for the lack of food.
During the Guanghe period, Tan Shihuai died at the age of forty-five, and his son Helian inherited the position.
He Lian's ability was not as good as his father's, and he invaded and plundered the Han border many times. He Lian was greedy and dissolute by nature, and the lawsuit was unfair, and half of the people betrayed him.
Later, when he went out to attack Beidi, a man from Lian County who was good at archery hit Helian and was shot to death immediately.
Helian's son Qianman was young, and Helian's nephew Kuixi succeeded to the throne.
Later, when Huaman grew up, he competed with Yanqu for the country, and the tribe was divided and disbanded.
After the death of Huang Nu, his younger brother Bu Dugen succeeded to the throne.
Since Tanshihuai, the leaders of various tribes have been inherited from generation to generation.
The argument goes: The barbarians from all directions are violent and mutually powerful.
The Xiongnu were powerful during the Moxing period, and the Xiqiang were ferocious during the Zhongxing period.
But between Emperor Ling and Emperor Xian, Wuhuan and Xianbei were successively stronger, Tanshihuai was brave and fierce, occupying all the Shanyu's territory, and Tadun was extremely fierce, openly occupying the land in western Liaoning.
They invaded across the Central Plains, causing disasters to the people, and there was no peace in any period.
However, the superior strategies for subduing and controlling foreigners have not been heard of in the past dynasties; the strategies of the Zhou and Han dynasties are only good at middle and low strategies.
Could it be that the number of days has caused such a result?
Zan said: Wuhuan and Xianbei were watching and harming the moral integrity of our northern border court, so they were tamed; when the times were declining, they turned away.
summary:
The Wuhuan originated from the Donghu tribe. After the Xiongnu leader Maodun defeated Donghu in the early Han Dynasty, the survivors took refuge in Wuhuan Mountain and adopted the name as their tribal title. They were skilled horsemen and archers, primarily hunting birds and animals, and practiced nomadic pastoralism without fixed residences. Their felt tents faced east, and they subsisted on meat, cheese, and clothing made from animal hairs. They valued youth over the elderly, had fierce tempers, and would kill fathers and brothers in anger but never mothers, as mothers had their own tribes for revenge. Leaders were chosen based on bravery and strength, not heredity, with towns forming tribes under small leaders. They used carved wood as talismans for commands, lacked writing, and had no fixed surnames, adopting the names of strong leaders instead. Marriage involved abducting women, cohabiting for months, then paying betrothal gifts in livestock. Sons-in-law served their wives' families for one to two years before receiving dowries. They practiced levirate marriage, burying stepmothers and sisters-in-law with their original husbands. Women’s opinions were heeded in strategy, but men decided in battle. They shaved their heads, with women growing hair only after marriage, and wore headdresses decorated with gold and jade. Women embroidered leather and wove wool; men made bows, arrows, saddles, and smelted copper and iron for weapons. They cultivated crops like Biaozi and Aunt, which matured in ten months, and used the pregnancy of black beasts to distinguish seasons. They honored death in battle, used coffins, and conducted mourning rituals with singing and dancing, burning a fat dog with a colored rope along with the deceased’s possessions to guide the soul to Chishan, akin to the Central Plains’ Mount Tai. They sacrificed cattle and sheep to gods, ghosts, heaven, earth, and ancestors, burning the offerings completely. Disobedience to the leader was punishable by death; feuds could be settled with livestock. Wuhuan was located southwest of Dingling and northeast of Wusun, with many vipers.

After Maodun’s defeat, Wuhuan remained weak, often submitting to the Xiongnu and paying annual tribute. Emperor Wu moved them outside the five counties of Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong to spy on the Xiongnu. Their leaders paid homage to the emperor annually, and Wuhuan captains were established to supervise them. During Emperor Zhao’s reign, Wuhuan grew stronger, desecrated a Xiongnu chanyu’s tomb, and was attacked by the Xiongnu. General Huo Guang sent Fan Mingyou to intercept, but the Xiongnu had retreated; Fan then attacked Wuhuan, killing over 6,000. Under Emperor Xuan, Wuhuan gradually surrendered and guarded the border. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he conscripted Wuhuan troops, holding their families hostage, leading to rebellion and hatred. The Xiongnu lured Wuhuan leaders to join them. In the early Guangwu period, Wuhuan and Xiongnu jointly invaded, devastating border counties. In the 21st year of Jianwu, Ma Yuan attacked Wuhuan but achieved little. In the 22nd year, Wuhuan defeated the weakened Xiongnu, and the emperor bribed them with money and cloth. In the 25th year, Hao Dan and 922 others paid tribute, and the emperor appointed 81 Wuhuan leaders as princes and commanders, settling them in border counties to scout for the Han. Later, Wuhuan captains were re-established to supervise them. From Emperor Ming to Emperor He, Wuhuan guarded the frontier peacefully. During Emperor An’s reign, Wuhuan invaded Daijun and Shanggu, and later Yanmen Wuhuan joined Xianbei and Southern Xiongnu in attacking Wuyuan, defeating the Han. The court sent He Xi and Liang Dong to defeat them, and Wuhuan gradually became closer to the Han. Under Emperor Shun, Wuhuan invaded Yunzhong, but Geng Ye repelled them. In the 5th year of Yonghe, Wuhuan leaders rebelled but were defeated by Zhang Dan. During Emperor Huan’s Yongshou period, Wuhuan in Shuofang rebelled but were pacified by Zhang Huan. In the 9th year of Yanxi, Wuhuan, Xianbei, and Southern Xiongnu invaded nine counties, but Zhang Huan drove them out. Under Emperor Ling, leaders like Nanlou and Qiu Liju claimed kingship. In the 4th year of Zhongping, Zhang Chun rebelled, joined Qiu Liju, and invaded four provinces. Liu Yu pacified the north. During Emperor Xian’s Chuping period, Tadun succeeded Qiu Liju and controlled three counties. Yuan Shao granted Tadun and others Chanyu seals. Later, Yan Rou killed the Wuhuan captain and replaced him. When Yuan Shang failed, he fled to Tadun. Cao Cao conquered Wuhuan in the 12th year of Jian’an, killed Tadun, captured 200,000, and moved the remaining people to the Central Plains.

Xianbei, also a Donghu branch, relied on Xianbei Mountain. Their customs were similar to Wuhuan, but they shaved their heads for marriage and gathered by the Raole River in spring. Their region had unique animals like wild horses and horned oxen, whose horns were used for bows. Mink and mole furs were valuable. In the early Han, Xianbei was defeated by Maodun and fled to Liaodong, with no contact with the Han. In the early Jianwu period, they invaded the north. In the 21st year, Ji Xu defeated them, and they later exchanged envoys with Han. Ji Xu bribed them to attack the Northern Xiongnu, and they received rewards. During the Ming and Zhang reigns, they guarded the border peacefully. Under Emperor He, Dou Xian defeated the Xiongnu, and Xianbei occupied their territory, absorbing 100,000 Xiongnu remnants and growing strong. They invaded Liaodong, Youbeiping, and Yuyang, with mixed results. During Emperor An’s Yongchu period, Yan Liyang paid tribute, and the court built facilities for trade and hostages. Xianbei alternately surrendered and rebelled, clashing with Xiongnu and Wuhuan. In the 2nd year of Yuanchu, they surrounded Wulu County but gained nothing. In the 4th year, Lianxiu invaded, but Wuhuan leader Yu Zhiju defeated him. In the 5th year, 10,000 Xianbei cavalry invaded Daijun, burning government offices. The court mobilized troops to guard Shanggu. In the 6th year, Deng Zun defeated Xianbei. In the 1st year of Yongning, Wulun and Qizhi Tar surrendered. In the 1st year of Jianguang, Qizhi Tar rebelled, invaded Juyong, and killed the prefect. Geng Kui relieved the siege. Qizhi Tar grew stronger, invading Yanmen, Dingxiang, and Taiyuan. In the 2nd year of Yanguang, he invaded the east, killing over 1,000. In the 3rd year, he invaded Gaoliu. Under Emperor Shun, Qizhi Tar invaded Dai County, killing the prefect. Zhang Guo defeated him in the 2nd year of Yongjian. Xianbei from Liaodong invaded but were repelled by Geng Ye. In the 3rd and 4th years, they invaded Yuyang and Shuofang. In the 6th year, Geng Ye defeated them. In the 1st year of Yangjia, Geng Ye sent Rong Zhumo to attack Xianbei successfully. Xianbei later invaded Liaodong, and Geng Ye moved to Wulu City. In the 2nd year, Zhao Chou defeated Xianbei. Under Emperor Huan, Tanshihuai emerged. His father Touluhou doubted his birth, but his wife claimed a miraculous conception. Tanshihuai grew brave and resourceful, recovering stolen cattle and becoming leader. He established a royal court by the Geqiu River, subdued tribes, and expanded territory from Dingling to Wusun, covering 14,000 miles east-west. In the 2nd year of Yongshou, he invaded Yunzhong. In the 1st year of Yanxi, Zhang Huan killed 200 Xianbei. In the 2nd year, they invaded Yanmen. In the 6th year, they invaded Liaodong. In the 9th year, tens of thousands invaded nine counties, but Zhang Huan drove them out. The court tried to make Tanshihuai king, but he refused and intensified raids. He divided Xianbei into three parts: east, middle, and west. Under Emperor Ling, Xianbei invaded the three provinces of Youzhou, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou annually. In the 3rd year of Xiping, Xia Zhi defeated them. In the 5th year, they invaded Youzhou. In the 6th year, they invaded three borders. Xia Yu proposed a winter-spring campaign, but the court disagreed. Tian Yan sought to lead an expedition, but Cai Yong advised against it, citing past failures and current poverty. The court ignored him, sending Xia Yu, Tian Yan, and Zang Man with 10,000 cavalry each. Tanshihuai’s forces defeated them, killing 70-80% of the troops. The generals were imprisoned. In the 1st year of Guanghe, Xianbei invaded Jiuquan. Tanshihuai, facing food shortages, attacked the Japanese eastward, capturing over 1,000 to fish. He died at 45, succeeded by his son Helian, who was less capable and lost half his people. Helian was killed by a Han archer. His son Qianman was young, and his nephew Kuixi succeeded. Later, Qianman competed with Kuixi, dividing the tribe. Budugen succeeded after Kuixi’s death. From Tanshihuai, leadership became hereditary. The text concludes that Wuhuan and Xianbei caused continuous border troubles, with no effective strategies to control them.
