He appointed Kong Xi as a doctor, gave him money and silk to praise Chenghou and the Kong family, ordered Kong Xi to return to the capital with him, and asked him to correct his books in Dongguan.
In the winter of this year, when the Jin Dynasty was granted the order, Cui Xiang used the "Jialin" to divine. He couldn't tell, so he stopped Kong Xi and said, "You might as well resign."
Kong Xi said: Studying is not about being a person, and officials are not about choosing what kind of official they should be. Good or bad luck depends on oneself. Is it a matter of divination?
If you die in office, your will will be buried on the spot. The second sons, Chang Yan and Ji Yan, are both in their teens.
Pu Ban ordered Xu Junran to persuade them to return to their place of origin in Lu, and replied: "To return with my father's coffin now is a violation of my father's will; to leave without leaving the tomb is unbearable."

The emperor remained silent, and everyone around him hated Kong Jiyan.
If you want to be filial and honest, you won't be able to do it.
Three years later, at the age of forty-seven, he died at home.
In the past, Emperor Ping took power over Wang Mang. He named Kong Jun, a descendant of Confucius, as Baochenghou, and posthumously named Confucius as Baocheng Xuanni.

In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Shizu granted Kong Zhi, Kong Jun's son, the title of Marquis of Cheng.

In the fourth year of Yongyuan, he moved to Baotinghou.

After Kong Yao passed away, his son Kong Wan inherited the throne.
It has been passed down from generation to generation that in the early years of Emperor Xian's reign, all feudal states were cut off.
◆Yang Lun's biography, Yang Lun's courtesy name is Zhongli, and his name is Chen Liudong.
When he was young, he was a student and worshiped Situ Dinghong as his teacher and studied "Guwen Shangshu".
He was appointed as literary director of the county.

Even if you are beheaded, you will not change your mind, and you will not regret even after nine deaths.
The defense of an ordinary man is stronger than the three armies.
Because I dare to write lyrics.
The emperor then issued an edict saying: Yang Lun came out of the low place and went up to the high ground. He did not follow the king's orders and stopped the road without permission. He took advantage of his illness and indulged his wild ambitions.
So he recruited Tingwei and ordered him to forgive his sins.
Yang Lun was summoned three times, but he always disagreed with his opinions.
After returning home, he lectured behind closed doors and did not interact with others.
The bus was called again, and he escaped and died at home.
Guangwu Zhongxing, Beihai Mou Rong studied "Da Xia Hou Shangshu", Donghai Wang Liang studied "Xiao Xia Hou Shangshu", and Pei Guo Huan Rong studied "Ouyang Shangshu".
Huan Rong studied and taught for generations, and Tokyo said he was the most prosperous.
Fufeng Du Lin passed the "Gu Wen Shangshu", Jia Kui, a native of the same county as Du Lin, did textual research on him, Ma Rong wrote the biography, and Zheng Xuan made the annotations. Therefore, the "Gu Wen Shangshu" has become the most important in the world.
summary:
During the reigns of Wang Mang and Gengshi, the world fell into chaos, causing the collapse of rituals and music and the loss of documents. Emperor Guangwu, who favored classical studies, gathered scholars and restored texts. Scholars from across the land brought their books to the capital. The state established fourteen doctors for the Five Classics, each teaching according to their family methods. In the fifth year of Jianwu, the Imperial Academy was built, and later, structures like Piyong, Mingtang, and Lingtai were erected. Emperor Ming personally performed rituals, lectured on classics, and established separate schools for descendants of meritorious officials. The Xiongnu even sent their children to study. During Emperor Zhang’s reign, Confucians gathered at the White Tiger Hall to discuss texts, resulting in the "White Tiger General Meaning." However, under Empress Deng’s regency, scholarly activity waned. Emperor An neglected arts and literature, leading to the decay of school buildings. Emperor Shun rebuilt the academy, adding 240 rooms and 1,850 houses, and recruited students. By the time of Empress Dowager Liang, the number of students exceeded 30,000, but scholarly rigor declined. After the execution of party members, corruption and textual alterations spread. In the fourth year of Xiping, Emperor Ling ordered the Five Classics to be engraved on stone tablets in multiple scripts. When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, many texts were lost or destroyed, with only seventy carts remaining after transport to Chang'an, half of which were lost. Later, all were burned in the chaos of Chang'an.

The text records notable scholars. Liu Kun, a descendant of King Xiao of Liang, studied rituals and taught over 500 disciples during Wang Mang’s time. He performed ceremonies with great care, but Wang Mang arrested him for private gatherings. After Wang Mang’s failure, Liu Kun was spared. He later served as a county magistrate, where his prayers stopped fires and his benevolent governance caused tigers to leave. Emperor Guangwu appointed him as a tutor for the crown prince. Wa Dan, from Nanyang, taught the "Mencius Yi" and refused office under Wang Mang. He became a doctor under Guangwu and wrote seven chapters of "Yi Tong Lun." Ren An, from Guanghan, studied the "Mencius Yi" and mastered several classics, but refused official appointments due to illness. Yang Zheng, from Jingzhao, studied "Liang Shiyi" and was known for his eloquent explanations. He once pleaded for Fan Sheng’s release by appearing before the emperor, enduring wounds. He was known for his boldness and friendship with powerful figures. Zhang Xing, from Yingchuan, taught "Liangqiu Yi" and had nearly ten thousand disciples. Dai Ping, from Runan, studied "Jing's Book of Changes" and debated with scholars, earning a reputation for his expertise. He served as a minister and was known for his outspokenness. Sun Qi, from Jiyin, studied "Jingshi Yi" and "Guwen Shangshu," supporting his mother by raising pigs. His virtue inspired others, and even Yellow Turban bandits spared his home.

The text also covers scholars of the "Shangshu." Ouyang She, from Le'an, inherited the family tradition of teaching "Fu Sheng Shangshu" and served as a governor. He was imprisoned for corruption, but his student Lizhen pleaded to die in his place. Mou Chang, from Le'an, taught "Ouyang Shangshu" to over a thousand students and wrote "Mou Shi Zhang Ju." Song Deng, from Chang'an, taught "Ouyang Shangshu" and served as a prefect, known for his honest governance. Zhang Xun, from Jiyin, taught "Da Xia Hou Shangshu" and served as a minister. Yin Min, from Nanyang, studied various classics and corrected prophecies, but fell out of favor with the emperor. Zhou Fang, from Runan, studied "Guwen Shangshu" and wrote "Shangshu Miscellaneous Notes." Kong Xi, from Lu, inherited the tradition of "Guwen Shangshu" and "Mao Shi." He was accused of slandering Emperor Wu but defended himself in a letter, and the emperor appointed him as Lantai Order. Yang Lun, from Chenliu, studied "Guwen Shangshu" and taught over a thousand disciples. He criticized corruption and was dismissed but later pardoned. He refused further appointments and died at home.

The text concludes by noting that during Guangwu’s reign, scholars like Mou Rong, Wang Liang, and Huan Rong taught various versions of the "Shangshu." Huan Rong’s teachings flourished in Tokyo, while Du Lin’s "Gu Wen Shangshu" became prominent through the works of Jia Kui, Ma Rong, and Zheng Xuan.

◆The biography of Gao Xu, named Ji Hui, was from Pingyuan County.
Great-grandfather Gao Jia taught the Yuan Emperor with "Lu Shi" and became the prefect of Shanggu.
Gao Xu's father, Gao Rong, taught Gao Jiaxue when he was young, and became Guanglu doctor during the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping.
Because of his father's relationship, Gao Xu served as a doctor and taught "Lu Shi" from generation to generation.
He is famous for his honest words and deeds.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, the father and son pretended to be blind and ran away, refusing to serve as Wang Mang's officials.
When Guangwu came to the throne, the Grand Sikong Song Hong recommended him to be a high-ranking official, he was appointed as a Lang, and he was granted the title of Fu Lichang.
After resigning from the official position, he was recruited as a doctor.
In the eleventh year of Jianwu's reign, he was awarded the title of Grand Secretary of Agriculture.
He was famous in the imperial court for his official residence.
In the thirteenth year, he died in office and was given money and a cemetery plot.
◆Bao Xian's biography, Bao Xian's courtesy name is Ziliang, and he was born in Qu'a, Kuaiji.
When he was young, he was a Zhusheng and studied in Chang'an. He studied "Lu Shi" and "The Analects of Confucius" with his doctorate from Xijun as his teacher.
In the last years of his life, Wang Mang returned to his hometown and was arrested by red-browed thieves in the East China Sea.
For more than ten days, Bao Xian could chant sutras in the morning and evening freely. The red-browed thieves were surprised and sent him away.
So he lived in the East China Sea and built a monastery to teach.
After Guangwu ascended the throne, he returned to his hometown.
Huang Fan, the prefect, was appointed as the governor of the household, and wanted to find Bao Xian to teach his son.
Bao Xian said: Etiquette can be learned, not taught.
Huang Fan sent his son to ask him for advice, and he became his teacher. For filial piety and honesty, he was awarded the title of doctor.
During the Jianwu period, he entered the imperial court to teach the crown prince to study the Analects of Confucius, and also wrote chapters and sentences of the Analects of Confucius.
He was awarded the title of admonishment to the senior official, Shizhong, and Youzhonglang general.
In the fifth year of Yongping, he was promoted to Dahonglu.
Every time he came to see the emperor, the emperor would give him a few sticks.
If there is any doubt in the scriptures, Xiao Huangmen is often sent to his home to ask.
Xianzong believed that Bao Xian had the kindness of a teacher and lived a poor life. He often rewarded Bao Xian with rare silks and silks, and his salary was more than that of other ministers. Bao Xian was given to the poorest among the living.
When he was seriously ill, Xianzong went to see him in person.
Eight years later, at the age of seventy-two, he died in office.
His son Bao Fu was awarded the title of doctor, and he also used "The Analects of Confucius" to teach and teach in the imperial court.
◆In the biography of Wei Ying, Wei Ying was named Jun Bo and was a native of Rencheng.
It is easy to learn when you are young.
In the early years of Jianwu, he went to study for a doctoral degree and studied "Lu Shi".
He studied behind closed doors and made no friends, and everyone in the capital praised him.
Later he returned home and became a county official. He taught Ming scriptures and taught literature to King Yin.
He was dismissed from his official post due to illness and became a professor in Shan Zezhong, often with hundreds of students and disciples.
In the early years of Yongping, he became a doctor and was promoted to minister.
In the thirteenth year, he was promoted to Dahonglu.
In the eighteenth year, he was awarded Doctor Guanglu.
In the fourth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he was awarded the title of "Five-Guan Zhonglang General".
Wei Ying was proficient in Confucian classics and had a pure moral character. He had thousands of disciples who came from far away to learn from him.
Suzong valued him very much, visited him many times, discussed problems in front of the emperor, and received special rewards.
At this time, the Confucian scholars of the capital were gathered at Baihu Temple to discuss the similarities and differences of the Five Classics, and Wei Ying was asked to explain the difficulties. Chun Yugong, the servant, reported to the emperor. The emperor personally attended the meeting to preside over it, just like the old thing in Shiqu.
In the second year, Wei Ying was appointed as the governor of Shangdang and was awarded the title of cavalry captain. He died in office.
◆The biography of Fu Gong, Fu Gong's courtesy name Shuqi, was a native of Dongwu, Langfu, and the son of Situ Fuzhan's younger brother.
Fu Zhan's younger brother Fu An, whose courtesy name was Zhiwen, changed the chapters and sentences in order to clarify "Qi Shi" and wrote nine chapters of "Explanation". He rose to the rank of Guang Luxun. Fu Zhan had no sons, so he took Fu Gong as his queen.
Fu Gong has a filial nature and treats his stepmother with great respect. When he was young, he passed on the Fu An School and was appointed as a man.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he was awarded the title of county magistrate.
He served for thirteen years and became famous for his political integrity and fairness.
Qingzhou selected him as a special scholar. He ranked first in Taichang's classics examination, was awarded a doctorate, and was promoted to the prefect of Changshan.
He built schools and taught more than one disciple, so Beizhou was mostly Fu's school.
In the second year of Yongping, he replaced Liang Song as the imperial servant.
In the fourth year, the emperor personally went to Piyong and during the ceremony, he conferred Fugong the title of Sikong. Confucian scholars considered it an honor.
At first, Fugong's father Fu An's chapter was too complicated, so Fugong deleted the redundant words and the final version was 200,000 words.
After reigning for nine years, he asked to go home due to illness and was granted a salary of thousands of dollars to last his life.
In the fifteenth year, the emperor came to Langfu and introduced Fugong, which was like a ceremony to meet the three princes.
In the winter of the second year of Jianchu, Suzong held a feast and called Fugong the third elder.
In the 90th year of his reign, he passed away in the first year of Yuanhe and was buried under the Xianjie Mausoleum.
His son Fushou was promoted to the prefect of Dongjun.
◆In the biography of Ren Mo, his courtesy name is Shuben. He was a native of Fan County, Shu County.
When he was young, he studied "Qi Shi", traveled to the capital, and taught his disciples for more than ten years.
When his friend Dong Fengde died of illness in Luoyang, Ren Mo personally pushed the deer cart to carry Dong Fengde's funeral to the cemetery, which made him famous.
He was a meritorious officer of the county and resigned due to illness.
Later, Ben died on the road at the funeral of his teacher.
When he was about to die, he told his brother's son Ren Zao: "My body must be sent to the teacher. If I am still conscious after death, my soul will not feel ashamed; if I am not conscious, I have to leave it alone."
Ren Zao listened to him.

summary:
The transmission and scholarly traditions of classical Chinese texts, particularly the *Shi* (Poetry) and other classics, during the Han dynasty. The *Shi* of Lu, Qi, and Han schools each had established doctors, while the *Mao Shi* did not. The biographies of several scholars follow, detailing their studies, teachings, and official careers.

Gao Xu, from Pingyuan, studied the *Lu Shi* and served as a doctor, but feigned blindness to avoid serving Wang Mang. Under Emperor Guangwu, he held various posts, including Grand Secretary of Agriculture, and died in office. Bao Xian, from Kuaiji, studied *Lu Shi* and the *Analects* under a doctor. Captured by Red Eyebrow rebels, he was released for chanting scriptures. He later taught the crown prince, wrote chapters on the *Analects*, and held high offices, receiving generous rewards from Emperor Xianzong. Wei Ying, from Rencheng, studied *Lu Shi* and taught hundreds of students. He became a doctor, minister, and later Grand Herald, known for his moral purity and large following. Fu Gong, from Langfu, inherited his uncle Fu An's teachings on *Qi Shi*, served as a county magistrate, and became a doctor. He simplified his uncle's complex chapters and was honored as Sikong. Ren Mo, from Shu, studied *Qi Shi* and gained fame for personally transporting his friend's funeral. Jing Luan, from Guanghan, studied *Qi Shi* and other texts, writing extensively on various classics. Xue Han, from Huaiyang, studied *Han Shi* and was a leading authority on poetry and prophecies, but died in prison. Du Fu, from Wuyang, studied under Xue Han and taught *Han Shi* to many disciples. Zhao Xun, from Jiujiang, studied *Han Shi* and served as a cavalry captain and tutor to princes. Yang Ren, from Ba, studied *Han Shi* and served as a doctor, known for his advice on governance. Zhao Ye, from Kuaiji, studied *Han Shi* under Du Fu and refused official posts.

The text also covers other traditions. Wei Hong, from Donghai, studied *Mao's Poems* and wrote a preface, as well as works on ancient texts. The *Li* (Rites) tradition is traced from Gao Tangsheng through Hou Cang to Dai De, Dai Sheng, and Qing Pu, with three schools establishing doctors. Dong Jun, from Qianwei, studied the *Qing Shi Rites* and was consulted on ritual matters. The *Spring and Autumn Annals* traditions are detailed: the *Gongyang* school had Yan and Jiang families, while the *Zuo* school was transmitted by Jia Yi. Ding Gong studied *Gongyang Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals* and taught thousands of disciples. Zhou Ze, from Beihai, studied the same text and served as a doctor and minister, known for his honesty. Zhong Xing, from Runan, studied under Ding Gong and helped compile chapters for the crown prince. Zhen Yu, from Beihai, studied *Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals* and taught many students. Lou Wang, from Chenliu, studied the same text and became a leading Confucian with over 9,000 students. Cheng Zeng, from Yuzhang, studied *Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals* and wrote extensively. Zhang Xuan, from Hanoi, studied the same text and was admired for his erudition. Li Yu, from Fufeng, studied *Gongyang Chunqiu* and debated at the White Tiger Hall. He Xiu, from Rencheng, wrote a commentary on the *Gongyang* and refuted other interpretations. Fu Qian, from Henan, wrote a commentary on the *Zuo* tradition. Ying Rong, from Chen, studied the *Zuo* tradition and taught many disciples. Xie Gai, from Nanyang, was a famous scholar of the *Zuo* tradition. Xu Shen, from Runan, wrote *Shuowen Jiezi* and *Different Meanings of the Five Classics*. Cai Xuan, from Runan, taught thousands of disciples.

The text concludes with a historian's comment on the flourishing of Confucian studies after Guangwu, noting that despite political turmoil, the teachings of the classics maintained social order and delayed the Han dynasty's fall.

summary:
Emperor Guangwu had eleven sons. Queen Guo bore him several sons, including Liu Qiang, who was initially made crown prince. In the 17th year of Jianwu, Empress Guo was deposed, causing Liu Qiang great anxiety. He repeatedly expressed his wish to step down as crown prince and become a vassal king. Emperor Guangwu eventually agreed in the 19th year, naming him King of Donghai. The emperor, believing Liu Qiang was not at fault, granted him an exceptionally large fief of 29 counties, along with special honors like tiger-head talismans and palace bells and drums. Even after arriving at his fief, Liu Qiang repeatedly tried to return lands, but the emperor refused. He was later allowed to make Lu his capital. Liu Qiang died in the 1st year of Yongping. On his deathbed, he wrote a grateful and humble letter to the emperor, expressing his unworthiness of the honors and his concern for his son. The emperor was deeply saddened and ordered a grand funeral with special rites, attended by many nobles. To honor Liu Qiang's modesty, the emperor decreed a simple burial.

Liu Fu, another son, was made King of Pei. He was known for his dignified conduct and love for the classics, authoring the "Treatise on the Five Classics," which was called the "Pei Wang Tong Lun." He was cautious and disciplined, earning the title of a wise king. He died after 46 years of rule.

Liu Ying, King of Chu, was the son of a less favored concubine. He was fond of Huangdi and Laozi and studied Buddhism. In the 8th year of Yongping, he offered silk to atone for his sins, but the emperor returned it. Later, he was accused of treason for making talismans and fabricating prophecies. The emperor deposed him and moved him to Danyang, where he committed suicide. His kingdom was abolished. The ensuing investigation implicated many, leading to thousands of executions and exiles.

Liu Kang, King An of Jinan, was known for not following laws and socializing with guests. He was accused of conspiracy, but the emperor, due to their kinship, only reduced his fief. He later became extravagant, with many slaves, horses, and private lands. A governor admonished him, but he did not change his ways. He died after 59 years of rule.

Liu Cang, King Xian of Dongping, was intelligent and well-read. He served as General of Hussars under Emperor Xianzong and helped establish ritual systems. He often advised the emperor, once persuading him to cancel a hunting trip. He repeatedly asked to resign from his high post, which the emperor eventually allowed. He was known for his virtue and was greatly respected. The emperor frequently sought his advice on state matters. He died in the 2nd year of Jianchu, and his son succeeded him.

Liu Yan, King Zhi of Fuling, was arrogant and harsh. He was accused of making prophecies and was demoted to Marquis of Fuling. He later plotted rebellion again and was demoted again. He was eventually restored as king by Emperor Zhanghe.

Liu Jing, King Si of Guangling, was impatient and insidious. After Emperor Guangwu's death, he wrote a seditious letter to Liu Qiang, urging him to rebel. Liu Qiang reported him. The emperor concealed the matter. Liu Jing later consulted fortune tellers and claimed to resemble the late emperor, leading to further investigations. He eventually committed suicide.

Liu Heng, Duke Huai of Linhuai, died before becoming king, and his state was abolished.

Liu Yan, King Jian of Zhongshan, was the youngest son of Empress Dowager Guo and stayed in the capital. He was favored by the emperor. He once hanged his concubine and was punished by losing a county. He died in the 2nd year of Yongyuan.

Liu Jing, King Xiao of Langya, was respectful and filial, fond of Confucian classics. He was especially favored by Emperor Xianzong. He built magnificent palaces and wrote poems praising virtues. He died after 31 years of rule.

Preface to the Biography of Dang Guo, Confucius said: Their natures are similar, but their habits are far apart.
This means that people's likes and dislikes are the same in nature, but their education and environment make people's temperament and conduct very different.
Therefore, a virtuous person teaches others to cultivate their character, overcome dissolute behavior, be cautious in making friends, control bias, and be fair in dealing with situations.
Although people's emotions are vastly different, and their culture and quality are also different, as for cultivating talents and revitalizing customs, the principles are the same. In the chaos of the weekend, customs are superficial and hypocritical, the country is out of order, and disciplines are lax. There are also people who use the name of benevolence to achieve their own goals and rely on loyalty to make their careers successful.

Everyone cherished the mentality of aggression and condescension, despised life and death, valued loyalty, and repaid each other if they had grievances and virtues. Orders were given to private individuals, and power was in the hands of ordinary men. It became a social custom to let the knights be the best.
Since Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Confucianism has been promoted, and scholars of Confucianism and Confucianism can be found everywhere. There was even a debate about the Six Arts in Shiqu Pavilion, and those who agreed with me became friends; those who disagreed attacked me. People who value literature are at their peak at this time.
When Wang Mang took power and deceived himself, he finally usurped the throne of the Han Dynasty. Those who are loyal to the Han Dynasty and have a righteous mind are ashamed to serve as an official for Wang Mang, those who regard seclusion as an honor and are willing to be poor.
Although Guangwu was revived and Han Dynasty was re-established, his wiseness to protect himself and his uprightness and self-restraint still made everyone envious of him. The important issue of being an official and not being an official is of great importance in current affairs!

◆Cai Yan's biography, Cai Yan's courtesy name is Meng happy, a native of Xiang County, Runan County.
When he was young, he was proficient in Confucian classics, taught his disciples, and educated the villagers with courtesy.
When there were disputes in the village, they often went to Cai Yan's house to ask for settlement. After Cai Yan mediated, everyone said they had no objection.
He was promoted to the title of Xiaolian and the governor of Jizhou.
Ju Yuan, the official in charge of the imperial office, asked Cai Yan to nominate his younger brother as a maocai, but Cai Yan refused and ordered him to be arrested and asked to deliver letters.
He also impeached Cao Ding, the Prime Minister of Hejian, for embezzling millions of dollars in stolen goods.
Cao Ding is the younger brother of Zhongchang Shi Cao Teng.
Cao Teng sent General Liang Ji to write a letter to Cai Yan asking him to intercede, but Cai Yan ignored him. Cao Ding was therefore convicted and sent to Zuo School for labor reform.
The imperial court recruited Cai Yan to serve as Yi Lang and Fu Jie Ling.
Liang Ji heard that Cai Yan was talented and asked him to meet him. Cai Yan was ill and refused to go, so Liang Ji hated him.
At this time, Nanyang Governor Cheng Wang Jin and others were interrogated by the court captain for taking in the eunuchs. Cai Yan and Yilang Liu Yu came to rescue them.
Emperor Ling ascended the throne and was appointed Yilang again. He died of illness.
◆The biography of Yangzhi, the descendant of Yangzhi, was a native of Liangfu County, Taishan.
Generations are the family of officials.
When Yang Zhi was young, he was upright and knowledgeable. He was promoted as Xiaolian and conscripted into Taiwei Li Gu's mansion. Because of his excellent performance, he was promoted to a high rank and was appointed as Shi Yushi.
When Li Gu was executed, Yang Zhi was banned from being an official for many years because he was Li Gu's old official.
Because of his outstanding performance, he was promoted to the provincial governor of Jizhou.
Report cases of corruption and corruption, and wherever they go, corruption and perversion of the law will disappear.
He was promoted to Huben Zhonglang General, Chengmen Xiaowei, and Shangshu Ling three times.
At this time, Taiwei Zhang Hao, Situ Fanling, Da Honglu Guo Fang, Tai servant Cao Ling, and Da Sinong Feng Fang all had marriages with eunuchs, got together, and openly bribed eunuchs. Yang Zhi petitioned them one by one to remove them and expel them, but the emperor did not accept it.
Former Taiwei Liu Chong, Sili Colonel Xu Bing, Youzhou Governor Yang Xi, Liangzhou Governor Liu Gong, and Yizhou Governor Pang Ai were honest and upright in public affairs. Yang Zhi recommended them and promoted them. The emperor commended him and appointed him as Henan Yin.
He received salary on a daily basis, often ate dry rice and vegetables, and suppressed powerful people. All the officials in the capital were afraid of him. When troubles with the party occurred, he was removed from office, and he was imprisoned as an official. He died at home.
◆Zhang Jianzhuan, Zhang Jianzi Yuanjie, a native of Gaoping, Shanyang, a descendant of Zhao Wang Zhang Er.
His father, Zhang Cheng, was the governor of Jiangxia. Zhang Jian was initially recommended as a talented person by the villagers. He thought that the governor was not suitable for him, so he refused to go because of illness.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, the governor Zhai Chao asked him to be the postal supervisor in the east.
At this time, Zhongchang Shihou Lan's family was in Fangdong, and he was cruel to the people and lawless.
Zhang Jian exposed the crimes of Hou Lan and his mother and asked the court to execute them.
Hou Lan withheld Zhang Jian's seal, but the emperor did not see it, so he and Hou Lan became enmity.
Zhu Bing, a native of the country, was flattering, despicable and nasty by nature. Zhang Jian looked down upon him and hated him. He wrote a letter to accuse Zhang Jian and twenty-four people in the same county of being friends. The court then ordered Zhang Jian to be arrested and Zhu Bing's name to be cut off to show that he was keeping it secret.
Zhang Jian ran for his life and ran away in embarrassment. Wherever he ran, when it got dark, he would stay in any house. No one disrespected his reputation and character. Even though his family was ruined, they were still willing to take him in.
Later he went into exile in Donglai and stayed at Li Du's home.
Waihuang ordered Mao Qin to lead troops to his home. Li Du called Mao Qin and said: "Zhang Jian is famous all over the world. It is not his fault to escape."
Even if you see Zhang Jian, can you bear to capture him?
Mao Qin stood up and caressed Li Du and said: "It is shameful for Zang Boyu to think that he is a gentleman alone. Why do you only focus on benevolence and righteousness?"
Li Du said: Although I, Li Du, say I love righteousness, you have gained half of it today!
Mao Qin sighed and left.
Li Du was able to send Zhang Jian out of the fortress, and Zhang Jian was finally saved from death.
Dozens of people were executed in every house where Zhang Jian passed by, and all their clan relatives were killed, leaving the county in ruins.
In the first year of Zhongping, the party's imprisonment was lifted, and Zhang Jian returned to his hometown.
The generals and three princes all recruited him and recommended him with sincerity. He had the characteristics of the official carriage of the imperial court and was appointed to pay homage to the Shaofu, but he was not accepted.
In the early years of Emperor Xian's reign, the people were in famine, and Zhang Jian's family was relatively wealthy, so he shared his property with his fellow villagers. There are hundreds of people who survive on these properties.
In the early years of Jian'an, the imperial court recruited him as a guard, but he accepted it as a last resort.
Zhang Jian saw that Cao Cao had usurpation ambitions, so he closed his door and hung up his car.
More than a year later, he died in Xuzhou at the age of eighty-four.
The historian commented: In the past, Wei Qi avoided death, Yu Qing resigned and fled with him, Ji Bu fled for his life, and the Zhu family was willing to hide him and save him.
Zhang Jian offended the emperor and fled everywhere for his life. When people in the world heard about his integrity, they all liked his ambition and competed to be the host to take him in.
There are probably dozens of cases where he abandoned his city, lost his official position, and destroyed his body and clan. Isn't Zhang Jian still a virtuous person?
However, Zhang Jian tried to block the river with just one palm of his hand, and finally caused trouble because of his hatred for unkind people. This shows how overestimating his ability is!
◆Cen Hao's biography, Cen Hao's courtesy name was Gongxiao, and he was a native of Jiyang County, Nanyang County.
His father, Cen Yu, served as the governor of Nanjun and was killed for corruption.
When Cen Hao was young and not well-known, he went to see Zong Ci of the same county. Zong Ci was recruited for being a good man. The house was full of guests. They thought Cen Hao was not a good family son and were unwilling to meet him.
Cen Hao stayed outside the door for many days before being brought in.
Zong Ci talked to him and praised him greatly, so he took him to Luoyang to study at Taixue.
Cen Hao had superb talents, and Guo Linzong, Li Gongshu, etc. all became friends with him. Li Ying and Wang Chang said that he had the ability to govern the country. Although he was in the countryside, he was high-spirited and had the ambition to govern the world.
When the prefect, Hongnongcheng, came to the Jin Dynasty, he wanted to establish his authority. After hearing Cen Hao's name, he asked him to serve as a meritorious officer, and also appointed Zhang Mu as a thief officer.
King Cheng Jin trusted Cen Hao and Zhang Mu, rewarded good deeds and corrected mistakes, and purged the palace.
There was a wealthy businessman named Zhang Xun in Wan County, who was a relative of Emperor Huan's beauty. He could carve some ingenious and interesting things, and often gave them to eunuchs with bribes. As a result, he also obtained a prominent official position. With his skills, he could do whatever he wanted.
Cen Hao and Zhang Mu persuaded Wang Jin to arrest Zhang Xun and others. Later, when they were pardoned, Cen Hao still killed them and arrested their clan guests. He killed more than 200 people before reporting to the court.
So the wife of Zhang Xun, the official in charge of Zhang Xun, sent a letter to complain.
Emperor Huan was furious and conscripted King Jin into prison and died in prison.
Cen Hao and Zhang Mu were hiding between Qi and Lu.
Meet pardon and come out.
Later, he was elected by the state and county, and he was not accepted by the three governments.
After Li Gu and Du Mi were killed, he fled again and was heard to have died in the Jiangxia Mountains.
◆Chen Xiang's biography, Chen Xiang's courtesy name is Zilin, a native of Shaoling County, Runan County.
Grandfather Chen Zhen, Sili Xiaowei.
Chen Xiang was famous for his social skills when he was young.
He was promoted to Xiaolian, and Taiwei Zhou Jing promoted him with a high rank and appointed him as Shi Yushi.
At this time, on the first day of the first lunar month of the lunar calendar, Liang Ji, the general, showed his unkempt appearance and unkempt appearance. Chen Xiang reported to the emperor that Liang Ji was disrespectful to the emperor because of his good fortune, so he should be arrested and punished. People at the time thought he was a strange person.
He was promoted to prefect of Dingxiang, conscripted as Yilang, and promoted to governor of Yangzhou.
The emperor reported that Wang Yong, the prefect of Yuzhang, was a senior official, and Xu Shen, the prefect of Wu County, had committed corruption in office, and both were expelled from the imperial court.
Xu Shen is the younger brother of Xu Huang, the imperial minister.
As a result, his reputation grew.
He was also appointed as Yilang to supplement the imperial censor Zhongcheng.
He was interrogated by the Huangmen Beisi Prison due to party misfortune, but was exonerated because there was no evidence, and died at home.
◆The biography of Kong Yu, whose courtesy name was Yuan Dynasty, was from Lu County, Lu State.
Kong Ba, the seventh generation ancestor, served successively as Jiuqing when he became emperor, and was granted the title of Marquis.
From Kong Ba to Kong Yu, the title of nobility continued, and there were fifty-three ministers and ministers, including seven princes.
When Kong Yu was a child, he studied "Shang Shu" and was summoned by the general Liang Ji, but he did not respond.
Taiwei Ju Fangzheng disagreed with the emperor's questions, so he resigned due to illness.
Later, he was banned from serving as an official due to party disaster.
When Emperor Ling came to the throne, he conscripted Yilang in a public car to supplement the Luoyang order. Because of the death of his teacher, he abandoned his official position and died at home.
◆The biography of Yuan Kang, whose courtesy name is Zhongzhen, was born in Chonghe County, Bohai County.
When he was young, he studied in Taixue and was very close to Guo Linzong.
Raise filial piety and integrity, and then move to Yingyin Order. Known for his ability.
He was promoted to Taishou of Taishan.
Many surnames in the county were engaged in illegal activities. When Yuan Kang took office, he acted aggressively, got angry, and promulgated strict laws. No one dared to break the law.
Those who had invaded other people's fields and houses in the past were quickly returned to their original owners.
At this time, Zhang Jian of Shanyang killed Hou Lan's mother, who was often serving as a servant. Yuan Kang investigated her clan guests, some of whom were hidden in Taishan. He always hated eunuchs, so he arrested them all without missing or running away.
Hou Lan hated Yuan Kang to the extreme. He falsely accused Yuan Kang, Yanzhou Governor No. 5 and Duwei Hujia of surrendering, and summoned Yuan Kang to Tingwei Prison. He was commuted to the death penalty and demoted to Rinan.
Yingyin and Taiyangzhi waited until the court appealed for Yuankang and were pardoned. They were sent back to their own county and died at home.
◆Tanfu Zhuan, Tanfu Ziwenyou, a native of Xiaqiu, Shanyin County.
When I was young, I was Zhusheng. Although my family was poor, I had high ambitions and did not accept benefits from the wealthy people in the village.
In order to promote filial piety and honesty, the government called for him many times, but he still failed.
Jingshe teaches students, and hundreds of people often come to study from far away.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, he was recruited with a doctorate degree, but he was not successful.
When Emperor Ling came to the throne, Taiwei Huang Qiong promoted him to be Fangzheng. He answered the emperor's questions and met the requirements of the administration at that time. He was promoted to Yilang and supplemented the county magistrate of Meng.
Because the county guard was unpopular, he abandoned his official position and returned home.
The family has no property, but they live in the same clothes as their children and grandchildren, and eat by the sun.
He died at home at the age of eighty.
◆The biography of Liu Ru, whose courtesy name is Shulin, was from Yangping County, Dongjun.
Guo Linzong once said that although Liu Ru stuttered in speech, he was very smart and had an essence as white as jade.
He was promoted to be filial and honest, and he was promoted to a high rank due to his outstanding performance.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, disasters often occurred, and he issued edicts to ask for outspoken opinions. Liu Ru secretly wrote ten articles, expressing the gains and losses of the court with great loyalty and sincerity.
Emperor Huan could not accept it and appointed him as the Prime Minister of the city.
Soon, he was appointed Yilang.
After encountering Dou Wushi, he was imprisoned and committed suicide.
Jia Biao's biography, Jia Biao's courtesy name is Weijie, a native of Dingling County, Yingchuan County.
When he was young, he traveled to the capital. He had extraordinary integrity and impassioned generosity, and was as famous as Xun Shuang, a native of the same county.
He began to serve as an official in the state and county, promoted filial piety and integrity, and served as the county magistrate of Xinxi.
The people were poor and did not raise their children. Jia Biao established a strict legal system. Those who did not raise their children were as guilty as murdering people.
There were robbers and murderers in the south of the city, and women and children in the north. Jia Biao went to the scene of the crime to deal with it, and Shi Shi wanted to take Jia Biao to the south of the city.
Jia Biao got angry and said: "It is common sense for thieves and bandits to harm others; it is contrary to nature and human nature for a mother and her son to kill each other."
So he drove to the north of the city and punished the woman.
When the thieves in the south of the city heard about it, they also tied themselves up and went to the county to surrender.
Within a few years, thousands of people were raising children and they were all called "Jia Gongzhang". Those who gave birth to boys were named "Jia Zi" and those who gave birth to girls were named "Jia Nu".
In the ninth year of Yanxi's reign, a party disaster broke out. Taiwei Chen Fan opposed it but failed. All officials in the court felt chilled by it and did not dare to say anything more.
Jia Biao said to his colleagues: If I don't go westward, the disaster will not be relieved.
So he went to Luoyang and told the city gate captain Dou Wu, Shangshu Huo, Dou Wu and others to appeal to the emperor, and Emperor Huan therefore pardoned the party members.
Li Ying came out and said: I was able to avoid the party disaster because of Jia Sheng's strength!
At one time, Cen Hao was on the run due to party troubles, and his relatives and friends hid him. Jia Biao stayed behind closed doors and refused to accept him. People at that time hated him.
Jia Biao said: "The Biography" says: Act according to time and do not harm future generations.
Gongxiao brought the blame on himself for threatening the emperor to commit crime. Just because I cannot treat each other with hostility and hate him, how can I shelter him and hide him?
Due to party troubles, he was prohibited from becoming an official and died at home.
At first, the three Jia Biao brothers were all famous, and Jia Biao was the best. Therefore, there is a legend in the world: Among the three tigers of the Jia family, Wei Jie is the most angry. ◆The biography of He Yong, named Boqiu, was a native of Xiangxiang County, Nanyang County.
When he was young, he traveled to the capital to study.
Although He Yong is a junior, Guo Linzong, Jia Weijie and others are very close to him. Famous Imperial Academy.
His friend Yu Weigao had not avenged his father and was seriously ill and was about to die. He Yong went to see him. Yu Weigao cried to him. He Yong was moved by his righteousness and avenged him. He sacrificed the head of his enemy to the grave of Yu Weigao's father.
After Chen Fan and Li Ying failed, He Yong was framed by the eunuchs because of his friendship with Chen Fan and Li Ying. He then changed his name and fled to Runan County.
Wherever he went, he gathered heroes and became famous in Jingzhou and Yuzhou.
Yuan Shao admired his character, secretly interacted with him, and became his sworn friend.
At this time, the party was in trouble and many people in the world suffered. He Yong often went to Luoyang privately to discuss with Yuan Shao.
For some poor and helpless people, help them survive the disaster.
For some people who were being hunted, he made great suggestions, allowing them to escape or hide, and saved many people from party disasters.
After the party disaster was resolved, He Yong was recruited by Sikong Mansion.
In every meeting of the three governments, He Yong was always recommended as the leader.
Promoted several times.
Dong Zhuo was in power and forced He Yong to become a long history officer. He refused to accept it on the pretext of illness, and conspired with Sikong Xunshuang, Situ Wang Yun and others to kill Dong Zhuo.
Xun Shuang died, and He Yong was arrested by Dong Zhuo for other matters, and he died of sorrow and anger.
At first, when He Yong saw Cao Cao, he sighed and said: The Han family is about to perish, and this man must be the one who will bring peace to the world.
Cao Cao was very happy.
He once praised Yingchuan Xun as the weapon of Wang Zuo.
Xun Ren served as the Minister of Secretariat and sent people to the west to meet his uncle Xun Shuang. He Yong's body was collected and buried next to Xun Shuang's tomb.
summary:
Confucius stated that human natures are similar but habits diverge greatly, meaning education and environment shape conduct. Virtuous people teach others to cultivate character, overcome dissolute behavior, and be cautious in making friends. During times of chaos, customs became superficial, and some used benevolence and loyalty as tools for personal gain. By Emperor Gaozu's rise, martial advocates emerged, inheriting the style of the four lords—Xinling, Pingyuan, Chunshen, and Mengchang—where people valued loyalty and vengeance. Under Emperor Wu, Confucianism flourished, with scholars debating the Six Arts at Shiqu Pavilion, forming factions based on agreement or disagreement.

When Wang Mang usurped the Han throne, loyal scholars refused to serve him, preferring poverty and seclusion. Although Guangwu revived the Han, the issue of serving in office remained critical. During Emperors Huan and Ling's reigns, eunuchs controlled the government, and scholars considered it shameful to associate with them. Commoners became indignant, and upright scholars freely discussed governance, praising each other and criticizing ministers. This righteous atmosphere spread widely, but eventually led to the disaster of the Party禁锢, as seen with Fan Pang and Zhang Jian.

The party incident began when Emperor Huan, formerly Marquis of Liwu, studied under Zhou Fu and later promoted him. Yin Fangzhi of Henan was also famous, and their guests ridiculed each other, forming factions that divided Ganling into northern and southern parts. Later, Prefect Zongzi of Runan appointed Fan Pang, and Prefect Cheng Jin of Nanyang appointed Cen Ri. Ballads spread to the Imperial College, where over 30,000 students followed leaders Guo Linzong and Jia Weijie, respecting Li Ying, Chen Fan, and Wang Chang. Rumors praised Li Yuanli as a model, Chen Zhongju as fearless, and Wang Shumao as outstanding. Others like the Bohai clan and Fufeng Wei Qiqing dared to speak against the powerful.

Zhang Cheng of Hanoi, skilled in fortune-telling, predicted an amnesty and had his son kill someone. Li Ying, as Henan Yin, arrested and executed Zhang Cheng despite the amnesty. Zhang Cheng's disciple falsely accused Li Ying and others of forming cliques, slandering the court. The emperor arrested over 200 party members, with some escaping. The next year, officials petitioned for reconsideration, and the arrested were sent home but banned from office for life. Thereafter, upright people were abandoned, while the wicked colluded. Those pursuing high integrity praised each other, creating labels: Sanjun (Three Monarchs), Bajun (Eight Heroes), Bagu (Eight Supports), Baji (Eight Guides), and Bachu (Eight Assistants). Dou Wu, Liu Shu, and Chen Fan were Sanjun; Li Ying, Xun Yi, Du Mi, Wang Chang, Liu You, Wei Lang, Zhao Dian, and Zhu were Bajun; Guo Linzong, Zongci, Basu, Xia Fu, Fan Pang, Yin Xun, Cai Yan, and Yangzhi were Bagu; Zhang Jian, Cen Rizhi, Liu Biao, Chen Xiang, Kong Yu, Yuan Kang, Tanfu, and Zhai Chao were Baji; Du Shang, Zhang Miao, Wang Kao, Liu Ru, Hu Muban, Qin Zhou, Fan Xiang, and Wang Zhang were Bachu.

Zhu Bing, a native of Zhang Jian's hometown, wrote to accuse Zhang Jian and twenty-four others of being cronies. Emperor Ling issued an edict to arrest them, but Zhu Bing's name was omitted for secrecy. Cao Jie signaled officials to arrest former party members, and over 100 died in prison. Others escaped or died before capture. Anyone with personal grudges was classified as a clique, and six to seven hundred people were killed, exiled, or banned. In the fifth year of Xiping, Cao Luan wrote to defend party members but was beaten to death. An edict then examined party disciples, old subordinates, and relatives, banning five generations from office. In the second year of Guanghe, He Haishu argued that imprisoning five clans violated laws, and the emperor lifted all prison terms. In the first year of Zhongping, the Yellow Turban rebellion arose, and Lu Qiang warned that long imprisonment might cause party members to join the rebels. The emperor pardoned them, but the government later collapsed. The party incidents lasted over twenty years, affecting all good people in the world.

Liu Shu, from Hejian, studied the Five Classics and taught hundreds of students. He declined multiple invitations but was eventually carried to Luoyang, where he answered the emperor's questions and was appointed Yilang. He advised dismissing eunuchs, but the emperor did not adopt it. After Emperor Ling ascended, eunuchs falsely accused Liu Shu of conspiring with Dou Wu, and he committed suicide in prison.

Li Ying, from Yingchuan, was aloof and regarded Xun Shu and Chen Chen as mentors. He was recommended as Xiaolian and became governor of Qingzhou, where corrupt officials fled upon hearing of his arrival. He later served as Colonel Hu Wuhuan, defeating Xianbei invaders. As Henan Yin, he arrested and executed Zhang Cheng despite the amnesty, angering the emperor. During the party disaster, Li Ying was arrested and tortured to death at age sixty. His wife and children were exiled, and his students were banned from office.

Du Mi, from Yingchuan, was deep and simple. He served as prefect of Daijun and Taishan, arresting eunuchs' sons who committed evil acts. He discovered Zheng Xuan's talent and sent him to study. After the party broke out, he was dismissed and later committed suicide during a party summons.

Liu You, from Zhongshan, was familiar with history and skilled in writing. He exposed crimes of Liang Ji's disciple and removed corrupt officials in Hedong. As Si Li Xiaowei, he confiscated lands occupied by powerful ministers, angering Emperor Huan, who sentenced him to labor. After pardon, he returned to seclusion and died at home, spared from the party massacre.

Wei Lang, from Kuaiji, avenged his brother's murder and studied at Taixue. He served as Jiuzhen Captain, defeating thieves and beheading 2,000. As prefect of Hanoi, his governance was exemplary. During the party disaster, he was dismissed and later committed suicide at Niuzhu.

Xia Fu, from Chenliu, was upright and did not associate with wealthy families. He was framed by eunuchs as a party leader. While fleeing, he cut his beard, changed his appearance, and worked as a servant in a smelting family for years. His brother discovered him, but Xia Fu left at dawn and died before the party ban was lifted.

Zongci, from Nanyang, refused multiple government summons. He served as a military commander but abandoned his post when the prefect was corrupt. He died on the road while being summoned as Yilang.

Basu, from Bohai, conspired with Dou Wu and Chen Fan to kill eunuchs. After their failure, he was banned from office. Cao Jie arrested him, and Basu surrendered himself, saying he would not escape punishment. He was killed, and the governor carved a stone to record his deeds.

Fan Pang, from Runan, was appointed envoy to investigate thieves in Jizhou. He exposed corrupt officials and was praised for his integrity. During the party disaster, he was imprisoned and tortured. After release, he returned south but was later arrested again. His mother encouraged him to die for a good reputation, and he was executed at age thirty-three.

Yin Xun, from Henan, adhered to integrity despite his family's power. He participated in killing Liang Ji and was granted marquis. He wrote to explain Fan Pang's case but was later imprisoned and committed suicide due to Dou Wu's incident.

Cai Yan, from Runan, was proficient in Confucian classics and mediated village disputes. He refused to nominate a eunuch's relative and impeached corrupt officials. He died of illness after Emperor Ling ascended.

Yangzhi, from Taishan, was upright and knowledgeable. He reported corruption cases and recommended honest officials. He suppressed powerful people as Henan Yin but was removed during the party disaster and died at home.

Zhang Jian, from Shanyang, exposed Hou Lan's crimes but was framed by Zhu Bing. He fled for his life, with many houses sheltering him despite the risk of execution. Dozens were killed for hiding him. After the party ban was lifted, he returned home and shared his wealth with villagers. He died at age eighty-four during Jian'an.

Cen Hao, from Nanyang, studied at Taixue and befriended Guo Linzong. He served as a meritorious officer under Wang Jin, arresting and killing over 200 corrupt individuals. Emperor Huan imprisoned Wang Jin, and Cen Hao fled, later dying in the Jiangxia Mountains.

Chen Xiang, from Runan, reported Liang Ji's disrespect and was promoted to governor of Yangzhou. He expelled corrupt officials but was imprisoned during the party disaster. He was exonerated and died at home.

Kong Yu, from Lu, studied "Shang Shu" and refused Liang Ji's summons. He was banned from office due to the party disaster and later died at home after serving as Luoyang magistrate.

Yuan Kang, from Bohai, was strict as Taishan prefect, returning stolen lands. He arrested Hou Lan's clan guests hiding in Taishan. Hou Lan falsely accused him, and Yuan Kang was sentenced to death but later pardoned. He died at home.

Tanfu, from Shanyin, was poor but had high ambitions. He taught hundreds of students and refused multiple summons. He died at home at age eighty.

Liu Ru, from Dongjun, was intelligent despite stuttering. He wrote ten articles on governance but was imprisoned and committed suicide after Dou Wu's incident.

Jia Biao, from Yingchuan, was known for his integrity. As Xinxi magistrate, he punished those who did not raise children and stopped infanticide. During the party disaster, he appealed to Dou Wu and Huo, leading to the party members' pardon. He refused to shelter Cen Hao and was banned from office, dying at home.

He Yong, from Nanyang, avenged his friend's father and fled after Chen Fan and Li Ying's failure. He secretly helped many escape the party disaster. After the disaster ended, he was recruited but refused Dong Zhuo's offer. He conspired to kill Dong Zhuo but died of sorrow and anger after arrest. He once praised Cao Cao as the one to pacify the world.

Feng Yi, also known as Gongsun, was a native of Fucheng County, Yingchuan County.
He loves reading and is familiar with Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and Sun Tzu's Art of War.
When the Han army rose, Feng Yi supervised the five counties as a county magistrate, and guarded the city together with Miao Meng, the magistrate of Fucheng County, to resist the Han army for Wang Mang.
Guangwu took over the territory of Yingchuan, unable to attack his father's city, and stationed troops in Dongxiang.
Feng Yiwei traveled to the county and was captured by Han soldiers.
At that time, Feng Yi's cousin Feng Xiao and fellow county residents Ding Jinlin and Lu Yan all followed Guangwu, so they jointly recommended Feng Yi and was summoned by Guangwu.
Feng Yi said: My role alone is not enough to make people stronger or weaker.
There is an old mother in the city who is willing to go back and occupy five cities to repay her kindness with her service. Guangwu said: OK. Feng Yi went back and said to Miao Meng: "Now all the generals are strong men, most of them are tyrannical and tyrannical. Only General Liu does not plunder wherever he goes."
Judging from his words and deeds, he is not a mediocre person, so he can surrender to him. Miao Meng said: I live and die with you, and I respectfully listen to your opinions. When Guangwu returned to Wan in the south, more than ten people from Gengshi generals led their troops to attack the father city, but Feng Yi could not hold on. When Guangwu became the commander of the Sili school and passed by the father city, Feng Yi and others opened the door and offered cattle and wine to welcome him.
Guangwu ordered Feng Yi to be the principal for the time being, and Miao Meng to be the principal.
Feng Yi then recommended Yaoqi, Shushou, Duan Jian, Zuo Long and others from Tongyi. Guangwu all made them his governors and followed him to Luoyang.
Gengshi wanted to send Guangwu to capture Hebei several times, but all the generals thought it was impossible.
At this time, Cao Xu, the son of Cao Jing, the prime minister of the left, was the minister, and the father and son were in power. Feng Yi persuaded Guangwu to make a good marriage with them.
Later, when he crossed the Yellow River and headed north, Cao Xu helped him a lot.
Since Guangwu's brother Bosheng was killed by Gengshi, Guangwu did not dare to show his sadness. He often lived alone, did not eat food and wine, and often cried on his pillow and mat.
Feng Yi kowtowed to Guangwu alone to comfort him and comfort him.
Guangwu stopped him and said, "Don't talk nonsense." Feng Yi therefore took the opportunity again and said to Guangwu: "The whole world suffers from Wang Mang and has been thinking about the Han Dynasty for a long time."
Now Gengshi's generals are rampaging and tyrannizing the civilians, plundering wherever they go, leaving the people disappointed and unable to support anyone. summary:
Feng Yi, also known as Gongsun, was from Fucheng County, Yingchuan. He was well-read in the Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and Sun Tzu's Art of War. When the Han army rose, he served as a county magistrate and defended the city for Wang Mang alongside Miao Meng. Guangwu (Liu Xiu) captured Yingchuan but could not take Fucheng. Feng Yi was captured by Han soldiers while traveling. His cousin Feng Xiao and others recommended him to Guangwu. Feng Yi offered to return to the city and secure five counties in exchange for service. He persuaded Miao Meng to surrender to Guangwu, noting that Guangwu did not plunder like other generals. When Guangwu passed by, Feng Yi and Miao Meng opened the gates and welcomed him with gifts. Guangwu appointed Feng Yi as a principal, and Feng Yi recommended several others for positions.

Feng Yi advised Guangwu to build ties with Cao Xu, which proved helpful when Guangwu crossed the Yellow River northward. After Guangwu's brother Bosheng was killed, Feng Yi comforted him and urged him to act independently, perform kindness, and win over the people. When Wang Lang rebelled, Guangwu fled south, and Feng Yi provided him with bean porridge and other food during the harsh journey. Feng Yi was later made a partial general and granted the title of Marquis Ying after defeating Wang Lang. He was known for his humility, often hiding under a tree during discussions of merit, earning the nickname "General Big Tree." His troops were loyal to him, and Guangwu valued him highly.

Feng Yi wrote to Li Yi, a general under Gengshi, urging him to surrender by citing historical examples of those who changed allegiances. Li Yi, though hesitant due to past conflicts with Guangwu, agreed to stop fighting. This allowed Feng Yi to pacify several counties. Guangwu later revealed Li Yi's letter to Zhu Kun, who assassinated Li Yi in anger. Zhu Kun then attacked Feng Yi but was defeated. After Gengshi's fall, Feng Yi advised Guangwu to ascend the throne, citing a dream as divine will. In the second year of Jianwu, Feng Yi was made Marquis of Yangxia and sent to pacify the three auxiliary regions, where he defeated Chimei and other bandits.

Feng Yi faced Chimei in Huayin, fighting for over sixty days. Despite initial setbacks, he used an ambush strategy, dressing his troops like Chimei to cause confusion, and defeated them, forcing 80,000 to surrender. He then pacified Guanzhong, defeating various bandit leaders like Yancen and Zhang Han. Feng Yi governed with justice, recruiting people and redressing grievances. When rumors arose that he was acting arrogantly, Guangwu showed him the accusations, and Feng Yi wrote a humble apology, reaffirming his loyalty. Guangwu reassured him of their bond.

In the sixth year of Jianwu, Feng Yi visited the capital and was honored by Guangwu, who recalled his past aid. Feng Yi requested that Guangwu remember their shared hardships. He later defended the city of Xun against Wei Xiao's forces, using a surprise attack to defeat them. He continued to pacify the north, defeating Lu Fang and the Xiongnu. In the ninth year, he took command of Ji Zun's troops and fought against Wei Xiao's son and Gongsun Shu's forces. Feng Yi fell ill and died in the army, receiving the posthumous title of Jiehou. His descendants inherited his title, though some were later revoked and restored.

Cen Peng, courtesy name Junran, was from Jiyang County, Nanyang. During Wang Mang's reign, he served as a county magistrate. After the Han army rose, he was captured but later fled to Wan, where he defended the city with Yan Shuo. When food ran out, he advocated surrender. He was spared and made a marquis, serving under various leaders. He eventually joined Guangwu, who pardoned him after he explained his past. Cen Peng persuaded others to surrender and was appointed as an assassin general, helping to pacify Hebei.

After Guangwu became emperor, Cen Peng was made a court lieutenant and marquis. He besieged Luoyang with other generals and persuaded Zhu Kun to surrender by promising safety. Zhu Kun surrendered, and Guangwu kept his word. Cen Peng then attacked Jingzhou, capturing several cities. He fought against Qin Feng and Deng Feng, eventually defeating them with Guangwu's help. Cen Peng was made Marquis of Wuyin and continued to campaign in the south, defeating Tian Rong and other rebels. He established control over Jiangnan, receiving tributes from various prefects.

In the sixth year of Jianwu, Cen Peng was summoned to the capital and honored. He later fought in the west against Wei Xiao, but the campaign stalled due to food shortages. In the ninth year, Gongsun Shu's forces attacked, and Cen Peng built warships to counter them. In the eleventh year, he led a large force to Jingmen, using fire ships to destroy the enemy's pontoon bridges. He advanced into Shu, winning battles and winning over the people. However, he was assassinated by a fake slave at his camp. He was given the posthumous title of Zhuanghou, and the Shu people built a temple in his honor. His descendants inherited his title, though some were later revoked.

Jia Fu, courtesy name Junwen, was from Champion County, Nanyang. He studied the Book of Documents and was recognized as having the potential to be a general. During Wang Mang's reign, he gathered followers and joined Liu Jia, but left to join Guangwu in Hebei. Guangwu appointed him as a general, and he proved his bravery in battle, often leading charges. He was seriously wounded but recovered, and Guangwu promised to unite their families through marriage. Jia Fu fought in many campaigns, including against Zhu Kun and Chimei, and was known for his courage, though he rarely boasted of his achievements.

After Guangwu became emperor, Jia Fu was made a marquis and continued to fight, defeating Yin Zun and others. He was known for his humility and did not claim credit. In the thirteenth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Jiaodong. He later retired from military affairs to promote Confucianism, as Guangwu sought to end warfare. Jia Fu was one of the few meritorious officials allowed to discuss state affairs. He died in the thirty-first year of Jianwu, receiving the posthumous title of Ganghou. His descendants inherited his title, though some were later revoked and restored.

The historian comments that among the ZTE generals, Feng Yi and Cen Peng achieved the greatest feats, particularly in the west and south. Feng Yi and Jia Fu were humble and did not take credit, while Cen Peng's loyalty inspired his troops. The text notes that Feng Yi avoided disaster by leaving a place with an ominous name, while Cen Peng was unable to do so and met his end, suggesting that fate may play a role in such matters.

I feel depressed and have nowhere to complain, and I want to say it but I'm afraid of shocking others. Swallow the tears into your belly.

The mother's voice breaks her heart when she cries, and she covers her ears and dare not listen.

Thinking back on how heartless I was, my heart was filled with sorrow. Endless lamentation.
I always feel happy when I hear that there are guests from out of town.
When greeting guests to inquire about news, they are not from their hometown. Unexpectedly, his wish came true unexpectedly, and his relatives came to greet him.
He was able to escape the suffering, but he had to leave his son behind.
Relatives are naturally connected by heart, and there will be no time to meet again when they think of separation.

Mother is usually very kind, why is she not kind now?
I haven't grown up yet, why doesn't my mother think about it carefully?
Seeing this scene, my whole body was burning, my mind was in a daze and I was about to go crazy.
Crying and stroking her son, she was about to go on the road but hesitated again.
In addition, people who came at the same time came to say goodbye and see each other off.
They envied me for being able to go home alone, and their cries of sorrow were heartbreaking.
The horse was moved and hesitated, and the wheel stopped turning.
The people watching were crying and sobbing, and the pedestrians on the road were also crying softly. They cut off their love as they walked farther and farther, and the journey became farther and farther.
Three thousand miles away, when will we meet again?
Thinking of my biological son, my heart was filled with grief.
After arriving home, I found out that all my family members were dead and that I had no close relatives.
The city walls turned into mountains and forests, and thorns and wormwood grew in the courtyards.
There were bones of unknown persons everywhere, lying horizontally and vertically, none of them covered.
When I went out I heard no sound of people, only the howling of jackals.
Standing alone in front of the lonely figure, shocked, sad and heartbroken.

Entrust yourself to your newly married husband and encourage yourself with all your heart.

My son called for his mother but couldn't cry. I covered my ears and couldn't bear to hear him.

summary:
The moral and virtuous deeds of women from historical records, compiled into "Lienv Pian" since the ZTE period. It includes biographies of notable women, emphasizing their conduct and contributions.

Bao Xuan's wife, Shaojun, married him despite his poverty, returned her dowry, and lived frugally, earning praise for her virtue. Wang Ba's wife encouraged him to maintain his integrity over worldly honors, leading him to a life of seclusion. Jiang Shi's wife fetched river water for her mother-in-law daily, and when sent away, secretly provided food through a neighbor. Her filial piety moved bandits to spare her family, and she was later honored.

Zhou Yu's wife, Zhao A, committed suicide after her father-in-law blamed her for her husband's rudeness, unable to correct him. Ban Zhao, a learned widow, completed the "Book of Han" and advised Empress Dowager Deng on political matters, including accepting General Deng Zhi's retirement. She wrote "Female Commandments" and died at seventy, mourned by the empress dowager.

Leyangzi's wife urged her husband to return found gold and complete his studies, cutting cloth to illustrate wasted effort. She supported her mother-in-law and died defending her honor from robbers. Cheng Wenju's wife, Mu Jiang, treated her stepchildren kindly, leading them to reform and become virtuous. Cao E, a filial daughter, drowned seeking her father's body and was honored with a monument.

Wu Xusheng's wife, Lu Rong, supported her mother-in-law, encouraged her husband to study, and avenged his death. She died resisting bandits. Yuan Wei's wife, Ma Lun, defended her family's wealth and her father's reputation, matching her husband's wit. Pang Ao's mother, Zhao E, avenged her father's murder after years, surrendered, and was pardoned.

Liu Changqing's wife mutilated her ear to avoid remarriage after her son's death, earning recognition for chastity. Huangfu Gui's wife cursed Dong Zhuo for his atrocities and was beaten to death, later honored. Yin Yu's wife, Xun Cai, resisted remarriage and hanged herself after being forced to Guo's house. Shengdao's wife, Yuanjiang, took her husband's place in prison, allowing his escape, and was executed.

The filial daughter Uncle Xianxiong drowned herself after her father's death, emerging with his body. Dong Si's wife, Cai Wenji, was captured by Xiongnu, bore children, and was ransomed by Cao Cao. She saved her husband from execution and recited ancient texts from memory. Her poems recount her suffering and loss. The text praises these women's virtues and deeds.
