◆The biography of Liu Ping, named Gongzi, was from Pengcheng, Chu County.
His real name was Kuang, but it was changed to Ping after he became emperor.
During Wang Mang's time, he became a county official, guarding the Qiu chief, and flourished in politics and religion.
Later, when there were thieves in each county, Liu Ping was sent to guard them. Wherever he went, he was controlled. From then on, every county praised his ability.
During the Gengshi period, the world was in chaos, and Liu Ping's younger brother Liu Zhong was killed by thieves.
Later, the thieves suddenly arrived. Liu Ping supported his mother and ran away.
Liu Zhong's posthumous daughter was only one year old. Liu Ping embraced Zhong's daughter and abandoned his biological son.
The mother wanted to go back to get her son, but Liu Ping refused to listen and said: "I cannot support two children, and the second child cannot have offspring." So he left without caring, and hid in Nozawa with his mother.
Liu Ping went out to look for food in the morning. He met a hungry thief and was about to cook him. Liu Ping kowtowed and said, "I will find some wild vegetables for my mother to satisfy her hunger this morning. My mother is waiting for me to survive. I wish I could go back first. When my mother finishes eating, I will definitely come back and let you kill her."
So the tears continued. The thief saw that he was sincere, sympathized with him and let him go home.
When Liu Ping went back, after his mother finished eating, he said to his mother: "I just made an appointment with a thief, so I can't deceive others."
So he returned to the thief. Everyone was shocked and talked to each other: "I often hear about martyrs, but today I actually saw them."
Just go away, we can't bear to eat you. As a result, Liu Ping's life was saved.
In the early years of Jianwu, General Pang Meng of Pingdi made troops in Pengcheng and defeated the governor of the county, Sun Meng.
Liu Ping was working as a county official at that time. He risked his life by lying on Sun Meng's body and suffered seven stab wounds. He was so trapped that he didn't know what to do, so he cried and begged: "I am willing to replace the king with my body." The thieves gathered their weapons and stopped killing, saying, "This man is a righteous man, don't kill him." So dismissed and walked away.
Sun Meng was seriously injured and died. After a while, he came back to life. He was thirsty and looked for water. Liu Ping took blood from his own wound and gave it to him to drink.
After a few days, Sun Meng finally died, so Liu Ping bandaged the stab wound, helped carry Sun Meng's coffin, and sent it back to the county.
Later, Liu Ping was promoted to Xiaolian and became the Prime Minister of Jiyin County. The prefect Liu Yu attached great importance to him and appointed him to the county position.
When the mourning clothes are full, Quanjiao Chang is awarded.
People are grateful for political favors. Some increase wages or taxes, and some reduce the age and enter the service earlier.
The governor and the prefect came to inspect, but there were no prisoners in the prison. Everyone was in his place, and he didn't know what to ask. He just issued the edict and left.
Later he was dismissed due to illness.
In the early years of Emperor Xianzong's reign, Shangshu Pushe Zhongliyi wrote a letter recommending Liu Ping, Wang Wang of Langfu, and Fu Dao, King of Donglai: I personally saw that Liu Kuang, Wang Wang of Langfu, and Fu Wang of Donglai were both seventy years old.
I don't understand them well enough, I just envy them for promoting talented people. In the memorial, there was an edict to recruit Liu Ping and others, and they were given special money to do the work.
After arriving at the imperial court, they all worshiped him as Yilang and were introduced to him many times. Liu Ping was promoted to minister again, and in the third year of Yongping he was promoted to Zongzheng. He recommended famous scholars such as Chenggong and Xun Xun several times.
After eight years in office, Shangshu asked to retire and go home due to old age and illness, and died at home. ◆Zhao Xiaozhuan, Zhao Xiao was named Changnian and was from Peiguoqi.
His father, Zhao Pu, served as General Tianhe during Wang Mang's reign and appointed Zhao Xiao as Lang.
Every time I go home on leave, I often walk in white clothes and carry my own luggage.
I once returned home from Chang'an and wanted to stay overnight at the post office.
The chief of the pavilion first heard that Zhao Xiaohui was passing by and thought that an elderly guest was coming, so he swept the room and waited.
When Zhao Xiao arrived, he did not announce his name. The pavilion chief refused to accommodate him, so he asked: "I heard that the son of General Tian He is coming from Chang'an. When will he arrive?" Zhao Xiao said: It will arrive soon. So he left.
Later, the world was in chaos, and people were eating people.
Zhao Xiao's younger brother Zhao Li was captured by a hungry thief. When Zhao Xiao heard about it, he tied himself up and went to the thief, saying: "Zhao Li has been hungry for a long time and is very thin. He is not as fat as me." The thieves were shocked, so they released them and said to their brothers: "You can go home temporarily and get some food." Zhao Xiao searched for food but failed to find it, so he went back and told the thieves that he was willing to let them cook food.
Everyone found it strange and did not harm him.
The township party admired his loyalty.
When recruiting from prefectures and counties, etiquette must be observed when advancing or retreating.
He was promoted to be filial and honest, so he should not be drafted.
During the Yongping period, he was drafted into the Taiwei Mansion. Xianzong had always heard that Zhao Xiao had good conduct, and issued an edict to grant him the title of admonishing the officials. He was promoted to the rank of Attendant, and then to the rank of Changle Guardsman.
He also called his younger brother Zhao Li to be the censor Zhongcheng.
Zhao Li was also respectful, modest and restrained himself, similar to Zhao Xiao.
The emperor commended their brothers for their virtue and wanted to treat them specially. Zhao Li was ordered to go to Weiwei's Mansion once every ten days, and the eunuch delivered the offerings and told them to have a good time together.
A few years later, Zhao Li died, and the emperor ordered Zhao Xiao to attend the funeral and bury him as an official.
More than a year later, he returned home on leave from the Weiwei. Died at home. ◆ Chunyu Gongzhuan, Chunyu Gong's courtesy name is Meng Sun, Chunyu Ren in Beihai.
He is good at speaking about "Laozi", he is quiet and does not envy fame.
There are fruit trees in the mountains at home. If someone steals the fruit, he will help him harvest it.
He also saw someone stealing seedlings. Chun Yugong was worried that others would be ashamed, so he hid in the grass and waited for the thief to leave before coming out. The villagers were moved.
In Wang Mang's last years, there was famine and war. Chun Yugong's brother Chun Yuchong was about to be cooked by bandits. Chun Yugong asked to be replaced, and both of them were spared from death.
Later, Chunyu Chong died. Chunyu Gong raised his orphans and children, and taught them to learn. If they did not follow the law, he would beat himself with a stick to make the children understand. The children were indeed ashamed and changed their ways. At the beginning, thieves invaded, and the people could not engage in farming. Chunyugong often plowed the fields alone. The villagers tried to dissuade him, saying: The current situation is in great chaos, and life and death are still unknown. Why work in vain and ask for trouble? Chunyu Gong said: Even if I can't gain anything, what loss will it cause to others? Keep on plowing.
Later, the states and counties called for continuous recruitment, but none of them responded. So he lived in seclusion to cultivate his ambition, hiding in the mountains and rivers.
Every move and every turn of the week must be done according to etiquette.
During the Jianwu period, the county promoted him as a filial and honest person, and Sikong promoted him, but he was not worthy. The guest lived in seclusion in Langfu, Guizhou, and Zou Mountains for several decades.
In the first year of Jianchu's reign, Emperor Suzong issued an edict praising Chunyu Gong for his ordinary conduct, notifying the county to grant him twenty pieces of silk, dispatching a public carriage, and worshiping him as a counselor.
The introduction lasted a whole day, asking him many political questions, and promoted him to the rank of captain of the cavalry in the palace. He was treated with great courtesy.
All the famous people he recommended were recruited by the imperial court.
In the court, he always responded to the political affairs presented by the emperor based on morality. There was not a single conversation between the emperor and him without a good word.
Five years later, he became seriously ill, and the emperor sent people to express condolences. He died in his official position.
The imperial edict was written with praise and praise, and he was given a thousand dendrobium grains and carved stones in the palace to commend him.
His son was given the title of filial piety and the title of Prince Sheren.
◆Jiang Ge's biography, Jiang Ge's courtesy name was Cweng, and he was a native of Linzi, Qi State.
His father died when he was young, and he lived alone with his mother.
When the world was in chaos and thieves broke out, Jiang Ge fled with his mother on his back. He encountered many dangers and often picked wild fruits to survive.
Several times he met thieves, and some wanted to kidnap him. Jiang Ge cried and begged, saying that his mother relied on him to support him. His tone was very sincere and touching.
The thief couldn't bear to invade him, and someone even showed him where to escape, so both mother and son had to survive the disaster safely.
When Jiang Ge arrived in Xiapi, he was so poor that he was barefoot and shirtless. He relied on working to support his mother. He tried his best to provide the necessary things around him.
In the last years of Jianwu, he returned to his hometown with his mother.
At the end of every year, interviews were held in the county. Jiang Ge didn't want to move around because his mother was there, so he pulled the cart by himself in the shaft without using oxen or horses. From then on, the village called him "Jiang Da Duozi".
The prefect once prepared a gift to invite him, but Jiang Ge refused because his mother was old.
After his mother's death, his true nature was about to be extinct. He used to sleep next to the tomb, and when the mourning period expired, he couldn't bear to get rid of her.
The county governor sent a minister to take off his mourning clothes and asked him to become an official.
In the early years of Yongping, Jiang Ge was promoted to Xiaolian and was awarded the title of Taipu of Chu.
After more than a month, he voluntarily abandoned his official position and left.
Chu Wangying sent people to chase him quickly and refused to go back.
He also asked his master to give him gifts, but he refused to accept them.
Later, I went several times in response to Sangong's orders.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Taiwei Mou Rong promoted virtuous and upright people, and Jiang Ge was promoted to Sikong Changshi again.
Suzong treated him with great respect and courtesy, and promoted him to the rank of General of the Five Features.
During every court meeting, the emperor often sent tiger tigers to assist him, and often kept an eye on him when he came to worship.
At this time, Jiang Ge was ill and could not attend court, so the emperor sent an eunuch to bring him wine and food. The favor was very special.
Therefore, Ma Liao, a noble of the capital, and Dou Xian, a lieutenant in the capital, were envious of Jiang Ge's character, and each sent him letters and gifts. Jiang Ge neither replied nor accepted gifts.
The emperor praised him even more.
Later, Jiang Ge wrote a letter requesting to retire and return to his hometown. The imperial court turned him into an admonishing doctor and granted him the title of "Resigning to his hometown." However, Xie fell seriously ill.
During the Yuanhe period, the emperor missed Jiang Ge's good conduct and drafted an edict to Prime Minister Qi: I would like to advise the doctor Jiang Ge. He returned home due to illness. How is his daily life now?
Filial piety is the first of all actions and the beginning of all good deeds.
Whenever the country misses people with lofty ideals, they always think of Jiang Ge.
The county was ordered to use Dendrobium dendrobium as a gift to Juxiao. Every August, officials were sent to express condolences and give him sheep wine until his lifetime.
If something unfortunate happens, use the middle prison to offer sacrifices. From then on, the title of "Ju Xiao" became popular all over the world.
After his death, the imperial edict granted him a thousand dendrobium grains.
◆Liu Banchuan, also known as Liu Banxing, was the great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan.
Emperor Xuan granted his son Liu Xiao to Chu, making him the Xiaowang.
The filial king gave birth to Wang Yan, which gave rise to Wang Yu, and Yu gave rise to commonness.
From Liu Xiao to Liu Ban, they accumulated benevolence and righteousness, and were famous for generations, and Liu Yu was especially kind and kind.
His mother died in his early years, and his brother Hou Ping from Yuanxiang was still young. Liu Yu raised him personally and often slept and ate with him.
When he became a man, he never left his side.
After Liu Ping died of illness, Liu Yu cried and vomited blood and died a few months later.
At first, Liu Yu was granted a title by the king, but when Wang Mang usurped the throne, he was deposed as an ordinary citizen and lived in Pengcheng.
Liu Ban's father died when he was several years old, and he lived alone with his mother.
Wang Mang failed and the world was in chaos. When Tai Fu heard that Emperor Gengshi had ascended the throne, she went to Chang'an with Liu Ban.
When Gengshi failed, he and Liu Ban turned around during the military revolution. They traveled westward to Long and lived in Wuwei.
Although Liu Ban was young, he was determined to cultivate his moral character and never neglected to recite poems and books.
His mother and uncles believed that living in a remote area, where life and death were unpredictable, they should not study hard and meditate like this. They preached to Liu Ban several times, but Liu Ban still did not change his career.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, Kuai Xiao was defeated and Hexi was able to communicate with the mainland. Liu Ban moved his family east to Luoyang and studied Confucian classics under his teacher.
In the second year, Emperor Guangwu issued an edict, conferring Liu Ban the title of Qiuhou, enshrining him as King Xiao, and sending him to the capital.
Later, because the country belonged to the King of Chu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Zhu Qiu.
In the 19th year, the emperor came to Pei and issued an imperial edict to inquire about the character and talents of the princes in the county.
The eunuch recommended Liu Ban, saying that he practiced well and could serve as a model for the princes.
After hearing this, the emperor commended him, so he gave Liu Ban a ribbon, millions of dollars, and hundreds of pieces of silk work.
Twenty years later, he met the driver again in Pei, so he followed the emperor back to Luoyang, gave him grain and other things, and left him as a minister of the temple.
In the first year of Yongping, the country belonged to Pei and he was granted the title of Chaohou.
For several years, Yangzhou Governor Guan Xun recommended Liu Ban to the country. He did not speak unchosen words and acted without any resentment. He should be commended.
Xianzong commended him.
In the tenth year, Liu Ban was summoned to carry out the duties of Jinwu. He went from the emperor to Nanyang and came back to become a court prince.
Next year, he will also serve as the captain of the cavalry school.
At that time, the officials of the five schools were idle, and the houses in the temples were spacious, the carriages and uniforms were clean and gorgeous, and they were well equipped with skills. Therefore, most of them were occupied by clan members and relatives of the emperor.
Every time the holy chariot went out to inspect the country, Liu Ban often sent Hu from Changshui to follow him.
The emperor once wanted to set up Changpingcang, and the ministers thought it was very convenient.
Liu Ban believed that Changpingcang had the reputation of benefiting the people on the outside, but it actually harmed the people on the inside. The wealthy gentry used excuses to cause trouble, and the common people could not benefit from it. It was not necessarily convenient to set up it.
The emperor stopped.
At this time, the imperial court issued an order prohibiting people from engaging in two professions, that is, farmers were not allowed to engage in business. In addition, due to the rinderpest outbreak in the county, farming was implemented in separate areas, and when officials went to inspect, most of the results were inconsistent with the actual situation, making the people very worried.
Liu Banshang said: Due to the official ban on two industries in the county, people with land were not allowed to fish or hunt.
Nowadays, most of the counties along the rivers and lakes plant mulberry and raise silkworms. The people supplement their food rations by fishing and hunting. Besides, there are leisure months in spring, which does not affect farming.
The benefits of fishing and hunting, removing pests from the fields, and contributing to grain production have nothing to do with engaging in the two professions.
In addition, due to cattle epidemic, floods and droughts in the county and cultivated land were reduced, so the edict was issued to order planting in separate areas and to increase the number of acres for the benefit of the people.
However, the officials organized field cultivation in order to increase the yield compared with the previous year, so they also rented out the areas that were not used for farming.
You can order the governor and two thousand stones to be verified. If there is an increase, it will be the same crime as seizing the land. The emperor obeyed them all.
After Suzong ascended the throne, Liu Ban was appointed as the Shaofu of Changle.
In the second year of Jianchu, he was promoted to Zongzheng.
When Liu Ban's wife died, the court gave her many gifts and gave her a cemetery under the Xianjie Mausoleum.
Liu Ban discussed political affairs many times during his reign. His actions in recuperating the nine tribes were particularly significant, and people at the time praised him very much. He died in the third year of Jianchu at the age of sixty.
◆In the biography of Zhou Pan, Zhou Pan's courtesy name was Jianbo, and he was an adult in Runan. A member of the same tribe as the conqueror Zhou Xie.
His grandfather Zhou Ye was the prefect of Tianshui in the early years of Jianwu.
Zhou Pan traveled to the capital when he was young and studied "Guwen Shangshu", "Five Elements of Hong Fan" and "Zuo Shi Zhuan". He liked to talk about etiquette and had good conduct. He would not speak anything that was not in line with the classics. Most Confucian students regarded him as their master.
The family was poor, and it was not enough to support his mother.
I once recited "Poetry" to the last chapter of "Ru Tomb", which was very generous and lamentable, so I dismissed Wei Dai and participated in the recommendation of Xiaolian.
In the early years of Emperor He's reign, he paid homage to him, was appointed city mayor, and was promoted to magistrate of Yangcheng and Chonghe counties. He experienced good political achievements in the three cities. Later, he missed his mother and abandoned his official position and returned to his hometown.
When his mother died, her body was almost destroyed by grief, and her mourning period expired, so she took up residence next to the grave.
The professor often has thousands of disciples.
The government called Zhou Pan three times, and they all thought Zhou Pan was a virtuous man and invited him to come out. Zhou Pan said to his friends: In the past, Fang Hui and Zhifu rejected Yao and Shun and rested their minds at home, not disturbing their health care for glory and profit.
My mother is dead, why do I need foreign objects? So he didn't apply.
In the first year of Jianguang, he was seventy-three years old. Every New Year's Day, the court gathered all the students and gave lectures all day long. So he said to his two sons: The day before yesterday, I dreamed that my master, Mr. Dongli, was talking to me in the underworld. Then he sighed and said: Is my age already over?
If the tomb coffin is large enough to contain the body at the end of life, the outer coffin can be used to hold the inner coffin. Wrap it in clothes and hang it directly into the tomb. Use washed clothes and a scarf. Weave a two-foot-four-inch long bamboo slip and copy an article from "Yao Canon", together with a knife and pen, and place them in front of the coffin to show that you have not forgotten the holy way.
On the 15th of this month, he died without illness. Scholars believe that he was a man who understood destiny.
◆Zhao Zichuan, named Wenchu, was from Yan in Dongjun.
His father, Zhao Chang, has a doctorate.
Zhao Zi's father died when he was young. He behaved filially and was recommended by the prefectures and counties as filial and honest, but he refused.
In the first year of Yanxi's reign, Chen Qi, the chief minister, recommended Zhao Zi, saying that he was extremely filial and moral, so he was promoted to a doctorate.
In the early years of Emperor Ling's reign, Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were killed by eunuchs, so Zhao Zi resigned due to illness.
Taiwei Yang Ci specially invited him and asked him to use a scarf as jewelry and not add a crown to go in and give lectures to everyone.
Later, he was promoted to high rank and became the governor of Dunhuang several times.
Later, he was dismissed from his post due to illness and returned home, where he personally led his children and grandchildren to make a living in the fields.
One time, robbers came to his house at night to rob him. Zhao Zi was afraid of disturbing his mother, so he went to the door to greet the robbers. The robbers asked him to prepare meals. He declined and said, "My mother is eighty years old. She is sick and needs treatment. The family is very poor and has no food for shelter. Please leave some clothes and food." Apart from his wife, he had nothing. The robbers felt ashamed and sighed, knelt down and said goodbye: "We are too rude and should not intrude on the wise man."
After saying that, they all ran away.
Zhao Zi chased them out to give them something, but failed to catch up.
It became even more famous from then on. The imperial court summoned Yi Lang to pay homage to him, but he was unable to do so. He issued an imperial edict and reprimanded him, and the prefectures and counties greeted him with courtesy. He went back and forth several times before going to answer the call as a last resort.
He also worshiped Zhao Zi as the Prime Minister of the East China Sea.
When he was going to take office, he passed by Xingyang. The county magistrate Dunhuang Cao Fan and Zhao Zi's old Xiaolian were waiting for him on the roadside. So he dropped his seal and ribbon and pursued him to the East China Sea.
After meeting Zhao Zi, he resigned and returned home.
This is how he was valued by people at that time.
When Zhao Zi was an official, he was honest and simple. He paid his salary according to his time. The powerful party was afraid of his frugality.
After serving as an official for three years, he asked to be dismissed due to illness and was appointed as Yilang.
He arrived in the capital while ill, and when he was about to die, he sued his former officials Zhu Zhi, Xiao Jian and others, asking them to use a thin plain coffin and pad it with loess, hoping that the body would decay quickly and return to the earth as soon as possible, and not let his descendants change their plans.
So he wrote a suicide note to his son Zhao Yin and said: "Human beings are alive and must die. This is the decree of heaven and earth, and it is the natural end."
Therefore, wise people see life clearly and believe that life and death are like darkness and light, and life and death are like morning and evening. Therefore, they do not pursue entertainment when they are alive, and they do not feel sad when they die.
The so-called death is just that the vitality leaves the body and the soul wanders everywhere, returning to the original state and returning to nothing. It has disappeared and returned to the dung.
The soil is discarded. Does it still have a nature? Do you want to regulate its thickness and regulate its dryness and moisture?
It's just that the living people can't bear to see the bodies of their loved ones destroyed, so they have to bury the bones.
"Book of Changes" says: In ancient times, those who were buried were clothed with salary and hidden in the middle of the field. The saints of later generations buried them in coffins and coffins. The production of coffins began with the Yellow Emperor.
From the Tao and Tang Dynasties, to the Yu and Xia Dynasties, simplicity was still advocated, some using tiles and some using wood. It was only in the Yin and Shang Dynasties that the number increased.
Inherited from the Zhou Dynasty, the system has two generations.
They also added decorations such as wall wings, used inscriptions to indicate the identity of the deceased, paid attention to etiquette such as including rice, selected the date of the funeral tomb, selected the coffin and used it, and the quilts were also divided into grades and layers. This kind of thing is cumbersome and impractical, and the goods are trivial and difficult to obtain.
However, there are different levels of official rank.
Below Zicheng and Kang, the regulations are slightly different.
During the Warring States Period, it gradually declined, the laws were relaxed, and the upper and lower levels were out of position.
Finally, the Marquis of Jin asked for a tunnel, Uncle Qin buried a living person, Doctor Chen set up a wooden gate, and Sima of the Song Dynasty built a stone and wooden guo.
When the Qin Dynasty came, it violated morality, abolished the system of the three generations, and instituted lewd and evil methods. The country's wealth was wasted under the three springs, manpower wasted on Li's tombs, good games were wasted on dung, and skills were wasted on the strings.
Since the beginning of the people, there has been no such custom of burying the dead in such a generous manner.
Although Zhongni reaffirmed the Zhou rites and Mozi tried to follow the ancient ways, he still could not resist.
Therefore, Chinese people compete with each other, violate the fundamentals of etiquette, engage in the end of etiquette, advocate luxury, abandon simplicity, use all their family wealth to support each other, abolish life and pay attention to death, ignore health care and only care about rich burials. Is this the original intention of the saints in making rituals?
"Ji" says: Although there are etiquette in funerals, mourning is the main thing. He also said: It is better to mourn than to be sad. This is not the case now. I think it is the way to be filial to the emperor, and to use it to express sympathy for the coffin. This is what I dare not do.
In the past, Emperor Shun was buried in Cangwu, but his two concubines refused to follow him. Is there any chance of getting married and staying in the usual place?
If the Holy Lord and Mingjun are like this, let alone the common people, whose etiquette is beyond their reach.
The ancients said that meetings are the same at the same time, but different at different times. Movements and stillness should be in line with etiquette, and situations should be adapted to local conditions.
The kings and grandsons were buried naked, and the bodies of Mo Yi were exposed in the wild, all of which were based on human nature and rationality and valued rapid change.
Liang Boluan's father died and was buried in a banquet. Even after his death, he did not return to his hometown.
Are these people being unfavorable to their relatives and forgetting the principles of loyalty and filial piety?
What's more, I am not moral and sensitive, I have a weak mind and a bright mind. I have the ambition to admire the ancient sages. I am the same as the ancients, and I am not to blame.
Be sure to carry out a light burial and avoid any suspicion.
I am afraid that what you see with your eyes, stomachs, dogs, and ears will make you want to change the funeral and go against my ambitions. Therefore, I adopt the practices of ancient saints from afar and practice them closely to make you aware.
Just dig a ditch that can accommodate the coffin. Bury the coffin as soon as it is returned. There is no need to build a grave on flat ground. There is no need to choose a date, no need to pay homage, no need to mourn beside the tomb, and no need to plant trees at the head of the tomb.
Woohoo boy, please act with encouragement, I have nothing more to say!
When Zhu Zhi and Xiao Jian arrived home for the funeral, their son Zhao Yin couldn't bear to let his father's body merge with the earth, and wanted to change the burial method. Zhi and Jian told his father's last order, so he followed the instructions. At that time, people said that Zhao Zi was a wise man.
summary:
Biographies of several individuals from the Han dynasty. Liu Ping, originally named Kuang, was from Pengcheng. During Wang Mang's time, he was a county official. During the Gengshi period, when thieves arrived, he fled with his mother, abandoning his own son to save his orphaned niece. He later encountered a hungry thief who wanted to eat him, but Liu Ping begged to feed his mother first and promised to return. The thief, moved by his sincerity, let him go. Liu Ping kept his promise and returned, but the thief spared him. In the early Jianwu years, he risked his life to protect the wounded governor Sun Meng, suffering seven stab wounds and even offering his own blood to the thirsty Sun Meng. Liu Ping was later promoted to Xiaolian and became Prime Minister of Jiyin County. He was later recommended by Zhongliyi and served as Yilang and Zongzheng, recommending famous scholars. He died at home after requesting retirement due to old age and illness.

Zhao Xiao, named Changnian, was from Peiguo. His father served under Wang Mang. Zhao Xiao was known for his humility, traveling in plain clothes. During a famine, his brother Zhao Li was captured by hungry thieves. Zhao Xiao bound himself and went to the thieves, offering his own fatter body in exchange. The thieves released them. He was later recruited and served as an admonishing official and Changle Guardsman. His brother Zhao Li also became an official. The emperor favored them, but Zhao Li died a few years later. Zhao Xiao died at home after returning from leave.

Chunyu Gong, named Meng Sun, was from Beihai. He was a quiet man who studied Laozi. When someone stole his fruit, he helped them harvest it. When he saw a thief stealing seedlings, he hid to avoid shaming him. During a famine, he offered to replace his brother Chunyu Chong who was about to be cooked by bandits, and both were spared. He raised his brother's children, disciplining them by beating himself. He continued to farm despite chaos. He refused multiple calls to serve, living in seclusion for decades. Emperor Suzong eventually summoned him, made him a counselor, and later promoted him. He died in office, and the emperor ordered a stone carving to commend him.

Jiang Ge, named Cweng, was from Linzi. He fled with his mother on his back during chaos, picking wild fruits to survive. When thieves tried to kidnap him, he cried and begged, saying his mother depended on him, and the thieves spared him. He worked to support his mother in poverty. After returning home, he pulled his mother in a cart himself, earning the nickname "Jiang Da Duozi." He refused official invitations due to his mother's age. After her death, he slept by her tomb. He was later promoted to Xiaolian and served as Taipu of Chu, but abandoned the post. He later served as Sikong Changshi and General of the Five Features. The emperor treated him with great respect. He refused gifts from nobles. He requested retirement and was made an admonishing doctor. The emperor later issued an edict praising his filial piety and ordered the county to give him gifts.

Liu Ban was the great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan. His father Liu Yu raised his younger brother Liu Ping after their mother died, and died of grief after Liu Ping's death. Liu Ban lived with his mother during Wang Mang's failure. He studied diligently despite his family's concerns. In the eighth year of Jianwu, he moved to Luoyang to study. He was later enfeoffed as a marquis. The emperor commended him for his good conduct. He served as Jinwu and captain of the cavalry school. He advised against establishing the Changpingcang, arguing it would harm the people. He also argued against a ban on farmers engaging in fishing and hunting, and against officials inflating land cultivation figures. He died at age sixty.

Zhou Pan, named Jianbo, was from Runan. He studied classics and was known for his good conduct. He left his official post to return home when he missed his mother. After his mother died, he lived next to her grave and taught thousands of disciples. He refused multiple government calls, saying he had no need for external things after his mother's death. At age seventy-three, he predicted his death, gave his sons instructions for a simple burial with a copy of the "Yao Canon," and died without illness.

Zhao Zi, named Wenchu, was from Dongjun. He was known for his filial piety. When robbers came to his house, he asked them to leave some food for his sick mother. The robbers, ashamed, left. He was later summoned to be an official and became Prime Minister of the East China Sea. He was known for his frugality. Before his death, he instructed his son to use a simple, thin coffin to allow his body to decay quickly and return to the earth. He wrote a long suicide note criticizing lavish burials and advocating for simplicity, citing ancient examples. His son followed his instructions.

◆Zhuomao Biography: Zhuomao, courtesy name Zikang, was a native of Wan, Nanyang County.
Both his father and grandfather were officials and county guards.
Zhuomao studied in Chang'an during the reign of Emperor Yuan. He studied "Poetry", "Li" and Calendar under Dr. Jiang Weng. He exhausted his teacher's scholarship and was called Tongru.
Tolerant and respectful in nature.
Although his behavior and talents are different from Zhuo Mao's, they both admire and associate with him.
At first, he was recruited as an official in the prime minister's palace. From Kong Guang, Kong Guang called him an elder.
Once on a trip, someone recognized his horse.
Zhuomao asked: How long has your horse been lost?
The man replied: It has been lost for more than a month.
Zhuomao's horse had been with him for several years. He knew that he had admitted his mistake, but he untied the horse and gave it to him. He drove the cart away, and turned back to the man and said: If this horse is not yours, I hope you can take it to the Prime Minister's Mansion and return it to me.
Later, the horse owner found his lost horse, so he sent Zhuomao's horse to the Prime Minister's Mansion to return it to him and kowtow to apologize.
This is how Zhuomao has no disputes with others.
Later, he was elected as a minister with Confucianism, served in Huangmen, and moved to Mi County as magistrate.
He works diligently and conscientiously in his duties, treats the people as his sons, practices good governance and teaches others, speaks no evil words, and the officials and the people love him and cannot bear to bully him.
Some people once said that the chief of the pavilion under Zhuomao once accepted his gifts of rice and meat. Zhuomao avoided his subordinates and asked him, "Did the pavilion chief comply with your request, or did you accept it because you had something to tell him?"
Or was it given to him because you usually felt that he was kind to you? The man said: I gave it to him myself.
Zhuo Mao said: You gave it to him and he accepted it, why did he say it out loud?
The man said: I heard that a wise king can make people not afraid of officials, and officials will not take people's property.
Now I'm afraid of the officials, so I gave him something. Since the chief of the pavilion has accepted it, that's why I said it.
Zhuo Mao said: You are an ignorant person.
The reason why humans are more valuable than animals is because they have benevolence and know how to treat each other with respect.
Nowadays, the elders of the neighborhood even give away food. This is the reason why humans are close to each other, not to mention the officials and the people?
Officials should not use their power to force money from the people.
In this world, people live in groups, so there are brokers and etiquette to communicate with each other.
If you don’t want to repair your interpersonal relationships, how can you still fly away and not live in this world?
The chief of the pavilion has always been a good official, so it is appropriate to give something during the Chinese New Year. The man said: If this is the case, why is it prohibited by law?
Zhuo Mao smiled and said: What the law sets is Dafa, and what is polite is human relationships.
Now if I teach you with etiquette, you will have no resentment. If I punish you with the law, you will be caught off guard!
Within a sect, small ones can be discussed, but big ones can be beheaded.
Go back and think about it.
So the people accepted his teachings, and the officials remembered his kindness.
At first, Zhuomao went to the county and ignored the government orders. The officials laughed at him, and those in neighboring cities despised him for his incompetence.
Henan County appointed a guardian for this purpose. Zhuomao did not mind this matter and still handled government affairs as before.
A few years later, enlightenment was widespread, and no relics were picked up along the way.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, a great locust plague broke out all over the country. More than 20 counties in Henan Province were affected by the locust plague, except that it did not enter the county boundaries of Mi County.
The postal supervisor reported it, but the prefect didn't believe it. He went to the county to investigate in person and was convinced only after seeing the true situation.
At this time, Wang Mang was in charge of the government and appointed six ministers of agriculture and agriculture to guide and assess farmers and mulberry trees. He moved Zhuomao to be the minister of the capital. The people of Mi County, old and young, cried to see each other off.
When Wang Mang was living in the country, he was exempted from returning to the county because of his illness. He often offered wine to his disciples and refused to serve as an official.
Gengshi was established, and Zhuomao was appointed as his attendant to offer wine. He followed him to Chang'an. Knowing that Gengshi was in political turmoil, he asked to resign and return home because of his old age.
At this time, when Guangwu came to the throne, he first went to visit Zhuomao, and Zhuomao went to Heyang to see him.
Guangwu issued an edict saying: Zhuomao, the former magistrate of Mi County, restrained and cultivated himself, was honest and steady in his duties, and could do things that others could not do.
At first, Zhuomao and his six comrades, Kong Xiu from the same county, Cai Xun from Chenliu, Liu Xuan from Anzhong, Gong Sheng from Chu, and Bao Xuan from Shangdang, did not serve in the reign of Wang Mang, but were famous at that time.
Kong Xiu, whose courtesy name was Ziquan, was the county magistrate of Xindu in the early days of Emperor Ai.
Later, when Wang Mang assumed power, Kong Xiu resigned from office and returned home.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he sent an envoy with Xuan Jinxun and silk to ask him to be the national advisor. Kong Xiu vomited blood and blamed his illness, and Du Men committed suicide.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he asked the descendants of Kong Xiu and Cai Xun to give him grain to show his power.
Liu Xuan, courtesy name Zigao, was a cousin of Anzhonghou Liu Chong. Knowing that Wang Mang would usurp the throne, he changed his name and hid in the mountains holding scriptures.
When Jianwu first came out of the mountain, Guangwu attacked Liu Xuan and granted him the title of Marquis of An.
Gong Ci, Gong Sheng's son, was promoted to be the prefect of Shanggu. The historian commented: At the beginning of the founding of the military, the heroes were quarreling, shouting and shouting, and those who defended themselves in the city looked at each other. This was the time when there were too many things to do.
Zhuomao, a small county magistrate with no other extraordinary talents and over seventy years old, was able to be appointed as the first to be appointed and receive great gifts and words. How is this different from King Wu of Zhou who appointed Bigan to watch Shang Rong and King Zhao of Yan to serve as Guo Wei's tutor in building a palace?
Therefore, many guests who harbored righteous indignation and hoped to return to the right path crossed the dangerous mountains and abandoned their clans in order to exclude the Jinmen embroidered households.
Being kind and lenient is closer to benevolence, and not repaying someone for committing a crime is closer to forgiveness. If you can do this, will anyone still be resentful?
Lu Gong's biography, Lu Gong's courtesy name was Zhongkang, and he was a native of Pingling, Fufeng.
His ancestors came from Lu Qinggong, who was destroyed by Chu and moved to Xiayi, so he took Lu as his clan surname.
Generations are worth two thousand stones. During the Aiping years, they migrated from Lu.
During the reign of Wang Mang, his grandfather Lu Kuang was an official in charge of the four seasons. He had great authority and was known as the "think tank".
His father, Lu, was the prefect of Wuling in the early days of Jianwu, and he died in the official position.
At that time, Lu Gong was only twelve years old and his younger brother Lu Pi was only seven years old. The two brothers were crying and jumping day and night. They did not accept the funeral gifts from the county, so they went home to mourn. The etiquette was even more considerate than that of adults. The villagers were deeply surprised.
At the age of fifteen, he, his mother and his younger brother Lu Pi all lived in Taixue, where they studied "Lu Shi", lectured and recited it behind closed doors, and ignored external affairs. Both brothers were praised by the Confucian scholars, and the bachelors rushed to join them.
Taiwei Zhao admired his ambition and sent his son to ask if there was a shortage of wine or food during every year and festival, but he refused.
Lu Gong felt sorry for Lu Pi because he was young and wanted him to achieve his fame first. He pretended that he was ill and would not serve as an official.
The county invited him several times with courtesy, but Lu Gong thanked him and refused to respond. His mother forced him to send him out. Lu Gong had no choice but to go west, because he stayed in Xinfeng as a professor.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Lu Pi was promoted to Fangzheng, and Lu Gong began to serve as a county official.
Taifu Zhao heard the news and called him out to serve.
Suzong gathered many Confucian scholars at Baihu Temple, and Lu Gongte summoned him with the Ming Sutra to participate in the discussion.
Zhao also recommended Lu Gong outspokenly and waited for the imperial edict to be sent to the public carriage to pay homage to Mou Ling.
Lu Gong specialized in moral transformation and did not regard punishment. The litigants Xu Bo and others were fighting for land, and successive orders could not be settled. Lu Gong commented on the merits of the case for them, but in the end they all retreated and blamed themselves, and stopped farming to give up the land to each other.
The director of the pavilion borrowed someone else's cow and refused to return it, so the owner of the cow sued Lu Gong.
He respectfully summoned the chief of the pavilion and ordered him to return the cow to its owner. He urged him repeatedly, but he still refused to return the cow.
Lu Gong sighed and said, "This is a teaching that doesn't work."
Prepare to resign and leave.
The ministers cried and tried to persuade each other to stay. The chief of the pavilion felt deeply regretful and returned the cow.
So the officials and the people were convinced.
In the seventh year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, borers were infested in the county and the crops were damaged. The boundaries of the counties were intertwined, but the borers could not enter the middle.
Henan Yin Yuan'an heard that the suspicion was not true, so he sent Renshu and his relatives to investigate.
Lu Gong followed him as he walked among the streets and sat under a mulberry tree. A pheasant flew by and stopped nearby. There happened to be a child next to him. The fat relative said to the child: "Why don't you catch the pheasant?"
Tong'er said: This pheasant is hatching chicks.
The fat relative stood up in alarm and said goodbye to Lu Gong: "I came here to inspect your political performance."
Nowadays, moths do not attack Zhongmou, which is one wonder; virtue is extended to birds and beasts, which is the second wonder; even children have benevolence, which is the third wonder.
If I stay here for a long time, I can only disturb the wise man.
Returning to the mansion, he made a truthful report to the governor Yuan An.
This year, particularly strong seedlings grew in the side room of Lu Gong's residence. Yuan An therefore wrote a letter explaining the situation, which surprised the emperor.
Just then, he ordered hundreds of officials to recommend virtuous and upright people. Lu Gong recommended Wang Fang, a famous scholar in Zhongmu. The emperor immediately summoned Wang Fang to the official carriage and treated the virtuous and upright people recommended by the minister with the same etiquette. Wang Fang became an official in the service.
During Lu Gong's three years in office, he excelled particularly well in the state examinations. It coincided with the death of his mother and his resignation, and officials and people all missed him.
Later, he became the imperial censor.
When Emperor He was first established, he was preparing to send the cavalry general Dou Xian and the western general Geng Bing to attack the Xiongnu. Lu Gong wrote a letter to admonish: Your Majesty works personally on the holy body, does not eat during the sun, and is worried about military service. The reason is to stabilize the northern border, eliminate troubles for the people, and plan for the future.
But I thought to myself that I had not seen the convenience.
The plan for the country and the lives of thousands of people depend on one move.
For several years, the autumn harvests have failed, people have not enough food, warehouses are empty, and the country has no reserves.
It happened that Emperor Zhang died, and people were filled with fear.
Your Majesty, who has practiced the virtues of a great saint and performed the most filial piety, should spend three years in mourning and listen to the funeral rites.
The people were sad, and they could not hear the sound of police for three hours, and they all felt anxious and worried, as if they were asking for something but not getting it.
Today, in the full month of spring, we launch military campaigns, disrupt the world, and stalemate with the barbarians. This is not a move to show favor to China and change the time of the Yuan Dynasty, from the inside to the outside.
All peoples are born from heaven.
God loves his children, just like parents love their sons.
If something is out of place and the weather is wrong, let alone people.
Therefore, those who love others will be rewarded.
In the past, Taiwang Gugong passed away because he cherished human life, so he was blessed by God.
Yi Di is the strange spirit in all directions.
Ping Siju is arrogant, unruly and rude, no different from birds and beasts.
If they live together in China, they will confuse the weather and insult good people. Therefore, the system of the Holy King is just a constant restraint on them.
There is nothing happening on the border today. We should practice benevolence, practice righteousness, and advocate inaction, so that our families can have enough people and have a safe and prosperous career.
If the human way is stable at the bottom, the yin and yang will be harmonious at the top, and the auspicious wind and rain will cover the distance, then Yi Di will pay tribute through many translations.
"Book of Changes" says: With good faith and accumulation, it is like rainwater filling a small pot, and the result will be other auspicious events. It means that if the sweet rain fills my earthenware fou, if I have integrity, it will be auspicious for someone to come and join me.
Those who conquer others with virtue will prosper, and those who conquer others with strength will perish.
Today, the Xiongnu were defeated by Xianbei and are hiding far west of the Shihou River, thousands of miles away from the frontier fortress. To take advantage of their wastage and weaken them to attack them is not moral.
The former servant Ji Tong went far beyond the fortress, but in the end he could not see a single Hu soldier and he was already trapped.
The disasters in Baishan are endless. The protector Chen Mu was trapped, and the soldiers died in large numbers, and they are still suffering from his poison to this day.
The feeling of loneliness and sorrow has not disappeared. The benevolent think of it and think it is holding their breath. Why do they want to continue its legacy and ignore the adversity?
Now the levy has begun, but the chief minister, Nong, has insufficient dispatch. The envoys are at the road, and the branches are supervising. The top and bottom are facing each other, and the people are in serious embarrassment.
There is little rain in Sanfu, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou, the wheat roots are withered, and the cows die every day. This is an effect that is not in accordance with the will of heaven.
The officials and the people all said that this could not be done. How could your Majesty only think of one person, abandon the lives of thousands of people, and not be considerate of the voices of the people?
Observing the heart of heaven from above and the will of people from below are enough to know the gains and losses of things.
I am afraid that if this continues, China will no longer be China, and the Huns will not become the Huns!
Your Majesty, please retain your holy grace, stop dismissing your soldiers, and obey the will of Heaven.
The book was sent to the emperor, but the emperor refused to obey.
Whenever political affairs were discussed, as long as they were beneficial to others, Lu Gong would always speak frankly and hide nothing.
Later, he became a doctor of "Lu Shi". From then on, the family's legal scholars became more and more prosperous.
He was moved to serve as a servant, and he held banquets several times to ask about his gains and losses. His rewards, favors, and favors were different from ordinary people.
Later, he was moved to the position of Liu Chong, the king of Qiancheng.
At this time, there were many thieves in Dongzhou, and they formed groups to attack and plunder, causing trouble to all the counties.
After Lu Gong arrived, he bought rewards with heavy sums of money and spread the favor widely. His commander-in-chief Zhang Han and others led his faction to surrender. Lu Gong used him as Han supplicant Bo Changwei.
In the ninth year of Yongyuan, he was recruited and worshiped as Yilang.
In August, he drank pure strong wine and met at Zhangtai. He ordered Xiaohuangmen to lead Lu Gong forward.
That night he worshiped as a servant and ordered an envoy to accompany him to express his condolences and ask for his kindness.
In winter, Luxun was moved to Guangzhou, and the election was pure and fair. No one from the capital could distort his integrity.
In the thirteenth year of Yongyuan, he replaced Lu Gai as Situ.
In the fifteenth year, the emperor visited Nanyang and appointed his son Lu Fu as the doctor. He was given a deputy horse to drive.
At this time, his younger brother Lu Pi also became a servant.
Brothers, father and son sit side by side in the court.
Later, he was dismissed from office due to his clan brother's affairs.
Emperor Shang ascended the throne and appointed Lu Gong as the Changle Guard.
In the first year of Yongchu's reign, Liang Quan was replaced as Situ.
At first, in the last years of Emperor He's reign, he ordered that the sentences be reduced during the wheat and autumn seasons. However, the prefectures and counties liked to govern with harshness, so they suspended sentences in the midsummer season.
Lu Gong went to the imperial court and remonstrated: When I saw the edict and respected Heaven, I thought of all the people and advocated harmony. The crime does not necessarily lead to death, so I will not investigate and confirm it for the time being.
Advance in kindness, retreat from greed and weakness, and act in accordance with the times.
This will help benevolent and virtuous, comply with Haotian, bring harmony, and benefit the people.
The old system stipulated that light punishments would be implemented at the beginning of autumn. Since the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, Meng Xia has been used instead. However, the governor and the governor did not think deeply about the principle of caring for the people and redressing the troubles, and promoted the virtuous and the corrupt. Instead, they recruited farmers in midsummer, arrested and tested the evidence. The cases were implicated in each other, and the case was delayed.
Sili Xiaoweidian leads the capital, taking all parties as the criterion. Recently, in the spring, he has branched out into various ministries, using pretexts and words to convey the poor, without mercy on the actual situation below, disturbing the counties and counties, scrutinizing those who have to be dealt with urgently, and arresting one person.
According to the "Nuhou Gua" in the fifth month of the "Book of Changes", the "Nvhou Gua" says: There is wind in the world, and the monarch gives orders to regulate the four directions.
It is said that the monarch uses the summer solstice to issue orders to stop those traveling in all directions to help the occurrence of slight clouds.
If the traveler wants to stop, how much more to arrest, test, plunder, and seize the time?
In recent years, floods and droughts have damaged agriculture, and people have been dispersed due to hunger.
This summer has just begun, the beginning of the harvest, the time when all things are pregnant and developing.
Since March, there has been a lack of warmth and coldness, and living things should change without being harmonious.
"Moon Order": Meng Xia cut off light punishment and released minor offenders.
When the autumn order comes, bitter rains will come frequently and the grain will not be ripe.
He also said: In mid-summer, the prisoners should be lenient and their food should be increased.
When the autumn order is carried out, vegetation falls and people are injured by diseases.
Therefore, it is necessary to give a lighter sentence because the crime is minor and he has repented. He should not be kept in prison for a long time, so the decision is made promptly.
I think that the current system of Mengxia can be implemented according to this order. Its prison sentences are all judged by the beginning of autumn. This will follow the seasons and cultivate all things. Then the heaven and the earth will be harmonious and the punishment will be clear.
At first, during Suzong's reign, the prison was broken before the winter solstice, and later commentators refuted each other.
Empress Dowager Deng ordered the ministers to hold a meeting to discuss. Lu Gong discussed and reported: The qi of yin and yang support each other and move, and each has its own season.
If it is not in season, then things will be damaged accordingly.
Although the kings have different qualities and literary talents, this principle has not changed. The administration of the four seasons is implemented in the same way.
The "Moon Order" was formulated by the Zhou Dynasty, and it was based on the time of the Xia Dynasty. The only changes were the Zhengshuo, clothing colors, and the livestock, emblems, and instruments used in sacrifices.
Therefore: Yin Yin copied Xia Li, Zhou Yin copied Yin Li, and the gains and losses of additions and deletions can be known.
The Book of Changes says: It symbolizes the lurking dragon, so it is better not to use it.
It means that the Yang Qi is hidden in November and December, making it inconvenient to use.
Although the gentle wind blows and warms all things and maintains the roots, there is still a lot of yin above, the ground is frozen and the water is frozen, and the yang energy is blocked and closed for the winter.
Therefore, it is said: If you walk on the frosty ground, you will know that the season of solid ice is coming, and the Yin Qi will begin to condense. If it goes down, it will naturally condense into solid ice.
It means that it starts to be slightly overcast in May and solid ice forms in November.
What the king does is based on the seasons.
Emperor Xiaozhang thought deeply about the ways of the ancients, and formulated laws and regulations to help his son Chou Yin's weak Yang Qi, hoping to be in harmony with the seasons in order to follow the heart of heaven and obey the fate of things.
However, judging from the reality since the reform, the years are not rich, the price of grain is very high, and people are uneasy.
If the county officials do not agree with the state, they will execute prisoners who have committed capital crimes in November. They will kill them without asking the merits. Even if the circumstances of some cases are suspicious, they will not be reviewed and corrected.
If one person complains about injustice, then the king's rule is wrong. What if many people are like this?
"Yi" November: A gentleman should review and suspend the death penalty for suspects.
Doubtful criminals can be ordered to follow this method in detail, and the death penalty subjects will not be terminated until the end of the winter month.
When the beginning of spring is in mid-December, you don’t need to file a petition for a report and still do it as before.
It was later implemented.
Lu Gong held the position of public minister, selected and appointed senior officials, and appointed dozens of ministers and county guards.
However, some elders with the same surname may be resentful because they were not recommended for promotion.
After Lu Gong heard this, he said: "The lack of learning is my worry."
Don’t all the students have their own villages to recommend them to?
So the complainer has nothing to say. Lu Gong had a humble nature and based his opinions on the classics. Although he benefited a lot, he never showed himself, so he was not known for his uprightness. After three years, he stopped writing due to old illness and illness. Six years later, at the age of eighty-one, he died at home.
◆In the biography of Wei Ba, Wei Ba's courtesy name is Qiao Qing, a native of Jiyinjuyang.
There is etiquette from generation to generation.
Wei Ba had been bereaved since childhood, and his brothers lived together. The state admired the harmony between their brothers.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he was promoted to Xiaolian and moved eight times. By the time of Emperor He, he was the prefect of Julu.
Live by simplicity and forgiveness.
When a governor makes a mistake, Wei Ba first criticizes his mistakes, and only removes those who do not correct them.
Officials sometimes denounced each other's complaints, but Wei Ba always praised the merits of the officials and never mentioned their shortcomings. As a result, those who denounced each other felt ashamed, and the trend of bad words and false accusations subsided.
In the 16th year of Yongyuan, he was worshiped as an official in charge of building palaces.
In the second year, Emperor He died, and Wei Ba took charge of the construction of Shunling.
It was a severe winter and the envoys sent by the palace were very strict in urging and punished the county officials several times to encourage Wei Ba.
Wei Ba only comforted them and did not blame the people below him. He also comforted them and said: It is my master craftsman's fault that you are being insulted now.
The officials were grateful and tried their best to speed up the progress of the project.
In the first year of Yanping, Dai Yinqin was appointed Taichang.
In the second year, he resigned due to illness and became Doctor Guanglu.
In the fifth year of Yongchu, he worshiped Changle Weiwei, begged for his illness, and became Guanglu doctor again. He died in the official position.
◆Biography of Liu Kuan Liu Kuan, courtesy name Wenrao, was a native of Hongnong and Huayin.
His father, Liu Qi, was a Situ during the reign of Emperor Shun.
Liu Kuan once went out and someone lost his cow. He found a cow in Liu Kuan's car and said it was his.
Liu Kuan made no excuse and got out of the car and walked home.
Soon, the man who recognized the cow found his lost cow and returned it to Liu Kuan. He kowtowed and apologized, saying: "I am ashamed of my elders, and I am willing to accept your punishment for me."
Liu Kuan said: Things are similar, and mistakes are allowed. Please send it back. How can I thank you?
The people in the state admired his magnanimous and non-confrontational spirit.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, General Liang Ji conquered him and was promoted to Situ Changshi five times.
At that time, there was an earthquake in the capital, so he was specially interviewed and asked.
He moved again and left the capital to become the prime minister of Liu Zhen, King of the East China Sea.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, he was worshiped as Shangshu Ling and moved to Nanyang to be the prefect.
In charge of the three counties, he was gentle, benevolent and forgiving. Although he was in a hurry and urgent, he was not quick to express his anger.
It is often thought that punishments are used to govern the people. Although the people do not commit punishments, they will inevitably behave shamelessly.
When officials and common people have offenses, they only use a few whips with grass whips to show insult, without causing any pain to the flesh.
Wherever there is merit, it is attributed to the following.
When disaster occurs, take responsibility yourself.
Every time he stopped at the Tingchuan Inn in the county, he would be greeted by academic officials offering wine and virgins holding scriptures in their hands to talk to each other.
When you see your elders, you comfort them with words from the farm; when you see young people, you encourage them with the words of filial piety and brotherhood.
People are motivated to practice virtue when they feel it, and education is becoming more and more popular.
At the beginning of Emperor Ling's reign, he was worshiped as Taizhong doctor and served as lecturer in Huaguang Palace.
When he moved to serve as a servant, he was given a set of clothes.
He was transferred to Tunqi Xiaowei, moved to Zongzheng, and transferred to Guangluxun.
In the fifth year of Xiping's reign, Xu Xun was appointed Taiwei.
Emperor Ling loved learning arts very much. Whenever he introduced Liu Kuan, he often asked him to give lectures on Buddhist scriptures.
Liu Kuan once fell asleep after being drunk on his seat.
The emperor asked: "Is the Taiwei drunk?"
Liu Kuan raised his head and replied: "I dare not get drunk, but the task is heavy and the responsibility is great, and I am so worried that I am drunk."
The emperor valued his words.
Liu Kuan simply liked to drink, but did not like to wash his hands and bathe, so the capital became a proverb.
I once sat with a guest and sent an old servant to the market to buy wine. After a long time, the old servant came back drunk.
The guest was unbearable and cursed: "Beast."
Liu Kuan soon sent someone to visit the old servant, suspecting that he would commit suicide.
He said to his left and right: "This man, call him a beast. Is there any greater insult than this?"
So I'm afraid that he will commit suicide.
The madam wanted to try to make Liu Kuan angry once. When the court meeting was held, after dressing up, the special envoy's maid pretended to accidentally spill meat soup on Liu Kuan, and the court clothes were also stained.
The maid hurriedly retreated, but Liu Kuan showed no anger and his expression remained unchanged. He slowly said to the maid: "Did the soup hurt your hand?"
Such was the magnanimity of his temperament.
People all over the country call him the elder.
Later he was dismissed due to a solar eclipse.
He paid homage to the Weiwei again.
In the second year of Guanghe's reign, Duan Yu was appointed Taiwei again.
After three years of service, the employee will be exempted on a day-to-day basis.
He also paid homage to the Shaofu of Yongle and moved to Guangluxun, in order to predict the Yellow Turbans' conspiracy. Based on this incident, he made a report and sealed 600 households of the local marquis.
He died in the second year of Zhongping at the age of sixty-six.
His son Liu Song succeeded to the throne, and his official position was Zongzheng.
summary:
**Zhuomao Biography:** Zhuomao, a native of Wan in Nanyang County, studied in Chang'an under Dr. Jiang Weng, mastering the "Poetry," "Li," and Calendar, and was called a Tongru for exhausting his teacher's scholarship. He was tolerant and respectful. Once, a man mistakenly claimed Zhuomao's horse as his own; Zhuomao gave it to him without dispute. When the man later found his own horse, he returned Zhuomao's horse with apologies. As magistrate of Mi County, Zhuomao governed diligently, treating the people as his sons. When a man admitted to giving gifts to a pavilion chief, Zhuomao explained that such exchanges were part of human relationships, not illegal coercion, and the people accepted his teachings. During a locust plague under Emperor Ping, locusts did not enter Mi County, a fact confirmed by the prefect. Under Wang Mang, Zhuomao was appointed minister of the capital but later resigned due to illness. When Gengshi was established, Zhuomao served briefly but resigned, knowing the political turmoil. Guangwu later visited him, praising his integrity. Zhuomao and six comrades, including Kong Xiu and Liu Xuan, refused to serve Wang Mang. Kong Xiu committed suicide when Wang Mang usurped the throne. Liu Xuan hid in the mountains until Jianwu. The historian noted that Zhuomao, a small county magistrate over seventy, was honored by Guangwu, akin to ancient kings honoring virtuous men.

**Lu Gong Biography:** Lu Gong, from Pingling, Fufeng, was orphaned at twelve. He and his younger brother Lu Pi mourned their father with exceptional propriety. They studied "Lu Shi" at Taixue, ignoring external affairs. Lu Gong let his brother achieve fame first, feigning illness to avoid office. He later served as a county official and was summoned by Suzong to discuss at Baihu Temple. As magistrate of Zhongmu, he focused on moral transformation, not punishment. When a pavilion chief refused to return a borrowed cow, Lu Gong prepared to resign, prompting the chief to return it. During a borer infestation, pests did not enter Zhongmu, and a child showed benevolence by not catching a pheasant hatching chicks. Lu Gong later became imperial censor and admonished Emperor He against attacking the Xiongnu, citing poor harvests, empty granaries, and the need for mourning. He argued that virtue conquers, not force, and warned of disaster. The emperor ignored him. Lu Gong later served as a doctor of "Lu Shi" and as a servant, speaking frankly. He became Situ but was dismissed due to a clan brother's affairs. He later served as Changle Guard and again as Situ. He remonstrated against harsh punishments in summer, advocating for seasonal justice. He died at eighty-one, known for his humble nature and reliance on classics.

**Wei Ba Biography:** Wei Ba, from Jiyinjuyang, was known for family etiquette. He lived with his brothers harmoniously. As prefect of Julu, he governed with simplicity and forgiveness, praising officials' merits and ignoring shortcomings, which curbed false accusations. He oversaw construction of Shunling under Emperor He, comforting officials despite harsh palace envoys. He later served as Taichang and Guanglu doctor, dying in office.

**Liu Kuan Biography:** Liu Kuan, from Huayin, was known for his magnanimity. When a man mistakenly claimed his cow, Liu Kuan gave it without argument; the man later returned it with apologies. As Nanyang prefect, he governed with gentleness, using only light whips for punishment and attributing merit to others. He taught filial piety and brotherhood, inspiring virtue. Under Emperor Ling, he served as Taiwei and lecturer. Once drunk at court, he claimed worry, not drunkenness. He disliked bathing, and when a maid spilled soup on him, he asked if she was hurt. He was called an elder. He died at sixty-six, with his son Liu Song succeeding him.
