It didn't take long for him to recover from his illness. He was given the seal and ribbon, and then he became a regular servant again. He was promoted to a special rank and was awarded two thousand stones. Soon he was promoted to Changqiu.
In the first year of Xiping, Empress Dowager Dou passed away. I don't know who wrote in Zhuque Que: The world was in chaos. Cao Jie and Wang Fuyou killed the empress dowager. Chang Shi Hou Landuo killed party members. The ministers were all people who had nothing to do with their bodies and had no loyal words.
So he ordered Commander Liu Meng to arrest them one by one and report them every ten days.
Liu Meng believed that the slanderous letter was honest and refused to rush to arrest him. For more than a month, the main culprit was not caught.
Liu Meng was convicted and demoted to the position of admonishment official, and he was replaced by Yushi Zhongcheng Duan. So he searched everywhere and arrested more than a thousand people including Taixue wanderers.
Cao Jie and others resented Liu Meng, so they sent Duan to do other things to punish Liu Meng, so as to offend Liu Meng and send him to the left school labor camp.
Many people in the court spoke up for him, so he was exempted from punishment and was recruited in a public car.
Cao Jie, together with Wang Fu and others, falsely accused Emperor Huan's brother Bohai Wang Kui of treason, and Liu Kui was executed.
Twelve people were sealed for their merit.
Wang Fu was awarded the title of Champion Hou.
Cao Jie also added 4,600 households to the city, adding a total of 7,600 households to the previous ones.
Their father, brother and children are all public ministers, ministers, pastors and commanders, and they are all over the world.
Cao Jie's younger brother Cao Poshi was the captain of the Yueqi camp. Wubai had a beautiful wife in the Yueqi camp. Cao Poshi proposed to Wubai, but Wubai did not dare to disobey him. His wife refused and committed suicide.
His fornication and immorality are mostly like this.
In the second year of Guanghe's reign, Wei Yangqiu, the commander of the Sili School, executed Wang Fu and his sons, Wang Meng, the Shaofu of Changle, and Wang Ji, the Prime Minister of Pei. They all died in prison.
There were often disasters at this time, and the doctor Liang Zhong believed that it was caused by the sins of Zhu Wangyu and others, and wrote a letter saying: I heard that when a country is governed by virtuous people, it will be safe, but if it loses virtuous people, it will be in danger. Therefore, Shun had five ministers and the world was peaceful, and Tang Wu used Yi Yin, so bad guys could not enter.
When the emperor came to the throne, he could not take care of everything. The empress dowager thought that you still needed to be taken care of, so she temporarily acted as a political agent. Su Kang and Guan Ba ​​were often killed in the front and middle.
Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu scrutinized their party members and determined to clean up the politics of the court.
Zhu Wangyu, the Marquis of Huarong, knew that a disaster would be imminent if the incident broke out, so he launched a rebellion, disrupted the royal family, trampled the palace, snatched seals and ribbons, forced and threatened the emperor, gathered ministers, alienated the relationship between mother and son, and killed Chen Fan, Dou Wu, Yin Xun and others.
Therefore, they jointly divide the country and reward themselves.
Fathers, sons, and brothers all enjoy honors, and people who are usually close to each other are scattered across the prefectures and counties, some occupying the ninth rank, and some occupying the third division.
He does not want to pay attention to his position and responsibilities, but only wants to engage in personal fraud, accumulate more wealth, build houses, and fill alleys.
He stole the water in the palace and used it for fishing, chariots, horses, clothing and playthings to compare with the emperor.
All the officials and ministers kept their mouths shut and did not dare to say a word.
The state, animal husbandry and county governors followed their will and recruited and elected them. They rejected the talented people and promoted those who were ignorant.
Therefore, locusts broke out and the barbarians were in chaos. God's will is full of resentment, which has accumulated for more than ten years.
Therefore, there are solar eclipses above and earthquakes below for consecutive years. This is a warning to the master, hoping that the master will wake up and kill the bad guys.
In the past, Emperor Gaozong cultivated virtue and revived the Shang Dynasty due to the mutation of the pheasant rising to the level of the tripod's ear.
Recently the gods enlightened the emperor and made him furious. Wang Fu and his son were killed in time, and everyone on the road, regardless of gender, clapped and cheered, as if they had avenged their parents.
But it is strange that the emperor tolerates the evil officials and does not eliminate them all.
In the past, Qin Xin and Zhao Gao caused the country to fall, and Wu appointed him as a torturer, but he was killed by the torturer.
Duke Yu held the treasure and led the horse, and Lu Zhao was expelled from Qianhou. They both perished and were humiliated because they did not listen to Gong Ziqi and Zi Jiaju.
Now, with the unbearable kindness, I am pardoning the heinous crime of the Yi people. Once the evil plan is completed, it is too late to regret!
I have been a man for fifteen years, and I have heard and seen what Zhu Wangyu did, which the emperor and heaven can no longer forgive.
May your Majesty spare a little time to look at my list and wipe out the ugly ones to answer the wrath of God.
When questioning Zhu Wangyu, if there are any untruthful words, he is willing to be killed and his wife to move with him to stop the way of speaking nonsense.
The memorial was suppressed.
Cao Jie also served as minister of law.
Four years later, he died and was presented to the general of chariots and cavalry.
Later, Zhu Wangyu also died of illness, and both adopted sons to pass on the country.
Shen Zhong was named Gongcheng, and after being killed by the eunuchs, he was summoned to the palace.
◆Biography of Lu Qiang, whose courtesy name was Han Sheng and a native of Chenggao, Henan.
When he was young, he served as an eunuch as a small Huangmen, and then he was promoted to a regular attendant.
He is honest, loyal, and law-abiding.
During the reign of Emperor Ling, he was granted the title of eunuch in accordance with the regulations, and Lu Qiang was granted the title of Duxiang Marquis. Lu Qiang's words were sincere and he refused to accept them, so Emperor Ling had no choice but to obey him.
At that time, Emperor Ling accumulated a lot of private wealth and collected treasures from the world. The contribution of the county and the country had to be paid to the internal affairs department first, which was called "guide fee". In the first year of Zhongping, the Yellow Turban bandits were causing trouble. Emperor Ling asked Lu Qiang what to do.
Lu Qiang's opinion was to first kill the corrupt elements around the emperor, grant amnesty to party members, and examine the merits of the governor and Erqianshi.
Emperor Ling accepted it. So he first granted amnesty to the party members.
In this way, the various ministers resigned from the court at everyone's request, and each recalled their relatives and children in the prefectures and counties.
Zhao Zhong, Xia Yun and others jointly framed Lu Qiang, saying: Lu Qiang discussed the court with party members, often read "Huo Guang Zhuan", and wanted to depose the emperor and establish another emperor.
Wherever the Lu Qiang brothers were, there was corruption and perversion of the law.
The emperor was unhappy and sent Zhonghuangmen to summon Lu Qiang with weapons.
When Lu Qiang heard that the emperor called him, he said angrily: If I die, the country will be in chaos!
How can a doctor, who is loyal to the country, obey the jailer's instructions?
Just commit suicide.
Zhao Zhong and Xia Yun also framed him and said: Lu Qiang was summoned by the emperor for questioning. He didn't know what to ask, but committed suicide in the weeds outside. It was obvious that he had a conspiracy.
At that time, the eunuchs Jiyin Dingsu, Xiapi Xuyan, Nanyang Guo Dan, Ruyang Li Xun, Beihai Zhao and other five people named Qingzhong were all in the alleys, not fighting for power. Li Xun thought that the doctors were taking exams for subjects A and B. The superiors and inferiors talked to each other, and one even offered bribes to change the characters of the Lantai lacquer script to suit his article. So he told the emperor that he and other Confucian scholars would carve the "Five Classics" on the stone, and ordered Cai Yong and others to correct the characters.
Since then, the Five Classics have been affirmed, and the debate has ceased.
Zhao was erudite, read a lot, wrote and revised books, and was praised by all Confucian scholars.
Also, the Wu couple in Ganling, Xiaohuangmen, wait for the wind in all directions to predict good and bad luck. They are broad-minded and have a reputation of being law-abiding.
Knowing that he would not be appointed, he often returned to his dormitory due to illness and calmly cultivated his ambitions.
◆Zhang Rangzhuan, Zhang Rang was from Yingchuan County; Zhao Zhong was from Anping.
When he was young, he worked in the palace, and Emperor Huan served as the Xiaohuangmen.
Zhao Zhong was granted the title of Marquis of the capital for his participation in the execution of Liang Ji.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, he was deposed as Marquis of Guannei and rented thousands of dendrobium from the county.
During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong were promoted to the rank of Zhongchangshi and were granted the title of lord. He is in harmony with Cao Jie, Wang Fu and others both internally and externally.
After Cao Jie's death, Zhao Zhong concurrently took charge of Changqiu.
Zhang Rang had slaves in charge of housework, colluded with powerful people, accepted bribes, and gained great prestige.
Meng Tuo, a native of Fufeng, had a wealthy family. He became friends with Zhang Rang's slaves and gave all he had to the slaves, leaving nothing he loved.
The prison slave was grateful to him and asked Meng Tuo: "What do you want?"
I can do it for you. Meng Tuo said: I just want you to bow to me. At that time, guests requesting to see Zhang Rang often had hundreds or thousands of cars parked at the door. Meng Tuo also went to see Zhang Rang at that time, but because he arrived later and could not go in, the prison slaves led their slaves to greet Meng Tuo on the road, and together they carried his cart through the door.
The guests were greatly surprised, thinking that Meng Tuo and Zhang Rang were very close friends, and they all tried to bribe him with treasures and curiosities.
Meng Tuo gave some to Zhang Rang, who was overjoyed and made Meng Tuo the governor of Liangzhou.
At this time, Zhang Rang, Zhao Zhong, Xia Yun, Guo Sheng, Sun Zhang, Bi Lan, Li Song, Duan Wanggui, Gao Wang, Zhang Gong, Han Kui, and Song Dian were all appointed as regular servants, and were granted the title of marquis. Their fathers, sons, and brothers served as officials in various prefectures and counties. They were corrupt and cruel, and were a scourge to the people.
The Yellow Turbans create chaos, and thieves are like boiling porridge. Zhang Jun, a doctor in Zhongshan, wrote a letter saying: I think the reason why Zhang Jiao was able to raise armies and cause chaos, and thousands of people were willing to follow him, was because he sent their fathers, brothers, children, relatives, and guests to various states and counties to monopolize wealth and plunder the people. The people had nowhere to redress their grievances, so they plotted evil and gathered together to become thieves.
The ten permanent servants should be killed and their heads hung in the southern suburbs to apologize to the people. Then send envoys to inform the world, so that there is no need to use troops, and the big bandits will disappear on their own.
The emperor showed Zhang Jun's memorial to Zhang Rang and others. They all took off their hats and boots, kowtowed to plead guilty, begged to be sent to Luoyang Prison, and used their family wealth to support the military.
The emperor ordered them all to put on their hats and boots and work as before.
The emperor was angry at Zhang Jun and said: You are really a madman!
Isn't there a good one among the ten regular attendants?
Zhang Jun wrote another letter, which was still the same as the last memorial. But they were always detained and refused to report.
The emperor ordered the imperial eunuchs and censors to investigate those who engaged in Zhangjiao's Taiping Dao. The censors, adhering to the wishes of Zhang Rang and others, falsely accused Zhang Jun of learning the Yellow Turban Dao, arrested him, tortured him, and died in prison.
However, Zhang Rang and others colluded with Zhang Jiao.
Later, Zhongchang Shifeng and Xu Feng's collusion with the Yellow Turbans was exposed and killed. The emperor became angry and asked Zhang Rang and others: You often say that the party members are plotting evil, and you order to imprison and kill some of them. Now that the party members have become useful talents in the country, you have an affair with Zhang Jiao. Can you kill him or not?
Zhang Rang and others all kowtowed and said, "This was done by Wang Fu and Hou Lan, who were often at the front and center."
The emperor did not pursue it.
The next year, Nangong suffered a fire.
Zhang Rang, Zhao Zhong and others persuaded the emperor to collect land tax of ten yuan per mu from all over the world and use it to build palaces.
Timbers and patterned stones from Taiyuan, Hedong, and Didao counties were recruited. Whenever the prefectures and counties sent these things to the capital, Huangmen Changshi always ordered to reprimand those who failed to deliver the wood and stone. They also forcibly discounted the price and bought it at a low price. They only paid one cent in ten and sold it to the eunuch. The eunuch did not accept it immediately. As a result, the wood piled up and rotted, and the palace could not be repaired year after year.
The governor and prefect secretly increased the number of conscripts, and the people cried out and sighed, suffering unspeakably.
Whenever the emperor asked for something, he would send knights in the Western Garden to secretly carry the emperor's orders, known as "envoys", to intimidate states and counties, and often accept bribes.
The governor, Erqianshi, Maocai and Xiaolian were all promoted and appointed, and they were all ordered to provide military supplies and palace repair money. For large counties, the amount was 20 to 30 million, and the rest were different.
Anyone who should take office must first go to Xiyuan to assess his worth before going there.
Some people don't pay enough and even commit suicide.
Those who maintained their innocence begged not to take office and were sent by force.
At that time, the newly appointed governor of Julu County, Sima Zhi, who was from Hanoi County, had a clear name, so he reduced the number and was ordered to pay three million.
Sima went directly to the edict and said melancholy: "As the parents of the people, I plunder the people to meet today's needs. I can't bear it!"
Resigning due to illness is not allowed by the superiors. Walking to Mengjin, he wrote a letter to state the faults of his time and the lessons of ancient and modern disasters, and then committed suicide by taking medicine.
After the memorial was published, the emperor temporarily suspended the collection of palace repair money for this purpose.
He also built the Wanjin Hall in the Western Garden, collected money and silk from the farmers, and filled it with silk.
He returned to Hejian to buy land and houses and build mansions and buildings.
Emperor Ling was originally a marquis and had always been poor. He often lamented that Emperor Huan could not buy a family property, so he collected money and property as private property, and also collected tens of millions each from the small Huangmen's regular servants.
Emperor Ling often said: Zhang Changshi is my father-in-law, and Zhao Changshi is my mother.
The eunuchs were successful and fearless, and everyone built private residences imitating the palaces.
Emperor Ling often climbed to the Yong'an Marquis Tower. The eunuch was afraid that he would see his residence, so he sent Shang Dan, the great minister of Zhongda, to persuade the emperor: "The emperor should not climb high. If you climb high, the people will be scattered."
From then on, the emperor no longer visited the pavilions.
The next year, he sent Gou Dun to order Song Dian to repair the Yutang of Nangong.
He also sent Ye Ting to order Bi Lan to cast four bronze figures and arrange them in front of Canglong and Xuanwu palaces. Four more bells were cast, which could hold two thousand grains, and were hung in front of the Yutang and Yuntai Halls.
He also cast a Tianlu shrimp toad, spitting water to the east of the bridge outside Pingmen, and then diverted the water into the palace.
They also built overturned carts and placed them on the west side of the bridge to spray the roads in the northern and southern suburbs to save the people the cost of spraying the roads.
Four more coins were cast, each with four patterns connected to the side wheels.
People who understand privately say that luxury and tyranny have reached the extreme. When a sign appears, this kind of money must be scattered in all directions.
When the capital was in chaos, this kind of money was indeed scattered all over the world.
He also appointed Zhao Zhong as a general of chariots and cavalry, and was dismissed from his post after more than a hundred days.
In the sixth year of Zhongping, Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty died. Yuan Shao, the lieutenant of the Central Military Academy, persuaded General He Jin to order the killing of eunuchs to make the world happy.
The plan was leaked, and Zhang Rang, Zhao Zhong and others took advantage of He entering the palace and jointly killed He Jin.
Yuan Shao led his troops to kill Zhao Zhong, hunted down the eunuchs, and killed them all, young and old.
Zhang Rang and dozens of others took the emperor hostage and fled to the Yellow River. They were pursued urgently. Zhang Rang and others cried sadly and said goodbye to the emperor, saying: "We will be extinct, and the world will be in chaos!"
I hope your Majesty will take good care of yourself!
After saying that, they all committed suicide by throwing themselves into the river.
The historian commented: Since ancient times, the loss of the country and the destruction of the clan did not happen overnight, but happened slowly.
The Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties brought disasters due to lust, Qin Shihuang caused troubles due to luxury and cruelty, the Western Han Dynasty died due to relatives, and the Eastern Han Dynasty lost the country due to eunuchs.
Success or failure has been discussed a lot in history books in the past.
As for the crime of eunuchs, there is probably something to discuss.
Why?
People like eunuchs are different from ordinary people. They have a bad reputation and are not from noble families. His skin and blood cannot be passed on to future generations. On the surface, no disadvantages can be seen in him. He can easily gain trust in his work. In addition, he is well-informed in the court and familiar with the rules and regulations. Therefore, the young monarch relies on his cautious and sophisticated strengths, and the female monarch uses him to come in and out to obey orders. There is no suspicion or fear when visiting him, and there is a joyful feeling when approaching him.
There are also those who are loyal and upright, and use their skills to correct evil; there are those who are quick to deal with things and use tricks to confuse things; there are also those who borrow the reputation of being loyal and good and gain reputation in advance.
Not all of them are wanton and evil, they are just blindly violent.
However, the truth and falsehood go hand in hand, seemingly loyal, but actually evil, so it can confuse the weak and weak master, and confuse the audience. There is probably a certain reason in it.
Since there are many fraudulent profits and the number of party members is growing, loyal ministers will definitely leak out in advance if they protest outright. They are worried and angry and want to impose sanctions, which just gives them the opportunity to seize it.
"Book of Changes" says: Walking on frost and solid ice.
That is to say, it has been around for a long time. Did it just happen overnight?
summary:
The preface to the biographies of eunuchs in the *Book of the Later Han* explains that eunuchs have served in imperial courts since ancient times, as evidenced by celestial signs and classical texts like the *Book of Changes* and the *Rites of Zhou*. Initially, they were employed for their perceived lack of evil thoughts and suitability for managing the inner palace. However, over time, their roles expanded. While some, like Bo Diao and Guan Su, made contributions to states, others caused disasters, such as in Qi and Song. During the Han Dynasty, the system continued, with eunuchs like Zhang Qing serving Empress Lü and later emperors. Their power grew significantly during the Eastern Han, starting with Zheng Zhong, who helped Emperor He eliminate the Dou Xian faction and was enfeoffed, marking the beginning of eunuch influence. This trend continued under subsequent rulers, with eunuchs like Sun Cheng playing key roles in supporting emperors, leading to their increased authority and the granting of titles and lands.

Cai Lun, a eunuch known for his talent and integrity, served under several emperors and is credited with inventing paper. He supervised the production of imperial instruments and later oversaw the collation of classics. However, he was implicated in a past conspiracy and committed suicide after being ordered to confess. Sun Cheng, another prominent eunuch, led a coup to establish Emperor Shun, killing rival eunuchs and officials. He and eighteen others were enfeoffed as marquises for their efforts. Despite later being dismissed and recalled, Sun Cheng’s legacy included the formalization of eunuch adoption rights. Other eunuchs like Cao Teng served four emperors without error, recommending worthy officials and maintaining a reputation for integrity, even when falsely accused.

The power of eunuchs peaked during the reign of Emperor Huan, when five eunuchs—Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Xuanguan, and Tang Heng—helped the emperor eliminate the powerful Liang Ji family. They were all enfeoffed as marquises on the same day, becoming known as the "Five Marquises." Their influence led to widespread corruption, with their relatives and associates plundering the people and causing chaos. Despite some attempts at reform, the eunuchs’ power only grew, leading to the persecution of upright officials and the establishment of party prisons. The historian notes that while Yuan Shao later killed all eunuchs, this merely replaced one form of violence with another, and the Han dynasty ultimately fell due to its reliance on eunuchs.

The biographies of individual eunuchs detail their rise and fall. Hou Lan, a favorite of Emperor Huan, amassed immense wealth through bribery and corruption, with his brother Hou Shen committing atrocities. Hou Lan was eventually impeached by Zhang Jian, but he retaliated by having Zhang Jian killed. He later committed suicide after being stripped of his titles. Cao Jie, who served under Emperor Shun and Huan, helped Emperor Ling ascend the throne and was instrumental in the massacre of the Dou Wu and Chen Fan factions. He and his associates, including Wang Fu, were granted extensive titles and lands, leading to widespread corruption and abuse of power. Despite some opposition, Cao Jie died in office, and his adopted son inherited his title.

Lu Qiang, a eunuch known for his honesty, advised Emperor Ling to eliminate corrupt officials and grant amnesty to party members during the Yellow Turban rebellion. However, he was falsely accused by other eunuchs and committed suicide. Other eunuchs like Zhao and Li Xun were noted for their learning and integrity, but they were exceptions. Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong, who served under Emperor Ling, were among the most powerful eunuchs. They controlled the court, collected exorbitant taxes, and built lavish palaces. Their corruption and cruelty drove many to join the Yellow Turbans. After Emperor Ling’s death, Yuan Shao led a massacre of eunuchs, killing thousands. Zhang Rang and others fled with the emperor but eventually committed suicide by drowning.

The historian concludes that the fall of the Eastern Han was due to the gradual accumulation of eunuch power, which corrupted the court and alienated the people. While some eunuchs were loyal and capable, the majority were self-serving and destructive. Their influence, combined with the weakness of young emperors and the machinations of female regents, led to the dynasty’s collapse. The historian emphasizes that the eunuchs’ ability to gain trust and manipulate the court, coupled with their lack of familial ties, made them particularly dangerous. The decline was not sudden but a slow process, as warned in the *Book of Changes*: "Walking on frost, solid ice will come."

◆Cui Xiang's biography, Cui Xiang's courtesy name was Tingbo, and he was a native of Anping, Zhuo County.
My great-great-grandfather, Cui Chao, worked for Youzhou during the reign of Emperor Zhao, and he advised the governor not to associate with King Yan Ci.
Later, he failed to assassinate the king and was promoted to Shi Yushi.
He gave birth to a son named Cui Shu, who successively served as the governor of four counties. He was known as capable wherever he went.
Cui Shu's youngest son was named Cui Xiang. When Wang Mang was a county scholar, he was summoned to the bus by Ming Jing.
Zhen Feng, the Taibao, appointed him as an infantry captain. Cui Xiang said: I heard that when conquering a country, one does not ask for benevolent people, and when fighting, one does not visit Confucian scholars.
How can I find this move?
So he confessed his fault and went home.
Wang Mang hated those who did not agree with him and often used methods to slander them.
At that time, Cui Fa, Cui Peng's brother, was favored by Wang Mang because of his cleverness, and his official position reached the rank of Da Sikong.
The mother was a master of Confucian classics and the language of hundreds of schools of thought. Wang Mang favored her with special gifts and gave her the title of Mrs. Yicheng, with a gold seal and purple ribbon, and a Wenxuan Danbo, which became apparent in the new Mang generation.
Later, Cui Xiang was appointed as the Grand Yin of Jianxin. Cui Xiang had no choice but to sigh and said: I was born in the age of Wuwang, and met such kings as Chu and Yi. I have an old mother above me and brothers below me. How can I put my body in danger by myself?
He went to the government office on his bicycle, claiming that he was ill and had nothing to do. He did not go to the county for three years to encourage farmers to grow mulberry trees.
Ni Chang, an official under his command, persuaded him, and Cui Cheng reluctantly stood up and issued the Spring Order.
In the counties I visited, the prisons, large and small, were full of people.
Cui Xiang cried and said: Oh!
If the punishment fails, the person is trapped in a trap.
What crime do these people have to be locked up here!
After a fair trial, more than 2,000 people were released.
The official kowtowed and advised: In the early days of the imperial government, the state pastoralists were in serious trouble.
Forgiving the criminal is indeed the heart of a benevolent person; however, if you are the only one who does this, will you regret it?
Cui Heng said: Duke Wen of Zhu would not change his life just because of one person, and a gentleman would say that he knew his fate.
For example, killing a large Yin to redeem two thousand people is what I want.
So he was sick and left.
In the early years of Jianwu, the imperial court recommended many people, and the governor of Youzhou also recommended Cui Heng as a virtuous person.
Cui Xiang felt ashamed that his clan was favored by Wang Mang, so he resigned and refused to serve as an official. Living in Xingyang, he reflected behind closed doors and wrote sixty-four chapters of "Book of Changes", which were used to judge good and bad fortunes, and many of them were used for predictions. Before his death, he wrote a poem to express his condolences, called "Comfort". Cui Heng gave birth to Cui Yi, who became invisible due to illness.
Cui Yi gave birth to Cui Xiang. At the age of thirteen, he was proficient in the Book of Songs, the Book of Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was erudite and talented. He understood the exegesis of hundreds of schools of thought, both ancient and modern, and could write articles.
When he was young, he traveled to Taixue and became as famous as Ban Gu and Fu Yi.
He often makes his career by studying classics, not to mention being an official.
At that time, some people ridiculed him for being too mysterious and quiet, and he would lose his reputation in the future. Cui Xiang imitated Yang Xiong's "Jie Mo" and wrote "Da Zhi" to reply to them. During the Yuanhe period, Emperor Suzong practiced ancient rituals and visited Fang Yue.
Cui Xiang wrote "Ode to the Four Patrols" to praise the Han Dynasty. The diction is very elegant, but there are too many words so I won't record it here.
The emperor is always good at writing, and after reading Cui Xiang's ode, he often sighed. Said to the attendant Dou Xian: Do you know Cui Xiang?
Answer: Ban Gu told me about him many times, but I didn’t see him.
The emperor said: "You like Ban Gu but ignore Cui Xiang. This is because Ye Gong is a good dragon."
Please see him.
Cui Xiang greeted Dou Xian.
Dou Xian hurriedly put on his shoes and greeted Ma Yin at the door. He smiled and said to Ma Yin: "Ting Bo, I made friends with you on the emperor's order. You won't treat me poorly, right?"
So I bowed down and became a guest.
Not long after staying, the emperor came to Dou Xian's house. Cui Xiang was at Xian's house at that time. The emperor heard about it and wanted to summon him.
Dou Xian dissuaded him, thinking that he should not meet the man in white.
The emperor understood and said: I can make Cui Xiang be by my side day and night, why bother here!
Just as he was about to ask him to be an official, the emperor passed away.
When Empress Dowager Dou came to court, Dou Xian used his relatives as cashiers to receive orders.
Cui Xian wrote a letter warning: "Ma Yin heard that friendship is shallow and words are deep, it is stupid, it is foolish to expect a noble person from a low position, it is slander to accept good advice without believing it."
None of the three items are suitable, but if you want to give it a try, you just want to imitate me, and you are angry and can't stop yourself.
I have seen privately that he has a pure and graceful posture, a masterful attitude, a beautiful mind and a powerful spirit, and has the demeanor of a virtuous person.
Ma was lucky enough to be admitted to the pavilion and ranked in the back row, so he tried his best to dare to say a word.
The ancients said: Those who are born rich are proud, and those who are born noble are proud.
There is no one who can be born into wealth and not be proud.
Now that the favor is rising and the officials are watching, when Yao and Shun were in their heyday and at the peak of their splendor, how could they not be concubine for a few days so as to make people's reputation last longer, promote the reputation of Shen Bo, and achieve the achievements of Zhou Gong and Zhao Gong?
An old saying goes: If you don't have trouble, you won't be in position; if you have trouble, you will be established.
In the past, the relatives of King Feng Ye held high positions and were called virtuous ministers; recently, the Yin Weiwei restrained himself and returned to ritual, and finally gained great blessings.
The ancestors of the Tan family are not disrespectful, and the Yangping clan is not prosperous.
The heavy marquis had many generals, built the Tianshu, and held the handle of the fighting. The reason why he was ridiculed at that time, especially in later generations, was why?
Just because he is full but not full, he has more than enough position but not enough benevolence and righteousness.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, during the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there were only four members of the ancestral family of twenty, and the entire Bao clan.
"Shu Jing" says: In view of the Yin Dynasty.
Isn't it prudent? The rise of the Dou family began with Emperor Xiaowen.
The eldest lord and the younger lord were honest and upright, and became famous the day before yesterday; Anfenghou Dou Rong was virtuous by supporting orders, and showed his self-resurgence.
Internally he was loyal to himself, and externally he used laws to guard himself. Finally, he enjoyed the national honor and has been blessed to this day.
The light of modesty is praised in the Book of Changes; the position of overflowing is warned by Taoism.
Therefore, when a gentleman is prosperous, he will be more cautious; when he is prosperous, he will be more respectful.
There are rules to follow when looking at distance and pitch, which are engraved on several sticks and between the pans.
Work diligently and never dare to be idle.
In this way, a hundred blessings will come, and the flow of celebration will be endless.
When Dou Xian became a general of chariots and cavalry, he summoned Cui Xiang to be a courier.
The Xian Mansion was noble and had thirty people, all of whom were former governors and had two thousand stones. Only Cui Heng, who was a young scholar, was promoted among them.
Dou Xian was arrogant and unbridled in his power, but Cui Cheng tried to dissuade him many times. When the Xiongnu attacked, there were more illegal things on the road. Cui Xiang took charge of the book and recorded it dozens of times, pointing out the pros and cons.
Dou Xian couldn't tolerate it and alienated him slightly. Because Cui Xiang was born in Gaodi, he asked him to be the magistrate of Changling County.
Cui Xiang thought that he was not satisfied with his departure, so he returned home without receiving his official position.
In the fourth year of Yongyuan's reign, he died at home.
He has written a total of twenty-one poems, poems, poems, inscriptions, odes, books, notes, tables, "Seven Yis", "Wedding Conclusion", "Declaration of Purpose" and "Drinking Police".
Cui Yuan, the middle son.
◆Cui Yuan's biography, Cui Yuan's courtesy name is Ziyu. He lost his father in his early years. He was eager to learn and try his best to inherit his father's business.
At the age of eighteen, he went to the capital, where he served Jia Kui, a servant, who treated him well. Cui Yuan then had the opportunity to study abroad, and then Mingguan, Lishu, "Jingfang Yi Zhuan", six days and seven minutes.
All Confucian scholars regard him as their sect.
He was particularly friendly with Fufeng Ma Rong and Nanyang Zhang Heng.
At first, Cui Yuan's brother Cui Zhang was killed by the people of the state. Cui Yuan took revenge with a bare blade and ran away for his life.
I met Amnesty and returned home.
The family is poor, the brothers have lived together for decades, and the town has been influenced by them.
Cui Yuan was in his forties before he became a county official.
He was imprisoned in Faqian County, Dong County due to the incident.
During the prison meeting, Cui Yuan often read "Book of Rites" after conducting examinations.
He was attentive and eager to learn, even in bad times.
Later, when the matter was clarified, he was released home and was summoned by Deng Zun, the general of Liao Dynasty.
Soon, Deng Zun was killed and Cui Yuan was dismissed from his post and returned.
Later he was summoned to the palace of Yan Xian, the general of chariots and cavalry.
At that time, the Queen Mother Yan took the title of regent and acted on behalf of the emperor. Yan Xian entered the court to participate in political affairs.
First, Emperor An deposed the prince as King of Jiyin and made Beixiang Marquis his heir.
Cui Yuan believed that setting up a marquis was not correct. Knowing that Yan Xian would fail, he wanted to abolish the order, but Yan Xian was too drunk to see him.
So he told Chen Chan, the chief minister: "Zhongchang served Jiang Jing, Chen Da, etc., and bewitched the late emperor because of his favor, so he deposed the orthodox ones and supported the evil ones."
When the young emperor ascended the throne, he became ill in the temple, and Zhou Bo's autocratic power reappeared here.
Now I would like to seek an audience with Chang Shijun, and persuade the general to ask the Queen Mother to arrest Jiang Jing and others, depose the young emperor, and install King Jiyin. This will surely harmonize the hearts of heaven and the hopes of people.
Yi and Huo's meritorious deeds did not leave the table, and the generals and brothers would pass on their achievements to infinity.
If you refuse to disobey God's will and remain empty of the throne for a long time, your innocence will turn into a great evil.
This is the opportunity for misfortune and fortune, the time for division of merit.
Chen Chan hesitated and did not dare to obey.
When the Marquis of Beixiang died, Sun Cheng established himself as King Jiyin. This was Emperor Shun.
The Yan Xian brothers were all killed, and Cui Yuan was also ostracized.
Disciple Su Yuanshi knew all about Cui Yuan's intentions and wanted to write a letter to explain the situation clearly, but Cui Yuan stopped him immediately after hearing it.
At that time, Chen Chan became the captain of the Sili school and summoned Cui Yuan. He said to Yuan: "But after listening to Su Yu's letter, please let me bear witness for you."
Cui Yuan said: This is just like a son and a young wife talking privately. I hope you won't say it out loud.
So he resigned and returned home, no longer answering the orders of the state and county.
After a long time, General Liang Shangchu opened his mansion and summoned Cui Yuan.
Officials who thought they were noble relatives might be reprimanded again, so they resigned because of their illness.
In the middle of the year, he was promoted to Maocai and appointed county magistrate.
While in office, he talked about current affairs several times and cultivated hundreds of hectares of rice fields for the people.
After seven years in office, the people sang his praises.
In the early years of Han'an, Hu Guang, the chief minister, and Dou Zhang, the chief minister, jointly recommended Cui Yuan as a great scholar of virtue. He had made great achievements in politics and should not be in the lower position for a long time, so he was promoted to the prime minister of Jibei.
At this time, Li Gu was the governor of Taishan. He praised Cui Yuan for his elegance and presented him with a letter to express his hospitality.
For more than a year, Guanglu doctor Du Qiao served as eight envoys and traveled around the country. Cui Yuan was accused of embezzlement and summoned to Tingwei.
Cui Yuan filed a petition to sue himself and found out the facts of the case and released him.
Soon he died of illness at the age of sixty-six.
When he was dying, Cui Chen, Gu Ming's son, said: People live by the energy of heaven and earth. When they die, their essence returns to heaven and their bones return to earth.
Do not bury your body anywhere, and do not return to your hometown.
Those gifts that are offered as sacrifices to sheep and pigs are not allowed to be accepted.
Cui Chen followed his will and was buried in Luoyang.
Cui Yuan has a high level of literary skills, and is especially good at composing books, records, proverbs, and inscriptions. He has written fuss, stele, inscriptions, proverbs, odes, "Qi Su", "Nanyang Literary Official Chronicles", "Sighs", "Yishe Wen", "Repentance Prayer", "Cursive Calligraphy Art", and a total of fifty-seven articles in seven characters.
His "Nanyang Literary Official Chronicle" was known in later generations, and those who could write thought they could not catch up.
Cui Yuan loves scholars, welcomes guests, prepares dishes and meals, and uses all the delicacies, regardless of how much is left.
My daily diet is just vegetables and vegetable soup.
The family did not have much savings and was considered very honest in the world.
◆The biography of Cui Chen, Cui Chen, Yu Zizhen, also known as Tai, with the courtesy name Yuanshi.
When I was young, I was very quiet and loved reading.
After his father died, he stayed at the tomb to mourn.
When the mourning period was over, the three princes invited him to serve as an official, but he refused to go.
In the early years of Emperor Huan's reign, the emperor issued an edict to the governors and counties to recommend people with extremely filial piety and good moral character.
Cui Chen was unable to attend the interview due to illness and became a man. Cui Chen was very shrewd about political systems and had strong official abilities. He wrote dozens of opinions commenting on contemporary political affairs, titled "Political Commentary".
Aiming at the key points at the time, the discussion was very correct and won praise from contemporary people.
Zhong Changtong said: All kings should copy it as a motto.
The article says: Since Emperors Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, they have relied on wise ministers to assist them, and learned men as advisers.
So Gao Tao wrote "Mo" and Tang Yu prospered; Yi Yin and Ji Zi wrote "Xun" and Shang and Zhou Dynasties also prospered.
When future generations of monarchs want to make great achievements, why not rely on sage ministers to advise them?
When the world is not governed well, it is often because the monarch has been in peace for too long, customs have gradually declined without realizing it, politics has gradually become corrupt without repentance, and he has turned a blind eye to the dangerous and chaotic environment.
Some people are intoxicated in selfish desires and ignore national affairs; some people cannot listen to good words and confuse right and wrong; some people are wandering at the crossroads, not knowing where to go; some people have credible assistants around them, but they are not allowed to speak; some people see alienated ministers and cannot listen because of their low status. Therefore, Wang Gang is idle at the top, and the wise men are melancholy at the bottom. How sad and lamentable! It has been more than three hundred and fifty years since the rise of the Han Dynasty.
The government orders are covered with dust, the superiors and subordinates are lazy, the customs are decayed, there are many people who are cunning and hypocritical, and the people are talking about it, all hoping that it will be saved if they rise to power.
Besides, the method of saving the world must be governed by the methods of Yao and Shun.
As long as we can make up for the shortcomings, add pillars to support the building, prescribe the right medicine according to the actual situation and tailor the situation, in short, we must put the country in a peaceful state.
Therefore, the sage is responsible for weighing and formulating countermeasures according to the actual situation. The steps are different and each has its own clever arrangement.
It is not advisable to force people to do things they cannot do, and to pursue what they hear is contrary to the urgent needs of the time.
In the past, Confucius' answers to the monarch's questions varied based on people and circumstances. His answer to Duke Ye's question about government was to ask those who are near to be pleased and those who are far away to come; his answer to Duke Ai of Lu was that "policy depends on selecting talents"; his answer to Duke Jin of Qi was that "government depends on saving money". It is not that the way of government is different, but that the priorities are different.
Therefore, those who have just accepted the destiny to be king often have some unique regulations, and the king of Zhongxing also has to correct the mistakes made at that time.
In ancient times, Pan Geng wanted to revive the Shang Dynasty and moved the capital from Geng to Bo; King Mu of Zhou made mistakes and asked Fuhou to amend the criminal law.
However, there are some common people who stick to ancient written records, do not know how to make changes, listen to strange news, and ignore the reality before them. How can we discuss national affairs with them!
Therefore, although talking about political affairs sounds like it is in line with holiness, it actually does not work.
Why?
Those stubborn people had no understanding of the situation at that time and were accustomed to following the same old path. I don’t know how to enjoy the success, how can I think about creating a new situation, just follow the old rules.
Some of those knowledgeable people boast about themselves, are jealous of others, are unwilling to cooperate with those who have different political views, and write eloquent articles to express their meaning. However, the minority is outnumbered after all, and is eventually abandoned.
Even if wise ministers like Ji and Qi are still there, it will still be difficult.
This is the reason why Jia Yi was ostracized by Jiang and Guan, and why Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao" to vent his anger.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was so wise, Jia Sheng was so talented, and Jiang and Guan were so loyal. If there was such a result, what about the rest of the people? Virtue is measured by strength, this is mentioned in "Spring and Autumn".
Now we cannot completely follow the methods of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. We should participate in some hegemony, govern the country with heavy rewards and deep punishments, and clearly formulate laws to check all work.
If you do not possess superior moral character, you will be able to govern strictly if you are strict, but you will be disordered if you are loose.
How do you know this is the case? In modern times, Emperor Xiaoxuan understood the way of being a king and studied the principles of government, so he adopted severe punishments to scare the bad guys out of fear, and the domestic political discipline was strict and the world was peaceful.
His merits were reported to the ancestral temple and he was given the posthumous title of Zhongzong.
His plans and effects surpassed that of Emperor Xiaowen.
Later, when Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he mostly used loose politics, but the result was a complete failure, and his authority was usurped, which became the source of troubles for the decline of the Han Dynasty.
The good and bad of politics can be seen clearly here.
In ancient times, Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, praising Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin for their hegemony, and commending Guan Zhong for his contributions.
Don’t you know the right way to praise King Wen and King Wu of Zhou?
It is indeed the principle of using power and change to save the decline.
Therefore, saints can adapt to changes in the situation, but laymen do not understand changes. They believe that the ancient method of knotting ropes can be used to control the chaos of the Qin Dynasty, and the dance of "Qian Qi" can relieve the siege of Pingcheng, the emperor of the Han Dynasty. Isn't this a thousand miles apart? Although imitating the movement of a bear and stretching the neck of a bird to inhale is a way to prolong life, it cannot cure typhoid fever; breathing and exhaling can increase lifespan, but it cannot connect broken bones.
The method of governing a country is a bit like treating a disease. You should pay attention to how to maintain your health and prescribe the right medicine when you are sick.
Punishment is like a prescription to cure troubled times; moral education is like meat that nourishes the body.
Using moral education to eliminate cruelty is equivalent to using meat to cure diseases. Using punishment to govern a peaceful world is equivalent to using medicinal stones for nutrition.
Now is the period of decline and decline of the Hundred Kings, the time of misfortune.
For several generations, the government has been generous and lenient, just like the driver of the carriage has lost his horse's faucet, and the horse has no bit, allowing the four stallions to run wild and almost fall over on the road.
It's time to add a dragon head chew to save it. Do you have time to listen to them ringing the bells and pressing the bridle rhythmically?
In the past, the emperor of the Han Dynasty asked Xiao He to make nine chapters of the law, which included provisions for killing three tribes, including carving on the face, cutting off the nose, cutting off the toes, cutting off the tongue, and beheading, so it was called the Five Punishments.
Although Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty abolished corporal punishment, those who should have their noses cut off were given three hundred boards, those who had their left toes chopped off were given five hundred boards, and those who should have their right toes chopped off were decapitated.
But those who had their right toes cut off were already dead, and those who were hit with boards were often beaten to death. Even if they were given a reduced punishment, they still killed a lot of people.
At this time, people all hoped to resume corporal punishment.
In the first year of Emperor Jing's reign, he issued an edict: "Being beaten more times is no different from a serious crime. Even if you are lucky enough to survive, you will be disabled."
So the law was revised to reduce the number of floggings.
From then on, those who were flogged were able to save their lives.
In this way, Emperor Wen of Han was still punished severely, not lightly. Peace is achieved through severe punishment, not through forgiveness.
We must make sure that our actions and words are consistent, and we should start from the fundamentals, so that people can learn from the Five Emperors and Three Kings. Break the corrupt customs of the Qin Dynasty, abide by the legacy of the previous kings, abandon measures that only seek temporary peace, repeat the old traces of ancient times, restore the five titles of duke, marquis, uncle, son, and male, and establish the well-field system of one part public land and eight parts private land.
Then he selected wise ministers like Ji and Qi as assistants, and selected Yi Yin and Lu Shang as prime ministers. When playing music, the phoenix led hundreds of birds to the court, struck stone chimes, and hundreds of beasts came to dance.
If not, then any more is just a burden.
Later, the imperial court asked Cui Chen to serve as an official in the mansion of Taiwei Yuan Tang and General Liang Ji, but Cui Chen refused to go.
Taisi Nongyang Fu and Shaofu He Bao wrote to recommend Cui Chen, saying that Cui Chen was very talented and capable and should be an official in the court.
So the emperor made Cui Yilang, promoted General Liang Ji to Sima, and wrote books and theories in Dongguan with Bian Shao, Yandu and others.
Later, Cui Chen became the governor of Wuyuan.
The soil in Wuyuan is suitable for growing hemp, but the local people do not know how to weave cloth. The people have no clothes to wear in winter, so they pile some fine grass to sleep in the grass, and when they see the officials, they come out covered with grass.
After Cui Chen took office, he asked the people to sell their stored grains, buy textiles, weave 纟第, 緺箷 and other tools for them and teach them how to use them, so that the people could avoid the suffering of cold and exhaustion.
At this time, the Xiongnu invaded Yunzhong and Shuofang successively, killing and plundering officials and people, and fled for their lives nine times in a year.
Cui Chen strengthened his troops and ordered beacon towers to conduct reconnaissance. The enemy did not dare to invade, making it the quietest place on the frontier.
When Cui Chen was ill, he was worshiped as Yilang, and he reviewed the Five Classics with famous Confucian doctors at the time.
It happened that Liang Ji was killed. Cui Chen was an old official of Liang Ji. He was implicated, dismissed from his official position, and was imprisoned for several years.
At that time, Xianbei invaded the border many times, and the emperor issued an edict to recommend powerful strategists to the three princes. Sikong Huang Qiong recommended Cui Chen, who was worshiped as the governor of Liaodong.
Halfway through the journey, his mother Liu died of illness. Cui Chen asked Shangshu to go home to attend to the funeral.
My mother, Mrs. Liu, was of very good character during her lifetime and read a lot of books.
At first, Cui Chen served as the prefect of Wuyuan, and his mother often taught him how to manage political affairs. Cui Chen's good achievements were very helpful to his mother.
After the mourning was over, the emperor made him minister again.
Cui Chen was dismissed from his post and returned home after a few months on the grounds that the current situation was in chaos and he was ill and could not work.
When Cui Chen's father died, Cui Chen sold his property, made a tomb, and erected a tombstone.
After the burial, all the family property was sold. Because of poverty, he made a living by selling wine and porridge.
At that time, many people ridiculed him for this, but he never changed.
When he does business, he just wants to make enough money, and he doesn't want to make more money.
Later, when they became officials, they were mostly in border areas, so they were even poorer.
He died during the Jianning period.
The family was very poor and had no money to bury him, so Guang Luxun Yang Ci, Imperial servant Yuan Feng, Shaofu Duan Yu and others prepared coffins and burial materials for him. Dahong Yuan Wei built a monument for him to praise his merits.
He wrote a total of fifteen inscriptions, essays, proverbs, inscriptions, answers, seven words, temples, essays, tables, notes and books.
summary:
Cui Xiang, courtesy name Tingbo, was from Anping, Zhuo County. His great-great-grandfather Cui Chao served Youzhou under Emperor Zhao, advising the governor against associating with King Yan Ci. After failing to assassinate the king, he was promoted to Shi Yushi. His son Cui Shu governed four counties capably. Cui Xiang, Cui Shu's youngest son, was summoned by Ming Jing during Wang Mang's era. When Taibao Zhen Feng appointed him infantry captain, Cui Xiang refused, stating that conquering a country does not require benevolent people or Confucian scholars, and resigned. Wang Mang, who hated dissent, favored Cui Xiang's brother Cui Fa, making him Da Sikong. Cui Xiang's mother was a Confucian scholar honored as Mrs. Yicheng. Later, Cui Xiang was forced to become Grand Yin of Jianxin. He reluctantly served, claiming illness and neglecting duties for three years. After releasing over 2,000 prisoners through fair trials, he resigned, saying he would rather die than harm innocents. In the early Jianwu years, he refused a recommendation due to shame over his clan's ties to Wang Mang, living in Xingyang and writing sixty-four chapters of the "Book of Changes" before his death.

Cui Xiang's son Cui Yi was reclusive due to illness. Cui Yi's son Cui Xiang (the younger) was proficient in classics at thirteen, studied at Taixue, and was famed alongside Ban Gu and Fu Yi. He wrote "Da Zhi" to defend his reclusive nature. During the Yuanhe period, he praised Emperor Suzong with "Ode to the Four Patrols." The emperor admired his work and urged Dou Xian to meet him. Cui Xiang became Dou Xian's guest, but after the emperor's death, he warned Dou Xian against arrogance, citing historical examples. When Dou Xian became general, he appointed Cui Xiang as a courier. Cui Xiang repeatedly admonished Dou Xian for his excesses, leading to alienation. He was made magistrate of Changling but refused and died at home in 92 AD, leaving numerous writings.

Cui Yuan, courtesy name Ziyu, lost his father early and studied under Jia Kui, mastering classics and astrology. He avenged his brother's murder by fleeing, later returning after an amnesty. Poor, he lived with brothers for decades. At forty, he became a county official but was imprisoned. During imprisonment, he studied the "Book of Rites." After release, he served under generals Deng Zun and Yan Xian. When Empress Dowager Yan regented, Cui Yuan advised Yan Xian to depose the young emperor and install King Jiyin, but Yan refused. After Emperor Shun's rise, Yan Xian was killed, and Cui Yuan was ostracized. He later served as county magistrate, cultivating rice fields for seven years. Recommended as a virtuous scholar, he became prime minister of Jibei. Accused of embezzlement, he defended himself and was released. He died at sixty-six, requesting a simple burial in Luoyang. He wrote fifty-seven works, including "Nanyang Literary Official Chronicle," and was known for his hospitality despite poverty.

Cui Chen, courtesy name Zizhen, was quiet and studious. After his father's death, he mourned at the tomb. Refusing official invitations, he wrote "Political Commentary" criticizing contemporary governance. He argued for adapting policies to circumstances, citing historical examples like Emperor Xuan's strict laws versus Emperor Yuan's laxity. He advocated severe punishment for troubled times, comparing it to medicine. He served as governor of Wuyuan, teaching weaving to locals and strengthening defenses against Xiongnu. Later, as Yilang, he reviewed classics but was imprisoned for ties to Liang Ji. After release, he became governor of Liaodong but resigned due to his mother's death. He died during the Jianning period, impoverished, with his burial funded by officials. He wrote fifteen works.

◆Zuo Xiong's biography, Zuo Xiong's courtesy name is Bohao, a native of Nieyang, Nanyang.
During the reign of Emperor An, he was elected as Xiaolian and promoted to the governor of Jizhou.
There are a lot of people in the state who like to build relationships and go through the back door. Zuo Xiong often kept the door closed and did not interact with them.
Deal with those corrupt, cunning and ferocious Erqianshi without any respect.
In the early years of Yongjian's reign, public buses were sent to pay homage to Yilang.
At this time, Emperor Shun was newly established, and the ministers were following the rules, and many tasks in the court were not completed.
Zuo Xiong wrote several times with fierce words. Minister Pushe Yu Xu believed that Zuo Xiong was loyal and upright, and wrote a report to the emperor recommending him, saying: I have seen that most of the officials below the public minister are silent and self-respecting. They regard showing kindness as a virtue and loyalty to the court as a fool.
I saw that Zuo Xiong dared to mention the fact that the emperor was in trouble in several memorials, and I took it as a warning. He really has the loyalty and upright spirit of a minister, and has the high demeanor of Zhou Gong to assist the king. If he serves as an official, he will definitely get the benefits of correcting and assisting.
Therefore, he worshiped Zuo Xiong as minister and was promoted to minister. Zuo Xiong said in a memorial: I heard that we should adopt a tolerant policy towards remote areas and use peaceful means towards the inland. The most important thing in doing so is to ensure that the people can get peace, and the most important thing in order for the people to be peaceful is to appoint wise men. But using the wise man’s method, there must be rewards and punishments.
Therefore Gao Tao replied to Xia Yu: The most important thing is to know people. To make the people peaceful, you must love the people. In this way, the people will love you. When he was granted the title of Bo and built a marquis, he cared for the people on behalf of the emperor, so the people became harmonious and respectful, and the custom of courtesy and concessions flourished.
Therefore, "The Book of Songs" says: The clouds are cloudy and the good rain is like silk. Let it rain in the public fields first!
Fall into my private land again. In the chaotic era of King You and King Li, the country was not governed well and Baosi was dictatorial. The seven sons formed a gang and ran rampant. There was no distinction between the wise and the foolish. Deep valleys turned into high mountains.
Therefore, there is a poem that goes: In a country with four directions, political corruption is due to the lack of talented people. He also said: People nowadays are pitiful! Like a lizard, it runs away when it sees an official.
Although the Han Dynasty did not restore the ancient system, it was able to carefully select officials, abolish tyranny, correct shortcomings, appease the people, and solve their difficult problems.
In the Wen and Jing eras, the peace in the world was really the result of quietness and careful selection of officials.
Down to Emperor Xuan, because he came from a humble background, he followed his name and his responsibilities, and knew what was wrong with the politics at that time. Officials such as the governor and the prime minister should be introduced in person and their every word and deed should be scrutinized. If they believe in rewards, they must be punished.
Emperor Xuan sighed and said: The people are now peaceful and have no resentment because of good policies and good officials.
Those who have reached this point with me are all these very good two thousand stones! It is believed that when officials change frequently, the subordinates will not be satisfied with their jobs. If they work for a long time, the people will be influenced by his education.
Those who perform well will write letters of encouragement, be promoted and receive bonuses. Some were promoted to the rank of Marquis of Guannei, and if there were any vacancies among the ministers, they would be filled accordingly.
Therefore, the officials are all competent and the people live and work in peace and contentment.
There were the most good officials in the Han Dynasty at this time. Therefore, the auspicious omen of the Five Arrivals of the Phoenix occurred, and the achievements of Zhongxing were built. From the early years of the Han Dynasty to the present, more than three hundred years have passed, and customs have gradually deteriorated. Counterfeiting and cleverness have flourished, with the lower levels concealing their deceit and the upper levels ruthlessly tyrannizing.
Both the governor and the county magistrate were transferred too frequently. Everyone had their own ideas and did not make long-term considerations.
It is said that killing the innocent is a sign of authority, that extortion and extortion is a method, that it is mediocre and incompetent to lead by example and to calm the people, that it is inflexible and inflexible to abide by the law and act in accordance with the law.
For trivial matters, people's hair is often shaved off and their necks are tied up with iron rings.
Between joy and anger, people are often killed.
Treat the common people as enemies, levy taxes, and be as fierce as tigers, leopards, and wolves.
The officials responsible for supervision looked at each other before and after, but worked together in collusion. Don’t expose wrongdoing when you see it, don’t picket up bad things when you hear them. Observing politics at the post station and asking for success in career in a short period of time can only mean that goodness is not called virtue, merit is not actual performance, deception is used to gain a good reputation, and prudent people are slandered.
Some run away because of their sins in order to gain a noble reputation, while some act based on people's colors and gain a good reputation.
The state chiefs do not conduct assessments, but strive for recommendation and recruitment, continuous promotion, and super promotion.
Some were about to be arrested and brought to justice, but they escaped and were not punished; when they encountered amnesty, they bribed them generously, but nothing happened.
The red and purple colors are mixed together, and the clear and turbid colors are indistinguishable.
Therefore, there are many cunning people, so you can go wherever you like. The orders of appointments flow like a stream, and there are often hundreds of omissions.
Township officials, general officials, have low-level positions, meager salaries, and their carriages, horses, and clothing all come from the common people. The honest ones will be fine if they get enough, but the corrupt ones will have everything for the whole family. Special selections and recruitments are carried out one after another, which causes a lot of trouble and expense, harming the government and harming the people.
If there is no harmony and misfortune persists, the source of guilt lies here.
The current county magistrate is equivalent to the ancient princes. Appointed by the government, there are regulations on clothes and horses, but in fact they are no more than ordinary boys, running away to avoid debts. This cannot be said to be serious about law and discipline, emphasizing governance, and caring for the people.
Although I am ignorant, I believe that those who keep the prime minister and have outstanding administrative achievements can be promoted on the spot and are not allowed to migrate. Unless their parents are dead, they are not allowed to leave their jobs.
Those who disobey the law or obey the king's orders will be banned from serving as officials for life. Even if they are pardoned, they will not be allowed to be among the good people.
If he is impeached, he should be punished by law. If he escapes and disobeys the law, he will move to remote areas to punish future generations.
Officials in the countryside who are close to the people are all Confucian scholars who are clean and capable of serving in politics. If they owe money, they will not be forced to pay. They will increase their salary by a certain amount. After serving for one year, they can be recruited and recommended by the prefectures and counties.
In this way, the way of arrogance and domination is cut off, there are no more frauds, the amount of labor sent to us is reduced, and the source of arbitrary expropriation is blocked.

In the eastern suburbs of Yingchun, since there is no one to go there in person, it is appropriate to commend the people, so that we can usher in peace and attract the wind of the times.
"Yi" says that a gentleman is constantly striving for self-improvement. This is the truth.

During the Heping years, he was selected into the palace to give lectures to the emperor.

Select wise men among ordinary people, and reward meritorious ones when there is no sign of the world.
In war, etiquette and justice were also emphasized, and in times of chaos, moral education was also followed.

Blocking the emperor's ears and eyes made him a deaf and blind monarch. The late lieutenants Li Gu and Du Qiao were loyal and outspoken, assisted the government with virtue, and worried about the country. They forgot everything about themselves and repaid them with death.

Things react to each other, and this must be the case.

Seeing that Liang Ji was about to be defeated, he attacked Liang Ji on the surface and expressed his loyalty to the emperor. In this way, his treacherous plan succeeded and he was granted the title of marquis.
In addition, the Huangmen cooperated with evil and formed cliques with each other. Since Liang Ji took power, he followed each other, made plans day and night, and helped each other with evil. The emperor did not clarify the truth, distinguished the true from the false, and sealed them at the same time as the loyal ministers, mixing the red and purple into one color, the white and the black, throwing gold and jade into the gravel, and smashing the king's jade into the soil.
When everyone heard this, everyone sighed with indignation. Once upon a time, Zengzi was a filial son, but his loving mother threw herself into a tree and ran away after listening to slander. Boqi, the most virtuous, was eventually exiled.
Slander and flattery can reach no matter how high the place is; party suppression can stir up ripples no matter how deep the water is.

However, the fear of death makes the guilt even deeper. Therefore, I dare to state what I shouldn't say at the moment of death, hoping that one ten thousandth of it can help the emperor. summary:
Zuo Xiong, courtesy name Bohao, was a native of Nieyang, Nanyang. During Emperor An's reign, he was elected as Xiaolian and became governor of Jizhou. He kept his door closed to avoid those who sought connections through back channels and dealt harshly with corrupt officials. In the early Yongjian years, Emperor Shun appointed him as Yilang. Zuo Xiong submitted several fierce memorials, and Minister Pushe Yu Xu recommended him for his loyalty and uprightness.

Zuo Xiong was promoted to minister and submitted a memorial discussing governance. He advocated for tolerant policies toward remote areas and peaceful methods inland, emphasizing that peace for the people required appointing wise men with proper rewards and punishments. He cited historical examples from the Wen and Jing eras through Emperor Xuan's reign, noting that careful selection of officials and long tenure led to good governance. He criticized the current state of affairs where officials were transferred too frequently, corruption flourished, and supervision was ineffective. He proposed that officials with outstanding achievements should be promoted on the spot and not transferred unless for parental death, while those who disobeyed laws should be banned from office for life.

Emperor Shun was moved by Zuo Xiong's words but never implemented them due to eunuch power. In the third year of Yongjian, earthquakes occurred, and in the fourth year, floods struck. Zuo Xiong warned of impending rebellion, and soon thieves arose in Qingzhou, Hebei, and Yangzhou. He later petitioned with Guo Qian about bandits but was not accepted. He also advocated for respecting classics and building the Imperial Academy, which Emperor Shun approved.

In the first year of Yangjia, the Taixue was completed. Zuo Xiong proposed that those under forty should not be recommended as Xiaolian unless they had special talents, and they should first study at government offices. Emperor Shun accepted this. When Xu Shu of Guangling was elected underage, Zuo Xiong questioned him and dismissed him. Several officials, including Hu Guang, were dismissed for election errors, while only about thirty people like Chen Fan and Li Ying were approved. Thereafter, officials feared recommending Xiaolian carelessly.

Zuo Xiong also requested recruiting famous Confucian scholars as doctors and increasing salaries for the virtuous. He petitioned to appoint twelve-year-old Xie Lian and Zhao Jian as boy scholars, attracting many students to the capital.

Zuo Xiong secretly wrote against granting titles to wet nurse Song E and Liang Ji, citing Emperor Gao's rules and past disasters from such grants. He advised following ancient laws and not ruining national ceremonies for small favors. He repeatedly advised against granting titles, warning of disasters. Song E eventually asked to resign her title, but the emperor still made her Lord of Shanyang. She later lost her title due to conspiracy.

When Chief Minister Liu Zhi was beaten for dereliction, Zuo Xiong argued that beating Jiuqing was improper, and the emperor stopped the practice. Zuo Xiong was promoted to Sili Xiaowei. He recommended Zhou Ju as minister, and when Zhou Ju later impeached Zuo Xiong for Feng Zhi's crimes, Zuo Xiong praised Zhou Ju's integrity. He died in the third year of Yonghe.

Zhou Ju, courtesy name Xuanguang, was from Ruyang, Runan, son of Chenliu Prefect Zhou Fang. He was short and ugly but erudite, respected by Confucianists. In the fourth year of Yanguang, he served in Situ Li He's mansion. When eunuch Chen Chan suggested moving Empress Dowager Yan to separate residence, Zhou Ju advised Li He to respect the Queen Mother, citing historical examples. Li He submitted this, and Emperor Shun later made peace with the Queen Mother.

When Sun Cheng and others were exiled for competing for merit, Zhou Ju urged Zhu Qian to advise the emperor, saying they should not kill meritorious officials. Zhu Qian's advice was accepted. Zhou Ju was later promoted to Maocai and appointed Pingqiu Ling. He wrote passionately about governance, impressing Shangshu Guo Qian and Ying He.

As governor of Taiyuan, Zhou Ju abolished the custom of prohibiting fire during Jie Zitui's death month, which caused many deaths from cold food. He posted messages explaining this was not a sage's intention, and customs gradually changed.

In the third year of Yangjia, Zuo Xiong recommended Zhou Ju as minister. He worked with Pushe Huang Qiong, gaining court respect. During a severe drought, the emperor asked about governance. Zhou Ju criticized the emperor for following Qin's luxurious path, having many resentful women in the palace, and lacking a crown prince. He blamed eunuchs for harming families and recommended releasing excess women, rectifying injustices, and eliminating eunuch expenses. The emperor summoned him and others to discuss governance.

Zhou Ju was promoted to Sili Xiaowei. In the first year of Yonghe, when disasters occurred, the emperor asked about burying the Marquis of Beixiang with royal rites. Zhou Ju argued against giving him a posthumous title, and most officials agreed. He was later transferred to Shu County governor but dismissed.

General Liang Shang recommended Zhou Ju as Zhonglang. When Liang Shang died, he recommended Zhou Ju as an admonishing official. Zhou Ju was sent as one of eight envoys to inspect customs, known as the "Eight Heroes." He was promoted to Dahonglu. When the Empress Dowager Liang wanted Emperor Shang's temple order below Emperor Shun's, Zhou Ju argued for proper order, and the Queen Mother agreed. He died in the third year of Jianhe, and the court mourned deeply.

Zhou Xie, courtesy name Jusheng, liked Xuanxu studies. He resigned from office due to his father's connections. When his father's old subordinate summoned him, Zhou Xie secluded himself. He refused Liang Ji's conscriptions three times and later declined recruitment due to illness. He lived in seclusion for over ten years. In the second year of Yanxi, he opened his door to guests. Liang Ji was killed that autumn, and Zhou Xie died at year's end, aged fifty.

Huang Qiong, courtesy name Shiying, was from Anlu, Jiangxia, son of Huang Xiang. He initially refused appointments due to illness. During Yongjian, he was recruited but refused until officials reported him as disrespectful. Li Gu wrote to him, advising him to enter politics. Huang Qiong became Yilang and was promoted to Minister of Public Affairs.

During disasters, Huang Qiong advised Emperor Shun to consult records, recruit Confucian scholars, and dismiss the unworthy. He recommended several scholars. During a severe drought, he advised examining political measures, practicing frugality, and releasing prisoners. The emperor accepted his memorial.

Huang Qiong petitioned to resume the emperor's plowing ceremony, which had been abandoned. He argued it was a grand national ceremony and cited historical examples. The emperor accepted. He was promoted to minister and proposed increasing filial piety subjects. He defended the reexamination method for officials against Zhang Sheng's proposal to abolish it.

During Emperor Huan's reign, when the emperor wanted to commend Liang Ji, Huang Qiong argued that Liang Ji's rewards should be comparable to Deng Yu and Huo Guang, not the Duke of Zhou. Liang Ji held a grudge. Huang Qiong was dismissed during an earthquake but later reappointed. He refused to appoint those Liang Ji recommended.

After Liang Ji was killed, Huang Qiong became Taiwei and was granted a marquisate, which he repeatedly declined. When five princes took power, Huang Qiong excused himself due to illness. He was dismissed several times due to disasters. In his final illness, he submitted a memorial criticizing the court for eunuch power, corruption, and the deaths of loyal officials like Li Gu and Du Qiao. He died at seventy-nine, posthumously titled Zhonghou.
