"The Book of Songs" says: Receiving blessings from heaven, congratulations come from all directions.
This year is the year of Yin, Cang Long Jiayin, Virtue is in the East Palace.
We should take advantage of the good time, follow the rules of Tang Yao, inherit the great cause of Emperor Xiaowu, hold an eastward hunting tour in February, seal Mount Tai, show the master of Zhongxing, record meritorious deeds, restore the traditions of our ancestors, report to the gods, pay homage to the fathers of Liang, worship the gods of the earth, and pass blessings to our descendants. This is the foundation of all generations.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the emperor visited Mount Tai in the east, accompanied by Zhang Chun, the imperial censor, and the Yuan Dynasty sealed the music and carved stone inscriptions.
In March, Zhang Chun died and was given the posthumous title of Jiehou.
◆Cao Bao Biography, Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was born in Xue, Lu State.
His father, Cao Chong, insisted on studying the "Qingshi Rites". During the Jianwu period, he became a doctor. He followed the emperor on a hunting trip to Mount Tai and established the Zen Rite. After returning, he was ordered to establish etiquette such as Qijiao, Sanyong, Dashe, and Elderly Care.
After Xianzong came to the throne, Cao Chong said: If the Han Dynasty receives the mandate of heaven again, there will still be a matter of enshrining Zen, but the rituals and music are incomplete and cannot be used as an example for future generations.
The five emperors did not inherit each other's music, and the three kings did not follow each other's old rituals. The great Han should make his own rituals and use them as examples for generations of descendants.
The emperor asked: How to make rituals and music?
Chong replied: "He Tu Kuo Di Xiang" says: "Elegance in rituals and music emerged in the Han Dynasty."
"Shang Shu·Ji Qian" says: There was an emperor who came out of the Han Dynasty. He was virtuous and happy, and his name was Yu.
The emperor appreciated it very much and issued an edict: Now the official name of Taiyue will be changed to Taiyule, and he will sing poems and perform music, and wait for future gentlemen to supplement it.
He worshiped Cao Chong as his servant.
It was difficult to argue chapters and sentences, so "Qingshi Xue" came out.
Cao Bao was ambitious and generous when he was young. When he was twenty, he inherited his father's studies. He was knowledgeable and especially fond of etiquette.
He often felt that the imperial system was incomplete and envied Shusun Tong for establishing etiquette for the Han Dynasty, so he studied it morning and night and concentrated on thinking. He held the letters in his arms when sleeping and recited the documents while walking. When he was so fascinated by his thoughts, he forgot which way he should go.
Cao Bao was first promoted to Xiaolian, and then to the magistrate of Yuxian County. He used etiquette to govern people and virtue to change customs.
At that time, five thieves from other counties came into Yuxian County and were captured by the officials. Ma Yan, the prefect of Chenliu, was very angry after hearing this and ordered to go to the county to kill them.
Cao Bao said to the officials: Those who cut off human life will be cut off by God.
It is said that Gaotao did not enact the death penalty for thieves, but Guan Zhong was promoted to a public minister when he met a thief.
Now to kill them according to the order from above is to violate God's will and obey the governor, and the punishment is too severe.
If I can save the life of the thief and let me be punished, I am willing.
So he didn't kill those five people.
Ma Yan reported that Cao Bao was weak and dismissed him from his post. He returned to the county and became a meritorious Cao Cao.
Later, Cao Bao was recruited to become a doctor.
It happened that Suzong wanted to formulate rituals and music. In the second year of Yuanhe, an edict was issued: "He Tu" said that Chijiu would be prosperous, with light in the tenth generation and prosperity in the eleventh.
"Shang Shu Ji Qian" says: It describes Yao's management of the world, the standardization of rituals and music, and the writings of the Tang Dynasty.
I am the last boy, entrusted to the end, how can I inherit the great legacy of my ancestors and save the people?
"Emperor's Mingxian" says: Shun Yao tests morality and establishes images according to the questions.
Moreover, the steps of the Three Sovereigns and the Five Emperors have different advantages and disadvantages. Moreover, I am very stubborn and cannot bear the responsibility. Even if I want to follow them, I cannot do it.
Every time I see the book, I feel very ashamed.
Cao Bao knew that the emperor's will was to make a difference, so he went to the emperor and said: In the past, when the saints were appointed by heaven to be kings, they would always make rituals and music to show their merits.
The purpose of enjoying success and making custom rituals is to save the world, attract good fortune, and bring blessings to all surnames. Now the emperor has sent blessings, good omens have appeared, and the talismans made are better than the records in words.
It should be written down and written into Han rites to show the beauty of the virtues of our ancestors.
The memorial was issued to Taichang, and Taichang Chaokan regarded it as the grand ceremony of a lifetime. Cao Bao could not decide it alone and disagreed.
The emperor knew that the officials were too reserved and it was difficult to discuss matters with them. The court's etiquette and laws must be settled in time, and the next year an edict was issued: "My own moral character is not enough, and I am responsible for the great cause of my ancestors."
Recently, Luan and Phoenix have gathered together, Linlong has appeared, nectar has fallen at night, Jiagu has grown everywhere, and mascots such as red grass have been recorded by historians.
I was very awed in the morning and evening. I could not praise the late emperor's meritorious service to my superiors, and I could not take care of the spiritual creatures.
When the Han Dynasty succeeded the Qin Dynasty, the rituals and music were incomplete, and there was no benefit in continuing to do things as usual. If anyone has knowledge in this area, please do your best.
Cao Bao thought about his intention, and then sighed and said to everyone: "In the past, Xi Si sang about Lu, and Kaofu praised the Shang Dynasty."
It is a virtue for ministers to honor the monarch and commend the emperor according to the great righteousness.
It’s my duty to do so, why should I refuse?
So he went on to explain the fundamentals of rituals and music and the meaning of system reform.
The emperor then appointed Cao Bao as a doctor, and followed the emperor on a tour to the south. After returning, he handed over the matters concerning the etiquette to the Three Dukes. Before he had time to report, he summoned Xuanwu Sima Bangu to ask about changes to the etiquette system and other matters.
Ban Gu said: There are many Confucian scholars in the capital, and most of them are good at talking about etiquette. We should recruit them widely to discuss the pros and cons together.
The Emperor said: As the saying goes: It will take three years to build a house next to the road. When we gather at the house for ceremony, it is superficially a discussion, but in reality it is mutual suspicion, and we are delayed in writing.
In the past, Emperor Yao used a minister named Kui to compose the Great Chapter.
In the first month of the first year of Zhanghe, he summoned Cao Bao to Jiademen and ordered Xiaohuangmen to take the twelve chapters of "Han Yi" written by Shu Suntong, which Ban Gu had attended, and ordered Cao Bao to say: "This Han Yi is very loose and inconsistent with the meaning of the scriptures. Some modifications should be made now to make it practical."
You can concentrate on your work in Nangong and Dongguan.
After receiving the order, Cao Bao arranged the order of etiquette, based on the old scriptures, mixed with the prophecies of the Five Classics, and wrote out the system of etiquette from the emperor to the common people, including the good and bad luck of weddings, etc., a total of 150 articles, written on two-foot-four-inch bamboo sketches, and memorialized in December of that year.
The emperor thought that it was difficult for everyone to agree on the opinions, so he only accepted them and no longer asked the officials to comment.
When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended the throne, Cao Bao wrote chapters and sentences, and the emperor put the two chapters of "New Rites" at the top.
Cao Bao was promoted to supervise Yulin Zuoqi.
In the fourth year of Yongyuan's reign, he was promoted to the rank of Colonel Shesheng.
Later, Taiwei Zhang Youfu, Shangshu Zhang Min and others complained that he had made the "Han Rites" without authorization and that he should be beheaded if he broke the sacred law.
Although the emperor put down the memorial, the "Han Rites" was not implemented.
When Cao Bao was shooting the captain, there were more than a hundred coffins in the camp but no burials. Cao Bao personally investigated and asked what the reason was.
The official replied: Most of these people have no descendants since the founding of the military, so they cannot be buried after their death.
Cao Bao was very sad after hearing this, so he bought an open space and used it all to bury those without owners and set up sacrifices to worship them.
He was promoted to city gate captain and will be a great craftsman.
At that time, the epidemic was prevalent. Cao Bao visited the patients, found medicine for them, prepared thick porridge, and saved many people.
In seven years, he became the governor of Hanoi.
At this time, there was a severe drought in spring and summer, and food prices soared.
After Cao Bao took office, he laid off officials and eliminated bad guys. Rain fell several times.
There was a great harvest in autumn this year, the people's homes were well fed, and all the wandering people came back.
Later, Cao Bao was dismissed from his post for committing the crime of falsely reporting the disaster.
Soon he was recruited, promoted, and became a servant.
Cao Bao is knowledgeable and understands ancient culture and is the master of Confucianism.
He died in office in fourteen years. He wrote twelve chapters of "Tongyi", 120 chapters of "Exemplary Classics", and forty-nine chapters of "Book of Rites". He taught more than a thousand students, and Qing's theory became popular in the world.
◆Zheng Xuan's biography, Zheng Xuan's courtesy name was Kangcheng, and he was a native of Gaomi, Beihai.
His eighth-generation ancestor Zheng Chong was the minister of public affairs at the time of Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty.
When Zheng Xuan was a boy, he worked as a small official in the countryside in charge of litigation and tax collection. Whenever he went home on vacation, he always had to go to school and was not happy to be a small official. His father was angry many times but could not stop him.
So he went to study at Taixue in Beijing, where he became a teacher under Wu Yuanxian, a native of Jingzhao, and then he became proficient in "Jingshi Yi", "Gongzhu Chunqiu", "Santong Calendar" and "Nine Chapters of Arithmetic".
He also studied "Zhou Guan", "Book of Rites", "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu", "Han Shi" and "Guwen Shangshu" from Zhang Gongzu of Dongjun.
Because there was no one in Shandong who could question him, he went west and entered the customs. After being introduced by Lu Zhi of Zhuojun, he became his disciple Fufeng Ma Rong.
Ma Rong had more than 400 students, and only about 50 people were taught by Ma Rong personally.
Ma Rong was an arrogant person, and Zheng Xuan had not seen him for three years under his tutelage. Ma Rong just sent his senior disciples to tutor Zheng Xuan.
Zheng Xuan studied day and night and never slackened off.
One day, Ma Rong summoned his students to study Tuwei. Hearing that Zheng Xuan was proficient in arithmetic, he summoned him upstairs. Zheng Xuan took this opportunity to ask Ma Rong many difficult questions.
After asking, he said goodbye to Ma Rong and returned to his hometown in Shandong. Ma Rong said to his students with emotion: Now that Zheng Sheng has left me, my teachings will spread eastward.
Since Zheng Xuan went out to study, it took more than ten years before he returned to his hometown.
His family was poor and he went to Donglai to work as a farmer. There are hundreds of students studying with him.
When the disaster of party imprisonment occurred, more than 40 people including Zheng Xuan and Sun Song from the same county were imprisoned. So he immersed himself in studying the classics and stayed behind closed doors.
At that time, He Xiu, a native of Rencheng, loved the theory of "Gongyang", so he wrote "Gongyang Mo Shou", "Zuo Shi's Death" and "Gu Liang's Failed Disease". Zheng Xuan wrote articles refuting "Mo Shou", "Gao Ming" and "Fei Ji".
He Xiu saw it and sighed: Zheng Kangcheng walked into my house, picked up my spear, and came to attack me!
In the early years of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Li Ming, and Jia Kui were debating ancient and modern theories. Later, Ma Rong replied to Liu Mo and Zheng Xuan, the prefect of the North. He Xiu said that because of the profound research on doctrine and theory, the ancient classics became prosperous from then on.
In the last years of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, the party ban was lifted, and the general He Jin heard of Zheng Xuan's reputation and recruited him.
The prefectures and counties believed that He Jin was a powerful nobleman and did not dare to go against his wishes, so they forced Zheng Xuan to obey the call. Zheng Xuan had no choice but to go and answer the imperial edict.
He Jin set up several canes for him and treated him very generously.
Zheng Xuan did not accept the court robes, but came to see He Jin in Confucian attire wearing a turban.
He stayed one night and then escaped.
Zheng Xuan was already sixty years old at that time, and his students came from far away places, such as Zhao Shang from Hanoi, and there were thousands of them.
Later, General Yuan Wei recommended him as a minister, but he did not take up the post due to his father's death.
Kong Rong, the Prime Minister of the country, respected Zheng Xuan very much. He hurriedly came to his home and instructed the magistrate of Gaomi County to set up a special township for him. He said: In the past, Qi State had a "Scholar Township", and Yue State had a "Gentleman Army", etc., which meant treating the virtuous with courtesy.
Zheng Xuanjun was eager to learn and had noble virtues.
In the past, Taishi Gong, Tingwei Wu Gong, and Ye Zhipushe Deng Gong were all famous officials in the former Han Dynasty.
There are also Yuan Gong and Xia Huang Gong in the Four Hao Mountains of Nanshan. Their talents and virtues are hidden and not exposed. The world respects their nobleness and calls them "gong".
If this is the case, then the so-called "gong" is the proper name for a virtuous person. You don't have to be a Taiwei, Situ or Sikong to be called a public official.
Now the township of Zhengxuan should be named Zhenggong Township.
In the past, Donghai Yugong only had a moral character of ending prisons fairly. He also warned the villagers to expand the gates of their lanes in order to prepare future generations for high-ranking officials.
What's more, Zheng Xuan has such virtue, how could he not walk the road of a horse and a high chariot. The gate of Zhengxuanli Lane should be enlarged and the road in front of it should be widened so that it can pass high-covered vehicles. This can be named Tongdemen.
Dong Zhuo moved the capital to Chang'an, and the minister recommended Zheng Xuan as the prime minister of Zhao. However, he was unable to take office because of the road obstruction.
When the Yellow Turban Army attacked the Qingzhou area, Zheng Xuan took refuge in Xuzhou. Xuzhou Mu Tao Qian received him as a teacher and friend.
In the first year of Jian'an, Zheng Xuan returned to Gaomi from Xuzhou and encountered tens of thousands of Yellow Turban troops on the way. When the Yellow Turban Army saw Zheng Xuan, they all bowed down and agreed not to enter Gaomi County.
Later, Zheng Xuan suffered from a serious illness and feared that he would not die soon, so he wrote to his son Zheng Yien, saying: Our family used to be very poor, but with the tolerance and support of our parents and brothers, we resigned from the small officials like humble servants and went to Zhou, Qin and other places to study. What makes me most proud is that these Confucian scholars accepted my advice and taught me something.
Therefore, I extensively researched the "Six Arts", browsed biographies, and read the rare national documents from time to time to get a glimpse of the secrets of the national prophecies.
After he was forty years old, he returned home to support his parents, renting land and farming to spend his time.
When the eunuchs monopolized power, I was implicated by the party members and imprisoned. It took fourteen years for me to be pardoned. Later, he was recommended as a virtuous, upright, and virtuous man many times. He was recruited by the generals and the three ministers, and twice by the imperial court.
Some of the other people who were on the same list as me were already prime ministers.
Thinking of those people with virtues and talents, they are capable of fulfilling the duties of ministers and should therefore be appointed.
I didn't think I had the talent to hold such a position. I just wanted to expound the original meaning of the Confucianism of the late sage Confucius and unify the differences among various schools. I also wanted to use my talents to the fullest, so I received the call but did not accept the call.
The Yellow Turban made me travel north and south, wandering, and now I am returning to my hometown.
By this year I am seventy years old.
The academic quality of the old days has become desolate, and there are still some mistakes. According to the rules of the ceremony, the management of the family should be passed on to the son.
Now I tell you that when I am old, I will leave all my housework to you. I will live in peace and quiet, thinking deeply to complete my career.
Unless I accept the king's orders, condolences the sufferings of my relatives, visit the tombs, observe and inspect wild animals, how can I ever go out with a stick?
Household chores, big and small, are all your responsibility.
It's a pity that you are alone and have no brothers or sisters to rely on.
You must work hard, pursue the cultivation of a gentleman, and study unremittingly. Be careful to pay attention to your attitude and appearance, and get close to those who are virtuous.
A distinguished reputation is promoted by colleagues and friends, and virtue is established by one's own ambition.
If you get a good reputation, you can also bring glory to your parents. Shouldn't you think deeply about this?
Although I am not as distinguished as a high-ranking official, I am as noble as a prince. I enjoy myself by commenting on and compiling classics, hoping that I will not be ridiculed by future generations.
Finally, what makes my heart uneasy is that the graves of my deceased parents have not been completed, and most of my favorite books are rotten. I cannot finalize them in the hall where learning rituals are taught and pass them on to the people who should teach them.
I am like the setting sun, approaching twilight. Can I still complete these tasks?
Our family is a little better than it used to be. As long as you work hard and cherish your time, you will not be afraid of lack of food and clothing.
Simple food and simple clothes, if I can control these two aspects, I will have no regrets.
If you forget my words and don't appreciate my painstaking efforts, then forget it.
At this time, General Yuan Shao was commanding the army in Jizhou.
He sent an envoy to invite Zheng Xuan as a guest. Zheng Xuan arrived last, and Yuan Shao invited him to his seat. Zheng Xuan was tall, could drink a handful of wine, had fine features, handsome appearance, and was gentle and majestic.
Most of Yuan Shao's guests were handsome, talented, and good at debating. They saw that Zheng Xuan was a Confucian scholar and thought that he was not a knowledgeable person.
So everyone rushed to imagine some tricky and weird questions, and various schools of thought put forward their opinions one after another.
Zheng Xuan answered and responded according to the orthodox Confucian views, and the content exceeded the scope of the question. Everyone gained knowledge that they had never heard of before, and no one did not admire and admire Zheng Xuan. At this time, Ying Shao from Runan also joined Yuan Shao, so he introduced himself: Ying Zhongyuan, the former governor of Qinshan, would you like to call me your disciple from the north? How about it?
Zheng Xuan smiled and said: Confucius's students had to take exams in four subjects: morality, speech, political affairs, and literature. Students like Yan Yuan and Zigong never claimed their official titles or family status.
Ying Shao felt ashamed after hearing this.
Therefore, Yuan Shao recommended Zheng Xuan as Maocai, and the above table recommended him as Zuo Zhonglang General. Zheng Xuan did not take office.
The imperial court conscripted him as the chief minister of agriculture, gave him a safe car, and stipulated that wherever he passed, officials in charge would greet him and see him off.
Zheng Xuandu requested to return home because he was ill.
Yuan Shao ordered his son Yuan Tan to send envoys to force Zheng Xuan to join the army. Zheng Xuan had no choice but to take his illness to Yuancheng County, where he was seriously ill and unable to advance. Zheng Xuan died in June of this year at the age of seventy-four.
Zheng Xuan's will was buried sparingly.
At that time, more than a thousand people who had been students under Zheng Xuan's sect, including county magistrates and officials, came to the funeral in solemn mourning clothes.
Zheng Xuan's students co-wrote Zheng Xuan's answers to questions raised by his disciples from the "Five Classics" during his lifetime, and compiled it into "Zheng Zhi" in eight chapters according to the style of "The Analects of Confucius".
In total, the books that Zheng Xuan annotated include "The Book of Changes", "Shangshu", "Mao Shi", "Ritual", "Book of Rites", "The Analects", "The Book of Filial Piety", "Shangshu Da Zhuan", "Zhonghou", and "Cheqi Xiangli". Zheng Xuan's self-authored books include "Seven Political Treatises on Astronomy", "The Comprehensive Theory of Lu Li and Emperor Xuan", "Six Art Theory", "Mao Shi Pu", "Refutation of the Different Meanings of Xu Shen's Five Classics", and "Reply to the Difficulty of Lin Xiao and Preserving Zhou Rites", with a total of more than one million words.
Zheng Xuan strived to be simple and realistic in his interpretation of classics. Many knowledgeable people ridiculed this approach as too cumbersome. As for his rich understanding of classics' annotations, he may be called a pure Confucian. People in Qilu respect him as their master.
His students, Xi Luguan from Shanyang, Wang Quan from Donglai, and Cui Yan from Qinghe were all famous in the local area.
Guoyuan and Rengu Duan, both of whom were also from Le'an, were very young at that time. Zheng Xuan praised Dao Guoyuan as a pillar of the country, Ren Gu Duan had noble moral character, and many others also commented and recommended him.
Later, the achievements of these people were as he said. Zheng Xuan only had one son named Zheng Yien. When Kong Rong was the Prime Minister of Beihai, he recommended him as Xiaolian. When Kong Rong was besieged by the Yellow Turban Army, Yi En died in danger.
Yi En had a posthumous son, and Zheng Xuan named him Zheng Xiaotong because his hand lines were similar to his own.

Zhang Chun, courtesy name Boren, was from Duling in Jingzhao. His great-great-grandfather Zhang Anshi served as General Sima Wei under Emperor Xuan and was granted the title of Marquis Fuping. His father Zhang Fang served Emperor Cheng. Zhang Chun inherited his father's title young and served as minister under Emperors Ai and Ping, and continued under Wang Mang. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Zhang Chun retained his title due to his honesty and compliance with law.

In the early Jianwu years, he became a doctor in Taizhong and led troops to farm in Nanyang. Emperor Guangwu refused to abolish his position, renaming him Wu Shihou with half of Fuping County's salary. Zhang Chun was well-versed in old affairs and decided many rituals including sacrifices, weddings, and funerals. The emperor appointed him Huben Zhonglang General, introducing him sometimes four times daily.

Zhang Chun and Zhu Fu memorialized about ancestral temple matters, arguing for proper ritual order. They proposed abolishing the current Qin Temple and following old scriptures. The emperor consulted ministers who recommended replacing the ancestral temple with five emperors and four generations. The emperor complied. Zhang Chun later became imperial servant, then Great Sikong. He opened the Yang Canal for water transportation, benefiting the people. He established regulations for sacrificial ceremonies every three and five years. He proposed building schools and discussed establishing Piyong and Mingtang. In the 30th year, he submitted a memorial about holding a Zen ceremony. In the first Zhongyuan year, the emperor visited Mount Tai with Zhang Chun, who died in March and received the posthumous title Jiehou.

Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was from Xue in Lu State. His father Cao Chong studied the "Qingshi Rites" and became a doctor during Jianwu, establishing various rituals. After Xianzong ascended, Cao Chong discussed ritual and music matters with the emperor, who appreciated his views and appointed him as servant.

Cao Bao was ambitious and generous, inheriting his father's studies at twenty. He was knowledgeable and fond of etiquette, often feeling the imperial system was incomplete. He studied morning and night, even forgetting directions while walking. He was first promoted to Xiaolian, then magistrate of Yuxian County, governing with etiquette. When five thieves were captured, he refused to kill them despite orders, saving their lives. He was dismissed for this but later recruited as a doctor.

When Suzong wanted to formulate rituals and music, Cao Bao presented a memorial. The emperor appointed him as doctor. Later, the emperor ordered him to work on "Han Yi" in Nangong and Dongguan. Cao Bao wrote 150 articles on ritual systems from emperor to commoners. After the emperor died, Cao Bao was promoted to various positions. Some officials complained about his "Han Rites," which was not implemented. He bought land to bury unclaimed coffins, visited patients during epidemics, and saved many lives. He became governor of Hanoi, where rain fell during drought and harvests were abundant. He died in office in fourteen years, having written numerous works including "Tongyi" and "Exemplary Classics," teaching over a thousand students.

Zheng Xuan, courtesy name Kangcheng, was from Gaomi in Beihai. His eighth-generation ancestor Zheng Chong was minister of public affairs under Emperor Ai. As a boy, Zheng Xuan worked as a small official but preferred studying. He studied at Taixue in Beijing under various teachers, becoming proficient in multiple classics. He later studied under Ma Rong, who had over 400 students. Zheng Xuan studied diligently for three years before meeting Ma Rong personally, asking difficult questions before returning home.

After more than ten years of study, he returned to farm in Donglai with hundreds of students. During the party imprisonment disaster, he was imprisoned but continued studying. He refuted He Xiu's theories, impressing He Xiu. When the party ban was lifted, General He Jin recruited him, but Zheng Xuan escaped after one night. At sixty, he had thousands of students. He declined various official positions.

During the Yellow Turban uprising, he took refuge in Xuzhou. In the first Jian'an year, he returned to Gaomi, encountering Yellow Turban troops who bowed and agreed not to enter the county. When seriously ill, he wrote to his son about his life, studies, and hopes for his son's cultivation. Yuan Shao invited him as a guest, where he impressed everyone with his knowledge. He declined Yuan Shao's recommendation as Zuo Zhonglang General. The imperial court conscripted him as chief minister of agriculture, but he requested to return home due to illness. Forced by Yuan Shao's son to join the army, he died at seventy-four in Yuancheng County, buried simply with over a thousand mourners.

His students compiled his answers to questions into "Zheng Zhi." He annotated numerous classics including "The Book of Changes," "Shangshu," "Mao Shi," and "The Analects," writing over one million words. He was respected as a master in Qilu, and his students became famous in their regions.

◆Zhang Zongchuan, also known as Zhang Zongzi Zhujun, was born in Luyang, Nanyang.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he served as the assistant of Yangquan Township in this county.
When Wang Mang failed and rebels broke out, Zhang Zong led three to four hundred people from Yangquan to seize the territory and marched west to Chang'an. Emperor Gengshi appointed Zhang Zong as a partial general.
Zhang Zong saw the political chaos in Gengshi, so he sent his family to Anyi.
Later, the Great Situ Deng Yu went on an expedition to the west and settled Hedong. Zhang Zong went to Deng Yu's place and went back on his own.
Deng Yu heard that Zhang Zongsu was very powerful, so he recommended him to be a partial general.
When Deng Yu's army arrived at the city, the Red Eyebrow Army was approaching. Deng Yu thought that the city was not strong enough to defend and wanted to lead his troops to defend the city. However, everyone was afraid of being chased by thieves and afraid of being a rearguard.
Deng Yu then wrote the names of the generals on the bamboo slips in order, put them randomly in the box, and asked everyone to draw lots.
Zhang Zongdu refused to smoke. He said: Life and death are determined by fate. Is Zhang Zong a person who will give up when it is difficult? Deng Yu sighed and said: "The general has old relatives and weak sons in the camp, why don't you consider it?" Zhang Zong said: I heard that if a soldier tries his best, a hundred people cannot stop him; if ten thousand soldiers are willing to die, they can dominate the world.
Zhang Zongjin has thousands of troops and can withstand the power of the army. Why should he immediately expect defeat? So I stayed and refused.
After all the camps had led their troops and set off, Zhang Zong urged his soldiers to build strongholds and defend them without retreating.
When Deng Yu arrived at Qianxian County, he heard people commenting: "With General Zhang's manpower, trying to stop an army of millions is like throwing Xiaoxue into boiling water. No matter how hard he tries, he can't do it." So he sent 2,000 infantry and cavalry back to greet Zhang Zong.
Zhang Zong led his troops to set out, but the Red Eyebrow Army hurriedly arrived. Zhang Zong fought with him, drove them back, and then returned to the camp. The generals admired his bravery.
After returning to Chang'an, Zhang Zong led his warriors into the city at night to attack Chimei. He was shot between the arms by the enemy.
When Deng Yu was recalled to the capital, Guangwu appointed Zhang Zong as the capital's auxiliary captain. He led the sudden cavalry and conquered the west general Feng Yi to attack the various camps in Guanzhong. After defeating them, he was promoted to the captain of Henan.
In the sixth year of Jianwu's reign, he became the governor of the province and became a senior official in Taizhong.
In the eighth year, bandits arose in Yingchuan Sangzhong, and Zhang Zong led his troops to defeat them and put them down.
Later, bandits from Qingzhou and Jizhou gathered in the mountains and swamps, and Zhang Zong used his visitors to urge the soldiers of the counties to fight for peace.
In the 16th year, bandits from Langyi and Beibu broke out again. Zhang Zong supervised the soldiers of the two counties to attack them. He then formulated a strategy and clearly rewarded those who surrendered. The enemies were all broken up. The bandits in Pei, Chu, Donghai and Linhuai were afraid of his might and killed thousands of each other. The enemies in Qingzhou and Xuzhou were very afraid.
Later, Zhang Zong was promoted to Langfu Prime Minister. His policies were harsh and he dared to kill.
In the second year of Yongping, he died in his official position.
◆Faxiong's biography, Faxiong's courtesy name is Wenqiang, a native of Fufeng County. Descendants of King Qi Xiang Fa Zhang.
The Qin State destroyed the Qi State, and their descendants did not dare to use the surname Tian, ​​so they used the surname Tian.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he moved to Sanfu and made two thousand stones from generation to generation.
Faxiong initially served as a meritorious officer in the county, and later he was promoted to the mansion of Taifu Zhang Yu, where he was promoted to a high rank and appointed chief of the Ping clan.
Faxiong is good at political affairs and likes to expose bad guys. Thieves rarely occur, and officials and the people fear him and love him.
Bao, the prefect of Nanyang, was promoted to the magistrate of Wanling County.
In the third year of Yongchu's reign, the pirate Zhang Bolu and more than 3,000 people, wearing red hats and red clothes, calling themselves "generals", invaded nine coastal counties and killed 2,000 commanders.
At first, the imperial court sent Pang Xiong, the imperial censor, to urge the state and county soldiers to attack them. Bolu and others surrendered, and soon gathered together again.
The next year, Bolu and Pingyuan Liu Wenhe and more than 300 people called him "envoys". They attacked the city of Weichi, killed the officials, and moved to Gaotang County. They burned the official temple and released the prisoners. The leaders were all called "generals" and met Bolu together.
Bo Lu wears a five-beam crown and a seal ribbon, and there are more and more party members.
The imperial court sent Wang Zong, the royal censor, Zhongcheng, to mobilize tens of thousands of soldiers and horses from counties in Youzhou and Jizhou with talismans, and promoted Faxiong to be the governor of Qingzhou to join forces with Wang Zong to attack them.
Lien fought against the thieves, beheaded and drowned hundreds of people, and the rest fled, and confiscated a lot of equipment and property.
Just when the edict of pardon arrived, the thieves still thought that the armor had not been lifted and did not dare to come back and surrender.
So Wang Zong summoned the governor and governor to discuss together, and they all agreed that an attack should be carried out immediately.
Faxiong said: This cannot be the case. Soldiers are weapons and war is dangerous.
Courage cannot be relied upon and victory cannot be guaranteed.
If thieves go out to sea by boat and go deep into distant islands, it will not be so easy to attack.
When the pardon comes, you can temporarily withdraw your troops to comfort and lure them, which will inevitably lead to disbandment, and then think of ways to gain stability without fighting. Wang Zong agreed and immediately stopped his troops.
The thieves were overjoyed when they heard this, so they returned the captives.
However, the Donglai County soldiers did not remove their armor. The thieves were frightened and fled to Liaodong, where they stayed on the island.
In the spring of the fifth year, due to lack of food, they surrounded Donglaijian again. Faxiong led the county soldiers to defeat them. The thieves fled back to Liaodong. Li Jiu and others from Liaodong joined forces to kill them, so the state border became quiet.
Every time Faxiong patrols various ministries, registers prisoners and observes their colors, he can often get the truth of the case. Those who do not implement the law will be relieved of their seals and ribbons and leave their posts.
Faxiong stayed in the state for four years and was promoted to the prefect of Nanjun. He had fewer prisons and fewer provinces, and his household registration increased.
The county is close to Jiangmi, and there is Yunmengsouze. During the Yongchu period, there were many tigers and wolves intruding. The former prefect offered rewards to recruit hunters to capture them, and many people were killed by tigers and wolves.
Faxiong then sent an official document to Qu Dao: Wherever tigers and wolves are in the mountains and forests, it is equivalent to people living in cities.
In the most civilized era of ancient times, ferocious beasts did not invade, all because of the emperor's kindness and kindness, and his kindness spread to all birds and beasts.
Although the prefect was not benevolent enough, he did not dare to forget this meaning.
After the documents arrive, all the wells will be destroyed, and no wild animals will be hunted in the mountains and forests. From then on, the tiger damage stopped and the people lived in peace.
For several years in the county, there were good harvests year after year.
He died in official position in the early Yuan Dynasty.
◆Teng Fu's biography, Teng Fu's courtesy name Shufu, was a dramatist in Beihai.
At first he served as an official in a prefecture and county, and later he was promoted to the magistrate of Zhuo County. He had both civil and military talents.
The prefect thought that he was capable and appointed him to the county post, taking charge of six counties at the same time.
He is politically wise and deeply loved by the people. He has been in office for seven years and has not lost track of his mistakes.
In the last years of Emperor Shun's reign, thieves were everywhere in Yangzhou and Xuzhou, colluding with each other year after year.
In the first year of Jiankang, Fan Rong, Zhou Sheng and others from Jiujiang gathered to rebel and settled in Liyang, which caused a catastrophe in the Jianghuai River. The imperial court sent the Censor Zhongcheng General Feng Zui to urge Yangzhou Governor Yin Huozhai and Jiujiang Governor Deng Xian to attack them. Yao and Xian were defeated and killed by thieves.
Xu Feng, Ma Mian and others from Yinling also invaded counties and killed officials and people.
Xu Feng wore red clothes with a black ribbon and called himself the "Supreme General". Ma Mian wore a fur hat, yellow clothes, and a jade seal. He was called the Yellow Emperor and built a fort in Dangtu Mountain.
So he established a reign title, appointed hundreds of officials, and sent Marshal Huang Hu to capture Hefei.
The next year, Guangling thief Zhang Ying and others gathered thousands of people to rebel and occupied Guangling.
The imperial court extensively solicited generals, and the three princes recommended Teng Fu, saying that he had all-round talents in both civil and military affairs. He was appointed the captain of Jiujiang, and he and the general Zhao Xu assisted Feng Yu in the crusade together with tens of thousands of people from prefectures and counties.
They also widely opened up rewards, money, and towns, each with different levels.
The Empress Dowager Liang was worried that the generals would be unable to subdue the thieves who were stationed there and colluded, so she suggested sending Lieutenant Li Gu.
Before setting off, they encountered Teng Fu and others advancing to attack the thieves. They defeated them and beheaded one thousand and five of Ma Mian, Fan Rong, Zhou Sheng, etc. Xu Feng led the rest of the army to attack Dongcheng County.
Xie An, a native of Xiapi, responded to the call and led his clan members to set up an ambush to attack Xu Feng and beheaded him. The imperial court granted Xie An the title of Marquis of Pingxiang, with a city of 3,000 households.
He worshiped Teng Fu as Zhonglang General and supervised the affairs of Yangzhou and Xuzhou.
Teng Fu attacked Zhang Ying again and captured more than a thousand people.
Zhao Xu committed the crime of cowardice and falsely increased his rank, so he was recalled to have his head executed in public.
In addition, the Liyang thief Hua Meng claimed to be the "Black Emperor" and attacked Jiujiang, killing the county guard.
Teng Fu took advantage of the victory to attack and defeated Hua Meng and other 3,800 people, and captured more than 700 people, including cattle, horses and property.
So everything in the southeast was pacified, and the army was reorganized and returned.
The imperial court appointed Zuo Fengyi as governor, except for one son who was appointed as Lang.
All the rewards Teng Fu received were given to his subordinates.
Teng Fu had an upright character and did not associate with powerful people, so the eunuchs held grudges.
When the time came to reward him based on his merits, the Taiwei Hu Guang recorded the minister's affairs and submitted an imperial edict to depose Teng. The whole world became resentful.
Later, Teng Fu died at home.
◆The biography of Feng Kui, whose courtesy name was Hongqing, was from Danqu, Ma County. When he was young, he studied "Spring and Autumn" and "Sima's Art of War".
His father, Feng Huan, served as the governor of Youzhou during the reign of Emperor An. He hated traitors and punished them many times for their crimes.
At that time, Yao Guang, the prefect of Xuantu, also had uncoordinated personnel relations.
In the first year of Jianguang, the resentful people forged seals to condemn Feng Huan and Yao Guang, and gave them European swords.
He also issued an edict to Pang Fen, the captain of Liaodong, to execute the punishment as soon as possible. Pang Fen executed Yao Guang and detained Feng Huan.
Feng Huan wanted to commit suicide. Feng Sui suspected that the edict was false, so he stopped Feng Huan and said: "When you were in the state, you wanted to get rid of the evildoers. There is really no other reason. The murderer must be blackmailing and using poisonous tricks."
I would like to report the matter to the higher authorities. If it is true, it is not too late to plead guilty. Feng Huan listened to his son's words and wrote a letter to tell the truth. It was indeed a cunning person. The emperor summoned Pang Fen to plead guilty.
It happened that Feng Huan died in prison, and the emperor sympathized with him. Feng Huan and Yao Guang were given 100,000 yuan each, and their sons were appointed as doctors.
Feng Cui became famous from then on.
Feng Nian's family was rich and he was fond of charity and helped the poor and needy, so he was loved by the people in the state.
At first, he was promoted as Xiaolian, promoted seven times to become the captain of the Guanghan vassal state, and was also recruited to be the censor Zhongcheng.
In the last years of Emperor Shun's reign, the imperial court sent Feng Kui to supervise the military affairs of the counties in Yangzhou. Together with Zhonglang General Teng Fu, he defeated the bandits and moved to Longxi as the prefect.
After telling everyone to surrender, the barbarians stopped their activities and dispersed back to their original places. Later, Feng Zui became Jing Zhaoyin and transferred to Sili Xiaowei, and established threats and punishments wherever he was.
Later he was promoted to Tingwei and Taichang.
At this time, the Changsha barbarians invaded Yiyang and gathered there for a long time. By the fifth year of Yanxi, there were more followers, and the Lingling barbarians also colluded with them. A total of more than 20,000 people attacked and burned the city, killing and wounding the officials.
In addition, all Wuling barbarians rebelled and plundered the Jiangling area. Liu Du, the governor of Jingzhou, and Li Su, the governor of Nanjun, both abandoned their posts and fled, and Jingnan fell into enemy hands.
The imperial court then appointed Feng Kui as the general of chariots and cavalry, and led more than 100,000 people to attack them. The edict was written to Feng Kui: The barbarians invaded China, and they did not attack them for a long time. They burned the capital and trampled on the officials and people.
The generals and officials of the prefectures and counties, and the ministers who were dead in their duties, ran away from each other and never looked back. How shameful.
The general had a reputation for being powerful, so he was promoted to the Sixth Division.
The disciples of Chen Tang, Feng and Fu in the previous generation used less to attack more. The enemies of Zhizhi, Yelang and Loulan had their heads hung in the streets for public display. Wei Qing and Huo Guang went to the north and made great achievements. This is all known to the general.
Now, if not the general, who can restore the achievements of the previous dynasty?
Advances and retreats, as well as strategies for power and time, are all under the exclusive control of the general, and matters outside the suburbs are no longer managed internally.
An official has been ordered to hold a farewell ceremony at the gate of the country.
Didn't "The Book of Songs" say: When a tiger minister enters the country, he will be like a nine-strong tiger.
General, encourage me!
At this time, there was famine in the world and the treasury was empty. Every time we sent out troops to fight, the salaries of ministers were often reduced, and they borrowed taxes from princes and sent generals forward and backward.
Feng Zui had a strong and upright character and could not take bribes, but he was afraid of being slandered by the eunuchs, so he went to the court and said: If you listen to slander, Boyi can also be suspicious. If you are not suspected, Robber Zhi can also be trusted.
So Leyangzi performed the formation meritorious service, and Marquis Wen gave him a basket of slanderous letters.
I would like to ask you to send a permanent servant to supervise the military finances. Shangshu Zhu Mu reported that Feng Kui used money to avoid suspicion, which was against the integrity of a minister.
There is an edict not to impeach anyone.
Feng Cui's army arrived in Changsha. After hearing the news, the thieves all went to the camp road to beg for surrender.
Feng Kui attacked the Wuling barbarians, beheaded more than 4,000 people, and surrendered more than 100,000 people. Jingzhou was pacified.
The imperial edict granted 100 million yuan, but Feng Zui refused.
Feng Cui led the army back to the capital, commended him for his merits to Zhonglang Yingfeng, and recommended him to be the Sili Xiaowei. However, he wrote a letter requesting to retire, but the court refused.
Zhang Chang, the eunuch who oversaw the army, followed the eunuch's decree and followed Feng Gui, Fu and his maidservants, in uniform. He often carved stones in Jiangling to commemorate his achievements, and requested to issue edicts to the officials for trial.
The minister ordered Huang Jun to report that there was no justice for the crime and should not be entangled.
It happened that the bandits in Changsha recurred and attacked Guiyang and Wuling. Feng Zui was dismissed because the army returned and the bandits recurred.
Soon, he was promoted to be a great craftsman and promoted to Henan Yin.
The letter said: According to the old rules, children of middle-ranking officials are not allowed to hold the position of shepherd. The emperor did not accept it.
He became a Tingwei again.
At that time, Shanyin prefect Shan Qian was imprisoned for his crime, and Feng Kui examined him and sentenced him to death.
Shan moved, so he was the younger brother of Chariot and Cavalry General Shan Chao. The middle and high-ranking officials protected each other, so they falsely accused Feng Zui, and together with Li Ying, the lieutenant of Sili School, and Liu, the chief minister of Nong, were defeated by the Zuo School.
You should intercede with Shu Weijian and others, and you will be exempted from guilt. Later, he became a captain of the Cavalry School and a court captain, and died in his official position.
◆Du Shangzhuan, whose courtesy name was Boping, was from Shanyin Hulu.
He was from a poor family, had not completed his studies, and was not recommended by the village.
After many years of poverty, he took care of the land for his eunuch, Marquis Lan of the same county, became the county's accountant, became a doctor, and was appointed chief of Yu.
He is very strict and knows how to spot bad people and bad deeds. Officials call him a god.
Later, he was promoted to the magistrate of Wen'an County. When a disease was prevalent and the nobles were hungry, Du Shang opened a warehouse and took out grain to rescue the sick, and the people received relief.
At that time, Zhu Mu, the governor of Jizhou, came to inspect and was very surprised to see Du Shang.
In the fifth year of Yanxi's reign, a total of seven or eight thousand bandits from Changsha and Lingling, who were called generals, invaded Guiyang, Cangwu, Nanhai, and Jiaozhi. The governor of Jiaozhi and the prefect of Cangwu Wangfeng fled, and both counties fell into the hands of thieves.
The imperial court sent the censor Zhongcheng Shengxiu to recruit troops to attack, but he could not win.
There were more than 600 people from Ai County in Yuzhang who applied for the army but did not receive any reward. Feeling resentful, they rebelled, burned the counties in Changsha, invaded Yiyang, killed the county magistrate, and the number of followers increased.
The imperial court also sent an envoy, Ma Mu, to supervise Liu Du, the governor of Jingzhou, to attack. The battle was defeated, and both Ma Mu and Liu Du fled.
Emperor Huan ordered the ministers to recommend someone to replace Liu Du, and Shangshu Zhu Mu recommended Du Shang, who was promoted from the right school magistrate to the governor of Jingzhou.
Du Shang personally led his men and worked and rested with them. At the same time, he recruited all kinds of barbarians and offered rewards. He attacked the thieves and defeated them. Tens of thousands of people surrendered.
The old bandit leaders in Guiyang, Bu Yang and Pan Hong, were afraid of Du Shang's majesty and fled to the valley.
Du Shang pursued for hundreds of miles, and the thieves arrived in the South China Sea. They broke into three villages and obtained many treasures.
However, there were still many party members such as Bu Yang and Pan Hong. Du Shang wanted to continue the pursuit, but the soldiers were proud and had no fighting spirit.
Du Shang thought that if he delayed his troops, he would not be able to fight, and if he was forced to fight, he would flee, so he threatened Buyang and Pan Hong who had been thieves for ten years and were accustomed to attacking and retreating. Now there are too few soldiers to attack easily. You should wait for all the troops from the counties to arrive before you attack with them.
He also ordered the troops to go hunting. The soldiers were so happy that they all went hunting together.
Du Shang then secretly sent his cronies to secretly burn down the fortress, destroying all his treasures and savings.
Everyone came back from hunting without crying.
Du Shang expressed his condolences to everyone and deeply blamed himself, so he said: "Bu Yang and others have enough wealth to support several generations, but you are just not doing your best."
There are so few things lost, so why bother. After hearing this, everyone was indignant and excited, and came forward. Du Shang ordered the horses to have breakfast, and early the next morning, they went straight to the thief's residence.
Bu Yang, Pan Hong and others thought that the fortress was deep and solid, so they no longer took precautions. The officials attacked with vigor, and then defeated the bandits and leveled the bandits' nest.
Three years after Du Shang sent troops, all the bandits were put down.
In the seventh year, he was granted the title of Marquis of Youxiang and promoted to the prefect of Guiyang.
The next year, the capital was recalled.
At this time, Jingzhou soldiers Zhu Shan and others had been out for a long time and had insufficient financial resources. The soldiers were resentful and started rebellion again. Together with the Guiyang thief Hu Lan and more than 3,000 people, they attacked Guiyang again and burned the counties. The prefect Ren Yin abandoned the city and fled, and the number of thieves increased to tens of thousands.
Turning to attack Lingling, the prefect Chen Qiu defended the city and resisted the enemy.
The imperial court then sent Du Shang as Zhonglang General, leading 26,000 infantry and cavalry from Youzhou, Jizhou, Liyang, and Wuhuan to rescue Chen Qiu. He also mobilized troops from various counties with Changsha Governor Kang Xu and others to attack together, and defeated the thieves, beheading Hu Lan and other 3,500 people. The remaining thieves fled to Cangwu.
The imperial court issued an edict to reward Du Shang with a million yuan, and the rest of the people received different rewards.
At this time, Kangxu and Dushang were both famous generals and had made many meritorious deeds.
Xu, courtesy name Boxu, was from Danyang, and his countrymen praised him for his courage and wisdom.
At the beginning of the trial of guarding Xuancheng, all the natives who were far away in the deep forest, with their vertebrae and chirping in their buns and chirping birds, moved to the county. From then on, there were no more thieves in the territory.
Later, he became the Sima of the Zhongzi branch of Zhonglang General, defeated the Taishan bandits Gongsun Ju and others, defeated them, beheaded more than 3,000 people, and was granted the title of Marquis of Dongxiang, Wucheng, and enjoyed the title of 500 households in the city.
Later, he was promoted to the captain of Taishan, and the bandit Wangfeng escaped.
After arriving in Changsha, all the old thieves were put down.
Die in office.
Emperor Huan issued an edict and granted 500 additional households in Xu, adding to the previous total of 1,000 households.
The imperial court also sent Du Shang to be the governor of Jingzhou.
Du Shang saw Hu Lanyu's party fleeing south to Cangwu, and was afraid of being defeated by him, so he fabricated news that Cangwu bandits were invading the Jingzhou border, and summoned Zhang Panxia Tingwei, the governor of Quzhi.
He was pardoned before the petition was written.
Zhang Pan refused to be released from prison because he insisted on holding on to his weapons. The jailer said to Zhang Pan: "God's grace is unprecedented but you don't come out, is that okay?" Zhang Pan then defended himself and said: In the past, Hu Lan, the Changsha thief, made trouble in Jingzhou, and the remaining party dispersed into Jiaochangzhi.
Wearing armor, I risked my life to fight against the vicious thieves and killed their leader. The rest of the gang fled and returned to Jingzhou.
The governor, Du Shang, was afraid that I would speak first, and that he would be blamed and that he would be wronged in the memorial.
I am preparing to serve as Fang Bo, a minion of the state, but I was wronged by Du Shang and sentenced to prison.
Things may be false or true, and laws may be right or wrong.
I really have no fault and nothing can be forgiven.
If you endure it, you will suffer the shame of being insulted forever, live as a bad official, and die as a ghost.
The request for transmission came to Tingwei. Faced with the merits, it was clear whether it was true or false.
For those who have not yet been punished, I will bury their bones in a prison and never come out for the rest of my life, hoping to clear up the injustice. The Tingwei sent his petition, and the emperor issued an edict to summon Shang to the Tingwei. He resigned and suffered the punishment, and was forgiven because he had performed meritorious service first.
Zhang Pan, courtesy name Zishi, was from Danyang and was known for his innocence. He died while serving as the governor of Hujiang.
Dushang later became the governor of Liaodong. A few months later, the Xianbei people led their troops to attack Dushang, fought with him, and defeated him. From then on, the Rong and Di were afraid.
At the age of fifty, in the ninth year of Yanxi's reign, he died in office.
◆Yang Xuan's biography, Yang Xuan's calligraphy is Jiping, Kuaiji Wushangren.
My great-great-grandfather, Yang Mao, was originally from Hedong. He followed Emperor Guangwu in his conquests, became a powerful general of the invaders, and was granted the title of Marquis of Wushang Xinyang Township.
During the Jianwu period, he arrived in the capital and was granted the third title. He was later dismissed for being guilty, so he returned to his hometown.
His father, Yang Fu, was the governor of Jiaozhi and had a reputation for being capable.
My elder brother, Yang Qiao, became a minister. He had a beautiful appearance and wrote many letters to discuss political affairs. Emperor Huan liked his talent and appearance and issued an edict to marry the princess to him. Yang Qiao refused firmly, but the emperor refused to listen, so he kept silent and refused to eat. He died in seven days.
Yang Xuan was initially promoted to Xiaolian, and after some time, he became the prefect of Lingling during the reign of Emperor Ling.
At this time, cunning thieves from Cangwu and Guiyang gathered together to attack the counties. There were many thieves but Yang Xuan's troops were weak. The officials and the people were very worried. Yang Xuan then specially built dozens of carriages, filled the carriages with a row of bags filled with lime, and tied cloth ropes to the horses' tails. He also made military carriages, specially equipped with bows and crossbows, and agreed on a date for the battle.
So he ordered the carriage in front, blowing up the ashes with the wind, so that the thieves could not open their eyes, and burned the cloth with fire. The horses were frightened and rushed into the bandit formation. Then they called the carriage behind and fired their bows and crossbows. The sound of drums and drums shook the sky. The thieves scattered in fear. They chased, wounded and beheaded countless thieves, and the leader's head was displayed to the public. Peace was restored within the county.
Zhao Kai, the governor of Jingzhou, falsely accused Yang Xuan of not killing the thieves himself, but of claiming his merits.
Yang Xuanxiang and Zhang Zuo, Zhao Kai had party members to help, so the court used a carriage to recall Yang Xuan.
The ban was tight and there was no chance to explain the reason, so he bit his arm and it bled, and wrote a memorial in blood, detailing the situation of defeating the thief. He also talked about Zhao Kai's false accusation and secretly called his relatives to report to the court.
The imperial edict forgave Yang Xuan and worshiped him as Yilang, but Zhao Kai was accused of falsely accusing others.
Yang Xuan was promoted three times and became the prefect of Bohai. He showed signs of heterodoxy wherever he went, and was later dismissed due to circumstances.
Later, the minister ordered Zhang Wente to recommend him to the minister, Pushe.
He asked to retire due to illness and died at home.
summary:
Zhang Zong, from Luyang, served as an assistant during Wang Mang’s reign. After Wang Mang’s fall, he led 300–400 people to seize territory and was appointed a partial general by Emperor Gengshi. Seeing political chaos, he moved his family to Anyi. Later, he joined Deng Yu, who recommended him as a partial general. When the Red Eyebrow Army approached, Deng Yu wanted to retreat, but Zhang Zong refused to draw lots for rearguard duty, declaring he would not abandon his post. He defended his camp, and Deng Yu sent reinforcements. Zhang Zong fought bravely, driving back the Red Eyebrows. He later attacked them at night in Chang'an and was wounded. Under Guangwu, he became a captain, fought in Guanzhong, and was promoted. He suppressed bandits in Yingchuan, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, and later in Langyi and Beibu. As Langfu Prime Minister, he governed harshly. He died in office in the second year of Yongping.

Faxiong, from Fufeng, was a descendant of King Qi Xiang. After Qin destroyed Qi, his family used the surname Fa. He served as a meritorious officer and later as chief of Ping clan, known for exposing criminals. In the third year of Yongchu, pirate Zhang Bolu led 3,000 rebels, invading nine counties. Faxiong was promoted to Qingzhou governor to join Wang Zong in attacking them. After initial victories, a pardon arrived. Faxiong advised against immediate attack, suggesting withdrawal to lure the rebels into surrender. Wang Zong agreed, but Donglai soldiers kept their armor, causing rebels to flee to Liaodong. In spring of the fifth year, rebels returned, and Faxiong defeated them. He later became Nanjun prefect, where he reduced tiger attacks by ordering the destruction of traps and halting hunting. He died in office in the early Yuan Dynasty.

Teng Fu, from Beihai, served as Zhuo County magistrate, known for civil and military talents. In the first year of Jiankang, rebels Fan Rong and Zhou Sheng rose in Jiujiang, and Xu Feng and Ma Mian rebelled in Yinling. The court sent Teng Fu as Jiujiang captain with General Zhao Xu to suppress them. They defeated the rebels, beheading 1,500, including Ma Mian and Fan Rong. Xu Feng was killed by Xie An. Teng Fu became Zhonglang General, overseeing Yangzhou and Xuzhou. He defeated Zhang Ying and later Hua Meng, pacifying the southeast. He was appointed Zuo Fengyi but was deposed by eunuchs due to his upright character. He died at home.

Feng Kui, from Ma County, studied *Spring and Autumn* and *Sima's Art of War*. His father Feng Huan was falsely accused and imprisoned. Feng Kui suspected the edict was forged and urged his father to appeal, revealing the truth. Feng Kui became famous for his charity. He served as Guanghan captain and censor, later defeating bandits with Teng Fu. As Longxi prefect, he pacified barbarians. He became Jing Zhaoyin and Sili Xiaowei, known for strictness. Later, as Tingwei and Taichang, he led 100,000 troops to suppress barbarian revolts in Changsha and Wuling, beheading 4,000 and surrendering 100,000. He refused rewards and retired, but was recalled. He was dismissed after bandits recurred but later reinstated as Henan Yin and Tingwei. He died in office.

Du Shang, from Shanyin, rose from poverty to become Yu chief, known for strictness. As Wen'an magistrate, he relieved famine. In the fifth year of Yanxi, bandits from Changsha and Lingling invaded several counties. Du Shang was appointed Jingzhou governor, personally leading troops and offering rewards. He defeated the bandits, pursuing them to Nanhai. To motivate his soldiers, he burned his own treasures, then led a surprise attack, destroying the bandits' nest. He was made Marquis of Youxiang and Guiyang prefect. Later, when rebels rose again, he was sent as Zhonglang General, defeating them and beheading 3,500. He became Jingzhou governor again but falsely accused Zhang Pan. After a trial, he was pardoned for prior merits. He later served as Liaodong governor, defeating the Xianbei. He died in office at age fifty.

Yang Xuan, from Kuaiji, was a descendant of Yang Mao. His brother Yang Qiao refused to marry a princess and starved to death. Yang Xuan became Lingling prefect during Emperor Ling's reign. When thieves attacked, he used lime-filled carts and burning cloth to blind and scatter them, defeating the rebels. Governor Zhao Kai falsely accused him, but Yang Xuan wrote a blood memorial to the court, clearing his name. He was promoted to Yilang, and Zhao Kai was punished. He later became Bohai prefect but was dismissed. He retired due to illness and died at home.

◆Zhang Hao's biography, Zhang Hao's courtesy name was Shuming, and he was a native of Wuyang, Qianwei County. Zhang Liang, the sixth generation ancestor, was the prince's young master during the reign of Emperor Gao and was granted the title of Liuhou.
When Zhang Hao was young, he traveled to the capital to study. In Yongyuanzhong, he returned to the prefecture and served as an official. He established the mansion of General Deng Zhi. He was promoted to Shangshu Pushe five times and served for eight years before becoming the prime minister of Pengcheng.
In the first year of Yongning, he was promoted to Tingwei.
Although Zhang Hao was not a Legalist, he paid attention to punishment and imprisonment, and often argued with ministers to correct doubts and doubts. Most of his opinions were adopted after careful consideration.
At this time, Emperor An deposed the crown prince as King of Jiyin, and Zhang Hao argued with Taichang Huanyan and Taipu about the origins of the throne in the court, but to no avail.

Cao Jie said nothing more, so the discussion was settled.

Zhang Hao, courtesy name Shuming, was from Wuyang, Qianwei County. His sixth-generation ancestor Zhang Liang served as prince's young master under Emperor Gao and was granted the title of Liuhou. Zhang Hao studied in the capital as a youth, later served as an official, and was promoted five times to Shangshu Pushe before becoming prime minister of Pengcheng. In Yongning's first year, he became Tingwei. Though not a Legalist, he emphasized proper punishment and often debated with ministers to correct doubts. When Emperor An deposed the crown prince, Zhang Hao argued unsuccessfully with officials. He later submitted a memorial citing historical examples of wrongful accusations and urging the selection of virtuous advisors for the young prince, but his advice was rejected. Under Emperor Shun, Zhang Hao became Sikong and promoted many talents. When Zhao Teng and others were arrested for criticizing the government, Zhang Hao admonished the emperor, citing ancient practices of accepting remonstrance, and persuaded him to reduce their sentences. He was removed from office due to natural disasters, reinstated as Tingwei in Yangjia's first year, and died in office at age eighty-three.

Zhang Hao's son Zhang Gang, courtesy name Wen Ji, was proficient in Confucian classics and strictly maintained integrity. He became imperial censor under Emperor Shun. Distressed by the emperor's indulgence of eunuchs, Zhang Gang submitted a memorial contrasting the frugal governance of earlier Han emperors with current corruption, urging reform. The emperor did not accept it. In Han'an's first year, when eight envoys were selected to inspect customs, Zhang Gang alone buried his carriage wheel in Luoyang, declaring he would investigate the powerful rather than minor officials. He submitted a report condemning General Liang Ji and his relatives for corruption and tyranny. Though the emperor knew Zhang Gang was truthful, he did not act due to Liang Ji's influence. Liang Ji then appointed Zhang Gang as prefect of Guangling, hoping the bandit troubles there would destroy him. Zhang Gang went alone with few officials to meet the bandit leader Zhang Ying, persuading him to surrender through sincere discussion of loyalty and consequences. Over ten thousand people surrendered. Zhang Gang died at forty-six, with the people mourning deeply and Zhang Ying leading over five hundred in mourning attire to build his tomb.

Wang Gong, courtesy name Bo Zong, was from Gaoping County, Shanyang. He served as Qingzhou governor, impeaching corrupt officials, and was promoted to Shangshu. He became Runan prefect, where he promoted moderate governance and introduced talented individuals like Huang Xian and Chen Fan. When Chen Fan left a note claiming illness after not being immediately received, Wang Gong initially wanted to dismiss him but was persuaded otherwise by meritorious official Yuan Lang. Wang Gong later became Taiwei, maintaining strict propriety and appointing respected elders. Concerned about eunuch power, he submitted a memorial requesting their banishment. Eunuchs retaliated by falsely accusing him, and Emperor Shun ordered him to confess. Li Gu wrote to General Liang Shang urging intervention, citing historical precedents, and the matter was resolved. Wang Gong served five years before retiring due to age and illness, dying at home.

Wang Gong's son Wang Chang, courtesy name Shumao, was known for honesty. He served in various positions including Yuyang prefect, where he was praised for seriousness and shrewdness. After being dismissed, he was recommended by Taiwei Chen Fan and became minister, then Nanyang governor. He harshly punished corrupt officials, demolishing houses and cutting down trees of those who concealed stolen goods. Meritorious official Zhang Chang advised leniency, citing historical examples of benevolent governance. Wang Chang accepted this advice and implemented lenient governance. He personally practiced frugality to correct extravagant habits. When advising young Liu Biao, Wang Chang emphasized moderation and cited historical examples of integrity. He later became Sikong but was dismissed due to floods, dying at home the following year.

Zhong Hao, courtesy name Jing Bo, was from Luoyang County. After his father died, he used his inheritance to help the poor. He was recommended as filial and incorrupt by Wang Chen, who recognized his potential. Zhong Hao served as censor under Emperor Shun, impeaching corrupt officials recommended by Liang Ji. When eunuch Gao Fan came to meet the crown prince, Zhong Hao prevented him from entering without proper authorization, earning imperial praise. As Yizhou governor, he extended Han influence to foreign tribes. He exposed a prefect who presented gold snakes to Liang Ji, earning Liang Ji's enmity. After being framed by Liang Ji, he was pardoned due to Li Gu's intervention. He later served as Liangzhou governor, winning great popularity, and as Hanyang prefect, where he taught Qiang and Hu people. As general against the Xiongnu, he secured border peace through sincere persuasion. He became Situ in Yanxi's fourth year, recommending capable ministers, and died at sixty-one, mourned by border residents and even the Xiongnu.

Zhong Hao's son Zhong Dai, courtesy name Gongzu, loved learning but refused official appointments, dying of illness. His brother Zhong Fu, courtesy name Yingbo, served as Wan County magistrate, where he shamed corrupt officials into reform. He became Sikong but was dismissed due to earthquakes. When Li Chu and Guo Si rebelled, Zhong Fu fought to the death in the palace, dying alongside his son Zhong Shao. Zhong Shao, courtesy name Shenfu, served as an admonishing official. He confronted Dong Zhuo, forcing him to retreat. After Dong Zhuo seized power, Zhong Shao refused high office, declaring he could not face the emperor while his father's murderers remained unpunished. He joined Ma Teng and others to attack Li Chu and Guo Si but died in battle.

Chen Qiu, courtesy name Bo Zhen, was from Huaipu County, Xiapi. He was learned in Confucianism and law. As Fanyang magistrate, he refused to send bribes to the Wei prefect, who could not dismiss him due to his good reputation. As Lingling prefect, he defeated bandits and suppressed a rebellion, using innovative defensive tactics. He later became Nanyang governor but was slandered by powerful families and returned home. As Tingwei, he argued successfully for Empress Dowager Dou to be buried with Emperor Huan, despite opposition from eunuchs Cao Jie and Wang Fu. He later became Sikong but was dismissed due to earthquakes. He secretly plotted with Liu to kill eunuchs, but his wife's relative Cheng Huang betrayed them to Cao Jie. The emperor imprisoned Chen Qiu, who died in prison at sixty-two.

After he was promoted to a servant, the emperor led him into the palace and satirized him.
