He criticized prophecies as false, noting they emerged only after the Cheng and Ai periods and contradicted classical texts. He urged their suppression to prevent confusion.

Later, as Prime Minister of Hejian, Zhang Heng curbed the king's arrogance and lawlessness, earning a reputation for integrity. After three years, he requested retirement and died at sixty-two. He authored thirty-two works, including poems and essays. He also sought to correct historical records, arguing that Wang Mang's biography should focus on usurpation and that Gengshi's title should precede Guangwu's, but his proposals were not accepted. The historian praised his profound wisdom and mechanical ingenuity, noting that his virtue was not diminished by his skills.

translation:
In the beginning, Guangwu was born among the people. He knew the truth of the world very well and witnessed the hardships of farming and the diseases of the people. Therefore, after the world was settled, he strived for peace, eliminated the complicated methods of Wang Mang's period, and restored the lenient methods of the Han Dynasty.
He wears rough clothes without a second color. Guang Wu's ears do not listen to the sound of Mi Mi, his hands do not play with pearls and jade, there is no preference in the harem, and the ministers near him are not treated differently.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, foreign countries presented famous horses that could run thousands of miles in a day, and also presented swords, which were worth hundreds of kilograms of gold. The edict ordered the chariots to be driven by horses and drums, and swords were given to the knights.
They also reduced the number of officials in Shangzheng Garden and abolished things like traveling and hunting.
The handwritten letters given by the emperor to localities and vassal states are all in ten lines and written in small characters.
The atmosphere of diligence and frugality prevailed in the imperial court.
The emperor repeatedly asked ministers and generals to sit on the throne.
He visited extensively to inquire about the sufferings of the people and collected folk songs.
Therefore, no one inside or outside the court dared to slack off, and the people got a rest.
The local governors competed for their efforts.
For example, Du Shi served as the governor of Nanyang and was called "Du Mu". Ren Yan and Xiguang changed the customs in the border areas. These are the people with the most remarkable political achievements.
There are also Wu Lun, Song Jun and others, who also have many things worthy of praise.
However, during the Jianwu and Yongping years, political affairs were too strict and detailed, and local governors were replaced many times based on rumors and one-sided remarks.
Therefore, Zhu Fu wrote many times and put forward sharp opinions. Zhong Zhengtong and others also repeatedly gave advice. They spoke as loyal and generous elders, but they were not adopted.
Therefore, Mosaic during the ZTE period still had shortcomings.
Since Emperor Zhang and Emperor He, some officials with outstanding political achievements have continued to appear.
For example, Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan and the four county magistrates of Tichuan all used their benevolence, faith, loyalty and honesty to prevent people from cheating; Wang Tang and Chen Chong appointed virtuous and talented people, and political affairs were naturally managed: these can move all things and promote education.
Bian Feng and Yan Du successively served as Jing Zhaoyin, and people compared them to Zhao Guangmo and Zhang Chang.
In addition, Wang Huan and Ren Jun served as the Luoyang Order, publicly punishing bad people and bad things, and the officialdom improved, and what was forbidden was naturally prohibited. Although there were some imperfections in terms of morality and etiquette, they were still good officials at that time.
Now the good officials with outstanding achievements are brought together as "Xunli Chapter".
◆The biography of Wei Sa, Wei Sa, courtesy name Zichan, was a martial arts practitioner in Hanoi.
Wei Sa came from a poor family but loved learning. He studied with a teacher but had no food, so he often relied on work to survive.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he served as the governor of Yuzhou.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he went to serve in the mansion of Grand Situ Deng Yu.
He was appointed as an imperial censor and a magistrate of Xiangcheng for recommending talented people to handle heavy official duties.
He had a good reputation and achievements in politics, and was promoted to the prefect of Guiyang.
Guiyang borders Jiaozhou and is greatly influenced by Jiaozhou. The people do not know etiquette.
After Wei Sa took office, he built schools, rectified education, and formulated marriage etiquette.
In one year, the atmosphere has changed drastically.
Originally, the three counties of Hancheng, Yanyang and Qujiang belonged to the Yue region. After Emperor Wu pacified the Yue region, they were restored to Guiyang.
The people live in the mountains, relying on streams, following the customs and habits of the past, and do not pay land rent.
Some places far away from the county are nearly a thousand miles away.
When officials come and go to do business, they always dispatch people to drive boats to pick them up, which is called "passenger service".
Every time an official goes out, corvee service is assigned to several houses, and the people suffer.
Wei Sa then dug more than 500 miles of mountain roads, built inns, and set up a post office.
This reduces labor and eliminates the cunning of officials.
The expatriate people slowly came back and gradually gathered into villages and towns, and then they were required to pay taxes like common people.
In addition, Leiyang County produces iron ore, and people from other counties often gather together to smelt iron privately. As a result, they attract desperadoes and lead to many robberies.
Wei Sa then wrote to ask for the establishment of officials responsible for iron casting, and did not allow private iron casting. This would increase the annual income by more than 5 million yuan.
Wei Sa is good at handling civil affairs and is considerate of people's sentiments. Being an official is like managing his own family, and all the policies he implements are reasonable.
He served for ten years and the county was in peace.
In the twenty-fifth year, Wei Sa was requisitioned by the imperial court.
Guangwu wanted to appoint him as the Shaofu, but just as he was ill and unable to take charge, Guangwu ordered him to go home to recuperate as the governor of Guiyang and wait for the Shao Shu.
Two years later, Wei Sa came to the court sick and said that he was seriously ill. The emperor then took back his seal and ribbon and gave him one hundred thousand yuan. He later died at home.
Zhilijie directly served as the governor of Zhuwu for Lao, and he was also good at governance.
He taught the people to plant mulberry, hemp, and other things, and encouraged them to raise silkworms and weave shoes, and the people benefited a lot.
◆Ren Yanchuan, Ren Yan, courtesy name Changsun, was from Wan County, Nanyang.
At the age of twelve, he became a student of Taixue and studied in Chang'an. He was proficient in "Shi Zhi", "Book of Changes" and "Spring and Autumn". He was famous in Taixue and was called "Ren Shengtong" in the academy.
Catching up with the war and chaos, he took refuge in Longxi.
At that time, Kaixiao had occupied the four counties of Longxi and sent people to invite Ren Yan, but Ren Yan ignored him.
In the first year of Gengshi, Ren Yan was appointed as a subordinate of Da Sima and awarded the post of Captain of Kuaiji.
He was nineteen years old at the time, and the officials who came to pick him up were surprised to see him young.
After he arrived at the county, he was indifferent and did nothing. He just sent people to bring sacrifices to sacrifice Yanling Jizha.
At that time, the world had just been peaceful and the roads were blocked. Those who came to the south of the Yangtze River for refuge did not return to the Central Plains, so there were many talented people in Kuaiji.
After Ren Yan took office, he hired all persons of high moral character, such as Dong Ziyi and Yan Ziling, and treated them with the courtesy of mentors and friends.
When his subordinates were in need, he would always use his salary to help them.
He laid off his soldiers and asked them to cultivate the public fields in order to feed the poor.
Every time he visited various counties, he always sent people to visit his filial sons and entertain them for meals.
There was a man named Long Qiuchang in the Wu region who lived in seclusion in Taimo and remained determined.
During Wang Mang's period, the Fourth Assistant and the Third Duke called him to serve as officials one after another, but he refused to go.
The governor reported to Ren Yan and asked him to be summoned.
Ren Yan said: Mr. Longqiu practices morality and justice, and has the integrity of Yuan Xian and Boyi.
I came to the house to sprinkle water and sweep the floor, and I was worried about humiliating him, so summoning him was absolutely not allowed.
So he sent a meritorious officer to visit him with gifts, wrote him letters, and sent him medicine. The messengers came one after another.
A year later, Long Qiuchang came to the county government by car and expressed his willingness to serve in the county before his death.
Ren Yan repeatedly declined, and finally asked him to serve as a temporary minister to discuss Cao's offer of wine.
Long Qiuchang died of illness soon, and Ren Yan personally attended to his funeral and did not deal with government affairs for three days.
Therefore, talented scholar-bureaucrats in the county competed to serve under him.
In the early years of Jianwu's reign, Ren Yan resigned and went back to see the emperor.
The imperial edict summoned Ren Yan and appointed him as the governor of Jiuzhen.
Guangwu summoned him, gave him horses and various silk products, and asked his wife and children to stay in Luoyang.
Jiuzhen's occupation is hunting and he doesn't know how to cultivate land and grow food. The people often go to Jiaozhi to buy food, which often leads to poverty.
So Ren Yan asked them to make farm tools and taught them to cultivate wasteland.
In this way, the cultivated land increases year by year, and the people are self-sufficient and wealthy.
Moreover, the people of Luo Yue had no marriage etiquette. They each followed their own sexual preferences. They had no fixed wives, and they did not understand the nature of father and son and the principles between husband and wife.
Ren Yan then sent documents to all counties, requiring men to be between twenty and fifty years old, and women to be between fifteen and forty, to be married according to age.
For those who were poor and could not afford the betrothal gift, officials below the senior level were required to use part of their salary to help them.
As a result, more than 2,000 people were married at the same time.
In the next year, the weather will be smooth and the food will be abundant.
These people only know their family name after giving birth to children.
They all said: Renjun is the one who made me have children!
Many people name their children Ren.
So the barbarian Yelang and other tribes outside the border admired Deyi and were willing to guard the border. Therefore, Ren Yan removed the scouts and soldiers guarding the border.
At first, during the reign of Emperor Ping, Xiguang, a Hanzhong native, served as the prefect of Jiaozhi. He guided the barbarians and gradually influenced them with etiquette and justice.
His reputation for civilizing barbarians is similar to that of Ren Yan. In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, Xiguang blocked the border and sent troops to defend it.
In the early years of Jianwu, he sent envoys to pay tribute and was named Marquis of Yanyan.
There is a Chinese custom in Lingnan, which started from these two prefects.
Ren Yan served in Jiuzhen for four years. The emperor summoned him to Luoyang. Due to illness, his trip was delayed and he was demoted to the order of Suiyang. Jiuzhen officials and people built ancestral halls for him when he was alive.
After arriving in Beijing, he was appointed as the prefect of Wuwei. The emperor personally summoned him and warned him: Serve your superiors well and don't ruin your reputation.
Ren Yan replied: I have heard that loyal ministers are selfless, and those who are selfish are disloyal.
Serving the country wholeheartedly is the duty of a minister.
It is not His Majesty's blessing that the top and bottom are the same.
Serve your superior officials well, I dare not accept your instructions.
The emperor sighed and said: You are right.
After arriving in Wuwei, Tian Cang, the commander of the army at that time, was a prominent family in the county. His nephews and guests harmed the people. Ren Yan arrested Tian Cang, and five or six of his father, son and guests were executed.
Tian Xiang's youngest son, Tian Shang, gathered hundreds of dissolute and frivolous people, called themselves generals, and attacked the county government at night.
Ren Yan immediately sent troops to defeat Tian Shang.
Since then, his prestige has been greatly shaken, and officials and people are cautious.
Wuwei faces the Huns to the north and the Qiang to the south. The people are afraid of the invasion and plunder of the Huns and Qiang, and many people have abandoned farming.
After Ren Yan arrived, he selected a thousand people who knew how to use soldiers, and stated rewards and punishments, asking them to lead the Hu people of various races to massacre Huangshi's cavalry to occupy key places, so that in case of emergency, they could fight and pursue the enemy.
The enemy will suffer many casualties in every battle. From now on, we will not dare to fight again. In the past, Hexi was short of rain, so Ren Yan appointed officials in charge of water conservancy to build ditches and channels, which benefited the people.
He also built schools and sent officials to manage them. Since then, the descendants of officials below have been allowed to go to the schools to receive education and exempt them from corvee labor.
Those who are familiar with the meaning of the scriptures are all appointed to make them proud.
Since then, Wuwei has learned and talented people. Later, Ren Yan was demoted to Zhaoling Order for killing Qiang people without authorization.
Xianzong ascended the throne and was granted the title of prefect of Yingchuan.
In the second year of Yongping, the emperor summoned him to school and then appointed him as the governor of Hanoi.
He served for nine years and died of illness.
His youngest son Ren Kai was very successful in his official career.
◆Wang Jingzhuan, Wang Jing, courtesy name Zhongtong, was born in Lelang, Jiahan.
His eighth generation ancestor, Wang Zhong, was originally from Langxie.
Wang Zhong likes Taoism and understands celestial phenomena.
When Zhu Lu was in rebellion, King Ai of Qi Liu Xiang planned to send troops and asked Wang Zhong for advice many times.
When Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, rebelled, he wanted him to serve as military advisor. Wang Zhong was afraid of disaster, so he took a boat across the sea and fled to Lelang Mountain, where he settled down.
Wang Jing's father, Wang Hong, served as the third elder of the county.
After the reform failed, local Wang Tiao killed the county governor Liu Xian and called himself the general and the governor of Lelang.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, Guangwu sent the prefect Wang Zun to lead an army to attack Wang Tiao.
When Wang Zun arrived in Liaodong, Wang Hong, together with the governor Cao Shi Yangyi and others, killed Wang Tiao and welcomed Wang Zun. The emperor made them all princes, but Wang Hong refused to give up his official title.
The emperor was surprised and summoned him to Beijing. Unexpectedly, he died of illness on the way.
Wang Jing studied "The Book of Changes" since he was a child, and then read various books extensively. He also liked things such as astronomy and mathematics, so he had a deep personality and was good at many skills.
Sikong Fugong called him to serve in the government.
At that time, someone recommended Wang Jing to be able to control floods, and Xianzong issued a letter from Shao asking him to build the Dredging Yi Canal together with Wang Wu, who was going to be the emissary.
Wang Wu adopted the low dam method proposed by Wang Jing to block water, so there was no more water damage.
At first, during the reign of Emperor Ping, the Yellow River and Bianshui River burst and destroyed the river banks, leaving no time to control them.
In the tenth year of Jianwu's reign, Yangwu ordered Zhang Si to write a letter saying: The Yellow River has been blocked for a long time, causing harm every day, and the Jiqu canal flooded dozens of counties.
Spend some money to control water and achieve success is not difficult.
It is best to rebuild the river embankments to bring peace to the people.
After the memorial was sent up, Guangwu immediately sent out soldiers.
While planning to regulate the Yellow River, Junyi ordered Lejun to write again: In the past, during the reign of Emperor Wu, there was a large population, and they all cultivated and planted along the river embankment. However, the Huzi River breached for more than 20 years, so it would not be blocked immediately.
Nowadays, the population is sparse and the fields are vast. Although there is no management, the disasters can still be tolerated.
Moreover, after the war, labor was now introduced. Once there was too much toil and resentment, the people could not bear it.
It's best to wait until things are stable before discussing the matter.
When Guangwu saw this opinion, he canceled the water control project.
Later, the flow of the Bian Canal became larger and larger, and the original location of the sluice reached the middle of the Yellow River. People in Yanzhou and Yuzhou complained that the imperial court often mobilized other laborers without considering the most urgent matters of the people first.
In the twelfth year of Yongping, the emperor discussed the management of Bianqu and summoned Wang Jing to inquire about the geographical situation and convenient conditions for water control.
Wang Jing stated the pros and cons of water control, and he was very quick and agile. The emperor appreciated it very much.
And because he had managed Junyi, he was given the "Book of Mountains and Seas", "Book of Rivers and Canals", "Pictures of Tribute to Yu" as well as coins, cloth, clothing and items.
In the summer, the imperial court finally mobilized hundreds of thousands of troops and sent Wang Jing and Wang Wu to build channels and embankments. It was more than a thousand miles from Rongyang to Qiancheng Haikou.
Wang Jing then measured the terrain, opened up the mountains, cleared the sand and gravel from the water, directly cut off the deep ditches, built dams at key points, and dredged and guided the blocked water flow. He built a sluice every ten miles so that the water could flow back and forth without causing the danger of bursting.
Although Wang Jing saved project costs, the cost was still calculated in tens of billions.
The next summer, the canal was built.
The emperor personally inspected and issued an edict to rely on the Yellow River counties to establish officials responsible for the river embankments, just like the system of the Western Han Dynasty.
Wang Jing became famous from this.
Wang Wu and those engaged in tax affairs all had their first-level official salaries increased.
Wang Jingjing was promoted three times and served as Shi Yushi.
In the fifteenth year, he followed the emperor to inspect Shubu. When he arrived in Wuyan, the emperor praised his achievements, awarded him the position of embankment visitor, and gave him carriages, horses, fine silk and coins.
In the seventh year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Wang Jing was transferred to the post of governor of Xuzhou.
Prior to this, Du Du, a native of Duling, presented "On the Capital Fu" to the emperor, hoping to move the capital to Chang'an.
After the elderly people heard about it, they all began to miss their hometown and looked westward for a long time affectionately.
Wang Jing believed that the palace and ancestral temple had been built, and he was worried about people's doubts. At that time, divine sparrows and other auspicious signs appeared, so he wrote the "Jinren Lun" to praise the beauty of Luoyi and the corresponding auspiciousness between heaven and man. The article has merit.
The next year, Wang Jing was transferred to Lujiang Prefecture.
Before this, the people in Lujiang did not know how to use cattle to plow the land, resulting in a situation where the land was fertile but the food was often insufficient.
On the border of the county is the Shaopi rice field built by Chu State Prime Minister Sun Shuao.
Wang Jing then led the officials and people to reclaim the barren land and teach the people to cultivate the land with plows. In this way, the cultivated fields more than doubled the original land, and the county had abundant food.
So the commandments were carved on stones so that the people would know the general prohibitions.
In addition, he guided the people to raise silkworms and weave cloth, formulated laws and regulations for them, and engraved all the laws and regulations on pavilions in the countryside. The provisions he formulated are also circulated in Lujiang.
Wang Jing died in office.
At first, Wang Jing thought that everything recorded in the "Six Classics" was all about the dragonfly, and everything was done in accordance with the requirements of the turtle. However, the good and bad fortunes described in the books were inconsistent, so he compiled the books on numerology from various schools, as well as the applicable parts such as taboos on building tombs and houses, yin and yang Feng Shui, astrology, etc., and compiled it into "Dayan Xuanji".
◆Chuan of Qin Peng, Qin Peng, courtesy name Boping, was born in Maoling, Fufeng.
Since the Han Dynasty, the Qin family has inherited official positions from generation to generation.
Qin Peng's sixth ancestor Qin Xi served as Ying! There are five people who hold the position of two thousand stones at the same time, so they are called the Wanshi Qin family in the Sanfu area.
Qin Peng's sister entered the palace as a noble during the reign of Emperor Xianzong and was very favored.
In the seventh year of Yongping, as the elder brother of Peng Guiren, Qin Peng was promoted to Kaiyang City Gate Marquis along with Xiaohou, a relative of the fourth surname.
In the fifteenth year, he was awarded the position of Captain of Cavalry and helped Captain Geng Bingbei to conquer the Xiongnu.
In the first year of Jianchu's reign, Qin Peng was promoted to Shanyang Prefect.
He educated the people with etiquette and justice without punishment.
He respected Confucianism and advocated education.
Every time during the Spring and Autumn period when people were eating and drinking, he would always revise the etiquette of ascending and descending, as well as the courtesy of guests and hosts.
He formulated four precepts for the people to determine the etiquette between father and son, brothers, husband and wife, elder and younger.
Anyone who abides by the teachings will be promoted to the third elder of the village, and he will often be given wine and meat as encouragement in August.
When an official commits a crime or fault, he or she should be removed from his official position and sent away without humiliation.
As a result, the people all had benevolent hearts, and no one deceived or violated each other.
He cultivated thousands of hectares of rice fields. Every farming season, Qin Peng personally measured the acres of land, classified the fertile and barren land, classified them into three grades, recorded them in official books, and stored them in the township and county.
In this way, cunning officials dare not act rashly and cannot hide their evil deeds.
Qin Peng then wrote to the court, saying that it would be best to implement this system throughout the country.
The edict distributed the provisions he listed to the three governments and issued them to the prefectures and counties.
Qin Peng served for six years and was transferred to Yingchuan Prefecture. There are often auspicious signs such as phoenixes, unicorns, particularly strong rice crops, sweet rain and dew, appearing everywhere in the county.
Suzong went out for inspections and when he came to Yingchuan again, he always rewarded him with money and food, and was particularly fond of him.
He died in the second year of Zhanghe.
Qin Peng's younger brothers Qin Dun and Qin Guo served as captains of Shesheng together.
◆Biography of Wang Huan, Wang Huan, courtesy name Zhizi, was from Zheng County, Guangmo.
Wang Huan's father, Wang Shun, served as the governor of Anding.
Wang Huan has been fond of chivalry and advocating martial arts since he was a child. He has interacted with strong and agile young men many times.
Later, he changed his conduct, paid attention to Confucianism, studied "Shangshu", recited the law, and was able to roughly grasp its main meaning.
He served as the meritorious officer of the prefect Chen Chong, and he dared to make decisions regardless of the powerful.
Chen Chong's reputation for political governance spread widely, and he served as chief agricultural officer in the capital.
Emperor He asked him: What method did you use to govern the county?
Chen Chong kowtowed and resigned and said: I have appointed King Huan of Cao Cao to select wise and capable people, and I have appointed Tan Xian, the chief secretary, to correct mistakes and make up for omissions. I just want to read Shao Shu.
Emperor He was very happy after hearing this. Wang Huan became famous from this.
The state government recommended him as Maocai, and the imperial court appointed him as the magistrate of Wen County.
There are many cunning and cunning people in the county, who have caused disasters to the people for a long time.
Wang Huan tried every means to attack the bad guys and eliminate them all.
Since then, the territory has been peaceful, and merchants can spend the night on the roadside.
Those who herded cattle often said that they gave the cattle to Wang Huan, and there was never any violation of the cattle.
Wang Huan stayed in Wenxian for three years and was promoted to the governor of Yanzhou. He governed the counties of Yanzhou by law, and moralization and prestige were widely promoted.
Later, he was convicted because his monstrous remarks were not consistent with the truth.
A few years later, he was recruited by the imperial court and granted the position of Shi Yushi.
In the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, Wang Huan followed the emperor to the south for inspection and served as the Luoyang order after returning.
Wang Huan was upright in his conduct and could be lenient and strict in his administration.
For those unjust and doubtful cases that have been litigated for a long time, which have not been resolved by several county magistrates, and which are difficult to judge based on legal basis, Wang Huan can skillfully clarify the truth of the case and eliminate everyone's doubts.
He can also use his uncanny skills to discover hidden bad guys and evil deeds.
The people in the capital all praised and marveled, thinking that Wang Huan had a wonderful plan.
In the first year of Yuanxing, Wang Huan died of illness.
No matter whether it is a city resident or a traveler, everyone sighs.
Men, women, old and young gathered money and food from each other, and thousands of people held memorial ceremonies for him.
Wang Huan's coffin returned to the west and passed through Hongnong on the way. The people set up plates and tables on the roadside and placed sacrifices.
The officials asked them why, and they all said that they usually brought food to Luoyang, but it was plundered by soldiers and officials, and they often lost half of it.
Since Wang Huan became the county magistrate, he has never been invaded again, so he came to repay his kindness.
Wang Huan's administration influenced the people to such an extent.
The people missed his kindness and built an ancestral hall for him to the west of Anyang Pavilion. They sang chords and paid homage to Wang Huan every time they had meals.
In the second year of Yongchu, Empress Dowager Deng issued an edict saying: Only with loyal and talented officials can the country be governed.
The imperial court was very diligent in seeking such officials, but received very little.
So Jie Yizi said: It is difficult to be talented, isn't it?
In the past, when the great ministers Nong Zhuyi and Youfufeng Yin Weng returned home, they had outstanding political achievements and their reputations were praised everywhere. Emperor Xiaoxuan praised them and issued a letter from Shao to reward their sons with a hundred catties of gold.
Wang Huan, the former magistrate of Luoyang, maintained his integrity, followed the meaning explained in "The Poetry of the Lamb", served the public wholeheartedly, and wholeheartedly benefited the people. Unfortunately, he died prematurely because his achievements were not successful. The people remembered him and built an ancestral hall for him.
If he hadn't been extremely loyal and kind, who could have reached such a state!
Now Wang Huan's son Wang Shi is appointed as a doctor to reward those who work hard for the country and the people.
During the Yanxi period, Emperor Huan followed Huang Lao's theory and destroyed all the ancestral halls. He only issued a special edict to preserve the temple of former Taifu Zhuomao in Mi County and Wang Huan's ancestral hall in Luoyang.
Tanxian was also famous later. He served as the governor of Yuzhou during the reign of Emperor An.
At that time, there was a famine in the world and people were vying to become thieves. Almost 10,000 people were arrested in Yuzhou.
Duoxian sympathized with the poverty of these people and would rather break the law himself. He often pardoned criminals without permission, thus impeaching himself.
The emperor issued an edict not to accept Tanxian's self-impeachment.
Tanxian later became Changle Weiwei.
Since the death of Wang Huan, the emperor has successively sent Shao letters to the three princes, asking them to select Luoyang orders specifically, but none of the ones selected are incompetent.
During the Yonghe period, the imperial court appointed Ren Jun, the magistrate of Juxian County from Bohai, as the magistrate of Luoyang.
Ren Jun selected civil and military officials and gave full play to their talents. These people cut off the evil thieves and never shrink back, so the number of cases to be decided in a year is only a few dozen. Ren Jun surpassed Wang Huan in terms of prowess, but was not as good as Wang Huan in terms of virtuous governance.
Ren Jun, also known as Shugao, died while serving as the prefect of Taishan.
◆Xu Jingchuan, Xu Jing, courtesy name Shaozhang, was born in Yangxian, Kuaiji.
His grandfather Xu Wu was recommended as Xiaolian by the prefect Wu Lun.
Xu Wu wanted to make his two younger brothers Xu Yan and Xu Pu famous because they were not yet famous, so he called them and said: According to the principle of separation of etiquette, there is also a principle of separation of family property.
So the property was divided into three parts. Xu Wu himself took the portion of the rich fields, the spacious house and the slaves who could handle it, while the two younger brothers received a smaller and smaller portion.
People in the same town praised Xu Wu's brother for his humility and despised Xu Wu's greed. Therefore, Xu Yan and Xu Pu were elected. Xu Wuqian gathered his clan relatives and said with tears: As an elder brother, I behaved unethically and stole my reputation and status. My two younger brothers have grown up and have not received wealth and salary, so I asked for a share of the property, and I was willing to be ridiculed.
Now the property under management has tripled than before. I gave it all to my two younger brothers, leaving nothing behind.
So the public opinion in the county unanimously praised Xu Wu.
Xu Wu became the Shaofu of Changle.
Xu Jing was a county official when he was young. His brother's son Xu Shi once killed someone in revenge. People who resented Xu Shi brought weapons to settle the score with him.
After Xu Jing learned about it, he went out to meet his enemies, knelt down and said: "Xu Shi was rude before and offended you, and I am responsible for my failure to teach him."
My brother passed away a long time ago, and I only have one son to continue the bloodline. If the deceased is to suffer the pain of the extinction of the bloodline, I am willing to die instead.
The enemy helped Xu Jing up and said, "You are praised as a virtuous person in the county. How dare we be rude to you?"
So let it go.
Xu Jing's reputation became even more prominent.
The prefect Huang Jing recommended him as Xiaolian.
During the reign of Emperor He, Xu Jing was gradually promoted to the prefect of Guiyang.
Guiyang is close to Nanzhou, and its customs and customs are very frivolous and do not understand knowledge and morality.
Xu Jing made a wedding and funeral system for them to let the people know the etiquette, justice, laws and prohibitions.
He once visited Moyang County in the spring. There was a man named Jiang Jun. Brothers accused each other of fighting over property.
Xu Jing faced the two brothers and sighed: I bear the important responsibility of the country, but the education has not been implemented. The responsibility lies with me, the prefect.
So he turned around and asked the officials around him to write to the court to explain the situation and request to be punished by the court captain.
The Jiang Jun brothers felt regretful and each asked to be punished.
Xu Jing served as governor for twelve years, and the people praised him.
Due to illness, he wrote to the court, and was summoned and appointed as an admonishment official. He died in office.
People in Guiyang built a temple and a monument for him.
Xu Jing's grandson Xu Jian served as Taiwei during the reign of Emperor Ling.
◆Biography of Mengchang, Mengchang, courtesy name Bozhou, was born in Shangyu, Kuaiji.
His ancestors served as county officials for three generations, and they all died in the chaos.
Mengchang cultivated his conduct since he was a child and served as a household official in the county.
There was a widow in Shangyu who took care of her mother-in-law with great filial piety. Her mother-in-law passed away in old age. Her sister-in-law was originally jealous, so she falsely accused the widow of being tired of supporting her mother-in-law, poisoned her mother, and complained to the county.
The county government closed the case and convicted the widow without any investigation.
Mengchang originally knew the widow's grievances and told the eunuch the details, but the eunuch did not go to trial.
Mengchang cried outside the county mansion, so he resigned from his official position on the pretext of illness. The widow eventually died unjustly.
Since then, there has been two consecutive years of drought in the county, and no amount of prayer has any effect.
Later, the prefect Yin Dan took office and inquired about the cause of the drought. Mengchang went to the county government to describe in detail the incident of the widow's unjust death. By the way, he said: Once upon a time, there was a filial woman in Shuhai.
The gods were moved to cause drought. With a word from the public, heaven immediately sent down sweet rain.
The person who complained should be killed to apologize to the souls who died unjustly, hoping that the grievances in the underworld would be redressed and the rain could be counted on.
Yin Dan listened to his advice and immediately punished the woman who complained and offered sacrifices to the widow's grave. As a result, heavy rain fell from heaven and the crops were harvested.
Mengchang was later named Xiaolian by Ce and recommended as a scholar.
The imperial court appointed him as the magistrate of Xu County. The state and county governments wrote letters recommending his talents, so he was promoted to the governor of Hepu.
Hepu does not produce food, but the sea produces treasures. Hepu borders Jiaotong, and there are often traders coming and going to buy and sell grain.
Most of the former governors were greedy and asked people to collect pearls without knowing the limit, so the pearls gradually found their way to Jiaoshi County.
As a result, the journeys stopped, people and livestock had nothing to eat, and the poor died of starvation on the roadside.
After Mengchang took office, he got rid of the shortcomings of the past and visited the people's sufferings and things that were beneficial to the people.
In less than a year, the lost beads returned to Hepu, the people resumed their business, merchants began to come and go, goods began to circulate, and Meng Chang was praised as wise as a god.
Meng Chang resigned due to illness. The imperial court summoned him and he was about to return to the capital. Officials and people grabbed Meng Chang's car and begged him to stay.
Since Mengchang couldn't leave, he took a villager's boat and left overnight.
Mengchang lived in seclusion in a remote swamp and farmed by himself.
Scholars and people in neighboring counties admired Mengchang's virtues, and more than a hundred people moved to live with him.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, Yang Qiao, a native of the same county as Shangshu, wrote to recommend Meng Chang, saying: I have written seven times to recommend Meng Chang, the former prefect of Hepu, but he was so indifferent that he was never considered.
I confessed my heart to him, but it had no effect.
Meng Changan enjoyed benevolence, promoted morality, and was especially obsessed with morality. His behavior was noble and refined, and his talents were outstanding.
When he was a prefect, he changed customs and reformed politics. The lost pearls came back again, and the hungry people relied on him to survive.
Moreover, there are many treasures in the South China Sea, and it is easy to accumulate property. The treasures in his hands are worth more than gold. However, Mengchang retired due to illness alone and worked in the fields himself, hiding his traces and style and not revealing his brilliance.
He is really a great talent used as wings, not as a bundle of feathers on his lower abdomen and back.
However, he was buried in the wilderness, and good officials and nobles had no share in him, causing the national treasure to be abandoned in a ditch.
Besides, his years are limited, he is nearing his twilight years, and his loyal integrity has long withered in the era of sage.
My heart was really hurt, and I shed tears in private.
Objects obtained from far away places were regarded as curiosities, and were generally regarded as precious, unlike the scholars.
The twisted and rotten tree cannot be used by the emperor because of the carvings and decorations by his subordinates.
When the emperor appoints scholars, he should select people who are respected by everyone.
The minister, with his limited talents and short-term talents, rushes around the emperor, thinking about establishing a trivial moral integrity, and does not dare to have secret affairs with his fellow countrymen. In private, he is moved by the behavior of birds of prey, and recommends talented people regardless of his life.
Mengchang was not hired in the end.
He died at home at the age of seventy.
◆The fifth interview, the fifth interview, named Zhongmou, was from Changling, Jingzhao, and the grandson of Sikong Wulun.
The fifth interview: He lost his father when he was a child. He often farmed in order to support his brother and sister-in-law because his family was poor.
Whenever I have free time, I learn Taoism.
He served as the meritorious officer of the county government, was selected as Xiaolian, and was appointed as the new capital magistrate.
He administered policies fairly and promoted enlightenment. Within three years, people from neighboring counties came to join him, and their household registration increased tenfold.
He was promoted to governor of Zhangye.
There was a famine every year, and the price of one stone of grain rose to several thousand dollars. On the fifth visit, the granary was opened to help the people through the crisis.
Officials were afraid of being held accountable and rushed to report the matter to the court.
The fifth interviewer said: If you submit a letter and wait for a reply, you are leaving the people alone.
I am willing to use my own life to save the people!
So he took out food and distributed it to the people.
Emperor Shun issued the fifth interview of the Shaoshu Commendation.
The people of the whole county were saved.
More than a year later, there were enough officials and people, and no treachery or robberies occurred in the county.
Later he was transferred to Nanyang Prefecture.
After leaving office, he was awarded the post of Colonel Protecting Qiang, and people in the border areas were convinced of his authority.
The fifth visit died in office. ◆Biography of Liu Chong, courtesy name Zurong, a native of Mouping County, Donglai County. Qi mourned the descendants of King Hui.
Prince Hui and Xiao Wang Jianglu, the young son of Lu was granted the title of Hou of Mouping, and his descendants lived in Mouping.
Liu Chong's father, Liu Pi, was very knowledgeable and was called Tongru.
Liu Chong learned from his father when he was young. Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he was promoted as Xiaolian and appointed as the magistrate of Dongpingling County. He was loved by the officials and people because of his kindness and kindness to the people.
My mother was ill and left her official position to return home.
The people sent him off, but even the road was blocked and the car could not move forward, so he ran back in civilian clothes.
Later, he was promoted to the post of Yuzhang Prefect four times and to Kuaiji Prefect three times.
Some people in the mountains are simple and reserved, but some have never been to a city since they were young, and are often deceived by officials.
Liu Chong removed those cumbersome rules and regulations and prohibited his subordinates from disturbing the people and other illegal behaviors. The county was in order and the people lived and worked in peace and contentment. He will be appointed as a minister.
There were five or six old men in Shanyin County, their eyebrows and hair were all gray, who came out of the Ruoxie Valley, and each of them gave Liu Chong a hundred coins.
Liu Chong comforted them and said, "Elders, why are you doing this?"
He replied: The ignorant people in the valley have never seen the governor.
In the past, when the prefect was in office, he would send officials to the people to search for property day and night. Sometimes dogs barked all night, and the people had no peace.
Since you took office, no dogs can be heard barking at night, and the common people cannot see the officials.
It is rare for us in our old age to enjoy this peaceful time. Now I heard that you are leaving office, so we are here to send you a gift.
Liu Chong said: How can my politics be what your elders say?
Thank you for your hard work!
He picked a big one from each person's money and accepted it.
Transferred to Zongzheng and Dahonglu.
In the fourth year of Yanxi's reign, he replaced Huang Qiong as Sikong. He was dismissed because of the cloudy and foggy weather.
Soon, he was awarded the title of Great Craftsman and was appointed Zongzheng again.
In the first year of Jianning, he succeeded Wang Chang as Sikong, and was successively appointed as Situ and Taiwei.
In the second year, he was dismissed from office due to a solar eclipse and returned to his hometown.
Liu Chong was successively appointed as the governor of two counties, and served as prime minister and high official many times. However, he was honest and simple, and his family did not have much wealth.
He once went out from the capital and wanted to rest in a pavilion. The pavilion official stopped him and said: "We are tidying up the house and cleaning it to wait for Liu Gong's arrival. You are not allowed to rest here."
Liu Chong left without saying anything. People at that time called him an elder.
Died at home due to old age and illness.
Liu Chong's younger brother Liu Fang was promoted to Shanyang Prefecture.
Liu Fang had two sons: Liu Dai, nicknamed Gongshan, and Liu Yao, nicknamed Zhengli.
Brothers have the same name.
Dong Zhuo entered Luoyang, and Liu Dai served as the governor of Yanzhou.
He loved things with an open mind and was supported by scholars.
In the third year of Chuping, the Yellow Turban bandits from Qingzhou entered Yanzhou, killed Zheng Sui, the prime minister of the city, and then moved into Dongping.
Liu Dai attacked the Yellow Turban bandit and died in battle.
During the period of prosperity, Liu Yao was appointed as Yangzhou Shepherd and General Zhenwei.
At this time, Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, and Liu Yao had no choice but to move to Qu'a.
When the country was in chaos, many friends of the scholar-bureaucrats fled to the south. Liu Yao took him in and adopted him, sharing the hardships with them and gaining a good reputation.
Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack Liu Yao, but Liu Yao ran to Yuzhang and died of illness.
◆Qiu Lan's biography, Qiu Lan's courtesy name is Jizhi, his surname is Xiang, and he is a native of Kaocheng County, Chenliu County.
When he was young, he was a scholar, simple and silent, and no one in the village knew about him.
When he was forty years old, the county government called him to serve as a supplementary official and he was promoted to chief of Pu Pavilion.
Advise the people to manage production and formulate regulations and laws to ensure that there are as many fruits and vegetables as there are chickens and hogs. After the farm work is finished, the children are gathered together to study in school.
Those who were idle and doing evil were made to farm and cultivate mulberry trees, and were strictly disciplined.
He personally managed funerals for the people and helped the poor and widowed.
Within a year, the education was widespread.
When Qiu Lan arrived at the pavilion, there was a man named Chen Yuan who lived alone with his mother. His mother went to Qiu Lan to accuse Chen Yuan of being unfilial.
Qiu Lan said in surprise: "I passed by your house recently. The courtyard is neat and cultivated on time."
He is not a bad person, maybe it is because my education is not up to standard.
The mother is widowed and has worked hard to raise orphans until she grows old. Why does she want to cause her son to be unjust when she gets angry?
The mother was moved after hearing this, regretted it, and went back in tears.
Qiu Lan personally went to Chen Yuan's house to have a drink with his mother and son. He talked to them about human ethics and filial piety, and warned them about the dangers and benefits.
Chen Yuan finally became a filial son.
There is a popular proverb in the countryside: Where are my parents? They were born in my garden and were fed by my owl.
At this time, King Huan of Hanoi, the commander of Kaocheng, was a fierce advocate for politics. Hearing that Qiu Lan used virtue to transform people, he appointed him as chief administrator.
Said to Qiu Lan: You know Chen Yuan's fault. If you don't deal with him, you may be lacking a little bit of falconry.
Qiu Lan said: It is better to be a falcon than a phoenix.
Wang Huan sent him off and said: "Zhiji is not a place where Luan Feng lives. Is this small county of mine a place where great sages display their talents?"
Nowadays, the Taixue is dragging his robes and flying in fame. They are all descendants of the master!
Give him a month's salary and encourage him to achieve noble virtues.
Qiu Lan entered Imperial College.
At this time, Fu Rong, a famous person from the same county, was a neighbor of Qiu Lan, and the house was full of guests.
Qiu Lan often tidied himself up and did not talk to Fulong.
Fulong looked at Qiu Lan's every move and felt that this person was a bit strange, so he said to Qiu Lan: "I am from the same hometown as my husband, and we are neighbors."
Episode 4 of Today's Heroes of the Capital is a time for ambitious people to get together. Even though they emphasize studying classics, why should they be so stubborn?
Qiu Lan said seriously: Did the emperor establish the Imperial Academy just to allow people to talk here?
He gave a long bow and left, not talking to him anymore.
Later, Fulong told Guo Linzong about this. Lin Zongyin and Fulong took their business cards to visit Qiu Lan, and Qiu Lan stayed with them.
Guo Linzong sighed and got out of bed to worship.
After Qiu Lan returned to his hometown after studying, the prefectures and counties invited him to go, but Qiu Lan couldn't leave because of illness.
Even if you are at home on weekdays, you must still ask for etiquette.
My wife has it, and she often takes off her hat and blames herself.
His wife thanked him in court and waited for Qiu Lan to put on his hat before he dared to go to the court.
The family members did not see any strange emotions or emotions.
Later, he conquered Fangzheng and died of illness.
The three sons all have literary and historical talents. The youngest son Qiu Xuan is the most famous.
◆Tong Hui's biography, Tong Hui's courtesy name was Han Zong, and he was a native of Gumu Mu, Langfu County.
His father, Tong Zhongyu, encountered a period of severe famine and used all his family property to provide relief. Hundreds of people from the nine tribes and the village relied on him to survive.
Tong Zhongyu died very early.
When Tong Hui was young, he worked as an official in the state and county. Situ Yangci knew that he was fair in enforcing the law, so he recruited him.
When Yang Ci was impeached and should be removed from office, all his subordinates abandoned him and left. Only Tong Hui went to the court to argue for Yang Ci.
Yang Ci's case was vindicated, and all his subordinates came back, but Tong Hui drove away.
Therefore, public opinion praised him.
He was then conscripted into the government, but was not given the order.
County officials and the people should be educated at any time if they break the law; if the officials are competent and if some of the people have done good deeds, they will be rewarded with food and wine to encourage and dissuade them.
There are regulations for farming, textile and other production undertakings.
The whole place is quiet, and the prison has been empty for years without a single prisoner.
The exiled population from neighboring counties came to join us, and more than 20,000 households moved there.
The common people were often harmed by tigers. They set up fences to catch tigers and captured two tigers alive.
Tong Hui came out and scolded the tiger: "Of all things in nature, only human beings are the most valuable."
Tigers and wolves should eat horses, cattle, sheep, chickens, dogs, and hogs, but you are cruel and harmful to people.
According to the king's law, those who kill people are put to death, and those who hurt people are punished.
If you have murdered someone, you should bow your head and confess your guilt; if you think you have done nothing, you should cry out for injustice.
Yihu lowered his head and closed his eyes, showing a look of shock and fear, and immediately killed him.
The other tiger looked at Tong Hui and roared and kept jumping. Tong Hui ordered it to be let go.
County officials and people sang his praises.
Qingzhou recommended him for his outstanding achievements and promoted him to the prefect of Danyang, but he died of a sudden illness.
His younger brother, Tong Yi, had Chinese characters and was more famous than Tong Hui, so the prime minister promoted him first.
Tong Yi could not speak due to illness and refused to serve as an official. After Tong Hui was ordered, he became filial and honest, and was awarded the title of "Xuchangchang".
There are special achievements in education, and county officials and people are born to erect monuments.
I heard that the recommender was about to die and abandoned his official position.
Later he was promoted to a distinguished scholar, but he died at home.
Zan said: The most fearful thing about governance is that it is too strict. Proper governance is as easy as cooking a small fish.
Extend loyalty and forgiveness to yourself and others, and many ills will naturally be eliminated.
One person can grasp the sentiments of the people, and thousands of families can play the piano and make music.
Remember their kindness and remember the sages of previous generations forever.
summary:
Emperor Guangwu, having risen from the common people, understood the hardships of farming and the suffering of the people. After unifying the realm, he pursued peace, abolished the complex policies of Wang Mang's era, and restored the lenient Han methods. He dressed simply, avoided luxury, and showed no favoritism in his court. When foreign states presented valuable horses and swords, he ordered the horses used for carriage and the swords given to knights. He reduced officials, abolished hunting expeditions, and wrote imperial letters in small characters, fostering an atmosphere of diligence and frugality. He frequently consulted ministers and visited the people to learn of their grievances, leading to diligent governance and rest for the populace. Local governors competed in their efforts, with figures like Du Shi, Ren Yan, and Xiguang achieving notable political successes. However, during the Jianwu and Yongping eras, governance was overly strict and detailed, leading to frequent replacements of officials based on rumors. Despite sharp advice from Zhu Fu and others, their counsel was not adopted, leaving shortcomings in the restoration period. From the reigns of Emperor Zhang and Emperor He onward, officials like Lu Gong, Wu You, and Liu Kuan used benevolence and integrity to prevent deceit, while Wang Tang and Chen Chong appointed virtuous talents, promoting education. Others like Wang Huan and Ren Jun, as Luoyang magistrates, punished evil and improved officialdom, though they had imperfections in morality and etiquette.

Wei Sa, from a poor family, studied diligently and served as a magistrate and prefect. In Guiyang, he built schools, established marriage rites, and transformed local customs. He constructed roads and inns, reducing corvée labor, and regulated iron smelting, increasing annual revenue. He governed with consideration for the people, maintaining peace for ten years. Ren Yan, a learned scholar, served as a young prefect of Kuaiji, where he hired virtuous men and supported the poor. In Jiuzhen, he taught farming, established marriage regulations, and civilized the people, leading to prosperity and admiration from barbarian tribes. He later governed Wuwei, where he executed corrupt officials, defended against invaders, built irrigation systems, and promoted education, leaving a lasting legacy.

Wang Jing, a scholar of the *Book of Changes* and other subjects, was summoned to control floods. He successfully built canals and embankments over a thousand miles, using sluices to manage water flow, saving costs and preventing disasters. He later served as a prefect in Xuzhou and Lujiang, where he taught cattle plowing, reclaimed land, and guided sericulture, engraving laws for the people. Qin Peng, from a prominent family, governed Shanyang with etiquette and education, establishing moral precepts and agricultural classifications. He cultivated rice fields and implemented a grading system to prevent official corruption, later serving in Yingchuan with auspicious signs. Wang Huan, initially chivalrous, later studied Confucianism and served as a magistrate, eliminating cunning criminals and ensuring peace. As Luoyang magistrate, he resolved difficult cases and uncovered hidden evils, earning widespread praise. After his death, the people built a shrine for him, and even Emperor Huan later preserved it.

Xu Jing, as Guiyang prefect, established wedding and funeral rites and resolved a property dispute between brothers by taking responsibility himself, leading to their repentance. Mengchang, known for his integrity, cleared a widow's wrongful conviction, ending a drought. As Hepu prefect, he reformed pearl collection, restoring the pearl trade and reviving the local economy. He retired to farming, and despite recommendations, was never hired, dying at seventy. The Fifth Fang, a grandson of a former minister, governed Zhangye during a famine by opening granaries without awaiting orders, saving the people. He later served in Nanyang and as Colonel Protecting Qiang. Liu Chong, a descendant of royalty, governed with kindness, removing oppressive rules. When leaving Kuaiji, elders gave him coins, but he accepted only one from each. He held high offices but remained frugal, dying at home.

Qiu Lan, a quiet scholar, governed as a pavilion chief, promoting agriculture and education. He resolved a filial piety dispute by counseling a mother and son, transforming the son into a filial child. He later entered the Imperial College but avoided frivolous talk, maintaining strict personal conduct. Tong Hui, known for fairness, argued for his superior Yang Ci when others abandoned him. As a magistrate, he educated offenders, rewarded good deeds, and captured tigers harming people, executing one and releasing another. His governance led to peace and an influx of refugees.

◆The biography of Du Du, named Jiya, was born in Duling, Jingzhao.
The great ancestor was Du Yannian, who served as a censor during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
When Du Du was young, he was very knowledgeable and did not practice small things. The people in the village did not treat him well.
He lived in Meiyang and had good relations with Meiyang Ling. He asked him to do things for him many times, but Meiyang Ling didn't do it for him and hated him. In anger, Meiyang Ling arrested Du Du and sent him to the capital.
When the great Sima Wu Han passed away, Guangwu ordered all the Confucian scholars to express condolences. Du Du wrote an edict in prison with elegant speech. Guangwu praised him for his good writing and gave him silk and exempted him from punishment. Du Du believed that the mountains inside Guanzhong and the river outside were the former capital of the late emperor, and Luoyi should not be rebuilt, so he wrote a "Fu on the Capital" and presented it to the emperor.
Du Du later became an official in the county literature department, but due to eye disease, he did not go to the capital for more than 20 years.
Du Du's maternal great-grandfather, Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian, was famous for his military strategies.
Du Du often sighed and said: Du's civilization is good at politics, but Du Du is not appointed as an official. Xin's upright and martial, but Du is timid and afraid of getting into trouble.
Five generations have passed, but my generation has declined!
Du Du's sister married the Ma family in Fufeng.
In the third year of Jianxin, the chariot and cavalry general Ma Fang attacked the Xiqiang. He asked Du Du to be his lieutenant and died in the battle at Shegu Mountain.
Du Du wrote a total of eighteen articles including Fu, Elegy, Diao, Shu, Zan, "Seven Characters", "Nv's Commandments" and essays.
He also wrote fifteen chapters of "Lun on the Ming Dynasty".
His son Du Gu is a heroic hero and famous for his business.
◆Biography of Wang Long, whose courtesy name is Wenshan and Feng Yi was born in Yunyang.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he was appointed as Lang because of his father's relationship. Later he fled to Hexi and served as Dou Rong's left guard.
In Jianwu, he served as the magistrate of Xinji County.
He is capable of articles and has written a total of twenty-six poems, poems, inscriptions and books.
At that time, in the last years of Wang Mang, Cen Zixiao, the historian of Pei State, was also famous for his articles. Wang Mang was appointed as the emissary and wrote four articles in total: eulogy, elegance, "Fu Shen" and "Shuo Ji".
According to the biography of Xia Gong, Xia Gong was named Jinggong and was a native of Meng, Liang State.
He studied "Han Shi" and "Mencius' Book of Changes" and had thousands of disciples.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, thieves emerged and captured the prefectures and counties. Because of his kindness and trust, Xia Gong was attached to the people, and he defended the area with troops, thus gaining safety.
Guangwu ascended the throne, praised him for his loyalty and courage, called him a doctor, and then promoted him to the captaincy of Taishan.
He gathered the people and was very popular with them.
Xia Gong is good at writing articles, and has written a total of 20 fus, odes, poems and "Encouraging Learning".
He died in office at the age of forty-nine, and all the Confucian scholars jointly gave him the posthumous title "Xuanmingjun".
His son Xia Ya learned a lot when he was young and wrote a total of forty poems, poems, poems and poems.
When the junior middle school was built, Suzong recruited literary scholars extensively, appointed Fu Yi as the Lantai Lingshi, and was awarded the title of doctor. Together with Ban Gu and Jia Kui, he was in charge of the correction of books.
Fu Yi believed that Emperor Xiaoming had the highest merit, but there were no temple odes, so he imitated the "Qing Temple" and wrote ten "Xianzong Odes" to commemorate the emperor. His elegance became famous in the court.
As a relative of the general Ma Fang, he respected Fu Yi very much. He asked Fu Yi to serve as army commander and treated him with the courtesy of a master and friend.
Ma's family was defeated and was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown.
In the first year of Yongyuan, Dou Xian, the general of chariots and cavalry, asked Fu Yi to take charge of the record office and Cui Xiang to take charge of the book.
Dou Xian was promoted to general, Fu Yi was appointed Sima, Ban Gu was appointed as the Central Protector, and General Dou Xian was promoted to general. His articles were the most prosperous at that time.
Fu Yi died young and wrote a total of 28 poems, fuses, poems, odes, congratulations, "Qi Ji" and lianzhu.
◆Huang Xiangzhuan, whose courtesy name is Wenqiang, was from Anlu County, Jiangxia County.
I lost my mother at the age of nine. I miss her so much that I feel haggard and almost dead. The villagers praised him as a filial son.
When he was twelve years old, the prefect Liu Hu heard about it and summoned him as a "filial son". He liked him very much and respected him.
Huang Xiang's family was poor and he had no concubines. He worked hard and took care of himself. He also recited classics extensively, studied Taoism, and wrote good articles.
There is a popular saying in the capital: Jiangxia Huangtong is unparalleled in the world.
He was first appointed as a doctor. In the first year of Yuanhe, Emperor Suzong ordered Huang Xiang to go to Dongguan. Huang Xiang read books he had never seen before.
Huang Xiang later asked for leave. When he returned to the capital, King Qiancheng performed a crowning ceremony. The emperor summoned Huang Xiang to His Highness at his Zhongshan mansion. Looking back at the kings, he said: This is Jiangxia Huangtong who is unparalleled in the world.
Everyone around him looked at him differently.
Later, he was summoned to the Anfu Hall to discuss political affairs, and was awarded the title of Shangshulang. He stated the gains and losses of the court many times, and the rewards increased.
I once slept alone on the stage, never leaving the palace gate day and night. The emperor heard about it and praised him.
In the fourth year of Yongyuan, he was awarded Zuo Cheng. After his merits were fulfilled, he should be promoted. Emperor He retained him and increased his salary.
In six years, he was promoted to Shangshu Ling.
Later, he was appointed as the prefect of Dongjun. Huang Xiang resigned and said: "I am a lonely, humble, ignorant and ignorant person in the Jianghuai area. I have nothing to say about my Confucian classics, conduct, and ability."
Encountering a peaceful and prosperous age, he received the remaining blessings from his ancestors, so he was able to be recruited by the emperor when he was weak and promoted continuously, even to the minister.
So far, he has no meritorious deeds that can be described. He should have died in repayment of his kindness, but unexpectedly, he was appointed as the prefect of the nearby county of the capital, and his position was thousands of miles away.
I heard that when people are awarded officials based on their ability, they will do a good job, and when they are awarded titles based on their merit, the wise and the foolish will all be in their proper place.
I, Huang Xiang, am an unknown person, born in various sects, guarding a county and serving in politics, and I am not qualified for the job.
I'm really afraid that because of my confusion, I will live up to the emperor's kindness.
I also think that the post of Shangshuling is the most confidential and noble, and it is not something that I, Huang Xiang, should hold for a long time.
After receiving the emperor's edict, I was terrified and didn't know what to do.
I, Huang Xiang, am young and just driven.
I would like to beg for mercy, stay as a redundant official, supervise minor duties, do some chores in the palace, and realize my yellow-scented ant-like ambition. This is my great wish until death, and it will be a great honor after my death.
The emperor also loved Huang Xiang's ability and studied history for a long time. He still stayed on as minister, increased his salary by 2,000 dan and gave him 300,000 yuan. From then on, he was in charge of secrets, trusted him very much, and used him highly.
Huang Xiang also works diligently and worries about state affairs as well as family affairs. In the twelfth year, Dongping and Qinghe reported that the court minister Zhong Liao and others had spread rumors to confuse the public and implicated nearly a thousand people.
Huang Xiang told the truth and saved many people.
Suspicious cases in the county and state are often dealt with lightly, and human life is cherished, but I am afraid that I cannot do it.
He is also familiar with border defense affairs. The deployment of military and political affairs is very appropriate.
The emperor knew that he worked hard for the country and rewarded him many times. He expressed condolences when he was sick and gave him medicine.
There were many recommendations during his reign, and the emperor was very fond of him. Public opinion ridiculed him for being overly favored.
In the first year of Yanping, he was promoted to the prefect of Wei County.
The county originally had inner and outer gardens, which were often planted separately with others, and thousands of dendrobiums could be harvested a year.

Du Du, styled Jiya, was from Duling, Jingzhao. His great ancestor was Du Yannian, a censor under Emperor Xuan. Though knowledgeable, Du Du was not well-regarded locally. After a conflict with Meiyang Ling, he was arrested and sent to the capital. While imprisoned, he wrote an edict for Guangwu, who praised his writing, gave him silk, and pardoned him. Du Du later argued against rebuilding Luoyi, writing a "Fu on the Capital." He served as a county literary official but did not go to the capital for over twenty years due to eye disease. He lamented his family's decline, noting his ancestors' achievements contrasted with his own lack of appointment. He died in battle serving as a lieutenant under Ma Fang. His works include eighteen articles and fifteen chapters of "Lun on the Ming Dynasty." His son Du Gu was a heroic figure.

Wang Long, styled Wenshan, from Yunyang, served as Lang under Wang Mang, then fled to Hexi. Under Jianwu, he became magistrate of Xinji County. He wrote twenty-six poems and other works. Cen Zixiao of Pei State was also famous for his articles under Wang Mang.

Xia Gong, styled Jinggong, from Liang State, studied "Han Shi" and "Mencius' Book of Changes," teaching thousands. During Wang Mang's reign, he defended his area with troops. Guangwu appointed him doctor, then captain of Taishan. He wrote twenty works, including "Encouraging Learning," and died in office at forty-nine, posthumously named "Xuanmingjun." His son Xia Ya wrote forty poems.

Fu Yi, a literary scholar under Suzong, served as Lantai Lingshi and doctor, correcting books with Ban Gu and Jia Kui. He wrote ten "Xianzong Odes" to honor Emperor Xiaoming. He served under Ma Fang, but was dismissed after Ma's defeat. Later, he worked for Dou Xian. He died young, leaving twenty-eight works.

Huang Xiang, styled Wenqiang, from Jiangxia, was known for filial piety after losing his mother at nine. At twelve, Prefect Liu Hu summoned him as a "filial son." He was poor but studious, earning the saying "Jiangxia Huangtong is unparalleled in the world." He served as doctor, Shangshulang, and Shangshuling, often discussing court affairs. He declined a post as prefect of Dongjun, citing his inadequacy. The emperor retained him, increasing his salary. He handled border affairs well and saved many in a rumor case. He later became prefect of Wei County, where he rented out gardens to avoid competing with the people, and distributed wages during a flood. He died at home after dismissal. He wrote five poems and other works.

Liu Yi, son of King Jing of Beihai, was known for literary debate. He published "Lun on Han De" and "Lun on Constitution," earning praise and a grant from Emperor An.

Li You, styled Boren, from Guanghan, was famous for his articles. Jia Kui recommended him to Emperor He, and he served as Lantai Lingshi and admonishing official. He co-authored "Han Ji" and remonstrated against deposing the prince. He died at eighty-three, leaving twenty-eight works. Li Sheng, also from his county, wrote dozens of poems.

Su Shun, styled Xiaoshan, from Jingzhao, was known for talent and learning under Emperors He and An. He favored health techniques and lived in seclusion, later becoming a doctor. He wrote sixteen works. Cao Zhong and Bo Shi of Fufeng were also talented, writing four works. Cao Shuo wrote four chapters of "Ode to the Han Dynasty."

Liu Zhen, styled Qiusun, from Nanyin, was eager to learn. He served as a servant under Empress Dowager Deng, collating classics. He wrote biographies of famous officials and served as Zongzheng and Weiwei. He wrote seven works and thirty chapters of "Shiming."

Ge Gong, styled Yuanfu, from Liang State, was known for writing under Emperor He. He served as magistrate of Dangyin and Linfen, achieving political success. He wrote twelve works.

Wang Yi, styled Shuyuan, from Nanjun, served as school secretary and servant under Emperor Shun. He authored "Chu Ci Chapters and Sentences" and 123 chapters of "Chinese Poems." His son Wang Yanshou wrote "Ode to Lingguang Palace" and died young.

Cui Qi, styled Ziwei, from Zhuo County, was known for extensive articles. He admonished Liang Ji for illegal acts, writing "Admonitions to Foreign Relatives" and "White Bird Ode." Liang Ji sent an assassin, but the assassin spared Cui Qi. Liang Ji later arrested and killed him. He wrote fifteen works.

Bian Shao, styled Xiaoxian, from Chenliu, was famous for writing and teaching. He was quick-witted, once defending his daytime sleep with a clever rhyme. He served as Prime Minister of Linying, governor, and Shangshu, dying in office. He wrote fifteen works.
