◆The biography of Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Zijian, was from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, and the son of Situ Li Hui.
Li Hui's deeds are in "The Biography of Fang Shu".
The statue of Li Gu has a peculiar appearance. There are bones on the head that protrude like a tripod foot, which rise into the hairline, and there are turtle inscriptions on the feet.
When he was young, he was eager to learn and often traveled thousands of miles to find teachers on foot.
So I read many ancient books and made friends with many wise men.
People with lofty ideals from all over the world envy his style and come to learn from him.
Everyone in the capital admired and said: This is the second Mr. Li again. Both Sili and Yizhou ordered the county governors to promote Li Gu as Xiaolian and call him Sikongpu, but they did not take office.
In the second year of Yangjia, there were earthquakes, landslides, fires and other changes. The ministers recommended Li Gu to take countermeasures. The emperor issued an edict specifically asking him about the shortcomings of the contemporary era and what he should do for government.
Li Gu replied: "I heard that the king regards heaven as his father and earth as his mother, and possesses the treasures of mountains and rivers."
If the royal way works, then Yin and Yang will be harmonious; if politics is disobedient, landslides and earthquakes will become disasters.
This is all related to the heart of heaven, and the results are achieved in achieving things.
The so-called transformation is achieved by job, and officials are able to manage.
In ancient times, those who became officials were all virtuous and had titles; those who become officials today only have wealth and strength.
The ministers heard that the imperial edict sought to be lenient and generous, but resented harshness and cruelty.
However, today's chief officials have made a name for themselves by killing more, and they will definitely be promoted and rewarded; while those who are kind-hearted and have no support from party members are often ostracized and exiled.
Therefore, honest and honest customs cannot be promoted, and Zhou's thin customs cannot be reformed.
Even if we use heavy punishment and heavy prohibition, what is the benefit?
The former Emperor Xiao'an messed up the old rules and conferred a title on his mother, Wang Sheng, thus creating a monster, which allowed Fan Feng and others to take advantage of their power and usurp the majesty of the Lord.
Since he emerged from the crisis and became emperor, everyone in the world is looking up to him, hoping that the political system will change.
After a long time of accumulation, it is easy to revive, and one should indeed be generous and think about the way to do good; but the people who discuss it also say that the current things are the same as before.
The minister crouched among the mountains and grass, feeling very sad.
Recalling that since the rise of the Han Dynasty, for more than three hundred years, sages and ten and eight monarchs have appeared one after another.
Don’t you have the kindness of Ah Ru?
Have you forgotten the favor of the noble noble?
However, the superiors are afraid of the power of God, and the inferiors know according to the scriptures that they must not violate moral principles, so they do not add rewards.
Now, although Mrs. Song has the character of great merit and diligence, as long as she is rewarded, it will be enough to repay her hard work; as for the enfeoffment of land, it is really contrary to the old rules.
It is said that my grandmother is modest in nature and will inevitably be unreasonable. Your Majesty should praise her noble spirit of resigning from the country and make her a blessing to everyone. Generally speaking, the reason why concubines’ homes are rarely complete is due to nature?
It's just because the title is too high and too obvious, and they monopolize power, and the way of heaven hates fullness the most, but they don't know how to harm themselves, so they fall down.
The late emperor's favor met the Yan family, and his title was established too quickly, so the disaster did not last long.
"Laozi" said: The advance is rapid, and the retreat is rapid. Nowadays, the Liang family's relatives live in the Jiao Fang where the Queen lives. According to etiquette, they cannot treat their wife's parents as ministers. However, it is still okay to treat them as nobles.
However, her children and nephews were both prosperous and distinguished. The story of Yongping and Jianchu years is probably not like this.
Isn't it great that the infantry captain Liang Ji and the other servants should still serve as Huangmen officials, so that the power of the country can be removed from the hands of relatives and the political power should be returned to the country? The reason why the edict prohibits ministers and ministers from serving as officials to inspect filial piety and integrity is because they have authority, take care of personal affairs, and grant requests.
But Zhongchang serves beside the sun and the moon, and his influence is vibrating throughout the world. There is no limit for his children to be officials.
Although he seems to be humble on the outside and does not interfere with the state and county, those who are flattering and hypocritical are relying on the wind to recommend him.
Now you can set up permanent bans, the same as Zhongchen. Once upon a time, Princess Guantao, the third daughter of Emperor Guangwu, asked for a groom for her son. Emperor Ming disagreed and gave her tens of millions of dollars.
Why do we give less generous gifts than give more emphasis on positions? It is because officials lose their talents and harm the people.
I heard secretly that Wuxuan, the Sima of Changshui, and Yangdi, the Hou of Kaiyang City Gate, etc., had no other merits and deeds, so they made up for it when they first paid homage to the officials.
Although this is a small mistake, it slowly breaks the old rules.
The laws of the sages should be adhered to unswervingly. Once there is a mistake in politics and religion, it will take a hundred years to recover.
The Book of Songs says: God is dull, but the people are miserable. This is a mockery of King Zhou Li's way of changing the previous kings, which made his people sick. Now that Your Majesty has a minister, it is like having the Big Dipper in the sky.
Beidou is the mouthpiece of Heaven, and Shangshu is the mouthpiece of His Majesty.
The Beidou measures the vitality and regulates the weather of the four seasons.
The minister pays the king's orders and governs the world. He has great power and responsibility.
If you don't act calmly, disaster will inevitably come.
Indeed, people should be chosen carefully to make up for the holy government.
Now the people who jointly govern the world with Your Majesty are the public officials and ministers on the outside, and the Huangmen on the inside. For example, within a family, if the affairs of the family are peaceful, everyone will be blessed, and if there is danger, everyone will suffer together.
The governor and Erqian Shi control the ministry on the outside, but are restricted by laws on the inside.
If the surface of anything is distorted, the shadow will be slanted, and the clear water will be clean. It is like knocking on the root of a tree and shaking all the branches.
"Song of Zhou" says: If a thin word shakes it, it will all shake. This means that what is moved in the heart is reflected on the outside.
So, can this dynasty issue orders casually?
Once the gap is opened, evil people will have their own thoughts; if the gap is temporarily open, then the road to benevolence and righteousness will be blocked.
The punishment cannot be reinstated, and the deeds will become bad as a result.
This is the order of the world and the current urgent task.
Your Majesty should open the book in the golden cabinet in the stone chamber, display the books, and recruit a group of Confucian scholars to ask questions about the gains and losses of government, criticize changes, and seek God's will.
What they say makes sense, they implement it immediately, select their people, and commend those who are capable.
Then holy virtues are heard every day, and loyal ministers use their wisdom.
The eunuchs should also be dismissed, their authority should be removed, and two regular servants should be appointed, upright and virtuous people, and let them inspect the affairs on the left and right; five people from Xiaohuangmen, who are intelligent and elegant, should be allowed to work in the palace.
In this way, the people who talk about it will become tired of it, and a peaceful world will come.
The reason why I dare to state foolish words and take the liberty to report to you is that if the emperor wants to enlighten your majesty, your majesty should consider your words carefully and have mercy on me and pardon my death penalty.
Emperor Shun saw the above countermeasures and adopted many of them. He immediately asked his mother to move back to his younger brother's house. All the regular servants kowtowed and apologized, and the court's political discipline was solemn.
He also appointed Li Gu as his minister, but the eunuchs around his mother hated Li Gu for being too outspoken, so they fabricated crimes to frame Li Gu, and everything went from bad to worse.
The chief minister Huang Shang and others asked the general Liang Shang, and the servant Huang Qiong investigated Li Gu's case. It took a long time before he was appointed as Yilang.
Li Gu went out to become the magistrate of Luo County in Guanghan. When he arrived at Baishui Pass, he removed his seal and ribbon, returned to Hanzhong, and closed his door to avoid interacting with others.
For half a year, Liang Shang asked Li Guzuo to work as a lieutenant.
Liang Shang assisted the government as his father, but he was meek and defensive, unable to rectify the situation. Disasters occurred many times, and the power below him became increasingly powerful. Li Gu wanted to ask Liang Shang to rectify his morals first and resign from his position as Gao Man, so he wrote a memorial to Liang Shang: "Spring and Autumn" praises Yi father to open up the path of righteousness, and blames Wu Hao to close the door of benefit. When the way of righteousness is closed, the door of profit is opened; when the door of profit is opened, the way of righteousness is blocked.
The former Emperor Xiao'an appointed Borong, Fan Feng and others internally, and Zhou Guang, Xie Yun and others were appointed externally. They accepted bribes and hired people improperly. There was a lot of discussion in the world and the voice of resentment was everywhere.
When the imperial court was first established, it was relatively quiet. Within a few years, it gradually deteriorated.
As the party advances, people are promoted every day, and those who stick to the good path are at the end of their rope, without any way to correct their shortcomings and establish righteousness.
After taking the throne for more than ten years, the crown prince has not yet been established, and everyone is looking forward to it.
The number of concubines in the palace can be reduced, and people of low status but suitable for having children can be selected to join the emperor and help God's will.
If there is a prince, the mother should breastfeed the baby herself, and should not leave it to the witch doctor who protects the concubine, which may lead to the disaster of murdering her son like Zhao Feiyan.
The generals of the Ming Dynasty have high prestige and status. They should worry about world affairs, advocate modesty and frugality, and set an example for everyone.
However, building a new ancestral hall requires hundreds of millions of labor and is not to show virtue or frugality.
Over the past few years, disasters have appeared many times, and it has not rained for many consecutive years, but it has been gloomy and cloudy.
There must be a conspiracy within the palace.
Confucius said: A wise man thinks of punishment when he sees a change, but a fool hides his name when he sees something strange. There is no distinction between closeness and distance in the way of heaven, which can be respected.
The recent lunar eclipse has been on the side of Duanmen. Moon, the symbol of the minister.
Generally speaking, if it is too high, it will be dangerous; if it is too full, it will overflow; if the moon is full, it will be short; and if the sun is at noon, it will shift.
These four items are natural numbers.
In the heart of heaven and earth, blessings should be modest and should not be prosperous. Therefore, virtuous people will retire after success, preserve their reputation, and live their lives well, without fear or worry.
If Wang Gang is kept intact, his conduct is loyal, Ming Gong follows the path of Bo Gao, and his immortal reputation is preserved, is it the same as these mediocre relatives who enjoy a good position?
I am a foolish person who is ignorant of the general situation. I secretly feel that the ancients repaid a favor with a meal. How much more can I not do my best to receive care and preferential treatment?
Liang Shang did not listen.
During the Yonghe period, bandits arose in Jingzhou and could not be pacified for many years, so the imperial court appointed Li Gu as the governor of Jingzhou.

Today's collapse, people and gods are moved, how can any ministers rebel against the Communist Party and hide it?

Recently, the Marquis of Beixiang died, and the Yan brothers, Jiang Jing and others also concealed the secret, so Sun Cheng committed murder.

Lieutenant Li Gu, for official duties and private interests, acted evil in accordance with the good, alienated close relatives, and established his own branch.

His travels are excessively extravagant, and the curtains on his carriages are bright and sunny.

Before the emperor's mausoleum was built, he went against the old rules, took credit for all the good things, blamed all the faults on the king, expelled the old ministers, was not allowed to serve, and acted arrogantly. No one was more powerful than Li Gu.
I heard that the prime minister's job is to regulate yin and yang. If Xuanji is unjust and bandits cause trouble, the responsibility lies with the Taiwei.

There is no loyalty and no slander.
The crime of a son is no greater than that of burdening his father, and the crime of a minister is no deeper than that of ruining the king.
Li Gu's crime should be beheaded.
After the letter was submitted, Liang Ji told the Queen Mother, please submit it to the people below for trial.

It can be seen that the matter is of great importance and must be carefully considered!

summary:
Li Gu, courtesy name Zijian, was from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, and the son of Situ Li Hui. He had a peculiar appearance with bones on his head protruding like a tripod foot and turtle inscriptions on his feet. He was an eager learner who traveled thousands of miles to find teachers, befriended many wise men, and attracted students from across the land. He was promoted as Xiaolian but did not take office.

In the second year of Yangjia, after earthquakes and landslides, the emperor asked Li Gu for advice. Li Gu replied that if the royal way works, Yin and Yang are harmonious; if politics are disobedient, disasters occur. He criticized that officials today only seek wealth and power, and that harsh officials are promoted while kind ones are ostracized. He advised against enfeoffing the emperor's grandmother, citing the danger of excessive power for relatives, and warned against the influence of the Liang family and eunuchs. He urged the emperor to select virtuous officials, dismiss eunuchs, and follow the laws of sages. Emperor Shun adopted many of his suggestions, but eunuchs framed Li Gu, leading to his dismissal. He later became a magistrate but resigned and returned home.

Liang Shang asked Li Gu to be a lieutenant. Li Gu wrote to Liang Shang, criticizing the corruption of previous reigns and urging him to rectify morals, reduce palace concubines, and establish a crown prince. He warned against building new ancestral halls and noted that disasters and eclipses indicated conspiracies within the palace. Liang Shang did not listen. During the Yonghe period, Li Gu was appointed governor of Jingzhou, where he pardoned bandits and pacified the region within half a year. He reported corrupt officials, who bribed Liang Ji, leading to Li Gu's transfer to Taishan. There, he dismissed most soldiers and used kindness to subdue bandits within a year.

Li Gu was promoted and recommended several scholars. He later became Taiwei under Emperor Chong. When the emperor died, Li Gu insisted on immediate mourning, opposing the Empress Dowager's delay. He advocated for establishing an older, virtuous emperor, but Liang Ji appointed the young Liu Zuan as Emperor Zhi. Li Gu reduced burial costs for the emperor. He dismissed over a hundred improperly appointed officials, who then slandered him to Liang Ji, accusing him of nepotism, extravagance, and lack of mourning. The Empress Dowager spared Li Gu from death. Liang Ji later poisoned Emperor Zhi. Li Gu cried over the emperor's body. When establishing a new emperor, Li Gu advocated for Liu Lian, the King of Qinghe, but Liang Ji, persuaded by eunuchs, chose Liu Zhidang (Emperor Huan) instead. Liang Ji later falsely accused Li Gu of plotting to make Liu Lian emperor and imprisoned him. Despite public support, Liang Ji had Li Gu killed at age 54. Before death, Li Gu wrote to Hu Guang and Zhao Jie, blaming them for following Liang Ji and causing the decline of the Han dynasty. His sons died in prison, and his body was exposed. His disciple Guo Liang and others mourned him, and the Empress Dowager eventually allowed his burial.

Du Qiao, courtesy name Shurong, was from Linli, Hanoi. He served as a prefect and later as a servant. He reported that Li Gu had the best political performance and that others, including Liang Ji's relatives, had embezzled money. He was promoted to Minister of Agriculture. He remonstrated against granting titles to Liang Ji's relatives and eunuchs without merit, warning it would cause chaos. He refused Liang Ji's requests to borrow evidence and attend his daughter's funeral, earning Liang Ji's hatred. As Guang Luxun, he opposed lavish gifts for Liang Ji's sister becoming queen and refused to appoint a corrupt official. After Li Gu was deposed, Du Qiao remained serious and unyielding. He was dismissed due to an earthquake. Eunuchs and Liang Ji framed him for opposing the emperor's ascension and colluding with Li Gu. He was arrested and died in prison. His body was exposed, but his former subordinate Yang Kuang mourned him and requested burial, which the Empress Dowager granted. The historian commented that Li Gu and Du Qiao sacrificed their lives for righteousness, unlike Hu Guang and Zhao Jie.

In Jianwu 5-6, he led troops against Hanzhong bandits and Gongsun Shu, defeating them. As peace prevailed, Li Tong sought to retire due to illness, but Guangwu refused. He became Grand Sikong but remained humble, often taking sick leave. Guangwu favored him, granting his son Li Xiong a marquisate. Li Tong died in Jianwu 18, posthumously titled Gonghou. Wang Chang, convinced of the Han's destiny, persuaded his reluctant generals Cheng Dan and Zhang to join, citing the people's longing for Han. They united, defeated Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci, and supported Gengshi. Wang Chang became a court official and marquis, later serving as Nanyang prefect under Gengshi. After Gengshi's fall, he surrendered to Guangwu, who forgave him and appointed him Zuocao. Wang Chang campaigned against various rebels, including Deng Feng and Wei Xiao, and pacified regions. He died in Jianwu 12, posthumously titled Jiehou. His son Wang Guang succeeded but lost the fief due to involvement in a rebellion.

Deng Chen, courtesy name Weiqing, from Xinye, Nanyang, married Guangwu's sister Liu Yuan. During Wang Mang's reign, he heard a prophecy about Liu Xiu becoming emperor and bonded with Guangwu. When Han forces rose, Deng Chen joined Guangwu at Jiyang. After a defeat, Guangwu fled with his sister Boji, but Liu Yuan and her daughters were killed. Deng Chen's home was defiled, yet he remained loyal. Under Gengshi, he became a partial general, fighting alongside Guangwu. He served as Changshan governor, supporting Guangwu during Wang Lang's rebellion. After Guangwu's ascension, Deng Chen became a marquis. He governed Zhongshan and Runan, building irrigation systems that enriched the region. He died in Jianwu 25, posthumously titled Hui. His lineage continued until it ended without heirs.

Lai She, courtesy name Junshe, from Xinye, was the son of an admonishing official who married Guangwu's aunt. His sister married Liu Jia, King of Hanzhong. After Gengshi's fall, Lai She persuaded Liu Jia to join Guangwu, who appointed him Taizhong doctor. Lai She volunteered to negotiate with Wei Xiao, securing his son as hostage. When Wei Xiao hesitated to attack Shu, Lai She angrily confronted him, nearly assassinating him. Wei Xiao imprisoned him but released him due to his reputation. In Jianwu 8, Lai She attacked Lueyang, holding it against Wei Xiao's siege until Guangwu relieved him. He later campaigned against Gongsun Shu and Qiang tribes, pacifying Longxi. In Jianwu 11, he was assassinated by Shu agents. Before dying, he reprimanded General Gai Yan for weeping and dictated a memorial recommending Duan Xiang and pleading for his brother. Guangwu mourned deeply, granting him posthumous honors. His son Lai Xi succeeded, and his brother was made a marquis. The historian praised Lai She's integrity as an envoy, noting his sincerity earned trust without selfish ambition.

◆In the biography of Li Xun, Li Xun was born in Linjing, Anding.
He studied "Han Shi" at a young age and taught hundreds of students.
Li Hong, the prefect of Yingchuan, asked Li Xun to be appointed as a meritorious official. However, he failed to take up the post, and the prefecture called him to work.
When Li Hong died, Li Xun responded to the state's order and sent Li Hong back to his hometown for his funeral.
He has been buried, and the grave has been left to mourn for three years.
Later Li Xun was called into Situ Huanyu's mansion.
Later he was promoted to the imperial censor, and he went to Youzhou as an envoy to declare the emperor's favor and comfort Beidi. Wherever he went, he described the mountains and rivers, as well as the conditions of villages and settlements, etc., in more than a hundred volumes, all of which were sealed. Emperor Suzong commended him and appointed him as the governor of Yanzhou.
He set an example by keeping promises, often using sheepskin as a mat and a quilt as a cover.
He was promoted to the governor of Zhangye and gained a prestigious reputation.
At that time, General Dou Xian and his soldiers were stationed in Wuwei. No matter how far or near the country was, no one in the country did not practice rituals and gifts of property. Li Xun was not loyal to his duty and was dismissed by Dou Xian.
Later, he was recruited as a visitor and made Chijie the captain of the Western Regions.
The Western Region was rich and rich, and there were many treasures. The servants and envoys of various countries and merchants from Hu Dynasty gave Li Xun many things such as slaves, horses, gold, silver, and fragrant yokes, but Li Xun refused to accept any of them.
The Northern Xiongnu cut off Cheshi and Yiwu in the Western Regions several times, and missions in the area west of Longsha were blocked. Li Xun offered a reward, so he beheaded the commander and hung his head at the military gate.
From then on, the road was clear and smooth, and kindness and power flowed side by side.
Later he moved to Wuwei to be the prefect.
He was dismissed from his post for some reason and walked back to his hometown. He lived in seclusion in the mountains and swamps, making a hut from grass and weaving mats with other people to support himself.
When the Xiqiang rebelled, Li Xun went to the farm and was captured by the Qiang people.
The Qiang people always heard Xun's name and sent him away.
Xun went to Luoyang to express his gratitude.
At that time, there was a famine. Sikong Zhang Min, Situ Lu Gong and other sons sent grain to Xun, but Xun did not accept it.
He moved to Xin'an Pass and picked up acorns to fill his stomach.
Died at the age of ninety-six.
◆Chen Chan's biography, Chen Chan's courtesy name is Jishan, and he was a native of Anhan, Ba County.
He was a meritorious officer in the county, doing good and punishing evil, and was feared by the people in the country.
He was inspected for being filial and honest, and he was appointed in the state to be engaged in governance.
At that time, the governor was accused of accepting bribes, and Chen Chan should be arrested and investigated. He had no property, just some funeral utensils.
After arriving, the plunder was in vain, all the five poisons were used, the Zen mind was at ease, the confession remained unchanged, and the case was solved.
Deng Zhi, the general of chariots and cavalry, heard about his reputation and summoned him, making him a talented person.
At that time, the barbarians in Hanzhong rebelled and made Chen Chan the governor of Hanzhong.
The barbarians always surrendered immediately when they heard about his reputation.
Chen Chan was promoted to Zuo Fengyi and entered the court to worship as an admonishing doctor.
In the first year of Yongning, the king of the Shan Dynasty in the southwest presented music and illusions to people who could spit fire, dismember their bodies, and replace the heads of cattle and horses.
In the second year of Yuanhui, there was a performance in the court. Emperor An and his ministers watched it together and found it strange.
Chen Chan left the table alone and raised his hands and said loudly: In the past, Qi and Lu had a meeting in the valley, and Qi was enjoying the dwarfs. Confucius took photos of ministers and thought it was an insult to the princes, so he beheaded the dwarfs.
He also said: If you listen to the sound of Zheng, you will be far away from the sycophants.
It is not appropriate for the imperial court to have the skills of barbarians and Di.
Shangshu Chen Zhonggai reported to Chen Chan: In ancient times, the music of Hehuan was danced in the hall, and the music of the four barbarians was played in the door. Therefore, the Book of Songs said: To the south of Yiya, Zhu Li was appointed in the late Wei Dynasty.
Today, the Shan State passes through the Liusha River and crosses the county mountains, coming thousands of miles to contribute. It is not the voice of Zheng Wei, it is comparable to the sycophants, but Chen Chan ridiculed the government in the court, and asked Chen Chan to be impeached and imprisoned.
There was an edict stating that arrests were not allowed and he was demoted to the rank of Xuantuhou Chengzhaowei. The edict said: If you dare not take up the post, report the name of your wife's servant.
Chen Chan has already set off, and the court is accusing him.
When the Northern Huns invaded Liaodong, they pursued Chen Chan as the governor of Liaodong.
The Hu people were afraid of his power and retreated hundreds of miles.
Chen Chan did not add troops to pursue them, but only sent officers and soldiers to Xiaoyu to comfort them. Chanyu followed the envoy back to the county.
Chen Chan studied etiquette and taught moral principles to influence them.
Chanyu was convinced and sent away some of Hu's treasures.
Later, Deng Zhao was killed, and Chen Chan was dismissed from office because he was Deng's former official.
He also made a long history of the chariot and cavalry general Yan Xian.
Emperor Shun ascended the throne and was promoted to Sili Xiaowei.
The next year, he died in the government.
His son, Chen Cheng, had a clear name and became the prefect of Hanzhong.
◆Pang Can's biography, Pang Can's courtesy name is Zhongda, and he was a native of Fengshi, Henan.
He began to serve as an official there, and was unknown. Henan Yin Pangfen saw it and thought it was strange. He promoted him to Xiaolian and worshiped him as Zuo Xiaoling.
He broke the law and was sent to Ruolu Prison.
In the first year of Yongchu, the Zhongqiang people in Liangzhou rebelled, and the imperial court sent cavalry general Deng Zhi to attack them.
When Pang Shen was in exile, he sent his son Pang Jun to write: "Nowadays, the refugees in Xizhou are causing disturbances, the conscription continues, the water supply continues, and the soil does not recover."
In addition, the army was deployed, the distant garrison was very tired, the farm work was busy transferring, and all the resources were exhausted.
The fields cannot be cultivated, the crops cannot be harvested, there is no plan, and there is no hope for autumn.
The people were exhausted and could not bear it.
The foolish minister thinks that transporting grain thousands of miles away is as far away as the Qiang Rong. It is better to gather troops to support the people and wait until they are tired.
Deng Zhao, the general of chariots and cavalry, was supposed to lead his troops on the expedition, leaving Ren Shang, the captain of Zhengxi School, to supervise the people of Liangzhou and move to Sanfu.
Let the corvees rest to help them during their time, and stop the fertilization to increase their wealth, so that the men can farm and the women can weave, and then recharge their batteries, take advantage of the slack, and attack when they are surprised and unprepared. Then the revenge of the border people can be avenged, and the shame of running north will be avenged.
When the book was sent out, the imperial censor, Fan Zhunshang, recommended Pang Shendao: "I heard that there are hundreds of birds of prey, but they are not as good as one osprey."
In the past, Emperor Xiaowen understood Feng Tang's words and pardoned Wei Shang's crime, making him a border guard. The Huns did not dare to take a step south.
Use a minister's body to solve a party's difficulties and choose people.
I saw that Pang Shen, the former commander of the Zuo School, was brave, resourceful, unique, talented in military strategy, and had the demeanor of Wei Shang.
I committed a micro-law in the past and lost my job for a long time.
Now the Qiang and Rong are in danger, and the army is stationed in Xitun. I think that people like Pang Shen should be included in the army.
I hope that the Ming Dynasty will adopt the measures of the previous life, observe Wei Shang's contribution, pardon Pang Shen's punishment, and use it as a military vanguard, it will be effective and help the country's prestige.
Empress Dowager Deng accepted his words, immediately promoted Pang Shen from among his disciples, worshiped him as a visitor, asked him to go to the west to supervise the three auxiliary military camps, and summoned Deng Stallion back.
Four years later, the Qiang bandits came back again. Military expenditures were increasing, and the harvests had been poor year after year. Each stone of grain cost more than 50,000 yuan.
Pang Shen reported to Deng Zhi: "Qiang bandits have been particularly troublesome in Longyou in recent years. The expenditure on corvee taxes and services has been huge, and the government's debt has reached billions."
Now he collects grain and silk from the people and sells various items to meet the needs of the officials.
The Qiang captives were injured externally and trapped internally.
So he transported grain thousands of miles to the west county of Wudu.
The road is dangerous and there are too many difficulties. If you go fast, the money will be damaged, and if you go slowly, the grain will be damaged. The grain will be scattered in the wilderness, and the cattle and horses will die in the mountains and swamps.
There are not enough county officials, so they often borrow money from the people.
The people are already poor, who will they turn to for help?
In name, he rescued Jincheng, but actually trapped Sanfu.
Sanfu was already poor, which in turn became a disaster for Jincheng.
Shen had said several times before that the Western Regions should be abandoned, but he was laughed at by the scholar-bureaucrats in Xizhou.
Now if we covet the barren land, care about the useless people, let the army suffer in the Yiwu wilderness, and worry about the other three tribes, if Liangzhou is destroyed, the chaos will continue to this day.
The open borders are not peaceful and are of no benefit to the strength of the country; if there are many fields left uncultivated, how can we avoid famine!
Therefore, those who know how to govern a country must focus on the country and not seek external benefits; they must make the people rich and not greedy for the vast territory.
Sanfu Mountain is far away and the people are sparse, so the county is empty, but there are many places for people to live.
Nowadays, those border counties that cannot survive on their own should be moved to Zhuling and fields to garrison the old counties.
There are isolated cities and counties, so they are forced to move; it is expensive to transport people far away, but they gather together to get close; there are too many corvees, so let them rest.
This is the best of the best strategies.
Deng Zhao and his ministers wanted to follow Pang Shen's suggestion due to insufficient state resources, but many people disagreed, so they stopped.
Later, he worshiped Pang Shen as the prefect of Hanyang.
Ren Tang, a county man, has a strange festival and lives in seclusion to teach apprentices.
When Pang Shen took office, he went to visit him first. Ren Tang didn't talk to him. He just placed a big book of sage and a bowl of water in front of the screen, and he lay down under the door with his grandson in his arms.
The chief clerk reported that Ren Tang was arrogant.
Pang Shen thought about his intention, and after a long time he said: "Ren Tang wants to tell the prefect: Shui, you want me to be innocent."
Pull out a big book of sage, and you want me to attack the powerful clan.
Holding a child in your arms, you want me to open the door and take pity on the orphan.
So he sighed and returned.
When Pang Shen was in office, he was indeed able to restrain the strong and help the weak, and win the hearts and minds of the people with favorable policies.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, he was promoted to the captain of the Qiang Protector. The rebel Qiang missed his kindness.
The next year, many of the Shaodang Qiang people surrendered, and then they were allowed to return to their capital and live on the road to the west of the river.
At this time, the Xianling Qiang tyrants were arrogant in the north, and the imperial court ordered Shen to lead 7,000 Hu soldiers who surrendered to the Qiang and Huangzhong uprisings, and made an appointment with Sima Jun, the general who was marching to the west, to meet in the north to attack them.
Pang Shen was defeated by the Qiang people on the road.
He had missed his deadline, so he claimed he was ill and brought his troops back. He was called to jail for the crime of false illness.
Ma Rong, the school's doctor, wrote a request: "The Xirong rebelled and the bandits invaded the five states. Your Majesty sympathizes with the suffering of the people, mourns the unemployment of the people, and uses up all the property in the treasury to support the army."
In the past, during the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the yongnu invaded Haohe Fang. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Xiongnu also invaded Shangjun. However, King Xuan made great contributions to the revival, and Emperor Wen established the title of Taizong.
Not only were the two emperors wise and talented, but also because of the help of the tiger generals who defended the city, "Nan Zhong Hehe" was listed in "Zhou Shi", and Yafu Jiujiu was recorded in Han Ce.
Pang Shen, the former guard of the Qiang School, was a versatile man of both civil and military talent and far-reaching intellect. He had both a sense of righteousness, bravery and perseverance, as well as a talent for erudition and profound planning.
He also conquered the Liao general Liang Jinjin. He had commanded the Western Regions and worked hard for several years. He returned and stayed in the third auxiliary. He was able to achieve results and was idle in the north. Chanyu surrendered.
Now they are all locked up and trapped in the legal system.
In the past, Xun Lin's father was defeated in Bi'an, and the Marquis of Jin restored his position; Meng Mingshi lost his division in Gu, but Qin Bo did not depose him.
Therefore, Jin Jing merged with Chi Di's land, and Qin Mu Gong dominated Xirong.
We should look at the two monarchs from a distance and allow Pang Shen and Liang Jinjin to be forgiven. This will indeed be beneficial to Zhechang and conducive to sanctification.
According to the memorial, Liang Jinjin and Pang Shen were pardoned.
Later, Pang Shen was appointed as the governor of Liaodong.
In the first year of Yongjian's reign, he was promoted to general of Liao Dynasty.
Four years later, he entered the imperial court and became Da Honglu.
The minister's servant shot Yu Xu and recommended him, saying that he had the skills and talents of a prime minister. During the reign of Emperor Shun, he was appointed as a Taiwei to record the affairs of the minister.
At this time, among the three princes, Pang Shen had a reputation of being loyal and upright. He was framed and slandered many times by the left and right. He believed that the person he appointed was against the emperor's decree, so he was put under charge of Chengfeng.
At this time, the meeting was about Mao Cai, Xiao Lian, and Pang was imprisoned. He said that he was ill and could not meet at the meeting.
In the plan, Duan Gong of the Han Dynasty in Guangzhou met to clear the road: I saw people walking on the road, farmers and weavers, and they all said: Taiwei Pang Shen pays homage to his loyalty, but because of the straight road, he cannot do anything against his will, so he is isolated among the evil people, and he is in a place where he will be slandered.
I also hope that I will be safe in Your Majesty's life, but because of the slanderous people, I hurt the loyal and upright people. This is the great prohibition of heaven and earth and the sincerity of the human master.
In the past, Bai Qi gave death, and the princes drank wine to congratulate each other; when Ji Zi came back, the people of Lu were happy that he had alleviated the national crisis.
The country is transformed because of its virtuous ministers, and its monarch is at peace because of its loyal ministers.
Today, everyone is happy that your Majesty has such a loyal and virtuous minister, and I hope that he will be favored and appointed in order to bring peace to the world.
According to the memorial, the imperial court sent Xiaohuangmen to monitor Pang Shen's illness, and sent an imperial doctor to deliver sheep wine.
Later, Pang Shen hated his ex-wife's son and threw him into a well to kill him.
Pang Shen had always been at loggerheads with Zhu Liang, the commander of Luoyang. When Zhu Liang heard about this, he led his officials into the Taiwei's Mansion to find out what was going on. He then reported Pang Shen's crime, and he was averted because of the disaster.
Some officials thought that Zhu Liang insulted the prime minister without reporting it first and was thrown into prison.
I wish Liang could win the hearts of the people, and Luoyang officials would guard the palace and ask for punishment, tens of millions of people every day, and they would be exempted from punishment according to the edict.
In the fourth year of Yangjia, Pang Shen was appointed as Taiwei.
In the first year of Yonghe, he was dismissed from office due to long illness and died at home.
◆Chen Gui's biography, Chen Gui's courtesy name is Shuzhen, and he was born in the Shangdang family.
His family background was that of a border general. He learned to bow and horse since he was a child, and he dominated Beizhou.
Chen Gui was ambitious at a young age.
During the Yongjian period, he was promoted to Xiaolian, promoted five times, and became the prefect of Wuyuan.
In the fifth year of Yonghe's reign, he was appointed as Zhonglang General who was sent as envoy to the Xiongnu.
At that time, the left wing of the Southern Xiongnu was in rebellion. Gui believed that the Chanyu could not subdue his subordinates and was submissive on the outside but rebellious on the inside, prompting him to commit suicide. He was ordered to be jailed for committing a crime and was exempted from execution.
After being promoted twice, he was worshiped as Jing Zhaoyin.
At this time, the powerful clans of the three auxiliaries invaded the people many times.
When Chen Gui took office, he exercised great authority and tried all those who had suffered grievances. The people in the county were very happy.
When the Qiang and Hu invaded the border, they killed the officials and drove away and plundered the people. Emperor Huan believed that Chen Gui had been familiar with border customs for generations and worshiped him as the general who conquered Liao.
When Chen Gui was leaving, he said to the emperor: "I have received the emperor's favor and galloped on the border. Although I displayed the role of hawks and dogs, I died in the court of the barbarians. My soul did not return to the Han Dynasty. I used foxes as sacrifices, but I could not repay the emperor even one tenth of his kindness."
I am an extremely stubborn servant and cannot be cut with a lead knife. I have received favors from the country and have received superior honors and ranks. I am afraid that I will never be able to repay my favor when I am alive or on the day of my death.
I heard that Sanchen was unruly, so I promoted a scholar to be the prime minister; the barbarians were disrespectful, so I selected soldiers to be generals.
I have no talents in civil and military affairs, but I have fulfilled my responsibilities as an eagle. I am ashamed of my sage, and I am afraid of vegetarian food. Even if I try my best and die, it will not be of any benefit.
Today, in the border areas of Xizhou, the land is barren. The people are accustomed to saddle horses and hunt as their occupation. The men do not know how to farm and the women do not know how to weave. They guard the fortress and wait, hanging on the edge of the sword. They hear urgent orders and drive for a long time. After leaving, they do not want to come back.
In recent years, the Huns have attacked the camp headquarters several times, killing officials and plundering the people.
Soldiers die in the desert, and residents hang their saddles on their heads.
In some places, corpses are buried all over the country, and all kinds of things are wiped out. Orphans and widows cry in empty cities. There is no green grass in the fields, and the houses are like hanging chimes.
Even if there is still life, it is like a dead tree.
In previous years, there was too much rain in Bingzhou, causing damage caused by plague borers. The crops were wasted and the rents and taxes were vacant.
The old are worried that they will not live to be old, and the young are afraid of being in trouble.
Your Majesty regards the common people as your sons, and the common people regard you as their father. How can you not work hard every day and appreciate the kindness of Xun?
Emperor Yao of the Tang Dynasty gave up his throne to Yu Shun, his son, because he wanted the people to meet a sage king instead of a tyrant.
Therefore, when the ancient father-in-law moved to Qishan, the number of people flocking to him increased five times compared with before. King Wen Xibo practiced benevolent government, and the people of the world joined him.
Do you want to use gold chariots and treasures to show kindness to the people?
Recently, Emperor Xiaowen was moved by the words of a woman named Tiying. He abolished the law of corporal punishment, practiced morality and benevolence, and became a wise king in the Han Dynasty.
Your Majesty inherited the tradition of Zhongxing, inherited the foundation of Emperor Guangwu, and took charge of government affairs without retaining the holy will.
Moreover, if the pastoral care is not good, or if he becomes a middle-ranking official, he is afraid of disobeying the will and takes over the present.
The sound of shouting brings disaster, and the barbarians are fierce and take advantage of the weakness.
However, the treasury fell into the mouths of jackals and the merits had no effect. This was all due to the disloyalty of the generals and the gathering of traitors.
When Zhu Liang, the former governor of Liangzhou, first arrived in the prefecture and county, he was punished many times and nearly half of the prefectural commanders were demoted. His administration was not outdated and his results were remarkable.
He should be rewarded to encourage meritorious people to be appointed as shepherds and guardians to scold the traitors and cripples.
It is also necessary to select more generals and lieutenants from the Huns and Wuhuan to protect the Qiang. They should be concise in civil and military affairs and give them laws. In addition to the two states of Liang and Liang, they should be rented this year. They should be pardoned and punished.
Then the good officials know how to serve the public, and the evil people know the harm of selfishness. Hu Ma can't peek at the Great Wall, and there is no danger of waiting behind the wall.
The emperor was awakened, so he selected the governors of Youzhou and Bingzhou, and appointed them as prefects and governors of their own counties and below. Many of them were dismissed. He issued an edict to General Chen to reduce the one-year rent of Bingzhou and Liangzhou in order to give it to the officials and the people.
After Chen Gui took office, the prefectures and counties were so scared that Xianbei did not dare to approach the frontiers, thus saving hundreds of millions of dollars in interest and expenses every year.
General Liang Ji had a long-standing quarrel with Chen Gui, and he told the monarch that Chen Gui had destroyed the country's prestige and gained fame alone, and was not feared by the barbarians.
Chen Gui was recalled and asked to retire and return to his hometown.
Later, he became a minister.
Liang Ji's tyranny increased day by day. Chen Gui explained his crimes and asked for his death.
The emperor is not aware.
Chen Gui knew that he would be killed by Liang Ji, so he went on a hunger strike for seven days and died.
The Hu barbarians in the Western Regions and the people in Bingzhou and Liangzhou all mourned for him and paid homage to his grave.
◆The biography of Qiao Xuan, the ancestor of Qiao Xuan, was a native of Suiyang, Liang State.
Qiao Ren, the seventh generation ancestor, learned from Dade in the same county and wrote forty-nine chapters of "Book of Rites", known as "Qiao Jun Xue".
When he became emperor, he became Dahonglu.
Grandfather Qiao Ji served as the prefect of Guangling.
My father was serious and had served as the governor of Donglai.
Qiao Xuan was a county meritorious official when he was young.
At that time, Zhou Jingxing, the governor of Yuzhou, went to Liang State. Qiao Xuan paid a visit to Zhou Jing, so he lay down on the ground and told Chen Xiang Yangchang's crimes, and asked to be the leader of Chen to conduct an in-depth investigation of his crimes.
Zhou Jing thought Qiao Xuan was very brave, so he wrote his name and dispatched him.
After Qiao Xuan arrived, he arrested all Yangchang's guests and interrogated Zang Zui in detail.
Yang Chang had always had a close friendship with General Liang Ji, and Liang Ji rushed to the rescue for him.
Zhou Jing summoned Xuan according to the order, but Qiao Xuan still didn't say anything, so the investigation became more urgent.
Yangchang rode in a carriage to answer the call, and Qiaoxuan became famous from then on.
Qiao Xuan was promoted to Xiaolian and supplemented Luoyang Zuowei.
At this time, Liang Buyi became the Yin of Henan Province, and Qiao Xuan went to the government for official duties. He did not want to suffer the humiliation, so he abandoned his official position and returned to his hometown.
Later, he was promoted to Qi Xiang four times, and was punished as Cheng Dan for committing crimes.
After his sentence was completed, he was conscripted, promoted to the governor of Shanggu, and then the governor of Hanyang.
At this time, Shang Guizhen ordered Huangfuzhen to be guilty of Zang. Qiao Xuan arrested him and punished him with whippings and other punishments. He died in the city of Ji County, which shocked the whole country.
Jiang Qi, a native of the county, lived in seclusion and guarded the road, and his reputation spread throughout Xizhou.
Qiao Xuan called him an official, but he refused to come out because he was ill.
Qiao Xuan was angry and ordered the governor Yin Yi to force him, saying: If Jiang Qi doesn't come, he will marry his mother.
Yin Yi insisted on trying not to get it, and quickly enlightened Jiang Qi.
Qi Jian couldn't get up.
The scholar-bureaucrats in the county also tried to dissuade him, and Qiao Xuan stopped his action.
People were quite ridiculed at that time.
Later, Xie was dismissed due to illness and was summoned to the post of Chief Situ in a public car. He was worshiped as a general and a great craftsman.
In the last years of Emperor Huan's reign, the Xianbei, Southern Xiongnu and Gaogouli's heir Bogu rebelled together and became bandits. The four prefectures held Qiao Xuan as the general who conquered the Liao Dynasty and faked Huang Yue.
When Qiao Xuan arrived at the town, he rested his troops to recuperate his troops, and then supervised the generals to attack the Hulu and Bo Gu. They were all defeated and retreated.
After three years in office, the border is quiet.
In the early years of Emperor Ling's reign, he was summoned to serve as the magistrate of Henan, transferred to the Shaofu, and made Dahonglu.
In the third year of Jianning, he was promoted to Sikong and transferred to Situ.
Qiao Xuan had always had a quarrel with Chen Qiu, the prefect of Nanyang. When he was in the position of Sangong, he recommended Chen Qiu to be the court captain.
Qiao Xuan believed that the country was weak and his own strength was useless, so he blamed himself for causing disasters by claiming that he was ill and neglected.
So let's do it.
After more than a year, he became the minister.
At that time, Gai Sheng, a senior official in Taizhong, had an old relationship with the emperor. He was the prefect of Nanyang and gained hundreds of millions in stolen goods.
Qiao Xuanzhuo asked Gai Sheng to be removed from his post and imprisoned, confiscating his financial bribes.
The emperor disagreed and promoted Gai Sheng to be a servant.
Qiao Xuan was dismissed from his post due to illness and became a doctor of Guanglu.
In the first year of Guanghe, he was promoted to Taiwei.
A few months later, he resigned from office due to illness, became a Taizhong doctor, and sought medical treatment.
Qiao Xuan's youngest son was ten years old and was traveling alone. Three men with sticks kidnapped him, took him to a house and climbed a building, and asked Qiao Xuan for his property, but Qiao Xuan refused to give it.
Soon, Sili Colonel Chen Qiu led Henan Yin and Luoyang orders to surround and guard Qiaoxuan's house.
Qiu and others were afraid of killing his son as well and did not want to force him.
Qiao Xuan stared and shouted: "Traitors have no law, how can I let go of a national traitor just because of the life of a son?"
Urging the troops to advance.

Cao Cao was often grateful that he was a confidant.
Later, I passed Qiao Xuan's tomb and paid homage sadly.

The country thinks clearly about the instructions, and the scholars think about the instructions.
The ghost is still there, but the beauty is far away.

Increased glory is all rewarded, which is equivalent to Confucius saying that he is not as good as Yan Yuan, and Li Shenghou sighed at Jia Fu.
A man dies for his close friend, and will never forget this.

Although it was a temporary joke, how could he say it if he was not a close relative?
I miss my old relationship and feel sad.
I was ordered to march eastward and stationed myself in the countryside, looking north to the precious land and my heart to the mausoleum.
Cut it to a thin layer and enjoy it publicly!

summary:
Li Xun was born in Linjing, Anding, and studied "Han Shi" from a young age, teaching hundreds of students. He was appointed as a meritorious official by Prefect Li Hong of Yingchuan but failed to take up the post initially. After Li Hong's death, Li Xun served three years of mourning at his grave. He later served in Situ Huanyu's mansion and was promoted to imperial censor, traveling to Youzhou and Beidi to declare the emperor's favor. He documented mountains, rivers, and villages in over a hundred volumes. Emperor Suzong appointed him governor of Yanzhou, where he lived frugally with sheepskin mats and quilts. He was later promoted to governor of Zhangye with a prestigious reputation.

When General Dou Xian stationed troops in Wuwei, Li Xun refused to participate in corrupt gift-giving practices and was dismissed. He was later recruited as a visitor and made captain of the Western Regions. Despite receiving many valuable gifts from foreign envoys and merchants, he refused all of them. When the Northern Xiongnu cut off routes to Cheshi and Yiwu, Li Xun offered rewards, resulting in the enemy commander's beheading. The roads became clear, and his kindness and power spread. He later became prefect of Wuwei but was dismissed and walked home, living in seclusion and weaving mats. When the Xiqiang rebelled, he was captured but released due to his reputation. During a famine, he refused grain from officials, moved to Xin'an Pass, and ate acorns. He died at age ninety-six.

Chen Chan, courtesy name Jishan, was from Anhan, Ba County. As a county meritorious officer, he punished evil and was feared by the people. After being recommended as filial and incorruptible, he served in the state government. When the governor was accused of bribery, Chen Chan was arrested for investigation but remained composed under torture, maintaining his confession. General Deng Zhi summoned him. When barbarians rebelled in Hanzhong, Chen Chan became governor, and they surrendered upon hearing his reputation. He was promoted to Zuo Fengyi and became an admonishing doctor.

In the first year of Yongning, the Shan Kingdom presented performers who could spit fire and perform illusions. In the second year of Yuanhui, Emperor An watched these performances. Chen Chan protested, citing Confucius's execution of dwarfs at the Qi-Lu meeting and arguing that barbarian skills were inappropriate for court. Shangshu Chen Zhonggai defended the performances as legitimate tribute and requested Chen Chan's impeachment. The emperor demoted Chen Chan to Xuantuhou Chengzhaowei. When the Northern Huns invaded Liaodong, Chen Chan became governor. The Hu people retreated in fear, and Chen Chan used moral influence to persuade the Chanyu, who sent treasures. After Deng Zhao's death, Chen Chan was dismissed as Deng's former official. He later served under Yan Xian and was promoted to Sili Xiaowei under Emperor Shun, dying in office the following year.

Pang Can, courtesy name Zhongda, was from Fengshi, Henan. He began as an obscure official until Henan Yin Pangfen promoted him to Xiaolian and Zuo Xiaoling. After breaking the law and being imprisoned, during the Yongchu period when the Zhongqiang people rebelled, Pang Can sent his son with a memorial advising against distant military campaigns and advocating for gathering troops to support the people. The imperial censor Fan Zhunshang recommended him, comparing him to Wei Shang. Empress Dowager Deng promoted him to visitor and sent him west to supervise military camps.

Four years later, when the Qiang rebelled again, Pang Can advised abandoning the Western Regions and moving border counties to Zhuling. Though Deng Zhao agreed, many opposed, so the plan stopped. As prefect of Hanyang, Pang Can understood the cryptic advice of recluse Ren Tang to be upright, attack powerful clans, and pity orphans. He governed by restraining the strong and helping the weak. Promoted to Qiang Protector captain, many Qiang surrendered. When ordered to lead troops against the Xianling Qiang, he was defeated and jailed for falsely claiming illness. Ma Rong petitioned for his release, citing historical precedents. Later pardoned, Pang Can became governor of Liaodong, then general of Liao Dynasty, and finally Da Honglu. Recommended by Yu Xu, he became Taiwei under Emperor Shun. Despite his reputation for loyalty, he was slandered and imprisoned. After being cleared, he was restored but later accused of killing his ex-wife's son. He was dismissed but later reinstated as Taiwei in the fourth year of Yangjia, dying at home in the first year of Yonghe.

Chen Gui, courtesy name Shuzhen, was from a border general family in Shangdang. He learned archery and horsemanship as a child, dominating Beizhou. During the Yongjian period, he became Xiaolian and later prefect of Wuyuan. In the fifth year of Yonghe, he became Zhonglang General envoy to the Xiongnu. When the Southern Xiongnu's left wing rebelled, Chen Gui blamed the Chanyu and was jailed but spared execution. As Jing Zhaoyin, he punished powerful clans and brought justice. When Qiang and Hu invaded, Emperor Huan appointed him general who conquered Liao. Chen Gui advised the emperor on border policies, recommending rewards for good officials and punishment for corrupt ones. The emperor selected new governors and reduced taxes. Chen Gui's administration so frightened Xianbei that they avoided the borders, saving millions annually. General Liang Ji, who had a long-standing quarrel with Chen Gui, accused him of destroying national prestige. Chen Gui was recalled and later became a minister. As Liang Ji's tyranny grew, Chen Gui accused him and requested his death. When the emperor ignored him, Chen Gui starved himself for seven days and died. People in the Western Regions, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou mourned him.

Qiao Xuan was from Suiyang, Liang State. His ancestor Qiao Ren wrote forty-nine chapters of the "Book of Rites." Qiao Xuan began as a county meritorious official. When Governor Zhou Jing visited Liang State, Qiao Xuan accused Chen Xiang Yangchang of crimes and investigated thoroughly despite Yangchang's friendship with General Liang Ji. Qiao Xuan became famous. After being promoted to Xiaolian and Luoyang Zuowei, he resigned when Liang Buyi became Henan Yin. He later became governor of Shanggu and Hanyang, punishing corrupt officials severely. When recluse Jiang Qi refused to serve, Qiao Xuan threatened to marry his mother, but relented after persuasion. During Emperor Huan's reign, when Xianbei, Southern Xiongnu, and Gaogouli rebelled, Qiao Xuan became general who conquered Liao. He rested his troops and defeated the rebels, bringing border peace for three years.

Under Emperor Ling, he became Henan magistrate, then Sikong and Situ. Despite quarreling with Chen Qiu, he recommended him as court captain. Qiao Xuan later became minister and accused official Gai Sheng of corruption, but the emperor protected Gai Sheng. Qiao Xuan resigned due to illness. When kidnappers took his ten-year-old son and demanded property, Qiao Xuan refused and ordered troops to attack, resulting in his son's death. He then requested an edict that hostage-takers be killed without ransom. This law ended hostage-taking among nobles. Qiao Xuan died at seventy-five. He was humble and thrifty, leaving little property. When Cao Cao was young and unknown, Qiao Xuan recognized his potential, saying Cao would stabilize the world. Cao Cao later visited Qiao Xuan's tomb and wrote a memorial poem honoring him.

Dugan has an upright and down-to-earth nature and is impatient.

Du Gen believed that Emperor An was old and should be in charge of political affairs, so he and his contemporaries wrote a letter to directly remonstrate.

The emperor said that Du Gen was dead, so he issued an edict to the world to recruit his descendants.
As soon as Du Gen returned to his hometown, he was recruited into the public car and appointed as an imperial censor.
First, Cheng Xushi, an official from Pingyuan County, admonished the Queen Mother to return to power and was convicted. At this time, he and Du Gen were recruited and elected as Shangshu Lang, and both of them were appointed.

Dugan said: "It is impossible not to leave traces among the people. If I are discovered accidentally, disaster will befall my relatives and friends, so I did not do this."
During the reign of Emperor Shun, he was promoted to the prefect of Jiyin.
He resigned from office and returned home. He died at the age of seventy-eight.

During the Yanguang period, Fan Feng, the imperial minister, and Wang Sheng, the emperor's wet nurse, jointly slandered the crown prince and deposed him as King Jiyin.
Cheng Yishi wrote letters of defense one after another, saying that Fan Feng and Wang Sheng framed the crown prince and deceived the emperor.
The emperor refused to listen to him, so Fan Feng and others framed him with a serious crime and sent him to prison to be executed. An edict only removed him from his official position and released him to his own county.
When King Jiyin was established, he became Emperor Shun. Sikong Zhang Haobi promoted him.
Zhang Hao recommended Cheng Yi as Yilang because he defended the crown prince's dethronement before his death.
Cheng Yishi himself thought that his contribution was not great, and he was embarrassed to accept the position, so he asked to go back.
The three public forces frequently conquered and conquered, but they should not respond.
The minister's servant She Yuyi thought highly of Cheng Yishi and wanted to recruit him to participate in the government affairs, so he wrote a letter to recommend him and conscripted him as Yilang.
Later, the minister ordered Zuo Xiong and Pushe Guo Qian to appoint him as minister again.
He was unsmiling and unsmiling in the court, and all the officials respected and loved him.
◆The biography of Luan Ba, named Shuyuan, was from Huang County, Wei County.
Good Taoism.

Because Guiyang County was located in the southern border area and was not familiar with the classics, it established marriage and funeral etiquette for officials, established schools, and rewarded progress.
Even if they are minor officials, they are all allowed to study and take exams, and they will be promoted or given officials according to their abilities.

Li Gu, the governor of Jingzhou, recommended Luan Ba's political achievements, recruited Yilang, acted as Dr. Guanglu, and inspected the prefecture and county with Du Qiao, Zhou Ju and other eight people.

The emperor was angry, issued an edict, and arrested Jiao Tingwei.
Luan Ba ​​committed suicide, and his son Luan He became the governor of Yunzhong.
◆The biography of Liu Tao, Liu Tao's courtesy name is Ziqi, his famous name is Wei, he was a native of Yingyin County, Yingchuan County, and the successor of Liu Bo, the Zhen King of Jibei Province.

clearly visible. I also heard that in times of crisis, it is not the benevolent who cannot help them, and in troubled times, it is not the wise that cannot save them. If I dare to say such inappropriate words in a government that refuses to remonstrate, I will be destroyed like frost meeting the sun.
First I felt sad for the world, but now the world should feel sad for my stupidity!

I am a wild man from Dong Ye who is secretly ignorant of the true meaning. I will ask you this question and my answer will be as above. He knew that he would be punished and be ridiculed by everyone in the world.

I once played on the stage. We must immediately stop the tax transfers in various counties, hoping for stability. The matter was handed over to the competent authorities and has been shelved to this day without anyone asking.
Now the common people in the three counties have fled, heading south to Wuguan and north to Hugu. They are all falling apart. I'm afraid they are still to come.

The enemy in the west gradually moved forward and was very close to our position. The Hu cavalry had already arrived at the cemeteries.
General Zhang Wen is strong and brave, but the leadership is pressing day and night, and the army has no backup. If it fails, it will be irreparable.
I know that I am annoying when I talk too much, but I still keep talking because when the country is peaceful, I will be happy. If the country is in chaos, I will die first.
Here are eight urgent matters today. Please adopt them immediately. The so-called eight things mainly mean that the country is in chaos, all due to eunuchs.

Now that there is peace in all directions, Liu Tao hates the lack of political clarity in the court and talks about Zhang Jiao as a monster. The prefectures and counties did not report it. How did Liu Tao know this?

He said to the envoy: What did the imperial court say when it made me the Marquis of Zhongling Township?

If one dies by holding one's breath, there will be no one in the world who is not grieved.
Liu Tao wrote hundreds of thousands of words, and also wrote "Qi Yao Lun", "Kuang Laozi", "Anti-Han Fei", "Reply to Mencius" and letters on current affairs, doctrines, poems, memorials, notes, and debates, totaling more than 100 articles.
At this time, Situ Donghai and Chen Dan also died together with Liu Tao without guilt. Chen Dan was praised for his loyalty and held the position of three ministers.
In the fifth year of Guanghe's reign, officials were ordered to report those who caused harm to the governor and Erqian Shi based on the folk songs.
At that time, Taiwei Xu Youyou and Sikong Zhangji looked at the eunuch's face and took bribes. Although the eunuch's children and guests were corrupt and despicable, they didn't dare to ask. Officials and people went to the capital to complain. Chen Dan and Yilang Cao Cao wrote to Cao Cao, saying: "The ministers are too protective of people related to them. The so-called report is to let the owl go and imprison Luan Feng."

◆Li Yunzhuan, Li Yunzi Xingzu, a native of Ganling County.
He is eager to learn and has good communication with yin and yang.

Dahonglu and Chen Fan came to Li Yun's rescue and said: Although Li Yun did not know what should be said and what should not be said, and even violated the emperor's will, his original intention was to be loyal to the emperor.

Killing Li Yun today, I am afraid that the incident that the predecessors ridiculed King Zhou of Pibi Ganxin will happen again today!

Taichang Yang Bing, Luoyang Mayor Mu Mao, and doctors all went to Shu to request Li Yun's rescue.

Later, Jia Cong, the governor of Jizhou, visited the county, went to Li Yun's tomb to worship, and carved a stone to commemorate him.
The historian commented: Li has five kinds of admonishment: ironic admonishment, obedient admonishment, quell admonishment, pointing admonishment, and trapping admonition, among which satirical admonishment ranks first.
Borrowing objects to express one's feelings and writing articles to state one's intentions, the most important thing is that the meaning is clear, the language is smooth, and the truth is pure.

◆The biography of Liu Yu, named Jiji, was from Guangling.

Yang Bing's talents for the country were not put to use, and unfortunately he died too early.
When I was in the countryside, I heard some songs about proud ministers who brutally harmed the people. There were sighs and sighs everywhere. The most bitter and unpleasant smell made people cry.
I am happy to be recommended. When answering the emperor's questions, I should express my feelings with complete loyalty and not dare to deceive others.
I sincerely ask Your Majesty to take a moment to look at the facts of the past and today. Why do people lament and sigh, and why does heaven change?
Most of the positions of the princes are in the twenty-eight constellations of the Dharma, guarding the four directions for the emperor, and the celestial phenomena shine. This is a major event related to the rise and fall of the country.
Nowadays, the eunuchs are so evil that they are tearing apart the soil and making marquises. They are also vying to create offspring and inherit the title. Some beg sons from estranged relatives, and some buy sons on the street. This goes against the founding principles of inheriting the family.

Nowadays, beauties and seduces fill the harem, and they are provided with treasures and ornaments. They eat without working. The palace is empty, the energy is exhausted, and all kinds of diseases occur.

The characteristics of heaven and earth are that the yin and yang are in the correct period. If the yin and yang are not separated, floods or droughts will occur. "The Book of Songs" says: Five days are the limit, six days are not enough.

What's more, these palace maids have been hiding in the deep palaces since they were young. You can imagine their resentment.
In addition, eunuchs such as Chang Shi and Huang Men also took many wives and concubines, and their malicious spirit created monsters and sins.
Pedestrians on the road said that officials robbed other people's girls and then married them and then abandoned them. Everyone was frightened by this.
Who doesn't know? Such rumors would never happen without reason.
Zou Yan was no more than an ordinary man, and Qi was no more than an ordinary woman. Nowadays, the princes have more and more mansions, which are very ingenious. They dig mountains and dig stones. They do not care whether they are busy in farming or not. They are forced to use harsh criminal laws and threaten them with the laws of the country.
The people are originally innocent, but they can be charged at will; the people originally have land, and they can rob it at will.

The common people could not express their sorrows and grievances, so they rose up to join the bandits, and the government therefore used arms to attack them.
Poor people even sold their heads to get rewards, fathers and brothers mutilated each other's bodies, and husbands and wives separated each other.
Isn't it sad to be in such poverty and persecution?
Also, the emperor is as noble as Beichen and the lord of the country, but he casually walks into the homes of some people and enters the eunuch's room. The guests therefore buy things in the city, the streets are noisy, and rape and indulgence are reached to the extreme.
Now that the three princes are in office, they are all knowledgeable and highly virtuous people. However, they are only upright themselves and cannot be of much help to the emperor. It is not that they lack knowledge and ability, but they are afraid of the death penalty.
I think the emperor appointed seven ministers, including three ministers, Qianyi, Houcheng, Zuofu and Youbi.
The purpose is to open up the path of remonstrance and open up the books of the Jin and Teng historians in the Eastern Preface, follow the civil and military methods of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and make the world prosperous and peaceful, depose those bad guys who flatter and do evil, and abandon the voices of Zheng, Wei and Mimi. In this way, the natural government will be peaceful, and the people will be universally enlightened.
I sincerely express my feelings, but there is nothing worthy of the emperor's choice in what I say. I am afraid that I will offend the emperor and be very frightened. After the emperor's death, the general Dou Wu wanted to kill the eunuchs. He appointed Liu Yu as his minister and Yin Xun as his minister, and they planned together.
When Dou Wu failed, Liu Yu and Yin Xun were both killed, which is recorded in "The Biography of Dou Wu".
Yin Xun, courtesy name Boyuan, was from Henan.
His great-uncle Yin Mu once served as Taiwei, and Yin Mu's grandson Yin Song once served as Situ.
Yin Xun is a man of uprightness and perseverance.
When I was studying in my youth, every time I read about loyal ministers and righteous men, I would often discard the book and look up to the sky and sigh.
I think that my conduct is not in line with the times and I am not subject to the etiquette of the state, county and government.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, he was drafted for his moral character and moved to the ministerial order.
In the middle of Yanxi period, the general Liang Ji was killed. The emperor summoned Yin Xun to deploy various positions. He was very talented and was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang Township.
Pu Shehuo, Shangshu Zhang Jing, Ouyang Shen, Li Wei, Yu Fang, and Zhou Yong were all granted the title of Tinghou.

In the eighth year, Zhongchang's servants such as Ju Yuan and Zuo Xuan were dismissed from office because of their convictions, and their fiefdoms were removed. Because of this, Yin Xun was deposed from his title.
After Liu Yu was killed, the eunuchs burned all his letters, thinking they were wrong remarks.
Liu Yu's son Liu Wan passed on Liu Yu's studies and knew about divination and could point out the causes of disasters.
It is said that it is square and it should not be done.
◆Xie Bi Chuan, courtesy name Fuxuan, was a native of Wuyang County, Dongjun.
Zhongzheng is upright and upright, and he is admired and respected by his hometown clan.
In the second year of Jianning, an imperial edict was issued to recruit virtuous men. Xie Bi, Chen Dun of Donghai, and Gongsun Du of Xuantu all passed the examination and were awarded the title of doctor.
At this time, a green snake appeared in the front hall, and the strong wind blew down the trees. He ordered the officials below to report their mistakes in political affairs.
Xie Bi sent a secret report and said: I heard that harmony comes from virtue, and evil comes from political failure.
God has issued a warning, and the emperor must think about his faults; if there are shortcomings in politics and religion, traitors should be punished. Snakes are born from Yin energy and are similar to dragons. Dragons have scales and are the symbols of armored soldiers.
"Hong Fan Zhuan" says: When Jue is extremely weak, he will suffer from the sins of snakes and dragons.

I also heard that a snake is a symbol of auspiciousness for a woman.

Recruiting the former Sikong Wang Chang and Changle Shaofu Li Ying to jointly manage political affairs. In this way, the disasters of the common people can be eliminated and the country can be peaceful.
I am a commoner in the mountains and I don’t know the country’s laws. The emperor told me not to hide anything, that is to say, I don’t have any worries. How dare you not speak freely and forget your taboos?
