summary:
**Du Gen** (courtesy name Bojian) was from Dingling County, Yingchuan. His father Du An was known for his integrity, entering Imperial College at thirteen and gaining fame as "Qitong." Du Gen was elected Xiaolian in Yongchu's first year and appointed as a doctor. When Empress Dowager Deng controlled the government, Du Gen believed Emperor An was old enough to rule and wrote a direct remonstrance. The Queen Mother had him beaten nearly to death in the palace. He feigned death for three days until maggots appeared in his eyes, then escaped and worked as a busboy in Yicheng for fifteen years. After Deng's execution, he was recruited as an imperial censor. During Emperor Shun's reign, he became prefect of Jiyin, resigned, and died at seventy-eight.

**Cheng Yishi** (courtesy name Jiming) was studious and familiar with Taoism. During Yanguang period, when Fan Feng and Wang Sheng slandered the crown prince, Cheng wrote defenses but was framed and imprisoned. When the prince became Emperor Shun, Sikong Zhang Hao recommended Cheng as Yilang, but Cheng declined, feeling his contribution was insufficient. He was later conscripted again as Yilang. He was unsmiling in court, and all officials respected him.

**Luan Ba** (courtesy name Shuyuan) was from Huang County, Wei County, and practiced Taoism. During Emperor Shun's reign, he served as a eunuch in Yeting against his wishes. He had a simple, upright temperament and studied Confucian classics. After his yang energy returned, he requested to quit the eunuchship, became a doctor, then governor of Guiyang. He established marriage and funeral rites, built schools, and promoted officials based on ability. After seven years, he resigned due to illness. He later became governor of Yuzhang, where he used Taoist skills to destroy demonic sacrifices and eliminate monsters. When Emperor Shun died, Luan Ba remonstrated against destroying small tombs near the imperial mausoleum. Empress Dowager Liang interrogated him, convicted him, and sent him home. Over twenty years later, Emperor Ling ascended, and Luan Ba was recruited as Yilang. When Chen Fan and Dou Wu were killed, Luan Ba was relegated to Yongchang Prefect. He wrote an extreme remonstrance about their unjust case, and the emperor ordered his arrest. Luan Ba committed suicide.

**Liu Tao** (courtesy name Ziqi) was from Yingyin County, Yingchuan, descendant of Liu Bo, King of Jibei. He was simple and made friends only with like-minded people. When General Liang Ji held power and disasters struck, Liu Tao studied at Taixue and submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor for allowing villains to torture the people, causing heaven to send disasters. He recommended Zhu Mu and Li Ying as capable officials. The emperor did not accept his advice. When officials proposed recoining money, Liu Tao argued that food was more urgent than currency, stating that people could live without money but not without food. The emperor stopped minting money. Liu Tao later became chief of Shunyang, where he recruited former criminals to help catch traitors. He was dismissed due to illness, and the people made a song missing him. He annotated the Shangshu and Chunqiu. When Zhang Jiao rebelled, Liu Tao warned the emperor but was ignored. After Zhang Jiao's rebellion caused chaos, the emperor made Liu Tao Marquis of Zhongling Township and promoted him to Shangshu Ling. Because of his remonstrances, powerful ministers feared him and transferred him to Jing Zhaoyin. He refused to buy his position with money and resigned due to illness. The emperor valued his talents and conscripted him as an admonition official. Liu Tao submitted eight urgent matters blaming eunuchs for the country's chaos. The eunuchs framed him, and he was tortured in prison. He wrote hundreds of thousands of words, including "Qi Yao Lun," "Kuang Laozi," "Anti-Han Fei," and "Reply to Mencius." He died in prison.

**Li Yun** (courtesy name Xingzu) was from Ganling County. He was learned in yin-yang and became magistrate of Baima County. In Emperor Huan's second year of Yanxi, after Liang Ji was executed, Shan Chao and others were made marquises, and a popular woman became queen. Disasters struck, and Li Yun submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor's rewards and the disorder of official positions. The emperor became furious and ordered Li Yun's arrest. Du Zhong and Chen Fan pleaded for him, but Li Yun died in prison.

**Liu Yu** (courtesy name Jiji) was from Guangling, descendant of King Jing of Guangling. He was skilled in astronomy and mathematics. In Yanxi's eighth year, Taiwei Yang Bing recommended him as virtuous and upright. He submitted a memorial criticizing eunuchs for creating offspring to inherit titles, the harem's excess, and the people's suffering. He advised the emperor to open the path of remonstrance. When General Dou Wu failed to kill the eunuchs, Liu Yu was killed.

**Xie Bi** (courtesy name Fuxuan) was from Wuyang County, Dongjun. In Jianning's second year, he was recruited as a doctor. When a green snake appeared and strong winds blew, Xie Bi submitted a secret report blaming the emperor's weakness, the Queen Mother's imprisonment, and the execution of Chen Fan. He recommended recruiting Wang Chang and Li Ying. The emperor's attendants sent him to be prime minister of Guangling. He later resigned. Cao Shao, nephew of eunuch Cao Jie, hated Xie Bi and had him tortured to death in prison. In Chuping's second year, Zhao Qian avenged Xie Bi by arresting and killing Cao Shao.

**Yang Zhong** (courtesy name Zishan), from Chengdu, Shu County, became a county official at thirteen. The prefect, impressed by his talent, sent him to study the *Spring and Autumn Annals* in the capital. During Emperor Xianzong's reign, he served at Lantai as school secretary. In the first year of Jianchu, during a severe drought and high grain prices, Yang Zhong submitted a memorial arguing that excessive imprisonment and military settlements in remote areas caused widespread suffering. He cited historical precedents, including the Qin dynasty's harsh policies and Emperor Gaozu's reforms, urging the emperor to show mercy. When officials debated his proposals, Yang Zhong defended his position by referencing historical examples of wise rulers who changed harmful policies. The emperor eventually accepted his advice, recalling exiles and ending border settlements. Yang Zhong also advocated for scholarly examinations following the Shiqu Pavilion model, leading to the Baihu Temple conference. Despite imprisonment, he was pardoned and participated. He later edited the *Tai Shi Gong Shu* and wrote on the *Spring and Autumn Annals*. He died in the twelfth year of Yongyuan.

**Li Fa** (courtesy name Bodu), from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, was well-read and upright. In the ninth year of Emperor Yongyuan's reign, he became a doctor and later Shizhong and Guanglu doctor. He criticized harsh government policies, excessive eunuch power, and favoritism toward concubines, which led to his removal from office. He returned home and lived in seclusion for eight years, refusing to discuss politics with friends. He later served as Yilang and admonished officials, maintaining his principles. As governor of Runan, he achieved political success before returning home and dying.

**Zhai Youfu** (courtesy name Zichao), from Luo, Guanghan, was skilled in the *Book of Songs*, *Laozi*, astronomy, and calendar calculation. After avenging his uncle, he fled to Chang'an, worked as a fortune teller, and later shepherded sheep in Liangzhou. He eventually became a court official. When a vacancy arose, he manipulated the examination process out of fear of competition. He submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor for granting excessive power to relatives and eunuchs, warning of historical disasters from such practices. He advocated for frugality and wise counsel. His memorial was ignored, and he became feared by the emperor's favorites. As prefect of Jiuquan, he defeated Qiang rebels, beheading 900. He later served as Jing Zhaoyin and Guanglu doctor. He was falsely accused, imprisoned, and eventually cleared. He wrote twelve chapters on classical texts and advocated for restoring the Imperial Academy, which the emperor approved.

**Ying Feng** (courtesy name Shishu), from Nandun, Runan, was exceptionally intelligent, memorizing everything he read. As governor, he visited forty-two counties and accurately recalled prisoner details. He wrote the *Preface to the Book of Han*. During a Wuling Man rebellion, he was appointed prefect and successfully pacified them through diplomacy. He later served as Sili Xiaowei, known for his severity. When Emperor Huan wanted to make Tian Guiren queen, Ying Feng advised against it, citing historical disasters from such choices. The emperor accepted his advice. He later resigned due to illness and wrote thirty chapters commemorating Qu Yuan.

**Ying Shao** (courtesy name Zhongyuan), studious and well-read, served as a messenger under Emperor Ling. During border conflicts, he argued against recruiting Xianbei soldiers, citing their unreliability and past betrayals. His view prevailed. As prefect of Taishan, he defeated 300,000 Yellow Turban rebels. After failing to protect Cao Song, he fled to Yuan Shao. He wrote extensively on legal matters, compiling works like *Han Yi* and *Customs of Customs*. He refuted legal precedents, arguing that punishment should follow established principles. His writings totaled 136 works, and he interpreted the *Book of Han*. He died in Ye.

**Huo Chen** (courtesy name Shuzhi), from Ye, Wei County, was a young scholar. When his uncle Song Guang was falsely accused and imprisoned, fifteen-year-old Huo Chen wrote to General Liang Shang, arguing for leniency based on the *Spring and Autumn Annals* principle of judging intent. Liang Shang pardoned Song Guang, and Huo Chen became famous. He served as prefect of Jincheng, respected by the Qiang and Hu. After his mother's death, he resigned for mourning. He later served as prime minister of Beihai and minister, courageously opposing Liang Ji's power. After Liang Ji's death, Emperor Huan honored him. He died in office.

**Yuan Yan** (courtesy name Jiping), from Chenliu, was poor but studious. He served as a village official, known for benevolent governance. When Emperor Huan asked what kind of ruler he was, Yuan Yan replied he was a "Lord of Hanzhong," explaining that while Chen Fan handled affairs well, eunuchs interfered. The emperor appointed him to various positions. Yuan Yan warned against favoring unworthy associates, citing historical disasters from such practices. He urged the emperor to distance himself from flatterers and eunuchs. He later retired due to illness and died.

**Xu Chu** (courtesy name Mengyu), from Guangling, was learned and served as governor of Jingzhou. He prosecuted corrupt officials, including Zhang Zhong, despite pressure from the Empress Dowager. He defeated Yellow Turban rebels but was falsely accused by eunuchs and dismissed. He later served as prime minister of Donghai. When Emperor Xian moved the capital, Xu Chu was kidnapped by Yuan Shu but refused to serve him. After Yuan Shu's defeat, Xu Chu recovered the imperial seal and returned it. He served as Taichang and died in office.

Later, a crested sparrow took three fishes and flew in front of the lecture hall. The lecturer held the fish and said: Snakes are the symbol of Doctor Qing's clothes.
Three means three stations, and Mr. will be promoted from now on.
He became a state and county official only when he was fifty years old.
General Deng Zhi heard that Yang Zhen was a talented person and promoted him to Maocai. He was promoted four times to the governor of Jingzhou and the governor of Donglai.

Yang Zhen said: Old friends know you, why don’t you know old friends?

Wang Mi left in shame.
Later he became the prefect of Zhuo County.
Be fair and honest, and do not accept personal requests.
His descendants lived a vegetarian diet and lived a simple life. Some of his old friends or elders wanted him to buy property for his descendants. Most of the previous doctorate elections were not worthy of their name. Yang Zhen recommended Chen Liu, Yang Lun and other famous scholars who were proficient in Confucian classics to teach their studies, which was praised by Confucian scholars.
In the first year of Yongning, he replaced Liu Kai as Situ.

Emperor An's nanny, Wang Sheng, was responsible for raising Emperor An. She relied on the emperor's favor and was lawless. Wang Sheng's daughter Bo Rong went in and out of the palace, taking bribes and perverting the law.
Yang Zhen went to Shu.
Said: I heard that politics relies on talents, and those pests must be removed to govern the country.

Wang Sheng came from a humble background and met with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to raise Sheng Gong. Although she had some merit, the reward she received far exceeded her hard work. And she was greedy to no end. Asking for help outside, disturbing the world, harming the court, and bringing discredit on the emperor's face.
The Book of Books warns hens against rooster crows, and the Book of Songs satirizes women in mourning for their country.
In the past, Zheng Yangong followed his mother's selfish desires, indulged his proud younger brother, and did whatever he wanted, almost destroying the country, and then came back to govern. "Spring and Autumn" once criticized him and thought that education was not good.
Those women and villains will be happy if you are close to her; if you stay away from her, they will resent you. It's very difficult to deal with.
"Yi" said: Don't indulge, just do it in the kitchen.
This means that women are not allowed to interfere in politics!
Wang Sheng should be allowed to leave the palace as soon as possible, let her live outside, cut off relations with Bo Rong, and not allow them to interact with each other, so that they can be kind and virtuous, both above and below.
I hope that the emperor will get rid of his personal love, eradicate his intolerance, pay attention to national affairs, carefully select his ministers, and reduce expenses and taxes.
As a result, there are outstanding talents from all over the world, and the officials of the imperial court have no regrets about being an official in troubled times. The poems in "Dadong" that satirize the troubled times cannot be used today, and the people have no complaints about "not being well-off yet."
Isn’t it good to imitate the past and share the virtues of the sages of all ages?
Emperor An showed it to his mother, Wang Sheng and others, and they all held grudges.
But Bo Rong's arrogance and promiscuity became even more serious. He hooked up with Liu Gui, the brother of Liu Hu, the former Marquis of Chaoyang. Liu Gui actually married her and took Liu Hu's title, rising to the rank of servant.
Yang Zhen was so filled with hatred that he went to Shangshu again and said: I heard that Emperor Gaozu made an appointment with his officials. It was not that meritorious officials could not be granted titles. The system of governing the country stipulates that after the father dies, the son succeeds, and after the brother dies, the younger brother succeeds, so usurpation is prevented.
Today, there is an edict to ennoble the former Chaoyang Marquis Liu Hu, and then his brother Liu Gui takes the title of Marquis of Liu Hu. Liu Hu's younger brother Liu Wei is still there.
I've heard that the emperor only confers meritorious titles, and the princes only ennoble them with virtue.
Now Liu Gui has no other merits. Just because he was married to his mother's daughter, he suddenly became both a servant and a prince. This was inconsistent with the old system and the scriptures. Passers-by were noisy and the people were uneasy.
The emperor should learn from the past and abide by the ways of being an emperor.
The emperor ignored him.
In the second year of Yanguang's reign, he replaced Liu Kai as Taiwei.
The emperor's uncle Dahong Geng Bao recommended the elder brother of Li Gui, who often served as a servant, to Yang Zhen, but Yang Zhen refused.
Geng Bao went to ask Yang Zhen and said: "Li Changshi is the most important person in the country. The emperor wants you to recommend his brother. I, Geng Bao, am just conveying the emperor's opinion."
Yang Zhen said: If the imperial court wants to have the three prefectures recommend candidates, there should be an order from the minister.
Rejecting him, Geng Bao left in anger.
The queen's brother Zhi Jinwu Yan Xian also recommended to Yang Zhen that he befriend his relatives, but Yang Zhen refused.
Sikong Liu heard the news and immediately recommended these two people, and both were promoted within ten days.
Therefore, Yang Zhen suffered even more resentment.
At that time, an edict was sent to build a house for Queen Mother. Fan Feng, the chief minister, and Zhou Guang, Xie Yun, etc., encouraged them to disturb the court.
Yang Zhen went to Shu again.
Said: I heard that in ancient times, after nine years of farming, there must be three years of savings. Therefore, floods caused disasters in Yao's time, and the people did not suffer from hunger.
Now the disaster is serious and the people are empty and unable to provide for themselves.
In addition, the locusts are causing damage, the Qiang bandits are looting, and the border areas are uneasy. The fighting has not continued until now, and the soldiers have no food and grass. The treasury of Da Sinong is empty, which is not a time for national peace.
The edict was written to build a house inside Jincheng Gate for my mother, which was combined into one, connected to the street, and decorated with carvings, which was extremely gorgeous.
It is now summer, when the soil is prosperous, and they go up to the mountains to quarry stone. The master craftsmen from Zuo School and other departments are working on dozens of places, urging each other, and spending more than hundreds of millions!
Brothers Zhou Guang and Xie Yun, who had no flesh-and-blood ties to the country, relied on a group of treacherous men to share authority and power with Fan Feng, Wang Yong and others, liaise with the prefectures and counties, and evade the ministers.
The recruitment of the prime minister was carried out in accordance with the orders from above. Corrupt people from all over the country were recruited and bribes were accepted from them. Even those who had not used the bribes were reused.
Confusing black and white, not distinguishing between pure and dirty, the whole world was in an uproar, and they all said: The wealth is in the upper reaches, which is a source of ridicule for the court.

Resentful people should not be used again. So it is said: If the people are not enough, who will be enough for you?
I hope the emperor will consider it.

Yang Zhen went to the countryside again due to the earthquake.

I heard the teacher say: The earth belongs to the yin essence, so it should be quiet and support the yang.
The reason why I am shaking now is that my vagina is too full.
On that day, the Wu Gan Chen branch combined with the earth movement, and all three were earth. They were located in the middle palace. This is a symbol of the central minister's near-official power.
I think the emperor worked very hard because of the unrest on the border. The palace building was tilted, and only one pillar was used to support it. When civil engineering is not prosperous, I want to make people far and near know that the government is clean and honest, and the capital is solemn and majestic, regardless of the high towers and pavilions.
However, some flatterers could not agree with the emperor. They were arrogant and extravagant and exceeded the law, wasted labor, overhauled houses, and acted arrogantly.
There was a lot of talk on the road, everyone heard and saw it.
The mutation of the earthquake occurred near the capital, probably because of this.
There was no snow in the winter, and no rain during the Spring Festival. All officials were anxious, and construction continued, which was really a harbinger of drought.
"Shangshu" says: If you arrogate the sun, the minister has no authority and becomes the Duke of Fuyu.
That is to say: only the king can enjoy special blessings and delicacies. Your Majesty, please carry forward a strong and upright spirit, abandon those arrogant and extravagant people, ignore the source of the evil talk, adhere to the warning of the Emperor, and do not let your majesty and power be left behind for a long time.
Yang Zhen came forward and spoke passionately, and the emperor was already displeased with him, while Fan Feng and others looked sideways and resented him, but because he was a Confucian, they did not dare to harm him.
Soon, a man from Hejian went to the court to write a letter, describing the gains and losses of the government.
The emperor was angry and ordered his arrest and imprisonment, which was deemed as bullying and immorality.
Yang Zhen went to Shu to rescue him again and said: I heard that during the time of Yao and Shun, he was admonishing drums and slandering trees and standing in the court; the masters of sages of Shang and Zhou dynasties complained about villains, but they also checked themselves and encouraged themselves.
This is to open up channels of speech, brainstorm ideas, and make people feel better.

Yang Zhen sent Gao Shu to summon the master craftsman Shi Shi to investigate the matter. After obtaining the false edict from Zhao Feng and others, he wrote a memorial and wanted to wait for the emperor to return before delivering it.
When Fan Feng and others heard about it, they were terrified. It happened that Taishi said that Xingbian was rebellious, so he framed Yang Zhen together and said: Since Zhao Teng's death, Yang Zhen has been deeply resentful. And he held a grudge against Deng Zhi's old subordinates.
When the emperor returned, he waited in Taixue for an auspicious day to enter the palace. In the evening, he sent an envoy with an order to collect Taiwei Yang Zhen's seal and ribbon. Yang Zhen then closed the door to exclude guests.
Fan Feng and others still hated him, so they asked General Geng Bao to report that Minister Yang Zhen refused to plead guilty and was resentful, and ordered him to be sent back to his hometown.
Yang Zhen walked to Jiyang Pavilion in the west of the city and said generously to his son and student: Death is inevitable for a person.
I am favored and occupy the position, but I hate the traitorous ministers who are cunning but cannot be punished, and the evil mistresses who are causing chaos but cannot be restrained. How can I show my face to the world?
On the day of death, a coffin of mixed wood is used, and the body is only covered with a sheet. There is no burial place or a shrine.
So he took poison and died at the age of seventy.
In response to the orders of Fan Feng and others, the prefect of Hongnong moved to Liang and sent officials to stay at Yang Zhen's funeral in Shaanxi County. They exposed the coffin beside the road and ordered Yang Zhen's disciples to post and write letters on their behalf. Everyone on the road shed tears for it.
When Emperor Shun was over, Fan Feng, Zhou Guang and others were put to death. Yang Zhen was a student of Yu Fang, and Chen Yi went to the court to complain about Yang Zhen.
The imperial court called him Yang Zhenzhong. He issued an edict to confer the title of Lang to his two sons, gave him a million yuan in money, and buried Yang Zhen in Tongting, Huayin with proper ceremony.
Ten days before the burial, a large bird with a height of more than ten feet flew to Yang Zhen's funeral. It leaned down and screamed in mourning, weeping on the wet ground. After the burial, it flew away.
The county reported the situation.
At that time, disasters occurred one after another. The emperor felt that Yang Zhen was an unjust case, and issued an edict saying: The late Taiwei Yang Zhen was an upright person, so he assisted in current affairs.
My stupidity aggravated this sin. The mountains collapsed and the pillars were broken. How dangerous I was!
Now let the prefect and prime minister use the palace to have a shrine with soul and spirit, or come and enjoy these sacrifices of mine.
So people erected a stone bird statue in front of Yang Zhen's tomb to commemorate him.
Yang Zhen was framed, Gao Shu was also convicted, and he was accused of reducing his death.
When Yang Zhen was vindicated, Gao Shu paid homage to the censor and went to Jingzhou to judge the history.
Yang Zhen has five sons.
The eldest son Yang Mu was appointed Prime Minister of Fubo.

After Emperor Shun ascended, Fan Feng was executed. Yang Zhen's students petitioned, and the emperor posthumously honored him, granting titles and money, and buried him with ceremony. A large bird mourned at his funeral, and a stone bird was erected in his memory. His son Yang Mu became Prime Minister of Fubo.

◆Huan Rong's biography, Huan Rong's courtesy name is Chunqing, and he was a native of Longkang, Pei County.
When he was young, he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" in Chang'an, with Jiujiang Zhu Pu as his teacher. His family was poor and he often relied on servants to support himself. He was energetic and tireless. He did not go home to visit for fifteen years and did not return until Wang Mang usurped the throne.
When his teacher Zhu Pu passed away, Huan Rong went to Jiujiang to attend the funeral. He carried the soil to build his teacher's grave, so he stayed to teach and had hundreds of disciples.
Wang Mang failed and the world was in chaos. Huan Rong took the scriptures and fled into the valley with his students. Although he was often hungry, he continued to lecture on scriptures and treatises. Later, he taught in the Jianghuai area.
In the 19th year of Jianwu's reign, when Huan Rong was over sixty years old, he was awarded the post of Grand Situ.
At that time, Xianzong had just been established as the crown prince, and he chose to seek Ming scriptures. He promoted Huan Rong's student Yuzhang Hetang to be the general of Huben Zhonglang, and taught the prince in the Book of Documents.
Shizu calmly asked He Tang who his master was, and He Tang replied: Huan Rong of Pei State.
The emperor immediately summoned Huan Rong and ordered him to explain "Shang Shu". He thought it was very good.
He worshiped Huan Rong as Yilang, gave him one hundred thousand yuan, and allowed him to enter the palace and teach the prince.
At every court meeting, Huan Rong was often asked to explain the scriptures in front of the ministers.
The emperor praised: It's too late to get Mr.
It happened that Dr. Ouyang was vacant, and the emperor wanted to use Rong.
Rong kowtowed and said in resignation: "I am not as good at Confucian classics as my fellow disciples Peng Hong and Yangzhou engaged in Gaohong."
The emperor said: OK, go ahead, you can do the job.
So he worshiped Huan Rong as a doctor, and recommended Peng Hong and Gao Hong as doctors.
The emperor drove to the university, and just as the doctors were discussing issues, Huan Rong was dressed in Confucian clothes. He was gentle and respectful, broad and erudite. He argued clearly about the classics and the meaning of the scriptures. He always showed courtesy and submission, and did not use words to win over others. None of the Confucian scholars could compare with him, so the emperor specially rewarded him.
The emperor also ordered all the students to play the chime, which lasted all day.
Later, when Huan Rong entered the court, the emperor gave him a strange fruit. The recipients all took it into their arms. Huan Rong raised his hand and held the fruit in his hands to thank him.
The emperor smiled and pointed at him and said, "This man is really a Confucian scholar!"
From then on, he became more respected and was often asked to stay in the palace of the Crown Prince.
Five years later, Huan Rong recommended his disciple Hu Xian from Jiujiang to serve as a lecturer. He just listened and went to the palace once every morning.
Huan Rong was once ill. The prince sent his master to inquire about his illness in the morning and evening. He gave him delicacies, curtains, slaves, etc., and said: "If there is any problem, don't worry about the family."
Later, he recovered from his illness and went to the palace to give lectures.
In the twenty-eighth year, there was a meeting of hundreds of officials in the DPRK, and the emperor asked who could be the prince's master? The ministers observed the idea and all said that the prince's uncle could hold Jinwu's original deerhou Yinshi.
Doctor Zhang Yi said seriously: "Your Majesty, when you appoint a prince, is it for the Yin clan or for the world?"
If it is the Yin family, then Yinhou can do it; if it is the world, then the talents of the world can be used.
The emperor thought it was a good statement and said: I want to set up the Taifu to assist the prince.
Now the doctor can't help me, let alone the prince?
So he worshiped Zhang Yi as the crown prince and tutor, and Huan Rong as the young tutor, and gave him carriages and horses.
Huanrong gathered all the students, displayed the chariots and horses, seals and ribbons and said: "Today I am given a gift from the emperor. This is the power of archaeological records. Can't you encourage me?"
Huan Rong thought that the prince's study of the Confucian classics had been completed, so he thanked him and said: "I am fortunate enough to have been able to lecture on the Confucian classics for several years. However, my knowledge is shallow and short-lived, and it cannot be of great benefit."
Now the crown prince relies on his intelligence and aptitude for understanding the classics and understanding ancient and modern times. No other prince can be as knowledgeable as this.
This is really a blessing to the country and a blessing to the world.
I have finished my duties as a minister, and the rest are all in the hands of the prince. I would like to ask Chen Chen to pay his respects and go home again.
The prince resumed his belief in Taoism: Zhuang Yi was a boy who had studied Taoism for nine years and knew nothing.
The "Five Classics" is so vast and the sacred words and teachings are so profound. How can one who is not the smartest person in the world master it?
What's more, if you are not as talented as me, you dare to teach and teach.
In the past, there were many teachers who thanked their disciples. At first, they understood the purpose of the scriptures and understood the chapters and sentences. At the bottom, they went to their homes and villages to thank their masters.
Now that I am experiencing the following, I dare not say anything. I hope you will recover and eat well, and take good care of your body.
In the 30th year, Huan Rong was worshiped as Taichang.
Huan Rong began to suffer, and he and his tribemate Huan Yuanqing were starving, but Huan Rong continued to recite scriptures.
Yuan Qing sneered and said: "It's just self-destruction. When will I use it again?"
Huan Rong smiled and refused.
After doing Taichang, Yuan Qing sighed: I am from a peasant family. I never thought that knowledge could be so useful.
When Xianzong came to the throne, he respected Huanrong as his master of etiquette. He was very close and respected, and he worshiped Huanrong's second son as his husband.
Huan Rong was over eighty years old and thought he was getting old. He wrote several times to request for retirement, and each time he received additional rewards.
The emperor once drove to Taichang Mansion, asked Huan Rong to sit on the east side, set up a few staffs, and gathered hundreds of officials, including Hussar General Dongping, Wang Cang, and Huan Rong's students, and hundreds of Huan Rong's students. The emperor personally practiced medicine and said every time he opened his mouth: "Master is here."
After the ceremony, all the official gifts were given to the Taichang family.
Such is its gift.
In the second year of Yongping, it was built at the beginning of Sanyong, and Huanrong was worshiped as a supporter of Wu Geng.
Every time after the Dashe old-age ceremony was held, the emperor would lead Huan Rong and his disciples to the hall, hold the scriptures and speak in a few words.
So Huanrong was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a settlement of five thousand households.
Every time Huan Rong fell ill, the emperor sent envoys to express condolences, and there was an endless stream of officials and doctors.
Later, when he became seriously ill, Huan Rong came to express his gratitude and let him return his title.
The emperor personally went to his house to say hello, got off the bus in the street, came up with scriptures in his hands, caressed Huan Rong, shed tears, and gave him bedding, curtains, swords, clothes and quilts, and then walked away for a long time.
From then on, the princes, generals and officials who asked about illness no longer dared to ride to the door and prostrated themselves under the bed.
After Huan Rong died, the emperor personally changed his clothes, buried him before the funeral, and gave him a tomb in the south of Shouyang Mountain.
Except for the two brothers and the son who made up four hundred stones, eight students made up two hundred stones, and most of the other disciples became ministers. ◆Ding Hongchuan, named Xiaogong, was a native of Dingling, Yingchuan.
His father, Ding Linlin, whose courtesy name was Youchun, served as the Yingyang Wei in the last years of Wang Mang's life.
Shizu occupied Yingyang, but Yingyang city could not be defended. Ding Linlin persuaded the county magistrate and surrendered with him. The ancestors were overjoyed and rewarded them greatly. He used Ding Jinlin to lead the soldiers to cross the river first, send a message to the prefecture and the country, attack the camp and seize the territory, and captured 21 counties in Henan, Chenliu and Sichuan.
In the first year of Jianwu, Ding Linlin was worshiped as the governor of Henan.
When it came time to award the meritorious officials, the emperor asked everyone to do what they wanted. All the generals occupied Fengyi Mei County, but Ding Linlin was the only one willing to grant the title to his hometown.
Someone said to Ding Jinlin: Everyone wants to occupy the county, but you only want the hometown. Why is this?
Ding Jinlin said: In the past, Sun Shuao told his son that when he was granted a title, he must seek a barren land. Now that I can do a small job, it will be great to get a rural pavilion.
The emperor obeyed and named him Marquis of Xin'an Township, Dingling, with a settlement of 5,000 households. Later, he was renamed Marquis of Lingyang.
When Ding Hongnian was 13 years old, he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" from Huan Rong. In three years, he understood the chapters and sentences, could debate and speak for everyone, so he determined to further his studies, put on civilian clothes, carried his luggage, and traveled thousands of miles to study.
At first, Ding Jinlin followed Shizu in the expedition, and Ding Hong lived with his younger brother Ding Sheng. They loved Ding Sheng when he was young and lived a poor life together.
After Ding Jinlin's death, Ding Hong was granted the hereditary title and wrote a letter to transfer the country to Ding Sheng, but received no reply.
His father had been buried, so he hung mourning clothes in the tomb and slipped away, leaving a message to Ding Sheng: "Hong was greedy for scriptures. He ignored his kindness and righteousness. He studied with his teacher when he was young. He did not support his parents during his life. He could not fulfill his filial piety until his death. The ancestors of the emperor and heaven did not bless and help him. He was seriously ill and could not bear the soil."
The last time I wrote a letter stating my illness, I was willing to resign my title to my younger brother, but the memorial was shelved without a reply, and the time was approaching for me to be granted a title.
I would like to give up the title and seek good doctors abroad.
If the disease cannot be cured, forget about dying in a ravine.
Ding Hong initially became a student with Huan Rong, a colleague of Bao Jun from Jiujiang, and the two had a close friendship. Later, Ding Hong escaped from the throne and met Bao Jun in the East China Sea. Ding Hong pretended not to know Bao Jun.
Bao Jun took Ding Hong's arm and scolded him: "In the past, Boyi and Wu Jizha were in troubled times, so they had to express their ambition to surrender the country."
The great righteousness of "Spring and Autumn" is not to waste the king's affairs because of family affairs. Now you are using your brother's affair to cut off your father's immortal inheritance. Can you say it is smart?
Ding Hong was very moved and sighed in tears, so he returned to his country and taught apprentices.
Bao Jun also wrote a letter saying that Ding Hong was a good scholar and practiced the classics, and Xianzong appreciated him very much.
In the 10th year of Yongping, the emperor issued an edict to recruit talents. Ding Hong was summoned when he arrived and told the story of "The Order of Marquis Wen". The emperor bestowed royal robes and ribbons, food and carriage, and received the same courtesy as a doctor.
Soon, he became a servant.
In the thirteenth year, he also served as the captain of Shesheng.
In the fourth year of Jianchu period, he was granted the title of Marquis of Luyang Township.
Suzong ordered Ding Hong, Wang Xian of Guangping, and other Confucian scholars such as Lou Wang, Cheng Feng, Huan Yu, Jia Kui, etc. to discuss the similarities and differences of the Five Classics at the White Tiger Temple in the Beigong. Wei Ying, the minister of five sense organs, took over the task of handling the problem, and Chunyu, the servant, went to Gongzou, and the emperor personally announced the decision.
Ding Hong was highly talented and the most eloquent in discussing difficult issues. He was praised by many scholars and even praised by the emperor many times.
People at that time sighed: "There is no one like Ding Xiaogong in the palace."
Ding Hong was rewarded many times and promoted to school secretary, so he replaced Cheng as Shaofu.
From then on, the sect became more prosperous, with thousands of people coming from far away.
Liu Kai from Pengcheng, Bamao from Beihai, and Zhu Xian from Jiujiang all became public ministers.
In the third year of Yuanhe, he was renamed Marquis of Mating Township.
Emperor He ascended the throne and was promoted to Taichang. In the fourth year of Yongyuan, Yuan An became Situ.
At this time, Empress Dowager Dou came to power, and her brothers Dou Xian were each good at authority.
Ding Hong took advantage of the solar eclipse and said to the minister: "I heard that the sun is the yang essence, and it is the symbol of the king. The moon is the yin essence, and there are certain rules for waxing and waning. This is the appearance of the minister."
Therefore, when the sun eclipses, the minister is above the king, and the yin dominates the yang; the moon is full but not waning, and the lower part is arrogant and full.
In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was in decline, Huangfu and others were monopolizing power, and the party was strong and suppressed the main force, so the sun and moon were eclipsed. "The Book of Songs" says: At the turn of October, on the new moon and Xin Mao, the sun has an eclipse, which is also the You ghost of Kong.
"Spring and Autumn" records: thirty-six solar eclipses and thirty-two regicides.
Change does not occur in space, and each responds to its own kind.
No authority should be given up, and no sharp weapon should be used as a dummy.
Looking at the past, and looking at the rise of the Han Dynasty from a closer look, all the disasters and dangers have arisen from this.
Therefore, Sanhuan was in charge of Lu, Tian was good at the administration of Qi, Liuqing divided up the Jin Dynasty, and Lu controlled the Han Dynasty. The heirs changed several times. In the last years of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, the ancestral temple could not offer sacrifices.
Therefore, although he is related to the Duke of Zhou, he does not have the virtue of the Duke of Zhou and cannot exercise his power. Now the general Dou Xian, although he wanted to restrain himself and did not dare to overstep his power, but the people all over the world were afraid to accept the decree. The governor, Er Qianshi, paid his respects at the beginning and asked for permission to be reported.
Carrying the royal family on your back and walking toward a private door is because the authority of the superiors is reduced and the power of the inferiors is increased.
Humanity is contrary to what is below, but the results are shown in heaven. Although there is a hidden plot, the gods will observe the situation and look down at the elephant to see warnings to warn the king.
Recently, on the first day of the month, there is still no shortage after the fifteenth day. This is because the ministers are proud, disobey the king, and work alone.
Your Majesty did not notice it, so God has warned you again and you should be afraid to prevent disaster.
The Book of Songs says: Respecting Heaven's anger, one dare not play with Yu.
If we restrain our efforts and blame ourselves, and guard against the slightest, then the evil monster will be eliminated, the harm will be eliminated, and blessings will come. The water that destroys cliffs and rocks comes from trickling springs; the big trees that cover up the sun with dry clouds originate from green seedlings.
It is easy to stop the subtle things, but it is difficult to save them from the end. People often ignore the small things, which can lead to great disasters.
I can't bear to teach, but I can't bear to cut. After the incident is over, there is no clear mirror of what happened.
The foolish minister thought that all the ministers who were attached to the left official and relied on the powerful to subvert and flatter him in order to be flattered should be killed.
Recently, the general has come out again and has shaken up the prefectures and counties. They have collected taxes from the officials and sent envoys to contribute supplies.
Although the general said he would not accept it, he did not return the property to his owner, and the officials who deployed him were fearless, committed illegal acts, and refused to admit their crimes. Therefore, greed and cunning became common in the country, and people competed for traitors. The common people sighed and were filled with resentment.
I have heard that Heaven cannot be uncharitable, and if it is not strong, the Three Lights will not be clear; the king cannot be devoid of strength, and if he is not strong, he will dominate and control his herds.
We should take advantage of the great changes to correct political failures and supplement God's will.
More than ten days after the memorial was published, the emperor sent Ding Hongxing, a Taiwei and a guard, to station in the South and North Palaces.
So General Dou Xian's seal and ribbon were confiscated, and Dou Xian and his brothers committed suicide.
At that time, the large counties recommended two filial and honest people for every five to six hundred thousand people, and the small counties also recommended two people for every two hundred thousand barbarians. The emperor thought it was unfair and submitted it to a meeting of ministers.
Ding Hong and Sikong Liu Fang said: "Anyone who uses population as a standard should have grades. Barbarians are mixed and mixed and cannot be included in the number."
From now on, in every county and state, one person for every 200,000 people will be promoted to be filial and honest, two people for every 400,000 people, three people for 600,000 people, four people for 800,000 people, five people for one million people, and six people for 1.2 million people.
If the amount is less than 200,000, one person will be promoted every two years, and if the amount is less than 100,000, one person will be promoted every three years.
The emperor obeyed.
Ding Hong died in six years, and the gifts were more than usual.
