translation:
◆Dou Wu's biography, Dou Wu's courtesy name is You Ping, a native of Pingling County, Fufeng County, and the great-great-grandson of Dai Hourong of Anfeng County.
His father, Dou Feng, was the prefect of Dingxiang.
When Dou Wu was young, he was famous for his virtues in Confucian classics. He once taught Osawa Zhong. He was not involved in current affairs, and his reputation was prominent in the Kansai area.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, the eldest daughter was elected to the palace. Emperor Huan appointed her as a nobleman and appointed Dou Wu as the doctor.
In the winter of this year, the noble lady was made queen, Dou Wu was promoted to Yueqi Xiaowei, and was granted the title of Marquis of Huaili, with 5,000 households.
In the winter of the second year, he was awarded the title of captain of the city gate.
During his tenure, he recruited famous people, was honest and dedicated to the public affairs, deeply hated bad people and bad deeds, did not accept gifts or bribes, and his wife had only enough food and clothing for food and clothing.
At this time, the Qiang barbarians were in rebellion, the harvest was poor, and the people were hungry. General Dou gave all the rewards from the two palaces to the students of the Imperial Academy, and he also used carts to carry food and meals to the poor on the roads.
Dou Shao, the son of Dou Wu's brother, was appointed as Huben's lieutenant general and had a lazy and extravagant temperament.
Dou Wu often reprimanded him severely, but he still didn't realize it, so he wrote a letter requesting that Dou Shao be removed from his post. He also blamed himself for not being able to discipline Dou Shao well and that he should suffer first.
From then on, Dou Shao abided by restraint and did not dare to violate anything illegal, no matter how big or small.
At that time, there were many political mistakes in the country. The eunuchs had exclusive power. Li Ying, Du Mi and others were arrested and interrogated for party affairs.
In the first year of Yongkang, Dou Wu Shangshu said: I heard that a wise emperor is not afraid of people saying sarcastic words in order to understand some dark facts; loyal ministers are not afraid of causing harm by admonishing the emperor, in order to make everything smooth for the country.
Therefore, the harmony between the monarch and his ministers will be famous for centuries.
I was lucky enough to live in the prosperous Ming Dynasty and be enlightened by civil and military forces. How dare I protect the throne in order to escape crime and not be sincere and wise to the emperor?
The emperor first lived in a vassal state and later ascended to the throne. The whole world rejoiced and thought it was the rejuvenation of the country.
However, since taking office, no good political measures have been seen.
Although Liang Ji, Sun Shou, Kou Rong, and Deng Wandai were executed, the eunuchs who often served him continued to cause trouble, bully His Majesty, and engage in deceit. They created systems without authorization and gave officials and titles to bad people at will. The politics of the court became worse day by day, and the treacherous ministers became stronger day by day. I recall that the Western Han Dynasty indulged the Wang family and ruled with flattering ministers, and finally lost the world.
Ignore the lessons of previous failures and continue on the wrong track; I am afraid that the disaster of Hu Hai, the second emperor of the Qin Dynasty, will definitely happen again, and the chaos of Zhao Gao will come either in the morning or in the evening.
Recently, the Treacherous Officials' Prison was used to create a party meeting and arrested and interrogated former Sili school captain Li Ying, Taipu Du Mi, Yushi Zhongcheng Chen Xiang, Taiwei Peng Fanpang and others. Hundreds of people were implicated and detained and interrogated for a whole year without any factual basis.
I think Li Ying and others were loyal to the royal family and aspired to the royal family. They were really assisting the emperors Ji, Xian, Yi, and Lu, but they were framed by traitorous ministers and traitors. The whole world was chilled by this and the people of the whole country were disappointed.
Your Majesty, please pay attention to the matter and deal with it immediately to meet the expectations of humans and ghosts.
I heard that in ancient times, a wise ruler must have wise assistants to make his politics clear.
The ministers who are close to the court now, such as Shangshu Ling Chen Fan, Pushe Hu Guang, Shangshu Zhu Yu, Xun Nu, Liu Wei Lang, Liu Ju, Yin Xun, etc., are all reliable talents of the country and good assistants of the court.
The ministers Zhang Ling, Gui Hao, Yuan Kang, Yang Qiao, Bian Shao, Dai Hui, etc. were gentle and well-educated and familiar with the country's rules and regulations.
In matters both inside and outside the imperial court, all kinds of talents are there, at your Majesty's disposal.
However, His Majesty appointed a group of villains to create gluttonous, corrupt and cruel villains, and made them serve as state and county officials outside the country and as confidants in the court.
They should be demoted one by one, punished according to the severity of their crimes, deprived of the titles of eunuchs who deceived the country, and punished for their crimes of illegally deceiving the king. They should appoint loyal and virtuous people, distinguish between good and bad, make the right and wrong, repute each one in accordance with their true nature, cherish the official position, and only grant it to good people.
In this way, disasters can be eliminated and God's response can be realized immediately.
Recently, Jiahe, Zhicao, and Huanglong have appeared.
Those auspicious things come from good people, and good fortune comes from good people. Virtue is auspicious, and lack of virtue is disaster.
What your Majesty did was not in line with God's will and should not be celebrated.
He was sent up by Shu and returned to the captain of the city gate and the Hou Yinshou of Huaili with his illness.
The emperor did not allow it, and there was an edict to free Li Ying, Du Mi, etc. from the Huangmen North Temple, Ruoxu, and all the prisons in the capital, and all the prisoners with minor crimes were released.
In the winter of this year, Emperor Huan died without any sons.
Dou Wu summoned Liu Min, the censor of Hejian, to ask him which of the princes and marquises in the country was the best. Liu Min said that Liu Hong, the Marquis of Jiedu Ting, was the best.
Dou Wu went to the palace to report to the Queen Mother, so he conscripted Liu Hong to be the emperor, the Ling Emperor.
He appointed Dou Wu as the general and lived in the palace.
After Emperor Ling came to the throne, he judged his merits and made Dou Wu the Marquis of Wenxi; his son Dou Ji, the Marquis of Weiyang, was appointed as the Shizhong; his elder brother Dou Shao was the Marquis of Yu and was promoted to the infantry captain; Dou Shao's younger brother Dou Jing was the Marquis of Xixiang and was the Shizhong, supervising Yulin Zuoqi.
After Dou Wu assisted the dynasty, he often had the idea of ​​​​killing eunuchs, and Taiwei Chen Fan also had this plan for a long time.
When they were meeting in the court, Chen Fan quietly said to Dou Wu: Zhongchang's servants Cao Jie, Wang Fu and others manipulated the power of the country during the reign of the late emperor, causing the world to be in chaos and causing chaos among the people. They are the fault.
If Cao Jie and others are not killed now, it will be difficult to do so in the future.
Dou Wu agreed very much. Chen Fan was so happy that he pushed the seat away with his hands and stood up.
Dou Wu then recruited his comrades Yin Xun as Shangshu Ling, Liu Yu as Shizhong, and Feng Shu as Tunqi Xiaowei. He also recruited the deposed former Sili Xiaowei Li Ying, Zongzheng Liu Meng, Imperial Servant Du Mi, Lujiang Prefect Zhu Yu, etc. to gather at the court.
Therefore, all the talented people in the world, knowing the trend of the situation, raised their heads, stood on their heels, and wanted to contribute their talents.
At the time of the solar eclipse in May, Chen Fan said to Dou Wu again: In the past, Xiao Wangzhi was harmed by Shi Xian. Recently, Li Ying and Du Mi have caused harm to their wives, families and children. Not to mention that there are dozens of people in Shi Xian today!
As an eighty-year-old man, I want to help the general eliminate harm. Now I can use the solar eclipse as an excuse to repel and depose the eunuchs to counteract the changes in heaven.
Also, Mrs. Zhao and the female minister are harassing the Queen Mother from morning to night. They should be eliminated as soon as possible.
I hope the general will consider it carefully!
Dou Wu then told the Queen Mother: The old rule is that Huangmen and regular attendants should serve in the palace, guard the door, and be in charge of the money and goods in the palace.
Now they are allowed to participate in political affairs and hold important positions, and their children are everywhere, specializing in corruption and violence.
This is the reason why the world is in turmoil.
They should all be killed and the court cleared.
The Queen Mother said: The old rules since the Han Dynasty have been passed down from generation to generation. Only those who commit crimes should be killed. Can they be abolished?
At that time, the minister Guan Ba ​​was very talented and controlled everything in the palace.
Dou Wu first asked Guan Ba ​​and Zhongchang Shi Su Kang to be executed. After the executions, Dou Wu asked Cao Jie and others to be executed again. The Queen Mother hesitated and the matter was pending for a long time.
By August, Taibai Star appears in the west.
Liu Yu usually knew a lot about astronomy and thought it was unlucky. He wrote to the Empress Dowager and said: Taibai star is in the left corner of the house star, and the general star is in Taiwei star. The divination result is: the palace gate should be closed, it is not good for the general, and the traitor is next to the master.
Please take precautions as soon as possible.
He also wrote to Dou Wu and Chen Fan that the stars were out of position and that it was not good for the ministers, so they should make a decision as soon as possible.
Dou Wu and Chen Fan received Liu Yu's letter and prepared to launch a campaign to kill the eunuchs, so they appointed Zhu Yu as Sili Xiaowei, Liu as Henan Yin, and Yu Qi as Luoyang order.
Dou Wu asked to remove Wei Biao's Huangmen Order and replace it with his trusted Xiao Huangmen Shanbing.
Shan Bingzou asked Changle Shangshu Zheng Sa, who was always cunning and extremely ruthless, to be sent to Beisi Prison.
Chen Fan said to Dou Wu: These guys should be killed immediately, why bother interrogating them!
Dou Wu did not listen to his opinions and ordered Shan Bing, Yin Xun, and Shi Yushi Zhu Wangjin to interrogate Zheng Sa in a chaotic manner. Sa's confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu.
Yin Xun and Shan Bing petitioned to arrest Cao Jie and others, and asked Liu Yu to report to the Empress Dowager.
At this time, Dou Wu went out to stay and returned to his mansion. The person in charge of Zhongshu first reported him to Zhu Wangyu, the official historian of Changle.
Zhu Wangyu stole Dou Wu's memorial and read it, and cursed: Of course the eunuchs who indulge in illegal acts can be killed.
What sin do we people have, and why should we be exterminated together?
So he shouted: Chen Fan and Dou Wu asked the Queen Mother to depose the emperor. This is treason!
So in the evening, he summoned seventeen of his cronies, including the official Shi Gongpu and Zhang Liang from Changle, and made an alliance with livestock blood in their mouths to kill Dou Wu and others.
After hearing this, Cao Jie told the emperor in panic: "It's very tense outside. Please come out of Yu Deyang's front hall."
The emperor was so excited that he drew his sword, and asked the wet nurse Zhao Rao and others to support and protect the left and right, collect the entrance certificates, and close all the forbidden doors.
Summon the ministers and officials, threaten them with swords, and make them write edicts.
He appointed Wang Fu as the Huangmen Order and went to Beisi Prison to arrest Yin Xun and Shan Bing with the emperor's order.
Shan Bing was suspicious and refused to accept the edict, so Wang Fu killed him.
So Yin Xun was killed and Zheng Sa was released.
They came back together to kidnap the Queen Mother and seize the seal.
Those who are exhausted are ordered to guard the Nangong, close the door, and cut off any further path.
Zheng Sa and others were ordered by the emperor to arrest Dou Wu and others together with the imperial censor and the envoys.
Dou Wu refused to accept the order, ran into the barracks, and shot the envoy together with Dou Shao.
He summoned thousands of soldiers from the five Northern Army schools to station under the capital pavilion, and ordered the sergeants to say: The eunuchs in Huangmen have rebelled, and those who try their best to kill them will be rewarded heavily.
The imperial edict ordered Shaofu Zhou Jing to march and ride on General Zhang Huan to lead five battalions of soldiers to attack Dou Wu.
Late at night, Wang Fu led more than a thousand people including Hu Ben, Yu Lin, Mang Ma Cu, Du Hou, and Jian Zhuo Geshi to go out of Zhuqueye Gate to join Zhang Huan and other troops.
Early the next morning, the entire army was stationed under the palace gate to confront Dou Wu's troops.
Wang Fu's troops gradually increased, and he ordered the soldiers to shout to Dou Wu's army: "Dou Wu rebels, you are all forbidden soldiers. You should protect the palace and province. Why do you follow the rebels?"
The first to surrender will be rewarded!
The camp was usually afraid of subduing the eunuchs, so Dou Wu's army returned to Wang Fu.
From morning to lunch, Dou Wu's troops had almost surrendered.
Dou Wu and Dou Shao fled and were pursued and surrounded by Wang Fu's army. They both committed suicide and showed their heads to Luoyang Duting.
Their clansmen, guests, and in-laws were all captured and killed. Liu Yu and Feng Shu all annihilated their clans.
Moved Dou Wu's family to Rinan and moved the Queen Mother to Yuntai.
At this time, the vicious eunuch succeeded, and the upright people were discouraged and dared not say anything.
Dou Wu's official Hu Teng from Guiyang, who learned from Dou Wu when he was young, collected and buried Dou Wu's body alone, so he was imprisoned and was not allowed to be an official.
Dou Wu's grandson Dou Fu, who was only two years old at the time, was not harmed because he escaped.
Later he was discovered, and Cao Jie and others arrested him urgently.
Hu Teng and Ling Shi Nanyang and Zhang Chang helped Dou Fu escape to Lingling, pretending to be dead. Hu Teng considered him his son and got a wife for him.
Later he was promoted to Guiyang Xiaolian.
During Jian'an, Liu Biao, the herdsman of Jingzhou, heard about it and recruited him as an official. He returned to the surname Dou and reported his facts to the court. When Liu Biao died, Cao Cao pacified Jingzhou. Dou Fu and his people moved to Ye. He was recruited into the Prime Minister's Mansion and joined the army to conquer Ma Chao. He was hit by a stray arrow and died.
At first, Dou Wu's mother gave birth to a snake while giving birth to Dou Wu, and sent the snake into the forest.
Later, Dou Wu's mother died and was buried before the coffin was placed. A big snake came out of the forest and came to the funeral site. It hit the coffin with its head, tears and blood flowed, and it lay bent and bent, as if weeping, and then left after a while.
At that time, people knew that it was the auspiciousness of the Dou family.
Hu Teng's courtesy name is Zisheng. At first, Emperor Huan went on a tour of Nanyang and used Hu Teng as his escort.
The ministers, nobles, and relatives have tens of thousands of entourages, and there is no end to the demand for money and labor.
Hu Teng wrote a letter saying: The emperor has no inside or outside. The place where he goes is the capital.
I asked Bi Si, the governor of Jingzhou, to serve as the school captain, and I myself served as the official of Tongdu.
The emperor complied.
From then on, the followers did not dare to ask for anything without authorization, and Hu Teng became famous for this.
After the party ban was lifted, the official became minister.
◆He Jinzhuan, He Jinzhuan, courtesy name Suigao, was from Wan County, Nanyang.
The half-brother and daughter were selected as nobles in the palace. Emperor Ling liked her and appointed He Jin as the doctor. He was promoted to the general of the doctor in Huben and became the prefect of Yingchuan.
In the third year of Guanghe's reign, the nobleman was appointed as the queen. He was recruited to the capital and served as a servant. He was appointed as a master craftsman and Henan Yin.
In the first year of Zhongping, the Yellow Turban thief Zhang Jiao and others rose up, appointed He Jin as the general, and led the five battalions of Yulin on the left and right to station in the capital pavilion to repair equipment and defend the capital.
Zhang Jiao's faction, Ma Yuanyi, conspired to raise troops in Luoyang. He Jin discovered his treacherous plot and was granted the title of Marquis Shen for his merits.
In the fourth year, thousands of Xingyang thieves rioted, attacked and burned the county, and killed the county magistrate of Zhongmou. He Jin's younger brother Henan Yin Hemiao was ordered to fight. He Miao defeated the thieves, quelled the riot and returned to the capital.
The imperial edict sent an envoy to Chenggao to welcome him, and appointed He Miao as a chariot and cavalry general and the Marquis of Jiyang.
In the past five years, the world has become more chaotic. The angry people think that there will be soldiers in the capital, and the two palaces will bleed. General Xu Liang and fake Sima Wudang said to He Jin: "Tai Gong's Six Tao" has the emperor's military affairs, which can control the four directions.
He Jin thought it was right and went to court to tell the emperor.
So he ordered He Jin to send out troops from all directions, hoping that the situation would be peaceful.
A large altar was built, with twelve layers of colorful canopies, ten feet high, built on it. A small altar was built in the northeast of the altar, and another nine layers of canopies, nine feet high, were built. Tens of thousands of infantry and knights were lined up in a camp. The emperor personally came out to review and stationed under the big canopy. How could he station under the small canopy?
After the ceremony, Emperor Ling, wearing armor and horse, called the "Supreme General" and circled the formation three times before returning.
He Jin was ordered to lead the entire army to watch.
At this time, eight captains of Xiyuan were set up, with Xiaohuangmen Jianshuo as the upper military captain, Huben Zhonglang Yuan Shao as the middle military captain, Tunqi Commander Bao Hong as the lower military captain, Yilang Cao Cao as the dian military captain, Zhao Rong as the assistant military captain, Chunyu Qiong as the assistant military captain, and the left and right captains.
Emperor Ling believed that Jian Shuo was strong and capable of military strategy. He trusted him especially and appointed him as a marshal, supervising and supervising the commanders and subordinates below the school captain. Even the generals were also under his leadership.
Although Jian Shuo was in charge of military power in the imperial court, he was still a little afraid of being jealous of He Jin, so he talked to Emperor Ling with his ministers and asked him to send He Jin to the west to attack Bian Zhang and Han Sui.
Emperor Ling listened to them and rewarded He Jin with hundreds of military chariots, tigers, sharp axes and axes.
He Jin secretly knew this was a conspiracy. So he submitted a petition to send Yuan Zhaodong to attack Xu and Yanzhou soldiers. He wanted to wait for Yuan Shao to return before sending troops to delay time.
At first, Queen He gave birth to Prince Bian, and Wang Gui gave birth to Prince Xie.
The ministers asked for a crown prince, but Emperor Ling thought that he was too frivolous and unworthy to be a king. However, the queen was favored by Emperor Ling, and He Jin held great power, so he hesitated to decide.
In the sixth year, Emperor Ling was seriously ill and asked Jian Shuo to assist Liu Xie.
Jian Shuo had received the imperial edict and had always looked down upon and envied brothers He Jin and He Miao. When Emperor Ling passed away, Jian Shuo was in the palace and wanted to kill He Jin first and establish Xie as emperor.
When He Jin came in from outside, Jian Shuo Sima Pan Yin and He Jin had known each other for a long time, and they welcomed He Jin with his eyes. He Jin was frightened and rode back to the camp from a shortcut, leading his troops to the Baijun Mansion, so he refused to go in because of illness.
Jian Shuo's plot did not come true, and Prince Bian became emperor. The Empress Dowager He came to the court to attend to the affairs of state, while He Jin and the Grand Tutor Yuan Kai assisted in the administration and also took charge of the affairs of the Secretariat.
He Jin had known for a long time that eunuchs were hated by everyone in the world, and he hated Jian Shuo for plotting to harm him and for taking over the power of the court, so he secretly arranged to kill the eunuchs.
Yuan Shao also had a plan for a long time, and asked He Jin's relative Zhang Jin to persuade He Jin: Huangmen Changshi has been in power for a long time, and he has committed adultery with the Empress Dowager Changle. The general should select virtuous talents to rectify the world and eliminate harm to the country.
He Jin thought it was right.
In addition, the Yuan family has been favored for many generations and is supported by people at home. Yuan Zhao was good at raising scholars, and the heroes were willing to be used by him. His younger brother Huben Zhonglang, General Yuan Shu, was also fond of chivalry, so they all accepted him favorably.
Therefore, more resourceful people such as Feng Ji, He, Xun You, etc. were recruited and became close friends with them.
Jian Shuo was suspicious and uneasy, so he wrote a letter to Zhao Zhong and others, saying: The generals and brothers are in power and are now plotting with the people of the world to kill those close to the late emperor and to eliminate us. It is only because I am in charge of the forbidden troops, so I am temporarily hesitant.
Now we should work together to close the Shangge and kill them urgently.
Guo Sheng, the regular servant of Zhongchang, was from the same county as He Jin.
Fortunately for the Queen Mother and He Jin, Guo Sheng stepped in and helped.
Therefore, Guo Sheng trusted the He family, so he discussed with Zhao Zhong and others, not to follow Jian Shuo's plan, and handed over Jian Shuo's letter to He Jin.
He Jin sent the Huangmen Order to arrest and kill Jian Shuo, and then commanded the garrison himself.
Yuan Shao also persuaded He Jin: In the past, Dou Wu wanted to kill his favorite but was killed because what he said was leaked. The officials in the five camps obeyed the eunuchs and were afraid of the eunuchs.
Now the general has such an important position as his uncle, he and his brothers command powerful troops, and his subordinates are all handsome and distinguished men, and they are willing to do their best to report their fate. The matter is in control. This is the opportunity of God's help.
A general should eliminate harm for the world and be famous for future generations.
Although Uncle Shen of the Zhou Dynasty was nothing!
Now the master's coffin is in the front hall. The general is ordered to command the forbidden troops and should not enter or leave the palace at will.
He Jinshen thought it was true, so he excused himself from attending the funeral because of his illness, and refused to attend the funeral.
That is to say, he made a plan with Yuan Shao and told the Queen Mother about the plan.
The Queen Mother refused to listen and said: Eunuchs rule the forbidden provinces. From ancient times to the present, the old rules of the Han family cannot be abolished.
Moreover, the late emperor has just passed away, how can I openly work with scholars?
He Jin could not disobey the Queen Mother's will and wanted to kill those who were in charge.
Yuan Shao believed that the eunuchs were close to the emperor and issued orders. If they were not eliminated now, they would definitely cause harm in the future.
The Queen Mother's mother Wuyang Jun and He Miao accepted bribes from various eunuchs many times. Knowing that He Jin wanted to kill them, they told the Queen Mother many times to protect them.
He also said: The general is good at killing his cronies, and he monopolizes power to weaken the emperor.
The Queen Mother suspected that this was the case.
Some of the eunuchs had been at the emperor's right and left for decades. They were granted high titles and favors, and their internal and external collusion was extremely consolidated.
He Jinxin was in charge of important tasks and was usually afraid of them. Although he was famous outside, he could not make a decision in his heart, so things could not be settled for a long time.
Why did Yuan Shao and others plan to summon more powerful generals and a large number of heroes from all over the world, so that they could lead their troops to the capital to threaten the Queen Mother.
He Jin agreed.
Chen Lin, the chief bookkeeper, advised him: "The Book of Changes" states that if the deer is released, it cannot be caught. As the saying goes: Hunting sparrows while blindfolded.
If you can't deceive small things with success, how much more can you use deceit to obtain important national affairs.
Now the general has the imperial power, controls the military power, the dragon and the tiger step, whether it is high or low, it is all in your heart. This is like burning the hair on a stove. What's the difficulty?
It conforms to the Tao, goes against the scriptures, and is obeyed by heaven and man. Instead, abandon the weapon and look for foreign aid.
When the soldiers gather together, the stronger becomes the hero. This is what is called fighting and turning the tables on others. If you give the handle to others, the success will never be achieved, and the vain efforts will become the steps for chaos and evil.
He Jin refused to listen.
He summoned former general Dong Zhuo from the west to garrison in Shanglinyuan in Guanzhong, and sent Wang Kuang of Taishan to mobilize the strong crossbowmen of his county. He summoned Qiao Mao, the prefect of Dongjun, to garrison in Chenggao. He sent Ding Yuan, the commander of Wu Meng, to burn Mengjin. The fire lit up the city red, and they all said they wanted to kill the eunuchs.
The Queen Mother still disagreed.
He Miao said to He Jin: "In the beginning, we all came from Nanyang. We were poor and lowly, so we relied on the palace to gain wealth."
National affairs are not easy either!
The poured water cannot be recovered, so you should consider it carefully and maintain peace with the palace.
He Jin's thoughts became even more suspicious.
Yuan Shao was worried that He Jin would change his mind, so he threatened him: "The combined situation has been revealed. If things are not done, something will happen. What is the general waiting for? Why didn't he decide earlier?"
He Jin then appointed Yuan Shao as the commander of the Sili school, holding the talisman and commanding special orders to attack. Wang Yun, who was engaged in Zhonglang, was appointed as Henan Yin.
Yuan Shao sent Luoyang military officials to monitor the eunuchs, and sent Dong Zhuo and others to the post to prepare for the invasion.
The Queen Mother became frightened and dismissed all Xiaohuangmen and returned their envoys to their homes. Only those who were close to He Jin were left to guard the province.
All the ministers from Xiaohuangmen went to He Jin to plead guilty and listen to what He Jin would do.
He Jin said to them: "The world is in trouble, and it is the kings who are causing harm!"
Now that Dong Zhuo will arrive soon, why don't you all return to your kingdoms as soon as possible?
Yuan Shao advised He Jin to execute them at this moment, but He Jin refused again and again.
Yuan Shao also wrote to various states and counties, pretending to convey He Jin's intention to arrest the eunuch's relatives.
He Jin planned for too long, and things were leaked, and the eunuch was afraid and wanted to change.
Zhang Rang's wife, the Queen Mother's sister, Zhang Rang kowtowed to his wife and said: "I have offended the old minister, so I should stay in a private house with my bride."
I have been favored for many lifetimes, and now I have to stay away from the palace, reluctant to leave. Please enter the palace again, so that I can temporarily see the Queen Mother and the Emperor, and then go back. I will die without regrets.
The wife told Lord Wuyang that Lord Wuyang had told the Queen Mother, so he ordered all the regular attendants to return to the palace.
In August, He entered Changle and told the Queen Mother that she would kill all the regular servants and below, and select three ministers to enter the palace to guard the eunuch's palace.
The eunuchs said to each other: "The general excused himself from mourning because he was ill and did not attend the funeral. Now he suddenly came to the palace. What do you want to do?"
Did the Dou family incident happen again?
Zhang Rang and others also sent people to eavesdrop, and they listened completely to what he said, so they led the regular attendants Duan Wanggui, Bi Lan and dozens of others to quietly enter from the side door with weapons and ambush the palace. When He Jin came out, he pretended to be the Queen Mother and summoned him.
When He entered the palace, Zhang Rang and others questioned He Jin and said: "The chaos in the world is not only our fault."
The late emperor once had a feud with the Queen Mother and almost deposed her. We cried to save her, and each of us gave tens of millions of our wealth as gifts to please the Emperor. We just wanted to rely on your He family's family.
Now we actually want to kill our race. Isn't it a bit excessive?
You say that the palace is filthy and filthy, but who is loyal and honest below the rank of minister?
So Shangfang's supervisor, Qu Mu, drew his sword and killed He Jin in front of the Jiade Hall.
Zhang Rang, Duan Wanggui and others issued an edict to appoint the former Taiwei Fan Ling as the Sili school attaché, and the Shaofu Prime Minister Xu as Henan Yin.
The minister received the edict, suspected it was false, and said: "Please invite the general to come out and discuss it together."
Zhonghuangmen threw He Jin's head to the minister and said: "He Jin has rebelled and has been killed."
He Jin's subordinate generals Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang were He Jin's cronies. They heard that He Jin had been killed outside and wanted to lead troops into the palace. The palace was closed and no one was allowed to enter.
Yuan Shu and Wu Kuang worked together to cut and attack, while Zhonghuang Gate defended the pavilion with weapons.
At sunset, Yuan Shu set fire to the Nine Dragon Gate of Nangong and the East and West Palaces, and wanted to threaten Zhang Rang and others to come out.
Zhang Rang and others went in and told the Queen Mother that the general had rebelled, burned the palace, and attacked the Shangshu Gate, so he kidnapped the Queen Mother, the Emperor, and King Chenliu, and also robbed the palace officials and their families, and took the North Palace via Fudao.
Shangshu Lu Zhi held a sword under the window of the pavilion, raised his head and scolded Duan Wanggui.
Duan Wanggui was afraid and released the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother jumped from the pavilion and escaped without being robbed.
Yuan Shao and his uncle Yuan Wei falsely claimed that the emperor ordered Fan Ling and Xu Xiang to be killed.
He Miao and Yuan Shao then led troops to station under Zhuque Tower, arrested Zhao Zhong and others and killed them.
Wu Kuang waited for a long time and complained that He Miao was not of the same mind as He Jin. He also suspected that he was conspiring with the eunuchs, so he ordered the army to say: The one who killed the general was the chariot. Can you avenge the general?
He Jin was kind and kind to his subordinates, and all the soldiers cried and said: I am willing to die in repayment!
Wu Kuang led his troops and Dong Zhuo's younger brother, Fengche Duwei Dong, attacked and killed He Miao and dumped his body in the garden.
Yuan Shao closed the North Palace Gate and ordered his soldiers to capture the eunuchs. No matter how big or small, kill them all.
Some were mistakenly thought to be killed by eunuchs, while others exposed themselves and were spared from being killed.
More than two thousand people died.
Yuan Shaoyin marched into the palace, and some people from the upper gates attacked the palace.
Zhang Rang, Duan Wanggui and others could not escape the siege, so they kidnapped the emperor and dozens of King Chen Liu and fled to Xiaopingjin.
The ministers all came out from Pingtang, and no one ran with them. Only Lu Zhi, the minister, rode on horseback on the river at night. Wang Yun sent Minggong from central Henan to follow Lu Zhi.
Mingong arrived and killed several people with his sword, while the rest jumped into the river and died.
The next day, the ministers and officials welcomed the emperor back to the palace, appointed Min Gong as the doctor, and granted the title of Marquis of Ting.
Dong Zhuo then deposed Emperor Ling, forced the Queen Mother to be killed, and killed Lord Wuyang. The He family died, and the Han Dynasty also fell into chaos.
The historian commented: Dou Wu and He Jin, as uncles, held the power of assisting the government. Inside the palace, they relied on the power of the Queen Mother to listen to the government, and outside they had favorable conditions for heroes to ride on the wind. Finally, they were defeated by the eunuchs, died in power, and were lamented by the world. Is it possible that they lacked intelligence but had more power?
"Zuo Zhuan" says: Heaven has abolished Shang for a long time, but you will revive it.
This is the reason why Song Xianggong was defeated by Hong!
summary:
Dou Wu, a native of Fufeng, was known for his virtue and Confucian scholarship. He entered officialdom after his daughter became Empress to Emperor Huan, rising to Colonel of the City Gates. He was known for his integrity, recruiting worthy men, and refusing bribes. During a famine, he distributed his own rewards to students and the poor. He strictly disciplined his extravagant nephew, Dou Shao, even requesting his dismissal. When eunuchs seized power and arrested scholars like Li Ying and Du Mi in a party affair, Dou Wu memorialized the emperor, criticizing the eunuchs' corruption and warning of historical disasters like the fall of the Qin dynasty. He defended the arrested scholars and recommended virtuous ministers. After Emperor Huan died without an heir, Dou Wu consulted with an official and installed Liu Hong as Emperor Ling. He was made a general and marquis.

Dou Wu, along with Grand Tutor Chen Fan, planned to eliminate the eunuchs. Chen Fan urged immediate action, citing a solar eclipse as an omen. Dou Wu proposed the plan to the Empress Dowager, but she hesitated, citing tradition. After executing some eunuchs, Dou Wu's plan to kill others like Cao Jie stalled. When an astrological omen appeared, Dou Wu and Chen Fan prepared to act. They appointed allies to key posts and arrested a eunuch, whose confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu. However, a eunuch stole the memorial and alerted his colleagues. They falsely accused Dou Wu of treason to the young emperor, seized the Empress Dowager, and issued an edict for Dou Wu's arrest. Dou Wu refused to submit, rallied troops, but his soldiers were persuaded to defect by the imperial edict. Pursued, Dou Wu and his nephew committed suicide. Their clans were exterminated, and the Queen Mother was moved. Dou Wu's grandson, Dou Fu, was saved by a former student, Hu Teng, who hid him and later helped him establish a family.

He Jin, from Nanyang, rose to power after his half-sister became Empress to Emperor Ling. He was made a general to suppress the Yellow Turban rebellion and later a marquis. He and his brother He Miao defeated a rebellion of thieves. Emperor Ling established a new army with eight colonels, entrusting the eunuch Jian Shuo with overall command. Jian Shuo, fearing He Jin, plotted to send him away. When Emperor Ling died, Jian Shuo planned to kill He Jin and install Prince Xie as emperor, but He Jin was warned and avoided the trap. He Jin then made Prince Bian emperor, with the Empress Dowager as regent. He Jin, hating the eunuchs and Jian Shuo's plot, planned to eliminate them with Yuan Shao's support. However, the Empress Dowager refused, and He Jin's relatives, bribed by eunuchs, also opposed him.

He Jin hesitated, and Yuan Shao suggested summoning provincial generals like Dong Zhuo to threaten the court. Despite advice against this, He Jin agreed. The eunuchs, fearing for their lives, tricked their way back into the palace. When He Jin went to the palace to urge the Empress Dowager to act, the eunuchs ambushed and killed him. His subordinates then attacked the palace. Yuan Shao and others massacred the eunuchs, killing over two thousand. During the chaos, the eunuchs kidnapped the emperor and his brother, but were eventually killed. Dong Zhuo then deposed the emperor, killed the Empress Dowager, and the He family was destroyed, plunging the Han dynasty into chaos. The historian comments that both Dou Wu and He Jin, despite their power and favorable positions, were defeated by eunuchs due to a lack of wisdom and excessive reliance on power.

translation:
◆Dou Rong's Biography: Dou Rong's courtesy name was Duke of Zhou, and he was a native of Pingling County, Fufeng County.
Dou Guangguo, the seventh generation ancestor, was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen and was named Zhang Wuhou.
His great-great-grandfather moved from Changshan with two thousand stones as an official during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
Dou Rong has been an orphan since he was a child.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he was the Sima of Wang Jun, the strong crossbow general. He attacked Zhaiyi in the east and Huaili. He was named Jianwu Nan for his military merits.
The younger sister is the younger wife of the great Sikong Wangyi.
He lived in Chang'an, visited noble families, made friends with local heroes, and was famous for his chivalry and righteousness. However, he served his mother and elder brother and raised his weak younger brother, practicing benevolence and righteousness.
In the last years of Wang Mang, bandits broke out in Qingzhou and Xuzhou. Wang Kuang, the Grand Master, asked Dou Rong to help the army and join him in the eastern expedition.
When the Han army rose, Dou Rong was defeated by Wang Yi at Kunyangxia and returned to Chang'an.
When the Han army commander entered the pass, Wang Yi recommended Dou Rong as General Bo Shui, rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold, and led his troops to Xinfeng.
When Wang Mang was defeated, Dou Rong led his army and surrendered to Zhao Meng, the commander-in-chief of Gengshi. Zhao Meng regarded Dou Rong as a school captain and thought highly of him. He recommended Dou Rong to be the prefect of Julu.
When Dou Rong saw the new establishment and the chaos in the east, he didn't want to leave the country. He remembered that his great-great-grandfather was the governor of Zhangye, his grandfather was the captain of the Qiang Guard, and his younger brother was the governor of Wuwei. They had been in Hexi for several generations and knew the local customs, so he said to his brothers alone: The safety of the world is still unknown. Hexi is rich and fertile, and the Yellow River is very strong. Zhangye's vassal state has thousands of elite soldiers and cavalry. In the event of an emergency, it will be enough to defend itself by eliminating the crossing of the Yellow River. This is a good place for us to leave to our descendants.
The brothers all agreed. Dou Rong asked to see Zhao Meng that day, resigned as Julu governor, and asked to go to Hexi.
Zhao Meng told Gengshi, and he became the captain of Zhangye's vassal state.
Dou Rong was so happy that he took his family to the northwest.
When he arrived in Zhangye, he made friends with local heroes and lived in harmony with the ethnic minorities. He was very popular with the people from all over the world, and Hexi quickly surrendered to him.
At this time, Liang Tong, the prefect of Jiuquan, Shejun, the prefect of Jincheng, Shi Bao, the captain of Zhangye, Zhu Zeng, the captain of Jiuquan, Xin Xu, the captain of Dunhuang, and all the heroes of the prefectures and counties, Dou Rong treated them kindly.
When Gengshi failed, Dou Rong and Liang Tong discussed the situation and said: "Today there is chaos in the world, I don't know what the outcome will be."
Hexi is in a dangerous position between Qiang and Hu. Without concerted efforts, we cannot defend ourselves. The power is generally great, and there is no leader.
One person should be elected as a general to ensure the security of the five counties and observe changes in the current situation. After deliberation, it was decided that Dou Rong should be the general of the five counties in Hexi.
At this time, Ma Qi, the governor of Wuwei, and Ren Zhong, the governor of Zhangye, were both isolated and had no party members, so they jointly informed them in letters, and they took off their seals and resigned.
So Liang Tong was appointed as the prefect of Wuwei, Shi Bao as the prefect of Zhangye, Zhu Zeng as the prefect of Jiuquan, Xin Xu as the prefect of Dunhuang, and Shengou as the prefect of Jincheng.
Dou Rong still lives in the vassal state, and his concurrent post as captain remains unchanged, and he is assigned to supervise the five counties.
The folk customs in Hexi are simple, and the politics of Dou Rong and others are also tolerant. They are friendly to each other, and they are safe and prosperous.
He repaired his troops and horses, practiced archery, and sounded the beacon fire alarm at the border. When Qiang and barbarians invaded the border fortress, Dou Rong often led his troops to rescue the troops together with the counties. He always arrived as scheduled and often defeated the invaders.
Later, the Huns also learned their lesson and rarely invaded again. The Qiang and Hu who were attached to the fortress were frightened by their relatives, and the homeless people who suffered from starvation in Anding, Beidi, Shangjun and other places came back in an endless stream.
When Dou Rong and others heard that Guangwu had ascended the throne, they wanted to go east to Luoyang, because the river and the west were far apart and could not be reached by themselves.
At this time, Wei Xiao first took the title of Jianwu, Dou Rong and others accepted Zhengshuo, and Wei Xiao all pretended to be his general's seal and ribbon.
Kuai Xiao looked obedient to others but harbored dissatisfaction inside. He sent the debater Yong Lian to lobby Hexi and said: Gengshi became emperor and soon fell into ruin. This is the result of a surname that cannot be revived.
Now if you identify a master and establish a relationship of dependence with him, once you are controlled by him, the power in your hands will be lost. If you encounter danger in the future, you will regret it.
Now the heroes are competing, and the outcome is undecided. They should each occupy their territory and join forces with Long and Shu. If you are high, you can become the king of a country like the Six Kingdoms, and if you are low, you can be a captain of the South China Sea like Zhao Tuo. Dou Rong summoned the heroes and prefects to discuss the matter together. The brave and wise among them all said: The Han Dynasty inherited the lineage of Yao and cultivated it for a long time.
Now the emperor's surname is found in the Hetu Chifu Fu Book. Since the ancient Taoist scholars Gu Ziyun and Xia Heliang have revealed that the Han Dynasty will receive the talisman again, it has been said a long time ago, so Liu Zijun changed his name to Liu Xiu in the hope that the talisman will be fulfilled.
In Wang Mang's last years, the Taoist priest Ximen Junhui said that Liu Xiu should be the emperor, so he prepared to establish Liu Zijun.
After the incident was discovered, Liu Zijun was killed. The people watching said: Liu Xiu is really your master.
This was exposed not long ago and is common to all wise people.
Let’s not talk about destiny, but let’s comment on human affairs: there are countless people who are now emperors, and Luoyang has the largest land, the strongest armored soldiers, and the clearest orders.
Observing fortune and personnel, he is probably incompetent for the position of emperor. The prefects of various counties each had guests, some of whom were in favor and some who were against it.
Dou Rong made a detailed comparative analysis and decided to go eastward.
In the summer of the fifth year, Liu Jun, the commander-in-chief, was sent to present a letter and horses to Guangwu.
First, the emperor heard that Hexi was complete and wealthy, bordering Long and Shu. He often wanted to recruit Dou Rong to force Kaixiao and Gongsun Shu, so he sent an envoy to write to Dou Rong. He happened to meet Liu Jun on the road, so they returned together.
The emperor was very happy to see Liu Jun, received him very politely, and asked him to go back. He gave Dou Rong a seal saying: The imperial edict is to act as the general of the five counties in Hexi Province in military affairs and the capital of the country. I wish you to guard the five frontier counties with strong soldiers and horses, abundant warehouses, and rich people. You have defeated the Qiang and Hu invasions externally, and enabled the people to live a happy life internally.
I heard about the mighty virtue, and I looked at it humbly, but the road was blocked, which made me despair!
I have received all the books and horses presented by Chang Shi, and I am fully aware of your kindness.
Today there is Gongzi Yang in Yizhou, and General Wei in Tianshui. Shu and Han are attacking each other, and the power lies in the hands of the general. You can see the importance by making a move.
From this point of view, is there a limit to a close relationship?
Everything has been seen by the long history and known by the general.
The rise of kings is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
If you want to establish the cause of Qi Huan, Jin Wen, and assist the small country, you should work hard to complete the assisting work; if you want to make three tripods, connecting horizontally and vertically, you should also depend on the time.
There is no unity in the world. You and I are not in the same region, and we are not countries annexing each other.
The current deliberation must have Ren Xiao follow Zhao Tuo's plan to control the seven counties.
The king divides the land but does not divide the people. He just handles his own affairs well.
Now I will give the general two hundred pounds of gold. Please write to me if you have time. So Dou Rong was appointed as the pastor of Liangzhou.
As soon as the seal arrived, everyone in Hexi was shocked, thinking that the emperor had seen it thousands of miles away and was trying to catch Zhang Li's feelings.
Dou Rong then sent Liu Jun to write a letter saying: Dou Rong secretly thought to himself that he was lucky enough to entrust the last relative of the late emperor to be favored as a relative, and he was given two thousand stones from generation to generation.
In my generation, he was also appointed as a captain, pretending to be a general, guarding the northwest corner.
It is easy to say that if you are entrusted to the county, it will be easy to make efforts if you are loyal to the king.
Letters are not enough to express sincerity, so Liu Jun is sent to express his sincerity to you verbally.
I showed everything inside and out, hiding nothing.
However, the seal book is said to be the two masters of Shu and Han, with three-thirds of power. Ren Xiao and Wei Tuo's plans make me sad.
Although I, Dou Rong, have no knowledge, I still know the difference between good and bad, good and bad.
How can we betray the true and old master and serve the traitor and hypocrite? Abandon the loyalty and loyalty, and go against the grain to overthrow the country. Abandon the established foundation and seek hopeless profits.
Although these three people are asking a crazy man, they still know where to go, but why do I, Dou Rongdu, care about it!
I would like to send my half-brother Dou You to Beijing to verbally explain my mere intentions. When Dou You arrived at Gaoping, Kuai Xiao rebelled and the road was blocked, so he had to return and sent Sima Xifeng to Luoyang via the trail to submit a letter.
The emperor again sent a banquet to the brothers Dou Rong and Dou You, and was very considerate in comforting and encouraging them.
Since Dou Rong was well aware of the emperor's intention, he wrote to Kai Xiao to rebuke him, saying: The general makes the country rich and the government cultivates, and the soldiers embrace it.
In a time when his family was in danger and the country was unfavorable, the general kept his integrity and served his dynasty, and his eldest son, Kai Xun, committed himself to the country. His undoubted sincerity can be seen here.
This is why Dou Rong and others readily admire the general's noble loyalty and are willing to serve him.
Later, out of temporary personal anger, the general changed his temper and planned another big event, and the emperor and his ministers fought with each other.
It would be a pity to abandon the achievements that have been achieved and create new ones that are difficult to achieve, betray the righteousness of Shandong, and plan to connect with Western Shu. The accumulated achievements of hundreds of years are destroyed once!
Is it because the people below you are greedy for credit and offer tricks that lead to this? Rong really feels sorry for it!
Today, Xizhou's terrain is cramped and its troops are scattered. It is easy to assist others but difficult to create a situation on your own.
If you don't turn back after taking the wrong path, and are still confused after hearing the truth, you will either be annexed by Gongsun Shu in the south, or you will have to join Lu Fang's group in the north. Relying on false friendship to defeat a strong opponent, relying on distant rescue and despising the powerful enemy in front of you, there is no benefit.
Rong heard that wise people do not harm others to do things, and benevolent people do not create loyalty to achieve merit.
Now, if we have a small enemy but a big one, what can we say about the safety of everyone?
What does it say about your son's righteousness if you abandon your son for meritorious service?
Moreover, when you were a minister of this dynasty and bowed to the north, you were loyal to your ministers.
Later, he sent his son to the court and said goodbye with tears, which was the kindness of a loving father.
How will the officials think of you if you throw away all the kindness of a loyal minister and a loving father?
If you have the heart to abandon your flesh and blood, how will I miss you if you call me Liuzi?
Since the beginning of the army, attacks have turned around, and the entire city has been reduced to ruins, and many people have died in the ravines. Those who survive today are either those who escaped from the knife gap, or are singles in exile.
Up to now, the injured body has not recovered, and the sound of crying is still wailing in my ears.
Fortunately, destiny has eased a little bit, but the general is going to have another disaster. This is to prevent the long-sick people from recovering, and to make the young orphans suffer from the pain of being homeless again. This is grief, especially pity and heartache, and it makes people's noses sore!
If a mediocre person can't bear it, how much more can a benevolent person do?
It is easy to blend hearing and hearing into loyalty, but it is really difficult to be loyal appropriately.
Worrying too much for others will inevitably lead to resentment based on good deeds. I know that I will offend the general with my words.
It's just a tribute, I hope the general will realize it.
Wei Xiao refused, so Dou Rong and the governor of the five counties strengthened their troops and asked Shangshu for the date of departure.
The emperor admired Dou Rong's actions very much, and gave Dou Rong a picture of his subordinates and Tai Shigong's "Five Sects", "Family of Foreign Relatives", and "Biography of Wei Qihou".
The edict reported: "Every time I remember my relatives, Emperor Xiaojing comes from the Dou family, Prince Ding, the son of Emperor Jing, and is my ancestor."
In the past, due to Wei Qi's words, the orthodoxy was inherited. The eldest king and the young king respected their masters and cultivated good virtues, which were extended to their descendants. This is the spirit of the empress dowager. God bless the Han Dynasty.
People from Tianshui wrote a letter from the general instructing Wei Xiao, which was painful to the bones.
When the traitor sees it, he or she will feel ashamed, the loyal minister will feel sore and runny when he sees it, and the righteous will be bright-eyed when he sees it. How can this be done if it is not loyalty, filial piety and sincerity?
How can a person with poor moral character endure this!
Kuai Xiao knew that without the help of Hexi, the disaster of annihilation of the clan was coming, so he wanted to sow discord and spread rumors to confuse the people, so as to explain the conspiracy and make him treacherous.
In addition, all the officials in the capital did not understand the true intentions of the country and the generals, so they often resorted to hypocrisy, exaggerated nonsense, disappointed loyalty and filial piety, and made rumors untrue.
Reputation and reputation are not accidental and must be considered.
Now that the thieves in Guandong have been pacified, the entire army should now head west. The general invites fresh horses and strong troops to wait for the rendezvous. After Dou Rong received the edict, he led his troops into Jincheng with the governors.
At first, during the Gengshi period, Xianling Qiang Feng He Zhuzhong killed the prefect of Jincheng and occupied Jincheng. Kuai Xiao sent envoys to bribe Feng He and form an alliance with him, preparing to use his tribe.
Dou Rong and others therefore sent troops to attack Fenghe, defeated his army, beheaded more than a thousand people, obtained tens of thousands of cattle, horses and sheep, and tens of thousands of grains, so they showed off their power according to the Yellow River, waiting for the arrival of Guangwu.
Later, because the soldiers did not advance, Dou Rong returned.
The emperor further rewarded Dou Rong for doing what he said, and ordered You Fufeng to repair Dou Rong's father's tomb and use a large prison to worship him.
He sent Qingqi back and forth several times and presented delicious food to all directions. Liang Tong ordered someone to assassinate Zhang Xuan, so he was cut off from Kai Xiao, and both of them took off their fake general seals.
In the summer of the seventh year, Zhu Zeng, the prefect of Jiuquan, left the county because his younger brother had committed murder. Dou Rong followed the emperor's wishes and worshiped Zeng Zhu as General Wu Feng, and replaced Zhu Zeng with Xin Wen as the prefect of Jiuquan.
In autumn, Wei Xiao sent troops to invade Anding. The emperor was preparing to personally march westward, so he first warned Dou Rong about the date of sending troops.
It happened to be raining, the road was blocked, and Kaixiao's soldiers had retreated, so they stopped.
Dou Rong arrived in Guzang and was ordered to leave.
Dou Rong was afraid that the troops would be delayed for a long time, so he wrote a letter saying: "Kai Xiao heard that you will lead the army to the west. Dou Rong sent troops to the east. The soldiers were in a commotion and decided not to resist."
Weixiao general Gao Jun and others wanted to welcome the army. Later, they heard that the army had retreated, and Gao Jun and others became suspicious again.
Wei Xiao threatened that there was a change in the east, so the heroes of Xizhou went to join Wei Xiao. Wei Xiao also invited General Gongsun Shu and ordered them to guard the city gate.
Dou Rong is lonely and weak, between Long and Shu. Although His Majesty has the power and spirit, he must be rescued as soon as possible.
The country is in front, and Dou Rong's troops are behind him. The priorities are intertwined, and the head and tail are taking care of each other. Wei Xiao is in a tight situation and cannot advance or retreat, so he will definitely be defeated.
If the army does not advance early and suspicions arise for a long time, then the foreign minister will be jealous and internally distressed and weak, and the slanderous evil will have an opportunity to take advantage of it. I am really worried, and I ask for your mercy.
The emperor expressed his deep praise.
In the summer of the eighth year, Guangwu personally marched westward to Kaihuo. Dou Rong led the five prefects, the Qiang captives, the Xiaoyue clan, etc., with tens of thousands of troops on foot and more than 5,000 vehicles of baggage. They met with the army at the first city of Gaoping. Dou Rong first sent an envoy to ask about the etiquette of the meeting. At this time, the army was changing, and the generals were on the wrong side of the road with the three princes, and some were whispering behind the back of the envoy.
The emperor was very happy when he heard that Dou Rong asked about etiquette first, so he announced it to all officials.
So a grand banquet was held and Dou Rong and others were introduced and treated with special etiquette.
He worshiped his younger brother Dou You as the captain of Fengche, and his younger brother Dou Shi as the doctor of Taizhong.
So they marched together, and the Kuihuo tribe was defeated, and all the cities surrendered.
In recognition of Dou Rong's meritorious service, the emperor issued an edict to confer Dou Rong as the Marquis of Anfeng in the four counties of Anfeng, Yangquan, Liao and Anfeng, and his younger brother Dou You as the Xianqinhou.
He named the generals in turn: General Zhu Zeng of Wufeng was the Marquis of Zhuyi, Wuwei Prefect Liang Tong was the Marquis of Chengyi, Zhangye Prefect Shi Bao was the Marquis of Baoyi, Jincheng Prefect Shejun was the Marquis of Fuyi, and Jiuquan Prefect Xin Xu was the Marquis of Fuyi.
After the knighthood was completed, Guangwu returned to the east and sent Dou Rong and other officials to the west to control Fuyuan County.
Dou Rong received a title as his brother and had been in the northwest for a long time. He was afraid and couldn't calm down. He wrote several times to ask for someone to replace him.
The edict replied: "The general and I are like right and left hands. You have asked to abdicate several times. Why are you not satisfied?"
I hope you will encourage the religious people not to leave the army without permission.
When Long and Shu were pacified, Dou Rong and the five prefects were ordered to come to the capital to report. They were accompanied by officials and guests, more than a thousand cars, and horses, cattle, and sheep everywhere.
Dou Rong arrived at the gate of Luoyang City and presented the seals and ribbons of the Mu of Liangzhou, the Captain of Zhangye County, and the Marquis of Anfeng. The emperor ordered the envoys to return the seals and ribbons of the Marquis.
After the introduction, he was given the title of prince, and he was given more favors and favors, which moved the capital.
A few months later, he was promoted to Jizhou Mu, and after more than ten days, he was promoted to Da Sikong.
Dou Rong thought that he was not an old minister. Once he entered the court, he would be ranked above the meritorious ministers. Every time he came to the meeting, his appearance and tone of voice were extremely humble, so the emperor became closer to him and loved him more.
Dou Rong was cautious and could not keep himself at ease. He resigned his title several times and asked Jin Qian, his servant, to convey his sincerity.
Another Shangshu said: Dou Rong was fifty-three years old and had a son who was fifteen years old and had a naughty and blunt character. Rong taught him the arts day and night, and did not allow him to watch astronomy or read prophecies. The purpose was to make him respectful, serious, not trouble-free, and able to follow the rules and follow the right path. He did not want him to have talents, let alone pass him to Liancheng Guangshi, so that he could enjoy the special treatment of the princes and kingdoms? So he once again asked to see him at his leisure, but the emperor refused.
Later, after the court affairs were over, Dou Rong carefully retreated to his seat. The emperor knew that Dou Rong wanted to resign again, so he ordered him to pass out.
When we meet tomorrow, we welcome Dou Rong and say: A few days ago, the official wanted to resign and return to his hometown, so I asked you to go home and rest on your own in the hot summer.
When we meet today, it is appropriate to discuss other matters and not talk about resignation. Dou Rong therefore did not dare to submit any further invitations.
In the 20th year, the great Situ Daishe was imprisoned for stealing gold by someone he recommended. The emperor asked the three ministers to participate in the ministry, so he had to avoid being suspected and resigned from the post of Dou Rong, the great minister.
In the second year, extra seats were added.
In the twenty-third year, Dai Yin Xingxing was engaged in the work of Weiwei, and he continued to advance as before, and he also led generals as great craftsmen.
His younger brother Dou You is the captain of the city gate school, and his brothers are also in charge of the forbidden troops.
Dou Rong once again asked to resign and return to his hometown. The emperor often rewarded him with money and silk, and the eunuch in charge of the royal diet often sent rare foods.
After Dou's friend died, the emperor took pity on Dou Rong's old age and frailty, and sent his regular attendants and ministers to Dou Rong's bedroom to force him to drink and eat.
Dou Rong's eldest son, Dou Mu, married Princess Neihuang and became the city gate captain on behalf of Dou You.
Dou Mu's son Dou Xun married Princess Pubiyang, the strong daughter of King Gong of the East China Sea, and Dou You's son Dou Gu also married Princess Nieyang, the daughter of Guangwu.
Xianzong ascended the throne and appointed Dou Lin, the son of Dou Rong's elder brother, as the Colonel Protecting Qiang. The Dou family has the special favor of one prince, two princes, three princesses, and four or two thousand stones, all at the same time.
From ancestors to grandsons, they have lived in the official residence of the capital and have thousands of slaves and maids. Among the many relatives and heroes, no one can compare with him.
In the second year of Yongping, Dou Lin, the son of Dou Rong's brother, was killed for committing a crime.
The emperor then issued several edicts to censure Dou Rong, citing the historical fact that Dou Ying and Tian Chong were responsible for the defeat.
Dou Rong was frightened and asked to return to his hometown, so he ordered him to return to his mansion to recuperate.
When he was more than a year old, he received Dou Rong's seal and ribbon from the imperial guard, and was given cattle and bottles of wine.
Dou Rong had been in Suwei for more than ten years. He was getting old, and his descendants were indulgent and lawless.
Dou Mu and others interacted with some frivolous people, and they were entrusted to the county to interfere with political affairs.
Because he was enfeoffed in Anfeng and wanted all his in-laws to occupy the original Liu'an kingdom, he asked the Queen Mother of Yin to order Liu Xu, the Marquis of Liu'an, to divorce his wife and marry his daughter to Liu Xu.
In the fifth year, Liu Xu was abandoned and his wife's family wrote a letter to report the situation. The emperor was furious and dismissed Dou Mu and others from their official positions. All the ministers in Dou took their families back to their hometowns in the countryside. Only Dou Rong stayed in the capital.
Dou Mu and others went west to Hangu Pass, and there was an imperial edict to recover them all.
When Dou Rong died at the age of seventy-eight, he was given the posthumous title of Marquis of Dai. He sent a lot of money to help with the funeral.
The emperor thought that Dou Mu could not cultivate himself and had a lot of wealth, so he often ordered Ye to guard his family alone.
The audience reported that Dou Mu and his son had complained several times since they lost power, and the emperor ordered him to take his family back to the original county. Only Dou Xun, the son-in-law of Princess Biyang, was able to stay in the capital.
Dou Mu was arrested and brought to justice by the county for bribing minor officials. Both Dou Mu and his son Dou Xuan died in Pingling Prison, and Dou Xun also died in Luoyang Prison.
A long time later, the imperial edict was issued to bring back Mrs. Dou Jia and a young grandson to their residence in Luoyang.
In the fourteenth year, Dou Rong, Dou Xun's younger brother, was granted the title of Marquis of Anfeng, with a settlement of 2,000 households, and was succeeded by Dou Rong's descendants.
At the beginning of Emperor He's reign, he was the Shaofu.
When Dou Xunzi, General Dou Xian was killed, he was spared from the country.
Dou Jia died and was succeeded by his son Dou Wanquan.
After Wanquan died, his son Huizong succeeded him.
Dou Wu, a disciple of Dou Wanquan, has a unique legend.
The historian commented: Dou Rong began to be known as a heroic hero, standing tall in the dust, and then emerged from the prince's position during the break, and finally won the title of minister. This is really a man who has a tendency to achieve merit.
When his title is high and perfect, he can put aside his power and favors, fearing as if he has no choice. How smart is this!
I once savored this man's demeanor in detail. Although his talents in the latitude and longitude of the country are not enough to talk about, the etiquette of advancing and retreating is worth talking about.
summary:
Dou Rong, courtesy name Duke of Zhou, was from Pingling County, Fufeng. His seventh-generation ancestor Dou Guangguo was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen. Orphaned young, he served as Sima under Wang Jun during Wang Mang's reign, earning the title Jianwu Nan for military merit. He was known for chivalry and filial piety, caring for his mother, elder brother, and younger sibling.

During the chaos at the end of Wang Mang's rule, Dou Rong initially served under Wang Yi but later surrendered to Gengshi's general Zhao Meng. Seeking stability, he requested and received the position of Captain of Zhangye's Vassal State, moving his family to Hexi. There, he befriended local heroes, harmonized with ethnic minorities, and gained widespread support. After Gengshi's fall, Dou Rong was elected General of the Five Counties in Hexi, overseeing a peaceful and prosperous region with tolerant governance and strong defenses against Qiang and Hu invasions.

When Guangwu ascended the throne, Dou Rong considered allegiance but was courted by Wei Xiao, who urged independence. After consulting with local leaders, Dou Rong decided to support Guangwu, citing prophecies and the strength of Luoyang. He sent an envoy with gifts, and Guangwu responded by appointing him General of the Five Counties and later Liangzhou Mu. Dou Rong rebuffed Wei Xiao's attempts at alliance, writing letters to persuade him to submit, but Wei Xiao refused. Dou Rong then prepared for military action against Wei Xiao.

Dou Rong joined Guangwu's campaign against Wei Xiao, leading troops from five counties. After Wei Xiao's defeat, Dou Rong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfeng. Despite his high rank, he remained humble and repeatedly sought to resign, but Guangwu refused. His family became powerful, with multiple marriages to royalty, but later fell from grace due to misconduct. Dou Rong died at seventy-eight, posthumously honored as Marquis of Dai. His descendants continued, though some faced imprisonment and loss of titles.

The historian comments that Dou Rong rose from obscurity to high office through merit, wisely yielding power when at his peak. While not a great strategist, his conduct in advancing and retreating was exemplary.

◆Biography of the Eight Kings of Emperor Zhang, Emperor Xiaozhang’s eight sons: Song Gui was born as Xiao Wang Liu Qing of Qinghe, Liang Gui was born as Emperor Liu Zhao, Shen Gui was born as King Hui of Jibei Liu Shou, and King Xiao of Hejian Liu Kai. The other four kings do not remember their mother's name.
Liu and his wife, the king of Qianchengzhen, were granted the title in the fourth year of Jianchu.
Emperor He ascended the throne. Because Liu and his wife were the eldest brothers, they respected him very much and treated him with courtesy. He died in the fifteenth year of his life.
His son Liu Chong succeeded to the throne. Liu Chong was named Fu Hu.
In the seventh year of Yongyuan, the country was renamed Le'an.
He died in the twenty-eighth year of his reign and became the king of Yi.
Both father and son died in the capital and were buried in Luoyang.
His son Liu Hong succeeded to the throne. Emperor An Liu Hu passed away before he left for his country.
Liu Hong gave birth to Emperor Liu Zan. After Emperor Zhi was established, the Empress Dowager of Liang issued an edict, believing that the land of Le'an was despicable and humid, and there were too few rents and taxes, so she changed the title of Liu Hongbo to King of Hai.
He died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign and was named King Xiao.
Prince Xiao had no children, so the Empress Dowager made Emperor Huan Liu Zhi's younger brother Liwuhou Liu Kui the King of Bohai to serve Liu Hong's sacrifices.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, Liu Kui conspired and the relevant officials requested that Liu Kui be deposed. Emperor Zhi could not bear to depose him, so he demoted him to the title of King Ying Tao and had to pay the tax of a county.
Later, Liu Kui wanted to rely on Wang Fu, the official official of Zhongchang, to restore his feudal state, and promised to give him 50 million yuan as a gift to thank him.
Emperor Zhi was about to die and issued an edict to restore Liu Kui to the throne of Bohai.
Liu Kui knew that it was not Wang Fu's credit, so he refused to thank Wang Fu for the money.
Wang Fu became angry and secretly collected Liu Kui's crimes.
At first, when the Ling Emperor Liu Hong was proclaimed, there were rumors on the road that Liu Kui did not establish himself as emperor, but held a grudge and wanted to seize the conscription documents by force. Both Zhong Chang Shi Zheng Sa and Zhong Huangmen Dong Teng had the courage to associate righteousness with the strong and light men, and colluded with Liu Kui many times.
Wang Fu conducted reconnaissance and thought there must be a conspiracy, so he secretly reported it to Duan Zhen, the captain of Sili School.
In the first year of Xiping, Zheng Sa was arrested and sent to Beisi Prison.
The minister ordered Lian Zhong to submit a report to slander Zheng Sa and other plots to welcome Liu Kui, which was a treasonous act.
So he ordered the governor of Jizhou to arrest Liu Kui and question him about the implementation. He also sent Dahong Zhijie, Zongzheng and Tingwei to Bohai to force Liu Kui to denounce him, and Liu Kui committed suicide.
Eleven concubines, seventy children, and twenty-four prostitutes all died in prison.
Fu, Prime Minister and below were all executed for the crime of disloyalty by leading King Bohai Liu Kui.
In the twenty-fifth year of Liu Kui's reign, the feudal state was removed.
The people all sympathized with him.
In Pingchun, King Liu Quan was mourned, and he was granted the title in the fourth year of Jianchu. He died that year and was buried in the capital.
Having no children, the feudal state was removed.
Liu Qing, the Xiaowang of Qinghe, whose mother was a noblewoman of the Song Dynasty.
Guiren, the eighth grandson of Song Chang, was born in Pingling County, Fufeng County.

summary:
The lives and fates of Emperor Zhang's eight sons, focusing on the lineages of several kings. Liu Qing, King Xiao of Qinghe, was born to Noble Consort Song. His mother and aunt were favored by Emperor Zhang but were framed by Empress Dou after the death of Empress Dowager Ma, leading to their forced suicide. Liu Qing was deposed as crown prince in favor of his half-brother Liu Zhao (Emperor He). Despite this, Liu Qing maintained a close and respectful relationship with Emperor He, who treated him with great favor and trust. Liu Qing was known for his filial piety, caution, and grief over his mother's unjust death, often making private sacrifices. He died at age 29 and was buried in Guangqiu. His son Liu Hu succeeded him but died without heirs, leading to the appointment of Liu Yanping, son of Liu Chong, as King of Qinghe. Later, Liu Qing was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaode, and his mother as Empress Jingyin.

Liu Shou, King Hui of Jibei, was born to Noble Consort Shen. He was granted his kingdom in the second year of Yongyuan. Emperor He, following his father's customs, kept his brothers in the capital, and they were very close. Liu Shou died after 31 years as king. His descendants included Liu Deng, Liu Duo (who died without sons), and Liu Anguo, who was appointed king. Liu Ci, son of Liu Anguo, was noted for his extreme filial piety during his father's mourning, for which Empress Dowager Liang granted him an additional 5,000 households. The Jibei line ended when Liu Zheng died without sons in the eleventh year of Jian'an.

Liu Kai, King Xiao of Hejian, was granted his kingdom in the second year of Yongyuan. He was known for abiding by the law and was respected by his subordinates. He died after 42 years as king. His son Liu Zheng was arrogant and cruel but was reformed by the strict Prime Minister Shen Jing. Liu Zheng's descendants included Liu Jian, Liu Li, and Liu Ye, who was made Marquis of Chongde when Wei accepted the Han abdication. Liu Yi, a son of Liu Kai, was initially favored by Empress Dowager Deng but was later framed and demoted. He eventually became the father of Emperor Huan, who honored Liu Kai as Emperor Xiaomu. Liu Shu, another son of Liu Kai, was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan by his son, Emperor Ling.

The text also briefly mentions other sons of Emperor Zhang: Liu Quan, King of Qiancheng, who died without heirs; Liu Shu, King Huai of Chengyang, who died without children; Liu Wansui, King Ai of Guangzong, who died the same year he was enfeoffed; and Liu Sheng, King Huai of Pingyuan, who died young without heirs. The historian's commentary notes that the descendants of Emperor Zhang, known for their virtue and honesty, became the rulers of the Han dynasty, fulfilling an ancient saying.

When I returned home, I didn't say anything, but I raised my head and sighed. No one knew how wronged I was, and no one dared to disobey His Majesty.
What I am saying now is indeed that I will die without regrets. The emperor understood what he meant and issued an edict asking Hanlang to go out.

He was also promoted as Xiaolian.
