During the Yongyuan period, he was promoted to the prefect of Qinghe, but was dismissed for violating the law.
In the third year of Yongchu's reign, Taiwei Zhang Yu recommended Han Lang as a doctor and conquered the public carriage. He met Han Lang and died at the age of eighty-four.
summary:
Fifth Lun, courtesy name Boyu, was from Changling, Jingzhao, descended from the Tian clan of Qi. Upright from youth, he built fortresses during Wang Mang's era to defend against bandits like Bronze Horse and Red Eyebrow, successfully repelling attacks. He served under Yin Xianyu Bao, who recognized his talent, and later became a village official, gaining popularity through fair tax collection and dispute mediation. He moved to Hedong, changed his name to Wang Boqi, and worked as a salt carrier. Recommended by Xianyu Bao, he became chief bookkeeper under Jingzhao Yin Yanxing, where he rectified market scales and coins, earning public trust. Promoted to Xiaolian in 51 CE, he served as chief medical officer for Huaiyang State. Emperor Guangwu, impressed by his governance insights, appointed him governor of Fuyi, then Kuaiji. In Kuaiji, he banned superstitious cattle sacrifices and witch fraud, restoring order. Transferred in 62 CE for legal violations, he was pursued by weeping locals. After release, he farmed privately until appointed magistrate of Danqu County, then governor of Shu Commandery, where he dismissed corrupt officials and promoted virtuous ones, ending bribery. As Sikong under Suzong, he warned against the power of Empress Dowager Mingde's Ma relatives, citing their lavish gifts and potential corruption. He also opposed Ma Fang's Western Qiang campaign, fearing nepotism. Known for strictness but leniency, he criticized harsh governance, advocating for benevolent officials. He retired in 86 CE with honors and died over eighty, receiving imperial burial gifts.

Zhongli Yi, courtesy name Zi'a, from Shanyin, Kuaiji, began as a county governor. During a plague in 38 CE, he personally provided medicine to victims. Promoted to Xiaolian, he served under Grand Situ Hou Ba, showing compassion by arranging clothes for a sick disciple. As Xiaqiu magistrate, he privately forgave an official's theft, leading the thief's father to force his son's suicide. As Tangyi magistrate, he allowed a prisoner, Guang, to bury his mother, later securing his pardon. Under Xianzong, as minister, he refused tainted pearls from corrupt official Zhang Hui, earning imperial praise and a reward. He criticized the emperor's frequent hunts at Guangcheng Garden, urging frugality during a drought. He also defended a clerk's clerical error, taking blame himself. Known for bold remonstrance, he rescued ministers from punishment and advised leniency in governance. As prime minister of Lu for five years, he promoted moral education, dying in office. His final words urged gentle rule, and the emperor granted burial funds.

Song Jun, courtesy name Shuxiang, from Nanyang, became a doctor at fifteen via his father's appointment. Proficient in classics, he served as Chen Yang's assistant, establishing schools and banning improper sacrifices. He led 3,000 troops to rescue General Liu Shang but arrived after his death. With General Ma Yuan, he faced disease and blockades, so he forged an imperial edict to accept barbarian surrender, dispersing their forces. Emperor Guangwu pardoned his unauthorized action, rewarding him. As Shangcai magistrate, he refused to enforce strict funeral bans, prioritizing justice. As Jiujiang governor, he attributed tiger attacks to corrupt officials, removing traps and promoting virtue, causing tigers to leave. He ended a marriage sacrifice custom in Junqiu County. Promoted to prime minister of East China Sea, he was later dismissed but recalled due to public demand. As minister, he defended his principles against imperial anger, earning praise for his integrity. As Hanoi governor, he was beloved by the people. He retired due to illness, receiving honors. He advocated lenient governance, blaming harsh laws for social ills, and died in 76 CE.

Han Lang, courtesy name Boqi, from Xue, Lu, survived abandonment as an infant during chaos. A Confucian scholar, he taught *Shang Shu* and served as imperial censor during Yongping. In the Chu prison case, he investigated four marquises implicated by false confessions, finding no evidence. Despite imperial anger, he argued against mass accusations, warning of wrongful deaths. His plea led to the release of over a thousand prisoners. He later imprisoned himself after the accused died, but was amnestied. Under Suzong, he was appointed Yizhou magistrate, then Luoyang magistrate, resigning after his mother's death. In 87 CE, he was promoted to Situ Prefecture, then Qinghe governor, dismissed for legal violations. Recommended as a doctor in 109 CE, he died at eighty-four.

Being frightened, he died and hid in Rang.
A few years later, Ji Tui found it and merged with more than ten members of his family.

Geng Yan decided to make plans for Hebei and Nanyang, and he also saw that Guangwu's imperial career would be successful.

Geng Yan's subordinates Sun Cang and Wei Bao conspired to join Wang Lang, but Geng Yan rebuked them, calling Ziyu a deceitful thief. He went to Chang'an to explain the usefulness of troops from Yuyang and Shanggu, then traveled to Taiyuan and Daijun. Upon returning, he attacked with cavalry, but Sun and Wei refused and surrendered to Wang Lang. Hearing Guangwu was in Lunu, Geng Yan went north to meet him. Guangwu kept him as a subordinate, and Geng Yan persuaded him to send troops to pacify Handan. Guangwu praised his ambition.

Geng Yan followed Guangwu to Ji. When Handan soldiers approached, Guangwu planned to return south. Geng Yan advised against it, proposing to mobilize troops from Yuyang and Shanggu, which would make Handan easy to capture. Despite opposition, Guangwu appointed Geng Yan as his guide north. After a commotion in Ji, Geng Yan found his father Geng Kuang and persuaded him to join forces with Kou Xun and Peng Chong, each providing 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 infantry. Geng Yan, Jing Dan, and Kou Xun marched south, killing over 400 of Wang Lang's officials, capturing 125 seals, and beheading 30,000 people. They subdued 22 counties before meeting Guangwu at Guang'a. Guangwu was delighted and promoted them all.

Geng Yan and others attacked Handan. Gengshi Emperor summoned Zhao Yong, but Geng Kuang advised him to join Guangwu. When Zhang Ye rebelled with Xiongnu and Wuhuan aid, Guangwu sent Geng Yan's brother Geng Shu to defeat him. Gengshi, suspicious of Guangwu's growing power, sent envoys to make Guangwu King of Xiao and ordered him to stop fighting. Geng Yan advised Guangwu to ignore the order, warning of chaos under Gengshi and urging him to seize the world. Guangwu appointed Geng Yan as general to recruit troops from Youzhou. Geng Yan killed Gengshi's governors Wei Shun and Cai Chong, while Wu Han killed Miao Zeng. They led Youzhou's soldiers south, defeating multiple rebel groups. Geng Yan often led the vanguard.

Guangwu ascended the throne and made Geng Yan General Jianwei. In the second year of Jianwu, he was made Marquis of Haoju. In the third year, he defeated Yan Cen and Du Hong, capturing over 3,000 heads and 5,000 prisoners. In the fourth year, he was ordered to attack Yuyang but hesitated due to family ties. The emperor reassured him. Geng Yan later defeated mountain bandits and, with Wu Han, captured Fuping, causing 40,000 thieves to surrender. He then attacked Zhang Bu, using strategy to lure Fei Yi into battle, defeating him and capturing Juli. He took Linzi in half a day, isolating Xi'an. Zhang Bu attacked with 200,000 troops but was defeated twice. Geng Yan pursued him, and Zhang Bu surrendered. Geng Yan pacified the region, capturing 300 cities without defeat.

Geng Yan died at fifty-six, posthumously titled Minhou. His descendants served as generals and married into the imperial family. The historian commented that Geng Yan, like Han Xin, foresaw Guangwu's success. Though he achieved no new feats after conquering Qi, the Geng family's military legacy endured for generations, possibly because they used war to end killing.

Su Jing, courtesy name Bo Kuang, was a scholar from Pingling, Fufeng, proficient in the Book of Changes and skilled in drawing. During Wang Mang’s reign, he compiled books with Liu Xin and served as Lieutenant of Daijun, where he kept the northern frontier safe from Hunnic raids. Under Emperor Guangwu, he became Governor of Daijun and strengthened defenses against the Xiongnu. In the fifth year of Jianwu, Lu Fang plundered the north; Su Jing, gravely ill, handed his troops to his brother and went to the capital to apologize. He was appointed a servant but dismissed months later due to illness.

While in Nanyang, Su Jing wrote to Liu Gong, Liu Xin’s nephew, who served as an adviser to the bandit Deng Zhongkuang. He urged Liu Gong to abandon rebellion, citing historical examples like Zhiguo and Chen Ping, who wisely avoided harm. He argued that the Han dynasty, despite Wang Mang’s usurpation, was revived by Guangwu, and that celestial signs—such as irregular movements of Taibai and Yinghuo—foretold doom for rebels like Dong Xian and Peng Chong. He warned against following false prophecies and urged surrender, comparing Liu Gong’s potential choice to the virtuous actions of Duke Zhou’s uncle Kang and King Jibei Liu Zhi. Su Jing also wrote to Deng Zhongkuang, who eventually surrendered with Liu Gong. Su Jing died at home at age seventy, leaving writings like *Records of Teachings*.

Yang Hou, courtesy name Zhonghuan, was from Guanghan. His grandfather Yang Chunqing, skilled in prophecy, served Gongsun Shu but committed suicide after Han’s victory, instructing his son Yang Tong to study secret records. Yang Tong learned prophecy and astronomy, served as a magistrate, and prayed for rain during droughts. He wrote two volumes on prophecy and died at ninety. Yang Hou, his son, studied these arts. In Emperor An’s third year, when Taibai entered Beidou and Luoyang flooded, Yang Hou advised sending princes back to their states; the queen mother complied, and the omens ceased. He was appointed a middle man but dismissed after displeasing the queen mother with his prophecies. Later, he refused official posts, citing illness. In Emperor Shun’s reign, he predicted disasters like locust plagues and barbarian revolts, which occurred. He declined gifts from the powerful Liang Ji and retired to teach Huang-Lao arts to over 3,000 disciples. He died at eighty-two, posthumously named Wen Fu, with a temple built by his students.

Therefore, although Shengjiao has been abandoned in the imperial court, the custom of integrity is still preserved among the people.

**Xun Shu (Jihe)** was a native of Yingyin, Yingchuan County, and the eleventh-generation grandson of Xun Qing. From youth, he possessed noble virtues and profound knowledge, though he disliked detailed textual analysis and was looked down upon by vulgar scholars. During Emperor An's reign, he was recruited as a doctor and later promoted to Tu Chang, but resigned to return home. The famous sages Li Gu and Li Ying respected him as their teacher. When Empress Dowager Liang governed, Xun Shu was promoted to answer imperial questions, where he criticized the emperor's noble relatives and favored people. General Liang Ji, jealous of him, transferred him to serve as Marquis of Langling. Known for his upright governance, he was called the "divine king." He soon resigned and returned home, distributing family property among clan members. He died at sixty-seven in the third year of Jianhe. Li Ying mourned him for three years. Both counties built temples in his honor. Xun Shu had eight sons—Jian, Nian, Jing, Tao, Wang, Shuang, Su, and Zhuan—all famous, known as the "Eight Dragons." Their neighborhood was renamed Gaoyangli after the ancient Gaoyang family's eight talented members. Xun Jing, a virtuous man who refused office, died at fifty and was named Mr. Xuan Xing. Xun Shu's sons Xun Yu and Xun Tan both hated evil and sought to eradicate eunuchs, killing even minor offenders among eunuch branches. Xun Yu later died with General Dou Wu and Li Ying, while Xun Tan was imprisoned for life.

**Xun Shuang (Ciming)** was eager to learn from childhood, understanding "Spring and Autumn" and "The Analects" by age twelve. Taiwei Du Qiao praised him as capable of being a teacher. Xun Shuang delved deeply into the scriptures, ignoring village celebrations and funerals. In the ninth year of Yanxi, he was recommended as filial and incorruptible, becoming a doctor. In response to an imperial question, he discussed the Han Dynasty's virtue of fire, filial piety, and the importance of proper mourning rites. He criticized officials who failed to observe three-year mourning periods and advocated for correcting funeral etiquette. He also addressed the improper subordination of husbands to wives in marriage rituals, arguing it violated cosmic principles. He condemned the excessive number of palace women—five to six thousand—which drained the treasury and caused disasters, urging their release to restore harmony. He further criticized ministers who usurped imperial privileges in dress and luxury. After submitting his memorial, he abandoned his post. Later, due to conflicts with eunuchs, he lived in seclusion for over ten years, writing books and becoming a great Confucian. After the party ban was lifted, he was recruited multiple times but refused. When Yuan Feng died, Xun Shuang mourned him for three years, setting a custom. He later served under General He Jin and then Dong Zhuo, rising to Sikong within ninety-five days. Seeing Dong Zhuo's cruelty, he conspired with Wang Yun but died of illness at sixty-three. He wrote numerous works, including "Li," "Yizhuan," and "Hanyu," totaling over a hundred chapters, many now lost.

**Xun Yue (Zhongyu)** was the son of Xun Jian, who died early. At twelve, Xun Yue could explain "Spring and Autumn." Despite poverty and lack of books, he could recite most texts after reading them at others' homes. During Emperor Ling's reign, when eunuchs held power, he feigned illness and lived in seclusion. He later served under Cao Cao and became Minister of Huangmen. Emperor Xian, fond of literature, conversed with Xun Yue and Kong Rong daily. As political power shifted to Cao Cao, Xun Yue wrote five chapters of "Shenjian" on governance, emphasizing benevolence and righteousness. He identified four troubles—hypocrisy, selfishness, debauchery, and luxury—and five policies: promoting agriculture, distinguishing good from evil, spreading culture, establishing military force, and enforcing rewards and punishments. He also criticized the marriage system for placing women above men and advocated for historical recording. The emperor, finding Bangu's "Hanshu" too lengthy, ordered Xun Yue to write thirty chapters of "Han Ji" in the style of "Zuo Shi Zhuan." Xun Yue's work was concise yet detailed. He also wrote "Chongde" and "Zhenglun." He died in the fourteenth year of Jian'an at age sixty-two.

**Han Shao (Zhonghuang)** was from Wuyang County, Yingchuan. He served as a county official and was recruited into the Situ Mansion. When Taishan bandit Gongsun Ju caused trouble, Han Shao was appointed county magistrate. The bandits, hearing of his reputation, avoided Ying County, but other counties suffered. Many fled to Ying County, and Han Shao opened granaries to feed over 10,000 families, despite objections from supervisors. He died in office. Li Ying, Chen Chen, Du Mi, and Xun Shu erected monuments praising him. His son Han Rong became a servant under Emperor Xian and died at seventy.

**Zhong Hao (Ji Ming)** was from Changshe County, Yingchuan, from a family proficient in law. Praised for honesty, he lived in seclusion teaching poetry to over a thousand students. He befriended Chen Chen and served as the county's meritorious officer. Recruited nine times by the government, he never accepted. Both Zhong Hao and Xun Shu were admired by scholar-bureaucrats. Li Ying said Xun Shu's knowledge was hard to match, but Zhong Hao's virtue could be a teacher's example. Zhong Hao's nephew Zhong Jin married Li Ying's sister. Zhong Hao died at sixty-nine at home. Confucian scholars praised his virtue. His grandson Zhong Yao became Sili Xiaowei.

**Chen Chen (Zhonggong)** was from Xu County, Yingchuan, of humble origin. From childhood, he was respected by peers. He served as a county official and studied at Taixue. When falsely accused of murder, he was tortured but released. Later, as postal supervisor, he treated his accuser with courtesy, earning admiration. As a meritorious officer, he refused to appoint an unsuitable candidate recommended by eunuch Hou Lan, taking the blame himself. He served as Chief of Taiqiu, governing with virtue and quietness. During the party arrests, he willingly imprisoned himself. He mourned for Zhang Rang's father, later saving many lives during renewed party persecutions. In his village, he settled disputes fairly. When a thief entered his home, he admonished him and gave him silk, ending burglaries in the county. He repeatedly refused high positions, closing his door to retire. He died at eighty-four in the fourth year of Zhongping. Over 30,000 mourners attended his funeral. His posthumous title was Mr. Wen Fan. His sons Chen Ji and Chen Chen were also virtuous. Chen Ji served under Dong Zhuo but opposed moving the capital, warning of destruction. He later became Dahonglu and died at seventy-one. Historians praised Chen Chen's virtue, noting that while imperial teachings declined, integrity survived among the people.

translation:
Dong Zhuo, courtesy name Zhongying, was from Lintao, Longxi.
He has a rough and scheming temperament.
When he was young, he traveled among the Qiang and tried his best to make friends with the leaders.
Later, when he returned home to farm, some of the leaders came to join him. Dong Zhuo slaughtered cattle for them and had banquets with them. The leaders thanked him for his kindness and collected the remaining heads of various livestock as gifts to him after returning. From then on, he became famous for his bravery and chivalry.
The soldiers and horses who were appointed as state guards once patrolled and guarded under the fortress.
Dong Zhuo has extraordinary physical strength. He wears two bow boxes and shoots them left and right. The Qiang and Hu people are afraid of him.
In the last years of Emperor Huan's reign, as a son of a good family in six counties, he was appointed Yulin Lang, and followed Zhang Huan, the general of Zhonglang, as a military commander. Together they went to attack the rebellious Qiang people in Hanyang. After defeating them, he was named Langzhong and was rewarded with nine thousand bundles of silk.
Dong Zhuo said: I am the one who records the merits, and the soldiers are the ones who make the merits.
So they were all distributed to the soldiers, leaving nothing behind.
He was gradually promoted to the rank of captain of Wuji School in the Western Regions, but was dismissed for some reasons.
Later he became the governor of Bingzhou and the governor of Hedong.
In the first year of Zhongping, he was appointed as Shu Zhonglang General. With integrity, he went to Xiaquyang to attack Zhangjiao on behalf of Lu Zhi. He was defeated and punished.
That winter, the Ling Qiang and Paohan Heguan bandits in the north rebelled, so they jointly supported Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, the Hu people who had surrendered to Huangzhong, as generals, and killed the Qiang captain Ling Zheng.
Boyu and others kidnapped Bian Zhang and Han Sui, who came to Jincheng, and made them specialize in military administration. Together they killed Jincheng prefect Chen Yi, attacked and burned the prefectures and counties.
In the spring of the next year, he led tens of thousands of cavalry to invade the Third Auxiliary and approached the royal cemetery, under the pretext of killing the eunuchs.
The imperial court issued an edict appointing Dong Zhuo as Zhonglang General and serving as the deputy of Zuo Chaoqi General Huangfu Song to conquer them.
Huangfu Song was dismissed and recalled due to ineffectiveness, while Bian Zhang, Han Sui and others became more powerful.
The imperial court also appointed Sikong Zhang Wen as the general of chariots and cavalry. During the holiday, Yuan Pang, the commander of Jinwu, was appointed as his deputy.
Dong Zhuo was appointed as the Polu General, and he and Zhou Shen, the Dangqi General, were under the command of Zhang Wen.
A total of more than 100,000 infantry and cavalrymen from all counties were combined and stationed at Meitun to protect the royal cemetery.
Bian Zhang and Han Sui also marched into Meiyang.
Zhang Wen and Dong Zhuo always lost when they fought with them.
In November, there was a shooting star like fire at night, with a light of more than ten feet long, shining in Bianzhang and Han Sui's camp. Donkeys and horses were braying together. The thieves thought it was unlucky and wanted to return to the Golden Globe. Emperor Dong was overjoyed when he heard about it. The next day, he joined forces with You Fufeng, Bao You and others to attack, defeating the enemy and beheading thousands of people.
Bian Zhang and Han Sui were defeated and fled to Yuzhong. Zhang Wen sent Zhou Shen with 30,000 people to pursue them.
Zhang Wen's military officer Sun Jian said to Zhou Shen: There is no food in the city. The rebels will transport food from outside. I hope to give them tens of thousands of people to cut off their food routes. The general will follow with his troops. The rebels must be too tired to fight.
If they escape into the Qiang and join forces to attack them, then the state can be pacified.
Huangyuan refused to listen and led his troops to surround Shengcheng.
However, Bian Tong and Zheng Sui divided their troops to garrison Zheng Liyou, which cut off Lizuo's food route.
Zhou Shen was afraid, so he abandoned his baggage and retreated.
Zhang Wen also sent Dong Zhuo to lead 30,000 troops to attack the Xianling Qiang. Dong Zhuo was surrounded by Chasu in the north of Wangyuan. Food was cut off and it was difficult to advance or retreat.
So they built a weir on the river they crossed and pretended to fish, but quietly withdrew their troops from the north of the weir.
When the thieves came to chase him, the water he released was already too deep to cross.
At that time, all armies retreated, and only Dong Zhuo's army returned intact. They stationed themselves in Fufeng and granted him the title of Marquis of Lianxiang, with a settlement of 1,000 households.
In the spring of the third year of Zhongping, the imperial court sent envoys holding Fujie to Chang'an to appoint Zhang Wen as Taiwei.
When Sangong was outside the capital, Zhang Wen was the first to set an example.
That winter, Zhang Wen was summoned back to the capital. Han Sui killed Bian Zhang, Boyu and Wenhou, led more than 100,000 troops, and marched to besiege Longxi.
The prefect Li Xiangru rebelled and joined forces with Han Sui to kill Geng Bi, the governor of Liangzhou.
Geng Bi's Sima Fufeng and Ma Teng also led troops to rebel, and the Hanyang Kingdom claimed to be "General He Zhong", all of whom allied with Han Sui.
They jointly elected Gu Gu as their leader, and took all their troops to invade and plunder the three auxiliaries.
In the fifth year of Zhongping, Chencang was surrounded.
The imperial court then appointed Dong Zhuo as a former general, and he and left general Huangfu Song defeated them.
Han Sui and others jointly deposed the kingdom, and hijacked the original capital of Han Yang Jianzhong and asked him to command various ministries. Yan Zhong was ashamed of being coerced by everyone, and became angry and died of illness.
Han Sui and others gradually fought for power and killed each other, and their various armies also fell apart.
In the sixth year of Zhongping, Dong Zhuo was recruited as the Shaofu, but he refused to take office. He wrote a letter saying: The subordinate tribes in Huangzhong and the Qin and Hu soldiers I brought came to me and said: The food and salary are not uniform, the things issued by the court are also cut off, my wife and children are hungry and cold, and they support my cart, preventing me from going on the road.
The Qiang and Hu people were so cruel that I couldn't stop them, so I had to boldly violate the will and obey them to appease them.
If there are other circumstances, I'll tell you more. The court could not govern and was very worried about him.
When Emperor Ling fell ill, he issued an edict to appoint Dong Zhuo as the shepherd of Bingzhou and asked him to hand over his troops to Huangfu Song.
Dong Zhuo wrote again, saying: I have neither foresight nor great feats, so I accept the emperor's wrong love and make me take charge of the army for ten years.
The soldiers have been close to each other for a long time. They cherish my kindness in raising them and are willing to do their best for me. Please take them with you to serve on the frontier.
So he stationed troops in Hedong to observe changes in the situation. When Emperor Ling died, General He Jin and Sili Colonel Yuan Shao planned to kill the eunuchs, but the Queen Mother did not agree, so they privately summoned Dong Zhuo to lead troops into the court to intimidate the Queen Mother.
After Dong Zhuo was summoned, he set out on the road that day.
He also wrote a letter saying: Zhang Rang, the minister of the Central Committee, and others stole the favor and caused chaos in the world.
I have heard that raising the soup to stop it from boiling is not as good as drawing fuel from the bottom of the cauldron; although it hurts to break a malignant sore, it is worse than having it invade the inside.
In the past, I went to martingale to raise troops in Jinyang to drive away the evildoers around the monarch.
Now I am going to Luoyang with drums to arrest Zhang Rang and others in order to eliminate the evil and filth.
He Jin was defeated and died before Dong Zhuo arrived. Huben Zhonglang general Yuan Shu burned down the Nangong Palace to attack the eunuchs. Duan Gui, the general servant, and others kidnapped the young emperor and King Chenliu and fled to Xiaopingjin at night.
Dong Zhuo saw the fire from a distance and led his troops forward quickly. He arrived at the west of the city before dawn. He heard that the young emperor was in Beimang, so he went to greet him.
When the young emperor saw Dong Zhuo coming with his troops and horses, he was frightened and cried.
Dong Zhuo talked to him, but he couldn't answer; he talked to King Chenliu and found out the cause of the trouble.
Dong Zhuo believed that King Chenliu was wise and was born to the Empress Dowager Dong. Dong Zhuo believed that he was of the same clan as the Empress Dowager and had plans to dethrone the emperor.
When Dong Zhuo entered Beijing, he had only three infantry and cavalrymen. He felt that he had few troops and was afraid that he would not be subdued by people near and far. For about four or five days, he secretly separated his troops from the city at night and camped nearby. After dawn, he returned to the city with great fanfare, making people think that the army from the west had arrived again, and no one in Luoyang knew it.
Soon the troops previously led by He Jin and his brother He Miao all surrendered to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo asked Lu Bu to kill Zhijin Wu Dingyuan and annex his tribe. Dong Zhuo's army greatly increased.
So he signaled the court to remove Sikong Liu Hong and replace him himself.
Then he summoned the courtiers to discuss deposing the emperor.
All the officials gathered together, and Dong Zhuo held his head high and said: The greatest relationship is the relationship between heaven and earth, and the second is the relationship between monarch and ministers. This is the foundation of government.
The emperor is ignorant and cowardly, unable to serve the ancestral temple and be the monarch of the world.
Now I want to follow the old rules of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and establish King Chenliu instead. How about that?
No one below the rank of Duke dares to speak.
Dong Zhuo said loudly: "In the past, Huo Guang made decisions and Tian Yannian supervised them with his sword. Anyone who dared to hinder the policies and plans would be dealt with according to military law."
Everyone present was shocked.
Only Shangshu Lu Zhi said: In the past, after Taijia came to the throne, King Lu Yi had more than a thousand sins, so there was something about abolishing the throne.
The current emperor is still young and his behavior is not inappropriate and cannot be compared with previous cases.
Dong Zhuo was furious and left the table.
The next day, he summoned all the officials in the front hall of Chongde, and then threatened the Queen Mother, asking her to issue an edict to depose the young emperor.
Said: During the period of mourning for the late emperor, the emperor did not have the mentality of a son, and did not behave like a monarch. Now he is deposed as King Hongnong.
So he established King Chenliu and created Emperor Xian.
He also pointed out that the Queen Mother persecuted the Queen Mother Yongle, causing her to die of depression. She violated the etiquette of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, and had no filial qualities. She moved her to Yong'an Palace, where she was subsequently murdered and died.
Dong Zhuo was promoted to Taiwei, acting as the agent for the affairs of the former general. He added the certificate of carriage and horse riding at the post station during the Xijie Festival and the warriors with axes and iron tigers, and was granted the title of County Lord.
Dong Zhuo, together with Situ Huang Wan and Sikong Yang Biao, all brought Zhuan to the court and wrote to the court, demanding that Chen Fan, Baowu and other party members be traced in order to comply with people's wishes.
So the titles of Chen Fan and others were completely restored, and their descendants were promoted and appointed.
Soon after, Dong Zhuo was granted the title of Prime Minister, and he could enter the court without any hesitation, and go to the palace with a sword and shoes.
He named his mother Chiyangjun and appointed Lingcheng and other officials for her.
At that time, the residences of the emperor's relatives in Luoyang City were connected, and every family had a lot of gold and silk property.
Dong Zhuo indulged his soldiers, rushed into their homes, raped and robbed women, and robbed their property. He called this "prison raids."
He also raped and harassed the princess, occupied and robbed the palace maids, and indiscriminately inflicted cruel punishments. Anyone with a little hatred would be killed. No one in the palace or outside the palace could protect himself.
Dong Zhuo once sent troops to Yangcheng. At that time, people were gathering in front of the Tutu Temple. Dong Zhuo ordered them to go forward and kill all the people, take away the belongings on the carts, load the robbed women, tie their heads to the shafts of the carts, and return to the capital singing and shouting.
They also destroyed the five-baht coins and cast them into small coins. They also collected all the bronze men, Zhongxu, Feilian, bronze horses and so on from Luoyang and Chang'an to use as materials for coining coins.
Therefore, money is cheap and goods are expensive, and a stone of millet is worth tens of thousands.
In addition, the money he cast had no outline patterns, making it inconvenient for people to use.
At that time, people thought that Qin Shihuang saw a long man in Lintao, so he cast a bronze man.
Dong Zhuo, a native of Lintao, has now destroyed it.
Although the casting and melting are different, the violence is similar.
Dong Zhuo had always heard that people all over the world hated the eunuchs who killed Zhongliang. When he took control of the government, although he did not follow the right path, he still pretended to be temperamental and promoted and appointed many scholars, such as the Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, Secretary of Hanyang Zhou, Shizhong Runan Wu Qiong, Minister Zheng Gongye, and Chang Shi He Xian, etc.
Xun Shuang, a scholar without an official position, was appointed as Sikong.
Chen Ji, Han Rong and others who were implicated by the party all became ministers.
Those who sink and are buried are often promoted.
Appoint Shangshu Han Fu as the governor of Jizhou, Shizhong Liu Dai as the governor of Yanzhou, Chen Liu and Kong Dian as the governor of Yuzhou, and Yingchuan Zhang Zi as the governor of Nanyang.
Dong Zhuo's cronies were not in prominent positions, they were just generals.
In the first year of Chuping, when Han Fu took office, he and Yuan Shao and more than ten others formed an alliance to attack Dong Zhuo, while Wu Qiong and Zhou secretly acted as internal correspondents.
At the beginning, in the last years of Emperor Ling's reign, the Yellow Turban remnant party Guo Tai and others started an uprising in the Baibo Valley of Xihe River, and invaded Taiyuan, and then conquered Hedong. The people fled to Sanfu and called them "Baibo Bandits", with more than 100,000 people.
Dong Zhuo sent Zhonglang General Niu Fu to attack them, but they could not retreat.
When Dong Zhuo heard about the rise of troops from the east to attack Dong Zhuo, he was frightened and poisoned King Hongnong with poisonous wine and wanted to move the capital to Chang'an.
The ministers were summoned to discuss the matter, but Huang Wan, the Taiwei, and Yang Biao, the Situ, tried their best to dissuade him. Wu Qiong and Zhou Shai tried their best to dissuade him.
Dong Zhuo then became furious and said: When I first entered the court, these two men advised me to use virtuous people, so they obeyed. However, after you took office, you raised troops to attack me.
These two betrayed me, how can I feel sorry for them!
So Wu Qiong and Zhou Suo were killed.
Yang Biao and Huang Wan were frightened, so they went to Dong Zhuo to apologize and said: "The villain is nostalgic for the old place, not to prevent national affairs. Please punish us for our ill-considered sins."
After Dong Zhuo killed Wu Qiong and Zhou Mi, he soon regretted it, so he asked Yang Biao and Huang Wan to be appointed as Guanglu doctors.
So the emperor moved to the Western Capital.
At the beginning, Chang'an suffered from the turmoil of the Red Eyebrow Period. The palaces and civil and military official residences were burned and destroyed. Only the Gaomiao and Jingzhao Mansion were left in the period of the Imperial Period, so they chose an auspicious day for the emperor to move in.
Later it was moved to Weiyang Palace.
So millions of people from Luoyang were moved to Chang'an. The infantry and cavalry drove and forced them all the way, trampling on each other, and being starved and plundered. The roads were filled with corpses.
Dong Zhuo himself stayed in Bigui Garden and burned down all the surrounding palaces, temples, government offices and residential buildings, leaving no one inhabited within 200 miles.
He also sent Lu Bu to dig up the tombs of the emperors and officials below, and collect the treasures therein.
At that time, Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, also led soldiers and horses from various counties in Yuzhou to attack Dong Zhuo.
Dong Zhuo first sent generals Xu Rong and Li Meng out to capture and plunder.
Xu Rong met Sun Jian in Liangcheng, fought with him, defeated Sun Jian, captured Ying Prefect Li Man alive, and boiled him to death.
The rebel soldiers captured by Dong Zhuo were all wrapped in cloth, stood upside down on the ground, and poured with hot oil to death.
At that time, Wang Kuang, the governor of Hanoi, stationed troops in Heyangjin and wanted to attack Dong Zhuo.
Dong Zhuo sent suspicious soldiers to challenge, but let his elite soldiers sneak north of Xiaopingjin ferry crossing, defeated Wang Kuang, and killed almost all his soldiers.
The next year, Sun Jian gathered the scattered soldiers and stationed at Yangren in Liang County.
Dong Zhuo sent his generals Hu Zhen and Lu Bu to attack him.
Lu Bu was at odds with Hu Zhen. The army was frightened and the soldiers were scattered.
Sun Jian pursued them, but Hu Zhen and Lu Bu were defeated.
Dong Zhuo sent General Li to urge Sun Jian to ask for peace, but Sun Jian refused and marched to Dagu, ninety miles away from Luoyang.
Dong Zhuo personally sent troops to fight with Sun Jian in the area of ​​​​the imperial mausoleums. Dong Zhuo was defeated and retreated to garrison in Turtle Chi and gathered troops in Shaanxi.
Sun Jian entered the gate of Xuanyang City in Luoyang and attacked Lu Bu. Lu Bu was defeated and fled again.
Sun Jian then cleaned the royal ancestral temple, filled the excavated tombs, and divided his troops out of Hangu Pass to between Xin'an and Xingchi to cut off Dong Zhuo's retreat.
Dong Zhuo said to Chief Shi Liu Ai: The generals in Guandong have been defeated several times and can't do anything good anymore.
Only Sun Jian is a little angry. Generals, please be careful.
So he sent Dong Zhonglang general Dong Yue to Xingchi, Zhonglang general Duan Xuan to Huayin, Zhonglang general Niu Fu to Anyi, and the remaining Zhonglang generals and lieutenants were distributed in various counties to resist Shandong's army.
Dong Zhuo signaled the imperial court to send Guang Luxun Xuanyao to hold the talisman to worship Dong Zhuo as Grand Master, which was above the princes and kings.
So he withdrew his troops and returned to Chang'an.
All the officials went to the roadside to greet the worshipers. Dong Zhuo used carriage and horse clothing that transcended his status. He rode in a green umbrella-covered carriage with golden flowers and outlined the barriers on both sides of the carriage. At that time, it was called "Ganmo carriage", which means that his clothing was close to that of the emperor.
He appointed his younger brother Dong Man as General Zuo and the title of Marquis of E. His elder brother's son Dong Huang was appointed as Shizhong and Zhongjun Xiaowei, both of whom controlled the army.
So everyone inside and outside the clan held official positions.
Even if his descendants are still young, the males will be granted the title of marquis and the females will be granted the title of king of the city.
Dong Zhuo held banquets with hundreds of officials several times and indulged in carnivalesque.
He set up camp in the east of Chang'an City.
He also built a castle in Yong, each seven feet high and thick, called Wansuiwu.
Thirty years of food savings.
He said: If things succeed, he will dominate the world; if they fail, staying here will be enough to support him in his old age.
He once visited the castle in Yong, and all the officials from Duke to lower level went to Hengmen to set up sacrifices to see him off.
Dong Zhuo set up a tent and held a banquet. He killed hundreds of rebels from the North who had been lured to surrender at the banquet. He first cut off their tongues, then chopped off their hands and feet, then gouged out their eyes and boiled them in a pot.
Those who were not dead were writhing and struggling in the banquet.
The attendees were trembling with fear and could not hold their chopsticks, but Dong Zhuo looked at ease when eating.
If the generals speak inappropriately, they will be killed on the spot.
He also killed the famous old families in Guanzhong one by one and framed them for treason.
At that time, Taishi observed the clouds and said that ministers would be killed.
Dong Zhuo had people falsely accuse Wei Wei Zhang Wen of colluding with Yuan Shu, so he whipped Zhang Wen in the market and killed him to cope with the changes in the celestial phenomena.
In the past, Zhang Wen went out of the capital to garrison troops in Meiyang, and ordered Dong Zhuo to fight Bian Zhang and others, but he was defeated. Zhang Wen summoned him but did not return in time, and when he arrived, he spoke rudely.
At that time, Sun Jian joined Zhang Wen's army and advised Zhang Wen to deploy troops to kill him.
Zhang Wen said: Dong Zhuo is famous and we are relying on him to march westward.
Sun Jian said: Duke Ming personally leads the imperial army and is powerful in the world. Why should we rely on Dong Zhuo?
I heard that famous generals in ancient times used their swords to lead the army, and there was no one who did not kill them as a demonstration of force.
So Zhou Ju killed Zhuang Jia, and Wei Jiang killed Yang Qian.
If you let him go today, you will lose your prestige and regret it!
Zhang Wen did not accept it, but Dong Zhuo still harbored a grudge, so Zhang Wen suffered.
Zhang Wen, courtesy name Boshen, had a reputation when he was young and gradually rose to the rank of public minister. He also secretly plotted with Situ Wang Yun to kill Dong Zhuo, but was killed before he could take action.
Runan Wufu, the Yueqi captain, hated Emperor Dong for his cruelty and wanted to kill him with his own hands, so he hid a knife in his court uniform and went to see Dong Zhuo.
Wu Fu said goodbye and left. Dong Zhuo stood up and escorted him to the pavilion, patting his back with his hand. Yu Cheng took out his knife and stabbed Emperor Dong, but missed.
Dong Zhuo was able to save himself, so he hurriedly shouted to the left and right to kill him, and cursed Wu Fu: "You want to make a slave!"
Wu Fu shouted: "I wish I could chop the traitor into pieces on the street to comfort the world!"
He was killed before he finished speaking.
At that time, Wang Yun, Lu Bu and the servant Sun Rui planned to kill Dong Zhuo.
Someone wrote the character "LV" on the cloth and carried it on his back in the market, singing: "Bu!"
Someone told Dong Zhuo that Dong Zhuo had not realized it.
In April of the third year of Chuping, the emperor recovered from his illness and held a grand gathering in Weiyang Hall.
Dong Zhuo boarded the carriage wearing court clothes. Then the horse was frightened and fell into the mud. He went back to the house to change clothes.
His concubine refused to let him go, but Dong Zhuo refused to listen, so he set off.
So the troops lined up along the road, from his camp to the palace, with infantry and cavalry on the left and right, closely guarding him layer by layer, so that Lu Bu was waiting in front and behind to be on guard.
Wang Yun and Shi Sunrui secretly reported the murder of Dong Zhuo, and asked Shisun Rui to write a letter of Shao himself and send it to Lu Bu. He ordered Li Su, the Cavalry Commander, and more than ten warriors who were aligned with Lu Bu to put on the uniforms of Dong Zhuo's guards and wait for Dong Zhuo inside Beiye Gate.
When Dong Zhuo was approaching, the horse was frightened and refused to go forward. He felt strange and afraid and wanted to go back.
Lu Bu persuaded him to enter the palace, so he entered the palace gate.
Li Su stabbed him with a halberd, but Dong Zhuo couldn't penetrate his face and was wearing pin armor. His arm was injured and he fell off the carriage. He turned around and shouted: "Where is Lu Bu?"
Lu Bu responded and said: There is an edict to attack the traitors.

summary:
Dong Zhuo, a man of rough and scheming temperament from Lintao, Longxi, rose to prominence through his interactions with Qiang leaders, distributing rewards to soldiers and gaining a reputation for bravery. He served as a military commander under Zhang Huan, defeating rebellious Qiang forces, and was later appointed to various posts, including Governor of Bingzhou and Hedong. During the Zhongping era, he was tasked with suppressing rebellions, including those led by Bian Zhang and Han Sui, but faced defeats. Despite setbacks, he managed to preserve his army and was granted the title of Marquis of Lianxiang.

After Emperor Ling's death, Dong Zhuo was summoned to the capital by He Jin and Yuan Shao to intimidate the Empress Dowager. He entered Luoyang with a small force but cleverly expanded his army by integrating defectors, including troops from He Jin and He Miao. He deposed the young emperor, established Emperor Xian, and assumed the role of Prime Minister, wielding immense power. His rule was marked by brutality, including the massacre of civilians, looting, and the destruction of the economy through coinage reforms. He also moved the capital to Chang'an, forcing millions to relocate, causing widespread death and destruction.

Dong Zhuo's tyranny led to a coalition of regional governors, including Yuan Shao and Sun Jian, rising against him. He was eventually assassinated in a plot by Wang Yun and Lü Bu in 192 AD. His death was followed by chaos, as his former subordinates Li Jue and Guo Si seized control of Chang'an, leading to further violence and famine. The capital was devastated, with widespread cannibalism and depopulation.

The aftermath saw continued infighting among Dong Zhuo's former allies and the rise of Cao Cao, who eventually took control of the imperial court. The text concludes with a critical assessment of Dong Zhuo as a ruthless and destructive figure whose actions plunged the empire into turmoil, leading to the collapse of central authority and widespread suffering.

summary:
Cai Yong, courtesy name Bo Zhe, was a native of Chenliuyu County. His sixth-generation ancestor Cai Xun served under Emperor Ping but refused to serve Wang Mang, fleeing into the mountains with his family to maintain loyalty to Han. Cai Yong's father, Cai Leng, was known for his integrity. Cai Yong himself was filial, tending to his ill mother for three years without rest, and after her death, he built a hut by her tomb and observed strict mourning rituals. He lived harmoniously with his uncle and brothers for three generations, earning local praise. Erudite from youth, he studied under Hu Guang and excelled in literature, mathematics, astronomy, and music.

During Emperor Huan's reign, eunuchs like Xu Huang and Zuo Guan summoned Cai Yong to play the qin, but he feigned illness and returned home. He wrote "Explanation" to encourage himself, inspired by Dongfang Shuo and others. In the third year of Jianning, he served under Situ Qiaoxuan. Later, as Yilang, he noted errors in the classics and, in the fourth year of Xiping, petitioned Emperor Ling to correct the Six Classics. He personally wrote the text on steles, which were set up outside Taixue, attracting over a thousand visitors daily.

Cai Yong submitted a memorial criticizing the "three mutual laws" that prevented officials from serving in related regions, arguing they hindered governance in You and Ji provinces. He urged their abolition to select talented officials promptly, but his advice was not adopted. He also addressed disasters and Xianbei invasions, proposing seven reforms: proper imperial sacrifices, recruiting virtuous scholars, rewarding loyal officials like Zhang Wen, empowering honest governors, and ending corrupt recruitment practices. His memorial was leaked by Cao Jie, leading to false accusations from enemies like Yang Qiu. Cai Yong was imprisoned and sentenced to death, but Lu Qiang interceded, and his sentence was commuted to exile in Shuofang. Despite assassination attempts by Yang Qiu, he survived.

After nine months, a general amnesty allowed his return, but he fled to Wuhui after offending Wang Zhi. He lived in Wu for twelve years, once crafting a famous "Jiaowei Qin" from a burnt tung tree. In the sixth year of Zhongping, Dong Zhuo forced him into service, promoting him rapidly. Cai Yong advised Dong Zhuo against excessive honors but grew disillusioned with his tyranny. After Dong Zhuo's execution, Cai Yong expressed regret, angering Wang Yun, who imprisoned him. Despite pleas from scholars like Ma Rishidan, Wang Yun executed him, fearing his historical writings would slander the court. Cai Yong died at sixty-one, mourned by many. His works included poems, inscriptions, and 104 other pieces, though much was lost in chaos. The historian noted his tragic fate, bound by loyalty and circumstance.

At this time, Henan Yin Zhu Genjun was planning military affairs for Dong Zhuo.
Dong Zhuo rebuked Zhu Quanjun and said: I am victorious in every battle and I am dedicated to my affairs. Don't talk nonsense, even my knife will get dirty.
Gai Xun said: In the past, a shrewd emperor like Wu Ding still asked for advice from others. He said to Fu Shuo: Enlightenment is the heart, and my heart is fertile.
Dong Zhuo said: Just kidding.
Gai Xun said: I have never heard that the angry curse can be said to be a joke.
Dong Zhuo then apologized to Zhu Quanjun.
Although Gai Xun was strong and unyielding, he hated Dong Zhuo in his heart. He was dissatisfied and died of gangrene. Year fifty-one.
The will does not accept Dong Zhuo's funeral gifts. Dong Zhuo wanted to pretend to be tolerant and magnanimous, so he asked Dongyuan to give him the secret weapon of Dongyuan, chariots, horses and silk, as a gift to help him survive and die.
Buried in Anling.
His son Gaishun was promoted to prefect of Yongyang.
◆Zang Hongchuan, whose courtesy name is Ziyuan, was born in Sheyang County, Guangling County.
Father Zang Min is talented.
In the first year of Xiping, Xu Zhao, a monster thief from Kuaiji, raised troops and called himself a general. He appointed his father Xu Sheng as the king of Yue. He conquered the city and captured tens of thousands of people.
The imperial court appointed Zang as the governor of Yangzhou.
Zang Min led Chen Wei, the governor of Danyang, to defeat Xu Zhao.
Xu Zhao still gathered his troops to harm the people.
Zang Min and others sent troops to conquer and fought for three years before finally pacifying Xu Zhao, capturing Xu Zhao and his son, and killing thousands of people.
Zang Min was promoted to be the envoy to the Xiongnu Zhonglang General.
In the fifteenth year of Zang Hong's year, because of his father's contribution to the country, he was appointed Dong Zilang, who was famous in the Imperial Academy.
His physical appearance is different from ordinary people.
He was promoted to be filial and honest, and he was appointed as a complement to Lang Qiuchang.
At the end of Zhongping Dynasty, he resigned and returned home. The prefect Zhang Chao asked him to be a meritorious official.
At this time, Dong Zhuo killed the emperor and wanted to seize the Han Dynasty.
Zang Hong said that Zhang Chao said: The prefect has been favored by the imperial court for generations, and his brothers have all served as high counties. Now the royal family is in danger, and thieves and ministers are watching. This is really the time for those who are loyal to the country to serve.
Now that the county is still intact and the people are prosperous, if the war drums sound, we can gather 20,000 people and lead them to kill the national traitors and hold high the flag of righteousness for the world. Wouldn't it be great?
Zhang Chao agreed with his opinion and went to Chenliu with Zang Hongxi to discuss with his brother Zhang Miao.
Zhang Miao first said to Zhang Chao: I heard that you are a prefect and leave government affairs to Zang Hong. What kind of person is Zang Hong?
Zhang Chao said: Zang Hong is a strange man in the country. He is more talented and resourceful than me.
Zhang Miao immediately talked to Zang Hong and greatly appreciated him.
He sent Zang Hong to see Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, and Kong Danyou, the governor of Yuzhou, and they both became close friends with each other.
Zhang Miao originally had an agreement. When Zhang Chao arrived, he made the decision, so he held a meeting with the herdsmen in Suanzao.
They set up a altar and prepared to make an alliance, but they gave in to each other. No one dared to go first, and everyone recommended Zang Hong.
Zang Hong then raised his clothes to the altar, expressed his blood and made an alliance, saying: The Han Dynasty was unlucky, and the rules and regulations of the court were in chaos. The traitor Dong Zhuo took the opportunity to cause harm, and the disaster fell on the emperor and poisoned the people.
The most terrifying thing is that the Han Dynasty fell and the country was ruined.
Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, Kong Qianyou, the governor of Yuzhou, Zhang Miao, the governor of Chenliu, Qiao Mao, the governor of Dongjun, Zhang Chao, the governor of Guangling, etc., gathered volunteers to fight against the national calamity.
All those who are in our alliance will work together to fulfill the loyalty of our ministers and kill their heads as they please without any second thought.
If he violates the oath, he will die and die without any descendants.
The emperor, the queen, the earth, the ancestors and the gods all learn from each other.
Zang Hong's poems were so passionate that everyone who listened to them got excited.
From then on, each army hesitated, and no one dared to go first, resulting in insufficient military supplies and the disintegration of the soldiers.
At this time, Gongsun Zan, the commander-in-chief of the imperial army, had a disagreement with Liu Yu, the commander-in-chief. Zhang Chao sent Zang Hong to find Liu Yu to discuss the plan to defeat the bandits. When they walked to the river, they encountered a war between You and Ji, and the road was blocked, so they went to Yuan Shao's place.
Yuan Shao met Zang Hong and admired his talent. He became friends with Zang Hong and asked Zang Hong to act as the governor of Qingzhou.
The former governor, Jiao He, had a false reputation and was a master of empty words.
At this time, yellow scarf thieves were scurrying everywhere, and the people in Qingzhou were rich and had many troops and equipment.
Jiao He wanted to go to the capital with various allies, but before he left, the Yellow Turban thieves had already arrived, conquered the city and massacred the people.
Jiao He didn't know anything about military affairs, so he just invited the witch Zhu Shi to his house to pray for God's blessing.
He was also afraid that yellow turban thieves would cross the river during the freezing period, so he ordered many ice-trap pills to be made and placed in the river.
His tribe was disbanded and Jiao He also died of illness.
Zang Hong gathered together to comfort the scattered tribes, and the people were at peace.
In the second year of his reign, Yuan Shao was afraid of his incompetence and appointed him as the prefect of Dongjun, with his capital in Dongwuyang.
At this time, Cao Cao surrounded Zhang Chao in Yongqiu, and the situation was very dangerous.
Zhang Chao said to the soldiers: Zang Hong is the only one who will come to save me today.
Some people say: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao are getting along well, and Zang Hong is Yuan Shao's man. I'm afraid Zang Hong will not come far away, and he will bring disaster instead of good fortune.
Zhang Chao said: Ziyuan is a righteous man in the world and will never deviate from his original aspirations. He may be held hostage by force, but there is nothing we can do!
Zang Hong began to hear that Zhang Chao was surrounded, cried barefoot, and prepared his troops to rescue Zhang Chao.
Thinking that his troops were too weak, he asked Yuan Shao for troops, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao's defense was breached and Zhang Chao's entire clan was killed.
Zang Hong resented Yuan Shao and severed ties with him.
Yuan Shao sent troops to surround Zang Hong, but could not capture it after many years. Yuan Shao sent Zang Hong to write a letter to Zang Hong from Chen Lin, a county resident, explaining the blessings and misfortunes to Zang Hong, and blaming each other with personal kindness and national justice.
Zang Hong replied: Missing each other after farewell often occurs when we are asleep.
We are not far apart, but each of us has taken a different path, and each of us has a different mood. How can we describe it in just one or two sentences?
A few days ago, I promised you that I would never give up, and I sent you frequent letters, describing the good and bad fortunes, gains and losses, and public and personal friendships, which were the most cordial.
How could a talented person like you, Botong Classic, be so secretive as to be ignorant of my aspirations?
Therefore, I did not reply to you. I also wanted you to understand my character from a distance.
Recently I received a handwritten letter from you, which was quoted a lot. Although I don’t want to reply, you said it sincerely and I shouldn’t ignore it rashly.
I am a villain, with no great ambitions. Because I was serving abroad, I was acquainted with Duke Yuan. I was deeply gracious and affectionate, and was able to seize the big state. Who is willing to go back and be slaughtered by myself today?
Every time I went to the city for military parade, I saw Yuan Gong's flags and drums, looked at Yuan Gong's tent in the distance, and the old friend's repeated dealings, I was even more excited. I held the string and pointed the arrow, and burst into tears!
Why?
I personally feel that I have no regrets in assisting Mr. Yuan. Mr. Yuan treated me much better than he treated his peers.
When they were first appointed, they were all focused on national affairs: clearing out the rebellion of foreign invaders and jointly supporting the royal family.
Unexpectedly, the state was invaded and the county general was in trouble. I asked Yuan Gong for more troops, but he was rejected. I resigned and was detained. My old leader was exterminated because of this.
I have such a small selfishness and have not received sympathy. How can I resume my friendship and seriously damage my reputation of loyalty and filial piety?
So I waved my hand with sorrow, wiped away my tears and said goodbye to him.
If Mr. Yuan is a little bit loyal and forgiving, and greets you at the side table when he comes, but restrains himself and blames himself when he leaves, then I will support Jizha's ambition to escape from the throne, and we will not fight today.
Once upon a time, Zhang Jingming ascended the throne and pledged his blood as an alliance, and went back and forth with letters. Finally, he made Han Fu give up his seal, and Yuan Gong gained control of Jizhou.
Later, Zhang Jingming was destroyed just because he worshiped the leader of the Zhang Dynasty and was given a title and passed down the throne. He was not given a chance to change his ways and was destroyed.
Lu Feng first attacked Dong Zhuo and came to ask for help from Yuan Gong. He refused to send troops and said goodbye and returned to Luoyang. What crime did he commit?
But Duke Yuan actually sent troops to kill him. Liu Zihuang was ordered to go on an envoy, but his request to resign his mission was not approved after the time limit was exceeded. He was afraid of the emperor and cherished his relatives, so he used deception to seek return. It can be said that he was determined to be loyal and filial, but not overbearing. He was also killed without any reduction.
The officer who wanted to be promoted was killed in violation of his will. This was the benefit of Duke Yuan, not the wish of the wanderer.
Therefore, in the past, as a warning, sticking to a poor city was nothing more than a gentleman fleeing and not going to the enemy's country.
I have seen the siege for a long time, but there is no relief, and the reinforcements have not arrived. I feel the love of marriage, and by extension my lifelong friendship, I think it is better to live under the righteousness than to die upholding the righteousness.
In the past, Yan Zi did not surrender because Cui Zhu had a white sword on his neck, and the Nanshi family did not bend their writing to survive because Tai Shi died. Therefore, the image will be passed down from person to person and the name will be passed down to future generations.
What's more, if I hold the golden city firmly and use the bravery of the people and soldiers to use three years' savings for one year, to relieve the sleepy, make up for the lack, and please the world, why should I use it to build houses and plow the land instead?
But fearing that the autumn wind would blow up the dust, Bo Han would drive his horse south, Zhang Yang and Fei Yan would work together to cause chaos, and the alarm would be heard on the northern border, and the brothers and sisters would be asked to return to save themselves.
Therefore, Mr. Yuan should learn from his peers at this time, roll up his flag and retreat. He has been angry for too long and it is not appropriate to expose his majesty to my city.
You ridiculed me for relying on Montenegro for rescue. Why don't you remember the Yellow Turban's unity?
In the past, Emperor Gaozu collected Peng Yue in the vast wilderness, and Guangwu established his foundation in the green forest. In the end, he could either receive orders from heaven or revive the imperial industry.
If it can help the monarch prosper and become a king, then what does it matter?
What's more, I personally signed the seal and worked with him!
Farewell to Kong Zhang, I invite you to help outside the country, Zang Hong surrenders to your relatives; you entrust Yuan Shao, and my name is Chang'an.
You say that my body and reputation will be destroyed, and I will also laugh at you that your life and death will be unknown. We are the same but we are different, we work hard, what else is there to say?
Yuan Shao read Zang Hong's reply and knew that he had no intention of surrender, so he increased his troops and attacked quickly.
There was no food in the city, and there were no reinforcements outside. Zang Hong himself was probably going to die, so he called the officials and said: "Yuan Shao is unethical and has evil intentions. He also does not rescue my general Zang Hong. I have no choice but to die out of righteousness."
I think you were fine and suffered this disaster in vain. You can lead your wives and children out of the city before the city is broken.
The generals all cried and said: "You and the Yuan family have no quarrel before. For the sake of the general, we are in such danger. How can we bear to leave you?"
At first, they dug up mice and boiled tendons to eat, but then they had nothing to eat. The chief clerk brought out three buckets of rice from the kitchen and asked him to cook some porridge for Zang Hong. Zang Hong said, "How can I eat alone?"
Let it be cooked into porridge, and be eaten by all the soldiers.
He also killed his beloved concubine and gave it to the generals to eat.
The soldiers and generals were in tears and could not raise their heads.
Seventy or eighty men and women died together, and no one betrayed them.
The city was broken and Zang Hong was captured alive.
Yuan Shaosheng opened the curtains, and all the generals in the assembly met with Zang Hong.
Said: Why is Zang Hong so disobedient!
Are you convinced today?
Zang Hong's eyes widened in anger and he said: "Yuan Yuan was a minister of the Han Dynasty, four generations and five princes, and he was deeply favored. Now that the imperial court is weak, he has no intention of helping others in danger. Instead, he intends to take advantage of the opportunity to achieve his ulterior motives." Kill many loyal and good people to establish your own treacherous power.
I saw with my own eyes that the general called Zhang Chenliu his brother, so my prince Zhang Chao should also call him his brother. He could not work together to eliminate harm for the country, but had an army and watched others beheaded.
It's a pity that my troops are not strong enough to avenge Mr. Zhang. What does it mean to surrender!
Yuan Shaoben loved Zang Hong and thought that as long as he surrendered, he would be forgiven. After seeing his passionate words, he knew that he would never be used by him, so he ordered him to be killed.
Chen Rong, a native of Zang Hong's county, was a young scholar. He envied Zang Hong's character and became the Prime Minister of Dongjun with him.
Before the city was broken, Zang Hong sent him to Yuan Shao.
Zang Hong was captured after the city was broken. When the generals were meeting, Chen Rong was present. Seeing that Zang Hong was about to die, he stood up and said to Yuan Shao: The general is carrying out a major event and wants to wipe out violence from the world, but he kills the loyal and righteous people first. Is this in line with God's will?
Zang Hong raised his troops for the sake of the county general, how to kill him!
Yuan Shao was so ashamed that he had Chen Rong taken out and said, "You are not one of Zang Hong's group. Why are you doing this in vain?"
Chen Rong turned around and said: Does benevolence and righteousness have a fixed place? If you practice benevolence and righteousness, you are a gentleman; if you do not practice benevolence and righteousness, you are a villain.
Today I would rather die on the same day as Zang Hong than be born on the same day as your general!
Therefore he was also killed.
Everyone sitting there sighed. Whisper: Why kill two martyrs in one day?
The historian commented: Cao Cao surrounded Zhang Chao in Yongqiu, and Zang Hong was extremely moved and indignant. It was so pitiful to see him crying barefoot, arranging his uniform, and calling for troops to rescue him!
What heroes pursue is probably different from the thoughts of those who uphold justice, right?
As for those who conspire, collude with each other, and have deceitful tricks to show off, they are all based on interests and interests.
What's more, Yongqiu City in a corner is already very dangerous. When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao were on good terms, Zang Hongkong wanted to use the power of foreign enemies to relieve Zhang Chao's crisis.
Those who fight over small things and become angry are called angry teachers. It is impossible to win a battle, and military strategists should prevent it.
It can be said that Zang Hong once applied for Baoxu to Qin to beg for an army, cried in the court of Qin, and asked Qin to save Chu. However, the application for Baoxu was successful. Qin sent troops to help Chu defeat Wu, but Zang Hong failed to achieve his goal.
summary:
Yu Xu, from Wuping in Chen, was known for his integrity. His grandfather, a prison officer, handled cases with compassion. Yu Xu was orphaned young and cared for his grandmother, refusing an official post until after her death. He later served as a doctor. When General Deng Zhi proposed abandoning Liangzhou due to Qiang rebellions, Yu Xu argued against it, stating it would expose the imperial tombs and that Liangzhou's people were a vital defense. He suggested controlling local leaders by giving their sons official posts to prevent rebellion. Deng Zhi, resentful of Yu Xu's opposition, sent him to govern Chaoge, a bandit-ridden area. Yu Xu used deception, recruiting former bandits to ambush others and marking thieves' clothes with silk threads, leading to their dispersal. Promoted to Wudu's prefect, he again used deception against the Qiang, increasing his campfires to feign strength and marching rapidly. He then used a strategy of weak arrows to lure the Qiang into range of his strong crossbows, defeating them. He improved the county by building fortifications, opening waterways for transport, and increasing the population. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached powerful officials, earning their hatred. He was framed and sentenced to hard labor, but eunuch Sun Cheng defended him, leading to his release and promotion. He later abolished the practice of "righteous money" and argued for fair treatment of petitioners. He remained upright despite nine reprimands and three punishments, dying as Shangshu Ling. On his deathbed, he regretted killing many bandits at Chaoge, believing it brought divine punishment.

Fu Xie, from Lingzhou, was known for his caution in speech and action. He served as Sima under Huangfu Song against Zhang Jiao's Yellow Turbans. Before the campaign, he warned the emperor that the real threat was internal, from eunuchs like Zhao Zhong, and that evil and good cannot coexist. Despite his merits, Zhao Zhong framed him, but the emperor spared him. Later, when Situ Cui Lie proposed abandoning Liangzhou during a Xiqiang rebellion, Fu Xie vehemently opposed him, arguing that Liangzhou was the empire's shield and that abandoning it would empower the barbarians. The emperor agreed. Fu Xie refused to curry favor with the powerful eunuch Zhao Zhong, even when offered a marquisate. As Hanyang's governor, he pacified the Qiang. He warned Governor Geng Bi against attacking Han Sui with untrained troops, predicting disaster. Geng Bi ignored him and was killed. When Hanyang was besieged, Fu Xie refused to abandon the city despite his son's pleas and the offer of safe passage from grateful Hu cavalry. He chose to die in battle, cursing a defecting official. His posthumous title was Zhuangjiehou.

Gai Xun, from Dunhuang, was a Xiaolian and Hanyang's chief historian. He refused to take revenge on an enemy, Su Zhenghe, when the governor wanted to kill him to cover for a corrupt prefect, arguing it was wrong to kill a good man. He later remonstrated with Governor Zuo Chang for embezzling funds, but Zuo Chang sent him to a dangerous post. Gai Xun survived and later rescued Zuo Chang from a siege by Bian Zhang. He criticized Governor Song Xiao's plan to teach the *Classic of Filial Piety* to pacify the border, calling it impractical. During a battle against Qiang rebels, he was wounded but refused to flee, cursing his captors. The Qiang, respecting his courage, released him. As a famine relief official, he used his own grain to save over a thousand people. Summoned by Emperor Ling, he blamed eunuchs for the world's chaos. He planned with Liu Yu and Yuan Shao to kill the eunuchs, but was made Jing Zhaoyin instead. There, he prosecuted a corrupt official despite pleas from nobles. After Emperor Ling's death, he wrote to Dong Zhuo, criticizing his deposition of the young emperor. He openly defied Dong Zhuo in court, refusing to bow. He died of illness at 51, refusing Dong Zhuo's funeral gifts.

Zang Hong, from Guangling, was made a Dong Zilang due to his father's military merits. After Dong Zhuo killed the emperor, Zang Hong urged Prefect Zhang Chao to raise an army. He helped organize an alliance at Suanzao, where he gave a passionate oath, calling for the destruction of Dong Zhuo. The alliance, however, failed to act decisively. Later, Zang Hong served Yuan Shao as Qingzhou's governor, pacifying the region. When Cao Cao besieged Zhang Chao, Zang Hong begged Yuan Shao for troops to rescue him, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao was killed. Enraged, Zang Hong broke with Yuan Shao, who then besieged him. Despite a letter from Chen Lin urging surrender, Zang Hong refused, accusing Yuan Shao of betraying allies and killing loyal men. He stated he would rather die for righteousness. During the siege, he shared his last food with his soldiers and even killed his concubine to feed them. The city fell, and Zang Hong was captured. He defiantly cursed Yuan Shao for his treachery and was executed. His subordinate Chen Rong also chose to die with him.
