translation:
Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was born in Gaoping, Shanyang, and was a descendant of King Lu Gong.
Liu Biao was more than eight feet tall, with a gentle appearance and a burly build.
Together with Zhang Jian and others from the same county, he was slandered and discussed as "Ba Gu". The emperor issued an edict to arrest the party members and punish them, but Liu Biao escaped without being caught.
After the party ban was lifted, Liu Biao was summoned by General He Jin as an assistant.
In the first year of Chuping, Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, killed Wang Xu, the governor of Jingzhou, and issued an edict appointing Liu Biao as the governor of Jingzhou.
At that time, there were many bandits of the same clan in the south of the Yangtze River, and Yuan Shu's troops were stationed in Luyang to block the road. Liu Biao could not reach Jingzhou, so he rode into Yicheng alone and invited Kuai Yue from Nanjun and Cai Mao from Xiangyang to discuss countermeasures.
Liu Biao said to Kuai Yue: Although there are many thieves in the same clan, no one will join them. If Yuan Jie takes advantage of them, disaster will inevitably come.
I want to recruit troops, but I'm worried that I can't combine them. What strategy should I use?
Kuai Yue replied: When governing peace, benevolence and righteousness should be the first priority; when governing war, the first priority should be to use contingency strategies.
The army does not have a large number of people, the important thing is to get the right talents.
Yuan Shu was proud and had no strategy, and most of the thieves gathered from his own clan were greedy and cruel.
Among them are people who I usually support. If I send someone to tell them the benefits, they will definitely lead their troops over.
You kill the cruel ones among them and appoint the talented ones among them. Once your prestige and kindness are established, people will come to you carrying their children in swaddling clothes.
The soldiers gathered and the people surrendered. Jiangling was captured in the south and Xiangyang was defended in the north. The eight counties under Jingzhou's jurisdiction could be pacified with a single proclamation.
Even if Yuan Gongli arrives, there is nothing he can do.
Liu Biao said: Yes.
So he asked Kuai Yue to send people to lure the leaders of thieves from his own tribe. Fifteen people came, killed them all and captured their tribes by surprise.
Only when the Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li gathered their troops to occupy Xiangyang City, and Liu Biao sent Kuai Yue and Pang Ji to inform them, did they surrender.
Everything south of the Yangtze River was pacified.
Many prefects and county magistrates heard about Liu Biao's reputation, and many of them took off their seals and ribbons and left.
Liu Hu then organized his troops in the fortress area to observe changes in the current situation.
There was a gap between Yuan Shu and his cousin Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao was friends with Liu Biao, so Yuan Shu and Sun Jian jointly attacked Liu Biao from the north and south.
Liu Biao was defeated, and Sun Jian then surrounded Xiangyang.
Just as Liu Biao's general Huang Zu came to rescue him, Sun Jian was shot by a stray arrow and died, and the rest of the people retreated.
When Li Cui and others entered Chang'an, in winter, Liu Biao sent envoys to pay tribute to the emperor.
Li Ji appointed Liu Biao as the General of Zhennan and the Shepherd of Jingzhou, and made him a Marquis of Wu, holding the Emperor's Talisman as his aid.
In the first year of Jian'an, the hussar general Zhang Ji fled from Guanzhong to Nanyang, attacked Lucheng along the way, and was shot to death by a flying arrow.
Officials and subordinates from Jingzhou came to celebrate.
Liu Biao said: Zhang Ji came because he was in embarrassment, and the master did not treat him politely, which resulted in a fight. It was not my idea to send him away. I accept condolences but not congratulations.
He sent people to receive Zhang Ji's troops. The soldiers were very happy and surrendered to Liu Biao.
In the third year, Zhang Xian, the governor of Changsha, led Lingling and Guiyang counties to betray Liu Biao. Liu Biao sent troops to besiege him, defeated Zhang Xian and pacified these areas.
In this way, the area that Liu Biao expanded was very wide. It connected with Wuling in the south and Han in the north. It was thousands of miles in radius and had more than 100,000 armored warriors.
At first, the people in Jingzhou were prone to harassment. In addition, there was shock and fear in all directions, and bandits were rampant, so there was turmoil everywhere.
Liu Biao summoned and persuaded well, and used force and appeasement in a coordinated manner. Among the thieves, the cunning and cunning old thief even helped him, and he leveled everything within ten thousand miles. Everyone, young and old, was convinced by him.
Thousands of scholars and literati from Guanxi, Yanzhou, and Yuzhou came to seek refuge. Liu Biao gave comfort and relief, and these people were fully supported.
So Liu Biao established a school and extensively visited people with Confucianism. People like Qi Muhe, Song Zhong and others wrote chapters and sentences of the "Five Classics", which is called Houding.
Liu Biao cared for the people, supported the scholars, and calmly defended Jingzhou.
When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao were confronting each other in Guandu, Yuan Shao sent people to ask for help. Liu Biao agreed, but he did not send troops or reinforce Cao Cao, and wanted to wait and see the changes in the world.
Han Song, a Nanyang native, and Liu Xian, a lieutenant in charge, persuaded Liu Biao: Now heroes are competing with each other, two powerful people are confronting each other, and the key to the world lies with you.
If you want to make a difference, raising troops when they are tired is a feasible way; if you don't want to do this, you must choose appropriate measures. How can you have an army of 100,000, sit back and watch the success or failure of others, refuse to rescue others when they ask for help, and refuse to submit to wise people when you see them!
In this way, the resentment of both parties will be concentrated on you, and I'm afraid it will be impossible for you to obtain neutrality.
Cao Cao is good at using troops, and most of the wise and outstanding people defect to Cao Cao. This situation will definitely defeat Yuan Shao, and then mobilize his troops to attack the Yangtze River and Han River area. I am afraid that the general will not be able to resist.
The best way at the moment is to surrender the entire Jingzhou to Cao Cao. Cao Cao must value the grateful general. You can enjoy the status of fortune and wealth for a long time and pass it on to future generations. This is an extremely perfect strategy.
Kuai Yue also tried to persuade Liu Biao.
But Liu Biao was hesitant and sent Han Song to Cao Cao to see what was going on.
Liu Biao said to Han Song: Now I don't know who can pacify the world, but Cao Cao supports the emperor to make Xu County his capital. You can go and see the truth for me.
Han Song replied: In my opinion, with Cao Gong's wisdom, he will definitely be able to realize his wish to unify the world.
If the general wants to submit to Cao Cao, he can send me. If he is undecided, I go to the capital and the emperor offers me an official position. If my refusal is not accepted, then I will become the emperor's minister and the general's former subordinate.
When you are with the Emperor, you will be loyal to the Emperor, and I will no longer devote myself to you.
I hope you reconsider.
Liu Biao thought that he was afraid of sending an envoy and forced him to go.
After arriving in Xu County, the emperor appointed Han Song as his minister and prefect of Lingling.
After returning, Han Song strongly praised the kindness of the emperor and Cao Cao, and persuaded Liu Biao to send his son to serve.
Liu Biao was furious, thinking that Han Song had double-minded intentions, so he displayed his troops, insulted Han Song, and prepared to kill him.
Han Song's expression remained unchanged as he slowly recounted what he had said before leaving.
Liu Biao's wife Cai knew Han Song's virtues and dissuaded Liu Biao.
Liu Biao was still furious, so he tortured and killed Han Song's entourage.
Liu Biao learned that Han Song had no other intention but to imprison him.
In the sixth year, Liu Bei came from Yuan Shao and defected to Jingzhou. Liu Biao treated Liu Bei favorably and made friends with him, but he could not use him.
In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao personally led an army to conquer Liu Biao but did not reach Jingzhou.
In August, Liu Biao died of malignant sores on his back.
Liu Biao had been in Jingzhou for nearly twenty years, and his family had no extra savings.
Liu Biao had two sons: Liu Qi and Liu Cong.
At first, Liu Biao thought Liu Qi looked like him and liked him very much. Later, he married Liu Cong's niece, Cai's niece. Cai then liked Liu Cong and hated Liu Qi. Liu Biao heard words slandering Liu Qi and praising Liu Cong every day.
Liu Biao loved his second wife deeply, so he believed and accepted these words every time.
In addition, Liu Biao's brother-in-law Cai Mao and nephew Zhang Yun were both placed in important positions by Liu Biao, and they were also close friends with Liu Cong.
Liu Qi felt that he was not safe and once discussed with Zhuge Liang, a man from Langxie, how to protect himself.
Zhuge Liang didn't answer at first.
Later, the two climbed up the tall building together, and then Liu Qi asked someone to take away the ladder. He said to Zhuge Liang: Today, the sky can't be seen from the top, and the ground can't be seen from the bottom. The words that came out of your mouth reached my ears. Can you speak?
Zhuge Liang said: "Don't you see that Shen Sheng is in danger at home and Chong'er is safe when he lives abroad?"
Liu Qi realized in his heart and secretly planned a way out. It happened that Huang Zu, the governor of Jiangxia under Liu Biao, was killed by Sun Quan, so Liu Qi asked to take over the position.
When Liu Biao was seriously ill, Liu Qi came back to visit him. Because Liu Qi was kind and filial by nature, Zhang Yun and others were afraid that they would have a father-son relationship after seeing Liu Biao. Liu Biao once again wanted to let him succeed, so he said to Liu Qi: The general has ordered you to govern Jiangxia. This responsibility is of great importance.
If you leave your subordinates and come here without permission, you will definitely be scolded.
It is not filial piety to ruin your father's interest and aggravate his illness.
So he blocked the door and prevented him from seeing Liu Biao.
Liu Qi left in tears, and many people sighed after hearing this.
In this way, Liu Cong succeeded to the throne.
Liu Cong awarded Liu Qi the seal of the feudal lords. Liu Qi became angry and threw the seal to the ground, preparing to take advantage of the funeral to make trouble.
Just as Cao Cao's army arrived in Xinye, Liu Qi fled to the south of the Yangtze River.
Kuai Yue, Han Song and Dong Cao's Fu Xun persuaded Liu Cong to surrender to Cao Cao.
Liu Cong said: Now that I have the entire territory of Chu State with you, I can preserve the career of the late emperor and use it to observe the situation in the world. Why not?
Fu Xun said: There are important principles for rebellion and surrender, and there are certain situations between strong and weak.
It is rebellious to fight against the emperor as a minister; to rely on the newly created Chu land to resist the central power will be dangerous; to antagonize Cao Gong for Liu Bei's sake is not worth it.
These three aspects are all shortcomings, and if you want to use them to resist the king's army, this is the road to inevitable destruction.
How does the general compare with Liu Bei?
Liu Cong said: I am not as good as him.
Fu Xun said: If Liu Bei's ability is not enough to resist Duke Cao, then even if he owns the entire Chu land, he cannot protect himself.
If Liu Bei is strong enough to resist Duke Cao, then Liu Bei will not be under your control.
I hope the general won't doubt it.
When Cao Cao's army reached Xiangyang, Liu Cong asked for the surrender of the entire Jingzhou, and Liu Bei rushed to Xiakou.
Cao Cao appointed Liu Cong as the governor of Qingzhou and made him a marquis.
Fifteen people including Kuai Yue were granted the title of marquis.
Then Cao Cao released Han Song from prison. Because of his high reputation, he treated him with special courtesy and asked him to list the talents in Jingzhou. All those he recommended were promoted and appointed.
Appoint Han Song as Da Honglu and treat him as a friend.
Kuai Yue was appointed Guang Luxun, and Liu Xian was appointed Shangshu Ling.
At first, Liu Biao made friends with Yuan Shao, but Deng Yi tried to dissuade him from doing so, but Liu Biao refused to listen. Deng Yi resigned on the pretext of illness and did not serve as an official while Liu Biao was alive. Cao Cao appointed him as a servant. Many others have become high-ranking officials.
Cao Cao was later defeated in Chibi, and Liu Bei wrote a letter recommending Liu Qi to be the historian of Jing.
He died the following year.
The argument goes: Yuan Shao initially won many people because of his heroic and chivalrous behavior, so he had the intention of becoming the hegemon. All the people in the world who could serve as soldiers and hold high the banner were all in the name of the Yuan family.
When it comes to a decisive battle with the enemy on the battlefield, the brave people will fight for him; if there is foresight behind the curtain, the wise people will plan for him.
How powerful are the conditions on which he relies!
Han Fei said: Being fierce but not gentle, insisting on going your own way when it comes to mistakes and liking to fight for victory, despising the son born from a legitimate wife and valuing the son born from a concubine, this can be said to be a sign of destruction.
Liu Biao's morality was not higher than that of others, but he was as stupid as a puppet if he wanted to lie down and accept the fate of God and imitate the three-part world.
Praising: Yuan Shao has a magnanimous and elegant appearance, and Liu Biao is also considered a loyal elder.
One dominates north of the Yellow River, and the other shows off his strength in the southern part of the Central Plains.
The warships in Han River are as dense as a school of fish, and the war horses in Jizhou are as numerous as clouds.
From this, I wanted to spy on the prophecies, aspire to the throne, worship heaven, and worship the gods of society. Although it was said that it was God's will, it also relied on human faith.
People who rely on their own strength rarely succeed. What can people who sit and talk talk expect?
Uncertainty in choosing between legitimate son and favor leads to ruin of reputation and ruin of career.
summary:
Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was a descendant of King Lu Gong from Gaoping, Shanyang. Over eight feet tall with a gentle appearance and burly build, he was implicated in the "Ba Gu" party affair and escaped arrest. After the party ban was lifted, he served as an assistant to General He Jin. In the first year of Chuping, he was appointed Governor of Jingzhou following Sun Jian's murder of Governor Wang Xu. Unable to reach Jingzhou due to bandits and Yuan Shu's troops blocking the road, Liu Biao rode alone to Yicheng and consulted Kuai Yue and Cai Mao. Following Kuai Yue's advice, he lured and killed fifteen clan bandit leaders, then pacified their tribes. The Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li surrendered after negotiations, and the region south of the Yangtze River was subdued. Liu Biao organized troops to observe the situation.

Yuan Shu and Sun Jian attacked Liu Biao, but Sun Jian was killed by a stray arrow during the siege of Xiangyang. Liu Biao sent tribute to Emperor Xian and was appointed General of Zhennan, Shepherd of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Wu. When Zhang Ji attacked Lucheng and was killed, Liu Biao accepted condolences and recruited Zhang Ji's troops. He suppressed rebellions by Zhang Xian and others, expanding his territory to connect with Wuling in the south and Han in the north, commanding over 100,000 armored warriors. Liu Biao pacified bandits, supported scholars, established schools, and commissioned commentaries on the Five Classics.

During Cao Cao and Yuan Shao's conflict at Guandu, Liu Biao remained neutral despite advice from Han Song and Kuai Yue to submit to Cao Cao. He sent Han Song to observe Cao Cao, but after Han Song praised Cao Cao and urged submission, Liu Biao imprisoned him. Liu Bei defected to Jingzhou in the sixth year of Jian'an, but Liu Biao did not utilize him. In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao marched south, and Liu Biao died of illness in August after nearly twenty years in Jingzhou.

Liu Biao favored his son Liu Qi initially but later favored Liu Cong due to his wife Cai's influence. Liu Qi, feeling unsafe, sought advice from Zhuge Liang and requested to govern Jiangxia. When Liu Biao fell ill, Liu Qi was prevented from visiting him, and Liu Cong succeeded. Liu Cong surrendered Jingzhou to Cao Cao, who appointed him Governor of Qingzhou and granted marquisates to others. Cao Cao later released Han Song and appointed him Da Honglu. Liu Biao's alliance with Yuan Shao was criticized by Deng Yi, who resigned. Cao Cao was defeated at Chibi, and Liu Bei recommended Liu Qi as Jingzhou's historian; Liu Qi died the following year. The text concludes that Liu Biao's indecision and favoritism led to his downfall.

Xiqiang originally came from Sanmiao, another branch of the Jiang surname.
The Western Qiang Kingdom is close to Nanyue.
When Shun exiled four stubborn people, he exiled them to Sanwei, which is the Qiang area southwest of Heguan. This area is wrapped around the Cizhi River and stretches for thousands of miles to the head of Cizhi River.
The gift branch is the analysis branch mentioned in "Yu Gong".
This area borders the barbarians outside the borders of Shu and Han to the south, and borders Shanshan, Cheshi and other countries to the northwest.
The Xiqiang people do not have fixed residences. They migrate with water and grass.
Grains are rarely grown on this land, and they mainly rely on livestock raising.
The custom of Xiqiang is that clans are not fixed. Some clans use the father's name and the mother's surname as the title of their tribe.
After the twelfth generation, clans intermarry with each other. After the father dies, he marries his stepmother, and after his elder brother dies, he marries his widower. Therefore, there are no widowers or widows in the Xiqiang country, and the population reproduces quickly.
Xiqiang does not have a king or ministers, and no one is its leader. If the power is strong, they will separate into races and become chiefs. If the power is weak, they will become subordinate tribes of others. They plundered and invaded each other, ruling the roost with violence.
Kill for life, there is no other prohibition.
The soldiers of Xiqiang are good at fighting in the valleys, but not on the plains; they cannot fight for a long time, but they dare to charge into battle; they regard death in battle as auspicious, while death from illness is considered unlucky.
The Xiqiang people can endure cold and hardship just like animals.
Even when women give birth to children, they do not hide from the wind and snow.
The Xiqiang people are strong and brave in fighting for the land, and they have accepted the energy of the metal element in the five elements and the west.
If the emperor's government is clear and clear, the barbarians will surrender; if the emperor loses virtue and education, the barbarians will invade and cause chaos.
In the past, Taikang, the king of the Xia Dynasty, lost the world and all the barbarians rebelled.
When the later prime minister came to the throne, he conquered the Yiyi. Seven years later, the Yiyi came to submit.
After Houxie, the title of nobility was added to Ruyi, and Ruyi obeyed the Xia Dynasty from then on.
When Hou Jie was in turmoil, the Yi people came to live in the Linqi area. After the rise of Chengtang, he conquered the Yiyi and made them retreat.
When the Yin Dynasty weakened in the middle period, all barbarians rebelled.
When Wuding arrived, he conquered Xirong and Guifang, and it took three years to conquer them.
So the poem says: Since the time of Di Qiang, no one has dared not to come to pay homage to the Emperor.
When Wu Yi was brutal and cruel, and the dog soldiers invaded the border, Zhou Gugong Yi's father crossed Liangshan and took refuge at the foot of Qishan Mountain.
At the time of his son Ji Li, he conquered the Xiluo Guirong.
During the reign of Taiding, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe in Yanjing, and the Rong tribe defeated Zhou's army.
Two years later, when Zhou's troops defeated Yu Wu's Rong tribe, Taiding appointed Ji Li as priest.
From then on, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe of Shihu and Yitu, and won both of them.
When King Wen was appointed as the Western Bodhisattva, there were Kun barbarians to the west of the Zhou Dynasty, and there were dangers to the north from the Ming dynasties. So King Wen repulsed the Rong and Di and garrisoned troops there, and all of the Rong and Di surrendered.
King Wen then commanded the Xirong and conquered the countries that had betrayed the Yin and Shang dynasties to serve King Zhou.
When King Wu attacked Shang, the Qiang people and Zhang Ren led their troops to meet in Muye.
At the time of King Mu, the Rongdi did not pay tribute to the Zhou Dynasty. King Mu then marched westward against the Quanrong, captured the five kings of the Quanrong, and obtained four white deer and four white wolves. King Mu then moved the Rong people to Taiyuan.
During the reign of King Yi, the Zhou Dynasty was weak and the Rong people from the outlying areas did not come to worship. The emperor ordered Duke Guo to lead a division of six armies to attack the Rong people in Taiyuan as far as Yuquan and obtained a thousand horses.
King Li was cruel, and the Rong and Di invaded and plundered. He even entered Quanqiu and killed Qin Zhong's family. The emperor ordered to conquer the Rong people, but they could not win.
In the fourth year after King Xuan succeeded to the throne, he sent Qin Zhong to attack the Rong people, but Qin Zhong was killed by the Rong people.
The emperor then summoned Duke Zhuang, son of Qin Zhong, and gave him seven thousand troops to conquer the Rong people. He defeated the Rong people, and the Rong people retreated slightly.
Twenty-seven years later, the emperor sent an army to attack the Rong people in Taiyuan, but could not win.
Five years later, the emperor conquered Tiao Rong and Ben Rong, and the emperor's army was defeated by the Rong people.
Two years later, the Jin people defeated the Beirong at Xiaxi by the Fen River. The Rong people also destroyed Jianghou's fiefdom.
The next year, the emperor conquered Shen Rong and defeated him.
Ten years later, King You ordered Bo Shi to conquer the Rong people in Liuji. As a result, the army was defeated and Bo Shi died there.
This year, the Rong people surrounded Quanqiu and captured Qin Xianggong's brother and uncle.
At that time, King You was fatuous and cruel, and barbarians from all directions invaded alternately. As a result, King You deposed Queen Shen and made Bao Si the queen.
The Marquis of Shen was angry, so he invaded the Zhou Dynasty with his troops and killed King You in Mount Li. Zhou then moved eastward to Luoyi, and Qin Xianggong attacked the Rong people to rescue the Zhou Dynasty.
Two years later, Xinghou defeated Beirong.
By the end of King Ping's reign, the Zhou Dynasty finally weakened. The Rong people are approaching the Central Plains, and there are Rong people everywhere from Longshan to the east to Yishui and Luoshui.
At this time, there were the armies of Di, Xi, Bang, and Ji in the upper reaches of the Wei River, the Rong of Yiqu in the north of the Jing River, the Rong of Dali in the Luo River, the Li Rong in the south bank of the Wei River, the Rong of Yang Ju and Quan Gao in the upper reaches of the Yishui River, and the Rong of Manshi in the west of the upper reaches of the Ying River.
During the Spring and Autumn Period, Rong people occasionally entered the Central Plains and participated in alliances with various Chinese countries.
Duke Zhuang of Lu attacked Qin and captured the state and the army of Ji.
More than ten years later, Jin lost Li Rong. At this time, Yi and Luo Zhirong became stronger and invaded Cao and Lu eastward. Nineteen years later, they finally entered the capital of the emperor. So Qin and Jin attacked the Rong people to rescue the emperor of Zhou.
Two years later, the Rong invaded the capital again. Duke Huan of Qi fine-tuned the troops of the princely states to garrison in Zhou.
Nine years later, Lu Hunrong moved from Guazhou to Yichuan, and Yunrong moved to the Weishui and Youshui areas, and he arrived in Nanyuan with his face tied.
Those south of the Yellow River and north of the mountains are called Yinrong, and the Yinrong race multiplies more and more.
Duke Wen of Jin wanted to establish his hegemony, so he bribed Rong Di and asked them to open a road to assist the emperor of Zhou.
Duke Mugong of Qin got the rest of the Rong people and finally dominated Xirong and opened up thousands of miles of land.
At the time of Duke Mourning of the Jin Dynasty, Wei Jiang was sent to make peace with the Rong and once again established his hegemony.
At this time, Chu and Jin were very powerful and used their power to make the Rong obey. Lu Hun, Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong served Jin, but the Man clan followed Chu.
Later, Lu Hun betrayed the Jin State, and the Jin State sent Xun Wu to eliminate Lu Hun.
Forty-four years later, the Chu State captured the Man clan and imprisoned them all.
At this time, Yiqu and Dali were the most powerful, building dozens of cities and calling themselves kings.
In the eighth year of King Zhen of Zhou, Duke Li of Qin destroyed Dali and occupied Dali's territory.
The State of Zhao also destroyed Dai Rong, which was Beirong.
Han and Wei gradually annexed Yi, Luo Zhirong and Yin Rong and eliminated them.
Those Rong people who slipped through the net all fled westward over the Pishan and Longshan mountains.
Since then, no Rong people have invaded the Central Plains, leaving only the Yiqu Rong tribe.
In the twenty-fifth year of King Zhen's reign, Qin attacked Yiqu and captured King Yiqu.
Fourteen years later, Yiqu invaded Qin and reached the south bank of the Wei River.
More than a hundred years later, Yiqu defeated the Qin army in Luoshui.
Four years later, war broke out in Yiqu. King Qin Hui sent his concubine Chang Cao to lead the army to pacify Yiqu. From then on, Yiqu became a vassal of Qin.
Eight years later, Qin attacked Yiqu and occupied Yuzhi.
Two years later, Yiqu defeated the Qin army at Li Bo.
The next year, Qin attacked Yiqu and captured twenty-five cities in Tujing.
When King Zhao of Qin succeeded to the throne, the Yiqu Dynasty met King Qin and had an affair with King Zhao's mother, Queen Mother Xuan, and gave birth to two sons.
Forty-three years to King Nan of Zhou Dynasty. Empress Dowager Xuan trapped and killed King Yiqu in Ganquan Palace, then sent troops to destroy the Yi orangs, and began to set up Sui Ning, Li Ning and Shang Deng there.
The Rong people originally had no kings and leaders. In the late Shumu years, at the turn of Hu and Er, some Rong people followed the princes and mubos in the battles and made meritorious service. The emperor granted them titles and became vassal states.
During the Zhoutang period, Luo Yun Rong and Man clan Rong were called sons. During the Warring States period, Dali and Yiqu were called kings. When the Rong clan declined and perished, the remaining Rong people all resumed their former title of chief.
The Qiang people were unyielding and were captured by the Qin State during the reign of Duke Li of Qin and became slaves.
I don’t know which Rong tribe Yuan Yi belongs to.
Later, Xingren was able to escape, but the Qin people pursued him closely, so he hid in a cave and escaped.
The messenger said that Miao Xing was hiding in a cave and wrapping his face, and Tongken people burned him with fire. Something like a tiger blocked the fire for Yuan Ren, and Yuan Ren was able to survive.
After escaping, he met the woman whose nose had been cut off in the wild, and they got married.
The woman felt ashamed of her appearance, so she let her hair cover her face. Therefore, the Qiang people made it a custom to wear their hair. Yuanren and his wife fled together to the three rivers.
The Qiang people were surprised to see that Yuan Ren was not burned to death. They thought that Yuan Ren was a god. They all respected him, served him, and elected him as their chieftain. The Yellow River and Huangshui areas are short of grain and have many animals, so the Qiang people make hunting their main occupation. Yuan Ren taught the Qiang people to farm and raise livestock, and finally gained the respect and trust of the Qiang people. The number of messengers from the tribe who defected to him increased day by day.
The Qiang people called Nu "Wu Yi". Because Yuan Ren had been a slave, they called him "Wu Yi".
Since then, Yuan Ren's descendants have been the leaders of the Qiang people for generations.
By the time of Yuan Chi's great-grandson Mo, Duke Tong Fu had just succeeded to the throne. Duke Xu wanted to restore the achievements of Duke Mu of Qin, so he sent troops to reach the upper reaches of Chengcheng and wiped out Di Maungrong.
Ren's uncle Yin was afraid of the power of Qin, so he led his tribe and affiliated tribes southward, out of the meander of the Cizhi River, and then westward for thousands of miles. He was far away from other Qiang tribes and no longer had any contact with them.
Their descendants separated and became tribes, and they moved wherever they pleased.
Some become yak species, which are poor in crossing mountains; some become white horse species, which are poor in huts; some become silver carps, which are poor in far-out tunnels.
Mo and his younger brother Wu stayed alone in Huangzhong and married many wives.
The nine sons born to Ren became the nine races, and the seventeen sons born to Wu became the seventeen races. The prosperity of the Qiang people began at this time.
When Ren's son Yan succeeded to the throne, Qin Xiaogong became powerful and dominated, and used force to make the Qiang Rong obey.
Duke Xiao of Qin sent Prince Si to lead ninety-two Rong Di Kingdoms to pay homage to King Zhou Xian.
Yan is very strong, so the Qiang people call the descendants of Qiang Yanzhong.
By the time of Qin Shihuang, the Qin State was bent on annexing the six kingdoms and was busy fighting against the princes. The army did not go westward, so the Qiang people were able to thrive.
After the Qin State annexed the world, it sent Meng Tian to lead the army to capture the land, expel the Rong tribe to the west, drive back the Di tribe to the north, and build the Great Wall to block the Qiang and Di tribes. The Qiang people never crossed south again.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu Maodun had a strong army, defeated the Donghu, drove away the Yuezhi, and shocked the barbarians and made the Qiang people surrender.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Yanzhong Liuhe led his tribe and requested to guard the Longxi frontier fortress, so he moved Liuhe and others to Didao and Angu, and some moved to Lintao, Didao and Qiangdao counties.
By the time Emperor Wu conquered the barbarians, he opened up the country, expanded the country's borders, defeated the Xiongnu to the north, and expelled the Qiang to the west. He then crossed the Yellow River and Huangshui River and built Lingju fortress. He began to open up the Hexi Corridor, set up four counties, and opened the road to Yumen Pass, which separated the Qiang and Hu people, so that the Qiang and Hu people could not collude in the north and south.
During the war, the castles and beacon towers of the frontier fortress stretched thousands of miles beyond the Great Wall.
At that time, the Xianling Qiang and Fengyang Laojie settled their grievances, formed an alliance, colluded with the Xiongnu, and gathered more than 100,000 troops to attack Lingju and Angu together, and then surrounded Paohan.
The Han Dynasty sent General Li Xi and Lang Zhongling Xu Ziwei with 100,000 troops to attack and put down the invaders.
The imperial court began to set up captains to protect the Qiang and lead the Qiang people with integrity.
Only then did the Qiang people leave Huangzhong and live near the West Sea and Yanchi.
The Han Dynasty relied on the mountains as a barrier and the Hexi area was empty and deserted. The court gradually moved the population to enrich Hexi.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Yiqu Anguo, the Guanglu doctor, was sent to inspect various Qiang tribes. The first Ling Qiang chieftain said: "I hope I can cross the Huangshui River and go to places where people do not farm to graze their cattle."
Anguo reported the matter to the court, but the later general Zhao Chongguo thought he could not agree.
In the future, because of the previous words, the Qiang people will cross the Huangshui River, and the counties will be unable to stop them.
In the third year of Yuankang, Xianling Qiang formed a large-scale alliance with various Qiang tribes and swore an oath to invade the border.
After the emperor found out, he sent Sere to lead an army to observe the movements of the Qiang people.
As soon as Anguo arrived, he summoned more than forty chiefs of the Xianling Qiang and killed them. Then he allowed his troops to attack the Xianling Qiang and killed more than a thousand people.
In this way, all the Qiang people were resentful and angry, so they invaded Jincheng.
The imperial court sent Zhao Chongguo and other generals to lead 60,000 troops to attack the Qiang people, and defeated and put down the police.
Sun Shaodang, the thirteenth generation of Yan, succeeded to the throne.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, seven Qiang tribes including Xiangjie invaded Longxi. The imperial court sent right general Feng Fengshi to defeat the Qiang people and make them surrender.
From the fifth generation of Yuanren to Yan, Yan was the strongest. From then on, the Qiang people used Yan as their tribal title.
Thirteen generations later, Shaodang was passed down to Shaodang. Shaodang was strong and strong, and the descendants of Shaodang took Shaodang as their tribal name.
In the decades since the surrender of Xiangjie Qiang, barbarians from all over the world have surrendered, and no war has occurred on the border.
When Wang Mang assisted the government, he wanted to show off his force and virtue, and under the pretext of pacifying the remote areas, he asked the translator to tell the Qiang people to donate their land in the West Sea. Then he began to open up the West Sea area into a county and built five counties. The beacon towers on the border and the West Sea can see each other.
Dian Liang is the great-great-grandson of Shaodang.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, barbarians from all directions invaded the interior. After Wang Mang's defeat, various Qiang tribes returned to occupy the West Sea and become bandits.
At the time of Gengshi and Chimei, the Qiang people indulged themselves and invaded Jincheng and Longxi.
Although Weixiao had an army, he was unable to attack the Qiang people, so he sent people to comfort and accept them, and took the opportunity to recruit the Qiang people to fight against the Han people.
In the ninth year of Jianwu's reign, Kui Xiao died. Situ sent Ban Biao to report: Nowadays, many Qiang people in the Liangzhou governor's department have surrendered. The Qiang and Hu people wear their hair down and their clothes turn to the left, and they live mixed with the Han people. Their customs are different and their language is blocked. They have been bullied and robbed many times by petty officials and cunning people. They are poor, resentful, and have no support, so they rebel.
Barbarian invasions and rebellions are all due to this reason.
The previous system was that the Yizhou Ministry set up the barbarian cavalry captain, the Youzhou Ministry set up the Wuhuan captain, and the Liangzhou ministry set up the Qiang protection captain. They all held the emperor's talisman to protect the barbarians, deal with their resentments and frustrations, and patrol throughout the year to inquire about their sufferings.
He also sent translators many times to inform the situation, and allowed the Qiang and Yi people outside the frontier to serve as the officials' eyes and ears, so that the prefectures and counties could be on guard and on guard.
It is time to restore the previous system to demonstrate deterrence and prevention.
Guangwu adopted Ban Biao's advice and immediately appointed Niu Han as the Colonel Protecting Qiang, holding the Emperor's Talisman as before.
When Niu Han died, he was relieved of the post of Colonel Protecting Qiang.
Ten years later, the chiefs of Xianling colluded with the Qiang people of other tribes and invaded Jincheng and Longxi again. The imperial court sent Zhonglang Lai She and others to attack the invading Qiang people, and defeated the Qiang people. The incident has been recorded in the "Biography of Lai She".
In the summer of the eleventh year, Xian Lingzhong invaded Lintao again. Ma Yuan, the prefect of Longxi, defeated Xian Lingzhong and made them surrender.
Later, all the Qiang people surrendered, and the imperial court moved the Qiang people to Tianshui, Longxi, and Fufeng counties.

Sometimes, although the Qiang chiefs were killed and defeated, their affiliated tribes were destroyed, the surrendered Qiang people and prisoners were all over the road, and the cattle and sheep obtained were all over the mountains and fields, the military documents did not report the victory and loss, while the Qiang rebellion had been reported first.
Therefore, the gains outweigh the losses, and the achievements are not worth half of the expenditure.
The army was outside and failed to win for many years. The officials were exhausted and the heroes died of grief and anger.
Duan Yi accepted the appointment and was in charge of military affairs. With his Shanxi brave personality and familiarity with the customs and moods of Xirong, he devised strategies and deployed all his elite troops to deal with the Qiang Rong.
Duan bent forward with his bow and arrows on his back and charged forward. He risked his life hundreds of times, faced the ice and snow, and walked through hundreds of twists and turns in the mountain roads before annihilating the Western Qiang people and finally pacifying the enemy invaders.
As for those who were killed and injured while charging into battle, those who were crushed and trampled during pursuit and escape, those whose heads were chopped off at the bottom of mountains thousands of feet deep, and those whose limbs were separated on thousands of cliffs, it is impossible to count.
Those who were able to escape through grass and rocks and protect themselves from swords and arrows could not exceed one or two out of a hundred people.
However, Zhang Huan strongly advocated that Rong Di and we were born from the same energy, and they should not all be killed. Bloodshed would stain the wilderness, which would destroy the coordination of yin and yang and lead to monsters.
What a pedantic statement!
Although the Qiang people are suffering from external diseases, they are actually very deep internal diseases. If they are not treated at the root, they will keep the disease in their hearts.
Unfortunately, the enemy invaders were largely suppressed, and Han's imperial fortune also declined.
Alas!
In the past, the former kings governed the nine states and divided the kingdoms and outlying areas. They knew that the barbarians had different temperaments and were difficult to control morally, so they excluded them from China, reduced their tribute, and only made alliances with them.
The methods used by Qian Mo and Hou Mo to control Xirong are fundamentally wrong.
Why?
When Ling invaded the border, Tachong's troops invaded the hinterland; when Jiandang invaded, Ma Wenyuan moved Jiandang to Sanfu.
They are greedy for temporary stability, believe that the Qiang people can be tamed, calculate the expediency of daily expenses, and forget the long-term strategy of governing world affairs. Is this what people who understand the subtleties do?
So Wei Zi shed tears when he saw the ivory chopsticks, and Xin Gen Zheng Tan Cong sighed.
Zan said: The Qi of Jin Xing was strong and spread, giving birth to Xiqiang.
The chieftains of Di Chai separated their tribes and became stronger in the end.
They killed and plundered in the north of Yingnai, and arrogated the title of king in Jingmo.
The court worked hard and was busy making plans; the army was exhausted and unable to retreat from the enemy outside.
summary:
The Xiqiang people, originally from Sanmiao, a branch of the Jiang surname, lived in a region near Nanyue, stretching from the Cizhi River to the borders of Shu and Han in the south and Shanshan and Cheshi in the northwest. They were nomadic, migrating with water and grass, relying primarily on livestock rather than grain. Their society lacked fixed clans, with tribes named after paternal or maternal lines. After twelve generations, intermarriage occurred, and customs included marrying stepmothers after a father's death and widows after an elder brother's death, leading to rapid population growth. They had no central ruler; power determined leadership, with violence and plunder common. Their soldiers excelled in valley combat but not on plains, valued death in battle over illness, and endured harsh conditions.

Historically, the Xiqiang's relationship with Chinese dynasties fluctuated. During the Xia Dynasty, Taikang's loss of control led to barbarian rebellion, but later rulers like Houxiang and Houxie subdued them. Under the Yin Dynasty, Wuding conquered Xirong and Guifang, but Wu Yi's brutality provoked Dog Soldier invasions. The Zhou Dynasty saw King Wen and King Wu command Xirong, while King Mu campaigned against Quanrong. As Zhou weakened, Rong tribes invaded, leading to conflicts with Qin and Jin. During the Spring and Autumn period, Rong groups like Yiqu and Dali grew powerful, building cities and claiming kingship. Qin gradually absorbed them, with King Zhao of Qin destroying Yiqu in the 4th century BCE.

Under the Han Dynasty, the Xiqiang faced expulsion and relocation. Emperor Wu expanded borders, building fortresses and separating Qiang from Xiongnu. In 42 BCE, Xianling Qiang allied with Xiongnu, attacking Lingju and Paohan, but were suppressed by General Li Xi. Later, Zhao Chongguo defeated them in 60 BCE. During Wang Mang's reign, Qiang lands were seized, but after his fall, they rebelled. In 25 CE, Guangwu restored the Qiang Protectorate, but conflicts persisted. Ma Yuan defeated Qiang rebellions in 35 CE, moving them to Tianshui and Longxi. By 58 CE, Dianwu's rebellion was crushed, and Qiang were resettled in Sanfu.

The Qiang continued to resist Han rule. In 77 CE, Miwu led a revolt, defeating Han forces. Fu Yu, the Qiang Protector, was killed in 87 CE. Zhang Yu retaliated by poisoning Qiang leaders, but Miwu's son Mitang continued raids. Deng Xun and later officials used bribery to divide the Qiang, but conflicts resumed. In 107 CE, the Qiang rebellion under Dianling and others devastated border regions, costing billions and causing massive displacement. Ren Shang and Deng Zun campaigned against them, but corruption and mismanagement plagued efforts. By 118 CE, the Qiang were largely subdued, though sporadic revolts occurred.

In later years, the Qiang faced further suppression. Ma Xian defeated them in 141 CE, but his death in battle in 144 CE led to renewed chaos. Zhao Chong and others campaigned, but the Qiang declined by the 2nd century CE. During the Han dynasty's decline, Qiang allied with Yellow Turban rebels in 184 CE. By the 3rd century CE, the Qiang had fragmented into 150 tribes, with the Zhong Qiang being the most powerful, fielding over 100,000 warriors. The Yuezhi Hu, a related group, intermarried with Qiang and lived in Huangzhong.

The text concludes that the Qiang's persistent harm stemmed from Han mismanagement, including broken promises and exploitation. The Yongchu period saw widespread rebellion, with Qiang plundering Sanfu and cutting off Longxi. Despite costly campaigns by generals like Deng Lu and Ren Shang, the Han failed to achieve lasting peace. The author criticizes the policy of relocating Qiang into Han territory, which exacerbated conflicts. Ultimately, the Qiang were suppressed by Duan Yi, but the Han dynasty's decline followed. The narrative emphasizes the cyclical nature of Qiang-Han relations, marked by rebellion, suppression, and eventual fragmentation.

Preface to the biographies of Yimin. "The Book of Changes" says: The meaning of Dun Gua is very great!
He also said: Don't serve princes and nobles, keep your noble reputation. Therefore, Emperor Yao took heaven as the law and could not make Chao Fu and Xu You accept his throne; King Wu of Zhou was a perfect man, and in the end he could only fulfill the innocent reputation of Boyi and Shuqi, the two sons of Lord Guzhu, for not eating Zhou Su.
Since then, the trend of seclusion has become more popular. Most people's deeds are roughly the same, but their motivations for seclusion are very different.
Some live in seclusion to satisfy their ambitions; some avoid the entanglements of big men to perfect their moral character; some seek a quiet environment to suppress impatience; some avoid dangerous disputes to seek temporary safety; some are cynical to establish their integrity; some despise wealth and honor to preserve their innocence.
However, seeing that they are willing to work in the fields and fish in the rivers and seas, must they be so interested in fish, birds, forests and grass?
But everyone has different personalities.
Therefore, even though Liu Xiahui suffered humiliation and was dismissed three times, he still refused to leave Qi. Lu Zhonglian would rather jump into the sea and die than respect Qin as emperor. Even his status as the king of a thousand-year-old country could not tempt him.
If they were put in another position, they wouldn't act the same way. Their stubbornness does have the appearance of seeking fame and fame, but they are like cicadas shed in the dust, jumping out of this filthy environment, far behind those who sharpen their heads to pursue fame and fortune.
Xunzi said it well: If you have high ambitions, you will look down on wealth; if you are moral, you will look down on princes.
The middle path of the Han Dynasty declined and Wang Mang usurped the throne. People with lofty ideals had strong indignation.
At that time, I don’t know how many people threw away their black gauze hats and left their official positions.
Yang Xiong said: The swan geese flew so high that the hunter’s arrow missed.
It is a metaphor for those who have traveled far away.
Emperor Guangwu came to the throne and sat sideways waiting for the wise men. He was hungry and thirsty. He sent people to recruit people from Qiuyuan with banners, silk and push carts. There was an endless stream of messengers on the rugged mountain roads.
For example, Xue Fang, Feng Meng and others invited him but refused to come out. Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, Wang Ba and others came out but refused to take their seats.
At that time, all conditions were in place, and people with lofty ideals were also thinking about the sage emperor. Isn't this a great opportunity to promote the free people and make the people of the world surrender?
Emperor Suzong also paid courtesy to Zheng Jun and hired Gao Feng to complete their honor.
Since then, the emperor's virtue has gradually declined, and villains have taken over. The hermits are wary and feel that it is shameful to stand with those ministers. They even walk away, losing the way of neutrality. Now record those who lived in seclusion, and those who returned to seclusion one after another after coming out, are listed in this article. Xiang Changchuan, whose courtesy name is Ziping, was born in Chaoge, Hanoi. He lives in seclusion and does not serve as an official. He has a moderate personality and is proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes.
He was poor and had no resources for food. If a good person gave him some food, he would accept part of it and return the rest.
Wang Mang's chief minister, Wang Yi, summoned him, but it took several years for him to arrive. He wanted to recommend him to Wang Mang, but Xiang Chang resolutely refused.
Hidden at home.
After reading the "Book of Changes" to the two hexagrams "Loss" and "Benefit", I sighed deeply and said: I already know that wealth is worse than poverty, and nobleness is worse than lowliness, but I don't know how death is worse than life.
During the Jianwu period, after his son and girl got married, he severed ties with his family and said, "Just think of me as dead."
So he acted randomly and traveled to the famous Five Mountains with his friend Beihai Qinqing, but in the end he didn't know where he ended up.
Feng Meng's biography, Feng Meng's courtesy name is Zikang, and he was born in Duchang, Beihai.
His family was poor and he worked as a pavilion chief in the county.
At that time, the county captain passed by the pavilion, and Peng Meng was waiting to greet him. He dropped his wooden shield and sighed, "How can a man serve as a servant for others?"
So he went to Chang'an to study and became proficient in the Spring and Autumn Classic.
At this time, Wang Mang killed his son Yu. Pengmeng said to his friends: The three cardinal principles are severed!
If you don't leave, disaster will bring harm to others.
He immediately took off his hat and hung it on the gate of Dongdu City. After returning, he moved his family to the seaside and lived in Liaodong.
Fengmeng had always understood the art of yin and yang, and knew that Wang Mang would be defeated soon, so he put a clay basin on his head and cried in the market: "New! New!"
So he hid.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he went to Langfu Mountain to cultivate his aspirations and practice Taoism. Everyone was influenced by his virtues.
The governor of Beihai heard about his noble character and sent officials to pay homage to him, but he did not respond to his courtesy.
The prefect held a grudge and sent people to arrest him.
The official kowtowed and said: "Zikang is a great sage and is famous all over the world. Wherever he is, people respect him like a father. If you go, you will definitely not be able to catch him. You will only bring humiliation to yourself."
The eunuch became angry, imprisoned the officials, and sent others to go.
When the man walked to Laoshan, people united to defend him with crossbows. The officials were wounded and bleeding and ran back.
Later, the imperial court summoned Fengmeng with an edict. Meng told the envoy that he was too old and had lost his way to the east-west direction, and said to the envoy: "The reason why the imperial court summoned me is because it thought I would be beneficial to politics. I don't even know the direction. How can I help the time?"
Hitched home immediately.
If you don't come out for continuous recruitment, you will die.
At first, Fengmeng was good friends with Xu Fang, Pingyuan Li Ziyun, and Wang Jungong from the same county. They all knew the theory of yin and yang and harbored virtuous behavior.
Xu Fang and Ziyun each raised thousands of apprentices. When the emperor was in trouble, he would not leave alone, but he worked as a cattle broker and secluded himself.
People at that time commented: "The King of the East Wall is a refuge from the world."
Biography of Zhou Dang, named Bo Kuang, a native of Guangwu, Taiyuan.
The family fortune is thousands of gold.
His father died when he was young and he was raised by his tribe. However, he was not treated politely and when he grew up, his property was not returned.
Zhou Dang went to the township and county to file a lawsuit, and the owner was returned to him.
Soon, he dispersed his family property to the clan and dismissed all his servants, so he went to Chang'an to study.
At first, Xiang Zuo once insulted Zhou Dang in front of everyone, and Zhou Dang remembered it for a long time.
Later, after reading "Spring and Autumn", I understood the meaning of revenge, so I stopped talking and went back, notifying my hometown assistant to set a date for the fight.
After a confrontation, Zhou Dang was injured by Xiang Zuo and was trapped.
Xiang Zuo was impressed by his loyalty and sent him home in a car to recuperate. He revived after a few days and left when he woke up.
From then on, he restrained himself and cultivated his will, and the state praised him for his noble character.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, the Zhou party refused to leave due to illness.
From now on, the thieves will run rampant and destroy the counties and counties. They will not come in until they reach Guangwu and pass through the city gate.
During the Jianwu period, he called Zhou Dang to serve as Yilang. He resigned due to illness, so he sent his wife to live in Mianchi.
When he was summoned again, he had no choice but to put on short cloth and single clothes, and a silk head made of grain husk, waiting to see the minister.
When Guangwu introduced him, Zhou Dang fell to the ground and paid homage. He stated that he was willing to abide by his will, and the emperor agreed.
Dr. Fan Sheng reported that the Zhou Dynasty was ruined: I heard that Emperor Yao did not need Xu You and Chaofu, but established his name in the world; the Zhou Dynasty did not wait for Boyi and Shu Qi, but the king's way was achieved.
I met Zhou Dang of Taiyuan, Wang Liang of Donghai, Wang Cheng of Shanyang, etc., and received great favors. The envoy invited me repeatedly before I was willing to get on the carriage.
When your majesty came to see the court, the Zhou party did not show courtesy, bowed down and refused to pay homage, and showed off their arrogance and arrogance. They all left at the same time.
Zhou Dang and others were incapable of romance in humanities and incapable of killing the king in martial arts. They had a good reputation and were almost ranked among the three princes.
I am willing to sit with them under the cloud platform and test the methods of governing the country.
If it is not what I said, I am willing to bear the sin of vanity.
It is disrespectful to dare to use false reputation for personal gain and boast.
In the memorial, the emperor passed it to the ministers.
The edict reads: Since ancient times, the Ming King and the Holy Lord must have some unwelcome guests.
Boyi and Shuqi did not eat millet from the Zhou Dynasty, and the Zhou party in Taiyuan did not receive my salary, but they also had their own ambitions.
Give forty pieces of silk.
Zhou Dang lived in seclusion in Mianchi, wrote the first and second chapters of the book, and died.
The people of the city considered him a worthy person and built a temple to commemorate him.
At first, Zhou Dang, Tan Xianbosheng and Yanmen Yinmo, both of the same county, kept their integrity and refused to serve as officials for Wang Mang.
During the Jianwu period, he could not be summoned.
Wang Ba's biography, Wang Ba's courtesy name is Ru Zhong, and he was born in Guangwu, Taiyuan.
There are clear festivals in childhood.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he gave up his crown and belt and broke off all relations with the officials.
During the Jianwu period, he was called to the minister's office and paid homage to him by name, but not as a minister.
Someone asked him why.
Ba said: The emperor has dissatisfaction with his subjects, and the princes have dissatisfaction with others.
Situ Houba gave way to Wang Ba.
Yan Yang ruined the king's domineering ways: Wang Ruzhong, a secular party in Taiyuan, had this kind of trend.
So it was stopped.
Returned home due to illness. Live in seclusion and keep your ambitions, with a thatched hut.
After failing to call for several times, he died.
Yan Guangzhuan, Yan Guang, courtesy name Ziling, also known as Zun, was born in Yuyao, Kuaiji.
He became famous at a young age and traveled and studied with Emperor Guangwu.
When Guangwu became emperor, Yan Guang changed his name and lived in seclusion.
The emperor missed his talent, so he sent someone with the image to find it.
Later, someone from Qi State reported that there was a man wearing a sheep fur fishing in the lake.
The emperor suspected that it was Yan Guang, so he prepared a carriage and black silk and sent someone to invite him.
It took three times to come out.
Let him live in the military camp, make a bed, and have meals delivered by the eunuch in the morning and evening.
Situ Houba and Yan Guang were old friends and sent someone to deliver the letter.
The messenger said by the way: When Mr. Hou heard that your husband had arrived, he wanted to see you immediately, but he was busy with official duties, so he did not come.
I hope you will go to him at dusk and talk.
Yan Guang didn't answer, so he gave the visitor a pen and paper, and said to himself: "Mr. Junfang, it's very good to be a third official."
I hope you can have a kind heart, supplemented by morality, and make the world happy. If you flatter and follow the will, you will be killed.
Hou Ba read the letter, sealed it and sent it to the emperor. The emperor smiled and said: "What a crazy slave."
So I drove to the hotel immediately.
At this time, Yan Guang was still sleeping and had not gotten up. The emperor walked to the bedside. Touching his belly and saying: Oh! Ziling, can't you help me govern the country?
Yan Guang still slept silently. After a long time, he opened his eyes and stared at the emperor and said: In ancient times, Tang Yao was very virtuous and wanted to give up the throne to Father Chao. Father Chao washed his ears after hearing this.
Scholars all have their own ambitions, so why force others?
The emperor then said: Ziling, how can I not make you submit?
So he got in the car and left with a sigh.
Another time, the emperor invited Yan Guang in and talked with him about the past. The two talked to each other for several days.
The emperor calmly said to Yan Guang: How am I better than before?
Answer: You are a little fatter than before.
So they slept together, Yan Guang put his feet on Guangwu's belly.
The next day, Taishi reported that there was a guest star in the sky invading the throne of the emperor, and the situation was urgent.
The emperor smiled and said: I am sleeping with my old friend Yan Ziling!
Emperor Guangwu worshiped Yan Guang as an admonishment official, but Yan Guang refused to do so, so he farmed in Fuchun Mountain. Later generations called the place where Yan Guang fished Yan Linglai.
In the seventeenth year of Jianwu's reign, he sent someone to invite Yan Guang, but he still refused to come out.
Yan Guang lived to the age of eighty and died at home.
The biography of Jing Dan, named Dachun, was born in Fufeng.
When he was young, he studied in Taixue. He was proficient in the Five Classics and was good at talking about it. Therefore, people in the capital said this: The Five Classics are rich in content and spring.
He has a high-spirited nature and has never greeted anyone with a business card.
In the last years of Jianwu, King Pei Liu Fu and other five kings lived in the Beigong. They were all very good guests. They sent people to invite Jing Dan again, but they couldn't come.
Xinyang Hou Yinjiu, the younger brother of Queen Guanglie, relied on the status of his relative Guisheng, so he lied to the Five Kings and asked for tens of millions of dollars to make an appointment to invite Jing Dan, and also had someone rob him on the way.
Jing Dan had no choice but to arrive, so Yin deliberately prepared wheat rice, green onion leaves and other food. Jing Dan refused to push it away and said: "I think the monarch can provide delicious food, so I came to visit, why are you so meager?"
So they set up a separate banquet before eating.
When Yin got up, the people on the left and right pushed a chariot. Jing Dan smiled and said: I heard that Xia Jie once used people to drive. Is this it?
All the guests sitting there changed their colors.
Yin had no choice but to ask someone to replace the chariot.
From then on, Jing Dan lived in seclusion, not interacting with people, and died.
Liang Hongchuan, whose courtesy name was Boluan, was born in Pingling, Fufeng.
His father, Liang Rang, served as a minor official guarding the city during Wang Mang's time and was granted the title of Yuan Bo. Wang Mang asked him to sacrifice to Emperor Shaohao, so he lived in the north and died.
Liang Hong was young at the time. Because of the troubled times, he rolled up a mat and buried his father hastily.
Later, Liang Hong entered Taixue to study. Because his family was poor, he was very frugal. He has read a lot of books and is very proficient, but he doesn't like writing articles.
After studying, he herded pigs in Shanglin Garden.
Once, a fire accidentally broke out and burned down someone else's house. Liang Hong found the burned house, learned about the damage, and used pigs as compensation.
The owner of that house is still too few.
Liang Hong said: I have no other property and am willing to use my own labor as compensation.
The master agreed.
So I worked very hard in the morning and evening.
The neighbor old man saw that Liang Hong was not an ordinary person, so he blamed the owner of the house and called Liang Hong an elder. From then on, the owner respected Liang Hong and returned all his pigs.
Liang Hong refused to accept it and returned to his hometown.
Some wealthy families envied Liang Hong's noble moral character and wanted to marry their daughters to him, but Liang Hong refused.
There was a girl from the Meng family in the same county. She was fat, ugly and dark, but she could lift a stone mortar. She didn't like the girl she chose, and she was still unmarried at the age of thirty.
The father asked why, and the daughter said: I want to find someone like Liang Boluan.
When Liang Hong heard about it, he went to pay the betrothal gift.
The woman requires cloth clothes, hemp shoes, thread baskets, textiles and other tools as dowry.
When you get married, you dress up and enter the house.
After seven days, Liang Hong stopped talking to his wife.
The wife knelt in front of the bed and said: I heard that you have high moral character and are very strict in choosing your partners. You have not agreed to several women, and I have also chosen several people.
Now that I have been chosen by you, please tell me clearly if I have made any mistakes so that I can correct them.
Liang Hong said: I want to find someone who is dressed simply and live in seclusion in the mountains together.
Now that you are wearing nice clothes and applying makeup, are you the person I want?
The wife said: I tested you on purpose. I still have clothes for seclusion.
So he changed his hair into a bun, put on cloth clothes, dressed himself up for work, and stepped forward.
Liang Hong said happily: "This is really Liang Hong's wife!"
You can spend a lifetime with me!
So he named her De Yao and named her Meng Guang.
Not long after, the wife said: I often hear that you want to live in seclusion to avoid danger. Why are you silent now? Do you want to bow to power?
Liang Hong said: You are right.
So they went into Baling Mountain together and started farming and weaving.
On weekdays, he spends his time reading poetry and playing the piano. I often envy the elegant people of my predecessors and write hymns for the twenty-four sages after Shangshan Sihao.
One day, I went out along the east gate and passed the capital, and wrote a song called "Song of Five Ains": Climbing Beimang Mountain, I saw that the imperial capital was very gorgeous, the palaces towered into the clouds, and the hard work of life was infinite and endless.
Suzong was very disapproving after hearing this and sent people to look for Liang Hong, but he could not find him.
So Liang Hong changed his surname to Yunqi, his given name was Yao, and his courtesy name was Hou Guang. He lived with his wife in the Qilu area.
Not long after, I went to the Kingdom of Wu again, and when I was about to set off, I wrote a poem: Passing through the old country and running into the distance, my future stopped and I thought about the southeast. I was confused and haggard, and my ambition was rising and falling.
I want to ride a horse and gallop, but I hate the slanderous words that hurt people.
He actually promoted the villain and abandoned the virtuous, and shouted first with a sharp tongue.
Bo Luan is not ashamed to be independent, maybe Bo Le lives in a foreign country.
What is the need for temporary freedom? Learn from Confucius and travel around.
If I could see a virtuous person and my heart would be happy, I would rather abandon my carriage and ride a boat.
When I arrived at Yanling, I asked for Ji Zha, and when I arrived at Haiyu, I met Lu Lian.
Even if the sages cannot be found, they are still willing to meet the gods.
The smoke scenery is beautiful in March in Yangchun, and the wheat is green and in bud.
Good times don't last forever, and the fragrance turns into a fishy smell in an instant.
My heart is sad and unhappy, and my stomach is full of knots and worries.
The crowd kept shouting, and it was hard to find a place to hide.
So when I arrived in Wu, I found a wealthy man named Gao Botong who lived under the eaves and pounded rice for others.
When he comes home every day, his wife cooks for him. She dare not raise her eyes to look at her husband, but often raises the plate to her eyebrows.
Botong felt strange when he saw it, so he said: "This hired man can make his wife respect him so much. He is definitely not an ordinary person."
So he was allowed to live at home.
Liang Hong wrote more than ten articles behind closed doors.
Later, he fell ill and felt very sleepy, so he told his master: "In the past, Yanling Jizi buried his son between Yingbo and did not go to the countryside. After I die, please don't let my son carry the coffin back."
After Liang Hong died, Bo Tong and others buried him next to Yaoli's grave in the state of Wu. They all said: Yaoli was a martyr, and Liang Boluan was very noble, which allowed them to get close.
After the burial, the wife returned to Fufeng.
At first, Liang Hong's friend Gao Hui from Jingzhao liked to read "Laozi" when he was young and lived in seclusion in Huayin Mountain.
When Liang Hong traveled east, he thought of Gao Hui and wrote a poem: Birds are chirping looking for friends, and I also think of Gao Hui, hoping he can come here. The two never met again.
Gao Hui was also a proud man and had never been an official in his life.
Gao Fengzhuan, Gao Feng, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Nanyang Ye.
When he was young, he was a student, and his family was engaged in farming. However, Gao Feng specialized in reading and never rested day and night.
My wife once went to work in the fields and dried the wheat in the courtyard, calling Gao Feng to protect the chickens.
At this time, it was raining heavily, but Gao Feng was holding a bamboo pole and chanting scriptures. Unconsciously, the rainwater flowed into the wheat.
When his wife came back, she felt strange and asked him, and he realized it.
Later he became a famous Confucian and taught his disciples in the Western Tang Mountains.
Neighbors who were fighting over property were fighting with weapons. Gao Feng went to try to persuade him. As a last resort, he took off his turban, knelt, and resolutely requested: "Why have you forgotten all about benevolence, righteousness, and humiliation?"
The combatants were moved and put down their weapons to apologize to him.
Gao Feng was old, but he persisted in his ambitions tirelessly, and his reputation spread far and wide.
The eunuch continued to summon him, but Gao Feng was afraid that he would not be able to avoid it. He claimed that he was from the Wu family and should not be an official. He also pretended to have a lawsuit with his widowed sister-in-law over property, so he did not go out to serve as an official.
He fished invisibly and died at home. Tai Tong's biography, Tai Tong's courtesy name is Xiaowei, and he was born in Ye, Wei County. He lives in seclusion in Wu'an Mountain, digging caves as his residence and collecting medicine as his occupation.
During the early years of Jian's reign, he was not summoned by the state.
When the governor arrived at Ye, he sent an official to visit Tai Tong.
Tong Zaibing went to express his thanks.
The governor took the meeting gift and asked Tong: "It's very hard for Xiaowei to live like this. What should I do?"
Tong said: Fortunately, I was able to save my life and maintain my peace.
Isn't it like having an envoy read out the imperial edict in the morning and working hard at night? Isn't it not painful?
So he left, secluded himself, and never disappeared.
According to the biography of Han Kang, Han Kang's courtesy name was Boxiu, also known as Tianxiu, and he was a native of Baling, Jingzhao.
The family background is very famous.
He often went to famous mountains to collect medicinal herbs and sold them in Chang'an market. The price was always the same for more than thirty years.
At that time, a girl asked Han Kang to buy medicine, but Kang insisted that the original price should remain unchanged.
The girl lost her temper and said: Are you Han Boxiu?
Aren't they sold at two prices?
Han Kang sighed and said: "I originally wanted to keep my name from others, but now the little girl knows my name, why are I selling medicine?"
So he fled to Baling Mountain.
The doctor invited Han Kang several times on his bus, but Han Kang never came.
Emperor Huan prepared a black silk curtain as a gift and used a carriage to hire him.
The envoy went to Han Kang's home with the emperor's edict, but Han Kang had no choice but to agree.
But instead of taking an An chariot, he took a diesel chariot and set off early in the morning before the messenger set off.

When I was young, I loved the learning of Huangdi and Laozi. I lived in seclusion in the valley, built a house in a cave, and admired the skills of pine and Qiao Daoyin.

I think what do you think of it, sir?

In today's Ming Dynasty, the world has opened up. Chao and Xu Wuwei are in Jishan, while Yi and Qihui are in Shouyang Mountain.
Being able to ride a dragon or a phoenix or fly among the clouds with one single step is beyond the imagination of a fox, rabbit or sparrow.
Jiao Shen didn't answer.

Ma Yao, a native of the same county as Jiao Shen, lives in seclusion in the mountains and makes a living by catching rabbits.

Dai Liang's talents were both high and unique, and often surprised the common people.
Xie Jixiao from the same county asked: Who do you think can be compared with others in the world?

He is a great Confucian in Kansai who is eager to learn and not stick to any particular school. He is well versed in both internal and external classics.

The true nature of Dharma is quiet and has few desires, and is not interested in hearing about human affairs.

Tongjun Tian Ruo recommends Fa Zhen Dao: A scholar of Fa Zhen, proficient in poetry, calligraphy, etiquette, and music, with all the knowledge and classics, goes out of the deep mountains, entertains himself peacefully, and is happy to forget his worries. I wish that the Holy Dynasty would add the post of Sangong, and I would definitely be able to sing the song "Qing Temple" and attract the phoenix.
It happened that Emperor Shun was on a hunting tour in the west, and Tian Ruo recommended him.
Emperor Xu wanted to invite him, so he called him four times.
Fazhen said: Since I can't escape from this world, how can I drink the water that Xuyou washes my ears with?

My friend Guo Zhengcheng said: Fazhen's name can be heard, but his body is rare. If he runs away from his name but his name follows me, he avoids his name but his name follows me. He can be regarded as a master of all generations.
