He died at the age of eighty-nine, five years after his death.
The biography of Hanyin Laofu, Hanyin Laofu, I don’t know who he is.
During the Yanxi period of Emperor Huan, the emperor was lucky enough to visit the mausoleum, pass by Yunmeng, and visit the Mianshui River. The common people all went to see it, and there was an old man who continued to farm alone.
Zhang Wen, the minister of Nanyang, felt strange and sent someone to ask: "People are coming to watch, but my father keeps plowing alone. Why?"
The old man smiled but did not answer.
Zhang Wen came down and walked a hundred steps to talk to his father in person.
The old father said: I am a savage and I don’t understand this.
May I ask why the emperor was established because of chaos in the world?
Or is it to establish the emperor because of governance?
Is the purpose of establishing the Son of Heaven to be the father of all people in the world?
Or enslave the common people to support the emperor?
In the past, the sage kings ruled the world, raised rafters and raised rafters, and all surnames were peaceful.
Today, your king works hard for the people but indulges himself and enjoys leisurely life without restraint.
I'm ashamed of you. How can you bear to let others watch?
Zhang Wen was greatly ashamed after hearing this.
Ask him his name and leave without telling him.
The biography of Chen Liu's father, Chen Liu's father, I don't know who he is.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, the party's insurrection broke out, and Huang Shuwai ordered Zhang Sheng, a native of Chenliu, to leave his official position and return to his hometown. Meeting friends on the road, we spread the grass together and sat on the ground to talk.
Zhang Sheng said: I heard that the people of Zhao killed Mingdu, and Confucius went to the riverside and returned;
Today there is chaos in the officialdom and the slander of loyal and good people. Will the virtuous and gentlemen leave the court?
If virtue is not established and people are helpless, their lives will be inevitable in the future. What should we do?
So they hugged each other and cried.
The old father walked past in a hurry, leaning on his staff and sighing: Oh, why is the second doctor crying so sadly?
The dragon does not hide its scales, the phoenix does not hide its feathers, the snare is hung high, no matter where it goes, what is the use of crying?
The two wanted to talk to him, but left without knowing where they ended up.
The biography of Pang Gong, Pang Gong, was from Xiangyang, Nanjun.
They live in the south of Xian Mountain and have never been to the city. The husband and wife treat each other as if they were guests.
Liu Biao, the governor of Jingzhou, invited him several times but could not give in, so he went to visit him.
He said to him: If you can protect yourself, how can you protect the world?
Pang Gong laughed and said: "The swan makes its nest in the high forest, and only has a place to rest at night; the stork makes its nest in the abyss, and only finds its home at night. People's choices and actions are also human nests."
For the time being, everyone has his own place to stay, the world is not protected.
So he plowed the soil on the ridges while his wife weeded the fields.
Liu Biao pointed out and asked: "Master works in the fields and refuses to receive official salary. What will he leave to his descendants in the future?"
Pang Gong said: "Everyone in the world leaves danger to their descendants, but now I leave peace to our descendants. Although the legacy is different, it can't be regarded as no legacy."
Liu Biao sighed and left.
Later, Pang Gong and his wife went to Lumen Mountain, but they never came back because they were collecting medicinal herbs.
summary:
The preface explains that seclusion has been a respected tradition since ancient times, as seen in figures like Chao Fu and Xu You, who refused Yao’s throne, and Boyi and Shuqi, who rejected Zhou’s rule. The motivations for seclusion vary: some seek to fulfill ambitions, perfect moral character, suppress impatience, avoid danger, establish integrity, or preserve innocence. While some criticize such acts as seeking fame, the preface argues that true hermits transcend worldly pursuits, as Xunzi noted: high ambitions despise wealth, and strong morals disdain princes. During Wang Mang’s usurpation, many abandoned office, and under Emperor Guangwu, hermits like Yan Guang and Zhou Dang were recruited but often refused to serve. The text records those who lived in seclusion or withdrew after serving.

Xiang Changchuan, a hermit from Hanoi, refused Wang Mang’s summons, studied the *Book of Changes*, and after his children married, he severed ties with his family and disappeared into the Five Mountains. Feng Meng, from Beihai, left his post as a pavilion chief, studied the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, and fled to Liaodong after Wang Mang killed his son. He later refused Guangwu’s summons, claiming old age and disorientation, and died in seclusion. Zhou Dang, a wealthy man from Taiyuan, studied in Chang’an, fought a duel over an old insult, and later refused to serve Wang Mang. Under Guangwu, he was summoned but declined, and the emperor defended his choice, granting him silk. Zhou Dang wrote books and died in Mianchi.

Wang Ba, also from Taiyuan, abandoned his official post during Wang Mang’s reign and refused to serve Guangwu, citing the emperor’s lack of respect for his subjects. Yan Guang, a childhood friend of Guangwu, changed his name and fished in seclusion. The emperor found him, but Yan Guang refused to serve, famously putting his feet on Guangwu’s belly while sleeping. He later farmed in Fuchun Mountain and died at home. Jing Dan, a scholar from Fufeng, was known for his pride and refused invitations from princes. When tricked into a banquet by a relative of the empress, he criticized the host’s meager food and left, living in seclusion thereafter.

Liang Hong, from Fufeng, studied in Taixue, worked as a pig herder, and compensated a neighbor for a fire by labor. He married Meng Guang, who dressed simply and shared his life of seclusion. They fled to Baling Mountain, then to Wu, where Liang Hong worked as a rice pounder. His wife served him with respect, raising the tray to her eyebrows. Liang Hong died in Wu and was buried near the martyr Yaoli. Gao Feng, a scholar from Nanyang, was so absorbed in reading that he let rain ruin his wheat. He mediated disputes and refused official summons, pretending to have a lawsuit to avoid service. Tai Tong, from Wei County, lived in a cave, collected herbs, and refused summons, stating his life was peaceful compared to officials’ toil.

Han Kang, from Jingzhao, sold herbs at a fixed price for thirty years. When a girl recognized him, he fled to Baling Mountain and refused Emperor Huan’s summons, escaping halfway. Jiao Shen, from Fufeng, studied Huang-Lao, lived in a cave, and refused to marry. He predicted his death and later was seen in Dunhuang, rumored to be immortal. Dai Liang, from Runan, imitated his mother’s braying for fun, and after her death, he ate meat while mourning, arguing that rituals should not suppress genuine emotion. He refused office and fled to Jiangxia, marrying off his five daughters with simple dowries.

Fa Zhen, a great Confucian from Fufeng, refused a prefect’s offer of office, saying he would rather be north of Beishan or south of Nanshan. He was recommended to Emperor Shun but declined, living in seclusion and earning the title Mr. Xuande. The Hanyin Old Man, during Emperor Huan’s visit, continued plowing and criticized the emperor for indulging in leisure while the people suffered. The Chenliu Old Man, during the party insurrection, told weeping officials that crying was useless, as the world’s traps were everywhere. Pang Gong, from Xiangyang, refused Liu Biao’s summons, saying he left peace to his descendants, not danger. He and his wife later retreated to Lumen Mountain.

Return home after a few years.

Guangwu laughed and left him to sleep and chat.

The four parties are falling apart and the situation is clearly visible.
Although Ming Gong has established a meritorious service in assisting the royal family, he may not be able to achieve great success.
For the current plan, it is better to recruit heroes from all over the world, make sure to please the people, build the great cause of the great ancestor, and save the lives of the people.

Let him stay in the tent and discuss strategic plans together.
When Wang Lang raised his army, Guangwu went from Ji to Xindu and sent Deng Yu to recruit "quick troops" from various counties. He got thousands of people and ordered him to personally lead them to attack Leyang County.
Deng Yu said: Now there is chaos in the sea, and people miss Ming Jun like a baby longing for its loving mother. In ancient times, it was the strength of virtue, not the size of the land, that made great achievements and conquered the world. Guangwu is happy.
When appointing generals at that time, they often visited Deng Yu. The talents recommended by Deng Yu were all worthy of their positions. Guangwu believed that Deng Yu knew people.
He was sent to lead another cavalry team with Gai Yan and others to attack the bronze horses in Qingyang.
Gai Yan and others arrived first, but lost the battle and retreated to protect the city. They were trapped by the thieves. Deng Yu advanced to fight with the thieves, defeated the thieves and captured their general alive.
From Guangwu chasing the thieves to Puyang, they won consecutive battles and Beizhou was generally pacified.
When Chimei entered the pass in the west, Gengshi sent Duke Kuang of Dingguo, Chengdan of Xiangyi, General Liu Jun of Anti-Wei and other generals to guard Hedong and Hongnong counties respectively to resist.
The Red Eyebrow tribe gathered in large numbers, and Wang Kuang and others could not resist it. Guangwu expected that the Red Eyebrow Army would break through Chang'an and wanted to take advantage of the opportunity to annex Guanzhong. However, he was busy with Shandong and did not know who to entrust with the Western Expedition. Since Deng Yu had the demeanor of a general, he gave him the strategy of Western Expedition.
He worshiped Deng Yu as the former general and divided his 20,000 elite troops equally. He sent him to the west and ordered Deng Yu to select the generals and subordinates who could join him in the western expedition.
So Han Xin was appointed as the military advisor, Li Wen, Li Chun, and Cheng Liu were used as sacrificial wines, Feng Yiyin was appointed as General Jinu, Fan Chong was appointed General Xiaoqi, Zong Xin was appointed General Chariot, Deng Xun was appointed General Jianwei, Geng Jinjin was appointed General Red Eyebrow, and Zuo Yu was appointed General Advisor, and they led the army westward.
In the first month of the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong County from Jiguan. The captain of Hedong County guarded the pass and refused to open it. Deng Yu attacked for ten days and broke through the pass, seizing more than a thousand vehicles with baggage.
He entered Anyi and was unable to capture it for several months.
Gengshi General Fan Shen led tens of thousands of people and crossed Dayang to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu sent his generals to attack south of Jie County, defeated Fan Shen's army and beheaded Fan Shen.
So Wang Kuang, Cheng Dan, Liu Jun and others combined an army of more than 100,000 to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu's army was disadvantaged and Fan Chong died in the battle.
It was sunset and the fighting was over. Seeing that the army was in ruins, military advisor Han Xin and other generals advised Deng Yu to leave at night, but Deng Yu refused to listen.
On the second day of Guihai, Wang Kuang and others believed that Guihai was an unlucky day in Liujia and no troops were sent out all day, so Deng Yu was able to stop his weapons and readjust his troops.
The next morning, Kuang's entire army went out to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu ordered his troops not to move rashly. When Wang Kuang's army arrived at the camp, Deng Yu sent an order to the generals to march forward with great noise and defeat Wang Kuang's army.
Wang Kuang and others abandoned their troops and fled, but Deng Yu led his light cavalry in pursuit. He captured Liu Jun, Hedong Governor Yang Bao, and Chijie Zhonglang General Mi Xi. He killed them all, confiscated six talismans, five hundred seals and ribbons, and countless weapons, and Hedong County was pacified.
In the same month, Guangwu ascended the throne in Gaohuang and sent envoys to worship Deng Yu as the chief minister.
The order of the official appointment said: The former general Deng Yu is ordered to: Adhere to loyalty and filial piety, and plan strategies with me to win a decisive victory thousands of miles away.
Confucius said: Since I had Yan Hui, my disciples have become increasingly close.
He beheaded the generals and defeated the army, and pacified Shanxi, which was a particularly outstanding achievement.
If the people are not close to each other and lack the teachings of the Wuchang, you, as a Situ, should give the people the teachings of the Wuchang. The teachings of the Wuchang lie in generosity.
Now I am sending you Captain Fengche to grant you the seal and ribbon, and you will be granted the title of Marquis of Zan, and you will be able to live in the city for ten thousand households.
Deng Yu was only twenty-four years old at this time. So Deng Yu crossed the Fenyin River and entered Xiayang County.
Gengshi Zhonglang sent Zuo Fuduweigong to She, leading his troops of 100,000, and together with Zuo Fengyi's soldiers, they resisted Deng Yu in Yaxian County. Deng Yu again broke through and drove them away, and the red eyebrow army entered Chang'an.

The three counties of Shangjun, Beidi, and Anding are vast, sparsely populated, and plentiful in grain, rice, and livestock. Zongyu, the prefect of Xihe, sent his son to surrender with Deng Yu's documents from various places in hand, and Deng Yu sent him to the capital.

Brother Liang attacked and had no heirs. In the sixth year of Yongchu, Shao granted Kang Kang the title of Marquis of Yi'an.
At that time, all those who were granted the title of Shao lived half of the rent from their homeland. Kang, who was a relative of the empress dowager, only had three to two of his own, and served as the auxiliary of the Yue Cavalry School.
The Empress Dowager Kang Yi had been in the government for a long time, and the clan was full of people. She wrote several letters to Changle Palace to advise against the disputes. She should worship the public office at the expense of her private rights.
The Queen Mother refused.
Kang was afraid, so in the first year of Yongning, he declined due to illness.
The Queen Mother asked her servants to ask.
At that time, the people in the palace came and went, and many of them could be criticized or praised. Among them, the elders were all called Zhongdaren.
The envoy was the maidservant of the Kang family, who was also from Tongzhong.
When Kang heard about it, he criticized him and said: "How dare you come from my family?" The maid was resentful and said that it was not good for Kang to pretend to be ill.
The Queen Mother was furious, so she dismissed Kang as an official and sent him back to his country without any official status.
After his brother was executed, Emperor An of Zhengkang became his minister.
After Emperor Shun was established, he was appointed as a servant. He had the title of Fangzheng and was well-known in the court.
Avoid illness and get special promotion.
He died in the third year of Yangjia, and his posthumous title was Hou Yi.
The historian commented: In the era of change, kings and ministers choose each other, which is the key to the initial planning of things.
Deng Gong carried food on foot and ran alone in the chaos. It can be said that he knew where he was going and what he would do. He divided half of the army to attack the gap in Shanxi, so that the east of the river and the west of Guanxi were shaken. Those who defected to his command felt as if they had returned home.
Although the achievements were not completed, the moral virtues were promoted.
Later, although the power of the city was lost, the troops dispersed in Yiyang, and Situ's seal and ribbon were handed over, the marquis still died in his years, glorious and haggard, but his subordinates were always the same. He was promoted to an official, and he returned to the court in frustration. Guangwu never doubted him, so that future generations would not see any flaws or barriers in the beauty of the monarch and his ministers. Isn't this the most perfect act of a benevolent gentleman?
Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping County, Shanggu County, and his surname has been prominent for generations.
Kou Xun was initially a meritorious officer of the county, and the prefect Geng Kuang thought highly of him.
When Wang Mang failed, Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoys to declare to the various counties that those who surrendered first would have their titles restored.
Kou Xun followed Geng Kuang to greet the envoy at the border. Geng Kuang presented the seal and ribbon. The envoy accepted it and had no intention of returning it all night.
Kou Xun brought weapons to see the envoy. Please return the seal and ribbon.
The messenger refused to give it and said: I am the messenger of the King of Heaven. Does the master want to coerce me? Kou Xun said: "It's not that I dare to coerce you, but privately I feel sad for your poor plan."
Now that the world has been settled, the country's credibility has not been declared, so the king can establish a talisman to carry out missions to all directions. Everyone in the county and country stretches their necks and tilts their ears, watching for the wind and returning to their fate.
Now that you first arrived in Shanggu, you destroyed Daxin, discouraged the whole county's desire to return to Hue, and created a gap for centrifugal betrayal. How will you command other counties?
Moreover, Lord Geng was in Shanggu and had been trusted by the officials and the people for a long time. Now if he is replaced, if he is succeeded by a virtuous man, Geng will be uneasy, and if he is an unworthy person, he will be reborn in chaos.
In order to make your plans better, there is no better way to restore Geng Kuang's position as governor to bring peace to the people. The envoy did not agree, and Kou Xun angrily scolded the people around him to summon Geng Kuang according to the envoy's order. When Geng Kuang arrived, Kou Xun gave the seal and ribbon to Geng Kuang.
The envoy had no choice but to reinstate Geng Kuang in accordance with the emperor's will. Geng Kuang returned from his post.
When Wang Lang raised his troops, he sent generals to attack Shanggu and urgently ordered Geng Kuang to send troops.
Kou Xun and his disciple Yu Minye jointly said to Geng Kuang: Handan has suddenly risen, and it is difficult to trust and return.
In the past, when Wang Mang was king, only Liu Boxheng was the most rare.
Now I heard that Grand Sima Liu Gong was the half-brother of Liu Boxheng. He respected the virtuous and corporal officers, and many scholars attached themselves to him and could be attached to him. Geng Kuang said: Handan is very powerful now and we cannot resist it alone. What should we do? Kou Xun said: Now Shanggu is complete and complete, with thousands of soldiers and cavalry, and has the conditions for a large county. You can choose where to go.
I ask Dong to make an appointment with the governor of Yuyang to work together as one, Handan is not worth considering. Geng Kuang agreed and sent Kou Xun to Yuyang to conspire with Peng Chong.
Kou Xun returned to Changping, attacked the envoy sent by Handan, killed him, and captured his army. Then he and Geng Kuang's son Geng and others went south to pursue Guangwu in Guang'a.
Guangwu worshiped Kou Xun as a partial general, named Chengyihou, and followed him to defeat the bandits.
He discussed with Deng Yu many times. Deng Yu was so impressed with his talent that he offered him cattle wine to drink and have sex with him.
Guangwu Nan secured Hanoi, while Gengshi Commander-in-Chief Zhu Jun and others occupied Luoyang with large troops. Moreover, Bingzhou was not yet stable, so Guangwu was in a dilemma as to who should guard Hanoi. Asked Deng Yu: "Who among the generals can be entrusted to guard Hanoi?" Deng Yu said: In the past, Emperor Gaozu appointed Xiao He to Guanzhong, and he no longer had to worry about looking west, so he was able to plan Shandong carefully and achieve great success.
Today, Hanoi is adjacent to the Yellow River. It is very stable and has a well-established household registration. It is connected to Dang in the north and close to Luoyang in the south.
Kou Xun was well-equipped in civil and military affairs, and had the ability to govern the people and control them all, so he was the only one who could do it. Guangwu then appointed Kou Xun as the prefect of Hanoi and acted as the general in military affairs.
Guangwu said to Kou Xun: Hanoi is intact and prosperous, and I will rise because of it.
In the past, Emperor Gaozu left Xiao He to guard Guanzhong. Now I entrust you with Hanoi to guard the transportation, provide adequate army rations, lead and encourage the soldiers, defend and contain other soldiers and horses, and prevent them from crossing north. Guangwu then went north to conquer Yan and Dai.
Kou Xun transferred letters to each county, discussing military training on horseback and archery, cutting down bamboo in Qiyuan, making more than a million arrows, raising 2,000 horses, and collecting rents of 4 million dendrobium, all of which were transferred to the front line.
When Zhu Tuna heard that Guangwu was heading north and Hanoi was isolated, he sent his general Su Mao and deputy general Jia Qiang to lead more than 30,000 troops across the Gong River to attack Wen.
When the message arrived, Kou Xun immediately led his troops and rushed out, telling all the subordinate counties to send troops to join forces at Wenxia.
The military officers all advised and said: Now Luoyang soldiers are crossing the river, and they are inexhaustible in front and back. They should wait until the troops and horses from all places are gathered before attacking. Kou Xun said: Wen is the barrier of the county. If Wen is lost, the county cannot be defended. So he rushed to Wenzhou.
The battle began at dawn, and the reinforcements sent by General Feng Yi and soldiers from various counties happened to arrive. The soldiers and horses were gathered together, and the flags were flying to cover the field.
Kou Xun then ordered his soldiers to ride in the city and beat drums, shouting: "Liu Gong's soldiers are here!" When Su Mao's army heard that the formation was loose, Kou Xun led his army to attack, defeated Su Mao's army, chased him to Luoyang, and beheaded Jia Qiang.
Thousands of Sumao soldiers themselves threw themselves into the Yellow River and died, while more than ten thousand were captured alive.
Kou Xun and Feng Yi crossed the Yellow River and returned.
From then on, Luoyang was shaken and frightened, and the city gates were closed during the day.
At this time, Guangwu heard that Zhu Jun had defeated Hanoi. Soon Kou Xun's letter arrived. Guangwu was overjoyed and said: I know Kou Ziyi is capable of the job! The generals celebrated and gave Guangwu a title, and Guangwu ascended the throne.
At that time, there was an urgent shortage of military rations. Kou Xun used rickshaws and horse-drawn carriages to transport the rations continuously. The minister only sent the amount of rations to the officials.
Emperor Guangwu comforted Kou Xun several times with simple policy letters. Dong Chong, a fellow student from Maoling, said to Kou Xun: The emperor has newly ascended the throne, and the four parties have not yet been settled. At this time, the princes occupy the major counties, win the hearts of the people internally, destroy Sumao externally, intimidate the neighboring enemies, and have great fame. This is the time for treacherous people to look at and cause resentment!
In the past, when Xiao He was guarding the pass, Mingwu adopted Bao Sheng's suggestion and Gao Zu was overjoyed.
The people you are leading now are all Kun brothers of the Liu clan. I'm afraid you want to serve as a warning to those who came before you! Kou Xun thought it was true and pretended to be sick.
The emperor's general attacked Luoyang and went to Hanoi first. Kou Xun asked to join the army.
The emperor said: Hanoi cannot leave you! The emperor refused to listen to his repeated requests, so he sent his brother's son Kou Zhang and sister's son Gu Chong to lead a commando team willing to be the vanguard of the army.
The emperor praised him, but everyone thought he was partial to the general.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Kou Xun was dismissed from his post because he was involved in the case of investigating the petition.
At this time, Yan Zhong and Zhao Dun from Yingchuan gathered more than 10,000 people in their tribe and joined forces with the secret man Jia Qi to become bandits.
Kou Xun was dismissed from office for several months, and was worshiped as the prefect of Yingchuan. He jointly attacked with Hou Jin, the traitor general.
Within a few months, Jia Qi's head was beheaded, and Yingchuan County was all pacified.
He was granted the title of Kou Xun Yong Nuhou, and he was able to feed thousands of households in the city.
When Zhijinwu Jiafu was in Runan, his generals killed someone in Yingchuan, and Kou Xun arrested him and imprisoned him.
At that time, the legal system was in its infancy, and those who broke the law in the military camp were mostly tolerated and tolerated, but Kou Xun beheaded him in the city.
Jia Fu sighed in shame.
He passed by Yingchuan on his return and said to his surroundings: "I am the same general as Kou Xun, and now I have been framed by him. How can a man refuse to fight despite being attacked?"
When I see Kou Xun now, I will kill him with my own hands! Kou Xun knew his plan and did not want to meet him.
Gu Chong said: I am a general, but I can wait with my sword at my side. If there is a sudden change, I can withstand it.
Kou Xun said: Otherwise.
In the past, Lin Xiangru was not afraid of King Qin and gave in to Lian Po, just for the sake of the country!
How can I forget that this kind of righteous deed can be done by a mere Zhao country? So he ordered each county to make a large display of offerings, store enough wine and mash, and lead King Wu's army into the border, so that each person could get wine and food for two people.
Kou Xun then went out to meet Dao, then pretended to be ill and returned.
Jia Fu wanted to lead his troops to pursue him, but the officials and soldiers were all drunk, so he went over.
Kou Xun sent Gu Chong to explain the situation to the emperor, and the emperor summoned Kou Xun.
Kou Xun went to Luoyang and was introduced to the emperor. Jia Fu was sitting there first and was about to get up to avoid it.
The emperor said: The world has not yet been peaceful, how can two tigers fight privately?
Today I reconcile for you. So we sat together, very happy, and then we took a bus out of the city and parted ways as good friends.
Kou Xun returned to Yingchuan.
In the third year of Jianwu's reign, the emperor sent an envoy to worship Kou Xun as the prefect of Runan, and also sent the hussar general Du Mao to lead his troops to help Kou Xun attack the bandits.
The thieves were eliminated and the county was quiet.
Kou Xun was always eager to learn, so he built a rural school, taught students and apprentices, and hired people who could teach Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals. He himself listened to the teacher's lectures.
In the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Zhu Fu was replaced by King Wu.
The next year, following Guangwu's attack on Kuaixiao, a group of bandits emerged in Yingchuan. The emperor then led his troops back and told Kou Xun: Yingchuan is approaching the capital and should be pacified as soon as possible.
Thinking of it, you are the only one who can put down the thieves. Come back from the high position of Jiuqing and worry about the country. Kou Xun replied: Yingchuan is strong and agile. I heard that your Majesty went on a dangerous expedition to deal with Long and Shu, so the rebellious and cunning people took the opportunity to cause chaos.
If they hear that His Majesty is heading south, the thieves will surely surrender in fear.
I am willing to lead the elite as a pioneer. That day, he drove south to march, and Kou Xun followed him to Yingchuan. All the thieves surrendered, but he was not appointed as the county guard.
The people gathered in the street and said, "I hope to borrow Kou Jun from your majesty for another year." So Kou Xun was left in Changshe to pacify the officials and the people, and to accept the remaining surrenderers.
At first, the Kaixiao tribe settled Gao Jun, supported tens of thousands of troops, and occupied the first city of Gaoping County. The emperor sent Ma Yuan to recruit Gao Jun to surrender, thus opening the Hexi passage.
Zhonglang came to serve Gao Jun as the general of Tongtong under the orders of Emperor She, and was granted the title of Marquis of Guan Nei. Later, he belonged to the Grand Sima Wu Han, and together they surrounded Weihuo in Hebei.
When the Han army retreated, Gao Jun fled back to his old camp, and then helped Kuai Xiao to defend Longnan Di.
After Wei Xiao's death, Gao Jun occupied Gaoping County and stood firm in fear of execution.
General Geng of Jianwei led Dou Shi, the senior official of Taizhong, Liang Tong, the prefect of Wuwei, and others to besiege Gaoping, but they could not capture it for a year.
In the tenth year of Jianwu's reign, the emperor entered the pass and prepared to conquer it personally. Kou Xun followed Guangwu at that time and advised: "Chang'an is located between Luoyang and Gaoping, so it is convenient to connect. Anding and Longxi will definitely feel shaken and fearful. This is because being comfortable in one place can subdue the four directions."
Now that the soldiers and horses are tired and have just come out of danger, this is not a good strategy for His Majesty to secure the country. The historical events that happened in Yingchuan the year before last can serve as a warning. The emperor did not listen.
After marching to the county, Gao Jun still could not be captured. The emperor discussed sending an envoy to persuade Gao Jun to surrender, and said to Kou Xun: "You stopped my action before, now go for me."
If Gao Jun does not surrender immediately, I will lead Geng and other five battalions to attack. When Kou Xun came to the first city with the seal, Gao Jun sent military advisor Huangfu Wen to pay an audience, but he refused to obey any words or etiquette.
Kou Xun was angry and prepared to kill Huangfu Wen.
The generals remonstrated and said: "We have ten thousand elite soldiers with many powerful crossbows. They have blocked the Long Road in the west and have not been able to capture it for years."
I'm afraid it's not possible to ask him to surrender and kill his envoy now, right? Kou Xun refused and killed Huangfu Wen.
Let his deputy go back and tell Gao Jun: "The military advisor was rude and has been killed."
If you want to surrender, hurry up; if you don't want to surrender, just hold on. Gao Jun was frightened and immediately opened the city gate and surrendered.
All the generals celebrated and said: "Excuse me, I killed his envoy and Gao Jun surrendered the whole city. What is the reason for this?" Kou Xun said: Huangfu Wen is Gao Jun's confidant, and Gao Jun draws all his strategies from him.
Now that he is here, his words are unyielding and he will have no intention of surrender.
If you let him go, Gao Jun will succeed in his plan; if you kill him, Gao Jun will be frightened and surrender. All the generals said: We didn't expect it. So Gao Jun was arrested and returned to Luoyang.
Kou Xun was proficient in classics and cultivated virtues, and his reputation was more important than that of the court. He used all his salary and salary to give generously to his friends, old friends, and officials who followed him.
Often said: I relied on the help of scholar-bureaucrats to get where I am today. How can I enjoy wealth alone? People at that time regarded him as an elder and thought he had the talents of a prime minister.
He died in the twelfth year of Jianwu and was given the posthumous title of Weihou.
Zi Kou lost his heirship.
Kou Xun's brother from the same mother, his brother's son, and sister's son were named marquises for their military merits, a total of eight people. They were all marquises for life but were not passed down to future generations.
At first, Min Ye was planning affairs with Kou Xun. Kou Xun explained his loyalty to the emperor many times, and the emperor conferred on him the title of Marquis of Guannei and the post of governor of western Liaoning.
In the 13th year of Jianwu's reign, he again granted the title of Marquis of Jiujiao to his brother Shou, who had lost his concubine.
Later, he was granted the title of Marquis of Jieliu by Kou Shan.
After Kou Xi's death, his son Kou Li succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Shangxiang.
After Kou Li died, Zi Kou succeeded to the throne.
Kou Xun's granddaughter was the wife of General Deng Zhao, so the Kou family was very successful during the Yongchu period of Emperor An.
Kou Xun's great-grandson Kou Rong.
The historian commented: "Zuo Zhuan" states that there are very few people who have restrained joy and anger, but there are many people who are moody.
Only a gentleman is the one who is happy but does not compare with others, and thinks of other people's difficulties when angry, right?
Confucius said: Boyi and Shuqi do not remember the past insults made by others, so others do not hold grudges against them.
We can see this kind of character in Kou Gong.
summary:
Deng Yu, courtesy name Zhonghua, was from Xinye County, Nanyang. At thirteen, he could recite poems and studied in Chang'an, where he befriended Guangwu, recognizing his extraordinary nature. After returning home, he refused offers from other heroes when the Han army rose. He told Guangwu he wished to serve him and achieve lasting fame. Guangwu kept him close, and Deng Yu advised that while Gengshi held Guanxi, instability in Shandong and bandit groups like the Red Eyebrows threatened order. He urged Guangwu to recruit heroes, win over the people, and build a great cause. Guangwu appointed him General Deng and consulted him on strategies.

Deng Yu recruited troops for Guangwu, defeating enemies like the bronze horses in Qingyang. When the Red Eyebrows threatened, Guangwu entrusted Deng Yu with the Western Expedition, appointing him Former General with 20,000 elite troops. In the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong, defeating Gengshi generals and pacifying the region. Guangwu ascended the throne and made Deng Yu Chief Minister, praising his loyalty and achievements. At twenty-four, Deng Yu crossed into Xiayang, defeating more enemies as the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an. His disciplined troops attracted many followers, and he became famous in Guanxi.

Deng Yu advised against directly attacking Chang'an, citing the Red Eyebrows' strength and advocating a strategy of gathering resources in the north to observe their weaknesses. He led his army north, defeating Red Eyebrow camps and gaining surrenders. However, internal conflicts among his generals led to setbacks. In the second year of Jianwu, Deng Yu was made Marquis of Liang. He fought the Red Eyebrows but faced defeats, and Guangwu recalled him, advising caution. Deng Yu, ashamed, continued fighting but was ultimately defeated in the third year, returning to Yiyang with few men and resigning his posts. He was later reinstated as Right General and achieved victories against Yan Cen.

In the 13th year of Jianwu, Deng Yu was made Marquis of Gaomi. He was known for his filial piety, modesty, and avoidance of fame and power. He had thirteen children, each skilled in a craft, and lived frugally on his fiefdom taxes. He served as Acting Situ again and accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai. Under Xianzong, he was made Grand Tutor and treated with great respect. He died at fifty-seven in the first year of Yongping, posthumously titled Yuan Hou. His sons inherited his titles, and his descendants continued in service, though some faced downfall due to political incidents.

Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping, Shanggu, from a prominent family. He served as a county officer under Prefect Geng Kuang. When Gengshi sent envoys, Kou Xun ensured Geng Kuang retained his position by persuading an envoy to return the seal. When Wang Lang rose, Kou Xun advised Geng Kuang to ally with Guangwu, citing his virtue. He attacked Handan's envoys and joined Guangwu, who made him a partial general. Deng Yu admired him, and Guangwu entrusted him with guarding Hanoi, comparing him to Xiao He.

Kou Xun fortified Hanoi, supplying Guangwu's army with arrows, horses, and grain. When Zhu Tuna attacked Wen, Kou Xun led a swift defense, defeating Su Mao and Jia Qiang with reinforcements. Guangwu praised him and ascended the throne. Kou Xun continued supplying the army, but heeded advice to feign illness to avoid suspicion. He later served as Prefect of Yingchuan, suppressing bandits, and was made Marquis of Yongnu. He avoided conflict with General Jia Fu, reconciling with him for the nation's sake.

Kou Xun governed Runan, building schools and teaching the Spring and Autumn Annals. He pacified Yingchuan again when bandits rose, and the people begged for his continued service. He advised Guangwu against personally attacking Gaoping, but when the campaign stalled, he persuaded Gao Jun to surrender by executing his advisor. Kou Xun was known for his virtue, generosity, and learning, and was considered prime minister material. He died in the 12th year of Jianwu, posthumously titled Wei Hou. His descendants continued his legacy, and his family remained influential. The historian praised his ability to control his emotions and avoid grudges, likening him to Boyi and Shuqi.

translation:
◆Deng Biao's biography, Deng Biao's courtesy name was Zhibo, a native of Nanyang, the same clan as Taifu Deng Yuzhi, his father was Deng Han. In the early days of the Zhongxing Dynasty, he was granted the title of Marquis of Monument due to his meritorious service, and his official position was the Prefect of Bohai Sea.
When Deng Biao was young, he focused on inspiration and practicing filial piety.
After his father died, he left the country to his half-brother Jing Feng. Emperor Xianzong believed that his character was noble and he issued an edict to agree to it.
Deng Biao later served as an official in prefectures and counties, was promoted to the government, and moved to Guiyang for five years.
In the 17th year of Yongping's reign, he was recruited as a servant.
A few years later, his stepmother died and she left home due to illness. The imperial edict granted him the service of Guanglu Dafu. After completing his service, he was worshiped as the Captain of Fengche and promoted to Dasi Nong.
A few months later, he replaced Bao Yu as Taiwei.
When Deng Biao was in power, he was very clean and set an example for all officials.
After serving as an official for four years, he resigned due to illness.
In the first year of Yuanhe, he was dismissed from office, given 300,000 yuan as a gift, and lived with a salary of 2,000 dan for the rest of his life.
He also ordered Taichang to send the sacrificial meat from the ancestral temple in all seasons. The Cheng Cunwen of Yinpai County in Henan often sent sheep wine and other items on the first day of the eighth month.
Emperor He ascended the throne, appointed Deng Biao as Taifu, recorded the ministerial affairs, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei.
In the early years of Yongyuan, the Dou family was autocratic, arrogant and indulgent, and many people in the court criticized and disputed it. However, Deng Biao only cultivated himself in office and could not make any corrections.
He also once submitted a memorial to remove the censor Zhongcheng Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu failed to do so, so some people ridiculed him for this, but people at that time respected his courtesy.
When Dou was killed, Deng Biao returned to the cardinal position due to his old age and illness, and he was given permission to raise cattle and wine.
In the spring of the fifth year, he died in office, and the emperor came to his home to pay his respects.
◆Zhang Yu's biography, Zhang Yu's courtesy name was Boda, and he was a native of Zhao Guoxiang.
Grandfather Zhang Kuang's clan sister was the wife of Emperor Zukao. She traveled to Nanton many times and met Emperor Guangwu.
Guangwu was the Grand Sima and passed through Handan. Zhang Kuang was a county official and paid an audience with Guangwu.
Guangwu said happily: Now I have found my uncle!
So we went north together to Gaoyi, and used Kuang as the Yuan family order.
He was promoted to the governor of Zhuo County.
He also became the chief of Changshan Pass.
Just as the Red Eyebrow Army was attacking Guancheng, Zhang Kuang was killed.
His father, Zhang Xin, first fled for revenge. Later he became the Prime Minister of Huaiyang and died in the post of magistrate of Ji County.
Zhang Yu was honest and thrifty.
After his father's death, the officials in Ji County offered him millions in donations, but none of them were accepted.
He also gave the land and house to his uncle and stayed there by himself.
In the eighth year of Yongping, he was promoted to Xiaolian and promoted slightly. In the early years of Jianchu, he was appointed the governor of Yangzhou.
When he crossed the river for inspection, the people in China thought that the river had the god Zixu, making it difficult to cross the river.
When Yu was about to cross the river, the officials made a firm request, but Zhang Yu refused to listen.
And he said sternly: If Zixu has a spirit and knows that my purpose is to investigate unjust, false and wrong cases, will he still harm me?
So he paddled over.
After passing through counties and cities, he went to all the remote places and personally interrogated the prisoners. Many cases were understood and dealt with.
The officials and the people rarely see the messengers, and the people are happy and complain about the good and the bad, and they all return home.
In the second year of Yuanhe, he was transferred to the governor of Yanzhou, and he also had the reputation of Qingping.
Three years later, he was promoted to Xiapi Prime Minister.
There is Puyangpo in the northern boundary of Xu County. There are many fertile fields nearby, but they are abandoned and no one is cultivating them.
Zhang Yu opened the water gate for them and directed irrigation, and hundreds of hectares of mature farmland became available.
He persuaded and led the officials, lent them seeds, and personally encouraged them to work, so that they could reap abundant harvests.
More than a thousand impoverished households from neighboring counties were relocated, and the houses were connected together, forming a market below.
Later, more than a thousand hectares were reclaimed every year, and the people were able to provide themselves with food and clothing.
Shi Dairun, a meritorious officer, was an old Taiwei official and had great power in the county.
If there was a small reproach, Zhang Yu asked him to surrender himself to Xu Prison and then punish him.
Since the beginning of history, everyone has been shocked and respected.
In the sixth year of Yongyuan, he entered the imperial court and became the Grand Sima, worshiped as Taiwei, and Emperor He treated him politely.
In the fifteenth year, the emperor visited the ancestral temple in the south, and Zhang Yu stayed behind as a Taiwei and a guard.
Hearing that the chariot was about to enter Jiangling, Zhang Yu thought that he should not take the risk of traveling far, so he immediately advised him.
The imperial edict said: "The visit to the temple has been completed. We should go to the south to offer sacrifices to Dajiang. After receiving your memorial, we should go to the Han River to return home."
After returning to the court, Zhang Yu was rewarded.
In the first year of Yanping, Zhang Yu was promoted to Taifu and recorded the affairs of the minister.
Because the Emperor Shang was born, the Empress Dowager Deng wanted to have the important officials live in the forbidden area, so she issued an edict to ask Yu to live in the palace, provide curtains and beds, and make the officials eat in the morning and evening, and return home once every five days.
Every time I go to court, I give special praise and have a special dinner with the three princes.
Zhang Yu said: "When the house is fierce and quiet, it is not appropriate to do business in the garden as usual."
Open spaces such as Guangcheng and Shanglin should be temporarily allocated to the poor.
The Queen Mother obeyed.
When Emperor An came to the throne, Zhang Yu petitioned several times to resign. He sent an imperial edict to Xiaohuangmen to inquire about his illness. He was given an ox and ten dendrobiums of wine, and was advised to recuperate.
They also sent money, cloth, swords, and clothes many times.
In the first year of Yongchu, Zhang Yu was granted the title of Marquis of Anxiang due to his merits in making decisions, with a settlement of 1,200 households. He was granted the title on the same day as Taiwei Xu Fang and Sikong Yinqin.
In the autumn of this year, Xu Fang and Yin Qin were dismissed from their posts due to water and rain disasters by bandits. Zhang Yu felt uneasy and wrote a letter requesting to resign and be promoted to Taiwei.

**Deng Biao** (courtesy name Zhibo), a native of Nanyang and of the same clan as Taifu Deng Yuzhi, was the son of Deng Han. In the early Zhongxing Dynasty, he was made Marquis of Monument for his service and served as Prefect of Bohai Sea. Known for filial piety, he ceded his inheritance to his half-brother Jing Feng after his father's death, a decision Emperor Xianzong approved. He held various official posts, including Guiyang magistrate, and was recruited as a servant in Yongping's 17th year. After his stepmother's death, he served as Guanglu Dafu, then Fengche Captain and Dasi Nong, eventually replacing Bao Yu as Taiwei. Known for his integrity, he resigned due to illness after four years. In Yuanhe's first year, he was dismissed with a gift of 300,000 yuan and a lifelong salary of 2,000 dan. Emperor He later appointed him Taifu and Marquis of Guannei. During the Dou family's autocracy, he remained self-cultivating but made no corrections. He died in office in the spring of the fifth year, and the emperor visited his home.

**Zhang Yu** (courtesy name Boda), from Zhao Guoxiang, was the grandson of Zhang Kuang, whose clan sister married Emperor Zukao. Zhang Kuang met Emperor Guangwu and served as Yuan family order, Zhuo County governor, and Changshan Pass chief, dying in battle against the Red Eyebrow Army. Zhang Yu's father, Zhang Xin, sought revenge and later became Prime Minister of Huaiyang. Zhang Yu was honest and thrifty, refusing donations after his father's death and giving his land to his uncle. Promoted to Xiaolian in Yongping's 8th year, he became Yangzhou governor in Jianchu's early years. He famously crossed the river despite fears of the god Zixu, personally interrogating prisoners and resolving cases. As Yanzhou governor, he gained a reputation for fairness. As Xiapi Prime Minister, he irrigated Puyangpo, reclaiming hundreds of hectares and attracting over a thousand poor households. He punished the powerful official Shi Dairun, earning respect. In Yongyuan's 6th year, he became Grand Sima and Taiwei, advising Emperor He against risky travel. Promoted to Taifu in Yanping's 1st year, he lived in the palace under Empress Dowager Deng's orders, advocating for allocating open lands to the poor. He served Emperor An, resigning several times but receiving gifts. He was made Marquis of Anxiang in Yongchu's 1st year. He advised the Empress Dowager to return to the palace during her mother's illness. After years of famine, he requested tax collection for relief. He was dismissed in the 5th year due to yin-yang disharmony and died at home seven years later.

**Xu Fang** (courtesy name Yeqing), from Pei, learned from his father and grandfather, who taught Wang Mang the Book of Changes. Promoted to Xiaolian during Yongping, he became Shangshulang, serving two emperors without fault. Under Emperor He, he served as Sili Xiaowei, Wei County prefect, Shaofu, and DaSinong. In Yongyuan's 14th year, he became Sikong. He proposed reforming the examination system for doctors, advocating for testing based on famous scholars' chapters and verses to prevent private interests and disputes. His suggestions were followed. In the 16th year, he became Situ, then Taiwei in Yanping's 1st year, participating in Shangshu affairs with Taifu Zhang Yu. Emperor An made him Marquis of Longxiang. He was dismissed due to disasters and bandits, the first of the three ministers to be exempted. After his death, his son Xu Heng inherited, later passing the title to his brother Xu Chong.

**Zhang Min** (courtesy name Boda), from Molan, Hejian, was promoted to Xiaolian in Jianchu's 2nd year. He opposed the "Insult Law," arguing it opened the way to killing and promoted sin. He cited Confucius and the Spring and Autumn Annals, advocating for removing complicated laws. Emperor He agreed. In the 9th year, he became Sili Xiaowei, then Runan prefect, known for fairness. After dismissal, he became Yilang and Yingchuan prefect in Yanping's 1st year. In Yongchu's 1st year, he was recruited as Sikong, serving according to law. He requested retirement due to illness but was refused. In the spring of the 6th year, he fell during a grand shooting ceremony and was dismissed, dying at home.

**Hu Guang** (courtesy name Boshi), from Huarong, Nanjun, was a descendant of the virtuous Hu Gang. Orphaned and poor, he worked as a casual official. Recommended by Fazhen, he was tested by Zhang Zhi and deemed the best in the world by Emperor An. He became Shangshulang and Shangshu Pushe. He advised Emperor Shun against drawing lots to choose a queen, advocating for selecting based on virtue, age, and appearance. He opposed Zuo Xiong's proposal to set a minimum age of 40 for officials, arguing for flexibility based on talent. He served as Chenliu prefect, Jiyin prefect, Runan prefect, and Da Sinong. In Han'an's 1st year, he became Situ, then Taiwei, establishing Emperor Huan and becoming Marquis of Yuyang Anle Township. He served multiple terms, including as Sikong and Taiwei, but was dismissed after Liang Ji's death. He later served under Emperor Ling as Taifu. Known for his gentle and discreet nature, he mastered court rules and was praised in the capital: "Ignore everything and ask Bo Shi, there is only Hu Gong among the mediocre." He served six emperors for over 30 years, holding high offices repeatedly. He died at 82 in Xiping's 1st year, receiving grand honors. He also compiled the "Baiguan Zhen" and other works. Emperor Ling later had his portrait painted in the province.

Although Yao and Shun were saints, they must have observed the calendar, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the positions of the five latitudes. Therefore, they could live a hundred years and become an example for all generations.
I saw privately that in May last year, the star Yinghuo invaded the Taiwei star, invaded the throne of the emperor, went out of the Duanmen, and did not move as usual.
In the leap month and Gengchen, the Taibai star invades the house star, offends the small star in the heart, and shakes the center.
Zhongyao is the King of Heaven; the little star next to him is the son of the King of Heaven.
Taiwei Tianting is the seat of the five emperors, and Venus and Mars are shining in it. According to divination, the emperor is the main evil; and they all enter the house star and the heart star, so there is no heir.
This year, Sui Xing stayed in Taiwei for a long time and traveled westward to Yemen, approaching the law enforcement.
The year is Jupiter, which means good things happen and bad things happen, but it can't stay there. The fault lies in not cultivating benevolence and virtue, and the punishments are too cruel.
In December of the first seven years, both Yinghuo and Sui entered Xuanyuan and went retrograde for more than forty days, and Queen Deng was killed.
That winter was very cold, killing birds and beasts, harming fish and turtles, and the leaves of bamboos and cypresses near the city were damaged and withered.
I heard the master say: If the cypress is damaged and the bamboo withers, within three years, the emperor will be the one to do it.
Nowadays, people in the city of Luoyang shout for no reason at night, saying that there is fire and turning around, and people startle each other, which is the same as the dead leaves of bamboo and cypress when doing divination.
Since the spring and summer, there have been continuous frosts, hail, heavy rains, thunder and lightning, which may be due to the ministers' arrogance and imminent punishment. The prefect of Taiyuan, Liu Wangzhi, and the prefect of Nanyang, Cheng Wangjin, were determined to get rid of the treacherous people. The people they killed were all in line with everyone's wishes. However, your majesty listened to the slanderous talk of eunuchs and went far away to arrest them.
The Third Duke wrote a letter asking for forgiveness from Liu Wangzhi and others, but was not investigated and was severely condemned.
The loyal ministers who are worried about the country will be silenced and silenced. I heard that if you kill innocent people and kill virtuous people, the disaster will spread to three generations.
Since your Majesty came to the throne, he has been killing people continuously. Liang Ji, Kou Rong, Sun Shou, Deng Wanshi, etc. have all been exterminated. There are also countless people involved in crimes.
Li Yun wrote a letter to the Ming Dynasty, saying that the emperor should not be taboo, and the Du people begged for death, so as to understand the Holy Dynasty, but they were not pardoned, but were killed. Everyone in the world knew that they were unjust.
Since the rise of the Han Dynasty, there has been no refusal to punish the virtuous, and the punishments used are too much like today. In the old code of the Yongping period, those felons were sent to winter prison, and they were asked for instructions before being tortured, in order to value human life.
In recent decades, states and counties have neglected their duties and want to avoid the trouble of having to ask the court officials for instructions on suspicious cases. They often die due to illness and often die in prison.
The chief officials had the power of life and death, and many of the deaths were not their fault. The souls and spirits were filled with grievances, and there was no place to appeal. From then on, serious sexual diseases and epidemics began.
In ancient times, King Wen of Zhou had one wife who gave birth to ten sons. Nowadays, there are thousands of maids in the palace, but none of them are known to have children.
We should cultivate virtue and avoid punishment, so as to seek the blessing of many children and grandchildren.
On the 13th day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Yanxi, a dragon died on Yewang Mountain in Hanoi. It was about dozens of feet long.
There are stars in Fufeng that have fallen into stone, and the sound can be heard in three counties.
Dragons have different shapes, small and big, so the Book of Changes compares them to adults, and emperors think they are lucky.
Someone heard that a dragon was dying in Hanoi and mistook it for a snake.
Dragons can change, and snakes have gods, so they don't deserve to die.
Once upon a time when the Qin Dynasty was about to fall, the God of Huashan gave it to Zheng Ke with a piece of jade and said: This year the ancestor dragon will die. The First Emperor fled from it and died in the sand dunes.
In the second year of Tianfeng's reign, Wang Mang falsely claimed that there was a strange thing about a dead dragon in Huangshan Palace. Later, the Han Dynasty killed Wang Mang and revived Emperor Guangwu.
This is still true of false talk, is it true?
The stars are beautiful in the sky, just like the king of all nations.
Those below will rebel against their superiors, so the stars will rebel against the sky.
The one who rocks is safe, and the one who falls loses his power.
During the Spring and Autumn Period, five stones fell on the Song Dynasty. Later, Song Xianggong was captured by the Chu Kingdom.
When Qin fell, the stone fell on Dongjun.
Now the meteorite has fallen in Fufeng, which is close to the tomb of the late emperor. If there is no great mourning, there must be rebellion. According to the ancient emperors and the Spring and Autumn Period, there was no such thing as the clear water of the Yellow River and the self-destruction of the school.
I believe that the Yellow River symbolizes the status of princes. The clear part belongs to Yang and the turbid part belongs to Yin.
When the river is turbid but turns clear, it means that the yin wants to become yang, and the princes want to be emperor.
Taixue is the emperor's palace of education. Its doors self-destroyed for no reason, indicating that civilization and virtue will be lost and education will be weakened.
Jingfang's "Yi Zhuan" said: The river water is clear and the world is peaceful.
Nowadays, the sky is hanging down, the earth is spitting out evil spirits, and people are suffering from severe epidemics. The three items appearing at the same time, plus the clear water of the Yellow River, are equivalent to the appearance of Kirin in the spring and Autumn period. Confucius wrote in the history book that it was a disaster. I previously wrote a letter saying that Langfu Palace respected and accepted the Qianji Divine Book, which was not acceptable to the Ming Lord.
I have heard that the cuckoo crows in Mengxia and the cricket chirps in early autumn. Although things are small, they are not unfaithful, and people are loyal even if they are humble.
Although I am very humble, I sincerely wish to give you some free time and do what you say.
The report was not inspected by the emperor.
More than ten days later, he wrote again: I saw Taibai Venus entering the north for a few days and then emerging from the east. According to the divination, a large army should appear. China is weak and the foreign barbarians are strong.
The minister pushed forward again, Yinghuo star should appear now but cannot lurk out, there must be a conspiracy.
All due to many unjust cases in prison, loyal ministers were killed.
This is also the reason why Dexing has been enforcing the law for a long time.
Your Majesty, in accordance with God's will, investigated the unjust imprisonment, defended the king of Liu, rectified the sins of the king and Jin Dynasty, and traced the descendants of Li Yun, Du Zhong and others. If the emperor serves the heaven unfilially, there will be eclipses of the sun and stars.
In recent years, there has been a solar eclipse in Zhengshuo. The three lights of the sun, moon and stars are unclear, and the five latitudes are wrong.
Some time ago, Gong Chong presented a sacred book, which was dedicated to the five acts of worshiping heaven and earth, and also had methods for revitalizing the country and promoting heirs.
Its text is clear and easy to understand, and it can be read from the same classics. However, Emperor Shun could not do it, so the country was not prosperous, and the two emperors, Xiao Chong and Xiao Zhi, were short-lived. I also heard that if you get the favor of the master, you are not in the right way, and the gods will be cruel to you.
Therefore, the Zhou Dynasty declined, and the princes used military conquest as the fashion. Therefore, Xia Yu, Shen Xiu, Song Wan, Peng Sheng, and Ren Bi lived in that era.
King Zhou of Yin was lustful, so Daji came out.
Ye Gong loves dragons, and real dragons swim in the courtyard.
Today, Huangmen is a regular attendant, and your Majesty treats those who have been punished by heaven with love and doubly favors them. No heirs are born. Isn't this the reason?
The stars of the heavenly officials are not in the Purple Palace but in the Heavenly City. It is clearly stated that they should be given to the envoys to take charge of the city.
Now he is in Uncle Chang's position, which is really not God's will. I also heard that the palace established a temple for Huang Lao and Fu Tu.
This Tao advocates purity and emptiness, admiring nothingness, loving life and killing evil, avoiding selfish desires, and getting rid of extravagance.
Now, your majesty will not get rid of your desires, and you will kill and punish unjustly. If you follow your own path, how can you get any blessings?
Some people say that when I entered Yi Di, I became a pagoda.
The pagoda does not spend three nights under the mulberry tree, and does not want to have a loving heart for a long time, which is extremely refined.
God sent a good girl, the pagoda said; This is just a leather bag filled with blood.
Not even looking. Only by keeping it in this way can he become enlightened.
Today, your majesty’s concubines are as gorgeous as the world’s, and they are rich and delicious. How can they want to become Huang Lao?
After writing the memorial, the emperor immediately summoned the minister to ask about the situation.
Xiang Kai said: I heard that there were no eunuchs in ancient times. In the last years of Emperor Wu, when he was already old and visited the harem several times, there were no eunuchs.
Later, I gradually met Ren, and when I arrived at Emperor Shun, there were more and more people.
Now His Majesty will give them titles, ten times more than before.
There is no prince to take over, isn't it because of liking them?
The minister relayed his words, and the edict was handed over to the department for correction.
The minister received the order and said: The official positions of eunuchs were not established in modern times.
In the early years of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Ze served as a great visitor and helped Jianghou kill Zhu Lu; Emperor Xiaowen sent Zhao Tan to participate in the riding, and his descendants prospered.
Xiangkai is not correct in his rhetoric, pointing out the important affairs of the country, but breaking the law with analysis, violating the classics and art, using the stars and gods, falsely entrusting gods, creating personal agendas, and slandering the Holy One for neglecting state affairs. Please hand it over to Sili, and he will be imprisoned in Luoyang Prison for the crime of Zhengkai.
The emperor believed that although Xiangkai's words were passionate, they were all astronomical and constant phenomena, so he was not killed, but was handed over to the commander of the army for deliberation.
At the beginning, during the reign of Emperor Shun, Langfu Palace Chong came to the court and presented one hundred and seventy volumes of sacred books that his master Ganji had obtained in the Quyang Spring. They were all written in white, with Zhu Jieqing's head and eyes, and they were called "Taiping Qingling Shu".
His language is based on yin and yang and the five elements, and is mostly based on shamanism and miscellaneous language.
One official reported that the book written by Gong Chong was monstrous and unreliable, so he kept it.
Later Zhang Jiao had his own writings.
When Emperor Ling came to the throne, he believed that Xiangkai's book was correct.
Grand Tutor Chen Fan appointed him as Founder, but he did not take up the post.
Whenever the governor of the village comes to take office, he always greets him with courtesy.
During the Zhongping period, both Xun Shuang and Zheng Xuan were recruited as doctors, but they did not go and died at home.
summary:
Lang Yi, courtesy name Yaguang, was born in Anqiu, Beihai. His father, Lang Zong, studied the "Jing's Book of Changes," excelled in divination and astrology, and supported himself by fortune-telling. Emperor An summoned him, and his responses set a standard for Confucian scholars. He later became magistrate of Wu County, where he accurately predicted a fire in the capital through divination. The imperial court summoned him with a doctor's title, but Lang Zong, ashamed of being known for fortune-telling, fled by night, hanging his seal in the county court, and never served as an official again.

Lang Yi inherited his father's studies, lived in seclusion by the sea, and taught hundreds of disciples. During Emperor Shun's reign, disasters occurred frequently. In the first month of the second year of Yangjia, Lang Yi was summoned to court. He submitted a memorial attributing disasters to the ruler's governance, urging the emperor to practice frugality, reflect on faults, and reform policies. He warned that luxury, excessive construction, and harsh punishments caused celestial anomalies like prolonged cloudiness, cold spells, and fires. He cited classical texts to argue that the emperor should reduce palace expenditures, release palace maids to restore harmony, and dismiss incompetent officials. He also predicted earthquakes, floods, and invasions if reforms were not enacted.

In a dialogue with the minister, Lang Yi elaborated on seven urgent matters: cemetery fires due to extravagance, hypocritical officials causing yin-yang imbalances, impending droughts and floods, the need to establish an heir, white rainbow portending coups, and the necessity to change the calendar and official titles. He recommended recruiting virtuous men like Huang Qiong and Li Gu to stabilize the state. Despite his detailed warnings, Lang Yi resigned from his appointed doctor position and returned home. His predictions of earthquakes, droughts, and barbarian invasions later proved accurate. He was eventually killed by a local knight-errant, Sun Li.

Xiang Kai, courtesy name Gongju, was from Xiyin, Pingyuan. During Emperor Huan's reign, eunuchs dominated, punishments were brutal, and disasters were frequent. In the ninth year of Yanxi, Xiang Kai submitted a memorial citing astronomical anomalies—Mars and Venus invading key stars—as warnings against harsh rule and unjust executions. He criticized the killing of loyal officials like Li Yun and Du Zhong, the neglect of heirs due to excessive palace maids, and the decline of education. He noted omens like a dead dragon and falling stars, linking them to past dynastic collapses. He urged the emperor to reform punishments, release prisoners, and promote virtue.

Emperor Huan initially ignored Xiang Kai's reports. When summoned, Xiang Kai condemned eunuchs, stating their proliferation caused the lack of an heir. The minister of corrections accused him of slander, but the emperor spared him, citing the astronomical basis of his words. Xiang Kai later refused official posts, including one offered by Grand Tutor Chen Fan, and died at home during the Zhongping period.
