◆Zheng Taichuan, also named Gongye, was born in Kaifeng, Henan. The great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong.
He was talented when he was young. In the last years of Emperor Ling's reign, Mrs. Zheng knew that the world would be in chaos, so she secretly made friends with heroes.
His family was very wealthy, with 400 hectares of land, but he often had no food to eat. He was very famous, and everyone in Shandong knew about him.
At the beginning, he was promoted to Xiaolian, and he was recruited from the three government offices and buses, but he was not accepted.
After the general He Jin assisted in the administration, he recruited famous people and appointed Zheng Gongye as the Minister of the Secretariat and promoted to the Censor.
He Jin was preparing to kill the eunuchs and wanted to recruit Dong Zhuo, the governor of Bingzhou, as his assistant.
Zheng Gongye said to He Jin: Dong Zhuo is violent, cruel, unloyal, and very ambitious.
If you lend him the government affairs and grant him important tasks, you will be able to fulfill your evil desires and endanger the court.
With your important position as a pro-German, you have the authority to guide the emperor and preside over state affairs. Chengyi is arbitrary and punishes the guilty, so he really shouldn't use Dong Zhuo's power as a back-up.
And things change over time, and lessons are never far away.
Why enter Chen's top priority?
He Jin couldn't use it, so he abandoned his official position and left.
He said to Xun You, a native of Yingchuan: Mr. He is not easy to help.
He Jin was soon killed, and Dong Zhuo indeed rebelled.
Zheng Gongye and others, together with his servant Wu Qiong and Dong Zhuo's chief historian He, jointly talked about Dong Zhuo and appointed Yuan Shao as the prefect of Bohai to carry out Shandong's plan.
When the rebels arose, Dong Zhuo convened a discussion with the ministers and sent out a large army to attack the rebels. All the officials did not dare to violate Dong Zhuo's will.
Zheng Gongye was worried that if Dong Zhuo had more soldiers, he would become more arrogant and vicious and difficult to control. He said: "Ruling a country depends on virtue, not on having many soldiers."
Dong Zhuo was unhappy and said: According to what you say, soldiers are useless?
Zheng Gongye became frightened, so he made up a lie and said to Dong Zhuo: "I'm not saying that soldiers are useless, I just mean that Shandong doesn't have enough soldiers."
If you don't believe it, I can give you a rough idea.
Now Shandong is colluding, the states and counties are connected, and the people are united, it cannot be said that it is not strong. However, since Guangwu, the country has been safe and sound, the people have lived a prosperous life, and have long forgotten about the war.
Confucius said: To teach the people to fight without educating them is to abandon the people.
Therefore, although there are many of them, they are not enough to cause harm. This is one thing.
You were born in Xizhou and became a general of the country at a young age. You are familiar with military affairs and have participated in many battles. You are famous in the world. Everyone is afraid of you and obeys you. These are two.
Zhang Mengzhuo is a loyal elder in Dongping, and he doesn't look around.
Kong Gongxu was a clear talker, impartial and impartial.
These people have no military talent or experience in fighting. They are not your opponents in a decisive battle. This is three.
Talents in Shandong are never brave.
We don't have the bravery of Meng Ben, the agility of Qingji, the solid defense of Liaocheng, or the strategies of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping.
This is four.
Even if there are people who can be appointed, there is no distinction between superiority and inferiority, and the title of the country is not given to them. They rely on the number of people and their strength. They will stand alone and wait to see success or failure, and are unwilling to work together to advance and retreat together.
This is five.
Most of the counties in Guanxi are familiar with military affairs. In recent years, they have fought against the Qiang many times. Women also wear halberds and spears, and carry bows and arrows. How much more brave soldiers to resist untrained people!
Victory is inevitable.
This is six. Moreover, among the powerful and brave people in the world, those who are afraid of the common people are the Bing and Liang people, as well as the Xiongnu, Tuge, Huangzhong Yicong, and Xiqiang. You have them as your minions, just like driving tigers to attack dogs and sheep, and they are invincible.
This is seven.
Moreover, your generals are all cousins ​​​​and are your confidants. They have been with you for a long time. They are kind and trustworthy, loyal and trustworthy, and your intelligence can be relied on.
With a united army, we can defeat the scattered enemy like a strong wind sweeping away dead leaves.
This is eight.
We know that there are three kinds of destruction in war: destruction by using chaos to attack reason, destruction by using evil to attack righteousness, and destruction by using counterattack and obedience.
Now you govern the country with justice, destroy the eunuchs, and your loyalty has been established.
Use these three virtues to kill the three of them, and follow the orders of the imperial court to attack the guilty ones. Who dares to resist!
This is nine.
The knowledge of Zheng Xuan in Dongzhou includes modern and ancient times, and Bingyuan in Beihai is honest and upright. They are all admired by Confucian scholars and are models for all scholars.
If their generals ask Zheng Xuan and Bing Yuan about their plans, they can know which one is stronger and which one is weaker.
In the past, Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Liang were not weak, but they were eventually destroyed by Qin; Wu and Chu were not weak, and they were finally defeated by Zhou Yafu in Xingyang.
What's more, now that the government is clearly virtuous and the virtuous are assisted, will Zheng Xuan and Bing Yuan agree with their plan to create rebellion and encourage banditry?
Definitely not.
This is ten. If what I said can be adopted at all, it is that we should not conscript troops to disturb the world and make the people who are afraid of conscription gather together to commit evil. If you don't abandon your virtue and rely on the public, you will lose your dignity.
Dong Zhuo was happy. Make Zheng Gongye the general and lead all armies to attack Guandong.
Someone said to Dong Zhuo: Zheng Gongye is very resourceful and has conspired with foreign invaders. Now giving him an army is helping his party members. I think it is terrible.
Dong Zhuo then took back the troops given to Zheng Gongye and appointed him as Yilang.
Dong Zhuo moved the capital to Chang'an, and there was famine and turmoil in the world, and many scholar-bureaucrats were unable to survive.
But Zheng Gongye's family had plenty of money, and he invited guests to have fun every day. He saved many people.
He, He and Xun You jointly planned to kill Dong Zhuo.
When the incident was leaked out and the others were arrested, Zheng Gongye escaped from Wuguan and returned east to Yuan Shu.
Yuan Shu made a memorial to appoint him as the governor of Yangzhou.
He did not take office and died on the road at the age of forty-one.
◆Biography of Kong Rong, Kong Rong was a native of Lu and the 20th grandson of Confucius.
Kong Ba, the seventh generation ancestor, was the disciple of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty and served as an official.
His father, Kong Zhou, was the captain of Taishan.
Kong Rong had special talents when he was a child.
At the age of ten, he went to the capital with his father.
At that time, Henan Yin and Li Ying kept themselves simple and strict, and did not receive scholar-bureaucrats and guests casually. They were not allowed to inform anyone who was not a contemporary celebrity or a family with whom they had known each other for generations.
Kong Rong wanted to see what kind of person Li Ying was, so he went to Li Ying's house and knocked on the door. The person who answered the door said, "I am a descendant of Li Juntong's family."
The gatekeeper told Li Ying that Li Ying asked Kong Rong to meet him.
Question: Did Grandfather Gao Ming ever have any friendship with me? Kong Rong said: Yes.
The ancestor Confucius and your ancestor Li Laojun have the same virtues and synonyms, and they have a mentor-friend relationship. Then, I, Kong Rong, and you have been friends for generations.
Everyone sitting here was impressed by it.
Taizhong doctor Chen Wei arrived later, and those present told Chen Wei this.
Chen Wei said: Oh, people are smart when they are young, but they may not be of much use when they grow up.
Kong Rong continued what he said: According to what you said, were you quite smart when you were young? Li Ying laughed and said: You will be very promising in the future.
When Kong Rong was thirteen years old, his father died. He was so grieved that he had to be helped to stand up. The state praised his filial piety.
He has a good nature to learn and is well-read.
Shanyang Zhang Jian was hated by Hou Lan, the official of Zhongchang. Hou Lan concealed his name and sent a memorial to the prefectures and counties to arrest Zhang Jian. Zhang Jian was friends with Kong Rong's brother Kong Bao, so he fled to Kong Bao's home, but Kong Bao was not there.
Kong Rong was sixteen years old at this time. Zhang Jian thought Kong Rong was young and did not tell him. Kong Rong saw Zhang Jian's embarrassed look and said to Zhang Jian: Although my brother has not returned home, can't I be your host?
So Zhang Jian was left to live in his home.
Later, the matter was leaked out, and the Prime Minister and others were secretly arrested, and Zhang Jian was able to escape. So Kong Bao and Kong Rong were arrested and sent to prison.
I don’t know who of the two was convicted.
Kong Rong said: I was the one who sheltered and hid Zhang Jian, and I am the one who is guilty.
Kong Bao said: "It's not my brother's fault that Zhang Jian came to me. It's my fault. I'm willing to do so."
The official asked their mother, who said: "The elders are in charge of the housework, and the blame lies with me."
One sect was fighting to the death, and the county could not make a decision, so it asked the court for instructions.
The edict finally convicted Kong Bao.
Kong Rong was famous for this, and he was as famous as Pingyuan Tao Qiuhong and Chen Liubian Rang. He was appointed by the prefectures and counties according to etiquette, but he was not qualified.
Recruit Situ Yang to give his residence.
At that time, he secretly inspected the corrupt elements in the bureaucracy and prepared to demote and remove them. Kong Rong prosecuted most of them as relatives of eunuchs.
The minister was afraid of offending the emperor's favor, so he summoned his officials to question and rebuke them. Kong Rong stated their crimes without any secret.
When He Jin, Yin of Henan Province, was to be promoted to general, Yang Ci sent Kong Rong to congratulate He Jin with his business card. However, without informing him in time, Kong Rong took the invitation back to the palace and went back home, blaming himself.
The officials of Henan Yin thought they had lost face and sent private swordsmen to hunt down Kong Rong. A visitor said to He Jin: Kong Wenju has a great reputation. If the general has a grudge with him, people from all over the world will follow him and flee.
It is better to treat him with courtesy and let everyone in the world know that the general has a broad mind.
He Jin thought it was right, and after being appointed as a general, he conquered Kong Rong, promoted him to a high rank, and became the imperial censor.
Because he was at odds with Zhongcheng Zhao She, he returned home due to illness.
Later he was conscripted as Sikong Peng and awarded the title of Military Marquis.
After three days in office, he was promoted to General of Tiger and Lieutenant Commander.
When Dong Zhuo deposed the Young Emperor and established the Xian Emperor, Kong Rong often corrected his mistakes when answering questions. Therefore, he violated Dong Zhuo's wishes and was transferred to Yilang.
At that time, the Yellow Turbans invaded several states, and Beihai was the place where thieves attacked the most. Dong Zhuo then signaled the three governments to jointly appoint Kong Rong as the Prime Minister of Beihai.
Kong Rong went to the county, summoned the soldiers and people, raised troops and taught martial arts. He not only issued proclamations, but also wrote letters himself, communicating with the prefectures and counties, and planning together.
The thief Zhang Rao and other 200,000 people returned from Jizhou. Kong Rong faced him and was defeated by Zhang Rao. So he gathered scattered soldiers to defend Zhuxu County.
Then he slowly gathered more than 40,000 officials and people, men and women who had been misled by the Yellow Turban, and built cities and schools, praised Confucianism, and recommended virtuous people such as Zheng Xuan, Peng Chu, and Bing Yuan.
Zhen Ziran, a county native, was famous in Linxiaocun. He died young. Kong Rong regretted not seeing him. Ordered to distribute food to the county society.
Even if the others have only a small amount of good deeds, they will not be treated with courtesy.
County residents who had no descendants and travelers from all over the country who died were buried in coffins.
At this time, the Yellow Turbans invaded again. Kong Rong then went to Duchang County and was surrounded by the thief Guan Hai.
Kong Rong was in great danger and sent Donglai Taishi Ci to ask for help from Pingyuan Prime Minister Liu Bei.
Liu Bei said in surprise: Kong Beihai actually knew that there was another Liu Bei in the world.
Three thousand soldiers were immediately sent to rescue him, but the thief escaped because he was scattered.
At that time, Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were very powerful, and Kong Rong did not rely on anyone.
Zuo Chengzu was rich in strategy and advised Kong Rong to join forces with Cao Cao and Yuan Shao.
Kong Rong knew that Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were ultimately trying to usurp the Han Dynasty, and he didn't want to get involved with them, so he killed Zuo Chengzu in a rage.
Kong Rong himself thought that he had a noble spirit and was determined to quell the country's crisis, but he failed because of his limited talents and empty ideas.
After six years in the county, Liu Bei recommended him to concurrently serve as the governor of Qingzhou.
In the first year of Jian'an, he was attacked by Yuan Tan. From spring to summer, there were only a few hundred soldiers left. Arrows came like rain, and the city was already in close combat.
Kong Rong could read a few books and talk and laugh freely.
The city fell at night and he fled to Shandong. His wife was captured by Yuan Tan.
When Emperor Xian arrived, he made Xuchang his capital and recruited Kong Rong as a general to be a great craftsman and promoted to Shaofu.
Every time the emperor visited and summoned his ministers, Kong Rong often made decisions, and the ministers and officials were just in name. In the past, Taifu Ma Rishi was sent to Shandong as an envoy to Huainan. He was dissatisfied with Yuan Shu many times. Yuan Shu despised him, insulted him, and took away his talisman. Ma Rishidan was so worried and angry that he vomited blood and died. Ma Rishidan's funeral was returned to the capital, and the court wanted to arrange a funeral ceremony. Kong Rong said: Ma Rishidan was ordered to handle local affairs directly by relying on his noble status as a prince and the integrity of the emperor. He calmed down Dongxia and even flattered a traitor. He was instigated by him. Ma Rishidan was the first to sign and sign the articles. Relying on subordinates, deceiving the court, and serving the emperor treacherously.
In the past, the state assisted the enemy Jin army and was not convinced. Yi Liao's expression did not change in front of the shining white sword.
Can court ministers be threatened as an excuse?

**Zheng Taichuan (Zheng Gongye)** was born in Kaifeng, Henan, as the great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong. Talented from youth, his mother foresaw chaos in the final years of Emperor Ling's reign and secretly befriended heroes. Despite owning 400 hectares of land, he often lacked food. He was renowned throughout Shandong. Initially recommended for office, he declined multiple appointments. When General He Jin recruited him as Minister of the Secretariat and Censor, Zheng warned against recruiting Dong Zhuo, predicting his violent ambition would endanger the court. He Jin ignored this advice, so Zheng resigned. After He Jin was killed and Dong Zhuo rebelled, Zheng conspired with others to oppose Dong Zhuo. When Dong Zhuo wanted to attack the rebels, Zheng argued that governing depends on virtue, not military might. Fearing Dong Zhuo's anger, he fabricated a flattering analysis listing ten reasons why Dong Zhuo would defeat the rebels. Dong Zhuo appointed him general, but others warned of Zheng's cunning, so Dong Zhuo revoked the command. Zheng later plotted to kill Dong Zhuo, but the plan leaked. He escaped to Yuan Shu, who appointed him Governor of Yangzhou, but he died en route at age forty-one.

**Kong Rong**, a descendant of Confucius, showed exceptional intelligence as a child. At ten, he cleverly gained an audience with Li Ying by claiming family friendship through Confucius and Laozi. When Chen Wei dismissed him, Kong retorted sharply. At thirteen, his father's death caused such grief he needed support to stand. At sixteen, he sheltered the fugitive Zhang Jian, leading to his brother's execution when the family competed to take blame. Kong Rong became famous and was recruited as an official. He criticized corrupt eunuch relatives, offended He Jin, and later opposed Dong Zhuo's deposition of the Young Emperor. Dong Zhuo sent him to troubled Beihai as punishment. There, Kong Rong built cities, schools, promoted Confucianism, and recommended worthy men. When surrounded by Yellow Turban rebels, Liu Bei rescued him, amazed that Kong Rong knew of him. Kong Rong refused to ally with Yuan Shao or Cao Cao, knowing they would usurp the Han. After six years, Liu Bei recommended him as Qingzhou governor. Yuan Tan attacked; though outnumbered, Kong Rong remained calm, reading and laughing until the city fell. He fled, but his wife was captured. Later serving Emperor Xian, Kong Rong often made court decisions. He opposed corporal punishment, argued against publicizing Liu Biao's treason, and criticized Cao Cao's massacre of Yecheng and his son's marriage to Yuan Xi's wife. He mocked Cao Cao's campaigns and opposed his alcohol ban. Cao Cao, though outwardly tolerant, grew jealous. Eventually, Cao Cao had Kong Rong executed for treason at fifty-six. His children were also killed; his seven-year-old daughter and nine-year-old son calmly accepted death, saying a destroyed nest cannot have unbroken eggs.

**Xun Yu**, grandson of Magistrate Xun Shu, was recognized as extraordinary by He Yong. Recommended as Xiaolian, he abandoned office when Dong Zhuo rebelled. He warned his clan to flee Yingchuan, predicting war; those who stayed were later killed. He joined Yuan Shao but, seeing the Han's chaos, left for Cao Cao, who called him "my Zhang Liang." When Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled, Xun Yu defended Zhen City, outsmarting their deception and personally meeting Guo Gong to prevent his alliance with rebels. He secured three cities for Cao Cao's return. Xun Yu advised Cao Cao to stabilize Yanzhou before attacking Xuzhou, leading to Lu Bu's defeat. He urged Cao Cao to welcome Emperor Xian to Xuchang, arguing this would bring legitimacy. Xun Yu recommended talented men like Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Guo Jia. He predicted Yuan Shao's defeat despite his strength, correctly assessing his generals' weaknesses. During the Guandu stalemate, when Cao Cao wanted to retreat, Xun Yu insisted on holding position, leading to Yuan Shao's defeat. He advised against attacking Liu Biao before pacifying Yuan Shao's remnants. When Cao Cao wanted to restore the ancient Jiuzhou system, Xun Yu warned it would cause panic, and Cao Cao abandoned the plan. Cao Cao praised Xun Yu's strategies as turning defeat into victory. When Dong Zhao proposed making Cao Cao Duke of Jin, Xun Yu opposed it, saying Cao Cao should remain loyal to Han. Cao Cao grew resentful. During a southern campaign, Cao Cao kept Xun Yu at his camp, then sent him an empty food box. Xun Yu took poison and died at fifty. The next year, Cao Cao declared himself Duke of Wei.

Zheng Xing, courtesy name Shaogan, was born in Kaifeng, Henan. He studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" in his youth and later "Zuo Shi Zhuan," becoming so knowledgeable that his classmates regarded him as their teacher. During the Tianfeng period, he taught Liu Xin the meaning of "Zuo Shi Zhuan." When Gengshi ascended the throne, Zheng Xing served as chief historian and advised the emperor to move west to Chang'an rather than stay in Luoyang, arguing that the people missed Han virtues and that delaying would cause alienation and rebellion. Gengshi appointed him as an admonishment official and later governor of Liangzhou.

After being dismissed following a rebellion in Tianshui, Zheng Xing joined Wei Xiao. When Wei Xiao considered declaring himself king, Zheng Xing dissuaded him by citing historical examples of King Wen of Zhou and Emperor Gaozu of Han, warning that such ambition would bring disaster. He also advised against establishing excessive official positions. When Wei Xiao refused to let Zheng Xing return home to bury his parents, Zheng Xing argued that using his parents as leverage was improper, and Wei Xiao eventually relented.

In the sixth year of Jianwu, Du Lin recommended Zheng Xing to the emperor, praising his knowledge and virtue. Zheng Xing was recruited as Taizhong doctor. After a solar eclipse, he submitted a memorial discussing celestial omens and advising the emperor to select officials based on merit rather than personal grudges. The emperor once asked Zheng Xing about using prophecies for suburban sacrifices, but Zheng Xing admitted he did not understand prophecies, which limited his advancement. In the ninth year, he was sent to supervise military campaigns and later demoted for privately purchasing slaves. He died at home after retiring from official service.

Fan Sheng, courtesy name Bianqing, was from Daijun. Orphaned young, he studied "Liangqiu Yi" and "Laozi." During Wang Mang's reign, he criticized the heavy taxes and military conscription, warning that the policies would lead to rebellion. His advice was ignored, and he later joined the Han forces.

In the second year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu appointed him as a doctor. Fan Sheng declined, recommending two older scholars instead, but the emperor refused. He debated against establishing "Zuo Shi Chunqiu" as an official study, arguing it lacked proper lineage and that establishing it would open the door to other heretical texts. He presented fourteen discrepancies in "Zuo Shi" and thirty-one instances where it contradicted the "Five Classics." Later imprisoned after accusations by his divorced wife, he was released and returned home. He served as Liaocheng Order during Yongping but was dismissed and died at home.

Chen Yuan, eldest grandson of his family, was born in Guangxin, Cangwu. He inherited his father Chen Qin's study of "Zuo Shi Chunqiu" and made annotations for it. During the early Jianwu period, he was considered an authentic scholar alongside Huan Tan, Du Lin, and Zheng Xing.

When Fan Sheng opposed establishing "Zuo Shi" as a doctoral study, Chen Yuan submitted a memorial arguing that "Zuo Shi" was personally taught by Confucius to Zuo Qiuming, unlike "Gongyang" and "Guliang." He refuted Fan Sheng's criticisms as nitpicking and argued that later emperors need not follow predecessors' decisions. After ten debates, the emperor established "Zuo Shi" studies, and Chen Yuan became the first of four doctors. However, when Li Feng died, the study was abandoned again. Chen Yuan later served as Sikong Litong's assistant and advised against establishing a supervisory office over the three highest officials, arguing it would undermine trust. He died at home due to old age.

Jia Kui, courtesy name Jingbo, was born in Pingling, Fufeng. He inherited his father Jia Hui's studies, mastering "Zuo Shi Zhuan," "Guoyu," "Zhou Guan," and ancient texts. At twenty, he could read "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and the "Five Classics." He wrote fifty-one chapters of exegesis on "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and "Guoyu," which Emperor Xianzong valued and stored in the secret hall.

When a divine bird appeared, Jia Kui explained it as an omen of Hu people's surrender. Emperor Suzong appreciated his lectures and asked him to demonstrate how "Zuo Shi Zhuan" surpassed "Gongyang" and "Guliang." Jia Kui presented thirty examples promoting proper君臣 relations and argued that "Zuo Shi" alone contained texts proving the Liu family descended from Emperor Yao. The emperor rewarded him generously and ordered talented students to study the Four Classics, which became popular worldwide. Jia Kui wrote over a million words of exegesis and various literary works. He died at seventy-two, and the court appointed his sons as officials.

Zhang Ba, courtesy name Bo Rao, was from Chengdu, Shu County. Known for filial piety and humility from childhood, he was called Zhang Zengzi by villagers. He studied "Yanshi Gongyang Chunqiu" and extensively read the "Five Classics." During Yongyuan, he became prefect of Kuaiji, where he promoted talented individuals and encouraged moral cultivation, leading thousands to study scriptures.

Zhang Ba simplified Fan Min's edition of "Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals" to 200,000 words, calling it "Zhang's Studies." He pacified thieves through rewards without military force. After three years, he requested sick leave, citing the principle that fullness leads to decline. Later promoted to Attendant, he declined friendship with the powerful Deng Zhi. He died at seventy, instructing his sons to bury him simply where he died rather than transport his body home. His disciples posthumously titled him Xianwen.

He has suppressed his troops and cultivated civilized governance. The generals have all returned to the court. There is peace in the country, blessings for all generations, and the world is lucky."
Only the Xiongnu, who do not know their virtues, are still causing trouble in the northwest frontier, tyrannizing China, and the people on the border are wasted and unable to defend themselves. I am worried that although the brave generals try their best to defend the border, they still cannot stop fighting.
Generally speaking, if an army is always busy fighting without getting rest, the soldiers will be resentful. If the army is hard at work without rest, the soldiers will also be resentful. It is difficult for a resentful army to accuse them of making new achievements again.
I saw the mood of the generals and the wish of the heroes. They wanted to return to the county to have a rest, and then accept the order to go on the expedition, so that there would be no resentment.
I believe that the division's victory lies in harmony rather than in numbers. Although your Majesty is concerned about the northern border, you should alternately use offensive and rest tactics.
In the past, King Wu of Shang, Tang and Zhou was good at controlling the masses, so there were no cruel and vicious masters.
It has been thirteen years since Your Majesty raised the army. The generals are harmonious and the soldiers are happy.
Now if the officials and governors are from the military, then the generals will encourage each other; if the soldiers can be treated like the central guards, then the soldiers will have a hundred times more courage.
Why?
Because the world has become stable, people value their lives, and ministers and below all miss the peaceful place. If they are not rewarded and appointed according to their merits, there will be no way to encourage them.
Your Majesty should indeed leave the positions of several county guards vacant to wait for the return of meritorious generals, and give many generous rewards to soldiers who have served for a long time.
In this way, the troops stationed on the border will risk their lives and the officials who go to the city to guard the fortress will not hesitate to work hard. In this way, the alarm system of the border fortress will be very accurate and the defensive operations will be indestructible.
The government of the Holy King must be in compliance with the people's hearts.
You are now using me, a foolish and incompetent person, to block the desire of heroes to be loyal and remonstrate. This is very inappropriate. I, Du Shi, secretly thought to myself, I was originally a small official as a historian, but it was your majesty's opportunity to create a great cause. All the heroes were away from home, and there was a shortage of talents in the court.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, I wrote a letter asking for merit, but His Majesty was so kind that he did not allow me to abdicate.
I, Du Shi, have received a particularly generous favor. According to the law, I dare not take the risk and cannot suppress my urgent wish. I am willing to step down from the position of a high county and accept a low-level position.

The emperor cherished his talent and did not allow it.
Du Shi usually liked to recommend talented people, and several times recommended famous people such as Liu Tong of Qinghe and Dong Chong, the magistrate of Luyang County.
At first, the ban was relatively simple, but the troops were dispatched with a seal and no tiger talisman as a token. Du Shi wrote a letter saying: I heard that soldiers are the weapons of the country, and saints are very cautious.

Only when the symbols are consistent can you gain the other party's complete trust, so you can reveal the state's orders and grasp the authority of the court.
Recently, only seals or edicts are used to mobilize the army. If someone forges it, it will not be detected.
I think that now that the war is still going on and the internal and external bandits have not been eliminated, we should be particularly cautious when recruiting troops from states, counties and feudal countries. We can set up tiger talismans as a voucher for sending troops to prevent treachery and hypocrisy.
In the past, Prince Xinling of Wei, Lord Wuji, overpowered his neighboring countries, and faked the military talisman of the King of Wei to break Qin's siege on Zhao. Although some things are troublesome, they cannot be saved. The so-called cost-effectiveness is probably referring to this kind of military dispatch system.
According to the memorial, the emperor accepted his suggestion.
Although Du Shishen was a local official, he devoted himself to the court. He had upright opinions and good strategies, and he was willing to accept every situation.
After serving for seven years, political education became popular in the county.
In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, he was recruited due to the case of sending guests to avenge his younger brother.
At this time, Du Shi died of illness. Bao Yong, the captain of Sili School, wrote a letter saying that Du Shi was poor and had no land and house, and there was no land to bury him after his death.
The emperor issued an edict to organize the funeral in the county residence, and gave thousands of pieces of silk as funeral expenses.
◆Kong Fenchuan, whose courtesy name is Junyu, was born in Maoling, Fufeng.
His great-grandfather Kong Ba was an attendant during the reign of Emperor Yuan.
Kong Fenshao studied "The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Zuo Family" from Liu Xin. Liu Xin praised him and said to the students: I have learned from Jun Yu.
Affected by Wang Mang's rebellion, Kong Fen, his mother and young brother fled to Hexi.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Dou Rong, the general of Hexi Province, asked Kong Fen to consult with Cao Yu and act as the chief aunt.
In the eighth year, he was given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
At this time, the world was in chaos, and only Hexi was peaceful. Guzang was called a wealthy town, and Qiang and Hu were the currency.
Kong Fen stayed in office for four years, but his property did not increase at all.
He served his mother as a filial piety, and although he was frugal, he was extremely devoted to his mother's support.
He and his wife eat vegetables and rice together.
At that time, the world was uncertain, and most of the scholars did not practice moral integrity. However, Kong worked hard to be clean and was laughed at by everyone. Some people thought that he was covered in grease and could not moisturize himself, which only added to the hardship.
Kong Fen had already established a righteousness, and governance was based on benevolence, love and fairness. The prefect Liang Tong treated him with deep respect and did not treat him with the courtesy of an official. He always greeted him at the gate and introduced him to his mother.
After Long and Shu were at peace, all the governors in Hexi were recruited, and all the goods and goods were included in the carts. The rivers and lakes were full of them, but Kong Fen had no money and could only ride a bicycle on the road.
The officials and people of Guzang and the Qiang and Hu even said to each other: Mr. Kong was honest, benevolent and virtuous, and the whole county was favored. Now that he has left, why don't we repay his kindness together?
So they jointly donated more than ten million in cattle, horses and utensils, and chased them hundreds of miles away.
Kong Fen only expressed his gratitude and received nothing from the utensils.
After arriving in the capital, he was worshiped as the Commander-in-Chief of Wudu.
At that time, the remaining thieves from Longxi, Kui Mao and others, attacked the mansion at night and massacred the county guard. The thieves were afraid that Kong Fen would pursue him urgently, so they captured his wife and son and wanted to use them as hostages.
Kong Fen was fifty years old and had only one son. He finally pursued his wife and son relentlessly regardless of the safety of his wife and son.
The officials and the people felt their loyalty and worked harder.
There are many Di people in the county and they are familiar with the environment of the valley. Its powerful man Qi Zhongliu is believed and admired by the Di people.
Kong Fen then led Zhong Liu and others to cover and attack, and cooperated with each other internally and externally.
The thieves were embarrassed and fearful, so they pushed Kong Fen's wife and son into the front car to force the officers and soldiers to retreat. The officers and soldiers attacked even more fiercely, so they captured Kui Mao and others and eliminated them. Kong Fen's wife and son were also killed by the thieves.
Shizu issued an edict to commend his merits and worship him as the prefect of Wudu.
Kong Fen became the official of the government, and he was respected. After he was worshiped as the prefect, everyone in the county did not do evil and did good, and changed their conduct.
Kong Fen made clear decisions in politics, knew what was good and what was wrong, and when he saw virtues, he loved them as relatives. He hated those without virtues as if they were enemies. The county was called Qingping.
His younger brother Kong Qi studied in Luoyang.
Kong Fen regarded Kong Qi as an official because he was proficient in Confucian classics. Kong Fen resigned from the official position due to illness, kept his promise to his hometown, and died at home.
Kong Qi Botong classics, wrote "Zuo Shi's Deletion of Spring and Autumn Period".
In his later years, Kong Fen had a son, Kong Jia, who was promoted to Chengmen school captain and wrote Zuo Shi Shuo.
◆Zhang Kanzhuan, named Junyou, was born in Wan, Nanyang County. It is a common surname in the county.
Zhang Kan was orphaned at an early age, leaving his late father's remaining wealth of millions to share with his brother and son.
When he was sixteen years old, he went to study in Chang'an. Zhimei behaved seriously and his classmates called him "Holy Boy".
When Shizu was young, he often praised Zhang Kan when he saw his ambition and integrity.
After he ascended the throne, the lieutenant general recommended Zhang Kan to the ministers in the future, called him to pay homage to him, and moved to visit him three times.
He was sent to deliver silk and lead 7,000 horses. He followed the Grand Sima Wu Han to attack Gongsun Shu. On the way, he was worshiped as the prefect of Shu County.
At that time, the Han army only had seven days of food left, so they secretly prepared ships to withdraw and escape.
Zhang Kan heard about it and ran to see Wu Han and said that Gongsun Shu would be defeated and it was not appropriate to retreat.
Wu Han obeyed and showed weakness to challenge. As expected, Gongsun Shu went to fight on his own and died in the battle.
After Chengdu was captured, Zhang Kan entered the city first, inspected the treasury, collected the treasures, and made a list of them all, without any selfishness.
He comforted the officials and the people, and the people of Shu were very happy.
Zhang Kan stayed in Shu County for two years and was worshiped as the Cavalry Commander. Later, he led the Cavalry General Du Mao to defeat the Huns at Gaoliu and was worshiped as the Governor of Yuyang.
If he catches the cunning and cunning, he will surely reward and punish him, and the officials and the people will be happy to use him.
The Huns once invaded Yuyang with 10,000 cavalry. Zhang Kan led thousands of cavalry to attack and defeated the Xiongnu troops, and the Yuyang County was peaceful.
So he opened more than 8,000 hectares of rice fields in Hunu, encouraged the people to cultivate, and became rich.
The people sang: The mulberry trees have no branches, the two branches are covered with wheat ears, Zhang Jun is in charge, and the people are overjoyed.
After eight years of supervision, the Huns did not dare to invade the fortress.
The emperor summoned the officials in charge of accounting books in various counties and asked them about their customs and the political achievements of the previous and previous county governors.
Fan Xianjin, the commander of Shu County, said: Zhang Kan, the governor of Yuyang, was in Shu in the past. His kindness was enough to favor his subordinates, and his prestige was enough to attack the traitors.
When the former Gongsun Shu was defeated, the treasures were piled up like mountains, and the things he mastered were enough to make him rich for ten generations. But on the day when Zhang Kan resigned, he was riding in a folded carriage with a quilt bag.
As for Emperor Gaozu summoning Jibu, Emperor Ming introduced Lian Fan, angered him, stimulated his ambition, and killed him, which further increased his favor and obedience to justice. This is really what a monarch needs.
However, Shu Mufan, who is reasonable, opened the gate because of his feelings. ◆Lian Fan Chuan, Lian Fan's courtesy name Shudu, was a native of Duling County, Jingzhao County, and a descendant of Zhao general Lian Po.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, because the Lian family was a large clan, they moved him from Kuxing County to Duling.
He has been a frontier county guard for generations, and some of his ancestors were buried in Xiangwu, Longxi, so his descendants became officials in Longxi.
His great-grandfather Lian Bao was the right general when he became Emperor Ai. His grandfather, Lian Dan, was the minister of the Great Sima Yong during Wang Mang's reign, and both were famous in their previous lives.
Lian Fan's father suffered a massacre and died in the Shu Han Dynasty, so Lian Fan lived in Xizhou.
After Xizhou was pacified, he returned to his hometown.
When he was fifteen years old, he bid farewell to his mother and went to Xizhou to welcome his father's death.
Zhang Mu, the prefect of Shu County, was an old kinsman of Lian Fan's grandfather Lian Dan. He offered Lian Fan a large amount of money, but Lian Fan did not accept it and walked back to Jiameng with his guests to bear his father's funeral.
The boat carrying the coffin hit the rocks and sank. Lian Fan hugged the coffin and drowned together. Everyone mourned his filial piety and rescued him with a hook. He survived after being recuperated and rescued.
Zhang Mu heard about it and sent another envoy to catch up with Lian Fan with the money and goods he had given to Lian Fan before. Lian Fan refused again.
After carrying his father's coffin back for burial, he went to the capital to study under Dr. Xue Han.
Jingzhao and Longxi counties competed to invite him, but Lian Fan refused. In the early years of Yongping, Deng Rong, the governor of Longxi, prepared gifts and asked Lian Fan to be his meritorious officer. At this time, Deng Rong was accused of committing a crime by the state. Lian Fan knew that his crime was difficult to solve, so he wanted to use his power to help him. Pretending to be sick, Deng asked for leave and left. Deng did not understand Lian Fan's feelings and resented him very much.
Lian Fan then went east to Luoyang, changed his name and asked to act as Tingwei's jailer.
Not long after, Deng Rong was arrested and imprisoned, and Lian Fan was able to serve as a bodyguard and work diligently.
Deng Rong was surprised that he looked like Lian Fan. He didn't understand why, so he asked, "Why do you look like my former hero?"
Lian Fan reprimanded him and said, "You must be blinded by the predicament!"
He no longer answered his words.
Deng Rong was released from prison because he was sleepy and ill. Lian Fan followed him to recuperate and take care of him. He never mentioned this matter until Deng Rong died. He also personally drove Deng Rong's coffin to Nanyang for burial, and left only after the burial.
Later, Pi was summoned to the palace, and it happened that Xue Han was killed because of the rebellion of King Chu Ying. None of Xue Han's old students dared to see him, so Lian Fan went to collect Xue Han's body alone.
The officials reported to the government, and Xianzong was furious. He summoned Lian Fan to see him and questioned him, saying: "Xue Han conspired with the King of Chu to cause chaos in the world. You are a government official and you do not agree with the court. Instead, you go to collect the corpses of criminals. Why is this?"
Lian Fan kowtowed and said, "I am foolish and ignorant. I think that all the Han people have already fallen into disgrace. The teacher's love must not be forgotten. His crime shall be punished by death."
The emperor's anger subsided and he asked Lian Fan: "Are you a descendant of Lian Po?"
Is it related to the late right general Lian Bao and the great Sima Liandan?
Lian Fan replied: "Bao is Chen's great-grandfather, and Lian Dan is Chen's grandfather."
The emperor said: No wonder your ambition and courage dare to do this!
Therefore, his sins were pardoned, and Lian Fan's reputation became even more prominent from then on.
He was promoted as a scholar, and a few months later he was promoted to the governor of Yunzhong.
Coinciding with the Huns' large-scale invasion of the frontier fortress, the beacon tower sounded alarms all day long.
According to the old practice, if the attacking enemy exceeds 5,000, a letter must be sent to the neighboring county.
The officials wanted to send a message to the neighboring county for help, but Lian Fan refused to listen and led his soldiers to resist.
There were so many enemy troops that Lian Fan's soldiers could not resist.
At dusk, Lian Fan ordered the sergeants to tie two torches each into a cross shape, light three torch heads, and hold one end, so that the camp was lined up like stars.
When the enemy saw the many torches, they thought it was Han reinforcements arriving and were shocked.
Wanting to wait for dawn to retreat, Lian Fan ordered the sergeant to eat well at night and launch a pursuit at dawn. Hundreds of people were beheaded, and the Huns soldiers trampled each other. More than a thousand people died, and they never dared to attack Yunzhong again.
Later, he served as the prefect of Wuwei and Wudu counties. He educated and induced people according to the people's customs and managed them well.
He built a junior high school and moved to the post of prefect of Shu County. The custom in Shu is to favor literary debate and argue with each other. The honest model always encourages them to be honest and honest, and not to be affected by the frivolous and frivolous atmosphere.
Chengdu is rich in folk goods, and the urban houses are close together. In the past, citizens were prohibited from working at night to prevent fires. However, citizens still worked secretly at night, hiding from each other, and fires often broke out.
Lian Fan then abolished the shilling and strictly stipulated that sufficient water should be stored for fire prevention.
The people thought it was convenient, so they sang about it and said: "Uncle Lian Du, where did you come from?"
There is no fire, and the people live in peace. I have never had a short coat in my life, but now I have five pairs of trousers.
After staying in Shu for several years, he was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown for breaking the law.
Lian Fan has been around for generations, has many fields, and has saved a lot of money and food, which are used to provide relief to family friends.
When Suzong died, Lian Fan rushed to Jingling.
At that time, Yan Lin, the governor of Lujiang County, was ordered to mourn the country and met on the road.
Yan Lin was riding in a small car, but his horse died because of the deep mud and could not move forward. Lian Fan was very sympathetic when he saw it, and ordered him to dismount and give Yan Lin a ride, and left without telling him.
After Yan Lin finished his work, he didn't know who to return the horse to, so he followed Lian Fan's whereabouts.
Someone told Yan Lin: Therefore, Lian Shudu, the governor of Shu County, likes to help people in emergencies and difficulties. Now that you are mourning the country, it must be him.
Yan Lin also heard about Lian Fan's reputation for a long time and thought it was right, so he took the horse to Lian Fan's house, thanked him and returned the horse to him.
Everyone in the world admires his kindness, but some people ridicule him for relying on General Dou Xian. Died at home. At first, Lian Fan and Luoyang Qinghong were close friends. At that time, people praised him and said: before him, there was Guan Zhong and Uncle Bao, and after him, there was Qinghong and Lian Fan.
Qinghong was generous and loyal, and became the prefect of Langfu and Kuaiji counties, where he performed unusual deeds.

At first, he promoted the most talented people and moved him to Gucheng County Magistrate, and his governance was famous.
In Yongchuzhong, Kouba County of Western Qiang was in trouble for the people. The imperial edict sent Zhonglang General Yin Jiu to attack and conquer, but he failed for several years.
The three prefectures had great achievements in government affairs and were worshiped as the prefect of Bajun.
Wangtang sent troops to attack the bandits and killed more than a thousand Qiang captives. Ba and Yong were left in peace. The officials and the people built a shrine for Wangtang during his lifetime.
The governor Zhang Qiao showed his ability in governance and moved to Youfufeng.
During Emperor An's expedition to the west, wet nurse Wang Sheng, Zhongchang Shijiang Jing and others invited their families to belong to the hall, but the king's hall was not used.

The family members will be sent back today and the concierge will be closed.

In the second year of Yongjian's reign, he was recruited as a general and a master craftsman.
In the fourth year of Yongjian's reign, he changed his position to Yilang due to official business.
He paid homage to Prime Minister Lu again, and his administration was simple and simple. He did not file a lawsuit for several years.
He moved to Runan to be the prefect, collected talented people, treated the virtuous and corporal officers, and did not do anything on his own, so he taught the history: The ancients were busy seeking talents and were comfortable with envoys, so they were able to keep things clean at the top and rectify things at the bottom.

The chief secretary Ying Si is responsible for handling government affairs and filling in gaps.

From then on, he sincerely asked for his duties, and no longer had any presumptions about teaching, and the county was governed.
At that time, Liang Shang, the general, and Yuan Tang, the minister, hated him because they were unable to seek help.
Later, when thieves from Lujiang entered the Yiyang realm, Wang Tang mobilized troops to pursue them, and the thieves fled. However, Liang Shang and Yuan Tang still held a grudge and falsely accused Wang Tang of being without police during his term of office, and were exempted from returning home.
Died at the age of eighty-six.
The legacy was ordered to be buried in a thin coffin with tiles.
The prince is a pure man but not an official.
Great-grandson Wang Shang, Yizhou Shepherd Liu Yan regarded him as the prefect of Shu County and had a reputation for governance.

The eighth generation ancestor Su Jian was the right general during the reign of Emperor Wu.
Grandfather Su Chun, courtesy name Huan Gong, had a brilliant reputation. He was strong-willed and obsessed with reputation and reputation. Scholars and friends were in awe of him. When they met, they talked about him and said: "When I see Su Huan Gong, I am afraid that he will speak out and teach others. When I don't see him, I miss him again."
Sansuke calls him "Sir".

Su Zhang was erudite and capable of writing when he was young.
During the reign of Emperor An, he was a virtuous and upright person with excellent performance in countermeasures, and was named Yilang.
He stated his gains and losses several times, and his words were very upright. When he was appointed as the magistrate of Wuyuan County, Su Zhang often opened a granary and rescued more than 3,000 households when there was a famine.
During the reign of Emperor Shun, he moved to Jizhou as governor.
The old man was the governor of Qinghe, and Su Zhang inspected him to punish him for being a traitor and embezzling stolen goods.
Su Zhang then invited the prefect to have dinner and wine, and talked about his life's good deeds.

So he was punished.

He was replaced as the governor of Bingzhou, and in order to defeat the powerful and powerful, he violated the order and was dismissed.

The seventh generation of his ancestor was Erqian Shiqingxiao. His grandfather, Yang Ke, was the Sili Xiaowei during the reign of Emperor An.
His father, Yangru, was Taichang during the reign of Emperor Huan.
Yang Xu was regarded as a descendant of a loyal minister and was worshiped as a doctor. After he resigned from the official position, he was conscripted into the mansion of General Dou Wu.
After Dou Wu failed, he was imprisoned for more than ten years due to party affiliation and lived in seclusion.
When the party ban was lifted, he was conscripted into the Taiwei Mansion and moved to Lujiang Prefecture.
Later, the Yellow Turban bandits in Yangzhou attacked Shu and burned the city walls. Yangxu recruited all the men in the county who were over twenty years old. They all held troops and put out the fire. The weak ones participated in fetching water to put out the fire. They gathered tens of thousands of people and fought hard. They defeated the Yellow Turban bandits and the county boundaries were pacified.
Later, the Anfeng thief Dai Feng and others caused trouble, and Yangxu defeated them again, beheaded more than 3,000 people, and captured their commander alive. The rest of the party were civilians, and they were given farming tools so that they could engage in legitimate agricultural production.
In the third year of Zhongping, Zhao Ci, a soldier of Jiangxia, rebelled, killed Qin Jie, the prefect of Nanyang, captured six counties, and worshiped Yang as the prefect of Nanyang.
When he entered the county, he would patrol incognito and take a boy with him to inspect the county and collect rumors before entering.
Some commanders were greedy and officials and people were cunning, but he knew the situation, and everyone in the county was frightened and frightened.
So he sent troops and Wang Min, the governor of Jingzhou, to attack Zhao Ci and beheaded him. He was killed by more than 5,000 people. The remaining thieves in the county came to surrender to Yangxu, and Yangxu appealed to them to pardon the remaining gang members.
After the thieves were put down, political decrees were issued to meet the urgent needs of the people, and the people were happy and admired.
At that time, many powerful families were extravagant, and Yang Xu was very ill. He often had poor food and clothing, and drove an old horse and a broken carriage.
Fu Cheng once offered him raw fish, and Yang Xu accepted it and hung it in the court. Fu Cheng later offered it to him, and Yang Xu showed him the raw fish hanging in the court to stop him from offering fish.
Later, Yangxu's wife and son Yangmi arrived at the county house, but Yangxu refused to accept them. His wife took Yangmi away with only cloth quilts, rags, salt, and a few bushels of wheat. She turned around and said to Yangmi: How can I support your mother and son if I treat myself so poorly?
Let both mother and son go home.
Six years later, Emperor Ling wanted to make Yangxu the Taiwei.
At that time, those who worshiped the Three Dukes would give tens of millions of gifts to Dongyuan and order the envoys and governors to pay the money, which was named "Zuozou".
Wherever he went, he was often greeted with salutes and generous bribes.
Yangxu sat on the single table, held up his old cotton robe to show it off, and said, "This is all my property."
The emperor was displeased with Zuo Zou's report, so Yang Xu failed to ascend to the throne.
However, he was drafted too often and died of illness at the age of forty-eight before he could set out.
The deceased will be buried with a thin will and no legacy will be accepted.
According to the old system, after the death of an official with two thousand dan, he would be paid a million yuan. Jiao Jian, the prime minister of the government, followed Yang Xu's will during his lifetime and received nothing.
The emperor praised Yangxu with an edict and ordered the Taishan prefect to give Yangxu money from the government to support his family.

He was promoted to Xiaolian, then moved to the capital, and had political achievements.
There are many precious products in the old Jiaozhi soil. Mingji, green feather, rhinoceros, elephant, tortoise shell, exotic fragrant and beautiful trees all come from Jiaozhi.

Emperor Ling specially ordered the three palaces to select capable officials, and one official recommended Jia Cong to be the governor of Jiaozhi.

Jia Wangzong immediately sent a letter to inform the people, so that the people could settle down in their own affairs, recruit people who had fled the famine, exempt them from corvee service, execute the generals who caused harm, and select good officials to try to guard the counties. Within a year, the whole territory was settled, and the people were in peace.
There is a song in the lane: "Jia's father came late, so I rebelled first; now that there is peace, the officials dare not eat."
After three years of service, he became the best among the thirteen states and was worshiped as Yilang.
At that time, the Yellow Turbans had just been defeated. After the brutal war, the counties and counties imposed excessive taxes and levies, which led to adultery.
The imperial edict sent Sha to eliminate the governor and two thousand stones, and to select honest and capable officials, so Jia Wangzong was appointed as the governor of Jizhou.
According to the old system, a post car is used to accompany the driver, and red curtains are hung to greet the state border.
When Jia Wangzong arrived, he Shengcha said: "The governor should watch from a distance and listen widely, correct and examine the good and evil. How about those who hang up curtains to cover themselves up?"
So he ordered the driver to take off the curtains.
People everywhere were naturally shocked when they heard the news.
Those officials who had made mistakes were sent away by looking at the wind to remove their seals and ribbons. Only Dong Zhao, the chief of Yingtao, Jiyin, and Liang Guohuang, the chief of Guanjin, served as officials and waited for Jia Wangzong, so the state boundaries became peaceful and smooth.
Emperor Ling died, and the general He Jin recommended Jia Wangzong as the general of Liao Dynasty. He died in the official position.
◆Biography of Lu Kang, Lu Kang's courtesy name was Jining, and he was a native of Wu County, Wu County.
Grandfather successively, in "The Biography of Du Xing".
His father, Lu Bao, was ambitious, but he refused to go even though the imperial court continuously conscripted him.
Lu Kang had been an official in the county since he was a child and was known for his righteousness and righteousness. Zang, the governor, promoted his talents and appointed him as the magistrate of Gaocheng County.
Gaocheng County is on the border. According to the old system, it is ordered that one person in each household must have a crossbow in case of unpreparedness, and no contact is allowed.
When new chief officials arrive, they often send out migrant workers to repair the city walls.
When Lu Kang arrived, no one was sent, and the people were very happy.
Lu Kang governed with kindness and trust, and the bandits and bandits were gone, and the states and counties reported their results.
In the first year of Guanghe, he moved to the post of Wuling Prefect and then became the Prefect of Guiyang and Le'an counties. The county where he lived praised him.
At that time, Emperor Ling wanted to cast bronze figures, but the court's resources were insufficient, so he issued an edict to transfer people's land and charge ten yuan per mu.
At that time, floods and droughts damaged farmers and made the people poor.
Lu Kang came up and remonstrated: I heard that the former kings governed the country by caring for the people.
Eliminate corvee, lighten taxes, and reduce taxes, so as to bring peace to the world, eliminate troubles and become simple, and worship simplicity. Therefore, all surnames obey the teachings, and all kinds of spiritual creatures sense kindness.
The Lord of Decline in the last days is extremely extravagant and unprovoked, and has developed all kinds of new methods to work hard and exploit the people below to satisfy his own meager needs. Therefore, the people lament and Yin and Yang are moved.
His Majesty's holy virtues should be promoted and enlightened, but he actually issued an edict to collect land money for each acre and cast them into bronze figures. I read the edict with melancholy and worried that this was a mistake.
The tax on the eleventh day was called "Che" in the Zhou Dynasty, and "Che" means "tong", which means that this kind of law can be implemented throughout the ages.
Therefore, Duke Xuan of Lu changed the old system of public land and implemented a tax on acres, but the insect plague occurred naturally; Duke Ai of Lu increased taxes, which Confucius thought was wrong.
Is there anyone who seizes the people's belongings to build useless bronze figures, abandons the admonitions of the saints, and follows the same path as the fallen master?
It is said in the legend: What you do must be recorded in a book. If the book fails to follow the law, what will future generations say?
Your Majesty should be careful and reflect on your behavior, and try to change your ways for good, so as to eliminate the resentment of the people.
When the book was circulated, the concubines falsely accused Lu Kang of quoting the subjugation of the country as a metaphor for a saint, which was disrespectful, and sent him to the imperial court in a prison car.
Liu Dai, the imperial censor, examined the matter. Liu Dai gave an explanation, dismissed him, and returned him to the fields.
Later he was worshiped as Yilang.
By chance, Lujiang thief Huang Rang and others joined forces with Jiangxia barbarians with more than 100,000 people, captured four counties, and worshiped Lu Kang as the governor of Lujiang.
Lu Kang declared rewards and punishments, defeated Huang Rang and others, and the rest of the party surrendered.
The emperor commended him for his contribution and appointed Lu Kangsun and Lu Shang as his doctor.
When Emperor Xian came to the throne, the world was in chaos. Lu Kang risked his life and sent filial and honest officials to pay tribute to the imperial court.
At that time, Yuan Shu was stationed in Shouchun, but his troops were hungry, so he sent an envoy to ask Lu Kang to transport soldiers and armor.
Lu Kang believed that Yuan Shu was rebellious and closed himself off to others. He practiced war preparations internally and prepared to resist.
Yuan Shu was furious and sent his general Sun Ce to attack Lu Kang and besieged the city several times.
Lu Kang stood firm, and some of the officials and soldiers were already on vacation. They all returned from hiding and entered the city at night.
After two years of being attacked, the city fell.
More than a month later, he fell ill and died at the age of seventy.
More than a hundred members of the clan suffered from famine, and half of them died.
The imperial court showed pity for his integrity and worshiped his son Lu Xie as the doctor.
The youngest son, Lu Ji, served in Wu as the governor of Yulin. He was well-known for his erudition and good governance.
When he was six years old, he paid a visit to Yuan Shu and brought three tangerines to the table. After the visit, the tangerines fell to the ground. Yuan Shu asked him why, and he said he wanted to take them back to his mother to eat.
summary:
Guo Ji, from Maoling, Fufeng, was born into a family with a knightly ancestor and a prefect father. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, he served in the Da Sikong Mansion and became Yuyang Duwei. Under Wang Mang, he was Great Yin of Shanggu. During the Gengshi era, when the three auxiliaries were invaded, Gengshi appointed him Zuo Fengyi to pacify the people. After Shizu ascended, Guo Ji became Yongzhou's pastor and later a minister offering loyal advice. In the fourth year of Jianwu, he became prefect of Zhongshan, then governor of Yuyang after Peng Chong's defeat. There, he eliminated bandits through punishment and reward, and organized defenses against the Xiongnu, who ceased border incursions. After five years, household registrations doubled. In the ninth year, he became prefect of Yingchuan to suppress bandits, successfully recruiting Zhao Hong and Zhao Wu to surrender. Later appointed Bingzhou pastor, he advised selecting officials from worthy candidates nationwide rather than exclusively from Nanyang. He was known for keeping promises to children who welcomed him on horseback. He served long in Bingzhou due to Lu Fang's troubles, eventually forcing Lu Fang to flee to the Xiongnu. He resigned due to age and illness, became Taizhong doctor, distributed his wealth among his clan, and died at eighty-six.

Du Shi, from Ji County, Hanoi, was talented from youth. He served as a county meritorious official, then joined the Da Sima Mansion. In the first year of Jianwu, he became Shi Yushi and executed the violent General Xiao Guang, receiving ceremonial halberds from Liu Xiu. He later killed the traitor Yang Yi and others. As magistrate of Chenggao, then captain of Pei and Runan, he governed well. In the seventh year, he became Nanyang Prefect, known for frugality and honesty. He invented a water-powered piston bellows for iron smelting, making agricultural tools more efficiently. He repaired ponds and expanded farmland, enriching the county. People compared him to former prefect Zhao Xinchen. Feeling uneasy about his merit, he requested demotion, arguing that troops needed rest and that meritorious generals should be rewarded with county positions. The emperor refused. Du Shi recommended talented people and proposed using tiger talismans for troop mobilization to prevent forgery, which the emperor accepted. After seven years, he was recalled due to a case involving his brother's revenge. He died poor without land or house; the emperor provided funeral expenses.

Kong Fen, from Maoling, Fufeng, studied the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals under Liu Xin. During Wang Mang's rebellion, he fled to Hexi with his mother and brother. In the fifth year of Jianwu, Dou Rong appointed him as chief aunt. He became Marquis of Guannei. Despite Guzang's wealth, Kong Fen's property did not increase in four years. He served his mother filially, eating vegetables with his wife while others laughed at his frugality. After Long and Shu were pacified, when other Hexi governors left with满载 goods, Kong Fen rode alone with nothing. The people offered him cattle, horses, and utensils worth over ten million, but he accepted nothing. In the capital, he became Commander of Wudu. When thieves captured his wife and son as hostages, he pursued relentlessly, resulting in their deaths. The emperor commended him and made him prefect of Wudu, where he governed with clarity. He resigned due to illness and died at home. His younger brother Kong Qi and son Kong Jia both wrote works on the Zuo Commentary.

Zhang Kan, from Wan, Nanyang, was orphaned early and shared his father's wealth with his brother and son. At sixteen, he studied in Chang'an, where classmates called him "Holy Boy." Shizu praised him early on. After ascending, the emperor appointed him as an official. He delivered silk and horses to Wu Han for attacking Gongsun Shu, becoming prefect of Shu County. When the Han army had only seven days of food and planned retreat, Zhang Kan persuaded Wu Han to stay, leading to Gongsun Shu's defeat. After capturing Chengdu, Zhang Kan inspected the treasury without taking anything. He comforted the people, who were delighted. Later, as Governor of Yuyang, he defeated a Xiongnu invasion of 10,000 cavalry with only 1,000 horsemen. He opened over 8,000 hectares of rice fields, enriching the county. The people sang his praises. After eight years, the Xiongnu dared not invade. A Shu County commander testified that when Gongsun Shu was defeated, Zhang Kan left with only a quilt bag despite mountains of treasure.

Lian Fan, from Duling, was a descendant of Zhao general Lian Po. His family had served as frontier county guards for generations. After his father died in Shu Han, fifteen-year-old Lian Fan went to retrieve his body. The prefect offered money, which he refused. When the coffin boat sank, Lian Fan clung to it and was rescued. He studied under Dr. Xue Han. When Xue Han was killed for involvement in King Chu Ying's rebellion, Lian Fan alone collected his body. The emperor questioned him but pardoned him for his courage. As governor of Yunzhong, when the Huns invaded with overwhelming numbers, Lian Fan ordered soldiers to light multiple torches, making the enemy think reinforcements had arrived. He pursued at dawn, killing hundreds. The Huns never attacked Yunzhong again. As prefect of Shu County, he discouraged frivolous debate and abolished night work restrictions, instead requiring water storage for fire prevention. The people sang his praises. He was known for generosity, once giving his horse to a mourning official without revealing his identity. He died at home.

Wang Tang, from Guanghan, was promoted from county magistrate due to his governance. During Yongchu, when Western Qiang rebels troubled Ba County, Wang Tang became prefect, killed over a thousand Qiang captives, and pacified the region. The people built a shrine for him. As You Fufeng, he refused to accommodate the powerful wet nurse Wang Sheng and eunuch Jiang Jing during Emperor An's western expedition, closing his gate to them. Falsely accused, he was vindicated after the emperor's death and Jiang Jing's execution. He later served as Prime Minister of Lu, then prefect of Runan, where he delegated authority to capable subordinates like Chen Fan and Ying Si, achieving good governance. He was hated by General Liang Shang and Minister Yuan Tang, who falsely accused him and had him dismissed. He died at eighty-six, requesting a simple burial.

Su Zhang, from Pingling, Fufeng, was an eighth-generation descendant of General Su Jian. His grandfather Su Chun was a respected scholar. Su Zhang was erudite and capable of writing. During Emperor An's reign, he became Yilang for his virtuous countermeasures. As magistrate of Wuyuan, he opened granaries during famine, saving over 3,000 households. As governor of Jizhou, he invited the corrupt prefect of Qinghe for dinner, discussing good deeds before publicly punishing him. He was known for selflessness. As governor of Bingzhou, he was dismissed for opposing the powerful. He hid in the countryside and refused to serve as Henan Yin. He died at home.

Yang Xu, from Pingyang, Taishan, was a descendant of officials. He served as a doctor and joined General Dou Wu's mansion. After Dou Wu's failure, he was imprisoned for over ten years due to party affiliation. When the ban was lifted, he served in the Taiwei Mansion and became prefect of Lujiang. When Yellow Turban bandits attacked Shu, Yang Xu mobilized all men over twenty to fight, defeating the bandits. He later defeated the Anfeng thief Dai Feng, beheading over 3,000 and giving farming tools to the rest. As prefect of Nanyang, he traveled incognito to gather information, then attacked and killed the rebel Zhao Ci. He lived frugally, driving an old horse and broken carriage. When offered fish, he hung it in the court to discourage further gifts. He refused to let his wife and son stay with him, sending them home with only basic necessities. He was nominated for Taiwei but failed due to refusing bribes. He died at forty-eight, requesting a simple burial.

Jia Wangzong, from Liaocheng, Dongjun, was promoted to the capital for his political achievements. Jiaozhi was rich in precious products, but corrupt governors exploited the people, causing rebellion. In the first year of Zhongping, Emperor Ling sent Jia Wangzong as governor of Jiaozhi. He investigated, found heavy taxes caused the rebellion, and issued proclamations to settle the people, exempt corvee, execute harmful generals, and select good officials. Within a year, the territory was pacified. The people sang his praises. After three years, he became the best among thirteen states. As governor of Jizhou, he ordered the removal of curtains from his carriage, saying the governor should observe openly. Corrupt officials fled. He died in office as General of Liao Dynasty.

Lu Kang, from Wu County, was known for righteousness. As magistrate of Gaocheng County, he governed with kindness and trust, eliminating bandits. As prefect of Guiyang and Le'an, he was praised. When Emperor Ling wanted to cast bronze figures and tax land ten yuan per mu during floods and droughts, Lu Kang remonstrated, citing historical examples of how excessive taxes caused disasters. Concubines falsely accused him of disrespect, and he was sent to court in a prison cart. He was dismissed but later became Yilang. When the Lujiang thief Huang Rang gathered over 100,000 people, Lu Kang became prefect of Lujiang, defeated them, and the rest surrendered. During Emperor Xian's reign, he sent tribute to court despite chaos. When Yuan Shu demanded soldiers and armor, Lu Kang refused, preparing defenses. Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack; Lu Kang held out for two years before the city fell. He died a month later at seventy. His youngest son Lu Ji served Wu as governor of Yulin and was known for filial piety, once taking oranges from Yuan Shu's table for his mother.
