◆Guo Taichuan, named Lin Zong, was born in Jiexiu, Taiyuan. Family background is poor and humble.
His father died early, and his mother wanted him to work in the county.
Lin Zong said: How can a man engage in such a despicable job?
Just quit.
He studied with Chenggao Qu Boyan, graduated in three years, and became well-versed in many books.
He is good at speaking, eloquent, and has a loud voice.
While traveling in Luoyang, he first met Li Ying of Henan Province. Li Ying praised him greatly, and they became good friends and became famous in the capital.
Later, when I returned to my hometown, the scholar-bureaucrats and Confucian scholars brought thousands of cars to the river.
Guo Linzong only crossed the river with Li Ying in the same boat. The guests seeing him off looked at them like gods.
Situ Huang Qiong recruited him, and Taichang Zhao Dianju was wise.
Someone advised Guo Linzong to become an official. Lin Zong replied: I watch the sky at night and investigate social and human affairs during the day. It is unsupportable to abandon the destiny.
So, he didn't respond.
He is talented in understanding people and likes to reward and educate scholars.
He is eight feet long, has a tall and majestic appearance, wears loose clothes and wears a large belt, and travels around the country.
I once walked between Chen and Liang, and when it rained, I folded a corner of the towel and put it up. At that time, people also learned to deliberately fold a corner of the towel, which was called Lin Zongjin. Most people admired it like this.
Someone asked Fan Pang of Runan: What kind of person is Guo Linzong?
Fan Pang said: Living in seclusion like Jie Zitui does not violate the mother's will; serving as an official is like Liu Xiahui, who is loyal and not pretentious. The emperor cannot treat him as a minister, and the princes cannot treat him as a friend. Others, I don't know.
Later, his mother died and he had a reputation of being extremely filial.
Although Guo Linzong was good at identifying and criticizing people, he did not make passionate and profound discussions, so the eunuch dictatorship could not harm him.
The party disaster arose, and most of the famous people suffered from it. Only Guo Linzong and Runan Yuan Hong were spared.
So he taught behind closed doors and had thousands of students.
In the first year of Jianning, Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were killed by eunuchs. Guo Linzong cried in the wild and was extremely sad.
Because he sighed and said: When people die, the country is also in danger.  The crow landed on that person's house.
In the spring of the next year, he died at home at the age of forty-two.
More than a thousand people from all over the world came to pay their respects to the funeral.
The comrades then carved a stone and erected a stele together, and Cai Yong wrote the inscription. When it was completed, he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: I have written many inscriptions! Everyone felt a little ashamed, but Guo Youdao was the only one who didn't feel ashamed.
The scholars rewarded and selected by Guo Linzong were all as he appraised.
He speaks first and then proves it, and everyone admires him. Later, those who liked to appreciate characters might add exaggerations, so there were some flashy and grotesque words added, just like a book of divination.
Now I record the facts that clearly show effect and write them at the end of the article.
Zuo Yuan, Chen Liuren. As a county student, he broke the law and was expelled.
Guo Linzong once met him on the road and held a banquet to comfort him.
He said to him: In the past, Yan Zhuoju was a big thief of Liang Fu, and Duan Qianmu was a big market broker in the Jin State. In the end, he became a loyal minister of the Qi State and a famous sage in the Wei State.
Qu Yuan and Yan Hui are not without faults, let alone ordinary people?
Don't be angry, just ask yourself and blame yourself.
Zuo Yuan accepted his opinion and left.
Some people also ridiculed Guo Linzong for associating with bad people. He replied: If a person is unkind, hating him too harshly will force him to do more bad things.
Later, Zuo Yuan suddenly became more resentful and gathered guests to take revenge on all living beings.
Guo Linzong was at school that day. Zuo Yuan felt ashamed that he had failed to live up to what Guo Linzong had said before, so he left.
Later the story leaked out and everyone thanked him. Mao Rong, courtesy name Jiwei, was born in Chenliu.
In his forties, he was plowing in the wild. At that time, he and his peers were sheltering from the rain under a tree. Everyone was squatting facing each other, and Mao Rong was sitting alone, very respectful.
Guo Linzong felt strange when he saw that he was different from everyone else. Because of the conversation with him, Mao Rong invited Lin Zong to stay at his house.
The next morning, Mao Rong killed a chicken and made vegetables. Lin Zong thought it was for him. Later he found out that it was for his mother, and he used vegetables to eat with the guests.
Guo Linzong bowed to him and said, "You are so wise!"
Because he persuaded him to study, he finally became a moral person.
Meng Min, courtesy name Shuda, was a native of Yang County, Julu County.
When he was a guest in Taiyuan, he was carrying a steamer. The steamer accidentally fell to the ground and broke. He left without even looking at it.
Guo Linzong saw him and asked what he meant. Meng Min replied: The steamer is broken, what's the use of it?
Guo Linzong believed that Meng Min was not an ordinary person and advised him to study abroad.
After ten years of becoming famous, he was recruited by all three princes, but none of them went.
Yucheng, whose courtesy name was Shiyou, was from Yanling County, Yingchuan County.
When he was young, he worked as a servant in the county. Guo Linzong saw him, promoted him, and persuaded him to study as an official because all students were doing odd jobs.
Later, when he was able to lecture on knowledge, he thought that he was from a humble background and often sat in the lower seat. Students and doctors asked him questions, so in the school, he was regarded as the most respected person in the lower seat.
Later, when the imperial court called for him, he didn't answer the call. People called him "Zhengjun".
Song Guo, courtesy name Zhongyi, was born in Fufeng.
He has a strong personality and likes to avenge others and cause suffering for the county.
Guo Linzong then taught him the right way of life and threatened him with disaster and failure.
Song Guo was moved by him and repented, kowtowed and admitted his mistake. Therefore, correct your evil ways and discipline yourself.
Later, he became famous for his uprightness. He was recruited by the government and served as a censor and governor of Bingzhou. Wherever he went, he taught widely.
Jia Shu, whose courtesy name is Zihou, is a fellow villager of Guo Linzong.
Although he comes from a family that has been officials for generations, his character is sinister and the village is troubled by him.
Guo Linzong's mother passed away, Jia Shu went to express condolences, and later Julu Sun Weizhi also arrived.
Sun Weizhi thought that Guo Linzong was a virtuous man but accepted the condolences of a wicked man. He felt strange and left without entering the house.
Guo Linzong caught up with Sun Weizhi and said: Jia Zihou is indeed a bad person, but he has changed his mind and changed his mind.
Zhongni does not refuse to visit home, so I allow him to come in.
Jia Shu listened, changed her ways, encouraged herself, and eventually became a good person.
When there were people in distress in the village, Jia Shu often tried her best to rescue them, and was praised by the governor.
Shi Shubin, Chen Liuren.
He was famous when he was young.
Guo Linzong told people when he met: "The wall is high but the foundation is low. Even if you gain something, you will definitely lose it."
Later, he really lost his reputation because of his flattery.
Huang Yun, courtesy name Ziai, was born in Jiyang.
Famous for his outstanding talents.
Guo Linzong met him and said: You have extraordinary talents and can become a great weapon.
However, I'm afraid that if you don't stick to the truth, you may lose what you gain.
Later, Situ Yuan Wei wanted to propose to his niece. When he saw Huang Yun, he sighed and said, "I am so satisfied with my son-in-law."
When Huang Yun heard about it, he dismissed his wife Xiahou.
Xiahou said to her aunt: Now that I have been abandoned, I will break up with Huang Yun. I will invite relatives to express my feelings of separation.
So there were more than 300 guests gathered. Xiahou sat in the middle, rolled up his sleeves and counted Huang Yun's fifteen filthy and evil things. After that, he took the car and left.
Huang Yun was despised by people at the time.
Xie Zhen, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Zhaoling County, Runan County.
Both Chen Liu and Bian Rang were good at talking and both were famous.
Chang Tong always went to see Guo Linzong day and night. Guo Linzong said to his disciples: These two people are talented, but neither of them has entered Taoism. What a pity!
Xie Zhen later failed to pay attention to details and was attacked by public opinion.
Bian Rang was killed by Cao Cao for insulting Cao Cao.
Wang Rou, also known as Shuyou, and his younger brother Wang Ze, named Jidao, were from Jinyang County in the same county as Guo Linzong.
When the brothers were young, they went to see Lin Zong together and asked each other about the direction of talent development.
Lin Zong said: Shuyou should make a fortune as an official, and Ji Dao should become famous for his expertise in Confucian classics. However, changing direction and doing something else will not reach this point.
Later, as he said, Wang Rou served as a protector of the Xiongnu Zhonglang General, and Wang Ze became the prefect of Daijun.
He also met Zhang Xiaozhong among the woodcutters and herders, and met Fan Tezu in the post office. Zhao Gongzi and Xu Wei were both butchers and wine servants, while Sima Ziwei was an ordinary soldier.
As well as sixty people from the same county, including Guo Changxin, Wang Changwen, Han Wenbu, Li Zizheng, Cao Ziyuan, Dingxiang Zhou Kangzi, Xihe Wang Jiran, Yunzhongqiu Jizhi, Hao Lizhen, etc., all became famous because of him. ◆The biography of Fulong, whose courtesy name is Weiming, was from Junyi, Chenliu County. When he was young, he served as a capital official. He thought it was shameful and abandoned him.
Later, he traveled to Taixue and became a teacher of Shaofu Li Ying.
Li Ying had a noble and pure temperament. Every time he met with Fulong, he often declined other guests and listened to Fulong's words.
Fulong waved his sleeves and talked fluently, while Li Ying often held his hands and sighed.
Guo Linzong began to go to the capital, and he didn't know each other at the time. Fulong admired him when he met him, and introduced him to Li Ying. Guo Linzong became famous all over the world.
At that time, Wenjing of Jin Dynasty in Hanzhong and Huang Ziai of Liang Dynasty all relied on their talents to show off to the capital, and excused themselves to stay home due to illness and did not receive guests.
Sergeant Luo, a nosy doctor, admired his reputation and sat outside his door to ask questions, but did not receive him.
Sangong was recruited and often visited him, using what they said was good or bad as a criterion for choosing.
Fulong understood that there was a lie in it, so he went to Taixue and met with Li Ying. He said: "I have not heard that these two people have any virtues, and they consider themselves heroes. Therefore, I sent the minister to ask about their illness. Wang Chen sat outside the door and asked to receive him."
I'm afraid they are heresy, with false reputations and no facts. We should examine them carefully!
Li Ying thinks it is right.
From then on, the reputation of the two gradually declined, and there were fewer guests and disciples. Within ten days, they ran away with a sigh of shame.
Later I found out that they were really frivolous boys and both were abandoned for committing crimes.
Fulong became more famous because of this.
The prefectures and counties invited him with courtesy and commended him for his filial piety and integrity. The government summoned him many times, but he failed.
The prefect Feng Dai was famous. When he arrived, he asked Fulong to meet him.
As soon as Fulong left, he recommended three county officials, including Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, and Kong Qianyou, but excused themselves from contact with the prefect because of illness.
In case of party disaster, he was also banned from serving as an official.
His wife died, and she was too poor to bury her. The villagers wanted to help him organize a coffin, but Fulong refused to accept it.
Said: In ancient times, dead people were thrown into the wild.
Only my wife can carry out my will, so let me bury her in the ground.
Tian Sheng, whose courtesy name was Zhongxiang, was from the same county as Fulong. He was close to Guo Linzong and had a good understanding of people. He did not hold an official position and was carefree and died at home.
◆The biography of Xu Shao, named Zijiang, was from Pingyu County, Runan County.
When he was young, he established a reputation, was morally responsible, liked to talk about people, and was appreciated by many people.
For example, Fan Zizhao and He Yangshi were all famous at that time.
He began to serve as a meritorious officer in the county, and the prefect Xu Chu respected him very much.
When I heard that my son was going to be an official, there was no one in the government who would not change his conduct and be careful about his words and deeds.
Yuan Shao, a member of the same county, was a noble knight. He left the Puyang Order and returned home with a large number of carriages and horses. He was very luxurious. When he was about to enter the county, he sent away the guests and others and said, "Can Xu Zijian see my carriage and horse attire like this?"
So I just took a car back home.
Xu Shao once went to Yingchuan, and the people who traveled with him were some moral and knowledgeable elders. He did not visit Chen Chen alone.
Chen Fan's wife died and she returned to her hometown for burial. Everyone in the village went to attend the funeral, but Xu Shao did not go.
Someone asked him why, and Xu Shao said: Taiqiu's Taoism is too broad, and it is hard to be thorough in wideness; Zhongju has a severe temperament, and he cannot be thorough in Jun.
So I won't go.
Most of his comments on people are like this.
When Cao Cao didn't want to make a name for himself, he once made generous gifts and humbly asked Xu Shao to talk to him.
Xu Shao looked down on him and refused to speak, so Cao Cao found an opportunity to threaten Xu Shao. Xu Shao had no choice but to say, "You are a traitor in a time of peace and a hero in a time of trouble."
Cao Cao left very happily.
Xu Shao's uncle Xu Jing, Xu Jing's son Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang were all ministers of the Three Dukes. Because Xu Xiang flattered the eunuchs, he went to Taisi to grant him the title of Marquis. He sent people to invite Xu Shao many times. Xu Shao thought that Xu Xiang had no virtue and behaved abominably, so he never visited him.
Li Kui, a native of the same county as Xu Shao, was upright and had noble ambitions. Xu Shao began to be friendly with him, but later they had conflicts and discord with his brother Xu Jing. Public opinion at that time was dissatisfied with him.
At first, Xu Shao and Xu Jing were both well-known and liked to comment on township party figures. They changed the topic every month, so there was a custom of commenting on the first day of the month in Runan.
When Sikong Yang Biao summoned Xu Shao, he promoted him as upright, upright, and honest, but he failed to respond.
Someone advised Xu Shao to become an official. He replied: "Now that the villain has succeeded, the royal family will be in chaos. I want to go to Huaihai to escape to save the children and the elderly."
So we went south to Guangling.
Tao Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, treated each other with courtesy and was extremely considerate.
Xu Shao felt uneasy and told his disciples: "Tao Gongzu has a good reputation on the surface, but he is not true in his heart."
Although it is very kind to me, this situation cannot last long, so it is better to leave.
So he went to Qu'a to join Liu Yao, the governor of Yangzhou.
Later, Tao Qian indeed captured the guests who were staying with him. After Sun Ce pacified Wu, Xu Shao and Liu Yaonan fled Yuzhang and died there at the age of forty-six.
Xu Shao's brother Xu Qian was also famous. People in Runan said Pingyu had two dragons.
summary:
Guo Taichuan, also known as Lin Zong, was born into a poor family in Jiexiu, Taiyuan. After his father's early death, he refused his mother's suggestion to work in the county, instead studying under Chenggao Qu Boyan. He became well-versed in many books, eloquent, and renowned for his loud voice. While traveling in Luoyang, he befriended Li Ying of Henan, gaining fame in the capital. Returning home, he crossed the river alone with Li Ying, impressing onlookers. Despite recruitment offers from officials like Situ Huang Qiong, he declined, citing his observations of heaven and society. He was known for his tall, majestic appearance and his habit of folding a corner of his towel, which others imitated as "Lin Zongjin." Fan Pang praised him as a man who could not be treated as a subject or friend. After his mother's death, he was known for extreme filial piety. During the party disaster, he avoided harm by refraining from passionate discussions, teaching behind closed doors with thousands of students. In the first year of Jianning, he mourned the deaths of Chen Fan and Dou Wu, predicting the country's danger. He died at home at forty-two, with over a thousand mourners. Cai Yong wrote his epitaph, feeling no shame in doing so.

Guo Linzong was skilled in identifying and rewarding scholars. He advised Zuo Yuan, a disgraced county student, to reform, citing historical examples. Zuo Yuan later attempted revenge but left out of shame. He recognized Mao Rong's filial piety, persuading him to study and become virtuous. He advised Meng Min, who ignored a broken steamer, to study abroad, leading to his fame. He promoted Yucheng from a servant to a respected scholar. He reformed Song Guo, a vengeful man, into an upright official. He accepted Jia Shu, a sinister man, after his mother's death, leading to Jia's transformation. He predicted Shi Shubin's loss of reputation due to flattery. He warned Huang Yun about losing gains without truth, which came true when Huang dismissed his wife. He noted Xie Zhen and Bian Rang's talents but lack of Taoism, leading to their downfalls. He correctly predicted Wang Rou and Wang Ze's career paths. He also discovered talents among commoners, such as Zhang Xiaozhong and Fan Tezu.

Fulong, from Chenliu, abandoned his post as a capital official and studied under Li Ying. He introduced Guo Linzong to Li Ying, making him famous. Fulong exposed the false reputations of Wenjing and Huang Ziai, causing their decline. He refused official posts and buried his wife simply. Tian Sheng, his close friend, was also skilled in understanding people.

Xu Shao, from Runan, was known for moral responsibility and commenting on people. He influenced Yuan Shao to reduce his luxury. He avoided visiting Chen Chen and Chen Fan, citing their flaws. He famously called Cao Cao a "traitor in peace, hero in trouble." He refused to visit his uncle Xu Xiang due to his flattery of eunuchs. He and his brother Xu Jing held monthly critiques in Runan. He declined official posts, fleeing to Guangling and later to Qu'a to join Liu Yao. He died in Yuzhang at forty-six. His brother Xu Qian was also famous, known as the "two dragons of Pingyu."

◆The biography of Guo Gong, named Zhongsun, was born in Yangzhai, Yingchuan. The family has been officials for generations.
His father, Guo Hong, studied "Xiao Du Lv" and the prefect Kou Xun used Guo Hong to make judgments on Cao Cao. He stayed in prison for thirty years and his methods were fair.
In all cases judged by Guo Hong, there is no resentment when he retreats. The county will compare Hong to Donghai Yugong.
Guo Hong died at the age of ninety-five.
Guo Gong inherited his father's business when he was young and taught hundreds of disciples.
Later he became a county official and was called into the government.
During the Yongping period, Dou Gu, the captain of Fengche, sent troops to fight against the Huns, and Qin Peng, the captain of cavalry, served as deputy commander.
Qin Peng was stationed elsewhere and often killed people according to the law. Dou Gu reported that Qin Peng had exclusive power and requested that he be killed.
Xianzong then cited officials and ministers to assess Qin Peng's crime.
Because Guo Gong understood the law, he was summoned to the court to participate in the review.
Everyone who discussed it agreed with what Dou Gu said, but Guo Gong said alone: ​​According to the law, Peng should be beheaded.
The emperor said: When the army goes out for battle, the captain is unified under the governor.
Since Peng has no axe, can he have the power to kill people?
Guo Gong replied: "Unifying under the governor is a matter of trilogy." Today's special general Peng Zhuan is a little different from this.
Military affairs are as urgent as human breathing, and the commander is not allowed to be notified in advance.
Moreover, under the system of the Han Dynasty, Zhuoge was the same as Wu, and he was not considered guilty legally.
The emperor listened to Guo Gong's opinion.
There are also brothers who commit murder together, and it is hard to pin the blame on whom.
The emperor believed that the elder brother should not discipline his younger brother, so he reported that the elder brother should be sentenced severely and the younger brother should be commuted to death.
The imperial edict was read out by Sun Zhang, who made a mistake and was punished twice. The minister reported that Sun Zhang had falsely conveyed the imperial edict and should be cut in half for his crime.
The emperor called Guo Gong to ask again, and Guo Gong replied: Sun Zhang should be fined.
The emperor said: Sun Zhang falsely issued an imperial edict to kill people, how can he say that he was only fined?
Guo Gong said: In law, there is a distinction between intentional homicide and manslaughter. Sun Zhang's mistake in conveying the order is considered manslaughter, and manslaughter is lighter in terms of regulations.
The emperor said: Sun Zhang lives in the same county as the prisoner, so I suspect he did it on purpose.
Guo Gong said: The road is as flat as a hammer, and as straight as an arrow. A gentleman will not cheat and deceive. The king regards heaven as the law, and punishment should not be compromised.
The emperor said: OK.
He was awarded the title of Tingweizheng, but was later dismissed for breaking the law.
Later, he was promoted three times, and in the third year of Yuanhe, he was promoted to Tingwei.
Guo Gong's family has been in charge of law for generations, and their affairs are in Kuanping. When he was a magistrate, he decided on prisons and sentences, and mostly acted on the principle of mercy. Therefore, he reported to the emperor the forty-one things that meant severe punishment could be mitigated, and everything was implemented according to the law. In the first year of Zhanghe, the prisoners in the world were pardoned before Bingzi in April, and their death penalty was reduced to one level, without being flogged, and they were sent to Jincheng. However, the article did not mention those who escaped unnoticed.
Guo Gong went to Fengshi and said: The reason why the holy grace reduces the death penalty and makes the border guards more important is that human life is the most important thing.
There are probably tens of thousands of people on death row today, and since the pardon, many criminals have been arrested. Even if the edict does not involve them, they should all be punished with serious crimes.
Thinking of God's kindness, all those who were convicted of capital crimes were reborn, but those who were arrested after escaping did not benefit from the kindness.
I think that those who have committed capital crimes before and are imprisoned after the pardon may not be flogged to Jincheng, so as to save lives and benefit the frontier.
Suzong thought it was very good and immediately issued an edict to pardon him.
Guo Gong reported on the legal system, and many people saved their lives.
In the sixth year of Yongyuan, he died in the official government. The middle son, Guo Rizhi, also understood the law. His official position was the prefect of Nanyang, and he was famous in politics.
◆Chen Chong's biography, Chen Chong's courtesy name is Zhaogong, and he was a member of the Pei Kingdom.
My great-grandfather, Chen Xian, served as Minister of Law and Order during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang assisted the government and made many changes to the Han Dynasty system, which made Chen Xian dissatisfied.
When Wang Mang killed He Wu, Bao Xuan and others who were not attached to him because of Lu Kuan's affairs, Chen Xian sighed: "The Book of Changes" says: "A gentleman acts when the opportunity arises. If I don't wait until the end of the day, I can pass away!"
Immediately asked to resign and left.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he summoned Chen Xian to serve as the chief bandit officer, but Chen refused to take up the post on the grounds of illness.
At this time, the three sons Shen, Feng, and Qin were all in official positions, so they were all dismissed from their positions. The father and son returned to their hometown together, staying behind closed doors. They still held sacrifices in the twelfth lunar month according to the custom of the Han family.
When people asked him why, Chen Xian said: Do my ancestors know about Wang's wax sacrifice?
Later, Wang Mang summoned Chen Xian and said that he was seriously ill, so he collected all the laws and regulations at home and hid them in the walls.
Chen Xian had a kind and tolerant character, and often warned his descendants: When negotiating for others, you should rely on lightness. Even if you have the benefit of a hundred gold, never compare yourself with others.
In the early years of Jianwu's reign, Chen Qinzi and Chen Gong served as the left prisoner of the Tingwei and died early.
Chen Gong gave birth to Chen Chong, who learned about the family business. When he was young, Chong served as a state and county official and was called to Situ Baoyu's mansion.
At this time, the three houses were very friendly, and it was considered noble to refuse to do anything.
Chen Chongchang disagreed and worked hard alone, explaining contemporary politics to Bao Yu several times.
Bao Yu was convinced of his ability to favor, so he resigned from Cao Cao and took charge of the world's lawsuits.
His judgment was fair and did not fail to satisfy everyone's wishes.
At that time, Situ's lawsuits were delayed for decades. The matters were complicated and easy to judge, and bad officials had to rely on them to make a difference.
Chen Chong wrote seven volumes of "Resignation and Litigation Bi" for Bao Yu. The rules for dealing with the case were all in accordance with the categories of things.
Bao Yu played this, and later the government took it as an example.
After being promoted three times, in the early years of Emperor Suzong's reign, he became minister.
At this time, the old practices of the Yongping period were inherited. The official administration advocated strictness, and the ministers generally tended to impose heavy sentences in handling cases. Chen Chong believed that the emperor had just ascended the throne and the harsh politics of the previous generation should be changed.
So Shangshu said: I have heard that in the previous king's government, rewards were not excessive and punishments were not excessive. Rather than being forced to do so, I would rather be excessive than excessive.
Therefore, Tang Yao wrote the "Yao Canon", which advocated "forgiveness of disasters". The Duke of Zhou gave a precept, not to miss the rules of Boyi in prison, but to respect the five punishments in order to achieve the three virtues.
From this point of view, the government of sages is centered on punishment.
In the past, prisons were strictly enforced, so bad guys were dealt with harshly. Since bad guys are equal, it is better to be lenient. After His Majesty came to the throne, most of them followed this rule, calling on the officials many times to promote the moderate policy.
However, some officials did not obey everything, and used harsh punishments.
Those who try cases are eager to torture, and those who enforce the law are tired of slandering fraud and abuses. Some even pretend to be public and practice private, and show dominance.
Being in charge of government is like playing the harp. If the big string becomes too fast, the small string will break.
Therefore, Zigong denied Zang Sun's fierce methods and praised Zheng Zhiqiao's benevolent government.
"The Book of Songs" says: Neither hard nor soft, administration is excellent.
Nowadays, holy virtues fill the heaven and earth. We should follow the ways of the ancestors and eliminate the cumbersome methods. Use punishment lightly to benefit the people, promote virtue, and serve the heart of heaven.
The emperor respectfully accepted Chong's words and advocated generosity in everything.
Later, he called on officials to put an end to cruel punishments, lift the ban on evil, exonerate the innocent of his predecessors, and write down more than fifty things in the law and fix them on the law.
From then on, the folk customs were peaceful and good omens appeared frequently.
In the Han Dynasty, it was customary to decide cases and impose the death penalty in the third month of winter. At this time, the emperor changed the date to the first ten months of winter.
In the second year of Yuanhe, there was a drought. Jia Zong, the captain of Changshui School, and others came forward and believed that the prison would not last for three winters, so the yin energy was weak and the yang energy vented, causing the drought. This is the root of the matter.
The emperor handed his words to the ministers for discussion, and Chen Chong reported: During the winter solstice, Yang Qi sprouts, so in November there are orchids, Shegan, Yun, Lychee and other flowers.
"Shi Ling" says: All things are shaken, and the body is settled.
Heaven regarded it as right, and Zhou Dynasty used it as the beginning of the year.
In December, when Yang Qi rises and domestic chickens and pheasants hatch, the earth is considered to be in good health, and it was regarded as the beginning of the year in the Shang Dynasty.
In the twelfth month of the twelfth month, Yang Qi has arrived, heaven and earth have joined together, all things have emerged, and stinging insects have begun to vibrate. People think it is righteous, and the Xia Dynasty regarded it as the beginning of the year.
The three micro-forms are written to connect the three unifications.
Zhou began with heaven, Shang began with earth, and Xia began with humans.
If the execution is carried out at this time, then the capital of Shang and Zhousui should bleed, which is not in line with the people and the will of God.
"Moon Order" says: Mengdong's moon is like prison and punishment, and there is no crime left.
It shows that the punishment should be completed at the beginning of winter.
"Moon Order" also says: In the midwinter moon, the body wants peace and things want to be quiet.
If one uses force to reduce anger, it cannot be said to be peaceful; if one uses severe punishment, it cannot be said to be tranquility.
Those who discussed it all said: The cause of the drought is due to the change of laws.
I believe that the Shang and Zhou dynasties did not use trivial measures to end the prisons, but turned them into a prosperous and peaceful world without disasters.
Since the Yuanhe period, three winters have been used, and floods and droughts often cause disasters.
From this point of view, disasters are caused by themselves, not because of changes in the law.
The Qin Dynasty was an tyrannical government and carried out executions in all seasons. The Han Dynasty had just emerged and changed to simpler methods.
Xiao He drafted the criminal law and set it in the autumn of the year to avoid the beginning of spring, without considering the righteousness of heaven and earth, and the spring of the king of Yin and Tuesday, which is really against the right path.
Your Majesty explores the secrets and analyzes the details, believes in the right way, eradicates the mistakes of a hundred years, and establishes the great achievements of eternal life. There are teachings of welcome from above, and the benefits of flattery from below. Check the text of "Spring and Autumn", and it is consistent with the meaning of "Yue Ling". There should be no doubt about the holy merits and beautiful deeds.
The emperor accepted the memorial and made no further changes.
Chen Chong has a thoughtful nature and often talks about the meaning of being a minister. He is not afraid of hardship.
Since he was in the Privy Council, he had sent his disciples to his disciples and refused to be close friends. He only stayed in public houses. The court valued him very much.
The queen's younger brother, Dou Xian, recommended Zhen Ding to make Zhang Lin the minister. The emperor asked Chen Chong about this. Chong replied: Although Zhang Lin is talented, his daily behavior is corrupt. Dou Xian deeply hated Chen Chong because of this.
Zhang Lin was finally used, and Zang Xun was used to atone for his crime.
After the emperor's death, Dou Xian and others came to power and often hated Chen Chongxian. So he reported to the Queen Mother and asked Chong to be in charge of the funeral, trying to find fault and slander him.
Bao De, the minister of Huangmen, always respected Chen Chong and persuaded Dou Xian's younger brother Xia Yanghou Dou Dao: "When Chen Chong served the late emperor, he was very trusted, so he stayed in Taige for a long time, and the reward was somewhat special."
Now that he is not rewarded for his loyalty and ability, and cares about his minor mistakes, it will indeed harm the virtue of assisting the government and allowing loans.
Dou was also a good scholar and believed that Chen Chong was right, so Chen Chong got the opportunity to become the prefect of Taishan.
Later he became the prefect of Guanghan.
The wealthy gentry in Xizhou engaged in mergers and acquisitions, many officials were treacherous and corrupt, and hundreds of lawsuits were filed every day.
When Chen Chong took office, he appointed good officials Wang Huan and Tan Xian as his confidants. The number of lawsuits was gradually reduced, and the county was quiet and serious.
In the south of Xunluo County, every time it rains, cries are often heard in the house for decades.
Chen Chong heard about it and suspected that there must be a reason for it, so he sent officials to investigate the case.
The official came back and reported: When the world was in decline, many people died down here, but their bones were not allowed to be buried. Is this the possible reason?
Chen Chong sighed sadly and ordered the county government to collect all the coffins and bury them.
From then on the crying stopped.
Later, when Dou Xian became the general to conquer the Huns, there was no one below the rank of public minister or in the county who did not send officials' children as gifts. However, Chen Chong and Zhongshan Prime Minister Runan Zhang Chen and Dongping accordingly followed the right path and did not flatter.
Later, Emperor He heard about it and promoted Chen Chong to the position of Chief Agriculture Officer, Zhang Chen to the position of Imperial Servant, and Ying Shun to the position of Zuo Fengyi.
In the sixth year of Yongyuan, Chen Chong replaced Guo Gong as a court captain.
Kind and reserved personality.
Later, he became a judge. He discussed difficult cases many times and often presented memorials in person. Every time he attached a sutra, he asked for forgiveness. The emperor often listened to him and saved many prisoners.
Only at this time did the number of cases with profound stories decrease a lot.
Chen Chong also cleaned up the laws and regulations, and eliminated them out of "Fu Xing".
He also said: I have heard that there are three hundred rites and three thousand majestic rituals, so in the "Fu Xing", the decapitation of the great punishment is two hundred, and the five punishments and the like are three thousand.
Where etiquette goes, punishment takes away. If etiquette is violated, punishment will follow. They are both exterior and interior.
Today's law decrees six hundred and ten death sentences, one thousand six hundred and ninety-eight punishments, and two thousand six hundred and eighty-one atonements. It comes from the one thousand nine hundred and eighty-nine in "Fu Xing", of which four hundred and ten are great punishments, one thousand five hundred for one's punishment, and seventy-nine atonements.
"Spring and Autumn Period Baoqian Tu" says: The king will practice his method every three hundred years.
In the three hundred and two years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the constitution has been slightly increased and the regulations are unlimited.
There are three schools of law, and their explanations are different.
It is necessary to order Sangong and Tingweiping to make decrees that should be consistent with the law, so that the general punishment can be 200, and the punishment and atonement can be 2800, and the total number can be 3000, and all the remaining orders should be deleted, corresponding to the etiquette, so as to change the hearing and hearing of thousands of people, so as to obtain the reputation of not using punishment measures, which can be passed down to endless generations.
There was no time to implement it, so the jailer was ordered to socialize with the prisoners to compensate for the crime.
The imperial court issued an edict to exempt him from punishment and worship him as minister.
Promoted to Dahonglu.
Chen Chong experienced two counties and three ministers, and his deeds were famous at that time.
In the 16th year, he served as Sikong on behalf of Xu Fang.
Although Chen Chong specializes in law, he is also a master of classics. He made a report to Wen Cui and was named Prime Minister.
He died after reigning for three years.
Tai Chang Nanyang Yin Qin replaced Sikong.

◆Preface to the biographies of ruthless officials. The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent and uneasy era of the Warring States Period, which affected many people, including those who were arrogant and cunning.
Those who use the big to swallow up the small, cross the country and the city, and those who are strong and unruly become the kings and hegemons in the countryside. The prefectures and counties govern vast areas and have many household registrations.
Therefore, officials can act arbitrarily and arbitrarily, and the traitors should be killed first and then punished.
Show off his staunch spirit and achieve his unyielding power.
He stood up to others and used his own opinions to reveal his unpredictable wisdom.
As for the intricacies of the text, the indiscriminate accusations, and the infuriating of people, they are countless.
Some pits were even filled with corpses, bleeding for miles.
So Wang Wenshu has the reputation of a tiger-crowned official, and Yan Yannian has the reputation of being a butcher. Is this false?
However, those among them who suppressed the strong and suppressed the ministers to the point of breaking their minds and ignoring them can be considered very heroic.
Since the ZTE, the laws have gradually become stricter, and fewer officials and common people break the law than in previous lives.
But eunuchs and relatives harm the world.
They even ordered Yang Qiu to dig up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian to dissect Cao Jie's tomb.
Such and such, although it vents public anger and is pleasing to everyone, it can also be said to be too cruel.
Zhang Jian is a well-known figure, so he is included in the "Party Man Chapter".
◆Dong Xuan, courtesy name Shaoping, was a native of Yuxian County, Chenliu County.
At first he was recruited by Situ Houba and recommended as a person with excellent performance. He was gradually promoted to the state minister of Beihai County.
When he arrived, he appointed Gongsun Dan as the chief minister of the five sense organs.
When Gongsun Dan built a new house, the fortune teller believed that someone would definitely die, so Gongsun Dan asked his son to kill passers-by and put the corpses in the house to ward off his disaster.
When Dong Xuan found out, he arrested and killed Gongsun Danzi.
More than thirty people from Gongsun Dan's clan and close associates came to Dong Xuan's government with weapons and complained about their injustice. Dong Xuan believed that Gongsun Dan had taken refuge with Wang Mang before, and was worried that they had colluded with pirates, so he arrested them all and imprisoned them in Jixian Prison. He sent his subordinate Zuo Shuiqiu Cen to kill them all.
The governor of Qingzhou thought that he had killed too many people, so he wrote to the emperor to report Dong Xuan and examine his charges. Dong Xuan was found guilty and recruited into the imperial court.
Dong Xuan was in prison, reciting poems and poems morning and night, without any worries.
When it was time for him to be released from prison and sentenced, the officials and his family prepared a meal for him. Dong Xuan said sternly: "I, Dong Xuan, have never eaten other people's food in my life, let alone when I die?"
Get in the car and drive away.
Among the nine people who were tortured together at that time, it was Dong Xuan's turn. Emperor Guangwu hurriedly sent his attendant knights to rush over. He only pardoned Dong Xuan's death penalty and ordered him to return to prison.
An envoy was sent to interrogate Dong Xuan about killing innocent people. Dong Xuan answered the envoy with all the facts and said that Shui Qiucen was acting in accordance with his will and the fault was not his. He is willing to kill himself and let Shuiqiu Cen live.
The envoy told Emperor Guangwu of these circumstances, and Emperor Guangwu issued an edict to demote Dong Xuan to the position of county magistrate of Huai County, and ordered the governor of Qingzhou not to investigate Shui Qiucen's crimes.
Shui Qiucen was promoted to Sili Xiaowei.
Later, the giant thief Xia happy and others invaded Jiangxia County. The imperial court appointed Dong Xuan as the governor of Jiangxia.
Dong Xuan arrived at the border of Jiangxia County and issued a document saying: The imperial court believes that this prefect can capture the traitor, so he accepted this task.
Now you are commanding troops and horses in Jiangxia County. When the message arrives, I hope you will consider your fate.
Xia happy and others were frightened after hearing this and immediately surrendered and disbanded.
His maternal relative, Yinshi, was the captain of Jiangxia County. Dong Xuan despised and insulted him, so he was dismissed from his post.
Later, the imperial court specially summoned Dong Xuan as the county magistrate of Luoyang.
At that time, the slave of Princess Huyang committed murder during the day, but because he was hiding in the princess's house, the officials could not arrest him.
When Princess Huyang went out, she used this murderous slave to accompany her. Dong Xuan was waiting for Princess Huyang at Xiamen Pavilion, stopped the princess's carriage, stopped the princess's horse, scratched the ground with a knife, loudly listed the princess's faults, scolded the slave to get out of the car, and then killed him.
Princess Huyang immediately returned to the palace and told Emperor Guangwu. Emperor Guangwu was furious, summoned Dong Xuan, and wanted to beat him to death with a stick.
Dong Xuan kowtowed and said: I beg to say a word before I die.
Emperor Guangwu said: What do you want to say?
Dong Xuan said: "Your Majesty's holiness revitalized the Han Dynasty, but he allowed his servants to kill good people. How will he govern the world?"
I don’t need to be beaten with a stick, please let me commit suicide.
He hit his head against the pillar and his face was covered with blood.
The emperor ordered Xiaohuangmen to support him and asked Dong Xuan to kowtow to the princess to apologize. Dong Xuan refused to obey, so Xiaohuangmen forced him to kowtow. Dong Xuan held the ground with both hands and refused to bow his head.
The princess said: When Uncle Wen was a common man, he hid fugitives and those who had committed capital crimes, and officials did not dare to come and arrest them.
Now that you are the emperor, can't you impose your authority on a county magistrate?
Emperor Guangwu smiled and said: The emperor cannot be like the common people.
Then he ordered the stiff-necked county magistrate to go out.
Dong Xuan was given 300,000 yuan, and Dong Xuan gave it all to his officials.
From then on, Dong Xuan attacked powerful people, and everyone was shocked and trembling. The capital called him "Crouching Tiger" and sang in praise of him: "Dong Xuan has no injustice in front of the Yamen."
Dong Xuan served as the magistrate of Luoyang County for five years and died in office at the age of seventy-four.
The emperor issued an edict and sent envoys to his home to have a look. They saw the body covered with a quilt, and his wife and children were crying in front of him. There are several bushes of barley and a broken car at home.
Emperor Guangwu said sadly: Dong Xuan was an honest official. You will only know after he dies!
Because Dong Xuan once served as the prefect of the county with two thousand stones, he was given a silver seal and a royal ribbon, and he was buried with a doctor's ceremony.
His son Dong Bing was granted the title of doctor, and later Dong Bing served as the prime minister of Qi County.
◆Biography of Fan Ye, named Zhonghua, a native of Xinye County, Nanyang County.
He had a good relationship with Guangwu when he was young.
At the beginning of Jianwu's reign, he was recruited to serve as a censor, promoted to captain of Hedong, and introduced in Yuntai.
At first, when Guangwu was poor and humble, he was detained in Xinye for some reason. Fan Ye was appointed as a city official and sent a box of dry food to Guangwu. Guangwu was grateful for his kindness and did not forget it. He invited Fan Ye to eat many times and provided clothes for his carriage and horse.
Because he joked: How about becoming a captain with a box of dry food?

summary:
The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent Warring States period, fostering arrogant and cunning individuals who used power to dominate regions. Officials acted arbitrarily, killing traitors before reporting, displaying staunch spirit and unyielding power. Countless injustices occurred, with corpses filling pits and blood flowing for miles. Figures like Wang Wenshu and Yan Yannian gained reputations as tiger-crowned officials and butchers. After the Zhongxing period, laws tightened, but eunuchs and relatives harmed the world, leading to excessive acts like Yang Qiu digging up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian dissecting Cao Jie's tomb, which vented public anger but were deemed too cruel.

Dong Xuan, from Chenliu, was recommended as a person of excellent performance and became state minister of Beihai. He killed Gongsun Danzi for murdering a passerby to ward off disaster, then arrested and executed over thirty of Gongsun Dan's clan. The governor of Qingzhou reported him, and Dong Xuan was imprisoned but remained calm. Emperor Guangwu pardoned him, demoting him to county magistrate of Huai. Later, as governor of Jiangxia, he intimidated the giant thief Xia happy into surrendering. As magistrate of Luoyang, he killed Princess Huyang's murderous slave, defying the emperor's order to apologize. He died in office at 74, leaving a poor household, and was honored posthumously.

Fan Ye, from Nanyang, was a friend of Guangwu from youth. He served as censor and captain of Hedong, punishing Ma Shikuang and eliminating thieves. As state animal husbandry, he taught farming and management. After Wei Xiao's elimination, he became prefect of Tianshui, applying strict laws like Han Fei. His harsh rule made the road safe at night, and Liangzhou people sang of his severity. He died in office after 14 years, and Emperor Xianzong later granted his family millions.

Li Zhang, from Huai, studied Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals and served under Guangwu. As Yangping Order, he killed the powerful Zhao Gang at a banquet and pacified the area. As prefect of Langxie, he attacked rebels imprisoning the prefect, killing leader Xia Changsi. He was later conscripted for land measurement issues but released due to merit, dying of illness.

Zhou Jin, from Pixu, liked Han Fei's methods. As a county official, he killed dozens of powerful bad guys. As Bo Ping Ling, no one left prison alive. He hid pardon orders to execute criminals first. He was dismissed for killing innocents but later promoted to Zhaoling Prime Minister. He exposed Ting Yu's deception and, as Luoyang Order, intimidated nobles. He clashed with Huangmenlang Dou Du, was imprisoned, pardoned, and later dismissed for harshness. He returned as Yushi Zhongcheng, but was removed again. He later impeached Xia Yanghou, becoming Sili Xiaowei, and died in office.

Huang Chang, from Kuaiji, studied Confucian classics and served as a judge. As magistrate of Wan, he exposed hidden evildoers, catching a thief who stole his hood. As governor of Shu, he handled over 700 lawsuits and arrested bandits. He reunited with his long-lost wife, captured by thieves. He executed Mrs. Peng for watching him from a high building. He served as prefect of Yingchuan and died as Taizhong doctor.

Yang Qiu, from Yuyang, was strict and liked Shen Buhai and Han Fei. He killed a county official who insulted his mother. As prefect of Jiujiang, he eliminated thieves and executed corrupt officials. He was dismissed for cruelty but later promoted to Yilang. As Sili Xiaowei, he arrested and tortured Wang Fu and his son, tearing Wang Fu's body apart. He attempted to impeach Cao Jie but was demoted to Weiwei. He was later executed for plotting against eunuchs.

Wang Ji, adopted son of Wang Fu, was cruel as Prime Minister Pei. He killed over 10,000 people in five years, using harsh methods like killing parents who didn't raise children. He was detained and died in Luoyang prison when Yang Qiu impeached Wang Fu.

The historian commented that ancient people were generous, but in later times, severe torture and killing led to cruel officials. Some were brave and skilled, but their methods varied. Power and punishment caused sloppy behavior, while benevolence and faith could prevent evil. The gains and losses of numerous punishments and lawsuits could be understood from one state to the whole world.

The thief Li Xiong is a strong man in Ye. Li Xiong's younger brother Li Lu wants to plot a rebellion in the city to welcome Tanxiang.

Yaoqi is more important than faith. Since he became a general, he often sent troops to the city, but he never captured the people.
Serving in the imperial court, caring about the country and loving the Lord, and if there is anything that has to be remonstrated, it must be a crime to remonstrate.

Zi Yaodan succeeded to the throne.

Yao Yu passed away and was succeeded by his son Yao Cai Si.

He has been fond of the legal system for generations. His father was a county magistrate, and Ba himself was a jailer when he was young.
He often lamented that he was not happy with his official position. His father felt strange and sent him west to Chang'an to study.
When the Han soldiers rose up and Guangwu passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba led his guests to meet him and said: "The general is raising righteous soldiers. I don't know what I think. So Cong Guangwu defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi in Kunyang, and then rested in the countryside.
When Guangwu became the captain of Sili school and passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba asked his father for instructions, hoping to follow Guangwu.
His father said: I am old and not qualified for military service. You go and do your best! Wang Ba and Guangwu went to Luoyang.
When Guangwu became the Grand Sima, he took Wang Ba as his meritorious officer and ordered him to cross Hebei.
The guests followed Wang Ba's dozens of people and gradually left.
Guangwu said to Wang Ba: All the people who followed me in Yingchuan have left, but you are left alone.

When Wang Lang raised his troops, Guangwu was at Ji. Wang Lang sent a letter offering a reward for Guangwu's capture.
Guangwu ordered Wang Ba to go to the city to recruit people and prepare to attack Wang Lang.
The people in the city laughed and raised their hands to tease and ridicule. The king was ashamed and cowardly and returned.
Guangwu immediately galloped south to Xiaquyang.
It was rumored that Wang Lang's soldiers were behind him, and everyone who followed him was afraid.
When we arrived at the Hutuo River, the reconnaissance officials came back and reported that the river was filled with ice and could not be crossed without a boat.
The officials were greatly frightened when they heard this.
Guangwu ordered Wang Ba to go and have a look.
Wang Ba probably frightened everyone and wanted to cross the river, but was blocked by the water. When he came back, he falsely claimed that the ice was strong and could be crossed. The officials and their families were all happy.
Guangwu smiled and said, "The detective officials are indeed lying."
So move forward. When they arrived at the river, the ice had closed up, so they ordered Wang Ba to protect them across the river. There were still a few riders left to cross the river, but the ice thawed.
Guangwu said to Wang Ba: "It's your credit that stabilized the troops and enabled the army to cross the river safely." Wang Ba thanked him and said: This is the supreme virtue of Ming Gong and the protection of the gods. Even if it is the induction of Wu Wang Baiyu, it cannot compare with it. Guangwu said to his officials: "It is a blessing from heaven that Wang Ba defrauded others because of his power." With Wang Ba as military commander, he was given the title of Marquis of Guan Nei.
After arriving at Xindu, he sent troops to attack Handan.
Wang Ba chased Wang Lang, got Wang Lang's seal and ribbon, and was named Wangxianghou.
Following the pacification of Hebei, he often camped with Zang Gong and Fu Jun. Wang Ba alone was good at comforting the soldiers. When the soldiers died, they took off their own clothes to bury them, and when they were injured, he personally healed their wounds.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he believed that the king knew military affairs, loved the soldiers, and could serve alone, so he was worshiped as a partial general and led the troops of Zang Gong and Chen Jun, while Zang Gong and Chen Jun were appointed as cavalry captains.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Wang Ba was granted the title Fubohou.

Ma Wujun ran through Wangba's camp and shouted for help.

In the sixth year of Jianwu, Xin'an was established.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, he stationed at Hangu Pass and defeated the bandits in Xingyang and Zhongmou.

Wu Han returned to Luoyang and ordered Zhu You to garrison Changshan, Wang Chang to garrison Zhuojun, and Hou Jin to garrison Yuyang.
Xishu worshiped Wang Ba as the prefect of Shanggu, and led the troops as in the past, hunting barbarians without being restricted by county boundaries.

General Zuonan of the Xiongnu led thousands of cavalry to rescue Jia Lan. Wang Ba and others fought with him at the foot of Pingcheng, defeated the enemy troops, pursued him out of the fortress, and beheaded hundreds of people.
Wang Ba and other generals returned to Yanmen and joined forces with General Du Mao to attack Lu Fang General Yin Yuguo County and Fan County, but failed to win.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of households in the city was increased, and Wang Ba was granted the title of Xianghou.
At this time, Lu Fang, together with the Xiongnu and Wuhuan soldiers, invaded and plundered more frequently, making the borderland miserable.
Wang Ba was ordered to lead more than 6,000 prisoners who were freed from their shackles, and he and Du Mao managed Feigu Road, piled stones and earth, built pavilions and barriers, and traveled more than 300 miles to Pingcheng.
Wang Ba fought hundreds of battles with the Xiongnu and Wuhuan, large and small, and was well versed in border defense affairs. Later Nan Danyu and Wuhuan surrendered. The north side is quiet and uneventful.
Wang Ba has been in Shanggu for more than 20 years.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Huailing.
In the second year of Yongping. He was dismissed due to illness and died a few months later.

Wang Du died, and his son Wang Xin succeeded to the throne.
Ji Zun's younger brother Sun was a native of Yingyang, Yingchuan.
When I was young, I loved scriptures.
The family is wealthy, but Ji Zun is respectful, frugal and doesn't like to wear fancy clothes.
After her mother died, she carried the earth to her grave.
Once bullied by government officials, Ji Zun befriended guests and killed the government officials.
At first, the county thought he was weak, but later became afraid of him.

From Hebei, he was ordered to serve as a military commander.
The son in the house broke the law, so Ji Zun killed him.
Guangwu was angry and ordered Ji Zun to be arrested.
At this time, the chief registrar, Deputy Chen, advised him: "Ming Gong always wants the army to be in order. Now he can obey the law and not avoid the power. This is what is needed to educate the law." Guangwu pardoned him and made him an assassin and traitor general.
To the generals: Be more careful with Ji Zun!
He will still kill my son if he breaks the law, and he will never show any favoritism to you. Soon after, he paid homage to the partial general, followed him to pacify Hebei, and was granted the title of lord for his merits.
In the spring of the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was appointed General of the Conquering Capture Army and granted the title of Marquis of Yingyang.
He entered Jiguan with the hussar general Jing Dan, the Jianyi general Zhu You, the Han loyal general Wang Chang, the cavalry captain Wang Liang, Zang Gong and others, and attacked the Hongnong, Yanxin and Baihua barbarians in the south.
Ji Zun was hit by a crossbow arrow and his wound was bleeding. When everyone saw that Ji Zun was injured, they gradually retreated. Ji Zun kept shouting and scolding, and the soldiers fought harder and harder, thus defeating the enemy.
At that time, Zhang Man, a bandit among the Xincheng barbarians, gathered soldiers in dangerous places to harm the people. He ordered Ji Zun to attack, but Ji Zun cut off Zhang Man's food route. Zhang Man challenged him several times, but Ji Zun held on to the barrier and could not leave.
The remnants of Yanxin and Baihua reunited with Zhang Man and captured Huoyangju. Ji Zun then divided his troops to defeat them and force him to surrender.
In the spring of the third year of Jianwu, Zhang Man was hungry and sleepy. Ji Zun attacked his city and captured Zhang Man alive.
At first, Zhang Man offered sacrifices to heaven and earth, saying that he should be the king. When he was caught, he sighed: The prophecy was wrong to me! So he, his wife, and his children were beheaded.
Ji Zun led his troops south to attack Deng Feng's brother, Du Yan, and finally defeated him.
At this time, Zhang Feng, the governor of Zhuo County, caught the envoy and raised his troops to rebel. He claimed to be the supreme general and joined forces with Peng Chong.
In the fourth year of Jianwu, Ji Zun, Zhu You, Jianwei General Geng Yan, and Xiaoqi General Liu happy jointly attacked Zhang Feng.
Ji Zun's soldiers arrived first and attacked Zhang Feng in a hurry. Zhang Feng's hero Cao Meng captured Zhang Feng and surrendered.
At first, Zhang Feng was fond of alchemy. A Taoist priest said that Zhang Feng was regarded as the emperor. He wrapped a stone in a colorful bag and tied it to Zhang Feng's elbow, saying that there was a jade seal in the stone.
Zhang Feng believed it and rebelled.
After being caught and beheaded, he also said: There is a jade seal on his elbow. Ji Zun broke his stone vertebrae, and Zhang Feng realized that he had been deceived by the Taoist priest. He looked up to the sky and sighed: "I will die without regrets!" All the generals were led back, and Ji Zun was ordered to stay in Liangxiang to resist Peng Chong.
Therefore, he sent the guard Fu Xuan to attack Peng Chong's general Li Hao and Yu Lu, and defeated his army, beheading more than a thousand people.
They resisted each other for more than a year and were defeated several times. Many of Peng Chong's followers surrendered.
When Peng Chong died, Ji Zun marched to pacify his territory.
In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, he ordered Ji Zun and Jianwei General Geng Yan, Huya General Gai Yan, Han Zhong General Wang Chang, Capture General Ma Wu, Xiaoqi General Liu Xin, Wuwei General Liu Shang and others to attack Gongsun Shu from Tianshui.
The army stopped in Chang'an, and Guangwu's chariots also arrived, but Kaixiao did not want the Han soldiers to go to Long, so he excused himself.
Guangwu summoned the generals to discuss. They all say: You can temporarily delay the period of the sun and the moon of Wei Xiao, and add titles to his generals to promote their dispersion and disintegration. Ji Zun said: Kui Xiao has been plotting for a long time.
If he stands still and procrastinates for a while now, it will prompt him to deepen his deception and make Gongsun Shu increase his security, so it is better to march directly. Guangwu obeyed and sent Ji Zun as the vanguard.
Kaixiao sent his general Wang Yuan to stay at Longdi, and Ji Zun attacked, defeated Wang Yuan's army, and pursued him to Xinguan.
When the generals arrived, they fought with Kai Xiao but failed, so they retreated to Long.
Guangwu ordered Ji Zun to garrison troops in Qi, ordered Geng Yan to garrison troops in Qi, ordered General Feng Yi to garrison troops in the city, and ordered Grand Sima Wu Han and others to return to Chang'an.
Since then, Ji Zun has defeated Kuai Xiao several times.
See "Feng Yi Zhuan" for details.
In the autumn of the eighth year of Jianwu, he went up to Long from Guangwu.
When Kuai Xiao was destroyed, Guang Wu returned eastward and passed through Qian. He went to the Ji Zun military camp, comforted and fed the soldiers, and performed Huangmen martial arts, which stopped late at night.
At this time, Ji Zun was ill and was given a thick mattress to sit on, which was covered with the emperor's royal canopy.
Then let him march to Longxia.
When Gongsun Shu sent troops to rescue Wei Xiao, Wu Han, Geng Yan and others all fled back, except for Ji Zun who remained.
In the spring of the ninth year of Jianwu, he died in the army.
Ji Zun was an honest, conscientious, careful, self-denial, and dedicated to the public service. He always gave all the rewards he received to his soldiers. He had no private property at home. He wore a Wei belt, a quilt, and a quilt, and his wife's clothes were not colorful. Therefore, the emperor valued him.
After his death, sympathy and mourning were especially intense.
When the coffin arrived in Henan County, the emperor sent hundreds of officials to gather at the funeral site. Guangwu came in white mourning clothes and looked at the coffin in mourning.
When I walked back through the city gate and saw the funeral car, I couldn't help crying.
After the funeral ceremony was completed, he personally offered sacrifices with Tailao ceremony, just like Emperor Xuan performed Huo Guang's funeral.
Da Changqiu, Yezhe, and Henan Yin were ordered to carry out funeral arrangements, and Da Si Nong was responsible for the expenses.
Dr. Fan Shengshangshu, who was posthumously named Ji Zun, said: I heard about the noble virtues of the late king, respected the good, and rejected the ugly.
In the past, the great sage, the Great Ancestor, had far-sightedness, divided up nobility and territory, and divided the merits with his subordinates. He recorded the deeds of the heroes in books and praised their virtues.
During the lifetime, special etiquette is used to show favor. There is no need to sign up for events, and there is no need to leave in a hurry when entering the house.
After his death, he was granted a title so that he would have no heirs, and a deed was given to him to enjoy privileges from generation to generation, so that his favor would be passed on to eternity.
This is a long-lasting kindness bestowed by our great Han Dynasty to the descendants of heroes, so it has affected more than ten generations and lasted for more than two hundred years. It was abolished and revived, and it was extinct and continued.
Your Majesty is entrusted with the task of being extremely virtuous, promoting the ways of the ancestors, commending assistants in turn, and rewarding meritorious ministers, in line with the laws of the ancestors.
The marquis of Yingyang, Ji Zun, the conquering general, unfortunately died young.
Your Majesty is so kind and grieved that he welcomes you from afar to Henan. Sorrow and mourning are expressed in holy bows, funeral expenses are donated by the state, and wives and children are given to them in countless ways.
It is given to the deceased to benefit the living, and to provide kindness to the deceased to comfort relatives, to correct the world, to encourage education, and to be as high as the sun and the moon.
In ancient times, when a minister was ill, the king came to visit him, and when a minister died, the king came to mourn him. This was a profound virtue.
But this kind of gentlemanly virtue has been destroyed for a long time.
His Majesty restored this kind of etiquette, and all his ministers were moved by it, and they all encouraged themselves.
The minister privately saw that Ji Zun had accumulated good deeds and was loyal to the country. He went north to pacify Yuyang, and went west to resist Long and Shu. He ascended Longdi first and captured Lueyang deeply.
All the soldiers and horses retreated, but he remained alone.
He can control and control the soldiers so that they do not exceed the law.
The officials and people where his army was located were unaware of its existence.
The reputation of purity spreads throughout the country, and the reputation of honesty and innocence is known throughout the world.
He often distributed all the rewards he received to officials. He wore no expensive clothes and had no private property at home.
The brother of the same mother, Ji Wu, thought that he had no children, so he took a concubine for him and gave it to him. Ji Zun refused to accept it, thinking that he was in charge of state affairs, and did not dare to covet life and consider the private affairs of his heirs.
Before he died, he also ordered in his will to carry his coffin in an oxcart and bury him sparingly in Luoyang.
I asked him about his family affairs, but he always said nothing.
There is a long way to go, and death is the end of it.
When Ji Zun is a general, he uses Confucianism to select talents. When drinking and playing, he must sing elegant poems and throw pots.
After he built a temple for Confucius, he appointed a doctor of the Five Classics.
Although he is in the military, he does not forget to perform sacrifices. He can be said to be a person who obeys etiquette, enjoys rituals and music, and adheres to the good way.
Ritual, you have a title when you are alive, and you should be given a posthumous title after death. The title is used to distinguish between superior and inferior, and the posthumous title is used to understand good and evil.
I think that after Ji Zun's death, he should discuss his many achievements, follow the posthumous law in detail, and complete it with ancient rituals.
To show that the country abides by ancient rules and regulations and establishes heirs for future generations. The emperor then showed Fan Sheng's memorial to the minister.
After the burial, the emperor's chariot driver came again in person, presented the seals and ribbons of the generals and marquises, and carried them in a cart with red painted wheels. The warriors lined up in a military formation for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title of Marquis Cheng.
After the burial was completed, Guangwu visited his grave again and properly placed his wife's family.
Later, during the court meeting, the emperor often sighed: How can we get ministers like Ji Zun who care about the country and serve the public? Ji Zunzhi sees and thinks about Guangwu so deeply.
Without children, the feudal state was abolished.
My brother offered sacrifices at noon, and he was promoted to the prefect of Jiuquan.
summary:
**Yao Qi** (courtesy name Ci Kuang) was born in Jiaxian County, Yingchuan. Standing eight feet two inches tall with a striking appearance, he was known for solemnity and majesty. After his father Yao Meng, Governor of Guiyang, died, Yao Qi observed three years of mourning, earning village praise. When Guangwu raided Yingchuan, he recruited Yao Qi to attack Ji. During Wang Lang's rebellion, Yao Qi cleared crowded roads by brandishing his halberd and shouting, broke through a closed city gate, and later served under Deng Yu. Deng Yu recognized Yao Qi's capability, making him a partial general with 2,000 soldiers. Yao Qi captured several counties, fought bravely against Wang Lang's forces—killing over fifty enemies despite a forehead wound—and was appointed General Huya after Wang Lang's death. He advised Guangwu to consolidate Hebei's elite forces, and Guangwu smiled at his boldness. Yao Qi fought the Bronze Horse rebels, killing many despite initial setbacks, and later defeated bandits attacking his baggage, sustaining three wounds. After Guangwu ascended the throne, Yao Qi became Marquis of Ancheng with 5,000 households. As Prefect of Wei County, he suppressed Zhuo Jing's rebellion, beheading over 600, and pacified the region. When Li Lu plotted rebellion, Yao Qi showed mercy to Li Xiong, leading Li Lu to suicide from shame. Yao Qi served as Taizhong大夫 and Weiwei, known for integrity and remonstrating with the emperor, once stopping Guangwu from careless travel. He died in the tenth year of Jianwu, receiving posthumous honors as Marquis Zhong.

**Wang Ba** (courtesy name Yuan Bo) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. His family valued legal traditions, and he worked as a jailer before studying in Chang'an. When Guangwu passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba joined his army, fighting at Kunyang. Despite others leaving, Wang Ba remained loyal; Guangwu praised him, saying "The strong wind knows the strong grass." During Wang Lang's rebellion, Wang Ba falsely claimed the Hutuo River was frozen to calm frightened troops, and the ice miraculously formed, allowing crossing. He became a military commander and Marquis of Guan Nei, later capturing Wang Lang's seal. Known for comforting soldiers, he was made a partial general after Guangwu's ascension. In the fourth year of Jianwu, Wang Ba employed strategic patience against Su Mao, closing his camp and refusing battle until the enemy tired, then launching a surprise attack that routed them. He served as General Against Captives, fought Xiongnu forces at Gaoliu, and became Prefect of Shanggu. For over twenty years, he managed border defenses, built roads and barriers, and advocated peace with the Xiongnu. He died in the second year of Yongping, having been granted Marquis of Huailing.

**Ji Zun** (younger brother's grandson) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. Though wealthy, he was respectful and frugal. After killing a bullying government official, he joined Guangwu. As a military commander, he executed Guangwu's own son for breaking the law, earning Guangwu's respect. He became a partial general and Marquis of Yingyang. Ji Zun fought bravely despite arrow wounds, defeated Zhang Man by cutting his food supply, and captured him alive. He attacked Zhang Feng, whose rebellion stemmed from a Taoist priest's deception about a jade seal. Ji Zun resisted Peng Chong for over a year, and after Peng's death, pacified his territory. In the sixth year of Jianwu, he argued for direct attack against Kui Xiao, serving as vanguard. He remained steadfast when others retreated, dying in the army in the ninth year of Jianwu. Ji Zun was known for self-denial, giving rewards to soldiers, owning no private property, and wearing plain clothes. Guangwu mourned deeply, personally attending his funeral. Posthumously named Marquis Cheng, Ji Zun was praised for his purity, loyalty, and Confucian conduct—selecting talents by Confucian standards, reciting poetry, and establishing a Confucian temple. He had no children, so his title was abolished.

◆The biography of Chen Fan, whose courtesy name is Zhongju, was born in Pingyu, Runan.
My grandfather served as the governor of Hedong.
When Chen Fan was fifteen years old, he lived in a room with nothing to do, and it was very dirty inside and outside. His father's friend Xue Qin, who was from the same county, came to see him and said to Chen Fan: "Child, why don't you clean up to welcome the guests?"
Chen Fan said: When a real man is alive, he should sweep away the rubbish in the world. How can he only care about his own room?
Xue Qin knew that he had the ambition to clarify the world and admired him very much.
At first, he served as an official in the county and was elected as Xiaolian and awarded the title of doctor.
Because his mother passed away, he resigned from office and lived in mourning.
When the mourning period expired, the governor Zhou Jing called him to serve as a chariot, but because he had different opinions on his advice, he abandoned the talisman and left.
Later, the government recruited Fang Zheng, but he didn't go.
Taiwei Li Gu recommended him and promoted him to Yilang, and then he was promoted to the prefect of Le'an.
At this time, Li Ying was appointed as the governor of Qingzhou, and he was famous for his strict governance. After hearing the news, everyone in the subordinate city asked to leave. Chen Fan stayed alone because of his clean and honest performance.
Zhou Chu, a county man, kept himself clean and cared for himself. He was invited by the county guards before and after him, but he refused to go.
Only Chen Fan can recruit him. Chen Fan called him by his name instead of his name and respected him very much.
A bed was specially built for him. After Zhou Chu left, the bed was hung up.
The common man Zhao Xuan buried his relatives without closing the tomb passage, and lived in it for more than 20 years. The towns and cities praised his filial piety, and the states and counties treated him with courtesy several times. The county recommended him to Chen Fan and asked about his wife and children. They found out that Zhao Xuan's five children were all born during his mourning period.
Chen Fan then said angrily: "Sages make rituals, and moral people must abide by them, and unworthy people should also strive to do so."
And the number of sacrifices does not need to be too many, as too much would be disrespectful.
You are sleeping in the tomb, raising your children in the tomb, deceiving the world, stealing your reputation, confusing the people, and insulting the ghosts and gods. How is this unreasonable!
So his crime was punished.
General Liang Ji was a powerful man in the world. At that time, he sent a letter to Chen Fan, asking Chen Fan to handle private matters. The messenger was not allowed to see him, so he lied and asked to see Chen Fan. Chen Fan got angry and beat the messenger to death, and was sentenced to military service for his crime.
After a slight promotion, he was appointed as minister.
At this time, mountain bandits in Lingling and Guiyang were in harm's way, and the minister considered sending troops to fight. The emperor also ordered the prefectures and counties to select filial piety, integrity, and maocai as appropriate.
Chen Fan went to the Supreme Court to argue and refute, saying: In the past, when Emperor Gaozu established a great cause, the people in the country were relieved, and the officials raised the people as if they were their own sons.
Now the common people in the two counties are all the sons of the emperor. Isn't the cause of the harm to the sons caused by the corruption and cruelty of the local officials?
We should strictly instruct the three government agencies to secretly evaluate the prefects, governors, and county magistrates. Those who are misbehaving in politics and harming the people should be reported to the court immediately, and people who are upright, virtuous, honest, honest, able to promote laws and love the people should be selected to replace them.
