Shi Sunrui said: Since the end of the year, the sun has not been seen, it has been raining for a long time, the moon has violated the law star, comets and stars are still appearing, it is cloudy during the day and sunny at night, and the fog invades. This is a victory that should be completed in a short time and launched from within.
This opportunity is not to be missed, so hurry up and make plans.
Wang Yun thought Shi Sunrui was right. So he secretly combined with Dong Zhuo's general Lu Bu and made him an internal correspondent.
Just as Dong Zhuo entered the court to congratulate Emperor Xian on his recovery, Lu Bu had time to kill Dong Zhuo.
The words are in "The Biography of Dong Zhuo".
Wang Yun began to want to pardon Dong Zhuo's subordinates, and Lu Bu also persuaded Wang Yun many times.
But Wang Yun finally became suspicious and said: These people are not guilty and are just following Dong Zhuo.
Now if you think that they are rebellious and you are pardoning them, it will just make them doubt themselves. This is not a way to make them stable.
Lu Bu also wanted to reward Dong Zhuo's property to the ministers and generals, but Wang Yun refused.
Wang Yun usually looked down on Lu Bu and treated him like a swordsman.
Lu Bu also believed that he had merit and boasted about his achievements. He was not satisfied and gradually became at odds with Wang Yun.
Wang Yun has a strong temperament and hates evil as much as hatred. He began to be afraid of the jackal Dong Zhuo, so he suppressed himself and obeyed his will.
After Dong Zhuo was annihilated, he thought that there would be no more troubles. In public places, he rarely had a gentle look, maintained the right path and was prudent, and did not use expedient measures. Therefore, the people below him did not support him very much.
Most of Dong Zhuo's generals and serving officers were from Liangzhou, so Wang Yun considered dismantling Dong Zhuo's original troops.
Someone said to Wang Yun: Liangzhou people have always been afraid of the Yuan family and feared Guandong. Now if it is revoked, everyone in Guandong will be in danger.
Huangfu Yizhen can be the general and lead this army, so that he can stay in Shaanxi to appease them, and slowly conspire with Guandong to observe its changes.
Wang Yun said: Otherwise, those who raise volunteers in Guandong are all my people.
Now if troops are stationed in Shaanxi far away from danger, although it can appease Liangzhou and make Guandong suspicious, this is extremely unacceptable.
At that time, people spread rumors that all the people in Liangzhou would be killed, so they were afraid of each other and rioted.
Those in Guanzhong all defended themselves with troops.
They also told each other: Ding Yansi and Cai Bojie were both implicated and convicted just because they were friendly with Dong Gong. Since we are not pardoned now, we want to cancel the army. If we cancel it today, tomorrow we will be slaughtered for the sake of fish and meat!
Dong Zhuo's generals Li Chun, Guo Si and others had previously placed troops in Guandong, so they felt uneasy and conspired to cause chaos and besieged Chang'an.
The city was broken and Lu Bu fled.
Lu Bu stood outside Ma Qingsuo's gate and called to Wang Yun: "Can you go?"
Wang Yun said: If I get the blessing of the emperor, it is my wish to secure the country.
Otherwise, he will die for his country. The Emperor is young and only relies on me. I can't bear to try to escape by chance when he is in trouble.
I would like to ask all the princes of Guandong to think of the country.
At first, Wang Yun used Song Yi from the same county as Feng Yi on the left and Wang Hong as Fufeng on the right.
At that time, the people of Sanfu were prosperous, there were many soldiers, and there was a lot of food. Li Ju and others wanted to kill Wang Yun, fearing that the two counties would be troubled. So Song Yi and Wang Hong were recruited first.
Wang Hong sent an envoy to tell Song Yi: "Guo Si and Li Chu were out of town, so they did not harm Wang Yun."
If we apply today, tomorrow we will all be exterminated. What are your plans? Song Yi said: Although misfortune and fortune are unpredictable, the king's destiny cannot be evaded.
Wang Hong said: The reason why the rebels are fierce is Dong Zhuo, not to mention his party members?
If you lead the troops to jointly attack the evil people around the monarch, Shandong will definitely respond. This is a plan to turn disaster into blessing.
Song Yi refused.
Wang Hong could not be independent by himself, so he recruited all of them and sent them to the judicial authorities.
Li Chu then arrested Wang Yun, Song Yi, and Wang Hong, and sentenced them all to death.
Wang Yun was fifty-six years old at this time.
The eldest son Shizhong Wang Gai, the second sons Wang Jing, Wang Ding and more than ten members of their clan were all killed. Only the elder brothers Wang Chen and Wang Ling were able to escape back to their hometown.
The emperor was grieved and the people were dejected. No one dared to collect Wang Yun's body. Only the old official Ping Ling ordered Zhao Jian to abandon his official camp for mourning.
Wang Hong's long prose was full of energy when he was young and he didn't pay attention to small details.
When he first served as the prefect of Hongnong, he interrogated those who served eunuchs in the county and bought titles. Although their official titles reached two thousand dan, they were arrested, tortured, and killed dozens of people, which shocked the neighboring counties.
On weekdays, he had conflicts with Hu Zhong, the captain of Sili School. When Wang Hong was imprisoned, Hu Zhong couldn't wait to kill him.
Before Wang Hong died, he cursed: Song Yi was a stupid Confucian and was not capable of planning big things.
Hu Zhong gloats over misfortune, and disaster will befall him.
Later, when Hu Zhong was sleeping, Wang Hong often beat him with a stick, so he fell ill and died within a few days.
Later, the capital was moved to Xuchang. The emperor missed Wang Yun's loyalty and reburied Wang Yun. He sent General Huben Zhonglang to carry out hanging sacrifices, gave him the secret weapon of Dongyuan, gave him his official seal and ribbon, and returned it to his county.
King Yun Sun Wanghei was granted the title of Marquis of Anleting, with a settlement of 300 households.
Shi Sunrui, courtesy name Junrong, was born in Fufeng County. Very talented and strategic.
Scholar Sun Rui was spared from death because of Wang Yun's dedicated campaign against Dong Zhuo.
Later he became the third elder of the country and the Guanglu doctor.
When the three Dukes were vacant, Yang Biao and Huangfu Song both gave way to the scholar Sun Rui.
In the second year of Xingping, he returned eastward from the emperor and was killed by the rebels.
Zhao Jian, courtesy name Shumao, was a native of Changling County. He had a simple and upright character and was resourceful.
In Yongpingzhong, he is the minister and is in charge of elections.
Dong Zhuo repeatedly wanted to ask him to do something privately, but Zhao Jian refused to listen and spoke harshly.
Dong Zhuo was angry and called him to kill him. Everyone was afraid, and Zhao Jian's words and demeanor did not change his normal state.
Dong Zhuo regretted and released him.
There was great chaos in Chang'an and he was a guest in Jingzhou. Liu Biao treated him generously.
Cao Cao pacified Jingzhou and promoted him. Holding Zhao Jian's hand, he said: "I regret meeting you too late."
He died during the tenure of Prime Minister Zhong Yao.
The historian commented: Although the scholar-bureaucrats set themselves up to do things right, they might as well use power to help others.
If Wang Yun respected Dong Zhuo and cited his authority, and took advantage of his unpreparedness to punish his crimes, then the world would be safe and peaceful.
The reason why he was not found guilty in the end was because he knew he was sincere and loyal.
Therefore, Wang Yun's recommendation of Dong Zhuo cannot be called injustice, decentralization of power cannot be called a random measure, and taking advantage of someone's unpreparedness cannot be called deceit.
When the plan is realized, it will be right and there will be no need to plan anymore.
summary:
Chen Fan, courtesy name Zhongju, was born in Pingyu, Runan. His grandfather served as Governor of Hedong. At fifteen, he lived in a dirty room. When his father's friend Xue Qin asked why he didn't clean it, Chen Fan replied that a real man should sweep away the world's rubbish, not just his own room. Xue Qin admired his ambition.

Chen Fan began as a county official, was elected Xiaolian, and became a doctor. After his mother's death, he resigned to mourn. When the mourning period ended, Governor Zhou Jing summoned him, but Chen Fan left due to differing opinions. He later refused government recruitment. Taiwei Li Gu recommended him, and he became Prefect of Le'an. He remained in office while others fled from strict Governor Li Ying. Chen Fan recruited the reclusive Zhou Chu, treating him with great respect. He exposed Zhao Xuan's false filial piety—Zhao had lived in a tomb for over twenty years but fathered five children there—and punished him for deceiving the world.

When General Liang Ji sent a messenger requesting private favors, Chen Fan beat the messenger to death and was sentenced to military service. He later became a minister. When mountain bandits threatened Lingling and Guiyang, Chen Fan argued against sending troops, stating that corrupt officials caused the unrest and that replacing them with virtuous men would resolve the problem without military action. He also criticized the expedient recommendation of talents. Because he offended the emperor's associates, he was sent to be Governor of Yuzhang.

Chen Fan was promoted to Dahonglu. When Emperor Huan wanted to execute Li Yun for blunt remonstrance, Chen Fan wrote to save him and was dismissed. He was later reinstated as Guangluxun. He advised Emperor Huan against excessive titles and rewards, particularly for Deng Zun and Huang Jun, warning that improper enfeoffments caused cosmic disorder, crop failure, and poverty. He noted that thousands of palace maids impoverished the country and urged their release. Emperor Huan adopted some advice, releasing five hundred maids and limiting titles.

Chen Fan advised against Emperor Huan's hunting at Guangcheng Garden, citing the "Three Empties"—empty fields, court, and warehouses—and ongoing wars. The emperor ignored him. As Guangluxun, Chen Fan and Huang Wan conducted elections without favoring the powerful, leading to false accusations and his dismissal. He was soon recalled as a servant and later became Taiwei, though he declined, citing his inferiority to Hu Guang, Wang Chang, and Li Ying.

Chen Fan defended Li Ying and others punished for violating the emperor's will, weeping as he pleaded. He argued for leniency toward officials who executed eunuch associates despite pardons, comparing them to loyal ministers of old. Emperor Huan grew angrier and ignored him. The eunuchs hated Chen Fan, but because of his reputation, they dared not harm him directly.

When Li Ying was imprisoned for party affiliation, Chen Fan wrote a strong remonstrance, comparing the persecution to Qin's book burning. He warned that punishing the innocent would cause chaos and noted that droughts and famines plagued the land while the palace hoarded wealth. Emperor Huan dismissed Chen Fan for allegedly selecting inappropriate talents.

After Emperor Huan's death, Empress Dowager Dou appointed Chen Fan as Grand Tutor. When ministers feigned illness during the succession crisis, Chen Fan reproached them, and they returned to court. Emperor Ling granted Chen Fan the title of Marquis of Gaoxiang with three hundred households, but Chen Fan declined ten times.

Chen Fan and General Dou Wu planned to eliminate the eunuchs. Chen Fan warned the Empress Dowager about eunuch corruption, but she ignored him. When the plot was exposed, Cao Jie forged orders to kill Dou Wu. The seventy-year-old Chen Fan led over eighty officials and students into the palace, shouting against the eunuch rebellion. He was arrested, kicked and stepped on by eunuch soldiers, and killed that same day. His family was exiled, and his clan and disciples were imprisoned. His friend Zhu Zhen collected and buried his body, hiding Chen Fan's son Chen Yi. Zhu Zhen endured torture without revealing the son's location. Chen Yi later became Prime Minister of Lu.

The historian commented that during Emperors Huan and Ling's reigns, Chen Fan established a reputation for moral integrity, speaking out against corruption and competing with eunuchs despite great danger. Though his plans failed, his faith sustained the people, and the Han dynasty survived over a hundred years due to his efforts.

translation:
Kaixiao, courtesy name Jimeng, was from Chengji County, Tianshui County.
When he was young, he served as a state and county official.
Wang Mang's imperial advisor Liu Xin introduced Kai Xiao as his Yuanshi.
After Liu Xin died, Wei Xiao returned to his hometown.
His uncle, Kui Cui, had always been bold and chivalrous, and was supported by everyone.
When he heard that Gengshi was proclaimed emperor and that Wang Mang's troops were defeated, he planned to raise troops to respond to the Han army with his brother Wei Yi, Yang Guang from Shanggui, and Zhou Zong from Ji.
Wei Xiao stopped him and said: "Sending troops to fight is a dangerous thing!"
What sin does our clan have? Wei Cui refused to listen, so he gathered thousands of people to attack Pingxiang and killed Wang Mang's Zhenrong Dayin. Wei Cui, Yang Guang and others thought that if they wanted to take action, they should appoint a general to unify everyone's thoughts. They all said that Wei Xiao was well-known and loved scriptures, so they jointly recommended Wei Xiao as the general.
Wei Xiao resigned and had no choice but to say: "Fathers and wise men think highly of me, young man, and must use my opinion before I dare to obey." Everyone said: OK.
After Kuai Xiao was established, he sent an envoy to hire Fang Wang from Pingling as a military advisor.
Fang Wangzhi suggested to Kaixiao: "I want to obey the destiny of the people and support the Han Dynasty and start an uprising. Today, I am standing in Nanyang. Wang Mang is still guarding Chang'an. Although he wants to act in the name of the Han Dynasty, he has not actually received the order from the Han Dynasty. What will he do to convince everyone?"
We should quickly build a temple for Emperor Gaozu, worship him as a minister, and use the so-called "Shinto teachings" to seek help from humans and gods.
Moreover, etiquette may be added or deleted from time to time, and there is no standard between simplicity and splendor.
Cutting the ground to open a sign area, even if it is a hut with earthen steps, can still show respect.
Although it is simple and has no material equipment, the gods will not leave here. Kuai Xiao listened to his advice and built a temple in the east of the city to worship Gaozu, Taizong and Shizong.
Wei Xiao and others all called themselves ministers and deacons, and Zhu Shi held a jade in his hand to appeal to the gods.
After the blessing, various functional officials came and went in the court, some leading horses and wielding swords, some carrying plates and spoons, so they killed animals and formed an alliance.
Alliance Dao: There are a total of thirty-one generals with 16 surnames in the alliance, who follow the way of heaven and raise troops to assist Liu Zong.
If there is someone with evil intentions, the gods will destroy him.
Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Wu caused his death, the clan was bloodbathed, and the race was destroyed. The officials marched forward with spoons containing the blood of the sacrifices. The guards held up their hands and bowed to the generals, saying: "The spoons are not stained with blood. If you don't drink the blood, you will deceive the gods and punish him according to the oath of the alliance." In this way, the blood of the sacrifice was applied on the mouth and the covenant was carried out exactly according to the ancient rituals.
At the end of the ceremony, a document was issued to all counties saying:
The first day of the seventh month of the first year of the Han Dynasty is Jiyou Day.
On the past day, General Wei Xiao, White Tiger General Wei Cui, Left General Wei Yi, Right General Yang Guang, Mingwei General Wang Zun, Yunqi General Zhou Zong, etc., sent a proclamation to the state shepherds, department supervisors, county pawns, company leaders, Dayin, Yin, Wei team officials, subordinate Zheng, and subordinate orders: Wang Mang, the former lord of Xindu, insulted and neglected the world, violated the Tao, and violated the principles. He poisoned Emperor Xiaoping and usurped the throne.
Pretending to be destined by heaven, he forged talismans and falsely said that he should replace the Han Emperor, deceiving the people and angering heaven.
Being arrogant and violent is used to cover up the false text and serves as auspicious talismans.
They make fun of the gods with nonsense words and sing praises of disaster.
Although there are many bamboos in Chu and Yue, they are not enough to describe their crimes.
Everyone in the world heard and witnessed what he did.
Now I will briefly mention a few major aspects to explain to the officials and the people.
Heaven is the father and the earth is the mother, and they use corresponding time to respond to misfortunes and blessings.
Wang Mang clearly knew the principle of telepathy between heaven and man, but he was stubborn and deliberately offended, regardless of taboos. Whenever there was a disaster, he quoted historical biographies to distort explanations and cover up his crimes.
In the past, Qin Shihuang destroyed the posthumous title system and called himself the First Emperor while he was still alive. From then on, it was passed down from generation to generation, hoping to proclaim himself emperor from generation to generation until eternity. Wang Mang followed in the footsteps of Qin Shihuang and promulgated a thirty-six thousand year calendar, claiming that the Wang regime would be passed down from generation to generation during these years.
Along the path of the Qin Dynasty's demise, endless calendars can be derived.
This is his grave sin.
Wang Mang divided the prefecture, cut off its boundaries, and renamed Tianxia Tian as Wang Tian.
Buying and selling is prohibited. It was stipulated that famous mountains and swamps should be imprisoned, taking away the people's livelihood of fishing and hunting.
The construction of nine temples was extremely wasteful and extravagant.
Dig up all the tombs in the east of the river and plunder the hills and ridges.
This is his grave sin against the earth.
Respecting crooks, trusting traitors, killing loyal and upright people, creating excuses, cars with red curtains galloping on the road, officials wearing ceremonial crowns arrest innocent people morning and night, and kill all the people's families at every turn.
Use the cruel incineration method to burn good people to death, abolish the laws and regulations that were in good time in the past, and use alcohol to break the five poisons.
Government orders change every day, official names remain the same every month, currency changes every year, officials and people make mistakes and don't know what to do, and merchants and travelers are poor and distressed, crying in the market streets.
The law that established six administrations increased taxes, exploited the people, filled private pockets to enrich themselves, bribed public officials, and confiscated wealth to the three ministers and the assistant minister, and there was no inspection at all. The common people made money for their crimes, tied their necks with iron chains, and were enslaved by bell officials. Hundreds of thousands of prisoners and slaves gathered together. Craftsmen starved to death, and the stench of corpses could be smelled in Chang'an City.
It has messed up China, and its arrogance is even more arrogant. It attacks the Hu in the north, disturbs the Jinyue in the south, invades the Qiang and Rong in the west, and harasses the Qian in the east. The neighboring countries on all sides have merged into the border and become troubles. The counties and counties on the border, along the rivers and seas, have suffered misfortune and all the people have died.
Therefore, under Wang Mang’s tyrannical rule, there were tens of thousands of people killed and injured in wars, people framed under the brutal criminal laws, people who froze to death and starved to death, and diseases and plagues that killed tens of millions of people.
The corpses of the dead were thrown into the wild and could not be buried, the living fled and fled, and young orphans and women were displaced and plundered.
This is his grave sin against humanity. Therefore, God took pity on the people and punished Wang Mang. Several of his sons were killed by himself, and his wife was also angry to death.
The ministers rebelled against him, and the situation for his demise was already set.
Grand Sima Dong Zhong, Imperial Advisor Liu Xin, and General Wei Wang She all united to disintegrate from within; Si Ming Kong Ren, Nayan Yanyou, and Zhizong Chen Mao surrendered outside.
Today, there are more than two million soldiers in Shandong. They have pacified Qi, Chu, Xia Shu, and Han, and pacified Wan and Luo. They are based in Aocang, guarding Hanguan, and spreading their orders everywhere, proclaiming their reputation in Zhongyue.
Reviving the Han Dynasty to succeed Liu Si, enfeoffing all the kingdoms, following the old system of Emperor Gaozu, restoring the traditional virtues of Xiaowen, and quelling those who dare to disobey the order by force.
Send envoys to neighboring countries to restore their original titles.
Then he returned to reorganize his troops and put away the bows, arrows, and golden drums.
I specifically order the people to stay in their own place, live and work in peace and contentment, and they will live up to their responsibilities.
Wei Xiao then led an army of 100,000 to kill Chen Qing, the shepherd of Yongzhou.
Prepare to attack Anxi.
Wang Xiang, the Great Yin of Anding, was the son of Wang Mang's cousin Ping'ahou Wang Tan. He was quite popular in the Anding state, and no one in his county rebelled against him.
Wei Xiao then wrote to Wang Xiang, telling him the destiny of heaven, and repeatedly gave him instructions, but Wang Xiang never obeyed.
So they marched in, captured him, declared to the people, and then killed him, and all Anding surrendered.
At this time, someone in Chang'an City raised troops and killed Wang Mang.
Wei Xiao then sent his generals to seize Longxi, Wudu, Jincheng, Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang, and captured them all.
In the second year of Gengshi, envoys were sent to recruit Wei Xiao, Wei Cui, Wei Yi and others.
Wei Xiao was about to meet with Gengshi. Fang Wang believed that Gengshi's future was still uncertain and resolutely stopped him, but Wei Xiao refused to listen.
Fang Wang wrote a letter of thanks and left, saying:
Generals like Yi Yin and Lu Shang will establish the achievements of the founding of the country and carry forward achievements that are not common in one generation. But now when major events are still being hastily established, heroes and heroes have not yet gathered together.
I am from a different county, and my faults have not yet been exposed. I originally wanted to follow Guo Wei's example in serving King Yan Zhao, so as to attract a great hero like Le Yi and join him under the general's command. Therefore, when you hired me, I came with the wind and did not refuse.
The general respects the talented with the highest virtue, widely adopts his plans, his actions are meritorious, and his troops can hit the key points. Now the foundation has been set, and the Prime Minister's great achievements are being achieved.
Nowadays, there are many talented people, and their wings are already full. I hope that I don’t have any virtue or talent above ordinary people. I am really ashamed to be ranked first among the guests.
Although I have a moral integrity and want to weigh the expediency of resigning and staying in my job, I will never abandon my original intention and have other ambitions.
Why?
After Fan Li helped Gou Jian destroy Wu, he accepted his guilt and took a boat to the five lakes. Jin Wengong's uncle's uncle also stopped on the river on the way back to the country with Wen Gong, apologized to Wen Gong and asked to resign.
With the virtues of Fan Li and Zifu, they have left their names in the history books of Yue and Jin. If they still blame themselves for requesting to return to their hometown, I hope that they have no merit, so it is very appropriate to resign.
I heard that there is Longchi Mountain in Wushi County, with a small road leading to the south, connecting it with the Han Dynasty. There are often strange people and strangers there. In your spare time, you can seek out the truth.
May the general encourage him.
Wei Xiao came to Chang'an, and he was appointed as the right general. Wei Cui and Wei Yi still maintained their original titles.
In the winter of that year, Wei Cui and Wei Yi planned to rebel against Gengshi and return to the north. Wei Xiao was afraid of harming himself, so he reported the matter to Gengshi, and Wei Cui and Wei Yi were killed.
Gengshi felt that Kui Xiao was loyal to him, so he made him the imperial censor.
In the summer of the next year, Chimei entered the pass and was disturbed by Sanfu.
It was rumored that Guangwu was already located in Hebei, so Wei Xiao suggested to Gengshi that he should hand over the power to Liu Liang, Guangwu's uncle, but Gengshi refused to listen.
The generals wanted to kidnap Gengshi when he returned to the east, and Wei Xiao also participated in this plan.
After the incident was exposed, Gengshi sent someone to summon Wei Xiao. Wei Xiao claimed that he was ill and would not go away, so he and his subordinates Wang Zun and Zhou Zong led their troops to defend themselves.
Gengshi sent Jinwu Deng Ye to lead an army to surround Kaixiao, but Kaixiao closed the gate and refused to defend. At dusk, he could not hold on and broke the siege. Kaixiao and dozens of riders cut down the city gate at night and fled back to Tianshui.
Then he gathered his old troops, occupied the original territory, and called himself General Xizhou.
When the reform failed, all the senior scholar-bureaucrats in Sanfu fled to Tianshui to join Kaixiao.
Kui Xiao has always been honest and respectful, and he tries his best to introduce famous people as common people's acquaintances.
In the past, Wang Mang's Pinghe great Yin Chang'an Gu Gong was appointed as the official in charge, Pingling Fan Ku was appointed as his mentor, Zhao Bing, Su Heng, and Zheng Xing were the wine drinkers, Shen Tugang and Du Lin were the book holders, Yang Guang, Wang Zun, Zhou Zong and Pingxiang people were on patrol, Wang Jie from Heyang and Wang Yuan from Changling were the generals, and the relatives of Du Ling and Jin Dan were the guests.
From this, he became famous in Xizhou and became famous in Shandong.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, the great Situ Deng Yuxi attacked Chimei and settled in Yunyang. Deng Yu Pi led his troops to rebel against Deng Yu and headed west toward Tianshui. Wei Xiao met the attack, defeated Feng Huanyin at Gaoping, and captured all the baggage.
Therefore, Deng Yu followed the emperor's will and sent a special envoy, Ji Jie Ming, to serve as the general of Xizhou, and he was able to dominate the political affairs of Liangzhou and Shuofang.
When Chimei went to Chang'an and wanted to go west to Long, Kaixiao sent general Yang Guang to attack and defeated Chimei. He also pursued and defeated Chimei between Wushi and Jingyang.
Wei Xiao not only made contributions to the Han Dynasty, but also accepted the title of nobility from Deng Yu, and was able to appoint his confidants. Many people advised him to be the envoy to the capital.
Three years later, Wei Xiao wrote to the capital.
Guangwu had always heard of his virtues and reputation, so he rewarded him with special etiquette, addressed him by name, and used the etiquette of a state guest to comfort and recommend him deeply.
At this time, Lü Kun, a native of Chencang, supported tens of thousands of people, and was connected with Gongsun Shu, and invaded the three assistants.
Wei Xiao once again sent troops to help General Feng Yi attack the west, drove Lu Qian away, and sent an envoy to report.
The emperor politely replied in handwriting:
I admire your virtue and want to befriend you.
In the past, King Wen of Zhou had two out of three parts of the world, and he also served the Yin Shang Dynasty.
But the blunt sword of the horse cannot be forced to be used.
I have received patronage ten times the price of Bole several times. A fly can only fly a few steps away, but if it is attached to its tail, it can surpass a group of flies.
You and I are blocked by thieves and cannot greet each other often.
The general was loyal and courteous, supported and rescued people in danger, resisted Gongsun Shu's troops in the south, and resisted the Qiang and Hu bandits in the north. Therefore, Feng Yi marched westward, and thousands of people were trapped in Sanfu. Without the help of the general, Xianyang would have fallen into the hands of the thieves.
Nowadays, the bandits in Guandong often gather in groups, aiming to achieve great success and have no time to spare, so they did not parade in Chengdu to compete with Gongsun Shu.
If Gongsun Shu invades Hanzhong and Sanfu, I would like to borrow the general's troops and horses to have a showdown with him.
If this can be done, it will be a blessing from God, and it is time for wise men to plan their achievements, cut off territories, discuss merits and reward them.
Guan Zhong said: It was my parents who gave birth to me, and it was Uncle Bao who helped me succeed. From now on, you and I can communicate with each other in handwriting, and don't believe in the rumors of others to sow discord.
From then on, Guangwu's kindness to him became even more grand.
Later, Gongsun Shu sent troops to Hanzhong several times, and sent envoys to confer the title of Grand Sikong, King of Fu'an, Yinshou on Kaixiao.
Wei Xiao believed that he had once been an enemy of Shu and felt that it was shameful to be his minister, so he beheaded the envoys and sent out troops to attack and defeated Gongsun Shu's army. Therefore, Shu soldiers no longer went north.
At this time, the generals of Guanzhong wrote several times about the situation of Shu's attack. The emperor conveyed these opinions to Wei Xiao and asked him to send troops to attack Shu to test his credibility.
Wei Xiao then sent his chief to write a letter in the history, saying that the three auxiliary forces were weak and with Lu Fang at his side, it was not appropriate to attack Shu.
Guangwu knew that Wei Xiao wanted to step on both sides of the boat and did not want the world to be unified, so he slightly lowered the courtesy to Wei Xiao and corrected the etiquette between the monarch and his ministers.
At first, Wei Xiao had a good relationship with Lai She and Ma Yuan, so the emperor sent Lai She and Ma Yuan several times as envoys to persuade Wei Xiao to enter the court and promise him a high title.
Kuai Xiao was unwilling to return to the east, so he sent envoys to see him one after another with memorials expressing his humility, saying that he had no merit and would wait until the four sides were settled before resigning and returning to his hometown.
Five years later, the emperor once again sent Lai She to persuade Kaixiao to send his son to serve. Kaixiao heard that both Liu Yong and Peng Chong had been destroyed, so he sent his eldest son Wei Xun to follow Laishe to the capital to pay a visit. He was named Hu Qi Xiaowei and Marquis of Qiang.
However, Wang Yuan and Wang Jie, the generals of Wei Xiao, often thought that the success or failure of the world was still unknown and were unwilling to submit to Guangwu wholeheartedly.
Wang Yuan then said to Wei Xiao: "In the past, Chang'an, the capital of the West, was responded to by all directions, and the world looked up to him, saying that the world was at peace."
Once the reform fails, the king will have almost no place to stay.
Now there are Gongsun Shu in the south, Lu Fang in the north, Jianghu Haitai, Zhang Bu, Dong Xian and more than a dozen princes, each occupying one side. They want to accommodate Ma Yuan's opinions, give up the Qiancheng foundation, and live as guests in dangerous countries in order to be safe. This is following the track of overturning the car, and it is not a good plan.

Emperor Guangwu wanted Gongsun Shu to surrender, so he issued an edict to inform Gongsun Shu: In previous years, edicts were issued frequently to enlighten and show kindness. Don't doubt yourself because of the harm done to She and Cen Peng.
Now as long as you return as scheduled, you can ensure the integrity of the family; if you are confused and don't realize it, it will be like sending meat into the tiger's mouth, but there is no way to do it!
Your generals are tired, and all the officials want to go home and are unwilling to continue to garrison. There are countless notes in the edict, but I will not break my promise. Gongsun Shu finally had no intention of surrendering.
In September, Wu Han defeated and beheaded its chief disciple Xie Feng and its chief Jinwu Yuan Ji, and Han troops stationed in Chengdu.
Gongsun Shu said to Yancen: What should we do now? Cen said: A man should survive in death, how can he sit and wait for death?
Wealth is easy to accumulate and should not be grudged. Gongsun Shu took out all the gold and silk and recruited more than 5,000 death squads. They cooperated with Yancen at the city bridge, pretending to raise flags and beating drums to challenge, but secretly sent strange troops to go behind Wu Han's army to attack and defeat Wu Han's army.
Wu Han fell into the water and managed to get out of the water by grabbing the horse's tail.
In November, Zang Gong's army arrived at Xianmen.
Gongsun Shu saw that the divination said: "Capture and die below the city." He was overjoyed and thought that Wu Han and others should die under the city.
So he personally led tens of thousands of people to attack Wu and Han, causing Yancen to reject Zang Palace.
In the big battle, Yancen won three times in three games.
From early morning to noon, the soldiers had no food and were very tired. Wu Han ordered the strong men to attack. Gongsun Shu's soldiers were in chaos. Gongsun Shu was shot in the chest and fell off his horse.
The people on the left and right used cars to rescue Gongsun Shu into the city.
Gongsun Shu handed over his troops to Yancen and died in the evening.
The next morning, Yancen surrendered to Wu Han.
Wu Han then killed Gongsun Shu's wife, killed all the Gongsun clan, and also killed the entire Yancen clan.
He also sent troops to loot and burn Gongsun Shu's palace.
Guangwu got angry when he heard this and condemned Wu Han.
He also ordered Liu Shang, the deputy general of Wu Han, to say: "The city has been surrendered for three days, and all the officials have obeyed. There are tens of thousands of children, mothers, and mothers. Once the troops are set on fire, it will make people's noses sore when they hear it!"
The descendants of your clan, Liu Shang, have also experienced official positions. How can they bear to do such a thing?
Looking up at the sky, looking down at the earth, Qin Xiba letting go of the rice to return to his mother or Le Yang sipping the son's soup, which one is more benevolent?
It is a loss of morality to kill generals and hang their people.
At first, Chang Shao and Zhang Long persuaded Gongsun Shu to surrender to the Han Dynasty, but Shu refused. Chang Shao and Zhang Long both died of depression.
Guangwu issued an edict to posthumously confer Chang Shao as Taichang and Zhang Long as Shao Luxun. They were buried in the same ceremony as Taichang and Guang Luxun.
All those who were loyal and upright were commended and honored.
Cheng Wu and Li Yu were both promoted and employed because of their talents.
So all the people in the West were happy, and there was no one who was unwilling to return.
Historians commented: In the past, Zhao Tuo established himself as the king of South Vietnam due to the unrest in the early Han Dynasty. Gongsun Shu also stole the emperor's seat in the Shu Han Dynasty. It is presumed that he had no other functions and only perished in the end. Could it be that he was able to live in a corner because of the remote location?
Although Gongsun Shu was a Han official, he did not have much capital to rely on. He only enjoyed himself in culture and customs, so that he could realize his wishes and strategies.
If the Dao is insufficient but the intention is sufficient, you cannot take advantage of the opportunity to make meritorious deeds to observe the changes of the times. Instead, you should sit on the edge and take comfort in the depth. This is the same as when the Marquis of Wei rejoiced in the solidity of rivers and mountains, and Wu Qi said to him that the country's strength lies in virtue and not in danger.
When he thanked his subordinates and insisted that rise and fall were fate and refused to surrender, he was no longer the same as Sun Haoni, who surrendered to King Xu Rui and Xu Nan, who met Chu Zi with a jade in his head.
summary:
Kui Xiao, courtesy name Jimeng, was from Chengji County, Tianshui. He began his career as a local official and later served under Wang Mang's advisor Liu Xin. After Liu Xin's death, Kui Xiao returned home. His uncle, Kui Cui, a bold and chivalrous figure, planned to raise troops to support the Han dynasty after hearing of Gengshi's proclamation and Wang Mang's defeat. Kui Xiao initially advised against it, warning of the dangers of war, but Kui Cui proceeded, gathering thousands to attack Pingxiang. The group then appointed Kui Xiao as general due to his reputation and knowledge of scriptures. Kui Xiao accepted on condition that his advice be heeded.

Following Fang Wang's counsel, Kui Xiao built a temple to honor Han emperors Gaozu, Taizong, and Shizong, where he and his allies performed rituals and swore an oath to assist Liu Zong, invoking divine punishment for betrayal. They issued a proclamation condemning Wang Mang for crimes against heaven, earth, and humanity, including usurpation, tyranny, and exploitation. Kui Xiao then led 100,000 troops, killing Yongzhou shepherd Chen Qing and capturing Anding after executing Wang Xiang. He later seized Longxi, Wudu, Jincheng, and other commanderies.

In the second year of Gengshi, Kui Xiao was summoned to Chang'an and appointed Right General. After his uncle and brother plotted rebellion, Kui Xiao reported them, leading to their deaths, and was made Imperial Censor. When Chimei rebels threatened, Kui Xiao suggested Gengshi delegate power to Liu Liang, but was ignored. He later participated in a plot to kidnap Gengshi, which failed, forcing him to flee to Tianshui, where he declared himself General of Xizhou. He attracted many scholars and officials, gaining fame in the west.

Under Guangwu, Kui Xiao initially cooperated, defeating Chimei and aiding General Feng Yi. Guangwu praised him in letters, offering rewards and urging unity against Gongsun Shu. However, Kui Xiao's generals, Wang Yuan and Wang Jie, advised him to maintain independence, citing the dangers of submitting to Guangwu. Kui Xiao agreed, sending his son as a hostage but secretly planning to dominate the region. Over time, his support waned as Guangwu's forces grew.

In the sixth year of Jianwu, Guangwu ordered Kui Xiao to attack Shu, but he refused, citing difficult terrain. Guangwu then led a campaign against him, but Kui Xiao resisted, leading to defeats. He apologized but remained defiant. Guangwu's attempts to recruit him failed, and Kui Xiao allied with Gongsun Shu, who named him King of Shuoning. Kui Xiao invaded Anding but was repelled. Many of his generals, including Wang Zun, defected to Guangwu.

In the eighth year, Guangwu's forces besieged Kui Xiao, who fell ill and died of anger. His son Kui Chun was made king but later surrendered. Kui Xiao's legacy was marked by his initial righteousness but eventual failure due to isolation and overreliance on natural defenses.

Gongsun Shu, courtesy name Ziyang, from Maoling, rose to power during Wang Mang's decline. He defeated local rebels and declared himself King of Shu, later emperor, citing prophecies and omens. He expanded his territory, gathering troops and resources. Despite Guangwu's letters urging surrender, Gongsun Shu refused, believing in his destiny. His rule was marred by cruelty and poor governance, leading to internal dissent.

In the eleventh year, Guangwu's generals attacked, defeating Gongsun Shu's forces. He was wounded in battle and died, leading to the fall of his regime. Guangwu condemned the subsequent massacre of Gongsun Shu's family and officials. Historians noted that Gongsun Shu's downfall stemmed from his reliance on geography rather than virtue, echoing past failures.

◆Ma Yuan's biography: Ma Yuan was named Wenyuan and was a native of Maoling, Fufeng.
His ancestor Zhao She was a general of Zhao, with the title of Ma Fujun, and his descendants considered him a surname.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, he moved two thousand stones from Handan to Maoling.
Ma Tong, his great-grandfather, was granted the title of Chonghehou due to his meritorious service. His brother Ho Luo was implicated in the rebellion and was killed, so Ma Yuan's grandfather and father were not allowed to be prominent officials.
Ma Yuan's three elder brothers, Ma Kuang, Ma Yu, and Ma Yuan, were all talented. At the time of Wang Mang, they were all worth two thousand shi.
Ma Yuan was orphaned when he was twelve years old. He was young and ambitious, and his brothers thought he was strange.
He once taught him to learn Qi poetry, but Ma Yuan could not stick to the chapters and sentences, so he said goodbye to his brother Ma Kuang and wanted to farm and herd in the border counties.
Ma Kuang said: You have great talent, and you will be able to succeed later in the evening.
Good craftsmen don't tell people to use big wood, but just follow your preferences.
On the first anniversary of Ma Kuang's death, Ma Yuan wore mourning clothes and did not leave the tomb. He respected his widowed sister-in-law and would not enter the cottage until he had good hair and a good hat.
Later, he became the postal supervisor of the county and sent prisoners to Siming Mansion. The prisoners had serious crimes, so Ma Yuan took pity on him and let him go, then fled to the north.
After he was pardoned, he left his livestock behind. Many of his guests joined him, and hundreds of families joined him.
When he traveled to Longhan, he often said to his guests: A man's ambition should be stronger when he is poor and more heroic when he is old.
Because they are engaged in farming and grazing, they have thousands of cattle, horses and sheep, and tens of thousands of grains.
Then he sighed: Any property obtained from farming, animal husbandry and commerce is valuable because it can help others, otherwise you will be nothing more than a miser!
So he distributed all his property to his elder brother and his old friend. Living in sheepskin pants.
At the end of Wang Mang's reign, armies from all directions rose up. Wang Mang recruited heroes from his younger brother, General Wang Linguang. He recruited Ma Yuan and Yuan She from the same county as couriers and recommended them to Wang Mang.
Wang Mang took Yuanshe as the great Yin of Zhenrong, and Ma Yuan as the new great Yin.
When Wang Mang was defeated, Ma Yuan's brother Ma Yuan left the county with Ma Yuan to lead the Zengshan Company, and fled to Liangzhou.
When Shizu ascended the throne, the horsemen went to Luoyang first. When the emperor sent the horsemen back, they were still led by Zengshan Company and died in the official position.
Ma Yuan therefore stayed in Xizhou. Kuai Xiao respected him very much, regarded him as General Suide, and made joint decisions with him.
At this time Gongsun Shu proclaimed himself emperor in Shu, and Wei Xiao sent Ma Yuan to Shu to observe.
Ma Yuan and Gongsun Shu were from the same hometown, and they had always been good friends. He thought that Gongsun Shu would shake hands with him after he left, and he would be as happy as before. But this time Gongsun Shu showed his favor to the imperial guards and invited Ma Yuan to meet him. After paying homage, he took Ma Yuan to the residence, made Ma Yuan cloth clothes for him, gave him a hat, met with all the officials in the ancestral temple, and set up his old friend's seat.
Gongsun Shu held the emperor's Luan flag and Yanqi, and all the guards on the left and right got on the chariot like an emperor, and entered with their bodies bent like chimes. There were many officials in charge of ceremonies and banquets, and they wanted to confer Ma Yuan with the title of general.
The guests were all happy to stay, and Ma Yuan Xiao told everyone: "The outcome of the world is uncertain. Gongsun Shu does not welcome the talented people in the country with courtesy and courtesy, and discusses success or failure together. Instead, he embellishes his appearance and acts like a puppet. How can this son be able to remain a talent in the world for a long time?"
So he resigned. He told Wei Xiao, "Gongsun Shu is just a frog in the well, but he is arrogant. You might as well concentrate on running the East."
In the winter of the fourth year of Jianwu, Kuaixiao sent Ma Yuan to Luoyang with a letter.
When Ma Yuan arrived, the emperor received him in Xuande Hall.
Shizu went out to greet Ma Yuan and said with a smile: "You have been running around between the two emperors. Seeing you now makes people feel ashamed."
Ma Yuan kowtowed and said goodbye. Therefore, it is said: In today's world, not only the monarch chooses his ministers, but the ministers also choose the monarch.
Gongsun Shu and I were from the same county, and we were friendly when we were young. The last time I went to Shu, Gongsun Shu ordered his ministers to stand guard on both sides with halberds, and then summoned me to see him.
I am here from afar, how do you know that I am not an assassin and a traitor, yet you are so careless?
The emperor smiled again and said: You are not an assassin, you are just a lobbyist.
Ma Yuan said: "There are so many people in the world who steal names. Now that I see your majesty, he is magnanimous and magnanimous, just like Gaozu, I know that the emperor is naturally true."
The emperor praised his words very much.
Ma Yuan went from Di to Liqiu and then to the East China Sea.
After returning, he was asked to be on standby for the time being and sent Taizhong doctor to Shezhijie to see Ma Yuanxi back to Longyou.
Wei Xiao lay down with Ma Yuan and asked him about the news he had heard in the east and the gains and losses in the capital.
Ma Yuan said to Wei Xiao: "The last time I came to the court, the emperor met with me more than ten times. Every time I talked with him at the banquet, from night to morning, the emperor's talent and bravery were unmatched by others. He was frank and sincere and had nothing to hide."
He is broad-minded and has great integrity, which is probably the same as Emperor Gao. However, his profound knowledge of Confucian classics, handling of political affairs and writing and rhetoric are unparalleled in previous generations.
Wei Xiao said: What do you think he is compared to Emperor Gao?
Ma Yuan said: Not as good as that.
Emperor Gao could do anything in heaven or on earth; Guangwu loved political affairs and could handle them appropriately, but he did not like drinking.
Wei Xiao was unhappy and said, "As you put it, Guangwu is better than Gaozu?"
However, he trusted Ma Yuan very much, so he sent his eldest son Kai Xun to the capital as a hostage.
Therefore, Ma Yuan and his family returned to Luoyang with Wei Xun.
I haven't received a new appointment for several months.
Ma Yuan's three auxiliary lands were vast and fertile, and he brought many guests. So he wrote a letter requesting to farm in Shanglin Garden.
Guangwu agreed. When Wei Xiao used Wang Yuan's plan, he became even more suspicious. Ma Yuan wrote several times to reprimand Wei Xiao. Wei Xiao hated Ma Yuan for betraying him. After gaining trust, his hatred increased, and later he sent troops to resist the Han.
Ma Yuan said to Guangwu Shangshu: I wanted to return to the Holy Dynasty and serve His Majesty. I didn't have a word of recommendation from the three ministers, nor did anyone around me speak first for me.
If I don't say it myself, how can your Majesty hear it?
Being in the front does not allow people to differentiate between high and low, and being in the back does not allow people to differentiate between important and important. You can't cause trouble to others. This is something I feel ashamed of.
Therefore, I dare to violate the taboo of sin and risk my life to express my sincerity.
Wei Xiao and I were originally friends.
At the beginning, Kaixiao sent his ministers to Luoyang and said to me: I originally wanted to serve as a Han, so please go and have a look first. If you think it is okay, I will concentrate on serving the Han.
When I get back, I will repay Kui Xiao with my whole heart. I want to sincerely induce him to do good things, and I dare not instigate him to think that he is doing something unjust.
But Kui Xiao harbored a traitorous intention. I secretly hate His Majesty, and attribute this resentment to me.
If I don't say it, there will be no way for my opinion to be expressed.
I would like to come to you in person and state the strategy to eliminate Weihuo. I would like to be able to say everything I want to say and explain my humble opinion, and then return to my hometown to farm and die without regrets.
The emperor then summoned Ma Yuan to discuss the matter, and Ma Yuan made suggestions.
Therefore, Ma Yuan was sent to lead five thousand assault cavalry, and went back and forth to persuade Wei Xiao's generals Gao Jun, Ren Yu's subordinates, and the heroes of the Qiang to analyze the situation and explain the blessings and disadvantages for them, so as to alienate Wei Xiao's party members.
Ma Yuan also wrote to Wei Xiao's general Yang Guang, asking Yang Guang to persuade Wei Xiao. Said: Chunqing is fine.
We parted ways in southern Hebei Province, but there has been no communication. Ma Yuan returned to Chang'an by chance, so he stayed in Shanglin.
I see that the world has been settled, and the people are united, but Kuai Xiao has refused to betray, and has been criticized by the world.
I was often afraid that the country would hate him and wanted to kill him and quarter him, so I wrote to him. Love leads to compassion.
I heard that Wei Xiao was blamed on me, and I accepted Wang Yuan's theory of treachery. I thought that the west of Hangu Pass was safe. Looking at the current situation, what exactly is going on?
Ma Yuan once went to Hanoi to visit Bo Chun and saw Qinuji returning from the west. He said that Bo Chun's younger brother Zhongshu saw Ji and wanted to ask Bo Chun if there was any accident, but he could not speak and sobbed morning and night, silently in the dust.
He also said that the sad situation of his family was indescribable.
Resentment and hatred can be stabbed but not destroyed. Ma Yuan cried unknowingly after hearing this.
Ma Yuansu knew Kui Xiao's filial piety, and even Zeng Shen and Min Zijian would not surpass him.
How can a person who is filial to his parents not be kind to his son?
How can one have the heart to let his son wear the shackles, while the father is still acting arrogantly, like Le Yang, who has the heart to eat soup made from his son's flesh?
Throughout his life, Wei Xiao said that the reason why he supported the army was just to preserve the country of his parents and keep the tombs of his ancestors intact, and he also said that he only treated the scholar-bureaucrats favorably.
But now those who want to preserve it will be destroyed, those who want to be whole will also be destroyed, and those who want to be treated favorably will be treated poorly.
Wei Xiao once humiliated Gongsun Shu and refused to accept Gongsun Shu's grant. Now he is collaborating with Gongsun Shu and still wants to join him. Don't you feel embarrassed?
If Gongsun Shu asked Wei Xiao to send his son to Luoyang as a hostage, where would he get his son?
In the past, Gongsun Shu wanted to make you king, but you refused to accept it. Now that you are old, do you still want to lower your head and eat with the younger generations, side by side in the court of the Yu family?
Why should a man be restricted to swimming when he drowns?
Now that the country has deep intentions for you, you should ask Niu Ruqing and the elders to work together to convince Wei Xiao. If the plan is not accepted, you can lead him away.
Looking at the map, I saw that there are 106 counties and states in the world. How can I use two mere states to resist the 104 states in the world?
When you are doing things, you have the righteousness of a monarch and a minister on the outside, and the way of a friend on the inside.
For rulers and ministers, they should face admonishment and disputes; for friends, they should discuss and discuss matters.
How could he know that he would not succeed, yet be weak and dare not speak, and follow him with his hands crossed to torture his parents, brothers and children?
If the current plan is successful, the remuneration will still be generous; it would be a pity to miss this opportunity.
Qilai Junshu is a believer in the world, and the court respects him. He often speaks for Xizhou and feels reluctant to leave.
I guess the imperial court, in particular, wants to establish its trust in this matter so that it will not break its promise.
Ma Yuan will not stay long. I hope you will reply soon.
Yang Guang didn't even reply.
In the eighth year, the emperor personally marched westward from Kaixiao and arrived at Qixian County. All the generals believed that the king's division was important and should not go deep into the dangers, so they were hesitant about the plan.
The emperor was overjoyed when he called for horse assistance, which arrived at night. He introduced the emperor and asked for his decision-making with everyone's opinions.
Ma Yuan therefore said that General Kaixiao was on the verge of collapse and that he would be defeated if he advanced with troops.
They gathered rice together in front of the emperor to make a model of the valley, drew out the situation, pointed out which mountain road the army should enter and exit from, and analyzed the twists and turns to make it clear.
The emperor said: The enemy is already in my eyes.
The next morning, they marched to the first place and were defeated by the army.
In the ninth year, he worshiped Ma Yuan as Taizhong doctor and helped the generals who came to pacify Liangzhou.
Since the last years of Wang Mang, the Western Qiang invaded the border and moved to the Senei. Most of the counties under Jincheng were occupied by the Qiang.
Lai She reported that the land in Longxi that had been invaded could not be settled without Ma Yuan.
In the summer of the eleventh year, Xi Shu worshiped Ma Yuan as the governor of Longxi.
Ma Yuan then sent out 3,000 infantry and cavalry, defeated the Xianling Qiang in Lintao, beheaded hundreds of people, and captured more than 10,000 horses, cattle and sheep.
More than 8,000 Qiang defenders surrendered to Ma Yuan. Tens of thousands of people from all ethnic groups gathered to attack and plunder, refusing to defend the pass.
Ma Yuan and General Yangwu Ma Cheng launched an attack.
The Qiang then moved his wife's baggage and blocked it in Yunwu Valley. Ma Yuan secretly took a small road and suddenly attacked his camp.
The Qiang people were frightened and moved further to Tangyi Valley, where Ma Yuan pursued them again.
The Qiang led their elite troops to the northern mountains of Tunxi, and sent horses to support Chen's army. They sent hundreds of horsemen to go behind the Qiang soldiers, set fires at night, and beat drums to shout. The Qiang soldiers were routed and more than a thousand people were beheaded.
Ma Yuan had few troops, so he could not pursue them. He collected his grain and livestock products and returned.

At this time, the court officials thought that Jincheng was in the west of Poqiang, and the road was far away and there were many bandits, so they decided to abandon it.
Ma Yuan wrote a letter saying that most of the cities to the west of Poqiang are intact and strong and easy to defend; their fields are fertile and have good irrigation.
If the Qiang people are allowed to stay in Huangzhong, the harm will continue, so we cannot give up.
The emperor agreed, so he ordered the prefect of Wuwei to order all the residents of Jincheng in Wuwei to return to Jincheng.

Undo Ma Chengjun.

Ma Yuan focused on spreading favor and trust, being lenient to his subordinates, and appointing officials according to their positions, while he himself only focused on major issues.
Guests and old friends gradually gathered under his door.
When subordinate officials sometimes talked about external affairs, Ma Yuan always said: "This is the task of the chief historians and secretaries, so you don't need to tell me."
Feeling pity for me, I am able to enjoy my leisure time.
If the big surname bullies the small people and the cunning Qiang people disobey, it is the governor's business.

Daochang Di came to the door and asked to close the city gate and send troops to attack. At this time, Ma Yuan was drinking with the guests and laughed and said: How dare the Shao Qiang come to attack me again.
Tell Taoist Master Di to go back and guard the house. Those who are timid and afraid of death can hide under the bed.
Later, the turmoil calmed down, and everyone in the county was convinced of Ma Yuan's courage.
He served in Longxi for six years and was called back to worship him as Huben Zhonglang.
At first, when Ma Yuan was in Longxi, he wrote a letter saying that five baht coins should be minted as in the past.
The imperial court transferred the matter to the offices set up by Taiwei, Situ and Sikong. The three palaces reported that it was unacceptable, so the matter was shelved. When Ma Yuan returned to the capital, he obtained the memorials from the previous three palaces from the government, debated more than ten points, explained them with the ultimatum, and stated the reasons in a table.
The emperor agreed, and the world relied on his convenience.
Ma Yuan returned to the capital and was summoned many times.
Ma Yuan paid attention to grooming his beard and hair, and his features were picturesque. He is good at answering questions and is especially good at telling stories about past lives.
Every time I talk about the elders from the three auxiliaries to the young people in the countryside, it is very touching.
When the crown prince and the attendants of the kings heard this, they all listened so much that they forgot to get tired.
He is also good at using military strategies. The emperor once said: "Fu Bo discusses military affairs, which agrees with me." Every time he came up with a suggestion, there was no one that was not adopted.

Later, his disciples Li Guang and others declared that Wei Si would become immortal and deceive the people.

So we moved forward along the sea road and followed the mountains for more than a thousand miles.
In the spring of the 18th year, the army went to Liubo, fought with the bandits, and defeated the bandit army. Thousands of people were beheaded, and more than 10,000 people were surrendered.
Ma Yuan pursued Zheng Bian and others to the Forbidden River and defeated the bandits several times. The thieves dispersed and fled.
In the first month of the second year, Zheng Side and Zheng Er were beheaded, and their heads were brought to Luoyang.
Ma Yuan was granted the title of Marquis of Xinxi, with a settlement of 3,000 households.
Ma Yuan killed the ox and poured wine to comfort the soldiers.
He calmly said to the officials: My younger brother Shaoyou often laments my generosity and ambition, saying that as long as a scholar has food and clothing, can ride a short-hub cart in the swamp, drive a slow-moving horse, be the governor of the county, guard the graves of his ancestors, and be praised by the villagers as a good man, that will be all.

When I was between Langbo and Xili, before the thieves were extinguished, there was water below and fog above, fumigated by poisonous gas. The officials all fell to the ground and said long live.
Ma Yuanlou had more than 2,000 large and small ships and more than 20,000 soldiers. He attacked the Jiuzhen thieves and conquered the remaining party Duyang and others. From futile to dominant, they captured more than 5,000 people and Lingnan was all pacified.
Ma Yuan reported that there were 32,000 households in the west county, and the boundary was more than a thousand miles away from the county. He requested that the county be divided into two counties: Fengxi and Wanghai. The emperor agreed.
Wherever Ma Yuan went, he managed cities and towns for counties and dug canals for irrigation to benefit the people.
He also made it clear that the Yue laws were not exactly the same as the Han laws, and stated a dozen things that were different from the Han laws, and explained the old system to the Yue people to restrain them. From then on, Luo Yue abided by General Ma's old system.
In the autumn of the 20th year, after reorganizing the army and returning to the capital, four to five out of ten military officials died of miasma and epidemics. They were rewarded with a horse reinforcement chariot, and their status was second only to Jiu Qing when they came to court.
Ma Yuan loved horseback riding and was good at identifying famous horses. He got the Luo Yue bronze drum in Jiaochangzhi, and used it to cast a model of the horse, which he presented to the emperor upon his return.

I am now strictly based on the Yi family's horse head, the Zhongbo family's mouth, the Xie family's lips and the mane, and the Ding family's body, and gathered the bones of these families on one model to serve as a standard.
The horse is three feet five inches high and four feet five inches wide. The emperor ordered this horse model to be given to His Highness Xuande as a standard model for famous horses.
At first, when Ma Yuan's army came back and was about to arrive, many old friends welcomed him to express their condolences. Meng Ji, a native of Pingling, who was famous for his strategizing, was here to congratulate Ma Yuan.
Ma Yuan said to him: I hope you have kind words to encourage me, but are you like everyone else?

How can you help me sir?

Ma Yuan said: Now the Xiongnu and Wuhuan are still intruding in the north. I would like to ask for a crusade. The man should die in the wilderness and come back to be buried with his body wrapped in horse leather. How can he sleep in bed and watch over his wife and children?
Meng Ji said: A true martyr should be like this.
More than a month after returning, the Xiongnu and Wuhuan invaded Fufeng. Ma Yuan used his three assistants to invade Sao. Yuanling was in danger. He requested to send troops and was allowed.
After arriving in Beijing in September, he sent troops to station in Xiangguo in December.
When the officials were ordered to bid farewell, Ma Yuan said to Liang Song and Dou Gu, Huangmenmen: When a mortal becomes a noble, he must also be able to become poor and lowly. As expected, Liang Song later suffered a disaster because of his excessive wealth, and Dou Gu was almost unavoidable.
In the autumn of the next year, Ma Yuan led three thousand horses out of Gaoliu and marched to Yanmen, Daijun, Shanggu and other frontier fortresses.
When Wuhuan's scouting horse saw the Han army arriving, he fled. Ma Yuan returned with nothing to gain.
Ma Yuan was ill. Liang Song came to greet him and met him under the bed, but Ma Yuan did not respond.
After Liang Song left, his sons asked, "Liang Song is the emperor's son-in-law. He is a high-ranking official in the court. Everyone below is afraid of him. Why don't you respond to him?"
Ma Yuan said: "I am a friend of Mr. Liang's father. Although he is expensive, how can I lose my seniority?"
Song therefore hated Ma Yuan.

Ma Yuan was sixty-two years old at this time. The emperor felt pity for his old age and disagreed.
Ma Yuan asked himself: "I can still put on my armor and mount my horse." The emperor ordered him to try it.
Ma Yuan looked left and right while leaning on the saddle to show that he was available.
The emperor smiled and said: This old man is so healthy!

Ma Yuan said goodbye to those who were seeing him off at night, and told his friend Du Xu, who was paying homage to him, saying: "I have been greatly favored. Fu Bo used his troops like Jia Hu in the Western Regions. He stopped moving forward after reaching a certain point, so he lost.

Du Jiliang, named Bao, was born in Jingzhao and was a Yueqi Sima at that time.

The imperial edict removed Du Jiliang from his official position.
Long Bogao Mingshu, who was also from Jingzhao, was the county magistrate of Shandu, so he was promoted to the prefect of Lingling.

Ma Yuan was favored by the emperor at that time, so no one dared to report to the court.

Trembling in the palace.

At first, brother Ma Yuan's son-in-law was named Wang Pan Zishi, and he was the son of Wang Mang's brother Ahou Wangren.
Wang Mang was defeated, and Wang Panzishi owned property and lived in his former residence. He was a man of integrity and caring and liked to give alms. He was famous in the Jianghuai River. Later, he became friendly with Wei Wei Yinxing, Da Sikong Zhufu and Qi Wangzhang.
Ma Yuan said to his sister's son Cao Xun: "The Wang family is now a collapsed family. Zi Shi should live in seclusion and keep to himself. summary:
Ma Yuan, styled Wenyuan, was a native of Maoling, Fufeng. His ancestor Zhao She was a general of Zhao, and his descendants adopted the surname Ma. During Emperor Wu's reign, the family moved from Handan to Maoling. Ma Yuan's great-grandfather Ma Tong was granted the title of Chonghehou, but his brother was implicated in a rebellion and killed, preventing Ma Yuan's grandfather and father from holding prominent positions. Ma Yuan's three elder brothers were all talented and served as officials worth two thousand shi under Wang Mang. Orphaned at twelve, Ma Yuan was ambitious and unconventional. He left his studies to farm and herd in border counties, eventually amassing great wealth, which he distributed to his brother and friends, living frugally.

During the end of Wang Mang's reign, Ma Yuan served as a county official and later fled to the north after releasing a prisoner. He was pardoned and became a successful farmer and herder. He joined Wei Xiao, who respected him and made him General Suide. Ma Yuan was sent to observe Gongsun Shu in Shu but was unimpressed by his pompous behavior, calling him a "frog in a well." He then went to Luoyang to meet Emperor Guangwu, who received him warmly. Ma Yuan praised the emperor's magnanimity and wisdom, comparing him favorably to Gaozu. He returned to Wei Xiao but eventually sided with Guangwu, writing letters to persuade Wei Xiao's generals to defect. Ma Yuan's military strategies were highly valued, and he led campaigns against the Qiang and other rebels, achieving significant victories.

Ma Yuan served as Governor of Longxi, where he focused on spreading favor and trust, appointing capable officials, and encouraging agriculture and animal husbandry. He successfully pacified the region and proposed minting five-baht coins, which was implemented. He later led campaigns against the Wuxi barbarians in Wuling, but died of illness at age 62. After his death, he was falsely accused of bringing back treasures from the south, leading to the emperor's anger and the revocation of his marquis title. His family was disgraced until a letter from Zhu Bo, a former associate, helped clear his name. Ma Yuan's daughter later became empress, and he was posthumously honored as Marquis Zhongcheng. His sons included Ma Liao, Ma Fang, Ma Guang, and Ma Keqing, the latter dying young. The historian notes Ma Yuan's rise to fame and his tragic fall due to slander, reflecting on the perils of fame and the importance of self-reflection.

Soon, the Qiang rebels in Longxi and Wuhuan invaded and plundered Shangjun, just as Ma Rong said.
After three official transfers, he was the prefect of Nanjun during the reign of Emperor Huan.
First, something happened to Ma Rong that violated the will of the general Liang Ji. Liang Ji hinted that the officials would accuse Ma Rong of corruption in the county, dismissed him from office, shaved off his hair, and moved to Shuofang.
If you commit suicide but do not die, you will be exempted from guilt. I paid homage to Yilang again and wrote in Dongguan. Resigned due to illness.
Ma Rong was a man of great talent and profound knowledge, and was a general expert in the world. Professors tutor students, often by the thousands.
Lu Zhi of Zhuojun and Zheng Xuan of Beihai were both his students.
He knows how to play the drums and harp, and is good at playing the flute. Be free and willful and not be bound by the small details of Confucianism. The house is furnished with clothes, advocating luxury, and often sits in a high hall with a red gauze hanging. There are students in front of the teacher and female musicians in the back. The disciples taught the teachings one by one, and few entered the room.
I once wanted to annotate "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu". When I saw the annotations by Jia Kui and Zheng Zhong, I said: Jia Jun is good but not knowledgeable, and Zheng Jun is good but not good.
You are knowledgeable and knowledgeable, I have nothing more to say. He only wrote "The Theory of Similarities and Differences in Three Biographies".
Annotated "The Classic of Filial Piety", "The Analects of Confucius", "Poetry", "Yi", "Three Rites", "Shangshu", "Biography of Lienu", "Laozi", "Huainanzi", "Li Sao", and wrote a total of twenty-one poems, odes, stele, memorials, books, notes, tables, memorials, seven-character poems, zither songs, countermeasures and testaments.
At first, Ma Rong was punished by Deng, and he did not dare to offend the powerful family again. He drafted a memorial for Liang Ji to frame Li Gu, and wrote the general "Ode to the West". Therefore, he is quite ridiculed by ordinary honest people.
He died at home in the 88th year of Yanxi's reign.
The will was buried poorly.
The grandson of the clan, Ma Ri Shi Dan, was promoted to Taifu when he was presented to the emperor.
The historian commented: Ma Rong resigned from Deng's order and wandered between Long and Han, perhaps because he was demanding that his words and deeds should be consistent.
However, he soon became ashamed of the formal details of the country folk and cherished his rich body. Finally, he was ridiculed for his extravagant and lewd pleasures. There are too few people who are intellectually correct!
When the work is hard, the feeling of cherishing and preserving becomes thinner. Life is precious, so the thoughts of safety and survival are more numerous.
Those who are not afraid of climbing high are those who are being punished because they have no regard for life or death.
If you don't sit under the eaves for fear of the tiles falling down and hitting you, you are the son of a rich man!
Examine the main reasons and seek peace of mind.
We have different views on things, and we can't help but laugh at each other.
summary:
Ma Rong, courtesy name Ji Chang, was born in Maoling, Fufeng, as the son of Ma Yan. He was handsome, talented, and eloquent. He studied under the recluse Zhixun in Nanshan, mastering the classics, and Zhixun married his daughter to him. In the second year of Yongchu, General Deng Zhi summoned him, but Ma Rong refused and lived as a guest in Liangzhou. During a Qiang rebellion, famine struck, and Ma Rong, facing hardship, regretted his refusal, citing the value of life from Laozi and Zhuangzi, and accepted Deng Zhi's call. In the fourth year, he became a calligrapher at Dongguan Dian School, collecting secret books.

During Empress Dowager Deng's regency, Confucian scholars advocated abolishing martial arts, leading to widespread banditry. Ma Rong disapproved, arguing that civil and military affairs were both essential. In the second year of Yuanchu, he wrote "Guangcheng Ode" to satirize this policy, suggesting that the emperor should engage in hunting and martial training to promote harmony. This offended Deng, and he was confined to Dongguan for ten years without promotion. After his nephew's death, he resigned and returned home, angering the Empress Dowager, who banned him from office. After her death, Emperor An recalled him, and he served as chief of the stables for the King of Hejian. He wrote "Ode to the Eastern Tour" for the emperor's pilgrimage to Mount Tai, earning a promotion to doctor.

Later, as governor of Wudu during a Xiqiang rebellion, Ma Rong proposed a swift military campaign to defeat the rebels, but his advice was ignored. He accurately predicted the subsequent invasions. Under Emperor Huan, he became prefect of Nanjun but was framed by General Liang Ji, exiled to Shuofang, and later pardoned. He returned to writing at Dongguan before retiring due to illness.

Ma Rong was a renowned scholar with thousands of students, including Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan. He was skilled in music, lived luxuriously, and taught with a red gauze curtain, separating male and female students. He annotated many classics, including the "Classic of Filial Piety," "Analects," and "Book of Songs." However, he was criticized for drafting a memorial for Liang Ji to frame Li Gu. He died at home at age 88, with a simple burial. The historian noted his initial integrity but later indulgence in luxury, reflecting the tension between valuing life and maintaining moral principles.
