translation:
The founder of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Emperor Guangwu Liu Xiu, whose courtesy name was Uncle Wen, was born in Caiyang, Nanyang. He was the ninth-generation grandson of Liu Bang, the great ancestor of the Han Dynasty. It comes from Liu Fa, the king of Shading who was born under Emperor Jing.
Liu gave birth to Liu Mai, the Marquis of Chung Ling Festival, Liu Mai gave birth to Liu Wai, the governor of Yulin, Liu Hui, the captain of Julu, was born to Liu Wai, Liu Qin was born to Liu Qin, the Nandun order, and Liu Qin was born to Guangwu.
Guangwu lost his father at the age of nine and was raised by his uncle Liu Liang.
He is seven feet three inches tall, has thick eyebrows, a wide mouth, a protruding nose, and a full forehead.
He is industrious by nature and enjoys farming. His elder brother Bo Sheng was fond of chivalry and raising people. He often ridiculed Guang Wu for only working in the fields and compared him with Liu Bang's second brother Liu Zhong.
It was not until the reign of Wang Mang and Tianfeng that Guangwu came to Chang'an to study "Shang Shu" as a disciple and roughly understand the gist of the book.
In Wang Mang's last years, there were successive locust plagues in the country, and bandits and bandits were raging.
In the third year of Emperor Di Huang's reign, there was a serious famine in Nanyang, and most of the family's guests went out to rob and steal.
In order to avoid the government, Guangwu fled to Xinye County and transported the harvested grain to Wancheng to sell.
Li Tong and others from Wan used prophecies and talismans to tell Guangwu: The Liu family has risen again, and the Li family will be the assistant. Guangwu didn't dare to act rashly at first, but then he thought that his brother Bo Sheng would do great things by making friends with diners. Moreover, Wang Mang's regime showed signs of decline and destruction, and the world was in turmoil, so he planned with the Li family and decided to raise an army, so he began to purchase various weapons.
In October, he and Li Tong's cousin Li Yi and others raised troops in Wancheng. He was 28 years old at the time.
In November, the comet appeared in Zhangsu in the south.
Guangwu then led his retainers back to Chongling.
At this time, Bo Sheng had gathered the people to raise troops.
At first, the children of each family were very frightened. They ran and hid, saying: "Bosheng wants to kill us!"
When they saw Guangwu in crimson robes and crowns, they were all surprised and said: "Uncle Wen, who is cautious and kind, has also raised an army!"
Only then did everyone settle down. Bo Sheng then recruited troops from Xinshi and Pinglin, and together with his leaders Wang Feng and Chen Mu, went west to attack Changju.
Guangwu first rode the bull, and then he was able to ride the horse after killing Xin Yewei.
He entered Tu Tangzi Township and killed the Huyang county captain.
The wealth obtained by the army was unevenly distributed, and everyone was angry. The soldiers wanted to counterattack the Liu family.
Guangwu then collected all the property from his clan and gave it all to the soldiers. Only then did everyone feel satisfied.
He then attacked and captured Jiyang, and fought with Wang Mang's former commander Zhen Fu and Zhengliangqiu in Xiaochang'an. As a result, the Han army was defeated and had to retreat to Jiyang.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of Gengshi, the Han army fought against Zhenfu and Liangqiuci in the west of Xianshui River. They defeated the enemy and killed Zhenfu and Liangqiuci.
Bo Sheng defeated Wang Mang's general Yan You and Zhizong's general Chen Mao in Huoyang, and then besieged Wancheng.
On the first day of February, Liu Xuan was proclaimed emperor. Liu Xuan appointed Bo Sheng as the Great Situ and Guang Wu as the Taichang Commander.
In March, Guangwu and other generals attacked Kunyang, Dingling and Lu, and captured them all.
A lot of cattle, horses and property were seized, as well as hundreds of thousands of grains, which were transferred to the troops under Wancheng.
When Wang Mang learned that Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci had been killed and that the Han Emperor had been established, he was very frightened, so he sent Grand Situ Wang Xun and Grand Sikong Wang Yi to lead millions of troops, including 420,000 armored soldiers. In May, he arrived at Yingchuan and joined forces with Yan You and Chen Mao.
At first, Guangwu complained to Yan You about the rent arrears of Chonglinghou's tenants. Yan You treated Guangwu differently when he saw him.
Now, Yan You listened to the people who surrendered to him in the city and said that Guangwu did not collect property, but only trained soldiers to make plans.
Yan You smiled and said: Is he the man with the bushy eyebrows?
Why would he do this!
At the beginning, Wang Mang recruited hundreds of people from sixty-three families in the world who knew the art of war and appointed them as military officers. He selected and trained guards, recruited warriors, and carried banners and baggage for thousands of miles.
At that time, there was a giant named Big Mac, who was ten feet tall and ten inches thick at the waist. He was appointed as a lieutenant in the military base. He drove wild beasts such as tigers, leopards, rhinoceros, and elephants to boost the military's power.
The grand occasion of leaving the army was unprecedented since the Qin and Han Dynasties.
Guangwu led thousands of troops to intercept Wang Mang's army at Yangguan.
When the generals saw that Wang Xun and Wang Yi's troops were strong, they turned around and ran away, rushing back to Kunyang. They were all afraid and worried about their wives and children, so they wanted to disperse and return to their respective cities.
Guangwu suggested: Now we have few troops and food, but the foreign invaders are strong. If we work together to resist, we may be able to achieve success; if we are scattered, we will definitely not be able to survive.
Moreover, Wancheng has not been captured, and the troops there cannot rescue us. Once Kunyang is captured, all our ministries will be wiped out within one day.
Now, instead of working together to gain fame, do we want to keep our wives, children, and property? The generals said angrily: "Why did General Liu say such a thing!" Guangwu stood up with a smile.
At this time, the enemy cavalry who happened to be watching came back and said that a large number of enemies were coming to the north of the city. The army and horses were lined up for hundreds of miles, and the tail of the team could not be seen.
The generals quickly said to each other: It is better to ask General Liu for advice on how to deal with it. Guangwu also planned success or failure strategies for everyone.
The generals were worried and embarrassed, and they all said: Just do it like this!
At this time, there were only eight or nine thousand people in the city, so Guangwu asked Chengguo Duke Wang Feng and Tingwei General Wang Chang to guard the city. He, Hussar General Zong Yan, Wuwei General Li Yi and other thirteen people rode out of the south gate of the city at night to organize troops outside.
By this time, nearly 100,000 Wang Mang's troops had arrived at the city gates, and Guangwu could hardly get out of the city.
When they arrived at Lin and Dingling, they mobilized all the troops from all the barracks, but the generals were greedy for money and wanted to divide their troops and stay behind.
Guangwu said: Now if we defeat the enemy, the treasure will be ten thousand times greater, and we will achieve great success; if we are defeated by the enemy, we will not be able to save our heads, so how can we have any wealth?
Everyone followed Guangwu's advice. Yan You advised Wang Yi, saying: Kunyang City is small but strong, and Liu Xuan, who has claimed to be the emperor, is in Wancheng. If we quickly send a large army to attack, they will definitely escape. If Wancheng is defeated, Kunyang will naturally surrender. Wang Yi said: In the past, as General Huya, I besieged Zhai Yi and was blamed for not capturing him alive.
Now with an army of millions, how can we justify it if we encounter a city and cannot take it? So they surrounded Kunyang dozens of times, set up hundreds of camps, and erected a cloud chariot more than ten feet high. Looking down at the city, flags were everywhere, dust filled the sky, and the sound of golden drums could be heard for hundreds of miles.
Some troops dug tunnels, and some troops used wooden dolls and carts to attack the city.
Bows and crossbows fired wildly, arrows rained down like rain, and the people in the city had to carry door panels on their backs to draw water.
Wang Feng and others asked to surrender, but were not allowed.
Wang Xun Wang Yi thought that his success was instantaneous, and he was in a leisurely and contented mood. Meteors fell into the barracks at night, and clouds appeared during the day. The camp fell like a collapsed mountain, and it dispersed less than a foot away from the ground. All the officers and soldiers lay prone on the ground.
On the first day of June, Guangwu advanced with the army. He led more than a thousand infantry and cavalry and set up a formation four or five miles in front of Wang Mang's army. Wang Xun and Wang Yi also sent thousands of soldiers to fight.
Guangwu rushed to kill the enemy troops and killed dozens of them.
All the subordinates said happily: "General Liu has been afraid of weak enemies all his life, but today he is unstoppable when he encounters strong enemies. It is very strange, and he is at the front again."
Let us also assist the general! Guangwu rushed towards the enemy. Wang Yi and Wang Xun's troops retreated. Taking advantage of the victory, his troops attacked and killed hundreds or thousands of the enemy.
After repeated victories, the team moved forward.
At this time, Bo Sheng had captured Wancheng for three days, but Guangwu didn't know it yet, so he sent someone pretending to be an envoy from the troops under Wancheng, and brought a letter to report to the city, saying that reinforcements from Wancheng had arrived, but he pretended to accidentally lose the letter.
Wang Xun and Wang Yi's letters made me unhappy.
The Han army won several victories and became more courageous. One man was worth a hundred.
Guangwu led another 3,000 death squads and charged at the enemy's backbone from the water west of the city. Wang Xun and Wang Yi's military formations were in chaos. Guangwu used his vigor to destroy the enemy formation and killed Wang Xun.
Kunyang City also beat drums and shouted and rushed out. The internal and external attacks were combined, the sound shook the heaven and the earth. The reckless army was defeated. The fleeing soldiers trampled each other, and the casualties were scattered for more than a hundred miles.
There happened to be a strong thunder and strong wind in the sky, and the roof tiles were blown away. Heavy rain poured down and the water in the Sichuan River surged. Tigers and leopards trembled with fear. Soldiers rushed to cross the water to escape. Tens of thousands drowned and the river stopped flowing. Wang Yi, Yan You, and Chen Mao rode lightly on horseback and escaped across the river on the dead men. They were so powerful that the Mang army's food, grass, equipment, tanks, armor, and treasures were countless. They couldn't move them all for several months, and some had to be burned.
Guangwu took advantage of the situation and captured Yingyang County.
At this time, Liu Boxheng was killed by Liu Xuan, the Gengshi Emperor. Guangwu immediately rushed from his father city to Wancheng to apologize.
The officials of the Situ Mansion all came to express their condolences to Guangwu. Guangwu was not in a position to discuss anything with them in private, but he only blamed himself deeply.
He never boasted about his achievements in the Battle of Kunyang, nor did he dare to mourn for Bo Sheng. He ate, talked and laughed as naturally as usual.
Emperor Gengshi felt guilty about this, so he worshiped Guangwu as the general of Polu and named him Marquis of Wuxin.
On the third day of September, the three auxiliary heroes of Chang'an worked together to kill Wang Mang and sent his head to Wancheng.
Emperor Gengshi was about to go north to make his capital Luoyang, so he asked Guangwu to act as Sili Xiaowei and asked him to go to Luoyang first to repair the palace and government offices.
Guangwu then set up subordinate officials to draft official documents to conduct historical inspections and illegal affairs, and everything was handled according to the old system of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the three auxiliary officials went east to welcome Emperor Gengshi. When they saw the generals passing by, they all wore civilian headscarves, women's clothes, large tie-ups and embroidered half-armor, and everyone laughed at them.
Some even run away in fear of disaster because of the ominous things they are convinced of. When they saw Guangwu's staff, they were all overjoyed.
Some old officials shed tears and said: "I didn't expect to see the majesty and grace of my Han officials again today!" From then on, all knowledgeable people turned to Guangwu.
When Gengshi arrived in Luoyang, he appointed Guangwu as General Polu to act as Grand Sima.
In October, Guangwu took the talisman and crossed the Yellow River to the north to calm the officials and people of the prefecture and county.
When arriving at a county, he would meet with the county governor, chief officials, three elders, officials, and officials, down to the assistant historian, to inspect promotion matters, just like a state herdsman inspecting the county to handle affairs.
He vindicated wrongful cases, released prisoners, got rid of Wang Mang's harsh rule, and restored the official title of the Han Dynasty. The officials and the people were happy, and they rushed to greet them with cattle and wine.
When they arrived at Handan, Liu Lin, the son of the late King Mu of Zhao, offered advice to Guangwu: The Red Eyebrow Army is now in the east of the river. As long as the Yellow River is opened to flood them, the Red Eyebrow Army of millions will become fish and shrimps in an instant. Guangwu didn't answer and left Handan for Zhending.
Zhao Lin asked Wang Lang, who was engaged in divination, to pretend to be Liu Ziyu, the son of the emperor. In December, he proclaimed Wang Lang the emperor, made Handan his capital, and sent envoys to persuade the counties to surrender.
In the first month of the second year of Gengshi, Guangwu went north to inspect Jidi because of Wang Lang's new rise.
Wang Lang issued a proclamation, promising to kill those who captured Guangwu and grant him the title of 100,000 households. Liu Jie, the son of the late King Liu Jia of Guangyang, raised an army in Jizhong to support the king. The city of Jicheng was disrupted and the people were frightened. It was also said that an envoy from Handan had just arrived, and officials with a weight of less than two thousand stones went out to welcome him.
So Guangwu hurriedly drove south, not daring to go into the city in the morning or at night. He only stopped by the roadside to eat and sleep.
When they arrived at Raoyang, the officers and soldiers had nothing to eat.
Guangwu claimed to be an envoy from Handan and went to the post station to rest.
The person in charge of the post station had just brought the food, and Guangwu's people were so hungry that they scrambled for food.
The clerk at the inn suspected that Guangwu was a fake, so he beat the drum dozens of times and lied about the arrival of General Handan, which made the officials' faces change with fear.
Guangwu got into the car and wanted to run away, but then he was afraid that he would not be able to escape, so he calmly sat down and said, "Please come in, General Handan!" After waiting for a long time, I drove away.
The people at the inn told the gatekeeper from a distance not to let him in.
The official guarding the gate said: How can we predict the overall situation of the world? How dare you trap a noble person in the city?
Guangwu then left the city through the south gate. We traveled day and night, covered in frost and snow, and it was so cold that our faces were cracked by the frost.
When we arrived at the Hutuo River, there were no boats, and the river was frozen. Cars were able to pass, but almost before the last few cars had completely passed, the ice collapsed.
When they arrived at the west of Xiabo City, they were hesitant and confused, not knowing where to go. An old man in white clothes on the roadside pointed them out and said: Work hard, the people of Xindu County are still guarding the Chang'an government, which is still eighty miles away from here. Guangwu rushed over immediately, and the prefect Ren Guang opened the door to greet him.
Guangwu then recruited soldiers and horses from surrounding counties, and got a total of 4,000 people. He first attacked Tangyang and Jin counties, and both places surrendered to Guangwu.
Wang Mang and Chengzu Zhengpitong also led the entire county to surrender.
Liu Zhi, a native of Changcheng, and Geng Chun, a native of Song Dynasty, led their descendants to occupy the county town and dedicated it to Guangwu. Then they went north to capture Quyang. Their tribesmen gradually gathered, and tens of thousands of people were willing to rely on Guangwu.
Guangwu then attacked Zhongshan State to the north and occupied Lunu County. Wherever he went, he recruited "benming soldiers" and sent messages to the border ministries, asking them to attack Handan together. All counties and counties responded one after another.
Going south, he conquered Xinshi, Zhending, Yuanshi, and Fangzi, and then entered the realm of Zhao.
At that time, Wang Lang's general Li Yu was stationed in Bairen County. The Han army entered the area without detecting the enemy's situation. The advance guard generals Zhu Fu and Deng Yu were defeated by Li Yu, and all the supplies in the army were lost.
Guangwu learned the news later, gathered the defeated stragglers of Zhu Fu and Deng Yu, fought fiercely with Li Yu at the outer city gate, defeated Li Yu, and confiscated the grain, grass and supplies that Li Yu had obtained during the battle with Zhu and Deng.
Li Yu retreated to the small town, but Guangwu could not attack it, so he led his troops to capture Guang'a County.
At this time, it happened that Geng Kuang, the governor of Shanggu, and Peng Chong, the governor of Yuyang, respectively sent generals such as Wu Han and Kou Xun to lead elite cavalry to assist in attacking Wang Lang. Emperor Gengshi also sent Shangshu servant She Xie Gong to attack Wang Lang. Guangwu rewarded the soldiers well, and then marched eastward and surrounded Julu City.
Wang Lang's general Wang Rao defended the city, and Guangwu failed to capture it for more than a month.
Wang Lang also sent Ni Hong and Liu Feng to lead tens of thousands of troops to rescue Julu. Guangwu went to Nanxian to attack them head-on, killing thousands of enemy troops.
In April, he marched again and besieged Handan, winning consecutive battles.
On the day of Jiachen in the fifth month, Handan was captured and Wang Lang was killed.
The documents were seized and it was discovered that the Han military officials had colluded with Wang Lang to slander Guangwu's letter, which was called Qianzhang.
Without even looking at it, Guangwu summoned the generals to burn them, saying: "Let those who are tossing and turning calm down."
Emperor Gengshi sent his censor, Shi Zhifujie, to make Guangwu the King of Xiao, asking him to cease the war and return to the seat of Emperor Gengshi.
Guangwu declined, saying that Hebei had not yet been pacified and would not accept the order.
From then on, Guangwu began to have second thoughts about Emperor Gengshi.
At that time, the political situation in Chang'an was in chaos, and all parties rebelled against Gengshi Emperor.
Liu Yong, the king of Liang, acted exclusively in Suiyang County, Gongsun Shu proclaimed himself king in Bashu, Li Xian established himself as the king of Huainan, Qin Feng claimed to be the king of Chuli, Zhang Bu raised troops in Langxie, Dong Xian raised troops in Donghai, Yancen raised troops in Hanzhong, and Tian Rong raised troops in Yiling. They all appointed generals and invaded various counties.
There were also bandits from various places with nicknames such as Tongma, Daxi, Gaohu, Chonglian, Tieshan, Dajiao, Youlai, Shangjiang, Qingdu, Wuxiao, Tanxiang, Wufan, Wulou, Fuping, Huosuo, etc. Each led his troops, totaling millions of people, to plunder in their respective counties.
Guangwu was preparing to attack these thieves, so he first sent Wu Han to recruit soldiers and horses from ten counties to march north.
When Miao Zeng, the governor of Youzhou, refused to obey, Wu Han killed him and mobilized his troops.
In autumn, Guangwu attacked the Bronze Horse Army in the county. Wu Han led the elite cavalry to Qingyang County to join Guangwu.
The Bronze Horse Army repeatedly challenged them, but Guangwu stood firm in the barracks and refused to fight back. Once someone from the Bronze Horse Army went out to rob property, Guangwu sent people to intercept them and cut off the Bronze Horse Army's food and grass channels.
After more than a month of this, the Bronze Horse Army ran out of food and fled in the middle of the night. Guangwu led his army to pursue them to Guantao County and defeated the Bronze Horse Army.
Before all the Bronze Horse Army surrendered, Gaohu and Chonglian came from the southeast to join the remaining Bronze Horse Army. Guangwu then fought fiercely with them in Puyang, defeated the enemy forces across the board and made them surrender, and named their generals as marquises.
The surrendered generals still felt uneasy. Guangwu knew their doubts and asked them to return to their respective armies to manage the soldiers, and then he leisurely rode on horseback to inspect each battalion.
The surrendered people talked among themselves and said: King Xiao confides in us, how can we not retaliate with death? From then on they were all convinced.
Guangwu distributed all the surrendered troops to the generals, and his troops expanded to hundreds of thousands. The people in Kansai therefore called Guangwu the "Bronze Horse Emperor".
The generals of other branches of the Red Eyebrow Army and more than 100,000 horses from Daxu and Qingdu gathered at Shedog. Guangwu led his troops to attack and defeated the Red Eyebrow Army. All the troops fled.
Guangwu sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to attack Yecheng and killed Xie Gong.
Qingdu and Chimei troops entered Hangu Pass and attacked Emperor Gengshi.
Guangwu then sent Deng Yu to lead his six lieutenants to march westward to take advantage of the war between Emperor Gengshi and Chimei.
At this time, Emperor Gengshi sent Grand Sima Zhu Tuna, Wuyin King Li Yi and others to garrison in Luoyang. Guangwu also ordered Feng Yi to defend Mengjin against them.
In the first month of the spring of the first year of Jianwu, Fang Wang, a native of Pingling, made Liu Ying, a young boy of the former Han Dynasty, the emperor. Gengshi sent Prime Minister Li Song to attack him and kill Liu Ying.
Guangwu attacked Youlai, Daqiang, and Wuban Yuyuan in the north, and pursued them to Youbeiping, winning successive victories.
They also fought in the north along the river, taking advantage of the victory to easily advance, but were defeated.
The thieves followed closely, and Guangwu jumped to the high bank, where he met Wang Feng, a sudden rider. Wang Feng dismounted and gave his horse to Guangwu. Guangwu pressed Wang Feng's shoulders and mounted, turned around and smiled at Geng Yan and said: "I almost made the bandits laugh!"
Geng Yan shot repeatedly to drive back the enemy and avoid suffering. Thousands of soldiers died, and the remaining troops retreated to Fan Yang.
The troops could not see Guangwu. Some people said that Guangwu was dead, and the generals did not know what to do.
Wu Han said: "Everyone, please work hard. Brother Xiao Wang's son is in Nanyang. Why worry about having no owner!" Everyone was in panic and fear, and it took several days to calm down.
Although the thieves won the battle, they were always afraid of the glory of military power and did not understand each other's situation, so they led their troops away at night.
Guangwu marched to Anci again, fought with the enemy, defeated the enemy, and killed more than 3,000 people.
When the enemy retreated into Yuyang, Guangwu sent Wu Han commander Geng Yan, Chen Jun, Ma Wu and other twelve generals to pursue the enemy east of Lucheng and as far as Pinggu, where they destroyed Youlai and other tribes.
Zhu Tun sent the general Su Mao to attack Wencheng. Feng Yi and Kou Xun fought against him, defeated Su Mao's army and killed Su Mao's general Jia Qiang.
So the generals began to discuss the matter of Guangwu proclaiming himself emperor.
Ma Wu first said: There is no master in the world. If a saint rises up while taking advantage of the decline, even if you make Confucius the prime minister and Sun Tzu a general, it may still be difficult to save it.
Who is the thief now, and we gallop into battle to attack him?
Guangwu said in surprise: "Why would the general say such a thing?" He deserves to be beheaded!
Ma Wu said: All the generals have this view!
Guangwu envoy Ma Wu informed the other generals and led his troops back to Jicheng.
In the fourth month of summer, Gongsun Shu claimed to be the emperor.
Guangwu returned from Jixian and passed through Fanyang. He ordered the remains of officers and soldiers to be buried.
When they arrived at Zhongshan Kingdom, the generals reported again: The Han Dynasty encountered Wang Mang's rebellion, the ancestral temples and temples were abandoned and sacrifices were abandoned, the heroes were angry and angry, and the people of Li were in dire straits.
The king and Bo Sheng led the uprising, and Emperor Gengshi occupied the throne by virtue of his seniority, but he could not flatter the Han Dynasty and violated the general laws and regulations, which led to the proliferation of bandits and the world was in crisis.
And in your first battle at Kunyang, Your Majesty, Wang Mang was defeated. Later, you captured Handan and pacified the northern states. You occupy two-thirds of the world, occupy the territory of various states and counties, and have millions of elite soldiers.
When it comes to force, no one can compete with you; when it comes to benevolence, no one can compare with you.
I heard that the throne of the emperor cannot be vacant for a long time, and God's will cannot be humbly resigned. I sincerely hope that your Majesty, your Majesty, will put the great plans of the country first and take the people of Li and Li into your heart. Guangwu still didn't listen.
When they marched to Nanpingji, the generals resolutely asked Guangwu to proclaim himself the emperor. Guangwu said: The bandits have not been wiped out and they are surrounded by enemies on all sides, so why bother proclaiming the emperor in a hurry?

summary:
Emperor Guangwu Liu Xiu, courtesy name Uncle Wen, was born in Caiyang, Nanyang, as the ninth-generation grandson of Liu Bang. He lost his father at age nine and was raised by his uncle Liu Liang. Described as tall with distinctive features, he was industrious and enjoyed farming, unlike his elder brother Bo Sheng who favored chivalry. During Wang Mang's reign, Liu Xiu studied the "Shang Shu" in Chang'an.

When locust plagues and famine struck, Liu Xiu fled to Xinye County to avoid government persecution. After receiving prophecies about the Liu family's revival, he initially hesitated but eventually planned with the Li family to raise an army. In October, at age 28, he raised troops in Wancheng. When local families saw the cautious Liu Xiu had joined the uprising, they stopped hiding. After initial victories and defeats, the Han army captured several cities.

Wang Mang sent Grand Situ Wang Xun and Grand Sikong Wang Yi with a massive army. Liu Xiu advised unity against the enemy, though generals initially resisted. With only 8,000-9,000 troops in Kunyang, Liu Xiu organized defenses and gathered reinforcements. Wang Mang's forces surrounded Kunyang with overwhelming numbers, using siege towers and tunnels. Despite the enemy's strength, Liu Xiu led a daring counterattack with 3,000 elite troops, breaking the enemy formation and killing Wang Xun. A storm aided the Han forces, causing panic and massive casualties among Wang Mang's army.

After Bo Sheng was killed by Emperor Gengshi, Liu Xiu rushed to apologize without boasting of his achievements. Emperor Gengshi appointed him General Polu and Marquis of Wuxin. When sent to Luoyang, Liu Xiu restored Han dynasty administrative practices, winning popular support. He crossed the Yellow River to pacify northern regions, releasing prisoners and abolishing Wang Mang's harsh policies.

When Wang Lang proclaimed himself emperor in Handan, Liu Xiu faced numerous hardships, including food shortages and dangerous river crossings. After gathering forces, he captured Handan and killed Wang Lang. He burned documents revealing officials' collaboration with Wang Lang, saying this would calm those who were anxious.

As chaos spread across the empire, Liu Xiu pacified various rebel groups including the Bronze Horse Army. He won over surrendered troops by personally inspecting their camps, earning their loyalty. His forces grew to hundreds of thousands.

After repeated requests from his generals, Liu Xiu ascended the throne on June 22, establishing the Jianwu reign period. He granted amnesty, appointed officials, and made Luoyang his capital. He enfeoffed meritorious officials as princes, warning them to remain cautious and respectful.

The Red Eyebrow Army captured Chang'an and looted Guanzhong. Liu Xiu personally led campaigns against various rebels, defeating the Red Eyebrows and recovering the imperial seal. He continued military campaigns against Liu Yong, Dong Xian, and others while implementing administrative reforms, including releasing prisoners during drought and restoring Han dynasty institutions. He established the Imperial Academy and promoted agriculture as wild grains gradually decreased and cultivated fields increased.

Emperor Xiaohuan Liu Zhi, great-grandson of Emperor Suzong Zhang, succeeded his father Liu Yi as Marquis of Liwu. In the first year of this century, Empress Dowager Liang summoned him to Luoyang, intending to marry her sister to him. After Emperor Zhi's death, Empress Dowager Liang and her brother General Liang Ji decided to install Liu Zhi as emperor. He ascended the throne at age fifteen, with Empress Dowager Liang still governing. Emperor Xiaozhi was buried in Jingling.

The emperor issued edicts calling for filial and honest officials to govern well, but noted that officials were negligent and selections were disorderly, harming the people. He urged officials to benefit workers and eliminate corruption. Only those with over ten years of service and special talents could be selected; descendants of corrupt officials were barred. He honored his ancestors posthumously.

In the first year of Jianhe, a solar eclipse occurred. The emperor ordered officials to discuss government affairs, granted amnesty, and provided relief to the needy. Disasters struck various regions, including earthquakes, floods, and famines. The emperor responded by ordering disaster relief, reducing taxes, and recommending virtuous officials. summary:
Emperor Xiaoling, Liu Hong, was the great-great-grandson of Emperor Suzong. His great-grandfather Liu Kai was the Xiaowang of Hejian, his grandfather Liu Shu and father Liu Chang were both Marquises of Duting, a title Liu Hong inherited. His mother was Mrs. Dong. After Emperor Huan died without children, Empress Dowager Dou and her father Dou Wu sent officials to escort Liu Hong to Luoyang. He became emperor at age twelve in the first year of Jianning (168 CE), with Chen Fan as Taifu and Dou Wu and Hu Guang assisting in governance.

The early years saw military campaigns against the Xianling Qiang, natural disasters including earthquakes and floods, and political purges. In 169 CE, eunuch Cao Jie falsely claimed an imperial order to kill Chen Fan, Dou Wu, and others, with their families executed. The Empress Dowager was moved to Nangong. Party member persecutions intensified, with over a hundred people imprisoned and their families exiled. Solar eclipses, epidemics, and barbarian rebellions occurred frequently.

In 172 CE, the reign name changed to Xiping. Empress Dowager Dou died, and eunuch Hou Lan committed suicide after being found guilty. The Xianbei raided Bingzhou. In 175 CE, the Five Classics were carved on stone tablets outside the Taixue. Floods, locust plagues, and Xianbei raids continued. In 178 CE, the reign changed to Guanghe, and the Hongdumen school was established. The West Residence began selling official positions, with prices varying by rank. Earthquakes, solar eclipses, and the deposal of Empress Song occurred.

In 179 CE, party members were pardoned. In 180 CE, Empress He was established. The emperor built shops in the inner palace where concubines traded, and he dressed as a merchant, playing with dogs and driving donkey carts. In 184 CE, Zhang Jiao led the Yellow Turban Rebellion, with followers wearing yellow scarves. The emperor appointed He Jin as general, established eight passes, and pardoned party members except Zhang Jiao. Generals Lu Zhi, Huangfu Song, and Zhu Jun suppressed the rebellion, killing Zhang Jiao and his brothers.

In 185 CE, Nangong caught fire, and taxes were levied per mu for palace construction. Black Mountain bandits and Xianbei raids continued. In 186 CE, Zhao Ci rebelled and was killed. In 187 CE, Zhang Chun and Zhang Ju rebelled in Yuyang, claiming emperorship. In 188 CE, the emperor proclaimed himself "Supreme General" and reviewed the army. Eight captains were established in Xiyuan. The Liangzhou bandit kingdom surrounded Chencang.

In 189 CE, Huangfu Song defeated the kingdom. The emperor died in Nangong at age thirty-four. Prince Bian became emperor at seventeen, with Empress Dowager He regent. Eunuch Zhang Rang and others killed General He Jin, leading to Yuan Shu burning the palaces and Yuan Shao massacring eunuchs. The young emperor and Prince Xie were kidnapped but later returned. Dong Zhuo deposed the emperor as Prince Hongnong. Heavy rain fell from June to September.

summary: Xiaoxian Emperor Liu Xie, the son of Emperor Ling, ascended the throne at age nine in September 189, moving the Empress Dowager to Yong'an Palace and granting amnesty. Dong Zhuo soon killed the Empress Dowager and appointed himself Prime Minister. In 190, prefectures raised troops against Dong Zhuo, who killed the former emperor Liu Bian and moved the capital to Chang'an, burning Luoyang's palaces. Dong Zhuo destroyed five-baht coins for small coins. In 191, Dong Zhuo became Grand Master, and Sun Jian defeated his general. Dong Zhuo excavated imperial tombs. In 192, Dong Zhuo was executed, and his clan was wiped out. His generals Li Jue and Guo Si rebelled, capturing Chang'an and killing over 10,000 officials and civilians. Li Jue killed Wang Yun and others. In 193, Yuan Shu killed the Yangzhou governor and occupied Huainan. In 194, a severe drought and locust plague caused famine, with grain prices soaring and cannibalism. The emperor personally inspected relief efforts. In 195, Li Jue killed Fan Chou and fought Guo Si, forcing the emperor to flee. The emperor began his journey back to Luoyang, facing attacks from Li Jue and Guo Si, with many officials killed. In 196, the emperor arrived in Luoyang, but the palace was burned, and officials suffered from hunger. Cao Cao took control, moving the capital to Xuchang and appointing himself Sikong. In 197, Yuan Shu claimed emperorship. In 198, Cao Cao killed Lü Bu. In 199, Yuan Shao captured Gongsun Zan. In 200, Dong Cheng's plot to kill Cao Cao failed, and Cao Cao killed him. Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao at Guandu. In 207, Cao Cao defeated the Wuhuan. In 208, Cao Cao became Prime Minister, defeated Liu Biao's son, but was defeated by Sun Quan at Red Cliffs. In 213, Cao Cao became Duke of Wei. In 214, Cao Cao killed Empress Fu. In 215, Cao Cao captured Hanzhong. In 216, Cao Cao became King of Wei. In 220, Cao Cao died, and his son Cao Pi succeeded. Emperor Xian abdicated, becoming Duke of Shanyang. Liu Bei proclaimed himself emperor of Shu, and Sun Quan became king of Wu, dividing the realm into three. Emperor Xian died in 234 at age 54, buried with Han rites. Historians note that Han's decline began long before his reign, and he was a victim of his era.

In the past, the story of King Wen burying dead bones was always praised by people.
Now we send people to inspect and patrol all areas, and if we find that the deceased has no family members or is too poor to pay for his burial, we will provide pensions anytime and anywhere to comfort the lonely souls.
This month, Xie An, a native of Xiapi, responded to the recruitment and attacked Xu Feng and others, killing Xu Feng.
In June, Xianbei bandits harassed Dai County.
On the first day of the seventh lunar month in autumn, Fuling King Liu Dai passed away.
The Lujiang bandits attacked Xunyang and Xutai. Teng Fu sent Sima Wangzhang to defeat them.
On September 22, Taifu Zhao Jun passed away.
On the second day of the eleventh month in winter, Han Zhao, the governor of Nanyang, was imprisoned for corruption and bribery.
On the 19th, Zhonglang sent Teng Fu to attack Guangling thief Zhang Ying and defeated him.
On the 20th, Zhonglang's general Zhao Xu was beheaded in the busy market for taking money.
Hua Meng, a thief in Liyang, claimed to be the "Black Emperor" and attacked and killed Yang Cen, the prefect of Jiujiang. Teng Fu led his generals to attack Hua Meng, defeated him and killed him.
On the tenth day of the first lunar month of spring in the first year of Benchu, the edict said: In ancient times, Yao ordered his four sons to respect the emperor and the heaven. Heaven gave the Dafa "Hongfan" to Xia Yu, who divided it into nine categories, including different symbols of good and evil, good and evil.
Auspiciousness comes because of purity and harmony, and misfortune comes because of going against the grain and being out of season. Although the prohibition is small, the fulfillment is huge.
Just like what Emperor Yao and Jizi paid attention to. Recently, states and counties have neglected the enforcement of laws and the prevention of illegal activities, but they have indulged in cruelty and cruelty to each other, creating and setting up some regulations to frame innocent people.
Or they act emotionally, follow their own moods, repel senior officials, flatter themselves for personal gain, impose unfair punishments, and take advantage of opportunities to vent their hatred, resulting in endless lawsuits in government offices.
Send away the old people and welcome the new people who have just arrived. People suffer disasters, and resentment hurts harmony, thus causing disasters and violence.
"Shangshu" says that one must have perfect virtue and punish with caution.
Now is the time for spring plowing and production. All things are developing in a small way, so we should cherish the budding state.
We now order those in charge that if the criminal is not to be beheaded, he will not be interrogated for the time being as a sign of forgiveness.
On the 26th, Wang Xi, the prefect of Guangling, was imprisoned because he did not actively fight against the thieves and refused to move forward.
On February 24, the edict stated: Jiujiang and Guangling counties have suffered many attacks from Zhang Ying and Hua Meng, and the devastation and injuries were the most severe.
Those who live are ruined, and those who die are buried in the wilderness.
Politicians in ancient times regarded it as their own fault if something did not get the proper status it deserved.
What's more, the vast number of people in Li are being troubled and poisoned in this way. Now is the lunar month of spring, a time to prepare for spring plowing, to provide relief to the poor and suffering, and to bury the dead bones and carrion that have been left in the wild.
The existing valleys in nearby counties should be allocated to provide relief to the poor, old and young, collect the bones and remains, and provide them with compensation, in order to satisfy my wishes.
On the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month in the summer, the prefectures and states were ordered to recommend Confucian scholars who were proficient in Confucian classics and were over fifty but under seventy to be sent to Taixue.
From the rank of general to the rank of six hundred stones, all the children are sent to school and get a job. When they are old enough, they will take an examination. The top five with the best test scores will be appointed as doctors, and the sixth to tenth will be appointed as princes.
Thousands of stones, six hundred stones, subordinates of the four mansions of General, Taiwei, Situ and Sikong, three ministers from Wuguansu, Zuosu and Youshu, and Xiaohou with four surnames: Fan, Guo, Yin and Ma. Those who can understand the classics first are called poets for poetry, and they are called Lijia for etiquette. They all follow the family rules. Those with the highest rankings will report their names, and they will be rewarded and used in turn.
On the sixth day of May, King Le'an was transferred to King Bohai.
The sea water overflowed and caused disaster.
On the 24th, visitors were sent to inspect and bury the dead who had been drowned by seawater in Le'an and Beihai. They also used the valley to provide relief to the poor, old, young and infirm.
On the 26th, Taibai star clashed with Yinghuo star.
On the third day of the sixth lunar month, a general amnesty was granted to the whole country, and the people were given various titles, grain, and silk.
On the first day of the sixth lunar month, the general Liang Ji secretly poisoned Emperor Zhi to kill him. The emperor died in the front hall of Yutang at the age of nine.
On the fourth day of the Lunar New Year, Taiwei Li Gu was dismissed from his post.
On the fifth day of the lunar month, Situ Hu Guang was appointed Taiwei, Sikong Zhao Jie was appointed Situ, and Liang Ji participated in the post of general secretary.
He appointed his servant Yuan Tang as Sikong.
The historian praised: When Emperor Shun first became emperor, he had many outstanding people around him, but he was unable to forge ahead and carry out reforms. In the end, he indulged in personal favors and practices, relied on peace, and was greedy for goods and bribes to increase the number of people.
He trusted two generations of relatives, so the government was in a state of decline.
Chong Di Yaoshang is not sensible at all.
Emperor Zhi was smart and precocious, but he was killed by Liang Ji.
summary:
In the first year of Yongning, Liu Bao, son of Emperor An, was made crown prince. His mother, Mrs. Li, had been killed by Queen Yan. In the third year of Yanguang, the prince's wet nurse Wang Nan and kitchen supervisor Bing Ji were killed after being framed by Wang Sheng, Jiang Jing, and Fan Feng. Liu Bao sighed repeatedly, leading Wang Sheng and others to fear consequences and frame him, resulting in his deposition as King of Jiyin.

When Emperor An died in March of the fourth year of Yanguang, Liu Yi became emperor. Liu Bao was barred from attending the funeral, causing him to wail and refuse food, moving officials inside and outside. After Liu Yi's death, Empress Dowager Yan's brother Yan Xian and Jiang Jing plotted to secretly not announce the mourning and conscript another prince. Liu Bao closed the palace gates and defended himself. On the fourth day of November, an earthquake struck sixteen places. That night, Sun Cheng and others killed Jiang Jing, Liu An, and Chen Da, welcoming Liu Bao to ascend the throne at age eleven.

The ministers reported that due to treacherous ministers, the emperor had become a vassal king, but destiny favored the Han family. The emperor succeeded to the throne according to heaven's will and the people's wishes. He ordered the organization of rituals. Yan Xian's brothers led troops into the North Palace but were fought by Guo Zhen, who killed Yan Jing. On the fifth day, envoys seized the seal, and the emperor arrested and executed Yan Xian and his brothers. On the sixth day, the palace gates were opened. On the ninth day, an order was issued that only close relatives of Yan Xian and Jiang Jing would be punished.

The emperor visited Gaomiao and Guangwu Temple. He ordered the use of Baoxie Road instead of Ziwu Road. Liu Yi was buried with royal rites. Sikong Liu was dismissed, and ministers were rewarded. Tao Dun was appointed Sikong. A major epidemic occurred in the capital. The edict deposing Liu Bao as King Jiyin was returned. In the first year of Yongjian, a general amnesty was granted, with various rewards and exemptions. Empress Dowager Yan passed away. Taifu Feng Shi, Taiwei Liu Xi, and Situ Li were dismissed. Queen Ansi was buried. Taichang Huanyan was appointed Taifu; Zhu Chong was appointed Taiwei; Zhu Qian was appointed Situ.

The Zhongqiang in Longxi rebelled but were defeated by Ma Xian. Governors were ordered to verify officials and organize border fortifications. Liu Xian was made King of Jinan. Ren Weiwei was appointed general of chariots and cavalry. Xianbei bandits raided Daijun, killing Li Chao. The emperor began to order Sangong and Shangshu to report state affairs. Prisoners with capital crimes were moved to border areas. Sikong Taodun was dismissed. Xianbei invaded border areas. The Liyang Battalion was sent to garrison the northern border of Zhongshan. Five captains of crossbow divisions were selected. Tingwei Zhang Hao was appointed Sikong. Due to severe epidemic, common people lost half of their field rent.

In the second year, King Liu Hong of Le'an paid homage. King Liu Zhang of Changshan passed away. Xianbei raided Liaodong and Xuantu. Grain relief was provided to poor people in four prefectures. Geng Ye led Nan Shanyu to attack Xianbei and defeated them. There was a drought. Shule State sent envoys. Imperial concubine Li was given the posthumous title of Queen Gongmin. Ban Yong and Zhang Lang attacked Yanqi, Yuli, and Weixu, defeating them. A solar eclipse occurred. Taiwei Zhu Chong and Situ Zhu Chong were dismissed. Liu Guang was appointed Taiwei; Xu Jing was appointed Situ. King Liu Cheng of Xiapi passed away.

In the third year, an earthquake struck the capital and Hanyang. The edict provided compensation for the injured. Land rent and population tax were not collected in Hanyang. Dr. Guanglu was sent to inspect and provide grain loans. There was a drought. King Liu Xian of Jinan passed away. A fire broke out in the Mausoleum Mausoleum. Xianbei raided Yuyang. Grand Tutor Huan Yan was dismissed. In the fourth year, an edict granted amnesty and restored official ranks. The emperor was crowned. Rewards were given. Officials were ordered to inspect civilians cutting rocks. The prefect of Guiyang presented a pearl, which was returned. Rain fell in five states. Envoys were sent to verify the deceased. Taiwei Liu Guang and Sikong Zhang Hao were dismissed. Stability was restored in Beidi and Shangjun. Pang Can was appointed Taiwei; Wang Gong was appointed Sikong. Situ Xu Jing was dismissed. Xianbei plundered Shuofang. Liu Qi was appointed Situ. Kuaiji was divided into Wu County. Kumi Kingdom sent envoys.

In the fifth year, Shule, Dayuan, and Shache sent envoys. There was a drought in the capital. Poor people were exempted from border guard duties. Locust plagues struck. Prisoners were sent to guard borders. Hou Banshi was executed for killing his wife. In the sixth year, King Liu Kai of Hejian passed away. Yiwu's farming was restored. The Imperial Academy was repaired. Geng Ye attacked Xianbei and defeated them. The King of Khotan sent his son. An edict exempted land rent in Hebei due to disasters. Rinan Waiye Tiaoguo and Shan State sent envoys. A guest star appeared near Altair. The King of Khotan sent his son again.

In the first year of Yangjia, Queen Liang was established. Rewards were given. Pirate Zeng Jing plundered Kuaiji. The queen paid homage to temples. There was a drought. Prayers were held for rain. Grain was loaned to Hebei. An edict prayed to mountains and rivers. Demon thief Zhang He plundered forty-nine counties. The emperor held a great shooting ceremony and granted amnesty. Liu Hui of Fuling passed away. Taishi Ling Zhang Heng made bronze instruments. Taixue disciples were increased. Ninety senior scholars were appointed. Xianbei raided Liaodong. Wolves devoured women in Wangdu and Puyin. The county was ordered to recommend filial and honest officials over forty. King Liu Chang of Dongping passed away. Xuantu County's tuntian divisions were restored. Lang officials over forty could participate in elections. A guest star appeared in Tianyuan. The governor and Erqianshi were selected by Taiwei, Sikong, and Situ. A fire broke out at Gongling Mausoleum. Xiyuan was built.

In the second year, seed rations were lent to Wu County and Kuaiji. Wang Chou attacked Xianbei and defeated them. Forty-eight old Confucian scholars were appointed. The southwestern Longnan captaincy was restored. An earthquake struck the capital. An edict acknowledged natural disasters and sought advice. Sikong Wang Gong was dismissed. Kong Fu was appointed Sikong. Shule presented lions and oxen. Luoyang collapsed. There was a drought. Taiwei Pang Shen was dismissed. Shi Yan was appointed Taiwei. Xianbei invaded Daijun. A sacrificial ceremony was held in Piyong.

In the third year, due to drought, prisoners were not questioned. Yizhou thieves killed princes. Sima attacked the Xiongnu and captured the Chanyu's aunt. An edict granted amnesty and rewards. Zhongqiang bandits raided Longxi and Hanyang. Feng Xu defeated them. Situ Liuqi and Sikong Kongfu were dismissed. Huang Shang was appointed Situ; Wang Zhuo was appointed Sikong. Wudu blocked the Tun Qiang and attacked.

In the fourth year, eunuchs were allowed to adopt sons. There was a drought. Ma Xian attacked Zhong Qiang. Taiwei Shi Yan was dismissed. Liang Shang was appointed general; Pang Shen was appointed Taiwei. King Liu Kuang of Liang passed away. King Liu Deng of Jibei passed away. A solar eclipse occurred. Wuhuan raided the clouds. Geng Ye was surrounded in Lanchi but rescued. An earthquake struck the capital.

In the first year of Yonghe, King Fuyu paid homage. An edict acknowledged disasters and sought advice. Sacrifices were held in Mingtang. A locust plague struck Yanshi. A fire broke out in Chengfu Palace. Taiwei Pang Shen was dismissed. Xianglin barbarians rebelled. Wang Gong was appointed Taiwei. Wuling barbarians rebelled. The captain of Guanghan defeated the Baima Qiang. Li Jin defeated the rebels. King Liu Yi of Beihai passed away. Sikong Wangzhuo passed away. Guo Qian was appointed Sikong. An earthquake struck the capital. Rinan barbarians rebelled. Soldiers from Jiuzhen and Jiaozhi rebelled. Mars opposed the Southern Dipper. Jiangxia thieves killed the magistrate. The emperor visited Chang'an and provided relief. He visited Weiyang Palace. Sacrifices were held at Gaomiao and the Eleven Tombs. An earthquake struck the capital. The emperor returned to Luoyang.

In the third year, earthquakes struck the capital, Jincheng, and Longxi. Taibai opposed Mars. Cai Bo harassed county boundaries. Dr. Guanglu was sent to inspect Jincheng and Longxi. Cai Bo surrendered. An earthquake struck the capital. Yangzhen rebelled but was killed. King Liu Zun of Langfu passed away. Zhu Liang and Zhang Qiao calmed Rinan barbarians. King Liu Duo of Jibei passed away. Situ Huangshang was dismissed. Liu Shou was appointed Situ. The general and three princes were ordered to recommend capable individuals. Qiang invaders burned Jincheng but were defeated by Ma Xian. A solar eclipse occurred.

In the fourth year, Zhang Kui, Zang Zheng, and Yang Ding were executed. An earthquake struck the capital. Ma Xian attacked the Shaodang Qiang and defeated them. A general amnesty was granted. Liu An was made King of Jibei. There was a drought in Taiyuan. Dr. Guanglu was sent to inspect. The emperor hunted in Shanglin Garden and visited Guangcheng Garden.

In the fifth year, an earthquake struck the capital. King Liu Hong of Zhongshan passed away. Wusi and Cheniu rebelled but were defeated by Ma Xu. A solar eclipse occurred. Frozen Qiang bandits robbed Sanfu. Prisoners were allowed to atone. Fufeng and Hanyang built barriers. Taiwei Wang Gong was dismissed. Huanyan was appointed Taiwei. Xihe, Shang, and Shuofang counties moved their capitals. Julongwusi established Cheniu as chanyu. Zhang Dan defeated Cheniu.

In the sixth year, Ma Xian was defeated by Qie Dong Qiang. The king and marquis were exempted from rent. Gongtang Qiang raided Longxi. A comet was seen. Zhao Chong defeated Gongtang Qiang. Sikong Guo Qian was dismissed. King Liu Zheng of Hejian passed away. Zhao Jie was appointed Sikong. King Liu Wuji of Qi passed away. Zhang Dan defeated Wuhuan and Qianghu. Gongtang Qiang raided the north. Common people borrowed money from wealthy households. Liang Shang passed away; Liang Ji became general. Various Qiang raided Wuwei. A solar eclipse occurred. Anding and Beidi moved their capitals. Zhang Qiao acted as general of chariots and cavalry.

In the first year of Han'an, a general amnesty was granted. The general and ministers were ordered to recommend virtuous individuals. Chenghua stables were set up. Julong Wusi rebelled. Du Qiao and others were sent to inspect prefectures. Zhang Ying invaded Guangling. Taiwei Huan Yan and Situ Liu Shou were dismissed. Zhang Qiao left. Zhao Jun was appointed Taiwei; Hu Guang was appointed Situ. Wu Meng was selected. Zhang Ying surrendered.

In the second year, Shan Zang and Shan Guo sent envoys. Zhao Chong and Zhang Gong defeated He Qiang. Yinghuo opposed Saturn. Douluo Chu was appointed Southern Danyu. Prisoners were allowed to atone. Officials' salaries were reduced. Alcohol sales were prohibited. Zhao Chong defeated Shaodang Qiang. Ma Chen assassinated Julong Wusi. Yang and Xu bandits attacked. 180 earthquakes occurred in Liangzhou.

In the first year of Jiankang, an edict acknowledged earthquakes and provided relief. King Liu Guang of Pei passed away. Wei Ju defeated rebellious Qiang. Nanjun and Jiangxia bandits plundered. Ma Chen defeated the southern Xiongnu. Prince Liu Bing was made crown prince. King Liu Yanping of Qinghe passed away. Fan Rong and Zhou Sheng plundered. The emperor passed away at age thirty. Historians commented on Emperor Shun's reign.

Emperor Chong Liu Bing ascended the throne at age two. The Queen Mother handled state affairs. Zhao Jun was appointed Taifu; Li Gu was appointed Taiwei. Emperor Shun was buried. Earthquakes struck the capital, Taiyuan, and Yanmen. Virtuous individuals were recommended. Qiu Teng was executed. Yin Yao and Deng Xian were killed by bandits. Rinan barbarians attacked. King Liu Yi of Changshan passed away. Liu Kang was imprisoned. Xu Feng and Ma Mian attacked. Prisoners were moved. Huang Hu attacked Hefei. Xianling Tomb was excavated. Zhao Chong died in battle.

Emperor Chong died at age three. Liu Zuan was summoned. He became emperor at age eight. Emperor Chong was buried. Zhang Ying rebelled again. Xu Feng attacked. A general amnesty was granted. Liu Dao of Pengcheng passed away. Qiang surrendered. Ma Mian was killed. Prayers were held for rain. King Liu An of Jibei passed away. Lu Gong besieged the city but was defeated. An edict acknowledged drought and provided relief. Xie An killed Xu Feng. Xianbei harassed Dai County. King Liu Dai of Fuling passed away. Lujiang bandits attacked. Taifu Zhao Jun passed away. Han Zhao was imprisoned. Teng Fu defeated Zhang Ying. Zhao Xu was executed. Hua Meng was killed.

In the first year of Benchu, an edict emphasized virtue and punishment. Wang Xi was imprisoned. Relief was provided to Jiujiang and Guangling. Confucian scholars were recommended. Children of officials were sent to school. King Le'an was transferred to King Bohai. Seawater overflowed. Relief was provided. Taibai clashed with Yinghuo. A general amnesty was granted. Liang Ji poisoned Emperor Zhi, who died at age nine. Li Gu was dismissed. Hu Guang was appointed Taiwei; Zhao Jie was appointed Situ; Liang Ji participated in the general secretary. Yuan Tang was appointed Sikong. Historians praised Emperor Shun but noted his decline. Emperor Zhi was killed by Liang Ji.

Emperor Xianzong Xiaoming Mingzhuang, the fourth son of Emperor Guangwu.
His mother was Queen Yin, and Emperor Ming was born with a square face. He could read the Spring and Autumn Annals at the age of ten. Guangwu was very surprised by his talent.
In the fifteenth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Duke of Donghai, promoted to king in the seventeenth year, and crown prince in the nineteenth year.
He became a disciple of Dr. Huan Rong and studied Shangshu.
On the fifth day of the second lunar month in the second year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, he ascended the throne and was thirty years old.
Respect the queen as the empress dowager.
On the fifth day of the third lunar month, Emperor Guangwu was buried in the original mausoleum, and a priest named him the ancestor of the emperor.
On the 24th of April in the summer, Emperor Ming issued an edict saying: I am a young man who has inherited the great legacy of my ancestors. I am terrified day and night and dare not act casually.
The late emperor upheld the destiny of heaven and revitalized the Han Dynasty. His moral character was the same as that of the emperor. Offer sacrifices to mountains and rivers, bring peace to all gods, and bestow favors on widows and widowers.
I bear the great fortune of the country. Inheriting the political system, adhering to civility and morality, and not knowing the hardships of farming, I am only afraid of neglect and mistakes.
Our ancestors' wills warned us to cherish and respect the world and put the people first.
How will you, my ministers and your officials, assist me in my shortcomings?
Today, men in the world are given the title of nobility, each with two levels; the three elders, filial brothers, and Li Tian each have three levels. If the title is above eight levels, they can be transferred to the son or the half-brother or the son of the half-brother; as well as homeless people without household registration who want to surrender themselves, each one will be given one level; widowers, widows, orphans, alone, and terminally ill people will each be given ten dendrobium of millet.
On April 11, the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, prisoners who were released from their shackles and those who committed crimes but were arrested later will be exempted from punishment.
Before the amnesty on April 11, civilians on the border who became the wives of people from the inner county due to violence would be sent back to the border, completely subject to their own wishes.
Those who were demoted from 2,000 shi down to 200 shi, and those who paid for atonement were restored to official rank and paid back the ransom.
Now that there is no emperor above and no local governor below, it is like crossing an abyss without a boat.
The throne is very important, but I am still young and have superficial thoughts. I really rely on the guidance and help of talented people.
Deng Yu, the Marquis of Gaomi, was the most accomplished, and Liu Cang, the King of Dongping, was magnanimous, knowledgeable and resourceful, and would not give in during important events. They could all be entrusted to assist the young master in governing the world. Deng Yu is now appointed as Taifu, and Liu Cang is appointed as General of Hussars.
Taiwei Zhao Xixin announced his posthumous title to the southern suburbs, Situ Li Fanjin was entrusted with the late Emperor Zi's palace, and Sikong Feng Li general overthrew the school.
Today, Zhao Xi is granted the title of Marquis of Jiexiang, Li Fanjin is granted the title of Marquis of Anxiang, and Feng Li is granted the title of Marquis of Yangyi.
In the ninth month of autumn, the Shaodang Qiang invaded Longxi and defeated the Longxi County soldiers at Yunjie.
The prisoners in Longxi will be pardoned, their crimes reduced to one level, and they will not be charged for this year's rent transfer.
In addition, the three thousand people from Tianshui who were recruited were exempted from the tax for this year. Zhang Hong was sent to Yunwu to attack the rebellious Qiang. Zhang Hong's army was defeated and Zhang Hong was killed.
In November of winter, he sent General Dou Gu to supervise the captured general Ma Wu and other two generals to attack the Shaodang Qiang.
On December 26, Emperor Ming issued an edict: It is spring now, and people are busy plowing the fields and raising silkworms.
All officials must comply with the solar terms and not interfere with agricultural work.
The desperadoes in the world were sentenced to beheading or less, and they were asked to atone for their sins: for the crime of death, twenty pieces of steel were cut off, and then the right foot was cut off until it reached the edge of the city, and ten pieces of steel were put into it.
Didn't realize that those who surrendered before the edict was issued would have their redemption items halved.
Nowadays, the election is not real, and the evil and sycophants have not been removed. The powerful are bribed and cruel, and the officials are greedy and do whatever they want. The people are miserable and complain, and there is no way to report the truth. The relevant government officials should clearly report the crime and punish those who recommend improperly.
Every time the counties and counties imposed labor levies, they easily made profits, deceitfully scolded and intimidated the poor and weak civilians, and made them anxious.
Now it is necessary to make the labor even and not unjust.
In the first month of the spring of the first year of Yongping, Emperor Ming led officials below the public minister to pay homage to the original mausoleum, just like the Yuan Hui ceremony.
In the fifth month of summer, Taifu Deng Yu passed away.
On the 22nd, Liu Qiang, the king of the East China Sea, passed away. He sent Sikong Fenggui to hold the talisman festival to watch the funeral, and rewarded him with a rising dragon head, a ruan, and a dragon flag.
On June 24, Prince Gong of Donghai was buried.
In the seventh month of autumn, the captured general Ma Wu and others fought against the Shaodang Qiang, and the Qiang were defeated.
Soldiers were recruited to guard Longyou, and each man was rewarded with 30,000 yuan.
On the fourth day of August, King Liu Jing of Shanyang was transferred to King Guangling and ordered to enter the fiefdom.
In this year, the governor of Liaodong sacrificed to Xianbei and attacked Wuhuan in Chishan. He defeated Wuhuan and beheaded his commander-in-chief.
Yuegu Fuyi rebelled, and the state and county troops attacked and put down the rebellion.
On the 19th day of the first lunar month in the second year of spring, Emperor Guangwu was worshiped in Mingtang. The Emperor Ming and his ministers and princes began to wear crowns, clothes, jade pendants, and colorful robes for the ceremony.
After the salute, he ascended to the mourning platform.
The minister was sent to hold the Fujie edict and ordered the Hussar General and Sangong to say: On this auspicious day, we will sacrifice Emperor Guangwu in the Mingtang to be worthy of the Five Emperors.
Preparing ritual objects, music and music, singing about blessings, dancing to show merit, announcing the seasons, and admonishing the queen.
After the ceremony, go up to the spiritual platform, look at the clouds, play wind instruments, and observe the changes in things.
Hundreds of officials, vassal assistants, descendants of the clan, officials from prefectures and counties, and barbarian leaders Wuhuan and Sui Suiyu all came to assist in the ceremony. The Xiongnu Chanyu served the son of the Han Palace, and the Marquis of Gudu also came to attend the ceremony.
This was the power inspired by the merits of the Holy Ancestor that brought them together.
I am dim and humble, but I have accumulated great achievements. I personally hold Wang Guibi and offer sacrifices to heaven and earth.
In memory of the late emperor who was resurrected by destiny, he brought order out of chaos, brought peace and happiness to the world, enshrined Mount Tai, built Mingtang, erected a memorial hall, and set up a spiritual platform, so as to carry forward the cause of building a country and loving the people.
Grace spreads all over the earth. But I don't have the talent of King Cheng and King Kang of the Zhou Dynasty, and the ministers don't have the same strategies as Lu Shang and Ji Dan. With a humble nature, he becomes even more frightened when big events happen. Therefore, it is said: A graceful and generous gentleman is always calm and comfortable, while a villain who can't pretend to be troublesome is always worried. We now order the whole country to be exempted from punishment, from those sentenced to beheading to those who conspire to rebel and commit treason.
All officials must handle their duties diligently and carefully, comply with the seasons, respect heaven, and enable hundreds of millions of people to live a happy life.
In March, Emperor Ming came to Piyong and held the great shooting ceremony for the first time.
In the ninth month of autumn, King Liu Fu of Pei, King Liu Ying of Chu, King Liu Kang of Jinan, King Liu Yan of Huaiyang, and King Liu Zheng of Donghai came to pay homage.
On the fifth day of the tenth lunar month in winter, Emperor Ming came to Piyong and held a pension ceremony for the first time.
The edict said: Emperor Guangwu built Mingtang, Piyong, and Lingtai as gifts for three dynasties, but he did not have time to reward and entertain the elders.
I, the insignificant one, inherit the throne.
Taking advantage of the good time of March in late spring, I performed the great shooting ceremony at the beginning, and on the beautiful first day of October, I went to Piyong again.
Respect the three elders, take care of the five brothers, install the soft wheel of the car, and personally hold the sash.
When the princes and kings set up the gravy, and the ministers set out the delicacies, I would personally cut off my legs with my sleeves exposed, hold a wine glass, and rinse the old man's mouth.
Afraid that the old man would choke, he beat his back back and forth. He sang "Deer Ming" at the top and "New Palace" at the bottom. Eight hundred people lined up and ten thousand people danced in the court.
I know very well that I have little virtue, how dare I act like that?
"Yi" says that a villain who wears a gentleman's utensils will become a thief. "Poetry" also satirizes those who illegally make and use utensils. They will always feel guilty and remember this in their hearts.
The third elder, Li Gong, is a man of advanced learning.
At five o'clock in the morning, Huan Rong taught me Shangshu.
"The Book of Songs" says: No virtue will not be repaid, no words will not be rewarded.
Huan Rong is now granted the title of Marquis in Guannei and has a settlement of 5,000 households.
The third elder and the fifth elder all receive a salary of two thousand dan for life.
Today, the three elders in the world are given a stone of wine and forty pounds of meat each. The officials should greet and comfort the elderly, show mercy to the young orphans, and benefit the widows and widowers. This is in line with my wishes.
Liu Yan, the king of Zhongshan, began to go to his fiefdom.

Before the Xia and Shang dynasties, records of the concubine system were sparse. "The Rites of Zhou" describes the emperor's harem hierarchy: a queen, three wives, nine concubines, twenty-seven wives, and eighty-one female concubines, each with specific duties. The queen held equal status to the emperor, while wives assisted her in women's ethics. Concubines taught women's virtues, speech, appearance, and merits. Female officials managed rituals, dining, and sleeping arrangements, with a female historian recording merits and demerits. This system aimed to maintain order and prevent corruption, as seen in Queen Kang of Zhou's virtuous conduct. However, after the Zhou capital moved to Luoyang, etiquette declined. Dukes like Huan of Qi and Xian of Jin indulged in multiple wives, leading to succession conflicts and state ruin. During the Warring States period, moral decay worsened, causing widespread destruction.

Qin Shihuang unified China but imitated the six kingdoms' palaces, recruiting beauties. The Han dynasty initially lacked a formal harem system, leading to lax morals under Emperor Gaozu and favoritism under Emperor Xiaowen. From Emperor Wu onward, concubine numbers swelled to three thousand, with fourteen grades, fostering corruption and foreign relatives' power. Emperor Guangwu of Eastern Han simplified the system, reducing titles to queen and noble, with minimal salaries. He sent officials to select virtuous girls aged 13-20 for the harem. Emperor Ming upheld these standards, emphasizing moral character, but failed to prevent promiscuity. From ancient times, emperors relied on governors, not women, to rule. The Qin dynasty's Queen Mother Mi set a precedent for regency, which Han emperors followed, leading to power struggles. Eastern Han saw four emperors with regent empresses, like Empress Dowager Zhang Di and Hexi Deng, who controlled state affairs, causing disasters. Empress Dowager Huansi Dou was exiled, and her father executed, illustrating the cycle of ruin.

The text then details specific queens. Queen Guangwu Guo, from Zhending, married Guangwu during his campaign. She became queen and bore Prince Liu Qiang, but her favor waned, leading to her deposition as Queen Mother of Zhongshan. Her brother Guo Kuang was honored but later implicated in a rebellion, with his family exiled. Historians note that favor and disfavor follow natural laws, and Queen Guo's decline was due to lost affection, yet she retained honor. Queen Guanglie Yin, from Nanyang, was admired by Guangwu for her beauty. She married him and became noble, refusing the queen title due to Guo's son. After Guo's deposition, Yin became queen, praised for her humility and virtue. She died at sixty, buried with Guangwu. Emperor Ming mourned her deeply.

Empress Ma of Mingde, daughter of General Ma Yuan, lost her parents young and managed household affairs at ten. She entered the crown prince's palace at thirteen, serving Queen Yin with grace. She raised Emperor Zhang as her own, despite having no children, and was made queen. She wore simple clothes, avoided luxury, and advised Emperor Ming on legal matters, reducing punishments. As empress dowager, she refused to ennoble her brothers, citing historical precedents of foreign relatives' downfall. She maintained frugality and moral standards, dying at forty. Jia Guiren, mother of Emperor Zhang, was not honored as queen, as Emperor Zhang considered the Ma family his maternal relatives. Empress Zhang De Dou, from Fufeng, was chosen for her talent and beauty. She became queen but, lacking children, grew jealous, causing the deaths of Song and Liang nobles. After Emperor Zhang's death, she served as regent, but her brothers' rebellion led to her posthumous demotion, though she was buried with Emperor Zhang.

Queen Yin, great-niece of Queen Guanglie, was deposed for witchcraft and died in sorrow. Queen Hexi Deng, granddaughter of Tai Fu Deng Yu, was known for her intelligence and virtue. She entered the palace at sixteen, serving Queen Yin humbly. After Yin's deposition, she became queen, banning luxury and refusing to ennoble her family. As empress dowager, she ruled during crises, reducing expenses, pardoning exiles, and promoting education. She died at forty-one, buried with Emperor He. Historians criticize her for holding power too long, leading to resentment, but acknowledge her efforts to stabilize the state.

Emperor Suzong Xiaozhang, named Huodan, was the fifth son of Xianzong. He became crown prince in the third year of Yongping and ascended the throne on the sixth day of August in the eighteenth year of Yongping at age nineteen. He honored the queen as empress dowager and issued a general amnesty, granting titles and grain to various groups including widows, orphans, and the poor. In his edict, he acknowledged his modest virtue and fear of making mistakes, emphasizing the importance of following proper governance as taught in the Book of Songs. He appointed Zhao, Marquis of Jiexiang, as Taifu and Mourong as Taiwei, urging officials to correct his errors and serve with loyalty.

On November 24, Wu Lun became Sikong. General Geng Bing was ordered to garrison Jiuquan, and Duan Peng was sent to rescue Geng Gong. A solar eclipse occurred on the 30th, prompting Emperor Zhang to avoid the main hall, cease military actions, and not hold court for five days. Officials were instructed to submit criticisms and suggestions. On December 20, officials praised Emperor Xiaoming’s simple virtue and hard work, noting his kindness spread far and wide, defeating ghosts and developing the Western Regions. Emperor Zhang approved the proposal to honor Xianzong in the temple and perform the "Wude" dance.

A cattle plague and severe drought struck the capital and three prefectures, leading to exemptions from land rent and aid for the poor. In the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Emperor Zhang ordered loans for the poor, support for wandering people returning home, and strict oversight to prevent corruption. He encouraged farming and mulberry cultivation, postponed trials except for capital crimes, and urged officials to select virtuous candidates. Duan Peng defeated the Che Division, and the Wuling barbarians rebelled. Earthquakes occurred in Shanyang and Dongping.

Emperor Zhang issued an edict acknowledging disasters and his lack of wisdom, calling for the promotion of talented individuals regardless of background. He ordered each official to recommend one virtuous and upright person. In the fifth month, Xiaolian were recommended, and in the seventh month, land from Shanglin Garden was given to the poor. A comet appeared in August, and the Yongchang Ailao Yi rebelled in September. Wuling County forces defeated the rebels in October, and Fuling King Liu Yan was demoted to marquis in November.

In the second year, Emperor Zhang criticized the extravagance of nobles and close relatives, ordering strict enforcement of laws. He sent troops to Yiwulu and pacified the Ailao rebellion. In April, he allowed 400 families displaced by rebellions to return home. The Shaodang Qiang rebelled in June, and Hao Chong was defeated. Ma Fang was sent to suppress the rebellion in August. A comet appeared in December.

In the third year, Emperor Zhang performed ancestral rites and issued an amnesty. He made the noble Dou family queen and granted titles and grain. Construction of river canals was halted in April. Ma Fang defeated the Shaodang Qiang, and Banchao defeated Gumo. Ma Fang was appointed general of chariots and cavalry. Lingling offered zhicao.

Emperor Zhang issued an edict emphasizing Confucian education, leading to the gathering of scholars at Baihu Temple to discuss the Five Classics, resulting in the "Baihu Tong."

In the eighth year, King Dongping died. The Northern Huns surrendered. Emperor Zhang emphasized agriculture and ordered support for poor farmers. He promoted the study of Zuo Shi Chun Qiu and other texts. Locusts plagued the capital.

In the first year of Yuanhe, various kings died. Emperor Zhang prohibited cruel torture and changed the era name. He ordered reduced punishments and inspected the south, offering rewards.
