It traces the evolution of imperial consort titles from ancient times through the Zhou dynasty, when the emperor established one queen, three wives, nine concubines, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one royal wives to manage the inner palace. The text emphasizes that virtuous empresses served as maternal role models who promoted imperial teachings and ensured dynastic prosperity, while those who abused their power brought disaster upon their houses.

The biographies of individual empresses and concubines follow. Empress Xuanmu Zhang, from Pinggao, Hanoi, was known for her wisdom and decisiveness. She once killed a maid who witnessed her husband feigning illness to prevent exposure of the deception. Despite being neglected when another concubine gained favor, she maintained her dignity. She died at fifty-nine during the Wei Zhengshi era and was posthumously honored after Emperor Wu accepted the throne.

Empress Jinghuai Xiahou, from Pei state, was elegant and knowledgeable, often planning ahead for Emperor Jing. However, as she was a niece of the Wei imperial family, Emperor Jing grew suspicious of her, and she died by poison at twenty-four. Empress Jingxian Yang, from Mount Tai, was intelligent and virtuous. After Emperor Jing married and divorced another woman, he married Yang, who bore no sons. She lived to sixty-five and was buried with Emperor Jing.

Queen Wenming Wang, from Tan county, demonstrated exceptional intelligence from childhood, reciting classics at eight and managing household affairs at a young age. Her grandfather lamented she was not born male. She married Emperor Wen, bore several children including Emperor Wu, and served her parents-in-law devotedly. She warned against trusting Zhong Hui, who later rebelled. As Empress Dowager, she lived simply, weaving her own cloth and wearing washed garments. She died at fifty-two and was buried with Emperor Wen.

Empress Wu Yuanyang, named Yan, from Huayin, was naturally beautiful, skilled in calligraphy and crafts. Emperor Wen selected her for his son. She bore Emperor Hui and other children. When Emperor Wu doubted the crown prince's capability, she insisted on primogeniture. She was jealous, selecting only fair-skinned, tall women for the harem while rejecting beautiful candidates. On her deathbed at thirty-seven, she recommended her cousin to succeed her.

Empress Wu Daoyang, cousin of Wujiang, was established as queen in the second year of Shengkong. She personally collected mulberries and raised silkworms. After Emperor Wu's death, she became Empress Dowager but was falsely accused of conspiracy by Empress Jia, deposed as a commoner, and died at thirty-four after a hunger strike. Her title was posthumously restored in the first year of Yongjia.

Concubine Zuo Fen, known for literary talent despite plain appearance, wrote the melancholy "Lisi Fu" expressing sorrow at separation from family. She composed eulogies for Empress Yuan Yang and Princess Wannian. Hu Guifei, named Fang, was selected in the ninth year of Taishi and became the most favored concubine, once scratching Emperor Wu's finger during a game. Mrs. Zhuge, named Zhuge Wan, entered the palace in the ninth year of Taishi.

Queen Huijia, named Nanfeng, was married to the crown prince despite Emperor Wu's reservations. She was jealous and cruel, killing several people with her own hands and causing a pregnant concubine to miscarry. After becoming empress, she grew increasingly dissolute, engaging in affairs with physicians and luring young men into the palace. She conspired against the crown prince and was eventually deposed and forced to commit suicide by King Zhao Sima Lun.

Queen Huiyang, named Xianrong, was established as queen in the first year of Tai'an but was deposed and restored multiple times amid political turmoil. After Emperor Hui's death, she attempted to install a different successor but failed. When Luoyang fell, she was taken by Liu Yao, who made her his queen. Mrs. Xie, named Xie Jiu, from a poor family, was selected as a talented person and sent to serve the prince, bearing Prince Minhuai. Empress Jia kept her isolated, and she was eventually killed.

The text concludes with brief accounts of Empress Dowager Huai, named Xie Tan, who died young and was posthumously honored, and the concubine of Marquis Yuanxia, named Guangji, who married into the Langye royal family and bore Emperor Yuan.

In the early years of Wuken, he and his elder brother were moved to Luzhou and were killed on the road.
The rebel army arose and he was given the posthumous title of Taichang Qing.
Cousin Chenzhi let his son Wenhui inherit the title.
After Song accepted the abdication, the feudal state was cancelled.
Han Yanzhi, named Xianzong, was from Zheyang, Nanyang, and was a descendant of Wei Situ Han Ji.
When he was young, he was known for his honor and loyalty.
At that time, Emperor An served as General Jianwei and Zhizhong of Jingzhou. He was transferred to Pingxi Prefecture to record affairs and join the army.
Because Liu Yu's father's name was Qiao, the character was Xianzong, so Yanzhi took the courtesy name Xianzong and named his son Qiao to show that he would not surrender to the Liu family.
He defected to Yao Xing with Xiuzhi.
Liu Yu entered the Pass and defected to Wei.
Sima Qing's courtesy name was King Jing, and he was initially named Guangjin Bo.
He died early and had no sons. His elder brother Sima Tian asked his son Yunzhi to inherit.
Sima Mu, King of Gaoyang, named Ziyou, was the younger brother of Sima Xun, King of Qiao.
In the Wei Dynasty, he was the Marquis of Anpingting and served successively as the imperial censor.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession and granted him the title of King of Zhongshan, granting him a fief of 5,200 households.
Sima Mu himself petitioned to build an ancestral temple according to Liu Liao's sacrifice to Gao Tao and Gao Qi's sacrifice to the prime minister.
The matter will be left to Taichang for review in accordance with etiquette.
Doctors offered wine to Liu Bang and others discussed: According to the "Book of Rites and Kingship", the princes set up five temples, two Zhao and two Mu, plus the Taizu temple, a total of five.
According to this, the temple of the ancestor is established, which refers to the inheritance of the direct line system, and one person can establish it.
If the brothers on the side branch are all princes, the first monarch who was granted the title cannot build a temple.
Nowadays, Sima Mu is not orthodox. If the ancestral temple is built, Zhongshan cannot be parallel.
Only the king of Zhongshan in later generations could build a temple for Sima Mu, as the ancestor of future generations.
The edict said: The provisions of the etiquette system are unclear. This is a major matter related to the system. It should be reviewed in detail and handed over to the etiquette officials for extensive discussion before handling the matter.
In the third year of Xianning, Sima Mu sent people to recruit more than 700 people who had migrated to eight counties in the country to accept the escape, privately owned and changed their names, and pretended to be exempted from corvee. Du You, the governor of Jizhou, reported to Sima Mu that he recruited people who were seduced and fled, and was not suitable to be the king of a country.
The relevant officials reported that the incident occurred before the amnesty and should be forgiven.
The edict said: How did King Zhongshan reach this point? Reading the memorial makes people confused.
Extensively appoint relatives, relying on them to assist the royal family on the upper side and provide favors to the people on the lower side.
Is it possible to make people violate the law just for the sake of glorifying Zhongda itself?
There should be an in-depth discussion of the pros and cons of any matter, as this is what distinguishes good things.
If it is not suitable to be the king of a country, why should we make judgments before and after the pardon order?
Sima Mu was demoted to county marquis.
So he was granted the title of Marquis of Danshui County.
After the Kingdom of Wu was pacified, Taikang issued an edict in the early years to restore his title.
The officials asked him to be crowned King of Jiangyang, and the emperor said: Sima Mu retreated to calmly think about his mistakes and re-cultivate his moral character. Now he has a title and land, not just because of the pardon.
Jiangyang was dangerous and far away, so Gaoyang County was granted to him.
So he was named King of Gaoyang.
In the first year of Yuankang, he was appointed Zongzheng.
He died in office, his eldest son Sima Wei died early, and his grandson Sima Yi succeeded to the throne.
He was promoted to Sanqi Shilang and died in Shile during the Yongjia period.
In the first year of Long'an, Shaoshu appointed Wen Shen, the son of Huizhi, the second son of Sima Tian, ​​King of Qiaojing, as Sima Yi's successor.
After five years on the throne, he died without any sons, and was succeeded by Fa Lian, the son of King Sima Chun of Gaomi.
Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled.
Sima Ling, King of Renchengjing, whose courtesy name was Zishan, was the son of Sima Tong, the younger brother of Emperor Xuan, Wei Sili, who was the Tinghou of Ancheng.
At first, the official paid homage to Yilang.
In the first year of Taishi, he was granted the title of King of Beihai and granted 4,700 households.
In the third year, he was transferred to the title of King of City and went to Fengguo.
Xianning died in the fifth year, and his son Sima Ji succeeded to the throne.
The official title is "Sanqi Shilang", "Gei Shizhong", "Sanqi Shilang", "Sanqi Changshilang", and "auxiliary general".
Following Sima Yue, king of Shuhai, in Xiangdi, he was killed by Shi Le, and his two sons died.
He has two younger brothers: Sima Shun and Sima Bin.
Sima Shun, whose courtesy name was Zisi, was initially named the Marquis of Xiyangting.
When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Sima Shun sighed and said: The matter is contrary to that of Lu and Yu, and it is in the name of abdication!
So he cried sadly.
Therefore, he was deposed and moved to Guzang County, Wuwei.
Although he was punished and exiled, he persisted in his views until his death.
Sima Bin, King Mu of Xihe, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, was the Zhonglang of Wei.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and granted him the title of King Chen, granting him a fief of 1,710 households.
Three years later, it was renamed Xihe.
Xianning died in the fourth year, and his son Yinli succeeded to the throne.
When Qian dies, his son inherits the throne.
Shi Chenri: In the early years of Taishi, there were few affairs in the world. We eliminated the shortcomings left by Wei Dynasty. We followed the old rules and established the clan together as a barrier to protect the country.
Those of the father's generation have the same nobility as Yu Cui, and the brothers enjoy the blessings of Lu and Jie. They think that the generations will last forever, and the authentic side branches will be passed down from generation to generation.
Anping's demeanor is majestic and elegant, and his utensils are elegant. He promotes morality internally and demonstrates loyalty externally.
When Duke Gaogui was killed, he would lie on the body and cry bitterly. When King Chenliu went to Jinyong City, he would kneel down and say goodbye, weeping in sorrow.
As the saying goes, "The strong wind knows the strong grass", which can be used to describe King Xian.
Therefore, he can be ranked among the top ministers, enjoy a long life, and be a model of extreme beauty. He is a talented person of the Jin clan. His descendants will follow his career and be loyal to his good deeds from generation to generation.
The King of Gaomi has a quiet and unconventional style, is simple and lacks desires. He flatters his relatives with filial piety and the court with loyalty. Compared with other side clansmen, it can be said that he is the pillar of the country.
King Xincai and King Nanyang both ruled one side.
It was a time when the royal family was in trouble and the central plains were desolate and blocked. It showed loyalty and integrity and made achievements in difficult and dangerous times.
At that time, there were too many evil people, and their evil power became more and more successful day by day. There was a huge disparity in power and insufficient manpower, so they perished one after another. How sad!
King Qiao Min was brave and resourceful and guarded the south.
At a time when evil spirits were causing wanton rebellion, they raised troops to bully the imperial court.
King Qiao Min worked hard with loyalty and raised righteousness in Xiangzhou. Jing Mian responded and many talents contributed.
Although there is no meritorious service, it shows loyalty and integrity and leaves the achievements to future generations. Isn’t it gratifying that generations of people have been loyal and virtuous!
Sima Xun was entrusted with the clan and had a violent nature.
Still carrying the trust of the imperial court, he was promoted to Liang Min, so he betrayed the king of his clan, failed to live up to his kindness and abandoned his order.
Relying on the wealth of mediocrity, he concealed his dissatisfaction; relying on the solidity of the country, the treacherous plot became deeper and deeper.
Therefore, the officials gnashed their teeth and vented their long-term dissatisfaction; the righteous men worked hard and sharpened their moral integrity.
The way of heaven brings disasters to evil and pacifies them at the right time.
In the past, when Ji An was still there, King Huainan put aside his plans. If Zhou Fu were alive, Sima Xun would not dare to cause trouble. Because evil scruples integrity, the same principle applies to different dynasties.
"Poetry" says that you leave sadness to yourself, and it is Sima Xun who you are talking about.
Marquis Xiyang Ting was blessed because he was born into a royal family. He remained frugal and reclusive. He put his emotions aside from the world. He admired and followed things beyond the world. He cared about being alone. He valued the principles of being knowledgeable and ethical. He should be lucky to be famous for his words.
Praise said: King Anping established integrity and had a noble character, loyal and wise.
King Gaomi had a harmonious heart and was a celebrity in the clan.
King Xincai was killed, but his loyalty was preserved at the cost of his life.
King Qiao Min died for justice, and he spread the word with all his strength and ambition.
Sima Xun asked for trouble, and his reputation was ruined and he died.
Sima Shun had no scruples and became famous far and wide.
summary:
Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's second brother. He was one of the "Bada" (Eight Talents) along with his brothers, known for their fame. Sima Fu was gentle, honest, upright, and widely read in classics. During the late Han Dynasty's turmoil, he maintained simple living while studying tirelessly. He was open-minded, tolerant, and held no grudges. When Yin Wu of Chenliu, a nationally known figure who had been punished, was visited by Sima Fu, they ate and lived together, earning praise.

Sima Fu served as literary director under Cao Zhi, King of Chensi, offering sincere advice that Cao Zhi eventually accepted. After Emperor Wu of Wei died, Sima Fu advised the crown prince against excessive mourning, emphasizing his responsibilities to the ancestral temple and feudal states. When ministers gathered weeping without forming a procession, Sima Fu sternly organized them, completed funeral arrangements, and supported the crown prince's ascension as Emperor Wen. During official selections, Sima Fu opposed nepotism, advocating for recruiting talented individuals nationwide.

When Sun Quan claimed vassalage to Wei but delayed sending hostages and returning Yu Jin, Sima Fu advised leniency, suggesting military preparation while observing developments. Yu Jin eventually returned, detained due to illness, but hostages never arrived. Sima Fu later served as Diannong in Hanoi, Marquis of Guannei, and Prefect of Qinghe. Emperor Ming appointed him Duzhi Shangshu, remarking he had "two Sima Yis." Sima Fu proposed preparing 20,000 infantry and cavalry as reserves against Zhuge Liang's invasions and stationed 5,000 farmers in Shangying for agricultural-military training, ensuring Guanzhong's surplus and defense readiness.

During Cao Shuang's corrupt regime, Sima Fu maintained rectitude and avoided harm. After Emperor Xuan executed Cao Shuang, Sima Fu was granted the title of Marquis of Changshe County and appointed Minister. When Wu general Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng, Sima Fu commanded 200,000 troops, deliberately delaying before advancing, causing the Wu army to flee. Regarding funeral flags for Wei Ming's mourning, Sima Fu argued against writing "Wei" or surnames, citing classical precedents, and his view prevailed.

Sima Fu served as Sikong, then Taiwei. When Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Longyou, Sima Fu guarded Guanzhong, and Jiang Wei withdrew. After Lord Gao Gui was killed, Sima Fu alone wept over his body, requesting investigation of the mastermind. He petitioned for royal burial rites, which were granted. Sima Fu was cautious, humble during Emperor Xuan's time, and uninvolved in monarch depositions. He was granted the title of Duke of Changle. When Emperor Wu accepted abdication and King Chenliu departed, Sima Fu bid farewell tearfully, vowing lifelong loyalty to Wei. He was made King of Anping with 40,000 households, later promoted to Dazai and Commander-in-Chief. Despite honors, Sima Fu remained unassuming and often sorrowful. Before death at age ninety-three, he ordered simple burial in ordinary clothes. The emperor mourned three days and provided lavish funeral gifts, though Sima Fu's family followed his wishes and used none.

Sima Fu had nine sons: Sima Yong, Sima Wang, Sima Fu, Sima Yi, Sima Huang, Sima Quan, Sima Gui, Sima Heng, and Sima Jing. Sima Yong died before his father. Sima Wang, adopted by his uncle Sima Lang, served as Prefect of Pingyang and Luoyang Diannong, followed Emperor Xuan against Wang Bo, and was named Yong'an Tinghou. He later served as General of Hussars and Situ. Emperor Wu made him King of Yiyang with 10,000 households. He was promoted to Taiwei, commanding troops against Wu invasions. He died at sixty-seven, known for frugality and money accumulation, leaving four sons.

Sima Hong, King of Hejian, was adopted by his uncle Sima Qian. He served as Diannong Zhonglang Jiang and Yuanwu Taishou, was made King of Hejian by Emperor Wu, and died after twelve years. Sima Wei, his son, succeeded but was later transferred to Zhangwu. Sima Wei flattered Sima Lun, king of Zhao, and served as Zhongshu Ling during Sima Lun's usurpation. After Sima Lun's failure, Emperor Hui ordered his execution. Sima Zheng died before his father Sima Wang and was posthumously named King of Sui County.

Sima Qiao, King of Jingling, was initially Marquis of Lelingting. Emperor Wu made him King Shuping. He was skilled at flattery, served Yang Jun, but avoided punishment after Yang Jun's execution due to connections. He later served as Dahonglu and Minister. During Sima Lun's usurpation, Sima Qiao was appointed General of the Guard. After Sima Lun's failure, he was dismissed. He later served as General of Chariots and Cavalry, but was defeated by Tian Hui and fled to his kingdom. Emperor Huai changed his title to King of Jingling. When Sima Yue became shepherd of Yuzhou, Sima Qiao attempted to attack him but failed. He escaped and was later killed by rebels when Luoyang fell.

Sima Fu became King of Taiyuan, then King of Bohai with 5,379 households. He served as Weiwei and Dongzhonglang General, later moved to King of Taiyuan, supervising Bingzhou's military affairs. He died in the fifth year of Taikang. His son Sima Hong succeeded him. Sima Huang, King of Xia Pi, was granted title by Wei, served as Huangmen Shilang and Prefect of Sechai. Emperor Wu made him King of Wu, then King of Xia Pi. He was filial, honest, and respected by the clan. He served as Changshui Captain and Nanzhonglang General, later as General of Zhendong. During Emperor Hui's reign, he served as General of Chariots and Cavalry. He died in the sixth year of Yuankang, posthumously awarded Taifu.

Sima Quan, King of Taiyuan, was Marquis of Changleting in Wei, later Marquis of Guishou Township. He served as General Zhenwei and Secretary Supervisor. Emperor Wu made him King of Taiyuan with 5,496 households. He was given Gun Mian attire and moved to General of Shu Zhonglang. He died after ten years, posthumously awarded General. His son Sima Ji succeeded him. Sima Gui, King of Gaoyang, was talented and famous young, served as Magistrate of Henan and Huangmen Shilang. Emperor Wu made him King of Gaoyang with 5,570 households. He served as General Beizhonglang, supervising Yecheng's military affairs. He died after ten years, posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. Since he had no son, Sima Zhouwei, son of King Sima Fu of Taiyuan, inherited the title.

Sima Heng, King of Changshan, was Marquis of Deyang Township in Wei, later Ruyangzi and Prince-in-law. Emperor Wu made him King of Changshan with 3,790 households. He died without sons, succeeded by Sima Yin, fourth son of Sima Yong. Sima Jing, King of Pei, was Le'anting Marquis of Wei, served as Admonishment Official. Emperor Wu made him King of Pei with 3,400 households. He died after eleven years, succeeded by his son Sima Tao.

Sima Quan, King Mu of Pengcheng, was son of Sima Kui, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He inherited the title and served as a servant. Emperor Wu made him King of Pengcheng with 2,900 households. He served as Beizhonglang General, died in the first year of Xianning, succeeded by his son Sima Zhi. Sima Zhi served as General, Minister of Wine, Imperial Servant, Minister, and General Anshu. He died of depression, posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry with 15,000 households. His son Sima Shi succeeded him, serving as General Nanzhonglang and General Pingnan. After his death, his son Sima Xiong succeeded but was killed for defecting to Su Jun. Sima Xian, son of Sima Shi, then succeeded.

Sima Xian, courtesy name Weide, was initially Duke of Tangyi County. Emperor Yuan succeeded him to Sima Ju, King of Gaomi. He served as Minister of Sanqi and Lieutenant of the Yi Army. After Sima Xiong's execution, Sima Xian returned to inherit his clan. He served as Prince of the Country, Wine Officer, and Sanqi Changshi. He suffered from madness, sometimes attacking military temples and officials. He was impeached but Emperor Cheng issued an edict allowing him to keep his position. He died in the eighth year of Xiankang, posthumously awarded Dr. Sanqi Changshi. He had two sons: Sima Xuan and Sima Jun. Sima Xuan succeeded him but hid five households, violating the Gengxu system. Huan Wen reported this, and Sima Xuan was arrested but later pardoned. He served as Minister of Zhongshu. After his death, his son Sima Hongzhi succeeded, then Sima Shao, then Sima Chongzhi, then Sima Ji. After Song accepted abdication, the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Jun, Prince Gong, was adopted by King Sima Lue of Gaomi, served as Sanqi Changshi. After his death, his son Sima Chunzhi succeeded, serving as Neishi of Linchuan and Minister of Shaofu. After his death, his son Sima Hui succeeded. In the last years of Yixi, he concurrently served as Taiwei. After Song accepted abdication, the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Tai, King of Gaomi, was younger brother of Sima Quan, King of Pengcheng. He was Marquis of Yangting in Wei, served as Prefect of Fufeng. Emperor Wu made him King of Longxi with 3,200 households, serving as Guerrilla General. He served as Governor of Yanzhou and General Yingyang, later as General Anxi and Governor of Yizhou, but claimed illness and did not go. He served as General Anbei, then General of Zhenxi. He died in the ninth year of Yuankang, posthumously awarded Taifu. Sima Tai was clean, quiet, not close to musical women, dressed and ate like ordinary people, filial and humble. Among the kings, only Sima Tai and Sima Huang, King of Xia Pi, were praised for self-control. He had four sons: Sima Yue, Sima Teng, Sima Lue, and Sima Mo.

Sima Lue, King Xiao, was filial and kind, treating wise men with caution and humility. He served as Minister of Sanqi Huangmen and Secretary Supervisor, later as General Annan and General Anbei. He threatened Governor Cheng Mu of Qingzhou and took charge himself. When Liu Gen raised troops, Sima Lue could not resist and defended Liaocheng. Emperor Huai moved him to Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou's military affairs. He defeated Wang Di's rebellion. He died in the third year of Yongjia, posthumously awarded Shizhong and Taiwei. His son Sima Ju succeeded him but died without sons. Sima Xian, son of King Kang of Pengcheng, succeeded, then returned to his clan, and Sima Xian's son Sima Jun became heir.

Sima Teng, King of Xincai, served as Prefect of Nanyang and Wei, competent in office. He was recruited as Zongzheng, moved to Taichang, then served as General Ningbei and Governor of Bingzhou. When Emperor Hui attacked Sima Ying, Sima Teng and Wang Jun defeated Sima Ying's forces. Sima Ying fled with the emperor to Luoyang. Sima Teng was promoted to General Anbei, later General of Chariots and Cavalry. He was renamed King Xincai. When Ji Sang and others rebelled, Sima Teng dismissed them as insignificant but was killed by Li Feng. Sima Teng had four sons: Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sima Shao, and Sima Que. Sima Teng was frugal and stingy, not giving relief to people, leading to disaster. His bones were not recovered. Sima Que succeeded him, served as General Dongzhonglang, guarded Xuchang, and was killed by Shi Le. He had no sons, so Sima Tao, son of Sima Hun, was asked to worship Sima Que, later Sima Bi, son of Sima Ku, succeeded. Sima Bi died without sons, succeeded by his brother Sima Miao. After his death, his son Sima Huang succeeded, but Huan Wen deposed him. Emperor Xiaowu established Sima Chong as heir. Song accepted abdication and the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Mo, King of Nanyang, was eager to learn young, famous with Emperor Yuan and Sima You. He was initially named Pingchang Gong. He served as Crown Prince's Concubine and Official Attendant. Sima Yue appointed him Beizhonglang General to guard Ye. He was promoted to King of Nanyang. During famine in Guanzhong, Sima Mo cast bronze vessels into cooking utensils for food, criticized by commentators. Sima Yue summoned him as Sikong, but Sima Mo refused, persuaded by Chun Yuding. He was promoted to Taiwei and Grand Governor. When Luo Jing fell, Sima Mo surrendered to Zhao Ran, who recited his crimes and sent him to Liu Can, who killed him. Sima Mo's son Sima Bao succeeded him.

Sima Bao, courtesy name Jingdu, was talented in literature. When Sima Mo was killed, Sima Bao was in Shangying. He controlled Qinzhou, appointed officials, and Di and Qiang people obeyed him. Emperor Min appointed him Right Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief. After Emperor Min's humiliation, Sima Bao claimed to be King of Jin. Famine struck Shangbang, and Zhang Chun escorted Sima Bao to Nan'an. Sima Bao died of illness at twenty-seven. He was tall, fat, weighed 800 jin, slept well but was impotent. Having no sons, Zhang Chun established Sima Zhan as successor. Chen An attacked Zhang Chun, Sima Zhan surrendered to Chen An, who sent him to Liu Yao, who killed him. Chen An buried Sima Bao with emperor's rites, posthumous title Yuan.

Sima Sui, King of Fanyang, was younger brother of Sima Quan, King of Pengcheng. He was initially an Admonishment Official, granted title in the first year of Taishi, reigned fifteen years, died in the fifth year of Xianning, succeeded by his son Sima Gai. Sima Gai was famous for studiousness, studied classics, good at speaking. He served as Sanqi Changshi, Minister, General Annan, guarding Xuchang, promoted to General Conquering the South. Sima Yong proposed appointing Wang Siyan. Sima Gai, Sima Liu, and Zhou Fu reported to the emperor about Sima Ying's failures and recommended Zhang Fang. They urged the emperor to give Guan You to Dazai and send Zhang Fang back to the county. Sima Gai led everyone from Xu to Rongyang to garrison. When Emperor Hui moved west, Sima Gai formed an alliance with Sima Mo and elected Sima Yue as leader. Liu Qiao attacked Xu, Sima Gai crossed the Yellow River, defeated Liu Qiao. Sima Ji killed Zhang Fang and sent his head to Sima Yue. Sima Gai escorted the emperor back to the capital, worshiped as Situ. He died at thirty-seven, no sons, adopted Sima Mo's son Sima Li, who was killed in Chang'an.

Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, was son of Sima Xun, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Guannei in Wei, promoted to Marquis of Qianchang Ting, served as Dianjunlang. In the second year of Jingyuan, he was granted title of Rural Marquis of Wucheng, Governor of Yecheng and General Beizhonglang. He was named Zhu Abo, moved to Champion General. Emperor Wu made him King of Jinan. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Dan and Sima Ji. Sima Dan succeeded, renamed King of Zhongshan, died without sons, Sima Ji succeeded. Sima Ji served as General Jianwei, fought against Wang Chuang, died in battle. Without sons, the feudal state was cancelled. Later, Sima Sui's great-grandson Sima Xun, named Wei Chang, was adopted by Liu Yao's general Linghu Ni. He returned from Guanyou in the sixth year of Xianhe, claimed to be Sima Xun's descendant, paid homage to Pu She. He served as Governor of Liangzhou, attacked Chang'an, captured Hecheng. Guanzhong responded to him. During the Yonghe period, he entered Chang'an, killed Zhang Ju, but was defeated by Fu Xiong. He was promoted to General Conquering the Captives, Marquis of Tongjiting. He was tyrannical, killing wealthy families who disagreed with him. He planned to occupy Shu territory. Huan Wen sent troops to attack him, Sima Xun was captured and killed.

Sima Xun, King of Qiao Gang, was son of Sima Jin, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Wei Guannei, granted title of Marquis of Yangting of Chengcheng, served as General Qingche and Zuojian Yulin. He was named Jingyang Nan. Emperor Wu made him King Qiao with 4,400 households. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Sui and Sima Cheng. Sima Sui succeeded, died in Shile. Emperor Yuan asked Sima to succeed him. Sima Cheng, King Min, was loyal and virtuous young. He served as General Guangwei and Protector of Anyi. He returned to Luoyang with Emperor Hui, became Guerrilla General. During Yongjia period, he secretly attached himself to Shan Jian. When Shan Jian died, he entered Wuchang. When Emperor Yuan guarded Yangzhou, Sima Cheng returned to Jiankang, served as Military Counselor and Wine Worshiper. Emperor Yuan changed his title to King Qiao. He served as Captain of Tunqi School, General of the Auxiliary State and Left Army. He was frugal, did not take concubines. When Wang Dun was disloyal, the emperor summoned Sima Cheng at night, showed him Wang Dun's memorial. Sima Cheng advised early action. The emperor appointed him to guard Xiangzhou. Sima Cheng traveled to Wuchang, saw Wang Dun unarmed. Wang Dun tested him but let him go to his post. Sima Cheng was frugal, rode a reed cart, comforted people, earned good reputation. Wang Dun feared him, requisitioned his ships. When Wang Dun rebelled, Sima Cheng raised righteous deeds, but the city fell after more than a hundred days. Wei Yi sent him to Jingzhou, where Wang Yu killed him on the way at fifty-nine. After Wang Dun was pacified, Sima Cheng was posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. His son Wuji succeeded him.

Sima Wuji, King Lie, escaped when young during Sima Cheng's trouble. He served as Sanqi Shilang, moved to Tunqi Xiaowei and Zhongshu. He tried to kill Wang Yu's son Qizhi for revenge but was stopped. The emperor pardoned him. He served as Sanqi Changshi and Censor Zhongcheng, then General of the Auxiliary State and Prime Minister of Changsha. He followed Dandan in expedition against Shu, given title of Duke Guangzhi. He died in the sixth year of Cheng Mian, posthumously awarded General Wei. He had two sons: Sima Tian and Sima Qing. Sima Tian succeeded him.

Sima Tian, King Jing, served as Sanqi Shilang, Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng. When Duke Haixi was deposed, Sima Tian impeached Grand Sima Xun for disrespect. The emperor sighed at his courage. Sima Tian was loyal, upright, talented, feared by officials. He served as General of the Right Guard, Shangshu, Shizhong, and General of the Left Guard. He was appointed Domestic History of Wu and Prince Zhanshi. Emperor Xiaowu relied on him heavily, appointed him Military Governor of several states and General of Zhenbei. He died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. He had four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi, and Xiuzhi. Shangzhi succeeded him.

Sima Shangzhi, King Zhong, served as Secretary-General and Sanqi Shilang. He guarded Jingkou as General Zhenwei and Prime Minister Guangling. After his father's death, he served as Hussar Consultant. Within the clan, outstanding figures appeared generation after generation. When Wang Guobao was executed, Shangzhi advised King Daozi of Kuaiji to release Liu Zhenzhi and others. Daozi obeyed. Wang Gong, Governor of Yanzhou, jealous of Shangzhi's power, raised troops with Yu Kai and others. Daozi ordered Shangzhi to resist Yu Kai. Shangzhi defeated Yu Kai's forces. Daozi appointed Shangzhi as General Jianwei and Governor of Yuzhou. Shangzhi's power surpassed others. Later, Yuan Xian came to power and relied on him. Shangzhi scolded Yuan Xian's favorite Zhang Fashun, earning Yuan Xian's resentment. When Yuan Xian attacked Huan Xuan, Shangzhi was ordered to be vanguard. Huan Xuan attacked, Shangzhi's army collapsed, and Huan Xuan had Shangzhi killed. The emperor posthumously awarded General Wei to Shangzhi. His cousin Kangzhi was renamed King of Qiao County. Later, Wensi, Xiuzhi's eldest son, succeeded Shangzhi but was cruel and rebellious. Liu Yu killed him, and the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Huizhi served as Commander of Hsiao Cavalry and Danyang Yin. After Shangzhi was killed, Huan Xuan moved Huizhi and others to Guangzhou, killing them on the way. Emperor An posthumously awarded him General Fujun. Sima Xiuzhi served as General Longxiang and Governor of Xiangcheng. When Shangzhi was defeated, Xiuzhi fought hard but failed, then joined Murong Chao. He returned to the capital hearing of the rebel army's rise. He was appointed to supervise military affairs of six states and serve as Governor of Jingzhou. Huan Zhen attacked Jiangling, Xiuzhi was defeated and fled to Xiangyang. He returned to his post but was later relieved. He served as General of the Empress and Internal Secretary of Kuaiji. He was demoted for violating the ban. When Lu Xun rebelled, he was appointed military commander. He was dismissed due to official crimes. Later, he was appointed Governor of Jingzhou. Because his son Wensi made trouble, Xiuzhi apologized and asked to be relieved. The emperor forbade it. Later, Xiuzhi colluded with Lu Zongzhi to kill those in power. Liu Yu personally conquered Xiuzhi. Xiuzhi was defeated and defected to Yao Xing with Zongzhi. Liu Yu pacified Yao Hong, and Xiuzhi defected to Wei but died on the road.

Sima Yunzhi passed to his uncle Sima Qing, inherited the title of Guangjin Bo, served as General of the Auxiliary State. When Wang Gong, Yu Kai, and Huan Xuan conquered the country, Yunzhi's brothers resisted but were defeated. He and his elder brother were moved to Luzhou and killed on the road. The rebel army arose, and he was posthumously awarded Taichang Qing. His cousin Chenzhi let his son Wenhui inherit the title. After Song accepted abdication, the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Mu, King of Gaoyang, was younger brother of Sima Xun, King of Qiao. In Wei, he was Marquis of Anpingting, served as Imperial Censor. Emperor Wu made him King of Zhongshan with 5,200 households. Sima Mu petitioned to build an ancestral temple according to Liu Liao's sacrifice to Gao Tao. The matter was left to Taichang for review. Doctors offered wine to Liu Bang and others discussed the etiquette. The edict said the provisions were unclear and should be reviewed. In the third year of Xianning, Sima Mu recruited more than 700 migrants, and Du You, Governor of Jizhou, reported him. The relevant officials said the incident occurred before amnesty and should be forgiven. The emperor demoted Sima Mu to Marquis of Danshui County. After Wu was pacified, the edict restored his title. He was named King of Gaoyang. In the first year of Yuankang, he was appointed Zongzheng. He died in office, his eldest son Sima Wei died early, and his grandson Sima Yi succeeded. Sima Yi served as Sanqi Shilang, died in Shile during Yongjia period. In the first year of Long'an, Wen Shen, son of Huizhi, second son of Sima Tian, was appointed as Sima Yi's successor. He died without sons after five years, succeeded by Fa Lian, son of King Sima Chun of Gaomi. Song accepted abdication and the feudal state was cancelled.

Sima Ling, King of Renchengjing, was son of Sima Tong, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Tinghou of Ancheng. Initially, he served as Yilang. In the first year of Taishi, he was granted title of King of Beihai with 4,700 households. In the third year, he was transferred to King of City. He died in the fifth year of Xianning, succeeded by his son Sima Ji. Sima Ji served as Sanqi Shilang and Auxiliary General. Following Sima Yue, King of Shuhai, in Xiangdi, he was killed by Shi Le, and his two sons died. He had two younger brothers: Sima Shun and Sima Bin. Sima Shun, courtesy name Zisi, was initially Marquis of Xiyangting. When Emperor Wu accepted abdication, Sima Shun sighed and cried sadly, saying the matter was contrary to Lu and Yu. He was deposed and moved to Guzang County, Wuwei. He persisted in his views until death. Sima Bin, King Mu of Xihe, was Zhonglang of Wei. Emperor Wu made him King Chen with 1,710 households. Three years later, it was renamed Xihe. He died in the fourth year of Xianning, succeeded by his son Yinli. When Yinli died, his son succeeded.

The historical commentary notes that in the early years of Taishi, the clan was established as a barrier to protect the country. Anping's demeanor was majestic and elegant, promoting morality internally and demonstrating loyalty externally. When Duke Gaogui was killed, he wept bitterly. When King Chenliu went to Jinyong City, he bid farewell tearfully. He could be ranked among top ministers, enjoy a long life, and be a model of extreme beauty. The King of Gaomi had a quiet style, simple and without desires, filial to relatives and loyal to the court. King Xincai and King Nanyang both ruled one side. During the royal family's trouble, they showed loyalty and made achievements in difficult times. King Qiao Min was brave and resourceful, guarding the south. When evil spirits rebelled, he raised righteousness in Xiangzhou. Although without meritorious service, he showed loyalty and left achievements to future generations. Sima Xun was entrusted with the clan but had a violent nature, betraying the king and failing to live up to kindness. His treacherous plot deepened, and he was eventually pacified. Marquis Xiyang Ting was frugal and reclusive, putting emotions aside from the world, valuing the principles of being knowledgeable and ethical.

Lithos
Wang Xiang, whose courtesy name was Xiuzheng, was born in Linyi, Langye, and was a descendant of Wang Ji, an admonishing official of the Han Dynasty.
His grandfather, Wang Ren, was the governor of Qingzhou.
His father, Wang Rong, was recruited by the government, but he refused to become an official.
Wang Xiang is very filial by nature.
His mother died when he was young, and his stepmother Zhu was not loving and spoke ill of him many times, thus losing his father's love.
Wang Xiang is often asked to clean the cattle pen, and Wang Xiang is more respectful and cautious.
When his parents were ill, he couldn't take off his clothes, so he had to taste the medicine himself first.
His stepmother once wanted to eat live fish. It was freezing cold at that time. Wang Xiang took off his clothes and was about to break the ice to catch fish. The ice suddenly cracked on its own and two carps jumped out. He took the fish home.
Stepmother wants to eat roasted oriole again. Dozens more orioles flew into his tent and took them to his stepmother.
The villagers were amazed and thought it was caused by the influence of filial piety.
There was a red sand fruit tree bearing fruit, and his stepmother ordered him to guard it. Whenever there was wind or rain, Wang Xiang would hug the tree and cry.
His filial piety reaches such an extent.
During the war at the end of the Han Dynasty, he supported his mother and took his younger brother Wang Lan to escape to Lujiang. They lived in seclusion for more than 20 years and refused to accept appointments from prefectures and counties.
When her mother passed away, she became ill due to grief and could only stand with a cane.
Lu Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, asked him to be his guest. Wang Xiang, who was nearly sixty years old, resolutely refused to accept the offer.
Wang Lan persuaded him and prepared an ox cart for him. Only then did Wang Xiang answer the call, and Lu Qian handed over the affairs of the state to him.
At that time, there were robbers and thieves everywhere. Wang Xiang led and encouraged the soldiers to defeat the enemy many times.
The state is peaceful and peaceful, and political decrees and enlightenment are passed unimpeded.
People at that time sang: Haiyi's happiness really depends on Wang Xiang.
The fact that the feudal country is not poor is due to others.
Wang Xiang was recommended as a scholar, appointed as Wen Ling, and promoted to Da Sinong many times.
Gaogui Xianggong ascended the throne, participated in the planning and made meritorious services, and was named Guannei Marquis. His official title was Guang Luxun, and he was transferred to Sili Xiaowei.
Following his attack on his mother Qiu Jian, he increased his residence by 400 households, was promoted to Taichang, and was granted the title of Marquis of Wansui Ting.
The emperor came to the Imperial Academy and ordered Wang Xiang to be the third elder.
Wang Xiang faces south, leaning on several tables and holding a walking stick, and considers himself a teacher.
The emperor asked for advice from the north, and Wang Xiang taught him the key points of political education for emperors and ministers of the Ming Dynasty. Everyone who heard this was inspired.
When the noble countryman was killed, the ministers of the court held a mourning ceremony. Wang Xiang cried and said, "The old minister has no face to see others." His nose burst into tears and everyone looked ashamed.
Soon after, he was promoted to Sikong, and was transferred to Taiwei, and then to Shizhong.
He was awarded the fifth-class title and was named Suiling Marquis, with a settlement of 1,600 households.
When Emperor Wen became the king of Jin, Wang Xiang and Xun Pin went to see him. Xunjie said to Wang Xiang: "The Prime Minister respects his position. He Hou has already respected him, so he should kneel down and worship him now."
Wang Xiang said: The prime minister is indeed noble, but he is the prime minister of Wei.
We are the three princes of the Wei State. The difference between the prince and the king is only one level, and the ranks are the same. How can the three princes of the emperor be bowed to others easily?
It damages the prestige of the Wei Dynasty and the reputation of the King of Jin. A gentleman treats others with courtesy, so I will not bow down.
After entering, Xunjie knelt down and worshiped, while Wang Xiang performed a long salute alone.
Emperor Wen said: Today I know the reason why you are appreciated!
When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he granted Wang Xiang the title of Taibao, promoted him to the title of Duke, and granted him the powers of seven additional officials.
Not long after Emperor Wu came to the throne, he humbly sought out honest opinions.
Wang Xiang, He Zeng, Zheng Chong and other senior ministers wished to see him again, so the emperor sent Ren Kai, an aide-de-camp, to inquire about the gains and losses and the primary measures for political enlightenment.
Wang Xiang requested to retire many times on the grounds of old age and frailty, but the emperor refused.
The censor, Zhongcheng Hou Shiguang, requested that Wang Xiang be removed from his official position on the grounds that Wang Xiang had been ill for a long time and could not attend court.
The emperor issued an edict saying: The Taibao is an experienced official with high qualifications and high virtues, and I rely on him to govern.
I have not complied with his wishes despite humility and concessions many times before and after. This is not something that officials can discuss.
So the memorial of Bao Huangguang was withheld.
Xingmang firmly requested to resign and issued an edict to allow Duke Suiling to return to his residence. His official position was the same as that of Baofu. He was above the three divisions and his salary was the same as before.
The edict said: People in ancient times retired and no longer served princes.
Now, although he is staying in the capital as the Duke of the country, he should not be made to suffer any more hardships due to court invitations.
Give him a cane for several cases, so you don't have to go to court. Ask him for advice on important matters.
He was given a chariot and four horses, a house, one million dollars, five hundred pieces of silk, beds and mats, six housekeepers named Suiling Gong's housekeepers, and twenty officers and cavalrymen.
Wang Zhao, Wang Xiang's son, the Cavalry Commander, was appointed to serve as a minister, so that he would always have time to pay respects to Wang Xiang.
Because Taibao was of high moral character and did not have a house at home, he temporarily stayed in the house until the house given to him was completed before moving out.
When he was critically ill, he wrote a will to instruct his descendants: "Within life comes death. This is a natural principle."
I am eighty-five years old, what regrets do I have when I die?
Failure to leave any last words will leave you with nothing to follow.
I was born in the last days and was selected for important positions. I had no meritorious service and could not repay it after I died.
After dying, you only need to wash your hands and feet. You don’t need to take a bath. You don’t need to wrap your body around your body. You only need to wear old clothes you find in the wash and wear them according to the season.
Do not put the Shanxuan jade pendant, Wei jade piece, and ribbon that were given to me into a coffin.
The soil on Ximang is inherently solid and clean, so there is no need for bricks, stones or grave mounds.
The pit should be dug two feet deep and the coffin should be large enough to hold the coffin.
It is not necessary to build a front hall, set up a sacrificial feast, set up bookcases, mirrors, etc. Just set up a bed in front of the coffin.
A plate of dry food and dried meat, and a cup of black wine, as a morning and evening memorial.
Family members do not need to be buried, only special sacrifices are held on the anniversary and second anniversary.
Don't disobey my orders!
Gao Chai cried for three years, and Confucius said he was stupid.
Minzi took off his mourning clothes and came out to meet people. He played the harp sadly, and Confucius said he was filial.
Therefore, the expression of sorrow by crying decreases with the passage of time, and the sacrifice of food and drink has its own system.
Being consistent in words and deeds is the pinnacle of faith; giving a good reputation to others while shouldering the blame yourself is the pinnacle of virtue; spreading a good reputation to make relatives famous is the pinnacle of filial piety; brotherly harmony and clan rejoicing are the pinnacle of brotherhood; there is nothing better than humility in the face of property: these five principles are the foundation of a good life.
The remarks made by Yan Zi were not thought through and are not far from these five points.
The sons were ordered to do so.
When Taishi died in the fourth year, an edict was issued to give the nobles a coffin, a set of court clothes, a set of clothes, three hundred thousand money, and one hundred pieces of cloth.
It had just been a month since the death of Empress Dowager Wenming. After this, Xia Shaoshu said: I express my condolences to Duke Sui, and the matter has been postponed until today.
Although I often feel sad for him, I never express my sorrow specifically.
Cry him today.
In the second year, he was granted the title Yuan.
When Wang Xiang passed away, the mourners were either wise ministers in the court, relatives or former officials. There were no idle mourning guests in the house.
Wang Rong, the grandson of the family, sighed and said: The Taibao can be said to be honest and open-minded!
He also said: During the Zhengshi period, Wang Xiang was not among the celebrities who were good at speaking.
When talking to him, the truth is fresh and profound. Isn't it because his virtues cover up his kind words?
Wang Xiang had five sons: Wang Zhao, Wang Xia, Wang Fu, Wang Lie, and Wang Fen.
Wang Zhao was a concubine, Wang Xia died early, and Wang Fu inherited the title.
In the early years of Xianning, because Wang Xiang's family was very poor, he was given 300 pieces of silk and appointed Wang Fu as the prefect of Shangluo. After his death, he was named Xiao.
His son Wang Gen inherited the title and was appointed Sanqi Lang.
From Wang Zhaogong to Shiping, he was the prefect.
Wang Zhao's son Wang Jun was appointed Prince Sheren and was granted the title of Eternal Marquis.
Wang Jun's son Wang Xia was appointed as the governor of Yulin.
Wang Lie and Wang Fen both became famous when they were young and were loved by Wang Xiang.
The two sons died at the same time.
When he was about to die, Wang Lie wanted to be buried in his hometown, and Wang Fen wanted to be buried in the capital.
Wang Xiang said with tears: Not forgetting your hometown is benevolence; not being nostalgic for your homeland is broad-minded.
Ren and Da, our two sons are ready.
Wang Lan's courtesy name is Xuantong.
His mother, Mrs. Zhu, treated Wang Xiang unkindly.
When Wang Lan was a few years old, he cried and hugged Wang Xiang when he saw Wang Xiang being beaten by a branch.
As an older child, he often remonstrated with his mother, who somewhat restrained her cruelty.
Zhu repeatedly drove Wang Xiang unreasonably, so Wang Lan went with Wang Xiang.
He also tortured and instigated Wang Xiang's wife, and Wang Lan's wife also did the same.
When Mr. Zhu had concerns, he gave up sending his talents.
After the death of his father, Wang Xiang gradually gained reputation.
Zhu was deeply jealous and secretly poisoned Wang Xiang with poisonous wine.
Wang Lan found out about this and got up to get the wine.
Wang Xiang suspected that the wine was poisonous and fought for it but refused to give it to him. Zhu quickly grabbed the wine and poured it away.
After that, Zhu gave Wang some food, and Wang Lan tasted it first.
Zhu was afraid that Wang Lan would be poisoned first, so he gave up.
Wang Lan has a lower reputation than Wang Xiang in terms of filial piety, kindness and respect.
When Wang Xiang became an official, Wang Lan also responded to the call from the county and was gradually promoted to Situ Xicao and Qinghe prefect.
After being awarded the fifth-class title, he was named Jiqiuzi and was granted a settlement of 600 households.
In the last years of Taishi's reign, he was appointed as the Shaofu of Hongxun.
After serving in the province, he was transferred to Taizhong doctor, and his salary and reward were the same as those of the minister.
In the early years of Xianning, Xia Shao wrote: Wang Lan had good conduct since he was a child, and he was benevolent and righteous in his work. His chaste conduct became more stable as he grew older.
Wang Lan was appointed Zong Zhengqing.
Soon, he submitted a letter requesting to resign on the grounds of illness.
Xia Shaoshu agreed that he would return to his old age as a Taizhong doctor, give him two hundred thousand yuan, a bed tent and a mattress, and send palace doctors to treat his illness and deliver medicine.
Later, he became a doctor of Guanglu, and a wooden frame was set up in front of the door to block the passage of people and horses.
He died in the fourth year of Xianning at the age of seventy-three, and his nickname was Zhen.
He has six sons: Wang Cai, Wang Ji, Wang Hui, Wang Zheng, Wang Yan and Wang Chen.
Wang Cai, whose courtesy name was Shichu, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of the Fu Army.
Wang Ji's courtesy name was Shixian, and he was appointed as the Censor of Zhishu.
Wang Hui's courtesy name was Shihe, and he was appointed as the censor.
Wang Zheng, courtesy name Shize, was appointed Shangshulang.
Wang Yan, nicknamed Shizhi, was appointed as the Central Guard.
Wang Chen, whose courtesy name was Shiwei, was appointed as the son of the state to offer wine.
At first, Lu Qian had a sword. The craftsman looked at it and thought that it must be someone who was in the position of Sangong and could wear this sword.
Lu Qian said to Wang Xiang: If it were not so, this sword might be a disaster.
You have the courage of a public servant, so I will give you the knife.
Wang Xiang firmly refused, but Lu Qian insisted that he accept.
Before Wang Xiang died, he handed the sword to Wang Lan and said: Your descendants will be prosperous enough to match this sword.
Wang Lan's descendants had many talented people from generation to generation and prospered in Jiangzuo.
There is another biography in this book about Wang Cai's son Wang Dao.
Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was born in Kaifeng, Rongyang.
He was born in a poor and humble background, and established moral integrity beyond ordinary people. He was quiet and had few desires. He loved to ponder the classics and history, and he had extensive research on Confucianism and hundreds of schools of thought.
He has good looks and good reputation, must follow etiquette in his actions, be sincere and self-responsible, and does not seek the reputation of his hometown people. Therefore, the state and county did not discover his talent for a long time.
When Emperor Wen of Wei was the crown prince, he searched for and promoted lowly talents, appointed Zheng Chong as the literary minister, and was promoted to Shangshulang many times. He also went to Beijing to replace Chenliu as the prefect.
Zheng Chong regards elegance as his virtue. He does not have the reputation of being talented or magnanimous in his position. He only needs food and clothing and does not seek wealth. The world values ​​him for this.
General Cao Shuang recommended him to serve as a lieutenant, and then he was promoted to a regular attendant of Sanqi and Guang Luxun.
In the third year of Jiaping's reign, he was appointed Sikong.
When the Duke of Gaogui was giving lectures on Shangshu, Zheng Chong took the scriptures and taught them in person, and was rewarded together with his attendant Zheng Xiaotong.
Soon he was transferred to Situ.
Chang Daoxiang came to the throne and appointed him as Taibao, ranking above the three divisions, and named him Shouguang Hou.
Although Zheng Chong's official rank is the same as that of prime minister, he does not interfere in world affairs.
At that time, Emperor Wen assisted the government and after pacifying the Shu Kingdom, he ordered Jia Chong, Yang Hu and others to formulate etiquette and legal regulations respectively. They all asked Zheng Chong first and then implemented them.
When Emperor Wei announced his abdication, he sent Zheng Chong to present the policy letter.
Emperor Wu ascended the throne, appointed him as Taifu, and promoted him to Duke.
Soon, Si Li Yi and Zhong Cheng Hou Shi Guang wrote a letter saying that Zheng Chong, He Zeng, Xun Hao and others should be relieved of their official positions due to illness.
The emperor did not allow it.
Zheng Chong then stopped dealing with political affairs and asked to resign.
He issued an edict to dissuade him with good words, and sent someone to explain.
Zheng Chong resolutely refused and handed over Diao Chan's seal ribbon, but the edict did not allow it.
In the sixth year of Taishi, Xia Shao Shu said: In the past, the emperor of the Han Dynasty was able to pacify the world by relying on his knowledge of people and his good deeds. He traced his merits and attributed his good name to the three heroes.
So he made an oath with the meritorious ministers to collect Fu Jiefeng and kept it in the ancestral temple, and the copy was left in the relevant departments, so as to show his virtue and appoint meritorious service, thereby protecting the auxiliary royal family.
In the past, my ancestors encountered difficulties in the world, recruited and appointed talented people, and worked with them to achieve worldly things and establish the great cause of the country.
The Grand Tutor Shouguang Gong Zheng Chong, the Taibao Langling Gong He Zeng, and the Taiwei Linhuai Gong Xun Hao each advocated virtue, benevolence and righteousness, were wise, fair and loyal, assisted the late emperor and prospered the emperor's career.
The former Sikong Bo Ling Yuan Gong Wang Shen and Wei General Ju Ping Hou Yang Hu were talented in both civil and military affairs, and they were loyal, respectful and upright. I admire them very much.
Didn't "Shang Shu" say: The order of heaven is polite, and the five levels of clothing and color are used to distinguish the superior and the inferior!
He appointed Langzhongling for Shouguang, Langling, Linhuai, Boling and Juping, gave seals to his wife and prince, and received one-third of the original official salary. Everything was like a prince in a county.
In the ninth year, Zheng Chong went out to resign again.
The edict said: The Taifu contains virtues, noble conduct, and is extraordinary. He is truly unparalleled in the world.
He has been involved in royal affairs for more than sixty years and is loyal to the public and does not consider personal gain.
According to everyone's recommendation, he once ascended to the position of Sangong.
He is still responsible for the important task of protecting the emperor, diligently discussing Taoism, and assisting generation after generation. He has completed the responsibilities entrusted by God, contributed strategies, and achieved great achievements. He can be said to be an outstanding veteran in the court and a person respected by everyone.
I am ignorant about politics, and many things have not been done yet. I rely on the advice of my old ministers to enlighten me. I hope that by relying on the virtue of my ministers, great things can be done.
However, the Duke resigned from his post many times on the grounds of old age and serious illness.
If I follow the Duke's wishes, then who should I ask for advice?
It’s like crossing a river on foot and not knowing where to get into the water.
So I didn't allow it, and it's been several years now.
However, my desire to resign became more and more determined, and it was difficult to go against my sincere intentions. Looking at his good intentions, I felt disappointed.
It is a sign of a noble person to accomplish something without enjoying it. Fulfilling the good deeds of others is what a gentleman should do.
Do you have to obey my wish to rely on dependence and violate the request of a talented and virtuous person to resign?
Now he obeys his wishes and returns to the mansion as Duke Shouguang. His status is like that of Taibao Taifu, above the three divisions.
Gong should maintain his spirit and maintain the harmony of yin and yang in order to enjoy his life.
I was given a cane for several cases, so I didn't have to go to court.
The sage kings of ancient times admired and respected the senior ministers of the country, imitated their actions, and solicited their opinions to make up for their shortcomings.
If there is any important matter in the court, go and ask them.
He was also given four chariots and horses, a house, one million coins, five hundred pieces of silk, beds and mats, six servants, and twenty cavalry. The eldest son Zheng Hui was appointed as a regular attendant of Sanqi, so that he would always have free time to pay respects to Zheng Chong.
Salaries, rewards and supplies, as well as orders and ritual systems, are all more comprehensive according to the old regulations.
He died the following year.
The emperor expressed his condolences in the court hall and posthumously presented Zheng Chong as Taifu. He also gave the nobles a coffin, court robes, a set of clothes, 300,000 yuan, and 100 pieces of cloth.
Mi Hao succeeded.
In the early years of Xianning, relevant officials reported that Zheng Chong, Anping King Sima Fu and other twelve people set up inscriptions in Taichang Temple and attached sacrifices in the temple.
At the beginning, Zheng Chong, together with Sun Yong, Cao Xi, Xun Hao and He Yan, collected various commentaries on "The Analects of Confucius", selected the good ones and recorded their names, followed their opinions, and changed the comments where inappropriate, which was called "Collected Commentary of the Analects of Confucius".
After the book was completed, it was reported to the Wei Dynasty and has been passed down to this day.
Zheng Chong had no sons, so his nephew Zheng Hui inherited the title and became an official in Pingyuan Neishi.
When Zheng Hui died, his son Zheng Jian inherited the title.
He Zeng, courtesy name Yingkao, was born in Yangxia, Chen State.
His father, He Kui, was the Taipu of Wei and the Marquis of Yangwu Ting.
He Zeng inherited the title when he was young. He was eager to learn and knowledgeable, and had a reputation with Yuan Kan from the same county.
Emperor Wei Ming was originally a Marquis of Pingyuan, but he was not a literary scholar.
When the emperor came to the throne, he was promoted many times to the positions of Minister of Sanqi, General of Diannong in Jijun, and Minister of Huangmen in Guishi.
He Zeng Shangshu said: I heard that the rule of the country is based on tranquility, and the people based on good officials.
Nowadays, the world is empty and depleted, and there are many corvees. We should be considerate of the people and make them happy to pay taxes.
Although the power of the county governor is light, he is in charge of thousands of miles of territory. Compared with ancient times, he is the king of all countries.
To those above, one should respectfully and publicize the court's grace in order to gain harmony, while to those below, one should promote benefits and eliminate harm.
If you employ people appropriately, you will have stability; if you employ them inappropriately, you will have disaster.
Therefore, Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty said: The reason why the people can live and work in peace and contentment without any resentment is because the politics are fair and the litigation is reasonable.
The people who started my business with me relied on those good officials with a salary of two thousand dan!
This can actually be said to be the foundation of knowing how to govern.
Nowadays, the country vigorously recruits talents, and there are often dispatches and transfers, military expeditions, and hard work.
The people can enjoy success with the court, but it is difficult to think about the beginning together.
Foolish people can be satisfied with the current small hardships and forget about the big disasters that cause turmoil. Therefore, the county governor cannot appoint inappropriate people.
It is difficult to find talented people, so it is better to use people who are a little dignified and trusted and respected by the people.
I heard that some county guards, some of whom are old or sick, leave political affairs to their subordinate officials and do not worry about political affairs.
Some people are lazy by nature and do not take government affairs to heart.
He has been in office for many years and has not been kind to the people.
However, when officials are evaluated, they will not be dismissed if they commit crimes.
Therefore, he can go year after year without being dismissed.
I think we can secretly send people in charge to secretly examine and inspect the county governors. Those who are too old and sick to be in charge, and those who lack grace among the officials and like to engage in personal affairs and annoy the people can be recalled to Beijing and replaced by replacements.
Soon, he was promoted to a regular attendant of Sanqi.
When Emperor Xuan was about to attack Liaodong, he went to Emperor Wei and said: I heard that the former king must be cautious and thorough when formulating laws and regulations.
Therefore, when officials are appointed, deputy assistants are set up; when generals are dispatched, deputy posts are set up to supervise the army; when orders are announced and envoys are dispatched, deputies are set up; when fighting the enemy, a right guard is set up, all for the purpose of careful planning and preventing changes in safety.
Therefore, in times of danger and difficulty, the powers are sufficient to restrict each other; in the event of injuries or shortages, they are sufficient to provide substitutes.
Construction has far-reaching significance for national defense.
In the Han Dynasty, the old rules were also followed. When Han Xin conquered Han, his 丸 was his deputy; when a donkey conquered Han, his legs were his deputy.
The events of past lives are written in history books.
Now the Taiwei is ordered to punish the criminals. The soldiers are brave and have sharp weapons. There are tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry. The road is winding and dangerous, and it is four thousand miles long.
Although with the power of God, there is no battle, the enemy may abscond and kill time.
There is no fixed date for military orders, and people are not gold and stones. For comprehensive and far-reaching considerations, there should be a deputy position.
Nowadays, the generals of the Northern Army and the people led by the Taiwei are all subordinates, and there is no difference in their status. They have never had the status and the prestige of commanding the army. Suddenly, there is an emergency and they cannot control them.
It is the decision of a sage king to worry about defeat when you win.
I think we should select the most prestigious ministers and veterans among the famous ministers and generals, arrange their official positions, and send them to the Northern Army to plan the advance together and retreat as their deputies.
Even if something unexpected happens, the army commander will still have a deputy position, so there will be no worries.
The emperor did not listen.
He left the capital to serve as the governor of Hanoi, and had a majestic reputation in office.

summary:
Wang Xiang, courtesy name Xiuzheng, was from Linyi, Langye, a descendant of Han official Wang Ji. His grandfather Wang Ren served as Qingzhou governor, while his father Wang Rong refused government service. Wang Xiang was exceptionally filial. After his mother died young, his stepmother Zhu treated him poorly and spoke ill of him, causing his father to lose affection for him. Despite being ordered to clean cattle pens, Wang Xiang remained respectful. When his parents fell ill, he personally tasted their medicine. During freezing weather, his stepmother desired live fish; Wang Xiang removed his clothes to break ice, and two carps leaped out spontaneously. When she wanted roasted oriole, dozens flew into his tent. Villagers attributed these events to his filial piety. During late Han warfare, he supported his mother and younger brother Wang Lan while hiding in Lujiang for over twenty years, refusing official appointments. After his mother's death, he became ill from grief. At nearly sixty, he initially refused Governor Lu Qian's invitation but eventually accepted after Wang Lan's persuasion. He defeated bandits, brought peace to the state, and was praised in song. Wang Xiang held various official positions including Wen Ling, Da Sinong, and was named Guannei Marquis. He served as Sili Xiaowei, Taichang, and Marquis of Wansui Ting. The emperor appointed him as third elder at the Imperial Academy, where he taught political education. He was promoted to Sikong, Taiwei, and Shizhong, eventually becoming Suiling Marquis with 1,600 households. When Emperor Wen became King of Jin, Wang Xiang refused to kneel, stating that as a Wei official, he would not bow to others. Emperor Wu appointed him Taibao and promoted him to Duke. Despite repeated retirement requests due to age, the emperor refused, granting him privileges including exemption from court attendance. Upon critical illness, Wang Xiang instructed his descendants on simple burial, forbidding elaborate ceremonies and expensive items. He died in the fourth year of Taishi at age eighty-five. His sons included Wang Zhao, Wang Xia, Wang Fu, Wang Lie, and Wang Fen.

Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was from Kaifeng, Rongyang. Born poor, he established moral integrity, was quiet with few desires, and extensively studied Confucian classics. He followed etiquette strictly and did not seek local fame. Emperor Wen of Wei appointed him literary minister, later promoting him to Shangshulang and Chenliu prefect. He valued elegance over wealth, earning respect. Cao Shuang recommended him as lieutenant, then Sanqi Changshi and Guang Luxun. In Jiaping's third year, he became Sikong, later Situ. He was appointed Taibao and named Shouguang Hou. Though holding prime ministerial rank, he avoided worldly affairs. When Emperor Wei abdicated, Zheng Chong presented the policy letter. Emperor Wu appointed him Taifu and promoted him to Duke. Despite illness-related requests for removal, the emperor refused. In the sixth year of Taishi, the emperor praised Zheng Chong, He Zeng, and Xun Hao for their virtue and service. Zheng Chong repeatedly resigned, and the emperor eventually allowed him to return to his mansion as Duke Shouguang with full privileges. He died the following year, receiving posthumous honors. Zheng Chong compiled "Collected Commentary of the Analects of Confucius" with others. Having no sons, his nephew Zheng Hui inherited his title.

He Zeng, courtesy name Yingkao, was from Yangxia, Chen State. His father He Kui was Taipu of Wei. He Zeng inherited his title young, was eager to learn, and gained reputation. He served as Sanqi Changshi, Diannong General, and Huangmen Shilang. He submitted memorials advising careful selection of county governors. He served as governor of Hanoi with majestic reputation. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached the favored official Yin Mo. He criticized Ruan Ji's dissolute behavior during mourning. He held various positions including Zhenbei General and was granted Marquis of Yingchang Township. Emperor Wu appointed him Taibao and later Taifu. He was known for filial piety, treating his wife with formal respect. However, he was extremely extravagant, spending ten thousand on daily meals, with luxurious carriages and clothing exceeding imperial standards. He died at age eighty, receiving the posthumous name Xiao. His sons He Zun and He Shao inherited his wealth. He Shao served as prince's grand master and Situ, maintaining similar extravagance.

Shi Bao, courtesy name Zhongrong, was from Nanpi, Bohai. Known for beauty and intelligence, he was discovered by Guo Xuanxin who predicted his future as minister. He served as Sima of Emperor Jing's Imperial Guard. Despite concerns about his character, Emperor Jing defended him, comparing him to Guan Zhong and Chen Ping. He served as Ye Diannong Zhonglang Jiang, governor of Donglai and Langye, and Xuzhou governor. During Zhuge Dan's rebellion, Shi Bao led troops and defeated Wu forces. He was granted Marquis of Shuguang and later promoted to Grand Sima and Duke of Leling County. Suspected of rebellion due to rumors, he was dismissed but later reinstated as Situ. He focused on agricultural policies and died in the eighth year of Taishi. His sons included Shi Yue, Shi Qiao, Shi Tong, Shi Jun, Shi Jun, and Shi Chong. Shi Chong, known for wealth and extravagance, competed with royal relatives in luxury, owning numerous slaves and treasures. He was executed at age fifty-two during political conflicts, with his entire family killed.
