At that time, the grain harvest had not been harvested for several years, and the Western Qiang and Hu people were harassing the border. The emperor issued an edict for the ministers to discuss.
Fu Xuan responded to the emperor's questions and stated his reasons sincerely and straightforwardly. Although he did not implement everything, he was often tolerated.
Transferred to the post of Sili Xiaowei.
Queen Xian passed away in Hongxun Palace, and a place of mourning was set up.
According to the old system, the minister should sit outside Duanmen, sitting alone above the other ministers.
Entering the palace, according to the official rank of this product, under the ministers, sit in order and sit at the same table with others.
The visitors believed that Hongxun Palace was within the palace, and placed Fu Xuan's position under the position of Qing.
Fu Xuan was furious and shouted at the visitors.
The visitor pretended that it was arranged by the Minister, and Fu Xuan cursed the Minister in front of all the officials and left the table.
Yu Chun, the imperial censor, reported to Fu Xuan how disrespectful he was, but Fu Xuan's report was inconsistent with the facts, so he was dismissed from office.
However, Fu Xuan was by nature severe and impatient, and could not be tolerant when things happened. Every time there was a memorial to report, or when it was late, he would hold the memorial in his hand, straighten his crown and belt, and restlessly not sleep, but sit and wait for dawn.
As a result, those princes and nobles without official positions were afraid to surrender, and the minister suddenly gained prestige.
Soon he died at home at the age of sixty-two. His posthumous title was Gang.
Fu Xuan took refuge in Hanoi when he was young and concentrated on reading. Although he became rich and powerful, his writings were not neglected.
He wrote a book that commented on the three religions and nine streams of governing the country and the three historical events, and judged the pros and cons, each with regulations. The book is called "Fu Zi", which is divided into three chapters: internal, external and middle. It has four parts and six records, with a total of 140 poems and hundreds of thousands of words. It has been popular in the world together with more than 100 volumes of collected works.
Fu Xuan originally wrote the internal chapter, and his son Fu Xian gave it to Sikong Wang Shen to read.
Wang Chen wrote to Fu Xuan: I saw your book, which contains grand words and well-equipped principles, plans for governing the country, and attaches great importance to Confucian education and morality. It is enough to block the debauchery of Yang Zhu and Mo Zhai's teachings, and can be compared with Xun Kuang and Meng Ke in ancient times.
Every time I open the book, I sigh with emotion. Without seeing Jia Yi, I thought I was better than him, but now I know I can't compare to him.
That’s so true! Later, he was granted the title of Marquis of Qingquan, and his son Fu Xian inherited the title.
Fu Xian's character is "Yu", and he has a strong sense of uprightness.
He has a strict demeanor and conduct, is well-informed, intelligent and wise, hates evil as much as his enemies, recommends talents, is willing to do good, and often looks up to the ambitions of Ji Wenzi and Zhongshanfu.
I like to write literary essays. Although my literary talent is not brilliant, my remarks can serve as a warning.
Yu Chun of Yingchuan often lamented: Fu Changyu's articles are close to the poet's creation.
In the early years of Xianning, he inherited his father's title and worshiped him as Prince Xima. He moved to Shangshu Youcheng and went to court to serve as the governor of Jizhou. His stepmother Du refused to go with Fu Xian, so Fu Xian petitioned to be dismissed.
Thirty years later, he was appointed Situ Zuo Changshi.
At that time, Emperor Wu paid attention to political affairs and issued an edict to visit courtiers to inquire about political affairs.
Fu Xian wrote a letter saying: Your Majesty is in the most distinguished position, but you do what commoners do, take care of everything yourself, and work hard until the sun is in the west.
The emperors of the past, even if they personally did small things to benefit the world, they would not surpass His Majesty.
However, it has been fifteen years since the founding of Thailand, but the army and the country are not strong enough, and the people are not rich enough. When a year is not good, famine will occur. It is indeed because there are too many official positions and complicated affairs, and there are too many people who are exempted from corvee. There are many people who cannibalize and few people who work in agriculture.
Because of my ignorance and carelessness, I am ashamed of my position. Every time I see the edicts worrying about the people's famine in the years and being unable to help, I feel extremely ashamed. How dare I not use all my stupidity to answer the emperor's inquiries?
There used to be four governors, but now including the supervisors, there are more than ten.
Xia Yu divided the land into nine states. The current number of governors is almost doubled, the household population is only one-tenth that of the Han Dynasty, and there are even more counties and counties.
The empty gate of the captain's teeth is of no use to the palace guards, but military mansions are set up out of thin air, and there are often hundreds of them.
The fifth-level princes also set up official subordinates.
All kinds of favored provisions were taken from the people.
If a person does not farm, someone will suffer from hunger. There are countless people who do not farm now.
Even if the grain harvest is good, it can only meet the needs of the green and yellow; if there is a sudden disaster, it will not be enough.
I believe that the top priority is to consolidate official positions, simplify trivial matters, stop doing errands, stop corvee work, and work together to devote ourselves to agricultural production.
Fu Xian was always able to uphold justice during his tenure.
Xia Houjun, the Dazhongzheng of Yuzhou, wrote: "The Xiaozhongzheng of Lu and Kong Yu, the Sikong Sima, have been moved to recuperate four times and cannot receive guests. They request that Cao Fu, the Minister of Finance, be allowed to replace Kong Yu." More than ten days later, he went to Shu to let Kong Yu continue to be in the middle.
Situ refused to accept the offer three times, but Xia Houjun still insisted on his opinion.
Fu Xian believed that Xia Houjun praised and criticized Xiahou Jun at will, so he petitioned to remove him from the post of Dazhongzheng.
Situ Wei Shu and Xia Houjun were related by marriage and repeatedly refused to sign. Fu Xian tried his best to argue with his arguments.
Wei Shu finally disagreed, so Fu Xian submitted a letter alone.
Wei Shu reported that Fu Xian's slander was excessive and lacked integrity, so he issued an edict to transfer him to the position of Chariot and Cavalry Commander.
Seeing the luxury of the world, Fu Xian wrote again: I think food and clothing are difficult to produce. If we don't use them sparingly, there is no reason why we should not be in shortage.
Therefore, the former king was popular in the world, and the meat and silk he ate were all customized.
I privately believe that extravagance and waste are worse than natural disasters.
In ancient times, the emperor Yao only had thatched houses, but now common people are competing to build spacious houses; in ancient times, ministers did not have exquisite food, but now businessmen can feast on delicious food; in ancient times, only concubines had special clothes, but now slaves, wives and concubines all wear silk and satin; in ancient times, only doctors had chariots, but now lowly slaves also drive light chariots and fat horses.
In ancient times, the reason for having savings in a densely populated area was due to frugality; now the land is vast and the population is sparse, but there are not enough worries because of luxury.
If you want to be thrifty, you should prohibit luxury; if luxury is not prohibited, you will compete with others.
In the past, when Mao Wangjie was the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, no one dared to wear beautiful clothes or eat delicious food.
Emperor Wu of Wei lamented: My laws are not as good as those of Mao Shangshu.
If all the ministries have the same intentions as Mao Wangjie, it is indeed not difficult to change customs.
They also discussed moving the county prison to the county and establishing two communes, and the court agreed.
Moved to the post of Minister Zuocheng.
Emperor Hui Sima Zhong succeeded to the throne, and Yang Jun assisted in government affairs.
Fu Xian said to Yang Jun: Things change at any time, and etiquette and justice are appropriate at any time. The emperor has not implemented the system of mourning for a long time.
Because the world is in decline, political affairs cannot be managed by others, so even though we are in a period of mourning, we still have to take care of everything ourselves.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Liu Heng, believed that the world was huge and mourning was too heavy to last, he decided to remove the mourning after burial.
Emperor Wu Sima Yan was very filial and honest, and he also decided to stay in mourning for three years. As for the day-to-day affairs, he was so busy that he had no time to spare.
Now the Holy One wants to hand over political affairs to you and let him stay in mourning. Although this is a humble attitude, people in the world don't think it is very appropriate.
The reason why it is not very appropriate is because all the people admire and respect the emperor. If he obeys the emperor's orders, it may block the light of the sky.
Since people's hearts are like this, it won't be easy for you to be in the regent position.
I privately think that the funeral is over, and you should think about the appropriate time for the funeral.
Duke Zhou is a saint and cannot avoid slander.
It can be inferred from this that it is no longer easy to handle the appointment of Duke Zhou, not to mention that the age of the Holy Emperor is not that of King Zhou Cheng?
I was so proud that I forgot to speak, and it was not easy for me to express myself clearly.
If you can sense my sincerity, why does it matter how many words you have?
At that time, Si Li Xun Kai's cousin died, and he went to attend the funeral. Before the imperial edict was issued, Xun Kai visited Yang Jun.
Therefore, Fu Xian wrote in a memorial: "The death of a brother is sad, and the death of a brother is even more sad. Xun Kai died in the same house only a few days ago. The emperor took pity on him and allowed him to mourn."
Before the edict was issued, he went to bid farewell and visit important people, eager to show flattery and respect, but without the true feelings of brotherly friendship.
He should be severely demoted and deposed in order to uphold customs and enlightenment.
The emperor thought that Yang Jun was in charge of the affairs of the court, and when he was asked about the imperial edict, Yang Jun was very frightened.
Fu Xian wrote another letter to Yang Jun, his satirical remonstrances were straightforward. Yang Jun restrained himself slightly and gradually became dissatisfied.
He wanted Fu Xian to serve as the governor of Jingzhao and Hongnong. Yang Jun's nephew Li Bin persuaded Yang Jun that upright people should not be criticized for serving as foreign officials, so he was able to stop.
Yang Jun's younger brother Yang Ji has always been friendly with Fu Xian. He wrote to Fu Xian: The flowing water of the river and sea is rolling in waves, so it can achieve its depth and breadth.
The world is a big thing and it is impossible to understand it very well, but I think you want to understand everything.
You are born with dementia, but you can understand official affairs, and official affairs are not easy to understand.
It is also a happy thing to understand that official affairs are the time to be stupid.
Zuo Cheng leads the imperial court and assists eight ministers and hundreds of officials. This position is not easy to occupy.
It is even more difficult to be in a position that is not easy for you to speak out with your willfulness.
Thinking about it gives me a headache, so I state it as above.
Fu Xian replied: Duke Wei said that killing people with wine and sex is more powerful than upright people.
I have no regrets about dying because of drunkenness and lust.
In advance, you are afraid that being upright will lead to disaster. This is because your heart is not upright, and you want to live an ignoble life as a wise sage!
Since ancient times, people who have caused disasters because of their integrity should have gone too far or been not loyal enough. They have to use extreme cruelty to establish their reputation, so they are resented.
How can anyone be sincere and loyal yet be envied and hated?
Soon after, Yang Jun was executed, and Fu Xian was transferred to the position of Prince's concubine and promoted to Yu Shi Zhongcheng.
At that time, Dazai and Runan King Sima Liang assisted the government. Fu Xian wrote a letter saying: I think that Taijia of the Shang Dynasty and Chengwang of the Zhou Dynasty were young, so Yi Yin and Zhou Gong assisted the government.
The sages of the previous generations were inevitably doubted, not to mention that the current ministers are not saints, and the kings are not cowards. How can we imitate the old deeds of Yi Yin and Zhou Gong!
The monarch was in mourning and obeyed the orders of the Grand Prime Minister. Yang Jun was rude, but he wanted to be the Duke of Yiyin and Zhou, thinking that he could assist the government and stabilize the world, so he died.
His crimes are countless, as you have witnessed, Your Highness.
Yang Jun was attacked because of the emperor's sage. Meng Guan and Li Zhao only participated in and knew the secret decree.
As for the credit for commenting, it should go to the Emperor.
Meng Guan and others were already marquises in a large county with thousands of households. The Holy Emperor was extremely happy to kill Yang Jun, so he would rather reward generously to express his joy.
This is a fact that ministers and subordinates should weigh. But now they are inciting and inciting them to make Duke Dong'an king, Meng Guan and Li Zhao are both county princes, and the rest are named marquis, uncle, son, and male. After the false titles were added, the third class was promoted to an exceptional level.
This illustrious momentum shook the earth. There had never been such a reward since ancient times.
If there is no merit but generous rewards, no one will be unhappy when the country suffers disasters, because when disasters arise, great achievements will be made.
People take pleasure in causing chaos, so where is the limit?
This practice all came from Dong'an Gong.
After His Highness takes office, he should find a way to correct it.
If we use the Great Way to make things right, why should people be angry?
What everyone is angry about is just unfairness.
Nowadays, everyone is talking behind his back, and no one is not disappointed.
I was stupid, not just disappointed, but secretly worried.
In addition, when you denounced Yang Jun, Your Highness was still outside the court and you really did not participate.
Now we have to entrust you with an important task, so let His Highness discuss his merits.
Discussing merit is really not easy to deal with. It is better to sit back and watch the pros and cons, and you will have the fact that you are upright in your position.
Fu Xian also remonstrated because Sima Liang was in charge of the government and said: "Yang Jun has the power to shock the monarch. He appoints relatives. This is the reason for the uproar in the world."
Now that you are serving as assistant to the government, you should correct this mistake.
I think we should calm down and recuperate. If there are big gains and losses, we will continue to deal with them. Except for major issues, we should refrain from dismissing them.
During my four visits to your residence and when I pass by your door on a regular basis, I always see officials and officials crowding the streets. This habit should be stopped.
In addition, Xiahou Changrong was envoyed to pray for the late emperor, but his prayers did not move God. When the late emperor passed away, Xiahou Changrong should blame himself. But now you are asking for the credit of asking for life, and you appointed him as the young man.
I privately think that Xiahou Changrong is your in-law, that's why it's like this. The shape of a dog barking, the sound of a group of dogs barking.
Because he was afraid of the barking of the dogs, he could not obey. As a person, I can't flatter and obey someone in person, and I can't even slander someone behind my back.
It turns out that I once offended Yang Jun and almost suffered disaster, not to mention that I should cherish His Highness.
When I was riding with you earlier, you said to me: Don’t you know what Han Feizi said: Offending a human being is like touching the scales of a dragon? And you are actually touching the scales of the Emperor's inversion.
I know that what I stated is indeed touching the beard of the beast without stopping.
And the reason why I dare to speak out is that I hope that you, Your Highness, will understand my mere thoughts.
When I touched the scales of the emperor before, I wanted to be loyal; now when I touch the beard of a beast, I don’t want to do evil, so I will be forgiven.
Sima Liang did not adopt it.
Xiahou Changrong is Xiahoujun.
On May 28th, an edict was issued asking all officials to recommend officials from counties and counties to supplement the court officials.
Fu Xian wrote again: I believe that the key to national prosperity and education lies in selecting talents and giving them appropriate official positions. There is more than one type of talent, and there are different positions.
For example, forest trees, thick and thin, curved and straight, have their own uses.
Therefore, people with humble backgrounds are carefully observed and recommended, and people who are planning and consulting, regardless of whether they are internal or external, and whether they are serving internally or externally, only seek suitability. Nowadays, only internal officials are recommended for selection and appointment. The recommendation of local officials has been partial and full of side effects, and people are vying to become government officials and despise local appointments. It becomes a custom.
This shortcoming should be corrected immediately to make the selection channels for internal and external officials smooth and impartial.
After making the channels smooth and unbiased, if the selection is unfair, there will be a way to impose heavy penalties; if the penalties are increased, there is no need to worry about unfairness.
Besides, you can't tune the harp if you stick to the strings, not to mention how can you restrict the selection of talents?
I think the reason for the restriction is to prevent the selection from being beyond the general public. If it cannot be beyond the general public, sanctions should be based on the situation, and there is no need to restrict the selection method.
There are restrictions on the selection method. If you want to implement it for a long time, I am afraid it is too rigid!
Some people think that if there is no selection method, why should we select? I have heard that punishments are used to punish villains, and morality is used to demand gentlemen. The requirements for gentlemen are in the heart and not in restrictions.
During the Zhengshi period, He Yan was entrusted with the election, and various officials inside and outside the court received suitable talents, and there were many outstanding talents.
Therefore, this is not caused by restrictive control, nor by measures, but the reason for the appointment. The worries of the appointee are more serious than the restrictive method.
This is because the method is wrong and it is not your own fault. Since the fault is not yours, there is no need to worry about blaming him. As the saying goes, using criminal laws to unify people's actions, although people are exempted from breaking the law, they have no sense of shame.
If the method of appointment is used, one is to consider that the guilt will be implicated on oneself, and the other is to fear being resented and slandered.
If you are happy, you will be praised both inside and outside the court, if you are not good, all kinds of evil will be committed. Which is more effective, this kind of frightening people, or relying on restrictive laws to avoid it?
Fu Xian was once again appointed Zhengzheng of the county, but resigned when his stepmother died.
Soon he was promoted to Yilang and concurrently served as Sili Xiaowei.
Fu Xian declined many times but was not approved. The imperial court sent an envoy to his home to confer duties, and Fu Xian returned the seal and ribbon.
He was not informed on the bus and urged to take office as director.
Since Fu Xian had no brothers and no one would conduct the funeral, he asked again to allow him to set up a memorial tablet in his official residence.
Fu Xian went on to say, "Since I am dull and cowardly, I cannot take on important responsibilities."
In addition to mourning and asking for leave to rest, Your Majesty was too gracious and granted me a position that I was unable to perform.
I expressed my sincerity and risked my life to report it. I have violated the edict and will not change in the end.
Although I cannot sacrifice my life to preserve the ethics, I cannot change my mind according to morality and receive grace in vain.
In the past, he accepted strict orders and when he took office, he swore privately that he would die as retribution.
Because bribery is so popular, it should be strictly eradicated, and the governor must be ordered to take this matter as the top priority.
But after years and months, nothing has been achieved.
This is because His Majesty has a way to reward people. Considering that ignorant people will definitely die or be guilty, it is natural to cover up their mistakes to avoid being exposed.
Having been in office for a long time, without any outstanding behavior, and unable to follow the lead, who would still be afraid?
Therefore, Liu Yi, the official of Guanglu, was appointed as the official, and his prestige shocked both inside and outside the court, and he was respected far and near.
Not only did Liu Yi have the integrity to assist the royal family and be loyal to the king, but also because he obeyed everything he told him, so he could display his majesty.
The edict said: You should only think that everything is in compliance with Shengmo's laws and let your prestige spread day by day. How can you be just Liu Yi?
At that time, the politics of the imperial court were relaxed, the powerful and powerful families indulged in unbridled affairs, made personal friends and favors, and the government and the public were in chaos.
Fu Xian submitted a petition to depose Henan Yin Dan, Zuo Jiangjun Qian, Tingwei Gaoguang, and Henan Yin Hepan. The capital was in awe, and the nobles were intimidated and subdued.
Fu Xian believed that only when saints govern the country for a long time can the world be enlightened.
Therefore, Yao and Shun evaluated political performance in three years and discussed promotion and demotion in nine years.
"The Rites of Zhou" also implements a three-year competition.
Confucius also said: It takes three years to achieve success.
But in recent times, long-term officials have taken up posts in government offices and were soon reassigned. The people are troubled by the lack of fixed officials, and the officials are tired of seeing off the old and welcoming the new.
At that time, the servant Wang Rong was also in charge of the official department. Fu Xian reported: Wang Rong was in the position of Taifu and was also in charge of elections, but he did not calm the customs and gather achievements, which made people uneasy and uneasy, and opened up the wind of frivolous competition.
The lieutenants Li Chong and Li Yi did not correct him.
I request that Wang Rong and others be relieved of their duties.
The edict said: The foundation of political ethics is that one should serve for a long time. Fu Xian's report is correct.
Wang Rong's duty is to review affairs. He is recommended by me and cannot be removed from office.
Yushi Zhongcheng Jiejie believed that Fu Xian's impeachment of Wang Rong violated the code, violated the rules, interfered with matters that were not within his authority, so he submitted a memorial to remove Fu Xian from his official position, but the edict did not agree.
Fu Xian Shangshu believed: According to the law, the imperial minister supervises all officials.
Regarding matters below the Crown Prince, those who violate laws and regulations must be impeached and corrected within the scope of the inspection and censor's control. Even outside the scope of the inspection, if the supervisor does not investigate, he can be impeached.
According to the provisions of the law, riding a horse violates the constitution and is considered to be a prohibited matter. Prevention is prohibited in the palace and cannot be carried out by foreign officials, so Zhongcheng is given the full responsibility.
Nowadays, roads and bridges have not been built, and there are constant fights and lawsuits between butchers and customers. For such things, Zhongcheng shirks the responsibility to the governors of prefectures and counties. This is what is now called the implementation of prohibitions and precautions during horseback riding.
Since it is said that Zhongcheng supervises hundreds of officials, why bother talking about Xingma within?
Since we talk about Baiguan, we can no longer talk about Xingma. All kinds of officials inside and outside are called Baiguan. Originally, the internal and external colluded.
The reason why Sili stopped talking about traveling on horseback was because he had already told Zhongcheng about the prohibitions and precautions.
Zhongcheng and Sili both supervise all matters below the crown prince. In fact, they are jointly in charge of internal and external matters. It does not mean that Zhongcheng is in charge of all officials in the inner court, and Sili is in charge of all officials in the outer court. Since Sili and Zhongcheng have been in charge, they have been interfering with internal and external officials. But I am afraid there will be no internal or external restrictions on what they inspect.
However, Jie Jie suddenly accused me. The reason why I did not defend myself before was because I hoped Jie Jie's memorial would fulfill my wish.
Now that I can't do what I want, and the edict says it's just a mistake, and it's not something I didn't say, I forgive him.
I am in charge of direct remonstrance, and I should correct my own moral character to set an example for others. If I make a mistake, I dare not accept forgiveness, so I will state my humble opinion.
If Sili and Zhongcheng jointly correct all matters below the crown prince, then there will be no one from the crown prince on down who cannot correct them.
If the crown prince can be interrogated but the minister cannot be interrogated, this is something I cannot understand.
Does the Crown Prince count as a traveler? If the crown prince can check him within walking distance of the horse, but the minister cannot check him within the walking distance of the horse, there is no such reason.
The truth is very clear, but Jiejie accused me of it.
I can't be resentful, but onlookers shouldn't be surprised either?
I remember that Shi Gong took off his clothes in the palace and was played by Xun Kai, the minister. The late emperor did not think it was wrong. At that time, no one said that it was an infringement of his position and overstepped his authority. Now that I am interrogating the minister, should I be considered guilty?
Fu Xian repeatedly cited past facts in his letters, which were clearly organized and could not be changed by the court.
Gu Rong of Wu County often wrote to his relatives: Fu Xian was a secretary, he was upright, loyal, brave and courageous, and the impeachment memorial was surprising.
Although he is not a perfect talent, he is very valuable in terms of integrity.
Yuankang died in the official office in the fourth year of his reign at the age of fifty-six. The edict gave him the title of Sili Xiaowei, a set of court uniforms, a collar and a robe, 200,000 yuan, and a posthumous title of Zhen.
Fu Xian had three sons: Fu Fu, Fu Rixi and Fu Zuan.
The eldest son Fu Fu inherited the title.
summary:
Fu Xuan, courtesy name Xiu Yi, was from Niyang in the north. His grandfather Fu Xie was a Han prefect, and his father Fu Qian was a Wei governor. Orphaned and poor in youth, Fu Xuan was erudite, skilled in writing, and knowledgeable in music. He had a strong, upright character and could not tolerate others' faults. He was appointed as a county planner, recommended as Xiaolian twice, and recruited by the Taiwei, but did not take the post. He passed the scholar examination, became a doctor, and was selected with Donghai Mushi to compile Wei books. He later held various military and civil posts, including prefect of Hongnong and captain of Diannong School, and was known for his competent governance and many petitions. After the fifth-grade system was established, he was granted the title of Baron Quail. Under Emperor Wu of Jin, he was promoted to viscount and Prince Consort and Commander-in-Chief.

As an admonishment officer, Fu Xuan submitted a memorial criticizing the decline of benevolence and righteousness since the Qin and Wei dynasties, praising Emperor Wu's virtue, and urging the recommendation of courteous ministers and removal of hypocritical ones. The emperor agreed and asked him to draft an edict. Fu Xuan further wrote on the importance of proper official appointments, advocating for long-term positions and the division of labor among scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants. He stressed the need for a system to plan the number of people in each class, emphasizing agriculture and Confucian education. He also proposed that idle officials should farm, and that the government should evaluate officials every three years, with promotions after nine years. The emperor praised his sincerity and ordered further study of his proposals.

In the fourth year of Taishi, Fu Xuan became Yushi Zhongcheng. During floods and droughts, he submitted five proposals: adjusting the share of harvest for soldiers using government cattle; enforcing Han-era laws to punish negligent officials; improving water conservancy by dividing responsibilities; reforming land tax to rest labor; and establishing a new county in Gaopingchuan to manage the Xianbei tribe and prevent border unrest. The emperor approved these as fundamental to governance. In the fifth year of Taishi, Fu Xuan became a servant. Despite grain shortages and border troubles, his sincere advice was often tolerated. He later became Sili Xiaowei, but was dismissed after a dispute over seating at a mourning ceremony. He died at home at age sixty-two, posthumously titled Gang.

Fu Xuan wrote "Fu Zi," a book on governance and the three religions, divided into internal, external, and middle chapters, with over 100 volumes. His son Fu Xian inherited his title. Fu Xian, courtesy name Yu, was upright, strict, and hated evil. He served as Prince Xima, Shangshu Youcheng, and governor of Jizhou, but resigned when his stepmother refused to accompany him. Later, as Situ Zuo Changshi, he criticized the emperor for overworking himself and proposed consolidating official positions, simplifying affairs, and promoting agriculture. He also petitioned against extravagance, citing ancient frugality. During Emperor Hui's reign, he advised Yang Jun on regency matters and later criticized Sima Liang for excessive rewards. Fu Xian was known for his fearless impeachments, including against Wang Rong, and his advocacy for long-term official tenures. He died in office at age fifty-six, posthumously titled Zhen. He had three sons: Fu Fu, Fu Rixi, and Fu Zuan.

Shantao is named Juyuan, and Hanoi embraces people.
Father Shan Yao is Wanjuling.
Shantao lost his father in his early years and his family was poor. When he was young, he was thoughtful and unique.
He likes "Zhuangzi" and "Laozi" and often hides himself without showing his talents.
He had friendship with Ji Kang and Lu An, and later met Ruan Ji, and established a friendship in the bamboo forest and became the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Forest. They had a tacit understanding of understanding each other without having to speak. Ji Kang was later convicted. Before his execution, he said to his son Ji Shao: With Juyuan here, you are no longer an orphan.
Shan Tao was forty years old, and he was initially appointed as the princess's administrator, meritorious officer, and chief planner.
He was elected Xiaolian, and the state called him to serve in the Ministry of Henan.
Living with Shi Jian, Shan Tao wrapped himself up at night and pushed Shi Jian awake and said: "When are you still sleeping now?"
Do you know what Tai Tu meant by calling him sick?
Shi Jian said: "The prime minister failed to come to court three times, so I issued an edict to let him go home. What are you worried about?"
Shan Tao said: Alas, Mr. Shi will not be in danger during the war!
He threw down the talisman and left.
Within two years, Cao Shuang changed his mind and he became invisible and no longer participated in world affairs.
After Yu Xuanmu was a middle cousin, he met Emperor Jing.
Emperor Jing said: "Does Lu Wang want to be an official?"
He was ordered to recommend him as a scholar and a doctor.
He was transferred to General Wang Chang and served as a lieutenant.
After a long time, he paid homage to Zhao Guoxiang. He was promoted to minister of official affairs.
Emperor Wen wrote to Shan Tao: You are honest and smart in doing things, and your elegant conduct is beyond the world.
Considering your shortage of various supplies, I will send you 200,000 yuan of money and 200 dendrobium of grain today.
Emperor Wei once gave spring clothes to Emperor Jing, who in turn gave them to Shan Tao.

Shantao, also known as Juyuan, was a man of Hanoi who lost his father early and grew up in poverty. He was thoughtful from a young age, favored the works of Zhuangzi and Laozi, and often concealed his talents. He formed deep friendships with Ji Kang, Lu An, and later Ruan Ji, becoming one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Forest. At forty, he began his official career, serving in various roles such as the princess's administrator and chief planner. He was known for his integrity and wisdom, once warning Shi Jian about the dangers of Cao Shuang's rebellion. After Cao Shuang's downfall, Shantao withdrew from public life for a time.

Shantao later served under Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen, holding positions such as Zhao Guoxiang and minister of official affairs. He was praised for his honesty and intelligence, receiving generous gifts from the emperor. In his later years, he interacted with high-ranking officials like Zhong Hui and Pei Xiu, maintaining harmony among them. He was promoted to general and lieutenant, and during the campaign against Shu, he was entrusted with guarding Ye. In the early years of Xianxi, he was named Xin Da Zi and later served as Prime Minister Zuo Changshi.

When Emperor Wu succeeded, Shantao advised against appointing Sima You, citing the importance of proper succession. He served as Dahonglu and later as Fengche Captain. As governor of Jizhou, he reformed local customs by recommending talented individuals. He resigned multiple times due to his mother's age, but was eventually persuaded to return to office. He served as Shangshu of the Ministry of Personnel, selecting officials based on merit. Despite facing criticism, he continued his work, earning the title "Monkey Announcement" for his screening methods.

In his later years, Shantao faced the dictatorship of the Hou party and advised the emperor without success. He resigned due to old age and illness, but was repeatedly called back to service. He was promoted to Youpuse and Guanglu doctor, but continued to decline due to health. After Wu was pacified, he advised against withdrawing military forces, a warning that proved prescient during later chaos. He was appointed Situ but refused, eventually dying at seventy-nine. He was given posthumous honors and his family was provided for by the emperor.

Shantao was known for his frugality and loyalty, never taking concubines despite his high status. He distributed his salary to relatives and friends. He once accepted silk from a corrupt official but kept it sealed, later returning it when the official's crimes were exposed. He had five sons: Shan Gai, Shan Chun, Shan Yun, Shan Mo, and Shan Jian. Shan Gai inherited his title and served as governor of Bingzhou. Shan Jian, known for his gentle temperament, became a prominent official, serving as minister and governor of various regions.

Wang Rong, courtesy name Junchong, was from Linyi. He was known for his intelligence and calmness from a young age, once standing unafraid during a tiger's roar. He was friends with Ruan Ji and others, and was known for his insight. He served in various official roles, including governor of Jingzhou and Yuzhou, and was involved in the conquest of Wu. He was known for his filial piety, though he did not strictly adhere to rituals. He was criticized for his greed and stinginess, often calculating his wealth day and night. He died at seventy-two, posthumously named Yuan.

Wang Yan, courtesy name Yifu, was known for his clear expression and elegance. He was a leading figure in the Qingtan movement, advocating the philosophy of nothingness. He held high positions but was criticized for his lack of integrity and self-preservation. During the chaos of the Jin dynasty, he advised his brothers to take up posts in strategic regions, a plan known as the "cunning rabbit's three burrows." He was captured by Shi Le and killed after refusing to take responsibility for the dynasty's fall. He was fifty-six at his death.

Le Guang, courtesy name Yanfu, was known for his calm and far-sighted nature. He was skilled in conversation and used simple words to explain profound truths. He served as Henan Yin and was known for his ability to resolve disputes. He once cured a guest's illness by explaining the illusion of a snake in a cup. He was praised for his integrity and adherence to ritual, even during times of chaos. He died of worry after being slandered. He had three sons: Le Kai, Le Zhao, and Le Chen.

Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanchong, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan.

Wang Hun is deep, elegant and thoughtful.

summary:
Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanchong, was from Jinyang, Taiyuan, and inherited his father Wang Chang's title of Marquis of Jingling. He served under Cao Shuang but was dismissed after Shuang's execution. Later, he held various posts, including Governor of Xuzhou, where he opened granaries to relieve famine. During the Taishi era, he was transferred to guard Zhuchang and frequently submitted governance strategies that were often adopted. As General of Conquering Captives in Yuzhou, he attracted many surrenders. He defeated Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu, earning his son Wang Shang the title of Marquis of Guannei. As General Andong in Yangzhou, he repelled Wu forces, burning their grain and ships. During the major campaign against Wu, Wang Hun led troops from Hengjiang, capturing Wu generals and receiving surrenders from Chen Dai and Zhu Ming. He defeated Wu Prime Minister Zhang Ti, killing 7,800, leading to Sun Hao's surrender via He Zhi and Sun Yan. However, Wang Jun later took Sun Hao's surrender, causing Wang Hun shame and jealousy. He reported Wang Jun's crimes, drawing public ridicule. The emperor praised Wang Hun's role in pacifying Moling, adding fiefs and promoting him to Duke. He was later transferred to General Zhengshu, where he comforted surrendered Wu people. As Shangshu Zuopushe, he advised against sending Prince Sima You to a vassal state, citing historical precedents and urging retention for state security, but the emperor did not accept. In the Taixi era, he became Situ. Under Emperor Hui, he was given military command but insisted on wearing black robes to avoid impropriety, earning praise. When Prince Sima Zhang of Chu sought to kill Sima Liang, Wang Hun feigned illness and resisted with soldiers, and Sima Zhang was later killed. The emperor consulted Wang Hun on customs inquiries; Wang Hun proposed detailed questioning of local planners, which was approved. He died at seventy-five, posthumously named Yuan.

Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi, was Wang Hun's son. He was exceptionally talented, skilled in archery and the "Yi," "Zhuang," and "Lao" texts, and married Princess Changshan. He served as Zhongshu Lang and later as a servant, known for his eloquence and favored by Emperor Wu. However, he was inwardly jealous and harsh with words. He opposed sending Prince Sima You away, crying with the princess, which angered the emperor and led to demotion. As Henan Yin, he was dismissed for whipping an official. He was extravagant, paving a riding track with money and betting a prized cow with Wang Kai, cutting it up after winning. He once served human-milk-steamed food to the emperor, who left displeased. He understood horses, once recognizing a horse's reluctance to cross mud. He died at forty-six, posthumously named General of Hussars. At his funeral, Sun Chu brayed like a donkey in tribute, making guests laugh. He married a blind, jealous princess and had two sons by a concubine.

Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was from Hongnong Lake. He was well-read and handsome, initially lacking reputation but later changed his ways. He built a house with a wide gate, saying it would accommodate halberds and flags. He married Xu Miao's daughter after she saw him at a gathering. Yang Hu recognized his talent and helped him. As Governor of Bajun, he eased corvée for newborns, saving thousands. As Governor of Guanghan, he was benevolent. He dreamed of knives, interpreted as a sign he would govern Yizhou, and became its governor, pacifying rebels. He built large ships for attacking Wu, with iron cones and locks countered by rafts and torches. He captured Wu territories, and Sun Hao surrendered. Wang Jun entered Shitou, accepting Sun Hao's surrender. He was promoted but conflicted with Wang Hun, who accused him of violating orders. Wang Jun defended himself, citing edicts and circumstances. He was made General of the Auxiliary State but felt under-rewarded, often complaining. He died at eighty, posthumously named Wu. His descendants later fell into poverty, prompting Huan Wen to request restoration of their title.

Tang Bin, courtesy name Confucian, was from Zou. He was skilled in riding and archery and studied the "Book of Changes." He served as a county official and was recommended for his talent. He investigated Deng Ai's execution, reporting no border concerns. As Governor of Yiyang, he stabilized the people. He was appointed General Guangwu to supervise Badong military affairs. During the Wu campaign, he served as vanguard, capturing Xiling and Lexiang. He feigned illness near Jianye to avoid credit disputes. He later guarded the northern border, training soldiers and expanding farmland, restoring the Great Wall and securing peace. He died at sixty, posthumously named Xiang. The historian's commentary notes that Wang Hun and Wang Jun both contributed to pacifying Wu but were marred by jealousy and conflict, while Tang Bin's humility preserved his integrity.

Sima Liang, king of Runan, often entertained ministers and drank wine with glass bells.

Yang Jun was killed, Cui Hong was close to Wang You, the envoy of Dushui, and was deposed for being implicated in the crime.
Later he became the great minister of agriculture and died in office.

So Yang Hu was sent out of the border to travel a hundred miles, and was punished and dismissed from office.
In the last years of Xianxi's reign, he was the Prime Minister of Emperor Wen.

Emperor Wu ascended the throne and built the East Palace for the first time, with Guo Yi and Zheng Mo as the middle sons.
He was promoted to the right guard and the general of the heroic cavalry, and was granted the title of Ping Lingnan.

After Guo Yi completed the review, he said: How can a man seek fame after his elder sister?

To promote filial piety and honesty, the state is used as a special vehicle.
In the early years of Chenli's reign, he was appointed as Luoyang Diannong Zhonglang General and granted the title of Guan Zhonghou.
In the early years of Taishi, he was appointed as the regular attendant of Sanqi, and soon he was also appointed as the middle attendant.

Hou Shiguang is relaxed but not indulgent in his work.

Later he was promoted to Shaofu, and when he died in office, he was given a court uniform, a regular uniform, 300,000 yuan, and 100 pieces of cloth.
After the burial, another edict was issued saying: Shi Guang was resolute and poor, with integrity and loyalty.

Hou Shiguang was good at Confucianism and was familiar with ancient times. He had remarkable achievements in his tenure and his writings and memorials were well organized.
The eldest son Hou Xuan succeeded him and became the prefect of Xuan Tu.
After his death, his son Hou Shi succeeded him and became the prefect of Dongguan.
He Pan, whose courtesy name was Huixing, was from Pi, Shu County. Served as state registrar.
At this time, the governor Huangfu Yan was killed by Yamen Zhang Hong, who was framed for treason.
At that time, He Pan was catching up with his mother's funeral, so he went to Liangzhou to submit a memorial to prove that Huangfu Yan had not rebelled, so Huangfu Yan could appeal his grievances.
Wang Jun is the governor of Yizhou and serves as a special driver.
Wang Jun planned a crusade against Yu You and sent Bao Pan to the central government with a memorial to describe the opportunity. Shaoling introduced him again and ordered Zhang Huayu to plan the crusade.
Wang Jun also sent He Pan to pass by Yanghu to present the strategy of attacking Wu.
He Pan was good at conveying orders, and the emperor cherished him and allowed him to join Wang Jun's military affairs.
When Jianbi surrendered to Wang Tan, Wang Yun was angry because he was late and wanted to attack Wang Jun. He Pan persuaded Wang Jun to give Sun Hao to Wang Tan, and the conflict was resolved.
He Pan was appointed as Wang Jun's auxiliary Sima, and was granted the title of Marquis of Guan Nei.
He was changed to Rongyang Ling, and he reported ten things that were beneficial to the country, which was highly praised.
When he was appointed Tingwei, Zhuge Chong, the Tingwei minister at that time, despised him because he was from Shu. He did not start to admire him until they jointly tried difficult cases.
He was promoted to the prefect of Xuancheng, but before he left, he was appointed as the minister of Sanqi.
When he was in power, he used relatives more, promoted rewards, and wanted to use favors to defend himself.
Jian! thought it was inappropriate, so they impeached him together with Gensai.
The memorial can be found in "The Biography of Shi Chong".
The emperor did not accept it.
Because of his meritorious service in participating in the plot to kill Zizhui, he was granted the title of Marquis of Xicheng, with a settlement of 10,000 households, and a reward of 10,000 pieces of silk. His younger brother Bao Feng was made Marquis of Pingxiang, and his nephew Yukui was made Marquis of Guanzhong.

He was promoted to the rank of captain of Yijun, and soon he was appointed as the captain of Shuqiang.
He was appointed as the governor of Yangzhou. He served for three years and was promoted to Da Si Nong.
He was changed to the governor of Manye and general Yingyang was appointed, but he resolutely declined.
Taichang Shengsai and General Zuo Industrial Control persuaded him to take office. The emperor was urging him urgently, but he refused to take office claiming that he was ill.
When King Zhao Sima Lun usurped the throne and sent someone to summon He Pan, he increasingly said that he was seriously ill.
Sima Lun was angry and wanted to kill him, so he had no choice but to answer the call despite being sick.
Died in Luoyang at the age of fifty-eight.
He Pan was fair-minded, serious as an official, appreciative of people, respecting Confucianism and loving talents.
Ren Liang and Yizhou Zhongzheng cited buried talents.
Chen Shou, Yan Yi, and Jianwei Feili were all famous figures in Xizhou. They were slandered by the villagers and criticized for more than ten years.
He Pan can clarify the right and wrong and clear up the wrongdoing.
Although He Pan held a high position, his family was very poor. He had no concubines, maids, dancing girls or musical instruments, so he only did charity work for the poor.
His son, He Zhang, also inherited his father's legacy.
Shi Chen said: King You and King Li of Zhou lost their status as kings, but the virtuous ones still had the heart to do good; while Gonggong and Jidou were in power, the Holy Saint could not bear it.
What's more, a person with lofty ideals and benevolence will just agree with it casually!
Being favored by the monarch and being given an official rank means thinking about his survival.
Although the hundred swords are decorated with gold, caressed by the light, and reported to the court, they are still trampled by defeated chariots. It is not easy to admonish the king, but it is really difficult to ridicule the courtiers.
Liu Yi encountered tolerance, and Ren Kai and He Wei were slandered twice. After observing the remaining brave men in detail, they each had their own ideas.
For example, Wu Ye still regarded himself as a minister of Wei, Cui Hong liked him but talked about the truth, Liu Tun advised Wang Mi to dominate, and He Pan obeyed the orders of King Sima Lun. To know the character of a gentleman, you can see how he handles things.
Praise says: When Zhongxiong first took office, his loyalty spread throughout the court.
Compared with Zhuge Liang, he compared the emperor to Emperor Huan and Emperor Mo Ling of Han Dynasty.
Guo Yi criticized Yang Jun, and Ren Kai condemned Jia Chong.
The bridges are smooth and can be used as pillars.
No one paid a private visit to Cui Hong, but his reputation spread throughout the government and the public.
Hou Shiguang and Wu Ye were also talented assistants.
Wherever there is fairness, injustice and cruelty are often corrected.
summary:
Liu Yi, courtesy name Zhongxiong, was from Ye in Donglai, a descendant of Liu Zhang, King of Yangjing. His father, Liu Zhe, served as Prime Minister. Liu Yi was filial in his youth and cultivated noble integrity, but he enjoyed commenting on people and was wary of princes and nobles. When Du Shu, the prefect of Qi, appointed him as a meritorious official, he eliminated over a hundred county officials, earning praise from the people of the Three Wei Dynasties. They remarked, "We only heard of Liu Gongcao, not Du Fujun." At the end of the Wei Dynasty, he was recommended as Xiaolian and appointed as Si Li Duguan, bringing order to the capital. When Liu Yi sought to impeach Yin of Henan, Sili objected, but Liu Yi insisted, saying, "A dog can catch animals and kill rats—what harm is there?" He then resigned.

Wang Ji recommended Liu Yi to the government, praising his uprightness and honesty. Liu Yi later served as an official in Pingyang and was known for his dignified conduct. Taichang Zheng Miao recommended him as a doctor, and Emperor Wen appointed him as a prime minister, but he declined due to illness. People said Liu Yi was loyal to the Wei family, and the emperor suspected him of nostalgia for the old dynasty, threatening death. Frightened, Liu Yi accepted the role of chief registrar. When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, he made Liu Yi a minister and prince-in-law, later appointing him as an admonishment officer. Liu Yi served as city gate school captain, servant, and minister, but was dismissed for crimes. In the early years of Xianning, he was reappointed as a regular attendant and doctor, then as Sili school lieutenant, where he suppressed powerful families and brought order to the capital. Officials feared him, and he was compared to Zhuge Feng and Gai Kuanrao.

When the crown prince entered the court, Liu Yi blocked the band from entering Dongye Gate, deeming it improper, and impeached officials. The emperor pardoned them. After a ceremony at the southern suburbs, the emperor asked Liu Yi which Han emperor he compared to. Liu Yi replied, "Emperor Huan and Emperor Ling." The emperor was displeased, noting his own achievements, but Liu Yi retorted, "They sold offices for the treasury; you sell them for private gain." The emperor laughed, acknowledging Liu Yi's directness. Zou Zhan praised the emperor's tolerance, comparing it favorably to Emperor Wen of Han. Liu Yi later criticized the appearance of a dragon in the arsenal well, arguing against congratulations, citing historical precedents. The emperor accepted his view.

Liu Yi criticized the nine-rank Zhongzheng system, listing eight drawbacks: it relied on personal connections, ignored true talent, caused disputes, and led to corruption. He argued it failed to select virtuous officials and advocated for its abolition. The emperor did not implement his proposal. Liu Yi was dedicated to public service, speaking sincerely, and was respected by all. He was strict with his family, punishing his wife for visiting him during a fast. Despite his poverty, the emperor rewarded him generously. At seventy, he retired but was later recommended as Qingzhou's Grand Central Magistrate, though some officials opposed it. Sun Yin argued for his appointment, citing his integrity and ability. Liu Yi died in the sixth year of Taikang, and the emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously honoring him.

Liu Yi's son, Liu Tun, inherited his father's integrity. He served as a doctor and was punished for opposing the emperor's will. Later, he became Suanzao Ling and Shi Yushi, impeaching Wang Hun for misconduct. Liu Tun also criticized Guo Zhang for failing to put out a fire, causing Guo to reform. He served as Taiyuan's internal history, refused to serve under King Sima Lun, and participated in the three kings' revolt. He was appointed as Zuocheng and censor Zhongcheng, impeaching many officials. He was knighted for his role in attacking Sima Tong but dismissed after Sima Yi's death. He later served as Sili school lieutenant again, defending Queen Yang against King Sima Yong. He fled to Sima Lue and helped repel Liu Gen. After the emperor's return, he was honored but later killed by Shi Le's patrol cavalry.

Other figures include Cheng Wei, a strict official recruited by Liu Yi; He Xiao, a capable administrator praised for his integrity; Wu Yi, a perceptive official who criticized figures; Ren Kai, a loyal minister who opposed Jia Chong and was slandered; Cui Hong, a stern censor who punished misconduct; Guo Yi, a magnanimous official who recognized talent; Hou Shiguang, a loyal and frugal minister; and He Pan, a fair-minded official who helped clear injustices. The text concludes with a commentary praising these officials for their integrity and service, despite facing challenges and slander.

translation:
Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was born in Guangling and was a descendant of Liu Xu, King Li of Guangling in the Han Dynasty.
It has been a prestigious family for generations.
There were four surnames in the same county: Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu, all of which came from the surname Liu. People at that time made up proverbs for them and said: Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu, Liu is the most ancestor.
His father's name is Liu Guan, and he served as the prefect of Pingyang.
Liu Song was able to analyze physics since he was a child and was praised by people at the time.
He was recommended as a filial, honest and scholar, but he was not accepted.
Emperor Wen called him to serve as an official in the Prime Minister's Mansion and was ordered to go to Shu as an envoy.
At that time, Shu had just been pacified, the people were hungry, and the land was desolate. Liu Song petitioned for relief, but did not wait for an answer before granting relief. Therefore, he was removed from his official position.
Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty ascended the throne and appointed Liu Song as Shangshu Sangonglang, who was responsible for presiding over laws and decrees and redressing unjust cases.
Gradually he was promoted to the position of Vice Minister of Zhongshu.
During the Xianning period, Liu Song and Sanqi Lang Bai Bao were ordered to inspect the Jingyang area. Because the envoys were in compliance with the decree, they were transferred to Huang Menlang.
Then he moved to Yilang and acted as Tingwei.
At that time, Shi Huyin was not guilty and imprisoned. Shao sent Liu Song to review. He presided over the proof of innocence and Hu Yin was exempted. At that time, people compared Liu Song to Zhang Shizhi.
He has been on the job for six years and is known as being thorough and fair.
Qiahui destroyed the Kingdom of Wu. The generals competed for merit and sent Liu Song to investigate the matter. Liu Song believed that Wang Hun should be the one with the highest merit and Wang Jun should be the middle merit.
The emperor thought that Liu Song was unreasonable in enforcing the law, so he was demoted to the prefect of Jingzhao. Before taking up the post, he was transferred to Hanoi.
Before departure, it is often used to report things that will benefit the country.
Many water dams were set up by the public within the boundaries of each county, blocking the water flow and causing disasters. Liu Song petitioned to have these water dams demolished, which brought convenience to the people.
Soon he left his job due to the death of his mother.
After the mourning period expired, he was appointed Prime Minister of Huainan.
During his tenure, he was serious and organized and had great political achievements.
In the past, the construction of Shaopi required tens of thousands of labors a year. The powerful took advantage of the opportunity to annex the land, and the weak and poor people lost their fields. Liu Song asked the old and young to work together, and the value was calculated according to the amount of repairs. The people praised him for his fair administration and benefiting the people.
Liu Song wrote in the county:
I used to serve in Hanoi. When I was leaving, I received an edict and said: "What you talked about are all very important things. After taking office, you should report all the big and small things."
I usually have a lot to do, so I may not be able to give you all the answers, so please don’t doubt me because of this.
On the day when the minister accepted the edict, he was filled with joy and fear, and he was even more thoughtful about doing his best to be loyal. Therefore, he forgot his own contempt and was willing to use a small candlelight to increase the glory of the emperor.
After I took office in the county, I scribbled down the following words. Before I could submit the memorial, I happened to suffer the death of my mother and was suspended from office for many years. Now I am cautiously relaying the things I wanted to memorialize before.
Although my talents are not good enough to govern well, and my words are superficial and wrong, I hope that Your Majesty can review them so that my loyalty can be known to His Majesty and I will not be discarded in the pile of documents.
If there are any suggestions that can be adopted, I hope that they can provide some assistance to the governance of the country.
I saw in the edict that it was said to open up a territory, establish a century-old foundation, enfeoff relatives, and let them go out to guard the vassal state. Don't you miss them, but this is the justice.
The construction of a sound national system has been successful to this day, surpassing the narrow etiquette system of Qin, Hui, and Xiuji, and carrying forward the annihilation of the Five Emperors and Three Conquests.
The achievements are spread all over the world, and the glory shines on future generations. It is so majestic and beautiful that some emperors of the previous generation may feel ashamed that they are not kind and virtuous.
Why?
Because they achieved great achievements by following nature, which is fundamentally different from today's creation of great achievements after extinction.
Even so, in my opinion, it is not the best to assign the young prince to Xingshu.
The people in the Wu and Yue areas are frivolous, while the Lu and Shu areas are dangerous and far away, so accidents and rebellions often occur, making it a place where things can easily happen.
Moreover, since the pacification of Wu, having soldiers from the six southeastern states guard the lower reaches of Kenliao has been the biggest hidden danger at present.
In addition, the inland troops were out guarding other places, and the Wu people themselves did not trust the imperial court. They should have strong generals to guard and appease them, so that they could be content with the status quo both internally and externally.
After the Sun family founded the country, there were many civil and military officials, the number of which was similar to that of our dynasty. Once the country was destroyed, they would be the same as the common people.
They did not see the benefit of being reborn, but believed that disaster and hardship forced them to lose their original land, so they harbored the intention of causing chaos.
Now there should be an elderly and virtuous king to rule the land of Wu, appointing officials according to their talents, using both civil and military services, so that the army and all kinds of labor do not come from these places, and those who want to seek wealth and honor can seek it within the feudal state.
The internal troops can be disbanded, and the newly acquired feudal state can be safe. It is the best of both worlds, and the dispatch is also very appropriate.
Therefore, among the kings with the same surname, those who are over 20 years old and have talents should be selected to entrust Wu and Shu.
Depending on the distance they traveled, the land given to them was twice that of the previous feudal countries.
For example, if the prince is young when he moves to the old place, it will not be too late to send him to rule those areas when he grows up.
It is more appropriate to deal with the urgent matters in those areas and obtain an older feudal lord.
The matters related to enfeoffment that I have reported have been summarized in general, but there are other matters that, if applicable, can be used as a reference for various previous systems, so they are all listed below.
I know: He who is not afraid of danger and disaster, but is willing to contribute what he hears and sees, is a loyal minister; he who listens to harsh words and is willing to accept bitter words is a king who can govern the world.
I am lucky and have the honor to meet the court who has no taboos.
Although he once wrote frankly and made speeches, and discussed state affairs extensively, he still did not report everything he saw and heard, pointing out the pros and cons, and received grace in vain, just like ordinary people.
I feel very ashamed and am unable to give my loyal advice and repay the favor. I will only list my experiences below.
I really don’t dare to claim that what I said is definitely correct, but I probably mean that I don’t conceal what I think.
If there is anything that can be adopted, it will be the year of my rebirth; if it is all nonsense, it will also be a good thing for the country.
Please take a moment, Your Majesty, to read my memorial.
I think that although Your Majesty obeyed the destiny and ascended the throne and became the founder of the country, the opportunity he encountered was the end of the world.
Why do you say this?
At the end of the Han Dynasty, the eunuchs monopolized the power, villains controlled the government, and the gentlemen were in the opposition. The country was abandoned and the people were scattered, and finally it declined and perished.
Emperor Wu of Wei used his talents and strategies to correct chaos and rectify culture and education. After decades of accumulation, by the beginning of Yankang, the officials were honest and the people were obedient, and the legal system was widespread in the world.
When it came to Emperors Wen and Ming, they were arrogant and extravagant. Become the leader who brings down the country.
However, it is still popular to travel and enjoy music and beauty at home, and there are threats from heroes from the three parties outside. All major national affairs can be successful, and there are few mistakes. What is the reason for this?
In fact, it was all based on previous prosperity to support current performance.
However, systems such as legislation, criminal administration, etc. have gradually declined.
From the early years of Jiaping, when the Jin Dynasty was established, to the last years of Xianxi, it took many years.
Although iron instruments of torture are often used to cut off some cruel people, the good people who are left behind are all given temporary favors and cannot be punished by the law.
In the early years of Taishi, after His Majesty ascended the throne, the people he appointed were all descendants of the heroes of the previous generation, either their descendants or their great-grandsons.
The ancients said that the nature of coveting delicious food is difficult to correct, so I said that I have met the end of the world.
In the troubled autumn, the world has just stabilized, and it is an opportunity to change one's mind and rectify the principles of discipline.
However, His Majesty still believes in employing appropriate personnel and loose laws. Over time, the Han Dynasty will be different from the entrepreneurs of the Han and Wei Dynasties. Our dynasty, which only emerged after three ancestors, did not use strict laws to rule overnight. This is indeed the case.
But in terms of government, correcting various things should naturally be based on the path of justice, and the law should be just and majestic, moving towards rectification day by day, just like a boat on the water. Although it cannot cross the rapids, it can move sideways and gradually move forward, and eventually it can cross the river.
From a little to a lot, you can now govern the country well.
However, in the past thirty years since the Taishi period, the achievements in state affairs have not been in line with the will of the Holy One, and various undertakings have not been as good as in the past.
With your Majesty's wisdom, you have not changed the ills of the last days, but you have accomplished great things and passed them on to future generations. Don't you have any worries?
In other words, can’t my words be placed in the heart of the Holy One?
Looking back on the major events of thousands of years, there are two truths.
Once a country in the world is stable, it is difficult to overturn it, and once it is overturned, it is difficult to correct it.
Therefore, a monarch who thinks about the longevity of future generations must carefully manage the current political affairs. Only by stabilizing the political power and leaving great achievements can future generations have something to rely on.
If the princes and kings are established at the same time and the vassal state is established and deeply rooted, the national destiny will continue endlessly and can be compared with the three generations.
If the state affairs and legacy of one's reign cannot be passed on to future generations, even if a vassal state is established, the system that builds the foundation of a great country is not established, and the successors can only rely on their own talents to build the great cause of the country.
If we cannot act according to reason, even in the future, the responsibility for the troubles will still be held on His Majesty. What will we do then?
I hope that Your Majesty can govern today's country well and establish an indestructible force, so that there will be no trouble in the world.
Saint wisdom cannot be passed on to future generations, and those who follow it are not necessarily wise. This is common sense.
Therefore, those who are good at governing the world will adapt to the situation rather than relying on others.
Complying with the situation refers to enfeoffing princes; relying on people refers to counties and counties.
By inspecting counties and counties, small political affairs can be managed but the big situation is very critical; as a vassal state, the princes will make many mistakes in the past but be very stable in the long run.
The sage emperor speculates on the shortcomings of the past and the present, weighs the principles of importance, tolerates the small mistakes of the princes, and stabilizes the great stability. This is enough to consolidate the domestic and foreign vassals and maintain the rule of the world.
King Wu was the holy master, and King Cheng was his virtuous successor. However, the reason why King Wu did not rely on King Cheng's virtuousness to establish a feudal kingdom was because he considered the long-term spread of the country's great cause.
Moreover, those who are good at talking about today's national affairs must use what happened in ancient times as verification.
There are incomplete historical records of events before Tang and Yu, so it is difficult to know the details at that time.
In the third generation, the benevolence of the saints and the relatives who established emperors were entrusted to them according to the fifth-level titles, so that they could establish the country and inherit the family, which was used to protect the royal family and ensure the long-term destiny of the country. The short time was five to six hundred years, and the long time was nearly a thousand years.
In the Qin Dynasty, the princes were dismissed and prefectures and counties were established. The emperor, princes and younger brothers were not given any land, so they were isolated and without help, and they perished in two generations.
After the Han Dynasty inherited the Zhou Dynasty and the Qin Dynasty, the princes, prefectures and counties were mixed and established, and each of them lasted for more than 200 years.
At that time, there was no need for enfeoffment. Although the vassal states had different strengths and weaknesses, and the system was full of mistakes and incomplete, the signs of their decline often showed that the kings with the same surname lost their power. The power of the vassal kings was weak, not because of their strength.
When the Lu family was in rebellion, they relied on the assistance of the two kings of Qi and Dai to stabilize the country.
When the Seven Kingdoms rebelled, King Liang defended the country and finally put down the rebellion.
From then on, the power of the princes and kings was reduced, and they only had the right to enjoy the rents and benefits of feudal states, and what was worse, they even had the power to ride in carts pulled by oxen.
Therefore, Wang Mang was able to usurp the Han Dynasty and realize his treacherous plan, causing the world to overturn and turmoil and harm the people.
After Emperor Guangwu succeeded to the throne, although he appointed his children as kings, he did not establish the system of establishing a country, and the country's destiny did not last long.
The Wei family inherited the Han Dynasty, confined relatives, and imprisoned their children. As a result, the fate of the country quickly collapsed, and the destiny was transferred to His Majesty.
From this we can see the fulfillment of strengths and weaknesses, and the signs of disaster and blessing.
In addition, although the Wei family was in the right position, facing south and proclaimed the emperor, the three parties had not yet submitted, and the imperial power could not override those areas. In fact, it formed a situation of confrontation between various countries during the Warring States Period.
The rise of the Jin Dynasty, Emperor Xuan pacified Yan, Taizu pacified Shu, and His Majesty destroyed Wu. It can be said that his achievements are unparalleled in the world. The territory is wider than that of the three kings. Places that can be accessed by cars and ships, and places that can be reached by human beings have become His Majesty's slaves. The unification of the four seas begins today.
We should take advantage of the opportunity of the great achievements of the emperor and the time of His Majesty's sage to enfeoff the land, make the children of the same surname the princes and kings, and establish long-lasting peace and stability for thousands of generations, which will be passed down from generation to generation.
I also heard that if a country has capable ministers, it will be peaceful, but if it has powerful ministers, it will be chaotic.
As for the imperial system, the monarch appoints the prince as his legitimate son instead of according to his age, and appoints his legitimate son as the older one rather than according to their virtuousness. This cannot be changed.

summary:
Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was born in Guangling and descended from Liu Xu, King Li of Guangling in the Han Dynasty. His family had been prestigious for generations, belonging to a group of four surnames—Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu—all originating from the Liu surname. His father, Liu Guan, served as the prefect of Pingyang. Liu Song demonstrated analytical abilities from childhood and was praised by contemporaries. Though recommended as a filial and honest scholar, he declined the position. Emperor Wen summoned him to serve in the Prime Minister's Mansion and sent him as an envoy to Shu, which had just been pacified. Finding the people hungry and the land desolate, Liu Song petitioned for relief but granted aid without waiting for approval, resulting in his removal from office.

When Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty ascended, Liu Song was appointed Shangshu Sangonglang, presiding over laws and redressing injustices. He gradually rose to Vice Minister of Zhongshu. During the Xianning period, he inspected Jingyang with Sanqi Lang Bai Bao and was transferred to Huang Menlang, then to Yilang and acting Tingwei. He reviewed the case of Shi Huyin, who was imprisoned without guilt, and proved his innocence, earning comparison to Zhang Shizhi. After six years in office, he was known for thoroughness and fairness. When Wu was conquered and generals competed for merit, Liu Song investigated and determined Wang Hun had highest merit and Wang Jun middle merit. The emperor considered this unreasonable and demoted Liu Song to prefect of Jingzhao, then transferred him to Hanoi. Before departing, he reported matters benefiting the country, petitioning to demolish water dams that caused disasters, bringing convenience to the people.

After his mother's death, Liu Song left office. Following the mourning period, he became Prime Minister of Huainan, where he was serious and organized with great political achievements. He reformed the construction of Shaopi, which previously required tens of thousands of laborers annually, by having the old and young work together with compensation based on repairs, earning praise for fair administration. Liu Song submitted a lengthy memorial discussing various state affairs, including the establishment of feudal states, the importance of enfeoffing princes to create stable foundations, and the dangers of relying solely on county systems. He argued that enfeoffment would ensure long-term stability, drawing comparisons between the Zhou Dynasty's long duration due to feudal systems and the Qin Dynasty's rapid collapse after abolishing them.

Liu Song also discussed the need for proper official evaluation, reducing labor burdens, developing agriculture, and maintaining grain prices. He criticized current governance for focusing on minor faults while ignoring major crimes, comparing this to leaving dangerous beasts on the road while strictly prohibiting mice. He advocated for simpler governance, long-term official appointments, and proper assessment of achievements. The imperial edict replied acknowledging his loyal service and requesting continued reports.

In the early Yuankang period, Liu Song followed Sima Yun into court. When Yang Jun was executed, Liu Song guarded the palace and was appointed Minister of the Three Lords. He later transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, establishing a nine-class system to reduce official turnover, but Jia Guo's specialized government prevented implementation. When Sima Lun killed Zhang Hua, Liu Song wept bitterly and rejoiced upon learning Zhang Hua's son had escaped. When Sun Xiu and others praised Sima Lun's achievements and proposed adding Jiuxi, Liu Song opposed it, citing historical precedents. Zhang Lin was furious but spared Liu Song due to Sun Xiu's advice. Liu Song soon died of illness, receiving imperial condolences and gifts.

Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng, was born in Zhongwu, Jiangxia. His father, Li Jing, was governor of Qinzhou. Li Chong was studious and talented, becoming orphaned early and living with his younger brothers, known for his friendship. He discussed the nine-grade system, arguing it was a temporary military measure, not a long-term governance method. He advocated for simpler systems with fewer grades and long-term official positions. He opposed limiting slaves and property, arguing that without restoring the well-field system, such restrictions were impractical. He recommended promoting reclusive talents like Huo Yuan, emphasizing the importance of selecting virtuous people regardless of background. Li Chong served as Protector of Expeditions and Prefect of Pingyang, respecting moral education and promoting talents. After his brother's death, he resigned. He died of illness at age forty-eight, leaving his family poor with no place for his coffin.

The historical commentary praised Liu Song for his loyalty, extensive discussions on feudal states, and refusal to compromise with the king of Zhao. Li Chong was commended for his integrity, uprightness, and recommendation of virtuous recluses. Both were considered cornerstones of the country.
