Over the next two nights, the emperor's condition worsened, so the queen asked Yang Jun to assist the government, and the emperor nodded and agreed.
So he summoned Zhongshu to supervise Hua Lu and Zhongshu Ling He Shao, and declared that the emperor had ordered them to issue an edict, saying: In the past, Yi Yin and Jiang Wang assisted in government affairs, and their merits will be immortal. Zhou Bo and Huo Guang were appointed, and their reputations were the greatest in previous dynasties.
Yang Jun, a servant, general of chariots and cavalry, the prince's Taibao, and a former general, has virtues and talents, clear and far-reaching judgments, assistants in the palace, and obvious loyalty and respect. His position should be corrected to be the third Duke, which is the same as the prime minister.
Yang Jun was appointed as Taiwei, Prince Taifu, Jiajie, and Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese and foreign military affairs. His positions as Minister, Recorder, and former General remained unchanged.
Set up six soldiers, 3,000 infantrymen, and 1,000 cavalrymen, and move them to the former residence of the vanguard general Yang Jue.
If there are bodyguards living in the palace, send 20 Sima each from the left and right guards, and 10 Sima from the palace to Yang Jun, so that they can go in and out with troops.
The edict was written, and the queen presented it to the emperor in front of Hua Guang and He Shao. The emperor read it in person and said nothing.
The emperor passed away two days later, and Yang Jun was entrusted by the emperor to live in Tai Chi Hall.
The emperor's coffin was about to be buried, and the Sixth Palace went out to say goodbye, but Yang Jun did not leave the palace and defended himself with hundreds of warriors.
The signs of disrespect started at this point.
Emperor Hui ascended the throne and promoted Yang Jun to the rank of Taifu, Grand Governor, and Fake Huangtie. He was in charge of the government affairs and all officials were under his control.
Worried about alienating him, he asked his nephews Duan Guang and Zhang Shao to serve as close attendants.
All orders issued by Shao were read by the emperor, presented to the Queen Mother, and then issued.
Yang Jun knew that Queen Jia's temperament was difficult to control and was very afraid of her.
He also extensively cultivated cronies and party members, all of whom led the forbidden troops.
So the clan complained and the whole world was indignant.
Yang Jun's younger brothers, Yang Jue and Yang Ji, both had outstanding talents. They repeatedly advised him not to do this again, but Yang Jun could not accept it, so he abandoned them at home.
Yang Jun did not understand the ancient meaning and acted in violation of the old rules.
The change of Yuan Dynasty less than a year after Emperor Wu's death was considered by those who discussed it to be contrary to the ancient meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals that the emperor's accession to the throne should be recorded after one year.
The imperial court felt sorry for the previous mistake and asked the historian to cover up the matter, so the year name was changed again in the first month of the next year.
Yang Jun knew that he had never had a good reputation and was afraid that he would not be able to live in harmony with the people around him, so he followed the precedent set by Emperor Wei Ming when he came to the throne and granted officials and rewards in an attempt to please everyone. He is strict and trivial in his political life, stubborn and self-willed, and cannot harmonize with the public.
Sun Chuping, the prefect of Feng Yi, had a close relationship with Yang Jun and advised him: As a foreign relative, in a position as important as that of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, holding great power and assisting weak masters, he should seriously think about the ancient morality of extreme respect, extreme honesty and humility.
In the Zhou Dynasty, Zhou Gong and Zhao Gong were the prime ministers, while in the Han Dynasty, Zhu Xu and Dong Mou were the prime ministers. No one with a foreign surname had the exclusive authority to succeed in the end.
Nowadays, the clan is close to the powerful, and the vassal king is powerful, but you do not participate in state affairs with them, harbor suspicions and jealousies on the inside, and cultivate cronies and secret parties on the outside. It will not take long for disaster to come.
Yang Jun couldn't obey.
Kuai Qin, the young master of Hongxun, was the son of Yang Jun's aunt. The two had been close since they were young. He was honest and honest, and offended Yang Jun many times with his stern words. Both Yang Jue and Yang Ji were heartbroken by him.
Kuai Qin said: Although Yang Wenchang is fatuous, he still knows that people are not guilty and cannot kill indiscriminately. He will definitely alienate me.
I could be alienated and excluded, I could not die with him.
Otherwise, how long will it take for the clan to fall?
Meng Guan and Li Zhao, the lieutenants in the palace, were not treated politely by Yang Jun, so they secretly fabricated Yang Jun's plot to gain national power.
Empress Jia wanted to interfere in government affairs, but because she was afraid that Yang Jun would not be able to do so, she was unwilling to serve the empress dowager in a womanly manner.
Dong Meng of Huangmen was appointed as eunuch supervisor when the emperor was the crown prince, and served the Empress Mai in Shu Palace.
After buying it, he secretly exchanged information with Dong Meng and planned to depose the Queen Mother.
Dong Meng then colluded with Li Zhao and Meng Guan to rely on each other.
Empress Jia ordered Li Zhao to inform Da Sima and Runan King Sima Liang, asking him to gather troops to attack Yang Jun.
Sima Liang said: Yang Jun is fierce and cruel, and death is right in front of him, so there is no reason to worry.
Kui Zhao notified Sima Zhang, King of Chu, and Sima Zhang agreed to his request and asked to enter the court.
Yang Jun had always been afraid of Sima Zhang, and had wanted to summon him back to the court to prevent him from causing trouble, so he allowed him to enter the court.
When Sima Zhang arrived, Meng Guan and Li Zhao petitioned the emperor to write a Shao book all night and enforce martial law inside and outside. They sent envoys to depose Yang Jun and return home as a marquis.
Ma Yao of Shu'an Company led 400 people in the palace to follow the envoy to attack Yang Jun.
Duan Guang knelt on the ground and said to the emperor: Yang Jun was favored by the late emperor and devoted himself to assisting the government.
Besides, without a son, how can there be any reason to rebel?
May your Majesty consider it carefully.
The emperor did not answer.
At that time, Yang Jun lived in Cao Shuang's former residence, which was on the south side of the armory. He heard that there were changes in the palace and summoned all the officials to discuss it.
Taifu's chief secretary, Sai Mian, persuaded Huaoxiang and said: "Now there is a change in the palace, and its intention can be predicted. It must be the eunuchs and ministers setting up schemes for Empress Jia, which is not good for the public."
We should burn the Yunlong Gate to protest, demand the heads of those who caused the trouble, open the Wanchun Gate, attract troops from the East Palace and the outer camp, and support the prince himself to protect the crown prince and enter the palace to arrest the traitor.
The palace was shocked and frightened, so the traitor must be killed and sent away, so as to avoid disaster.
Nanbi was always cowardly and unable to make a decision, so he said: Emperor Wei Ming has built such a big project, how can he burn it?
Fu Zhi, the servant, told Nuo Hui that night and asked him to go to Yunlongmen with Genjuan to observe the situation.
Baodui took the opportunity to tell the officials that it was not suitable for anyone to be alone in the palace, and then he stood up and said goodbye, so everyone ran away.
Soon Gong Bao sent out troops, burned Yang Jun's house, and ordered archers to shoot arrows at Yang Jun's house from a high place in the attic. Yang Jun's soldiers were unable to get out.
Yang Jun fled to the stables and was killed by a halberd.
Meng Guan and others received secret orders from Empress Jia to kill Yang Jun's relatives and associates. All three tribes were annihilated, and thousands of people died.
She also ordered Li Zhao to burn Yang Jun's private collection of books. Empress Jia did not want the imperial edict sent by Emperor Wu to be known to the outside world.
After Yang Jun was killed, no one dared to collect his body. Only Taifu Sheren, Basi Yanzun, collected and buried him.
At the beginning, Yang Jun recruited Sun Deng, a scholar, and gave him a quilt as a gift.
Sun Deng cut off the quilt in front of the door and shouted: "Cut, chop, stab."
Ten days later, he claimed to be sick and pretended to be dead. When the incident happened, his words came true.
During the Yongxi period, there was a man in Wen County who was like a lunatic. He wrote a book saying: The light is long and the euphorbia is the wall.
Although poison is popular, it still hurts oneself.
When Yang Jun lived in the inner palace, he used the halberd as a defensive weapon.
In the early years of Yongning, Shao Shu said: The uncle's family has lost its moral integrity and the clan has fallen. The feelings of the nephew and uncle are very sad.
I ordered Yang Chao, the Marquis of Xinting, to serve as the imperial captain and the captain of the cavalry, in order to soothe my feelings as expressed in the poem "Polygonum".
Yang Jue, whose courtesy name was Wenju, served successively as Shangshu Ling and General Wei.
He has always been famous and was favored by Emperor Wu. At that time, his reputation was higher than that of Yang Jun.
Because his brother was in a distinguished and distinguished position, he knew that power and favor could not last long, so he begged to resign. He was sincere and sincere several times, but he never received permission.
When he first married the queen, Yang Jue said: Looking at ancient and modern dynasties, if two queens were born in a family, none of them could be saved. Instead, they suffered the disaster of overthrowing the family.
Please keep this watch in the ancestral temple. If it goes as I said, it will save me from disaster.
Complied with him.
Zhao Xiu, the governor of the right army, wrote a letter saying: There are five sons in Wang Mang's family, and they are replaced by brothers.
Nowadays, the three princes of the Yang family are all in high positions, and God has repeatedly shown changes. I am secretly worried about this matter for Your Majesty.
Therefore, Yang Yao became even more frightened and insisted on dismissing his official position. The emperor obeyed him and granted him one million dollars in money and five thousand pieces of silk.
Yang Yao was known for his humility at first, but in his later years he gathered his cliques and framed Qi King Sima You to force him to leave the capital.
Yang Jue, the commander of the Central Guard Army, and Cheng Can, the commander-in-chief of the Northern Army, plotted to kill Yang Jue with his own hands when he saw him.
After learning about it, Yang Yao claimed that he was ill and could not go out, suggesting that the relevant officials would write a letter to impeach Yang Lin and have him be transferred to the position of imperial servant.
From then on, no one in the entire court dared to resist him, and his good reputation was completely lost.
When Yang Jue was about to be executed, he cried out for injustice and said: Everything is wrapped up in the stone box. You can ask Zhang Hua.
At that time, everyone said that reasons should be stated for him to comply with the precedent of the Zhong Yu incident.
However, Gendan's relatives treated the troubler as an enemy, and the person who urged the execution killed him. Everyone at that time lamented this.
Yang Ji, whose courtesy name was Wentong, served successively as the general of Zhennan and the general of Zhengbei, and then moved to the position of crown prince and tutor.
Yang Ji was talented and skilled. He once followed Emperor Wu to hunt under Beimang. He and his attendant Wang Ji both wore cloth trousers and jackets and rode in front of the chariot with a horned bow.
The beast suddenly appeared, and Emperor Wu ordered Wang Ji to shoot it, but it fell to the ground.
After a while, another one appeared. Yang Ji accepted the order and shot it again. The Sixth Army cheered loudly.
The emperor valued military attachés and often awarded appointments to noble relatives based on their reputation. Yang Ji was known as a competent official because of his martial arts skills.
He and his brother Yang Jue were deeply worried about complacency, so they earnestly advised him with his nephew Kuixun and others.
It was Yang Ji's strategy to demote Wang Zuo and leave the capital to serve as governor and establish the crown prince.
At first, Yang Jun was worried about Sima Runan and Sima Liang, the king, and urged him to go to the vassal state.
Yang Ji and Li Bin repeatedly tried to stop him, so Yang Jun alienated Yang Ji.
Yang Ji said to Fu Xian: If my brother Zhang Zheng transferred Sima to the capital and showed humility to him, our family would be saved from disaster.
Otherwise, it will definitely bring disaster to the family.
Fu Xian said: As long as the levy commander Sima returns to Beijing and works together to promote justice, peace can be established and there is no need to evade.
Ministers cannot have exclusive power. Should it be limited to relatives?
Nowadays, the clan is estranged and relies on the closeness of its relatives for peace. If the relatives are in danger, they must rely on the dignity of the clan as backup. This is the so-called lip-to-tooth dependence, which is the best strategy.
Yang Chuan was even more frightened and asked Husai: What do people think now?
Husai said: Your brother is in power and alienates and excludes the clan. He should be in charge of the government together with the four parties.
Yang Ji said: You can mention this when you meet my brother.
Shi Chong saw Yang Jun and said this, but Yang Jun did not accept it.
Later, he and several brothers were killed.
On the night when the disaster occurred, Yang Ji was summoned by the East Palace.
Yang Ji said to Pei Kai: Where should I go to wrap my clothes?
Feihu said: As the guardian, you should go to Shugong.
Chao Fei liked giving alms and had been in charge of the army for a long time. The more than 400 people who followed him were all strong men from the Sedi. They could hit the target as long as they shot arrows, and they all wanted to save Yang Ji.
Longmu has entered the palace, and everyone sighs and regrets.
Shi Chen said: Jia Chong, with his shallow qualities of flattery and mediocre talents in writing and writing, was lucky enough to catch up with the prosperous era, but he was unable to occupy a high position.
He drew his troops to commit rebellion without even the thought of suspicion and fear; when he was given the military power to attack Wu, he actually asked to retreat despite the difficulties. This was not only Wei's rebellion, but also Jin's sinner!
However, he enjoyed great favor and glory, held important civil and military positions, shouldered the important responsibilities of prime minister while he was alive, and had the honor of having tangerine sacrificed to the royal family after his death. It can be said that he enjoyed a generous salary without virtue, and disaster was about to happen.
As for his descendants, they are like beggars, inheriting the root of bad habits and indulging in evil and evil virtues.
For inciting that scheming woman to pursue that kind of family and world situation, even if she was killed, how could she be said to be absolved of her guilt?
In the past, Wei's collapse was due to Jia Zeng's hard work, and Jin's collapse was due to his hard work. It can be said that if you start in this way, you will end in this way. This is really true!
Yang Jun was favored by virtue of his status as a relative, so he took on the important responsibility of being a pillar. He was afraid that it would be too late to be respectful, but instead he was arrogant and extravagant. Can he avoid disaster?
Tong Kuo's mother saved herself because of her wisdom, Zhong Hui's brother was pardoned because of his words, Wen Ju had the same knowledge as his ancestors, but received the same punishment as his ancestors, how sad!
Zan said: The public flatters sycophants, and the thoughts are contrary to the right way.
When a good opportunity comes, he ascends to a prominent position.
Beggars carry on the family line, causing harm to the family and disrupting politics.
A mediocre writer occupies an important position.
He occupies a high position due to incompetence and eventually perishes.
Although Yang Yao was aware of it in advance, he also suffered disaster.
summary:
Jia Chong, courtesy name Gonglu, was from Xiangling, Pingyang. His father, Jia Kui, served as Governor of Yuzhou under Wei and was the Marquis of Yangliting. Jia Kui fathered Jia Chong in his later years, naming him "Chong" (meaning "fill") in anticipation of future joyful celebrations filling the streets. Jia Chong lost his father young and was renowned for his filial piety in mourning. He succeeded his father's marquisate and began his official career as Shangshu Lang, where he analyzed classical rules and regulations for his work. He later held positions including Huangmen Shilang and Jijun Diannong Zhonglang.

Jia Chong participated in military campaigns under Emperor Jing against Qiu Jian and Wen Qin at Lejia. When the emperor fell ill and returned to Xuchang, Jia Chong was left to supervise military affairs, earning an additional 350 households in his fief. He later served as Sima under Emperor Wen and was transferred to You Changshi. Emperor Wen, newly in power, sent Jia Chong to Zhuge Dan under the pretext of discussing plans to attack Wu, but actually to observe his intentions. During their conversation, Jia Chong hinted at the possibility of a dynastic change, but Zhuge Dan sternly rebuked him, declaring his loyalty to Wei. Jia Chong reported to Emperor Wen that Zhuge Dan would surely rebel, advising that summoning him would trigger a minor rebellion, while delay would cause greater harm. Emperor Wen summoned Zhuge Dan as Sikong, and Zhuge Dan indeed rebelled. Jia Chong accompanied the expedition and proposed a strategy of digging deep moats and building high forts to besiege the rebels without battle, which succeeded.

After the city fell, Jia Chong was promoted to Marquis of Xuanyang Township with an additional 1,000 households. He became Tingwei, known for correcting wrongful cases, then Central Guards Army commander. When Gaogui Xianggong attacked the Prime Minister's Mansion, Jia Chong led troops at Nanque. As his forces faltered, Cheng Ji asked what to do, and Jia Chong replied, "I have raised you for just this day." Cheng Ji then killed Gaogui Xianggong. Under the new emperor, Jia Chong was made Marquis of Anyang Township with 1,200 additional households, commanding城外 armies. When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Jia Chong was sent to supervise Guanzhong and Longyou, but Zhong Hui died before his arrival.

Jia Chong was deeply trusted by Emperor Wen, revising laws alongside Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, Yang Ku, and Xun Xu. He received the highest-class house and was named Marquis of Linyi. Initially, Emperor Wen considered passing the throne to Wuyang Hou Sima You, but Jia Chong praised Emperor Wu's virtues as the eldest son, convincing him to choose Emperor Wu. Upon Emperor Wu's succession, Jia Chong became General of the Guards of Jin, Yitong Sansi, and Marquis of Linying. He was later promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Attendant, and Minister of Public Affairs for his role in establishing the dynasty.

Jia Chong oversaw the revision of laws, which were praised for their leniency and simplicity. The emperor rewarded him with a marquisate for one of his children and 500 bolts of silk, which Jia Chong declined but was overruled. He succeeded Pei Xiu as Shangshu Ling while retaining his other posts. After his mother's death, he was recalled from mourning after 60 days due to affairs in the southeast. He devoted himself to agricultural savings and streamlining officials, earning imperial praise. Jia Chong recommended talents and treated others with sincerity, though he lacked integrity and relied on flattery, earning hatred from upright officials like Ren Kai and Yu Chun.

When Di and Qiang rebelled, Jia Chong was sent to guard Guanzhong as commander of Qin and Liang provinces. However, through Xun Xu's influence, his daughter was married to the crown prince, allowing him to remain in the capital. During the campaign to conquer Wu, Jia Chong was appointed supreme commander but was reluctant, fearing failure. He repeatedly advised against the campaign, but the emperor insisted. After Wu's surrender, Jia Chong was heavily rewarded but felt ashamed of his lack of strategy. He died in the third year of Taikang at age 66, receiving grand posthumous honors.

Jia Chong's wife, Guo Huai, was extremely jealous, causing the deaths of two sons by killing their wet nurses. After Jia Chong's death, his grandson Han Mi was made heir. His daughter Jia Wu secretly married Han Shou after an affair, which Jia Chong discovered but concealed. Jia Chong's descendants, including Jia Mi, became powerful but were eventually killed during political turmoil. The text concludes with commentary on Jia Chong's flattery and lack of virtue, contrasting him with his brother Yang Yao, who foresaw disaster but could not avoid it.

Yang Hu Du Yu
Uncle Yang Hu was born in Nancheng, Mount Tai.
He has been an official of two thousand shi for generations, and he has been in Yanghu for nine generations. They are all famous for their integrity and virtue.
His grandfather, Yangxu, served as the prefect of Nanyang in Han Dynasty.
His father, Yang Gou, was appointed as the prefect of Shangdang.
Yang Hu is the grandson of Cai Yong and the younger brother of Queen Jingxian.
Yang Hu's father passed away when he was twelve years old. He obeyed filial piety more than etiquette and served his uncle Yang Dan with great respect.
Once when he was playing by the Wenshui River, he met an old man who said to him: This boy has good looks and is less than sixty years old. He will definitely make great achievements in the world.
After he left, no one knew where he was.
When he grew up, he was erudite and could write articles, and he was seven feet three inches tall. The man is handsome and good at talking.
Xiahou Wei, the general of the county, thought he was unusual and married his brother Xiahou Ba's daughter to him.
He was recommended as a planner, and he was called up four times to serve as an official or scholar in the state. He refused to take up the post in any of the five prefectures.
Guo Yi from Taiyuan saw him and said: This is Yan Hui today.
Both Wang Chen and Wang Chen were recruited by Cao Shuang.
Wang Chen persuaded him to apply, but Yang Hu said: It is not easy to entrust yourself to others to do things for others.
When Cao Shuang failed, Wang Chen survived as an old official, so he said to Yang Ku: "Always remember what you said before."
Yang Ku said: "It was not what I considered at the beginning."
He was so prescient and boastful.
Xiahou Ba surrendered to Shu, and his in-laws broke off all relations with him. Only Yang Hu got along with his wife calmly, and was more loving and courteous.
Soon his mother passed away, and his eldest brother Yangfa died again. He lived in mourning for more than ten years. He regarded himself as honest and honest, like a Confucian scholar.
Emperor Wen appointed him as a general and summoned Yang Hu, but he did not go. Instead, he was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu in a public car, and soon he was promoted to Shizhong and Huangmenlang.
At that time, the prince of Gaogui County was fond of writing articles, and those in official positions often contributed poems and poems. Runan and Di were reprimanded for violating the emperor's wishes.
King Chenliu ascended the throne and granted him the title of Marquis of Guanzhong and the title of 100 households.
Because the young emperor was unwilling to serve as a minister, Yang Hu asked to leave the palace to find a position to fill the vacancy, and was appointed secretary supervisor instead.
When the fifth-level title was established, he was granted the title of Jupingzi and was granted the title of 600 households.
Zhong Hui is favored and jealous, and Yang Ku is also afraid of him.
Zhong Hui was executed and appointed as the Prime Minister of the country, Zhonglang, and jointly took charge of Zhongshu affairs with Xun Xu.
He was promoted to the leader of the central army, and all the guards were under his command. He was on duty in the palace, in charge of the imperial army, and took care of both inside and outside the palace.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession, and because of his assistance, Yang Hu was promoted to the rank of general of the central army. He was given the rank of casual cavalry and permanent attendants, and was granted the title of county prince, with a settlement of 3,000 households.
He resolutely refused to be ennobled, so he changed the title to marquis, set up a doctor's order, prepared the positions of nine officials, and added a lady's seal and ribbon.
At the beginning of Taishi, the edict stated: Unifying the key institutions that govern the political power, and fairly managing the six official duties of governance, education, and etiquette are the foundation of the government.
Yang Hu has a high moral character, is loyal, upright, simple and excellent, is proficient in civil and military affairs, and is devoted to the country. Although he is entrusted with important responsibilities, he does not take charge of the country's important affairs, which is not in line with my original intention of handing the responsibility to the ministers and governing by doing nothing.
He appointed Yang Hu as Zuopushe and General Wei, and gave him soldiers in his camp.
At that time, Wang You, Jia Chong, and Pei Xiu were all famous people in the previous dynasty. Yang Hu was always humble and would not let his position be higher than theirs.
The emperor had the ambition to reduce Wu, and appointed Yang Hu as the commander-in-chief of Jingzhou's military affairs, holidays, casual cavalry and general guards.
Yang Hu led his troops to guard the south, opened schools, and comforted people near and far, which was very popular among Jiang and Han people.
Show your sincerity to the person who surrendered, and the person who surrendered will be free to leave if he wants.
At that time, the chief official died in office, and the next chief official was taboo and often destroyed the old government office. Yang Ku believed that life and death were in vain and had nothing to do with living quarters, so he sent underground documents to the guards to ban them generally.
Wu State was more than 700 miles away from each other, which often caused border troubles. Chai Hu was worried about this and used strategies to make Wu State give up its defense.
So the number of soldiers guarding the border was reduced by half, and more than 800 hectares of farmland were given to the soldiers, which made a huge profit.
When Chai Nian first took office, the army did not have a hundred days of food reserves. After a few years, it had ten years of savings.
Xia Shao dismissed the governor of Jiangbei and appointed General Nan Zhonglang. He added all the troops under his command in Jiangxia in the east of Han Dynasty to Lan Bing.
In the army, Shengjie often wore a light belt and no armor. In the place where he lived, he only had more than a dozen bodyguards, and he often neglected government affairs because of hunting and fishing.
I once wanted to go out at night. Military commander Xu Yin blocked the door with a weapon and said: "General and governor Wanli, how can you be negligent!"
The safety of the general is also the safety of the country.
If I die today, this door can only be opened.
Yang Hu smiled and admitted his mistake, and rarely went out after that.
Later, chariots and cavalry generals were added, and government offices were established to set up subordinates similar to the etiquette system of the three divisions.
Yang Hu resolutely declined and said: "I heard Shao Shu, promoted me like a Tai Secretary."
Since I became an official, it has only been more than ten years. I have accepted internal and external appointments, which are often very prominent and important positions.
Often because my intelligence cannot grow in a short time and grace cannot be bestowed upon me for a long time, I tremble all day long and regard glory as worry.
I heard that the ancients said that if one's virtue is not admired by others and receives a high title, a talented minister will not be promoted; if one's merit is not admired by others and enjoys a generous salary, then the meritorious minister will stop working hard.
Now, because I am a relative, things are related to the current situation. What I have to guard against is being overly favored and not afraid of being forgotten.
However, an edict was issued to bestow upon me glory that should not be given to me.
What achievements do I have that I can bear, and what mood do I have that I can enjoy with peace of mind.
After humiliating the high position, the overthrow will soon come. At that time, if you want to guard the shabby house of your ancestors, how can it be possible!
Disobeying the emperor's orders does offend the power of heaven, but so does submissive obedience.
It is said that the ancients were able to express their ambitions and maintain the moral integrity of ministers because they were known to others, and they did not force themselves if they did not want to.
Although I am a villain, I have such thoughts because I have received grace.
It has only been eight years since enlightenment was implemented in the world today. Although I seek talents on the sidelines and do not send away people who live in seclusion or low status, I cannot recommend virtuous people and make meritorious officials prominent, so that the emperor knows that there are many people who are better than me and there are many people who cannot be distinguished.
If there are virtues that have been neglected in the market, and there are talents who live in seclusion among the people, and the imperial government does not think it is a mistake to use me, and I do not feel ashamed to be in a high position, isn't the loss not great?
Although I have been in the official position for a long time, I have never been as favored as I am today by having both civil and military positions, and enjoying a high position equal to that of a prime minister.
Moreover, although my knowledge is not broad, as far as I know, the current Guanglu doctor Li Yi is of high moral character and fair in his office; Guanglu doctor Lu Zhi is incorruptible and has few desires, and is modest but different from others;
Although they are also favored and serve as officials inside and outside, they are no different from me, but they have not yet received such favors. If I surpass them, how can I satisfy the world's expectations, and how can it be of any benefit to the future!
Therefore, I vow to stick to my integrity and have no intention of seeking promotion.
Now the country is not yet stable and the border is troubled. Please retain the previous grace and allow me to return to the border as soon as possible.
If you stay in the capital, you will definitely suffer from external worries.
The ambition of an ordinary man cannot be taken away.
The emperor doesn't allow it.
When he returned to his post, Bu Chan, the governor of Wu Xiling, came to surrender from the city.
Wu general Lu Kang attacked fiercely, and ordered Yang Hu to respond to Bu Chan.
Yang Hu led 50,000 troops from Jiangling and sent Yang Zhao, the governor of Jingzhou, to attack Lu Kang, but failed to win. Bu Chan was finally captured by Lu Kang.
Relevant officials reported: Yang Hu led an army of more than 80,000 people, but the enemy army was only 30,000.
Yang Ku was slow to mobilize his troops in Jiangling, which allowed the enemy to set up defenses.
So Yang Zhao was sent to involve part of the army into the dangerous situation. There were few soldiers and food supplies, and the army suffered a setback.
Disobeying orders and not having the integrity of a minister.
He could be relieved of his duties and return home as a marquis.
Because of his crime, he was eventually demoted to General Pingnan, and Yang Zhao was dismissed as a civilian.
Yang Hu saw that Meng Xian was running a military prison and the Zheng people were afraid of it, and Yan Ruo was stationed in Cambodia and Laizi was obedient. He then invaded the strategic location, built five cities, collected fertile land, and seized the Wu people's wealth. The west of Shicheng was all owned by the Jin.
From then on, people continued to surrender, and they promoted virtue and credibility to appease those who had just come to rely on him, and they naturally had the ambition to annex Wu.
Every time he fought with the Wu people, he fought only on the day of open battle and did not carry out sneak attacks.

In the past, the governors of the Han Dynasty also reported their work at the end of the year. There were no unified regulations for examination, and only general conditions were listed for whether their political achievements were good or bad.
The Wei family's assessment of officials, that is, the dispatch of officials from the capital, can be said to be extremely detailed.
However, because it is too detailed, it violates the original intention, so it has not been adopted in the past dynasties.
It is better to reiterate Tang Yao's old scriptures, discard the details and keep it simple, which will be simple and easy to implement.
It is human beings who can explain the common sense of things thoroughly and understand it from the heart and be able to analyze it.
It is unreasonable to exclude people and use the law exclusively.
Nowadays, the quality of the imperial examination is not as good as appointing prominent officials to evaluate the people under their jurisdiction.
After serving for one year, the outstanding person will be selected as the superior person every year, and the poor person will be classified as the inferior person. The name will be announced at that time.
For six years like this, the people in charge collected files and appointed those with outstanding performance over the past six years. Those who had been inferior in the past six years were dismissed from their posts.
Nowadays, the evaluation of political performance is indeed divided into difficulties and difficulties because of the different conditions for holding the position.
If something is considered superior because it is difficult, or inferior because it is easy, the person in charge must weigh the severity and slightly lower the grade, without completely bending the regulations.
"Edict of Ji Chou" believes that assessment is difficult to implement and uses the method of joint recommendation.
The reason for the recommendation is also based on hearsay.
It is not recommended to be promoted after six years, and it is not in line with the original intention of the ancient three-year assessment.
Nowadays, when there is an annual assessment, those who accumulate excellent ratings will be promoted, and those who accumulate poor ratings will be dismissed.
With the heart of a scholar and a gentleman, there will be no upright officials who are dismissed six times in six years, and officials with poor performance who are promoted six times in six years.
The Supervisor will also impeach at any time.
If officials at both the upper and lower levels blatantly tolerate mistakes, it means that public opinion is completely corrupted, and it has nothing to do with the assessment for dismissal and promotion.
Shi Jian, the captain of the Sili school, impeached Du Yu because of his original resentment, and Du Yu was dismissed from office.
At that time, the enemy invaded Longyou and appointed Du Yu as the military commander of Anxi, giving him 300 soldiers and 100 mounts.
When he arrived in Chang'an, he was appointed as the governor of Tongye, and concurrently as the captain of the Eastern Qiang army, the general of Qingche, and the official of Jiajie.
When the enemy was strong, Shi Jian was the general of Anxi and sent Du Yu to attack the enemy.
Si Geng believed that the enemy had strong soldiers and horses, but there was a huge disparity in strength between the government and the army. He should concentrate his forces and wait for the opportunity to attack in the spring. He stated five opinions that were not allowed and four that were not necessary.
Shi Jian was furious. He also reported that Du Yu had decorated the official residence at the city gate without authorization, and wasted military supplies by staying there. He sent the censor to deliver Du Yu to the court in a carriage.
Because Du Yu married a princess, within the scope of the eight arguments to reduce the punishment, he was treated as a marquis atonement. Later, the situation in Longyou finally turned out as Du Yu expected.
At that time, the imperial court believed that Du Yu was good at planning. When the Xiongnu commander-in-chief launched a fierce rebellion, he went from the west of Chazhou to Hedong and Pingyang. He ordered Si Yu to set up a strategy in the palace as a Sanhou, and soon he was appointed as the Minister of Zhi.
Zhu Ling then submitted a report to establish Yutian, a stable border, and other important matters of governing the country.
He also asked the producers to arrange new tools, build Changping warehouse to regulate grain prices, regulate grain prices, approve salt trafficking, formulate tax regulations, and made more than 50 suggestions that would benefit the country internally and aid the frontier fortresses externally, all of which were adopted.
When Shi Jian returned to the court from the army, his report of merit was not true, and he was impeached by Du Yu. They hated each other and had constant quarrels. Both of them were convicted and dismissed from office, and they assumed the title of marquis concurrently.
A few years later, he was appointed Shangshu of Duzhi.
The coffin of Queen Yuan will be moved to Junyang Mausoleum.
The old system was that after the burial, the emperor and his ministers were in mourning.
According to the minister's report, the crown prince should also remove his mourning clothes.
Du Yu suggested that the crown prince should restore ancient laws and mourn according to the emperor's wishes, and he obeyed.
Because the calendar at that time had errors and did not match the regular scales, Du Yu wrote the "Dual Dual Calendar", which became popular in the world.
Du Yu also requested to build a river bridge in Fupingjin because the Mengjin ferry was dangerous and there was a hidden danger of ships being sunk.
The reviewers believed that it was the place where the Yin and Zhou dynasties built their capital. Since the sages of the past dynasties had not built it, there must be a reason why it could not be built.
Du Yu said: "Building boats and building bridges" refers to building bridges on the river.
When the bridge was completed, the emperor and officials went to inspect it. They raised their glasses and said to Du Yu: If it weren't for you, this bridge couldn't be built.
Du Yu said: If it weren't for His Majesty's wisdom, I wouldn't be able to achieve this.
The water container from the Zhou Dynasty was still beside the emperor's throne when it arrived in Han Dynasty.
Due to the war in Momo, it no longer exists, and its shape and scale have not been passed down.
Du Yu creatively built it and reported it to the emperor. The emperor was very happy and praised it.
In the autumn of the fourth year of Xianning, heavy rains continued and locusts were infested.
Du Yu wrote a book about important matters for promoting agriculture, which were recorded in "Shi Huo Zhi".
During Du Yu's seven years in the court, he made countless reforms in various government affairs. He was praised both inside and outside the court, calling him "Du Wuku" and saying that there was no success that he did not participate in.
At that time, the emperor secretly had a plan to destroy the state of Wu, but most of the discussions in the court were contrary to this. Only Du Yu, Yang Hu, and Zhang Hua were in agreement with the emperor.
When Yang Hu fell ill, he recommended Du Yu to replace him, so he used his original official position as a leave to replace General Ping Cambodia and also conquered the Southern Army Division.
After Yang Hu's death, he paid homage to the general of Zhennan and the commander-in-chief of all the military forces in Jingzhou, and gave him a chariot and a second son-in-law.
After Du Yu took office, he repaired mail weapons, showed force, selected elites, attacked Wu Xiling and governor Zhang Zheng, defeated the enemy army, and increased the number of food households by 365 households due to his meritorious service.
Zhang Zheng was a famous general in the Wu Kingdom. He occupied a key position. He was ashamed of his unpreparedness and failed, and did not tell Sun Hao the truth about the casualties.
Du Huan wanted to alienate the Wu border generals, so he sent a petition to return the captured Wu soldiers to Sun Hao.
As expected, Sun Hao summoned Zhang Zheng and sent Wuchang Supervisor Liu Xian to replace Zhang Zheng.
Therefore, when the army arrived, Wu Guozheng changed his generals, which led to annihilation.
After Du Yu made the arrangements, he reported the date for the crusade against Wu.
The emperor replied that large-scale operations could not be carried out until next year. Du Yu listed the best strategy and said: Since the leap month, the enemy has only been on alert, and no troops have been raised downstream.
Judging from the rational situation, the enemy is short of troops and cannot protect both ends. He must first protect the upper stream and try his best to protect the lower stream. He will live in an ignoble manner and will not send a large number of troops westward to empty the capital.
But His Majesty misheard, so he abandoned his plan and indulged the enemy.
Conquering Wu is indeed the country's long-term plan. If action will lead to failure, there is no need to take action.
The policy of attacking Wu is to ensure safety.
If you succeed, you will be able to create a Taiping foundation; if you fail, it will just take some time, so why not give it a try!
If we wait until the year after tomorrow, the weather and personnel will not remain unchanged, and I am afraid that it will be even more difficult to defeat Wu.
His Majesty's previous opinion was to order us to march separately in the territory we guarded. The restraints on the troops should be the same in the east and west. This is a foolproof plan and there is no worry of failure.
I do understand in my heart, and I dare not seek trouble with vague opinions.
Please consider it, Your Majesty.
More than ten days later, Du Yu wrote again: "Yang Hu has many differences with the ministers of the imperial court. Instead of planning extensively first, he secretly implemented this plan with His Majesty, which aroused even more different opinions."
Everything should be done by comparing the pros and cons. Now this action is nine out of ten beneficial, and the other one or two are nothing more than futile.
Those who talk about ruined situations are also impossible, but because the strategy did not come from themselves and the credit does not come from themselves, everyone is ashamed of his previous remarks, so he insists on his own opinion.
Recently, the imperial court has different opinions on both big and small matters. Although people's hearts are different, and because they rely on favor and do not consider the consequences, they easily express the same or opposite opinions.
In the past, Emperor Moxuan commented on Zhao Chongguo's superiority. After the incident came to pass, he scolded those who disagreed and kowtowed to apologize, in order to block heresy.
Since the autumn, the situation of crusade against the enemy has been initially revealed.
If it is stopped now and Sun Hao is afraid and comes up with a plan, maybe moving the capital to Wuchang, further improving and building the cities in the south of the Yangtze River, moving the residents to distant places, the cities cannot be attacked, there is nothing to plunder in the fields, and accumulating large ships in Xiakou, then next year's plan may come to nothing.
At that time, the emperor was playing Go with Zhongshu Ling Zhang Hua, and Du Yu's above table happened to be delivered.
Zhang Hua pushed away the chessboard and said in his hand: Your Majesty is wise and powerful, the court is peaceful both inside and outside, the country is rich and the military is strong, and your orders are consistent. The king of Wu State was dissolute and tyrannical. Killing the virtuous and conquering Wu now can be done without any effort.
The emperor agreed.
In the first month of the first year of Taikang, Du Yu sent troops to Jiangling. He sent troops such as Fan Xian, Yin Lin, Deng Gui, and Xiangyang Governor Zhou Qi to lead the army along the western Liaoning. He was granted control and dispatch authority. Within ten days, he continuously captured the city, just as Du Yu expected.
He also sent Yamen Guangshang, Qie Zhi, Yuken and others to lead a surprise force of 800 people to cross at night by boat and attack Lexiang. They set up many flags, lit fires in Bashan, and moved in key places to weaken the enemy's confidence.
Sun Xin, the governor of Wu, was extremely panicked and wrote to Wu Yan: The armies from the north flew across the river.
More than 10,000 Wu men and women surrendered. Danzhi, Huzhen and others ambush the army outside Luanchi City.
Jiti sent his army to fight against Wang Jun, but was defeated and returned to the city.
The ambush of Zhou Zhi and others followed Zhuti's army into the city, but Xunti did not notice it until he returned under the military tent and captured Qiang Xin.
Therefore, there was a song in the army saying: Instead of fighting, one person is worth ten thousand.
So they invaded Jiangling.
The governor of Wu State pretended to surrender and mounted his troops on the city wall, and Du Yu conquered it.
After pacifying the upper reaches, south of Yuanxiang and as far as Jiaoguang, all the prefectures and counties of Wu State came to see the wind and presented seals and ribbons. Du Yu held the talisman to appease them with the emperor's order.
Fourteen Wu governors and supervisors were killed or captured alive, as well as more than 120 Yamen and county guards.
Relying on the power of the army, the families of migrating soldiers and garrison troops were replenished in the north of the Yangtze River. The places where the southern county was past were appointed officials, and the Jing land was cleaned up. The people from Wu came to seek refuge as if they were returning home.
Wang Liao first reported that he had received Xun Ti's head, and then Si Xi sent Sun Xin alive. Luoyang regarded Sun Xin as a big joke.
At that time, the generals gathered for discussion, and some people said: The enemy has been invaded for hundreds of years and cannot be completely conquered.
Summer is coming soon, there is a lot of rain, and diseases and plagues will occur. We should wait until winter before taking any big action.
Du Yu said: In the past, Zuosu annexed the powerful Qi State with the help of Zha west. Now the military power has been strengthened and the momentum is overwhelming. After a few sessions, everything is solved and there is no longer any effort.
So he ordered the commanders to go straight to save the situation.
There was no city that did not give up resistance.
The dissenters then wrote to apologize.
After being pacified, the army triumphantly returned. Due to his meritorious service, he was promoted to the title of Marquis of Dangyang County. He increased the number of fiefs to a total of 9,600 households plus the previous ones. He named his son Du Dan the Marquis of Ting, with 1,000 households, and was given 8,000 bolts of silk.
When they first attacked Jiangling, the Wu people knew that Du Yu had a tumor on his neck. They were afraid of his plot and tied a gour around the dog's neck to display it. Whenever there is something like a lump on the big tree, it is cut down to reveal the white color and written "Du Yu Neck" on it.
When the city is captured, hunt and kill all those people.
After Du Yu returned to his post, he repeatedly stated his family background and official position, said that military service was not his specialty, and requested to retire.
The emperor did not allow it.
Du Yu believed that although the world was stable, he forgot that war would be dangerous; so he worked hard to teach military preparations and establish schools. Jianghan showed his kindness and his education affected all directions.
Break through the mountains and barbarians, set up military camps, occupy key areas, and stabilize the situation.
They also built the ruins of Shao Xinchen, blocked and cleared several rivers to irrigate more than ten thousand hectares of farmland, and carved stone tablets to divide the boundaries of the fields so that there were regulations and public and private benefits could be achieved at the same time.
The people trusted him and called him Father Du.
The old waterway only led from Mianhan to Jiangling for a thousand and several hundred miles, and there was no passage to the north.
Baqiu Lake, where Yuan and Hunan meet, has mountains and rivers inside and outside. It is indeed dangerous and solid, which is what Jingman relies on.
Du Yukaiyang traveled more than a thousand miles from Xiashui to Baling, eliminating water dangers in the Yangtze River internally and communicating with Linggui's water transport externally.
The South eulogized him and said: There will be no rebellion in the future generations due to Duong, who can understand the wisdom, fame and bravery.
There was nothing Du Yu knew about the public affairs that he would not do without doing it.
Everything that is built and formulated must be inspected from beginning to end, and there are very few mistakes.
Some people ridiculed him for his meticulousness, but Du Yu said: Yu Ji's achievement was to save the world, and I did the same thing.
Du Yu valued leaving a name for future generations. He often said that "high banks can become canyons, and deep valleys can become mountains and mausoleums." He carved two stone tablets to record his achievements. One stone sank under the Wanshan Mountains, and the other stood on the Xian Mountain. He said: "Who knows that they will not become mountains and mausoleums and deep valleys in the future!"
Du Yuxing didn't ride a horse and couldn't shoot through armor, but whenever there was a big event, he stood among the generals.
Make friends with others, be respectful and courteous, ask them nothing to hide, teach others tirelessly, be smart in doing things and cautious in speaking.
After achieving meritorious service, he took it easy and indulged himself in the classics and wrote "Collected Commentary of Zuo's Classics in the Spring and Autumn Period".
He also referred to the genealogy of each family and wrote "Explanation of Examples".
He also wrote "Picture of the Alliance" and "Chunqiu Long Calendar", forming a family study, which was completed when he was almost old.
He also wrote "Praise to Women".
Commentators at the time said that Du Yu's writing was straightforward and unpretentious, and was not valued by the world. Only secretary Zhi Yu praised it and said: Zuo Qiuming originally wrote a biography of "Spring and Autumn", and "Zuo Zhuan" became independent in the world. "Explanatory Notes" was originally written for "Zhuan", but it expounded more than "Zuo Zhuan", so it is unique in the world.
At that time, Wang Nai knew how to tell horses and loved horses very much, and Nian Neng was very good at amassing money. Zhu Yu often said that "Wang Zha has a horse addiction, and Nie Wan has a money addiction."
After Genshi heard about it, he said to Zhuxuan: What is your hobby?
He replied: I have a "Zuo Zhuan" addiction.
When Du Yu was in the town, he coveted gifts to the powerful and important people in Luoyang many times.
Someone told him the reason, Du Yu said: I am afraid that they will do bad things, and I do not seek any benefits.
When Du Yu first arrived in Jingzhou, he fell drunk in the house because of a party.
People outside heard the sound of vomiting, peeked into the house secretly, and saw a big snake lowering its head and vomiting.
People who heard about it thought it was strange.
Later, he was conscripted as Sili Xiaowei, and was promoted to a special rank. He died while traveling to Deng County at the age of sixty-three.
The emperor expressed his condolences and gave posthumously the titles of General Zhengnan and Kaifu Yitong.
Du Yu made a will in advance and said: "In ancient times, people were not buried together. I understand the truth from beginning to end, just like starting from something to nothing."
The saints in the Middle Ages were buried together, probably because they were not buried separately, but because they were alive to show their enlightenment.
From then on, gentlemen were buried together or separately. They could not know life, so how could they know death?
When I was working as a Tailang, I once passed by Xingshan in Mi County on official business.
There was a tomb on the mountain. When I asked the farmer, he said it was Dr. Zheng's memorial to Zhong, or it was the tomb of Zichan, so he led his entourage to pay homage and watch.
The tomb is built on the top of a mountain, with a wide view on all sides. It connects the middle of the north and south of the mountain and is tilted to the northeast, facing Xinzheng City, which shows that we have not forgotten our roots.
The tunnel blocks the back of the tomb and leaves the front empty without filling it with earth, which means that there are no treasures in the tomb and the method of deep burial is not adopted.
There are many beautiful stones on the mountain but they are not used. We must collect natural stones from the Lishui River to build the tomb. The purpose is not to waste labor, but these stones have no use in the world.
The gentleman praised the tomb for its friendship and meaning, but the villain had no profit. It has not been destroyed after thousands of years. This is because it was buried sparsely.
When I entered the imperial court last spring, because of the death of the Guo family, according to the old regulations of the mausoleum, I proposed to build a future cemetery south of Shushouyang in Luoyang City.
There is a hill in the middle of the obtained area, and there are no old tombs on it.
Although it is not as tall as Xingshan Mountain, it is close to the Erling Tombs in the east, the palace can be seen in the west, Yishui and Luoshui can be seen in the south, and Boyi and Shuqi can be seen in the north. The place is open and has a wide view, making it a safe place to rest.
Therefore, trees were planted to clear the way and construction was carried out according to a certain system. At that time, all the round stones from Luoshui will be used to open a tunnel to the south. The etiquette will be imitated by Dr. Zheng, hoping to improve himself with a thin burial.
Coffins, small burials and other matters should be commensurate with this.
The descendants fully abide by the will.
His son Siwang succeeded him.
Du Xi's courtesy name is Shigu.
He was famous when he was young. His first official position was the literary scholar Wang Yi of Changsha, and he was gradually promoted to the crown prince.
He has an upright and loyal temperament. He has repeatedly advised the prince to express his sincerity, which makes the prince feel worried.
Later, a needle was placed in the felt where Du Xi usually sat, causing Du Xi to bleed.
Afterwards, the prince asked Du Xi: What are you doing recently?
Du Xi replied: I was drunk and didn’t know.
The prince asked: "You like to be harsh on others, why do you do wrong things yourself?"
Later he was transferred to the post of General Guard Commander Shi.
Zhao Wanglun usurped the throne and appointed him as the censor of the book.
Sun Xiu asked to date Du Xi, but Du Xi rejected him. Although Sun Xiu was resentful, she was afraid of his high reputation and did not dare to harm him.
Emperor Hui was restored to power and promoted Du Xi to the rank of official official and prefect of Chengyang. However, he did not accept the offer and promoted him to Zuocheng, the minister of finance.
When he died at the age of forty-eight, he was given as a posthumous gift a regular attendant on horseback.
His son Du Yi succeeded him, see "Biography of Foreign Relatives".
Shi Chen said: During the Taishi period, people and gods gave gifts, and Yang Gong proposed a strategy to pacify the Wu Kingdom. This shows the heart of heaven and earth.
In the past, the Qi State had Qianfu, and the Yan people worshiped ghosts at the north gate; the Zhao State had Li Mu, and the King of Qin stopped the momentum of annexing eastward.
Repay evil with kindness and eliminate old grudges.
Showing integrity in the south, the Wu people were defeated by the Han River, Jiangnan was pacified, and men, women, old and young returned home together.
As for success without taking any credit, he wears a scarf and lives in a poor alley. He is a generous and generous person.
Du Yu didn't know it from birth, he learned it with time, attacked cities and captured towns with his whip, and turned to war in the style of a Confucian general.
Confucius praised the four major disciples, but Du Yu respected three of them; "Spring and Autumn" is divided into five schools, and Du Yu was good at one of them, isn't he excellent!
Three years of funerals, no distinction between high and low.
It is lamentable that a person with a low status surpasses a person in power; it is too cruel for the prince to take off his mourning clothes after the burial.
He obeyed casually, did not seek the right path, and regarded the most outstanding people of the contemporary era as the concubines of the princes. Tan Gong learned to adapt etiquette, and Du Yu probably had the same situation.
Praising: Choosing water is dangerous and the river turns into a whirlpool.
Zhi Cocoon is kind and faithful, and millions of people surrender.
He swore an oath to go into battle without asking for a title.
In the literary world, Du Yu can be called omniscient.
summary:
Yang Hu, a native of Mount Tai, came from a lineage of high-ranking officials renowned for integrity. Orphaned at twelve, he was known for his filial piety and erudition, standing seven feet three inches tall with a handsome appearance and eloquence. He repeatedly declined official appointments, demonstrating foresight by avoiding service under Cao Shuang, whose subsequent downfall vindicated his caution. After his mother and brother died, he observed mourning for over a decade. He later served Emperor Wen as a palace attendant and was enfeoffed as a marquis. Fearing the favored Zhong Hui, he was relieved when Zhong was executed. Under Emperor Wu, he rose to general and marquis, but humbly declined higher titles. As commander in Jingzhou, he reduced border troops, opened schools, and won the loyalty of the people through sincerity and leniency toward defectors. He implemented agricultural policies that amassed a decade’s worth of grain reserves. Despite his relaxed demeanor, a military officer once blocked his unauthorized night outing, and Yang Hu accepted the reprimand. He repeatedly refused promotions, citing his lack of merit and fear of disgrace. His campaign to support Wu defector Bu Chan failed due to slow mobilization, leading to his demotion. He later built strategic cities, expanded farmland, and treated Wu soldiers with humanity, returning captives and compensating for requisitioned crops. His virtuous conduct so impressed Wu general Lu Kang that they exchanged envoys and medicine without suspicion. Yang Hu hated sycophants like Xun Xu and Feng Tong, and predicted that his nephew Wang Yan would corrupt morals. He advocated for conquering Wu, arguing that Sun Hao’s tyranny and Wu’s internal discord made victory certain. Despite opposition, he persisted, but died at fifty-eight before the campaign succeeded. His death caused widespread mourning, even among Wu soldiers. He was buried with honors, and his posthumous title reflected his humility. Two years later, Wu was pacified, and the emperor credited Yang Hu’s plans.

Du Yu, from Duling, was knowledgeable and pragmatic, believing virtue could not be forced but deeds could be achieved. His father’s conflict with Emperor Xuan delayed his career, but he married a princess and served as a minister. He survived Zhong Hui’s rebellion through wisdom. He codified laws, emphasizing simplicity and clarity to prevent violations. As Henan Yin, he advocated for straightforward official assessments, arguing that overly detailed regulations bred hypocrisy. He was dismissed after a conflict with Shi Jian but later served as a military commander, correctly predicting the enemy’s actions. He proposed numerous reforms, including new tools, granaries, and tax regulations. He built a bridge at Fupingjin despite skepticism, and crafted a water clock. Appointed to replace Yang Hu in Jingzhou, he repaired weapons, trained troops, and defeated Wu general Zhang Zheng, then alienated Wu by returning captives. He urged immediate conquest of Wu, countering objections about summer rains by citing overwhelming momentum. His forces captured Jiangling and other cities, leading to Wu’s surrender. He was enfeoffed as a marquis. After the war, he focused on education, irrigation, and stabilizing the region, earning the people’s trust. He carved stone tablets to record his achievements, predicting geological changes. Though not a horseman or archer, he led effectively and was known for his humility and dedication to the *Zuo Zhuan*, which he annotated extensively. He died at sixty-three while traveling, leaving instructions for a simple burial. His son Du Xi served as a crown prince’s tutor, known for his integrity, and survived political turmoil. The chroniclers praised Yang Hu’s strategic vision and Du Yu’s multifaceted talents, noting their contributions to unifying the realm.

Emperor Xuan's name was Yi, whose courtesy name was Zhongda. He was from Xiaojingli, Wen County, Henan, and his surname was Sima.
His ancestors were descendants of Chongli, the son of Emperor Gaoyang, namely Xia Guan Zhurong. After experiencing the Tang, Yu, Xia and Shang dynasties, he inherited this official position.
During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the person who served as Sima of the Xia Dynasty was a man named Cheng Baixiu's father. Because he conquered and pacified Xu Fang as a world official, he was given the family name of Sima.
Therefore, Longmo became their last name. During the Chu and Han Dynasties, Sima Yan was a general who joined the army of the princes in conquering the Se country.
After the fall of the Qin State, it was established as: Mudou, and the king's capital was established in Chi.
He designated the land as a county, and his descendants lived here permanently.
From Sima, the eighth generation descendant, Sima Gou, the general of the Western Conquest, named Shuping.
Sima Gou Sheng invited Tong Taishou to cultivate the land, named Gong Ji.
Dandan was born in Yuanbei, Dankentan, the prefect of Yuanbei, with the courtesy name Wuken.
When Siya was born and fled, Siken fell to Yin, whose name was Jiangong.
Emperor Xuan was Si Yaduo's second son.
Emperor Xuan had extraordinary integrity when he was young. He was smart, bold and had lofty ambitions. He was erudite and devoted to Confucianism.
At the end of the Han Dynasty, the world was in chaos, and Emperor Xuan often lamented and worried about the world.
Nanyang Prefect Dangyu, who was from the same county and was known for being good at identifying talents, met Emperor Xuan, who was underage at the time. He thought Emperor Xuan was an unusually talented person.
Cui Yanyu, a native of Qinghe who served as minister, was a friend of Emperor Xuan's brother Sima Lang. He once said to Sima Lang: Your brother is smart, wise and honest, and his decisive ability is outstanding. He is not comparable to ordinary people.
Six years after the founding of the Imperial Household, the county recommended candidates for the imperial office.
At that time, Yan Gen Zaoxuan invited Sikong to serve. After hearing about Emperor Xuan's reputation, he recruited him.
Emperor Xuan understood that Yi's fortune was declining, and he was unwilling to lose his integrity and succumb to Tadang, so he declined on the grounds that he had wind paralysis and was unable to eat and live normally.
Wei Genzuo sent a secret agent at night to spy on the situation, but Emperor Xuan lay motionless on the bed.
When Emperor Wu of Wei was appointed prime minister, he summoned Emperor Xuan to be a literary advisor and ordered the people sent there: If he makes excuses again, he will be imprisoned.
Emperor Xuan was afraid and took office.
From then on, Emperor Wu of Wei ordered Emperor Xuan to accompany the prince at all times. He was promoted to the position of Huangmen Shilang, then Yilang, Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, and soon he was transferred to the chief secretary.
Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to attack Zhang Lu and advised Emperor Wu of Wei: Liu Bei captured Liu Zhang through deception and force. The Shu people sent troops to fight for Jiangling before they surrendered. This opportunity cannot be missed.
Now if we go to Hanzhong to display our troops and show off our power, Yizhou will panic and seize the opportunity to march and attack the city, which will inevitably lead to collapse.
With this momentum, it is easy to establish achievements.
A saint cannot go against heaven's timing, nor can he lose his opportunity.
Emperor Wu of Wei said: People are suffering from lack of satisfaction. They have captured Longxi and still want to capture Shu!
In the end, he did not listen to Emperor Xuan's opinion.
Soon Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to conquer Sun Quan and defeated Sun Quan's army.
After the army triumphantly returned, Sun Quan sent an envoy to beg for surrender, presented a memorial to him, and stated that this was his destiny.
Emperor Wu of Wei said: This boy wants to roast me on the fire!
Emperor Xuan replied: The fate of the Han Dynasty is coming to an end, and the prime minister owns nine-tenths of the world, and serves the emperor accordingly.
Sun Quan became a minister, which was the common wish of heaven and man.
The reason why the Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou dynasties refused to give in and refuse was precisely because they feared God and knew God's will.

summary:
Emperor Xuan, named Sima Yi with the courtesy name Zhongda, was from Wen County, Henan. His ancestors traced back to Chongli, a descendant of Emperor Gaoyang, who served as Xia Guan Zhurong. During the Zhou Dynasty, a descendant named Cheng Baixiu's father was granted the surname Sima for pacifying Xu Fang. In the Chu-Han period, Sima Yan was a general. By the eighth generation, Sima Gou emerged, and Emperor Xuan was the second son of Si Yaduo.

From a young age, Emperor Xuan displayed extraordinary integrity, intelligence, and lofty ambitions, being erudite in Confucianism. During the late Han Dynasty's chaos, he lamented the state of the world. Nanyang Prefect Dangyu recognized his talent early on, and Cui Yanyu praised his wisdom and decisiveness. In the sixth year of the founding, he was recommended for office but initially declined due to illness, fearing the declining fortunes of the Han. When Emperor Wu of Wei (Cao Cao) summoned him as a literary advisor, he was threatened with imprisonment and reluctantly took the post. He served as Huangmen Shilang, Yilang, and Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, eventually becoming chief secretary.

Emperor Xuan accompanied Cao Cao on campaigns, advising against missing opportunities to attack Shu after capturing Hanzhong, but Cao Cao refused. He later followed Cao Cao to defeat Sun Quan. After Sun Quan's surrender, Emperor Xuan argued that the Han dynasty's fate was ending and Cao Cao should accept heaven's will. In the Wei Kingdom, he became crown prince and concubine, trusted by the prince, and was known as one of the four friends with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo. As Army Sima, he advocated for agricultural cultivation to support the military, which Cao Cao adopted, enriching the state. He also criticized corrupt officials Hu Xiu and Fu Fang, but Cao Cao ignored him; they later surrendered to Guan Yu, worsening Cao Ren's siege. Emperor Xuan advised against moving the capital, suggesting instead to ally with Sun Quan against Guan Yu, which led to Guan Yu's death. He also opposed relocating people from Jingzhou, allowing exiles to return home.

After Cao Cao's death, Emperor Xuan managed the funeral and escorted the coffin to Ye. Under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), he was made Marquis of Hejin Ting and Prime Minister Chang Shi. When Sun Quan attacked, he advised against recalling Cao Ren from Xiangyang, but was ignored; Cao Ren burned the city, and Sun Quan did not invade, causing regret. After the Han abdication, Emperor Xuan served as Shangshu, then military governor and censor Zhongcheng, later becoming Shizhong and Shangshu Youpushe. He guarded Xuchang and was granted titles, though he refused honors. During campaigns against Wu, he stayed behind to manage affairs. On his deathbed, Emperor Wen entrusted him, Cao Zhen, and Chen Qun with assisting the government.

Under Emperor Ming, Emperor Xuan became Wuyang Marquis. He repelled Sun Quan's forces, killing Zhang Ba. He was promoted to General of Hussars and garrisoned in Wan. When Shu general Meng Da rebelled, Emperor Xuan suspected his cunning and, despite warnings, marched swiftly, capturing and executing Meng Da in sixteen days. He then dealt with Shen Yi, who had forged edicts, and exiled Meng Da's followers. He advised leniency for surrendered border counties and proposed attacking Wu via Xiakou and Shuguan. He was promoted to general and joined Cao Zhen against Shu, but heavy rain forced a retreat.

When Zhuge Liang invaded, Emperor Xuan was sent west to command forces. He marched to Yumi, forcing Zhuge Liang to flee. He defeated Shu forces at Kongshan, capturing thousands. He predicted Zhuge Liang would not attack for three years due to food shortages, so he moved farmers and dug canals to enrich the state. In the second year, Zhuge Liang led 100,000 troops to Wuzhangyuan. Emperor Xuan avoided battle, despite Zhuge Liang sending women's clothes to provoke him. He petitioned for a decisive battle but was stopped by Xinpi. Zhuge Liang died, and Emperor Xuan pursued, confirming his death. He later learned Zhuge Liang ate little and handled all affairs, predicting his early death. He defeated Shu general Ma Dai and accepted surrenders from Di kings.

When Gongsun Wenyi rebelled in Liaodong, Emperor Xuan predicted he would hold the Liao River and estimated a year for the campaign. He advised halting palace construction to relieve the people. In the second year of Jingchu, he led 40,000 troops, crossing the Liao River and feinting south while crossing north. He besieged Xiangping, ignoring calls to attack the enemy camp, and defeated Wenyi after three battles. Despite heavy rain, he forbade moving camp, beheading a violator. He rejected surrenders, executed Wenyi, and killed 7,000 men over fifteen, plus 2,000 officials. He released Gongsun Gong and honored loyalists. He refused to give short coats to soldiers, citing public property. He dismissed elderly soldiers and mourned the dead.

Returning, he was granted more fiefs. When Emperor Ming was dying, he entrusted Emperor Xuan with the young King Qi, alongside Cao Shuang. Emperor Xuan became Taifu with high honors. He refused titles for his sons. Under King Qi, he repelled Wu attacks, digging canals for farming. He advised against Cao Shuang's Shu campaign, which failed. When Cao Shuang moved the Empress Dowager and controlled the government, Emperor Xuan feigned illness. He tricked Li Sheng into thinking he was dying, so Cao Shuang relaxed. In the first year of Jiaping, he deposed Cao Shuang during an imperial visit, executing him and his party. He refused the prime minister position and Jiuxi honors.

Emperor Wu, named Sima Yan with the courtesy name Anshi, was the eldest son of Emperor Wen of Jin. He was known for his tolerance, kindness, and magnanimity. During the Jiaping period of Wei, he was granted the title of Tinghou of Beiping and held various military positions. He welcomed Changdao Xianggong to the throne in Wuyang, became Zhongfujun, and was granted the title of Xinchang Xianghou in Jin. When the Jin state was established, he was made heir apparent and given the title of General of Fujun. Emperor Wen initially intended to pass the legacy to Sima You, but after opposition from He Zeng and others, Sima Yan was established as crown prince in May of the second year of Xianxi. Upon Emperor Wen's death in August, he inherited the titles of Prime Minister and King of Jin, implementing policies to relax punishments, pardon sinners, and reduce corvée.

In December of the first year of Taishi, Sima Yan ascended the throne as emperor after a formal ceremony in the southern suburbs, attended by numerous ethnic minorities. He issued an edict of general amnesty, changed the reign name, and granted various titles and rewards. He honored his ancestors with posthumous titles and established many kings and dukes. He promoted frugality, distributed palace treasures, and reformed the calendar. He also issued edicts to simplify laws, lift restrictions on certain clans, and allow officials to observe mourning periods. Throughout his reign, he conducted inspections, established institutions, and responded to natural disasters with relief efforts.

Emperor Wu's reign saw numerous military campaigns, including conflicts with Wu and various barbarian tribes. He expanded the empire, eventually conquering Wu in the first year of Taikang, capturing Sun Hao and unifying the realm. He implemented policies to stabilize the newly conquered territories, granted amnesty, and rewarded officials. He also faced internal challenges, such as rebellions and natural disasters, which he addressed through edicts and relief measures.

In his later years, Emperor Wu became neglectful of political affairs, indulging in banquets and favoring the queen's family, leading to the rise of relatives and nobles in power. He failed to depose the incapable crown prince, leading to chaos after his death. Despite his initial successes, his reign ended with turmoil, as the Western Jin dynasty eventually collapsed due to his lack of foresight and poor decisions. Historians note that while he had a good beginning, his later years were marked by decline and disaster.

Emperor Jianwen, named Sima Yu with the courtesy name Daowan, was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan. He was exceptionally intelligent as a child and beloved by his father. The diviner Guo Pu predicted he would revitalize the Jin Dynasty. Sima Yu grew to be pure-hearted with few desires, particularly skilled in discussing metaphysical matters. He was granted the title of King of Langxie in the first year of Yongchang, and later became King of Kuaiji. Throughout his career, he held various high-ranking positions including General of the Right, General of the Fu Army, and concurrently served as Secretary and Supervisor.

After the deposed emperor was removed, the Empress Dowager issued an edict declaring Sima Yu the rightful heir to the throne. In the eleventh month of the first year of Xian'an, he ascended as emperor. Huan Wen, who had previously deposed the former emperor, maintained significant power. When Huan Wen insisted on executing Sima Xi, the King of Wuling, Emperor Jianwen personally issued an edict refusing, stating that if the Jin Dynasty was destined to continue, Huan Wen should follow his previous edict, but if the dynasty's fortune was exhausted, he would make way for worthier men. Huan Wen was so frightened by this response that he broke into a cold sweat and abandoned the matter.

Emperor Jianwen was known for his graceful demeanor and disregard for material circumstances. He could remain calm even when Huan Wen deliberately created chaotic situations to test him. Despite his knowledge, he lacked grand strategies for saving the world. He was often afraid of being deposed, especially when the disaster star entered Taiwei after his ascension. He died at age fifty-three in the East Hall and was buried in Gaoping Mausoleum with the temple name Taizong.

Emperor Xiaowu, named Sima Yao with the courtesy name Changming, was Emperor Jianwen's third son. He was initially made King of Kuaiji, then Crown Prince, and ascended the throne upon his father's death. His reign saw significant events including the death of Huan Wen, after which the Empress Dowager briefly returned to court. The famous Battle of Fei River occurred during his reign, where Jin forces defeated Fu Jian's massive army, capturing tens of thousands of enemy soldiers.

Emperor Xiaowu was known for his intelligence and enlightenment in youth. After establishing his authority, however, he became indulgent in wine and sensual pleasures, often drinking through entire nights. He showed little concern for celestial omens, once toasting a comet and declaring that no emperor had ever lived ten thousand years. His reign was marked by natural disasters including earthquakes, floods, and droughts. He died suddenly at age thirty-five after drunkenly teasing his favored consort Zhang Guiren about her age, which led to her killing him in anger. He was buried in Longping Mausoleum.

The historical commentary notes that Emperor Jianwen governed during difficult times with Huan family controlling government orders. After Emperor Xiaowu's ascension, treacherous officials perished naturally, and capable ministers like Xie An, Wang Biaozhi, Huan Chong, and Xie Xuan emerged. However, the decline of the Jin Dynasty was ultimately attributed to human failings rather than divine will.

Emperor Jing's famous teacher, named Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.
Elegant and charming, calm and perseverant, with far-reaching strategies.
When he was young, he had a good reputation and was as famous as Xia Houxuan and He Yan.
He Yan often said: Sima Ziyuan is the one who can achieve great things in the world.

Formulate methods for selecting talents, promote people without exceeding their merits, and officials have no selfish feelings.
