summary:
It describes the Zhou etiquette system, where the emperor maintained a hierarchy of concubines—three wives, nine concubines, twenty-seven wives, and eighty-one royal wives—to govern women's education. The "Huanyi" compares the emperor and empress to the sun and moon, complementing each other like yin and yang. During the early Yi Dynasty, Qin titles were adopted, with the emperor's mother called empress dowager and his wife called empress, while other women received titles like beauty, beloved, eighth son, and seventh son. By the time of the ridge stem, there were fourteen titles including Jieyu. From the Wei and Zhi dynasties onward, queen mother titles followed Mo Dynasty rules, while wife titles varied by generation.

Emperor Gaozu, learning from past extravagance that led to ruin, practiced frugality, ate simple food, and wore plain clothes. His first wife died early, leaving the queen position vacant, and concubine numbers remained stable. Taizong and Shidan, heirs from outside the country, had concubines who died before them, so no new boudoirs were built. The text then details the lineage of a queen, whose grandfather was a salt magistrate. Her mother, Mrs. Xiao, was Saitong's cousin. The queen became Saitong's concubine during Sai Chengtai's reign, bearing King Lu Deng of Xuanwu in Changsha, Lu Ti of King Zhao of Yongyang, and Zhidan. Early in her household, she saw Changpu flowers glowing in the hall, swallowed them, and conceived Gaozu. Before giving birth, she saw many people in the hall. She later gave birth to Xiao Chang, King Xuan of Hengyang, and a daughter. She died in the seventh year of Taishi in the Song Dynasty and was buried in Dongcheng Mountain. In the first year of Tianjian, she was posthumously honored as queen with the title Mi.

Her father, Mu Zhi, was a sixth-generation grandson of Zhang Hua, a Jin Dynasty Sikong. After Zhang Hua's punishment, Mu Zhi's great-grandfather was transferred but recalled. Mu Zhi served as a member of the Communist Party of China during the Song, Yuan, and Jia years, befriending Jiang Zhan and Yuan Shu. Foreseeing disaster, he sought an outside post, becoming General Ningyuan and Governor of Jiaosha, where he governed well. After the governor's death, he calmed the territory. Emperor Severn praised him but he died before being appointed governor of Manye. His son Hongji died in office. Gaozu posthumously gave Mu Zhi the title of Guanglu Doctor and a gold medal, later adding Ting Wei Qing. Hongzhan had no sons, so his nephew Hongce's son Zhang Lan became his heir.

Empress Xiao Yan, Emperor Wu of Liang, was from Jinxiang, Gaoping. Her grandfather Xi Shao was a teacher to King Shu Hai, and her father Xi Ye was a crown prince who died early. Her mother, Princess Xunyang, dreamed of having a son before her birth. At birth, a red light shone, alarming the family. A wizard performed an exorcism. The queen was intelligent, skilled in calligraphy, and loved history. She refused marriage proposals from the Song deposed emperor and Anlu King Xiao Mian. At the end of Jianyuan, Gaozu became engaged to her. They had three daughters. In the first year of Chengtai, she served as governor of Zong Maggot, then died in Xiangyang in the first year of Yongyuan at age thirty-two. She was buried in Dongchengshan. In the second year of Zhongxing, she was granted the title of Liang Gong Concubine, and later queen. Her posthumous title was Empress De, and her tomb was Xiuling. Her father Xi Ye was posthumously named Doctor Jin Ziguanglu.

Taizong's Queen Jian, named Wang, was from Linyi, Langxie. Her grandfather Wang Jian was a Taiwei and Duke Wenxian. She was gentle and wise, becoming Princess Jin'an in the eleventh year of Tianjian. She bore Prince Ai, Prince Zuolian of Nanjun, and Princess Chengshan. She became crown princess in the third year of Zhongdatong and died in the third year of Li Zha at age forty-five. Taizong posthumously titled her empress with Mi Jian, and she was buried in Zhuangling. An imperial decree mandated frugality for her funeral, citing historical precedents. Her father Wang Qian, originally named Si Ji, changed his name to avoid conflict with Emperor Qi Gao. He served as a foreign minister, Prince Xima, and prefect of Yixing, later becoming a hussar councilor and Huangmenlang. He was calm and did not seek advancement. At the end of Yongyuan, he refused promotion to Shizhong. Under Gaozu, he served as Grand Sima consultant and later Shizhong. After the abdication, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nanchang County. He died in the third year of his life at age forty-nine, posthumously granted Shizhong and Jin Ziguanglu Doctor.

Emperor Gaozu's concubine Ding, named Lingguang, was from Qiao State, living in Xiangyang. Born in Fancheng with a divine light and purple smoke, she was named "Light." A fortune teller predicted her wealth. At fourteen, Gaozu married her. She had a red mole on her left arm that disappeared when she was sent away. She served Empress De carefully and once saw divine figures. During Gaozu's rebellion, Crown Prince Zhaoming was born. In the first year of Tianjian, she was made a noble concubine, living in Xianyang Hall. A minister argued that her status should be respected due to her son, citing historical precedents. She was kind, frugal, and avoided luxury. She promoted Buddhism, refused meat, and ate only vegetables. On her ordination day, sweet dew fell. She was proficient in the Pure Name Sutra. She died in the seventh year of her life at age forty-two. A condolence poem praised her virtues. She was posthumously titled Mu. After Taizong ascended, she was honored as Empress Dowager Mu. Her father was a governor.

Emperor Gaozu's doctor, Zhao Yao, originally surnamed Hu, was from Hejikung Yao. King Zha Shi'an took her as a concubine. After Dong Guang's defeat, she was brought into the palace by Donghun Hou. After Jianchenyuan was pacified, Zhidan accepted her as a palace maid. In the seventh year of Yue, she gave birth to Shidan and was granted the title of Xiurong. She died in the sixth year of Zuo Hui at age sixty-seven and was buried in Tongwang Mountain. After Shidan became emperor, she was honored as Empress Dowager Wenxuan. Her father was posthumously granted titles, and her mother was made a marquis's wife.

Shizu's concubine Xu, named Zhaopei, was from Tan in the East China Sea. Her grandfather was a Taiwei and Duke Wenzhong, and her father was a general. In the 16th year of Tianjian, she was named Princess Xiangshu. She bore Fang Deng and Princess Hanzhen. In the third year of Taiqing, she was ordered to commit suicide and buried in Waguan Temple. The text concludes that the empress supported royal customs, while Mu Guifei's glory was displayed through her son, but the ancestor's concubine Xu lacked virtue and brought about her own destruction.

Pei Ziye, whose courtesy name was Jiyuan, was a native of Wenxi, Hedong, and the eighth-generation grandson of Pei Kang, Prince Zuo of the Jin Dynasty.
His elder brother Pei Li and his younger brothers Pei Kai and Pei Chuo were all famous and were called the Four Peis.
Great-grandfather Pei Songzhi was a Taizhong doctor in the Song Dynasty.
His grandfather Pei Si was a foreign soldier of Nan Zhonglang and joined the army.
My father Zhaoming is a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi.
His mother died after Ziye was born. He was raised by his grandmother. When he was nine years old, his grandmother passed away. He burst into tears and his family was surprised.
When he was young, he was studious and good at writing articles.
He started his career and entered the court as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. He joined the army as the King of Jiangxia on the right and resigned due to his father's death.
His behavior during the period of mourning was completely in line with etiquette. Every time he went to the tomb, the grass withered for him when he was crying, and a white rabbit crouched beside him.
In the early years of Tianjian, Shangshu Pushe Fan Yun praised his conduct and was about to report it to the emperor. However, due to Fan Yun's death, the matter was not completed.
Ren Fang, a Le'an native, had a good reputation and was admired by his descendants. Anyone who studied under him would be recommended by Ren Fang.
Ziye is Ren Fang's cousin, but he doesn't go to see him, and Ren Fang resents him.
After a long time, in addition to being granted the title of King Ancheng of the Right Army to join the army, he was immediately moved to the post of concurrently serving as Wei Zheng.
At that time, criminal judgment documents were jointly signed by officials from the three parties. Once when Ziye was absent, his colleagues signed his name. The memorial was not approved, and Ziye was implicated and was dismissed.
Someone advised him to explain the facts to Yusi, and he would be clear of fault.
Ziye smiled and replied: "Although I feel ashamed that I don't have Liu Ji's conduct, I can't get a job by litigating."
He has been deposed for a long time since then and has no hatred at all.
In the second year, Xiao Jing, Marquis of Wu Ping, was appointed as the governor of Southern Yanzhou. He was introduced to serve as the champion. After Xiao Jing was transferred, he was dismissed.
At that time, Zhongshu Fan Zhen had no contact with Ziye, but he praised him when he heard that he had good character and industry achievements.
Fan Zhenqian was appointed as the doctor of Guozi, and he immediately recommended Ziye, saying: I heard that Pei Ziye, the former secretary of the Champion Mansion, joined the army in Hedong. He was forty years old and had a few words. He was endowed with superhuman conduct when he was young. When he grew up, he developed excellent moral integrity. He followed etiquette during mourning. Grief was almost life-threatening. After the mourning period was over, he still had no food.
He was in a lower position, with a humble body and a low reputation, but his temperament was not greedy and he did not deceive his spouse. Therefore, knowledgeable people respected him and people in his hometown admired him.
Moreover, his family knowledge has been passed down from generation to generation, he has studied Confucianism and history, read a lot of books, and devoted himself to research and writing in his daily life and actions.
He is the author of twenty volumes of "Song Lue", which runs through the beginning and end, writing the history of a dynasty and writing articles and records, which are worth watching.
Moreover, the analysis of chapters and sentences is accurate and detailed, and the explanations of words can be handed down from generation to generation. If he is allowed to serve in the school, it will be a great reward for future generations, and the debate on misinformation issues such as Yikui can be found.
The royal family is glorious, the court is full of wise men, the officials have surpassed the era of Youma, and the number of talented people has surpassed the era of Ji. Even small kindnesses are recorded. No matter how big or small, as long as there is a little bit of use, there is no limit to the level.
I have read all the things that the kings of ancient and modern times respected and liked the virtuous and virtuous, but I have never been as diligent as this dynasty.
I dare to follow the truth and show my foolish opinions, and I beg to be given the position I am unworthy of, and to give it back to Ziye.
In this way, the virtuous and the unworthy will each have their own place, and everyone will be asked for their opinions, and everyone will respect and trust them.
Although the minister and Ziye never drank together, they rarely made any falsehoods when visiting people in the city. They expressed their opinions very respectfully and took the liberty to state what they heard.
May Your Majesty have mercy on my sincere heart, recognize my foolish loyalty and offense, and beg for forgiveness.
Some officials believed that Pei Ziye's qualifications did not meet the qualifications for promotion and he was not approved.
Soon he was awarded the title of Minister Bibu Lang, and joined the army in Renwei Jishi.
When he was appointed as a censure and order, whipping was not carried out when he was in the county. If the people had disputes, he explained the truth to them clearly, and the people praised him, and there were no lawsuits in the whole territory.
At first, Pei Ziye's great-grandfather Pei Song was ordered to continue the "History of the Song Dynasty" compiled by He Chengtian during the Song and Yuan Dynasties. He died before completing it. Ziye often wanted to complete his father's work.
By the end of the Yongming Dynasty of Qi Dynasty, the "Book of Song" written by Shen Yue had been published, and Ziye edited and edited the history of the Song Dynasty into twenty volumes of "Song Lue".
His narrative comments were full of sublime points. Shen Yue read them and praised them, saying: I can't keep up with him.
Xiao Chen from Lanling, Fu Gu from Beidi, and Dantu from Dayi all praised him and valued him.
As a result, the Minister of Civil Affairs, Daedian, recommended him to Shandan and appointed him as a writer, responsible for compiling national history and daily life notes.
Immediately, he was concurrently appointed Zhongshu Tongshi Shiren, and soon he was appointed Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, and his duties as author and Shiren remained as before.
He was also ordered to be in charge of Zhongshu's imperial edicts.
During the period of the Han Dynasty, there were Baiti and Hua Kingdoms outside the Great Wall in the northwest, and they sent envoys from the Minshan Road to pay tribute.
These two countries have never had envoys to meet with each other in the past dynasties, and they do not know the national conditions.

The imperial order still asked him to compile the "Picture of Envoys from Fang Kingdom", which extensively described the grand occasion of attracting people from outside the Great Wall. From remote areas to overseas, there were a total of twenty countries.
Ziye and Liu Xian from Peiguo, Liu Zhilin from Nanyang, Yin Yun from Chenjun, Ruan Xiaoxu from Chenliu, Gu Xie from Wujun, and Wei Leng from Jingzhao were all well-read and deeply appreciated and loved each other. Liu Hao respected Ziye even more.
At that time, Xiao Kan, the Marquis of Wuping, and Zhang Zuan, a native of Fanyang, asked Ziye to judge whenever they discussed ancient books and had any disputes.
In the seventh year of the ordinary year, Wang Shi went north to conquer Wei and ordered Ziye to draft an edict against Wei. Ziye immediately wrote it after receiving the edict. Because of the heavy weight of the matter, Gaozu summoned Xu Mian, Prince Zhanshi Zhoushe, Hongluqing Liu Zhilin, and Zhongshu Minister Zhu Yi to gather in Shouguang Hall to read the article. Everyone present was amazed.
Emperor Gaozu looked at Ziye and said: Although his appearance is weak, his writing is heroic.
Immediately, he was ordered to draft an edict to Wei Xiangyuan. After accepting the edict that night, Ziye thought that it could be submitted tomorrow, so he did not start writing. After the performance, the stage manager was very complimentary.
Naturally, he was asked to draft all kinds of talismans.
Ziye's articles were elegant and quick to write, and he did not advocate gorgeous words and sentences. His style mostly imitated the ancients, which was different from today's style. Some people slandered him at the time, but they all respected him later.
When asked about the reason why he wrote quickly, Ziye replied: "People's articles are written by hand, and I wrote them with my heart alone. Although there are differences that I can see and cannot see, the modifications are the same."
Soon he was moved to the post of Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and the other posts remained as before.
In the first year of Datong, he was transferred to Hongluqing, and then concurrently served as the infantry captain.
Ziye served in the palace for more than ten years. He was quiet, clean and self-respecting. He never made any demands. Since his mother's family and father's family were poor, he gave all his salary to them.
There was no residence, so we borrowed two acres of official land and built several thatched houses.
His wife and children often suffered from hunger and cold, but he only focused on teaching. His children and nephews respected him as they served their father.
In his later years, he believed deeply in Buddhism, strictly abided by religious rules, and only ate vegetarian food throughout his life.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he died in office at the age of sixty-two.
First, Ziye himself estimated that his death date would not be past the Gengxu year.
In the year of Zao, he reflected on himself and asked to retire. He said to his colleague Liu Zhiheng: I am going to pass away.
We must be frugal and moderate in dispatching and funeral arrangements.
Emperor Gaozu mourned and shed tears for him.

Sudden loss makes people sad and missed.
He can be given as a posthumous gift to the regular attendants of Sanqi, 50,000 yuan for the funeral, and 50 pieces of cloth, and he will be buried in the near future.

Shaoling also compiled twenty volumes of "Biography of Gan Seng", two volumes of "Hundred Officials and Nine Ranks", one volume of "Fu Yi Mi Fa", one volume of "Pictures of Fang Guo Envoy", and twenty volumes of collected works, all of which have been circulated in the world.

Pei Ziye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was from Wenxi, Hedong, and a descendant of Jin Dynasty royalty. He was raised by his grandmother after his mother died at his birth, and showed deep filial piety when she passed when he was nine. Known for his studiousness and literary skill, he began his official career as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. His mourning period for his father was so exemplary that withered grass and a white rabbit appeared at his father's tomb. Fan Yun praised his conduct but died before reporting it to the emperor. Ren Fang, a famous scholar, resented Ziye for not visiting him, despite being a cousin. Ziye later served as a military advisor but was dismissed when a document was signed in his absence without his knowledge. He refused to litigate to clear his name, accepting the dismissal without resentment.

Fan Zhen later recommended Ziye, praising his moral integrity, filial piety, and scholarly achievements, including his twenty-volume "Song Lue." Despite some officials objecting to his qualifications, Ziye was appointed as Minister Bibu Lang and later as a county magistrate, where he resolved disputes through reasoning, eliminating lawsuits. He completed his great-grandfather's unfinished history, earning praise from Shen Yue and others. He was then appointed as a historian and editor, known for his broad knowledge, such as identifying the origins of envoys from the Baiti and Hua kingdoms. He compiled the "Picture of Envoys from Fang Kingdom" and was admired by contemporaries like Liu Xian and Liu Zhilin. In the seventh year of the ordinary year, he drafted an edict against Wei quickly, impressing Emperor Gaozu with his heroic writing. Ziye's style imitated the ancients, and he wrote quickly, saying he wrote with his heart. He served in the palace for over a decade, living frugally, giving his salary to poor relatives, and supporting his family on borrowed land. He was a devout Buddhist vegetarian in his later years. He died at sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him, granting posthumous honors and a burial. His works include "Collection of Mourning Clothes," "Continued Biography of the Pei Family," and others.

Gu Xie, courtesy name Zhengli, from Wu County, lost his father young and was raised by his grandfather. As a child, he expressed a desire for seclusion, impressing his maternal grandfather. He was studious and praised for his concentration. He began his career as a historian in Yangzhou and later as a Taixue doctor. Minister Shen Yue praised his policy essay as unmatched since the Eastern Jin. He served in various roles, including as a magistrate and military advisor. At sixty, he was recommended for his conduct and knowledge, though he remained indifferent to fame. He was appointed as a minister and died at seventy-three. The emperor mourned him, noting his honesty and lack of close relatives. Gu Xie was known for his integrity, refusing gifts and living frugally. He married his uncle's daughter in his sixties, having no children. He was well-read and compiled works like "Yi Xing Yuan" and "Suo Yu."

Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, from Donghai, was studious and known for his innovative writing. He served as a Taixue doctor and was recommended by Zhou She to accompany Prince Jin'an, despite his plain appearance. He held various posts, including as a magistrate and military advisor. His writing style, known as "gong style," was imitated in the palace, initially angering Emperor Gaozu but later earning his favor. Zhu Yi, feeling threatened, had Xu Zhai appointed as prefect of Xin'an, where he governed fairly and improved customs. He later served as a general and advisor on marriage rituals, advising the emperor on proper etiquette. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Xu Zhai stood firm, impressing Hou Jing with his fierceness. He died at seventy-eight after refusing a general title. His eldest son, Xu Ling, was famous.

Bao Quan, courtesy name Runyue, from Donghai, was well-read and skilled in writing. He served Emperor Yuan and was appointed governor of Xinzhou. He defeated Xiao Yu but was later accused of delaying the king's army and imprisoned by Wang Sengbian. He was forgiven and later served as chief historian in Yingzhou. The city fell due to neglect by Fang Zhu and Bao Quan, who were captured by Hou Jing. Bao Quan was killed in Jiangxia. He had prophetic dreams about his fate. He was an expert on "Ritual" and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi."

Yao Cha noted that Ruan Xiaoxu observed that virtue and literature rarely coexist, but Pei Ziye exemplified both, combining the qualities of Ziyou, Zixia, Yan Hui, and Ziqian.

Yuan Ang, courtesy name Qianli, was from Yangxia, Chen County. His grandfather and father were military officials in the Song Dynasty; his father was killed after supporting Prince Xun of Jin'an. At age five, Yuan Ang was hidden in Lushan by his wet nurse, returning home at fifteen after a pardon. He mourned his father deeply, vomiting blood and building a hut by the grave. Raised by his brother Yuan Yuzeng, he later served in various official posts under the Qi Dynasty, including Secretary Cheng and Huangmen Shilang. Emperor Wu of Qi renamed him Yuan Ang, using his courtesy name Qianli.

During the Liang Dynasty, Yuan Ang held numerous high-ranking positions, such as Censor Zhongcheng, Prefect of Wuxing, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He was known for his integrity, once impeaching a corrupt official despite the latter's powerful connections. When his mother died, he tied himself to her coffin during a storm, vowing to sink with it; the storm ceased, and his boat alone survived.

At the end of the Yongyuan period, when the righteous army arrived, Yuan Ang initially resisted but later surrendered after Emperor Gaozu wrote him a letter. He was pardoned and continued to serve, eventually becoming Sikong, Shizhong, and Shangshuling. He died at age eighty, posthumously titled Muzheng Gong. In his final words, he refused posthumous honors, citing his humble origins and gratitude for imperial grace. His son, Zijun, also served in official posts but died of illness after Hou Jing's rebellion.

The historical commentary praises Yuan Ang for his unwavering loyalty and integrity, comparing him to the virtuous Boyi and Shuqi, and noting his role in supporting the Liang dynasty.

Zhang Shu was moved to various posts, including Zhonglang of Shangshu Palace and Xizhonglang. He served as prince to wash horses and later as chief minister of the state. He wrote "Wai Shao Fu," praised by Emperor Gaozu, who compared him to Sima Xiangru and Mei Gao. He was moved to Secretary Cheng and treated with great honor. In March of the fourth year, a banquet was held in Huaguang Hall, where he wrote a poem about a dancing horse. He later served in various posts, including Zhongquan Jian'an Wang Zhongji's Office and Yunhui Zhongji Office. He stayed in the palace for ten years, receiving great favor. After returning to the capital, he served as a servant of the prince and later as General Zhaoyuan. He was moved to Huangmen Shilang and later became prefect of Xin'an. He died before the mourning period for his mother was over at age fifty-three. Prince Zhaoming sent an envoy to present funeral property. Zhang Shu liked drinking, was tolerant, and did not mind housework. He wrote fifteen volumes of "Wenheng" and thirty volumes of collected works.

Liu Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, was from Pengcheng. His grandfather Liu Meng was Duke Zhongzhao of Sikong in the Song Dynasty, and his father Ming Hui served as a lieutenant. Xiaochuo could write articles at seven and was admired by his uncle Wang Rong as a child prodigy. He drafted for his father during the Qi Dynasty. Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and Fan Yun visited him, with Ren Fang particularly appreciative. In the early years of Tianjian, he started as Zuo Lang and wrote "Poem of Returning to Mu." He was moved to Prince Sheren and later served as an official and minister of the Ministry of Water. Emperor Gaozu praised his articles and appointed him to various posts, including Secretary Cheng. He served as a consultant to King Ansheng and later as Minister of the Taifu and Prince's Servant. Prince Zhaoming treated him as a distinguished guest and had his portrait painted in Lexian Hall. Xiaochuo compiled the prince's collection and wrote the preface. He was moved to Sanqi Changshi and later served as Tingweiqing. He was dismissed after being impeached for bringing his concubine into the government while his mother lived elsewhere. He wrote letters criticizing Dao Qia, which were burned by Prince Zhaoming. He later served as Xizhong Lang to consult with the king of Xiangdong. He thanked the emperor and crown prince for their favor. He later served as a servant of the prince and died at age fifty-nine. Xiaochuo was famous but willful and scornful of others. His articles were highly valued and widely circulated. His three younger sisters were married to talented men, and his wife was particularly elegant.

Wang Jun, also named Yuanli and Derou, was from Linyi, Langxie. His grandfather Jianglu served as Duke of Kong Gelong, and his father Dan served as Taizhong doctor. Wang Jun could write articles at seven and wrote "Ode to Peony Root" at sixteen. He was as famous as his cousin Wang Tai. He started his career joining the army as King Xing of Linchuan and later served as Prince Sheren. He was appointed Zhonglang of the Shangshu Palace, a rare position for the Wang family. Shen Yue praised his articles, saying he was unmatched. Wang Jun wrote poems with uncommon rhymes and was highly regarded by Prince Zhaoming. He served as Danyang Yin Cheng and later as Zhongshu Lang. He compiled "Zhongshu Biaozuo" and other works. He was appointed Shangshu Libulang and later served as Prince's concubine. After Prince Zhaoming's death, he wrote a mourning poem. He served as General Zhenwei and Prefect of Linhai but was sued. He later served as Yunzhang Wang Changshi and moved to secretary supervisor. He died at age sixty-nine after falling into a well during a thief attack. Wang Jun was generous and loyal, famous for his talents. He wrote extensively, copying many classics himself. His collection included one hundred volumes of articles.

translation:
Yuan Faseng is a relative of the Wei family.
His ancestor was Emperor Daowu of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
His father, Zhong Kui, was named King of Jiangyang.
Fa Seng served as an official in the Northern Wei Dynasty, serving successively as Guanglu doctor, and later as envoy Chijie, governor of Xuzhou military affairs, Xuzhou governor, and guarding Pengcheng.
In the fifth year of ordinary times, the Wei family was in chaos. Fa Seng occupied Pengcheng and proclaimed himself emperor. He punished dissidents, established various princes as kings, and arranged generals, hoping to revive the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Soon after the civil strife in the Northern Wei Dynasty was calmed down, the monks were about to attack the monks. The monks were afraid, so they sent envoys to express their submission to the Liang Dynasty and asked him to become a vassal of the Liang Dynasty. Emperor Gaozu agreed and appointed him Shizhong and Sikong.
When the Northern Wei army approached him, Fa Seng asked to return to the Liang Dynasty, and Emperor Gaozu sent Zhu Yi, a member of Zhongshushe, to greet him.
When he came to Liang Dynasty, he was extremely favored.
At that time, he was attracting people who had returned, and he was friendly to those who surrendered. He also gave the Dharma monk a house, female music, and gold and silk.
When Fa Seng was in the Northern Wei Dynasty, he had been a border guard official for a long time. Every time he invaded and plundered, he killed many people. He asked for troops to be sent for self-defense. Shao ordered him to have hundreds of guards wearing armor and weapons, and they were prohibited from entering and leaving the palace.
In the second year of Datong, he was appointed as the champion general.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was transferred to the general of chariots and cavalry.
In four years, he was promoted to Taiwei and received gold and purple light.
At that time, he was established as the lord of the Eastern Wei Dynasty, but he did not return to the Wei Dynasty. He was appointed as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, general of Hussar, Kaifu Tongsansi Zhiyi, and governor of Yingzhou.
In the second year of Datong, he was recruited as Shizhong, Taiwei, and general of the army division. He died at the age of eighty-three.
The two sons, named Jinglong and Jingzhong, followed Fa Seng into the Liang Dynasty during the ordinary years.
Jinglong was granted the title of Duke of Chuanyang County, with a settlement of thousands of households, and served as Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of Guangyue, Jiaogui and other thirteen states' military affairs, General Pingnan, General Lang of Huyue Zhonglang, and Governor of Guangzhou.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong and General Anyou.
In the fourth year, he was appointed as the General of Zhengbei and the Governor of Xuzhou, and was granted the title of King of Pengcheng.
In the early years of the Taiqing Dynasty, he also served as envoy Chijie, governor of Guangyue Jiaogui and other military forces in thirteen states, general of the southern expedition, general of Pingyue Zhonglang, and governor of Guangzhou. He traveled to Leishou and died of illness at the age of fifty-eight.
Jing Zhong was granted the title of Duke of Zhijiang County, with thousands of households living in the city, and was appointed as Shizhong and Right Guard General.
In the third year of Datong, the number of new towns was increased to 2,000 households, and a female musical instrument was also given.
He served as Chijie, governor of Guangyue and other thirteen states' military affairs, general Xuanhui, general Pingyue Zhonglang, and governor of Guangzhou.
During the Zuohui period, he was recruited as Shizhong and Zuowei General.
His elder brother Keelung also served as governor of Guangzhou.
Hou Jing started a rebellion. He thought Jing Zhong was a member of the Yuan family, so he sent an envoy to persuade him and promised to make him the leader of the country.
Jing Zhong then raised his troops to respond to Hou Jing.
At that time, Chen Baxian, the governor of Xijiang, and Wang Huaiming, the governor of Chengzhou, and others launched an army to attack Jingzhong. Baxian announced to Jingzhong's soldiers: Because the traitors of Yuan Jingzhong and Yuan have united from the north to the south and are plotting to harm the country, the imperial court has sent Xiao Bo, Duke of Qujiang, as the governor to control this state.
After hearing this, everyone abandoned their armor and dispersed. Jing Zhong hanged himself and died.
Yuanshu, whose courtesy name was Junli, was also a close relative of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
His grandfather was Emperor Xianwen.
His father Yuan Xi was granted the title of King of Xianyang.
Yuan Shu served as an official in the Wei Dynasty and served as Zong Zhengqing. At the time when Erzhu Rong was in rebellion, Yuan Shu returned to the country in the eighth year of Tianjian.
In the sixth year of ordinary life, when the Yuan Dynasty monk returned to the court, he was transferred to the envoy Chijie, the governor of Ying, Si, and Huo, the three states of military affairs, the general of Yunhui, and the governor of Ying state.
After conquering the Southern Barbarians and pacifying them, he was appointed as a regular servant of the Sanqi and General of Anxi, and granted 500 additional households.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong and Zhenyou General.
In the fourth year, he was appointed as envoy Chijie, general of Zhenbei, and governor of Beichai military affairs, and he also added a department of advocacy. Let him attack Jiu Wei and capture Zhong Ji in Tanjian.
Dugu, the general who sent Jiuqiao at that time, came to help as he wished, so he surrounded Yuanli. The city was captured and he was arrested. He died angrily in the Northern Wei Dynasty at the age of forty-eight.
During the Datong period, Zi Yuanzhen requested to follow Cui Changqian, the Wei envoy, to Ye to bury his father. After returning, he was appointed Prince Sheren.
In the early years of Zuo Zha's reign, Baoliang surrendered and invited his relatives from far away to be the king of the country. Shao Ling made Zhen the king of Xianyang and sent him back to the north with the etiquette of the emperor. At that time, Hou Jing failed and returned.
Yuan Yuanda was also a branch of Wei Shu.
His grandfather was Emperor Ming Yuan.
His father was named King Leqian.
Yuanda served as an official in the Northern Wei Dynasty, serving as Zhongshu Ling and the governor of Ying Zhao.
In ordinary years, the army went north to attack Yiyang, hoping to reach the territory of Xianzhou and submit it. He was granted the title of Duke of Leping, with a settlement of thousands of households, and was given the mansions of wealthy nobles and female musicians.
Later, he served as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Xiangzhou, general Pingnan, and governor of Xiangzhou.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong, Taizhong doctor, and Yizuo general.
In the third year of Datong, he died at the age of fifty-seven.
Wang Shennian was from Qi, Taiyuan.
When he was young, he was fond of Confucianism, especially Buddhist scriptures.
He started as an official in the Northern Wei Dynasty and served as the governor of the state. Soon he was promoted to the prefect of Yingchuan, and he took over the county and returned the money.
When the Wei army arrived, he crossed the river with his family and was granted the title of Marquis of Nancheng County, with a settlement of 500 households.
Soon after, he was appointed as the internal history of Ancheng, and successively as the internal history of Wuyang and Xuancheng, all of whom made remarkable achievements in politics.
He returned to the capital and was appointed Taipuqing.
He served as Chijie, governor of the military affairs of Qing and Ji states, general Xinwu, and governor of Qing and Ji states.
Wang Shennian has an upright temperament, and the prefectures and counties he has visited will prohibit unnecessary temples.
At that time, there was Shilu Mountain near the sea in the northeast of Qing and Jizhou. There used to be a temple. The witch deceived the people. People from far and near came to pray. There was a lot of waste. When the money came to send parcels, they ordered the temple to be demolished, and the customs changed.
In ordinary years, he launched a large-scale Northern Expedition and was recruited as a right-guard general.
In the sixth year, he was transferred to envoy Chijie, Sanqi Changshi, and minions general, but the right guard remained as before.
He fell ill and died at the age of seventy-five.
Shaoling gave posthumously to his own official, the governor of Hengzhou, and also gave a piece of propaganda.
Mi's name is Zhuang.
Wang Shennian was good at riding and shooting when he was young, and he never failed in his old age. He once held two swords and shields in front of Emperor Gaozu, passed them from left to right, galloped back and forth, and his martial arts skills overwhelmed the crowd.
At that time, there was Yang Hua, who was able to shock the army and cavalry. It was a moment of great success. Emperor Gaozu deeply admired them.
The son respects his career, and his official position reaches the rank of Imperial Servant.
After his death, he posthumously awarded General Xinwei, governor of Qingzhou and Jizhou, and a volume of advocacy.
The second son, Seng Bian, has another biography.
Yang Hua was from Qiuchi, Wudu.
His father, Big Eyes, was a famous general in the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Yang Hua was brave and handsome when he was young. Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei Dynasty forced him to commit adultery. Yang Hua was afraid of disaster, so he led his troops to surrender.
Empress Dowager Hu recalled that he could not control him, so she composed "Yang Baihua's Song" for him, and asked the palace people to sing with arms and legs all day and night. The song was extremely sad.
After Yang Hua participated in many expeditions and had military exploits, he served as a taipuqing, led by the prince Zuowei, and was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang County.
During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled, and Yang Hua wanted to establish a moral integrity. However, his wife and children were captured by thieves, so he surrendered and died in the thieves' territory.
Yangkan, named Zuxin, was a descendant of Liangfu in Mount Tai and a descendant of Yangxu, the prefect of Nanyang in the Han Dynasty.
Grandfather Yang Gui, when Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty was appointed as the governor of Xuzhou, he was recruited to serve as a wine minister and a great official.
It happened that Xue Andu surrendered to Jiugui with the cutting ball, and Jiugui was trapped in the ravine. Jiuwei awarded him the title of General of Wei and Governor of Yingzhou.
His father, Yang Zhi, served as a servant in the Northern Wei Dynasty and was a doctor named Jin Ziguanglu.
When Yang Kan was young, he was tall and handsome, seven feet eight inches tall. He was very fond of literature and history, and was well versed in books and memorials. He was especially fond of Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and Sun Wu's Art of War.
When he was twenty years old, he followed his father to make military exploits in Liang Cong.
Tanji teased Li Nianwen and was gradually promoted to a special general.
At that time, Mo Zhe Niansheng, a Qiang people in Qinzhou, occupied the state and rebelled, proclaiming himself the emperor. He sent his younger brother Tiansheng to lead his troops to capture Qizhou, and then invaded Yongzhou.
Yang Yi was appointed as a partial general, and he went to fight under Lu Xuanyu. He was patrolling in the ditch and waiting for an opportunity to shoot Tiantian. Tiantian was shot and fell down, and his soldiers immediately dispersed.
Due to his merit, he was promoted to envoy Chijie, Zhengshu general, Shudaoxingtai, Taishan prefect, and was promoted to the title of Jupinghou.
At the beginning, his father had many wishes to return to the south, and often said to the disciples: How can one stay in a foreign land for a long time in his life? You should return to Shu Dynasty.
Yang Kanzhi will help fulfill his father's wish.
Yang Dun, the governor of Yanzhou, was Yang Kan's cousin. When he learned of this secretly, he resisted Yang Kan based on the state's territory.
Yang Kanyuzu led 30,000 elite troops to attack him. He failed to capture the city, so he built more than ten cities to guard it.
The rewards and official positions given by the imperial court were the same as those of Yuan Fa Seng.
Yang Yaren and Wang Bian were sent to lead an army to pick him up, and Li Yuanlu transported food and weapons to him.
When Emperor Wei learned of this, he sent an envoy to confer the title of General of Hussar, Situ, and Taishan County Duke to Yang Kan. He was appointed governor of Yanzhou. Yang Kan killed the envoy in public.
The people of Wei were shocked and ordered servant She Yuhui to lead his troops to deliver 100,000 troops. Gao Huan, Ji Zhuyangdu and others came one after another and surrounded Yangkan with more than ten layers inside and outside. Many of Yangkan's soldiers were killed and wounded.
The bows and arrows in the camp fence were exhausted, and the army from the south broke out at night. They fought and marched for a day and a night before leaving Wei territory.
When they arrived at Zakou, there were still more than 10,000 soldiers and 2,000 war horses. They were about to enter the Southern Dynasty. The soldiers sang mournfully all night long.
Yang Kan then declined and said: "You miss your homeland, so you should not follow me. I hope you can decide whether to stay or leave, and we will say goodbye here."
So the soldiers bowed and resigned.
Yang Kan arrived in the capital in the third year of Datong, and was appointed envoy Chijie, Sanqi Changshi, Commander Xiaqiu to conquer all military affairs, General Anbei, and Xuzhou governor. His brother Yang Mo and his three younger brothers Yang Chen, Yang Gei, and Yang Wu were all appointed governors.
Soon after, he was appointed as the commander-in-chief to attack the military forces in the north and sent troops to guard Richeng. At this time, Chen Qingzhi lost the battle and Yangkan's troops stopped advancing.
In this year, Shaoling appointed him as Chijie, General Yunhui, and governor of Qingji Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, Shaoling appointed him as envoy Chijie, commander-in-chief of Xiaqiu Zhujun, general Anbei, and governor of Yanzhou, and followed Taiwei Yuanfaseng to attack the north.
Dieseng announced in advance: I have an old friendship with Yang Kan, and I hope to go with him.
Emperor Gaozu summoned Yang Kan to ask him about the strategy of the Northern Campaign, and Yang Kan stated his aggressive strategy in detail.
Gaozu therefore said: I know that you are willing to go with the Taiwei.
Yang Kan said: I left the north and returned to the court. I often wanted to serve the court, but I really didn't want to go with this monk.
Although the northerners call me a Chengren, the southerners have already called me a northerner. Now I am traveling with Dharma monks, and the same kind of people are still following each other. This not only goes against my original intention, but also makes the Huns look down on the Han people.
Zhi Sip said: The imperial court needs your companions today.
So in the lower Shao Dynasty, he appointed Jianyi as Sima of the army.
Zhidan said to Fucu: The post of Army Sima has been abandoned for a long time, and now it is reserved for you.
Marching to Guanzhu, Yuansu defeated the mourning division at Zhanqiu.
The northern expedition was stopped and he was appointed as a servant.
In the fifth year, he was granted the title of Marquis of Gaochang County and was granted the title of Marquis of Gaochang County, with a thousand households living in the city.
In the sixth year, he served as General Yunhui and Grand Administrator.
The customs of the country and ridge favored rebellion, and the successive governorships failed to stop it. Yang Kan came and attacked, killing the leaders Chen Cheng, Cheng Mai and others. As a result, the county was purged and no one dared to commit rebellion.
Soon, he was recruited as the prince's left guard.
In the third year of Datong, Emperor Gaozu was lucky enough to visit Le Yuyuan, and Yang Kan attended the banquet.
At that time, the Shaofu reported that a new two-edged sword was made, which was two feet and four feet long and one foot and three inches in circumference. Emperor Gaozu gave Yang Kanma to him to try out the sword.
Yang Kan mounted his horse and stabbed left and right. His performance was so wonderful that Emperor Gaozu praised him. He also compiled thirty rhymes of "Wu Yan Shi" for Yang Kan to read. Yang Kan improvised the poem in response to the imperial edict. After reading it, Emperor Gaozu said: I heard that people with benevolence have courage. Now I have seen that people with courage have benevolence. It can be said that Confucius and Mencius followed the trend, and the virtuous people have not stopped.
In the sixth year, he was moved to the post of Situ Zuo Changshi.
In the eighth year, he was moved to the post of Du Guan Shangshu.
At that time, He Jingrong was in power, and he was also in Shangshu Province, but Yang Kan never visited him.
The eunuch Zhang Sengyin visited Yang Kan, and Yang Kan said: My bed is not something someone can sit on.
He didn't even go to receive him, but the public praised him for his chastity.
In the ninth year, he served as envoy Chijie, general Zhuangwu, and governor of Hengzhou.
In the first year of Taiqing, he was recruited as a servant.
At this time, the imperial court raised troops for the Northern Expedition, and appointed Yang Kanzhijie and Champion to supervise the construction of the Hanshan Weir fortifications. The weir was built in only twenty days.
Yang Kan persuaded Marshal Zhenyang Hou to take the water to attack Pengcheng, but was not accepted. Soon reinforcements from Shu Wei arrived in large numbers. Yang Kan repeatedly advised Zhenyang Hou to take advantage of Shu Wei's troops to attack from afar. The next morning, he also advised him to go out to fight, but he did not listen. Yang Kan led his soldiers to guard the weir.
After the defeat of all the armies, Yang Kan's soldiers formed a formation and slowly withdrew.
In the second year, he was appointed as the governor of the capital.
Hou Jing rebelled and captured Liyang. Emperor Gaozu asked Yangkan about his strategy to attack Hou Jing.
Yang Kan said: The signs of Hou Liang's rebellion have long been revealed. Perhaps he will rush into the capital and occupy the quarry quickly, so that King Shaoling can attack Shouchun.
Hou Liang's advance was not allowed to move forward, and when he retreated and lost his base camp, the mob naturally disintegrated.
The discussants said that Hou Jingwei did not dare to approach the capital immediately, so they put aside his strategy and ordered Yang Kan to lead more than a thousand cavalry to guard the country's gate.
When the army of Semi arrived, they chased back Yun and dug into the city to assist King Xuanji in supervising all the military forces in the city.
At that time, as many troops as possible arrived suddenly, people rushed into the city, public and private personnel were in chaos, and there was no order.
Yang Kan then separated them and put them on guard, and put them all under surveillance by the clan members.
Soldiers rushed into the arsenal to pick up their own weapons and inspect their armor. The officials in charge could not stop it. They had to stop it only when Fu Tan ordered several people to be killed.
When the thieves approached the city, everyone was frightened and shocked. Yang Kan pretended to have received a letter from outside the city, saying that reinforcements led by King Shaoling and Marquis of Xichang had arrived nearby.
Everyone is at peace.
The thieves attacked Shuye Gate and set the fire very vigorously. Yang Kan personally directed the resistance, poured water on the fire, and the fire subsided. He drew his bow and killed several people before the thieves retreated.
He was appointed as a sergeant and general as a military advisor.
Shao Ling once presented five thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and ten thousand pieces of silk as gifts to the soldiers, but Yang Kan refused.
More than a thousand people were rewarded with private money.
The thief made a pointed wooden donkey to attack the city, but the arrows and stones could not subdue it, so Yang Kan made a pheasant tail torch, put an iron arrow on it, poured oil on it, threw it on the wooden donkey and burned it, and soon the wooden donkey was burned.
The thieves then piled mountains of earth on the east and west sides of the city. They stood on the mountains and watched the city wrap around. The people in the city were shocked. Yang Kan ordered tunnels to be dug under the mountains of earth and the earth was transported away secretly. The mountains of earth could not be piled up.
The thieves also made a cart for climbing the city, which was more than ten feet high. They wanted to climb the city and shoot inwards. Yang Kan said: The cart is high and the soil in the ditch below the city is empty.
When the truck started to move, he fell down and everyone admired him.
Since the thieves could not win with frequent attacks, they built a long siege.
Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan discussed how to attack the bandits. Emperor Gaozu asked Yang Kan for his opinion, and Yang Kan said: "No."
The thieves had been attacking the city for many days, but since they could not capture it, they built a long siege to lure out the surrendered people in the city.
If we attack him now, if we send out few troops, we will not be able to defeat the thieves. If we send out more troops, if we lose, our own people will overrun each other, and the city gates will be narrow and the bridges will be small, which will definitely lead to great setbacks. This is to show weakness to the thieves, rather than to display the king's power.
Emperor Gaozu did not listen to his advice, so he sent more than a thousand men to fight. Before they could fight, they retreated. As expected, they fell into the water while fighting for the bridge, and most of them died.
At the beginning, Yang Kan's eldest son, Yang Lu, was captured by Hou Jing. Now he was brought to the city for Yang Kan to meet. Yang Kan said to the thief: I just destroyed the clan to serve the king, and I still hate it. How can I care about this son? I hope you can kill him early.
After meeting for a few days, Yang Kan said to Yang Lu: I thought you would die for a long time, how come you are still alive?
I pledged my life to the country and swore to die on the battlefield. Your life and death cannot determine my progress or retreat.
So he drew his bow and shot at him.
The thief was moved by Yang Kan's loyalty and did not harm Yang Yang.
Hou Jingqianyi and Fu Shizhe called Yang Kanyu and said to him: "The king Hou came from afar to greet the emperor. Why did he refuse behind closed doors and not accept him in time?"
The minister is a minister of the country and should report to the court.
Yang Kan said: After General Hou fled from the Eastern Wei Dynasty, he returned to the country and allowed him to guard the Great Wall in the north with heavy troops and serve as a high-ranking official to express his trust. What hardships did he have that suddenly led to the recruitment of troops?
Now we drive the mob down to the foot of the royal city, let the captive horses drink from the Huai River, and point their bows and arrows at the imperial palace. Is there any minister who can do this?
I have been greatly favored by the country, so I should only follow the imperial court's strategy and eliminate the treacherous and evil people. I should not accept idle talk and open the door to salute the robbers.
Please thank the prince and think about yourself as soon as possible.
Shi Zhe also said: The prince has done his best to serve the king, but the court does not know about it. He is planning to report to the Supreme Being in person in order to eradicate the treacherous ministers in the court. Since you are in the army, why would you bring your armor to the court?
Yang Kan said: The Holy Sage has ruled the world for about fifty years. He has a clear understanding of affairs and is holy and wise. There is no dark place where he cannot shine. Who is able to be a treacherous person in the court?
If you want to cover up your sins, how can you do it without sophistry?
Moreover, the prince personally raised his white sword and pointed it at the capital, doing his duty to the king. Is this what he did?
Shizhe was speechless, so he said: In the north, I have admired his grace and character for a long time. Every time in my life, I regret that I have not been able to get the opportunity to talk sincerely. I hope I can take off my military uniform and meet him.
Yang Kan took off his helmet for him, and Shizhe looked at him for a long time before leaving.
He was admired by the northerners just like this.
Later, it rained heavily and the earth and mountains in the city collapsed. The thieves took advantage of the situation and were about to attack the city. The fierce fighting could not be stopped. Yang Kan ordered more torches to be thrown to form a fire city to cut off the thieves' approach. They calmly built the city on the outside so that the thieves could not advance.
In December, he fell ill and died in Taiwan at the age of fifty-four.
The imperial edict gave the coffin for the official to be used after his death, 500 pieces of cloth and silk each, and 3 million in money. He also gave it as a posthumous gift to the ministers, the generals who guarded the army, and a propaganda section.
When Yang Kan was young, he was brave and mighty, with extraordinary physical strength. The bow he used had a draw strength of more than ten stones.
I once climbed up the wall of Yao's temple in Yanzhou, reaching up to five fathoms, and there were seven traces across it.
There were several stone figures at Siqiao, eight feet high and ten meters thick. Yang Kan raised the stone figures and struck them with each other, and they were all smashed.
Yang Kan has a luxurious temperament and is good at music. He wrote two songs, "Lotus Picking" and "Table Song", which are very innovative.
The family was filled with concubines and concubines who were extremely extravagant and extravagant; there was a zheng player named Lu Taixi, who wore a plucked deer's antler claws that were seven inches long; a dancer named Zhang Jingwan, whose waist was only one foot and six inches, and it was said at the time that this person could dance in the palm of his hand.
There is also Sun Xingyu, who can turn his waist and put his head on the ground, and hold the hosta on the mat with his mouth.
The emperor rewarded him with the singer Wang E'er, and the prince also rewarded him with the singer Ren Qu. Both of them could sing extremely wonderful and strange songs. No one could equal them at that time.
When I first went to Hengzhou, I built three small houses with beams between the two ships. They were decorated with pearls and jade, with gorgeous paintings, curtains, and female musicians. They unmoored the boats at high tide and placed wine by the water. Along the edge of the pond, the crowds of people watching were crowded.
During the Datong period, Danlu, an envoy of Yue, and Chaitan were classmates in the north. One Shao ordered Yangkan to invite Yangfei to a banquet.
There were more than three hundred guests, and the utensils on the table were all made of gold and jade. Three female music pieces were played. At night, more than a hundred maids and maids held gold candles.
Yang Kan cannot drink alcohol, but he likes to socialize with guests, drinking with them all day long, and getting drunk with them.
With a generous temperament and talent, Zeng Nan returned to Liankou and held a banquet. There was a guest named Zhang Rucai who got drunk and caught fire on the boat. More than 70 boats were burned, and the gold and silk burned were beyond the limit.
After Yang Kan heard about it, he didn't care at all and ordered him to keep drinking.
Rucai was afraid and ran away by himself. Yangkan comforted him and let him come back, treating him as before.
The third son is the sheep.

summary:
The lives of several individuals from the Northern Wei Dynasty who later served the Liang Dynasty, focusing on their careers, military actions, and fates.

Yuan Faseng, a relative of the Northern Wei imperial family, served as an official and later declared himself emperor during a period of chaos. He submitted to the Liang Dynasty and was granted high titles. He died at age 83, and his sons, Jinglong and Jingzhong, also served the Liang. Jingzhong later rebelled with Hou Jing but was defeated and hanged himself.

Yuanshu, another Northern Wei relative, served as an official and later defected to the Liang. He was appointed to military and civil posts, captured a city, but was eventually captured and died in the Northern Wei at age 48.

Yuan Yuanda, a branch of the Wei family, served in the Northern Wei and later submitted to the Liang, receiving titles and positions. He died at age 57.

Wang Shennian, from Qi, was a Confucian scholar who served as a prefect in the Northern Wei and later defected to the Liang. He was known for his uprightness, destroying a fraudulent temple. He died at age 75, and his son also served as an official.

Yang Hua, from Qiuchi, was a brave general forced into adultery by Empress Dowager Hu. He defected to the Liang, served in expeditions, and later surrendered to Hou Jing, dying in the rebel territory.

Yang Kan, from Tai Shan, was a tall and learned man who followed his father in military service. He shot a rebel leader, was promoted, and later defected to the Liang with his family. He was besieged by Wei forces but broke out, arriving in the Liang capital. He served in various military posts, advised against attacking Hou Jing prematurely, and defended the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion. He refused bribes, used tactics to counter siege engines, and remained loyal despite his son being captured. He died of illness at age 54, known for his bravery, strength, and luxurious lifestyle.

Yang Yaren, also from Tai Shan, was brave and served as an official. He defected to the Liang, was granted a marquisate, and held military commands. He was sent to pick up Hou Jing but later feared punishment. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he aided the court but was defeated. After the capital fell, he served Hou Jing but planned to flee, eventually being killed.

The text concludes with a commentary praising the loyalty of Yang Kan and Yang Yaren during the Taiqing period, comparing their steadfastness to ancient martyrs.

summary:
Chen Qingzhi, courtesy name Ziyun, from Yixingguoshan, served Emperor Gaozu from youth. Gaozu loved chess, playing tirelessly; while others tired and slept, Qingzhi remained alert and responsive, earning high regard. He followed Gaozu to pacify Jianye, served as chief secretary, and recruited soldiers with dispersed funds. He was granted an imperial invitation. In the ordinary years, Wei's Xuzhou governor Yuan Faseng sought attachment to Pengcheng. Qingzhi, as a powerful general, led Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun to escort him. After returning, he became General Xuanmeng and Commander Wende, leading 2,000 troops to guard Xuzhou with Xiao Zong. Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Yuan of Linhuai with 20,000 troops to resist at Zhikou. Yanming's general Qiu Dagan built a fort at Xunliang; Qingzhi defeated him in a single battle. Later, King Yuzhang fled to Wei, causing a rout. Qingzhi cut bolts, breached the city, and retreated at night, saving his sergeants.

In the seventh ordinary year, General Yuan Shu of Anxi went to Shouchun. Wei's Yuzhou governor Li Xian sent his son to build forts; Qingzhi attacked, Li Xian surrendered, and Qingzhi occupied the city. He was transferred to Donggong Zhihe and titled Marquis of Guanzhong. In Datong's first year, a subordinate leader fortified and conquered Yan. General Changshan Wang Yuanzhao led 150,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue, reaching Tuojian, 40 miles from Guoyang. Qingzhi wanted to fight, but Tong Zhen advised caution. Qingzhi argued the Wei were tired and unsuspecting; he led 200 cavalry to defeat their front army. The Wei were horrified. Qingzhi then returned, and the generals attacked together, occupying Woyang City. From spring to winter, hundreds of battles ensued. The army grew exhausted, and Wei reinforcements threatened. Zhongzong and others planned retreat, but Qingzhi insisted on fighting, capturing four of thirteen Wei fortifications. Wang Wei of Woyang surrendered. Qingzhi displayed captured ears, beat drums, and attacked, causing the enemy to collapse. Over 30,000 men and women were captured. West Xuzhou was established on Guoyang's land. Emperor Gaozu praised Qingzhi in a personal letter.

In early Datong, Wei's Wang Yuanhao surrendered due to internal chaos, seeking to become lord of Wei. Emperor Gaozu appointed Qingzhi as Jiejie and Biaoyong General, sending Yuan Hao north. Yuan Hao declared himself Emperor of Wei at Huanshui. Qingzhi, as Chijie and commander, advanced from Liao County to Suiyang. Wei general Qiu Dagan had 70,000 troops in nine forts; Qingzhi captured three by afternoon, and Daqian surrendered. Wei's Jiyin Wang Yuanhuiye led 20,000 troops to rescue; Qingzhi built a fortress on water, captured the city, and seized 7,800 tax vehicles. Heading to Dafun, enemies surrendered at the sight of his flag. Qingzhi became General of the Guard and Governor of Lansu. He led forces west. Wei's Yang Yu, Xi'a Wang Yuanqing, and Yuan Xianggong led 70,000 troops to hold Rongyang. Qingzhi failed to capture it. Wei general Yuan Tianmu's army approached; Qingzhi, with only 7,000 troops against 300,000 captives, rallied his men, conquered Rongyang, and defeated Tianmu's army. He entered Hulao, and Zhu Shichen fled. Yuan Ziyou fled, and Yuan Hao entered Luoyang Palace, ascending the throne. Qingzhi was appointed servant and general, with increased households. Wei generals led 40,000 troops to capture Daliang; Qingzhi's white-robed subordinates were invincible. A Luoyang nursery rhyme warned: "Thousands of troops should avoid white robes." From Zhixian to Luoyang, in 140 days, Qingzhi leveled 32 fortresses and fought 47 battles, unstoppable.

Yuan Hao indulged in wine and sex, plotting against Qingzhi. Qingzhi planned secretly but was alienated. Yuan Hao refused to send more troops. Qingzhi's deputy warned of danger, suggesting killing Yuan Hao, but Qingzhi refused. Yuan Hao appointed Qingzhi governor of Xuzhou but feared him and didn't send him. Wei's Ji Zhufu and others, claiming millions, attacked Yuan Hao. Qingzhi crossed the Yellow River to defend Beizhonglang City, fighting eleven times in three days. Ji Zhurong nearly retreated but was advised to stay. He crossed the river, defeated Yuan Hao, and Luoyang fell. Qingzhi, with thousands, formed a formation and returned east. Ji Zhurong pursued; Songgao Mountain flooded, scattering his soldiers. Qingzhi shaved his head, became a monk, and traveled to Yuzhou. He was secretly sent to the capital, awarded General Youwei and Yongxing County Fortress. Later, as Chijie and governor of Northern Yanzhou, he defeated the demon thief monk Tan Qiang, killing him in twelve days. In Zhongdatong's second year, he became military governor of four states. He opened 6,000 hectares of land, filling warehouses. In Datong's second year, Wei's Hou Jing invaded Chuzhou; Qingzhi defeated him in snowy conditions. He was promoted to General Renwei. During a famine in Yuzhou, he opened warehouses for relief. He died at fifty-six, posthumously honored. Qingzhi was cautious, wore no silk, disliked music, and comforted his soldiers well.

His son Chen Zhao was heir. Fifth son Chen Ting, courtesy name Junzhang, could ride and shoot at seven. At twelve, he followed his father to Luoyang but fell ill. He impressed Zhu Yi by drawing maps in soil. In Datong's fourth year, he was appointed Changshi and leader of the right guard, sent to Yiyang. He defeated Yao Xiong, a fierce Wei general. In the sixth year, he was titled General Weiyuan and Lord of Xiaoxian. In the tenth year, he pacified the demon thief Wang Qinzong. In Taiqing's second year, Hou Jing surrounded Liyang. Chen Ting advised guarding the quarry but was captured by Hou Jing. Hou Jing tried to use him, but Chen Ting refused. He was killed by Hou Jing at thirty-three. Lanqin, courtesy name Xiu Ming, was from Zhongchang Wei. His father Lan Yun served as governor of Jizhou. Lanqin was decisive and agile, following his father in the northern expedition. In Datong's first year, he attacked Wei Xiao City and defeated various generals. He captured Juegu and defeated Liu Haiyou. He pacified barbarians in Guiyang and Yangshan, was titled male in Anhuai County. He defeated Duiqi Manshuai and rescued Yuan Qinghe. He was granted command of four states, captured Tongsheng, and pacified Luan and Yi. He was promoted to General Zhiwu. Later, as governor of Hengzhou, he defeated Wei's Dong Shao and Zhang Xian. He governed Guangzhou, defeating Chen Wenche. In Hengzhou, he was promoted to General Zinan and Duke of Qujiang County. Officials requested a monument for his virtues. He was recruited as a regular servant but was poisoned by a cook at forty-two. His son Zi Xia Li attacked Hou Jing at Liyang and died. The historian comments that Chen Qingzhi and Lanqin rivaled ancient generals in military strategy. Qingzhi was intelligent and served Zhidan long, earning honors through caution and respect.
