In the seventeenth year, Xiao Chang died at the age of thirty-nine.
His son's name is Xiao Boyan.
Xiao Ang, whose courtesy name is Ziming, is Xiao Jing's third younger brother.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was transferred to Situ Youchangshi many times, served as general of light vehicles, and supervised southern Yanzhou.
At the beginning, when his brother Lu Liang was appointed as the governor of Yinchaye for the second time, his merits and favors were still in people's hearts. When Xiao Ang came to replace him, people compared him to Feng.
Xiao Ang was recruited as the prefect of Langye and Pengcheng counties, and the military trumpets remained as before.
He also served as the governor of Guangzhou with the official position of General Qingche.
In the second year of ordinary life, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi and general Xinwei.
In the fourth year, he was transferred to the rank of minister of Sanqi, the leader of the army, the prince's concubine, and the prefect of Wuxing County.
In the second year of Datong, he was summoned to serve as General Renwei and Weiweiqing. Soon he was appointed as a minister and concurrently as the leading general.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was appointed as the leading general.
In the second year, he was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangyin County and was granted a residence of one thousand households.
He served as the governor of Jiangzhou.
In the first year of Datong, Xiao Ang passed away at the age of fifty-three.
Mi shouted Gong.
Xiao Yu, also known as Zizhen, is Xiao Jing's fourth younger brother.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was awarded the title of Secretary Lang, and was moved to the position of Prince Sheren, Xima, Zhongshu Sheren, and Zhongshu Shilang many times.
He often asked for self-examination, and Emperor Gaozu appointed him as the governor of Jinzhi County, Yongjia County, and Xiangyang County, but he refused to take office.
He volunteered to go to the border states and counties. Emperor Gaozu thought that he was frivolous, unstable and lacked prestige, so he suppressed him and refused to allow him to go.
Later he was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen.
Xiao Yu wrote to the emperor and said: The statement I submitted at the beginning of summer was not approved. Looking back on the past, shame and fear, really makes me tremble in my heart.
I heard that it rains heavily in the summer and is cold in the winter, and the villains still complain. Who can forget whether they are proud or frustrated in politics, whether they are favored or humiliated?
With the help of past connections, I was able to join the ranks of royal relatives and gain attention; the opportunities for repaying my gratitude were already mixed, and I was facing a fate of poverty and frustration.
In the past, at the end of the Qi Dynasty, when the righteous armies first emerged, I was still young and just a little sensible. Because the traffic between the east and the west was blocked, I had no way to join the righteous armies. Although I could not hold a spear and wore a bell armor, I actually had tears in my eyes and was full of resentment.
I lurked in the eastern border and experienced hardships and dangers. It lasted three years and moved to several places. Even though I was hungry and cold, I did not suffer from cold and exhaustion.
Whenever I encounter doubts, I am so frightened that I lose my soul. I have violated my fatal integrity and feared being tortured in vain. My body and head are separated. I look forward to the day when we can be prosperous and peaceful, and we can enjoy happiness together. Who knows that after waiting for more than 20 years, there is no fame to record, and my whole body will also fill the ravine. My sincere heart and pure wishes are suddenly over forever. I bow my head and pity alone, can I not sigh sadly!
It is indeed despicable to introduce oneself and show off oneself; it is really shameful to praise oneself and praise oneself.
However, if you have a clear understanding of your own situation and can use your talents to take up an official position, you will not dare to talk empty words, so you often hope to give it a try and ask others for help many times.
To say that it can respond to celestial phenomena, I dare not be so greedy, but if the brocade is not cut, it is really difficult to make clothes.
Because all the bad consequences I did in my previous life have become obstacles in this life, so I am now violating my calculations.
Since the Holy One thinks that I am stupid and defective and cannot be tried, how can I be tolerated to live in the forbidden area of ​​the royal family for a long time and soil the position of Huangmen official in vain.
I am ashamed of my official position. As time goes by, I am afraid that I will be criticized by people. Please relieve me from my position today and beg me to return home.
I prostrated myself and asked the Emperor for special permission.
Although I received the favor and honor from the two palaces, I was unable to repay my service and went against the wishes of the palace. I feel deeply nostalgic and afraid.
Emperor Gaozu wrote Shao Shu in his own hand and replied: This is what Xiao Yu said above.
In ancient times, when employing people, they must first be interviewed. They must have established merits and be very effective, so that they can show their high style of humility.
At that time, Liu Zhang and Liu Xing, the sons of Emperor Moguang Wu's brother, were both well-known in the clan. However, if they wanted to become officials, Liu Zhang became the magistrate of Pingyin County and Liu Xing became the prime minister of the Gou family. After they became capable in political affairs, they were moved to the post of county governor. Not only were they praised for their political achievements, they were also nephews of Emperor Guangwu.
Xiao Yu, how can your talents and insights be compared with theirs!
In the past few years, you were asked to serve in Huainan County, but you refused to go; then you were asked to serve as General Zhaoyuan, Chief Superintendent of Zhenbei, and Governor of Xiangyang County, but you turned it down on the pretext that it was a remote area; later, you were appointed General Zhaoyuan and Governor of Yongjia County, but you said that going to the mainland was not your wish; I asked you again about the two places of Jin'an and Linchuan. It was your choice, but you refused to go.
There is nothing trivial about taking off the headscarf and taking up an official position. However, you have made excuses several times, so where are your wishes?
Besides, several of your brothers, Xiao Yu, have successively served as county guards, commanders, etc., and they have recommended each other, and they have not been lacking for a year.
Your brother Xiao Jing is now a official living in the feudal town.
Do I treat Xiao Jinghou well and you Xiao Yu poorly? This is what everyone in the court is talking about. Such an order is the same for you, so you are not ashamed.
Needless to say, this cannot be the case today; brothers Xiao Yu were ordinary people back then, and because they were in their growth period, how could they indulge themselves in violating the right path and going against heaven and earth?
Who says the imperial court doesn't have a charter? It's just that it doesn't want to put you in front of the court.
Since you have submitted a request for dismissal, let's do what you requested.
Xiao Yu was dismissed from his official position as a result.
From then on, he paid homage to guests and never went to the court to see the emperor again. He was no longer notified to attend any national celebrations or funerals.
In ordinary five years, Xiao Yu broke the law because he minted coins in his own home. The relevant officials reported the copy to the imperial officer. He was spared death and moved to Linhai County.
As soon as he reached Shangyu, he was chased by the emperor's order, asking him to go back and receive the Bodhisattva's warning.
After Xiao Yu arrived in the capital, he followed the requirements of etiquette very respectfully and carefully, changed his will, followed the rules, and fasted very carefully and cleanly. Emperor Gaozu admired him very much and appointed him as General Zhaoyuan and Prefect of Jinling County.
After Xiao Yu took office, he encouraged himself with his fame and achievements, eliminated too many excessive taxes and miscellaneous taxes, affirmed the legal charter, strictly controlled the cunning officials, and implemented a policy of good care for the people. As a result, within ten days, great changes took place in Jinling County.
Soon, Xiao Yu fell seriously ill and passed away. The people in the county, whether they were walking or sitting, cried loudly after hearing the news. The streets and alleys were abuzz with noise, and more than 400 people gathered in the courtyard of the county to pay homage.
There was a woman named Xia in the farmhouse by the field, who was over a hundred years old. When she heard the news of Xiao Yu's death, she came to the county government with her great-grandson in her arms and cried sadly, unable to control herself.
It can be seen that the influence of Xiao Yu's favorable policies is so great.
The people built temples and erected steles for Xiao Yu one after another to commemorate his merits.
They went to the capital to ask for a favor for Xiao Yu.
When the emperor came to Shao, he posthumously appointed Xiao Yu as the governor of Xiangzhou.
Mi Hao Gong.
Shi Chen said: "Zhidan owns the world, and rewards and appointments are generally given. Those relatives and related people are all appointed and treated with courtesy."
Lu Liang's talent, insight and judgment can be beneficial to the government and assist in current affairs. He is probably a person with good grace and dignity in the You clan.
summary:
Xiao Jing, courtesy name Zizhao, was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu. His father Xiao Chongzhi was a son of Xiao Daomo, who had three sons: Xiao Shangzhi, Emperor Taizu Wen, and Xiao Chongzhi. Xiao Shangzhi was known for his virtuous conduct and served as an infantry captain, dying in office. Posthumously titled Wenxuanhou in the early Tianjian era, his son Xiao Lingjun served as a county magistrate and was later granted the title of Marquis of Dongchang County. Xiao Chongzhi, a champion general and Dongyang governor, was killed during a rebellion in the Yongming era and posthumously titled Marquis Zhongjian.

Xiao Jing became famous at age eight for his grief during mourning. He loved learning, was decisive, and served as Chengkong County Magistrate, where his political performance was exemplary. After resigning due to illness, he returned to court and was appointed Infantry Colonel. Following Gaozu's uprising, he became General Ningshuo and pacified the Chu people on the Yangtze's north bank. After Gaozu ascended, Xiao Jing was granted the title of Marquis of Wuping County and governed several states. He was known for his honesty, strictness, and efficiency, with no backlog of documents. During a famine, he provided relief and coffins. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he led an army in the Northern Expedition. After his mother's death, he resigned but was later reappointed to various positions, including General Zuo Xiaoqi. He was strict with officials, causing resentment among favored supervisors, leading to his transfer to Yongzhou as governor.

In the eighth year, when Wei's governor Wu Jin invaded, Xiao Jing accepted surrendered barbarians, defeating the enemy and burying the dead. He built barracks, strengthened defenses, and encouraged farming, resulting in a peaceful and theft-free territory. He was later recalled to court and served in various roles, including General Youwei. In the thirteenth year, he was summoned as leading general, receiving a salary increase. Xiao Jing was personable and well-spoken, and Gaozu treated him with great courtesy, consulting him on military and state affairs. He declined a promotion to Yangzhou governor but was eventually appointed. His strictness was legendary; an old woman noted his talismans were like fire. He died at age forty-seven, posthumously titled Shizhong.

Xiao Chang, Xiao Jing's second brother, served in various roles, including governor of Hengzhou, but was dismissed for crimes. He was understanding but prone to drinking and making mistakes, often killing people while drunk without remorse. He died at age thirty-nine.

Xiao Ang, the third brother, served as governor of Southern Yanzhou and Guangzhou, among other roles. He died at age fifty-three, posthumously titled Gong.

Xiao Yu, the fourth brother, served as Secretary Lang and other positions but frequently refused appointments. He wrote a memorial expressing shame and fear, requesting dismissal. Emperor Gaozu replied, criticizing his refusals and dismissing him. Later, Xiao Yu was exiled for minting coins but was recalled. He became a model of propriety and was appointed Prefect of Jinling County, where he implemented beneficial policies. He died after a severe illness, mourned by the people, who built temples and steles for him. He was posthumously appointed governor of Xiangzhou, titled Gong.

The historian comments that Xiao Jing's talent and judgment benefited the government, making him a person of grace and dignity in the You clan.

translation:
Liu Jun, whose courtesy name was Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan.
His father, Liu Ge, was the internal historian of Shixing in the Song Dynasty.
When Liu Jun was just one year old, his mother took him back to his hometown.
In the early years of Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei people. When Liu Jun was eight years old, he was kidnapped and taken to Zhongshan. Liu Shi, a wealthy man in Zhongshan, sympathized with Liu Jun's plight and redeemed Liu Jun with five pieces of silk and taught him to write and read.
The people of Wei heard that Liu Jun had relatives in Jiangnan, so they moved him to Sangqian.
Liu Jun was eager to learn, his family was poor, and he lived in other people's homes, but he set his own study schedule. He often lit a torch made of hemp straw and read all night. Sometimes he fell asleep and the torch burned his hair. When he woke up, he resumed reading and stayed up all night.
During the next year of Qi Yong, Liu Jun was able to return to Qi from Sangqian. He thought that his knowledge was not extensive, so he went to look for other books that he had never seen. When he heard that there was such a book in the capital, he would rush to ask for it to be borrowed. Cui Weizu of Qinghe called him a "book slut".
At that time, Xiao Ziliang, the real fallen minister, was recruiting scholars, and Xingjun asked for a position in Xiao Ziliang's kingdom through others. Xu Xiaosi, the Minister of Civil Affairs, devalued him and refused to agree. He was only appointed as the minister of Nanhai King, but he refused to take up the post.
By the time of Emperor Ming, Xiao Yaoxin was appointed governor of Yuzhou and appointed Liu Jun as the prisoner of the government. He was treated very generously.
Xiao Yaoxin passed away soon, and Liu Jun was not allowed to raise his tune for a long time.
In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Jun was called to the Western Province and served as the secretary of the school with He Zong, a bachelor.
Liu Jun's brother Liu Longqing was serving as governor at the time. Su asked for leave to visit him. He was impeached by the official for transporting prohibited items without permission and was dismissed from office.
He liked learning. When he was transferred to the governor's office, he was promoted to join the army as a product of Cao. He was provided with some books and asked him to copy them into a book by category and named it "Lei Yuan". Before the book was compiled, Liu Jun left because of illness. He built a house there and lived there because he visited Ziyan Mountain in Dongyang.
Liu Jun wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi", and the writing is beautiful.
Emperor Gaozu recruited literary people, and those with high talents were often recommended for promotion, often without qualifications.
Liu Jun acted according to his own temperament and could not follow the ups and downs of others. Emperor Gaozu disliked him very much, so he did not use him.
Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings. The article said:
The emperor once talked about Guan Ren with many famous sages, and lamented that there were talented people in charge but their official positions were not high.
A friend was in the court at that time and heard this discussion, so he told me when he came back.
I believe that the embarrassment and enlightenment of a scholar's situation are all determined by fate, so I respectfully describe the outline of destiny and my own ambitions.
In my opinion, the governor is a talent sent from heaven, magnificent and outstanding, with outstanding talents and excellent character. He is really a hero in the country, and he is not just an ordinary divination and blessing.
But his official position is only that of Shaofu Cheng, and he is forty-eight years old. How few people God has given him to govern!
However, talented people do not have prominent official positions, while gluttonous, cruel and greedy people are in prominent official positions. This phenomenon has often made people sigh since ancient times, how can it be just Gong Ming?
Therefore, no one can understand the difference between human nature and endowment, a lifetime of embarrassment and enlightenment, setbacks, failures, and successes.
When talking about this issue, Wang Zhongren covered up its root cause, and Sima Zichang expressed his doubts.
As for the poor and humble people who wear humble clothes and live in thatched huts, they must say that their destiny is controlled by God, and good and bad fortunes depend on luck. For wealthy and wealthy families, it is said that misfortunes and misfortunes do not distinguish between families, but are only caused by people's virtues.
There was a lot of talk and arguments, and various opinions emerged one after another.
Li Xiaoyuan talked about the foundation of fate but did not explain its changes. Guo Zixuan talked about the changes of fate but did not clarify its origin.
Let me try to talk about this issue: The Great Way gives birth to all things, so it is called Tao; if it is born without any master, it is called nature.
Nature means that all things grow, but they don’t know why they grow; all things get their own place, but they don’t know why they get their own places.
He stirs up the world and creates all things, but he does not regard it as his own strength or his own achievements. There is no intention to nurture it while alive, and death is not caused by killing. Falling into the abyss and becoming a fish and dragon is not a punishment from God; rising to the sky and becoming a bird is not a favor from God.
This Tao is boundless and broad, and all things change with it; but it is also deep and pure, and it never changes once it is created.
Once it is created, it will not change. This is called destiny.
Fate refers to the fate sent down from heaven.
Destiny is determined in the dark and will never change.
Ghosts and gods cannot predict it, and sages cannot examine it. The force that knocks down the mountains cannot be resisted, nor can the sincerity that causes the sun to return cannot be affected. If destiny comes quickly, it cannot be delayed for a moment, and if it comes slowly, it cannot be missed in advance. The most virtuous sages cannot transcend the destiny, and the wise people cannot escape the constraints of destiny.
Therefore, in the era when Fangxun was in power, the floods were so powerful that the mountains and mausoleums were submerged; in the era when Chengtang was the emperor, droughts were raging and the gold and stone were scorched.
Jin Wengong suffered repeated setbacks, and Kong Xuanni was in Chen Jueliang. Yan Hui's hair turned gray prematurely, and Ran Geng suffered from a serious illness. Boyi and Shuqi starved to death because of the woman's words, and Mencius was embarrassed because of Zang Cang's slander.
Sages can't escape the arrangement of fate, let alone mediocre ordinary people!
As for the corpses of the soldiers who were thrown into the river; Dr. Qu Yuan of Sanlu sank in the Xiang River; Dr. Jia was demoted to Kensha because of frustration in his ambition; Feng Duwei and Feng Tang spent time in the office until his hair turned white; Huan Junshan entered the official career, but his wings were broken due to the Yuntai controversy; Feng Jingtong had the virtue of a phoenix, but his wings were destroyed because of slander and slander. Are these people lacking in talent and lacking in virtue?
In modern times, Liu Shan of Pei State and Liu Shan's younger brother Liu Fa were both outstanding talents at that time.
Liu Shan was none other than Kansai Confucius. He was familiar with the Six Classics extensively, followed instructions and taught the younger generations, and wholeheartedly followed Confucian principles.
Liu Long's character is noble and pure, like autumn frost, and his heart is pure, like the jade from Kunlun Mountain. He is unique and has outstanding character. He does not follow the crowd and conforms to the world.
Both of them came from poor families, but they both cultivated virtues and their reputations spread throughout the world.
However, their official position was lower than that of the minister, and their status was not as good as that of the bodyguard. These two people died one after another, and there was no one to inherit the sacrifice.
From what happened to these two sages, we can see some patterns in ancient times: those sages who were as talented and handsome as gold and jade were all abandoned at that time. They had talents but no one used them. They withered like grass and trees, died like elk, their anointed blood spilled across the fields, and their bones filled the valleys. There are countless people like this who have faded into obscurity, and it’s impossible to describe them endlessly!
From this point of view, the noble prime minister and the lowly Zaoli, the long-lived Rong Chenggong, Peng Zu and the Shangzi who died in their youth, the rich Yidun and the poor, the beautiful Yangwen and the ugly girl Dunqia are all produced naturally, not by talent.
People say that life and death are all determined by fate, and wealth and poverty are determined by God. This is probably what they are referring to.
However, the forms of fate appear everywhere and are ever-changing. Some people cry first and then laugh in life, some people have good fortunes and then misfortunes, some people have good fortunes and disasters come uninvited, and some people have to rely on the power of others to realize their destiny.
Various destinies are intertwined and intertwined, good and bad come and go, and misfortunes and misfortunes tolerate each other. They cannot be tested by one principle or verified by one method. However, the laws of fate are subtle and strict. They have no sound or form, so they cannot be seen or heard.
Destiny must rely on people to show its effectiveness, and also rely on people to embody its symptoms. It is like the crown of the emperor, and it is like appointing hundreds of officials to take charge of their respective duties.
When some foolish people saw King Cheng Tang and King Wu ascending to the throne, they thought they relied on the power of divine martial arts to quell troubles; when they heard that Confucius and Mo Zhai were morally virtuous at that time, they thought it was their extraordinary speeches that made them wise;
Some people have beautiful appearance and delicate skin; some people have ugly appearance and abnormal facial features. This is a physical difference.
Some people are born early in the morning and die early in the morning; some people are like turtles and cranes, living for thousands of years. This is the difference in lifespan.
Some people can cope with things easily and react quickly, while others are confused and confused. This is a difference in intelligence. We all know that these three aspects are determined by God, but people's honor and disgrace are said to be determined by people. Creation is like knowing only two fives, but not understanding that they add up to ten. This is the first confused concept.
The dragon, rhinoceros and sun horns are the appearance of an emperor; the turtle eyes and turtle inscriptions on the river are the appearance of a prince.
If you look in the mirror, you will know that you will be tortured; if you press the secret seal when worshiping God, it means that you will inherit the throne.
The stars are like rainbows and thunder and lightning circle the center, which is a sign of the birth of the Holy King; Lao Shan cried at night and said that the Red Emperor killed the White Emperor, and the red clouds gathered during the day, which was an auspicious sign that an emperor would rise.
Creation is a sign that appears in advance, spreads and becomes reality in future generations.
If you think that by leading warriors on the battlefield and raising weapons to attack the enemy, you can enter the palace and ascend to the throne of God, then you do not understand the situation in the underworld and the laws of destiny arranged by gods.
This is the second area of ​​confusion. The land of Kongsang where Confucius was born has turned into a big river; the county of Liyang has turned into a lake where fish and turtles play in the water.
Xiang Yu's army slaughtered the soldiers of the King of Han, and the Sui River was blocked by corpses, so that the river could not flow; the Qin army buried Zhao's soldiers alive, and their cries were like thunder.
Fire burned down Kungang, and beautiful jade and sand were burned together; severe frost fell at night, and Vanilla Zhilan froze to death together with Xiao Ai.
Even if talented people like Ziyou and Zixia, Yi Yin and Yan Yuan were able to predict the signs and have great foresight, how could they resist such a thing from happening?
This is a third-party confused concept.
Some people say that the Pearl of the Bright Moon will never be without its kind; the Queen of Xia's Huang will never be without flaws.
Therefore, when Cui Tingbo died, he only served as the county magistrate of a small county, and Sima Changqing also only served as the magistrate of Xiaowen Garden. Their talents cannot be regarded as outstanding, and the monarch they met cannot be said to be unsage, but the radiant and moist green jade is broken, and the beautiful xuanli jade that shines in the night is incomplete. Could it be that the inch is long and the ruler is short?
If this is the case, if Zhufu Yan and Gongsun Hong were not promoted after participating in the countermeasures, and their repeated suggestions were not accepted, then they would still be in Zi!
They herd pigs in the fields and were abandoned by the local governor of their hometown. If their short life passed quickly and they died suddenly due to illness, then how could the shame they left behind be like that of Cui Tingbo and Sima Changqing?
When the palace is opened for them and they are appointed as noble officials, their reputation shines like lightning and spreads like the spring breeze, spreading throughout the country and abroad. Is it because they were ignorant in the past and wise in the future? What they said and done in the past was wrong but what they said and done in the future will be correct?
Or is it that there are certain arrangements for glory and humiliation, and there are certain principles for destiny?
To make rash comments without understanding these is the fourth aspect of confused concepts. When the tiger roars, the wind comes immediately; when the dragon flies, the clouds come one after another. Therefore, when Yu Shun ascended the throne, the Eight Yuans and Eight Kais were employed, and when Shang Zhou ascended the throne, Fei Lian was favored.
However, there are few good people and many evil people in the world; there are many foolish kings and few wise and sage kings.
Vanillas and stinkweeds will not be stored in the same container, and owlbirds and luancrows will not live together.
In this way, evil people like Hun Chao and Yao Zhu were entrenched in the Yuntai Bookstore one after another, and wise men like Ku Cha and Chan Jian were allowed to work under the rocks in the mountains.
Faced with this situation, he said indifferently that the success or failure of the country depends entirely on me and has nothing to do with God. This is the fifth area of ​​confusion.
The Wei State is a country of Rong and Di. They have human faces and beast hearts and they are in the midst of pleasure, which leads to the disaster of death.
They regard killing and killing as their morality, and regard lust and incest as their benevolence and righteousness. Even the strong winds that cause harm in Qingqiu and the chisel teeth that cause harm in Huaye cannot be compared with the ferocity of the wolves and Rongdi in the country.
Since the decline of Zhisu, the world has been in turmoil. The ugly prisoners of Zuo Jin saw the opportunity and attacked quickly, so they occupied Shanghai and Luo and captured the five capitals.
Live in the hometown of previous emperors. Stealing the title of emperor in the Central Plains. Fight for the people of the three emperors, seize the land of the five emperors, and breed their descendants, so that the seeds of Rong and Di fill China. Alas!
God sends blessings to good people and disasters to evil people. It is just empty words.
Isn't this not the existence of misfortunes and blessings in opposition to each other, alternate rise and fall, and let people come to disturb the world?
This is the sixth area of ​​confusion.
However, the ten aspects of destiny, life and death, nobility, wealth and poverty, national chaos, misfortunes and blessings, are all given by God.
Foolishness, wisdom, good and evil, these four aspects are practiced by people.
If a person is not wise and wise like Shun and Yu, nor has an evil heart like Danzhu and Shangjun, as long as his talent is at a moderate level, then whether he is good or evil depends on the influence and influence of the environment.
Therefore, white silk will not stay white for a long time, sometimes it will turn black, and sometimes it will be dyed yellow; abalone will stink, orchid will fragrant, and it will naturally change when it enters this environment.
Therefore, Zhilu's study with Jianxing sharpened his integrity and integrity, and King Qian of Chu consulted with Ying, who became the culprit of the regicide rebellion.
However, a wicked person like Tong Dan, King of Chu Mu, would have descendants with great virtues; a good person like Ji Lu would not be able to cause the enemy to stop attacking and die in battle while tying the tassel.
Creation means that the rightness of actions is determined by people, but the good and bad are determined by fate.
Some people believe that ghosts and gods harm arrogant and complacent people, while God protects virtuous and kind people.
Therefore, Song Jinggong's benevolent words made Ying Huoxing, known as the star of law enforcement, step back. Emperor Yin Tang cut his hair and nails and prayed to the God for rain. Clouds thousands of miles away gathered and rain fell immediately.
If we say that good and evil are not fulfilled, it is inconsistent with the principles of these things.
Moreover, the father of Dingguo, Gao Jianmen, waited for the carriages and horses of his ennobled descendants, and the mother of Yan Yannian cleaned the cemetery to prepare for the coffin of her son who was about to be defeated. These are the actions of a gentleman to encourage himself to constantly strive for self-improvement.
If there is no reward for practicing benevolence and righteousness, why do you still do good deeds and gain a reputation?
This is an extreme statement.
The sage's words are simple yet profound, subtle yet euphemistic, and the truth is profound and difficult to fully understand. They are like the water flow of rivers and Han Dynasties, which are deep, wide and boundless.
Sometimes education is provided to make lazy people who do not seek progress progress, and sometimes destiny is discussed to reveal people's inner world. A house that accumulates good deeds must have Yu Qing. The saying of "Yu Qing" is to carry out education; the sigh of "when the phoenix does not come" and the sage is not met is to talk about destiny.
Now we only use fragments of the saint's words to understand the essence of the saint's thoughts. This is no different from talking about the changes in the spring and autumn seasons!
Moreover, King Zhao of Chu also said the same benevolent words as Jinggong of Song, but the clouds symbolizing the evil spirit did not disappear; King Xuan of Zhou also prayed for rain like Shang Tang, and all the jade stones were dedicated to the gods, but there was no rain.
The moral virtue accumulated by Yu Dingguo's father could not match that of Fang Xun and Shun Hua; Yan Yannian's cruelty and ferocity could not compare with Tao Zhi's.
The good deeds done are the same, the evil deeds done are the same, but the blessings and misfortunes obtained are not the same, and the rise and fall are also inconsistent.
Is this the case with the vast, vast and omniscient God?
"Poetry" says: Although the wind and rain never stop and the sky is dark, the chickens always crow.
So good people always do good things, how can they stop!
Eating rice, eating fish, wearing fox fur and fur, wearing pure white silk, watching wonderful and exquisite dances, and listening to the music of Yunhe's fine materials. These are the needs of the people's life, and they do not require anything to do so.
Cultivate morality, learn benevolence and righteousness, establish deep feelings of filial piety and brotherhood, establish loyalty and integrity, be infiltrated and influenced by ritual and music, and follow the rules of the past kings. Yu Zhongrong only had similar personalities and good friendships with Wang Ji, Xie Jiqing and others. Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were not in harmony with everyone at that time, so the three of them socialized together, drank as much as they wanted, and no longer paid attention to ethics.
After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was appointed as a consultant to join the army and left the capital to serve as the magistrate of Yi County.
When the turmoil broke out during the Taiqing period, Yu Zhongrong lived in Kuaiji and died of illness at the age of seventy-four.
Yu Zhongrong copied thirty volumes of books by various scholars, twenty volumes of geography books of various schools, three volumes of Biography of Women, and twenty volumes of collected works. These books are all circulated in the world.
Lu Yungong, named Zilong, was from Wujun.
His grandfather Lu Xian lived in Renzhou.
His father, Lu Wan, had a long history with Ren Ningyuan.
When Lu Yungong was five years old, he could recite "The Analects of Confucius" and "Mao Shi". When he was nine years old, he could read "Han Shu" and memorize everything.
His grandfather Lu Bian and Pei Guo Liu Xian asked him about ten things in the "Book of Han", and he could answer them one by one without making any mistakes. Liu Xian was full of praise and thought he was different from ordinary people.
When he grew up, Lu Yungong was studious and talented.
He was elected as a scholar in the state.
Lu Yun Gongjigong was transferred to the throne of Xuanhui, King of Wuling, and King of Pingxi, Xiangshu, to join the army.
Lu Yungong originally wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele". Zhang Zuan, the governor of Wuxing, left his post and returned to the capital. On the way, he read the inscription written by Lu Yungong and said with emotion: This man is simply the contemporary Cai Bojie.
After Zhang Zuan arrived in the capital, he was in charge of the selection of officials. He recommended Lu Yungong to Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu then called Lu Yungong to serve as the minister of Yi Cao Lang. He was soon appointed to this position and was assigned to Shouguang Province. He also used his original official position to know how to serve as a minister.
Soon after, in addition to being awarded the title of Writer, he was moved to the post of Zhongshu Huangmenlang and was in charge of writing.
Lu Yungong was good at playing Go. He once accompanied Gaozu at night. The crown he was wearing caught the light of a candle. Gaozu smiled and said to him: The candle burned the mink tail on your hat.
Gaozu was about to appoint Lu Yungong as his minister, and his crown would be decorated with a mink tail, so Gaozu used these words to joke with Lu Yungong.
At that time, a new bream boat was built in Tianyuanchi. The boat was wide and short. Gaozu often took this boat to ride on the waves in his spare time. Among the courtiers, he only brought Taichang Liu Zhilin, Guozi to Gai, and Youwei Zhu Yi. Lu Yungong was young at that time and his position was not high, but he was also among the courtiers who accompanied Gaozu on the boat.
Emperor Gaozu's favor and favor towards him reached such an extent.
In the first year of Taiqing, Lu Yungong passed away at the age of thirty-seven.
Emperor Gaozu was deeply saddened by his death and wrote an edict in his own hand, saying: I serve as the minister of Huangmen and as Duke Lu Yungong. He is a rising star with beautiful demeanor and broad knowledge.
His sudden death is deeply saddening.
A date should be set to mourn him. He donated 50,000 yuan and 40 pieces of cloth to help his family with funeral arrangements.
Zhang Zan was the governor of Xiangzhou at the time. He wrote to Lu Yungong's uncle Lu Xiang and his elder brother Lu Yanzi, saying: Messengers from the capital have come to know that your virtuous brother's son and virtuous brother, Huangmen Shilang, has unfortunately passed away. This is not only the loss of an outstanding talent in your family, but everyone who knew him feels the same sadness, and the sorrow and regret cannot stop.
The son and younger brother of a wise brother, his natural talents have long been revealed, and his talent is even more extraordinary in his weak years. Once the book is passed through, there is no need to read it a second time.
Like Lu Ji's filial piety and Wang Xiang's love for his mother, this is a natural talent; being able to sit down and study hard and rise to the ranks of talents is not dependent on the help of outsiders.
When scholars gather together, he can stand out among the scholars with his own writings; when asked and answered, he can express his own experience and often have unique insights.
Just after his weak years, he was already proficient in diction and the six arts. He commented on many scholars. He was an outstanding poet.
I used to be an official of the imperial court with him, we followed each other, and we had a deep friendship. Because we had similar aspirations, we became close friends. We spend the whole year together, getting along day and night.
From morning to night, I read ancient books and wrote articles. Almost all of my lifelong close friends have gradually faded away. I remember my old friends, but there are not many of them alive anymore.
As for how much time I have left in my life, the most satisfying thing is to associate with him.
My position was transferred to Xiao and Hunan. The boat stopped on the riverbank in Beijing. When I was about to leave, I could see the deep affection between him and me.
Staying temporarily on the outskirts of the capital in the evening, he and I chatted intimately. We stayed there night after night, reluctant to leave, shaking hands and saying goodbye, holding back the sadness, and each headed for a bright future.
I worked abroad for several years and was plagued by illness. I became confused and angry, and stopped interacting with others for a long time.
I relied on several dictations, but I never had any talented people who could be trusted with this task. I wrote by myself, and the weight of my handwriting was uneven, which made me feel even more guilty.
All the old friends in the capital were like clouds and rain. Some were separated, and some never said goodbye. Only the exchanges with him, and letters asking each other, never broke off.
Our communication is beyond the traces and will not be blocked by the long distance; our friendship is in our arms and will not change with the passage of time.
I have been working as an official away from home for five or six years, and I earnestly look forward to returning to my hometown. I look forward to Shu returning to the capital every day and reliving our old affection with him.
Why did this separation actually make us separated forever?
When I waved goodbye, who could keep myself alive for a hundred years? I was only afraid that I would suddenly decline, so I had no other arrangements.
Unexpectedly, he died at a young age, and the learned and wise man was buried, which makes people even more sad.
I think back then I recommended him because he has always had a firm ambition and you have a deep relationship as brothers. In addition, as we regard him as the real asset of the Lu family, we have even greater love for him.
Suddenly encountered this sad and heartbreaking thing, what else can I say!
Writing a letter increases the sadness and pain, making the words incoherent.
Lu Yungong's cousin Lu Caizi was also famous for his talent. He successively served as Zhongshulang, Xuancheng Wangyou, and Prince's concubine. Ting Weiqing died before Lu Yungong.
Lu Caizi and Lu Yungong both have collections of essays, which are also circulated in the world.
Ren Xiaogong, whose courtesy name is Xiaogong, was born in Linhuai.
His great-grandfather was a farmer and the governor of Southern Yuzhou during the Song Dynasty.
Ren Xiaogong lost his father when he was young. He served his mother very filially and became famous for this.
Ren Xiaogong was dedicated and diligent in his studies. His family was poor and he often asked people to borrow books when he had no books to act in.
Every time he read it, he could recite it without missing anything.
Ren Cuoyu's maternal grandfather, Qiu Ta, had a relationship with Emperor Gaozu. Hearing that Ren Xiaogong was talented and learned, he summoned him to the Western Province to compile history books.
Ren Xiaogong was first appointed to the imperial court, and was promoted to Shouguang Province as the Minister of Si Wen. Soon he was also appointed as Zhongshu General Shiren.
Emperor Gaozu issued an edict and ordered Ren Xiaogong to write the "Inscription under the Temple of Jianling Temple". Ren Xiaogong also presented the "Preface" to the collected works of Emperor Gaozu written by himself. The words were rich and gorgeous. From the time of the Han Dynasty, Ren Xiaogong was in charge of the court's documents full-time.
Ren Xiaogong wrote articles quickly, and he could write them immediately after receiving the imperial edict. It seemed that he didn't spend much time on it. He wrote good articles and presented them to memorials. Emperor Gaozu always praised his well-written articles and gave him gold and silk many times.
When he was young, Ren Xiaogong read scriptures with Master Xiao Siyun and was well versed in Buddhist teachings. When he was sent away, Ren Xiaogong only ate vegetables, followed the precepts, and believed in Buddhism very sincerely.
However, Ren Xiaogong liked to show off his achievements by nature, and often relied on his talents to put himself above others. He often showed contempt for famous figures at that time, and the world looked down upon him because of this.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Ren Xiaogong started recruiting sergeants. He led the recruited soldiers to be affiliated with Xiao Zhengde and stationed on the south bank of the Yangtze River.
When the rebel army arrived, Xiao Zhengde led his army to surrender to Hou Jing, and Ren Xiaogong returned to rush to the palace city. The gate of the palace city had been closed, so Ren Xiaogong fled into Dongfu. Soon Shufu was attacked by the rebels, and Ren Xiaogong was killed.
Ren Xiaogong's collected works are circulated in the world.
Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi, Langxie.
His ancestor Yan Han, seven generations ago, served as Shizhong, Guozi Jijiu, and Jinghou of Xiping during the Jin Dynasty.
His father is far-sighted, knowledgeable, ambitious and ethical.
In the past, when Emperor Qi He was guarding Jingzhou, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to join the army for the green affairs. When Emperor Qi He ascended the throne in Jiangling, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to serve as the official secretary and censor, and soon became the Zhongcheng.
After Emperor Gaozu accepted Qi's abdication, Yan Jianyuan went on a hunger strike and died in anger for several days.
When Emperor Gaozu heard the news, he said: I am following the destiny of heaven and obeying the will of man. What does it have to do with the scholar-bureaucrats in the world?
And Yan Jianyuan actually did such a thing!
Yan Xie lost his father when he was young and was raised by his uncle's family.
He has been praised for his magnanimity since childhood.
Yan Xie has extensively dabbled in group calligraphy and is good at writing cursive script and official script.
When Yan Xie first became an official, he took up the post of permanent attendant of the Xiangdong Kingdom, and also served as the official secretary of the government.
Shizu came out of the capital to guard Jingzhou, and Yan Xie was transferred to the office of actual professors and records.
At that time, Gu Xie of Wu County also served in the palace. He and Yan Xie had the same names, and their talents and learning were comparable. They were called "Er Xie" in the palace.
Yan Xie's uncle, Chen Jun Xie Chen, passed away. Yan Xie mourned his uncle with the same etiquette as he would an uncle because of his kindness to his uncle. People who talked about this matter valued Yan Xie's friendship more.
Yan Xie also felt that his father at home died for his righteousness, so he did not pursue prominent positions and often refused calls from the court, only serving in the feudal prince's palace.
In the fifth year of Datong, Yan Xie passed away at the age of forty-two.
Shizu lamented his death and wrote "Nostalgic Poems" to mourn him.
One of the chapters says: With great magnanimity and elegant demeanor, he is truly a talent in name and in reality!
Although they have been promoted, they have not yet been promoted, resulting in talented people still staying in positions with low salaries.
Five chapters of "Biography of Jinxian" and two volumes of "Disasters of the Sun and Moon" written by Yan Xie were burned down due to fire.
Yan Xie had two sons: Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, both of whom became famous very early.
During the Chengsheng reign, Yan Zhitui was promoted to Zhengyuan Lang and Zhongshu Sheren.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Civil Affairs of Chen, said: Emperor Wen of Wei said that few ancient scholars could maintain their reputation. Why?
Literati must use their intelligence skillfully and reveal their ambitions differently. Therefore, they are prone to look down on their peers and show off their arrogance.
On big occasions, he will insult and despise princes and kings; on small occasions, he will look down on and insult his friends, which will lead to jealousy and sin.
For example, Qu Yuan and Mai Yi were ostracized and exiled, and Huan Tan and Feng Yan were reprimanded and dismissed. Sending them out was something that only happened once in a generation. It was really the disaster brought about by the arrogance of these literati!
The literary men recorded above were in an era of prosperous education, and they wrote articles with gorgeous rhetoric. They did not have depression and worries, and they did not encounter the disasters that the previous generations of literati suffered. It is really great.
The discussion shows that he is a kind of person who pays attention to destiny.
Sages rarely talk about things like fate. They tend to talk about fate and believe that fate must control life. This is not the meaning of the sages' classics.
summary:
Liu Jun, courtesy name Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan. His father was Liu Ge. At age one, his mother took him home. During Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei, and at eight, Liu Jun was kidnapped to Zhongshan. A wealthy man, Liu Shi, redeemed him and taught him. The Wei moved him to Sangqian. He was an eager learner, often reading by torchlight all night, sometimes burning his hair. During Qi Yongming, he returned to Qi. He sought out rare books, and Cui Weizu called him a "book slut." He sought a position under Xiao Ziliang but was devalued by Xu Xiaosi. He served under Xiao Yaoxin, who treated him generously. After Xiao Yaoxin's death, Liu Jun was long without promotion. In early Tianjian, he served as a secretary. He was dismissed for transporting prohibited items. He was later given books to compile "Lei Yuan," but left due to illness. He wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi." Emperor Gaozu disliked him for not following others, so he was not used. Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings.

The article "Discrimination of Fate" argues that a scholar's situation is determined by fate. It laments that talented people like Guan Ren have low positions. It states that the difference between human nature and endowment, and a lifetime of setbacks, cannot be understood. It discusses the concepts of Tao and nature, stating that destiny is determined in the dark and never changes. It lists sages like Jin Wengong and Confucius who could not escape fate. It mentions modern examples like Liu Shan and Liu Fa, who were talented but died in obscurity. It argues that nobility, longevity, and wealth are produced naturally, not by talent. It lists five areas of confusion regarding fate, including the belief that honor and disgrace are determined by people, that success comes from martial power, that good and evil are always rewarded, and that a country's success depends on its ruler. It concludes that a gentleman follows the right path, obeys heaven, and secures his own destiny, understanding that fate is beyond human control.

After Liu Jun's "Distinction of Fate" was written, Liu Bo of Zhongshan wrote to refute him. Liu Jun replied, but Liu Bo died before seeing the reply. Liu Jun wrote a letter to the deceased Liu Bo, expressing his sorrow. Liu Jun's paper was not published due to its length. Liu Jun wrote an "Automatic Preface" comparing himself to Feng Jingtong, listing three similarities and four differences. He lived in Shuyang, where many studied under him. He died at sixty, and his disciples gave him the posthumous name Mr. Xuanjing.

Liu Bo, courtesy name Mingxin, was from Zhongshan. He was good at writing articles and knowledgeable. He held various official positions and died during a dispatch.

Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia. His great-grandfather was Xie Lingyun. He was a child prodigy. He once threw himself into a river when his father was demoted. He was studious and had literary talent. He held various official positions, including Censor. He was open-minded and not bound by court laws. He was once dismissed for misconduct. He later petitioned to accompany the Northern Expedition but was dismissed after the army was defeated. He lived in seclusion, often drinking with friends. He died of illness. He had a collection of essays.

Liu Xie, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Ju. He lost his father early, did not marry, and lived with a monk, becoming proficient in Buddhist scriptures. He became an official in early Tianjian. He suggested changing suburban sacrifices to fruits and vegetables, which was adopted. Prince Zhaoming admired him. He wrote "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons" in fifty chapters. The preface explains his motivation, stating that a gentleman wants to establish merit and write books. He dreamed of following Confucius. He argues that articles are branches of classics. He criticizes previous literary critics like Cao Pi and Lu Ji for being incomplete or trivial. His book discusses rhymed and unrhymed passages, analyzes emotions and literary talents, and covers various aspects of writing. He sought evaluation from Shen Yue, who valued the book. Liu Xie later became a monk, changing his name to Huidi, and died less than a year later.

Wang Ji, courtesy name Wenhai, was from Linyi. He could write at seven. He was talented and once wrote a poem that Shen Yue appreciated. He held various official positions, including magistrate, but was dismissed for misconduct. He visited mountains in Kuaiji, sometimes staying for months. He wrote a famous poem with the line "The forest with noisy cicadas is more quiet." He died soon after. His son Wang Bi died before him.

He Sicheng, courtesy name Yuanjing, was from Tan. He was diligent and good at writing. He held various official positions. Shen Yue admired his poem and had it inscribed on his wall. He was recommended to compile "Qing Lue." He moved to the position of Censor. He was knowledgeable and admired by Xu Mian and Zhou She. He died at fifty-four. He had fifteen volumes of collected works. He once said that He Xun was the most talented among the three Hes, but meant the reputation should go to himself. He Zilang, also from the same clan, was talented and died at twenty-four.

Liu Yao, courtesy name Shishen, was from Pingyuan. He was studious and well-read. Shen Yue and Ren Fang often asked him about forgotten knowledge. He corrected Shen Yue's interpretation of ancient sacrificial bottles. He was knowledgeable about many things, including the origin of the "long-necked king." Shen Yue praised his writings. He held various official positions, including magistrate, and had a clean record. He was recommended to compile "Bianlue." He wrote "Lin Ting Fu," which Wang Sengru praised. He died at fifty. He was honest and frugal. He wrote several books, including "Ya Ya" and "Chu Ci Cao Mu Shu."

Xie Zheng, courtesy name Xuandu, was from Yangxia. He was smart and handsome, fond of learning. He held various official positions. He once finished a poem in one second at a banquet, which Emperor Gaozu admired. He was appointed to discuss the appointment of a new crown prince. He died at thirty-seven. His friend Wang Shuan compiled his manuscripts.

Zang Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, was from Ju. He was filial and studious. He wrote "Tuenyou Fu," which Ren Fang admired. He was upright and did not follow rules. He was knowledgeable, especially in "Han Shu." He served as a county governor in barbarian areas, where he quelled banditry. He died during his tenure. He has ten volumes of collected works.

Fu Ting, courtesy name Shibiao. He was smart and talented, good at five-character poems. Ren Fang admired him. He met Emperor Gaozu at eighteen and was promoted. He lectured on "The Analects." He later built a house in the eastern suburbs and stopped serving. He wrote a letter to Xu Mian, expressing his desire for seclusion. Xu Mian replied, praising him but encouraging him to serve. Fu Ting later became an official again but was accused of accepting bribes. He hid as a Taoist priest. He later served under King Shaoling. He died during Hou Jing's rebellion. He wrote ten volumes of "Yi Shuo" and twenty volumes of collected works. His son, Fu Zhiming, served Hou Jing and died in prison.

Yu Zhongrong, courtesy name Zhongrong, was from Geling. He lost his father young and was studious. He was appointed as a crown prince through his uncle's request. He was knowledgeable but impulsive and liked to drink. He was friends with Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing. He died at seventy-four. He copied many books and wrote several works.

Lu Yungong, courtesy name Zilong, was from Wujun. He could recite classics at a young age. He was studious and talented. He wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele," which Zhang Zuan praised. He was called to serve by Emperor Gaozu. He was good at Go. Emperor Gaozu favored him greatly. He died at thirty-seven. Emperor Gaozu mourned him. Zhang Zan wrote a letter expressing his sorrow.

Ren Xiaogong, courtesy name Xiaogong, was from Linhuai. He was filial and studious. He was summoned to compile history books. He wrote quickly and was praised by Emperor Gaozu. He was well-versed in Buddhism. He was arrogant and looked down on others. During Hou Jing's invasion, he led soldiers but was killed when the rebels attacked.

Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi. He lost his father young. He was magnanimous and good at calligraphy. He served in the Xiangdong Kingdom. He and Gu Xie were called "Er Xie." He mourned his uncle with proper etiquette. He did not pursue prominent positions. He died at forty-two. His works were burned in a fire. His sons, Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, became famous early.

translation:
"Yi" says: A gentleman escapes from the world and does not feel bored. He is independent and does not know fear.
Confucius called Chang Ju and Jie Dun hermits.
Some hermits in ancient times were ashamed to hear about the Zen Dynasty, considered it noble to give up the throne, regarded the Wancheng throne as a disgrace, and went to death without any regrets.
This kind of person despises life and values ​​morality. He is rare in the world and appears occasionally. He is a superior hermit.
Some work as prison gates to support themselves, and work as officials under the pillars to support themselves. They live a simple life to realize their ambitions, and their status is low but they don't show any shame.
He was a so-called great hermit who hid in the city and court, and his status was lower than that of the superior hermits.
Some exposed their bodies, pretended to be crazy, blinded their eyes, made their voices hoarse, renounced the world, abandoned rituals and music to return to the right path, and suppressed the need to talk about filial piety, love, and family affection.
This kind of person protects himself, avoids harm, masters the way of escaping from the world, and his status is lower than that of the great hermit.
However, these people have not forgotten the key to keeping silent, staying on the right path in seclusion, and finally getting good results.
How can they and those who join in troubled times, compete for wealth and cater to the world, say the same thing? "Mencius" says: For people nowadays, regarding juelu, getting it is like gaining life, losing it is like losing life.
"Huainanzi said: People use still water as mirrors, not running water."
To be able to inspire righteousness, wash away filth, curb corruption and bend the law, and stop the pursuit of power and profit, I am afraid only a hermit can do it!
Since ancient times, there has been no emperor who did not respect the conduct of hermits.
Even Tang Yao couldn't make Chaofu and Xu You obey each other, and King Wu of Zhou couldn't make Boyi and Shuqi abandon their integrity and become ministers. Mo Gaozu was arrogant but respectful to Qili Ji and Xia Huang Gong. Mo Guang Wu Emperor governed the world according to the law but was submissive to Yan Guang and Zhou Dang. Since then, this has been the case for generations.
During the Liang Dynasty, the country prospered and inherited the moral education and governance of the previous generation. All the hermits whose morals were worthy of imitation and whose knowledge could serve as role models were included in the "Chushi Pian".
When the word Zixi comes, the Lujiang River sneaks in.
His grandfather, He Shangzhi, served as Sikong during the Song Dynasty.
His father, He Shuo, was appointed governor of Yidu.
He Shuo had always suffered from madness. He killed his wife for no reason and was executed according to the law.
He Dian was eleven years old at the time, and his life was almost destroyed by the grief of losing his parents.
When he grew up, He Dian was saddened by the disasters that had happened in his family and wanted not to get married or become an official, so He Shangzhi forced him to marry the Wang family of Langye.
All other etiquette had been completed, and when the wedding ceremony was about to take place, He Dian cried to He Shangzhi again and again, begging to be allowed to stick to his original wishes, so that the wedding was suspended.
He Dian has a dignified and comely appearance, is well-read, and is good at talking and discussing.
The He Dian family was originally a wealthy family, with many in-laws serving as high-ranking officials.
Although He Dian did not enter the city or enter the government, he only wore household clothes, without hairpins or belts, and traveled among the people. Sometimes he drove a chariot and wore straw sandals. At that time, people called this point "Tongyin".
He Dian's brother He Qiu also lived in seclusion in Huqiu Mountain in Wu County.
After He Qiu's death, He Dian only ate vegetarian food and did not drink alcohol during the period of mourning for his brother. After the three-year mourning period was over, He Dian's waist circumference had been reduced by half.
In the early and late years of the Song and Tai Dynasties, the imperial court conscripted He Dian to serve as the prince to wash horses; in the early years of the Qi Dynasty, the court repeatedly recruited He Dian to serve as Zhongshulang and the prince's concubine, but none of them accepted the call.
He became close friends with Xie Man of Chen Jun, Zhang Rong of Wu State, and Kong Zhigui of Kuaiji.
He Dian's cousin, He Dun, gave He Dian a manor in Donglimen to live in, and Kong Zhigui built a house in the garden for He Dian.
There is Bian Zhongzhen's tomb in the garden. He planted flowers on the side of the tomb. Every time he drank, he must first sprinkle the wine on the ground to pay homage to Bian Zhongzhen.
At first, when Chu Yuan and Wang Jian were prime ministers, He Point said to people: I wrote "Qishu Praise", which said: "Chu Yuan is from a noble family, and Wang Jian is also a talented person in the country. Who can care about the country without relying on these close relatives and old ministers?"
When Wang Jian heard this, he originally wanted to visit Hedian, but later he realized that he could not see Hedian, so he gave up the plan.
Xiao Yi, the king of Yuzhang, drove to visit He Dian, but He Dian escaped through the back door.
Xiao Ziliang, King of Situ Jingling, wanted to condescend to meet He Dian. He Dian was at Falun Temple at that time. Xiao Ziliang went to Falun Temple to request to meet He Dian. He Dian dressed up as a hermit and sat at the table. Xiao Ziliang was so happy that he gave Ji Shuye's wine glass and Xu Jingshan's wine pot to He Dian.
He Diandian suffered from thirsty dysentery when he was young and was not cured for many years.
Later, He Dian established a forum at Wuzhong Shifo Temple. He once took a nap in the place where he lectured. He dreamed that a Taoist with a special appearance gave him a handful of pills. He swallowed the pills in his dream, and he recovered from his illness. People at that time believed that this was a blessing brought by honest virtue.
He Dian was free-spirited by nature, not constrained by trivial matters, and loved to give to others. He would not disobey anything given to him by people near or far, he would accept everything, and then give away what he received to others.
He Dian once passed by Zhuquemen Street in a car. Someone stole He Dian's clothes from the back of the car. He Dian saw it but kept silent. Someone caught the person stealing the clothes and handed it to He Dian. He Dian then gave the clothes to the person who stole the clothes. The person who stole the clothes did not dare to accept it. He Dian threatened to report it to the government. The person who stole the clothes was scared, so he accepted the clothes donated by He Dian. He Dian urged the person who stole the clothes to leave quickly.
He Dian is very discerning in identifying talents, and he has identified and recommended many people. When Wu Xingqiu Chi was still a child, he admired him very much; when Ji Yang Jiangyan was still in a low status, Bao Shu praised him.
Later, both of them showed their talents as He Dian said. When He Dian grew old, he married the daughter of Kong Si of Lu, who was also a hermit.
Although He Dian was married, he did not meet his wife and built another house to accommodate her. No one understood his intention to do this.
Zhang Rong of the State of Wu was dismissed from office when he was young. There are sentences in the poems he wrote that indicated that he did not seek official advancement. The poem "He Dian Reward" said: In the past, I heard about Sedu, but I was not in front of the bamboo slips.
This means that Zhang Rong was removed from his official position and was no longer busy with paperwork.
Although this is a joke, Rei Rong has always regarded writing poems as a problem. Later, when He Dian got married, Zhang Rongcai wrote another poem to He Dian, saying: What a pity, the dusk is so desolate.
Joking about Bao Wei's marriage incident in his later years. He Dian also regarded this poem as a problem in his heart, but he never found a chance to resolve it.
Gaozu and He Dian had a relationship. After Gaozu ascended the throne, he wrote an edict with his own hand and said: In the past, because I had more free time, I was able to associate with you. We sat together in the bamboo forest, perched on the clear pond, forgetting the troubles in front of us, and discussing ancient people and events. How happy it was.
It has been fourteen years since I temporarily bid farewell to my hometown. It is impossible to describe the difficulties and obstacles I have encountered.
Ever since I followed my destiny and ascended to the throne of God, I have often thought about meeting you. How is my health lately? On which mountain have I been tired?
In the past, Yan Guang pushed open the door of the palace, walked up the steps of the palace, talked with Emperor Guangwu about the ways of heaven and man, and reminisced about old feelings. What kind of behavior did he not obey the way of ministers? What was the hindrance to his noble conduct?
Now I will give you a deerskin scarf and other items.
I hope you can come to the palace in a few days.

I don’t have the ability to repay others, so how can I always feel guilty?
Not long after, Liu Xian wrote "The End of the Revolution", which advocated changing funeral customs. The time was the 17th year of Tianjian. The treatise says: Sages rarely talk about matters of life and death.
Confucius said: When the spirit of spirits gathers and becomes a human being, the soul will change when it wanders away. From this, we know that the situation of ghosts and gods is similar to that of heaven and earth without departing from it.
His words are concise, and the purport of his words is exquisite. What he talks about is very profound, and the meaning of his words is very mysterious. It cannot be inferred by guessing, and it is difficult to examine carefully. I will rely on my ignorance and boldly try to talk about things related to communication.
The combination of body and spirit is life, the separation of spirit and body is called death, the combination of the two is called speech and action, and the separation of the two is silence.
When there are words and actions, everyone knows the manifestation of the spirit; when there is silence, no one can know the whereabouts of the spirit.
If everyone knows it, then it will be very clear even without explaining the truth. If no one knows it, then the more you explain it, the more mysterious the truth will be.
Therefore, Yixun, Hua Kuang, Mo Chen, Ji, and Kong Yi all avoided this issue and did not comment on it. The sages of the previous generation also often had different opinions.
Jizha said: After death, the flesh and blood return to the earth, and the soul can go anywhere.
Zhuang Zhou said: Life is like serving a corvee, and death is like being motionless.
Looking at the two statements, it seems that the views are opposite.
Why?
The soul can go everywhere, which means that the spirit exists; death is like standing still, which means that the spirit does not exist.
Yuan Xian said: The Xia Hou family used bright weapons to sacrifice the dead. This clearly told the people that people have no consciousness after death. The people of Yin used sacrificial vessels to offer sacrifices to the dead, which clearly told the people that people still have consciousness after death.
People in the Zhou Dynasty used both visible and sacrificial vessels when offering sacrifices to the dead. This was to tell the people that they were still uncertain about whether people had consciousness after death.
Examining ancient books and historical records of previous dynasties, it is impossible to describe all the debates about knowledge and ignorance after death. If we check based on Buddhist teachings and judge based on Buddhist scriptures, then we can find basis for the remarks of the above people. There are no mistakes in the etiquette of the three generations.
Why?
The spirit is the foundation of life, and the body is the shell of life. After death, the spirit leaves the shell and attaches to other objects outside the shell.
Although the dead cannot be resurrected, the spirit has evolved and has never been extinct.
When the spirit leaves the body, all human insight and ability are gone. Therefore, the Xiahou family sacrifices the deceased with an open weapon to express that the spirit will never come back.
When attached to other objects, it turns out that the person's spiritual consciousness is also completely lost, so the Yin people used sacrificial vessels to send the deceased to show that the spirit still exists.
The statement that the spirit will not return is consistent with Zhuang Zhou's point of view, and the statement that the spirit still exists is consistent with Jizha's point of view. Each captures an aspect and does not undermine the understanding of life and death.
In essence, people are unconscious after death, so people in the Zhou Dynasty had the etiquette of using both visible and sacrificial vessels when offering sacrifices to the dead. Isn’t it exactly like this when Confucius proposed the idea that the soul wanders?
If we abandon the paranoid views and explore a compromise between the two ends, then the accusations of being unkind and unwise can be put to rest.
The body is the insensible shell, the spirit is the sentient nature.
The spirit is sentient but cannot exist alone. It can only stand on its own by being attached to a body without sentience. Therefore, the body is like a hotel on a journey to the spirit.
When a person dies, his spirit leaves this hotel and goes somewhere else.
The spirit has left, why does the hotel still exist?
After death, it is reasonable to believe that people should be buried sparingly and die quickly.
The spirit has gone to another place, so what is the object of sacrifice?
Sacrifice goes against the truth.
But the teachings of Zhou Gong and Confucius are not like this. I am afraid there are other reasons!
Probably because the ritual and music system was established in an era when folk customs were weak; the use of sacrificial utensils and the regulations of dance steps emerged from vulgar folk customs.
Setting up spiritual feasts, placing coffins, offering memorial offerings, and building tombs are all for the purpose of giving filial sons a place to remember their deceased relatives. What benefit does this have to the departed spirit?
So in ancient times, when people died, they were simply wrapped in firewood and abandoned in the wild. Can we say that the Zunlu family, the Hexu family, the Huangxiong family, and the Yan Emperor did something that went against the law?
Therefore, Tantai Ziyu sank his son's body into the river for a water burial. Jing Mobo only asked to be buried in a cave. Zhao Wenchu ​​left orders to spread loess in the coffin, and Huangfu Shi'an only asked to tie the body with hemp ropes.
These four gentlemen can be said to have mastered the laws of nature and have forgotten the teachings.
If I can follow these four gentlemen, then my lifelong ambition will be realized.
However, the customs have been passed down for many years, and it is difficult to change the funeral rules all at once. If I suddenly have to completely comply with my own ideas, I worry that my relatives will not obey me out of love.
Now I just want to get rid of the cumbersome etiquette and get rid of the custom of extravagant burials. The funeral must be frugal, the etiquette must be simple, not so radical, and the body should be buried naked, and it must not be too conservative. It must be different from the inherent customs, not hurt the feelings of relatives in the world, and also conform to the standards of a high-minded person.
Confucius said: After death, the body is wrapped up and transported back to the hometown for burial. There is a coffin but no coffin.
Funeral is also the funeral etiquette of poor families. How can I regard this kind of etiquette as simple?
Moreover, Zhang Huan left a message to wrap his body in a scarf, Wang Su said to wash his hands and feet, Fan Ran said to be buried immediately after the burial ceremony, and Xi Zhen left a message not to hold a few banquets in front of the soul. Sai Zhi's last words were to use an old ship as a coffin, He Zilian's last words was to use an ox cart to transport his coffin, Shu Qi's last words were to warn his descendants not to build a tomb for himself, and Zheng Kangcheng's last words were not to use divination to choose a burial place.
The above-mentioned ancestors only asked for a simple funeral, let alone how can people like us pursue a luxurious funeral!
Now I want to imitate the noble virtues of the sages and use their actions as my own standards. Maybe I can conform to the golden mean and hope to avoid the criticism of wasted time.
After I die, there is no need to hold a soul-calling ceremony. After washing my body, I can bury it. I only need to spend one thousand yuan to prepare a coffin and buy ordinary dresses, towels, pillows, shoes, etc.
Apart from this, there is no need to prepare other items for offering sacrifices to the deceased, utensils for burial in the coffin, and items for offering libations before burial.
Most people in the world believe what Peng Zu and Li Er said, which can be regarded as confusion.
Taking Confucius and Buddha as my teachers can help me avoid this confusion.
After the body is buried, the coffin is transported in a car without a curtain and buried in the hometown. You can find a piece of land at random. You can dig a pit in this land, as long as the pit can accommodate the coffin. Do not build tombs with bricks and tiles, do not pile earth into tombs, plant trees as decorations, do not display offerings for sacrifice, and do not set up several banquets. There is no need to set up a empty seat to worship like you did to Mao Jun; nor do you need to use a cup of water to worship like you did to Boyi.
As for the sacrifices of future generations, I will not mention it here. The things mentioned above are only for me. Do not let this affect the education.
Adults and children at home, relatives inside and outside, and friends, as long as they come to my apartment, I hope they can help realize my last wish, and I hope they will not go against my wishes.

In his later years, Yu Shen particularly respected Buddhism. He set up a monastery in his house to chant sutras and worship, and surrounded the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas every day to worship and repent, day and night.

Later one night, Yu Shen suddenly saw a monk. The monk called himself Yan Gong. His appearance and behavior were very special. He called Yu Mr. Dagger Xing, handed the incense to Li Miao and left.
