"Yi" said: "Kang has regrets". The meaning of the word "Kang" means that he only knows how to advance in officialdom, but does not know how to retire; he only knows how to survive, but does not know how to die.
I am afraid that only a saint can understand the principles of advance and retreat and survive without losing track of the right path!
"The Biography" says: If you are content, you will not be humiliated; if you know how to stop, you will not be in danger.
According to this, if you don’t know how to advance or retreat, if you don’t understand the principle of knowing where to stop and be content, you will be humiliated, embarrassed, and in a dangerous situation, and you will soon be in a dangerous situation.
The advancement of the ancients was to help people govern the world, and the retreat of the ancients was to promote the right path and encourage folk customs.
However, people's advancement in officialdom is glorious and easy, so it is the goal that ignorant people strive to pursue; people's retirement requires adhering to integrity and persisting in hardships and dangers, so it is something that mediocre people are afraid of.
Although it is common for people to see and hear cases of people who seek to advance in officialdom encounter disaster or defeat, people who live in seclusion are rarely seen in previous history books.
Moji retired from the emperor after his success, and was lying in his sick home, practicing the method of immortality. This is better than wandering around after he succeeded in Luanqi and Jianlong.
Later, Zheng Guangde, Shuguang, Shushou and others retired according to the court's etiquette and left their jobs to live in their homes, which is also worthy of praise.
Yu Kun's "Wei Lue Zhizuo Zhuan" compared Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu. In fact, their principles of conduct were originally different.
Xie Lingyun's "Jin Shu Zhizu Zhuan" first comments on those Jin Dynasty literati who escaped from the turmoil. They probably did not belong to the Zhizu type of people; only Ruan Sikuang liked to escape from the world, abandoning glory and wealth, which was considered to be far away from the embarrassing and dangerous situation of humiliation. "Song Book."
In "The Legend of Zhizu" there are biographies of Cha Ao and Wang Miao, both of whom are similar characters to the previous ones.
During the Revolution, Zhou Suyou, also named Wangbi, refused to be an official, insisted on integrity, traveled in the mountains and forests, cultivated his ambition, did not feel sad and sorrowful in poverty, and did not pursue wealth and glory greedily. He was a noble person among Confucian scholars.
After Liang took over the world, the way of villains declined, and wise men and officials invited each other to gather in the court to measure their own strength and stick to their ambitions of retirement. Those who have not been heard of in the contemporary era. Occasionally, some people retired due to old age, and some had little ambition and weak desires. The history of the country recorded the deeds of these people and compiled it into the "Zhizu Zhuan".
Gu Xian's courtesy name was Shisi, and he was a native of Wu County, Wu County.
His grandfather Gu Qianzhi was the general of the town army and the governor of Xiangzhou during the Song Dynasty.
Before he reached the age of twenty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed by the state as a councilor, promoted scholars, and accumulated merits and was promoted to Prince Sheren, Shangshu Bibu Lang, and Fujun Chief.
During the Yuan Dynasty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed as the Jiankang Order.
At that time, someone was stealing cattle, and the stolen cattle were recognized by the owner of the cattle. The person who stole the cattle also said that the cattle were his own. The verbal evidence on both sides was similar. No one of the previous county magistrates could decide this case.
After Gu Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case materials and then said to both parties: "No need to say more, I have thought of a solution."
So Gu Xianzhi ordered his people to untie the rope from which the cow was tied and let the cow go wherever it wanted. The cow went straight back to its original owner's house, and the thief confessed his crime.
Gu Saizhu exposed the evildoers hidden in the dark. He was so smart and decisive in many such things that people at the time called him a god.
As for dealing with the private requests of dignitaries and dignitaries in the imperial court, he never flattered or obeyed. He never tolerated the corruption and cruelty of his officials, and he judged them all fairly and in accordance with the law.
Gu Xianzhi was honest and frugal by nature, and worked hard to handle political affairs, so he won the hearts of the people. Therefore, drinkers in the capital got mellow and delicious wine, and often called the wine "Gu Jiankang". This means that Gu Xian's purity, purity, harmony and beauty are like good wine.
Gu Xianzhi moved to the post of chariot and cavalry meritorious officer, and was a friend of King Xi of Jin Dynasty.
Emperor Qi Gao took charge of the imperial court and ordered Gu Xianzhi to join the army as a hussar and green officer, and to move to the post of Taiwei Xicao.
After the establishment of the Qi Wangtai Mansion, Gu Xianzhi was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu.
When Emperor Gao of Qi ascended the throne, Gu Xianzhi was dismissed and appointed as the internal history of Hengyang.
Before Gu Xianzhi took office, there had been plagues in Hengyang for several years, and more than half of the people died of the disease. The price of coffins was extremely expensive, so the people all wrapped the dead in reeds and dumped them on the roadside.
As soon as Gu Xianzhi took office, he notified the counties under his jurisdiction to find the relatives of the dead and ordered them to bury the dead.
For those dead people who had no relatives, Gu Xianzhi took out his salary and ordered the chief clerk of the government to organize the burial.
According to the local folk custom in Hengyang, when people in the mountains are sick, they often say that the disaster was caused by their ancestors, so they dig graves, open coffins, and wash the bones of the dead with water. This is called "removing evil spirits".
Gu Xianzhi used principles to educate the people, explaining to them the difference between the living and the dead, and pointed out that diseases were not caused by the dead, and the local customs were therefore changed.
At that time, the governor Wang Huan had just taken office, and there was only one county in Hengyang where no one came to the governor's office to complain. So Wang Huan sighed and said: Gu Hengyang's education has reached a very good level.
Suppose all nine counties of this state are like this. So what else is wrong with me?
Gu Xianzhi returned to Beijing and served as Taiwei and Zhonglang.
He also left the capital and served as the chief historian of Shuzhong and engaged in the affairs of Kuaiji County.
Lu Wendu, a native of Shanyin, was favored by Emperor Wu of Qi, so he built a mansion in Yuyao and acted freely and unscrupulously in the area.
When Gu Xianzhi took office in Kuaiji County, he immediately went to court to demolish Lu Wendu's mansion.
Lu Wendu later went back to his hometown to bury his mother. Officials from counties and counties rushed to express their condolences, but Gu Xianzhi refused to associate with him.
Lu Wendu deeply hated Gu Xianzhi in his heart, but in the end he could not slander Gu Xianzhi.
Gu Xianzhi moved to Nanzhonglang and was appointed as the chief historian of Baling King. He also added General Wei to conduct affairs in southern Henan and southern Yanzhou.
At that time, King Situ Jingling established a military camp at the junction of Xuancheng, Lincheng and Dingling counties, demarcating Baili Mountain and marsh, and prohibiting people from entering to collect firewood. Gu Xianzhi resolutely stated that this could not be done, and his words were sincere and straightforward.
King Jingling answered him: If it weren't for you, I wouldn't be able to hear such sincere and kind words.
King Jingling immediately ordered the lifting of the ban.
Gu Xianzhi was moved to serve as the Minister of Huangmen and the doctor of the Ministry of Officials.
When he was still in the Song Dynasty, Gu Xianzhi's grandfather Gu Jianzhi served as the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs. When he was in office, he planted a row of orange trees in the courtyard of the government and said to people: I planted this tree for Xian.
By this time, Gu Xianzhi was indeed serving in the Ministry of Personnel.
Gu Xianzhi went to Beijing again to serve as the chief historian of the conquest, and went to Yanzhou in the south.
He left his job to mourn his mother's death. After the mourning period was over, during the Jianwu period, he was appointed as the minister of Huangmen and the captain of the infantry school. Before he could receive the ceremony, he was moved to the position of the prince's concubine and led the Zhongzheng of Wu Yi.
He left the capital and was appointed as General Ningshuo and Internal Secretary of Linchuan. Before he could take up his post, he was awarded the title of General of Auxiliary State and Prefect of Jinling.
Soon, Gu Xianzhi fell ill, and Chen Zuo fell ill, so he was dismissed and returned to his hometown.
In the early years of Yongyuan, Gu Xianzhi was recruited as a court official. He did not accept the post and was appointed as the internal history of Yuzhang.
There was a chaste woman named Wan Xi in Yuzhang. She lost her husband when she was young and became a widow with no children. She served her parents-in-law with great filial piety. However, her parents wanted to force her to change her ambition and remarry, but she refused to agree to her death. Gu Xianzhi gave Wan Xi five pieces of silk to commend her for her integrity.
In the second year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, the rebel army who attacked Qidong Hunhou pacified Jiankang. Emperor Gaozu was appointed as the shepherd of Yangzhou, and Gu Xianzhi was recruited to serve as a historian.
By the time Gu Xianzhi arrived in the capital, Gaozu had accepted Qi's concession and ascended the throne. Gu Xianzhi's condition gradually became serious due to a stroke, so he firmly requested to return to his hometown of Wuxian.
In the second year of Tianjian, the imperial court sent people to Gu Xian's home to confer him the title of Taizhong doctor.
Although Gu Xianzhi served as county magistrate many times, he did not even have any savings. When he returned to his hometown, his family was destitute, so he was inevitably suffering from hunger and cold.
In the eighth year of Tianjian, Gu Xianzhi died at home at the age of seventy-four.
When he was dying, Gu Xianzhi wrote in advance instructions on the funeral arrangements and warned his son:
From birth to death, Taoism changes like day and night.
Since we don’t know where life comes from, how can we know where we will go after death?
There is a reason why Yanling said that after a person dies, his essence rises and returns to heaven, his flesh and blood returns to the earth, and his soul can go anywhere.
Although this statement is difficult to understand and difficult to verify, it should not be false.
A person's life will pass quickly, like a fleeting moment.
I have written down the instructions for the funeral ceremony in advance. After I retire, I hope you will all follow my instructions and not go against my wishes.
Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming were people who understood life well and were not bothered by worldly affairs; Yang Wangsun and Huangfu Shi'an were people who corrected the world's customs with their own actions.
If I advance, I cannot reach a state where I am not burdened by worldly affairs, and if I retreat, I will not be able to correct the world's customs.
I often say that the funeral rituals formulated by Confucius in Zhongdu are not only in line with natural principles, but also satisfy people's feelings of missing and respecting their relatives.
After death, clothes can wrap around the body to show that it does not violate etiquette; the coffin can hold the clothes of the corpse, enough to cover the stench.
Nothing else is needed to put in the coffin.
When buried, the coffin is transported in an oval cart and covered with coarse cloth so as not to offend people.
Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty was a noble emperor, and he also proposed that only a glass of water, dried meat, and food should be used as a memorial. Fan Shiwen, a well-known and ethical scholar, also left a message that only cold water and dry rice could be used as a memorial.
What's more, I'm just a humble and mediocre person, how can I not control my desires?
Rather than having thoughtful etiquette in funerals, I would rather feel sad in my heart, which is the deep feeling of missing my loved ones; rather than being extravagant and extravagant in etiquette, I would rather be simple and frugal, in order to suit my heart.
There is no need to hold a permanent memorial feast in front of the spirit. You can just light an oil lamp so that the mourners have something to rely on.
On the first and fifteenth day of the lunar month, the commemorative days of Daxiang and Xiaoxiang, or the anniversary of death, you can temporarily set up a small couch with a few tables and seats. You only need to buy a few vegetarian items, and do not use cattle, sheep, or pigs as memorials.
The sacrifice of smoke and taste to ancestors cannot be abandoned no matter how high or low they are.
It is difficult to prepare complete ritual utensils, which often leads to negligence.
The rituals for worshiping ancestors were previously stipulated and cannot be omitted.
Starting from me, only vegetables and fresh fruits will be used for sacrifices after death, not the same as those for ancestors of previous generations.
Just teach your children and grandchildren clearly not to forget your parents and relatives throughout the year.
Confucius said: Even if you use vegetable soup and vegetable food to offer sacrifices, you must do so respectfully, as if you are fasting.
The most important thing is sincerity and respect. What does it mean that the etiquette utensils must be complete? Gu Xianzhi wrote dozens of poems, poems, inscriptions, praises and "Hengyang County Records".
Tao Jizhi was born in Moling, Danyang.
His grandfather Tao Minzu was the governor of Guangzhou during the Song Dynasty.
His father, Tao Jingren, served as a doctor in Zhongsan.
Tao Jizhi was very intelligent when he was young. Tao Minzu liked him very much and thought he had an unusual temperament.
Tao Minzu once placed four envelopes of silver in front of him and ordered his grandchildren to take them. Tao Jizhi was just four years old at that time, and he was the only one who did not take money.
When asked about the reason why he did not take money, Tao Jizhi said: If my grandfather has a reward, it should be given to his father and uncles first, and should not be given directly to his grandchildren, so I do not take money.
When Tao Minzu heard this, he was even more surprised by his temperament and intelligence.
Tao Jizhi's mother died when he was five years old. He was as sad as an adult.
At first, when his mother was still sick, he was ordered to become a monk. After his mother died, his family redeemed him. Tao Jizhi hugged his mother's body and cried in mourning. Everyone who heard it was moved by sadness.
After growing up, Tao Jizhi loved learning and had little desire to pursue glory, fame and fortune.
When he first became an official, he was appointed as the Minister of the Guiyang Kingdom. He went west to join the army in Beizhonglang Town, but he did not take up the post. At that time, people called him "Bei Jun".
Tao Jizhi was in mourning because of his father's death. After the mourning period expired, Liu Bing, the Shangshu of Danyang Yin, promoted Tao Jizhi to the post of chief of the rear army and the county's meritorious officer.
Tao Jizhi went to Beijing again to serve as Wang Cai Ling, but was soon dismissed due to illness.
At that time, Liu Bing and Yuan Can plotted to overthrow Emperor Qi Gao because Emperor Qi Gao was becoming increasingly powerful.
Liu Bing had always respected Tao Jizhi, and he wanted to ask Tao Jizhi to study strategies to deal with Emperor Qi Gao. Tao Jizhi believed that both Yuan and Liu were Confucian scholars, and their conspiracy would definitely lead to their destruction, so he resolutely refused to keep the appointment.
Soon Liu Bing and others were executed for their crimes.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, Tao Jizhi was appointed as Shangshu Bibulang. At that time, Chu Yuan was appointed as Shangshu Ling. He had always been on good terms with Tao Jizhi, so he successively ordered Tao Jizhi to serve as Sikong and Situ chief clerk, and left the affairs of the mansion to Tao Jizhi.
After Chu Yuan passed away, Wang Jian, the minister of state, thought that Chu Yuan had noble virtues and wanted to confirm that Chu Yuan's title was Wen Xiaogong. Tao Jizhi made a request and said: "Wen Xiao" is the nickname of Sima Daozi. I am afraid that he is not perfect. Chu Yuan should not use the same nickname as him. It is better to give Mi as "Wen Jian".
Wang Jian followed Tao Jizhi's advice.
Tao Jizhi also asked Wang Jian to erect a monument for Chu Yuan. After the stele was erected, Tao Jizhi protected the stele well from beginning to end and maintained the ethics of an official. People at that time praised Tao Jizhi for this kind of virtue.
Tao Ji moved directly to the Taiwei Ji office and joined the army.
He also came to Beijing to serve as Champion Sima and Dongguan Prefect. During his tenure, Dongguan County was known as peaceful and stable.
Tao Jizhi returned to Beijing and was appointed as the minister of Sanqi, leading the left guard Sima, and was transferred to Zhenxi to consult and join the army.
Emperor Wu of Qi died, and Emperor Ming of Qi became prime minister. He punished dissenters, but Tao Jizhi refused to flatter him. Emperor Ming of Qi was very afraid of him, so he asked him to leave the capital and serve as the chief minister of the auxiliary state and the prefect of Beihai.
The subordinate officials of the DPRK held posts in border towns, and it was rare for scholars to be appointed as officials.
Someone advised Tao Ji to come to Emperor Qi Ming to apologize. After Emperor Ming of Qi met with Tao Jizhi, he left him in the capital and appointed him as a hussar to consult with the army and to serve as minister Zuo Cheng.
Then he was moved to the post of governor of Jian'an. Tao Jizhi advocated tranquility in his administration, and the people felt comfortable.
Tao Jizhi returned to Beijing and served as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and then moved to the post of guerrilla general and court lieutenant.
When Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, Tao Jizhi moved to serve as the Minister of Huangmen.
Tao Jizhi often said that when an official reached a position with a salary of two thousand dan, all his life's wishes were fulfilled. He no longer pursued glory and wealth in the world, so he resigned and returned to his hometown on the grounds of illness.
In the early years of Tianjian, the imperial court sent people to his home to confer him the title of Taizhong doctor.
Emperor Gaozu said: Liang ruled the world, but he could not see this person.
In the tenth year of Tianjian, Tao Jizhi died at home at the age of seventy-five.
Tao Jizhi had always lived a poor life, no one could compare with him, and he had been living in seclusion for more than ten years. When he died, his family was destitute and his descendants had no money to bury him. Everyone who heard about the incident felt sad for his integrity. Xiao Wangsu was born in Lanling.
His grandfather Xiao Sihua was posthumously awarded the title of General Zhengxi and Kaifu Yitong Sansi in the Song Dynasty. His father, Xiao Huiming, served as the prefect of Wuxing. His grandfather and father both had great reputations.
Xiao Wangsu lost his father very early and his family was poor. He was adopted by his uncle Xiao Huixiu.
When he first became an official, he served as Situ Fa of Qi, Cao Xing joined the army, and moved to Zuo Lang, Prince Sheren, and Shangshu Sangong Lang.
In the last years of Yongyuan, Xiao Shisu was appointed as the prince to wash horses.
Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, and Emperor Gaozu selected him as a lieutenant in the Hussar Records Office to join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xiao Shisu was appointed as Wangyou of Linchuan, and then as Prince Zhongsheren, Danyang Yincheng.
When he was first appointed to the official position, Emperor Gaozu gave Xiao Wangsu 80,000 yuan, and Xiao Wangsu gave all the money to his relatives and friends at once.
Xiao Wangsu moved to Situ Zuoxi and governed the center of Xuzhou in the south.
Xiao Shisu had a quiet and humble temperament, a pure heart, and a fondness for learning. He could talk about the mysteries of Lao and Zhuang, and he never talked about wealth and wealth, and his joy and anger were indistinguishable.
Regardless of whether he was living without an official or holding an official position, he acted according to his own temperament, was open-minded and frank, never arrogant, and showed his simple and simple nature. Scholars therefore respected him.
When he took office in Jingkou, he came up with the idea of ​​settling down in Jingkou for the rest of his life, so he built a house in Sheshan.
At this time, the imperial court recruited him as the minister of Zhongshu, so he refused to be an official and took up the post. He returned to his residence in Sheshan and lived alone without being concerned about worldly affairs. If he was not a relative, he would not be able to reach the gate of his residence.
Xiao Wangsu's wife was the daughter of Taiwei Wang Jian. Xiao Wangsu had separated from her a long time ago and had no children.
In the eighth year of Tianjian, Xiao Shisu passed away.
His relatives and friends inspected his deeds and conferred upon him the title of Mr. Zhenwen.
Shi Chen said: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi were people who retired to prolong their lives, but Xiao Shisu lacked enthusiasm for being an official. Compared with those who miss their salary, indulge in favors, and work hard in the world, there is indeed a big difference.

Xiao Zong, the king of Yuzhang, whose courtesy name was Shiqian, was the second son of Emperor Gaozu.
In the third year of Tianjian's reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Yuzhang County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
In the fifth year of Tianjian, he left the capital as envoy Chijie, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in South Xuzhou, general Renwei, and governor of South Xuzhou. Soon he was promoted to the title of Beizhonglang General.
In the tenth year of Tianjian's reign, he was transferred to the governorship of Yingsi, Huo Sanzhou Zhujun, General Yunhui, and Yingzhou governor.
In the 13th year of Tianjian, he was promoted to General Anyou and led the stone garrison army.
In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, he was moved to the post of General Xizhonglang and General of the Guard Army, and then moved to General Anqian and Danyang Yin.
In the 16th year of Tianjian's reign, he was appointed as Beizhong Langjiang and South Xuzhou Governor.
In the second year of ordinary life, he entered the court as Shizhong and Zhenyou General, and his subordinates began to set up assistant historians.

When Xiao Zong was in Xuzhou, his decrees and punishments were very cruel.
Xiao Zong was strong and could subdue a galloping horse with his bare hands.
He often went out at night wearing casual clothes to conceal his identity, and was unrestrained.
Whenever Emperor Gaozu's appointment came, he would always show resentment, and no one among the ministers would dare to advise him.
Xiao Zong built the Qi family's seven temples in a special house and often went to worship. He also wore casual clothes to kneel down at the mausoleum of Emperor Ming in Qu'aqi.

Xiao Zong secretly dug up Qi Shuhunhou's grave, took out the bones, and dripped blood from his own arm on the bones for testing. At first, when Xiao Zong was frustrated, he wrote "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves" to express his thoughts and feelings.

Listen to the sound of the bell, listen to the sound of the bell in not one place.

Former friends and loved ones now have their own things and can no longer be together like fallen leaves.

Lamenting the fallen leaves, the leaves fall continuously, layer upon layer.
The leaves fall and fly, sometimes flying horizontally and never to return.
Lamenting the fallen leaves, how sad are the fallen leaves? Life is like the fallen leaves, falling and withering cannot last forever.
Lamenting the fallen leaves, when will the fallen leaves return?
They were all born from the same foundation in the past, but now they are no longer related to each other.
No one who read his poems at that time did not feel sad.
King Lan Ji of Wuling, courtesy name Shixun, was the eighth son of Emperor Gaozu.
He has been diligent and studious since he was a child, and is very talented in literature. He does not like to be frivolous and extravagant when writing articles, but pays attention to profound and touching things.

He successively served as General Ningyuan, Grand Administrator of Langye and Pengyuan County, General Qingche, and Danyang Yin.

Later he left Beijing and served as general Xuanhui and governor of Jiangzhou.

In the eleventh year of Datong, the imperial court awarded him the titles of Changshi of Sanqi, General of the Expedition to the West, and the third division of Kaifu Yitong.
In the past, during the Tianjian period, lightning struck the Sun Gate, and the traces of the lightning strike formed the character "Shaozong Liang Weiwang". The interpreter believed that King Wu referred to King Wuling, so people inside and outside the court turned to him.
During the Taiqian period, Hou Jing rebelled and did not send troops to reinforce the capital.

He also told people close to him: In the past, when Huanxuan was a great tycoon, knowledgeable people said it was February, and Huanxuan's defeat was indeed in February.
This year King Wuling named his reign Tianzheng, and the correct character is Yi Zhi. Can he last long?
In the summer and April of the fifth year of the Taiqing Dynasty, Xiao Ji led his army down the river to Bajun, in the name of attacking Hou Jing, and planned to capture Jingshan and Shaanxi.
Xiao Ji heard that the Western Wei Dynasty had invaded Shu, so he sent his general Qiao Yan, the governor of Nanliang Province, to lead his army back to Shu for reinforcements.

Lu Fahe was in emergency several times within ten days.
Shizu then promoted Ren Yue, who was in prison, to be King Sima of Jin'an, withdrew his own soldiers to lead him, and sent General Xuanmeng Liu Fen and Ren Yue to the west to reinforce Lu Fahe.

Shizu wrote to Xiao Jishao: The emperor paid tribute to the fake yellow cymbal Taiwei King Wuling: Since Jiuli invaded and attacked, and Sanmiao plundered and harassed, the world has been suffering from death and disaster for many years.

Xiao Ji disobeyed Shidan's edict and only responded to Shizu's letter according to family etiquette.
On Gengshen Day, Lu Qi's general Chi led his troops along the mountain to plan an attack. Yu Mian and Xie Da Ren fought with him and defeated Mi.

In the summer of June, the weather is extremely hot, gold and stone are melting, mosquitoes gather, the sound is like thunder, and foxes come and go thousands of miles to harm people. With your noble body, you march hard and line up. I care about you very much. How can you bear such hard work?

The friendship between brothers is separated in body but connected in breath.

King Xiao Zhengde of Linhe, also known as Gonghe, was the third son of King Jinghui of Linchuan.
When he was young, he was rough, evil, and disrespectful of etiquette.
At first, when Gaozu had no sons, he adopted him as his son. When Gaozu ascended the throne, Xiao Zhengde hoped to make himself the prince. Later, Gaozu established Prince Zhaoming and named Xiao Zhengde the Marquis of Xifeng, with a settlement of 500 households.

In ordinary six years, he appointed Huangmen Shilang as Qingche General and appointed an assistant historian.
Soon, he fled to Wei, and a minister asked Gaozu to remove the officials he had granted.
In ordinary seven years, Xiao Zhengde escaped from Wei again. Emperor Gaozu did not blame him, restored his title, and then appointed him as the general to conquer the captives.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, Xiao Zhengde was appointed General Xinwu and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
Later, the imperial court recruited him as a servant, a general of the Fu army, and appointed him as an assistant historian. He was also named the king of Linhe County, with a settlement of 2,000 households, and he was also made a general of the left guard.
But he became increasingly violent and recruited desperadoes.
Hou Jing knew that he had a treacherous plot, so he secretly sent people to seduce and lobby him, and they had close contacts with him and colluded with each other.
Hou Jing sent a letter to Xiao Zhengde saying: Now that the emperor is old, the treacherous ministers are disrupting the country, the rules and regulations are disordered, and the political orders are reversed, in my opinion, Gaozu will definitely be defeated.
Besides, you were supposed to be crown prince, but you were abandoned in the middle. All the righteous people in the world are very sad in private. Although I, Hou Jing, are foolish and loyal, I can't help feeling resentful about this.

I hope you will obey the wishes of the people of the world and understand my sincerity. Xiao Zhengde was very happy after reading Hou Jing's letter and said: Hou Jing's meaning coincides with mine. This is God's support for me.

When Hou Jing arrived at the river, Xiao Zhengde secretly brought an empty boat, pretending to load it with reeds, but actually using it to carry Hou Jing across the river.
The imperial court did not know Xiao Zhengde's conspiracy and sent him to guard Zhuquehang.
When Hou Jing arrived at Zhuquehang, Xiao Zhengde led his army to attack the capital together with Hou Jing. Hou Jing supported Xiao Zhengde as emperor, changed the year to the first year of Zhengping, and Hou Jing became prime minister.
After the capture of Taicheng, Hou Jing restored the Taiqing era title and demoted Xiao Zhengde to Grand Sima.
Xiao Zhengde had a complaint. When Hou Jing found out about it, he was worried that he would rebel, so he falsely conveyed the imperial edict and killed him.
The great-grandson of Xiao Yu, King of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming.
In ordinary two years, he was named the Duke of Zhijiang County.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Gaozu changed his title to the king of Hedong County, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
And appointed him as General Ningyuan and Shitou garrison.
Later, he was transferred out of the capital to serve as the prefect of Langxie and Pengcheng counties.
Later, he was transferred back to the capital and served as Shizhong and Qingche General, and was appointed as an assistant historian.
Later, he was transferred to Nanzhong Langjiang and Xiangzhou Governor.
Soon, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xiao Yu led the army to come for reinforcements. When the army arrived at Qingcao Lake, Taicheng had fallen. An order was issued to withdraw the troops and turn back. Luo Yu led the army back to Xiangzhou to defend it.
At that time, Shizu led his army and was stationed there. Zhang Zuan, the newly appointed governor of Yongzhou, reported secretly to Shizu: "Kou Yu is recruiting troops to start a rebellion in Hedong and gathering food and grass in Yueyang. These are all illegal things. They plan to attack Jiangling."
Shidan was very frightened after hearing this, so he walked back to Jiangling by a small road, and sent Zhou Hong to consult with Xiao Yu's naxiang to supervise Xiao Yu's grain and army.
Xiao Yu said: We are all governors, why do we suddenly want to be subordinate to others?
Shizu sent people there three times, but Xiao Yu refused to obey Shizu.
Shi Dan was furious and sent his son Lu Chabi to conquer him, but his friends were defeated and killed by Lu Yu.
Shizu also ordered Bao Quan, the governor of Xinzhou, to attack Xiao Yu, and wrote a letter to Chen, pointing out the blessings and misfortunes, and allowing him to change his ways and do good.
Xiao Yu did not reply, so he strengthened the city wall and deepened the moat in order to resist defense. Xiao Yu said to Bao Quan: What qualifications does a defeated general have to talk about bravery?
If you want to hit, just hit forward, no need to say anything.
Bao Quan's army was stationed at Shiceng Temple. Xiao Yu led all the troops to attack him. Xiao Yu failed to capture Bao Quan's military camp and retreated.
Bao Quan marched to Juzhou again, and Xiao Yu sent out all his elite troops to attack him, but failed to win.
When he was dispatched, it was sunset and the soldiers were exhausted. Bao Quan took the opportunity to attack and defeated Xiao Yu. He beheaded three thousand people and drowned more than ten thousand people in the water.
Xiao Yu therefore burned the outer city of Changsha and drove the residents into the city. Bao Quan mobilized troops to surround Changsha City.
Xiao Yu was brave and courageous when he was young. He was able to appease the soldiers and was very popular among the soldiers.
After being besieged for a long time, although the inside and outside were cut off, the defense was still very strong.
Later, Shizu sent the leading general Wang Tanluan to attack Ludeng instead of Baose. Wang only avoided building earth mountains and stayed close to the city. He attacked hard day and night. Arrows and stones were like rain, and more than half of the soldiers in the city were killed or injured.
Xiao Yu was very embarrassed and anxious, so he secretly equipped a large ship and prepared to break out.
Just as Xiao Yu's general Murong Hua was leading Wang Shidao into the city, Lu Deng looked around and saw that all the people close to him were scattered, so he was captured.
Xiao Yu said to his guard: "Don't kill me. I want to meet Shizu. I want to rebuke this thief who slandered others. I will die without regret."
The person in charge of guarding him said: I was ordered not to allow it.
So he beheaded him and sent his head to Jingzhen. Shizu sent his head back and buried him.
At first, when Xiao Yu was about to fail, he secretly looked at his face in the mirror, but his head was not visible. He also saw a tall man lying on the house, with his hands on the ground looking down at his navel. He also saw a white dog as big as a donkey, running out of the city and gone somewhere.
Xiao Yu hated this phenomenon, and soon the city was captured.
Shi Chen said: Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde were both rebellious and wanted to do as they pleased, so it was right for them to bring about their own destruction.
During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled and invaded the capital. Xiao Ji took advantage of the rich resources of Yong and Shu, but did not lead his army to rescue the court in danger, which showed his integrity. When the rebel Hou Jing was killed, he began to raise troops, and his troops were unknown, which caused a disaster.
Alas!
He was punished like Guan Shu and Cai Shu, the ministers who caused chaos in the Western Zhou Dynasty. The disaster was brought about by himself.
summary:
Xiao Zong, Prince of Yuzhang, was Emperor Gaozu's second son. He held various military and civil posts, including governor of South Xuzhou and Yingzhou. His mother, Wu Shuyuan, was a former concubine of the Marquis of Shuhun of Qi, and Xiao Zong was born seven months after Gaozu married her, leading to suspicions he was not Gaozu's biological son. Xiao Zong grew up talented but resentful, believing Gaozu did not understand him. He performed a blood-dripping test on the bones of the Marquis of Shuhun and his own son, confirming his paternity, which fueled his rebellious intentions. He eventually surrendered to Wei, changed his name to Xiao Zuan in memory of the deposed Emperor Shuhun, and was killed by Wei at age 49. His poems, "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves," expressed his sorrow and frustration.

Xiao Ji, King of Wuling, was Gaozu's eighth son. He was diligent and talented in literature. He held several official positions, including governor of Jiangzhou and Yangzhou. During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled, and Xiao Ji did not send troops to reinforce the capital. After Gaozu's death, he proclaimed himself emperor in Shu with the reign name Tianzheng. He killed advisors who warned him, and his rule was marked by omens, such as flowers growing from palace pillars. He led an army downriver to attack Hou Jing but was defeated by Western Wei forces. He was captured and killed at age 46. His reign name Tianzheng was considered unlucky, and he was posthumously given the surname Taotie.

Xiao Zhengde, Prince of Linhe, was the third son of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan. He was adopted by Gaozu but became dissatisfied when he was not made crown prince. He fled to Wei but later returned. He conspired with Hou Jing, who supported him as emperor with the reign name Zhengping. After Hou Jing captured Taicheng, he demoted Xiao Zhengde and later killed him out of fear of rebellion.

Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming. He held various posts, including governor of Xiangzhou. When Hou Jing invaded the capital, Xiao Yu led reinforcements but arrived after Taicheng fell. He returned to Xiangzhou to defend it. Shizu, suspicious of Xiao Yu's intentions, sent forces to attack him. Xiao Yu was besieged in Changsha for a long time but eventually captured and beheaded. Before his fall, he experienced ominous visions, including his head disappearing in a mirror and a large white dog fleeing the city.

The historical commentary concludes that Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde's rebellions led to their own destruction, while Xiao Ji's failure to aid the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion and his subsequent uprising brought disaster upon himself.

Hou Jing, whose courtesy name was Wanjing, was from Shuofang. Some people say he was from Yanmen.
When he was young, he behaved wildly and his fellow villagers were afraid of him.
When he reached adulthood, he was vigorous and strong, and was good at horseback riding and archery.
Therefore, he was selected as a garrison in Beizhen and gradually made meritorious service in the army.
In the first year of Wei Xiaochang, Xianyu Xiuli, a soldier from Huaishuo town, rebelled in Dingzhou and captured the county. At the same time, Tujin Luozhou, a soldier from Rouxuan town, led his party to invade Youzhou and Jizhou. They joined forces with Xianyu Xiuli, totaling more than 100,000 people.
Later, Xianyu Xiuli was killed by Yuan Hongye, and his men were scattered. Ge Rong, the general of Huaishuo Town, took the opportunity to gather Xianyu Xiuli's scattered soldiers, attacked and killed Tujinluozhou, and annexed all Tujinluozhou's troops. People called him "Ge Thief".
In the fourth year of Xiaochang, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu came to rule. Tianzhu General Er Zhurong raised troops from Jinyang and entered Luoyang, killing Empress Hu and Hu's relatives.
Hou Jing initially brought his army to see Er Zhurong. Er Zhurong thought that Hou Jing had a genius and immediately appointed him as a general to lead the troops.
When they were dispatched, Ge Rong's bandits marched south to Luoyang. Er Zhurong went to conquer it in person. He ordered Hou Jing to be the vanguard and led his army to Hanoi to attack Ge Rong. He defeated Jiang's army and captured Ge Rong alive. Because of his great achievements, Hou Jing was promoted to the governor of Dingzhou, Daxingtai, and was granted the title of Duke of Puyang.
Hou Jing became famous from then on.
Soon, Emperor Shenwu of Qi became the prime minister of Wei. He led his army into Luoyang and killed the Zhu family. Hou Jing led his army to surrender to Gao Huan and was appointed by Emperor Shenwu.
Hou Jing was cruel and tyrannical, and controlled the army strictly. However, all the treasures he plundered from the enemy were distributed to the soldiers, so the soldiers were happy to serve him and often won battles.
General Hou Jing holds military power, which is equal to that of Emperor Shenwu.
Wei appointed him as Situ and Nandaoxingtai, with an army of 100,000, and he controlled Henan alone.
Later, Emperor Shenwu fell ill. When he was seriously ill, he said to his son Gao Cheng: Hou Jing is cunning, scheming, and capricious. It is difficult to understand and control him. He will definitely not want to be used by you after I die.
So he wrote a letter to summon Hou Jing to come.
Hou Jing knew that he wanted to get rid of himself and was afraid of disaster, so in the first year of Taiqing, he sent his Xingtai doctor Ding He to ask Gaozu for surrender. The surrender letter said:
I heard that if the important ministers of the country unite and cooperate like human limbs, the country will be unified and peaceful; if the top and bottom are jealous and have different intentions, the country will fall apart.
Therefore, his auxiliary ministers Zhou and Shao were of the same mind and had the same virtue, and the kingdoms of Yue Chang also came to pay tribute; while his ministers Fei and E were disloyal, and as a result all the princes betrayed him.
Creation is the reason for success and failure, which is the same truth from ancient times to modern times.
I used to fight side by side with the Prime Minister of Wei, King Gao, and we worked together to quell chaos, rescue people in danger, support the young master, assist in government affairs, and govern the country.
After the Zhongxing Year, there was not a single battle that I did not take part in. From the Tianping Year to the present, whenever there is a war, I am always the first to fight.
Every time we siege a city, we must capture it, and every time we fight in the field, we must annihilate the enemy. All my energy was spent on fighting and all my loyalty was exhausted.
Because of a good opportunity, my official rank was promoted to the position of Third Duke. I should swear to the death and repay the kindness of the court. Even if I am asked to die, I will not have second thoughts.
But why are we talking about surrender now?

Emperor Gaozu completely agreed with Zhu Yi's words and believed in his previous dream, so he decided to accept Hou Jing.
When Marquis Zhenyang's army was destroyed, the border towns were in fear and panic. Emperor Gaozu was already very worried about this, but he said: Now that we have reached the point of being sent away, do we have to give up the country like the Jin Dynasty?
Previously, Danyang Tao Hongjing lived in seclusion in Huayang Mountain. He was very knowledgeable and knowledgeable. He once wrote a poem and said: The Yifu was willful and unrestrained. He sat in Mangtan and talked about fantasy Buddhism. Unexpectedly, Zhaoyang Palace turned into the Shanyu Palace of the Xiongnu.
In the last years of Datong, scholars competed to talk about mystical principles and did not study military affairs. Now Hou Jing has indeed entered Zhaoyang Palace.
During the Tianjian period, there was a Shi Zhizhi that said: A dog with a tail dug suddenly went crazy, biting people when they were still alive, and then killed itself, fell from the white wall, and died in three embraces.
He also said: The boy from the Shan family stretched out his clothes, raised his arms, and turned into a tiger in front of the Tai Chi Hall, staring eagerly.
The tail-hunting dog and the mountain boy are both shaped like monkeys.
In this way, Hou Jing destroyed and captured Kyoto and poisoned the royal family.
During the Datong period, the imperial physician ordered Zhu Dan to stay in the forbidden province. Not long after, he dreamed that a dog and a sheep were sitting on the emperor's throne. When he woke up, he was disgusted by this. He told others: Dogs and sheep are not good things. They occupy the emperor's throne. Will there be chaos in the country?
Afterwards, it turned out that the emperor suffered a disaster, and Hou Jing ascended the main hall.
When Hou Jing was about to be defeated, there was a monk named Seng Tong. His temperament was like a madman, and he drank and ate meat just like ordinary people. He had been wandering around the world for decades, and no one knew his name and place of origin.
What he said had obscure meanings that could only be verified after a long time. People called him Tianli, and Hou Jing believed and respected him very much.
Hou Jing once shot arrows with his followers in the back hall. At that time, Seng Tong was also there. He took Hou Jing's bow and shot an arrow at Jing Yacan, shouting "I'm a slave."
Wu Jing later held a banquet to gather with his followers, and summoned Seng Tong to the banquet. Seng Tong took the meat, rubbed it with salt, gave it to Hou Jing, and asked: "Is it okay?"
Hou Jing replied: It's just too salty.
Sengtong said: If the meat is not salted, it will stink.
Sure enough, Hou Jing's body was sealed with salt.
Wang Wei, a native of Chen Liu, was very talented and learned when he was young. Hou Jing's tables, letters, letters, and messages were all drafted and produced by Wang Wei.
After Hou Jing succeeded, he planned to usurp the throne, and it was Wang Wei who made the plans for him.
Later, Wang Wei was imprisoned and sent to Jiangling, where he was cooked in the market. The people who had been poisoned by Wang Wei cut off his flesh and roasted it for eating.
Shi Chen said: The way of heaven will not be peaceful for a long time, nor will the destiny of the country be peaceful for a long time. This is because embarrassment and prosperity have a certain end, and prosperity and decline alternate with each other. This is the reason why the Liang Dynasty suffered misfortune.
A boy like Hou Jing was domineering in his own country, his knowledge could not protect him, and his courage was not outstanding, but Wang Wei became his mastermind and made his evil conspiracy succeed.
He led a group of party members to cross the Yangtze River, and with the help of halberds and powerful crossbows, he captured the capital, brought disaster to the emperor, and caused disaster to all the people in the world. He acted arbitrarily, causing the disaster of usurping and stealing the throne.
Alas!
When the country is about to perish, evil spirits will surely descend.
Although this is a matter of human power, it is also a matter of time.
In the past, Yi Yi caused chaos in the Xia Dynasty, and dog soldiers harmed the Zhou Dynasty. In the Han Dynasty, Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo spread disasters. In the Jin Dynasty, Wang Dun and Huan Xuan caused trouble. The Jie thieves were more cruel than them. How sad!
summary:
Hou Jing, courtesy name Wanjing, was from Shuofang, possibly Yanmen. Wild in youth, he became a strong, skilled horseman and archer, serving as a garrison in Beizhen. During Wei Xiaochang's first year, Xianyu Xiuli rebelled in Dingzhou, joined by Tujin Luozhou, amassing over 100,000 troops. After Xianyu Xiuli was killed, Ge Rong gathered his forces, killed Tujin Luozhou, and became known as "Ge Thief." In the fourth year, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu ruled. Er Zhurong raised troops, killed her, and appointed Hou Jing as a general. Hou Jing served as vanguard against Ge Rong, capturing him alive, earning promotion to governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Puyang.

Hou Jing later surrendered to Gao Huan, becoming Emperor Shenwu of Qi. He was cruel but shared plunder with soldiers, ensuring loyalty. He held military power equal to Emperor Shenwu, controlling Henan with 100,000 troops. When Emperor Shenwu fell ill, he warned his son Gao Cheng of Hou Jing's cunning. Hou Jing, fearing for his life, surrendered to Liang's Emperor Gaozu in Taiqing's first year, citing Gao Cheng's threats. Emperor Gaozu accepted, making Hou Jing King of Henan. Qi's Murong Shaozong besieged Hou Jing, who sought Western Wei aid, forcing a retreat. Hou Jing then occupied Xuanhu and Xiangcheng.

Qi's Emperor Wenxiang wrote to Hou Jing, urging his return with promises of rank and family safety. Hou Jing replied, justifying his actions and rejecting the offer. In December, Hou Jing besieged Qiaocheng, failed, but captured Chengfu. He proposed selecting a Yuan descendant as Wei's lord for a Northern Expedition; Emperor Gaozu agreed. Qi's Murong Shaozong pursued Hou Jing to Woyang, where Hou Jing's army disintegrated due to starvation. He fled to Shouchun with 800 horses, where Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, appointing him shepherd of Yuzhou.

In Shouchun, Hou Jing rebelled, conscripting residents and stopping taxes. He requested brocade for uniforms but received green cloth, which he used. After a defeat, he sought funds from the court, which were granted. In the second year, Emperor Gaozu discussed peace with Wei, alarming Hou Jing, who sent arrogant memorials opposing it. Poyang King Xiao Fan and others reported Hou Jing's rebellion intentions, but official Zhu Yi dismissed them. Hou Jing secretly allied with Linhe King Xiao Zhengde. In August, Hou Jing rebelled, attacking Ma Tou and Muzha. Emperor Gaozu ordered multiple governors to counter him.

In October, Hou Jing feigned an attack on Hefei but took Qiaozhou, capturing Fengcheng Hou Xiaotai. He crossed the Yangtze from Caishi with hundreds of horses and thousands of soldiers, unnoticed. He divided troops to attack Gushu, then reached Cisu. Defenders fled, and Hou Jing advanced to the palace city, burning gates. After failed assaults, he built a barrier, cutting off supplies. He established Xiao Zhengde as emperor in November, naming himself Prime Minister. Hou Jing attacked Dongfu City, capturing it and killing over 2,000 officials. He built earth mountains to monitor the city, forcing labor, with weak killed to fill them.

Reinforcements arrived, but Hou Jing defeated them. Food ran out, leading to cannibalism. Hou Jing sought peace, demanding four Yangtze-right states and hostages. An alliance was made, but Hou Jing broke it, attacking again. The palace city fell; Hou Jing plundered, captured officials, and burned corpses. He falsely issued edicts, demoted Xiao Zhengde, and appointed his own governors. Emperor Gaozu died in May, reportedly from anger after Hou Jing's actions. Hou Jing hid the death for over twenty days before proclaiming the crown prince emperor.

Hou Jing continued campaigns, killing Xiao Zhengde and appointing puppet kings. He faced rebellions, including Zu Hao's in Guangling, which he crushed, killing all residents. In Dabao's first year, he granted himself titles and privileges. He defeated various forces, capturing cities. In October, he killed Wulin Hou Xiao Zhen. He falsely issued an edict, granting himself the title "General of the Universe." Qi's Xin Shu besieged Yangping but retreated. Xu Wensheng defeated Hou Jing's navy, but Hou Jing later captured Yingzhou. He failed to take Baling due to disease and fled after Ren Yue's defeat.

Hou Jing deposed Taizong, imprisoning him, and established Xiao Dong as emperor. He killed Taizong with a silk cloth weighted with earth. In October, he forced Xiao Dong to abdicate, proclaiming himself emperor with the era name Taishi. He changed Liang's regulations to Han's, but his ignorance of ancestry caused ridicule. In the second year, his forces were defeated by Wang Sengbian. Hou Jing fled east with his sons in leather bags. At Hudouzhou, former prince's servant Yang Kun killed him. His body was displayed, and people ate his flesh, burned his bones, and mixed ashes with wine.

Hou Jing was under seven feet tall with handsome features but was cruel, often mutilating victims before death. He wore a white gauze hat and green robe, sometimes with a tooth comb in his bun. He rode a white horse; it neighed before victories and lowered its head before defeats. Emperor Gaozu's dream of中原 prefectures surrendering led him to accept Hou Jing, a decision later regretted. Omens, including a poem by Tao Hongjing and a prophecy about a dog and sheep, foretold Hou Jing's rise. A monk named Seng Tong, whom Hou Jing respected, made cryptic remarks about salt, foreshadowing Hou Jing's body being salted after death. Wang Wei, Hou Jing's adviser, was later cooked in the market. The historian noted that Hou Jing's cruelty surpassed previous usurpers, attributing his rise to divine timing and human folly.

translation:
Prince Zhaoming Xiao Tong, courtesy name Deshi, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu of Liang.
The biological mother is Ding Guibi.
At first, Emperor Wu of Liang had no boys. When Emperor Wu of Liang led an uprising against the Marquis of Donghun, Xiao Tong was born in Xiangyang in September of the first year of Zhongxing in Qi.
After Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, a minister submitted a letter requesting the establishment of a crown prince. Emperor Wu of Liang believed that the world had just stabilized and many systems were lacking and needed to be further improved, so he did not agree to appoint a successor to the throne.
Later, at the firm request of the ministers, in November of the first year of Tianjian, Xiao Tong was made the crown prince by Emperor Wu of Liang.
The prince was young at that time and still lived in the palace. Prince Xiao Tong was born with intelligence and cleverness. He started learning "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius" at the age of three. By the age of five, he had learned all the Five Classics and was able to recite them.
On June 17, the fifth year, he moved out of the palace and moved into the East Palace.
Xiao Tong was kind and filial by nature. Since leaving the palace, he often missed his parents and was always in a depressed mood.
After Emperor Wu of Liang knew about this situation, he asked him to visit the court every five days, and he often stayed in Yongfu Province, sometimes for three days, sometimes for five days, before returning to the East Palace.
In September of the eighth year, Emperor Wu of Liang inspected his son's studies in Shou'an Hall and asked Xiao Tong to explain the "Book of Filial Piety". Xiao Tong's explanation was clear and clear.
After the explanation, he personally went to the Chinese Academy of Sciences to arrange a banquet to pay homage to the most holy teacher.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the 14th year, Emperor Wu of Liang met with his ministers on the platform in front of the palace and held a crowning ceremony for Prince Xiao Tong in the Taiji Palace.
In the past, it was stipulated that the prince should wear a crown of distant travel and a golden tassel of green cicadas; this time the emperor issued an order for the prince to wear a crown of Jinbo Mountain.
Xiao Tong was handsome and well behaved.
When reading, you can count the lines at a glance and be able to remember everything.
Every time there is a grand gathering of ancestral feasts, poems can be composed with dozens of rhymes.
Sometimes Emperor Wu of Liang asked him to compose dramatic rhyme poems, and he could always compose them with a little thought without any modification or modification.
Emperor Wu of Liang vigorously promoted Buddhism and personally explained Buddhist scriptures. Prince Xiao Tong also believed in the Three Jewels of Buddhism: Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and read many Buddhist scriptures.
And the Huiyi Hall was built in the palace as a church to explain Buddhist doctrines. It attracted famous monks and often discussed and studied Buddhist scriptures together.
Xiao Tong himself also created the Two Truths Dharmakaya Sutra, which has his own unique insights.
In April of the first year of the ordinary year, nectar fell on the Huiyi Palace. Everyone thought it was the prince's virtue that moved heaven.
In November of the seventh year, Ding Guibi, the biological mother of Prince Xiao Tong, fell ill. He returned to Yongfu Province and stayed by the hospital bed day and night to observe the condition and did not even take off his clothes when sleeping.
Later, Ding Guifei died after ineffective treatment. Xiao Tong followed the team carrying the body back to the palace on foot. When his mother's body was placed in the coffin, he did not eat a morsel of food or drink a sip of water. He was so sad that he could hardly breathe when he cried.
Emperor Wu of Liang sent Gu Xie, a member of Zhongshushe, to read out the imperial edict and said: During the period of mourning, the filial son's body will be weakened by reducing the amount of food due to sadness, but the filial son should not be allowed to starve to death because of this. This is the etiquette established by the saints.
"Book of Rites" says that due to excessive grief, a filial son becomes too weak or even dies, and cannot complete the three-year mourning mission, which is the same as not showing filial piety. I'm still alive, how could you ruin yourself like this! You should force yourself to eat and drink immediately.
Prince Xiao Tong ate a few hens of rice porridge after receiving the emperor's imperial edict.
From then until Ding Guifei was buried, she only ate one liter of rice porridge every day.
Emperor Wu of Liang issued another edict, saying, "I heard that you eat too little food every day, your body is very weak, and you are about to fall ill. Although I don't have other diseases, it is because of your current condition that I feel depressed and sick."
So you should force yourself to eat some thick porridge and don't let me worry about you all the time. But even though Xiao Tong received imperial edicts many times and no matter what the persuasion, he still insisted on eating only one rice porridge every day and not eating any vegetables, melons and fruits.
Xiao Tong's body has always been very strong. His belt used to be ten girth, but now he has lost more than half of his weight. Every time he entered the court, officials and civilians would burst into tears when they saw how thin he was.
Since the crowning ceremony of Prince Xiao Tong, Emperor Wu of Liang asked him to participate in national affairs. Memorials from various departments inside and outside the court were piled in front of him. Xiao Tong knew a lot of things among the people, and he would check out every detail. Every time he found that there were errors or omissions in the reported matters or that they were out of touch with the truth, he would analyze and identify them at the time, tell the people who reported them whether they were right or wrong, and let them gradually correct their mistakes. No one was impeached for this matter.
When sentencing prisoners and judging cases, he often pardoned and pardoned criminals, and the people praised him for his benevolence, justice and kindness.
Xiao Tong was generous by nature, friendly to others, got along well with others, and was very nurturing. He kept his emotions and sorrows deep in his heart and never showed them on his face.
Recruit people with real talents and knowledge, and highly respect and care for them, never getting tired of them.
He often studies knowledge by himself, and sometimes discusses the past or current events with some talented people. Whenever he has free time, he keeps writing poems and articles and develops a habit.
At that time, there were almost more than 30,000 volumes of books in the East Palace, and famous talents gathered there. Literary creation flourished, and there was a grand occasion unprecedented since the Jin and Song Dynasties.
Xiao Tong liked to travel in mountains and rivers. He dug and built pools in Xuanpu Garden, built stone mountains, and built pavilions and buildings. He often visited the garden with learned officials in the court or famous people in the garden to enjoy the scenery and recite poems and compose poems.
Once while rowing in the back pool of the Imperial Garden, Hou Gui of Panyu praised the elegant environment and beautiful scenery here, and said: It would be even more beautiful if there were more female musicians here.
Prince Xiao Tong did not answer his words, but just recited two sentences from Zuo Si's "Poem of Zhaoyin": Why bother with silk and bamboo? Landscapes have clear sounds.
Hou Gui felt very ashamed and said no more.
After leaving the palace for more than 20 years, she has never taken in any dancing prostitutes or singing girls.
When he was young, Emperor Wu of Liang issued an edict to give him a play called Tai Le Female Prostitute, but he didn't like it at all.
In ordinary years, the Liang Dynasty's army marched north to the Wei State, and the price of grain in the capital was very high. When Prince Xiao Tong saw this, he ordered to save food and clothing, and changed the original family banquet to an ordinary light meal.
Whenever it rains continuously or snows heavily, he will send his trusted ministers to go through the streets and alleys to check on poor families. If there are people who are homeless and living on the streets, he will often provide money and materials to help them.
He also donated the silk floss and fabrics he used to make his own robes to make short clothes and jackets, and gave them to the poor and cold in the cold winter months.
If someone dies and cannot be buried, the prince will buy a coffin for him.
As soon as he heard that people from far and near were overtaxed and worked too hard, he stopped smiling and became very unhappy.
He often feels uneasy because of the poverty and overwork of the people.
Wuxing County's agricultural harvests often failed due to river flooding. Someone wrote a letter suggesting building a large canal to discharge floodwaters from Zhejiang.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Wu of Liang issued an edict to send Wang Bianzhi Fujie, the former governor of Jiaozhou, to recruit migrant workers from Wujun, Wuxing and Yixing counties to dig the canal.
Prince Xiao Tong submitted a memorial, believing that it would disturb the people's agricultural work, and requested to suspend the corvee service. Emperor Wu of Liang issued a special edict to enlighten him.
The prince Xiao Tong was particularly cautious and filial. Every time he went to court, he would wait outside the city gate before the drum beat.
Although the East Palace where the prince lives is inside the inner hall, he always faces the southwest whether he is sitting or standing. If he is summoned to go to court at night, he will half kneel and half sit until dawn.
In March of the third year, the prince was bedridden. He was afraid of worrying Emperor Wu of Liang. Every time Emperor Wu of Liang sent someone to ask questions about political affairs, he always wrote to the emperor himself.
On the sixth day of April, Xiao Tong died of illness at the age of thirty-one. Emperor Wu of Liang came to the East Palace in person, held the prince's coffin and cried loudly.
An edict was issued to bury Xiao Tong in gong robes and mian robes.
Everyone knew that the prince was benevolent and virtuous. After his death, both the government and the public felt regretful and shocked.
Men and women from the capital went to the crown prince's palace to pay their respects, and the streets were full of weeping people. People from all over the country and soldiers guarding the territory were very sad when they heard the news of his death.
He has written twenty volumes of collected works; he has also written ancient and modern imperial edicts; he has written ten volumes of "Preface"; his better five-character poems have been collected into twenty volumes of "Wen Yinghua"; and thirty volumes of "Selected Works".
Prince Ai, named Renzong, was the eldest son of Taizong.
Ding You is usually born in May of the fourth year.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was granted the title of Prince of Xuancheng County and was granted a land of two thousand.
Soon he was appointed as Shizhong and General of Zhongwei, and was given the first group of drum music.
In the fourth year of Datong, he was appointed envoy Chijie, governor-general of Chao, Tu of the military affairs of the two states, general of the Chinese army, and governor of Chao, and he still served as a minister.
In October of the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing attacked the area where Kyoto was located, and Shao appointed Prince Shao as the governor of Taipei.
In May of the third year, Taizong ascended the throne as emperor.
On Dinghai Day in June, he was made the crown prince.
In August of the second year of Dashi, the traitor Hou Jing deposed Taizong and was about to kill the prince. At that time, the traitor's subordinates claimed that Hou Jing had ordered the prince to be summoned. The prince was studying "Laozi" and was about to get out of bed when the executioner quietly approached.
The prince remained calm and said slowly: I knew something like this would happen a long time ago, but I still lament that it came too late.
The executioner wanted to hang him with his belt.
The prince said: You can't kill me even if you kill me.
He pointed to the rope under the bamboo poles that tied the tent and told them to take it and hang him to death. He was twenty-nine years old.
The prince was generous and easy-going by nature, coupled with his dignified and intelligent mental temperament. Under the control of traitors, he often showed an unyielding will.
At first, Hou Jing traveled westward and took the prince with him. When he returned from defeat, the troops were no longer orderly and serious, and the prince's boat was behind and could not catch up with the rebels. His confidants on the left and right advised him to go north for refuge.
The prince said: Now that my family and country have been destroyed, I don't want to survive. The Lord is in trouble, but I can't bear to take refuge.
If I run away now, it will be betraying my father, not avoiding a thief.
After saying this, he burst into tears and ordered to move forward immediately.
Because of the prince's courage and magnanimity, the traitor always feared him and worried about the trouble he would cause in the future, so he suffered first.
In April of the first year of Chengsheng's reign, he was given the title Prince Ai.
Prince Minghuai, Fang Ju, whose courtesy name was Degui, was the fourth son of Shizu.
At first, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nan'an County and followed Shizu to guard Jingcheng.
In the early years of the Taiqing Dynasty, he served as envoy Chijie, supervising the military affairs of the seven states of Hunan, Ying, Guining and Chenghe, Luo, general Zhennan, and governor of Xiangzhou.
Soon he was recruited as a servant and general of the central guard, and he was given a set of drum music.
In accordance with the emperor's will, Shizu made him the prince and changed his name to Yuanliang.
On the 11th day of the 11th year of Chengsheng's reign, he was made the crown prince.
When the army of the Western Wei Dynasty captured Jingcheng, the prince and Shizu were killed by the Wei soldiers.
The prince is smart and enlightened, and has a demeanor that is worthy of the world, but he is fierce and jealous.
Jing Tong adhered to the emperor's will and added his nickname of Prince Mihuai.
Yao Cha, Chen's Minister of Civil Affairs, said: Meng Ke gets up when he hears something, and he who does good deeds diligently is a good student of Shun.
If an ordinary citizen works as a farmer in the fields and does farm work all day long, the benefits he brings are numerous.
What's more, if the prince is in an important and prominent position and occupies an orthodox and respectable position, if he can restrain his heart and be honest and filial like Zhaoming, then how far will it be to have the virtues of Shun?

translation:
Fan Yun, courtesy name Yanlong, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang, and was the sixth-generation descendant of Jiewang, the Pingbei general of the Jin Dynasty.
When he was eight years old, he met Yin Yan, the governor of Yuzhou in the Song Dynasty, on the road. Yin Yan saw that his appearance was very unusual, so he invited him to sit with him.
Yin Yan asked him to compose a poem, and he wrote it immediately.
Everyone present was impressed. Fan Yun once studied with his relative Yuan Zhao and worked tirelessly day and night.
Yuan Zhao patted his shoulder and said, "You are bright and cheerful, and you are diligent in studying." He will definitely be a talented person in the future.
Fan Yun has been smart and flexible since he was a child, and he is insightful when dealing with things. He is good at writing articles and is familiar with various literary styles such as letters.
His father, Fan Kang, served in the Ying Mansion and joined the army. Fan Yun lived with his father in Fubao. At that time, Shen Yue from Wuxing, Yu Daizhi from Xinye, and Fan Kangtong were working in Ying Mansion. Fan Yun immediately became good friends after meeting them.
Fan Yun first served as Shuzuo of Xicao in Yingzhou, and then joined the army as Cao Xing of Facao.
Soon Shen Youzhi rebelled and raised troops to besiege Ying City. Fan Kang was appointed Changliu of Ying Mansion at that time and entered the city to take charge of defense, leaving his family members outside the city.
Fan Yun was captured by enemy soldiers, and Youzhi interrogated him personally. His tone was very stern, but Fan Yun's appearance remained unchanged and he answered calmly.
After hearing this, Youzhi smiled and said: "You are such a pleasant child. Go home for now."
The next morning, Youzhi sent for Fan Yun again and ordered him to deliver a message to Cheng Bao.
Some of the defenders in the city advocated killing Fan Yun. Fan Yun said: I have an old mother and a young brother at home outside the city. Their lives are all in Shen's hands. If I disobey orders, they will be harmed. Today I am killed for them, and I am willing to die without any regrets.
Longshi Ryu Shiryong Pingsuo was friendly with Fan Yun and managed to save him from death.
In the early years of Jianyuan of Qi Dynasty, Prince Liang of Jingling became the prefect of Kuaiji, and Fan Yun just started to follow Prince Jingling at that time.
The king didn't know him well. It happened that King Jingling was visiting Qinwang Mountain. The king asked the people around him to identify the ancient characters on the stone inscriptions, but no one could understand them. Only Fan Yun could read the inscriptions. King Jingling was very happy. From then on, Jiang Zhou was favored more than anyone else in the same house.
When King Jingling was appointed Danyang Yin, Fan Yun was summoned to be the chief administrator, and he was highly valued by his close associates.
When he came to see Emperor Gao of Qi, someone happened to offer a white crow. Emperor Gao asked what this meant was a sign. Because Fan Yun was in a low position, he finally replied: I heard that when the emperor worships the ancestral temple, white crows will come.
At that time, the visit to the ancestral temple had just ended.
Emperor Yigao said: Just as you said.
The principle of induction between heaven and man can be so miraculously consistent.
Fan Yun later transferred to the prison of the North and South County Prince to join the military. He also served as the chief secretary and was promoted to the position of Zhonglang in the Shangshu Palace.
When Xiao Ziliang was a Situ, Jianyun joined the military affairs department and was soon awarded the title of Minister of Tongzhi Sanqi, and also the chief of the Honshu Dazhongzheng.
Later, he served as the internal history of Lingling. During his tenure, he was able to keep himself clean and tidy, eliminating many cumbersome government orders and unnecessary expenses, so that the people could live and work in peace and contentment.
Emperor Qi Ming summoned Fan Yun back to the capital. After arriving, he was granted the title of Minister of Sanqi.
He also served as the internal history of Shixing.
There are many powerful and cunning families in Shixing County. If the county governor does not treat them well, they will conspire to kill him together. If they fail, they will drive the governor away.
The border counties of Shixing were inhabited by barbarian tribes, and there were particularly many thieves in these areas. In the past, all the officials in the imperial office wore weapons for self-defense.
After Fan Yun arrived in Shixing, he used his kindness to appease them and removed the surveillance post.

Fan Yun, courtesy name Yanlong, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang, and was a sixth-generation descendant of Jiewang, a Jin Dynasty general. At age eight, he impressed Yin Yan, a Song Dynasty governor, by composing a poem on the spot. He studied diligently with his relative Yuan Zhao, who predicted he would become a talented person. Fan Yun was intelligent, insightful, and skilled in writing various literary styles. He lived with his father, Fan Kang, in Fubao and befriended Shen Yue, Yu Daizhi, and Fan Kangtong.

Fan Yun began his official career as Shuzuo of Xicao in Yingzhou. During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Fan Yun was captured but remained calm under interrogation, earning his release. He later delivered a message for Youzhi, risking death to protect his family. Longshi Ryu Shiryong saved him. In the early Qi Dynasty, Fan Yun served Prince Jingling, impressing him by reading ancient inscriptions on Qinwang Mountain. He became a trusted chief administrator and was favored by Emperor Gao of Qi for interpreting a white crow as an auspicious sign.

Fan Yun held various positions, including prison officer, chief secretary, and Zhonglang in the Shangshu Palace. As internal history of Lingling, he governed with integrity, reducing burdens on the people. He later served as internal history of Shixing, where he pacified powerful families and barbarian tribes through kindness, removing surveillance posts and ensuring safety for merchants. He was promoted to General Jianwu and Governor of Guangzhou.

Fan Yun was recalled to the capital due to a dispute involving his friend's brother and was imprisoned but pardoned. In the second year of Qi Yongyuan, he became Dr. Guozi. He met Liang Gaozu at Prince Jingling's residence and later served as a staff officer during the rebellion against Saihunhou. After the Liang Dynasty's establishment, Fan Yun became Shizhong and remonstrated with Gaozu about marrying Qi Shuhunhou's concubine Yu, advising him to prioritize state affairs. Gaozu accepted his advice and rewarded him.

In the first year of Tianjian, Fan Yun participated in the southern郊 sacrifice. Gaozu praised his caution, and Fan Yun was appointed Changshi of Sanqi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Marquis of Xiaocheng County. He was promoted based on his friendship with Gaozu and served loyally. Gaozu instructed his sons to treat Fan Yun as a brother. Fan Yun later became crown prince's concubine and right servant of the minister but was dismissed for employing people against the emperor's will.

Fan Yun was honest, easy-going, and devoted to his widowed sister-in-law. He helped the poor, such as transporting the deceased commander Shi Wangke's body for burial. He advised Prince Jingling on political matters without flattery. Emperor Wu of Qi initially considered Fan Yun mediocre but later praised his sincerity after reading his admonitions. Fan Yun advised Prince Qi Wenhui to understand farming hardships. As an official, he handled documents efficiently but was criticized for his straightforwardness. He distributed his income to relatives and friends, leaving no savings.

Fan Yun died at age fifty-three in the second year of Tianjian. Gaozu mourned deeply and issued an edict praising his loyalty and wisdom. He was posthumously given titles and honors, including Shizhong and General of the Guard. His collected works comprised thirty volumes. His son Fan Xiaocai inherited his title.

Shen Yue, courtesy name Xiuwen, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. His grandfather was General Shen Linzi, and his father was Prefect Shen Yilong. After his father's execution, Shen Yue hid to avoid persecution. He studied diligently, often reading at night despite his mother's concerns. He served as a court official and impressed Cai Xingzong, who appointed him as a recorder. Shen Yue later held various positions, including Shangshu Duzhilang and captain of the infantry school. He was close to the prince and served in the East Palace.

Shen Yue joined Prince Jingling's circle of talented individuals. He held positions such as Minister Zuocheng and Yushi Zhongcheng. Under Emperor Ming of Qi, he became General of the Auxiliary State and Minister of the Five Arms. After Emperor Ming's death, he wrote decrees for the prime minister. He later served as Left Guard General and Zhi Sanqi. In the second year of Yongyuan, he resigned due to his mother's age but was awarded titles.

Shen Yue advised Gaozu to ascend the throne, citing divine signs and public support. Gaozu agreed, and Shen Yue drafted the abdication decree. After the Liang Dynasty's establishment, Shen Yue became a regular servant of Sanqi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Marquis of Changxian County. His mother was honored as Mrs. Jianchang. He later held positions such as Zuopushe and Shangshu Ling. Despite his high status, Shen Yue lived frugally and built a house in Dongtian, writing "Residence in the Suburbs" to express his feelings.

Shen Yue died at age seventy-three in the twelfth year of Tianjian. He was given posthumous honors. He was extremely intelligent, with two pupils in his left eye and a purple mole on his waist. He owned 20,000 volumes of books. Despite past grievances, he appointed a clansman who had insulted him as a county minister. He was knowledgeable about laws and regulations and excelled in poetry and writing. However, he was arrogant and obsessed with fame, and after becoming prime minister, he failed to recommend talents. He died of fear after Gaozu condemned him for protecting his family. He wrote numerous works, including "Book of Jin," "Song Book," and "Four Tone Spectrum," though Gaozu disliked the latter.

Yao Cha, the Minister of Chen Libu, commented that during the Qi Dynasty's decline, Gaozu relied on Fan Yun and Shen Yue to strategize and complete his imperial career. Fan Yun was alert and capable, while Shen Yue was talented and knowledgeable, second only to Sima Qian and Dong Hu.
