Zongyang, also known as Mingzha, was from Nieyang County, Nanyang, and had lived in Jiangling for generations. His grandfather Zong Bing was a renowned scholar who declined an official appointment. His father Zongfan served as Xizhonglang. Zongyang was diligent and talented, passing the Yingzhou scholar exam at twenty. He served as a regular attendant and knight for King Lin, and was among scholars painted in the West Residence by King Jingling of Southern Qi. During the Yongming era, he received Wei envoys with Ren Fang. He managed secretarial duties for Prince Nanjun, known for his calligraphy and integrity. After Prince Wenhui's death, he served the emperor's grandson but later distanced himself due to the ruler's failings, becoming magistrate of Moling and Shangshu Duguanlang. During the Longchang era, he survived disasters due to his integrity. Under Emperor Ming, he governed Yingzhou competently but resigned to care for his aging father. He later served Liang Gaozu, providing strategies and supplies, and held various posts including Censor Zhongcheng and Champion General. He died at forty-nine, succeeded by his son Zong Yaoqing. His cousin Zongyue was also renowned.

Liu Tan, courtesy name Dedu, was from Anzhong County, Nanyang, a descendant of General Liu Qiao. He served as official servant to the Nanjun King and magistrate of Xiaoling, known for his administrative skills. Under King Nankang, he joined the army and managed Changliu. During Liang Gaozu's uprising, he became a consultant. He advised sending a veteran to govern Xiangzhou, was appointed Assistant Chief Historian and Governor of Changsha, where he mobilized over 300,000 hu of rice for troops. He suppressed rebellions by Wang Sencan and others, using strategy to kill the traitor Zhong Baoti and pacifying the region. For his merits, he was made Lord of Yiqiu Shu and later served as Sima Pingxi and prefect of Xinxing. He died at sixty-two, succeeded by his son Liu Quan.

Bimai, courtesy name Lanwei, was a descendant of Bi Tong from Chenmo County, living in Jiangling. As a child, he impressed his uncle Zong Maggot by choosing books over other items. He served King Yi of Yuzhang as chief administrator and later joined the army. After his father's death, he resigned but was recalled. He impressed Xiao Yi with his knowledge of local geography and customs. He restored Jingzhou's official buildings after a rebellion, completing the work quickly without conscripting laborers. He served in various roles under Liang, including Minister of Huangmen and Yushi Zhongcheng. He was known for his fairness and knowledge, once correctly attributing a missing silk net to natural decay. He later became governor of Guangzhou, where he killed the rebellious Xu Yuanyu. He died in office. His sister, married to Liu Qiu, was praised for her virtue. His son Le Nazuo, courtesy name Genbei, was also renowned, serving in various posts including Qibu Lang and Taizhou Qing, known for his integrity and refusal of unearned salary. He died at sixty-three.

Yao Cha commented that these three men were key figures in Chu, contributing to Liang's establishment: Liu Tan in military affairs, Le Ai in official duties, both achieving high positions as expected.

Fourteen years after leaving prison, Jihe was promoted to General Pingbei, Colonel Ningman, and Governor of Yuzhou.

At that time, Emperor Gaozu was concentrating on believing in Buddhism, and the people of the world followed suit; Wei San had always been relatively weak in faith, and he was an official and a minister, so he was unwilling to be influenced by the world, and his behavior was the same as in the past.
In the summer of the first year of Liang Pongtong's reign. Wei San moved to serve as a servant and general of chariots and cavalry. Due to illness, he did not pay homage to the official position.

Posthumously presented to the three divisions: Shizhong, Chariot and Cavalry General, and Kaifu Yitong.
Mi's name is Yan.

Wei San's sons include Wei Fang, Wei Zheng, Wei Ling, and Wei An. Wei Fang has another biography.
Wei Zheng, whose courtesy name was Jingzhi, started his career as King Xing of Nankang and joined the army. Soon he was moved to the position of minister of Zhongshu and became the governor of Xiangyang.
In the past, Wei Zheng was very friendly with King Shuhai, Seng Ru. When Seng Ru was a minister and participated in the imperial election, all the guests and friends fawned over him, but Wei Zheng took it indifferently.

Wei Leng was an upright person with a calm and simple temperament. He served as a historian who recorded events. He was knowledgeable and well-informed. Scholars at the time asked him to answer difficult questions.
Wei Leng started his career in Prince Ancheng's palace and joined the army. Soon he was moved to serve as the official secretary and censor, the prince's servant, and Guanglu Qing.

Wei Ai, younger brother of Wei San clan.

Great-grandfather Wei Gui moved south to Xiangyang in the early Taiyuan years of Emperor Guiwu's reign in the east, where he served as the minister of the local cavalry and scattered cavalry.
His grandfather, Wei Gongxun, served as the prefect of Yiyang in Song Dynasty.
His father, Wei Yizheng, passed away at an early age.

In the second year of the reign of Emperor Zhongxing of Qi Dynasty, he followed Emperor He and sent him to Xia along the Yangtze River.

His son Wei Qianxiang was promoted to General Xiaoqi, and served as the governor of Changshi and Ruyin and Zhongli counties in the north.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Chen's Ministry of Civil Affairs, said: In the past, Dou Rong moved the land on the right side of the river to submit to the Han Dynasty, and eventually became a wealthy family; Liu Hui led Nanzheng to respond to Gaozu's righteous deeds, and the reputation of his family for generations has not been ruined, all because it was in line with the trend of the times. Liu Chen's plans were also very effective, which is a reflection of his wisdom.
Wei San led the mediocre troops to join Gaozu. His place was smaller than Liu Hui's, but after the battles of Hefei and Shaoyang, his achievements were even more remarkable, but he did not take any credit or be arrogant. What a gentleman!
summary:
Liu Xun, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Hedong. He began his official career at seventeen under Emperor Wu of Qi, serving in various posts including Sangonglang and Prince Zhongsheren. He befriended Prince Xiang of Badong but foresaw disaster due to the prince’s association with villains, returning to the capital feigning illness. He later served as Minister of Zhongshu, Commander of the Zhonghu Army, and Prefect of Xin'an, though he was dismissed for lack of political achievements. During the Jianwu era, he became captain of Xirong and governor of Liang, Nan, and Qin states. When Emperor Gaozu rebelled, Liu Xun responded with Hanzhong troops. Under Emperor He, he served as a servant and general, and later as Prince Zhan Shi under Emperor Gaozu. Gaozu praised him in a poem and consulted him on pardoning Xu Yuanyu’s disciples, to which Liu Xun wisely replied, earning acclaim. He died in office in October of the sixth year at age forty-six, posthumously honored as Shizhong and General of the Fu Army, with the title Mu. He authored "The Biography of Renzheng" and various poems.

Liu Chen, courtesy name Wenruo, was Liu Xun’s fifth younger brother. Known for filial piety, he cared for his ill parents without undressing for years. He served as Situ Xing and Prince Zhongsheren. During Qi Donghunhou’s reign, he advised Xiao Yingzhou against attacking Emperor Gaozu, warning of mutual destruction and citing past examples. His counsel led Yingzhou to ally with Gaozu. Liu Chen later held posts such as Shangshu Libu Lang, General of the Assistant State, and Prefect of Nanping. He opposed moving the capital to Xia, arguing it would destabilize the people, and was proven correct when Ba Shu attacked. Under Emperor Gaozu, he became Minister of the Five Arms and was enfeoffed as Prefecture Lingbo. He died at home at age forty-one, posthumously honored as Zhongshu Ling with the title Mu.

Xi Chanwen, from Anding, lost his parents young and loved reading. He befriended Xiao Yingzhou and served as a doctor in Xizhong. He persuaded Yingzhou to support Gaozu’s rebellion, secretly sending a silver sword and receiving a gold Ruyi in return. Under Emperor He, he became minister of Huangmen and later Weiqing. After Yingzhou’s sudden death, he stabilized the region by welcoming Xiao Qi to govern Jingzhou. Under Emperor Gaozu, he served as official minister and was enfeoffed as Shanyang Bo. He died in office after two years as prefect of Shuyang, known for his integrity.

Wei Rui, courtesy name Huaiwen, was born in Duling. He was filial to his stepmother and praised for his integrity. He served under various officials, avoiding disaster by requesting a post in Yicheng County during Yuan Yun’s rebellion. During the Qi Dynasty turmoil, he predicted the failure of rebels Chen Haoda and Cui Huijing, and allied with Gaozu, bringing 2,000 men and 200 horses. Gaozu appointed him champion general and prefect of Jiangxia. During a plague in Ying City, he personally comforted survivors and ensured proper burials. After the Liang Dynasty’s establishment, he became Dali and later Tingwei. He repelled Northern Wei invasions and led successful campaigns, including the capture of Xiaoxian City and Hefei, using strategic weirs and naval attacks. At Shaoyang, he defeated a massive Wei army, causing over 100,000 casualties. He was promoted to Marquis and served in various high offices. Known for humility, he treated old friends kindly and avoided boasting. He died at seventy-nine, posthumously honored as Shizhong and Chariot and Cavalry General, with the title Yan. His sons included Wei Fang, Wei Zheng, Wei Ling, and Wei An.

Wei Ai, courtesy name Xiaoyou, was calm and thoughtful. He lost his father young, served his mother filially, and was dedicated to learning, often studying alone in a dusty room. He was erudite in Zhouyi and Chunqiu Zuoshi. During Gaozu’s rebellion, he pacified local rebels and later followed Xiao Qi to Jingzhou. He died of illness en route to attack Liu Jilian, leaving a legacy of integrity.

Xie Bei, courtesy name Jingchong, was a native of Yangxia, Chen County, born into a distinguished family with his grandfather and father both holding high offices in the Song Dynasty. A child prodigy, he could write essays at age ten and was highly praised by his father Xie Zhuang and Wang Jingwen of Langye. Emperor Xiaowu also recognized his talent. Xie Bei began his official career as Fujun Fa Cao Xing and joined the army, later becoming Prince Sheren but resigning due to his father's death. After mourning, he held various positions including Zhongshulang and Huangmen侍郎. He served as internal history of Linchuan but was impeached for bribery, though the case was shelved by Yuan Can.

During Qi Emperor Gao's reign, Xie Bei was among the "four friends" of the emperor, serving as chief historian and later Shizhong. When Emperor Gao sought to usurp the throne, Xie Bei expressed reluctance, citing historical precedents, which displeased the emperor. He was eventually dismissed and stayed at home. In the Yongming era, he was recalled to serve as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi and later as champion general and prefect of Yixing, where he neglected official duties but amassed wealth. He refused several appointments, including Shizhong and Zhongshuling, preferring to avoid political turmoil.

Under Emperor Ming, Xie Bei was summoned but declined, building a house in the county. He was later forced to serve under Emperor Gaozu, accepting positions like Shizhong and Situ, though he often feigned illness. He died at sixty-six, receiving posthumous honors. His son Xie Mo was dismissed for killing cattle, and his nephew Xie Lan, known for his literary talent and demeanor, served in various roles, including prefect of Wuxing, where he suppressed bandits and corruption. Xie Lan died in office at thirty-seven. Yao Cha commented that Xie Bei was loyal to the Song Dynasty, while Xie Lan excelled in governance.

One day, the emperor asked a painter to draw a portrait of Kang Xuan, and sent an eunuch to take the painting and ask Kang Xuan: Do you know anyone from the palace?
This shows how close he is.
At that time, Wang Zu, who had surrendered from Wei, came up with a plan and asked for a dam to be built on the Huai River to flood Shouyang with water.
Wang Zu quoted a northern nursery rhyme and said: Jingshan is the upper grid, Fushan is the lower grid, Tongtuo is the Jigou, and it is filled with Ju Yeze.
Emperor Gaozu thought it was reasonable and asked hydraulic engineer Chen Chengbo and Caiguan General Zuqu to inspect the terrain. After their inspection, they both said that the sandy soil in the Huaihe River was light and not solid, so dams could not be built.
Emperor Gaozu did not adopt their opinions and mobilized the people of Xuzhou and Yangzhou to transfer dings to build dams at the rate of 5 dings for every 20 households.
Granting Kang Xuan a holiday, he commanded the military forces in Huaishang and supervised the construction of weirs and dams. There were as many as 200,000 migrant workers and soldiers serving.
In Zhongli, it starts from Fushan in the south and reaches the rocks in the north. It piles earth along the river bank and joins it in the middle stream.
In the fourteenth year, when the weirs and dams were about to be closed, the Huaihe River became fast and turbulent, and the weirs were washed away by the water again. Everyone was worried about it.
Some people say that there are often dragons in the Yangtze and Huaihe rivers. They can ride on the wind and rain and destroy the cliffs and embankments. However, they are naturally afraid of iron. Therefore, people introduced iron tools smelted from the east and west, ranging from large pots like kefu to small shovels for farming. Iron tools weighing tens of millions of kilograms were sunk into the water where the big weir is.
Still unable to close it, they cut down trees to make manhole railings, filled the middle with large rocks, and added soil on top.
Within a hundred miles along the Huaihe River, all the trees and stones on the hills and hills, no matter how big or small, were chopped down, and the shoulders of those who carried the trees and burdens were worn out.
In the summer, an epidemic broke out, and the dead migrant workers piled together, sleeping on each other, and the sound of mosquitoes, flies and insects continued day and night.
Emperor Gaozu felt sorry for the slaves who had to work for too long, so he sent Shangshu's right servant She Yuan Ang and his minister Xie Ju Chijie to the construction site to express condolences and exempt them from taxes.
This winter was very cold. The Huaihe River and swimming pools were all frozen. Seventy-eight percent of the migrant workers and soldiers died. Emperor Gaozu also sent people to give clothes and trousers to the workers.
In November, Wei sent General Yang Dayan claiming to open Dayan. Kang Xuan ordered all troops to withdraw from the barracks and sleep in the open, waiting for the arrival of the Wei army.
He sent his son Kang Yue to challenge and killed Xu Fangxing, the Sima of Wei Xianyang Palace. The Wei army retreated slightly.
In December, the state of Wei sent Minister Li Tanding to lead an army to challenge. Kang Xuan, Xuzhou governor Liu Sizu and others resisted.
Emperor Gaozu also sent right-guard general Chang Yizhi, imperial servant Yu Hongwen, Zhihe Cao Shizong, and Xu Yuanhe to resist the guards one after another.
In April of the fifteenth year, the weir was built.
It is nine miles long, one hundred and forty feet wide at the base, forty-five feet wide at the top, twenty feet high, and nineteen feet five feet deep.
There is a dike in the middle. Willow trees are planted on the dike, and the soldiers and civilians live side by side on it.
The river water is very clean. Looking down from above, you can see the houses and tombs below at a glance.
Someone said to Kang Xuan: The Yangtze River, the Huaihe River, the Yellow River, and the Jishui River are used by God to regulate and release its Qi, and they should not be blocked for a long time.
If a culvert is dug to allow water to pour eastward, the flow will be wide and gentle and the weir will not be damaged.
Kang Xuan thought he was right, so he dug a hole to the east and filled it with water. He also sent people to Wei State to counterattack and said: The people of Liang Dynasty were most afraid of digging holes, but they were not afraid of fighting in the wild.
The Wei people believed this and dug a cave five feet deep. They opened a hole in the embankment and let the water flow north into the cave. The river flowed day and night, but the water in the cave remained unabated.
That month, all the Wei troops were defeated and returned.
Wherever the river reaches, there are hundreds of miles along the Huaihe River.
The garrison of Shouyang City in the Wei State had to move to Bagong Mountain to settle down. It was a graveyard formed by scattered people from the south.
Initially, when Dayan was being built within the boundaries of Xuzhou, Zhang Baozi, the governor, threatened everywhere within the territory that he would definitely take charge of the matter.
Later Chenmian sent other officials to supervise and supervise this work. King Jibao felt very ashamed.
Soon, the emperor ordered Zhang Baozi to be under Kang Xuan's command and to consult him first on everything. Therefore, Zhang Baozi falsely accused Kang Xuan of colluding with the state of Wei. Although Gaozu did not accept his words, he still consulted Kang Xuan on everything.
Soon after, Kang Xuan was transferred to Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Sizhou, General Xinwu, and governor of Sizhou. He also served as the prefect of Anlu County, adding 200 households to the city.
After Kang Xuan returned, Zhang Baozi stopped building the dam until the autumn and August of the Qian year. The backwater surged, all the weirs and dikes were broken and destroyed, and the river flowed all the way to the sea. Zuqu was arrested and imprisoned.
During Kang Xuan's three years in office in the state, he overhauled the city moat and gave strict orders to the government.
In the eighteenth year, Kang Xuan was called to serve as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi, and also served as the captain of Changcheng. He was on duty in the palace with the guard Tong He and the prince's right guard led Huang Jian.
In the first year of ordinary life, Kang Xuan was awarded the title of Wei Qing, but he passed away before he could formally become an official. He was fifty-seven years old.
The emperor went to mourn in person that day.
He was posthumously awarded the title of General Youwei and given to the Ministry of Advocacy.
One hundred thousand dollars and one hundred bolts of cloth were given for the funeral.
Mi Hao Zhuang.
Chen's face is generous and cheerful, and his joy and anger are invisible. In the court, when he sees others, he looks like a person who can't speak, so he is called a long and thick person.
In the provincial capital, every time in the cold winter months, when I saw the provincial officials in ragged clothes, I would give them cotton-padded clothes. This was how he was so kind and charitable.
His son Kang Yue succeeded him.
Chang Yizhi, Bi Yan: Sister. He had a strong body when he was young.
During the first expedition, he followed Xuanxu in the expedition and made many military exploits.
When Cao Hu took office in Qian, he asked Zhan Zhi to fill the post of Fanghe and serve as the garrison commander of Feng Yi.
When Xuanxu was exchanged, Zhanzhi stayed to serve Zhizhuo. At that time, the world was in chaos, and Gaozu treated justice well.
After the righteous army rose up, Shanzhi was awarded the title of general of the auxiliary country and military commander, and was appointed as the middle soldier of King Jian'an to join the army.
At that time, Tong Zuodeng's Tongdan had a warehouse for storing military supplies. Chantan sent him to fight, and he won every time.
When the uprising army was stationed in Saimi, Chang Yizhi followed Wang Jian and fought hard in Qianhuang and Yuquexiao, killing and capturing many of them.
After Jiankang City was pacified, Emperor Gaozu appointed Chang Yizhi as General Zhihe and Lord of Ma Youjiahu.
The first year of Tianjian. The owner of the lamp was granted the title of Lord Chengfengxuanbao, and he was granted the title of Lord of Chengfengxuanbao, with a settlement of 500 households.
Ren Xiaoqi General.
Served as the prefect of the disgraceful face sculpture.
In the second year, he was moved to the post of Jiejie, supervising the military affairs of Xu maggot in the north, general of the auxiliary state, governor of Rentiao Prefecture, and guarding Zhongli.
The Wei army invaded Jitu and was defeated by Dan Zhanzhi's troops.
Three years later, Chang Zhanzhi was awarded the title of Champion General and added 200 households in the city.
In the fourth year, Luanqu launched a large-scale Northern Expedition. King Linchuan, the governor of Yangzhou, commanded various armies to be stationed in Chi. Zhanzhi led the state soldiers to accept Jiedu and served as the front army, attacked Wei's Liangcheng garrison and captured the garrison.
In the fifth year, Zhidan felt that the military conscription was too long, so he ordered the army to return to the court, and all the troops retreated. Wang Chenglong of Zhongshan in Wei State took advantage of the situation to follow and pursue, and captured Matou City. The city packed the stored grain, and all the Soviet troops moved to the north.
Commentators all said: The troops transported the rice back to the north, so they should not invade further south.
Shandan said: No, the Japanese must be marching into the army. The current situation is not the truth of the matter.
So he sent civil craftsmen to build clock plates and ordered Danzhan to prepare for war.
In the winter of this year, Cheng Ji indeed led an army of hundreds of thousands including King Seruan Wu Huaqie, General Pingdong Yang Zuozu, and invaded Zhongli southward.
The north side of Zhongli City was blocked by Qishui, so the Wei army built a pontoon bridge on the west bank of Yingbao Xun across the Huaihe River as a passage.
Yuan Ying occupied Shu'an, Yang Dayan occupied the west bank, and attacked the city with a hammer.
At that time, there were only 3,000 people in the city, and Chang Yizhi led them to resist at any time.
The Wei army then loaded trucks with earth to fill the trenches, and asked the Wei army soldiers to follow them carrying the earth on their backs. Officers rode behind them to urge them. Some people had not had time to come back, and the earth followed them, and soon the trenches were filled.
Yuan Ying and Yang Dayan personally supervised the battle, attacking hard day and night, taking turns in the battle, climbing up again after falling down, and no one retreated.
They also erected flying towers and rushed cars to ram the city wall. Wherever they hit, the soil on the city wall collapsed.
Chang Yizhi used mud to fill the gap. Even if the car crashed into the city wall, it could not destroy the city wall.
Chang Yizhi was also good at archery. When the city was in danger of being attacked, Yoshizhi rushed to the rescue. Every time he bent his bow and drew an arrow, he was invincible and no one fell down.
There were dozens of rounds of fighting in a day, with tens of thousands of casualties before and after. The number of soldiers killed by the Wei army was as high as the city wall.
In April of the sixth year, Emperor Gaozu sent Cao Jingzong and Wei Jiao to lead an army of 200,000 troops to come to the rescue. When they arrived at Zhongli, they fought with the Wei army and defeated the Wei army. Wujie, Lao Qumeng and others escaped each other.
Danxianzhi led the light cavalry and pursued them all the way to Luokou before returning. In this battle, countless Wei troops were killed or captured alive.
Due to his meritorious service, Dan Zhanzhi was promoted to the title of Military Advisor General, and he was granted an additional 200 households in the city. He was moved to the post of Chijie, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Qingji and Qingji Prefectures, General of Conquering Captives, and Governor of Qing and Hebei Prefectures.
Before formally becoming an official, he was appointed governor of the military affairs of the five states of Southern Yanzhou, Xu Qingji, general of the auxiliary state, and governor of Southern Yanzhou.
Because he committed the crime of taking prohibited items out of his jurisdiction, he was dismissed from office by the relevant officials.
In the same year, Yizhi was appointed as Zhu Yi Zhihe and was awarded the title of General Zuo Xiaoqi. He still served as Zhihe.
Later, he moved to the right guard of the crown prince, and concurrently served as the Yueqi school captain.
In the eighth year, Chang Yizhi was appointed as Chijie, Supervisor of all military affairs in Chiye, General of Expeditions, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
In the ninth year, he returned to the court with his original title and was soon appointed Sima, King of Sikong Linchuan. His position as general remained as before.
Ten years later, he was promoted to right-guard general.
In the thirteenth year, he was appointed general of Zuowei.
In the winter of the Qian year, Emperor Gaozu sent Prince Youwei to lead Kang Xuan to supervise the army's construction of Jingshan Weir.
The next year, Wenwang sent Kui Kenxuan to lead an army to advance towards Xingshan, threatening to open the dam. The emperor ordered Yi Zhijie to lead his servant Qing Yu Hongwen, Zhihe generals Cao Shizong, Xu Yuanqu and others to rescue Chenmian. Before the army arrived, Chenxuan and others had defeated the Wei army.
The Qiao army sent General Kui Nuo to attack Chu, and surrounded General Zhihe Zhao Zuyue. Chang Yizhi then led Zhu Yi Zhihe, Wang Shennian and others to rescue him.
At that time, the morale of the Wei soldiers was high. Wang Shennian failed to attack the pontoon bridge in Xia Shi, so reinforcements could not come in immediately, so Xia Shi was trapped.
When Changyi's teacher returned to the court, he was presented with a memorial by the relevant officials. Emperor Gaozu thought that he was a meritorious official and did not ask about his faults.
In the fifteenth year, Chang Yizhi was appointed as envoy Chijie, governor of Xiang maggot military affairs, general Xinwei, and fishery governor.
In the same year, he was changed to the governor of North Xuzhou, Yuanjin Zhujun, the general of Pingbei, and the governor of North Xuzhou.
Changyi had a generous nature, and as a general, he could soothe people's hearts and rule well, so he could be rewarded by his subordinates for their desperate efforts. When he was an official in the feudal state, his subordinates and the people were very stable.
Soon, the emperor gave him a piece of propaganda, and he was granted the title of Marquis of Yingdao County, with the same number of households as before.
After three years of Xuanbi's reign, Dan Zhanzhi was summoned to serve as the general of the army, and his propaganda continued as before.
Died in October four years.
Emperor Gaozu deeply regretted his death and wrote in the edict: Chang Yizhi, the general who protected the army and the founder of Yingdao County, was steady in his work, successful in his strategy, broad-minded and majestic, and outstanding in loyalty. At the beginning of the national destiny, he served on the border and achieved results.
After he was declared an important minister of the country, he was assigned to command the imperial guards. His sudden death is extremely sad.
He can be posthumously given the title of regular servant of scattered cavalry, general of chariot cavalry, and a department of advocacy.
Give Shuyuan a secret weapon and a set of court uniforms.
Send 20,000 yuan, 200 pieces of cloth, and 200 catties of wax.
Mi Hao Lie.
Chang Yizhi's son Chang Shiye succeeded him, and his official positions reached General Zhihe and Governor of Qiaozhou.
Ta Sai, the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs of Nansu Eyelashes, said: Ji Saiyi, Zhou Kan, Chen Mian, Chang Yizhi, when he first followed the emperor, his achievements were still very slight.
When a group of bandits burned the city gates, Zhang Huishao showed his merits by fighting hard; when the two cities of Hedan and Dankuang were besieged, Mai Daogen and Chang Yizhi made the most contributions; when the battle of Can broke out, it was Chun Xuan who was in charge: each of them had their own merits, so they were favored, and it was natural for them to be promoted to officials.
Before that, when Saturn was guarding the Tianjiang star, a large dam was built. After Saturn moved its position, the dam broke. This was not just a matter of personnel, but the will of heaven.
summary:
Zhang Huishao, courtesy name Deji, was from Yiyang. During the reign of Emperor Qi Ming of the Southern Dynasty, he served as Zhihe and garrison commander of Jingling Hengsang. After his mother's death in the early Yongyuan period, he returned home for burial. Upon hearing of Liang Gaozu's righteous army, he joined as a soldier and was appointed General Ningshuo. He defeated Shen Nandang's navy, seized weapons, and made many military exploits at Xinlin and Zhuque. After Jiankang was captured, he became General of the Auxiliary State and was later granted the title of Marquis of Shiyang County with 500 households. When remnants of Donghun Hou's forces attacked the palace gates, Huishao led his men to defeat them, killing many. He was promoted to Crown Prince's Right Guard and increased his residence by 200 households. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he attacked Suyu and captured the city lord Ma Chenglong. However, after Wei reinforcements arrived and defeated his general Lan Huaigong, Huishao fled to Huaiyin. In the sixth year, he fought at Zhongli under Cao Jingzong, contributing to the defeat of the Wei army. He later served as Governor of Northern Yanzhou, where he managed affairs well and was beloved by officials and people. He died at age sixty-three in the eighteenth year of Tianjian, receiving posthumous honors.

Feng Daogen, courtesy name Danji, was from Luluo. Orphaned young and poor, he worked to support his mother, gaining fame for filial piety at thirteen. At sixteen, he rescued fellow villager Tomb Daowang from barbarians, killing many enemies. During the Yongyuan period, after his mother's death, he joined Gaozu's righteous army, leading village youths. He served under Cai Daofu and later commanded his troops after Daofu's death. After Gaozu ascended, Daogen was made General Xiaoqi and Male of Zengcheng County with 200 households. He suppressed Chen Bozhi's rebellion. As Grand Administrator of Muliang County, he prepared defenses despite ridicule, then defeated General Yu Shifu's 20,000 troops by opening the city gates and sending out 200 elite soldiers. He later captured Wei army's Gujiao Army honor guard, cutting off their food supply. At the battle of Zhongli, he built fortresses and attacked the Wei army's bridge, contributing to their defeat. Daogen was cautious and generous, never boasting of his achievements. Gaozu compared him to General Big Tree. He lived frugally in a simple house with no walls or guards. Though uneducated in youth, he later became proficient in writing. He died at fifty-eight in the first year of the ordinary period, with Gaozu personally mourning him.

Chen Mian, from Huashan County, had ancestors from Chenjuli who migrated during the Jin Dynasty. Outstanding in youth, he was called to serve as secretary of Xicao. After his mother's death, he became Grand Administrator of Huashan County, where he treated people with sincerity. When Gaozu raised troops, Chen Mian led 3,000 brave men and 250 horses to join him. He was granted the title of Male of Nan'an County with 300 households. He rescued Liang Su from Wei siege and later served as Governor of Northern Yanzhou. He supervised construction of the Jingshan Weir on the Huai River, mobilizing 200,000 workers. The weir was nine miles long, but the Huai River's currents repeatedly damaged it. Iron tools were sunk to counter dragons, and trees were cut for construction. An epidemic killed seventy-eight percent of workers. In the fifteenth year, the weir was completed, but later broke. Chen Mian served as Governor of Sizhou for three years, overhauling city moats. He died at fifty-seven in the first year of the ordinary period. He was generous and cheerful, giving cotton-padded clothes to poor officials in winter.

Chang Yizhi, with a strong body in youth, followed Xuanxu on expeditions. When Gaozu's righteous army rose, he was made General of the Auxiliary State. He fought bravely at Qianhuang and Yuquexiao. After Jiankang was pacified, he became General Zhihe and Lord of Ma Youjiahu. As Governor of Zhongli, he defeated Wei invaders. In the sixth year, when Wei armies besieged Zhongli with only 3,000 defenders, Yizhi led resistance, using mud to repair walls damaged by siege engines. He was skilled in archery, killing many enemies. Cao Jingzong's relief army arrived and defeated the Wei forces. Yizhi pursued them to Luokou. He later supervised construction of Jingshan Weir under Chen Mian. He had a generous nature, soothing people's hearts as a general. He was granted the title of Marquis of Yingdao County. He died in October of the fourth year of Xuanbi's reign, with Gaozu deeply regretting his death and issuing a posthumous edict.

Because the terrain in the south was low and humid, he declined to take up the post and moved to serve as the Minister of Huangmen.
Soon Wang Liang became the governor of Jinling. He was honest and fair and had good political measures.
Emperor Qi Ming was the prime minister at that time. After hearing about it, he praised him and recommended him as the leader of the army. He was highly appreciated and accepted.
When Emperor Ming of Qi came to the throne, Wang Liang was moved to the crown prince's concubine, Shangshu Libu Lang. He was famous for explaining things clearly and clearly, and he was also moved to serve in the palace.

Jiang Yan, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng, Jiyang. He was lonely and impoverished in his youth but diligent, studious, and reserved. He began his official career as an appointee in Southern Xuzhou and later served at the imperial court. He followed Prince Jingsu of Song Jianping to southern Yanzhou. When Guangling Magistrate Guo Yanwen was convicted, Jiang Yan was imprisoned. From prison, he wrote a letter to Jingsu, pleading his innocence and loyalty, citing historical examples of unjust suffering. He described his humble origins and sincere service, lamenting that slander had led to his imprisonment. He begged for mercy, and Jingsu, moved by the letter, released him that day.

Jiang Yan was soon promoted and served in various posts, including as a scholar in Southern Xuzhou and Zuo Changshi of Baling Kingdom. When Jingsu became governor of Jingzhou, Jiang Yan followed him. As Jingsu grew arrogant and plotted rebellion, Jiang Yan repeatedly advised him against it, warning of historical disasters. Jingsu ignored him. When Jingsu was stationed in Beijing, Jiang Yan served in the army and governed Nandonghai. He wrote fifteen poems to satirize Jingsu’s schemes. After a dispute over county governance, Jingsu had Jiang Yan demoted to Jian'an Wuxingling, where he served for three years.

When Qi Yi came to power, he recruited Jiang Yan as Shangshu Jiabulang. During Shen Youzhi’s rebellion, Emperor Gao consulted Jiang Yan, who analyzed the strengths of the emperor and the weaknesses of the rebels, predicting victory. Emperor Gao was pleased and entrusted Jiang Yan with drafting military documents. Jiang Yan held numerous high offices under Qi, including Hussar Yuzhang Wang Ji's Office, Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and General Xiaoqi. He served as governor of Luling and later returned to the capital as General of Cavalry and Minister Zuocheng. As Censor Zhongcheng, he impeached several officials for negligence and corruption, earning praise from Emperor Ming for his strictness.

Under Emperor Ming, Jiang Yan held positions such as Chief Historian of the Chariot and Linhai King, Shizhong, and Prefect of Xuancheng. During the Yongyuan period, when Cui Huijing besieged the capital, Jiang Yan feigned illness and avoided the rebels, earning admiration for his foresight. He later served as Secretary Supervisor and Guard, though he felt unqualified. He was enfeoffed as Founding Uncle of Linju County. In his later years, he expressed contentment and a desire to retire. He died at age sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him with gifts. Jiang Yan was known for his literary talent in youth but declined in later years. He authored over a hundred works and ten records of "History of Qi."

Ren Fang, courtesy name Yansheng, was a native of Bochang, Le'an. His father was Yao, a doctor of Zhongsan in Qi. Ren Fang was studious and became famous early. At sixteen, he served as chief bookkeeper for Song Danyang Yin Liu Bing. He later held various posts, including Dr. Taichang and chief secretary for Wang Jian. Ren Fang was known for his filial piety, mourning his parents with extreme devotion. He served as a defense officer and secretary of Guan Dong Palace. During Qi Mingdi’s reign, he drafted a memorial declining high honors, citing his inadequacy and the state’s troubles. His refusal angered the emperor, stalling his career.

Ren Fang excelled in writing essays, biographies, and memorials, often composing without revision. He was admired by contemporaries like Xuan. After the dynasty’s fall, he served under Liang, holding posts such as Huangmen Shilang and Minister of Personnel. As governor of Yixing, he lived frugally, eating only wheat. He later served as Censor Zhongcheng and Secretary Supervisor, personally proofreading library titles. As governor of Xin'an, he governed simply, deciding lawsuits on the road. He died in office at age forty-nine, and the people built a shrine for him. The emperor mourned deeply.

Ren Fang was generous with friends, recommending scholars and hosting many guests. He was called "Renjun" for his patronage. Despite poverty, he accumulated over ten thousand books. After his death, the emperor took rare books from his collection. Ren Fang’s writings totaled hundreds of thousands of words. However, after his death, his children were neglected. Liu Xiaobiao wrote an essay criticizing fair-weather friends, describing five types of snobbish acquaintances: those drawn to power, wealth, reputation, shared misfortune, and calculated gain. He lamented that Ren Fang’s former friends abandoned his family.

Yao Cha commented that Jiang Yan and Ren Fang were talented writers of their time. Jiang Yan’s calm and cautious nature allowed him to maintain his reputation, though he relied on prior connections. Ren Fang’s works included 247 volumes of "Miscellaneous Biography," 252 volumes of "Diji," and 33 volumes of articles. His son Seri resembled him and served as Shangshu Waibinglang.
