Wang Gui, courtesy name Weiming, was from Linyi, Langxie. His grandfather Wang Jian was a Taiwei during the Qi Dynasty, and his father Wang Qian served as a doctor. At age eight, Wang Gui lost his biological mother and showed extreme filial piety during mourning, moving Taiwei Xu Xiaosi to tears. His uncle Wang Chen praised him as "my family's horse." By twelve, he understood the Five Classics, and as he grew, he became eloquent and learned. He was promoted as a scholar, served as Secretary Lang, and held various posts including Prince Sheren and Prince Xima. In the twelfth year of Tianjian, he presented the "New Hall Fu" after the Taiji Hall was rebuilt. He served as Secretary Cheng, Prince's Zhongsheren, and other roles. Selected by Xiao Gang, king of Jin'an, as Yunhui to consult and join the army, he later became prefect of Xin'an but resigned due to his father's death. After mourning, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nanchang County and appointed as Minister of Huangmen of Zhongshu. He served the prince alongside others, and Prince Zhaoming treated them with courtesy. At a banquet, Wang Gui noted that making drinking orders had not occurred since the Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo, impressing officials. In the early years of ordinary times, he warned against Chen Qingzhi's Northern Expedition, predicting disaster, which soon came true. In the sixth year, Emperor Gaozu admired his poetic talent at a banquet and appointed him minister. He held various posts, including Minister of the Fifth Army and infantry captain. In the second year of Zhongdatong, he became prefect of Wu County, where he distanced himself from the powerful Rui Zhenzong, leading to a transfer. He resigned due to illness and built a house in Songxi Temple. He died at age forty-five, and the emperor posthumously awarded him titles and gifts. The crown prince mourned him, praising his charm and talent. Wang Gui collected different versions of the "Book of the Later Han" and annotated 200 volumes of the "Sustained Book of Han" and 20 volumes of collected works.

Wang Gui's son Wang Bao, courtesy name Ziyuan, could write at age seven. Grandfather Sikong Yuan Ang praised him as a future distinguished nephew. At twenty, he was promoted as a scholar and served as Secretary Lang, but left due to his father's death. After mourning, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nanchang and held various posts. During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing captured the capital, and Wang Bao stood firm in Ancheng against rebels. In the second year of Dashi, Emperor Shizu summoned him to Jiangling, appointing him General Zhongwu and Internal History of Nanping. He was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Shizhong, then to right servant of Shangshu and Zuopushe. In the third year of Chengsheng, Jiangling was captured, and he surrendered to the Zhou Dynasty. Wang Bao wrote "Young Training" to warn his sons, emphasizing the importance of studying diligently and adhering to Confucian principles while also respecting Taoism and Buddhism. He noted that since the Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo, the three schools had not been annihilated.

Liu Yu, courtesy name Zhongshi, was a seventh-generation descendant of Yin Liu Zhenchang. He was well-behaved and talented, serving as Ning Hailing and later as Prince of Xiangdong to join the army. During the Zuochang period, he helped suppress a rebellion and was favored by Shizu. He served as Minister Zuocheng and Yushi Zhongcheng, and in the second year of Cheng Sheng, he became Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Guozi Jijiu. Zong Mao, courtesy name Yuan, was from a family that moved to Jiangling during the Yongjia Rebellion. He was studious and called "Boy Bachelor." He served as secretary and later as Shangshu Lang, granted the title of Marquis of Xin'an County. In the third year of Chengsheng, Jiangling was captured, and he belonged to the Zhou Dynasty. Wang Cheng, courtesy name Anqi, was proficient in the "Book of Changes" at seven and served as Secretary Lang. He loved Confucian classics and taught students. He served as Guozi Jijiu, and three generations of his family held this position, considered a great honor. He died in Shuyang County at forty-one. He despised powerful people and, along with his brother Wang Zhi, avoided visiting the influential Zhu Yi, earning praise. Chu Xiang, courtesy name Shiju, lost his parents young and became knowledgeable. He served as Secretary Lang and various posts, known for his uprightness and handsome appearance. He died in office at age forty-four, and his cousin Xie Gao wrote an epitaph praising his character. Chu Xiang was filial and once saw a strange light while praying for his mother's illness, which was cured. Xiao Jie, courtesy name Mao Jing, was knowledgeable and good at writing. He served as Prince Sheren and Shangshu Jinbulang, with outstanding political achievements. He was appointed as prefect of Shixing and later as Shaofu Qing. He advised against accepting Hou Jing, warning of his treacherous nature, but Emperor Gaozu did not adopt his advice. Xiao Jie died at seventy-three. Xiao Qia, courtesy name Hongcheng, was smart and loved learning. He served as prefect of Southern Xuzhou, known for his honesty. He died at fifty-five, leaving twenty volumes of collected works. Chu Qiu, courtesy name Zhongbao, was poor but studious. He served as magistrate of Liyang and later as censor Zhongcheng, known for his fairness. He died at seventy. Liu Ru, courtesy name Xiaozhi, could write at seven and was filial. He served as Tai Mo Ling and was admired by Emperor Gaozu. He died at fifty-nine, leaving twenty volumes of collected works. His brothers Liu Lan and Liu Zun were also notable. Liu Qian, courtesy name Xiaoyi, was a generous person who served his widowed sister-in-law respectfully. He died at sixty-seven, leaving twenty volumes of collected works. His brothers Liu Xiaosheng and Liu Xiaowei were also talented. Yin Yun, courtesy name Guanshu, was free-spirited and studious, dying at fifty-nine. Xiao Ji, courtesy name Dexuan, could write at ten and was gentle and self-reliant. He died in office as prefect of Xin'an. The historian comments that these individuals were all famous and showed their talents when opportunities arose.

translation:
The scriptures say: Filial piety is the foundation of virtue.
Filial piety is an important thing for the people, and it is the first thing that a king should do well!
Emperor Gaozu founded the emperor's career and practiced virtue to transform customs. The corrupt and superficial atmosphere was changed, and the rule of governing the country with filial piety was demonstrated.
Every time an edict is issued, more praise is given to those who obey filial piety.
Every family is kind and peaceful, but few people pursue the honor of deceiving the world. It has become a custom to hide one's own talents and not expose them, and everyone hides his achievements that surpass others.
Therefore, not much is seen and heard by people.
Now collect their deeds to complete the story of their disappearance. Teng Tanggong was born in Nanchang, Yuzhang.
When he was five years old, his mother, Yang, contracted a fever and wanted to eat cold melons, but they were not produced locally. Teng Tanggong searched everywhere but could not find them. He felt sad and in great pain.
Soon Teng Tangong met a monk. He was in pain and sorrow among the monks. Teng Tangong told the monk everything.
The monk said: I have two cold melons, and I will give one to you.
After Teng Tan respectfully thanked the monk, he took the melon home and presented it to his mother.
The whole family was very surprised.
Everyone was looking for the monk everywhere, but no one knew where the monk was.
After his parents died, Teng Tanggong did not eat or drink for about ten days. He cried so sadly that he vomited blood, fainted and then woke up.
Teng Tanggong did not wear cotton-padded clothes during the mid-winter season and only ate vegetables throughout his life.
Every time on the anniversary of the death of my parents, I can't bear the longing, and I cry heartbroken day and night.
There were two winter trees outside Teng Tangong's house. Suddenly a divine light appeared from the trees. Soon the image of the Buddha and the guards of honor on both sides appeared. Their appearance was clear. They walked into Teng Tangong's house from the gate. Everyone in the Teng family, big and small, bowed and worshiped the Buddha. It took a long time for the Buddha's image to disappear. Monks and people from far and near preached and performed things.
The prefect Wang Sengqian recommended Teng Tanggong to be a meritorious officer, but Teng Tanggong firmly refused to take up the post.
Wang Jian followed Wang Sengqian in the county at that time, and he called Teng Tanggong Teng Zengzi.
In the first year of Tianjian, Lu Lian was ordered to serve as an envoy to visit various places to understand the customs and conditions of the people. He reported Teng Tangong's filial piety and his response to the gods and Buddhas. Teng Tangong had three sons, all of whom were virtuous and accomplished.
At that time, there was also Xu Puji, a native of Linxiang, Changsha.
He was in mourning and the coffin had not yet been buried. A fire broke out in his neighbor's house and the fire spread to his house. Xu Puji howled and cried bitterly and leaned on the coffin, trying to cover the fire with his body.
Neighbors went to rescue him, but he was roasted until he passed out. It took many days for him to wake up.
There was a girl in Wanling, Xuancheng, who was sleeping in the same bed with her mother. Her mother was caught by a tiger. The girl screamed and grabbed the tiger, and all the tiger hairs were caught by her. After running for more than ten miles, the tiger dropped the girl's mother. The girl carried her mother home, and her mother was still alive. It took an hour before she died.
The prefect Xiao Chen presented gifts to her family to help with the funeral and reported the situation to the emperor.
Shen Chongsu, whose courtesy name is Si Zheng, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
Shen Chongsu's father, Shen Huaiming, served as the governor of Yanzhou during the Song Dynasty.
When Shen Chongsu was six years old, his father died. During the funeral, the ceremony of crying and dancing exceeded the usual ceremony.
When he reached adulthood, he would work as a copywriter to support his mother.
In the early years of Qi Jianwu's reign, Shen Chongsu was recruited from his home to serve in court.
In the late years of Yongyuan, he moved to Situ Xing to join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, he served as the former army king of Poyang and participated in the military affairs.
In the third year of Tianjian, the prefect Liu Pang summoned Shen Chongdai to be the chief bookkeeper.
After Shen Chongsu followed Liu Pan to the county town, he went home to pick up his mother. Her mother passed away.
Shen Chongsu wanted to express his filial piety by dying because he had not been able to serve his sick mother. He couldn't get enough water and rice. He howled and cried day and night for more than ten days, and was about to die.
The brothers said to him: "The funeral ceremony has not yet been carried out. To suddenly mutilate yourself so quickly is not the way to fulfill your filial piety wholeheartedly."
Shen Chongsu then went to the place where his mother was buried. No matter whether it rained or snowed, he lay on the grave and cried bitterly.
Every night, ferocious beasts often came and looked at him from a distance, making sounds like sighs.
Because Shen Chongsu's family was poor and could not afford to rebury her, she begged others and it took a long time to rebury her mother.
Soon Shen Chongsu built a straw hut next to his mother's tomb. He thought that the funeral etiquette held at the time was incomplete, so he kept the mourning for another three years after the reburial.
For a long time, I only ate wheat crumbs, without salt or vinegar, and sat and slept on straw mats. As a result, my whole body was swollen and I couldn't move.
The county reported his extremely filial conduct.
When Emperor Gaozu heard about this situation, he sent people from Zhongshushe to comfort and encourage him. So an edict was issued saying: Shen Chongsu, a former soldier who joined the military, had been ambitious and moral since he was a child. During the period of mourning, his grief exceeded common courtesy.
The mourning for my mother was not over yet and I could not hold a grand funeral. I thought that the etiquette of the mourning was lacking because of the many years of begging. I wanted to use the long days of longing for my loved ones as the beginning of a second mourning.
Although this kind of sentiment is worthy of sympathy, it is clearly stipulated in the etiquette.
He should be asked immediately to remove his mourning clothes and be promoted to the post of prince's horse washer.
The door panel is decorated with banners to encourage this custom.
Shen Chongdai obeyed Shao's order and took off his mourning clothes, but he mourned and cried as if he was still in mourning. He resolutely refused and refused to accept the official position.
Thinking that he could not support his parents with his salary, he became even more sad when he thought about this. He could not bear the grief, so he died in Yongning County at the age of thirty-nine.
Xunjiang, also known as Wenshi, was born in Yingyin. He was the ninth generation descendant of Xun Xu, the Taibao of Jin Dynasty.
Xun Jiang's grandfather, Xun Qiong, avenged his father in the Chengdu market when he was fifteen years old, and was therefore famous for his filial piety.
In the late years of the Song and Yuan Dynasties, Xunjiang crossed the river and rushed to King Wuling to join the rebel army. He was killed by the culprit's pursuers. The imperial court awarded him the posthumous title of Yuanwai Sanqi Shilang.
Xun Fachao, the father of Xunjiang, was appointed as Anfu Ling in the late years of Zhongxing in Qi Dynasty, and died while serving.
When the bad news reached the Xun family, Xunjiang howled and cried bitterly. He passed out and his whole body was cold. He didn't wake up until night.
Not long after, Xunjiang went to mourn. Every time he stayed by the river, the business travelers who came and went couldn't bear to hear his mournful cries.
Before the mourning was over, Xun Fei, Xun Jiang's brother, was recruited from home to serve as the governor of Yulin. When he was conquering the slang bandits, he was shot by a stray arrow and died in the battle.
When the coffin was brought back, Xunjiang went to Yuzhang to greet him. He saw the boat carrying the coffin from a distance and jumped into the water. People on both sides rushed to rescue him and barely rescued him.
After the coffin arrived home, he could not be buried on time because his family was poor, so he mourned for his father and brother and did not step out of the mourning hut for four years.
After the mourning began, Xunjiang stopped combing and washing his hair, and all his hair fell out.
He cried without timing, his voice became hoarse and then he cried silently, his eye sockets were all rotten, his body was haggard and emaciated, and he was so skinny that even his family no longer recognized him.
The prefectures and counties reported this situation to the court, and Gaozu Xiashao sent Zhongshushe to remove his mourning clothes and promoted him to the Zuo Changshi of the Yuzhang Kingdom.
Although Xunjiang had removed his mourning clothes, he was even more sad and haggard.
His grandfather Sun Qian told him: Your Majesty governs the world with filial piety, and your conduct exceeds that of the ancients, so I issued an edict to remove you from obedience and promote you to this position.
Not only is your father's order irresistible, but it will also make you famous in future generations. It's not just your reputation that will be made famous!
Xunjiang then accepted the official position.
In the end, he died at home due to grief and physical damage. He died at the age of twenty-one.
Yu Qianlou's courtesy name is Zizhen, a new savage.
Yu Yi, the father of Yu Qian Lou, was recruited as the chief secretary of Situ. He refused to take office, so he was famous.
Yu Qianlou was eager to learn since he was a child. He often discussed and recited the "Book of Filial Piety" with others. He never blushed in front of others because he couldn't answer an answer. Nanyang Gaoshi Liu Qiu and Zong Chai thought he was a genius and praised him greatly.
Yu Qianlou was recruited from his home to serve as the governor of the state, and moved to Pingxi to join the army.
He was also appointed as the county magistrate and had special achievements in governing the county.
Before Zuo Moyuan took office as county magistrate, there were many incidents of tigers injuring people and animals in the county. After Yu Qianlou took office, all the tigers crossed the river to Linju County. At that time, people thought that this was caused by the influence of benevolence and righteousness.
In the early years of Yongyuan of Qi Dynasty, Yu Qianlou was appointed as the magistrate of Xiaoling County. Less than ten days after arriving in the county, Yu Qianlou fell ill at home. Qian Lou suddenly felt frightened and sweated all over. He abandoned his official position and returned home that day. Everyone in his family was surprised by his sudden return.
At that time, Yu Yi had only been ill for two days. The doctor said: If you want to know whether the patient's condition is getting better or worse, just taste the stool to see if it is bitter or sweet.
Yu Yi had diarrhea, so Yu Qianlou tasted the excrement. The smell of the excrement became sweet and smooth, and his heart became more sad and painful.
At night, Yu Qianlou often kowtowed to the North Star and prayed, asking to replace his father with his life.
Soon I heard a voice in the air saying: "Yu Zhengjun's life has expired and cannot be extended any longer. Your sincere prayer has let the gods know that Yu Fengjun's life can only be extended until the end of the month."
At the end of the month, Yu Yi died of illness. During Yu Qianlou's mourning period, his mourning behavior exceeded the common etiquette. He built a thatched cottage next to the tomb and lived in the thatched cottage to mourn.
When Emperor He ascended the throne, he was about to appoint Yu Qianlou, who was in mourning. Xiao Yingzhou, the commander of the town, wrote a letter to persuade him, but Yu Qianlou firmly refused.
After the period of mourning expired, Yu Qianlou was awarded the title of Cao Lang, the Minister of Xitai.
After the Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, Deng Yuan became the governor of Yizhou. He proposed that Yu Qianlou be appointed as the governor of the mansion and the governor of Zitong County in Brazil.
After Chengdu was pacified, the treasures in the city were piled as high as a mountain. Deng Yuanqi distributed all the treasures to his subordinates, but Yu Qianlou took none.
Deng Yuanqi felt uncomfortable with his unsociable behavior and said sternly: Why does Yu Changshi act like this alone?
In order to show that he would not disobey Deng Yuanqi's order, Yu Qianlou asked for a box of books to be distributed to him.
Soon, Yu Qianlou was appointed as the prefect of Shu County. During his tenure, he was upright and honest, and he was praised by the people.
After Deng Yuanqi died in Shu, all his subordinates dispersed. Yu Qianlou personally organized his funeral and escorted his coffin back to his hometown.
After Yu Qianlou returned to Beijing, he was appointed as Shangshu Jinbu Lang, and moved to the Central Army's Report Office to join the army.
After the establishment of the Prince's East Palace, Yu Qianlou served as the Crown Prince's attendant in his original official position, and was highly regarded. The emperor's subordinates, Shao Yu Qianlou and the Prince's concubine Yin Gou, Zhongsheren Daoqia, Guozi doctor Ming Shanbin and others took turns explaining the meaning of the Five Classics to the crown prince every day.
Yu Qianlou moved to Sanqi Shilang and Jingzhou Dazhongzheng.
He died at the age of forty-six.
Ji Feo's courtesy name is Yanxiao, and he is a native of Feng Yilianshao. His family has lived in Xiangyang for generations.
Ji Feo was very filial when he was young.
When he was eleven years old, his biological mother passed away. During the mourning period, Ji Feol was in a state of poverty, almost destroying his life due to grief. His relatives were surprised by his filial piety.
In the early years of Tianjian, Ji Min's father served as the original township magistrate of Wuxing. He was framed by treacherous officials and was arrested and handed over to Tingwei for interrogation.
Ji Feo was fifteen years old at the time. He stood on the thoroughfare and cried, begging the ministers to avenge his father's justice. The passers-by who saw this scene shed tears for him.
Ji Fol's father is theoretically innocent, but he is ashamed of being interrogated by officials, so he bears the guilt out of thin air and will be sentenced to death if convicted.
Ji Fol then rushed outside the court to beat the Dengwen drum set up for people to redress their grievances, and asked to die in his father's place.
Emperor Gaozu felt strange about the incident, and ordered Cai Fadu, the court official, to say: "Ji Feo asked to die to redeem his father's life. Although this kind of friendship is commendable, he is only a young child and may not be able to come up with this idea on his own. You can force him severely and induce him to tell the truth."
Cai Fadu accepted the order of Emperor Gaozu and returned to his own government. He laid out all the instruments of torture and asked his officials to stand in the hall. Then he asked Ji Feo in a stern tone: "You asked to die on behalf of your father. The emperor has issued an order to agree to it. You should be sentenced to death in accordance with the law. But the knife and saw are inflicted on your body and it is very painful. Can you really die? Besides, you are a child and you have not thought of such an idea in your heart. You must have been instigated by others."
Whoever is the instigator's name should be answered one by one.
If you regret it and change your mind, I will listen to you.
Ji Fol replied: Although I am a young and ignorant prisoner, don't I know that death is a scary thing?
It's just that my brothers are young, but I am the older one. I couldn't bear to see my father suffer the death penalty and survive on my own, so I made a decision in my heart, reported my thoughts to the emperor, and begged the emperor.
Now I want to sacrifice my life to save my father and abandon my body to hell. It is not a trivial matter. How can I be instigated by others?
The Emperor is wise and has written a letter to allow me to die in my father's place. To me, this is no different from allowing me to ascend to heaven and become an immortal. How can I regret it?
Cai Fadu knew that Ji Ce had a sincere heart to die on his father's behalf and could not force him to give in. So he used a kind and pleasant look to persuade Ji Feo and said: The emperor knows that your father is not guilty and will be pardoned and released soon.
Seeing that you are intelligent and beautiful, you can be regarded as an outstanding child. If you change your original situation, you will be lucky enough to be rescued together with your son. Why do you have to seek the pain of torture at this young age?
Ji Feo replied: All fish and ants still cherish their own lives, let alone humans, who would be willing to be shattered into pieces.
Just because my father was guilty of a serious crime and must be executed according to law, I thought about dying myself, hoping to prolong my father's life.
Now I close my eyes and stretch my neck, waiting for the beheading and display of the corpse. I have expressed all my feelings and have nothing more to say.
When Ji Fol was first imprisoned, the jailer put handcuffs on his legs and feet in accordance with the law. Cai Fadu took pity on him and ordered the jailer to remove his handcuffs and wear a small instrument of torture.
Ji Fol refused to comply. He said: Ji Fol asked to die on behalf of his father, who was a prisoner sentenced to death. The instruments of torture for death row prisoners should only be made heavier, how can they be made lighter?
In the end, he refused to remove the shackles.
Cai Fadu reported the whole situation to Gaozu, who then forgave Ji Fe's father.
Danyang Yin Wangzhi visited Jifu and asked him to stay in Danyang. He wanted to recommend him to the court as an outstanding person with filial piety at the beginning of the second year.
Ji Feo said: Wang Yin is so weird. Why do you think that I, Ji Feo, are so shallow?
If the father is humiliated, the son should die. Morality should be like this. If I accept Wang Yin's recommendation with a thick face and no shame, it will be to gain fame through my father. What a shame.
Ji Fei rejected Wang Zhi's request.
When Ji Fol was seventeen years old, he was called up to be the chief registrar of the state.
He was released from prison in Wannian County and served as county magistrate for one year. His education moved the people and benevolence and righteousness prevailed.
Ji Feo returned to Ying from Yong, and Liu Chen, the governor of Xiangzhou, summoned Ji Feo to take charge of the book.
Later, Pei Jian, a fellow countryman of Ji Ce, Danyang Yin Cheng Zang Dun, Yangzhou Zhongzheng Zhang Ping and others jointly recommended Ji Fe, thinking that he was filial, sincere and sincere, and he was proficient in "Yi" and "Laozi".
The emperor ordered Taichang to be commended and recommended.
At first, Ji Fol suffered from heart palpitations because his father was falsely accused of guilt, and later died of heart palpitations.
Zhen Tian, ​​courtesy name Yanyue, was born in Wuji, Zhongshan, and had lived in Jiangling for generations.
Zhen Tian's grandfather, Zhen Qinzhi, was appointed Chang Ningling.
His father selected him and Renzhou engaged in it.
Zhen Tian's father passed away when he was only a few years old. He was as sad and painful as an adult.
The family felt sorry for his young age and fed him rice with broth, but Zhen Tian refused to eat it.
When he was eight years old, he asked his mother about his biological father. He felt sorry for not remembering his father's image, so he cried sadly for several days. Suddenly, he seemed to see someone. The appearance of this person was his father. People at the time thought that this was filial piety that moved the gods.
His family is poor, but he feeds his mother with delicious dishes.
During the mourning time, a thatched cottage was built next to the tomb in the villa area. Black and yellow birds of various colors often gathered in the trees next to the thatched cottage. When Zhen Tian cries, the birds chirp, and when Zhen Tian stops crying, the chirping of the birds stops.
There was also a white sparrow perched on his thatched cottage.
Xiao Dan, the king of Shixing in the state, came to report Zhen Tian's virtue and performance.
The emperor went down to Shao and said: I admire sages with all my heart, think about my dreams all day long, and issue edicts to ministers from all over the world. I must do my best to search for, recommend and commend them.
Zhen Tian's filial piety is particularly outstanding, and her reputation is well-known in her hometown. This has many benefits for the honest and honest folk customs.
The magistrate presented the dispatches just as I saw them with my own eyes.
His whole family should be commended and he should be given a title.
Zhen Tian was appointed an official and went to Annan to join the army.
Han Huaiming, a member of the Shangdang Party, lived in Jingzhou.
When he was ten years old, Han Huaiming's mother suffered from tuberculosis, and each attack was often dangerous.
Han Huaiming was kowtowing and praying under the starry sky at night. It was very cold at that time. He suddenly smelled the fragrance. Someone in the air said to him: Little child, your mother will recover permanently in a while, and you don’t have to worry about it anymore.
Before dawn, his mother's illness had recovered.
The fellow villagers were surprised by this.
When Han Huaiming was fifteen years old, his father passed away. He was extremely sad during the funeral, almost to the point of destroying his life. He piled dirt on his back and made a grave, and did not accept any gifts or help from others.
After the mourning period expired, he and his fellow villager Guo Mo went to Nanyang to worship Liu Qiu as their teacher.
Liu Qiu once stopped teaching one day and was alone, crying sadly.
Han Huaiming secretly asked others why Liu Qiu was sad and alone. Liu Qiu's family replied: Today is the death anniversary of my grandfather's death.
Liu Qiu's mother had also died at that time.
When Han Huaiming heard about this, he stopped studying that day and went home to support his mother.
Liu Qiu sighed and said: Han Sheng no longer has the regret of not being able to support his parents like Qiu Wuzi.
Han Huaiming's family was poor, so he often tried his best to provide his mother with delicious food, and often laughed at his mother's side to make her happy. He would not leave his mother's side all day long.
When his mother was ninety-one years old, she passed away. Han Huaiming was deprived of water and food for ten days, howling and crying incessantly.
A pair of white doves built a nest on the thatched cottage where he was mourning. They laid eggs and raised small birds. They were very close to people, just like poultry. The white doves did not leave until the mourning period of Han Huaiming was over.
After the mourning period expired, Han Huaiming only ate vegetarian food for the rest of his life and did not change his clothes.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xiao Qi, the governor of Shixing, went to the court to commemorate Han Huaiming's filial piety.
Han Huaiming was called up many times by the state capital, but Han Huaiming failed to do so and died at home.
Liu Tanjing, courtesy name Yuanguang, was born in Lu County, Pengcheng.
Liu Tanjing's grandfather, Liu Yuanzhen, served as the prefect of Huainan and was convicted while serving in the county. Liu Tanjing's father, Liu Huijing, went to the court ministers to plead for mercy one by one. His feelings were sad and pitiful, and his words were very sincere, so he became famous for his filial piety.
Liu Tanjing practiced filial piety and possessed the character of his father.
Liu Tanjing first became an official and served as the Zuo Changshi of the Ancheng Kingdom. His father died in the county. He went to attend the funeral and did not eat or drink for many days. He fainted and regained consciousness many times.
Every time I cried, I cried until I vomited blood.
After the mourning period expired, he became thin and sick due to excessive grief during the mourning period.
It happened that the emperor issued the Shao Order, instructing the gentry to recommend talents according to four subjects. Liu Tanjing's uncle Liu Huifei recommended Liu Tanjing to be a filial scholar, and Gaozu appointed Liu Tanjing as the Haining Order.
Because his brother had not yet obtained the post of county magistrate, Liu Tanjing gave up the order of Haining to his brother, and the court then appointed him to join the army for the Anxi expedition.
After Liu Tanjing's father died, he served his mother with utmost sincerity and filial piety. He cooked the rice and porridge himself and did not leave the chores to others.
When his mother was sick, he took care of her day and night without taking any clothes off.
After his mother died, he went without food or water for nearly ten days.
His mother's coffin was temporarily buried at Yaowang Temple. The weather was cold at that time. Liu Tanjing, wearing single clothes, built a thatched cottage at the place where the coffin was buried to observe the mourning. He cried continuously day and night, and his grief moved everyone on the way. Within a year, Liu Tanjing himself passed away.
He Jiong, courtesy name Shiguang, was born in Dan County, Lujiang.
His father, He Huan, served as a doctor in Taizhong.
When He Jiong was fifteen years old, he followed his brother He Yin in his profession, and within one year he read through the general outline of the Five Classics.
He Jiong has fair skin and handsome appearance. His cousins ​​He Qiu and He Dian often praise him and say: "Wei Niushi has a clear mind, and Du Hongzhi has a beautiful appearance. Now when I look at the child, I seem to see Wei and Du again."
He Jiong often yearned for a quiet and retired life and was not willing to enter an official career.
He Jiongtang's uncle He Changyu said to him: "Why do you want to live in seclusion? You should not behave like this again."
Moreover, every gentleman has his own way of becoming an official and retiring from office.
When Yu Yan was nineteen years old, he became an official for the first time and held the owner's book.
He was recommended as a scholar, and was successively promoted to the royal palace to join the army, Shangshu Bing, and the second caolang of the Treasury.
He left the capital and served as Yongkang Ling, and was famous for his harmonious handling of affairs.
He returned to Beijing and served as the internal record office of Renwei Nankang King, and moved to the post of official secretary and censor.
Because his father was ill, He Jiong stayed naked for more than ten days without combing or washing his hair. He was busy serving his father. In two or three nights, his appearance suddenly changed a lot.
After his father passed away, He Jiong howled and cried constantly, sitting and lying on the ground, and sleeping with his head on the earth. As a result, his waist and kidneys were weak and his feet were swollen. Eventually, his body was destroyed by excessive grief and he died.
Yu Shami, a native of Yingyin.
The sixth generation grandson of Jin Si Kong Yubing.
His father, Yu Peiyu, served as the official governor of the state and the internal history of Changsha. During the reign of Emperor Shengming of the Song Dynasty, he was executed for being convicted of Yu Shami's affair. Yu Shami had just been born at that time.
When Yu novice was five years old, his biological mother made him a minor's dress, but he often refused to wear it. When his mother asked him why he refused to wear it, he answered with tears: Our family has suffered a tragic disaster, what's the use of sending things away!
After growing up, he wore civilian clothes and ate a vegetarian diet throughout his life.
Yu Shami was recruited from his family to serve as the Zuo Changshi of the Linchuan Kingdom, and moved to the Central Army Tian Caoxing to join the army.
When his aunt passed away and fell ill, Yu novice stayed by her side morning and evening, undressed, and sometimes needed acupuncture treatment, so Yu novice would test it on his own body first.
After his aunt's death, he had no food or drink for many days. Until the period of mourning is over, he does not take off his mourning clothes and does not leave the gate of the mourning hut. He howls and cries day and night, and the neighbors cannot bear to hear his cry.
My aunt's tomb was built in the new forest, and then there were more than a hundred unplanted pine trees growing beside the tomb.
Yu Yong, the official minister of the capital of Yushami tribe, reported Yushami's filial piety and recommended him to the subject of pure filial piety. Emperor Gaozu summoned Yushami, commended him for his filial piety, and appointed him as the replacement magistrate of She County.
After returning to Kyoto, he was given a light chariot by King Shaoling to join the military, and he followed King Shaoling in the palace of Kuaiji.
When his biological mother died again, Yu novice escorted the coffin back to the capital. When crossing Zhejiang, the ship encountered a strong wind in the center of Zhejiang and almost sank. Yu novice hugged his biological mother's coffin and howled bitterly. After a while, the wind dried up and the sea calmed down. This was probably because his filial piety moved the gods.
After the mourning period expired, Yu Shami was awarded the title of Xinwei Penal Prison and joined the army and Danyang County Koukou. He was repeatedly promoted to Ningyuan Lushi, joined the army, and was transferred to Sima.
He served as the Great Wall Order and died.
Jiang Yu, whose courtesy name is Hanjie, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang.
His father, Jiang Bei, served as doctor Guanglu.
Jiang Bian had a filial nature since he was a child. When he was thirteen years old, his father suffered from an eye disease. Jiang Biao served his sick father for nearly a year without taking off his clothes.
He dreamed of a monk at night who said: People suffering from eye diseases will definitely be cured by drinking Eye Wisdom Water.
Jiang Pu woke up and told the story, but no one could explain the meaning of "Hui Yan Shui".
Jiang Pu's third uncle Liao Zheng had a good relationship with Master Zhizhe of Caotang Temple, so he went to consult Master Zhizhe.
Master Wise said: "The Infinite Life Sutra" says: The wise eye sees the truth and can cross to the other side.
Jiang Hao followed the inspiration of the wise master and dedicated a house in Niutun, Tongxia County, as a temple, asking God to give him a good name.
The imperial edict replied: A loyal minister and a filial son are responsive everywhere.
Yan Han of the Jin Dynasty finally saw the medicine sent from the underworld.
I met a wise man recently and learned that your second son had a dream because of his sincerity, saying that he wanted to drink the water of wisdom.
Wisdom Eye is the name of one of the five eyes. If you want to build a temple, you can use Wisdom Eye as the name of the temple.
When they built the temple, they discovered an old well with clear water, which was different from ordinary spring water.
Jiang Bei took water from the well to wash her eyes and boil medicine according to what Jiang Xia saw in her dream. She gradually felt better and her eye disease was cured.
People at that time thought this was an expression of filial piety.
The King of Nankang was the governor of Southern Xuzhou, and he summoned Pi to be the chief official.
Dou Mian is quiet by nature, likes the mystical words of "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi", is especially proficient in the essence of Buddhism, and is not willing to enter an official career.
After his father passed away, Jiang Huai built a thatched cottage next to his father's tomb, howling and crying all day long. More than a month later, Jiang Pu also passed away.
Liu Ji, courtesy name Shiju, was from Pingyuan.
His grandfather Liu Chengmin was the governor of Jizhou during the Song Dynasty.
His father, Liu Wenwei, was a member of the imperial family during the Qi Dynasty.
When Liu Ji was nine years old, he could recite "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and his relatives were surprised by his talent.
When he was fourteen years old, his father died. Liu Ji had a natural sense of filial piety and cried until he vomited blood every time.
The family was poor, so Liu Ji and his younger brothers Liu Yao and Liu Di encouraged each other and devoted themselves to study.
After growing up, Liu Ji has been involved in a wide range of subjects and is knowledgeable and talented.
During the Tianjian period, Liu Ji was recruited from his home to serve at the court's invitation. He was gradually promoted to Xuanhui and joined the army in Jin'an Palace.
He also went to Beijing and served as Minister of Host and Guest. Within a year, he was appointed as the Order of Haiyan.
Liu Ji served as magistrate of two counties. During his tenure, he was known for his harmonious handling of affairs.
When he returned to the capital, he was appointed as Jian Kangzheng, but he did not like the position. He was soon dismissed because of illness.
Soon he was awarded the Jiankang Order, but he did not accept the appointment.
Liu Ji's mother, Mingshi, fell ill. Liu Ji was already fifty years old at that time. He served his mother untiedly for seventy days and recited the "Avalokiteśvara Sutra" ten thousand times. At night, he had a dream due to emotion. In his dream, he saw a monk saying to him: My wife's life span has been exhausted. With your sincerity and sincerity, I will extend your wife's life for you.
Liu Ji's mother passed away more than sixty years later.
Liu Ji built a thatched hut next to his mother's grave to mourn. His grief exceeded common courtesy.
There is often a pair of white cranes flying docilely beside the thatched cottage.
Ruan Xiaoxu, a virgin, wrote to him to comfort and enlighten him. But Liu Ji still missed his deceased mother endlessly, and died before the mourning was over. He died at the age of fifty-two.
Liu Ji is the author of eight volumes of "Explanation of Common Sayings" and ten volumes of collected works.
The deeds of his younger brother Liu Yao are in "The Biography of Literature", and the deeds of Liu Di are in "The Biography of Chu Shi".
Chu Xiu was a native of Qiantang, Wu County.
His father, Chu Zhongdu, was proficient in "The Book of Changes" and his knowledge was the most profound at that time.
During the Tianjian period, Chu Zhongdu successively served as a doctor of "Five Classics".
Chu Xiu inherited his father's studies since he was a child. He was also proficient in "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius". He was good at writing letters and articles.
Chu Xiu initially served as the minister of the Xiangshu Kingdom, and gradually moved to the Qingche Xiangdong Prefecture to join the army, and also served as an assistant to the emperor.
King Wuling was appointed as the governor of Laoye, and he was recommended! He was succeeded by Xuanhui and joined the army, and was limited to the internal record office.
Chou Kai was a very filial man by nature. When his father died, he grieved beyond the ordinary limits, which damaged his body and suffered from Qi reversal.
When his mother died, he couldn't eat or drink for twenty-three days, falling into unconsciousness and waking up again and again. He often howled and cried so hard that he vomited blood and eventually died from excessive physical weakness.
Xie Lin, whose courtesy name is Xiru, was born in Yangxia, Chen County.
He is the eighth generation grandson of Jin Taifu Xie An.
Xie Lin's father, Xie Jing, was appointed Beizhonglang to consult and join the army.
When Xie Lin was five years old, whenever her parents had not eaten yet, her wet nurse would ask Xie Lin to eat first. Xie Lin said, "I don't feel hungry yet."
Even if he is forced to do so, he still refuses to eat.
When his uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard about this, he praised him and said: "If you leave your children at home, you are like Zengzi, and if you serve the king, you are like Lin Sheng."
So he was named Lin.
Gradually he was taught to read classics and history books, and Xie Lin could recite them just by looking at them.
Ruan Xiaoxu always said that Xie Lin was the Wei Yangyuan of our family.
When Xie Lin was mourning for his father, he howled and cried day and night. His body was weakened by grief, and only a skeleton was left in his body. Xie Lin's mother, Ruan, often watched over him in person, comforted and enlightened him.
After the mourning period expired, Xiao Zihao, the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, presented a memorial to Xie Lin Duhou for his filial piety, and promoted him to join the army as the royal family's Fa Caoxing. He was repeatedly promoted to join the army in the foreign military record office.
At that time, nectar fell in the Shilin Pavilion, and Xie Lin wrote an ode and presented it. Emperor Gaozu highly praised it, so he ordered Xie Lin to write the "Stele of Xiao Kai's Dezheng, the Governor of Northern Yanzhou".
In the first year of the Taiqing Dynasty, Xie Lin moved to serve as the minister of Sanqi and the regular servant of Sanqi, and was sent as an envoy to Wei.
Just when Hou Jinglue surrendered, there was a war on the border. Xie Lin's mother was worried that Xie Lin would not be able to return and would contract the disease and die.
Xie Lin completed his appointment and returned to the country. He had an ominous dream that night, and the next morning he submitted a petition to impeach himself and hurried back.
When he rushed home, he howled and cried so much that he vomited blood. He was unconscious for a long time and couldn't eat any water or rice.
Relatives and friends were worried about his accident and cried bitterly to him, reluctantly persuading him to drink porridge and soup.
Xie Lin reluctantly accepted it at first, but in the end he couldn't eat it anymore. After more than a month, when he was crying one night, Xie Lin also passed away. He was thirty-eight years old when he died.
There are dozens of poems, poems and odes composed by Xie Lin.
Gao Chai, Zhong You, Zeng Shen, and Min Sun followed the saints and received teachings. They were pious and respectful and observed filial piety. There is no water in the mouth, and I cry and vomit blood all year round. Didn’t Zeng Shen and others understand that their parents were deeply hurt when their parents died? Didn’t they know that the feelings of filial son who cannot be raised forever and who are deeply missed like the poem "Polygonium" recited created what people said was that the ancestors established the etiquette and the sages followed it respectfully.
As for Ruqiu and Wu, they eventually lost their lives due to grief.
People like Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Yu, and Xie Lin must have the same ambitions as Qiu and Wu!
summary:
Filial piety as the foundation of virtue, emphasizing its importance for both the people and rulers. Emperor Gaozu promoted filial piety through edicts, transforming customs and encouraging virtuous behavior. The text then recounts the deeds of several individuals known for their exceptional filial piety.

Teng Tanggong, from Nanchang, demonstrated filial piety at age five by seeking cold melons for his ill mother, which a monk miraculously provided. After his parents' deaths, he mourned excessively, refusing food and warm clothing. Divine signs, including a vision of Buddha, appeared at his home. He refused official positions and was praised as "Teng Zengzi."

Xu Puji, from Linxiang, protected his mother's coffin from a fire, suffering severe burns. A girl from Wanling fought a tiger to save her mother, carrying her home before she died. Shen Chongsu, from Wuxing, mourned his mother with extreme grief, lying on her grave in all weather. Despite an imperial edict promoting him, he refused the position and died from grief at age thirty-nine.

Xunjiang, from Yingyin, mourned his father and brother with such intensity that he lost his hair and eyesight. He was promoted by imperial decree but died at twenty-one from grief. Yu Qianlou, from Xinye, tasted his father's excrement to check his health and prayed to die in his father's place. He served as an honest official, refusing treasures, and died at forty-six.

Ji Feo, from Xiangyang, begged to die for his father, who was falsely accused. At fifteen, he beat the Dengwen drum and faced torture without flinching. His father was pardoned, but Ji Feo later died from heart palpitations. Zhen Tian, from Jiangling, mourned his father from childhood, with birds responding to his cries. He was commended by the emperor and appointed to a military post.

Han Huaiming, from Jingzhou, prayed for his mother's recovery and heard a divine voice. He mourned his father excessively and served his mother with devotion. White doves nested at his mourning hut. He refused official posts and died at home. Liu Tanjing, from Pengcheng, mourned his father with vomiting blood and later served his mother with care, dying within a year of her death.

He Jiong, from Lujiang, served his ill father without rest, changing appearance drastically. He died from grief after his father's death. Yu Shami, from Yingyin, refused fine clothes due to family tragedy. He served his aunt with devotion, and pine trees grew at her tomb. He was commended for filial piety and died in office.

Jiang Yu, from Kaocheng, served his blind father, dreaming of "Wisdom Eye Water." He built a temple where an old well appeared, curing his father's eyes. He mourned his father excessively and died. Liu Ji, from Pingyuan, mourned his father with vomiting blood and served his mother, reciting sutras. White cranes appeared at his mourning hut. He died before mourning ended at fifty-two.

Chu Xiu, from Qiantang, mourned his parents with extreme grief, fasting for twenty-three days and dying from weakness. Xie Lin, from Yangxia, refused food before his parents ate. He mourned his father excessively and later his mother, dying from grief at thirty-eight. The text concludes by comparing these individuals to ancient filial exemplars like Zeng Shen, noting that some, like Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Yu, and Xie Lin, died from grief, similar to Ruqiu and Wu.

translation:
Wei Can, whose courtesy name is Changxi, is the grandson of Wei Rui, the cavalry general, and the son of Wei Gan, the governor of Northern Xuzhou.
Wei Can has the demeanor of his father, loves to learn, is willful, eight feet tall, and tall.
He first became an official and served as the king of Jin'an in Yunhui and joined the army. Soon he acted as Fa Cao and moved to join the army as a foreign soldier and concurrently as a Chinese soldier.
At that time, Ying! Yu Zhongrong and Wu Jun Zhang Shu were both well-known figures in the past. They were colleagues with Wei Can and had become close friends with each other.
The king of Jin'an moved to be the governor of Yongzhou, and Wei Can also followed the palace and was transferred to the record office, but his position as a military soldier remained unchanged.
King Jin'an was established as the crown prince, and Wei Can was moved to the rank of infantry captain. He entered the court and served as the leader of the East Palace. He resigned when his father died.
Soon he was reinstated as General Zhaoyuan. The army was appointed as the leader.
After the mourning period expired, he inherited the title of Marquis of Yongchang County and was appointed as a consultant to the king of Anxi and Xiangdong. He was repeatedly promoted to the prince's servant, led by Zuowei, and his position as leader remained unchanged.
Because Wei Can had an old friendship with the crown prince, he was often appointed to positions close to him. Although his position changed many times, he often stayed in the palace and served as a guard, which was quite prestigious. Moreover, Wei Can had an unruly and arrogant personality, so the celebrities at the time felt deeply unfair.
The right guard general Zhu Yi once said to Wei Can in a stern voice during a banquet: How can you put on the face of a leader and face others!
In the 11th year of Datong in Central China, Wei Can was moved to serve as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi. Before he took office, he left the capital to serve as the governor, supervising the military affairs of Hengzhou, general Anyuan, and governor of Hengzhou.
The Crown Prince came out of the palace and was farewelling the boy. He took Wei Can's hand and said, "You and I won't be apart for a long time."
In the first year of Taiqing, not long after Wei Can arrived in Hengzhou, he petitioned to be dismissed.
In the second year, the imperial court recruited Wei Can as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
Wei Can returned to the capital and walked to Luling. When he heard about Hou Jing's rebellion, he selected 5,000 elite soldiers and 100 horses from his subordinates, and rushed to the capital day and night to rescue him.
When they arrived in Yuzhang, a messenger reported: The rebels have arrived at Hengjiang. Wei Can immediately went to the internal historian Liu Xiaoyi to discuss countermeasures.
Liu Xiaoyi said: If this is really the case, there should be another order. How can one send an envoy credulously and act in panic? Maybe this is not the case.
At that time, Liu Xiaoyi was giving a banquet to entertain Wei Can. Wei Can became angry, threw the cup on the ground and said: The rebels have crossed the river and are about to invade the capital. All water and land routes have been cut off. Where will there be messengers to return the favor? If the order is not issued, can you feel at ease?
How can I, Wei Can, think about drinking now?
After saying that, he immediately rode out and deployed his troops to prepare for departure. Just as Xiao Daxin, the governor of Dangyang in Jiangzhou, sent an envoy to invite Wei Can, Wei Can rode to see Xiao Daxin and said: Among the vassal towns in the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, only Jiang maggot is the closest to the capital. Considering the situation of His Highness, it is really necessary to go to the rescue first; but the position in the middle reaches is important, and your task of garrisoning Jiangzhou is important. Others also need your support to rescue the capital. Wei Guo cannot be left unattended.
Now you just need to bluff, move troops to guard Huancheng, and then send a general to follow me, and the affair will be done.
Xiao Zuozhi thought he was right, so he sent Liu Xin, a middle soldier, to lead two thousand soldiers to follow Wei Can.
Wei Can left all his family members behind and set off in a light boat.
When they arrived in Nanzhou, Wei Can's cousin Liu Zhongli, the governor of Sizhou, also led more than 10,000 infantry and cavalry to Hengjiang. Wei Can immediately sent him food and weapons, and distributed his personal money and cloth to reward Liu Zhongli's soldiers.
Prior to this, Anbei general Poyang Wang Xiaofan also sent Pei Zhigao, the governor of Western Yuzhou, and his eldest son Pei Si from Hefei to lead the Jiangxi troops to the capital and stationed at Zhang Gongzhou, waiting for the arrival of reinforcements from upstream.
When he was dispatched, Pei Zhigao sent a boat to pick up Liu Zhongli's army from the Liao Dynasty, and joined him to garrison in Wangyouyuan.
Wei Can proposed that Liu Zhongli should be elected as the commander-in-chief and inform the armies downstream.
But Pei Zhigao thought that he was older and more respected than Liu Zhongli, so he said: "Liu Jiexia is already the governor of a state, why should I appoint him?"
So we discussed all day long and could not make a decision.
Wei Can angrily said to the generals: Now we are going to the national crisis together with the purpose of wiping out the rebels. The reason I propose to recommend Liu Sizhou is because he has been guarding the border for a long time. Hou Jing has long been afraid of him. Moreover, Liu Sizhou has strong soldiers and horses, and no one can surpass him.
In terms of official position, he is below me, and in terms of age, he is younger than me. This is just because considering the fate of the country, we can no longer care about these things.
In the current situation, the most important thing is the harmony between the generals; if people's hearts are not in harmony, the country's affairs will be over.
Duke Pei is a well-respected veteran of the imperial court, and he is highly respected. How could he sabotage the rescue plan out of selfish motives?
Please allow me to remove this obstacle for you.
So Wei Can took a small boat to Pei Zhigao's military camp and sternly rebuked Pei Zhigao, saying: A few days ago, the generals recommended Liu Sizhou as the governor.
If you must have two minds, I will only fight you with a sword.
Pei Zhigao cried and said: I have been favored by the country, so I should naturally take the lead. I just hate that I am old and weak and cannot serve the country. I hope to work with Liu Shixing to eradicate the traitors. I think everyone's ideas have been implemented and there is no need to wait for me to make a decision.
If you must suspect that I have other ideas, I can show you my heart.
So the generals jointly made a decision, and Liu Zhongli was able to lead the troops.
Shan Shan led his troops and was stationed in Xinting, while the rebels set up a battle formation at Zhongxing Temple. The two sides held a stalemate until night, and each of them withdrew their troops and returned to their camp.
On the night of Qiantian, Liu Zhongli came to the military camp of Huangsai to deploy his troops and prepare for the next day's battle. The generals each guarded one side. Liu Zhongli ordered Wei Can to garrison Qingtang.
Wei Can faced the middle of the Qingtang. Wei Can considered that the fence and fortress had not been built yet, and the rebels would definitely come to fight for it, so he was quite worried. He said to Liu Zhongli: I don't have the ability to resist foreign enemies, I just want to die for my country. I hope you will use your talents appropriately and avoid any losses due to improper employment.
Liu Zhongli said: "I am building a camp fence in Yishan, close to the entrance. I want all the grain storage vehicles and ships to dock there." This is a big deal, and it must be borne by you, brother.
If you are worried about the lack of troops, I can send more troops to help you.
So he sent General Liu Shuyin of Zhihe to lead his army to help Wei Ken. They led their troops to march together by land and water.
At that time, there was a heavy fog, and the soldiers lost their way. When they arrived at Qingtang, it was already past midnight, and the camp fence was not completed until dawn.
Hou Jing climbed to the attic of Chanling Temple and saw from a distance that the fence of Wei Can's fortress was not completed, so he led his elite troops to attack.
Army deputy Wang Changmao advised to hold on to the camp and wait for the enemy. Wei Can did not listen to his advice and ordered the army commander Zheng Yi to attack the enemy. He also ordered Liu Shuyin to use the navy to cut off the enemy's retreat.
Liu Shuyin was too timid and afraid to lead his troops forward, so Zheng Yi was defeated.
The rebels took advantage of the victory and rushed into the military camp. People around Wei Can pulled him away, but he remained motionless and loudly ordered his children to fight desperately. Almost all the soldiers were killed, and Wei Can was also killed. He was fifty-four years old at the time.
Wei Can's son Wei Ni and Wei Can's three younger brothers Wei Zhu, Wei Jing, Wei Gou, and cousin Wei Ang were all killed in the battle. Hundreds of his relatives died in the battle.
The rebels took Wei Can's head to the palace gate and showed it to the people in the palace. When Taizong learned about it, he cried and said: The safety of the country depends on Wei Gong. Why is it so unfortunate that he died in the battle first?
So Xia Shao gave Wei Can the posthumous title of general guarding the army.
After the emperor put down Hou Jing's rebellion, he posthumously awarded Wei Canmi the title of loyalty, Wei Zhu, Wei Jing, Wei Gou and Wei Ni as Zhongshu Lang, and Wei Ang as a member of the Foreign Sanqi Changshi.
Wei Zang, the eldest son of Wei Can, was given the courtesy name Junli.
Wei Zang once served as the Third Duke of Shangshu, the prince washed horses, and the palace leader.
When Hou Jing was besieging the capital, he led his troops to garrison Xihua Gate.
After the fall of Beijing, he fled to Jiangzhou, gathered his old troops, and guarded Yuzhang. He was later killed by his subordinates.
Jiangzi, whose name is Yuanzhen, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang. He is the seventh generation descendant of Jiang Tong, a regular servant of Sanqi during the Jin Dynasty.
His father, Jiang Facheng, was appointed to the imperial court during the Tianjian period.
When Jiangzi was young, he loved to study, was ambitious and moral, but because his family was poor and his parents did not provide enough support, he became a vegetarian all his life.
He first took up an official position as the minister of the kingdom and was invited by the court.
He petitioned to go to the secret pavilion to read. Emperor Gaozu agreed and ordered Jiang Ziyi to be on duty in Hualin Province.
Jiang Ziyi's uncle, Youwei General Sai Yu, was a powerful figure in the dynasty. Whenever he went home on vacation, his house would be crowded with guests, but Jiang Ziyi never came to visit him. His conduct was so noble.
Later, Jiang Ziyi gradually moved to the post of Minister Caolang, and went to Beijing to serve as the magistrate of Suichang and Qu'a counties, all of which achieved good political performances.
Jiang Ziyi was appointed as the Minister of Tongzhi Sanqi. He left Beijing and served as General Rongzhao and Colonel Nanjin.
Jiang Ziyi's younger brother Jiang Zisi once served as Shangshu Jinbulang. In the early years of his reign, he moved to Youcheng.
Both brothers have strong personalities.
Jiang Wangpan, as You Cheng, presented the seal to the court and spoke freely about the court's gains and losses. Gaozu appreciated it very much and ordered the minister to carefully examine it and choose the good ones for implementation.
Zuo Minlang Shen Jiong and Shaofu Cheng Gu Qi once scolded them sternly because of improper performance. Jiang Zisi quickly stepped forward to answer for Shen Jiong and Gu Qi. His words were very fierce and forthright. Gaozu angrily called for people to tie him up. Jiang Zisi fell on the ground and refused to be bound. Gaozu's anger subsided and he asked people to let him go. However, he was still convicted and dismissed.
Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and was about to cross the Hengjiang River. Jiang Ziyi led more than a thousand naval troops to intercept Hou Jing downstream. His deputy general Dong Taosheng, who lived in the north of the Yangtze River, fled with his accomplices.
So as soon as Jiang Zi retreated to Nanzhou, he gathered the remaining troops and hurried to the capital on foot from the alley.
The rebels soon arrived in the capital. Jiang Ziyi reported to Taizong: The rebels' encirclement has not been closed yet. We can try to break out. If we wait for them to build all the fortresses, then we will have no use.
Jiang Ziyi requested that he and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu lead more than a hundred soldiers to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the rebels. The rebels agreed.
Jiang Zi took the lead and rushed into the enemy camp alone with his sword. The rebels attacked him, and the people behind him did not dare to rush in. Seeing that the situation was critical, Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu followed them and rushed into the enemy camp. All three of them were killed.
The emperor wrote to Shao Shu: The former general Rong Zhao, the minister of Tongzhi Sanqi, the Nanjin school captain Jiang Ziyi, the former minister Youcheng Jiang Zisi, and the commander-in-chief of the East Palace Zhidian Jiang Ziwu. I am deeply saddened by the news of their death. According to the original regulations, the awards and memorials for their sacrifices should be given a higher level.
Jiang Shang can be given posthumously as the Minister of Huangmen, Jiang Zisi as the Minister of Zhongshu, and Jiang Ziwu as the Minister of Sanqi.
After the Hou Jing Rebellion was settled, Shidan posthumously gave Jiang Ziyi the title of Shizhong and Mi's adopted son; Jiang Zisi's posthumous title of Huangmen Shilang and Mi's title Yizi; Jiang Ziwu's posthumous title of Zhongshu Shilang and Mi Mi's title Liezi.
Jiang Ziyi once continued to write "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin", as well as dozens of poems, poems, rhymes and prose, all of which have been circulated in the world.
Zhang Sheng, named Sishan, was the son of Zhang Ji, the general of Zhenbei.
When Zhang Sheng was young, he behaved upright and elegantly, had ambition and integrity, and was able to talk about mysteries.
When his father was governing Qingzhou, he was killed by the local people. Zhang Zhu was so sad about the disaster at home that he ate vegetarian food and wore common clothes all his life, without holding a knife in his hand.
The state promoted him as a scholar.
Zhang Sheng first became an official and served as Secretary Lang. He was repeatedly promoted to Prince Sheren, Xima, Situ Zuoxi, and Zhongshu Lang.
He left the capital and served as the internal history of Yongyang. After returning to the capital, he was appointed as the Sima of Xuancheng King of the Chinese Army and the regular attendant of Sanqi.
Later, he went to the capital to serve as the chief historian of Zhennan Yersai and the prefect of Xunyang.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited and appointed as Taifu Qing, and soon moved to Wuxing Taishou.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged the capital. Zhang Sheng sent his younger brother Zhang Yi to lead thousands of troops from the county to rescue him.
In the third year of the Taiqing Dynasty, the palace city was captured. Shen Jun, the censor Zhongcheng, fled eastward and returned to his hometown. Zhang Sheng went to see him and said: Now the rebels are bullying the lord, and the country is in danger and the king is humiliated. This is the time for the ministers to serve loyally. Now I want to gather troops to defend your hometown of Wuxing.
If God does not bless me and my wish to be loyal and loyal cannot come true, I will have no regrets even if I die because of it.
Xuanjun replied: Although our Wuxing County is small, you resist the rebels with justice. Who dares not to obey!
Xuan Peng firmly encouraged Ji Yan to organize volunteers to resist the rebels.
So Ji Crocodile gathered his soldiers and built a city wall and fortress.
At that time, King Shaoling fled eastward to Bilu. When he heard about the Japanese incident, he ordered Zhang Yan to be appointed General Zhengshu in the name of the royal family and was given the official street of Jiuqing.
Zhang Sheng said: The imperial court is in a critical situation and the emperor has suffered humiliation. How do I feel about accepting the title of Wei Guangrong now?
He just left the document conferring an officialship from the royal palace.
The traitor Liu Shenmao from Xingtai captured Yixing. He sent envoys to persuade Zhang Sheng, saying: If you surrender early, you will still be made the county guard, and you will be given official rewards.
Zhang Sheng ordered the envoy to be beheaded, and then sent the army leader Wang Xiong and others to lead his troops to meet Shen Mao at Yudu and defeated him. Shen Mao fled.
Hou Jing heard that Shenmao had been defeated, so he sent his central army officer Hou Zijian to lead 20,000 elite troops to help Shenmao attack Zhang Sheng. Zhang Sheng sent his army leader Fan Zhilang to the west of the county to resist, but was defeated by Shenmao and then retreated.
The rebel cavalry took advantage of the victory and burned the camp fence, and the defenders inside the fence collapsed.
Zhang Sheng took off his military uniform and sat in the hall. The rebels threatened him with a knife, but he still refused to give in.
So the rebels tied him up and sent him to Hou Jing. Hou Jing killed him in the capital market, and more than ten of his disciples were killed together with him. Zhang Sheng was sixty-two years old when he died.
After Hou Jing's rebellion was settled, Shizu posthumously awarded him the titles of Shizhong, Zhongwei General, and Kaifu Yitong.
He was given the nickname Zhongzhenzi.
Shen Jun, courtesy name Shuyuan, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
His grandfather Shen Xian was a regular servant of Sanqi during the Qi Dynasty. There is a biography of Shen Xian in the history of Qi.
Shen Jun was erudite and talented when he was young. He served successively as the magistrate of Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang counties, and had a reputation for being able to handle affairs.
He went to Beijing and served as Zhongshu Lang and Shangshu Zuocheng.
When Hou Jing besieged the capital, he moved to the post of censor Zhongcheng.
At that time, reinforcements from all walks of life arrived near the capital, and Hou Jing petitioned to conclude an alliance, and the emperor agreed.
After the covenant was made, Qiang learned that a plague had broken out in the city, so he had treacherous intentions and delayed leaving.
Several days later, the Crown Prince ordered Shen Jun to go to Hou Jing's military camp. Hou Jing said: The weather is getting hotter. It's not the time to march. How can I leave with 100,000 troops?
I still want to serve the imperial court. You can apply for me. Shen Jun replied: The general's real intention in saying these words is to seize the palace city.
The troops and food in the city can still last for a hundred days. Your food reserves have been exhausted. The court's reinforcements are gathering outside. What will you use to feed one hundred thousand soldiers?
When you say these words, do you want to threaten the court?
Hou Jing put the knife across his knees and scolded Shen Jun with his eyes wide open.
Shen Jun sternly condemned Hou Jing and said: You are a minister of the imperial court, but you launched a mutiny and besieged the capital. The wise monarch has given grace to forgive your sins, and we have also concluded a covenant together. Now that the blood of the covenant has not been dried, you will regret it.
I am already sixty years old, and I am the envoy of the Emperor. I am determined to live or die by my fate. Am I afraid of the blade of a traitor like you?
After saying that, he went out without looking back.
Hou Jing said: This man is truly Sizhi who is loyal to the country!
Yet I still harbor a grudge against him.
After breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp, Hou Jing searched for Shen Jun and killed him.
Liu Jingli is the grandson of Liu Qingyuan, the third minister of Kaifu Yitong.
His father Liu Jin was appointed Prince Zhan Shi.
Liu Jingli and his elder brother Liu Zhongli were famous for their loyalty and bravery when they were young.
Liu Jingli was recruited from his family to serve as Zuo Lang, and gradually he was promoted to the governor of Fufeng.
When Hou Jing was crossing the river, Liu Jingli led 3,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue him. When he arrived near the capital, he defended Qingxidai and fought with Hou Jing many times. He often took the lead in charging into the city and gained far-reaching prestige.
After the palace city was captured, both Liu Jingli and Liu Zhongli went to see Hou Jing. Hou Jing sent Liu Zhongli to govern the upper reaches of the river, leaving Liu Jingli as a hostage and appointing him as a guard.
Hou Jing held a banquet for Liu Zhongli in Houzhu to see him off. Liu Jingli secretly said to Liu Zhongli: Hou Jing came to the banquet today. I hugged him tightly, so you pulled out your sword and killed him. I will die without regrets.
Liu Zhongli thought his words were very heroic and agreed to his request.
After drinking for a few rounds, Liu Jingli signaled Liu Zhongli with his eyes. Liu Zhongli saw that the surroundings were heavily guarded and did not dare to take action, so his plan failed.
Later, when Hou Jing was conquering King Xi of Jin Dynasty, Liu Jingli and Nankang King Xiao Huili discussed sending troops to attack the city where Hou Jing was guarding. They had agreed on a date to prepare for the uprising. Jian'an Marquis Xiao Bi knew about it and reported them, so Liu Jingli was killed.
Shi Chen said: Morality is more important than life, which is the admonition left by the ancient books. This is also the character valued by the sages.
Therefore, King Gen said, life is what I want to get, and justice is also what I want to get. If I cannot get both at the same time, I would rather sacrifice my life for righteousness.
People like Ji Cricket sacrificed their lives for their country and returned home even if they died. Their heroic spirit and unyielding integrity shine through the ages. People should know that there were loyal ministers in the Liang Dynasty!
summary:
Wei Can, grandson of General Wei Rui and son of Governor Wei Gan, was a tall and learned man who served in various official positions under Prince Jin'an. He became close friends with Yu Zhongrong and Zhang Shu. As the prince rose to crown prince, Wei Can held several palace guard roles, though his arrogant nature caused resentment among peers. General Zhu Yi once rebuked him for his haughty demeanor. In 545, Wei Can became governor of Hengzhou, but resigned shortly after. Recalled in 546, he learned of Hou Jing's rebellion while traveling and rushed to the capital with 5,000 elite troops. After consulting with officials Liu Xiaoyi and Xiao Daxin, he coordinated with his cousin Liu Zhongli and General Pei Zhigao, eventually securing command for Liu. During battle at Qingtang, Wei Can ignored advice to hold position, ordered an attack, and was overwhelmed by Hou Jing's forces. He and his sons, brothers, and cousin were killed at age 54. The emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously promoted him.

Jiangzi, a seventh-generation descendant of Jiang Tong, was a studious and principled man from a poor family. He served as a county magistrate with distinction before becoming a court official. His brother Jiang Zisi served as Youcheng and once boldly defended colleagues Shen Jiong and Gu Qi during a court dispute, angering Emperor Gaozu but eventually being pardoned. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Jiangzi led naval forces to intercept the rebels but was betrayed by his deputy. He retreated to Nanzhou and then to the capital, where he proposed a breakout. He and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu charged into enemy lines alone and were killed. The emperor posthumously honored them with high titles. Jiangzi also authored works like "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin."

Zhang Sheng, son of General Zhang Ji, was a virtuous and scholarly man who became a vegetarian after his father's murder. He held various official posts, including governor of Wuxing. During Hou Jing's siege of the capital, he sent troops to help. After the city fell, he organized resistance in Wuxing, defeating rebel Liu Shenmao. When Hou Jing sent reinforcements, Zhang Sheng's forces were overwhelmed. He refused to surrender, was captured, and executed at age 62. He was posthumously honored as Zhongzhenzi.

Shen Jun, a learned official from Wukang, served as magistrate of several counties and later as censor. During Hou Jing's siege, he negotiated with the rebel leader, boldly condemning his treachery. Hou Jing admired his loyalty but later killed him after breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp.

Liu Jingli, grandson of Liu Qingyuan, was known for bravery. He defended Qingxidai during Hou Jing's invasion, leading charges. After the palace fell, he plotted with his brother Liu Zhongli to assassinate Hou Jing at a banquet, but the plan failed due to heavy guards. Later, he conspired with Prince Xiao Huili to attack Hou Jing's stronghold but was betrayed and killed.

The historian concludes that these men exemplified the principle of sacrificing life for righteousness, proving that the Liang Dynasty had loyal ministers.
