summary:
Wang Sengbian, son of General Wang Shennian, began his military career during the Tianjian period, serving under various princes in positions such as Zuo Changshi and military advisor. He quelled a rebellion in Wuning County and held several governorships, including Wuning, Guangping, and Anlu. When Hou Jing rebelled, Wang Sengbian led 10,000 naval troops to aid the capital, but the palace was captured. He briefly surrendered to Hou Jing before rejoining Shizu (Emperor Yuan of Liang). Ordered to attack the governor of Xiangzhou, Wang Sengbian delayed departure due to insufficient troops, angering Shizu, who struck him with a sword and imprisoned him. He was later pardoned to defend against King Yueyang's attack, successfully defeating him and replacing Bao Quan to pacify Xiangzhou.

Wang Sengbian then defended Baling against Hou Jing's invasion, employing strategies like sinking ships and stockpiling supplies. Despite fierce assaults, including fire attacks and siege equipment, the rebels were repelled. Rewarded as General of the East Conquest and Duke of Changning, he led forces to capture Lushan and Yingcheng, defeating Song Zixian and capturing him alive. He advanced to Jiushui, and after learning of the emperor's death, urged Shizu to take the throne. Marching toward Jianye, he allied with Chen Baxian at Baimaozhou, swearing an oath to destroy Hou Jing. Their combined forces defeated the rebels at Stone City, and Hou Jing fled. Wang Sengbian captured rebel leaders and restored order, earning the title of General of the Town Guard and Situ.

Later, Wang Sengbian suppressed the rebellion of Lu Na in Xiangzhou, using cautious tactics to surround and defeat him. He then guarded against Qi invasions, defeating their forces at Dongguan. After his mother's death, he received honors and a eulogy from the emperor. When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Wang Sengbian was summoned but failed to arrive before the capital fell. He supported Emperor Jing and negotiated with Qi to accept Xiao Yuanming as emperor, sending hostages and meeting him at Jiangningpu. This led to conflict with Chen Baxian, who attacked Jiankang. Wang Sengbian, caught off guard, was captured and killed by Chen Baxian. His sons met various fates: Wang Chan died early, Wang Jie fled to Qi, Wang Hao died of grief, and Wang Ban was captured by Western Wei. The historian notes that despite his merits, Wang Sengbian's decision to install a puppet emperor under Qi coercion led to his downfall.

After the Zhengshi period of the Wei Dynasty, the Taoist theory of Xuanyuan Nihility was gradually advocated, and therefore fewer people studied Confucianism.
At that time, Xun Pin, Zhi Yu and others, although they deleted new rituals and changed official positions, they could not change the customs.

Because the state only provided empty provisions in the regulations for the establishment of schools, they were suddenly abandoned.
There are no schools in each township, and few ministers are proficient in the classics. The great scholars in the court only practice the classics themselves but refuse to teach students. The young people are ignorant and have no place to study and study the classics. The three virtues and six arts have been neglected for a long time.
After Emperor Gaozu became emperor, he was deeply saddened and worried about this situation, so he issued an edict to search for knowledgeable scholars, rectify the five rituals, approve the six laws, revise the calendar, and correct the balance.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu issued an edict saying: There are no wise men in the two deserts who have not taught Confucianism by virtue of their classics and skills, and have established a good reputation and achieved moral success.
In the Wei and Jin dynasties, the atmosphere was turbulent and Confucian learning declined. Perhaps because of this, the moral integrity could not be established.
I leave the court very late every day, just because I want to hear news about talented people. If you appoint talented people to get talented people, you should be rewarded.
Doctors on the Five Classics should be established, with one doctor for each classic, and schools should be established widely to accept young people to study.
So Pingyuan Mingshanbin, Wu Jun Lu Lian, Wu Xing Shen Jun, Jianping Yan Zhizhi, Kuaiji Hechang, etc. were appointed as replacement doctors, and each of them presided over a school.
There were hundreds of students in the academy, and the imperial court provided them with salaries.
Among them, those who choose things to report, if they are enlightened and wise, will be awarded as officials.
For more than ten years, people who were proficient in Confucian classics and well-read in Confucian classics gathered in the capital.
He also selected students to go to Yunmen Mountain in Kuaiji and study with He Yin in Lujiang.
Doctors were sent to each state and county to establish schools.
In the seventh year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu issued another edict: To establish a country and be the monarch of all people, establishing enlightenment and promoting education are the most important things; cultivating knowledge and sharpening virtues, classics study is the must way.
I have established a foundation that has spread throughout the world. Although I have worked hard to develop Confucianism, there are not many talented people, and the virtues are still lacking. I want to encourage them to respect their elders, practice it at home, and then become a model for the world.
Wherever the prestige is now, the Rong people in China are also inspired. They should vigorously open schools and widely recruit the children of the royal family and nobles to practice the ten ethics and promote the three virtues, so that the imperial education can be spread far and wide, and the exquisite words can be promoted.
So the crown princes, princes, royal families, and princes began to study in schools.
In vain, Emperor Gaozu condescended to go to the school in person to pay tribute to Zizi and other saints of the previous generation, talk to the students, encourage them, and comfort them with silk. The school was solemn and the students were numerous, and the journey of the Great Way reached such a prosperous level.
Among them, Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi and Fan Zhen were already famous in contemporary times; among the famous Confucian scholars at that time, Yan Zhizhi, He Yu and others were among the top candidates.
Now the deeds of these people are connected together and compiled into "The Scholars".
Fu Manrong, courtesy name Gongyi, was born in Anqiu, Pingchang.
His great-grandfather Fu Tao was a scholar in the Jin Dynasty.
His father Fu Yinzhi was the chief secretary of Sikong during the Song Dynasty.
Fu Manrong lost his father very early, and he lived in the South China Sea with his mother and brother.
Fu Manrong has been attentive and studious since he was a child, and he is proficient in "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He is bold and free and likes to exaggerate. Fu Manrong gathered students to teach them their studies and regarded this as his profession.
Fu Manrong Ren Piao rode to join the army.

Fu Manrong moved to Situ to join the army.

At the end of the Ming Dynasty, he served as the governor of the auxiliary state and the governor of Nanhai.

In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, he led the crown prince's orders and served the crown prince.

The deeds of Fu Manrong's son Fu Qu are in "The Biography of Good Officials".
He Tong, whose courtesy name was Shiwei, was from Sa County, Lujiang. He was the sixth-generation grandson of He Pang, the governor of Yuzhou.
His grandfather He Shaozhi was a member of the imperial court during the Song Dynasty.
His father, He Xin, was invited to the court by Qi Shi.

In the early years of ZTE, He Tongzhi was worshiped as a general of heroic cavalry.

He Tongzhi wrote about one hundred articles in "Li Yi".
He Tongzhi's sons were named He Chaoyin and He Chaohui.

Xiao Ziliang firmly believes in Buddhism, while Fan Zhen strongly claims that there is no Buddha.

Your Majesty, you are the one who is on the mat; this is the case with me, your Majesty, who is lying next to the filthy pit.
Although high and low have different paths, where does cause and effect ultimately end?

Someone asked me: You said that the spirit will disappear. How do you know that it will disappear?
The answer is: The spirit is the body, and the body is the spirit. Therefore, when the body exists, the spirit exists. When the body withers, the spirit disappears.
Jian: Body is the name for things without consciousness, and spirit is the name for things with consciousness.

Answer: The body is the material form of the spirit, and the spirit is the external expression of the body. Therefore, the body refers to its material form, and the spirit refers to its external expression. The body and the spirit cannot be separated from each other.

Question: The relationship between a knife and sharpness may be just like what you just said; but the relationship between body and spirit is not the same.
Why do you say this?
The material entity of trees has no consciousness, but the material entity of people has consciousness. People have both material entities like trees, but also have consciousness that is different from trees. Isn't it true that trees only have the same body, but people have both body and spirit?
Answer: What you said is really strange!
If a person has a material form like a tree as his body and a consciousness different from that of a tree as his spirit, then he can be like what you just said.
Now the material entity of human beings itself has consciousness, while the material entity of trees itself has no consciousness. Question: The difference between the physical entity of humans and the physical entity of trees is precisely because humans have consciousness.
If people have no consciousness, what is the difference between them and trees?
Answer: People do not have unconscious material entities, just as trees do not have sentient material entities.
Question: Isn’t the body of the deceased a material entity without consciousness?
Answer: This form is a material entity without human consciousness.
Question: In this case, people really have material entities like trees, and they also have perceptions that are different from trees.
Answer: Dead people have material entities like trees, but they have no consciousness different from trees; living people have consciousness different from trees, but they do not have material entities like trees.
Question: Aren’t the bones of a dead person the same as the remains of a living person?
Answer: The physical skeleton of a living person is different from the physical skeleton of a dead person, and the physical skeleton of a dead person is different from the physical skeleton of a living person. The difference is already very clear. How can there be a physical skeleton of a living person and the skeleton of a dead person?
Question: If the skeleton of a living person is not the skeleton of a dead person, then the skeleton must not have been transformed from the skeleton of a living person. If it was not transformed from the skeleton of a living person, then where did the skeleton of the dead come from?
Answer: This is the form of a living person turned into the skeleton of a dead person.
Question: Although the body of a living person has turned into the skeleton of a dead person, isn’t it because there is a living body and then a dead body? Then we can know that the dead body is the living body.
Answer: It is like changing from a living tree to a dead tree. Could it be that the material entity of the dead tree is the form of the living tree?
Question: If the living tree body becomes a dead tree body, then the dead tree body becomes the living tree body; the silk body becomes the thread body, and the thread body becomes the silk body. What is the difference between the two?
Answer: If a dead tree is a living tree and a living tree is a dead tree, then it should wither when its branches and leaves are lush and bear fruit when it is withered.
And a living tree should not become a dead tree, because a living tree is a dead tree, and there is no need for change.
A living tree is the same as a dead tree, so why don't they wither first and then grow and flourish?
Generally speaking, trees always flourish first and then wither. Why?
What you said about silk and glutinous rice can also be refuted in the same way.
Question: The fading of the living form should be eliminated all at once. Why does it take a long time when it is about to become a dead form?
Answer: This is because the formation and destruction of bodies generally follow a certain procedure.
Those things that are suddenly created must suddenly disappear, and those things that are gradually generated must be gradually destroyed.
Things that arise suddenly, such as storms and rains, are of this type; things that are formed gradually, animals and plants are one type of creation.
Some are formed suddenly and some are formed gradually. This is the law of all things.
Question: If the body is the spirit, are things like hands also the spirit?
Answer: These types of things are all part of the spirit.
Question: If they are all part of the spirit, then if the spirit can think, should things like hands also be able to think?
Answer: Things like hands should also feel pain and itching, without thinking about right and wrong.
Question: Are perception and thinking the same thing or different things?
Answer: Perception is thinking, shallow thinking is called perception, and deep thinking is called thinking.
Question: In this case, there should be two kinds of thinking. Since there are two kinds of thinking, are there two kinds of spirit?
Answer: There is only one human body, how can there be two kinds of spirit!
Question: If there cannot be two kinds of spirit, then where can there be the perception of pain and itch, and the thought of judging right and wrong?
Answer: Creation is like brothers and feet, although they are different, they all belong to the same person; judgments of right and wrong, feelings of pain and itch are different, but they all belong to the same spirit.
Question: The thought of judging right and wrong has nothing to do with siblings, so where does it have something to do with it?
Answer: The thinking of right and wrong is governed by the heart.
Question: Does the heart refer to the heart among the five internal organs, or does it not refer to the heart of the five internal organs?
Answer: It refers to the heart among the five internal organs.
Question: What are the differences between the five internal organs, but the heart only has the worry of judging right and wrong?
Answer: What is the difference between the seven orifices? Their functions are different.
Question: Thoughts have no definite direction, so how do we know that thoughts are governed by the heart?

Kong Qian was a Confucian scholar who only knew the classics and was not good at governing the people. He had no political achievements during his tenure as county magistrate.
When turmoil broke out during the Liqian period, Kong Yu died at home.
Kong Chuxuan, the son of Kong Qian, focused on studying Confucianism, and his official position was promoted to Doctor of Taixue.
Kong Chuxuan, the son of brother Kong Ling, was also proficient in the "Three Rites" and had a great reputation, but he died young.
Lu Guang, a native of Fanyang Zhuo, said he was a descendant of Lu Chen, a middle-ranking official in Zhi Sikong.
Lu Chen was trapped and died in the army during the rebellion. During the Jin Dynasty, Lu Chen was still among the famous families in the Central Plains, and there were descendants of Lu Chen.
Lu Guang was proficient in scriptures since he was a child and had Confucian knowledge.
Lu Guang returned to chisel during the Tianjian period.
At first he was appointed as the Minister of Sanqi, a member of the Yuanwai Sanqi family, and then went to Beijing to serve as the prefect of Quanda. However, he was dismissed from office because of his guilt.
Soon, Lu Guang was appointed as General Zhechong, and the imperial court assigned him a thousand soldiers for the Northern Expedition. After returning to the imperial court, he was worshiped as an infantry captain and a doctor of Guozi, and taught all the "Five Classics" in the academy.
At that time, Confucian scholars from the north, including Cui Lingen, Sun Xiang, Jiang Xian and others, gathered students to teach Confucian classics, but their pronunciation was vulgar and clumsy; only Lu Guang spoke clearly and elegantly, unlike the northerners.
Pushe Xu Mian was also proficient in Confucian classics, and he deeply appreciated Lu Guang.
Soon after, Lu Guang was appointed as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi, but his position as a doctor remained unchanged.
He also left the capital and served as Xinwu, the successor of Guiyang, Changshi, and the prefect of Xunyang.
He was also appointed as the chief historian of Wuling King, and his post as governor remained unchanged. He died during his tenure.
Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
The family has been a farmer for generations, until Yingkong. He loved learning, and he and his uncle Taishi Shuming chose Shen Jun as their teacher from the same clan. He studied under Shen Junmu for many years. He assigned himself tasks to study day and night. Sometimes he would doze off and hit himself with a wooden stick. He was so concentrated.
After Shen Lin's death, Licai left the capital and traveled to various schools, so he became proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites.
Shen Jun initially served as the lieutenant of the kingdom, and was gradually promoted to the rank of minister and assistant to the prince.
At that time, Lang Lubao, the official of the Ministry of official affairs, wrote a letter to Pu She Tu Pad to recommend some candidates: Doctor Chen Zhida in the "Five Classics" must be replaced, considering that the imperial court must carefully select suitable talents to replace him.
As long as it is a sage's book that can be studied and its views must be established based on "Zhou Guan", then "Zhou Guan" is actually the source and foundation of various scriptures.
However, the knowledge of "Zhou Guan" has not been taught to each other for many years. Sun Xiang and Jiang Hao from the north also studied and taught it. However, because their pronunciation is like that of Southern Chu and Zhu Xia, which is far apart and difficult to understand, students are reluctant to study. Only the assistant teacher Shen Jun is particularly proficient in the book "Zhou Guan".
Recently, he often opened lectures. Many Confucian scholars, such as Liu Hua, Shen Hong, and Shen Xiong, came to his forum to worship him as their teacher, and brought scriptures to listen to his lectures. None of them were not impressed, and no one had any criticism.
I think that such a person should be recruited immediately and ordered to specialize in this subject of knowledge and teach "Zhou Guan" over and over again, so that the authentic classics of the saints can be valued again after being abandoned, and the knowledge that has been lost for many years can be taught to scholars.
Xu Mian followed Lu Ren's suggestion and wrote a memorial recommending Shen Jun as a doctor of the Five Classics.
Shen Jun lectures in the school, and there are often hundreds of students attending his lectures.
Shen Jun left the capital and served as Huarong Ling. After returning to the capital, he was awarded not only as a member of the Sanqi Shilang, but also as a doctor of "Five Classics".
At that time, He Chen, a member of Zhongshushe, was ordered by the emperor to compile "Liang Guan", so he petitioned Shen Jun and Confucius Qubu to serve as bachelors in the Western Province to help him write "Liang Guan".
After the book "Liang Guan" was completed, Shen Jun entered the court and served as Zhongshu General.
Later he left the capital and served as Wukang Ling, and died during his tenure.
Shen Jun's son, Shen Wen'a, inherited his father's studies, and was especially proficient in "The Biography of the Zuo Family".
During the Taiqing period, Shen Wen'a was promoted from assistant teacher of Guozi to doctor of "Five Classics".
Those who inherited Shen Jun's studies include Zhang Ji of Wujun and Confucius Yun of Kuaiji. Their official positions were promoted to doctor of the Five Classics and minister of the temple.
Taishi Shuming was a native of Wucheng, Wuxing. He was a descendant of Wu Taishi Ci.
Taishi Shuming was proficient in "Zhuangzi" and "Laozi" since he was a child. He also studied "The Book of Filial Piety" and "Book of Rites". He was particularly proficient in the three books of "Zhuangzi", "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He was second to none at the time. During each lecture, there were often more than 500 people listening.
Uncle Taishi served as Guozi's assistant coach for consecutive years.
He liked Taishi Shuming's knowledge. When he came to Beijing to serve as the governor of Jiangzhou, he also took Taishi Shuming to Jiangzhou.
He was appointed governor of Yingzhou, and Taishi Shuming moved to Yingzhou with the palace. Everywhere he went, Taishi Shuming opened a school to teach, and people in the south of the Yangtze River inherited his teachings.
In the thirteenth year of Datong, Taishi Shuming passed away at the age of seventy-three.
Confucius was born in Shanyin, Kuaiji.
He lost his father when he was young, and his family was poor, but he loved learning. When he was cultivating fields and collecting wood in the mountains, he often took books with him and read and recited them whenever he had free time.
He worked hard and persevered, and finally became proficient in Confucian classics, especially "Guwen Shangshu".
Confucius Qu initially served as the Minister of the Successor of Changsha and as an assistant to the Confucius of the Kingdom. He lectured on "Shang Shu" forty times, and there were often hundreds of people listening to his lectures.
He Chen, a member of Zhongshushe, was ordered by the emperor to compile "Liang Guan". He petitioned Confucius Qu to be a bachelor of the Western Province to help him write "Liang Guan".
After the book "Liang Guan" was completed, Confucius served as Minister Wen, but he did not take up the post.
A long time later, he also served as host, guest, and guest, and his position as a bachelor remained unchanged.
He also accumulated merit and was promoted to be the minister of the Xiangdong Kingdom, a permanent minister, and a minister of scattered cavalry outside the service. He was also appointed as Yunhui Lujiang Gongji Office to join the army, and was transferred to serve as Zhongshu General Secretary.
Soon he was moved to the rank of infantry school captain, but his position remained unchanged.
When Emperor Gaozu wrote the "Explanations of the Five Classics" and "The True Sayings of Confucius", he specifically ordered Confucius to check various books and find materials to prove his righteousness.
After the matter was completed, Gaozu ordered Jie Ziguai, right guard Zhu Yi, and Zuo Cheng He Chen to take turns every day in the Shilin Pavilion to practice scriptures, ask questions, and assess the scholars.
Zhizi Qu accumulated merit and was promoted to Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, but his position remained unchanged.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, Confucius died during his tenure at the age of fifty-one.
Confucius Qu wrote a total of 20 volumes of "Shang Shu Yi", 30 volumes of "Collected Comments on Shangshu", a 100-volume continuation of Zhu Yi's "Collected Comments on Zhouyi", and a 150-volume continuation of He Chengtian's "Ji Li Lun".
Huang Kan, a native of Wu County, is the ninth generation descendant of Huang Xiang, the governor of Qingzhou.
Huang Kan loved studying since he was a child. He worshiped He Chang as his teacher and devoted himself to learning from He Chang. As a result, he became proficient in Confucian classics, especially the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects of Confucius.
When he first became an official and served as an assistant to Guozi, he gave lectures on classics and meanings in the academy, and hundreds of students attended his lectures.
Huang Kan wrote fifty volumes of the "Book of Rites". After it was completed, it was presented to the emperor, who ordered it to be handed over to the secret pavilion for collection.
Soon, Huang Kan was called to Huayongji to lecture on "Book of Rites". Zhidan thought that he was very knowledgeable, so he was appointed as a member of the Yuanwai Sanqi Shilang, and his position as an assistant teacher remained unchanged.
Huang Kan was very filial by nature, and often required him to recite the "Filial Piety Sutra" twenty times a day, which was modeled on the recitation of the "Avalokiteśvara Sutra".
When Huang Kan's mother passed away, he resigned from his post and returned to his hometown to mourn.
King Shaoling of Qianxi admired Huang Kan's knowledge and went to welcome Huang Kan with generous gifts.
After Huang Kan went to King Shaoling, he contracted a heart disease and died in Xia Shou in the eleventh year of Datong at the age of fifty-eight.
The ten volumes of "On Meaning" and "Book of Rites" written by Huang Kan were valued by scholars at that time, and some scholars inherited his theories.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Chen's Ministry of Civil Affairs, said: In the past, Shusun Tong lectured on Confucian classics on horseback during the war years, and Huan Rong lectured on Confucian classics during the turmoil and hunger.
Fu Manrong and He Tongzhi taught Confucian classics in the late Qi Dynasty, but did not change their ambitions due to the current situation. He Chang, Yan Zhizhi and others encountered the opportunity of Liang's advocating Confucianism and attaching importance to Confucianism. They all enjoyed high officials and generous salaries, and studied ancient rituals as a reference for the contemporary era. These Confucian scholars did their best.
Fan Zhen wore black mourning clothes to welcome the rebels, and Yi Yuan was lucky enough to be favored. It was only right that his intention was not realized!
summary:
The Han Dynasty, learning from the Qin Dynasty's book burning, vigorously promoted Confucianism, with the Imperial Academy often hosting over ten thousand students and schools flourishing even in remote areas. However, at the end of the Han Dynasty, political turmoil led to Confucianism's decline. During the Wei Dynasty's Zhengshi period, Taoist philosophy gained prominence, reducing interest in Confucianism. Figures like Xun Pin and Zhi Yu attempted reforms but failed to change customs. After the Jin Dynasty's founding, the Central Plains fell into chaos, and the court moved south, leaving no time for education. During the Song and Qi Dynasties, schools were sporadically opened but quickly abandoned, with no sustained encouragement. Local schools vanished, ministers rarely mastered the classics, and young people had no means to study. The three virtues and six arts were neglected for a long time.

Emperor Gaozu of Liang, deeply concerned, issued edicts to seek scholars, rectify rituals, revise laws, and correct standards. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he decreed the establishment of Five Classics doctors, one per classic, and the widespread opening of schools. Scholars like Pingyuan Mingshanbin, Wu Jun Lu Lian, Wu Xing Shen Jun, Jianping Yan Zhizhi, and Kuaiji He Chang were appointed as doctors, each presiding over a school. Hundreds of students received salaries from the court, and those who excelled were appointed as officials. Over a decade, many proficient in Confucian classics gathered in the capital. Students were also sent to study with He Yin in Kuaiji. In the seventh year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu further decreed the promotion of education, encouraging the children of nobles to study the ten ethics and three virtues. The crown prince, princes, and nobles began attending schools, and the emperor personally visited to honor sages and encourage students. The school became solemn and prosperous, with scholars like Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, and Fan Zhen gaining fame.

Fu Manrong, from Anqiu, lost his father early and lived with his mother and brother in the South China Sea. He was studious, proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes, and bold in speech. He gathered students to teach and held various official positions, including Piaoqi Canjun and Nanhai Prefect. During the Qi Dynasty, he served as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi and later as Zhongshu Lang. He was known for lecturing on scriptures at home, attracting dozens or hundreds of students. In the Liang Dynasty, he was appointed as Sima and Linhai Prefect, dying at eighty-two. He authored annotations on the Zhouyi, Mao's Poems, and other works.

He Tongzhi, from Lujiang, was deeply interested in the Three Rites from childhood, studying independently and mastering three hundred chapters of the Li. Respected by Taiwei Wang Jian, he held various posts, including Shangshu Temple Minister and Infantry Colonel. During the Yongyuan period, despite war, he continued lecturing. After Emperor Gaozu's ascension, he became Zuocheng, aiding in system creation. He died at fifty-five, posthumously honored as Huangmen Shilang. He wrote about one hundred articles on Li Yi.

Fan Zhen, from Nanxiang, lost his father young and served his mother filially. He studied under Liu Shan, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as an envoy to the Wei and was known for his straightforward nature. He debated Buddhism with Xiao Ziliang, arguing against the existence of gods. His "Theory on the Destruction of Gods" sparked controversy. He held various posts, including Yidu Prefect and Jin'an Prefect, dying as Zhongshu Lang. His son Fan Xu inherited his knowledge.

Yan Zhizhi, from Jianping, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Three Rites. He served as Luling Kingdom Minister and Guanghan Kingdom Right Changshi, known for his righteousness in handling the Guanghan King's funeral. He was appointed as a Five Classics doctor, lecturing to hundreds of students. He died at fifty-two, leaving his family in poverty. He authored 479 volumes of Annotations on Evil Etiquette.

He Chang, from Kuaiji, inherited family education in the Three Rites. Recommended by Liu Xian, he served as Taichang Cheng and Five Classics doctor, lecturing on the Li. He authored works on etiquette and the Five Classics, dying at fifty-nine. His son He Ge also became a renowned scholar, lecturing on the Three Rites.

Sima Yun, from Hanoi, lost his father young but loved learning, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as Shangshu Temple Minister and debated mourning rites for loving mothers. He died as Shixing Neishi. His son Sima Shou inherited his studies.

Bian Hua, from Jiyin, lost his father young but studied the Five Classics, especially the Book of Changes. He served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his eloquence and musical expertise. He died as Wuling Prefect.

Cui Lingen, from Qinghe, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites and Three Commentaries. He served as Taichang Doctor in the Northern Dynasties before returning to Liang, where he lectured to hundreds. He authored numerous works on the classics.

Kong Qian, from Kuaiji, studied under He Yin, excelling in the Five Classics. He served as a Five Classics doctor but was not skilled in governance. He died during the Liqian turmoil.

Lu Guang, from Fanyang, was proficient in scriptures and served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his clear pronunciation. He died as Xunyang Prefect.

Shen Jun, from Wuxing, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites. Recommended as a Five Classics doctor, he lectured to hundreds. He died as Wukang Ling.

Taishi Shuming, from Wuxing, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Book of Changes, lecturing to over five hundred. He died at seventy-three.

Confucius Qu, from Kuaiji, lost his father young but became proficient in the Guwen Shangshu. He served as a lecturer and helped compile the Liang Guan. He died at fifty-one, authoring works on the Shangshu.

Huang Kan, from Wu County, studied under He Chang, excelling in the Three Rites. He lectured to hundreds and authored the Book of Rites. He died at fifty-eight.

Yao Cha noted that these scholars, despite varying fortunes, contributed to Confucian learning during the Liang Dynasty.

translation:
Hu Sengyou, whose name is Yuanguo, is a champion in Nanyang. He has been brave and decisive since he was a child, and has the ability to be a soldier.
He served as an official in the State of Wei and reached the rank of Yinqing Guanglu. He returned to the capital in the second year of Datong and frequently applied for titles. Emperor Gaozu thought highly of him and awarded him the title of "Fake Festival", "Super Military General" and "Wende Commander", and sent him to guard Xiangcheng. Xiangcheng was captured, and Hu Sengyou fell to Wei again.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, Chen Qingzhi sent Wang Yuanhao of Wei Beihai to Luoyang. Hu Sengku was able to return to the capital and was awarded the title of prefect of Nantianshui and Tianmen counties. He left good political achievements wherever he served as an official.
Hu Sengku liked reading by nature, but he was not good at writing poems and compositions. However, every time at the court banquet, Hu Sengyou would try his best to compose poems. The poems were vulgar and often ridiculed by others. Hu Sengyou was happy as usual, thinking that his poems were indeed exquisite.
Conceit and boasting are even more powerful. Hu Sengyou served Shizu in his later years and served as Zhenxi Lushi to join the army.
When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Jumans also rebelled. Shizu ordered Hu Sengcoff to attack the Western Jumans, and ordered Hu Senghu to kill all the barbarian chiefs and leaders. Hu Sengyou came to remonstrate and was imprisoned for violating Shizu's will.
In the second year of Dashi, Hou Jing invaded Jingshan and surrounded Wang Sengbian in Baling. The emperor summoned Hu Sengyou from prison, awarded him the title of General Jiajie and Wumeng, and named him the Marquis of Xinshi County, and ordered him to rush to aid Wang Sengbian.
When Hu Sengyou was about to set off, he said to his son: You can open two gates, one gate is to be turned into a red gate, and the other gate is to be turned into a white gate.
Good luck will enter the house through the red door, and bad luck will enter the house through the white door. I will not go home unless I win.
When Shizu heard Hu Sengyou's words, he felt that he was brave and commendable.
Hu Sengku led his army to Yangpu and sent his general Ren Gou to lead 5,000 elite soldiers to guard the fort and wait for Hu Sengyou's army to fight from a distance.
Hu Sengyou advanced westward by another road. Ren Yue thought that they were retreating because they were afraid of him, so he led his army to pursue them in a hurry. They caught up with Hu Sengku at Qiankou, Nan'an. Ren Yue called to Hu Sengyou and said: "Wu'er, why don't you surrender early?"
Where to escape to?
Hu Sengyou ignored his answer and secretly led his army to retreat. When they arrived at Chisha Pavilion, Lu Fahe and his army arrived. Hu Sengyou and Lu Fahe attacked Ren Yue together with the two armies, defeated Ren Yue's army, captured Ren Yue alive and sent him to Jiangling. Hou Jing led his army to escape after hearing the news that Ren Yue had been captured.
Shizu appointed Hu Sengyou as a minister and general, and recruited him back to Jingzhou.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, Hu Senyou was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Kaifu Yitong Third Division, while all other positions remained unchanged.
When the enemies of the Western Wei Dynasty invaded, Hu Sengyou was appointed as the governor of the city to supervise all military affairs.
The Wei army launched attacks from all sides, with many units attacking at the same time. Hu Sengyou personally braved the rock with arrows, supervised the battle day and night, rewarded the soldiers, and strictly rewarded and punished them. The soldiers were moved by him and were willing to fight to the death for him.
Wherever Hu Sengyou went, Naxiang's enemies were destroyed, and no enemy dared to attack again.
Soon Hu Sengyou was shot by a stray arrow and died at the age of sixty-three. When Shizu heard the news, he rushed to the east of the city to mourn.
As a result, everyone inside and outside the imperial court was in panic, and the city was finally captured.
Xu Wensheng, courtesy name Daomao, was born in Pengcheng.
His family has been serving as officials and generals in Wei for generations.
Xu Wensheng's father, Xu Qingzhi, led more than a thousand people to surrender in the early years of Tianjian, but he died on the way before they arrived.
Xu Wensheng continued to command more than a thousand men and horses, and gradually made many achievements. Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably and favored him.
In the last years of Datong, Emperor Gaozu appointed Xu Wensheng as the governor of Ningzhou and the governor of Zhijie.
Before Xu Wensheng took office, Ningzhou was located in a remote area, and the barbarians under its jurisdiction did not understand the etiquette and etiquette of education. They were just greedy for money, and robberies and robberies continued one after another. No one who served as governor could stop it.
Xu Wensheng expressed his sincerity and compassion, showing both power and virtue. All the Yi officials were influenced by him, and the customs of Ningzhou changed.
In the second year of Taiqing, Xu Wensheng heard that the country was in trouble, so he recruited soldiers. He led the recruited 10,000 people to come to the rescue.
The emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him as Chijie, Changshi of Sanqi, General of Zuowei, Supervisor of Liangnan, Qinsha, Shuyi, Babeiba and the six states of military affairs, General Renwei, and governor of Qinzhou, and entrusted him with the strategy of marching eastward.
So Xu Wensheng led the troops down the river and marched eastward. When they arrived at Wuchang, they met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue. Xu Wensheng then faced off against Ren Yue for a long time.
Shizu also ordered the guard general Yin Yue, Pingshu general Du Youan, Bazhou governor Wang Xi and others to lead their troops to meet with Xu Wensheng, asking them to obey Xu Wensheng's command.
Xu Wensheng and others attacked Ren Yue in Beji. Ren Yue was defeated and retreated to Xiyang. Xu Wensheng marched to occupy Luzhou and held a stalemate with Ren Yue.
When Hou Jing heard the news about the Japanese, he led his army up the river and westward to rescue Ren Yue, and also reached Xiyang.
Xu Wensheng did not dare to fight.
All his generals said: Hou Jing's navy advanced rashly, and the soldiers were hungry and tired. If we can seize the opportunity to attack them, we will definitely win a great victory.
Xu Wensheng refused.
Xu Wensheng's wife, Shi, was originally in Jianye. When she was dispatched, Hou Jing took Shi on a boat and sent her back to Xu Wensheng. Xu Wensheng was deeply grateful to Hou Jing, so he sent envoys to secretly communicate with Hou Jing without any intention of fighting. His generals were angry and resentful.
Du Youan and Song Yao led their troops to advance alone, fought with Hou Jing, defeated Hou Jing's army, and captured Hou Jing's ships before returning.
At that time, Hou Jing secretly sent cavalry to attack Yingzhou from the trail. Yingzhou was captured. Xu Wensheng's army was frightened and uneasy, so the whole army was defeated.
Xu Wensheng fled back to Jingzhou, and Shizu appointed Xu Wensheng as the governor of the north of the city.
Xu Wensheng also engaged in corruption and bribery, amassing a lot of property. The emperor was very angry and ordered Xu Wensheng to be punished. He listed ten crimes against him and removed his title.
After Xu Wensheng lost his military power, he was resentful. When Shizu found out about it, he imprisoned Xu Wensheng.
Ren Yue was also captured at that time and was imprisoned in the same place as Xu Wensheng.
Xu Wensheng said to Ren Yue: Why didn't you surrender earlier, and now I am imprisoned in this place.
Ren Yue said: There are no traces of your horse hooves outside the gate of my military camp. How can I surrender?
Xu Wensheng had nothing to say and eventually died in prison.
Du Chan was born in Duling, Jingzhao.
His ancestors returned to the Southern Dynasty from the north and lived in Xiangyang, Yongzhou, where their descendants settled.
Du Ze's grandfather, Du Lingqi, was appointed to Shizhong during the Qi Dynasty.
Du Qi's father, Du Huaibao, was ambitious and upright since he was a child, and often encountered good opportunities.
Gaozu led the rebel army to denounce Donghun Hou along the river, and Du Huaibao followed Xiao Wei, the king of Nanping, to stay and guard Xiangyang.
During his imprisonment, Du Huaixuan's merits gradually increased, and his official position was promoted to the rank of Fierce General and Liangzhou Governor.
In the early years of Datong, Yuan Luo, the governor of Liangzhou in Wei, led the state to surrender, and Du Huaibao went to supervise Huazhou.
At the time when the king of Genbian District under Qinzhou rebelled, Si Huaiyi led his army to defeat Sanmi.
In the fifth year of Taitong, Du Huaishi died at the place where he served.
Du Ze is Du Huaishi's seventh son.
He has been ambitious since he was a child and is known in his hometown for his courage and bravery.
When he first became an official, he was appointed as a soldier in Lujiang Huqi Prefecture and joined the army.
When Shizu was in charge of Jingzhou, Du Zhu still joined the army for the shogunate and later served as the governor of Qixing.
In the second year of Taiqing, Du Tuan followed King Yueyang to invade Jingzhou. Because of his long-standing friendship with Du Ze, Shizu secretly invited Du Qi to join him. Du Tuan, his elder brother Du An, his younger brother You'an You'an, his elder brother's son Zhuan Xin and others returned to Shisu at night. Shizu conferred the title of Silk Witch as Chijie, General Xinwei, and the governor of Wuzhou.
Soon he was promoted to General Xuanyi, leading the Zhenman Guards and the internal history of Wuling. He was granted the title of Marquis of Zhijiang County and was granted the title of a thousand households in the town.
Shizu ordered Du Ze to follow Wang Sengbian and march eastward to conquer Hou Jing.
When he led his army to Baling, he was met by Hou Jing who came to attack. Hou Jing attacked for ten days and ran away after failing to win.
Du Xun was promoted to Shizhong and Zuowei General, his title was promoted to Duke, and he was granted an additional 500 households.
Du Xun continued to follow Wang Sengbian in pursuit of Hou Jing until he reached Shitou, where he held a stalemate with the rebels at Jinling.
When the two sides fought, Hou Jing personally led the elite soldiers, charging left and right. Du Juan rushed out from behind the ridge, intercepted and killed Hou Jing's army. Hou Jing was defeated and fled east to Jinling, while Du occupied Stone City.
After Hou Jing's rebellion was put down, Du Yajia added Sanqi Changshi, Zhijie, supervised the military in Jiangzhou, and the governor of Jiangzhou, adding thousands of households to the city.
This month, Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qinzhou governor Yan Chaoyuan in Qin County. Wang Sengbian ordered Du Juan to rush to the rescue, and Chen Ba also led his army from Kamu to join Si Ouyanghe.
They fought against Shilin in Yuanjian. Chen Baxian ordered a volley of powerful crossbows, and Yuan Jian's army retreated. Du Juan took the opportunity to attack and defeated Guo Yuanjian's army, killing more than 10,000 people and capturing more than a thousand alive. Jian gathered up the remaining soldiers and fled.
At this time Shizu was holding Wang Lin in Jiangling, and his subordinates such as Shilu Na and others rebelled in Changsha. Shizu recruited Du Chan and Wang Sengbian to fight together.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, the people fought in the wheel, were defeated, and captured two of their fortresses. Shilu Na and others fled to Changsha to defend, and Du Chan and others surrounded him.
Later, Shilu Na and others surrendered, and Du Juan and Wang Sengbian marched westward to conquer King Wuling. The army arrived and immediately defeated the rebels and put down the rebellion.
So he returned to town, fell ill and died.
Shidan Xiashao said: Du Juan is a member of the Jingzhao family, a descendant of Yuan Kai, his family education has been passed down from generation to generation, and he has been loyal from generation to generation.
Since he was recruited as an official on both sides of the river, he has been praised as being able and honest in his administration; he has been worshiped as a general in Qianyuan, and the world has become peaceful because of this.
The sudden loss made me sad and sad, and the grief was difficult to control.
You can give it to the general of chariots and cavalry, and add a piece of propaganda.
Give silence as a weapon.
There are nine Du Chan brothers. The elder brothers Du Song, Du Cen, Du Qi, Du Qi, Du Yi, Du Xi, Du An and the younger brother You'an are all famous in contemporary times.
Du An's courtesy name is Gongheng.
He has had military talents since he was a child, and he likes to join forces vertically and horizontally to lobby.
During the Taiqing period, Du An and Du Xun returned to Shizu together. Shizu granted Du An the title of Chijie, General Pingbei, and governor of Beiliang Prefecture. He was also granted the title of Marquis of Jiangling County and a settlement of 1,000 households.
Du An asked for permission to lead his troops to attack Xiangyang, and Shizu agreed.
Du An then traveled day and night to attack Xiangyang City first. Before it was conquered, King Yueyang arrived, and Yueyang fled to rely on his brother Du Guo, who was the governor of Nanyang at the time.
Yueyang soon sent troops to capture the city, and Du An and his brother Du Xie were killed together.
Du Youan was the most filial by nature, generous to others, and extremely brave.
During the reign of Zuo Zha, Du You'an and his brother Du Guan joined Shizu. Shizu granted him the title of General Yunhui, governor of West Jingzhou, and the title of Marquis of Huarong County, with a settlement of 1,000 households.
Shizu ordered him to go to Changsha with Pingnan General Wang Sengbian to conquer Hedong Wang Yu and quell the rebellion.
Shi Piao also ordered Du Youan to lead 10,000 elite troops to assist Zuowei General Xu Wensheng in marching eastward to conquer Hou Jing.
When they arrived at Beji, they met Ren Yueyue, the general waiting for Jing, to fight against him. He fought with Ren Diao and was defeated. He killed the puppet official Yi Tongchi Luo Zitong, the Xiangzhou governor Zhao Weifang and others, and sent their heads to Jiangling.
So he marched until he went there and held a stalemate with Hou Jing.
In addition, he sent people to attack Wuchang and pull it out.
Hou Jing crossed Liao from the upper reaches of Luzhou to attack Xu Wensheng and others. You'an and other troops attacked Hou Jing. Hou Jing was defeated and all the ships were captured.
At that time, Hou Jing secretly sent troops to attack and capture Jianye, and captured Lu Zuozhan, the governor of Jianye, and others and brought them back. Xu Wensheng and the army were frightened and panicked. Xu Wensheng fled back from Hankou. All the troops were defeated. Du You'an surrendered to Hou Jing. Hou Jing killed Du You'an because of his erratic behavior.
Du Gong is the son of Du Cen, Du Gong's second brother.
He was very strong and brave when he was young, and was good at using soldiers. During the Taiqing period, he and his uncles joined Shizu. Shizu awarded him the title of Chijie, Zhongwu General, Yunzhou Governor, and the title of Marquis of Zhonglu County, with a settlement of 1,000 households.
His uncle Du Youan followed Wang Zengluan to conquer the King of Return to Tomb and put down the rebellion.
He followed Wang Sengbian down the river and arrived at Baling after Xu Wensheng's army. Hearing that Hou Jing had attacked and captured Yingzhou, he was heading up the river and marching westward. When he was about to reach Baling, Du Chong, Wang Sengbian and others defended Baling and waited for Hou Jing to attack.
Hou Jing went to Baling and besieged it for dozens of days, but could not conquer it and then escaped.
Du Chong moved to the post of Taifu Qing, General Anbei, supervising the military affairs of Dingzhou, and governor of Dingzhou. He was also granted the title of Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi, and added 500 households in the city.
Du Fu continued to follow Wang Sengbian in pursuit of Hou Jing as far as Jiangxia, and besieged the city of Jiangxia.
Hou Jing's general Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled. Du Chong pursued him to Yangpu and captured Song Zixian alive.
In the third year of Dashi, various armies arrived at Gushu. Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian fought against him. Du Chong, Chen Baxian, Wang Lin and others led the elite soldiers to attack and defeated Hou Zijian, so the army arrived at Shitou.
Hou Jing personally led his rebels into battle. Du Chong and all the troops fought together and defeated Hou Jing's rebels, and Hou Jing fled eastward.
After inspecting his military merits, Du Chong found him to be the best, so he was awarded the title of General Pingshu and the governor of Shu Yangzhou, and he was granted an additional 1,000 households.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, Du Chong and Wang Sengbian went to Changsha to conquer Lu Na and others, forcing Lu Na and others to surrender.
He went to Xiling to conquer King Wuling and quelled the rebellion.
After Jiangling was captured, Qi State sent Marquis Zhenyang to inherit the throne of Liang State. After Zhenyang Hou ascended the throne, he appointed Du Chong as the governor of Zhenzhou and the prefect of Wuxing.
He was also awarded the title of General of Zhennan, Commander-in-Chief of all military forces in Southern Yuzhou, Governor of Southern Yuzhou, and Marquis of Liyang County, and was given the rank of Advocate; he was also granted the title of Regular Attendant of Disciplined Cavalry, and General of Zhenshu.
Just as Chen Baxian attacked and captured the capital, he captured Wang Sengbian and killed him.
Du Chong was Wang Sengbian's son-in-law and served as the prefect of Wuxing.
He believed that Chen Baxian was not from a noble family, and his soldiers were disorganized. When handling military affairs, he did not take Chen Baxian into consideration at all. When managing the affairs of the county, he always dealt with Chen Baxian's fellow clan members according to law and discipline without mercy. Chen Baxian hated this and gritted his teeth.
After Wang Sengbian was killed, Du Chong defended Wuxing to resist Chen Baxian, and sent his deputy Du Tai to the Great Wall to attack Chen Bei. Du Tai was defeated by Chen Hao.
Chen Baxian then sent his general Zhou Wenyu to attack Du Chong. Du Chong ordered his cousin Du Beisou to fight, but was defeated by Zhou Wenyu. He then fled to Yixing, and Chen Baxian personally led an army to surround them.
When Qi general Liu Damo and others attacked the capital, Chen Ba was frightened and returned to the capital to make peace with the Qi people.
Du Chong surrendered after hearing that the Qi army had returned to the country, and was killed.
Yin Zichun, whose courtesy name is Youwen, was born in Guzang, Wuwei.
In the last years of Jin Yixi, Yin Zichun's great-grandfather Yin attacked and moved south with Song Gaozu to Nanping, where he settled down.
Yin Zichun's father, Yin Zhibo, lived next to Gaozu, and the two had been very friendly since childhood. Yin Zhibo once entered Gaozu's bedroom and saw the strange brilliance of five colors in the room. He took Gaozu's hand and said: You will be very noble in the future, no longer a minister.
The world is in turmoil, and the one who can calm the people is probably you!
Emperor Gaozu said: I hope you won’t say too much.
As a result, the friendship between the two became more and more profound. Whenever Gaozu needed something, he would get it from Yin Zhibo's place, just like getting it from a warehouse outside his home.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Yin Zhibo was promoted to governor of Liang and Qin states.
Zichun, in the early years of Tianjian, Yin Zichun was recruited from his family to serve as General Xuanhui and Prefect of Xiyang.
During ordinary years, Yin Zichun was promoted to General Mingwei and the governor of Nanliang Prefecture many times. He was also promoted to General Xinwei, governor of the military affairs of the three prefectures of Chitaigui, and governor of Liang and Qin Prefectures.
In the second year of Taiqing, Yin Zichun conquered the rebellious barbarians and put down the rebellion.
He was conscripted as the general of the left guard and moved to the rank of servant.
At the time of Hou Jing's rebellion, Shizu ordered Yin Zichun to follow the leading general Wang Sengbian to Yingzhou to conquer King Shaoling and pacify Yingzhou.
He also marched eastward with Xu Wensheng, the general of the left guard, to conquer Hou Jing. When they arrived at Beji, they met Hou Jing. Yin Zichun fought hard, often ranking first among the troops in military exploits, and defeated Hou Jing many times.
Just as Yingzhou was captured, the army retreated.
In the second year of Dashi, Yin Zichun died in Jiangling.
Sun Hao has been famous since he was a child.
When he first became an official, he was invited by the court to serve as Shangshu Jinbulang.
Yinhao later attached himself to Zhou.
He wrote twenty volumes of "Qiong Lin".
Shi Chen said: Hu Sengyou has long been famous for his military talents. He pulled down the enemy's flag and broke the enemy's formation, and made many military exploits. He even sacrificed his life to maintain his integrity and died in the king's affairs. Even among the loyal and martyrs in ancient times, there is no one who can surpass him.
Xu Wensheng made great achievements initially, but was unable to maintain his existing reputation in the end. This is unjust.
Du Xun understood the principle of change and the appropriate choice of direction. In addition, he was in charge of the army many times, frequently annihilated rebellions, and made outstanding achievements. In the end, he became the hero of the Liang Dynasty's resurgence. He was really moral!
summary:
The lives and military careers of several figures from the Liang Dynasty. Hu Sengyou, a brave champion from Nanyang, served Wei and later returned to Liang, where he was appointed to guard Xiangcheng. After its capture, he returned to Wei but eventually came back to Liang, serving as a prefect with good governance. Despite his poor poetry, he remained confident. He was imprisoned for remonstrating against killing barbarian chiefs but was later released to aid Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing. He defeated Ren Yue, captured him, and caused Hou Jing to flee. He died at 63 from a stray arrow while defending against Wei, leading to the city's fall.

Xu Wensheng, from Pengcheng, led his father's troops to surrender to Liang and became a governor of Ningzhou, where he reformed corrupt barbarian customs. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he was sent eastward but hesitated to fight, influenced by his wife's return from Hou Jing. His army was defeated after Yingzhou's capture, and he fled to Jingzhou. He was imprisoned for corruption and resentment, dying in prison after a taunt from Ren Yue.

Du Chan, from Duling, was the seventh son of Du Huaibao. He joined Shizu and followed Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing, defeating him at Baling and Shitou. He later fought Qi general Guo Yuanjian and suppressed rebellions in Changsha and against King Wuling. He died of illness. His brothers Du An and Du Youan also served, with Du An killed attacking Xiangyang and Du Youan surrendering to and killed by Hou Jing. Du Chong, Du Chan's nephew, was a brave general who defeated Hou Jing's forces, captured Song Zixian, and later resisted Chen Baxian after Wang Sengbian's death, ultimately surrendering and being killed.

Yin Zichun, from Guzang, served as a general and prefect, suppressing barbarian rebellions. He fought with Wang Sengbian and Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing, achieving many victories, but died in Jiangling after the army retreated. The text concludes with a commentary praising Hu Sengyou's loyalty, criticizing Xu Wensheng's failure, and lauding Du Chan's moral choices and achievements.

translation:
Queen Taizong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daqi, Prince of Nanjun, Xiao Dalian; Chen Shurong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daxin of Xunyang; Mrs. Zuo gave birth to Prince Xiao Dalin of Nanhai, and Prince Xiao Dachun of Anlu; Mrs. Xie gave birth to Duke Xiao Daya of Liuyang; Mrs. Zhang They gave birth to Xiao Dazhuang, the king of Xinxing; Xiao Dajun, the king of Xiyang, was born to Bao Zhaohua; Xiao Dawei, the king of Wuning, was born to Mrs. Fan; Xiao Daqiu, the king of Jianping, was born to Chu Xiuhua; Xiao Daxin, the king of Yi'an, was born to Mrs. Chen; Xiao Dazhi, the king of Suijian, was born to Mrs. Zhu.
The deeds of the other sons are not recorded in this book.
Xiao Daxin, king of Xunyang, was named Renshu.
He has been smart and enlightened since childhood and is good at writing articles.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was granted the title of Dangyang Gong because of his status as the emperor's grandson, and was granted a residence of 1,500 households.
In the first year of Datong, he went to Beijing to serve as envoy Chijie, governor of Ying's southern and northern divisions, Dingxin's military forces of the five states, general of light vehicles, and governor of Yingzhou.
Xiao Daxin was only thirteen years old at that time. Because of his young age, Taizong was worried that he would not be able to understand the people's sentiments, so he warned him: No matter how big or small, all matters should be handed over to the Xingfu and state officials who are in charge of the affairs. There is no need to worry about anything.
Although Xiao Daxin does not personally manage state affairs, his opinions are always reasonable. Everyone was amazed and admired.
In the seventh year of Datong, Xiao Daxin was recruited as a servant and a stone garrison.
In the first year of Taiqing, he came to Beijing and served as General Yunhui and governor of Jiangzhou.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing invaded the capital. Xiao Daxin recruited soldiers, and people from far and near joined him. The army reached 10,000 people. He and the troops from the upper reaches of the Yangtze River rushed to the capital to rescue the imperial court.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, the capital city was captured. Xiao Shao, the Marquis of Shangjia, fled south. He read the Emperor's Secret Shao to Xiao Daxin and gave Xiao Daxin the title of "General of Pingnan".
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Daxin was named King of Xunyang and had 2,000 households in the city.
In the past, Zhuang Tie, the prefect of Liyang, led the city to surrender to Hou Jing, and soon he brought his mother to Xiao Daxin. Because Zhuang Tie was his old subordinate, Xiao Daxin treated Zhuang Tie generously and left all matters of leading the army to war to Zhuang Tie, and then appointed Zhuang Tie as the internal historian of Yuzhang.
Hou Jing repeatedly sent troops westward upstream to invade and plunder. Xiao Daxin ordered Zhuang Tie to defeat the invading rebels, so that the rebels could not advance.
At that time, Poyang King Xiao Fan led his army to abandon Hefei and stationed at Zhakou, hoping to wait until all the reinforcements gathered before marching together.
When Xiao Daxin heard the news, he sent someone to invite Xiao Fan to go up the river and march westward, and gave Xiao Fan the city to garrison. The food supplies were very generous, and the two of them worked together to put an end to the chaos.
When Zhuang Tie occupied Yuzhang and rebelled, Xiao Daxin ordered his soldiers to join the army. Wei Yue and others led the army to attack Zhuang Tie. Zhuang Tie was defeated and asked to surrender.
Xiao Si, the eldest son of King Poyang, had friends with Zhuang Tie before. During the war, he praised Zhuang Tie to King Poyang, saying that Zhuang Tie was talented and well versed in strategy. Moreover, he was a veteran general in the army. If he wanted to achieve great things, he should rely on Zhuang Tie's strength. If Zhuang Tie surrenders to King Xunyang of Jiangzhou, he will definitely not be able to save his life. Xiao Si asked King Poyang to send troops to rescue Zhuang Tie.
Xiao Fan, the king of Poyang, listened to Xiao Si's advice and sent general Hou Ti to lead 5,000 elite troops to rescue Zhuang Tie. Hou Ti made a surprise attack at night and attacked Wei Yue and other military camps.
Xiao Daxin was very panicked and frightened when he heard the news. As a result, a rift developed between the two vassal kings, and their hearts were divided and they had different aspirations.
Hou Jing's general Ren Yue attacked the city and reached Huancheng. Xiao Daxin sent Sima Weizhi to lead his army to resist, but was severely defeated.
At that time, Xiao Daxin still had more than a thousand warriors under his command. Everyone advised Xiao Daxin: Since there is no food reserve in Baogao, it will be difficult to hold on to it. It is best to lead Qingqi to Jianzhou and plan to revitalize it later.
Xiao Daxin was hesitant and did not make a decision. His mother Chen Shurong said: Now that the emperor is old and the prince is in good health, you have been away from the court for a long time and do not care to pay homage to the emperor and the prince. Besides, I am old, but you want me to travel long distances and embark on a dangerous road with insufficient food supply. How can I be considered a filial son?
I will not set off after all.
After saying that, he clapped his chest and cried bitterly, so Xiao Daxin stayed and never left.
Xiao Daxin then made an agreement with Ren.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Daxin was killed at the age of twenty-five.
Xiao Dalin, king of Nanhai, was named Renxuan.
In the second year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Ningguo County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
Xiao Dalin has been smart and smart since he was a child.
When he was eleven years old, his biological mother, Mrs. Zuo, passed away. He cried every day, which made him weak and thin, so he was famous for his filial piety.
Later, Xiao Dalin entered Chinese studies, ranked first in the Ming Dynasty's archery examination, was awarded the title of Minister of Zhongshu, and was transferred to Minister of Huangmen.
In the eleventh year of Datong, he was appointed as the chief and also as the minister.
After leaving the capital, he became General Qingche and Grand Administrator of Langye and Pengcheng counties.
Hou Jing rebelled, and Xiao Dalin was appointed by the imperial court as envoy Chijie and General Xuanhui, stationed in Xinting.
Soon he was recruited back to Beijing and stationed at Duanmen, where he oversaw the military affairs in the south of the city.
People who discussed political affairs at that time advised Xiao Dalin to collect private property in order to use it as rewards, but Xiao Dalin said: Property can only be given to scholars, but cattle can be used to reward soldiers.
He ordered to collect cattle and got more than a thousand cattle. With these cattle, he was able to comfort the soldiers in the city.
In the first year of Dabao, Xiao Dalin was granted the title of Prince of Nanhai County and was granted the title of 2,000 households in the town.
Later he went to Beijing and served as envoy Chijie, commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Yangnan and Xuzhou, general Annan, and governor of Yangzhou.
He was also appointed as General Anshu and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
At that time, Zhang Biao organized a rebel army in Kuaiji to oppose Hou Jing. Wu people Lu Linggong, Ying Zuo Meng Qing and others persuaded Xiao Dalin to leave the county and join Zhang Biao.
Xiao Dalin said: If Ji Biao succeeds, he will not provide us with troops; if he suffers setbacks and fails, he will use me as a bargaining chip to escape.
You can't take refuge with Zhang Biao.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Dalin was killed in Wujun. He was twenty-five years old when he died.
Xiao Dalian, the king of Lu County, has the given name Renjing.
He was handsome and cheerful since he was a child. He was good at writing articles, spoke elegantly and gracefully, often had some surprising insights, was proficient in music, and was also good at painting.
In the second year of Datong, Xiao Dalian was granted the title of Duke of Lincheng County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
In the seventh year of Datong, he and King Nanhai entered Chinese studies together, lived together in the Jia Department for the exam, and became the Minister of Zhongshu.
In the tenth year of Datong, Emperor Gaozu visited Seili, and Xiao Dalian and his elder brother Xiao Dalin accompanied him.
Emperor Gaozu asked them: Have you learned how to ride?
They replied: We have not received the destiny, so we dare not learn riding skills without permission.
The high-ranking officials gave them horses to try out. The Xiao Dalian brothers sat on the saddles and drove the horses back and forth. They both mastered the essentials of galloping. Emperor Gaozu was very happy and rewarded them with the horses they rode.
They submitted a memorial to express their gratitude, and the words in the memorial were beautiful.
One day Gaozu said to Taizong: Yesterday I saw Dalin and Dalian. Their demeanor and temperament were very lovely. It was indeed a comfort to me in my old age.
Xiao Dalian was transferred to serve as the Minister of Huangmen, then to the Minister of the Middle School, and soon he also served as the Shitou garrison.
In the first year of Taiqian's reign, he left Beijing to serve as envoy Chijie, General Qingche, and governor of Dongyangzhou.
Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xiao Dalian led 40,000 troops to rescue him.
Taicheng was captured, the reinforcements dispersed, and Xiao Dalian returned to Yangzhou.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, bandits Tian Lingqun from Kuaiji gathered tens of thousands of people to attack Yangzhou. Xiao Dalian ordered soldiers to join the army and Zhang Biao met him and killed Tian Lingqun.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dalian was granted the title of King of Nanjun, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
Hou Jing frequently sent his generals Tang Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack, while Xiao Dalian deployed garrison troops to wait for the enemy.
Just when his general Liu Yi led the city to surrender to the rebels, Xiao Dalian abandoned the city and fled. When he arrived at Xin'an, he was captured by the rebels.
Hou Jing appointed Xiao Dalian as General of Qingche, responsible for conducting affairs in Yangzhou, and moved to General of Pingnan and Governor of Jiangzhou.
After Xiao Dalian was trapped in the hands of the rebels, he often thought about escaping, so he made an appointment with the rebels and said: "I will not participate in the affairs of leading the army and governing the people. If you want to know whether I live or die, just listen to the bells in my house."
This was because he wanted to avoid seeing the traitor less and escape. The traitor also believed him, but his escape failed.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Dalian was killed at the age of twenty-five.
Xiao Dachun, King of Anlu, was named Ren Jing.
He has dabbled in various books since childhood.
He is respectful and filial by nature, has a beautiful appearance, a strong body, and a belt with ten girths.
In the sixth year of Datong, Xiao Dachun was granted the title of Duke of Xifeng County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
He was appointed as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu.
Later he was appointed as General Ningyuan and learned about the military affairs of Shitou garrison.
Hou Jing attacked the capital, and Xiao Dachun fled to Jingkou. As King Shaoling rescued the capital, he fought with the rebels at Zhongshan, and Xiao Dachun was captured by the rebels.
After the capital was captured, in the first year of Dabao, Xiao Dachun was granted the title of Prince of Anlu County, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
He left Beijing as envoy Chijie, General Yunhui, and governor of Dongyangzhou.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Dachun was killed at the age of twenty-two.
Xiao Daya, Duke of Liuyang, was named Renfeng.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Liuyang County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
Xiao Daya was smart and alert since she was a child, with beautiful appearance and good demeanor. Gaozu especially loved her.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, the capital city was captured, and the rebels had climbed onto the city wall. Xiao Daya still ordered his attendants to fight. As the number of rebels gradually increased, he was able to hang himself down from the city wall with a rope.
Xiao Daya became ill and died because of this hatred. She died at the age of seventeen.
The emerging king Xiao Dazhuang was named Renli.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Gaotang County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
In the first year of his reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Xingxing County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
He left the capital and served as envoy Chijie, governor of Yu Tusu and other military affairs, general Xuanyi, and governor of Southern Xuzhou.
Dabao was killed in the autumn of the second year at the age of eighteen.
Xiao Dagou, King of Xiyang, was named Renfu.
He is honest and steady by nature and does not play casually.
When he was seven years old, Emperor Gaozu once asked him what book he had read, and he replied that he should study "Poetry".
Emperor Gaozu ordered him to recite it. When he recited it, his voice was clear and loud, so Emperor Gaozu rewarded him with a scroll of calligraphy written by Wang Xizhi.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dagou was granted the title of King of Xiyang County and was granted a settlement of 2,000 households.
He left the capital and served as General Xuanhui and Danyang Yin.
In the second year of Dashi, he was appointed as the governor of Yangzhou, but his title of general remained unchanged.
In the autumn of the Qian year, Xiao Dagou was killed at the age of thirteen.
King Xiao Dawei of Wuning was named Renrong.
Her appearance and temperament are both beautiful, and her eyebrows are as painted.
In the first year of Dabao, he was granted the title of King of Wuning County and had 2,000 households in the town.
In the second year of Dabao's reign, he left the capital and became General Xinwei and Danyang Yin.
In the autumn of this year, Xiao Dawei was killed at the age of thirteen.
Jianping Wang Xiao Daqiu's courtesy name is Renjue.
In the first year of Dabao's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jianping County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
Xiao Daqiu is smart and precocious by nature.
When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Emperor Gaozu had always sincerely believed in Buddhism. Every time he swore an oath and made a wish, he often said: If there are any sufferings that sentient beings should suffer, I, Xiao Yan, will bear them all.
Xiao Daqiu was just seven years old at that time. He was surprised when he heard what he said, so he said to his mother: If the emperor is like this, how dare I refuse to suffer?
Therefore, when paying homage to the Buddha at six o'clock in the morning, at noon, at sunset, at the beginning of the night, at the middle of the night, and at the end of the night, he also said: All the suffering and retribution that sentient beings should suffer will be borne by me, Lu Quebi, on your behalf.
This is how he was smart enough to meet people at a young age.
In the second year, he left Beijing and served as general of light vehicles and military commander of Shitousheng.
In the autumn of this year, Xiao Daqiu was killed at the age of eleven.
Xiao Daxin, King of Nghe An, also had the courtesy name Renlang.
When he was four years old, his mother, Mrs. Chen, passed away. He missed his mother and became sad and haggard, just like an adult mourning.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, during the mourning period, he went to greet Tai Sai, crying softly and unable to control himself. Seeing this scene, all the attendants on the left and right also covered their faces and cried.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dating was granted the title of King of Yi'an County and was granted a settlement of 2,000 households.
In the second year of Zuoxuan's reign, he left the capital to serve as General Ningyuan and Governor of Langye and Pengcheng counties. He was killed before he could go to his post. He was eleven years old when he died.
Xiao Dazhi, king of Suijian, had the courtesy name Renying.
He has been brave and strong since he was a child, with courage and courage. After the capital was captured, he said with emotion: The real man will destroy these thieves.
The wet nurse was frightened, covered his mouth and said to him: Don't speak carelessly, otherwise disaster will come.
Xiao Dazhi smiled and said: The disaster is not caused by these words.
In the first year of Dabin, Xiao Dazhi was granted the title of Prince of Suijian County, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
In the second year of Dashi, he served as General Ningyuan and was killed. He was ten years old when he died.
The sons of the ancestors: Concubine Xu gave birth to a loyal and strong son, Xiao Fang, etc.; Wang died and gave birth to a Zhenhui son, Xiao Fangzhu; the concubine Prince Xiao Fangju, this book does not record his biological mother, but there is another biography about him; Concubine Xia Xian gave birth to the respectful emperor.
None of the other disciples have been passed down in this book.
Xiao Fang, the Zhongzhuang prince, is the eldest son of Shizu.
The mother is Concubine Xu.
Xiao Fang and others have been smart since childhood and have outstanding talents. They are good at riding horses and archery, and are especially good at coming up with some ingenious ideas.
He naturally loves mountains, forests, springs and rocks, especially a leisurely and secluded life.
I once wrote an article in which I said: Human life in this world is just as short-lived as a white horse encountering a gap.
A pot of wine is enough to nourish your temperament; a basket of food is enough to make your body comfortable.
What is the difference between living among basil and being buried in a ravine after death, and sleeping in a tile coffin or a stone coffin?
I once dreamed that I turned into a fish and then a crow.
Nothing can compare to the joy of being in a dream, and the worries after waking up are not as heavy as anything else. It's really because I'm so far behind Yuwu.
So the fish floats and the crows fly, letting their own temperament flow, while my progress and retreat are always under control. I raise my hands for fear of being touched, and move my feet for fear of falling.
If I could always hang out with fish and birds, then I would leave the world without a care, just as easily as taking off my shoes.
At first, Xu Maggot lost the emperor's favor because of jealousy, and Xiao Fang and others were frightened and uneasy. When Shizu heard about this situation, he hated Xiao Fang and others even more. Xiao Fang and others were even more frightened, so they wrote a treatise to express their aspirations.
When Gaozu wanted to see the eldest son of the kings, Shizu sent Xiao Fang and others to the capital to serve Gaozu. Xiao Fang and others boarded the ship happily, hoping to avoid humiliation and relieve their worries.
When the boat arrived at Yaoshui, Hou Jing was rebelling. The ancestor summoned him back. Xiao Fang and others started a memorial and said: In the past, Shen Sheng did not care about life. How could Fang and others care about life?
When Shizu read Xiao Fang and others' memorial, he sighed. Knowing that Xiao Fang and others had no intention of returning, he assigned Xiao Fang and others 10,000 infantry and cavalry and ordered him to rescue the capital.
Every time the rebels came to attack, Xiao Fang and others would brave the arrows and go to the battlefield in person.
After the palace city was captured, Xiao Fang and others returned to Jingzhou, gathered troops, and won the hearts of the people. The ancestors were amazed by his talents.
Xiao Fang and others also encouraged everyone to build city walls and fences to prepare for danger.
After it was completed, the towers and battlements were connected for more than seventy miles.
Seeing this scene, Shizu was very happy. He entered the palace and said to Concubine Xu: If there is another son with such talent, I have nothing to worry about.
Concubine Xu did not answer and left in tears.
Shizu was very angry about this, so he listed Xu Fei's unruly behavior one by one, and wrote it down and published it in the main cabinet.
