summary:
This historical text records the lineage and fates of the sons of Emperor Taizong and Shizu during a period of rebellion. Queen Taizong bore Prince Xiao Daqi and Xiao Dalian; other consorts and ladies bore numerous other princes, including Xiao Daxin, Xiao Dalin, Xiao Dachun, Xiao Daya, Xiao Dazhuang, Xiao Dajun, Xiao Dawei, Xiao Daqiu, Xiao Daxin, and Xiao Dazhi. The deeds of some sons are not recorded.

Xiao Daxin, King of Xunyang, was intelligent and a skilled writer. Ennobled as a duke at age thirteen, he was appointed to military and gubernatorial posts. Despite his youth, his opinions were wise. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he raised a 10,000-man army to rescue the capital. After the capital fell, he was made King of Xunyang. He relied on his former subordinate Zhuang Tie, who later rebelled. A conflict arose with King Poyang, who aided Zhuang Tie, causing a rift. After a military defeat, Xiao Daxin hesitated to flee, persuaded by his mother to stay. He was killed at age twenty-five.

Xiao Dalin, King of Nanhai, was also intelligent and known for filial piety after his mother's death. He held various official posts. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he was stationed at Xinting and later oversaw military affairs. He collected cattle to reward soldiers. He was made King of Nanhai. He refused to join a rebel army, deeming it unwise. He was killed at age twenty-five.

Xiao Dalian, King of Nanjun, was handsome, a skilled writer and painter. He and his brother Xiao Dalin impressed Emperor Gaozu with their riding skills. He held ministerial posts and led 40,000 troops to rescue the capital during the rebellion. After the capital fell, he defended Yangzhou from bandits. He was made King of Nanjun. Captured by rebels after a subordinate's betrayal, he was appointed to posts but plotted escape. He was killed at age twenty-five.

Xiao Dachun, King of Anlu, was well-read, filial, and physically strong. He held posts and was captured by rebels while fleeing. He was made King of Anlu and later killed at age twenty-two. Xiao Daya, Duke of Liuyang, was beloved by Gaozu. During the capital's fall, he fought rebels until overwhelmed and died from illness at age seventeen. Xiao Dazhuang, King of Xinxing, was killed at age eighteen. Xiao Dajun, King of Xiyang, was honest and recited poetry for Gaozu. He was killed at age thirteen. Xiao Dawei, King of Wuning, was handsome and killed at age thirteen. Xiao Daqiu, King of Jianping, was precocious and, at age seven, vowed to bear others' suffering. He was killed at age eleven. Xiao Daxin, King of Yi'an, mourned his mother deeply as a child. He was killed at age eleven before assuming his post. Xiao Dazhi, King of Suijian, was brave and vowed to destroy rebels. He was killed at age ten.

The text also records Shizu's sons. Xiao Fang, the Zhongzhuang prince, was intelligent and loved nature. He wrote a treatise expressing his desire for a carefree life. After his mother lost favor, he felt endangered. He led troops to rescue the capital and later to conquer the King of Hedong, but was defeated and drowned at age twenty-two. Shizu was not saddened by his death but later posthumously honored him. Xiao Fangzhu, the Zhenhui prince, was erudite and favored. After his brother's death, he was appointed to guard Jiangxia but neglected duties, enjoying leisure. He was captured by a surprise rebel attack and killed. The historian laments that these princes, though ennobled, were imprisoned by bandits and died untimely deaths during the era's chaos.

Emperor Gaozu Wu, named Yan, with the courtesy name Shuda and nickname Lian'er, was a descendant of Xiao He, the Han Dynasty Prime Minister, from Zhongduli in Nanlanling. His lineage traced back through generations of officials, including his father Shunzhi, who was granted the title of Marquis of Linxiang County for assisting the emperor. Gaozu was born in the eighth year of the Ming Dynasty in Moling County, displaying unusual traits like connected bones in his legs, a protruding head, and a tattoo of "Martial" on his right hand. He grew up knowledgeable, skilled in strategy, and talented in civil and military affairs, often surrounded by clouds and mist in his residence.

He began his official career as a king of Baling and was later promoted to general. Wang Jian predicted he would become a poet within thirty years. Gaozu socialized with notable figures like Xie Tiao and Wang Rong, known as the Eight Friends. Wang Rong respected him greatly, believing he would rule the world. After his father's death, Gaozu served as General Ningshuo to guard Shouchun, then as crown prince's concubine and assistant minister. He was granted the title of male from Jianyang County for his role in establishing the emperor.

In the second year of Jianwu, the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Sizhou. Gaozu, as champion general, led reinforcements. Despite fear among the troops, he marched ahead, surprising the Northern Wei army and forcing them to retreat. He was later appointed as Sima and Grand Administrator of Huailing. In the fourth year, he defended against another invasion, leading his army to resist and kill nearly a hundred enemies, returning intact while others suffered losses. He was then appointed to conduct affairs in Yongzhou.

After Emperor Ming's death, six officials took turns governing, causing chaos. Gaozu warned his brother Zhang Hongce about the dangers of multiple rulers, predicting internal conflict. He advised gathering his brothers and preparing for potential turmoil. He secretly manufactured military equipment and stored bamboo in Tanxi River for shipbuilding. In the second year of Yongyuan, after Xiao Yi's murder, Gaozu summoned his staff and planned an uprising. He recruited over 10,000 soldiers, 1,000 horses, and 3,000 ships, building warships from bamboo.

Gaozu sent letters to various states, anticipating that Liu Shanyang, sent by Donghun to attack Xiangyang, would be killed. His strategy succeeded, and Shanyang was beheaded. Gaozu then marched from Xiangyang in February of the third year, leaving his brothers to guard key cities. He issued a proclamation condemning the cruel ruler for his tyranny, including killing loyal ministers, indulging in debauchery, and causing widespread suffering. He called for a righteous uprising to restore order.

The army advanced, defeating enemy forces at various locations. Gaozu's forces captured key cities, and many officials surrendered. In December, Donghun was beheaded, and Gaozu entered the martial arts hall, issuing orders for a general amnesty and reforms. He abolished harsh taxes and punishments, promoted frugality, and established new regulations. He was appointed as Grand Sima and Duke of Jian'an, later promoted to Duke of Liang with nine gifts.

Gaozu refused the title of King of Liang multiple times but eventually accepted after repeated requests from officials and auspicious signs. He implemented reforms in the election system, emphasizing talent over family background. In April, Queen Xuande issued an order for the abdication of the Southern Qi throne to King Liang, citing his virtues and achievements. Gaozu initially declined but eventually accepted, becoming Emperor Gaozu of the Liang Dynasty.

The text declares that the Qi dynasty had exhausted its fortune, and prosperity was imminent, with heaven's inspiration bestowed upon Xiao Yan. It justifies the dynastic change by citing historical precedents like Yao, Shun, Han, Wei, and Jin, emphasizing that rulers are chosen based on worthiness, not hereditary right. The Qi monarch's cruelty and corruption led to chaos, prompting Xiao Yan to raise an army, defeat the tyrant, and establish a new ruler. Auspicious signs from the sun, stars, and mountains confirmed the shift in destiny, and officials urged him to accept the throne. Despite his humility, he yielded to heaven's will and the people's wishes, performing the Zen ritual and ascending to the Tai Chi Palace.

summary:
Emperor Taizong, named Gang, was the third son of Emperor Gaozu and half-brother of Prince Zhaoming. Born in Xianyang Hall in 464 AD, he was granted the title King of Jin'an in 467 AD with 8,000 households. Over the years, he held various military and civil posts, including General Yunhui, governor of multiple states, and commander-in-chief of military affairs. He was appointed crown prince in 531 AD after Prince Zhaoming's death and became emperor in 549 AD upon Emperor Gaozu's death.

Upon ascending the throne, he issued edicts to reduce sentences, release northern slaves, and appoint officials. He faced challenges such as rebellions, famines, and invasions. In 550 AD, Hou Jing forced him to visit Xizhou and later proclaimed himself prime minister. Hou Jing deposed Taizong as King of Jin'an in 551 AD, imprisoned him, and killed many of his family members. Taizong died in Yongfu Province at age 49, suffocated by a bag of soil. He was posthumously named Emperor Ming, later changed to Emperor Jianwen.

Taizong was exceptionally intelligent, able to compose at age six, and known for his broad-mindedness and literary talents. He wrote numerous works, including "The Biography of Prince Zhaoming" and "Changchun Yiji." Despite his virtues, he was controlled by traitors and met a tragic end.

Now you write a letter saying that the granaries in the city are empty, the people are poor, and robbers and thieves are rampant. You are the prime minister and cannot govern. You ask for grain and rice to atone for your sins and to retire and become a commoner.
You know well that the people are in distress, but you ask for an increase in taxes and sway the people. Now that the people are in danger, you want to resign from your position. Who do you blame?
If you take it for granted, you can return home!
Gen Qing was a simple man. When he saw the emperor's edict asking him to go home, he thought he had the emperor's permission and wanted to return the prime minister's seal ribbon.
Shi Qing believed that being severely reprimanded by the emperor and finally sent home was the harshest criticism. Some people advised Shi Qing to commit suicide.
Shi Qing was frightened and didn't know what to do, so he went to the court again to manage things.
When Gen Qing was the prime minister, he was very scheming and had no talent.
Mi died more than three years later and was named Tianhou.
The second son Shi De is Shi Qing's favorite.
The emperor let Shi De inherit the title, and later he was appointed Taichang. He was dismissed for breaking the law and the feudal state was abolished.
When Shi Qing was Prime Minister, there were thirteen people among his descendants who were serving as minor officials up to two thousand shi.
After Gen Qing's death, some people were deposed for committing crimes, and the virtue of filial piety and respect also declined.
Wei Wan, a native of Dai Ren Ling, was a knight with outstanding chariot skills. He followed Sai Tong and was promoted to the rank of Zhonglang General due to his merit. He was honest and cautious and had no other ambitions.
When Xiao Liangcha was the crown prince, he summoned the emperor's close friends to have a drink, but Xun excused himself because he was ill.
Before Secha died, he told Emperor Xiaojing: Wei Wan is a highly respected person, treat him well.
When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he did not ask about Wei Wan's situation for more than a year. Wei Wan encouraged himself to be cautious every day.
Emperor Jing went on a tour to Shanglin, and ordered Zhonglang to be a charioteer. When he came back, he said, "Do you know why I can let you be a charioteer?"
Wei Wan said: I am a charioteer in the state of Dai. I was lucky enough to be promoted due to my merits and became a general of the rank and file. I don’t know why.
The emperor asked: I called you when I was the prince, why did you refuse to come?
He replied: This is really a capital crime, I am sick.
The emperor gave him the sword. Wei Wan said: The late emperor gave me six swords, and I dare not accept this reward again.
The emperor said: "Swords, people often exchange them, do you still keep them to this day?" Wei Wan said: "They are all here."
The emperor sent someone to fetch six swords. The swords were all well preserved and had never been worn.
When a Lang officer made a mistake and was criticized, Wei Wan often took the blame himself, did not argue with other generals, and often gave up his military merits to other generals.
The emperor believed that he was honest, loyal and magnanimous, so he appointed Wei Wan as the tutor of Liu De, the king of Hejian.
When the vassal states of Wu and Chu rebelled, the emperor issued an edict to appoint Wei Wan as general. He led the army in Hejian to attack the states of Wu and Chu and made military exploits. The emperor promoted him to lieutenant.
Three years later, Wei Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Jianling because of his military exploits.
In the second year, the emperor deposed the prince and executed Li Qing and others.
The emperor thought that Wei Wan was a kind elder and could not bear to send him, so he ordered Wei Wan to retire and return to his hometown, while Zhi Du was responsible for arresting Li Qing and others.
After the incident was over, the emperor appointed King Micellar as the prince and ordered Wei Wan to be the prince's tutor. Later, he was promoted to the imperial censor.
Five years later, when Tao Hou Liu She was replaced as prime minister, Wei Wan only reported routine matters and did not discuss anything else.
However, since he became an official until he was promoted to prime minister, he has been unable to build or abolish anything.
The emperor believed that Wei Wan was a kindhearted person and could assist the prince, so he respected and favored him and rewarded him with many things.
Wei Wan served as prime minister for three years. After Emperor Jing's death, Emperor Wu ascended the throne.
In the middle of the Jianyuan year, because officials imprisoned many innocent people when Emperor Jing was ill, Wei Wan refused to redress the grievances of the people, so he was dismissed.
After Wei Wan died, Mi was named Aihou.
His son Wei Xin inherited his title, but was convicted of insufficient tribute for sacrifices, and the princely state was abolished.
There is no doubt that he is from Nanyang. As a Langguan, he served Emperor Wen.
Someone of his fellow-shalangguan asked for leave to go home and mistakenly took away the gold of his fellow-shalangguan.
Soon his colleague Shalang found out that he had made groundless speculations about Zhi Busuo. Zhi Busuo apologized and said that he had indeed taken the gold, so he bought the gold to compensate him.
Later, the official Lang who took leave returned and returned the gold to the man who had lost the gold. This made the man who had lost the gold very ashamed, so he called Zhi Busuo an elder.
Soon, Zhi Busuo was promoted to a middle doctor.
When he went to court to pay homage to the emperor, some people slandered him and said: "Zhi is handsome, but how could he have an affair with his sister-in-law?"
After hearing this, Zhi Buyi said: I have no brother.
However, he never defends himself.
When Wu and Chu rebelled, Zhi Busuo led an army of two thousand stones to attack the rebels.
In the first year of Emperor Jing's reign, he was appointed as the imperial censor.
When the emperor recorded his military exploits in quelling the Wu and Chu rebellions, he granted Zhi the title of Marquis of Sai.
Emperor Wu ascended the throne and was dismissed together with Prime Minister Wei Wan for faults.
Zhi Buyi is proficient in the theory of inaction in Laozi.
When he is an official, he does everything according to the previous system, lest people know about his achievements as an official.
He doesn't like to build a reputation and people call him an elder.
After Zhi Buyi's death, Mi was given the title of Marquis of Xin.
The throne was passed to his grandson Zhi Pengzu. He was convicted of insufficient money for the sacrifice and the feudal state was abolished.
Zhou Ren's ancestor was from Rencheng.
He was summoned by the emperor because of his excellent medical skills.
When Emperor Jing was the crown prince, he was a sacrificer and was promoted to Taizhong doctor through meritorious service.
When Emperor Jing just came to the throne, he worshiped Zhou Ren as his doctor.
Zhou Ren is a deep and steady person and does not reveal other people's secrets.
He usually wore patched and dirty clothes and deliberately showed that he was unclean, so he was favored and entered the palace bedroom.
The emperor was playing with the concubines in the harem. Zhou Ren was often beside him, but he never spoke.
The emperor sometimes asked people about their merits. Zhou Ren said: The emperor himself can observe it.
Although Zhou Ren knew the shortcomings of others, he did not slander them in front of the emperor, that's all.
Emperor Jing personally visited his home twice.
His family moved to Yangling.
The emperor gave many rewards, but he often declined and did not dare to accept them.
He also refused to accept bribes from princes and ministers.
After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was respected as a minister of the late emperor.
Zhou Ren was dismissed from his post due to illness and returned home with a salary of 2,000 shi to provide for his old age. His descendants all became high-ranking officials.
Zhang Shi, courtesy name Zhao, was the youngest son of Anqiu Hou Jiyue, a great hero.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Tuiya assisted the prince by studying the science of punishment names, but he was very kind-hearted.
When Liangtong was in power, he respected him very much and served as Jiuqing.
During the reign of You Wusu, he replaced Dong Guo as the imperial censor.
As an official, Zhang Ou never punished others, but only acted with sincerity and kindness.
His subordinates considered him an elder and did not dare to deceive him too much.
When he reported a case, he would return whatever could be returned; if he could not, he would weep for the sinner and seal the document as he could not bear to read it.
He cares about people like that.
Zhang Ou was old and asked to retire, but the emperor still gave him the salary of a doctor or above to go home and spend his old age.
The family lives in Yangling.
His descendants are all high officials.
Praise: King Kong said: A gentleman should talk less and do more. Isn't this what it means to fall into the Five Stars, build the Linghou, fortify the fortress, and withdraw from the army?
Therefore, educating others can achieve the goal without being harsh, and being an official can govern the country without being dignified.
As for Shi Jian's laundry, Zhou Ren wore torn clothes and diapers, and was ridiculed by gentlemen.
summary:
Several officials from the Han dynasty, beginning with Wan Shijun (Shi Fen), a man from Zhao who served Emperor Gaozu at age fifteen due to his respectful demeanor. He rose through ranks, becoming Prince Taifu and later Jiuqing under Emperor Jing, who named him Lord Wan Shi for his family’s collective high salaries. Wan Shijun was known for extreme caution and filial piety, retiring in old age but maintaining strict rituals, such as bowing at palace gates and fasting when descendants erred. His sons, especially Shi Jian and Shi Qing, emulated his virtues. Shi Jian, a filial son, washed his father’s clothes secretly and served as Lang Zhongling, while Shi Qing became prime minister under Emperor Wu, though he was passive and avoided policy advice, leading to criticism during crises like refugee migrations. Shi Qing was eventually dismissed but died later. His descendants’ filial piety declined over time.

Wei Wan, a charioteer from Dai, rose to Zhonglang General through merit and caution. He served Emperor Jing, who valued his honesty, appointing him as prince’s tutor and later prime minister. Wei Wan avoided innovation, focusing on routine, and was dismissed under Emperor Wu for failing to redress grievances. Zhi Busuo, a Lang official under Emperor Wen, was known for not defending himself against slander, such as false accusations of incest. He became Marquis of Sai for quelling the Wu-Chu rebellion but was dismissed with Wei Wan. Zhou Ren, a physician from Rencheng, served Emperor Jing as a doctor, known for secrecy and humility, refusing bribes and rewards. He retired with a pension. Zhang Shi (Zhang Ou), a son of a marquis, served as imperial censor under Emperor Wu, practicing leniency and weeping for condemned prisoners, retiring with honors. The text concludes with a praise emphasizing silent virtue and criticizing excessive displays like Shi Jian’s laundry or Zhou Ren’s torn clothes.

translation:
Dongfang Shuo, courtesy name Manqian, was born in Yanci County, Pingyuan County.
Not long after Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he asked the world to recommend scholars with talents such as integrity, virtuousness, and literature, and appointed them with special positions. Scholars from all over the world wrote letters to discuss the gains and losses of national affairs. As soon as Dongfang Shuo arrived in Chang'an, he wrote a letter saying: I, Dongfang Shuo, lost his parents when he was young and was raised by his brother and sister-in-law.
He started studying at the age of thirteen and learned writing and note-taking in three years.
Learned fencing at the age of fifteen.
At the age of sixteen, he studied the Book of Songs and Shangshu and recited 220,000 words.
At the age of nineteen, he studied Sun Wu's Art of War, and recited 220,000 words on battle formations, control of the advance and retreat of troops during battles, etc.
I memorized a total of 440,000 words.
He is also often familiar with Zilu's remarks.
I am twenty-two years old, nine feet three inches tall, my eyes are as bright as hanging pearls, my teeth are as neat and white as strings of shells, I am as brave as Meng Ben, as agile as Qing Ji, as honest as Uncle Bao, and as trustworthy as Weisheng.
A person like this can be a minister of the emperor. My minister Dongfang Shuo risked his life to pay homage to the emperor again.
Dongfang Shuo's letter was not modest, but he praised and promoted himself. However, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty thought that he was a great man and ordered him to stay with Shao in the Gongche Mansion. However, his salary was meager and he could not receive an interview from Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
After a long time, Dongfang Shuo once coaxed the dwarf who guarded the royal horse pen and said: The emperor thinks that you people are of no use to the court. Of course, you cannot keep up with others in farming. You are an official above the people and cannot manage civil affairs. You are not qualified to fight with soldiers when you join the army. You are of no use to the country. You will only waste food and clothing. Now the emperor wants to kill you all.
The dwarfs were very frightened and cried.
Dongfang Shuo instigated them and said: The emperor is about to pass by here, you must kowtow and apologize.
After meeting for a while, they heard that the emperor was passing by, and the dwarfs all knelt on the ground and kowtowed in tears. The emperor asked: Why are you doing this?
The dwarfs replied: Dongfang Shuo said that the emperor wants to kill us all.
The emperor knew that Dongfang Shuohuahua had a lot of intestines, so he summoned Dongfang Shuo and asked him: Why did you threaten those dwarfs?
Dongfang Shuo replied: My minister Dongfang Shuo will say it even when he is alive, and he will say it even after he is dead.
The dwarf is more than three feet tall and his salary is two hundred and forty yuan for a bag of millet.
The minister Dongfang Shuo is more than nine feet tall, and his salary is a bag of millet, worth two hundred and forty yuan.
The dwarf was starving to death, and his minister Dongfang Shuo was starving to death.
If my words can be accepted, I hope you will change your etiquette towards me; if not, please let me go home and don't let me eat rice from Chang'an in vain.
Emperor Wu laughed when he heard this, so he asked Dongfang Shuo to wait for Shao Jin Mamen, and gradually gained the emperor's closeness.
Emperor Wu once asked some magicians who were good at divination to cover the gecko under a basin and asked them to guess what it was, but they couldn't guess it. Dongfang Shuo introduced himself and said: I once studied "Yi", please allow me to guess what it is.
So he arranged the yarrow into various hexagrams and replied: I think it is a dragon without horns, but I think it is a snake with legs, its limbs are connected by pulses, and it is good at climbing walls. This thing is either a gecko or a lizard.
The emperor said: You guessed it right.
Give him ten pieces of silk.
He was also asked to guess other things, and he guessed correctly every time. He was given silk every time.
At that time, there was a favored actor Guo Sheren in the palace. He was very funny and often accompanied Emperor Wu. He said: Dongfang Shuo is too crazy. It was just a lucky guess. There is no real magic.
I hope to let Dongfang Shuo guess again. If he guesses correctly, he will give me a hundred lashes; if he guesses incorrectly, he will give me silk.
So he put the parasitic thing growing on the tree under the pot and asked Dongfang Shuo to guess what it was. Dongfang Shuo said: It is Baosou.
Guo Sheren said: I really know that Dongfang Shuo will not guess correctly.
Dongfang Shuo said: Raw meat is called 荍, dried meat is called preserved meat, attached to a tree is called parasite, and covered under a basin is called dou sau.
The emperor ordered Chang Jian to whip Guo Sheren. Guo Sheren was in unbearable pain and howled loudly.
Dongfang Shuo laughed at him and said: Hey, there is no hair on his mouth, he is screaming, and his butt is getting higher and higher.
Guo Sheren said angrily: Dongfang Shuo dared to slander and insult the emperor's attendants. He should be sentenced to death for abandoning the market.
The emperor asked Dongfang Shuo: Why did you slander and insult him?
Dongfang Shuo replied: I dare not slander or insult him, I just told him a riddle. The emperor asked: What riddle are you talking about?
Dongfang Shuo said: The hairless mouth is a dog hole; the cry is the cry of a mother bird when feeding her chicks; the buttocks are getting higher and higher, which is the look of a crane lowering its head to peck at food.
Guo Sheren was not convinced and said, "I hope to ask Dongfang Shuo a riddle as well. If he doesn't know it, he should also be whipped."
He immediately made up a riddle with homophonic sounds and said: Ling Huhan, Lao Botu, Yiyouya, Biaopanya.
What is said?
Dongfang Shuo said: Ling is an order.
Pots are used to hold things.
It means the teeth are not straight.
Lao is an old man that everyone respects.
Bai is the palace of ghosts.
Painting is a road that is soaked.
Iyoya's words were slurred.
Biaopanya is a fight between two dogs.
Dongfang Shuo answered Guo She's riddles in the world, with many clever and clever changes. No riddle could stump him, and everyone present was very surprised.
The emperor appointed Dongfang Shuo as the Chang Shilang, and he gained the favor and favor of Emperor Wu.
After a long time, on a doggy day, Emperor Wu ordered that meat be rewarded to the attendant officials.
The high official did not come to divide the meat until nightfall, so Dongfang Shuo drew his sword and cut the meat alone, saying to his colleagues: "I should go home early in the dog days of summer. Please allow me to accept the emperor's reward."
Then he wrapped the meat in his arms and left.
Daguancheng reported this matter to the emperor.
When Dongfang Shuo entered the palace, Emperor Wu said: Yesterday, you gave me meat, but you cut the meat with your sword and left without waiting for the order to be issued. Why is this?
Dongfang Shuo took off his hat and knelt down to apologize.
The emperor said: Sir, stand up and blame yourself.
Dongfang Shuo paid his respects again and said: Dongfang Shuo!
Dongfang Shuo!
How rude to accept a reward without waiting for the order to be issued!
Drawing a sword to cut flesh, how heroic!
Not much meat is cut, but how honest it is!
How kind it is to go home and give meat to your wife to eat!
The emperor smiled and said: Mr. Jean blames himself, but he actually praises himself!
He also gave him a stone of wine and a hundred catties of meat and asked him to go home and give them to his wife.
At the beginning, in the third year of Jianyuan, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty began to travel incognito, traveling to Chiyang Palace in the north, Huangshan Palace in the west, Changyang Palace in the south, and Yichun Palace in the east.
Traveling in private is often done every year when the new wine is brewed and drank in the ancestral temple.
In August and September, the emperor agreed to wait at the gate of the palace with his attendants, regular attendants, and martial cavalry, as well as the good men from Longxi County and Beidi County in Shaoguan who were good at riding and shooting. Therefore, the title of "Qimen" came from this time.
When Emperor Wu traveled incognito, he would wait ten quarters at night before setting off, often pretending to be Cao Shou, Marquis of Pingyang.
At dawn the next day, when they arrived at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain, they shot deer, pigs, foxes and rabbits, or struck bears with their bare hands, running through the rice fields. The farmers shouted and cursed loudly, gathered together, and complained to the magistrates of Yuxian and Duxian counties.
The county magistrate went to the hunting place and asked to see Pingyang Hou. The attendants on horseback wanted to whip the magistrate.
The county magistrate was furious, and his subordinates scolded and stopped him. Several horsemen who were hunting were detained, so they took out the emperor's royal belongings and struggled for a long time before they were able to leave.
At the beginning, the emperor left the palace late at night and returned the next evening. Later, he carried food for five days. He did not return to the capital until the fifth day when it was time to go to Changxin Palace to see the Queen Mother.
Emperor Wu liked this kind of hunting in disguise very much. After that, the people at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain learned that the emperor often went hunting incognito, but Emperor Wu was still under pressure from the Queen Mother and did not dare to travel far.
The Prime Minister and Censor knew the emperor's intentions, so he sent Lieutenant You Fu to patrol east of Changyang Palace, and ordered You Neishi to recruit civilians and go to the place where the emperor hunted to wait for orders.
Later, dressing rooms were privately set up for the emperor, and palace staff were also assigned. A total of twelve dressing rooms were set up from the south of Xuanqu Palace for the emperor to rest and change during the day, and to stay in various palaces at night. Emperor Wu often visited Changyang, Wuzha, Beiyang, Xuanqu and other palaces.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty thought that the journey was long and hard and hated by the people, so he sent King Wuqiu Shou, the Taizhong doctor, and two people who knew arithmetic to collect the area south of Acheng, Yanliyishu, and west of Yichun Palace. The total number of acres of farmland and the converted value of the farmland were compiled into a book. He planned to build Shanglin Garden here to connect it with Zhongnan Mountain.
Emperor Wu also ordered the lieutenants and internal historians to set aside wasteland belonging to the county, hoping to compensate the farmers in Guo and Du counties.
King Wuqiu Shou reported what he had done to the emperor. The emperor was overjoyed and praised him for a job well done.
At that time Dongfang Shuo was nearby and admonished the emperor:
I heard that if a man is humble, quiet, and prudent, heaven will show retribution and repay him with blessings; if a man is arrogant and extravagant, heaven will also show retribution and repay him with disasters.
Now that your majesty is building a terrace and gallery, you are worried that it will not be high enough; your hunting area will not be wide enough.
If heaven does not bring disaster, then the three auxiliary areas can be used as His Majesty's gardens. Why limit it to Gaixia, E, Du and other places?
Luxury went beyond etiquette, and heaven brought disasters. Although Shanglin Garden was small, I thought it was too big.
Zhongnan Mountain is a dangerous place in the world, with the Yangtze River and Huaihe River to the south, and the Yellow River and Weishui River to the north. This place stretches from Yanshui and Longshan to the west of Shang and Luo counties. The land is fertile and the products are rich.
When the Han Dynasty was established, he left Sanhe and lived west of Ba River and Tong River. His capital was Chang'an, south of Jing River and Wei River. This area is called Tianxia Mountain! The land of land and sea is a land with abundant products. The reason why Qin was able to surrender to Xirong and annex the six kingdoms of Shandong was because it occupied this land.
This mountain produces jade, gold, silver, copper, iron and other minerals, as well as Yuzhang, sandalwood, eucalyptus and other precious woods. It is a strange and strange thing, and its origin cannot be explored. This mountain contains the raw materials for hundreds of industries, and it is a treasure land on which all peoples depend for prosperity.
It is also rich in japonica rice, pears, chestnuts, mulberries, hemp, and bamboo shoots. The soil is suitable for growing ginger and taro, and the water is rich in frogs and fish. The poor people rely on these to have enough food and clothing, and do not have to worry about hunger or cold.
Therefore, the land between Feng and Dy is known as fertile soil, and the price of this land is one pound of gold per mu.
Now it is classified as a garden, cutting off the benefits of Pichi water and swamp, and occupying the fertile land of farmers, starving the country of finances, and depriving the people of the farming and mulberry industry that they rely on to make a living. Abandoning success will lead to failure and reduce food income. This is the first reason why Shanglin Garden cannot be built.
Moreover, it makes the thorn jungle dense and prosperous to support the growth of elk, expands the garden where foxes and rabbits live, expands the mounds where tigers and wolves roam, destroys people's tombs and cemeteries, demolishes people's homes and houses, makes the young and weak homesick, and the elderly weep and mourn. This is the second reason why forest gardens cannot be built.
Expanding the land for construction, building walls for gardens, riding horses to the east and west, driving cars to the north and south, and having deep ditches and canals, a day of hunting in the fields will not endanger the emperor's infinite wealth. This is the third reason why Shanglin Garden cannot be built.
Therefore, ensuring that the garden is vast and not caring about the farming season is not a way to strengthen the country and enrich the people.
King Zhou of Yin built the Palace of Nine Municipalities, so the princes rebelled; King Ling of Chu built Zhanghua Terrace, so the people of Chu were dispersed; Emperor Qin Shihuang built Afang Palace, so the world was in chaos.
Ignorant ministers who are as filthy as dirt, forgetting their lives and violating the death penalty, disobeying the emperor's great wishes and grand edicts, deserve to be punished by death, but they can't fulfill their great wishes. I hope Chen will read the "Tai Jie Six Talisman Sutra" and use it to observe the changes in the celestial phenomena. This must be observed.
On this day, because of the "Taijie Six Talisman Sutra", Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty made Dongfang Shuo the Taizhong doctor and rewarded Shizhong with one hundred catties of gold.
However, Emperor Wu still built Shanglin Garden according to the plan submitted by King Wuqiu Shou.
After a long time, Princess Longlu's son Zhaopingjun married Princess Yi'an, the daughter of Emperor Wu of the Yahan Dynasty. When Princess Longli was critically ill, she offered a thousand catties of gold and ten million yuan to redeem Lord Zhaoping from his death penalty in advance, and Emperor Wu agreed to her request.
After the death of Princess Longli, Lord Zhaoping became increasingly arrogant. He got drunk and killed Princess Yi'an's nanny. He was arrested and imprisoned in the inner palace.
Because he was the son of Princess Longlu, Tingwei asked the emperor for instructions to convict Zhaoping Jun. The ministers on the left and right interceded for Zhaoping Jun: Princess Longlu paid a large sum of money to atone for his death penalty before, and your Majesty approved Princess Longlu's request.
Emperor Wu said: My sister only had such a son in her old age, and she entrusted him to me before she died. So she shed tears and sighed about Lord Zhaoping. After a long time, he said: The law was made by the late emperor. If I violate the law of the late emperor out of sympathy for my sister, how can I have the dignity to enter the temple of Emperor Gao!
Besides, I feel sorry for the people.
So he approved Tingwei's petition to convict Zhaohujun. Emperor Wu couldn't stop mourning, and everyone around him was very sad.
However, Shu Fangshuo stepped forward to wish Emperor Wu a happy birthday and said: I heard that a wise king is in power and does not avoid his enemies in giving rewards and does not choose whether he is his or her own flesh and blood.
"Shangshu" says: Don't show favoritism and don't be partial, and the king's way is open and unobstructed. These two are highly respected by the five emperors, and even the three kings find it difficult to achieve.
Your Majesty has done this, so all the people in the four seas can find their own place, and the world is very lucky!
The minister Dongfang Shuo raised his glass and made a toast, risking his life to bow again and wish the emperor long live.
Emperor Wu actually stood up and went back to the palace. In the evening, he summoned Dongfang Shuo and scolded him: "The ancient book says that you should speak only when it is time to speak. Others are not tired of his words. Is it time for you to wish me a birthday today?"
Dongfang Shuo took off his hat and kowtowed and said: I have heard that excessive happiness will lead to excessive yang energy, excessive sadness will lead to loss of yin energy, and variations in yin and yang will cause restless heart energy. Restless heart energy will lead to mental disorder, and mental disorder will allow evil spirits to take advantage of the weakness.
Nothing can relieve worries like wine. The reason why my minister Dongfang Shuo wishes His Majesty a birthday is to show that His Majesty is upright and upright, so I use wine to soothe His Majesty's sorrow.
I am ignorant and don’t know taboos, so I deserve to die.
Prior to this, Dongfang Shuo had entered the palace drunk and urinated in the palace, and was impeached for the crime of disrespect. Emperor Wu issued an edict to demote him to a commoner and wait for the eunuch in the eunuch's office. Because of this conversation with the emperor, he was appointed as Zhonglang and given a hundred pieces of silk.
At the beginning, Princess Guantao, the aunt of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, was known as Mrs. Dou, and Chen Wu, the Marquis of Tangyi, married her.
After Chen Wu's death, the Grand Master became a widow. He was over fifty years old, but he was close to and favored a young man named Dong Yan.
At first, Dong Yan and his mother made a living by selling pearls. Dong Yan was thirteen years old at the time and often accompanied his mother to the home of Taizu Dou.
Empress Dowager Dou's attendants all praised Dong Yan's handsomeness. Empress Dowager Dou summoned Dong Yan's mother and son and said to Dong Yan's mother, "I will raise this child for you."
So he stayed in the mansion and taught him writing, arithmetic, horsemanship, driving, archery and other skills, and also let him read some biographical books.
When Dong Yan reached the age of eighteen, he was crowned. He would drive the master when he went out, and he would serve him when the master returned home.
Dong Yan has a gentle and loving temperament. Because Taishu Bao doted on him, many princes welcomed him, and he became famous in Chang'an City, known as Dong Jun.
Grand Master Bao took the opportunity to recommend him and asked him to spread his wealth and make friends with scholars. He ordered the Zhongfu official in charge of the gold and silk in the palace to say: Dong Jun will report to me only when the gold and silk he spent in a day exceeds one hundred catties, the money reaches one million, and the silk exceeds one thousand pieces.
Uncle Yuan, a native of Anling County, was the son of Yuan Ang's brother and was close to Dong Yan. He said to Dong Yan: You serve Taizu Dou privately and are hiding unpredictable disasters. How do you want to find peace with yourself?
Dong Yan said fearfully: I have been worried about this for a long time, and I don't know how to get rid of it.
Uncle Yuan said: The Gucheng Temple is far away from Chang'an and there is no palace for the emperor to live. It is surrounded by bamboo and catalpa trees for the emperor to play, and it also has the emperor's home fields. The emperor wants to patrol the crops in person. Why don't you tell the emperor to dedicate Changmen Garden to the emperor?

He planned to build Shanglin Garden, but Dongfang Shuo admonished him, citing three reasons: it would ruin fertile land, destroy homes and tombs, and waste resources. He warned against luxury, referencing historical examples like King Zhou of Yin and Qin Shihuang. Despite this, Emperor Wu built the garden but promoted Dongfang Shuo to Taizhong doctor.

When Lord Zhaoping, son of Princess Longlu, killed a nanny and faced execution, Emperor Wu mourned but upheld the law. Dongfang Shuo congratulated him, praising his impartiality. The emperor initially scolded him but later accepted his explanation that wine could relieve sorrow. Dongfang Shuo was demoted for urinating in the palace but reinstated after this exchange. He also advised against allowing Dong Yan, a favorite of Princess Guantao, into the palace, citing three crimes. Emperor Wu heeded his advice, and Dong Yan's influence waned.

Dongfang Shuo urged Emperor Wu to emulate Emperor Wen's frugality to reform society, criticizing the current extravagance. When asked to compare himself to other scholars, he humorously belittled them. He wrote "Replying to Guests" and "On Mr. Feiyou," defending his low status and arguing that times had changed. In "On Mr. Feiyou," he discussed the dangers of outspoken advice and the importance of wise rulers. His works were recorded by Liu Xiang, though many rumors about him were false. Historians note his wit and humor, comparing him to a comedic figure, but his advice was often insightful.

translation:
Yan An is from Linmiao.
As the late Prime Minister Shi, he wrote a letter saying:
"Zou Zi" among the ministers said: Political decrees and education have the characteristics of the times and are used to rectify current ills. Use them if they are in line with the social reality at that time, discard them when they are outdated, and change them if they should be changed. Therefore, adhering to certain political decrees and education without changing them is not seeing the importance of politics.
Nowadays, the wealthy people in the world use their property excessively and extravagantly. They decorate their carriages, horses, clothes, and palaces. They adjust the five sounds of palace, shang, horn, zheng, and yu to make them advance, stop, and restrain. They mix the five colors of green, red, yellow, white, and black to make them elegant. They harmonize the five flavors and display them in front of the abbot. They show off and show that they want to be envied by everyone in the world.
Those people's taste is to enjoy good things when they see them. This is using luxury to educate the people.
Luxury without restraint will lead to dissatisfaction, and people will deviate from their original karma and pursue their last karma.
The huge profits from the last industry cannot be obtained in vain, so officials are not afraid of breaking the law and extorting money, and warriors with swords compete to kill people, cheat and plunder, but the people of the world do not know shame, so treacherous and evil behaviors gradually grow.
Beautiful and rare things are originally beautiful to look at and pleasant to listen to, so if you lose your cultivation, you will become arrogant; if you don’t have healthy music, you will become immoral; if you lose etiquette and justice, you will be literal; if you give up education, you will become hypocritical.
Treachery, deceit, excess, lewdness, and arrogance—these are all behaviors that cannot be used to legislate and educate the people.
Therefore, the pursuit of fame and fortune by the people of the world will not stop, and there will definitely be many people who break the law and cause chaos.
The minister hopes to establish laws and regulations for the people to prevent them from being extravagant, so that the rich and the poor will no longer show off to each other, and to alleviate people's envy of luxury.
Their thoughts have become mellow, and their temperaments will become peaceful and comfortable.
If the temperament is quiet and comfortable and does not engage in personal gain, thieves will disappear; if thieves are eliminated, punishments will be reduced; if punishments are reduced, yin and yang will be harmonious, the four seasons will be correct, wind and rain will be timely, vegetation will be luxuriant, grains will be plentiful, livestock will multiply, the people will be disease-free, and harmony will be at its peak.
I heard that the Zhou Dynasty ruled the world for more than three hundred years. The two dynasties of King Cheng and King Kang were prosperous, and the punishments were not used for more than forty years.
It took more than three hundred years for the Zhou Dynasty to decline, so the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn Period emerged one after another.
The overlord is one who always assists the emperor in promoting benefits and eliminating harm, punishing violence and prohibiting evil, and promoting righteousness at home, and uses these to respect the emperor.
After the death of the Five Hegemons, there was no wise king or saint to inherit their cause, and the emperor was isolated and weak, unable to give orders.
The princes acted arbitrarily, using the strong to bully the weak, and the many to bully the few.
Tian Chang usurped the power of the Qi State, and Zhi, Fan, Zhongxing, Han, Tang, and Wei Liuqing divided the power of the Jin State, and they all became warlike countries. This was the beginning of the people's hardship.
At this time, the strong countries are committed to attacking, while the weak countries are repairing their defenses and joining forces vertically and horizontally. Envoys, chariots and horses are galloping and colliding with each other. The soldiers' armor is covered with lice, and the common people have nowhere to complain.
When the King of Qin won the government, he encroached on the world and annexed other countries. He was named "Emperor", unified the domestic decrees, and demolished the castles of the princes.
The captured weapons were destroyed and made into bells, indicating that they would no longer be used.
The common people were spared the pain of the turmoil of the Warring States Period, and everyone thought that they had met the wise emperor and gained a new life.
If the Qin Dynasty had leniently suspended punishments, lightened taxes and levies, eliminated corvees, valued benevolence and righteousness, despised power, advocated loyalty, despised sycophancy, changed customs, and promoted enlightenment at home, then the Qin Dynasty would have had peace from generation to generation.
The Qin Dynasty did not advocate the promotion of such social customs, but continued its old customs. Those who played with cleverness and power were promoted, and those who were honest, loyal, and upright were dismissed. The laws were harsh, the decrees were harsh, and there were many flatterers. The emperor listened to their sweet words and praises every day, and he was full of ambitions and fantasies.
Wanting to show off his power overseas, he sent Meng Tian to lead troops to attack the Xiongnu in the north, expand the territory, and guard Beihe. He ordered the people to quickly transport grain and fodder to follow the army.
He also sent the commander-in-chief Tu Sui to lead the soldiers of the building boats to attack Baiyue, and sent the censor Lu Shilu to dig the Ling Canal to transport grain, and went deeper into the country, and more people fled.
The war lasted for a long time and the food supply was insufficient. The Yue people launched an attack and the Qin army was defeated.
The Qin Dynasty then sent Wei Tuo to lead troops to garrison the territory of Yue. At that time, the Qin Dynasty's troubles were that the north was resentful of the Xiongnu and the south was enmity with the Yue people. The troops were stationed in useless places and could not retreat when they advanced.
More than ten years passed like this, with the male serving as a soldier and the female transporting. They were miserable and hanged themselves on a tree by the roadside, looking at each other.
When Qin Shihuang died, the world was in rebellion.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang captured Chen, Wu Chen and Zhang Er captured Zhao, Xiang Liang defeated Wu, Tian Dan captured Qi, Jing Ju went to Ying, Zhou Shi fell to Wei, Han Guang raised Yan, and the mountains were full of heroes, which is unforgettable.
However, these people are not the descendants of princes, nor are they local governors. They have no power at all. They started in Yanxiang, holding the handles of spears and halberds. They followed the trend of the times, started troubles at the right time, gathered together by chance, attacked cities and plundered lands, and finally became kings. This was the result of the education at that time.
The emperor of the Qin Dynasty was regarded as the Son of Heaven, rich in the world, and his lineage was exterminated and sacrifices were cut off. This was a disaster caused by military violence.
Therefore, the fault of the Zhou Dynasty was that it was weak, and the fault of the Qin Dynasty was that it was strong. Both of them were unable to adapt to the times, which led to the disaster of national destruction.
Now the Han court wants to appease the Nanyi, send Yelang to come to the court, surrender Qiang Fen and Lingzhou, and build cities there. It also wants to penetrate deeply into the Xiongnu and burn their dragon city. The discussants praise these plans.
This is the selfish desire of ministers and is not a long-term strategy for governing the world.
Now China doesn't even have a dog barking alarm, but it is implicated in foreign defenses, causing the country to wither and decline. This is not the way to nurture the people.
In order to realize the endless desires, just to be happy and to have grudges with the Huns, this is not a way to stabilize the border.
If the scourge is not resolved, the war will cease and then be provoked again, causing sorrow to those nearby and fear to those far away. This is not a lasting solution.
Nowadays, people all over the world have to forge armor, sharpen swords, straighten arrowheads, draw bowstrings, and transport military supplies. There is no end in sight. This is a common worry for everyone.
Using troops for too long will cause chaos, and too many things will cause people to doubt.
Nowadays, the land of foreign counties is nearly a thousand miles long, with dozens of cities connected. The mountains and rivers are enough to threaten the people in the counties and threaten the nearby princes. This is not the interest of the Han Dynasty clan.
The reason for the demise of Qi and Jin is that the imperial family is weak and the six ministers are too strong; the reason for the fall of Qin is that the punishments are harsh and the law is cruel, and the desires are too great and inexhaustible.
Now, the power held by the county governor is not as heavy as that of the six ministers of the Jin Dynasty; the land is thousands of miles away, and it is not just the lanes; the armor and weapons are not just as useful as spears and halberds. With these favorable conditions, if there is a world chaos, what situation will happen cannot be concealed.
Later, Yan An was appointed as the riding order.
Zhongjun, named Ziyun, was from Jinan County.
He was fond of learning when he was young, and was famous in the county for his eloquence and writing of articles.
At the age of eighteen, he was elected as a doctoral disciple.
He was selected to send him to the capital. When he reported to the prefect's mansion, the prefect heard that he had outstanding talents and summoned him. He thought he was very strange and became friends with him.
Zhongjun bid farewell to the prefect and went to Beijing. He went to Chang'an to write a letter to express his opinions. After reading it, Emperor Wu thought that his writing was unusual, so he appointed Zhongjun as his emissary to the emperor.
The final army followed Emperor Wu to Yong County to worship Wuzhi. Emperor Wu captured a white unicorn with one horn and five legs.
At that time, I discovered a strange tree. Its branches stretched out to the side, and then bent over to attach to the tree.
Emperor Wu felt that these two animals and plants were very strange, and asked the officials extensively what they thought of them.
Zhongjun wrote a letter and replied:
I heard that the "Book of Songs" praises the virtues of the monarch, and the "Book of Music" praises the achievements of the emperor. The scriptures are different but have the same purpose. They all show the prosperity of great virtue.
The South Vietnamese fled and hid in the reeds, keeping company with birds and fish. The education of the Han Dynasty had no influence on their customs.
Relevant officials led troops to garrison at the border, Shu Ou surrendered to the Han Dynasty, the King of Fujian pleaded guilty, and South Vietnam relied on rescue.
The Xiongnu in the north often moved their residences with their livestock. They walked like animals and had a heart like tigers and wolves. They have never been able to surrender since ancient times.
General Wei Qing holds an ax and iron, the Xiongnu Chanyu flees to Mobei; Husband General Huo Qubing holds the battle flag high, and Wusun Kunxie is naturalized in China.
Deze is distributed in the southern border and reaches the northern kingdom with great power.
If punishment is not partial to those close to you, if people are recommended and not sent away from distant places, if officials are set up to offer rewards for the wise men to come and perform meritorious services, those who are talented will be promoted and keep their salary, and those who are incompetent will be dismissed and return to their hometowns to farm, and laws will be implemented throughout the country.
He has many beauties but is not satisfied, has a holy mind but is not authoritarian, and establishes the system of Mingtang, Piyong, and Lingtai. The text and content meet the requirements and are applicable for a long time. It commends those who are conscientious and competent in their work. The previous generation of Fengdang monarchs have not heard of such beautiful virtues.
The monarch who first accepted the destiny made everything first. In order to achieve the same climate within the Liuhe and the unified system of the nine states, he must wait for the sage monarch to polish it and pass on the achievements of his ancestors forever.
Therefore, when the Zhou Dynasty reached King Zhou, the system was finalized, and then the verification response of Jiamei appeared.
Your majesty is prosperous and shines in the light of the sun and the moon, hanging down the thoughts of the saints for meditation; you concentrate on worshiping the gods, going to Taizhi to offer sacrifices to the sky, and to the back earth to offer sacrifices to the earth. The spirit of offering wine and food moves the gods, and the air of peace fills the heaven and earth. Every place where the sun and the moon shine is reached, and strange beasts appear and are captured. This is as it should be.
Once upon a time, when King Wu of Zhou was on his way to the middle of the Yellow River during his expedition against the Shang Dynasty, a white fish jumped into the boat that King Wu of Zhou was riding in. King Wu leaned over to pick it up and grilled it over a fire. Everyone said, "What auspiciousness!"
Nowadays, when people offer sacrifices to heaven and earth in the countryside, they do not see the gods of heaven and earth, but they get strange beasts to sacrifice. This is the sky using it to show that they have enjoyed the sacrifice, and it is consistent with the auspiciousness of sincerity and sincerity.
We should choose an auspicious time, change the year name, weave mats, put white cogon grass on them, float them on the Yangtze River and Huaihe River, and climb Mount Tai to seal them, so as to harmonize the light and make it recordable by historians.
The six parrots flying back symbolize the rebellion of the princes; the white fish boarding the boat symbolizes the submission of the princes to King Wu.
Signs of light and darkness confuse the birds in the sky, stir up the fish underwater, and so on.
Now the white unicorn has a single horn on its head, indicating that it has the same origin; the branches of the strange tree are attached inside, indicating that it has no outward orientation.
When this phenomenon comes to fruition, the surrounding ethnic minorities will probably untie their hair, abandon their left-front clothing, wear hats and belts, and wear Han clothes to accept the enlightenment of the Central Plains.
These are just waiting for their arrival!
The countermeasures were presented to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu thought it was unusual, so he changed the reign name to Yuanshou.
A few months later, famous kings from Yue and the Huns came to surrender to the Han Dynasty with their troops. At that time, people thought that Zhongjun's words were right.
During the Yuanding period, Dr. Xu Yan was sent as an envoy to inspect the customs and education of the county.
Xu Yan pretended to act under the orders of the imperial court and asked Jiaodong and Lu to cast iron and dry it with salt. After returning to Beijing, he reported what he had done and was transferred to Taichang Cheng.
Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, impeached Xu Yan for acting under the pretense of imperial orders, which was a great harm to the country and should be executed according to the law.
Xu Yan believed that according to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", when officials go out of their borders and encounter matters that can stabilize the country and comfort the people, they can handle it arbitrarily.
Zhang Tang could only judge Xu Yan's crime according to the law, but could not refute the meaning of "Spring and Autumn" he used to defend himself. Emperor Wu ordered Zhongjun to interrogate the case. Zhongjun interrogated Xu Yan and said: In ancient vassal states, the customs of different countries were different, and they could not communicate with each other within a hundred miles. There were often appointments and alliances between the court, and the situation of stability or danger would change in a breath. Therefore, there was talk of acting arbitrarily without asking for instructions and pretending to be ordered by the court. Now that the world is unified, the customs are the same within thousands of miles, so the "Spring and Autumn Annals" said There is nothing like a king.
You patrolled the territory, and what did you say about the territory?
Besides, there is plenty of treasure in Yantie County. Even if the salt and iron from Micelle and Lu are abolished, it will not be of any interest to the country. Yet you use the excuse of stabilizing the country and pacifying the people. Why?
The final army questioned Xu Yan again and said: Jiaodong is close to Langye County in the south and Beihai County in the north. Lu State is adjacent to Taishan County in the west and Shuhai County in Shuhai, and they use their salt and iron.
Do you estimate that the population and fields of the four counties of Langye, Beihai, Taishan, and Donghai, as well as their iron utensils and salt, are not enough to supply Micellar and Lu?
Or should there actually be excess salt and iron, but officials cannot supply it?
How do you explain this problem?
You asked them to cast iron tools under the guise of an order from the imperial court. You wanted to catch up with spring farming and ensure that the people would have iron tools for use.
Nowadays, when Lu State casts iron, various preparations should be made first, and then it can be ignited and smelted in the autumn.
Isn’t this inconsistent with actual needs?
You sent three requests to Miaojie and the State of Lu to operate salt and iron, but the imperial court did not respond to the edict. You did not think about what you wanted to do and did not approve it. Instead, you directly relied on the imperial court's orders to act in a way that obeyed the wishes of the people and gained reputation. This is an act that a wise king must punish. Bend one foot and straighten eight feet. Mencius said this is not possible. Now the crime you have committed is heavy and the thing you have accomplished is small. Do you think you will die and do this?
Or are you lucky enough to avoid being punished and use it to gain reputation?
Xu Yan was speechless and resigned, and he should die if he admits his crime.
The final report of the interrogation was reported by the army: Xu Yan acted with authority under the guise of relying on imperial orders and violated the system of inspections by envoys. Please issue an edict to the censor to summon Xu Yan to plead guilty immediately.
Finally, the army's memorial was approved.
Emperor Wu appreciated Zhongjun's questioning of Xu Yan very much, and asked him to show it to Zhang Tang, the imperial censor.
When Zhong Jun went to the capital from Jinan to visit the doctor, he walked through Hangu Pass. The official guarding the pass gave Zhong Jun a talisman made of silk.
Zhong Jun asked: What are you using this for?
The official replied: "When I come back, I will use it as a road sign. I will pass this bundle and take it to match it."
Zhong Jun said: When a man travels to the west, he does not need it as a way back.
He threw down the silk talisman letter and left.
After Zhongjun was appointed as the envoy, he was envoyed to inspect the prefecture and the country. He went out to Hangu Pass to patrol the east with the talisman festival. The officials guarding the pass remembered him and said: This envoy is the Confucian scholar who abandoned the silk talisman letter before.
Finally, the army patrolled the prefectures and reported to the court when they encountered suitable things.
After returning from the mission, he reported his work to Emperor Wu, who was very happy to hear it.
When the imperial court sent an envoy to the Xiongnu, Zhongjun himself requested to be envoyed, saying: "I didn't even make the envoy fall, so I was listed as a minister of the Suwei and received a five-year salary."
There are warnings of war on the border from time to time. I should put on strong armor and hold sharp weapons, face the rain of arrows and stones, and open the way forward.
But I am not familiar with the matter of charging into battle. Now that I heard that an envoy is going to be sent to the Xiongnu, I am willing to do my best to inspire the spirit, assist the wise envoy, and plan good and bad things in front of the Xiongnu Chanyu.
I am young and have low talents, and I have failed to live up to my expectations. I cannot serve as an official to defend the border. I am not strong enough to stand alone. I feel depressed in private.
Emperor Wu went down to Shao and asked Zhongjun about his request to send an envoy to the Xiongnu to plan for good or bad luck. Emperor Wu thought that Zhongjun's answer was unusual and promoted him to the position of admonishing doctor.
South Vietnam and the Han Dynasty made peace, so Emperor Wu sent Zhongjun as an envoy to South Vietnam to lobby the King of South Vietnam to allow him to come to Beijing to see him, and his treatment was similar to that of the princes and kings in the mainland.
The final army volunteered and said: I hope your majesty will give me a long tassel, and I will tie up the King of Nanyue and bring him to the palace.
The army went to South Vietnam to lobby the King of Yue. After listening to the army's words, the King of Yue agreed to lead all the Yue people to join the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu was very happy and gave the South Vietnamese minister a seal, allowing the South Vietnamese king to uniformly use the legal system of the Han Dynasty to change the customs and habits of the Vietnamese people, and ordered the envoys to stay in the army to stabilize and appease South Vietnam.
Lu Jia, the Prime Minister of South Vietnam, was unwilling to join the Han Dynasty and sent troops to attack the King of South Vietnam. He also killed the Han Dynasty envoy Zhong Jun and others.
The words are in "The Biography of Nanyue".
Zhong Jun was only in his twenties when he died, so the world called him "Zhong Tong".
Wang Bao, whose courtesy name was Ziyuan, was from Shu County.
When Huang Tong was a child, he compiled the old affairs of the time of Cheng Zhi, talked about "Poems", "Books", "Li", "Music", "Yi", "Spring and Autumn" and other books, and extensively and exhaustively collected strange things. He recruited people from Jiujiang County who were proficient in "Chu Ci". Emperor Xuan summoned him and asked him to recite "Chu Ci". He also recruited outstanding talents Liu Xiang, Zhang Ziqiao, Hua Long, Liu Bao and others to wait for the imperial edict to Jinmamen.
During the years of Shenjue and Wufeng, the world was prosperous and auspicious signs appeared many times.
Emperor Xuan liked to compose poems and sing songs, and was planning to start a business of correcting music and rhythm to make it harmonious. The prime minister, Wei Xiang, summoned Tanding from Bohai County and Gong De from Liang who knew music and were good at playing Yaqin. Emperor Xuan summoned them and asked them to wait for the imperial edict.
At this time, Wang Xiang, who made the history of Yizhou, wanted to promote customs and enlightenment among the people. Hearing that Wang Guo was a talented person, he invited Wang Guo to meet him and asked him to compose "Zhonghe", "Music Responsibilities" and "Announcement Poems", and select enthusiastic people to sing according to the music of "Lu Ming".
At that time, Fanxiang Hou Hewu was still a minor and was selected to participate in singing.
After a long time, He Wu and others went to Chang'an to study vocal music and sang in Taixue. The matter was reported to the emperor.
Emperor Xuan summoned He Wu and others and said to them: This is a matter of Xinglong Dejiao, how can I stop them!
After Wang Bao wrote an ode to Wang Xiang, the governor of Yizhou, he also wrote a biography for him. Wang Xiang then wrote to Emperor Xuan, saying that Wang Bao had outstanding intelligence.
Emperor Xuan summoned Wang Bao.
After Wang Bao arrived in the capital, Emperor Xuan issued an order for Wang Bao to write a song with the theme of a wise monarch getting a wise minister.
Wang Bao's ode said:
A person who carries a wool felt on his shoulders and wears fine black animal hair is not worth talking about the beauty of silk and cotton; a person who eats poor food is not worthy of talking to him about the taste of cattle, sheep, and pigs.
Nowadays, I live in a remote place in Western Shu, growing up in a poor alleyway under a house made of reeds and reeds. I do not have the knowledge to travel widely. Instead, I am burdened by extremely ignorance and shallowness. I am unable to satisfy my ardent hopes and respond to the will of the sage.
Even so, how dare I not briefly state my humble opinion and express my sincerity!
The book of notes says: Respectfully think about the "Spring King's first month of the first year" as the norm in "Spring and Autumn". The purpose of these five beginnings is just to examine your own correct system.
A virtuous person refers to a person with useful talents in the country.
If the people appointed are capable, they will be good at making choices and achieve a wide range of effects; if the tools are convenient, they will use less effort and achieve more results.
Therefore, when workers use blunt instruments, they work hard and work tirelessly all day long.
When the skillful craftsmen forged the Ganjiang sword, they quenched the edge with clean water and sharpened the blade with sharp stones produced in the Yue region. The sword could cut off dragons in the water and cut the skin of rhinoceros on land. It was as easy as sweeping the watered ground with a broom or scratching in the mud with a knife.
In this way, if Li Lou, who has excellent eyesight, is asked to see the line, and the skilled craftsman Gongshu Ban cuts ink, even if he builds a five-story high platform with a width of 100 feet, there will be no confusion, because the craftsmen and the tools are in harmony.
A mediocre driver controls the horse, hurts the horse's mouth, breaks the riding whip, but still can't run fast, panting, the skin is sweaty, and the horse is tired and sleepy.
When you ride a good horse, let Wang Liang hold the bridle, and Han Ai serve as the driver, you can gallop as fast as the shadow of the swaying and floating sunlight. Crossing the city and country is like passing through a piece of soil; chasing lightning, faster than the wind, traveling to far-flung places in all directions, thousands of miles away can be reached in a breath.
Why can it run so far?
This is a match between man and horse.
Therefore, those who wear cool Gebu clothes do not worry about the sweltering heat of summer; those who wear mink and fox fur coats do not worry about the cold of winter. Why?
Because they have clothes for summer and cold, they can easily prepare for summer and winter.
Wise men and gentlemen are also the important force that sage kings rely on to change the world.
Therefore, the king accepted them with joy and opened wide and prosperous roads for them, so as to attract the talents of the world.
Those who use all their wisdom to rely on wise people will surely come up with benevolent and righteous strategies; those who use their heart to seek wise people will surely achieve the achievements of overlords.
In the past, the Duke of Zhou vomited food three times, bathed three times and caught the hair, and treated the virtuous subordinates with courtesy, so the world was in great order, punishments were not used, and prisons were empty. Duke Huan of Qi used the ceremony of burning in the court to receive those who contributed ninety-nine calculations. Soon, wise men came one after another, and Duke Huan finally unified the world, united the nine princes, and achieved hegemony.
From this point of view, a monarch is diligent in visiting talented people, but he feels comfortable because he is assisted by others.
The same is true for people and ministers.
In the past, when a wise man had not met a wise master, he would make suggestions but the king would not adopt his opinions, express his opinions and express his loyalty but the master would not believe them, he would not be effective when he became an official, and it was not his fault that he would be expelled or removed from office.
Therefore, Yi Yin carried the cooking tripod and Zu in an attempt to assist Shang Tang, Jiang Taigong was trapped in Chao Ge, slaughtered cattle to make a living, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Zi fed cattle, all encountered different hardships.
When you meet a wise king and meet a holy master, your plans are in line with your will, your advice and remonstrances are listened to, your loyalty can be understood both in advance and retreat, and you can use your strategies in office. You leave the humiliating and dirty place and become a minister of the court. You leave the rough food, take off your wooden clogs, enjoy the delicious food, divide the talismans, and honor the ancestors, pass them on to your descendants, and pass them on to your descendants.
Therefore, there must first be a wise king in the world, and then there can be wise ministers.
Therefore, the tiger roars and the wind blows, the dragon soars and rises in the clouds, the cricket shuts up in late autumn, and the mayfly lives in the morning and dies in the evening.
"Book of Changes" says: Flying dragons in the sky are good for seeing adults.
"The Book of Songs" says: Beautiful and numerous wise men were born in the country of King Zhou.
Therefore, in the world, the peaceful monarchs, sages, and capable people will come by themselves, just like Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen Wang, Wu Wang and other monarchs, and they have Ji, Qi, Gaotao, Yi Yin, Lu Wang and other virtuous ministers.
Even if Zu Boya plays the bells and bends the black trumpet bow at the door, it is still not enough to describe the above scene.
Therefore, the holy master will wait for the virtuous ministers to promote his great achievements, and the talented and elegant people will wait for the wise king to show off their virtues.
The king and his ministers all realized their wishes and rejoiced with each other. For a thousand years, the king and his ministers spoke without suspicion. They spread their wings and soared like a feather in the wind, the water flowed swiftly and the giant fish leaped into the gully.
If the king and his ministers are as happy as they want, what else cannot be forbidden, what orders cannot be carried out?
The enlightenment spreads to all four sides, overflowing into infinity. Minorities from far away come to contribute, and all kinds of auspiciousness come.
Therefore, the sage king can see clearly without looking around, hear clearly without leaning his ears, the grace soars with the auspicious wind, the virtue wanders with the harmony, the duty of peace is fulfilled, the wish of leisurely travel is achieved, and he follows the trend of wandering in nature. , wandering in the tranquil and inactive place, good signs will come by themselves, long life without any boundaries, calm and unhurried, arching and doing nothing, for eternity, why should we bend and stretch like Peng Zu, breathe loudly like Wang Qiao and Chisongzi, and pass away in a worldly way!
"The Book of Songs" says that there are many talents in one place, and King Wen found peace because of it. It turns out that he believed that the king felt peace because he got wise men!
At this time, the emperor liked the magic of immortals very much, so Wang Bao talked about immortal things when he composed a hymn.
Emperor Xuan ordered Wang Guo, Zhang Ziqiao and others to wait for the imperial edict together. He repeatedly asked Wang Guo and others to participate in large-scale hunting expeditions as attendants. summary:
Yan An, from Linmiao, wrote a letter as the late Prime Minister Shi, criticizing the extravagance of the wealthy, who decorated their carriages, clothes, and palaces excessively, leading to social ills like greed, lawlessness, and moral decay. He argued that luxury without restraint causes dissatisfaction, drives people from their proper occupations, and fosters treachery and violence. Yan An proposed laws to curb extravagance, reduce envy, and promote harmony, which would lead to peace, reduced crime, and natural prosperity. He contrasted the Zhou Dynasty's long rule with its decline due to weak leadership, leading to the Warring States period and the rise of the Five Hegemons, who upheld the emperor's authority. The Qin Dynasty, under Emperor Qin Shi Huang, unified China but failed to reform its harsh laws and heavy taxes, instead expanding aggressively against the Xiongnu and Baiyue, causing widespread suffering and rebellion. Yan An warned the Han court against similar overreach, advocating for domestic stability over foreign conquests, and noted that the Zhou's weakness and Qin's strength both led to their downfalls due to inflexibility.

Zhongjun, from Jinan, was a talented scholar who became Emperor Wu's envoy. He wrote a response to Emperor Wu's discovery of a white unicorn and a strange tree, interpreting them as auspicious signs of the Han dynasty's virtue and the submission of foreign peoples. He advised the emperor to perform sacrifices and change the reign name, which Emperor Wu did, renaming it Yuanshou. Later, Zhongjun interrogated Dr. Xu Yan for falsely claiming imperial orders to operate salt and iron in Jiaodong and Lu, exposing his deceit and securing his conviction. Emperor Wu praised Zhongjun's handling of the case. Zhongjun also volunteered to envoy to the Xiongnu and South Vietnam, famously requesting a "long tassel" to bind the King of South Vietnam. He successfully persuaded the king to submit to Han rule, but was killed by the South Vietnamese prime minister Lu Jia during a rebellion.

Wang Bao, from Shu, was a poet summoned by Emperor Xuan to compose songs and odes. He wrote an ode praising wise rulers and ministers, using metaphors like the Ganjiang sword and fine horses to illustrate the harmony between talent and leadership. He argued that virtuous ministers naturally appear under sage kings, citing historical examples like the Duke of Zhou and Duke Huan of Qi. Emperor Xuan enjoyed Wang Bao's works, which included references to immortals, and promoted him to advisory doctor. Wang Bao also served the prince during illness, reading his compositions to cheer him. He died while on a mission to Yizhou to obtain treasures.

Jia Ganzhi, great-grandson of Jia Yi, advised Emperor Yuan against attacking Zhuli County (in modern Hainan), which had repeatedly rebelled since its establishment. He argued that the territory was not worth the cost, citing historical precedents like Yao, Shun, and the Zhou Dynasty, which did not forcibly conquer distant lands. He contrasted Emperor Wen's frugality and peace with Emperor Wu's costly expansions, which led to widespread suffering and rebellion. Emperor Yuan accepted his advice and abandoned Zhuli County. Later, Jia Ganzhi and Yang Xing, a favored official, conspired to recommend each other for high positions, but Shi Xian reported their scheme. They were tried for deceit and leaking palace secrets; Jia Ganzhi was executed, and Yang Xing was reduced to penal servitude.
