Please confiscate the property and return it to the public. Everyone who was promoted to an official position because of Dong Xian was dismissed.
His father Dong Gong, brother Dong Kuanxin and their families moved to Hepu, while his mother returned to her hometown Julu.
The small and medium-sized people in Chang'an were in an uproar and went to Dong's house to mourn, trying to take the opportunity to steal property.
The government sold off the Dong family's property for 4.3 billion yuan.
Dong Xian's grave was dug, his body was examined naked, and he was immediately buried in prison.
The official Zhu Xiang of Peijun, whom Dong Xian loved, impeached himself and left Da Sima's mansion. He bought coffins and clothes to bury Dong Xian's body.
Wang Mang was furious when he heard about it and killed Zhu Yi on other charges.
His son Zhu Fu was a prominent figure during the Jianwu period of Emperor Guangwu, and he rose to the rank of Grand Sima, Sikong, and Marquis.
Wang Hong was the prefect during Wang Mang's time, and his political performance was commendable. After Wang Mang's defeat, he resigned to serve the people.
Shizu issued an edict: King Wu destroyed the Shang Dynasty and went to commend Shang Rong among the sages of the Shang Dynasty. Wang Hong cultivated his virtues and strictly regulated his conduct. After the war broke out, the officials and the people did not fight for his head.
Let Wang Hong's son be an official today.
His womb reached the magistrate of a county and died in office. He was Xiao Xian's grandson.
Praise: Being gentle, charming, and considerate is not just for women, a man's attachment is equally attractive.
Ju Ru, Hong Ru, Deng Tong and Han Yan were favored in different ways, but Dong Xian was favored the most. Dong Xian and his son were both ministers. It can be said that the wealth and importance they received were unparalleled among the ministers.
However, these people did not achieve their fortunes by relying on holy ways and conventions. Their social status far exceeded their positions and abilities, and they all did not end well. Tao's pampering of them just harmed them.
Throughout the Western Han Dynasty, under Emperors Yuan and Cheng, the country began to decline. Under Emperors Ai and Ping, various conflicts broke out, and the trend of collapse was like overwhelming water.
The emperor was ill and childless, and there was no one to pass on the throne. The petty ministers in the palace took the opportunity to rise to the position of auxiliary to the country and specialized in government affairs.
Once the emperor died, treacherous ministers took over the power of the court, Dong Xian was forced to hang himself, Ding Ming and Fu happy were exiled, and the disaster was implicated on the empress dowager, who was demoted and abdicated. The mistake that caused this unmanageable situation was basically that the relatives were not human and the people appointed were not virtuous.
That’s why Confucius said that there are three kinds of friends who harm people. As the emperor, the emperor and the king cannot appoint people to officials based on personal feelings. This is probably the reason.
summary:
Since the Han Dynasty's founding, sycophants and favored ministers who gained imperial favor through flattery appeared regularly. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, there was Ji Ru; under Emperor Xiaohui, there was Hong Ru. Neither possessed outstanding talents, relying solely on flattery to gain wealth and favor. They accompanied the emperor closely, influencing even ministers who used them to communicate with the throne. Their impact was so great that Emperor Hui's officials adopted their customs, decorating hats with delicate feathers, belts with seashells, and applying makeup—a trend attributed to figures like Ji Ru and Hong Ru. Both became wealthy and noble in their lifetimes, later moving to Anling.

Subsequent favored figures included Deng Tong, eunuch Zhao Tan, and Beigong Bozi under Emperor Wen; Han Yan and eunuch Li Yannian under Emperor Wu; eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian under Emperor Yuan; Zhang Fang and Chun Yuchang under Emperor Cheng; and Dong Xian under Emperor Ai. Emperors Jing, Zhao, and Xuan had no notable favorites, though Zhou Ren under Emperor Jing, Jin Shang under Emperor Zhao, and Peng Zu under Emperor Xuan received some favor without causing harm.

Deng Tong, from Nan'an in Shu, was known as Huangtoulang for wearing a yellow hat while rowing. Emperor Wen once dreamed of ascending to heaven but was unable until a yellow-headed man pushed him upward. After waking, the emperor sought the man and found Deng Tong, whose clothing matched the dream. Delighted, the emperor favored him greatly, rewarding him with tens of thousands in cash and high office. Deng Tong was cautious and solemn, avoiding outsiders even during holidays. A fortune-teller predicted he would die poor and hungry, but the emperor, confident in his power, gave him Tongshan Mountain in Shu to mint coins, making Deng Tong immensely wealthy. When Emperor Wen developed abscesses, Deng Tong sucked them with his mouth. The emperor asked who loved him most, and Deng Tong replied the prince. The prince, uncomfortable with sucking the sores, later resented Deng Tong. After Emperor Wen's death, Emperor Jing dismissed Deng Tong. Accused of minting coins outside, Deng Tong was convicted, his property confiscated, and he died penniless in another's home.

Zhao Tan gained favor through astrology, and Beigong Bozi through elder-like generosity, but neither matched Deng Tong. Han Yan, grandson of Gonggaohou Qidang, studied with Emperor Wu during his youth. After Emperor Wu became emperor, Han Yan's skills in horseback riding and archery, along with his intelligence, earned him favor comparable to Deng Tong. He often slept and rose with the emperor. Once, while hunting, King Jiangdu mistook Han Yan's entourage for the emperor and knelt, but Han Yan passed without noticing. The king complained to the empress dowager, who hated Han Yan thereafter. When adultery rumors reached her, she had Han Yan killed despite the emperor's pleas. Han Yan's brother, Han Shuo, also favored, was later killed during the witchcraft disaster.

Li Yannian, from Zhongshan, was a musician who suffered corruption and managed the emperor's dogs. His sister, favored as Lady Li, gave birth to the King of Changyi. Li Yannian's musical talents earned him high rank, equal to Han Yan. After Lady Li's death, his brother Li Ji's promiscuity led to their execution. Thereafter, favored ministers were mostly relatives. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, though favored, rose through genuine military merit.

Shi Xian, from Jinan, and Hong Gong, from Pei, both suffered corruption and served as eunuchs. Under Emperor Xuan, Hong Gong became Zhongshu Ling, skilled in laws and reports. After Hong Gong's death, Shi Xian succeeded him under Emperor Yuan. When Emperor Yuan fell ill, he entrusted all government affairs to Shi Xian, who became all-powerful. Shi Xian was cunning, using strict laws to attack opponents. He persecuted Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng, leading to Xiao's suicide and the others' imprisonment. Later, Zhang Meng, Jing Fang, Chen Xian, and others who exposed Shi Xian's faults were convicted. Su Jian, who reported Shi Xian's private letters, was executed. Officials feared Shi Xian, who formed a clique with Lao Liang and Wulu Chongzong. A folk song mocked their power. Shi Xian tried to attach himself to Feng Fengshi but recommended Feng Kui, who then exposed Shi Xian's monopoly. The emperor dismissed Feng Kui. When the censor position opened, ministers recommended Feng Kui's brother, but Shi Xian blocked it. Shi Xian often feigned self-criticism to maintain trust. After Emperor Yuan's death, Emperor Cheng demoted Shi Xian, who died on the road. His followers were dismissed.

Chun Yuchang, from Yuancheng, served Wang Feng diligently, becoming his nephew. Before Wang Feng's death, he recommended Chun Yuchang to the empress dowager and emperor. Chun Yuchang helped make Feiyan empress, earning a marquis title. He became wealthy, marrying many concubines and having an affair with Xu Wei, sister of deposed Empress Xu. Empress Xu bribed Chun Yuchang to regain favor, but he deceived her. Wang Mang, fearing Chun Yuchang's rise, exposed his crimes to Wang Gen and the empress dowager. Chun Yuchang was dismissed and exiled, dying in prison. His family was exiled, and many officials lost their posts.

Dong Xian, from Yunyang, served as prince's minister under Emperor Ai. His handsome appearance won favor, and he became Huang Menlang. He rode with the emperor and slept with him. Once, when Dong Xian slept on Emperor Ai's sleeve, the emperor cut it off rather than wake him. Dong Xian's family received immense rewards, and he became Grand Sima at age twenty-two. After Emperor Ai's death, the empress dowager summoned Wang Mang, who impeached Dong Xian for failing to care for the emperor. Dong Xian and his wife committed suicide. Their property was confiscated, and his family exiled. The text concludes that these favored ministers, lacking virtue, met bad ends, and their rise contributed to the Western Han's decline.

translation:
Fu Jiezi was from the North and was promoted to an official because he joined the army.
It turns out that both Qiuci and Loulan had killed envoys of the Han Dynasty, which was recorded in "Biography of the Western Regions".
During the Yuanfeng period, Fu Jiezi requested to be sent to Dayuan as an envoy of Junma, and took the emperor's Shao letter to condemn Loulan and Qiuci.
When Fu Jiezi arrived in Loulan, he blamed the King of Loulan for encouraging the Huns to intercept and kill the Han Dynasty envoys. He said: The large army is about to arrive. If you don't encourage the Huns, why don't you report the Huns' envoys to other countries after passing through?
King Loulan expressed his guilt and said: The Huns envoy has just passed by. He should have gone to Wusun and passed through Qiuci on the way.
When Fu Jiezi arrived at Kucha, he blamed the King of Kucha again, and the King of Kucha also admitted his guilt.
Fu Jiezi returned to Kucha from Dayuan. The Kucha people said that the Huns envoy was here after returning from Wusun.
Fu Jiezi took the opportunity to lead his officers and soldiers to kill the Huns envoy.
Fu Jiezi returned to the capital to report the situation, and the emperor issued an edict appointing him as Zhonglang and promoted him to Ping Yue Supervisor.
Fu Jiezi said to the general Huo Guang: Loulan and Qiuci have been capricious many times but have not been condemned. They cannot be used to punish other countries.
When I passed through Qiuci, their king was very close to others and could easily be attacked. I was willing to go and assassinate him, so as to establish my prestige and announce it to other countries.
The general said: "Qiuci country is far away, so let's go to Loulan to test this method for now."
So he told the emperor to send him there.
Fu Jiezi and the soldiers brought gold and silver coins together, claiming that they were gifts to foreign countries.
When they arrived at Loulan, King Loulan seemed unwilling to get close to Fu Jiezi, so Fu Jiezi pretended to leave. After arriving at the western border of Loulan, Fu Jiezi ordered an interpreter to say to King Loulan: The envoys of the Han Dynasty traveled around with gold and brocade to give to various countries. If the king does not come to receive the gift, I will leave for the country to the west.
He immediately took out the gold coins and showed them to the translator.
The translator came back and reported the situation to King Loulan. King Loulan was greedy for the property of the Han Dynasty, so he came to meet the envoy.
Fu Jiezi sat drinking with him and showed him his belongings.
After drinking, Fu Jiezi was drunk and said to King Loulan: The emperor sent me to report some things to the king privately.
King Loulan got up and followed Fu Jiezi into the tent. The two were talking alone. Two strong men stabbed King Loulan from behind. The blades met in the chest. King Loulan died immediately.
His nobles and left and right officials all fled.
Fu Jiezi told them that King Loulan was guilty of the Han Dynasty, and the emperor sent me to kill him. The prince who had been left as a hostage in the Han Dynasty should be replaced as king.
The Han army has just arrived. Don't act rashly. If you make any move, your country will be wiped out!
After that, he took the head of King Loulan back to Beijing to deliver the order. The ministers, generals and others all praised his achievements.
The emperor then issued an edict saying: King Angui of Loulan had acted as a spy for the Huns, secretly spying on the envoys of the Han Dynasty, and sent troops to kill and plunder three guards, including Ma Anle, Guanglu Dafuzhong, and Qi Menlang Suicheng, as well as envoys from Anxi and Dawan.
Fu Jiezi, the supervisor of Pingle, went out as an envoy with the talisman and killed King Angui of Loulan. He hung his head on the north tower and repaid the resentful people with integrity without disturbing the troops and stirring up the crowd.
Fu Jiezi was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang and given to 700 households in the city.
Among the soldiers who assassinated King Loulan, they all replaced their officials as ministers.
After Fu Jiezi died, his son Fu Chang was guilty and could not inherit the title, and the feudal state was abolished.
In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the descendants of the heroes were renewed, and Fu Chang, the great-grandson of Fu Jiezi, was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang. It was only after Wang Mang's failure that the throne was cut off.
Chang Hui is from Taiyuan.
When he was young, his family was poor, so he volunteered to join the army. He followed Su Wu, the eunuch of Zhizhong, on an envoy to the Huns. They were detained by the Huns for more than ten years and were not able to return until Emperor Zhao.
In order to reward his hard work, the Han Dynasty appointed him Guanglu Doctor.
At this time, Princess Wusun wrote a letter saying: The Xiongnu mobilized their cavalry to colonize the Che Division. The Che Division and the Xiongnu army merged into one to jointly invade Wusun. I hope the emperor will come to rescue us. The Han Dynasty recruited troops and raised horses, and discussed preparations to attack the Xiongnu.
After the death of Emperor Zhao, Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne. In the second year of his reign, Chang Hui was sent as envoy to Wusun.
Princess Wusun and King Wusun both sent envoys to the court, and wrote through Chang Hui that the Xiongnu sent large troops to attack Wusun one after another, captured Cheyan, Eshi and other places, and robbed all the local people. They also sent envoys to threaten to marry Wusun Gonggui, in an attempt to isolate Banjie from Xuansu.
King Wu Zhu was willing to recruit half of the elite troops in the country, equip himself with 50,000 soldiers and horses, and do his best to attack the Xiongnu.
I hope the emperor will send troops to save the princess and King Wusun!
So the Han Dynasty mobilized a large scale of 150,000 cavalry, and the five generals set off in separate directions. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of the Xiongnu".
Chang Hui was appointed as the captain of the school and commanded Wusun's army with the talisman.
King Wusun himself led more than 50,000 cavalrymen under Linghou to march from the west to Yougu Liting, and captured Chanyu's father and his entourage, his sister-in-law and princess, famous princes, cavalry generals and 39,000 subordinates, and captured more than 50,000 horses, oxen, donkeys, mules, camels, and more than 600,000 sheep. Wusun took the captured things himself.
Jusai led more than a dozen officers and soldiers to return to the army with King User. Before arriving at Wusun, the Wusun people stole Chang Hui's official seal and talisman.
Chang Hui returned to the capital, thinking that he would be beheaded.
At that time, the five generals of the Han Dynasty had no merit. The emperor felt that Chang Hui's mission was successful, so he named him Changluo Hou.
He also sent Chang Hui back with gold silk ribbons to reward Wusun dignitaries and meritorious people. Chang Hui took the opportunity to report that the Kucha Kingdom had killed the captain Lai Dan and did not punish them. Please go and attack Kucha. Emperor Xuan did not agree.
General Huo Guang hinted that Chang Hui would make his own decisions based on the situation.
Chang Hui arrived at the Wusun Kingdom with 500 officers and soldiers. When he came back and passed by Kucha, he recruited 20,000 troops from the western country. He ordered his deputy to send 20,000 troops from Kucha to tie up the country. Wusun sent 7,000 troops to attack Kucha from three sides. Before the army could gather together, they sent someone to accuse King Qiuci of killing the envoys of the Han Dynasty in the past.
King Qiuci apologized and said: This is the result of being harmed by the noble Gu Yi when I was the late king. I am not guilty.
Chang Hui said: Even so, Gu Yi must be tied up, and I can let the king go.
King Qiuci tied up Guyi and took him to Chang Hui. Chang Hui killed Guyi and went back.
Later, Chang Hui replaced Su Wu as the vassal state. He was familiar with the situation in foreign countries and worked hard many times with meritorious deeds.
In the middle of the year of Ganlu, the later general Zhao Chongguo passed away, and the emperor appointed Limulus Tomb as the right general, and the official position of the Dian vassal state remained as before.
When Emperor Xuan died, Chang Hui served Emperor Yuan. He died three years later, and his nickname was Zhuang Genyao.
The feudal state was passed down to the great-grandson, and was discontinued in the middle of Jianwu year.
Zheng Ji is from Kuaiji. Because he served in the army and went on several missions to Yousu, he was named Lang.
Dian Mu is a strong and persistent person and is familiar with foreign affairs.
Since the fortress was connected to Youqiu and Kui Luxing was conquered, school captains were set up to work in Quli.
At the time of Emperor Xuan, Zheng Ji worked in Quli as a minister and accumulated grain. He then mobilized armies from various countries to defeat the chariot division. He was promoted to Sima of the Guard and sent to guard the southern road west of Shanshan.
In the middle of the year of Shenjue, internal turmoil broke out among the Xiongnu. The Xianxian Shan, the king of Chu, planned to surrender to the Han Dynasty and sent someone to contact Zheng Ji.
Zheng Ji mobilized 50,000 people from Quli, Qiuci and other countries to meet King Yue Zhu. There were 12,000 people. Xiao Wang sent 12 people to follow Zheng Ji to Hequ. Many people fled. Zheng Ji chased these people and killed them, and then brought the remaining people to the capital.
Emperor Mo granted King Ri Zhu the title of Marquis of Guide.
After Zheng Ji defeated the chariot division, he surrendered and surrendered to the king. His reputation shocked the Western Regions, so he also took charge of the North Road to the west of the chariot division, so he was known as the Protector.
The establishment of Duhu began with Zheng Ji.
In order to commend him for his achievements, the emperor issued an edict saying: Zheng Ji, the captain of the cavalry in the Western Regions, appeased the foreign barbarians, declared his hope and credibility, welcomed the cousin of the Xiongnu Chanyu, King Ri Zhu, and his men, and attacked the Cheshi Douzi City, which was a remarkable achievement.
Zheng Ji was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan, and was granted food to 1,000 households in the city.
Zheng Ji then established a shogunate in the center of various countries in the Western Regions, and the official office was in Wulei City to pacify the various countries, kill, conquer, appease and recruit them.
The orders of the Han Dynasty were issued to the Western Regions, and construction was started by Zhang Qian and completed by Zheng Ji. These are recorded in the "Biography of the Western Regions".
After Zheng Ji passed away, he was given the title of Marquis Mu.
His son Zheng Guang inherited the title, but he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished.
In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, among the meritorious officials who were not expelled due to crimes, Zheng Yong, the great-grandson of Zheng Ji, was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan.
Gan Yanshou, courtesy name Junkuang, was from Yuzhi in the north.
When he was young, he was selected as Yu Lin because he was good at horseback riding and archery. His skills in throwing stones and jumping were unparalleled among his peers. He once jumped into Yu Lin's pavilion, so he was promoted to Lang.
After testing his hand-fighting skills, he was appointed as a disciple. He relied on his strength and was favored.
Soon he was transferred to the post of governor of Liaodong and was dismissed.
The cavalry general Xu Jia recommended Gan Yanshou as a doctor and admonished the doctor. He went to the Western Regions as an envoy to protect the cavalry captain. Together with the deputy captain Chen Tang, he killed Zhizhi Shanyu and was named Yichenghou.
After Gan Yanshou died, Mi was named Zhuanghou.
The feudal state was passed down to his great-grandson. After Wang Mang failed, the feudal state was ended.
Chen Tang, whose courtesy name is Zigong, is from Shanyang Xiaqiu.
When he was young, he liked to read, he was knowledgeable and well-versed in affairs, and he could write good articles.
The family was poor and relied on begging and borrowing money to make a living. He had no moral integrity and was not praised by the people in the state.
Chen Tang went west to Chang'an to seek an official position, hoping to become an eunuch and serve as a prime minister.
A few years later, Zhang Bo, the Marquis of Fuping, dated Chen Tang and admired his talent.
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Shao of the Yuan Dynasty ordered the princes to recommend talents, and Zhang Bo recommended Chen Tang.
In order to wait for promotion, Chen Tang did not go to the funeral after his father's death. Sili impeached Chen Tang for not observing filial piety. Zhang Bo's election and recommendation were fraudulent and did not follow the actual situation. He was cut off from 200 households. When he died, he was given the title of Mihou.
Chen Tang was imprisoned and sentenced.
Later, he was recommended to the rank of Lang again and requested to be sent to foreign countries several times.
After a long time, he was appointed as the deputy captain of the Western Regions and went on an envoy to the Western Regions together with Gan Yanshou.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, internal conflicts among the Xiongnu intensified, and five Chanyus competed for the throne. Huhanxie Chanyu and Zhizhi Chanyu both sent their sons as hostages, and the Han Dynasty accepted them.
Later, Hu Hanxie personally went to the Han Dynasty to proclaim himself a vassal to see Emperor Xuan. Zhizhi Chanyu thought that Hu Hanxie was weak and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Just in time for the Han Dynasty to send troops to escort Huhanxie Chanyu back, the Zhizhi moved westward and attacked Huji, Jiankun and Dingling, annexed the three kingdoms and unified them.
Zhizhi Chanyu resented that the Han Dynasty supported Huhanxie Chanyu but did not help him, so he trapped the Han Dynasty envoy Jiang Naishi and others and humiliated them.
In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Chanyu Zhizhi sent an envoy to pay tribute, and asked him to take away his son who was serving as a servant and was willing to surrender to the court.
The Han Dynasty discussed sending the Wei Si Ma Guji to escort the servant.
Dr. Gong Yu and Dr. Kuang Heng believed that the Spring and Autumn Annals stated that all the requirements of the Yi and Di could not be met. Now Zhizhi Chanyu's heart towards enlightenment is not pure yet, and his place is quite far away. It is best to send an envoy to send his son to the border area and then return.
Gu Ji wrote a letter and said: China and the Yi Di have a bond but never extinguish them. Now that they have raised his children for ten years, the favor has been very great. Now he goes to a remote and empty place without escorting him, and returns when he reaches the frontier. This means that he has abandoned him and no longer loves him, causing them to lose their attachment. It is not appropriate to abandon the previous favor and create subsequent resentment.
The discussants saw that Jiang Naichi had no way to deal with the enemy before, lacked wisdom and courage, and suffered humiliation, so they worried about the minister in advance.
If my minister is fortunate enough to be able to hold on to the strong man's talisman, uphold the sage's orders, and declare his profound kindness, he should not dare to be cruel and cunning.
If he has the heart of an animal and behaves cruelly to his ministers, then the Chanyu will be burdened with deep sins for a long time, and he will definitely flee far away and not dare to approach the border.
It is the interest of the country and the wish of the ministers to lose a person and stabilize the people.
I hope to send him to the Zhizhi court.
The emperor presented Gu Ji's memorial to his superiors. Gong Yu argued again, believing that Gu Ji's visit would definitely bring disaster and trouble to the country, and he could not agree to his memorial.
The right general Feng Fengshi thought it could be dispatched, and the emperor agreed.
After arriving at the royal court of Zhizhi, Shanyu Zhizhi became angry and even killed Gu Ji and others.
Zhizhi Chanyu himself knew that he had betrayed the Han Dynasty, and he also heard that Huhanxie was more powerful, so he fled west to Kangju.
King Kangju married his daughter to Chanyu Zhizhi as his wife, and Zhizhi also married his daughter to King Kangju.
King Kangju respected Zhizhi Chanyu very much, and planned to rely on his power to coerce other countries. Zhizhi borrowed troops several times to attack Wusun, and went deep into Chigu City, killing and plundering the people, seizing livestock and property. Wusun did not dare to pursue them, and the west was empty. There was no one living in the area thousands of miles around.
Zhizhi Chanyu thought he was a great country, had a great reputation and was respected by others, and was proud of his victory. He was not treated politely by King Kangju. In anger, he killed King Kangju's daughter and hundreds of his dignitaries and people. Some of them were cut into pieces and thrown into the Du Lai water.
The people were recruited to build the city, five hundred people were used every day, and it stopped after two years.
He also sent envoys to ask Hesu and Dayuan to pay tribute every year, but they dared not refuse to pay.
The Han Dynasty sent three groups of envoys to Kangju to ask for the bodies of Gu Ji and others. Zhizhi Chanyu trapped the envoys and humiliated them. He refused to obey Shao's order, but wrote a letter through the governor, saying: I am in hardship and danger. I am willing to surrender to the powerful Han Dynasty and send my son as a hostage.
Zhizhi Shanyu was so proud and neglectful.
In the third year of Jianzhao's reign, Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou went to the Western Regions as envoys.
Chen Tang was a calm, brave and resourceful man with many strategies. He liked to build outstanding achievements. Every time he passed through capitals, towns, mountains and rivers, he would often climb to high places to take a look.
After receiving the mission to a foreign country, he planned with Gan Yanshou and said: "The Yi and Di are afraid of obeying the big tribes. This is their nature."
The Western Region originally belonged to the Xiongnu, but now Zhizhi Chanyu has spread far and wide, invading and bullying Wusun, Dayuan and other countries. He often advises Kang Ju and wants to surrender them.
If we can get these two countries, attack Yili in the north, Parthia in the west, and arrange Ji Yuezhi and Shanli Wuyi in the south, within a few years, the situation of several countries with capitals will be critical.
Moreover, their people are fierce, like to fight, and often win. If they are indulged for a long time, they will definitely become a hidden danger in the Western Region.
Although Zhizhi Chanyu was located quite far away, the barbarians did not have solid city walls or powerful swords and crossbows to defend themselves. If they mobilized the officers and soldiers stationed in the fields and led Wusun's troops to attack them all the way to the city, they would have nowhere to go when they fled, and they would not be able to defend in vain. Thousands of years of achievements could be accomplished in one day.
Gan Yanshou also believed that this was the case, so he prepared to submit a memorial to ask for instructions. Chen Tang added: "All major national affairs must be discussed by ministers. Extraordinary strategies are beyond the imagination of ordinary people, and things must not be approved."
Gan Yanshou hesitated and did not listen.
It happened that he had been ill for a long time, so Chen Tang alone relied on the imperial court to mobilize the troops from various countries in the towns and the officers and soldiers of the Che Division and Guowuji Colonel in the field.
When Gan Yanshou found out, he got up in panic and planned to stop him.
Chen Tang got angry, held down his sword and scolded Gan Yanshou, saying: The troops have gathered, do you want to ruin everyone's affairs?
Gan Yanshou had no choice but to obey him. The marching formation was deployed, and three schools of Yangwei, Baihu and Heqi were added. The total number of Han soldiers and Hu soldiers was more than 40,000. Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang submitted a self-impeachment report to the emperor and stated the situation of the use of troops.
On the same day, they led the army to separate routes and divided them into six schools. Three of them crossed Congling from the south road to Dawan. The other three schools were led by the governor himself. They set out from Wensu State, entered Chigu via the north road, passed Wusun, and reached the border of Kangju, all the way to the west of Tianchi.
The deputy king of Kangju, Baotian, led thousands of cavalry and invaded the east of Chigu City. He killed and robbed more than a thousand of King Wusun's people and took away many livestock and property. They encountered the Han Dynasty army at the rear and robbed a considerable amount of the baggage of the troops at the rear.
Chen Tang released the Hu army to attack them, killed 460 people, and obtained the 470 people they had robbed, and returned them to King Yada Wusun. The horses, cattle, and sheep obtained were used for military purposes.
He also captured Yinudu, a prominent figure in Baotian.
When they arrived at the border of Shubu in Kangju, Chen Tang ordered the army not to loot.
He secretly called Tu Mo, a prominent figure in Kangju, to meet him, explained to him the power and credibility of the Han Dynasty, drank wine with him and formed an alliance, and then let him go.
Leading the army forward from the trail, they stopped advancing and set up camp when they reached a place about sixty miles away from Shanyu City.
He also captured Kaimo, the son of Beise, a prominent figure in Kangju, and asked him to serve as a guide.
Beise's son was also the younger brother of Tu Mo's mother. They all resented Shan Yu, so they knew Zhizhi's situation in detail.
The next day he led the army forward again. He was still thirty miles away from the city and stopped to set up camp.
Shanyu sent an envoy to ask why the Han army came, and replied: Shanyu wrote to say that he was in a difficult situation now, and he was willing to surrender to the Han Dynasty and come to the Han Dynasty in person to see him.
The emperor felt sorry for Shanyu who left the vast territory of the Xiongnu and was wronged in Kangju, so he sent the general guard to welcome Shanyu's wife and children. I was afraid that your surroundings would be alarmed, so the army did not dare to go to the city.
Envoys came and went several times to inform each other of the situation.
Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang then reproached Shan Yu and said: "We have come all the way for Shan Yu, but up to now no famous princes or ministers have come to see the general to accept orders. How could Shan Yu ignore the big plan and lose the etiquette of a host towards his guests?"

summary:
Fu Jiezi, from the North, became an official through military service. During the Yuanfeng period, he was sent as an envoy to Dayuan and condemned the kings of Loulan and Qiuci for killing Han envoys. After returning, he proposed to General Huo Guang to assassinate the King of Loulan to establish Han prestige. Huo Guang agreed, and Fu Jiezi used gold and silk as bait to lure the king. During a private meeting, two soldiers stabbed the king to death. Fu Jiezi declared the king's guilt and installed a new ruler. He was rewarded with the title of Marquis of Yiyang and 700 households. His title was later abolished due to his son's crime but restored under Wang Mang.

Chang Hui, from Taiyuan, was detained by the Xiongnu for over a decade while accompanying Su Wu. After Emperor Zhao's reign, he was sent to Wusun, where he coordinated a joint Han-Wusun attack on the Xiongnu, resulting in significant victories. He later executed a noble from Qiuci for killing a Han captain. Chang Hui succeeded Su Wu as a vassal state official and served under Emperors Xuan and Yuan, earning the posthumous title Zhuang Genyao.

Zheng Ji, from Kuaiji, served as a military officer and became an expert in foreign affairs. He established agricultural colonies in Quli and defeated the Che division, earning the title of Protector of the Western Regions. He was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan with 1,000 households. His son died without an heir, ending the title, but it was later restored to his great-grandson.

Gan Yanshou, from Yuzhi, was a skilled horseman and archer. He served as an envoy to the Western Regions and, with Deputy Captain Chen Tang, killed Zhizhi Chanyu. He was named Marquis of Yicheng. His title passed to his great-grandson before ending under Wang Mang.

Chen Tang, from Shanyang, was a learned but poor man who sought office in Chang'an. He was recommended by Zhang Bo but imprisoned for failing to attend his father's funeral. Later, as Deputy Captain of the Western Regions, he and Gan Yanshou led a campaign against Zhizhi Chanyu, who had killed Han envoys. They mobilized over 40,000 troops, besieged Zhizhi's city, and killed the chanyu. Despite their success, they faced criticism for acting without orders. After a lengthy debate, Emperor Yuan granted them titles and rewards, though Chen Tang was later dismissed for misconduct. He was eventually exiled to Dunhuang but recalled before his death in Chang'an.

Duan Huizong, from Tianshui, served as Protector of the Western Regions and was respected for his integrity. He killed a rebellious Wusun prince, Fanqiu, with a small force, earning the title of Marquis of Guannei. He died in Wusun at age 75, mourned by all nations.

The text concludes that from Zhang Qian's time to Wang Mang's era, 18 protectors served, with notable figures like Zheng Ji, Gan Yanshou, and Chen Tang. Chen Tang's unruliness led to his downfall, but his deeds are recorded for posterity.

People like Wang Feng cannot be allowed to rule for a long time. He should be allowed to retreat to the palace and other loyal and wise ministers should be chosen to replace him.
Since Wang Feng suggested deposing Wang Shang and later sent King Dingtao back to the feudal state, Emperor Cheng was filled with anger and dissatisfaction.
After listening to Wang Zhang's words, Emperor Cheng realized something, so he adopted Wang Zhang's opinion and said to Wang Zhang: Without Jing Zhaoyin's outspoken advice, I would not have heard of such a national plan!
Besides, only wise people can understand wise people. Try to find me a few people who can assist in government affairs.
So Wang Zhang wrote a secret memorial, recommending Prince Xiao of Zhongshan's uncle Langye Prefecture Feng Yewang. He was the second minister during the late emperor's reign. He was loyal, upright, and very resourceful.
As the uncle of King Xiao, King Feng Ye served as a foreign official and was recalled because of his virtue. This shows that a wise monarch likes to appoint wise men.
When Emperor Cheng was the crown prince, he heard many times that King Feng Ye was a famous minister of the late emperor, and his reputation was far higher than that of Wang Feng, so he planned to let him replace Wang Feng.
At the beginning, every time Wang Zhang was summoned, Emperor Cheng would retreat.
At that time, the Queen Mother's cousin Wang Yin, the son of Changle Guardsman Wang Hong, eavesdropped on their conversation, knew everything about Wang Zhang's plan, and told Wang Feng.
After Wang Feng heard this, he complained of illness and returned to his mansion. Shangshu asked to resign and return to his hometown. He said goodbye to the emperor: "I am stupid and stupid, but I was able to make seven of my relatives and brothers a prince. My family received the emperor's favor and received countless rewards."
I have been assisting the government for seven years, and the emperor has entrusted me with important responsibilities. I listen to people's suggestions and often appoint wise men and women.
Nothing was done well, which led to disharmony between yin and yang and frequent disasters. The root cause was that I had no merit in my tenure. This was the first reason why I should retire.
The records in the "Five Classics" and what the scribes said all attribute the blame for the solar eclipse to the improper appointment of ministers. The "Book of Changes" says that I broke my right arm. This is the second reason why I should retire.
Since the Heping period, I have been ill for many years and have been recuperating at home many times. I have ignored government affairs and only received rank and salary. This is the third reason why I should retire.
Your Majesty cannot bear to depose me because of the Empress Dowager. I also know that I should be exiled to a distant place, but I also think in my heart that the holy grace my family has received is immeasurable. I should be diligent in royal affairs and not hesitate to break my body. I should not have the thought of leaving the emperor just because I am useless. Over the past year or so, my illness has indeed gotten worse and worse day by day, and my wish has been difficult to realize. I just want to resign and go back to my hometown to recuperate on my own. I hope that I can rely on His Majesty's gods to survive and recover within a month and see Your Majesty again. Otherwise, I will be buried underground.
I have no talent, but I am favored by His Majesty, and everyone in the world knows that I have received great favor from the Emperor. When I resigned and returned to my hometown due to illness, everyone in the world knows that I was pitied and favored by Your Majesty, and the Emperor's favor is so great.
My return to my hometown will be of great benefit to the country and will not cause much discussion.
Please have mercy on me, Your Majesty!
The words were very sad, and after hearing about it, the Queen Mother cried for him and couldn't eat.
Emperor Cheng had relied on Wang Feng since he was a child. He couldn't bear to remove him, so he replied to Wang Feng: I am not good at managing government. There are many flaws in the management of state affairs. Therefore, God has repeatedly caused disasters, which are all my responsibility.
The general took all the blame on himself and planned to resign and return home. So who will I rely on?
Isn’t it said in the Book of Books? Don't go away and put me in trouble. You must cheer up, calm down, and restrain yourself. I hope that the disease can be cured immediately, and I will be satisfied.
So Wang Feng rose up and took charge again.
Emperor Cheng sent a minister to impeach Wang Zhang for his crime, saying: Knowing that King Feng Ye had previously served in the capital as the uncle of King Xiao, he recommended him privately in order to make the ministers in the court attach themselves to the princes and kings; and he also knew that Zhang Meiren was serving the emperor, but he led Qiang and Hu people to kill the first child to pure blood. This is not what a minister should say.
Then Wang Zhang was handed over to the judge for trial.
The Tingwei accused Wang Zhang of treason, thinking that he wanted to cut off the emperor's heirs by comparing the emperor to the Yi Di; he betrayed the emperor and secretly planned to be King Dingtao.
Wang Zhang died in prison, and his wife and children were exiled to Hepu.
From then on, when the ministers saw Wang Feng, they did not dare to look directly at him, and the local officials in the prefecture and state were all his cronies.
He also named Wang Yin, the imperial servant in the palace, as the official censor, ranking among the three nobles.
The five younger brothers who were granted the title of marquis, competed to spend extravagantly, bribed and gave away treasures in an endless stream. Each family had dozens of concubines in the back courtyard, and there were hundreds or even thousands of slaves. They rang bells and chimes, beautiful women danced, watched acrobatics, and sensual dogs and horses;
The common people sang songs for them and said: When the five princes first became prosperous, Quyanghou was the strongest. He destroyed Gaodu and built a palace, and then spread to the Waidu area. The earth and mountains gradually became taller, like the emperor's White Tiger Palace.
They are so extravagant and arrogant.
But these people are well versed in the ways of the world, like to cultivate wise men, and spend all their money in this area to show that they are not vulgar.
Wang Feng assisted the government for a total of eleven years.
In the autumn of the third year of Yangshuo, Wang Feng was seriously ill. Emperor Cheng personally visited his home many times. He held his hand and cried and said: The general is seriously ill. If he fails, let Ping'ahou Wang Tan take his place.
Wang Feng kowtowed and said with tears: Although Wang Tan and others are my closest relatives, they advocate extravagance and cannot set an example for the people of the world. They are not as cautious as Wang Yin, the imperial censor. I am willing to die to recommend them.
When Wang Feng died, Shangshu thanked the emperor, but insisted on recommending Wang Yin to replace him, saying that Wang Tan and other five people must not be reused.
Emperor Cheng agreed.
At first, Wang Tan was arrogant and refused to serve Wang Feng, but Wang Yin respected Wang Feng and was as humble as a son to his father, so Wang Feng recommended him.
After Wang Feng's death, Emperor Cheng went to pay his respects in person and presented it to the Wang family as a light chariot and warrior. During the funeral, soldiers lined up from Chang'an to Weiling, and Mi was given the title of Marquis Jingcheng.
Wang Feng's son Wang Xiang inherited the title of Marquis and served as a Weiwei.
Wang Yin, the imperial censor, finally replaced Wang Feng as the Great Sima Cavalry General, and Ping'ahou Wang Tan was given the special rank to command the troops defending the city.
Gu Yong persuaded Wang Tan not to accept the position of guarding the city gate, and he became dissatisfied with Wang Yin from then on. This incident is recorded in "Gu Yong's Biography".
As a cousin, Wang Yin took charge of political affairs beyond his close relatives. He was cautious and managed the political affairs himself. More than a year later, Emperor Cheng went to Shao and said: General Wang Yin of Chariots and Cavalry is serving in the palace. He is loyal and pure, and works hard for state affairs. He was originally a censor. As a foreign relative, he should be in charge of the army. He also became a general. I am very sorry that he did not get the reward from the prime minister!
Wang Yin was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang, and the enfeoffment was the same as that of the Five Marquises, with a total of 3,000 households.
At first, Prince Shang, the Marquis of Chengdu, fell ill and wanted to escape the summer heat, so he asked the emperor to borrow the Mingguang Palace. Later, he passed through the capital Chang'an, led the Lishui River into the big pond at home for boating, erected umbrellas decorated with green feathers, set up curtains, and asked the boatmen to sing Yue songs.
Emperor Cheng visited Wang Shang's residence and saw him passing through Chang'an City to divert water. He was very angry, but he was jealous and did not speak out.
Later, when I was traveling incognito, I passed by Quyanghou's house and saw that the earth-mountain terrace in the garden was similar to the White Tiger Palace.
The emperor was furious and blamed the chariot general Wang Yin.
Brothers Wang Shang and Wang Gen planned to tattoo their faces and cut off their noses to apologize to the Queen Mother.
Emperor Cheng became even more angry after hearing this, and sent his minister to question Sili Xiaowei and Jing Zhaoyin. Knowing full well that the Marquis of Chengdu, Wang Shang, crossed the capital without authorization and introduced Lishui River, the Marquis of Quyang was arrogant and extravagant, and the expenses of the mansion were arrogant to the emperor. The stone steps were painted red, and the doors were engraved with cyan patterns.
The two kowtowed and went home to reflect.
He also gave a document to General Wang Yin of Chariots and Cavalry, saying: There is no one in the family who is willing to be defeated, but he wants to be tattooed and tortured himself, and to suffer this humiliation in front of the Queen Mother, hurting the heart of a loving mother, and causing trouble to the country!
The cousin's family is powerful, but the emperor's power has been getting weaker and weaker for a long time, and now he wants to use punishment.
You gather those princes together and wait for Shao's fate at your house.
On this day, Shao ordered Shangshu to report the old story of the execution of General Bo Zhao during the reign of Emperor Wen.
The chariot general Wang Yin sat on a straw mat and begged for punishment. Wang Shang, Wang Li, and Wang Gen all came carrying axes and begged for punishment.
Emperor Cheng couldn't bear to kill them, so he gave up.
After some time, Ping'ahou Wang Tan died, Mi was named Anhou, and his son Wang Ren inherited the title.
The Queen Mother felt sorry that her younger brother Wang Man had died early and was not able to become a marquis. Wang Man's widowed wife Qu also served her. Her son Wang Mang lost his father when he was young and could not be compared with others, so she often mentioned him in front of Emperor Cheng.
Prince Tan of Ping'a, Prince Shang of Chengdu and some officials all praised Wang Mang.
Later, Emperor Cheng issued an edict to postulate Wang Man as the Marquis of Ai of Xindu, and his son Wang Mang inherited the title as Marquis of Xindu.
Later, Chunyu Chang, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, was granted the title of Marquis of Dingling.
Among the relatives of the Wang family, there are a total of ten people who have been granted the title of marquis.
Emperor Cheng regretted that he had dismissed Ping'a Hou Wang Tan and died without being able to assist the government, so he gave the title of Chengdu Hou Wang Shang Tejin, allowing him to command the troops defending the city, set up a shogunate, and recommend officials like a general.
Du Ye persuaded the cavalry general Wang Yin to get close to Wang Shang. This incident was recorded in the "Biography of Du Ye".
The Wang family's official ranks were getting higher and higher, but Wang Yin was the only one who paid attention to the law, spoke out and persuaded many times, and had the character of a loyal minister. He assisted in political affairs for eight years and passed away.
Emperor Cheng personally went to pay his respects as he did to Wang Feng, presented him with honors and favors, and gave him the title of Jinghou.
Wang Yin's son Wang Shun succeeded to the throne and became the imperial servant.
Te Jin, the Marquis of Chengdu, Wang Shang, replaced Wang Yin as General Sima Wei, and gave Hong Yang Hou Wang the position of Te Jin, allowing him to command the troops defending the city.
Wang Shang assisted the government for four years when he became seriously ill and asked to resign. Emperor Cheng took pity on him and made him a general. He also rewarded 2,000 households and 1 million yuan.
When Wang Shang passed away, Emperor Cheng personally paid his respects according to the old system of generals and bestowed him with honors and favors. Mi was given the title Marquis of Jingcheng. Wang Shang's son Wang Kuang succeeded him as Marquis.
The Marquis of Hongyang should have joined the court to assist the government in order, but he committed a crime and gave up. This incident is recorded in "Sun Baozhuan".
Emperor Cheng gave up Wang Li and appointed Guangluxun Quyanghou Wanggen as the Grand Sima Hussar General. More than a year later, 1,700 households were added as fiefs.
The Marquis of Gaoping had neither talent nor fame. He died that year and was given the title of Marquis of Dai. His son Wang Maizhi succeeded him as Marquis of Dai.
In the first year of Suihe, Emperor Cheng had ascended the throne for more than 20 years and still had no heirs. King Dingtao Gong had died and his son succeeded to the throne.
Queen Dingtao, the grandmother of King Dingtao, bribed General Wang Gen with generous gifts in the hope of making King Dingtao the prince. Wang Gen spoke on her behalf. Emperor Cheng also planned to make King Dingtao the prince, so he summoned him to the capital to be crowned prince.
At this time, Wang Gen had been assisting the government for five years. He asked to resign and return to his hometown. Emperor Cheng added 5,000 households to Wang Gen's fiefdom, rewarded him with a carriage, four horses, and five hundred catties of gold. He dismissed his official position and returned to his mansion.
Previously, Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, was able to make suggestions as a relative and served as a guard official, assisting in government affairs.
In this year, Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, reported Chun Yuchang's past crimes and had colluded with Hongyang Marquis Wang Li. Chun Yuchang was imprisoned and died, and Wang Li returned to his fiefdom. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Chunyu Chang".
Therefore, Wang Gen, the Marquis of Quyang, recommended Wang Mang to replace him. Emperor Cheng also believed that Wang Mang was loyal and upright, so he promoted Wang Mang from the position of Guanglu Guanglu to the rank of Chief Sima.
More than a year later, Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai ascended the throne.
The Queen Mother issued an edict asking Wang Mang to resign and go home, but she avoided the matter because he was a relative of the emperor.
Emperor Ai began to treat Wang Mang preferentially but refused to agree.
Wang Mang wrote a letter insisting on resigning.
Emperor Ai came to Xia Shao and said: During his tenure, Wang Gen, Marquis of Quyang, had some strategies to govern the country and secure it.
Anyanghou Wang Shun, the servant in charge of the imperial court, went to take care of the prince's family and enlightened me. I am loyal and have no second heart, but have old kindness.
Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, has worked hard for state affairs and upheld justice, and he hopes to assist me in governing the country. I am very sorry that the Empress Dowager has sent him to retire and go home.
Two thousand households of Wang Gen were granted fiefs, five hundred households of Wang Shun, and three hundred and fifty households of Wang Mang.
Wang Mang was given the position of special advancement, and Wang Mang entered the palace to see him on the first day of the lunar month.
He also asked Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, to return to the capital.
Emperor Ai was very young, but he was unhappy when he heard that the Wang family was arrogant and prosperous. Because he had just ascended the throne, he gave them preferential treatment.
A month later, Lieutenant of Sili Jieguang reported: The family of Quyanghou Wanggen is powerful and distinguished. Three generations have been in power, five generals have controlled political affairs, and the people of the world have a tendency to flatter and please. Wang Gen was greedy and evil, amassed a lot of money, and acted recklessly. He overhauled the palace, built a rockery in the palace, and set up two markets. The steps in front of the palace were painted red, and the doors were engraved with cyan patterns. When he went hunting, he ordered his servants to wear bell armor, hold bows and arrows, and line up like infantry; Wang Gen was evil in his heart and planned to control the government. He elected Zhang Ye, a close official, to serve as minister, deceived the emperor, blocked the opinions of his ministers, blocked the way to achieve the king's career internally, made friends with princes and kings externally, was arrogant and extravagant, and exceeded his status. Destroy the system. Wang Gen was a close relative of the late emperor and an important minister of the country. After the late emperor's death, Wang Gen did not feel sad and missed the late emperor. Before the late emperor's mausoleum was built, he openly married the former Yeting kabuki performer Wang Feijun and others. They held banquets and indulged in singing and dancing, abandoning the late emperor's deep kindness to him and violating the etiquette and justice that a minister should abide by.
Wang Gen's brother's son, the Marquis of Chengdu, Wang Kuang, was fortunate enough to succeed his father as a foreign relative and become the minister of the princes. However, he did not miss repaying the profound favor of the emperor, and also married a nobleman from Yuanting.
Therefore Emperor Ai said: The late emperor treated Wang Gen and Wang Kuang and his son with great kindness, but now they have betrayed their kindness!
Because Wang Gen once helped Emperor Ai become the prince and let him return to the fiefdom.
Wang Kuang was dismissed from his official position and became a commoner, and returned to his hometown.
Those whom Wang Gen and Wang Kuang's father Wang Shang recommended to serve as officials were all dismissed.
Two years later, Empress Dowager Fu and Emperor Ai's mother Ding Ji were honored as Empress Dowager Tai and Empress Dowager respectively.
A minister reported that: Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, who had previously been the Grand Sima, suppressed the proposal of adding a title, which was detrimental to filial piety, and Wang Ren, the Marquis of Ping'a, was harboring relatives of Tsang Zhaoyi. Both of them should be moved back to their fiefdoms.
Many people in the world feel wronged for Wang.
Yang Xuan, the remonstrating official, wrote a secret letter saying: Emperor Xiaocheng took into account the country's great plans, praised your majesty's noble morals and allowed your majesty to inherit the throne. The late emperor's strategy was far-reaching and his kindness was extremely generous.
Thinking of the late Emperor's wishes, didn't he want His Majesty to take his place and provide for the Queen Mother?
The Empress Dowager was seventy years old and had experienced sad changes many times. She ordered her relatives to retreat on their own to avoid the Ding and Fu families.
Everyone who travels will shed tears for this, not to mention His Majesty, if you climb high and look far away, wouldn't you be worthy of the late emperor of Yanling!
Aihu was deeply moved by his words, and made Wang Shang's second son Wang Yi the Marquis of Shengdu.
In the first year of Yuanshou, a solar eclipse occurred.
When the wise and kind-hearted ministers and Confucian scholars stated their political opinions in response to the imperial edict, most of them complained about the new capital, Wang Mang, so Emperor Ai summoned Wang Mang and Ping Ahou Wang Ren to return to the capital to serve the Queen Mother.
Wang Gen, Marquis of Quyang, died and the feudal state was abolished.
In the second year, Emperor Ai died without a son. The Empress Dowager appointed Wang Mang as the Grand Sima, and together with him, he summoned King Zhongshan as Emperor Ai, who became Emperor Ping.
Emperor Ping was only nine years old and fell ill that year, so the Queen Mother came to the court to handle the affairs and entrusted the affairs of the court to Wang Mang.
Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, was Wang Mang's uncle, and Wang Ren, the Marquis of Ping'a, had always been upright. Wang Mang was wary of them, so he ordered his ministers to fabricate charges and petition to have Wang Li and Wang Ren return to their fiefdoms.
Wang Mang deceived the Queen Mother all day long, saying that he was assisting the government to bring peace to the world. The ministers submitted a petition requesting that Wang Mang be honored as Duke Anhan.
Later, Wang Mang sent envoys to force Wang Li and Wang Ren to commit suicide. Wang Limi was given the title of Huanghou, and his son Wang Zhu succeeded him. Wang Renmi was given the title of Rahou, and his son Wang Shu succeeded to the title.
One year was created, which was the third year of Yuanshi.
The next year, Wang Mang hinted to the ministers to ask for his daughter to be appointed queen.
He also requested that Wang Mang be made Prime Minister, and Wang Mang's mother and two sons were named marquises. These events are recorded in the "Biography of Wang Mang".
Externally, Wang Mang controlled the words and deeds of ministers, asking them to praise his merits. Internally, he flattered the Queen Mother's attendants below the imperial level, bribing them with tens of thousands of dollars.
She also reported to the Queen Mother that her sisters Jun Xia should be named Guangenjun, Junli should be named Guanghuijun, and Jun's younger brother should be named Guangshijun. They were all rewarded with food. They praised Wang Mang together in front of the Queen Mother all day long.
Wang Mang also knew that the Queen Mother, as a woman, hated the life of living in the palace for a long time, so he planned to entertain the Queen Mother in exchange for greater power. He asked the Queen Mother to travel around the suburbs of the capital in four seasons to greet orphans, widows and chaste women.
In the spring, they visited the Cocoon Pavilion and led the queen and the wives of the princes to plant mulberry trees and pray for blessings and eliminate disasters by the Ba River; in the summer, they played between Sunsu, E, and Du; in the autumn, they visited Shu Pavilion, looked at Kunming from afar, and gathered at the Huangshan Palace; in the winter, they held banquets and drinks in the Feiyu Pavilion, hunted in Shanglan, climbed to the Changping Pavilion, and visited the scenery along the Jingshui River.
Whenever the Queen Mother passed through a county, she would show great kindness to the people and reward the people with money, silk, cattle and wine. This gradually formed a habit.
The Queen Mother said with a gentle face: When I first entered the Prince's house, I was summoned in the Bing Hall. It has been fifty or sixty years now, and I can still remember the scene at that time.
Wang Mang said, "The prince's palace is nearby. You can go there for fun without any trouble."
Therefore, the Queen Mother visited the Prince's palace and was very happy.
Nong'er, who was beside the Queen Mother, fell ill and lived in a foreign house. Wang Mang went to greet him personally.
Wang Mang went so far as to cater to the Queen Mother's wishes.
Emperor Ping died without heirs, so Wang Mang summoned Liu Ying, the youngest great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Marquis Guangqi, who was only two years old, on the pretext that he would divine the most auspicious divination.
It suggested that the ministers petitioned to establish Liu Ying as a son, and let the Prime Minister Anhan Duke Mang temporarily occupy the position of emperor and handle political affairs, just like the story of Zhou Gong assisting the king.
The Queen Mother believed that this was not allowed, but she could not stop it with her own strength, so Wang Mang became the regent, changed the reign name, and exercised the power of the emperor.
Not long after, Liu Chong, the Marquis of Anzhong of the clan, Zhai Yi, the prefect of Shujun, and others were disgusted with Wang Mang and raised troops one after another to kill him.
When the Queen Mother heard the news, she said: People think the same thing.
Even though I am a woman, I also know that Wang Mang will definitely be worried about his own safety and cannot do this.
Later, Wang Mang used the talisman to establish himself as the true emperor, and first presented those auspicious signs to the Queen Mother, who was shocked.
At the beginning, when Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty entered Xianyang and reached Bashang, Prince Qin Ying surrendered at Zhidao Pavilion and presented Qin Shihuang's national seal.
When the great ancestor executed Xiang Ji and ascended the throne as the emperor, he personally wore this national seal and passed it down from generation to generation, known as the Mochuan national seal. Because Ruzi had not yet ascended the throne, the imperial seal was kept in Changle Palace.
When Wang Mang came to the throne, he wanted to pass on the national seal, but the Queen Mother refused to give it to him.
Wang Mang instructed Anyang Marquis Wang Shun to convey his intention to the Queen Mother.
Wang Shun has always been cautious and thoughtful, and the Queen Mother usually likes to trust him.
Wang Shun paid a visit to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother knew that he was here to ask for the imperial seal for Wang Mang, so she angrily scolded him and said: Your father and son families have been favored by the Han family and have been rich and powerful for generations. Not only did you not repay the favor, you accepted the task of entrusting the orphans, but you took the opportunity to seize other people's countries. You no longer care about your kindness.
People like this are worse than pigs and dogs. How can there be brothers like you in the world!
Besides, I used the Golden Chamber Talisman to become the new emperor and changed the calendar and the system of clothing, carriages and horses, so I should make my own national seal and pass it on to all generations. Why do I need to come here to get the national seal that is unlucky for the country to perish?
I am an old widow of the Han family. I am about to die. I want to be buried with this Fang Chuanguo Seal, but you will not be able to get it in the end!
The Queen Mother cried while speaking, and all the waiters below the chief minister beside her shed tears.
Wang Shun couldn't restrain his sadness. After a long time, he raised his head and said to the Queen Mother: We people have nothing to say.
Wang Mang must get the imperial seal, can the Queen Mother never give it to him?
When the Queen Mother heard Wang Shun's sincere words, she was afraid that Wang Mang would threaten her, so she took out the imperial seal and threw it on the ground to Wang Shun, saying: I am old and dying, and if you brothers behave like this, the Wang family will be exterminated!
Wang Shun got the imperial seal and presented it to Wang Mang. Wang Mang was so happy that he held a banquet for the Empress Dowager at the terrace of Weiyang Palace and had fun.
Wang Mang also wanted to change the Queen Mother's Han Dynasty title and her seal, but he was afraid that she would not agree. Wang Mang's distant cousin, Wang Jian, wanted to flatter Wang Mang and wrote a letter saying: God abolished the Han Dynasty and established a new house. The Empress Dowager can no longer have the honorary title and should be abolished along with the Han Dynasty to comply with the destiny of heaven.
Wang Mang took a carriage and horse to the East Palace and personally reported the contents of the memorial to the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother said: This is right!
Wang Mang said: This is an immoral minister, and the crime he committed should be punished with death!
Therefore, the champion Zhang Yong presented a bronze biscuit engraved with fortune-telling. The text on it was "The Empress Dowager shall be the new wife's mother, the Empress Dowager."
Wang Mang then issued an edict: "I showed it to all the ministers, and they all said it's so beautiful!"
The words above were not carved or painted, they were created by nature. I thought that God had appointed me as the emperor by destiny, and also appointed the empress dowager as the new empress dowager. This was consistent with the alternation of the old and new dynasties, and did not treat the Mo family unfairly.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, it was popular among the people to pass on plans and offer wine and food to the Queen Mother of the West. This was a sign that the Queen Mother should become the mother of the country in the change of dynasty.
I obey the destiny, how dare I disobey!
He deliberately chose an auspicious month and period, personally led the ministers, and presented the empress dowager's seal and ribbon to respond to God's will and make it known to the world.
The Queen Mother accepted Wang Mang's suggestion.
Wang Mang killed Wang Jian with poisoned wine and made Zhang Yong a tribute fuzi.
At the beginning, when Wang Mang was the Duke of Anhan, he flattered the Queen Mother and requested that the temple name of Emperor Yuan be Gaozong. After the death of the Queen Mother, he could be assigned to the Temple of Emperor Yuan according to etiquette.
When Wang Mang changed the title of the Queen Mother to Xinshi Wenmu, she severed her relationship with the Han Dynasty, not wanting her to be worthy of the Yuan Emperor.
Emperor Xiaoyuan's dormitory temple was destroyed and a new dormitory temple was built for Empress Dowager Wenmu. The original main hall of Xiaoyuan Temple was specially used as a place for Wenmu to hold banquets. After it was completed, it was named longevity palace.
Because the Queen Mother is still alive, it is not called a temple.
Because the Queen Mother liked to go out for sightseeing, Wang Mang held a banquet in the Longevity Palace and invited the Queen Mother there by car.
After the Queen Mother arrived, she was shocked to see the dilapidated Xiaoyuan Temple. She cried and said: This is the ancestral temple of the Han family. It is blessed by gods and has nothing to do with you. Why did you destroy it?
Besides, if ghosts and gods have no consciousness, why build a temple?
If the ghosts and gods knew it, how could I, as the late emperor's concubine, humiliate the late emperor's temple and display sacrifices for me!
He privately said to the waiters on his left and right: This man has repeatedly disrespected the gods. How can he be blessed for a long time?
This drinking session ended on bad terms.
Since Wang Mang usurped the throne, he knew that the Queen Mother was resentful, so he tried every means to flatter the Queen Mother. However, the Queen Mother became increasingly unhappy.
Wang Mang changed the system of wearing sable among the servants of the Mo family, so that all the servants wore yellow sable. He also changed the dates of Zhengshuo and Fula in the Han family.
The Queen Mother made her subordinates all wear sable. On New Year's Day and the twelfth lunar month of the Han Dynasty, she would sit and drink with the waiters around her to show that she did not forget the Han Dynasty.
When the Queen Mother was eighty-four years old, in February of the fifth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Guichou died.
In March Yiyou, he was buried in Weiling together with Emperor Yuan.
Wang Mang issued an edict and asked the doctor Yang Xiong to write a sacrificial text, saying: The essence of Taiyin, the spirit of Shalu, the sky unites with Han, and the matching element is generated.
It shows that she is in harmony with Shalu of Yuancheng.
The essence of Taiyin means that the Queen Mother was born from a dream of the moon.
Ten years after the death of the Queen Mother, Han soldiers killed Wang Mang.
At the beginning, Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, returned to his fiefdom of Nanyang and formed a relationship with the Liu family's children. Wang Li's youngest son, Wang Dan, became the prefect of Zhongshan.
When Emperor Guangwu of Shizu just raised an army, Wang Dan surrendered and he became a general and died in battle.
Shizu took great pity on him and named his son Wang Hong the Marquis of Wuhuan. This title has been passed down to this day.
Situ Peng Ban Biao said: Since the Three Dynasties, the reasons for the demise of princes and monarchs recorded in the "Spring and Autumn" have rarely been caused by favored women.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, the concubines' families, the Lu family, the Huo family, and the Shangguan family, nearly endangered the country several times.
The rise of Wang Mang was due to the fact that after Xiaoyuan, there were four generations of emperors in the Han Dynasty. Her mother respected the world. She reigned for more than sixty years. Her younger brothers came to power one after another and controlled the government. They granted a total of five generals and ten princes. Finally, Wang Mang, the new prince of the capital, realized his ambition.
The dynasties have changed, but the Queen of the Yuan Dynasty is still loyal and holds the imperial seal in her hand, and does not want to hand it over to Wang Mang. The kindness of a woman is really pitiful!
summary:
Queen Xiaoyuan was the aunt of Wang Mang, who claimed descent from the Yellow Emperor. According to Wang Mang's autobiography "Ziben," the lineage traced from the Yellow Emperor through Yu Shun to various descendants who were granted titles during the Zhou Dynasty. The family eventually took the surname Wang after Tian An, a descendant of Qi royalty, lost his feudal state during the Han Dynasty and was called "Wang Family" by the people of Qi.

Wang Mang's ancestor Wang He (Wengru) served as Emperor Wu's embroidered censor. Unlike other harsh officials who killed tens of thousands, Wengru showed leniency and was dismissed for not following the emperor's wishes. He saved over ten thousand people and predicted his descendants would prosper. After resigning, he moved to Yuancheng in Wei County, where a divination predicted that a virtuous woman would appear in 645 years, and later that the Wang family would have a noble daughter who would flourish.

Wengru's son Wang Jin fathered Wang Zhengjun, who became Empress of Emperor Yuan. Before her birth, her mother dreamed of the moon falling into her belly. Zhengjun was gentle and virtuous. After two betrothals ended with her fiancés dying, a fortune-teller declared her extremely valuable. She entered the palace at eighteen and became pregnant after being summoned by the crown prince, giving birth to Emperor Cheng.

When Emperor Yuan considered deposing the prince due to his fondness for King Dingtao Gong, Wang Feng (the queen's brother) worried alongside the queen. Emperor Yuan ultimately did not depose the prince due to the queen's caution and the late emperor's regard for him. After Emperor Yuan's death, Emperor Cheng ascended, honoring his mother as Empress Dowager and appointing Wang Feng as Grand General. The Wang family's prosperity began, with five brothers granted marquisates on the same day, known as the Five Marquises.

Wang Feng held immense power, with Emperor Cheng afraid to act independently. When Emperor Cheng wanted to appoint Liu Xin as a regular attendant, he was told to ask Wang Feng first, who refused. Emperor Cheng had no choice but to give up. Wang Feng dominated all state affairs, and ministers dared not look directly at him.

After Wang Feng's death, Wang Yin succeeded him as Grand Sima, followed by Wang Shang and Wang Gen. The Wang family's extravagance was legendary, with concubines, slaves, and lavish palaces. The common people sang songs comparing their palaces to the emperor's White Tiger Palace. Despite their excesses, they cultivated wise men to appear refined.

Emperor Cheng had no heirs for over twenty years. King Dingtao's grandmother bribed Wang Gen to make him crown prince. After Emperor Cheng's death, Emperor Ai ascended but was unhappy with the Wang family's power. He eventually forced Wang Mang and others to return to their fiefdoms. When Emperor Ai died without an heir, the Empress Dowager appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima, and they installed Emperor Ping, who was only nine years old.

Wang Mang gradually consolidated power, eventually becoming regent and later usurping the throne to establish the Xin dynasty. The Empress Dowager refused to give him the imperial seal, angrily denouncing him for betraying the Han dynasty. She threw the seal on the ground, predicting the Wang family would be exterminated. Wang Mang changed her title to "New Empress Dowager Wenmu," severing her connection to Han. She died at eighty-four, and ten years later, Han soldiers killed Wang Mang.

The historian Ban Biao noted that since the Three Dynasties, few dynasties fell due to favored women. The Wang family's rise came through four generations of empresses, with five generals and ten marquises, culminating in Wang Mang's usurpation. The Yuan Empress Dowager's loyalty, holding the imperial seal and refusing to surrender it, was truly pitiful.

translation:
Gongsun He, courtesy name Zishu, was born in Yiqu County, Beidi County.
Gongsun He's grandfather Kunxie was the prefect of Longxi County during the Han Dynasty. He was named Pingquhou because of his meritorious service in leading the army to attack the rebellious Wu, Chu and other countries. He wrote more than a dozen books.
Gongsun He was a knight when he was young, joined the army and made many military exploits.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was the crown prince, Gongsun He sacrificed his life for the prince. When Emperor Wu came to the throne, he promoted Gongsun He to the rank of servant.
Gongsun He's wife Wei Junru was the sister of Queen Wei, and Gongsun He was favored for this reason.
During the Yuanguang period of Emperor Wu, he was appointed General of Qingche and garrisoned in Mayi.
Four years later, he led his army out of Yunzhong to attack the Xiongnu.
After another five years of encountering him, he followed the general Wei Qing as a chariot and cavalry general to attack the Huns. With meritorious service, he was named Marquis of Nanao.
Later, as General Zuo, he attacked the Xiongnu from Dingxiang County, but failed. He was convicted of offering gold of insufficient quality and lost his title as a marquis.
Then General Fuju went out of Wuyuan County for more than 2,000 miles to attack the Xiongnu, but to no avail.
Eight years later, he finally replaced Shi Qing as prime minister and was named Ge Yihou.
At that time, the imperial court was very busy, supervising and punishing ministers.
After Gongsun Hong, the prime ministers Li Cai, Yan Qingzhai, and Zhao Zhou were convicted and died one after another.
Although Shi Qing died a good death because of his caution, he was criticized many times.
When Gongsun He was appointed as prime minister, he was unwilling to accept the Prime Minister's seal, kowtowed and cried, saying: I am originally from the border, and I became an official by relying on my ability to ride and shoot on horseback, but I am really not qualified to be prime minister.
When the emperor and his ministers saw Gongsun He's sorrow, they were moved to tears. Emperor Wu said: Help the prime minister up.
Gongsun He refused to get up, so the emperor got up and left. Gongsun He had no choice but to accept the appointment.
After leaving the palace, the ministers asked Gongsun He why he did not want to be the prime minister. Gongsun He said: Your Majesty is wise, but I am not qualified to be the prime minister. I am afraid of heavy responsibility, and I will be in danger from now on.
Gongsun He's son Gongsun Jingsheng replaced Gongsun He as the imperial servant, and father and son lived together as ministers.
Gongsun Jingsheng relied on the fact that he was the son of the queen's sister. He was arrogant and extravagant and did not abide by the law. During Emperor Wu's Zhenghe period, he embezzled 19 million of the Northern Army's money without authorization. After the incident was discovered, he was arrested and imprisoned.
At this time, the emperor issued an edict to search for Zhu Anshi from Yangling County, but he had not yet been captured. The emperor was eager to arrest him and bring him to justice. Gongsun He himself requested to hunt down Zhu Anshi to atone for Gongsun Jingsheng's crime.
The emperor agreed to Gongsun He's request.
Later, Gongsun He indeed captured Zhu Anshi.
Zhu Anshi was a great knight in the capital. Hearing that Gongsun He wanted to use him to atone for his son's sins, he smiled and said: The prime minister's disaster has implicated his clan.
I am about to report the Prime Minister's illegal activities. There are many words in the lawsuit, and I can't finish all the bamboos cut down in Nanshan. I can't use the wood of the inclined valley as shackles to restrain me and prevent me from reporting.
Zhu Anshi then wrote a letter from prison, reporting Gongsun Jingsheng's affair with Princess Yangshi, and instructing wizards to curse the emperor during sacrifices. He also went to Ganquan Palace to bury puppets on Chidao and cursed in very vicious words.
Emperor Wu ordered the relevant authorities to interrogate and examine Gongsun He, and thoroughly investigate the crimes he committed. As a result, the father and son died in prison, and the entire family was wiped out.
The witchcraft disaster started with Zhu Anshi and was completed by Jiang Chong. It eventually involved the princess, queen and prince, who all died due to the failure.
The words are in "The Biography of Jiang Chong" and "The Biography of Liyuan".
Liu Quyou was the son of Liu Sheng, the half-brother of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Prince Jing of Zhongshan. It is not clear how he started to be promoted.
In the spring of the second year of Zhenghe, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty sent a letter to the censor in Shao and said: The former prime minister, Gongsun Heyi, relied on his old relationship with me to do evil things by taking advantage of his high position and power to increase fertile farmland for the benefit of his children and retainers, regardless of the suffering of the people. The soldiers guarding the border were short of food and could not think of ways to increase it. He was greedy for money, causing the people to bribe high-ranking officials. I have tolerated these things he did for a long time.
However, he did not repent on his own. Instead, he arbitrarily extended favors to the border counties in order to seek support for himself. He ordered the counties and counties in the interior to reduce costs to build vehicles for the troops garrisoning in the border counties. He also asked the farmers to transport grain to the border counties themselves, which resulted in poverty for the farmers, fatigue of livestock, loss of horses, and weakening of military equipment. The officials below increased taxes at will, causing the people to go bankrupt and exile. He also faked an edict and arrested Zhu Anshi on charges of treachery.
