The case of Gongsun He and his son has been correctly handled by the judge.
He appointed Liu Qushou, the governor of Zhuo County, as the left prime minister, divided the prime minister's long history into two mansions, and waited for a wise man to be appointed as the right prime minister.
Keep close relatives and appoint talented people. This is the common method of Tang Yao and Western Zhou Dynasty.
The 2,200 households in Pengdi were granted the title of Penghou to Zuo Prime Minister Liu Quyou.
In the autumn of the second year of Zhenghe, Jiang Chong made false accusations that Prince Ru was involved in the witchcraft case. Prince Ru killed Jiang Chong and led his troops to attack the Prime Minister's Mansion. Liu Quyou escaped and lost the official seal of Prime Minister Zuo.
At the time of the dispatch, Emperor Wu was vacationing in Ganquan Palace. Prime Minister Chang Shi took a horse from the post house and went straight to Ganquan Palace to report the matter to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu asked: "What are you doing, Prime Minister?"
Prime Minister Chang Shi replied: The Prime Minister is blocking the news and does not dare to send troops.
Emperor Wu said angrily: "When things have reached this level, how can we block the news?"
The prime minister does not have the demeanor of Zhou Gong.
Didn’t Duke Zhou kill Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai?
So he gave an edict to Prime Minister Liu Quyang saying: If you hunt and kill the rebels, I will naturally reward you.
Surround the rebels from a distance and use the bullock cart as a shield. Do not engage the rebels in close combat, thereby killing more soldiers.
Close the city gates and don't let the rebels escape.
Since the prince had killed Jiang Chong and led his troops to rebel, he announced that Emperor Wu was seriously ill in Ganquan Palace. The prince sent troops because he suspected that something had happened in the capital and that treacherous officials wanted to cause chaos.
At this time, Emperor Wu returned to Chang'an from Ganquan Palace and visited the Jianzhang Palace in the west of Chang'an City. He issued an edict to recruit the troops of Jing Zhaoyin, Zuo Fengyi, and You Fufeng from various counties in Chang'an. The deployment was led by officials with a weight of less than 2,000 dan, and the left prime minister Liu Quyou also served as general.
The prince also sent envoys to falsely pass on the edict to pardon the prisoners in the capital's government offices in Chang'an City, and mobilize the troops guarding the arsenal. He ordered Shao Fu Shide and retainer Zhang Guang to lead them respectively. He also sent prisoners in Chang'an City such as Hou Chijie to recruit Changshui Xiaowei and Hu Qi from Xuanqu Palace, all carrying weapons and equipment to assemble in Chang'an City.
The minister, Mang Tong, was ordered to go to Chang'an City as an envoy, so he pursued Ruhou and told Hu Qi: There is fraud in the way of mobilizing troops, so don't listen to Ruhou.
So he killed Ruhou and led the Hu cavalry into Chang'an. He also recruited sailing soldiers and handed them over to the leadership of Dahonglu Shang Qiucheng.
In the beginning, the talismans for mobilizing troops in the Han Dynasty were all red. Because the prince held a red talisman, later the emperor's talismans for mobilizing troops were decorated with yellow yak tails to distinguish them.
The prince summoned Ren An, the envoy to supervise the Northern Army, to mobilize the Northern Army troops. After Ren An accepted the talisman for troop deployment, he closed the gates of the Northern Army and refused to respond to the prince.
The prince had no choice but to lead his troops to leave the Northern Army, and drove tens of thousands of people from the four cities of Chang'an. When they came to the west gate of Changle Palace, they encountered the army of Left Prime Minister Liu Quyou. After five days of melee, tens of thousands of people died, and blood flowed into the sewers on both sides of the street.
The number of troops who joined Liu Quyou, the prime minister of the left, gradually increased. The prince's army failed and fled south to Fu'eng City Gate and out of the city.
On the night of the creation of the sky, the army led by Prime Minister Sizhi Tianren closed the gate to guard the city. Tian Ren was convicted for letting the prince escape from the city, and the left prime minister Liu Quyou wanted to kill Tian Ren.
The imperial censor Yu Shengzhi said to Liu Quyou: "Sizhi is an official of two thousand stone. You should first ask the emperor for instructions on how to deal with it. How can you kill him without permission?"
Liu Quyou released Tian Ren.
Emperor Wu was very angry after hearing the report, and sent officials to question the censor doctor about his sudden victory: Si Zhitianren let the rebels go, and the prime minister killed him in accordance with the law. Why do you stop the prime minister without authorization?
He was so frightened by the sudden victory that he committed suicide.
As for Ren An, the envoy of the Northern Army, he accepted the prince's order to mobilize troops, but was convicted of having second thoughts. Tian Ren let the prince go, and both of them were sentenced to be cut in half.
Emperor Wu said: The minister Mang Tong captured the rebel general Ruhou, and the Chang'an man Jing Jian followed Mang Tong to capture the young master Shi De. It can be said that he made a great contribution.
Dahong Lu and Shang Qiucheng fought hard to capture the traitor Zhang Guang.
Mangtong was granted the title of Chonghehou, Jingjian was granted the title of Dehou, and Shangqiu was granted the title of Jiehou.
The prince's retainers, all who had ever entered or exited the palace, were beheaded.
Those who followed the prince and launched an army to rebel would have their entire families exterminated in accordance with the laws that punished rebels.
Officials and soldiers who took advantage of the chaos to rob were all exiled to Dunhuang County.
Since the prince was on the run, troops were stationed at the gates of Chang'an City from this time on.
More than twenty days later, the prince was captured in Hu County.
The words are in "The Story of the Prince".
The next year, General Li Guang of the Second Division led his troops to attack the Huns. Prime Minister Liu Quyou hosted a farewell banquet for Li Guangli and sent it to Weiqiao. Liu Quyou and Li Guangli said goodbye.
Li Guangli said: I hope that the king will ask the emperor to make the king of Changyi the crown prince soon.
If King Changyi is established as emperor, what will you worry about in the future?
Liu Quyou agreed to Li Guangli's request.
King Changyi was the son of Li Guangli's sister, Mrs. Li.
Li Guangli's daughter was the wife of Liu Quya's son, so both Li Guangli and Liu Quya wanted to make the king of Changyi the crown prince.
At this time, the investigation of the witchcraft prison was very tight. The insider ordered Guo Chen to report the wife of Prime Minister Liu Qumo because Liu Qumo was reprimanded by the emperor many times, instructing the wizard to curse the emperor when offering sacrifices to the earth god. There were vicious words, and Liu Qumo and Li Guangli prayed and sacrificed together, hoping to make King Changyi the emperor.
The officials in charge reported the matter to Emperor Wu and requested an interrogation and examination. Emperor Wu approved it, and the investigators convicted Liu Quya of treason.
Emperor Wu ordered Liu Quya to be put on a cart carrying food and paraded through the streets, and then beheaded in half in Shushi, Chang'an. Liu Quli's wife was taken to Huayang Street and beheaded in public.
Li Guangli's wife and children were also imprisoned.
When Li Guangli heard the news, he surrendered to the Huns and all his clan were executed.
Che Qianqiu's original surname was Tian, ​​and his ancestors were the Tian family from Qi State in the Spring and Autumn Period. Later, a branch of the Tian family moved to Changling County.
Che Qianqiu served as the official guarding the tomb of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
When Prince Wei was slandered by Jiang Chong and was defeated, after a long encounter, Che Qianqiu submitted a memorial of serious emergency, defending the crown prince, saying: The son who played tricks on his father's army should be whipped; the emperor's son accidentally killed someone due to negligence, what crime should he be sentenced to?
I once saw an old man with white hair in a dream who told me how to convict someone.
At this time, Emperor Wu already knew clearly that the prince sent troops out of fear and had no intention of rebellion. After reading Che Qianqiu's letter, he was deeply touched and came to his senses, so he summoned Che Qianqiu.
Che Qianqiu came forward to pay homage to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu saw that Che Qianqiu was more than eight feet tall and handsome and liked him very much. He said to him: It is difficult for others to talk about matters between father and son. Only you understand that this is not the case.
This is the god of Gaomiao asking you to enlighten me, so you should be my assistant.
Immediately ordered the car to be sealed for Qianqiu as Da Honglu.
A few months later, he succeeded Liu Quyou as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fumin.
Che Qianqiu had no other talents or knowledge in Confucian arts, nor any achievements or qualifications. He only made Emperor Wu realize with one sentence that the prince's death was unjust, and he was made prime minister and made a prince within ten months. This was unprecedented in the world.
Later, when an envoy from the Han Dynasty went to the Xiongnu, the Xiongnu Chanyu asked him: I heard that the Han Dynasty appointed a new prime minister. Why did he get the position of prime minister?
The messenger replied: Because of the things mentioned in the letter.
Shan Yu said: If this is the case, the Han Dynasty will set up a prime minister, and it will not require talented people, just any man can get it by submitting a letter.
After the envoy returned, he reported to Emperor Wu what Shan Yu had said.
Emperor Wu thought that the envoy was a disgrace to his mission and wanted to hand him over to the officials.
After a long time, he was released.
However, Che Qianqiu was kind-hearted and resourceful, and he was very competent in the position of prime minister, surpassing those before and after him.
Che Qianqiu had just started to take charge of the work of the prime minister. He saw that Emperor Wu was pursuing the case of the prince's unjust death for many years, and many people were killed and punished.
So together with the censor and Zhong Erqianshi, he congratulated Emperor Wu on his birthday, praised the emperor's virtues, and urged the emperor to extend favors, reduce sentences and punishments, enjoy music, nourish the spirit, and seek entertainment for the sake of the people of the world.
Emperor Wu replied: "I don't show kindness. It started when Prime Minister Liu Quyou of the Left and General Li Guangli of the Second Division secretly conspired to rebel. The disaster of witchcraft and poison spread to the scholar-bureaucrats. I have only eaten one meal a day for several months. What kind of music do I still listen to?"
The scholar-bureaucrats who often grieve over the death of the prince in battle cannot pursue the matter anymore in the past.
Even so, when the witchcraft disaster first occurred, the Prime Minister and Jiao Shi were ordered to supervise the county guards to search for and arrest the people, and the Ting Wei tried to interrogate them, but they did not hear anything from Jiu Qing and Ting Wei.
In the past, Jiang Chong interrogated people from Ganquan Palace and then transferred to Jiaofang Palace where the Empress of Weiyang Palace lived. Later, Gongsun Jingsheng and Li Yu conspired to seduce the Xiongnu. The relevant officials found no evidence of crime. Now the prime minister personally excavated Lantai to check for witchcraft, and he clearly knew that witchcraft existed.
Until now, there are still wizards who practice witchcraft and evil spirits, and evil thieves invade the body. There are wizards from far and near who secretly cast witchcraft. I feel very ashamed. What else is worth wishing for my birthday? Thank you for your kindness. I will not serve you the birthday wine! Please tell the Prime Minister and the two thousand stone officials to return to their official residences. "Shang Shu. Zhou Shu. "Hong Fan" said: Don't be paranoid, don't be protective, the way of the Holy King is open and unobstructed, don't go to court again because of this matter. More than a year later, Emperor Wu became seriously ill and appointed the prince born to Mrs. Gou Yi as the crown prince. He ordered General Huo Guang, Chariot and Cavalry General Jin Yuetan, Imperial Censor Sang Hongyang and Prime Minister Che Qianqiu to accept the imperial edict and assist in educating the young master Liu Fuling.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Zhao just came to the throne, he could not handle political affairs. All government affairs were decided by the general Huo Guang.
Che Qianqiu is the prime minister, loyal, honest and virtuous.
Whenever ministers and ministers met, Huo Guang would say to Che Qianqiu: "Back then, I accepted the Emperor's mission with you. Now that Huo Guang is in charge of internal affairs and you are in charge of foreign affairs, what should I have to enlighten and urge me so that I don't let down the trust of the people of the world?"
Che Qianqiu said: General, please pay more attention, it will be the greatest honor in the world.
He always refused to express any objection to Huo Guang's dictatorship.
Huo Guang therefore valued Che Qianqiu very much.
Every time an auspicious occasion appears, he will praise and reward the prime minister with a thousand-year-old car.
Until the death of Emperor Zhao, the country had few affairs and the people gradually became rich and fulfilled.
In the sixth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Zhao Shao ordered the county to recommend virtuous and literary people, and asked them about the sufferings of the people, which led to the discussion of salt and iron.
Che Qianqiu served as prime minister for twelve years. After his death, Mi was named Dinghou.
At first, when Che Qianqiu was old, the emperor treated him favorably and showed up to the court. He was allowed to enter the palace in a small car, so he was known as the "Prime Minister of Cars".
Che Qianqiu's son Tian Shun succeeded him as a marquis and became the prefect of Yunzhong County. At that time, Emperor Xuan was serving as General Huya to attack the Xiongnu. He was convicted of committing suicide for illegally increasing the number of prisoners and taking credit, and the feudal state was cancelled.
Sang Hongyang worked as a censor for eight years. He thought it would benefit the country and boasted about his achievements. He wanted to get official positions for the children of the Sang family. He resented Huo Guang and rebelled against Shangguan Jie and others, and was finally executed.
Wang Xin is from Jinan County.
As a junior official in the county, he accumulated merit and was gradually promoted to the magistrate of Baiyang County.
In the last years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the army often went on expeditions, and thieves gathered in the counties and counties. The embroidered censor's sudden victory directed the envoys to hunt down the thieves with axes, and dealt with the property collected by the local officials according to the amount of property collected and handed over to the court for military use. Officials with less than 2,000 dan who disobeyed orders were executed.
Baoshengzhi inspected Beiyang and wanted to kill Wang Xin. Wang Xin had undressed and was lying on the chopping board under the guillotine. Gongxin raised his head and said to Baoshengzhi: You have the power of life and death and are powerful in the county. Killing another Wang Xin now will not increase your prestige. It is better to be lenient according to the situation to show your kindness and mercy. Let me try my best to repay you.
Bao Shengzhi admired what he said and forgave him without killing him. Therefore, Bao Shengzhi and Wang Xin became close friends.
After Shengzhi completed his mission and returned to Beijing, he recommended Wang Xin to the emperor. Emperor Wu recruited him to serve as the captain of Youfu, acting as Youfu Feng.
Emperor Wu visited Saitong and Jiidi many times. When he passed through Diehuang, Tanqiu sent people to clean the palace, make the roads smooth, and set up curtains and curtains for comfort.
Emperor Wu was very happy, commended Wang Xin, stopped the car, and changed Wang Xin's official position to a regular one, and he ruled for more than ten years.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, Wang Xin served as the imperial censor, succeeded Che Qianqiu as prime minister, and was named Marquis of Yichun.
He died the next year and was named Jinghou.
Wang Xin's son Wang Tan inherited his father's title, and as a prince participated in the plan to abolish the king of Changyi, support Emperor Xuan, and increase the number of 300 households in the land.
After Wang Tan died, his son Wang Xian inherited his title.
Yucha's wife was Wang Sheng's daughter. After Wang Chai usurped the throne, Wang Sheng's family respected her because she was a relative.
Starting from Wang Xin, the feudal state was passed down to Great-grandson, and was discontinued after Wang Mang's defeat.
Yang Chang is from Huayin County.
When he served in the general Tingguang shogunate, he was appointed military commander. Huo Guang liked and treated him favorably, and he was gradually promoted to chief agricultural officer.
During the Wuhuang period of Guitong, the rice field envoy You Dong learned of the rebellion conspiracy of Emperor Jie and others and informed Yang Chang of the matter.
Yang Chang was always cautious and fearful, and did not dare to report to Emperor Zhao, so he wrote a letter claiming to be ill and emigrated.
Yan Cang told the news to Du Yannian, the admonishing doctor, and Du Yannian reported it to Emperor Zhao.
Yan Cang and Du Yannian were both granted the title of marquis for their meritorious service. As the ninth minister, Yang Chang heard the news of the rebellion but failed to report it in time, so he was not granted the title of marquis.
Later, he was promoted to imperial censor, succeeded Wang Xin as prime minister, and was granted the title of Marquis of Anping.
In the second year, Emperor Zhao died.
The king of Changyi came to Beijing to take the throne after being summoned by the ministers. He was promiscuous and immoral. The general Huo Guang conspired with the chariot general Zhang Anshi to depose the king of Luyi and reestablish the emperor.
It was agreed upon that Da Si’s farmland would be extended to inform Yang Chang.
Yang Chang was very frightened after hearing this. He didn't know what to say. His back was wet with sweat and he could only make a "weiwei" sound.
Tian Yannian got up and went to the dressing room to change clothes. Yang Chang's wife hurriedly came out of the side room and said to Yang Chang: This is a national event. Now the general's plan has been decided. I asked Dasi Nanyang Yannian to tell you.
If you don't agree quickly and work together with the general, if you hesitate, you will be killed first.
When Tian Yannian came back from the dressing room, both Yang Chang and his wife and Tian Yannian agreed with the general's decision and asked to obey the general's order. So the court ministers deposed King Changyi and established Emperor Xuan.
More than a month after Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Yang Chang died, and Mi was named Jinghou.
His son Yang Zhong inherited the title. Because Yang Chang was the prime minister, he participated in the formulation of the strategy of deposing the king of Changyi and replacing him with Emperor Xuan. He made great contributions to the stabilization of the Moshi ancestral temple and the increase of 3,500 households in the city.
Yang Zhong's younger brother Yang Yun, named Ziyou, relied on Yang Zhong's official position and was appointed Lang Guan according to the Han Dynasty's son appointment system, filling the post of Chang Shiqi. Yang Yun's mother was Sima Qian's daughter.
Yang Yun first read "Tai Shi Gong Ji" written by his grandfather, and was also familiar with "Spring and Autumn".
Because of his talent, he is praised by people.
He liked to make friends with handsome and outstanding Confucian scholars. He became famous in the court and was promoted to Zuocao.
Yang Yun first heard about the Huo family's rebellion and reported it to the emperor through his servant Jin An. The emperor summoned Yang Yun and asked him to report the Huo family's rebellion.
The Huo family pleaded guilty and were executed. Yang Yun and five other people were awarded titles for their merits in the prosecution. Yang Yun was made Hutonghou and promoted to Zhonglang General.
The old practice of Lang Guan was to ask Lang Gong to pay the property expenses and provide documents himself before he got the opportunity to serve as an additional official, so he was also called "Shan Lang".
If a lieutenant takes sick leave for a full day, he must use a vacation day to make up for it. Some lieutenants cannot get a vacation for more than a year.
Nazhe: Lang officials who came from rich families went out to have fun and play all day long. Some used money to pay bribes to get jobs in good departments.
Bribery is popular and everyone is imitating it.
Yang Yun served as Zhonglang General, exempted from the old practice of "Shanlang", and handed over the annual expenditure plan of Langguan's office to Da Sinong, who provided financial expenses.
Lang Guan's sick leave, family leave, and family leave are all handled in accordance with the law.
If any of the ministers or visitors committed a crime, they would be removed from office. Those who had excellent work in the palace and had both ability and political integrity would be recommended to be promoted to officials.
The ministers were enlightened by this, and they all motivated themselves to perform their duties diligently. They got rid of the shortcomings of asking for favors and giving gifts, and enforced orders and prohibitions. The ministers in the palace worked together as one.
Therefore, the emperor promoted Yang Yun to the position of Guang Luxun among the officials and became a trusted minister to handle political affairs.
At first, Yang Yun accepted five million in money from his father. When he was granted the title of Pingtong Hou, he gave all the money his father gave him to people of the same clan.
His stepmother had no sons and had millions of money, which she left to Yang Yun after her death, and Yang Yun gave it all to his stepmother's brothers.
Yang Yun inherited a total of more than 10 million in money twice, and he took it all out and distributed it to others.
This is how he takes money lightly and loves justice.
As an official in the palace, Yang Yun was honest and selfless, and all the officials praised him for his fairness.
However, Yang Yun often boasted about his virtue and ability to do things. He was also mean by nature and liked to expose other people's secrets. If any of his colleagues disobeyed him, he would definitely try to harm him. He relied on his ability to be arrogant and domineering. Therefore, he offended many people in the court, fell out with Dai Changle, the imperial servant, and finally ruined himself because of this incident.
Dai Changle was Emperor Xuan's close friend among the people. When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he promoted him to a trusted minister.
Dai Changle once performed the emperor's affairs on his behalf when practicing the rituals of the ancestral temple. When he came back, he said to the emperor: I met the emperor and accepted Shao's order to practice the etiquette on the emperor's behalf. The prince of Wei drove me.
Someone reported in a divination that Dai Changle had spoken inappropriately, and the emperor handed the matter over to Tingwei for trial.
Dai Changle suspected that Yang Yun instigated others to report him, so he also wrote a letter to accuse Yang Yun of his crime, saying:
Dong Zhong, the Marquis of Gaochang, drove into Beiye Gate. Yang Yun said to Zhang Yanshou, the Marquis of Fuping: I heard that a Mercedes-Benz car crashed into the palace gate before, breaking the latch and killing the horse. Then Emperor Zhao died.
Now something like this happened again. It was destiny, not man-made. Zuo Fengyi and Han Yanshou were convicted and imprisoned, and Yang Yun wrote a letter to defend him.
The doctor Qiu Chang said to Yang Yun: I heard that you defended Han Fengyi. Can you save him?
Yang Yun said: How can things be so easy!
An upright person may not be able to protect himself.
I can't save it in vain, just like people say that a mouse cannot enter the hole because it has a sinus number in its mouth that is larger than the mouth of the mouse hole. Once again, Zhongshu Ye ordered Xuan to translate the words of the Xiongnu Chanyu envoy into words and show them to the generals and the two thousand stone officials of China and Korea.
Yang Yun said: "Modun Chanyu received the delicious food as a reward from the Han Dynasty, but he said it was rotten and smelly. Isn't it obvious that the Chanyu did not come to see him?"
Yang Yun looked at the figures painted on Xihe, pointed to the portraits of Xia Jie and Shang Zhou and said to Wang Wu, the Marquis of Lechang: When the emperor passes by this place, he can learn from it by asking about the mistakes Jie and Zhou committed. The characters in the book include Yao, Shun, Yu and Tang. Yang Yun does not praise them, but lists Jie and Zhou.
When Yang Yun heard that the Xiongnu surrenderers said that Shanyu had been killed, he said: There is such an unwise monarch. The good plans planned by the ministers are not used, but he himself is destroyed.
Just as the Qin Dynasty only appointed treacherous and sycophantic ministers as its ministers, and killed the loyal and good, and eventually perished because of it; if it had been able to appoint wise and upright ministers, the Qin Dynasty could have continued to this day.
The bad guys in ancient times and today are like the same breed. Yang Yun arbitrarily quoted the example of the country's subjugation to slander the current court, without the etiquette of a minister.
Yang Yun also said to me, Dai Changle: Since the first month, the weather has been cloudy and rainless for a long time. This celestial phenomenon is recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Xia Housheng said this when he advised the king of Changyi.
The emperor must not go to the Houtu Temple in Hedong to offer sacrifices. Yang Yun made fun of the emperor, which was especially rebellious and violated ethics.
Yang Yun's case was handed over to Ting Wei for trial.
Tingwei conducted an interrogation in Dingguo and found out Jinqing with the evidence of witnesses.
Yu Dingguo reported to the emperor: Yang Yun did not plead guilty, but secretly summoned the general, hoping that he would warn Fuping Marquis Zhang Yanshou, saying that Dai Changle, the imperial servant, had several things that could lead to death, and he would be executed sooner or later.
Yang Yun is fortunate enough to be married to Marquis Fuping. Now only the three of you have talked about Yang Yun's case together. As long as Marquis Fuping says that he did not hear Yang Yun say anything at that time, it will naturally conflict with what the servant revealed. General Hu said, "No."
Yang Yun was furious, holding a big sword in his hand, and said: If the servant gets help from Fupinghou, and according to the testimony revealed by the servant, I will be sentenced to genocide!
You are not allowed to reveal what I said. If the servant knows these words, it will increase my other crimes.
Yang Yun was lucky enough to be ranked as the ninth minister, and he served as a minister of Guangluxun. He was a close guard of the imperial court. He was trusted by the emperor and participated in political affairs. Instead of being loyal to the emperor and caring for the people, and fulfilling his duties as a minister, he arrogantly vented his resentment, spread evil words, and was treasonous. He requested to be arrested and punished.
Emperor Xuan could not bear to sentence him to death. Xia Shao exempted Yang Yun and Dai Changle from being civilians.
After Yang Yun lost his title, he ran businesses at home, built houses, and relied on money to make himself happy.
More than a year later, his friend Sun Huizong from Xihe, the prefect of Anding County, was a man of intelligence and strategy. He wrote to Yang Yun to advise him, telling him that after ministers were dismissed from office and retired, they should shut themselves up and think about their mistakes, be frightened, behave in a pitiable manner, and should not run businesses, make friends with guests, and have a reputation that is praised by others.
Yang Yun was the son of Prime Minister Yang Chang. He was famous in the court when he was young. Once he was deposed because of some unidentified remarks, he felt dissatisfied and wrote a reply to Sun Huizong:
I have low talents, despicable behavior, and no foundation in academic accomplishment. Fortunately, I relied on the merits left by my father and was able to serve as a guard in the court. When I encountered the Huo family's rebellion, I was awarded a title for my merits in reporting on it, but I was not qualified after all, and finally suffered disaster.
I feel sorry for my ignorance, and I am grateful for this letter, which teaches and explains the truth that I have not realized. My sincere affection is profound.
But I privately complained that I did not think deeply about the whole story and easily believed the slanders of worldly people.
Let me tell you my humble and stupid thoughts, as if I have violated the will of my subordinates, and I am trying to justify my mistakes; I should remain silent, and I am afraid of betraying the meaning of Confucius' "Each person expresses his ambition," so I dare to briefly state my humble opinion. Please consider it.
When my family was prosperous, there were ten people riding the chariot, among the nine ministers, with the title of marquis, commanding the attendants, and participating in court affairs. However, I was unable to make any achievements at this time, to promote the emperor's virtues and education, and I could not work together with the officials to assist the court in filling vacancies. I have been accused of stealing official positions for a long time.
I was greedy for salary and power, and could not retire on my own initiative. I encountered changes and was slandered by others. I was imprisoned in the Guanlou to the north of the palace. My wife and children were also imprisoned in prison.
At this time, I felt that extermination of the clan would not be able to compensate for the crime. How could I have thought that I could save my life and worship the tombs of my ancestors?
I feel that the grace of Emperor Shengming is truly immeasurable.
A gentleman pursues morality and justice and is happy but forgets his worries; a villain preserves his life and is happy but forgets his sins.
I thought privately that my sins were already great and my character was lacking, so I should spend the rest of my life as a farmer.
So he led his wife and children, worked hard to cultivate crops and mulberry trees, irrigate gardens, run industries, and pay taxes to the court. Unexpectedly, he was ridiculed and criticized for this.
Things that cannot be avoided by human relationships are not forbidden even by saints. Therefore, even if it is the most noble monarch or the closest father, the funeral for them has to come to an end.
It has been three years since I was convicted.
When farmers work hard, they cook mutton and lamb every year during the solstice and twelfth lunar month, and pour wine to masturbate.
My hometown was originally in Qin, and I can sing songs from Qin.
My wife is a woman who walks on the ground and is good at playing the harp.
There are also some slaves who can sing. After drinking, their ears will become hot, they will look up to the sky, beat the fou with their hands, and sing a black song.
The lyrics of the song go: The fields in the southern mountains are filthy and untamed. If you plant a hectare of beans, they will fall into bean sprouts.
To enjoy life, you need to be wealthy!
On days like this, I was so happy that I shook my clothes, waved my sleeves, sometimes lowered, sometimes raised, stamping my feet and dancing. It was so indulgent that I didn't know why it couldn't work.
Fortunately, I still had some money left over from my salary, so I bought low and sold high, in pursuit of a tenth of the profit. This is what businessmen do, and it is also a shameful thing, and I have done it myself.
People with low status are the targets of slander. I shudder when I think about this.
Even people who know me very well slander me, so how can anyone praise me?
Didn't Dong Zhongshu say that those who work diligently and diligently to pursue benevolence and righteousness often worry about not being able to educate the people is a matter for the officials; those who diligently and diligently pursue wealth and gain often worry about living in poverty are a matter for the common people.
Therefore Confucius said: If the ways are different, they should not conspire against each other.
How can you still use Doctor Qing's code of conduct to blame me now?
Xihe was the land of the Wei State during the Warring States Period. It was the place where Wei Wenhou rose. Duan Ganmu and Tian Zifang had the style of sending people to stay. Both wise men had noble moral integrity and magnanimity, and knew the right amount of resignation and appointment.
Recently, I left my hometown of Xihe and arrived at Anding County. It is located in the valley and is the old land of Kunrong. The people there are greedy and despicable. Is it because the local customs have changed your character?
It is only today that I see your ambition clearly. It is the heyday of the Han Dynasty. I hope you will work hard to establish your reputation. There is no need to discuss it with me anymore.
Anpinghou Yang Tan, the son of Yang Yun's brother Yang Zhong, was appointed as a vassal. He told Yang Yun: Du Yannian, a native of Jianping, the governor of Xihe County, was dismissed from his official position due to crimes. Now he is recruited as a censor.
If you have committed a minor crime and have made meritorious deeds, you will be re-appointed.
Yang Yun said: What is the use of having merit?
The Emperor is not worthy of my efforts for him.
Yang Yun had always been on good terms with Gai Kuorao and Han Yanshou. Yang Tan immediately said: This is indeed the case with your Majesty. Gai Sili and Han Fengyi were both officials who worked hard for the imperial court, but they were all killed for trivial matters.
At this time, there was a solar eclipse, and a low-level official named Cheng, who was in charge of carriages and horses, wrote a letter to accuse Yang Yun of being arrogant and unrepentant, and he was the cause of the solar eclipse disaster.
Emperor Xuan handed this memorial to Tingwei for interrogation and examination. During the interrogation, a letter written by Yang Yun to Sun Huizong was found. Emperor Xuan hated Yang Pan after reading it.
Tingwei convicted Yang Yun of treason and immorality and sentenced him to beheaded in half.
His wife and children were exiled to Jiuquan County.
Yang Tan did not persuade Yang Yun to repent, but instead interacted with him, made resentful remarks, removed him from his official position, and demoted him to a civilian.
Emperor Xuan summoned and appointed Cheng Langguan. Those who were serving as officials and had a close friendship with Yang Yun, such as Wei Xuancheng, the Weiyang palace guard, Zhang Chang, Jingzhao Yin, and Sun Huizong, were all dismissed from their official positions.
Cai Yi was born in Wen County, Hanoi County.
Because he was proficient in classics, he served in the shogunate.
My family is very poor and I often walk. Being poor and unable to prepare gifts, some good-hearted people among the family pooled their money and bought Cai Yi a bullock cart for him to ride on.
A few years later, Cai Yisheng served as the gatekeeper of the city gate.
After a long time, the emperor issued an edict to look for people who could master "Han Shi" and recruited Cai Yi to wait for the edict, but he could not see the emperor for a long time.
Cai Yishangshu said: I am a commoner in the fields of Shandong. My virtue, intelligence and appearance are not comparable to others, but I have not abandoned human relations. This is because I privately learned morality from my ancestors and devoted myself to Confucian classics.
I hope that Your Majesty will grant me a quiet and peaceful place so that I can devote all my careful thinking on the meaning of the scriptures.
The emperor summoned Cai Yi and asked him to lecture on the Book of Songs. The emperor was very satisfied with what he heard and promoted him to the position of Guanglu doctor. He was given to Shizhong and taught in the palace by Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty.
A few years later, he was appointed Shaofu and promoted to Yushi Dafu. He replaced Yang Chang as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Yang Ping.
And because of the decision to increase the reward for Anzong Temple, he was given an additional 200 jins of gold.
Cai Yi was already over eighty years old when he became prime minister. He was short in stature, had no beard, and lost his eyebrows. His face looked like that of an old woman. He walked with a stooped back and often had to be supported by two subordinates to walk.
At that time, the general Huo Guang was in power. Some people who discussed the matter said that Huo Guang appointed prime ministers instead of selecting talented people and appointed people who could be arbitrarily controlled by him.
After Huo Guang heard this discussion, he said to his ministers, attendants and subordinates: I think the emperor's teacher should be the prime minister. How can I say that we should not choose talented people?
This kind of discussion cannot be heard by the world.
Cai Yi died after serving as prime minister for four years, and Mi was known as the Marquis of Jie.
He had no sons and the feudal state was abolished.
Chen Wannian, courtesy name Yougong, was born in Xiang County, Pei County.
At first he was an official of Pei County. After inspection, he was recommended and promoted to county magistrate. He was also promoted to prefect of Guangling. Because of his excellent political performance, he went to Beijing to serve as You Fufeng, and was further promoted to be a royal servant.
Chen Wannian was honest and fair, and cultivated virtue at home, but he was good at handling affairs and treating others. He donated property to his relatives, the Xu family and the Shi family, spent all his family's money, and especially made friends with and served Shi Gao, the Marquis of Leling.
Prime Minister Bingji fell ill, and officials with more than two thousand dan came to visit him.
Bingji sent Jiacheng out to express his gratitude. After the Jiacheng expressed his gratitude, all the officials left. Only Chen Wannian stayed and did not go back until late at night.
When Bingji became seriously ill, the emperor went to visit him in person and asked Bingji about his views on the virtues and talents of the ministers in the DPRK.
Binggu recommended Yu Dingguo, Du Yannian and Chen Wannian. Chen Wannian finally replaced Yu Dingguo as the imperial censor, and died of illness eight years later.
Chen Wannian's son Chen Xian, named Zikang, was eighteen years old. Due to Chen Wannian's merits, he was appointed Lang Guan according to the Renzi system.
He had special talents, was frank and honest, discussed things many times, dared to ridicule the emperor's trusted ministers, wrote dozens of letters, and was promoted to Zuocao.
Once, Chen Wannian fell ill and summoned Chen Xian to his bedside to teach and admonish him. He continued talking until midnight when Chen Xian fell asleep and hit his head on the screen.
Chen Wannian was very angry and wanted to beat Chen Xian with a stick, saying: "Your father taught you, but you fell asleep and didn't listen to me. Why?"
Chen Xian kowtowed and admitted his mistake and said: I fully understand what you said. In the final analysis, you are teaching me to flatter you.
Chen Wannian stopped talking.
After Chen Wannian's death, Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty promoted Chen Xian to the position of censor Zhongcheng. He oversaw the affairs of the prefectures and counties and assessed the performance of the governors. In the palace of law enforcement, all officials below the public minister were in awe of Chen Xian.
At this time, Zhongshu ordered Shi Xian to be in power. Chen Xian often discussed Shi Xian's shortcomings, which made Shi Xian and others hate Chen Xian.
At that time, Zhu Yun, the magistrate of Huaili County, brutally and mistakenly killed an innocent man by decree. The relevant officials wrote a memorial, but the emperor did not issue a memorial.
Chen Xianqiansu and Zhu Yun were close friends. Zhu Yun inquired about the seriousness of the matter from Chen Xian, and Chen Xian taught Zhu Yun to write a letter to defend himself.
At this time, Shi Xian secretly sent someone to find out about this situation, and reported that Chen Xian had leaked the secrets of the palace. He was sent to prison, beaten and interrogated, and his death penalty was reduced. Kun was made the Dan of the City, so he was deposed from his official title.
When Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, the general Wang Feng believed that Chen Xian had a loyal and upright character when he accused Shi Xian in the past, so he asked Emperor Chen Cheng to allow Chen Xian to serve as Chang Shi.
Later, Chen Xian was promoted to the governor of Jizhou and was ordered to act in accordance with the emperor's wishes. He was recruited and appointed as an admonishing doctor.
Later, he served as the domestic history of Chu, the prefect of Beihai County, and the prefect of Shu County.
Because Chen Xian was recommended by Jingzhao Yin Wang Zhang, he was promoted to the throne. Wang Zhang broke the law and was killed. Chen Xian was dismissed from office and was recruited to serve as the prefect of Nanyang County.
Killing is used to establish dignity in the place where he works. If the powerful officials and aristocratic families break the law, they will be escorted to the prefecture on trial. Officials in charge of the service will be arranged according to legal procedures to set up earth mortars and pestles, and let the criminals use the wooden pestles to pound the earth mortars. If the criminals do not meet the requirements, or if they arbitrarily remove the iron pincers around their necks or the iron shackles on their feet, or if the clothes they wear do not comply with the law, they will be punished and beaten.
People were assigned to strictly supervise the work, and the labor was so intense that the criminals could not bear the pain. Some of them hanged themselves. Hundreds of criminals died in a year. Over time, the bodies became maggots and rotted, and the criminals' families were unable to bury them.
He imitated Yan Yannian in governing political affairs, but was not as honest as Yan Yannian.
The food produced in the county is distributed to the place where he works to support himself. He lives a luxurious life and has delicious food as good as jade.
However, he controlled the history and ordered the county officials to restrain themselves behind closed doors and could not break the law.
He also publicly warned them in writing: "If everyone wants to pursue their own happiness, how can this happen when there are a hundred prefects in one county!"
All the officials under his command were afraid of him, and they were tyrannical and intimidating, imposing orders and prohibitions, but he was deposed because of this.
Chen Xian was the son of Sangong, and he was very famous in the court when he was young. Xue Xuan, Zhu Bo, Zhai Fangjin, Kong Guang, etc. became officials far behind Chen Xian. However, they all became high officials with integrity and frugality, while Chen Xian was stagnant in the position of county guard.
At that time, Wang Yin, the chariot and cavalry general, assisted the government and trusted Chen Tang.
Chen Xian bribed Chen Tang with gifts many times, and wrote to him: If I can get help from my son-in-law and be able to enter the capital and become an official, I will not regret it even if I die.
Later, he was finally recruited to Beijing and became the Shaofu.
The Shaofu was in charge of a lot of real objects. Chen Xian checked all the officials and found the treasures they had secretly hidden, so he took it for granted without the receipt.
Reports were filed against subordinate officials and officials at Huangmen, Goudun, and Yeting in the central palaces, who were examined and convicted. These officials were afraid of Chen Xian and lost their courage.
Chen Xian served as the Shaofu for three years and was at odds with Zhai Fangjin.
Zhai Fangjin was the prime minister, and he reported to the emperor: Chen Xian used to be a county governor, and he was cruel in every aspect, inflicting politics like a poisonous sting on the officials and the people.
Guarding and stealing. And he openly flattered the evil minister Chen Tanglai to seek recommendation.
It is shameless and shameless to seek official positions and is not suitable for holding official positions anymore.
Chen Xian was convicted and dismissed from office.
Soon, Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, recommended Chen Xian to be upright and upright. After being appointed as Guanglu doctor, Zhai Fangjin petitioned the emperor to remove Chen Xian from his official post.
A few years later, Wang Li returned to his feudal country after being convicted of a crime. Zhai Fangjin asked the emperor to send Chen Xian back to his hometown. Chen Xian died of depression.
Zheng Hong, courtesy name Zhiqing, was born in Gang County, Taishan County.
His elder brother Zheng Chang, named Ciqing, also loved learning. He was proficient in Confucian classics and was proficient in law and political affairs.
The second minister served as the prefect of Taiyuan County and Zhuo County, and Zheng Hong was the prefect of Nanyang County. Both of them had outstanding political achievements. The articles, decrees, laws and systems of their administration were described by later generations.
The second minister's punishments were harsh and not as gentle as those of Zheng Hong. Zheng Hong was transferred to Huaiyang as the Prime Minister. Because of his outstanding political achievements, he came to Beijing to serve as You Fufeng. People in the capital praised him.
His descendant Wei Xuan became the imperial censor.
Six years later, he was convicted and expelled from office for discussing the government affairs with Jingfang. The matter is recorded in "Jingfang Biography".
Zanri: The discussion of the so-called salt and iron policy began in the first year of the Yuan Dynasty. Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty ordered the recruitment of literary and virtuous people, and asked about strategies for governing the world and rectifying chaos. They all replied that they hoped to abolish the salt and iron, wine and grain, and lose-all policies of the county, to focus on agriculture, suppress the end of industry and commerce, and not to compete with the people of the world for profits, and then enlightenment can flourish.
Sang Hongyang, the imperial censor, believed that the above policies were used to stabilize the border and control surrounding ethnic minorities. They were the fundamental cause of the country and could not be abolished.
At that time, Sang Hongyang and literary virtuous people were arguing with each other, and there were many articles on their debates.
At the time of Emperor Xuan, Duke Huan Kuanci of Runan County studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" and was recommended as a Langguan. He later became the prefect of Lujiang County. He was erudite and proficient in writing essays. He deduced and derived discussions about salt and iron.
Huan Kuan's Literary Saying: Look at Gong Qing's virtuous literary discussions, Different from what I have heard, Zhu Sheng of Runan said that at this time, heroes and talents were advancing side by side, such as the virtuous Tang Sheng from Maoling and the literary Lu people. More than 60 people gathered in the court to talk about the customs of the six arts and state the governance of the country. The origin of the world, the wise praise their thoughts, the benevolent reveal their measures, the brave show their determination, the debaters use their words, argue endlessly, and show a strong look. Although the discussion is not detailed, it can be briefly seen.
Liu Zi, a native of Zhongshan, reasoned about the royal way, corrected the shortcomings of today's society, and brought it back to the right path. He was a gentle and learned gentleman.
Zhu Sheng, a native of Jiujiang County, carried forward Shi Yu's integrity, expressed his anger, ridiculed the ministers, and was upright and unyielding. It can be said that he was not afraid of rape.
Based on the reality of today's society, Dr. Sang is in line with the changes in the current situation, and advocates the strategy of fighting for power and profit. Although it is not a legitimate method, a learned scholar cannot seek explanations by himself. Sang Hongyang's theory cannot be used to explain the truth. He is a learned and understanding man.
However, he handled the power of the ministers and did not imitate the ancients. He indulged his mind and pursued business profits. He was not in his position and acted in the wrong way. As expected, he lost his life because of his rebellion with Shangguan Jie, which also affected his clan.
Prime Minister Che Qianqiu entered the ranks of auxiliary ministers like Yi Yin and Lu Shang, holding important positions and presiding over political affairs. However, when Huo Guang was in power, Che Qianqiu remained silent on political affairs. He was as cautious as a bag tied around the mouth. Although he died whole body, a person like him is not worthy of praise.
As for the people in the prime minister's and imperial censor's offices who cannot adhere to correct opinions to assist the prime minister, and flatter and unprincipledly agree with those who have common interests in order to please their superiors, these people are like what Confucius said is a person with inferior materials and equipment, and they are not worthy of praise.
summary:
Gongsun He, a native of Beidi Commandery, rose from a knight-errant background through military merit. He became favored due to his marriage to Empress Wei's sister and served as a general under Emperor Wu, earning the title of Marquis of Nanao for attacking the Xiongnu. After losing his marquisate for presenting inferior gold, he eventually became Chancellor and was titled Marquis of Ge Yi. He reluctantly accepted the position, weeping and predicting his own danger. His son Gongsun Jingsheng, arrogant and corrupt, embezzled military funds. To atone for his son, Gongsun He captured the knight Zhu Anshi, who retaliated by reporting Gongsun Jingsheng's affair with a princess and accusations of witchcraft against the emperor. Both father and son died in prison, and their clan was exterminated. This incident sparked the witchcraft disaster that ultimately led to the deaths of the princess, empress, and crown prince.

Liu Quli, son of Prince Jing of Zhongshan, replaced Gongsun He as Left Chancellor. Emperor Wu issued an edict condemning Gongsun He's corruption and appointed Liu Quli as Marquis of Peng. During the witchcraft rebellion, Crown Prince Ju killed the accuser Jiang Chong and raised troops. Liu Quli led imperial forces against the prince, resulting in a five-day battle with tens of thousands dead. The prince fled but was captured twenty days later. The following year, Liu Quli conspired with General Li Guangli to make the Prince of Changyi crown prince. This conspiracy was discovered, and Liu Quli was executed by waist-cutting, while Li Guangli surrendered to the Xiongnu.

Che Qianqiu, originally named Tian, served as guardian of Emperor Gaozu's tomb. After the crown prince's defeat, Che submitted a memorial defending the prince, arguing that a son who mobilizes troops against his father should only be whipped. Emperor Wu, already regretting his actions, was moved and appointed Che as Grand Herald, then Chancellor within months, creating the unprecedented precedent of becoming Chancellor through a single memorial. Though lacking scholarly talents, Che proved competent and kind-hearted. After Emperor Wu's death, Che served under Emperor Zhao alongside General Huo Guang, deferring to Huo's authority while maintaining loyalty. He served as Chancellor for twelve years and was posthumously titled Marquis Ding.

Wang Xin of Jinan Commandery rose from minor official to magistrate. When Imperial Censor Bao Shengzhi investigated and prepared to execute him, Wang Xin pleaded for mercy, arguing that killing him would not increase Shengzhi's prestige. Impressed, Shengzhi spared him and later recommended him. Wang Xin served Emperor Wu competently, becoming You Fufeng. Under Emperor Zhao, he succeeded Che Qianqiu as Chancellor and was titled Marquis of Yichun, dying the following year.

Yang Chang of Huayin Commandery served in General Huo Guang's staff, rising to Minister of Agriculture. Learning of a rebellion conspiracy, Yang Chang, being cautious, feigned illness rather than reporting it. Another official reported the matter and received a marquisate, while Yang Chang was denied this honor. He later became Imperial Censor and succeeded Wang Xin as Chancellor, titled Marquis of Anping. After Emperor Zhao's death, when Huo Guang planned to depose the immoral King of Changyi, Yang Chang initially hesitated but was persuaded by his wife to cooperate. He died shortly after Emperor Xuan's accession.

Gongsun Hong was born in Xue County, Sichuan State.
He worked as a jailer when he was young. Removed from office for committing a crime.
Because his family was poor, he made a living by herding pigs on the beach.
When he was in his forties, he began to study "Spring and Autumn" and miscellaneous treatises of various schools.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he recruited virtuous and literary people. At this time, Gongsun Hong was sixty years old and got a doctorate as a virtuous and literary person.
He was sent as an envoy to the Huns and returned to the court to report, which was not in line with the emperor's wishes. Emperor Wu was very angry and thought he was incompetent, so Gongsun Hong wrote a letter claiming to be ill and was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown.
In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty once again selected virtuous literary people, and Dong Weihui once again recommended Gong Zhucong.
Gong Chuicong declined and said: I went west to Beijing in the past and was dismissed because of my incompetence. I hope to choose someone else.
But the people of the country insisted on recommending him, so Gongsun Hong came to Taichang.
The emperor went down to Shao Shu Ce and asked all the Confucian scholars:
The bookmaker wrote: I heard that in ancient times, when politics was perfect, the punishment for criminals was to mark their clothes and hats and let them wear special clothes, but the common people did not break the law. At that time, Yin and Yang were in harmony, the grains were abundant, the livestock were multiplying, the dew fell from the sky, the weather was smooth, the rice with full grains grew, the red auspicious grass appeared, the mountains were covered with dense forests and lush grass, and the lakes did not dry up. Unicorns and phoenixes appear in the lakes on the outskirts of the city. Turtles and dragons swim in the ponds, rivers produce pictures, and Luo produces books. A son will not die before his father, nor will a younger brother die before his elder brother. At that time, as far as Qusou in the north and Jiaodu in the south, as long as it was reachable by cars and boats and people could walk, all living beings had their own place.
I admire that era very much. How can we govern the country now to reach this state?
You have studied the laws of the sages, you are well versed in the principles of the superiority and inferiority of kings and ministers, and you are very insightful in your discussions. You are all very famous today. I dare to ask you: What is the most fundamental way of heaven and man?

Bu Shiba was promoted from herding, Hongyang was promoted from the Jia people, Wei Qing was promoted from the slaves, and Jin Yuechan was promoted from the captives. These are the ancient version of building and selling cattle.
Mozhi has its talents flourished here, Confucianism and elegance include Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, and Ni Kuan, loyalty includes Shi Jian and Shi Qing, simplicity includes Ji An and Bu Shi, recommending sages include Han Anguo and Zheng Shi, enacting laws and regulations include Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang, writing articles include Sima Qian and Sima Xiangru, and humor includes Dongfang Shuo and Meigao, Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen responded to the emperor's questions, Tang Du and Luoxia Hong were listed, Li Yannian coordinated music, Sang Hongyang was responsible for financial planning, Zhang Qian and Su Wu were sent as envoys, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were leaders, Huo Guang and Jin Yueyan were sent to protect the young master, and the rest are indescribable.
Therefore, he made great achievements and established the system, which was not as good as that of later generations.
Xiao Xuan inherited the great unification, continued to build the magnificent imperial cause, taught the six arts, and recruited outstanding talents. Xiao Wangzhi, Liang Qiuhe, Xia Housheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi were promoted through Confucianism. Liu Xiang and Wang Bao became famous with their articles, and their generals and ministers were well-prepared. An Shi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bingji, Yu Dingguo, Du Yannian, and others who governed the people included Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Zhao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhao Guangmo, Yan Yannian, and Zhang Chang, all of whom have made great achievements in the world.
Examining his famous ministers, he was second only to the talents of Emperor Wu's era.
summary:
Gongsun Hong, born in Xue County, Sichuan State, began his career as a jailer but was dismissed for a crime. Left impoverished, he herded pigs until his forties, when he started studying the "Spring and Autumn" and various philosophical texts. At sixty, he was recruited as a virtuous and literary person under Emperor Wu of Han, but his mission to the Huns displeased the emperor, leading to his dismissal. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, he was recommended again and, despite initial reluctance, presented a detailed policy response. His essay emphasized governance through righteousness, trust, and eight principles: appointing by talent, avoiding useless discussions, reducing taxes, not harming agriculture, promoting the virtuous, rewarding merit, punishing crime appropriately, and rewarding virtue. He argued that harmony between heaven and earth arises from unified virtue, and that floods and droughts under Yu and Tang were due to prior misrule. His response was ranked first by the emperor, who appointed him as a doctor.

Gongsun Hong rose quickly, becoming Zuo Neishi within a year, known for cautious debate and Confucian decorum. He avoided court confrontations, often aligning with the emperor’s wishes, which drew accusations of hypocrisy from Ji An. Gongsun Hong defended himself, and the emperor favored him more. He served as imperial censor and later prime minister, receiving the title Marquis of Pingjin. Despite his high rank, he lived frugally, eating simple meals and using cloth quilts, spending his salary on guests and relatives. However, he was inwardly vengeful, contributing to the downfall of rivals like Dong Zhongshu. During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellions, he fell ill and offered to resign, but the emperor refused, granting him leave. He died in office at eighty.

Bu Shi, a farmer and herder from Henan, donated half his wealth to support border campaigns against the Xiongnu, but Gongsun Hong advised against accepting, calling it irregular. Later, during a famine, Bu Shi gave 200,000 yuan to aid refugees, earning imperial recognition. He was appointed as a langzhong to herd sheep in Shanglin Garden, where he excelled. The emperor, impressed, made him a magistrate, then tutor to the King of Qi, and eventually prime minister. During the Lu Jia rebellion, Bu Shi offered to fight, but the emperor honored him instead. As imperial censor, he criticized salt and iron taxes, displeasing the emperor, and was demoted.

Ni Kuan, a scholar of "Shangshu," worked as a farmer while studying. He became a Tingwei official, known for his writing and legal expertise. Promoted by Zhang Tang, he served as Zuo Neishi, where he encouraged farming, reduced punishments, and built irrigation canals. When dismissed for poor tax collection, the people paid their debts, restoring his position. He advised on the Fengshan ceremonies, supporting the emperor’s plans, and helped establish the Taichu calendar. As imperial censor, he became complacent and died in office after nine years.

The text concludes that Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Ni Kwan rose from humble origins due to the Han dynasty’s prosperity under Emperor Wu, who recruited diverse talents. This era saw a flourishing of Confucians, loyalists, legalists, writers, and generals, achieving great deeds. Later, under Emperor Xuan, similar talents emerged, but none matched the brilliance of Emperor Wu’s reign.
