translation:
Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County, Shangdang County, and later moved to Duling.
His ancestor Feng Ting was the governor of Shangdang County in South Korea.
Qin attacked Shangdang and blocked the passage in the Taihang Mountains. South Korea could not defend it, so Feng Ting dedicated Shangdang City to Zhao and defended it.
The State of Zhao granted Feng Ting the title of Lord of Huayang, and together with General Zhao Kuo of the State of Zhao, he resisted the State of Qin and died in battle in Changping.
Since then, the Feng family has dispersed in various places, some staying in Lu County and some traveling to other places.
Those in Zhao became official generals, and the sons of official generals became prime ministers of the country.
After Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, Feng Ting's descendants Feng Wuze, Feng Quji, and Feng Jie all became Qin's generals.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Feng Tang was very famous during the reign of Emperor Wen. He was the son of the Prime Minister of Dai.
By the end of Emperor Wu's reign, Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan because he was a son of a good family.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, he was appointed as the Chang Palace of Wu'an County in accordance with the size and order of his achievements.
When he was dismissed from office, he was already in his thirties. He only studied "Spring and Autumn", studied its subtle meanings, read the art of war, and knew its contents and examples. Former general Han Zeng reported to him and appointed him as the military commander.
During this period, he accompanied the army to attack the Xiongnu.
After the war, he became a Langguan again.
Prior to this, the Han Dynasty sent envoys to the Western Regions several times, but most of them failed to fulfill their mission, some were corrupt, and some were made difficult and insulted by foreign countries.
At this time, the Wusun Kingdom was very powerful and had the merit of attacking the Xiongnu. At the same time, the countries in the Western Regions had just reconciled with the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty was preparing to treat them well. If they wanted to take the opportunity to appease these countries, they selected people who could be sent as envoys to foreign countries.
Former general Han Zeng recommended Feng Fengshi to escort guests from Dawan and other countries back home as an envoy.
When they arrived at Yixiu City, Captain Song said that the Shache people, together with some other countries, had attacked and killed King Wannian of Shache appointed by the Han Dynasty, and also killed Xi Chongguo, the envoy of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the Xiongnu sent troops to attack Cheshi City again, but they went back because they failed to capture it.
The Shache Kingdom sent envoys to threaten that the Northern Kingdoms had belonged to the Xiongnu. At that time, they attacked and plundered the Southern Kingdoms, and made a blood alliance with them to betray the Han Dynasty, cutting off all traffic from the Shanshan Kingdom to the west.
The Protector Zheng Ji and the Colonel Sima Yi were both trapped among the countries on the North Road.
Feng Fengshi discussed with his deputy Yan Lu and believed that if they did not attack quickly, the Shache Kingdom would become increasingly powerful, making the situation difficult to control and jeopardizing the entire Western Region.
So he notified the kings by envoys and mobilized their armies. A total of 15,000 people from the north and south attacked the Shache Kingdom and captured its city.
King Shache committed suicide and his head was sent to Chang'an.
All the countries were pacified, and Feng Fengshi's reputation shocked the Western Regions.
Feng Fengshi withdrew his troops and returned home, reporting the situation to the court.
Emperor Xuan summoned Han Zeng and said: Congratulations to the general on the competent person he recommended.
Feng Fengshi traveled west to the Kingdom of Dayuan.
The Kingdom of Dawan heard that he had killed King Shache and respected him more than other envoys.
After getting the famous horse Xianglong from Dayuan, he returned to Chang'an.
The emperor was very happy and issued an order to discuss the matter of rewarding Feng Fengshi.
The prime minister and the generals all said: The meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that when an official is on a mission abroad, if he encounters something that is beneficial to the country, he can take matters into his own hands.
Feng Fengshi's contribution is particularly significant, and he should be awarded a title and land.
Xiao Wangzhi, the Shaofu, believed that Feng Feng was on an envoy mission and had his mission, but he pretended to be the emperor's order and went against the will and sent troops from various countries. Although he had merit, he should not be used as an example for future generations.
If Feng Fengshi is to be rewarded, it will open the door for future envoys to use Feng Fengshi as an example to mobilize armies, claim credit and reward from thousands of miles away, and cause trouble for the country among the Yi and Di tribes.
This is an unacceptable example, and Feng Fengshi should not be rewarded.
The emperor thought Xiao Wangzhi's suggestion was good, and granted Feng Fengshi the titles of Doctor Guanglu and Captain Shuiheng.
Emperor Yuan came to the throne, and Feng Fengshi was appointed as Jinwu.
More than 10,000 Hu people from the vassal state of Shangjun surrendered to the Han Dynasty and rebelled.
At the beginning, in the last years of Emperor Zhao's reign, King Yiruo, a Hu from the Xihe County vassal state, also led thousands of people to rebel. Feng Fengshi immediately led an envoy and led an army to pursue them.
Chang Hui, the right general of the Dian Kingdom, passed away, and Feng Fengshi succeeded him as the right general of the Dian Kingdom, adding the titles of various officials.
A few years later, he became Guang Luxun.
In the autumn of the second year of Yongguang's reign, a branch of the Qiang village sisters in Longxi County rebelled. The emperor summoned Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng, imperial censor Zheng Hong, Da Sima Cavalry General Wang Jie, left general Xu Jia, and right general Feng Fengshi to come to the court to discuss countermeasures.
At that time, the crops were not harvested in consecutive years, and grain was sold for more than 200 fen per stone in Kyoto, 400 fen per stone in border counties, and 500 fen per stone in Kanto.
There was famine everywhere, and the court was worried about it, but it encountered a rebellion by the Qiang people.
Wei Xuancheng and others were silent and no one spoke.
Feng Fengshi said: The Qiang bandits are rebelling within the borders of the country. If they are not killed in time, there will be no way to subdue the barbarians far away.
I am willing to lead an army against them.
The emperor asked about the number of troops needed, and replied: I heard that those who are good at using troops will not use troops twice or transport food three times. Therefore, the army should not be deployed for a long time, and the crusade in obedience to God's will should be carried out quickly.
In the past, we often failed to measure the enemy's situation, and the army suffered losses; transporting food multiple times would take a long time and consume a lot of time, and the morale of the army would be low.
There are currently about 30,000 rebel soldiers. According to the law of war, an additional 60,000 people should be mobilized.
The Qiang Rong were an army that only used bows and spears. Their weapons were not sharp. They could mobilize 40,000 men and a month would be enough to solve the problem.
The prime minister, the censor, and the two generals all believed that the people were in the harvest season and could not send more troops; 10,000 troops were stationed for defense, which was almost enough.
Feng Fengshi said: No.
The country suffered from famine, the soldiers and horses were thin and few in number, and the war equipment had been left unmaintained for a long time. All the Yi and Di tribes had the intention to despise the border officials, so the Qiang people were the first to attack.
Now ten thousand men are divided into several places to defend several places. The traitors will not be afraid when they see that our army is small in number. In battle, the army will be damaged and morale will be low, and the rules will not be able to save the people.
If this happens and the cowardice is revealed, the Qiang people will take the opportunity to attack, and all the ethnic minorities will respond together and incite each other to raise troops. I am afraid that the Han Dynasty will have to collect more than 40,000 soldiers. This cannot be solved by money.
Therefore, sending less troops will take a long time. Compared with quickly solving the problem in one battle, the benefits and risks are ten thousand times different.
Feng Fengshi persisted in fighting but could not get more troops.
Another edict was issued to increase the number of 2,000 people.
Immediately dispatched Feng Fengshi to lead 12,000 soldiers and horses to set off, in the name of leading troops to farm.
Han Chang, the captain of the Dian Kingdom and the military guard, was appointed as the deputy general and went to Longxi County to station troops in three places.
Dian Zhuguo was appointed as the right army, stationed at Baishi; the guard captain Han Chang was appointed as the front army, stationed at Lintao; Feng Fengshi was appointed as the central army, stationed at Xiji Mountain in Shouyang County.
When the former army arrived at Tongban, they first sent a school lieutenant to compete with the Qiang people in front for favorable terrain, and then sent another school lieutenant to Guangyang Valley to rescue the people.
There were so many Qiang bandits that the officers and soldiers were defeated and two captains were killed.
Feng Fengshi reported the terrain and plans for how many troops would be needed to the emperor, and requested an additional 36,000 troops, which would be enough to resolve the war.
According to the letter, the emperor sent more than 60,000 troops and appointed Taichang Yiyang Marquis Ren Qianqiu as General Fenwu to help him.
Feng Fengshi reported: I hope to get a large number of soldiers, so I don't need to trouble the generals.
So Chen asked for the cost of transshipment.
At that time, the emperor sent a letter to express condolences to Feng Fengshi, but also blamed him, saying: The emperor expressed condolences to the right general who was leading the army. It was very hard to fight abroad.
The Qiang bandits invaded the border and killed officials and people, which was against the will of heaven, so they sent generals and army generals to kill them according to God's will.
With the outstanding qualities of a general, leading elite troops to attack unruly bandits, there is a principle of victory in every battle.
Now he actually has the reputation of not daring to attack in the face of battle, which is too embarrassing for the Han Dynasty.
Is it because I was not familiar with military affairs before?
Or is it because the favor is not widespread and military discipline is unclear?
I'm very strange.
You wrote a letter saying that the Qiang rebels had to divide their troops to occupy key areas due to the deep mountains and many small roads. Then they had to mobilize the garrisoned soldiers to solve the problem. The army deployment has been decided, and judging from the situation, no more generals can be arranged. I understand.
In the past, because the general lacked soldiers to defend, he dispatched nearby cavalry and rushed there day and night, not for offense.
Sanfu, Hedong, Hongnong Yueqi, Jishe, Youfei, Yuzhe, Yulin Orphan, Husuqi and Zhengzhong are currently being mobilized at a rapid pace.
War is a dangerous thing, and there will definitely be success or failure. I am afraid that the strategy is not agreed upon in advance, and it is not prudent to understand the enemy's situation, so I send General Fenwu.
The Art of War says that when a general goes on an expedition, he must have a supporting general to show off his power and provide advice. What doubts does the general have?
Care for the soldiers, gain military morale, and you will not regret your decision. You must be thorough in capturing the enemy. This is the responsibility of the general.
As for the transportation costs, special officials are responsible for them, so the general does not have to worry.
Wait until General Fenwu's troops arrive and attack the Qiang bandits together.
In October, the army gathered in Longxi County.
In November, attack together.
The Qiang thieves were defeated and thousands of their heads were beheaded, while the rest fled across the border.
When the outcome of the war was still undecided, the Han Dynasty recruited another 10,000 soldiers and appointed Han Anguo, the prefect of Dingxiang, as General Jianwei.
Before setting off, I heard that the Qiang rebels had been defeated. The emperor said: The Qiang rebels were defeated and punished, and fled from the border. Those soldiers who had a truce should leave more field guards to defend key points.
In February of the next year, Feng Fengshi returned to the capital and was appointed General Zuo, while Guang Luxun's position remained unchanged.
After recording his meritorious service and conferring a title, the emperor issued an edict saying: The Qiang thieves were cruel and cunning, killing officials and common people, attacking Longxi County government offices, burning post houses, and cutting off roads and bridges, which greatly violated the law of heaven.
The general of the left, Guang Luxun and Feng Fengshi, led an army to conquer the area, beheading more than 8,000 prisoners and seizing tens of thousands of cattle, horses and sheep.
Feng Fengshi was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, a settlement of 500 households, and 60 kilograms of gold.
More than thirty generals and lieutenants were rewarded.
More than a year later, Feng Fengshi died of illness.
He served as a military general for ten years. He was a veteran general who killed enemies and defended the country, and his reputation was second only to Tong Chongguo.
General Fenwu was appointed Qianqiu, and his father was appointed to the palace. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he used the prime minister's campaign to capture and kill the rebellious left general Shangguan Jie, and granted him the title of Marquis. Emperor Xuan was appointed Taichang and died.
Qianqiu inherited the title and was appointed Taichang.
When he became emperor, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Lechang, replaced Feng Fengshi as the left general, while Ren Qianqiu was appointed the right general, and later the left general.
Descendants inherited the title from generation to generation until the era of Wang Mang.
Two years after Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou, the governor of the Western Regions, was named a prince because he killed the Zhizhi Chanyu.
At that time, Prime Minister Kuang Heng also used Gan Yanshou's counterfeit edicts to cause trouble as an excuse. Based on Xiao Wangzhi's case, he believed that Gan Yanshou should not be made a marquis. However, the commentators all praised Gan Yanshou's achievements, and the emperor followed everyone's opinions and made him a marquis.
At that time, Du Qin went to Shangshu and praised Feng Fengshi's previous contributions: In the past, King Yarkand killed the envoys of the Han Dynasty and formed an alliance with other countries to betray the Han Dynasty.
General Feng Fengshi of the left, as a guard, sent troops to annihilate the King of Shache according to convenient conditions, used strategies to stabilize the city, and made great contributions to the border areas.
Commentators believed that Feng Fengshi had his mission as an envoy. According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, ministers cannot act arbitrarily. According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, it was a crime of restraint, so he could not be granted a title.
Now the Xiongnu Zhizhi Chanyu killed the envoys of the Han Dynasty and fled to the state of Kangju. The governor Gan Yanshou sent more than 40,000 soldiers from the city and soldiers in the field to kill him and made him a prince.
In my humble opinion, in terms of crime, Zhi Zhi Shan is lighter than Zhi Zhi; in terms of military strength, Yash Che is more than Zhi Zhi; in terms of the use of troops, Feng Fengshi is less; in terms of the degree of victory, Feng Fengshi has contributed to the peace of the border; in terms of failure, it is the disaster that Yanshou has brought to the country.
They had the same crime of disobeying orders and causing trouble. However, Yanshou ceded lands and made lords, but Feng Fengshi did not remember the rewards.
I heard that if the merits are the same and the rewards are different, the ministers who have worked hard will have doubts; if the crime is the same but the punishment is different, the people will be confused; doubts will lead to uncertainty, and confusion will lead to not knowing what to do; uncertainty will lead to unclear systems and directions, and not knowing what to follow will lead to the people not knowing how to act.
Feng Fengshi relieved the danger, risked his life in the battle, completed the mission with extraordinary achievements, and achieved a remarkable reputation. He was a model for generations of envoys, but he was suppressed and did not praise him. This is not the meaning of a sage monarch who eliminates doubts and encourages integrity.
I hope it will be handed over to the relevant departments for discussion.
The emperor believed that this was a matter of the late emperor's time, so he no longer accepted his opinion.
Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters.
The eldest daughter Feng Yuan was elected to the palace as Emperor Yuan Zhaoyi and gave birth to Prince Xiao of Zhongshan.
After the death of Emperor Yuan, Feng Yuan became the Queen Mother of Zhongshan and followed King Xiao of Zhongshan to the feudal state.
Feng Fengshi's eldest son, Feng Tan, was recommended by Taichang as Xiaolian to be a Langguan, and he was appointed Tianshui Sima in order of merit.
Feng Fengshi attacked Xiqiang. Feng Tan was a captain. He served in the army with his father and died of illness before he was promoted to an official.
Feng Tan's younger brothers Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen all became high officials.
Feng Yewang, nicknamed Junqing, studied with a doctor and was proficient in the Book of Songs.
When he was young, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine because his father was an official.
When he was eighteen years old, he wrote to the emperor hoping to be tried as the magistrate of Chang'an County.
Emperor Xuan was surprised by his ambition and asked Prime Minister Wei Xiang, who thought it was unacceptable.
Later, he was appointed Dangyang County Magistrate in order of merit, promoted to Liyang County Magistrate, and transferred to Xiayang County Magistrate.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, he was promoted to the prefect of Longxi County. Because of his outstanding political achievements, he entered the court and served as Zuo Fengyi.
For more than a year, the magistrate of Chiyang County, who was not known to be corrupt, despised King Feng Ye as a young relative, and did not correct his misdeeds in governance.
King Feng Ye deployed the postal supervisor Zhao Du from Touxu County to file a case for investigation and found out that the person in power was responsible for stealing ten gold coins from himself and arrested him.
When he refused to obey the arrest, Zhao Duge killed him.
Bing's family wrote a letter stating their grievances, and the matter was handed over to Tingwei.
Zhao Du committed suicide in front of the officials to prove that he had nothing to do with King Feng Ye. People in the capital praised his prestige and promoted him to Dahonglu.
A few years later, the imperial censor Li Yanshou died of illness, and many officials recommended King Feng Ye to succeed him.
The emperor sent the minister to select two thousand-level officials, and King Feng Ye ranked first in terms of character and ability.
The emperor said: If I use King Feng Ye as the three princes, future generations will definitely use this as an example to say that I prefer concubines in the harem.
Then Xia Shao said: The man who is strong and resolute, and truly has no selfish desires, is the king of Da Honglu and Feng Ye.
He can speak eloquently and can be sent to various places, such as Shaofu Wulu Chongzong.
The most honest and frugal person is Zhang Tan, the young master of the prince.
Shaofu Zhang Tan is now appointed as the imperial censor.
The emperor appointed Zhang Tan from a subordinate position and went beyond the rank to avoid suspicion and did not use Feng Yewang because he was Zhaoyi's brother.
King Feng Ye then sighed and said: Others are noble because of the emperor's favored concubine, but our brothers are humble because of it!
Although King Feng Ye did not become a third official, he was highly regarded and was very famous at that time.
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, the relevant departments reported that King Feng Ye was the uncle of the country and was not suitable for the post of Jiuqing. According to his rank, he will serve as the prefect of Shangjun and will be rewarded with one hundred catties of gold.
Xiao Yu, the governor of Shuofang, reported a secret report and recommended that King Feng Ye was of outstanding character and ability, capable of considering himself in domestic affairs and capable of strategy and enlightenment in diplomacy.
It is a pity that King Feng Ye is the pillar of governing the country, but he cannot assist the government and serve as ministers in the government.
King Feng Ye was previously transferred from the court because he was the uncle of the state, and he was also transferred to the court because of his virtuousness, which shows that the country is willing to employ virtuous people.
The emperor had heard of King Feng Ye since he was the crown prince.
It happened that he was dismissed from his post due to illness, and managed the Yellow River embankment at the original level of two thousand stones, so he was named Langxie Prefect.
At that time, the emperor's eldest uncle, Yangpinghou Wang Feng, was appointed as the Grand Sima General and had been assisting the government for eight or nine years. Several disasters occurred at that time. King Yin Zhang of Jingzhao ridiculed Wang Feng for his exclusive power and recommended that Feng Yewang replace Wang Feng.
The emperor initially accepted Wang Zhang's suggestion, but later Wang Zhang was executed, and the incident was recorded in the "Biography of the Empress of the Yuan Dynasty".
So King Feng Ye was frightened and uneasy, so he fell ill. After three months of sick leave, he took another sick leave and returned to Duling with his wife and children for treatment.
General Wang Feng instructs Yushi Zhongcheng to impeach King Feng Ye for taking leave to recuperate for his own well-being, and going home with a tiger talisman out of bounds, which is disrespectful to the emperor's edict.
Du Qin was in the shogunate of General Wang Feng at the time. He always respected the character and talents of Feng Yewang and his son, so he presented a memorial to Wang Feng and spoke for Feng Yewang: I saw the edict saying that two thousand stone-level officials asked for leave and passed through Chang'an to pay homage. There was no distinction between giving and reporting.
Now the relevant departments believe that King Feng Ye was able to recuperate his illness, but could not approve the prosecution. These are two levels of the same law, which loses the meaning of reducing the penalty.
The most prominent thing is to give a warning during the three performance appraisals, which is an order; to give a warning after three months of illness is to give a warning, which is an edict from the emperor to bestow favors.
Orders and reports can be obtained, but favors cannot be obtained, and the difference between importance and importance is lost.
In addition, there is a tradition that officials with two thousand stone rank are allowed to go home if they are sick, and there is no explicit rule that they cannot leave the county.
An old saying goes: Rewards are given when merit is unclear, in order to show kindness and encourage meritorious deeds; punishment should be waived when faults are not obvious, in order to be careful about punishment and not to deal with things that are difficult to know.
Nowadays, disregarding laws and old practices and relying on disrespectful laws is contrary to the original meaning of Quexin.
Even if there are two thousand stone-level officials guarding the surrounding area and holding important military positions, they should not leave the garrison and use punishment as the law of future generations. Then the crime of King Feng Ye is that he did not formulate a law before.
Punishments and rewards should be very credible and should not be lax.
Wang Feng refused to listen and was eventually removed from the Wild King's official position.
Officials with a rank of 2,000 or so in the county were told not to go home, and that was the beginning.
At first, King Feng Ye inherited his father's title as Marquis of Guannei and was dismissed from his post and returned home.
A few years later, he died at home of old age.
His son Feng Zuo inherited the title, but his grandson was stripped of his title because of the case of being the Queen Mother of Zhongshan.
Feng Kui's courtesy name is Zichan, and he is familiar with the Book of Changes. Taichang inspected those who were filial and honest and appointed them as Langguan, and supplemented those who were appointed as Ye.
During the Jianzhao period, he was elected as Futu Xiaowei.
Guang Luxun recommended him as a scholar in Yong and appointed him as the magistrate of Meiyang County.
In order of merit, he was promoted to Sima of Changle Palace Guards, Captain of Qinghe County, and Prefect of Longxi County.
His governance was honest and fair, and he died in his forties.
When he was the captain, he had some ideas about regulating the embankment of the Yellow River. For details, see the book "Gou Xi Zhi".
Feng Li, also known as Shengqing, was proficient in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Because of his father's relationship, he was appointed as Lang Guan, and then promoted to Cao Guan.
During the Jingning period, because he was the uncle of the state, he was appointed as the captain of the vassal state of Wuyuan County.
A few years later, he was promoted to the prefect of Wuyuan County, and then to the prefect of Xihe County and Shang County.
Feng Li was fair and honest as an official, and his political performance was roughly the same as that of King Feng Ye. He was often wise, generous and kind to others, and liked to formulate rules and regulations.
The officials and the people praised Feng Yewang and Feng Li for being the prefects before and after. They praised them by saying: Great Feng Jun and Xiao Feng Jun are brothers who serve as prefects. They are smart and wise and love the officials and the people. Their government is like Lu Weide's Hua Gou, Zhou Gong and Kang Shu are still two monarchs.
Later he was promoted to the prefect of Donghai County. The local terrain was low and humid, and he suffered from rheumatism.
When the emperor heard about the incident, he appointed Feng Li as the governor of Taiyuan.
He served as the governor of five counties successively and made political achievements wherever he went.
He died in office when he was old.
Feng Shen, courtesy name Shuping, was proficient in Shangshu.
When he was young, he served as Huang Menlang and worked as a palace guard for more than ten years. Feng Shen is a solemn and serious person, likes to modify his appearance and etiquette, behaves cautiously and honestly, and is very graceful.
Feng Shen is Zhaoyi's younger brother. He is cautious and prepared. Because he is serious and awe-inspiring, he cannot be the emperor's close minister.
During the Jingning period, he went to court as the uncle of the state and was appointed as the food officer of Weiling.
Because he was often sick, he was assigned to the position of sleeping lieutenant, and there was an edict that allowed him not to do anything.
In the year of Yangshuo, King Zhongshan came to pay homage, and Feng Shen was promoted to the rank of Captain of Shanghe Nong.
He was dismissed from office due to illness and was appointed as the lieutenant in the Weiling Palace.
During the Yongshi period, he was promoted to the prefect of Daijun.
Because the road was far away from the border counties, he was transferred to the prefect of Anding County.
A few years later, he was dismissed from his post due to illness and served as an admonishing doctor and also as a bodyguard Zuo Feng Yi Du Shui.
During the Suihe period, King Tao was made the crown prince. Because King Zhongshan was deposed, his uncle Feng Shen was granted the title of Marquis of Yixiang to appease King Zhongshan.
Feng Shen went to the feudal state and wrote to the emperor that he wanted to see the King of Zhongshan and the Queen Mother of Zhongshan.
King Zhongshan died before he arrived.
When the King of Zhongshan was ill, he wrote in a memorial that he hoped to demote Feng Shen's title and live in Chang'an as the Marquis of Guannei.
The emperor took pity on him and issued an edict: "King Xiao of Zhongshan died prematurely. I would like to ennoble my uncle Feng Shen, Marquis of Yixiang, as the Marquis of Guannei and return home. I pity him very much."
He asked Feng Shen to return to the capital and serve in the court as a prince.
The five princes of the Wang family respected and feared him.
Prime Minister Zhai Fangjin also respected him and said to Feng Shen several times: "The taboo on this matter is too much."
Because you are the uncle of the state and have been deposed, you are not allowed to occupy the position of public minister. Now the five princes have the most honorable status. You and they are equal, so you should be a little humble and show respect.
However, you pay great attention to grooming your appearance and treat them with dignity. This is not a way to show that you are lower than the five princes and benefit yourself.
Feng Shen was a man of etiquette by nature and never changed his conduct.
Soon, Emperor Ai came to the throne, and his grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu, came to power. She pursued the grudge against Feng Shen's sister, the Empress Dowager Zhongshan, and framed her for the crime of curse and treason. The incident was recorded in "The Biography of the Wife".
Because Feng Shen and she were born from the same mother, they should sit together. The emissary ordered Shao to capture Feng Shen and bring him to the court for interrogation. Feng Shen committed suicide.
When he was about to die, he looked up to the sky and sighed and said: My father, son and brothers, Feng Shen, are all high-ranking officials, marquises and knights. Now I am dying with a bad reputation. My sister and brother dare not feel sorry for themselves. What hurts me is that I have no face to see my ancestors in the ground.
Seventeen people were executed, and everyone felt pity for them.
The Feng family all moved back to their hometown.
Praise said: "The Book of Songs" says that the majesty of the dignified person is truly upright, and the virtue and appearance are integrated inside and outside.
Marquis Feng Shen of Yixiang worked hard, had good conduct, and was cautious in his words and deeds. He could be said to be a gentleman. However, he died innocently in the end and could not escape. It was so sad!
Slander and evil create chaos, and loyal and kind people are persecuted. This has been the case since ancient times.
That's why Boqi was exiled, the eunuch Mencius was tortured, Shen Sheng was hanged and died, and Qu Yuan drowned himself in the Xiang River. That's why poems like "Xiao Bian" and "Li Sao" emerged.
The Book of Songs says: The heart is sad and tears fall down.
The Feng Shen siblings are also miserable!
summary:
Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County in Shangdang, later moving to Duling. His ancestor Feng Ting, governor of Shangdang under South Korea, surrendered the city to Zhao during Qin's invasion and died at Changping. The Feng family dispersed; some became officials in Zhao, and after Qin's unification, descendants like Feng Wuze served as Qin generals. Under Han, Feng Tang gained fame under Emperor Wen. Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan under Emperor Wu, later serving as a military commander under General Han Zeng, accompanying campaigns against the Xiongnu.

During Emperor Xuan's reign, Feng Fengshi was sent as an envoy to the Western Regions. At Yixiu City, he learned that the Shache Kingdom had killed Han-appointed King Wannian and envoy Xi Chongguo, while the Xiongnu attacked Cheshi. Shache threatened the southern kingdoms, cutting off traffic from Shanshan westward. Protector Zheng Ji and Colonel Sima Yi were trapped. Feng Fengshi, with deputy Yan Lu, mobilized 15,000 troops from northern and southern kingdoms, attacked Shache, and captured its city. King Shache committed suicide, and his head was sent to Chang'an. Feng Fengshi's reputation spread across the Western Regions. After returning, Emperor Xuan praised Han Zeng for his recommendation. Feng Fengshi later obtained a famous horse from Dayuan. The court debated rewards: the prime minister and generals favored a title, but Shaofu Xiao Wangzhi argued against it, citing the precedent of unauthorized military action. The emperor agreed, granting Feng Fengshi the titles of Doctor Guanglu and Captain Shuiheng.

Under Emperor Yuan, Feng Fengshi became Jinwu and later Right General of the Dian Kingdom. In the second year of Yongguang, the Qiang rebelled in Longxi. Amid famine, Feng Fengshi volunteered to lead an army, proposing 40,000 troops for a swift campaign. The prime minister and others advocated for only 10,000, but Feng Fengshi warned that insufficient forces would embolden the Qiang and other tribes. He was granted 12,000 troops initially, later reinforced to 60,000 under General Fenwu Ren Qianqiu. After initial defeats, the combined forces defeated the Qiang in November, beheading thousands and driving the rest across the border. Feng Fengshi was appointed General Zuo and Marquis of Guannei with 500 households and gold. He died of illness over a year later, having served as a military general for ten years, with a reputation second only to Tong Chongguo.

After Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou was made a marquis for killing the Zhizhi Chanyu. Du Qin later petitioned, arguing that Feng Fengshi's similar merits had been overlooked due to Xiao Wangzhi's precedent, creating inconsistency in rewards. The emperor declined to revisit the matter.

Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters. His eldest daughter Feng Yuan became Emperor Yuan's Zhaoyi and mother of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan. His sons—Feng Tan, Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen—all held high offices. Feng Yewang, known for his character, was recommended for high posts but was passed over due to his sister's imperial favor, leading him to lament that their family was humbled by her status. He later served as prefect of several commanderies but was dismissed after being implicated in a political dispute. Feng Kui was known for his governance and died in his forties. Feng Li served as prefect of five commanderies, praised for his fairness. Feng Shen, cautious and dignified, was made Marquis of Yixiang but committed suicide under Emperor Ai after being framed for treason, along with seventeen family members. The Feng family then returned to their hometown. The historical commentary laments their tragic fate, comparing it to ancient figures like Boqi and Qu Yuan.

translation:
The ancestor of the Xiongnu was a descendant of the Xiahou family, named Chunwei.
Before Yao, Yu and Shun of the Tang Dynasty, there were Shanrong, Yanyun, Xunzhou and other branches. They lived in the northern border of China and moved along with water, grass and livestock husbandry.
Most of the livestock raised are horses, cattle, and sheep. The exotic livestock include camels, donkeys, mules, Yaosao, colts, and Yixi.
They migrated in pursuit of water and grass. They did not have cities or agriculture for permanent residence, but they also had separate grazing lands.
There are no written books, only words are used for restraint and management.
When the men were young, they could ride sheep, draw bows and shoot mice, and learn archery. When they grew up, they could shoot foxes and rabbits, and mostly ate meat.
Men in their prime are strong and can bend bows and shoot arrows, so they serve as armored cavalry.
The living customs of the Huns were that when there was no war, they would graze and hunt birds and animals as a way of making a living; in case of emergency war, people would practice battle formations to attack and plunder others. This was the nature of the Huns.
Their long weapons are bows and arrows, and their short weapons are swords and spears.
When fighting, attack if things go well, retreat if things go wrong, and don't be ashamed to run away.
If there is a profit, then etiquette and justice will be ignored.
The Huns, from the king on down, all eat animal meat, wear animal hides, and wear felt fur.
Strong young people eat rich food, and old people eat leftovers.
Those who are strong are valued and those who are old and weak are looked down upon.
When his father died, his son took his stepmother as his wife; when his brothers died, the surviving ones took their wives as wives.
The custom in terms of names is to have names, no taboos, and no epithet.
The Xia Dynasty declined, and Gong Liu, the ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, lost his position as a farmer, so he reformed and changed the customs of Xirong and established a capital in Bin.
More than three hundred years later, Rong Di attacked Yifu, King Tai of Zhou, and Yifu fled to the foot of Qishan Mountain. The Bin people followed Yifu to build houses and settle down under Qishan Mountain, and began to establish the Zhou Kingdom.
More than a hundred years later, King Wen of Zhou Dynasty Xi Bo Jichang attacked Yi.
More than ten years later, King Wu of Zhou attacked and destroyed him, and then built Luoyi. King Wu returned to Fengjing and Haojing to live, and exiled the Rong and Yi to the north of Jinghe and Luohe, requiring them to contribute gifts on time, and called them "Huangfu".
After more than two hundred years, the Zhou Dynasty declined, and King Zhou Duo went to attack Zuo Xi and returned with four white wolves and four white deer.
From then on, people from Huangfu no longer paid tribute to the Zhou Dynasty.
The Zhou Dynasty formulated the law of "Lu Xing" at that time.
By the time of King Zhou Yi, the grandson of King Mu of Zhou, the royal family of Zhou declined, and Rong and Di repeatedly attacked and ravaged various countries in the Central Plains.
The people of the Central Plains were deeply affected, and poets began to sing poems that hated them: No house, no home, this is all because of Yan Yun; When will I not be on guard? Yan Yun's attack was really urgent.
When King Xuan, the great-grandson of King Yi, sent a general to lead an army to attack Yan Yun, the poet praised: The expedition against Yan Yun reached Taiyuan; the chariots were dispatched to build a city in the north.
At that time, the surrounding ethnic minorities all surrendered to the Zhou Dynasty, which was known as Zhongxing.
When King You of Zhou Dynasty arrived, he had a conflict with Queen Shen's father, Shen Hou, because he doted on his beautiful concubine Gui Si.
The Marquis of Shen was very angry and joined forces with Quan Rong to attack King You, killed him under Mount Li, occupied the land of the Zhou Dynasty, plundered and lived between the Jingwei River, and invaded and ravaged the people of the Central Plains.
Qin Xianggong sent troops to rescue the Dan Dynasty, so King Qiewen left; Yan and Guzhi moved eastward to the capital of Tao Dan.
At that time, Tong Saigong attacked Zuosheng and went all the way to Guishan. At this time, Tong Cai began to be named a prince.
Sixty-five years later, the Shanrong crossed Zangli again to attack Bianli. Duke Manli led his army to fight the Shanrong at the border of Bianxi. Forty-four years later, Shanrong attacked Yan again.
Yan State asked Qi State for help. Duke Huan of Qi led his army to attack Shanrong in the north, but Shanrong fled.
More than twenty years later, Rong Zhai went to Luoyi and attacked King Xiang of Zhou Dynasty. King Xiang fled to Panyi in Zheng State.
At first, King Xiang of Zhou wanted to attack the State of Zheng, so he married Rong Zhai's daughter as his queen and joined forces with Rong Zhai to attack the State of Zheng.
Soon after, Empress Zhai was deposed, and Empress Zhai was very resentful. King Xiang's stepmother was named Empress Hui, and she had a son named Zidai. Queen Hui wanted to make Zidai king. So Empress Hui, together with Empress Zhai and Ziying, responded internally and opened the city gate to welcome Rong Zhai. Rong Zhai therefore attacked the city, defeated and drove away King Xiang, and established Zidai as King of Zhou.
At that time, some Rong Zhai were already living in Luhun, and Shu Bian arrived in Wei State, and the invasion became even more severe.
King Xiang of Zhou had been wandering for four years, so he sent an envoy to Jin to ask for help.
Duke Wen of Jin had just ascended the throne and wanted to establish hegemony, so he sent troops to attack Rong Zhai, killed Zidai, and welcomed King Zhou Xiang back to Luoyi.
At this time, Qin and Jin were very powerful.
Duke Wen of Jin attacked and expelled Rong Di. Rong Di lived between the Huan River and Luo River in the Xihe River, and they were called Chidi and Baidi.
Duke Mu of Qin got Yu Yu, and the eight kingdoms of Xirong surrendered to Qin.
Therefore, there are Rong tribes such as Mianzhu, Dengrong and Diyuan living in Longxi. To the north of Qishan, Liangshan, Jinghe and Qihe there are Rong tribes such as Yiqu, Dali, Wushi and Quyan. To the north of Jin there are Rong tribes such as Linhu and Loufan. To the north of Yan there are Donghu and Shanrong.
They live scattered in the valley, each with its own leader. There are more than a hundred Rong tribes living together, but they cannot be unified.
More than a hundred years later, the Duke of Jin sent Wei Jiang to negotiate peace with Rong Di, and Rong Di began to pay homage to the king of Jin.
More than a hundred years later, Tsai Xiangzi led his troops across Juzhu Mountain, conquered and annexed the state of Dai, and approached Hu Xian.
Later, Zhao Xiangzi, together with the Han and Wei families, destroyed Zhi, and the three families occupied the land of Jin. In this way, Zhao State occupied Daidi and the area north of Juzhu Mountain, while Wei State occupied Xihe and Shangjun, adjacent to the Rong people.
Later, the Rong people in Yiqu built cities for self-defense, while the Qin State slowly encroached on the land of Yiqu. When King Hui arrived, he captured twenty-five cities in Yiqu.
King Hui of Qin attacked the State of Wei, and the State of Wei dedicated all the areas of Xihe and Shangjun to the State of Qin.
During the reign of King Zhao of Qin, King Yiqurong had an affair with Queen Mother Xuan and gave birth to two sons. Queen Mother Xuan deceived King Yiqurong and killed him in Ganquan, and then raised troops to attack and eliminate Yiqu.
Therefore, the Qin State occupied Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun, and built the Great Wall to resist the Hu people.
King Wuling of Zhao also mutated the customs of his own country, wore the clothes of the barbarians, learned horseback riding and archery, and attacked Linhu and Loufan to the north. From Daidi along the foothills of Yinshan Mountain to Gaoque, he used it as his frontier fortress. And established Yunzhong County, Yanmen County and Dai County.
Later, a wise general from Yan State, Qin Kai, served as a hostage in the Hu area. The Hu people trusted him very much.
After returning, he led his troops to attack Ding Donghu, and Shu Hu retreated for more than a thousand miles.
Qin Wuyang, who later assassinated Qin Shihuang with Jing Ke, was Qin Kai's grandson.
The State of Yan also built the Great Wall, from Zaoyang to Xiangping, and set up Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong counties to resist the Hu people.
At that time, three of the seven highly civilized countries of the Warring States Period bordered on the Xiongnu.
Later, when General Li Mu of the State of Zhao was there, the Huns did not dare to invade the border of the State of Zhao.
Later, Qin Shihuang destroyed the six kingdoms and sent General Meng Tian to lead an army of hundreds of thousands to the north to attack the Xiongnu. He completely recovered the area south of the Yellow River. Using the Yellow River as a fortress, he built forty-four cities on the edge of the Yellow River and sent those who were punished for their crimes to guard the border to live there.
They also built a straight road from Jiuyuan to Yunyang; they also built the Great Wall along the dangerous chasms of the mountains and along the valleys, and repaired the places that could be repaired. It was more than 10,000 miles from Lintao to Liaodong.
Later, the Qin State crossed the Yellow River and occupied the northern false area of ​​​​Yangshan.
At that time, both Shuhu and Yuezhi were very powerful.
The Xiongnu Chanyu was named Touman. Touman could not resist Qin, so he moved north.
More than ten years later, Meng Tian died. The descendants of the original princes rebelled against the Qin State. The Central Plains area was in chaos. Those who had been exiled by the Qin Dynasty to guard the border left. As a result, the Xiongnu's situation improved and they slowly crossed the Yellow River. In the south, they were adjacent to the Central Plains with their original border fortress. Shan Yuli had a prince named Maodun.
Later, the Chanyu's favored Ban clan gave birth to a son. Chanyu Touman wanted to depose the crown prince Mao Dun and make his younger son the crown prince, so he sent Mao Dun to Yuezhi as a hostage.
After Maodun arrived at Yuezhi and became a hostage, Touman Chanyu immediately sent troops to attack Yuezhi.
Yuezhi wanted to kill Mao Dun, so Mao Dun stole Yuezhi's good horse and rode it back to the Huns.
Touman Chanyu thought that Mao Dun was brave, so he asked him to lead 10,000 cavalry.
Mao Dun then made the Ming Dy, or ringing arrow, and trained and constrained his cavalry in archery. He ordered them to say: If anyone does not follow and shoot the thing shot by my Ming Dy, he will be killed.
Mao Dun led his men out for hunting. Anyone who did not follow the target shot by She Ming Dy was immediately killed.
Soon, Mao Dun shot his own good horse with Wu Dy. Some people around him did not dare to follow suit, so Mao Dun immediately killed these people.
A few days later, Mao Dun himself shot his beloved wife with a hammer. Some people around him were very frightened and did not dare to shoot arrows. Mao Dun killed these people again.
Soon, Mao Dun led his men out for hunting and shot Shanyu's fine horse with a wu-dy, and everyone around him followed suit.
So Mao Dun knew that the people around him could be used for his own purposes. When he went hunting with his father Touman Chanyu, he shot Touman with a hammer. The people around him followed the lead and shot Touman, killing the Chanyu. Mao Dun also killed his stepmother, his younger brother, and all the ministers who disobeyed him.
So Maodun established himself as Chanyu.
When Mao Dun established himself as a chanyu, Dong Hu was very powerful. When Cambodian Hu heard that Mao Dun killed his father and established himself, he sent an envoy to Mao Dun and said: Dong Hu wants to get Tou Man, a good horse known as a thousand-mile horse.
Mao Dun asked the ministers, and they all said: "This is the Xiongnu's BMW and cannot be given to them."
Mao Dun said: How can we be neighbors and yet pity a horse?
So he gave the thousand-mile horse to Donghu.
Soon, Shu Hu thought that Mao Dun was afraid of him, so he sent an envoy to Mao Dun and said: Shu Hu wants to get Shan Yu, a Ban clan.
Mao Dun asked the ministers again, and the people around him were very angry and said: "The Shu Hu people are unreasonable and want Banshi from us!"
Please send troops to attack them.
Mao Dun said: How can we be neighbors and yet begrudge a woman?
So he gave his favorite Pi family to Ding Donghu.
King Shuhu became more arrogant and invaded westward.
There is an uninhabited wasteland between the Xiongnu and Donghu, which is more than a thousand miles away. The Xiongnu and Donghu each live on one side and set up observation posts.
Shuhu sent an envoy to Modu and said: The Huns cannot reach the deserted land guarded by the observation post on the border with us, and we want to occupy it.
Mao Dun asked the ministers, and some ministers said: "This is abandoned land, give it to them."
After hearing this, Mo Dun was furious and said: Land is the foundation of the country, how can you give it to others!
Those who said they could give land to Shuhu were killed.
Maodun mounted his horse and ordered his countrymen to kill anyone who retreated, so he went east to attack Donghu.
At first Shu Hu looked down upon Mao Dun and took no precautions.
When Mao Dun arrived with his troops, he completely defeated and eliminated King Donghu, captured the people of Ding Donghu, and plundered their livestock and products.
After returning, he sent troops to the west to drive away the Yuezhi, and to the south he annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan. He also completely recovered the Xiongnu territory that Qin sent Meng Tian to invade. Using the original Henan fortress as the boundary with the Han Dynasty, he reached Chaona and Fushi, and then invaded Yan and Dai.
At that time, Liu Han was fighting Xiang Yu, and the Central Plains was exhausted by the war, so Maodun was able to become strong and strong, with more than 300,000 warriors who could bend bows, ride and shoot.
It was more than a thousand years from Chunwei to Touman. Sometimes the Xiongnu were large, sometimes small, and their residences were scattered and separated. They were so long ago that their lineage inheritance cannot be arranged one by one in order.
However, when Maodun became the Chanyu, when the Huns were at their most powerful, all the ethnic minorities in the north were subject to his rule and became enemies of the Chinese ethnic groups in the south. It was only then that its lineage, surnames and official titles could be recorded.
The Chanyu's surname was Lyuta, and their people called the king "Pengli Gutu Chanyu".
The Huns called the sky "Plough Holder" and the son "Gu Tu". The name "Chanyu" means vast. This name means that the Chanyu is as big as the sky.
The Xiongnu had left and right Xian kings, left and right Guli kings, left and right generals, left and right captains, left and right Danghu, and left and right Guduhous.
The Huns called the wise "Tu Qi", so the prince often served as the Zuo Tu Qi King.
From King Youyouxian down to Danghu, the older ones led more than ten thousand cavalry, while the younger ones led thousands of cavalry. There were twenty-four leaders in total, and they were given the title of Ten Thousand Cavalrymen.
Their ministers all have hereditary official positions.
The Huyan family, the Lan family, and later the Xubu family, these three surnames were the noble families of the Xiongnu.
Those left kings and left generals all live in the east, facing the area bounded by Shanggu and Shu, which connects Hui Raccoon and North Korea; those of right kings and right generals live in the west, facing west of Shangjun, bordering the Di and Qiang; and the royal court of the Shanyu faces Daijun and Yunzhong areas.
They each have their own area and move with the quality of the water and grass.
The left and right Xianwang and the left and right Guli led the largest tribe, and the left and right Guduhou assisted in government affairs.
The twenty-four leaders also each have official positions such as Qianchang, Baichang, Shichang, Xiaowang, Xiang, Duwei, Duhu, and Qiequ.
In the first month of each year, the leaders of various tribes held a small gathering in the court of Chanyu and held a spring festival.
Every May, a grand gathering is held in Longcheng to worship their ancestors, heaven and earth, ghosts and gods.
Every autumn, when the grass is yellow and the horses are fat, a meeting is held in the hoof forest to count the population and livestock for tax collection.
Their law is that anyone who draws a knife and wounds someone within one foot shall be put to death; a person who commits the crime of stealing shall have his entire family's property confiscated; if he commits a crime, his bones shall be crushed for minor crimes, and his bones shall be crushed for serious crimes.
The length of jail time is no more than ten days, and there are only a few prisoners in jail across the country.
Chanyu walked out of his tent every morning and worshiped the rising sun; in the evening he worshiped the moon.
Their rules for sitting up are: the elder is on the left, facing north.
Advocate Wu said and Ji said.
Their funeral customs are: they are buried with coffins, gold and silver, and clothes, but there are no tombs, tomb trees, and mourning systems. If a Chanyu dies, dozens or hundreds of his close concubines will be buried.
The Huns often raised troops to fight according to the waxing and waning of the moon. They attacked when the moon was full and retreated when the moon was waning.
When they fought, whoever beheaded the enemy would be rewarded with a jug of wine, and the spoils captured would belong to him, and the captured people would be made slaves.
Therefore, when they fight, everyone moves forward bravely for the sake of gain, and is good at luring the enemy into the encirclement and then annihilating them.
Therefore, when they pursue interests, they fly together like birds; when they are in danger and collapse, they fall apart and disperse.
Whoever transports the deceased back during the war will own all the property of the deceased.
Later, Maodun Chanyu conquered the northern countries of Hunyu, Qushe, Dingling, Gekun, Xinhua and other countries.
At that time, the Hun nobles and ministers all admired Mo Dun and thought he was wise and talented.
At this time, the Han Dynasty had just settled down and moved King Han Xin to Daidi and established the capital in Mayi.
The Huns laid siege to Mayi, and Han Xin surrendered to the Huns.
After the Xiongnu got Han Xin, they led their troops southward across Juzhu Mountain, attacked Taiyuan, and reached the city of Jinyang.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally led his troops to fight against the Xiongnu.
It happened that the winter was very cold and it snowed heavily. Two or three out of ten soldiers had their fingers frozen off, so Mao Dun pretended to be defeated and escaped to lure the Han army.
The Han army pursued Mao Dun, but Mao Dun hid his elite soldiers and exposed the old and weak soldiers. So the Han army totaled 320,000 men, most of whom were infantry, and pursued Maodun northward.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty first led his troops to pursue Pingcheng, but not all the infantry arrived. Maodun sent more than 300,000 elite cavalry to besiege Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty at Baishan Mountain in Pingcheng for seven days. The desert army inside and outside could not provide food and grass to each other.
The Huns' cavalry was all white horses in the west, green horses in the east, black horses in the north, and red horses in the south.
Emperor Gao sent an envoy to secretly send generous gifts to the Min clan, and the Men clan said to Mao Dun: The coaches of both sides should not be forced.
Now that we have obtained Han territory, Shanyu you will not be able to live here after all.
Besides, the Lord of Han is blessed by the gods, so Shanyu, you should consider it carefully.
Mao Dun had made an appointment with Han Xin's generals Wang Huang and Cao Li, but the troops of Wang Huang and Bao Li were still late in arriving. Mao Dun suspected that they were conspiring with the King of Han, so he listened to Ban's words and opened a corner of the encirclement.
So Emperor Gao ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully, nock their arrows, face outwards, and rush out from the corner of the siege. Finally they joined the army, and Mao Dun led his army to retreat.
The King of Han also retreated with his troops and sent Liu Jing to make peace with the Xiongnu.
After that, Han Xin became the general of the Xiongnu, and together with Zaili, Wang Huang and others, he repeatedly betrayed the Han-Hungarian peace treaty and invaded Daijun, Yanmenjun and Yunzhongjun.
Soon after, Chen Xi rebelled against the Han Dynasty and conspired with Han Xin to attack Dai County.
The Han Dynasty sent Fan Sha to lead his troops to attack them, and recovered Daijun, Yanmenjun, Yunzhongjun and other counties without leaving the frontier to fight.
At that time, the Xiongnu generals of the Han Dynasty led their troops to surrender many times, so Maodun often came and went to invade Dai.
Emperor Gaozu was deeply worried, so he sent Liu Jing to send the royal daughter to the Que family who pretended to be a princess and sent a certain amount of silk floss, silk silk, wine and food to the Xiongnu every year.
Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled against the Han Dynasty and led nearly 10,000 of his associates to surrender to the Huns. They came and went to harass the people in the Shanggu Yisu area until the death of Emperor Gaozu.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun gradually became arrogant and even wrote a letter and sent an envoy to Empress Lu, saying: I am a lonely and helpless monarch. I was born in a humid swamp and grew up in a vast place where cattle and horses are grazed. I have been to the border many times, hoping to visit the Central Plains.
Your Majesty, you are an independent king, but you are also lonely and helpless, living alone.
We two monarchs were very unhappy and had nothing to entertain us. I hope that both of us can exchange what we have for what we don’t have.
Empress Dowager Lu was very angry after reading the letter. She summoned the prime ministers Chen Ping, Fan Sha and Ji Bu to discuss killing the Xiongnu envoys and sending troops to attack the Xiongnu.
Fan Sha said: I am willing to lead an army of 100,000 people to attack the Xiongnu territory.
Empress Lu asked Ji Bu, and Ji Bu said, "You can kill Fan!"
In the past, when Chen Xi rebelled in Dai, there were 320,000 Han soldiers, and Fan Sha was the general. At that time, the Huns besieged Emperor Gao in Pingcheng, but Fan Sha could not break through the siege.
People all over the world sang: It’s too hard under a flat city!
After seven days without food, the soldiers could not even draw their bows. Now the sound of people singing is still in their ears, and the wounded people have just stood up. But Fan Sha wants to shake the world, and talks nonsense about bringing a hundred thousand soldiers to the Xiongnu to go on a rampage. This is deceiving the emperor in person.
Moreover, these ethnic minorities are like animals. They don’t deserve to be happy when they hear good things about them, and they don’t deserve to get angry when they hear bad words. Queen Mother Lu said: That's fine.
So he ordered the great emissary Zhang Ze to write a letter in return, saying: The Chanyu has not forgotten our ruined country and has rewarded us with letters. We are very afraid.
After retiring from the imperial court, I thought to myself, I am old and weak, my hair and teeth have fallen out, and I can't walk steadily. Shanyu has heard others say wrong things, and it is not worth the humiliation that Shanyu has lowered and insulted me.
Our country has done nothing wrong and should be forgiven.
I have two chariots and eight horses for you to ride on.
When Mao Dun received a reply, he sent an envoy to apologize and said: "We have never heard of the etiquette of the Central Plains. Fortunately, Your Majesty forgives us."

summary:
The Xiongnu, whose ancestor Chunwei was a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern border of China. They raised horses, cattle, sheep, and exotic livestock, migrating with water and grass without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements. Men learned archery from youth, and in adulthood served as armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized the strong, who ate well while the elderly ate leftovers. Upon a father's death, a son married his stepmother; upon a brother's death, the surviving brother married the widow. They had no naming taboos or posthumous titles.

The text traces the history of interactions between the Xiongnu and various Chinese dynasties, beginning with the Zhou dynasty. The Zhou declined, and Rong and Di tribes frequently attacked. King Xuan of Zhou attacked the Xiongnu, but later King You was killed by Quan Rong. Qin and Jin became powerful, with Duke Mu of Qin conquering Xirong and Duke Wen of Jin expelling Rong Di. During the Warring States period, Qin, Zhao, and Yan built walls to resist the Xiongnu. Qin Shihuang sent Meng Tian to attack the Xiongnu, recovering land south of the Yellow River and building the Great Wall. After Meng Tian's death, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman.

Touman's son, Maodun, trained his cavalry with a signaling arrow, killing his father and establishing himself as Chanyu. Maodun defeated the Donghu, drove away the Yuezhi, and annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan, becoming powerful with over 300,000 warriors. The Xiongnu's official structure included left and right kings, generals, and governors, with the Chanyu's surname being Luanti. They held annual meetings, had strict laws, and practiced burial with concubines. Maodun later conquered northern countries, and the Han dynasty, under Emperor Gao, made peace through marriage alliances and tribute.

During the reign of Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun sent an insulting letter, but she responded diplomatically. Emperor Wen continued marriage alliances, though the Xiongnu frequently invaded. The Xiongnu Chanyu wrote to the Han, claiming to have conquered the Yuezhi and other states, and sought peace. The Han agreed, sending gifts. After Maodun's death, his son Laoshang Chanyu succeeded. A eunuch, Zhongxing, defected to the Xiongnu and taught them Chinese customs, advising against adopting Han ways. He argued that Xiongnu simplicity and mobility were strengths, while Han complexity led to internal strife.

Under Emperor Wu, the Han attempted to ambush the Xiongnu at Mayi but failed, leading to open conflict. The Han sent multiple campaigns, with generals like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing achieving victories, killing tens of thousands of Xiongnu and capturing their kings. The Xiongnu suffered heavy losses and fled north. The Han also expanded into the Western Regions, isolating the Xiongnu from allies. Despite peace negotiations, the Xiongnu continued border raids. The Han detained Xiongnu envoys, and the Xiongnu retaliated.

Later, the Xiongnu faced internal strife and external attacks from Dingling, Wuhuan, and Wusun, leading to decline. The Han sent multiple expeditions, further weakening the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu Chanyu sought peace, but the Han demanded the prince as a hostage, which the Xiongnu refused. The Xiongnu continued to raid, but the Han's military campaigns and alliances with Wusun and other states devastated them. The Xiongnu suffered from famine, disease, and livestock losses, with many tribes rebelling or surrendering to the Han.

The text concludes with the Xiongnu's continued decline, internal power struggles, and eventual submission to the Han. The Xiongnu Chanyu's lineage and official titles are recorded, highlighting their complex relationship with the Han dynasty, marked by periods of war, peace, and tribute.
