Han Chang and Zhang Meng saw that the Xiongnu tribe was prosperous and that all the animals under the fortress had been hunted down. The Chan Yu was strong enough to defend himself and was no longer afraid of Zhizhi.
Han and Zhang heard that many Xiongnu ministers advised the Shanyu to return to the north where they originally lived. They were worried that it would be difficult to govern the Xiongnu after they returned to the north. Han Chang and Zhang Meng made an alliance with the Shanyu, saying: From now on, the Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu are one family, and they are not allowed to deceive or attack each other from generation to generation.
When theft or robbery occurs, both parties must report to each other, punish the thief, and compensate for the lost property; when an enemy invades, they must send troops to rescue each other.
If either the Han Dynasty or the Xiongnu dared to betray the alliance first, they would be willing to accept the punishment of heaven.
Let their descendants and descendants suffer disaster just as the covenant says.
Han Chang, Zhang Meng, Hu Hanxie Chanyu and his ministers climbed to Nuoshuishu Mountain of the Xiongnu and killed the white horse. The Chanyu used a path knife and a golden plow to stir the wine mixed with the blood of the horse, and used the head of the Yuezhi King whom the old Shanyu had killed as a wine cup, and they drank the blood wine together as an alliance.
Han Chang and Zhang Meng reported this matter after they returned to the Han Dynasty. The ministers discussed the matter and said: "The Chanyu has promised us that we are willing to serve as a vassal to protect the frontier. Even if we want to return to the north, it will not pose a threat or hindrance to the Han Dynasty."
Han Chang and Zhang Meng acted without authorization and made an alliance with the Xiongnu on the future of the descendants of the Han Dynasty. This allowed the Chanyu to use evil words to tell heaven, humiliating the Han Dynasty and damaging the prestige of the country. This must not be done.
Envoys should be sent to appeal to Heaven and dissolve the former alliance with the Xiongnu.
Han Chang and Zhang Meng were ordered to go on a mission, which was not proper and their crimes were extremely treasonous.
The emperor alleviated their sins and issued an edict that Han Chang and Zhang Meng could be punished for their crimes but not terminate their alliance with the Huns.
Later, Huhanxie Chanyu finally returned to the court of Chanyu in the north. The Huns gradually surrendered to him, and the country settled down.
Chanyu Zhizhi killed the envoy of the Han Dynasty, and he knew that he had failed the Han Dynasty. He also heard that Huhanxie was getting stronger, so he was worried about being attacked and wanted to move to a distant place.
It happened that King Kangju was besieged by the Wusun Kingdom many times at this time. He discussed with his Xihous that the Xiongnu was a powerful country and the Wusun Kingdom had always been subordinate to it. Now that Zhizhi Chanyu was living in exile, he could welcome him and live in Shubu. The two sides worked together to defeat Wusun and let Zhizhi Chanyu become king there. In this way, there would never be worries from the Huns.
So he sent an envoy to Jiankun to tell Chanyu Zhizhi these words.
Chanyu Zhizhi was often worried about being invaded by Huhanxie and resented Wusun. He was very happy when he heard King Kangju's plan, so he joined forces with Kangju and led the army to the west.
Kangju also sent nobles with thousands of camels, donkeys, and horses to meet Zhizhi.
Many of Zhizhi's tribe died of cold and starvation on the road, and finally only 3,000 people were left to reach Kangju.
Later, the governor Gan Yanshou and the deputy governor Chen Tang sent troops to Kangju to kill Zhizhi Shanyu. These are recorded in the biographies of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang.
After Zhizhi Chanyu was killed, Huhanxie Chanyu was happy and scared, and wrote to the Emperor Xuan: I often hope to go to see His Majesty, but it is actually because Zhizhi Chanyu lives in the west, and I am worried that he will attack me with Mercer, so I cannot go to see the Emperor.
Now that Wai Mu has been convicted and killed, I hope that I can be allowed to come to the court to pay my respects.
In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie Chanyu came to the Han Dynasty again. The Han Dynasty treated him with the same courtesy and rewards as before, and increased the rewards of clothes, brocade, silk, and thick silk and cotton, which were twice as much as in the Huanglong year.
Chanyu himself said that he would like to be the son-in-law of the Han Dynasty to get closer to the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty gave Shanyu Wang Qiangzi Zhaojun, a good woman who was a servant of the harem, as his wife.
The Chanyu was very happy and wrote to the emperor, saying that he was willing to protect the Han Dynasty frontier from Shanggu west to Dunhuang and pass it on forever. He asked the emperor to withdraw the officials and soldiers guarding the border fortress so that the emperor's subjects could rest and recuperate.
The emperor handed the matter over to the ministers for discussion, and the ministers in charge thought it was very convenient.
Langzhong Linghou should be familiar with the affairs of the frontier fortress and thought that he could not agree to the Huns like this.
Emperor Mo Yuan asked him why, and Hou Ying replied:
Since the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the Xiongnu have been very violent and unruly, invading the frontiers. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, they suffered particularly serious consequences.
I heard that our northern border fortress reaches all the way to Liaodong. Outside is the Yinshan Mountains, which is more than a thousand miles long from east to west, with lush vegetation and many animals. This place was originally the place where Maodun Shanyu relied on. He made bows and arrows here, trained his troops, and came in and out of Yinshan to harass us. Yinshan was the garden where they raised animals.
When Emperor Xiaowu arrived, he sent troops to attack and capture the area and drove them to the north of the desert.
Border fortresses were built, sentry roads were built, cities outside the fortress were built, troops were stationed there, and then the border settled down a little.
The terrain to the north of the desert is flat, with sparse vegetation and mostly sand and gravel. When the Xiongnu invaded, there was nothing to hide from. From the frontier fortress to the south, it is difficult to travel on the mountain roads.
The old people on the border said that since the Huns lost Yinshan, they never failed to cry every time they passed by.
Now if we withdraw the soldiers guarding the border fortress and show them such good favorable conditions, this is the first thing we cannot do.
Now, the emperor, you are so generous and generous, and your kindness is like heaven covering the Huns. The Huns came to kowtow and proclaim themselves vassals because of the help of the Han Dynasty.
The temperament of those Huns is to be humble and submissive when in danger, and to be arrogant and rebellious when they are strong. This is their nature.
Some time ago, the Han Dynasty had abolished the cities outside the wall and reduced the number of troops stationed at checkpoints and key roads. The number now was enough to wait and see the situation and send beacon communications.
The ancients said that we should be prepared for danger in times of peace, and the Han army cannot withdraw again. This is the second rule.
In the Central Plains, there is education in etiquette and justice, and there are punishments as a means of punishment, but some ignorant people still dare to break laws and prohibitions, not to mention the Chanyu, can he definitely prevent his tribes from violating the covenant?
This is the third article. From the beginning, China has attached great importance to building passes to control the princes. This is to cut off the unreasonable ideas of the ministers.
Building border fortresses and setting up garrison troops is not only to protect against the Huns, but also to protect those vassal states and surrenderers. Some of them were originally Huns. We are worried that they will miss their hometown and run away. This is the fourth article.
In modern times, the Western Qiang protected the Han Dynasty's frontiers and interacted with the Han Dynasty. Some officials and people, greedy for small profits, invaded and robbed other people's livestock, property, wives and children. This aroused the resentment of the Western Qiang people and rebelled against the Han Dynasty. This situation continued for generations.
Now that the border guard troops have been withdrawn, it will gradually lead to mutual insults and bullying. This is Article 5.
Many people who joined the army to fight against the Huns were lost there and never came back. Their descendants were very poor. Once they escaped, they followed their relatives and never came back. This is Article 6.
In addition, the slaves on the border fortress were very miserable, and many wanted to escape. I heard that the Huns were very good there, but the sentries were watching closely and there was nothing they could do.
However, there are still people who escape from the frontier fortress from time to time. This is Article 7.
Robbers and thieves are very cunning and often work in groups to commit crimes. If they are forced to escape from the northern pass, there will be no way to restrain and punish them. This is Article 8.
I am worried that the ministers who discussed this matter did not consider the whole situation carefully, and just wanted to reduce the number of slaves and guards based on the current situation and current calculations. Ten years later, within a hundred years, if there is an emergency, the city gates have been destroyed, and the checkpoints and roads have been obliterated, people will have to be dispatched to station and repair. Things accumulated over several generations cannot be repaired at once. This is Article 9.
If we withdraw our guarding soldiers and reduce the number of lookout posts, the Chanyu will think that he is defending the border fortress for the Han Dynasty and feels that he has made great contributions to the Han Dynasty, and unknown disasters will occur.
This will open the door for the Hungarians and weaken the stability of our country's defense force. This is Article 10 that cannot be done.
Therefore, this is not a superior strategy to keep the border fortress stable forever and control other minority countries.
After Hou Ying's reply was reported to the emperor, the emperor issued an edict saying: Stop discussing the lifting of border defenses.
He also sent the chariot and cavalry general Xu Jia to deliver an oral message to Shanyu, saying: Shanyu wrote a letter saying that he hoped that the Han Dynasty would withdraw the officials and soldiers guarding the northern frontier and let the Huns guard it for generations.
Shanyu advocates etiquette and justice. It is very good for you to think about the people. This is also a long-term solution for Xianxun and reconciliation. I appreciate it very much.
There are bridges on all four borders of our country. It is not only to prevent the outside of the fortress, but also to prevent the bandits and bad guys in our country from running rampant and running out of the border to harm the Huns. Therefore, the laws are stated to punish the public.
I have understood Shanyu's intention, there is no doubt about it.
I was worried that Shanyu would blame me for not withdrawing the border defense, so I sent General Xu Jia, the commander of the chariot and cavalry, to tell Shanyu the reason.
Shanyu thanked him and said: I don't understand the emperor's profound thoughts, but thanks to the emperor sending ministers to tell me, I am very grateful.
At first, King Zuo Yi Zhizi made suggestions for Huhanxie Chanyu and asked him to submit to the Han Dynasty. Later, the Huns finally settled down because of this.
Later, some people slandered Yi Zhizi for showing off his achievements and being often unhappy and dissatisfied. Hu Hanxie became suspicious of him.
King Zuo Yi Zhizi was afraid of being killed, so he led more than a thousand of his men to surrender to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty made him the Marquis of Dingguannei, with a settlement of 300 households, and allowed him to wear the seal and ribbon of the original king.
During the Jingning period, Hu Hanxie Chanyu came to the Han Dynasty to pay homage to the Emperor of Han, and met King Zuoyi Zhizi. The Chanyu apologized and said: "My lord, you planned for me at the beginning. Your kindness and kindness have made us Xiongnu peaceful and peaceful to this day. These are all due to you, lord. How can I forget your kindness?"
It was my fault that I lost the favor of the prince and made the prince leave and no longer want to stay in the Huns. These are all my fault.
Now I want to talk to the emperor and ask you to return to the court of the Huns.
Yi Zhizi said: Shanyu relied on the arrangement of heaven to surrender to the Han Dynasty, and the Huns were at peace. Shanyu is a blessing from the emperor. What credit can I have!
Now that I have surrendered to the Han Dynasty, if I return to the Xiongnu, I will be half-hearted.
I am willing to be your envoy and stay in the Han Dynasty. If you ask me to go back, I will not obey your order.
The Chanyu made repeated requests, but in the end he could not change King Zuoyizhizi's mind, so he returned to the Huns.
Wang Zhaojun's title was Ninghu Pi, and he gave birth to a son named Yitu Zhiyaoshi, who was established as King Youri Zhu.
Hu Hanxie Shanyu reigned for twenty-eight years and died in the second year of Jianshi.
At first, Huhanxie Chanyu doted on the two daughters of King Huyan, brother of Zuoyi Zhizi.
The eldest daughter is Zhuanquban, and she gave birth to two sons. The eldest son is named Qiemoche, and the second son is named Nangzhiyasi.
The second daughter of King Hu Xian was of the Dapi family, and she gave birth to four sons. The eldest son was called Diao Tao Mogao, and the second son was named Qie Mixu, both of whom were older than Qie Moche. The two younger sons were Xian and Le, both younger than Nangzhi Yasi.
There were also more than ten other sons born to Pi.
Zhuanquban's family was noble, and Moche was also favored by Shanyu.
Hu Hanxie Shanyu was about to die of illness and wanted Qie Moche to succeed him. His mother, Zhuan Qupi, said: The Xiongnu have been in chaos for more than ten years, and this situation cannot be cut off like hair. Fortunately, with the help of the Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu was able to stabilize. The country has not been peaceful for a long time, and many people have been killed and injured in wars.
Moreover, Mo Che was still young and the people failed to rally to him. If he were to take the throne, it would probably put the Xiongnu in danger again.
Zuo Tiya and I are sisters, and we have the same sons. It would be better to have Tao Mogao carved as a chanyu.
Tai Laoya said: Although Mu Moche is young and has ministers to help handle national affairs, if he abandons the noble now and supports the humble, I am afraid there will be trouble in the future.
Huhanxie Chanyu finally followed Zhuanquban's suggestion and sculpted Tao Mogao as Chanyu and made a covenant to pass the country to his younger brother in the future.
After the death of Hu Hanxie, Diao Tao Mogao came to the throne and was called Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu.
After Fuzhu case Ruo Qian Chanyu came to the throne, he sent his son Youzhi to King Lu'er, Xiexie Tu Nuhou, to serve the emperor in He, and appointed the emperor. Mi Xu was appointed King of Zuo Xian, Danhuang Nuo was appointed King of Zuo Guli, and Nangzhi Yasi was appointed King of You Xian.
In the Fuzhu case, Shanyu also took Yudan Donkey as his wife and gave birth to two daughters. The eldest daughter Yun was the second, and the second daughter was the second.
In the first year of Heping, the Chanyu sent Yougao Lin Wang Yixiemoyan and others to the Han Dynasty to pay tribute and participate in the first month worship.
At the end of the dynasty, the Han Dynasty sent envoys to escort Yixiemoyan and others to Pufan.
Yixiemo made a speech: I want to surrender to the Han Dynasty. If you don't agree to this, I will commit suicide. Why won't I return to the Huns?
The envoys from the Han Dynasty came back to report, and the emperor handed over the matter to the ministers for discussion. Some people said that those who surrendered should be accepted as before.
Gu Yong and Yilang Duqin, Guanglu officials, believed that since the founding of the Han Dynasty, the Huns had repeatedly invaded and harmed the border areas, so we set up a generous reward of titles and money to attract the Huns who surrendered.
Now the Chanyu is very submissive, professing vassalage to the Han Dynasty, and is listed as a vassal state in the north. He sends envoys to the Han Dynasty to pay homage and congratulate him without any second thoughts. Therefore, the Han Dynasty should treat those who surrender differently from the past.
Now, since we have accepted the loyal invitations and tributes from Shan Yu, but also accepted their defected ministers, doing so is greedy for one person, but losing the loyalty of the people of the country, politely supporting the guilty ministers, and abandoning the monarch who admires benevolence and righteousness.
If the Shanyu has just ascended the throne and wants to get close to the Han Dynasty and come to pay homage to the Han Dynasty, but does not know what the attitude of the Han Dynasty is, whether it is good or bad for him, and secretly sends Yixie Moyan to pretend to surrender to see what the future will be like, if we accept the surrender, it will destroy the good deeds and be virtuous. Unfortunately, the Shanyu himself alienated us and did not get close to the officials on our frontier; or someone used rhetorical tactics to create discord between us. If we accepted the surrender, we would have fallen into his trap, allowing the Huns to accuse us of doing something wrong and blame us for being wrong.
This is actually the root cause of whether our border is safe or not. The starting point of whether the army is dispatched or not cannot be taken lightly.
It is better not to accept those who surrender, to show the Xiongnu our trust that is as unchangeable as the sun and the moon, to suppress the deceitful and evil plots, and to protect those who surrender to the Han Dynasty. This is a convenient strategy.
The emperor listened to their answers and followed their advice.
He also sent Wang Shun, the general of Zhonglang, to inquire about the situation of the surrendered people.
Ixiemo said: That's because I'm crazy and just talking nonsense.
The Han Dynasty sent him back.
After Yixe Moyan returned to the Huns, his official position remained the same as before, and he was not allowed to see the Han envoys again.
The next year, Fuzhuzong Shanyu wrote to the emperor, hoping to come to pay homage to Emperor Mo in the first month of the fourth year of Hehu. After that, he went to the court to pay homage. The Han Dynasty additionally rewarded him with 20,000 pieces of brocade silk and 20,000 catties of thick silk cotton. Other rewards were the same as during the Jingning period.
Yu Shanyu of Fuzhu reigned for ten years and died in the first year of Hongjia.
Passing the throne to his younger brother Ji Mi Xu, he was called Souxie Ruoqiandanzi.
After Souxie Chanyu came to the throne, he sent his son Quliu Sihou, King of Han of Zuozhudu, to serve the emperor of Han Dynasty, and appointed Qiemoche as King Zuoxian.
After eight years of Souxie Chanyu's reign, in the first year of Yuanyan, he went to the Han Dynasty to participate in the first dynasty in the first month of the second year. He set out from the Xiongnu and died of illness before he entered the frontier fortress.
His younger brother Qie Moche succeeded to the throne as Chanyu, making him Cheya Ruoqian Chanyu.
After Cheya Shanyu came to the throne, he sent his son Youyu Tuqiu Shan King Wuyi to serve the Han prince in the court. Appointed Nangzhi Yasi as King Zuoxian.
Cheya Shanyu reigned for four years and died in the first year of Suihe.
He passed the throne to his younger brother Nang Zhiyasi, who was called Wuzhu Liuruo Qian Chanyu.
After Wu Zhuliu Chanyu ascended the throne, he made his son Le, who was born to the second Ban family, the king of Zuoxian, and his son Yu, who was born to the fifth Ban family, to be the king of Youxian. He sent his son Wu Qianyasi, the slave king of Yougu, to serve the emperor of the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty sent Zhonglang General Xiahou Fan and deputy captain Han Rong as envoys to the Xiongnu.

Someone persuaded Wang Gen: "The Xiongnu has a steep and tall mountain close to the Han Dynasty, facing Zhangye County. Strange wood grows on the mountain, and it is very suitable for making arrow poles with the addition of bird feathers." If we can get it, we can enrich the frontiers, the country can benefit from expanding the land, and you, the general, can show your merits and pass them on forever.
Wang Gen told the emperor about the benefits of asking for this mountain. The emperor also wanted to ask Shanyu for this mountain, but he was afraid that the Huns would not agree and would undermine the emperor's dignity.
Wang Gen told Ding Xia and Wu Fan of the emperor's intention, and asked him to request Shan Yu in his personal capacity.
When Xiahou Fan arrived at the Xiongnu, he waited for an opportunity to give advice to Shanyu and said: I saw that the Xiongtan was connected to a steep mountain and entered the Han Dynasty. Facing Zhangye County, there were three captains of the Han Dynasty leading hundreds of soldiers stationed on the tomb. It was very cold and hard, and they had to work hard for a long time on duty.
Chanyu, you should write to Emperor Mo to donate this land and give it directly to the border officials. This will save two captains and hundreds of soldiers guarding the Han Dynasty, in order to repay Emperor Mo's kindness to the Xiongnu. The reward from the Han Dynasty must be very generous.
Shanyu asked: Is this an edict from the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, or is it a request from the envoy?
Xiahou Fan said: This is the emperor's will, but I just came up with a good idea for your sake.
The Chanyu said: Emperor Xiaoxuan and Emperor Xiaoyuan took pity on my father, Huhanxie Chanyu, and promised to return the area north of the Great Wall to the Xiongnu.
The place they want is where King Wen Outuo lives. I don't know what grows there or what it looks like. Please let me send an envoy to find out.
Xiahou Fan and Han Rong returned to the Han Dynasty.
Later, the two of them went on an envoy to the Xiongnu. When they arrived there, they asked the Chanyu for the place.
Shanyu said: According to legend, my father and brother have been there for five generations, and the Han Dynasty did not want this place. It was only when I became Shanyu that they asked for it. Why?
I have sent someone to ask King Wenqiuo that the vassal states in the west of the Xiongnu rely on the wood from this mountain to make tents and vehicles. Besides, it is a place left by the Huns ancestors, and I dare not lose it.
After Xiahou Fan returned, he was promoted to Taiyuan Prefect.
The Chanyu sent an envoy to the Han Dynasty to submit a letter to the emperor, telling the emperor about Xiahou Fan's request for land from the Xiongnu.
The Emperor of the Han Dynasty issued an edict to inform the Shanyu: Xiahou Fan requested land from the Shanyu without permission under the pretense of the emperor's edict, and should be executed according to law. After two amnesties, Xiahou Fan is now moved to the prefect of Jinan and will not be allowed to station in a place facing the Xiongnu.
The next year, Shan Yu's son who served in the court died and was buried with the Huns.
The Chanyu also sent his son Zuoyu, the king of Qiu Shan, Jiliu Kun to serve in the court.
In the second year of Emperor Ai's reign, the Wusun concubine Beiyuan Yinxihou's tribe invaded the western border of the Huns, robbed cattle, sheep and livestock, and killed many Huns.
After the Chanyu heard about it, he sent Wu Yiling, the leader of Zuo Danghu, to lead 5,000 cavalry to attack Wusun. He killed hundreds of people, plundered more than 1,000 people, and drove back the cattle and sheep.
Bei Yuanyi was frightened and sent his son Chulu to serve as a hostage to the Huns.
Shanyu accepted and reported the situation to the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent Ding Yelin, the lieutenant general, and Wei Gongchengyin, the deputy captain, on an envoy to the Xiongnu to blame the Chanyu and tell him to send back Bei Yuanzhang's son who was a hostage.
Chanyu accepted the order and put the people back.
In the fourth year of Jianping, Shanzi wrote a letter hoping to participate in the imperial court in the first month of the fifth year.
Emperor Ai was ill at that time, and some ministers said that the Huns coming from the upper reaches of China would bring disaster. Since the Huanglong and Jingning years, every time the Chanyu came to China to worship, a relative of the emperor would die.
The emperor felt very embarrassed and asked the ministers for their opinions on this matter. The ministers also believed that allowing Shanyu to come to worship would only be a waste of money, so they could not agree to Shanyu's request for the time being.
Shan Yu's envoy said goodbye and wanted to go back to the Huns. Before he left, Yang Xiong, a man from Huangmen, wrote to the emperor to advise him:
I heard that the way of governing a country discussed in the "Six Classics" advocates governing before there is chaos; military strategists advocate defeating the enemy before there is a battle.
The truths of these two statements are very subtle, but the fundamental principles for handling national affairs cannot but be observed.
Now I have submitted a letter requesting to see His Majesty, but His Majesty refuses to allow it and refuses. I foolishly believe that the Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu will have conflicts from now on.
Originally, even the Five Emperors could not make those ethnic minorities in the north surrender, and the Three Kings could not effectively control them. Therefore, it was obvious that we could not cause rifts in our relationship.
I dare not go too far, so please allow me to quote examples from the Qin Dynasty to illustrate: Qin Shihuang's strength and Meng Tian's might commanded more than 400,000 armored men, but they did not dare to peek into the Xihe River and only built the Great Wall as a boundary.
Just when the Han Dynasty was just established, more than 300,000 troops were besieged in Pingcheng due to the sacred power of Emperor Gaozu, and some people went without food for seven days.
At that time, Gaozu was surrounded by many clever and fickle counselors and courtiers who were good at planning. However, Gaozu and others were able to escape in the end, but it was through a method that people don't want to say.
In addition, Empress Gao was also very angry with the Huns and summoned ministers to discuss it in the court. Fan Yan asked to lead 100,000 cavalry to attack and rampage the Huns. But Ji Bu said: Fan Sha should be killed for so foolishly flattering the queen!
So the ministers made adjustments and wrote replies according to the words of the letter. Then the conflict with the Xiongnu was resolved and the worries that threatened China were calmed down.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Huns invaded the northern border, and Tan Ma went as far as Yonggan Spring. The capital was shaken. The emperor sent three generals to lead their troops to station in Zouliu, Jimen, and Bashang respectively to guard against the Huns. The Huns retreated a few months later.
Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne and set up an ambush in Mayi to lure and annihilate the Xiongnu. He sent Han Anguo to lead an army of 300,000 to intercept at the border. The Xiongnu found out and retreated. The Han Dynasty wasted money and the army's hard work was in vain. Not a single Xiongnu was seen, let alone a Chanyu!
Later, Emperor Xiaowu thought deeply about the country's plans and planned grand and long-term plans, so he mobilized hundreds of thousands of troops in large numbers, led by Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, and fought for more than ten years.
So the Han army crossed the Xihe River, crossed the desert, broke through Zhenyan, attacked the court of Shan Yu, and reached the farthest point of the Huns. They chased and annihilated the fleeing enemies, set up altars to worship heaven on Langjuxu Mountain, and worshiped earth on Guyan Mountain. They returned only after reaching Hanhai, capturing hundreds of Xiongnu princes and nobles.
From then on, the Huns were shocked and frightened, and even more urgently demanded peace with the Han Dynasty. However, they still refused to surrender to the Han Dynasty.
Besides, was the previous emperor willing to spend countless amounts of money and food to let innocent people serve as soldiers in the army, and only then was he happy to attack the north of Langwang?
He believed that there would be no long-term peace and happiness if he did not work hard once, and he would not have long-term peace if he did not spend a lot of time and effort to defeat the Huns. Therefore, he had the heart to dispatch millions of troops to attack the Huns, risking the same danger as a hungry tiger pulling out its teeth; just like filling up the ravines of Mount Lu, he used the money and grain accumulated in the national treasury to fight without regrets.
In the early years of this century, the Xiongnu became unruly again! He wanted to plunder the Wusun Kingdom and endanger the Han Dynasty princess who was married to Nabu, so the Han Dynasty sent five generals and 150,000 cavalry to attack the southern Xiongnu, and Changluo Hou led 50,000 Wusun cavalry to attack the western Xiongnu.
At that time, the people and horses from all walks of life achieved very little. They just showed their strength and showed that the desert army was as powerful as thunder and wind.
Although he left empty-handed and returned empty-handed, he still injured two generals.
Therefore, if the Huns in the north do not surrender, China will never be able to sit back and relax.
During the reigns of Yuankang and Shenjue, the emperor was divine, the country was in great rule, and his benevolence was widespread. However, civil strife broke out among the Xiongnu, and five khanyus fought for the throne. King Chu, Huhanxie khanyu, led his troops to return to a civilized country, and bowed down to the emperor of the Han Dynasty. However, the emperor still only implemented a policy of win-over and softness, and believed that it was still inappropriate to treat them as ministers and slaves.
From then on, the Xiongnu Chanyu would not refuse anyone who wanted to come to worship, and would not force anyone who did not want to come.
Why?
The Huns were rebellious by nature, with tall bodies, and relied on their own strength. It was difficult to educate them with kindness, but they were easily accustomed to do evil. Their stubbornness was difficult to yield, but their docility was rare and valuable.
Therefore, when they did not surrender, they did not hesitate to send troops to distant places to attack them. The whole country used financial resources to support the war, killed and injured soldiers, captured the city, and defeated the enemy.
In the past, we have conquered the cities of Dayuan, set foot on the fortress of Wuhuan, visited the military fortress of Guzhen, trampled on Dangjie's place, cut off the military flags of Korea and Vietnam, and conquered these places. The time it took to conquer these places was no more than ten days and a half months, and no more than half a year.

At this time, Xu Dang died of illness. Wang Mang married his concubine's daughter Lu Luren to Hou An Gongshe as his wife. He was very respectful and doting to her. After all, his purpose was to send troops to support him as a chanyu.
At that time, Han soldiers attacked and killed Wang Mang, and Yun and She were also killed.
In the winter of the second year of Gengshi, the Han Dynasty sent Zhonglang General Gui De Hou Sa and Da Sima Hujun Chen Zun as envoys to the Xiongnu. They awarded the Shanyu the original style of seal and ribbon and the seal ribbon to everyone below the prince. At the same time, all the surviving relatives who had followed Yunhe Xudang to the Central Plains and were still alive were sent back to the Xiongnu.
Chan Yuyu was very arrogant and said to Chen Zun and Wang Sa: The Xiongnu and the Han Dynasty were originally brothers. There was civil strife between the Xiongnu and Emperor Xiaoxuan. He helped Huhanxie Chanyu ascend the throne, so we surrendered to the Han Dynasty to show our respect.
Now there is civil strife in the Han Dynasty, the throne was usurped by Wang Mang, and we the Huns also sent troops to attack Wang Mang, leaving his border empty, making the people of the Han Dynasty riot, and people thinking about Han, so that Wang Mang finally failed and the Han Dynasty was revived. It was also thanks to the strength of our Huns that the Han Dynasty should respect us again!
Chen Zun and Shanyu refused to argue, but Shanyu always insisted on this statement.
In the summer of the next year, Wang Sa and Chen Zun returned to the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the Red Eyebrow Army happened to invade Chang'an, but Liu Xuan failed.
Praising: "The Book of Books" warns the barbarian minorities to disturb the Central Plains, "The Book of Songs" praises "the brave people to face the Rong and Di", "Spring and Autumn" says that the rulers with Tao are also supported by the ethnic minorities on all sides. The barbarians and Di have been harming the Central Plains for a long time.
Therefore, since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, those ministers with loyal advice and far-reaching strategies have worked hard to make plans and debate in the court how to deal with the Yi Di?
During the reign of Emperor Gaozu, there were Liu Jing, under Empress Lu, there were Fan Sha and Ji Bu, under Emperor Xiaowen, there were Jia Yi and Chao Cuo, and under Emperor Xiaowu, there were Wang Hui, Han Anguo, Zhu Maichen, Gongsun Hong, and Dong Zhongshu. People insisted on their own opinions, some were similar and some were different, but in summary, they were two opinions.
The gentry and Confucian scholars insisted on making peace with the Xiongnu, while the armored warriors insisted on conquering and attacking the Xiongnu. They all only focused on the beneficial or harmful paranoia of a certain period, but did not thoroughly examine the history of the Xiongnu from beginning to end.
From the establishment of the Han Dynasty to the present, many epochs have passed, more than the "Spring and Autumn Annals". The relationship between the Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu has not only advocated civil rule and implemented peacemaking, but also used force to conquer and fight. There are twists and turns, different changes, maybe I am strong, or you are weak, the status is opposite, so we can talk about the details.
In the past, it was Liu Jing who advocated peace with the Huns.
At that time, the world had just stabilized, and the Han Dynasty had just experienced the disaster of being besieged by the Xiongnu in Pingcheng. Therefore, the emperor followed Ya Ta's suggestion, discussed peace with the Xiongnu, and gave gold, silver, grain, and cotton to the Chanyu, hoping to stabilize the border.
When Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao were emperors, they obeyed the Huns and did not dare to disobey. However, the Huns' invasions did not reduce or stop at all, and the Chanyu became even more arrogant.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, he and the Xiongnu traded with each other, opened border markets, married Han princesses to singles, and increased the amount of property given to the Xiongnu, spending a thousand gold each year. However, the Xiongnu repeatedly violated the peace treaty, and the Han Dynasty's borders were repeatedly invaded.
Therefore, when Emperor Wen reached middle age, he became angry and strong. He personally put on military uniforms, mounted war horses, and led the strong and brave warriors from the six counties to practice horseback archery and battle formations in Shanglin Garden. He mobilized the best soldiers and generals from all over the world and stationed them in Guangwu City. Emperor Wen asked Feng Tang about generals and expressed his longing for famous officials in ancient times.
Therefore, it is very clear that there is no benefit in making peace with the Xiongnu.
Dong Zhongshu witnessed with his own eyes the events of the Fourth Dynasty of the Early Han Dynasty, but he still wanted to abide by the past regulations and greatly increased the agreement with the Xiongnu.
He believes that benevolence and righteousness can move gentlemen, and interests can inspire greedy villains. Like the Huns, you cannot use preaching to make them understand benevolence and righteousness. You can only use generous profits and money to make them happy, and swear an oath to heaven with them and form an alliance with them.
Therefore, we should give them more gold and silver to eliminate their violent aggression, swear an alliance with them in heaven to make the alliance between the two parties stronger, and let Shan Yu's beloved son come to the Han Dynasty as a hostage to hinder his determination. Even if the Xiongnu wanted to move around the frontier and attack the Han Dynasty, they could not do anything without worrying that they would lose money and profits, deceive God, and kill their beloved son.
The money collected to send gifts to the Xiongnu is not comparable to the military expenditures of sending out three armies to conquer the Xiongnu; the effectiveness of a strong city to defend the Xiongnu is no different from the effectiveness of sending honest people to enter into an alliance with the Xiongnu. But doing so can make the people who are guarding the border in the border city take off their ammonium armor and relax, so that their children can eat safely. Isn't it very convenient for the people of the world to stop the Huns' cavalry from peeking at the Great Wall of the Han Dynasty, and to stop the use of swords, guns, bows and arrows in the Central Plains?
However, if you examine Dong Zhuqian's remarks and compare them with the facts and situations at the time, you will know that what he said was out of date at the time, and also incorrect for later generations.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, although he gained a lot from attacking the Xiongnu, the number of soldiers and horses that died was roughly the same as what was gained. Although the wilderness south of Hetao was opened up and Shuofang County was built, more than 900 miles north of Zaoyang were abandoned.
The Xiongnu people often surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and the Chanyu always detained the Han Dynasty envoys in retaliation. Their unruly character was still the same, so how could they be willing to hand over their beloved sons to the Han Dynasty as hostages?
This is where Dong Zhongshu's remarks were inappropriate for the time.
If the Huns cannot be used as hostages, the marriage covenant will be a blank piece of paper. This will repeat Emperor Xiaowen's past mistakes and encourage the Huns' endless fraud.
We do not select military officers capable of defending the border to garrison the cities on the border; we do not build pavilions and roads to prepare means of defending the border fortress; we do not sharpen our halberds and prepare our bows so that we can have something to rely on, but we continue to exact levies from the people, travel far away to bribe the Xiongnu, and deprive the people of their property to give to our enemies.
Isn’t it too much to believe false good words, keep a promise of useless covenants, and expect the Huns not to invade?
summary:
After Huhanxie Chanyu returned to his court, he ended the war and appointed his brother Hutuwusi as King Zuoguli. He also ordered the killing of King Youxian. That winter, Dulongqi and King Youxian supported Zhu Wanglian as a rival chanyu and attacked Huhanxie, who was defeated and fled. Tuqi Chanyu then took control, appointing his sons as kings. The following autumn, Tuqi Chanyu stationed troops to guard against Huhanxie. Internal strife escalated when King Hujie slandered King Youxian, leading to his execution. This caused King Hujie to flee and declare himself Chanyu, followed by others, resulting in five rival chanyus.

Tuqi Chanyu attacked Cheli Chanyu and Wujii Chanyu, both of whom fled to join Hujie Chanyu. Tuqi then sent forces east and west, but Huhanxie Chanyu attacked and killed over 10,000 of Tuqi's troops. Tuqi retaliated with 60,000 cavalry but was defeated and committed suicide. Huhanxie Chanyu's general Dan Quli surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Huhanxie returned to his court with only tens of thousands of followers. Runzhen Chanyu and Zhizhi Chanyu emerged, with Zhizhi killing Runzhen and attacking Huhanxie, who was defeated.

King Zuoyi Zhizi advised Huhanxie to surrender to the Han Dynasty for stability. Despite opposition from ministers who valued Xiongnu martial traditions, Huhanxie agreed and led his people south, sending his son as a hostage. The Han emperor received Huhanxie with great honor, granting him titles, gifts, and troops for protection. Huhanxie requested to stay near the Han border for defense. The Han provided food and military support. Zhizhi Chanyu, meanwhile, moved west, attacking Wusun and other tribes, establishing his capital in Jiankun.

Emperor Yuan succeeded and Huhanxie requested aid due to poverty. The Han sent grain. Zhizhi, resentful of Han support for Huhanxie, killed a Han envoy. The Han sent envoys to escort Huhanxie's son back and made an alliance with him, pledging mutual defense. However, Han officials criticized the alliance as unauthorized. Huhanxie eventually returned north, stabilizing his rule. Zhizhi, fearing Han retaliation, moved further west and allied with Kangju, but was later killed by Han forces. Huhanxie, relieved, requested to visit the Han court again.

In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie visited the Han court and received generous gifts. He requested to become a Han son-in-law, and Emperor Yuan gave him Wang Zhaojun as a wife. Huhanxie offered to defend the Han border from Shanggu to Dunhuang and asked for the withdrawal of Han border troops. The emperor consulted officials, and Hou Ying argued against withdrawal, citing ten reasons: the strategic value of the Yinshan Mountains, the Xiongnu's untrustworthy nature, the need to prevent internal crime and defections, and the risk of future emergencies. The emperor agreed and declined Huhanxie's request.

King Zuoyi Zhizi, who had advised Huhanxie to submit to Han, later fell under suspicion and surrendered to Han. Huhanxie later apologized and asked him to return, but he refused. Huhanxie died after 28 years, succeeded by his son Diao Tao Mogao as Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu, following the advice of his mother Zhuanquban to avoid instability. The new chanyu appointed his brothers as kings and continued relations with Han. Subsequent chanyus maintained ties, sending sons as hostages and visiting the Han court.

During the reign of Wuzhuliu Chanyu, Han envoy Xiahou Fan requested land from the Xiongnu, but the chanyu refused, citing ancestral rights. The Han emperor punished Xiahou Fan. Later, conflicts arose over Wusun raids and Wuhuan tax issues. Wang Mang, after usurping the Han throne, changed the Xiongnu seal and imposed new regulations, causing resentment. The Xiongnu resumed border raids. Wang Mang's military campaigns failed, leading to chaos. The Xiongnu chanyu died, and his successor Xian sought peace with Han but continued raiding. Wang Mang's attempts to control the Xiongnu through titles and gifts ultimately failed, and the border remained unstable.

After Wang Mang's death, the Han Dynasty restored relations with the Xiongnu, but the chanyu remained arrogant. The historian concludes that peace treaties and military campaigns both had limitations, and the Xiongnu's nature made lasting peace difficult.

Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County, Cambodia.
His grandfather had been farming for generations, and when he came to Kuangheng, he liked to study. Because his family was poor, Kuangheng worked as a hired worker to pay for his expenses.

Kuang Heng was awarded the title of "Jia Ke", but because he failed to pass the "Jia Ke" regulations, he was only appointed as Taichang's storyteller, and later he was appointed as "Pingyuan County Literature".
Many scholars wrote letters recommending that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and was unparalleled in the world. He should be appointed as a literary scholar and go to the capital as an official. The younger generation were willing to follow Kuang Heng to study in Pingyuan County. Kuang Heng should not be an official far away from the capital.
The emperor handed this matter over to Prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and Shaofu Liang Qiuhe for questioning. Kuang Heng answered with the righteousness of the Book of Songs, which was very profound and brilliant.
Xiao Wangzhang reported that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and his lectures were passed down from a teacher's perspective, which can be viewed.
Emperor Xuan did not make much use of Confucian scholars, so he sent Kuang Heng back to his original place.
However, after the crown prince saw Kuang Heng's correct question, he secretly appreciated him.
When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, a relative of Leling Marquis Shi Gao was appointed as the Great Sima Cavalry General and concurrently as Minister, with former general Xiao Wangzhi as his deputy.
Xiao Wangzhi was a famous Confucian and the emperor's mentor. The emperor valued him and made great contributions in recommending talents.
Shi Gao, on the other hand, had no interest in political affairs and only had a reputation, which created a gap between him and Xiao Wangzhi.
Yang Xing, the magistrate of Chang'an County, persuaded Shi Gao: "The general assists in political affairs with relatives, and his reputation is noble and unparalleled in the world. However, in everyone's discussion, the good reputation and honor are not all attributed to the general. Why?"
Because they heard that generals cannot recommend virtuous and talented people.
As the shogunate of the shogunate, everyone in the world looks up to and admires him, but the people recommended by the shogun are just private guests and the children of wet nurses.
The general ignored everyone's comments because of favors and did not know that there was anything wrong with him. However, as long as one person discusses it in private, it will spread throughout the world.
Although you are rich and noble, the scholars do not praise you. It is like wearing a pure white fox fur coat, which is flashy.
The ancients were very taboo about such things, so they deigned to take the trouble to find worthy people as their own duty.
The Sutra says: Because wise men are rare, you cannot wait for wise men to arrive when doing things; because food is rare, you cannot wait for food to arrive when you are full.
There are more serious situations than this kind of waiting. Pingyuan Literature Kuang Heng's talents and wisdom were more than enough, and his attainments in classics were outstanding. Because he had no chance of promotion in the imperial court, he had to follow the selection and supplementary documents and move to a place far away from the capital to serve as an official.
If the general summons Kuangheng to serve in the shogunate, scholars all over the world will definitely follow him, let him participate in discussing political affairs, and recommend him to the court based on his expertise, and he will definitely become a pillar of the country. If you do this for everyone to see, your reputation will spread throughout the world.
Shi Gao thought Yang Xing was right, so he appointed Kuang Heng as the historian of Cao and recommended him to the emperor. The emperor asked him to be a doctor, and later he was promoted to a doctor and served concurrently as Shizhong.
At this time, disasters such as solar eclipses and earthquakes occurred. The emperor asked about the relationship between these changes and political gains and losses. Kuangheng Shangshu said:
I heard that the rituals of the five emperors were different, the politics and religion of the three kings were different, and the people's customs were very different. The reason is that the times have changed.
His Majesty has personally extended his holy virtues and opened the way to peace in the world. He has shown mercy to ignorant officials and people who have violated legal prohibitions. He has granted amnesty every year to allow the people to correct their behavior and reform themselves. It is indeed a blessing to the world.
I saw that after the amnesty, the cunning, treacherous and evil behavior has not decreased. Today I am amnesty, tomorrow I break the law, and then I am jailed again. This is probably to persuade the people to miss the point.
Generally speaking, to educate the people, as the "Book of Filial Piety" says: state morality and righteousness to them, publish the standards of good and bad to them, observe their mistakes and clarify the rules of conduct, so that actions will lead to harmony, and comfort will lead to peace and quiet.
Nowadays, the customs are greedy for wealth and disdain for benevolence and righteousness, fond of sensuality, advocating luxury, despising integrity, indulging in debauchery, and losing order. The natal families of distant wives and concubines are more important than the relatives of the same surname. The kindness between relatives is weak, and the trend of forming parties through marriage is prevalent. They act on each other's side and sell themselves for glory.

Confucius said: How can we govern a country with courtesy and humility?
The imperial court is the pillar that supports the world.
If the ministers and officials follow the etiquette and are respectful and modest to each other, then the people will not fight each other; if the ministers love benevolence and are willing to give charity, then the people will not use violence; if the superiors advocate high moral integrity, then the people will pay attention to their conduct; if the superiors are gentle and tolerant, then the people will love each other.

Long life and good health to protect my descendants. I heard that between heaven and earth, the qi of yin and yang interact with each other, forming disasters or auspiciousness, and good and evil evolve with each other. Your Majesty feared God's warning, cherished and mercied the people, and was very frugal. Let the moral ethos be carried forward in the capital and the good reputation spread abroad. After that, education can be achieved and etiquette and humility can become a common practice.
The emperor was very happy after hearing what he said, and promoted Kuang Heng to the rank of Guanglu Doctor and Prince Shaofu.

At the same time, because Fu Zhaoyi and his son King Dingtao were favored by the emperor, they surpassed the queen and crown prince.
Kuang Heng went to Shu again and said:
I've heard that the key to a country's peace and security lies in examining one's own intentions.
Generally speaking, the main task of an emperor who accepts the mandate of heaven is to establish a business and continue the power of the country. The main purpose of a monarch who inherits the system of the previous kings is to inherit and carry forward the virtues of the previous kings and praise the achievements of the previous kings.

The Book of Songs records this incident.
Zhou Song. "Min Yu Xiaozi" said: I miss the virtues of our late kings Wen and Wu, inherit and carry them forward, and all the ghosts and gods come to the court.
Creation means that King Zhou Cheng often thought about the achievements of his ancestors and moved the ghosts and gods of heaven and earth to bless him and help him govern the country. Daya. "King Wen" said: Always miss your ancestor and inherit and carry forward his virtues.

With "National Style." The reason for starting with "Guanyong" is to study human emotions and understand the way of human relations; the reason for starting with "Guanyi" and "Yi for Marriage" is to lay the foundation and nip problems in the bud.

Zhou Nan. "Guan Sui" chapter says: A lady who is quiet and dignified is the good spouse that a gentleman pursues.
