The imperial edict was issued to bury Sicheng Hou together with him to the south of Gucheng Temple in Qingdao, and to set up a cemetery, a family home and a Changcheng Palace, and to abolish the Sicheng Garden in Zhuo County.
Two people in the Wang family were granted the title of marquis. Wang Wuqi's son Wang Jie became the general of the Great Sima Cavalry, while Wang Wu's son Wang Shangguan became the prime minister. They all have their own biographies.
Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the mother of Wuhu.
Her father's name was Jiang Luxuan, a native of Dandan. When he was young, he worked for the king of Lu Yi.
Later, he followed Gen Xi to Ju Xingxuan and mistakenly put another man's saddle on his own horse. After he was discovered, the officials revealed that he had committed theft while traveling with the emperor. He should be sentenced to death. There was an edict ordering him to be castrated in the Jamshi room and avoid death.
Later he became a eunuch.
When Shangguan Jie rebelled, Guanghan searched for evidence of the crime. Shangguan Jie's palace house contained thousands of ropes that were several feet long and could be used to tie people up. They were packed in a sealed basket. Guanghan didn't notice it, but others saw it when they went there.
Guanghan was convicted again and was sentenced to prison and fined as hard labor. He was sent to Yeting and later became a miser.
At this time, Emperor Xuan was adopted in Yeting and was called the great-grandson of the emperor. He lived in the same official residence as Guanghan.
Zhang He, the order of Yeting, was originally a minor official in the family of Prince Wei. After the defeat of the crown prince, he was sentenced to castration. Because of his old kindness, he treated the emperor's great-grandson very well.
When the emperor's great-grandson grew up, Zhang He planned to marry his granddaughter to him.
At this time, Emperor Zhao had just turned twenty and was eight feet two inches tall.
Zhang He's younger brother Zhang Anshi served as the right general and worked with General Huo to assist Emperor Zhao. When he heard Zhang He praising the emperor's great-grandson and wanting to marry his granddaughter to him, he became angry and said: The emperor's great-grandson is a descendant of Prince Wei. He is fortunate enough to be supported by the court as a commoner. It is enough. Don't mention marrying his granddaughter to him.
Therefore Zhang He had to give up.
At that time, Xu Guanghan had a daughter named Pingjun, who was fourteen or fifteen years old. She was supposed to be the daughter-in-law of the concubine Ling Ouhou.
When it was time to get married, Ouhou's son died.
Her mother asked a fortune teller to tell her that she would be rich and wealthy, and her mother was secretly happy.
Zhang He heard that Xu Shifu had a daughter, so he held a banquet for him. When he was drinking well, he said, "The emperor's great-grandson is close relatives with the emperor. Even if his talents are inferior, he can still be a Marquis of Guannei. You can betroth your daughter to him as your wife."
Guangmo agreed. The next day, Pingjun's mother heard the news and was very angry.
But Guangmo hired someone to act as a matchmaker again, so he married his daughter to the emperor's great-grandson, and gave birth to Emperor Yuan a year later.
A few months later, the emperor's great-grandson was appointed emperor, and Lord Xu Ping was named Qizai.
At this time, General Huo also had a young daughter who was not married and was related to the Empress Dowager.
The ministers proposed to appoint a queen, and they all preferred General Huo's daughter, but no one spoke.
Emperor Xuan issued an edict to find an old sword he had owned when he was poor and humble. The ministers understood the emperor's intention and petitioned to appoint Xu Jianzi as queen.
After the queen was appointed, Huo Guang believed that the queen's father Xu Guangmo was a man who had been castrated and was not suitable for managing the place. It took more than a year before he named him Lord Changcheng.
Huo Guang's wife Huo Xian wanted to make her little daughter noble, but she couldn't think of a way.
The next year, Queen Xu fell ill when she was about to give birth.
The female doctor Chun Yuyan had a close relationship with the Huo family and once went to the palace to serve the queen.
Chunyu Yan's husband was appointed as a household guard in Yeting, and he said to Chunyu Yan, "Go and say goodbye to Mrs. Huo, and ask for the position of Anchi Supervisor for me."
Chunyu Yan told Huo Xian.
Huo Xian had an idea. He backed away and said to Chunyu Yan, "Young master, please ask me for something. I also want to ask you for help. Is that okay?"
Chunyu Yan said: There is nothing wrong with what Madam said!
Huo Xian said: The general has always loved his youngest daughter Chengjun. He hopes that she will be noble and wants to trouble the young husband.
Chunyu Yan said: What does this mean?
Huo Xian said: A woman's childbirth is a big event, and she will escape death.
Now that the queen is about to give birth, we can take this opportunity to throw poison to get rid of her, and Chengjun can become the queen.
If you are willing to work hard to accomplish this, I am willing to share the wealth with you, young husband.
Chunyu Yan said: The medicine was prepared by many imperial doctors, and others had to taste it first. How could it be poisoned?
Huo Xian said: "It depends on your ability, young master." The general is in charge of the world, who dares to say anything about him?
I will protect you in times of crisis, but I'm afraid you don't mean it.
Chunyu Yan thought for a long time and said: I am willing to do my best.
She pounded the aconite into powder and brought it into Changding Palace.
After the queen gave birth, Chun Yuyan took out aconite and mixed it with the imperial physician's pills, and served the queen to take them.
After a while, the queen said: I have a headache. Is the medicine poisonous?
Chunyu Yan replied: No.
The queen became even more depressed and restless, and finally died.
Chunyu Yan left the palace and met with Huo Xian. Huo Xian comforted her but did not dare to thank her heavily.
Later, someone wrote a letter accusing the doctors of being useless in treating the queen, so they were imprisoned in Shao County to expose their treasonous crimes.
Huo Xian was afraid that the matter would be exposed, so he told Huo Guang everything about the incident, and said: Since this matter has been done wrongly, you should find a way to prevent the officials from questioning Chunyu Yan.
Huo Guang was stunned after hearing this and could not say a word.
Then he went to petition the emperor not to hold Chunyu Yan responsible anymore.
Queen Xu died three years after she was made queen. She was named Queen Gongai and was buried in Dunan, also known as Duling South Garden.
Five years later, she made her son the crown prince, and made the crown prince's grandfather, Changchengjun Xu Guanghan, the Marquis of Ping'en, granting him special advancement.
Four years later, Xu Guangmo's two younger brothers were also granted the title of Xu Shun as Bowang Marquis and Xu Yanshou as Lecheng Marquis.
There are three people in the Xu family who have been granted the title of marquis.
After Xu Guanghan's death, Mi was given the title Marquis of Dai. He had no sons, so the title was discontinued.
He was buried next to the South Garden, and three hundred households were set up. The chief of the garden and the chief minister were set up to guard and sweep in accordance with the law.
Emperor Xuan granted Xu Yanshou the title of Chief Chariot and Cavalry General to assist in government affairs.
After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he also named Xu Yanshou's middle son Xu Jia the title of Marquis of Ping'en. After inheriting the title of Marquis Dai, he also became the Great Sima Cavalry General.
Empress Huo of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the daughter of Sima General Bolu Hou Huo Guang.
Queen Huo's mother, Huo Xian, sent Chunyu Yan to kill Queen Xu secretly. Then she made Chengjun's wedding clothes, prepared the tools for entering the palace, and persuaded Huo Guang to send his daughter to the palace. Sure enough, Chengjun was appointed queen.
At the beginning, Empress Xu was from a humble background, and her time as empress was very short. Her servants, drivers, and attire were all very frugal. She went to Changle Palace to see the Empress Dowager every five days, and personally held a food table to offer food to the Empress Dowager, as a filial piety to her granddaughter-in-law.
When I arrived at Queen Huo, I also followed the old practices of Queen Xu. However, the Queen Mother was the daughter of Queen Huo's sister, so she was always cautious and respected her very much.
The queen's chariots and horses were very impressive, and she rewarded her subordinates with tens of millions of dollars, which was very different from that of Queen Xu.
Emperor Xuan also doted on her very much, and Queen Yuzu was the only one who was good at doting on her.
In the third year after Queen Huo was enshrined, Huo Guang passed away.
Another year later, Emperor Xuan appointed Queen Xu's son as the prince, and granted Chang Chengjun the title of Ping'enhou.
Huo Xian was so angry that he couldn't eat and even vomited blood. He said, "This is a child born in the common people. How can he be made a prince?"
If the queen gives birth to a son, can she only become the king?
She also instructed Queen Huo to poison the prince.
The queen summoned the prince many times to give him food, but the nanny always tasted it first, and the queen hid poison but could not use it.
Later, the murder of Queen Xu was gradually leaked out, and Huo Xian conspired with his son-in-law and his children. The plot was leaked, and Emperor Xuan had the Huo family wiped out.
He also sent a secretary to give the queen a document, saying: The queen has evil intentions and evil intentions. She conspired with her mother, Huo Xian, the wife of Hou Xuancheng and Bo Lu, to harm the prince. She has no kindness as a mother and is not suitable to worship the ancestors anymore, let alone accept the destiny. well!
He should retreat to the cold palace and return his seal and ribbon.
Queen Huo reigned for five years and was deposed and took refuge in Zhaotai Palace.
Twelve years later, when Huo was asked to move to Yunlin Pavilion, she committed suicide and was buried east of Kunwu Pavilion.
At first, Huo Guang and his brother Huo Qubing, the cavalry general, were both granted the title of marquis for their merits. Because of Huo Guang, Emperor Xuan made Huo Qubing's grandson Huo Shan and Huo Shan's younger brother Huo Yun both marquises. There were four people in the Huo family who were granted the title of marquis.
Emperor Xiaoxuan and Queen.
Queen Wang's ancestors were given the title of Marquis of Guannei due to their merit during Emperor Gaozu's reign, and they moved from Pei to Changling. The title was passed down to the Queen's father, Wang Fengguan.
Wang Fengguan liked cockfighting when he was young. Emperor Xuan met him many times when he was among the people and got to know each other.
Fengguang has a teenage daughter. Whenever she wants to get married, the other party always dies, so she has not been able to get married for a long time.
After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he summoned Fengguang's daughter into the harem and was gradually promoted to Jianxian.
At this time, Hua Jianzai, the mother of King Guantao, Zhang Jiandan, the mother of King Xian of Huaiyang, and Wei Jianzai, the mother of King Xiao of Chu, were all deeply favored by Emperor Xuan.
After Queen Huo was deposed, Emperor Xuan took pity on Prince Xu who lost his mother very early and was almost killed by the Huo family. Therefore, he selected people in the harem who were usually cautious and had no children.
Since Queen Wang became the queen, she was rarely summoned by the emperor and was not favored.
Emperor Xuan made the queen's father Wang Fengguan the Marquis of Qiongcheng.
In the sixteenth year after Queen Wang was enthroned, Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, and Queen Wang became the empress dowager.
Emperor Yuan granted the Queen Mother's brother Wang Shun the title of Marquis of Anping.
Two years later, Wang Fengguang died. Mi was named Gonghou and was buried south of Changmen. A cemetery and 200 households were set up, and Chang Cheng was ordered to guard it according to the law.
After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, the Queen Mother became the Empress Dowager.
He also granted the title of Marquis of Guannei to Wang Jun, the younger brother of the Empress Dowager, and granted him the title of a thousand households.
Two members of the Wang family were named marquis, and one was named Guannei marquis.
Wang Shun's son Wang Zhang and Wang Zhang's cousin Wang Xian both served as generals.
At that time, Emperor Cheng's mother was also named Wang, so the Empress Dowager was known as Empress Dowager Qiongcheng.
Empress Dowager Qiongcheng reigned for forty-nine years. She died in her seventies in the first year of Yongshi. She was buried with Emperor Xuan in Duling, called Shuyuan.
Wang Fengguan's grandson Wang Xun broke the law and was deprived of his title.
During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the Empress Dowager of Emperor Cheng issued an edict, saying: The Queen Mother of Emperor Xiaoxuan is my mother-in-law. I deeply miss her upbringing and teaching, and I will keep her kindness in my heart.
However, the title of Gonghou of Qiongcheng was abolished. I felt very sorry for him, so I named Wang Jianhou, the great-grandson of Gonghou, as the Marquis of Qiongcheng.
This title was not abolished until Wang Mang.
summary:
Since ancient times, emperors who founded dynasties and monarchs who inherited thrones have relied not only on their own virtues but also on the help of their relatives. The rise of the Xia Dynasty was tied to the Tushan clan, while Jie's exile was due to Moxi; the Yin Dynasty's rise involved thieves and marries, and Zhou's demise came from favoring Daji; the Zhou Dynasty depended on Jiang Xi, Tairen, and Taisi, and King You was captured by Rong Di because of his lewd relationship with Guo Si. Thus, the "Book of Changes" begins with the hexagrams "Qian" and "Kun," "The Book of Songs" starts with "Guan Ju," "Shangshu" praises Tang Yao for marrying his daughters to Yu Shun, and "Spring and Autumn" criticizes Duke Yin of Lu for his marriage. The relationship between husband and wife is a matter of human ethics, and marriage must be handled with caution. Only when music is harmonious can the four seasons be harmonious, and the changes of yin and yang create all things. People can carry forward the great road but cannot control destiny. The affection between spouses is paramount, and even a king or father cannot force his children to surrender. The love between husband and wife is joyful, but some cannot have children or have children who die young—this is destiny. Confucius rarely spoke of the Mandate of Heaven, probably because it was difficult to explain. Without understanding yin and yang, one cannot know life.

The Han Dynasty followed Qin titles: the emperor's mother was the empress dowager, his grandmother the grand empress dowager, his wife the queen, and concubines were called madam. Titles like Beauty, Beloved, Eighth Son, Seventh Son, Long Envoy, and Young Envoy existed. Under Emperor Wu, Jieyu, Xi'e, Suhua, and Chongyi were established, with fourteen levels under Emperor Yuan. Zhaoyi's salary rank equaled the prime minister, and her title equaled princes and kings. Jie Jie equaled a high official, nephew'e equaled two thousand stones, Ronghua equaled two thousand stones, beauty equaled two thousand stones, Bazi equaled Ganshi, Chunyi equaled Qianshi, the seventh son equaled eight hundred stones, a good man equaled eight hundred stones, the chief envoy equaled six hundred stones, a minor envoy equaled four hundred stones, the five senses equaled three hundred stones, and it was usually two hundred stones. Wujuan, Gonghe, Yuling, Baolin, Liangshi, and Yezhe equaled a hundred stones. Sons of upper and middle families equaled fighting for food with rank. Those below the five sense organs were buried outside Simamen after death.

Empress Lu of Emperor Gaozu was the daughter of Lu Gong, who married her to Gaozu when he was poor, seeing him as extraordinary. She gave birth to Emperor Hui and Princess Lu Yuan. Gaozu became king of Han and made Lu Gong the Marquis of Linsi. He later married Qi Ji of Dingtao, who gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao. Gaozu wanted to replace the kind-hearted prince with Ruyi, but ministers opposed it. Empress Lu, resolute and assisting Gaozu, had brothers Lu Ze and Lu Shizhi as generals. After Gaozu's death, Empress Dowager Lu imprisoned Qi Ji, shaved her hair, and made her pound rice. Qi Ji sang about her son being a king and she a slave, angering the Queen Mother, who summoned King Zhao to Chang'an. Emperor Hui protected him, but the Queen Mother poisoned King Zhao. She then mutilated Qi Ji, calling her a "human pig." Emperor Hui, horrified, fell ill and died seven years later. The Queen Mother, advised by Zhang Piqiang, appointed Lu Tai and Lu Chan as generals, consolidating Lu family power. She killed several of Gaozu's sons and named Lu family members kings. After her death, ministers Zhou Bo and Chen Ping executed the Lu family and established Dai Wang as Emperor Xiaowen.

Empress Zhang of Emperor Xiaohui was the daughter of Zhang Ao and Princess Lu Yuan. Empress Dowager Lu married her to Emperor Hui, hoping for a son. When she had none, the Queen Mother pretended she was pregnant and passed off a beauty's son as hers, killing the mother. After Emperor Hui's death, the prince became emperor but learned the truth and threatened revenge. The Queen Mother imprisoned and deposed him, then made Hengshan King Liu Hong emperor. After her death, ministers killed the Lu family and the non-biological sons of Emperor Hui, leaving only Queen Xiaohui, who died in the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign.

Gaozu's Bo Ji was the mother of Emperor Wen. Her father had an affair with Wei Lao, giving birth to Bo Ji. During the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself king, and Bo Ji entered his palace. Xu Fu predicted she would give birth to an emperor. Wei Bao betrayed Han, was captured, and Bo Ji was sent to the weaving room. Gaozu saw her and included her in the harem but did not favor her for over a year. She was close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier, who later laughed at her alliance. Gaozu pitied her, summoned her, and she became pregnant, giving birth to Emperor Wen. After Gaozu's death, Bo Ji, rarely favored, followed her son to Dai and became Queen Mother Dai. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, ministers, hating the Lu family, praised Bo Ji's kindness and made King Dai emperor. Bo Ji became Empress Dowager, and her brother Bo Zhao was named Zhihou. She died in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign and was buried in Nanling.

Empress Xiaowen Dou was the mother of Emperor Jing. She was elected to the palace during Empress Dowager Lu's reign. When maids were sent to princes, she wanted to go to Zhao but was mistakenly sent to Dai. In Dai, King Dai favored her, and she gave birth to Emperor Jing. After King Dai became emperor, Dou Ji was made queen. Her brother Dou Guang, sold as a child, was later found and rewarded. Dou Changjun and Dou Shaojun became humble gentlemen. Queen Dou later became blind. After Emperor Wen's death, she became Empress Dowager and granted Dou Guang the title of Marquis Zhangwu. During the rebellion of the seven states, Dou Ying was made a general and later Marquis Weiqi. Empress Dowager Dou liked Huang-Lao teachings and died in the sixth year of Yuanguang, buried with Emperor Wen.

Emperor Xiaojing and Empress Bo were the daughters of Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Bo. Empress Dowager Bo married her to Emperor Jing as crown prince. After becoming emperor, he made her queen, but she had no sons and was not favored. After Empress Dowager Bo's death, she was deposed and died four years later.

Empress Xiaojing Wang was the mother of Emperor Wu. Her father Wang Zhong died, and her mother Zang'er remarried. Zang'er, divining that her daughters would be noble, sent her eldest daughter to the crown prince's womb. Mrs. Wang dreamed of a sun entering her belly, giving birth to a son. After Emperor Jing became emperor, Mrs. Wang's son became prince. The eldest princess Liu Piao wanted to marry her daughter to the prince, but Li Ji refused. The princess then spoke ill of Li Ji and praised Mrs. Wang's son. Emperor Jing deposed the prince and made Mrs. Wang queen. Her son became Emperor Wu. Empress Dowager Wang reigned for twenty-five years and died in the third year of Yuanshuo, buried with Emperor Jing.

Empress Chen of Emperor Xiaowu was the daughter of the eldest princess. She was favored but had no children for over ten years. When Wei Zifu was favored, Empress Chen used sorcery, leading to her deposition and retreat to Nagato Palace. She died and was buried in Baling.

Empress Xiaowu Wei, also known as Zifu, was a singer of Princess Pingyang. Emperor Wu favored her, and she gave birth to a son, Liu Shi, who was made prince. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing became generals. Later, Empress Wei's appearance deteriorated, and she faced a witchcraft disaster. The prince killed Jiang Chong and raised an army but was defeated. Empress Wei committed suicide. After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, she was reburied with the posthumous title of Empress Mi.

Mrs. Li of Emperor Xiaowu was a singer. Her brother Li Yannian sang about a beauty, and Emperor Wu summoned her. She gave birth to King Ai of Changyi but died young. Emperor Wu mourned her and later gave her the title of Queen Xiaowu. Her brothers Li Guangli and Li Yannian were rewarded, but the Li family was later exterminated.

Gouyi of Emperor Xiaowu was the mother of Emperor Zhao. Emperor Wu summoned her, and she gave birth to Emperor Zhao after fourteen months. After Crown Prince Wei's defeat, Gou Yizi was made prince. Emperor Wu appointed Huo Guang to assist him. After Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, Gouyi was honored as empress dowager, and her father was named Marquis of Shuncheng.

Emperor Xiaozhao and Queen Shangguan were the granddaughter of Huo Guang. She became queen at six years old. Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An plotted to kill Huo Guang but were exposed and exterminated. The queen, young and uninvolved, was not deposed. After Emperor Zhao's death, she became empress dowager and died at fifty-two, buried with Emperor Zhao.

Shi Liangdi of Crown Prince Wei was the grandmother of Emperor Xuan. She gave birth to Liu Jin, who was killed in a witchcraft disaster. Emperor Xuan, as a baby, was saved and raised by Shi Gong. After becoming emperor, he honored Shi Liangdi as Mourning Queen.

Mrs. Wang Sun, Emperor Xuan's mother, was named Wengxu. She gave birth to Emperor Xuan but was killed in the disaster. Emperor Xuan honored her as Mourning Queen and found his grandmother Wang Yu, who was named Lord Boping. The Wang family had two marquises.

Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the mother of Wuhu. Her father Xu Guanghan was a eunuch. Emperor Xuan, as a great-grandson, married Xu Pingjun, who gave birth to Emperor Yuan. After becoming emperor, Xu was made queen. Huo Guang's wife Huo Xian had her poisoned to make her daughter queen. Queen Xu died and was named Queen Gongai.

Empress Huo of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the daughter of Huo Guang. After Queen Xu's death, she became queen. Huo Xian tried to poison the prince but failed. The murder was exposed, and the Huo family was wiped out. Queen Huo was deposed and committed suicide.

Emperor Xiaoxuan and Queen Wang were from a family with a marquis title. She became queen after Queen Huo's deposition, rarely favored. After Emperor Xuan's death, she became empress dowager and died in her seventies, buried with Emperor Xuan.

translation:
The queen of Emperor Xiaoyuan was the mother of Emperor Cheng.
The Wang family has a total of ten princes and five chief ministers. Among the relatives, no one is more prosperous than their family.
Queen Wang's relatives have their own biographies.
Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of Ping Enhou Xu Jia, the general of the Great Sima Chariot Cavalry.
Emperor Yuan mourned the death of his mother and mourned the murder of the Huo family for a short period of time in her reign. He specially selected Xu Jia's daughter to be betrothed to the crown prince.
When Mrs. Xu first entered the crown prince's palace, the emperor sent his ministers and close associates from Huangmen to serve him. When these people came back, they told how happy the crown prince was. Emperor Yuan was overjoyed and said to his left and right: "Please pour some wine to congratulate me!"
Everyone on the left and right shouted long live.
After meeting for a long time, Concubine Xu gave birth to a son who died in infancy.
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he appointed Concubine Xu as empress. Empress Xu gave birth to another daughter, who also died in infancy.
At first, the queen's father, Xu Jia, had been appointed as a general in charge of carriage and cavalry to assist the government since the Yuan Dynasty. It had been eight or nine years.
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he named his uncle Wang Feng, Marquis of Yangping, the Great Sima General, alongside Xu Jia.
Du Qin believed that according to the old rules, the queen's father's status should be more noble than the emperor's uncle, so he advised Wang Feng: "The chariot general's status is extremely noble. General, you should respect him and do not go against his wishes."
Even small differences can lead to catastrophic hostility, so we must not be careless.
At that time, the glory of General Wei was greater than that of Gaihou. In modern times, older people often talk about it and hope that the general will consider it carefully.
Later, the emperor planned to appoint only Wang Feng, so he gave Xu Jiawen a letter saying: The general has a distinguished status and should not be burdened by his official position.
He was rewarded with two hundred catties of gold and established in the court with a special promotion position.
More than a year later, Xu Jia passed away and was given the title Gonghou.
Queen Xu was intelligent by nature and good at writing official scripts. From the time she became the crown prince to the time she was appointed queen, she was often favored by the emperor. Women in the harem were rarely summoned by the emperor.
The empress dowager and the emperor's uncles were worried that the emperor would have no heirs. At this time, disasters occurred repeatedly. Liu Xiang, Gu Yong and others all reported that the fault was in the harem.
The emperor thought they were right. Therefore, the expenses for the Queen's Palace and Yeting were reduced.
The queen went to the court and said:
I came from a poor family with a poor diet, and I was young, ignorant, and ignorant of the truth. I was fortunate enough to be able to leave a commoner's home and serve His Majesty in the harem.
Thanks to your majesty's wrong love, I am in the position of queen that I should not have earned. However, I cannot keep myself clean and fulfill my duties. I have always violated laws and regulations and undermined the system. Even though I was sentenced to exile, it was not enough to justify my crime.
So the edict was read out in the Changqiu period of Renyin: The queen should follow the etiquette and laws, dress her carriages and horses, take the property from the official office, make useful items, and reward her relatives and families, all in accordance with the old practices before Emperor Xiaoyuan.
I secretly thought to myself that since I became the Queen, the rewards for my family have never exceeded the system. Every time I discuss the decision with Your Majesty, Your Majesty can verify everything.
Nowadays, times are different, and the system will also change. Increases and decreases complement each other. As long as it does not exceed the customization of the Han family, it is difficult to achieve complete consistency in details.
Can Emperor Xiaoyuan and Emperor Xiaoxuan do the same thing?
Officials don't understand these principles. Once I get such an edict, I will make mistakes at every turn.
The current announcement that property cannot be taken from the official office probably means that Weiyang Palace is where His Majesty lives and does not belong to me, so I cannot take property from it.
But if you say that even the private government cannot obtain property from it, I don't understand it.
Since I was fortunate enough to be rewarded with a fief to support myself, that is, I got some wealth from it, what's wrong with it logically?
The Shao Book also said that the level of extravagance and frugality in making all practical items should be consistent with that before Emperor Xiaoyuan, but the officials must not understand this meaning, and they just asked me to make things exactly the same as in the old days.
If I plan to build a certain kind of screen and want to put it somewhere, or the old regulations do not allow it, or there is no precedent at all, the officials will definitely use the words in the Shao Book to restrict me.
These two things are indeed not feasible. I hope your Majesty will understand clearly.
Officials are jealous and vicious, and they must express themselves clearly.
I was in a distinguished position at that time, and they were still using trivial matters to control others. What's more, now they are even more excessive, and with such a shao shu, once they hold us hostage, how can we express our grievances?
Your Majesty saw that I was a queen and refused to give me any supplies.
If I don't get some wealth in my private life, what else can I rely on?
In the old days, the queen would often privately seize the cloths and carriage clothes of the attendants, claiming that they were given to be repaired by the imperial edict, and then take them back to her own possessions.
The people in the palace are secretly resentful, and I am ashamed to do things like making things.
In the old practice, bulls were used to sacrifice their grandparents. Both Daihou and Jinghou were able to use the Tailao ritual to sacrifice due to divine grace. Now we should also follow the old system. May your majesty have mercy on my family!
Now that the officials had just received the edict, they threatened to let the queen know this, and they could no longer take property from the private house as in the past.
They wanted to control me from the beginning, which was probably unnatural.
Now, if we only reduce the cost of carriages and horses, and do not take property from Weiyang Palace, but reward the maternal family according to the old practice, that will be fine.
The rest of the regulations are too pressing. What should we do?
My fate is not good, but it happens to be according to the old practice before Emperor Xiaoyuan. It was different then than it is now.
In the old days, the reward of wine and meat to a foreigner's family could only be decided by divination and petition.
Also, it turns out that Du Ling and Liang Meiren’s family are given one stone of wine and one hundred catties of meat every year. I think it is too little. Tian Bazi should be rewarded more than Liang Meiren.
There are many more such things, it is impossible to list them all.
I hope that I can be summoned by the emperor to tell you all these things in detail. Please let your majesty watch carefully!
Emperor Cheng followed the words of Liu Xiang and Gu Yong and answered the queen:
The emperor comforted the queen, I have heard everything you said.
The sun is the source of yang energy between heaven and earth, and is the most precious light in the sky. The appearance of a king is the dignity of a monarch.

The rest of the people were exterminated at worst or exiled at worst, alas!
If you use this as a reference when dealing with people, you can cope with various changes.
summary:
The Wang family, relatives of Emperor Xiaoyuan's queen, produced ten princes and five chief ministers, making them the most prosperous among all imperial relatives. Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of General Xu Jia. Emperor Yuan selected her for the crown prince after mourning his mother's death. She initially brought joy to the court, but her children died in infancy. After Emperor Cheng ascended, he appointed her empress and appointed his uncle Wang Feng alongside Xu Jia as co-regents. Du Qin advised Wang Feng to respect Xu Jia's superior status according to tradition. Eventually, the emperor appointed only Wang Feng and granted Xu Jia a special retirement with gold. Xu Jia died over a year later.

Empress Xu was intelligent and skilled in calligraphy, enjoying the emperor's favor for many years while other concubines were rarely summoned. When disasters occurred repeatedly, officials Liu Xiang and Gu Yong blamed the harem, leading to reduced expenses for the queen's palace. The empress petitioned the emperor, arguing that her rewards to her family had never exceeded proper limits, that changing times required adapting systems, and that officials were using vague edicts to restrict her unfairly. She requested clarification on what property she could obtain and asked to maintain traditional practices for sacrifices and family rewards. Emperor Cheng responded by citing numerous natural disasters and celestial omens—solar eclipses, white vapors, meteors, floods, earthquakes, and fires—as evidence that excessive yin energy from the harem was causing the royal family's lack of heirs. He urged the empress to practice frugality and virtue.

As Wang Feng dominated the government, three years of famine led critics to blame him, but Gu Yong continued faulting Empress Xu. The emperor's favor diminished, and the empress's sister Xu Ye was discovered cursing pregnant concubines and Wang Feng. The empress dowager had Xu Ye executed, and Empress Xu was deposed after fourteen years. Nine years later, Emperor Cheng showed mercy to the Xu family, allowing them to return to the capital. The deposed empress died after her sister's affair with Chunyu Chang led to a scheme to reinstate her. Chunyu Chang made inappropriate remarks in letters, and when reported, the emperor sent poison for her to commit suicide.

Ban Jiantun entered the harem when Emperor Cheng ascended and soon gained favor. When the emperor wanted her to share his chariot, she refused, citing ancient examples of wise monarchs accompanying ministers rather than favored women. The empress dowager praised her comparison to Fan Ji of ancient times. Ban Jiantun studied classical texts and always followed ancient etiquette. As the emperor's favor shifted to other concubines, she presented her maid Li Ping to the emperor, who became favored and was given the surname Wei. Later, the Zhao sisters rose to even greater prominence. When Zhao Feiyan falsely accused Empress Xu and Ban Jiantun of cursing the harem, Ban Jiantun defended herself by stating that if ghosts and gods were aware, they would not accept improper prayers, and if ignorant, prayers were useless. The emperor pitied her and rewarded her. Fearing the Zhao sisters' jealousy, she requested to serve the empress dowager in Changxin Palace, where she wrote poems lamenting her fate and describing her lonely life in the palace. After Emperor Cheng's death, she guarded his cemetery until her death.

Empress Zhao, originally a palace official in Chang'an, was abandoned at birth but survived. She learned singing and dancing at Princess Yang'a's house and was called Feiyan. Emperor Cheng visited incognito, became enamored with her, and brought her to the palace. Her sister also entered the palace, and both received unprecedented favor. After Empress Xu was deposed, the emperor wanted to make Zhao empress, but the empress dowager objected due to her low birth. Through Chunyu Chang's mediation, the emperor made Zhao's father a marquis, and Zhao became empress. Her sister became Zhaoyi and lived in unprecedented luxury. After more than a decade without children, they were bribed by King Dingtao's grandmother to support him as crown prince. Emperor Cheng died suddenly while in good health, and Zhao Zhaoyi was blamed. An investigation revealed that two other concubines had borne sons who were killed by Zhao Zhaoyi's orders. After Emperor Ai's death, Wang Mang reported to the empress dowager, who demoted and then deposed Empress Zhao, who committed suicide after sixteen years as empress.

Ji Bu, a native of Chu, was famous for his chivalry.
Xiang Yu asked him to lead troops, which put the king of Han in difficulty several times.
After Xiang Yu was wiped out, Emperor Gaozu spent a thousand taels of gold to purchase Ji Bu. Anyone who dared to harbor Ji Bu would be punished by the three tribes.
Ji Bu hid in Zhou's house in Puyang. Zhou said: The Han Dynasty is anxious to find the general and will come to my house to look for him soon. If you can listen to me, I will dare to find a way for you; if you can't listen to me, I am willing to commit suicide first.
Ji Bu agreed.
So he treated Ji Bu as a criminal, shaved off his hair, tied his neck with an iron ring, put on the prisoner's coarse cloth, and put him in a funeral car. Together with dozens of his slaves, he went to the Zhu family's home in Ludi and wanted to sell them.
Zhu Jiaxin knew that he was Ji Bu, so he bought it and placed it in a house in the countryside.
He himself went to Luoyang to see Xia Houying, the Marquis of Ruyin, and asked, "What crime did Ji Bu commit?"
As ministers, they were their own masters at the beginning and were in charge of their duties. Should all Xiang Yu's ministers be executed?
Now, the emperor has just brought peace to the world, and if he rewards a person with a thousand pieces of gold for his personal grudge, doesn't it show that he is not broad-minded?
Moreover, given Ji Bu's talents, the Han Dynasty captured him so quickly. Didn't this force him to flee north to the Huns and south to South Vietnam?
To hate strong men and force them to go to the enemy's country is not the lesson of Wu Zixu who helped Wu destroy Chu and dug up the tomb of King Ping of Chu and whipped his corpse.
Why don't you speak to the Emperor in a gentle manner?
Xiahou Ying knew in his heart that the Zhu family were famous chivalrous people, and guessed that Ji Bu was hiding in the Zhu family's home, so he agreed.
While serving Tian Guang, he indeed told the emperor what the Zhu family said.
Liu Bang then pardoned Ji Bu.
At that time, some elders in the society praised Ji Bu for his ability to turn toughness into softness, and the Zhu family became famous all over the world because of this incident.
Ji Bu was summoned by the emperor. Ji Bu expressed his gratitude and confessed his crime, and the emperor appointed him as a doctor.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Jibu Guan rose to Zhonglang General.
The Xiongnu Chanyu once wrote a letter to insult the Queen Mother Lu. The Queen Mother was very angry and summoned the generals to discuss countermeasures.
General Fan Kuai said: I am willing to lead an army of 100,000 to sweep across the Xiongnu.
The generals all obeyed Empress Lu's will and believed that Fan Kuai's statement was correct. Ji Bu said: Fan Kuai should be beheaded.
In the past, Emperor Gao led more than 300,000 soldiers and was surrounded by the Xiongnu in Pingcheng. At that time, Fan Kuai was also surrounded and surrounded.
How could Fan Sha be able to sweep away the Xiongnu with more than 100,000 men now? This is a lie to his face.
Moreover, the Qin Dynasty's use of troops against the Xiongnu led to an uprising by Chen Sheng and others.
A few days ago, the wounds of the war had not yet been healed, and Fan Kuai flattered him in person, hoping to shake the world.
At that time, everyone in the palace was frightened, and the Queen Mother immediately withdrew from the court and never discussed the attack on the Xiongnu again.
Later, Ji Bu became the governor of Hedong County.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone told Emperor Wen that Ji Bu was talented and virtuous, and Emperor Wen wanted to summon him to the capital to serve as a censor.
Others said that Ji Bu was very brave, but he drank too much and was willful, so he was not suitable for being a close minister.
Jibu arrived in the capital and stayed in a guest house for a month. After being summoned, he was sent back to his original county.
Ji Bu then advanced and said: "I am in Hedong, fearing that I will be punished for not doing my job well. Your Majesty summoned me to the capital for no reason. Someone must have falsely praised me and deceived Your Majesty."
Now that I have come, your Majesty has not given me any ministry, and has asked me to return to my original county. Someone must be slandering me.
Your Majesty summoned me because someone praised me, and sent me back because someone slandered me. I am worried that the knowledgeable people in the world will know the depth of your Majesty after hearing about this incident.
Emperor Wen was silent after hearing this, and said with shame: Hedong County is a county that I rely on as much as my thighs, so I specially summoned you!
Ji Bu resigned and returned to his original post as governor of Hedong County.
Cao Qiusheng, who was good at rhetoric, repeatedly sought power and was entrusted by others to collect money from the entrusters. He served the eunuch Tantan and others, and was friendly with Baochangjun, the uncle of Emperor Jing.
Ji Bu knew about it and wrote a letter to advise Baochangjun, saying: "I heard that Cao Qiusheng is not an honest and honest person. Don't associate with him."
Later, when Cao Qiusheng returned to his hometown, he wanted to ask Bao Changjun to write a letter to introduce him to Ji Bu.
Mr. Chang said: "General Ji doesn't like you, so don't go."
Keep asking for letters, and then hit the road.
Cao Qiusheng sent someone to deliver the letter first. Ji Bu was really angry and waited for Cao Qiusheng to come.
When Cao Qiusheng arrived, he bowed to Ji Bu and said, "There is a proverb in the Chu region: It is better to get Ji Bu's promise than to get a hundred catties of gold. How did you get such a good reputation in the Liang and Chu areas?"
Besides, you and I are both from Chu. Wouldn’t it be great if I could make your name known to the world?
Why are you so distant from me?
Ji Bu was very happy to hear this, and welcomed him into the inner room, where he stayed for several months and was treated like a distinguished guest. Before leaving, I prepared a generous gift for him.
The reason why Ji Bu's reputation grew bigger and bigger was because Cao Qiusheng promoted it to him.
Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin was the most brave in Guanzhong. He was respectful and cautious to others, and he was a chivalrous and righteous man. Scholars from thousands of miles around rushed to work for him.
Because he killed someone, he fled to the state of Wu and hid in Yuan Ang's house. He served Yuan Ang as an elder brother and regarded Guan Fu, Ji Fu and others as brothers.
Lieutenant Zhi did not dare to treat him disrespectfully as he was a Sima who was subordinate to the lieutenant.
Some young people often use his name to do things.
At that time, Ji Xin was famous for his bravery and Ji Bu for his promise.
Ji Bu's half-brother Ding Gong served as Xiang Yu's general. He once pursued Han Emperor Gaozu and trapped him west of Pengcheng.
During the hand-to-hand fight, the king of Han was in danger and turned back to Ding Gong and said: Are two wise men going to persecute each other?
Ding Gong then led his troops to withdraw, and the king of Han was able to escape.
After Xiang Yu's death, Duke Ding went to pay homage to Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu asked him to be paraded in the military camp and said: Duke Chang was disloyal because he was a subject of Xiang Yu, and he was the one who caused King Xiang to lose the world.
So he beheaded Duke Ding and said: "I want all future ministers not to imitate Duke Ding!" Luan Bu was from Liang.
When Peng Yue was still a civilian, he had a relationship with Le Bu. Because of poverty, he worked as a laborer in Qi and was employed by Qi Diyi. hotel.
He left a few years later and was kidnapped and sold as a slave to the State of Yan.
He avenged his master and was elected as the captain by Yan general Zang Tu.
Later Zang Tu became king of Yan, and Lebu was appointed as a general.
When Zang Tu rebelled, the Han army attacked Yan and captured Le Bu.
The king of Liang, Peng Yue, found out about this and interceded with the Emperor of Han, asking for Le Bu to atone for his sins and let him be appointed as the official of the Liang Kingdom.
Peng Yue sent him as an envoy to Qi, but before he returned, the Han court summoned Peng Yue, accused him of treason, and killed all members of the Pengyue clan. Peng Yue's head was hung under the gate of Luoyang City for public display. He also issued an order from Shao: Anyone who cries or cares for Peng Yue's head will be arrested immediately.
Lebu returned from Qi and reported under Peng Yue's head. While offering sacrifices, he cried bitterly.
The messenger arrested Le Bu and reported it to the emperor.
The emperor summoned Le Bu and scolded him: Are you plotting rebellion with Peng Yue?
I forbid people to collect or see his head, but you still go to sacrifice and cry bitterly, which shows that you are conspiring with Peng Yue, and I will cook you to death as soon as possible.
Just as he was about to lift Lebu closer to the oil pan, Lebu turned around and said: I want to say something before I die. The emperor said: What did you say?
Le Bu said: When you were trapped in Pengcheng and defeated Rongyang and Chenggao, the reason why King Xiang could not successfully attack to the west was because King Peng was guarding Liang and united with Han to trouble the Chu army.
At that time, King Peng was a little sidelined. If he united with Chu, Han would be defeated. If he united with Mo, Chu would be defeated.
Moreover, in the siege of Gaixia, without King Peng, Xiang Yu would not have perished.
Now that the world has been peaceful, King Peng accepted the court's letter and became king, hoping to pass it on to his descendants for generations to come.
Now the imperial court is recruiting troops from the Liang Kingdom. King Peng is ill and cannot come, so he is suspected of treason.
I didn't see the fact that he wanted to rebel, but I punished him for trivial matters. I'm worried that all the meritorious officials will be in danger.
Now that King Peng is dead, it would be better for me to be alive than to be dead. Please cook it immediately.
So the emperor released him and worshiped him as captain.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Lebu was the prime minister of Yan State, and his official rank was general.
He publicly declared: If poverty fails to lower one's ambitions and humiliate one's body, one is not a good man; if wealth fails to bring comfort, one is not a wise man.
Therefore, he will give generous rewards to those who have been kind to him; he will definitely try to destroy those who have hatred towards him.
When Wu Chu rebelled, Lebu was named Langhou for his meritorious service. Once again, he was the prime minister of Yan State.
Ancestral temples were built for him in Yan and Qi areas, known as Le Commune.
After Luan Bu's death, his son Le Bi succeeded him as marquis. During the reign of Emperor Mowu, he was appointed Taichang; because the livestock used in the sacrifices were illegal according to the regulations of the law, the vassal state was abolished.
Uncle Tian was a native of Xingcheng, Zhao State, and his ancestor was the Tian family of Qi State.
He loved sword dancing and learned the art of Huang Lao under Le Jugong. He is an upright, upright and chivalrous person, and often socializes with local leaders.
Someone recommended him to Prime Minister Chang Wu, and Chang Wu was introduced to Chang Wang Zhang Ao, and he was appointed as a doctor.
A few years later, Tong Gong thought he was talented and had not had time to promote him.
It happened that Zhao Wu, Guan Gao and others were surrounding and plotting to assassinate the emperor. They were discovered and the emperor issued an order to arrest the king and the ministers who followed him in the rebellion.
Those who follow the king to rebel will be guilty of the three clans.
Only Uncle Tian, ​​Meng Shu and more than ten people, wearing reddish-brown prison clothes, shaved their heads, and tied their necks with iron rings, followed the king to Chang'an.
Later, the affairs of Chang Wang Zhang Ao were clarified and he was released, but was demoted to the title of Marquis of Xuan Ping. Zhang Ao reported to the emperor that Uncle Tian and other ten people were there.
The emperor summoned them and after talking with them, he felt that no official in the Han Dynasty could surpass them.
The emperor was very happy and appointed them all as county guards or prime ministers of vassal states.
Therefore, Uncle Tian served as the county guard in Hanzhong County for more than ten years.
When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, he summoned Uncle Tian and asked: Do you know any honest and honest people in the world?
Uncle Tian replied: How can I know?
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: You are an honest and honest person, so you should know.
Uncle Tian kowtowed and said: Meng Shu, the former governor of Yunzhong County, was a man of integrity and sincerity.
At that time, Meng Shuzheng was blamed for the large-scale invasion of the Huns and was relieved of his post as county guard.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: The late Emperor appointed Meng Shu as the governor of Yunzhong County for more than ten years. Once the Xiongnu invaded, he could not hold on and hundreds of soldiers died in battle for no reason.
Is it true that people with integrity will kill people?
Uncle Tian kowtowed and said: Back then, when Guan Gao and others planned to kill the emperor, the emperor issued an edict that anyone who dared to follow the king in the country would be punished.
However, Meng Shu shaved off his hair, tied his neck with an iron hoop, and followed the king to kill him. How did you know you would be the governor of Yunzhong County later?
When Han and Chu faced each other, the soldiers were exhausted. However, the Xiongnu Maodun Shanyu had recently surrendered to the northern ethnic minorities and was in full force to invade the border. Menshu knew that the soldiers were very tired and could not bear to send them out to fight. However, the soldiers rushed out of the city to kill the enemy, just like sons fighting for their fathers, and hundreds of them died.
But it was not Meng Shu who drove them to fight and die!
The result was that Meng Shu was honest and sincere, and had people working for him. Emperor Wen of Han then praised: Meng Shu. O wise man!
He also appointed Meng Shu as the governor of Yunzhong County.
A few years later, Uncle Tian lost his official position for breaking the law.
Emperor Jing's brother Liang Xiaowang Liu Wu sent people to assassinate Yuan Ang, the minister in charge of discussing political affairs in the Han Dynasty. Emperor Jing summoned Uncle Tian to investigate the matter and fully grasped the facts.
After he came back, he reported it to Emperor Jing. Emperor Jing said: "Did King Xiao of Liang do this?" He replied: "It is true."
Emperor Jing asked: What is the specific situation?
Uncle Tian said: Your Majesty, it is best not to ask about King Liang Xiao's affair.
Now the King of Liang is being punished for not obeying the law, but for abandoning the laws of the Han Dynasty. If he is sentenced to death according to the law, the Queen Mother will not be able to eat well or sleep well, and Your Majesty will also be worried about it.
So Emperor Jing thought Uncle Tian was very virtuous and appointed him prime minister of Lu.
Uncle Tian was the prime minister of Lu. When he first took office, more than a hundred people reported to King Lu that he had taken away their property.
Uncle Tian caught the twenty leaders and whipped them, and said angrily: "Isn't King Lu your master?"
How dare you sue the master!
King Lu was deeply ashamed when he heard this. He took the money out of the treasury and asked Uncle Tian to pay it back to the people.
Uncle Tian said: King Lu will send someone to repay it himself. Otherwise, you become the bad guy and I become the good guy.
King Lu loved hunting, and Uncle Tian often followed him into the gardens. King Lu immediately stopped him and asked him to rest in the garden.
But Uncle Tian often sat outside his room to wrap himself in the open air, and never went into the house to rest. He said: "The king of Lu is wrapping his clothes in the open air, how can I wrap myself in the house alone?"
For this reason, King Lu did not go out much for hunting.
A few years later, Uncle Tian died in office. The State of Lu offered a hundred catties of gold as a sacrifice, but his youngest son Tian Ren refused to accept it, saying: Morally, the honor of his father cannot be harmed.
Because Tian Ren was strong and brave, he became a household official of General Wei Qing. He followed Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu several times.
General Wei recommended him to Emperor Mowu, and he was appointed as a doctor. He was transferred to Erqianshi and served as prime minister for a long time. Later, he was dismissed due to some affairs.
Later, he was appointed as the governor of Sanhe County. When he returned to Beijing to report his affairs, he was in line with Emperor Wu's wishes and was appointed as the capital of Jingfu.
More than a month later, he was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi.
A few years later, Liu Zheng, the crown prince of Emperor Wu, raised an army due to an incident. At that time, Tian Ren was in charge of opening and closing the city gates. He asked the prince to flee the city. He was exterminated for indulging the rebels.
Praise said: While Xiang Yu was heroic, Ji Bu was famous for his bravery in Chu State. He defeated the enemy many times and took up his banner. He can be called a hero!
Even when he was in trouble and became a slave, he still lived quietly without changing. What is the reason?
It's because he is conceited of his talents. Being insulted without feeling ashamed is to hone some of your deficient qualities. As a result, Ji Bu finally became a famous general in the early Han Dynasty.
A virtuous person attaches great importance to the value of his own death.
However, ordinary slaves, wives, concubines and other lowly people would commit suicide due to some emotion. This is not only not brave, but the idea is boring to the extreme.
Lebu cried and offered sacrifices to Peng Yue, and Uncle Tian followed Zhang Ao. They all regarded death as homecoming, because they knew that doing so was due to their faith and their death was worthwhile.

He died in office, and his son Tian Ren refused funeral gifts, later serving as a general under Wei Qing. Tian Ren was executed for allowing the crown prince to flee during a rebellion.

Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.
Note that the empress gave birth to Emperor Xiaoyuan, the urgent maggot gave birth to King Xian of Huaiyang, Zhiyin, the envoy of Wei gave birth to King Xiaoxiao of Chu, Xingxiao, the nephew of Gongsun, Prince Shuhusi, King Liu, and the nephew of Rong, Prince Ai of Zhongshan, died.
Huaiyang Xianwang Liu Qin was established as king in the third year of Yuankang, and his mother Zhang Shidan was favored by Emperor Xuan.
After Queen Huo was deposed, the emperor wanted to make Zhang Tuzi his queen.
As time went by, I was wary of Huo's intention to harm the crown prince, so I changed my mind and chose someone who had no sons in the harem and was cautious. So I made Wang Jiantun, a native of Changling, the queen, and asked her to raise the crown prince like a mother.
The queen was not favored and rarely slept with or met the emperor. Only Zhang Jiantun was favored the most.
When King Xian of Huaiyang grew up, he liked scriptures and laws, was smart and talented, and Emperor Xuan liked him very much.
The prince was kind-hearted and fond of Confucianism. Emperor Xuan praised King Xian several times and said, "You are really my son!"
I often wanted to make Zhang Jianzi the queen and Prince Xian the prince. However, because the prince grew up in civilian life, Emperor Xuan relied on the Xu family when he was young, and Empress Xu had been killed when he came to the throne. The prince lost his mother when he was young, so he couldn't bear it.
After a long time, Emperor Xuan summoned and made Wei Xuan the lieutenant of Huaiyang Kingdom because Wei Xuancheng, the son of the former prime minister Wei Xian, pretended to be crazy and gave the marquis to his brother. He was praised by the court for his knowledge of Confucian classics and noble conduct.
When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he ordered King Xian to go to the feudal country.
At this time, Zhang Biandan had passed away. King Xian had a maternal grandmother. His uncle Zhang Bo and his three brothers would be rewarded by King Xian if they went to Huaiyang to visit their mother every year.
Later, King Xian wrote a letter asking for the relocation of the Zhang family to Huaiyang. Zhang Bo wrote a letter saying he hoped to stay at his ancestral graves but refused to move.
King Xian resented him.
Later, when Zhang Bo went to Huaiyang, King Xian rewarded him less.
Zhang Bo said: The debt is several million. I hope King Xian will repay it for me.
King Xian refused. Zhang Bo left and sent his brother Zhang Guang to threaten King Xian, saying that he was even more lax in treating his grandmother. Zhang Bo wanted to write a letter to his mother asking for leave to go home.
King Xian sent someone to give Zhang Bo fifty pounds of gold.
Zhang Bo was happy and wrote back a letter of thanks. He praised King Xian very much with flattering words, and said: There are no good ministers in the court today, and disasters have occurred many times, which makes the court miserable. later.
The people all place their hopes on the king. Why does the king quietly do not ask to visit the court and assist the emperor?
His younger brother Zhang Guang persuaded King Xian several times to follow Zhang Bo's strategy. He himself went to the capital to lobby the powerful dignitaries to request an audience on King Xian's behalf.
King Xian did not adopt his opinion.
Later, Zhang Guang wanted to go to Chang'an. When he said goodbye to King Xian, he said that he would do his best to work with Zhang Bo to petition for the king's admission to the court.
The king is about to arrive in Chang'an and can rely on Marquis Pingyang.
When Zhang Guang heard that King Xian wanted to request an audience, he sent Pegasus to tell Zhang Bo.
Zhang Bo knew about King Xian's change of mind and sent another letter to King Xian, saying: "Zhang Bo is fortunate to be the king's confidant. He has made stupid suggestions several times, but they have not attracted your attention."
I traveled north to Yanzhao and other places, and wanted to visit the reclusive scholars in various places. I heard that there was a Mr. Si in Qi who was familiar with "Sima's Art of War" and was a talented general. Zhang Bo once paid a visit to him and took the opportunity to go and inquire about the ruling principles of the Five Emperors and Three Kings. His words were brilliant and could not be understood by ordinary people.
Now the border is unstable and the world is in turmoil. Unless this person, no one else can bring peace to the world.
I also heard that there is a wise man next to Beihai. He is a rare talent that can only be found in several lifetimes, but it is difficult to attract him.
Acquiring these two talents and recommending them to the court would be a great achievement.
I am willing to rush west to Chang'an to recommend these two people to help the Han Dynasty in crisis, but I don't have the money to reach the dignitaries.
The king sent an audience to reward me with oxen, wine, and thirty pounds of gold, but I refused. He also sent someone to ask for my daughter's hand in marriage, offering a bride price of two hundred pounds, but I did not agree.
I happened to receive a letter from Zhang Guang saying that the king had sent him west to Chang'an, and he and I would try our best to request an audience.
I thought that the king had given up on this matter, but I didn't expect that the king would change his mind and befriend me kindly. I am willing to repay your kindness with my life.
What's the matter with the court meeting?
If your Majesty gives me some money and allows me to work hard, this is the reason why Tang Yu achieved great achievements.
Mr. Si has a profound knowledge of Taoism and has a wide range of books. He hopes to know the king's hobbies and can present them in time.
King Xian was very happy to receive the letter and wrote back to Zhang Bo: Fortunately, Zigao, you condescended to be considerate, and the compassion from your heart showed extremely high sincerity, offered good strategies, and told me the most important thing. Although I am not smart, how dare I not understand your thoughts!
Now send a company to repay your debt of two million.
At this time, Jingfang, Zhang Bo's son-in-law, died because of Mingxiao's "Yi Yi". "Yin Yang" won the emperor's favor and summoned him several times to discuss state affairs.
He thought he was ostracized by Shi Xian and Wulu Chongzong, and his plan was not adopted. He told Zhang Bo these things many times.
Zhang Bo often wanted to deceive the King of Huaiyang and show off to him, so he recorded all the disasters reported by the capital and the secret words the emperor said when he summoned him, and gave them to the King of Huaiyang as evidence. He lied to him that he had seen Zhongshu Ling Shijun requesting an audience and promised him five hundred catties of gold.
A wise man only considers merit and does not care about the cost.
Although Dayu made the people exhausted when he controlled the floods, his success benefited the people for generations to come.
Now it is said that the emperor is less than forty, his hair and teeth have fallen out, the prince is young, the sycophants are dictatorial, and the yin and yang are not balanced. Nearly half of the people died due to disease, epidemics, and famine, and the harm of floods was no more than this.
Your Majesty is preparing to save the world and will compare his merits with those of the ancient holy kings. How can you slack off?
I have already made a memorial to the king with a learned and enlightened scholar, stating the way to protect the country and pointing out the dangers of disasters. When the king meets, he will first explain the general idea and then give a memorial. The emperor will definitely be very happy.
When things are successful and achievements are established, the king will have the reputation of Zhou Gong and Shao Gong. The treacherous ministers will flee in all directions. The ministers will change their moral integrity and their merits will be unparalleled. The emperor's favor for Liang Wang and Zhao Wang will definitely be transferred to the king. We foreigners will also be rich. How can we count on the king's money?
King Xian was happy and wrote back to Zhang Bo: "In the past, edicts were issued prohibiting princes from attending court. I feel so sad that I don't know what strategy to use."
Zi Gao, you have always had the talent of Yan Yuan and Ran You, the intelligence of Zang Wu Zi, the eloquence of Zigong, and the bravery of Bian Zhuang Zi. You have the best of all four, which is rare in the world.
It's been started, and I hope it will finally come to fruition.
Asking for an audience is a reasonable thing, but how to use money?
Zhang Bo wrote back and said: I have promised Shi Jun that I need to use it to accomplish this.
King Xian gave Zhang Bo five hundred catties of gold.
It happened that Jingfang left the capital to serve as county governor and left the emperor's side. Shi Xian knew the whole situation and reported it.
The conversation in the imperial palace was leaked by the Jingfang, and the Zhang Bo brothers misled the princes and kings, slandered the government, and acted cunningly, so they were all arrested.
Relevant departments submitted a petition to arrest Liu Qin, but the emperor could not bear to bring him to justice, so he sent Wang Jun, an admonishing doctor, to reward Liu Qin with a seal and a letter saying: The emperor told the King of Huaiyang.
Relevant departments have accused you. Your uncle Zhang Bo has written to you many times, slandering the state affairs, ridiculing the emperor, praising and recommending princes, and citing the conquests of Zhou Gong and Shang Tang to confuse you. What he said is particularly bad and disobedient.
You didn't report him, but you often gave him money and kind words in return. Your sin has reached a point where it cannot be forgiven. I can't bear to hear this, and I feel sad for you.
Looking at the origin, the bad things come from Zhang Bo. Your intentions are different from those of evil people.
I have ordered you not to punish you, but I have sent Wang Jun to remonstrate with you to explain my intention.
Doesn’t the Book of Songs say it? Be loyal to your position and behave with integrity. You have to encourage me!
Wang Jun pointed out the king of Huaiyang and said: Etiquette is a ritual for the princes to make a joint pilgrimage to pay homage to the betrothal gift. Therefore, they should fulfill the etiquette with one heart and one mind and serve the emperor with respect.
Besides, didn’t Wang study the Book of Songs?
"The Book of Songs" says: He was made a prince in the state of Lu and a vassal of the royal family of Zhou. Now Wang uncle Zhang Bo has written to you many times, and what he said is contrary to the holy way.
Fortunately, you are bound by the edict, understand the classics, and know that your status as a prince should not leave the country.
The emperor's kindness spreads to everyone in the court, but you calmly accept Zhang Bo's words, often give him money, and respond to each other. There is no greater sin of disloyalty than this.
As always, if a prince commits a crime in the capital, no matter how serious it is, even if he is not killed, he will definitely be punished by exile, removal from office, demotion, dethronation, etc., and there will be no one who will not be held accountable.
Now the sage monarch pardons your crimes, but also takes pity on you for going astray and forgetting your duty, being deceived by Zhang Bo. He gives you a seal and a letter, and sends an admonishment official to explain your intention. How can we estimate the great kindness of the emperor!
The crime committed by Zhang Bo and others was serious, and the officials attacked him together, which cannot be forgiven by the king's law.
From now on, you should no longer worry about Zhang Bo and others, and you must abandon him together with everyone else.
The meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that the most important thing is to be able to change one's past.
"The Book of Changes" says that if you use Imperata for sacrifices, you will not encounter any mistakes. It means that the ministers must correct their mistakes and purify themselves to assist the emperor, and then they can avoid mistakes.
You should be careful and vigilant, consider how to repent and change your behavior, make up for the heavy responsibility, and express the emperor's great kindness.
In this way, you will enjoy long-lasting wealth and honor, and the country will be stable.
At that time, King Liu Qin of Huaiyang took off his hat, kowtowed and apologized, saying: I failed to fulfill my duties as a king of princes, and my crime was so obvious that your Majesty could not bear to punish the crime according to law, so he showed great kindness and sent envoys to explain the truth and fulfill the duties of princes.
Considering that Zhang Bo's crime is particularly serious, he should be sentenced to death.
The minister Liu Qin is willing to reform himself wholeheartedly and accept the edict respectfully.
I should deserve to die.
The three brothers Jingfang and Zhang Bo were all exiled from the city, and their wives and children were exiled to the border.
When Emperor Cheng came to the throne, because King Huaiyang was his uncle as a relative, he was respected by Emperor Cheng, far above other princes and kings.
The King of Huaiyang wrote a letter stating that his uncle Zhang Bo was being bullied by Shi Xian and others, so he requested to return to his hometown for the exiled Zhang Bo's family.
The prime minister and the imperial censor impeached the King of Huaiyang again: He and Zhang Bo had communicated privately with each other in the past, and their intentions were not what a prince should have. Thanks to the emperor's grace, he was not punished. The matter happened before the pardon.
Instead of repenting, he quoted past events and thought he was upright, which was unbecoming of a prince and committed the crime of disrespect.
However, the emperor granted King Huaiyang's request and promised King Xian to move the exiles back.
King Xian died in his thirty-sixth year.
His son King Wen Liu Xuan succeeded to the throne and died after reigning for twenty-six years.
His son Liu Yan succeeded to the throne, but was cut off by Wang Mang.
Liu Xiao, King Xiao of Chu, was established as King Dingtao in the second year of Ganlu's reign, and was granted the title of King of Chu three years later. Emperor Cheng entered the dynasty during the Heping period. He was ill at that time. The emperor took pity on him and issued an edict: It is said that human beings are the most noble of life in the world, and filial piety is the most important thing in human behavior. King Liu Xiao of Chu has always been filial and kind. In the more than 20 years since he became a feudal country, he has not heard of any minor mistakes. I admire him very much.
Now he is suffering from bad luck and is seriously ill. The Master deplored it and said: What a sad fate! Can such a person suffer from such a disease?
I feel sorry for him.
He is kind and noble without appearing to be different from the public. How will the princes be encouraged?
Didn't "Shang Shu" say that? Rewards are given to virtuous people in recognition of their kindness. Now is the first month of the dynasty. King Xiao is ordered to come to court with one of his sons, and his son Liu Xun is named the Marquis of Guangqi with a settlement of 4,300 households in Guangqi County.
The next year, Liu Xiao died.
His son Liu Wen, King Huai, succeeded to the throne and died a year later. He had no sons and was cut off.
In the second year, Emperor Cheng appointed Liu Wen's younger brother Liu Yan, Marquis of Lu, as King Si.
He died in the 21st year of his reign, and his son Liu Yu succeeded to the throne, which was cut off by Wang Mang.
At the beginning, when he became emperor, Liu Jing, Liu Yu's younger brother, was appointed King of Dingtao.
When Liu Xun, Marquis of Guangqi, died, Mi was named Yanghou, and his son Liu Xian succeeded him.
Emperor Ping died without a son, so Wang Mang made Liu Xian's son Liu Ying his son, who succeeded Emperor Ping.
Wang Mang usurped the throne and made Liu Ying the Duke of Ding'an.
After Wang Mang was executed by the Han Dynasty, Liu Ying was in Chang'an during the Gengshi period. Fang Wang and others from Pingling knew the astronomical phenomena very well and believed that the Gengshi Emperor would definitely fail. Liu Ying was the one who should be established as emperor according to the imperial tradition. Together they sent troops to take Liu Ying to Linjing and established him as the emperor.
Emperor Gengshi sent Prime Minister Li Song to defeat them and kill Liu Ying.
Liu Zi, the king of Dongping, was established as king in the second year of Ganlu.
Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and went to the feudal state.
When he grew up, he committed a crime for colluding with bad people. The emperor refused to punish him because he was the closest relative. His master was in line with the country.
After some time, King Si served the Queen Mother, which was not in line with the Queen Mother's wishes. The Queen Mother wrote about this and asked to guard Du Mausoleum.
The emperor then sent Zhang Zijiao, the Taizhong doctor, to receive the seal order and inform him, saying: The emperor told King Shuping.
It is said that the kindness of close relatives is not more important than filial piety, and the principle of respecting noble people is not greater than loyalty. Therefore, when the princes are in power, they should not be proud to fulfill their filial piety, and be temperate and prudent to assist the emperor. In this way, they can maintain wealth and national stability forever.
Now I hear that you have a lack of self-cultivation, there is disharmony within the feudal country, rumors have appeared one after another, and slander has arisen from within. I feel sorry for you and I am afraid for you.
Doesn’t the Book of Songs say it? Miss your ancestors, cultivate your own morality, always follow the destiny, and pray for blessings.
I know that when you were in the prime of your life, you neglected your morality, your mind was deviated, and you did not take good advice, so I personally sent Zijiao, the Taizhong doctor, to convey my wishes to you.
Confucius said: If you fail to correct your mistakes, this is a fault. You should think carefully and do not go against my will.
He also specially gave it to the Queen Mother with a seal, saying: The emperor sent officials and eunuchs to report this to the Queen Mother of Dongping.
I heard something and the Queen Mother paid a little attention to it.
There is no greater happiness in a happy family than harmony, and there is no greater source of disaster than internal division.
King Dongping was raised by you, and therefore he is on the throne. He is still young and full of energy, and has little time to study. He despises his ministers, and his relationship with you, the Queen Mother, is different from others. Under such circumstances, the only person who can do it without disrespecting etiquette is a saint!
Legend: When a father conceals something for his son, integrity lies in it. The Queen Mother clearly understands this meaning and must be careful.
Within a family, between mother and child, they are connected by blood but have different voices. How can the kindness of flesh and blood be ignored?
Can it be ignored?
Once upon a time, Zhou Gong warned Bo Qin: "You can't abandon an old friend if he's not making any serious mistakes. Don't seek perfection from a person."
Because it is an old friend's kindness, I still tolerate his small shortcomings, not to mention such a flesh-and-blood relationship!
I have sent a messenger to tell King Si that he has repented and confessed his crime. Queen Mother, please be lenient and tolerant to ease this matter. He should not dare to do so in the future.
Queen Mother, please try your best to eat, stop worrying, treat illness carefully, and take care of yourself.
Liu Yu was ashamed and frightened. He kowtowed in front of the messenger and apologized, willing to change his mind and make amends on his own.
The edict also ordered Si Wang's master and the state minister to say: Human nature has five qualities: benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faith. When he grows up, what he hears and sees is related to his hobbies and desires. Therefore, after the five permanent things disappear, evil thoughts arise, lust disturbs his nature, and profit overcomes his moral heart. There is no one who does not lose his home.
King Si is now in the prime of life, strong and mighty, but he has received little instruction from his master, and has little knowledge. From now on, if he dares to tell King Si about anything other than serious knowledge of the Five Classics, such as outings and hunting, etc., his name will be reported immediately.
Liu Yu reigned for twenty years, and Emperor Yuan died.
Liu Yu told Xin and others in the palace: The ministers of the Han Dynasty commented that the emperor was young and could not govern the world. They thought that I knew the system and laws, and suggested that I assist the emperor.
I saw the minister working hard at night. If I were to do this job, I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to do it.
The weather is hot now and the emperor is young. I am afraid there will be no place to observe filial piety. I almost got the throne!
When Emperor Yuan was buried, Liu Yu cried three times in total, drank wine and ate meat, and never left his wife and concubines.
The concubine Qucuo was originally favored by him, but later became estranged from him. She often sighed and called to heaven.
When Liu Yu heard about this, he deposed Qu Teng as a palace maid with no status, asked her to clean the palace streets, and often whipped her.
Qu Suo secretly wrote down Liu Yu's faults in separate notes, and asked his family to report him several times.
When Liu Zi found out, he hanged Qu Chang.
Relevant departments petitioned to arrest Liu Yu, and the emperor issued an edict to cut off Fan and Kangfu counties.
Three years later, the emperor ordered Yousi to say: It is said that benevolent government is to be close to one's relatives. This is an ancient truth.
In the past, King Dongping made mistakes and the relevant departments asked him to be deposed. I couldn't bear it.
I also asked for the reduction of the feudal state. I dare not be arbitrary, because he is the closest relative and has never been forgotten.
Now I am pleased to hear that he has repented, respects the art of practicing scriptures, is close to benevolent people, and does not ask for illegal requests from officials.
Didn’t the legend say that?
If you change it day by day, a gentleman will praise it.
Restore the closed counties that were removed before.
In the court meeting the following year, Shangshu asked for the books of the Confucius and the "Historical Records". The emperor asked the general Wang Feng about this matter, and replied: I heard that the princes went to court to recruit people, study articles, and correct laws and regulations. I did not mention anything that was not in line with etiquette.
Now that King Dongping has the honor to come to the court, he does not consider restraint and prudence to prevent mistakes, but asks for books, which is not the principle of court employment.
Some of the books of the philosophers are against the classics and slanderous saints, some record ghosts and gods, and believe in strange objects and strange phenomena; the "Historical Records" contains the treacherous strategies of the powerful forces in the Warring States Period, the strange strategies of the counselors when the Han Dynasty just emerged, catastrophic changes in the sky, and dangerous terrain: none of them are suitable for princes and kings.
Can't give it to him.
The excuse for disagreeing should be: The Five Classics were produced by sages, and everything is recorded.
The king is indeed willing to follow the right path. His masters and ministers are all Confucian scholars. He teaches and recites morning and evening, which is enough to correct his behavior and cheer his mood.
