translation:
Zhang Tang was from Duling.
His father was the magistrate of Chang'an County and was away on business, so Zhang Tang took care of the house as his son.
When his father returned home, he found that the mice had stolen the meat. He lost his temper and whipped Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang dug a rat hole and found the rat that had stolen the meat and the leftover meat. He stated the crime of the rat, tortured and interrogated it, sent out the interrogation record, and specified the procedure for reporting the verdict after the interrogation.
When his father saw this scene and saw that the diction of his judgment was like a seasoned judge, he was very surprised and asked him to learn prison documents.
After his father's death, Zhang Tang served as a county official in Chang'an.
When Zhou Yanghou Tiansheng was serving as the ninth minister, he was imprisoned in Chang'an Prison. Zhang Tang did his best to help and take care of him.
After Zhou Yanghou was released from prison, he was granted the title of Marquis. He became very friendly with Zhang Tang and introduced Zhang Tang to important people.
Zhang Tang was a subordinate of the internal historian and served as an official of Ning Cheng. Ning Cheng believed that Zhang Tang was extremely talented and recommended him to the Prime Minister's Office. He was transferred to Maolingwei to be in charge of the civil engineering of the mausoleum.
Marquis Wu'an served as prime minister, and Zhang Tang was appointed as an official in the prime minister's palace.
He recommended him to the emperor and served as his censor. When dealing with Queen Chen's witchcraft case, he investigated his accomplices in depth. The emperor believed that he was capable and promoted him to Taizhong doctor.
He and Zhao Yu jointly formulated various laws, focusing on strict binding and strict restraint on serving officials.
Soon, Zhao Yu was promoted to Shaofu, and Zhang Tang was appointed as a court captain. The two became friendly, and Zhang Tang treated Zhao Yu like an elder brother. Zhao Yu was honest and arrogant, while Zhang Tang liked to control others by playing tricks.
At first he became a minor official, speculating for profit, and secretly colluded with the wealthy businessmen Tian Jia and Yu Wengshu in Chang'an.
When he was in the position of Jiuqing, he recruited famous people and officials from all over the country. Although he disagreed with them in his heart, he pretended to respect them.
At this time, the emperor was fond of Confucianism. Zhang Tang decided a major case and wanted to adhere to the ancient principles, so he asked his disciples to study "Shangshu" and "Spring and Autumn" and serve as the history of the imperial court to correct the doubtful aspects of the law.
When submitting difficult cases for adjudication, all aspects of the reasons must be analyzed in advance to the emperor. Whatever the emperor affirms, the case will be accepted as a case decided in accordance with the law and entered into the court's written regulations to promote the sage of the Lord.
If the report work was criticized, Zhang Tang would admit his mistake and apologize. Following the emperor's intention, he would definitely name the capable assistant officials or clerks and say: They originally suggested to me, just as the emperor asked me to do. I was stupid enough not to adopt it.
Therefore his faults are often forgiven.
Sometimes he would submit a memorial to discuss matters. When the emperor approved of the memorial, he would say: I didn't know that such a memorial was written.
He wants to recommend his subordinates, promote someone's strengths or cover up someone's shortcomings.
If the emperor wants to impose more crimes on a case, he will hand it over to supervisors who enforce the law strictly; if the emperor wants to tolerate a case, he will hand it over to supervisors who enforce the law lightly.
If the person being tried is a powerful person, he will definitely play with the legal provisions and severely punish him; when he encounters a poor person being tried, he often says that even if he is convicted according to the law, the emperor will still make a ruling and review.
So it is often as Zhang Tang said.
Although Zhang Tang was a high official, his private life was very serious. He made friends with guests, entertained and dined, and took better care of his old friends and children who were serving as subordinates, as well as his poor brothers of the same clan. He went to greet Sangong without avoiding the severe cold and heat.
Therefore, although Zhang Tang was profound in his methods but not pure and fair in his heart, he still gained this good reputation.
Most of the harsh and vicious officials who worked for him relied on Confucian scholars.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong praised him many times.
When investigating the rebellion cases of Huainan King, Hengshan King, and Jiangdu King, they all got to the bottom of it.
The emperor wanted to pardon Yan Zhu and Wu Bei, but Zhang Tang argued: Wu Bei originally planned a rebellion, while Yan Zhu was deeply favored and was a confidant who went in and out of the forbidden gates of the palace, but he had liaisons with the princes. If such people are not killed, similar situations in the future will not be easy to deal with.
So the emperor agreed to their sentence.
He handles cases to attack ministers and thinks it is his own merit. There are many such things.
As a result, Zhang Tang became more favored and trusted, and soon he was promoted to the imperial censor.
At that time, King Hunxie and others surrendered, and the Han Dynasty sent large-scale troops to attack the Xiongnu. Shandong was hit by floods and early disasters. The poor people were displaced and moved, relying on the government to provide food and clothing, and the warehouses were empty.
At this time, Zhang Tang obeyed the emperor's wishes and petitioned to mint silver coins and five-baht copper coins, monopolize the country's salt and ironware, squeeze out wealthy merchants, issue proclamations, eradicate the powerful mergers and acquisitions of large households, and play tricks on the legal provisions to assist the implementation of severe punishments.
Every time Zhang Tang went to court to report on his work, it took so long to talk about the state's financial expenses that the emperor forgot to eat.
The prime minister at the right time is just a vacant position, and all national affairs depend on Zhang Tang.
The common people could not live peacefully, there were riots, the government's undertakings did not gain benefits, and corrupt officials stole and embezzled, so they were punished severely.
Therefore, everyone from the ministers to the common people blamed Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang fell ill once, and the emperor went to inquire about his illness in person. He was such a noble person.
The Xiongnu came to ask for peace, and the ministers discussed it in front of the emperor. Dr. Dishan said: It is suitable to get married.
The emperor asked him the appropriate reason, and Di Shan said: Weapons are deadly weapons, so don't use them easily and frequently.
Emperor Gao wanted to attack the Xiongnu, but was besieged in Pingcheng, so he finally concluded a peace.
During the period of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao, the country was peaceful and happy. When Emperor Wen wanted to deal with the Xiongnu, the northern border was harassed and the people suffered from war.
During the period of Emperor Jing, seven kingdoms including Wu and Chu rebelled. Emperor Jing went back and forth between the two palaces to discuss the matter and worried about it for several months.
After the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were crushed, Emperor Jing never talked about war, and the country became rich and fulfilled.
Since your Majesty deployed troops to attack the Xiongnu, the country has become empty, and most of the people on the border are in embarrassment and poverty.
From this point of view, it is better to get married.
The emperor asked Zhang Tang, and Zhang Tang said: This is a stupid Confucian scholar who is ignorant.
Di Shan said: Although I am foolish and loyal, but Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, is deceitful and loyal.
For example, Zhang Tang used harsh and severe methods in handling the cases of King Huainan and King Jiangdu, wantonly slandered the princes, and alienated the emperor's closest relatives, thus making the kings of various feudal states feel uneasy. I already knew that Zhang Tang was cheating.

summary:
Zhang Tang, a native of Duling, demonstrated legal acumen early in life when, as a boy, he interrogated a rat for stealing meat, impressing his father, a county magistrate. After his father's death, Zhang Tang served as a county official in Chang'an. He befriended Zhou Yanghou Tiansheng, who later introduced him to influential figures. Recognized for his talent by Ning Cheng, Zhang Tang was recommended to the Prime Minister's Office and later appointed as an official in the prime minister's palace under Marquis Wu'an. He was promoted to censor after investigating Queen Chen's witchcraft case, and later became Taizhong doctor. Alongside Zhao Yu, he formulated strict laws, eventually becoming a court captain. Zhang Tang was known for his cunning, often colluding with wealthy merchants while pretending to respect Confucian scholars to please the emperor. He manipulated legal cases to align with the emperor's wishes, admitting faults to gain forgiveness and promoting subordinates to deflect blame. His private life was serious, and he cared for old friends and poor relatives, earning a good reputation despite his harsh methods.

Zhang Tang handled major rebellion cases, such as those of the Huainan, Hengshan, and Jiangdu kings, often arguing for severe punishments. He gained the emperor's favor by proposing financial policies like minting coins and monopolizing salt and iron, which strained the populace. His influence grew to the point where national affairs depended on him, leading to widespread blame from ministers and commoners. When the Xiongnu sought peace, Zhang Tang opposed the advice of Dr. Dishan, who advocated for marriage alliances. Dishan criticized Zhang Tang's deceitful and harsh methods, but the emperor sided with Zhang Tang, sending Dishan to a border fortress where he was killed by the Xiongnu. This incident intimidated other ministers.

Zhang Tang's downfall began when his former friend Tian Jia criticized his moral faults. As imperial censor for seven years, he faced hostility from Li Wen, a censor Zhongcheng. Zhang Tang's favorite official, Lu Yeju, plotted against Li Wen, but the scheme unraveled when King Zhao reported Zhang Tang's inappropriate behavior toward Lu Yeju. Lu Yeju's brother later exposed their conspiracy. Additionally, Zhang Tang clashed with Prime Minister Qing Zhai over a tomb robbery, refusing to apologize and attempting to impeach the prime minister. Three chief ministers, including Zhu Maichen, conspired against Zhang Tang, accusing him of hoarding supplies and dividing wealth with subordinates. The emperor, believing Zhang Tang treacherous, sent envoys to question him. Zhang Tang refused to explain and, under pressure from envoy Yu, committed suicide. His family was found to have minimal wealth, and his mother insisted on a simple burial. The emperor later regretted his actions, executed the three chief ministers, and promoted Zhang Tang's son, Zhang Anshi.

Zhang Anshi, known for his meticulousness and loyalty, served under Emperor Zhao and Huo Guang. He was appointed as a general and marquis, playing a key role in deposing the King of Changyi and enthroning Emperor Xuan. Despite his high position, Anshi remained humble and cautious, often feigning illness to avoid political entanglements. He managed his household frugally, with his wife spinning crops and servants skilled in industry. His brother Zhang He cared for Emperor Xuan as a child, and after Zhang He's death, the emperor posthumously honored him. Anshi's descendants, including Zhang Yanshou and Zhang Lin, maintained the family's reputation for humility and frugality. Zhang Fang, a later descendant, was favored by Emperor Cheng but faced criticism for his arrogance and misconduct, leading to his dismissal. The Zhang family remained prominent through the Han dynasty, with many serving as high officials. The text concludes by praising the Zhang family's enduring favor and virtue, contrasting Zhang Tang's harshness with Anshi's righteousness and humility.

Now he has just arrived in Chen and proclaimed himself king, revealing his selfishness in front of the world.
I hope that the general will not become the king, and quickly lead the troops to the west, and send people to establish descendants of the six countries and establish party members for himself.
In this way, the violent Qin can be eliminated without fighting, you can occupy Xianyang and issue orders to the princes everywhere, and the great cause of proclaiming emperor can be completed.
If he were to become the king in Chen County now, I am afraid that people in the world would become disloyal.
Chen She refused to listen, so he set up his own business.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu further advised King Chen: Your Majesty launched an uprising from Liang and Chu in order to invade Guanzhong and had no time to capture Hebei.
We have been to the State of Zhao before and are very familiar with the heroes of the State of Zhao. Please let us lead a team to capture the territory of the State of Zhao by surprise.
King Chen agreed to their request, and sent the military ministers from Chen whom he admired as generals, with Zhang Er and Chen Yu as captains. He led three thousand soldiers, crossed the Yellow River at Baimajin, and came to the counties in Hebei. He said to the heroes in Naguo: The Qin State imposed tyranny and torture and harmed the people of the world. There were corvees building the Great Wall in the north, and soldiers conquering the Five Ridges in the south. There was turmoil inside and outside, and the people were exhausted.
Excessive levies were collected for military expenses, and the people were depleted of money. Coupled with the harsh criminal laws, fathers and sons in the world could not protect each other.
Now King Chen holds high the banner of righteousness and advocates for the world, and the people all respond. Every family got angry and vented their resentment. The magistrates and county magistrates of each county were killed, and the county guards and county lieutenants were killed in each county.
Now the Chu regime was established, he proclaimed himself king in Chen County, and sent Wu Guang and Zhou Wen to lead a million-strong army to the west to attack Qin. Under such circumstances, those who cannot achieve the feat of becoming a lord are not heroes in the world.
Now is a good opportunity to use the power of the people of the world to attack those unrighteous monarchs, to avenge my father and brother, and to complete the feat of owning land and dominating one country.
The heroes all thought this was correct.
So he expanded his army while marching and added tens of thousands more soldiers. The military minister named himself Lord Wu Xin.
They captured more than a dozen cities in the land, and the rest defended the cities and refused to surrender.
So he led his army to attack Fan Yang in the northeast direction.
Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang, persuaded the county magistrate Xu Gong to surrender to Lord Wu Xin, and also persuaded Lord Wu Xin to make the magistrate of Fanyang a marquis.
The incident is recorded in "The Biography of Kuai Tong".
When Zhao heard about this, more than thirty cities surrendered without fighting.
When they came to Handan, Zhang Er and Chen Yu heard that Zhou Zhang's army had entered the pass and was defeated when they attacked the theater. They also heard that the generals from all walks of life attacked the city and captured the territory for King Chen, but they were killed because someone else made a speech in front of King Chen.
In addition, Zhang Er and Chen Yu complained that King Chen did not appoint them as generals, but made them captains, so they proposed to the military officials: King Chen may not necessarily appoint the descendants of the Six Kingdoms as kings.
Now that the general has captured dozens of cities across the land and is stationed alone in Hebei, he may not be able to rule unless he becomes king.
Moreover, the King of Chen believed the slander and ordered you to return to Chen. I am afraid you will not be able to escape disaster.
I hope the general will not miss this opportunity.
Wu Chen accepted this suggestion and declared himself King of Zhao.
Chen Yu was appointed as the general and Zhang Er as the prime minister.
Wu Chen sent someone to report to King Chen. King Chen was furious and wanted to kill Wu Chen and his family, and then send troops to attack.
King Chen's prime minister, Lord Fang, remonstrated and said: "Qin has not yet been eliminated, and now we are killing the families of military officials and others. This is tantamount to establishing another enemy like Qin."
It is better to take advantage of the situation and send people to congratulate them, so that the military officials can immediately lead the army to the west to attack Qin.
King Chen followed his strategy and placed only the military officials and other family members under house arrest in the palace. He named Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao the king of Chengdu, sent envoys to congratulate Zhao, and urged the Zhao army to march westward and enter the pass.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu advised the military officials: Your Majesty, you are proclaimed king of Zhao State not because of Chu's wish, but because of expediency, you came to congratulate the king.
As long as Chu State destroys Qin, it will definitely send troops to attack.
I hope that King Tang will not send troops to the west, but will capture Yan and Dai in the north, and Hanoi in the south to expand his country's territory.
If Zhao was guarded by the Yellow River in the south and Yan and Dai were in the north, even if Chu defeated Qin, he would not dare to send troops to capture it.
King Zhao thought this was correct. Instead of sending troops westward, he sent Han Guang to attack Yan, Li Liang to attack Changshan, and Zhang Wei to attack Shangdang.
Han Guang entered Yan, and the people of Yan supported him as king of Yan.
King Zhao, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu led their troops to station at the border of Yan, preparing to attack Yan.
King Tang went out once and was captured by the Yan army.
The generals of the State of Yan imprisoned King Zhao as a hostage and demanded that the State of Zhao cede the land to Yan before returning it to King Zhao.
The envoys sent by Zhao were all killed by Yan, who insisted on letting Zhao cede territory.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu were worried about this.
A servant in the army said to his roommate: I am going on a mission for the second Duke to convince Yan that he can come back with King Zhao.
His roommates all laughed at him and said, "The envoys you sent were killed every time. How could you save King Tong?"
He came to the camp of the Yan army and was received by the general of the Yan army. The servant asked the Yan general: "Do you know what I want to do?"
Yan Jiang replied: I want to get your King Zhao back.
Question: Do you know what kind of people Zhang Er and Chen Yu are?
General Yan said: A worthy person.
Asked again: Do you know what their purpose is?
Yan Jiang replied: I want to save their king Tang.
Zhao's servant smiled and said, "You don't know what they really think."
At that time, Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu captured dozens of cities in the country without using any troops. All three of them wanted to ascend the throne of the king.
How can the status of a monarch and a minister be compared?
Considering that the general situation had just stabilized, he first established the military minister as king based on his age to stabilize the people of Zhao.
Now that the country is stable, the two of them also want to divide the country and become kings on their own, but the opportunity is not yet ripe.
Now you imprison King Tread. On the surface, the two of them want to save King Tread, but in fact they hope that Yan will kill King Zhao so that they can divide the land of Zhao and become king.
With the strength of Zhao State, it can easily defeat Yan State, let alone two wise kings united. If you attack the State of Yan on the charge of killing King Tiao, the State of Yan will soon be destroyed.
General Yan thought his words were reasonable, so he returned King Zhao.
The servant himself drove back with King Zhao.
After Li Liang captured Changshan, he came back and reported to King T'ao, who ordered Li Liang to capture Taiyuan.
Li Liang led his troops to Shiyi, but it was difficult to advance because Qin was heavily guarded at Jingxing.
The leader of the Qin army lied that Qin II sent an envoy to Li Liang to send an unsealed letter. The letter said: Li Liang once followed me, and I use him very much. If Li Liang can rebel against Zhao and submit to Qin, he will be forgiven of Li Liang's sins and given a high official and generous salary.
Li Liang was also very suspicious when he saw the letter. Don't believe it.
So he returned to Handan, preparing to ask for military support.
On the way, I met Wang Tong's sister, followed by more than a hundred people.
Li Liang saw it from a distance and thought it was King Zhao, so he knelt down by the road.
King Zhao's sister was drunk and did not know that he was a general, so she sent a knight to thank Li Liang.
Li Liang has always had a high status. After he got up, he felt that he had lost face in front of his subordinates.
One of the followers said: "Everyone in the world is against Qin. Whoever has the ability will be the first to become king."
Besides, the status of King Tang has always been lower than that of the general. Now that their girl dares not to get out of the car and salute the general when she sees him, please let us chase her and kill her!
Because Li Liang received Qin's letter, he had the idea of ​​​​anti-Zhao but was hesitant. After hearing this, he was furious and immediately sent people to hunt down King Zhao's sister, and led the army to attack Handan.
Handan was completely unprepared, and Li Liangjing killed the military minister.
Many people in Tongguo informed Zhang Er and Chen Yu, so they were able to escape. They packed up the remaining Tong army and gathered tens of thousands of troops.
A guest advised Zhang Er and Chen Yu: "You two are from a foreign land. It is difficult to get the people of Zhao to join you." It would be better to establish the descendants of King Zhao of the Six Kingdoms as kings and complete the great cause of restoration in the name of assisting him.
So he found Zhao's descendant Dan Xie, made him the king of Dan, and lived in Xindu.
Li Liang raised his troops to attack Chen Yu, but was defeated by Chen Yu.
Li Liang fled to Qin general Zhang Han.
Zhang Han led his army to Handan, moved the people in Nabu to Hanoi, and razed the city of Handan to the ground.
Zhang Er and Wang Danxie fled to Julu City together and were surrounded by Wang Li.
Chen Yu gathered Changshan's army in the north, added tens of thousands of people, and stationed himself north of Julu.
Zhang Han was stationed at Jiyuan, south of Julu, and built a channel on the river to transport military supplies for Wang Li.
Wang Li's army had sufficient food and immediately attacked Julu. However, Julu City ran out of food. Zhang Er repeatedly sent people to ask Chen Yu to send troops to relieve the siege. Chen Yu believed that his troops were too small to compete with the Qin soldiers and did not dare to send troops.
After being besieged for several months, Zhang Er was furious and resentful of Chen Yu. He sent Zhang Dao and Chen Shi to rebuke Chen Yu and said: "You and I were life-and-death friends at first, but now the lives of King Zhao and I are at stake. You have tens of thousands of troops, but you refuse to save us. Why don't you rush to the Qin army and die with us?"
Maybe there is still a glimmer of hope for survival.
Chen Yu said: I don’t want to die together, but I want to avenge King Zhao and Jun Zhang.
If everyone goes to die now, it is equivalent to sending meat into the tiger's mouth. What good will it do?
Zhang Yan and Chen Shi said: The situation is urgent now. We can only keep our word through life and death. How can we care about what will happen in the future?
Chen Yu said: It doesn't matter if I die, but what's the benefit?
So they sent 5,000 men, led by Zhang Dao and Chen Shi, to attack the Qin army, but the entire army was destroyed.
During the rest of the time, Yan, Qi, and Chu heard that King Zhao was in danger and all came to help him.
Zhang Ao also regained the land of Dai in the north, recruited more than 10,000 people, and set up camp near Chen Yu's army.
Xiang Yu's army blocked Zhang Han's passage many times, causing Wang Li's army to lack food and grass.
Xiang Yu's entire army crossed the river and defeated Zhang Han's army.
Only then did the armies of various princes dare to attack the Qin army and captured Wang Li.
Zhang Er and Tan Xie were rescued from Julu. As soon as Zhang Er met Chen Yu, he blamed Chen Yu and asked where Zhang Yan and Chen Shi were.
Chen Yu said: Zhang Yan and Chen Shi asked me to fight to the death with the Qin army. I asked them to lead five thousand people to attack the Qin army to try, but the entire army was destroyed.
Zhang Er didn't believe it, thinking that Chen Yu had killed the two men, and questioned Chen Yu many times.
Chen Yu said angrily: I didn't expect your resentment towards me to be so deep!
Do you think I can't bear to part with this title of general?
So he took off the seal and asked to return it to Zhang Er, but Zhang Er refused to accept it.
When Chen Yu went to the toilet, a guest advised Zhang Er: "If you hear God's gift but refuse to accept it, there will be no good consequences."
Now Chen Yu is giving you the seal and ribbon. If you don't accept it, it will be unlucky to go against God's will.
Hurry up and accept it!
Zhang Er then wore Chen Yu's seal and ribbon and recruited Chen Yu's subordinates.
When Chen Yu came back and saw this situation, he complained that Zhang Er refused to give in, and left angrily.
Zhang Er then took over Chen Yu's army.
Chen Yu and hundreds of his followers went to the lakes and swamps along the Yellow River to engage in hunting and fishing.
From then on, there was resentment between Zhang Er and Chen Yu.
Zhao Xie, the king of Zhao, returned to Xindu.
Zhang Er followed Xiang Yu into the pass.
When Xiang Yu divided the princes, Zhang Er made many friends and many people praised him.
Xiang Yu often heard that Zhang Er was a virtuous person, so he separated a land from the Zhao Kingdom, made Zhang Er the King of Changshan, and established the capital of Xindu, which was renamed Xiangguo.
Chen Yu's old guests all told Xiang Yu: "Chen Yu and Zhang Er have also made great contributions to the state of Zhao."
Xiang Yu thought that Chen Yu did not follow him into the Pass, and when he heard that he was now in Nanpi, he conferred three counties near Nanpi on Chen Yu, and changed the title of Tang Wang Tang Xie to Dai Wang, and moved the capital to Dai County.
When Zhang Er returned to his kingdom, Chen Yu became even more angry and said: "Zhang Er and I have equal merits. Now he has been made a king, and I have been made a marquis."
When Tian Rong of the Qi State betrayed the Chu State, Chen Yu sent an envoy Xia Shuo to persuade Tian Rong: Xiang Yu is the ruler of the world, but it is unfair. He gave good lands to other kings and generals, but moved King Tread to a bad place. King Tread still lives in Dai County!
I hope you can lend me some troops and would like to use Nanpi as a vassal screen.
Tian Rongzheng wanted to establish party members, so he sent troops to Chen Yu.
Chen Yu recruited soldiers from three counties to attack Zhang Er, the king of Changshan.
Zhang Er was defeated and fled, saying: The King of Han and I have friendship, but Xiang Yu's power is strong, and I am entrusted by King Xiang, so I plan to go to Chu.
Duke Gan said: When the king of Han entered the pass, the five stars in the sky gathered in the east well.
Shujing is a divided territory of Qin, and whoever arrives first will become hegemonic.
Although Chu is now powerful, the world still belongs to Han in the end.
So Zhang Er fled to Han Dynasty.
The king of Han led his troops to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties and surrounded Zhang Han in Feiqiu.
Zhang Er paid homage to the King of Han, who treated him very favorably.
Chen Yu defeated Zhang Er, regained all the land, and brought the king back from Dai County, where he was still the king. King Zhao was grateful to Chen Yu and named him acting king.
Chen Yu thought that the King of Zhao was weak and the country was in the early stages of peace, so he stayed to assist the King of Zhao, and sent the Prime Minister Guo Xia to garrison Dai.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, King Shujin of Han attacked the state of Chu. He sent someone to inform Zhao, asking him to send troops to attack Chu together.
Chen Yu said: I will send troops only if the Han kills Zhang Er.
So the king of Han found a man who looked like Zhang Er, killed him, and gave his head to Chen Yu, who then sent troops to aid Mo.
As a result, the Han army was defeated by the Chu army west of Pengcheng. Chen Yu heard about Zhang Er's fake death and betrayed Mo.
Han sent Zhang Er and Han Xin to capture Zhao's Jingxing, killed Chen Yu at the bank of the Sang River, and pursued him to Xiangguo and killed the king of Zhao, Dan Xie.
In the summer of the fourth year, Mo made Zhang Er the king of Tong.
In the autumn of the fifth year, Zhang Er died, and the Han Dynasty named him Mi King Jing.
His son Zhang Ao inherited the throne and married Princess Lu Yuan, the eldest daughter of Emperor Gaozu, as his queen.
In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu came to Zhao from Pingcheng. King Tong personally served him with food and drinks in the morning and evening, with a very humble attitude and the courtesy of a son-in-law.
But Gaozu sat there and shouted and scolded him loudly, looking down on him very much.
The prime minister, Guan Gao and Zhao Wu, was over sixty years old. He was a former disciple of Zhang Er. He said angrily: Our king is really a cowardly king!
He advised Zhang Ao: "There are many heroes in the world, and the talented ones should be the first to be kings." Now you are very respectful to Gaozu, but Gaozu is rude to you. Please let us kill him for you.
After hearing this, King Zhao bit his finger and it bled, and said, "How could you say such a thing!"
My father lost his country, but it was Gaozu who helped him to restore his country, and De Ze was passed down to future generations. All this is the power of the emperor.
I hope you won't say such things again.
Guan Gao and more than a dozen people discussed among themselves and said: We were wrong.
Our king is a loyal elder who refuses to betray his obligations.
But we can't stand insults. Now Gaozu insults our King Zhao, so he wants to kill him. What does this have to do with our king?
If things succeed, let's vent our anger for the king; if things fail, then we should bear the blame ourselves.
In the eighth year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu passed through Shuyuan and visited the country.
Guan Gao sent people to hide in the wall of Bairen County Hall, preparing to wait for an opportunity to kill Hu Zu.
When Emperor Gaozu arrived in Bairen and wanted to stay overnight, he suddenly felt something moved and asked: "What county is this?" Answer: Bairen County.
Zhitan said: The Bai people are forced by others.
So he left without staying overnight.
In the ninth year of Han Dynasty, Guan Gao's enemies learned of their plan and reported him.
So Gaozu arrested King Zhao and other people who were trying to rebel.
A dozen people including Chang Wu rushed to commit suicide by cutting their necks. Only Zhishang cursed angrily: Who told you to do this?
Now Yusi has not rebelled, but he has been arrested together. If you are dead, who will prove that King Zhao did not rebel?
Together with King Zhao, they were taken to Ken'an in a sealed prison car.
Guan Gao said to the jailer: "This is what we people did. King Zhao doesn't know."
The jailer beat him thousands of times with whips and stung him with red-hot iron. Guan Gao was covered with wounds, but he didn't say a word.
Empress Lu said several times that King Zhao was the husband of Princess Lu Yuan and would not rebel.
Emperor Gaozu said angrily: If Zhang Ao ruled the world, would he care about your daughter?
Tingwei reported Guan Gao's confession to Emperor Gaozu, and Emperor Gaozu said: "What a strong man!"
Anyone who is familiar with him can ask him privately.
Zhongdafu Xiegong said: I know him well. He is a person in Zhao who pays attention to honor and integrity and never breaks his promise.
Emperor Gaozu asked Xie Gongzhijie to ask in front of his chair.
Guangao raised his head and looked at Xie Gong, chatting happily as usual.
During the conversation, Duke Xie asked King Zhao if it was true that he had not rebelled.
Guan Gao said: How can a human being not love his parents, wife and children?
Now that all three members of my family are going to be executed for this, will I use my relatives to protect King Tang?
It is indeed because King Tang did not rebel, it was just what we did.
He told the whole story in detail and the situation that King Tong didn't know about at all.
So Duke Xie told Gaozu what Guan Gao said, and Gaozu pardoned King Zhao.
Emperor Gaozu appreciated Guangao's ability and courage to act and keep his word, so he asked Duke Xie to tell Guangao: "Zhang Ao has been released. The emperor appreciates you very much, so he pardons you."
Guan Gao said: The reason why I will not die is to prove that King Tang did not rebel.
Now that King Tong has been released, my responsibility has been fulfilled.
But as a minister with a reputation for usurpation, how could he still have the dignity to serve the emperor?
So he cut his neck and committed suicide.
After Zhang Fang was released from prison, he still respected Princess Lu Yuan as before, and was named Marquis of Xuanping by Emperor Gaozu.
At that time, Emperor Gaozu appreciated the guests of the king very much. They were either appointed as prime ministers of the princes or as county guards.
It is recorded in "The Biography of Uncle Tian".
By the time of Xiaohui, Gaohou, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, the descendants of King Zhao's guests had become officials worth two thousand shi.
At the beginning, during the reign of Emperor Xiaohui, King Hui of Qi dedicated Chengyang County to Princess Lu Yuan and honored her as the Queen Mother.
In the first year of the reign of Emperor Gao, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan passed away.
Six years later, Zhang Ao, the Marquis of Xuanping, also passed away.
Empress Dowager Lu appointed Zhang Ao's son Zhang Yan as King of Lu because his mother was the Queen Mother of Qi.
Empress Lu sympathized with Zhang Yan's young age and frailty, so she granted Zhang Ao's two sons from his first marriage the title of Marquis of Lechang and Zhang Chi as Marquis of Xindu.
After Empress Gao died, the ministers killed many of Empress Lu's people. The king of Lu and the second prince were deposed.
After Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, he granted the title of Marquis of Nangong to the original Lu King Zhang Yan.
After Zhang Yan's death, his son Zhang Sheng succeeded to the throne.
By the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Sheng was removed from his title for being convicted, and the feudal state was abolished.
During the Yuanguang period, Zhang Guangguo, Zhang Yan's grandson, was granted the title of Marquis of Suiling.
After his death, his son Zhang Chang succeeded to the throne.
During the Taichu period, Zhang Chang was dismissed from his title for committing the crime of disrespect, and his feudal state was abolished.
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty of Xiaoping, in order to promote prosperity, Zhang Qingji, the great-great-grandson of Zhang Ao, was granted the title of Marquis of Xuanping, with thousands of households in the city.
Praising said: Zhang Er and Chen Yu are recognized as sages by the world. Their guests and servants are all heroes in the world. No matter which country they are in, they all have the status of minister.
But Zhang Er and Chen Yu trusted each other when they were poor and humble at first, and they were close friends of life and death. Is there anything to doubt?
When they had high positions and competed for power, they finally killed each other. Why were they so admiring and trusting in the past, but now they betray each other?
The ancients were ashamed of being a snobbish friend. This is probably what they are talking about.
summary:
Zhang Er, a native of Daliang, was once a retainer of Wei nobleman Wuji. After losing his household registration, he wandered to Waihuang, where a wealthy family's daughter left her husband on the advice of her father's guest and married Zhang Er with a substantial dowry. This allowed him to befriend many guests and become the magistrate of Waihuang County. Chen Yu, also from Daliang, was a Confucian scholar who married into a wealthy family in Zhao. He regarded Zhang Er as a father figure, and they formed a life-and-death friendship. When Emperor Gaozu was a commoner, he had ties with Zhang Er.

After Qin destroyed Wei, a reward was offered for Zhang Er and Chen Yu, so they changed their names and became gatekeepers in Chendi. When a minor official whipped Chen Yu for a mistake, Zhang Er stopped him from retaliating, advising patience. When Chen She revolted, Zhang Er and Chen Yu joined him. They advised Chen She not to declare himself king prematurely but to establish descendants of the six states to win support. Chen She ignored them and made himself king. Later, they persuaded Chen She to let them lead troops to capture Zhao territory. They recruited soldiers and won over local heroes, capturing many cities. Wu Chen declared himself King of Zhao, with Chen Yu as general and Zhang Er as prime minister. Chen She initially opposed but later confirmed Wu Chen's title under advice.

Wu Chen was captured by Yan forces, but a clever servant convinced the Yan general that Zhang Er and Chen Yu secretly wanted Wu Chen dead to divide Zhao, so Yan released him. Li Liang, a Zhao general, rebelled after feeling insulted by Wu Chen's sister, killed Wu Chen, and attacked Handan. Zhang Er and Chen Yu escaped, gathered troops, and established Zhao Xie, a descendant of Zhao royalty, as king. Li Liang was defeated by Chen Yu and fled to Qin general Zhang Han, who razed Handan.

Zhang Er and Zhao Xie were besieged in Julu by Qin forces. Chen Yu, stationed nearby, refused to send troops, believing his forces too weak. Zhang Er sent envoys to rebuke him, but Chen Yu only sent 5,000 men, who were annihilated. After Xiang Yu defeated the Qin army, Zhang Er blamed Chen Yu for the deaths of the envoys, leading to a bitter rift. Chen Yu offered his seal to Zhang Er, who accepted it after persuasion, taking command of Chen Yu's army. Chen Yu left in anger, and the two became enemies.

After Xiang Yu divided the realm, Zhang Er was made King of Changshan, while Chen Yu received only three counties. Chen Yu, resentful, allied with Tian Rong of Qi to attack Zhang Er, who fled to Han. The Han king treated him well. Chen Yu later demanded Zhang Er's death before aiding Han, but the Han king sent a fake head. After Han's defeat, Chen Yu learned the truth and abandoned Han. Han later sent Zhang Er and Han Xin to defeat and kill Chen Yu and Zhao Xie. Zhang Er was made King of Zhao and died in the fifth year of Han. His son Zhang Ao succeeded him and married Princess Lu Yuan.

Emperor Gaozu treated Zhang Ao rudely, angering his ministers Guan Gao and Zhao Wu, who plotted to kill Gaozu. Zhang Ao refused to participate. The plot failed, and Guan Gao took full blame, enduring torture to prove Zhang Ao's innocence. Gaozu eventually pardoned Zhang Ao and admired Guan Gao's loyalty, but Guan Gao committed suicide. Zhang Ao remained respectful to Princess Lu Yuan and was made Marquis of Xuanping. His descendants held various titles, though some were later stripped due to crimes.

The historian comments that Zhang Er and Chen Yu were initially life-and-death friends but turned against each other over power, illustrating the shame of fair-weather friendships.

translation:
Zhang Liang's courtesy name is Zifang, and his ancestors are Korean.
My grandfather opened land and became the prime minister of Han Zhaohou, King Xuanhui and King Xiangai.
His father, Zhang Ping, was the prime minister of King Li and King Hui.
In the twenty-third year of King Hui's reign, Zhang Ping died. Twenty years after his death, Qin subjugated Han.
Zhang Liang was young and had not been an official in Han.
When Han died, Zhang Liang had 300 slaves in his family. His younger brother died without being buried. He used all his family wealth to seek assassins to kill the King of Qin and avenge Han because his father had been the Prime Minister of Han for five generations.
Zhang Liang once studied etiquette in Huaiyang. He traveled eastward to meet Lord Canghai and found a strong man who made an iron vertebra weighing 120 kilograms.
The Emperor of Qin went on a tour to Bolang Sand. Zhang Liang and his assassins ambushed the Emperor of Qin and accidentally hit the passenger car.
Emperor Qin was furious and searched the world on a large scale, eager to find the thief.
Zhang Liang then changed his name and fled to Xiapi.
Zhang Liang once had time to take a leisurely stroll on the Xiapi Bridge. An old man, wearing coarse cloth, walked up to Zhang Liang and deliberately dropped his shoes under the bridge. He turned back and said to Zhang Liang: "Children, go down and pick up your shoes!"
Zhang Liang was surprised and wanted to beat him.
Because he was old, he endured it and went down to pick up shoes, so he knelt down and offered them to him.
The old man put on his feet and walked away with a smile.
Zhang Liang was very surprised.
The old man left for about a mile, then came back and said: Young people deserve instruction.
Five days later, at dawn, I'll be waiting for you in Xianbao.
Zhang Liang felt strange, knelt down and said: OK.
Five days later, Zhang Liang left at Pingming.
The old man had arrived first and angrily said: "I made an appointment with the old man and arrived late. Why?"
Come on, come see you early in five days.
Five days later, when the rooster crows, go.
The old man arrived first again and yelled angrily: "You're late, what's the matter?"
Go, come back early in five days.
Five days later, Zhang Liang went there in the middle of the night.
After a while, the old man also came and said with a smile: "It should be the same."
He took out a book and said: If you read it, you can become the teacher of the king.
Rise ten years later.
Thirteen years later, the young man came to see me. The yellow stone at the foot of Jibei Gucheng Mountain was me.
Then he left and disappeared.
After dawn, I read the book. It was "Tai Gong's Art of War".
Zhang Liang was surprised and often recited it.
Living in Xiapi, he loves to fight against injustice.
Xiang Bo once killed someone and took refuge with Zhang Liang.
Ten years later, Chen She and others started an uprising, and Zhang Liang also gathered more than a hundred young men.
Jing Ju established himself as the false king of Chu and stayed in Liu.
Zhang Liang wanted to follow him and met Pei Gong on the road.
Peigong led thousands of people to capture Xiapi, and Tuidan followed him.
Centipede worshiped the retired emperor and became the general of the stable.
Egg King lectured Pei Gong on "Tai Gong's Art of War" many times. Pei Gong was very happy and often adopted his strategies.
Zhang Liang told others, but they didn't understand.
Zhang Liang said: Pei Gong is probably a talent given by heaven.
Then he followed him and never left.
Duke Pei went to Xue, met with Xiang Liang, and together they supported King Huai of Chu.
Zhang Liang persuaded Xiang Liang: "You have established a descendant of Chu. Mr. Han, Hengyang Jun, has become a virtuous man. He can be established as king and have many party members."
Xiang Liang sent Zhang Liang to find Han Cheng and establish him as King of Han.

From then on, there was a conflict between King Xiao of Liang and Yafu.
After returning, he appointed Taiwei officers.
Five years later, he was promoted to prime minister, and Emperor Jing valued him very much.
The emperor abolished Prince Li. Yafu argued resolutely but failed.
The emperor therefore distanced himself from him.
And every time Liang Xiaowang went to court, he often talked to the Queen Mother about Yafu's shortcomings.
Empress Dowager Dou said: The empress's brother Wang Xin can be made a marquis.
The emperor reproached him and said: In the past, Nanpi and Zhangwu, the first emperors, did not ennoble themselves as marquises, but when their ministers came to the throne, they would do so. Wang Xin could not do so.
Empress Dowager Dou said: In life, everyone acts according to the current situation.
When Dou Changjun was still alive, he could not be granted the title of marquis in the end. After his death, his son Peng Zu was granted the title of marquis.
I regret it very much.
The emperor quickly makes Wang Xin a marquis!
The emperor said: Please allow me to discuss this with the prime minister.
Yafu said: Emperor Gao stipulated that it was not that the Liu family could not be granted the title of king, nor that the Liu family could not be granted the title of marquis without merit.
If he did not abide by the regulations, everyone in the world attacked him. Now, although Wang Xin is the elder brother of the queen, he has no merit and is granted a title, which is against the regulations.
The emperor remained silent and stopped the matter.
Later, King Xu Lu of the Xiongnu and five others surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The emperor wanted to make him a marquis to encourage his descendants.
Yafu said: He betrayed his master and surrendered to your majesty, and your majesty made him a marquis. How can he blame his unruly ministers?
The emperor said: The prime minister's suggestion cannot be adopted.
Then they all conferred the title of marquis on Xulu and others.
Yafu then claimed that the disease was exempting him from the phase.
Soon, the emperor was in the palace and summoned Yafu to reward him with food.
Just a big piece of meat, not chopped meat, and no chopsticks.
Yafu was dissatisfied and turned around to ask the chairman to get his chopsticks.
The emperor looked at him and smiled and said: Doesn't this satisfy your needs?
Yafu took off his hat and apologized to the emperor. The emperor said: Get up.
Yafu walked out quickly in small steps.
The emperor saw him off and said: He is dissatisfied and not a minister of the young master.
Not long after, Yafu's son bought five hundred Shangfang Jiaxun from the work officer for his father, preparing to be buried with him.
The hired workers work hard and are not paid.
The hired workers knew that he secretly bought the emperor's utensils, resented him and informed the court that he wanted to rebel. The matter affected Yafu.
After the letter was submitted, the emperor asked it to be handed over to the officials for investigation.
The officials used the official documents to question Yafu, but Yafu did not answer.
The emperor scolded him and said: I don't need you to answer.
Summoned to the Tingwei.
Tingwei asked, "Why did you build it?"
Yafu said: What I bought is a burial vessel. How can it be made?
The clerk said: Either you want to rebel on the ground, or you want to rebel underground.
The clerk bullied him even more.
At first, the officials arrested Yafu. Yafu wanted to commit suicide, but his wife stopped him. So before he could commit suicide, he was imprisoned in the court, where he did not eat for five days and died of vomiting blood.
The feudal state was abolished.
A year later, the emperor changed the title of Zhou Jian, another son of Jianghou Zhou Bo, to the title of Pingquhou and succeeded Jianghou.
He passed it on to his son Jiande and became the crown prince and tutor. He was dismissed from office because the amount of money offered as an aide was insufficient.
Later he was found guilty and the feudal state was abolished.
Yafu indeed starved to death.
After his death, the emperor made Wang Xin a marquis.
In the second year of the Yuanshi period of Emperor Ping, in order to inherit the kingdom of Juesi, Zhou Gong, the son of Zhou Bo's great-great-grandson, was granted the title of Marquis of Jiang, with the title of a thousand households in the city.
Zan said: After hearing Zhang Liang's wisdom and bravery, I thought he was tall and majestic, but I didn't know that he looked like a woman.
Therefore, Confucius said that people should be judged by their appearance and made mistakes with Ziyu.
Scholars all suspect ghosts and gods. For example, Zhang Liang got a book from an old man, which was also strange.
Emperor Gaozu was in trouble many times, and Zhang Liang often came to the rescue. Can it be said that it was not God's will?
Chen Ping's ambition was expressed in the society, and he defected to the chaotic Chu and Wei, and finally returned to Yimo and became a counselor.
When he arrived at Empress Lu, many things happened, but Chen Ping was actually safe and managed to live an old age with wisdom.
Wang Ling argued in the court and isolated himself from the world, which was also his own ambition.
When Zhou Bo was a commoner, he was a clumsy and mediocre person. When he became a minister, he helped the country in crisis, killed the surname Lu, established Xiaowen, and became the Yi Zhou of the Han Dynasty. How prominent!
At first, Empress Lu asked about the choice of prime minister. Gaozu said: Chen Ping is resourceful and Wang Ling is a bit straight-forward, so he can assist him; it must be Zhou Bo who can stabilize the Liu family.
He asked the next person again and said, "You can't see anything more than this."
In the end, everyone agreed with these words. What a sage!
summary:
Zhang Liang, courtesy name Zifang, was of Korean ancestry. His grandfather and father served as prime ministers to five generations of Han kings. After Qin conquered Han, Zhang Liang, though young and never an official, used his family wealth to hire an assassin to avenge Han. He ambushed the First Emperor at Bolangsha but struck the wrong carriage. Forced to flee, he changed his name and hid in Xiapi.

On a bridge in Xiapi, an old man deliberately dropped his shoe and ordered Zhang Liang to retrieve it. Zhang Liang complied despite his initial anger. The old man later gave him a book, the "Tai Gong's Art of War," and predicted he would become a teacher to a king. Zhang Liang studied it diligently.

During the uprisings, Zhang Liang gathered followers and joined Pei Gong (Liu Bang). He frequently advised Pei Gong using the Art of War, and Pei Gong often adopted his strategies. Zhang Liang believed Pei Gong was a heaven-sent talent and remained with him. He later persuaded Xiang Liang to establish Han Cheng as King of Han, and Zhang Liang became Han's Minister of Education.

Zhang Liang advised Pei Gong against attacking Qin's strong forces directly, suggesting instead to bribe the Qin general and attack when the troops were lax. This led to a great victory and Qin's surrender. When Pei Gong was tempted by the luxuries of Qin's palace, Zhang Liang urged him to leave, warning that indulgence would harm his cause. Pei Gong heeded this and returned to Bashang.

During the Hongmen Banquet crisis, Zhang Liang refused to abandon Pei Gong and helped reconcile with Xiang Yu through Xiang Bo. Later, when Pei Gong became King of Han, Zhang Liang advised burning the plank road to show no intention of returning east, stabilizing Xiang Yu. He also recommended using Han Xin, Peng Yue, and King Bu of Jiujiang to defeat Chu.

Zhang Liang opposed enfeoffing descendants of the six kingdoms, arguing it would undermine support for the Han king. He convinced the king to destroy the seals prepared for this purpose. He also advised granting titles to Han Xin and others to secure their loyalty.

After the Han dynasty was established, Zhang Liang was granted the title of Marquis of Liu. He declined a larger fief, citing his lack of military exploits. He advised the emperor to first enfeoff Yong Chi, a man the emperor resented, to reassure other generals and prevent rebellion. He also supported Liu Jing's proposal to make Guanzhong the capital, arguing its strategic advantages.

When the emperor wanted to depose the crown prince, Zhang Liang initially refused to intervene. Pressed by Empress Lü, he suggested recruiting four reclusive sages to support the prince. The emperor, seeing the prince had their support, abandoned the plan. Zhang Liang later withdrew from worldly affairs, studying Taoism and seeking immortality. He died six years after Emperor Gao, receiving the posthumous title Marquis Wencheng.

Chen Ping, from a poor family, was known for his height and good looks. He married a wealthy woman after a local elder recognized his potential. During village festivals, he divided meat evenly, saying he would govern the world similarly.

Chen Ping served Wei and then Chu, but fled both when his advice was ignored or he feared execution. He joined Liu Bang, who appointed him a captain despite objections from other generals. Chen Ping explained his past changes of allegiance by saying his former masters could not use him properly. He proposed using gold to sow discord among Xiang Yu's advisors, leading to Xiang Yu's suspicion of his strategist Fan Zeng.

Chen Ping advised the emperor to capture Han Xin by feigning a visit to Yunmeng, rather than attacking him directly. He also helped the emperor escape a siege at Pingcheng using a secret plan. He served as a strategist for six major campaigns, each time increasing his fief.

After Emperor Gao's death, Chen Ping pretended to indulge in wine and women to avoid suspicion from Empress Lü. He outwardly complied with her appointing Lü family members as kings, but later conspired with Zhou Bo to eliminate the Lü clan and establish Emperor Wen. As prime minister, he famously told the emperor that a prime minister's role is to oversee officials, not handle specific tasks.

Zhou Bo, a simple man from Pei, began as a funeral flutist. He followed Liu Bang from the start, distinguishing himself in battle by often being the first to scale city walls. He served as a general under Emperor Gao, pacifying many regions and capturing numerous enemy officials.

After Emperor Gao's death, Zhou Bo served as Grand Commandant. When Empress Lü died, he and Chen Ping plotted to eliminate the Lü clan. Zhou Bo, as commander of the Northern Army, rallied the soldiers by showing them his seal and declaring loyalty to the Liu family. They killed the Lü kings and established Emperor Wen.

Zhou Bo became Right Chancellor but feared his power and resigned. Later accused of rebellion, he was imprisoned and bribed a jailer for advice. He was released after his wife, the emperor's daughter, testified for him. He remarked on the harshness of jailers. His son Zhou Yafu succeeded him.

Zhou Yafu, known for his strict military discipline, refused to let Emperor Wen enter his camp without proper protocol, earning the emperor's praise as a "true general." During the Rebellion of the Seven States, he advised letting Liang bear the enemy's attack while cutting off their supply routes. He ignored the emperor's order to save Liang, focusing on his strategy, which ultimately defeated Wu and Chu.

As prime minister, Yafu opposed enfeoffing the queen's brother and Xiongnu defectors, arguing it violated Emperor Gao's rules. The emperor overruled him. Later, Yafu's son bought imperial burial items, and Yafu was accused of rebellion. He starved himself in prison, fulfilling a prophecy that he would die of hunger.

The historian comments that Zhang Liang, despite his wisdom, looked like a woman. Chen Ping used clever schemes to survive the Lü clan's rule. Zhou Bo, though crude, stabilized the Han dynasty, fulfilling Emperor Gao's prediction that he would secure the Liu family.

translation:
Zhang Qian was from Hanzhong. During the Jianyuan period, he was appointed as Lang Guan.
People who surrendered to the Xiongnu at that time said that the Xiongnu defeated the Yuezhi King and used the Yuezhi King's head as a drinking vessel. The Yuezhi fled and resented the Huns because they had no one to fight with them.
The Han Dynasty was planning to engage in a war to eliminate the Xiongnu. When they heard this, they wanted to send people as envoys to the Yuezhi. However, the Xiongnu Kingdom was the only way to go, so they recruited people who could go as envoys.
Zhang Qian was recruited as an envoy to Yuezhi as a Langguan. He left Longxi with Gan Fu, Tangyi's servant.
Passing by the Huns, he was intercepted by the Huns and sent to the Shanyu in a conveyor.
Shanyu said: The Yueshi are to the north of me. How can the Han Dynasty people send envoys there?
If I want to send someone as an envoy to South Vietnam, will the Han Dynasty let our people pass by?
Zhang Qian was detained for more than ten years. He married him and gave birth to a son. However, Zhang Qian still insisted on the Han Dynasty and still maintained his status as an envoy.
Because he lived in the western part of the Huns, Zhang Qian took the opportunity to lead his subordinates to flee towards the Yueshi. After running west for dozens of days, we arrived in Dawan.
Dawan heard that the Han Dynasty was rich in wealth and wanted to have contacts with the Han Dynasty but could not find the opportunity. He was very happy to see Zhang Qian and asked him where he was going.
Zhang Qian said: We were sent as an envoy to the Yuezhi on behalf of the Han Dynasty, but the Huns blocked the road and refused to allow passage. Now we are fleeing to your country. I hope that the king can send someone to lead the way and send us there. If we can reach the Yuezhi, after we return to the Han Dynasty, the property that the Han Dynasty will give to the king will be indescribable.
Dawan thought it was okay, so he sent them there and sent translators and guides for them.
They were sent to Kangju, who sent them to Dayuezhi in a conveyor.
At this time, the original King of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his wife was made king.
Da Yuezhi had made Daxia surrender and ruled over it.
The land there was fertile, the produce was abundant, there was no intrusion, and they felt relaxed and happy. They considered themselves far away from the Han Dynasty and did not want to get close to the Han Dynasty. They had no intention of revenge against the Huns. From Yuezhi to Daxia, Zhang Qian never received a clear statement from the Yuezhi King.
After staying for more than a year, I had to return. Along the Nanshan Mountains, I wanted to return to the Han Dynasty from the place where the Qiang people lived, but I was intercepted by the Xiongnu again.
After being detained for more than a year, it happened that the Chanyu died and the Xiongnu country was in chaos. Zhang Qian fled back to the Han Dynasty with his Hun wife and Tangyi Ganfu.
The imperial court granted him the official position of Taizhong Taifu, and Tangyi Ganfu also became the envoy.
Zhang Qian is strong and perseverant, magnanimous and sincere in his treatment of others. He is liked by ethnic minorities.
Tangyi's father was a Huns who was good at archery. When he was extremely poor, he shot animals for food.
At the beginning, there were more than a hundred people when Zhang Qian traveled. After thirteen years, only he and Tang Yi's father came back.
Zhang Qian had personally visited places such as Dayuan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, Kangju and other countries. He heard that there were five or six big countries next to these countries. He told Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty one by one about the topography and products of these countries. The contents mentioned are all contained in "The Biography of the Western Regions".
Zhang Qian said: When I was in Daxia, I saw bamboo sticks from Qiong and fine cloth produced in Shu County. I asked them where they got them. The people of Daxia said: Our merchants bought them from the country of Shendu.
Shendu Country is located in the southeast of Daxia, about thousands of miles away.
The custom of Nahuo is to live a settled life, which is the same as that of Daxia, but the terrain is low-lying, humid, and the climate is hot.
People there rode elephants to fight, and the country was bordered by floods. According to my guess, Daxia was about 12,000 miles away from the Han Dynasty and to the southwest of the Han Dynasty.
Now Shendu is thousands of miles southeast of Daxia, and there are products from Shu County. It seems that Shendu is not far from Shu.
It is very dangerous for the envoy to Daxia to pass through the Qiang area. The Qiang people hate the Han Dynasty. If you go a little north, you will be captured by the Huns. If you go from Shu County, it will be a convenient road and there will be no intrusion.
Emperor Mowu heard that Dayuan, Daxia, Parthia and other countries were big countries with many strange products and lived a settled life, which was the same as the customs of the Han Dynasty. However, the military strength is very weak and they value the property of the Han Dynasty. To the north are the Dayuezhi, Kangju and other countries, which have strong military strength. They can be lured to come to see the Emperor of Han by giving them property and benefits.
If we can really do this and use moral power to make them join the Han Dynasty, then the Han Dynasty can expand its territory by more than 10,000 miles. People from some ethnic groups who come to the court will have to go through multiple translations to understand the language. Some ethnic minorities with strange customs will also come to join the Han Dynasty. The prestige and virtue of the Han Dynasty will spread all over the world.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was very happy and thought Zhang Qian's words made sense.
So he ordered envoys to be sent to explore the road through Shu County and Jianwei County, and they set off in four groups at the same time. Starting from Ranchi all the way, starting from Jedudu all the way, starting from Yiheqiong all the way, and starting from Fen all the way, each has a distance of one or two thousand miles.
However, the northern passage was blocked by the clans and Jeduyi, and the southern passage was blocked by Ling and Kunming.
Kunming and other ethnic minorities have no rulers and are good at plundering and stealing. Every time they killed passing Han envoys and took away their property, this road finally failed to open.
However, I heard that about a thousand miles west of Kunming, there is Chengxiang Kingdom, named Dianyue. Some businessmen from Shu County who privately trade goods have been there. So the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom in search of the road to Daxia.
At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to communicate with the southwestern barbarians, but stopped this work because it was too expensive.
When Zhang Qian said that it was possible to reach Daxia via the Southwest Yi, the Han Dynasty began to open up the route to the Southwest Yi.
Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing to attack the Huns as a captain. Because he knew where the water and grass were distributed, the army could not lack supplies, so he made Zhang Qian the Marquis of Bowang.
This year is the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Two years later, Zhang Qian, as a guard, set out from Youbeiping with General Li Guang to fight against the Huns.
General Li was surrounded by the Xiongnu, and the Han army suffered heavy casualties. However, Zhang Qian arrived later than the agreed time and was punished by beheading according to military law. He used his property to redeem himself as a civilian.
This year, Husband General Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu in the west, killing tens of thousands as far as the Qilian Mountains.
In autumn, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his tribe to surrender to the Han Dynasty. As a result, the area from Jincheng, Hexi Corridor, along the Qilian Mountains to Yanze was empty of Xiongnu.
During the Xiongnu period, some scouts might come, but they were very few.
Two years later, the Han Dynasty defeated the Xiongnu Chanyu and rushed to Mobei.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty asked Zhang Qian many times about the situation in Daxia and other countries.
At this time, Zhang Qian had lost the title of Hou, so he replied: When I lived in the Xiongnu, I heard that King Wusun was named Kunmo.
Kunmo's father, Nan Doumi, originally lived in the Qilian Mountains and Dunhuang area with Da Yuezhi, which was a small country.
Dayuezhi attacked and killed Nandoumi and seized his land. The Wusun people fled to the Huns.
Nan Douli's son Kunmo was just born at that time. Fu's father Buju Linghou carried him and fled. On the way, he put him in the grass and went to find food for him. When he came back, he saw a wolf feeding him and a crow hovering next to him with meat in his mouth. He thought Kunmo was a god, so he embraced Kunmo and joined the Huns. The Chanyu liked him and raised him.
After Kunmo grew up, Shanyu returned his father's people to him and asked him to lead troops in war. Kunmo repeatedly made military exploits.
At that time, the Yuezhi had been defeated by the Xiongnu and attacked the king of Sai westward.
The King of Sai moved to distant places during his southern tour, and the Yuezhi people lived in the King of Sai's territory.
After Kunmo's strength grew, he personally asked Shan Yu for permission to avenge his father, and then went west to defeat the Dayue clan.
The Dayuezhi people fled west again and moved to the place where the Daxia people lived.
Kunmo plundered their people and stayed in the land of the Da Yueshi people. His army gradually became stronger, and just when the Xiongnu Chanyu died, he refused to enter the court to serve the Xiongnu again.
The Xiongnu sent troops to attack him but could not defeat him. They even thought Kunmo was a god and stayed away from him.
Now Shan Yu had just been defeated by the Han Dynasty and was in a difficult situation, and Kunmo's original place was uninhabited.
The ethnic minorities are attached to their homeland and are greedy for the property of the Han Dynasty. If we send more property to Wusun at this time to attract them to come to Shubian to live on their original land, and the Han Dynasty sends a princess to King Wusun as his wife, and the two parties form a brotherly relationship, based on the above analysis of the situation, Wusun will definitely listen to our suggestions, then it will be equivalent to cutting off the right arm of the Xiongnu.
By uniting with Wusun, Daxia and other countries west of Wusun can be recruited as your foreign ministers.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty believed that Zhang Qian was right, and awarded Zhang Qian the official position of Lieutenant General. He led 300 people, each with two horses, driving tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, carrying gold and gifts worth tens of millions, and many deputy envoys accompanying him on a mission to Wusun.
If the road is convenient, he will send deputy envoy Chijie to the country next to Wusun.
After Zhang Qian arrived at Wusun, he gave Emperor Wu's gifts to King Wusun and conveyed Emperor Wu's wishes, but failed to obtain a clear statement from King Wusun. The specific content is recorded in "The Biography of the Western Regions". Zhang Qian then sent deputy envoys to Dayuan, Kangju, Yuezhi and Daxia respectively.
King Wusun sent an interpreter and guide to escort Zhang Qian. Wusun envoys of dozens of people and dozens of horses followed Zhang Qian back to the Han Dynasty to thank Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. They took the opportunity to let them inspect the situation of the Han Dynasty and understand the vastness of the Han Dynasty.
Zhang Qian returned to the Han Dynasty and was awarded a senior official.
More than a year later, Zhang Qian passed away.
More than a year later, most of the deputy envoys he sent to Tongdaxia and other countries returned to the Han Dynasty together with the envoys from these countries, and the northwest countries began to communicate with the Han Dynasty.
However, because Zhang Qian opened the way to the Western Regions, those who later went to the Western Regions as envoys followed Zhang Qian's example and were called Bowang Hou, in order to win the trust of foreign countries, and foreigners trusted them.
After that, King Wusun finally married Princess Xuan.
At the beginning, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty opened the Book of Changes for divination and said: The divine horse will come from the northwest.
He thought it was good to get the Wusun horse, so he named it Tianma.
When they got the Dawan Khan-blooded horse again, it was fatter and stronger than the Wusun horse, so they renamed the Wusun horse "Xijima" and the Dawan horse "Tianma".
In addition, the Han Dynasty began to build fortresses from Lingju to the west and established Jiuquan County to facilitate access to various countries in the Western Regions.
The Han Dynasty then sent additional envoys to Anxi, Yancai, Yaxuan, Tiaozhi, and Shendu countries.
Emperor Mowu liked Dayuan horses, and the envoys sent to the Western Regions met each other on the road. There were a large group of hundreds of people and a small group of more than a hundred people. The things they carried completely imitated the grand occasion of Zhang Qian, the Marquis of Bowang.
Later, as they became more familiar with the situation in the Western Regions, the number of envoys in each batch became smaller and smaller.
During the Han Dynasty, there were probably more than ten batches of envoys a year, and as few as five or six batches. They could travel back and forth as far away as eighty or nine years, and in recent years.
At this time, the Han Dynasty had destroyed South Vietnam, and the southwestern barbarians connected with Shu County were shocked. They asked the Han Dynasty to establish a rule there and send officials to govern it.
The Han Dynasty established the counties of Yangke, Yueling, Yizhou, Shenli, and Wenshan in the southwestern Yi. They wanted to use the method of setting up counties in the southwestern Yi to connect the land boundaries and lead to Daxia.
Therefore, the Han Dynasty sent more than ten batches of envoys every year from these newly established counties, but they were once again blocked by the Kunming barbarians. The envoys were killed and the gifts were robbed.
So the Han Dynasty sent troops to attack Kunming and beheaded tens of thousands.
Later, envoys were sent, but they were unable to pass.
Details are contained in "The Biography of Southwest Yi".
Since Zhang Qian opened the road to the Western Regions and gained a distinguished status, those officials have been vying to write letters discussing the strangeness of foreign products and the interests of the envoys, requesting envoys.
Because the Western Regions were remote and far away, not everyone was willing to go there, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty accepted their words and gave them the talisman to go as envoys. He recruited officials and common people regardless of the identity and qualifications of the applicants. He prepared entourages for these people and sent them on their missions, thereby expanding the source of personnel for envoys to the Western Regions.
When these people came back, they would inevitably have plundered and stolen property, and they would have violated the will of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty when performing their missions. Because they were familiar with the situation in the Western Regions, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty would often examine them and punish them with serious crimes, so as to inspire them to work hard to atone for their sins and request to be sent to the Western Regions again.
There are endless reasons for sending envoys to the Western Regions, and they despise breaking the law.
Those officials often praised foreign products. Those who exaggerated to a greater extent were given talisman and were designated as chief envoys, and those who exaggerated to a lesser extent were designated as deputy envoys. Therefore, those who talk nonsense and those who have no good conduct are eager to imitate him.
Most of the envoys kept the gifts given by the emperor to the countries in the Western Regions for themselves, hoping to sell them at a lower price to make a profit.
Foreigners were also disgusted by the Han envoys who spoke untruthfully. They estimated that the Han army would not be able to reach the Han envoys because of the distance, so they cut off the food supply of the Han envoys, leaving them in a difficult situation.
The Han envoys lived in poverty, condemned and complained, and even attacked each other.
Small countries such as Loulan and Gushi were located on strategic transportation routes, and they were particularly powerful in attacking and plundering Han envoys such as Wang Hui, and the Xiongnu troops intercepted Han envoys from time to time.
The envoys argued that conquering these countries would be beneficial to the Han Dynasty, and not conquering them would be harmful to the Han Dynasty. These countries had cities, and their armies were weak and easy to attack.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty sent Zhao Ponu, the Marquis of Piao, to lead tens of thousands of cavalry and troops from various counties in the Western Regions to attack the Xiongnu. All the Xiongnu soldiers fled.
The next year, Zhao Ponu defeated Gu Shi and captured King Loulan.
In the Han Dynasty, border posts were set up from Jiuquan County to Yumen Pass.
The Dawan countries sent envoys to follow the Han envoys to the Han Dynasty. Seeing the vastness of the Han Dynasty, they presented ostrich eggs and Yak Xuan magicians to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was very happy.
The Han envoys exhausted the source of the Yellow River. There were many jade in the mountains there, and the Han envoys collected them and transported them back to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty studied ancient maps and books and named the mountain where the Yellow River originates from Kunlun Mountain.
At this time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty happened to visit the beach many times, and he was surrounded by foreign guests. They would pass through large cities or places with a large number of people, distribute property, cloth, and reward them, and prepare generous gifts for them to show the financial strength of the Han Dynasty.
They performed novelties such as big horns and strange plays, which attracted many onlookers and rewarded them generously. The foreign guests were allowed to see the accumulations in various warehouses of the Han Dynasty, hoping to show the vastness of the Han Dynasty and make them admire and be surprised by the power of the Han Dynasty.
As for increasing the skills of illusionists and increasing the number of tricks and tricks every year, their further rise began in the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Moreover, foreign envoys continued to come and go in an endless stream.
The countries west of Dawan all considered themselves far away from the Han Dynasty and were still proud and indulgent. The Han Dynasty failed to make them surrender, so it maintained contact with them through courtesy exchanges and sent envoys to these countries.
There were many envoys from the Han Dynasty to the Western Regions. Those young envoys often used false words to encourage Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, saying that there were good horses in Ershi City in Dawan and they hid them so that the Han envoys would not see them.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty liked the Wan horse. After hearing about it, he wanted to get it. He sent his warriors and chariots to ask the King of Dayuan to give Ershi City a good horse with a thousand pieces of gold and a golden horse.
Dawan had a lot of property from the Han Dynasty. They discussed with each other: The Han Dynasty is far away from us, and people who pass through the salt marsh area often die. Passing from the north is harassed by the Xiongnu, and there is a lack of water and grass from the south. In addition, there are no cities along the way, and there is often a lack of food.
The Han sent a group of hundreds of people to come, and they often lacked food. More than half died. How could a large army be sent in such a situation?
Besides, the Ershima is Dawan’s BMW.
Finally, he refused to be envoyed to the Han Dynasty.
The envoy of the Han Dynasty was furious, cursed and ran away with broken vertebrae of the golden horse.
The nobles of Dayuan said angrily: The Han envoys despise us too much!
He ordered the Han envoys to leave Dayuan, and asked King Yu Cheng of Shubian to intercept them, kill the Han envoys and seize their belongings.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was furious.
Yao Dinghan and others who had been on an envoy to Dayuan said: Dayuan's soldiers are weak. If nearly three thousand Han troops are used to shoot at them with strong bows and powerful crossbows, they can be defeated.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty had sent Zhao Ponu, the Marquis of Zhao Ye, to attack Loulan, and arrived at Loulan with 700 cavalry first and captured the King of Loulan. Therefore, he thought that what Yao Dinghan and others said was reasonable, and wanted to make the brother of his favorite concubine, Mrs. Li, a marquis, so he appointed Li Guangli as his general to attack Dayuan.
Zhang Qian's grandson Zhang Meng, also known as Ziyou, was quite intelligent. During the Yuan Dynasty, he was the official of Guanglu. He served as an envoy to the Huns and was promoted to Shizhong. He was framed by Shi Xian and committed suicide.
Li Guangli's sister, Mrs. Li, was favored by the emperor and gave birth to King Ai of Changyi.
In the first year of Taichu, Guangli was appointed as the general of the Second Division. He led six thousand cavalry from the vassal state and tens of thousands of young men with bad conduct from the county. He used these troops to attack Dawan. He expected to capture good horses from the city of the Second Division, so he was called "General of the Second Division".
Wang Hui, the former Haohou, led the army and served as a guide.
The troops of the General of the Second Division had already encountered Yanyan to the west. The small countries along the route were in panic and tightly defended their castles. They did not supply the Han army with food and could not be defeated.
Those who can be captured will have food to eat, and those who cannot be captured will have to leave in a few days.
By the time they reached Yucheng, there were only a few thousand soldiers left, and they were all hungry and tired.
They attacked Yucheng City and were defeated, with many casualties.
The general of the Second Division discussed with his left and right: We can't capture it until Yucheng, let alone the capital of King Dawan?
Just retreat with the troops.
It took two years of traveling back and forth. When we returned to Dunhuang, only one-tenth of the soldiers were left.
