summary:
Emperor Xiaojing had fourteen sons by various consorts. Among them, Liu De, the King of Hejian, was a notable scholar who loved ancient texts. He diligently collected books from the people, offering generous compensation for rare copies, amassing a collection as vast as the imperial library. Unlike King Huainan of An, whose books were often useless, Liu De’s collection consisted of pre-Qin classics like the *Zhou Guan*, *Shangshu*, *Rites*, *Mencius*, and *Laozi*, all attributed to Confucius’s seventy disciples. He established doctors for the *Mao Poetry* and *Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Annals*, practiced rituals and music, and adhered to Confucian teachings, attracting many scholars from Shandong. During Emperor Wu’s reign, he presented elegant music and answered over thirty questions from the court with clarity and reason. After reigning for twenty-six years, he died, praised by officials for his uprightness, kindness, and frugality. His descendants ruled Hejian for generations, though later kings like Liu Yuan faced scandal and deposition for cruelty and misconduct, leading to the kingdom’s abolition and restoration under Emperor Cheng.

Other sons of Emperor Xiaojing had varied fates. Liu Rong, the Min King of Linjiang, was once crown prince but was deposed and later committed suicide after being accused of building a palace on temple grounds. Liu Yu, the King of Lu, was known for building palaces and raising dogs and horses, but he had a stutter and disliked literature. His descendant, Liu Gong, destroyed Confucius’s old house to expand his palace but stopped upon hearing music, discovering ancient scriptures in the walls. Liu Fei, the King of Yi in Jiangdu, was a talented youth who fought against Wu during the rebellion, but later became arrogant and extravagant. His son, Liu Jian, was notoriously depraved, committing adultery, murder, and even plotting rebellion with weapons and seals. He was eventually forced to commit suicide, and his kingdom was abolished. Liu Duan, the King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and physically weak, often killing officials who tried to govern lawfully, leading to his kingdom’s reduction and eventual abolition.

Liu Pengzu, the King of Zhao, was deceitful and flattering, using sophistry to frame officials and amassing wealth through trade. He died after sixty years of rule, but his son Liu Dan was executed for promiscuity and murder. Liu Sheng, the King of Zhongshan, was a drunkard with over 120 children, but he famously wept before Emperor Wu, complaining of officials’ encroachments on princes’ rights. This led to Emperor Wu’s policy of dividing princes’ lands among their sons, weakening their power. Liu Fa, the King of Changsha, was born from a concubine’s deception and ruled a poor, humid kingdom. His descendants faced scandals, including a king who burned houses and killed people. Liu Yue, the King of Guangchuan, died early, and his son Liu Qi was accused of incest and false accusations, leading to his kingdom’s temporary abolition. Liu Qu, a later king, was a scholar who studied the *Yi* and *Analects*, but he became tyrannical, torturing and killing concubines under the influence of his queen, Zhaoxin. He was deposed and committed suicide.

Other kings included Liu Shun of Changshan, who was arrogant but often forgiven by his father. His son Liu Bo was deposed for neglecting his father’s funeral, and the kingdom was divided among his brothers. Liu Ji of Jiaodong was cautious during the Huainan rebellion, but his sons were made kings of smaller states. The text concludes with a reflection on the dangers of luxury and power, noting that most princes became arrogant and immoral, except for the noble King Xian of Hejian.

translation:
Li Guang, a native of Shengqi, Longxi County.
His ancestor Li Zhi was a general in the Qin Dynasty and once hunted down Prince Dan of Yan State.
Li Guang's family has been learning archery for generations.
In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan in large numbers. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at archery, he killed and captured many enemies. He became a Langguan of the Han Dynasty and served as a riding attendant.
Li Guang often went hunting with Emperor Wen and killed fierce beasts, so Emperor Wen said: It's a pity that you didn't get the chance; if you were in the era of Emperor Gao, it wouldn't be a problem to be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households!
Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne, and Li Guang was appointed Cavalry General.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Li Guang served as the commander of Xiaoqi. He followed Taiwei Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and made outstanding achievements in Changyi City.
Because the King of Liang privately awarded General Li Guang the seal, he did not receive the reward after returning to the court.
He was transferred to the prefect of Shanggu and fought many battles with the Xiongnu.
Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, said to the emperor with tears in his eyes: "Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world." He relied on his own ability and fought against the enemy many times, fearing that he would be sacrificed.
So he was transferred to the prefecture of Shangjun.
The Huns invaded Shangjun, and the emperor sent noble men to follow Li Guang and lead his own troops to fight against the Huns.
The noble man galloped with dozens of cavalry, met three Huns, and fought with them.
The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the noble man and killing almost all the cavalry he had brought with him.
The noble man ran to Li Guang. Li Guang said: This must be the Condor Shooter.
Li Guang then led a hundred cavalry to chase the three men.
The three men walked dozens of miles without riding horses.
Li Guang ordered his cavalry to disperse to the left and right, and Li Guang shot the three men himself, killing two and capturing one alive. It turned out to be the Huns' eagle shooter.
As soon as they tied up the man and went up the mountain, they saw thousands of Xiongnu cavalry. They saw Li Guang and thought it was the cavalry who was seducing them. They were all surprised and went up the mountain to get ready.
Li Guang's one hundred cavalry were frightened and wanted to run back quickly.
Li Guang said: We are dozens of miles away from the main army. If we run away with a hundred cavalry like this, if the Huns chase and shoot us, we will all die immediately.
Now that we stop, the Xiongnu must think that we are decoys of the army and will not dare to attack us.
Li Guang ordered: Forward!
After entering about two miles away from the Huns' position, they stopped and ordered: "Everyone, dismount and unsaddle!"
His cavalry said: There are many enemies and they are close. What if there is an emergency after unsaddled?
Li Guang said: Those enemies thought that we would escape, and now they took off their saddles to show that they would not leave. They used this method to confirm their suspicions.
So the Huns' cavalry finally did not dare to attack.
A general on a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang mounted his horse, galloped over with more than a dozen cavalry, and shot the Xiongnu general on a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry, took off the saddle, and ordered the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down.
It was almost dusk on this beautiful day, and the Huns soldiers were always uncertain and did not dare to attack.
In the middle of the night, the Huns also thought that the Han army had an ambush nearby and would attack them at night, so the Huns all retreated.
Early the next morning, Li Guangcai returned to his main army.
Later, he successively served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen and Yunzhong.
When Emperor Wu came to the throne, his ministers said that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred to the Weiyang Palace Guards, while Cheng Bushi also served as the Changle Palace Guards at that time.
In the past, Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both led the army as governors of border counties and stationed fields to guard the border.
When he sent out troops to attack the Huns, Li Guang's army did not have strict organization, queues or formations. They stationed themselves near good water sources and grasslands, and stayed and stayed at their own convenience. They did not patrol or patrol at night to defend themselves. The military's documents and books were kept simple, but reconnaissance posts were also set up in the distance, so they did not encounter any danger.
Cheng Bushi strictly required the establishment, formation and formation, and patrolled at night, and the officers processed military documents until dawn, and the troops were not allowed to do what they wanted.
Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's troops were very casual, but when the enemy suddenly attacked them, they were unable to parry them; and his soldiers were comfortable and happy, and they were all willing to die for him.
Although my troops are busy and busy, the enemy does not dare to invade us.
At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi, the prefects of border counties in the Han Dynasty, were famous generals. However, the Huns were afraid of Li Guang's strategy, and the soldiers mostly liked to follow Li Guang but were reluctant to follow Cheng Bushi.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Cheng Bushi was appointed Taizhong doctor because of his repeated outspoken advice. He is an honest man and obeys the law.
Later, the Han Dynasty used the city of Mayi to lure Chanyu. A large army was sent to ambush in the valley near Mayi. Li Guang served as the general of the cavalry and was controlled by the guard general Han Anguo.
At that time, Shanyu noticed this situation and retreated, leaving the Han army with no military exploits.
Four years later, Li Guang was transferred from a guard to a general and attacked the Huns from Yanmen County.
The Huns had more soldiers and defeated Li Guang's army and captured Li Guang alive.
Shan Yu always heard that Li Guang was talented and issued an order: If Li Guang is captured, he must be delivered alive.
The Huns cavalry captured Li Guang, who was injured at the time. They placed Li Guang between the two horses and used ropes to form a net bag for Li Guang to lie down.
After walking for more than ten miles, Li Guang pretended to be dead and squinted at a Hun boy riding a good horse next to him. Li Guang suddenly jumped up, climbed on the Hun boy's horse, held the boy in his arms and rode south for dozens of miles, and gathered the remaining troops of him.
Hundreds of Xiongnu cavalry chased him. As he ran, Li Guang picked up the bow and arrow of the Xiongnu boy and shot the chasing cavalry to death, thus escaping.
So he returned to the Han capital, and the Han court handed Li Guang over to the judge.
The judge ruled that Li Guang had lost many men and horses and was captured alive by the enemy. He should be beheaded and use money to atone and become a civilian.
A few years later, Li Guang and Guan Qiang, the grandson of the former Yingyin Marquis who had retired to Lantian County, often went hunting in the Nanshan Mountains.
One night, I went out with a cavalryman and drank with others in the fields.
Returning to Ba Ling Pavilion, Ba Lingwei was drunk and yelled at Li Guang to stop him. Li Guang's subordinates said: This is the former General Li.
Tingwei said: The current general cannot pass at night, let alone his predecessor!
Li Guang was detained and lodged under Baling Pavilion.
Soon after, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the governor of Liaoxi and defeated General Han.
Later, General Han was transferred to Youbeiping and died.
So the emperor recruited and appointed Li Guang as the right governor of Beiping.
Li Guang then asked to send Lieutenant Ba Ling to go with him and kill him when he arrived in the army. Then he wrote a letter to apologize.
The emperor replied: Generals are the backbone of the country's defense.
The Art of War in "Sima Fa" says: There is no need to salute when boarding a chariot, and there is no need to wear mourning clothes when encountering a funeral. Reorganize and appease the army to conquer rebellion; unify the will of the three armies and stimulate the combat effectiveness of the soldiers. Therefore, showing anger can shock thousands of miles, and showing majesty can surrender. All things; therefore, the prestige is applied to the minority areas, and the power of the gods frightens the neighboring countries. He uses his anger to eradicate the harm and makes them give up cruelty and massacre. This is exactly what I want the general to do; if he takes off his hat, barefoot and kowtows to apologize, it is not my will!
The general should lead his army to consolidate the army and stabilize the frontiers to welcome the battle in the golden autumn of Youbeiping.
When Li Guang was in the border county, the Huns gave him the title of "Han Fei General", and they avoided Li Guang and did not enter the border for several years.
Li Guang went out hunting and saw a stone in the grass. He thought it was a tiger and shot an arrow. The arrow penetrated the stone. When he got closer, he saw that it was a stone. Then I tried to ejaculate again, but I couldn't ejaculate anymore.
In the county where Li Guang was located, when he heard that there was a tiger, he often went to shoot it himself.
When he was stationed in Youbei, he shot a tiger once. The tiger jumped up and wounded Li Guang. Li Guang also shot the tiger to death.
Lang Zhongling Shi Jian passed away, so the emperor recruited Li Guang to replace Shi Jian as Lang Zhongling.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang was transferred to the rank of general and followed the general's army to attack the Huns from Dingxiang County.
Many of the generals were awarded the title of Marquis for their meritorious service for killing and capturing the enemy, but Li Guang's troops had no merit.
Three years later, Li Guang, as Lang Zhongling, led four thousand cavalry from Youbeiping. Bowang Hou Zhang Qian led 10,000 cavalry and went with Li Guang in two directions.
After walking for several hundred miles, King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led 40,000 cavalry to surround Li Guang. Li Guang's soldiers were frightened, so Li Guang sent his son Li Gan to attack the enemy with a fast horse.
Li Gan galloped away with dozens of cavalry alone, passed through the encirclement of the Huns' cavalry, picked out the enemy's left and right wings, and returned, reporting to Li Guang: "The Huns are easy to deal with."
The soldiers finally settled down.
Li Guang formed a circular formation, facing the outside world. The Huns attacked them fiercely, raining down arrows.
More than half of the Han soldiers died, and the Han army was almost running out of arrows.
Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the enemy's lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns gradually relaxed.
It happened to be dark, and the officers and soldiers were pale, but Li Guang looked as usual and commanded the army more energetically.
The soldiers in the army admired his courage.
The next day, they continued to fight hard, and Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns army finally relieved the siege.
The Han army was tired and could not pursue him.
At this time, Li Guang's army was almost wiped out and he had to withdraw his troops.
According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, Bowang Hou delayed the scheduled date and was sentenced to death. He paid for his sins and was reduced to a commoner.
Li Guang's military merit was equal to his criminal responsibility, so he was not rewarded.
At the beginning, Li Guang and his cousin Li Cai were both appointed as Langguan and served Emperor Xiaowen together.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Li Cai received a salary of two thousand stone levels for his accumulated merit.
During the Yuanshuo period of Emperor Xiaowu, he served as General of Qingchao and followed the general to attack King Youxian. His meritorious service reached the standard of reward and he was named Marquis of Le'an.
In the second year of Yuanshou, he replaced Gongsun Hong as prime minister.
Li Cai's character was among the lowest, and his reputation was far below that of Li Guang. However, Li Guang did not receive a title or fief, and his official position did not exceed Jiuqing.
Many of Li Guang's officers and soldiers were awarded the title of Marquis.
Li Guang once chatted with Wang Shuo, a Wangqi master, and said: Ever since the Han Dynasty attacked the Huns, I have never been absent from them. However, the talents of each army commander and below are not average enough. However, there are dozens of people who have obtained marquises because of their military exploits in attacking the Huns. However, I did not fall behind others, but I did not have a small amount of merit to obtain a fief. What is the reason?
Shouldn’t my life be granted a title of marquis?
Wang Shuo said: General, think about it yourself, has there ever been any regret?
Li Guang said: I was once the governor of Longxi. The Qiang people rebelled. I lured them to surrender. More than 800 people surrendered. I used deception to kill them on the same day. So far, my biggest regret is only this incident.
Wang Shuo said: There is no greater sin than killing someone who has surrendered. This is why the general cannot be granted the title of marquis.
Li Guang served as the governor of seven counties for more than 40 years. After receiving rewards, he immediately distributed them to his subordinates, and shared his food and drink with the soldiers.
There is no extra property in the family, and I have never talked about buying property in my life.
Li Guang was tall, long-armed, and talented in archery. Even if his descendants and others learned archery from him, they could not catch up with him.
Li Guang was arrogant and did not talk much to others. He lived with others and drew battle formations on the ground. He shot arrows wider and narrower than the area he shot. If he lost, he drank wine as a penalty.
Specialized in archery as a game.
When leading troops on the march, they encounter a shortage of food and water. When they see water, not all the soldiers drink the water. He does not go near the water. Not all the soldiers have food. He does not taste the food. He treats soldiers generously and carefully, so soldiers like to work for him.
When he shoots an arrow and sees an enemy within a few dozen steps, he probably won't hit the target and will fall to the ground as soon as he shoots.
Therefore, he led his troops in battle and was besieged by the enemy many times. He even shot wild beasts and was injured several times.
In the fourth year of Yuanshou, the generals and hussar generals sent out large-scale troops to attack the Xiongnu. Li Guang took the initiative to request to go several times.
The emperor thought he was old and did not allow him. After a long time, he finally allowed him and sent him to serve as a former general.
General Wei Qing left the border fortress, captured prisoners, and learned where Shan Yu lived. He personally led his elite troops to attack, and ordered Li Guang's troops to merge with General Right's troops to attack from the east.
The east road is a little circuitous, and the large army is traveling through a place with few water and grass, so it is unable to gather and march.
Li Guang personally requested: "I am a former general of the army, but now the general has asked me to send troops from the east route. Besides, I have been fighting against the Xiongnu since I was young. Today is the first time I have to fight against the Shanyu. I am willing to be the vanguard and fight the Shanyu to the death first."
General Wei Qing was secretly instructed by the emperor, thinking that Li Guang was old and had suffered many embarrassments, so he should not be allowed to confront Shanyu head-on, as he might not be able to realize his wish.
At this time, Gongsun Ao had recently lost a marquis and was serving as lieutenant general. The general also wanted Gongsun Ao to fight against Shanyu with him, so he transferred former general Li Guang.
Li Guang knew this situation at the time and resolutely refused to be transferred to the general.
The general refused to listen and ordered the chief historian to send a document to Li Guang's shogunate, saying: Go to the military headquarters where you are and do as the document says.
Li Guang set out without saying goodbye to the general. He went to the military headquarters in anger, led his soldiers and the right general to the place where they joined forces, and set off from the east road.
He lost his way and fell behind the general.
The general fought with Shanyu, but Shanyu fled and returned without any victory.
The army crossed the desert southward before meeting the former general and the right general.
After Li Guang met with the general, he returned to his army.
The general sent Chang Shi to bring wine and food to Li Guang, and asked Li Guang and Zhao Shiqi how they had lost their way, and said: "Wei Qing wants to write a letter to report the twists and turns in the emperor's army."
Li Guang didn't answer.
General Shi ordered Li Guang's shogunate staff to write a report and go to the hearing.
Li Guang said: "The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will give a confession in person and wait for interrogation."
Returning to his shogunate, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have experienced more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was young. This time I had the honor to follow the general to fight against Shanyu's direct troops. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and distant road, and they lost their way again. Isn't it God's will?
Besides, I am over sixty years old, and after all, I can no longer deal with the insults of interrogators.
Then he took out his knife and killed himself.
When the people heard this, whether they knew him or not, whether they were old or young, they all shed tears for him.
The right general Zhao Shiqi was sent to the judge alone and sentenced to death. He paid for his sins and was reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang had three sons, named Li Danghu, Li Jiao, and Li Gan, all of whom served as Lang Guan.
One time the emperor was playing with Han Yan, and Han Yan was a little rude. Li Danghu hit Han Yan, and Han Yan ran away, so the emperor thought Li Danghu was brave.
Li Danghu died early, and the emperor appointed Li Jiao as the prefect of Daijun, both of whom died before Li Guang.
When Li Guang died in the army, Li Gan was following the hussar general.
In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai became the prime minister. He should be punished by the judge for occupying the open space of Emperor Xiaojing's Yangling Mausoleum. The open space given to him at that time was only 20 acres, and Li Cai occupied three hectares. After selling the land, he received more than 400,000 yuan. He also occupied an acre of land outside the Shinto as a cemetery. He was sentenced to prison, so Li Cai also committed suicide.
As a school captain, Li Gan followed the hussar general to attack King Zuoxian of the Huns. He fought hard and captured King Zuoxian's war drum and flag. He beheaded many of the enemies. He was awarded the title of Marquis of Dingguannei and enjoyed the title of 200 households. He succeeded Li Guang as the doctor's order.
Soon, Li Gan resented the general Wei Qing for causing his father to die out of hatred, so he wounded the general, but the general concealed the incident.
Not long after, Li Gan accompanied the emperor to Yongzhou Ganquan Palace for hunting. General Huo Qubing resented Li Gan for injuring Wei Qing and shot Li Gan to death.
Huo Qubing was favored by the nobles at that time, but the emperor concealed the truth and said that a wild deer killed him.
More than a year later, Huo Qubing died.
Li Gan had a daughter who was the prince's maid and was favored.
Li Gan's son Li Yu was also favored by the prince, but he was fond of wealth and had courage.
He once drank with a nobleman in his attendants and insulted him, but the nobleman did not dare to say anything.
Later, he told the emperor. The emperor summoned Li Yu and asked him to stab the tiger. He hung down to the tiger enclosure, but before he reached the ground, he ordered Li Yu to be pulled up.
Li Yu cut the rope from the net and wanted to stab the tiger.
The emperor thought he was brave, so he rescued him and stopped him from stabbing the tiger.
Li Danghu had a posthumous son named Li Ling, who led an army to attack the Huns. He was defeated and surrendered to the Huns.
Later, someone accused Li Yu of trying to follow Li Ling and was executed.
Li Ling, whose courtesy name is Shaoqing, was appointed as the Jian Zhang Supervisor of the Imperial Palace when he was young.
He is good at riding and shooting, loves and cares for others, and is humble to his subordinates. He has a good reputation.
Emperor Wu felt that he had Li Guang's demeanor, so he asked him to lead 800 cavalry and penetrated more than 2,000 miles into the Huns' territory. He passed through the Juyan area and inspected the terrain. When the Huns were not seen, he returned.
He worshiped the official Cavalry Captain and led 5,000 warriors to teach archery in Jiuquan and Zhangye areas to prevent the Huns from invading.

summary:
Li Guang, a native of Longxi County, was a descendant of a Qin general and came from a family skilled in archery. He began his military career during Emperor Wen's reign, fighting the Xiongnu at Xiaoguan, where his archery skills earned him a position as a Langguan. Emperor Wen lamented that Li Guang's talents would have earned him a marquisate in the era of Emperor Gaozu. Under Emperor Jing, he served as a Cavalry General and fought in the campaign against the rebellious seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, but was denied a reward due to accepting a seal from the King of Liang. He later served as the Prefect of Shanggu and other border commanderies, frequently battling the Xiongnu.

During a campaign in Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu. He cleverly halted his men and dismounted, convincing the enemy they were a decoy, which prevented an attack. After nightfall, the Xiongnu withdrew, suspecting an ambush. Li Guang later served as a palace guard under Emperor Wu, alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng Bushi's army was strictly disciplined, Li Guang's was more relaxed, yet his soldiers were loyal and willing to die for him. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategies, and soldiers preferred serving under him.

Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu in a later campaign but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting his pursuers. He was sentenced to death for his losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner. He later served as the Right Governor of Beiping, where the Xiongnu avoided him for years. During a hunt, he famously shot an arrow into a stone, mistaking it for a tiger. Despite his reputation, Li Guang never received a marquisate, a fact he lamented to Wang Shuo, who attributed it to Li Guang's past deception and killing of surrendered Qiang rebels.

In his final campaign, Li Guang served as a former general under Wei Qing. Ordered to take a circuitous eastern route, he lost his way and failed to join the main force. After Wei Qing's interrogation, Li Guang, feeling humiliated and over sixty, committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning. His son Li Gan later wounded Wei Qing in revenge and was killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer attack. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling led a campaign against the Xiongnu with 5,000 infantry, fighting bravely but ultimately surrendering after running out of arrows and reinforcements. The emperor, misled by reports that Li Ling was training the Xiongnu, executed his family. Li Ling remained with the Xiongnu, marrying a Chanyu's daughter and dying there years later.

Su Wu was sent as an envoy to the Xiongnu in 100 BCE. When a conspiracy involving his deputy Zhang Sheng was exposed, Su Wu attempted suicide to avoid disgrace. He survived and was imprisoned, surviving on snow and felt. Exiled to the North Sea to herd rams, he steadfastly refused to surrender, even when his former friend Li Ling tried to persuade him. After nineteen years, the Han Dynasty learned he was alive through a clever ruse involving a wild goose with a message. Su Wu returned to Chang'an, honored for his loyalty, though his son was later executed for conspiracy. He died in his eighties, and his portrait was later placed in the Qilin Pavilion among eleven notable ministers of Emperor Xuan's reign. The text praises Li Guang's integrity and Su Wu's unwavering loyalty, noting the tragic fate of the Li family and the exemplary virtue of Su Wu.

When Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Du Ye wrote another letter saying: The Wang family has been in power for too long, and there are no honest and upright ministers in the court.
Prince Quyanghou was an assistant to the three princes in the past. When he knew that Zhao Zhaoyi had killed the prince, he did not report it immediately. With this person in court, Your Majesty can sit back and relax.
In the past, when Zhu Lu wanted to harm the Liu family, it was only because Zhou Bo and Chen Ping were still there, otherwise they would have been ridiculed by the treacherous ministers.
Du Ye also said that a temple should be built in the capital for Prince Gong to show his filial piety.

summary:
Du Zhou, a native of Du Yan County in Nanyang, rose from being an assistant to Governor Yi Zong to an official historian under Zhang Tang. He gained the emperor's trust by convicting and executing many during investigations of border counties, serving as Zhongcheng for over a decade. Taciturn and slow-tempered but kind-hearted, Du Zhou succeeded Xuan as Tingwei, modeling his governance after Zhang Tang and adeptly reading the emperor's intentions. He would frame those the emperor wished to exclude and prolong imprisonment for those the emperor wished to forgive, secretly revealing their grievances. When criticized for not following established laws, Du Zhou argued that laws were created by monarchs and should adapt to current circumstances. As Tingwei, he handled over a thousand cases annually, with large cases involving hundreds of witnesses. Many fled or hid upon hearing of impending arrests, and cases could drag on for over a decade through multiple amnesties. Prisons held 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, with ordinary officials adding up to 100,000. Du Zhou was later deposed but returned as Jinwu, harshly pursuing thieves and interrogating Sang Hongyang's sons and Queen Wei's brothers. Promoted to imperial censor, his family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions. His two sons served as governors, but only his youngest, Du Yannian, was kind-hearted.

Du Yannian, well-versed in law, served under Emperor Zhao with General Huo Guang in power. He led Nanyang soldiers to suppress a rebellion in Yizhou and later reported the rebellion of Shangguan Jie and others, earning the title of Marquis of Jianping. As a subordinate of Huo Guang, Yannian advocated lenient punishments. When Hou Shiwu was implicated for harboring Sang Qian, Yannian argued against harsh penalties, balancing the court's harmony. He advised Huo Guang to promote frugality and tolerance, leading to the abolition of monopolies on wine, salt, and iron. During Emperor Zhao's illness, Yannian managed prescriptions. After the emperor's death, he helped establish Emperor Xuan, gaining additional fiefs. Despite being an old member of the Huo family, Yannian was dismissed after Huo Guang's death due to legal violations but later reinstated as governor of Xihe, where he achieved peace. He served as censor during the Wufeng period but resigned due to old age and illness, dying a few months later. His son Du Xu succeeded him as marquis.

Du Xu served as a Langguan, followed General Pulei against the Xiongnu, and later became Taichang. He was known for his kindness, often drinking and saving food during winter verdicts. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he donated money and grain to support the army. Du Xu had six younger brothers, five of whom became senior officials. His brother Du Qin, though blind, was renowned for his knowledge and strategy. Du Qin advised General Wang Feng on establishing a system of nine concubines to ensure heirs and longevity, warning against lust and its consequences. He also addressed solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of weak yang and strong yin, urging the emperor to restrain female favors and promote frugality. His countermeasures at the White Tiger Palace emphasized filial piety, righteousness, and the importance of knowing and employing people. Du Qin later warned Wang Feng against excessive power, citing historical examples. After Wang Zhang's death, Du Qin advised Wang Feng to clarify the matter to dispel rumors. Du Qin never became an official and died of old age.

Du Ye, Du Qin's nephew, inherited the marquis title and served as Taichang. He criticized Prime Minister Zhai Fangjin for bias and corruption, and later defended Dong Hong's proposal to honor the emperor's mother. Du Ye was demoted to captain of Shangdang and eventually dismissed from office. When Wang Mang came to power, Du Ye, fearing punishment, fell ill and died. The Du family, starting with Du Zhou and Du Yannian, were known as harsh officials but produced virtuous sons. Their lineage continued until the end of the Han Dynasty, with no one surpassing them after the great heroes and scholars.

Yang Wangsun was from the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Learn the art of Huang Lao, make a fortune, pay attention to health preservation, and try to get everything that is beneficial to health.
When he was critically ill and dying, he first ordered his son in his instructions: "When I die, I will be buried naked. Let me return to the way of nature. I must not change my wishes."
After death, I put the body in a cloth bag and put it seven feet into the ground. After putting it down, I pulled the cloth bag off my feet so that my body was in direct contact with the soil.
His son wanted to silently disobey, but found it difficult to disobey his father's orders; he wanted to obey his father's wishes, but he couldn't bear it, so he went to visit his father's friend Qi Hou.
Qi Hou wrote a letter to Yang Wangsun saying: You are suffering from illness. I was eager to follow the emperor to Yong County to offer sacrifices, so I was unable to visit you at the house.
I hope you can keep your spirits up, think less about problems, seek medical treatment, and take good care of yourself.
I heard that you made an order to be buried naked after death. If the deceased is unconscious, forget it. If the deceased is conscious, you will kill the body underground and go to see the ancestors naked. I don’t think you should do this.
Moreover, the "Book of Filial Piety" says that coffins, coffins, and quilts are provided for the deceased. This is also a system passed down by the saints. Why should you insist on your own opinions alone?
I hope you will review my comments.
Yang Wangsun wrote back and said: I heard that the ancient sage kings followed human feelings and did not suppress their relatives, so they planned funerals for people. Now they go beyond the etiquette regulations and practice rich burials. Therefore, I asked for a naked burial, intending to correct the social trend of rich burials.
A grand burial is really not beneficial to the deceased, but secular people compete with each other and spend all their money to buy funeral objects, leaving these things to rot in the ground.
Or it may be buried in the ground today and exhumed tomorrow. It is really no different from the corpse wilderness!
Moreover, the so-called death is the end of life and the destination of all things.
The destination can be reached, the dead can be transformed, and creation means that objects return to their origins.
Returning the origin to the underworld, invisible and silent, is in line with reason and emotion.
Decorating the appearance to attract attention, burying it in a luxurious manner and isolating the origin, making it impossible to reach the final destination and unable to change the deceased, are causing objects to lose their place.
And I heard that the spirit belongs to heaven, and the body belongs to the earth.
The spirit leaves the body and returns to its original state, so it is called a ghost. Ghost means returning.
How can a dead body be conscious when it is as empty and alone as a clod of soil?
The corpse was wrapped in silk, and the coffin was used to isolate the soil. The limbs were wrapped and bound, and the jade was held in the mouth. He tried to melt it but couldn't, and turned into a mummy in depression. After a thousand years, the coffin rotted, and he could return to the earth and his true destination.
From this point of view, why stay as a guest for a long time?
In the past, when Yao was buried, he hollowed out wood to make a coffin and tied it with kudzu vines on the outside. The grave was dug so deep that it was not as deep as the spring water, so that the rotten gas did not leak out.
Therefore, it is easy to respect a wise king when he is alive, and easy to bury him when he is dead.
Don't spend your time on useless things, and don't waste money without a purpose.
Nowadays, money is wasted on lavish burials, preventing the deceased from returning to the earth, and isolating them from their origins. The dead do not know, and the living cannot realize their wishes of filial piety. It can be said that it is too confusing. Alas!
I won’t give him a grand burial!
Qihou read Yang Wangsun's reply and said: Well said.
After Yang Wangsun died, he was finally buried naked.
Hu Jian, courtesy name Zimeng, was from Hedong County.
During the Tianhan period of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he was appointed military official for trial. His family was poor and had no money to buy a carriage and horses. He often walked and lived with his officers, so he took the opportunity to comfort the officers, which was very popular.
At that time, the censor of the Imperial Army committed a crime and cut through the wall of the Northern Army's fortress to build a small house for selling goods for profit. Hu Jian wanted to kill him, so he invited the officers and said, "I plan to kill someone with you. If I tell you to catch him, you will catch him; if I ask you to kill him, you will kill him."
So it was scheduled to be the day to select soldiers and horses for the operation. On that day, the censor and the military guards were sitting in the corridor. Hu Jian and his officers walked quickly to the corridor to pay homage. When Hu Jian got up, he took advantage of the momentum and climbed onto the corridor, and the officers followed closely.
Hu Jian pointed at the censor and said: "Catch him."
The officer stepped forward and grabbed the censor and dragged him down the hall. Hu Jian said: Kill him!
The officer hacked the censor to death.
The guards and schools were all shocked and didn't know why.
Hu Jian had already carried the written memorial in his arms, so he submitted the memorial and said: I have heard from military law that military force is established to command authority over the masses, and that evildoers are punished to prohibit evil.
Nowadays, the imperial censor openly cuts through the walls of the military fortress to seek the interests of merchants, and privately engages in business with the scholars. He does not have a strong heart and courage, and is unable to lead the scholar-officials and set an example for them. It is extremely unjust and unfair.
If you let the civil servants discuss the crime, they will be punished severely.
"Huangdi Li Fa" says: After the barrier is formed, drilling holes violates the regulations of the camp, and it is considered a treacherous person, and the treacherous person will be put to death.
I act strictly in accordance with military law. Military law says: Military officers are not affiliated with generals. If a general commits a crime, military officers can report it to the emperor. Officials with a value of less than two thousand shi can be dealt with according to military law.
Jun Zhengcheng is under the jurisdiction of Junzheng. According to the military law, it is doubtful that Jun Zhengcheng killed the censor of the army. However, the deacons should immediately punish the illegal behavior and should not pass the matter to their superiors. Therefore, I killed the censor of the army according to the military law and risked my life to report the matter.

King Yu of Xia, Tang of Shang, and King Wen of Zhou sometimes swore an oath in the army to ask the people to consider their own plans first; sometimes they swore an oath outside the military gate to ask the people to mentally prepare for war; sometimes they swore an oath when the two armies were about to confront each other to inspire the people's courage.
Why should you be suspicious?

The assassin was hiding in the building owner's villa, and the officials did not dare to catch him.
Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian led officers and soldiers to surround the villa to arrest the assassin.
When Gai Zhu heard about it, he and his fellow Ding, Hussar General Shangguan'an, and many slaves and soldiers came over. They ran and shot at the officials, who then fled in all directions.
Lord Gai ordered his servants to impeach Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian, who sent a parade to injure Lord Gai's servants.

Lord Gai was very angry and sent a letter to falsely accuse Hu Jian of violating and insulting the eldest princess, and shot an arrow at the gate of Lord Gai's mansion.
Hu Jian knew clearly that his subordinate officials had harmed the princess's domestic slave, but he avoided retribution and deliberately did not pursue the investigation.
General Huo Guang suppressed their memorial.
Later, when Huo Guang fell ill, Shangguan Jie took charge of government affairs and ordered the officials to arrest Hu Jian. Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide.
Officials and people all said that he died unjustly, and his ancestral hall is still built in Weicheng.
Zhu Yun, whose courtesy name was You, was a native of Lu and later moved to Pingling.
When he was young, he made friends with the agile and powerful knights, and used the knights to take revenge.
He is more than eight feet tall, has a majestic appearance, and is famous for his courage.

During the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty, Gong Yu, a native of Langye County, was appointed as the imperial censor. Zhu Yun, a native of Pingling, is good at both civil and military affairs, loyal and wise. He can be allowed to try his best to serve as the imperial censor with an official rank of 600 stones.
Emperor Yuan asked the ministers for their opinions on this matter.
Prince Fu Kuangheng believed in the countermeasures: Ministers are the pillars of the country and the objects of admiration by all the people. Sage kings choose carefully.
Ancient books say that if the people despise high officials and humble people try to become powerful ministers, the country will be shaken and the people will be uneasy.

summary:
Yang Wangsun, a man from Emperor Wu's reign, studied Huang-Lao teachings and focused on health preservation. When terminally ill, he ordered his son to bury him naked, directly in contact with soil, to return to nature. His son consulted their friend Qi Hou, who argued against this, citing filial piety traditions requiring coffins and burial clothes. Yang Wangsun responded that lavish burials were wasteful and harmful, preventing the dead from returning to their natural state. He argued that the spirit returns to heaven and the body to earth; elaborate burials only create mummies that cannot decompose properly. He insisted on naked burial, which was ultimately carried out.

Hu Jian served as a military official during Emperor Wu's Tianhan period. When a military censor illegally built a shop within the army fortress for profit, Hu Jian gathered his officers, seized and executed the censor on the spot. He submitted a memorial citing military law, arguing the censor's crime warranted death and that military officers could handle such matters without civilian court involvement. The emperor approved his actions, citing the principle that military and civil laws differ. Hu Jian later became magistrate of Weicheng County. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he arrested an assassin hiding in a noble's villa, angering Princess Gaichang and General Shangguan An. After General Huo Guang fell ill, Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide, though people considered his death unjust.

Zhu Yun, originally a chivalrous man, later studied the Book of Changes and Analects. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he debated Wulu Chongzong on the Liangqiu interpretation of the Book of Changes, defeating him soundly. He became a doctor and later magistrate of several counties. He criticized powerful officials including Shi Xian and Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng. After being convicted of murder, he fled and sought help from Chen Xian, who was also imprisoned. During Emperor Cheng's reign, Zhu Yun requested the emperor's sword to kill sycophantic minister Zhang Yu. The emperor was furious and ordered his execution, but Zhu Yun clung to a palace railing, breaking it. General Xin Qingji intervened, and Zhu Yun was spared. He retired, taught students, and died at home in his seventies, requesting simple burial.

Mei Fu studied in Chang'an, mastering the Book of Documents and Guliang's Spring and Autumn Annals. He repeatedly submitted memorials criticizing the growing power of the Wang family and urging Emperor Cheng to recruit talented advisors. He warned that killing honest officials like Wang Zhang silenced criticism and endangered the state. He advocated establishing Confucius' descendants as heirs to the Shang dynasty's sacrifices. His advice was largely ignored. During Wang Mang's reign, Mei Fu abandoned his family and disappeared, later seen working as a market servant in Wu County under a false name.

Yun Chang studied under Wu Zhang, a famous scholar of the Book of Documents. When Wu Zhang was executed for conspiring against Wang Mang, his disciples denied their connection. Yun Chang alone admitted being Wu Zhang's student, collected his body, and arranged proper burial. He later served as an official under Wang Mang but resigned due to illness and died at home.

The commentary praises Yang Wangsun's noble aspirations, Hu Jian's decisive bravery, and Mei Fu's principled words. Yun Chang's integrity was revealed through burying his teacher, and he wisely withdrew from service during troubled times.

summary:
The five kings of Chu were brothers, with the same father. They were fond of reading and versatile. In childhood, they studied the *Classic of Poetry* with Ni Qiuyuan, Lu Musheng, Bai Sheng, Shen Gong, and Fu Qiubo, who was a disciple of Se Qing. Their studies were dispersed when the Qin dynasty burned books.

Emperor Gaozu of Han had four brothers: Liu Bo (eldest, died early), Liu Zhong (second), and Gaozu himself. When Gaozu became Duke of Pei, Jing Ju declared himself King of Chu. Gaozu sent Liu Zhong and Shen Shiqi to serve the emperor, while Liu Jiao, Xiao He, Cao Shen, and others accompanied Gaozu to meet Jing Ju. They met Xiang Liang and together supported King Huai of Chu. They attacked Nanyang, entered Wuguan, and battled Qin at Lantian. At Ba Shang, Gaozu made Liu Jiao the King of Wenxin. Liu Jiao followed Gaozu into Shu Han, returned to conquer the Three Qin, and helped kill Xiang Ji. After ascending the throne, Liu Jiao and Lu Wan often served the emperor closely, conveying internal affairs. The emperor's cousin Liu Jia led troops in many battles. In the sixth year of Han, King Xin of Chu was deposed, and his territory was divided. Liu Jia was made King of Jing, and Liu Jiao was made King of Chu, ruling thirty-six counties due to their meritorious service. Later, Liu Zhong was made acting king, and Gaozu's eldest son Liu Fei was made King of Qi.

Initially, when Gaozu was humble, he often ate at his sister-in-law's house with guests. She hated this and pretended the soup was finished, scraping the pot. Gaozu saw soup remained and resented her. After the kings of Qi and Dai were established, only Liu Bo's son was not enfeoffed. The Supreme Emperor spoke for him, and Gaozu said he dared not forget to confer a title because his mother was unkind. In October of the seventh year, Liu Xin, Liu Bo's son, was granted the title of Genjiehou.

When King Yuan arrived in Chu, he appointed Musheng, Bai Sheng, and Shen Gong as middle-level officials. Fuqiu Bo was in Chang'an, and King Yuan sent his son Ying Ke to complete his studies with Duke Shen. During Emperor Wen's reign, Duke Shen was appointed a doctor for his proficiency in the *Classic of Poetry*. King Yuan liked the *Poetry*, and all his sons studied it. Duke Shen wrote a biography of the *Poetry*, called the *Lu Shi*. King Yuan also compiled a biography, called the *Poems of King Yuan*. King Yuan ordered Ying Ke to be Zongzheng and granted him the title of Pihou. King Yuan died in his twenty-third year, and his son Pifei died first. Emperor Wen ordered Ying Ke to become King Yi. Duke Shen became a doctor and later returned with Ying Ke as a middle doctor. After four years, Liu Wu succeeded. Emperor Wen favored King Yuan and gave him the title of Prince Bi. Emperor Jing named five of King Yuan's favored sons as marquises.

Initially, King Yuan respectfully treated Musheng, who did not like drinking. King Yuan often prepared sweet wine for him. When Liu Wu came to the throne, he continued this but later forgot. Musheng said, "If I don't serve sweet wine, the king will be indifferent. If I don't leave, the people of Chu will pin me down in the market." He claimed illness and stayed in bed. Duke Shen and Bai Sheng urged him to get up, saying, "Don't you think of the late king's kindness? Now if the king loses a small courtesy, how could you end up like this!" Musheng replied, "The *Yi* says it is probably God who knows the omens. Omens are subtle signs of action and early manifestations of good or bad luck. A gentleman takes action when he sees signs and does not wait. The late king treated us courteously because the Great Way existed; to ignore it now is to forget the Way. How can you stay with someone who has forgotten the Tao? Is it just a small gift?" So he resigned, claiming illness. Only Shen Gong and Bai Sheng remained. Liu Wu gradually became promiscuous and committed adultery during the mourning period for Empress Dowager Bo. He reduced Shuhai and Xuejun and secretly communicated with Wu. The two refused to listen to advice and were punished. Xiuhou sent someone to remonstrate, but the king said, "Ji's father does not agree with me. After I rise, I will capture Ji's father first." Xiuhou fled to the capital with his mother.

In the spring of the 21st year, the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, as documents to reduce fiefdoms arrived, Liu Wu responded to King Yu's rebellion. His state minister and tutor tried to persuade him but failed. He killed Chi Shang and Guo Wu, raised troops, and joined the Xing army to attack westward, capturing Kuibi. He battled Dannuo south of Dandan. Choosing to block food roads, his soldiers grew hungry. The king fled and committed suicide, and the army surrendered. When Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing established Liu Li as King of Chu, succeeding King Yuan as King Wen. After four years, Liu Dao succeeded as King An. After 22 years, Liu Zhu succeeded as King Xiang. After 14 years, Liu Chun succeeded. After 16 years, his son Yanshou succeeded. When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Yanshou believed King Guangling Liu Xu, son of Emperor Wu, would be supported if the world changed. He secretly wanted to help him, marrying the daughter of King Guangling to his queen's brother Zhao Heqi. He planned with He Qi to join forces with King Guangling. He sent He Qi with a letter to King Guangling. He Qi's father reported him for years. The matter was brought to Yousi, who verified the confession, and Yanshou committed suicide. After 32 years, the feudal state was abolished.

Liu Fu, the Marquis of Xiu, fled to the capital. When Liu Wu rebelled, Liu Fu and others were dismissed. Later, hearing he had repeatedly advised Liu Wu, his title was changed to Honghou. The Dowager Dowager was related to Empress Dowager Dou. She requested to stay in the capital, which was granted. Liu Fu's son Piqiang and four others supported her and served as officials. When the wife passed away, she was given a cemetery. Liu Fu passed the kingdom to his great-grandson, but he had no sons, and the kingdom was cut off. Piqiang, courtesy name Shaoqing, was good at reading the *Poetry* and could write articles. During Emperor Wu's reign, he followed Erqianshi Discussion as a clan son and was the head of each clan. He was pure-hearted and refused to be an official. When Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, someone persuaded General Huo Guang to make more friends with the clan. Huo Guang agreed and chose available people in the clan. Piqiang's son Liu De was in the Prime Minister's Palace. He was in his thirties and wanted to be hired. Some said his father was still there and favored by the late emperor. So Piqiang was made Doctor Guanglu and Guardsman of Kenle. He was eighty years old then. He was promoted to Zongzheng and died within months. Liu De, named Lu Shu, practiced Huang Lao's skills and had strategies. He discussed political affairs and was summoned to Ganquan Palace. In Emperor Zhao's early years, he became Zong Zhengcheng and participated in executing Liu Ze's imperial edict. He became Dahonglucheng, then Taizhong doctor, and later Zongzheng, participating in torturing the Shangguan family and Gaizhu. Liu De held the *Laozi* idea of contentment. After his wife died, Huo Guang wanted to marry his daughter to him, but Liu De refused, fearing prosperity. He repeatedly blamed Princess Gai for inappropriate behavior. The censor thought Huo Guang resented Liu De and wanted to impeach him. Liu De avoided being a commoner and lived in seclusion. Huo Guang was angry and summoned Liu De to guard Qingzhou. Over a year later, he became Zongzheng again and participated in establishing Emperor Xuan. He was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and later Marquis of Yangcheng. His son Anmin became a doctor's assistant, and over 20 people in the clan became officials due to Liu De. Liu De was generous and rehabilitated sinners. He used his family property to support brothers and guests, saying, "Wealth is resented by the people." In his eleventh year, his son Liu Xiang should be punished for casting fake gold, and Liu De filed a lawsuit. When he passed away, Dahonglu wrote to defend his son's crime. Shao Ling said to give him the title of Muhou and establish heirs. It was passed to Sun Qingji, who became Zong Zhengtai Chang. After his death, his son Liu Cen succeeded and became a general. After death, it was passed to his son, but when Wang Mang failed, it was discontinued.

Liu Xiang, courtesy name Zizheng, originally named Gengsheng. At twelve, he became a chariot man due to his father Liu De's favor. After the crowning ceremony, he was promoted to a doctor of admonishment. At this time, Emperor Xuan recruited famous Confucian and talented people. Geng Sheng was proficient and able to connect words, so he presented poems and poems. The emperor believed in magical alchemy again, and there was the *Secretary of Hongbaoyuan in the Pillow* from Huainan. The book told of gods instructing ghosts to cast gold and Zou Yan's method of righteousness and longevity. No one could see it, but Geng Sheng's father Liu De got it when handling the Huainan case. Geng Sheng read it and offered it, saying it could make gold. The emperor ordered him to cast it, but it cost much and was ineffective. The emperor handed him to officials, who impeached him for casting fake gold and sent him to jail to die. His brother Anmin wrote a letter, willing to pay half of the households to atone for his sin. The emperor thought him a genius and reduced his death sentence. When *Guliang Chunqiu* was established as an academic official, he was recruited to study it and lecture on the *Five Classics* in Shiqu. He was made a doctor and given to Shi Huangmen. He was promoted to Sanqi, admonished official, and given to Shizhong. When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and Young Fu Zhou Kan were in charge of secretarial affairs. Geng Sheng was younger but they thought highly of him. He was promoted to Sanqi Zongzheng, serving as Shizhong, and served with Jin Chang. Fan Kuai, a native of Peixian County, was a dog butcher by trade. He hid with Emperor Gaozu in the Mangshan and Cishan areas to avoid official duties. During Chen Sheng's uprising, Xiao He and Cao Shen sent Fan Kuai to retrieve Gaozu, who became Peigong. Fan Kuai served as a Sheren, attacking Huling, Fangyu, and Fengyi, defeating the Sishui County Supervisor. He pacified Peixian County and defeated the Sishui County Governor at Xuexian. He fought Sima Chao in Ci County, beheading fifteen enemies, earning the title of doctor. Fan Kuai frequently followed Peigong, leading assaults on Puyang, Chengyang, and Hufu, beheading many enemies and receiving promotions. He fought at Chengwu, Boyi, Gangli, and Kaifeng, beheading a commander and sixty-eight enemies, earning the title of minister. He defeated Yang Xiong at Quyu, ascended Wanling first, and was named Xianchengjun. He fought at Changshe, Nianyuan, and the Yellow River ferry, defeating Qin forces at Xixiang and Nianyi. He defeated Nanyang's Shouling at Yangcheng, ascended Wancheng first, and repelled enemies at Li County. At Wuguan and Bashang, he beheaded a captain and ten enemies, capturing 146 and surrendering 2,900 soldiers.

At the Hongmen Banquet, Xiang Yu prepared to attack Peigong. Peigong apologized to Xiang Yu via Xiang Bo. During the feast, Yafu ordered Xiang Zhuang to assassinate Peigong with a sword dance, but Xiang Bo protected him. Fan Kuai, hearing the urgency, entered the camp with sword and shield, confronting Xiang Yu. He drank wine and ate pork leg, condemning Xiang Yu for listening to slander and estranging Peigong. Xiang Yu remained silent. Peigong left, and Fan Kuai escorted him back to Bashang, leaving Zhang Liang to apologize. Xiang Yu abandoned his plan to kill Peigong. Later, Xiang Yu entered Xianyang, burning and killing, and made Peigong King of Han. Fan Kuai was made Marquis of Linwu, then doctor, and followed the king to Hanzhong. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, attacking Xixian, Yong County, Yongxian, and Tengcheng, ascending cities first. He attacked Zhang Ping at Haozhi, beheading a magistrate and a deputy, and was promoted to Cavalry General. He defeated Qin chariot and cavalry forces at Shumian and Rangxiang, becoming a general. He attacked Zhao Bi, occupying Jun, Huaili, Liuzhong, and Xianyang, diverting water to irrigate waste hills. The King of Han granted him Fan Township in Du County as a food town.

Fan Kuai followed the king to attack Xiang Yu, slaughtering Zaoyi and defeating Wang Wu and Cheng Chu at Waihuang. He attacked Zouxian, Luxian, Xiaqiu, and Xuexian. After Xiang Yu defeated the king at Pengcheng, Fan Kuai returned to Rongyang, receiving 2,000 households in Pingyin and garrisoning Guangwu Mountain for a year. He surrounded Xiang Yu at Chen County, defeating him and bloodbathing Hu Ling. After Xiang Yu's death, the king became emperor, granting Fan Kuai 800 households. He followed Gaozu to suppress Zang Tu's rebellion, capturing Zang Tu and pacifying Yan. He arrested Han Xin at Chen County, pacifying Chu. Gaozu granted Fan Kuai the title of Marquis of Wuyang, exempting previous titles. He followed Gaozu to attack Chen Xi in Daidi, pacifying Dai land and increasing households by 1,500. He attacked Chen Xi and Manqiuchen, capturing Bairen County, ascending cities first, and pacifying Qinghe and Changshan counties (27 total), destroying Shuyuan County, and becoming Left Prime Minister. He defeated Qi Muyin and Yin Pan at Wuzhong and Guangchang, and Chen Xi's general Wang Huang at Daidi, attacking Han Xin at Shenhe. His men killed Han Xin, defeated Xiongnu cavalry at Henggu, and captured General Zhao Ji, Prime Minister Feng Liang, and others. He pacified 72 counties in Dai. He attacked Lu Wan, pacifying 18 counties and 51 townships in Yan. Gaozu added 1,300 households, totaling 5,400 in Wuyang. Fan Kuai beheaded 176 enemies, captured 287, defeated seven armies, occupied five cities, and pacified six commanderies and 52 counties. He married Empress Lu's sister, Lu Xu, and had a son, Fan Kang. He was closest to the emperor.

During Yingbu's rebellion, Gaozu was ill and refused to see anyone. Fan Kuai opened the palace door, weeping and rebuking Gaozu for isolating himself like Zhao Gao. Gaozu smiled and rose. Later, Gaozu sent Fan Kuai to attack Lu Wan. Slandered for colluding with the Lu family, Gaozu ordered Chen Ping to behead him, but Chen Ping arrested him instead. Gaozu died, and Empress Lu released Fan Kuai, restoring his title. Fan Kuai died in the sixth year of Xiaohui, posthumously named Marquis Wu. His son Fan Kang succeeded. Lu Xu was made Marquise of Linguang, but after Empress Lu's death, ministers killed her and Fan Kang. The title was suspended until Emperor Xiaowen granted it to Fan Kuai's concubine's son, Fan Shi. After Fan Shi's death, his son Fan Tuoguang inherited, but was later deposed for illegitimacy. In the second year of Yuanshi, Emperor Ping granted Fan Zhang, a descendant, the title of Marquis of Wuyang with 1,000 households.

Li Shang of Gaoyang County gathered youths during Chen Sheng's uprising. He surrendered 4,000 men to Peigong, attacking Changshe and ascending first, becoming Xinchengjun. He attacked Fengshi, blocked the Yellow River, defeated Qin at Luoyang, captured Wan and Xing, pacifying 17 counties. He assisted in taking Shanguan Pass and pacifying Hanzhong. Peigong became King of Han, making Li Shang Xinchengjun and Captain of Longxi. He pacified Beidi, defeating Zhang Han's deputies, and received 6,000 households in Wucheng. He commanded the Imperial Guard for a year. In October, as Right Prime Minister, he attacked Chen Xi, destroying Shuyuan. He attacked Yingbu, breaking barriers and capturing two formations, becoming Marquis of Quzhou with 5,100 households. His military achievements included defeating three rebels, pacifying six counties and 73 counties, capturing one prime minister, one acting prime minister, one general, and 19 officials. He assisted Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu. After Empress Lu's death, he was ill. His son Li Ji, friendly with Lu Lu, was used by Zhou Bo to deceive Lu Lu, allowing Zhou Bo to enter the Northern Army and kill the Lu family. Li Shang died that year, posthumously named Jinghou. Li Ji inherited, but was criticized for betraying friends. During Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Li Ji besieged Tong City for seven months without success, but Lebu captured it. Li Ji was stripped of his title for wanting to marry Lord Pingyuan. Emperor Jing named Li Jian, another son, Marquis of Mu. The title passed to Xuansun Su, who was executed for witchcraft. During the Second Beginning, descendants were granted Marquis of Guannei.

He was made Marquis of Ruyin with a talisman. He attacked Dai, going to Wuquan and Yunzhong, adding 1,000 households. He attacked Han Xin at Jinyang, defeating the enemy. Surrounded at Pingcheng for seven days, he advised slow retreat, escaping. He received Xiyang as a food town. He attacked Xiongnu cavalry at Juzhu and Pingcheng, receiving 500 households. He attacked Chen Xi and Yingbu, adding 1,000 households, totaling 6,900 in Ruyin. He served Gaozu until his death, then served Emperor Hui and Empress Lu. They thanked him for rescuing Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan, giving him a first-class residence. After Empress Lu's death, he supported Emperor Wen, remaining a royal servant. He died eight years later, posthumously named Wenhou. The title passed to Xiahou Po, who married Princess Pingyang but committed suicide, ending the feudal state. Xiahou Ying was originally named Teng Gong, and his descendants changed their surname to Sun.

Guan Ying of Suiyang County was a silk merchant. He served as a follower in Zhongjuan under Peigong. He defeated Qin's Shujun at Chengwu and Gangli, becoming Seventh Doctor. He attacked Qin at Bo, Kaifeng, and Quyu, becoming Xuanling Jun. He attacked west of Yangwu to Luoyang, defeating Qin north of Xi. He crossed the Yellow River, defeated the Nanyang governor, pacified Nanyang, entered Wuguan, fought at Lantian, and became Zhigui and Changwenjun. Peigong became King of Han, making him a doctor and then a lieutenant. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, captured Shuoyang, and surrendered to the King of Sai. He besieged Zhang Han at Feiqiu. He followed the king east, defeated King Yin, and pacified his territory. He attacked Xiang Yu's general Long Qie and Xiang Tuo at Dingtao, defeating them. The king granted him the title of Changwen Marquis with a seat in Pingxiang. He followed the king to conquer Ci and attack Pengcheng. After Xiang Yu's victory, he garrisoned Yongqiu, defeating Wang Wu and Wei Gongshen. He captured Wai and went to Rongyang. The king appointed him as a cavalry general with Li Bi and Luo Jia. He attacked Chu cavalry at Rongyang, cutting off their food routes. He attacked Xiang Guan at Lu, killing a You Sima and a cavalry general. He defeated Duke Zhe and Wang Wu at Yan, killing five generals. He defeated Dan Ying at the imperial palace. He led cavalry across the Yellow River, escorted the king, and met the prime minister's army at Yisu. He returned to Aocang, becoming imperial censor. In the third year, he received a food town in Pingxiang. As censor, he led cavalry east, defeating rebels at Lixia, capturing Hua Wushang and 46 officials. He captured Linzi and Qi Prime Minister Tian Guang. He pursued Tian Heng to Ying and Bo, defeating his cavalry. He captured Gu and Bo, killing Tian Su at Qiancheng. He followed Han Xin to attack Longdan at Baoshi, killing Longdan and capturing Zhou Lan. After Qi was pacified, Han Xin became king of Qi, sending Guan Ying to attack Chu's Gong Dai at Lu. He defeated the Xue County governor, capturing a cavalryman. He attacked Fu Yang and marched to Tong, Qili, and Xu. He crossed the silver carp, capturing cities to Guangling. He defeated Xideng and Langsheng at Gongpi, killing Zheng Gong. He defeated Chu cavalry at Wangdang, pacified Pengcheng, capturing Xiang Tuo and Liu, Xue, Pei, Deng, Lu, and Dao. He attacked Xuanse and Zhese, capturing a deputy general. He joined the king at Yixiang, defeating Xiang Lan at Chen. His men killed two generals and captured eight. The king added 2,500 households. He pursued Xiang Ji to Shucheng, defeating him. Five of his men killed Xiang Ji, becoming marquises. He captured 12,000 enemies and all generals. He captured Shucheng and Liyang. He crossed Dansi, defeated the Chengsu county magistrate, and pacified 52 counties north of Jin Hui. After the king's ascension, he added 3,000 households. As a chariot general, he attacked Zang Tu and captured Han Xin. He received a talisman and 2,500 households in Yingyin. He attacked King Xin of Han at Daidi, capturing six counties north of Loufan, beheading the left general. He defeated Xiongnu cavalry at Wuquan. He attacked Han Zhi and Bao Chu at Jinyang, killing a general. He led troops from Yan, Zhao, Qi, Liang, and Chu to defeat Xiongnu at Bishi. Surrounded at Pingcheng, he followed the emperor to attack Chen Xi, killing Hou Chang and five generals. He attacked Quni, Lunu, Shangquyang, Anguo, and Anping. He captured Dongdanse. When Yingbu rebelled, he attacked first, defeating Yingbu's generals at Xiangdi, beheading three deputy generals. He destroyed Yingbu's Shangzhu State and Da Sima. He defeated Fei Zhu. He captured Zuo Sima, and his men killed ten young generals, pursuing to the Huaihe River. The emperor added 2,500 households. After Yingbu's defeat, the emperor granted him 5,000 households in Yingyin. He captured two generals with 2,000 stone salaries, destroyed the enemy 16 times, occupied 46 cities, and pacified one traitor, two counties, and 52 counties. He captured two generals, one Zhuguo, and one Xiang. He served Emperor Hui and Empress Lu. After Empress Lu's death, Lu Lu and others rebelled. Guan Ying was sent to attack the Qi army but stationed at Rongyang, persuading the King of Qi to focus on the Lu family. After the Lu family was punished, he supported Emperor Wen, receiving 3,000 households and 1,000 catties of gold, becoming Taiwei. In the third year of Emperor Wen, he became Prime Minister. He led 85,000 cavalry against the Xiongnu, who retreated. He died as prime minister. The title passed to his grandson Bi Qiang, who lost it for crimes. During Emperor Wu's reign, his grandson Yi Zi was made Marquis of Linru but later deposed.

Fu Kuan, a cavalry officer of Wei, followed Peigong, raising troops in Hengyang. He captured Anyang and Gangli, defeated Zhao Ben at Kaifeng, and attacked Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu, killing 12 enemies, becoming a duke. Peigong became King of Han, making him Gongdejun. He entered Guanzhong as a right-hand cavalry general. After pacifying the Three Qin Dynasties, he received Diaoyin as a food town. He attacked Xiang Ji, following the king at Huai County, becoming Marquis of Tongde. He attacked Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Qie, killing a cavalry general. Under Han Xin, he defeated Qi Zaili and attacked Tian Jie. Under Cao Shen, he destroyed Bo County. For pacifying Qi, he received a talisman and 2,600 households in Yangling, becoming Marquis of Yangling. He became Right Prime Minister of Qi, then Prime Minister. In April, he attacked Chen Xi under Zhou Bo. In January, he became Xiangguo of Dai, commanding the garrison. Two years later, he became Prime Minister of Dai. He died in the fifth year of Xiaohui, posthumously named Jinghou. The title passed to his great-grandson Fu Yan, who was executed for treason.

Zhou Jie of Pei followed Gaozu as Zhongjuan, raising troops in Wanqu. He attacked Jiyang, defeated Li You, and attacked Qin at Shumian and Kaifeng, beheading a thousand-general and 57 enemies, capturing 73, becoming Lord Linping. He fought at Lantian, killing two chariot commanders, one cavalry commander, and 28 enemies, capturing 57. At Bashang, Peigong became King of Han, making him Marquis of Jianwu and Captain of Cavalry. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, attacking Zhang Ping at Longxi, occupying six counties, killing four chariot commanders and four horsemen. He attacked Chu eastward to Pengcheng. After defeat, he held Yongqiu, defeating Wang Wu. He captured Liang, attacking Xing Shuo at Jun County, capturing two captains, 12 Sima, and surrendering 4,680. He defeated Chu at Rongyang, receiving 4,200 households. He led an army to Hanoi, defeating Chu Bi at Chaoge, capturing two cavalry generals and 250 chariots. He attacked Anyang to Jipu, occupying ten counties. He defeated Tong's army, capturing two generals and four Sima, surrendering 2,400. He captured Handan, leading an army to capture Pingyang, beheading a governor and pacifying Ye County. He attacked Chaoge and Handan, defeating Chang's army, capturing six counties in Handan. He returned to Aocang, defeating Xiang Ji south of Chenggao, cutting off Chu's food routes. He defeated a champion in Ludi, occupying Gao, Tan, Xiapi, Qixian, and Zhuyi. He attacked Xiang Han at Jiyang. He returned to Chen, defeating Xiang Ji's army, pacifying Jiangling.
