translation:
Emperor Xiaowu had six sons.
Queen Wei gave birth to Prince Ru, Zao Jieyu gave birth to Emperor Xiaozhao, Mrs. Wang gave birth to King Huai of Qi Liu Hong, Li Ji gave birth to King Liu Dan of Yanla, King Li of Guangling Liu Xu, and Mrs. Li gave birth to King Ai Liu of Changyi.
The ruthless prince Liu Ju was established as the crown prince in the first year of Yuanshou. He was seven years old at that time.
At the beginning, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was only 29 years old and he was the crown prince. He was very happy and built a Plum Temple for this purpose. He ordered Dongfang Shuo and Meigao to write congratulations to worship the Plum God.
When the prince grew up, he was ordered to study "Gongyang Chunqiu" and "Gu Liang Chunqiu" from Duke Xiaqiu Jiang.
When he was twenty years old, he was crowned and lived in the Tai Palace. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty built Bowang Garden for him, allowing him to interact with guests and act according to his interests. As a result, many heresies came to him as tribute.
In the fourth year of Yuanding's reign, he married Shi Liangdi and gave birth to his son Liu Jin, who was called the grandson of Emperor Shi.
In the later years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the imperial guard fell out of favor and Jiang Chong was reused. Jiang Chong had grudges against the prince and the Wei family, and was worried that the prince would execute him after Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. At this time, a witchcraft case occurred, and Jiang Chong took advantage of this to seek personal revenge.
At that time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was already old and tired of things. He suspected that everyone around him was guilty of curses and poisons, and issued an edict to investigate the matter severely.
Prime Minister Gongsun He and his son, the princesses of Yangshi and Zhuyi, and the Queen's brother's son Changping Houwei and his wife were all implicated and killed.
All these are recorded in "The Biography of Gongsun He" and "The Biography of Jiang Chong".
Jiang Chong was responsible for investigating the witchcraft case. He already knew the emperor's mood, so he told the emperor that there was a poisonous atmosphere in the palace. He entered the palace and went to the emperor's residence, demolished the throne and dug up the ground.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty sent Hou Hanshuo, Yushi Zhanggan, Huangmen Suwen and others to assist Jiang Chong.
Jiang Chong went to the prince's palace to dig for poisonous things and found a little figure carved from paulownia wood.
At that time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was ill and went to Ganquan Palace to escape the summer heat. Only the queen and the prince were in the palace.
The prince summoned his young master Shi De and asked him what he should do about this matter. Shi De was afraid that he would be executed together because he was the master, so he said to the prince: Before this, the prime minister and his son, the two princesses, and the Wei family were all implicated and punished. Now the witch and the officials who came to investigate the matter dug up the ground and found the evidence. We don't know if the witch put it there intentionally, or if it was really there. We can't explain it ourselves. We can pretend to be an imperial edict and use talismans to arrest Jiang Chong and others in jail, and trace out their treacherous conspiracy.
Besides, the emperor is recuperating in Ganquan Palace, and the greetings from the queen and the prince's staff have not been answered. The emperor's life or death is unknown. And now that a traitor has done such a thing, prince, don't you remember the murder of Prince Fusu of the Qin Dynasty?
The prince was very anxious and accepted Shi De's opinion.
On Renwu day in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenghe, the prince sent a retainer to pretend to be a messenger and arrest Jiang Chong and others.
According to Dao Hou Han Shuo, he suspected that the envoy was deceitful and refused to obey the edict, so the retainers killed Han Shuo.
Yushi Zhanggan escaped after being chopped and ran back to Ganquan Palace.
The prince ordered his family to be abandoned and entered the Changqiu Gate of the Weiyang Palace overnight with the talisman. He reported it to the queen through Changyu Yihua, sent a carriage wrapped in the middle stable to load the archers, moved the weapons from the arsenal, dispatched the Changle Palace guards, declared to the civil and military officials that Jiang Chong was rebelling, and then killed Jiang Chong to patrol the government and the public, and burned the barbarian shaman to death in Shanglin Garden.
Then he deployed the guests as generals to fight against the army of Prime Minister Liu Quli and others.
There was great chaos in Chang'an City, and there were rumors that the prince was rebelling, so the people refused to join the prince.
The prince's army was defeated and he fled without being caught.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was furious, and his officials were worried and didn't know what to do.
A Huguan elder named Mao wrote a letter saying: Sir, I heard that father is like the sky, mother is like the earth, and children are like all things in the world.
Therefore, if the balance of the heaven and earth is peaceful and the yin and yang are harmonious, all things can flourish and grow; if a father is kind and the mother is loving, within the family, the children will be filial.
If Yin and Yang are not in harmony, all things will be injured and die prematurely; if father and son are not in harmony, the family will be in disarray and die.
Therefore, if the father is not like the father, the son will not be like the son; if the king is not like the king, the subjects will not be like the subjects. Even if there is food, can we eat it?
In ancient times, Yu Shun was the most filial person, but he did not please his father Gusou. His filial piety was slandered, and Boqi was exiled. Although they were the closest relatives, father and son were suspicious of each other.
Why is this?
It is caused by the accumulation of more and more slander.
From this point of view, no son is unfilial, but fathers are sometimes unaware. The current crown prince is the direct heir of the Han Dynasty, inheriting the legacy of thousands of generations, and feeling the weight of the creation of his ancestors. In terms of kinship, he is your eldest son.
Jiang Chong is just a commoner, a lowly official in the countryside. Your Majesty allows him to be prominent and put him in important positions. He passes your supreme orders to persecute and embarrass the crown prince. He forges to cover up his evil deeds and deceit. He is a bunch of villains who confuse right and wrong, causing a gap between relatives and preventing them from communicating.
The prince came forward to express his gratitude but was not received by the emperor. He retreated and defended himself and was besieged by the rebellious ministers. Because he had been wronged and had nowhere to appeal, he could not bear the grief and anger, so he raised an army to kill Jiang Chong. Afterwards, he was frightened and fled out. This was just the son secretly using his father's troops to solve problems and save himself. I privately believe that the prince has no evil intentions.
"The Book of Songs" says: The black flies flying around are covered with fences; a gentle and kind-hearted gentleman should not listen to simple words; endless slanders will cause chaos and unrest in neighboring countries.
In the past, Jiang Chongjin slandered and killed the crown prince of King Zhao. Everyone in the world knew that he should have been killed.
Now, without understanding the truth, His Majesty thought that the Crown Prince had made a mistake and severely blamed him. He was so angry that he sent a large army to capture the Crown Prince. My lord, I secretly feel sad for this.
I heard that Wu Zixu lost his title for being loyal, Bigan sacrificed himself for being benevolent, and the loyal ministers were loyal and expressed their opinions regardless of the sword or ax on their necks. Their purpose was to help the king stabilize the country.
The Book of Songs says: Catch those bad guys who are slandering and throw them to the wolves, tigers and leopards. I hope your majesty will feel relieved and appreciate the relationship between father and son a little. Don't worry about the prince's mistakes, withdraw your troops quickly, and don't let the prince live in exile for a long time.
Your Majesty, I am very sincere. Once the king's order is issued, I will be punished respectfully under the Jianzhang Gate.
After reading the letter, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was moved and woke up.
The prince fled eastward to Hu County and hid in a common people's house in Quanjiu.
The family was poor and often sold shoes to support the prince.
The prince had an old friend living in Hu County. Hearing that he was wealthy, he sent someone to call him, and he was discovered.
The local officials brought people to round up the prince. The prince thought that he could not escape, so he went into the house, closed the door and hanged himself.
Zhang Fuchang, a big man from Shanyang County, was a soldier. He kicked the door open. Shi Lishou, the magistrate of Xin'an County, hurriedly stepped forward to untie the prince and hug him. The owner of the house fought with the soldiers and died, and the two royal grandchildren were killed together.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was already sad about the death of the prince, but he still issued a Shao Shu saying: "The promised reward is to prove our faith."
Li Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Han, and Zhang Fuchang was granted the title of Marquis of Ti.
After a long time, most of the stories about witchcraft harming people were untrue.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty knew that the prince was just scared and ran away, and had no other intentions. In addition, Che Qianqiu once again appealed for the prince's grievances. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty promoted Che Qianqiu to the rank of prime minister, and then executed Jiang Chong's entire family.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was saddened that the prince had died innocently, so he built the Palace of Thoughts and a Tower for Returning and Watching Thoughts upon Return in Hu County.
Everyone in the world felt sad after hearing about it.
At the beginning, the prince had three sons and one daughter. The daughter was married to the son of Chengsi of Marquis Pingyu.
When the prince failed, they were all killed at the same time.
Empress Wei and Shi Liangdi were buried in the south of Chang'an City after their deaths.
His grandson, his concubine, his wife, and his granddaughter were buried in Guangmingyuan.
The two grandsons who fled with the prince were buried in Hu County with the prince.
The prince had a grandson who survived, and he was the son of Emperor Shi and Mrs. Wang. When he was eighteen years old, he inherited the throne and became Emperor Mo Xiaoxuan. As soon as Emperor Xiaoxuan came to power, he issued an edict saying: The former crown prince is buried in Hu County. There is no Mi name and a temple to hold sacrifices throughout the year. It is necessary to decide on the Mi name, build a cemetery and arrange for the households to guard the tomb.
Relevant officials petitioned and said: According to etiquette and law, if you become someone else's heir, you must be someone else's son. Therefore, your biological parents were demoted and condescended to enjoy no sacrifices. This was out of respect for their ancestors.
Your Majesty is the successor of Emperor Xiaozhao. He must inherit the great sacrifices to his ancestors and the etiquette must not go beyond the limits.
You must act respectfully and in accordance with Emperor Xiaozhao's decision: the former crown prince's mausoleum will be built in Hu County, Shi Liangdi's mausoleum will be built in the north of Bowang Garden, and the mausoleum of your father Shi Huang's grandson will be built in the north of the Guangming Garden wall.
According to the Mi method, Mi is an actual assessment of the behavior during life. I think your biological father's Mi name can be used as a mourning, and your biological mother can be mourned. After that, a cemetery will be built according to the specifications of the princes and kings, and three hundred households will be allocated with the land for worship.
The former crown prince Mi's nickname was Ru, and he was assigned 200 households to enshrine the land.
Shi Liangdi was Mrs. Ru, and she was assigned thirty families to guard the tomb.
The cemetery is set up with official positions such as chief and chief to protect, worship and protect the surrounding area according to the regulations.
Therefore, Xieliju, Quexiang, Hu County, was designated as the Violent Garden, the area east of Baiting in Chang'an County was designated as the Violent Houyuan, and Chengxiang in Guangmingyuan was designated as the Mourning Garden.
Mausoleums were built and buried.
Eight years later, the relevant officials said: "Li" records that the father is a scholar. If the son becomes the emperor, the father must also perform sacrifices according to the emperor's standards.
The mourning king should be honored as Huang Kao, build an ancestral temple, build a dormitory hall on the basis of the cemetery, and offer sacrifices and enjoyment here on time.
The number of households dedicated to the mausoleum reached 1,600, and Fengming County was established here.
Mrs. Li was respected as Queen Li, and a cemetery and a land for worship were set up. It was also necessary to increase the number of households in Liyuan and Lihouyuan, each with a total of 300 households.
King Huai of Qi Liu Hong, King Liu Dan of Yan, and King Liu Xu of Guangling were canonized on the same day. They were all given policy books. Taking into account the different folk customs of each fiefdom, they made separate admonitions and admonishments, saying: On Yisi day of April in the sixth year of Yuanshou, the emperor sent Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, to consecrate the prince Liu Hong as the king of Qi in the temple. The book said: Woohoo!
Less than Liu Hong, he accepted the green social soil.
In accordance with the order arranged by the Emperor of Heaven, and with reference to the ancient system, I established your country, established it in the east, and served as a barrier and auxiliary wing of the Han Dynasty from generation to generation.
Alas!
Remember, please listen to my edict.
Destiny is fickle, and a person's love for benevolence can make him smart and brilliant; if he does not pursue benevolence and righteousness, it will make a gentleman slack.
If you wholeheartedly adhere to the virtues of being righteous and tolerant, you will be able to preserve the blessings given to you by the Emperor of Heaven forever; if you commit sins and behave badly, disaster will befall your kingdom and yourself. Alas!
To protect the country and govern the people, can we not be cautious?
You, the king, need to be vigilant!
Liu Hong's mother, Mrs. Wang, was favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. Liu Hong was especially favored by Emperor Wu. Eight years after becoming king, he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished.
The policy letter to Liu Dan, King of Yanla, said: Woohoo!
Little Liu Dan, accept this black soil, build your country, seal it in the north, and serve as a barrier and auxiliary wing of the Han Dynasty for generations.
Alas!
The Xunhuan family mistreats the elderly, has a heart like an animal, and uses cunning and cunning to conquer hundreds of thousands of people on the border.
I ordered the generals to go and punish them for the crimes they committed.
The commanders of tens of thousands, the commanders of thousands, and the thirty-two military commanders all stopped their troops and rushed to surrender to us.
Xunhuan migrated to other places, and my northern region was peaceful.
You must be whole-hearted, do not create any grudges, do not do immoral things, and do not weaken border defenses.
Soldiers who have not received training are not allowed to be called into battle.
You, the king, need to be vigilant!
When Liu Dan grew up, he came to the feudal state. He was an eloquent person, studied classics and various schools of thought extensively, and was fond of astrology, calendars, mathematics, advocating leisure travel, archery and hunting, etc., and attracted knights and warriors.
When Prince Wei was defeated and King Huai of Qi died again, Liu Dan thought that he should be made the crown prince according to the ranking of his brothers, so he wrote a letter requesting to return to Beijing to stay in the palace.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was angry and imprisoned the envoy he sent to write the letter.
Later, because of harboring fugitives, his fiefdom was cut off from Liangxiang, Anci, and Wen'an counties.
From then on, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty disliked Liu Dan, and later made his youngest son the prince.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty died, the prince succeeded to the throne and was named Emperor Xiaozhao. He issued letters stamped with jade seals to various princes and kings.
When Liu Dan received the letter, he refused to mourn. He said: The envelope containing the seal is small. I suspect there has been a change in the capital.
He sent his cronies Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru and others to Chang'an to inquire about the news in the name of asking about etiquette.
Wang Ru went to see Jinwu Guo Guangyi and asked what kind of illness the emperor had when he died, who succeeded him and how old he was.
Guo Guangyi said that at that time, he was waiting for the emperor's edict in Wuzha Palace. People in the palace were clamoring that the emperor had died. The generals supported the prince as emperor. The prince was about eight or nine years old and would not leave the palace during the funeral.
Wang Ru and others came back and reported to King Yanla.
King Yanla said: "The emperor abandoned his ministers and left without saying anything. The eldest princess of Gaiyi was not seen. It's very strange."
Then he sent a senior official to Chang'an, the capital, to write a letter saying: I privately saw Emperor Xiaowu practicing the way of a sage. He was filial to his ancestors and loving to his relatives. He harmoniously united his subjects and billions of people. His benevolence united the heaven and earth. The sun and the moon shined brightly. Might permeated the world. Countries from far away offered treasures. Come to worship, add dozens of counties and counties, nearly double the territory, offer sacrifices to Mount Tai, worship Father Liang, travel around the world, and place treasures and foreign objects from far away in the Ancestral Temple. His benevolence is so majestic and grand. I request that temples be built for Emperor Xiaowu in every county.
The memorial was submitted and reported back that the emperor had read it.
At that time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government and rewarded King Yan with 30 million yuan and increased the number of 13,000 households in the fiefdom.
Liu Dan said angrily: I should be the emperor, how can you reward me!
So he formed a conspiracy with Liu Chang, the son of King Ai of Zhongshan, and Liu Ze, the grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others in the clan. They lied that they had received an edict from Emperor Wu and could take charge of local administration, build military preparedness, and prepare for extraordinary incidents.
Liu Chang then issued an order to the ministers on behalf of Liu Dan: "I relied on the virtue of the late emperor to lead the northern vassal country. I personally accepted the wise edict. I have to take charge of local administration, command the arsenal and weapons, organize the military equipment. I have important responsibilities and work hard from morning to night. How will you, the officials, assist me with advice?"
Furthermore, although the Yan State was small, it was founded in the Zhou Dynasty. The first was Zhao Gongxi, and the second was King Zhao and Xiang of the Six Kingdoms period. It has been a thousand years, how can we say that there are no wise men in the Yan Kingdom?
It has been more than 30 years since I took charge of the government and listened to the government, but I haven't heard anything yet.
Is it because I have poor hearing and vision?
Or is it that the doctors’ thinking is insufficient?
What's the mistake?
Now I want to correct evil and prevent bad behavior, commend knowledge and promote gentleness, appease the people, and change customs. Where should I start?
Doctors, please answer with all your heart, I will consider and adopt your suggestions.
All the ministers took off their hats and thanked him.
Cheng Zhen, the doctor, said to Liu Dan: Your Majesty, you have lost the status you deserve. Now you can only get up and claim it, not sit back and wait.
As long as the king joins the army, the people, subjects, and even women in the country will move forward and follow the king.
Liu Dan said: In the past, when Empress Lu was in power, she made Liu Hong, the son of Emperor Hui, the emperor through deception, and the princes and kings served him for eight years.
Later, Empress Dowager Lu died, and the ministers killed all the kings of the Lu family and ushered in Emperor Xiaowen of the Han Dynasty. Only then did the world know that Liu Hong was not the true son of Emperor Xiaohui.
As the eldest son of Emperor Wu, I was not able to be established as emperor. I wrote a letter suggesting building a temple for Emperor Wu, but it was not accepted.
I doubt that the current emperor is from the Liu family.
He then planned with Liu Ze and others to write a proclamation of fraud and slander, claiming that the young emperor was not the son of Emperor Xiaowu, but was a forgery planned by some ministers, and that the people of the world would rise up to attack him.
Send people to spread the news to all counties and counties to shake the people's hearing and hearing.
Liu Ze planned to return to Linzi to send troops and launch an uprising together with King Yan.
Liu Dan immediately took action to recruit local evil people, collected copper and iron to make armor and weapons, drilled chariots and cavalry officers and soldiers many times, built flag and drum chariots, and used the horse-headed knight as the pioneer.
Liu Dan, an official from prime minister to lieutenant, supervised the chariots, cavalry and horses, mobilized the people to gather and set up paddocks, and conducted large-scale hunting in Wen'an County to train soldiers and horses and wait for the arrival of the uprising.
The doctor Han Yi and others repeatedly tried to stop Liu Dan, but Liu Dan killed Han Yi and fifteen others in total.
At this time, Liu Cheng, the Marquis of Fu, learned of the plot of Liu Ze and others, and reported it to Jun Buyi, the governor of Qingzhou, who arrested Liu Ze and reported it to the court.
The emperor sent Da Honglucheng to review the matter, which implicated King Yan.
The edict did not punish King Yan, but put Liu Ze and others to death.
Liu Cheng, the marquis of Fu, was granted the title.
After a long time, Liu Dan's sister Eyigai Princess, Zuo General Shangguan Jie and his son had a feud with Huo Guang because of the struggle for power. They all knew that Liu Dan resented Huo Guang, so they secretly formed a relationship with the Yan State.
Liu Dan sent Sun Zongzhi and other more than ten groups of people to bring a lot of gold, silver, treasures and horses as gifts to Princess Gai.
Shangguan Jie and the imperial censor Sang Hongyang colluded with Liu Dan. They wrote down Huo Guang's faults many times and told Liu Dan, asking him to report Huo Guang to the emperor.
Shangguan Jie wanted to send his memorial to all the officials from the palace.
Liu Dan was very happy when he heard about it, so he went to the bookstore and said: In the past, King Qin Zheng seized the throne of the emperor, controlled the order of a generation, and intimidated all the nations. Che Qianqiu's intelligence may not be better than others, but because he eliminates bad luck, curbs the source of disaster, eliminates major disasters in times of crisis, and guides good fortune, he attracts the blessing and help of the Emperor of Heaven and the people.
summary:
Emperor Xiaowu had six sons from various consorts. Prince Ru, born to Queen Wei, was established as crown prince at age seven in the first year of Yuanshou. Emperor Wu was delighted and built a Plum Temple, ordering Dongfang Shuo and Meigao to write congratulations. The prince studied classical texts under Duke Xiaqiu Jiang, was crowned at twenty, and resided in the Tai Palace, where Emperor Wu built Bowang Garden for him to interact with guests.

In the fourth year of Yuanding, the prince married Shi Liangdi and fathered Liu Jin. In Emperor Wu's later years, Jiang Chong gained favor and held grudges against the prince and the Wei family. When witchcraft accusations arose, Jiang Chong exploited them for revenge. Emperor Wu, elderly and suspicious, ordered severe investigation. Prime Minister Gongsun He, his son, princesses, and the queen's brother's son were all implicated and killed.

Jiang Chong investigated the witchcraft case, claiming poisonous air in the palace. He entered the palace, demolished the throne, and dug up ground. Assisted by others, he went to the prince's palace and found a small figure carved from paulownia wood. Emperor Wu was ill at Ganquan Palace, leaving only the queen and prince in the palace.

The prince consulted his young master Shi De, who warned him about the fate of Prince Fusu of Qin and advised pretending to issue an imperial edict to arrest Jiang Chong. The prince agreed. On Renwu day in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenghe, the prince sent retainers to arrest Jiang Chong and others. One official was killed, another escaped to Ganquan Palace. The prince entered Weiyang Palace, reported to the queen, mobilized weapons and guards, declared Jiang Chong a rebel, killed him, and burned a shaman. He then deployed guests as generals against Prime Minister Liu Quli's army. Chang'an fell into chaos, and the prince's army was defeated. He fled but was not caught.

Emperor Wu was furious. A Huguan elder named Mao wrote a letter arguing that the prince had no evil intentions, comparing the situation to ancient examples of slander causing family discord. He urged the emperor to understand the prince's actions and withdraw troops. Emperor Wu was moved and awakened.

The prince fled east to Hu County, hiding in a commoner's home. The family was poor, selling shoes to support him. When discovered by local officials, the prince hanged himself. His two grandsons were also killed. Emperor Wu, saddened, later learned the witchcraft accusations were mostly untrue. He executed Jiang Chong's family, built the Palace of Thoughts and a tower in Hu County, and mourned the prince's death.

The prince had three sons and one daughter, all killed when he failed. Empress Wei and Shi Liangdi were buried south of Chang'an. One grandson survived and later became Emperor Xiaoxuan. Upon ascending, he issued edicts regarding proper burial and memorial arrangements for his father, the former crown prince, establishing cemeteries and households for worship.

King Huai of Qi, Liu Hong, died without son after eight years. King Liu Dan of Yanla was eloquent, studied classics, and attracted knights. After Prince Wei's defeat and Liu Hong's death, Liu Dan believed he should be crown prince. Emperor Wu became angry, imprisoned his envoy, and later cut off his fiefdom. Emperor Wu disliked Liu Dan and made his youngest son prince instead.

When Emperor Wu died and the prince succeeded as Emperor Xiaozhao, Liu Dan refused to mourn, suspecting changes in the capital. He sent inquiries and later requested temples be built for Emperor Wu. General Huo Guang rewarded him, but Liu Dan angrily claimed he should be emperor. He conspired with others, claiming the young emperor was not Emperor Wu's true son. The plot was discovered, and Liu Dan's co-conspirators were executed. Later, Liu Dan's sister and others conspired with him against Huo Guang. The fourteen-year-old Emperor Zhao trusted Huo Guang and distrusted Liu Dan. The conspiracy was exposed, and Liu Dan hanged himself after receiving an imperial seal condemning his actions.

King Li of Guangling, Liu Xu, was strong and liked entertainment. He coveted the throne when Emperor Zhao was young and childless. He employed witches to pray for his ascension. When Emperor Zhao died and King Changyi succeeded, Liu Xu had witches curse him. After King Changyi was deposed and Emperor Xuan ascended, Liu Xu continued his schemes. His treason was discovered, and he hanged himself after a final banquet.

King Ai of Changyi, Liu He, was summoned to preside over Emperor Zhao's funeral. He traveled hastily, causing horses to die. During his twenty-seven days as emperor, he behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang deposed him and returned him to his hometown. Later, Emperor Xuan granted him the title of Marquis of Haihun. After his death, his title was terminated.

The text concludes with a reflection on the witchcraft case's harm, noting it was not solely Jiang Chong's fault but also divine will, comparing the situation to the Qin dynasty's downfall and emphasizing that war, like fire, burns itself if not stopped.

translation:
King Li of Huainan, with a long name, was the youngest son of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty. His mother used to be the beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao.
In the eighth year of Emperor Gao's reign, Emperor Gao passed by the State of Zhao from Dongyuan. King Tong presented a beautiful woman to Emperor Gao. This was King Li's mother. She became pregnant after being favored.
King Zhao did not dare to let her return to the palace, so he built an outer palace for her to live in.
When the rebellion by Guangao and others was discovered and King Zhao was implicated, King Tong's mother, brothers and beauties were all arrested and imprisoned in Hanoi.
King Li's mother was also imprisoned. She told the officials: I was once favored by the emperor and had a son.
After hearing this, the officials told the emperor that the emperor was very angry with King Zhao and ignored King Li's mother.
King Li's uncle Chang Jian told Empress Lu through Piyanghou. Empress Lu was jealous and refused to defend them, and Piyanghou did not fight for him.
Queen Li's mother committed suicide out of resentment and anger after giving birth to Queen Li.
The officials sent King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it very much and asked Queen Lu to raise King Li, and she was buried in the county where King Li's mother lived.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Huainan, Yingbu, rebelled. The emperor personally led his troops to destroy Yingbu, so he made his son Liu Chang the king of Huainan.
King Huainan lost his mother when he was young and often relied on Empress Lu. During the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, he was favored for this reason and had no trouble. However, he often resented Marquis Piyang in his heart, but he did not dare to show it.
In the early days of Emperor Xiaowen's accession to the throne, he thought he was the closest person to the royal family and was proud and indulgent, breaking the law several times.
The emperor forgave him.
In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he behaved very arrogantly when he came to court.
He followed the emperor to the royal gardens for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother".
King Li was powerful and could lift the cauldron, so he went to pay homage to Marquis Piyang.
When Marquis Piyang came out to receive him, King Li took out the iron spine hidden in his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his followers to chop off his head.
Then he drove his horse to the emperor's palace, took off his shirt, exposed his arms, and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have committed a crime and been imprisoned for visiting the king. Marquis Piyang had the ability to persuade Empress Lu to save her, but he did not try his best to save her. This is the first crime."
King Zhao Ruyi and his mother were both innocent. Empress Lu murdered them, and Marquis Piyang did not try his best to dissuade them. This was the second crime.
Empress Lu wanted to harm our Liu family by conferring the title of king on the Lu family. Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade her. This is the third crime.
I just killed bad guys for the people of the world and avenged my mother. I am willing to confess my sin to Your Majesty.
Emperor Wen took pity on him because he was avenging his relatives and pardoned his sin.
At that time, everyone from Queen Mother Bo to the Crown Prince and all the ministers were afraid of King Li. As a result, King Li returned to the feudal state and became more arrogant and indulgent. He did not obey the laws of the Han Dynasty. He had left and right guards and clear roads like the emperor when he came in and out. He made his own laws and showed disrespect when writing to the emperor several times.
Emperor Wen could not blame him personally.
At that time, the emperor's uncle Bo Zhao was a general. Emperor Wen respected him and ordered Bo Zhao to write to King Li, admonishing him many times:
I heard that the king is upright and brave, charitable and generous, loyal and decisive. This is God using the talents of a saint to greatly reward the king. You must not understand these.
The king's behavior today is inconsistent with this God-given wisdom.
The emperor had just ascended the throne and wanted to transfer the title of Hou Yi in Huainan to another place, but the king said it was unnecessary.
The emperor finally changed the title, and the king received the benefits of three counties, which was very generous.
The king asked to enter the court to see the emperor because he had never seen him before, but before he could finish talking about his brotherhood, he killed the princes.
The emperor did not send officials to investigate the matter and pardoned the king. This was very generous to the king.
The Han law stipulates that if there is a shortage of officials of two thousand stones, the emperor must report to the court to send someone to supplement them. However, the king expelled the officials appointed by the court and requested that he establish a prime minister and two thousand stone officials.
The emperor violated the solemn laws of the world and allowed the king to do this. This is very generous to the king!
The king wants to abandon his feudal state and become a commoner, guarding the ancestral graves of Zhending.
The emperor disagreed and asked the king not to lose his status as King of Huainan. This was very kind to the king!
Your Majesty, you should obey the laws day and night and be loyal to your duties, so as to live up to the emperor's love for you. But now you speak arrogantly, do whatever you want, and are slandered by everyone in the world. It is not a wise move to send you away.
The king controls thousands of miles and rules over thousands of people. This is Emperor Gao's kindness to you.
Emperor Gao dined and slept in the open, rain or shine, braved the rain, arrows and rocks, fought in the field and attacked the city, and was seriously injured. He created a great cause for future generations. It was extremely difficult and dangerous. Your Majesty does not think about the difficulties of your ancestors in starting a business. He always reflects and is vigilant, cultivates his moral integrity, raises livestock, harvests rice, and prepares many sacrifices to worship his ancestors, so as not to forget the great kindness and virtue of his ancestors. However, your Majesty wants to abandon his feudal state and become a common man. This is a big mistake.
Moreover, coveting the reputation of surrendering the country and abandoning the great cause of the late emperor is unfilial.
Our fathers conquered the country. If your children cannot hold on, this is unworthy.
It is unjust to go to Zhending instead of guarding Changling, and to put mother before father.
It was disobedient to disobey the emperor's orders many times.
It is rude to guard one's mother's grave just to show one's superiority over one's brothers.
If a favored minister is guilty, he may be punished by asking for execution, or he may be punished with physical punishment at the most serious level. This is unkind.
It is unwise to regard being a commoner as a high priority and regard the status of a prince as low.
It is unlucky not to work hard to study and delve into the great road, but to act arbitrarily based on emotional impulse.
The above eight points are all dangerous paths, and you, my king, have implemented them all. Abandoning the position of king, showing the bravery of Zhuan Zhu and Meng Ben, often walking in and out of dangerous roads. In my opinion, the incense of Emperor Gaozu can no longer be inherited with you. Please think clearly, your Majesty.
In the past, the king of Zhou killed Uncle Guan and exiled Uncle Cai to stabilize the Zhou Dynasty; Duke Huan of Qi killed his brothers and returned to Qi. Qin Shihuang killed his two younger brothers and moved his mother to Xianyang Palace to stabilize the Qin state; King Liu Zhong of Qing fled when the Xiongnu attacked Daidi, and Emperor Gao deprived him of his feudal state in order to enforce national laws; King Xingju of Jibei rebelled with his troops, and the emperor killed him to stabilize the Han Dynasty.
Therefore, in ancient times, the kings of Zhou and the Marquis of Qi did this. Today, the kings of Qin and Han emperors still use this method. The kings do not understand the methods of governing the country and bringing peace to the world in the past. Instead, they expect the emperor to be lenient and boundless because of their kinship. This is impossible.
Anyone who flees to the vassal states or harbors criminals will be punished by law.
Even in the king's place, all the officials in charge must bear the responsibility.
Nowadays, those who are officials in the vassal states are under the supervision of the censor; those who are military officials are under the supervision of lieutenants; guests who come in and out of the palace are under the supervision of Weiwei and Daxing; those who come from minority areas and have no names in the household registration book and report their household registration are under the supervision of internal history and county magistrates.
The Prime Minister of the Kingdom wants to pass the responsibility to the lower palace. It is impossible for him to have no responsibility.
If the king does not correct his mistakes, what will you do when Moting imprisons the king in the palace and interrogates people below the prime minister?
Ruining my father's great cause, becoming a pitiful person for the common people, having all my favorite ministers punished, and being laughed at by everyone in the world is a disgrace to the late emperor's merits. I think your Majesty should not be like this.
You should immediately change your ways, write a letter of apology to the emperor, and tell him: Unfortunately, I lost my father at an early age and was lonely since I was a child. When the Lu family was in power, I was often threatened with death.
After you came to the throne, Your Majesty, I relied on your kindness to be extravagant and licentious, and did many unscrupulous things.
Thinking about the mistakes I had made, I was filled with fear. Now I am lying on the ground waiting for the Fa-rectification and dare not get up.
The emperor will definitely be happy after hearing this.
Your Majesty, if your brothers above are happy, your ministers below will live longer. If there is harmony between above and below, the world will be at peace.
May your Majesty accept my suggestion and implement it immediately.
If you hesitate and refuse to implement it, disaster will be like an arrow that has been shot out and cannot be taken back.
King Li was very unhappy after receiving the remonstrance.
In the sixth year, he sent Dan and other seventy men to conspire with Chai Qi, the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, and sent forty military chariots back to the valley, and sent people to Minyue and Xiongnu.
After the incident was discovered, the emperor wanted to punish him, so he sent someone to summon King Huainan to Beijing.
After the King of Huainan arrived in Chang'an, Prime Minister Zhang Cang and Dianke Feng Jing acted on behalf of the imperial censor. After interrogating Zong Zheng and Ting Wei, they reported: Liu Chang abandoned the laws of the late emperor and did not obey the orders of Emperor Shao. He lived extravagantly. He made chariot and horse umbrellas that could be compared with those of the emperor. He made laws without implementing the laws of the Han Dynasty.
He appointed officials on his own, made Lang Zhongchun the prime minister, gathered the guilty fugitives among the princes and kings of the desert, made them hide and arranged residences for them, managed their families, gave them money and items, granted them titles, and gave them land and houses as salaries. Some were as high as Guannai Marquis, and were given a salary of two thousand dan.
Seventy people, including Dan, the doctor, and Kaizhang, who had lost his official title due to guilt, and Chai Qi, the prince of Jipuhou, conspired to rebel, endangering the national power of the Han Dynasty, and planned to let the Minyue and Huns send troops.
After the incident was revealed, Chang'an Wei Qi and others went to arrest Kaizhang. Liu Chang hid him instead of handing him over to the officials, and conspired with the former lieutenant Lin Ji to kill Kaizhang. They prepared a coffin and clothes for him, buried him in Feiling, deceived the officials sent by the court and said: I don't know where he is, and built a tomb for him.
In addition, Liu Chang secretly killed an innocent person; ordered officials to kill six innocent people; made those guilty who should be punished in public hide; deceived the arresting officials in order to absolve them of their crimes; and gave people without authorization Fourteen people were sentenced to death for crimes above Chengdu without reporting the crime; 18 people were pardoned for crimes that should have been punished by death; 58 people were pardoned for crimes that should have been less than Chengdu; 94 people were given titles below Guannei Marquis.
Liu Chang fell ill a few days ago. His Majesty was very worried and sent an envoy to deliver preserved dates. However, Liu Chang refused to go out to see the envoy sent by the emperor.
The common people in the Nanhai area on the border of the Lujiang River made trouble. The King of Huainan sent troops to attack the rebels. His Majesty sent an envoy to deliver fifty pieces of silk as rewards to those who worked hard among the officers and soldiers.
Liu Chang did not want to accept the reward, but said contemptuously: "There is no hard work."
Wang Zhi of Nanhai wrote a letter to the emperor asking for jade and silk, but Qu Ji burned the letter without reporting it to the emperor.
Officials asked to summon Qu Ji to Chang'an, but Liu Chang refused to let Lin Ji come, saying that "Yin Ji was ill."
The crime Liu Chang committed should be beheaded in the market, and we request that he be sentenced in accordance with the law.
The emperor issued an edict saying: I cannot bear to punish King Li, so I should discuss it with the princes and the two thousand officials.
After discussion, the princes, 2,000 officials and 43 officials and infants all agreed that the matter should be dealt with according to law.
The emperor ordered: Then pardon Liu Chang's death penalty and dethrone him from the throne.
The officials reported: I request Zaoshang to exile him to Qiongdi, Yandao County, Shu County, and order his children and their mother to live with them. The Yandao County magistrate can build a house for them, and provide firewood, vegetable salt, cooking utensils and mats for each meal.
The emperor ordered: Supply Liu Chang with food, give him five kilograms of meat and two measures of wine.
He ordered ten favored concubines of his past to live with him.
So all the people who conspired with Liu Chang were killed.
He dispatched Liu Chang and sent them heavy-loaded carriages and horses, and all the counties they passed through were equipped with carriages to transport them one by one.
Yuan Ang remonstrated with the emperor and said: The emperor has always indulged the King of Huainan and did not set up strict prime ministers and tutors, which has led to this situation today.
The King of Huainan has an upright character, and now the Emperor has suddenly given him such a big blow. I am afraid that he could not withstand the fog, cold and dew and died of illness on the road. Then His Majesty has the reputation of killing his brothers. What should I do?
The emperor said: I am also troubled by this. I just let him regret himself and recalled him.
The King of Huainan asked the waiter: Who said you, me, and I are brave?
I ended up like this because I was arrogant and didn't know my fault.
So he stopped eating and starved to death.
The county escort did not dare to open the prison van.
When they arrived at Yongxian County, the magistrate of Yongxian County opened the prison car and reported to the emperor that King Huainan was dead.
When the emperor heard about it, he cried sadly and said to Yuan An: I didn't listen to you, and the result was that King Huainan died.
Yuan Ang said: The King of Huainan is already like this. There is no other way. Please be at ease, Your Majesty.
The emperor asked: What should we do?
He replied: Only by killing the prime minister and censor can we apologize to the world.
The emperor immediately ordered the prime minister and censors to arrest those who did not deliver food and food to the king of Huainan from various counties and beheaded them on the street. So the King of Huainan was buried in Yongdi according to the treatment of the princes, and thirty families were arranged to guard his tomb.
In the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the emperor took pity on King Huainan. He still had four sons, all seven or eight years old, so he named his sons Liu An the Marquis of Fuling, Liu Bo the Marquis of Anyang, Liu Ci the Marquis of Yangzhou, and Liu Liang the Marquis of Shucheng.
In the twelfth year, there was a folk song about the King of Huainan, saying: A foot of cloth can be sewed; a bushel of millet can be pounded.
The two brothers are incompatible!
After hearing this, the emperor said: In the past, Yao and Shun exiled their own flesh and blood, and Zhou Gong killed Guan Shu and Cai Shu. The whole world called them saints, and they would not harm the national interests for selfish reasons.
How can people in the world think that I am coveting the land of King Huainan?
So King Chengyang was moved to the old land of Huainan to become king, and King Mi of Huainan was named King Li, and his cemetery was set up according to the etiquette of the princes.
In the 16th year, the emperor took pity on King Huainan because he abolished Han law without authorization and behaved indulgently, which caused him to lose his feudal status and died at an early age. Therefore, he moved King Liu Xi of Huainan back to Chengyang as king, and established King Li's three sons as kings in his hometown of Huainan. They are: Fuling Hou Liu An as the King of Huainan, Anyang Hou Liu Bo as the King of Hengshan, and Yangzhou Hou Liu Ci as the King of Lujiang. Liu Liang, the Marquis of Shucheng, died young and had no descendants.
In the third year of Xiaojing's reign, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled. Wu's envoys went to the King of Huainan, who wanted to send troops to meet the King of Wu.
His prime minister said: If your Majesty must raise an army with King Wu, I would like to be a general.
The king of Huainan then handed over the army to the prime minister.
After the prime minister had led the army, he held fast to the city and refused to obey the king's orders and went to the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty also sent the Marquis of Qucheng to lead troops to rescue the Huainan Kingdom, so the Huainan Kingdom was preserved.
The envoy of the King of Wu went to Lujiang, but the King of Lujiang did not respond, so the envoy came to Yue again; when they arrived at Hengshan, the King of Hengshan stood firm and had no intention of rebelling against the Han.
In the fourth year of Xiaojing's reign, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were wiped out. King Hengshan came to see the emperor. The emperor thought he was loyal and trustworthy, and comforted him by saying: The south is low and humid.
So the king of Hengshan moved to Jibei and became king to praise him.
When he died, he was given the title Zhen Wang.
The King of Lujiang was located on the border with Yue. He sent envoys to interact with Vietnam many times. Later, he was changed to the King of Hengshan and became king in the Jiangbei area.
Liu An, the king of Huainan, likes reading and playing the piano, but does not like hunting or riding horses. He plans to rely on his kindness to appease the people and leave a good reputation.
He gathered thousands of guests and travelers from all over the world to compile twenty-one "Inner Books", more "Outer Books", and eight volumes of "Middle Chapters". The book discussing the techniques of immortal alchemy also has more than 200,000 words.
At that time, Emperor Wu also loved literature. As uncles, Liu An and others were eloquent and good at diction, so the emperor respected him very much.
Every time he wrote a letter or received a reward, the emperor often ordered Sima Xiangru and others to read the draft first and then copy it and send it.
At first, when Liu An entered the court, he presented his "Neipian" to the emperor. Because the book was a new work, the emperor kept it secretly.
Let him write "Li Sao Zhuan", receive the edict in the morning, and submit it to the emperor during lunch.
He also presented "Ode" and "Ode to the Capital of Chang'an" to the emperor.
Every time we have a banquet to meet the emperor, we talk about ancient and modern gains and losses, folk skills, and poems, and they don't stop until the evening.
Liu Ang just entered the court and was very friendly to the Taiwei Wu'anhou. When Wu'anhou greeted him, he said to him: Now the emperor has no prince. The king is the grandson of Emperor Gao. He is benevolent and righteous, and everyone in the world knows it.
Once the emperor dies, who else can he stand but you?
The King of Huainan was very happy, so he gave Marquis Wuan jewelry and other items.
Most of his ministers and guests were frivolous and mean people from the Jianghuai area. They died because of King Li's migration, so they were extremely grateful to Liu An.
In the sixth year of Jianyuan, a comet appeared, and Wang Xinhuo of Huainan felt strange.
Someone said to the King of Huainan: Earlier when the King of Wu sent troops, a comet appeared that was several feet long, so he launched a campaign and blood flowed thousands of miles.
Now comets are so long that they can reach the sky, and a great war is about to happen in the world.
The King of Huainan thought that the emperor had no crown prince, and if there was chaos in the world, the princes would fight for it, so he wanted to increase the army's equipment and accumulate money to bribe other counties. The tourists flattered the King of Huainan with nonsense words, which made him happy, so he gave them many rewards.
The King of Huainan has a daughter named Liu Ling, who is intelligent and eloquent.
The King of Huainan loved Liu Ling very much and gave her a lot of money to secretly spy in Chang'an and get to know the emperor's ministers.
In the second year of Yuanshuo, the emperor gave King Huainan several cases and a walking stick, so that he did not have to worship the emperor.
Queen Tu was favored and gave birth to a son Liu Qian, who was established as the crown prince and married the daughter of the Queen Mother's grandson Xiu Chengjun as the crown princess.
The King of Huainan conspired to rebel. He was afraid that the Crown Princess would know the inside story and leak the rebellion, so he planned with the Crown Prince and asked him to pretend that he didn't love her and not eat at the same table for three months.
King Huainan pretended to be angry with the prince and locked him up with the princess, but the prince still did not get close to the princess.
The princess asked to leave, so King Huainan wrote a letter to apologize to the emperor and asked to let her go back.
Queen Tu, Prince Liu Qian and daughter Liu Ling took over the power in the country, seized people's fields and houses, and arrested people at will.
The prince was learning to dance the sword, and he thought that no one could surpass him. He heard that the doctor Lei was good at sword dancing, so he summoned him to compete with him. Lei Ben gave in repeatedly, and then accidentally hit the prince. The prince was furious, and Lei Ben was frightened.
At this time, it happened that someone who was willing to join the army came to Chang'an, and Lei was immediately asked to attack the Huns.
The prince slandered Lei Quan many times, and the king of Huainan sent a doctor to order him not to go, so that future generations would not dare to imitate him.
In the fifth year of Yuanshuo, Lei was fled to Chang'an and wrote a letter to the emperor explaining the matter.
The matter was investigated and handled by Tingwei and Henan County.
Henan ordered to arrest the prince of Huainan King. The king and queen of Huainan decided not to send the prince to Henan, so they rebelled.
The plan has not been made yet and I have been hesitating for more than ten days.
At this time, the emperor issued an order to interrogate the prince in Huainan. The Huainan King's prime minister, Shouchun Cheng, complied with the Huainan King's intention and only arrested the prince instead of sending him away. He was angry and impeached Shouchun Cheng for disrespecting the emperor.
The King of Huainan asked the Prime Minister for help, but the Prime Minister refused to listen.
The King of Huainan sent a letter to the emperor to inform the prime minister, and the matter was investigated and handled by Tingwei.
During the review, the matter involved King Huainan, who sent people to the capital to inquire closely about the matter.
The princes of Mo asked the emperor to arrest and punish King Huainan. King Huainan was frightened and wanted to send troops to rebel.
Prince Liu Qian planned and said: The Han sent envoys to arrest the king. We can have people put on the clothes of guards and stand beside you with weapons. If they find bad guys, we will assassinate them. I also sent people to assassinate Lieutenant Huainan. It is not too late to send troops again.
At this time, the emperor did not agree to the request of the minister, and sent Lieutenant Hong of the Han Dynasty to interrogate King Huainan on the spot. Seeing that the interrogator's face was gentle, King Huainan only asked about the reprimand and the lei. He guessed that there was no danger, so he did not send troops.
After the lieutenant returned, he reported to the emperor.
The ministers said: Liu An, the king of Huainan, stopped Lei Fei who asked to attack the Xiongnu and delayed the imperial edict. He should be beheaded.
The emperor issued an edict not to allow it.
The ministers also requested that the King of Huainan be deposed, but the emperor did not agree.
The emperor requested to reduce the five counties of the feudal state, and the emperor agreed to reduce the number of two counties.
Lieutenant Hong was sent to pardon his crime and punish him by reducing his fiefdom.
The lieutenant entered the territory of Huainan and announced that the emperor would pardon the king of Huainan.
At first, he heard that the minister requested to kill him, but he didn't know that he would only reduce the fiefdom. So when he heard the Han envoys coming, he was afraid that they were coming to arrest him, so he and the prince planned to act according to the previous rebellion plan.
Lieutenant, he congratulated the King of Huainan, and the King of Huainan did not send troops because of this.
Later he said sadly: I practice benevolence and righteousness but my fiefdom has been reduced. I feel very shameful.
The desire to create is even stronger.
The envoys came from Chang'an and talked frivolously, saying that the emperor had no son, and he was very happy. He got angry when he said that the court was being governed and that the emperor had a son, and he thought it was nonsense and untrue.
The King of Huainan and Zuo Wu and others deployed the army's offensive route day and night according to the terrain map.
The King of Huainan said: The emperor has no prince. Once the emperor dies, the ministers will definitely summon King Jiaojian or King Changshan. The princes will compete for it. How can I not be prepared!
Moreover, I am the grandson of Emperor Gao, and I practice benevolence and righteousness. I can tolerate His Majesty's kindness to me. After the Emperor's death, how can I go north and become a minister?
King Huainan had a concubine named Buhai, who was the oldest. King Huainan did not like him, the queen did not regard him as her son, and the prince did not regard him as his brother. Buhai's son, named Jian, was talented and ambitious, and he often complained that the prince did not visit his father.
At that time, all the princes were allowed to ennoble their own children as marquises. King Huainan had two sons, one of whom was established as the prince, but Liu Jian's father was not allowed to be established as a marquis.
So Liu Jian secretly made some friends and wanted to murder the prince and let his father be the prince instead.
When the prince found out, he arrested and whipped Liu Jian many times.
Liu Jian knew about the prince's plot to kill Lieutenant Mo, so he sent his friend Shouchun to write a solemn letter to the emperor, saying: Good medicine is bitter and good for the disease, and loyal advice is hard on the ears and good for action.
Nowadays, Liu Jian, the grandson of King Huainan, is very talented, so Liu Qian, the son of King Huainan and Queen Tu and Tu, often frame him.
Liu Jian's father was imprisoned many times despite being innocent. They wanted to kill him.
Now that Liu Jianren is here, His Majesty can interrogate him personally, and he will know the plot of King Huainan.
After receiving the memorial, the emperor handed over the matter to Tingwei and Henan Order.
This happened in the sixth year of Yuanshuo.
Shen Qing, the grandson of the late Piyang Marquis, was close to the Prime Minister Gongsun Hong. He hated Huainan King Li for killing his grandfather, so he secretly requested that the Huainan King's case be handed over to Gongsun Hong.
Gongsun Hong suspected that the King of Huainan had a conspiracy, so he pursued the case in depth.
After the Henan Order interrogated Liu Jian, Liu Jian confessed to the prince and his accomplices.
At first, the King of Huainan discussed raising troops with Wu Bei. Wu Bei often advised him to take the chaos of Wu and Chu as a warning.
The king of Huainan cited the cases of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang who successfully raised troops to refute. Wu was replied that the situation was different, and that raising troops now would inevitably fail.
When Liu Jian was questioned, King Huainan was afraid that the conspiracy would be exposed, so he thought of going to war and asked Wu Qui for his opinion. Wu Bei was said to be able to send troops, but it depended on the situation. This was recorded in "The Biography of Wu Bei".
So the King of Huainan was ready to go, and ordered his official slaves to go to the palace to carve the emperor's jade seal, as well as the prime minister, imperial censors, generals, officials, two thousand stones, the official order of the capital, the seal of the chief minister, and the seal of the prefect of the neighboring county, and the seal of the captain, and also made official hats for the envoys of the Han Dynasty.
According to Wu Bei's plan, King Huainan planned to send someone to pretend to be afraid of crime and flee to Chang'an to serve the general and the prime minister. Once the army was launched, he would first assassinate the general Wei Qing and then persuade the prime minister Gongsun Hong, which would be easy.
The King of Huainan plans to mobilize the soldiers in the country. Is he afraid of the Prime Minister? Er Qian Shi refused to listen, so he conspired with Wu Bei to set fire to the palace and pretend there was a fire. When the prime minister and Er Qian Shi went to put out the fire, they killed them.
The King of Huainan also planned to send people to pretend to be arresters, rush from the south with urgent military documents, shout that South Vietnam has sent troops to attack, and then take advantage of the situation to raise troops.
So he sent people to Lujiang and Kuaiji to serve as arresters, but the final decision was not made.
Wei Ting reported the matter of Liu Jiangong and Prince Liu Qian, and the emperor sent Wei Jian Ting and Lieutenant Huainan to arrest the prince.
When they arrived in Huainan, the king of Huainan heard about it and conspired with the prince. He summoned the prime minister and two thousand stones to kill them and then raised an army.
The prime minister was summoned. The prime minister came, but the internal history declined the future.
The lieutenant said: I have a mission from the emperor. I cannot come to see the king.
The king of Huainan thought that it would be meaningless to just kill the prime minister and leave the history and lieutenant in the future, so he ordered the prime minister to go back.
When he was hesitating, the prince thought that the crime they committed was just the murder of a Han Dynasty lieutenant, and all those involved in the murder were dead and there were no witnesses, so he said to the King of Huainan: All the useful officials among the officials have been arrested, and now there is no one who can help in the rebellion.
If your Majesty raises troops at an inappropriate time, I'm afraid it won't be successful. It's better to let them arrest me.
The King of Huainan became less and less willing to take action, so he agreed to the prince's request.
The prince committed suicide but did not die.
Wu Ban went to surrender and confessed to the rebellion against the King of Huainan.
The officials of the Han Dynasty arrested the prince and the queen, surrounded the palace, took away all the guests of King Huainan, copied the utensils used in the rebellion, and reported them to the emperor.
The emperor sent his ministers to investigate and investigate. Thousands of princes, erganshi, and heroes were implicated in King Huainan's rebellion. They were all punished according to the severity of their crimes.
Hengshan Wang Xingmeng, the younger brother of Huainan Wang Xingxuan, should be arrested.
Someone asked for the arrest of the King of Hengshan, and the emperor said: "The princes each have their own enfeoffments and govern the country, and they should not be implicated."
Please discuss and discuss with the princes, kings and princes.
Forty-three people including Diesi Qiandan and Liehou Rang all said: Liu An, the king of Jinnan, is treasonous and treasonous. The evidence of rebellion is conclusive and he should be questioned and executed.
Liu Duan, King of Jiaoxi, said: Liu An is lawless, does not follow the right path, has ulterior motives, and is ready to disrupt the world, confuse the people, betray his ancestors, and confuse the public with his evil words. "Spring and Autumn" says: If the minister does not use the general, he will be executed.
Liu An's crime did not just sprout, his rebellion was already a fact.
In my opinion, after identifying the tools of his rebellion, he can be punished.
Officials of the Huainan Kingdom with a salary of more than 200 shi and those with a salary equivalent to this, as well as favorites of the royal family, who have not rebelled but failed to assist the King of Huainan should be dismissed from their posts, and their titles can be reduced to civilians, and they will not be allowed to serve as officials again.
The other people who were not officials each paid two catties and eighty taels of gold to atone for their death penalty, so that Liu An's crimes could be publicized, so that everyone in the world would understand the way of being a minister and would not dare to have bad intentions and rebel against the court.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Tingweitang and others reported their opinions to the kings, and the emperor sent Zongzheng to punish Liu An.
Before Zong Zheng arrived, Liu An committed suicide.
The queen, prince and other people involved in the rebellion were all executed.
Huainan Kingdom was abolished and changed to Jiujiang County.
Queen Chengshu of Hengshan King Liu Ci gave birth to three children: the eldest son Liu Shuang was the prince, the second daughter Liu Wucai, and the youngest son Liu Xiao.
The beloved concubine Xu Lai gave birth to four children, and the beautiful concubine Jue Ji gave birth to two children.
The king of Huainan and the king of Hengshan blamed each other and complained, and there were constant conflicts.
The King of Hengshan heard that the King of Huainan was preparing to use the utensils for rebellion, and secretly recruited talents to deal with them to prevent them from being annexed by him. In the sixth year of Yuanguang, King Hengshan went to the capital to pay homage. The visitor, Wei Qing, knew magic and wanted to write a letter to serve the emperor. The King of Hengshan became angry and impeached Wei Qing for committing a capital crime. He tortured Wei Qing to extract a confession and made him admit to the capital crime.
The internal historian believed that the case was untrue and withdrew.
King Hengshan sent a letter to the internal historian. When the internal historian was interrogated, he pointed out that King Hengshan was not upright and had repeatedly invaded other people's fields and used other people's cemeteries as fields.
Some officials requested that King Hengshan be arrested and punished, but the emperor did not allow it. He only deprived King Hengshan of the right to appoint officials with a salary of more than 200 shi.
The King of Hengshan was very dissatisfied and conspired with Xi Ci and Zhang Guangchang to find people who could use military astrology to plot rebellion day and night.
After Queen Chengshu died, King Hengshan made Xu Lai his queen, and Jue Ji was also favored.
Xu Lai and Jue Ji were jealous of each other. Jue Ji slandered Xu Lai in front of the prince: Xu Lai sent his slaves to kill the prince's mother using witchcraft.
The prince resented Xu Lai.
Xu Lai's brother came to Hengshan. The prince drank with him and stabbed him with a knife.
The queen hated the prince because of this and slandered the prince in front of King Hengshan.
After the prince's sister Wucai got married, her husband divorced her and she committed adultery with a guest.
The prince scolded her many times, and she was unhappy and stopped interacting with the prince.
After the queen heard about it, she won over Wucai and Liu Xiao.
Liu Xiao lost his mother when he was young and grew up with the queen. The queen doted on him because of her plans. Liu Xiao and the queen went to King Hengshan to slander the prince, and King Hengshan whipped the prince many times.
During the fourth year of Yuanshuo, someone injured the queen's stepmother. King Hengshan suspected that the prince had sent someone to do it, so he whipped him.
Later, when the King of Hengshan fell ill, the prince said that he was also ill and refused to attend to him.
Liu Xiao and Liu Wucai slandered the prince together and said: He is actually not sick. He said this himself, and he was very happy when he said it. King Hengshan was furious and wanted to depose the crown prince and install his younger brother Liu Xiao.
After the queen learned that King Hengshan was determined to depose the crown prince, she wanted him to depose Liu Xiao together.
The queen had a waiter who was good at dancing, and the King of Hengshan favored her. The queen wanted to send the waiter to have an affair with Liu Xiao, and after making Liu Xiao responsible for the crime, she also deposed the two brothers so that her son Liu Guang could replace them.
After the prince found out, he hated the queen for harming him many times and there was no end to it, so he also wanted to silence her with the crime of fornication.
The queen invited the prince to drink. When the prince came to celebrate her birthday, he hugged her thigh and asked to sleep with her.
The queen was furious and told the king of Hengshan.
The King of Hengshan summoned the prince and wanted to tie him up and whip him.
The prince knew that the king often wanted to depose him and make Liu Xiao the prince, so he told the king of Hengshan: Liu Xiao has committed adultery with the king's attendants, and Wucai has committed adultery with his slaves. Your king, please pay attention to your diet. I am going to sue the emperor.
Then he turned around and left. King Hengshan sent people to stop him, but they couldn't stop him, so he chased after him and caught him.
The prince talked nonsense, so King Hengshan locked him up in the palace.
Liu Xiao became more and more popular with King Hengshan.
The King of Hengshan valued his talent, so he put the royal seal on him, made him a general, let him live in his grandfather's house, and gave him a lot of money to recruit talents.
Some of the guests who came to defected knew a little bit about the rebellion of King Huainan and King Hengshan, so they took advantage of the opportunity to persuade them.
The King of Hengshan then sent Liu Xiao's guests Mei He and Chen happy from Jiangdu to battle chariots with bows and arrows, and to engrave the emperor's jade seal and the seals of the generals, prime ministers, and military officers.
King Ye of Hengshan recruited strong men like Zhou Qiu and others, and talked many times about the strategies used by Wu and Chu when they rebelled.
The King of Hengshan did not dare to ascend the throne like the King of Huainan, but he was afraid that the King of Huainan would raise an army and annex his kingdom. He thought that after the King of Huainan sent troops to march westward, he might send troops to occupy the Jianghuai area, and he only hoped for this.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuanshuo, King Hengshan should go to Beijing to pay homage. In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, King Hengshan passed by Huainan.
The King of Huainan recalled the deep love between brothers, and the two sides abandoned their differences and agreed to rebel together.
The King of Hengshan immediately wrote a letter saying that he was ill, and the emperor agreed that he would not come to worship.
The King of Hengshan also sent a letter asking for the deposing of Prince Liu Shuang and the appointment of Liu Xiao as Tai Guang.
After Liu Shuang heard about it, he immediately sent his friend Bai Ying to Chang'an to write a letter, saying that King Hengshan and his son were planning to rebel, that Liu Xiao had made military chariots, bows and arrows, and that Liu Xiao had committed adultery with King Hengshan's attendant.
Bai Ying was arrested before he could file a petition in Chang'an because he was suspected of the Huainan King case.
After King Heng heard about it, he was afraid that he would reveal his secret, so he wrote to the prince and accused him of treason.
The case was handed over to Pei County for trial.
In the winter of the first year of Yuanshou, Yousi requested the arrest of people related to the rebellion of King Huainan, and Chen happy was captured at Liu Xiao's house.
Officials impeached Liu Xiao for harboring Chen happy.
Liu Xiao believed that Chen happy had discussed the rebellion with the King of Hengshan many times in the past and was afraid that he would expose him. He heard that the law stipulated that the person who surrendered first could be exempted from punishment. He also suspected that the prince sent Bai Ying to write a letter to expose his affairs, so he surrendered first and confessed Mei He, Chen Xi and others who participated in the rebellion.
After interrogation, Tingwei found that the evidence was conclusive, so he demanded that King Hengshan be arrested and punished.
The emperor Bu said: Don’t catch me.
Lieutenants An and Da Xingxi were sent to interrogate King Hengshan, and King Hengshan confessed truthfully.
The officials surrounded the palace and stood guard there.
Lieutenant and Daxing returned to Beijing to report to Emperor Ming.
The minister requested that Zongzheng and Daxing be sent together with the governor of Pei County to investigate the King of Hengshan.
When the King of Hengshan heard about it, he committed suicide.
Liu Xiao was exempted from the crime of rebellion because he surrendered for rebellion.
Liu Xiao committed adultery with the maid of the King of Hengshan, Queen Xu Lai killed the former Queen Chengshu, and Prince Liu Shuang was beheaded in public for accusing his father of being unfilial.
Others who conspired with King Hengshan were executed.
The kingdom was deposed into counties.
Liu Bo, the Zhenwang of Jibei, moved in the fourth year of Emperor Jingdi's reign.
Two years after the migration, plus his previous time as King of Hengshan, he died after reigning for fourteen years.
His son Liu Hu, king of Shi, succeeded to the throne and died fifty-four years later.
Liu Hu's son Liu Kuan succeeded to the throne.
When Liu Kuan reigned for 12 years. Because he committed adultery with his father's wife, Queen Guang, and his concubine Xiaoer, which was contrary to human ethics, and he cursed the emperor during the sacrifice, some officials demanded that he be put to death.
The emperor sent Dahong Li to summon Liu Kuan to the capital, but Liu Kuan killed himself with a knife.
The kingdom was abolished as Bei'an County and belonged to Taishan County.
Zan said: "Poetry" says: Ao Da is cheating, Jing Shu is punishment. This statement is absolutely true!
King Jinzhi and King Hengshan were both flesh and blood of the emperor, with a vast territory of thousands of miles, and were classified as vassals. However, they did not abide by the ways of vassals and assist the emperor. Instead, they had ulterior motives and deliberately rebelled. Both father and son perished, and their tribe did not have a good death.
This is not only because of their poor quality as kings, but also because of the vulgar ethos of their kingdom and their ministers drifting with the crowd, which leads to this kind of drama.
People in Jingchu have always liked to offend their superiors and cause trouble. This has been recorded since ancient times.
summary:
King Li of Huainan, the youngest son of Emperor Gao of Han, was born to a former beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao. His mother became pregnant after being favored by Emperor Gao during a visit to Zhao. When King Zhao was implicated in a rebellion, she was imprisoned and revealed her pregnancy, but Emperor Gao ignored her pleas. After giving birth to King Li, she committed suicide out of resentment. Emperor Gao regretted this and had Empress Lu raise the child. In the eleventh year of his reign, Emperor Gao made Liu Chang the King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion.

King Li grew up relying on Empress Lu and was favored during the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, but he resented Marquis Piyang for not saving his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, King Li became arrogant and broke laws repeatedly. In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes: failing to save his mother, not preventing Empress Lu's murder of King Zhao Ruyi, and not stopping Empress Lu from ennobling the Lu family. Emperor Wen pardoned him out of pity, but King Li grew more defiant, making his own laws and acting like an emperor.

Emperor Wen's uncle Bo Zhao admonished King Li in a letter, listing eight dangerous behaviors: abandoning his state, disobeying orders, prioritizing his mother's grave over his father's, and more. He warned that disaster would follow if King Li did not reform. King Li was displeased and ignored the advice. In the sixth year, he conspired with seventy men, including Chai Qi, to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and King Li was summoned to Chang'an. After interrogation, officials reported his crimes: abandoning Han laws, appointing officials without authorization, harboring fugitives, and planning rebellion. They demanded his execution, but Emperor Wen commuted the sentence to exile in Shu County.

King Li refused food and died on the way. Emperor Wen mourned and executed the officials who failed to provide food. He later enfeoffed King Li's four sons as marquises. In the sixteenth year, he made three of them kings in Huainan. During the Rebellion of the Seven States, King Huainan Liu An initially considered joining Wu but was restrained by his prime minister. Liu An, known for his literary pursuits, compiled the "Inner Books" and other works. He plotted rebellion after a comet appeared, believing the emperor had no heir. His daughter Liu Ling spied in Chang'an. The plot was exposed when his grandson Liu Jian informed on him. King Huainan committed suicide, and his kingdom was abolished as Jiujiang County.

King Hengshan Liu Ci, brother of King Huainan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his son, Prince Liu Shuang, and favored his younger son Liu Xiao. After Queen Chengshu died, Queen Xu Lai and concubine Jue Ji slandered the prince. The prince was whipped and later accused his father of rebellion. King Hengshan committed suicide when investigated. His kingdom was also abolished. The historian comments that both kings, despite being imperial relatives, perished due to their rebellious nature and the corrupting influence of their ministers, noting that people of Jingchu have historically been prone to insurrection.
