translation:
Wang Mang, also known as Jujun, is the nephew of Queen Xiaoyuan.
Empress Yuan's father and brothers all became marquises during the reigns of Emperor Yuan and Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, held important positions, and assisted in government affairs. There were nine people in the family who were granted the title of marquis and five chief ministers. These words are recorded in the "Biography of the Empress of the Yuan Dynasty".
Only Wang Mang's father, Wang Man, died earlier and was not granted a title.
Wang Mang's uncles and brothers were all the sons of generals and marquises. They took advantage of the time when their fathers were powerful and lived a luxurious and lavish life. They showed off and compared each other with tall carriages and horses, talented singers and concubines, beautiful concubines, and novel games. Wang Mang was the only one who was lonely and poor, so he treated others with humility and lived a simple life.
He worshiped Chen Shen, a native of Pei County, as his teacher, studied "Etiquette" and "Zhou Rites", worked diligently and extensively, and dressed like an ordinary scholar.
He served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, raised his fatherless nephew, and behaved with great caution.
In addition, he made friends with outstanding talents outside and served his uncles and uncles in the family with tact, thoughtfulness and courtesy.
During the Yangshuo period, his uncle, the general Wang Feng, fell ill. Wang Mang served him and took the medicine himself. He did not comb his hair or wash his face, resulting in unkempt appearance. He went to bed without taking off his clothes for several months.
When Wang Feng was dying, she entrusted Wang Mang to the Queen Mother and Emperor Cheng. He was appointed Huang Menlang and was later promoted to Shesheng Xiaowei.
After a long time, his uncle Chengdu Marquis Wang Shang wrote to the emperor, expressing his willingness to allocate his own households to Wang Mang. Others, such as Changle Shaofu Dai Chong, Shi Zhong Jin She, Hu Qi Xiao Lieutenant Ji Hong, Shanggu Du Wei Yang Bing and Zhonglang Chen Tang, were all very famous people at the time. They all spoke for Wang Mang. From then on, the emperor considered Wang Mang to be a wise man.
In the first year of Yongshi, Emperor Cheng granted Wang Mang the title of Marquis of Xindu. The Marquis was built in the capital of Xinye County, Nanyang County, with 1,500 households.
Later he was promoted to the rank of Cavalry Captain and Guanglu Doctor, and he served as a guard in the palace. He was cautious and considerate. As his official position became higher and higher, his attitude became more and more humble.
He distributed carriages, horses, and light warm clothing, and gave alms to the guests, so that there was no extra clothing in the house.
He accepted and supported famous people and made friends with many generals, prime ministers, and officials.
Therefore, people in important positions recommended him more, and celebrities in the society advocated for him. His reputation spread throughout the government and the public, surpassing his uncles.
He dares to behave in a pretentious manner without feeling ashamed.
Wang Mang's brother Wang Yong, who had served in various Cao Cao positions, had died long ago. He had a son named Wang Guang, and Wang Mang asked him to study under a doctor.
When Wang Mang was on vacation, he drove his chariot and horses, brought sheep and wine, and went to comfort his teacher. He even gave gifts to his classmates.
It attracted many scholars to watch and the old people admired it.
Wang Guang was younger than Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, so Wang Mang asked them to get married on the same day. The hall was filled with congratulatory guests.
After a while, one person said that his mother had some kind of illness and what medicine she should take. By the time the guests left, he had already gotten up several times.
He once secretly bought a maidservant, and word gradually spread among his brothers. Wang Mang said: "The later general Zhu Ziyuan has no sons. I heard that this woman can have many sons, so I bought her for him."
The maidservant was given to Zhu Ziyuan that day.
Wang Mang went to such an extent to hide his true feelings and pursue fame.
At this time, Chun Yuchang, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, was ranked among the nine ministers because of his talents. He was an official before Wang Mang and his reputation and status were above Wang Mang.
Wang Mang secretly collected his crimes, and reported his situation to Emperor Cheng through the Grand Sima Quyanghou Wanggen. Chunyu Chang was killed by the law, and Wang Mang gained a reputation for loyalty and integrity. These words are recorded in the "Chun Yu Chang Biography".
Wang Gen therefore requested to retire and recommended Wang Mang to replace him. The emperor then promoted Wang Mang to be the Grand Sima.
This year is the first year of Suihe, and Wang Mang is thirty-eight years old.
Since Wang Mang had surpassed his peers and assisted the emperor after his four uncles, he planned to make his reputation better than that of his predecessors, so he set strict demands on himself and worked tirelessly. He hired many virtuous people to serve as subordinate officials, and all the rewards from the emperor and the income from fiefdoms were used to entertain the scholars. He himself became more frugal and frugal.
His mother was ill, and the princes, ministers and princes sent their wives to inquire about her condition. Wang Mang's wife went out to greet her, but she did not have a floor-length gown, and her sarong only reached her knees.
Those who saw her thought she was a slave, but when they asked, they found out that she was Wang Mang's wife, and they were all surprised.
Wang Mang assisted the government for more than a year. Emperor Mo Cheng died and Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne. He honored the Empress Dowager as the Empress Dowager.
The Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to resign and go home, giving up power to Emperor Ai's maternal family.
Wang Mang then submitted a memorial and asked to resign. Emperor Ai sent his minister Shao to order Wang Mang to say: The late emperor entrusted the government to you and abandoned his subordinates. I can take over the country and I really hope to be of the same mind as you.
Now that you have written a letter saying that you are ill and requesting resignation, it seems that I cannot obey the late emperor's will. I am very sad about this.
The minister has been ordered to wait for you to come to court to report.
He also sent Prime Minister Kong Guang, Grand Sikong Hewu, General Zuo Shidan, and Weiwei Fu happy to report to the Queen Mother: The emperor was very sad when he heard the Queen Mother's edict.
If Da Sima did not become an official, the emperor would not dare to handle government affairs.
The Queen Mother also appointed Wang Mang as director.
At this time, Emperor Ai's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Dingtao, and her mother, Liao Ji, were still alive. Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, wrote a letter saying: According to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", mothers are more valuable than their children, so Ding Ji should be given the honorific title.
Wang Mang and Shi Dan jointly impeached and exposed Dong Hong for misleading the court and violating principles. These words were recorded in "The Biography of Shi Dan".
Later, a banquet was held in Weiyang Palace, and the insider ordered a curtain to be set up for Empress Dowager Fu to sit next to the Empress Dowager.
When Wang Mang saw her during his inspection, he scolded his concubine and said: "The Empress Dowager of Dingtao is the empress dowager of the vassal king and the concubine of Emperor Yuan. How can she be ranked with the most noble person!"
The curtains were removed and seats were installed. When Empress Dowager Fu heard about this, she was very angry and refused to attend the banquet. She was extremely resentful of Wang Mang.
Wang Mang asked to resign again, and Emperor Ai rewarded Wang Mang with five hundred catties of gold, a chariot and four horses, and he was relieved of his duties and returned to his palace.
Many princes, ministers and officials praised him, and the emperor gave him preferential treatment and love. He arranged for special envoys to serve him at home, and asked the eunuchs in the palace to reward him with food and drink every ten days.
Xia Shaoshu said: Wang Mang, the lord of Xindu, worries about the country and always acts according to the rules. I can almost achieve peace with him.
The Empress Dowager Shao ordered Wang Mang to return to his residence. I regret this very much.
The three hundred and fifty households that Huang You gathered should be sealed to Wang Mang, and he should be given the official title of "Special Advancement". Whenever he attends court meetings on the first and fifteenth day of the lunar month, the emperor will receive him with the same etiquette as when he receives the three princes. When the emperor travels, he will follow him in a green car.
Two years later, Empress Dowager Fu and Ding Ji both had honorable titles. Prime Minister Zhu Bo wrote a letter saying: Wang Mang was unwilling to promote the principle of respecting elders and suppressed and lowered the honorable title of the Empress Dowager, which was detrimental to filial piety and should be punished. Fortunately, he was pardoned and should not have a title or land. Please remove me and demote me to civilian status.
The emperor said: Because Wang Mang is related to the Empress Dowager, he will not be exempted from his title and fief, and orders him to return to his country.
Wang Mang thanked guests behind closed doors and kept to himself. His second son Wang Huo killed his slave. Wang Mang severely blamed Wang Huo and asked him to commit suicide.
After staying in the feudal state for three years, hundreds of officials wrote to redress Wang Mang's grievances.
In the first year of Yuanshou, there was a solar eclipse. The virtuous Zhou Hu, Song Chong and others praised Wang Mang's meritorious deeds when answering the emperor's questions, so the emperor recalled Wang Mang.
When Wang Mang returned to the feudal state, the Nanyang Prefect, because of Wang Mang's high and important status, selected Kong Xiu, a native of Wan County, an official of the Prefect's Yamen, to temporarily serve as the Prime Minister of the new capital.
Kong Xiu went to see Wang Mang, and Wang Mang took the initiative to make friends with him through all manners. Kong Xiu also knew his reputation and interacted with him.
Later, when Wang Mang fell ill, Kong Xiu greeted him. Wang Mang repaid Kong Xiu's deep friendship and gave him his own sword inlaid with jade, intending to establish a friendly relationship with him.
Kong Xiu refused to accept it, so Wang Mang said, "I did see scars on your face. Beautiful jade can be used to remove the scars. I just want to give you this sword nose."
Then he took off the sword nose, but Kong Xiu refused again. Wang Mang said: Do you think its price is too high?
So he smashed the sword's nose with vertebrae, wrapped it up and gave it to Kong Xiu, and Kong Xiu accepted it.
When Wang Mang was summoned to the court and about to leave, he wanted to see Kong Xiu, but Kong Xiu excused himself from meeting because he was ill.
Wang Mang returned to the capital Chang'an for more than a year. Emperor Ai passed away without a son, and both Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Ding died before Emperor Ai. The Empress Dowager went to Weiyang Palace to collect the seal ribbon and sent an envoy on Pegasus to summon Wang Mang.
Order the minister, all the official documents of the imperial court to send troops, all civil and military officials to report the affairs of the court to the emperor, and the eunuchs in the inner palace and the emperor's personal soldiers are all under Wang Mang's command.
Wang Mang reported: "Da Sima Gao'an Hou Dong Xian is too young and does not meet everyone's wishes, so his seal will be confiscated."
Dong Xian committed suicide that day.
The Empress Dowager Shao ordered the princes and ministers to recommend people suitable to succeed Da Sima. Da Situ Kongguang and Da Sikong Pengxuan recommended Wang Mang, and former general He Wu and latter general Gongsun Lu recommended each other.
The Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima and discussed with him the selection of a successor to the throne.
Wang Shun, the Marquis of Anyang, was Wang Mang's cousin. He was cautious and trusted by the Queen Mother. Wang Mang proposed that Wang Shun be the chariot general and asked him to greet the King of Zhongshan to succeed him as emperor, creating Emperor Xiaoping.
When Emperor Ping was just nine years old, the Queen Mother came to the court to act as an agent in government affairs and entrusted the government affairs to Wang Mang.
Tu Mang pointed out that the Tang family had killed the prince in the past, and the Fu family was proud and arrogant, so he deposed Empress Xiaocheng Tang and Empress Xiaoai Fu and ordered them to commit suicide. These words are recorded in "The Biography of the Wife".
Because the great Situ Kong Guang was a famous Confucian scholar, Wang Mang had assisted three emperors, namely Cheng Emperor, Ai Emperor and Heping Emperor. He was respected by the Empress Dowager and trusted by the people of the country, so he treated Kong Guang with great respect and recommended Kong Guang's son-in-law Zhen Han to serve as a servant and captain of the car.
For all the relatives of Emperor Ai and the ministers in important positions whom he disliked, Wang Mang wrote a memorial asking for instructions and asked Zhen Han to bring them to Jie Guang.
Kong Guang has always been fearful and cautious, and he dared not fail to report the matter. Wang Mang reported to the Queen Mother again, and the Queen Mother agreed to these memorials.
So the former general He Wu and the latter general Gongsun Lu were dismissed from their posts because they recommended each other to be appointed as Grand Sima. The relatives of Ding, Fu and Dong Xian were all removed from their official positions and titles and were exiled to distant places.
Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, was the younger brother of the Queen Mother. Although he was not an official, Wang Mang respected him in his heart because he was his uncle. He was afraid that Wang Li would enlighten the Queen Mother when he was free so that he would not be able to do whatever he wanted. He also asked Kong Guang to report Wang Li's past crimes to the Queen Mother: Wang Li knew that Dingling Marquis Chunyu was a long-time criminal. After committing the crime of treason, he also accepted a large amount of bribes from him, interceded for him, and misled the court; later, he reported that the illegitimate son of the official slave Yang Ji was used as the prince. Everyone said that Empress Lu and the young emperor were resurrected. There were different opinions, making the world suspicious. This made it difficult to show future generations and complete the task of protecting the young master.
Please let Wang Li return to his feudal kingdom.
The Queen Mother did not follow his advice.
Wang Mang said: Now that the Han Dynasty is in decline and there are no heirs for several generations, it is really terrible for you, Queen Mother, to take charge of the government on your own instead of your young master. You try hard to set an example for the world with a fair attitude, but you may not obey me. If you don't listen to my opinion out of personal love, then the officials will have evil thoughts, and disaster will happen!
He should be sent back to the feudal country for the time being, and then transferred back after the country's affairs have stabilized a bit.
The Queen Mother had no choice but to let Wang Li return to his country.
These were all the methods Wang Mang used to coerce and blackmail the Queen Mother and her ministers.
In this way, those who relied on and obeyed him were promoted, and those who opposed and resented him were killed.
Wang Shun and Wang Yi became his confidants, Zhen Feng and Zhen Han were in charge of pickets, impeachments, and trials, Ping Yan was in charge of confidential military and political affairs, Liu Xin was in charge of rituals, music, and regulations, and Sun Jian became his right-hand assistant.
Zhen Feng's son Zhen Xun, Liu Xin's son Liu Cai, Cui Fa from Zhuojun, and Chen Chong from Nanyang were all favored by Wang Mang because of their talents.
Wang Mang looked stern and spoke seriously. If he wanted to do something, he only needed to give a slight hint with his expression and face, and the party members would clearly report his intention to the superiors. Wang Mang would kowtow and cry and resolutely refuse to give in. This was used to confuse the Queen Mother, and to show integrity to the common people.
At first, Wang Mang politely signaled to the Yizhou Order to let the barbarians outside the Great Wall donate white-feathered pheasants. In the first month of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Wang Mang reported to the Queen Mother and issued an edict to use white-feathered pheasants as offerings to the ancestral temple.
The ministers then reported to the Queen Mother: The Queen Mother appointed Grand Sima Wang Mang to make the decision to support the new emperor, thus bringing stability to the court.
The previous great Sima Huo Guang was credited with stabilizing the country and adding 30,000 households in the fiefdoms. It was also stipulated that after his death, his descendants would inherit the title and the number of fiefdoms would be equal to his, just like that of Xiao Xiangguo.
Wang Mang should be awarded the title according to Huo Guang's example.
The Queen Mother asked the princes and ministers: Is it really because Da Sima has made great contributions that he should be praised?
Or is he different because he is my closest relative?
So the ministers vigorously stated: Wang Mang's meritorious deeds brought about the same auspicious omen as the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng of Zhou in obtaining the white pheasant. They were separated by thousands of years, but the fortunes were the same.
The law of a sage emperor is that if a minister has made great achievements, he can get a good title during his lifetime, so the Duke of Zhou can use the title of Zhou as his title when he is still alive.
Wang Mang had great merits in stabilizing the country and stabilizing the Han Dynasty. He should be granted the title Anmo Gong, increase the number of households, and stipulate that after his death, his descendants would be granted the same title as him when they inherit the title. This is far in line with the example of Zhou Gong when Zhou became king, and more recent is like the precedent of Huo Guang. Wang Mang should be given equal rewards in order to comply with the will of God.
The Queen Mother ordered the minister to prepare for this matter.
Wang Mang wrote a letter saying: I, Kong Guang, Wang Shun, Zhen Feng, and Zhen Han have jointly agreed on the plan to establish a new emperor. Now I hope to only list the merits and rewards of Kong Guang and others, and leave aside Wang Mang, and do not compare with them.
Zhen Han reported to the Empress Dowager in her letter to Shao, saying: "There is no partiality or favouritism. The righteous path followed by the late king is broad and flat."
There should be no partiality towards people who are related to each other.
You have contributed to the peace and stability of the country, and you cannot withhold praise just because you are a close relative.
I hope you won't refuse.
Wang Mang wrote another resignation letter.
The Queen Mother ordered the visitor to guide Wang Mang to the side room of the main hall to wait, but Wang Mang refused to go to the hall because of illness.
The Queen Mother asked the minister to order Yao Xun to order him: "You are declining because the court wants to commend you for your merits and rewards. You have a heavy responsibility and have to go. You should go to the court as soon as possible to receive the title."
Wang Mang refused firmly.
The Queen Mother also asked Wang Hong, a servant of Changxin, to summon Wang Mang with the imperial edict, but Wang Mang still insisted on not going out because of his illness.
The ministers on the left and right reported to the Queen Mother not to go against Wang Mang's wishes, but only to list the merits and rewards of Kong Guang and others, so that Wang Mang would be willing to go to the court to govern.
The Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: Taifu Boshanhou Kongguang stayed and guarded the emperors of the four dynasties. He had served as Taifu and Prime Minister for several generations. He was loyal and filial, benevolent and righteous, and his behavior was in line with the standards. He was famous throughout the world. He proposed to make a decision to support the new emperor, increase the fiefdom by 10,000 households, and appointed Kong Guang as the Grand Master to participate in the decision-making of the four assistants.
The Chariot and Cavalry General Anyang Marquis Wang Shun had a long history of benevolence, righteousness, loyalty and filial piety. He was sent to welcome the King of Zhongshan and repel the enemy troops. He traveled thousands of miles and made outstanding achievements in morality. He added 10,000 households to the fiefdom and appointed Wang Shun as the Taibao.
The general of the left, Guang Luxun, Zhen Feng, served and guarded the emperors of three dynasties. He was loyal, honest, and benevolent. He sent him to welcome the King of Zhongshan, assist in persuading him, and stabilize the country. Zhen Feng was granted the title of Marquis of Guangyang, with a settlement of 5,000 households, and Zhen Feng was appointed as the young master.
All three were granted the position of fourth assistant, and their descendants could inherit their titles and fiefs in the same way, and each of them was rewarded with a mansion.
Zhen Han, the captain of the chariot captain, worked hard as a guard and worked hard. He proposed to support the new emperor and granted Zhen Han the title of Marquis of Chengyang, with a settlement of 2,000 and 400 households.
Four people had already received awards, and Wang Mang had not yet come to the court to manage the affairs of the country. The courtiers reported again: Although Wang Mang was self-denial and modest, the court should still commend him and increase the awards in a timely manner to show that the court valued the minister who made the most contribution and not to disappoint the civil and military officials and the common people.
The Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: Wang Mang, the lord of the new capital of Sima, served as the three princes of the three dynasties, inherited the responsibilities of Zhou Gong, and formulated strategies to ensure long-term peace and stability for future generations. His merits and virtues were admired by loyal ministers, and his teachings spread throughout the country. People in distant lands also admired his righteousness, so the Yue Shang family came to offer white pheasants.
Twenty-eight thousand households in Zhaoling and Xinxi counties should be granted to Wang Mang, exempting his descendants from taxes and corvee, stipulating that his descendants can inherit his title and fiefdom unchanged, and the rewards should be in accordance with Xiao Xiangguo's rules.
Wang Mang was appointed as Taifu, in charge of the affairs of the Fourth Assistant, and his title was Anhan Gong.
Take the former luxurious residence of Xiao Xiangguo as the residence of Duke Anhan, and put these into writing to spread them to infinity.
So Wang Mang looked frightened and had no choice but to go to court and accept the order.
The policy book reads: The Han Dynasty is in crisis and there is no successor to the throne. It is you who have stabilized the court; you have assumed the duties of the four assistants and the three public officials; you have controlled the civil and military officials: you have outstanding merits and deeds, and the country has been stabilized because of you. It seems that the auspicious sign of the white pheasant you invited is the scene of Duke Zhou assisting King Cheng of Zhou.
Therefore, I give you the beautiful title of An Mo Gong, assist the emperor, hope to bring peace to the world, and do not violate my will.
Wang Mang accepted the titles of Taifu and An Mogong, and resigned from the increased fiefdom and the rewards that stipulated hereditary titles and fiefdoms for his descendants. He said that he was willing to wait until the common people had enough food and clothing before accepting such rewards.
The ministers argued again, and the Queen Mother went down to Shao and said: Duke Anhan himself proposed that every family with the same surname should be self-sufficient for a period of time, so she listened to his opinion.
His salary, private staff, and rewards should be doubled.
When the people had enough food and clothing, Da Situ and Da Sikong reported it.
Wang Mang declined again and did not accept it, but suggested that the princes, their descendants, and the descendants of the heroes since Emperor Gaozu should be established as princes with great achievements, or given the title of marquis in Guan Nei and the fiefdom of collecting taxes. All the princes and ministers in office should be rewarded according to their grades.
On the one hand, they respected their ancestors and increased the etiquette and band size during ancestor worship; on the other hand, they extended favors to scholars, commoners, widowers and other helpless old people, and all policies of benevolence and good deeds were implemented.
These words are recorded in "Hu Di Ben Ji".
After Wang Mang won the favor of the public, he wanted to be dictatorial. Knowing that the Queen Mother disliked government affairs, he hinted to the princes and ministers to write a memorial saying: In the past, officials who were promoted to two thousand stones based on merit, and officials who were recommended by the state department as outstanding scholars, were mostly incompetent. They should all come to see Duke Anhan and accept the assessment.
Furthermore, it is not appropriate for the Queen Mother to personally interfere with trivial matters.
Let the Queen Mother issue an edict saying: The emperor is still young, and I will be in charge of the government for the time being until the emperor comes of age and is crowned.
Nowadays, many government affairs are complicated and trivial. I am old and unable to handle them mentally and physically. This is probably not the way to maintain my body and educate and train the emperor.
Therefore, we must choose loyal and capable people and establish four assistants to ensure that all officials are loyal to their duties and maintain the stability and peace of the country forever.
Confucius said: How great it is that when Yu Shun and Xia Yu governed the world, they appointed virtuous ministers to achieve their success without personally participating in their affairs!
From now on, only the matter of knighthood can be reported, and other matters will be evaluated and decided by Anhan Gong and Sifu.
When officials of the state shepherd, 2,000-stone rank, and scholar-born officials were required to report matters when they were first appointed to their posts, they were brought to the public office near the palace to report to Duke Anhan, inspect their original official duties, and inquire about their newly appointed positions to know whether they were qualified for the job.
So Wang Mang interviewed and questioned these officials one by one, tried his best to express his care and love, and gave many gifts. If he didn't like them, he would clearly petition to be removed from his official position. His power would soon be equal to that of the emperor.
Wang Mang planned to use false reputations to please the Queen Mother, and said in a memorial that after the Ding family and the Fu family were extravagant and wasteful during the reign of Emperor Xin Chengxiao, the people would not be able to keep warm and full. The Queen Mother should temporarily wear silk fabrics without patterns and slightly reduce the delicacies of mountains and seas to show the world.
Immediately afterwards, Wang Mang wrote another letter, willing to spend one million dollars and donate thirty hectares of land to Da Sinong to help the poor people.
So the princes and ministers all followed his example.
Wang Mang led the ministers to report: Your Majesty is old and has been wearing rough silk for a long time. Reducing dishes is indeed not a way to maintain physical and mental health, educate the emperor, and stabilize the country.
Wang Mang, the minister, went to the palace to kowtow to the provincial department many times and tried his best to report, but was not allowed.
Now relying on Your Majesty's kindness, the weather has been favorable recently, nectar has fallen from the sky, Ganoderma lucidum has appeared, and yellow pods, red grass, golden harvests and auspicious omens have arrived together.
The greatest wish of your Majesty, Wang Mang, and others is that your Majesty will conserve your energy, recuperate your mind, broaden your mind, reduce your thoughts, wear the royal clothes, and restore the emperor's usual meals prescribed by the eunuchs, so that your ministers can show their love to you and offer you the items of support.
I hope you will be compassionate and considerate!
Wang Mang also asked the Queen Mother to write a letter to Shao, saying: I heard that the Queen Mother's rule is that ideological activities should not exceed the boundaries of the palace.
The country has not been blessed by God, and the emperor is still young and cannot govern himself. I am frightened and cautious, fearing that the country will not be peaceful.
Without me, who would be in charge of the country's supreme power?
Therefore, Confucius met Nanzi and Duke Zhou took charge of the government, which was based on the needs of the situation at that time.
I have exhausted my body, exhausted my mind, worried and toiled, and have no peace of mind. Therefore, when the world advocates luxury, I use frugal style to show the world that correcting deviations often requires more than the limit. If I don't take the lead personally, what will the people of the world do?
I dream about a good harvest day and night, so that every household of the common people can have enough food and clothing. When the emperor comes of age, I will hand over the government to him.
Now I really don’t have time to enjoy soft clothes and delicious food. I hope to achieve something with the officials, so I should encourage you!
Whenever there was a flood or drought, Wang Mang would only eat vegetables and his attendants would report the situation to the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother sent an envoy to Wang Mang and said: I heard that you only eat vegetables. You are too worried about the suffering of the people.
Fortunately, the harvest this year is abundant. As you are so diligent and dedicated, you should eat some meat on time. Please take good care of your body for the sake of the country.

summary:
Wang Mang, also known as Jujun, was the nephew of Empress Xiaoyuan. During the reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Empress Yuan's father and brothers all became marquises, held important positions, and assisted in government affairs. Nine family members were granted the title of marquis, and five served as chief ministers. Only Wang Mang's father, Wang Man, died early and was not granted a title. Wang Mang's uncles and brothers, as sons of generals and marquises, lived luxurious lives, but Wang Mang, being lonely and poor, treated others with humility and lived simply. He studied "Etiquette" and "Zhou Rites" under Chen Shen, dressed like an ordinary scholar, served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, raised his fatherless nephew, and behaved with caution. He made friends with outstanding talents and served his uncles with tact and courtesy. During the Yangshuo period, his uncle Wang Feng fell ill, and Wang Mang served him diligently, not combing his hair or washing his face for months. When Wang Feng was dying, he entrusted Wang Mang to the Queen Mother and Emperor Cheng, leading to Wang Mang's appointment as Huang Menlang and later promotion to Shesheng Xiaowei.

Over time, his uncle Chengdu Marquis Wang Shang and other notable figures spoke highly of Wang Mang, leading Emperor Cheng to consider him a wise man. In the first year of Yongshi, Wang Mang was granted the title of Marquis of Xindu with 1,500 households. He was later promoted to Cavalry Captain and Guanglu Doctor, serving as a guard in the palace. As his official position rose, his attitude became more humble. He distributed his wealth to guests, leaving no extra clothing in his house, and supported famous people, making friends with many officials. His reputation spread throughout the government and public, surpassing his uncles. Wang Mang's brother Wang Yong had died, leaving a son named Wang Guang, whom Wang Mang had study under a doctor. During his vacations, Wang Mang visited his teacher with gifts and gave presents to classmates, attracting admiration from scholars and elders. Wang Guang married on the same day as Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, with a hall full of congratulatory guests. Wang Mang once secretly bought a maidservant, claiming he bought her for General Zhu Ziyuan because she could bear many sons, and gave her away that day, hiding his true feelings to pursue fame.

Wang Mang secretly collected crimes of Chun Yuchang, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, and reported him to Emperor Cheng through Grand Sima Wanggen. Chunyu Chang was executed, and Wang Mang gained a reputation for loyalty. Wang Gen then recommended Wang Mang to replace him, and Emperor Cheng promoted Wang Mang to Grand Sima at age thirty-eight. Wang Mang set strict demands on himself, hired virtuous people as subordinates, and used his rewards and fiefdom income to entertain scholars, living frugally. His wife, when greeting guests, wore a sarong that only reached her knees, surprising those who mistook her for a slave. After Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai succeeded, the Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to resign, but Emperor Ai refused his resignation and reappointed him. Wang Mang later clashed with Empress Dowager Fu, leading to his resignation again. He was rewarded with gold and chariots and returned to his palace. Many officials praised him, and the emperor treated him with favor, sending special envoys to serve him at home.

After three years in his feudal state, hundreds of officials petitioned for Wang Mang's recall. In the first year of Yuanshou, a solar eclipse occurred, and virtuous men praised Wang Mang's merits, leading the emperor to recall him. When Wang Mang returned to the capital, Emperor Ai died without a son, and the Queen Mother summoned Wang Mang to take control. Wang Mang reported that Da Sima Gao'an Hou Dong Xian was too young and not suitable, so his seal was confiscated, and Dong Xian committed suicide. The Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima, and they selected the King of Zhongshan to succeed as Emperor Xiaoping. When Emperor Ping was nine, the Queen Mother acted as regent and entrusted government affairs to Wang Mang. Wang Mang deposed Empress Xiaocheng Tang and Empress Xiaoai Fu, ordering them to commit suicide. He treated Grand Situ Kong Guang with respect and used him to report on officials he disliked, leading to their dismissal or exile. Wang Mang also forced his uncle Wang Li to return to his feudal country, using coercion and blackmail to control the Queen Mother and her ministers.

Wang Mang promoted those who obeyed him and killed those who opposed him. He used false humility to confuse the Queen Mother and the public. When the Yizhou Order offered white-feathered pheasants, Wang Mang reported it to the Queen Mother, and the ministers recommended he be granted the title of Anmo Gong with increased fiefdoms. Wang Mang refused multiple times, but the Queen Mother eventually granted him the title. He accepted the titles of Taifu and An Mogong but resigned from the increased fiefdom and hereditary rewards. He suggested rewarding other officials and implementing benevolent policies. After winning public favor, Wang Mang wanted to be dictatorial and hinted to officials to write memorials saying the Queen Mother should not interfere in trivial matters. The Queen Mother issued an edict allowing Wang Mang to evaluate and decide on official matters, giving him power equal to the emperor.

Wang Mang used false reputations to please the Queen Mother, donating money and land to help the poor. He led ministers in reporting auspicious omens and asked the Queen Mother to conserve her energy. During floods or droughts, Wang Mang only ate vegetables, and the Queen Mother urged him to eat meat for his health. Wang Mang sent envoys to the Xiongnu Chanyu, who changed his name to comply with Chinese customs. Wang Mang also gave his daughter to Emperor Ping as queen to consolidate his power, despite initial refusal. The ministers insisted, and Wang Mang's daughter became queen. Wang Mang declined increased betrothal gifts and distributed them to poor families. Chen Chong, a Grand Situ Sizhi, wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang's virtues and merits, comparing him to the Duke of Zhou and recommending he be granted the title of prime minister. The Queen Mother showed the memorial to the ministers, and they discussed it.

Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, fearing Emperor Ping's resentment, conspired with his teacher Wu Zhang and brother-in-law Lu Kuan to smear Wang Mang's mansion with blood to frighten him. Wang Mang arrested Wang Yu, who drank poison and died. Wang Mang killed Wang Yu's wife after she gave birth and used the incident to kill the Wei family and others, implicating many counties and feudal states. Hundreds of people died, shocking the world. Chen Zuo, the Grand Sima Hujun, praised Wang Mang for punishing his son like the Duke of Zhou. The ministers requested that Wang Mang's admonitions be distributed and treated like the "Book of Filial Piety." In the spring of the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, people worshiped heaven and offered sacrifices to Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Xiaowen. Wang Mang's daughter was made queen, and a general amnesty was announced. Eight officials were dispatched to inspect social customs. Taibao Wang Shun and others reported that Wang Mang's merits should be rewarded like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. The ministers requested that Wang Mang be given the title of prime minister, ranking above the three dukes, with various honors and rewards.

Wang Mang refused the rewards, but the Queen Mother insisted. He eventually accepted the titles and rewards, including the prime minister's seal. Wang Mang proposed building a Mingtang, a national imperial college, and other structures, recruiting scholars from across the country. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's merits were evident, and the construction was completed quickly. The Queen Mother agreed to reward Wang Mang with nine kinds of utensils. In the fifth year of the Yuan Dynasty, many princes and officials petitioned for Wang Mang's rewards. Wang Mang wrote a letter declining, but the Queen Mother insisted. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's merits were like those of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and they requested the reward of nine tins. The Queen Mother approved, and Wang Mang received various honors and items, including a green apron, formal dress, a jade-inlaid saber, chariots, and military equipment. He was also given a red painted door and steps inside the eaves, with guards and officials appointed to assist him.

In the autumn, Wang Mang dug the Ziwu Road due to an auspicious sign from his daughter, Queen Wang. Eight custom envoys returned, reporting that the customs of the world were uniform and forging folk songs praising virtues. Wang Mang reported this and recorded it in documents. He also reported that there were no lawsuits, thieves, or hungry people, and the system of men and women not walking together was implemented. Twelve people, including Liu Xin and Chen Chong, were granted the title of marquis for building the Mingtang. Wang Mang sent envoys to attract the Qiang people, who offered their land to become subjects. Wang Mang proposed establishing Xihai County and revising state names and boundaries. The memorial was approved, and fifty additional laws were added, with violators exiled to Xihai County. The people became resentful. Liu Qing, Marquis of Quanling, wrote a letter suggesting Wang Mang act as regent like the Duke of Zhou. The ministers agreed. When Emperor Ping fell ill, Wang Mang prayed for his safety and offered to sacrifice his own life. Emperor Ping died, and Wang Mang recruited scholars to participate in the decision to mourn for three years. He selected Liu Ying, a two-year-old great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan, as the successor.

A white stone with vermilion words reading "Announcement of Prince Mang of Anhan to be the emperor" was discovered. Wang Mang asked the princes to report this to the Queen Mother, who initially refused but eventually agreed to let Wang Mang act as regent. The ministers reported that Wang Mang should ascend the throne and exercise imperial power, following the example of the Duke of Zhou. The Queen Mother issued an edict allowing Wang Mang to serve as regent and act as the emperor. Wang Mang then sat on the throne, wore the emperor's clothes, and accepted the worship of the ministers. The next year, the name was changed to Jushe. In the first year of Jushe, Wang Mang worshiped the gods and held ceremonies. Liu Ying was made the crown prince, known as Ruzi. Wang Shun, Zhen Feng, and Zhen Han were appointed as officials. In April, Liu Chong, Marquis of Anzhong, attacked Wancheng but failed. Wang Mang pardoned those who surrendered. Liu Jia wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang and suggesting severe punishment for Liu Chong. Wang Mang was pleased and granted Liu Jia a fiefdom. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's power should be increased to conquer the world. The Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to call himself the "fake emperor" when seeing her. In December, the ministers petitioned to increase Wang Mang's official offices and household staff. The memorial was approved.

In the spring of the second year, new currencies were minted, and a ban was issued on carrying gold privately. In September, Zhai Yi, the prefect of Dongjun, raised troops and elected Liu Xin as emperor, accusing Wang Mang of poisoning Emperor Ping. Wang Mang was frightened and sent eight generals to attack Zhai Yi. Tang Ming and Huo Hong also raised troops to respond, growing to nearly 100,000 people. Wang Mang sent generals to resist them and appointed Zhen Han as the general. In December, Wang Yi and other generals defeated Zhai Yi. Chen Chong wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang's wisdom. Wang Mang was very happy. In the spring of three years, an earthquake occurred, and Wang Mang announced a general amnesty. Wang Yi and others defeated Ming Dynasty and Huo Hong. Wang Mang held a banquet to reward the generals and wrote a memorial suggesting that the Zhou system be followed for titles and fiefs. The memorial was approved, and several hundred people were granted titles. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's sons should be promoted to the title of Duke. The Queen Mother agreed, and Wang An and Wang Lin were made dukes. Wang Guang was granted the title of Yan Gonghou. Wang Mang then planned to ascend to the true throne.

In September, Wang Mang's mother died. Instead of expressing grief, Wang Mang asked the Queen Mother to discuss his mourning clothes. The doctors and Confucian scholars said that the regent should not wear mourning clothes for his biological mother. Wang Mang implemented their suggestion. Chen Chong reported that Wang Guang had privately told Zhi Jinwu Shi Ji to kill for him. Wang Mang was furious, and Wang Guang and his mother committed suicide. Wang Mang wrote a letter about the prohibition of playing music and asked about the grades of music. In this year, Liu Jing, Hu Yun, and Zang Hong reported auspicious omens. Wang Mang readily accepted them. On Jiazi day in November, Wang Mang wrote a memorial to the Queen Mother, citing various omens and requesting to be called the "false emperor" and to change the calendar. The memorial was approved. The common people learned of his belief in the talisman, and the ministers discussed it widely. Aizhang, a native of Zitong County, made a copper cabinet with inscriptions claiming Wang Mang was the true emperor. Wang Mang went to the Gaodi Temple to receive the copper cabinet, wore the crown, and ascended the throne as the True Dragon Emperor. He declared a new country, changed the calendar, and set the colors of carriages, horses, and clothing to yellow.

summary:
In the fourth year of his reign, Wang Mang granted titles and rewards to several officials, including Lu Ta and Xian Zhi, who received the rank of special advance and were treated with the same etiquette as the three princes. He also awarded them houses, money, and ceremonial items. In June, he formally enfeoffed princes at the Mingtang, claiming he had spent nearly nine years planning the land system and feudal hierarchy based on classical texts. However, Wang Mang was known for his empty rhetoric and stinginess, using the undetermined land plan as an excuse to delay actual implementation while granting symbolic titles to appease those who desired rank.

Wang Mang reaffirmed six financial management systems, establishing harsh laws with punishments including execution for violations. He levied taxes on slave owners, requiring 3,600 yuan per slave, which caused widespread resentment and led to the rise of bandits. When officials like Nayan and Feng Chang advised against these policies, Wang Mang removed them from office. He appointed law enforcement officers with powers similar to Han dynasty governors to supervise the six systems. Rebellions erupted across the country, including Guatianyi's occupation of Changzhouyuan and Lu Mu's uprising in Langxie County, where a woman whose son was unjustly killed by a county magistrate gathered followers, attacked Haiqu County, and eventually commanded tens of thousands of troops.

Wang Mang's envoys reported that thieves dispersed but regrouped due to harsh prohibitions, heavy taxes, and the inability of people to make a living. Wang Mang dismissed officials who reported these truths and promoted those who flattered him. In August, he forged a copper weapon shaped like the Big Dipper to intimidate peasant armies, but during its casting, extreme cold killed many officials and horses. Fires broke out at the Northern Army camp, and when newly appointed officials like Fei Xing suggested lenient policies to address the root causes of rebellion, Wang Mang dismissed them. Officials across the country sought illegal profits due to unpaid salaries, amassing fortunes.

Wang Mang's grandson Wang Zong was discovered drawing himself in imperial regalia and engraving seals with rebellious inscriptions. After investigation, Wang Zong committed suicide, and his sister Wang Zhi also died after being implicated in murder and witchcraft. The Red Eyebrow Army, led by Li Zidu and Fan Chong, began their uprising in Langxie County due to famine, gathering ten thousand troops. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them failed. In the sixth year, Wang Mang calculated a 36,000-year calendar and changed the year name, claiming to follow divine instructions, but people laughed at these practices.

The Kanto region suffered from drought and famine for consecutive years, causing rebel numbers to grow. Wang Mang recruited strong men, condemned criminals, and slaves to form elite troops, collecting one-thirtieth of property from officials and civilians to fund military campaigns. He also recruited specialists with unique skills to attack the Xiongnu, including a man who claimed to be able to fly but only managed a few hundred steps before falling. Wang Mang appointed them all as commanders despite knowing their claims were false.

Wang Mang's policies led to widespread suffering. People abandoned their homes, the old and weak died on roadsides, and the strong joined thieves. Officials like Han Bo tried to ridicule Wang Mang with absurd reports, but Wang Mang executed them. He changed the year name to Emperor of the Earth and issued harsh decrees allowing executions even in spring and summer, terrifying the people. When natural disasters occurred, Wang Mang blamed his officials rather than his own policies.

The rebellion continued to spread, with various leaders emerging across the country. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them through military force and harsh laws only worsened the situation. His officials grew increasingly fearful, and the people's suffering intensified. The Han dynasty eventually revived under Emperor Gengshi, who captured Chang'an and executed Wang Mang's supporters. The Red Eyebrow Army later overthrew Emperor Gengshi, causing further destruction, until Emperor Shizu restored order and peace to the realm.
