Yanqi State lied about surrendering and ambushed its troops to attack Wang Jun and others. They all died.
Guo Qin and He Feng arrived late, attacked their old and weak remnants, and entered the border via Huangmianli.
Yu Mang appointed Guo Fu as the general outside the town, granted him the title of Maggot King, and Dan Guo as Ji Hu Nan.
From then on, it severed all relations with other countries in the Western Regions.
summary:
On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Wang Mang led the princes and ministers to present the newly made Imperial Seal of the Empress Dowager to her, thereby removing the name of the Han Dynasty. Wang Mang had married the daughter of the Wang family of the Marquis of Yichun as his queen, who bore him four sons: Wang Zi, Wang Huo, Wang An, and Wang Lin. Two of his sons had been executed earlier. Due to Wang An's confusion, Wang Lin was made crown prince, and Wang An was given a new title. Six sons were granted the title of king. An amnesty was announced for the whole world. Wang Mang then wrote a policy letter ordering the boy Liu Ying to step down, granting him the title of Ding'an Gong and making him a guest of the new dynasty. Queen Xiaoqian was named the Queen Mother of Ding'an. After reading the policy, Wang Mang personally held the boy's hand, sighed with tears, and expressed his sorrow. The middle master took the boy down to the palace, and the boy faced north, calling himself a minister. Hundreds of officials accompanied him, and no one was unmoved.

According to the instructions on the gold cabinet, the auxiliary ministers held appointment ceremonies. The Taifu, Zuo Fu, and Husband General Anyang Hou Wang Shun were appointed as the Grand Master and granted the title of An Xingong; the Great Situ Juudehou Pingyan was appointed as the Grand Tutor and granted the title of Xingong; Shao'a, Xihe, and Jingzhao Yin Hongxiu Hou Liu Xin were appointed as the Imperial Preceptors and granted the title of Jiaxin Gong; Aizhang, a native of Zitong County in Guanghan County, was appointed as the State General and granted the title of Mei Xingong. These were the fourth assistants, ranking in the rank of Grand Duke. The Taibao and later Chengyang Marquis Zhen Han was appointed as the Great Sima and granted the title of New Gong; the Marquis of Pi Jin, Wang Xun, was granted the title of the Great Situ and granted the title of the New Duke; the infantry general, the Marquis of Chengdu, was granted the title of the Grand Sikong and granted the title of Long Xingong. These were the three Dukes. Da'a, Youfu, Da Sikong, and Wei generals Guangyang Hou Zhenfeng were appointed as Gengshi generals and granted the title of Guangxin Gong; Wang Xing from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the Wei general and granted the title of Xingong; General Qingche Cheng Wuhou Sun Jian was appointed as the founding general and granted the title of Xingong; Wang Sheng from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the former general and granted the title of Chongxin Gong. These were the four generals. Eleven males in total. Wang Xing was the original official of the city gate, and Wang Sheng was a cake seller. Wang Mang found more than ten people with such names according to the talisman, and they were directly recruited from civilians to show their magic. Others with the same name were awarded the title of Langguan. On this day, a total of several hundred people were awarded the official positions of minister, minister, and minister. Members of the royal family surnamed Liu who served as county governors were all transferred to admonish the officials. Mingguang Palace was changed to Ding'an Pavilion, and Queen Mother Ding'an was allowed to live there. The former Dahonglu official residence was used as a public residence in Ding'an, with guards and envoys set up to monitor and manage it. The nursery staff and nanny were warned not to talk to him, and he was allowed to stay in a small room surrounded by four walls. Later, Wang Ling married his granddaughter Wang Yu's daughter to him.

Wang Mang issued a policy document stipulating the responsibilities of the officials, linking them to the five planets and the moon, sun, and Beidou. Other officials made regulations according to their duties. There were appointed Grand Sima Siyun, Grand Situ Sizhi, and Grand Situ Kong Siruo, all of whom were appointed as Guqing. Da Sinong was renamed Xihe, and later Nayan, Dali was renamed Zuoshi, Taichang was renamed Zhizhong, Dahonglu was renamed Dianle, the Shaofu was renamed Gonggong, and the Shuiheng Duwei was renamed Yuyu. In addition, the three company ministers were renamed nine ministers in total, and they were placed under the jurisdiction of the three princes. There were three officials under each minister, and three officials under each official. A total of twenty-seven officials and eighty-one officials were in charge of all the duties of various government offices in the capital. Guang Luxun was renamed Sizhong, the imperial servant was renamed Taiyu, the Weiwei was renamed Taiwei, Zhijinwu was renamed Fenwu, the lieutenant was renamed Junzheng, and a large official was set up to be in charge of the emperor's vehicles, clothes and utensils, and later in charge of military supplies. The positions were all senior ministers, called the Sixth Supervisor. The prefect of the county was renamed Taiyin, the captain was renamed Taiwei, the county magistrate and magistrate were renamed Zai, the censor was renamed Enforcement, the carriage driver was renamed Wanglu Simen, Changle Palace was renamed Changleshi, Weiyang Palace was renamed Shouchengshi, the front hall was renamed Wanglutang, and Chang'an was renamed Chang'an. The people with a salary of 100 stones were renamed common people, those with a salary of 300 stones were renamed corporals, those with a salary of 400 stones were renamed sergeants, those with a salary of 500 stones were renamed Mingshi, those with a salary of 600 stones were renamed yuanshi, those with a thousand stones were renamed xiaodafu, those with 2000 stones were renamed middle doctors, 2000 stones were renamed shangdafu, and those with 2000 stones were renamed qing. The carriages, horses, dresses, and hats they use all have different levels. Doctors Sigong, Situ, Siming, Sicong, Sizhong, poetry reciters, and Che Shanzai were also appointed to detect faults.

Wang Mang issued a policy letter saying that there are no two suns in the sky, and there are no two kings on the earth. Some of the princes of the Han Dynasty were called kings, until foreigners from all over the world also imitated the title of king, which violated the ancient system and deviated from the principle of unification. It should be ensured that the names of princes and kings are all called Gong, and that the names of foreigners from all over the world who steal their names and call themselves kings are changed to Hou. He also said that the emperor's lineage should be inherited, developed and integrated; the lineage with noble virtues should enjoy sacrifices for a long time. He thought that Huangdi, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diru, Yao of Tang, Yushun, Xia Yu, Gaotao and Yiyin all had sage virtues. He admired them, sought their descendants, and intended to continue their sacrifices. He believed that the surname Wang was a descendant of Yu Shun and came from imperial learning; the surname Liu was a descendant of Tang Yao and came from Zhuan Xu. So Yao Xun was granted the title of Marquis of Chumu, the descendant of the Yellow Emperor; Liang Hu was the descendant of Xiu Yuanbo, the descendant of Shaowu; the grandson of the emperor Gonglong Gongwang Qian was the descendant of the emperor; Liu Xin was the descendant of Qi Liebo, the descendant of Zhuan Xu; the country Liu Xin's son Liu Die was Yixiuhou and inherited the descendants of Tang Yao; Machang was Shimuhou and inherited the descendants of Yu Shun; Shan Zun was Baomou's son and inherited Gaotao's descendants; Yixuan was Baohengzi and inherited Yiyin's descendants. Liu Ying, the descendant of the Han Dynasty, Ding'an Gong, was a state guest. Ji Dang, a descendant of Duke Wei of the Zhou Dynasty, was renamed Duke Zhang Ping and was also a state guest. Song Gong Kong Hong, a descendant of the Yin Dynasty, had his fortune changed and his position moved. He was renamed Zhang Zhaohou and his status was that of a distinguished guest. Si Feng, a descendant of the Xia Dynasty from Liaoxi County, was granted the title of Zhang Gonghou and was also an honored guest. The ancestors of the Xia, Yin, Zhou, and Han dynasties were worshiped together in the Mingtang, and they were allowed to follow the great imperial ancestor Yu Shun to share. The descendants of Zhou Gong praised Lu Zi Ji Ji, and the descendants of Confucius praised Cheng Zi Ji Gou. It has been determined before.

Wang Mang continued that when he was the regent, he built suburban sacrificial altar sites, established ancestral temples, and set up Tugu Shrine. The gods repaid him with brilliance from above covering the bottom, flowing down and turning into old crows, and yellow air rising and shining brightly to highlight the afterglow of Huangdi and Yushun. From the Yellow Emperor to King Bo of Jinan, there were five surnames of our ancestors. Huangdi had twenty-five sons and gave them twelve surnames. The surname accepted by the ancestors of Yu and Shun was Yao. In the Tao and Tang Dynasties, the surname was Yu, in the Zhou Dynasty, the surname was Chen, in Qi State, the surname was Tian, ​​and in Jinan, the surname was Wang. He prostrated himself in memory of the great emperor Kao Huangdi, and the great emperor Kao Yushun. They have been worshiped together in the Mingtang, and they should also be included in the ancestors' temples. Five ancestral temples and four ancestral temples should be built, and their queens or wives should all enjoy them. When offering sacrifices to heaven and earth, let the Yellow Emperor share with the sky, and let the Yellow Queen share with the earth. The east residence of Xin Duhou was used as the Ancestral Temple, and sacrifices were made on time every two years. The ancestors respected by the people should also be worshiped from generation to generation. The imperial court has set an example for the whole country. People with the five surnames of Yao, Ma, Chen, Tian, ​​and Wang are all descendants of Huangdi and Yushun, and they all belong to my clan. Didn’t the Book of Books say it? In order to promote love and harmony among the nine clans, all parts of the country should be ordered to report the names of these five surnames to the Zhizong clan and treat them as royal clans. Grant them immunity from taxation and labor for generations to come, and have nothing to do with it. Among them, the Wang surname in Yuancheng County is not allowed to marry each other with the surnames Yao, Yan, Chen, and Tian, ​​so as to distinguish clans and separate relatives. Chen Chong was granted the title of Tongmuhou to inherit the descendants of King Hu; Tian Feng was granted the title of Shimuhou to inherit the descendants of King Jing. Because of the rebellion of Zhai Yi, Tang Ming and others in the past, the state pastors and county governors across the country were able to occupy their states and counties. They were loyal and filial, and granted the governors the title of baron and the governor the title of annexed city. He also granted the title of baron to the sons of his old benefactors Dai Chong, Jin She, Ji Hong and Yang Bing. They sent Weixiao and others from Qidu to repair the Yellow Emperor's tomb in Shangdu Bridge, Yu Shun's tomb in Jiuyi, Lingling County, King Hu's tomb in Chen County, Huaiyang County, King Jing's tomb in Linzi County, Qi County, King Min's tomb in Ju County, Chengyang State, King Bo's tomb in Shupingling County, Jinan County, and King Ru's tomb in Yuancheng County, Wei County, and envoys were sent to offer sacrifices according to the seasons. Their ancestral temple should be built, because the country has just been pacified, and for the time being, joint sacrifices will be held in the Mingtang Ancestral Temple. Take Han Gaodi Temple as Wenzu Temple. Wang Mang said that his great emperor Kao Yushun accepted the ceded political power from Tang Yao. The early ancestor of the Han Dynasty was Tang Yao. He wanted to praise and treat the previous dynasty, how could he forget it? There were seven ancestors of the Han Dynasty, and ancestral temples should be built in Ding'an State according to etiquette. The temples attached to their cemeteries in the capital should not be abolished, and the sacrifices should continue as before. He would personally go to the ancestral temples of Emperor Gao, Emperor Yuan, Emperor Cheng, and Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty to offer sacrifices in September in autumn. The names of the royal families surnamed Liu were transferred to the management of Jingzhao Dayin. Their privileges of exemption from taxes and labor should not be revoked. They should be limited to themselves. The state pastor should often go to condolences and prevent them from being wronged and persecuted.

translation:
At that time, King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou of Shang, destroyed the Shang Dynasty, and moved the Nine Tripods, which symbolized state power, from the Shang capital to Luoyi. Boyi and Shuqi believed that King Wu was unfaithful and unfilial, so they ate Zhou millet in shame and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain. Even the people of Zhou praised them for their noble moral character.
Confucius thought the two of them were virtuous and praised them for not changing their ambitions and not allowing themselves to be humiliated.
Mencius also said: Hearing Boyi's demeanor is enough to make greedy people honest and cowardly people to establish their ambitions; to inspire behavior before a hundred generations, everyone after a hundred generations will be deeply inspired. Who can do this if he is not a sage?
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, there were Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong and Mr. Jiao Li. When the Qin Dynasty ruled the world, these four people fled to the depths of Shangluo Mountain and waited for the world to be peaceful.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty heard about it and summoned them, but they did not come.
Later, Empress Lu adopted the strategy of leaving Zhang Liang behind, and asked the crown prince to bring silk fabrics, bow down and greet him with humility, and use a small car to welcome him to her side to assist her.
After the four arrived, they followed the prince to see Gaozu. Gaozu respected them and treated them as honored guests. From this, the prince was taken seriously and his position was stabilized.
This incident is recorded in detail in "The Biography of Liuhou".
Later, there was Zheng Zizhen in the mouth of the valley, and there was a strict gentleman in Shu. They were able to cultivate themselves and respect themselves, not wearing what they shouldn't wear, and not eating what they shouldn't eat.
When Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty was in power, his uncle and general Wang Feng recruited Zizhen with courtesy, but Zizhen did not accept the call and ended up not yielding.
A gentleman was doing divination in the Chengdu market. He thought: Although divination is a humble profession, it can benefit everyone.
If someone inquires about something evil or unfair, tell him the pros and cons according to the yarrow and the shell of a tortoise.
The divination for a son is based on the principles of filial piety; the divination for a younger brother is based on the principle of obedience; the divination for a minister is based on the idea of ​​loyalty to the king. In this way, we can take advantage of the situation and guide different people towards the good side. More than half of the people obey my words.
He only receives a few people every day. When he can earn a hundred yuan to survive, he closes the stall and teaches "Laozi" at home.
He also read a lot of various books and became proficient in them all. According to the theories of Laozi and Zhuangzhou, he wrote more than 100,000 words of books.
Yang Xiong studied with him when he was young, and later became an official in the capital and became famous. He repeatedly praised Yan Junping's conduct to the virtuous officials in the court.
Li Qiang, a native of Duling, had always been very good with Yang Xiong. Later he became an official and became a shepherd in Yizhou. He happily said to Yang Xiong: Now I really want to get King Yan Zhou. Hexiong said: You have to treat him with courtesy. He is a person who can be seen and cannot be used by others.
Li Qiang disagreed in his heart.
After he took office in Shu, he met Junping with courtesy, but he still dared not bring up the matter of calling him as an official, so he sighed: "Yang Ziyun really understands people!"
Yan Junping lived to be more than ninety years old, and he continued to work on divination and fortune-telling until his death. People in Shu loved and respected him, and they still praise him to this day.
Later, Yang Xiong wrote a book about the people of the world, praising these two people in particular.
He commented: There is a world: a gentleman is afraid that he will live his whole life without a name, so why not use the power of a famous minister to achieve his name?
I believe that if a gentleman accumulates his own virtues, his reputation will be established.
Liang, Qi, Chu, Zhao and other princes and kings are not without wealth and honor, but what do they use to achieve their reputation?
Gu Zhengzi really persevered in his ambition and worked under the rocks, but his reputation spread throughout the capital. Is it because he was a public official?
Is it because he is a minister?
The two gongs in the Chu land are white and clean, and they have the name of Qingming!
The strict gentleman of Shu County is deep and has no desires. He does not seek favors for sexual relations, does not engage in the career of seeking profit, and lives in seclusion for a long time without changing his moral integrity. Even if it is the pearl of Suihou or the jade of He family, how can it be compared with it?
If this person is raised and used, isn’t he also a treasure of the country?
Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong, Mr. Jiao Li, Zheng Zizhen, and Yan Junping were not officials. However, their demeanor and reputation were enough to deter greed and inspire the world. They were people who lived in seclusion in modern times.
For example, Wang Ji, Gong Yu, and Liang Gong all knew how to be courteous and courteous when going out to serve and when they retired.
Wang Ji, courtesy name Ziyang, was born in Langxie, Gao and Yu.
He was eager to learn when he was young and was proficient in classics. He first served as a county official. He was elected as a Lang due to his filial piety and integrity, filling the position of Lu Youcheng, and later he was appointed as the Yunyang County Magistrate.
Ju Xianliang was appointed as the lieutenant of Changyi. The king of Changyi liked hunting and often drove horses galloping in the country. His behavior was uncontrolled. Wang Ji therefore admonished the minister and said:
I heard that in ancient times, the army usually marched thirty miles a day, but it only marched fifty miles for auspicious occasions. "The Book of Songs" says: The wind is blowing, the car is speeding, I look around and feel sad in my heart.
It means: The rapid and erratic hair is not the ancient way of wind; the horse is driven at a gallop, this is not the ancient way of chariot. Hence the sadness.
Now the king is on a tour of Xingfang and the county. He has traveled two hundred miles in less than half a day. Many people have abandoned their farm work to build roads and lead their horses. I think the people should not be changeable.
In the past, when Duke Zhao took office, he would do business under the Gantang tree when farming was busy.
At that time, everyone had his own place, and later generations of owners also remembered his benevolence and kindness, so much so that they did not cut down a cang tree to commemorate him. The poem "Gantang" in the Book of Songs describes this incident.
Your Majesty, you don't like to study and study, but like to travel. You lean on the carriage rails all day long to drive and ride horses. Your tongue is tired from shouting and yelling, your arms are sore from driving and riding horses, and your body is tired from the jolting of carriages and horses. You face fog and dew in the morning and are covered with dust during the day. You are scorched by the scorching heat in summer and bitten by the biting cold in winter.
Repeatedly using your weak body to withstand the abuse of hard work is not conducive to longevity, nor is it conducive to the growth of benevolence and righteousness.
In the spacious and bright room, on the exquisite and gorgeous carpets, teachers with both ability and political integrity are teaching earnestly in the front, and diligent and inquisitive students are studying hard in the back. They discuss the old events of the Tang and Yu Dynasties, and the grand events of the Yin and Zhou Dynasties, and inspect The demeanor of a benevolent and sage person, learning how to govern the country and the people, being leisurely and contented, working hard and forgetting to eat, constantly improving and perfecting one's own moral cultivation, how can the pleasure and joy in it be compared to driving a horse and traveling around!
When resting, bend, bend and stretch to activate the body's tendons, walk in and out instead of driving to strengthen the legs, spit out the old and absorb the new to practice the Qi of the five internal organs, and concentrate on concentrating the mind to nourish the spirit and calm the mind. If you use the above methods to maintain your health, can't you still live a long life?
If your Majesty truly acts with sincerity, you will have the ambitions of Yao and Shun in your heart, and the longevity of Qiao and Song in your body. Your praise will rise and be heard by the emperor, and you will be blessed with good fortune and the country will be stable.
Today's saint is a benevolent and wise saint. Since the late emperor Yanjia, he has been thinking about him endlessly. He has never been involved in traveling to palaces, gardens, hunting and other recreational activities. Your Majesty, you should always bear these in mind and understand the holy will.
Among all the princes, there is no one who has a closer relationship with the emperor than you, the king. From the perspective of biological relationship, the king is the descendant. According to the status of the king and the minister, the king is a minister, and you have double responsibilities. In this position, if the king is slightly imperfect in benevolence and righteousness, and the emperor knows about it, it will not be a good thing for inheriting the country.
Your Majesty, I am ignorant and straightforward, I hope your Majesty will understand.
Although Changyi King Liu He did not follow the right path, he still knew how to treat Wang Ji with respect and courtesy, so he issued an order: "It is impossible for me to be lax in my moral character. Lieutenant Wang Ji is loyal and has corrected my mistakes many times."
Therefore, I ordered Qianqiu to give the lieutenant five hundred catties of beef, five stones of wine, and five bunches of dried meat.
After that, Liu He indulged himself as usual.
Wang Ji always fulfilled his duty as an assistant minister by admonishing and arguing according to reason. Although he did not directly participate in the governance of the people, everyone in the feudal country did not respect him.
After a long time, Emperor Zhao died and he had no crown prince. The general Huo Guang came to power and sent Dahonglu Zongzheng to welcome the king of Changyi to the capital.
Wang Ji immediately wrote a letter to warn the king of Changyi: I heard that Emperor Gaozong was in mourning and did not speak for three years.
Now that your Majesty has been summoned for a funeral, you should mourn and weep day and night, and do nothing else.
Besides, why should funerals be like this? Why would the king of the south ever say too much?
The sky is silent, the four seasons are still changing according to the time, and all things in the world are still living and multiplying. I hope your Majesty will understand clearly.
General Huo Guang is kind, wise and brave, and his character of loyalty and integrity is known to everyone in the world. He has served Emperor Xiaowu for more than 20 years without ever making a mistake.
When the late emperor passed away, he entrusted the world and the young orphan to him. The general supported the infant emperor, issued decrees to educate him, and maintained the stability of the country. Even Zhou Gong and Yi Yin could only do this.
Now that the emperor has passed away without an heir, the general considers that he can inherit the Han Dynasty and the ancestral temple, and uses promotion to welcome the king as king. His benevolence and generosity are really unparalleled!
I hope that the king will serve him and respect him, and that all state affairs will be subject to his arrangements. You only need to do nothing to rule the south and call yourself the king.
I hope your Majesty will consider my suggestions and keep them in mind.
After King Changyi arrived in the capital, he took the throne for more than 20 days and was deposed for his lewd behavior.
The ministers of the Changyi feudal state did not report the crimes of King Changyi during the feudal period, so the court did not know the character of King Changyi; and because they failed to fulfill their duties as assistants and guides as ministers, King Changyi committed serious crimes and were all imprisoned and executed.
Only Wang Ji and his lieutenant Gong Sui escaped death because of their loyalty and uprightness and repeated admonitions. They were sentenced to shave their heads and build the city.
Later, he rose up and returned to serve as the governor of Yizhou, but soon resigned due to illness. He was also recruited as a doctor to advise the doctors.
At that time, Emperor Xuan tried his best to follow Emperor Wu's example and restored the rules and regulations of Emperor Wu's time. The palaces, carriages, clothing, etc. were all larger than those of Emperor Zhao's time.
At this time, Xu, Shi, Wang and other relatives were also favored and honored. Emperor Xuan personally handled political affairs and appointed capable officials.
Wang Jishangshu commented on its gains and losses:
His Majesty personally presides over the affairs of all parties with dignity. The national map and household registration are displayed in front of his eyes every day. He is devoted to national government affairs and strives for peace in the world.
Every time Shao Shu was passed down, the people were overjoyed and felt like they had been given a new life.
I believe that although these measures are the greatest favor to the people, they cannot be said to have fulfilled the fundamentals of government affairs.
There are not always monarchs who want to make a difference. The ministers are lucky enough to encounter such an era. The monarchs can listen to the suggestions and advice of the ministers, but they do not have a long-term strategy to establish an eternal foundation, and they do not create wise kings and saints like the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties in their heyday.
Only focusing on matters such as the transfer of property from the court or the government to the settlement of lawsuits is not the basis for establishing a peaceful society.
I heard that when a sage monarch promotes virtue and education, he must start from the present.
If the court is not in order, it will be difficult to govern the country; if the people around the monarch are not upright, it will be difficult to educate people far away.
Although the people are weak, they cannot be bullied, and although they are ignorant, they cannot be deceived.
The Holy Lord lives alone in the deep palace. If his actions win people's hearts, the world will praise him. If he loses people's hearts, the world will talk about him.
Although the emperor's actions are done before the eyes, their influence is far-reaching. Therefore, the left and right ministers and envoys around him should be carefully selected. The left and right ministers are set up to correct the emperor's words and deeds, and the envoys are set up to promote the emperor's kindness. The Book of Songs says: Talents abounded, and King Wen was able to stabilize the world.
Creation is the foundation of national government affairs.
The unified politics with the emperor as the center advocated by "Spring and Autumn" means that the customs and education of all parts of the country are the same, and the policies and orders of the nine states are unified.
Nowadays, those mediocre and incompetent officials govern the people, not relying on the etiquette and norms that can be used in all generations for education, but only relying on criminal laws to achieve their goals.
Those officials who want to make a difference cannot carefully examine the rules, regulations, etiquette and norms. Instead, they follow their own will, get what they need, speculate and act arbitrarily. Therefore, once the situation changes, it will be difficult to continue to implement their decrees.
As a result, the customs within a hundred miles are different, the education within a thousand miles is different, every family is engaged in different things, everyone wears different colors, and treachery and deceit compete with each other. There is no end to the abuse of punishment, the simple folk customs are disappearing day by day, and the affection of love is gradually weakening.
Confucius said that the best way to stabilize the political power and govern the people is to rule by courtesy. This is not an empty talk.
As the king of a country, before a new system of etiquette and justice has been formulated, he should choose and apply the parts of the etiquette and justice system established by the previous kings that are suitable for the current situation.
Your Majesty, I hope that your Majesty will obey the way of heaven, strive for great achievements, study the old rites together with the ministers and Confucian scholars, declare the royal system, and govern the world with benevolence, justice and etiquette, so that the people can bathe in your majesty's grace, live in comfort and live a long life. In this way, why worry about the world's customs and education not being as good as those of the Cheng and Kang eras, and the long-term peace and stability of the country not being as good as that of King Wuding of Yin?
Your Majesty, I personally believe that there are some things in today's society that are not in line with etiquette and justice, and I would like to submit a list of them for your Majesty's Holy Judgment to make a clear decision.
Wang Ji believes that husband and wife are the most important relationship among human beings. It is related to life, old age, illness and death.
Nowadays, secular people get married too early and have children before they understand the principles of parenthood. Therefore, not only is it difficult to implement moral education, but people are also prone to premature death.
Marrying a wife and having children is expensive and poor families cannot afford it, so they dare not have more children.
In addition, the princes of the Han Dynasty married princesses, and the people in the princely kingdoms married the daughters of princes. This system made men serve women and husbands submitted to their wives, which reversed the order of yin and yang, so disasters caused by women were prone to occur.
In ancient times, clothes, carriages and horses had certain regulations according to the status of their owners, to commend virtuous people and distinguish between superior and inferior. However, nowadays, the superior and inferior are arrogant and chaotic. Everyone does their own thing without certain restraint. Therefore, people are greedy for money and pursue personal gain without risking their lives.
The reason why the Zhou Dynasty was able to achieve great order in the world without punishment was because it curbed all kinds of evil and evil before they occurred.
Wang Ji also said: Yu Shun and Shang Tang did not appoint the hereditary sons of Sangong and Jiuqing, but selected Gao Tao and Yi Yin as ministers, so that those who were slanderous and unkind were alienated.
Nowadays, the children of officials are allowed to serve as officials. Most of them are proud and arrogant, and do not understand the affairs of the past and present. As for accumulating merits and governing the people, it is of no benefit to the people. This is the Book of Songs. The phenomenon satirized in "Cutting the Sandalwood".
Open selection should be implemented to recruit talented people, and the system in which sons and daughters serve as officials under the shadow of their father and elder brothers should be abolished.
Foreign relatives, relatives and friends can give them more money, but they should not be allowed to hold high official positions. They should abandon the play of extortion, reduce the number of Yuefu, lay off the craftsmen who are in charge of craftsmanship, and make it clear to the world that they are determined to advocate frugality.
In the past, craftsmen did not make exquisitely carved utensils, and merchants did not circulate extravagant and wasteful goods. This was not because these craftsmen and merchants were uniquely virtuous, but the result of the political education of the rulers.
When the people of the world see the government's determination to abandon extravagance and adopt frugality, they will return to the fundamentals of agriculture. Once the fundamentals are established, the related industrial and commercial sectors will be able to develop on the right track. The core idea of ​​Wang Jishangshu was roughly the same. The emperor believed that his remarks were unrealistic, so he didn't think highly of him.
Wang Ji then excused himself to feel unwell and returned to his hometown of Langye.

In the evening, the discussion ended.
The discussion continued the next day. General Zuo Gongsun Lu asked Gong Sheng: "Your argument yesterday was unfounded. Today, the results of the discussion will be reported to the emperor. Which opinion will you ultimately decide to obey?"
Gong Sheng said: If the general thinks my opinion is inappropriate, he can impeach me as well.
Dr. Xia Hou saw that the conversation between Gong Sheng and Gongsun Lu was unpleasant, so he got up and went to Gong Sheng and said to him: You should agree with what Shangshu said.
Gong Sheng pushed Xia Houchang and said: "Go away!"
A few days later, the ministers gathered again to discuss whether Xiaohui and Xiaojing temples could be restored. All the participants said they should be restored, but Gong Sheng said: etiquette should be followed.
Xia Houchang said to Gong Sheng: "The etiquette system has also changed."
Gong Sheng immediately retorted: Go away!
Times have changed.
Xia Houchang became angry and said to Gong Bo, "Do you know what I think of you?" If you want to be unconventional and deliberately different from others in order to gain favor and gain fame, you are just like people like Shentu Di in the late Yin Dynasty!
Before that, Xiahou Chang had told Gong Sheng that a man in Gaoling had killed his mother. Gong Sheng reported the matter to his superiors, and the minister asked: Who did you listen to?
Gong Sheng replied: Listen to what Xia Hou often said.
The minister asked him to ask Xia Houchang for details again. Lou Mi reprimanded Xiabao rewards one after another during the political discussion. He was very angry with Gong Sheng, so he replied: I just listened to what the servants in the government said casually, and I asked you not to talk about it outside. Why did you report it to the superiors? If you don't know the details of the incident, you will be punished if you casually report it to the authorities.
Gong Sheng had no way to explain to the minister, so he wrote a letter to impeach himself, saying that quarreling with Xiahou often was an insult to the dignity of the court.
The matter was reported to Yushi Zhongcheng, who summoned Gong Sheng and Xia Houchang to question him and impeached him, saying: Gong Sheng was an official of two thousand shi, and Xia Hou always held the position of a high official. They were all fortunate enough to participate in the affairs of the court, but they did not respect the etiquette and justice of the court. They were in public office, but they criticized and resented each other, quarreled and debated loudly, and said and acted wantonly without any reason. These are all disrespectful behaviors.
The emperor ordered: Each of them was demoted one level.
Gong Sheng apologized and asked to resign and return to his hometown.
The emperor also rewarded him, appointed his son Gong Bo as his minister, and appointed Gong Sheng as the governor of Bohai.
Gong Sheng refused to take up his post, claiming to be ill. He was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown six months later.
Emperor Ai also recruited Gong Sheng as Doctor Guanglu. Gong Sheng often claimed to be ill and bedridden, and many times asked his son to write letters requesting to be dismissed from office and return home, which coincided with the death of Emperor Ai.
At the beginning, Bing Han, a native of Langxie, was also recruited because of his noble character. He was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin and later became a doctor in Taizhong.
After Wang Mang became proficient in government affairs, both Gong Sheng and Bing Han requested to retire and return home.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, Han Fu, a native of Zhuojun, was recruited to Chang'an, the capital, for his outstanding virtues. Emperor Zhao gave him a policy letter and a bundle of silk to allow him to return to his hometown.
The edict was issued: I can't bear to let you worry about state affairs at such an old age. After returning to your hometown, please work hard to educate the villagers with the principles of filial piety and brotherhood.
On the way back home, you can eat, sleep and rest in the government's post station. Counties along the way must prepare wine and meat to provide food and drink for your entourage, carriages and horses.
The local officials in Zhuo County should pay regular condolences and give him a sheep and two hugs of wine every August.
If he dies unfortunately, the government will give him a funeral quilt and perform sacrifices according to the rites of the prison.
When sending them, Wang Mang followed the old rules and gave permission to send Gong Sheng and Bing Han back to their hometowns.
He also wrote a policy letter saying: In June of the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, two old men, Dr. Guanglu and Dr. Taizhong, resigned from office due to old age and serious illness.
The Empress Dowager sent an emissary, Pushe, to convey Shao Ling to them: I heard that in ancient times, officials resigned and went into seclusion when they reached a certain age, in order to respect the latter and preserve a certain amount of spare power.
Now that the two officials are old, I can no longer bother them with official matters. You can choose one of your sons, grandsons, brothers, or brothers' sons to serve in the court.
After the doctor returns home, please cultivate your moral integrity and live a peaceful life.
They were given cloth and allowed to rest overnight at various inns along the way. The specifications of the sheep, wine, clothes and quilts provided by the government on time every year were in accordance with Han Fu's old practice.
One of the recommended children, grandchildren, brothers of the same clan, or sons of brothers will be appointed as Lang.
So Gong Sheng and Bing Han returned to their hometown.
Bing Han's elder brother's son was named Manrong. He was also capable of self-cultivation and determination. He refused to exceed the rank of six hundred shi as an official. Once he exceeded 600 shi, he would be dismissed from office and resigned. His reputation surpassed that of Bing Han.
At first, Gong She was recruited as an admonishing doctor because of Gong Sheng's recommendation, but he was dismissed due to illness.
Later, he was recruited as a doctor and resigned due to illness.
Soon, Emperor Moai sent an envoy to Chu State to worship Gong She as the governor of Taishan.
Gong She lived in Wuyuan, and the envoy went to the county to invite Gong She, who was going to go to the county government hall to worship and receive the seal.
Gong She said: The king regards the world as his home, so why must he go to the county government hall to receive Shao orders?
So he accepted Shao Shu at his home and took office on the road.
A few months after taking office, he wrote a letter requesting to retire and return to his hometown.
The emperor also recruited Gong She to serve in Hu County in the Jingzhaoshu region, but Gong She refused because he was seriously ill.
The emperor had no choice but to send an envoy to take back the seal ribbon and worship Gong She as Guanglu doctor.
The emperor warned him many times, but Gong She still refused to accept the appointment, so the emperor had to let him return home.
Gong She was also familiar with the "Five Classics" and once taught his disciples "Lu Shi".
After Gong She and Gong Sheng retired and returned to their hometowns, the chief officials of their counties and counties, such as Erqian Shi and other officials, would come to their homes to pay tribute to teachers and students when they first took office.
Gong She died at the age of sixty-eight when Wang Mang was regent.
After Wang Mang usurped the state power, he sent General Wuwei to inspect the customs of the world. The general personally visited Gong Sheng with fat sheep and wine.
The next year, Wang Mang sent an envoy to pay homage to Gong Sheng for giving lectures and offering wine. Gong Sheng refused to enlist because he was ill.
Two years later, Wang Mang sent an envoy with the seal of the imperial edict and the seal and ribbon of the prince's mentor and friends, and sent a four-horse chariot to greet Gong Sheng in a grand manner. He planned to go to Gong Sheng's hometown to worship him as a high-ranking official with the rank of high minister, and to give him a gift in advance. Gong Sheng received six months' salary so that he could buy his luggage. Wang Mang's envoys, together with more than a thousand people including the prefect, county magistrates, three elders, prominent people in the township, and disciples, came to the village where Gong Sheng lived to deliver the edict.
The messenger wanted Gong Sheng to stand up and greet him, so he stood outside the door and waited for a long time. Gong Sheng claimed that he was seriously ill and could not get up to greet him, so he set up a bed under the south window of the west room of his home. He wore court clothes and lay on the bed with his head facing east.
The envoy entered the house, walked west, then stood facing south, conveyed the edict, handed over the seal, then stepped back and saluted again, presented the seal and ribbon, and drove the welcoming chariots and horses into the courtyard. Before entering, he said to Gong Sheng: The holy dynasty has not forgotten you, old man. The world system is not yet settled, and I look forward to your participation in political affairs. I hope to hear your suggestions and guidance on the country's major policies, so as to stabilize the world.
Gong Sheng replied: I have always been ignorant, and because of my old age and illness, my life is on the line. If I follow you on the road, I will definitely die on the way. This will be of no benefit to the country or to myself.
The envoy tried his best to persuade and even went forward to put the seal and ribbon on Gong Sheng, but Gong Sheng refused.
The messenger had no choice but to report to Wang Mang: It is now the scorching heat of summer, and Gong Sheng is physically ill and weak, so it is not suitable to go out. He can wait until the autumn cools before embarking on the road.
Wang Mang issued an edict and agreed.
The messenger came with the prefect every five days to ask about his diet, daily life and physical condition, and said to Gong Sheng's two sons and disciples Gao Hui and others: The imperial court is humbly looking forward to Mr. Gong Sheng and wants to make him a marquis. Even if he is seriously ill, he should get up and live in the post to show his intention to go. This will definitely leave a great legacy for future generations.
Gao Hui and others told Gong Sheng what the envoy said. Gong Sheng knew that his words were not listened to, so he said to Gao Hui and others: I have received great kindness from the Han royal family, and I can't repay it. Now that I am old, I may die at any time. Can I serve two surnames all my life, and then go to the underworld to see my old master after my death?
So Gong Sheng ordered his descendants to prepare a coffin and other funeral matters for him, saying: After I die, as long as my clothes are not exposed, my clothes are not exposed.
Do not follow the current social trend and bury many items along with the tomb to avoid excavation. Do not plant pines and cypresses or build an ancestral hall next to the tomb.
After giving the instructions, he stopped eating or drinking, and passed away fourteen days later at the age of seventy-nine.
Envoys and prefects all came to attend the funeral. According to the old customs, they were given quilts and offered sacrifices to the temple in the style of a prison.
Hundreds of his disciples wore mourning clothes to pay their respects.
An old man came to express his condolences and cried sadly. After crying, he said: Alas!
Lavender burns itself because of its fragrance, and oil burns itself because it can illuminate.
Gong Sheng died before his full life. He was not my kind of person!
After saying that, he hurried out of the door. No one knew who he was.
Gong Sheng lived in Lianli, Pengcheng, and later generations carved stones to commemorate his hometown gate.
Bao Xuan, courtesy name Zidu, was born in Gaocheng, Bohai Sea.
Diligent and studious, proficient in classics and meanings, he first served as a miserly official in the county and township, and temporarily acted as the county magistrate of Shuzhou.
Later, he became a meritorious officer of the Duwei Prefecture. He was elected as a Lang due to his filial piety and integrity. He resigned due to illness and worked for the state again.
Wang Shang, the general of Sima Wei, once conquered Bao Xuan and recommended him as Yilang, but he later resigned due to illness.
When Emperor Ai came to the throne, the great Sikong Hewu worshiped Bao Xuan as the Western Cao Dynasty. He respected him very much and recommended him as an admonishment official. He was also transferred to Yuzhou as a pastor.
More than a year later, Prime Minister Si Zhi Guo Qin reported: Bao Xuan's administration was cumbersome and harsh. He appointed officials to handle lawsuits on behalf of the county governor, and the issues he supervised exceeded the regulations established by the emperor.
When he went out for inspection, he did not follow the regulations for driving. He drove a horse and stayed in a pavilion overnight, which was criticized by everyone.
Bao Xuan was dismissed as a result.
A few months after returning home, he was recruited as an admonishing doctor.
When Bao Xuan was an official, he often wrote letters to give advice and argue with reason. His words were rarely empty, but they were simple and relevant to the current situation.
At that time, Emperor Ai's grandmother, Empress Dowager Fu, wanted to have the same title as Emperor Cheng's mother, and to confer officials and titles on her relatives. Prime Minister Kong Guang, Grand Sikong Shidan, He Wu, Grand Sima Fu Xi and others insisted on justice from the beginning, so they violated Empress Dowager Fu's will, and were dismissed from office.
The relatives of Ding and Fu were promoted, and Dong Xian was favored and became prominent. Bao Xuan, as a remonstrating official, followed Kong Guang, Shi Dan, He Wu, Fu happy and others, and wrote a letter to remonstrate:
I saw privately that when Emperor Xiaocheng was in power, his relatives were in power, and everyone attracted their close relatives to fill the court, blocking the advancement of virtuous people, making the world chaotic, extravagant, and the people poor. As a result, there were nearly ten solar eclipses in the sky and comets appeared four times.
Your Majesty saw those signs of danger with your own eyes. Why are they worse now than before?
Among the ministers of the imperial court, there were no upright Confucian scholars, no senior and experienced old people, and no strong warriors. There was no one who was familiar with ancient and modern history, could respond to a hundred calls, and worried about the country and the people as if he was hungry and thirsty but thought about food.
He relied heavily on his foreign cousin Xiaotong and his sycophantic minister Dong Xian to occupy important positions in the imperial court. It would be difficult for Your Majesty to work with these people to carry out destiny and stabilize the world.
Nowadays, the world regards people who lack wisdom as capable people, and people who are talented as incompetent.
In the past, Emperor Yao of the Tang Dynasty exiled four sinners, Gonggong, Guandou, Sanmiao, and Gun, and the world surrendered. Today, when he appoints an official, everyone is doubtful. In ancient times, people were still obedient when they were punished, but now they are rewarded and people are doubtful.
They ask each other to carry out treacherous plots, and the interests of the villain are put to good use.
The state treasury is empty and expenses are insufficient.
The people went into exile and left the city, thieves swarmed in, and officials harmed the people, which became more and more serious every year.
There are seven reasons for the unemployment and displacement of the common people: first, the yin and yang are not in harmony, and floods and droughts cause disasters; second, the county magistrates impose heavy taxes and new taxes; third, corrupt officials embezzle public property and continuously plunder; fourth, powerful families encroach upon the land. Insatiable; fifth, the harsh and violent officials imposed corvee duties, which delayed the farming season; sixth, the sound of drums and drums to warn thieves was heard from time to time in rural villages, and people, regardless of gender, had to go out to attack and hunt; seventh, thieves robbed and plundered people's property.
Not to mention these seven causes of people being displaced and unemployed, there are also seven factors that lead to people's death: first, being killed by cruel officials; second, the verdict and sentencing are too harsh and harsh; third, unjustly framed innocent people; fourth, thieves suddenly appear; fifth, those who have grudges kill each other; sixth, the harvest is poor and people suffer from famine; seventh, the climate is bad and diseases are prevalent.
It is really difficult for the country to have stability when the people suffer seven losses and nothing is gained; it is also difficult for the people to put aside the punishment when they suffer seven deaths but nothing to live.
Isn't this situation caused by the greed and cruelty of local officials such as ministers and county governors?
Ministers are fortunate enough to hold high positions and receive generous salaries. Who among them can sympathize with the sufferings of the people and assist His Majesty in imparting kindness and enlightenment?
Their thoughts are only used to run private interests, recruit and buy guests, and covet illegitimate benefits.
Everyone considers flattery and obedience as virtuous, and being wise and protecting oneself while only receiving salary as a silent person is considered smart, while people like me who dare to speak out are regarded as stupid.
Your Majesty, you select your ministers in the caves of the mountains, in the hope that they will be of help to the court and the country. Does your Majesty just want your ministers to enjoy high-ranking officials, rich salaries, fine clothes and fine food, in order to increase the majesty of the palace?
The world belongs to the Emperor. Your Majesty is the son of the Emperor above and the parents of the people below. He rules and raises all living beings on behalf of the Emperor. You should treat them equally, just as the poem "Corpse Dove" in the Book of Songs says.
Nowadays, the poor people have no food to eat, no clothing to cover their bodies, and father and son are unable to protect each other. It is really sad.
If Your Majesty does not save them, where will they end up?
Why do you only treat your relatives and fortunate minister Dong Xian favorably, and give them tens of thousands of rewards, so that their servants, servants and retainers regard wine and meat as the most common and low-grade food, and even the servants and servants have become rich!
This is against God's will.
As for Fu Shang, the Marquis of Ruchang, he was awarded a title without merit.
The official title is not His Majesty's official title, but the official title of the world.
How is it possible for Your Majesty to confer an official title that does not belong to you to someone who is not worthy of the official title, but still expect heaven to please people?
The sophistry of Sun Chong, the Marquis of Fang Yang, and Xi Fu Gong, the Marquis of Yiling, is enough to impress everyone, and their power is strong enough to stand alone. They are the most dangerous people among the traitors, and we should find an opportunity to avoid them in time.
As for those relatives and children who do not understand the classics, they should be allowed to leave their jobs and study as teachers.
The former Grand Sima Fu happy should be immediately recruited and given command of his relatives.
The former Grand Commander He Wu and Shi Dan, the former Prime Minister Kong Guang, and the former Zuo General Peng Xuan were all proficient in classics and meanings. They had all held Ph.D. degrees, and all held the rank of Three Dukes. Their intelligence and prestige were enough to establish education and plan for the survival of the country.
With Gong Sheng as the director, the prefectures and states take elections seriously. The losing officials of the third auxiliary committee of Gyeonggi do not dare to opportunistically, so they can be entrusted with big responsibilities.
His Majesty had previously dismissed He Wu and others because of a minor dissatisfaction and could not bear it. The people of the country were very disappointed.
Since you can even tolerate that large group of people who have no merit, why can't you tolerate He Wu and others?
Those who govern the world should think about what the people in the world think, and should not act based on their own likes and dislikes.
There is condemnation from the emperor and heaven above, resentment from the people below, and even the subordinates who dare to rebuke directly rise up to fight. Even if your majesty wants to reduce your own power and increase the power of evil people, no one in the world will listen.
Although I am stupid, don't I know how to receive more salary and rewards, build a big palace, eat delicious food, expand my farm and house, raise my wife and children well, and not make grudges with evil people in order to live a stable life?
In fact, he was forced to act out of great righteousness. Officials regard admonishment as their bounden duty and dare not not exhaust their loyalty.
I hope your Majesty will pay more attention to it, read the contents of the Five Classics, explore the sincerity and profound meaning of the saints, and ponder the warnings of heaven and earth.
Chen Bao declares that his words are slow, his feelings are sincere, and he is loyal and honest.
Because Bao Xuan was a Confucian, the emperor was very tolerant of him and did not blame him.
At this time, an earthquake occurred in the county, and rumors spread among the people that they were asking for fortune-telling. There was a solar eclipse on the first day of the first lunar month of the next year. The emperor summoned Kong Guang, dismissed Sun Chong, Xifu Gong, and dismissed dozens of Cao Huangmenlang and other servants.
Bao Xuan wrote again:
Your Majesty should serve the sky as you serve your father, you should serve the earth as you serve your mother, and you should raise the people as you would your own children. Since Your Majesty came to the throne, the sky has lacked light, the earth has trembled, and rumors have spread among the people to frighten each other.
Nowadays, a solar eclipse appears at the beginning of the year, month, and day, which is really scary.
Ordinary people are afraid of destroying utensils on the first day of the first lunar month, let alone when the sun is in decline?
Your Majesty can deeply blame himself, avoid the main hall, appoint people who dare to rebuke directly to review his own mistakes, remove relatives and useless people around you who are free of salary, worship Kong Guang as the Guanglu doctor, examine the faults and sins of Sun Chong and Xifu Gong, and let them be dismissed from office and return to their own kingdoms. Everyone will be reconciled and everyone will be happy.
Heaven and man are of the same mind, and if people's hearts are at peace, then the will of Heaven will be reconciled.
By Bingxu in February, there was a white rainbow, and there was no rain. This was a sign that the sky was still full of worries and the people were still dissatisfied.
Dong Xian, the consort in the palace, was not related to the royal family at all, but he was promoted through clever words, flattery, and flattery. The emperor was not restrained in his rewards. He exhausted the treasury and merged three residences to give him. Although they were too small, he also gave him a place to live in a violent house.
Dong Xian and his son sat there and ordered the emperor's envoys and craftsmen to build houses, and the officials who patrolled the houses at night were rewarded.
When visiting his family's grave or having a banquet, the young official would be required to provide supplies and organize the event.
Tribute items from all over the country were originally intended to support the emperor, but now they are all concentrated in Dong Xian's home. Isn't this in line with God's will and the people's will?
God's will and the people's heart cannot be let down for a long time. Treating Dong Xian so favorably is actually harming him.
If your Majesty really loves Dong Xian, you should apologize to heaven and earth for him, eliminate the resentment of the people in the world against him, remove him from his official position, let him return to his feudal country, confiscate his carriage and various utensils, and return them to the county magistrate.
In this way, father and son can still live the rest of their lives in peace; otherwise, those who are hated by the world will not be able to live a stable life for a long time.
Sun Chong and Xi Fu Gong are not suitable for holding important positions. They can be dismissed to show the world.
He Wu, Shi Dan, Peng Xuan, Fu happy and others were requisitioned to enable the people to see a clear and cheerful new atmosphere, to comply with the emperor's will, to establish a sound political system, and to revive the cause of peace in the world.
Gaomen is only a few dozen steps away from the provincial residence. It is just a matter of going in and out, but it has not been done for two years. Under such circumstances, it is impossible to reach remote places in the world by yourself!
I hope that your majesty will grant me a moment to state my humble opinion, and then, even if I am buried in hell, I will die with no regrets.
The emperor was greatly surprised by what Bao Xuan said, so he adopted his advice and appointed He Wu and Peng Xuan. They were reinstated as three Dukes in ten and a half months.
Bao Xuan was appointed Sili.
At this time, Emperor Ai changed the title of Sili Xiaowei to Sili, and his official rank was equivalent to Sizhi.
Prime Minister Kong Guang was responsible for inspecting the gardens and mausoleums at all times. One of his subordinates violated the regulations by relying on the emperor's order and was walking on the road in a car. Bao Xuan happened to meet him when he was out. Bao Xuan asked his subordinates to detain Prime Minister Shi Shi and confiscate his carriage and horse, humiliating the prime minister.
The matter was handed over to the censor Zhongcheng Nabao. The censor went to the Sili government office and wanted to arrest Bao Xuan's accompanying officials, but Bao Xuan closed the door and refused to let him in.
As a result, Bao Xuan committed crimes such as refusing to accept the envoy, being disrespectful, disrespectful, and unethical, and was arrested and sent to Tingwei Prison.
Wang Xian, a disciple of the doctorate from Jinan, held a flag to the gate of Taixue and said: "Those who want to save Bao Sili please gather under this flag."
More than a thousand people gathered from the Imperial College.
On the day of going to court, they stopped the prime minister to explain the situation himself. The prime minister's carriage and horses could not move forward, and they waited in front of the palace gate to write to the emperor.
The emperor then reduced Bao Xuan's death sentence by one level, shaved off his hair, and tied his neck with an iron ring.
After Bao Xuan was sentenced, his family moved to Shangdang. He believed that the Shangdang area was suitable for farming and grazing, and there were few talented people who could easily lead the way, so he settled in Changzi County, Shangdang.
After Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, Wang Mang was in power and secretly wanted to usurp the throne. So he hinted at Luo Zhi in various states and counties to frame and kill heroes. As for ministers who were loyal and upright to the Han Dynasty and did not want to cling to him, Bao Xuan, He Wu and others were executed.
At that time, Xin Xing from Longxi was wanted. Xin Xing and Bao Xuan's son-in-law Xu Cang went to Bao Xuan's house together, had a meal and left. Bao Xuan did not know the truth, was implicated, was arrested and imprisoned, and committed suicide.
From the time when he became emperor to Wang Mang, there were people who were honest and upright, such as the Langxie people who rebelled against Wang Mo.
Ji Kui and the Tang Dynasty both served as officials during the reign of Wang Mang, and were awarded the title of marquis. They were honored and distinguished, and ranked as public ministers.
Lu Zheng had written many letters to admonish Jing, and he had a loyal and upright character.
Lu Dian wore shabby clothes, wore perforated shoes, and ate and drank from rough earthenware vessels. He also gave these rough earthenware vessels to ministers, earning him a reputation as a hypocrite.
Xi Yue and Xi Xiang were brothers of the same clan. They were both promoted as filial, honest and maocai by the prefectures and counties. They resigned several times due to illness.
Xun Yue distributed more than tens of millions of property accumulated by his ancestors to the villagers of the nine ethnic groups in the prefecture, and his loyalty was particularly noble.
Prime Minister Xun was recruited as one of the four friends of the prince when Wang Mang was in power. After he died of illness, Prince Wang Mang sent an envoy to present mourning clothes and quilts. Prime Minister Xun's son held the coffin and refused to accept the gifts. He said: My deceased father left a message and did not accept gifts from his mentors and friends. Now, my father can be regarded as a friendly official to the crown prince, so he cannot accept gifts from the prince.
People in the capital praised his behavior. Xue Fang once served as a county clerk to offer wine sacrifices. The imperial court summoned him, but he did not answer the call. When Wang Mang was in power, he greeted him with a carriage.
The messenger told Wang Mang what he said. Wang Mang was very happy and stopped forcing him.
Xue Fang taught Confucian classics at home, liked to write articles, and wrote dozens of poems.
Guo Qin, a native of Mi, was originally named Prime Minister Sizhi during the reign of Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty. He once wrote a letter asking for the removal of Yuzhou Mu Bao Xuan, Jing Zhao Yin Xue Xiu and others. He also wrote a letter to impeach Dong Xian. He was demoted to the magistrate of Lunu County, and was promoted to the prefect of Nanjun during the reign of Emperor Ping.
And Jiang Fanqing, a native of Duling, served as the governor of Yanzhou and was also known for his integrity and uprightness.
When Wang Mang was regent, Guo Qin and Jiang Yi both claimed illness and were exempted from official duties. They returned to their hometowns. They were bedridden because of illness and could not leave the house, and died at home.
Li Rongkeqing of Qi State, Qinqing Zixia of Beihai, Su Zhangyouqing, and Cao Jingziqi of Shanyang were all Confucian scholars. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, they all abandoned their official positions.
After Wang Mang's death, Liu Xuan, Emperor Gengshi of the Han Dynasty, summoned Cao Jing as prime minister and granted him the title of Marquis, hoping to show the world his sincerity in recruiting wise men and eliminating bandits.
Cao Jing refused to accept the title.
It happened that the Red Eyebrow Army invaded Chang'an and wanted Cao Jing to surrender. Cao Jing fought with his sword and died.
After Shizu ascended the throne, he summoned Xue Fang. Xue Fang died of illness on his way to Beijing.
The descendants of Gong Sheng, Gong She and Bao Xuan were all commended and promoted to high officials.
Zan said: "The Book of Changes" says that the way of a gentleman is to be an official or to live in seclusion, or to be silent or to make suggestions. It means that each of them obtains an aspect of the way, just like the orchids and osmanthus plants. Although they are of different types, they all show their fragrance.
Therefore, it is said that people in the opposition can no longer hide in hiding after becoming an official, and people in the government can no longer hide in hiding after becoming an official. Both have their own shortcomings.
From the senior officials of various states in the Spring and Autumn Period to the generals, ministers and ministers since the rise of Han Dynasty, how many people have missed their official positions, indulged in favors and favors, and have lost the moral integrity of the world!
Therefore, those with high moral character are extremely rare.
However, most people can only govern themselves but cannot govern others.
Talents like Wang Ji and Gong Yu are far superior to Gong Sheng, Gong She and Bao Xuan.
By adhering to the good path until death, Gong Sheng truly practiced the way of a saint.
Consistent and intelligent, Xue Fang's words and deeds are close to those of a saint.
Guo Qin and Jiang Yi avoided chaos and did not taint their integrity. They were completely different from Ji Kui, Tang Lin, Tang Zun and others.
summary:
King Wu of Zhou overthrew King Zhou of Shang, moving the Nine Tripods to Luoyi. Boyi and Shuqi, deeming King Wu unfaithful and unfilial, starved to death on Shouyang Mountain rather than eat Zhou grain, earning praise for their moral purity. Confucius lauded their unwavering resolve, and Mencius declared that hearing of Boyi’s conduct could reform the greedy and cowardly, inspiring generations. After the Han rose, four recluses—Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong, and Mr. Jiaoli—fled to Shangluo Mountain during Qin rule. Emperor Gaozu summoned them in vain, but Empress Lu, following Zhang Liang’s strategy, had the crown prince humbly invite them with gifts. Their presence stabilized the prince’s position, as recorded in the *Biography of the Marquis of Liu*. Later, Zheng Zizhen of Gu Valley and Yan Junping of Shu cultivated self-respect, refusing improper attire or food. Zheng Zizhen declined recruitment by General Wang Feng. Yan Junping, a diviner in Chengdu, used his trade to guide people toward filial piety, obedience, and loyalty, earning a modest living before teaching Laozi. He authored over 100,000 words on Daoist philosophy. Yang Xiong, who studied under him, praised his conduct to officials, noting that Yan could be seen but not employed. Yan lived past ninety, revered by the people of Shu. Yang Xiong later wrote that a gentleman’s virtue establishes his reputation, contrasting the wealth of princes with the enduring fame of recluses like Zheng Zizhen and Yan Junping, whom he deemed national treasures.

Wang Ji (Ziyang) of Langxie excelled in classics, serving as a county official and later as lieutenant of Changyi. He admonished King Changyi for excessive hunting, citing ancient customs and the *Book of Songs* to urge moderation, warning that reckless travel harmed health and governance. He advocated study, ritual, and self-cultivation over indulgence. The king, though flawed, rewarded Wang Ji for his loyalty but continued his ways. After Emperor Zhao’s death, General Huo Guang summoned King Changyi to the capital. Wang Ji advised the king to mourn silently and defer to Huo Guang, comparing him to Zhou Gong and Yi Yin. The king was deposed after 20 days for lewdness; most of his officials were executed, but Wang Ji and Gong Sui were spared due to their admonitions, though sentenced to shave their heads and build cities. Wang Ji later served as governor of Yizhou and a court doctor. Under Emperor Xuan, he criticized the court’s focus on trivial matters over foundational governance, urging ritual education, selection of virtuous aides, and rejection of hereditary offices. He proposed reducing extravagance, abolishing coinage, and promoting agriculture. The emperor deemed his ideas impractical, so Wang Ji resigned, returning to Langxie. His reputation for integrity was marred by a minor incident: he divorced his wife for picking dates from a neighbor’s tree, though neighbors persuaded him to take her back. Wang Ji taught the Five Classics and died en route to a summons from Emperor Yuan. His son Wang Jun, also virtuous, served as an admonisher and governor, known for his capability alongside Zhao Guanghan and Zhang Chang. Wang Jun, after his wife’s death, refused remarriage, citing lack of virtue. His son Wang Chong became a censor but was demoted for pleading for a relative; later, under Wang Mang, he became Grand Sikong and Marquis of Fuping, but died by poisoning. The Wang family maintained honesty across generations, though their love for fine carriages and clothes puzzled contemporaries, leading to the saying “Wang Yang could turn gold.”

Gong Yu (Shaoweng) of Langxie, known for his classic learning, served as a doctor and governor of Liangzhou before resigning. Recruited by Emperor Yuan, he advised frugality, citing ancient standards: few concubines, simple palaces, and light taxes. He criticized the extravagance of Emperor Wu’s era, noting that officials and nobles overstepped ranks, leading to waste and poverty. He urged reducing palace horses, craftsmen, and concubines, and returning gardens to the poor. Emperor Yuan adopted some suggestions, cutting horse feed and distributing land. Gong Yu later became a censor, submitting dozens of memorials. He argued that taxes on three-year-olds caused infanticide, proposing taxes start at age seven. He condemned coinage for diverting labor from farming, causing hunger, and advocated returning to barter. He also criticized atonement laws for encouraging corruption, urging strict punishment for dishonest officials. Emperor Yuan implemented the seven-year tax rule and reduced palace guards, though other reforms stalled. Gong Yu died shortly after becoming censor; the emperor granted his son a post. His proposals on temple abolition were later enacted but criticized by scholars.

Gong Sheng (Junbin) and Gong She (Junqian) of Chu, known for integrity, were called the “Two Gongs.” Gong Sheng served as an admonisher under Emperor Ai, criticizing poverty, crime, and official corruption. He accused Dong Xian of disrupting court order, leading to conflict with colleagues. After a dispute with Xiahou Chang over ritual, he was demoted and resigned. Recruited again, he refused to serve under Wang Mang, who sent envoys with lavish gifts. Gong Sheng, bedridden, refused the seal, saying he could not serve two dynasties. He starved himself to death at 79, instructing simple burial. Gong She, also a classicist, served briefly as governor of Taishan but resigned due to illness. He died at 68 during Wang Mang’s regency. Bao Xuan (Zidu) of Bohai, a diligent scholar, served as an admonisher under Emperor Ai. He wrote vehemently against the favoritism shown to Dong Xian and the Fu and Ding clans, warning that corruption, heavy taxes, and harsh laws caused seven reasons for displacement and seven causes of death. He urged the recall of virtuous officials like He Wu and Kong Guang. Emperor Ai initially tolerated him, but after Bao Xuan humiliated a prime minister’s subordinate, he was imprisoned. Over a thousand students protested, leading to his sentence being reduced to shaving and iron chains. He later moved to Shangdang, where Wang Mang had him executed for associating with a wanted man. Other figures like Xin Xing, Ji Kui, and Xue Fang displayed varying degrees of integrity, with some refusing Wang Mang’s summons. The historian concludes that while hermits and officials each have merits, true virtue lies in unwavering adherence to the good path, as exemplified by Gong Sheng and Xue Fang.

translation:
Gai Kuanrao, courtesy name Cigong, was from Weijun.
Because he was proficient in classics, he served as a county scholar, and because of his filial piety and integrity, he became a Langguan.
He was promoted to the title of Founder, took the imperial examination and achieved excellent results, was promoted to the imperial censor, and acted as the deputy general of the household.
He impeached Pengzu, the son of General Zhang Anshi of the Imperial Guard, for refusing to get out of the car in front of the palace gate, and because Anshi had no political achievements in his official position.
Peng Zu actually got off the car in front of the palace gate at that time. Kuan Rao committed the crime of reporting the minister's misrepresentation and was demoted to Sima Wei.
Before that, Sima Wei was in the official office. When he saw the Wei Wei, he wanted to pay homage and often went out to buy things for the Wei Wei.
After Kuanrao became the Sima of the Guards, according to the previous system, he bowed his hands and saluted the officials who were responsible for patrolling the guards.
Weiwei sent Kuanrao out privately, and Kuanrao went to Shangshu Yamen to submit an application according to the system.
The minister then questioned the Wei Wei, and from then on the Wei officials no longer sent Pai Hou and Sima without permission.
Hou and Sima no longer paid homage to the emperor. When the emperor traveled, Hou and Sima, as the forerunners, had to give memorials first, and this was institutionalized from then on.
Kuanrao was appointed as Sima Chu. He did not leave the palace gate, cut his single coat short so that it could leave the ground, wore a big hat, and carried a long sword. He personally visited the soldiers' houses, inspected their diet and daily life, personally comforted and asked the sick soldiers, gave them medicine, and treated them very kindly.
When the shift was handed over at the end of the year, the emperor personally rewarded the retired soldiers. Thousands of soldiers kowtowed and asked to stay and serve for another year to repay the generous kindness.
Emperor Xuan commended him for his kindness, appointed him as Taizhong doctor, and asked him to inspect the customs of various places. He commended, recommended, demoted, and deposed many people, and completed the mission in line with the emperor's wishes.
Therefore, he was promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei, and he was able to inspect and expose the mistakes of officials without hesitation. Small and big matters were reported to the public, and many people were impeached. The Tingwei dealt with them according to the law, and half of his opinions were adopted and half were not adopted. However, the ministers, nobles, and officials of the county and state who were envoys to Chang'an were all too afraid to violate the ban, and the capital was peaceful.
When Ping Enhou Xu Bo moved into his new residence, all the prime ministers, censors, generals, and officials with a salary of two thousand dan went to congratulate him, but Kuan Rao did not go.
Uncle Xu invited him, so he went up to the hall from the west steps and sat alone facing the east.
Uncle Xu poured him wine himself and said: "You are late."
Kuanrao said: Don't pour more wine for me. I'll go crazy if I drink too much.
Prime Minister Wei Hou smiled and said: "You are a little crazy when you are awake. Why do you have to drink?"
Everyone present looked at him with contempt.
When the wine was in full swing, the music started playing. Tan Changqing, the young master of Changxin, got up and danced, performing a monkey and dog fight, and everyone present laughed.
Kuangrao was unhappy, looked up at the roof and sighed, "How beautiful!"
However, wealth is impermanent, and everything changes in a blink of an eye. When the owner changes, the building becomes like a hotel. I have seen it a lot.
Only by being cautious can we maintain our long-term success. How could you not be vigilant?
So he stood up and walked out quickly, impeaching Changxin Shaofu to perform the monkey dance as a minister, which was disrespectful.
The emperor wanted to punish the young master, but Xu Bo apologized for him. After a long time, the emperor stopped pursuing the case.
Kuan Rao is an upright person with high integrity and determination to serve the court.
His family was poor, and his monthly salary was several thousand, half of which was used to pay for the officials and common people who investigated and reported the situation for him.
As an official, his son once walked to the northern border to work as a guard. He was fair and honest to the point where he was fair and honest.
However, he was a serious man and liked to frame others. People in power and relatives of the emperor resented him. He also liked to ridicule political affairs and offend the emperor's will.
The emperor treated him favorably and tolerantly because he was a Confucian, but he was not promoted.
Some people who had the same position as him or who entered the officialdom later than him had already reached the rank of Jiuqing. Kuan Gao believed that he was honest, capable, and capable of making contributions to the country. However, he was even more frustrated when ordinary and mediocre people surpassed him. He wrote several memorials to remonstrate with him.
The prince's concubine Wang Sheng thought that leniency was a noble act, but he did not approve of his doing so, so he wrote to him: The wise emperor knows that you are honest, just, and not afraid of violence, so he put you in the official position in charge of reporting and granted you the power to execute the emperor's edict. You have been given high official and generous salary.
