You should think about the important tasks of the day day and night, implement laws, preach education, and share the labor and relieve the worries of the people in the world. Even if you contribute every day and make merit every month, you are still not qualified enough to repay the emperor's great kindness.
The country has been governed since ancient times, and the three generations have had different ways of governing the country.
Now it's just that you don't strive to fulfill your duties, but you want to use ancient examples to correct and assist the emperor. Several times your advice cannot be adopted or is difficult to be obeyed, and you use it to discuss with the emperor's left and right. This is not a way to spread a good name and save your life.
The people in power today are very familiar with the law. Their words are enough to distort your words, and their articles are enough to make you wrong. Instead of learning from Zang Boyu's foresight, you repeat Wu Zixu's mistakes and use your precious body to approach that unfathomable danger. I feel sad for you privately.
A gentleman is upright but not stiff; he is crooked but not yielding at all.
The Book of Songs says: Only those who understand the truth and have wisdom can protect themselves.
The saint can also choose to adopt what the mad man says.
I hope you will review the ruling.
Kuan Rao did not take his words into consideration.
At this time, the emperor was governing the country with criminal laws. He trusted the eunuchs of Zhongshangshu and handed over a sealed memorial saying: Nowadays, the tradition of saints is gradually abandoned and Confucian scholarship cannot be implemented. The intruders who have been punished by castration are regarded as the Duke of Zhou summoning the public, and the law is regarded as the "Book of Poetry".
It also quoted the "Han Shi Yi Zhuan" as saying: The five emperors regarded the world as the commonwealth, the three kings regarded the world as the family, passed on the world as the family to their descendants, and regarded the world as the commonwealth to pass on to the virtuous. Just like the movement of the four seasons, those who have accomplished something will leave, and those who are not the right person will no longer be in their place.
After sending the seal to the emperor, the emperor thought that he had not repented after all, so he handed over his memorial to Zhong Erqianshi.
At that time, Zhi Jinwu commented that Lenon's intention was to ask the emperor to abdicate, which was treason.
Zheng Chang, the admonishing doctor, had pity on Gen Geng, was loyal, upright and concerned about state affairs. Because his discussion of state affairs was not in line with the emperor's wishes, he was slandered and slandered by the officials who were eloquent. So he wrote a letter to praise Gen Geng and said: I heard that there are ferocious beasts in the mountains, so tribulations are not picked; the country has loyal ministers, so treacherous people dare not rise up.
The captain of Sili lived generously and did not seek comfort or food. He was in the imperial court but had a concern for the country. He retreated to the fields but had the loyalty to sacrifice his life for his moral integrity. He did not seek refuge with the families of Xu and Shi at the top, and did not accept the requests of Jin and Zhang at the bottom. His true duties were Supervise, insist on doing things in the right way, have many enemies and few party members, write memorials to state important national affairs, and officials impeach him on charges of serious punishment. I am fortunate to follow the doctor and hold an official position known as admonishment, and I dare not not say it.
The emperor refused to obey, so he handed over mercy to the jailer.
Kuanrao drew his sword and committed suicide at the foot of the North Tower. People all pitied him.
Zhuge Feng, whose courtesy name was Shaoji, was from Langxie.
Because he was proficient in classics, he took charge of the county's literature and was famous for his independence, strength and integrity.
Gong Yu was the imperial censor. He appointed Zhuge Feng as a subordinate official, and later recommended him to serve as the censor.
Emperor Yuan promoted him to the position of Sili Xiaowei, and he was able to avoid any investigation or prosecution. People in the capital made up a sentence for him: Why haven't we seen each other for a long time? It's just because I met Zhuge.
The emperor commended him for his integrity and awarded him the title of Doctor Guanglu.
At that time, Xu Zhang, the servant, was honored and favored by virtue of his status as a relative. He was extravagant and did not abide by the law. One of his retainers committed an offense and was implicated in Xu Zhang.
Zhuge Feng investigated Xu Zhang in accordance with the law and wanted to report his case. He happened to meet Xu Shizhong going out privately. Zhuge Feng stopped the car, raised the talisman in his hand and ordered Xu Zhang: "Come down!"
Want to arrest him.
Xu Zhang was embarrassed and drove away, with Zhuge Feng chasing him behind.
Xu Shizhong was then able to enter the palace gate and beg for mercy from the emperor.
Zhuge Feng also submitted a memorial, and at that time the emperor confiscated Zhuge Feng's talisman.
Sili's cancellation of the Talisman Festival began with Zhuge Feng.
Zhuge Feng wrote a letter to apologize and said: I am dull and cowardly. My literary side cannot encourage good deeds, and my military side cannot suppress evil deeds.
Your Majesty, you did not examine my ability, so you appointed me as the Sili Xiaowei. I have not made any contribution, and you also named me Guanglu doctor. The official position is noble and has great responsibilities. This is really not what I am suitable for.
Moreover, I am approaching my twilight years, and I often worry that I will die suddenly and be unable to repay your great kindness, causing people to ridicule me for not contributing to the country and forever being known as a freeloader.
So I often hope that I can dedicate the rest of my life, cut off the heads of traitors at any time, hang them in the market, write out their crimes, and let people from all over the world know the punishment for doing evil, so that I can retire and accept severe punishment in the future. This is indeed what I am willing to do. Scholars who are willing, like civilians, have friends who can live and die together. Nowadays, with the vastness of the world, there are no ministers who are willing to sacrifice justice. Instead, most of them are just to cater to them, just colluding with party members to do whatever they want, only caring about their own personal interests and forgetting the political affairs of the country.
The evil, filthy and turbid atmosphere touched the heavens, so disasters and accidents occurred many times, and the people were in poverty and poverty.
This is the consequence of my disloyalty, and I am truly ashamed of it.
Most people do not want to live a good life and hate danger and death. However, the reason why loyal ministers and upright people do not avoid hardship and disaster is actually for the sake of the king.
Now, Your Majesty, you are like the sky that covers all things and like the earth, you bear everything, no matter what is not tolerated, you sent the minister Yao to give me an edict saying: Si Li investigates and reports those who do not abide by the law, commends good deeds and punishes evil deeds, and is not allowed to act arbitrarily.
We must strive to implement the principle of moderation and harmony and do things according to the meaning of the scriptures. You have profound kindness. I kowtow to you and feel extremely honored.
Privately, I can't bear the worry, anger and boredom. I hope you will reward me with a leisurely life and I hope you will judge.
The emperor did not allow it.
After that, what he said was less and less accepted, and Zhuge Feng wrote again: I heard that Boqi was filial but was abandoned by his parents, Zixu was loyal but was killed by the king, Yin Gong was kind but was killed by his younger brother, Shuwu respected his elder brother but was killed by his elder brother.
With the virtues of these four people and Qu Yuan's talents, he still couldn't let himself show off and was killed instead. Isn't that enough of a lesson?
If I can give my life to stabilize the country and be killed to bring glory to the king, I am really willing to do it.
I'm afraid that it will not be beneficial to the country, but will be squeezed out by some evil forces, allowing those who blindly speak ill of people behind their backs and frame others to succeed. The path of upright people will be blocked, loyal ministers will be cold-hearted, and wise people will be silenced. This is what I am afraid of.
Zhuge Feng arrested and punished prisoners in spring and summer, and many people in power spoke ill of him.
The emperor transferred Zhuge Feng to serve as the city gate captain. Zhuge Feng wrote a letter to accuse Guanglu Xun Zhou Kan and Guanglu doctor Zhang Meng.
The emperor thought that Zhuge Feng was wrong, so he issued an edict to the censor: Zhuge Feng, the captain of the city gate school, once worked with Guanglu Xun Zhou Kan and Guanglu doctor Zhang Meng in the court. He praised the merits of Zhou Kan and Zhang Meng many times.
Zhuge Feng, a former Sili school captain, did not follow the seasons or follow the rule of law, but specialized in harsh cruelty, thus gaining false prestige. I could not bear to hand him over to the jailer, so I asked him to serve as the city gate school captain.
Instead of introspecting, he instead resented Zhou Kan and Zhang Meng, seeking revenge. His words of conviction had no evidence, he exposed crimes that were difficult to verify, and he relied solely on subjective wishes to slander and praise others, regardless of what he had said before. This was a serious act of not being trustworthy.
I pity Zhuge Feng that he is old and cannot bear to impose punishment, so I order him to be removed from his official position and become a commoner.
Zhuge Feng died at home.
Liu Fu is a member of the royal family of Hejian Kingdom.
He was promoted to Xiaolian and served as the county magistrate of Xiangbi.
He wrote a memorial to discuss the gains and losses of national affairs, and was summoned by the emperor. The emperor appreciated his talents and promoted him to the position of admonishing doctor.
Just in time when Emperor Cheng wanted to make Tang Jiandan his queen, he first issued an edict to confer the title of prince to Lin, the envoy's father.
Liu Fu wrote a letter and said: I heard that if God agrees, he will definitely give auspicious signs, and if God disagrees, he will definitely send disasters and changes. This is a sign from the gods and a natural prediction.
In the past, King Wu and Duke Zhou obeyed the will of heaven and earth, and thus received the auspiciousness of white fish and red crows. However, the monarchs and ministers were still worried, shocked, and vigilant in admonishing each other. How much more so in today's last days, when they have not received the blessing of offspring and descendants, but have repeatedly suffered disasters caused by the power and wrath of heaven?
Even if you blame yourself every day, correct your mistakes and behavior, fear the destiny, think of the achievements of your ancestors, choose a virtuous family, pray for a beautiful and capable woman to inherit the ancestral temple, comply with the will of the gods, and satisfy the wishes of the people of the world, The auspiciousness of procreating descendants, which I was worried had come too late, now triggers my affection and indulges my desires. I am devoted to this humble woman and want to regard her as the mother of all people in the world. I am not in awe of God and not ashamed of the people. There is nothing more stupid than this.
As the saying goes: Rotten wood cannot be used to make pillars, and lowly people cannot be made masters. If God and the people disapprove of it, it must be harmful but not beneficial. This is a truth that everyone in the market and on the road knows, but no one in the court is willing to tell the truth. I secretly feel sad.
I thought that because I was promoted because I have the same surname as the emperor, I only enjoyed the salary but did not show loyalty, and insulted the official position of the remonstrance. I dare not risk my life to speak out. I hope that your majesty will examine it deeply.
After the memorial was presented, the emperor sent his censor to arrest Liu Fu and imprison him in a secret prison in the harem. None of the ministers understood the reason.
At that time, the Chinese left general Xin Qingji, the right general Lian Bao, Guang Lu Xun Crocodile, and Taizhong doctor Gui Su all reported: We have heard that a wise king listens widely to opinions, pays attention to the admonition of quiet officials, opens the way for loyal and upright people, and does not punish arrogant and impatient remarks. Then all ministers keep their own positions and try their best to contribute their loyalty and wisdom. The court has no worries, there are no flattering officials in the court, and the monarch has no fault of deviating from the right path.
We have privately seen that Liu Fu, the admonishing doctor, used to meet the emperor as a county magistrate and was promoted to admonishing doctor. This shows that his opinions must be extraordinary, accurate and in line with the holy content, so he can be promoted to such a position.
However, within ten days, he was arrested and imprisoned in a secret prison. We were ignorant and thought that Liu Fu was lucky enough to be entrusted as a relative of the royal family and to be in the ranks of admonishers. He came from a lower position and did not know the imperial system. He violated taboos on his own and was not worthy of further investigation.
Small crimes should be tolerated. If there are major crimes, they should be handed over to judicial officials for public trial, so that everyone can know his crimes and punish him together.
Once upon a time, Confucius went to Jianzi to kill his doctor Mingdu. Confucius walked to the Yellow River and returned.
Nowadays, God's will is not happy, disasters are coming frequently, and floods and droughts are coming one after another. It is the time to be generous, solicit opinions widely, and praise integrity to maximize the power of the people.
However, he carried out tragic and sudden executions on ministers who dared to remonstrate, which shocked everyone and chilled the hearts of loyal and upright people.
If Liu Fu did not commit a crime because he spoke out and dared to remonstrate, then no one in the world would know about the crime he committed if he did not publicly announce it.
A minister who has the same surname as the emperor and is close to the emperor originally gained high status because he dared to tell the truth. From the perspective of dealing with relatives and protecting loyal people, he should not be secretly imprisoned in Yeting Prison.
When the ministers and officials below saw that Your Majesty was so eager to promote Liu Fu, but was so brutal in attacking and injuring him, everyone was filled with fear. Their will to be enterprising disappeared and they became weak. They no longer dared to perform their duties faithfully and uphold the right opinions. This was not the practice of Yu and Shun who listened to the opinions of his ministers and promoted good moral character.
We are privately deeply saddened by this and hope you will pay attention and review it.
The emperor then moved and imprisoned Liu Fu to the imperial prison under the control of the Shaofu, reduced the death penalty to one degree, and sentenced him to hard labor in the ancestral temple.
He is always at home.
Zheng Chong, also known as Ziyou, originally belonged to a wealthy family in Gaomi Kingdom and had been intermarrying with the Wang family for generations.
My grandfather moved to Pingling because he had money.
His father, Zheng Bin, was well versed in laws, served as a royal censor, and served Duke Gong. He was known for his fairness and uprightness.
Zheng Chong served as the literary historian of the county when he was young, and later became a chariot attendant in the Prime Minister's Mansion.
His younger brother Zheng Li and Gao Wuhou Fu Xi studied under the same teacher and were friendly to each other.
When Fu happy became the Grand Sima, he recommended Zheng Chong, and Emperor Ai promoted him to the position of Minister of Public Affairs.
He asked to see the emperor several times to remonstrate, and the emperor initially accepted his opinions.
Every time he saw him dragging his rawhide shoes, the emperor smiled and said: I can hear Zheng Shangshu's footsteps.
After a long time, the emperor wanted to knight Fu Shang, the cousin of his grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu. Zheng Chongjin advised him: Emperor Xiaocheng made five of his uncles marquis. As a result, the sky turned red and yellow, the daytime became dim, and there was black energy in the sun.
Now your grandmother's two cousins ​​have become marquises.
Marquis Kongxiang was the father of the queen; Marquis Gaowu was granted the title of Marquis based on his status as the Third Duke. It can be said that there are certain reasons for these.
Now he wants to ennoble Fu Shang for no reason, which creates havoc and disrupts the system. It goes against the will of God and people's hearts, and is not Fu Kuang's blessing.
I heard the teacher say: Those who violate Yang are extremely weak, and those who violate Yin will be short-lived and premature. Those who violate others will be in danger of disaster and destruction, and those who offend the gods will be in danger of illness and death. So the Duke of Zhou wrote a precept and said: The king who does not know the difficulties of the country and indulges in entertainment rarely can live a long life. Therefore, the king in the period of decline will die young and die prematurely, which is a disaster that violates the principles of Yin.
I would rather use my own life to resist the disaster of the country.
Zheng Chong then stood up holding the edict board.
Empress Dowager Fu said angrily: How could anyone who is the emperor be subdued by a minister?
The emperor then issued an edict saying: I became an orphan when I was young. I was raised by the emperor's wife herself. She educated me when I was a baby and taught me etiquette and justice until I grew up. I was deeply benevolent. I want to repay this kind of kindness, God, my heart is endless. In the past, the father of the Queen Mother was named Chongzu Hou. I feel very ashamed when I think that I have not repaid her kindness enough.
Fu Shang, the Guanglu doctor in the service, was the nephew of the Empress Dowager's father. The Empress Dowager raised him since he was a child, and he was the closest to him in kindness and kindness.
The order was given to seal the fort as this Danbao, let him be the descendant of Sai Lord, and changed the title of Sai Danhou to Rulu Aihou.
Zheng Chong also remonstrated with the emperor because Dong Xian was too favored by the nobles, and therefore committed a serious crime.
He was reprimanded several times for his duties, and he developed paralysis in his neck. He wanted to request that he return to his hometown for retirement, but he did not dare to complain.
The minister ordered Zhao Chang to be a treacherous and flattering person. He had always been jealous of Zheng Chong and knew that he had been alienated. Therefore, he sent a report saying that Zheng Chong was colluding with the royal family and suspected of being a treacherous person. Please investigate him.
The emperor reproached Su Sai and said: You yourself have a large family, why do you blame the emperor?
Zheng Chong replied: Although I have a court like a city, my heart is calm. I am willing to be tortured and interrogated.
The emperor was furious and imprisoned Susai for thorough investigation. Zheng Chong died in prison.
Sun Bao, whose courtesy name was Ziyan, was the founder of Tibei Jianjian. Because he was proficient in classics, he served as a county official.
The imperial censor urgently recruited Xunxuan as his subordinate, hoping that he would teach his son Confucian classics, and also arrange a house for him and set up spare utensils.
Lian Xuan himself explained his shortcomings and asked to leave. Chui Gu repeatedly tried to persuade him to stay, but he felt unconvinced in his heart.
Later, Zhang Zhong appointed Sun Bao as acting chief registrar, and Sun Shi moved into a new residence, offered sacrifices to his beloved gods, and invited his neighbors.
Zhang Zhong observed secretly and was surprised by his actions, so he sent his trusted aide to ask Sun Bao: "In the past, the imperial censor arranged a spacious residence for you. The reason why you exposed your shortcomings and asked to leave is to show your noble integrity."
Nowadays, noble people in the prime minister's and imperial censor's houses refuse to serve as chief administrators as usual, but you yourself have taken up this position and are very happy to move into the new house. Why is it inconsistent?
Sun Bao replied: "Noble people do not serve as chief registrars, but the imperial censor thinks that I can be the chief clerk. No one in the government said it is inappropriate. How can a scholar promote himself in this way?"
Not long ago, the son of the imperial censor wanted to study scriptures and asked me to move closer to his residence.
According to etiquette, only students come to the teacher to learn, and according to reason, no teacher goes to the students to teach. Teachers should not be wronged, and what harm does it do to an individual if he is wronged?
And there is nothing impossible for people who encounter bad things, let alone being the chief bookkeeper!
Zhang Zhong felt very ashamed when he heard these words, so he wrote a memorial recommending Sun Bao, saying that he was proficient in classics, had an upright character, and was suitable to serve as a close minister of the emperor.
Sun Bao was appointed Yilang and later promoted to Admonishment Officer.
During the reign of Emperor Cheng Hongjia, thieves broke out in the Guanghan area, and Sun Bao was selected as the governor of Yizhou.
Hu Shang, the prefect of Guanghan County, was the nephew of Wang Yin, the cavalry general of the Grand Sima, and was cowardly and incompetent for his position.
Sun Bao came to the area under his jurisdiction, went deep into the valley in person, and told the thieves that as long as they were not the initiators of chaos, even the leaders could surrender and be sent back to their hometowns.
Later, Sun Bao himself exposed his mistake and accused Hu Shang of being the culprit of the rebellion. According to the righteousness of "Spring and Autumn", only the culprit was punished.
Hu Shang also reported that some of the thieves released by Sun Bao were leaders who should be convicted.
Hu Shang was conscripted and imprisoned, and Sun Shi was dismissed from his post for releasing a condemned criminal.
Officials and people in Yizhou made many statements about Sun Shi's achievements, saying that he was squeezed out by the generals of chariots and cavalry.
The emperor once again worshiped Sun Bao as the governor of Jizhou, and was later promoted to prime minister Sizhi.
At that time, the emperor's uncle, Hongyang Hou Wangli, sent retainers to occupy hundreds of hectares of reclaimed land through Li Shang, the prefect of Nanjun. Many of them were hillside rivers and swamps in Shaofu that the common people had rented. Most of them had been developed. Wang Li wrote a letter to newly reclaim the land and was willing to hand it over to the government.
The emperor issued an edict asking the county government to pay Wang Li the ordinary land price, which exceeded the current price by more than 10 million yuan.
After Sun Bao heard about this incident, he sent Prime Minister Shi to verify the facts and expose their treachery. He reported and accused Wang Li and Li Shang of being treacherous and deceiving the king, and being cunning and unethical.
Li Shang was imprisoned and died.
Although Wang Li was not convicted, later his brother Wang Shang, the Great Sima Wei General, died. According to the order, he should succeed Wang Shang. The emperor passed him and appointed his younger brother Quyanghou Wang Gen as the Great Sima Hussar General.
At that time, there happened to be barbarian riots in Yizhou, and the Bashu area was very unstable. The emperor thought that Sun Shi was very prestigious in Xizhou, so he made him the governor of Guangmo, with a salary of two thousand dan and thirty kilograms of gold.
The barbarians settled down, and officials and people praised him.
Sun Shi was recruited as Jing Zhaoyin.
The former official Hou Wen was strong and upright and refused to be conciliatory. He often claimed to be ill and did not want to be an official. Sun used kindness and etiquette to invite Hou Wen and wanted to become a commoner friend with him. They would have wine and food every day, and his wife and children would accompany him.
Hou Wen asked to be appointed as a subordinate official and to be treated as a guest when he entered the mansion.
A few months later, on the day of the Beginning of Autumn, Sun Bao appointed Hou Wen to be the postal supervisor of the Ministry of Shipping.
Hou Wen entered the house to see Sun Bao, and Sun Bao asked him: "Today the falcons started fighting. We should arrest the evildoers according to the weather to complete the task of severely cracking down. Are there such people in your jurisdiction?"
Hou Wen raised his head and said: Without such a person, I would not dare to accept the position you appointed in vain. Sun Shi said: Who is it?
Hou Wen said: Du Zhiji of Ba Ling.
Sun Shi said: Who else is next?
Hou Wen said: It is not appropriate to ask the fox when the jackal is in charge.
Sun Bao was silent.
Zhiji is a great knight, and is close friends with Wei Wei Chun Yuchang, Da Honglu and Xiao Yu.
Sun Bao had offended General Chariot and Cavalry in the past and had a quarrel with Hongyang Hou, so he was afraid that he would be in danger. At that time, Chunyu Chang had just gained favor and was very friendly to Sun Bao. Sun Shi also wanted to rely on him. When he first took office, Chunyu Chang entrusted Sun Bao with Zhiji's affairs, so Sun Shi was in trouble and could not reply to Hou Wen.
Hou Wen saw that Sun Bao was dejected and felt strange. Knowing that there must be a reason, he said: "You have always been prestigious. Now you dare not take Zhiji, so you should close the door for the time being and don't interfere."
If you wait like this until the end of the year, officials and people will not dare to slander you.
If you let go of childhood and punish other things, public opinion will become uproar and your life will be ruined. Sun Shi said: Accept the advice.
Zhi Ji had many ears and eyes. After hearing about the incident, he closed the door and refused to interact with people outside. He dug through the wall behind the house to open a small door and only managed the garden with a hoe. He stated these situations himself through people who had close connections with Hou Wen.
Hou Wen said: "Zhiji and I are fortunate to be from the same hometown. We usually don't even have a small quarrel. We just accepted the order of the prefect. My duty should be to punish you."
If you can truly correct your mistakes, I will no longer pursue the past. If you don't change your mind and just change your appearance, it will only accelerate the arrival of disaster.
Zhiji finally did not dare to break the law again, and Sun Bao did not punish others throughout the year.
The next year, Zhiji fell ill and died.
Sun Bao served as Jing Zhaoyin for three years, and people in the capital praised him.
When Chunyu Chang fell, Sun Bao, Xiao Yu and others were implicated and were dismissed from office.
Hou Wen also left his official position again and died at home.
Zhiji's son Du Cang, also known as Jun Ao, was more famous among the knights than Ji Ji.
When Emperor Ai came to the throne, he recruited Sun Shi as an admonishing official, and was later promoted to Sili.
At first, Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Feng, the mother of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, served Emperor Yuan together. There was a rift between the two. Empress Dowager Fu sent officials in charge to torture Empress Dowager Feng and forced her to commit suicide. People all thought she was wronged.
Sun Bao submitted a memorial requesting for investigation. Empress Dowager Fu was furious and said: The emperor set up a secretary and sent an envoy to interrogate me.
The fact of Feng's rebellion is very clear, and some people deliberately want to find fault with me.
I want him to sit down together.
The emperor then followed the Queen Mother Fu's order and put Sun Bao in prison.
Shangshu Pushe Tang Lin argued the matter. The emperor believed that Tang Lin had formed a clique for personal gain and demoted him to the post of Dunhuang Yuzezhan Marquis.
Grand Sima Fu happy and Guanglu Doctor Gong Sheng persisted in their efforts, and the emperor interceded on their behalf with the Queen Mother, and then Sun Bao was released and his official position was restored.
Soon after, Zheng Chong was imprisoned. Sun Bao wrote a letter saying: I heard that people with distant relationships do not interfere with those who are close to each other, and outsiders do not consider other people's family affairs.
I am fortunate to be able to accept the mission and have the responsibility of prosecuting and reporting. I dare not avoid the power of the powerful and favored people to block the emperor's hearing and hearing so that the emperor does not know the true situation.
Shangshu Lingchang falsely accused his servant of shooting Zheng Chong and put him in prison for investigation and investigation. Zheng Chong was tortured to death. As a result, he did not give a confession. Even passers-by on the road said that he was unjustly accused.
I suspect that Chang and Zheng Chong have a rift, and the slanders are gradually increasing to frame each other. He is a close minister of the emperor, and he has been wronged, harming the country, and causing a lot of public criticism.
I sincerely request that Chang be punished to ease the people's sentiments.
After the report was made, the emperor was not happy. Because Sun Bao was a famous minister, the emperor could not bear to kill him, so the emperor issued an order to the prime minister and Grand Sikong: Sun Shi, the minister, reported that Zheng Chong, the former minister's servant, had been wronged, and requested that Shangshu Lingchang be imprisoned for review.
Zha Zhengchong is a minister around me, and his crimes are obvious, but Sun Shi has evil intentions, colludes with his ministers to deceive the emperor, and slanders and deceives him in the spring moon to realize his evil intentions. Isn't it said in "The Analects of Confucius"?
A person who subverts the country with his evil words and sophistry. He ordered Sun Bao to be dismissed as a civilian.
When Emperor Ai passed away, Wang Mang asked the Queen Mother to recruit Sun Shi to serve as Guanglu doctor, and went with Wang Shun and others to welcome the King of Zhongshan.
Emperor Ping ascended the throne, and Sun Bin served as chief agricultural officer.
It happened that Yuejun County reported that Huanglong was traveling in the river. Grand Master Kong Guang, Da Situ Ma Gong and others praised Wang Mang for his merits and virtues, which were comparable to those of Zhou Gong, and he should be sacrificed to the ancestral temple.
Sun Shi said: Duke Zhou is a great sage, Duke Zhao is a great sage. There were times when there was disharmony, as recorded in the scriptures, but this did no harm to either.
Nowadays, the wind and rain are unpredictable and the people are not yet rich. Whenever something happens, all the ministers agree with it. I'm afraid it's not very good.
At that time, the expressions of the ministers all changed, and Zhen Han, the captain of the imperial court, immediately ordered to stop the discussion.
It happened that Sun Shi sent officials to greet his mother. His mother fell ill on the way, so he stayed at his younger brother's house and only sent his wife and children to the capital.
Si Zhi Chen Chong made a case against Sun Bin, and the emperor handed the matter over to Sangong for interrogation on the spot.
Sun Shi replied: I am already seventy years old and my mind is confused. My affection for supporting my mother has become weak. I only care about my wife, family and children, just as the memorial said.
As a result, Sun Bao was dismissed from office and stayed at home for the rest of his life.
During the Jianwu period, virtuous ministers were appointed, and Sun Bao's grandson and his wife were appointed county magistrates of various counties.
Wu Jianglong, named Junfang, was from Lanling, Shuhai.
Wang Yin, the cavalry general of the Grand Sima, was in charge of Shangshu affairs inside the court and commanded troops and horses outside the court. Following the old practice, he selected and set up a Zhonglang to participate in the discussion and decision-making. He petitioned Wu Jianglong to be appointed Zhonglang, and was later promoted to an admonishing doctor.
In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, Wu Jianglong handed over a sealed memorial saying: In ancient times, princes were selected to serve as ministers in the imperial court in order to praise their merits. King Dingtao should be recruited and let him live in the mansion in Beijing in order to pacify the world.
After that, the emperor finally appointed King Tao as the crown prince, and Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jizhou Mu and Yingchuan Prefect.
After Emperor Ai came to the throne, Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin because of his excellent examination results, and was later promoted to Zhi Jinwu.
At that time, Dong Xian, the servant, was being favored. The emperor sent Zhong Huangmen to take out the weapons from the arsenal. There were ten batches before and after, and they were sent to the homes of Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse Wang A.
Wu Jianglong wrote in his memorial: The weapons contained in the arsenal are common to the whole world and are designed for national armament. The funds required for their repair and manufacture are all paid by Bai Dasinong.
Even the emperor's carriages, horses and utensils could not be used for expenditures in Da Sinong's funds. The emperor's offerings and rewards were all paid from the Shaofu.
The reason is that fundamental economic reserves cannot be used for unimportant expenditures, and people's financial resources cannot be used for flashy expenditures, so as to distinguish between public and private affairs and show the right way.
In ancient times, princes and magistrates could independently control the power of conquest, and the emperor gave them axes and iron. The officials on the Han border were responsible for resisting the enemy, so they were given weapons from the arsenal. They all performed such duties and then accepted these weapons.
According to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", the family of a senior official is not allowed to collect bells and armors. This is used to suppress the power of ministers and reduce personal power.
Nowadays, Dong Xian and others are either used to courting the emperor's jesters, or they are women of low status who only have personal favors, but you, the emperor, give them private things that are common to the world, and provide them with utensils that represent the majesty of the country for their private use.
The people's financial resources are distributed to jesters, weapons are placed in the homes of women of low status, and the system established is not in line with the national system, so as to condone and breed arrogance and overstep the bounds of etiquette. This cannot be used to show the world.
Confucius once said: How can the emperor's etiquette appear in the halls of three officials?
I ask that you return the weapons.
The emperor was very unhappy.
Soon after, Empress Dowager Fu sent a visitor to buy some official maids, and bought them at a very low price. She also bought eight official maids for Jinwu.
Don't tell the emperor that the price is too low and ask for a fair price.
The emperor then issued an order to the prime minister and the imperial censor, saying: If the etiquette of mutual humility prevails, then lawsuits like the one between Yu and Rui will naturally subside.
Wu Jianglong was ranked as the ninth minister, and he had no ability to correct the improper handling of the court. Instead, he petitioned Yongxin Palace to dispute the purchase and sale price, and announced the content of the petition. Everyone knew about it.
His actions and behavior were unreasonable, and the trend of fishing for fame and reputation began.
Because Wu Jianglong had previously made plans to stabilize the country, he was only demoted to the rank of captain of Peijun, and was later promoted to the prefect of Nanjun.
When Wang Mang was young, he wanted to make friends with Wu Jianglong, but Wu Jianglong didn't attach much importance to him.
After the death of Emperor Ai, Wang Mang came to power and asked the great situ Kong Guang to report Wu Jianglong's handling of the case of Empress Dowager Feng of Zhongshan when he was the shepherd of Jizhou. He wronged and framed a person who was not guilty and was not suitable to hold an official position in the central area of ​​​​the country.
In fact, it was the ministers who originally ordered Shi Li and Shi Dingxuan to investigate and interrogate the case in person. They only wrote a joint letter with Wu Jianglong to discuss the matter.
At this time, Shi Li was the servant of Zhongtai, Ding Xuan was the governor of Taishan, and Zhao Chang, the minister, who had framed Zheng Chong, was the governor of Hanoi. They were all removed from the palace and exiled to Hepu.
He Bing's courtesy name was Zilian. His grandfather moved from Pingyu to Pingling as an official with a rank of 2,000 stone.
He Bing served as a county official and became a ministerial official, serving He Wu.
He Wu believed that he had noble aspirations and moral integrity, and praised him for his ability to handle heavy government affairs, so He Bing served as the magistrate of Changling County. His political performance was so good that he was not dismissed.
Once upon a time, the Wang family of Empress Dowager Qiongcheng's maternal grandfather had a prominent position. Wang Linqing, the servant in charge, exchanged views with the Jianghu knights, and they were powerful in the capital.
Later, he was dismissed from his official position for breaking the law, and there were more and more guests. He returned to Changling to sweep the tomb, and drank with the guests for many days.
He Bing was afraid that he would break the law, so he went to see Lin Qing personally and said to Lin Qing: "The tomb is outside, you should go home in time."
Lin Qing said: Okay.
Before this, Lin Qing had killed the husband of a maidservant and buried him in a tomb. He Bing knew all about this, but he thought that the incident did not happen when he was in office, and saw that he had recently been removed from his official position, so he did not want to expose him, but just wanted him not to stay in his territory, so he sent his subordinates with business cards to send him away.
Lin Qing was always proud and did not want to embarrass himself in front of the guests, so he expected that he would cause trouble, so he arranged troops to deal with him.
After Lin Qing left, he passed the Jinghe Bridge north and asked a servant on horseback to return to the county government office, where he slashed the drum hanging on the pillar of the county government office with a knife.
He Jing personally led the officials and soldiers to chase Lin Qing.
After walking for dozens of miles, Lin Qing was desperate, so he asked his servant to put on his hat and short coat instead. He got into the car and asked the servant on horseback to follow him. He changed his clothes and ran forward from the road.
Just as the sun was going down, He Jing caught up with him and tied up the servant wearing Lin Qing's hat. The man said, "I am not a servant, just his servant."
He Bing knew that Lin Qing had escaped, so he said: The king was forced to have nowhere to hide, and he claimed to be a servant. Do you want to escape the death penalty?
So he ordered his men to cut off his head and bring it back, hang it on a broken drum, and put it under the pavilion of the city. He wrote: The former servant Wang Linqing committed murder. He buried the murdered man in the house guarding the tomb, and asked his servants to chop up the drum in front of the government office.
Officials and people were shocked and frightened.
Lin Qing then ran for his life, and people started talking, thinking that he was really dead.
Because Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng loved Lin Qing, Emperor Cheng shed tears when she heard about this incident, and told Emperor Ai about it.
Emperor Ai inquired about the situation and thought that the matter was done well, so he promoted him to be the governor of Longxi.
Later, He Bing was transferred to Yingchuan Prefecture, succeeding Yan Xiang from Lingyang.
Yan Xiang originally became an official based on his filial piety. He regarded his subordinates as teachers and friends. When he made mistakes, he would blame himself behind closed doors and never spoke much.
There was a riot in the county. Wang Mang sent people to recruit Yan Xiang. Several hundred officials gathered to prepare a farewell banquet for him. Yan Xiang fell on the ground and cried.
The subordinates said: It is a good thing that you were called up today. It should not be like this.
Yan Xiang said: I am a scholar who pities Yingchuan. I have nothing to worry about: I was recruited because of my weakness, and the court will inevitably choose a strong person to replace me.
Once the replacement arrives, there will be people who are bedridden, so it will be sad.
After Yan Xiang arrived, he was appointed as the envoy of beauty and customs.
At this time, Zhong Yuan, a native of Yingchuan, served as Shangshu Ling and concurrently as Ting Wei, handling affairs with authority and making changes.
His younger brother Zhong Wei was a subordinate of Yingchuan County and illegally hid a large amount of gold.
He Bing served as the prefect and told Zhong Tingwei about the incident when he saw him. Zhong Tingwei took off his hat and asked for a reduced death penalty for his brother, hoping to accept the punishment of crotch clamps as soon as possible.
He Bing said: The fault lies with your brother for violating the king's law, not with the prefect.
Zhong Yuan was afraid and sent Pegasus to greet his brother.
Yangdi's rangers Zhao Ji and Li Kuan supported many guests, used their strength to rob the neighbors, and even raped other people's wives and daughters. They took advantage of the officials' shortcomings and ran rampant in the county. When they heard that General He was coming, they all fled.
As soon as He Bing took office, he sought out nearly ten officials who were brave and knowledgeable about the law. He sent civilian officials to review the cases of the three people and military attachés to arrest them. Each had their own arrangements.
The order said: These three people did not fail the prefect, but violated the king's law, so they had to be punished.
Zhong Wei had committed many crimes before the amnesty, so he was driven into Hangu Pass to prevent him from harming the people. If he did not enter the pass, he would be arrested.
Zhao and Li are the chief culprits. Although they have escaped far away, they should be killed and apologize to the people.
Zhong Wei relied on his elder brother to stay in Luoyang, and the officials who pursued him killed him.
They also captured Tong and Li in other counties and brought their heads back. He then hung their heads and all the charges against them in the downtown area.
There was a peaceful and quiet situation in the county. He commended the good deeds and respected the scholars. He was well-known in Yingchuan, and his reputation was second only to Huang Ba.
How can he be honest and honest, and his wife and children are not in the government office.
Died a few years later.
When he was seriously ill, he asked his assistant to write a suicide note, saying: Tell my son Hui that I have spent a long time eating for nothing in my life. Although I will receive the legal condolence gift after my death, I do not want to receive it.
Use a small coffin for burial, as long as it can accommodate the coffin.
Bao Zheng did as his father said.
Yuling selected Hengzheng as Guan Duwei.
During the Jianda period, Tan Bing's grandson was appointed as Lang Guan.
Praise said: As a procurator, Gai Kuorao stood above the court with integrity. Even the "Director of the State" mentioned in the "Book of Songs" was nothing more than this.
If he can adopt Wang Sheng's words until he is old, he will be close to the wise ministers of ancient times.
Although Zhuge, Liu, and Zheng were somewhat arrogant and ignorant, they had unique ambitions.
Confucius said: I have never seen an upright person.
With the reputation and deeds of these people, there are still things like Wu Jianglong being stained in Jizhou and Sun Bao succumbing to Dingling Hou, let alone ordinary people?
He Bing's integrity is second only to Yin Wenggui.
summary:
Gai Kuanrao, from Weijun, rose through the ranks due to his classical knowledge and filial piety. As an imperial censor, he impeached Pengzu, son of General Zhang Anshi, for refusing to dismount at the palace gate. However, since Pengzu had actually dismounted, Kuanrao was demoted for misrepresentation. As Sima of the Guards, he reformed protocols, personally cared for soldiers' welfare, and earned such loyalty that retiring soldiers requested to serve another year. Emperor Xuan promoted him to Sili Xiaowei, where he fearlessly investigated officials, creating peace in the capital. At a celebration for Xu Bo's new residence, Kuanrao sat apart and warned about the impermanence of wealth. He later impeached a performer for disrespectful dancing. Despite his integrity and poverty—using half his salary to pay informants—his harshness and tendency to frame others created enemies. Wang Sheng advised him to be more cautious, but Kuanrao ignored this counsel. He submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor's reliance on eunuchs and suggesting that rulers should yield to the worthy. The emperor deemed this treasonous. Despite Zheng Chang's defense, Kuanrao was imprisoned and committed suicide.

Zhuge Feng, from Langxie, became Sili Xiaowei under Emperor Yuan. He attempted to arrest the favored relative Xu Zhang but was thwarted when Xu fled to the palace. The emperor confiscated Zhuge's talisman, ending the Sili's traditional authority. Zhuge apologized in a memorial but continued criticizing corrupt officials. He was transferred to city gate captain after arresting prisoners in spring and summer. When he accused former colleagues, the emperor removed him from office for untrustworthiness, and he died at home.

Liu Fu, a royal family member, became an admonishing doctor under Emperor Cheng. He opposed making Tang Jiandan queen, arguing it defied divine will. The emperor imprisoned him in a secret prison. Several high officials petitioned for his release, arguing that punishing remonstrators chilled loyal hearts. The emperor reduced his sentence to hard labor.

Zheng Chong served under Emperor Ai, known for his distinctive leather shoes. He opposed ennobling Fu Shang, the emperor's grandmother's cousin, citing precedents where such actions caused celestial disturbances. Despite the Empress Dowager's anger, Zheng persisted. He also criticized Dong Xian's excessive favor. After being alienated, he was accused of colluding with the royal family and died in prison.

Sun Bao served as Yizhou governor, quelling rebellions by offering amnesty to non-leaders. He exposed corruption involving the emperor's uncle Wang Li. As Jing Zhaoyin, he was pressured to protect the knight Du Zhiji but managed to avoid confrontation. He was dismissed when Chunyu Chang fell from power. Recalled under Emperor Ai, he investigated Empress Dowager Feng's death, angering Empress Dowager Fu, who had him imprisoned. Released after appeals, he later defended Zheng Chong but was dismissed. Under Emperor Ping, he opposed praising Wang Mang's virtues, was dismissed again, and lived in retirement.

Wu Jianglong advised Emperor Cheng to recruit the Prince of Dingtao as heir. Under Emperor Ai, he criticized giving weapons from the imperial arsenal to Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse. After Empress Dowager Fu's maid purchase dispute, he was demoted. Wang Mang later exiled him for his role in Empress Dowager Feng's case.

He Bing, as Changling magistrate, killed the fugitive Wang Linqing, who had murdered a servant. Though Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng grieved, Emperor Ai promoted He Bing. As Yingchuan prefect, he arrested criminals Zhao Ji and Li Kuan, and drove out Zhong Wei, whose brother was a powerful official. He Bing governed with integrity, his family not living in the government office. On his deathbed, he requested a simple burial.

The commentary praises Gai Kuanrao's integrity but notes he should have heeded Wang Sheng's advice. Zhuge, Liu, and Zheng had unique ambitions. Even these upright officials had flaws, showing how difficult true integrity is. He Bing's character rivaled Yin Wenggui's.

translation:
Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu and Fan.
He was young, fashionable and chivalrous, and liked cockfighting and horse racing. Later, his style changed drastically and he studied "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong.
Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he became a Yilang, and he reached the official position of Fuli Jieliang.
In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao Yuanfeng's reign, there was a roar like thousands of people coming together from the south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. When the people went to look, they saw a big stone standing up by itself. It was one foot to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight people surrounded it, and it was eight feet deep into the ground. There were three other stones as the feet of the big stone.
After the boulder stood on its own, thousands of white crows flew down and gathered around it.
At the same time, the dead trees in the Changyi Shrine and Temple came to life again, and the big willow tree that had been broken and withered and lying on the ground in Shanglin Garden actually stood up on its own and regained its vitality. There were many insects eating the leaves of the tree, and the leftover leaves were shaped like these words: Gongsun Bing has been established. Suihong then deduced the main idea of ​​"Spring and Autumn" and believed that: Stones and willows are both negative objects, symbolizing the common people at the bottom, while Mount Tai is the head of the mountains, and it is the place where emperors worshiped heaven to repay their merits after the change of dynasties.
Nowadays, big rocks stand on their own and dry willows come back to life. They are not made by human beings. Their creation shows that ordinary people will become emperors.
The resurrection of dead trees in the temple symbolizes the revival of the previously deposed Gongsun clan.
Suihong didn't know where the Gongsun family was, so he said: My ancestor Dong Zhongshu once said that even if there is a monarch who succeeds the emperor and abides by virtue, it will not prevent the saint from receiving orders from heaven.
The Han family is a descendant of Yao, and they are destined to pass on their surname to the country. Emperor Mo should tell the world about it.
He solicited talented people and abdicated the throne to him, while he abdicated and granted a land of hundreds of miles, just like the descendants of King Zhou of Yin, in order to obey the destiny.
Suihong asked his friend who was an internal official to write this book for him.
At that time, Emperor Zhao was still very young, and the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government. Huo Guang hated this very much, so he handed Suihong's memorial to Tingwei.
Huo Guang sent a memorial to Ci and Sui Hong, who deceived the public with their demonic words and committed treason. Both of them were sentenced to death.
Five years later, Emperor Xiaoxuan rose from the ranks of the people and ascended the throne, so he recruited Suihong's son as Lang.
Xiahou Shichang was from Lu.
Proficient in the Five Classics, he teaches Qi Shi and Shangshu.
After the deaths of Dong Zhongshu and Han Ying, Emperor Wu paid great attention to Xiahou Shichang.
Shichang knew the way of yin and yang. He once predicted the date when a fire would break out in Bailiang Terrace, and it turned out that a fire broke out on that day.
At that time, King Changyi was favored because he was the youngest. Emperor Wu chose a teacher for him, and Shichang became a tutor.
Shichang died of old age.
Xia Housheng, the son of his brother, was also famous as a Confucian scholar.
Xiahou Sheng's courtesy name is Chang Gong.
When the King of the Communist Party of Lu granted Ningxiang in western Lu to his son Jiehou, Ningxiang belonged to Dahe. Dahe was later renamed Shuping, so Xiahou Sheng was from Shuping.
Xia Housheng lost his father when he was young, but he was very studious. He studied "Shang Shu" and "Hong Fan's Five Elements" with Shi Chang, and discussed disasters and strange phenomena.
Later, he studied under Jian Qing and then studied under Ouyang.
Xia Housheng was sophisticated and proficient in learning, and he studied under more than one person.
Xia Housheng is good at telling the ceremony of dress.
He was recruited as a doctor and Guanglu doctor.
At this time, Emperor Zhao died and King Changyi succeeded to the throne. King Changyi often traveled.
One time, Xia Housheng blocked the carriage of the King of Changyi and came forward to remonstrate: "It has been overcast for a long time without raining, which may lead to some ministers plotting against the emperor. Where else is your majesty going to go?"
The king of Changyi was furious and said that Xia Housheng was deceiving the public with his evil words, so he tied him up and handed him over to the officials.
The official reported the incident to the general Huo Guang, but Huo Guang did not punish Xiahou Sheng.
At this time, Huo Guang and the cavalry general Zhang Anshizheng were discussing how to depose the king of Changyi.
Huo Guang blamed Zhang Anshi for leaking the truth, but in fact An Shi did not leak it.
So Xia Housheng was interrogated, and Xia Housheng replied: "The Biography of Hong Fan" says that if an emperor does not rule according to the rules, he will be punished by the constant evil. At this time, there will be a crusade against him by the subordinates. It is just because the taboo is so obvious, so it is only said that there are ministers plotting against the emperor.
Huo Guang and An Shi were both shocked, and they valued Confucian scholars even more from then on.
More than ten days later, Huo Guang and An Shi finally petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan.
Huo Guang believed that the ministers reported political affairs to the East Palace and the Queen Mother inspected government affairs, so they should understand the classics, so he asked Xia Housheng to teach the Queen Mother "Shangshu".
After Xiahou's victory, he was appointed as the Shaofu of Changxin and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei. He participated in the planning of the abolition of the establishment and the major decision-making of the ancestral temple and the country. Later, he was added to the food fiefdom of a thousand households.
As soon as Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he wanted to praise Emperor Wu's achievements. Prime Minister Xuan Shao said: In my humble status, I have received the kindness of my ancestors, inherited the saint's career, and worshiped the ancestral temple. I dare not forget it day and night.

Those below who serve as officials, have nothing special to do and are not knowledgeable, and those who have no literary talents among the doctors should be sent back and let them engage in agriculture. This will show the world that the court is full of virtuous and gentlemen, so that the people will pay attention to the court and respect the king, and eliminate evil disasters to bring peace and tranquility. This is fundamental.
I know that what I said is very harmful to myself, but I still risk my life to speak out. I hope you can listen to my opinion and consider my words again and again.
At this time, Emperor Ai had just ascended the throne, and Emperor Cheng's cousin Wang had not yet been deposed. Emperor Ai's relatives Ding and Fu had just become honored. Grandmother Fu was especially arrogant and wanted to claim the honorary title.
Prime Minister Kong Guang and Grand Sikong Shidan were in power and tried their best to dissuade her. After a long time, the emperor had no choice but to dismiss Kong Guang and Shidan and honor the Queen Mother Fu.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Shi Dan".
Although the emperor did not act according to Li Xun's words, he accepted his words and would ask Li Xun whenever he encountered something special.
Li Xun's answer was fulfilled many times, and he was promoted to Huangmen Minister.
According to Li Xun's words, there would be floods, so he appointed Li Xun as the Cavalry Captain and asked him to guard the river embankment.
When he became emperor, Gan Zhongke, a native of Qi, forged twelve volumes of "Tianguan Calendar" and "Bao Yuan Taiping Jing", saying that the Han family was at the end of heaven and earth and should be re-empowered by heaven. The emperor of heaven sent the real person Chi Jingyu to go down to the heaven to teach me the art of Taoism.
Therefore, Zhongke taught Zhongping Xia Heliang, Rongqiu Dingguangshi, Dongjun Guochang and others. Zhongke Colonel Liu Xiangxiang reported that Zhongke used ghosts and gods to deceive the king and confuse everyone, so he was thrown into prison and sentenced to death. He died of illness before execution.
He Liang and others were also implicated, and were punished with disrespect for studying Zhongke Shu. Later, He Liang and others discussed and taught each other in private again.
When Emperor Ai just came to the throne, Lieutenant Jie Guang of Sili was also favored because he was proficient in classics and knew about disasters and disasters. He wrote a letter saying that He Liang and others still had a book of loyalty.
This matter was reported to Liu Xin, the captain of Fengche. Liu Xin believed that it was inconsistent with the Five Classics and could not be implemented.
And Li Xun also likes these.
Jie Guang said: In the past, Liu Xin's father Liu wrote to Zhong Ke to be imprisoned. How could Liu Xin be willing to give them this convenience?
Guo Chang was the county magistrate of Chang'an at that time and persuaded Li Xun to help He Liang and others.
Li Xun then wrote to He Liang and others to stay at Shaohuangmen. He was summoned several times and told by Chen Mo that his fate had declined and that he should be reassigned.
Becoming an emperor was not in line with destiny, so he had no descendants.
Now His Majesty has been ill for a long time, and accidents and disasters are frequent. This is God's warning to people.
The Yuan Yi name should be changed immediately to prolong life. As soon as the prince is born, the disaster will subside.
If you know the Tao but cannot practice it, you will definitely be in trouble and will perish. Otherwise, floods will come, fires and other disasters will also occur, leaving the people in dire straits.
Emperor Ai had been bedridden for a long time, hoping that it would be really beneficial, so he listened to the opinions of He Liang and others.
So he issued an edict to the Prime Minister and the Censor: I heard that there is a saying in "Shangshu": "Test one's destiny in five days." This means that once the destiny and great fortune are over, it is necessary to re-record the beginning of heaven and earth and the beginning of the human world.
I inherited Taizu's great cause with my humble body, obeyed the emperor's orders, commanded the princes and ministers, and nurtured the people of Ming Dynasty, but I failed to achieve the results of obeying the will of heaven.
In the nearly three years since he took the throne, many disasters and accidents have occurred. The sun and the moon have lost their regularity, the stars have become disordered, landslides have occurred, water has dried up, major disasters have occurred frequently, and thieves have appeared one after another.
I am very worried and trembling, fearing that the country will gradually weaken and perish.
Thinking that it has been two hundred years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the fortune of the country has begun again, the emperor has given me grace to protect me, and the country has regained the fortune to bear the destiny of heaven. Although I have no saintliness, how dare I not obey and accept the great destiny of heaven. We must work with the people of the world to eliminate the old and establish the new.
I hereby decree a general amnesty for the whole world, and regard the second year of Jianping as the first year of Taichu. My title is Emperor Chen Sheng and Liu Taiping.
The scale of the clepsydra is divided into one hundred and twenty degrees.
Announce it to the world and let everyone know clearly.
More than a month passed after this, and the emperor was still ill.
He Liang and others wanted to make random changes in political affairs, but the ministers advised the emperor that they could not allow it.
He Liang and others reported that the ministers did not know the destiny, so they should dismiss the prime minister and censor, and use Jie Guang and Li Xun to assist the government.
Because what they said before had no effect, the emperor handed He Liang and others over to the law enforcement officials and issued an edict saying: I can succeed to the throne and protect the ancestral temple, but my governance is poor and disasters occur frequently. I am worried and afraid, and I don't know what to do.
After the edict, He Liang and others suggested that changing the name of the Yuan Dynasty and increasing the scale of the clepsydra would make the country more stable for a long time.
I did not believe in the teachings of the saints and misunderstood their words, hoping to seek blessings for the people.
But in the end there was no good effect, and the long-term drought caused disaster.
He questioned He Liang and others about this, and they replied that the system should be changed again. Everything he said deviated from the meaning of the scriptures, violated the system of the saints, and was inappropriate for the times.
Making a mistake and refusing to correct it is the real mistake.
All the edicts issued on Jiazi Day in June were abolished except for the Amnesty Day Order.
He Liang and others have deviated from the truth and confuse the public with their evil words. Their crimes must be thoroughly investigated.
They were all imprisoned. Guanglu Xunping, Guanglu doctor Mao Moru, Yushi Zhongcheng and Tingwei jointly tried the case and sentenced He Liang and others to use evil ways to disrupt the government, subvert the country, deceive the emperor and commit treason.
He Liang and others were all killed.
Li Xun's crime was reduced to one level and he was exiled to Dunhuang County.
Praising: "Book of Changes" and "Spring and Autumn" should be recommended first among those who can profoundly explain the supernatural powers of gods and understand the way of heaven and man.
However, Zigong still said: We can hear the Master's articles, but we cannot hear the Master's remarks about sex and the way of heaven.
Since the founding of the Han Dynasty, those who have speculated on the differences between yin and yang in discussing disasters include Dong Zhongshu and Xiahou Shichang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu; Suimeng and Xiahou Sheng during the reigns of Emperors Zhao and Xuan; Jingfang, Yifeng, Liu Xiang, and Gu Yong during the reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng; and Li Xun and Tian Zhongshu during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping.
These are some of the famous figures whose theories were adopted by the monarchs of the time.
Looking at what they said, it seems to be exactly the same.
Under the guise of borrowing scriptures and relying on anomalies in celestial phenomena to discuss the gains and losses of political affairs, sometimes it is unavoidable to make repeated guesses.
Zhongshu was imprisoned by officials, Xiahou was imprisoned, Suimeng was brutally killed, and Li Xun was exiled. These are all things that scholars should take as a warning.
As a young official in the capital, he disregarded his safety and spoke frankly to satirize the current affairs, offending the treacherous ministers in power. Although the disaster of death soon came, it was also because of his imprudent speech that he died tragically. How sad!
summary:
Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu. Initially fond of cockfighting and horse racing, he later transformed his character and studied the "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong. Through his mastery of Confucian classics, he became a Yilang and reached the position of Fuli Jieliang.

In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao's Yuanfeng reign, a great roar was heard south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. A large stone stood up by itself, measuring one to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight arm spans, and eight feet deep into the ground, with three other stones serving as its feet. Thousands of white crows gathered around it. Simultaneously, dead trees in the Changyi Shrine revived, and a broken willow in Shanglin Garden stood up and regained life, with insects eating its leaves into shapes resembling the words "Gongsun Bing has been established." Suihong interpreted these events through the "Spring and Autumn," concluding that stones and willows symbolized common people, while Mount Tai represented the site of imperial ceremonies. He argued that these phenomena indicated commoners would become emperors and the deposed Gongsun clan would revive. He advocated for the Han emperor to abdicate in favor of a worthy successor. His friend, an internal official, submitted this memorial. Since Emperor Zhao was young and General Huo Guang governed, Huo Guang was angered and had Suihong and his friend executed for treason. Five years later, when Emperor Xiaoxuan rose from the people to the throne, he recruited Suihong's son as a Lang.

Xiahou Shichang, from Lu, was proficient in the Five Classics and taught Qi Shi and Shangshu. After Dong Zhongshu and Han Ying died, Emperor Wu valued him greatly. Shichang understood yin and yang, once predicting the exact date of a fire at Bailiang Terrace. He served as tutor to King Changyi and died of old age. His nephew Xiahou Sheng, courtesy name Changgong, was also a renowned Confucian scholar. Xiahou Sheng lost his father young but studied diligently, learning "Shang Shu" and "Hong Fan's Five Elements" from Shichang, and later studied under Jian Qing and Ouyang. He was sophisticated and learned from multiple teachers.

When King Changyi succeeded Emperor Zhao, he frequently traveled. Xiahou Sheng once blocked the king's carriage to remonstrate, warning that prolonged overcast weather without rain indicated ministers plotting against the emperor. The king was furious and had him bound, but Huo Guang did not punish him. When Huo Guang and Zhang Anshi were discussing deposing the king, Xiahou Sheng explained his prediction came from the "Hong Fan" biography, which stated that when an emperor rules improperly, subordinates will rebel. Huo Guang and Anshi were impressed and valued Confucian scholars more thereafter. They eventually petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan. Xiahou Sheng was appointed Shaofu of Changxin and given the title of Marquis of Guannei.

When Emperor Xuan wanted to honor Emperor Wu's achievements, Xiahou Sheng opposed, arguing that although Emperor Wu defeated barbarians and expanded territory, he killed many ministers, exhausted resources, and caused widespread suffering and cannibalism. The ministers impeached Xiahou Sheng for slandering the late emperor, and he was imprisoned. After an earthquake killed over six thousand people, Emperor Xuan issued a general amnesty, and Xiahou Sheng was pardoned and served as an admonition official. He was known for his forthrightness, addressing the emperor as "king" and calling colleagues by name in court. Emperor Xuan trusted him for this honesty. Xiahou Sheng died in office at ninety, and the Queen Mother mourned him for five days.

Jingfang, courtesy name Junming, studied "The Book of Changes" under Jiao Yanshou. Jiao Gan, his teacher, was known for predicting evil events and governing Xiaohuang County well. Jingfang was particularly skilled in connecting hexagrams with daily events and using meteorological changes as symptoms. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he predicted events accurately and was frequently consulted. He warned about disasters and criticized the appointment of flattering officials like Shi Xian. Jingfang recommended implementing a system to inspect officials' performance, but faced opposition from powerful ministers. He was eventually appointed prefect of Wei County but feared being isolated from the emperor. After sending several sealed memorials warning about yin energy overwhelming yang and predicting disasters, he was imprisoned and executed at age forty-one.

Yi Feng, courtesy name Shaojun, studied "Qi Shi" and was diligent in learning, preferring calendar and yin-yang divination to officialdom. Emperor Yuan respected him greatly. Yi Feng wrote extensively about using the twelve laws to understand human emotions and predict disasters. He warned about the dangers of powerful relatives and advocated for frugality, criticizing excessive palace construction. He proposed moving the capital to Chengzhou to reform institutions and reduce expenses. Although Emperor Yuan found his views unusual, Yi Feng became a doctor and admonishing official, dying in old age.

Li Xun, courtesy name Zichang, studied "Shangshu" and liked theories of disasters and strange phenomena. He served under various officials and warned about impending floods and chaos. During Emperor Ai's reign, he was summoned to discuss disasters and advised restraining relatives, selecting virtuous officials, and following seasonal orders. He later supported Gan Zhongke's forged texts about the Han dynasty's fate declining, advocating for changing the reign name to prolong the dynasty. Emperor Ai, ill for a long time, agreed and issued an edict changing the reign name to Taichu. When this had no effect, He Liang and others were executed for treason, and Li Xun was exiled to Dunhuang County.

The historian's commentary notes that since the Han dynasty's founding, those who discussed disasters and yin-yang differences included Dong Zhongshu, Xiahou Shichang, Suimeng, Xiahou Sheng, Jingfang, Yifeng, Liu Xiang, Gu Yong, Li Xun, and Tian Zhongshu. Their theories were sometimes adopted by rulers but often led to imprisonment or death. Suimeng was brutally killed, and Li Xun was exiled—warnings for scholars who spoke frankly about current affairs, offending powerful ministers and meeting tragic ends.
