Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan.
His family has been humble and humble for generations. Fang Jin's father Zhai Gong was fond of learning and served as a county scholar.
When Fang Jin was twelve or thirteen years old, his father died and he could no longer continue his studies. He worked as a minor historian in the prefect's mansion. He was considered slow and could not do good things, and was repeatedly scolded and insulted by the governor.
Fang Jin was very sad, so he went to meet Cai's father in Runan and asked him what he was suitable for.
Cai's father thought that his appearance was unusual and told him: You have the bone image of a feudal lord. You should use it according to the classics and study the knowledge of Confucian scholars.
Fang Jin was tired of being a minor historian. After hearing what Cai's father said, he felt very happy, so he returned home saying he was ill, said goodbye to his stepmother, and wanted to go west to the capital to study scriptures.
His mother felt pity for Fang Jin when he was young, so she came to Chang'an with him, knitted shoes for him to study, and taught him "Spring and Autumn" by a doctor.
After more than ten years of accumulation and study, he became proficient in Confucian classics, and his number of disciples increased day by day, and all the Confucian scholars praised him.
Take Shece Jiake as the man.
Two or three years later, he was promoted to Mingjing and moved to Yilang.
At this time, there was a mature and knowledgeable scholar Hu Chang from Qinghe, who was studying the same classics as Fang Jin.
Hu Chang was a senior, but his reputation was not as good as Fang Jin's. He was jealous of Fang Jin's talent, and did not praise Fang Jin when discussing.
After Fang Jin knew about it, he waited for Hu Chang to gather his students to give lectures, and sent students under his disciples to Hu Chang's place to ask for advice on difficult issues in the scriptures, and record Hu Chang's teachings accordingly.
After such a long time, Hu Chang felt uneasy knowing that Fang Jin respected and humbled him. From then on, he was known as Fang Jin among the scholar-bureaucrats, and they became close friends.
During the Heping period, Fang Jin became a doctor.
A few years later, he was moved to Shuofang as governor. When serving as an official, he is not cumbersome and harsh, and his observations are carried out in an orderly manner, which is very prestigious.
He reported to the imperial court many times and was moved to the position of Prime Minister Sizhi.
He followed Emperor Cheng to Ganquan and drove on the Chi Road. Chen Qing, the captain of Sili School, impeached him, so Fang Jin had his carriage and horses confiscated.
After arriving at Ganquan Palace, they gathered in the palace and talked with Chen Qing and Tingwei Fan Yanshou. At that time, Chen Qing was being impeached by a memorial. Chen Qing said himself: "What happened in the past should be punished as a crime. Now that the Minister has come with a memorial to impeach me, the verdict should be wrapped up here."
When I was a minister, I had something to report, but I suddenly forgot about it and put it aside for more than a month.
Fang Jin therefore impeached Chen Qing and said: Chen Qing was ordered to investigate and expose the ministers, so he was the minister. He understood that confidential matters were carefully arranged and planned, and the Ming Lord personally handled them without slacking off.
Chen Qing was guilty but did not punish him. He was not afraid of it and set up an example of not convicting him in advance.
Moreover, he leaked the information about promoting the minister, saying that speed does not matter, which undermines the wisdom and wisdom of Shengde, and is not careful in following the edict. These are all disrespectful manifestations, and I would like to impeach him for this.
Chen Qing was dismissed from his official post.
It happened that Haoshang from the North was arrested by the county magistrate of Yiqu and later fled. The magistrate captured his mother and tied her with the boar under the capital pavilion.
A guest at the Haoshang Brotherhood Conference, claiming to be Sili Peng and Chang'an County Lieutenant, killed six of the wife and children of the Yiqu County Magistrate and then escaped.
The prime minister and the imperial censor requested that the governor, the commander of the Sili school, and the governor of the ministry be sent to jointly hunt down the person and find out the person who had committed an unspeakable crime.
Juanxun, the captain of the Sili School, reported: According to the classics and meanings of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the king's humble official position is ranked above the official positions of the princes, which means respecting the king's order.
I was fortunate enough to accept the mission, with the responsibility of supervising and inspecting officials below the rank of minister. Now Prime Minister Xue Xuan has requested to send a censor to let the prime minister's subordinate officials supervise and inspect the emperor's ministers. This is very contrary to the principle of disobedience.
Xue Xuan originally did not have a teacher to learn Confucianism, so he relied on his ministry to establish his prestige. Looking at what Haoshang did, it was nothing more than a disaster to the family, but Xue Xuan wanted to be authoritarian because of this, which was harmful to our country and did the last thing he should have done.
It is hoped that the matter will be handed over to officials below the level of Zhongko, Tejin, Liehou, and General to rectify the country's legal system.
Commentators believed that it was not appropriate for the Prime Minister to send documents to supervise the ministers.
It happened that Haoshang was arrested and executed. His family was moved to Hepu.
According to the old practice, the position of Sili Xiaowei was below Sizhi. When he was newly appointed, he met the Prime Minister and the Censor. During the court meeting, the Sili Xiaowei was in front of Zhong Erqian Shi, and he and Sizhi welcomed the Prime Minister and the Censor.
At the beginning, Fang Jin had just taken up his post, and Wu Xun had recently been appointed as Sili, so he refused to meet the prime minister and the imperial censor. Later, when they met at court, the etiquette was very arrogant.
Fang Jin secretly observed him and found that Juanxun visited Guangluxun and Xin Qingji privately. He went out again and met his uncle Hou Shang of Chengdu on the road. He got off the car and stood aside, waiting for Wang Shang to pass before getting in the car.
Therefore, Fang Jin reported Juan Xun's crime and said accordingly: I heard that the revitalization of the country lies in respecting the elders and observing the etiquette of the nobles. This is the law and discipline of the king.
According to the scriptures and meanings of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Lord is respected as the Prime Minister, and everything in the country is under his command.
When the prime minister comes to see the emperor, the emperor should stand up from his seat; when the emperor is on the way, when the prime minister pays homage, the emperor should get off the car.
All ministers should accept the teachings of the Holy Dynasty and inform the world.
However, Juanxun was an official with two thousand stones. He was fortunate enough to be sent on an envoy, but he did not abide by the etiquette. He looked down upon the prime minister and despised the minister. He also distorted etiquette and lost his grace. He was treacherous and flattering and had no normal heart. He was dignified in appearance and cowardly in heart.
Those who destroy the dignity of the country and disrupt the order of the court should not hold official positions.
I request the Prime Minister to dismiss Juan Dong.
At that time, Taizhong doctor Ping was in charge of the affairs. He reported that Fang Jin was the minister of the country. He did not first correct himself to set an example for others. He had previously violated the law and drove on the road. Chen Qing, the minister, tried to impeach him fairly. Fang Jin did not feel guilty or regretful but harbored personal hatred. He recorded Chen Qing's chatting words in order to slander and deceive him and convict him.
Later, Prime Minister Xue Xuan asked to send a military official to supervise Sili Xiaowei because of a bad guy who killed six innocent family members. Sili Xiaowei Juanxun himself submitted a memorial to the court, and now Fang Jin impeached Juanxun again.
Commentators believe that Fang Jin does not use morality to assist the prime minister, but only favors and helps ministers. If he wants to win and establish authority, this source should be stopped and cut off.
Juanxun has always acted fairly and upright, and is disgusted by traitors. You can be a little tolerant and let him achieve his fame.
Because the emperor's impeachment by Fang Jin was appropriate, he could not abolish the law just because he suspected others of fraud in advance, so he demoted Juanxun to the rank of Changling Order.
Fang Jin dismissed two ministers in one year, and everyone in the court was afraid of him.
Prime Minister Xue Xuan valued Fang Jin very much and often warned the minister: "Serve Si Zhi with caution, and Zhai Fangjin will definitely be in power soon."
At this time, Changling was being built and the imperial mausoleums and cities were being built. Many of the emperor's internal and external relatives and the children and guests of his close ministers had exclusive power for personal gain. Fang Jin arranged for a historical inspection and revealed that tens of millions of filthy items had been secretly hidden.
The emperor believed that he was qualified for the position of public minister and wanted to use him to govern the people. He transferred him to the position of Jing Zhaoyin. Fang Jin attacked the powerful and powerful, and everyone in the capital was afraid of him.
At that time, Hu Chang was the governor of Qingzhou. When he heard about this, he wrote to Fang Jin: I heard privately that your decrees are very strict. With Jing Zhaoyin's talents, I am afraid that he will feel uncomfortable.
Fang Jin knew in his heart what Hu Chang was referring to, and then relaxed his dignity a little.
Fang Jin served as Jingzhaoyin for three years, and was promoted to imperial censor in the second year of Yongshi.
A few months later, Prime Minister Xue Xuan happened to be exempted from being a civilian because of the riots caused by thieves in the vast desert and the three auxiliary officials of Zha during the funeral of the Empress Dowager.
Fang Jin was also demoted to Zhijinwu because he was ordered to hold funerals when he was appointed Jingzhao Yin and disturbed the people.
Twenty days later, the official position of prime minister became vacant. Most of the ministers recommended Fang Jin. The emperor also valued Fang Jin's talents, so he promoted Fang Jin to be prime minister and made him the Marquis of Gaoling, granting him a land of thousands of households.
Fang Jin was already rich, but his stepmother was still alive. He paid attention to cultivating family conduct and worshiped his mother very piously and generously.
When his stepmother passed away and was buried twenty-six days later, he took off his funeral clothes and started working. He believed that as the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, he did not dare to go beyond the country's system.
As prime minister, he was impartial and honest, and did not ask the four counties and counties for personal matters.
The law is strict and strict, and the ministers and ministers are reported to the nine ministers. The laws are strict and detailed and are deeply slandered. There are many people who conspire to frame him.
People such as Chen Xian, Zhu Bo, Xiao Yu, Feng Xin, and Sun Hong all came from aristocratic families in the capital. Because of their talents, they served as ministers at a young age and were very famous at that time. However, Fang Jin came from behind because of his outstanding performance and was promoted to prime minister in more than ten years. Chen Xian and others were impeached according to the law, and they were all dismissed.
Previously, Chen Xian was the first to become an official, and he had become famous in the court since he was appointed as the censor in the early years of Emperor Yuan.
As soon as Emperor Cheng came to the throne, he was promoted to the governor of the Ministry, and successively served as the prefect of Chu, Beihai, and Shujun.
During the Yangshuo period, Jingzhao Yin Wangzhang was deeply responsible for the ministers, and recommended Feng Yewang, the prefect of Langye, to be suitable to replace the general Wang Feng to assist the government, and Chen Xian, the prefect of Shujun, to be the imperial censor.
At this time, Fang Jincai was appointed as governor from doctor.
Later, Fang Jin served as Jing Zhaoyin, and Chen Xian entered the imperial court from Nanyang Prefecture as Shaofu, and was very close to Fang Jin.
Previously, Fengxin had served as the governor of Gaodi County, Jingzhaoyin, Taipu, and Weiwei. His achievements and qualifications as an official were superior to Fang Jin's.
When the official post of imperial censor became vacant, Chen Xian, Fang Jin, and Feng Xin, all famous ministers, were all on the list of candidates, and Fang Jin got the official post.
It happened that Prime Minister Xue Xuan had something to do with Fang Jin, so the emperor sent two thousand stone and five people to jointly interrogate the prime minister and the censor. Chen Xian blamed Fang Jin, hoping to get his position as censor, so Fang Jin held a grudge.
Previously, General Wang Feng petitioned to appoint Chen Tang as Zhonglang, and all political matters were done after discussing with Chen Tang.
After Wang Feng's death, his cousin, Chariot and Cavalry General Wang Yin, replaced Wang Feng to assist the government, and he also valued Chen Tang.
Feng Xin and Chen Xian were both friendly with Chen Tang, and Chen Tang also repeatedly praised Feng Xin and Chen Xian in front of Wang Feng and Wang Yin.
A long time later, Wang Yin died, and Wang Feng's younger brother, Hou Shang of Chengdu, was appointed as General Sima Wei to assist the government.
Wang Shang had always hated Chen Tang, so he reported his crimes. The emperor asked Yousi to investigate and confirm, then dismissed Chen Tang and exiled him to Dunhuang.
At that time, Fang Jin was the new prime minister. Chen Xian was frightened and uneasy, so he ordered Xiaoguan Du Zixia to detect Fang Jin's intentions and secretly defend himself.
After Zixia visited Fang Jin, he found out Fang Jin's intentions and did not dare to speak for Chen Xian.
Not long after, Fang Jin reported that Chen Xian and Feng Xin were evil, corrupt and selfish.
They all knew that Chen Tang was treacherous, flattering, capricious, and eloquent and eloquent, but they still kept close contact with him and gave him money and gifts to seek his recommendation.
They later became Shaofu and donated property to Chen Tang many times.
Feng Xin and Chen Xian were lucky enough to be among the nine ministers. They did not want to be loyal and upright, and they knew in their hearts that improper behavior would have no effect. However, they flattered evil ministers in order to gain relatives and favors, and they were so harsh that they lost their integrity.
Confucius said: Can such a person serve the king with him?
I’m talking about Chen Xian and Feng Xin.
Their mistakes and evils have been revealed and they are no longer suitable for holding official positions. I request that they be removed to make it known to the world.
The emperor agreed.
More than two years later, the emperor issued an edict to recommend talents with Fang Zhengyan. Hongyang Marquis recommended Chen Xian to respond to policy questions. The emperor appointed Chen Xian as Guanglu doctor to Shizhong.
Fang Jin reported again: Chen Xian's former name was Jiu Qing, and he was dismissed because of his corrupt behavior. He himself knew that his crimes were exposed, and he was lucky enough to get the job thanks to Hongyang Houli, but no one dared to report him.
Chen Xian was corrupt, harsh and allowed to live in the world. He did not care about the shame. He should not accept Fang Zheng's recommendation and only occupied the position of minister in the inner dynasty.
Moreover, Hongyang Houli was impeached for deliberately not following the truth when selecting and recommending talents.
The emperor issued an edict to remove Chen Xian, but ordered not to impeach him.
A few years later, Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, the son of the Empress Dowager's sister, was found guilty. Because of the Empress Dowager, the emperor removed Chun Yuchang from his official position but did not punish him.
A senior official requested that Chun Yuchang be sent to his county. Chun Yuchang bribed Li with money and immediately submitted a sealed memorial to Chun Yuchang, requesting him to stay. He said: Your Majesty has already issued a Shao letter because of the empress dowager. You really can't have any other plan.
Later, Chunyu Chang was arrested and imprisoned because his secret affairs were exposed.
Fang Jin impeached Li for being treacherous, disrupting the government, trying to subvert and threaten the emperor, being cunning and unethical, and asked the emperor to sentence him to prison.
The emperor said: "Hongyang Hou is my uncle. I can't bear to use legal sanctions, so I send him to the county."
So Fang Jin went to Li's cronies again and said: "Li has always done many bad things, and everyone knows that."
The evil ministers took it upon themselves to collude with him and become close friends with him. They hoped that Li Neng would participate in political affairs and gain personal gain.
Now that he has been expelled to the county, the people he has close relationships with are not suitable to serve as ministers or county guards.
After the inspection, General Zhu Bo, Julu Prefect Sun Gui, and former Guanglu doctor Chen Xian became close friends and became each other's confidants. They had a pact to become buddies against justice and wanted to support each other until death; they all harbored inner feelings. He has an unkind character, but has outstanding intelligence, surpasses everyone, is brave and courageous, and does not hesitate in doing things. He usually advocates cruelty, cruelty, cruelty, and violence, and relies on cruelty and viciousness to establish prestige, without any intention of benevolence and benefit.
Everyone in the world knows it, and even fools are confused.
Confucius said: What should I do if I employ people without courtesy?
What should I do if I employ people who are not benevolent?
This means that people without benevolence and righteousness are of no use to the country. People without benevolence and righteousness who are very talented are a disaster for the country.
These three people are all treacherous and cunning, which is a concern for the country, but they are deeply colluded with each other to win the trust of noble relatives and treacherous ministers. This is a great worry for the country, and it is something that ministers should sacrifice their lives to admonish. In the past, Ji Sunxing's father once said: When you see someone who is good for you, you love him, just like a filial son who supports his parents, and when he sees someone who is disadvantageous, he attacks him, just like an eagle chasing away birds.
Even if the eagle's wings are injured, it will not escape.
It is indeed difficult to offend a noble relative's close friends. If they are offended, all the enemies will be resentful, and good and evil will cover up each other.
I am fortunate enough to serve as prime minister, and I dare not not do my best.
Ask the emperor to remove Zhu Bo, Sun Hong, and Chen Xian and return them to their former counties to eliminate the evil gangs and cut off the hope of the evil gangs.
The emperor is ready to play.
Chen Xian had been dismissed from office and prohibited from holding office again. He was sent back to his hometown and died of illness due to worry and anger.
Fang Jin was rich in knowledge and talent, and he also knew the law and officials. He decorated the law with elegant writing and was called the Tongming Prime Minister. Situ Peng Ban Biao said: Prime Minister Fang Jin took his mother to live in the capital when he was a child. As a master of Confucian scholars, he eventually became prime minister and became very prominent.
When Wang Mang raised his troops. Probably through the power of heaven, even with the bravery of Meng Ben and Xia Yu, what help would it be to fight against the enemy?
Zhai Yi overestimated his capabilities and started an uprising out of loyalty, but ended up destroying the entire family. How sad!
summary:
Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan, born into a humble family. After his father died when he was twelve or thirteen, he worked as a minor historian but was often scolded. Seeking guidance, he consulted Cai's father in Runan, who noted his noble bone structure and advised him to study Confucian classics. Inspired, he feigned illness, left his job, and traveled to Chang'an with his stepmother, who supported him by knitting shoes. He studied the "Spring and Autumn Annals" under a doctor, and over a decade became proficient in Confucian classics, gaining many disciples and acclaim.

He passed the imperial exams, became a doctor during the Heping period, and later served as governor of Shuofang, known for orderly governance. He was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi. While accompanying Emperor Cheng to Ganquan, he violated road rules, leading to his carriage being confiscated by Sili Xiaowei Chen Qing. Later, Fangjin impeached Chen Qing for disrespect, resulting in Chen's dismissal. He also impeached Juanxun, another Sili Xiaowei, for arrogance and disrespect, leading to Juanxun's demotion. Within a year, Fangjin dismissed two high officials, instilling fear in the court.

As Jingzhaoyin, he cracked down on powerful families, but at Hu Chang's advice, he moderated his strictness. After three years, he became imperial censor, then prime minister and Marquis of Gaoling. He was impartial and strict, often impeaching ministers like Chen Xian and Feng Xin for corruption, leading to their dismissal. He also targeted Chunyu Chang's associates, removing over twenty officials. Despite his harshness, Emperor Cheng trusted him.

Fangjin studied "Guliang Zhuan" but favored "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and astronomy. After nine years as prime minister, Mars entered the heart constellation, and his subordinate Li Xun warned of impending disaster. Fangjin grew anxious. The emperor later criticized him for poor governance and tax policies, but spared him. Fangjin committed suicide that day. The emperor honored him with posthumous titles and gifts.

His son Zhai Xuan was a gentleman, while another son, Zhai Yi, became a governor. During Wang Mang's regency, Zhai Yi rebelled, declaring Liu Xin emperor and amassing over 100,000 troops. Wang Mang crushed the rebellion, executing Zhai Yi and his family, and desecrating Fangjin's grave. The rebellion's failure led to Wang Mang's usurpation. Historian Ban Biao noted Fangjin's rise from poverty to prominence, but lamented Zhai Yi's doomed uprising.

Jing Wang Liu Jia, the cousin of Mo Gaozu Liu Bang, did not know when he participated in the uprising.
In the first year of Han Dynasty, when the king of Han Dynasty returned to the Three Qin Dynasty, Liu Mai was appointed as the general. After pacifying Sima Xin's territory, he followed Liu Bangdong to attack Xiangji.
The King of Han was defeated by Chenggao, crossed the Yellow River to the north, captured the armies of Zhang Er and Han Xin, and stationed their troops in Xiuwu County. On the one hand, they dug deep trenches and built high barriers; on the other hand, they sent Liu Mai to lead 20,000 troops and hundreds of cavalry to attack Chu, crossed Baima Jin, and entered the Chu land. They burned Chu's grain and grass, destroyed the Chu army's military supply, and made it impossible to supply food to King Xiang's army.
Soon, the Chu soldiers attacked, but Liu Jia always avoided it and did not fight the Chu soldiers. Instead, he and Peng Yue relied on each other to protect themselves.
The king of Han pursued Xiang Ji to Guling and sent Liu Mai to lead his troops south across the Huaihe River to surround Shouchun.
After returning, he sent people to alienate and recruit Zhou Yin, the great commander of Chu State, to surrender.
Zhou Yin rebelled against Chu and returned to Han, assisted Liu Mai in capturing Jiujiang, catered to Yingbu's army, fought at Gaixia, and defeated Xiang Yu.
Therefore, the King of Han sent Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang soldiers, together with Taiwei Lu Wan, to attack Linjiang King Gongwei in the southwest. After Wei Gong's death, Linjiang was renamed Nanjun.
Since Liu Jia had achieved great military exploits, the emperor's son at that time was young, had few brothers, and was not very talented and virtuous. He wanted to make someone with the same surname king to conquer the world, so Xia Shao said: "General Liu Mai has meritorious service, and he is qualified to choose the king among his descendants."
The ministers said: Let Liu Mai be made King of Jing and take charge of Huaidong.
Six years later, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and attacked Jingdi eastward.
Liu Mai fought with him but failed to win. He fled to Fuling County and was killed by Yingbu's pursuers.
Liu Ze, King of Yan, was the brother of Gaozu and his great-grandfather.
In the third year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Liu Ze became a doctor.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, as a general, he led troops to defeat Chen Xi's general Wang Huang and was named Yinglinghou.
When Empress Gao was in power, Tian Sheng, a native of Qi, was short of funds when lobbying outside, so he turned to Liu Ze for help by offering suggestions.
Liu Ze was very happy and gave Tian Sheng two hundred pounds of gold when he passed away. Tian Sheng got the gold and immediately returned to Qi.
The following year, Liu Ze sent a messenger to Tian Sheng: We are no longer friends!
When Tian Sheng came to Chang'an, he did not go to see Liu Ze. Instead, he stayed in a big house and asked his son to find a way to work under Zhang Qing, the great emissary favored by Empress Lu.
A few months later, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to his home as a guest, and Tian Sheng hosted a banquet for him in person.
Zhang Qing went there and was greatly surprised when he saw that the curtains and other decorative appliances wrapped in Tiansheng's house were in compliance with the standards of the princes.
When the wine was in full swing, Tian Sheng asked everyone to retreat and said to Zhang Qing: I have seen more than a hundred princes' postal residences, all of which were occupied by the meritorious officials of Emperor Gaozu.
Nowadays, the Lu family originally assisted Emperor Gao in conquering the world. Their contribution was very great, and they also had relatives such as the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother was old and the power of the Lu family was still weak. The Queen Mother wanted to establish Lu Chan as King Lu to rule over the country.
But the Queen Mother found it difficult to speak out, fearing that the ministers would disagree.
At present, you are the most favored, and the ministers respect you. Why don't you persuade the ministers to agree to make Zhu Lu king, and then report it to the Queen Mother, who will definitely be happy.
If the Lu family is granted the title of king, you must also be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households.
As a minister, if you don't realize what the Queen Mother wants to achieve quickly, I'm afraid there will be disaster.
After Zhang Qing heard this, he thought it was right, so he sarcastically persuaded the ministers to approve the granting of the title of Zhu Lu, and reported it to the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother went to court and asked the ministers for their opinions.
Ministers please grant Lu Chan the title of King Lu.
Afterwards, the Empress Dowager rewarded Zhang Qing with a thousand catties of gold. Zhang Qing gave half of it to Tian Sheng, but Tian Sheng refused and took the opportunity to persuade him: "Lü Chan can be crowned king, but the ministers may not be very convinced."
Now the Marquis of Yingling, Liu Ze, is the elder of the Liu clan and a general. He is the only one who harbors resentment for not being crowned king.
Now you go and tell the Queen Mother that more than a dozen counties in Qi will be crowned king. Liu Ze will be happy and leave, and the status of the Lu family kings will be more stable.
Zhang Qing told the Queen Mother.
And because the daughter of the Queen Mother's sister Lu Xu was the wife of Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, Liu Ze was granted the title of King Langxie.
King Langxie and Tian Sheng went to Fengguo, and Tian Sheng advised him to leave quickly and not to stay.
After walking out of Hangu Pass, the Queen Mother indeed sent someone to chase him.
Liu Ze had already left the customs, and the visitor went back.
The year after Liu Ze became King Langxie, Empress Dowager Lu died of illness. Liu Ze then said: The emperor is young, Zhu Lu is in power, and the Liu clan is lonely and weak.
So he led his troops and conspired with the King of Qi to march westward, intending to kill Zhu Lu.
When he arrived in Liangdi, he heard that General Guan Ying of the Han Dynasty was stationed in Rongyang, so he withdrew his troops and stationed them in the western frontier of his country, and then rushed to Chang'an alone.
At this time, Liu Heng, the king of Dai, also arrived in Chang'an, the capital of Dai. The generals and ministers and Liu Ze jointly supported the king of Dai as the emperor of the Han Dynasty, that is, Emperor Xiaowen.
In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Ze was renamed King of Yan. The Langye area was still given to Qi.
Liu Ze died after two years as King of Yan, and Mi paid tribute to him.
His son Kang Wang Liu Jia succeeded to the throne and died in the ninth year.
Dingguo, the son of King Kang, succeeded to the throne.
Dingguo committed adultery with his father's concubine. She gave birth to a boy, took his sister-in-law as a concubine, and committed adultery with her three daughters.
Dingguo planned to kill the Ying people, the magistrate of Feiru County. The Ying people and others reported to the court, and Dingguo sent envoys to kill the Ying people and silence them for violating other laws.
During the Yuanshuo period, the brothers of the Ying people once again wrote to the court to report Dingguo's crimes in detail.
Emperor Wu asked the ministers to discuss it, and they all said: Dingguo's behavior is like an animal, messing up human relations and violating the will of God, and he should be punished with death.
The emperor approved this proposal.
Dingguo then committed suicide. Forty-two years after the establishment of the feudal state, it was abolished.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, in order to continue the vassal family that had cut off the feudal state, Liu Guisheng, Liu Ze's great-great-grandson's grandson from Wuzhong County, who had only a first-class title, was granted the title of Marquis of Yingling. During the Gengshi period, Liu Guisheng was killed by soldiers.
King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, brother of Emperor Gao.
Emperor Gao made Liu Zhong the acting king.
When the Xiongnu attacked Dai, Liu Zhong could not hold on, so he secretly abandoned the country and fled, returning to the capital Chang'an from Luoyang. The emperor could not bear to bring him to justice, so he deposed him from the throne and demoted him to the rank of Marquis of Heyang.
His son Liu Bi was granted the title of Marquis of Pei.
King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled, and Emperor Gaozu personally led troops to attack him.
At this time, Liu Bi was twenty years old and followed Gaozu as a cavalry general to defeat Yingbu.
After King Liu Mai of Jing was killed by Ting Bu, he had no descendants.
Emperor Gaozu was worried that the people of Wu County and Kuaiji County were frivolous and fierce, and there were no powerful princes to control them. His son was still young, so he appointed Liu Bi as King of Wu in Pei, with jurisdiction over three counties and fifty-three cities.
After receiving the seal, Emperor Gaozu summoned him and gave him a face, saying: You have the appearance of rebellion.
I regretted that I should not have sealed him, but I could not take back my life, so I patted Liu Bi on the back and said: Fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty, there will be a rebellion in the southeast. Could it be you?
However, everyone with the same surname is one family, so don’t rebel!
Liu Bi kowtowed and said, "I don't dare."
During the reign of Emperor Hui and Empress Lu, due to the initial order of the world, all the princes in the prefectures and states were devoted to the rule of their own countries.
There was a copper-producing mountain in Yuzhang County of the State of Wu, which led to desperadoes from all over to steal coins and boil seawater in the southeast to make salt. Therefore, no taxes were collected from the people, and the country's finances were very rich.
During the reign of Emperor Wen, Prince Wu went to the capital for an audience and was able to accompany the crown prince to drink and play chess.
Prince Wu's masters were all from Chu, so he was as frivolous, fierce, arrogant and wanton as the Chu people.
When they were playing chess, they were competing for moves and were disrespectful to the crown prince. The crown prince raised the chessboard and threw it at Prince Wu, killing him and sending his body back to the state of Wu for burial.
King Wu said angrily: "Everyone with the same surname in the world is one family. If you die in Chang'an, you will be buried in Chang'an. Why should you be buried in Wu!"
He also sent Prince Wu's body back to Chang'an for burial.
As a result, the King of Wu became dissatisfied and gradually lost the etiquette of the princes towards the Han court. He pretended to be ill and refused to see the emperor.
The imperial court knew that it was because his son was killed, and after examination, he was actually not sick. Therefore, every time Wu sent envoys to him, he was always arrested and punished.
King Wu was afraid and even more determined to rebel against the court.
Later, Liu Bi asked someone to pay his respects to the emperor on his behalf, and Emperor Wen again questioned the envoy from Wu.
The messenger said: It would be unlucky for the emperor to find out about the private affairs of his ministers and cause them to worry and change.
Now the king of Wu began to lie about being ill, and the emperor noticed it. Seeing that he was punished quickly, he hid his conspiracy even more.
He was afraid that the emperor would kill him, and his plan would be of no benefit to the court.
It would be best if the emperor pardoned his past crimes. Therefore, the emperor pardoned all the Wu envoys and released them back to Wu. He also rewarded King Wu with Pingji and a walking stick, saying that King Wu was old and could not visit the emperor in the capital.
After King Wu was acquitted, his conspiracy became even more unscrupulous.
However, the state of Wu had profits from copper and salt, so the people did not have to pay taxes; if there were those who had to do hard labor, the government would also pay for them.
Every New Year's Day, we should visit the talented and learned people and give rewards to the residents of the village.
Officials from other counties were sent to the state of Wu to arrest criminals who had fled to Wu. The state of Wu also acquitted them of their crimes and strictly prohibited them.
It was governed like this for more than thirty years, and the king of Wu was able to serve his people.
Shi Chaocuo was the prince's family order and gained the prince's favor. He talked about King Wu's sins more than once and advocated cutting off his land and punishing him.
He also wrote to Emperor Wen several times about this matter. Emperor Wen was kind-hearted and could not bear to punish him, so King Wu became more and more arrogant.
Later, when Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo was appointed as the imperial censor. He told the emperor: Once upon a time, when the great ancestor first established the world, he had few brothers and his sons were young, so he made the same surnames the princes and kings. Therefore, Liu Fei, the concubine of Emperor Gaozu, was the King of Qi Huihui, and had jurisdiction over seventy-two cities; Liu Jiao, the concubine, was the King of Chu Yuan, and was in charge of forty cities in Chu; and his elder brother's son Liu Bi was the King of Wu, and was in charge of more than fifty cities in Wu.
These three vassal states occupy half of the country's land.
Now because his son was killed, the King of Wu lied about being ill and did not come to court. According to ancient laws, he should be executed.
Emperor Wen couldn't bear to execute King Wu, but instead rewarded him with a pen and a cane. His kindness to him was so profound.
However, instead of reforming his ways, the King of Wu became even more arrogant and indulgent. He openly minted money on the mountains and boiled seawater into salt, luring people fleeing from all directions to plot rebellion.
If his territory is reduced, he will rebel, and if it is not reduced, he will rebel.
If it is reduced, he will rebel faster and cause less harm; if his territory is not reduced, he will rebel later and cause greater harm.
In the winter of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, the King of Chu came to see the emperor. Chao Cuo said that King Chu Liu Wu had committed adultery in the mourning room during the mourning period for Empress Dowager Bo a few years ago, and he should be punished with death.
The emperor issued an edict to pardon his capital crime and only reduced his territory of Shuhai County.
Two years ago, King Zhao was guilty and cut off his territory of Changshan County.
Liu Yin, the king of Jiaoxi, committed a crime by selling his official title and was deprived of six counties.
When the ministers of the Han Dynasty discussed reducing the territory of Wu State, the King of Wu was worried that the land reduction would be endless, so he wanted to rebel according to the predetermined plan.
Considering that there was no one among the princes and kings who could scheme with him, I heard that the King of Jiaoxi was brave and fond of military affairs, and the princes were all afraid of him, so he sent Zhongda Yinggao to persuade the King of Jiaoxi and said: King Wu is incompetent and has worries day and night. We are one family, so he sent me to tell you what is on King Wu's mind.
King Jiaoxi said: Any advice?
Ying Gao said: Now the emperor appoints treacherous ministers, listens to slander, changes laws, invades the territories of princes and kings, and expropriates more and more things. The condemnation and punishment are too heavy, and they are increasing day by day.
As the saying goes: When a dog starts eating, he licks the chaff, and then he eats the rice.
Wu and Jiaoxi are famous among the princes. If they are investigated and punished for a while, they will not be able to act safely and indulgently.
King Wu was ill and could not see the emperor for more than twenty years. He was often afraid of being suspected, but could not explain clearly. He spent all day studying on his own, fearing that he would not be released by the court.

What do you want?

Now the King of Wu thinks that he is worried about the same thing as the King, and is willing to follow the timing and the laws of things, even if it means sacrificing his own life, in order to eliminate the disaster in the world. Do you think it's okay?
King Jiaoxi looked at him in surprise and said: How dare I do this?
Although the emperor is forcing us to be very anxious, we only have one chance of death. How can we disobey him?
Ying Gao said: Chao Cuo, the imperial censor, seduced the emperor, invaded the princes, and blocked the loyal and virtuous. All the ministers in the dynasty resented him, and all the princes and kings wanted to rebel. The matter was extremely bad.
Comet appears in the sky and locusts appear on the earth. This is rare in all the world. When the people are worried and laboring, it is time for the saint to take action.
King Wu's purpose for the Han court was to get rid of Chao Cuo, and for the princes, he followed the king and galloped around the world, surrendering wherever he went; wherever the army attacked, it collapsed, and no one dared to disobey.
If the king sincerely agrees and gives me a reply, then the king of Wu will lead the king of Chu to seize Hangu Pass, guard the food in Rongyang Aocang, resist the Han soldiers, build a simple house for the march to stop, and wait for the king.

Ying Gao went back and reported the situation to King Wu. The King of Wu was also worried that the King of Jiaoxi would not fulfill his promise, so he personally sneaked to Jiaoxi as an envoy and made an agreement with Liu Yin face to face.
Some of the ministers of the Jiaoxi Kingdom learned about the King of Jiaoxi's plan and advised him: "The territory owned by the princes is only two-tenths of the imperial court. It is not a good strategy to make the Queen Mother sad because of rebellion."
It is not easy to serve an emperor now. If the rebellion succeeds and two emperors compete for power, there will be more disasters.
The King of Jiaoxi did not listen to the advice, but sent envoys separately to make appointments with Qi, Miaochuan, Jiaoqiang, and Jinan, and they all agreed.
The princes were shocked and frightened by the new punishment of cutting off their lands, and most of them resented Chao Cuo.
When Shaoshu, who had beheaded Wu's Kuaiji and Yuzhang counties, arrived, the king of Wu first rebelled and executed the officials in the Wu court who were under two thousand stones.
The countries of Jiaoxi, Micelle, Miaochuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao then rebelled and marched westward.

The two kings of Jiaoxi and Miaojie were the commanders, and together with the king of Miaochuan and the king of Jinan, they jointly besieged Linli.
King Liu Sui also secretly asked the Xiongnu to join forces with him.
When the joint rebellion of the seven countries began, King Wu invested all his troops and issued an order to the country: I am now sixty-two years old, and I personally lead the troops on the expedition; my youngest son, who is fourteen years old, also leads the army.
All Chinese citizens who are older than sixty-two and younger than fourteen years old must join the army.
A total of more than 200,000 people were recruited.
At the same time, envoys were sent to Fujian and Shuyue in the south, and the two countries also sent troops to accompany them.
In the first month of the first year of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, King Liu Bi of Wu first raised his troops in Guangling, crossed the Huaihe River to the west, and joined the Chu troops.

It was his duty to plunder and insult the princes. He did not treat the Liu family members with the courtesy of princes, did not honor the late emperor's meritorious officials, used evil people, used deceptive words to harm the world, and put the country in danger.
The emperor was sick and obsessed with happiness and could not see the truth clearly.
Therefore, I want to raise my troops to kill Chao Cuo, and I would like to ask everyone for advice.
Although our country is small, with a radius of only 3,000 units, and although its population is small, it has 500,000 elite soldiers.
I have worshiped the South Vietnamese Kingdom for more than thirty years, and its king and leaders are willing to detach troops to support me, so I can get another three hundred thousand people.
Although I am incompetent, I am willing to follow the kings myself.
The South Vietnamese soldiers attacked the Changsha Kingdom from the north. After the prince pacified the north of Changsha, they then attacked Shujun and Mozhong westward.
Inform King Shuyue, King Chu, and the three kings of Huainan, Jibei, and Hengshan to march westward with me. After the kings of Qi and King Tou pacify Hejian and Hanoi, they will either enter Linjin Pass or join me at Luoyang; King Yan , King Zhao had an agreement with the Xiongnu Chanyu. After King Yan pacified Dai and Yunzhong in the north, he led the Xiongnu soldiers into Xiaoguan and took the capital Chang'an directly to save the world, secure the temple of Gaodi, and encourage all the kings.
The prince of Chu Yuan and the three kings of Huainan, Hengshan and Jibei have not received favor from the court for more than ten years, so they hate Moting deeply and have wanted to send troops to attack the Han Dynasty for a long time. I did not get the opinions of the kings and did not dare to listen to them.
Now, if the kings can save the country from subjugation, succeed in the peerless era, revitalize the weak, defeat the tyrannical, and stabilize the Liu family, it will be a great blessing for the country.
Although the state of Wu is poor, for more than thirty years I have scrimped on food and clothing, accumulated money, trained the army at night, and hoarded food.
All this is for this reason, and I would like to work with all the kings to achieve it.
Anyone who can capture and kill a general will be rewarded with five thousand jins of gold and be granted the title of 10,000 households; if he captures and beheads a general, he will be rewarded with 3,000 jins of gold and be granted the title of 5,000 households; if he captures and beheads a general, he will be rewarded with 2,000 jins of gold and be granted the title of 2,000 households.
If a person comes to surrender with an army and a city or land under his jurisdiction, and if he brings ten thousand soldiers and households each, the reward will be the same as if he captured a general; if he brings five thousand soldiers and households each, his reward will be the same as if he captures and kills a general; if he brings three thousand soldiers and three thousand households, he will be treated as if he captured and beheaded a general; if he brings one thousand soldiers and one thousand households, he will be treated as if he captures and kills a general. Other ordinary minor officials can enjoy titles and bounties according to their levels.
The rewards given were twice as many as those stipulated by the Han court.
Those with original titles and fiefs will be given additional rewards in addition to retaining their original titles.
I hope that the kings will openly announce it to the scholar-bureaucrats and others and not dare to deceive.
My gold and coins are available everywhere in the world, not necessarily from Wu, and the kings can use them day and night.
If there is anyone who deserves a reward, you can tell me and I will send someone to send gold and coins.
We respectfully inform you of the above situation.
When the Han court learned about the rebellion of the seven kingdoms, Emperor Jing sent Taiwei and Tiaohou Zhou Yafu to lead thirty-six generals to attack Wu and Chu; he sent Quzhou Hou Liji to lead troops to attack Tongguo; he sent General Lebu to lead troops to attack Qi; and General Dou Ying was stationed in Rongyang to monitor the movements of the Qi and Zhao armies.
At the beginning, when the news of Wu and Chu's rebellion had just been heard and before troops were sent out, Dou Ying told the emperor about Yuan An, the former prime minister of the state of Wu.
The emperor then summoned Yuan Ang and asked about strategies to resolve Wu Chu's rebellion. Yuan Cong said: Wu and Chu communicated with each other, and they both said that the traitor Chao Cuo had monopolized power, demoted the princes, reduced the invasion of the princes' fiefdoms, and rebelled because of this, which was called a crusade to the west. They jointly killed Chao Cuo, restored the original fiefdoms, and then stopped the army.
The only plan now is to put Chao Cuo to death, send envoys to pardon the sins of the seven kingdoms, and restore the original fiefdoms of the seven kingdoms. Then there will be no need to fight with swords, and bloodshed and sacrifice can be avoided.
The emperor followed his advice and beheaded Chao Cuo.
The details are recorded in "The Biography of Yuan Ang".
Therefore, Yuan Ang was granted the title of Taichang, in charge of worshiping at the ancestral temple, and sent an envoy to see the King of Wu. Dehou, the nephew of the King of Wu, was a Zongzhengguan and was sent to the State of Wu as an auxiliary envoy because he was closely related to Wu.
By the time they arrived at Wu State, the armies of Wu and Chu were already attacking the military camp of Liang State.
Because Zong Zheng was a relative, he went to see the King of Wu first and ordered the King to kneel down and accept the edict.
King Wu heard that Yuan An was coming and knew what he wanted to say. He smiled and replied: I am already Emperor Shu, who do I still want to bow to?
He refused to see Yuan An and detained him in the army, trying to force him to become a general of Wu.
Yuan Ang refused to agree, so the King of Wu sent troops to surround him and prepare to kill him.
Yuan An fled to Liang State at night, then returned to the capital and reported the situation to the emperor.
Tiaohou Zhou Yafu took six official carriages to pass the news and mobilized the army to join forces in Rongyang.
When he arrived at Luoyang, he met Ju Meng and said happily: "The Seven Kingdoms rebelled. I arrived here in an official car. I didn't expect that I could reach here safely."
I thought the rebellious princes had obtained Ju Meng. Now that Ju Meng has not wavered, I have occupied Rongyang, so there is no need to worry about the area east of Rongyang.
When he arrived in Huaiyang, he asked Captain Deng, who was his father's aide to Jianghou Zhoubo, "What's your plan?"
Captain Deng said: Wu's army is very elite, and it is difficult to win between them. The Chu army was impetuous and could not stay long.
Now for the general's plan, it is better to lead troops to the northeast and garrison Changyi, leaving Liang State to Wu State. Wu State will definitely attack Liang State with all its elite troops.
The generals dug deep trenches, built high fortifications, and sent light troops to guard the entrances and exits of the Huaihe River and the Swimming River to cut off Wu's food and salary supply.
Wu and Chu are exhausted and short of food and grass. We use the advantages of complete equipment and materials to control the disadvantageous situation of Wu and Chu who are eager to end the war due to lack of food and materials. This will definitely defeat Wu. Zhou Yafu heard this and said: This plan is very clever.
Therefore, he followed his strategy and stood firm to the south of Changyi. At the same time, he sent light troops to cut off Wu's grain transportation road.
When King Wu first started his army, his minister Tian Lubo was the general.
He said to the King of Wu: It is difficult to achieve success by gathering the troops to the west. There is no other way to win by surprise.
I am willing to lead 50,000 people to advance along the Yangtze River and Huaihe River, recover Huainan and Changsha, enter Wuguan, and then join the king. This is also a good plan.
The Crown Prince of Wu advised: Your Majesty raised the army in the name of fighting against the Desert, and it is difficult to lend the army to others to lead. What if others also rise up against King Wu?
Moreover, if someone else takes over the military power and divides the troops, if something goes against me, it will only be a waste of losses for myself.
King Wu therefore did not agree to Tian Lubo's request.
General Huan, the young general of Wu State, persuaded the King of Wu: Wu State has many infantry, which is beneficial to fighting in dangerous places; there are many chariots and cavalry in Moting, which is beneficial to fighting in plains.
I hope that if the city that the king passes through is not captured, he can go straight west for the time being, quickly occupy the weapons depot in Luoyang, seize the grain of Aocang, occupy the dangerous places on the mountains and rivers, and use this to command the princes. Then, even if he does not enter the pass, the world will be peaceful.
If the king marches slowly and stays in every city he encounters, once the desert army comes with chariots and cavalry and enters the outskirts of Liang and Chu, the war will fail.
The King of Wu asked the old generals for their opinions. The old generals said: This man is young. Although he can charge into battle, how can he know how to make foresight?
Therefore, the King of Wu did not adopt General Huan's strategy.
The King of Wu took over the power and personally led the troops. Before crossing the Huaihe River, many of his guests were named generals, lieutenants, marquises of Xingjian, Sima and other officials, but Zhou Qiu was not appointed.
Zhou Qiu, a native of Xiapi, was guilty of a crime and fled to the state of Wu. He was engaged in the wine business and behaved badly. The king of Wu looked down on him, so he did not appoint him.
So Zhou Qiu asked to see the King of Wu and said to the King of Wu: Because I am incompetent, I cannot take the blame and serve in the army.
I dare not ask the king to bring me some troops. I only hope that the king will give me a Desert Talisman Festival, and I will definitely repay you.
The king of Wu then gave him the Han Fu Festival.
Zhou Qiu got Hanjie and quickly entered Xiapi at night.
At that time, Xiapi had heard about Wu's rebellion, and they all defended the city.
Zhou Qiu arrived at the inn, summoned the county magistrate into the room, and announced the magistrate's crime. Let the attendants execute the county magistrate.
Then he called together the powerful officials who were friendly with his brothers and said: Wu: Zheng's troops are coming. It only takes one meal to kill all the people in Xiapi City.
Now that we surrender to Wu, everyone's family members and properties will definitely be saved, and the opportunity for those with great ability to fight for the title of marquis has arrived.
After these people went out, they informed each other, so Xiapi City surrendered.
Zhou Qiu obtained 30,000 soldiers overnight, so he sent people to report to the king of Wu and led his soldiers to attack the city and seize the territory in the north.
By the time they arrived in Chengyang, they had more than 100,000 soldiers and defeated the lieutenant's army in Chengyang.
After hearing the news of King Wu's defeat, he thought that he could not succeed with King Wu, so he returned to Xiapi with his soldiers.
On the way, he died of a poisonous sore on his back.
In February, the king of Wu was defeated and fled. The emperor was General Shao, who said: It is said that those who do good deeds will be rewarded with blessings, and those who do evil will be rewarded with disaster.
The merits of my dynasty will last forever, and I will establish a kingdom of vassals. King You of Zhao and King Hui of Qi had no Gen son to succeed them to the throne. Emperor Wen took pity on them and showed favor to them. He made Liu Sui, the most prosperous son of land reclamation, and Xingsheng, the prince of Pantou, etc., as vassal kings. He ordered them to continue to worship their ancestors' ancestral temples and became vassal states of the Han Dynasty. His kindness can be described as the sky is thick and the earth is thick, and the light is brighter than the moon.
However, King Liu Bi of Wu betrayed his moral integrity, lured outlaws from all over the world, minted coins privately, disrupted the country's currency system, and pretended to be ill and failed to see the emperor on time for more than 20 years.
The competent authorities requested that Liu Bi be punished several times, but Emperor Wen tolerated it and refused to punish him, in order to make him change for the better.
Now, he and King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Tang, King Liu Yin of Jiaoxi, King Liu Biguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Miao Chuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Miao Chuan agreed with each other to conspire against the will of heaven, rebel against the Han Dynasty, and raise troops to overthrow the central dynasty. The rebels killed the ministers and envoys of the Han Dynasty, forcibly robbed the people, killed innocent people indiscriminately, burned down people's houses, and dug up people's graves. They were very cruel.
But Liu Yin and others were even more rebellious and unscrupulous. They burned down the ancestral temples in the prefectures and looted the clothes and utensils used in the ancestral temples. I hated them very much.
Now I wear plain clothes and do not go to the main hall. I hope the generals will mobilize the scholar-bureaucrats to fight against these rebels.
In order to attack the rebels, they killed many people and went deep into the ground to plan their merits. Rebels with a salary of more than 300 dan were killed and were not allowed to be released.
Anyone who dares to discuss the edict or not do what it requires will be cut in half.
It turned out that after the King of Wu crossed the Huaihe River, he and the King of Chu went west to defeat the Liang army of Liu Wu, the younger brother of Emperor Jing, at Jibi. They took advantage of the victory and advanced to attack, making them unstoppable.
King Xiao of Liang was afraid of this and sent generals to attack him. The Wu and Chu armies defeated the two armies of Liang Guo again, and the soldiers all fled back.
King Xiao of Liang sent envoys several times to ask for help from Taiwei Zhou Yafu, but Zhou Yafu did not come to his rescue.
He also sent envoys to report Zhou Yafu's attitude to the emperor. The emperor sent people to ask Zhou Yafu to rescue Liang, but Zhou Yafu did not send troops to rescue Liang due to special circumstances.
The king of Liang then sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, the brother of Zhang Shang, the prime minister of Chu, who had killed himself to stop Chu's rebellion, as generals to lead the army, and they were able to slightly defeat the Wu army.
Wu soldiers wanted to advance westward, but Liang's cities were well defended, so they did not dare to go westward and instead ran towards Zhou Yafu's army.
In Xiayi, the Wu army asked for a fight, but Zhou Yafu stood firm and refused to fight.
The Wu army was out of food and the soldiers were hungry. They challenged Zhou Yafu several times, so they attacked Zhou Yafu's camp at night and pretended to attack the southeast. Zhou Yafu ordered to guard the northwest.
Sure enough, Wu soldiers attacked from the northwest, but failed to break through. Wu soldiers were defeated. Most of the soldiers starved to death or surrendered and dispersed.
So the king of Wu and his thousands of strong men fled at night. After crossing the Huaihe River, I followed Dantu and surrendered to Shuyue.
Shu Yue had about ten thousand soldiers and sent people to recruit deserters.
The Han court sent people to lure Dongyue, and Dongyue deceived the King of Wu. When the King of Wu came out to comfort the soldiers, he sent people to kill the King of Wu with a spear and halberd, put the King of Wu's head in a wooden box, and reported to the Han court on a flying horse.
Prince Wu Liu Ju fled to Fujian and Yue.
After the death of King Wu, the Wu army collapsed, and soldiers surrendered to Han Taiwei Tiaohou and Liang Jun anytime and anywhere.
King Liu Wu of Chu was defeated and committed suicide.
Jiaoxi, Micelle, Miao! The three kings besieged Linmiao in Qi State, but it lasted three months and still was not broken.
As soon as the Han soldiers arrived, they led their troops back to their countries. After the King of Jiaoxi returned home, he walked barefoot, slept on straw mats, drank plain water, and apologized to the Queen Mother.
His prince Liu De said: The Han army is already withdrawing. I think they are quite tired, so I can attack them. I hope the king will collect the remaining troops and pursue them. If he cannot win, he can escape to the sea before it is too late.
The King of Jiaoxi said: Our soldiers have suffered too many casualties and cannot fight anymore.
Not listening to his son.
The general of the Han Dynasty, Gong Gaohou Han Daodang, sent a letter to the King of Jiaoxi. The letter said: I have come to kill the rebels in accordance with the Emperor's Shao Shu. Those who surrender will have their sins pardoned and their original positions restored; those who do not surrender will be destroyed.
Wherever you go, King of Jiaoxi, I must deal with it accordingly.
The King of Jiaoxi went to the Han army camp with his chest and arms exposed, kowtowed to pay homage, and said: "Your Majesty Liu Yin was not cautious in obeying the law, so he frightened the people. General, I have come all the way to my poor country. Please give me the punishment of being chopped into meat sauce."
Han Dai met him with a golden drum in his hand and said: The King of Jiaoxi is distressed about sending troops to rebel. I am willing to hear your reasons for sending troops.
The King of Jiaoxi kowtowed, walked forward on his knees, and replied: It's like this: Chao Cuo was a minister in power before the emperor. He changed Emperor Gao's decree and invaded the territories of the princes. Liu Yin and others thought it was unfair.
We were afraid that he would bring chaos to the country, so the seven countries sent troops at the same time to kill Chao Cuo.
Now that they heard that Chao Cuo had been killed, Liu Yin and others wanted to withdraw their troops and return home.
Han Daedang said: If the king thinks that Chao Cuo did something bad, why not appeal to the emperor?
At the same time, without the emperor's edict and tiger talisman for sending troops, troops were sent to attack the just country without authorization.
Judging from this, your intention is not just to kill Chao Cuo.
He immediately took out the emperor's edict, read it to King Jiaoxi, and said: Your Majesty, commit suicide.
The King of Jiaoxi said: People like Liu Yin and others deserve to die.
So he committed suicide and died.
The queen mother and the prince also died.
When he was dispatched, the three kings of Miaochuan, Miaochuan and Jinan were also killed.
Li Shiqi led his troops to attack the State of Zhao, and fought for ten months before winning. Liu Sui, the king of Zhao, committed suicide.
The king of Jibei, Liu Zhichu, was coerced and plotted, but later he insisted on not sending troops, so he was pardoned but not killed. At the beginning, it was King Wu who rebelled first. He also led the troops of Chu and contacted Qi and Zhao.
Starting from the first month to the third month, they were all conquered and destroyed.
Zan said: The reason why Jing Wang Liu Jia was named king was because the world was not yet stable, so even though he was a distant relative of the Liu family, he was also named king and sat in the Jianghuai area.
Liu Ze's title of king began with Tian Sheng's plan. He first provoked Empress Lu to grant Lu Chan, and then asked people to ridicule Empress Lu to grant Liu Ze the title of king. Finally, he faced south and was left alone for three generations.
Once the matter is revealed, it will be a serious crime. Isn't it very dangerous?
King Wu Liu Bi had the exclusive advantage of mountains and seas, which could reduce taxes, win over and control the people, and the rebellion plan started when his son was killed.
The ancient vassal states were no more than a hundred miles in radius, not including mountains, forests, rivers and swamps. This was probably to prevent them from rebelling against the central government.
Chao Cuo thought of the country's long-term interests, but disaster struck him and he died. Don't be the mastermind of the rebellion, because you will suffer disaster. Isn't this exactly what Chao Cuo said?
summary: The histories of three Han dynasty princes: Liu Jia (King of Jing), Liu Ze (King of Yan), and Liu Bi (King of Wu). Liu Jia, a cousin of Emperor Gaozu, served as a general, leading campaigns against Chu forces, burning supplies, and later capturing Jiujiang. He was made King of Jing but was killed in battle against the rebel Yingbu. Liu Ze, a brother of Gaozu, was initially a marquis. Through a scheme by Tian Sheng, he was made King of Langye after persuading Empress Lu to enfeoff the Lü clan. After Empress Lu’s death, he joined others in supporting Emperor Xiaowen and was renamed King of Yan. His descendants included a son, Kang Wang, and a grandson, Dingguo, who committed adultery with his father’s concubine and sisters, leading to his suicide and the abolition of his state. Liu Bi, son of Liu Zhong, was made King of Wu after defeating Yingbu. He grew wealthy from copper and salt, and after his son was killed by the crown prince, he feigned illness and plotted rebellion. During Emperor Jing’s reign, Chao Cuo advocated reducing the princes’ territories, prompting Liu Bi to lead a rebellion of seven states (Wu, Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Zichuan) in 154 BCE. Liu Bi issued a call to arms, offering rewards for killing Han officials. Emperor Jing executed Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, but the rebellion continued. Zhou Yafu, a Han general, cut off Wu’s supply lines and defeated them. Liu Bi fled to Dongyue, where he was killed. The other rebel princes were also defeated or committed suicide. The text concludes that Liu Jia’s kingship was due to the unstable times, Liu Ze’s was based on a risky scheme, and Liu Bi’s rebellion stemmed from his wealth and personal grievance, leading to disaster.

Xiao He was from Peidi.
Because he could write documents without defects, he was appointed as an official of Pei Lord.
When Gaozu was still a commoner, Xiao He supported Gaozu in official affairs many times.
After Gaozu became the chief of the pavilion, he helped him again.
Gaozu went to Xianyang to serve as an official. The minor officials all contributed 300 yuan to see Gaozu off, but only Xiao He contributed 500 yuan.
Qin Yushi supervised the people of the county and was engaged in the inspection of his duties. Xiao He was awarded the post of official of Sishui County and was the best in the examination.
Qin Yushi planned to report to the court to recruit Xiao He, but Xiao He refused and was able to stay.
When Emperor Gaozu rose up and became Duke of Pei, Xiao He was appointed as the prime minister and governor.
When Pei Gong arrived in Xianyang, all the generals rushed to the treasury where gold and silk were stored to divide them up.
Only Xiao He went in first to collect the books on laws and regulations written by Qin Prime Minister and Censor. The reason why Pei Gong knew the fortresses in the world in detail, the number of households, the distribution of strength and weakness, and the people's hatred and sorrow was because Xiao He had received Qin's books.
Xiao He took over the remaining Ba and Shu as prime minister, pacified the people in the territory, and asked them to provide food for the army.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han and the princes attacked Chu. Xiao He stayed in Guanzhong, guarding the prince and governing Yueyang.
Formulate laws and regulations, establish ancestral temples, communities, palaces, and counties. They should be reported regularly and implemented if the emperor agrees. If it is too late to report the matter, then implement it in an appropriate manner and tell the Emperor after he comes back.
Calculating the number of households and transferring grain and wages to supply military supplies, the King of Han led his troops to escape many times. Xiao He often recruited soldiers from Guanzhong to supplement the front line. Therefore, the emperor specifically handed over Guanzhong affairs to Xiao He.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, there was a confrontation with Xiang Yu in Beijing and Suo. The emperor sent envoys many times to comfort the prime minister.
Bao Sheng said to Xiao He: Your Majesty, your clothes are drying in the sun and the hood of your car is wet with dew, but you have comforted you many times. This is because you are suspicious of you.
For your sake, it would be better to send all your descendants and brothers who are capable of fighting into the army, so that the emperor will trust you more.
So Xiao He followed his plan, and the king of Han was very happy.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu had passed away, and Liu Bang ascended the throne. He was awarded according to his merit. The ministers competed for merit. It was difficult to decide for more than a year. The emperor believed that Xiao He had made the greatest contribution, so he was first granted the title of Marquis of Feng, with a settlement of 8,000 households.
The heroes all said: We personally wore mail armor and held weapons. We experienced more than a hundred battles and dozens of rounds, conquering cities and territories.
Now Xiao He has no great achievements. He just expresses his opinions through writing and writing. He does not go to war, but his status is above us. Why is this?
The emperor said: Do you know about hunting? Everyone said: I know.
Asked again: Do you know hunting dogs?
Answered: I know.
The Emperor said: In hunting, dogs are the ones who chase and kill wild beasts, but humans are the ones who let loose and indicate where the wild beasts are.
Now you can only chase wild beasts, and the merit is similar to that of hunting dogs; as for Xiao He, he issues instructions, and the merit is the same as that of hunters.
And you are just following me with your own body, there are only three or two people, and dozens of people from Xiao He’s family are following me. The credit must not be forgotten!
From now on, all the ministers will not dare to say anything.
After the princes were awarded the title and their rankings were announced, they all said: Pingyang Hou Cao Shen was injured in seventy places. He made the greatest contribution to conquering the city and captured the territory, so he should be ranked first.
The emperor had already made the heroes surrender and granted Xiao He more titles. As for the position, there was no way to embarrass them anymore, but in his heart he still wanted Xiao He to be ranked first.
At that time, Eqiu, the Marquis of Guan Nei, came to visit him and said: "The opinions of all the ministers are wrong."
Although Cao Shen had the credit for strategically planning the country, this was only a temporary matter.
The emperor had a stalemate with Chu for five years, losing troops and generals, and fleeing many times. However, Xiao He often sent troops from Guanzhong to supplement them.
It wasn't the emperor's order to summon soldiers, but tens of thousands of people arrived when the emperor was in trouble.
Han and Chu had been guarding each other in Rongyang for many years, and there was no existing food in the army. Xiao He transferred food and wages from Guanzhong, and there was no shortage of supplies.
Although His Majesty lost Shandong many times, Xiao He always preserved Guanzhong and waited for His Majesty to return again. This is a tribute to all generations.
Now even if there are a hundred less people like Cao Shen, what will the Han lose?
The acquisition of Han does not necessarily have to wait for them to be preserved.
Why should the merit of one day be added to the merit of eternity!
Xiao He should be first, followed by Cao Shen.
The emperor said: OK.
So he made Xiao He the first, and gave him a sword and shoes to wear to the palace, so he didn't have to take small steps to enter the court.
The emperor said: I heard that those who want to be worthy will be rewarded. Although Xiao He's contribution is high, it can be clearly seen because of E Jun.
Therefore, Eqiu was granted the title of Marquis of Anping in addition to the two thousand households in the neighboring towns where Eqiu originally lived.
On this day, more than a dozen of Xiao He's parents and brothers were all rewarded with food.
Xiao He was also granted the title of 2,000 households to repay me for serving in Xianyang. Xiao He was the only one who gave me an extra 200 yuan.
Chen Xi rebelled, and the emperor personally led the army to Handan.
Han Xin rebelled in Guanzhong, and Empress Lu adopted Xiao He's strategy to kill Han Xin.
It is recorded in "Xin Zhuan".
When the emperor heard that Han Xin had been killed, he sent an envoy to worship the prime minister as the prime minister, granted five thousand households, and ordered 500 soldiers and a captain to protect the prime minister.
All the kings celebrated, but Zhao Ping expressed condolences.
Zhaoping was the original Marquis of Shuling of Qin.
After the fall of Qin, he became a commoner and very poor. He planted melons in the east of Chang'an City. The melons were very sweet, so the so-called "Shuling melon" in the world began in Zhaoping.
Zhao Ping said to Xiao He: The disaster began from now on.
The emperor is camping outside, but you stay behind in the court and do not suffer the pain of stone arrows. The reason why you are granted a title of guard is because the Marquis of Huaiyin has just rebelled internally and is suspicious of you.
Guards are assigned to you to protect you, not to favor you.
I hope you will refuse the reward and use all your family property to fund the army.
Xiao He followed Zhao Ping's plan, and the emperor was very happy.
In the autumn of this year, Yingbu rebelled, and the emperor personally led the army to attack. He sent envoys many times to ask what the prime minister was doing.
He replied: Because the emperor is in the army, the prime minister comforts and encourages the people and spends all his money to fund the military, just like Chen Xi did when he rebelled.
The retainer persuaded Xiao He again: "You will be exterminated soon."
As the Prime Minister of the country, your merits are the first and there are no more.
However, when you first entered the country, you were very popular with the people and have been doing so for more than ten years.
They have all attached themselves to you, but you are still working tirelessly to win the peace of the people.
The reason why the emperor has asked you many times is because he is afraid that you will disturb Guanzhong.
Now why don't you buy more land and borrow money at low interest rates to damage your reputation? The Emperor will definitely feel at ease.
So Xiao He listened to his plan, and the emperor was very happy.

After the emperor returned to court, Xiao He went to see him.
The emperor laughed and said: Now the prime minister is taking advantage of the people!
He gave Xiao He all the books written by the people and said: "You can apologize to the people yourself!"
Xiao He then made a request for the people: Chang'an is a narrow land, and there are many open spaces in the forest. They should be discarded and not used. I hope that the people can farm and not harvest the stalks for animal food.
The emperor was furious and said: Prime Minister accepted their bribe and asked for my Linyuan for them!
So Xiao He was handed over to Tingwei and imprisoned with torture instruments.
A few days later, Wang Weiwei served the emperor and asked: What serious crime has the Prime Minister committed that your Majesty detained him so roughly?
The emperor's divination said: I heard that Li Si served as the prime minister for the Qin Emperor. Any good deeds should be attributed to the Lord, and any wrongdoing should be attributed to himself.
Now the Prime Minister has been bribed by businessmen to ask for my forest garden for them, so that he can please the people himself, so he is arrested and punished.
Wang Weiwei said: It is the true responsibility of the prime minister to ask for the services that are beneficial to the people.
How can your Majesty suspect that the Prime Minister accepted money from businessmen!

If the prime minister is not seeking profit at this time, will he covet the businessman's money?
Moreover, Qin lost the world because he could not listen to his own faults. Li Si's fault with you was nothing to follow.
Why does Your Majesty think so little of the Prime Minister!
The emperor was not happy.
On this day, an envoy was sent to release Xiao He with the talisman of pardon.
Xiao He was old and always respectful. He went to court barefoot to apologize.
The emperor said: Prime Minister, don’t be like this!
