Accumulating good in oneself is like a person growing up without realizing it; accumulating evil in oneself is like a lamp burning oil, and it is not easy for people to see it.
Who can understand this truth unless he is a person who understands emotions and has insight into worldly situations?
This is the reason why Tang Yao and Yu Shun gained good reputations, but Xia Jie and Shang Zhou caused people pain and fear.
The consequences of good or evil actions are like shadows following human figures, reverberations following sounds.
Therefore, Jie and Zhou were violent and neglectful, the slanderous people were exploited, and the virtuous and wise people were hidden. As a result, Jie and Zhou's crimes became more and more obvious day by day, and the country became more and more chaotic. However, they were still peaceful and contented, thinking that they were like the sun in the sky, and finally gradually became corrupted and destroyed.
Those cruel and unkind monarchs did not perish all at once, but also gradually. Therefore, even though Jie and Zhou were immoral, they still reigned for more than ten years, which meant that they gradually declined and even perished.
Ce Wen said: The teachings of the three kings are imitated in different ways, and all have shortcomings. Some people say that they are eternal. Is there any difference in the intention of these two statements?
I have heard that the way of enjoying things without becoming sexually immoral and practicing them repeatedly without getting tired of them is called Tao.
The ways of the former kings must be biased and cannot be implemented, so in politics, there are sometimes dark and unworkable aspects. Just point out its biases and remedy its shortcomings.
Although the three kings follow different ways, they are not opposite. They are all designed to remedy mistakes and support decline. The reason why they are different is because the environment they encounter has changed.
Therefore Confucius said: The one who can govern the country without doing anything is Shun!
Shun only changed the calendar, changed the colors of carriages, horses, sacrifices, and clothing to comply with the destiny of heaven. The rest completely followed Yao's way of governing the country. Why should he change it!
Therefore, the king only changed the name of the system, but did not change the essence of the Tao.
However, the reason why the Xia Dynasty valued loyalty, the Yin Dynasty respected respect, and the Zhou Dynasty respected Wen is because when dynasties changed, the previous generation had faults, and this should be done in order to remedy them.
Confucius said: It can be known that the Yin Dynasty has increased or decreased according to the ritual system of the Xia Dynasty; that the Zhou Dynasty has increased or decreased according to the ritual system of the Yin Dynasty; and that others who succeeded the Zhou Dynasty have experienced hundreds of generations, but this can also be known.
Creation means that what hundreds of kings use are loyalty, respect, and culture.
The Xia Dynasty followed Yu and Shun, but did not mention additions or decreases. This is because the principles of the Xia Dynasty and Yu Shun were the same; the loyalty that the Xia Dynasty advocated was the same as that of Yu Shun.
The root of Tao comes from heaven. Heaven does not change and Tao does not change. Therefore, Yu inherited Shun's Tao, and Shun inherited Yao's Tao. The three saints taught each other and followed the same Tao. There were no measures to remedy disadvantages, so we do not say that they added or subtracted from Tao.
From this point of view, those who inherit the rule of the world have the same way; those who inherit the troubled times have to change their way.
Now that the Han Dynasty has inherited great chaos, it should reduce the literature of the Zhou Dynasty and use the loyalty of the Xia Dynasty.
Your Majesty has sage virtues and beautiful ways. He is saddened by the decline of the secular world and the unclearness of the royal way. Therefore, he elects virtuous and upright scholars, conducts discussions and tests, and intends to raise the virtues of benevolence and righteousness, clarify the emperor's legal system, and establish a peaceful way of governing the country.
I am ignorant and dishonest, recounting what I have heard, reciting what I have learned, and speaking the principles taught by the teacher, just to avoid forgetting them.
As for discussing the gains and losses of political affairs and studying the prosperity and poverty of society, these are the duties of ministers and assistants. The responsibilities of the three ministers and nine ministers are beyond the knowledge of Zhongshu. But I have a strange problem privately.
The world in ancient times is the world now, and the world now is the world in ancient times. They are the same world. In ancient times, the world was peaceful, in harmony, with beautiful customs. Things were done without orders and without restraint. Officials did not Evil, there are no thieves among the people, the prisons are empty, there are no prisoners, the kindness of the Lord has nourished the grass and trees, and spread to the four seas, the phoenix has flown, and the unicorn has appeared. If we compare the situation in ancient times to the present, how can it be so different?
What went wrong that led to this decline? I think maybe it goes against the ancient way of governing a country?
Maybe it goes against the laws of nature?
If you try to examine the past and trace it back to the laws of nature, you might be able to spot some problems, right?
Heaven gives creatures separately. Those who give sharp teeth will no longer give horns, and those who give wings will only give two feet. That is to say, if you accept the big one, you can no longer take the small one.
In ancient times, those who received salaries did not rely on manual labor for food, nor did they seek industrial and commercial benefits. This also accepted the big one and could not choose the small one, which was the same as God's will.
If you have already obtained the big one, and you go to take the small one, God cannot give it like that, let alone man?
This is the reason why people are suffering from insufficient food and clothing.
Those who are favored by the monarch and occupy high positions, whose families are well clothed, fed and provided with generous salaries, rely on their wealth and power to compete with the people below for profit. How can the people compare with them?
Therefore, those people used many slaves and maids, owned many cattle and sheep, expanded their fields and houses, expanded their industries, and increased their savings. They devoted themselves to these without any end, oppressed the people, made them frightened, and the people were exploited every day and gradually became poor.
The rich are extravagant and wasteful, the poor are poor and miserable; the poor are poor and miserable but those in higher positions do not provide relief, then the people will have no means of living; if the people have no means of life, the people will not even be afraid of death, so how can they be afraid of committing crimes!
This is the reason why there are many punishments, but treachery cannot be banned.
Therefore, families who enjoy their salaries should just live with their salaries and not compete with the people for profit-making industries. In this way, the benefits can be evenly distributed and the people can have enough money for their families.
This is the principle of heaven and the way of ancient times. The emperor should follow the legal system and the officials should abide by it.
So when Gongyizi was the prime minister of the State of Lu, he came home and saw his wife weaving silk. He was very angry and drove his wife away. When he was eating at home, he ate the sunflower seeds grown in his home. He angrily pulled out the sunflower seeds in the garden and said, "I already have a salary, do I want to take away the benefits of the vegetable growers and the weaver girls?"
In ancient times, wise men and gentlemen served as officials in this way. Therefore, the people respected their virtues and listened to their teachings. Influenced by their integrity, the people would not behave greedily and despicably.
By the end of the Zhou Dynasty, officials in the Qing Dynasty were less concerned about etiquette and justice and were eager to seek profits. They lost the spirit of humility and started lawsuits over land disputes.
Therefore, the poet hated and satirized them and said: That high Nanshan, the rocks are so stacked; O the famous Shi Yin, the people are all looking at you!
If an official has a heart for benevolence and righteousness, the people will naturally love benevolence and righteousness, and the customs will be kind; if an official is interested in profit, the people will not be upright, and the customs will be corrupted.
From this point of view, the emperor and the great officials are the examples that the people look up to and imitate. They are the people who look up to and imitate them from afar. How can they be in the position of sages and behave like common people?
Those who are busy seeking financial gain and often worried about poverty are the thoughts of the common people; those who are busy seeking benevolence and righteousness and often worried about not being able to educate the people are the thoughts of the officials.
"Book of Changes" says: Carrying things on your back and riding in a car will lead to the arrival of robbers.
Riding in a carriage means that you are in the position of a gentleman, and carrying things is the business of a villain. This means that if you are in the position of a gentleman but behave like a commoner, disaster will definitely come to you.
If you are in the position of a gentleman and do what a gentleman should do, then there is nothing else you can do except be like Gong Yixiu who was the prime minister of the state of Lu.
"Spring and Autumn" emphasizes unity, which is the eternal principle of heaven and earth and a common truth between ancient and modern times.
Nowadays, the principles stated by teachers are different from each other, and people's opinions are also different from each other. The research directions of various schools of thought are different, and their intentions are also different. Therefore, the superiors cannot grasp the unified standards, the laws and regulations have been changed many times, and the people below do not know how to abide by them.
I believe that all subjects that do not belong to the Six Arts and Confucian academic theories are prohibited and they are not allowed to develop in the same way.
Once the eccentric doctrines disappear, the academic system can be unified, the legal system can be understood, and the people will know who to obey.
After the countermeasures were completed, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty appointed Dong Zhongshu as the Prime Minister of Jiangdu to assist King Yi.
Liu Fei, King of Yi, was the elder brother of Emperor Wu of Han Dynasty. He was always very arrogant and liked to be brave.
Dong Zhongshu supported King Yi with courtesy and justice, and King Yi respected him very much.
After a while, King Yi asked Dong Zhongshu: King Gou Jian of Yue and the officials Xie Yong, Wen Zhong, and Fan Li conspired to attack the state of Wu, and finally reduced the state of Wu.
Confucius said that King Zhou of Yin had three benevolent people, and I think King Gou Jian of Yue also had three benevolent people.
During the Spring and Autumn Period, Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong to answer some difficult questions. I have questions, please explain.
Dong Zhongshu replied: I am ignorant and cannot answer your question.
I heard that in the Spring and Autumn Period, Duke Xi of Lu asked Liu Xiahui, an official of Lu: I want to attack Qi, what do you think? Liu Xiahui said: No.
When he returned home, he looked worried and said, "I heard that attacking other countries does not involve virtuous people. Why does the king want to attack Qi? Why do you ask me?"
Liu Xiahui was just questioned and felt ashamed, let alone plotting a false surrender to attack the state of Wu?
From this point of view, there is no benevolent person in Yue State.
A benevolent person upholds his righteousness but does not seek personal gain, and expounds his way but does not care about his own merits. Therefore, among Confucius's disciples, even underage children are ashamed to talk about the Five Hegemons, because the Five Hegemons promote deception and force and do not pay attention to benevolence and righteousness.
The king of Yue and his ministers were just practicing unfair tricks, so they were not worthy of discussion by Confucius's disciples.
The Five Hegemons are wiser than other princes, but compared with the Three Kings, they are like jade-like stones compared with beautiful jade. King Yi said: Well said.
When Dong Zhongshu governed the country, he used the disasters and changes recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals to find out the reasons for the misalignment of yin and yang. Therefore, when praying for rain, he closed the yang and moved the yin. When he stopped the rain, he closed the yin and moved the yang. This method of praying for rain to stop waterlogging has been implemented throughout Jiangdu, and everyone does what they want.
Later, Dong Zhongshu was deposed as a middle doctor.
Prior to this, fires broke out successively in the Gaomiao Temple in Liaodong County where emperors of the Han Dynasty worshiped their ancestors, and in the Gaoyuan Hall in Changling, where the emperors of the Han Dynasty worshiped their ancestors. Dong Zhongshu deduced the relationship between fires from heaven and the human world. He wrote the draft of the memorial but did not submit it. The master's father Yan came to visit Dong Zhongshu and read the draft of the memorial in private. He was always jealous of Dong Zhongshu, so he stole the draft of the memorial and handed it to Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty summoned many Confucian scholars and asked them to read the draft of Dong Zhongshu's memorial. Dong Zhongshu's student Lu Bushu didn't know that this draft of the memorial was written by his teacher, and thought it was very ignorant.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty handed Dong Zhongshu over to the officials for questioning and sentenced him to death. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty issued an edict to pardon him. From then on, Dong Zhongshu did not dare to talk about disasters and changes.
Dong Zhongshu is honest and upright.
At that time, the Han Dynasty was using troops from surrounding ethnic minorities. Gongsunhong's research on "Gongyang Chunqiu" was not as good as Dong Zhongshu's. However, Gongsunhong catered to the secular world, gained great power, and became a high official.
Dong Zhongshu thought Gongsun Hong was flattering, but Gongsun Hong hated Dong Zhongshu.
Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, was also the brother of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. He was particularly indulgent, cruel and arrogant, and repeatedly murdered two thousand stone officials sent by the imperial court.
Gongsun Hong told Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty: Only Dong Zhongshu can serve as the king of Jiaoxi.
King Liu Duan of Jiaoxi heard that Dong Zhongshu was a famous Confucian master and treated him with respect.
Dong Zhongshu was afraid that he would be punished by accident over time, so he resigned and went home on the grounds of old age and illness.
Dong Zhongshu served as prime minister of Jiangdu and Jiaoxi, assisting the arrogant princes and kings. He set an example for his subordinates by setting an example for his subordinates. He went to the eunuch many times to give outright advice, and formulated edicts to be implemented in the country. Both Jiangdu and Jiaoxi where he was located were well governed.
After he resigned from office and returned home, he didn't care about the family property at all. He just immersed himself in reading and writing books.
Dong Zhongshu was recuperating at home. If the court discussed important issues, it would send envoys and the court official Zhang Tang to his home to ask for his opinions. Dong Zhongshu's answers were all well-founded.
From the time when Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, Wei Qihou Dou Ying and Wu'an Hou Tian successively became prime ministers and began to promote Confucianism. Dong Zhongshu responded by promoting Confucius and suppressing hundreds of schools of thought.
It was Dong Zhongshu who set up officials to manage schools and recommended talents, filial piety and honesty in the prefectures and counties.
Dong Zhongshu died at home in old age. Later, his family moved to Maoling County, and his son and grandson became high officials based on their knowledge.
Dong Zhongshu's works all clarify the purpose of Confucian classics. Together with memorials and teachings, there are a total of 123 works.
There are dozens of articles explaining the gains and losses of the "Spring and Autumn" records, as well as "Wen Ju", "Jade Cup", "Fan Dew", "Qingming" and "Bamboo Forest", with more than 100,000 words, all of which have been passed down to later generations.
I selected the content that is relevant to today's society and the imperial court and wrote it in the article.
Praising day: Liu Xiang praised: Dong Zhongshu has the ability to be an assistant to the king. Even Yi Yin and Lu Wang cannot surpass him. Guan Zhong and Yan Ying are the assistants of the overlord, so I am afraid they are not as good as him.
Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin believed that Yi Yin and Lu Wang were the companions of a saint, and a king could not rise without them.
So when Yan Yuan died, Confucius said, "Oh!"
Heaven destroys me. Only Yan Yuan can compare with Yi Yin and Lu Wang. As for Zai Wo, Zigong, Ziyou, Zixia and others, they cannot be included in the ranks of saints.
After the Western Han Dynasty succeeded the Qin Dynasty and the burning of scholarship, Dong Zhongshu's "Six Classics" fell apart. So he put down his work and devoted himself to studying Confucian classics, which enabled later scholars to have a systematic and consistent understanding of Confucianism and became the leader of the group of Confucian scholars.
However, when examining the origins of his mentors and friends and looking at their influence on each other, Dong Zhongshu could not catch up with Zi You and Zi Xia, but it is wrong to say that Guan Zhong and Yan Ying were not as good as him, and Yi Yin and Lu Wang were not as good as him.
Liu Xiang's great-grandson Liu Gong is a gentleman who is good at commenting on figures. He believes that Liu Xin's evaluation of Dong Zhongshu is appropriate.
summary:
Dong Zhongshu, a scholar from Guangchuan, studied the "Spring and Autumn" Annals in his youth and became a court academician during Emperor Jing's reign. He lectured from behind a curtain, with senior disciples teaching junior ones, and some students never saw him. He was so devoted to his studies that he did not look at his garden for three years. His dignified conduct earned him the respect of all scholars.

When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he sought virtuous scholars, and Dong Zhongshu responded to the emperor's policy questions. The emperor asked about the principles of governance, the rise and fall of dynasties, and how to achieve harmony between heaven and humanity. He inquired why the virtuous ways of ancient sage kings declined, why disasters occurred, and how to reform governance to bring peace and prosperity.

Dong Zhongshu's countermeasure explained that heaven sends disasters to warn rulers of moral failings. He emphasized that diligent study and virtuous conduct are essential for good governance. He argued that ritual and music are tools for education, and that a ruler must first rectify his own heart to rectify the court and the people. He criticized the Qin dynasty for abandoning moral education and relying solely on punishment, leading to its rapid downfall. He urged the Han dynasty to reform its institutions, establish a national university, and promote Confucian education to cultivate virtuous officials.

The emperor, impressed, asked further about the differences between ancient rulers like Yao and Shun, who governed with ease, and King Wen of Zhou, who was constantly busy. Dong Zhongshu explained that the times differed: Yao and Shun inherited a peaceful world, while King Wen faced chaos. He stressed that the essence of governance—benevolence, righteousness, and ritual—remains constant, but methods must adapt to circumstances. He advocated for selecting officials based on merit, not seniority, and for establishing schools to train talent.

In a third response, Dong Zhongshu elaborated on the harmony between heaven and humanity. He argued that heaven's will is reflected in natural phenomena, and rulers must align their actions with it. He criticized the Qin for its harsh laws and urged the Han to adopt the Xia dynasty's emphasis on loyalty to remedy the Zhou's excessive refinement. He proposed banning non-Confucian teachings to unify thought and law.

After his countermeasures, Dong Zhongshu served as prime minister to the King of Jiangdu, advising him with propriety. He later became a palace attendant but was nearly executed after a rival stole a draft of his memorial on disasters. Pardoned, he remained honest and upright. He later served the King of Jiaoxi, but fearing danger, he retired to write. His works, including over 100,000 words on the "Spring and Autumn," clarified Confucian principles. He died at home, and his descendants became high officials.

Liu Xiang praised Dong Zhongshu as a king's assistant, comparable to Yi Yin and Lu Wang, surpassing Guan Zhong and Yan Ying. However, Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin argued that Dong, while a leader among Confucians after the Qin's destruction of texts, could not match Yi Yin or Lu Wang, though he was greater than Guan Zhong and Yan Ying. Liu Xin's view was later deemed accurate.

Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang County, had the same name as Emperor Wu, Kuai Che.
When the Chu and Han Dynasties first emerged, Wu Chen attacked and pacified Fangdi, and was known as Wu Xinjun.
Kuai Tong lobbied Xu Gong, the magistrate of Fanyang County, and said: "I am a citizen of Fanyang, my name is Kuai Tong. I feel sorry for you that you are about to die, so I express my condolences."
Nevertheless, I congratulate you for having a chance to survive because of me, Kuai Tong.
Xu Gong thanked him repeatedly and asked: "Why do you express condolences?"
Kuai Tong said: You have been the county magistrate for more than ten years. You have killed other people's fathers, made other people's sons orphans, chopped off people's feet, and given people tattoos. Too many people have suffered.
The reason why loving fathers and filial sons dare not insert a knife into your belly is because they are afraid of the laws of the Qin Dynasty.
Now the world is in chaos, and the Qin Dynasty's decrees cannot be implemented. In this case, those loving fathers and filial sons will rush to stab you with bayonets in your belly to avenge you and achieve fame. This is the reason for my condolences.
Xu Gong asked again: "Why do you congratulate me on getting a husband and finding a way out?"
Kuai Tong replied: Lord Wu Xin who traveled to the country did not know that I was incompetent, so he sent people to inquire about his good or bad luck. Now I am going to meet and persuade him, and say to him: You must defeat the enemy before you gain the territory, and conquer the city before occupying it. I privately feel that it is very dangerous.
If you adopt my strategy, you will gain land without fighting, occupy the city without attacking, and be able to pacify thousands of miles by sending messages. Is this okay?
He will ask: What is your strategy?
I took the opportunity to reply: Magistrate Fan Yang should have organized his army, guarded the city, and resisted, but because he was cowardly and fearful of death, greedy and fond of wealth, he wanted to surrender the city to you first.
If he is the first to surrender to you and you do not give him any favors, then all the cities in the border areas will tell each other: The magistrate of Fanyang County was the first to surrender and was killed. We will definitely defend the city and it will be as difficult to capture as Jincheng Tangchi.
For your sake, it would be better to welcome Magistrate Fanyang with a yellow-covered and red-wheeled chariot, and let him ride on the border between Yan and Pang to show off. Then the cities on the border will tell each other: Magistrate Fanyang surrendered first and gained wealth. There will be a race to surrender, as easy as a mud ball rolling down a hillside.
Create what I call the strategy of pacifying Qianli by sending a message. , Xu Gong thanked him repeatedly and prepared carriages and horses to send Kuai Tong away.
Kuai Tong persuaded the military ministers with these words.
The military officials used a hundred chariots and two hundred cavalry to greet Duke Xu.
When Yan and Fang heard about this, more than thirty cities surrendered, just as expected by Kuai Tong's strategy.
Later, the Han general Han Xin captured the King of Wei, conquered Tiao and Dai, made Yan surrender, and pacified the three kingdoms one after another, and then led his troops eastward to attack Qi.
The army had not yet passed Pingyuan County. When I heard that Liu Bang, the king of Han, had sent Li Shiqi to persuade Qi to surrender, Han Xin wanted to stop the advance.
Kuai Tong lobbied Han Xin and said: General, you were ordered by the King of Han to attack the State of Qi, and the King of Han sent a separate envoy who was also a spy to persuade the State of Qi to surrender. Is there an edict ordering you to stop attacking?
Why not march?
Moreover, Mr. Li, as a scholar, rode there and persuaded more than 70 cities of Qi to surrender with his sharp tongue. General, you led tens of thousands of troops to capture more than 50 cities of Zhao.
Having been a general for several years is not as great as the contribution of a Confucian scholar.
So Han Xin thought what he said made sense, adopted his suggestion, and finally crossed the Yellow River.
The King of Qi had listened to Li Shiqi's persuasion, so he left him behind, drank and had fun together, and removed the defense against the Han Dynasty.
Han Xin therefore attacked the Qi army in Lixia and came to Linmiao City.
The King of Qi thought that Li Shiqi had deceived him, so he put him in boiling water and boiled him to death. As a result, he was defeated and fled.
Han Xin finally pacified Qi and established himself as the acting king of Qi.
At that time, the King of Han was under siege in Rongyang, so he sent Zhang Liang to make Han Xin the official King of Qi, comfort him, and make him firmly side with the King of Han.
Xiang Yu also sent Wu She to persuade Han Xin to join forces with him.
Kuai Tong knew that the change of the world situation depended on Han Xin, and wanted to persuade Han Xin to betray the Han Dynasty, so he first hinted at Han Xin in cryptic words: I once learned the art of physiognomy, and observing your face, I can only be made a marquis, and you will always be in danger; but looking at your back, it is very noble and difficult to tell.
Han Xin asked: What do you mean?
Kuai Tong then asked others to go away, and then said: When the world first rises up, heroes and heroes establish themselves as princes and kings, raise their arms and shout, and the people of the world gather like clouds and mist, are mixed and accumulated like fish scales, and rise up quickly like a strong wind.
People often only worry about overthrowing the Qin Dynasty.
Now Liu Bang and Xiang Yu are fighting, and countless people have been displaced.
The King of Han led hundreds of thousands of troops to defend Gong and Luo. Taking advantage of the dangers of the mountains and rivers, he fought several battles in vain. He was defeated and fled without rescue. He was defeated in Rongyang, wounded in Chenggao, and fled to Wan and Ye. This is said to be a person whose wisdom and courage are in trouble.
The Chu people raised their troops in Pengcheng, fought many battles, and were invincible. They marched to Rongyang, taking advantage of the victory, and shocked the world. However, they were blocked between Jing and Suo, and they were unable to advance near Xishan. It has been three years now.
Their vigor was thwarted at the steep pass, the treasury was depleted of food, and the people were miserable, not knowing who to surrender to.
In my opinion, unless there are sages in the world. Otherwise, it will be impossible to eliminate the disasters in the world.
Now the fate of Liu Bang and Xiang Yu is in your hands.
If you help the King of Han, the King of Han will win; if you join forces with the King of Chu, the King of Chu will succeed.
I am willing to express my sincere sincerity to you, but I am afraid that you will not accept my suggestion.
Now for your sake, it would be better for both of them to benefit and coexist together. If the world is divided into three parts and they stand as a tripod, no one will dare to attack first.
With your wisdom and wisdom, you have many armies in mail, occupying the powerful state of Qi, uniting Yan and Zhao, sending troops to the empty land to control their rear, obeying the people's will, heading west to stop the fighting between Chu and Han, and saving the soldiers from death. No one in the world dares to disobey!
If you own the land between Huai and Si according to the original territory of Qi, appease the princes with your kindness, give them a home in peace, and treat the wise men with courtesy, then all the princes in the world will come to worship Qi.
I heard that if you don’t accept a gift from God, you will be blamed; if you don’t act when the time comes, you will get disaster. I hope you will think about it carefully.
Han Xin said: The King of Han treats me well, how can I be so unjust and ungrateful for the sake of profit?
Kuai Tong said: At first, Zhang Er, the king of Changshan, and Chen Yu, the lord of Cheng'an, formed a life-and-death relationship. When they quarreled over the affairs of Zhang Wei and Chen Shi, the king of Changshan fled with his head in his arms and joined the king of Han. He borrowed troops and fought in the north of Han. Lord Cheng'an died on the south bank of the Sishui River, and the family was divided.
When the two of them got together, they were so close that no one in the world could compare with them, but in the end they killed each other and perished. Why is this?
Disasters arise from too many desires and the unpredictable nature of the human heart.
Now you are loyal to the King of Han, and your relationship is no closer than those two, and the things you argue about are often more important than those between Zhang Wei and Chen Shi. So I think your belief that the King of Han will not harm you is wrong.
Dafu Wenzhong enabled the Yue Kingdom to survive, which was about to be destroyed, and enabled Gou Jian to dominate the Central Plains and become famous but was killed.
As the saying goes: When the wild birds are hunted down, the hunting dogs will be cooked and killed; when the enemy's country is destroyed, the advisers will die.
Therefore, in terms of making friends, no one can surpass Zhang Er and Chen Yu; in terms of loyal ministers, no one can compare with Dafu Wenzhong.
These two examples should be considered as enough reference. I hope you will think about it carefully.
Moreover, I have heard that those whose bravery and strategy make the monarch fearful will not be able to save their lives, and those whose achievements are overwhelming will not be rewarded.
You crossed the West River, captured the King of Wei, captured Xia Shuo alive, captured Jingxing, punished Cheng Anjun for his crimes and killed him. You were able to issue orders in the state of Chang, threaten the state of Yan, pacify the state of Qi, defeat the hundreds of thousands of soldiers of the state of Chu in the south, finally killed Lung Qie, and sent people to the west to report your merits to the king of Han.
Now your merits are so high that it is hard to reward you, and your majesty makes Jun Feng fearful. He surrenders to the Chu State, and the Chu people do not trust you; and surrenders to the Han State, and the Han people are afraid of you.
Who do you want to join with these achievements and prestige?
You are in the position of a minister and have a reputation that is higher than the world. I am really worried about you.
Han Xin said: Sir, go and rest for now, I want to think about it.
A few days later, Kuai Tong advised again: Whether one can listen to advice is a sign of success or failure; whether one's planning is appropriate is the key to survival.
If you work as a servant, you will lose the authority of Wan Chenggeren; if you keep a low salary, you will lose the opportunity to become a minister or prime minister.
If you understand this truth in your heart but dare not make a decision and take action, disaster will come one day.
Therefore, if a tiger hesitates, it is better than a bee or a scorpion stinging a person; if Meng Ben hesitates, it is better than a child to do it resolutely.
This means that the most important thing is to take practical action.
Achievements are difficult to achieve but easy to fail. Opportunities are hard to meet but easy to lose. Once the opportunity is lost, it will not come again: I hope you will not doubt my strategy.

Recently, Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, was appointed as the Great Sima Wei General, and Dingming, the Marquis of Yang'an, was appointed as the Great Sima Hussar General.

He is loyal and has no regard for himself, but he falls into the trap in vain.

The rainbow is bright but the sun is dim, and the evil spirit is dark but never disperses.

Look up at the moon and show your true heart, calling the sky to discern the right and wrong.
The autumn wind is meditative for me, and the floating clouds are gloomy for me.

When the monarch loses his support, he will miss me. A few years later, Xifu died, which was consistent with his final words.
Praise: Zhongni said that he hated eloquent people who harmed the country. Kuai Tong killed three heroes with just one mouthful. How lucky that he was not cooked to death!
Wu was in a country in turmoil. As the mastermind, he could not always be loyal, but he planned a deceitful strategy for the King of Huainan. Didn't he deserve to be killed?
There are records of the exile of four sinners in the Book of Books, and there is the poem "Blue Fly" in the Book of Songs. Since the Spring and Autumn Period, there have been too many disasters.
In the past, Ziyun plotted to kill Duke Huan of Lu, but Duke Yin of Lu was killed; Leshu framed the Shao family, and Duke Li of Jin was killed; Shuniu Zhong was driven away, and his uncle and grandson died; Qiu Bo slandered the Ji family, and Duke Zhao of Lu fled; Fei Ji married a Qin girl for King Ping of Chu, but Prince Jian fled; the prime minister slandered Wu Zixu, and Fu Chai perished; Li Yuan He sacrificed his sister, but Lord Chun Shen died; Shangguan Zilan framed Qu Yuan, and King Huai of Chu was captured by Qin; Chang Gao slandered Li Si, but Qin II was forced to hang himself; Yi Li forged a letter of alliance, but Song Cuo died; Jiang Chong created a witchcraft prison, and the prince committed suicide; Xifu Gong fabricated lies to deceive the monarch, and King Shu Ping was punished. These incidents are all caused by small things, causing big problems, and alienation harming relatives. How terrible!
How terrible!
summary:
Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang, lobbied Xu Gong, the magistrate of Fanyang, during the Chu-Han conflict. He warned Xu Gong that his harsh rule had created many enemies, and with Qin laws no longer enforceable, he was in danger. Kuai Tong then proposed a plan to Wu Chen, Wu Xinjun: rather than attacking cities, he should welcome Xu Gong with honor to encourage other cities to surrender. Wu Chen followed this advice, and over thirty cities surrendered without battle. Later, Kuai Tong persuaded Han Xin to attack Qi despite Li Shiqi's diplomatic mission, arguing that military conquest would earn greater merit. Han Xin agreed, crossed the Yellow River, and defeated Qi, leading to Li Shiqi's execution. Kuai Tong later urged Han Xin to betray Liu Bang and create a tripartite balance of power, warning that Han Xin's achievements made him a threat to the Han king. Han Xin hesitated, citing Liu Bang's kindness, and declined. Kuai Tong, fearing retribution, feigned madness. After Han Xin's execution, Liu Bang summoned Kuai Tong, who defended himself by saying a dog barks at those not its master. Liu Bang pardoned him. Kuai Tong later served as a guest to Cao Shen, the prime minister of Qi, and recommended the reclusive scholars Shu Guo and Liang Shijun. He also wrote a book on lobbying strategies.

Wu Bei, a descendant of Wu Zixu, served as a lieutenant in Huainan under King Liu An. When the king plotted rebellion, Wu Bei repeatedly admonished him, arguing that the Han dynasty was stable and prosperous, with orderly governance, thriving trade, and subdued enemies. The king dismissed this, citing the Qin collapse as precedent. Wu Bei countered that Qin's tyranny had caused widespread suffering, while the Han emperor ruled with benevolence and had popular support. He warned that rebellion would fail, as the king's forces were weak and the times were peaceful. The king ignored him and proceeded with plans, but the conspiracy was discovered. Wu Bei surrendered and confessed, but was executed despite his earlier praise of Han, as Zhang Tang argued his initial role in planning the rebellion was unforgivable.

Jiang Chong, originally named Jiang Qi, fled to Chang'an after a feud with Prince Liu Dan of Zhao. He reported the prince's incest and adultery, leading to Liu Dan's deposition. Jiang Chong gained Emperor Wu's favor through his appearance and advice on foreign policy. He was appointed to supervise the capital, enforcing laws against luxury and arresting offenders. He detained the prince's envoy for using the imperial road, earning the emperor's praise. Later, fearing the prince would harm him after the emperor's death, Jiang Chong fabricated a witchcraft scandal, accusing the prince of cursing the emperor. He tortured confessions, killing tens of thousands. The prince, unable to defend himself, arrested and executed Jiang Chong. The prince's rebellion failed, and Emperor Wu later annihilated Jiang Chong's clan.

Xifu Gong, a scholar from Heyang, gained fame through his friend Fu Yan, the queen's father. With Sun Chong, he fabricated a plot against King Shuping Liu Yun, accusing him of witchcraft. The king and his associates were executed, and Xifu Gong was made Marquis of Yiling. He became a close advisor to Emperor Ai, criticizing officials and proposing policies, including expanding irrigation canals. He suggested a deceptive strategy to weaken the Xiongnu by forging letters, but General Gongsun Lu opposed it. Xifu Gong also urged military preparations based on astrological signs, but Prime Minister Wang Jia warned against flattery and deceit. The emperor initially supported Xifu Gong, but after a solar eclipse, Dong Xian undermined him. Xifu Gong was dismissed and later accused of cursing the emperor. He died in prison, and his family was exiled. After Emperor Ai's death, Sun Chong and others were also exiled.

The text concludes with a lament on the dangers of eloquent but harmful advisors, citing historical examples from the Spring and Autumn period to the Han dynasty, where slander and deceit led to disasters, including the deaths of rulers and the ruin of states.

If Uncle Sun Qiao, a senior official in the Lu State, wanted to dominate the state affairs of the Lu State, he framed his elder brother Ji Sun Xingfu to the Jin State. The state of Jin arrested and imprisoned Xingfu to disturb the state of Lu. The Spring and Autumn Annals paid attention to and recorded this incident.
Now Fu Yan has given up the decree and destroyed the clan, interfered and disrupted the court affairs, and made friends with ministers to deceive the emperor. He set up schemes, which is the main source of trouble. He should be charged with the same crime as Zhu Bo and Tang Xuan, both of whom are guilty of treason.
The emperor exempted Fu Yan from the third-class death penalty, cut off a quarter of Fu Yan's food, and asked the visitors to summon the prime minister to the prison where the prisoners were held.
Zhu Bo committed suicide and the fief was taken back.
At the beginning, Zhu Bo was promoted from imperial censor to prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Yangxiang. Zhao Xuan was promoted from the Shaofu to the imperial censor, and he received his official position in the front hall together. When he was led to the hall to receive his orders, there was a loud sound like the ringing of a bell.
This incident is recorded in the "Five Elements Chronicles".
Zan said: Xue Xuan and Zhu Bo both came from Zushi, and successively held official positions and were promoted to prime ministers.
Xue Xuan's place was well governed, and he was a teacher of the officials of the time. When he became prime minister, he lost his reputation because he showed his shrewdness by being harsh and cumbersome, and his talents were indeed limited.
Zhu Bo worked hard to make progress without considering morality and justice, which was nothing worthy of praise. He also saw that during the Xiaocheng era, he entrusted important responsibilities to ministers, so he resorted to abusing his power.
The current monarch has changed, and his likes and dislikes are different from those of the previous monarchs. Zhu Bo relied on the Ding family and the Fu family, and obeyed the Marquis of Kongxiang.
After the incident was discovered, he was blamed and fell into the charge of deceiving the emperor. When the truth was revealed, he drank the poison.
Wang Yu said: Wang Chong has been cheating for a long time!
Celi is like this too!
summary:
Xue Xuan, a native of Tan County, Shuhai, rose from minor official posts to become a respected administrator. Known for his integrity and legal expertise, he served as Censor Zhongcheng under Emperor Cheng, advocating for simpler governance and criticizing harsh laws that disrupted social harmony. His memorials urged leniency and moral cultivation, which the emperor approved. As governor of Linhuai and later Chenliu, he quelled bandits and earned widespread respect. In Zuo Fengyi, he skillfully handled corrupt officials like Yang Zhan and Xie You, using subtle pressure to force their resignations, while also reassigning ineffective magistrates to improve governance. Xue Xuan’s fair and compassionate rule, including his handling of a jailer’s suicide, won him praise. He was promoted to Shaofu and later, on Gu Yong’s recommendation, became Imperial Censor and then Prime Minister, enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang. However, his tenure was marred by criticism for being overly meticulous and lacking depth in classical learning. After failing to quell uprisings in Guanghan and mishandling tax collection during a funeral, he was dismissed by the emperor for incompetence. Later reinstated as a special advisor, he was again dismissed for associating with the disgraced Chunyu Chang. His later years were troubled by family discord with his brother Xue Xiu over mourning rites, and his son Xue Kuang’s violent attack on Shen Xian, who had slandered Xue Xuan. Despite legal debates, Xue Kuang was exiled, and Xue Xuan died at home as a commoner.

Zhu Bo, from Duling, began as a poor county official, known for his boldness and friendship with elite sons like Chen Xian. He famously disguised himself to save Chen Xian from prison, enduring punishment himself, which launched his reputation. Under Wang Feng, he became magistrate of several counties, excelling in governance. As governor of Jizhou, he astutely handled a flood of complaints by issuing swift verdicts, astonishing officials. In Langye, he aggressively reformed lax customs, dismissing sick officials and enforcing strict dress codes, while using intimidation and rewards to control subordinates. His tenure in Zuo Fengyi was marked by cunning and harshness, such as rehabilitating a scarred thief as an informant and exposing corrupt officials through psychological tactics. Promoted to Da Si Nong and later Tingwei, he demonstrated legal acumen by correctly predicting case outcomes. He became Grand Sikong under Emperor Ai, advocating for restoring the Censor’s office over the Grand Sikong post, arguing it better suited the Han system. He also reversed the abolition of provincial governors, favoring their supervisory role. Frugal and workaholic, Zhu Bo shunned luxury but cultivated a network of guests, aiding their ambitions. However, he became entangled in court intrigues, allying with Fu Yan to please Empress Dowager Dingtao, leading to the dismissal of rivals like Kong Guang. As Prime Minister, he was pressured by the empress dowager to impeach Fu Xi, but the emperor discovered his collusion. Interrogated, Zhu Bo was charged with treason for manipulating affairs with relatives, and he committed suicide, his fief revoked. His rise and fall exemplified ambition without moral restraint, as noted in historical critiques.

Among the rulers of Nanyi, Yelang is the largest. To the west, Mimo is the largest, and Dian is the largest. From Dian to the north, Qiongdu is the largest.
People in these countries all wear cone-shaped buns, cultivate fields, and have their own small towns and villages.
In addition, from Tongshi in the west to Yeyu in the north, they are named Lun and Kunming. They all have braided hair and move around with the grazing livestock. They have no fixed residence and no ruler. Their range of activities is about several thousand miles.
From Song to the northeast, the king's length is calculated by ten, and the migration and extraction are the largest.
From Judu to the northeast, the ruler's length is calculated by ten, and Ran Xiao is the largest.
Among the customs there, some are settled and some are migrating.
To the west of Shu County, from Ranji to the northeast, the king's length is calculated by ten, and the white horse is the largest. These are all Di tribe.
The above are all barbarians outside the southwest of Bajun and Shujun.
At first, King Chu Wei sent General Zhuang Cuo to lead his army up the Yangtze River and captured the area west of Bajun and Qianzhong County.
Zhuang Qi is a descendant of King Zhuang of Chu. Zhuang Chu arrived at Dianchi Lake.
Dianchi Lake has a radius of three hundred miles, and beside the pool is flat land, fertile and fertile, with a radius of several thousand miles. Zhuang Zhen relied on the power of his army to pacify this area and make it belong to the Chu State.
Zhuang Jiao planned to return to Chu State to report, but the Qin State attacked Chu State and captured Bajun and Qianzhong County of Chu State. The road was blocked and he could not return, so he relied on his army to become king in Yunnan. Zhuang Jiao changed her clothes and followed the customs of Nabu in order to rule the barbarians in Nabu.
During the Qin Dynasty, this area was captured, the Five Feet Road was roughly opened, and officials were appointed for some countries in this area.
After more than ten years, the Qin Dynasty perished.
By the rise of the Han Dynasty, all these countries were abandoned and the original borders of Shu were used as passersby.
Some people from Bajun and Shujun secretly went out to do business in this area in exchange for horses from the capital, slaves and yaks from the Fen tribe. As a result, Bajun and Shujun became prosperous.
In the sixth year of the founding of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wang Hui was ordered to attack Shuyue. The Shuyue people killed King Ying of Dongyue and then told Wang Hui.
Taking advantage of his military power, Wang Hui sent Pan Yang to order Tang Meng to euphemistically inform Nanyue of the Han Dynasty's intention to launch an army.
The people of southern Guangdong entertained Tang Meng with wolfberry sauce from Shu. Tang Meng asked about the origin of the wolfberry sauce. The answer was: It was brought from Pangkejiang in the northwest. The Yangke River is several miles wide and flows under Panyu City.
Tang Meng returned to Chang'an and asked businessmen in Shu, only to learn that only Shu produced wolfberry sauce, and many Shu people secretly sold it to Yelang.
Yelang is close to the Pangke River, which is more than a hundred paces wide and can be used for boats. The people of Nanyue used their property to make Yelang surrender. The influence of Nanyue reached directly to the west of Tongshi, but they still could not use Yelang like a vassal.
Tang Meng then wrote to Emperor Mowu saying: The king of Nanyue took the yellow house and decorated the left banner. He occupied a territory of more than 10,000 miles from east to west. In name, he was a vassal of the country, but in fact he was the lord of a state.
Now Changsha Kingdom and Yuzhang County are going to conquer, and most of the waterways are cut off and difficult to navigate.
I heard that Yelang's elite troops, perhaps numbering 100,000, sailed down the Yangke River by boat to catch them by surprise. This was a clever trick to subdue southern Guangdong.
If we rely on the strength of the Han Dynasty and the wealth of the two counties of Ba and Shu, it will be easy to open the road to Yelang and set up officials for those places.
The emperor agreed to Tang Meng's suggestion.
So Tang Meng was appointed as Lieutenant General Lang, leading a thousand soldiers and more than 10,000 servants carrying food and baggage. Entering Yelang from Baduguan, he immediately met Yelang Hou Duotong.
Tang Meng rewarded Duotong heavily, told him the stakes, and agreed with Duotong to appoint officials to Yelang and let Duotong's son hold an official position similar to a county magistrate.
The small countries near Yelang all coveted the Han Dynasty's silk, and believed that the Han Dynasty's road to this area was difficult and dangerous, and they would not be able to possess them after all, so they temporarily accepted the alliance between Duotong and Tang Meng.
Tang Meng reported to the court, and the court designated the location of Yelang and these small countries as Jianwei County.
The Han Dynasty recruited infantrymen from Bajun and Shujun to build roads from Fendao to the Yangke River.
Sima Xiangru, a native of Shu County, also wrote a letter saying that counties could be established in the Qiongdu and Jiadu areas of Xiyi.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty asked Sima Xiangru to go to the Xiyi area as a lieutenant general and inform the Xiyi people of the court's intentions. The situation was the same as that of Nanyi. The imperial court appointed a county captain to Nahuo and established more than ten counties under the management of Shu County.
At this time, the four counties of Ba, Shu, Guangmo, and Hanzhong were building roads leading to the southwestern Yi region, and the transportation of grain and wages required for road construction was difficult.
After several years, the road was not repaired. Many of the soldiers who built the road died due to fatigue, hunger, and the heat and humidity. There were many rebellions in the southwestern barbarians. They mobilized troops to attack the rebels, but they spent money and resources without any results.
These situations made the emperor very worried, so he sent Gongsun Hong to those places to inspect and understand.
Gongsun Hong came back and reported that there was no benefit in setting up county officials there.
When Gongsun Hong served as the censor, the imperial court was building Shuofang County and driving out the Xiongnu according to the Yellow River. Gongsun Hong and others took the opportunity to state the damage caused by the campaign against the southwestern barbarians, and believed that the campaign against the southwestern barbarians could be temporarily suspended in order to concentrate on dealing with the Xiongnu.
The emperor agreed with these suggestions, abolished the officials in the Xiyi area, and only established two counties and one captain in the Nanyi area, allowing Jianwei County to protect itself and gradually improve its county system.
In the first year of Yuanshou, Zhang Qian, the Marquis of Bowang, said that when he was on a mission to Daxia, he saw the bundles of cloth produced in Shu and the bamboo sticks produced in Qiong Mountain. He asked where they came from, and he replied: They came from Shendu country in the southeast. Shendu country is about several thousand miles away from this place. I bought them from Shu merchants there.
He also heard that there was a country about two thousand miles west of Qiong Mountain.
Zhang Qian took the opportunity to declare that Daxia was located to the southwest of the Han Dynasty. It envied China and suffered from the Xiongnu blocking its communication with the Han Dynasty. If the road to Shu could be opened, it would be convenient for Shendu to communicate with the Han Dynasty, which would be beneficial to the Han Dynasty.
Therefore, the emperor ordered Wang Ranyu, Bai Shichang, Lu Yueren and more than ten people to search for a small road and set out from the southwestern Yi area to find the country of Shendu.
When they arrived in the Dian Kingdom, they were retained by Dang Qiang, the king of Dian, who sent people to the west to find a way for them.
After more than four years, all the explorers were blocked by Kunming Yi, and no one could pass.
The King of Dian asked the envoy of the Han Dynasty: Which one is bigger than the Han Dynasty and our Dian Kingdom?
When the Han Dynasty envoy arrived at Yelang, the Marquis of Yelang also asked the same question. These princes all thought they were kings of a state and had no idea of ​​the vast territory of the Han Dynasty.
After the envoy came back, he tried his best to declare that Dian was a great country in Nabo and could definitely attract its attachment.
The emperor also paid attention to this matter.
When the Southern Guangdong rebellion came, the emperor ordered Chiyihou to recruit the Nanyi army through Jianwei County. The leader of Qielan was worried that his army would go away during the expedition, and nearby countries would take the opportunity to plunder their own old and weak people, so he and his tribe launched a rebellion and killed the Han Dynasty envoys and the governor of Jianwei County.
The Han Dynasty dispatched criminals from Bajun and Shujun, who were supposed to attack southern Guangdong, and the Eighth School Lieutenant to attack Qielan.
Just in time to catch up with the defeat of South Vietnam, the eight lieutenants of the Han Dynasty did not go down the Yangke River as originally planned. Zhonglang generals Guo Chang and Wei Guang led their troops back and took advantage of the march to punish Qielan, who had blocked the Han Dynasty's road to the Dian Kingdom. He killed tens of thousands, and then pacified Nanyi and used the land as Yangke County.
Yelanghou relied on Nanyue at first. After the fall of Nanyue, the Han Dynasty's army returned and punished the rebellious countries. Yelanghou went to Beijing to see the emperor, who named him King Yelang.
After the fall of Southern Guangdong, the Han Dynasty killed Qielan and Qiongdu Lord, and also killed the Lord of Zhadu. The leaders of Ran Xiaoyi were shocked and panicked, and asked to submit to the Han Dynasty and let the Han Dynasty appoint officials. Therefore, the Han Dynasty designated the residence of Qiongdu Yi as Guangdong County, the residence of Zhadu Yi as Shenli County, the residence of Ran Xiaoyi as Wenshan County, and the residence of Baima Yi to the west of Guanghan County as Wudu County.
The emperor ordered Wang Ranyu to persuade the Dian king to join the dynasty with the military situation of destroying Eastern Guangdong and conquering the southern barbarians.
The King of Dian has tens of thousands of tribesmen, and in the northeast there are Laoshen and Mimo. They have the same surname as Dian and rely on each other. They do not listen to the advice about the King of Dian entering the dynasty.
Lao Shen and Mi Mo repeatedly offended the envoys, officials and soldiers of the Han Dynasty.
In the second year of Yuanfeng, the emperor mobilized troops from Bajun and Shujun to attack Laoshen and Mimo. The troops came to Dian Kingdom.
Since the King of Dian was originally friendly with the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty did not execute him.
The King of Dian broke away from the Western Yi, and the whole country surrendered to the Han Dynasty. He asked the Han Dynasty to appoint officials and go to Beijing to see the emperor. So the Han Dynasty made Nahuo a Yizhou county and gave the king of Dian the royal seal so that he could still rule his people.
There were hundreds of leaders of the southwestern barbarians, but only the leaders of Yelang and Dian received the royal seal.
Dian is a small country that was most favored by the Han Dynasty.
Twenty-three years later, in the first year of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, the people of Liantou and Guzhen in Yizhou rebelled and killed the chief officials.
More than 30,000 people from 24 countries including Pang Ke, Tan Zhi, and Tong Bing also rebelled.
The Han Dynasty sent Captain Shuiheng to mobilize more than 10,000 soldiers from Shu and Jianwei counties to attack Qunke and completely defeat the rebels.
Three years later, Guzhen and Ye Yu rebelled again. The Han Dynasty sent Shuiheng Captain Lu Pihu to lead county troops to attack the rebels.
Before Lu Pihu's army could advance to Yeyu and Guzhen, the barbarians killed the prefect of Yizhou and took advantage of the victory to fight Lu Pihu. More than 4,000 Han soldiers died in battle or drowned.
The next year, he sent troops such as Wang Ping and Dahong Tian Guangming to attack, completely defeating the rebels in Yizhou, capturing and killing more than 50,000 people, and capturing more than 100,000 livestock.
The Emperor said: Gou Ding Hou Neng Bo led the leaders and people of the small country under his jurisdiction to attack the rebels. He captured and killed them with meritorious service, and established Nang Bo as the King of Xuan Ding.
Dahonglu Tian Guangming was rewarded with the title of Marquis of Guannei and a settlement of 300 households.
A year later, the Di people in Wudu County rebelled. The imperial court dispatched Jinwu Ma Shijian, Long'ehou Han Zeng and Dahonglu Tian Guangming to lead troops to attack the rebels.
During the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty in Heping, Wang Xing of Yelang, Wang Yu of Gouding, and Hou Yu of Luwo raised their troops to attack each other.
The governor of Yangke requested to attack Yelang Wang Xing and others. Those who discussed troop deployment believed that the road was too far to attack, so the imperial court sent Zhang Kuangchijie, a Taizhong doctor from Shu County, to reconcile the conflicts between the barbarian princes.
Yelang, Wang Xing and others did not obey the orders of the Han Dynasty officials. They carved wooden figures that looked like Han Dynasty officials and stood on the roadside to shoot.
Du Qin said to General Wang Feng: Taizhong official Zhang Kuang sent an envoy to reconcile the disputes between the barbarian princes. The princes accepted the Shao Order of the Han Dynasty, but further attacked each other, despised the Han Dynasty envoys, and were not afraid of the country's power. This shows the effect of reconciliation.
Worried that the people who discussed sending troops were weak and insisted on reconciliation, the prefect observed the movements of the barbarians and reported to the police only when something happened.
Like this, it will take a few more months for the barbarian princes to organize their tribes and stubbornly adhere to their own strategies. They have many followers and are extremely angry, and they will definitely kill each other and eliminate them.
If he knows that he has committed a crime, he will suddenly become mad and rebellious and kill the prefect or captain. Traveling far and deep into hot, humid and poisonous weeds areas, even if there are generals like Sun Wu and Wu Qi, and warriors like Meng Ben and Xia Yu, is equivalent to being plunged into fire and water. If you go there, you will definitely be scorched and submerged, and you will not be able to use your wisdom and courage.
It would be too expensive to defend them in the field.
They should take advantage of the fact that their crimes have not yet been committed and there is no doubt that the Han Dynasty is going to attack them. They should secretly order the governors and captains of nearby counties to select soldiers and war horses. Da Sinong will allocate grain to key places in advance and select competent governors to go there. In the cool autumn, they will enter the area and kill the most unruly princes.
If you think that sage kings will not tire China with barren land and useless people, you should abolish the establishment of Naguo County, abandon the people of Naguo, sever relations with the princes of Naguo, and no longer have contact with them.
If the achievements made by the late emperor cannot be destroyed, we should eradicate the disaster when it is budding. Wait until the disaster has already occurred, and then go out to attack, hundreds of millions of people will suffer.
At this time, General Wang Feng recommended Chen Li, Sima of Jincheng, as the prefect of Yangke County.
Chen Li was a native of Linqiong. He had previously served as the magistrate of Lianran County and the magistrate of Buwei County. The barbarians were afraid of him.
When Chen Li arrived at Qunke, he informed Yelang Wang Xing of the court's intentions, but Xing did not obey the order. Chen Li requested to attack him.
Before receiving approval, Chen Li accompanied dozens of officials to the lower counties. When they arrived at Qie Tong Pavilion of Yelang Kingdom, they summoned Yelang Wang Xing. Yelang Wang Xing led thousands of people there. When they arrived at Qie Tong Pavilion, Yelang Wang Xing and dozens of Yijuns went in to see Chen Li.
Chen Li condemned and scolded them, and took the opportunity to kill King Yelang.
The princes who followed Yelang King said: The general killed the rude people who did not abide by the law and eliminated harm for the people. They hope to show Yelang King Xing's head to the public.
The head of King Yelang Xing was displayed to the public, and all the people of King Yelang laid down their weapons and surrendered.
King Yu of Gouding and Hou Yu of Luwo were frightened, so they paid a thousand bushels of dendrobium and some cattle and sheep to reward the officers and soldiers of the Han Dynasty.
When Chen Li returned to Pangke County, Yelang Wang Xing's father-in-law Weng Zhi and his son Zie Wu gathered up the remaining soldiers and forced twenty-two nearby cities to rebel.
In winter, Chen Li asked to recruit all the barbarians, and he would lead an army to attack Wengzhi and others separately from the captain and Chang Shi.
Weng Zhi relied on the steep terrain as a fortress. Chen Li used extraordinary troops to cut off Weng Zhi's route of transporting food and wages, and sent out questioners to seduce Weng Zhi's tribe.
Captain Wannian said: The army has not fought decisively for a long time, and the cost and supply cannot keep up.
So he led his army to attack alone. The attack failed and he fled to Chen Li's military camp.
Chen Li was angry and reprimanded Wan Nian under the banner of the general and ordered him to resist the enemy.
Captain Wannian returned to fight again, and Chen Li led his army to rescue him.
At this time, there was a severe drought, and Chen Li attacked to cut off the water channel.
So the barbarians beheaded Weng Zhi together and came out with Weng Zhi's head to surrender.
Chen Li had already pacified Xiyi, and the emperor summoned them to the capital.
When he caught up with thieves in Bajun, he appointed Chen Li as the prefect of Bajun, with Zhong Two Thousand Stones in his official position. The court rewarded him with the title of Zuo Shu Zhang.
Later, he was appointed as the prefect of Tianshui County. He encouraged the people to devote themselves to farming and mulberry trees, and he was the most outstanding in the world. The court rewarded him with forty pounds of gold. He entered the court and served as General Zuo Cao Wei and Captain of the Guards. He died in office.
Wang Mang usurped the throne, changed the system of the Han Dynasty, and demoted King Gouding to the title of Marquis of Gouding.
Wang Han of Gouching was resentful, and Zhou Qin, the great Yin of Yangke County, killed Han by deceitful means.
Hand's brother Cheng then attacked and killed Zhou Qin, and the prefectures and counties sent troops to fight back against the Gouding barbarians, but they could not subdue them.
The barbarians on the three sides were worried about the invasion, so they all rebelled and killed Chenglong, the great Yin of Yizhou County.
Wang Mang sent Pingman general Feng Mao to mobilize officials and soldiers from Bajun, Shujun and Qianweijun. Collect enough taxes from the people to attack the Yizhou barbarians.
Three years after the expedition, seven out of ten people died of disease and plague, causing unrest in Bajun and Shujun.
Wang Mang summoned Feng Mao to kill him.
Ningshi General Lian Danyuyong was reassigned to Mu Shixiong, and he mobilized cavalry from Tianshui and Longxi counties and 100,000 officials and civilians from Guangmo, Ba, Shu, and Jianwei counties, plus 200,000 people transporting military supplies, to attack the rebels.
When they first arrived, they killed thousands of people. Later, the transportation of military supplies could not keep up, and the soldiers became hungry and sick. Tens of thousands of people died in three years.
Moreover, Ren Gui, a barbarian from Jun County, Guangdong, killed the prefect Mei Gen and established himself as the king of Qiong Valley.
After Wang Mang failed to catch up with him, Han Guangwu Zhongxing killed Ren Gui and restored his original title.
Zhao Tuo, King of Southern Guangdong, was a native of Zhending County.
After Qin unified the world, he pacified Yangyue, established Guilin County, Nanhai County and Xiang County, and moved the people who were punished to Nahuo to live together with the Cantonese people.
Thirteen years later, during the reign of Qin II, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned the magistrate of Long County, Tuo Tuo, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others started an army to rebel, and the heroes rebelled against Qin and established themselves as kings. Nanhai County is in a remote place, and I am afraid that the bandit army will capture it.
I wanted to send troops to cut off the new road, defend myself, and observe the movements of the princes, but unfortunately I fell seriously ill.
The Panyu area is backed by mountains, the terrain is difficult, and it is thousands of miles in radius. With the help of many Central Plains people, it can also become the lord of a state and establish a country.
There is no one among the officials in the county who is worthy of my seeking advice, so I have invited you here to tell you what I think.
The relevant documents were immediately issued to Tuo Tuo, and he was asked to act as Nanhai County Lieutenant.
After Ren Xiao's death, Tu Tuo immediately issued a message, notifying Hengpu, Yangshan, Huangxiguan and others: The bandits' army is about to attack. Please cut off the passage immediately and gather troops to defend yourself!
So he used legal means to gradually kill the officials appointed by the Qin Dynasty, and appointed his cronies to perform their duties.
After the fall of the Qin Dynasty, Tuo Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin County and Xiang County, and established himself as King Wu of Southern Guangdong.
After Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty pacified the world, due to the continuous wars in the Central Plains and the hard work of the people, he spared Zhao Tuo and refused to punish him.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the Han Dynasty sent Lu Mai to establish Zhao Tuo as the king of southern Guangdong. He made a talisman with him and asked him to coordinate the security and control of Guangdong and avoid causing trouble on the southern border. Southern Guangdong borders the Changsha Kingdom of the Han Dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Gao, officials from relevant departments petitioned to prohibit the Southern Guangdong Kingdom from purchasing ironware in the Guan market.
Tu Tuo said: Emperor Gao made me the king of Nanyue, and the two sides exchanged envoys and goods. Now Gaohou listens to the slanderous ministers, regards the barbarians as aliens, and cuts off the circulation of artifacts. This must be the strategy of King Changsha. He wants to rely on the Han Dynasty to destroy Nanyue, swallow up Nanhai County, and rule together for his own benefit.
Therefore, Zhao Tuo proclaimed himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue and sent troops to attack the border areas of Changsha and defeated several counties.
Empress Gao sent General Long Luhou Zhou Zao to fight back. It was a hot and rainy day. Many soldiers were infected with the plague and the army could not cross the mountains.
More than a year later, Queen Gao died, and the Han Dynasty stopped military operations.
Tu Tuo took the opportunity to threaten Minyue and Xiouluo with force and bribe them with property, thereby enslaving them and making them belong to Nanyue.
In this way, the south of Guangdong reaches more than 10,000 miles from east to west.
Tu Tuo then rode in Zuohuan of Huangwu, proclaimed himself emperor, and competed with the emperor of Han Dynasty.
In the first year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, when the emperor had just begun to rule the world, he sent envoys to all the princes and foreign princes to inform them of his plans after entering the imperial court from Daiguo and becoming emperor, so that everyone would know about the emperor's holiness.
Therefore, a tomb guard house was set up for the tomb of Zhao Tuo's parents in Zhending, and sacrifices were made on time.
He summoned Zhao Tuo's cousins ​​and won them over with official posts and rewards.
He also issued an edict and ordered Prime Minister Chen Ping to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to Southern Guangdong. Chen Ping said that Lu Jia had been on an envoy to Southern Guangdong during the reign of Emperor Gao.
Emperor Wen summoned Lu Jia, appointed him Taizhong doctor, and appointed an emissary as deputy envoy. Emperor Wen's letter to Zhao Tuo said: The emperor respectfully greets the King of Nanyue with the most sincere heart.
I was not the legitimate son of Emperor Gao, but was sent to govern the country of Dai in the north. Due to the long distance and my own isolation and ignorance, I never exchanged envoys with southern Guangdong.
Emperor Gao passed away and left his ministers. Emperor Xiaohui came to the throne. Empress Gao personally took charge of the government. Unfortunately, she fell ill and her illness became increasingly serious. Therefore, the politics were harsh and unconventional.
The Lu family rebelled and deliberately violated laws and regulations. They could not rule alone, so they regarded other people's children as the heirs of Emperor Xiaohui and implemented puppet politics.
Relying on the blessing of the gods of the ancestral temple and the efforts of the heroes, the Lu family has now been exterminated.
I have repeatedly abdicated the throne, but the ministers did not allow it, so I had to establish myself as emperor, and now I have ascended the throne.
I once heard that you wrote to General Longluhou Zhouzao, requesting that your brothers in Zhending be found and that the two generals in Changsha be withdrawn.
In accordance with the request in your letter, I have withdrawn General Boyang Hou Chen Bi, your brother in Zhending, and I have also sent people to comfort and repair the tombs of your ancestors.
I heard before that you sent troops to attack the border and continued to cause trouble.
At that time, Changsha State suffered a disaster, and Nanjun suffered even more. Even your Nanyue State could only benefit?
We must sacrifice a large number of soldiers, harm excellent generals and officials, and cause the common people's wives to lose their husbands, their sons to lose their fathers, and their parents to lose their sons. This is what I cannot bear to do.
I wanted to add the intersecting border between Han and Southern Guangdong to Southern Guangdong, so I asked the relevant officials. The officials said that the boundary line was created by Emperor Gao to demarcate the land of Changsha, so I could not change it without authorization.
