The Western Regions began communication with the Central Plains during Emperor Wu of Han, originally comprising thirty-six countries that later divided into over fifty kingdoms, all located west of the Xiongnu and south of the Wusun. The region spans more than 6,000 miles east to west and over 1,000 miles north to south, bordered by the Han Dynasty to the east with Yumen Pass and Yang Pass as fortresses, and Congling to the west. Its central river has two sources: one from Congling Mountain and another from Khotan, flowing north to merge and eastward into Puchang Sea (also known as Yanze), a stable lake about 300 miles wide. The lake water flows underground, emerging at Jishi Mountain as the Huanghui in the Central Plains. Two main roads lead from Yumen and Yang Pass to the Western Regions: the south road via Shanshan and Yarkand, crossing Congling to reach Dayuezhi and Anxi; the north road via Cheshi and Shule, crossing Congling to reach Dawan, Kangju, and Yancai.

Most Western Region countries were settled, with cities, fields, and livestock, distinct from Xiongnu and Wusun customs. They were historically enslaved by the Xiongnu, who appointed a boy servant captain to manage the region, collecting taxes from various countries. After the Zhou Dynasty's decline, Rong and Di ethnic groups lived north of the Jingshui and Weishui rivers. Qin Shihuang drove them out and built the Great Wall, but the west did not exceed Lintao County. From the Western Han's establishment to Emperor Wu, Zhang Qian opened the road to the Western Regions. Later, Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu, leading to the surrender of King Hunxie and Xiutu. The Han Dynasty built beacons west of Lingju, established Jiuquan County, and later recruited people to settle in Wuwei, Zhangye, and Dunhuang, guarding Yumen and Yang Pass.

After Li Guangli attacked Dayuan, Western Region countries sent envoys to Chang'an. The Han Dynasty built pavilions and barriers from Dunhuang to Yanze, stationed field soldiers in Luntai and Quli, and set up envoys and captains to supervise farming. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Wei Sima oversaw several countries west of Shanshan. After defeating Gu Shi, the Han Dynasty divided it into the former and latter kings of Cheshi and the six kingdoms of Shanbei, initially supervising only the southern route. Later, King Rizhu betrayed Chanyu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Zheng Ji, the envoy protecting Shanshan, met King Rizhu, and both were granted marquis titles. The Han Dynasty established the Protectorate, beginning with Zheng Ji, who protected the North Road. The Xiongnu's child servant captain was dismissed, weakening the Xiongnu. The Han Dynasty moved people to farm in Beixu Tar, dividing Shache's land. The Protectorate monitored Wusun, Kangju, and other foreign countries, stationed in Wulei City, 2,738 miles from Yangguan, due to its fertile land and central location.

During Emperor Yuan's reign, Wuji Xiaowei was appointed to man fields. Wang Zilizhi of Baotui Dongpu surrendered with over 1,700 people, and the Protectorate allocated land for them. Since the Xuancha and Wutong period, Li Sculpture Chanyu Xianghui became a vassal, and details of land, mountains, rivers, and distances were recorded. Starting from the nearest west of Yangguan, the Laoqiang Kingdom had 450 households, 1,750 people, and 500 troops, living with livestock and not farming. The Shanshan Kingdom (formerly Loulan) had 1,570 households, 14,100 people, and 2,912 troops, with officials including Fu Guohou and translators. It produced jade, reeds, and willow, and its people lived with livestock. Initially, Emperor Wu was moved by Zhang Qian's words and sent many envoys to Dawan. Loulan and Gushi, on the main road, attacked Han envoys and acted as Xiongnu spies. Emperor Wu sent Zhao Ponu and Wang Hui to attack Gushi and capture the King of Loulan, leading to the construction of pavilions west to Yumen Pass. Loulan surrendered but later sent hostages to both the Han and Xiongnu. After King Loulan died, the Han Dynasty could not send back a castrated hostage, leading to a new king who declined to visit the Han emperor. Later, Wei Tuqi, the king's brother, surrendered to the Han Dynasty. In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, Fu Jiezi assassinated King Loulan, established Wei Tuqi as king, and renamed the country Shanshan. The Han Dynasty sent a Sima and forty officials to garrison Yixun, marking the beginning of official establishment there. Shanshan was a strategic point on the road to the Western Regions, with various countries like Qiemo, Xiaowan, Jingjue, Ronglu, Shanmi, Qule, Khotan, Pishan, Wushuo, Xiye, Puli, Yinai, Wulei, Nandou, and Jibin, each with specific populations, troops, and distances from Chang'an. Jibin, a large country not under the Western Region Protector, had a mild climate, produced various crops and metals, and had a market with gold and silver coins. The Han Dynasty's communication with Jibin began under Emperor Wu, but later conflicts arose, including the killing of Han envoys. Du Qin advised against further engagement due to the dangers and costs, and the Han Dynasty eventually limited contact. Wuyi Mountain, another large country, had similar customs to Jibin, with a hot climate and lush vegetation. Anxi Kingdom, a very large country with hundreds of cities, used silver coins and had a written language. Emperor Wu sent envoys to Parthia, who were greeted by a general with 20,000 cavalry. Dayuezhi, originally a nomadic country, was defeated by the Xiongnu and moved west to Daxia, establishing their capital. Daxia was divided into five tribes, each with its own marquis, all belonging to Dayuezhi. Kangju, with 120,000 households and 600,000 people, had customs similar to Dayuezhi and was restrained by the Xiongnu. During Emperor Xuan's reign, the Han Dynasty killed Zhizhi Chanyu. Under Emperor Cheng, King Kangju was arrogant, and the Protectorate recommended cutting ties, but the court maintained relations. Yancai, northwest of Kangju, had over 100,000 warriors and customs similar to Kangju. Dayuan, with 60,000 households and 300,000 people, produced good horses and used grapes for wine. Emperor Wu sent Li Guangli to attack Dayuan, resulting in the dedication of two Pegasus horses annually. From Dawan to Parthia, residents had different languages but similar customs, with deep-set eyes and long beards. They were skilled in business and obtained gold and silver from the Han Dynasty. After Huhanxie Chanyu submitted to the Han Dynasty, these countries respected the Han. Various other kingdoms like Taohua, Xiuxun, Zhendu, Shache, Shule, and Weitou had specific populations, troops, and distances, with some farming and raising livestock.

translation:
In the Wusun Kingdom, Da Kunmi governed Chigu City and was sent to Chang'an for 8,900 miles.
There are 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800 people.
There is a prime minister, a big official, two generals on the left and right, three marquis, one general and a captain, two eunuchs, one official, two senior officials in the house, and one knight.
It went as far as Wulei City, the headquarters of the Western Regions Governor, for 1,721 miles, and to the west as far as the hinterland of Kangju and Fan, 5,000 miles.
The land is grassy and flat, rainy and the climate is cold.
There are many pines on the mountain.
The residents do not farm or plant trees, but live with their livestock in search of water and grass, which is the same custom as the Xiongnu.
The country is prolific with horses, and wealthy people have as many as four to five thousand horses.
The people are strong-willed, greedy for money, unfaithful, and have many thieves. This is a powerful country.
He used to submit to the Xiongnu, but later he became powerful and adopted a restrained attitude towards the Xiongnu and refused to go to worship.
It borders the Xiongnu in the east, Kangju in the northwest, Dawan in the west, and the Chengguo Kingdoms in the south.
Zaojie was originally the land of the Sai people. The Dayue clan defeated and drove away the King of Sai to the west. The King of Sai moved to the south of the county, and the Dayue clan occupied the land of the Sai people.
Later, Wusun Kunmo defeated Dayuezhi, and Dayuezhi moved westward and surrendered to Daxia. Wusun Kunmo occupied the original Dayuezhi land, so Wusun residents included Sai people and Dayuezhi people.
At first, Zhang Qian said that Wusun and Da Yueshi were originally in Dunhuang. Although Wusun was now stronger, he could still give them some generous gifts to lure them back to their hometown; and then marry the princess to Kunmo, and!
The emperor urgently wanted to become a country of brothers and used this method to restrain the Xiongnu.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Zhang Qian". Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and ordered Zhang Qian to bring gold coins and treasures to Wusun.
Kun Mo met Zhang Qian with the attitude of the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian was very ashamed and angry, and said to Kun Mo: If you don't thank the emperor for giving you a gift, then return the gift to us.
Kunmo stood up and thanked him, but in other respects he remained the same.
At the beginning, Kunmo had more than a dozen sons. The middle son Dalu was very strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived elsewhere.
Dalu's brother was the prince, and the prince had a son named Cen Zuo.
The prince died early. Before his death, he said to Kunmo: "Cen Zou must be the prince."
Kunmo was sad and agreed.
Dalu was very angry about this incident, so he captured all the other brothers, led his soldiers to rebel, and prepared to attack Cen Zuo.
Kunmo gave Cen Zuo more than 10,000 cavalry and ordered him to station elsewhere. He also had more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense.
At this time, the country was divided into three parts, all under the control of Kunmo.
After Zhang Qian handed over the gifts given to Kunmo by the Han Dynasty, he said to Kunmo: If Wusun can return to his hometown, the Han Dynasty will send the princess as Kunmo's wife. The two countries will become brotherly countries and resist the Xiongnu together. The Xiongnu will definitely be defeated.
But Wusun was far away from the Han Dynasty, and the size of the Han Dynasty was unknown. Wusun himself was close to the Xiongnu and had obeyed the Xiongnu for a long time. None of the ministers were willing to move eastward.
Kunmo is old, the country is divided, and power cannot be concentrated. So an envoy was sent to take Zhang Qian back to Chang'an, and at the same time, he offered dozens of horses as a thank you.
The envoy saw that the Han Dynasty had a large population and rich products. After returning home, Wusun respected the Han Dynasty more and more.
When the Xiongnu heard that Wusun had contact with the Han, they were very angry and wanted to attack Wusun.
In addition, the envoys of the Han Dynasty passed south of Wusun to Dayuan and Yuezhi, and they were not stopped on the road.
Wusun was very frightened, so he sent an envoy to offer horses to the Han Dynasty and offered to marry Princess Mo, and the two countries became brothers.
The emperor asked the ministers for their opinions, and the court agreed. Decision: The bride price must be paid first, and then the princess must be sent away.
Wusun gave a thousand horses as a betrothal gift.
During the Yuanfeng period of the Han Dynasty, Xijun, the daughter of King Liu Jian of Jiangdu, was sent to marry Kunmo as a princess. The emperor gave her carriages, horses and royal utensils. He also equipped her with hundreds of officials, eunuchs, maids and servants, and gave her rich gifts.
Wusun Kunmo took Mr. Bin as his right wife.
The Xiongnu also sent women to marry Kunmo, and Kunmo took the Xiongnu girl as his left wife.
After the princess arrived in Wusun, she built a palace to live in. She had gatherings with Kunmo several times a year, drank and ate, and rewarded the nobles around Kunmo with property, silk fabrics, etc.
Kunmo was old and couldn't understand the language. The princess was very sad and composed a song by herself: My family married me to the far side of the sky, and asked King Yan of Wu to come to a foreign country far away.
The dome is the room, the walls are the walls, the meat is the food, and the cheese is the pulp.
Living in this land, I miss you and my heart hurts. I wish you could return to your hometown as a yellow swan.
When the emperor heard about it, he felt pity for her and sent envoys every other year to deliver curtains, brocade and other items.
Kunmo is old and wants his grandson Cen Zuo to marry the princess.
The princess disagreed and wrote to the emperor explaining the matter. The emperor replied: Following the custom of Wusun country, Mo wants to join forces with Wusun to destroy the Xiongnu.
Cen Zuo married the princess.
Kun Mo died, and Cen Zou became king in his stead.
Cen Zuo is an official title, and his name is Jun Xumi.
Kunmo is the king's name, and his name is Liejiaomi.
Later, the king was named Kunmi.
Cen Zuo married the princess of Jiangdu and gave birth to a daughter named Shaofu.
After the princess died, the Han Dynasty sent Jieyou, the granddaughter of King Liu Wu of Chu, to marry Cen Zou for the princess.
Cen Zou's son Nimi by his Hun wife was still young. When Cen Zou was about to die, he passed the throne to his uncle Dalu's son Weng Guimi. He said: When Nimi grows up, he will return the throne to Nimi.
Weng Guimi came to the throne and was named King Fei. He married Jieyou and gave birth to three sons and two daughters: the eldest son was named Yuan Guimi; the second son was named Wannian and was the king of Shache; the third son was named Dalue and was the general of Zuo; the eldest daughter was named Shi and was the wife of King Jiangbin of Qiuci; the younger daughter was named Suguang and was the wife of Ruohulinghou.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, Princess Jieyou wrote to the emperor, saying that the Xiongnu sent cavalry to farm in Cheshi, and that the Cheshi and the Xiongnu united to invade Wusun, hoping that the emperor would rescue them.
The Han Dynasty prepared soldiers and horses to attack the Xiongnu.
When Emperor Zhao died and Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne, Princess Jieyou and Kunmi both sent envoys to write, saying that the Xiongnu invaded and attacked Wusun in succession, captured Cheyan, Eshi and other places, and plundered all the local residents. He also sent an envoy to tell Wusun to send the princess to the Huns as soon as possible, hoping to destroy the relationship between Wusun and Han.
Kunmi is willing to send half of the country's elite troops and prepare 50,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu with all his strength.
I hope the emperor will send troops to rescue the princess and Kunmi as soon as possible.
The Han Dynasty sent an army of 150,000 cavalry, led by five generals.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns".
The Han Dynasty also sent Lieutenant Chang Hui as an envoy to protect the Wusun soldiers. Kunmi personally led a total of 50,000 knights under the Marquis of Ji to attack the Xiongnu from the west. When the Xiongnu arrived at the royal court of Yougu Li, they captured 40,000 people including Shanyu's father, sister-in-law, Juzi, Ming Wang, Ligu Duwei, Qian Chang, and cavalry generals, as well as more than 700,000 horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels. Wusun took these trophies away.
When the Han army returned home, Emperor Xuan granted Chang Hui the title of Marquis of Changluo.
This year is the third year of the original year.
The Han Dynasty also sent Chang Hui with valuable belongings and silk fabrics to be given to the nobles of Wusun who had made military exploits.
In the second year of Yuankang, Wusun Kunmi wrote to Emperor Xuan through Chang Hui, saying: I would like to make my grandson Yuan Guimi of the Han Dynasty the heir to the throne, and let him also marry a Han princess, form a double marriage, and sever ties with the Huns. I am willing to use a thousand horses and mules as a betrothal gift.
Emperor Xuan ordered ministers to discuss the matter. Xiao Wangzhi, the great emperor, thought: Wusun is located very far away and there is no guarantee that it will not change. Don't agree to their request.
Emperor Xuan admired Wusun's recent great achievements and found it difficult to sever the established marriage relationship, so he sent an envoy to Wusun to receive the betrothal gift first.
Kunmi, the crown prince, the left and right generals, and the captain sent a delegation of more than 300 people to the Han Dynasty to welcome the young princess.
Emperor Xuan took Princess Jieyou's niece and husband as the princess, and appointed more than a hundred officials, maids, etc. to live in Shanglin Garden and learn the Wusun language.
Emperor Xuan personally came to Pingganguang, met with the Huns envoys and foreign princes, performed a jiaoduan drama, music, singing and dancing, and then sent the princess to the west to marry. The envoy Chang Luohou Guanglu, the doctor Chang Hui assisted, and four people were envoys to send the young princess to Dunhuang.
Before leaving the frontier fortress, they heard that Wusun Kunmi Weng Guimi had died. According to the agreement made by Cen Zou during his lifetime, the Wusun nobles appointed Cen Zou's son Nimi as Kunmi, named Kuangwang.
Chang Hui wrote to Emperor Xuan saying: He wanted to keep the young princess in Dunhuang temporarily. Chang Hui rushed to Wusun and blamed Yuan Guimi for not appointing Yuan Guimi as Kunmi, and then took the young princess back to Chang'an.
The matter was discussed by the ministers, and Xiao Wangzhi said: "It is difficult to make a treaty with Wusun, who is headed by a rat."
Princess Jieyou has been in Wusun for more than 40 years. The relationship between the two countries is not close and the border is not peaceful. This is proved by creation.
Today, the young princess returned to Chang'an because Yuan Gui was not able to stand up. She did not feel sorry for Wusun, and it was also a blessing for the Han Dynasty.
If the young princess does not stop going to Wusun, the corvee will flourish, and this is where the roots begin.
Emperor Xuan accepted this opinion and took the young princess back to Chang'an.
The mad king married Princess Jieyou again and gave birth to a son named Ou Mi. The mad king was at odds with the princess and was cruel and unpopular.
The Han Dynasty sent Wei Si Ma Wei Heyi and deputy candidate Ren Chang to send a servant to Wusun. The princess told the Wusun people that the mad king was dissatisfied and said it would be easy to get rid of him.
So, they planned to have someone kill the mad king with a sword at the cocktail party.
The sword failed to cut accurately, and the mad king was injured, so he mounted his horse and fled.
His son Tao Shenshou led his troops to surround Princess Wei Heyi, Ren Chang and Heyou in Chigu City.
A few months later, Zheng Ji, the governor of the Western Regions, sent troops from nearby countries to rescue him and bundled up Shen Shou and fled.
The Han court sent Zhang Zun, a lieutenant general, to bring medicine to the mad king to treat his injuries. He also gave the mad king twenty kilograms of gold and various silk fabrics.
They also arrested Wei Heyi and Ren Chang, who were transported from Yuli to Chang'an in a prison car and beheaded.
The chariot general Shi Zhangweng stayed in Chigu to investigate the murder of the mad king by Princess Jieyou, Wei Heyi and Ren Chang. The princess was dissatisfied, kowtowed to Zhang Weng, and refused to plead guilty. Zhang Weng threw the princess's hair and cursed.
The princess wrote to Emperor Xuan, and Zhang Weng returned to Chang'an and was executed.
Ji Du, the deputy envoy of the Han Dynasty, led others to treat and nurse the mad king's injuries. When he returned to Chang'an, the mad king led more than ten knights to see him off.
Ji Du returned to Chang'an, knowing that the mad king was guilty and should be beheaded, but failed to get rid of the mad king and was castrated.
When the mad king was injured, Wujiutu, the son of Fat King Weng Guimi's Huns wife, fled to the northern mountains with all the princes, threatening that the Huns soldiers from his grandmother's house were coming soon, so many people surrendered to him.
Later, he attacked and killed the mad king and established himself as Kunmi.
The Han Dynasty ordered the Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian to lead 15,000 troops to Dunhuang. He sent people to measure the terrain, set up markers, dig the Beiqianhou Well, and open a canal to the west to prepare for transporting grain and building warehouses to attack Wujiutu.
Princess Jieyou originally had a waiter named Feng Liao, who knew history books and was familiar with the affairs of the Western Regions. She used to serve as an envoy of the Han Dynasty to various countries in the Western Regions to reward kings and nobles. She was respected and trusted by various countries and was known as Mrs. Feng.
Later, he married the wife of Wusun Youdajiang, who had a close relationship with Wujiutu. At this time, Zheng Ji, the governor of the Western Regions, sent Mrs. Feng to persuade Wujiutu, saying: The Han Dynasty is sending troops to the Western Regions, Wusun will be destroyed, so it is better to surrender early.
Wujiitu was very frightened and said: I just want to keep the title of Xiao Kunmi.
Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty summoned Mrs. Feng to Chang'an to personally inquire about Wusun's situation.
Later, he sent the visitors Zhu Ci and Qimen Gan Yanshou as deputy envoys to send Mrs. Feng back to Wusun.
Mrs. Feng rode in a brocade chariot and served as the official envoy of the Han Dynasty. She conveyed Emperor Xuan's edict and ordered Wujiitu to be sent to Luohou Changhui, the mayor of Chigu City.
Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian returned to Chang'an before leaving the fortress.
Later, the Wujiu Massacre failed to return all the people of the Xihous to their original owners. The Han Dynasty sent Changluohou Changhui to lead three schools to farm in Chigu, and divided the ruling areas within Wusun. Dakunmi had more than 60,000 households, and Xiaokunmi had more than 40,000 households. However, people's hearts were in favor of Xiaokunmi.
Yuan Guimi and Juan Mi both died of illness. The princess wrote to Emperor Xuan, saying that she was homesick in old age and hoped to die in Han.
Emperor Xuan took pity on her and sent someone to welcome her and her three grandchildren to Chang'an.
This year is the third year of Ganlu, and the princess is nearly seventy years old.
Emperor Xuan gave the princess fields, houses, slaves, etc., and she was well supported. The etiquette for meeting the emperor was the same as that for the emperor's own princess.
Two years later, Princess Jieyou passed away, and her two grandchildren stayed in Chang'an to guard the tomb.
Xingmi, the son of Yuanguimi, took the place of Dakunmi. He was still young. Mrs. Feng wrote to Emperor Xuan, hoping to send Wusun as an envoy to assist Xingmi.
Emperor Xuan sent more than a hundred people to escort Mrs. Feng to Wusun.
At first, Han Xuan, the Protector of the Western Regions, reported to Emperor Xuan and suggested that Wusun's officials, officials, and eunuchs be given gold seals and purple ribbons so that they could assist Da Kunmi. Emperor Xuan agreed.
Later, Han Xuan wrote that Xingmi was weak and could remove Da Kunmi and let his uncle Zuo Dajiang Le replace him as Da Kunmi. Emperor Xuan did not agree.
Later, Duan Huizong became the protector of the Western Regions, recruiting the rebellious population of Wusun, and the society was stabilized.
Xing Mi died, and his son Li Mi became Da Kun Mi.
Xiao Kunmi Wu was slaughtered to death, and his son Kaoli was named Xiao Kunmi.
Kaoli was killed by his younger brother Ri Er.
The Han Dynasty sent envoys to Wusun to establish Gaoli's son Anri as Xiaokunmi.
On the second day, he fled to Kangju.
The Han Dynasty moved Jixiaowei to station in Gumo, waiting for an opportunity to attack Japan.
Anri sent Gu Mo Ni and three other people to pretend to be defectors, defected to Yue Er, and assassinated Yue Er.
Lian Baobao, the Protector of the Western Regions, gave Gumon Ni and others twenty kilograms of gold and three hundred bolts of silk fabrics.
Later, Anri was killed by the surrendered people, and the Han Dynasty appointed Anri's younger brother Mo Zhen as Xiao Kunmi.
At this time, the great Kun Mi female Li Mi was strong and vigorous, and all the princes were afraid of him and obeyed him. The Linghous informed the people not to enter the herd area in Kunmi when herding horses and livestock to avoid confusion. The country is very peaceful, just like when Weng Guimi.
General Mo Zhen of Xiao Kunmi was afraid of being annexed by Da Kunmi, so he sent the nobleman Wu Ri to surrender to Feli Mi and assassinate him.
The Han Dynasty wanted to send troops to attack General Mo Zhen, but when he failed to send troops, he sent General Duan Huizong to the Western Regions with gold treasures and silk to make plans with the governor, and appointed Yi Zhimi, the uncle of Fei Li Mi and the grandson of Princess Jieyou, as the great Kunmi.
The Han Dynasty made Xiao Kunmi's servant in Chang'an an official slave.
A long time later, Xihou Nanqi of Dakunmi killed General Mo Zhen, and Anlimi, son of Anri of Xiaokunmi who was originally killed, was established as Xiaokunmi.
The Han Dynasty regretted not being able to kill General Mo Zhen himself, so he ordered Duan Huizong to kill General Mo Zhen's prince Fanqiu.
Duan Huizong returned to Chang'an and was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei.
This year is the second year of Yuanyan of Emperor Cheng.
Duan Huizong believed that Linghou Nanqi's killing of Mo Zhenjiang was not for the Han Dynasty, but it was in line with the Han Dynasty's purpose of punishing Mo Zhenjiang, so he petitioned Emperor Cheng to make him a strong guard.
The Han Dynasty blamed Da Lu, Da Li, Da Jian and other officials for being responsible for the murder of Li Mi. They took away their gold-seal and purple ribbons and replaced them with bronze-seal and ink ribbons.
Bei Yuanxun, the younger brother of Mo Zhenjiang, was originally involved in the murder of Da Kunmi's female Li Mi. Later, he led more than 80,000 people to the north and attached himself to Kangju, hoping to use Kangju's troops to annex Dakunmi and Xiaoyu Kunmi.
Both Kunmi were afraid of being humble and honest, so they attached themselves to the protector.
In the second year of Emperor Ai's reign, Dakun Miyi Zhimi and the Xiongnu Chanyu came to Chang'an to pay homage to Emperor Ai. The Han Dynasty felt it was an honor.
During the Yuanshi period of Emperor Ping, Bei Yuan directly killed Wu Yueling to serve the Han Dynasty, and the Han Dynasty named him Marquis of Guiyi.
Both the big and small Kunmi were weak. Bei Yuanting kept attacking the two Kunmi, and Sun Jian, the guardian of the army, attacked and killed Bei Yuanzhi.
Since Wusun separated the two Kunmi, the Han Dynasty sometimes appeased and sometimes suppressed, and there was no peace for a year.
In the Gumo Kingdom, the king governed Nancheng and extended it to Chang'an for eight thousand one hundred and fifty miles.
There are 3,500 households, a population of 24,500, and an army of 4,500.
There are one Gumohou, Fuguohou, Duwei, left and right generals, left and right cavalry monarchs, and two translators.
It takes 2,021 miles to reach Wulei City, the headquarters of the Western Region Governor. It takes fifteen days to reach Khotan in the south and connect with Wusun in the north.
Produces copper, iron, orpiment and other minerals.
It is six hundred and seventy miles from Cambodia to Kucha.
During the reign of Wang Mang, Wang Cheng of Gumo killed King Wensu and annexed the Wensu Kingdom.
In the Wensu Kingdom, the king governed Wensu City, which was eight thousand three hundred and fifty miles east of Chang'an. There are 2,200 households, a population of 8,400, and an army of 1,500.
There are two auxiliary princes, two generals on the left and right, two captains on the left and right, two knights on the left and right, and two chief translators.
It extends 2,380 miles to Wulei City, the headquarters of the Western Regions Protectorate, 300 miles to Weitou in the west, and 610 miles to Wusunchi Valley in the north. The land and products are the same as those of the Shanshan countries.
It was bound to Gumo for two hundred and seventy miles.
In the Kingdom of Qiuci, the king governed Yancheng, which was 7,480 miles east of Chang'an.
There are 6,970 households, a population of 81,317, and an army of 21,076.
There are one each of Da Du Wei Cheng, Fu Guo Hou, An Guo Hou, Chu Hu Hou, Que Hu Du Wei, Cha Cha Shi Du Wei, left and right generals, left and right captains, left and right cavalry lords, left and right auxiliary lords, two each from the east, west, south and north Qianchang, three from Quehu Jun, and four interpreters.
It is connected to Jingjue in the south, Qiemo in the southeast, Ganmi in the southwest, Wusun in the north, and Gumo in the west.
There are simple casting and metallurgical techniques, and lead is also produced.
It was sent to Wulei City, the headquarters of the Western Regions Governor, three hundred and fifty miles away.
Wulei has 110 households, a population of 1,200, and an army of 300.
There is one city captain and one interpreter.
Together with the Protector of Youyue, he governed Wuleiyue.
Three hundred and thirty miles south to Quli.
Quli has a city captain, one hundred and thirty households, a population of one thousand four hundred and eighty, and an army of one hundred and fifty.
It is connected to Yuli in the northeast, Qiemo in the southeast, and Jingjue in the south.
There is a river in the west, five hundred and eighty miles to Qiuci.
From the time when Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty opened the Western Regions, he set up school captains to plow and farm fields in Ququ.
At this time, the Han Dynasty continued to send troops for thirty-two years, and its national power was seriously depleted.
During the Zhenghe period, General Li Guang of the Second Division led his army to surrender to the Huns.
Emperor Wu regretted the expedition. At this time, Sang Hongyang, the captain of Susu, together with the prime minister and the imperial censor, told Emperor Wu: Luntai, with its beams of branches and ditches and plows, was the place where the country was founded in the past. The land is vast and the water and grass are rich. There are more than 5,000 hectares of irrigated fields. The climate is mild, the fields are fertile, and irrigation is convenient. Grains grown there mature at the same time as those in the Central Plains.
The neighboring country lacks iron tools such as awls and precious gold and colorful silk ribbons. Mo Mo can use these things to exchange for their grain to supply the field soldiers, so they don't have to worry about food shortages. The ministers and others thought that Mo could send soldiers to Yuan Luntai to consolidate the farmland, and set up three divisions of school captains to protect the troops. Let them draw maps of their respective areas, build irrigation ditches, and plant grain according to the seasons every year. Zhangye and Jiuquan counties each sent fake commanders and soldiers to look out for those who were working in the fields. Riding a fake Sima is within the control of the military commander in the field. If there is an important situation, you can use the post horse to report to the emperor.
If there is food stored in the fields for a year, people who are healthy and willing to migrate can be recruited to the farm. Using the stored food as a basis, they can expand the irrigated field area, build more pavilions, connect the cities to the west, and control the western countries with power, which is very beneficial to assisting the Wusun Kingdom.
The ministers and others can send the Chengchang Branch of the Expeditionary Affairs Bureau to patrol the western border areas, and strictly order the relevant prefects and captains to prepare beacon fires, select soldiers and horses, be cautious and vigilant, and store grain and grass.
I hope your Majesty will send envoys to Western countries so that they will not be uneasy because of fear of the Huns. I will risk my life to speak about this matter.
Emperor Wu issued a Shao Shu and deeply reflected on his past mistakes.
Shaoshu said: In the past, the relevant departments petitioned to increase the civil tax by thirty yuan per person to provide for frontier expenses. This is exacerbating the hardships of the elderly, weak and lonely population.
Today, please send soldiers to Luntai to farm.
Luntai is more than a thousand miles west of Cheshi. When Kailinghou attacked Cheshi, Weixu, Yuli, Loulan and other disciples from the Six Kingdoms in Chang'an returned home first to transport grain and livestock to meet the Han army. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty established four counties in Hexi and opened the Yumen Pass to connect the Western Regions to cut off the right arm of the Xiongnu and isolate the connection with the Southern Qiang and Yuezhi.
The Chanyu lost the support of the Western Region countries and the Qiang people, and fled to the distance. There was no royal court of the Xiongnu south of the desert.
After five generations of inaction and recuperation, the world became rich, had abundant financial resources, and had strong military and horse forces.
Therefore, when Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty saw rhinos, elephants, and tortoiseshells, he founded seven counties including Zhuya; he was inspired by wolfberry and bamboo sticks and established the counties of Yangke and Yuejun; and when he heard about Tianma and Putao, he opened the road to Dawan and Anxi.
Since its creation, the harem has been filled with treasures such as pearls, tortoise shells, rhinos, and green feathers. Horses of all kinds including Pushao, dragons, fish eyes, and sweats have filled the Yellow Gate. Elephants, lions, fierce dogs, and ostriches have roamed the gardens in droves.
Rare and strange things from far away come from all directions.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty expanded Shanglin Garden, excavated the Kunming Pool, built palaces with thousands of doors and households, built a platform for gods to reach the sky, made tents for armor and armor, tied with beads and biscuits.
Emperor Wu lived here and set up a wine pool and a meat forest to entertain the guests of the surrounding ethnic minorities; he performed the "Bayu" dance, Dulu, "Intestine Ji" in the sea, fish and dragon illusions, costumed horns and other plays.
There are also rewards and gifts, supplies for thousands of miles, and military expenditures, countless.
If the finances were not enough, the state would sell wine, salt and iron, cast platinum and leather coins as money, and levy taxes on vehicles, ships, and livestock.
The people's strength was exhausted, their wealth was exhausted, coupled with the famine years and poor harvests, bandits and bandits appeared together, and the roads were blocked, so Emperor Wu ordered his envoys to wear embroidered clothes, hold axes and iron, and go to various counties to suppress them, and then won victory.
In the last years of Emperor Wu's reign, he gave up farming in Yaluntai and issued a painful edict. Isn't this something that a benevolent saint would regret?
Moreover, on the road leading to the Western Region, there are Bailongdui nearby, Congling far away, and dangerous areas such as body heat, headache, and counties.
The Huainan kings Liu An, Du Qin, and Yang Xiong all believed that this was set up by heaven and earth to divide areas to isolate the inside and outside.
"Shangshu" says "Xirong is the preface", which means that after Yu controlled the floods and divided the nine states, he put the countries of Xirong within a certain range, and did not rely on the emperor's might to make them pay tribute.
The countries in the Western Region each have their own kings and commanders. Their armies are scattered and weak and cannot be unified. Although he once belonged to the Xiongnu, he was not close to them.
The Xiongnu could get their horses, livestock and felt kitchens, but they could not lead them to attack or retreat.
They are isolated from the Han Dynasty and the road is far away. It is not a benefit to get them and it is not a loss to abandon them.
The virtues of the Han Dynasty were created by ourselves and did not come from them.
Therefore, since the founding of Emperor Guangwu, all countries in the Western Regions have longed for the might and virtue of the Han Dynasty and have been willing to submit to them.
Only small countries such as Shanshan and Cheshi were close to the Xiongnu and were still controlled by the Xiongnu.
Other great powers, such as Yarkand and Khotan, sent envoys several times to bring hostages to the Han Dynasty, hoping that they would be allowed to become guardians.
Emperor Guangwu studied ancient and modern history, and based on the situation at that time, he adopted a policy of restraint. He disagreed with the dispatch of the Western Region Protector and also repatriated the hostages from various countries.
Although Dayu demarcated the territory of Xirong, Duke Zhou did not accept the white pheasants of the Yueshang clan, and Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty did not accept thousands of miles of horses, these were all beautiful things done by ancient sages, but Emperor Guangwu's actions all had this meaning, and there was nothing more clever than sending a man to do it.
summary:
The Wusun Kingdom, governed by Da Kunmi from Chigu City, was located 8,900 miles from Chang'an. It had 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800. The kingdom had a structured government with officials including a prime minister, generals, marquises, and eunuchs. The land was grassy, rainy, and cold, with residents practicing nomadic herding like the Xiongnu. The country was rich in horses, with wealthy individuals owning up to 4,000-5,000. The people were strong-willed but greedy and unfaithful. Wusun originally submitted to the Xiongnu but later became powerful and resisted them. It bordered the Xiongnu, Kangju, Dawan, and various Chengguo Kingdoms. The region was originally inhabited by the Sai people, then conquered by the Dayuezhi, and later by Wusun Kunmo, who incorporated both Sai and Dayuezhi populations.

Zhang Qian, sent by Emperor Wu of Han, attempted to persuade Wusun to return to their homeland and ally with Han against the Xiongnu. Kunmo initially treated Zhang Qian with Xiongnu-like arrogance but eventually showed respect. Wusun was divided among Kunmo's sons, with internal conflicts over succession. Despite Zhang Qian's efforts, Wusun was reluctant to move east due to distance and longstanding ties with the Xiongnu. However, after envoys saw Han's wealth, Wusun grew more respectful. The Xiongnu, angered by Wusun's contact with Han, threatened attack, leading Wusun to propose marriage to a Han princess. The Han agreed, and during the Yuanfeng period, Princess Xijun was sent to marry Kunmo. The Xiongnu also sent a bride, and Kunmo took both as wives. The princess, homesick and unable to communicate with the elderly Kunmo, composed a sorrowful song. Emperor Wu, pitying her, sent gifts regularly.

After Kunmo's death, his grandson Cen Zuo married the princess per Wusun custom, as Emperor Wu approved to maintain the alliance. Cen Zuo became king, and the princess bore a daughter. Upon her death, Princess Jieyou, granddaughter of a Han king, was sent to marry Cen Zuo. Cen Zuo's son by his Xiongnu wife was young, so the throne passed to his uncle's son, Weng Guimi, who married Jieyou and had three sons and two daughters. During Emperor Zhao's reign, Princess Jieyou sought Han aid against Xiongnu attacks. Emperor Xuan later sent a large force, including 150,000 Han cavalry and 50,000 Wusun troops, defeating the Xiongnu and capturing many people and livestock. Wusun took the spoils. Emperor Xuan rewarded Chang Hui, who had led the Wusun forces.

Wusun Kunmi proposed making his Han-descended grandson Yuan Guimi heir, with a double marriage to sever ties with the Xiongnu. Emperor Xuan agreed but faced opposition from officials like Xiao Wangzhi, who doubted Wusun's reliability. Despite this, the emperor proceeded, sending a young princess to Wusun. However, Weng Guimi died before her arrival, and the throne passed to Nimi, Cen Zuo's son. Chang Hui advised keeping the princess in Dunhuang, and after debate, Emperor Xuan recalled her. Princess Jieyou remained in Wusun for over 40 years, and the mad king, who succeeded, was cruel and unpopular. A plot to kill him failed, leading to conflict. The Han intervened, executing those involved. Later, Wujiutu, a son of Weng Guimi, killed the mad king and declared himself Kunmi. The Han sent forces but ultimately negotiated, dividing Wusun into two Kunmi with separate households. Princess Jieyou, now elderly, was allowed to return to Chang'an, where she died two years later.

The text also details various other kingdoms in the Western Regions, including Gumo, Wensu, Qiuci, and others, with their distances from Chang'an, populations, armies, and administrative structures. It describes the Han Dynasty's efforts to establish agricultural colonies, such as in Luntai, and the challenges of maintaining control over distant territories. Emperor Wu's later years saw a shift away from expansion, with a focus on domestic recovery and reduced military campaigns. The narrative covers conflicts with the Xiongnu, internal rebellions, and the eventual decline of Han influence in the region, culminating in the collapse of the Western Regions Protectorate during Wang Mang's reign. The summary concludes with a reflection on the costs and benefits of Han's Western Regions policy, noting that while the region offered exotic goods, it also drained resources and led to instability.

Gu Yong, named Ziyun, was from Chang'an.
His father, Gu Ji, served as Sima of the Wei Dynasty. As an envoy, he sent Shanyu Zhizhi's servant back to his country, but was killed by Zhizhi. This incident was recorded in the "Chen Tang Biography".
Gu Yong wrote a short history of Chang'an when he was young, and later studied the classics extensively.
During the reign of Emperor Jianzhao, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, heard that he had outstanding talents and appointed him as his subordinate. Later, he recommended him as Taichang Cheng. He wrote many memorials to discuss political gains and losses.
In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and an earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of scholars who were upright, dared to speak out, and could try their best to persuade. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to wait for the imperial edict.
Gu Yong replied:
Your Majesty has the purest moral character of the most sage. He is worried about the strange phenomena warned by heaven and earth. He organizes his own state affairs, inquires and adopts the suggestions of the ministers, and issues wise orders, asking the officials to recommend people who dare to speak out. He takes the time to summon them to explore the origins of the changes, to find the reasons for the heaven's punishment, so that we scholars can come to the court of the sage to accept the inquiry of the sage.
I am not very talented and have little knowledge, and I am not familiar with political affairs.
I have heard privately that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he should correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, establish the rules of imperial rule, and obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. Only in this way can many auspicious signs appear in sequence below, and only when the sun and moon move in the sky can there be Laws; if the king is too indulged in the harem, content with pleasure and hunting, and loses the correction of the five things, and the rules of rule cannot be established, then the signs of disaster will come and the six abnormal phenomena of punishment will appear.
All disasters and visions appear, each symbolizing a fault and warning the world according to its type.
So on the first day of the twelfth lunar month, when the solar eclipse was in Wu Nu, and the earthquake was in Xiao Qiang, both happened on the same day. I repeatedly told Your Majesty that those mistakes are not too far away, and you should deeply look for the reasons in yourself.
Is it God's will that His Majesty pays attention to women's sex, does not worry about political affairs, does not behave prudently, and repeatedly loses his integrity?
Is it because she dotes on concubines too much, because women do not abide by women's ethics, because they want to possess the Holy One alone due to jealousy, and hinder the prosperity of their descendants?
The ancient kings abolished the five principles of justice and lost the moral relationship between husband and wife. If their wives and concubines were favored, they could fulfill their requests internally and abuse their power externally, to the point of overthrowing the country and confusing and disrupting the order of yin and yang.
In the past, Guo Si was in power, and Zong Zhou lost his country because of it; Yan's wife was arrogant and pampered, so she became prosperous, so there was a solar eclipse.
This is a sign of a vision.
The scriptures say: The principle of imperial rule is to greatly establish the rule of justice.
The Sutra says: If the rules of governance are not upright, this is called non-establishment. At this time, the movement of the sun and the moon will be chaotic.
Your Majesty ascended the most noble throne and became the monarch of the world. He accepted the responsibilities of an emperor to rule all living beings. Peace and instability in the four directions are all under your control.
If you really can pay attention to self-correction, strive to do things to the best of your ability, reduce the time for private banquets to worry about the affairs of the world, give up and stay away from over-indulged pleasures, stop advocating for the entertainment of outstanding artists, put an end to behaviors that are not enjoyed by ghosts and gods, carefully control the fun of hunting and hunting, have certain rules in your daily life, follow the etiquette and law, manage political affairs personally, devote yourself to practical actions without being tired, and do everything with peace of mind as natural as nature.
The scriptures say: From now on, kings who inherit the ancestral inheritance should not indulge too much in banquets or indulge in hunting, but should only revise themselves respectfully.
There is no such thing as a lord who can cultivate the righteousness himself while his ministers are treacherous.
The relationship between husband and wife is the rule of law for the king and the key to the safety of the country. It is what a wise king should be most cautious about.
In the past, Shun warned the two women to speak and behave in a correct manner to make his noble character even nobler; King Zhuang of Chu endured the pain and did not see Danji, thus achieving the feat of overlord; King You of Zhou was deceived by Bao Si, and Zhou's virtue declined and the country perished; Duke Huan of Lu was coerced by Qi's daughter Jiang, and the state of Ji was overthrown.
If you can really regulate the affairs of the harem and clarify the order of superiority and inferiority, those with high status cannot monopolize the emperor's favor due to jealousy, so as to cut off the traces of arrogance and arrogance, and suppress the troubles such as Guo Si and Yan's wife. Those with low status can serve the monarch in order, and each can perform their duties. It can expand the continuation of future generations, quell the resentment of "White Flowers" and the like, and make them rich financially with relatives in the harem, and do not let them participate in political affairs. This can alienate people like the emperor's father who rely on favor to get official positions, weaken the power of the wife's party, and the world will be in chaos without the maintenance of the boudoir.
To conquer the distant place, we must start by governing the near place, and to learn good conduct must start from the people around us.
In the past, the dragon was in charge of Nayan, and Shun's orders were honest and obedient; the four assistants were complete, and the king made no mistakes.
If you can really tell the ministers who are in charge of everything, those who wear the golden mink ornaments and hold the responsibilities of Chang Bo, let them learn the ways of the previous kings and understand the righteousness between monarchs and ministers. Everyone will learn to be cautious and trustworthy, and will not play the fault of arrogance and indulgence. Then the ministers on the left and right will be respectful and obedient, and the officials will look up to them and follow their example, and the education will spread to all directions.
The scriptures say: We must first rectify and control the ministers on the left and right.
There is no right and left ministers who are upright but all the officials are dishonest.
If those who rule the world respect the virtuous and judge their merits, then the world will be peaceful; if they despise the virtuous, regardless of their merits, the world will be in chaos.
If you really can carefully consider the method of governing the people, rejoice in the blessing of capable people, select scholars based on their talents, and be sure to put them on trial for their positions, clearly define the assessment standards to measure their abilities, and examine their actual merits to evaluate their virtues, and do not use gangs to engage in private interests. If you don't listen to the false praises of others, and don't listen to the false accusations that are accumulated, then the officials who have the responsibility of correcting their merits will not have to worry about their merits being hidden and slandered. People who form cliques and engage in evil and cunning can't get official positions. The number of villains is decreasing day by day, and the number of talented and capable people is increasing day by day.
The scriptures say: The performance of officials is assessed once every three years. After three assessments, those who have done nothing but have no merit will be dismissed, and those who have merit will be promoted.
He also said: People with nine virtues are appointed to work, and those who are outstanding and capable are given official positions.
If rewards based on merit are not implemented, many talented people are placed in official positions, but the country is not peaceful.
During Yao's time, there was a flood, and the world was divided into twelve states. The power to control distant areas was weakened, but there was no disaster of rebellion. This was because Yao's virtues were honest and generous, and his people had no resentment.
The Qin Dynasty was on a smooth and unhindered land. One man raised his arms and shouted, and the whole world collapsed and disintegrated. This was because the punishments were severe and cruel, and the officials' behavior was cruel and vicious.
There is no one more powerful than a cruel and vicious official who disobeys God's will, corrupts morals, and brings resentment to the people on behalf of the monarch.
Can you really expel the cruel, cruel and cruel officials, abolish them, increase the number of gentle, kind and virtuous people to care for the people, ease the punishment and release the wronged people to regulate the lives of the people, reduce corvee labor, do not take away farm time, and collect less taxes. Taxes should not exhaust the people's financial resources, so that the people of the world can live and work in peace and contentment, not suffering from delayed labor, not worrying from harsh politics, and not suffering from cruel officials. Even if there was a great disaster in the Tang Dynasty, the people did not betray their monarch.
The scriptures say: He cares and settles the people, and shows kindness to the widowed and widowed.
There is no such thing as a monarch who is virtuous and honest, and officials who are virtuous, but the people are rebellious.
I heard that visions of disaster are used by the emperor to reprimand and warn people for their mistakes, just like the clear warnings of a kind and strict father.
If you are afraid of worry and correct yourself respectfully, then the disaster will disappear and blessings will come; if you ignore the warning of contempt, the punishment of disaster will not be eliminated.
The scriptures say: If you act in accordance with God's will, the five blessings will come; if you act contrary to God's will, the six extremes will come.
The Sutra says: Six kinds of disasters arise and appear. If you do not cultivate virtue respectfully to prevent disasters, the six kinds of punishments will invade, and the six kinds of disasters and strange phenomena will come.
In the past three years, disasters and visions have appeared in droves, both large and small. This is because the actions are not in line with the will of the Emperor of Heaven, and the Emperor of Heaven is not happy, which is very obvious.
If you don't seek the reasons within yourself, you won't be able to make corrections. If you recommend scholars quickly and solicit opinions widely, but don't adopt their opinions, you are following a path that is not in line with God's will. If you don't take practical actions to thank you, the punishment from the Emperor of Heaven will be heavier.
These five matters are the laws of the king's political affairs and are important matters for governing from the south. I hope your majesty will pay attention to them.
The emperor was surprised when the countermeasures were advanced and summoned Gu Cheng specially.
That summer, all the founders were ordered to come up with countermeasures. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Du Qin".
After Gu Yong finished answering, he continued: I was fortunate enough to be able to make a statement about the effectiveness of the disaster. The disaster was extreme, and the words were related to the sage you listened to.
The memorial statement was given in front of him, but His Majesty rejected it and refused to adopt it, but instead gave in to the correct countermeasures. He did not face up to the unusual phenomena that were worthy of worry, asked for ordinary opinions that were not urgent, and abolished the wise words that were in line with God's will. He offered useless empty words, trying to obliterate the disaster and deceive the emperor, so the emperor became angry. The storms between armies and Ji came three times, uprooting and breaking the trees. This is the most holy test of the emperor and cannot be deceived.
The emperor specifically asked Gu Yong, and Gu Yong replied: The solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine.
This incident is recorded in the "Five Elements Chronicles".
At this time, the emperor had just ascended the throne. He was modest and courteous and entrusted the political affairs to the general Wang Feng. Most of the ministers blamed Wang Feng.
Gu Yong knew that Wang Feng had just been trusted and took power, and secretly wanted to rely on Wang Feng, so he said:
Now that all the barbarians have surrendered, they have all become your concubines. There is no need to worry about making porridge or food in the north, and there is no need to worry about Zhao Tuo or Lu Jia in the south. The borders on three sides are stable, and there is no warning of military revolution.
The big princes only had salaries in several counties, and the officials of the imperial court controlled their power, preventing them from doing anything. There was no longer a situation where Wu, Chu, Yan, and Liang stood side by side.
Hundreds of officials are intertwined, close to each other, and the flesh and blood ministers are as loyal as Shen Bo, pious and respectful, cautious and fearful, and there are no rebellions such as Chonghe, Anyang, and Bolu.
These three aspects are not as fine as a hair, and cannot be blamed on the uncles.
This and those who want to use political affairs to find fault with the prime minister and his son, slander the ministers and eunuchs, and excuse unusual visions, are all people who use unreasonable fallacies to deceive the emperor of heaven.
Privately, I am afraid that Your Majesty will make obvious mistakes, ignore the clear warnings of heaven and earth, listen to the unreasonable fallacies of ignorant people, blame innocent people, attribute the occurrence of disasters to political affairs, and deeply lose the will of the Emperor of Heaven. This is extremely unacceptable.
His Majesty ascended the throne and appointed officials according to the old rules without any political fault.
In the first month of the first year, white air clearly rose from the east. By April of the first year, yellow turbid air filled everywhere, covering the capital, and major floods occurred, which were manifested by earthquakes and solar eclipses.
Each has its own account and fulfillment, and the exterior and interior are related to each other. There is nothing to attribute and rely on in all officials and affairs. Isn't it strange to Your Majesty?
The white air rising from the east is a sign that lowly people will rise; the yellow turbid air covering the capital is a sign of the decline and severance of the king's way.
The sluts are rising while the royal power in the capital is declining, which creates a bad experience in both aspects.
Your Majesty can really understand the words of my foolish minister, devote himself to worrying about the vision of heaven and earth, think long-term about the grand plan of the ancestral temple, change the mistakes of the past, get rid of indulgence, eliminate biased favor, strengthen the power of hard work, equally share the favor of the Emperor of Heaven, so that all the concubines can be served in turn.
Judging from this method, it is actually a blessing for Your Majesty to have descendants among humble people.
It's just to get the descendants to inherit. There is nothing mean about a mother.
Send harems and concubines who are suitable for the emperor's wishes, and widely seek among humble people, so that they can encounter the help shown by the emperor, comfort and resolve the worries and resentments of the empress dowager, reconcile and eliminate the blame and anger of the emperor, then the descendants will multiply, and disasters and strange phenomena will cease.
If your majesty fails to observe my words deeply and ignores the warnings of heaven and earth, the source of the disaster will not be eliminated. Water and rain disasters, mountain and rock strange phenomena will occur soon; so many disasters have occurred and have reached the extreme, and the changes in the celestial phenomena have taken shape. Even if I want to sacrifice my life and offer advice, it will be of no use.
He who alienates humble ministers dares to state the will of God forthrightly, rebukes and ridicules the privacy of the palace curtains, wants to alienate the noble queen and the favored concubine, but knows that his harsh words are not in line with the emperor's will, and he will definitely not be exempted from the punishment of soup and wok.
This is because the Emperor of Heaven has blessed the Han family and enabled me to dare to say this frankly.
After entering the sealed memorial three times, he was summoned; after ten days of waiting for the edict, he was able to see the Holy One.
It is very difficult to offer loyal advice from a distant and humble position; it is not easy to hear the will of God from the most exalted position.
These words must not be leaked. I hope to write down what I said in detail, and have the servants report it to Your Majesty, and show it to the ministers close to you.
The confidant minister thinks that it is not God's will, and I should be punished for lying. If I think it is God's will, why should I forget the fundamentals of the country and go against God's will to indulge my selfish desires!
Your Majesty, please carefully examine and consider carefully, and make many plans for the ancestral temple.
There were dozens of people who dealt with it at that time, and Gu Yong and Du Qin were the best among them.
The emperor showed all their memorials to the harem.
Later, the emperor sent a letter to Empress Xu, quoting Gu Yong's words to rebuke her. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Foreign Relations".
Gu Yong had secretly lobbied for General Wang Feng, and he was indeed the most talented, so he was promoted to Doctor Guanglu.
Gu Yongjin wrote a letter to thank Wang Feng, saying: I only have a talent as small as Dou Shuu, and I have little qualifications and poor knowledge. I have no one-day friendship with the general, and I have no introduction. The general appreciated my arrogant words and promoted me from the position of a small official in soap clothes to the last position of a remonstrating minister. I did not listen to Ji Jian! Deep accusation. If false slanders are not accepted, even if Qi Huan and Jin Wen appoint scholars who are close to each other and have a wise father and wise brother to protect and raise their children, it is really not possible to do more!
In the past, Yuzi swallowed charcoal, ruined his voice, and his face to repay the unusual treatment. The guests from the Qi family came to repay Lord Mengchang's kindness. Zhishi and Mengchang also had warriors who died for them, not to mention the general's disciples!
Wang Feng treated Gu Yong favorably.
Many years later, Gu Yong left the capital and became the prefect of Anding.
At that time, all the emperor's uncles were studying classics and taking charge of government affairs.
According to the order of age, Ping Ahou Wang Tan should succeed General Wang Feng to assist in political affairs, especially to be friendly with Gu Yong.
During the Yangshuo period, Wang Feng died.
When Wang Feng was seriously ill, he recommended his cousin Wang Yin, the imperial censor, to replace him.
The emperor followed his advice and appointed Wang Yin as the chief chariot and cavalry general to lead the ministerial affairs, while Ping'ahou Wang Tan gave him the official position of special promotion and led the city gate soldiers.
Gu Yong heard about this and wrote a letter to Wang Tan saying: You have the character of Zhou Gong and Zhao Gong, have the conduct of Guanzi and Yanzi, respect talented people and treat them with humility, and like to do good deeds tirelessly. You should have been a general long ago. Because of the general's presence, you are depressed at home and cannot express your sorrow and anger.
Now that the general has unfortunately passed away prematurely, it should be your turn to rank in order of closeness and ability.
On the day of the ceremony, the scholar-bureaucrats in the capital were disappointed.
This is all because we people are stupid and have low talents, and we cannot reward and praise even one ten thousandth of it.
Recently I heard that you lead the city gate soldiers with the special rank, which makes the general of chariots and cavalry in power in the court with grace and grace, while your dearest uncle is holding the keys to the city gate outside.
I'm personally unhappy for you.
You should resolutely demand to resign, state that your talents are not enough to strengthen the guards of the city gate, accept the name of Taibo's humility, keep the path of humility, close the door and sleep in peace, and be the leader of wise people.
I hope you will consider this matter with knowledgeable people, and I have arranged it for you.
Wang Tan was very moved by his letter, so he refused to accept the position of leading the city gate.
From then on, Wang Tan and Wang Yin were at odds with each other.
Gu Yong was working as a county official in a distant place. He was worried about being harmed by Wang Yin, so he claimed that he had been ill for three full months and was relieved of his duties.
Wang Yinzhuo asked Gu Yong to be appointed as the commander of the camp. Gu Yong apologized many times and stated his case, so he was transferred to the post of Chang Shi.
Because Wang Yin transcended his close relatives and assisted in political affairs as a cousin, his power and influence were lower than those of Wang Feng. Gu Yong then persuaded Wang Yin and said: "The general holds the position of general, enfeoffs the fertile land of the big city, bears the same responsibilities as Duke of Zhou and Duke of Zhao, and controls the secrets of the world. It can be called the ultimate wealth. If there is no second among ministers, the world's blame will come from all sides. What will you rely on to occupy this position?"
You should work tirelessly day and night, with a strong character like Yi Yin, to uphold your duties and assist the emperor, punish evildoers without avoiding those who are close to you, believe in and love them, and promote virtuous people without avoiding those who are hostile and hostile, so as to show the greatest justice and establish credibility in all directions.
Only by concentrating on implementing these three aspects can you be able to shoulder heavy responsibilities for a long time and enjoy deep favor for a long time.
Taibai appeared in the west for sixty days. According to the law, it should reach the sky. Now it has expired and is still among the mulberry trees. Its body is weak and its movement is slow. Its shape is small and its light is weak.
Yinghuojiao is strong, large and bright, and is located in Ojuku in retrograde motion.
When Mars is retrograde, it is fixed; when Mars is in Osu, it is mutable.
Does God's will mean that the general forgets the deep and hidden righteousness, is submissive, the deacon is not strong, does not widely appoint scholars, still has taboos about likes and dislikes, and the magnanimous character is not pure, and is the beginning of betrayal by the generals and ministers?
Why did Venus and Mars mutate like this when you just inherited the title of Sima?
God is the most holy and will not show visions out of thin air. I hope that the general will look at all this with awe and caution, think deeply about the reasons for the changes, and change the way to seek governance to comply with God's will.
Wang Yin still couldn't calm down and recommended Gu Yong to be the guardian envoy.
When Wang Yin died, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Chengdu, took his place as the Great Sima Wei General, and Gu Yong was promoted to the governor of Liangzhou.
After finishing the performance in the capital, it was time to go to the ministry. At that time, a black dragon appeared in Shulai. The emperor sent a minister to ask Gu Yong to hear what he had to say.
Gu Yong replied:
I heard that the people who rule the world and occupy the country are worried that the monarch's behavior will endanger the country, but the words of warning of danger cannot be heard by the monarch. If the words of warning of danger were heard by the monarch immediately, then the Shang and Zhou Dynasties would not change their surnames and rise alternately, and the three generations would not change their politics but use each other.
The Xia and Shang Dynasties were about to perish, and everyone on the road knew it, but the monarch safely thought that no one could harm him like the sun in the sky. Therefore, his sins became more and more serious, but he himself did not know it, and his fate was overthrown, but he did not realize it.
