Although Huainan is a small place, Yingbu once used it to rebel against the Han Dynasty. It was really lucky for the Han Dynasty to exist.
It would be unwise to let the enemy possess capital that could endanger the Han Dynasty.
Although King Li's four sons were separated, they had the same idea of ​​avenging their father.
Give them a lot of people and enable them to accumulate a lot of property. If they do not openly raise armies in the capital to avenge like Wu Zixu and Bai Gong, there will be assassinations like Zhuanzhu and Jingke. This is the so-called lending weapons to thieves and giving wings to tigers.
I hope your Majesty will give it some thought!
Liang Wang Liu Sheng fell from his horse and died. Jia Yi lamented that he had failed in his duty as a tutor and often cried. More than a year later, he also died.
Jia Yi was thirty-three years old when he died.
Four years later, King Qi Wen died without a son.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty remembered Jia Yi's words, so he divided Qi into six small kingdoms and made King Hui's six sons king respectively. He also transferred Huainan King Liu happy to Chengyang, divided Huainan into three small countries, and made King Li's six sons king respectively.
In the next ten years, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty died and Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Wu, Chu, Zhao and the four Qi kings jointly rebelled and marched westward to the Mojing city of Chang'an. Liang Xiao Wang Liu Wu defended Chang'an and finally defeated the Seven Kingdoms.
By the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the son of King Li of Huainan became king, and some of the two rebelled against him and were executed.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ascended the throne and appointed Jia Yi's two grandsons as prefects of the county.
Among them, Maijia is the most studious and inherits a scholarly family background.
Praise: Liu Xiangcheng Jia Yi talked about the significance of the Xia, Shang, Zhou and Qin dynasties in regulating chaos. His discussion was very beautiful. He was familiar with national regulations and systems. Even Yi Yin and Guan Zhong in ancient times could not surpass him.
If his ideas had been implemented at that time, his achievements and enlightenment would have been significant.
But it is really sad that he was framed by mediocrity.
Looking back, we can see that Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was quiet and inactive, and took action to change customs. The ideas stated by Jia Yi were slightly implemented.
When he wanted to change the system, because the Han Dynasty was a native country, he advocated yellow, and used five as the official seal number. When he wanted to try to own a vassal state, he used Jia Yi's "five baits" and "three watches" to tightly tie the Chanyu, and his method was effective.
Jia Yi died young. Although he did not become a public official, he was not without opportunities.
He wrote a total of fifty-eight articles, and the content relevant to current affairs was extracted and written in his biography.
summary:
Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was renowned for his literary talents at eighteen. Governor Wu Gong of Henan summoned him after hearing of his abilities. When Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne, he appointed Wu Gong as a court captain due to his excellent governance and connection to Li Si. Wu Gong recommended Jia Yi, who was then made a doctor at around twenty years old, the youngest among them. Jia Yi excelled in court discussions, impressing the emperor, who promoted him to Taizhong doctor within a year. Jia Yi proposed reforming the calendar, legal system, and rituals, drafting regulations with yellow as the noble color and a five-character seal. Emperor Wen hesitated to implement these changes, but many legal reforms and the relocation of princes were Jia Yi's ideas.

Jealous officials slandered Jia Yi, leading to his demotion as Tutor to the Prince of Changsha. On his journey, he wrote a poem mourning Qu Yuan, comparing their fates. The poem lamented Qu Yuan's unjust exile and suicide, criticizing a world that values the worthless over the worthy. Jia Yi advised retreat and self-preservation, using metaphors of dragons and phoenixes to urge distancing from corruption. He argued that Qu Yuan should have sought a wise ruler rather than cling to Chu.

In his third year in Changsha, an owl, an unlucky bird, entered Jia Yi's room. He wrote a poem exploring fate and fortune, reflecting on the cyclical nature of life and the futility of human concerns. The poem discusses the interplay of fortune and misfortune, using examples like Li Si and Fu Yue to illustrate unpredictability. It advocates detachment from worldly desires, embracing the Dao, and accepting life's transience. Jia Yi concluded that the owl's omen was trivial.

Emperor Wen later recalled Jia Yi, discussing ghosts and gods late into the night. Impressed, he appointed Jia Yi as Tutor to his favored son, King Huai of Liang. Jia Yi frequently advised on state affairs, highlighting crises: the Xiongnu threat, rebellious princes, and corrupt customs. He argued that the realm was not truly peaceful, comparing it to sleeping on a pyre. He proposed dividing large fiefdoms to weaken princes, using historical examples to show that power leads to rebellion. He urged the emperor to adopt a system of smaller states to ensure stability, warning that inaction would lead to disaster.

Jia Yi criticized the Xiongnu policy of appeasement, calling it humiliating and ineffective. He offered to subdue them through strategy. He also condemned lavish dress among commoners, which drained resources and undermined social hierarchy. He lamented the decline of moral standards, tracing it to Qin's abandonment of propriety. He advocated for early education of the crown prince, citing the long reigns of Xia, Shang, and Zhou, which prioritized ritual and moral instruction, unlike Qin's harsh laws that led to rapid collapse.

Jia Yi emphasized the importance of ritual over punishment, arguing that ritual prevents wrongdoing subtly, while punishment only reacts. He urged the emperor to respect ministers, using historical examples to show that honor fosters loyalty. He advised against humiliating officials, as it erodes their integrity. He used the case of Zhou Bo, falsely accused of treason, to argue for leniency. Emperor Wen heeded this, and thereafter, guilty ministers committed suicide rather than face execution.

Jia Yi later proposed strengthening the kingdoms of Huaiyang and Liang to counter powerful princes like Huainan. He warned against granting titles to the sons of the rebellious King Li of Huainan, predicting they would seek revenge. Emperor Wen partially adopted his advice, appointing Liu Wu as King of Liang. After Jia Yi's death at thirty-three, his predictions came true: the Seven Kingdoms rebelled, but Liang's strength helped suppress them. Emperor Wu later executed some of King Li's sons for rebellion.

The historian praised Jia Yi's insights on governance, comparing him to Yi Yin and Guan Zhong. Though his ideas were only partially implemented, his writings on statecraft were influential. His early death prevented him from reaching high office, but his legacy endured through his fifty-eight essays.

translation:
Jia Shan is from Yingchuan.
His grandfather Jia Qu was a doctoral student of King Wei during the Warring States Period.
Jia Shan studied under Jia Qu, and his remarks were widespread in various schools of thought, but he could not specialize in Confucianism.
He once worked under Marquis Yingyin as a riding attendant.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Jia Shan used Qin as an example to talk about the way to control chaos. He titled it "Zhi Yan" and said this:
I heard that as a minister, you should use your wholeheartedness and wisdom to advise your superior directly, even if you don't hesitate to behead him. This is what I did with Jia Shan.
I dare not give examples that are too far back. I would like to use Qin as an example. I hope your majesty will pay more attention to it.
People who are poor and humble can cultivate their own moral character, become famous in the world, and make future generations prosperous.
But the Qin Dynasty was not like this. With the dignity of the emperor and the great wealth in the world, it imposed tyranny and extorted money, which made the people tired of coping. The roads were filled with criminals, and there were hordes of thieves in the mountains and fields. Everyone in the world was eager to cause chaos.
One person raised his arms and shouted, and the whole country responded, creating the anti-Qin movement initiated by Chen Sheng.
Not only that, the Qin Dynasty also built more than 300 palaces from Xianyang to the west to Yongcheng, and added bells, drums and curtains to them, so that they can be enjoyed everywhere without having to remove them from elsewhere.
He also built the Epang Palace, which was dozens of feet high, five miles long from east to west, and a thousand paces wide from north to south. Cars and horses could gallop through it without any hindrance, and even the flags on the carriages could not be crooked.
He built such a magnificent palace, but his descendants did not even have a house to stay in.
He also built roads leading to various places, reaching as far as Yanqi, Wuchu in the south, the rivers and lakes, and the shores of the East China Sea, reaching everywhere.
The road is fifty steps wide, with trees planted every three feet. A thick wall is built outside the road, tamped with iron vertebrae, and green pine trees are planted.
Building such a spectacular road has left no room for future generations to pass through.
The Lishan Mausoleum, where the First Emperor was buried after his death, took ten years to build with the labor of hundreds of thousands of prisoners under the supervision of officials.
The tomb is deep, with spring water flowing down from it. Ore is collected, copper is smelted and the inner wall is cast to seal it. The outside is painted with raw lacquer and decorated with pearls, jade and jade. There are palaces and other playgrounds inside the tomb, and vegetation is planted on the tomb, just like a mountain forest. Building such a luxurious mausoleum deprived his descendants of even a small earthen grave with grass growing there.
Qin, with its strong national power, was as greedy as tigers and wolves, cannibalizing the princes and swallowing up the world without committing to the implementation of etiquette and justice, so the heaven sent disasters to punish it.
I'm risking my life to tell you. I hope you'll pay attention and carefully choose where it makes sense.
I have heard that when a loyal minister serves the monarch and his words are sincere but not trusted, his life will be endangered. If he is not sincere and sincere, he will not be able to explain the right way. Therefore, deep and sincere advice is what a wise monarch is eager to hear, and what loyal ministers want to say with all their wisdom and at the expense of their lives.
On barren land, even if there are good seeds, crops will not grow; on the silt land on the banks of rivers, even if there are poor seeds, lush seedlings can grow.
In the last days of the Xia Dynasty and Shang Dynasty, although there were sages like Long Feng, Ji Zi, and Bigan who sacrificed their lives for the way of justice, their way was not implemented.
During the reign of King Wen of Zhou, heroes and wise men could give full play to their talents, and common people who cut grass and collected firewood could also do their part. This was the reason for the rise of the Zhou Dynasty.
Therefore, the fertile land is conducive to the growth of seedlings, and the benevolent monarch is good at supporting outstanding talents.
Everything struck by thunder will be broken; everything pressed by ten thousand stones will be shattered.
Now the power of the monarch is more than just thunder; the weight of power is more than just the tyrannical force.
They open up a wide range of opinions in order to seek advice, accept and adopt their suggestions cheerfully, and give those who give advice a glorious status. Even so, the scholars are still afraid and dare not express their opinions fully. What's more, the monarch does whatever he wants, is tyrannical and hates to hear his own faults?
Use force and power to intimidate and suppress them. Even if there are people as wise as Yao and Shun and as brave as Meng Ben, who will not be crushed and subdued?
In this case, the monarch will not be able to hear his own faults; if he cannot hear his own faults, the country will be in danger.
The system of the ancient sage-kings was as follows: historians recorded the monarch's faults in front of them, poets recited proverbs to admonish the monarch, blind people recited poems to admonish the monarch, ministers gave honest advice, scholars passed documents to express their opinions, civilians criticized the monarch's faults on the road, and merchants discussed the monarch's faults in the market. Only then did the monarch hear his faults.
Correct your mistakes when you hear them, and follow the good ones, and you will rule the world for a long time.
With the dignity of the Son of Heaven, there is no one in the world who is not willing to be a subject out of kindness and righteousness.
However, he supported the three elders in Taixue. The emperor personally provided food and drink, and then brought wine and wine. Zhu Chi and Zhu Chi served him in the front and back. The ministers held canes for him, and the doctors put on his shoes. He promoted talented people to assist him, and sought out honest people to give advice.
Therefore, respecting the three elders with the dignity of the emperor is to show one's filial piety; appointing assistant ministers is to prevent one's own pride; appointing people to give direct advice is because one is afraid that one's faults will not be heard; asking for advice from those who cut grass and chop wood is because one seeks perfection and is never satisfied; businessmen and common people accuse one's own faults and are able to correct them because they follow the good and listen to everything.
Once upon a time, King Yingzheng of Qin conquered the princes by force, ruled the world, wiped out the six kingdoms, established counties and counties, and built the Great Wall as a border pass.
How can the stability, size, and importance of the Qin Dynasty be compared with the wealth of a family and the strength of one person?
However, the army was defeated by Chen She and the land was seized by the Liu family. What was the reason?
Because the King of Qin was greedy and tyrannical, he harmed the world and made the people miserable in order to satisfy his own desires.
In the past, there were about 1,800 princes in the Zhou Dynasty, and the people of Jiuzhou supported 1,800 monarchs. They did no more than three days of corvee work every year and collected one-tenth of the tax.
Qin Shihuang supported himself with 1,800 people from the princes, but the people exhausted their physical strength and could not complete the corvee service, and exhausted their property and could not meet his needs.
As a monarch, he only entertains himself by driving horses, shooting arrows and hunting, and the world's financial resources are in short supply.
The tired people had no rest, the hungry and cold people had no food and clothing, the innocent people were killed, and the tortured people had nowhere to file their grievances and judge their grievances, so that everyone resented him and every family hated him. As a result, Qin's world fell apart.
When Qin Shihuang was alive, the world had been corrupted, but he did not know it.
Qin Shihuang inspected the east and reached Kuaiji and Langye. He carved stones to describe his achievements, thinking that he could govern the world better than Yao and Shun. He weighed the weight of copper and iron to cast bells and yu, and sifted out fine and clean soil to build the Epang Palace. He thought that his descendants would forever own the world.
The ancient sage kings practiced Mi Dharma, and their descendants could rule for thirty or forty generations. Even Yao, Yu Shun, Xia Yu, Shang Tang, Zhou Wen, and Zhou Wu, who had extended their kindness and laid the foundation for future generations, could only rule for twenty or thirty generations.
Qin Shihuang said that after his death, he would be honored by Mi, which would sometimes lead to the duplication of the names of father and son. However, if he were named as the first, second, or even ten thousand generations, they would never be repeated. Therefore, he was called the First Emperor after his death, and his successor was the second emperor. He wanted to pass it on from one life to all generations.
Qin Shihuang considered his own merits and speculated on his future generations, thinking that he would rule forever from generation to generation. However, just a few months after his death, people from all over the world attacked the Qin Dynasty from all sides, causing the ancestral temple to become extinct.
Qin Shihuang was in danger of losing his country but he didn't know it. Why?
Because no one in the world dared to tell him.
Why didn't anyone dare to tell him?
Because he did not have the kindness to provide for the elderly, nor did he set up assistant ministers or remonstrators, he punished as he pleased, drove away those who criticized him, and killed those who remonstrated directly. Therefore, everyone catered to his taste, flattered and tolerated, and compared his virtues, he was said to be more merciful than Yao and Shun.
"The Book of Songs" says: It's not that wise people can't tell right from wrong and give advice. Why don't they give advice?
Because he was afraid of violating the monarch's taboos and being punished.
If you give advice and the monarch listens to it, you will state your opinions to the monarch in detail; if you give advice and the monarch does not listen, you will retreat and avoid it.
That's what it means. He also said: King Wen of Zhou was able to stabilize the world because he had many scholars.
The world has never been without scholars, but why is it only said that King Wen stabilized the world with many scholars? King Wen likes to be benevolent, so he can promote benevolent government; he can respect the scholars by getting native people, so the scholars can serve him, and he can use the scholars with propriety and justice.
Therefore, if you don’t have love and respect for the scholars, you can’t make them loyal; if you can’t be loyal, you can’t do your best; if you can’t do your best, you can’t achieve results. Therefore, a wise monarch treats his ministers with high titles and generous salaries. The monarch should wear linen and mourn for him, and attend the funeral three times in person; before the deceased was buried, the monarch would not drink alcohol or eat meat; before the deceased was buried, the monarch would not play music or entertainment; the minister happened to die during the ancestral temple sacrifice, so he should be spared the ancestral temple sacrifice.
Therefore, I dare not fail to serve the monarch with all my heart, so that my merits will be established in future generations and my reputation will be spread forever.
Now, Your Majesty, you miss your ancestors and recall their merits in order to show their illustrious achievements and beautiful character to the world. He ordered the world to recommend virtuous and upright divination, and the officials and people of the world rejoiced, saying that the emperor was going to implement the principles of Yao and Shun and create the achievements of the Three Kings.
There is no one in the world who does not work hard to cultivate his own moral character in order to receive the emperor's kindness.
Now the upright men have been selected into the imperial court, and the better ones are selected to serve as regular servants and officials, and they ride with them, shoot and hunt, and go out two or three times a day.
I am afraid that from now on, the government will be lax, the officials will be slack, and the princes will be lazy to perform their duties after hearing the news.
Since your Majesty came to the throne, you have encouraged yourself to be kind to the world, reduced food expenses, refused to listen to extravagant music, reduced the number of soldiers guarding the border and guarding the palace, stopped the county and state's annual contribution of gifts to the court; The number of horses in the palace stables was high, and the excess horses were given to the inns in various places. Many gardens were abolished and distributed to farmers for farming. More than 100,000 pieces of silk were given to the poor; they paid tribute to the elderly, those over ninety years old, One son is exempted from service, and two people in the family who are over eighty years old are exempted from taxes; all men in the world are rewarded with titles, and all ministers are promoted to public ministers; ministers and the emperor's clan are rewarded with gold from the royal palace, and all are favored by the emperor; sinners are pardoned, pity them for having no hair, and given them turbans, pity them for wearing ocher prison uniforms with writing on their backs, father, son, and brothers are embarrassed when they meet, so they are given clothes.
Everyone in the world will be happy if unjust prison sentences are redressed and punishments are reduced.
Therefore, in the first year of the year, there will be happy rains and abundant harvests. This is God’s way of helping you.
When the punishment is light, but the number of people who break the law is small, there is more food and clothing than in previous years, but there are fewer thieves. This is the reason why people in the world obey you.
I heard that when officials in Shandong issued edicts, the people, even the old, weak, sick and disabled, went to listen on crutches, hoping to live longer and see the arrival of a peaceful and prosperous age when virtue would influence people.
Now that my achievements have been achieved, my reputation for virtuous government has been known to the world, and I have won the admiration of all directions, but I lead virtuous ministers and upright people, and hunt and shoot arrows with them every day, chasing and chasing foxes, but my achievements have been greatly damaged, and everyone in the world has been disappointed. I am secretly sad about this.
"The Book of Songs" says: People are all close to the good path at the beginning, but few can persist to the end.
My greatest wish is that you will control your hunting activities, announce government decrees in the Mingtang in the second month of the lunar calendar, visit the students at the Imperial College, and practice the way of the ancestors.
The wind of benevolence and righteousness has been formed, and the foundation of eternity has been laid, and then you can leisurely enjoy yourself.
In ancient times, ministers were courteous and unobtrusive, so the monarch did not always appear very serious and intimidating.
Ministers cannot have fun with the monarch, and upright and honest people cannot go hunting with the monarch. Instead, they should devote themselves to their own duties and cultivate noble moral integrity. In this way, the ministers will not dare not correct their conduct, strengthen their self-cultivation, and perform solemn etiquette with all their heart.
In this way, your monarchy will be respected, your achievements will be promoted throughout the world, and passed down to future generations.
If you don't do this, your character and honor will be damaged day by day.
I secretly feel pity that the moral character cultivated by the wise men at home was destroyed in the emperor's court.
Your Majesty, you can have fun with the ministers, and discuss state affairs with the ministers and founders in the court.
The most important principles are to patrol without being disappointed, to go to court without being disrespectful, and to discuss politics without failing in policy.
Later, Emperor Wen abolished the law prohibiting private coinage, and Mai Shanyi wrote a letter to remonstrate, believing that it was wrong to change the former emperor's law.
He also appealed to the King of Huainan, believing that he was not guilty of any serious crime and that he should be returned to his own kingdom immediately instead of being exiled.
He also said that the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, had evil intentions and deserved to be warned.
Emperor Wen asked the relevant departments to question Maishan about the content of the petition. When answering the question, Maishan believed that: although money is a useless thing, it can be used to exchange for wealth.
Wealth and honor are the emperor's handle for governing the world. Allowing the people to mint their own money means letting the people and the emperor hold this handle together, and it will be difficult to maintain it for a long time.
Maishan's remonstrance was urgent and good at getting to the point of the matter, but Emperor Wen never punished him in order to open up the road to remonstration.
Later, private coinage was banned again. Zou Yang, a native of Qi.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the princes and kings personally governed the people and recruited talents.
King Wu Liu Bi recruited lobbyists from all over the country. Zou Yang, Yan Ji and Mei Cheng of Wu State all served as officials in Wu State. All three of them were famous for their ability to write articles and be good at debating.
After a long period of time, the King of Wu was dissatisfied because his prince was playing chess with Liu Qi, the prince of Emperor Wen at that time. The two had a dispute and the prince of Wu was beaten to death by Liu Qi. So he was dissatisfied and claimed that he was ill and could not go to court to see the emperor. He secretly had a conspiracy to rebel. Zou Yang wrote a letter to advise him.
Because the rebellion was not yet clear and could not be directly accused, I first used Qin as a metaphor, and then transferred to the speculation that Hu, Yue, Qi, Fang, Huainan, etc. were in trouble with the Han court, and then expressed my true intention.
The remonstrance is written like this:
I heard that the First Emperor of Qin was sitting in the Qutai Palace, imposing laws on the world, and drawing the boundaries of the land, but no one dared to offend, and the military power was imposed on Hu Yue; and when the Qin Dynasty declined, Zhang Er and Chen Sheng united with various soldiers and horses to attack Hangu Pass, thereby endangering Xianyang City.
Why is this happening?
Because the counties did not attach themselves to the Qin Dynasty, the people did not help the Qin Dynasty.
Now the Hu people have stepped outside Beihe many times, shooting birds from above, capturing and ambushes from below, and constantly attacking the border towns of the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty also constantly sent reinforcements to fight back, so that the dead followed, chariots carrying weapons were connected to each other, and vehicles carrying grain and grass were in an endless stream.
Why is this happening?
Because the powerful Zhao State wanted to seize Hejian from the Han Dynasty, the six kingdoms of Qi pursued grievances against Emperor Hui and Empress Lu. Liu Xi, the king of Chengyang, and Liu Xingju, the king of the north, were killed and resented the Han emperor. The Three Kingdoms of Huainan moved to the border area in memory of his father Liu Chang. On the way He died, looking for an opportunity to retaliate against the Han Dynasty. Don't worry, my king. I'm afraid that all countries have private grievances to avenge and are unwilling to concentrate on saving the Han Dynasty. The Hu tribe marched to spy on Handan, and the Yue tribe marched to Changsha by water and gathered warships in Qingyang.
Even if Liang Guo was allowed to jointly lead Huaiyang's army, march to Huaidong, cross Guangling, and cut off the Yue people's food routes, and the Han Dynasty also cut off the lower Xihe River and garrisoned Zhangshui in the north to assist in crossing the country, the Hu army continued to advance, and the Yue army continued to penetrate deeper. This is what worries you, your great king.
I heard that when a dragon raises its head and spreads its wings, it will float with the clouds, and the fog and rain will gather around it.
If the sage king sharpens his integrity and cultivates his character, then the people who talk about it will focus on benevolence and righteousness, and think about achieving fame.
Now that I have put forth my suggestions with all my heart, and used all my wisdom and counsel, there will be no country that cannot seek fame; if I repair my evil heart, then which king's disciples will not be able to obtain official positions?
However, the reason why I passed through the royal courts of several countries and came to the shore of Huaihe River from thousands of miles away to join your sect is not because I hate my country and like the people of Wu, but because I am listening below, secretly respecting and appreciating your deeds.
So I hope you don’t ignore it and listen carefully to my wishes.
I heard that a hundred geese all together are no match for one eagle.
When the kingdom of Tread was not divided, people with courage and ability to lift the cauldron, dressed in fine attire, gathered under the Congtai. It was like a market in an instant, but it could not prevent King Tread You from being imprisoned and killed by Queen Lu You.
The king of Huainan made friends with knights from Shandong, and the palace was filled with people who died in service. However, he was unable to cause Huainan King Li to be deposed and relocated, and died in Yong Dynasty.
It is obvious that even warriors like Zhuan Zhu and Meng Ben cannot rest in their positions if the plan is out of time.
Therefore, I hope that your Majesty will consider this matter carefully.
When Emperor Xiaowen entered Hangu Pass and ascended the throne as emperor, he thought the world was in trouble, so he was so worried that he got up before dawn.
After he was established as the emperor, he sent Shu Mouhou and Zhu Xuhou eastward to praise the King of Qi for raising an army to attack the Lu family. Prince Liu Wu and others, who were still ignorant children, set aside fiefdoms and made them kings.
His beloved son Liu Yi was granted the title of King of Liang, Liu Wu was granted the title of acting king, and Huaiyang was merged into the Liang Kingdom.
As a result, the King of Jibei was executed for treason, and his younger brother Liu Chang, King of Huainan, was exiled because of his guilt and died in Yong County. Isn't this because there were treacherous ministers like Xinyuan Ping in the two countries who persuaded the king to rebel? The current emperor has just inherited the late emperor's mission. He plans Shandong on the left and controls Guanzhong on the right. He has changed his plans and the ministers are unpredictable.
Your Majesty, if you do not investigate, I am afraid that the people who are planning for Wu will make wrong suggestions just like Xinyuan Ping lied about getting Zhou Ding in the Han court. If so, our country of Wu will be destroyed, the family will be destroyed, and the descendants will be extinct.
Emperor Gao burned down the plank road and poured water into Zhanghan. He destroyed everything he attacked. He gathered the exhausted people without stopping and rushed eastward out of Hangu Pass, defeating the army of Xiang Yu, the overlord of Western Chu.
Attack by water, Zhang Han lost the city, attack on land, Xiang Yu lost the territory, the Han Dynasty was stable, and the princes could not have any evil intentions.
I hope your Majesty will give it more thought.
The king of Wu did not listen to him.
At this time, King Liang Xiao, the younger brother of Emperor Jing, gained power and recruited scholars. So Zou Yang, Meicheng, and Yan Ji all knew that King Wu could not accept the advice, so they left King Wu and went to Liang to have friends with King Liang.
Zou Yang is very strategic and has a strong temperament. He is uncompromising and independent. He is independent between Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
Yang Sheng and others hated him and slandered him in front of King Liang.
King Liang was very angry and threw Zou Yang into prison, preparing to kill him.
Zou Yang was traveling in a foreign country and was slandered and arrested. He was afraid that he would leave a bad reputation after his death and be reviled by others, so he wrote to the King of Liang from prison:
I heard that loyalty is always rewarded, and honest people will not be suspected. I have always thought this is the case, but now it seems that it is just empty words.
In the past, Jing Ke admired the faith of Prince Dan of Yan, and his sincerity moved heaven, so that a white rainbow passed through the sun, but Prince Dan was afraid that Jing Ke would not assassinate the King of Qin; Mr. Wei planned the strategy of the Changping Battle for Qin, and the Taibai Star entered the Pleiades, covering up the brilliance of the Pleiades stars, but King Zhao of Qin expressed doubts.
The sincere heart caused the heaven and earth to mutate, but could not make Prince Dan and King Qin Zhao believe in them. Isn't this very sad!
Now I am sincerely stating my plan, hoping that you will know it, but your ministers are unclear, and finally I was interrogated by the judge and became suspicious of the world.
The creation is like Mr. Jing Ke and Mr. Wei being reborn, but Prince Dan and King Qin Zhao are still unaware.
I hope your Majesty will take a closer look.
In the past, Bian He offered jade to the King of Chu, but the King of Chu did not know the goods and punished Bian He instead. Li Si was loyal to Qin, but was severely tortured by Hu Hai.
Therefore, Jizi pretended to be crazy and took Yu to escape from the world because he was afraid of suffering such a disaster.
I hope that your Majesty, you will examine the sincerity of Bian He and Li Si, and do not listen to wrong opinions like King Chu and Hu Hai, and do not let me be laughed at by Ji Zi and Jie Yu.
I heard that Bigan was betrayed for his loyalty, and Wu Zixu was killed for his direct remonstrance. Put it into the horse leather, I didn't believe it at first, but now I understand.

Whenever Emperor Wu felt emotional, he asked Meigao to write a poem to express his feelings.
Meigao wrote articles very quickly, and every time there was an edict, it could be completed immediately, so he wrote many poems and poems.
Sima Xiangru was also good at writing articles, but he wrote very slowly, so he did not have many poems, but the quality was higher than that of Mei Gao.
In his poems, Meigao admitted that he was not as good as the poems written by Sima Xiangru. He also said that writing poems was the specialty of opera performers. He was regarded as a haiku and was not respected. He was annoyed that he was similar to a haiku.
So he wrote a poem to mock Dongfang Shuo and himself.
His poems are full of twists and turns, and they follow the situation. He always grasps the key points without losing the original intention, and is humorous and humorous without being too graceful and gentle.
There are one hundred and twenty chapters that can be read, but there are dozens more that are too frivolous and inelegant to be read.
Lu Wenshu, also known as Changjun, was from Shuli, Julu County.
His father worked as the prison gate in Shuli and asked Lu Wenshu to shepherd the sheep. Lu Wenshu collected cattails from the water, cut them into the shape of slips, tied them with ropes, and wrote on them.
When he made some progress in his studies, he asked to be a junior jailer, taking the opportunity to learn the laws and regulations, and was promoted to prison history. Every time the county encountered difficult cases, he asked him for advice.
The prefect inspected various counties. When he saw him, he felt that he was not an ordinary person, so he asked him to perform the task of judging Cao Shi on his behalf.
He also studied "Spring and Autumn" as a teacher and had a rough idea of ​​its general meaning.
He was promoted to Xiaolian and became the county magistrate of Shanyi County. He was dismissed for breaking the law and later became a county official.
During the Yuanfeng period, Li Guang, the court lieutenant, tried to interrogate the prisoners who were raped under the emperor's edict. He asked Lu Wenshu to represent Cao Yu on his behalf and also perform the duties of the court lieutenant's history.
Just in time for the death of Emperor Zhao, King Liu He of Changyi was established as emperor but was immediately deposed. Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne and proclaimed himself emperor. Lu Wenshu wrote to Emperor Xuan, suggesting that benevolence should be upheld and punishments should be lightened.
This is what he said:
I heard that in the state of Qi there was ignorance and rebellion, but Duke Huan of Qi rose up suddenly; in the state of Jin there was trouble with Li Ji, but Duke Wen of Jin dominated the princes.
In modern times, King Tong was imprisoned and died, the Lu family rebelled, and Emperor Xiaowen became the emperor of the Han Dynasty.
From this point of view, the occurrence of disasters opens the way for the emergence of the Holy King.
Therefore, Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin supported the weak emperor, revived the dilapidated princes, followed the cause of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, extended their kindness to the people, and performed meritorious deeds on the princes. Although they were not as good as the three kings, they made the people of the world return to benevolence and righteousness.
Emperor Wen always pursued the supreme virtue of government, complying with the will of God, respecting benevolence and righteousness, mitigating penalties, opening up bridges and bridges, making distance and distance the same, making transportation convenient, respecting worthy people as if they were distinguished guests, and caring for the people as if they were his own sons. He should think carefully about government orders with a generous heart, and only implement them throughout the country when he feels they are reasonable, thus creating a situation where the prisons are empty and the world is peaceful.
Following the chaos, there must be extraordinary kindness. This is the method used by sages to show their destiny.
In the past, when Emperor Zhao died and had no children to inherit the throne, the ministers were worried and discussed anxiously together. They all thought that Liu He, the king of Changyi, was the closest to Emperor Zhao and was his elder brother, with a higher position, so they invited him to be the emperor.
But God did not authorize him, but confused his heart and made him indulge in debauchery, and finally perished in vain.
If we carefully observe the cause of the disaster, we will find that God is opening the way for the saints.
Therefore, the general Huo Guang accepted Emperor Wu's order to assist the Han Dynasty. He was loyal and determined, decided on major plans, eliminated the unjust people, and established a virtuous king to do justice for heaven. Only then could the country be stable and the world peaceful.
I heard that "Spring and Autumn" was written in the first month of the first year of the throne, praising unity and attaching importance to the beginning.
Your Majesty, you have just ascended the throne of the emperor, and it is in line with God's will. You should correct the mistakes of the previous dynasty, correct the imperial line you just accepted, eliminate the cumbersome regulations, relieve the suffering of the people, and ensure the survival of the people in accordance with God's will.
I heard that the Qin Dynasty had ten major faults. One of them still exists today, and that is the officials who tried the prison.
When Qin ruled, he despised literature and classics, liked force and bravery, despised the benevolent and righteous people, and respected the officials in prison; correct words and advice were regarded as slander, and accusations of faults were regarded as lies.
Therefore, people with high moral character are not reused, their loyal hearts and sincere words can only be hidden in their chests, and the sounds of flattery are endless; false praises confuse their minds, and the real disasters are turned a blind eye.
This is the reason why the Qin Dynasty lost the world.
Now, thanks to your great kindness, people in the world are no longer in danger of war or suffering from hunger or cold. Fathers, sons, and husbands work together to build their homes. However, peace in the world has not yet been truly achieved. This is because of the destruction of prisons.
Prison is the key to ordering chaos in the country. Dead people cannot come back to life, and limbs that have been severed cannot be rejoined by electricity.
The Book of Books says: Rather than killing an innocent person, it is better to be unconventional.
Nowadays, the officials who handle prison sentences are not like this. They drive each other up and down, regard harshness as innocence, and gain a reputation for fairness by committing serious crimes. However, those who enforce the law fairly have many consequences.
Therefore, the officials in charge of the trial wanted the people under trial to be executed, not because they hated these people, but because the way to protect themselves was to let these people die.
Therefore, the blood of those who were convicted and killed flows all over the city, and people who are punished for their crimes are everywhere. Tens of thousands of people are sentenced to great punishment every year. This is the reason why the benevolent and holy government is damaged.
A peaceful and prosperous age cannot be realized, and this is probably where the problem lies.
As far as human relationships are concerned, when you are at peace, you love life, and when you are in pain, you think of death.
Under severe torture, what kind of confession can be obtained?
Therefore, a person who was imprisoned and tried could not bear the pain of torture, so he fabricated a confession, admitted his guilt, and gave the confession to the official who was interrogating him. The official who was interrogating him found it convenient, so he pointed out and guided him to make him understand his crime. When he reported it, he was afraid that it would be returned, so he repeatedly revised the memorial to make it flawless.
The crime stipulated in the memorial has been completed. Even if the lawsuit is dismissed, the convicted person will still be considered to have deserved his death. Why?
Because the memorial has been revised many times, the charges listed in the legal provisions are clear and correct.
Therefore, the prison officials invoke the law and fall into sin. They are harsh and cruel without limits, muddle along, act expediently, and do not consider the disaster they will bring to the country. This is the biggest disaster today.
Therefore, as the saying goes: if the painted ground is used as a prison, no one will dare to go to court to discuss politics; if the carved wood is used as an official, no one will dare to take measures.
These are all cries of grief and indignation made by hating officials who enforce the law harshly.
Therefore, there is no greater disaster in the world than prison. There is no one more powerful than an official who breaks the law, violates the right rules, separates relatives, and blocks the holy path.
This is one of the ten major faults of the Qin Dynasty that exists to this day.
I heard that where the eggs of crows and owls are not harmed, the phoenix will fall; the crime of slandering the monarch will not be punished, and only then will someone give honest advice.
Therefore, someone in ancient times said: The mountains have vegetation and poisonous things live in them; the rivers and lakes are vast and can accommodate muddy water; and the beautiful jade contains slight flaws. A ruler who is good at controlling his ministers should also tolerate the shame of being criticized.
As long as you exempt those who slander the monarch from the blame and accept straightforward advice, open up the channels of speech, eliminate the mistakes that led to the fall of Qin, follow the virtuous policies of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, reduce legal provisions, relax penalties, and abolish the prison of torture, then the age of peace and prosperity will come, with eternal peace and happiness, coexisting with heaven and earth, and everyone in the world will feel infinite joy.
Emperor Xuan appreciated Lu Wenshu's petition and promoted him to the position of head of Guangyang's private palace.
The internal history recommended Lu Wenshu as the first-class scholar in literature, and he was promoted to You Fufeng Cheng.
At that time, the emperor issued a Shao letter instructing the ministers to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to the Huns. Lu Wenshu submitted a letter, requesting that he be sent as an entourage to accompany the envoys on missions to the Huns in order to serve the emperor. The emperor reviewed the letter and forwarded it to General Fan Mingyou and his servant Du Yannian to inquire about the situation. Because his words were unreasonable, he returned to the Forbidden City.
A long time later, he was promoted to the prefect of Linhuai County. His political performance was very outstanding, and he died in office.
Lu Wenshu, who had learned almanac and astronomy from his grandfather, believed that the Han Dynasty would encounter a great disaster around 210 years after the founding of the People's Republic of China, so he secretly wrote to the emperor to take precautions.
When he became emperor, Gu Yong also said the same thing.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne and announced to the world the basis of Dai Mo, he publicized these words.
Lu Wenshu's sons and grandsons all became high-ranking officials such as state pastor and prefect.
Praise says: In the Spring and Autumn Period, Zang Sunda of the Lu State admonished the monarch with etiquette and righteousness. People with high moral character believed that his descendants would be prosperous.
Maishan pointed out the emperor's faults from below, and Zou Yang and Mei Cheng traveled to kingdoms that were in danger of collapse, but they were able to avoid being tortured and killed because they strictly adhered to the right way of speaking.
Lu Wenshu speaks softly and is sincere, so his descendants will serve as high-ranking officials for generations to come. It’s only fitting!
summary:
Jia Shan, from Yingchuan, studied under his grandfather Jia Qu and was known for his broad knowledge across various schools of thought, though he did not specialize in Confucianism. He served as a riding attendant under Marquis Yingyin. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Jia Shan used the Qin Dynasty as a cautionary example to discuss governance, titling his work "Zhi Yan." He criticized Qin's tyranny, excessive construction of palaces like Epang, extravagant roads, and the lavish Lishan Mausoleum, which drained resources and oppressed the people, leading to widespread rebellion. He emphasized the importance of loyal ministers and open communication, warning that rulers who suppress criticism and act tyrannically risk losing their realm. Jia Shan urged the emperor to adopt benevolent policies, listen to advice, and avoid Qin's mistakes.

Jia Shan also highlighted the Qin Dynasty's failure to maintain stability despite its vast power, contrasting it with the Zhou Dynasty's more moderate rule. He noted that Qin's harsh laws and exploitation led to its downfall, while wise rulers like King Wen of Zhou attracted talented ministers through benevolence. He advised the emperor to cultivate virtue, reduce punishments, and encourage honest counsel. Later, Jia Shan opposed Emperor Wen's decision to allow private coinage, arguing it would undermine imperial authority. Despite his urgent remonstrations, Emperor Wen did not punish him, aiming to keep open the path for advice.

Zou Yang, a native of Qi, served under King Wu Liu Bi of Wu. When the king harbored rebellious intentions after his son's death, Zou Yang wrote a letter advising against rebellion, using Qin's fall as a warning. He argued that unity and loyalty to the Han court were essential, warning that rebellion would lead to destruction. When King Wu ignored him, Zou Yang joined King Xiao of Liang. However, he was slandered and imprisoned. From prison, he wrote to King Liang, citing historical examples of loyal ministers who were misunderstood, such as Jing Ke and Bian He, and urged the king to trust his sincerity. King Liang eventually released him and made him a guest.

Mei Cheng, from Huaiyin, also served King Wu and advised him against rebellion, warning that the Han Dynasty's strength far exceeded Wu's. He used metaphors like a thread holding a heavy weight to illustrate the danger of rebellion. When King Wu persisted, Mei Cheng left for Liang. After Emperor Jing ascended, Chao Cuo's policies provoked the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion. Mei Cheng again advised King Wu to withdraw, but the king refused and was eventually killed. Mei Cheng later served King Xiao of Liang and became famous for his writings. Emperor Wu later summoned him, but he died en route.

Lu Wenshu, from Julu, studied law and the Spring and Autumn Annals. During Emperor Xuan's reign, he wrote a memorial advocating benevolence and lighter punishments, criticizing the harsh legal system inherited from Qin. He argued that severe torture led to false confessions and injustice, undermining peace. He urged the emperor to follow the virtuous policies of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, reduce penalties, and open channels for advice. Emperor Xuan appreciated his petition and promoted him. Lu Wenshu later served as prefect of Linhuai, where he performed excellently until his death. His descendants became high-ranking officials.

translation:
Zhao Chongguo, named Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi. He later moved to Jincheng Lingju.
He was just a knight at the beginning, but later he was a member of a good family in six counties and was good at horseback riding and archery and was promoted to a guard of the feather forest.
He was calm and courageous, with profound strategies. When he was young, he liked the integrity of a general, so he went to study the art of war and became familiar with the affairs of the barbarians in all directions.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Chongguo followed the Second Division General as a fake Sima to attack the Xiongnu, and was heavily surrounded by the enemy.
The Han army was without food for several days and suffered many casualties. Zhao Chongguo and more than 100 strong men broke through the siege and captured the enemy's formation. The general of the Second Division led the soldiers to follow him, and they were able to escape the siege.
Zhao Chongguo suffered more than 20 injuries all over his body. General Ershi reported the situation to Emperor Wu, who ordered Zhao Chongguo to be summoned to the place where he was traveling. Emperor Wu personally received Zhao Chongguo and visited his injuries. He praised him, awarded him the title of Zhonglang, and promoted him to the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, the Di people in Wudu County rebelled. Zhao Chongguo led troops to attack and quelled the rebellion as a general to protect the army. He was promoted to Zhonglang General and led his troops to garrison in Shanggu County. After returning, he was appointed as the captain of Shuiheng.
Later, he went to attack the Xiongnu and captured King Xiqi. He was promoted to the post-general, and he still served as the captain of Shuiheng.
Zhao Chongguo and General Huo Guang decided to support Emperor Xuan and were named Yingpinghou.
During the Benshi period, he used the post of General Pulei to conquer the Xiongnu and killed hundreds of enemies. After returning the army, he was appointed as the Hou General and Shaofu.
The Xiongnu mobilized more than 100,000 cavalry and went south to approach the Han Dynasty border fortress. They reached Mount Fuxi and prepared to invade and plunder.
Tichu Qutang, who had escaped from the Xiongnu, surrendered to the Han Dynasty and told the story. The Han Dynasty sent Zhao Chongguo to lead 40,000 cavalry to garrison the nine counties on the border.
After Shanyu heard what had happened, he led his troops and left.
At this time, Guanglu doctor Yiqu Anguo was on an envoy to inspect various Qiang tribes. The chief Xianling expressed his hope to cross the river to the north bank of the Huangshui River at a certain time to find places where Han people did not cultivate their livestock.
Anguo reported the dispatch to the emperor.
Zhao Chongguo impeached Anguo for the crime of disrespect after being ordered to send an envoy.
After that, the Qiang people violated Han law and crossed the Huangshui River as mentioned above, but the counties and counties could not stop them.
In the third year of Yuankang, Xianling resolved his grudges with more than 200 Qiang chiefs, exchanged hostages and signed an oath of alliance.
After the emperor learned about this, he consulted Zhao Chongguo. Zhao Chongguo replied: The reason why the Qiang tribe was easily suppressed is because each tribe has its own leader. They often attack each other and their forces cannot be unified.
More than 30 years ago, when the Xiqiang people created the Han Dynasty, they resolved their enmities in advance and made an alliance to attack Lingju and compete with the Han Dynasty. It took five or six years to calm down.
In the fifth year of Zhenghe, Xianling leader Feng Jian and others sent envoys to the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu sent envoys to Xiaoyueshi. Rumors told the tribes that: General Ershi of the Han Dynasty led more than 100,000 people to surrender to the Xiongnu.
The Qiang people had a hard time serving the Han Dynasty.
Digging? The land was originally our place, the land was fertile, and we could attack and occupy it together. From this, we can see that Bao Xi wanted to unite with the police for a long time.
Not long ago, the west side of Lisu was trapped. Hearing that Wudan was coming to defend the frontier, and fearing that the war would start from the east, he sent envoys to Weili and Weisu countries many times, promising to give them men and women and mink clothes, in an attempt to alienate the friendly relationship between them and Lian.
This plan did not materialize.
I suspect that Baosu sent envoys to the sent tribes to transport salt via the Shayin area. After passing the title, they entered Yongmu and went south to the Dangsu vassal state to join forces with Sailing.
I am afraid that the changes among the Qiang people are not limited to these, and that they will collude with other tribes. We should make preparations before this happens.
More than a month later, the shy retreat sent envoys to the Xiongnu to borrow troops, preparing to attack Chachencha and Dunhuang to cut off the channels of communication between Xuan and Youji.
Langtongli believes that the Langdan and Shaojiedan tribes are in the southwest of Tunhui, so it is impossible to make such a plan alone. I suspect that the envoys of Xiongqu have already arrived among the Qiang tribes, and they first broke off the enmity and entered into an alliance with Ling, Han, and Ji.
When the horses are fat in autumn, trouble will inevitably occur.
Envoys should be sent to patrol the border and prepare in advance, and give orders to tell the tribes not to let them resolve their grudges, so as to find out their plot.
So the two governments asked for instructions to send envoys from Yiqu Anguo to inspect the tribes and distinguish the good from the bad.
After An Guo went to Nabao, he summoned more than thirty leaders of the previous tribes. Since they were all particularly ferocious and cunning, he killed them all.
They also sent troops to attack their tribe and killed more than a thousand people.
So all the Qiang tribes who originally submitted to the Han Dynasty, as well as the Guiyi Qiang Marquis Yang Yu and others, were afraid and angry. They lost trust and returned to the Han Dynasty. They coerced and kidnapped the weak tribes, betrayed and invaded the border fortresses, attacked the cities, and killed the officials.
As the cavalry captain, Anguo led three thousand cavalry to assemble to defend against the Qiang people. When they arrived at Haodian, they were attacked by enemy soldiers and lost many vehicles, baggage and weapons.
An Guo led his troops back and reported the situation after arriving at Ling's residence.
This year is the spring of the first year of Shenjue.
Zhao Chongguo was already over seventy years old at that time. The emperor thought he was old, so he sent Bingji, the imperial censor, to ask who could lead the army. Zhao Chongguo replied: There is no one more than the veteran.
The emperor sent someone to ask again: "General, what do you think will happen to the Qiang enemy? How many people should be used?"
Zhao Chongguo said: Seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times.
The military situation is difficult to predict remotely. I hope to rush to Jincheng and formulate a battle plan before submitting it.
However, the Qiang Rong are just a weak Yi tribe. They have betrayed the country against God's will and will soon perish. I hope your Majesty will leave this matter to the old ministers and don't worry.
The emperor smiled and said: "Okay."
Zhao Chongguo arrived at Jincheng and waited until the army gathered 10,000 cavalry to prepare to cross the Yellow River. However, he was afraid of being intercepted by the enemy, so he sent three schools of troops to cross the river at night.
Dozens and hundreds of enemy cavalry came and entered and exited the edge of the military camp.
Zhao Chongguo said: "Our troops and horses are tired and cannot gallop to chase."
This is difficult for the enemy's brave cavalry to subdue, and I'm afraid this is a tactic used by the enemy to lure troops.
Attack the enemy with the goal of total annihilation. The small benefits are not worth coveting.
Zhao Chongguo sent an order to the army not to attack.
The cavalry was sent to conduct reconnaissance in the surrounding areas, but no enemy was found.
He led his troops upriver to Luodu at night, then summoned the Sima from each school and said to them: I already know that the Qiang people don't know how to use troops.
If the enemy sends thousands of people to stand in the middle of nowhere, how can our troops get in?
Zhao Chongguo often made it a priority to send scouts far away. He must be prepared for battle when marching and strengthen the forts when stationed. He must be cautious and prudent, love his soldiers, and plan in advance before fighting.
So Zhao Chongguo went west to the Western Commandant's Mansion, and rewarded the sergeants every day, and the soldiers wanted to serve him.
The enemy came to challenge him several times, but Zhao Chongguo could not hold on.
Once a prisoner was captured, and he confessed that the Qiang leaders blamed each other several times and said: "I told you not to do it. Today the emperor sent General Zhao. He is eighty or ninety years old and is good at using troops."
Is it still possible to fight to the death now?
Zhao Chongguo's son Youcao Zhonglang, general Zhao Yin, led Qimen Yinfei, Yulin Orphan, Hu and Yue cavalry as branch troops to Lingju. The enemy attacked at the same time and cut off the Han army's transportation routes. Zhao Yin reported the matter.
Xia Shao ordered him to lead the Eighth School Lieutenant, Xiaoqi Captain, and Jincheng Prefect to work together to hunt down the enemies in the mountains and clear the transportation roads and Jinliang Ferry.
At first, Midang'er, the leader of Han and Kai, sent his younger brother Diaoku to tell the captain that Xianling wanted to build it. After a few days, Xianling actually built it.
There were many people from the Diaoku tribe in Xianling, so the captain detained Diaoku as hostages.
Zhao Chongguo believed that he was not guilty, so he sent him back to tell the tribal leaders: The Han Dynasty army only killed guilty people. They should understand and distinguish among themselves and not destroy themselves together.
The emperor told the Qiang people of all tribes that those who broke the law could be captured and killed and other criminals could be exempted.
Anyone who kills a guilty leader can get a reward of 400,000 yuan; whoever kills a mid-level leader can get 150,000 yuan; whoever kills a low-level leader can get 20,000 yuan; whoever kills an adult man can get 3,000 yuan; whoever kills women, old people and children can get a reward of 1,000 yuan, and all the women, children and money and items he captured must be given to him.
Zhao Chongguo planned to use a combination of kindness and power to recruit Han, Kai tribe and other tribes that were coerced into rebellion, disrupt the enemy's conspiracy, and wait until they were in trouble before attacking again.
At this time, Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty had already recruited prisoners with reduced sentences from Sanfu and Taichang Temple, officials from Sanhe, Qingchuan, Peijun, Huaiyang, and Runan counties, knights and Qiang cavalry from Jincheng, Longxi, Tianshui, Anding, Beidi, and Shangjun, as well as troops stationed in the counties of Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan prefects, a total of 60,000 people.
Xin Wuxian, the prefect of Jiuquan, wrote a memorial saying: The troops of each county are stationed in the south of Qilian Mountain, and the north is empty. This situation will not last long.
Some people say that we will not send troops until autumn and winter. This is the strategy we adopt when the enemy is outside the country.
Now the enemy is harassing them day and night, and the land is cold and barren. The horses of the Han Dynasty cannot spend the winter in Zaobao. There are more than 10,000 horses stationed in Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan, and most of them are emaciated.
You can increase the horse's feed and carry thirty days of food and grass in early July. At the same time, send troops from Zhangye and Jiuquan to attack the troops of the Han and Kai tribes in the upper reaches of Xianshui.
The enemy regards livestock as their lifeblood and is now dispersed. Our army quickly divides its troops to attack. Even if we cannot kill them all, as long as we seize their livestock, capture their wives and children, retreat and return, and attack again in winter, the enemy will definitely collapse if large forces launch frequent attacks.
The emperor handed this memorial to Zhao Chongguo and asked him to discuss it extensively with the officers and soldiers below the captain who knew the situation of the Qiang people.
Zhao Chongguo and Chang Shi Dong Tongnian believed that Xin Wuxian wanted to lead 10,000 cavalry in two directions from Zhangye, which was a thousand miles away.
Assuming that a horse can carry food for thirty days, it needs to carry two bushels of rice, four bushels of rice, eight bushels of wheat, as well as luggage and weapons. It will be difficult for the horse to chase and run.
By the time they arrived with great difficulty and exhaustion, the enemy must have planned the army's itinerary, gradually retreated, and entered the mountains and forests along the water and grassland.
If we follow the enemy and go deeper, they will occupy the dangerous obstacles in front, guard the fortress behind, and cut off our food routes. This will definitely lead to the danger of casualties, which will be ridiculed by the Yi and Di, and will never be undone.
However, Xin Wuxian believed that he could seize the enemy's livestock and capture their wives and children. This was just an empty talk and not the best strategy.
Wuwei County and Zhangye Rile are both located in northern fortresses, with unobstructed valleys and abundant water and grass.
I am afraid that the Xiongnu and Qiang people have already planned a large-scale invasion. I hope to cut off the roads from Zhangye and Jiuquan to the Western Regions, so that the troops from the two counties will not be able to dispatch.
Xianzerg was the first to rebel, and the other tribes were simply hijacked by it.
Therefore, I have a stupid plan. I plan to ignore the mistakes of the Qiang people and hide them instead of publicizing them. First, I will eliminate them first and then shock them. I should make them repent and pardon their crimes. Then I will select outstanding officials who understand the customs of the Qiang people to appease and unite them. This is the best way to ensure the army's victory.
The emperor handed this memorial to all officials for discussion.
The ministers all believed that Xianling had strong troops and relied on the assistance of Han and Kai. If Han and Kai were not defeated first, Xianling would not be easy to deal with.
The emperor appointed Xu Yanshou, the successful lord of the imperial court, as the general of strong crossbows, and appointed Xin Wuxian, the prefect of Jiuquan, as the general of Po Qiang. He gave him a seal of Shao Shu to commend him for adopting his strategy.
He also wrote a letter blaming Zhao Chongguo, saying:
The emperor sent greetings to the general, who was marching very hard outside.
The general planned to attack Hanqiang in the first month. The Qiang people would have harvested their wheat, moved their wives and children, and assembled an elite force of 10,000 people to invade Jiuquan and Dunhuang.
We have few troops on the border, so farming cannot be carried out unless the people guard and protect it.
Nowadays, a stone of millet in Yishu area of ​​Zhangye costs more than one hundred yuan, and a bundle of hay and straw sells for dozens of yuan.
Transporting grain and grass from place to place added to the trouble for the people.
The general led a large force of more than 10,000 people, and did not take advantage of the convenience of sharing water and grass in autumn to fight for their livestock and food. If the enemy had already accumulated food by winter, most of them relied on dangers to hide in the mountains, and the general's soldiers had their hands and feet cracked by the cold. Wouldn't it still be advantageous?
The general does not care about the expense of the country and plans to defeat the enemy in a few years. Who is a general who would not be happy with this!
现在我已诏令破羌将军辛武贤带兵六千一百人，敦煌太守快带兵二千人，长水校尉富吕、酒泉候冯奉世率领蜡、月氏兵四千人，大概不下一万二千人。

Bring thirty days of food and grass, attack Hanqiang on July 22, enter the bend of the north bank of Xianshui, 800 miles away from Jiuquan and 1,200 miles away from the general.
The general will lead his troops to advance westward from the access road at the same time. Even if they cannot meet up, letting the enemy know that the armies from the east and north are coming together will distract the enemy's fighting spirit and separate their party members. Even if they cannot completely annihilate the enemy, it should still disintegrate them.
I have ordered Zhonglang General Zhao Yin to lead Hu, Yueyin Fei Archers and the Second Infantry School to increase the general's strength.
Now the five stars appear in the east, which will be of great benefit to China, and the barbarians will be defeated.
The Taibai Star appears in a high place, and those who lead troops deep into the field and dare to fight will be lucky, while those who dare not fight will be in danger.
General, hurry up and pack your bags, rely on the weather and attack the injustice, and you will be sure to be foolproof. General, don't have any more doubts.
After Zhao Chongguo received the edict blaming him, he believed that the generals leading troops outside should insist on their opinions according to the situation to stabilize the country.

After that, Xin Qingji was promoted to the right general, and the officials were sent to Shizhong. More than a year later, he was transferred to the left general.
Xin Qingji usually behaved respectfully and modestly, and was particularly frugal in food and clothing, but he was fond of carriages and horses, and his signs were very eye-catching. This was the only luxury.
As a brave minister of the country, when the world was at peace, the Xiongnu and the Western Regions closely attached themselves to him and respected his prestige.
The eldest son Xin Tong was dismissed from office due to old age, and his eldest son Xin Tong was appointed as the captain of the Huqiang School. His second son Xin Zun was appointed as the captain of Hangu Pass.
There are more than ten relatives from the side branches of the clan who are worth two thousand shi.
During the Yuanshi period, Prince Mang of Anhan controlled the government. Seeing that Xin Qingji was accomplished by General Wang Feng and that his three sons were very capable, he wanted to be close to him and treat him favorably.
At this time, Wang Mang had just established his authority and appointed Zhen Feng and Zhen Han to help him. Zhen Feng and Zhen Han were newly prominent and their power shocked the court.
Xin Mao, the captain of Shuiheng, thought that he was the descendant of a famous official. Since his brothers were both in high positions, it would not be difficult for him to serve his two wives.
Emperor Ping was young at that time, and his maternal grandfather's Wei family could not live in the capital. Brother Xinci, the eldest son of Xintong, the captain of the Qiang Guard, was usually very close to Emperor Ping's cousin Wei Zibo. Both of them had a knight-errant demeanor and had many guests.
When Lu Kuan's incident happened, Wang Mang killed the Wei family.
The two princes falsely accused the Xin brothers of secretly colluding with Wei Zibo and plotting to betray their kindness and dissatisfy Duke Anhan.
So Si Zhi, Chen Chong, reported that the Xin clan, Longxi Xinxing and others, violated and bullied the common people and were domineering in the prefectures and counties.
Wang Mang examined Xin Tong and his son, Xin Zun, Xin Mao brothers, and Xin Bo, the governor of Nanjun, and killed them all.
As a result, the Xin family declined.
Xin Qingji was originally from Didao County. After becoming a general, he moved to Changling.
After Changling was revoked, he stayed in Chang'an.
Zan said: Since the Qin and Han Dynasties, prime ministers have always appeared from Yishu on Mount Tai, and generals have often appeared from the west of Mount Tai.
General Bai Qi of the Qin Dynasty was from the county; Wang Jian was from Pinyang.
Since the founding of the Han Dynasty, Wang Wei and Gan Yanshou of Yuzhi, Gongsun He and Fu Jiezi of Yiqu, Li Guang and Li Cai of Chengji, Su Jian and Su Wu of Duling, Shangguan Jie and Zhao Chongguo of Shangbang, Lian Bao of Xiangwu, Xin Wuxian and Xin Qingji of Didao are all famous for their bravery and might.
Su and Xin father and son are both known for their integrity. This is something they can praise, and the rest are countless.
why is that?
Tianshui, Longxi, Anding, Beidi and other places to the west of Mount Tai are very close to the Qiang and Hu people. The folk customs teach armed war preparation and advocate bravery, horseback riding and archery.
Therefore, there is a "Qin Poetry" that says: If the king wants to fight, he will prepare his armor and weapons and go out with you.
It can be seen that their customs have been like this since ancient times. Today's songs sound impassioned, but the old style of singing is still there.
summary:
Zhao Chongguo, styled Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi and later moved to Jincheng Lingju. He began as a knight, was promoted to a guard of the feather forest for his skill in horseback riding and archery, and was known for his calm courage and strategic depth. He studied military strategy and became familiar with barbarian affairs. Under Emperor Wu, he served as a fake Sima under the Second Division General against the Xiongnu, breaking through an enemy siege with over 100 strong men despite heavy casualties and over 20 wounds. Emperor Wu personally honored him, appointing him Zhonglang and later General of Chariots and Cavalry. Under Emperor Zhao, he quelled a Di rebellion in Wudu, was promoted to Zhonglang General, and later captured Xiongnu King Xiqi, becoming a post-general. He supported Emperor Xuan’s ascension with Huo Guang and was named Yingpinghou. During the Benshi period, he led a campaign against the Xiongnu, killing hundreds, and was appointed Hou General and Shaofu.

When the Xiongnu mobilized over 100,000 cavalry near the border, Zhao Chongguo led 40,000 cavalry to garrison nine counties, causing the Shanyu to retreat. He later impeached Yiqu Anguo for disrespect after Anguo mishandled Qiang affairs. In the third year of Yuankang, Qiang chief Xianling formed alliances, and Zhao Chongguo warned of potential rebellion, citing past Qiang uprisings and Xiongnu collusion. He advised preparations, but Anguo’s subsequent actions—killing over 30 Qiang leaders and attacking their tribes—provoked a widespread Qiang revolt. Zhao Chongguo, over 70, was tasked with leading the campaign. He insisted on personal command, saying “seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times,” and Emperor Xuan agreed.

At Jincheng, Zhao Chongguo crossed the Yellow River cautiously, avoiding enemy traps. He prioritized reconnaissance, fortifications, and soldier welfare, refusing to engage in small skirmishes. His son Zhao Yin led reinforcements, but Zhao Chongguo advocated a strategy of kindness and power, recruiting Qiang tribes like Han and Kai to disrupt enemy plans. Emperor Xuan assembled 60,000 troops, but Zhao Chongguo opposed a proposed attack by Xin Wuxian, arguing it risked logistical failure and enemy ambush. He recommended a defensive approach, focusing on farming and waiting for the enemy to weaken. Despite imperial pressure, Zhao Chongguo submitted a memorial detailing a plan to withdraw cavalry and station 10,281 soldiers for farming, listing twelve benefits including cost savings, enemy attrition, and border security. Emperor Xuan eventually approved his strategy.

Zhao Chongguo’s campaign succeeded: over 10,000 Qiang surrendered, and by the following year, only about 4,000 enemies remained. He was praised for his foresight, though his son Zhao Yin committed suicide after a dispute. Zhao Chongguo retired with honors and died at 86. His portrait was placed in Weiyang Palace, and a eulogy by Yang Xiong celebrated his achievements. The text also covers Xin Wuxian and his son Xin Qingji, noting their military roles and eventual decline under Wang Mang. The commentary reflects on the martial traditions of western regions like Tianshui and Longxi, attributing the prevalence of generals there to proximity to Qiang and Hu peoples.
