Zhao Guang, whose Chinese name is Zidu, was a native of Liwu County, Zhuo County. Liwu County was originally part of the Hejian Kingdom.
When he was young, he worked as a county official and a state official. He was famous for his integrity, savvy, courtesy and corporal.
He was elected as Maocai and made a leveling order to manage market prices.
After assessment, he was appointed as the Yangdi Order.
Because his performance in managing government affairs was particularly outstanding, he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant of Jingfu, acting as Jing Zhaoyin.
When Emperor Zhao died, Xinfeng Du Jian was appointed as Jingzhao and was responsible for the construction of Emperor Zhao's tomb.
Du Jian has always been a hero, and his guests made illegal profits from it. When Guanghan heard about this, he tactfully warned him in advance.
Du Jian refused to change, so the case was closed and punished.
Many powerful people and eunuchs interceded on his behalf, but Guanghan finally did not listen.
The clan and guests planned to kidnap Du Jian. Guanghan learned all of their plans and the name and residence of the mastermind. He sent officials to tell them: If they plot like this, the whole family will be destroyed.
He ordered all the officials to execute Du Jian in the busy city, but no one dared to approach him.
Everyone in the capital praised him.
At that time, Liu He, the king of Changyi, was summoned to Beijing to ascend the throne. He behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang and his officials deposed the king of Changyi and established Emperor Xuan.
Guanghan was given the title of Marquis of Guannei because he participated in the discussion and formulation of strategies.
Guanghan moved to Yingchuan as governor.
The Yuan and Chu tribes in the county were rampant and their guests broke the law and became thieves. None of the former officials of two thousand stone could capture and subdue them.
A few months after Guanghan arrived, he killed the evildoers led by Yuan and Chu. The people in the county were shocked and frightened.
In the end, Yingchuan heroes entered into marriages with each other, and the government and the people formed a party.
Guanghan was very worried about this matter, so he rewarded those who could use it and let them know the contents of the indictment in advance. When there was a case to be interrogated, and the charges had been obtained, he would punish them according to the law. Guanghan deliberately leaked their words to make them blame each other.
He also asked the officials to make a snitch bucket. When he received the letter, he cut off the name of the snitch and pretended to be a son of a hero.
From then on, powerful families became enemies, traitors were dispersed and defeated, and customs changed greatly.
Officials and common people came to complain and expose, and Guanghan could use them as eyes and ears. Therefore, thieves could not commit crimes, and they would be caught if they committed crimes.
Everything was managed, and Guanghan's reputation spread so widely that the surrendered Huns said that all the Huns had heard of Guanghan.
In the second year of this year, the imperial court sent five generals to attack the Xiongnu, and requisitioned Guanghan to lead the army as a prefect, subordinate to Pulei general Zhao Chongguo.
After returning from the army, he still acted as Jing Zhaoyin, and was actually awarded Jing Zhaoyin a year later.
As a Yin of the capital, Zhao Guanghan accepted scholars and looked good. He treated his subordinates with comfort and recommendation, and was diligent and diligent.
When he succeeded, he declined the credit and attributed it to his subordinates, saying: "It was a certain officer who did it, and it is not what I can do with two thousand stones."
Actions originate from a sincere heart.
The officials who met him all confided their secrets without hiding anything. They were all willing to be used by him and would not escape even if they died.
Guanghan clearly knows what their abilities are suitable for and whether they can try their best. If anyone among them betrays him, let him know first. If he refuses to change after being advised, he will be arrested. If he cannot escape, he will be charged according to his crime and immediately punished.
Guanghan is a shrewd and capable man, and is naturally proficient in the ways of being an official.
You can stay up all night to meet with officials and people.
He is especially good at the art of hook distance, and can use this to find out the whole story.
The method of hook distance is, if you want to know the price of a horse, first ask the price of the dog, then the price of the sheep, then the price of the cow, and then the price of the horse. Compare these prices with each other, and measure them by category, and you will be able to know whether the horse is worthy or not.
Only Guanghan is the most proficient in the art of hook distance, and no one can catch up after others imitate it.
He knows the thieves in the county, the light knights in the house, their foundations and caves, as well as the subordinate officials who abuse the law and collect property, and he knows the most trivial treachery.
Several teenagers from Chang'an were planning to kidnap someone together in a secluded house in Lizhong. Before they could finish their words, Guanghan sent officials to arrest and punish them all and bring them to justice.
The rich man Su Hui was appointed as a man, and two people kidnapped him.
After a while, Guanghan arrived at their home with his subordinates. Guanghan stood in the court and asked Chang'an Prime Minister Gong She to knock on the door and tell the robbers, "Jingzhao Yin Zhaojun thanks you two, please don't kill the hostages. This man is the emperor's bodyguard."
If the hostages are released and do not resist, you will be treated well, and you may be lucky enough to receive a pardon order, or you may be exempted from the crime at that time.
The two men were shocked. They had heard of Guang Han's reputation again. They immediately opened the door and went down to the hall to kowtow. Guang Han knelt down and thanked him, saying: "I'm glad to have saved Lang Guan's life. You are very kind to others!"
Send the two to prison. Tell the jailer to treat each other with courtesy and provide him with food and wine.
In winter, when the two of them should be released from prison and sentenced to death, Guanghan prepared coffins for them in advance, provided them with burial utensils, and told them. Both of them said: There will be no resentment in death like this!
Zhao Guanghan once sent a message to summon the chief of the capital pavilion of Hu County. The chief of the capital pavilion went west to Jie Shang. The chief of the Jieshang pavilion joked: When you get to the county government, please ask Mr. Zhao for me.
When the pavilion chief arrived at the county government, Guang Han talked with him. After asking about official business, he said to him: "The chief of the pavilion in Jieshang sent me a message. Why don't you convey his greetings?"
The head of the pavilion kowtowed and was convinced that this was indeed the case.
Guang Han then said: Go back and ask the director of the pavilion for me to ask him to do his job well and do his best. Jing Zhao will not forget his loyalty.
He reveals private affairs like a god, and this is often the case.
Guanghan petitioned to increase the salary of the traveling wardens in Chang'an to a hundred shi. From then on, the subordinate officials who received a salary of a hundred shi were more self-respecting and did not dare to arrest people arbitrarily in violation of the law.
Jingzhao's politics were clear and clear, and officials and people were full of praise for him.
The elders rumored that no one who had managed Jingzhao since the rise of Bai Han could match him.
The official offices of Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng were both located in Chang'an, and criminals often traveled to the boundaries of Jingzhao to commit crimes.
Guang Han sighed and said: Those who disrupt my management are often Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng. If I can control the second assistant at the same time, it will be easier to govern Chang'an.
At the beginning, the general Huo Guang was in power, and Guanghan served Huo Guang.
After Huo Guang died, Guanghan knew the emperor's intentions and sent the Chang'an officials to lead him personally. They went with him to the residence of Huo Guang's son, Bolu Marquis Huo Yu. They broke into the palace gate, searched and arrested those who secretly slaughtered animals and sold wine, smashed Lu Yue with his spine, and cut off the door bolt with an axe.
Huo Guang's daughter was the queen at the time. When she heard about this incident, she cried to the emperor.
The emperor applauded this matter in his heart, so he only summoned Guanghan for questioning.
Guanghan offended his relatives and ministers.
Guang Hanping likes to appoint the young descendants of the old officials and blindly promote their strong and sharp spirit. When they see something happen, they can't avoid it. Most of them have the intention of making a decisive decision with him, and no one can support him in the crisis situation.
Guanghan eventually got into trouble because of this.
At first, a retainer from Guanghan was selling wine secretly in the Chang'an market, but the prime minister's officials drove him away. The retainer suspected that the man Su Xian had reported the matter, so he told Guang Han.
Guanghan sent Chang An Cheng to track down Su Xian, and Wei Shiyu therefore impeached Su Xian as a knight to station in Ba Shang, but he could not reach the station and lacked military supplies.
Su Xian's father filed a complaint against Guang Han, and the matter was dealt with again by the department. Yu was sentenced to death and asked to arrest Guanghan.
There was an edict to interrogate him on the spot, and Guanghanzhong surrendered. It happened that he was pardoned, and his salary was only reduced by one level.
Guanghan suspected that this incident was instigated by Rongwu, a man from Tongyi, and later killed Rongwu on other charges.
Someone wrote a letter to report this matter, and Emperor Xuan handed the case over to the prime minister and the imperial censor. The investigation was very urgent.
A Chang'an man who was closely trusted by the Guanghan faction served as a pawn in the prime minister's house and asked him to secretly inquire about illegal affairs in the prime minister's house.
In the middle of the seventh month of the third year of Dijie, the prime minister committed suicide by hanging himself with his maid.
Guanghan heard about this and suspected that the prime minister's wife had killed her in the mansion out of jealousy, while the prime minister was fasting to attend the ancestral temple for worship.
When Guanghan learned of the incident, he sent his lieutenant Zhao Fengshou to advise the prime minister, hoping to blackmail him and prevent him from pursuing his own affairs.
The Prime Minister refused to listen and the investigation became more urgent.
Guang Han wanted to report him, so he first asked Tai Shi, who knew the stars, and Tai Shi said that a minister would be killed this year, so Guang Han immediately wrote a letter to report the prime minister's crime.
The emperor ordered: Leave it to Jing Zhaoyin to handle.
Guanghan knew that the matter was urgent, so he led his troops to the prime minister's house, summoned the prime minister's wife to kneel in the court to listen to her speech, took away more than ten slaves, and interrogated them about killing the maid.
Prime Minister Wei Xiang wrote a letter stating: My wife did not kill her maid.
Guanghan committed many crimes and failed to acquit himself according to the law. He used deceptive means to coerce his minister Wei, but fortunately his minister Wei tolerated and did not complain.
I hope to send Qingming envoys to deal with the family affairs of the minister Wei Xiang confirmed by Guanghan.
The matter was handed over to the Tingwei. It was indeed the prime minister who whipped and expelled the maid because of his fault. The maid died after being driven out of the prime minister's house. This was not what Guang Han said.
Xiao Wang, the commander-in-chief, impeached him and said: "Guanghan insulted the ministers, wanted to threaten the prime minister, violated the law and harmed the morals. It was an unethical crime."
Emperor Xuan was disgusted with him and sent Guanghan to Tingwei Prison. He also killed innocent people, deliberately interrogated the case without knowing the truth, and arbitrarily rebuked the knights for their lack of armaments. The emperor approved his memorial.
Tens of thousands of officials and common people stood by the palace and wailed. Some said that the emperor's life was of no benefit to the imperial court, and were willing to die for Zhao Jingzhao so that he could live to support the people.
Guanghan was finally cut in half.
Although Guanghan was punished for breaking the law, he was an honest and upright person, restrained the powerful, and allowed the common people to take their own positions.
The people still miss him and praise him.
Yin Wenggui, named Zixiong, was originally from Pingyang, Hedong, and later moved to Duling.
Weng Gui lost his father when he was young and lived with Ji's father.
He works as a prison clerk and is familiar with the law.
He loves fencing and no one can resist him.
At this time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government. The Huo family lived in Pingyang. The slaves and guests of the family came to the market with swords and weapons to fight and cause chaos. The officials could not stop it. When Weng returned to work as a market official, no one dared to break the law and cause chaos.
He is fair and honest and does not accept gifts from concubines. Merchants are afraid of him.
Later he resigned and stayed at home.
It happened that Tian Yannian was the governor of Hedong and inspected various counties when he arrived in Pingyang. He summoned all the officials and soldiers in the past, fifty or sixty people.
After inspecting dozens of people, when it was Wenggui's turn, he fell to the ground alone and refused to get up. He replied: Wenggui is both civil and military, please arrange him.
The meritorious officer thought that this officer was arrogant and arrogant, so Yannian said: "What's the harm?"
So he called him forward to ask questions, and was surprised by his answers. He made him a soldier and followed him back to the county government.
Weng Gui inquired about the matter and exposed the adultery, and was able to tell the whole story. Yannian valued him very much and thought he was not as capable as Weng Gui, so he was transferred to acting postal supervisor.
There are twenty-eight counties in Heshu, which are divided into two parts. Hongru is in charge of the north of Fenshui, and Wenggui is in charge of the south of Fenshui.
Weng Gui acted in accordance with the law and arrested those who committed crimes. Even if the county magistrate secretly framed him, no one resented him.
After the assessment, he was appointed as the Lieutenant of the Feng family. He successively held various positions in the county. He managed the places he went to well. He was promoted to the imperial edict and became the Lieutenant of Hongnong.
He was appointed as the governor of Donghai and went to visit Yu Dingguo to bid farewell to the imperial officer.
Ding's country is in the East China Sea, and he wants to entrust the sons of two people from the same city to Weng Gui and let them sit in the back hall to wait for an audience.
Dingguo talked with Weng Gui for a whole day, but he did not dare to let the son of his fellow countryman come to see him.
After Weng Gui left, Dingguo said to Yizi: "He is a wise official. You don't know how to do things, and I can't ask for help based on personal relationships."
Weng Gui governs Shuhai and governs the Qingming Dynasty. We all know the virtuous and unvirtuous officials and people in the county, as well as their treacherous and evil crimes. Each county has its own registration book.
He personally handles the political affairs of each county. If there is an urgent order, he will delay it for a while; if the officials and people are slack, he will disclose the list of guilty persons.
Counties and counties arrested cunning officials and wealthy people, and after examination, they determined the charges, which could lead to the death penalty.
The arrests must be made during the official evaluation meetings in autumn and winter, and when going out to inspect various counties, not when there is nothing wrong.
He arrested people in order to convince the officials and the people to change their ways out of fear.
Xu Zhongsun of Tan County, a great gentry in Shuhai, was cunning and cunning, disrupting the administration of officials, and the county suffered from him.
The county guard wanted to arrest him, but he used his power to deceive and escape, and no one was able to subdue him.
After Weng Gui arrived, he sentenced Zhongsun to death and abandoned the market. The whole county was in trembling, and no one dared to violate the law.
Shuhai was therefore at peace.
Yin Weng was appointed to Youfufeng due to his excellent political performance, and was actually appointed to his post a year later.
He chose officials who were honest, just, and hated treachery as his assistants, treated them with courtesy, and had the same likes and dislikes as them; those who betrayed Weng Gui would also be punished.
The method of governance is the same as Shuhai's old method, and the crimes of treachery are also recorded in the county.
When a thief was discovered in the neighboring army, Weng Gui summoned the chief official of that county and told him clearly the name of the cunning chief culprit, and taught him to deduce the places where the thief had passed and where he had taken refuge. Most of them were as Weng Gui said, and no one escaped.
We will relax policies for the weak and step up the investigation of the powerful.
If a powerful person is found guilty, he will send it to the livestock officer and order him to cut the grass. The requirement is based on the number of people and days, which cannot be replaced.
Those who do not meet the quota will be punished by flogging, and in extreme cases, they will be killed by using a spear.
The capital was in awe of his majesty, and Fufeng became stable. Catching thieves was always the best among the three assistants.
Although Weng Gui attached great importance to law and punishment in his administration, he was known for his integrity, keeping his words to himself, being gentle and modest, and not looking down on others with his own talents. Therefore, he had a good reputation in the court.
He served for many years, and Yuan Kang died of illness four years ago.
There was no extra property in the family, so the emperor thought he was very wise, so he wrote to Shao Yushi: I work hard and sleep hard, taking the pursuit of talented people as the most important thing. I don't distinguish between relatives and friends, just to appease the people.
Fufeng Wenggui is honest, fair and upright, and it is unusual for him to govern the people. He was not able to complete his achievements because of his early misfortune. I pity him very much.
Give Weng Gui's son a hundred catties of gold to support the sacrifices in his family's temple.
Weng Gui's three sons all became county guards.
The youngest son Yin Cen successively served as Jiuqing and later general.
And Min Ru also reached the position of Guangling Prime Minister and had a reputation for being good at governance.
Therefore, the world praised Tian Yannian as a person who knew how to employ people.
Han Yanshou, named Xinggong, was originally from Handi, but later moved to Shizuo.
When he was young, he was a county literature scholar.
Father; Yu is Ci’s doctor.
Liu Dan, the assassin king of Yan, rebelled, and Han Zhan died for admonishing him. The whole people sympathized with him.
At this time, Emperor Zhao was already old, and General Huo Guang took control of the political power. He recruited virtuous writers from the county and asked them about political gains and losses.
At that time, Wei Chi responded as a writer, believing that the purpose of rewards and punishments is to encourage good and prohibit evil, which is the foundation of government.
In the past, King Yan behaved unethically, and Han Yi stood up to remonstrate with him, but was killed by King Yan.
Han Yi did not have the same kinship with King Yan as King Zhou did than Gan did, but he practiced the same moral integrity as King Yan. His son should be greatly rewarded, so as to show the world and clarify the principles of being a minister.
Huo Guang accepted his suggestion and promoted Yanshou to the position of admonishing doctor and to the post of Huaiyang prefect.
Yanshou was very famous in politics and was transferred to Yingchuan.
Yingchuan has many powerful people and is difficult to govern, so the state often selects powerful governors for it.
Before that, he went to Guanghan to serve as the governor. He was worried about the local custom of gathering friends and forming cliques, so he made friends with officials and people and asked them to report on each other. This expedient was to keep a close eye on political affairs. As a result, Yingchuan's reporting became common and the people often became enemies.
Yanshou wanted to change this trend and educate the people with courtesy, but he was worried that the people would not follow suit, so he summoned dozens of county elders who were trusted and respected by the villagers one after another. He held a banquet and personally accompanied them. He told them his idea of ​​implementing etiquette, asked them about the folk songs and the people's sufferings, and told them the way to eliminate hatred with harmony and love.
The elders all thought it was very beneficial and could be implemented, so they jointly agreed on the etiquette and levels of weddings and funerals, which were roughly based on ancient rituals and must not exceed legal limits.
Yanshou then ordered the officials and students of the liberal arts school to wear leather benches and hold ceremonial utensils such as beans in their hands to conduct funerals, weddings and other ceremonies for officials and people.
The people followed his teachings and abandoned the imitation civil and wooden carriages and horses used for funerals on the road.
A few years later, Yanshou was transferred to the post of prefect of Shujun. Huang Ba replaced Yanshou to govern Yingchuan. Huang Ba followed his method and thus Yingchuan was established!
Very stable. To extend life and serve as an official, he advocates etiquette and righteousness, and likes ancient teachings. He must hire local wise men wherever he goes, treat and appoint them according to etiquette, expand plans, and accept advice; he praises the behavior of giving up money in mourning, and commends filial piety and brotherhood; When repairing city walls and collecting taxes and rents, we must first make clear the date when the announcement will begin, and start taking action within the specified time limit. Officials and people will respect and abide by the regulations.
He also appointed the chief and the fifth chief as an example of filial piety and brotherhood, and did not tolerate treacherous people.
Once an accident occurs in Banli Qianbai, the officials will receive a report and the traitors will not dare to enter its territory.
This approach seemed very cumbersome at first, but later the officials did not have the trouble of chasing criminals, and the people did not have to worry about being punished, and they were all content with this kind of governance.
Yanshou treated his officials with great kindness and clear rules.
If someone cheats and betrays him, he will deeply blame himself: Did I betray him? Why did he do this?
When the officials heard this, they secretly regretted it. His county captain died of white thorns.
There was a robbery at the back door, but he was saved from death. As a result, he became mute and could not speak.
When Yanshou heard about this, he cried to Fu Shi and sent officials to treat him and take care of him.
He graciously exempted his family from taxes and corvee. Yanshou was about to go out. Before he got on the carriage, an official on horseback arrived late. Yanshou asked the meritorious officials to decide on a crime to punish him.
When Yanshou returned to the gate of the mansion, the doorman blocked the car and had something to say.
Yanshou stopped the car and asked him, and the servant said: "The Book of Filial Piety" says: Serve the emperor in the same way as the father, and the respect is the same. Therefore, serving the mother is based on love, and serving the monarch is based on respect. Serving the father with both respect and love is used.
You were going out early this morning, but you stopped for a long time before you could go out. The cavalryman's father came to the door and didn't dare to go in.
When the cavalry officer heard about it, he ran out to see his father and happened to catch up with you about to get on the car.
Wouldn't it be detrimental to Dahua to be punished for respecting his father?
Yanshou raised his hands in the car and said, "If it weren't for you, I wouldn't know my mistake."
Return to the house and summon the servants.
The doorman was originally a disciple. He heard that Yanshou was a wise man, but there was no way to recommend him, so he worked as a doorman for others. Yanshou retained him.
Yanshou listens to well-intentioned advice, mostly like this.
Yanshou stayed in Dongjun for three years. He enforced orders and banned them, and the number of prison cases was greatly reduced. He was the best in the world.
Han Yanshou tried to appoint Zuo Fengyi, and a year later he was deemed competent and was actually appointed to his post.
After more than a year, he refused to go out to inspect various counties.
The prime minister reported many times: You should travel around the county, observe the folk customs, and examine the political achievements of the officials.
Yanshou said: Each county has a wise official. It is enough for the postal supervisor to distinguish good from evil outside the office. I am afraid that there is no benefit to the provinces and counties, but only more troubles.
The prime minister thought that it was spring and he could go out to encourage farmers.

People all over the world say that the king is courageous and his attachment depends on wealth and honor. How can he be courageous?
That's how courageous I am.
The king's face changed slightly and he looked at Wang Zun, wanting to kill him in his heart. He immediately said to Wang Zun, Shanyan: I want to see your sword.
Wang Zun raised his arm, turned around and said to the servant nearby: "Come forward and show the king the sword. Does the king want to frame me for drawing the sword against the king?"
This is exactly what Wang intended. He also heard the name of Wang Zun, so he condescended to him and bought food and wine for him. He was very friendly to have a banquet with him.
The Empress Dowager's Report on the Campaign: The king's arrogance and arrogance as prime minister are inconsistent with the way of a minister. The king's temperament has not yet been determined and cannot be tolerated.
I'm really afraid that both mother and son will die from this.
Now I won't let the king see Wang Zun again.
If your majesty doesn't take it to heart, I will commit suicide first. I can't bear to see the king lose his morality.
Wang Zun was finally acquitted and became a commoner.
General Wang Feng wrote a letter requesting Wang Zunbu to be appointed Sima in the army and promoted to Sili Xiaowei.
At the beginning, Zhongshu Yezhe Ling Shi Xian was respected by the emperor and favored by the emperor. He specialized in power and did evil things.
Prime Minister Kuang Heng and imperial censor Zhang Tan both served Shi Xian respectfully and did not dare to say much.
After some time, Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng just ascended the throne. Shi Xian was transferred to the position of Zhong Tai servant and no longer held power.
Kuang Heng and Zhang Tancai reported Shi Xian's past evil deeds and requested that Shi Xian be demoted.
Wang Zun then impeached him and said: Prime Minister Kuang Heng and Yushi doctor Zhang Tan are the three public officials. They are in charge of the Wuchang and Nine Virtues. They have the responsibility of directing policies and strategies, unifying the program, broadcasting political and religious trends, and praising customs.
Knowing that Zhongshu Ye ordered Shi Xian and others to monopolize their power, exercise great power, act uncontrollably and fearlessly, they were a scourge in the sea. They did not ask for punishment at the time, but they followed the rules and conspired with evil intentions to confuse the country.
After the pardon was issued, Kuang Heng and Zhang Tan reported to Shi Xian. Instead of stating their charges of disloyalty, they instead promoted the late emperor's appointment of subversives and falsely claimed that the officials feared him more than the Lord.
Suppressing the monarch and exalting ministers is not worthy of praise, and it is beneath the dignity of a minister.
In the first month of the first lunar month, the emperor visited Qutai and came to express condolences to the guards. Kuang Heng, Zhong Erqianshi Dahong, Lu Shang and others sat under the palace gate. Kuang Heng sat facing south, and Shang and others sat facing west.
Kuang Heng arranged the seat for the reward again, stood up and asked the reward to take a seat, and had a private conversation for a meal?
Kuang Heng knew that the emperor was going to visit in person, all officials were doing their jobs, and everyone was gathering together, but he set up improper seats, made low-ranking people sit on the seats, and gave small favors to each other under the public gate. His behavior was not in line with etiquette and disturbed the ranking of the imperial title.
Kuang Heng also sent the palace servant into the palace to ask about the time of day of the procession. He reported that the team that had missed the fourteenth hour had arrived. Kuang Heng sat still, his face did not change, he had no fear and respect, and arrogance and disrespect were all crimes of disrespect.
The emperor's order does not need to be processed.
So Kuang Heng took off his official hat in shame and fear, begged to be punished, and handed over the seals and ribbons of the prime minister and the marquis.
Because the emperor had just ascended the throne, it was inconvenient to harm the ministers, so he ordered the censor to inquire about the truth.
The imperial censor Cheng impeached Wang Zun, arbitrarily slandering and slandering matters before the pardon, impeaching ministers many times, enforcing the law unfairly, dressing up minor offenses as major crimes, slandering the prime minister, insulting ministers, showing contempt for the country, and treating envoys disrespectfully.
There was an order to demote Wang Zun to the rank of Gaoling. After a few months, he was dismissed from office due to illness.
It happened that hundreds of bandits from the Nanshan group, including Zuizong, were endangering the officials and the people. The imperial court appointed Fu Gang, the former Hongnong prefect, as a lieutenant. He led a thousand people who could track them down to hunt them down, but they were unable to capture them for more than a year.
Someone persuaded the general Wang Feng: "There are hundreds of thieves at the emperor's feet. They launched an army to pursue them but they couldn't catch them. It was difficult to convince the barbarians."
Only the capable Jing Zhaoyin can be selected to handle it.
So Wang Feng recommended Wang Zun and recruited him as an admonishing doctor. He was appointed as the captain of Jingfu and was in charge of Jingzhao Yin's affairs.
The thieves were eliminated within a month.
Wang Zun was promoted to Guanglu doctor, and was appointed as Jingzhao Yin on trial basis. Later, he was promoted to official position and served for a total of three years.
He was convicted of being rude to the messenger.
Sili sent fake Zuo Fang to tell Wang Zun to send officials to arrest people according to the imperial edict. Fang said to Wang Zun: "Shao Shu wants to arrest people who should be kept secret."
Wang Zun said: The administration of affairs should be fair, and Jingzhao is good at leaking personnel information.
Fang said: If you want to arrest someone, you should send officers and soldiers now.
Wang Zun also said: There is no text about the capital in Shao Shu, so we should not send out officials.
Later, more than a thousand people were arrested in Chang'an in March.
When Wang Zun went out to inspect various counties, a man named Guo Ci complained to Wang Zun: More than ten people from Xu Zhong's family killed my brother Zhang and returned home openly.
The officials did not dare to arrest.
When Wang Zun came back from his inspection of the county, he wrote a memorial saying: The strong in each county will not bully the weak, each will get its own place, a tolerant policy will be implemented, and the atmosphere of peace can be seen everywhere.
The imperial censor reported to China and Korea that the king was tyrannical and unyielding, spoke nonsense outside, and arrogantly slandered his superiors. His prestige was increasingly low, and he was not suitable for the position of Jiuqing.
Wang Zun was dismissed from office because of this, and many officials and people praised him and felt sorry for him.
The third husband of Hu County Chengxing and others wrote a letter to defend Wang Zun, saying that his effectiveness in governing Beijing was increasingly obvious: In the past, bandits in Nanshan blocked the mountain roads and ran rampant, robbing kind people and killing officials who followed the law. The roads were blocked and warnings were posted on the city gates.
The infantry captain was ordered to hunt down the thief, which exposed the entire army, wasted time and money, and failed to capture the thief.
The second minister was convicted and demoted, the gang of thieves became more powerful, the morale of the officials was depleted, and rumors spread everywhere, becoming a worry for the country.
At this time, those who can catch and kill thieves will not hesitate to reward them with money and titles.
Kuanzhong, the Marquis of Guannei, sent someone to ask Wang Zun, the former Sili Xiaowei who had been recruited, about the strategy of capturing the bandits. He appointed him as the admonishing doctor, and he was appointed as the capital of Jingfu on trial to act as the agent for Jing Zhaoyin's affairs.
Wang Zun tried his best to be loyal and spend his energy, thinking about his duties at night, lowering his status to treat the scholars, motivating the officials who fled the battle, and boosting the depressed morale. Within two decades, the organization of the bandits was defeated, and the capital of Quebec surrendered.
The thieves were eliminated, the people returned to agriculture, the poor and weak were pacified, and the powerful were eradicated.
Chang'an Su's powerful and cunning Shushi Maiwan, Chengxi Wanzhang, scissors Zhang Jin, winemaker Zhao Fang, Duling Yangzhang and others all colluded with evil people to form gangs and secretly raised illegal and rebellious people. They offended the king's law at the top and disrupted the government's management at the bottom.
There were many officials in the past, but no one could catch or punish them in twenty years. Wang Zun tried and killed them according to the law, so that they were all punished.
The treacherous people were eliminated, and the officials and the people were happy and respected him.
Wang Zun's ability to rectify chaos and stop tyranny and evil was rare in the past and could not be matched by famous generals.
Although he was appointed as a formal official, no special praise or rewards were given to Wang Zun.
Now the imperial censor reported that Wang Zun harmed yin and yang and created troubles for the country. He did not abide by the edict's intention. He said that it was peaceful but was actually evading. It seemed to be respectful but was actually a heinous crime. The reason for investigating this matter was Yang Fu, the censor. He used to be Wang Zun's assistant. He had always been sinister, with a vicious mouth and a dishonest heart, so that he could frame people and be punished with his sword and pen.
Yang Fu once visited Li Jia, the leader of Wang Zun's slaves, when he was drunk. Li Jia grabbed his head and hit him on the cheek. Hong, the son of Li Jia's elder brother, drew a knife to kill him.
Yang Fu therefore harbored resentment and wanted to harm Wang Zun.
It is suspected that Yang Fu was resentful, and on the surface he came up with this idea in accordance with official business, compiled it into a memorial, and infiltrated it into a frame-up to avenge his personal resentment.
In the past, Bai Qi was a general of the Qin State. He conquered Han and Wei in the border area and captured the capital of Ying in the south. Because Ying Hou framed him, he was sentenced to death in Duyou. Wu Qi guarded the Xihe River for the Wei State, but Qin and Han did not dare to invade. There were slanderers who alienated him, so he was excluded and defected to the Chu State.
The king of Qin listened to the false accusation and killed the outstanding generals, and the king of Wei believed in the simple words and expelled the capable guards. This was a disaster caused by listening but not observing, and losing talents.
The ministers and others privately grieved that Wang Zun cleans himself and cultivates himself, practices frugality and devotes himself to serving the public, criticizes things without fearing the generals, kills evildoers without avoiding powerful men, kills lawless bandits, and relieves the country's worries. His achievements are remarkable, his contribution is outstanding, and his prestige is undefeated. He is indeed a powerful force for the country. Officials and ministers who had the courage to retreat from the enemy are now innocently subject to the hands of the enemy and harmed by slanderous and fraudulent memorials. They cannot be exonerated by their merits above and cannot be heard by the ministers below. They only cover up the enemy's evil advances and suffer the same misfortune as Gonggong. Unable to state grievances.
Wang Zun was defeated because of the capital? During the Kunlun Rebellion, a group of thieves arose and the talents were selected and recruited, and civilians were appointed as ministers. The thieves' rebellion has been eliminated, the powerful and cunning people have been punished, and they were immediately dismissed because of the treacherous tricks.
The same king, three years ago. Isn't it strange to be a virtuous official at one moment and a sycophantic minister at another?
Confucius said: If you like him, let him live; if you hate him, let him die. This is very confusing.
The false accusations cannot succeed, and I can be called a sage. I hope that the memorial can be sent to Dr. Yilang, the official doctor, to evaluate Wang Zunsu's character.
Injuring yin and yang as a human subject is a capital crime; false reporting of peace and actual evasion is also worthy of the death penalty.
If it is true as reported by the censor, Wang Zun should be punished by Guanque and exiled to a deserted place, not just dismissed from office.
The person who appoints and recommends the king should be charged with unworthy election, and it cannot just stop there.
Even if it is not as written in the memorial, but the words are modified to deepen the false accusation to accuse innocent people, they should be punished to punish the false accusation and eliminate the path of fraud.
I hope that the sage monarch will examine it carefully so that black and white can be distinguished.
After the memorial was published, the emperor appointed Wang Zun as the governor of Xuzhou and the prefect of Shujun.
After a long time, the water in the Yellow River surged and submerged the Golden Embankment of Huzi. All the old and weak people fled, fearing that the river would burst and cause harm.
Wang Zun personally led the officials and people to sink the white horse to worship the water god Hebo.
Wang Zun held the Guibi in his own hand and asked the wizard to predict the situation, asking for his own body to fill the golden embankment, so he stayed and built a thatched house to live on the embankment.
Tens of millions of officials and people kowtowed to stop Wang Zun, but Wang Zun still refused to leave.
When the embankment broke down, all the officials and people fled, except for the chief clerk, who was weeping beside Wang Zun and stood still.
The water wave retreated slightly and returned.
The officials and the people praised Wang Zun's bravery and integrity, and Zhu Ying, the third elder of Baima, reported his deeds.
I sent you to investigate and found out the truth.
So Shao ordered the censor: The water in the Yellow River in Shu County surged, destroying the golden embankment, which was only three feet short of breaching, and the people fled in fear.
The prefect was at the strategic point of the river, facing a dangerous place within easy reach. He did not avoid danger in order to calm people's hearts. The officials and the people returned to join in the work, so that the river would not overflow and cause disaster. I admire him very much.
The king was promoted to be the winner of two thousand stones and twenty kilograms of gold.
A few years later, Wang Zun died in office, and the officials and people missed him very much.
Wang Zun's son Wang Bo, who was also a Jing Zhaoyin, was removed from office because he was weak and incompetent.
Wang Zhang, courtesy name Zhongqing, was from Juping, Taishan.
He was a literary official when he was young, and later he was promoted to admonishing officials. He was famous for his outspokenness in the court.
In the early years of the Yuan Dynasty, he was promoted to Zuocao Zhonglang General. He was very friendly with Chen Xian, the imperial censor, and together they slandered Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian. They were framed by Shi Xian. Chen Xian commuted the death penalty and was sentenced to death, and Wang Zhang was dismissed from office.
When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he recruited Wang Zhang to advise the officials and was promoted to Sili Xiaowei. The ministers and nobles respected and feared him.
After Wang Zun was dismissed from office, his successor was incompetent and Wang Zhang was elected as Jing Zhaoyin.
At that time, the emperor's uncle, the general Wang Feng, assisted in political affairs. Although Wang Zhang was recommended by Wang Feng, he accused Wang Feng of being monopolistic and not close to Wang Feng.
It happened that there was a solar eclipse in the sun. Wang Zhang went to report to the emperor and was summoned. He said that Wang Feng could not be appointed and that loyal and capable ministers should be selected to assist the government.
The emperor initially accepted Wang Zhang's suggestion, but later he couldn't bear to dismiss Wang Feng.
Wang Zhang was suspected of this, so he was framed by Wang Feng and accused of treason.
This incident is recorded in the "Yuan Hou Zhuan".
At first, Wang Zhang was studying in Chang'an as a scholar, and he was the only one living with his wife.
Wang Zhang was seriously ill and lay in cow clothes without a quilt, crying and saying goodbye to his wife.
His wife angrily scolded him and said: Zhongqing, who is more distinguished in the imperial court than you?
Now that I am trapped by a serious illness, instead of encouraging myself, I start crying instead. How shallow!
Later, Wang Zhang held various official positions, and when he became King Zhaoyin, he wanted to submit a petition, but his wife stopped him and said: "People should be content. Don't you want to lie down in your cow's clothes and cry?"
Wang Zhang said: This is not something women should know.
The memorial was then entered, and as expected, he was sent to Tingwei's prison, and his wife and children were arrested.
Wang Zhang's youngest daughter, who was just twelve years old, woke up at night and cried loudly: "In the past, the jailer used to call the prisoners, and there were always nine prisoners, but now they stop calling when there are eight."
My father has always been upright, so he must be the first to die.
After questioning the next day, Wang Zhang was indeed dead.
His wife and children all moved to Hepu.
After the death of General Wang Feng, his younger brother Hou Shang of Chengdu became a general and assisted in political affairs. He informed the emperor that Wang Zhang's wife and children should return to their hometown.
His family members are all still alive, and pearl fishing has brought the property to millions. At that time, Xiao Yu was the prefect of Taishan and asked them all to redeem their original fields and houses.
Wang Zhang served as Jingzhao Yin for two years and died without punishment. The people thought he was wronged and commemorated him, so he was known as the Three Kings.
Wang Jun himself has a legend that Wang Jun is Wang Yang's son.
Zan said: Since Emperor Xiaowu established Zuo Fengyi, You Fufeng, and Jing Zhaoyin, the officials and the people have compiled a saying: There are Fang and Zhang in the front, and there are three kings in the back.
However, Liu Xiang's "New Preface" only wrote about the trip to Guanghan, Yin Wenggui, and Han Yanshou, Feng Shangxu's "Historical Records" wrote a biography of Wang Zun, and Yang Xiong's "Fayan" also praised Wang Zun.
Guanghan is wise and observant, and his subordinates cannot deceive him. Yanshou is strict and kind, and he can change customs wherever he goes. However, both of them revealed that their superiors were not trusted, so they lost their lives and ruined their achievements.
Weng Guijie was self-sufficient and dedicated to serving the public, which was a model for modern times.
Zhang Chang was shrewd and capable, loyal to his advice, specialized in elegance, punishments must be carried out, relaxations and pardons were limited, and regulations were clear, but he had a reputation of being frivolous and lazy.
Wang Zun is both civil and military, good at discerning, cunning and unconventional, and likes to talk big.
Wang Zhang was upright and uncompromising, so he was framed and tortured. His wife and children were exiled. How pitiful!
summary:
Zhao Guanghan, a native of Zhuo Commandery, began his career as a county and commandery official, known for his integrity and talent. He was elected as Maocai and served as a market price regulator before becoming the magistrate of Yangdi. His exceptional governance led to his promotion to Lieutenant of Jingfu and acting Jing Zhaoyin. After Emperor Zhao's death, he executed the corrupt Du Jian despite powerful intercessions, earning praise from the capital. He participated in deposing King Changyi and establishing Emperor Xuan, receiving the title of Marquis of Guannei. As Governor of Yingchuan, he suppressed the powerful Yuan and Chu clans and used innovative methods like the "snitch bucket" to break up local factions, restoring order. His reputation spread even to the Xiongnu.

As Jing Zhaoyin, Guanghan was diligent and generous, attributing successes to his subordinates. He was skilled in the "hook distance" method of investigation, uncovering crimes with precision. He once prevented a kidnapping by negotiating with the kidnappers and later treated them with dignity before their execution. He also exposed private affairs with uncanny accuracy, such as knowing a pavilion chief's message before it was delivered. He increased the salary of traveling wardens to prevent corruption, leading to a well-governed capital. However, after General Huo Guang's death, Guanghan raided his son's residence, offending the queen and powerful relatives. He eventually fell from favor after a series of conflicts, including a false accusation against the prime minister's wife. Despite his integrity and popularity among the people, he was executed by waist-cutting.

Yin Wenggui, from Hedong, lost his father early and worked as a prison clerk. As a market official, he curbed the violence of Huo Guang's retainers. Governor Tian Yannian recognized his talent and appointed him to oversee half of the commandery's counties. He later served as Governor of Donghai, where he maintained detailed records of officials' conduct and arrested criminals during official meetings, instilling fear. He executed the cunning Xu Zhongsun, pacifying the region. As You Fufeng, he continued his strict governance, targeting the powerful while being lenient with the weak. He was known for his integrity and modesty, dying in office with no surplus property. The emperor praised him and granted gold to his family.

Han Yanshou, from Handi, was promoted after his father died admonishing King Yan. As Governor of Yingchuan, he replaced Zhao Guanghan's confrontational methods with education in rites, consulting local elders and standardizing ceremonies. The people followed his teachings, abandoning lavish funerals. He later governed Shujun, hiring local worthies and promoting filial piety. He treated officials with kindness, blaming himself for their failures. As Zuo Fengyi, he resolved a land dispute by blaming himself, leading to the brothers' reconciliation. However, he was impeached for exceeding his authority and executed, despite public mourning. His sons resigned from office as he advised.

Zhang Chang, from Hedong, gained fame for admonishing King Changyi. He warned Emperor Xuan about the Huo family's power, advocating for their removal. As Governor of Shanyang, he requested to suppress bandits in Bohai, using rewards and amnesty to disperse them. He also advised the Empress Dowager to stop hunting. As Jing Zhaoyin, he recruited thief leaders to capture others, arresting hundreds in one day. He was known for his wit and leniency, but his frivolous behavior, like thrushing his wife's eyebrows, drew criticism. He served for nine years but was dismissed after killing a subordinate. He later governed Jizhou and Taiyuan, dying of illness. His brother Zhang Wu also governed Liang effectively.

Wang Zun, from Zhuo Commandery, began as a prison clerk and studied the classics. As magistrate of Guo County, he executed an unfilial son by shooting. As Governor of Anding, he issued strict notices and killed the corrupt Zhang Fu, shocking the commandery. He was dismissed for excessive killings but later served as Governor of Yizhou, famously scolding his horse at a dangerous pass. As Prime Minister of Dongping, he confronted the arrogant king, who eventually avoided him. He impeached Prime Minister Kuang Heng for misconduct but was demoted. As Jing Zhaoyin, he eliminated bandits in Nanshan and executed powerful criminals, but was dismissed again. He later prevented a Yellow River flood by personally staying on the embankment, earning a promotion. He died in office, remembered by the people.

Wang Zhang, from Taishan, was a blunt admonisher who slandered Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian, leading to his dismissal. Recalled by Emperor Cheng, he became Sili Xiaowei and later Jing Zhaoyin. He accused General Wang Feng of monopolizing power, leading to his execution for treason despite his wife's warnings. His family was exiled but later returned. He served for two years and was mourned by the people. The text concludes that Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, and Wang Zhang were notable officials, though some met tragic ends due to their integrity or conflicts with power.

translation:
Li Shiqi was born in Gaoyang, Chenliu County.
He likes to study, but his family is poor and he has no job to obtain food and clothing.
He worked as a gatekeeper for the village, but neither the officials nor the powerful people in the county dared to use him, thinking that he was a wild young man.
When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang and others revolted, various generals captured many areas. Dozens of them passed through Gaoyang County. Li Shiqi heard that these generals were narrow-minded, rigid about trivial etiquette, self-righteous, and unable to listen to good advice, so Li Shiqi hid.
Later, I heard that Pei Gong led his army to the suburbs of Chenliu. There was a cavalryman under Pei Gong who happened to be Li Shiqi's fellow villager. Pei Gong often asked him whether there were sages and heroes in the city.
When the knight returned home, Li Shiqi said to him: I heard that Pei Gong was arrogant and contemptuous of others, but he was very far-sighted. This is really the person I want to associate with. Let me introduce him first.
If you see Pei Gong, tell him: There is a gentleman named Li in my hometown, who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People think he is arrogant, but he himself said that I am not frivolous.
The cavalry said: Pei Gong does not like to associate with scholars. If any of the invited guests wears a Confucian hat, Pei Gong will take off his hat and urinate in the hat.
When talking to people, they often curse scholars, so don't talk like a Confucian scholar.
Li Shiqi said: Just say so.
The cavalryman calmly explained to Pei Gong as Li Shiqi had warned him.
Pei Gong arrived at the official residence in Gaoyang County and sent someone to summon Li Shiqi. When Li Shiqi arrived, Pei Gong sat on the bed and asked two women to wash his feet. This was how he summoned Li Shiqi.
When Li Shiqi entered the room, he handed over his hands without bowing and said: "Do you want to help Qin attack the princes?"
Or do you want to lead the princes to destroy the Qin Dynasty?
Pei Gong scolded: You despicable Confucian scholar!
The people of the world have suffered from Qin for a long time, so the princes led their troops to attack Qin one after another. How can you say you are helping Qin?
Li Shiqi said: If you want to gather the people and rally the rebels to overthrow the tyrannical rule of Qin, you should not sit by the bedside and summon the old man.
So Pei Gong stopped washing his feet, got up, put on his clothes, asked Li Shi to sit on his seat, and apologized to Li Shi.
Li Shiqi then talked about the situation when the six countries united. Pei Gong was very happy, gave Li food to eat, and asked: "Do you have any good plans?"
Li Shiqi said: You have gathered less than 10,000 untrained men. If you want to directly attack the powerful Qin State, it can be said that you are putting your hand into the tiger's mouth!
Chenliu County is located at the heart of the world and is connected in all directions. Now there is a lot of food stored in the city. I have always been friendly with the magistrate of Chenliu. Now please appoint me as your envoy to order him to surrender.
If he doesn't obey, you send troops to attack him, and I will respond internally.
So he sent Li Shiqi to Chenliu County, and Pei Gong led his troops to follow him, and finally captured Chenliu.
Pei Gong granted Li Shi the title of Lord of Guangye.
Li Shiqi recommended his younger brother Li Shang to lead thousands of people to follow Peigong to the southwest to seize land.
Li Shiqi often worked as a lobbyist, traveling among the princes to lobby.
In the autumn of the third year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu attacked the Han army and captured Rongyang. The Han army retreated to Gong County.
When the Chu army heard that Han Xin had captured Tongguo and that Peng Yue had repeatedly caused trouble in the Liang area, they divided their forces to rescue him.
When Han Xin just attacked Qi from the east, the king of Han was besieged in Rongyang and Chenggao many times. He planned to abandon the area bounded by Chenggao County and garrison Gongxian and Luoyang to fight against the Chu army.
Li Shiqi then said: I heard that those who know the reason why the sky is the sky can achieve the emperor's career; those who do not know the reason why the sky is the sky cannot succeed.
The king regards the people as his heaven, and the people regard food as their heaven.
Aocang has been a transportation hub in the world for a long time. I heard that Aocang has a lot of grain stored in it.
The Chu army captured Rongyang, but instead of holding on to Aocang, they marched eastward and left the punished soldiers to garrison in Chenggao. This was heaven coming to help the king of Han.
Now that the Chu army is easily captured and the Mo army is about to retreat, I have given up a favorable opportunity. I think I have gone too far.
Moreover, if the two heroes do not stand side by side, Chu and Han will be at war with each other for a long time. The people's lives will not be peaceful, the country will be in turmoil, farmers will not be able to farm, women will not be able to weave, and the people of the world will be uneasy.
I hope that the King of Han can march again as soon as possible, seize Rongyang, seize the grain of Aocang, block the danger of Chenggao, block the road of Taihang, seize the danger of Feihu, hold on to the crossing of Baima, show the princes that Mo has controlled the favorable situation, and the people of the world will know who to submit to.
Now the states of Yan and Zhao have been pacified, but only the state of Qi has not yet been conquered.
Now Tian Guang occupies the Qi State, which covers an area of ​​thousands of miles. Tian Jian commands an army of 200,000 and is stationed in Licheng. The Tian family is powerful, backed by the sea and Mount Tai, blocking the passage of the Yellow River and Jishui, and is approaching the Chu State in the south.
I ask for Shao Shu to persuade the King of Qi to make him Mo's neighbor. The king of Han said: Good!
The king of Han followed Li Shiqi's plan and stationed himself in Aocang. He also sent Li Shiqi to persuade the king of Qi, saying: "Does your Majesty know where the world belongs?"
King Qi said: I don’t know.
Li Shiqi said: If the king knows where the world belongs, then the state of Qi can be saved; if the king does not know where the world belongs, it will be difficult for the state of Qi to be saved.
King Qi said: Who should belong to the world?
Li Shiqi said: The world belongs to the King of Han.
King Qi said: Why do you say this, sir?
Li Shiqi said: The king of Han and Xiang Yu fought hard to attack the Qin army in the west, and they agreed to attack Xianyang first and become the king of Guanzhong. Xiang Yu broke the covenant and proclaimed himself king in Hanzhong.
King Xiang moved to kill Emperor Yi, and the king of Han sent the Shu Han army to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, went out to fight, accused Xiang Yu of his mistake in killing Emperor Yi, gathered soldiers from all over the world, and established the descendants of the princes.
Every city captured was given to the generals who surrendered and made a marquis. The property obtained by the King of Han was shared among the soldiers, and the benefits were shared with the people of the world. Heroes and wise men were willing to obey his use.
The armies of the princes arrived from all directions, and the food of the Shu Han Dynasty was transported by ship.
King Xiang was guilty of violating the covenant and killing the Righteous Emperor; he never remembered the achievements of others, but never forgot the mistakes of others; he was not rewarded for victory in battles, and he was not given titles for those who captured the city; he was not entrusted with important tasks if he was not a member of the Xiang family;

Shusun Tong came out and gave all the five hundred gold he had received to the Confucian scholars.
The Confucian scholars said happily: Mr. Shusun is really a saint and understands the world today.
In the ninth year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao promoted his uncle Sun Tong to the title of Crown Prince and Tutor.
In the twelfth year, Emperor Gao wanted to make King Zhao Ruyi the crown prince. Shusun Tong said: In the past, Duke Xiang of Jin deposed the crown prince and established Xi Qi instead because of Li Ji. The Jin Kingdom was in chaos for decades and was ridiculed by the world.
Because the Qin Dynasty did not appoint Fusu as the crown prince early, Hu Hai used deception to win the throne and reduced the Qin Dynasty. This was witnessed by your Majesty personally.
Nowadays, the prince's loyalty, filial piety and benevolence are known to everyone in the world; Empress Lu and Your Majesty have endured hardships and had a simple diet. How can you turn your back on her?
If Your Majesty must depose the eldest son and establish a younger son, I would like to be killed first and paint the earth red with the blood of my neck.
Gaodi said: Don't do this, I was just joking.
Shusun Tong said: The prince is the foundation of the world's stability. If the foundation is shaken, the world will be chaotic and turbulent. How can you make fun of the world?
Gaodi said: I obey your words.
When the emperor was holding a banquet, he saw four old gentlemen invited by Zhang Liang to follow the prince to see the emperor. The emperor no longer had any intention of changing the prince.
Emperor Gao died and Emperor Xiaohui ascended the throne. So he said to Shusuntong: No one is familiar with the etiquette of the late emperor's mausoleum and temple.
Sun Tong, his uncle, was promoted to Fengchang and formulated the etiquette of the ancestral temple.
All kinds of rituals and laws formulated in the Han Dynasty were written by Mr. Shusun.
Emperor Hui's visit to the Changle Palace in Shubian would disturb the people, so he responded. When the construction of the Wukunan area was just beginning, Mr. Shusun reported to the emperor and asked the emperor: Why does your majesty build a pavilion corridor from the mausoleum of Emperor Gao, prepare a royal tour every month, and travel once a month to display Emperor Gao's clothes in the high temple?
Why are future generations allowed to walk on the temple roads of Gaodi?
Emperor Xiaohui was very frightened and said: "Tear it down quickly."
Shusun Tong said: The emperor never does wrong things.
Now it has been done and the people know it.
I hope that your Majesty will build another Gaodi Temple to the north of the Weishui River as a temple for traveling and wearing clothes. This will also increase and expand the number of Gaodi ancestral temples. This is the foundation of great filial piety.
The emperor then ordered officials to rebuild the Gaodi Temple.
Emperor Xiaohui often visited the palace. Shusun Tong said: "The ancients presented fruits in spring. Now is the time when the cherries are ripe and can be presented. I hope that your majesty will travel and take advantage of the opportunity to present cherries to the ancestral temple."
The emperor agreed to do this.
This is how the ritual of offering fruits to the ancestral temple arose.
Praising: The emperor of the Han Dynasty conquered the world with his southern and northern expeditions, and the Confucian scholars used their eloquent talents to achieve the great cause of unifying the world.
"Shenzi" said: A temple is not built with a piece of wood, and an emperor's achievements are not built with the strength of one person.
It is indeed true! Liu Jing did not pull the chariot and persuaded Emperor Gao to make Guanzhong the capital to stabilize the country. Shusun Tong gave up the battle formation and did not create Modai etiquette. This was because the timing was good.
Li Shiqi hid and guarded the gate, waiting for Mingjun to come out, but he was still inevitably cooked to death.
Zhu Jian was upright and honest at the beginning and never made friends with Piyang Hou. However, he died because he could not always keep his integrity.
Lu Jia was a high official, but he did not serve as an official for the Lu family. He was beyond reproach. He joined forces with Chen Ping and Zhou Bo and relied on the generals to defend the country's power. His status and reputation were both glorious and he was the best among them!
summary:
Li Shiqi of Gaoyang was a learned man from a poor family who worked as a village gatekeeper. When various rebel generals passed through Gaoyang during the uprisings against Qin, he hid from them, considering them narrow-minded. Upon hearing that Pei Gong (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) was far-sighted, Li Shiqi arranged an introduction through a fellow villager serving under Pei Gong. Despite Pei Gong's disdain for Confucian scholars, Li Shiqi boldly criticized him for washing his feet while receiving visitors. Pei Gong apologized, and Li Shiqi advised him to seize Chenliu County, which had abundant food stores. Li Shiqi persuaded the magistrate to surrender, and Pei Gong captured Chenliu, granting Li Shiqi the title of Lord of Guangye. Later, when the Han army was besieged, Li Shiqi urged the King of Han to seize Aocang's grain supplies and strategic positions. He then volunteered to persuade the King of Qi to submit to Han, successfully convincing Tian Guang to surrender. However, Han Xin attacked Qi anyway, and Tian Guang, believing Li Shiqi had deceived him, executed him.

Lu Jia of Chu was a skilled orator who served as an envoy for Emperor Gaozu. He was sent to South Vietnam to grant Wei Tuo the king's seal. When Wei Tuo received him disrespectfully, Lu Jia warned him that the Han emperor could easily destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized and acknowledged Han's superiority. Lu Jia successfully secured South Vietnam's submission. Later, when Emperor Gaozu dismissed the value of studying the classics, Lu Jia argued that while one could conquer the world on horseback, one could not govern it that way. He wrote twelve essays explaining why Qin fell and Han succeeded, which became known as the "New Speeches." During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu Jia retired but later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo to counter the Lu family's conspiracy. His strategy helped preserve the Liu imperial house.

Zhu Jian of Chu served as prime minister to Yingbu, King of Huainan, and advised against rebellion. After Yingbu rebelled and was suppressed, Zhu Jian was rewarded. He was known for his integrity and refused to associate with the corrupt Marquis of Piyang, who was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. When Zhu Jian's mother died, Lu Jia advised the Marquis of Piyang to offer generous funeral gifts, which led to reconciliation. Later, when the Marquis of Piyang was imprisoned, Zhu Jian secretly instructed the emperor's favorite minister to plead for his release, saving his life. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Zhu Jian's earlier advice helped protect the Marquis of Piyang from execution. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Zhu Jian was implicated in a case involving the Marquis of Piyang and committed suicide to protect his family.

Lou Jing of Qi advised Emperor Gaozu to establish the capital in Guanzhong rather than Luoyang, arguing that Qin's former territory had natural defenses and abundant resources. Despite opposition from ministers from Shandong, Zhang Liang supported this plan, and the emperor adopted it, granting Lou Jing the surname Liu and the title of Feng Chunjun. Later, when the emperor planned to attack the Xiongnu, Lou Jing warned that the Xiongnu were deliberately showing weakness to ambush the Han army. The emperor ignored this advice, was besieged at Baideng, and later released Lou Jing, rewarding him. Lou Jing then proposed a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu, suggesting the emperor send his eldest princess to marry the Chanyu. Although Empress Lu objected, a substitute princess was sent. Lou Jing also recommended relocating powerful clans from various states to Guanzhong to strengthen the region.

Shusun Tong of Xue served under Qin II, cleverly avoiding punishment by calling rebels mere thieves. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai, and finally surrendered to the King of Han. Noticing the disorderly behavior of ministers at court, he offered to create court rituals. Despite criticism from conservative Confucian scholars, he adapted ancient and Qin rituals to create a practical system. After the completion of Changle Palace, the new rituals were implemented, impressing Emperor Gaozu, who remarked, "Now I know the dignity of being emperor." Shusun Tong was appointed Fengchang and rewarded with gold, which he distributed to his disciples. He later served as Crown Prince Tutor and successfully dissuaded Emperor Gaozu from replacing the crown prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, he continued to formulate rituals and established the practice of offering fruits at ancestral temples.

The multiplicity of laws and regulations breeds cunning and deceit, so the number of thieves increases.
This is really a wise and clear statement!
Laws and regulations are tools of governance, not the source of good or bad governance.
In the past, when the law was tight in the world, thieves became more and more numerous and developed to the extreme, causing the monarchs, ministers and people to avoid each other, resulting in the world being ruined and unable to be saved.
At this time, local governance was in crisis. If tough and harsh measures were not used, how could the governance be maintained?
Those who advocate morality adopt a relaxed approach.
Therefore, Confucius said: When trying lawsuits, I am no different from others. I must completely eliminate the litigation events!
Lao Tzu also said: It is in vain to ridicule a mediocre person who does not know the way.
These are not lies.
The rise of the Han Dynasty broke the square into a circle, returned to simplicity and truth, and the legal framework was extremely broad and sparse. However, the situation of officialdom is flourishing, banditry and chaos are not prevalent, and the people live and work in peace and contentment.
From this point of view, the key to official governance is not the harshness of the law.

After the Lu family was defeated, Hou Feng's family was eradicated.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo used sharp tactics to support his talents, and the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms was also caused by Chao Cuo, and finally Chao Cuo was killed.
Later, Zhidu and Ningcheng appeared again.
Zhidu was born in Dayang County, Hedong County.
Serve Emperor Wen as a Langguan.
Emperor Jing was the Zhonglang General at that time, and he dared to speak out to the emperor and rebuke the ministers' faults in person at the court.

Even if your Majesty doesn't care about yourself, how can you be worthy of the country and the Queen Mother?
After hearing Zhidu's words, the emperor retreated, and the wild boar did not harm Maiji.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. The emperor also rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. From then on, Zhidu was highly valued.
There were more than 300 families in Jinan's Kun clan. They were powerful and committed all kinds of evil. The prefect of the county could not subdue them, so Emperor Jing appointed Zhidu as the prefect of Jinan.
After Zhidu arrived, he immediately killed the chief culprit of the Shu clan, and the remaining members of other clans were so frightened that their thighs trembled.
Zhidu served as the prefect for more than a year, but Jinan County did not pick up the troops. The prefects of more than ten nearby counties feared Zhidu as they feared the superior palace.
Zhidu is brave and powerful, fair and honest, he does not open personal letters, and does not accept gifts or private entrustments from relatives and friends.
He often declares: I left my family behind and left my hometown to serve as an official. Of course I should be loyal to my duties and be loyal to the last bit of my life. In the end, I couldn't care about my wife and children.
Zhidu transferred the lieutenant, and Prime Minister Tiaohou was extremely noble and arrogant, but Zhidu bowed to him and refused to bow to him.
At this time, the folk customs were simple, and the officials and the people were afraid of offending the dignitaries and protected themselves wisely. When the princes and clans saw Zhi, they did not dare to look at him directly, and called him "Goshawk".
King Linjiang was summoned to the Lieutenant's Mansion to investigate the case. He wanted to get the knife, pen and ink to write a letter to apologize to the emperor, but Zhidu prohibited the jailer from giving it to him.
Wei Qihou sent someone to secretly deliver the sword and pen to King Linjiang.
After King Linjiang got it, he wrote a letter to apologize to the emperor and then committed suicide.
When Empress Dowager Dou heard about this, she was furious and slandered Zhidu with severe punishments. Zhidu was dismissed from his official position and returned home.
However, Emperor Jing sent someone to Zhidu's home to appoint him as the governor of Yanmen. He did not have to go to the court to say goodbye, but took a shortcut to his post. He could take advantage of the situation and handle government affairs with full authority.
The Huns were aware of Zhidu's integrity and all evacuated their border troops. After Zhidu's death, they did not dare to take a step near Yanmen.
The Huns carved a puppet figure that looked exactly like Zhidu, and ordered the cavalry to gallop and shoot, but none of them could hit. They were so frightened by Zhidu.
The Huns were worried about this situation and used the laws of the Han Dynasty to frame Zhidu. Emperor Jing said: "Zhi are all loyal ministers."
Want to free him.
Queen Mother Dou said: Isn't King Linjiang a loyal minister?
So Zhidu was beheaded.
Ningcheng was born in Zhang County, Nanyang County.
Serve Emperor Jing as a Langguan and a visitor.
He likes to be aggressive, and when he is a junior official, he must be superior to his superiors; when he is someone else's boss, he treats his subordinates as harshly and eagerly as tying wet sticks.
Cunning and cruel, domineering and domineering.
Gradually he was promoted to the rank of captain of Jinan, and he was appointed as the prefect of Jinan by Zhidu.

When Ning Cheng went to the county government, he broke in directly and insulted Zhidu. His arrogance was even higher than that of Zhidu.
Zhidu Sujian Ningcheng became famous, treated him well, and became a good friend with him.

Du Zhou was obedient to flattery, and it was important to speak less in everything.
After Zhang Tang's death, the law was strict and troubled, and the country became increasingly chaotic and desolate. The nine ministers were busy rescuing and fighting the chaos, so they had no time to discuss matters other than the rule of law!
From then until the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there were many cruel officials, but it is impossible to count them. Here we only select the famous ones and see them in the records.
Among them, those who are honest can serve as examples, while those who are dirty may have strategies and education, or may have the courage to punish traitors and thieves, and may also have literary talents and military strategies.
Although they are harsh, they are capable of doing their jobs.
The descendants of Zhang Tang and Du Zhou were famous and prosperous, so they were recorded in separate biographies.
summary:
Confucius taught that governance through laws and punishments only temporarily prevents wrongdoing without instilling shame, while governance through morality and rituals creates both shame and willing compliance. Laozi similarly distinguished between superior virtue aligned with nature and inferior virtue that is subjectively created. The text observes that excessive laws breed cunning and increase thieves, noting that laws are merely tools of governance, not its source. During the Han Dynasty's rise, broad and sparse legal frameworks allowed officials to flourish and people to live peacefully, demonstrating that effective governance depends not on harsh laws.

The text then chronicles several cruel officials. Zhidu served Emperors Wen and Jing, known for his bravery, integrity, and harsh enforcement. He once prevented Emperor Jing from risking his life to save a palace attendant from a wild boar. As governor of Jinan, he executed the chief culprit among powerful clans, causing such fear that the county became orderly. He declared his loyalty to duty over family. The Huns feared him so much they carved his likeness for target practice but could never hit it. Despite Emperor Jing recognizing him as a loyal minister, Empress Dowager Dou had him executed for his role in Prince Linjiang's suicide.

Ningcheng succeeded Zhidu as governor of Jinan, known for aggression and cruelty. After Zhidu's death, he became lieutenant and terrorized nobles. Under Emperor Wu, he was sentenced to shaving and iron collar, but escaped, became wealthy through land leasing, and wielded power greater than county governors. Zhou Yangyou was known for bending laws according to personal feelings, eradicating tyrants, and competing with superiors for power, eventually executed for his conflicts.

Zhao Yu served under Zhou Yafu, who recognized his integrity but considered him too harsh for important positions. Under Emperor Wu, he helped formulate legal regulations and became known for honesty, refusing all social invitations. Yi Zong rose from banditry to become an official through his sister's connection to the Empress Dowager. He governed with daring severity, eradicating powerful families in Hanoi. As governor of Dingxiang, he executed over 400 prisoners in one day. He was eventually executed for his actions.

Wang Wenshu began as a thief but became an official known for managing prisons. As governor of Guangping, he recruited brave men as informants, concealing their crimes while executing those who failed him. As governor of Hanoi, he arrested over a thousand people, executing the worst and confiscating property, with blood flowing for miles. He regretted that winter ended before he could eliminate all thieves. He became lieutenant but committed suicide when facing execution for his crimes, with his entire family executed.

Yan Yannian served as governor of Zhuojun and Henan, known for suppressing powerful families while protecting the poor and weak. He executed dozens from powerful clans, earning the nickname "Butcher." His mother rebuked him for relying on killing rather than kindness, predicting retribution. She returned home to prepare his burial place, and indeed he was later executed for his crimes. Yin Shang, as magistrate of Chang'an, built "Tiger Caves" - deep pits where he threw hundreds of criminals to die. He warned his children that being dismissed for cruelty was preferable to being dismissed for weakness.

The text concludes that while these officials were harsh, some were upright and understood principles, while others flattered monarchs and stirred trouble. Their descendants became prominent, recorded in separate biographies.
