Yingbu had a concubine who was ill and went to see a doctor.
The doctor's house was across from the doctor's house, so Benhe gave her very expensive gifts and had a banquet with his concubine at the doctor's house.
My concubine served the King of Huainan. During the chat, she praised Ben He as a loyal and mature man.
King Huainan was angry and said: Where did you know him?
The concubine explained the situation in detail. The King of Huainan suspected that she was having an affair with Ben He.
Ben He was afraid and said he was sick.
King Huainan became even more angry and wanted to capture Ben He.
Benhe wanted to report to Yingbu and take a post train to Chang'an.
Yingbu sent people to chase him, but he failed to catch up.
Benhe went to Chang'an and wrote a letter to report that Yingbu showed signs of rebellion and could kill him before the rebellion happened.
The emperor told Xiao Xiangguo about Ben He's petition, and Xiao Xiangguo said: Ying Bu should not have such a thing, I am afraid that someone who has hatred for him deliberately framed him.
Please imprison Ben He and send someone to secretly inspect King Huainan.
When Yingbu saw Benhe running away in fear of crime, he reported him to the court. He had already suspected that he had told some secrets of Huainan. However, the envoys of the Han Dynasty came again and proved it, so he killed Benhe's family and launched an army to rebel.
After the imperial court received reports of Yingbu's rebellion, the emperor pardoned Ben He and appointed him as a general.
The emperor summoned the princes and asked: Yingbu rebelled, what should be done to him?
The princes all said: If we send troops to bury this boy alive, what else can we do?
Teng Gong, the Marquis of Ruyin, asked his retainer Xue Gong what he thought of this matter. Xue Gong said: Yingbu should have rebelled.
Teng Gong analyzed: The emperor ceded territory and granted him titles to make him noble. He became the king of the south and became the monarch of a country of ten thousand chariots. What was the reason for his rebellion?
Duke Xue said: "In the past year, I killed Peng Yue and then killed Han Xin. These three people have equal merit and are of the same type."
He suspected that the disaster would involve him, so he rebelled.
Teng Gong reported these words to the emperor and said: My retainer is the former Chu State Commander Yin Xue Gong. If he has a plan for entering, you can ask him.
The emperor summoned Duke Xue to question him. Duke Xue replied: It is not surprising that Yingbu rebelled.
If Yingbu adopts the best strategy, the Shandong region will no longer be owned by the Han Dynasty; if he uses the middle strategy, victory or defeat will be unpredictable; if he adopts the lower strategy, his majesty can sit back and relax.
The emperor asked: What is the best policy?
Duke Xue replied: If you attack Wu State to the east, Chu State to the west, annex Qi State, seize the land of Lu, and send a document to Yan State and Zhao State to secure these places, Shandong area will no longer be owned by the Han Dynasty.
The emperor asked: What is Zhongce?
He replied: Attack Wu State from the east, Chu State from the west, annex South Korea, seize Wei State, occupy Aocang's grain, and blockade the main roads of Chenggao. It is difficult to predict whether we will win or lose.
The emperor asked: What is the next best option?
He replied: Go east to capture Wu State, go west to capture Cai Cai, hoard supplies to Yue, and live in Changsha. Your Majesty can sit back and relax, and the Han Dynasty will be safe.
The emperor asked, "What strategy will he adopt?" Duke Xue replied, "The next strategy will be adopted."
The emperor said: Why not adopt the best policy but adopt the worst policy?
Duke Xue said: Yingbu was originally a prisoner of Mount Li, and became the king of a great country. He did this all for his own sake, and did not think of the people or future generations, so he would adopt the worst policy. The emperor said: OK.
Grant Xue Gong a thousand properties.
So he sent troops and personally led the eastward attack on Yingbu.
When Yingbu began to rebel, he told his generals: The emperor is old and tired of war, so he will definitely not lead his troops in person.
He will send generals. Among the generals, I am only afraid of Huaiyin Hou Han Xin and Peng Yue. Now that they are dead, the rest are not worth fearing.
So they rebelled.
Sure enough, as Xue Gong analyzed, Yingbu attacked Jing State eastward, and Jing King Liu Mai escaped and died in Fuling.
Yingbu hijacked his troops and crossed the Huaihe River to attack Chu.
Chu State mobilized troops to fight with Yingbu between Xu County and Tong County. The Chu army was divided into three groups, trying to rescue each other and win by surprise.
Someone advised the generals of Chu State: Yingbu is good at using troops, and the people have always been afraid of him.
Moreover, the art of war says that when princes fight on their own land, they will easily escape.
Now the army is divided into three groups. If he defeats one of us, the rest will flee. How can we rescue each other?
Chu will not listen.
Yingbu really defeated one of them, and the other two disintegrated and ran away.
Yingbu advanced westward, met the emperor's army in the west of Qixian County, and fought in Zhenxiang.
Yingbu's army was very elite, so the emperor defended Yongcheng and saw Yingbu's army arrayed like Xiang Yu's army.
The emperor was disgusted by this. Seeing each other with Yingbu, he said to Yingbu from a distance: Why bother to rebel?
Yingbu said: I just want to be emperor.
The emperor scolded him angrily, so he fought and defeated Yingbu's army.
Yingbu's army was defeated and fled across the Huaihe River. They stopped and fought many times but always failed. Yingbu and more than a hundred people fled to the south of the Yangtze River.
Yingbu was originally married to Fanjun Wu Rui, so King Ai of Changsha deceived Yingbu and pretended to flee to South Vietnam with him. Yingbu believed him and followed him to Fanyang.
The Fanyang people killed Yingbu in Zixiang and finally destroyed Yingbu.
The emperor granted Benhe the title of marquis, and six other generals received the title.
Lu Wan, a native of Fengyi, was from the same hometown as Gaozu.
Lu Wan's father was friendly with Gaozu's father and had children at the same time. Gaozu and Lu Wan were born on the same day. The villagers brought sheep and wine to congratulate both families.
When Gaozu and Lu Wan grew up, they studied together and became friendly.
The villagers praised the two families for being friendly to each other. They gave birth to a son on the same day, and the son grew up to be friendly again. They once again congratulated the two families with sheep and wine.
When Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, Lu Wan always followed him around because he broke the law and evaded hiding.
When Emperor Gaozu raised troops in Pei County, Lu Wan followed him as a guest, entered Hanzhong and was promoted to general, often accompanying him in the inner court.
Following Gaozu's campaign against Xiang Yu, he always stayed close to him as a Taiwei, entering and leaving Gaozu's bedroom, receiving food, clothing, and various rewards, which none of the ministers dared to compare with.
Even though people like Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were respected only because of their career needs, as for the favor they received, no one could compare to Lu Wan.
Lu Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an.
Chang'an is the original Xianyang.
After Xiang Ji died, Lu Wan was asked to lead another army and attack Linjiang King Gongwei together with Liu Mai. After returning, he followed Emperor Gaozu to attack Zang Tu, King of Yan, and defeated the enemy and pacified those places.
At that time, there were seven princes who were not named Liu and were crowned kings.
The emperor wanted to make Lu Wan king, but the officials were dissatisfied and complained.
When Zang Tu was captured, he issued a letter from Shao and ordered the ministers and princes to choose the meritorious minister among the ministers to be crowned King of Yan.
The officials knew that the emperor wanted to make Lu Wan a king, and they all said: Lu Wan, the Taiwei Marquis of Chang'an, who often followed the emperor to bring peace to the world, and who made the most contributions, can be made king.
The emperor appointed Lu Wan as King of Yan.
Among the princes and kings, no one was as favored as King Yan.
Six years after Lu Wan was granted the title of King of Yan, Chen Xi collapsed due to suspicion of his rebellion.
Chen Xi was from Wanju County. He didn't know why he followed the King of Han in the first place.
When King Xin of Han rebelled against the Han and entered the Huns, and the emperor came back from Pingcheng, Chen Xi was granted the title of Marquis by the doctor, and as Zhao Xiangguo, he commanded and supervised the troops of Tangguo and Daiguo, and all the border defense troops belonged to him.
When Chen Xi was young, he often praised and admired Wei Gongzi Xinlingjun. When he was leading troops to guard the border fortress, he widely solicited and adopted guests.
When he returned to his hometown on vacation, he passed through the state of Zhao. There were more than a thousand cars with his guests, and the guesthouse of the Handan government was full.
Chen Xi treated his guests with the same etiquette as when interacting with civilians, always treating others with humility.
Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao State, requested to go to the capital to see the emperor. He explained in detail that Chen Xi had many guests and had many troops outside, so there was a fear that something might happen.
The emperor sent people to investigate and interrogate various illegal activities of Chen Xi's guests who lived in Daidi, and many of them implicated Chen Xi.
Chen Zhu was frightened and secretly asked the guests to send envoys to Wang Huang and Manqiuchen's residence.
In the autumn of the tenth year of the Han Dynasty, the emperor went to the emperor. The emperor summoned Chen Xi because of this incident. Chen Xici said that he was ill, so he rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself the acting king, and plundered the land.
When the emperor found out, he pardoned the officials and people who were not implicated by Chen Xi and held him hostage.
The emperor personally attacked Chen Xi and eliminated Chen Zhu's rebels. The matter is in "Gaodi Ji".
At first, the emperor went to Handan to attack Chen Xi's rebels, and King Lu Wan of Yan also attacked his northeast.
Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to the Xiongnu to ask for help. King Lu Wan of Yan also sent his subordinate Zhang Sheng as an envoy to the Xiongnu to inform Chen Xi and others that their army had been defeated.
Zhang Sheng went to the Xiongnu. Zang Yan, the son of Zang Tu, the former king of Yan, fled to the Xiongnu. He visited Zhang Sheng and said: The reason why you are respected in Yan is that you are familiar with Xiongnu affairs.
The reason why the Yan State was able to survive for a long time was that the princes frequently rebelled and could not be stabilized by the use of troops for many years.
Now you want to quickly eliminate Chen Xi and others for the sake of the Yan State. After Chen Xi and others are destroyed, it will be the turn of the Yan State, and you will also be prisoners.
Why don't you let King Yan let Chen Xi go for the time being and unite with the Xiongnu?
There is room for things to happen and he can rule the Yan Kingdom for a long time. If there is an emergency of the Han Dynasty's conquest, he can rely on this background to protect the country.
Zhang Sheng thought that what he said was right, so he ordered the Huns to attack Yan without permission.
The king of Yan, Lu Wan, suspected that Zhang Sheng was friends with the Xiongnu and plotted rebellion, so he wrote a petition asking his clan to destroy Zhang Sheng.
Zhang Sheng came back and reported in detail the reasons for doing so.
When Lu Wan came to his senses, he deceitfully sentenced other people, exonerating Zhang Sheng and his family members, allowing them to become spies for the Huns.
He also secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's residence, hoping to make the war against the imperial court continue for a long time.
The Han Dynasty beheaded Chen Xi, and his lieutenant surrendered, saying that King Lu Wan of Yan sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's station to inform him of his strategy.
The emperor sent an envoy to summon Lu Wan, but Lu Wan excused himself from illness.
The emperor also sent the Marquis of Piyang to examine Shiqi and the imperial censor Yao to meet Lu Wan, taking the opportunity to check with the people around King Yan.
Lu Wan became even more frightened, closed the door and hid, and said to his most trusted ministers: The only ones who are kings are not Liu, but the King of Changsha and I.
Last year, the imperial clan destroyed the Marquis of Huaiyin and killed Peng Yue. It was Empress Lu's plan.
Now that the emperor was ill, the power was entrusted to Empress Lu.
Empress Lu was a Taoist woman who wanted to find trouble and kill the king with a different surname and the great hero.
So he said he was sick and couldn't get up. His ministers fled into hiding.
Many of what he said were leaked. Marquis Piyang heard about it and returned to the capital to report to the emperor in detail, which made the emperor even more angry.
He also collected people who had surrendered from the Xiongnu and said that Zhang Sheng was living in exile in the Xiongnu and acting as an envoy to the Yan Kingdom.
So the emperor said: Lu Wan has really rebelled!
He sent Fan Sha to attack King Lu Wan of Yan.
Lu Wan, along with all his family members and thousands of cavalry, were stationed under the Great Wall to wait and watch, hoping that the emperor would recover and go to Beijing to plead guilty in person.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Lu Wan led his men to flee into the Huns, who made him King of East Hulu.
Lu Wan was bullied and plundered by the barbarians, and often thought of returning to the Han Dynasty.
More than a year later, he died in the Huns.
When he was the empress, Lu Wan's wife and son escaped from the Xiongnu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. When the empress became ill and could not be received, they were asked to live in Yan's mansion and planned to hold a banquet to invite them.
Empress Gao eventually passed away, and Lu Wan's wife also died of illness.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Lu Wan's grandson Lu Taren surrendered to the Han Dynasty as King Shuhu and was granted the title of Marquis of Evil Valley.
It was passed down to his great-grandson that the feudal state was abolished due to crime.
Wu Rui was the magistrate of Fanyang County during the Qin Dynasty. He was very popular among the people in the Jianghu area and was known as Fanjun.
The world began to rebel against the Qin Dynasty, Yingbu surrendered to Wu Rui, and Wu Rui married his daughter to him. So he led the Yue people to raise troops to respond to the anti-Qin struggles in various places.
Peigong attacked Nanyang County and encountered Wu Rui's general Mei Guo, so he and he attacked Xi County and Li County of Nanyang County. Both counties surrendered.
When Xiang Yu divided the princes among the princes, Wu Rui led the Baiyue soldiers to cooperate with the princes and followed them into Guanzhong, so he made Wu Rui the king of Hengshan and established Zhu as his capital.
His general Mei Guo had many merits and was granted the title of lord of 100,000 households.
After Xiang Yu's death, the emperor followed him into Wuguan because of his merits in the plum pot. So he was grateful to Wu Rui and changed his title to King of Changsha. He established his capital in Linxiang. He died a year later and was named King Wen. Zicheng Wang Wuchen succeeded to the throne.
When Wu Chen died, his son Ai Wang Hui succeeded to the throne.
Wu Hui died, and Wu You, the king of Zi Gong, succeeded to the throne.
Wu You died, and Wu Cha, the king of Zijing, succeeded to the throne.
Wu Chai died in the seventh year of Emperor Wen's reign without a son, and the feudal state was abolished.
At the beginning, King Wen Wu Rui, considered by Emperor Gaozu to be virtuous and loyal to the court, ordered the censor to say: The loyalty of the King of Changsha must be written in the decree.
At the time of Emperor Hui and Empress Gao, Wu Rui's two sons other than his legitimate son were granted the title of marquis. The title was passed down for several generations before being abolished.
Zan said: In the past, when Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, among the heroes who were not named Liu, there were eight countries who were crowned kings.
Zhang Er, Wu Rui, Peng Yue, Ting Bu, Zang Tu, Lu Wan and the two Han Xins were all able to adapt to the current situation, adapt to changes, and achieve success by virtue of cunning and strength. They all received fiefs, sat facing south, and called Gu the king.
Because they were powerful and were suspected by the court, they could not feel at ease. When things developed in the end, the situation was urgent and they were forced to plan a rebellion, and finally perished.
Zhang Er relied on his wisdom to save himself, and it was passed down to his son that he also lost his title.
Only Wu Rui did not violate the right path from the beginning, so he was able to pass the king's title to the fifth generation. However, the kingdom was abolished because there was no heir. There is a reason why his blessings were passed on to the descendants other than his legitimate son!
Written on important decrees issued by the imperial court to commend his loyalty!
summary:
Han Xin, born in Huaiyin, was poor and unable to become an official or engage in trade. He often relied on others for food. After his mother died, he buried her on a high, spacious site, hoping for future grandeur. He once ate at a pavilion chief's home, but the chief's wife resented him and prepared meals early, leaving none for him at breakfast. Han Xin understood and left. While fishing, an old woman rinsing silk fed him for dozens of days. Grateful, he promised to repay her, but she scolded him, saying she pitied him, not expecting repayment. A young man in Huaiyin insulted Han Xin, daring him to fight or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin stared, then crawled through, enduring public ridicule.

Han Xin joined Xiang Liang's army as a soldier, then served Xiang Yu as a郎中, offering advice that was ignored. He later defected to Liu Bang, King of Han, as a仓管员. Sentenced to death for a crime, he appealed to Teng Gong Xia Houying, who spared him after a conversation. Liu Bang made him a治粟都尉 but didn't value him. Han Xin fled when not promoted, but Xiao He chased him back. Xiao He convinced Liu Bang to formally appoint Han Xin as a大将, with a ceremony. Liu Bang asked Han Xin for strategies. Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses—his inability to delegate, stinginess with rewards, and cruelty—contrasting Liu Bang's potential to win hearts by appointing capable men, rewarding merit, and respecting the people's wishes. He predicted easy conquest of the Three Qin states. Liu Bang followed his plan, marching east through Chencang to pacify the region.

In the second year of Han, Liu Bang conquered Wei and Henan, then attacked Pengcheng but was defeated. Han Xin later joined forces to defeat Chu troops. After Wei Bao rebelled, Han Xin, as左丞相, attacked Wei. He feigned a river crossing at Linjin while secretly crossing at Xiayang, capturing Wei Bao. Han Xin then requested 30,000 troops to conquer Yan, Zhao, and Qi. Liu Bang agreed, sending Zhang Er and others. Han Xin defeated Zhao at Jingxing, using a背水阵 (back-to-water formation) to inspire his troops to fight desperately. He captured King Zhao Xie and killed Chen Yu. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised against attacking Yan and Qi directly, suggesting instead to intimidate Yan into surrender and then approach Qi. Han Xin followed this, and Yan surrendered.

Han Xin was later made King of Qi. After Xiang Yu's death, Liu Bang demoted him to King of Chu. Han Xin rewarded the old woman who fed him and the young man who humiliated him, making him a lieutenant. When Liu Bang suspected him of rebellion, Han Xin was captured and made Marquis of Huaiyin. He feigned illness, avoiding court. Later, he plotted with Chen Xi to rebel but was betrayed. Empress Lü and Xiao He tricked him into the palace, where he was executed, his clan exterminated. Before death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice.

Peng Yue, from Changyi, was a fisherman and bandit. He led a group of youths, enforcing strict discipline. He joined Liu Bang but later served Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang made him King of Liang. Accused of rebellion, he was captured, exiled, and killed by Empress Lü, his clan destroyed.

Ying Bu, from Liu County, was a convict who escaped to become a bandit. He joined Xiang Liang, then Xiang Yu, who made him King of Jiujiang. He killed the Righteous Emperor for Xiang Yu. Later, Sui He persuaded him to defect to Liu Bang. Ying Bu was made King of Huainan. After Han Xin and Peng Yue's deaths, he feared for his life and rebelled. He was defeated and killed by the emperor's forces.

Lu Wan, from Fengyi, was a childhood friend of Liu Bang. He became King of Yan. Suspected of colluding with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he fled to the Xiongnu after Liu Bang's death, dying there.

Wu Rui, a Qin magistrate, led Yue troops to support Liu Bang. Xiang Yu made him King of Hengshan, later Liu Bang made him King of Changsha. He died a year later, his kingdom passed down five generations before ending without an heir.

The historian comments that among the eight non-Liu kings, only Wu Rui remained loyal, his kingdom lasting longest due to his virtue.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had eight sons: Empress Lu begat Emperor Xiaohui, Lady Cao was the father of King Qiyouhui Liu Fei, Bo Ji was the father of Emperor Xiaowen, Lady Qi was the father of Zhaowu King Liu Ruyi, Gui Xun was the father of Huainan King Li Xingzhou, and other concubines were the children of Zhao Youwang Suqu, Zhao Gongwang Liu Yue, and Jixi King Liu Jian.
Huainan Li Wang Xingzhou has his own biography.
The mother of Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was Gaozu's mistress when he was a commoner.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Liu Fei was made king, and he had more than seventy cities under his control.
All the common people who could speak the language of Qi were given to the State of Qi.
In the second year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, King Qi went to the capital to meet Emperor Hui.
Emperor Hui held a banquet in front of Empress Dowager Lu to entertain King Qi. According to family etiquette, Emperor Hui invited his eldest brother, King Qi, to sit at the head of the table.
Empress Dowager Lu was so furious that she had two glasses of poisoned wine poured in front of her, and asked King Qi to offer wine to celebrate his birthday.
King Qi stood up, and Emperor Hui also stood up, wanting to celebrate his birthday with wine.
The Queen Mother was frightened, so she stood up and knocked over the wine glass.
King Qi felt strange and did not dare to drink anymore. He pretended to be drunk and left.
Later, I found out that the wine wrapped in wine was poisonous. I was very worried and thought that I would not be able to leave Chang'an and return home.
The historian said: The Queen Mother only gave birth to Emperor Hui and Princess Lu Yuan. Now there are more than seventy cities in your country, but the princess's food town is only a few cities.
You might as well dedicate a county to the Queen Mother and use it as a place to increase the princess's food and fiefdom. In this way, the Queen Mother will definitely be happy, and the King will be free from disaster.
Therefore, the King of Qi dedicated Chengyang County and honored Princess Lu Yuan as the Queen Mother.
Queen Mother Lu happily agreed.
So they held a banquet at Qi's residence in the capital, drank and had fun together, and sent King Qi back to his country.
Thirteen years later, King Liu Fei of Qi died, and his eldest son Liu Xiang succeeded to the throne.
Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao Yin, was established as King of Zhao in the ninth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign.
Four years later, Gaozu died, and Empress Dowager Lu summoned King Zhao Ruyi to Chang'an to kill him.
He had no sons and his country was extinct.
Liu You, King of Zhao You, was established as King of Huaiyang in the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign.
In the year when Zhao Yin King Liu Ruyi died, which was the first year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, he was granted the title of King of Zhao and reigned for fourteen years.
Liu You took the daughter of the Lu family as his queen. He did not love the queen, but loved other concubines.
The daughter of the Lu family left in anger and slandered the Empress Dowager Lu: "The King of Zhao said, why should a member of the Lu family hold the throne?"
After the death of the Queen Mother, I must kill them. The Queen Mother was furious, so she summoned King Zhao.
After King Zhao entered the capital, he abandoned his residence and refused to receive him. He also ordered guards to besiege him and refused to give him anything to eat.
The ministers of Zhao State sometimes gave him food in private, but they were immediately arrested and punished.
King Zhao was hungry and lamented: The Lu family is monopolistic, but the Liu family is weak; coerce the princes and give me concubines by force.
The concubine is so jealous that she falsely accuses me of a crime; the woman slanders her and ruins the country, but the emperor cannot know about it.
I have no loyal ministers, so why should I accept the call and abandon my country?
I am happy in the fields, hoping that heaven will come to judge my integrity!
It is impossible to regret, I would rather commit suicide earlier!
If you are a king and starve to death, who will take pity on you?
Mr. Lu violated the laws of nature. I could only ask heaven for revenge, so I died in confinement.
The imperial court buried him in Chang'an with the courtesy of a commoner.
After the death of Empress Dowager Lu, Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne and established Liu Sui, the son of King You, as King of Zhao.
The following year, the officials in charge asked the prince to be crowned king.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: King Zhao You died in confinement. I pity him very much.
His eldest son Liu Sui has been established as King of Zhao.
Liu Sui's younger brother Liu Piqiang, Prince Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi Yaohui, and Shu Mouhou Liu Xingju all have meritorious services and can be established as kings.
Therefore, Hejian County was taken from Zhao State and Liu Piqiang was established as King Wen of Hejian.
Thirteen years later, Liu Piqiang died and his son Liu Fu, King Ai, succeeded him.
Liu Fu died after one year as king. He had no sons and the feudal state was abolished.
King Zhao Liu Sui was king for twenty-six years. When Emperor Mo Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo thought that King Zhao was at fault and cut off the Changshan County of Zhao State. The princes were dissatisfied and Wu, Chu and other countries rebelled. Liu Sui also participated in the conspiracy and raised troops to attack the Han Dynasty.
Zhao's Prime Minister Jiande and Internal History Wang Han advised him, but Liu Sui not only refused to listen, but also burned Jiande and Wang Han to death. He sent troops to garrison the western border of Zhao, hoping to wait for the troops of Wu and Chu to join up and then move westward. He also sent people north to contact the Xiongnu.
The Han Dynasty sent Quzhou Hou Liji to attack Zhao. The King of Zhao garrisoned Handan and resisted the Han soldiers for seven months.
Wu and Chu were defeated. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they refused to send troops to help.
Shi! After defeating Manzhi, Xi led his troops back, joined forces with Li Zhou and others to attack Zhao, and diverted water to fill the city.
After the city was broken, the Zhao royal family committed suicide in a tunnel and Zhao Li was deposed.
Lian Kentong felt sorry for Zhao Moxiang and Nei Shi who died for insisting on respecting the imperial court, and named their sons as marquises.
Liu Hui, the king of the Communist Party of Zhao.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after he executed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, he established Liu Hui as king of Liang.
In the 16th year, Empress Dowager Lu killed King You of Zhao and moved Liu Hui to King Zhao. Liu Hui was unhappy.
Empress Dowager Lu married Lu Chan's daughter to King Zhao and became the queen. The queen's attendants were all members of the Lu family. They monopolized power in the palace and secretly observed King Zhao. King Zhao could not do whatever he wanted.
King Zhao had a beloved concubine who was poisoned to death by the queen with wine.
King Zhao composed a song in four chapters and ordered the musicians to sing.
King Zhao was overly sad and committed suicide six months later.
After Empress Dowager Lu heard about it, she thought it was a woman who committed suicide instead of offering sacrifices to the ancestral temple, so she deposed her country and cut off her inheritance of the throne. Liu Jian, King of Yanling.
In the eleventh year of Mo Gaozu's reign, King Lu Wan of Yan defected to the Huns. The following year, Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan.
In the fifteenth year, Liu Jian died, and his son by a beautiful woman was killed by Dan Liqiu's men. The heirs were extinct and the country was abolished.
Nine of the sons of King Hui of Qi Yao were established as kings: the prince Shengjin was the king of Qisei, the second son Xingtong was the king of Chengyangjing, Liu Xingri was the king of Ji Dongdou, Liu Laoyi was the king of Bian, Yan Jin was the king of Zhamu, Su Biguang was the king of Zamu, Xingtong was the king of Lancong, Xingsheng was the king of Zhuiyou, and Liu Xiongji was the king of bran.
Liu Xiang, King Ai of Qi, succeeded to the throne in the sixth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty. The following year, Emperor Hui died, and Empress Dowager Lu came to rule.
In the first year of Gaohou's reign, Lu Tai, the son of Queen Lu's brother, was granted the title of King of Lu, and the Jinan County of Naoqi was divided into his own state.
The next year, Liu Zhang, the younger brother of King Ai, was summoned to the capital to guard the Han court. He was named Zhu Xuhou and married to him Lu Lu's daughter.
Four years later, Liu Zhang's younger brother Liu Xingju was granted the title of Marquis of Cambodia, and both of them guarded the Han court in Chang'an.
In the seventh year of Emperor Gao's reign, the Langye County of Qi was divided, and Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was granted the title of King of Langye.
In the same year, King Zhao Liu You was imprisoned and died in the royal residence in the capital.
Since the three kings of Zhao were deposed, Empress Gao selected three from the Lu family as kings and took over the power to handle affairs.
Liu Zhang was twenty years old at the time and was very powerful. He was dissatisfied that Liu could not get his authority.
He once went to the palace to serve the Empress Dowager Lu at a banquet, and the Empress Dowager Lu ordered Liu Zhang to be the drinking officer.
Liu Zhang demanded: "I am a descendant of a military general. Please follow military laws and enforce the drinking order."
Queen Mother Lu said: Yes.
When he was enjoying his drink, Liu Zhang presented songs and dances for people to enjoy while drinking. After a while, he said: Please allow me to tell the Queen Mother about farming.
Empress Dowager Lu regarded Liu Zhang as a child and said with a smile: "I think your father knows about farming. You were already a prince when you were born. How can you know about farming?" Liu Zhang said: "I know."
The Queen Mother said: Try to tell me about plowing.
Liu Zhang said: When plowing deeply and planting densely, the remaining seedlings should be sparse; if they are not of the same kind, they should be hoed away.
The Queen Mother listened and remained silent.
After a while, one of Lu's children got drunk and ran away from the banquet. Liu Zhang chased after him, drew his sword and killed him. He came back and reported to the Queen Mother: There was a man who escaped drinking, and I beheaded him in accordance with military law.
The Queen Mother and the people around her were greatly surprised.
Because he had agreed to drink according to military law, he could not be punished, so the banquet was abandoned.
From then on, the descendants of the Lu family were afraid of Liu Zhang, and even the ministers obeyed Liu Zhang.
The Liu family became stronger.
The following year, Queen Mother Lu died.
King Lu Lu of Zhao was the general, and King Lu Chan was the prime minister. They both lived in Chang'an, the capital, and gathered troops to threaten the ministers and attempt to rebel and cause rebellion.
Liu Zhang's wife was Lu Lu's daughter, so she knew about their conspiracy. Liu Zhang then secretly sent someone to tell his brother King Qi that he wanted him to send troops to the capital. Zhu Xuhou, Dongmuhou and Han ministers acted as internal agents in order to kill the Lu family's descendants and make King Qi emperor.
When the King of Qi heard about this plan, he secretly prepared an army with his uncle Si Jun, Lang Zhongling Zhu Wu, and Lieutenant Wei Bo.
After Zhaoping, the Prime Minister of Qi, heard about this, he sent troops to surround the palace.
Wei Bo deceived Zhao Ping and said: King Qi wants to fight, but there is no tiger talisman from the Han Dynasty to verify it.
And it is good for the Xiang soldiers to surround the palace to protect the King of Qi.
I request you to lead soldiers to defend the King of Qi.
Zhaoping believed him and sent Wei Bo as general to lead the troops.
Since Wei Bo was a general, he sent troops to surround the Prime Minister's Mansion.
Zhao Ping said: Alas!
The Taoist maxim says: If you are unable to make a decisive decision, you will suffer the consequences.
That is, death by suicide.
Therefore, the King of Qi appointed Si Gou as the prime minister, Wei Bo as the general, and Zhu Wu as the internal historian. He recruited all the soldiers in the country and sent Zhu Wu to deceive King Langxie by saying: The Lu family is in rebellion, and the King of Qi wants to send troops to the west to attack.
The King of Qi considered himself a junior, young and not familiar with military affairs, so he was willing to hand over the army of the country to the king's command.
The king was a general during the reign of Emperor Gao and was familiar with military affairs.
Now the King of Qi does not dare to leave the army, so he sent me to invite the King to Linmiao to discuss with the King of Qi and lead the soldiers of Qi to march west to quell the rebellion in Guanzhong.
King Langye believed it and thought it was true, so he rode to see King Qi.
King Qi, Wei Bo and others took the opportunity to detain King Langxie, and sent Zhu Wu to mobilize all the troops of Langxie Kingdom, under the command of Zhu Wu.
Since Langxie King Liu Ze was deceived and could not return to his country, he persuaded the King of Qi: King Qi Huihui is the eldest son of Emperor Gao. In retrospect, the king is the eldest grandson of Emperor Gao and should be established as emperor.
Now the ministers are hesitant and undecided. And I, Liu Ze, am the oldest of the Liu family's children, so the ministers will definitely wait for me to participate in decision-making.
Now, the king has no use keeping me, so why not send me to the pass to discuss the matter of welcoming him.
King Qi thought this was right, so he prepared more chariots and horses and sent King Langxie away.
After King Langxie left, Qi State sent troops to the west to attack Jinan County of Lu State.
So the King of Qi sent people to send letters to various princes, which said: Emperor Gao has brought peace to the world and made all the sons of the clan kings.
After the death of King Hui of Qi Zhen, Emperor Hui sent Zhang Liang, the remaining marquis, to make his ministers the King of Qi.
After the death of Emperor Hui, Empress Gao came to power. Because of their age, the children of the Lu family were allowed to depose the vassal kings established by Emperor Gao and make Lu the king. They also killed the three Zhao kings of Yin Wang Ruyi, You Wang Liu You, and Liang Wang Liu Hui. They destroyed Liu's three kingdoms of Liang, Zhao, and Yan, and divided the original Qi kingdom into four parts.
The loyal ministers gave advice and advice, but the Lord was confused and refused to listen.
Now that Queen Gao is dead, the emperor is still young and incapable of governing the country. He must rely on the ministers in the court and various princes.
Now the descendants of the Lu family are good at high officials, gathering troops to show their majesty, threatening princes and loyal ministers, and commanding the world under the pretense of the emperor's edict. The Liu family is in danger.
I am now leading troops to the capital to kill those who should not be kings.
When the Han court heard the news that Qi had sent troops to march westward, Prime Minister Lu Chan and others sent General Yingyin Hou Guanying to lead troops to attack.
When Guan Ying arrived at Rongyang, he planned with the generals and said: The Lu family's children stationed their troops in Guanzhong and wanted to harm the Liu family and establish themselves as emperors. Now that we have defeated Qi and returned to report the victory, we have increased the power of the Lu family's children!
So he stood still and stationed his army in Rongyang, and sent people to inform the King of Qi and other princes to maintain friendly relations with them, so as to wait for the Lu family's children to mutiny and jointly attack them.
After hearing this, the King of Qi stationed troops on the western border of Qi State to wait for the agreement.
Lu Lu and Lu Chan were about to cause trouble, but Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, Taiwei Zhou Bo, and Prime Minister Chen Ping killed the Lu family.
Liu Zhang first killed Lu Chan, and then Taiwei Zhou Bo and others killed all the Lu family's descendants.
King Langxie also arrived in Chang'an from Qi.
The ministers discussed how to make the King of Qi the emperor, and they all said: The Sijun of the Queen of Qi's mother's family is very ferocious and is the biggest tiger.
Nowadays, the Lu family has almost brought chaos to the world because of its monopoly on power. Now they want to make King Qi the emperor in order to support another Lu family group.
Dai Wang's mother's family is Bo.
They are kind and kind people. Moreover, King Dai is the son of Emperor Gao, who is still alive and the oldest.
As the son of Emperor Gao, it is natural to inherit the throne. If a good person is the emperor, the ministers will feel at ease. So the ministers planned to welcome the acting king, and sent Liu Zhang to tell the King of Qi that the Lu family had been killed, and ordered him to stop his troops.
When Guan Ying was in Rongyang, he heard that Wei Bo had originally taught the King of Qi to rebel. After killing the Lu family, the Qi soldiers dismissed and returned, so he sent an envoy to summon Wei Bo to question him.
Wei Bo said: The house is on fire. Who has time to tell the parents first and then put out the fire?
So he stood back, trembling all over, too frightened to speak, and had nothing else to say.
Guan Ying looked at it for a long time and said with a smile: People say that Wei Bo is brave, but in fact he is just an arrogant mediocre person, how can he accomplish anything?
So Wei Bo was dismissed from his post. Wei Bo's father once met Qin Shihuang because he played the piano well.
When Wei Bo was a teenager, he tried to seek an audience with Cao Shen, the Prime Minister of Qi State. Because his family was poor, he had no way to get through, so he often went to Qi State Prime Minister's Mansion to sweep the floor alone early in the morning.
The stranger was surprised and thought it was a ghost, so he looked in secret and found that it was Wei Bo.
Wei Bo said: I want to see the Prime Minister but don't have the chance, so I clean the door for you in order to have the opportunity to see the Prime Minister.
So this person of the house introduced him to the prime minister Cao Shen, and Cao Shen asked him to become a person of the house.
Once he was driving for Cao Shen and made some suggestions on the way. Cao Shen thought he had talent and recommended him to King Hui of Qi.
The King of Qi summoned him and appointed him as internal history.
From then on, King Qi Hui gained the power to appoint officials with two thousand stones.
After the death of King Hui of Qi, King Ai succeeded to the throne, and Wei Bo came to power, with more power than the prime minister of Qi.
The King of Qi had withdrawn his troops and returned to his country, and King Dai was made emperor, the Emperor Wen of Han.
In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, Chengyang County, Langye County and Jinan County, which were separated from Qi State during the reign of Queen Gao, were returned to Qi State, and King Langxie was moved to Yan State as king.
Two thousand households each were granted the title of Marquis Zhuxu and Marquis Shumou. A thousand pounds of gold.
In this year, King Ai of Qi died, and his son King Sai Xin came to the throne.
He died in the fourteenth year without a son to succeed him. Bianyou was deposed and his territory returned to He.
Liu Zhang, King of Chengyang Jing, was established as king in the second year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty as Zhu Xuhou together with Liu Xingju, Shumuhou. He died in the second year of Emperor Wen's reign.
His son Liu happy, the co-king, succeeded to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, he was granted the title of King of Huainan. Five years later, he was renamed King of Chengyang. He reigned for a total of thirty-three years and died.
His son Liu Yan succeeded to the throne as King of Qing. Liu Yan died in his twenty-sixth year on the throne.
His son Liu Yi succeeded him as King Jing. Liu Yi died in the ninth year of his reign.
His son Liu Wu succeeded to the throne as King Hui, and Liu Wu died in his eleventh year as king.
His son Liu Shun succeeded him as King Huang. Liu Shun died in his forty-sixth year.
His son Liu Hui succeeded to the throne as King Dai. Liu Hui died after eight years as king.
His son Liu Jing succeeded him as King Xiao, and Liu Jing died in his twenty-fourth year.
His son Liu Yun succeeded to the throne as King Ai. Liu Yun died after one year on the throne. He had no sons. The country was exterminated and the territory was transferred to the Han Dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Liu Yun's brother Liu Li was made King of Chengyang. During the reign of Wang Mang, the feudal state was abolished.
Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, initially welcomed Emperor Wen to the official residence of Daiguo together with the ministers as Shu Mouhou. He said: "I have no merit in killing the Lu family. I request that I go to clean up the palace with my servant Teng Gong Xia Houying."
So he brought out the young emperor appointed by the Lu family and welcomed Emperor Wen of Han into the palace to rule.
At the beginning of the crusade against the Lu family, Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang made the greatest contribution. The ministers discussed and agreed to make Liu Zhang the king of all the territories of the Zhao State, and to make Liu Xingju the king of all the territories of the Liang State.
After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, I heard that Song Xuhou and Dongmuhou had wanted to make King Qi emperor, so they deposed him and reduced the credit of the Lu family.
In the second year, Emperor Wen made the princes kings, and then divided the two counties of Qi and made Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju the princes and kings.
Liu Zhang and Xingju believed that they had lost their merit because of their dereliction of duty.
More than a year later, Liu Zhang died. At that time, the Xiongnu invaded the border in large numbers, and the Han Dynasty sent a large number of troops. Prime Minister Guan Ying led the attack, and Emperor Wen personally went to Taiyuan to supervise the battle.
Liu Xingju believed that the emperor wanted to personally attack the Xiongnu, so he launched an army to rebel. When Emperor Wen heard about it, he stopped his troops and returned to Chang'an. He sent General Chai Wu, the Marquis of Jipu, to defeat the rebels and capture the King of Jibei.
The king of Jibei committed suicide and the country was abolished.
Emperor Wen took pity on the King of Jibei for rebelling and destroying himself. In the second year, he made Liu Bojun, the seven sons of King Hui of Qi, and others into princes.
In the fifteenth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, King Wen of Qi Liu Ze died without a son.
But at that time, the descendants of King Qi Huihui still had King Chengyang. Emperor Wen pitied King Qi Hui because he had no legitimate son to succeed him, so he divided the Qi country into six, and the six sons of King Hui who were previously named princes were still alive. Established as kings: Yang Xuhou Liu Jianglu is the King of Qi Xiao, Anduhou Liu Zhi is the King of Jibei, Wuchenghou Liu Xian is the Miao King, Baishihou Liu Xiongqu is the Micellar King, Pingchang Hou Liu Yin is the Jiaoxi King, and Jiehou Liu Biguang is the Jinan King.
In the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, six kings were made kings on the same day.
In the eleventh year of the reign of the above-mentioned six kings, that is, the third year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Wu and Chu rebelled. The four kings of Miaojie, Jiaoxi, Lei!, and Jinan all responded by sending troops to fight against the Han.
They wanted to invite King Qi to fight against the Han, but King Xiao of Qi was hesitant, so he held on to the city and refused to rebel.
The three kingdoms of Miaojie, Miaochuan, and Jinan sent troops to surround Qi. The King of Qi sent his envoy Dr. Lu Zhong to report to Emperor Mo. The Emperor ordered Dr. Lu Zhong to return to Qi to report to King Qi, asking King Qi to defend the city. The Mo soldiers had defeated Wu and Chu.
On the way, the doctor returned to Qi. Soldiers from the Three Kingdoms surrounded Linmiao City several times and were unable to enter the city.
The generals of the Three Kingdoms and the officials on the road swore an oath: If you turn around and say that the Han Dynasty has been conquered, Qi will surrender to the Three Kingdoms as soon as possible, otherwise the city will be massacred.
Although the doctor agreed on the way, he walked to the city, looked up and saw the King of Qi, and said: The Han Dynasty has sent millions of troops, sent Taiwei Zhou Yafu to defeat Wu and Chu, and is leading troops to rescue Qi State. Qi State must hold on and not surrender!
The generals of the Three Kingdoms killed the doctor on the road.
Before that, Qi State was besieged and in great danger. It had secretly negotiated with the Three Kingdoms. Before the alliance was concluded, a senior official from the Han Dynasty happened to be on the way. The ministers of Qi State once again advised the King of Qi not to surrender to the Three Kingdoms.
It happened that Han Dynasty general Le Bu, Pingyang Marquis Cao Xiang and others led troops to Qi State, defeated the armies of the three countries and lifted the siege.
Later, when I heard that the King of Qi had conspired with the Three Kingdoms, he wanted to send troops to attack Qi.
King Xiao of Qi became frightened and committed suicide by drinking poison.
The four kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Jinan, and Miaochuan were all beheaded. Their feudal state was also abolished, leaving only the King of Jibei.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty heard the news of King Qi Xiao's suicide, he believed that King Qi had no intention of rebellion at first and had other plans because of coercion. This was not his crime. Emperor Jing went down to Shao and established Liu Shou, the crown prince of Prince Xiao, as King Qi Yi.
King Yi died in the 23rd year of his reign, and his son King Li Liu Ciyuan succeeded him.
King Qi Li's mother was Queen Mother Ji.
The Queen Mother made her brother's daughter his queen, but King Qi did not love Queen Ji.
The Empress Dowager Ji wanted to pamper the Ji family for generations, so she ordered her eldest daughter Ji Wengzhu to enter the palace, control the harem, and prevent the concubines in the harem from getting close to the King of Qi. She wanted the King of Qi to love Queen Ji exclusively.
The king of Qi therefore committed adultery with his sister.
There was a eunuch named Xu Jia in the state of Qi who entered the palace to serve the empress dowager of the Han Dynasty.
The Queen Mother has a beloved daughter named Xiuchengjun. She is not born to the Liu family, and the Queen Mother loves her very much.
Xiu Chengjun has a daughter named Mo, and the Queen Mother wants her to marry the princes.
Xu Jia then requested to be sent as an envoy to the state of Qi, saying that he would definitely ask the king of Qi to write a letter requesting to marry E.
The Empress Dowager was overjoyed and sent Xu Jia to Qi.
At that time, the master's father Yan knew that Xu Jia had come to Qi to ask the King of Qi to marry the queen. He also took the opportunity to tell Xu Jia: If the matter succeeds, I hope that my daughter will be willing to join the palace of the King of Qi.
Xu Jia arrived in Qi and hinted this matter to the king of Qi.
Empress Dowager Ji was furious and said: The king of Qi has a queen, and the harem is ready.
Moreover, Xu Jia was a poor man in Qi. He had no future and became a eunuch. He went to the palace to do things. He did not do anything beneficial to Qi, but he wanted to disturb my Wang family!
Besides, what does Master Yan want to do?
I also want to enrich my daughter into my harem!
Xu Jia was greatly embarrassed and came back to report to the Queen Mother: The King of Qi is willing to marry E, but the matter may be harmful. I am worried that it will be like King Yan.
King Yan committed adultery with his daughter and sisters, and died after being found guilty.
Xu Jia therefore used the incident of King Yan to shake the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother said: Stop talking about marrying your daughter to King Qi!
Later, this matter gradually became known to the emperor.
As a result, Lord Fu Yan had a rift with the state of Qi.
When Zhufu Yan was favored by Emperor Wu and came into power, he took the opportunity to say: There are 100,000 households in Linmiao of Qi State, and the market transaction tax collected in one day is thousands of gold. The number of people and wealth exceeds that of Chang'an. No one who is not the emperor's biological brother or beloved son will get this throne.
Now the King of Qi is even more estranged from the royal family!
So, he told Emperor Wu from beginning to end, saying that Qi State wanted to rebel when Empress Dowager Lu was there, and when Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao of Qi almost also rose up in rebellion.
Now I heard that King Qi and her sister were committing adultery.
Therefore, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty worshiped his father Yan as the prime minister of Qi and asked him to preside over the trial.
The master's father Yan arrived in Qi State and quickly interrogated the eunuchs in the palace of the Queen of Qi who helped the King of Qi to clear the residence of his sister Wengzhu. His words also involved the King of Qi.
The young King of Qi was afraid that he would be arrested and executed by the officials for being guilty, so he drank poison and committed suicide.
At this time, Zhao Wang Liu Sui was afraid that his father Yan would defeat Qi as soon as he left the palace, and worried that he would gradually alienate the Liu family, so he wrote a letter saying that his father Yan had accepted bribes and had unfair intentions. The emperor also took this opportunity to imprison his father Yan.
Gongsun Hong said: The King of Qi died of worry and had no descendants. He could not satisfy the wishes of the people of the world without killing his father Yan.
The master's father Yan was killed in his seat.
King Li died after reigning for five years without any descendants, and his kingdom was abolished.
Liu Zhi, the king of Jibei, initially conspired with Wu and Chu when they rebelled, but later he held on to the city and did not send troops, so he was not executed and moved to be the king of Leichuan.
During the Yuanshuo period of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the Qi State lost its heirs and its territory returned to the Han Dynasty.
The descendants of King Qi Hui include Chengyang and Sichuan.
Sichuan was close to the State of Qi. Because Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty had the tomb of King Hui in Qi, he gave all the gardens surrounding the tomb of King Hui to the State of Sichuan so that it could offer sacrifices on time.
Liu Zhi died in his thirty-fifth year as king, and was named King Yi.
His son Liu Jian, King Jing, succeeded to the throne and died twenty years ago.
His son Liu Qian, King of Qing, succeeded to the throne and died in the thirty-fifth year.
His son Liu Zhonggu, King Si, succeeded to the throne.
In the fifth year of Emperor Mo Xuan's reign, the governor of Qingzhou reported to Emperor Xuan that Liu Zhonggu had his Ai slaves commit adultery with his concubines and many of the maids who served him. He either slept with them or made them naked during the day, like animals having sex, and Zhonggu watched in person.
When a child is born, he says: If he is in chaos and does not know his father, he will kill the child.
Emperor Xuan handed the matter over to the prime minister and the imperial censor for discussion. The prime minister and the imperial censor reported that he was the king of the vassals in ancient times, and asked him to set up a concubine with the title of eight sons, with a salary rank of 600 dan, in order to allow him to have more children to respect his ancestors.
However, Zhonggu behaves like an animal, messing up the relationship between monarch, ministers, and husband and wife, and violating human ethics. Please arrest him.
The emperor then issued a letter to Shao and cut off the four counties under his jurisdiction.
Died twenty-eight years later.
His son Liu Shang, king of Kao, succeeded to the throne and died five years ago.
His son, Xiao Wang Liu Heng, succeeded to the throne and died in thirty-one years.
His son Liu Jiao, King Huai, succeeded to the throne and died in six years.
His son Liu Yong succeeded to the throne, and by the time of Wang Mang, the feudal state was extinct.
Zan said: The state of Qi under King Hui of Qi is the largest among the vassal states.
Since the founding of the country at the beginning of the Yuan Dynasty, the world was peaceful, and the emperor's children were young. They felt ashamed that they were isolated and defeated without the help of the princes, so they made the children of the same surname the princes and kings to control the world.
At that time, the princes could appoint officials at all levels below the imperial censor on their own. The official appointments were the same as those in the Han Dynasty. The Han court only appointed prime ministers for them.
After the rebellion of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu was suppressed, the power of the princes was weakened. In response to Fu and Xiang's behavior of beautifying the princes and kings and not punishing the princes and kings when they were guilty, laws and regulations such as "Zuoguan Law" and "Law of Fuyi A Party" were formulated.
From then on, the princes could only receive food, clothing, fiefdom tax revenue, and some poor people could only ride ox carts.
summary:
Emperor Gaozu of Han had eight sons from various consorts. Empress Lu bore Emperor Xiaohui; Lady Cao bore Liu Fei, King of Qi; Bo Ji bore Emperor Xiaowen; Lady Qi bore Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao; and other concubines bore Liu You, Liu Yue, and Liu Jian. Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was granted over seventy cities in the sixth year of Gaozu's reign. During Emperor Hui's reign, King Qi visited the capital. Emperor Hui honored him as eldest brother at a banquet, angering Empress Dowager Lu, who attempted to poison King Qi. After discovering the plot, King Qi dedicated Chengyang County to increase Princess Lu Yuan's fiefdom, appeasing the Empress Dowager and securing his safe return. Liu Fei died thirteen years later, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang.

Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao, was killed by Empress Dowager Lu after Gaozu's death, leaving no heirs. Liu You became King of Zhao but was imprisoned and starved to death after his Lu-family queen falsely accused him of plotting rebellion. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Emperor Wen established Liu Sui as King of Zhao. Liu Sui later joined the Wu-Chu rebellion, was besieged for seven months, and committed suicide after the city fell.

Liu Hui was moved to Zhao against his wishes. His Lu-family queen poisoned his beloved concubine, causing him to compose a sorrowful song and commit suicide. Liu Jian, King of Yan, died, and his son was killed, extinguishing his line.

King Qi Yao's nine sons were established as kings. During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu-family members were granted kingdoms from Qi's territory. Liu Zhang, a grandson of King Qi, served at court and openly defied the Lu family during a banquet, killing a drunken Lu relative under military drinking rules. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. Liu Zhang secretly informed his brother King Qi, who raised troops. The Han generals killed the Lu family, and the ministers chose to make King Dai (Emperor Wen) emperor instead of King Qi, fearing the Qi queen's mother's family was too powerful.

Emperor Wen restored Qi's lost territories and granted titles to Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju. Liu Xingju later rebelled and committed suicide. Emperor Wen divided Qi into six kingdoms for King Qi Hui's sons. During Emperor Jing's reign, four of these kings joined the Wu-Chu rebellion. King Xiao of Qi initially hesitated, was besieged, but held out until Han forces arrived. After learning the king had negotiated with rebels, he committed suicide. Emperor Jing pardoned him posthumously.

Later, King Qi Li committed adultery with his sister. When Emperor Wu sent an investigator, the king committed suicide, leaving no heirs, and Qi was abolished. The remaining Qi territories eventually passed to the Han dynasty. Over time, the power of princes was reduced after the Seven Kingdoms rebellion, with laws restricting their authority until they could only collect taxes from their fiefdoms.

translation:
The Prime Minister of Wei, whose courtesy name is Wenweng, was born in Dingtao, Jiyin, and later moved to Pingling.
When Wei Xiang was young, he studied the Book of Changes and became the governor of the county. He was praised as a virtuous person. Because he ranked first in answering policy questions, he became the magistrate of Maoling County.
Soon, the guests of Censor Da Sang Hongyang came to Maoling and falsely claimed that Sang Hongyang was coming to the guest house.
The county magistrate did not go to see the guest on time, so he tied up the county magistrate. Prime Minister Wei suspected that the guest was causing trouble, arrested him, tortured him and learned about his crime, and sentenced the guest to be executed in the street. Therefore, Maoling is managed very well.
Later, the prime minister of Wei was promoted to the governor of Henan, where he prohibited bad people from doing evil things, and the local powerful were very afraid of him.
It happened that the prime minister Che Qianqiu died at the time. Che Qianqiu's son had been the commander of the Luoyang Armory. He saw that his father was dead, and the Wei Prime Minister was very strict in managing the affairs of the county. He was afraid that he would be blamed for it in the long run, so he resigned from the official position.
Prime Minister Wei sent Sasuke's own deputies to chase him and call him back, but he finally did not come back.
Prime Minister Wei himself sighed regretfully: When the general resigned after hearing this arsenal order, he would definitely think that I was disrespectful to his son because the prime minister was dead.
It will also make those powerful people in the world blame me. It’s dangerous!
When Che Qianqiu, the son of an arsenal commander, arrived in Chang'an, General Huo Guang scolded Prime Minister Wei for this: The young new emperor had just ascended the throne and believed that Hangu Pass was the strongest place to defend the capital and the weapons depot was a place where sophisticated weapons were stored, so he made the prime minister's brother the captain of Hangu Pass and the prime minister's son the commander of the weapons depot.
Now the governor of Henan, Wei Xiang, did not think deeply about the country's plans, but just dismissed the prime minister's son when he saw his death. How shallow is this!
Later, someone accused Prime Minister Wei of killing an innocent person, and the matter was brought to the competent government office.
There were two to three thousand officers from the Henan garrison who stopped the general Huo Guang and said they were willing to stay for another year to atone for the sin of the prefect Wei Xiang.
More than 10,000 old and weak people in Henan guarded Hangu Pass and asked to enter the pass to write to the emperor. The officials guarding the pass reported the matter.
General Huo Guang handed Wei Prime Minister to Tingwei for punishment because of the arsenal order.
Prime Minister Wei was imprisoned for a long time. After the winter, it happened that the imperial court pardoned the prisoners.
There was also an edict ordering Prime Minister Wei to serve as the magistrate of Maoling County again and promote him to the governor of Yangzhou.
Later, the imperial court inspected the ministers of the county and state, and many of them were demoted.
Prime Minister Wei and Bing Ji were close. At that time, Bing Ji's official position was Doctor Guanglu. He wrote to Prime Minister Wei and said: The imperial court has a deep understanding of your achievements and behavior and will appoint you.
I hope you will be cautious and self-respecting in everything you do and cultivate your talents.
Prime Minister Wei thought Bingji's words were right, so he restrained his dignity.
After serving as governor for two years, he was recruited as an admonishing official and then became the governor of Henan.
A few years later, Emperor Xuan ascended the throne and recruited Wei Xiang to join the imperial court as chief minister of agriculture, and was later promoted to imperial censor.
Four years later, the general Huo Guang died. The emperor missed his merits and virtues and made his son Huo Yu the right general. Huo Guang's nephew Huoshan, the Hou of Leping, was in charge of the affairs of the Shangshu Province.
Prime Minister Wei wrote to the emperor through Ping'en Hou Xu Bo, saying: "Spring and Autumn" ridicules people who have been ministers for generations, hates that all the three generations of Song Dynasty were officials, and even Lu Jisun's autocratic rule has put the country in danger and chaos.
Since the first year of Emperor Wu's reign, the royal family's children could receive salaries, but the country's political affairs had to be decided by Tsukasa.
Now that Huo Guang is dead, his son has become a general again, his brother's son has become a minister and holds political positions, and his brothers and sons-in-law have military power and are very powerful.
Huo Guang's wife Xian and their female relatives are all registered in Changxin Palace and can come and go freely. Sometimes they go in and out through the forbidden gate at night. They are arrogant, extravagant, and uninhibited. I am afraid that they will gradually lose control in the future.
We should try to weaken their power and dispel their conspiracy, so as to strengthen the foundation of the Han Dynasty for generations and preserve the reputation of the hero Huo Guang.
In addition, according to past regulations, anyone who wrote a letter to the emperor must make two copies of the memorial, one of which was a copy. The official in charge of the affairs of the Shangshu Province would read the copy first. If the content of the memorial was inappropriate, it would be shelved and not reported to the emperor.
Prime Minister Wei used Uncle Xu to remove the copy to avoid being blocked by Huo's people.
Emperor Xuan read the memorial of Prime Minister Ding and Wei and thought it was very good. He issued an edict to confer Prime Minister Wei on the throne and fully adopted Prime Minister Wei's memorial.

So he only removed Bingxian from his official position and cut off 400 households in the city.
Later, he was made the city gate captain.
After Bingxian's death, his son Bingchang assumed the title of Marquis of Guannei.
When the Emperor of the Han Dynasty became emperor, he rebuilt the abandoned achievements. Because Bingji had been particularly benevolent to the Han Dynasty in the past, so in the first year of Emperor Hongjia's reign, he sent a letter to the prime minister and the imperial censor in Shao, saying: I heard that praising meritorious and virtuous people and restoring the successors to the heroes who have no descendants is a good way to respect the ancestral temple, the country, and open the way to sages.
The late Boyang Hou Bingji was named a marquis because of his kindness to the late emperor. Now his descendants have become extinct. I feel very pitiful.
It is a common principle in ancient times that the most kind and beautiful behavior will be extended to descendants. I conferred Bingji’s grandson Zhonglang General Guannei Marquis Bingchang as Boyang Marquis to enshrine Bingji’s descendants.
Bingji's feudal state was continued thirty-two years later.
Bingchang passed the title to his sons and grandsons, and it was not until Wang Mang usurped the Han Dynasty that it was extinct.
Zan said: When the ancients made names, they must start from symbolizing similar things, looking for distant things from things, and looking for near things from themselves.
Therefore, the scriptures say that the king is likened to the human mind, and the ministers are like the legs and arms of a human being, indicating that the king and the ministers are likened to the entire human body, and they complement each other.
Therefore, it is a common practice throughout the ages for monarchs and ministers to assist each other. It is natural and inevitable.
Looking at the prime ministers of the Han Dynasty recently, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty established the foundation, Xiao He and Cao Shen were the top ministers, Emperor Xiaoxuan was the master of Zhongxing, and Prime Ministers Bingji and Wei also had good reputations.
At that time, officials were promoted and demoted in a reasonable manner, their responsibilities were clear, most ministers were competent and competent, and people at home treated each other with courtesy.
Observing their behavior and deeds, is it just a false name?
summary: Wei Xiang, courtesy name Wenweng, was a native of Dingtao, Jiyin, later moving to Pingling. He studied the Book of Changes in his youth, became a county governor, and was praised for his virtue. After ranking first in policy questions, he became magistrate of Maoling County. When a guest of Censor Sang Hongyang falsely claimed Sang was arriving and tied up the magistrate, Wei Xiang suspected foul play, arrested the guest, tortured him to reveal his crime, and executed him in the street, leading to excellent governance in Maoling. Promoted to governor of Henan, he prohibited evil deeds, instilling fear in local powers. When Prime Minister Che Qianqiu died, his son, commander of the Luoyang Armory, resigned fearing Wei Xiang’s strictness. Wei Xiang regretted this, fearing it would cause resentment. General Huo Guang later scolded Wei Xiang for dismissing the prime minister’s son after his death, calling it shallow. Accused of killing an innocent person, Wei Xiang faced investigation, but over 10,000 Henan residents petitioned for him. Huo Guang handed him to Tingwei for punishment, but he was pardoned and reappointed as magistrate of Maoling, then governor of Yangzhou. After demotions in an imperial inspection, Wei Xiang, close to Bingji, heeded his advice to restrain his dignity. He served as governor for two years, then became an admonishing official and later governor of Henan again. After Emperor Xuan ascended, Wei Xiang became chief minister of agriculture, then imperial censor. Four years later, Huo Guang died. Wei Xiang wrote to the emperor, warning against the Huo family’s power, citing historical precedents of autocratic rule causing chaos. He suggested weakening their influence to strengthen the Han dynasty. Emperor Xuan adopted his advice, deposing Huo Yu, Huo Yun, and Huo Shan. Wei Xiang became prime minister, replacing Wei Xian, and was named Gaopinghou. The Huo family later plotted to kill him but were discovered and executed. Emperor Xuan then personally governed, selecting good ministers, and Wei Xiang was popular as prime minister. During the Yuankang period, when the Xiongnu attacked Han forces, Wei Xiang advised against military retaliation, citing border poverty and internal social issues like 222 cases of familial killings. He urged focus on domestic stability. Emperor Xuan followed his advice. Wei Xiang, well-versed in the Book of Changes, studied Han history and advocated following past systems. He presented 23 items from the late emperor’s edicts, emphasizing agriculture, grain storage, and frugality to prepare for disasters. He warned of current grain price hikes and border conflicts, urging the emperor to care for the people. Emperor Xuan implemented his suggestions. Wei Xiang also presented chapters on Yin-Yang and seasonal governance, arguing that proper seasonal management prevents disasters and ensures prosperity. He recommended selecting ministers knowledgeable in Yin-Yang to oversee seasonal affairs. The emperor adopted his proposals. Wei Xiang’s commissioners reported irregularities from counties, often revealing unreported rebellions or disasters. He was severe and resolute, unlike the tolerant Bingji. He served as prime minister for nine years, dying in the third year of the Shenjue era, and was posthumously named Xianhou. His son Wei Hong inherited the title but was demoted to Marquis of Guannei during the Ganlu era due to a crime.
