Wei Bao was the son of Wei State during the Six Kingdoms period.
His elder brother Wei Jiu was named Lord Ningling at that time. After Qin destroyed Wei, he was deposed as a commoner.
After Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, Wei Jiu went to serve him.
Chen Sheng sent a Wei man named Zhou Shi to lead his troops to capture the land of Wei. After occupying it, he wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei.
Zhou Shi said: Only when the world is in chaos can the integrity of loyal ministers be seen.
Now that the whole world has betrayed Qin, it stands to reason that the king of Wei should be established after him.
Qi and Tang each sent fifty military chariots to help support Zhou Shi as king.
Zhou Shi refused to accept it and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu. After five trips, King Chen agreed to make Wei Jiu the king of Wei.
Zhang Han defeated King Chen and raised his troops to Linji to attack King Wei.
The king of Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements.
Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army together with Zhou Shi to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han defeated them again, killed Zhou Shi and others, and surrounded Linji.
In order to save the people in the city, Wei Jiu agreed to surrender to the Qin army.
After the agreement was made, Wei Jiu committed suicide and died.
Wei Bao fled to Chu.
King Huai of Chu sent thousands of troops to Wei Bao to recapture the land of Wei.
By this time, Xiang Yu had defeated the Qin army and captured Zhang Han. Wei Bao captured more than 20 cities and was made king of Wei by Xiang Yu.
Wei Bao led his army to follow Xiang Yu into the pass.
In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu divided the feudal lords. He wanted to occupy Daliang, so he moved Wei Bao to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty.
The King of Han almost ordered the Three Qin Dynasties to cross the Yellow River from Linjin. The King of Wei, Wei Bao, surrendered the whole country to the King of Han, and followed the King of Han to attack the Chu army in Pengcheng.
The king of Han failed and retreated to Rongyang. Wei Bao asked to go back to visit his mother's condition. After returning to Wei, he blocked the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han.
The king of Han said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao to submit.
Li Sheng arrived in Wei. Wei Bao declined politely and said: Life is very short.
The King of Han insults people at will and scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no courtesy at all. I don't want to bear the anger and go to see him again.
So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured him, and escorted him to Rongyang, dividing Wei Bao's original territory into three counties: Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang.
The king of Han asked Wei Bao to garrison Rongyang.
At that time, the Chu army was attacking Rongyang, and the situation was urgent. Zhou Ke said: "You cannot defend with those who betray the country."
Then he killed Wei Bao.
Tian Dan, a native of Di County, was a member of the Tian clan, King of Qi during the Six Kingdoms period.
Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong and Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng were both heroes. Their clans were powerful and respected.
Chen She sent Zhou Shi to capture Wei and went north to Di County, but failed to capture it in the end.
Tian Dan pretended to kill his slave, and brought his young men with him, tied up the slave, and came to see the magistrate of Di County. When he saw the magistrate, he took the opportunity to kill him.
Then he summoned the sons of powerful officials and said: "The princes from all walks of life have proclaimed themselves kings and rebelled against Qin. Qi is a country that was enfeoffed in ancient times. I, Tian Dan, am a member of the Tian family of King Qi, so I should be king."
So Tian Dan declared himself king and sent troops to attack Zhou City.
Zhou's army retreated, and Tian Dan took the opportunity to expand eastward and pacify Qi's territory.
The army of General Zhang Han of the State of Qin surrounded Wei King Wei Jiu in Linji, and the situation was urgent.
The King of Wei asked Qi for help, and King Tian Dan of Qi personally led an army to rescue the King of Wei.
Zhang Han sent troops to sneak around the streets at night, defeated the Qi and Chu armies, and killed Tian Dan at the foot of Linji City.
Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong gathered up the remaining soldiers of Qi and fled eastward to Dong'a.
When the people of Qi heard that Tian Dan had died in battle, they made Tian Jia, the younger brother of the former King of Qi Tian Jian, the king of Qi. Tian Jiao was appointed prime minister, and Tian Xian was appointed general to resist the princes.
Tian Rong was defeated and fled to Shu'a, but Zhang Han pursued and surrounded him.
Xiang Liang heard the news that Tian Rong was in danger, so he led his troops to defeat Zhang Han's army under Dong'a City.
Zhang Han fled to the west, and Xiang Liang took advantage of the situation to pursue him.
Tian Rong was very angry when he learned that the state of Qi had made Tianjie king. He led his army back to the state of Qi and defeated the king of Qi, Tianjia.
Tian Jia fled to Chu State, and Prime Minister Tian Jiao fled to Zhao State.
Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Xian had gone to Zhao State to request reinforcements before, so he stayed in Zhao State and did not dare to come back.
So Tian Rong made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi the king of Qi. Tian Rong assisted him, and Tian Heng became the general, and the Qi country was pacified.
Xiang Liang pursued Zhang Han, but Zhang Han's army became increasingly powerful. Xiang Liang sent an envoy to urge Qi to send troops to join the Chu army to attack Zhang Han.
Tian Rong said: Only when the Chu State kills Tian Jia and the Tong State kills Tian Jiao and Tian Xian will they be willing to send troops.
King Huai of Chu said: Tianjia is the king of my ally, and he surrendered to me when he had no other choice. It would be unethical to kill him.
The state of Tang was not willing to kill Tian Jiao and Tian Xian to please the state of Qi.
King Qi said: If the viper bites the hand, cut off the hand; if the viper bites the foot, cut off the foot.
Why?
Because if you don’t do this, it will harm your whole body.
Tianjia, Tianjiao, and Tianxian are not brothers to Chu and Tang, so why not kill them?
Moreover, if Qin can rule the world again, those who first raise armies and become kings will not only be humiliated, but also have their graves dug up after their death.
Chu and Tang did not follow Qi's advice, and Qi was very angry and refused to send troops.
Zhang Han indeed defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Liang.
The Chu army fled eastward, and Zhang Han crossed the river and surrounded Zhao at Julu.
Xiang Yu also resented Tian Rong for this.
Xiang Yu had secured Zhao State, surrendered Zhang Han, marched westward to Xianyang, destroyed Qin State, made a marquis and established a king, he changed the title of Qi King Tianshi to Jiaodong King, and established Jimo as the capital.
Tian Du, a general of the Qi State, participated in the rescue of the Zhao State and allowed Xiang Yu to enter the Pass. Therefore, Tian Du was made King of Qi and his capital was Linmiao.
Tian An, the grandson of Tian Jian, the former King of Qi during the Six Kingdoms period, captured several cities in Jibei when Xiang Yu crossed the river to rescue Zhao, and led his army to defect to Xiang Yu. Therefore, Xiang Yu made Tian An the king of Jibei and made Boyang his capital.
Because Tian Rong was carrying Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to help the Chu army attack the Qin army, he was not crowned king.
Chen Yu, the general of Zhao State, also failed to make him king because of his dereliction of duty.
Both of them hated Xiang Yu deeply.
Tian Rong sent troops to help Chen Yu and asked him to attack Zhao. Tian Rong himself also sent troops to attack Tiandu, and Tiandu fled to Chu.
Tian Rong detained King Qi Tianshi and refused to let him go to Micellar.
Tian Shi's cronies said: King Xiang is strong and violent. If you don't go and take office, there will definitely be disaster.
Tian Shi was afraid, so he secretly escaped to Miaojie and took up his post.
Tian Rong was furious, chased Tian Shi in Jimo and killed him, then turned around and attacked Tian An, the king of Jibei. So Tian Rong established himself as the king of Qi and annexed the territory of San Qi.
When Xiang Yu heard about the dispatch, he was furious and sent troops to attack Qi in the north.
Tian Rong sent troops to resist Xiang Yu in Chengyang.
Tian Rong was defeated and fled to the plains, where he was killed by the local people.
Xiang Yu burned down the walls of Qi and massacred wherever he went.
So the people of Qi gathered to resist him.
Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered up the remnants of Qi's troops and gathered tens of thousands of people to attack Xiang Yu's army in Chengyang.
At this time, Liu Bang, the king of Han, led various princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng.
When Xiang Yu got the news, he spared Qi and returned to Pengcheng to attack the Han army. As a result, he fought with Mo continuously, and the two sides were at a stalemate in Rongyang.
So Tian Heng restored the cities of Qi State and made Tian Rong's son Tian Guang the king of Qi. Tian Heng came to assist him. All political affairs of Qi State were decided by Tian Heng, no matter how big or small.
Tian Heng had been pacifying Qi for three years when he suddenly heard that Han Xin, the general of the King of Han, was leading his troops east to attack Qi. The State of Qi sent troops led by Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to garrison at Lixia to fight against the Han army.
It happened that Li Shiqi, the envoy of the King of Han, came to Qi to persuade King Tian Guang of Qi, Prime Minister Tian Heng and the King of Han to jointly attack Chu.
Tian Heng agreed, so Lixia's defense was lifted, and the soldiers drank freely. Just as he was about to send an envoy to negotiate peace with the King of Han, Han Xin had already crossed the plain, defeated the Qi army stationed at Lixia, and entered Linmiao.
Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng believed that Li Sheng was conspiring with Han Xin, so they cooked Li Sheng.
Tian Guang fled eastward to Gaomi, Tian Heng fled to Bo County, Prime Minister Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji garrisoned in Jiaodong.
The state of Chu sent Long Qie to rescue the state of Qi. King Qi and Long Qie's army met at Gaomi.
The Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated the Chu army, killed Long Qie, and captured Qi King Tian Guang.
Han general Guan Ying chased and captured Qi's Prime Minister Tian Guang and came to Bo County.
When Tian Heng heard that King Qi was dead, he proclaimed himself king and returned to attack Guan Ying. Guan Ying defeated Tian Heng's army.
Tian Heng fled to Liangdi and joined Pengyue.
At this time, Peng Yue was stationed in Liangdi. He courted both Mo and Chu and remained neutral. After Han Xin killed Long Qie, he then marched into Jiaodong and killed Tian Ji.
Guan Ying defeated Qi general Tian Su and killed Tian Su in Qiancheng, so Han Xin pacified Qi. The Han Dynasty destroyed Xiang Ji, the king of Han established himself as emperor, and Peng Yue was named King of Liang.
Tian Heng was afraid of being killed, so he fled to the sea with more than 500 of his subordinates and lived on the island.
When Mo Gaozu Liu Bang heard the news, he thought that Brother Tian Heng had already pacified Qi, and many wise men of Qi had joined him. Now that he was living on the sea, if he did not recruit him, there might be trouble in the future, so he sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summon him.
Tian Heng declined politely and said: I cooked your Majesty's envoy Li Shiqi. I heard that his younger brother Li Shang is now a general of the Han army and a virtuous man. I am very worried, so I dare not follow the imperial edict. I hope to be an ordinary citizen and live on the island.
The messenger came back and reported to the emperor. Emperor Gaozu summoned Weiwei Li Shang and told him: King Tian Heng of Qi will come, and whoever dares to touch his subordinates will be punished with genocide!
So he sent an envoy with a talisman to tell Tian Heng the order given by Emperor Gaozu to Li Shang, and said: When Tian Heng comes, the older one will be made king and the younger one will be made marquis. If Tian Heng doesn't come, we will send troops to attack him.
Tian Heng then took two retainers to Luoyang in a carriage.
When they arrived at the place where horses were prepared for the post in Xixiang, Tian Heng said to the envoy: As a minister paying homage to the emperor, he should take a bath to purify himself.
So it stopped.
Tian Heng said to his disciples: At first, like the King of Han, I was a man facing south and proclaimed himself king. Now the King of Han has become the emperor. And I have become a prisoner of the subjugated country. It is really shameful to ask the north to surrender to him.
Besides, I cooked someone else's brother, but I have to serve the same master with that person's brother. Even if he is afraid of the emperor's edict and dare not touch me, don't I feel ashamed in my heart?
Moreover, the reason why His Majesty summoned me was just to see my face.
Your Majesty is in Luoyang. Now, cut off my head and run for thirty miles. My appearance will not be corrupted, and you can still see what I look like.
After saying that he would commit suicide, let the disciples hold his head and follow the messenger to report it to Emperor Gao as soon as possible.
Gao Di said: Alas, it is not simple!
Starting as common people, three brothers became kings one after another. They are really virtuous!
He shed tears for this, and appointed two of Tian Heng's disciples as captains, and sent 2,000 troops to bury Tian Heng with the etiquette of a prince.
After the burial, the two retainers dug a hole beside Tian Heng's tomb and committed suicide.
Emperor Gao was greatly surprised when he heard this. He thought that Tian Heng's retainers were all virtuous. He heard that there were still five hundred retainers on the island in the sea, and sent envoy Shao to order them to Luoyang. When the retainers heard that Tian Heng was dead, they all committed suicide.
From this we can see that Brother Tian Heng is indeed someone who can be supported by the wise men.
King Xin of Han is the grandson of the original King Xiang of Han. He is eight feet five inches tall.
When Xiang Liang established King Huai of Chu, Yan, Qi, Tang, and Wei had all proclaimed themselves kings before that. Only South Korea had no descendants, so he made the South Korean prince Hengyang Juncheng the King of Han, hoping to appease and stabilize South Korea.
After Xiang Liang died in Dingtao, Han Wangcheng defected to King Huai of Chu.
Pei Gong led troops to attack Yangcheng and sent Zhang Liang to occupy Korea as a Korean Situ. He found Xin and asked Xin to command the Korean troops and lead the army to follow Pei Gong to Wuguan.
Pei Gong became the king of Han, and Xin followed him into Hanzhong. Xin persuaded the king of Han, saying: King Xiang has divided the generals, but you are stationed here alone. Change your place.
The soldiers following you are all from Shandong, and they are all looking forward to going back. Once the desire to return eastward is strong, you can use this to fight for the world.
The King of Han returned to his army and pacified the San Qin area. He promised to make Xin the king in the future, and first worshiped him as the Taiwei of South Korea, and led his troops to occupy South Korea.
All the princes and kings entrusted by Xiang Ji returned to their respective states. Because King Cheng of Han did not go to war with the army and had no meritorious service, he was not sent to South Korea and was instead granted the title of Marquis of Zhou. Later, he was killed.
Hearing that the King of Han sent a letter to seize the land of Han, he appointed Zheng Chang, the magistrate of Wu County when he was in Wu County, as King of Han to fight against the King of Han's army.
In the second year of Mo, Xinping pacified more than ten cities in Han.
When the King of Han came to Henan, he rushed to attack Han Wangchang, and Han Wangchang surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Liu Bang, the king of Han, established his trust as the king of Han and asked him to always accompany him with Korean soldiers.
The king of Han asked Han Wangxin, Zhou Ke and others to garrison Rongyang. The city was captured by the Chu army, and Han Wangxin surrendered to the Chu army.
Soon he found an opportunity and fled back to Han. The king of Han named him King of Han. Finally, he followed the king of Han and defeated Xiang Ji.
In the spring of the fifth year, the King of Han cut his talisman with him, and he was in Ying!
For the King of Han. In the spring of the sixth year, the emperor thought that King Xin of Han was brave and brave. The territory he assigned was close to Gongxian and Luoyang in the north, Wanxian and Yexian in the south, and the important town of Huaiyang was in Shubian. These places were garrisoned by elite troops, so he gave Taiyuan County to South Korea, so that King Xin of Han could resist the barbarians and move the capital to Jinyang.
The King of Han wrote a letter saying: The country is close to the border, and the Huns have invaded many times, but Jinyang is far away from the border, so he requested to make Mayi the capital.
The emperor agreed to his request.
In the autumn of that year, the Huns leader Mao Dun led a large army to besiege Han Wangxin. Han Wangxin sent envoys many times to seek reconciliation with the Hu people.
The Han Dynasty sent reinforcements to rescue King Xin of Han, and suspected that King Xin of Han had second thoughts in sending envoys to privately sue for peace with the Xiongnu many times.
The emperor sent a letter to reproach Han Wangxin, saying: As a general, focusing on fighting to death is not considered brave, and focusing on survival is not qualified for military command. The enemy is besieging Mayi, can't you hold on to your troops?
Even in a dangerous situation, you must persist in loyalty and integrity. This is what I want to blame you for.
King Xin of Han received the letter and was afraid of being killed, so he agreed with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Mo, gave Mayi to the Hu people, surrendered to the Xiongnu, and sent troops to attack Taiyuan.
In the winter of the seventh year, the emperor personally led his army to defeat Han Wangxin in Tongqian and killed his general Wang Xi.
King Xin of Han fled to the Huns. His generals Manqiuchen and Wang Huang were from Baitu County. They made Tali, a descendant of Shitang from the Six Kingdoms, king. They also collected the remaining soldiers of King Xin of Han and colluded with King Xin and Maodun of Han to attack Han.
The Xiongnu sent the right and left wise kings to lead more than 10,000 cavalry and Wang Huang and others to station in the south of Guangwu. They went to Jinyang to fight the Han soldiers, but were defeated by the Han soldiers. They pursued them as far as Lishi, where they were defeated again by the Mo army.
The Huns gathered their troops northwest of Loufan again.
The Han army also sent chariots and horses to attack the Huns, often defeating them. The Han army took advantage of the victory and pursued them north.
After hearing the news that Mao Dun lived in Daigu, the emperor went to Jinyang in person, sent people to scout Mao Dun, and reported back that it was possible to attack.
The emperor then came to Pingcheng and climbed Baishan Mountain.
Unexpectedly, the emperor was surrounded by Huns cavalry, so the emperor sent people to send many valuable gifts to Ban, the wife of the Huns.
Que persuaded Mao Dun, saying: Now that we have acquired Han land, it is still uninhabitable. Moreover, when the two masters meet, they cannot force each other into an embarrassing situation.
After seven days of confrontation, the Hu cavalry retreated a little.
Heavy fog fell from the sky, and the Han army sent people to and fro, but the Hu people were not aware of it.
Chen Ping, the lieutenant of the guard, said to the emperor: The weapons of the Hu people are bows and spears. Please ask the soldiers to add two arrows to each strong crossbow, pointing outwards, and move slowly to highlight the encirclement.
When the emperor ran into Pingcheng, reinforcements from the Han Dynasty also arrived. The Xiongnu cavalry dispersed, and the Han Dynasty also withdrew its troops.
After that, Han Wangxin led the Huns soldiers to and from the border to attack the Han army, and also asked Wang Huang and others to persuade Chen Xi.
In the spring of the eleventh year, Han Wangxin and the Hu cavalry were stationed in Shenhe County.
The Han Dynasty sent General Chai to attack. General Chai first sent a letter to King Han saying: Your Majesty is generous and kind. Although some princes defected, after they surrendered, they immediately restored their previous titles and did not kill them.
You know this.
Now that you have fled to the barbarians because of the defeat, there is no big crime. I hope you can come and surrender as soon as possible.
King Han Xin reported back: Your Majesty promoted me from the alleys to the south and became king. This is my honor.
In the Battle of Rongyang, I did not die in the battle, but became Xiang Ji's prisoner. This was my first crime.
The Hu invaders attacked Mayi, but I failed to hold on, but surrendered the city as a gift to the enemy. This is the second charge.
Now I have become a rebel bandit, leading the army to fight to the death against you. This is the third charge.
The former doctors Wen Zhong and Fan Li had no sins, but they escaped with death; I had three sins, but I wanted to survive. This was the reason why Wu Zixu offended Fu Chai, did not know how to escape, and finally died in the state of Wu.
Now I have fled to the valley, begging from the barbarians day and night to survive. My desire to return is very strong, just like a paralyzed person who wants to stand up, and a blind man who longs to see the light again, but the situation does not allow me to do so.
So the two sides fought.
General Chai led his troops to loot Shenhe and killed King Xin of Han.
When Han Wangxin fled to the Huns, the prince was with him. When they arrived in the city of Dandang, Han Wangxin gave birth to another son, named Dandang.
Prince Han also gave birth to a boy, named Ying. By the time of Emperor Xiaowen, Dandang and Han Ying led their subordinates to surrender to the Han Dynasty.
In the Han Dynasty, Han Daidang was granted the title of Marquis of Gonggao, and Han Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangcheng.
When Wu and Chu rebelled, Gong Gaohou was the most successful general in quelling the rebellion.
His title was passed on to his son and grandson. Because his grandson had no descendants, he lost his title.
Han Ying's grandson also lost his position due to the crime of disrespect.
The decadent concubine Han Yan was favored and had a great reputation at that time.
Han Yan's younger brother, Han Yue, led troops to attack the Huns as a school captain and was named Longlinghou.
Later, he lost his position because of the crime of insufficient gold. He was granted the title of General Henghai as a waiting edict. He led his army to defeat Shu Yue and was granted the title of Yingdaohou.
During the Taichu period, he served as a guerrilla general stationed in a city outside Wuyuan. After returning, he was appointed Guang Luxun. He was killed by the prince for digging puppets in the palace of the prince.
His son Han Xing succeeded to the throne and was killed for committing witchcraft.
The emperor said: The guerrilla general died in state affairs, his loyalty is pitiable.
Although Han Xing was executed today for witchcraft, his younger brothers and clan should not be criticized.
So Han Xing's younger brother Han Zeng was granted the title of Long'ehou. Han Zeng was a man when he was young, and served as the official Guanglu of various Cao officials. He also served as a former general during the reign of Emperor Zhao. Because he and the general Huo Guang decided to support Emperor Xuan, he was granted the title of a thousand households in the city.
In the second year of Benshi, five generals attacked the Xiongnu. Han Zeng led 30,000 cavalry from the clouds, killed more than 100 Xiongnu, and returned as scheduled.
In the first year of Shenjue's reign, he replaced Zhang Anshi as the chief carriage and cavalry general, and also served as minister.
Han Zeng has been honored for generations and has been a loyal minister since he was a child. He served three masters successively and made contributions to the court.
He was tolerant and reserved, and he was kind and courteous to both the emperor and his subordinates. He made no mistakes and protected himself by being favored, but he had no achievements.
Wufeng died in the second year of his reign and was granted the title of Marquis of An.
His son Han Bao succeeded him. Han Bao had no sons and lost his kingdom.
When he became emperor, in order to ensure that the heroes would have successors, Han Cen, the son of Han Zeng's brother, was granted the title of Long'ehou. After his death, his son succeeded him with a bow.
After Wang Mang's defeat, he lost his title.
Zan said: The Zhou royal family has declined, and by the end of the Spring and Autumn Period, all the princes have been reduced, but there are still many descendants of Emperor Yan, Emperor Huang, Tang Yao, and Yu Shun.
Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, and the ancient sending industry no longer existed.
During the war between Chu and Han, heroes became kings one after another. Only the brothers Wei Bao, Han Wangxin, and Tian Dan were descendants of the Six Kingdoms, but by their generation they were all extinct.
Tian Heng's integrity and the spirit of pursuing morality among the guests could not lead to the establishment of the country. Isn't this God's will?

summary:
The histories of three prominent figures from the Six Kingdoms period: Wei Bao, Tian Dan, and Han Wangxin, detailing their rise, fall, and the fates of their descendants.

Wei Bao, son of the Wei state, saw his brother Wei Jiu made king by Chen Sheng after the Qin collapse. Wei Jiu later surrendered to Qin to save his people and committed suicide. Wei Bao fled to Chu, recaptured Wei lands with King Huai's aid, and was made King of Wei by Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu moved him to Hedong, Wei Bao initially surrendered to the Han king but later betrayed him, blocking the Yellow River. The Han king sent Han Xin to capture him, and Wei Bao was eventually killed at Rongyang by Zhou Ke, who deemed him untrustworthy.

Tian Dan, a member of the Qi royal clan, declared himself king after killing a county magistrate and expanding Qi's territory. He died in battle against Qin's Zhang Han while aiding Wei. His cousin Tian Rong later made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi king, but conflicts arose with Xiang Yu over allegiances. Tian Rong was killed, and his brother Tian Heng restored Qi, making Tian Rong's son Tian Guang king. Tian Heng ruled Qi for three years until Han Xin's invasion. After a series of battles, Tian Guang was captured, and Tian Heng fled to the sea with 500 followers. Summoned by Emperor Gaozu of Han, Tian Heng committed suicide near Luoyang out of shame, and his followers also died, demonstrating his virtue.

Han Wangxin, grandson of the original Han king, was made King of Han by Xiang Liang. He later followed the Han king, was captured by Chu, but escaped and was reinstated. After the Han dynasty was established, Emperor Gaozu moved him to Taiyuan to resist the Xiongnu. Suspected of treason for negotiating with the Xiongnu, Han Wangxin surrendered to them and attacked Han. The emperor personally campaigned against him, and after a siege at Pingcheng, the Xiongnu retreated. Han Wangxin continued raiding until he was killed by General Chai in Shenhe County. His descendants, including Han Dangdang and Han Ying, later surrendered to Han and were granted titles, with some serving as generals and officials through subsequent reigns.

The text concludes with a reflection that while Wei Bao, Tian Dan, and Han Wangxin were descendants of the Six Kingdoms, their lineages ended. Tian Heng's integrity and his followers' loyalty did not lead to a lasting state, suggesting divine will. The Han family's resurgence through the Marquis of Gonggao is noted as possibly linked to ancient lineage.

The scripture says: The first is the five elements.
Five elements: first is water, second is fire, third is wood, fourth is gold, and fifth is earth.
The natural nature of water is that it can moisten downwards, the natural nature of fire is that it can burn upward, the natural nature of wood is that it can be bent or straight, the natural nature of gold is that it can change its shape and be melted and smelted, and the natural nature of earth is that it can be cultivated and harvested.
It is said in the legend: Those who do not follow the prescribed time when hunting, do not enjoy the gifts when drinking and eating, go out to fight without restraint, occupy the time for farming, and have evil plots, will lose the ability to be straight or straight.
Explained: Wood represents the east.

For the king's affairs, the majesty, appearance, voice and smile also need to pay attention to the effect of observation.

Ai Jia, this is a symbol of war.

It rains normally.

Confucius said: If the accumulation of secret slanders or rumors does not allow it to succeed, then it can be said that it is upright.

"Spring and Autumn" records that in August of the 14th year of Duke Huan, a fire broke out in the palace granary in Renshen.
Dong Zhongshu believed that the four countries had previously conquered the Lu State together and defeated the Lu State in the battle of Longmen.
The injured people of Lu State had not recovered, and their resentment had not yet recovered. The ministers despised this kind of scandal, so there were successive floods that year and the next year.
Liu Xin believed that before this, Lu Yangong decorated the ancestral temple, carved rafters, painted pillars, and painted red vermilion to show off to his wife, but he was disrespectful to the ancestral temple rituals, so he was severely punished by the Emperor of Heaven.
In the tenth year of Xuangong's reign, there were floods in autumn and famine occurred.
Dong Zhongshu believed that this was due to the frequent conquests of the Lu State at that time and the capture of the city, and the counterattacks and retaliations at the same time. As a result, war disasters continued, and the people were worried and resentful.
Liu Xiang believed that it was Lu Xuan Gong who killed Zi Chi and established himself as king. Zichi was born to the daughter of the Jiang family of Qi State, so he was afraid of being punished by Qi State, so he gave the land in Jixi to Qi State.
The son of Zhu was also born to a woman from the state of Qi. Now Duke Xuan was at war with the state of Zhu. The subjects were all worried that the strong state of Qi would punish the state of Lu for harming the state of Zhu. For this reason, they all despised or dissatisfied the Duke of Xuan for acting unfairly.
This is what caused the flood. In the autumn of the fifth year of Chenggong's reign, there was a flood.
Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang believe that at that time, Duke Cheng was still young and weak, and the government was in charge of the government. Before that, he had used troops to fight twice a year. In the second year, Pic City was built to strengthen private power. Zhongsun Mi and Shusun Qiaoru made an alliance with the Song and Jin countries without authorization. The yin energy prevailed over the yang energy, which led to the flood. In the autumn of the twenty-fourth year of Duke Xiang, there was a flood.
Dong Zhongshu believes that the year before, Qi State conquered Jin State, and Lu Xianggong sent officials to lead the army to rescue Jin State. Later, he invaded Qi State. Although his country was small and weak, it made enemies of powerful countries many times. The people were worried and resentful about this, and the Yin Qi was too strong and caused this flood.
Liu Xiang believed that before this, Lu Xianggong bullied his neighboring countries, which caused Zhu to attack from the south, Qi to attack from the north, and Ju to attack from Shumian. The people of Lu State were in a state of turmoil. But later, he invaded the powerful Qi state many times, causing a flood.
Floods flooded the crops, causing famine and grain failure. The disaster was very serious.
In the summer of the third year of Gaohou, a flood occurred in Hanzhong and Nanjun, flooding more than 4,000 people.
In the autumn of the fourth year, there was a flood in Henan. The Yi and Luo rivers overflowed, submerging more than 1,600 people, and the Ru River overflowed, submerging more than 800 people.
In the summer of the eighth year, another flood occurred in Hanzhong and Nanjun, flooding more than 6,000 people.
The Mianshui River in Nanyang flooded and more than 10,000 people were flooded.
At that time, the heroine, the Lu family, was in charge of the government, and all the Lu family members were granted the title of King Ya.
In the autumn of the third year after Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty, it rained heavily day and night for thirty-five consecutive days.
Flash floods broke out in Lantian, destroying more than 900 buildings.
The Han River flooded, destroying more than 8,000 houses and killing more than 300 people.
Prior to this, Xinyuan Qiangui, a traveler who could see the clouds and know the feng shui, was favored by the emperor, so he built the Five Emperors Temple on the north side of the Weishui River for Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty. If he wanted the Zhou Ding to reappear, he would have to hold a suburban sacrifice to pay homage to the Emperor of Heaven in April in the summer.
After going on for more than a year, the scam was exposed. Fearing that he would be executed, he conspired to rebel. When he was discovered, he was beheaded to death and the three tribes were annihilated.
At that time, the princess was sent several times to marry the Xiongnu Chanyu, and the gifts were also generous. However, the Xiongnu became more and more arrogant, often invading the northern border, and killing more than 10,000 people. For this reason, the Han Dynasty continuously sent troops to conquer the Xiongnu to defend the border.
In the fifth year of Emperor Yongguang's reign in the Han Dynasty, major floods occurred in the summer and autumn.
Heavy rains fell in Yingchuan, Runan, Huaiyang, and Lujiang River, destroying urban and rural houses and drowning many people in floods.
In the previous year, relevant officials petitioned to cancel the ancestral temples in various counties. This year, they also stipulated the replacement and abolishment of ancestral temples. The dormitory temples of Emperor Taishang and Emperor Xiaohui were abolished and will not be repaired. Mr. Bolu, who is well versed in Confucianism, believes that this violates ancient etiquette.
The eunuch Shi Xian took charge of the affairs.
In the summer of the third year after the founding of Emperor Cheng, there was a flood. Heavy rains continued for more than 30 days in Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng in the Chang'an area. It rained for 19 days in various counties and feudal states. Flash floods broke out, drowning more than 4,000 people in total, and destroying more than 83,000 official and civilian buildings.
In the first year of Jianshi, relevant officials petitioned to move the Taishi Temple in Ganquan and the Houtu Temple in Hedong to the southern and northern suburbs of Chang'an City respectively.
In the second year of its founding, the Five Seasons Temple in Yongdi and various old shrines in local counties were abolished, a total of six places.

Liu Xin believed Fu Xi received the "River Map" and created the Bagua, while Dayu received the "Luo Shu" and formed the "Hong Fan." After the Zhou dynasty defeated the Yin, King Wu consulted Jizi, who explained that God gave Dayu nine chapters of "Hongfan," which established the order of heaven, earth, and people. The text lists nine categories, including the Five Elements, Five Affairs, Eight Policies, and others, totaling sixty-five words that constitute the "Luo Shu." Liu Xin viewed the "He Tu" and "Luo Shu" as complementary, with the Bagua and Jiu Zhang as their expressions. The text traces the study of these principles through King Wen, Confucius, and later scholars like Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xin, culminating in the "Five Elements Chronicle," which records twelve dynasties up to Wang Mang's usurpation.

The first element, Wood, is associated with the east and represents the ability to be bent or straight. The text explains that improper hunting, feasting, and military campaigns disrupt wood's nature, leading to strange phenomena like wood ice. Liu Xin attributed wood ice to blocked yang and yin qi, while Liu Xiang linked it to excessive yin threatening noble ministers. Examples from the "Spring and Autumn" include rain and wood ice in the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng of Lu, interpreted as a sign of noblemen's troubles or military conflict.

Fire, the second element, represents the south and brilliance. Proper governance, including selecting wise officials and distinguishing virtue, allows fire to maintain its nature. Neglecting morality and allowing slander leads to fires that damage ancestral temples and palaces. The text cites numerous fires from the "Spring and Autumn," such as the palace granary fire in the fourteenth year of Duke Huan, interpreted by Dong Zhongshu as a warning against laziness and by Liu Xiang as a sign of the wife's rebellious heart. Other fires include those in Qi, the West Palace, Luoyang's Xuanxie, and the newly completed palace in Lu, each linked to political misdeeds like usurpation, improper marriages, or neglect of rituals.

Earth, the third element, is central and foundational for growth. Proper governance involves modest palaces, regulated marriages, and respect for relatives. Extravagance and promiscuity cause earth to lose its nature, leading to poor harvests. The text cites the death of wheat seedlings in the twenty-eighth year of Duke Yan of Lu, attributed by Dong Zhongshu to the wife's obscenity and by Liu Xiang to the construction of pavilions and immoral behavior.

Metal, the fourth element, represents the west and is associated with military campaigns. Proper use involves timely warfare and respect for life. Arrogance and disregard for the people cause metal to lose its properties, leading to strange events like speaking stones. The text references stones speaking in Jin during the eighth year of Duke Zhao, interpreted by Shi Kuang as a sign of exhausted people's power due to excessive palace construction. A similar event in the Han dynasty involved a large stone crying in Tianshui, linked to rebellions and the construction of Changling mausoleum.

Water, the fifth element, represents the north and is associated with ancestral rituals and proper governance. Neglecting sacrifices and issuing contrary orders cause water to lose its nature, leading to floods and continuous rains. The text lists numerous floods from the "Spring and Autumn" and Han dynasty, such as those in the first year of Duke Huan of Lu, attributed to the killing of Duke Yin and subsequent conflicts. Other floods are linked to scandals, improper marriages, and military campaigns. In the Han dynasty, floods occurred during the reigns of Gaohou, Emperor Wen, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Cheng, often tied to political turmoil, such as the Lu family's power, Xiongnu invasions, or the abolition of ancestral temples.

Humans imitate the shapes of heaven and earth, possess the five constant natures of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faith. They are intelligent, sensible, meticulous, and simple. They are the most spiritual among living animals.
Human hands and feet are not enough to provide for hobbies and desires, running is not enough to avoid harm, and there are no furs and feathers to protect against cold and heat. Therefore, humans must use all things to feed themselves. They use wisdom instead of relying on force. This is the reason why humans are noble.
Therefore, if people are not benevolent, they cannot form a group. If they cannot form a group, they cannot defeat external objects. If they cannot defeat external objects, their offerings will not be sufficient.
If a group is formed but the material is still not sufficient, the mentality of competition will arise. The saints of the previous generation deliberately took the lead in emphasizing the morality of respect, humility and charity, and the people were happy and followed them.
When the people who follow them form a group, they become monarchs; when everyone vie to join them, they become kings. "Shang Shu.
"Hong Fan" said: The emperor becomes the parents of the people and the emperor of the world.
The saints choose similar titles to rectify their status and call the king their parents. They understand that benevolence and humility are the foundation of kingship.
Benevolence will not be corrupted if it relies on reverence, and kindness must be majestic to survive for a long time. Therefore, etiquette is formulated to promote reverence, and criminal laws are formulated to show majesty.
Since the sage himself has the character of discernment, he must be familiar with the thoughts of heaven and earth, formulate rituals and education, establish legal systems and set up criminal laws, and always comply with the people's sentiments, so that he can manage the earth according to the laws of heaven.
Therefore, it is said that the previous kings established the ritual system based on the gods from heaven. According to the nature of the earth.
Prisons of punishment and majesty are used to imitate the killing power of God with thunder and lightning; gentleness, kindness, generosity and harmony are used to imitate God's ability to grow and nourish all things.
"Shangshu" says that Heaven rewards polite people according to their rank, and Heaven punishes sinful people.
Therefore, the sages formulated the five rites of good fortune, misfortune, military service, military affairs, and good fortune according to the order of heaven, and formulated the five punishments according to the principle of punishment from heaven.
For large punishments, armor is used, for lighter punishments, axes and irons are used; for medium punishments, knives and saws are used, for lighter punishments, drills are used; for small punishments, whips are used.
Large-scale punishments required the corpses to be displayed in the plains and wilderness, while small-scale punishments required public display in the streets and courts. This situation has a long history.
Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Battle of Zhuolu put down the Yandi Rebellion, and during the Zhuanxu Period, the Battle of Gonggong put down the Gonggong Rebellion.
During the reign of Tang Yu, he was able to bring peace to the world by offering sacrifices, and he still exiled Gonggong, banished Huandou, expelled Sanmiao, and killed Gun, and then the world surrendered.
In the Xia Dynasty, Youqi and the Youhu clan fought in Gan, and it was not until the Yin and Zhou dynasties that they used military force to pacify the world.
After the world was stabilized, weapons were collected and educated with etiquette and morality. However, the official position of Sima was also established, six armies were set up, mine fields were divided, and military taxes were formulated.
One mile of land area is divided into one well, ten wells form one link, ten links form one tenth, one tenth has a square of ten miles; ten points form one end, ten ends form one, and one has a hundred miles square; ten together form a seal, ten seals form a ji, and a ji has a thousand miles square.
If you have land to rent, you have to pay for soldiers.
Land is rented to meet food needs, and military taxes are used to meet military needs.
Therefore, four wells form a town, and four towns form a hill.
Qiu is the sixteen wells. There is one military horse and three oxen.
Four hills form a meadow.
There are sixty-four wells in Yidian, four military horses, one military chariot, twelve oxen, three soldiers, seventy-two soldiers, and weapons. The method of cultivating is called horse riding.
There are hundreds of miles together, with a total of ten thousand wells. Excluding mountains, rivers, salty land, water depressions, cities, villages, and gardens and avenues, there are a total of 3,600 wells, 6,400 wells required to pay military taxes, 400 military horses, and 100 military chariots. This is the largest among the official lands of Qing officials, and is called the House of Hundreds of Vehicles.
One letter is 316 miles long, with a total of 100,000 wells, of which 64,000 wells are required to pay military tribute, 4,000 soldiers and horses, and 1,000 chariots. This is the largest among the princes, and is called the Kingdom of Thousand Chariots.
The emperor's royal territory is thousands of miles square, with a million wells in total, 640,000 wells required to pay military tribute, 40,000 soldiers and horses, and 10,000 chariots, so he is called the Lord of Ten Thousand Chariots.
The soldiers and carriage drivers were always well prepared with weapons. They hunted in the spring to reorganize the troops, pulled weeds in the summer to repair the camp, trained and hunted in the autumn, and conducted a grand review of the army during the hunting in the winter. They all gave lectures and training during the farming season.
The five feudal states are one genus, and each vassal has an officer; the ten feudal states are one company, and each company has a commander; the thirty kingdoms are one pawn, and each pawn has an official; the two hundred and ten kingdoms are one state, and each state has a pastoral officer.
Liangong and commander-in-chief review military vehicles every year, junior officers and principal officers review personnel every three years, and Qunmu inspect military vehicles and personnel on a large scale every five years. This was the late king's general policy to build up the country's armed forces and enrich its military strength.
After the kingship of the Zhou Dynasty declined and the legal system was destroyed, it was not until Duke Huan of Qi appointed Guan Zhong that the country became prosperous and the people became stable.
Duke Huan of Qi asked about the method of using troops to achieve hegemony. Guan Zhong replied: If you want to stabilize the army and improve the armaments, big countries will do the same. But if a small country wants to build armaments to control the enemy, it will be difficult to achieve the goal quickly.
Therefore, we relied on the formulation of internal affairs to rectify the military laws and regulations. Therefore, the soldier system was established in the lizhong, and the military affairs were completed in the governance of the feudal towns.
If ten or five people are connected together, they can live together and share joys, share sorrows and sorrows, and share blessings and misfortunes. Therefore, when fighting at night, they can hear each other's voices, and when fighting during the day, they can see each other. In times of crisis, they are enough to die for each other.
The formation of this kind of education eliminated the intrusion of Yi and Di externally, respected the emperor internally, and stabilized the domestic princes.
After the fall of Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Wen of Jin succeeded him. He also first stabilized his people, formulated the law of being imprisoned, commanded the princes, and succeeded him as the leader of the alliance.
However, his etiquette system has gone beyond the bounds of duty and made many mistakes, and he always acted in discord in order to seek quick success and quick gain, so it cannot be regarded as the legal system of the former king.
After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, it gradually declined. By the time of Duke Cheng of Lu, a decree was made to make the hilly areas pay land tax. Duke Ai also assigned a tax to each of the land and family property. Things such as hunting, managing the army, and grand military parades all lost their orthodoxy.
"Spring and Autumn" recorded this and criticized it in order to preserve the royal way.
After that, wars broke out many times, and the people were weak and exhausted, and they lost the sense of sacrifice and sacrifice.
Confucius felt sad about this and said: To fight with untrained people is to abandon them.
Therefore, he praised Zilu and said: Zhong Yuan, when you go to a country with a thousand military chariots, you can put him in charge of the army.
Zilu also said: A country with a thousand chariots is sandwiched between several big countries. It is invaded by armies outside and famine inside. I will govern it. After three years, everyone will have courage and understand the truth.
This means that in managing taxes and the army, etiquette and righteousness must also be taught.
After the Spring and Autumn Period, weak countries were annexed and merged to form the Warring States Period. Some martial arts etiquette was slightly added as a game for fun and to show off to each other.
During the Qin Dynasty, it was renamed "Jiao Da". The etiquette of the previous kings was drowned in unrighteous music. Extraordinary and outstanding people assisted the situation according to the current situation. They used cunning and cunning to compete with each other. Wu had Sun Wu, Qi had Sun Bin, Wei had Wu Qi, and Qin had Shang Yang.
At this time, they joined forces vertically and horizontally, and turned to attack each other, competing for hegemony.
King Min of Qi became strong with the martial arts of Qi, King Hui of Wei worked hard with the soldiers of Wei, and King Zhao of Qin won with the sharp soldiers of Qin.
The secular world is fighting for utilitarianism, and the lobbyists regard Sun Bin and Wu Qi as the objects of respect.
At that time, Sun Qing was the only one who understood the royal way, so he criticized this situation and said: People like Sun Bin and Wu Qi advocate power and wealth and value cunning and cunning; when applied to a country that is violent, chaotic, ignorant and careless, it creates a gap between the monarch and his ministers, disunity between the superiors and subordinates, and poor political planning, so they can be cunning and cunning.
Those who are kind above are admired by those below, just like sons and brothers guarding their father and brothers, hands and feet guarding the brain and eyes. What can be compared with them?
Neighboring countries look at us from a distance, as happy as relatives, as fragrant as pepper orchid. Looking back at their king, it is like seeing fire in the eyes of enemies.
Is it human nature to be willing to attack what he likes for the sake of what he hates?
Therefore, using Jie to attack Jie can still be opportunistic; using Jie to deceive Yao is like using an egg to touch a stone, there is no chance of luck!
"Poetry" says: King Wu holds the flag and holds the weapon religiously, as fierce as fire, no one dares to stop us.
It is said that those who appease the people with benevolence and righteousness will be invincible in the world.
For example, Qi State competed in fencing skills, and received a bounty for each head.
If the military scale is small and the enemy is weak, this technique can be used. If the military scale is huge and the enemy is strong, it will be dispersed.
This is the army of a subjugated nation.
The Wei family used armed soldiers, wearing three layers of bell armor, wielding twelve-stone crossbows, carrying fifty arrows, putting their swords on top of their luggage, wearing helmets and carrying swords, carrying three days of food, and traveled hundreds of miles in one day. If he passed the exam, he would be exempted from taxes and given the benefits of land and housing.
If this is the case, then although their country's land is vast, their tax revenue must be very small, and their human strength will weaken after a few years.
This is an army that endangers the country.
The people of Qin were very narrow-minded in their education, but cruel and violent in their service.
He uses power to threaten the people, tortures them with poverty, makes them greedy for rewards, and uses punishment to guide the people, so that his people will be rewarded for their merits and will have no other way out if they don't go to war.
Merits and rewards increase mutually. Those who can get the heads of five people wearing bell armor can enslave five families. This is the most efficient, so it can take four generations to dominate the world.
However, the army is all seeking rewards and pursuing profits. It is a way for mediocre people to do business, but there is no stable system to maintain integrity.
Therefore, even if the land is vast and the army is strong, he is always afraid that the world will work together to suppress him.
As for the armies of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, it can be said that they were restrained to a certain extent, but they still did not follow the principles of benevolence and righteousness.
Therefore, Qi's method of stabbing cannot be used to withstand Wei's armed soldiers. Wei's armed soldiers cannot withstand Qin's elite soldiers. Qin's elite soldiers cannot be compared with the temperate troops of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin. The temperate troops of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin cannot compete with the benevolent and righteous troops of King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou.
Therefore it is said: Those who are good at commanding an army do not set up formations; those who are good at setting up formations do not fight; those who are good at fighting will not fail; those who are good at losing will not perish.
As for Shun's administration of hundreds of officials, he appointed Jiu Yao as the official in charge of justice and told him that the barbarians were disrupting China and were a group of people who looted and killed and committed crimes, and the criminal law had no effect. This means that those who are good at commanding the army do not need to form formations.
King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou went on an expedition and arranged their armies for mobilization before the war. Jie and Zhou were captured, which meant that those who were good at arranging formations did not fight.
Duke Huan of Qi conquered the powerful Chu State in the south and made it pay tribute to the Zhou Dynasty. He also attacked the Shanrong in the north and served as a vanguard for the Yan State.
King Zhao of Chu suffered from the disaster of the Lanlu war, the country was destroyed, the king went into exile, and the people came to see him off.
King Chu Zhao said: Go back!
Why worry about not having a monarch?
The people said: How can there be such a wise monarch?
and followed him together.
Some people ran to Qin, crying and asking for help, and Qin sent troops for them.
The two countries worked together to drive away the Wu army, and King Zhao of Chu returned to Chu. This means that those who are good at failure will not perish.
For example, the Qin State relied on the victory of the fourth generation to occupy the dangerous locations of the Yellow River and the mountains. It used wolves like Bai Qi and Wang Jian and their followers to conquer the six kingdoms and annex the world.
After exhausting force and treachery, neither the sergeants nor the people surrendered. The soldiers who served became slaves and became enemies, rising like strong winds, gathering like clouds, and finally overthrowing it together.
This is the most base strategy of using troops.
The army is used to resurrect a destroyed country, to reconnect the cutoff descendants, to save troubles and eradicate scourges.
Therefore, the descendants of generals like Yi Yin and Lu Wang had their own countries, and they shared the rise and fall of the Shang and Zhou dynasties.
In their last generation, they used cunning techniques at will, took pleasure in greed and cruelty, and filled the city with murder for the fight for the city, and filled the wilderness with the murder for the fight for the land.
Sun Bin, Wu Qi, Shang Yang, Bai Qi and others were all killed first, and their countries perished later.
The trend of retribution comes according to their categories, and this is their fate.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Gaozu himself was endowed with divine power, behaved generously and kindly, led heroes and heroines, and killed King Qin and Xiang Yu.
Adopt Xiao He and Cao Shen's literary governance, use Zhang Liang and Chen Ping's strategies, give full play to the eloquence of Lu Mai and Li Sheng, show the etiquette of Shusun Tong, and cooperate with each other in civil and military ways, and the general policy is complete.
After the world was stabilized, officials were set up in prefectures and counties according to the Qin State, and the northern and southern armies were stationed in the capital.
When Emperor Wu conquered Baiyue, seven more schools were established inside, and warships were built outside. They taught drills every season every year, and the armaments were managed.
In the reign of Emperor Yuan, according to Gong Yu's suggestion, the game of jiaodian was abolished, but there was no correct strategy for managing the army and reviving military morale.
The ancients once said: There are five natures in nature: metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. Human beings use them all. It is impossible to remove any of them. Who can remove the army?
When governing a family, whipping cannot be abandoned, when governing a country, punishment cannot be abolished, and when conquests cannot be eliminated from the world, when using them, one must distinguish the root from the bottom, and when implementing them, there must be adversity and smoothness.
Confucius said: If a craftsman wants to do things well, he must first make his tools sharp.
Wende is the sharp weapon of the emperor; power is the auxiliary of Wende.
If the influence of etiquette and music is deep, then force can make more people obey; if the scope of morality is wide, then the area controlled by prestige will be large.
The three generations were so strong that they reached the point where the army was stopped by punishment. They were not in order. This was the ultimate achievement of the emperor.
In the laws of the previous Zhou Dynasty, three categories of criminal laws, light, medium and heavy, were established to regulate the country and punish various ethnic groups: one is to punish new countries with light laws; the other is to punish peaceful and conservative countries with medium laws; the third is to punish disorderly countries with heavy laws.
Among the five punishments, there are 500 kinds of black punishment, 500 kinds of torture, 500 kinds of castration, 500 kinds of mutilation, and 500 kinds of death penalty. These are the so-called medium punishments used by the state to punish peace and prosperity.
Those who committed murder were beheaded in the market. Those who were tortured were asked to guard the city gates. Those who were tortured were asked to guard the gates. Those who were tortured were asked to guard the palaces. Those who were cut off were asked to guard the gardens. Those who had been shaved off after the punishment were asked to guard the accumulated supplies.
Among those slaves, the men were brought into the government as slaves, and the women were taken into the government to work as laborers in pounding rice and cooking.
Anyone with a title, as well as children over seventy years old and those who have not yet lost their teeth at seven years old, are not allowed to be slaves in the government.
After the decline of the Zhou Dynasty, King Mu became angry and indulged, and asked Fuhou to formulate criminal laws according to the times to punish the world.
There are one thousand clauses for the punishment of ink punishment, one thousand clauses for the punishment of shackles, five hundred clauses for the punishment of hip punishment, three hundred clauses for the punishment of castration, and two hundred clauses for the punishment of death.
There are a total of 3,000 items for the five punishments, which are more than the 500 items for the medium punishment in peaceful countries. The pursuit is the so-called heavy punishment for countries that control unrest.
During the Spring and Autumn Period, the royal way was gradually destroyed, and political and religious customs were not popularized. When Zichan was the Prime Minister of Zheng, he cast criminal laws on the tripod.
Uncle Xiang of Jin Dynasty accused him and said: In the past, the king first discussed the circumstances of the crime and then determined the crime.
We do not formulate criminal laws because we are afraid that people will have fighting thoughts, so we still cannot prohibit and defend them, so we use morality to prevent them, decrees to supervise, etiquette to demonstrate, integrity to maintain integrity, and benevolence to educate; we enact official and salary status to encourage them to obey, and severely sentence criminals to make them afraid of indulgence.
I am afraid that I will not achieve the goal, so I teach them with loyalty, reward them according to their behavior, teach them with current affairs, use them gently, face them seriously, monitor them with strong force, and sentence them decisively.
In this way, we should also seek princes with extraordinary moral intelligence, officials with insight, loyal and trustworthy elders, and teachers who are kind and kind.
In this way, the people can obey the orders and there will be no disasters or disturbances.
If the people know that there are criminal laws, they will not be afraid of their superiors. If they want to argue, they will seek proof in the criminal code. If they are lucky enough to evade the criminal laws, they will not be able to govern.
The Xia Dynasty established the Yu punishment for those who violated government orders, the Shang Dynasty established the Tang punishment for those who violated government orders, and the Zhou Dynasty established the Nine punishments for those who violated government orders.
The rise of the three generations of criminal law occurred at the end of each generation.
Now that you are governing the state of Zheng, it will be very difficult for you to refer to the criminal laws of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties and cast the criminal laws on the tripod to govern the people!
"Poetry" says: According to King Wen's practice of teaching with virtue, then there will be peace in all directions every day. It also says: If the punishment is like King Wen, then all nations will obey in good faith. In this case, why make criminal laws?
When the people know about the disputes, they will give up etiquette and justice and go to the criminal documents for proof.
Trying to fight for every little thing like the tip of a cone will make the cases of confusion more numerous, and bribery will occur simultaneously.
I am afraid that the state of Zheng will decline while you are alive!
Zichan wrote back and said: According to what you said, Gongsun Qiao has no talent and cannot consider his descendants. I only use this to save the present generation.
Frivolous politics started to spread from here.
Confucius felt sad about this, and said: Use morality to induce them, use rituals to rectify them, and the people will not only have a sense of integrity, but also have people's hearts submissive; use decrees to induce them, use punishments to rectify them, and the people will only be temporarily exempted from sins, but they will not have a sense of shame. If the system of rituals and music does not rise, punishments will not be appropriate; if punishments are not appropriate, the people will not even know where to bind their hands and feet.
Meng appointed Yangfu as a military officer, and he asked Zengzi for advice. Zengzi replied: If the people in high positions fail to regulate things, the people will have long since abandoned their moral principles.

The text discusses the evolution of criminal law from ancient times. The Zhou Dynasty established three categories of laws—light, medium, and heavy—with specific punishments for different crimes. After the Zhou decline, King Mu expanded the penal code to 3,000 items. During the Spring and Autumn period, Zichan of Zheng cast criminal laws on a tripod, drawing criticism from Jin's Shuxiang, who argued that public knowledge of laws would lead to disputes and decline. Confucius emphasized moral guidance over legal coercion. The Warring States period saw harsh laws under Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, culminating in Qin Shihuang's oppressive regime, which led to widespread rebellion. The Han Dynasty initially simplified laws under Gaozu, but later emperors like Xiaowen and Xiaojing reformed punishments, abolishing corporal punishment and reducing flogging. Despite these efforts, legal complexity grew, and by Emperor Wu's reign, laws became increasingly strict, with over 13,000 capital offenses. Emperor Xuan and Emperor Yuan attempted to simplify laws, but reforms were incomplete.

The text further examines the Han Dynasty's legal reforms and their shortcomings. Emperor Xiaowen abolished the law of arresting innocent relatives, but later reinstated it for certain crimes. The Zhou system of five hearings, eight discussions, and three pardons aimed for fairness, but Han officials often failed to implement these principles. Emperors issued edicts to protect the elderly, young, and disabled from harsh punishments. Despite these efforts, the number of lawsuits and executions remained high, with over 10,000 deaths annually. The root causes included lack of moral education, unclear laws, poverty, and corruption. Confucius noted that ancient judges sought to save lives, while modern ones sought to kill. The text concludes that the Han Dynasty's legal system, though improved, still fell short of ancient ideals. Xunzi argued that punishments should match crimes, and that heavy penalties are necessary in peaceful times to deter evil. The author suggests restoring ancient corporal punishments and simplifying laws to achieve harmony, as seen in the prosperous reigns of Cheng and Kang.

It then references the *Book of Changes* and *Shang Shu*, noting that during Yao's time, a flood submerged mountains and hills, isolating the world into twelve states. Dayu was sent to control the floods, and afterward, the regional system was changed to Kyushu, divided into five services, with tribute determined by land quality.

The text details the geography, soil, fields, tribute, and waterways of each of the nine provinces: Jizhou, Yanzhou, Qingzhou, Xuzhou, Yangzhou, Jingzhou, Yuzhou, Liangzhou, and Yongzhou. For each province, it describes the soil type, land grade, tribute items, and river routes for transportation. For example, Jizhou has white soil and first-grade tribute, while Yangzhou has moist mud soil and ninth-grade fields. The text also mentions the opening of mountains and dredging of rivers, such as the Yellow River being dredged from Jishi Mountain to Longmen Mountain.

After the pacification of Kyushu, the land became habitable, and the nine rivers were dredged. Taxes were levied based on land quality, and the area around the royal city was divided into five zones: Dianfu, Houfu, Suifu, Yaofu, and Huangfu, each with specific tribute requirements. The text then describes the succession of dynasties: Yao gave Dayu a black jade, Dayu became emperor as the Xiahou clan, the Shang inherited the Xia system, and the Zhou modified it, merging Xuzhou and Liangzhou into Yongzhou and Qingzhou and dividing Jizhou into Youzhou and Bingzhou.

The *Book of Rites of Zhou* describes the official Fang, who governed the land of the world and all countries in Kyushu. The text then lists the characteristics of each province, including mountains, lakes, rivers, irrigation canals, products, population ratios, and suitable livestock and grains. For instance, Yangzhou has Kuaiji Mountain, Juqu Lake, and Sanjiang River, with a population ratio of two men to five women, and is suitable for raising birds and animals and growing rice.

The Zhou Dynasty had five levels of nobility but only three levels of land enfeoffment: dukes and marquises with a hundred miles, counts with seventy miles, and sons and barons with fifty miles. There were about 1,800 small countries. After the Zhou Dynasty declined, the states were annexed and eliminated, leaving only dozens by the Spring and Autumn Period, with five hegemons. During the Warring States Period, the world was divided into seven countries, which were later unified by Qin. Qin, believing the Zhou's decline was due to enfeoffment, divided the world into counties and commanderies, eliminating the descendants of previous sages.

The Han Dynasty followed the Qin system but later expanded its territory under Emperor Wu, establishing Jiaoxu Prefecture in the south and Shuofang Prefecture in the north. A detailed census and geographical record of numerous commanderies and kingdoms in ancient China, primarily during the Han dynasty and the Xin dynasty of Wang Mang. It lists the administrative divisions, their populations, and notable geographical features such as rivers, mountains, and lakes. For each commandery, the text provides the number of households and total population, followed by a list of its constituent counties. Many entries include the name changes implemented during Wang Mang's reign. For example, Wudu County was established in the sixth year of Emperor Yuanding's reign and was called Leping County under Wang Mang, with 51,376 households and a population of 235,560. Similarly, Longxi County, established during the Qin dynasty, was renamed Yanrong County by Wang Mang, with 53,964 households and 236,824 people.

The text also records the origins and courses of major rivers. The Shuhan River, which receives water from the Didao River, is also called Mianshui and flows into the Yangtze River. The Ju River originates from the East Wolf Valley and flows into the Yangtze River, passing through five counties. The Yellow River is described as flowing outside the Great Wall, then northeast into it, and eventually into the sea in Zhangwu County, passing through 16 counties. The text notes the presence of iron and salt officials in certain commanderies, such as Longxi County, and mentions specific mountains like Jishi Mountain in Heguan County and Xiqing Mountain in Lintao County.

The summary continues with similar entries for many other commanderies, including Tianshui, Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang, each with their own population figures and county lists. For instance, Tianshui County had 63,700 households and 261,348 people, while Wuwei County had 17,581 households and 76,419 people. The text also details the administrative structure, noting the presence of various Duwei (military commanders) governing specific barriers or regions, such as the Northern Duwei governing the Shenquan barrier in Fuping County. The document covers a vast geographical area, from the western frontier commanderies like Dunhuang, which was established from Jiuquan County and had 11,200 households, to the eastern commanderies like Liaoxi, which had 72,654 households.

The text further records commanderies in the northern and central regions, such as Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, and Dingxiang, each with their own population data and county lists. For example, Shuofang County had 34,338 households and 136,628 people. A comprehensive system of Chinese astronomy, detailing 118 star officials governing 783 stars, which serve as celestial signs for states, officials, and events. Celestial phenomena—including the movements of the five planets (Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, Venus, Mercury), comets, meteors, solar and lunar eclipses, halos, and atmospheric changes—are manifestations of yin and yang, reflecting earthly governance. A wise ruler responds to these signs by correcting policies to avert disasters.

The celestial sphere is divided into palaces. The Purple Palace (central) contains the Tianji star (residence of Taiyi, the Heavenly Emperor), surrounded by stars representing the emperor’s sons, concubines, and vassals. The Big Dipper governs the seasons and calendar, with its handle indicating directions. Other asterisms include the Wenchang Palace (officials), the Three Energy Stars (harmony of ruler and ministers), and stars associated with prisons, warfare, and agriculture. The Eastern Palace (Canglong) includes the Heart (emperor’s hall) and Room (heavenly mansion), with stars predicting disease, war, and harvests. The Southern Palace (Red Bird) features the Hengxing (Taiwei enclosure, the emperor’s court) and Quanxing (Xuanyuan, the heroine), with stars for officials, generals, and law enforcement. The Western Palace (White Tiger) includes the Five Chariots and stars for barbarians, hunting, and border affairs. The Northern Palace (Xuanwu) contains the Yulin Heavenly Army and stars for floods, war, and funerals.

Each planet governs specific seasons, elements, and human virtues. Jupiter (wood, spring, benevolence) indicates prosperity or disaster based on its motion. Mars (fire, summer, ritual) signals chaos, war, and famine. Venus (metal, autumn, righteousness) is the star of war, with detailed rules for its appearance, color, and movement predicting military outcomes. Mercury (water, winter, wisdom) governs floods and military ambushes. Saturn (earth, late summer, faith) is the most auspicious, with its position indicating land gains or losses.

Conjunctions and interactions among the five planets predict major events: Jupiter-Saturn conjunctions indicate civil strife; Mars-Venus conjunctions bring mourning; and five-star gatherings signal a new ruler. Lunar eclipses and occultations of stars by the moon foretell the destruction of states or the death of kings. The text also describes comets, meteors, and other celestial objects (e.g., Tengu, Geze, Chiyou banners) as omens of war, rebellion, or natural disasters.

The sun’s path (ecliptic) and the moon’s nine orbits determine seasons and weather. Solar and lunar eclipses are linked to the ruler’s virtue and punishment. Clouds and vapors (qi) are used for divination, with colors and shapes indicating military outcomes, harvests, and regional events. The text includes historical examples from the Han dynasty, such as the five-star gathering at Dongjing (marking Emperor Gaozu’s rise), comets during the reign of Qin Shihuang, and planetary movements predicting rebellions (e.g., the Seven States Rebellion, the Huo Guang conspiracy). These examples illustrate how celestial phenomena were interpreted as direct responses to political events, from the decline of the Zhou dynasty to the usurpation of Wang Mang.

A comprehensive system of astronomical and calendrical calculations, beginning with a series of defined numerical constants and methods. The "method number" is derived from multiplying the original Huang Zhong Chujiu by itself. The "leap method" of nineteen is used as the number of years in a chapter. The "Tongfa" (1,539) is obtained by multiplying the leap number by the daily number, and the "Yuanfa" (4,617) is three times the Tongfa. Other key numbers include the "Zhang month" (235), "Moon Dharma" (2,392), and "Weekly days" (562,120). The text details the calculation of various astronomical cycles, including the synodic meeting, meeting months, and the cycles of the year star, Taibai Star, Zhenxing, Yinghuo, and the stars (Mercury). For each planet, the text provides specific numbers for its appearance, motion (direct, retrograde, and stationary), and the duration of its visibility and concealment, along with the degrees it travels.

The text then outlines methods for deducing the Sun-Moon Yuan Tong, calculating the winter solstice, and determining the positions of the five stars. It describes how to calculate the number of years since the original Shangyuan and the specific cycles of Jiazi, Jiachen, and Jiashen. Procedures are given for calculating the first day of the lunar month, the location of the leap remainder, and the twenty-four solar terms. The text also details the calculation of the stars' positions at morning and midnight, the lunar eclipse, and the complex numbers for the manifestation of the five stars. It explains how to determine the middle number of a star's appearance, the star and the moon, and the degree of the next day after entering the center.

The text provides a detailed breakdown of the five steps of calculation for the planets, using the number of days since their first appearance and their daily motion. It also describes the calculation of the age (Sui Xing) and its profits and losses, noting that the Sui star's misplacement can cause disasters. The text then lists the twelve celestial divisions (Xingji) from Dou Twelve Degrees to Dou Shidu, associating each with a solar term and the corresponding months in the Xia, Shang, and Zhou calendars. It provides the degrees for various constellations and explains the cycles of nine ends and three ends, which relate to the unification of the calendar.

The text includes a historical chronology, starting from the legendary emperors (Taiwu, Yandi, Huangdi, Shaowu, Zhuan Xu, Xue, Tang, Yu) and their associated virtues (wood, fire, earth, metal, water). It traces the lineage and reigns of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, providing specific years and astronomical events. For example, it notes that the Xia dynasty had 432 years, the Shang dynasty 629 years, and the Zhou dynasty 867 years. The text also details the reigns of the Qin dynasty and the early Han emperors, from Gaozu to Emperor Guangwu, providing the number of years for each reign and the total years since the Shangyuan. It concludes with the reign of Emperor Guangwu, noting that he reigned for 33 years.
