summary:
Emperor Xiaocheng, the son of Emperor Yuan and Empress Wang, was born while his father was crown prince and was greatly favored by his grandfather, Emperor Xuan, who named him Taisun. After Emperor Xuan’s death, Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and made him crown prince. As an adult, he was studious, broad-minded, and cautious. Once, when summoned urgently by his father, he avoided crossing the emperor’s road, taking a detour instead, which pleased Emperor Yuan, who then allowed him to cross. Despite later concerns over his drinking and pleasure-seeking, Emperor Yuan considered deposing him in favor of Prince Tao Gong, but was dissuaded by Shi Xian and the memory of Emperor Xuan’s affection.

Upon Emperor Yuan’s death in the first year of Jingning, the prince ascended the throne, honoring his mother and grandmother as empress dowagers. He appointed his uncle Wang Feng as Grand Marshal and Grand General, overseeing secretarial affairs. He agreed to stop burying chariots and animals with the dead, granted a general amnesty, and faced various omens: a fire in the ancestral temple, a comet, and a storm that killed envoy Yao Yin. He rewarded officials and the people, issued an edict acknowledging his faults, and promoted tolerance. He granted titles to his uncles and faced natural phenomena like yellow mist, swarms of flies, and a shooting star.

In subsequent years, he conducted suburban sacrifices, established Queen Xu, and dealt with droughts, floods, and rebellions. He reduced taxes, pardoned prisoners, and encouraged agriculture. He faced earthquakes, solar eclipses, and a comet, issuing edicts to seek advice and reform. He moved wealthy households to Changling, deposed Queen Xu, and suppressed uprisings like Zheng Gong’s rebellion. He stopped the costly Changling project, punished the architect Xie Wannian, and rewarded those who advised against it. He continued to face disasters, including fires and floods, and issued edicts against extravagance.

He appointed Liu Xin of Dingtao as crown prince, granted titles to descendants of previous dynasties, and reorganized offices. He died in Weiyang Palace and was buried in Yanling. Ban Gu noted his dignified appearance, knowledge, and eloquence, but lamented his indulgence in drink and women, leading to the rise of the Wang family and Wang Mang’s eventual usurpation.

Emperor Xiaowen was the fourth son of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and his mother was Bo Ji.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Chen Xi was executed and the Dai territory was pacified. He made him the Dai king and made his capital Zhongdu.
In the autumn of the seventeenth year of King Dai's reign, Empress Lu passed away, and Zhu Lu planned a coup to seize Liu Han's power.
Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Zhou Bo, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang and others jointly killed the Lu family and discussed the appointment of the acting king Liu Heng as the emperor.
The historical events are recorded in "Book of Han·Gao Hou Ji and Gao Wu Wang Biography".
The ministers sent people to greet the king.
After deliberation, Zhang Wu, the king's lieutenant, said: The ministers of the Han Dynasty are all veteran generals from the time of Emperor Gao. They are familiar with military affairs and well versed in intrigues and tricks. In their hearts, they are not satisfied with their current status. They are just afraid of the majesty of Emperor Gao and Empress Lu.
Now that Zhu Lu has been executed and blood has been spilled in the capital, it is unbelievable to welcome the king to the capital in the name of proclaiming himself emperor.
I hope your Majesty will not go there on the grounds of illness, so as to observe changes in the situation.
Lieutenant Song Chang added: Their comments are wrong.
The Qin Dynasty was in disarray, heroes arose, and there were no less than ten thousand people who wanted to replace the Qin Dynasty and claim the title of emperor in the south. However, in the end, only the Liu family was able to rule the world. People in the world who harbored evil thoughts were desperate. This was one of them.
Emperor Gao made his children kings, and the fiefdoms were intertwined. This became a rock-like core. The world obeyed Liu Han's strength. This was the second one.
The establishment of the Han Dynasty abolished the harshness of the Qin Dynasty, reduced punishments, extended kindness and benefits, and made everyone feel at ease, which won the hearts of the people.
With the majesty of the Empress Dowager Lu, she established Zhu Lu as the three kings and was good at despotic power. However, the Taiwei Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army with a talisman and called on the soldiers to support the Liu family and oppose Zhu Lu. As a result, the Lu family was wiped out.
This shows that Liu Han's regime was given by heaven and could not be changed by a few manpower.
Nowadays, although some ministers want to launch a coup, the people are unwilling to listen to them. Can they achieve their goals by relying on a small number of his party members?
Inside Kyoto, there is the unity of Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou, and outside there are the powers of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langwangya, Qi and Dai.
Nowadays, the only sons of Emperor Gao are the King of Huainan and you, the king. The king lives long, is a sage, benevolent and filial, and is famous all over the world. Therefore, the ministers in the court obey the wishes of the people and want to welcome the king, so the king does not have to worry.
Reporting to the Queen Mother on behalf of the king, it was difficult to make a decision for a while.
Then he asked someone to divine, and he got a great omen. The fortune teller said: Great, Gengen, I am the king of heaven, Xia Qiguang Zong Yaozu.
Dai Wang said: I am already a king, so why do I need to add a king's title?
The diviner said: The so-called king of heaven in the hexagram is the emperor!
So King Dai sent Bo Zhao, the younger brother of the Queen Mother, to meet with Taiwei Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo and others reported in detail the true intention of welcoming King Dai.
Bo Zhao reported back to Dai Wang: It is trustworthy and there is nothing to doubt.
The king of Dai smiled and said to Song Chang: "It's just as the teacher said."
So he sent Song Chang to be in charge of driving, and Zhang Wu and six other people were dispatched to Chang'an to report the news. The car stopped at the Mausoleum of Emperor Gao, and Song Chang was sent to Chang'an to observe the situation.
When Song Chang arrived at Weiqiao, officials below the prime minister came to greet him.
Song Chang went to Gaoling to report to King Dai, so King Dai also went to Weiqiao.
The ministers paid homage to the king as ministers, and the king also bowed humbly in return.
Taiwei Zhou Bo came forward and said: Please report to Chen secretly.
Song Chang said: If what the captain is stating is a public matter, please report it in front of all the ministers; if what is being stated is a private matter, the king is selfless.
Taiwei Zhou Bo knelt down and presented the emperor's jade seal.
He said goodbye on behalf of the king: Please come to the palace in Kyoto for further discussion.
On the 29th day of the ninth month, I entered the palace of King Dai.
All the ministers followed and presented a memorial: Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Minister Zhou Bo, General Chai Wu, Yu Shi Da Fu Chen Zhang Cang, Zong Zheng Chen Liu Ying, Zhu Xuhou Chen Liu Zhang, Dong Mou Hou Chen Liu Xingju, Dian Ke Chen Liu Jie again paid homage to the King and said: Zihong and others are not the sons of Emperor Xiaohui and should not inherit the throne.
I would like to invite Yin'an, Queen Qing, King Langya, the princes, and Li Erqianshi to discuss this matter. The king is the son of Emperor Gao and should inherit. May the king be the emperor.
Dai Wang said: "It is an important matter to enshrine Emperor Gaodi in the ancestral temple."
There are few people and no talent, and they are not enough to take on this responsibility.
I would like to ask the King of Chu, the younger brother of Emperor Gao, to consider a suitable candidate. I really don’t dare to take the position.
All the ministers prostrated themselves on the ground and firmly requested the king's consent.
On behalf of the king, he resigned three times to the west and twice to the south.
Prime Minister Chen Pingping said: I sincerely believe that it is most appropriate for your Majesty to inherit the throne of Emperor Gao. All the princes and people in the world believe that it is a natural and right thing to do. For the sake of the ancestral temple and the country, I do not dare to neglect, and ask your Majesty to obey my request.
I would like to present the emperor's jade seal to you.
Dai Wang said: Since the clan, generals and princes think that I am a suitable successor to the throne, I do not dare to refuse.
So he became the emperor.
The ministers all followed their original posts.
The servants Guan Ying and Dongmou Hou Xingju were sent to clean Weiyang Palace first, and then went to the palace of Dai Wang with the Emperor's guard of honor to greet him.
The emperor entered Weiyang Palace that evening.
That night, Song Chang was appointed as General of the Guard, commanding the Northern and Southern armies, and Zhang Wu was appointed as Lang Zhongling, patrolling the palace.
The emperor sat in the front hall and issued an edict: The Prime Minister, the Taiwei, and the Yushi Dafu: In the past, Lu Zhuan was in charge of power, conspired to usurp the throne, and wanted to harm the Liu family's ancestral temple.
When I first ascend the throne, I should grant a general amnesty to the world, and reward the men of the world with the rank of nobility, and the women of every hundred households should be given a number of cattle and a stone of wine.
Five days of gathering and drinking are a joy. On the second day of the tenth winter in the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, the emperor met with his ministers at the Gaozu Temple.
Sent Chariot General Bo Zhao to Daidi to welcome the Empress Dowager to Beijing.
The edict said: In the past, Lu Chan proclaimed himself the prime minister, and Lu Lu was the general. He sent General Guan Ying to lead an army to attack in an attempt to replace Liu Han.
General Guan stopped his troops in Xingyang and conspired with the princes to kill the Lu family.
Lu Chan wanted to usurp the throne, so Prime Minister Chen Ping, Lieutenant Zhou Bo and others conspired to seize the Northern Army controlled by Lu Chan.
Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang first captured Lu Chan.
Taiwei Zhou Bo personally led Xiangping Hou Tong to join the Northern Army with the imperial edict.
Dianke Liu Jiezhi seized Lu Lu's seal.
Therefore, he was granted the title of Taiwei Zhou Boyi to ten thousand households and was given five thousand catties of gold.
Prime Minister Chen Ping and General Guanying were granted the title of three thousand households each, and were given two thousand catties of gold.
The Marquis of Zhuxu, Liu Zhang, and the Marquis of Xiangping, Liu Tongyi, were granted the title of two thousand households each, with a thousand catties of gold.
Dian Ke Liu Jie was granted the title of Marquis of Yangxin and was given a thousand catties of gold.
In December, Liu Sui, the son of King You of Zhao, was made King of Zhao, and King Liu Ze of King Ya of Lang was transferred to King of Yan.
The Qi and Chu lands captured by the Lu family were returned to their original owners, and the Qin law was abolished, which stipulated that if one person is guilty, the whole family will be affected.
In the first month of the first month, relevant officials asked Emperor Wen to establish a prince early in order to respect the ancestral temple.
Emperor Wen issued an edict saying: My virtues are shallow, the gods in heaven are not willing to enjoy my sacrifices to them, and the people of the world also think that I am not their ideal emperor.
Today, I cannot seek out the world's sages and virtuous people to succeed the emperor, but I suggest that we should establish a prince early, which makes my bad virtue even worse.
How can this satisfy the expectations of the people in the world for me?
The matter of establishing a prince is postponed.
Relevant officials reported again: The early appointment of the prince was based on the emphasis on the ancestral temple and the country, which proved that the emperor always kept world affairs in mind.
The emperor said: The King of Chu is my uncle. He is old and virtuous, has rich experience and experience, and knows everything about governing the country.
King Wu, King Huainan and I are brothers. They are all virtuous to assist me, haven't they already arranged the successor to the throne?
There are many meritorious officials among the brothers of the princes, kings and clans, and there are many virtuous, benevolent and righteous people. If one of the above-mentioned wise men with noble virtues is selected to succeed me as the emperor who is not qualified for the position, this will be the spirit of the country and the blessing of the world.
If I do not elect virtuous people today, but say that I must establish a prince, people will think that I have forgotten the virtuous people and only want my son to succeed me. This is not really caring about world affairs, and I really do not want to adopt it.
Relevant officials repeatedly requested: In ancient times, Yin and Zhou conquered the world and enjoyed long-lasting peace and stability for nearly a thousand years. In the past, no one in the world could pass on the throne as long as the Yin and Zhou Dynasties. This is because both Yin and Zhou adopted the method of passing on the crown prince.
The crown prince must be the son of the emperor. This has always been the case in history.
Emperor Gao began to pacify the world, establish princes, and became the ancestor of Emperor Liu Han.
The princes, princes, and princes who began to receive feudal states also became the ancestors of the feudal states.
Succession by descendants from generation to generation is a universal justice.
Therefore, Emperor Gaozu established a prince to stabilize the world.
It was not Emperor Gao's original intention to give up on the task of establishing a son as prince today and instead choose him from among the princes and clans.
It would be inappropriate to elect another person.
Prince Qi is the eldest son, kind and generous, so he asks the emperor to make him the crown prince.
The emperor finally agreed.
Therefore, the people of the world should be given the title of nobility as their father's heirs.
General Bo Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Zhi.
In March, the relevant officials asked for the establishment of a queen, and the Empress Dowager said: Make Dou, the mother of the crown prince, the queen.
Emperor Wen issued an edict saying: When the spring breeze is gentle, flying animals, plants and other things have the joy of revival. However, the widowed, lonely and poor among our people may be struggling on the edge of death without receiving care and warmth. How can we, as parents of the people, feel at ease?
Relief should be discussed.
The edict also said: The old man will not be warm if he does not wear a cotton-padded jacket, and he will not be full if he does not eat meat.
In the early spring of this year, people were often sent to visit the elders. If they were not given some cloth, wine and meat, how could they help the descendants of the world to be filial and support their relatives?
I once heard that some officials gave old millets and rotten rice when distributing pension grains. Can this be said to be implementing the edict of providing pensions for the elderly?
The regulations will now be formulated in detail.
Relevant officials notified all counties and roads that those over eighty years of age would be given one stone of rice, twenty catties of meat, and five measures of wine per month.
For those who are over ninety years old, there will be an additional two pounds of silk and three pounds of catkins per person.
When giving gifts and pensions to elderly people over ninety years old, the county magistrate must personally supervise and inspect them, and the county magistrate or county lieutenant must personally deliver them.
Those who are less than 90 years old will be handed over by agricultural officials and regents.
High-ranking officials should send virtuous officials to patrol and inspect, and those who do not implement the edicts should be investigated and punished.
Elderly persons who have been sentenced and whose crimes will result in a sentence of more than two years are not subject to this order.
Liu Jiao, king of Chu Yuan, passed away.
In April, there was an earthquake in Qi and Chu. On the same day, twenty-nine mountains collapsed and floods surged.
In June, the county was ordered not to present property to the court.
The beneficial government spread throughout the world, and the princes and barbarians from far and near were grateful to the emperor for his kindness.

The edict said: When the ministers punished Zhu Lu and made me emperor, I had doubts and often advised me not to leave Dai. Only after Lieutenant Song Chang advised me to live up to public expectations did I decide to inherit the throne.

November 30th, partial solar eclipse.

should be abolished.

From now on, attempted crimes of this kind need not be prosecuted.

This year, half of the land rent payable by the people will be exempted as a reward.

The imperial edict said: In the past, there was an imperial edict to send all the princes back to their feudal states, but they refused and failed to do so.
The Prime Minister is the one I rely on most, and I hope to take the lead and set an example to return to my own kingdom.

summary:
Emperor Xiaowen, the fourth son of Emperor Gaozu of Han, was made King of Dai after the execution of Chen Xi. Following Empress Lu’s death, the Lu clan plotted to seize power but were killed by ministers Chen Ping, Zhou Bo, and others, who then decided to welcome King Dai as emperor. King Dai hesitated, with advisor Zhang Wu warning that the ministers were veteran generals skilled in intrigue and might not be trustworthy. However, Song Chang argued that the Han dynasty’s stability, the people’s loyalty to Liu, and the failure of the Lu clan’s usurpation proved divine support for Liu rule. After divination yielded a favorable omen, King Dai sent Bo Zhao to verify the ministers’ intentions. Zhou Bo confirmed their sincerity, and King Dai proceeded to Chang’an. At Weiqiao, Zhou Bo offered the imperial seal, but King Dai declined, insisting on discussing the matter at the palace. The ministers formally petitioned him to accept the throne, citing his lineage as Emperor Gaozu’s son. After three refusals, he agreed and became emperor.

Upon ascending the throne, Emperor Wen issued a general amnesty, rewarded those who had suppressed the Lu clan, and restored lands taken by the Lu family. He abolished the Qin law of collective punishment. When officials urged him to appoint a crown prince, he initially declined, citing his own unworthiness and suggesting a virtuous successor from among his relatives or ministers. After repeated requests, he appointed his eldest son, Prince Qi, as crown prince. He also established his consort Dou as empress. The emperor implemented benevolent policies, including tax relief for farmers, care for the elderly, and pardons for minor offenses. He abolished the crime of slander and attempted treason, emphasizing the importance of agriculture and reducing government expenditures.

During his reign, Emperor Wen faced challenges such as the rebellion of King Xingju of Jibei, which was swiftly suppressed, and conflicts with the Xiongnu, whom he managed through defense rather than costly campaigns. He promoted frugality, wearing simple clothes and forbidding lavish decorations. He also reformed the legal system, abolished corporal punishment, and encouraged the recommendation of virtuous officials. In his later years, he issued an edict on his deathbed, advocating simple funerals and urging the people not to mourn excessively. He was buried in Ba Ling with minimal ceremony, using earthenware vessels and no precious metals. Ban Gu praised Emperor Wen for his benevolence, noting that his reign saw prosperity, few imprisonments, and a flourishing of moral virtue.

It turned out that father and son Jie and An were fighting for power with the general Huo Guang and wanted to harm Huo Guang, so they deceived people to write to the court in the name of King Dan of Yan to expose Huo Guang's crimes.
Emperor Zhao was fourteen years old at this time and discovered his fraud.
Later, someone falsely accused Huo Guang, and Emperor Zhao was furious and said: "General, a loyal minister of the country, entrusted by the late emperor. Anyone who dares to make false accusations will be held accountable."
Huo Guang was thus able to be loyal to the best of his ability.
The incident was recorded in the biography of King Yan and Huo Guang.
In the tenth month of winter, Emperor Zhao issued an edict saying: The left general Anyang Hou Jie, the hussar general Sang Lehou An, and the imperial censor Hong Yang all repeatedly interfered with the government's affairs with evil deeds. If the general did not obey his instructions, they became dissatisfied and secretly colluded with the king of Yan. They set up special envoys to go back and forth and rebelled against the party.
The King of Yan sent Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi and others to bribe the eldest princess, Ding Weiren, the visitor Du Yannian, the general Shi Gongsun Yi and others to deliver the secret letter, and jointly planned to have the eldest princess hold a banquet to entertain the general Huo Guang, and took the opportunity to ambush and kill her. Later, he conscripted King Yan as the emperor, which was really treason.
Yancang, the envoy from the rice fields, first discovered it and quickly reported it to Yang Chang, the chief agricultural officer. Yang Chang urgently informed the doctor Du Yannian, and Yannian hurriedly reported it to the Ming Emperor.
The Prime Minister Zheng Gong personally captured and beheaded Shangguan Jie. The Prime Minister's Young Master Wang Shou lured Shangguan An into the palace and killed him together, so that the officials and the people were able to turn the crisis into safety.
For this reason, Du Yannian, Ren Gong and Wang Shou were granted the title of marquis.
The edict also said: The king of Yan had lost his wits due to Li Ling, and he had rebelled against Prince Liu Ze of Qi and others. At that time, he suppressed his crimes in the hope that he could change his ways. Now he conspired with the eldest princess, Zuo General Jie and others to harm the ancestral temple.
His subordinates were deceived by Shangguan Jie and others and coerced into participating in the rebellion, but if no specific facts were documented, they were exempted from criminal punishment.
In April of the second year of summer, Emperor Zhao moved from Jianzhang Palace to Weiyang Palace and held a banquet for all the ministers.
The man was given official silk and the clan members were given money, each of which was 200,000 yuan.
The officials and the people were given a piece of silk for each person who offered cattle and wine.
In June, there is a general amnesty.
The edict was issued: "I have no sympathy for the people, so I reduced the province and transferred 3 million shi to the capital the year before last."
Appropriate savings should be made on self-riding horses and garden horses to supplement the three auxiliary and border post horses.
The county is now ordered not to collect this year's horse mouth money. Sanfu and Taichang should be allowed to use Shu and Li as tribute money when paying taxes.
In the first month of the spring of the third year, a large stone stood up on its own in Mount Tai, and a willow tree in Shanglinyuan withered and grew green leaves again.
Eliminate taxes for poor households in Zhongmouyuan.
The edict said: Some time ago, the people suffered from floods and were in great difficulty with food rations. I transferred food from the national treasury and sent special personnel to provide relief to households in need.
The grain that should be handed over in the fourth year is now waived.
The relief loan issued three years ago was personally given by me, and the immigrants in the border counties who were working with oxen for plowing did not pay their debts.
In April of summer, Shaofu Xu Ren, Tingwei Wang Ping, and Zuo Fengyi Jia Shenghu were all guilty of condoning rebellion. Xu Ren committed suicide, and Wang Ping and Jia Shenghu were both cut in half.
In winter, Wuhuan rebelled in Liaodong. He sent Zhonglang General Fan Mingyou as the general of Liao Dynasty and led 2,000 cavalry soldiers from seven counties in the north to pacify Ding.
On the second day of the first lunar month in the fourth year of spring, Emperor Zhao paid a visit to the Gaozu Temple.
Give gold, silk, cattle and wine to all princes, kings, prime ministers, generals, princes, clans, and officials and people, each with their own differences.
He will be awarded with a title of less than 2,000 dan and nobility for all subjects in the world, and the payment of population tax for the fourth and fifth years will be stopped.
Those who have not paid the new tax three years ago will be exempted from payment. He ordered the whole world to feast for five days.
On February 21, Prime Minister Tian Qianqiu passed away.
In April of summer, Emperor Zhao issued an edict: When General Mingyou of Du Liao was serving as the captain of the Qiang cavalry school, he led the Qiang princes, princes and commanders to attack Yizhou to rebel against the captives. Later, he led the Qiang army to attack Wudu to rebel against the Di. Now he defeated Wuhuan and killed many prisoners, which is a meritorious service.
Specially ennoble Mingyou as Pinglinghou.
Fu Jiezi, the supervisor of Pingyue, went out as an envoy to kill the Loulan Wang An who was disobedient to the Han Dynasty. His head was hung in the North Tower and he was now named the Marquis of Yiyang.
In May, a fire broke out in the main hall of Xiaowen Temple. Emperor Zhao and his ministers all wore plain clothes and sent two thousand stones to lead the soldiers of the five schools to repair it, which was completed in six days.
Taichang and the imperial minister were both accused of dereliction of duty. When the general amnesty happened, Taichang Hou De of Liaoyang was exempted and became a commoner.
In June, there is a general amnesty.
In the first month of the spring of the fifth year, King Guangling went to the capital to pay homage, and granted a thousand more households in his kingdom. He also gave him 20 million yuan in money, 200 jins of gold, two sword handles, a chariot, and eight horses.
Summer, severe drought.
In June, young criminals from Sanfu and various counties who had fled due to reports were sent to garrison Liaodong.
In autumn, Xiang County was abolished and belonged to Yulin and Zoke County.
Winter, November, thunder.
On December 6, Prime Minister Wang Xin passed away.
In the spring and first month of the sixth year, prisoners from the county were recruited to build Xuantu City in Liaodong.
Xia, forgive the sinners in the world.
The edict was issued: "Generally, low prices of grain will hurt farmers. Now that grain prices have dropped in Sanfu and Taichang, various regions are specially ordered to use grain as tax payment."
The right general Zhang Anshi loyally and cautiously executed the guard and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuping.
Wuhuan once again invaded the border fortress and sent General Fan Mingyou, the general from Liao Dynasty, to lead the pursuit.
In the spring and February of the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao issued an edict saying: The world is based on farming and mulberry.
In the past period, we have saved money, cut redundant personnel, and reduced additional taxes. As a result, the number of people engaged in farming has increased, but the people are still not self-sufficient. I am deeply disturbed.
It is now decided to reduce the oral tax payment.
Someone petitioned for a reduction of three-tenths, and the emperor agreed.
On February 17, there was a meteor in the morning, as big as the moon, and the stars followed the meteor westward.
On April 17th in the summer, Emperor Zhao died in Weiyang Palace.
On June 7, he was buried in Pingling.
Ban Gu commented: In the past, King Cheng of Zhou inherited the throne with a young son, but there were rumors from Guan and Cai, slandering the Duke of Zhou who served as regent and assisted the young master.
When Emperor Zhao succeeded to the throne at a young age, Yan, Yong, and Shangguan also conspired to rebel and slander Huo Guang, who was regent and assistant to the young emperor.
King Cheng did not doubt Duke Zhou, and Emperor Zhao appointed Huo Guang. It is remarkable that both monarchs and ministers can become famous in their own time!
After Emperor Zhao succeeded Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he was very happy with his achievements and went on a military expedition. The domestic economy was in depression and the population was reduced by half. However, Huo Guangneng focused on the most urgent tasks, did light corvees and low taxes, and rested with the people.
During the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the country made peace with the Xiongnu on the outside and enriched the people on the inside.
He also recommended virtuous literature, inquired about the sufferings of the people, stopped selling salt, iron and wine, and did not compete with the people for profit. His posthumous title was Zhao, which is very appropriate!
summary:
Emperor Zhao of Han, youngest son of Emperor Wu, ascended the throne at age eight after his father’s death in 87 BCE. Huo Guang, appointed regent, managed state affairs with deputies Jin Rixi and Shangguan Jie. Early reign events included amnesties, a comet sighting, and Xiongnu raids repelled by garrisons. Auspicious signs like yellow swans prompted celebrations, while rebellions in Yizhou and by Liu Ze were suppressed. Reforms reduced taxes, exempted land rent, and provided relief to the poor. In 81 BCE, Emperor Zhao ended state monopolies on salt, iron, and wine after consulting virtuous scholars. Su Wu returned from 19 years of captivity among the Xiongnu and was rewarded.

In 80 BCE, a major conspiracy involving King Liu Dan of Yan, Princess Eyi, Shangguan Jie, and others to assassinate Huo Guang was foiled. Emperor Zhao, then 14, exposed the plot, leading to executions of the conspirators. Huo Guang’s loyalty was vindicated, and he continued as regent. Subsequent years saw further reforms: tax reductions, amnesties, and agricultural support. Emperor Zhao died in 74 BCE at age 21, buried in Pingling. Ban Gu praised his reign for restoring stability after Emperor Wu’s costly campaigns, implementing light corvée and low taxes, and fostering peace with the Xiongnu while enriching the people.

Chasing and killing Wu Wang Biyu Dan Tu.

Now that Liu Bi and others have been eliminated, the deceived officials and civilians and the soldiers who fled will not be held accountable for the law of sitting together, but will be pardoned.

Fengping Luhou Liu Li was made King of Chu to succeed King Yuan.

Change the method of dismemberment for death penalty to discard the corpse, and abolish the method of dismemberment.

Ban Gu commented: The Han Dynasty was founded in a turbulent period when heroes were vying for the throne. Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty brought order to the chaos, and Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing made recuperation and recuperation his top priority. However, there was still a lack of achievements in the cultural affairs of ancient rituals.
In the early days of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he resolutely dismissed hundreds of schools of thought and advocated Confucianism alone. He also sought advice from others, recommended talented people, and gave them opportunities to make contributions.
He established Imperial College, established suburban sacrifices, corrected Shuo, established calendar numbers, and harmonious rhythms, composed poems and music, established Zen confederations, and worshiped hundreds of gods. After inheriting the Zhou Dynasty, he issued orders and articles that can be described in a new way.
Inheriting the great achievements of his ancestors, he has the style of the emperors of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties.
Even if Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty had such a great talent and strategy, and if he did not change Wen Jing's frugality and put the common people on the throne of Renren, even the emperors praised in "Poems" and "Books" could not surpass him.
summary:
Emperor Xiaowu Liu Che, the second son of Emperor Jing, was born to Wang Meiren. At age four, he was made King of Jiaodong, and at seven, he became crown prince. At sixteen, in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, his father died, and Liu Che succeeded the throne. He honored Empress Dowager Dou and his mother as empress dowagers, and granted marquis titles to his maternal uncles. In the first year of Jianyuan, he ordered officials to recommend virtuous and upright individuals, but Prime Minister Wei Wan advised against promoting those who studied Legalist or strategist philosophies, which the emperor approved. He pardoned the world, rewarded the people, exempted taxes for the elderly, and issued three-baht coins. Edicts emphasized respect for elders, exempted families of those over ninety from corvée, and improved sacrifices to rivers and seas. He pardoned first offenders in the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion, reduced palace guards, opened horse-breeding gardens to the poor, and planned to build a Mingtang. He summoned the scholar Lu Shen Gong.

In the second year, officials Zhao Wan and Wang Zang committed suicide for failing to report to the Empress Dowager, and Prime Minister Dou Ying and Taiwei Tian Chong were dismissed. A partial solar eclipse occurred, and a night was as bright as day. Maoling-eup was established. In the third year, the Yellow River flooded, causing famine and cannibalism. Residents moving to Maoling received funds and land. A comet appeared in the northwest. King Liu Ming of Jichuan was deposed for murder. Minyue besieged Dong Ou, but Han forces caused their retreat. In the fourth year, red dust blew, drought struck, and comets appeared. In the fifth year, three-baht coins were abolished, half-liang coins issued, and Doctors of the Five Classics established. The emperor's grandmother died, locusts plagued, and two kings died. In the sixth year, fires at Gaozu Temple and Gaoyuan Bedroom led the emperor to blame himself. The Empress Dowager died, and a comet appeared. Minyue attacked South Vietnam, but the Yue people killed their king and surrendered.

In the first year of Yuanguang, counties recommended one filial and incorrupt person each. Generals Li Guang and Cheng Bushi withdrew troops. The emperor pardoned the world and restored clans of the Seven Kingdoms. He issued an edict praising ancient rulers and seeking advice, leading to the rise of Dong Zhongshu and Gongsun Hong. In the second year, the emperor worshipped the Five Emperors and discussed attacking the Xiongnu. Generals stationed 300,000 troops at Mayi to lure the Xiongnu Chanyu, but he escaped. General Wang Hui died in prison. In the third year, the Yellow River changed course, and five meritorious officials were made marquises. Flooding in Puyang led to disaster relief. In the fourth year, Dou Ying was executed, Prime Minister Chong died, frost damaged crops, and an earthquake occurred. In the fifth year, King Wang De of Hejian died, roads were built, and Queen Chen was deposed. Talented individuals were recruited. In the sixth year, taxes on merchants' vehicles began. The Xiongnu invaded, and General Wei Qing captured 700 heads, while Gongsun Ao and Li Guang were defeated. The emperor pardoned soldiers for disciplinary violations.

In the first year of Shuo, the emperor issued edicts promoting virtue and talent, ordering officials to recommend filial and incorrupt individuals. Queen Wei was established. In the first year of Yuanshuo, the Xiongnu invaded, and Wei Qing captured thousands of heads. Dongyi submitted, and Canghai County was established. In the second year, the emperor granted titles to princes' sons. Wei Qing recovered Henan, establishing Shuofang and Wuyuan counties. People were moved to Shuofang and Maoling. In the third year, Canghai County was abolished, and the Xiongnu invaded Dai and Yanmen. The Empress Dowager died. In the fourth year, the emperor visited Ganquan. In the fifth year, drought struck, and Wei Qing captured over 15,000 Xiongnu heads. The emperor promoted education and set up doctoral disciples. In the sixth year, Wei Qing defeated the Xiongnu in the desert, but Zhao Xin surrendered and Su Jian fled. The emperor established martial arts reward officers.

In the first year of Yuanshou, the emperor obtained a white unicorn and wrote a song. Kings of Huainan and Hengshan rebelled and were executed. The crown prince was established. The emperor issued edicts rewarding filial piety and caring for the elderly. Generals Huo Qubing and Gongsun Ao captured thousands of Xiongnu heads. The Xiongnu king Kunxie surrendered, and Wuwei and Jiuquan counties were established. In the third year, a comet appeared, and the emperor pardoned the world. In the fourth year, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu in Mobei, with heavy casualties. Li Guang committed suicide. In the fifth year, half-liang coins were scrapped, and five-baht coins issued. In the sixth year, the emperor established princes and issued edicts on currency reform. He sent officials to inspect the country and relieve the needy.

In the first year of Yuanding, a tripod was found in the Fen River. In the second year, officials died, and Bailiang Terrace was built. Floods caused starvation. In the third year, the emperor moved Hangu and ordered tax evasion rewards. In the fourth year, he built Hou Tu Temple and granted titles to Zhou descendants. In the fifth year, he sacrificed to the sun and moon, found a tripod, and composed songs. In the sixth year, Nanyue rebelled, and the emperor sent generals to suppress it. The Western Qiang and Xiongnu invaded. In the first year of Yuanfeng, the emperor patrolled the border, shocking the Xiongnu. Dongyue submitted, and people were moved. He climbed Mount Song, built altars, and issued edicts on reforms.

In the first year of Taichu, the emperor revised the calendar and built a palace. In the second year, he sacrificed to Houtu. In the third year, he built fortresses. In the fourth year, Li Guangli beheaded the King of Dayuan. In the first year of Tianhan, the Xiongnu returned envoys. In the second year, Li Guangli fought the Xiongnu, but Li Ling surrendered. Witchcraft was investigated. In the third year, the emperor sacrificed at Mount Tai. In the fourth year, he sent generals against the Xiongnu. In the first year of Taishi, Gongsun Ao was executed. In the second year, the emperor obtained a white unicorn and changed gold forms. In the third year, he visited the East China Sea. In the fourth year, he sacrificed at Mount Tai. In the first year of Zhenghe, witchcraft occurred. In the second year, the crown prince fled and committed suicide. In the third year, Li Guangli surrendered to the Xiongnu. In the fourth year, the emperor plowed land and repaired Mount Tai. In the first year of Hou Yuan, he pardoned the world. In the second year, he made Prince Fuling crown prince and died in Wuzha Palace.

Ban Gu commented: Emperor Wu dismissed hundreds of schools, promoted Confucianism, established Imperial College, and reformed rituals. He inherited ancestral achievements but lacked frugality, which even praised emperors could not surpass.

translation:
Empress Gao, the Lu family, gave birth to Emperor Hui, who assisted Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty to pacify the world. Her father and brother had three marquises under Emperor Gaozu.
After Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he honored Empress Lu as the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother made the daughter of Princess Lu Yuan, the sister of Emperor Hui, the Queen. She had no children, so she made the son of a beauty in the harem the Prince.
Emperor Hui died, and the prince was established as emperor. The emperor was young, and Empress Dowager Lu came to the court to perform the emperor's affairs and grant amnesty to the world.
Later, four of his brother's sons, Lu Tai, Lu Chan, Lu Lu, and Lu Tai's son Lu Tong were made kings, and six Zhu Lu were made princes.
The specific details can be found in "Book of Han·Biography of Wai Qi".
In the first month of the spring of the first year of Empress Lu's reign, she issued an edict saying: It turned out that Emperor Xiaohui intended to abolish the harsh laws that punished serious crimes and three clans, and regarded wrong words as evil words. He died before the resolution was resolved.
It has now been announced that it will be abolished.
In February, the people were rewarded with titles of nobility, one level for each household.
For the first time, an official with an annual salary of two thousand shi was set up to encourage the world's filial piety.
On the fourth day of May in the summer, a fire broke out in the Congtai of Zhao Palace.
Liu Qiang, the son of Emperor Xiaohui's harem, was made the King of Huaiyang, Liu Buyi was the King of Hengshan, Liu Hong was the Marquis of Xiangcheng, Liu Chao was the Marquis of Zhi, and Liu Wu was the Marquis of Huguan.
In autumn, peaches and plums bloom.
In the spring of the second year of Empress Lu's reign, she issued an edict saying: Emperor Gao unified the world and granted fiefs and feudal lordships to all the meritorious officials. All the people were safe and sound, and no one was immune from his kindness.
I consider that in the future, due to the passage of time, no one will remember his fame and honor, and will not be able to respect his great righteousness and pass it on to future generations.
Now I want to rank the status of each prince in the court according to the size of his merits. I will hide the merit book in the ancestral temple of Emperor Gao and pass it down from generation to generation. His descendants will inherit their merits and titles hereditary. Please work with the princes to submit a proposal.
Prime Minister Chen Ping reported: I have discussed with Jianghou Zhoubo, Quzhouhou Lishang, Yinhou Guanying, Anguohou Wang Ling, etc., that the princes were favored and were rewarded with rents and food. Your Majesty also extended extra favors and assigned grades based on merit. Please keep the merit book in the high temple.
Empress Lu approved this memorial.
On the 27th of the first lunar month of spring, an earthquake occurred and a landslide occurred in Wudu Road.
On June 30th in summer, there was a partial solar eclipse.
In the seventh month of autumn, Liu Buyi, the king of Hengshan, passed away and eight baht coins were used again.
In the summer of the third year of Empress Lu's reign, the Yangtze River and the Han River overflowed, flooding more than 4,000 houses.
In autumn, stars appear during the day.
In the summer of the fourth year of Empress Lu's reign, the young emperor secretly knew that he was not the empress's biological child, so he complained. The Empress Dowager put him under house arrest in a long alley.
The edict said: Anyone who governs the world and governs the people should have a mind that is as inclusive as heaven and as accommodating as the earth. The emperor governs the people from the perspective of caring for the people. Only when the people are sincere and sincere can they respect the emperor. Only when everyone is united can the country be peaceful and the people are safe.
Today's young emperor has been ill for a long time and has even gone insane. He is unable to inherit the throne, worship in the ancestral temple, guard the country, and assume the important responsibilities of the world.
Please suggest someone who can replace him.
All the ministers said: The Empress Dowager considers the fundamental interests of the country, which is crucial to the stability of the ancestral temple and the country.
The ministers and others bowed their heads and obeyed the edict.
On May 17, Wang Hong of Hengshan was made emperor.
In the spring of Empress Lu's fifth year, Wei Tuo, king of Nanyue, claimed to be Emperor Nanwu.
In the eighth month of autumn, Liu Qiang, king of Huainan, passed away.
In September, Hedong and Shangdang cavalry were mobilized to station in the north.
In the spring of Empress Lu's sixth year, stars appeared in the daytime.
In the fourth month of summer, there is a general amnesty for the whole world.
The Changling Mausoleum of Gaozu was upgraded to two thousand stones.
In June, a city was built around Changling.
The Xiongnu invaded Didao and attacked Heyang.
Exercise the nickel.
In the winter and twelfth month of the seventh year of Empress Lu, the Xiongnu invaded Didao and plundered more than 2,000 households.
On the 18th day of the first lunar month of spring, King Zhao Liu You was imprisoned in the palace and died.
On the 30th, there will be a partial solar eclipse first, and then a total solar eclipse.
Appoint Liang Wang Lu Chan as prime minister and Zhao Wang Lu Lu as general.
Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was made King of Langya.
On the 19th day of the fifth lunar month, an edict was issued saying: Mrs. Zhaoling is the imperial concubine; Marquis Wu Ai and Mrs. Xuan are the brothers and sisters of Emperor Gao.
The posthumous title is not commensurate with the status, please suggest another posthumous title.
Prime Minister Chen Pingping asked Mrs. Zhaoling to be Queen Zhaoling, Marquis Wu Ai to be King Wu'an, and Mrs. Xuan to be Queen Zhaoai. In June, King Zhao Liu Hui committed suicide.
In the ninth month of autumn, King Liu Jian of Yan passed away.
South Vietnam invaded Changsha and sent Longluhou Zhou Zao to lead troops to drive them away.
In the spring of the eighth year of Empress Lu's reign, she made the eunuch Zhang Shiqing a marquis.
The eunuchs in the palace and the Lingcheng in charge of the eunuchs all conferred the title of Marquis of Guannei and received the taxes from their towns.
In summer, the rivers and Han Rivers flooded, destroying more than 10,000 homes.
On the 30th day of the seventh month in the autumn, the Empress Dowager and Empress Lu died in Weiyang Palace. The imperial edict gave each prince a thousand pieces of gold, and distributed them among the ministers, princes, and officials according to their rank, and offered a general amnesty to the whole world.
General Lu Lu and Prime Minister Lu Chan specialize in military and political power. He knew that if he violated Emperor Gao's rule of "no merit-based nomination", he might be harmed by ministers and princes, so he conspired to cause chaos.
At this time, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi Hui, was in Kyoto. He was Lu Lu's son-in-law. When he learned of the plot, he immediately sent someone to inform his brother King Qi, asking him to send troops to the west.
Liu Zhang prepared to work with Taiwei Zhou Bo and Prime Minister Chen Ping as internal correspondents to kill Zhu Lu.
The King of Qi then raised an army, and instigated King Langya and King Liu Ze to mobilize the troops of his country to join forces and march westward.
Lu Chan, Lu Lu and others sent General Guan Ying to lead the troops to stop the attack.
Guan Ying went to Xingyang, sent people to inform the King of Qi and united with him, waiting for the Lu family to launch a coup before carrying out the execution.
Taiwei Zhou Bo conspired with Prime Minister Chen Ping. He believed that Ji, the son of Li Shang, the Marquis of Qu Zhou, was closely related to Lu Lu, so he sent people to force Li Shang to order his son Li Ji to deceive Lu Lu and said: Emperor Gao and Queen Lu jointly established the world. The nine kings established by the Liu family and the three kings established by the Lu family were discussed by the ministers.
The discussions and decisions have been informed to all the princes and kings, and all the princes and princes have expressed their approval.
Today, the Queen Mother has passed away and the Emperor is young. You are not in a hurry to defend your own kingdoms, but you have gathered troops to stay in Kyoto as generals, which has aroused the suspicion of the ministers and princes.
Why not immediately return the general's seal, pass the military power to the Taiwei, ask Liang Wang Lu Chan to return the prime minister's seal, explain it clearly to the ministers, and then return to the feudal country?
In this way, the troops can retreat, the ministers can rest assured, and they can sit back and be king of a country thousands of miles away. This is the benefit of all times!
Lu Lu agreed to his plan and sent someone to tell Lu Chan and his elders.
Some feel uneasy and have different opinions without making a decision.
Lu Lu believed in Li Ji and went with him to persuade Zhu Lu. They arrived at the home of Lu Xu's sister, Empress Lu.
Lu Xunu said angrily: As a general, you gave up military power, and the Lu family will die without a burial place.
She took out all the jewels and jade and threw them in the hall. She said, "I don't have to keep these things for others!"
In August, Cao Lan, Marquis of Pingyang, served as the imperial censor and met with Prime Minister Lu Chan to discuss state affairs.
The doctor ordered Jia Shou to return Qi, so he accused Lu Chan and said: If you didn't go to your feudal country as soon as possible, can you still leave now if you want to?
Tell Lu Chan specifically about Guan Ying's alliance with Qi and Chu.
After Pingyang Hou Cao Lan heard about it, he hurriedly informed Prime Minister Chen Ping and Taiwei Zhou Bo.
Bo wanted to join the Northern Army, but failed. Marquis Jitong of Xiangping was in charge of Fujie, so he falsely sent military orders in the name of the emperor to let Zhou Bo enter the camp and take charge of the Northern Army.
Zhou Bo also sent Li Ji and Dianke Liu Jie to persuade Lu Lu. They said: The emperor sent a Taiwei to take over the Northern Army. If you want everyone to return to the feudal country, you should resign the general and leave, otherwise disaster will be imminent.
Lu Lu took off the general's seal and gave it to Liu Jie, and handed over the military power to Taiwei Zhou Bo.
Zhou Bo entered the Chinese army's tent and sent an order to the army: Support Lu's right side and Liu's left side.
The officers and men were all left-handed.
Zhou Bo then took control of the Northern Army.
However, there were still Southern troops. Prime Minister Chen Ping summoned Marquis Zhu Xu and Liu Zhang to assist Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo sent Liu Zhang to supervise the military gate and Marquis Pingyang to inform the guards not to let Prime Minister Lu Chan enter the palace gate.
Lu Chan did not know that Lu Lu had lost control of the Northern Army and wanted to enter Weiyang Palace to launch a coup.
The guards at the palace gate refused to let him in, so he wandered back and forth outside the palace.
Pingyang Hou immediately reported to Taiwei Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo was afraid that it would be difficult to win. He did not dare to publicly announce the execution of the Lu family, so he told Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang: Enter the palace quickly to defend the emperor.
Liu Zhang asked Zhou Bo to send thousands of troops to the side gate of Weiyang Palace and saw Lu Chan walking around in the court.
At noon, they attacked Lu Chan, but Lu Chan escaped.
At this time, strong winds rose sharply, and Lu Chan's entourage was in chaos. No one dared to resist.
Liu Zhang led his troops to chase Lu Chan, rushed to the official toilet of Langzhong Mansion and killed him.
Liu Zhang had killed Lu Chan, and the Han Emperor sent his attendants to hold the emperor's talisman to comfort Liu Zhang. Liu Zhang wanted to seize the festival, but the attendant refused, so Liu Zhang and his attendants rode in a car together, and rushed into Changle Palace holding the emperor's talisman to kill the Changle Palace guard Lu Gengshi.
Liu Zhang returned to the Northern Army and reported the situation to Zhou Bo.
Zhou E immediately thanked and congratulated Liu Zhang. He said: The one who fears the most is Lu Chan. Now that Lu Chan has been executed, the world will be at peace.
So he beheaded Lu Lu and flogged Lu Xunu.
They sent out men and horses to capture the men and women of Lu, and killed them all regardless of old or young.
The ministers conspired with each other. They thought that the young emperor and his three younger brothers who were kings were not the sons of Emperor Hui, so they killed them all and enthroned Emperor Wen. The story is recorded in the "Book of Han·Zhou Bo and Gao Wu Wang Biography".
Ban Gu commented: When Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty was Xiao Hui and Empress Gao, the world was freed from the pain of war, and the monarchs and ministers wanted to rule by doing nothing. Therefore, Emperor Hui bowed down to bring peace to the world, and Empress Gao used women to preside over government affairs. The world was peaceful without leaving the palace, punishments were used sparingly, and the people could only work on farming, so that they had enough food and clothing.
summary:
Empress Gao, of the Lu family, was the mother of Emperor Hui and assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the realm. After Emperor Hui ascended, she became the Queen Mother. She arranged for her granddaughter, the daughter of Princess Lu Yuan, to be the Queen, who had no children, so a son from a harem beauty was made prince. Upon Emperor Hui's death, this prince became emperor, but due to his youth, Empress Dowager Lu ruled in his stead, granting amnesty and promoting her relatives: four of her brother's sons were made kings, and six others were made princes.

In the first year of her reign, she abolished harsh laws and rewarded the people. She established officials to encourage filial piety. In the second year, she ordered merit rankings for princes to be preserved in the ancestral temple. Natural events occurred: earthquakes, solar eclipses, and floods. In the fourth year, the young emperor, aware he was not the Queen's biological son, complained and was imprisoned. The Empress Dowager replaced him with Liu Hong, King of Hengshan. In the fifth year, Wei Tuo, King of Nanyue, declared himself emperor. In the sixth year, there was a general amnesty and construction at Changling. The Xiongnu invaded in the seventh year, and several kings died or were imprisoned. In the eighth year, Empress Lu died in Weiyang Palace.

After her death, Lu Lu and Lu Chan, holding military and political power, plotted rebellion. Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi, learned of this and coordinated with his brother, King Qi, and officials Zhou Bo and Chen Ping to counter them. King Qi raised an army, and General Guan Ying, sent to stop him, instead allied with him. Zhou Bo, using deception, gained control of the Northern Army by tricking Lu Lu into surrendering his command. Lu Chan, attempting a coup, was killed by Liu Zhang. The Lu family was then exterminated. The ministers, believing the young emperor and his brothers were not Emperor Hui's sons, killed them and enthroned Emperor Wen. Ban Gu noted that under Empress Gao, the world was peaceful, with reduced warfare and punishments, allowing the people to prosper in farming.

translation:
Han Gaozu was a native of Zhongyangli, Fengyi, Peixian County, and his surname was Liu.
His mother once closed her eyes and took a nap on the embankment of a pond, and unexpectedly met the god in her dream.
At that time, there was thunder and lightning and the sky was dark. His father Taigong went to Tangba to meet his mother and saw a dragon crawling on his mother's body.
Soon after, she became pregnant and gave birth to Han Gaozu.
Emperor Gaozu had a high nose, raised eyebrows, a beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
He is kind, generous and broad-minded.
Usually informal, but unwilling to engage in ordinary productive labor.
When he grew up, he served as a minor official and became the chief of Sishang Pavilion. But he looked down upon the officials in the government.
Emperor Gaozu loved wine and sex.
He often went to Wang Po and Wu Ma's hotel to buy wine on credit, and sometimes he was extremely drunk. Wang Po and Wu Ma saw strange phenomena appearing on his body while he was lying drunk.
Every time Gaozu drank wine on credit, the hotel always doubled the price of the wine. Later, seeing his mysterious atmosphere when he was drunk, when settling the wine bill at the end of the year, the two families often tore up the IOUs and waived his wine debt.
Emperor Gaozu once went to Xianyang, the capital of Qin, to do corvee service and saw the majesty of Qin Shihuang with his own eyes. He sighed and said: A real man should be like this!
Lu Gong of Shanfu County was a good friend of the magistrate of Pei County. Because he was hiding from his enemies, he stayed in the magistrate's apartment and later moved his family to Pei County.
Some prominent people in Peizhong heard that a friend of the county magistrate had moved to Pei, and they all went to congratulate him.
Xiao He is the county magistrate's assistant and is responsible for collecting gifts. I say to all the prominent figures: Anyone who can contribute less than one thousand yuan will sit down in the hall.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was the chief of the pavilion at this time. He usually looked down on these people, so he mischievously wrote his name on the red envelope and said "ten thousand yuan in congratulations", but actually did not give a penny.
When the gift package was delivered, Lu Gong was surprised to see the generous gift and went to the gate to greet him personally.
Lu Gong was good at fortune-telling, and when he saw Gaozu's extraordinary appearance, he also respected him very much. He led him into the living room and invited him to sit on the throne.
Xiao He said: Liu Ji usually only talks big words and seldom accomplishes good things.
Emperor Gaozu had long looked down on these prominent figures in the county, so he sat on the throne without humility and looked at ease.
When he was half drunk, Lu Gong asked Gaozu to stay with his eyes. When the banquet was over, he asked Gaozu to stay and slow down.
Lu Gong said to Emperor Gaozu: I have been studying physiognomy since I was young. I have seen many people, but none of them are as noble as yours. I hope you will take care of yourself. I have a biological daughter who is willing to marry you.
After the guests left, Ms. Lu yelled at Mr. Lu and said, "You always said that my daughter was blessed in life and would marry a noble man in the future."
Peiling is on good terms with you, but you want to marry my daughter but you refuse. Why do you want to marry me to Liu Ji today?
Lu Gong smiled and said: This is not what you women know.
In the end, he married his daughter to Gaozu.
Gong Lu's daughter was later Empress Lu, and gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui of Han and Princess Lu Yuan.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty once resigned as the pavilion chief and went home to work on the farm.
Queen Lu and her two children lived in a small shed in the field. An old man who was passing by asked him for water, and Queen Lu even let him have a meal.
The father-in-law looked at Empress Lu's compliments and said: "My wife is a noble person in the world."
Empress Lu asked him to look at the faces of the two children. He looked at Emperor Xiaohui and said: The reason why my wife became a noble person is because of this son.
He looked at Princess Lu Yuan again and said that she would be a noble person in the future.
After the father-in-law left, Gaozu returned from another farmhouse. Empress Lu told him about the past, saying that the father-in-law, my mother and my son were all high-ranking ministers.
Emperor Gaozu asked where his father-in-law was, and Empress Lu said: "He has not gone far."
Emperor Gaozu chased his father-in-law and asked him about his life.
The father-in-law said: Just now, I said that my wife and son are so noble in life, it is all due to your great blessing. Your life is priceless.
Emperor Gaozu quickly thanked him and said: "As the old gentleman said, I will always remember your kindness."
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, the whereabouts of this father-in-law was unknown.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty was the chief of the pavilion and wore a bamboo hat. He sent the thief-catching pavilion soldiers to Xuedi to learn the craftsmanship of making bamboo hats. He often wore this kind of hat and still wore it when he was in a high position. Later, this kind of bamboo hat was called "Liu Shi Guan".
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty sent servants to Lishan Mountain for Peixian County as the pavilion chief. Many servants escaped on the way.
When he thought about Lishan, they might all run away, so he went to Fengxi Zezhong Pavilion, asked the servants to stop and rest, invited everyone to drink, and let all the servants go at night. He said: Everyone should just run away!
I will fly far away from now on!
Among the servants, there were more than ten vigorous men who were willing to go with Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu took advantage of the drunkenness and led everyone to escape from the Zezhong trail, and sent one person to explore the road ahead.
The pathfinder came back and reported: There is a big snake blocking the road ahead. Let's go back.
Emperor Gaozu said drunkenly: Warriors march forward, why should they be afraid?
So he went forward himself, drew his sword and killed the snake. The snake was cut into two pieces, and the road was passable.
After walking for several miles, Emperor Gaozu was drunk and sleepy, so he lay down on the road.
Someone caught up from behind and passed by where Gaozu killed the snake. He saw an old mother crying by the roadside at night.
The man asked the reason, and the old mother said: Someone else killed my son.
This person said: Who killed my mother’s son?
The old mother said: My child is the son of the White Emperor. He turned into a big snake and blocked the road. When he met the son of the Red Emperor, he was beheaded, so I am crying here.
This person thought that the old mother was talking nonsense and wanted to cross-examine her, but she disappeared in the blink of an eye.
When this man caught up with Gaozu, Gaozu had already woken up.
This person told Gaozu about this, and Gaozu was secretly happy and believed that he would become a big success.
Those who followed him also grew in awe of him.
Qin Shihuang once heard someone say: There is the emperor's cloud in the southeast. So the First Emperor made an eastward tour to suppress this cloud.
Emperor Gaozu sometimes hid in the mountains and rivers of Mangdang. When Empress Lu and others went to look for him, it was always easy to find him.
Emperor Gaozu felt strange and asked the reason. Queen Lu said: There is a layer of clouds above where you are staying. If you look for the place where the clouds are, you will find it.
Gaozu was very happy again.
The children of Peizhong also heard this legend, and many people wanted to attach themselves to him.
In the autumn and seventh month of the first year of Qin II, Chen She revolted in Qixian County, arrived in Chendi, and proclaimed himself the king of Chu.
He sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to capture Zhao's territory.
In August, Wu Chen proclaimed himself King of Zhao.
In various counties and counties, major officials were killed one after another in response to Chen She.
In September, the magistrate of Peixian County wanted to respond to Chen She in Peixian County. His aides Xiao He and Cao Shen came forward and said: As an official of the Qin Dynasty, you now want to betray the Qin Dynasty and lead the children of Peizhong to revolt. I am afraid that everyone will not listen.
