He marched eastward to Xianyang, surrounded the waste hill that Zhang Han refused to defend, and then sent various generals to expand his territory.
Qi general Tian Rong was furious when he heard that Xiang Yu had moved King Tianshi of Qi to Jiaodong and made Tiandu the king of Qi. He led the Qi troops to intercept Tiandu, but Tiandu was defeated and surrendered to Chu.
In June, Tian Rong killed Tian Shi and proclaimed himself king of Qi.
At this time, Peng Yue garrisoned troops in Juye, with more than 10,000 soldiers but no one to belong to.
Tian Rong awarded Peng Yue the seal of general and ordered him to attack from Liang.
Peng Yue killed Tian An, the king of Jibei, and Tian Rong occupied the entire area of ​​Qi, Jibei, and Jiaodong.
Han Guang, King of Yan, also refused to move to Liaodong.
In the eighth month of autumn, Zang Tu, the new king of Yan, killed Han Guang and occupied his territory.
Sima Xin, king of Sai, and Dong Yi, king of Zhai, both surrendered to the Han.
At the beginning, the son after Xiang Liang established Korea became the king of Han, and Zhang Liang became the disciple of the king of Han.
Xiang Yu did not allow Zhang Liang to return to Han because he had followed the King of Han, and King Cheng of Han had not made any military exploits. He took him to Pengcheng and executed him.
At this time, Xiang Yu heard that the King of Han had annexed Guanzhong, and that Qi and Liang had rebelled against him. He was furious, so he sent Zheng Chang, the original Wu commander, as the King of Han to resist the Han soldiers.
He ordered Xiao Gongjiao to attack Peng Yue, but was defeated by Peng Yue.
During this period, Zhang Liang was touring Han and sent a letter to Xiang Yu, saying: The king of Han wants to capture Guanzhong. If he fulfills his promise to enter Guanzhong first, he will stop advancing and will not dare to continue to advance eastward.
Therefore, Xiang Yu had no intention of going west for the time being, and instead attacked Qi Wang Tianrong in the north.
In September, the King of Han sent generals Xue Ou and Wang Sui out of Wuguan to join the troops guarding Wang Ling in Nanyang, and went from Nanyang to Pei to meet the Taigong and Empress Lu.
When Xiang Yu heard the news, he sent troops to intercept them in Yangxia. Wang Ling and others were unable to advance.
In the winter of October of the second year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu sent Wang Yingbu of Jiujiang to kill Emperor Yi in Chen County.
Chen Yuhuai resented Xiang Yu for not making him king, so he asked Qi King Tian Rong to borrow troops to attack Changshan King Zhang Er.
Zhang Er was defeated and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The king of Han gave him a grand courtesy.
Chen Yu welcomed Dai Wang Xie and returned Zhao land, and Dai Wang Xie made Chen Yu the acting king.
Zhang Liang secretly came to the King of Han from Han, and the King of Han made him the Marquis of Chengxin.
The King of Han arrived in Shaanxi County to comfort the elders outside the Pass.
King Shenyang of Henan surrendered to the Han, and the Han established Henan County here.
Han Taiwei Han Xin was sent to attack Han, and Han King Zheng Chang surrendered.
In November, Taiwei Han was granted the title of King of Han.
The King of Han returned to Hanzhong, with his capital in Yueyang, and sent generals to seize the enemy's land and conquer Longxi.
Anyone who leads ten thousand people or a county to surrender will be granted the title of Ten Thousand Households.
Repair the river fort.
In the Qin Dynasty, farmers were allowed to cultivate the original royal zoological and botanical gardens and pools.
In the first month of the spring of the third year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu attacked Tian Rong in Chengyang. Tian Rong was defeated and went to Pingyuan. The people of Pingyuan killed Tian Rong.
All the people of Qi surrendered to Chu, and the people of Chu burned Qi's cities and counties, and the people of Qi rebelled against Chu.
The king of Han sent generals to conquer the north and captured Zhang Ping, the younger brother of King Yong.
Forgive sinners.
On February 5, the people were ordered to abolish the Sheji Altar, a symbol of the Qin Dynasty's political power, and to erect the Sheji Altar of the Han Dynasty.
Show kindness and bestow honor and wealth on the people.
The people of Shu Han were exempted from rent and taxes for two years because of the heavy burden of supplying military supplies.
If a soldier from Guanzhong joins the army, his family will be exempted from taxes for one year.
For ordinary people who are over fifty years old, have high moral standing and can lead everyone to do good, they are arranged to be three elders, one for each township.
One of the three elders was selected as the three elders of the county, who discussed political affairs with the county magistrate, county magistrate, and county lieutenant, and exempted them from military service.
October is regarded as the month to comfort the people with wine and meat.
In March, the King of Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Bao of Wei returned and led his troops to go out with the King of Han.
He conquered Hanoi, captured King Qiong of Yin, and established Hanoi County.
When the soldiers came to Xiuwu, Chen Ping escaped from the Chu army and submitted to the king of Han.
The king of Han talked with him and appreciated him very much. He was appointed as a sergeant to monitor the generals.
Crossing Pingyinjin in the south and arriving at Luoyang, Dong Gong, the third old man in Xincheng, stopped his horse and said to the king of Han: "I heard that those who follow the virtues will prosper, and those who go against the virtues will perish. If the troops are unknown, their actions will not be successful."
So it is said: Only by announcing the enemy's crimes can the enemy be defeated.
Xiang Yu has always been immoral and killed the Righteous Emperor, making him a sinner in the world.
If you are benevolent, you don't need to use bravery and the world will obey you. If you are righteous, you don't need to use force and the world will be convinced. Let the three armies put on the filial piety for the Righteous Emperor, and send a message to the princes, explaining that the troops are used to kill the Righteous Emperor and fight against the rebels in the east. In this way, people all over the world will respect the great virtue.
This is a righteous act that can be followed by the Three Kings.
The King of Han said: It is extremely correct. I would not understand it if it were not for the teachings of the old man.
So the king of Han mourned Emperor Yi, cried loudly according to the funeral ceremony, and mourned publicly for three days. Send envoys to all the princes: The world will establish a righteous emperor and face the north.
Now Xiang Yu killed the Righteous Emperor in the south of the Yangtze River, which was really an act of rebellion.
I mourned personally, and the whole army, all dressed in plain clothes, gathered all the soldiers from Guanzhong, gathered the soldiers of Sanhe, and went south along the Han River into the Yangtze River, hoping to follow the princes and kings to arrest the culprits of the regicide.
In the fourth month of summer, Tian Heng, the younger brother of King Tian Rong of Qi, recovered tens of thousands of people who had been defeated by Xiang Yu, and made Tian Guang, the son of Tian Rong, the king of Qi.
Although Xiang Yu had already heard about the Han king's eastward advance, he had already sent all his troops to attack Chu. He wanted to destroy Qi and then attack the Han army. Therefore, the Han king took the opportunity to annex the troops of Wei, Yin and other five princes and attack Chu eastward.
When the troops arrived in Waihuang, Peng Yue led 30,000 people to surrender to the Han.
The King of Han made Peng Yue Prime Minister of Wei. Let him pacify Liang Di.
The king of Han then entered Pengcheng, the capital of Chu Xiang. Collected Xiang Yu's beauties and treasures, and held a cocktail party to celebrate the victory.
After hearing the news, Xiang Yu sent another general to attack, and led 30,000 elite troops from Huling, Lu, to Xiao County. They attacked the Han army in the early morning and fought on the Sui River east of Pengcheng Lingbi.
The soldiers of Chu surrounded the king of Han three times.
A strong wind came from the northwest, breaking trees and breaking houses, flying sand and rocks, making the day look like night, and the Chu army was in chaos. The king of Han took advantage of the chaos and broke through the siege with dozens of cavalry to escape.
Traveling through Peixian County, he sent people to look for his family members, but the whole family had fled and their whereabouts were unknown.
The King of Han met his son Xiaohui and his daughter Lu Yuan on the way, and they boarded a chariot and left in panic.
The Chu cavalry chased the King of Han. Seeing the critical situation, the King of Han pushed his children out of the carriage.
Teng Gong put the two men in the car again and finally escaped from the tiger's mouth.
Shen Shiqi, the father of the Han Dynasty, the Grand Duke, and his wife, Empress Lu, escaped from the trail and met the Chu army. Xiang Yu placed them as hostages in the army.
When the princes saw that the Han army was completely defeated, they all fled.
King Xin of Sai and King Yi of Zhai surrendered to Chu, and King Qiong of Yin died.
Zhou Luhou, the brother-in-law of the King of Han, led troops and horses to station in Xiayi County, and the King of Han went there to settle down.
Gradually the scattered soldiers were gathered and stationed in Dang County.
The king of Han went west through Liang and arrived at Yucheng County. He said to Sui He, who asked to see him, "Master, go and persuade Yingbu, king of Jiujiang, to raise an army to rebel against Chu. Xiang Yu will leave his troops to attack Yingbu."
As long as Xiang Yu can keep his troops for a few months, I will surely conquer the world.
Sui He was ordered to persuade Yingbu, and as expected, Yingbu rebelled against Chu.
In the fifth month, the troops of the King of Han were assembled in Xingyang. Xiao He recruited all the old, weak and underage people in Guanzhong to join his army.
Han Xin also gathered his soldiers to join forces with the King of Han. At this time, the King of Han regained his military power.
He fought with the Chu army between Jing and Suo in the south of Xingyang and defeated the Chu army.
The Han army built walls on both sides of the road leading to the river to transport grain from Aocang, which was near the river and leaning on the mountain.
At this time, Wei Wangbao asked for leave and returned to his hometown in the name of visiting his mother's illness.
After returning home, he blocked the ferry and defended the Chu army against the Han army.
In the sixth month, the king of Han returned to his capital, Yueyang. On the sixth day of the lunar month, he established the crown prince and pardoned the sinners.
He ordered all the sons of the princes in Guanzhong to gather in Yueyang as guards.
They diverted water to attack Feiqiu, but Feiqiu surrendered and King Yong Zhanghan committed suicide.
Yongzhou was pacified, and there were more than eighty counties, located on the river, Weinan, Zhongdi, Longxi, and Shangjun.
The ancestral officials were ordered to worship the mountains and rivers of gods in the four directions of heaven and earth, and to perform ancestral sacrifices on time.
Send sergeants from Guan to guard the border fortress.
At this time, there was a great famine in Guanzhong. Dendrobium rice was worth tens of thousands of dollars, and people were eating people.
Arrangements were made for hungry people to gather in Shu and Han areas to survive the famine.
In the eighth month of autumn, the King of Han arrived in Xingyang and said to Li Shiqi: Please use your kind words to persuade King Bao of Wei. If the persuasion is successful, I will make you the Marquis of Ten Thousand Households in Wei.
When he was ordered to go there, King Bao of Wei refused to obey.
The king of Han sent Han Xin as prime minister of the left, and together with Cao Shen and Guan Ying, he attacked the king of Wei.
After eating his reward, the king of Han asked: "Who is the general of Wei?"
Eat it and answer: Bai Zhi.
The King of Han said: This is a young boy who lacks combat experience and is no match for Han Xin. Who is the knight? Shi Qi answered: Feng Jing.
The King of Han said: He is the son of Qin general Feng Wuze. Although he is talented, he is no match for Guan Ying.
Who is the step general? Eat it and say: Xiang it.
The king of Han said: He is no match for Cao Shen.
I don't have to worry anymore.
In September, Han Xin and others captured Wei Wangbao and escorted him to Xingyang.
The Wei region was pacified and Hedong, Taiyuan and Shangdang counties were established.
Han Xin sent an envoy to ask the King of Han for 30,000 troops, willing to destroy Yan and Zhao in the north, attack Qi in the east, and cut off Chu's grain road in the south.
The King of Han assigned Han Xin soldiers according to their numbers.
In the winter of the third year in October, Han Xin and Zhang Erdong went to Jingxing to attack Zhao, killed Chen Yu, captured Zhao Wangxie, and established Changshan and Daijun.
October 30th, solar eclipse.
On November 30th, there was another solar eclipse.
Sui He had persuaded Yingbu to join the Han, so Yingbu raised his troops to attack Chu. Chu sent Xiang Sheng and Long Qie to attack Yingbu, but Yingbu failed in the battle.
In December, Yingbu and Suihe took a small road to ask for help from the King of Han. The King of Han divided his troops to help, and together they withdrew their troops to Chenggao.
Xiang Yu repeatedly seized the passage for Han soldiers to obtain food, and the Han army was short of food. The king of Han discussed with Li Shiqi how to weaken Chu Xiang's power.
After Shi Qi wanted to establish the Six Kingdoms, he would be the wing of the Han Dynasty. The King of Han would engrave the seals of the Six Kingdoms and send Shi Qi to enfeoff.
Asked Zhang Liang's opinion, Zhang Liang believed that there were eight major problems in enfeoffing the six countries.
The King of Han immediately put down the bowls and chopsticks he was eating and said: "You have almost ruined my big event by eating this ignorant boy!"
An order was sent to quickly destroy the engraved seal of the Six Kingdoms.
He also asked Chen Ping for advice and followed Chen Ping's strategy. He gave Chen Ping 40,000 catties of gold to sow discord between Chu Xiang and his ministers.
In April of summer, Xiang Yu besieged Xingyang, the military center of the Han Dynasty. The king of Han requested peace, with Xingyang as the boundary and the west as the Han Dynasty.
Fan Zeng, his father-in-law, advised Xiang Yu to attack Xingyang, which made the king of Han deeply uneasy.
At this time, Chen Ping had bribed some generals of the Chu army to slander Fan Zeng. As expected, Xiang Yu became suspicious of Fan Zeng.
Fan Zeng left the Chu camp in anger, and died of gangrene in anger.
In May, General Ji Xin said to the King of Han: The situation is extremely serious!
The minister pretended to be the king to deceive the Chu army, so that the king could take advantage of the opportunity and escape from the siege.
So Chen Ping released more than 2,000 women at the east gate of Xingyang at night, causing Chu soldiers to chase them in all directions.
Ji Xin pretended to be the King of Han and rode in the chariot. King Huang Gai's banner came out of the east gate and he said: "The food supply has been exhausted. The King of Han surrendered to Chu."
The Chu army shouted "Long live victory" and went to the east of the city to watch the King of Han surrender, so the King of Han was able to lead dozens of cavalry out of the west gate and escape.
The imperial censors Zhou Ke, Wei Bao and Cong Gong were sent to guard Xingyang.
When Xiang Yu saw it was Ji Xin, he shouted loudly: "Where is the King of Han?"
Ji Xin replied calmly: He has already left far away.
Xiang Yu burned Ji Xin to death.
Zhou Ke and Cong Gong in the city discussed with each other and said: Wei Bao is a rebel king and it is difficult to defend the city.
Then he killed Wei Bao.
The King of Han walked out of the siege of Xingyang and marched to Chenggao. From Chenggao he entered the Pass and gathered troops and horses to prepare for another eastern expedition.
Yuan Sheng suggested to the King of Han: Han and Chu have been at a stalemate in Xingyang for two years, and Han has always been passive.
I hope that when the king's troops leave Wuguan, King Xiang will definitely lead his troops south, and the king will maintain a stalemate with them in deep ditches and high forts, so that the Han army in Xingyang Chenggao will have a chance to rest and reorganize.
He also sent Han Xin and others to stabilize Zhao in Hebei and unite Yan and Qi, and then the king sent troops to Xingyang again.
In this case, Chu will lengthen its defense line and disperse its forces.
After the Han soldiers have rested and recuperated, they will definitely defeat the Chu army if they fight again.
The King of Han accepted this clever plan and sent troops between Wan County and Ye County to conduct guerrilla warfare with Yingbu here.
Xiang Yu heard that the King of Han had garrisoned troops in Wan, and he indeed led his troops to attack south, but the King of Han stood firm and refused to fight with him.
In this month, Peng Yue crossed the Suishui River and fought with Chu generals Xiang Sheng and Xue Gong in Xia Qiong. They defeated the Chu soldiers and killed Xue Gong. Xiang Yu sent Zhong Gong to guard Chenggao and personally led his troops eastward to retaliate against Peng Yue.
The king of Han took advantage of the opportunity and led his troops northward, defeated the Chu general Zhong Gong who was stationed in Chenggao, and regained Chenggao.
In June, Xiang Yu had defeated and expelled Peng Yue. When he heard that the Han soldiers had captured Chenggao, he led his troops to attack Xingyang City to the west and captured the general Zhou Ke alive.
Zhou Ke angrily scolded: "If you don't surrender to the Han Dynasty quickly, you will become a prisoner soon!"
You are no match for the King of Han.
Xiang Yu killed Zhou Ke, executed Duke Cong, captured Han Wangxin, and then besieged Chenggao.
The king of Han fled in a hurry. He and Duke Teng drove out of the north gate of Chenggao, crossed the Yellow River north, and stayed in Xiaoxiuwu for the night.
In the early morning, claiming to be the envoy of the King of Han, he rushed into Zhang Er and Han Xin's positions and personally took control of the troops.
He sent Zhang Er to Zhao in the north to mobilize Han troops.
In autumn and July, a comet appears over Big Horn.
The King of Han regained his strength after capturing Han Xin's army.
In August, he led his troops to the south near the Yellow River and garrisoned in Xiaoxiuwu, hoping to fight the Chu army again.
Zheng Zhong, the doctor, dissuaded the King of Han and suggested that he should dig deep ditches and high forts and not fight the Chu army.
The King of Han followed his plan and sent Lu Wan and Liu Jia with 20,000 infantry and several hundred cavalry to cross the river from Baimajin into the Chu land. They assisted Peng Yue in burning the Chu army's grain and grass reserves. He also defeated the Chu army in the west of Yan County and captured seventeen cities in Suiyang and Waihuang.
In September, Xiang Yu said to Cao Jiu, the commander-in-chief of Haichunhou: Be careful to guard Chenggao.
Even if the King of Han wants to challenge him, you must not fight him. Just don't let the Han army advance eastward.
I will definitely be able to pacify Liang within fifteen days and then meet up with the general.
So Xiang Yu led his troops eastward to attack Peng Yue.
The king of Han sent Li Shiqi to persuade Qi Wang Tian Guang to stop the army's garrison and unite with the Han army.
In the winter and tenth month of the fourth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Han Xin used Kuai Tong's strategy to attack the Qi army by surprise.
The King of Qi killed Li Shengpan and fled eastward to Gaomi.
Xiang Yu heard that Han Xin had defeated the Qi army and wanted to attack the Chu army, so he sent Long Qie to lead his army to rescue the Qi army.
Sure enough, the Han army challenged the Chu army in Chenggao many times. The Chu army could not hold out and sent people to insult the Chu army for many days. The great commander Cao Jiu was furious and led his troops across the Si River. The Chu army had just crossed the halfway point when the Han army attacked, defeated the Chu army and captured all the gold and jade belongings of the Chu state.
The great Sima Cao Jiu and the Chang Shi Xin both committed suicide on the banks of Si River.
The King of Han led his troops across the Yellow River and reoccupied Chenggao. He garrisoned troops in Guangwu and transported grain from Aocang.
Xiang Yu captured more than ten cities in Liang. When he heard that Haichunhou was defeated by the Han army, he led his troops back.
The Han army was besieging Zhong Limei in the east of Xingyang. When they heard that Xiang Yu's troops had arrived, they all fled to a dangerous place.
Xiang Yu also garrisoned troops in Guangwu and confronted the Han army.
The young are tired of marching and fighting, and the old and weak are exhausted from transporting food and wages.
The King of Han and Xiang Yu went to Guangwu Stream to have a conversation.
Xiang Yu was about to challenge the King of Han to a decisive battle. The King of Han listed Xiang Yu's crimes and said: At the beginning, Xiang Yu and I both accepted the order of King Huai of Chu and agreed to conquer Guanzhong first and become the King of Guanzhong.
You Xiang Yu broke the agreement and made me the king of Shu Han. This is the first crime.
You, Xiang Yu, falsely conveyed the king's will and killed the champion of Qingzi, claiming to be a general. This is the second crime.
You, Xiang Yu, have rescued Zhao and should repay King Huai, but instead you coerce the troops of the princes to enter the pass with you without permission. This is the third crime.
King Huai agreed not to burn, kill or loot when entering Qin. Xiang Yu burned down the palaces of the Qin Dynasty, dug up the emperor's tomb, and took the finances of Qin for private use. This is the fourth crime.
He also killed Prince Qin Ying who had surrendered. This was the fifth crime.
Cruelly and deceptively, he buried 200,000 Qin soldiers alive in Xin'an, but then made their general king. This is the sixth crime.
The generals were sealed in good places, but they moved to drive away the original princes and kings, and allowed the subordinates to rebel in order to fight for the throne. This is the seventh crime.
After driving Emperor Yi out of Pengcheng, he established his capital there, seized the land of the King of Han, and annexed the Chu lands of Liang Dynasty, all of which were assigned to himself. This is the eighth crime.
He sent people to secretly kill Emperor Yi in Jiangnan. This was the ninth crime.
You are a minister but you murder the monarch and kill those who have surrendered. You govern unfairly. You uphold the covenant but do not keep your word. You are not tolerated by the world and are treasonous. This is the 10th offense.
I lead the rebels to fight against the princes, and I send a convicted criminal to beat you, so why bother me to challenge you in a one-on-one fight?
Xiang Yu was furious and shot the King of Han with a crossbow from an ambush. The King of Han was injured in the chest, but he touched his feet and said: "This thief shot my toes."
The King of Han fell down due to an arrow injury. Zhang Liang asked the King of Han to get up and go to condolences the soldiers, so as to stabilize the soldiers and prevent the Chu army from attacking after the victory.
When the King of Han went to inspect the military camp, his condition worsened and he immediately rushed back to Chenggao.
In November, Han Xin and Guan Ying defeated the Chu army, killed the Chu army general Long Qie, chased them to Chengyang, and captured Qi Wang Tian Guang.
Tian Heng, Prime Minister of Qi, proclaimed himself King of Qi and defected to Peng Yue.
The king of Han made Zhang Er the king of Zhao.
After the King of Han recovered from his illness, he traveled westward to the Pass and came to Yueyang, where he visited the local elders and held a banquet.
The head of Sima Xin, the former king of Si, was cut off and hung in Yueyang Market for public display.
After staying for four days, he returned to the army and garrisoned in Guangwu.
Guanzhong soldiers rushed to the Chu-Han battlefield in large numbers, while Peng Yue and Tian Heng occupied the Liang area, attacking and harassing the Chu army and cutting off their food channels.
After Han Xin captured Qi, he sent someone to tell the king of Han: Qi is close to Chu and its power is too small. If I don't become an acting king, I'm afraid I won't be able to stabilize Qi.
The king of Han was furious and wanted to attack him.
Zhang Liang said: It is better to take the opportunity to make him the king of Qi and let him guard the land of Qi.
In the second month of spring, Zhang Liang was sent with the royal seal to make Han Xin the king of Qi.
In the seventh month of autumn, Yingbu was made King of Huainan.
In August, the calculation method began to be implemented.
The Beibei and Yan people sent a group of brave cavalry to assist the Han army.
The King of Han ordered: If a sergeant unfortunately dies in battle, a special person will be sent to dress him, put him in a coffin, and send him back to his hometown.
All the people in the world have sincerely surrendered.
Xiang Yu knew that he lacked helpers and was about to run out of food and grass. Han Xin led troops to attack the Chu army many times, and he was very worried.
The King of Han sent Duke Hou to Chu to persuade Xiang Yu to release the Grand Duke and Empress Lu.
So Xiang Yu and the King of Han agreed to divide the world equally, using the chasm as the dividing line, with the west returning to Han and the east returning to Chu.
In September, Xiang Yu released the Grand Duke and Empress Lu, led his soldiers to relieve the difficulties in Xingyang, and then returned eastward.
The King of Han also had plans to return west to Guanzhong, but Zhang Liang and Chen Ping dissuaded him, saying: The King of Han now owns most of the world, and princes from all over the country have come to join him. But now the Chu army is exhausted and has run out of ammunition and food. This is really the best opportunity given by God to destroy Chu. If we let go of Chu people at this time, we will be raising tigers and causing trouble.
The king of Han listened to their opinions.
summary:
Han Gaozu, originally named Liu Ji, was born in Peixian County. His mother dreamed of a god during a thunderstorm, and his father saw a dragon on her, leading to his birth. He had a distinctive appearance with a high nose, raised eyebrows, a beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh. He was generous and broad-minded, disliking ordinary labor, and served as a minor official, often looking down on others. He loved wine and women, frequently buying wine on credit from Wang Po and Wu Ma, who noticed strange phenomena when he was drunk and eventually forgave his debts. While performing corvée in Xianyang, he saw Qin Shihuang and declared, "A real man should be like this."

Lu Gong, a friend of the Pei County magistrate, moved to the area, and Liu Ji falsely claimed a gift of ten thousand yuan at a gathering. Lu Gong, skilled in physiognomy, recognized Liu Ji's noble appearance and married his daughter to him, despite his wife's objections. This daughter later became Empress Lu, mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. After resigning as pavilion chief, Liu Ji worked on a farm. An old man predicted that Empress Lu and her children would be noble, and that Liu Ji's destiny was priceless. Liu Ji later wore a distinctive bamboo hat, known as the "Liu Shi Guan."

As pavilion chief, Liu Ji was tasked with sending servants to Lishan, but many escaped. He released them all, and over ten strong men chose to follow him. While fleeing, he killed a large snake blocking the path. An old woman later claimed the snake was the son of the White Emperor, killed by the son of the Red Emperor, which Liu Ji took as a sign of his destiny. Qin Shihuang heard of an emperor's cloud in the southeast and toured to suppress it. Empress Lu could always find Liu Ji by following a cloud above his hiding place, further convincing others of his destiny.

In the first year of Qin II, Chen She rebelled, and the Pei County magistrate considered joining. Xiao He and Cao Shen advised him to recruit fugitives, including Liu Ji. When Liu Ji arrived with followers, the magistrate reneged and tried to kill Xiao He and Cao Shen, who fled to Liu Ji. Liu Ji shot a message into the city, urging the elders to kill the magistrate and join the rebellion. They did so, and Liu Ji was elected Duke of Pei after multiple refusals. He honored Huangdi and Chiyou, used red flags, and quickly expanded his army to 3,000 men. Other rebellions followed, including Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu in Wu.

Liu Ji's forces grew through various battles, including victories at Huling, Fangyu, and Xue. He faced setbacks, such as Yong Chi's betrayal to Wei, but regained Feng. He joined Xiang Liang, who made Sun Mixin King of Chu Huai. After Xiang Liang's death, Liu Ji and Xiang Yu moved King Huai to Pengcheng. King Huai appointed Liu Ji as Marquis of Wu'an and ordered that whoever first entered Guanzhong would be king. Liu Ji was chosen for his kindness, while Xiang Yu was deemed too violent.

Liu Ji advanced westward, defeating Qin forces and accepting surrenders. He entered Wuguan and reached Bashui, where Qin Prince Ying surrendered. Liu Ji spared him, entered Xianyang, and issued the "three chapters of the law," abolishing harsh Qin laws. He refused gifts from the people, winning their support. He guarded Hangu Pass against Xiang Yu, who grew angry. Xiang Yu's uncle Xiang Bo warned Zhang Liang, leading to the Hongmen Banquet, where Liu Ji narrowly escaped assassination. Xiang Yu later entered Xianyang, killed Prince Ying, and burned the palaces, disappointing the people.

Xiang Yu violated the agreement, making Liu Ji King of Han in Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong, while dividing Guanzhong among three Qin generals. Liu Ji resented this but was dissuaded from attacking. He burned the plank road to show no intention of leaving Hanzhong. Han Xin, recommended by Xiao He, was made general and advised an eastern campaign. Liu Ji defeated Zhang Han and expanded, while rebellions by Tian Rong and others weakened Xiang Yu.

Liu Ji's forces grew, and he captured Pengcheng, but Xiang Yu counterattacked, defeating him. Liu Ji regrouped in Xingyang, using strategies like Sui He persuading Yingbu to rebel. He faced a famine in Guanzhong and sent Han Xin to conquer Wei, Zhao, and Qi. After a series of battles, including the siege of Xingyang, Liu Ji escaped using a decoy. He regained Chenggao and confronted Xiang Yu at Guangwu, listing ten crimes. Xiang Yu shot him, but he feigned a minor injury.

Liu Ji recovered, made Han Xin King of Qi, and Yingbu King of Huainan. With Xiang Yu's resources dwindling, they agreed to divide the world using the chasm. However, Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised Liu Ji to attack, leading to Xiang Yu's eventual defeat.

In the winter of tenth month of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu, the King of Han pursued Xiang Yu to the south of Yangxia, stopped advancing, and made an appointment with Qi King Han Xin and Wei Xiangguo Peng Yue to attack the Chu army. I'm afraid that if the owner doesn't respect talents, talents will not be discovered and put into use!
Today, I rely on the power of God and the support of the wise men and officials to conquer the world and become the unification of Liu and Han. I want to pass on the legacy for a long time and worship the ancestral temple from generation to generation without dying.
All the virtuous men and women have helped me to rule the world together, but you can't share the glory with me, okay?
As long as all the wise men and officials can work with me to govern the country, I will definitely give them high officials and generous salaries.
I am announcing this to the world so that everyone knows my intention.
The imperial censor Dafu Chang received the edict and forwarded it to the prime minister. The prime minister praised Marquis Xiao He and received the edict and sent it to all the princes and kings. The censor Zhongcheng received the edict and sent it to the governors of various places. All the wise and virtuous people recognized by various places should come to encourage them in person and send a car to Kyoto. They should first report to the prime minister's palace and fill in their occupation and age.
Those who conceal their talents and fail to report them will be dismissed from their posts after being discovered.
If you are old, tired or sick, there is no need to send them.
In March, Liang Wang Pengyue rebelled and was executed by the three clans.
The edict said: Choose someone who can be the king of Liang and the king of Huaiyang.
King Lu Wan of Yan and Prime Minister Xiao He asked Prince Hui to be crowned Prince of Liang, and Prince Friend to be Prince of Huaiyang.
Dongjun was abandoned and part of it was transferred to Liangdi; Yingchuan County was abandoned and part of it was transferred to Huaiyang.
In April of summer, I returned to Kyoto from Luoyang.
It was ordered that all people from Feng County who moved to Guanzhong were exempted from corvee for life.
In May, an edict was issued saying: It is the custom of the Cantonese people to fight with each other. In the past, the Qin Dynasty moved people from the Central Plains to enrich the three counties of Guilin, Xiangjun and Nanhai, so that they could mix with hundreds of Cantonese.
Later, when the world was about to punish Qin, Zhao Tuo, the captain of Nanhai, governed here for a long time and was very organized. The people who moved from the Central Plains were not harmed, and the trend of fighting among the Cantonese people stopped. This was all due to Zhao Tuo's good governance.
Now Zhao Tuo is made King of Southern Guangdong.
He sent Lu Jia to give Zhao Tuo a seal ribbon.
Zhao Tuo kowtowed and proclaimed himself a minister.
In June, it was decreed that all soldiers who entered Shu, Han, and Guanzhong from Emperor Gaozu would be exempted from hard labor for life.
In the seventh month of autumn, Wang Ying of Huainan rebelled.
The emperor asked the generals about their plans, and Duke Teng said that Duke Yin Xue, the former commander of Chu, had already had a clever plan.
The emperor immediately summoned him and Xue Gong analyzed the situation in Yingbu. The emperor was very satisfied and granted Xue Gong a thousand households.
The king and the prime minister were ordered to choose a person who could be made king of Huainan, and the ministers asked the prince to make his son the king.
The emperor then mobilized 30,000 soldiers from Shangjun, Beidi, Longxi Chariots, Bashu warriors and imperial guards to guard the crown prince and stationed troops in Bashang.
Yingbu did not go as Xue Gong expected. He attacked Jing King Liu Jia from the east, forced the Jing King's troops to surrender, crossed the Huai River to attack Chu, and Chu King Liu Jiao retreated to Xue.
The emperor pardoned all prisoners in the world who were guilty of less than capital crimes and joined the army; at the same time, he recruited soldiers from the princes and the emperor personally conquered Yingbu.
In the winter of the twelfth year in October, the emperor defeated Yingbu's soldiers in Huifou. Yingbu fled, and the emperor's faction gave chase.
When the emperor returned to the capital, he passed through his hometown of Peixian County and stopped temporarily. He held a banquet in Peigong and entertained all his old friends, fathers and children to drink.
He summoned one hundred and twenty men from Peizhong and taught them how to sing.
When the wine was in full swing, the emperor played a musical instrument and sang to himself: The wind is strong and the clouds are flying/Vega the four seas and return home/And the fierce warriors guard the four directions!
The sons and daughters all sang together.
The emperor danced to the song, was generous and sentimental, and shed tears.
To Peidi’s father and brother: Wanderers always miss their hometown.
Although I live in Guanzhong, after my death, my soul will still miss my hometown in Peidi.
Recalling that I served as Pei Gong and raised troops to overthrow the violent Qin Dynasty, and then conquered the world, I would like to use Pei as my Tang Muyi, exempt the people of Pei from corvee, and not pay taxes to the court from generation to generation.
The elders and old friends of Peixian County had a great time drinking together and telling stories about the emperor's past for fun.
More than ten days later, the emperor wanted to resign, but Peidi's father and brother insisted on staying.
The emperor said: I have many followers, and my father and brother cannot provide for them.
Just left.
Thousands of people in Peizhong sent the emperor to the west of the county and presented him with farewell gifts.
The emperor stayed again and opened his tent to entertain those who were leaving for three days.
The fathers and sons of Peixian County all kowtowed in gratitude and said: Peixian County was exempted from taxes and servitude by the emperor's favor, but Feng County failed to receive the favor. I hope the emperor will take care of Feng County.
The emperor said: Feng County is the place where I grew up, and I will never forget it.
I don't want to take care of him just because Yong Chi once rebelled against me here and returned to Wei.
Pei's father and brother repeatedly requested, and the emperor agreed to exempt Feng County from taxes and servitude, just like Pei.
The Han generals attacked the remaining troops of Yingbu in the north and south of Taoshui River, wiped out all the rebels, and pursued Yingbu in Fanyang.
Zhou Boping established the land of dynasty and killed Chen Yu in the city.
The emperor issued an edict saying: Wu is a country in ancient times. In the past, King Jing had his land, but today King Jing has died and has no heir.
I want to reestablish the king of Wu. Please recommend someone who can be appointed.
Changsha's royal ministers and others said: "Peihou Liu Bi is mature and prudent. Please make him king of Wu."
After the seal was sealed, the emperor summoned Liu Bi and said: "You look rebellious."
He put his hand on his back and said: "In the fifty years after the Han Dynasty, there was chaos in the southeast. Should it be your fault?"
But now we are a family with the same surname as Liu Han, so you must not rebel.
Liu Bi kowtowed in fear and said, "I don't dare."
In November, he returned to Kyoto from Huainan and passed through Lu, where he sacrificed a whole cow to Confucius.
In December, an edict was issued stating: The Emperor of Qin, King Yin of Chu, King Anxi of Wei, King Min of Qi, and King Daoxiang of Zhao all have no heirs. Twenty families are now designated to guard the tomb of the First Emperor of Qin, ten families each for the kings of Chu, Wei, and Qi, and five families each for the kings of Zhao and Wei Xinling. Their mission is to manage and guard the tombs and exempt them from other taxes and duties.
When Chen Yi surrendered and reported that Chen Yi was rebelling, King Lu Wan of Yan sent people to Chen Yi's office to participate in the conspiracy.
The emperor sent Biyang Hou Shenshi to invite Wan to return to the capital, but Lu Wan said that he was ill and could not come.
Shi Qi told the emperor that Lu Wan might join in the rebellion.
In the spring and February of the following year, Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo were sent to lead troops to attack Lu Wan.
The emperor issued a proclamation saying: King Yan and I have a very close relationship, and I love him like a son. I heard that he and Chen? There was collusion, but I thought it was untrue, so I sent someone to ask him to come to Kyoto to explain it. Lu Wan said he was ill and couldn't come, so he participated in Chen?
The conspiracy is clearly revealed. The officials and people of Yan are innocent, and every official in Yan who has more than 600 shi will be promoted to one rank.
Those who have connections with Lu Wan and are now able to abandon the dark side and turn to the bright side will be exempted from prosecution and will also receive a knighthood. He also ordered the princes and kings to recommend the person who could be made the king of Yan. The princes and ministers of Changsha asked the prince Jian to be the king of Yan.
In March, the emperor issued an edict saying: It has been twelve years since I ascended the throne as the Son of Heaven and proclaimed myself Emperor in the world.
Together with the heroes and wise men of the world, we will pacify the world and govern the world together. The superior officials with meritorious services will be granted the title of king, the second grade will be granted the title of marquis, and the inferior officials will be given special food and towns.
Some of the relatives of meritorious officials were granted the title of marquis, and were allowed to set up their own officials and collect their own taxes, and their daughters also had Tang Muyi.
Those who owned food and towns for the princes were given seals and ribbons and were rewarded with large houses.
Officials with two thousand shi moved to Chang'an and were rewarded with houses according to their rank.
The soldiers who followed me into the Shu Han Dynasty and settled the Three Qin Dynasties were all exempted from taxes and servitude for generations.
I have treated all the wise men and heroes in the world rightly.
If there is an ungrateful person who betrays the emperor and supports his troops, I will mobilize all the people in the world to punish him.
I am announcing this to the world so that everyone can understand what I mean.
When the emperor attacked Yingbu, he was shot by a stray arrow and fell ill during the battle.
The condition gradually worsened. Empress Lu invited a good doctor.
The doctor came in and the emperor asked what he thought of the injury.
The doctor said: The disease will get better.
At this time, the emperor laughed and cursed at the doctor. He said: I use a commoner to carry a three-foot sword to conquer the world. Isn't this destiny?
My destiny is in heaven, so what good will it do me if Bian Que, the miracle doctor, is reincarnated!
He refused to let the doctor diagnose the disease, rewarded him with fifty pounds of gold, and asked him to leave the palace.
Queen Lu asked: Your Majesty, a hundred years later, Prime Minister Xiao He will also pass away. Who can replace him as prime minister?
The emperor said: Cao Shen can do it.
Empress Lu asked who would succeed Cao Shen, and the emperor said: "Wang Ling can, but he has a somewhat upright character. Chen Ping can help him."
Chen Ping was resourceful, but it was difficult for him to serve as prime minister alone.
Zhou Bo was old and prudent but not good at diction, but it was Zhou Bo who stabilized Liu Han and allowed him to serve as Taiwei.
Empress Lu asked who would succeed him in the future, and the emperor said: "I can't say clearly in the future."
Lu Wan and thousands of others waited at the border fortress, hoping that the emperor would recover and go to court to apologize and defend himself against false accusations.
On April 25th in the summer, Emperor Gao died in Changle Palace. After hearing the news, Lu Wan fled to the Huns.
Empress Lu said to Shen Shiqi: Many generals and emperors were registered as civilians in the past. Later, they became ministers in the north, but they were always dissatisfied. Now they want to fight for the young master again. If they are not killed, the world will be uneasy.
Therefore, obituary notices of the emperor's death were not published.
Someone heard about the emperor's death and told Li Shang.
When Li Shang saw the emperor, he said: "I heard that the emperor had passed away, but he still did not mourn for four days, so he wanted to kill the princes."
If this is the case, the world will be in danger.
Chen Ping and Guan Ying led 100,000 troops to guard Xingyang, while Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo led 200,000 troops to suppress Yan and Dai. If they heard that the emperor had died and wanted to kill the generals, they would join forces and march to Kyoto to seize Guanzhong.
If the ministers rebel internally and the generals rebel externally, defeat will be inevitable.
Shen Shi conveyed this statement to Empress Lu, who announced a general amnesty on April 28th.
On May 17, the emperor was buried in Changling.
After the coffin was lowered, the Crown Prince and his ministers all returned to the Supreme Emperor's Temple.
The emperor and his ministers said: The emperor rose from the common people, turned the tide and returned to the right path, pacified the world, and became the founding ancestor of the Han Dynasty, with the highest credit.
His title is Emperor Gao.
Originally, Emperor Gaozu did not pay much attention to book knowledge, but he was cheerful and intelligent by nature, good at thinking, and able to gather opinions from everyone. He could get along easily with everyone from the people and officials to ordinary soldiers.
At the beginning of entering the Pass, he made three chapters in compliance with the people's wishes. After the world was peaceful, he ordered Xiao He to organize the laws and regulations, ordered Han Xin to establish and improve military disciplines, ordered Zhang Cang to unify the calendar, weights and measures, etc., ordered Shusun Tong to formulate various etiquette and rituals, and ordered Lu Jia to write a "Xinyu" summarizing the rise and fall of history.
He also cut the talisman and swore an oath with each of the meritorious officials, wrote an iron deed in elixir, stored it in a gold cabinet and stone chamber, and kept it in the ancestral temple.
Although Emperor Gaozu was busy with everything, the plans and measures he made were far-reaching.
Ban Gu commented: "Spring and Autumn" Jin historian Cai Mo said: The Tao Tang family established by Tang Yao declined. Later, Liu Lei learned the art of dragon training and ministered to Kong Jia, the son of Xia Dynasty. The Fan family of Jin was his descendant.
Fan Xuanzi, a doctor of the Jin Dynasty, also said: My ancestors were Tao and Tangmin from Yu and above, the Yulong family in the Xia Dynasty, the Wei family in the Shang Dynasty, the Du family in the Tang Dynasty, and the Fan family when the Jin Dynasty was the overlord.
The Fan family was the Zhengqing of the Jin Dynasty, and he fled to Qin during the reign of Duke Wen of Lu.
Later it returned to the Jin Dynasty, and the one who stayed in Qin was the Liu family.
Liu Xiang said that when the Kingdom was established, the Liu family returned to Wei from Qin, Qin attacked Wei, and the Wei capital moved to Daliang, all in Fengdi, so Zhou Shi persuaded Yong Chi and said: Feng is the place where Wei moved.
Accordingly, in praising the emperor of the Han Dynasty, he said: The lineage of the Han emperors comes from Emperor Yao of the Tao and Tang Dynasties.
It was passed down to the Zhou Dynasty, and his surname was Liu in Qin.
Passing through Wei and heading east, he became Feng Gong.
Feng Gong may be the father of the Supreme Emperor.
Not long after they moved to Feng, there were not many graves in Fengdi.
When Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, he set up ancestral temple officials, so there were ancestral temples in Qin, Jin, Liang, and Jing. From generation to generation, ancestral temples have been offering sacrifices to ancestors in heaven and earth, and the incense continues. This has its roots!
It can be inferred from this that the Han Dynasty inherited the fortune of Yao, and its virtues were at its peak. The prophecy of breaking the snake and reuniting it. The white emperor's son was killed by the red emperor's son. The flag is mainly red, which is a symbol of the virtue of fire. The natural induction of fire replacing wood is in line with the law of heaven's order.
summary:
In the winter of the fifth year, the King of Han pursued Xiang Yu but his allies Han Xin and Peng Yue failed to meet as scheduled. Xiang Yu defeated the Han forces, forcing the king to retreat and fortify his position. Following Zhang Liang's advice to share conquered territories, the king promised Han Xin the lands east of Chen to the Bohai Sea and Peng Yue the area north of Suiyang to Gucheng. Both then joined forces. Liu Jia invaded Chu, and Zhou Yin surrendered. In December, Han forces surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia. Hearing Chu songs on all sides, Xiang Yu fled with cavalry and was pursued to Dongcheng. The Chu lands were pacified, though Lu initially refused to surrender until shown Xiang Yu's head. Xiang Yu was buried with the rites of Duke of Lu.

In the sixth year, the king honored his brother as Marquis of Wu Ai, appointed Han Xin as King of Chu, and made Peng Yue King of Liang. A general amnesty was declared except for capital crimes. The princes petitioned the king to accept the title of Emperor, which he initially declined but eventually accepted on an auspicious day in the second month. Queen Lu was honored as empress, the prince as crown prince. Wu Rui was made King of Changsha, and the former King of Guangdong was restored. The capital was established at Luoyang. Soldiers were demobilized, with exemptions from taxes for those in Guanzhong and those returning home. Former slaves were freed, and military officials were granted titles and lands according to merit.

In subsequent years, the emperor dealt with various rebellions. Zang Tu of Yan rebelled and was captured. Han Xin of Chu was arrested on suspicion of rebellion and demoted to Marquis of Huaiyin. The emperor established various princes, including Liu Jia as King of Jing and Liu Fei as King of Qi. When generals grew restless over delayed rewards, Zhang Liang advised rewarding the emperor's former enemy Yong Chi first, which calmed everyone. The emperor honored his father as Supreme Emperor.

The Xiongnu besieged King Xin of Han, who surrendered. The emperor personally led campaigns against the Xiongnu and rebels, suffering defeats and victories. He established his son Ruyi as acting king of Dai. Xiao He constructed magnificent palaces, which initially angered the emperor but was justified as demonstrating imperial authority. The capital moved to Chang'an. Zhao officials plotted assassination but were exposed. The emperor dealt with Chen Xi's rebellion, personally leading forces to Handan and bribing enemy generals to surrender.

In the twelfth year, Han Xin was executed for rebellion in Chang'an. Peng Yue rebelled and was executed. Yingbu of Huainan rebelled; the emperor personally led forces against him, defeating him at Huifou. Returning through his hometown of Pei County, the emperor held a grand banquet, sang about returning home in glory, and exempted Pei from taxes. He was wounded by an arrow during the Yingbu campaign and grew ill. When Empress Lu asked about successors, he named Cao Shen, then Wang Ling with Chen Ping's assistance, and Zhou Bo as Taiwei. Emperor Gao died in Changle Palace in the fourth month. Empress Lu initially concealed his death to plot against the generals but was persuaded otherwise. He was buried at Changling and posthumously titled Emperor Gao.

translation:
In the past, the Zhou Dynasty learned from the lessons of the Xia and Shang dynasties. King Wen, King Wu, and Duke Zhou formulated laws and regulations, established five titles such as duke, marquis, uncle, son, and male, and enfeoffed 800 vassal states, among which more than 50 had the same surname as the emperor.
Zhou Gong and Kang Shu established vassal vassals in Lu and Wei, each with a radius of hundreds of miles; Jiang Taigong established vassal in Qi, which was also the place where the five princes and nine states were the chief.
The "Book of Songs" records the system at that time: The army is used as a fence, and the grand master is used as a wall.
Use the princes of the big country as a barrier, and use the royal family with the same surname as a pillar.
If one can govern with virtue, the world will be at peace, and the castle of the son of the feudal clan will be strong.
The castle cannot be destroyed and the clan cannot be isolated. Otherwise, fear and uneasiness will arise.
Therefore, relatives and virtuous people are awarded titles together, and commending and commending people with meritorious deeds is fundamental to the prosperity and decline of the country and the stability of the world, and cannot be changed.
Therefore, when the Zhou Dynasty was strong, the Dukes of Zhou and Shao participated in running the country, reaching a state where no one broke the law and the criminal law was put aside; when it declined, the Five Hegemons supported them and guarded the world together.
Since King You and King Ping, the country has been declining day by day, and has even become uneasy between powerful vassal states. It has also split into two small kingdoms, the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and the Western Zhou Dynasty. There is a high platform for the emperor to escape debts and refuge, and there are rumors that the guillotine, which symbolizes royal power, has been stolen and hidden.
However, the world still calls it the common master, and the powerful princes dare not destroy it.
After more than 800 years, all the merits were finally lost, the throne ended with King Nan, the emperor was demoted to a commoner, and died of natural causes.
Although the title and throne were lost in the world, the branches and leaves still seemed to be maintained. No one dared to occupy the empty throne. There was no emperor in the world for more than thirty years.
The Qin Dynasty relied on its superior terrain and deceitful troops to annex the six vassal states east of Mount Wei, and won victory in one go.
Therefore, it boasted that it knew the world well, thought that one person knew the cause of founding the country, slandered and ridiculed three generations, eradicated and eradicated ancient methods, and secretly gave itself the title of emperor, but its children were ordinary people, with no flesh and blood of the same origin to help them, and no vassal states with land to protect them outside.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up with a wooden stick, and Liu Bang and Xiang Ji immediately destroyed the Qin Dynasty.
Therefore, it is said that the Zhou Dynasty enjoyed the country for too long and the Qin Dynasty did not reach a hundred years, both of which were caused by the power of the country.
In the early years of the rise of the Han Dynasty, the world had just been peaceful and there were few clans with the same surname. Emperor Gaozu learned from the experience of the Qin Dynasty, which collapsed due to isolation and helplessness, so he began to divide the territory and establish princes and second-class titles.
There are more than a hundred cities and towns among the meritorious officials. The children of the royal family are more noble and have a territory larger than that of the Nine Kingdoms.
From Yanmen to the east to the north bank of the Liao River are the states of Yan and Dai.
Changshan Mountain to the south, Taihang Mountain to the east, across the river and Jishui, and into the sea, are the states of Qi and Zhao.
The Gushui and Swimming areas, including Guishan and Mengshan, were the two kingdoms of Liang and Chu.
Containing rivers and lakes in the east and close to Kuaiji, is the Kingdom of Wu.
To the north is the Huaihe River, including Mount Lu and Hengshan, and is the Huainan Kingdom.
Going south from the Han River to Jiuyi Mountain is the Kingdom of Changsha.
The vassal states are connected one after another, surrounded by the north, Shu, and south sides, and bordered by Hu Di and Nanyue.
The emperor himself has Hedong, Henan, Hanoi, Dongjun, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, from Jiangling to Bashu in the west, and from Yunzhong to Longxi in the north, including the capital, a total of fifteen counties, among which there are also the fiefdoms of princesses and princes.
A large vassal state spans several states and counties, connects dozens of cities, and has the same palace and official system as the capital. It can be said to be overkill.
Even so, Emperor Gaozu established the foundation and had no leisure for a day. Emperor Hui's reign was short, and Empress Gao used a woman as regent. However, the country was safe and sound, and there was no excess to worry about. Later, the disaster that destroyed the Lu family and the success of Emperor Wen's imperial career also relied on the power of the princes.
However, the feudal lords were originally powerful in their country, and the currents were overflowing. The smaller ones are dissolute and illegal, while the larger ones are rampant and unruly, causing harm to themselves and the country.
Therefore, Emperor Wen adopted Jia Yi's suggestion to divide Qi and Zhao, and Emperor Jing adopted Chao Cuo's strategy to weaken Wu, Chu and other states.
Emperor Wu implemented his father's plan and issued a favor order, which enabled the princes and kings to allocate part of the households and cities to their children without having to abolish the migration, and the vassal state itself fell apart.
From then on, the State of Qi was divided into seven small states, the State of Zhao was divided into six, the State of Liang was divided into five, and the State of Huainan was divided into three.
When the prince began to be crowned king, the larger ones were no more than ten cities.
Although Changsha, Yan, Dai and other countries still have their old names, they no longer have the previous north-south boundaries.
When Emperor Jing suffered from the disasters of the Seven Kingdoms, he suppressed and weakened the princes and dismissed officials from various countries.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, the two kings of Hengshan and Huainan rebelled, so they established laws on the officials of the princes and severely punished those who violated the law. The princes could only receive food, clothing, taxes, and rent, but could not participate in political affairs.
By the time of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, the princes were all descendants of their ancestors and had an alienated relationship with the emperor. They were born in palaces and were not respected by scholars and common people. Their power was no different from that of wealthy families.
The emperors all died young and had no heirs for three consecutive dynasties. Therefore, Wang Mang knew that the Han Dynasty was in danger both internally and externally and was weak, so he had no scruples and became treacherous. Relying on the authority of his aunt and the Queen Mother, he pretended to be Duke of Zhou to deceive people's hearts, dominate the court, and make the world run without going down the steps.
Once the treacherous plan was completed, he usurped the emperor's position, sent officials separately and quickly spread the word throughout the world, issuing the emperor's orders.
The princes and kings of the Han Dynasty were so frightened by the lustful power that they all prostrated on the ground and offered jade seals and ribbons, fearing that they would be left behind. Some even sang praises and flattery to please them. How sad!
So I found out how the princes changed from strong to weak from beginning to end, as a punishment.
